A regression should assert that one failed SMS schedule leaves the reminder, that a second failure removes it on the next run, and that email or WhatsApp reminders and already scheduled SMS rows are not deleted by the retryCount clause. Without that, the unscoped OR delete and the off-path skips (no phone number, persistence failure after Twilio accepts) can ship unnoticed.

title: Team/org auth SQL is an ungrouped OR, so extra AND filters skip team bookings
body: buildOrgAuthorizationCondition and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition return a top-level OR, e.g. (("teamId" = ANY(...)) AND ("isTeamBooking" = true)) OR (("userId" = ANY(...)) AND ("isTeamBooking" = false)), with no parentheses around the whole predicate. getBaseConditions returns that fragment unchanged whenever there is no eventTypeId/memberUserId filter (the common path; date bounds are not part of InsightsBookingServiceFilterOptions and must be applied by the caller). AND binds tighter than OR, so WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "startTime" >= ${start} AND "startTime" < ${end} is parsed as (team-booking match) OR (personal-booking match AND date range). Every team booking for that team/org is returned with no time bound, and any other caller AND (event-type allow-list, status, extra auth) is likewise dropped for the team-booking side. The same trap exists on the public event-type filter at the ungrouped OR in buildFilterConditions ("eventTypeId" = $1 OR "eventParentId" = $1): WHERE auth AND that fragment becomes (auth AND eventTypeId = $1) OR eventParentId = $1, which can return rows outside authorization. getBaseConditions only parenthesizes when both auth and filters are present, and the tests assert the ungrouped form, so they do not catch this. Wrap every returned fragment in an outer (...) so it is one grouped predicate before it is embedded.

title: ANY(${number[]}) does not bind a Postgres array, so team/org auth queries fail
body: Org and team authorization interpolate JavaScript number arrays as Prisma.sql`"teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})` and `"userId" = ANY(${uniqueUserIds})` (same pattern at the team-scope user list). Prisma.sql binds each interpolated value as one query parameter; a JS array is not expanded into a PostgreSQL int[]. At execution this typically errors with operator does not exist: integer = text or malformed array literal (the parameter is sent as text/JSON like [1,2,3], not '{1,2,3}'::int[]). Team and org insights then throw instead of returning rows. The length > 0 guard avoids an empty list but does not fix binding. Use a form Prisma actually supports, such as "teamId" IN (${Prisma.join(teamIds)}) or "teamId" = ANY(ARRAY[${Prisma.join(teamIds)}]::int[]), and keep the empty-list guard because Prisma.join([]) produces invalid IN (). The new tests never execute these statements: they deep-compare Sql objects, and the only $queryRaw case is user scope, which has no ANY().

title: Composed-condition assertions compare nested Sql objects to flat templates
body: Team scope (this expect), org scope, and the combined eventTypeId+memberUserId filter expect a single flat Prisma.sql`...` template. The service builds those predicates with reduce, nesting fragments (Prisma.sql`(${acc}) OR (${condition})` / AND). Prisma stores nested Sql instances on .values and only flattens them when the query runs, so Vitest toEqual compares different .strings/.values and these tests fail even if the rendered SQL matches. The author noted the suite was not run. User-scope and single-filter expects happen to be one template on both sides and can pass while the composed authorization paths stay red and unexecuted. Assert rendered SQL (or execute team/org conditions with $queryRaw, including a row that must be excluded) instead of structural equality of differently built Sql objects.

title: ANY() on JS arrays will fail when team/org SQL runs
body: Org and team authorization bind id lists as `"teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})` (line 164), `"userId" = ANY(${uniqueUserIds})` (line 168), and `"userId" = ANY(${userIdsFromTeam})` (line 201). Prisma's raw-query engine does not send a JavaScript number array as a PostgreSQL array parameter; it is passed as text such as `[1,2,3]`. PostgreSQL then rejects the statement (`malformed array literal` or `op ANY/ALL (array) requires array on right side`) instead of returning bookings. Team and org insights therefore error at runtime. Use scalar binding, for example `IN (${Prisma.join(ids)})` or `= ANY(ARRAY[${Prisma.join(ids)}]::int[])`, and keep the existing empty-list guard because `Prisma.join([])` throws. The new `$queryRaw` test only executes the user-scope predicate (`"userId" = $1 AND "teamId" IS NULL`), which never uses `ANY`, so this failure is not covered.

title: toEqual(Prisma.sql) does not match composed fragments
body: Team-scope (line 295), org-scope (line 332), and combined-filter (line 429) expectations are a single flat `Prisma.sql` template. The service builds those predicates with `reduce` into `Prisma.sql`(${acc}) OR/AND (${condition})`, which stores nested `Prisma.Sql` objects in `.values` and only flattens them when the query is executed. Vitest `toEqual` compares `.strings` and `.values` and does not render nested fragments, so these three assertions fail even when the SQL that would be sent is equivalent. User-scope and single-filter tests pass only because those paths return one flat template. Assert a flattened rendering, or build the expected value with the same nesting, otherwise CI cannot validate the composed authorization SQL.

title: Team scope without teamId now typechecks and returns no rows
body: The constructor previously required `InsightsBookingServiceOptions`, the zod discriminated union that makes `teamId` mandatory when `scope` is `"team"`. It now accepts `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`, where `teamId` is optional for every scope. A team-scoped call that omits `teamId` still fails `safeParse`, is stored as `this.options = null`, and `buildAuthorizationConditions` returns `1=0` with no error. Callers get an empty insights result that looks like "no bookings" instead of a compile-time or thrown validation error. Keep the discriminated union on the constructor, or throw when `safeParse` fails, so a missing `teamId` cannot be confused with an authorized empty set.

title: OR auth fragment is not fully parenthesized, so extra AND filters skip team bookings
body: Team and org authorization SQL is built as `(<team predicate>) OR (<user predicate>)` (org reduce at lines 171-174, team reduce at lines 204-207). Those parentheses wrap each branch only, not the whole OR. `getBaseConditions` returns that fragment as-is when there is no event-type or member filter (line 75). AND binds tighter than OR in PostgreSQL, so the intended caller query `WHERE ${await service.getBaseConditions()} AND "startTime" >= ${from} AND "startTime" < ${to}` — the replacement for the removed `findMany`, which ANDed caller filters onto the entire authorization object — is parsed as `team_booking_predicate OR (personal_booking_predicate AND startTime filters)`. Every team booking for that team or org is included no matter what date, status, or other AND predicates the caller adds. Insights over-count and can return bookings outside the window the caller applied. `getBaseConditions` only wraps the auth fragment when a service-level filter is also present (line 73). Wrap the full OR, and the final fragment returned to callers, in parentheses. The new tests expect this unparenthesized text and never run team/org SQL with an additional AND, so they do not catch it.

title: toEqual(Prisma.sql) does not match nested SQL fragments
body: Composed conditions are built by nesting `Prisma.sql` values (`(${acc}) OR (${condition})` and the filter AND reduce). Prisma does not flatten nested `strings`/`values` until execution, so the object from `getAuthorizationConditions`/`getFilterConditions` is not deeply equal to a single flat `Prisma.sql` template with the same text. `expect(conditions).toEqual(Prisma.sql`...`)` therefore fails for the team-scope assertion (line 295), the org-scope assertion (line 332), and the combined-filter assertion (line 429) — the cases that use `ANY(...)` and OR. Flat cases (user scope, a single filter, `1=0`) can still pass. The only test that executes SQL is the user-scope `$queryRaw` query, which never hits `ANY` or the OR precedence bug. Compare flattened SQL text and bound values, or run the team/org fragments, instead of `toEqual` on raw `Prisma.Sql` objects.

title: Empty updateMany throws after every cache write
body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) after upserting CalendarCache. Prisma Client rejects updateMany when data is an empty object ("Argument data needs at least one argument"), so this throws on every successful cache fill, including Google webhook refreshes and the refill at the end of unwatchCalendar. Callers that treat the throw as a sync/watch failure will retry, record errors, and can eventually stop watching the calendar even though the cache write already succeeded. An empty payload also does not reliably bump SelectedCalendar.updatedAt. The new repository method types data as SelectedCalendarUpdateInput, which is not assignable to updateMany's UpdateManyMutationInput. Pass an explicit update such as { updatedAt: new Date() }.

title: Cache delete does not refresh connected calendars
body: deleteCacheMutation only toasts and calls the optional onSuccess prop. Unlike the disconnect mutation in the same component, it never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars (or apps.integrations). The calendar settings query lives in SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper and onChanged is often omitted, so after a successful delete the dropdown still shows the previous Last updated time and the delete action. Users are told the cache was deleted while the UI keeps offering to delete it until a full reload.

title: Cache timestamp format is a type error and ignores locale
body: The last-updated label always does new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" }).format(new Date(cacheUpdatedAt)). cacheUpdatedAt is Date | null | undefined, and hasCache is a separate boolean, so TypeScript does not narrow it; new Date(cacheUpdatedAt) is not assignable under strictNullChecks and should fail typecheck. The formatter is also hardcoded to en-US, so the translated cache_last_updated string still shows a US timestamp for every locale. Format only a narrowed Date with the active locale.

title: Deleting cache does not stop watches that recreate it
body: deleteCacheHandler only runs calendarCache.deleteMany for the credential. It does not clear Google channel fields or stop notification channels. Webhook handling calls fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache, which writes CalendarCache again, so for any watched Google calendar the rows return on the next push and the delete looks like it failed. The new confirm_delete_cache string says the action cannot be undone, which is false while watches are active. Either stop watches the way unwatchCalendar does before deleting, or tell the user the cache will be rebuilt and trigger a refetch. The access check also throws a plain Error, which tRPC reports as an internal 500 instead of NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN.

title: Cache status counts expired rows as live cache
body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups every CalendarCache row for the credential and takes max(updatedAt), with no expiresAt >= now filter. Availability reads ignore expired rows, but the settings dropdown treats any truthy cacheUpdatedAt as live cache and offers Delete cached data. Credentials whose cache has fully expired still show a last-updated time. Restrict the query to unexpired rows, and return no status when every row is expired.

title: Existing cache rows are stamped with migration time
body: updatedAt is added as NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(), so every existing CalendarCache row gets the migration execution time rather than the last free/busy write. The new status query uses max(updatedAt), so after deploy every Google credential that already has cache will show that deploy timestamp as Last updated until the next Prisma upsert. Backfill from a closer signal (for example expiresAt minus the cache TTL) or keep legacy updatedAt null and only display a timestamp after a real update.

title: Webhook helper fails on Linux and writes the wrong env file
body: The script updates GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL with sed -i '', which is BSD/macOS sed and fails on GNU sed, so the env update does not work on Linux. ENV_FILE is ../.env relative to the current working directory, not the script or repo root. Running bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repository root therefore targets a path outside the repo, and if that file is missing touch creates it and writes the tunnel URL there instead of the project .env. Resolve the env path from the script directory and use a portable in-place edit.

title: No tests for cache delete authorization or status
body: deleteCache is a new mutation that deletes CalendarCache rows after an ownership check, and getCacheStatusByCredentialIds changes what connectedCalendars returns, but there are no unit or integration tests. A dropped userId filter, deleting another user's credential, or stale cacheUpdatedAt after delete would not be caught. Cover owner success, rejection of another user's credentialId, and that connected calendars no longer report cache after deletion.

title: Deleting cache does not refresh connected calendars
body: deleteCacheMutation only toasts and calls the optional onSuccess prop. Unlike the disconnect mutation in the same component, it never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars (or apps.integrations). SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper owns that query with refetchOnWindowFocus: false and passes props.onChanged, which is often undefined and is not a refetch of this query. After a successful delete the dropdown still shows the old "Last updated" time and "Delete cached data" until a full reload, so the action looks like it failed.

title: Cache timestamp render is not null-safe and ignores locale
body: cacheUpdatedAt is Date | null | undefined, and assigning isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt to hasCache does not narrow it. new Date(cacheUpdatedAt) is therefore a strict-null type error, and if a null/invalid value is formatted, Intl.DateTimeFormat.format throws RangeError and crashes the whole connected-calendars list. The formatter is also hardcoded to "en-US", so every locale sees US date/time formatting inside an otherwise translated string.

title: updatedAt backfill marks every existing cache as just written
body: ADD COLUMN updatedAt TIMESTAMP(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW() sets every existing CalendarCache row to the migration transaction time. The new UI treats that value as "Last updated", so on deploy every Google calendar with a cache row looks freshly synced even if the row is old or already past expiresAt. now() is STABLE, not a constant, so Postgres cannot use the PG11 fast-default path and will rewrite CalendarCache under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock. The header comment also says the column was added without a default, which is the opposite of this SQL. Backfill from a real write time (or leave the column nullable until the next upsert) and avoid a single volatile default on a large table.

title: Every cache fill rewrites all SelectedCalendar rows
body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache now calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) after writing CalendarCache. That runs on the Google webhook/cache-refresh path and updates every SelectedCalendar for the credential even though the selection did not change. The new UI never reads SelectedCalendar.updatedAt; it reads CalendarCache.updatedAt, which Prisma already bumps on calendarCache.upsert. The empty data object does not set updatedAt explicitly (it only works if Prisma injects @updatedAt), and updateManyByCredentialId types data as SelectedCalendarUpdateInput, which is not updateMany's UpdateManyMutationInput, so this can fail typecheck or throw at runtime after the cache write already succeeded. Remove the call.

title: Cache status ignores expiry
body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups CalendarCache by credentialId and takes max(updatedAt) with no expiresAt >= now() filter. getCachedAvailability only serves rows that have not expired, but the settings UI treats any returned updatedAt as an active cache and offers "Delete cached data". Expired rows therefore show a last-updated time and a delete action for data that availability will not use. After the migration backfill, that timestamp is also the deploy time rather than the last real refresh.

title: dev:cron now depends on undeclared npx tsx
body: dev:cron changed from ts-node, which is a devDependency of @calcom/web, to npx tsx. tsx is not declared in this package, and the app is on Yarn 3.4.1, where npx is not the project runner. yarn dev:cron will fail offline, in CI images without npm/npx, or by downloading an arbitrary tsx version outside the lockfile. Add tsx as a devDependency and invoke it via yarn, or keep ts-node.

title: Webhook helper writes the wrong env file and is macOS-only
body: ENV_FILE is ../.env relative to the process cwd, and the script never cds to its own directory. Running bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repo root (the usual way) creates or edits a .env outside the repo and still prints success, so GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL never reaches the app. The update uses sed -i '' (line 68), which is BSD sed syntax and fails on GNU sed, and cleanup always exits 0, including when the tunnel URL cannot be parsed or sed fails. Resolve the env path from the script location, use a portable in-place edit, and exit non-zero on failure.

title: Empty actions slot still reserves width
body: DisconnectIntegration used to be omitted entirely for delegation credentials and when connection changes are disabled. It is now always wrapped in a flex w-32 div, while CredentialActionsDropdown returns null when the user cannot disconnect and there is no cache. Those rows keep an empty 8rem actions column, shifting the calendar card and error alert layout.

title: No tests for cache delete authorization or status mapping
body: deleteCache is a new authenticated mutation that deletes CalendarCache rows after a userId ownership check, and connectedCalendars now exposes cacheUpdatedAt from getCacheStatusByCredentialIds. There are no tests for a missing/foreign credential, a successful delete, the plain Error (which tRPC surfaces as 500 rather than NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN), or for expired vs active cache rows. A regression in the where clause would let one user wipe another user's availability cache or leave the settings UI stale.

title: Deleting cache leaves the UI showing the old cache status
body: deleteCacheMutation only toasts and calls the optional onSuccess prop. Unlike the disconnect mutation in the same component, it never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. That query is what supplies cacheUpdatedAt, and SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper loads it with refetchOnWindowFocus: false. After a successful delete the menu still shows the previous "Last updated" time and "Delete cached data" until a full remount, so the action looks like it failed.

title: Cache status treats expired rows as a live cache
body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups CalendarCache by credentialId and takes max(updatedAt) with no expiresAt filter. getCachedAvailability only treats a row as a hit when expiresAt is still in the future. Any leftover expired row therefore makes connected calendars report cacheUpdatedAt and the dropdown offers "Delete cached data" even though availability lookups are already cache misses. The status does not mean the cache is serving data.

title: Backfill stamps every existing cache as updated at migrate time
body: The new updatedAt column is added as NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(), so every existing CalendarCache row gets the migration timestamp rather than when it was actually written. CalendarCache has no createdAt; the only freshness signal already stored is expiresAt (writes set it to about now + 30 days). After deploy, every Google credential with any historical cache row shows "Last updated" as the deploy time, including stale and expired caches, which defeats the status feature. Backfill from expiresAt minus the cache TTL (and drop the default only if you still want Prisma @updatedAt to own later writes) before this ships; it cannot be reconstructed later.

title: Cache delete is undone by active Google watches
body: deleteCacheHandler only runs calendarCache.deleteMany for the credential. It does not stop google channel subscriptions on SelectedCalendar, and GoogleCalendarService.fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache (called from the webhook path) writes CalendarCache again and then touches those selected calendars. The confirmation copy says the delete cannot be undone, but the next notification recreates the rows. Users clearing a bad cache will see it return with no explanation, and a reload can show a new timestamp as if the delete did not stick.

title: Delegation calendar cache is invisible to status and delete
body: Cache status is loaded only via getCacheStatusByCredentialIds(connected calendar credential ids). The same repository documents that in-memory delegation credentials use negative ids that are not stored on CalendarCache, and reads for those users are keyed by userId plus the free/busy key so they can reuse a real credential's cache. Those org/delegation Google connections — the users the calendar-cache feature flag is aimed at — always get cacheUpdatedAt null, so the new menu never offers delete. deleteCacheHandler cannot fix that either: it requires a Credential row with id = credentialId and userId = the session user, which does not match a negative in-memory id or a cache row owned by another credential id.

title: dev:cron now calls tsx, which this package does not depend on
body: dev:cron changed from ts-node cron-tester.ts to npx tsx cron-tester.ts. ts-node is a declared devDependency; tsx is not in this package.json, and the app pins Yarn 3.4.1, where npx is not the workspace runner and will try to fetch tsx outside the lockfile. yarn dev:cron fails offline or in CI, or runs an unpinned tsx. This change is unrelated to calendar cache and should stay on the declared runner or add tsx as a dependency and invoke it through Yarn.

title: Webhook helper is macOS-only and writes .env relative to the cwd
body: The new script updates GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL with sed -i '' (BSD sed). On GNU sed that form treats '' as the script and does not edit the file, so Linux developers never get the tunnel URL written. ENV_FILE is ../.env relative to the current working directory, not the script path: running bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repo root writes the parent directory's .env, not the app env file. cleanup also always exits 0, so a failed tunnel startup is reported as success.

title: No tests for deleteCache ownership or status mapping
body: deleteCache is a new authenticated mutation that deletes every CalendarCache row for a client-supplied credentialId after a userId check, and connectedCalendars now depends on getCacheStatusByCredentialIds. Nothing in the PR covers another user (or a negative delegation id) being rejected, a successful delete actually removing rows, or expired versus live rows being mapped to cacheUpdatedAt. A regression in the ownership where-clause would ship silently.

title: Reminder cancellation is fire-and-forget and can be dropped
body: On cancel, deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are started inside forEach and never awaited, and the handler returns after awaiting unrelated calendar/prisma work. The email path only persists WorkflowReminder.cancelled=true; it does not call SendGrid in this request. On a serverless API route the isolate can freeze before that update commits, so cancelled stays unset and the cron never cancels the batch. The same un-awaited forEach is used for reschedule in handleNewBooking.ts around line 966 (wrapped in a try/catch that cannot see async failures), requestReschedule in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx around line 488, and workflow delete/update in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx around lines 212, 376, 519, and 574. This PR removed the previously awaited workflowReminder deletes, so a dropped call now means the reminder email or SMS is still sent.

title: immediateDelete cancels SendGrid and then forgets the row
body: When immediateDelete is true, deleteScheduledEmailReminder POSTs a SendGrid batch cancel and returns without setting cancelled=true or deleting the WorkflowReminder. Reschedule (handleNewBooking.ts) uses this flag, so a failed or dropped SendGrid call leaves an active scheduled row that the cron will not retry, because the cron only cancels rows with cancelled=true. Workflow and step deletion also pass true and then cascade-delete the rows, so a failed cancel cannot be retried either. Immediate cancels also occupy a SendGrid scheduled_sends slot until the original send time. That is the 100-pending-cancellation cap this PR is trying to avoid, and rescheduling far-future reminders reintroduces it on the path the PR claims to fix.

title: Cron deletes cancelled reminders before cancelling them at SendGrid
body: The handler first deleteMany's every EMAIL WorkflowReminder whose scheduledDate is already in the past, including cancelled=true rows that were never cancelled at SendGrid. Only after that does it load cancelled reminders and POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends. The cron runs every 15 minutes and only attempts SendGrid cancel inside a one-hour window. If a run is skipped or the cancel loop throws while a cancelled reminder's send time elapses, the next run removes the row and leaves the SendGrid batch scheduled, so the reminder is still delivered. Past-due cancelled rows must be cancelled at SendGrid before deletion, and this deleteMany must exclude cancelled=true.

title: One SendGrid cancel error aborts every other cancellation
body: The cancel loop awaits client.request for each reminder and only deletes WorkflowReminder rows after the whole loop. Any throw (missing referenceId, an already-sent or already-cancelled batch, or SendGrid's 100 pending-cancellation limit) jumps to the catch, skips the rest of the list, and does not await the deletes already queued. Those in-flight deletes can also be dropped when the request ends. The next run loads the same rows. A single poison reminder therefore blocks cancellation of every other due reminder, and batches that were already cancelled are retried every 15 minutes, which can keep the account pinned at the cancellation cap. Each reminder needs its own try/catch, and its row should be deleted only after that reminder's cancel succeeds.

title: Deferred cancel still sends reminders due before the next cron tick
body: The non-immediate path only sets cancelled=true and waits for scheduleEmailReminders to POST the SendGrid cancel. That job runs every 15 minutes and only considers sends inside the next hour. A booking cancelled or rescheduled when the reminder is due sooner than the next cron run is still delivered, because nothing in the request calls SendGrid and there is no second chance once scheduledDate is in the past (those rows are deleted first). Sends already inside the cron interval need an immediate SendGrid cancel here; deferral is only safe for sends further out.

title: No tests for the deferred cancellation the last fix got wrong
body: This change replaces immediate SendGrid cancellation with a cancelled flag plus cron finalization, and it adds no tests. Nothing asserts that a cancelled reminder inside the next hour is cancelled at SendGrid and then deleted, that one SendGrid failure does not skip the rest, that past-due cancelled rows are not deleted before cancel, or that booking cancel and reschedule actually persist cancelled=true before the handler returns. The previous fix (#6991) shipped broken for this same production bug; this regression will not be caught.

title: Overdue cancelled reminders are deleted before SendGrid is cancelled
body: The cron deletes every EMAIL WorkflowReminder whose scheduledDate is already <= now before it looks up cancelled reminders. The cancel query only then loads rows with cancelled=true and scheduledDate <= now+1 hour, so any cancelled reminder whose send time has passed is already gone and never gets POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends status=cancel. Booking cancellation only sets cancelled=true and does not call SendGrid (handleCancelBooking.ts around the deleteScheduledEmailReminder call). Combined with a cron that the PR says runs every 15 minutes, a booking cancelled after the last tick before the reminder (or any missed run that returns after scheduledDate) still delivers the email, and the tracking row is removed so a later run cannot retry. Cancel SendGrid first, including slightly overdue cancelled rows, and do not delete those rows until the cancel succeeds.

title: Unscheduled reminder query ignores cancellation and booking status
body: The query that actually submits emails to SendGrid filters only method=EMAIL, scheduled=false, and scheduledDate within 72 hours. It does not exclude cancelled=true and does not check booking.status. Any leftover unscheduled reminder for a cancelled or rescheduled booking is therefore scheduled and sent. That leftover is guaranteed for paid cancellations, which return before reminder cleanup (handleCancelBooking.ts line 464), and also happens if the un-awaited reminder delete loses the race with this cron. Re-check cancelled and booking status immediately before sgMail.send, and skip or delete those rows.

title: immediateDelete does not persist cancellation or allow retry
body: When immediateDelete is true, deleteScheduledEmailReminder POSTs a SendGrid batch cancel and returns without setting cancelled or deleting the WorkflowReminder. handleNewBooking.ts line 968 uses this for every reschedule, and workflows.tsx uses it when a workflow or step is deleted (then cascade-deletes the rows). If SendGrid rejects the cancel — including the 100 pending-cancellation cap this PR exists to avoid — the error is only logged, cancelled stays unset, and the cron will never retry, so the email still sends. On success the cancel status still sits in scheduled_sends until the original send time, so reschedules keep filling that same 100 cap. Callers also fire this inside forEach without await, so the HTTP call can still be in flight when the mutation returns and, on workflow delete, when the referenceId row is cascade-deleted. Reschedule should use the deferred cancelled flag (and only cancel immediately when the send is inside the cron gap); immediate cancel must be awaited and must leave a retryable record if SendGrid fails.

title: One SendGrid cancel error skips the rest of the batch
body: All cancellations share one try/catch around the for-loop. client.request is awaited per reminder, but the prisma deletes are only executed after the entire loop via Promise.all. The first non-2xx response — an unknown batch id, an already-cancelled batch, a null referenceId, or the 100-cancellation limit — jumps to the catch, so later reminders are not cancelled and none of the already-successful cancels are deleted from WorkflowReminder. Those rows stay cancelled=true and are processed first on the next run, which can block every subsequent reminder until their scheduledDate passes and the opening deleteMany drops them without a SendGrid cancel. Handle each reminder independently, delete the row only after that reminder's cancel succeeds, and continue after a failure.

title: Paid cancellations return before workflow reminders are cancelled
body: If bookingToDelete.paid is true, the handler refunds and returns "Booking successfully cancelled." at line 464. The reminder cleanup that sets cancelled or deletes WorkflowReminder rows is only reached later (lines 484-493). Paid cancellations therefore never mark or remove email/SMS reminders. Already-submitted SendGrid batches still send, and unscheduled reminders are picked up by scheduleEmailReminders. Move reminder cancellation above this return, on the same path as the unpaid cancel.

title: No tests for the cancellation fix that already failed once
body: This PR replaces the SendGrid cancel path after #6991 did not stop reminders for cancelled and rescheduled bookings, but it adds no tests. Nothing covers: cancelled=true is set instead of calling SendGrid on booking cancel, the cron cancels only due reminders and does not delete them first, a SendGrid error does not abort the rest of the batch, reschedule does not lose the reminder when the immediate cancel fails, and paid cancels do not skip cleanup. Those are the paths that still send email if wrong.

title: Cancellation of reminders is not awaited and failures are ignored
body: Booking cancellation starts deleteScheduledEmailReminder / deleteScheduledSMSReminder inside forEach and never awaits them, and those helpers swallow errors. The previous code awaited prisma.workflowReminder deletes in Promise.all; that persistence was removed. On a serverless freeze after the handler returns, or if the update throws, cancelled stays unset and unscheduled reminder rows are not deleted. The scheduleEmailReminders cron will then submit those emails to SendGrid, so cancelled bookings still receive workflow reminders. SMS cancels have the same gap and no retry cron.

title: Paid booking cancels return before any reminder cleanup
body: When bookingToDelete.paid is true the handler refunds, marks the booking REJECTED, and returns at this line. Reminder cancellation only runs later (around the workflowReminders loop). Every paid cancellation therefore leaves WorkflowReminder rows active, including already-submitted SendGrid/Twilio sends, so the bug this PR claims to fix still happens for all paid bookings.

title: immediateDelete cancels SendGrid but does not record or retry it
body: If immediateDelete is set, deleteScheduledEmailReminder POSTs a SendGrid batch cancel and returns without setting cancelled or deleting the WorkflowReminder row. Success still leaves a pending cancellation in scheduled_sends until the original send time, which is the 100-cap failure this PR describes. Failure is only console.logged, so the row stays scheduled with cancelled unset and the cron will never retry. Callers cannot tell that cancellation failed. The non-immediate path also only flips cancelled, even when scheduledDate is already inside the 15-minute cron interval, so a reminder due before the next cron tick is still delivered.

title: Reschedule immediately cancels SendGrid and does not wait or roll back
body: Reschedule passes immediateDelete=true for every email reminder, so each reschedule of an already-submitted reminder adds a pending SendGrid cancellation until the original sendAt (up to 72 hours). Enough reschedules reproduce the 100 pending-cancellation outage the PR is fixing. The forEach is not awaited and the surrounding try/catch cannot see promise rejections. If the SendGrid call fails, the old email still sends and is not marked cancelled for the cron. Cancellation also runs before eventManager.reschedule; a failed reschedule is not rolled back, so the original booking can lose its reminders.

title: Request-reschedule no longer awaits reminder removal
body: requestReschedule used to await Promise.all of workflowReminder deletes after best-effort provider cancels. That await was removed. The replacement deleteScheduledEmailReminder / deleteScheduledSMSReminder calls are fired from forEach and not awaited, and email cancellation only sets cancelled when it completes. If the handler returns or the update fails, reminders stay scheduled on SendGrid/Twilio and are not flagged for the cron, so request-reschedule still sends the old workflow reminders.

title: Workflow delete cancels SendGrid in the background then destroys retry state
body: Deleting a workflow calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., true) and deleteScheduledSMSReminder from forEach without awaiting, then immediately await workflow.deleteMany, which cascade-deletes the reminder rows, and returns. The SendGrid/Twilio calls are still in flight when the handler finishes, so a serverless runtime can abort them. immediateDelete does not set cancelled, and the rows are gone, so the cron cannot retry. A workflow with many scheduled emails can also submit more than 100 pending cancels at once and fail the same way as the original bug. The same pattern is used when a step is deleted (immediateDelete then workflowStep.delete around line 521). Disabling an event type (around line 376) also dropped the awaited reminder deletes and only fire-and-forgets the new helpers.

title: One SendGrid cancel failure stalls the whole cancellation queue
body: All cancelled reminders due within the next hour are cancelled in one try/catch. DB deletes are queued and only committed after every SendGrid POST succeeds. If any request throws (invalid batch id, already cancelled, or SendGrid refusing a send inside its cutoff), the catch logs and skips Promise.all, so earlier successful cancels are not deleted. The next run loads those already-cancelled batches first, they fail again, and reminders later in the list are never cancelled until the blocking row ages out. A single bad row can therefore keep other cancelled-booking emails sending for up to an hour. The same loop also submits every due cancellation at once, so more than 100 in that hour recreates the pending-cancellation cap.

title: Due reminders are deleted before SendGrid is cancelled
body: The cron first deleteMany's every EMAIL WorkflowReminder with scheduledDate <= now, including rows with cancelled=true, and only then looks up reminders to cancel on SendGrid. A cancelled reminder whose send time has just passed, or that the previous run failed to cancel, is removed from the database with no SendGrid cancel and no retry. If SendGrid has not yet dispatched that sendAt, the email still goes out for a cancelled or rescheduled booking.

title: Scheduler still emails reminders for cancelled bookings
body: The unscheduled-email query only filters method, scheduled=false, and scheduledDate within 72 hours. It does not exclude cancelled=true and does not check booking status (CANCELLED/REJECTED). Far-future reminders are not on SendGrid yet; they are only safe if the cancel path deleted the row. When that delete is skipped, races, or fails (paid cancel, unawaited delete, swallowed error), this cron creates a SendGrid batch and sets scheduled=true, so the reminder is sent anyway.

title: No tests for deferred cancel, immediateDelete, or the cron
body: This change replaces awaited reminder deletes with a cancelled flag, a deferred SendGrid cancel, and an immediateDelete mode, but adds no tests. There is no coverage for paid vs unpaid cancel, reschedule, workflow delete, a SendGrid error mid-batch, or a reminder already inside the cron window. Those paths are what caused reminders to keep sending, and they can regress without a failing test.

title: Vital reschedule does not wait for calendar or video deletion
body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) does not await its callbacks, and the try/catch around it cannot see rejections from them. getCalendar is now async, so calendar.deleteEvent is not even started until that import resolves, and neither deleteEvent nor deleteMeeting is awaited. Reschedule then sends the reschedule email and returns true while the external calendar event and video meeting may still exist. On serverless, the handler can be frozen after the response, so the cleanup often never runs and the old slot stays busy. Failures become unhandled promise rejections. Replace this with await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...)) and await both deleteEvent and deleteMeeting inside the mapper.

title: WipeMyCal reschedule does not wait for calendar or video deletion
body: The same forEach(async) pattern was introduced here when getCalendar became async. Array.forEach ignores the promises returned by async callbacks, so the try/catch never observes getCalendar, deleteEvent, or deleteMeeting failures, and the function sends the reschedule email and returns true without waiting for those calls. Because the first await is now the dynamic app import, deletion is no longer even initiated before the handler continues. Serverless runtimes can freeze after the response and drop that work, leaving the cancelled event on the user's calendar and the slot blocked. Await Promise.all over a map, and await deleteEvent and deleteMeeting inside it.

title: requestReschedule returns before calendar and video cleanup
body: requestReschedule now uses bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) so it can await getCalendar, but forEach does not wait for those promises. The mutation marks the booking CANCELLED, sends the reschedule email, fires BOOKING_CANCELLED webhooks, and resolves while calendar.deleteEvent and deleteMeeting may not have started. Previously getCalendar was synchronous, so deleteEvent was at least invoked before the handler continued. Now the first await yields before any provider call, and a serverless isolate can exit before the dynamic import finishes. Rejected imports or delete failures are unhandled rejections with no surrounding try/catch. Collect the work with await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...)) and await both deleteEvent and deleteMeeting before sending email or returning.

title: Recurring cancel races calendar deletion against Promise.all
body: When cancelling all remaining instances of a recurring event, credentials are still walked with forEach(async), and this change added await getCalendar inside that callback before deleteEvent. forEach does not wait, and apiDeletes.push only happens after both awaits, so the later await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) (around line 652) usually runs while apiDeletes still lacks these deletions — often before deleteEvent has been called at all. The non-recurring else branch just below was correctly rewritten to a for-loop that awaits getCalendar and pushes the delete promise before continuing; the recurring branch was not. The handler can therefore return success while series events remain on the external calendar and those times stay busy. Errors in the callback are unhandled rejections. Await Promise.all on the credential list (and on each deleteEvent) instead of forEach, and push the promises before awaiting them if they must be included in apiDeletes.

title: Reschedule calendar/video cleanup is not awaited
body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) starts async work and immediately returns. getCalendar is now async (it awaits a dynamic import) and deleteMeeting is async, but nothing awaits the forEach callbacks, and the values they return (including calendar.deleteEvent) are discarded. The try/catch around forEach cannot see rejections from those callbacks. Reschedule then sends the reschedule email and returns true while deletions may not have started. On a serverless runtime the process can freeze after the handler returns, so the old calendar event and video meeting are left in place after the booking is already marked CANCELLED, and failures surface only as unhandled rejections.

title: WipeMyCal reschedule cleanup is not awaited
body: Same control-flow bug as the Vital reschedule handler: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) does not wait for getCalendar, calendar.deleteEvent, or deleteMeeting. Because getCalendar now awaits a dynamic app import before deleteEvent is even called, the deletion often has not started when this function sends the reschedule email and returns true. The surrounding try/catch does not catch async failures. Result: the booking is cancelled in the database while the external calendar event and video meeting can remain, blocking the slot and leaving a stale invite.

title: requestReschedule returns before integrations are deleted
body: requestReschedule marks the booking CANCELLED, then uses bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) to await getCalendar and call deleteEvent/deleteMeeting. forEach does not await those promises, and the mutation continues straight into sendRequestRescheduleEmail and the BOOKING_CANCELLED webhooks, then resolves. Callers therefore observe success before calendar and video teardown has run. With getCalendar and deleteMeeting now async, the external API calls are no longer even initiated synchronously, so a short-lived server handler can exit first and leave the original event on the calendar and the video meeting alive.

title: Cancelling remaining recurring events drops calendar deletes
body: When all remaining recurring instances are cancelled and a credentialId is present, calendar deletion is done with credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(await calendar.deleteEvent(...)) }). The async callbacks are never joined. Later, await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) runs while apiDeletes is still empty, because pushes happen only after getCalendar and deleteEvent resolve inside the detached callbacks. Those pushes also store settled results, not in-flight promises, so they cannot be tracked. Recurring bookings are marked CANCELLED and cancellation email is sent, but the external calendar events for those instances are not reliably deleted; import or API errors become unhandled rejections. The non-recurring branch just below was correctly rewritten to for...of and pushes the delete promise before awaiting; this branch needs the same treatment.

title: Reschedule cleanup uses async forEach and is not awaited
body: Making getCalendar async was handled by marking the forEach callback async and awaiting inside it. Array.forEach never waits for async callbacks, and the surrounding try/catch only covers the synchronous call, so getCalendar rejections and deleteEvent/deleteMeeting failures become unhandled rejections instead of being logged. The handler then sends the reschedule email and returns true while calendar deletes and video-meeting deletes are still in flight (or not started). On a serverless runtime that freezes after the response, those external events are often left behind after the booking is already marked CANCELLED.

title: WipeMyCal reschedule drops calendar and video deletes
body: The callback passed to bookingRefsFiltered.forEach was changed to async so it can await getCalendar, but forEach does not await that promise and the try/catch around it cannot see later rejections. calendar.deleteEvent and deleteMeeting are therefore fire-and-forget. The function continues to sendRequestRescheduleEmail and returns true without those calls finishing, so a cancelled booking can keep its old calendar event and video meeting, and import or API errors are unhandled.

title: requestReschedule does not wait for integration teardown
body: requestReschedule now awaits getCalendar inside bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...). forEach ignores the promises, nothing collects them, and there is no try/catch. The mutation then sends the reschedule email and BOOKING_CANCELLED webhooks and resolves successfully while calendar.deleteEvent and deleteMeeting may still be running or may never run if the process is frozen after the response. Organizers can be left with a cancelled booking whose external calendar event and video meeting were not removed, and a failed dynamic import surfaces as an unhandled rejection rather than a failed mutation.

title: Recurring cancel never joins calendar deletions
body: The all-remaining-bookings branch still uses forEach(async) and now awaits getCalendar before deleteEvent. That callback is not collected or awaited, and it pushes the resolved deleteEvent result onto apiDeletes only after the await. The later await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) evaluates concat synchronously, before those callbacks resume, so the snapshot does not include the recurring deletes. The non-recurring branch just below was correctly rewritten to for...of, await getCalendar, and push the delete promise. Recurring cancellations can therefore return after marking bookings CANCELLED without deleting each occurrence from the connected calendars, and getCalendar failures are unhandled rejections.

title: Video adapter import sits outside the Cal Video fallback
body: createMeeting awaits getVideoAdapters before the try block that falls back to createMeetingWithCalVideo and sends the broken-integration email. getVideoAdapters now awaits a dynamic import(), so a rejected app module throws out of createMeeting entirely. Previously that lookup could not fail at request time. A single broken or missing video integration then fails booking creation instead of falling back to Cal Video. The same uncovered await is at updateMeeting (line 111) and deleteMeeting (line 144): an import rejection fails reschedule or cancel cleanup instead of being handled per credential.

title: One app import failure fails every calendar lookup
body: getCalendar awaits appStore[type] with no try/catch. A rejected dynamic import now rejects the returned promise, whereas the old synchronous registry lookup only returned null for an unimplemented service. getCachedResults does await Promise.all on every calendar credential's getCalendar call, so one bad integration rejects the whole availability fetch and the booking page cannot compute busy times from the other calendars. createEvent and updateEvent likewise await getCalendar outside their create/update catch blocks, so an import failure aborts EventManager instead of recording a failed result for that credential only.

title: Working-hours recheck rejects valid slots whenever a host has more than one window
body: checkIfIsAvailable now runs for every isFixed host, and personal events, collective events, and round-robin fixed hosts are all marked isFixed. The new working-hours test uses Array.find and returns unavailable if the slot falls outside any single window whose days include the slot's UTC weekday. A host with a lunch break, or a single local range that getWorkingHours splits across UTC midnight into two entries on the same day, therefore fails the check for every slot: a 10:00 slot inside 09:00–12:00 is still outside 13:00–17:00, so find matches and the slot is dropped. The booking page then shows no times. The condition is also inverted for days off: if no window lists that weekday, find matches nothing and the host is treated as free, so a fixed host who does not work that day is not actually blocked. The end minute is copied from slot start (hour*60+minute of slotStartTime, not slot end), so a slot that starts inside a window but whose event length runs past endTime is accepted. Net effect is both false unavailability for ordinary split schedules and false availability outside hours.

title: Date-override hit skips busy times and mishandles multiple or empty overrides
body: On a day that has a date override, if the slot is considered inside an override, checkIfIsAvailable sets dateOverrideExist and returns true immediately, before the busy/booking loop. A fixed host (including every personal or collective host) who blocked 15:00 with a calendar event or Cal booking, but has a date override covering that time, is reported free, so the slot stays bookable and can double-book. The same find() treats "outside this one override" as a hard unavailable: two override windows on the same day reject a slot that sits in only one of them, because the other window's callback returns true. Zero-length overrides (the unavailable-day convention, start equal to end) are detected with dayjs object ===, which is never true for two instances, so that branch never runs. Day matching compares dayjs(date.start).add(offset).format (process-local mode) to slotStartTime.format (UTC mode), so when the server TZ is not UTC the override is attached to the wrong calendar day or ignored. A slot that starts before the override and ends inside it is not treated as outside, so it takes the early available return as well.

title: Override timezone shift uses Date.toString and drops times that cross midnight
body: Active date overrides are converted with dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone). Date.toString() is the process-local representation (and often includes a parenthetical zone name), so the parsed instant used for utcOffset is wrong or Invalid Date off UTC, and utcOffset becomes NaN. timeZone is optional on TimeRange; if it is missing, .tz(undefined) throws RangeError and getSlots fails for the whole day instead of falling back. The shifted clock time is then reduced with .hour() and .minute() only. Adding inviteeOffset-organizerOffset across midnight wraps to 0–24h on the unadjusted day (the activeOverrides filter still keys off the raw UTC start). When the wrapped end is less than the wrapped start, buildSlots drops the range (start >= end), so the override disappears. Attendees in a distant timezone see the override on the wrong date or not at all — the bug this change is meant to fix.

title: No test covers fixed-host overrides or the new availability recheck
body: The only new test re-queries a personal event date override in Asia/Dhaka and expects the same UTC instants as the IST case. It never builds a round-robin event with a fixed host, which is the main fix described in the PR, and it never hits checkIfIsAvailable's date-override or working-hours branches. Split working hours, an override day that also has a booking, an unavailable (start==end) override, and a timezone shift that crosses midnight are all untested, so the regressions above would merge green.

title: Date override match skips busy-time checks
body: When checkIfIsAvailable finds a same-day date override that overlaps the slot, it sets dateOverrideExist and returns true immediately. That return happens before the busy.every() calendar/booking conflict check. The function is used for every fixed host (all users on personal and collective events, and fixed hosts on round-robin) and for loose round-robin hosts. On any day a host has a covering date override, existing bookings and calendar busy times are ignored, so the slot stays bookable and the host can be double-booked.

title: Working-hours recheck rejects any split schedule
body: The new working-hours gate uses Array.find and treats a window as a hit when the slot is outside that window. A host with two windows on the same weekday (for example 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00) therefore fails the check for every slot, because the slot is always outside at least one window, and checkIfIsAvailable returns false. end is assigned the same minutes as start, so the event length is never compared to workingHour.endTime either. This runs for every isFixed user, which includes ordinary personal events, so split-shift availability disappears from the booking page. The inverse is also wrong: if no window lists that weekday, find returns undefined and the slot is not rejected, so a fixed host with no hours that day is still treated as free.

title: Override containment check is wrong for blocks and multiple ranges
body: The all-day block branch compares two dayjs objects with ===, which is reference equality and never succeeds, so a zero-length override (start equal to end) is not treated as blocking the day. A slot that overlaps that instant falls through and is marked available. Separately, dateOverrides.find returns true as soon as any same-day range does not cover the slot, so a second range that does cover it is ignored and the slot is rejected. A slot is also treated as inside a range on any overlap: slot start is not required to be at or after the override start, and slot end is not required to be at or before the override end, so a meeting that only partly fits the override is still offered.

title: Override day match formats local time against UTC
body: The same-day test compares dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset).format('YYYY MM DD') with slotStartTime.format('YYYY MM DD'). slotStartTime was created with .utc(), so its format is UTC, but the override side is a local-mode dayjs and formats in the process timezone. On any host whose local timezone is not UTC, the calendar day can differ around midnight, the override is not recognized, and the fixed-host date-override filter either does not apply or applies on the wrong day.

title: Timezone-adjusted overrides lose the day and can invert
body: Override start/end are shifted by inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset and then reduced with .hour() and .minute(), which wrap to 0–23 and drop any day the shift crossed. A UTC 22:00–23:30 override viewed in Asia/Kolkata becomes 03:30–05:00 on the invitee's current day instead of the next day. A short early override viewed behind UTC can wrap the end to 00:00 while the start stays late, so startTime >= endTime. buildSlots then skips that range (start >= end), but the code has already removed that user's normal working hours for the day, so the override day shows the wrong slots or none. This is the common case the timezone fix is meant to handle.

title: Override minutes are shifted again by today's DST delta
body: The new override math already converts wall-clock times using utcOffset at override.start for both the organizer zone and the invitee zone, so the resulting minutes are invitee-local on that date. Those minutes are then passed through buildSlots, whose getTime adds organizerDSTDiff - inviteeDSTDiff (today's offset minus the target day's offset). That correction exists for weekly hours, which were shifted with today's offset, not for these overrides. When either timezone is in a different DST period today than on the booked day, every override slot moves by that extra delta, typically 60 minutes, so the bookable times do not match the saved override.

title: New tests miss fixed-host overrides and real timezone shifts
body: The only new assertion re-queries the same personal-event date override in Asia/Dhaka and expects the same UTC instants as Asia/Kolkata. That does not cover the PR's main fix (round-robin slot must be hidden when a fixed host's date override makes them unavailable, including when the round-robin host is free). A +30 minute shift also never crosses midnight or a DST boundary, so the hour-wrap and DST bugs in getSlots, and the busy-time skip in checkIfIsAvailable, are not exercised.

title: In-override slots skip busy checks and can double-book
body: checkIfIsAvailable now returns true as soon as a date override exists for that calendar day and the slot is not strictly outside it. That return happens before the busy-interval scan, so calendar conflicts and existing Cal bookings are ignored for every fixed host (personal events, collective hosts, and round-robin fixed hosts all go through this path). A host who sets a date override and already has a meeting inside that window will still be offered those slots, and the booking can be confirmed on top of the conflict. Partial overlaps are treated as inside as well: a slot that starts before the override and ends during it is not rejected, so the meeting can begin outside the override hours.

title: Multiple override ranges on one day reject every slot
body: The date-override filter uses Array.find and treats a true callback as "this slot is not bookable". Each range returns true when the slot merely falls outside that one range. On a day with two ranges (for example 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-17:00), a slot inside the first range is outside the second, so find succeeds and checkIfIsAvailable returns false. Every slot is outside at least one range, so a split date override blocks the entire day instead of opening those windows. The start===end all-day-block branch just above never runs either: it compares two dayjs instances with ===, which is always false, so a zero-length override is not handled as a full-day block.

title: Working-hours fallback rejects valid split shifts and ignores the slot end
body: When no date override matches, availability is decided by workingHours.find: any same-day window whose range does not contain the slot makes the callback return true and the slot is rejected. A host with a lunch break (two windows on the same weekday) therefore loses every slot, including ones that sit fully inside the other window. The end minute is copied from slotStartTime rather than the slot end, so a slot that starts inside hours but runs past workingHour.endTime is treated as inside. Days with no working-hour entry never match, so they are treated as free; a fixed host who does not work that weekday is not excluded. For round-robin this filter is what is supposed to keep fixed hosts from being booked outside their own hours, and it does the opposite for split schedules.

title: Override timezone shift wraps at midnight and lands on the wrong day
body: Date-override start and end are shifted by inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset and then reduced to hour and minute only. Those values are minutes within 0-1439, so a shift that crosses midnight is applied to the invitee day already selected from the unadjusted UTC timestamp. An evening override viewed from a timezone ahead shows up as early-morning slots on the previous day; a morning override viewed from a timezone behind can produce endTime < startTime. buildSlots drops ranges with start >= end, and the caller has already removed that user's normal working hours for the day, so the override disappears and the host has no slots. The new test only compares +5:30 and +6:00, a 30-minute gap that never crosses midnight, so it does not catch this. Attendees several hours from the organizer still see the override at the wrong time, which is the bug this change is meant to fix.

title: Override day match compares server-local date to UTC
body: Whether an override applies is decided by formatting dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset) (local mode, so the server timezone) as YYYY MM DD and comparing it to slotStartTime, which was forced to UTC. isBefore/isAfter later compare absolute instants, but they only run after this date check. On any host whose TZ is not UTC, an override near midnight is attached to the wrong day or skipped entirely, and the fixed host's override is not enforced. Slot generation then falls through to weekly hours.

title: No test for fixed-host overrides on round-robin
body: The PR's stated fix is that a round-robin event must not offer slots when a fixed host's date override makes them unavailable, including across timezones. The only new assertion re-queries a single-user event in Asia/Dhaka and expects the same UTC instants as Asia/Kolkata. It never builds a ROUND_ROBIN event, never sets hosts[].isFixed, and never places a booking or calendar busy block inside an override. The double-book path, split override ranges, and fixed-host weekly hours can all regress without failing CI.

title: Migration crashes unless embed_category matches a category name
body: The migration always runs `execute(... embed_category ...)[0]['id']`. Discourse only persists site settings that were overridden, and the join is `site_settings.value = categories.name`. On a normal install embed_category is absent or blank, the result set is empty, and `[0]` is nil, so the migration raises NoMethodError. PostgreSQL rolls the transaction back, so the upgrade cannot complete and embedding cannot be moved off the old setting.

title: Existing allow-list is deleted and never copied
body: The copy of `embeddable_hosts` is gated on `embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0` after a SELECT. PG::Result#cmd_tuples is 0 for SELECT (row count is `ntuples`). The INSERT loop never runs, then the migration deletes the `embeddable_hosts` and `embed_category` site settings. Any site that gets past the category lookup loses its allow-list and embedding starts rejecting every referer.

title: Migrated hosts are interpolated raw and not normalized
body: Hosts are inserted with `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` and no normalization. A quote in a host aborts the migration (and is SQL injection if that setting was ever attacker-influenced). Protocol, path, and CR from the old newline list are stored as-is. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `URI#host` (e.g. `eviltrout.com`) to the stored string, so values the old setting accepted (`http://eviltrout.com`, `https://example.com/1234`) will not match after upgrade.

title: Host allow-list lookup ignores case and port
body: Lookup is `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` using `URI#host` unchanged. The column side is lowercased but the bind value is not, so a referer host `Example.com` does not match a saved `example.com` under PostgreSQL. The format validator explicitly allows `:port`, and `before_validation` keeps it, but `URI#host` never includes the port, so a saved host `example.com:3000` never matches `http://example.com:3000/...`. Those referers are rejected by `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` and `TopicRetriever`.

title: Import passes a category id through the name option
body: PostCreator is still called with `category:`, which previously received `SiteSetting.embed_category`, a category name (the migration joins that setting to `categories.name`). The new code passes `eh.try(:category_id)`, an integer. Nothing in this PR teaches PostCreator to treat that option as an id, so embedded topic creation will either raise or land in the uncategorized category instead of the host's chosen category. The new expectation in topic_embed_spec does not change PostCreator.

title: Nil host crashes before validation
body: `before_validation` calls `self.host.sub!` twice with no presence check. Create/update with a missing or null `embeddable_host[host]` (and any other save of a blank host) raises NoMethodError instead of a validation error, so the admin API returns 500 rather than the model's format error.

title: Update and destroy 500 when the id is missing
body: `update` and `destroy` load with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and immediately call `save_host(host)` / `host.destroy` without a nil check. An unknown id raises NoMethodError and returns 500 instead of 404. `save_host` also assumes `params[:embeddable_host]` is present, so a malformed body 500s the same way.

title: Hosts are not unique, so category assignment is arbitrary
body: There is no uniqueness validation and the migration adds no unique index on `host`. `record_for_host` uses `.first` with no order. Two rows for the same host (easy via the admin API, or a re-run of a fixed migration) make embed imports pick an arbitrary category, so "post to category" is not stable.

title: Plural id hydration throws when the ids value is null
body: The new `*_ids` branch always calls `obj[k].map(...)` and only then does `hydrated || []`. A rest payload with a null or missing array for any `*_ids` key (not just embeddable hosts) throws TypeError inside `_hydrate` and fails the whole `find`/`findAll`. The `|| []` never runs for null, and the ids key is deleted only after the map.

title: New embed admin API and migration are untested
body: The new controller specs only assert the class subclasses AdminController. They never hit create, update, destroy, a missing id, a blank host, or an unknown category. There is also no migration spec, so the empty `embed_category` crash, the `cmd_tuples` data loss, and un-normalized host inserts are not caught. `topic_spec`'s "embeddable_host is blank" example no longer stubs a host or an embed, so it does not lock the new `expandable_first_post?` behavior either.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category is unset
body: The migration does `execute(...)[0]['id']` on the embed_category name join, and the same pattern again for uncategorized_category_id. Discourse only writes site_settings rows when a setting is overridden, so a typical site has no embed_category row and this raises NoMethodError on nil before any fallback. A case mismatch or a setting that is not exactly a category name fails the same way. The upgrade cannot finish, so the new embeddable_hosts table is never created and embedding stays broken.

title: Migrated hosts are raw SQL and not normalized
body: Existing allowlist entries are inserted with string interpolation (`VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`) and are not run through EmbeddableHost normalization. A host containing a quote aborts the migration (or injects SQL). Values that the old setting accepted, such as `http://example.com`, `example.com/path`, or a trailing `\r`, are stored verbatim. Lookups compare URI#host (`example.com`) to that stored string, so previously working embeds stop matching, and the migration then deletes the embeddable_hosts and embed_category settings so there is no source left to repair from. The `change` method's raw `execute` calls are also not reversible.

title: Host allowlist match is case-sensitive on the input
body: record_for_host queries `lower(host) = ?` but binds `uri.host` without downcasing, and before_validation never downcases the saved host. Ruby's URI preserves case, so `lower('Example.com') = 'Example.com'` is false. A mixed-case saved host never matches, and a mixed-case Referer or embed URL never matches a lowercase row, so EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? and per-host category lookup fail closed and comments/import are rejected.

title: Hosts with ports can be saved but never match
body: The format validator explicitly allows `:port`, and before_validation only strips the scheme and path, so `example.com:8080` is stored. record_for_host then uses `uri.host`, which drops the port, and compares that to the stored value. A referer of `http://example.com:8080/...` therefore never matches the row the admin just saved, so that host is never treated as embeddable and never supplies a category.

title: Blank host raises in before_validation
body: before_validation calls `self.host.sub!` with no nil guard and there is no presence validation. Creating or updating with a missing host (the controller assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` straight through) raises NoMethodError instead of a validation error, so the admin request 500s rather than returning the JSON error the UI expects.

title: Update and destroy 500 when the id is missing
body: update and destroy load the row with `where(id:).first` and immediately call save_host or destroy. A stale or unknown id yields nil, so `host.host = ...` or `host.destroy` raises NoMethodError and the admin API returns 500 instead of 404. The new controller specs only assert the class ancestry, so this path is untested.

title: Duplicate hosts are allowed and category lookup is ambiguous
body: There is no uniqueness validation and the migration creates no unique index on host. Two rows for the same host (double-submit, or duplicate lines in the old setting) both save. record_for_host uses an unordered `.first`, so topic import can attach either category nondeterministically, which defeats the per-host category feature.

title: New host CRUD and migration behavior are untested
body: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController and Admin::EmbeddingController specs only check that the class subclasses AdminController. Nothing covers create, update, destroy, missing ids, blank host, category assignment, or the data migration. The expandable_first_post? example named "is false if embeddable_host is blank" also no longer sets embed_truncate or stubs an embed, so it passes for unrelated reasons and does not lock the new contract.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category is unset or unmatched
body: The data migration reads the old embed_category setting with execute(...)[0]['id'] and, only if that id is 0, does the same for uncategorized_category_id. Site settings at their default are often not stored, and embed_category was a free-text category name, so the join on categories.name commonly returns no row. [0] is then nil and nil['id'] raises NoMethodError before the category_id == 0 fallback. The same crash happens on the uncategorized lookup if that row is missing. Because this runs in the up migration that also deletes those settings, a typical upgrade aborts and never creates embeddable_hosts, while the new code no longer reads SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts. Handle an empty result and fall back to a real category id before inserting rows.

title: Migrated hosts are inserted raw and unquoted
body: Existing embeddable_hosts values are inserted with execute "INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)", bypassing EmbeddableHost's before_validation normalizer. The previous allow-list accepted http:// and https:// prefixes and paths (the old matcher used URI#host), but record_for_host compares only URI#host to the stored string. After upgrade, a saved value such as http://discourse.org or https://example.com/1234 will not match a referer host of discourse.org or example.com, so previously working embeds start returning invalid referer. A host containing a single quote also breaks the SQL or injects statements. Normalize (strip scheme, path, whitespace, and downcase) and insert with bound parameters. Windows newlines left by split("\n") have the same mismatch.

title: Allow-list lookup drops ports and mishandles case
body: record_for_host sets host = uri.host and queries lower(host) = ? with that value unchanged. uri.host never includes the port, but the format validator and before_validation keep an optional :port on the stored host, so an entry saved as example.com:8080 never matches a referer of http://example.com:8080/... and host_allowed? stays false. The lower() call is also only applied to the column: a referer whose host has any capital letter (URI preserves case, so Example.com) compares lower(stored) = 'Example.com', which is never true, so the allow-list rejects it. Downcase the lookup value and compare host and port the same way they are stored.

title: Host regex rejects hosts the old setting allowed
body: validates_format_of requires a dotted name ending in a letter TLD of 2 to 5 characters. The removed embeddable_hosts setting was a free-form host list. This regex rejects IPv4/IPv6, localhost, and any gTLD longer than 5 letters (.museum, .coffee, .international, and similar). Admins cannot save those hosts, and re-saving a migrated row fails validation, so those sites can no longer be allow-listed even though embedding used to work.

title: Nil host crashes before validation
body: before_validation calls self.host.sub! without checking host. Create/update with a missing or null embeddable_host[host] (the controller assigns params directly) raises NoMethodError instead of a validation error, so the admin API returns 500 rather than 422. Guard nil/blank host and let validates_format_of fail the save.

title: Update and destroy 500 when the host id is missing
body: update loads EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and passes it to save_host, which immediately writes host.host. destroy calls host.destroy on the same lookup. A stale or unknown id yields nil, so both actions raise NoMethodError instead of a 404. save_host also assumes params[:embeddable_host] is present; a body without that key raises before any error JSON is rendered.

title: Any category_id is stored with no existence check
body: save_host assigns category_id from params and only substitutes uncategorized when the value is blank. There is no Category.exists? check, no model validation, and the migration adds no foreign key. A nonexistent id is saved. TopicEmbed.import then passes that id into PostCreator, so new embedded topics are created with a dangling category_id. Deleting a category later leaves the same dangling pointer because nothing cascades.

title: Hosts are not unique, so category lookup is arbitrary
body: Nothing validates uniqueness of host, and the new table has no unique index (case-insensitive or otherwise). The admin API and the migration can store duplicate hosts, including Example.com and example.com. record_for_host uses an unordered .first, so two rows for the same host with different categories make the imported topic category nondeterministic. Add a case-insensitive unique index and a matching validation.

title: Category and embeddable-host fabricators are swapped
body: category_fabricator.rb now only defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host), and the category, diff_category, happy_category, and private_category fabricators were moved into spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb. Specs still pass only because every fabricator file is auto-loaded. Anything that loads category_fabricator.rb by path, or a cleanup that deletes the category definitions from the embeddable-host file, will break Fabricate(:category) and Fabricate(:private_category) across the suite. Put each fabricator back in the file that matches its name.

title: New host API and migration have no behavioral tests
body: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController and Admin::EmbeddingController specs only assert the class inherits AdminController. Nothing exercises create, update, destroy, a missing id, a blank category_id, or an invalid host, and there is no migration spec for missing embed_category / protocol-prefixed hosts. Those are the paths that 500 or drop existing allow-list entries, so the current suite will stay green if they are broken.

title: Downsize reads and writes the same tempfile
body: OptimizedImage.downsize is called with tempfile.path as both source and destination. convert (and gifsicle when animation is enabled) opens the output for writing before the input is fully read, and ImageMagick truncates that path immediately. This tempfile is the only copy of the upload, so a large image can become empty or partial before Upload.create_for. The loop also ignores downsize's false return, so a failed conversion is retried against the already truncated file and then handed to create_for. Write to a separate tempfile and replace the original only after a successful non-empty result.

title: Second downsize definition overwrites the width/height API
body: Ruby does not overload by arity, so downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) on line 149 replaces downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) on line 145. The width/height wrapper never exists at runtime. Callers that still use the previous signature — numeric max width and max height, which this pull request does not update anywhere else — now bind the height integer to opts. optimize then evaluates opts[:allow_animation] and raises NoMethodError instead of building a widthxheight geometry, so those calls 500.

title: Client size check hardcoded to 10MB for every type
body: validateUploadedFile used to enforce Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so images and attachments each honored their admin setting. It now always uses 10 * 1024. Attachments larger than 10MB are rejected even when max_attachment_size_kb allows them, and attachments between the real attachment limit and 10MB pass the client and fail only on the server. Images are capped at 10MB regardless of max_image_size_kb, so a site that allows larger images cannot upload them from the browser. The 413 handler on line 246 uses the same hardcode, so the dialog always claims the limit is 10240 KB even when the web server or site setting differs.

title: 80% geometry breaks animation and does not enforce the size limit
body: The new call passes "80%" and allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails.
