When that setting is false, downsize_instructions runs convert with a [0] frame selector, so a large animated GIF or multi-page image is permanently flattened to the first frame in the stored original; that setting is about thumbnails, not the upload. When it is true, gifsicle --resize-fit is given "80%", but it requires a pixel size such as 100x100, so it exits non-zero. The failure is ignored, and after five attempts the still-oversized file is passed to Upload.create_for anyway. The loop also does not fail the upload if the file is still larger than SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb after five 80% passes, so the comment's "reduced to allowed size" guarantee is not enforced for JPEGs or PNGs either.

title: API URL downloads capped at a hardcoded 10MB for all types
body: FileHelper.download's limit changed from SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes to 10.megabytes for every upload type, not only images that will be downsized. Non-image API URL uploads are therefore cut off at 10MB even when max_attachment_size_kb is higher, and they are no longer tied to the attachment setting at all. Image URL uploads also cannot exceed 10MB when max_image_size_kb is configured above that, so the admin setting and the new downscale path disagree.

title: No input size ceiling before repeated ImageMagick runs
body: The browser and the URL-download path are capped at 10MB, but the multipart file branch never checks an upper bound before the downsize loop. The client check is bypassable: any logged-in user can POST a huge image and force up to five ImageMagick convert runs plus ImageOptim inside Scheduler::Defer. A decompression bomb or a multi-hundred-megabyte image is fully decoded on each attempt, which is a CPU and memory exhaustion path. Reject or cap the input before calling downsize, and stop if an attempt does not shrink the file.

title: No tests for downsizing or the new size caps
body: This change alters client limits, URL download limits, and runs a five-iteration ImageMagick downsize before Upload.create_for, but no tests were added. Failures such as in-place conversion, the overwritten downsize signature, attachment versus image limits, a file that stays over max_image_size_kb, and animated GIF handling would not be caught before merge.

title: In-place downsize uses the open tempfile path and ignores failure
body: OptimizedImage.downsize is called with the same path for input and output (tempfile.path, tempfile.path). ImageMagick convert cannot safely read and write the same file: it typically truncates the output before the input is fully read, producing an empty or corrupt image, or it replaces the inode while the open Tempfile fd still refers to the old file. Upload.create_for is then given that same tempfile and tempfile.size, so it can store the truncated/stale bytes rather than the resized image. The path also has no image extension (Rack/URL tempfiles are extensionless), so convert often cannot pick an output format, and the GIF branch never runs because optimize only treats a path matching /\.GIF$/i as animated. "80%" is also not a valid gifsicle --resize-fit size, so animated GIFs fail even when the extension is present. The return value is ignored and the loop does not reject the upload if the file is still larger than SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb after five attempts, so a failed or insufficient shrink still proceeds to Upload.create_for.

title: Second downsize definition silently replaces the width/height API
body: Ruby keeps only the last def self.downsize. The new 3-argument form at line 149 replaces the width/height form at line 145, so that method is dead. Existing callers of OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) now bind max_height to opts. optimize then evaluates opts[:allow_animation] on an Integer and raises NoMethodError, and any resize geometry built from the numeric width is lost. Call sites that still pass width and height (thumbnail/downsize code outside this diff) will break at runtime.

title: Client upload cap ignores per-type site settings
body: validateUploadedFile used to enforce Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so images and attachments honored separate admin limits. It now always uses 10*1024 KB. Attachments larger than 10MB are rejected even when max_attachment_size_kb is higher, and images cannot exceed 10MB even when max_image_size_kb is higher (or 0, which this codebase treats as "do not enforce"). The 413 handler at line 246 has the same hardcode, so the file_too_large dialog reports 10240 KB regardless of the limit that actually rejected the upload.

title: Multipart uploads are resized with no server-side size cap
body: URL fetches were changed to a fixed 10.megabytes limit, but the new downsize loop on the multipart path has no upper bound. It runs ImageMagick (and ImageOptim inside convert_with) up to five times on any image larger than max_image_size_kb. The 10MB check exists only in client JS, which a direct POST or API upload can skip. A large or decompression-bomb image therefore reaches convert before Upload.create_for can reject it, tying up the deferred upload worker and memory.

title: No test covers automatic downsize-on-upload
body: The new shrink-before-create path has no test. A regression test would need an image over max_image_size_kb (including a GIF and an extensionless uploaded tempfile), assert the stored file is a valid image under the limit with updated filesize/dimensions, and assert that a failed or still-too-large downsize is rejected instead of saved. Without that, the in-place convert failure and the overridden downsize signature will not be caught.

title: In-place downsize can corrupt the upload and the result is ignored
body: The new loop calls OptimizedImage.downsize with the same path for input and output (tempfile.path to tempfile.path) and ignores the boolean it returns. ImageMagick convert cannot safely read and write one file: it often truncates the destination before the source is fully read, so a failed or partial convert destroys the upload. The open Tempfile still refers to the original inode, so after convert replaces the path, tempfile.size and whatever Upload.create_for reads from the handle can stay on the old bytes or sit past the new EOF. The loop then either keeps shrinking a stale size or stores a corrupt/empty/original image. If convert or ImageOptim fails, execution still falls through to Upload.create_for. Five 80% passes also only reach about a third of the linear dimensions, so a file can remain over SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb and still be uploaded.

title: Oversized GIFs lose animation and SVGs are sent through convert
body: Auto-downsize always goes through OptimizedImage.downsize, whose non-animated instructions run convert with [0] (first frame only). The animated/gifsicle path is selected only when the filesystem path matches /\.GIF$/i. Rack and FileHelper temp paths do not keep the original filename extension, and this call never copies the bytes to a path ending in .gif, so allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails never takes effect. Every oversized GIF is flattened to one frame and that result is what gets stored as the original upload, even when animated thumbnails are allowed. The same branch also runs for any FileHelper.is_image? filename, including SVG, unlike OptimizedImage.create_for which copies SVGs instead of converting them. convert will fail or rasterize the SVG and that output is then saved under the original .svg name.

title: Second downsize definition replaces the width/height method
body: Ruby does not overload methods. The new downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts) at this line replaces the downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) defined just above, so that width/height version never runs. Existing callers that pass numeric max width and height (the previous public signature, which this file still tries to keep) will bind the width to dimensions and the height to opts. optimize then evaluates opts[:allow_animation] and raises NoMethodError, or, if a hash is passed in the height slot, builds a geometry of just the width (for example "1024") instead of "1024x768". Thumbnail generation that still uses the old arity breaks. self.optimize's signature changed the same way (dimensions string instead of width, height), so any external optimize caller is broken too.

title: Client upload limit is hardcoded and ignores per-type site settings
body: validateUploadedFile used to enforce Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so images and attachments had independent admin limits. It now always rejects above 10 * 1024 KB and no longer uses type. Attachments larger than max_attachment_size_kb but under 10MB are sent and then fail (or are stored, if the server trusts the client). Images the admin allowed above 10MB are blocked in the composer even though they would not need downsizing. The 413 handler at line 246 has the same hardcode, so a proxy rejection is reported as a 10MB limit even when nginx or max_image_size_kb is different. uploads_controller.rb also downloads API URLs with a fixed 10.megabytes cap, so raising max_image_size_kb above 10MB cannot be honored on that path either.

title: Unsubscribe GET is not idempotent and does not stop topic emails
body: GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe changes notification_level on every request: tracking/watching (above regular) is set to regular, and regular or muted is set to muted. A watching user — the usual case for topic notification mail, including category auto-watch — is only dropped to regular, so reply, mention, quote, and category-watch emails continue, despite the email and page copy saying notifications for that topic will stop. Because the same transition runs again on refresh, prefetch, or a second click, that user is then muted. The action is also not safe to retry: there is no confirmation step and no check that the level was already updated.

title: Missing TopicUser crashes unsubscribe and the change is not recorded
body: TopicUser.find_by can return nil (user never had a topic_users row, or it was removed). The next line calls tu.notification_level and raises NoMethodError, so the unsubscribe link 500s instead of muting the topic. When a row does exist, tu.save! writes notification_level directly and skips TopicUser.change, so notifications_reason_id and notifications_changed_at stay unset and no MessageBus notification_level_change is published. update_last_read auto-promotes to tracking when notifications_reason_id is null and view time exceeds the auto-track threshold, which silently undoes the unsubscribe on a later visit. Other open tabs also keep the old level.

title: Topic unsubscribe is a cookie-authenticated GET with no recipient token
body: Both unsubscribe routes are GET and TopicsController#unsubscribe mutates notification state with no CSRF token and no per-recipient key (unlike digest unsubscribe). Rails does not check authenticity tokens on GET, so a logged-in user's browser will apply the change for any third-party page that can trigger the URL (img, redirect, or link prefetch). The link is also not bound to the email recipient: whoever is logged in is the account that is changed, and a logged-out recipient is not unsubscribed until after a login round-trip.

title: Unsubscribe template will not resolve for the new route
body: The route is registered as a top-level topicUnsubscribe (/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe), and the route, controller, and view files are all named topic-unsubscribe, so Ember looks up the template topic-unsubscribe. This file is registered as topic/unsubscribe (the nested topic.unsubscribe name). Nothing sets templateName or renderTemplate, so the confirmation copy and the topic-notifications-button never render. After the Rails action mutates notification level, the user gets a missing-template error instead of the unsubscribe page. The Ember route also never calls an unsubscribe API itself, so a client-side transition to this URL would show the "you will stop receiving notifications" text without changing the level even if the template name were fixed.

title: No tests for per-topic unsubscribe behavior
body: The only spec change passes unsubscribe_url into Email::MessageBuilder so the new %{unsubscribe_url} interpolation does not raise. Nothing asserts that the topic link is actually rendered, and there is no request/controller coverage for unsubscribe: missing TopicUser, watching vs regular vs muted transitions, a second request not changing the level again, slug redirect, or the login/CSRF constraints. The level rules are easy to get wrong and would regress silently.

title: Topic unsubscribe changes state on an unauthenticated GET
body: TopicsController#unsubscribe is routed only as GET (config/routes.rb) and immediately writes TopicUser.notification_level. Rails CSRF protection does not cover GET, and the link embedded in notification emails carries no per-recipient token. Any page that can make the browser request that URL while the victim is logged in (an img or link on another site, a link previewer in the same browser) will change that user's notification level using their session cookie. The link is also not bound to the mailbox recipient, so on a shared browser it mutates whichever account happens to be logged in, not the person who was emailed. Because the transition is not idempotent (watching/tracking becomes regular, a second fetch then mutes), a refresh or a second request does not even settle on the same level.

title: Unsubscribe 500s when the user has no TopicUser row
body: unsubscribe does TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) and then reads tu.notification_level with no nil check. TopicView succeeding only means the user can see the topic; it does not create a topic_users row. Any logged-in user who opens /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe for a topic they have never visited (or whose row was removed) gets NoMethodError instead of being muted. That URL is publicly linked from email and is not restricted to people who already have a TopicUser.

title: Watching and tracking users are not actually unsubscribed
body: If notification_level is above regular (tracking=2 or watching=3), the action sets regular (1); only regular or muted users are set to muted. Regular still emails replies, mentions, and quotes, and watching is exactly the level that emails every new post. The email copy in server.en.yml tells the recipient this link will "stop receiving notifications about this particular topic", and the confirmation string in client.en.yml always says they will stop receiving notifications. After one click a watcher is only demoted to regular, so those emails continue, and the confirmation is false. A second request (refresh, or the non-idempotent GET being fetched twice) then takes the else branch and mutes, so the end state depends on how many times the URL was hit.

title: Direct save skips notifications_reason_id so auto-track can undo the change
body: The new level is written with tu.notification_level= and tu.save! instead of TopicUser.change. change is what sets notifications_changed_at, notifications_reason_id (user_changed), and the MessageBus notification_level_change event. update_last_read in topic_user.rb promotes notification_level back to tracking whenever notifications_reason_id is still null and time-on-topic exceeds the auto-track threshold. Users who were at the default regular level (reason id null) and get muted here will be bumped back to tracking the next time post timings are recorded, so the unsubscribe does not stick. Other open tabs also never hear about the change.

title: Unsubscribe template path does not match the Ember route
body: The route is registered as top-level topicUnsubscribe (app-route-map.js.es6), and the controller and view are named topic-unsubscribe, so Ember looks up the template topic-unsubscribe. This file lives at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs, which compiles to the template name topic/unsubscribe used only by a nested topic.unsubscribe route. Nothing in the route calls renderTemplate to point at that name. After the server action runs, the Ember app transitions to topicUnsubscribe and renders a missing template: the confirmation text and the topic-notifications-button never appear, so the user gets a blank page and cannot correct the level the GET just wrote.

title: No spec covers the unsubscribe action or the new email link
body: The only test change is in spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb, which passes unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe" so I18n interpolation of the rewritten unsubscribe_link string does not raise. It never asserts that the per-topic sentence or URL is actually in the body. There is no controller or mailer spec for TopicsController#unsubscribe: missing TopicUser, watching versus regular, slug redirect, or that notification emails include topic.unsubscribe_url. The non-idempotent level change and the nil crash can ship unnoticed.

title: Unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser row
body: TopicsController#unsubscribe loads the per-user row with TopicUser.find_by and immediately reads tu.notification_level. If that row does not exist (logged-in user who can see the topic but has never had a topic_users record, or a category/mailing-list recipient whose row was never created), tu is nil and this raises NoMethodError. The email link then returns 500 and the notification level is not changed, so the unsubscribe action fails for exactly the people who need it. Use TopicUser.change (which inserts a row when missing) or create a muted row before updating.

title: One-click unsubscribe does not stop notifications for watching or tracking users
body: The email copy and the new client string both say the link stops notifications for this topic, but the action only mutes when notification_level is regular or already muted. Watching (3) and tracking (2) are greater than regular, so they are downgraded to regular instead of muted. Regular still generates reply, mention, and quote notifications, so a user who is emailed because they are watching the topic — the main case for a per-topic unsubscribe link — keeps receiving those emails after one click. The confirmation page always claims notifications have stopped, and nothing tells them they must click again to actually mute.

title: Direct TopicUser save leaves notifications_reason_id nil so auto-track undoes the change
body: The new action assigns notification_level and calls save! instead of TopicUser.change. change is what sets notifications_changed_at, notifications_reason_id (user_changed), and the MessageBus notification_level_change event. Leaving notifications_reason_id nil means the existing auto-track logic in TopicUser.update_last_read and TopicUser.auto_track will treat the row as never explicitly chosen and set it back to tracking once the user has viewed the topic long enough (or on the next auto_track call). A successful mute is therefore silently reverted the next time they read the topic, and other open tabs are not told the level changed.

title: Unsubscribe is a cookie-authenticated GET with no recipient token
body: GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe (and /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe, which 301s to the slugged URL) changes notification state with no CSRF token and no per-recipient unsubscribe key. ensure_logged_in only checks the browser session. Any site can trigger it while the victim is logged in (for example an to /t//unsubscribe); the browser sends session cookies, follows the 301, and the second request mutates state. The link also is not bound to the user who was emailed: whoever is logged in is the account that is changed, so a shared browser, staff session, or forwarded mail unsubscribes the wrong person while the recipient keeps getting mail. Email link scanners that do send cookies can apply the change without a click, and because the handler is not idempotent for watching users a second fetch drops them from regular to muted. This needs a POST (or a one-time key like the digest unsubscribe key) that identifies the recipient.

title: Unsubscribe template will not be resolved by the new route
body: The route is registered as a top-level topicUnsubscribe at /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe (app-route-map.js.es6). Ember resolves that to the template, controller, and view names topic-unsubscribe. The controller and view were added under those names, but the template was added at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs, which compiles to topic/unsubscribe and is only used by a nested topic.unsubscribe route. Nothing calls renderTemplate to bridge the gap, so after the server has already changed the notification level the confirmation UI throws a missing-template error (or renders an empty outlet). The stop-notifications copy and the notification-level dropdown never appear. Move the template to templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs, or nest the route as topic.unsubscribe and move the controller/view to match.

title: No coverage for the unsubscribe action or the new email link
body: The only spec change passes unsubscribe_url into an existing MessageBuilder example so I18n interpolation does not raise, and still only asserts that the preferences URL is in the body. Nothing asserts the new per-topic sentence or URL, and there is no request/controller spec for TopicsController#unsubscribe. The nil TopicUser crash, the watching-to-regular branch, the missing notifications_reason_id, the slug redirect, and the wrong-session GET mutation would all merge unnoticed.

title: Blocked-email check is case- and whitespace-sensitive
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? looks up the address with an exact BlockedEmail.where(email: email) match, and BlockedEmail only validates uniqueness of the raw email string (no downcasing or stripping in set_defaults). Signup stores whatever the user typed (User.new_from_params assigns params[:email] unchanged), while other paths such as change_email normalize with Email.downcase and strip. A blocked row for "bad@spam.com" therefore does not match "Bad@spam.com" or "bad@spam.com ", and the case-sensitive unique index will not treat those as the same address. Someone who was blocked can still register by changing case or surrounding whitespace.

title: Match stats are written inside validation and rolled back or double-counted
body: should_block? is invoked from EmailValidator during User validation, but it is not a pure check: it does match_count += 1, sets last_match_at, and calls save. User#save runs validations inside a transaction and raises ActiveRecord::Rollback when the user is invalid, so the counter update made while rejecting a blocked address is undone and never persisted on a normal save/save!/create. UsersController#create hides this for one path only: it calls user.valid? first (that increment commits) and then user.save (a second increment that rolls back), so the count is right there only by accident and any extra valid? double-counts. The same read-modify-write save also writes every column, so two concurrent matches can lose increments and a concurrent admin change to action_type can be overwritten. Match auditing is unreliable, and the new specs only call should_block? directly so they never catch the rollback.

title: Domain whitelist/blacklist regex is unanchored
body: email_in_restriction_setting? builds Regexp.new("@(#{domains})", true) after only escaping dots, then uses =~ with no end anchor or domain boundary. A whitelist value of company.com therefore matches user@company.com.attacker.example (and user@company.com.extra) as well as user@company.com, so a site that restricts signup to specific providers can be bypassed by any domain that merely contains the allowed domain as a substring. The same pattern makes a blacklist over-match unrelated hosts such as user@spam.com.legitimate.example. This is now the only server-side domain check (it was moved here from User), and nothing in the new specs covers whitelist or blacklist behavior.

title: should_block? write clobbers the row and double-counts
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? loads a row, increments match_count in memory, and record.save writes every attribute back. That is last-write-wins with no row lock and no atomic UPDATE match_count = match_count + 1, so a concurrent admin change to action_type (for example switching block to do_nothing) can be overwritten by an in-flight check, and overlapping checks lose increments. The write also runs inside email validation, and UsersController#create calls user.valid? and then user.save, so one signup attempt runs the validator twice and adds 2 to match_count whenever any BlockedEmail row matches, including action_type do_nothing. A frequently submitted blocked address becomes a hot-row write on every attempt, and the new specs only call should_block? once so they still expect a +1 change.

title: Blocked-email match is exact and case-sensitive
body: should_block? uses BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first, and the unique index on blocked_emails.email is case-sensitive. Elsewhere this app canonicalizes addresses with Email.downcase and strip (UsersController#change_email) before comparing, but signup validation neither normalizes the submitted address nor the stored block row. A block for blocked@spam.com therefore does not match Blocked@spam.com, surrounding whitespace, or other case variants, and those addresses pass validation and can register. Uniqueness on BlockedEmail has the same comparison, so both casings can be stored as separate rows and .first still only sees an exact match.

title: Domain allow/deny regex is not anchored
body: email_in_restriction_setting? compiles Regexp.new("@(#{domains})") with no end anchor after only escaping dots. For a whitelist entry example.com, user@example.com.evil.com matches because @example.com is only required as a substring, so the address is treated as allowed and signup proceeds. The same helper is now the only domain check on User. Other regex metacharacters in the site setting are also unescaped, so a malformed domain list can raise RegexpError and 500 registration instead of failing validation.

title: blocked_emails migration is not reflected in schema.rb
body: This migration creates blocked_emails, but db/schema.rb is not updated. Discourse loads fresh and test databases from schema.rb (db:schema:load / db:test:prepare) rather than replaying every migration. New environments and CI will not have the table, so BlockedEmail.should_block? and the new specs will raise a missing-relation error until the schema dump is regenerated and committed.

title: Any rejected email is shown as an invalid format
body: On a failed create, any result.errors.email causes the submitted address to be pushed onto rejectedEmails. emailValidation then always fails with I18n.t('user.email.invalid'), the format-failure string, whether the server rejected a blocked address, a disallowed domain, or a duplicate. The new server string user.email.blocked is never shown on the field. The address also stays rejected for the life of the controller, so a transient 'already taken' failure cannot be retried without a full reload.

title: Moved domain rules and block wiring are untested
body: The EmailValidator examples stub BlockedEmail.should_block? and only check whether an error was added. They never set email_domains_whitelist or email_domains_blacklist, so the domain-restriction logic moved out of User#email_validator can break without a failing test. Nothing exercises User save or UsersController#create with a real BlockedEmail row, so a case-variant bypass or a double match_count increment on valid? plus save would also pass CI.

title: Block-hit stats are rolled back on the signup they record
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? increments match_count and last_match_at and calls record.save while it is invoked from EmailValidator during User validation. User#save runs validations inside the same database transaction, and a blocked address fails validation, so that transaction rolls back and undoes the BlockedEmail update. On a normal install (SiteSetting.call_discourse_hub? false) UsersController#create only calls save, so blocked signup attempts never persist match statistics — last_match_at stays nil and match_count stays 0, which is the signal the model spec says admins use to see whether a rule has ever matched. When call_discourse_hub? is true, create calls user.valid? (line 168) before save, so the first increment commits and the second is rolled back, and the counter moves by 1 instead of 2. The write has to happen outside the user transaction (separate connection, or after the user save/rollback), or the stats feature does not work for the block action.

title: Exact email match lets blocked addresses sign up
body: should_block? loads BlockedEmail with a case-sensitive where(email: email) and never strips or downcases. Signup stores whatever was posted (User.new_from_params assigns params[:email] raw), while change_email in UsersController canonicalizes with Email.downcase(...).strip. A row for user@evil.com therefore does not match User@evil.com, user@evil.com with surrounding whitespace, or other case variants, so the new block is bypassed by changing case or padding the address. Uniqueness on blocked_emails.email is also case-sensitive, so both casings can be stored and .first can return either row. Normalize on write (set_defaults) and on lookup the same way change_email does, and compare the normalized value, or the blocklist does not actually block.

title: match_count increment loses updates under concurrency
body: The hit counter is read-modify-write: match_count += 1 followed by save. Two overlapping signup attempts that match the same blocked row both read the same count and both write count+1, so one hit is dropped. Popular blocked addresses are exactly the rows that get concurrent attempts. Even after the stat update is moved out of the user transaction, this still needs an atomic update (for example update_all("match_count = match_count + 1") on that id) rather than loading the integer into Ruby.

title: Tests stub the block check and miss signup behavior
body: EmailValidator examples stub BlockedEmail.should_block?, so they never hit the database, never assert the user.email.blocked message, and never run User#save. BlockedEmail specs only call should_block? directly, which commits the counter outside a user transaction, so they stay green while a real blocked signup rolls the stats back and while a case or whitespace variant is allowed through. There is also no coverage that the domain whitelist/blacklist logic moved out of User still rejects addresses. A User create/save example with a real BlockedEmail row (including a different-case address) is needed or these failures ship untested.

title: Embed template has invalid ERB (`end if`)
body: `<%- end if %>` compiles to the Ruby statement `end if`, which is a SyntaxError. Rendering `/embed/best` when a topic already exists (the success path in EmbedController#best) will raise while compiling the template, so the iframe never shows highlights. It must be `<% end %>`.

title: raw_html cook path stores and serves unsanitized HTML
body: Post#cook returns `raw` unchanged when cook_method is raw_html, skipping PrettyText and Discourse's sanitizer. TopicEmbed.import persists RSS/Readability HTML with that cook method, and the embed view prints it with `raw post.cooked` (the main topic UI also treats cooked as HTML). PollFeed does `CGI.unescapeHTML` on feed content first, so entity-encoded markup becomes live tags, and Readability's allow-list still permits `javascript:`/`data:` href and src. Any feed item or fetched page can therefore plant stored XSS that runs for every forum visitor, not just inside the embed iframe. The imported-from footer makes this worse by interpolating the URL into an href with no escaping (`<a href='#{url}'>` in TopicEmbed.import), so a quote in an otherwise allowed http(s) URL breaks out of the attribute.

title: Unauthenticated embed URL fetch is an SSRF and topic-spam vector
body: import_remote uses `open(url).read` (open-uri) with no timeout, size limit, or redirect restriction. EmbedController#best is a public GET whose only gate is `URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. Referer is client-controlled, so any caller can spoof it and pass `embed_url` on the configured host. TopicRetriever then fetches that URL; open-uri follows redirects to arbitrary hosts (including link-local and cloud metadata). Each miss also enqueues RetrieveTopic with no controller-side dedupe, so unique URLs create unbounded jobs and, on success, topics posted as embed_by_username. open-uri is not even required from this file, so the fetch only works if some other file has already patched Kernel#open.

title: Feed poll crashes unless every item has string content
body: `i.content.scrub` assumes every SimpleRSS item has a String `content`. RSS 2.0 items typically expose `description` and leave `content` nil; Atom can also omit it. Nil (or a non-string) raises NoMethodError, and because there is no rescue the hourly job aborts before later items are imported. `String#scrub` is also Ruby 2.1+ only, so this line fails on Ruby 2.0 even when content is present. Use description/content fallback and guard nil before unescaping.

title: postMessage targetOrigin is the full referer, so resize is dropped
body: The embed layout calls `parent.postMessage(..., request.referer)`. postMessage's targetOrigin must be an origin (`scheme://host[:port]`), not a full URL with path and query. Browsers drop the message (or throw) when it does not match the parent origin. embed.js also sets the iframe to `scrolling=no` and only grows it on `discourse-resize`, so the comments frame stays at the default height and clips the discussion. Pass the referer origin only (and escape it for the JS string).

title: Resize listener accepts any origin that is a prefix of discourseUrl
body: The check is `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`, i.e. accept when the sender origin is any substring of discourseUrl, not when it equals the forum origin. A shorter origin that is a prefix matches: if discourseUrl is `https://discuss.example.com`, a window at `https://discuss.example.co` has index 0 and is accepted. That page can postMessage a `discourse-resize` and set the iframe height arbitrarily (hide comments or stretch the frame over the host page). Compare parsed origins for equality, and require index 0 only if a prefix check is kept.

title: Embed controller spec expects a sync retrieve the action does not do
body: The 'no previous embed' example expects `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve` during `get :best`. EmbedController#best only calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`, so mocha fails this example and the job/throttle path is untested. The other success example renders `embed/best`, which currently raises SyntaxError on `end if`, so the `response.should be_success` after-hook fails as well. The spec will not pass as written and does not lock in the async behavior.

title: Disqus import drops category, original date, and offline permalinks
body: The importer no longer accepts `--category` and no longer passes `created_at` or `category` into topic creation. It now depends on `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which HTTP-fetches `t[:link]` and returns nil on any network/HTTP error. The following comment import is skipped entirely when that fetch fails, so a dead or blocked article URL drops the whole Disqus thread instead of creating the previous permalink stub. Category placement and original thread timestamps are also lost, and a single failed fetch aborts the rest of the file because nothing rescues `open`.

title: embed_url is varchar(255) but used as the unique lookup key
body: `t.string :embed_url` is a 255-character varchar, with a unique index on that column. TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed and import look up the full URL. Article and RSS links with tracking query strings routinely exceed 255 characters, so insert raises and the topic is never associated; truncated values would also collide or miss on lookup. Store embed_url as text (and index a hash if a unique constraint is still required).

title: content_sha1 is advanced even when the post is not updated
body: On change, import always calls `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` after `revise!`, without checking that revise!/save succeeded. PostRevisor#revise! returns false when raw is unchanged and still returns true if `save` fails; either way the SHA is overwritten. The next poll then treats the feed item as already imported and never retries, so the topic body stays stale. If the linked post was deleted, `embed.post` is nil and `PostRevisor.new(post)` raises, which aborts the rest of the feed run. Update the SHA only after a successful save, and skip or recreate when the post is gone.

title: Embed template has invalid ERB and will not render
body: The header conditional is closed with `<%- end if %>`, which compiles to invalid Ruby (`end if` with no condition) and raises a syntax error when the embed layout renders `best`. Any request that finds an existing topic therefore 500s instead of showing highlights, so the embed iframe never works for topics that have already been imported. It needs to be `<% end %>`.

title: Imported HTML is stored and rendered unsanitized
body: RSS and remote imports create the topic with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`. `Post#cook` then returns `raw` unchanged, skipping the normal cook/sanitize pipeline, and both the topic page and `embed/best.html.erb` (`raw post.cooked`) emit that HTML. `PollFeed` feeds `CGI.unescapeHTML` of the feed item straight into this path, and `import` also interpolates the source URL into an `<a href='...'>` without escaping. A feed item or fetched page can therefore store script or a broken-out URL (`http://host/'><script>...`) that runs in the forum origin for every visitor.

title: Unauthenticated embed fetch is an SSRF and topic-creation primitive
body: `import_remote` does `open(url).read` with no scheme allowlist, timeout, size limit, or redirect restriction, then publishes the body as a post by `embed_by_username`. `EmbedController#best` will enqueue that fetch for any client that sends `Referer` whose host equals `embeddable_host` (a header the caller sets; it is not a browser-only check) and any `embed_url` on that host. `open-uri` follows redirects, so a redirect on the allowed host makes the app request internal addresses (for example link-local metadata) and can turn the response into a public topic. The same `open` call is also missing `require 'open-uri'`; unless some other file has already loaded it, `Kernel#open` treats the URL as a local path, the retrieve job errors, and the embed stays on the loading page. `TopicRetriever` only calls `Jobs::PollFeed` (which does require `open-uri`) when feed polling is enabled, so the HTTP fallback is the path that breaks.

title: Feed poll crashes on typical RSS items and blocks embeds
body: `i.content.scrub` assumes every item has a `content` field and that `String#scrub` exists. Standard RSS 2.0 items only have `description`, so `i.content` is nil and this raises NoMethodError; `scrub` itself is also missing on Ruby 1.9/2.0, which this app still boots. The scheduled job sets `retry: false`, so one bad item aborts the whole import. `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute` synchronously before the HTTP fallback whenever feed polling is enabled, so the same exception also prevents on-demand embed retrieval and leaves the iframe reloading `loading` forever.

title: Resize postMessage uses the full referer as targetOrigin
body: The iframe sends `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')`. `postMessage`'s targetOrigin must be an origin (`scheme://host[:port]`), not the full referring URL. A path or query on the referer means the parent origin does not match, the resize message is dropped (or the call throws), and `embed.js` never updates `#discourse-embed-frame` height, so comments are clipped by `scrolling="no"`. The same interpolation is only HTML-escaped, not JavaScript-escaped, so a referer whose host is the configured embeddable host but whose path contains a quote (Rails 3 does not escape `'`) or a JS line terminator breaks out of the string and runs in the forum origin.

title: Throttle key can stick forever if expire does not run
body: The per-URL throttle does `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and only then `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process dies, the connection drops, or expire fails between those calls, the key is left with no TTL. `retrieved_recently?` then stays true for that embed URL forever (unless the caller is staff and passes `no_throttle`), so the article is never fetched and the embed never leaves the loading state. The set and TTL need to be a single atomic SET with expiry.

title: embed_url is varchar(255) with a unique index
body: `t.string :embed_url` is a 255-character varchar, and the unique index is on that column. Article URLs with query strings routinely exceed 255 characters. `TopicEmbed.create!` then raises, the import transaction rolls back, and that page can never be embedded. Two distinct URLs that share the same first 255 characters also collide on the unique index and one of them fails to import.

title: Disqus import now depends on a live fetch and drops category
body: The task used to create the topic locally from the export. It now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which `open`s `t[:link]` with no rescue. A single dead link, non-HTTP link, or timeout raises and aborts the rest of the threads (the `ensure` only restores the rate limiter and email blacklist). The `-c`/`category` option and the `category_id` passed to `PostCreator` were removed, and `TopicEmbed.import` has no category argument, so every imported thread lands in the default category instead of the one the operator selected.

title: Embed success example cannot pass as written
body: The "topic_id is found" example stubs `TopicView.new` but does not return a topic view (Mocha yields nil). The action then renders `best`, which immediately calls `@topic_view.posts` / `@topic_view.topic`. The shared `after` hook also requires `response.should be_success` and `X-Frame-Options == ALLOWALL`. Even after the `end if` template syntax error is fixed, this example 500s and the new controller spec fails, so it does not lock in the embed response.

title: Imported HTML is stored and rendered unsanitized
body: TopicEmbed.import appends the source URL into the post body with raw string interpolation (`<a href='#{url}'>`) and saves the whole document via PostCreator with cook_method raw_html and skip_validations. Post#cook then returns raw unchanged whenever cook_method is raw_html, so the normal PrettyText/Sanitize pipeline never runs. Cooked HTML is rendered with `raw` in the embed view and on the topic page. RSS items (PollFeed also runs CGI.unescapeHTML on the body, turning escaped markup back into tags) and any page fetched for an embed can therefore plant script, event handlers, or a quote-breaking URL such as http://host/?q='><script>… and get stored XSS in the forum origin. The existing sanitize gem is not used, and the topic embed spec locks in cooked == raw.

title: Embed template has invalid ERB (`end if`)
body: The header conditional is closed with `<%- end if %>`, which is not valid Ruby inside ERB. Rendering the success path (a topic id was found and best.html.erb is rendered) raises a SyntaxError/Template::Error, so the embed iframe 500s whenever a discussion already exists. It must be `<% end %>`.

title: Feed poll crashes on typical RSS items
body: poll_feed always does `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and then TopicEmbed.import. SimpleRSS leaves `content` nil for ordinary RSS 2.0 items that only have `description`/`summary`, so the first such item raises NoMethodError and the hourly job stops, importing nothing after it. String#scrub also does not exist on Ruby 2.0/1.9, which this app still references. There is no per-item rescue, and title/link can be missing the same way. Use a fallback (`content` or `description` or empty string), guard nil, and isolate item failures.

title: import_remote uses Kernel#open on attacker-influenced URLs
body: import_remote calls `open(url).read` without `require 'open-uri'` (unlike PollFeed) and without an http(s)-only client, timeout, or redirect check. If open-uri has not been loaded, Kernel#open treats the URL as a local filename and the fetch fails (Disqus import and embed retrieval blow up). Once open-uri is loaded, it follows redirects to any host with no read timeout, and non-URI strings fall through to file open or pipe execution. Embed URLs are supplied by visitors (TopicRetriever only compares URI#host to embeddable_host, not the scheme, and does not re-check redirects), and PollFeed does the same `open` on feed_polling_url. That is SSRF against internal HTTP services, worker hangs, and, for a non-http setting or feed link, local file read.

title: postMessage origin check is a substring match
body: The resize listener accepts a message when `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) !== -1`. That is the wrong direction and is not an origin equality check. Any origin that is a prefix/substring of the configured forum URL passes, for example origin `http://forum.example.co` against discourseUrl `http://forum.example.com`, or any shorter prefix. A page that can postMessage to the host page (opener or another frame) can then set the embed iframe height. Compare the message origin to the parsed origin of discourseUrl (scheme, host, and port) instead.

title: Embed controller specs assert the wrong control flow
body: The success example expects `TopicRetriever.new` and `retrieve` to run inside the request. EmbedController#best does not do that; it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, …)` and renders loading. That expectation fails. The other success example renders best.html.erb, which currently cannot compile (`end if`), so the after-hook `response.should be_success` fails as well. The specs will not catch the enqueue/host/throttle behavior that actually shipped.

title: Cache miss runs a full feed import and drops HTTP fallback
body: When feed polling is enabled, perform_retrieve synchronously runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` (download and import every feed item) inside the per-URL retrieve job, then only calls fetch_http if that returns normally and the URL is still missing. Any exception from the feed (network error, nil content, bad item) aborts the job before the single-page HTTP fetch, so the embed stays on the loading page forever. A single comment embed also triggers a full import with no timeout isolation.

title: Unauthenticated embed GETs enqueue unbounded jobs
body: best only checks that the Referer host equals embeddable_host, then enqueues retrieve_topic for whatever embed_url was passed. Referer is trivial to spoof, embed_url is not checked against embeddable_host or a rate limit in the request, and the Redis throttle lives inside the job and is per URL. An anonymous client can fill the Sidekiq queue with unique URLs; each job still does work (host parse, Redis, sometimes HTTP). Validate the embed URL host before enqueue and throttle enqueues.

title: embed_url is varchar(255) with a unique index
body: embed_url is a Rails string column (varchar 255) and is uniquely indexed. Article and tracking URLs routinely exceed 255 characters. Insert then raises on PostgreSQL, TopicEmbed.create! rolls the import back, and that URL can never be embedded. Store embed_url as text (and keep the unique index).

title: Disqus import now depends on a live remote fetch and drops category
body: The importer used to create a local topic from the export (permalink stub, optional -c category) and then attach comments. It now calls TopicEmbed.import_remote, which GETs t[:link] and returns nothing usable if the historical URL 404s, redirects oddly, or open() raises. The exception is not rescued inside the thread loop, so one dead link aborts the rest of the file (the ensure only restores the email blacklist and rate limiter). The category option and category_id lookup were removed, and TopicEmbed.import has no category argument, so surviving imports also land in the wrong category.

title: Post jobs are enqueued inside the outer import transaction
body: import wraps PostCreator.create in Topic.transaction. PostCreator commits its own nested transaction by joining that outer one, then enqueue_jobs (process_post, feature_topic_users) runs before Topic.transaction commits. If TopicEmbed.create! then fails (unique embed_url race, null id), the outer transaction rolls the post back but the jobs are already queued and run against a missing row. Even on success they can run before commit. Enqueue only after the outer transaction commits, and rescue RecordNotUnique so a raced import reuses the existing embed instead of erroring.

title: Throttle key can stick forever if expire is skipped
body: retrieved_recently? uses SETNX and then a separate EXPIRE of 60 seconds. If the process dies between those calls, the key remains with no TTL and that embed URL is never fetched again for non-staff users (they stay on the loading page). Use a single SET key 1 NX EX 60 so the lock cannot outlive the throttle window.

title: Small-action button float is ignored inside the new flex row
body: .small-action is now a flex container (flexbox() and align-items(center) at lines 264-265), but the action button is still placed with float: right. Float does not apply to flex items, and the patch never replaces it with margin-left: auto on the button or flex: 1 on .small-action-desc. For the usual short small-action label (closed, pinned, archived) in a wide post, the delete button therefore sits immediately after the text instead of at the right edge, which is where float: right put it. The description's old padding (0.5em 0 0.5em 4em) that cleared the 45px floated avatar was also reduced to 0 1.5%, so any browser that ignores every display value emitted by flexbox() still honors float: left on .topic-avatar and draws the label underneath that icon.

title: Header flex row overflows and pushes controls off-screen
body: .d-header .contents is now display: flex with the default flex-wrap: nowrap. .title, .extra-info-wrapper (only order: 2 in topic.scss), and .panel (only margin-left: auto and order: 3) never set min-width: 0, overflow: hidden, or flex-shrink: 0. Flex items default to min-width: auto, so they will not shrink below their content minimum, and margin-left: auto only eats positive free space — it does not stop overflow. A wide site logo (this file only sets #site-logo max-height: 40px, not a max-width) or a long docked topic title plus the 32px header icons therefore overflows the bar instead of ellipsizing or wrapping. On a narrow viewport the fixed header widens the page and login/notification controls are pushed out of view. The old float: left / float: right layout kept the panel shrink-to-fit on the right and let the middle content wrap inside the header width. Give the middle item flex: 1, min-width: 0, and overflow: hidden, and set flex-shrink: 0 on .title and .panel.

title: box-ordinal-group is not shifted to the 1-based scale
body: @mixin order writes $val unchanged to -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group. Those 2009 properties are 1-based (initial value 1) and reject non-positive integers, while order, -webkit-order, and -ms-flex-order are 0-based (initial value 0). The equivalent legacy value is $val + 1. Today's call sites pass 2 and 3, so they still sort after items that omit order (legacy groups 1, 2, 3 versus modern 0, 2, 3) and the header does not mis-order yet. The shared mixin is still wrong for the model it claims to support: order(1) ties with unstyled siblings instead of following them, and order(0) is an invalid ordinal so the declaration is dropped and the item stays in the default group.

title: 2009 box display prefixes drop the header float fallback
body: flexbox() emits display: -webkit-box and display: -moz-box (and inline-flex() emits the inline equivalents) before the 2012 and unprefixed values. Engines that only implement the 2009 box model will honor that display and ignore later ones. That model does not pack with margin-left: auto and ignores float on children, but this PR removed .d-header .title { float: left } and .panel { float: right } and now depends on margin-left: auto to keep login and notification controls on the right. Those browsers therefore lay the logo and the panel out together at the start. Engines that understand none of the prefixed display values also lose the float fallback, so .panel becomes a normal full-width block under the logo. Either omit the 2009 display values and keep the floats as the non-flex fallback, or implement the matching -webkit-box-pack / -webkit-box-flex rules; the prefixes as written do not reproduce the layout they replaced.

title: 2009 flexbox display values break the layouts that call these mixins
body: `flexbox()` and `inline-flex()` emit the 2009 box model (`display: -webkit-box`, `display: -moz-box`, `display: -webkit-inline-box`, `display: -moz-inline-box`) ahead of the 2012/modern values, and they never emit `display: -moz-flex` or `display: -moz-inline-flex`. Engines that only understand the 2009 keywords (Android 4.x stock browser, old iOS) will take that `display` and ignore the later ones. In that model `margin-left: auto` does not absorb free space, modern `align-items`/`order` do not apply, and `float` on the children is suppressed — so there is no float fallback either. That is exactly what the new call sites need: `.d-header .panel` was switched from `float: right` to `margin-left: auto`, and `.badge-wrapper.bullet` previously fell back to the parent `inline-block` when unprefixed `inline-flex` was ignored. Those browsers now drop the header controls (login, search, notifications) off the right edge and lay bullet badges out with the old box model. Firefox 22–27, which only had `-moz-flex`, gets no flex layout at all. Drop the 2009 `display: box` values; they are not a compatible prefix for the properties these call sites use.

title: order() mixin writes a 0-based value into 1-based ordinal-group
body: `@mixin order` assigns the same integer to `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group` as to `order` / `-webkit-order` / `-ms-flex-order`. The 2009 ordinal-group property is 1-based (initial value 1); `order` is 0-based (initial value 0). The legacy declarations must be `$val + 1`. As written, `@include order(1)` lands in the same group as items that set no order, so it will not sort after them the way `order: 1` does in modern browsers, and `order(0)` is an invalid ordinal-group. Header layout now depends on this mixin (`.panel` uses `order(3)`, `.extra-info-wrapper` uses `order(2)`). Those two values still sort after the default group by accident, but any `order(0)` or `order(1)` — including a plugin rule — will produce a different visual order in old WebKit than in current browsers and scramble the docked header.

title: Header panel is no longer right-aligned without modern flexbox
body: `.d-header .panel` lost `float: right` and `.d-header .title` lost `float: left`. The replacement is `margin-left: auto` and `order(3)` on the panel, which only pins the controls to the trailing edge when `.contents` is a modern flex container. If `display: flex` (and the 2012 prefixes) are ignored, `.panel` and `.title` are ordinary blocks: auto margins on a width:auto block compute to 0, so the logo and the header controls stack and the controls sit on the left. If the new mixin’s `display: -webkit-box` is what the engine honors, auto margins still do not pack to the end, and the removed floats cannot fall back because that display suppresses float. Login, search, and notification icons are the primary header controls. Keep `float: right` / `float: left` as the non-flex fallback, and do not activate a 2009 box display that disables it.

title: Docked topic title can push header controls off-screen
body: `.extra-info-wrapper` is now a flex item of `.d-header .contents` (`order: 2`, with `.panel` at `order: 3` and `margin-left: auto` so topic info sits between the logo and the controls). Nothing in the new rules sets `min-width: 0`, `overflow: hidden`, or a flex basis on `.extra-info-wrapper` or `.title`, and `.contents` does not set `flex-wrap` (so it stays `nowrap`). Flex items default to `min-width: auto`, which will not shrink below the content’s minimum size. A long docked topic title therefore widens the flex line past the viewport instead of ellipsizing, and `margin-left: auto` cannot pull `.panel` back in — the user menu and notifications are pushed off-screen. Set `min-width: 0` (and overflow/ellipsis on the title child) on `.extra-info-wrapper`.

title: Small-action row no longer spans the stream or pins its button
body: `.small-action` is now a flex row, but the action control is still `button { float: right }` (line 309) and `.small-action-desc` changed from `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` to `padding: 0 1.5%` with no `flex: 1` / `min-width: 0`. Float is ignored on flex items, and a float inside a flex item is positioned against that item’s content box, not the full row. The description (or a wrapping `.topic-body`) shrinks to its content, so expand/undo/remove buttons sit beside the text instead of at the right edge of the topic stream. In browsers that do not apply flex, `.topic-avatar` is still `float: left` (line 270) but the 4em padding that cleared that float is gone, so the description overlaps the icon. Vertical spacing was also removed (`margin-top: 5px`, `padding-top: 4px`, and custom-message `margin: 5px 0`), so multi-line custom messages are flush with the row edges. Give the text column `flex: 1` and `min-width: 0`, pin the button with `margin-left: auto` if it is a flex item, and keep a non-flex padding fallback so the text does not cover the avatar.

title: Small-action button float is ignored in the new flex row
body: .small-action is now a flex container (the new flexbox() mixin sets display:flex), but its action button is still float:right. Float and clear do not apply to flex items, so the button is laid out in source order immediately after .small-action-desc instead of at the right edge. Short rows such as closed, pinned, or autoclosed actions therefore show the delete/expand control beside the text rather than pinned to the far side, in every browser that honors the new display. The same change also drops the description's 4em left padding that previously cleared the floated avatar, so non-flex fallbacks will overlap the icon and the text. Put margin-left:auto on the button (and drop the float) to restore the right alignment; .topic-avatar's float:left is likewise ignored and should not be relied on.

title: Panel right-align does not work in the prefixed flex fallback
body: .panel used to be float:right (and .title float:left). Those floats were removed and replaced with margin-left:auto plus order, while flexbox() emits display:-webkit-box and display:-moz-box before the modern values. The 2009 box model does not treat auto margins as flexible space, so browsers that only understand those prefixed values (Safari 6.1/7, iOS 7, older Android) keep the notifications, search, and login cluster immediately after the logo instead of on the right edge of the header. The prefixes this PR adds are exactly the browsers that will miss the new alignment, and there is no float fallback left.

title: order() mixin writes a 0-based value into 1-based ordinal-group
body: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group are 1-based (initial value 1) and reject 0, while the modern order property and -ms-flex-order are 0-based (initial value 0). The new mixin assigns $val to all of them. Autoprefixer-style output must use $val + 1 for the box-ordinal-group properties. order(2) and order(3) in this PR still sort after default items by accident (old default 1 is less than 2 and 3; modern default 0 is less than 2 and 3), but order(1) will not move an item after default siblings in old WebKit/Firefox, and order(0) or a negative order is invalid or ignored in the 2009 syntax. This is the shared helper the header now depends on, so the off-by-one should be fixed before it is reused.

title: Header category bullet loses its 5px alignment offset
body: .extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper.bullet previously had margin-top:5px so the category bullet lined up with the docked topic title text. That rule was deleted. The badges change only routes the existing display:inline-flex and align-items:baseline through mixins, so it does not add a replacement offset, and the new line-height:1.5 on the wrapper does not shift the bullet relative to the label. Category bullets in the scrolling header extra-info will sit about 5px too high against the category name.

title: website_name bypasses TL0 website hiding
body: website is listed in untrusted_attributes, so anonymous viewers of a trust-level 0 user do not receive user_profile.website (anti-spam: the profile must not expose a new user's site). website_name is a new public attribute and is not in that list, and its method reads object.user_profile.website directly. Anonymous clients therefore still get the host, and the path whenever the domain heuristic matches, and user.hbs renders that as the globe label. The new specs never serialize a TL0 user with Guardian.new and assert website_name is absent, so this regression is untested.

title: include_website_name is never invoked
body: ActiveModel::Serializer only calls include_<attr>? (every other hook in this file uses that name). include_website_name has no question mark, so it is dead code and the attribute is always serialized. Users with a blank or unparsable website still get website_name: null in /users/:username.json, and any condition placed in this method will not run.

title: Same-domain path display is case-sensitive
body: website_host is taken from URI#host, which keeps the URL's casing, and is compared to Discourse.current_hostname with == and String#ends_with? (both case-sensitive). A site on example.com and a website of http://Example.com/user, or a site on forums.example.com and a website of http://Example.com/user, fails every branch and the profile shows only the host. The feature then does not show the path for ordinary mixed-case links. The specs only stub lowercase hosts.

title: Domain check mis-classifies hosts and misses www vs apex
body: The equal-label branch treats any two hosts with the same label count above 2 as the same site when every label but the first matches. On a forum at mysite.github.io or forum.co.uk, http://evil.github.io/phish and http://other.co.uk/phish are therefore rendered with the full path, not just the host. The else branch (discourse_host.ends_with?("." + website_host)) is true for any dotted suffix, so a website host of com or co.uk is treated as the parent of a normal forum hostname. The check is also asymmetric for the common www case: instance example.com vs website www.example.com/user does not match (label counts differ, and example.com does not end with .www.example.com), so the path is hidden, while instance www.example.com vs website example.com/user does show the path. None of these cases are covered by the new specs.

title: website_name bypasses TL0 anonymous website redaction
body: website, location, and bio are omitted for trust-level 0 users viewed anonymously via untrusted_attributes (include_<attr>? returns false when scope.restrict_user_fields? is true). website_name is derived from that same website value and is not in that list. The new include_website_name method is also never called: ActiveModel Serializers only invokes include_website_name? (every other hook in this file uses the question-mark form), so the attribute is always serialized. Even renaming the method would not close the hole, because it only checks website.present? and does not apply restrict_user_fields?. The profile template now renders the link from model.website_name instead of a client-side name computed from model.website. Previously the omitted website made that label empty and the link stayed hidden; anonymous visitors will now see the TL0 user's website host and, when the domain check matches, the path. Gate website_name with the same untrusted-attribute rule and cover it in the existing anonymous TL0 serializer spec with a website actually set.

title: Same-domain label check is case-sensitive, drops port, and mismatches subdomains
body: Whether to append the path is decided by case-sensitive equality of URI#host and Discourse.current_hostname, plus a case-sensitive ends_with? / dot-label split. Hosts are case-insensitive, so http://Example.com/docs on an example.com instance fails the match and the path this change is meant to show is dropped. URI#host also strips the port, unlike the removed client logic (website.split("/")[2] kept example.com:8080). A non-default port is therefore labeled example.com or example.com/admin while the href is still http://example.com:8080/..., so the link looks like the forum origin. Matching is asymmetric: forums.example.com shows the path for a website on parent example.com, but example.com does not show the path for https://www.example.com/docs or https://blog.example.com/docs, because those hosts are longer and are not a suffix of the instance host. The else branch's ends_with?("." + website_host) also treats any string suffix as the same site, so a website host of com or co.uk matches ordinary forum hostnames and gets its path appended. Compare downcased hosts, keep a non-default port in the label, and only treat equal hosts or a real parent/child relationship in both directions as the same site.

title: URI parse failure hides the website link entirely
body: website_name does URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil and returns nil when parsing fails. The profile template only shows the globe link when model.website_name is present, so a parse failure removes the website from the profile even though model.website is still set. Ruby's URI parser rejects non-ASCII IRIs and unescaped characters, including realistic values such as http://example.com/ü or a URL with a space in the path. The old client label used split("/")[2] and still displayed the host for those strings. Falling back to a host-only label (or an IDN-aware parser) is needed so a path the strict parser rejects does not drop the whole website.

title: website_name bypasses TL0 anonymous field hiding
body: website_name is derived from website but is not covered by untrusted_attributes, and website_name never calls scope.restrict_user_fields?. For a TL0 user seen anonymously, include_website? is forced false so website is omitted, yet website_name is still serialized. The profile template renders the globe label from model.website_name, so anonymous viewers get the host and, when the heuristic matches, the path of a field this serializer intentionally hides to limit new-user spam. Add website_name to untrusted_attributes (or apply the same guard in include_website_name?) and extend the existing TL0 anonymous serializer example; the new specs only cover a normal user.

title: include_website_name is never invoked
body: ActiveModel::Serializer only calls inclusion hooks named include_<attr>?, and every other hook in this file follows that form. include_website_name has no question mark, so it is dead code and website_name is always emitted, including null when the user has no website. Rename it to include_website_name?. As written it only checks website.present?, so renaming alone does not apply the TL0 restriction.

title: Same-domain check misclassifies hosts
body: The non-equal branches do not test whether the website is actually on the instance domain, so the profile label either appends a path for an unrelated site or drops it for the same site. The elsif treats hosts as the same domain when they have the same label count greater than 2 and share every label except the first, which matches community.co.uk with paypal.co.uk and foo.github.io with bar.github.io and then appends the path. The else branch uses discourse_host.ends_with?("." + website_host), which is true for any suffix, so a website host of com or co.uk matches every forum on that suffix. The common www case fails the other way: a forum on example.com and a website of http://www.example.com/docs has a different label count and example.com does not end with .www.example.com, so only the host is shown. Comparison is also case-sensitive against Discourse.current_hostname while URI#host is lowercased, so a mixed-case hostname misses the exact-match branch. The new specs only cover example.com vs discourse.org, an exact match, and a parent forums.example.com, so they do not catch this. Compare normalized registrable domains (and an optional www label) instead of stripping one label or using a raw suffix check.

title: Embedded-post author link inverts lightness percentages
body: `.topic-meta-data h5 a` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. This change passes `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` as the light-theme color and `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)` as the dark-theme color. Everywhere else in this PR the first `dark-light-choose` argument keeps the original lightness and the `$secondary` argument uses the complement (here that would be 30% / 70%). Light themes therefore render this link much lighter than before, and dark themes get a darker gray than the muted color this rule is meant to produce, so the embedded-post author name loses contrast on a dark background.

title: Group member name color collapsed to the title color
body: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, distinct from the adjacent `.title` at 50%. The replacement uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, the same pair as `.title`. Light-theme names become lighter than before, and names and titles are no longer visually distinct in either theme. The dark branch should be `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)` with the original 30% primary color kept for light themes.

title: Mobile group member name uses the title's 50% scale
body: Mobile `.group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` while `.title` was 50%. Both are now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. That lightens the name on light themes and removes the name/title contrast on light and dark themes. It should keep 30% of `$primary` for light and use 70% of `$secondary` for dark, matching the transform applied to other 30% primary colors.

title: Mobile topic-map heading lightness changed from 20% to 50%
body: `.topic-map h3` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. It is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, which is the h4 color copied onto the heading. The desktop rule for the same heading correctly keeps 20% of `$primary` and uses 80% of `$secondary`. On mobile, light-theme topic-map headings become lighter than before, and dark-theme headings do not match the desktop complement, so the heading is no longer darker/stronger than the h4 beneath it.

title: Mobile custom-message-length swaps the light and dark scales
body: `.custom-message-length` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The new value is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The desktop stylesheet for the same selector correctly keeps 70% of `$primary` and uses 30% of `$secondary`. On mobile the light-theme hint becomes much darker than the existing design, and the dark-theme color is the complement of 30% rather than of 70%, so it will not match desktop or the rest of this change.

title: Category badge notification color still scales $primary only
body: In the same file whose topic-list header, cell, excerpt, and education colors were wrapped in `dark-light-choose`, `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still sets `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`. On a dark theme `$primary` is already near white, so raising its lightness makes this transparent-background notification text nearly the same as primary text instead of the muted gray used by the neighboring list colors. It should follow the same 50% `$primary` / 50% `$secondary` pair used for the other 50% text colors in this file.

title: Embedded-post author color inverted for light themes
body: The embedded-post username link was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). This change sets the light-theme branch to 70% and the dark-theme branch to scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%). Light themes therefore render that name much lighter than before, and dark themes get a 30%-lightness secondary (a dark gray on a dark background) instead of the complementary 70%. The author name in expanded replies will lose the intended contrast in both schemes. Keep $lightness: 30% on $primary and use $lightness: 70% on $secondary.

title: Mobile topic-map heading lightness changed from 20% to 50%
body: Topic-map h3 was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%). The replacement uses 50% for both branches, matching the h4 rule below it rather than the original value. Desktop topic-map h3 in this same PR correctly becomes dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%)). On mobile, light-theme map headings will be washed out relative to the previous design and to desktop, and dark themes will not get the lighter complementary secondary. Restore 20% on $primary and 80% on $secondary.

title: Mobile custom-message-length light and dark branches are swapped
body: .custom-message-length was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%). The new rule uses scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) in the light branch and scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%) in the dark branch. Desktop modal.scss in this PR keeps 70% on $primary and 30% on $secondary. Mobile light themes will show a much darker hint than before, and dark themes will lighten $secondary by 70% instead of 30%, so the hint will not match desktop or the previous light-theme color. Swap the percentages back to 70% / 30%.

title: Group member name lightness raised from 30% to 50%
body: .group-member-info .name was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), distinct from the adjacent .title at 50%. The new color uses 50% for both the light $primary branch and the dark $secondary branch, so the name collapses to the same color as the title. Light themes lose that hierarchy, and dark themes get a 50%-lightness secondary instead of the complementary 70%. Use dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)).

title: Mobile group member name lightness raised from 30% to 50%
body: Same mistake as desktop user.scss: .group-member-info .name was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) and is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)), identical to .title. Light-theme names become lighter than before and no longer differ from titles; dark themes do not get the 70% secondary complement of the original 30%. Restore 30% on $primary and 70% on $secondary.

title: Category badge notification still scales $primary only
body: In the same file, topic-list header, cell, excerpt, and education colors were wrapped in dark-light-choose so dark themes scale $secondary. .topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification is still color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%) on a transparent background. On a dark scheme $primary is already the light text color, so this pushes the count further toward white and leaves the exact dark-theme failure this PR is fixing. Wrap it as dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)).

title: Embedded-post author color inverts the lightness conversion
body: The embedded-post author link was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). This change replaces it with dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). Every other conversion in this PR keeps the original lightness on $primary for light themes and uses the complement (100 minus that value) on $secondary for dark themes, which here would be 30% / 70%. The arguments are swapped, so light themes get a much lighter gray (weaker contrast on the light background) and dark themes get the value that was meant for light themes.

title: Mobile custom-message-length color is inverted versus desktop
body: .custom-message-length was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%). The mobile rule is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)). The desktop counterpart in this same PR correctly keeps 70% on $primary and uses 30% on $secondary. Light-theme mobile hint text therefore becomes substantially darker than before and no longer matches desktop, and the dark-theme value is the old light-theme color rather than the complement.

title: Mobile topic-map heading lightness collapsed from 20% to 50%
body: .topic-map h3 was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%). It is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)), which matches the h4 directly below rather than the original 20%. The desktop .topic-map h3 in this PR correctly becomes 20% on $primary and 80% on $secondary. Light-theme mobile map headings get lighter, lower-contrast text, and dark themes do not get the complementary secondary scale.

title: Group member name color no longer uses the original 30% lightness
body: .user-stream .group-member-info .name was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), intentionally darker than the sibling .title at 50%. It is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)), identical to .title. Light themes lose that distinction and render names lighter than before; dark themes get a 50% secondary scale instead of the 70% complement used for every other 30% conversion in this PR.

title: Mobile group member name color dropped from 30% to 50%
body: .user-stream .group-member-info .name was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). It is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)), the same value as .title. That changes the light-theme name color and does not apply the 30% / 70% primary/secondary pair used for the same original lightness elsewhere in this PR, so dark-theme names are also the wrong shade.

title: Category badge notification still scales $primary on dark themes
body: .topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification still sets color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%) even though this file otherwise wraps the same call in dark-light-choose(..., scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)). On a dark theme $primary is already light, so scaling its lightness further washes the badge text out against the dark background — the exact failure this PR is fixing for the other topic-list colors.

title: Public group members page only loads the first 50 users
body: setupController always calls Group.findMembers(), and that method now always requests limit 50 (the new model default) and offset 0.
