body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changed from 4 to 3, and 4 is now FEATURE_DISABLED. update-compatibility is invoked as a separate process, so callers branch on the numeric code, not this Java constant; recompiling in-repo Java does not update them. This PR does not change any operator production code that runs the check, and UpdateCommandDistTest never asserts an exit code: testFeatureNotEnabled only checks stderr text, and testWrongVersions only checks the incompatibility message. A caller still treating 4 as "incompatible, shut the cluster down first" will now take that path when the preview feature is merely off, and will not treat a real incompatibility (now exit 3) as recreate. That is the decision this tool exists to make; getting it backwards is either an unnecessary outage or a rolling update across incompatible versions. Lock both codes in the dist test and update every numeric comparison in the same change.

title: Exit code 4 is documented as a failed rolling-upgrade decision
body: The new exit-code row says exit 4 means "Rolling Upgrade is not possible" because rolling-updates is disabled. That is the same lead-in as exit 3, which means the deployment must be shut down before the new config is applied. The implementation does not evaluate compatibility in this case: UpdateCompatibilityCheck and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata print "Unable to use this command. The preview feature 'rolling-updates' is not enabled." and return FEATURE_DISABLED before any metadata is read. The guide tells automation to rely on these codes. Describing 4 as a negative compatibility result will cause pipelines to recreate or drain the cluster when the only required action is to enable the feature and rerun the check.

title: Default-strategy upgrade tests never enable rolling-updates
body: createInitialDeployment returns immediately when updateStrategy is null, so spec.features.enabled is left unset for the null cases of testImageChange and testCacheMaxCount. Those cases still call deployKeycloak(..., true), which waits until the CR is ready, and then assert an upgrade status. The operator guide added in this PR says that while the feature is preview it must be enabled or the Operator will fail, including for the default <not set> strategy that mimics 26.1. As written, the default-strategy tests do not meet that precondition and will time out if the warning is true. If they pass, the warning is false and tells every operator user to turn on a preview feature or expect a failed reconcile. Enable the feature for every parameter value, and append it to any features already on the CR instead of setEnabledFeatures(List.of(...)) replacing the whole list, or narrow the caution if the default path is intentionally exempt.

title: Default-strategy upgrade tests never enable rolling-updates
body: createInitialDeployment returns immediately when the parameterized strategy is null, so the new spec.features.enabled: [rolling-updates] setup never runs for that case. testImageChange(null) and testCacheMaxCount(null) still deploy that CR and expect a successful recreate or rolling upgrade. The operator guide added in this PR says the operator fails unless the preview feature is enabled, including for the default (unset) strategy. As written, those two cases either time out or fail reconciliation, or they pass only because the feature is not actually required and the new caution is wrong. Enable the feature for every deployment this class creates (and append it to any features already on the CR instead of replacing the enabled list), or narrow the caution so it does not claim the operator fails for the legacy default strategy.

title: Exit code 4 reused for a different outcome
body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changed from 4 to 3, and the new feature-disabled path exits 4. Until this commit the compatibility CLI returned 4 when a rolling upgrade was not possible. No operator upgrade source is updated in this PR, and the distribution tests only assert stderr text, not the numeric code. A caller that still treats 4 as recreate (the previous behavior, and the code the operator would have been written against) will scale the StatefulSet down when the preview feature is simply off, which is the default. A caller updated only to the documented recreate code 3 will treat the new 4 as an unexpected error and abort the upgrade. Do not reuse the old recreate code: keep 4 as recreate (it does not collide with picocli 1 and 2) and use a new code for feature-disabled, and assert both codes in UpdateCommandDistTest.

title: New exit code 4 and recreate code 3 are not asserted
body: testFeatureNotEnabled only checks that stderr contains the disabled-feature sentence. It does not assert exit code 4, and it only launches the metadata subcommand, not update-compatibility check, which is the command whose exit code the guide tells automation to branch on. testWrongVersions still only checks the incompatibility message after RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE moved from 4 to 3, so a process that still exits 4 (or 1) for an incompatible metadata file would pass. Assert exit code 4 for both subcommands when the feature is off, and assert exit code 3 for the incompatible-version check.

title: Default-strategy upgrade tests never enable rolling-updates
body: createInitialDeployment returns immediately when the update strategy is null, before spec.features.enabled is set to rolling-updates. The parameterized tests include that null strategy, which is the documented default, and still expect a successful rolling upgrade (cache max-count) or recreate upgrade (image change). The new operator guide says this preview feature must be enabled or the operator fails. Those default-strategy deployments therefore run without the feature this change requires, so reconciliation fails or the tests no longer cover the configuration operators must use. Enable rolling-updates on every deployment this helper returns, including the null strategy.

title: Exit code 4 is documented as a compatibility result
body: The check-command exit-code table says exit code 4 means "Rolling Upgrade is not possible" because rolling-updates is disabled. The implementation exits 4 before reading metadata or comparing versions, and prints that the command cannot be used. That is not a compatibility decision: a rolling upgrade may still be possible. The guide tells automation to branch only on these exit codes, and exit code 3 is the code that means shut the deployment down and recreate. Describing 4 the same way ("Rolling Upgrade is not possible") leads scripts to treat a missing feature flag as a required outage, or to treat an inconclusive run as a finished negative check. Document 4 as "command did not run; feature not enabled; result inconclusive", and note that the metadata subcommand uses the same code.

title: Changed CLI exit codes are not asserted
body: testFeatureNotEnabled only checks the stderr text for the metadata subcommand and never asserts exit code 4. The same gate in the check subcommand is not tested. testWrongVersions still only checks log text, so nothing locks the recreate result after this PR changes RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 and reuses 4 for feature disabled. Automation is supposed to choose rolling versus shutdown from these codes; swapping them would not fail CI.

title: All-groups VIEW permission is treated as manage
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE) succeeds, so a caller who only has the Groups VIEW scope on the all-groups resource is treated as a group manager. requireManage() is the gate for creating top-level groups (GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup). That caller can therefore create groups despite having only view access. canManage(GroupModel) correctly requires MANAGE, so the no-arg check is inconsistent with per-group enforcement and with the security model. The interface javadoc repeats the same VIEW-or-MANAGE rule and should be corrected with the implementation.

title: Group view filter stores authz resource ids, not group ids
body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() walks resources with findByType and then calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) and granted.add(groupResource.getId()). hasPermission treats its argument as a group id and looks the resource up with findByName. Instance group resources are named with the group id (resolveGroup returns group.getId()), while Resource.getId() is the authorization resource primary key, so the lookup misses the group resource and falls back to the all-groups resource. The id added to the set is also not a group id. UsersResource and BruteForceUsersResource put that set on the session as UserModel.GROUPS and pass it to getUsersCount. A non-empty set of authz ids makes user search and counts match no real groups (admins with view-members see nobody). The all-groups type resource itself is included by findByType; if it has view-members, its internal id is added and poisons the same filter. The set should contain resource names that are actual group ids, and the type resource named "Groups" must be skipped. Current tests still pass when the set stays empty because listing post-filters with canView, so they do not catch a wrong or empty id set on the count/search path.

title: Per-group authz resources are created without a type
body: getOrCreateResource creates the instance resource with resourceStore.create and updates scopes, but never calls setType(resourceType). The schema init path does set type on the type-level resources, which shows create() does not infer it. GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission depends on resourceStore.findByType(..., GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE). Group resources created for fine-grained permissions therefore are not returned, so view-members and manage-members grants on specific groups are invisible to user search and user-count filtering.

title: Existing admin-permissions clients never gain Groups scopes
body: init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already set, and nothing else reconciles the schema. Realms that enabled fine-grained admin permissions before this change keep a resource server that has no Groups type resource and no manage-membership, manage-members, or view-members scopes. Creating a group permission then hits getOrCreateResource, which throws ModelException("No scopes found.") when a schema scope is missing. Evaluations that fall back to getResourceTypeResource("Groups") get null, and GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission calls policyStore.findByResource and resource.getScopes() on that null, turning a missing schema into a 500 instead of a deny.

title: V2 group permission management throws and breaks group deletion
body: GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled (and isPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions, and the policy accessors) always throw UnsupportedOperationException. AdminPermissions.management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, and the GroupRemovedEvent listener still calls groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false) when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is also enabled. Deleting a group then fails the listener with UnsupportedOperationException and can roll back the delete. The same throw hits the group management/permissions admin endpoints, which still require the V1 feature and then call these methods. If only V2 is enabled, the listener is not registered at all, so deleting a group leaves its authorization resources and policies behind with no V2 cleanup.

title: Permission resource names are not resolved for groups
body: getResourceName special-cases only the Users type and otherwise returns resource.getDisplayName(). Group instance resources are created with the group id as the name and no display name, and this change never adds a Groups branch that loads the group and returns its name or path. Permission listings for the new Groups resource type therefore show null (or a raw id) instead of a group name, and a missing group is not reported the way a missing user is.

title: requireManageMembers javadoc cites the wrong check
body: The javadoc on requireManageMembers says it throws if canManageMembership(GroupModel) is false. The implementation throws when canManageMembers is false. Callers reading only the contract will enforce or test membership management instead of member management.

title: All-groups view permission grants realm-wide group manage
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when the caller has only the Groups VIEW scope on the all-groups resource (hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)). requireManage() uses that result, and GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() calls requireManage() before creating a group. An admin who was granted only view on all groups can therefore create groups (and pass any other no-arg requireManage()/canManage() check). Per-group canManage(GroupModel) correctly requires MANAGE, so this is an escalation specific to the type-level check. The interface javadoc on canManage() documents the same VIEW-or-MANAGE rule and should be corrected with the implementation; view must not imply manage.

title: Group member filter uses authorization resource ids, not group ids
body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() walks resources with findByType(..., GROUPS) and then calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) and granted.add(groupResource.getId()). hasPermission looks the argument up with resourceStore.findByName, but V2 group resources are named with the group id (resolveGroup / getOrCreateResource), while getId() is the authorization resource UUID. The name lookup misses, evaluation falls back to the all-groups resource, and the set stored on the session as UserModel.GROUPS is not a set of group ids. UsersResource and BruteForceUsersResource pass that set into user search, and UsersResource.getUsersCount uses it for counts. If all-groups has view-members/manage-members, every typed resource is treated as granted and search/count are constrained to nonexistent group ids, so members the admin is allowed to see disappear. Per-group grants are not applied as a group-id filter either (and getOrCreateResource never setType(GROUPS), so findByType does not return those resources). The type resource named "Groups" must be skipped; the granted value and the permission lookup must use the group id (resource name).

title: Created group resources are not typed as Groups
body: getOrCreateResource creates a per-object authorization resource and sets scopes, but never calls setType(resourceType). V1 group resources were explicitly typed "Group". GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() discovers candidates only via findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE). Individual group resources created for group permissions therefore never appear, so group-scoped view-members/manage-members permissions cannot drive the user-search group filter even after the id-versus-name bug is fixed. The all-groups resource created in init() is the only one with type Groups.

title: Existing admin-permissions clients are not upgraded with Groups
body: init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already set, and nothing else creates the new Groups resource type or the manage-membership, manage-members, and view-members scopes. Realms that already enabled admin permissions before this change keep a client whose schema has only the previous resource types and scopes. Creating or evaluating a Groups permission then fails (missing scope / "No scopes found") or NPEs in GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission when getResourceTypeResource returns null and that null is passed to policyStore.findByResource and resource.getScopes(). There is no migration to add the Groups resource and scopes onto an existing admin-permissions client.

title: Permission resource names are not resolved for groups
body: getResourceName only special-cases the Users resource type (labeling the type resource "All users" and resolving a user id to a username). Groups resources created by this change use the group id as the resource name and do not set a display name to the group name or path. Group permissions therefore fall through to resource.getDisplayName(), so the admin UI shows null or a raw id instead of the group name, and the all-groups resource is not labeled the way all-users is. A missing group also is not reported, unlike a missing user which throws ModelIllegalStateException.

title: Group permission check ignores which resource was granted
body: GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission accepts any permission in the evaluatePermission result whose scope list intersects the requested scopes. UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission, using the same evaluatePermission API, only accepts a scope when permission.getResourceId() equals the resource under check. Without that filter, a scope granted on a different resource included in the same decision is treated as view, manage, view-members, manage-members, or manage-membership on the group being checked, which over-authorizes group and group-member operations.

title: requireManageMembers javadoc cites the wrong check
body: The javadoc on requireManageMembers says it throws if canManageMembership(GroupModel) is false. The implementation throws when canManageMembers(GroupModel) is false. Callers and implementors following the comment will enforce group-membership management instead of member management.

title: All-groups VIEW is treated as manage
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when the caller has either VIEW or MANAGE on the all-groups resource. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() gates creating a group and moving an existing group to the top level with requireManage(), which only calls this no-arg canManage(). A principal granted only view-all-groups can therefore create groups and reparent any group to the top of the tree. Per-group canManage(GroupModel) correctly checks MANAGE only, so this is not the same as the view-implies-read checks. The new interface javadoc repeats the VIEW-or-MANAGE wording and should not be treated as the intended contract; the evaluation test states that creating a group requires the manage scope.

title: View-members group id lookup returns the wrong ids
body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() is what UsersResource and BruteForceUsersResource pass to user search and getUsersCount as membership constraints (session attribute UserModel.GROUPS). The V2 implementation does two things that make those ids unusable. It asks resourceStore.findByType for type "Groups", but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() never calls setType on the per-group resource it creates (only the synthetic all-groups resource is typed), so individual group resources are not returned. For whatever is returned it calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) and granted.add(groupResource.getId()). Authorization resource ids are not group ids; V2 stores the group id as the resource name (resolveGroup returns group.getId(), and hasPermission looks that up with findByName). The permission check therefore misses the group resource and falls back to the all-groups resource, and any ids that are added do not match membership rows. Result: an admin with VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS on specific groups gets an empty set (user counts stay 0 or unrestricted, and search is not limited to those groups), while the same scopes on all groups inject non-group ids and the search pre-filter drops every user before canView() can allow them. The new GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest only covers per-group user search, which still passes via the post-filter when the set is empty, so this path is untested.

title: Group deletion hits UnsupportedOperationException or leaks authz resources
body: GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled (and the other GroupPermissionManagement methods) always throw UnsupportedOperationException. AdminPermissions.registerListener still handles GroupModel.GroupRemovedEvent by calling management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false) whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled. This PR makes MgmtPermissionsV2.groups() return GroupPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, so a server with both features on will throw from that listener during realm.removeGroup. Provider event listeners are not swallowed, so deleting a group fails with a 500 and the removal is rolled back. If only the V2 feature is on, the listener is not registered at all, and nothing deletes the admin-permissions resource whose name is the group id, so group permissions survive as orphans after the group is gone.

title: Existing admin-permissions clients never gain Groups scopes or the type resource
body: init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already set, and that is the only place this PR creates the Groups resource-type resource and the new scopes manage-membership, manage-members, and view-members. Realms that already enabled admin permissions V2 (the client was created when the schema only had Users and Clients) are not updated. getOrCreateResource then fails with ModelException("No scopes found.") when a group permission is saved, because those scope names are missing. GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission falls back to getResourceTypeResource(..., "Groups"), which returns null, and policyStore.findByResource(server, null) / resource.getScopes() throws NullPointerException. Any fine-grained admin who can list groups but does not hold MANAGE_USERS/VIEW_USERS hits that path from canView(GroupModel), so group listing 500s instead of being filtered.

title: Group permission resources have no display name
body: getResourceName() only resolves a human-readable name for the Users resource type. Group resources created by getOrCreateResource are named with the group id and never get a display name. For a Groups policy the method therefore returns resource.getDisplayName(), which is null. Permission listings in the admin API/UI cannot show which group a permission applies to, unlike users, where the username is resolved from the same resource name.

title: requireManageMembers javadoc cites the wrong check
body: The javadoc on requireManageMembers says it throws when canManageMembership(GroupModel) is false. The implementation throws when canManageMembers is false. Those are different scopes (manage-membership vs manage-members). Callers reading only the interface will enforce or test the wrong permission. The new getGroupIdsWithViewPermission javadoc has the same problem: it says it returns a Stream of groups with view permission, but the method returns a Set and both implementations select groups by view-members/manage-members, not view.

title: Account UI message switched to Java MessageFormat
body: error-invalid-multivalued-size in the account-ui bundle was changed from i18next placeholders ({{0}}, {{1}}, {{2}}) to Java MessageFormat, including a ChoiceFormat fragment {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}. Every other string in this file uses {{ }} interpolation, and the account console translates with i18next, not MessageFormat. The validation error will show literal {0}/{1} and the choice pattern instead of the attribute name and limits. The embedded <values token can also be parsed as a tag if the string is rendered through i18next Trans, which this theme already uses for strings such as <0>{{username}}</0>.

title: Admin UI message switched to Java MessageFormat
body: error-invalid-multivalued-size in the admin-ui (keycloak.v2) bundle was changed from Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s). to a Java ChoiceFormat string. This file is consumed by the React admin console via i18next, which only interpolates {{ }} placeholders. Users will see the raw {0}, {1}, and {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values} text, so the multivalued-size validation error no longer names the attribute or the limits. The Java MessageFormat version belongs only in the server theme bundles under themes/src/main/resources.

title: Lithuanian account totpStep1 replaced with Italian

title: Illegal-HTML diff trim can throw and abort the build
body: When sanitized text differs from the message, the reporter trims a shared prefix (start) and shared suffix (end) and then calls value.substring(start, value.length() - end) and the same on sanitized. The loops do not stop when the two regions overlap, so start can be greater than length - end. That throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. A concrete case is value "aaa" and sanitized "aaaa" (or any insertion/deletion inside a run of identical characters): start and end both become 3 and substring(3, 0) throws. The exception is unchecked and is not turned into a messages entry, so the Maven plugin aborts with a stack trace and never reports which key had illegal HTML.

title: Anchor mismatch message omits key and file

The theme verifier scans every locale file; a CI failure then does not say which file or key introduced the href, so the anchor check cannot be acted on without rerunning under a debugger.

title: Message bundles are decoded as ISO-8859-1, not UTF-8
body: verifySafeHtml loads both the file under test and the English source with PropertyResourceBundle(InputStream) (lines 68 and 77). That constructor always decodes properties as ISO-8859-1, but these theme files are UTF-8 (raw Arabic, Chinese, Cyrillic, and so on, with no \u escapes). Every non-ASCII character is corrupted before the sanitizer comparison, so the check does not see the strings that are actually rendered. Violation snippets are mojibake, and any code point the sanitizer drops when it shows up as a C1 control in the mis-decoded text is reported as illegal HTML. Read both streams with an InputStreamReader in UTF-8.

title: Diff highlighter throws when prefix and suffix overlap
body: When sanitized text differs from the original, the common-prefix/common-suffix loops do not stop at the overlap point. substring(start, length - end) then throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException whenever start + end exceeds the string length, which happens for insertions and deletions inside repeated text (for example value "x" vs sanitized "xx"). The exception escapes the forEachRemaining callback and is not caught by verify(), so the rest of the file is never checked and the Maven plugin fails with an opaque runtime error instead of the Illegal HTML message.

title: Choice-format scrubbing skips HTML inside those messages

Anything inside that clause, including <script> or other markup, is never compared to the sanitizer output, so a translation can carry executable HTML in those user-visible strings and still pass the new check. The choice syntax needs to be recognized without discarding its replacement text, and that text still has to be sanitized.

title: Choice-format strip hides HTML from the sanitizer
body: For keys starting with linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit and for error-invalid-multivalued-size, normalizeValue deletes every {n,choice,...} substring with the regex \{[0-9]+,choice,[^}]*} before the HTML policy runs. [^}]* matches arbitrary markup, so a translation can put tags or script inside the choice subformat and the verifier will replace that whole subformat with "..." and then compare a string that no longer contains the HTML. Those keys are formatted with java.text.MessageFormat and the chosen alternative is inserted into login, admin, and email messages — including HTML email bodies — so this bypasses the check this PR adds. title: Diff highlighter throws when prefix and suffix overlap
body: When sanitized text differs from the message, the code walks a common prefix (start) and a common suffix (end) and then calls value.substring(start, value.length() - end) and the same on sanitized. If the prefix and suffix overlap — start > length - end — String.substring throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. That happens for ordinary edits, for example value "hello" versus sanitized "helo" (one repeated character removed): start=3 and end=2, and sanitized.substring(3, 2) throws. The exception escapes the forEachRemaining lambda, so verify() aborts without recording the "Illegal HTML" diagnostic and without checking the remaining keys of that file. PropertyResourceBundle key order is undefined, so a later illegal entry in the same file may never be reported.

title: Anchor mismatch message omits key and file
body: When a translation anchor does not exactly match the English tag, the verifier only records "Didn't find anchor tag " plus the tag text. Unlike the illegal-HTML message, this omits the message key and the properties file. The Maven plugin reports that string as the build failure, so a CI failure cannot be traced to a key without re-running the check by hand.

title: New getShortcut() method breaks existing grant factories at startup
body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is an existing SPI, and getShortcut() was added as an abstract method with no default. DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit casts every OAuth2GrantType factory and calls getShortcut() while building the shortcut maps. A custom grant factory compiled against the previous interface will throw AbstractMethodError during that postInit, which aborts Keycloak startup rather than only disabling that grant. Add a default implementation and treat a missing or null shortcut as unknown so already-deployed grant providers keep the server bootable.

title: Access-token ID matcher rejects a matching grant and checks the wrong slice
body: isAccessTokenId is what the updated CODE_TO_TOKEN, refresh, device, and CIBA event assertions now use, but matchesSafely is inverted and off by one. Encoded IDs are six characters before the colon: session type at 0-1, token type at 2-3, grant type at 4-5 (for example onrtac:<uuid>). The check uses substring(3, 5), which is the last character of the token-type shortcut plus the first character of the grant shortcut, and returns false when that slice equals the expected shortcut. For a correct ID the wrong slice does not equal the expected shortcut, so the method falls through and only checks that the suffix looks like a UUID. Integration tests therefore pass for any <prefix>:<uuid>, including a wrong grant shortcut or the na fallback, and they never check session type or token type. A prefix shorter than 5 characters also throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException out of the matcher instead of failing the match. The condition needs to require a 6-character prefix and compare substring(4, 6) to the expected shortcut.

title: Constructor null-checks grantType twice and allows a null raw token ID
body: The fourth Objects.requireNonNull call passes grantType again, with the message "Null rawTokenId not allowed", instead of checking rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is stored. encodeTokenId then concatenates it, and Java string conversion turns that into the literal suffix "null" (for example onrtac:null). Every such token shares the same jti, so revocation, event correlation, and replay checks that key on token ID collapse together. The check must be Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...).

title: Grant shortcuts are not constrained to 2 unique characters, so issued IDs cannot be decoded
body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() is documented as "usually like 3-letters", but the encoder writes the shortcut as-is and getTokenContextFromTokenId requires the prefix before ':' to be exactly 6 characters (2+2+2) and throws IllegalArgumentException otherwise. postInit stores whatever getShortcut() returns and only compares map sizes, so a 1-character, 3-character, empty, or colon-containing shortcut still starts the server and is embedded in new access-token IDs. Those tokens cannot be parsed by the same provider. The lazy refresh in getShortcutByGrantType (around line 113) and getGrantTypeByShortcut is worse: on a cache miss it puts the new shortcut into both maps with no length check and no uniqueness check, so a hot-deployed grant can overwrite another grant's shortcut. Decoding then either throws or reports the wrong grant type. Validate at registration and on the lazy path that every shortcut is exactly two characters, contains no ':', and is not already mapped to a different grant; fix the javadoc to match.

title: Unset grant type is silently encoded as na on issuance paths this PR did not update
body: getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext treats a missing ClientSessionContext Constants.GRANT_TYPE attribute as the shortcut na, and encodeTokenId will persist that into the access-token jti. This PR only sets the attribute in OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse, the ROPC and pre-authorized grants, StandardTokenExchangeProvider, and the refresh path in TokenManager.validateToken. Other callers of TokenManager.initToken / createClientAccessToken are unchanged. Implicit and hybrid access tokens are issued from the authorization endpoint, not the token endpoint, and legacy token-exchange providers other than StandardTokenExchangeProvider are not in this diff. Those tokens are minted with grant shortcut na even though the grant is known. Once introspection or session lookup trusts the encoded grant (the stated reason for this change), those tokens take the unknown-grant path and the optimization is wrong. Every access-token issuance path needs to set the real grant, or initToken must fail instead of writing na for a request whose grant is known.

title: Decode error claims the whole token ID must be length 6
body: When the prefix before ':' is not 6 characters, the exception says Incorrect token id: '<full id>'. Expected length of 6. The full jti is a 6-character prefix plus ':' plus a UUID, so the message describes the wrong length and will send operators looking at the wrong field when decode starts failing requests.

title: Constructor null-checks grantType instead of rawTokenId
body: AccessTokenContext's constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") after already checking grantType, and never checks rawTokenId. A null raw token id is therefore stored. encodeTokenId concatenates it with ':', which Java turns into the literal suffix ":null", so every such token shares the same jti suffix and the guard the error message describes is not actually enforced.

title: Access-token id matcher checks the wrong slice and inverts the result
body: isAccessTokenId is what expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken, and expectAuthReqIdToToken now use to assert Details.TOKEN_ID. The encoded id is six characters then a colon: session type [0,2), token type [2,4), grant shortcut [4,6). The matcher uses items[0].substring(3, 5), which is the last character of the token-type shortcut plus the first character of the grant shortcut (for a normal id such as onrtac this is "ta", never the grant shortcut). It also returns false when that slice equals the expected shortcut, so a correct comparison would reject valid tokens. As written, any "<prefix>:<uuid>" passes regardless of grant shortcut, and a prefix shorter than 5 characters throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of failing the assertion. The new integration assertions do not actually verify the grant encoded into the access-token id.

title: Grant shortcuts are not required to be exactly two characters
body: postInit records each OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() with no length or character check, and the hot-deploy refresh in getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut does the same. The default encoder just concatenates session shortcut + token-type shortcut + grant shortcut, while getTokenContextFromTokenId requires the prefix before ':' to be exactly 6 characters and otherwise throws IllegalArgumentException. OAuth2GrantTypeFactory's javadoc says the shortcut is "usually like 3-letters", which contradicts that layout. A custom grant (or a future built-in) that follows the javadoc will still issue access tokens, but those jti values can never be decoded by the default provider, so the session/token/grant context this PR adds for introspection and similar endpoints is unusable and can surface as a runtime exception.

title: Access-token id matcher is inverted and slices the wrong characters
body: isAccessTokenId is what expectRefresh, expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, and expectAuthReqIdToToken use to check the new jti format. matchesSafely returns false when items[0].substring(3, 5) equals the expected grant shortcut, so a correct shortcut is treated as a mismatch. The slice is also wrong: the prefix is session (2) + token type (2) + grant (2), so the grant shortcut is substring(4, 6), not substring(3, 5). A default regular refresh token id is like onrtrt:<uuid>; substring(3, 5) is rt, which equals RefreshTokenGrantTypeFactory.GRANT_SHORTCUT, so expectRefresh fails on a correctly encoded token. For authorization-code (ac), device (dg), and CIBA (ci) the wrong slice does not equal the shortcut, so the inverted check never fires and those assertions pass even if the grant shortcut is wrong, as long as the suffix looks like a UUID. If the prefix is shorter than 5 characters, substring throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of failing the assertion.

title: Null raw token id is not rejected
body: The AccessTokenContext constructor is meant to reject a null raw token id, but the fourth requireNonNull checks grantType again (the message says "Null rawTokenId not allowed") and never reads rawTokenId. A null raw id is stored. encodeTokenId concatenates it with ':', and Java string conversion turns that null into the literal characters null, so the jti becomes something like onrtac:null. Those ids are not unique and will not round-trip to a real token id. The check must be Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...).

title: Grant shortcuts are registered without length or uniqueness checks
body: postInit and getShortcutByGrantType (around line 113) register shortcuts with an unconditional Map.put. A shortcut that is already mapped is overwritten, so decoding that two-character code returns the newly registered grant and previously issued access tokens are classified as the wrong grant. The size comparison that is supposed to catch duplicate ids or shortcuts runs only at the end of postInit; the hot-deploy path that reloads a newly deployed grant does not repeat it. Shortcuts are also not required to be exactly two characters, which getTokenContextFromTokenId assumes (6-character prefix, three slices of 2). A shortcut of any other length, including the 3-letter form described on OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut, is stored and encodeTokenId will emit it, but decoding that jti throws IllegalArgumentException. A null shortcut NPEs inside ConcurrentHashMap.put and can abort startup or token issuance. Registration should reject null, non-length-2, and duplicate shortcuts instead of overwriting.

title: getShortcut() is a new abstract SPI method with no default
body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() was added with no default implementation. DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit calls it on every OAuth2GrantType factory. An existing custom grant-type factory compiled against the previous SPI will throw AbstractMethodError during that call and prevent the server from starting, and will not compile against this interface until it is updated. A default that returns a reserved unknown shortcut (or skipping factories that cannot provide one) would keep old providers from taking down startup. The new javadoc on line 30 also says the shortcut is "usually like 3-letters", but the encoder only accepts exactly two characters and will not successfully decode anything else.

title: User-storage write payload cannot be read back as a recovery-code credential
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential tells user storage to persist only a JSON array of the raw recovery codes (UserCredentialModel challenge response). It drops generatedAt, the user label, and the hashed RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel that createFromValues already built. RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean and RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator then take the first federated credential of this type and pass it to RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel, which requires secretData in Keycloak's hashed schema. A provider that stores the updateCredential value and returns that CredentialModel (secretData null, credentialData = the raw JSON) — the same shape this PR's test storage saves, and the same pattern used for OTP — makes the login form throw while parsing, or throws after isValid already accepted the code, so recovery-code login never completes. Only the test provider papers over this by ignoring the stored model and calling createFromValues inside getCredentials.

title: Used federated recovery codes are not consumed or deleted
body: After credentialManager().isValid succeeds, this authenticator assumes the credential row was already updated and, when allCodesUsed() is true, deletes it with removeStoredCredentialById. That side effect exists only in the local recovery-code credential provider. For the new user-storage path, isValid is delegated to the storage provider and this method never writes the remaining codes back with updateCredential. removeStoredCredentialById only deletes credentials stored in Keycloak's database, not credentials owned by user storage, and the id on a federated model is not a local credential id. A correct storage that marks codes used therefore leaves an exhausted credential in place: isConfiguredFor stays true, the browser flow keeps challenging for a recovery code before required actions run, and the user is locked out once the last code is consumed. A storage that does not mutate state on isValid (as the new test provider does) leaves every code reusable forever, and the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES action is never added.

title: Reference user storage accepts any recovery code forever and stores them in plaintext
body: updateCredential saves input.getChallengeResponse() verbatim in credentialData, which is the JSON array of raw codes, not hashes. isValid then returns true if any stored code equals the input and does not remove the match or require it to be the next unused code. getCredentials ignores that stored model and calls RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues on the original list, which assigns a new id and marks every code unused. So the code index shown at login never advances, allCodesUsed() is never true, removeStoredCredentialById cannot target the real id, and a captured code can be replayed indefinitely. testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin only signs in once with code 0, so it does not catch replay, a stuck index, plaintext persistence, or failure to force regeneration.

title: Recovery-code login form throws if the federated credential is missing or incomplete
body: The constructor always calls credentialModelOpt.get() and RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel, then getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get(). getCredential now prefers getFederatedCredentialsStream() over local storage. If that stream is empty (storage accepted updateCredential but does not implement getCredentials), if the model has no secretData, or if every code is already used, rendering the recovery-code page throws NoSuchElementException or a JSON error instead of a challenge. Previously this bean only read local credentials created by the credential provider, which always had the hashed schema and a remaining code when the form was shown.

title: Recovery-codes feature is enabled without restarting the server
body: @EnableFeature(RECOVERY_CODES, skipRestart = true) only flips the runtime profile flag. RecoveryAuthnCodesAction, the recovery-authn-codes credential provider, and RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticatorFactory are environment-dependent factories whose isSupported() checks that feature and which are registered at server start. Without a restart they stay undeployed, so the new browser-flow execution and CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action do not run createRecoveryCodesCredential. The test can fail or not exercise the user-storage path at all. Omit skipRestart so the server restarts with the providers loaded.

title: Recovery codes are handed to user storage in plaintext
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential JSON-serializes the raw recovery codes and passes that string as the UserCredentialModel value to user.credentialManager().updateCredential. The local fallback still uses the recovery-code credential provider, which persists only hashes via RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues. When a user-storage provider accepts the update — including the new BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage, which stores input.getChallengeResponse() and later compares it with String.equals — the codes are stored and checked in cleartext. Recovery codes are bearer login secrets, so a read of that user-storage attribute or row is enough to authenticate as the user, and the hashing applied to locally stored codes is skipped entirely.

title: Federated recovery codes are never consumed and cannot be removed
body: One-time use for locally stored recovery codes happens inside RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.isValid, which marks the presented code used before returning true. If user storage reports that it supports recovery-authn-codes, credentialManager().isValid is delegated to that storage and the local provider never runs, so Keycloak never records which code was used. The only follow-up is removeStoredCredentialById, and only when allCodesUsed() is true. That call deletes a local credential by id; it does not update or disable a federated credential, and allCodesUsed() stays false when the federated model does not track usage. A code that just authenticated the user remains valid and can be replayed, and using the whole set does not remove the federated credential or reliably force reconfiguration.

title: Login form requires a credential model user storage was never given
body: RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean loads the credential through RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential, which prefers getFederatedCredentialsStream, then immediately calls Optional.get() and RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel. That parser needs credentialData and secretData in the hashed recovery-code format (algorithm, iterations, per-code hash, used flag) to compute the next code number. createRecoveryCodesCredential never writes that model; it only sends a JSON array of raw code strings. A provider that stores and returns that payload, or whose getCredentials default is empty, makes the optional empty or unparsable. Rendering the recovery-code page then throws NoSuchElementException or a JSON error even though isConfiguredFor is true, so the user cannot sign in. The same createFromCredentialModel call in RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator runs after isValid succeeds and turns a valid code into an error before context.success().

title: Storage double and new test never check one-time use
body: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid accepts a recovery code if it equals any stored raw code and does not delete or mark that code used. getCredentials then rebuilds a model with RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues, which hashes the raw list again and assigns a new id, so every read looks like a fresh unused set and the id does not match the credential saved in updateCredential. testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin only signs in once with code index 0 and asserts the credential exists in user storage. It never checks that the used code is rejected, that the next prompt advances, that a wrong code fails, or that the local fallback still stores hashes, so the test passes while replay and the login-form credential contract stay broken.

title: Recovery-code login form crashes when the credential lives only in user storage
body: After this change, recovery codes can be stored only in user storage (updateCredential returns true, so no local credential is written). The login form still does RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) and immediately calls Optional.get() / createFromCredentialModel. getCredential only sees a federated credential if the storage provider overrides CredentialInputUpdater.getCredentials(); the SPI default is an empty stream, and a stored raw JSON blob is not a RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel. configuredFor can still be true via isConfiguredFor, so the authenticator runs and rendering the challenge throws NoSuchElementException or a JSON parse error. Users whose storage follows the existing OTP pattern (updateCredential / isValid / isConfiguredFor only) cannot open the recovery-code page.

title: Successful federated recovery-code login is treated as an exhausted credential
body: On a valid code the authenticator now loads the credential via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential. If that Optional is empty — the normal case when user storage accepted the credential but does not return a full RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel — recoveryCodeCredentialModel stays null and the code unconditionally adds CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES. Every successful use of a user-storage recovery code therefore forces the user through setup again, even when codes remain. If getCredentials returns a non-conforming model, createFromCredentialModel throws and a code that already validated still fails the flow.

title: Last federated recovery code is never removed
body: When the reloaded model reports allCodesUsed(), the authenticator calls removeStoredCredentialById. That API deletes only local DB credentials. A federated credential id is not found there, so the call is a no-op and the exhausted credential stays configured in user storage (isConfiguredFor remains true). The test storage makes this worse: getCredentials rebuilds the model with RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues, which does not copy the id assigned in updateCredential, so even a federated-aware delete would target the wrong id. Users keep being prompted for codes that can no longer succeed, or keep an exhausted factor alongside the reconfigure required action.

title: User-storage recovery codes are cleartext and never consumed
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential JSON-serializes the raw code list into UserCredentialModel's challenge and hands it to updateCredential, discarding the already-hashed RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel used for local storage. Nothing in the success path writes an updated set back after isValid. Local codes are single-use only because RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.isValid removes the used hash and saves the credential; that provider is skipped when user storage returns true. The payload is a static JSON array with no used-flag, stored by the new test provider in credentialData (the non-secret field) and checked with anyMatch against every code. A storage compromise yields immediately usable codes, and the same code can be replayed until the set is replaced. Persist the hashed model (or an equivalent remaining-code structure), and consume the presented code inside the storage isValid implementation.

title: Test user storage accepts any recovery code and cannot revoke them
body: isValid deserializes the stored list and returns true if any entry equals the challenge. It does not require the next unused code and does not delete the code it accepted, so the integration test's single login cannot catch replay. disableCredentialType only clears OTP and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream only advertises OTP, so admin or account disable of recovery-authn-codes logs 'Unsupported' and leaves recoveryCodes set. getCredentials also NPEs if getMyUser returns null, and on success rebuilds a model from the original full list, so the code number never advances. This is the only storage implementation of the new contract, and it does not enforce single-use or revocation.

title: Concurrency test can pass without catching the NPE
body: createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti starts a reader thread and then immediately deletes every group and sets deletedAll before asserting caughtExceptions is empty, without joining the reader or ensuring it has entered groups(). On a fast run the reader may not be scheduled until after deletedAll is already true, so the loop never calls the admin API and the assertion passes without exercising GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount. If a list call is in flight when deletedAll is set, the main thread can also assert before that call throws and the exception is added to caughtExceptions, so a reproduced NPE is ignored. The regression test therefore does not reliably fail if the concurrent-delete NPE returns.

title: Reader thread shares the admin client and outlives the test
body: The background thread calls managedRealm.admin().groups() in a tight loop while the test thread deletes groups through the same admin client, and the thread is never joined, interrupted, or marked daemon. The Keycloak admin client and its JAX-RS/HTTP client are not safe for concurrent use, so the two threads can corrupt in-flight requests and produce exceptions unrelated to the cache NPE (or hide it). Because the thread is not stopped before the test method returns, it can still be issuing list calls against the shared realm while later tests run, causing cross-test interference or a non-daemon thread that keeps the suite from exiting if a request hangs.

title: Same concurrent-delete NPE remains on subgroup stream lookups
body: getSubGroupsCount() now treats a null modelSupplier.get() as a missing group, but getSubGroupsStream(String, Integer, Integer), getSubGroupsStream(Integer, Integer), and getSubGroupsStream(String, Boolean, Integer, Integer) still call modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) with no null check. modelSupplier is the same LazyModel around getGroupById that returns null when the cached group was deleted by another request. Those three methods are used by subgroup listing and search, so the same race still throws NullPointerException and fails the admin call instead of degrading. They need the same null handling (and should not assume the delegate is present).

title: Missing group makes getSubGroupsCount return null
body: When the persistence delegate has disappeared, getSubGroupsCount() returns null rather than a count. GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount writes that value straight into GroupRepresentation.setSubGroupCount, so a brief group list that races with deletion now succeeds but emits a null subGroupCount for a group that is still in the response. Callers that unbox GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() (comparisons or arithmetic) still NPE; a deleted group has no children, so this path should return 0L.

title: Concurrent group test can pass without observing the race
body: createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti starts a non-daemon reader, deletes the groups, sets deletedAll, and immediately asserts caughtExceptions is empty without joining the reader or checking that it ran. The reader can still be inside groups() when the assertion runs, so an NPE from that in-flight call is recorded only after the test has already passed; conversely the deletes can finish before the thread is scheduled, so the test passes without ever overlapping read and delete. The thread is also left running with the shared admin client into later tests. Join it (with a timeout) before the assertion, and fail if it never completed a read.

title: Concurrency test can pass or hang without observing the race
body: createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti starts a non-daemon reader thread and then asserts caughtExceptions is empty without joining that thread (or setting a timeout). deletedAll is set true as soon as the deletes return, so the assertion can run while a groups() call is still in flight and record its exception only after the assert, or the reader may not have overlapped the deletes at all. The test can therefore pass even when the concurrent list still returns 500. If any remove() throws before deletedAll.set(true), the reader stays in while (!deletedAll.get()) forever and, because the thread is not a daemon and is never interrupted, it can hang the suite and keep calling the shared admin client during later tests. The flag needs to be set in a finally, the reader joined with a timeout before the assertion, and the test should fail if the reader never actually ran during the deletes.

title: Same null delegate still NPEs on paginated subgroup reads
body: getSubGroupsCount now treats a missing persistence delegate as null, which is the concurrent-delete case this change is fixing. The three paginated overloads immediately below still do modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) with no null check (lines 256, 262, and 268). modelSupplier is the same LazyModel over getGroupModel(), so when the group has been removed it returns null and those calls throw NullPointerException. Any admin or session path that lists children with search or paging while the group is deleted still fails with 500, which is the same failure mode left unfixed.

title: Optimized paginator crashes on datetime audit-log keys
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key (paginator.py:840) runs math.floor/math.ceil on the order-by attribute, and value_from_cursor (paginator.py:843) returns the raw cursor integer. OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint wires this class in with order_by="-datetime" (organization_auditlogs.py:79-80). AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime, so any optimized_pagination request that returns at least one row raises TypeError inside build_cursor when it calls get_item_key, and the client gets a 500. A later request that supplies a numeric cursor also fails in build_queryset, which compares the timestamp column to an integer instead of converting the cursor the way DateTimePaginator does (milliseconds to a timezone-aware datetime). The new path is unusable for real audit logs; it needs DateTimePaginator's key conversion, not Paginator's numeric key logic.

title: Negative cursor offsets raise ValueError, they do not paginate
body: When enable_advanced_features is set and cursor.offset < 0, OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result slices the queryset with a negative start (paginator.py:880-882). The audit-log endpoint always passes enable_advanced_features=True. Django's QuerySet.__getitem__ does not support negative indexes and raises ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported"); it does not compile SQL or clamp the range. Cursor.from_string accepts a negative offset (for example "0:-5:0"), and that value is client-controlled, so an optimized_pagination request with such a cursor returns HTTP 500. The fallback branch (paginator.py:884-886) does the same for previous-page cursors. The comments that this reaches rows past normal pagination bounds, and that queryset permissions make that safe, are false: the call fails before a query runs. Negative offsets should be rejected with BadPaginationError, not sliced.

title: BasePaginator silently rewrites negative forward offsets for every list API
body: The new start_offset logic is in BasePaginator.get_result, which Paginator and DateTimePaginator share, so it changes cursor pagination for every endpoint, not just audit logs. For a non-previous cursor, a negative offset is rewritten to 0 and the first page is returned. Previously queryset[negative:stop] raised ValueError. Cursors are not clamped in Cursor.from_string, so a client can send "0:-1:0". build_cursor still derives the next offset from the original negative cursor.offset (offset + limit when the sort key is unchanged), so Link headers can keep publishing a negative offset and a client can loop on the same first page. Previous-page cursors still pass the negative offset through and 500. This is not a performance fix and should be reverted or turned into an explicit BadPaginationError.

title: No tests for the new paginator or the shared offset change
body: The PR adds OptimizedCursorPaginator, switches OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint to it when optimized_pagination=true, and changes slicing in BasePaginator.get_result, but no tests were added or updated. A request against the audit-log endpoint with optimized_pagination=true and at least one AuditLogEntry would have failed on the datetime TypeError; a cursor with a negative offset would have failed on Django's ValueError; and existing paginator tests do not lock the new BasePaginator behavior for negative forward offsets. Without those tests the 500 on the new admin path and the silent first-page rewrite on every cursor API can merge unnoticed.

title: Optimized paginator cannot order audit logs by datetime
body: The new optimized_pagination path instantiates OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime", but that class copies Paginator's numeric key handling. get_item_key (paginator.py around line 840) does math.floor/math.ceil on AuditLogEntry.datetime, which raises TypeError as soon as a page has any rows, so build_cursor fails and the request 500s. value_from_cursor also returns the raw cursor number and build_queryset binds it to the timestamp column, so a follow-up request with a cursor produces a timestamp-vs-integer SQL error instead of a datetime bound. DateTimePaginator already converts keys to millisecond timestamps and back to timezone-aware datetimes; this path does not, and cursors are not interchangeable with the default endpoint. Any org owner or superuser who passes optimized_pagination=true gets a broken audit-log API, with no performance benefit.

title: Negative-offset "advanced" pagination always raises
body: When enable_advanced_features is set (the audit-log endpoint always passes True) and the client cursor offset is negative, get_result slices the queryset with that negative start. Django QuerySet explicitly rejects negative indexes with ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported."), so this is an unhandled 500, not bidirectional paging. The comments claiming the ORM handles negative slices and that this safely reaches rows beyond normal bounds are false; the queryset is still the same organization-filtered set, and the slice never executes. Cursor.from_string already accepts a negative offset (for example "0:-1:0"), so any caller who can hit this paginator can force the 500. Other paginators raise BadPaginationError for negative offsets; this path should reject the cursor the same way instead of slicing.

title: BasePaginator now hides invalid forward offsets on every endpoint
body: BasePaginator.get_result is shared by Paginator and DateTimePaginator, so this is not limited to audit logs. For a non-previous cursor, a negative offset is silently rewritten to 0 and the page is returned from the start of the key-filtered queryset. Previously the same slice raised ValueError. A tampered or corrupted cursor such as "<value>:-5:0" therefore yields a real page that does not match the requested offset, and the next/prev cursors built from that page continue from the wrong position. Previous-page cursors still pass a negative offset through and 500, so the comment that this safely enables negative offsets is also wrong. Valid non-negative cursors are unchanged, but the global contract change should be reverted; invalid offsets need to stay an error.

title: No tests for the new paginator or audit-log flag
body: The PR adds OptimizedCursorPaginator, changes offset handling in BasePaginator, and branches OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint on optimized_pagination, but no tests were added. Coverage of a datetime-ordered audit queryset (first page and a cursor page), a negative cursor offset, and a normal DateTimePaginator request would have caught the TypeError on datetime keys, the ValueError on negative slices, and the silent clamp of forward offsets. Without those tests this can ship and 500 privileged audit-log reads while also changing pagination for every other BasePaginator endpoint.

title: Optimized paginator crashes on datetime audit logs
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key applies math.floor/math.ceil to the order-by attribute, and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor number. OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint uses this class with order_by="-datetime" whenever optimized_pagination=true and the caller is a superuser or has global access. Audit log rows are ordered by a datetime, not a number. On a non-empty first page, build_cursor calls get_item_key and raises TypeError because math.floor cannot accept a datetime. On any request that includes a cursor, build_queryset compares the timestamp column to that raw integer (DateTimePaginator converts via fromtimestamp and a multiplier; this class does not), which PostgreSQL rejects. The opt-in path therefore returns HTTP 500 for every organization that has audit log entries instead of a page of results.

title: Negative cursor offsets raise ValueError
body: When enable_advanced_features is true (the audit log endpoint always passes True), OptimizedCursorPaginator slices the queryset with the raw negative cursor offset. Django's QuerySet rejects negative slice start or stop with ValueError ("Negative indexing is not supported") before any SQL runs, so this branch never returns rows. Cursor.from_string accepts a negative offset, so a client that sends optimized_pagination=true and a cursor such as 0:-1:0 forces an HTTP 500. The comment that the ORM handles negative bounds, and that this reaches rows outside normal pagination limits, is false: the request errors, and the later trim check len(results) == offset + limit + extra would also be wrong for a negative offset if slicing were forced. The same false assumption was copied into BasePaginator.get_result, which now forwards a negative offset into queryset slicing for every is_prev cursor on all BasePaginator endpoints.

title: No tests for the optimized audit-log pagination path
body: The new optimized_pagination branch and OptimizedCursorPaginator have no tests. A request with audit log rows, or a cursor with a negative offset, 500s, which an endpoint test or a paginator unit test against a datetime queryset would have caught before merge. The shared BasePaginator slice change is also untested, so a regression there would hit every cursor-paginated endpoint, not just audit logs.

title: Optimized audit-log paginator crashes on datetime ordering
body: With optimized_pagination=true and a superuser or global-access member, OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint switches from DateTimePaginator to OptimizedCursorPaginator while still passing order_by="-datetime". OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does math.floor/math.ceil on that field. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime, so the first page that contains any rows raises TypeError while building the next/prev cursor. value_from_cursor also returns the raw cursor integer instead of a datetime, so a later page would compare a timestamptz column to an integer and fail in Postgres. The new path is unusable and has no tests; the default path is unchanged.

title: Negative-offset pagination raises ValueError
body: When enable_advanced_features is true (the audit-log endpoint always passes that), OptimizedCursorPaginator slices with the raw cursor offset if it is negative: queryset[cursor.offset:stop]. Django QuerySet rejects a negative slice bound with ValueError ("Negative indexing is not supported") before any SQL runs, so a cursor such as 0:-1:0 returns HTTP 500. Cursor.from_string already accepts a negative offset, so any caller who can set the query flag can trigger it. The comments claim the ORM handles negative offsets and that this reaches rows outside normal pagination bounds; it does neither, and it does not bypass the organization filter.

title: Global paginator now mishandles negative cursor offsets
body: BasePaginator.get_result is shared by every DateTimePaginator/Paginator list endpoint. It now uses max(0, offset) for non-previous cursors and passes previous-cursor offsets through unchanged. A normal non-negative offset behaves as before, but a next cursor with a negative offset used to error and now silently starts at 0, returning the first page instead of the requested window. A previous cursor with a negative offset is still handed to the queryset, and Django raises ValueError, 500ing the request. The new comment says the queryset handles negative offsets; it does not. This change is unrelated to span buffering.

title: Eviction is not atomic with insert and can empty a segment
body: Span payloads are ZADDed in a separate non-transactional pipeline, and add-buffer.lua never receives the payload or score, so it cannot insert them. The 1000-span cap is a later ZPOPMIN using a count observed inside that script. Redis serializes each script, but two writers can both ZADD past the cap and both compute span_count-1000 from the pre-pop size. ProcessSpansStrategyFactory runs process_batch in a multiprocessing pool when num_processes != 1, and those workers share shards; rebalance/spillover can also double-write a trace. Two scripts that each see 2000 members will each pop 1000 and leave the segment empty. The old set-based union did not delete members on insert, so this data loss is new.

title: Set-to-sorted-set switch breaks existing span-buffer keys
body: The buffer keys stay span-buf:s:{project:trace}:span_id, but the script and SpansBuffer now use ZADD, ZCARD, ZUNIONSTORE, ZSCAN, and ZPOPMIN. The previous code stored those keys as Redis SETs (SADD/SCARD/SUNIONSTORE/SSCAN). There is no new prefix, TYPE check, or migration. After deploy, every live segment is still a set until redis_ttl (default 3600s). ZADD or ZSCAN on it raises WRONGTYPE, process_spans fails, and the consumer retries the same batch for every in-flight trace. Flush fails the same way, so those segments are neither emitted nor deleted until the key expires.

title: ZUNIONSTORE SUM and self-union UNLINK drop or mis-rank spans
body: Merges use ZUNIONSTORE with the default AGGREGATE SUM. A member present in both inputs (Kafka redelivery, or the same payload written to both the parent key and a child key) gets its end-timestamp scores added, so it sorts as far in the future and ZPOPMIN evicts other spans instead. If the resolved set id equals the current span id, span_key and set_key are the same key: the script unions the key with itself and then UNLINK span_key, deleting the destination the preceding ZADD just wrote. That hits a non-root span whose parent_span_id equals its span_id, or whose redirect chain resolves to its own id. Those spans are gone before flush.

title: Redirect walk cut from 10000 to 1000 splits deep traces
body: The parent-redirect loop now stops after 1000 hops, and the comment that this limit fails to join deep segment trees was removed. On a longer chain the loop exits at an intermediate span id, then HSET persists that partial redirect (span_id -> set_span_id). Later spans follow the truncated mapping, so the segment is permanently split and flushed as incomplete pieces. Child-first arrival stores one hop per ancestor, so a trace nested deeper than 1000 spans hits this. The previous cap was 10000 specifically because of that correctness limit.

title: Hardcoded eviction can drop the root and the flush guard is gone
body: The cap is ZPOPMIN of span_count-1000 with a literal 1000. SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans (default 1001) is no longer consulted, so that constructor argument does nothing. ZPOPMIN deletes the lowest end_timestamp_precise scores with no exception for the segment root, so a root that ended before a child (clock skew or a longer child) is discarded and the flushed segment has no root span. The flush-time check in _load_segment_data that skipped segments over max_segment_spans and emitted spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded was removed, so if insert-time eviction does not run the consumer loads and publishes the whole segment up to the 10MiB byte limit. Evictions are not metered.

title: No tests for eviction, score order, or the new paginator
body: Buffer tests were only updated to supply end_timestamp_precise. Every case still uses four or five spans with the same timestamp, so CI never hits ZPOPMIN, never checks that the oldest spans are removed, never checks that the root is kept, and never covers WRONGTYPE on existing set keys or the concurrent double-pop race. The new audit-log OptimizedCursorPaginator path also has no test, so the datetime TypeError and the negative-offset ValueError would not fail CI.

title: Optimized paginator crashes on datetime audit logs
body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint (organization_auditlogs.py around line 79) switches to OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime" when optimized_pagination=true. OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does int(math.floor/ceil) on the ordering field, and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor number. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime, so the first page with any rows raises TypeError inside build_cursor. A non-zero cursor then builds a WHERE clause comparing a timestamptz column to an integer and fails in SQL. The new path is untested and 500s for every admin who passes the flag; DateTimePaginator already implements the correct key conversion and was the previous paginator.

title: Negative cursor offsets break pagination globally
body: BasePaginator.get_result now does start_offset = max(0, offset) unless cursor.is_prev, and the comments claim negative offsets are safe because the queryset handles them. Django raises ValueError on any negative slice, so a previous-page cursor with a negative offset still 500s. A forward cursor with a negative offset is silently clamped to 0 while build_cursor still does next_offset = cursor.offset + limit using the original negative offset, so the next Link cursor skips or repeats rows. This is on every BasePaginator endpoint, not just the new class. OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result (line 877) goes further and, when enable_advanced_features is set, passes the client-supplied negative offset straight into queryset[start:stop], which 500s. That flag is turned on for audit-log superusers/global-access members via a query param. Client-controlled cursors must keep rejecting negative offsets instead of clamping or slicing with them.

title: ZUNIONSTORE sums scores and evicts the wrong spans
body: The merge from sets to sorted sets uses ZUNIONSTORE with the default AGGREGATE SUM (lines 47 and 53). Span payloads are the members and end_timestamp_precise is the score. On Kafka redelivery, or any merge where the same payload is already in both keys, the scores are added. Later zpopmin (line 63) keeps the highest scores, so redelivered spans look newer than they are and genuinely newer spans are dropped once the segment exceeds 1000. Unions should use AGGREGATE MAX (or otherwise preserve the original timestamp) so eviction order stays the end timestamp.

title: In-place SET to ZSET change will WRONGTYPE on rollout
body: Segment keys stay span-buf:s:{project:trace}:span_id, but process_spans now ZADDs and the Lua script uses ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZPOPMIN, while flush uses ZSCAN. Existing keys are Redis SETs. During a rolling deploy, old consumers SADD/SUNIONSTORE/SSCAN and new consumers ZADD/ZSCAN on the same keys, and both get WRONGTYPE. Batches fail, segments already buffered cannot be flushed or merged, and keys sit until TTL. Ship a new key prefix or an explicit migration; do not reinterpret live SET keys as ZSETs.

title: Flush no longer enforces max_segment_spans
body: The incremental ZSCAN loader used to stop and drop a segment once it passed max_segment_spans (default 1001). That guard is gone, and the new cap is a hardcoded 1000 inside add-buffer.lua, not self.max_segment_spans, and it is not passed into the script. ZADD runs in a separate pipeline before the Lua eviction, and the flusher can run concurrently with workers, so a flush can observe a segment before zpopmin. The flusher will now load and produce the entire segment, which can OOM the consumer on a large trace. The byte-size check does not replace a span-count ceiling. Eviction also uses zpopmin with no exception for the segment/root span, so a root whose end_timestamp_precise is not in the top 1000 scores is deleted and the segment is flushed without a segment span. Restore a flush-time cap wired to max_segment_spans, and do not evict the root span.

title: Redirect walk cap lowered and still writes a partial redirect
body: The parent-redirect walk used to stop at 10000 with a comment that deeper segment trees would not be joined correctly. It now stops at 1000 and, on exhaustion, still HSETs span_id to whatever intermediate set_span_id it landed on and continues the merge. A chain or cycle longer than 1000 hops is silently attached to the wrong segment instead of being left unjoined or failed. If the cap is only a Redis-latency bound, the script should not persist a truncated redirect.

title: No test for insert-time eviction or score-preserving merges
body: Existing buffer tests only insert a handful of spans that share one timestamp and then sort flushed output by span_id. Nothing covers a segment larger than 1000, which scores zpopmin keeps, whether the root/segment span survives eviction, ZUNIONSTORE score behavior on redelivery, or flush of a segment that exceeds max_segment_spans. Those are the behaviors this change adds, and the current assertions would still pass if eviction dropped the wrong spans or the cap never ran.

title: Audit log GET always dereferences member.has_global_access
body: Every audit-log GET now evaluates `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` before pagination, even when `optimized_pagination` is absent. `organization_context.member` is an RPC member and can be null (for example a superuser is short-circuited, but any non-superuser request with no member object is not). `has_global_access` is a Django OrganizationMember property, not a field on the RPC member. If the attribute is missing or member is None, this raises AttributeError and the entire audit log endpoint returns 500 for ordinary callers.

title: Optimized paginator cannot order audit logs by datetime
body: When `optimized_pagination=true` and the caller is a superuser or has global access, the endpoint switches from DateTimePaginator to OptimizedCursorPaginator while still passing `order_by="-datetime"`. OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key (paginator.py around line 840) does math.floor/math.ceil on the model attribute. For AuditLogEntry that attribute is a datetime, so the first page that has rows raises TypeError while building the next cursor. value_from_cursor also returns the raw numeric cursor instead of a timezone-aware datetime, so any later page would compare a timestamp column to an integer and fail in Postgres. The new path is unusable for this endpoint.

title: Negative cursor offsets intentionally bypass pagination bounds
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator, enabled on the org audit-log endpoint by the client-controlled `optimized_pagination=true` query param plus `enable_advanced_features=True`, feeds a negative cursor offset straight into queryset slicing. The comments state this is meant to read data beyond normal pagination bounds. Other paginators in this file reject a negative offset with BadPaginationError; this one special-cases it. Django QuerySet slicing raises ValueError on a negative start, so the path 500s today rather than returning extra rows, but the client supplies the cursor (`value:offset:is_prev`) and a slice implementation that accepts negative indexes would return rows outside the cursor window. BasePaginator.get_result (line 182) was also changed so previous-page cursors keep a negative offset on every endpoint that uses it. This is an unrelated bound-bypass and should not be merged.

title: Set keys switched to sorted sets with no migration
