body: Span buffer keys `span-buf:s:{project:trace}:span_id` were Redis SETs (SADD/SUNIONSTORE/SSCAN) and are now sorted sets (ZADD here, ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZPOPMIN in add-buffer.lua, ZSCAN in _load_segment_data). The key format is unchanged and nothing deletes or converts existing keys. After deploy, any in-flight segment still stored as a SET makes those commands fail with WRONGTYPE, so process_spans errors and those traces are not buffered until the key expires (redis_ttl defaults to 3600s). A rollback is equally broken: once a new process ZADDs a key, the old SADD/SSCAN code also gets WRONGTYPE. Mixed-version deploys cannot drain the buffer.

title: ZUNIONSTORE default SUM corrupts end-timestamp scores
body: Merging segment keys now uses ZUNIONSTORE with the default AGGREGATE SUM (both the span_key merge at this line and the parent_key merge just below). Members are span payloads and scores are end_timestamp_precise, used later by ZPOPMIN to decide which spans to drop. Redis sums scores when the same payload is in both keys. That overlap happens on Kafka redelivery: the span is ZADDed onto the grouped parent key in process_spans and is still present in the previous segment key that this script unions in. The summed score is no longer an end timestamp, so eviction keeps the redelivered span and drops a different span whose real timestamp is older. SUNIONSTORE used to dedupe without changing identity. The union needs AGGREGATE MIN or MAX so the score stays a timestamp.

title: Insert-time ZPOPMIN can drop the root span silently
body: Once a segment sorted set exceeds 1000 members, the script ZPOPMINs the lowest end_timestamp scores down to 1000. The root/segment span is not protected, and the has-root-span flag is set independently of whether that payload is still in the set. A root that ended before its children, or any span that loses the score tie-break, is deleted and never flushed, while the segment still looks complete downstream and may still use the shorter root timeout. The flush-time guard in _load_segment_data that skipped segments over max_segment_spans (1001) and emitted spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded was removed, and the 1000 cap is hardcoded in Lua rather than passed from SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans. Oversized segments that miss this script (WRONGTYPE, script error, crash between the earlier ZADD and EVALSHA) are now flushed in full with no metric. Drops are silent.

title: Redirect walk cap cut from 10000 to 1000
body: The parent-redirect walk that finds the segment key used to run up to 10000 hops, with a comment that a chain past that limit would not be joined correctly. It is now 1000, and the comment is gone. Each span adds a redirect entry. A parent chain longer than 1000 stops early, hsets the new span to an intermediate id, and merges into the wrong set. Those spans are flushed as a separate or truncated segment instead of the real trace segment, with no error.

title: No coverage for eviction, score merges, or the new paginator
body: Existing buffer tests only insert a handful of spans, all with the same end_timestamp_precise, and still only assert the full segment is flushed. Nothing covers a segment over 1000 spans, ZPOPMIN dropping or preserving the root, ZUNIONSTORE score behavior on redelivery, or WRONGTYPE against a leftover SET key. The audit-log OptimizedCursorPaginator path and negative-offset cursor handling also have no tests, so the datetime crash and bound-bypass path would ship green.

title: Buffer docstring still describes Redis sets
body: The module glossary and the insert steps still say span-buf:s:* keys are sets and that payloads are added to a set. They are sorted sets scored by end_timestamp_precise, trimmed with ZPOPMIN. Operators debugging Redis or a flush incident will run SET commands (SMEMBERS/SCARD) and get WRONGTYPE, and the docstring no longer mentions that spans above 1000 are discarded on insert.

title: Allowlist option is never registered and is read on every stats query
body: Every events-stats execution calls is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects, which on a cache miss calls options.get("issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist", []). This PR never registers that option (no defaults.py or options change). Sentry's options manager raises UnknownOption for unregistered keys even when a default is passed, so a cache miss 500s the whole organization events-stats endpoint, including non-error datasets and projects that should not be upsampled. If a deployment's options.get instead returns the default, the feature never turns on in production; the new tests hide that by mocking options. The lookup also does `project_id in allowlist` with no int/str normalization, so a JSON allowlist of string ids never matches int project ids (feature silently off), and a non-list value raises TypeError on this same hot path.

title: count() is rewritten to a column string the field parser will not accept
body: When upsampling is enabled, count() is replaced with the literal "upsampled_count() as count" and passed as a selected column / y-axis. Sentry's field parser treats a column as a function only when the string ends with ')'; this value does not, so it is resolved as a raw column name rather than the new upsampled_count aggregate. Allowlisted error count() stats queries then fail field validation (or, if an alias were accepted, the result key would not stay the `count` field the events-stats contract and the new test expect). Charts, top-events, and any client requesting yAxis=count() for an allowlisted project break instead of returning an upsampled series.

title: Upsampled count sums sample_weight, but nothing stores the inverse sample rate
body: upsampled_count is toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) with no ifNull/coalesce. The only write-path change is the test factory, which copies contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate onto sample_rate (the rate itself, e.g. 0.1), not sample_weight, and production ingest is not updated at all. Events therefore have no sample_weight. ClickHouse sum of nulls is 0, so once the rewrite runs, allowlisted error counts become 0 instead of the real count or 1/sample_rate. That also cannot satisfy the new stats test, which stores client_sample_rate 0.1 and expects count == 10. toInt64 additionally truncates any fractional weight. Historical events and transactions that lack the column are zeroed or fail the query rather than falling back to count().

title: Errors dataset always upsamples, but upsampled_count is only registered on discover
body: _should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns True for the errors snuba dataset with no query check, and the endpoint then rewrites count() to upsampled_count(). The new aggregate is added only to the discover dataset function_converter in this PR. Errors timeseries uses its own query builder/config; if that config does not inherit this converter, allowlisted dataset=errors count() requests fail with an unknown function. The new snuba tests never pass dataset=errors (they rely on discover plus event.type:error), so this path is untested and can 400/500 the errors stats API.

title: Error detection is a substring match and treats negated filters as errors
body: _is_error_focused_query lowercases the raw query and returns True if it contains the substring "event.type:error". That matches !event.type:error, !(event.type:error), event.type:error OR event.type:transaction, and the token as a prefix of a longer value or inside a message/tag search. For discover queries on allowlisted projects, count() is then rewritten to sum(sample_weight) even when the query is explicitly not errors. Transaction and other non-error events do not have a reliable sample_weight, so those stats queries either error or return zeros/inflated mixed counts. A search parser check for a positive event.type:error condition is required; substring matching is the opposite of the stated caution.

title: Upsampling decision ignores the dataset and query actually executed
body: _get_event_stats decides upsampling from the closed-over request dataset and request.GET, not from scoped_dataset or the query argument. Dashboard widget splitting calls this helper with a different dataset and rewritten queries (errors-only "!event.type:transaction", transactions-only "event.type:transaction", and the original metrics dataset). A metrics/discover split therefore either skips upsampling on the errors subquery (outer dataset is not errors/discover) or, when the original request string looks like an error query, applies sum(sample_weight) to the transactions-only probe. Split detection uses those counts (has_errors / has_transactions), so widget discoverSplitDecision can be saved incorrectly, and transaction probes can throw if sample_weight is absent. The eligibility check has to use the dataset and query string passed into this call.

title: Top-events ranking still uses raw count() while the series is rewritten
body: For topEvents, only the timeseries y-axis list is passed through transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling. orderby still comes from get_orderby(request) and selected_columns from get_field_list, on both the RPC path (orderby around line 241) and top_events_timeseries (orderby around line 259). A request ordered by count() or -count() therefore ranks the top N groups by the sampled count while the returned series uses upsampled_count. Callers get the wrong groups, or the top-N query fails if it also references the rewritten alias. orderby and any count() in the top-N selected columns need the same transform as the timeseries columns.

title: Eligibility cache key uses process-randomized hash() and cannot be invalidated
body: The cache key is error_upsampling_eligible:{org}:{hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))}. Python hash() is salted per process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so workers do not share keys, invalidate_upsampling_cache deletes a different key than other processes wrote, and nothing in this PR calls that invalidator when the allowlist changes anyway. A collision of two project-id tuples in one process also serves the wrong eligibility for 60 seconds and rewrites count() for projects that are not fully allowlisted. Use a stable key (for example a sorted, joined id list) and hook invalidation to allowlist updates, or drop the cache; options.get is already an in-process read.

title: Every events-stats query now takes a remote cache round trip
body: is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects always cache.get's before it knows the dataset is errors. That helper runs on every _get_event_stats call, including transaction, span, and metrics queries, and dashboard split runs it several times per request. options.get of the allowlist is already served from the in-process options cache; this adds a shared-cache RTT (and a hard dependency on that cache) on the events-stats hot path to avoid a cheaper lookup. A slow or failing cache delays or fails unrelated stats requests. The allowlist check should happen only after the dataset/query gate, and should not require a remote cache.

title: Accidental gitlink committed at the PR base commit
body: This change adds sentry-repo as a gitlink/submodule pointer to a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a (the PR base) with no .gitmodules entry and no relation to upsampling. Clones and CI that recurse into submodules, or tools that refuse gitlinks, will fail or nest a second checkout of this repo. The gitlink should be removed before merge.

title: Accidental git submodule committed
body: This adds a gitlink named sentry-repo pointing at a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a (the PR base) and does not add a .gitmodules entry. Merging records a broken submodule in the tree that is unrelated to error upsampling. Checkouts and tools that resolve gitlinks will fail or pull an unintended nested repository.

title: Substring check treats negated and mixed queries as error-only
body: _is_error_focused_query returns true whenever the raw query string contains "event.type:error". That matches "!event.type:error" and "event.type:error OR event.type:transaction", so those discover queries are treated as error-focused. After every project is allowlisted, count() is rewritten to sum(sample_weight). Transactions do not have that column (or have it null), so a normal negated or mixed stats query either fails in Snuba or returns a wrong count instead of the raw count. The docstring says the check errs on the side of caution; a substring test does the opposite.

title: Upsampling uses the outer dataset and request query, not the query being run
body: _get_event_stats decides upsampling from the closed-over dataset and request.GET, ignoring scoped_dataset and the query argument it is about to execute. The dashboard-widget splitter calls this with rewritten queries such as "({query}) AND event.type:transaction" and "({query}) AND !event.type:transaction", and sometimes with the discover dataset while the outer dataset is a metrics dataset. A transaction probe therefore still rewrites count() to sum(sample_weight) whenever the original request looked like an error query, so check_if_results_have_data can see empty weights and save_split_decision persists the wrong discover split. The error-only probe does the reverse: it will not upsample unless the original query string already contained event.type:error, so split error widgets keep raw counts.

title: Eligibility cache key uses process-randomized hash()
body: The cache key is built with Python's builtin hash() of the project-id tuple. hash() is salted by PYTHONHASHSEED, so the same organization and projects produce different keys in different workers. The shared cache therefore does not reuse another worker's result, and invalidate_upsampling_cache deletes a key no other process wrote. Allowlist changes cannot be flushed, and the 60-second cache does not actually avoid repeated option lookups across the fleet. Build the key from a stable digest of the sorted project ids. This also adds a remote cache round-trip to every events-stats request, including spans and transactions that can never upsample.

title: Integration tests share a 60s cache and bypass the options mock
body: is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects caches allowlist eligibility for 60 seconds using only organization id and project ids. These tests reuse the same two projects and only change the mocked options.get return value, but a cache hit never calls options.get. After test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects stores True, the partial-allowlist and empty-allowlist tests still upsample and assert count == 1, so they fail whenever the test cache retains values (Django locmem does). setUp does not clear the cache, and the unit tests never call the cached function, so this path is untested and order-dependent.

title: sum(sample_weight) zeroes legacy events and truncates fractional weights
body: upsampled_count is toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) with no coalesce. ClickHouse sum skips nulls, so events stored before sample_weight was set contribute nothing: once a project is allowlisted, historical error buckets become 0 instead of the real count. toInt64 also truncates toward zero, so one event with weight 1/0.3 (about 3.33) is reported as 3, and a float sum of 9.999 becomes 9. Counts are silently low. Aggregate round(sum(ifNull(sample_weight, 1))) so missing weights still count as 1.

title: Factory writes sample_rate, query sums sample_weight
body: _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling copies contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate onto sample_rate (0.1 in the new stats tests). Nothing in this change sets sample_weight or stores the multiplier 1/client_sample_rate. The new aggregate sums sample_weight, and OrganizationEventsStatsErrorUpsamplingTest expects one stored event to count as 10. Summing a rate of 0.1 becomes 0 after toInt64, and a missing sample_weight column fails the query, so the test setup cannot produce the asserted result unless an unshown ingest step inverts sample_rate into sample_weight. The helper also runs for every store_event and overwrites an existing sample_rate whenever that context is present.

title: Error-query check is a substring match and false-positives on exclusions
body: `_is_error_focused_query` lowercases `request.GET['query']` and returns true if it contains the substring `event.type:error`. That matches queries that are not error-focused, including the common discover filters `!event.type:error` and `NOT event.type:error`, as well as `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`. For an allowlisted project on the discover dataset, those queries rewrite `count()` to `sum(sample_weight)`. Transaction rows often have no error sample weight (or a different transaction sampling weight), so the events-stats request either 500s in Snuba or returns wildly inflated transaction counts. The same check misses real error queries such as `event.type:[error]`. Nothing in the new tests covers a negated or list-form `event.type` filter.

title: Upsampled count sums sample_weight, which this change never writes
body: `upsampled_count` is `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` with no null fallback, and the column rewrite assumes every event in an allowlisted project has a meaningful sample_weight. Nothing in this PR sets that column. The only new writer is the test helper `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling`, which stores `sample_rate` equal to `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate` (0.1 in the snuba test) and never sets `sample_weight` to `1/rate`. ClickHouse `sum` skips nulls and `toInt64` of an all-null sum is 0, so events without a weight disappear instead of counting as 1. The new stats test expects each single stored event to become `count == 10`; that cannot happen unless an unshown pipeline converts sample_rate 0.1 into sample_weight 10. Allowlisted project charts will undercount or show zeros, including for historical events ingested before weights existed.

title: Top-events ranking still uses raw count() while the series is upsampled
body: When upsampling is on, only `timeseries_columns` / `y_axes` are rewritten to `upsampled_count()`. `top_events_timeseries` still receives `orderby=self.get_orderby(request)` and `selected_columns=self.get_field_list(...)` unchanged, and the RPC top-events path at the `orderby=` call just above does the same. Top-N selection therefore ranks groups by stored rows, not by `sum(sample_weight)`. With uneven client sample rates that ranking is wrong: a group with 100 real errors at 1% (1 stored row, weight 100) loses to a group with 10 unsampled errors (10 stored rows). The plotted series for the chosen groups is then upsampled, so the chart both picks the wrong groups and does not match the totals used to pick them. `equations` are also left as raw `count()`, so equation widgets diverge from the rewritten count axis.

title: Accidental gitlink added without a submodule config
body: This PR adds a gitlink `sentry-repo` pointing at commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a (the PR base) and does not update `.gitmodules` or any other file. That is not part of error upsampling. Merging it records a broken submodule: clones and CI checkouts have no URL for that gitlink, so the tree is dirty or the path fails to populate.

title: Allowlist cache key uses process-randomized hash() and can serve the wrong decision
body: Eligibility is cached for 60s under `error_upsampling_eligible:{org}:{hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))}`. CPython `hash()` is salted per process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so the key is not stable across gunicorn workers or between the getter and `invalidate_upsampling_cache`. Shared cache entries never hit across processes, and a delete on one worker cannot evict keys written by another; nothing in this PR calls the invalidator anyway. Within a process, a hash collision between two project-id sets stores one allowlist boolean for both, so a non-allowlisted query can be rewritten to `sum(sample_weight)` (Snuba error or wrong counts) or an allowlisted query can skip upsampling. The key also omits the allowlist contents, so a cached True survives option changes for 60s. The new snuba tests mock `options.get` to different allowlists for the same projects and never clear this cache, so a locmem/Redis hit makes `test_error_upsampling_with_partial_allowlist` and `test_error_upsampling_with_no_allowlisted_projects` assert raw counts while the helper still upsamples. `options.get` is already in-process; this extra `cache.get`/`cache.set` on every events-stats request, including spans and logs, is a hot-path regression and ties the endpoint to cache availability.

title: Errors dataset always rewrites count() but upsampled_count is only registered on discover
body: `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns true for the `sentry.snuba.errors` dataset with no query check, and the events-stats endpoint then asks that dataset to execute `upsampled_count() as count`. The new aggregate is added only inside `discover.py`'s `function_converter`. The errors dataset is a separate snuba module with its own query builder/dataset config; unless that config inherits this exact converter, `dataset=errors` requests on allowlisted projects fail field resolution or Snuba with an unknown function. The new tests never pass `dataset=errors` (they use the default dataset and one discover transaction query), so this path is untested.

title: Upsampling decision ignores the dataset and query actually executed
body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset` and `query`, but eligibility calls `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(..., dataset, request)`, using the closed-over request dataset and `request.GET['query']`. `get_event_stats_factory` then calls this helper with a different dataset and a rewritten query: the dashboard split path runs discover with `({query}) AND !event.type:transaction`, and sometimes `event.type:transaction`, while the outer dataset is metrics performance. Those internal queries are therefore classified from the wrong inputs. Error-only split queries on allowlisted projects are not upsampled, and any path where the outer request looks error-focused will also rewrite a later transaction-only execution in the same request. The comment that the cached decision keeps behavior consistent across query execution is the opposite of what this does.

title: Helper tests override setUp without calling super and will not run
body: `ErrorUpsamplingTest.setUp` does not call `super().setUp()`. Sentry's TestCase setUp is what creates `self.user`, `self.team`, and the rest of the factory state that `self.create_project` uses (`teams=[self.team]` when teams are omitted). This setUp will raise AttributeError before any assertion, so the new unit tests do not actually cover allowlist checks, column rewrite, or the event.type filter.

title: Transaction upsampling test does not wait for the event to be stored
body: `test_error_upsampling_with_transaction_events` calls `store_event` for a transaction and immediately queries events-stats, asserting the first bucket `count == 1`. setUp in the same class waits with `wait_for_event_count` after its error inserts, which is required because Snuba ingestion is not synchronous. Without that wait, the transaction is often invisible and the bucket is 0, so the test flakes and does not prove that transaction queries skip upsampling.

title: Suspect-issue PR comments call methods that do not exist on the workflow
body: get_merged_pr_single_issue_template calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title, but _truncate_title is defined on CommitContextIntegration, not on PRCommentWorkflow. PRCommentWorkflow is a separate workflow type that holds an integration; it does not gain that staticmethod. GitHubPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body and GitlabPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body also call self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template and self.get_environment_info, which were added only on CommitContextIntegration. Generating a merged-PR suspect-issue comment therefore raises AttributeError and the GitHub/GitLab comment workflow fails instead of posting.

title: Issue titles are interpolated into markdown links unsanitized
body: MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE places the issue title inside a markdown link label: [**{title}**]({url}). Issue titles are attacker-controlled error text and are only length-truncated, not escaped. A title containing ](https://evil.example) or a newline closes the link early and can inject extra markdown into the comment the Sentry bot posts on the customer's GitHub/GitLab PR. Environment names are likewise dropped into the comment in backticks with no escaping.

title: Flagged table widgets render an empty table instead of query results
body: When organization feature use-table-widget-visualization is on, WidgetCardChart renders TableWidgetVisualization with columns={[]} and tableData hardcoded to data: [] and empty meta, ignoring result.data, result.meta, fields, loading, and the dataset field renderer. Dashboard table widgets for that org show a blank grid instead of the widget query. columns={[]} also does not fall back to meta.fields, because TableWidgetVisualization uses columns ?? derivedColumns and an empty array is not nullish.

title: Error context is paired by dict value order, not node id
body: fetch_error_details loads nodestore blobs with get_multi(node_ids) and then zips error_ids with events.values(). get_multi returns a dict keyed by node id; value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, and backends that omit missing keys shift every subsequent pair. The summary sent to Seer can attribute the wrong title, message, and timestamp to an error id, or drop the wrong events via the data is not None filter. Lookups need to be events.get(node_id) for each id. Timestamps are also used raw in gen_request_data comparisons; a non-numeric nodestore timestamp (ISO string) raises TypeError and fails the whole summarize request.

title: Replay error lookup depends on date filters the client never sends
body: Every summarize request now calls get_filter_params and query_replay_instance before building logs, and process_raw_response is given request.query_params.getlist('field'). The replay AI tab requests /summarize/breadcrumbs/ with no start, end, statsPeriod, or field=error_ids. If get_filter_params rejects a missing range, the previously working summary 400s. If it defaults to a recent window, error_ids is empty for replays outside that window, so error context is silently omitted. A Snuba failure also 500s a path that previously only needed recording segments. error_ids must be requested explicitly and the replay's own time range used, not the caller's page filters.

title: Hidden span attributes are only removed while searching
body: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES (is_segment, project_id, received) is applied only inside the search filter branch. When searchQuery is empty the function returns sortAttributes(attributes) immediately, so those internal fields stay visible in the default attributes tree. They disappear only after the user types a query, including when the query would otherwise match them. The exclusion needs to run before the early return.

title: Feedback summary ignores environment (and search) page filters
body: useFeedbackSummary requests /feedback-summary/ with only the normalized datetime and selection.projects. The feedback list page is scoped by the page-filter environment selection (and the search box), but those are not sent. With an environment selected, the Seer summary describes all environments in the projects while the list shows one environment, so the summary does not match the data on screen.

title: Feedback list no longer fills the grid cell and will not scroll
body: The list grid area used to be a FluidHeight Container, which constrained height and scrolled the list inside the 1fr row. It is now SummaryListContainer, a flex column with no min-height: 0, overflow: hidden, or height: 100%. Grid items default to min-height: auto, so the column grows with the summary plus the full list instead of staying in the viewport row, and the inner FluidHeight percentage height does not resolve to the leftover space. The feedback list scroll pane breaks once the summary is shown.

title: Attribute key hook returns undefined after a failed fetch
body: The old hook always reduced the response into a TagCollection, so a failed request still yielded {}. The new hook returns useQuery data directly (attributes: isFetching ? previous : data) and dropped retry: false. On error, data is undefined and isFetching is false, so attributes becomes undefined. Explore callers that spread or index attributes (string tags, number tags, has-tag) will throw when the trace-item attributes endpoint fails. Default react-query retry (3) and refetchOnWindowFocus also replace the previous retry: false and refetchOnWindowFocus: false, multiplying load on that endpoint.

title: 60s deadline is too short for a 100-identity SSO refresh batch
body: check_auth_identities now has processing_deadline_duration=60 while check_auth still hands it up to chunk_size (100) identities. Each identity can do an external IdP refresh. check_auth stamps last_synced before enqueueing this task, so if the worker kills the task at 60s the remaining identities are not refreshed and will not be selected again until the next AUTH_CHECK_INTERVAL (about a day). SSO validity checks are skipped for the tail of every oversized batch.

title: AI summary treats an unloaded project as missing
body: Project is resolved with useProjectFromId({project_id: replayRecord?.project_id}), which is undefined both while the project list is still loading and when the project truly does not exist. The new branch returns 'Project not found' whenever project_id is set and project is missing, before the isPending check, and the summarize query stays disabled. Users hit a hard error (at least a flash, or a stuck error if projects never include that id yet) instead of waiting for the project store.

title: Age/timestamp mutual exclusion treats 0 as absent
body: validate_timestamp and validate_age use initial_data.get('age') and initial_data.get('timestamp') as booleans. Reporting API age of 0 (report just generated) and timestamp of 0 are valid integers allowed by the field constraints, but both are falsy, so a report that includes both is accepted. Neither field is required, so a report with neither age nor timestamp also passes even though each spec needs one of them.

title: Flagged table widgets render empty data
body: When organization.features includes use-table-widget-visualization, tableResultComponent ignores the widget result and renders TableWidgetVisualization with columns={[]} and tableData whose data, fields, and units are all empty. The real eventView, fields, metadata, and result.data stay on the old StyledSimpleTableChart branch. Enabling the flag therefore blanks every dashboard table widget instead of showing the query results.

title: Replay error context pairs the wrong events and timestamps
body: fetch_error_details zips error_ids with nodestore get_multi(...).values(). get_multi returns a dict keyed by node id and omits missing keys, so values() is not aligned with error_ids: a missing event shifts later payloads onto the wrong ids, and a non-preserving dict order mislabels every error. It also reads data['timestamp'] as a float and gen_request_data compares that to segment event timestamps. Stored events usually keep an ISO datetime (often under datetime) while rrweb segment timestamps are milliseconds, so the comparison either raises TypeError and fails the summarize request, or orders every error at the start of the log.

title: PR comment helpers are not on the workflow that calls them
body: GitHubPRCommentWorkflow and GitlabPRCommentWorkflow call self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template and self.get_environment_info, but both methods were added to CommitContextIntegration. The template helper then calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title, while _truncate_title is defined on CommitContextIntegration. PR comment workflows do not inherit the integration class, so building a suspect-issue comment raises AttributeError and the GitHub/GitLab comment task fails. Separately, MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE interpolates the title into a markdown link with no escaping, so a title containing ] (typical of exception messages) terminates the link and corrupts the rest of the comment.

title: AI summary treats a still-loading project as missing
body: AiContent now does useProjectFromId({project_id: replayRecord?.project_id}) and, before the pending check, returns an error alert whenever replayRecord.project_id is set and project is falsy. That hook returns undefined both while the project store is loading and when the project is actually missing, so the Replay Summary tab shows "Project not found" and never starts the summarize request until a later render happens to have the project cached. A genuine load is indistinguishable from a missing project.

title: Report age/timestamp validation accepts invalid combinations
body: validate_timestamp treats age as absent when initial_data.get("age") is falsy, so age=0 (a valid Reporting API value meaning the report was just generated) plus a timestamp is accepted. Field validators also never run when the field is omitted, and neither age nor timestamp is required, so a report with neither time field passes. post() then returns 422 for the entire batch on the first invalid item, so one bad report in a browser batch drops metrics for every valid report in that request.

title: Hidden span attributes are only removed while searching
body: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES (is_segment, project_id, received) is applied only inside the searchQuery branch. With an empty search the full sorted attribute list is returned, so those fields stay visible in the default span attributes tree. Searching cannot find them either, because the same filter drops them before the name match. If they are meant to be hidden, the exclusion has to run before the search filter, not only when a query is present.

title: Attribute key hook returns undefined after a failed fetch
body: useTraceItemAttributeKeys used to always build a TagCollection object (empty when the request failed or returned nothing). It now returns attributes: isFetching ? previous : data from useQuery. On error, isFetching is false and data is undefined, and the first fetch has no previous value, so attributes is undefined. Callers that spread or iterate attributes without a null check throw, and isLoading is tied to isFetching so background refetches also flip loading even when previous data is on screen.

title: 60s auth-refresh deadline skips identities for a day
body: check_auth_identities now has processing_deadline_duration=60, but it loops a chunk of up to 100 identities and each one can call the IdP via provider.refresh_identity. check_auth already sets last_synced=now before enqueueing this task. If the worker is killed at the deadline, unfinished identities are not refreshed and will not be selected again until the next AUTH_CHECK_INTERVAL (about 22–24 hours), so SSO linked/invalid flags stay stale.

title: Merged PR comment helpers are not on the workflow class
body: get_merged_pr_single_issue_template and _truncate_title were added on the class that owns get_top_5_issues_by_count (the class immediately above OpenPRCommentWorkflow), but the body calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title. GitHubPRCommentWorkflow and GitlabPRCommentWorkflow invoke self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template / self.get_environment_info. Those workflow classes do not inherit this class, and PRCommentWorkflow does not define _truncate_title, so posting a suspect-issue PR/MR comment raises AttributeError and the comment task fails.

title: Issue titles are interpolated into a Markdown link unsanitized
body: MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE wraps the raw issue title in [**{title}**]({url}). Issue titles are attacker-controlled error messages and routinely contain ] (for example foo[0] or KeyError paths). In CommonMark that closes the link label early, so the Sentry bot comment on GitHub/GitLab gets a broken issue link and can be turned into an arbitrary link or extra Markdown. Truncation to 50 characters does not remove ] or newlines. Escape or strip those characters before formatting.

title: Table widget flag renders an empty table instead of query results
body: When organization.features includes use-table-widget-visualization, WidgetCardChart renders TableWidgetVisualization with columns={[]} and tableData hardcoded to data: [] and empty meta. The actual result.data, result.meta, fields, loading state, and custom field renderers are discarded. An empty columns array is also truthy, so the visualization will not fall back to meta.fields. Any org with the flag on sees blank dashboard table widgets.

title: Error payloads are zipped to ids by dict value order
body: fetch_error_details loads nodestore rows with get_multi(node_ids) and then pairs them with zip(error_ids, events.values()). get_multi returns a dict keyed by node id; .values() is not guaranteed to follow error_ids, and omitted missing keys shorten the sequence. The summary can attach the wrong title, message, and timestamp to an error id, or drop errors. Look up each node id explicitly. timestamp is also passed through uncoerced: if the stored event timestamp is an ISO string, error_events.sort and the < comparison in gen_request_data raise TypeError and the summarize request fails.

title: Hidden span attributes are only removed while searching
body: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES (is_segment, project_id, received) is applied only inside the search filter. When searchQuery is empty the function returns the full sorted list, so those fields still render. As soon as the user types a query they disappear, including when the query would otherwise match them. The exclusion needs to run before the empty-search return so the attributes are always hidden.

title: Report time-field validation accepts missing and zero values
body: validate_timestamp and validate_age only run when that field is present, and both use initial_data.get(...) which treats 0 as absent. A report can omit both age and timestamp and still pass, even though the two Reporting API drafts require one of them. A report with timestamp set and age=0 (a valid just-generated report) skips the mutual-exclusion check, so both fields are stored together. The collector then metrics and logs structurally invalid reports instead of returning 422.

title: 60s deadline cannot finish a 100-identity auth refresh batch
body: check_auth marks up to chunk_size (default 100) AuthIdentity rows last_synced=now and then enqueues check_auth_identities. That task now has processing_deadline_duration=60 while each identity does a provider refresh over the network. If the worker kills the task at 60s, the remaining ids in the chunk are not refreshed, and because last_synced was already bumped they will not be selected again until the next ~24h cutoff. Auth sessions that should have been invalidated can stay valid for a day.

title: Trace waterfall container no longer fills its parent height
body: The wrapper that was FlexBox (display:flex, flex-direction:column, flex-grow:1, height:100%) was replaced with Flex direction="column" flex={1}. flex={1} is flex: 1 1 0, not flex-grow: 1, and height: 100% was dropped. The waterfall and its virtualized list size against this container, so the trace view can collapse or stop scrolling to the full viewport height.

title: Token exchange drops the redirect_uri used to obtain the code
body: OAuthLoginView always sends redirect_uri on the GitHub authorize redirect (built at the redirect just above), but the access-token POST only sends code, client_id, and client_secret. OAuth 2.0 requires that if redirect_uri was included in the authorization request, the token request must repeat that exact value; GitHub otherwise rejects the code with bad_verification_code or redirect_uri_mismatch. Every install then dies on the generic authenticity error after the user consents. The new tests stub the token endpoint and never assert the POST body, so they cannot catch this.

title: Installer check is skipped when the Integration row does not exist yet
body: The new GitHub-user check is the point of this change, but GitHubInstallation only compares pipeline state github_authenticated_user to metadata sender after an Integration row already exists and has no OrganizationIntegration. If Integration.DoesNotExist — the normal case when the browser returns with installation_id before the installation webhook is processed, or if the webhook never arrives — dispatch calls pipeline.next_step() immediately. build_integration never reads github_authenticated_user either, so the OAuth login is discarded. Any Sentry user who completes OAuth as themselves can still bind an arbitrary Sentry GitHub App installation_id (leaked or raced) to their organization and inherit that installation's repo access. The stated mismatch failure does not cover the path that actually creates the integration.

title: Sender lookup assumes metadata shape and 500s otherwise
body: After finding an ACTIVE Integration with no OrganizationIntegration, the code compares the OAuth login to integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] with no guard. This pipeline never writes sender (build_integration only copies state["sender"], which nothing in the new flow sets), and older rows may not have that key or may store a non-dict. A missing or malformed sender raises KeyError/TypeError instead of the installation error page, so re-link/reinstall of those installations 500s and the security check never returns a controlled failure. The same block also re-fetches with status=ACTIVE and turns a non-active Integration into the generic authenticity error, which is a behavior change from the previous re-link path.

title: Not-found install test never reaches the GitHub 404 path
body: test_installation_not_found no longer starts a pipeline via init_path. It hits setup_path with only installation_id (no setup_action=install), which PipelineAdvancer treats as no pipeline and redirects to / with "Invalid request.", then issues a second request whose state (ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05) is not the pipeline signature used everywhere else (9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3). That cannot exchange a code, cannot call the stubbed 404 installation endpoint, and cannot produce the old "The GitHub installation could not be found." error. The assertion was weakened to the generic authenticity string, so the 404 contract is untested and this test should fail or pass for the wrong reason.

title: User-mismatch test signs the pre-mutation webhook body
body: test_github_user_mismatch loads INSTALLATION_EVENT_EXAMPLE, sets sender.login to "attacker", then posts that modified JSON with the original hardcoded X-Hub-Signature sha1=d184e6717f8bfbcc291ebc8c0756ee446c6c9486. The HMAC is over the raw body, so it cannot match after the mutation. If signature verification is on, the webhook is rejected, no Integration sender is stored, and the later check for "Invalid installation request." is the same string OAuthLoginView returns for a bad state — so the test does not prove the OAuth login was compared to the installing user. There is also no case where sender login matches the stubbed octocat user and an already-existing Integration is allowed to proceed.

title: Installer identity check is skipped when Integration does not exist yet
body: GitHubInstallation.dispatch treats Integration.DoesNotExist as success and returns pipeline.next_step() immediately. That is the normal first-install path: the installation webhook often has not created the Integration row before the browser returns with installation_id, and build_integration then creates the Integration and OrganizationIntegration from the caller-supplied installation_id alone. The new comparison of the OAuth login to metadata sender.login only runs after an Integration row already exists and has no OrganizationIntegration. GitHub installation ids are enumerable and webhook delivery is not ordered ahead of the redirect, so an attacker can attach a victim's GitHub App installation to their own Sentry org (or finish the link before the real installer) without ever matching the installer. The control the PR adds fails open on the path it must cover. Finish should be refused until the installer identity is known and matches the OAuth user.

title: Sender comparison crashes when metadata has no sender.login
body: The new check reads integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] with no guard. build_integration only copies sender into metadata when pipeline state already contains it, and this pipeline never binds sender. Integrations created via the API path, or any row written before sender was stored, therefore have no sender dict. On the re-link path (Integration exists, no OrganizationIntegration, status ACTIVE) a missing or non-dict sender raises KeyError or TypeError. That exception is not caught, so the request 500s instead of the installation error page, and a legitimate reinstall of an integration without sender metadata cannot complete. Look up sender.login safely and fail closed with the authenticity error when it is absent.

title: Token exchange omits the redirect_uri sent at authorize time
body: OAuthLoginView adds redirect_uri to the GitHub authorize URL, but the access-token POST only sends code, client_id, and client_secret. GitHub requires the same redirect_uri on the token request when one was supplied during authorization; otherwise the token endpoint returns redirect_uri_mismatch and no access_token. That response is collapsed into the generic authenticity error, so every install fails whenever the authorize redirect_uri is not treated as the app's default callback. Tests stub the token endpoint and never observe this. Send the same redirect_uri on the exchange. The safe_urlopen call and the following get_user_info call are also outside the try that only wraps the body parse, so a connection error or ApiError from GitHub becomes an unhandled 500 instead of that error page.

title: installation_id is written into pipeline state before state is validated
body: OAuthLoginView bind_state's request.GET installation_id before it checks that state equals pipeline.signature, including on requests that have no state at all. PipelineAdvancerView is csrf_protect=False and auth_required=False, and until OAuth finishes the current step is still OAuthLoginView. A cross-site top-level GET to /extensions/github/setup/?installation_id=<attacker> therefore overwrites the victim's in-progress pipeline (SameSite=Lax cookies are sent on that navigation) and then redirects them at GitHub again. The real OAuth callback carries code and state but not installation_id, so GitHubInstallation keeps the poisoned id. A rejected callback has already mutated session state. Bind installation_id only after the OAuth state check succeeds, and do not accept it from an unauthenticated request that is not a completed callback.

title: Installation-not-found test now fails the state check and never hits the 404
body: test_installation_not_found still replaces /app/installations/{id} with a 404, but the follow-up setup request sends state=ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05. assert_setup_flow in the same file shows a valid pipeline signature is 9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3. OAuthLoginView rejects any other state before GitHubInstallation or build_integration runs, so the new assertion that the body contains "Invalid installation request." passes because of the state mismatch, not because a missing GitHub installation is handled. The old "The GitHub installation could not be found." assertion was removed, and nothing else drives get_installation_info's 404 path. A break there would not fail CI. Call back with the pipeline's real signature after a successful token exchange and assert the installation-not-found error again.

title: User-mismatch test mutates the webhook body but keeps the old HMAC
body: test_github_user_mismatch changes installation id and sender.login to "attacker" and then posts X-Hub-Signature sha1=d184e6717f8bfbcc291ebc8c0756ee446c6c9486, which cannot be the HMAC of the mutated body. If the webhook view verifies the signature, the post is 401, the assert status_code == 204 fails, and the Integration sender row the test needs is never created. If verification is off in tests, the signature is meaningless. The later assertion only looks for "Invalid installation request.", which is also returned for a bad OAuth state, a bad code, or a missing login. The setup URL reuses state 9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3 while init_path_2 starts a new pipeline for another organization, so a state failure produces the same page. The test does not show that an OAuth login differing from metadata sender.login is what failed. Recompute the signature for the mutated payload and assert something only the sender comparison path can produce.

title: Installer identity is not checked when creating the integration
body: The new GitHub-user check only runs after an Integration row already exists and has no OrganizationIntegration. If Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id) raises DoesNotExist, GitHubInstallation.dispatch returns pipeline.next_step() immediately, and build_integration never reads github_authenticated_user. installation_id is taken from the query string ahead of pipeline state, and the row is then created with the app JWT via /app/installations/{id}. Anyone who finishes OAuth as themselves can therefore still bind a victim installation_id that is not stored locally yet (webhook not processed or failed, or the Integration row deleted while the GitHub App remains installed). That is the hijack this change is supposed to stop: the attacker's Sentry org gets the victim's installation and repo access. Ownership has to be verified before the integration is created — refuse to continue when the installer cannot be matched, or confirm with GitHub that the OAuth user can access that installation_id — not only in the webhook-already-created branch.

title: Token exchange omits the authorize redirect_uri
body: OAuthLoginView puts redirect_uri on the GitHub authorize redirect, but the access-token POST only sends code, client_id, and client_secret. OAuth 2.0 (RFC 6749 §4.1.3) requires that same redirect_uri on the token request when it was included in authorization, and GitHub responds with redirect_uri_mismatch or bad_verification_code otherwise. The comment says this follows OAuth2CallbackView.get_token_params, which does send redirect_uri. Tests stub https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token to always return an access_token, so they stay green while real installs fail into the generic invalid-installation page.

title: Sender lookup crashes when metadata has no sender
body: Once no OrganizationIntegration exists, the code compares the OAuth login to integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] with no guard. build_integration only copies sender when pipeline state already has it, and this flow never writes github_authenticated_user into metadata. An ACTIVE Integration without a dict-shaped metadata.sender (older rows, or rows created by this pipeline) raises KeyError or TypeError instead of rendering the installation-failed page. The request 500s, and a missing sender is not treated as a failed authenticity check.

title: Installation-not-found test no longer hits the 404 path
body: test_installation_not_found stubs GET /app/installations/{id} as 404 and previously asserted "The GitHub installation could not be found." It now sends a follow-up setup request with state ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05, while every successful flow in this file uses signature 9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3. OAuthLoginView rejects that state before build_integration, and the test only checks for the generic "Invalid installation request." string, so a regression of the 404 handling still passes. Nothing asserts that a mismatched GitHub user is rejected when no Integration row exists yet, which is the branch that skips the new check.

title: AssignmentSource.queued is frozen at import time
body: AssignmentSource.queued is declared as `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`. Dataclass defaults are evaluated once when the class body is executed, not on each construction, and datetime is not a default_factory. Every AssignmentSource created via from_integration or from_dict without an explicit queued value therefore shares the single timestamp captured when the module was imported. The field is meant to record when that assignment change was queued and is copied into every outbound task payload via to_dict, but rapid successive assignee updates (the case this PR is fixing) are indistinguishable by time, and freeze_time in tests cannot affect it. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each source gets its own timestamp.

title: AssignmentSource dict is not a safe Celery payload
body: to_dict() is dataclasses.asdict, so the dict passed to sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async in sync_group_assignee_outbound includes queued as a raw datetime. That task previously accepted only ints, a bool, and None. A datetime is not JSON-serializable: under a JSON task serializer, apply_async raises TypeError while handling the inbound webhook, after GroupAssignee.assign/deassign has already written the assignee. The webhook then errors, linked integrations other than the source never get the update, and retries repeat the failure. from_dict is also not an inverse of to_dict: it splats the dict into the constructor and only catches TypeError/ValueError, so an ISO-string queued value is accepted as a str rather than parsed, and any malformed payload returns None. The outbound task treats None as "no source" and calls should_sync without a source, which re-enables the echo and brings the sync loop back. Eager task tests never cross this serialization boundary, so they do not catch it.

title: Cross-integration and deassign cycle behavior untested
body: The new test only assigns with AssignmentSource.from_integration on the same integration that owns the single linked external issue and asserts sync_assignee_outbound is not called. Nothing covers a second linked integration with a different id, which is the case the change claims must still propagate, so a regression that skips every outbound sync whenever any AssignmentSource is present would still pass. Inbound deassign now also threads assignment_source through GroupAssignee.deassign, but the deassign test still only expects assignment_source=None and never asserts that a matching source suppresses the outbound unassign. Both paths are required to stop the Jira assignee loop.

title: queued timestamp is fixed at import, not per assignment
body: AssignmentSource.queued uses timezone.now() as a dataclass field default. Dataclass defaults are evaluated once when the class is defined, not on each instance, so every AssignmentSource that does not pass queued shares one timestamp: the time this module was imported (the worker/web process start under a preload). The field is then copied into every outbound task payload via to_dict(). Rapid assignee changes, which this PR is meant to disambiguate, all get the same queued time, and any later staleness or ordering check on queued cannot tell them apart. Use field(default_factory=timezone.now). The new tests only assert queued is not None, so they do not catch the shared value.

title: Task payload includes a raw datetime and will not round-trip
body: to_dict() is asdict(self), so assignment_source_dict contains a live datetime under queued. That dict is the Celery kwargs for sync_assignee_outbound (sync.py, the apply_async call). Other arguments on this task are JSON primitives; a JSON Celery serializer raises TypeError when publishing a datetime, so the inbound webhook path (the only caller that sets assignment_source) fails inside GroupAssignee.assign/deassign before any outbound task is queued. Those methods do not catch the error, so the webhook errors and assignee updates are not propagated to other integrations either. from_dict() does cls(**input_dict) and does not parse an ISO string back into a datetime, and nothing calls from_dict(to_dict()) or json-round-trips the payload. Eager task tests bypass the broker serializer, so this stays green. Serialize queued with isoformat() and parse it in from_dict.

title: Cycle guard skips every linked issue on the source integration
body: should_sync returns False when sync_source.integration_id matches the target installation's integration, and AssignmentSource does not carry the external issue key that triggered the webhook. sync_group_assignee_outbound enqueues one task per GroupLink, but each task then drops outbound assignee sync for the whole integration, not just the ticket whose webhook just ran. A Sentry issue linked to two Jira (or other) issues on the same integration will update Sentry and never push the assignee to the other ticket. That echo is not required to stop the loop: an API update on the other ticket webhooks back, assign/deassign sees no assignee change (affected is false / nothing to delete), and outbound stops. The new test only links one external issue, so this regression is untested.

title: No test that a different integration still syncs outbound
body: test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration only asserts that the same integration's sync_assignee_outbound is not called. There is no case with a second linked integration (or a second external issue on another provider) that must still receive the outbound assign, and no matching deassign case. The guard is if sync_source and ids match: return False. A bug that skipped outbound whenever any AssignmentSource was present would still pass this test, which is exactly the non-regression the PR claims (other integrations must keep propagating). Inbound deassign now passes assignment_source too, and nothing asserts that a same-integration unassign does not echo.

title: AssignmentSource.queued is a single import-time timestamp and does not survive the task hop
body: queued is declared as queued: datetime = timezone.now() on a dataclass. That call runs once, when the class body is executed, not when each AssignmentSource is constructed, and it is not a field(default_factory=...). Every source built via from_integration() therefore shares one timestamp from process import, so distinct rapid assignee events cannot be ordered or deduped by queued. to_dict() then puts that raw datetime into the Celery kwargs of sync_assignee_outbound. A JSON task serializer turns it into an ISO string; from_dict() does cls(**input_dict) with no parsing and no runtime type check, and only traps ValueError/TypeError, so reconstruction succeeds with queued as a str. Nothing in the new tests round-trips to_dict() through from_dict(), so this ships uncaught. Cycle suppression still works today because only integration_id is read, but the timestamp this carrier was added to record is wrong both before and after the queue.

title: Same-integration guard skips every linked issue, not just the one that webhooked
body: should_sync returns False whenever sync_source.integration_id matches the installation's integration, before looking at which external issue is being updated. sync_group_assignee_outbound enqueues one task per GroupLink and each task applies that same check. A group linked to two issues on one Jira (or other) integration will therefore not push the new assignee to the sibling ticket after an inbound change. Previously every linked external issue was updated. AssignmentSource only stores source_name, integration_id, and queued, so the worker cannot skip write-back only for the issue key that fired the webhook. Sibling tickets keep a stale assignee until someone assigns the Sentry issue directly. A write to a different issue on that integration would not by itself loop if the mapped Sentry user is unchanged, because GroupAssignee.assign does not emit outbound sync when the user id does not change.

title: Tests never prove other integrations still sync, or that inbound wiring suppresses the echo
body: The new test only assigns with AssignmentSource.from_integration on the same single integration and asserts sync_assignee_outbound was not called. A regression that skips outbound sync whenever any assignment_source is set would still pass, and so would removing assignment_source= from sync_group_assignee_inbound. Nothing covers a second linked integration still receiving the outbound call, deassign with a matching source, or from_dict(to_dict()) preserving integration_id and a real datetime. Those are the behaviors this change claims to preserve or rely on.

title: Registered metric-alert handler is now uninstantiable
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler and implements none of its abstract methods (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data). It is still assigned as MetricAlertFire.detector_handler, and Detector.detector_handler instantiates that class with no try/except. Any detector whose type slug is metric_alert_fire will raise TypeError inside process_detectors and abort the whole batch. Previously this handler was concrete and evaluate() returned an empty result, so the same detector was a no-op instead of a crash.

title: Group-key evaluation test builds the expected occurrence with the wrong group key
body: TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds the expected IssueOccurrence via build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", ...), so its fingerprint is derived from group key "val1". The call under test is evaluate_group_key_value("group_key", 10, ...), and StatefulDetectorHandler passes that group key into build_occurrence_and_event_data, which fingerprints "group_key". IssueOccurrence equality includes fingerprint, so this assertion cannot pass. The value passed to the helper (6) also does not match the evaluated value (10).

title: Occurrence test helper ignores the evaluated value, so the new hook is not actually checked
body: build_mock_occurrence_and_event accepts value but never uses it, and MockDetectorStateHandler.build_occurrence_and_event_data just calls that helper. Every new assertion rebuilds the expected occurrence with the same helper, so a regression that drops or swaps the value argument still passes. The inputs already disagree with the expectations: test_state_results_multi_group feeds group_2=10 but expects an occurrence built with 6; TestEvaluate uses packet values 100 and 8 while expecting occurrences built with 6. Those tests therefore do not lock in the contract this PR adds.

title: evaluate() docstring still says it returns a list
body: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate now returns dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult], and process_detectors depends on .values() of that dict. The docstring still says it returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult, which will mislead callers that were updated for the signature change.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract and cannot be constructed
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler and only has `pass`, but StatefulDetectorHandler declares abstract `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Instantiating it raises TypeError. It is still wired as MetricAlertFire.detector_handler, and Detector.detector_handler does `group_type.detector_handler(self)` with no try/except in process_detectors, so any detector whose type resolves to metric_alert_fire crashes the whole batch. The previous handler was a concrete evaluate() that returned no results. Implement the abstract methods (even as explicit stubs) or keep it on DetectorHandler until the stateful implementation exists.

title: Group-key evaluation test expects the wrong occurrence
body: TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds the expected IssueOccurrence with group_key "val1" (and value 6) but calls evaluate_group_key_value with group_key "group_key" and value 10. The handler fingerprints the occurrence from the evaluated group key, so the returned DetectorEvaluationResult cannot equal that expected result. The assertion is wrong and will fail, and it does not lock the new build_occurrence_and_event_data inputs.

title: Expected occurrences are built with the wrong value
body: Several new assertions build the expected occurrence with a hardcoded value of 6 that is not the value under test: test_state_results_multi_group uses group_2=10 but builds occurrence_2 with 6 (and asserts that payload to Kafka); TestEvaluate.test_results_on_change evaluates 100; TestEvaluate.test_dedupe evaluates 8. build_mock_occurrence_and_event ignores value, so the tests pass without checking that the new hook received the packet value. A later change that includes value in the occurrence will fail for the wrong reason, and a bug that forwards the wrong value will not be caught. Build each expected occurrence with the same group key and value the code evaluates.

title: evaluate() docstring still says it returns a list
body: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate now returns dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult], which is the contract change in this PR, but the docstring still says it "returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult". Callers and subclass authors will follow the wrong shape.

title: Registered metric-alert handler is now uninstantiable
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is still the detector_handler for the registered MetricAlertFire group type, but it now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler and implements none of the abstract methods (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data). Instantiating it raises TypeError. Detector.detector_handler constructs the class on access, and process_detectors does not catch that error, so a single metric_alert_fire detector aborts processing for the whole batch. Previously this handler was concrete and evaluate() returned an empty list.

title: Occurrence hook cannot see the packet that fired
body: build_occurrence_and_event_data is the new extension point for emitting an issue, but it only receives group_key, the numeric value, and the new priority. The DataPacket being evaluated is not passed through, nor is the previous DetectorStateData. A detector-specific occurrence (for example a metric alert) needs subscription id, timestamps, and other evidence that exist only on that packet. Implementers must stash the packet on the handler during get_dedupe_value or get_group_key_values, which is implicit and will force a breaking signature change as soon as a real subclass is written. Pass the packet into the hook.

title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
body: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate now returns dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult], and process_detectors depends on that mapping, but the docstring still says it returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult. Callers following the docstring will iterate the dict keys (group keys) instead of the result values.

title: Group-key evaluation test builds the expected occurrence for the wrong key
body: TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds the expected IssueOccurrence with group_key "val1" (and value 6) but calls evaluate_group_key_value with group_key "group_key" and value 10. build_fingerprint includes the group key, and IssueOccurrence equality includes fingerprint, so the expected DetectorEvaluationResult cannot equal the value under test. This test fails and does not lock the new occurrence hook.

title: Occurrence helper ignores value, and several expectations pass the wrong one
body: build_mock_occurrence_and_event accepts value but never puts it on the IssueOccurrence or event_data, so equality cannot tell whether evaluate forwarded the measured value into build_occurrence_and_event_data. Call sites also pass a value that does not match the packet: test_state_results_multi_group feeds group_2=10 but builds the expected occurrence with 6 (line 191); test_results_on_change evaluates 100 but expects an occurrence built with 6 (line 490); test_dedupe evaluates 8 but expects 6 (line 510). A regression that dropped or swapped the value argument would still pass.

title: Occurrence context ignores the schedule_type display copy
body: get_monitor_environment_context copies monitor.config and, when schedule_type is present, replaces it with get_schedule_type_display() on that copy. The returned context then sets "config" to monitor_environment.monitor.config, the original dict, so the display conversion is discarded. Issue occurrences therefore publish the raw schedule_type integer (for example 0/1) instead of "crontab"/"interval". The returned dict is also the live in-memory config object, so any later mutation of the event context config mutates the cached monitor instance. Return the modified copy.

title: Incident opens without N consecutive failures
body: try_incident_threshold treats failure_issue_threshold as a lookback window, then opens an incident whenever none of those rows are CheckInStatus.OK. It never requires len(previous_checkins) >= failure_issue_threshold, and it does not require every row in the window to be a failure status (ERROR, MISSED, or TIMEOUT). A new monitor whose config asks for 3 consecutive failures still flips to ERROR and creates a MonitorIncident on the first failure, because the query returns one row and that row is not OK. A window such as [IN_PROGRESS, ERROR] with threshold 2 also opens an incident after a single real failure, since IN_PROGRESS is not OK. That creates issues and fires monitor_environment_failed before the configured consecutive-failure count is met. Require a full window of failure statuses before transitioning status and creating the incident.

title: Occurrence context ignores rewritten schedule_type
body: get_monitor_environment_context copies monitor.config and, when schedule_type is present, replaces it with monitor.get_schedule_type_display(). The dict it actually returns uses monitor_environment.monitor.config, not that copy, so the rewrite is discarded. Monitor incident events therefore keep the raw schedule_type (typically an int) instead of the display value the copy was built to provide, and the occurrence payload aliases the monitor's live config dict.

title: Failure threshold can open an incident before N consecutive failures
body: try_incident_threshold treats a monitor as breached once the most recent check-ins (at most failure_issue_threshold of them) contain no CheckInStatus.OK row. It never requires that window to actually contain failure_issue_threshold check-ins, and every non-OK status, including in-progress, counts as part of the streak. With failure_issue_threshold greater than 1, the first failure on a new monitor, a short history after old check-ins are gone, or a window that still includes in-progress rows will mark the environment ERROR, create a MonitorIncident, and emit issue occurrences. The monitor is then stuck failed even though the configured consecutive-failure count was never reached.

title: Issue context sends raw monitor config, dropping schedule display name
body: get_monitor_environment_context copies the monitor config and, when schedule_type is present, replaces it with get_schedule_type_display() so the occurrence payload has a readable schedule. The dict it returns ignores that copy and puts monitor_environment.monitor.config in the "config" field instead. Issue occurrences therefore still carry the raw schedule type (the integer choice), and the display conversion never reaches Kafka. Consumers of the monitor context will show the wrong schedule type.

title: join() can return without force-stopping flusher processes
body: SpanFlusher.join sets stopped and then calls next_step.join with the full timeout. If that consumes the budget, remaining_time <= 0 and the loop breaks without process.terminate() for every flusher process. close() intentionally does not stop these processes (to avoid a Redis memory spike at the start of rebalance), so join is the only force-stop path. Arroyo calls join with a finite timeout on shutdown and rebalance, and the consumer process stays alive across rebalance, so an un-killed flusher keeps flushing shards this consumer no longer owns. Those segments race the new assignee and are produced again to the buffered-segments topic. The wait is also sequential, so one slow process can exhaust the deadline and skip terminate() for the rest. The previous single-process join always terminated after the wait. After signaling stop, join must terminate and reap every process even when the timeout is already spent.

title: Restart overlaps two flushers on the same shards
body: _ensure_processes_alive SIGKILLs a hung flusher and immediately calls _create_process_for_shards without joining the old process. Process.kill() only sends the signal and returns, so the old process can still be inside flush_segments, Kafka produce, or done_flush_segments while the replacement starts flushing the same shard list. Both then read and clear the same Redis segments and emit them to buffered-segments, duplicating downstream data, and they also race on the shared backpressure_since and healthy_since values. The old Process object is dropped without being reaped, so each restart leaks a zombie until the consumer exits. The replacement must be started only after the previous process has actually exited.

title: Comma-joined shard metric tags break tag parsing
body: shard_tag is a comma-joined list of every shard a process owns and is emitted as a metric tag on spans.buffer.flusher.produce (key shard) and spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce (key shards). DogStatsD, which sentry.utils.metrics uses, treats commas as tag separators, so a value like 0,1,2 is parsed as extra tags and the series is dropped or attributed to the wrong tags. With the new CLI default --flusher-processes 1, one process owns every assigned partition, so this is the default path whenever a consumer has more than one partition. The value is also unique per partition assignment, so rebalances create a high-cardinality series. wait_produce uses the key shards while produce uses shard, so the two timers cannot be correlated. Emit a bounded process index, or one tag per shard, and use the same key.

title: Drift wait is a no-op, so the flusher test stays racy
body: test_basic patches time.sleep to a no-op, then calls time.sleep(0.1) to give the flusher thread time to observe current_drift after it is set to 9000. That call is the patched no-op, so it does not wait. step.join() immediately sets stopped, which can exit the flusher before it flushes, and (msg,) = messages then fails intermittently. The new multi-process test only checks process counts and never asserts that shards split across flushers are actually produced once. Patch sentry.spans.consumers.process.flusher.time.sleep instead of time.sleep, and wait until a message is produced.

title: Hung spawn-context flushers are never killed on Linux
body: Restart and shutdown treat flusher children as multiprocessing.Process before calling kill() or terminate(). Production processes are created with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, which yields SpawnProcess. On Linux that class is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process (the fork context class bound when multiprocessing is imported), so both isinstance checks are false. A hung flusher is therefore left running, and _create_process_for_shards immediately starts another process on the same shards. Both call flush_segments, produce to buffered-segments, and done_flush_segments, so segments are duplicated and Redis flush state races. healthy_since is reset on restart and then updated by the new process, so the hang detector will not notice the leftover process. The same check at join() (line 346) also skips terminate(), so a flusher blocked in Kafka future.result() is not stopped on shutdown. Use multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess, or exclude threading.Thread, instead of multiprocessing.Process.

title: Replacement flusher starts before the old process exits
body: After the restart path tries to kill a flusher, it never join()s that process or waits until is_alive() is false before _create_process_for_shards starts a new one for the same shard list. kill() only sends SIGKILL and returns. Until the old process is actually dead it can still be inside flush_segments or producing a batch it already read, while the new process reads those same shards and produces again. done_flush_segments then runs in both processes. That duplicates segments on the buffered-segments topic and races Redis cleanup. The old Process object is also dropped without join(), so repeated restarts leave unreaped children.

title: Join timeout abandons still-running flusher processes
body: join() gives next_step.join the full timeout, then walks flusher processes against the same deadline. As soon as remaining time is <= 0 it breaks out of the loop and never terminate()s the current or later processes. With more than one flusher, the first process can consume the whole remaining timeout in the is_alive() wait, and every other process is left running. Those children are daemon processes, so they keep flushing and producing until the parent eventually exits, which can kill them mid-produce before done_flush_segments. Shutdown should terminate every still-alive process after the deadline instead of breaking, and join() each of them so they are reaped.

title: Flusher metric shard tags are comma-joined and inconsistent
body: shard_tag is every shard id for that process joined with commas, and it is sent as a single tag value. The consumer flag defaults to one flusher process, so in production this value is the full assigned-shard list (for example "0,1,2,...,31"). DogStatsD encodes tags as comma-separated key:value pairs, so a comma inside the value splits the metric into garbage tags and drops or mis-attributes spans.buffer.flusher.produce and segment_size_bytes. The tag also changes with every partition assignment, so it cannot be aggregated per shard. wait_produce makes this worse by using the different key "shards" (line 199) while produce uses "shard" (line 185), so the two timers cannot be correlated. Emit one tag value per shard, or omit the tag when a process handles more than one shard, and use the same key on both timers.

title: Consumer test sleep cannot actually wait for the flusher
body: test_basic monkeypatches time.sleep to a no-op at line 15, then calls time.sleep(0.1) specifically to let the flusher thread observe the drift update before join(). That call is the patched no-op, so it does not yield or wait. join() sets stopped immediately; if the flusher has not yet flushed with the new drift, it exits and the assertion that one segment was produced fails intermittently. The production spawn/kill/join path is also untested: produce_to_pipe forces threads, so the SpawnProcess isinstance bug and multi-process flush behavior never run in CI. Wait with a real sleep saved before the patch, and cover at least one multi-shard flush plus process restart.

title: Spawn flusher workers are never killed or terminated
body: Workers are created with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, so they are SpawnProcess instances. SpawnProcess subclasses multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess, not multiprocessing.Process (the default-context class).
