body: Team and org authorization build `"teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})` and `"userId" = ANY(${userIds})` by interpolating a JavaScript array into Prisma.sql (lines 164, 168, and 201). Prisma binds that array as one parameter; through the query engine it is not a Postgres integer array, so PostgreSQL rejects the predicate (`operator does not exist` / invalid array literal) when these conditions are executed. User-scope SQL does not use ANY, and the only `$queryRaw` test is user-scoped, so the suite never runs the broken statements. Use `IN (${Prisma.join(ids)})` or an explicit `ARRAY[${Prisma.join(ids)}]::int[]` cast, and execute team/org conditions against the database.

title: findMany removed; condition types changed to Prisma.Sql
body: InsightsBookingService no longer exposes findMany(BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedFindManyArgs), and getAuthorizationConditions / getFilterConditions now return Prisma.Sql instead of BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedWhereInput. This PR only updates the service and its tests, so existing callers that pass a Prisma where/select into findMany, or that AND these conditions into a Prisma where object, will not compile and cannot query. Either keep a findMany wrapper that applies the SQL via $queryRaw, or update every caller in the same change.

title: Empty updateMany cannot bump SelectedCalendar.updatedAt
body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) to refresh SelectedCalendar.updatedAt after writing cache. Prisma rejects updateMany when data is empty ("data must not be empty"), and even if it did not, @updatedAt is only rewritten when some other field changes. This runs after the cache upsert, so a successful Google cache refresh still throws and the timestamp the new status UI depends on is never updated.

title: Deleting cache does not refresh connected-calendars data
body: deleteCacheMutation only toasts and calls the optional onSuccess prop. Unlike the disconnect mutation in the same component, it never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper passes onChanged through and does not refetch that query itself, so after a successful delete the dropdown still shows the old cache timestamp and "Delete cached data" until a full reload.

title: Cache status ignores expiry
body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups every CalendarCache row for the credential and returns max(updatedAt) with no expiresAt >= now() filter. Expired rows still produce a cacheUpdatedAt, so CredentialActionsDropdown treats the credential as having live cache (hasCache is just a truthy timestamp) and offers delete for data the availability path will not serve.

title: dev:cron now depends on undeclared tsx
body: dev:cron was changed from ts-node (a declared devDependency of @calcom/web) to npx tsx, but tsx is not listed in this package. yarn dev:cron will download an arbitrary tsx via npx or fail offline/in CI, instead of using the previously pinned local runner.

title: Env rewrite uses macOS-only sed
body: The new webhook helper updates GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL with sed -i '' , which is BSD/macOS syntax. On GNU sed that form treats '' as the script and does not edit the file in place, so the script reports success while leaving .env unchanged on Linux.

title: Empty updateMany does not bump SelectedCalendar.updatedAt and can throw
body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache now calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) specifically to refresh SelectedCalendar.updatedAt after writing calendar cache. Prisma only applies @updatedAt when the update payload changes at least one field; an empty data object is either a no-op (updatedAt stays stale) or an invalid updateMany invocation that throws. This runs on the Google webhook/cache-refresh path after the cache upsert, so a throw fails the refresh even though the cache write succeeded, and a no-op means the timestamp this change exists to maintain is never updated.

title: Deleting cache does not refresh connected-calendar status
body: deleteCacheMutation only toasts and calls the optional onSuccess callback. Unlike the disconnect mutation in the same component, it never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. The settings page passes onChanged through, which is often undefined and is not the connectedCalendars query. After a successful delete the dropdown still renders the previous cacheUpdatedAt and still offers “Delete cached data” until a full reload.

title: Backfill stamps every existing cache row as updated at deploy time
body: The new NOT NULL updatedAt column is added with DEFAULT NOW() and no backfill from a real write time. Every pre-existing CalendarCache row, including expired ones, gets the migration timestamp. getCacheStatusByCredentialIds then takes MAX(updatedAt) with no expiresAt filter, so the new UI shows “Last updated” as the deploy time and treats expired legacy cache as present for every credential that has ever had a row.

title: Webhook tunnel script is macOS-only and writes the wrong .env
body: sed -i '' is BSD sed syntax and fails on GNU sed (Linux). ENV_FILE is ../.env relative to the process cwd, not the script directory, so bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repo root creates or edits a .env outside the repository instead of the app env file. The script then reports success while GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL was never set where the app reads it.

title: No tests for cache deletion authorization or status query
body: deleteCache is an authenticated mutation that deletes every CalendarCache row for a credential after a userId ownership check, and connected calendars now depend on getCacheStatusByCredentialIds. There are no tests for a matching owner, a credential owned by another user, a missing id, or the groupBy status mapping (including expired rows). A regression in the where clause would either 500 the calendar settings page or let one user wipe another user’s cache with no CI signal.

title: Empty updateMany will throw after writing calendar cache
body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache finishes by calling SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(credentialId, {}). Prisma rejects updateMany when data has no fields ("data argument must have at least one field"), and @updatedAt is not applied unless an update actually runs. Every successful Google cache fill (webhook refresh and fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache) will therefore throw after the cache write, failing the caller and never bumping SelectedCalendar.updatedAt.

title: connectedCalendars query crashes when the user has no calendars
body: The handler always calls getCacheStatusByCredentialIds with connectedCalendars.map(cal => cal.credentialId). For a user with zero connected calendars that array is empty, and Prisma rejects credentialId: { in: [] } (empty IN lists are invalid). The connectedCalendars query, which this settings page loads with suspense, then errors instead of returning an empty list.

title: Deleting cache does not refresh cache status in the UI
body: deleteCacheMutation only toasts and calls the optional onSuccess prop. Unlike the disconnect mutation in the same component, it never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. The parent passes onChanged through but does not refetch that query, so after a successful delete the dropdown still shows the old "last updated" timestamp and "Delete cached data" until a full reload.

title: Migration stamps every existing cache row as updated now
body: updatedAt is added as NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(), so every pre-existing CalendarCache row is recorded as updated at migration time rather than when it was actually written. The new cache-status UI uses max(updatedAt), so all current Google calendar caches will appear freshly updated even if they are old or near expiry. The SQL comment also still claims the column has no default, which is the opposite of what the statement does.

title: dev:cron now depends on tsx, which is not installed
body: The dev:cron script was changed from ts-node (a declared devDependency) to npx tsx, but tsx is not in package.json. yarn dev:cron will either fail or pull an unpinned tsx via npx, so the local cron tester no longer runs from the repo's locked dependencies.

title: Webhook helper is macOS-only and writes the wrong env file
body: sed -i '' is BSD/macOS syntax and fails on GNU sed, so the script cannot update GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL on Linux. ENV_FILE is also ../.env relative to the current working directory, not apps/web/.env, so even a successful run does not update the env file Next.js actually loads and the tunnel URL is never used.

title: Immediate email cancel neither retries nor records cancellation
body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder with immediateDelete=true only POSTs a SendGrid batch cancel and then returns. It does not set WorkflowReminder.cancelled, nor delete the row. Reschedule (handleNewBooking.ts around the deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., true) call), workflow deletion, and step deletion all use this path. That is the same SendGrid cancel that this PR says fails once 100 pending cancellations exist, and a failure is only logged. Because cancelled is never set, the new cron will not retry those batches, so rescheduled-booking reminder emails still go out — the bug the PR claims to fix. On success the row is also left behind with cancelled unset, so nothing later clears the scheduled_sends entry except the send time.

title: Cron deletes due reminders before cancelling them at SendGrid
body: The handler first deleteMany's every EMAIL WorkflowReminder whose scheduledDate is already <= now, then looks up cancelled reminders to POST a SendGrid cancel. Any cancelled reminder whose send time has passed, or passes before the next run, is removed from the database in that first query and is never sent to /v3/user/scheduled_sends. SendGrid still delivers it. The later cancel query cannot see those rows. Cancelled reminders inside the cron interval (about 15 minutes) have the same hole: they are only cancelled once they fall in the next-hour window, so a booking cancelled shortly before the reminder still sends.

title: One failed SendGrid cancel aborts the rest of the batch
body: remindersToCancel is processed in a single try/catch. Each item awaits client.request with batch_id: reminder.referenceId and only then queues a delete. referenceId is not checked, and there is no per-item catch. The first 4xx/5xx (null batch id, already-cancelled batch, or the 100 pending-cancellation limit this PR is working around) jumps to the catch, skips Promise.all on the queued deletes, and never cancels later reminders in that run. If a poison row stays inside the one-hour window, every subsequent cron can fail at the same item and leave the other cancelled emails scheduled.

title: Reminder cancellation is not awaited before the handler returns
body: On booking cancel, deleteScheduledEmailReminder / deleteScheduledSMSReminder are started inside forEach and never awaited. The only thing that stops an already-scheduled email is the cancelled=true write inside deleteScheduledEmailReminder. The handler then awaits unrelated Prisma/calendar work and returns. On a serverless runtime the isolate can freeze after the response, so the update never commits and the cron never sees cancelled=true — the reminder is still sent. The same fire-and-forget pattern is in viewer/bookings.tsx requestReschedule and in handleNewBooking's reschedule block, whose try/catch cannot see those async failures because forEach does not await the promises.

title: immediateDelete cancels at SendGrid but never records cancellation
body: When immediateDelete is true, deleteScheduledEmailReminder POSTs a SendGrid batch cancel and returns without setting cancelled or deleting the WorkflowReminder row. Reschedule (handleNewBooking.ts) and workflow/step deletion (workflows.tsx) pass immediateDelete: true. A failed cancel — including the 100 pending-cancellation cap this PR exists to avoid — is only logged, so cancelled stays unset and the cron never retries; the email is still sent. A successful cancel of a far-future batch also parks a pending cancellation until the original send time, which is exactly what fills that cap. Those callers should mark cancelled (and let the cron cancel within the hour) or, on immediate cancel, delete the row and fall back to cancelled=true if SendGrid fails.

title: Reminder cancellation is not awaited before the handler returns
body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are fired inside forEach and never awaited (same pattern in handleNewBooking.ts around the reschedule loop and in bookings.tsx requestReschedule). The new design depends on the cancelled=true write (or the Twilio/SendGrid call) finishing before the API route returns. On serverless the process can freeze after the response, so the flag is never committed, the cron does not cancel the batch, and the reminder email/SMS is still delivered. The try/catch in handleNewBooking also cannot see those rejections because forEach does not await the promises.

title: Cron deletes due reminders before cancelling them at SendGrid
body: The job first deleteMany's every EMAIL WorkflowReminder with scheduledDate <= now, then only SendGrid-cancels rows still marked cancelled whose scheduledDate is within the next hour. A cancelled reminder whose send time has just passed (late or missed 15-minute run, or a send inside the cron interval) is removed from the database without POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends status=cancel. SendGrid still has the batch and delivers the email for the cancelled or rescheduled booking. Past-due cancelled rows need a SendGrid cancel before they are deleted.

title: One SendGrid cancel error aborts the rest of the batch
body: The cancel loop awaits each SendGrid request inside a single try, and only after the whole loop does it Promise.all the queued deletes. If any request throws (null referenceId, already-cancelled batch, or the pending-cancellation cap), the catch logs and exits: later reminders in that run are not cancelled, and deletes already pushed for earlier successful cancels never run. Those rows stay cancelled=true and will be retried, but a persistent error on one row blocks every subsequent reminder in the same cron invocation, so those emails still go out. Each reminder should be cancelled and deleted independently, and rows with no referenceId should be deleted without calling SendGrid.

title: Cancellation of workflow reminders is not awaited
body: On booking cancel, request-reschedule (bookings.tsx around the workflowReminders.forEach), workflow update, and reschedule (handleNewBooking.ts), deleteScheduledEmailReminder / deleteScheduledSMSReminder are started inside forEach and never awaited. This PR removed the previously awaited prisma.workflowReminder deletes, so the only record that a reminder must not be sent is the cancelled flag (or row delete) inside those async functions. Next.js ends the request when the handler promise resolves, which drops in-flight work. If that update or delete never commits, the cron still treats the reminder as active and SendGrid/Twilio still deliver the cancelled or rescheduled booking email or SMS.

title: immediateDelete bypasses the cancelled flag and does not retry
body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., immediateDelete=true) posts a SendGrid batch cancel and returns without setting cancelled or deleting the WorkflowReminder row. Reschedule (handleNewBooking), workflow delete, and step delete all pass true. That is the same immediate scheduled_sends cancel the PR says fails once 100 cancellations are pending, and a failure is only logged. Because cancelled stays false/null, scheduleEmailReminders will never retry the cancel, so those emails are still sent. On success the orphaned row also remains until scheduledDate passes.

title: One SendGrid cancel error aborts every pending cancellation
body: The cron loads every reminder with cancelled=true and scheduledDate within the next hour, then calls SendGrid and queues the row delete inside a single try around the whole loop. Deletes run only after every request succeeds. Any failure (null or stale referenceId, already-cancelled batch, rate limit) jumps to the catch, so no rows from that run are deleted and later reminders in the list are not cancelled. The next run hits the same already-cancelled or invalid batch first, throws again, and never reaches the rest. Those emails stay scheduled at SendGrid until send time, which is the original bug. Each reminder needs its own try/catch, a skip when referenceId is missing, and the row must be removed or left retryable even when SendGrid errors.

title: Cron still schedules reminders that were cancelled but not yet sent
body: After the cancel pass, unscheduled email reminders (scheduled=false, scheduledDate within 72 hours) are loaded with no filter on cancelled and no check that the booking is still ACCEPTED. Reminders that were never given a SendGrid referenceId are only removed by the un-awaited delete in deleteScheduledEmailReminder. If that delete does not commit, or a row is marked cancelled while still unscheduled, this loop creates a batch, sends the email, and sets scheduled=true. The scheduling query needs to exclude cancelled reminders and cancelled/rescheduled bookings before calling SendGrid.

title: Calendar/video cleanup is not awaited on reschedule
body: getCalendar is now async, but the new await sits inside bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...). forEach does not wait for those callbacks, and the surrounding try/catch cannot see rejections from them. Reschedule therefore marks the booking cancelled, sends the reschedule email, and returns true while calendar deleteEvent / deleteMeeting are still in flight. On a serverless runtime the process can freeze before those calls finish, so the old calendar event and meeting are left behind and failures become unhandled rejections.

title: Calendar/video cleanup is not awaited on reschedule
body: Same as the vital reschedule path: await getCalendar was added inside bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...). The caller never waits for those promises, so cancellation of the previous calendar event and video meeting races the email send and the function return. Errors from getCalendar or deleteEvent are not caught by the try/catch, and a short-lived request can exit before the external events are actually deleted.

title: requestReschedule does not wait for calendar or video deletion
body: requestReschedule now uses bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) so it can await getCalendar, then continues immediately to sendRequestRescheduleEmail and BOOKING_CANCELLED webhooks. The deleteEvent/deleteMeeting promises are never collected or awaited, so a reschedule can be reported as done while the previous calendar event and meeting still exist. Rejections from the dynamic import or the provider call are unhandled.

title: Recurring calendar deletes are pushed after the await set is already consumed
body: When cancelling all remaining occurrences, credentials are walked with forEach(async ...) and getCalendar is awaited before calendar.deleteEvent. The resulting promises are pushed onto apiDeletes only after that await. Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) later in the handler therefore often runs while apiDeletes is still empty, so those deletes are not part of the awaited set. The handler can return, and a serverless isolate can exit, before recurring calendar events are removed.

title: Every app import() starts immediately and can reject unhandled
body: Each import() is invoked while evaluating the appStore object, so loading this module starts every app package at once and does not load an app only when it is used. A rejection is only handled if some caller later awaits that specific key. Any app whose promise rejects before it is awaited (failed module, missing dependency) is an unhandled rejection and can crash the Node process, even for a request that never touches that app.

title: Recurring calendar deletes are no longer awaited
body: When cancelling all remaining occurrences, calendar credentials are still walked with forEach(async ...). getCalendar is now awaited inside that callback, and deleteEvent is only pushed onto apiDeletes after that await. forEach does not wait for async callbacks, so execution continues and later Promise.all(apiDeletes) often runs before those pushes happen. Recurring Google/Outlook/etc. events can therefore be left on the calendar while the handler still returns success, and a rejection from getCalendar becomes an unhandled rejection instead of failing the request. Collect the credentials with a for...of (as the non-recurring branch just below does) and push each deleteEvent promise before awaiting them.

title: Reschedule calendar cleanup is fire-and-forget
body: requestReschedule marks the booking cancelled and then calls bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) to await getCalendar and deleteEvent/deleteMeeting. forEach ignores the returned promises, and the mutation immediately sends the reschedule email and BOOKING_CANCELLED webhooks without waiting. Because getCalendar is now async, the external delete is not even started until after the import resolves, so a serverless handler can finish and freeze before the calendar or video event is removed. Errors from getCalendar or deleteEvent are also unhandled. Await Promise.all over the references (or a for...of) before sending email and webhooks.

title: Vital reschedule try/catch no longer covers calendar deletes
body: The try block uses bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) and awaits getCalendar inside the callback. forEach does not await that callback, so the surrounding try/catch cannot see rejections from the new async getCalendar (or from deleteEvent). The function then sends the reschedule email and returns true while calendar/video deletion may still be pending or may have failed. Replace forEach with an awaited Promise.all/for...of so failures are logged and deletes finish before the email is sent. The same pattern is in packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts at the matching forEach.

title: getCalendarCredentials now returns a Promise as calendar
body: getCalendarCredentials stays synchronous but stores the result of the now-async getCalendar without awaiting it. The exported calendar field is therefore Promise<Calendar | null>, which is always truthy, rather than Calendar | null. getConnectedCalendars in this file awaits item.calendar, but any other caller that treats calendar as a Calendar instance (calling listCalendars/createEvent, or checking null) will either skip a missing integration incorrectly or throw at runtime. The return type should be updated and every caller should await the promise, or this helper should become async and resolve calendars before returning.

title: Reschedule calendar/video cleanup is not awaited
body: getCalendar is now async, but the only call site wraps it in bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...). forEach does not wait for async callbacks, and the returned promises are discarded, so the try/catch around it never sees rejections from getCalendar or deleteEvent/deleteMeeting. Reschedule then sends the reschedule email and returns true while external calendar events and video meetings may still be deleting, or may fail as unhandled rejections and leave the old event on the calendar.

title: Wipe-my-cal reschedule cleanup is not awaited
body: Same as the vital reschedule path: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) awaits getCalendar only inside a callback that nothing awaits. Calendar deleteEvent and video deleteMeeting are not part of the function's control flow, the surrounding try/catch cannot handle their failures, and the handler can finish (and email the user) before those integrations are actually torn down.

title: requestReschedule does not wait for integration deletes
body: requestReschedule now awaits getCalendar inside bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...), which does not await the callback. deleteEvent/deleteMeeting promises are dropped, so the mutation proceeds to send the reschedule email and BOOKING_CANCELLED webhooks without knowing whether the old calendar event or video meeting was removed. Failures become unhandled rejections instead of failing the mutation.

title: Cancel-all recurring events never waits on calendar deletes
body: When cancelling all remaining instances of a recurring booking, credentials are walked with .forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent) }). The callback is not awaited, and deletedEvent is the resolved value, not a promise, pushed only after deleteEvent finishes. Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) later in the handler therefore runs before those pushes, so recurring calendar events are not reliably deleted and errors are not surfaced to the cancel request. The non-recurring branch just below was correctly converted to for...of; this branch was not.

title: Dynamic imports still load every app immediately
body: Each app is stored as import("./...") in an object literal, so every promise starts as soon as this module is evaluated. Any importer of appStore (calendar, video, payment, bookings) therefore kicks off a load of every integration at once. That does not defer unused apps, and it replaces one static graph with many parallel chunks that all start together, which can make cold starts slower rather than lazy.

title: Date override short-circuits busy checks
body: In checkIfIsAvailable, once any date override is deemed to fall on the slot's calendar day and the slot is not rejected as outside that window, the function returns true immediately. That return happens before the busy-interval loop, so bookings, calendar busy times, and buffers passed in as busy are ignored for every slot on a day that has a date override. Fixed-host and round-robin filtering both call this helper with the host's busy list, so a host can be offered (and booked) during an override window where they already have a conflict.

title: Any non-covering override rejects the slot
body: dateOverrides.find treats a callback return of true as "slot is unavailable". The callback returns true when the slot ends at or before that override's start or starts after that override's end. If a host has more than one override window on the same day (for example 09:00-10:00 and 14:00-16:00), the window that does not contain the slot makes find succeed and the function returns false, even when another window fully contains the slot. Multiple date overrides on one day, which the product supports, will hide valid slots.

title: All-day block override is never detected
body: The unavailable-all-day case is written as dayjs(start).add(offset) === dayjs(end).add(offset). Dayjs instances are never strictly equal, so this branch never runs. A date override stored with equal start and end (the usual "block this day" shape) therefore does not force the slot unavailable. Combined with the later dateOverrideExist return, that day can be treated as open instead of blocked.

title: Working-hours gate does not enforce the host's day
body: The new working-hours check only returns false when it finds a WorkingHours row whose days include slotStartTime.day() and whose range excludes the slot. If the fixed host has no row for that weekday, find returns nothing and the slot is treated as inside working hours. Also both start and end minutes are computed from slotStartTime, so a slot that starts inside the range and ends past workingHour.endTime is not rejected. Round-robin aggregate slots that exist because another host works that day still pass for a fixed host who does not.

title: Override day compare mixes local and UTC formatting
body: The override side is dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset).format("YYYY MM DD"), which formats in the process local timezone, while slotStartTime is time.utc() and formats in UTC. On any server whose local zone is not UTC, the same instant can format as different calendar days, so a fixed host's override is applied to the wrong day or not applied at all. Availability then depends on where the Node process is running.

title: Timezone offset wraps override times at midnight
body: Override start and end are shifted by inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset and then reduced with .hour() and .minute() only. Those accessors wrap at 00:00/24:00, so a negative or positive offset that crosses midnight turns an evening window into a morning minute-of-day (or the reverse) on the invitee's current day instead of the adjacent day. Large timezone gaps, which this change is meant to fix, still produce the wrong slots or drop the override.

title: New tests do not cover the stated fixes
body: The added assertion only re-queries a single-user event in Asia/Dhaka and expects the same UTC slot list as the IST case. It does not cover a round-robin event with a fixed host date override (the #8207 fix), a blocked day, multiple override windows, a busy time inside an override, or a timezone offset large enough to cross midnight. Those are exactly the paths the new checkIfIsAvailable and offset math get wrong, so this suite will stay green while those bookings are still incorrect.

title: Date-override window check rejects valid slots and accepts partial overlaps
body: checkIfIsAvailable treats a slot as outside the date override if it is outside any one override range on that calendar day. dateOverrides.find returns the first range for which the slot ends before the range start or starts after the range end, and the caller then returns false. With two ranges on the same day (for example 09:00-11:00 and 14:00-16:00), a slot fully inside the first range is still rejected because it is outside the second. The inverse is also wrong: a slot that only partially overlaps a range does not hit either outside-condition, so it is treated as inside. Fixed-host round-robin days with more than one override, or slots that stick out of the override, are therefore bookable or hidden incorrectly.

title: All-day block comparison never matches
body: The unavailable-all-day branch compares two Dayjs instances with ===. That checks object identity, not time, so dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...) is always false. A date override stored with equal start and end (the usual all-day unavailable marker) never takes this path and depends on the other window checks, which do not treat a zero-length range as blocking the whole day.

title: Override match returns available before busy times are checked
body: If any date override exists on the slot's calendar day and the slot was not rejected by the window checks, checkIfIsAvailable returns true immediately. Busy calendar events, existing bookings, and buffers passed in busy are never consulted. A fixed host who set a date override can therefore be booked on top of a meeting that falls inside that override, which is a double-booking.

title: Working-hours fallback treats days off and later ranges as available
body: When no date override matches, availability is decided with workingHours.find that returns true (slot rejected) only when some entry both includes slotStartTime.day() and does not contain the slot start. If the weekday is absent from every entry, find returns undefined and the function falls through to the busy check and can return true, so a fixed host's day off is still bookable in round-robin. If several ranges share that weekday, the first range that does not contain the slot makes find succeed even when a later range does contain it, so a slot inside a second interval is rejected. end is also computed from the slot start minute, not slot start plus event length, so a meeting that starts inside hours and runs past workingHour.endTime is accepted.

title: Override offset is reduced to clock time and can drop the range
body: After shifting the override by inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset, only .hour() and .minute() are kept. A shift across midnight is applied as minutes-on-the-same-invitee-day that passed the activeOverrides filter, so the window lands on the wrong clock time (and often the wrong date). If the end crosses midnight and the start does not, endTime becomes less than startTime and buildSlots skips the range with start >= end, so that date override disappears entirely for attendees in a timezone on the other side of midnight from the organizer.

title: New test does not cover fixed-host overrides or a real timezone shift
body: The added getSchedule call asks for Asia/Dhaka but expects the same UTC slot list already asserted for Asia/Kolkata, and it uses a personal event with no hosts. It cannot fail if fixed-host date overrides are ignored in round-robin, if an override day still ignores busy time, or if the offset math moves slots across a date boundary. The PR's stated fixes (#8207 / fixed hosts, timezone-adjusted overrides) ship with no assertion that would catch the checkIfIsAvailable regressions.

title: Override days skip busy checks and can double-book
body: In checkIfIsAvailable, once any date override falls on the same calendar day as the slot, dateOverrideExist is set and the function returns true as soon as the slot is not rejected as outside that override. That return happens before the busy-interval loop. Fixed hosts and round-robin hosts therefore look free for every slot inside an override window even when they already have a Cal booking or calendar conflict covering that time, so the booking page will offer times that cannot actually be taken.

title: All-day blocked overrides never match
body: A zero-length date override (start equal to end) is the usual way an organizer marks a day unavailable. The check compares two separately constructed dayjs objects with ===, which is reference equality and is always false, so that branch never runs. Combined with the early return when dateOverrideExist is set, a blocked day is treated as fully available instead of closed, and busy times on that day are also skipped.

title: Working-hours filter rejects valid fixed-host slots
body: The new working-hours gate uses slot start minutes for both start and end, so a slot that begins inside hours but runs past endTime is not detected. It also uses Array.find and treats the first same-day range that does not contain the slot as 'outside hours'. A host with two ranges on one day (for example 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-17:00) will fail the check for almost every slot, because each slot misses at least one range. Those slots are then removed for every fixed host, which can make an otherwise bookable round-robin event show no availability. Days with no working-hour entry are not rejected at all, so a fixed host can still be offered on days they do not work.

title: Override date match mixes server-local and UTC formatting
body: slotStartTime is a UTC dayjs, but the override side is dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset).format(...), which formats in the server's local timezone, not UTC or the organizer zone. The offset itself is also applied to an absolute instant and then compared with UTC slot instants. On any host whose TZ is not UTC, or when the organizer offset moves the override across midnight, the same-day test and the isBefore/isAfter window checks attach the override to the wrong day or the wrong clock times, so fixed-host overrides still do not constrain the slots the PR is trying to fix.

title: Timezone-adjusted overrides lose the day when they cross midnight
body: Override start and end are shifted by inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset and then reduced to hour() and minute() only. If the shift crosses midnight, hour() wraps to the other side of the day (for example 01:00 minus a 10h offset becomes 15:00) and the previous/next day is discarded. buildSlots then places that window on the invitee's current day. Attendees in a timezone far from the organizer see the override on the wrong date, or miss it, which is the timezone bug this change is meant to fix whenever the adjusted range is not on the same calendar day.

title: New test does not cover either bug the PR claims to fix
body: The only added assertion re-requests the same personal-event override in Asia/Dhaka and expects the identical UTC slot list. It never builds a round-robin event with a fixed host, never asserts that slots outside the fixed host's override disappear, and never checks that an override moves to a different invitee-local calendar day. A regression in checkIfIsAvailable or in the midnight-crossing offset math would still pass CI.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category is unset
body: The migration does execute(...)[0]['id'] on the embed_category lookup (and the same pattern for uncategorized_category_id). Site settings at their default are often not stored as rows, and a renamed or missing category also yields no row, so [0] is nil and the migration raises NoMethodError before the category_id == 0 fallback. Upgrading a typical site that never set embed_category fails and never creates embeddable_hosts.

title: Migrated hosts are not normalized and are interpolated into SQL
body: Existing embeddable_hosts values are inserted raw with string interpolation. The old allow-list stripped http(s):// and paths at compare time, and the new model only normalizes on validation, so values like http://example.com or https://example.com/path are stored verbatim. EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares lower(host) to URI#host, so those rows never match and embedding/import silently stops after upgrade. A host containing a quote also breaks the INSERT or injects SQL. Normalize (scheme, path, case) and use bound parameters.

title: Import passes category id through the category-name option
body: TopicEmbed.import now sets PostCreator's category: to eh.try(:category_id). The previous embed_category setting was a category name, and PostCreator's :category option looks up by name; the id belongs in category_id:. Imported embed topics will not land in the host's category (they fall through to uncategorized or fail the name lookup), which defeats the feature this PR adds.

title: Host allow-list comparison is case-sensitive on the referer
body: record_for_host queries lower(host) = ? but passes uri.host unchanged, and before_validation does not downcase the stored host. A stored host Example.com compared to a referer host example.com (or the reverse) does not match, so EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? rejects a host the admin saved. The same lookup is used for comment embedding and TopicRetriever, so those hosts cannot embed or import. Downcase both sides. Ports allowed by the format regex are also stored (example.com:8080) while URI#host omits the port, so those rows never match either.

title: before_validation crashes when host is nil
body: before_validation calls self.host.sub! without a presence check. Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host assigns params[:embeddable_host][:host] directly, so a create/update with a missing or null host raises NoMethodError instead of a validation error.

title: Update and destroy 500 when the host id is missing
body: update and destroy load EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and then call save_host(host) or host.destroy with no nil check. An unknown id raises NoMethodError (500) instead of a 404. save_host also does not check that the category_id refers to a real category, so a bogus id is persisted and later imports attach topics to a missing category.

title: Hydrating *_ids throws when the value is null
body: The new plural branch always calls obj[k].map and then deletes the *_ids key. Any rest payload with a null or non-array *_ids field (not just the fruit fixtures) throws during find/findAll and drops the raw ids even when lookup fails, so embedded has-many hydration can break unrelated models.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category is unset
body: The migration always does execute(...embed_category...)[0]['id'] and, if that is 0, execute(...uncategorized_category_id...)[0]['value']. Both settings are optional: embed_category is usually absent, and uncategorized_category_id is a hidden default that often has no site_settings row. An empty result makes [0] nil, so the migration raises NoMethodError and cannot be applied on a normal site.

title: Migrated hosts are not normalized and will not match
body: Existing embeddable_hosts values are inserted with raw SQL, skipping EmbeddableHost's before_validation stripping of scheme and path. record_for_host/host_allowed? compare URI#host (hostname only) to the stored column, so values previously saved as http://example.com or https://example.com/path no longer match and embedding breaks after upgrade. The same interpolation of '#{h}' is also not quoted, so a host containing a quote aborts the migration or injects SQL.

title: Host allow-list lookup is case-sensitive on the parameter
body: record_for_host queries lower(host) = ? but passes uri.host unchanged. Ruby's URI does not downcase the host, so a referer or embed URL like http://EvilTrout.com looks up lower(host) = 'EvilTrout.com' and fails even when the stored host is eviltrout.com. That rejects legitimate embeds and topic retrieval.

title: Nil or port-bearing hosts cannot be saved or matched
body: before_validation calls self.host.sub! without a nil guard, so create/update with a missing host raises NoMethodError instead of a validation error. The format regex also allows a port (example.com:3000), but host_allowed? compares only URI#host, which drops the port, so a saved host that includes a port never matches the referer.

title: Missing host update/destroy returns 500
body: update and destroy load EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and immediately call save_host(host) or host.destroy. A bad id yields nil and a NoMethodError (500) instead of a 404. save_host also assumes params[:embeddable_host] is present.

title: No uniqueness on host makes category assignment nondeterministic
body: embeddable_hosts has no unique index on host, and the model does not validate uniqueness. record_for_host uses an unordered .first, so two rows for the same host can assign imported embed topics to different categories depending on which row the database returns. Duplicate allowed hosts are also possible from the admin UI.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category is unset
body: The migration always does execute(... embed_category ...)[0]['id'] before checking whether a row exists. embed_category was an optional site setting, so most databases have no site_settings row (or no category whose name matches it). An empty result makes [0] nil and the migration raises NoMethodError, so upgrades that never customized embedding cannot run this migration. The same pattern on the uncategorized_category_id fallback (line 15) crashes if that row is missing.

title: Migrated hosts are not normalized and are interpolated into SQL
body: Existing embeddable_hosts values are inserted with raw SQL, bypassing EmbeddableHost's before_validation that strips http(s):// and paths. record_for_host compares URI#host (e.g. eviltrout.com) to the stored string, so previously working entries like "http://eviltrout.com" or "https://example.com/path" no longer match and embedding/referer checks fail after upgrade. The same statement interpolates the host inside single quotes, so a value containing a quote breaks the migration or injects SQL.

title: Allowed-host lookup misses case and port
body: record_for_host compares lower(host) to URI#host without downcasing the URI host, so a referer or embed URL whose host has any uppercase letters never matches a stored row. It also drops the port, while the host format validation allows :port and before_validation does not strip it. A saved host such as example.com:8080 can never be allowed, because the lookup host is only example.com.

title: Nil host raises instead of failing validation
body: before_validation calls self.host.sub! with no nil guard. create/update pass params[:embeddable_host][:host] straight through, so a missing host raises NoMethodError (500) rather than a validation error from render_json_error. record_for_host also returns false (not nil) when the URI cannot be parsed; TopicEmbed.import then calls eh.try(:category_id) on false, which raises instead of falling back to no category.

title: Update and destroy 500 when the id is missing
body: update and destroy load the row with where(id:).first and immediately call save_host or host.destroy. An unknown id leaves host nil, so the action raises NoMethodError instead of a 404. save_host also does not check that category_id refers to a real category, so an admin can persist a dangling category_id and later imports will create topics in a category that does not exist.

title: Host regex rejects valid hosts the old setting allowed
body: validates_format_of requires a dotted hostname whose final label is 2–5 letters. That rejects IP addresses, localhost, and real TLDs longer than 5 characters (for example .museum or .cloud). Those values could be stored in the old embeddable_hosts setting and are inserted by the migration without validation, but they cannot be saved or edited through the new admin API.

title: Plural id hydration assumes a non-null array
body: The new *_ids branch always calls obj[k].map. Any rest-serialized payload that includes a plural foreign key as null (rather than []) now throws while hydrating, which breaks find/findAll for that type. Previously only singular *_id keys were handled, and only when a match was found.

title: Second downsize definition overrides width/height API
body: Ruby keeps only the later `self.downsize` (line 149). The method defined at line 145, which builds a `#{max_width}x#{max_height}` geometry, is never callable. Existing callers that pass numeric width and height now hit the dimensions form, so the height integer is treated as `opts`. `opts[:allow_animation]` then raises NoMethodError, and even if that is avoided the geometry is a bare width with the height dropped. Thumbnail/downsize jobs that still use the old signature will fail or resize incorrectly.

title: ImageMagick convert reads and writes the same tempfile
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` is invoked with the upload tempfile path as both source and destination. `convert` opens the output before it finishes reading the input, so an in-place resize commonly truncates or corrupts the file (often to an empty or partial image). The upload is then stored from that same path via `Upload.create_for`, so users can lose the original and end up with a broken image instead of a downsized one. Downsize must write to a separate temp path and replace the upload file only after success.

title: Downsize failures are ignored and 80% geometry is wrong
body: The loop never checks the boolean returned by `OptimizedImage.downsize`. On failure the same file is retried until `attempt` hits 0, then `Upload.create_for` still runs. The geometry passed is `"80%"`, and `downsize_instructions` always appends `\>` (shrink-only), producing `-resize 80%\>`. ImageMagick does not treat that as a valid percentage shrink, so convert typically exits non-zero and the image is never reduced below `max_image_size_kb`. Oversized uploads therefore still fail, or a partially written file is saved.

title: Client size check ignores site settings
body: `validateUploadedFile` used to compare against `SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` and now always uses `10 * 1024`. Attachments are no longer limited by `max_attachment_size_kb`, and images are no longer limited by `max_image_size_kb`. If an admin set a limit below 10MB, the composer accepts files the server will reject; if the image limit is above 10MB, legitimate uploads are blocked client-side and the automatic downsize path never runs. The 413 handler at line 246 has the same hardcoded 10MB, so the alert text does not match the real limit.

title: URL downloads always capped at 10MB for every type
body: `FileHelper.download` previously used `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` and now always passes `10.megabytes`, before the code knows whether the URL is an image. Non-image API uploads ignore `max_attachment_size_kb` (larger attachments that the site allows are truncated/rejected at 10MB; smaller limits are not enforced here). Image URLs bigger than 10MB never reach the new downsize loop, so the feature does not cover the large remote images it is meant to shrink, and the cap cannot be configured.

title: ImageMagick downsize reads and writes the same path
body: OptimizedImage.downsize is called with tempfile.path as both the source and the destination. convert_with shells out to ImageMagick `convert` (and ImageOptim) with those paths. ImageMagick truncates the output file before it finishes reading the input, so using one path for both commonly yields an empty or corrupt file. The upload then proceeds with that damaged tempfile, so large-image downsizing fails or stores a broken image instead of a reduced original.

title: Second downsize definition overwrites the width/height API
body: Ruby does not overload methods. The new downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts) at this line replaces the downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) defined just above, so that width/height implementation is dead. Existing callers that pass numeric max width and height now treat the width as a geometry string and the height integer as opts. optimize then evaluates opts[:allow_animation] and raises NoMethodError, so thumbnail downsizing that still uses the old signature breaks.

title: Upload size cap hardcoded to 10MB for every type
body: validateUploadedFile used to enforce Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so images and attachments had separate admin-configured limits. It now always uses 10 * 1024. Attachments ignore max_attachment_size_kb (users can submit files the server should reject, or are blocked below a higher attachment limit). Images are also capped at 10MB even when max_image_size_kb is larger, so previously allowed uploads are rejected. displayErrorForUpload's 413 branch (line 246) has the same hardcode and will report 10MB even when the real limit is different.

title: Downsize result is ignored and may never meet the size limit
body: The loop calls OptimizedImage.downsize but discards its false return value, and -resize 80% changes pixel dimensions rather than targeting a byte size. If convert fails, the file is unchanged or corrupt and the loop still retries the same path. If it succeeds, five 80% passes (about 33% of each side) often leave a JPEG/PNG larger than SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb. The code then always calls Upload.create_for on whatever is left, so an upload that the client just allowed can still be over the configured limit or be a failed conversion, with no error from this step.

title: Animated GIF downsize is passed a percentage geometry
body: When SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails is on and the file is a GIF, downsize uses gifsicle --resize-fit with the geometry "80%". gifsicle's --resize-fit expects pixel dimensions such as WIDTHxHEIGHT, not an ImageMagick percentage. Those attempts fail (convert_with returns false), the bytes are not reduced, and animated uploads that are over max_image_size_kb are never actually downsized.

title: Second downsize definition overwrites the width/height API
body: Ruby does not overload methods, so `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` replaces the method defined four lines above that takes max_width and max_height. Any existing caller that passes numeric width and height (the previous public signature) now treats the width as the geometry string and the height as `opts`. `opts[:allow_animation]` then raises, and even a rescued failure returns false so thumbnails and other downsizes stop being generated. Keep a single method that accepts either a geometry string or two integers.

title: Downsize reads and writes the same tempfile path
body: The new loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)`. ImageMagick `convert` cannot reliably use one path as both input and output: it often truncates or replaces the file before the source is fully read, producing an empty or corrupt image. The upload Tempfile is already open, so a convert that writes via a new inode leaves that FD on the original bytes while `tempfile.size` and `Upload.create_for` still use the open file. Downsizing then either no-ops or stores the undownsized (or empty) image. Write to a separate temp path, replace the upload file only after success, and reopen/re-stat before `create_for`.

title: Percentage geometry is invalid for the animated downsize path
body: When the upload is a GIF and `SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` is on, `optimize` switches to gifsicle instructions (`--resize-fit` plus the dimensions argument). Those instructions expect a WIDTHxHEIGHT, but the new caller passes `"80%"`. gifsicle then fails, `downsize` returns false, and the loop ignores that return value and retries the same file five times. Animated uploads are never reduced and still hit the size check. The non-animated instruction also appends `\>` , so the geometry becomes `80%\>` rather than a plain percentage. Use a WxH target (or a percentage only on the convert path) and stop the loop when downsize returns false.

title: Client size check hardcodes 10MB for every upload type
body: `validateUploadedFile` used to read `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, so images and attachments each followed their site setting. It now always uses `10 * 1024`. Attachments are no longer limited by `max_attachment_size_kb`, and an admin who raised `max_image_size_kb` above 10MB will have the client reject files the server would accept. The 413 handler at the same file was also changed from `max_image_size_kb` to 10MB, so the error text no longer matches the configured or proxy limit. Only relax the client cap for images that the server will downsize, and keep the attachment setting.

title: URL fetches always allow 10MB, including non-images
body: API uploads that pass a URL used to download at most `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`. The cap is now a fixed `10.megabytes` for every type, and the later downsize block only runs when `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` is true. Non-image URL uploads therefore bypass the configured size limit and can pull up to 10MB even when `max_attachment_size_kb` is much smaller. Limit the raised cap to images that will actually be downsized, and keep the site setting for other files.

title: No coverage for automatic downsize-on-upload
body: The new upload path (five 80% passes, same-path convert, GIF vs still image, and what happens when the file is still over `max_image_size_kb`) has no tests in this change. A failure of convert, a stale Tempfile size, or an attachment accidentally included in the 10MB cap would ship unnoticed. Add controller or model tests for a still image that shrinks under the setting, a GIF with animation allowed, a downsize that returns false, and a non-image that must still obey the attachment limit.

title: Unsubscribe is a state-changing GET with no token
body: GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe immediately writes the current user's TopicUser notification level, and check_xhr is skipped so a normal browser navigation (and cross-site requests that send the session cookie) can hit it. Mail-security scanners and link prefetchers issue GETs on email links, and any site can embed the URL to mute or demote a logged-in victim's topic notifications without CSRF protection. The link in the email is exactly this URL, so opening or previewing the message can change notification state before the user chooses anything. Unsubscribe needs a non-prefetchable method (POST) and a user-bound token, or a confirmation page that does not mutate on GET.

title: Unsubscribe crashes when no TopicUser exists
body: unsubscribe loads TopicUser with find_by and then calls tu.notification_level and tu.save! with no nil check. Users who were emailed but have no topic_users row (or whose row was removed) get a NoMethodError instead of an unsubscribe. The action should create the row (TopicUser.change / find_or_initialize) and set the level, including the notifications_changed_at / reason fields that change() normally writes.

title: Watching and tracking users are not actually unsubscribed
body: If notification_level is above regular (tracking=2 or watching=3), the action sets it to regular instead of muted. Those are the users who receive per-topic notification mail, and the new email copy says the link will stop notifications for this topic. One click only demotes them to regular, so reply, mention, and quote mail can continue. A second click is required to mute, and nothing in the email says that. The link should set muted (or whatever level truly stops topic mail) in one request.

title: Unsubscribe template is not resolved for the new route
body: The Ember route is registered as topicUnsubscribe (path /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe), whose controller, route, and view are topic-unsubscribe. This template lives at topic/unsubscribe.hbs, which the resolver binds to a nested topic.unsubscribe route that was never defined. After the server renders the app shell, the client route has no template, so the confirmation copy and the topic-notifications-button never render. Move the template to topic-unsubscribe.hbs (or nest the route as topic.unsubscribe and point the URL there).

title: No tests for the unsubscribe action
body: The new endpoint changes notification level, redirects on slug mismatch, and is linked from every notification email, but the only spec change is passing unsubscribe_url into MessageBuilder. There is no coverage for missing TopicUser, watching vs regular vs muted, unauthenticated access, or the slug redirect. Those paths can 500 or leave the user subscribed without a failing test.

title: Unsubscribe is a GET that mutates notification level
body: TopicsController#unsubscribe is routed as GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe and immediately writes TopicUser.notification_level. Mail clients, link scanners, and antivirus gateways prefetch URLs in notification emails, so merely receiving or opening the message can change the recipient's topic notification level. The action is also not idempotent: a watching or tracking user is first dropped to regular, and a refresh or second prefetch then mutes them. State changes from an email link need a POST (or a single-use token) and must not keep downgrading on repeat requests.

title: Missing TopicUser crashes unsubscribe
body: unsubscribe does TopicUser.find_by(...) and then calls tu.notification_level with no nil check. Users can be emailed about a topic without an existing topic_users row (or the row can be absent for other reasons). Clicking the new email link then raises NoMethodError instead of unsubscribing, so the feature 500s for exactly the people the link is meant to serve. Use TopicUser.change, which creates the row when missing.

title: Direct save leaves unsubscribe reversible by auto-track
body: The new action assigns notification_level and calls tu.save! instead of TopicUser.change. change sets notifications_reason_id to user_changed and notifications_changed_at, and publishes the level change. A raw save leaves notifications_reason_id nil. update_last_read then auto-promotes the user back to tracking whenever total time viewed exceeds the auto-track threshold, silently undoing the unsubscribe on the next visit or timing update. The open topic UI also never receives the MessageBus notification_level_change.

title: Preloaded topic JSON still has the old notification level
body: TopicView is built before the TopicUser row is updated, and perform_show_response serializes that same @topic_view into the preloaded topic payload. The notifications control on the page therefore still shows watching/tracking/regular after the server has already changed the level. The user is told notifications have stopped while the button shows the previous state, and using that button can write the stale level back.

title: Watching users are not actually unsubscribed
body: If notification_level is above regular (tracking or watching), the action sets regular instead of muted. Watching is the level that emails every reply, and the new server string says the link will "stop receiving notifications about this particular topic." After one click a watcher is still at regular, so mentions and replies-to-you still notify, and the client copy ("You will stop receiving notifications") is shown unconditionally. Only a second request mutes them, which is not what the email promises.

title: Unsubscribe template is not registered for its route
body: The Ember route is declared as topicUnsubscribe (templates/topic-unsubscribe, controller topic-unsubscribe). This file lives at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs, which Ember resolves only for a nested topic.unsubscribe route. After the full-page load boots the app, the topicUnsubscribe route has no template, so the confirmation text and topic-notifications-button never render. Move the template to topic-unsubscribe.hbs (or nest the route under topic and point it at this template).

title: No coverage for the unsubscribe action
body: The only spec change passes unsubscribe_url into MessageBuilder and still does not assert that the topic link is rendered. There is no request/controller spec for TopicsController#unsubscribe: missing TopicUser, watching vs regular vs muted, repeat requests, slug redirect, or that the preloaded payload matches the saved level. Those paths are easy to regress and currently untested.

title: Unsubscribe crashes when no TopicUser row exists
body: TopicsController#unsubscribe loads the user's TopicUser with find_by and immediately reads tu.notification_level. If the recipient has never had a topic_users row (or it was deleted), tu is nil and the action raises NoMethodError instead of unsubscribing. The email link is therefore a 500 for that user, and no muted/regular level is stored. Create the row (TopicUser.change) or no-op safely when it is missing.

title: Level change skips TopicUser.change and does not actually stop watching
body: The action assigns notification_level and calls save! instead of TopicUser.change. That skips notifications_reason_id and notifications_changed_at. auto_track and update_last_read only keep a user-chosen level when notifications_reason_id is set; with it left nil, the next visit or auto-track promotes the user back to tracking, so the unsubscribe does not stick. Separately, watching/tracking (level > regular) is only lowered to regular, not muted, while regular is muted. Watching users still receive reply, mention, and quote mail, which contradicts the new email copy that this link stops notifications for the topic. A second GET then takes the else branch and mutes them, so refresh or a double click changes the level again.

title: Topic unsubscribe is an unauthenticated-token GET that mutates state
body: t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe and t/:topic_id/unsubscribe are GET routes with no per-user unsubscribe key, and TopicsController#unsubscribe writes notification_level as a side effect. Rails CSRF protection does not cover GET, so any site can mute or downgrade a logged-in victim for a known topic id with an img or prefetch of that URL. Mail-gateway link scanners that follow the link in an already logged-in browser do the same. One-click email unsubscribe needs a POST or a secret, user-specific token, and must not depend on an existing session cookie.

title: No specs for the unsubscribe action
body: The only test change passes unsubscribe_url into MessageBuilder and still only asserts that the preferences URL appears. Nothing covers TopicsController#unsubscribe: missing TopicUser, watching vs regular vs muted outcomes, notifications_reason_id being set, idempotent repeats, or the email string interpolating unsubscribe_url. Those paths are where this feature breaks, so the PR can merge with the action crashing or not sticking.

title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive and unnormalized
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? looks up the address with an exact equality match and never downcases or strips it. Mailbox providers treat the domain (and almost always the whole address) as case-insensitive, and signup stores whatever case the client sent (User.new_from_params assigns params[:email] raw, while change_email downcases). An attacker who is listed as blocked@evil.com can register Blocked@evil.com or " blocked@evil.com" and skip the block entirely. The unique index on blocked_emails.email has the same problem, so both casings can be stored as distinct rows.

title: Domain whitelist/blacklist regex is unanchored and barely escaped
body: email_in_restriction_setting? only escapes dots, then matches /@(#{domains})/i anywhere in the address with no end anchor. A whitelist of example.com therefore accepts user@example.com.attacker.com (and any other string that merely contains @example.com). The same pattern makes a blacklist miss or over-match, and any other regex metacharacter in the site setting (|, +, parentheses) is interpolated live, so a bad setting raises RegexpError and turns signup validation into a 500. This is the only enforcement of those settings after the check was moved off User.

title: Block check writes match stats during validation
body: should_block? increments match_count and saves the row as a side effect of validation. UsersController#create calls user.valid? and then user.save, and save validates again, so a matching do_nothing row is counted twice on every successful signup attempt. The increment is also a non-atomic read-modify-write, so concurrent signups lose updates. A failed or rolled-back user save still leaves the counter changed, because the BlockedEmail write is a separate commit. Stats and last_match_at cannot be trusted, and every email validation now does an extra write.

title: Moved domain rules and real block lookup are untested
body: EmailValidator is the new home of the whitelist/blacklist checks, but the spec only stubs BlockedEmail.should_block? and never exercises domain settings, case folding, or a real blocked row. The old User#email_validator tests were deleted with the method, so a whitelist bypass or a block that does not fire on User save would not be caught.

title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive and unnormalized
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? looks up the address with an exact BlockedEmail.where(email: email) match, and neither this method nor EmailValidator downcases or strips the value first. PostgreSQL's unique index is also case-sensitive, so a row stored as "bad@spam.com" will not match a signup of "Bad@spam.com" or " bad@spam.com". The block is therefore bypassed by trivial casing or whitespace changes, and the new blocked-email control does not actually stop the address it was meant to stop.

title: Domain allow/deny regex is unanchored
body: email_in_restriction_setting? builds Regexp.new("@(#{domains})") and tests it with =~, with no end anchor and with only "." escaped. A blacklist entry of "gmail.com" therefore matches "user@gmail.com.evil.test" as well as the real domain, and a whitelist entry likewise treats that host as allowed. Attackers can evade the domain blacklist (and pass a whitelist) by appending another label, so the restriction this validator is supposed to enforce does not hold.

title: Block check writes stats and is counted twice per signup
body: should_block? increments match_count and saves last_match_at as a side effect of validation, using a non-atomic read-modify-write. UsersController#create calls user.valid? and then user.save, and save validates again, so one signup attempt runs EmailValidator twice and advances match_count by 2. Concurrent attempts can also lose updates. last_match_at and match_count therefore do not record how many times the address was actually submitted, which breaks the statistic this table is added to track.

title: Block match stats are rolled back or double-counted
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? increments match_count and calls save while EmailValidator is running inside User validation. UsersController#create calls user.valid? and then user.save, so the counter is updated twice. user.save wraps validations in a transaction, and when the email is rejected that transaction rolls back the BlockedEmail write. With call_discourse_hub off, a real blocked signup therefore leaves match_count and last_match_at unchanged; with it on, only the outer valid? write sticks. The model specs call should_block? directly, so they never see this and the block statistics are wrong in production.

title: Blocked-email lookup is an exact, case-sensitive match
body: should_block? looks up BlockedEmail.where(email: email) with the raw address and no downcase or strip. Postgres unique/equality on string is case-sensitive, and nothing in User.new_from_params or EmailValidator normalizes the address before this check. A row for bad@spam.com will not match Bad@spam.com or " bad@spam.com ", so a blocked address can still register by changing case or adding whitespace. The unique index has the same problem, so both casings can be stored as separate rows.

title: Domain whitelist/blacklist regex is unanchored
body: email_in_restriction_setting? builds Regexp.new("@(#{domains})") after only escaping dots, with no end anchor and no escape of other metacharacters. A whitelist entry gmail.com therefore matches user@gmail.com.evil.test (and any longer suffix), so the signup is treated as allowed. A blacklist entry can also false-positive on addresses that merely contain that domain string after @. This is the only domain check on User now that email_validator was removed, and the new spec stubs should_block? and never covers it.

title: Embed template has invalid ERB and will not render
body: `<%- end if %>` is not valid Ruby, so compiling `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` raises a SyntaxError. Any request that finds an existing topic and renders the best-comments iframe (the success path in EmbedController#best) fails instead of showing the discussion.

title: Feed import crashes when an item has no content
body: `i.content.scrub` assumes every SimpleRSS item has a non-nil `content` string. RSS items commonly only set `description` (and Atom items can omit content), and `String#scrub` does not exist on Ruby 2.0, which this app still boots. The first such item raises NoMethodError, aborts the whole hourly poll, and also aborts TopicRetriever when it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute` on an embed cache miss. There is no per-item rescue, so one bad entry blocks every later item.

title: Imported HTML and embed URLs are stored and rendered unsanitized
body: `TopicEmbed.import` appends the source URL into an HTML footer via string interpolation (`<a href='#{url}'>`) and saves the body with `cook_method: raw_html`. `Post#cook` then returns that raw string unchanged, and the embed view prints it with `raw post.cooked`. Feed items never pass through Readability or Sanitize, so script tags, event handlers, and `javascript:` URLs in RSS/Atom HTML are stored as the topic's cooked HTML and execute for every forum viewer, not just the iframe. The URL check only requires an `http(s)://` prefix, so a quote or `>` in the link/query breaks out of the footer anchor as well.

title: open-uri fetch of attacker-influenced URLs enables SSRF
body: `import_remote` does `open(url).read` with no redirect limit, timeout, or address filter, and `PollFeed` does the same for `feed_polling_url`. Embed misses enqueue `RetrieveTopic`, which calls this after only comparing `URI(embed_url).host` to `embeddable_host`. `open-uri` follows redirects, so a URL on the allowed host (or a feed entry whose link redirects) can make the app server request internal addresses such as link-local metadata endpoints. The embed referer check does not constrain where that URL ultimately connects.

title: postMessage targetOrigin is a full referer URL, so resize never arrives
body: `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')` passes the parent page URL, including path and query. `postMessage` requires `*` or an origin (scheme, host, port only). Browsers reject a URL with a path, so the `discourse-resize` message is never delivered and the iframe in `embed.js` stays at its default height.

title: Every embed cache miss re-imports the entire feed
body: When `feed_polling_enabled` is on and the embed URL is not yet stored, `perform_retrieve` runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute`, which downloads the feed and calls `TopicEmbed.import` for every item, synchronously inside the retrieve job. That work is already scheduled hourly, is not bounded by the 60-second per-URL Redis throttle once the job has started, and uses a blocking `open` with no timeout. A slow or large feed stalls Sidekiq and can be triggered repeatedly by embed traffic for URLs that are not in the feed.

title: embed_url is limited to 255 characters
body: `t.string :embed_url` uses the Rails default varchar(255), and `topic_id_for_embed` looks up the full URL exactly. Article and feed permalinks with long paths or tracking query strings will fail the insert (or be truncated, then never match the original `embed_url`). Those pages stay on the loading iframe and are re-fetched forever instead of embedding.

title: Embed controller spec expects a call the controller does not make
body: The success example stubs `TopicRetriever.new` and expects `retrieve`, but `EmbedController#best` only calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`. As written the example fails, and nothing asserts that a job is enqueued, that `embed_url` is restricted to `embeddable_host`, or that the loading template is rendered. The poll-feed spec likewise never exercises `poll_feed` item parsing.

title: Embed template has invalid ERB and will not render
body: `<%- end if %>` is not valid ERB/Ruby (it must be `<% end %>`). Rendering `embed/best` raises a syntax error, so every successful embed that already has a topic returns 500 instead of the discussion iframe.

title: raw_html posts skip cooking and sanitization
body: When `cook_method` is `raw_html`, `cook` returns `raw` unchanged and never runs the normal pipeline or Sanitize. Feed and readability imports store that HTML as the post body (`TopicEmbed.import` sets this cook method and `skip_validations: true`). The embed view then emits it with `raw post.cooked`, and the forum will too. A feed item or fetched page can therefore inject script/markup that runs on the Discourse origin for anyone who views the topic or the embed.

title: Imported URL is interpolated into HTML unsafely
body: The imported-from footer builds `#{url}` from the source URL after only checking that it starts with http/https. A URL containing a quote or other markup (for example `http://evil.test/' onclick='alert(1)`) breaks out of the attribute. Combined with the raw_html cook path, that markup is stored and rendered as HTML.

title: Feed poll crashes when an item has no content
body: `i.content.scrub` assumes every SimpleRSS item has an HTML `content` string. RSS 2.0 items usually only have `description`, and `content` is nil, so the hourly job raises NoMethodError and imports nothing. `CGI.unescapeHTML` on that body also turns escaped markup (`<script>`) into live tags before it is stored as raw HTML.

title: postMessage targetOrigin is a full referer URL
body: `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')` passes the full referer (scheme, host, path, and query). `postMessage` requires an origin (`scheme://host[:port]`) or `*`. A path-bearing referer throws, so the parent never receives `discourse-resize` and the iframe stays at its default height.

title: Resize messages accepted from any origin that is a substring of discourseUrl
body: The check is `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`, not an equality check against the forum origin. Any `e.origin` that appears inside `discourseUrl` is trusted. For example `http://localhost` matches `http://localhost:3000`, and a short prefix such as `https://forum` matches `https://forum.example.com`. A page on that origin can post a `discourse-resize` message and set the iframe height.

title: Embed controller spec expects a retriever the action never calls
body: The example stubs `TopicRetriever.new` and expects `#retrieve` when no embed exists. `EmbedController#best` only calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`. That expectation fails, so the new controller spec does not pass and does not actually cover the enqueue path, referer/host mismatch, or the loading template.

title: embed_url is limited to 255 characters
body: `t.string :embed_url` uses the default varchar(255) and a unique index. Article and feed URLs with long paths or query strings exceed that and `TopicEmbed.create!` fails, so those pages never embed and the retrieve job errors instead of importing.

title: Each cache miss synchronously polls the entire feed
body: `perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline whenever feed polling is enabled and this URL is not yet embedded. That opens the feed with no timeout and imports every item on the request/job that is only trying to fetch one URL. A slow or huge feed blocks the worker, and many distinct embed URLs repeat the full poll.

title: Any embed_url is enqueued after a spoofable referer check
body: Host allowlisting happens only later in `TopicRetriever`, not before `Jobs.enqueue`. The referer check uses a client-supplied header, so a caller can set `Referer` to the configured host and enqueue `retrieve_topic` for arbitrary `embed_url` values. That floods the job queue; URLs that do match `embeddable_host` are then fetched server-side with `open` (no timeout, redirects followed).

title: Embed template has invalid ERB (`end if`)
body: `<%- end if %>` compiles to the Ruby statement `end if`, which is a syntax error. Rendering `/embed/best` after a topic exists will raise ActionView::Template::Error instead of showing the discussion. It must be `<% end %>`.

title: Feed poll crashes when an item has no content
body: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every RSS/Atom item has a non-nil `content` string. SimpleRSS items often only set `description` (or neither). The first such item raises NoMethodError, aborts the rest of the feed, and — with `retry: false` — drops the hourly import until the next run. Nil-check and fall back to `description` before unescaping.

title: raw_html cook path stores and serves unsanitized HTML
body: `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged when `cook_method` is `raw_html`, skipping the normal Sanitize/PrettyText pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` writes RSS item HTML (and Readability output) with that cook method, and `embed/best.html.erb` prints it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. The same cooked HTML is what the main topic page serves. An RSS item can therefore inject script or event-handler markup into every viewer of the imported topic. RSS bodies need the same tag/attribute allowlist (and `javascript:` URL rejection) as the rest of post cooking before they are stored.

title: Embed URL is interpolated into HTML unescaped
body: The imported-from footer builds `#{url}` and then stores the string as raw HTML. The only check is `/^https?:\/\//`, so a URL such as `http://host/' onclick='alert(1)` or one containing `<` breaks out of the attribute/text and becomes stored XSS in the post and the embed iframe. Escape the URL for both the href attribute and the link text.

title: postMessage targetOrigin is a full referer URL
