body: `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')` passes the full referring page URL. `postMessage`'s targetOrigin must be an origin (`scheme://host[:port]`). A path-bearing referer does not match the parent origin, so browsers drop the message (or throw) and the parent iframe never receives `discourse-resize`. Height will stay at the default and the embed will clip. Pass only the referer origin.

title: Resize message origin check is inverted and too loose
body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts the message whenever `e.origin` is any substring of `discourseUrl`, including the empty string (sandboxed/data iframes, where `origin` is `""` and `indexOf` returns 0). It does not require `e.origin` to equal the Discourse origin. Any such frame can set the embed iframe height. Compare parsed origins for equality instead.

title: Remote fetch follows redirects off the embeddable host
body: `TopicRetriever` only checks that `URI(embed_url).host` equals `embeddable_host`, then `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read`. open-uri follows redirects by default, so a page on the allowed host (or a query-string URL an attacker can get that host to serve) can 302 to an internal address (`http://127.0.0.1`, cloud metadata, etc.). The Sidekiq worker will request that target and import the body as a topic. Disable redirects or re-check the host after each hop, and do the same for `PollFeed`'s `open(feed_polling_url)`.

title: Every embed miss enqueues a fetch with no host or dedupe check
body: `best` enqueues `retrieve_topic` for any `embed_url` as soon as no `TopicEmbed` row exists. It never checks that the URL's host is `embeddable_host` (that check is only inside the job) and does not dedupe. A page on the allowed host, or repeated views while the topic is still missing, fills the queue; if `embed_by_username` is blank or the fetch fails, nothing is created and `loading.html.erb` reloads every 30s forever. Validate the host before enqueue and avoid enqueueing when a recent attempt already failed.

title: Disqus import now depends on a live HTTP fetch
body: The importer used to create the topic from the XML export. It now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which `open`s `t[:link]` with no rescue. A dead, redirected, or non-HTML link raises and aborts the whole XML import; even a soft failure (`post` blank) silently skips every comment on that thread. Network errors need to be isolated per thread, with a fallback topic so comments are not dropped.

title: Small-action button no longer pins to the right
body: .small-action is now a flex container (display:flex plus the prefixed flexbox mixin), so the button's float:right is ignored in every browser that takes that display. The button is only a flex item with the default flex: 0 1 auto and no margin-left: auto, so it sits immediately after .small-action-desc instead of at the far edge of the row. The same change also drops the 4em left padding that used to clear the floated avatar; in browsers that do not apply flex, the avatar's float:left then overlaps the description.

title: Header panel alignment breaks under the prefixed flexbox the mixin enables
body: .panel lost float:right and now relies on margin-left:auto while .contents is turned into a flex container by the new flexbox() mixin, which emits display:-ms-flexbox and display:-webkit-box before display:flex. Those older flex models do not absorb auto margins, and once they apply, floats on flex items are ignored. In IE10 (and old WebKit that only honors the 2009 box syntax) the panel therefore stays next to the title instead of on the right. There is no float or justify-content fallback left in the rule.

title: order() mixin uses 0-based values for 1-based box-ordinal-group
body: The 2009 flexbox properties -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group are 1-based (the initial value is 1) and reject 0, while modern order and -ms-flex-order are 0-based. The mixin writes the same $val to all of them. order(1) therefore sorts with default siblings in old WebKit instead of after them, and order(0) is invalid there. Header and topic styles already call order(2) and order(3); those two happen to stay after default items, but any later order(0) or order(1) will not match modern layout in the browsers this mixin claims to prefix.

title: extra-info-wrapper order has no flex parent
body: order(2) is set on .extra-info-wrapper and order(3) on .d-header .panel, but this change only makes .d-header .contents a flex container. .extra-info-wrapper is not a descendant of .contents in these styles, so it is not a flex item and order does nothing. The docked topic title will not slot between the site title and the header panel the way the order values imply; only in-flow children of .contents participate.

title: Flex on .small-action drops the right-aligned action button
body: .small-action is now a flex container, but the action button is still only positioned with float: right (and .topic-avatar with float: left). Float is ignored on flex items, and .small-action-desc is left at the default flex: 0 1 auto with padding changed from 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em to 0 1.5%. The description therefore shrink-wraps its text instead of filling the row, and the button sits immediately after the label instead of on the far right of the post action. The old 4em left padding was what kept text clear of the avatar in the float layout; 1.5% of a shrink-wrapped flex item is effectively no gap, so avatar and text also collide or sit flush. Give the description flex-grow (and a real gap) and push the button with margin-left: auto, or do not make this row a flex container while it still depends on floats.

title: Custom action message paragraphs lose vertical separation
body: .small-action .custom-message p margin was changed from 5px 0 to 0 as part of the flex alignment tweak. That rule is the spacing between paragraphs inside the moderator/small-action custom message, which is not a flex item and is not centered by align-items on .small-action. Multi-paragraph action descriptions now render as a single unspaced block.

title: Header panel right alignment fails outside modern flex
body: .panel no longer uses float: right. Right alignment is only margin-left: auto plus order(3), and .d-header .contents is a flex container via the new mixin (including display: -webkit-box / -ms-flexbox). Auto margins do not absorb free space in the 2009 -webkit-box model those prefixes turn on, and in any browser that ignores display: flex the panel is a normal block whose auto margin computes to 0. The icons, login, and sign-up controls then stay on the left under the logo instead of the right side of the header. The prefixed mixin does not provide a float fallback for the technique that replaced float: right.

title: Header flex items cannot shrink, so long titles push the panel off-screen
body: .d-header .contents is display: flex with no min-width: 0, overflow, or flex-shrink override on its children. Flex items default to min-width: auto, so they will not shrink below their content. .extra-info-wrapper (order 2, the docked topic title) and the logo title sit in that row with .panel (margin-left: auto, order 3). A long topic title therefore forces the row wider than the viewport and shoves the header icons off-screen instead of ellipsizing, which the previous float layout did not do. Set min-width: 0 and overflow/text-overflow on the title/extra-info flex items.

title: order mixin uses one number for 0-based and 1-based flex specs
body: @mixin order writes the same $val to -webkit-box-ordinal-group, -ms-flex-order, and order. -webkit-box-ordinal-group is 1-based (initial value 1; 0 is invalid) while order and -ms-flex-order are 0-based (initial value 0). Call sites pass order(2) on .extra-info-wrapper and order(3) on .panel. In old WebKit those become ordinal groups 2 and 3 against siblings that stay at the default of 1, so source order among any items that should share a slot will not match modern flex, and a later order(0) or order(1) would be dropped or tied with defaults. The prefixed value needs to be $val + 1 for -webkit-box-ordinal-group.

title: Docked topic title can push header controls off-screen
body: .extra-info-wrapper is now a flex item of .d-header .contents (order 2) but never sets min-width: 0, flex-shrink, or overflow. Flex items default to min-width: auto, so a long topic title's min-content width cannot shrink. margin-left: auto on .panel then cannot keep the header icons in view: the row overflows and the panel is pushed past the viewport. The old float layout did not have this min-content floor. Give the wrapper flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0; overflow: hidden (and ellipsis on the title) so the title truncates and the panel stays on screen.

title: Small-action description no longer fills the row
body: .small-action is now a flex row, but .small-action-desc stays at the default flex: 0 1 auto and only has padding: 0 1.5%, replacing the old block padding (0.5em 0 0.5em 4em) that made the description full width beside the floated avatar. A flex item sizes to its content, so the button rule float: right (line 306) only floats inside that shrink-wrapped box, not to the right edge of the action row. Delete/expand controls that used to sit on the far right will sit immediately after the action text. Set flex: 1 1 auto and min-width: 0 on .small-action-desc (or margin-left: auto on the button if it is a flex item).

title: order() mixin is off-by-one for 2009 flexbox
body: @mixin order writes the same $val to -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group as to the modern order property. Those 2009 properties are 1-based (the initial value is 1), while order is 0-based (initial value 0). Autoprefixer and the usual Discourse mixin emit $val + 1 for the ordinal-group properties. As written, order(1) is a no-op in old WebKit (same as the default group), and order(0) or a negative order cannot be represented. Header .panel uses order(3) and .extra-info-wrapper uses order(2); those still sort after untouched siblings only by accident. Fix the two box-ordinal-group lines to $val + 1 so the prefixed output matches order.

title: website_name bypasses TL0 website hiding
body: include_website_name is missing the trailing ? that ActiveModel Serializers requires (every other include hook in this file is include_*?). The hook is therefore never called, so website_name is always serialized. The method also reads user_profile.website directly and is not listed in untrusted_attributes, which is what hides website from anonymous viewers of TL0 users. Those viewers now receive the website host and, when the domain heuristic matches, the path, defeating the spam/privacy restriction. The serializer spec's untrusted_attributes list was not updated, so this leak is untested.

title: Invalid or non-ASCII websites disappear from the profile
body: website_name parses the stored website with URI and rescues every error to nil, then returns nil when host is nil. The profile template now renders the globe link only when model.website_name is present, replacing the old client split that displayed the host segment of any non-empty URL. Ruby's URI rejects non-ASCII hosts (IDN) and many user-typed URLs, so those profiles lose the website label entirely instead of falling back to the hostname. The second URI() call that appends the path is outside the rescue, so a parse failure there raises during serialization.

title: Domain check treats unrelated hosts as the same site
body: The else branch treats the website as the same site whenever Discourse.current_hostname ends with '.' plus the website host, and the elsif branch equates any two hosts that share every label after the first when they have the same label count greater than 2. That matches public suffixes and unrelated names, not just the instance domain: a site at forum.example.com will expand http://com/login to 'com/login', and http://evil.example.com/phish will be expanded the same way as a real sibling such as www. Host comparison is also case-sensitive against Discourse.current_hostname while URI#host is lowercased, so Example.com vs example.com skips the equal-host branch and omits the path the feature is supposed to show.

title: website_name bypasses TL0 field hiding
body: include_website_name is never consulted: ActiveModel::Serializer only calls include_website_name?. website_name is also missing from untrusted_attributes, unlike website. Anonymous viewers of a TL0 user therefore still get website_name (host, and host+path when it matches the instance), which is the same profile URL the serializer is supposed to withhold. The new specs never cover a TL0/anonymous viewer, so this leak is untested.

title: Same-domain path display fails on case and www
body: Hosts are compared case-sensitively and without normalizing a leading www. A site at example.com will not treat http://Example.com/user or http://www.example.com/user as the same domain (lengths differ, and example.com does not end with .www.example.com), so the profile shows only the host. The inverse (instance on www, website on the apex) does append the path, so the feature is inconsistent with its own parent-domain rule. Comparisons should downcase both hosts and treat a single www label as equivalent before deciding whether to append the path.

title: website_name bypasses TL0 website hiding
body: include_website_name is missing the trailing ? that ActiveModel::Serializers uses (every other include hook in this file is include_*?), so the method is never called and website_name is always serialized. website_name is also absent from untrusted_attributes, which is what hides website, bio, and location for trust-level 0 users viewed anonymously. The profile template now renders model.website_name, so an anonymous visitor still sees a new user's site host and path even though website itself is omitted. That undoes the anti-spam/privacy gate. Add website_name to untrusted_attributes (which defines include_website_name?) and drop the dead include_website_name method; the serializer spec never covers a TL0 user who has a website.

title: Same-site host check is case-sensitive and www-asymmetric
body: website_host is compared to Discourse.current_hostname with == and ends_with? without downcasing. Ruby's URI does not lowercase the host, so http://Example.com/user on an example.com forum fails every branch and website_name is only Example.com, not Example.com/user. The same gap hits the common www vs apex pair: www.example.com (3 labels) vs example.com (2 labels) skips the equal-length sibling branch, and example.com.ends_with?('.www.example.com') is false, so the path is dropped. The reverse (forum on www, website on the apex) does show the path via ends_with?, so the feature is inconsistent for the same site. Normalize both hosts (downcase, and treat a single leading www label as equivalent) before comparing, and cover those cases in the serializer spec.

title: Embedded-post username color changed on light themes
body: The light-theme branch of `.topic-meta-data h5 a` was rewritten from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, and the dark branch uses 30% instead of the complement 70%. Light-theme embedded-post usernames become much lighter than before, and dark themes get the old light-theme shade rather than a readable secondary-based color.

title: Group member name lightness not preserved
body: `.group-member-info .name` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The replacement uses 50% for both `dark-light-choose` arguments. Light themes lose the darker 30% treatment (the sibling `.title` was already 50%), and dark themes do not get the complementary 70% on `$secondary`.

title: Mobile group member name lightness not preserved
body: Same mistake as desktop: `.group-member-info .name` changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(..., 50%, ..., 50%)`. Light-theme names are lighter than before, and the dark-theme color is not the 70% complement of the original 30%.

title: Mobile topic-map h3 lightness does not match desktop
body: `.topic-map h3` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and should map to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`, which is what desktop/topic-post.scss does. Mobile now uses 50%/50%, so light-theme map headings are much lighter and dark themes do not get the intended secondary shade.

title: Custom message length color arguments are inverted
body: `.custom-message-length` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The new call is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The light branch is no longer 70%, so light themes get a darker hint, and the dark branch keeps 70% on `$secondary` instead of the complementary 30% used everywhere else for a 70% primary scale.

title: Category badge notification still scales only $primary
body: In the same file this PR updates, `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still sets `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`. On dark themes that stays a lightened primary and will not follow the secondary-based color the neighboring topic-list text now uses.

title: Embedded-post author color changed in light theme
body: The topic-map embedded-post author link was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The replacement uses dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)), so the light-theme branch is no longer the previous value and the dark branch is the complement of 70%, not of 30%. Light-theme author names in expanded replies become much lighter, and dark theme does not get the muted color this change is supposed to produce.

title: Mobile topic-map h3 lightness not preserved
body: Topic-map h3 was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%). It is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)). Desktop keeps 20% for light and 80% for dark. On mobile, light-theme headings jump from a near-primary 20% to a mid gray, and dark theme is not the complement of the original 20%.

title: Mobile custom-message-length colors are swapped
body: .custom-message-length was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%). The new rule is dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)). Desktop correctly keeps 70% in the light branch and 30% in the dark branch. Mobile inverts both, so light-theme hint text gets darker and dark-theme hint text gets much lighter than the rest of this change.

title: Group member name color collapsed to title color
body: .group-member-info .name was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), distinct from .title at 50%. Both are now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)). Light theme loses that distinction, and the dark-theme name color is not the complement of the original 30%.

title: Mobile group member name color also rewritten
body: Same mistake as desktop user styles: .group-member-info .name was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) and is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)), matching .title. Light-theme names change shade, and dark theme does not use the complement of 30%.

title: Embedded-post username color lightness swapped
body: The embedded post username link was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The replacement is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, so the light-theme branch is no longer 30% and the dark branch is the inverse of the usual 100-minus mapping. Every other conversion in this PR keeps the original lightness on `$primary` and puts `100 - N` on `$secondary`. Light themes will render these names much paler (weaker contrast); dark themes will not get the intended muted secondary color.

title: Mobile flag length hint color inverted
body: `.custom-message-length` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. It is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The desktop counterpart in this same PR correctly keeps 70% on `$primary` and uses 30% on `$secondary`. On mobile light themes the hint becomes much darker than before; on dark themes it is lightened far more than the desktop rule, so the two layouts no longer match and contrast with the modal background changes.

title: Mobile topic-map heading lightness changed
body: `.topic-map h3` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The desktop topic-map heading in this PR correctly becomes `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`. Mobile light themes lose the stronger 20% color, and dark themes do not get the corresponding 80% secondary, so the heading is both a light-theme regression and inconsistent with desktop.

title: Group member name color flattened to 50%
body: `.group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The adjacent `.title` rule was already 50% and was converted correctly; the name rule was overwritten with that same 50/50 pair instead of `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. Light-theme group member names become lighter than before and no longer differ from titles.

title: Mobile group member name color flattened to 50%
body: The same mistake as desktop: `.group-member-info .name` changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, matching the sibling title instead of preserving 30% on `$primary` and using 70% on `$secondary`. Mobile light themes lose the darker name color, and dark themes do not follow the inversion used everywhere else in the PR.

title: Add/remove members reads group_id but the route supplies id
body: add_members and remove_member both do Group.find(params.require(:group_id)). The new routes are member routes on resources :groups (DELETE/PUT /admin/groups/:id/members), so Rails populates params[:id], not params[:group_id]. The client only puts the id in the path (/admin/groups/:id/members.json) and sends usernames or user_id in the body. params.require(:group_id) therefore raises ParameterMissing and every add or remove from the admin UI returns 400. Controller specs hide this by passing group_id directly and never hitting the router.

title: Creating a group drops alias_level
body: create only assigns name and visible. The admin form shows the alias-level combo for new groups, and Group#asJSON posts alias_level on POST /admin/groups, but the action never reads it. A group created with anything other than the default alias level (for example everyone / 99) is saved as the default, and the choice is silently lost. update does apply alias_level, so the field only works after the group already exists.

title: totalPages is one too high when count is a multiple of limit
body: totalPages is Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (50 members, limit 50) that is 2 instead of 1. showingLast stays false on the real last page, so Next is enabled. next then sets offset to user_count and findMembers loads an empty extra page. Use ceil(user_count / limit), and treat a zero count as zero pages.

title: Remove control ignores automatic groups
body: The member row is an itemView whose context is the user, not the group, so {{#unless automatic}} does not see the group's automatic flag. The flag is always falsy on the user, so the remove link is rendered for automatic groups (trust levels, staff, and so on). The server rejects those deletes with 422, and removeMember never surfaces the error, so the confirm dialog appears to succeed and the member stays. The add-members block in group.hbs correctly hides itself; this row does not.

title: Removing the last member on a page leaves a blank page
body: removeMember reloads with the current offset and does not move back a page when that page becomes empty. The members action echoes the requested offset and does not clamp it to the new total. After deleting the last user on a page, the response has members: [] while offset is still past the new user_count. The client stores that offset, so the admin stays on a blank page until they click Previous. findMembers only clamps offset against the stale user_count from before the delete.

title: Members limit and offset are not bounded
body: limit is (params[:limit] || 50).to_i and offset is params[:offset].to_i with no upper or lower bound, on a public endpoint that now paginates every group including large automatic ones. A caller can pass limit of millions or a negative limit/offset. limit(0) is also echoed back to the admin client, which then divides user_count by that limit and produces Infinity/NaN page numbers. Clamp limit to a small positive maximum (and offset to >= 0) before querying.

title: GET group members response shape changed without a compatibility path
body: GET /groups/:id/members used to render a JSON array of users via GroupUserSerializer. It now returns {members, meta}. Any plugin, theme, or external client that still treats the body as an array will break. The in-repo templates were updated, but nothing in this PR versions the endpoint or keeps the old array format.

title: Automatic-group remove spec uses PUT and never hits the route
body: The example "cannot remove members from automatic groups" calls xhr :put, :remove_member, while the route is DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members and the success example correctly uses :delete. Controller specs invoke the action by name and inject group_id, so this never checks routing or that params[:id] is what the action reads. That is why the group_id vs :id mismatch is untested. The members action's new {members, meta} contract also has no spec.

title: Member item template looks up a block variable that itemView does not define
body: group.hbs renders members with `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`, and this item template then uses `member` (`{{avatar member}}`, `{{member.username}}`, `{{action "removeMember" member}}`). An Ember itemView's context is the user record itself; the `each` block variable is not in scope inside `templateName`. Username and avatar therefore render blank, and removeMember is invoked with undefined, so the DELETE is sent without a user id (or not at all). The template should bind `username` / `this` (or `view.content`) on the item context.

title: remove_member deletes by raw id and skips Group#remove
body: `group.users.delete(user_id)` passes an Integer. On the Rails 4.1 association API this app uses, `has_many#delete` type-checks each argument and raises `ActiveRecord::AssociationTypeMismatch` unless the value is a User, so every removal 500s and the membership is unchanged (the new spec would fail). Even on a Rails version that accepts ids, `delete` skips `Group#remove` / GroupUser callbacks that the old patch path used, so counter caches and primary-group cleanup are not run. Load the user and call `group.remove(user)`.

title: totalPages is off by one when count is a multiple of limit
body: `totalPages` is `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When `user_count` is exactly divisible by `limit` (the default page size is 50, so 50, 100, … members) this reports an extra page. `showingLast` stays false on the real last page, Next stays enabled, and `next` then sets offset to `user_count`, which returns an empty page. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (and keep the zero-count early return).

title: Creating a group drops alias_level
body: `create` only assigns `name` and `visible`. The admin form shows the alias-level combo before the group has an id, and `Group#asJSON` / `Group#create` send `alias_level`, but the controller never reads it. A group created with "everyone" or "mods and admins" is stored at the column default (nobody) until a later update. `update` already applies `params[:alias_level]`; `create` needs the same assignment.

title: members offset/limit are not clamped
body: `offset = params[:offset].to_i` is passed straight to SQL. A negative offset (easy to send, and the client can also land past the end after the last member of a page is removed because the server echoes the requested offset) makes PostgreSQL raise `OFFSET must not be negative` and turns the members request into a 500. Limit is also unbounded, so `?limit=` can force the public members endpoint to load an entire automatic group (trust_level_0) into one response. Clamp offset to `>= 0` and to the last page, and cap limit.

title: Add/remove membership failures are swallowed
body: `removeMember` and `addMembers` only chain `.then` to reload the list. A 422 (automatic group, validation error) or network failure never surfaces a message, unlike `save`/`destroy` which bootbox the error. The admin UI keeps the old member list with no indication the change did not stick.

title: Add/remove members read group_id but the route only sets id
body: add_members and remove_member load the group with params.require(:group_id). The new routes are member routes on resources :groups (DELETE/PUT /admin/groups/:id/members), so Rails only populates params[:id]. The client calls /admin/groups/:id/members.json and does not send group_id in the body. Every add or remove therefore raises ParameterMissing (400) and membership changes never persist. Controller specs pass group_id directly and never hit the router, so they hide this. Use params[:id] (and fix the automatic-group spec, which calls remove_member with PUT instead of DELETE).

title: Member row template looks up member and automatic on the wrong object
body: group.hbs renders members with {{each member in members itemView="group-member"}} and no block. That item view's context is the user, and the each-block param member is not in scope in group_member.hbs. {{member.username}} and {{avatar member}} therefore resolve against the user (no member property), so names and avatars render blank, and {{action "removeMember" member}} passes undefined so removal cannot work. {{#unless automatic}} is also evaluated on the user, not the group, so it is always true and automatic groups still show a remove control. The template should use the item context (username / this) and the group's automatic flag from the parent controller.

title: Removing a member bypasses Group#remove
body: add_members still calls group.add(user), but remove_member does group.users.delete(user_id) and then group.save. Association delete skips Group#remove, which is what previously updated membership (user_count and other callbacks such as primary group). After a successful delete the join row is gone but denormalized group state can stay stale, so admin counts and anything keyed off user_count are wrong until some other process recomputes them. Call the same removal API used before (group.remove) instead of users.delete.

title: Creating a group drops alias_level
body: The admin form shows the alias-level combo before the group has an id, and Group#asJSON sends alias_level on POST /admin/groups. create only assigns name and visible (params[:visible] == "true") and never reads alias_level. The chosen level is discarded; it is only stored if the admin later hits update. Set alias_level on create the same way update does.

title: totalPages is off by one when the count divides evenly
body: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which is one page too many whenever user_count is a positive multiple of limit (50 members at limit 50 shows 2/2). showingLast stays false on the real last page, and next() then sets offset to user_count, so findMembers loads an empty page. Use ceil(user_count / limit), and do not advance offset to user_count.

title: Members endpoint accepts an unbounded limit
body: limit is (params[:limit] || 50).to_i with no upper bound, and offset is not clamped to >= 0. This action is public (only ensure_can_see!). A caller can pass a huge limit and force a full member serialization in one response, which is the opposite of the pagination this change adds and is an easy load amplifier. Cap limit (and reject negative offset/limit) before the query.

title: GET /groups/:name/members response shape changed
body: members used to render a JSON array of GroupUserSerializer objects. It now returns {members, meta: {total, limit, offset}}. Any client still expecting the array (plugins, API consumers) will break, and this PR adds no request spec for the new contract. Document the break or keep a compatible shape if this endpoint is public.

title: Fallback locale files are not loaded on translate
body: The on-demand loader in translate only calls load_locale for I18n.config.locale, and load_translations was patched to never load other locale YAML files. FallbackLocaleList therefore only works when something has already called I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!, which this PR does solely from ApplicationController#set_locale. Mailers, Sidekiq/jobs, the console, and any I18n.with_locale / I18n.locale= path never load the site-default or English files, so a missing key in the active locale stays missing instead of falling back. Server-side fallbacks are broken for most non-request translation.

title: Translation cache ignores dynamic fallback locale
body: The accelerator cache key is only key + current locale + backend object id. Fallback resolution now depends on SiteSetting.default_locale, which can change at runtime without replacing the backend. After an admin changes the site default locale, cached hits keep the translation resolved through the old fallback chain (or a previously cached missing result) until that LRU entry is evicted, so users see the wrong language for keys that are not defined in their own locale.

title: No tests for custom fallback chain or preload
body: FallbackLocaleList and the ensure_loaded! hook are new behavior with no specs. Nothing checks the user-locale → site default → :en order, that fallback YAML is actually loaded before lookup, or that translations outside ApplicationController#set_locale still fall back. The loader/cache bugs above would not be caught before merge.

title: Fallback locales are not loaded before translate caches a miss
body: I18n.translate only calls load_locale for config.locale, and the new fallback chain (site default locale, then :en) is loaded solely from ApplicationController#set_locale via I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!. Any I18n.t outside that filter—mailers, jobs, models, middleware, or a request that translates before set_locale—looks up fallbacks whose YAML was never loaded. The accelerator then freezes that result in the process-wide LRU (including the default missing-translation string). Later requests that do load :en still serve the cached miss until the entry is evicted or the process restarts, so users see raw keys instead of the intended site-locale or English fallback.

title: Translation cache ignores the site fallback locale
body: The LRU key is only key + I18n.locale + backend object_id. FallbackLocaleList resolves misses using SiteSetting.default_locale, but that value is not part of the key and nothing clears @cache when the setting changes. After an admin changes the site default locale, strings already resolved through the old fallback stay cached for each user locale, so the UI keeps showing the previous language until restart or an unrelated I18n.reload!.

title: Every fallback lookup reads SiteSetting.default_locale
body: Backend::Fallbacks calls I18n.fallbacks[locale] on each translate, and FallbackLocaleList#[] unconditionally calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym. That runs for every I18n.t once this initializer is loaded, including asset precompile, migrations, and boot paths where the settings store/DB is not available. Those tasks previously did not enable i18n fallbacks (the flag lived only in production/profile). They can now raise while building the fallback list, and a nil default_locale raises NoMethodError on to_sym instead of degrading to :en.

title: No tests for fallback order or lazy locale loading
body: The custom chain (requested locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en), the move of fallbacks out of the environment configs, and ensure_loaded! are untested. A regression that drops :en, skips loading a fallback file, or caches a miss would ship unnoticed, which is exactly the failure mode this change introduces next to the translate accelerator.

title: Fallback locale files are not loaded on translate
body: The on-demand loader in I18n.translate only calls load_locale for config.locale. FallbackLocaleList and I18n::Backend::Fallbacks then look up SiteSetting.default_locale and :en, but those YAML files stay unloaded unless something else has called ensure_loaded!. The only call site is ApplicationController#set_locale, so jobs, mailers, models, middleware, and I18n.with_locale blocks never load the fallback chain. Missing keys then raise or return the Rails "translation missing" string instead of the site-locale or English string. Because translate also LRU-caches that result (and the production exception handler returns a string rather than raising), a miss can stick in the cache even after the fallback files are loaded later in the same process.

title: Translation cache ignores the fallback chain
body: The LRU key is only "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}". With fallbacks enabled, the cached string can come from SiteSetting.default_locale or :en, but the key does not include that chain. default_locale is an admin-changeable runtime setting; after it changes, locales that were missing the key keep serving the previous fallback language until the 300-entry cache evicts the entry. ensure_loaded! loading the new locale file does not invalidate those entries.

title: No tests for fallback order or locale loading
body: The new FallbackLocaleList (user locale, then SiteSetting.default_locale, then :en) and the ensure_loaded! hook are untested. Nothing asserts that a key missing in the user locale resolves to the site locale before English, that string/symbol locales collapse, or that a translation outside ApplicationController#set_locale still loads fallback YAML. Those are the paths this change is most likely to get wrong, and a regression would ship user-visible missing or wrong strings.

title: Denial cache blocks grants for the full TTL
body: Check consults permDenialCache before both the permission cache and the new DB refresh, and on a DB deny it stores a 30s denial keyed by namespace/user/action/name/parent (lines 153-155) without ever deleting that entry when a later query would allow. Any Check that was denied for that tuple — the usual case before a share, role change, or retry after creating access — keeps returning Allowed=false until shortCacheTTL, even if the DB (and perm cache) now grant the resource. That reintroduces the staleness this PR is meant to remove, and it fails closed for up to 30 seconds after a real permission grant.

title: List still serves stale permission cache
body: List returns as soon as getCachedIdentityPermissions hits and never re-reads the DB when the cached scope map is missing a newly granted dashboard or folder. Only a total cache miss refreshes. Check was changed to fall through to the DB when the cached scopes do not allow the resource, but listing is the path that actually fetches dashboards and folders, so a creator (or anyone granted access) still omits the new resource for the permission-cache TTL (30s) if that action was cached before the grant. A prior Check can accidentally refresh the shared perm cache, but a list-only request will not.

title: Slow permission fetch overwrites newer cache and plants a denial
body: getUserPermissions no longer reads the cache and always writes permCache at the end of its singleflight callback. Check decides to refresh based on a snapshot taken before that call, then on deny writes permDenialCache. A request that started a DB read against old permissions can finish after another request has already cached the post-grant scopes, overwrite permCache with the older map, and set a denial for the new resource. Later Checks hit that denial first and stay denied for shortCacheTTL even though a fresher result was already known.

title: Denial-cache test does not override an allow
body: TestService_CacheCheck "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" comments that permCache allows dash1 so the denial short-circuit is proven, but it stores map["dashboards:uid:dash1"]=false. checkPermission treats a false value as no grant, so the test would still deny if the denial lookup were removed. It never shows that a real cached allow is ignored, nor that a grant after a cached deny is honored.

title: Denial cache pins false denies and skips permission refresh
body: Check writes a 30s denial (userPermDenialCacheKey) whenever the DB-backed check returns false, and the next Check returns that denial before consulting either the permission cache or the database. A negative result is often stale rather than authoritative: checkInheritedPermissions uses the separately cached folder tree, so a dashboard/folder under a newly created parent is denied even when the user has folders:uid:<parent> (or a permission row that was committed after the check). That false deny is then sticky for shortCacheTTL, including after the folder cache expires and after a later grant, which re-breaks the create-then-access case this PR is fixing. Denial entries are never deleted on a successful refresh.

title: Cached check error skips the DB permission fallback
body: If getCachedIdentityPermissions hits but checkPermission fails (typically buildFolderTree / folder store error while evaluating inheritance), Check returns the error immediately. It never reaches getIdentityPermissions, so a direct scope that exists only in the DB (the newly created dashboard/folder permission this change is meant to observe) is never loaded. A transient folder-store failure therefore fails the request even when the refreshed permission set would allow without walking the folder tree.

title: Warm permission cache no longer serves distinct denies
body: A permission-cache hit that does not contain the requested scope is treated as a miss and always calls getIdentityPermissions, which no longer reads the cache and always queries the DB (and then overwrites permCache). Previously one cached scope map answered every Check for that user and action. Now each distinct denied (namespace, user, action, name, folder) tuple hits the database until its denial entry is warm. Authorizing a page or search over many resources the user cannot access becomes a query stampede, and concurrent refreshes can also overwrite a newer permCache entry with an older snapshot.

title: Denial cache blocks the DB requery this PR adds
body: Check consults permDenialCache before cached permissions or the database, and on any final deny it stores that key for shortCacheTTL (30s). A later grant never clears the entry, so the new "requery when the scope is missing from cached permissions" path is skipped and Check keeps returning Allowed=false. That is the creator flow this PR is meant to fix: a check before the dashboard/folder permission row exists (or before a just-created parent is in the folder tree) records a deny, and the follow-up open still fails until the denial entry expires even if getIdentityPermissions would now allow it. Revocation stays cached on the allow path, so denials are strictly stickier than grants.

title: Denial cache key collides when UIDs contain underscores
body: userPermDenialCacheKey concatenates action, name, and parent with "_" and no delimiter that cannot appear in a UID. Grafana short UIDs may contain underscores, so name "foo" + parent "bar_baz" and name "foo_bar" + parent "baz" produce the same key. A cached deny for one resource then makes Check return Allowed=false for a different resource the user is allowed to access, for the full denial TTL.

title: List still serves stale permission cache
body: List returns getCachedIdentityPermissions immediately on a cache hit and never requeries when a newly created dashboard or folder scope is absent. Check was changed to fall through to the DB in that case, so after creation Check can allow a resource that List still omits for up to shortCacheTTL (30s). Callers that "fetch" newly created dashboards/folders via List keep the bug this PR describes.

title: Filtered Grafana rules render without a list key
body: FilterViewResults maps filtered rules into a list and previously passed key={key} to GrafanaRuleLoader. The replacement GrafanaRuleListItem is rendered with no key, even though getRuleKey still builds one. React will reuse the wrong row when pages append or the filter result set shifts, so action menus, drawers, and focus can attach to a different rule than the one the user clicked.

title: Pause is never offered in the ruler-less list
body: The list view now computes canPause from Grafana Prometheus abilities because ruler rules are no longer loaded, but the Pause item is still gated on rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule). GrafanaRuleListItem only passes promRule, so rulerRule is undefined and Pause stays hidden for every Grafana-managed rule even when the user is allowed to pause it.

title: Delete stays hidden without a ruler rule
body: canDelete is OR-ed with the new Prometheus ability so list-view permissions can allow deletion, but the Delete menu item is still rendered only when rulerRule is truthy. The new list never supplies a ruler rule, so users with delete permission cannot delete a Grafana rule from the list. The group-loader menu test also encodes this by expecting four items and omitting Delete despite granting AlertingRuleDelete.

title: Silence menu item opens nothing
body: AlertRuleMenu can show Silence from Prometheus-rule abilities and calls handleSilence, which only sets showSilenceDrawer. The drawer is still mounted only when rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) is true. In the list view rule is undefined, so clicking Silence notifications does not open SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer and the action is a no-op.

title: Federated rules are no longer treated as immutable
body: useAllAlertRuleAbilities used to set isFederated from isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) before deciding edit, delete, pause, and duplicate support. The refactor hardcodes isFederated to false and forwards every combined rule through useAllRulerRuleAbilities. Federated cloud rule groups, which this helper still serves outside the list view, can now be edited or deleted even though federation makes them immutable.

title: Rule view links drop the return path
body: The removed list item built the view href with createReturnTo() so leaving a filtered or grouped list could navigate back to that list. The new href is only /alerting/grafana/${uid}/view. Opening a rule from the list no longer preserves the list URL, so the rule view's back/return navigation lands somewhere other than the list the user came from.

title: Federated rules are always treated as editable
body: useAllAlertRuleAbilities now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which hardcodes isFederated to false (the old isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) check is gone, and RuleGroupIdentifierV2 cannot express source_tenants). Federated Mimir/GEM groups were previously immutable. Every consumer of useAlertRuleAbility / useAllAlertRuleAbilities will now offer edit, delete, pause, and duplicate on federated rules.

title: Delete is unreachable in the ruler-free list view
body: canDelete can be true from useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities when only a Prometheus rule is loaded, but the Delete item is still rendered only when rulerRule is defined, and onClick passes that rulerRule to handleDelete. GrafanaRuleListItem never supplies a ruler rule, and RuleActionsButtons already deletes via the identifier (showDeleteModal(identifier, groupIdentifier)), so the extra guard hides Delete for every Grafana rule in the new list. The group-loader menu test even asserts only four items and never looks for Delete despite granting AlertingRuleDelete.

title: Pause never appears without a ruler rule
body: canPause is OR-ed with the Prometheus-rule ability so the list view can authorize pause without the ruler API, but the menu item is still gated on rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) and MenuItemPauseRule requires a RulerGrafanaRuleDTO. In the new list, rulerRule is undefined, so Pause is never shown even for users who can edit the rule.

title: Silence action opens nothing in the list view
body: AlertRuleMenu can show Silence notifications from Prometheus-rule abilities and calls handleSilence, which only sets showSilenceDrawer. The drawer is rendered only when rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) is true. List items pass promRule and no ruler rule, so the click sets state and then renders nothing.

title: Recording-rule export and pause dropped
body: useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities sets ModifyExport, Pause, Restore, and DeletePermanently supported only when prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) is true. The ruler path used rulerRuleType.grafana.rule, which includes Grafana recording rules. Recording rules in the list therefore lose export and pause/restore even when the user has folder edit permission and the rule is not provisioned.

title: Filtered Grafana rows are rendered without a key
body: The grafana branch of rules.map used to pass key={key} into GrafanaRuleLoader. GrafanaRuleListItem is now returned with no key, while the datasource and unknown branches still set one. As pages append, React will reuse the wrong row instances, so action menus, links, and pause/health state can attach to the wrong rule.

title: Rule view links drop returnTo
body: The removed GrafanaRuleListItem built the view href with createReturnTo() so the detail page could navigate back to the current list URL (including filters). The replacement always links to /alerting/grafana/${uid}/view with no returnTo query. Opening a rule from the list no longer restores the filtered list on back navigation.

title: Delete never appears in the ruler-free list view
body: canDelete is now true when Grafana Prometheus abilities allow delete, but the Delete menu item is still rendered only when rulerRule is set, and its click handler still requires that ruler DTO. GrafanaRuleListItem (the new list view) passes only promRule, so the item is never shown even for users with folder delete permission. The new GrafanaGroupLoader test grants AlertingRuleDelete and then asserts the menu has exactly four items and does not include Delete, so this regression is untested. Users can no longer delete Grafana rules from the alert list.

title: Pause action is unreachable without a ruler rule
body: Pause is shown only when canPause is true and rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) is true, then MenuItemPauseRule is given that ruler rule. The list view no longer loads ruler rules and only supplies promRule, so the pause item is never rendered even though useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities can set canPause. Pausing a Grafana-managed rule from the new list is impossible.

title: Silence menu item does not open the drawer
body: AlertRuleMenu can show Silence notifications from Grafana Prometheus abilities and calls handleSilence, which only sets showSilenceDrawer. The drawer itself is still gated on rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) and is passed rulerRule. In the list view rule is undefined, so clicking Silence does nothing. The new group-loader test only checks that the menu item exists, not that the drawer opens.

title: Federated rules are no longer treated as immutable
body: useAllAlertRuleAbilities used to set isFederated from isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group), which blocked update, delete, pause, restore, and permanent delete. After this refactor it always delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which hardcodes isFederated to false (the source_tenants check is commented out and RuleGroupIdentifierV2 is not used to recover it). Federated Mimir/GEM rule groups can now be edited or deleted from every caller of the combined-rule ability hooks, not only the new list.

title: Filtered Grafana rules are rendered without a list key
body: The grafana branch of the filtered-results map used to pass key={key} into GrafanaRuleLoader. The replacement GrafanaRuleListItem element has no key, while the datasource and unknown branches still do. React will reuse the wrong row when the filter result set grows or shifts, so rule names, health, and action buttons can attach to the wrong rule. getRuleKey already exists for this list specifically to avoid duplicate keys.

title: Rule view links drop the list returnTo
body: The removed GrafanaRuleListItem built the view href with createReturnTo() so Back returned to the filtered or grouped list. The new item calls createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`) with no returnTo query. Opening a rule from the new list lands on the rule view with no way to return to the previous list filters or scroll position.

title: Modify export is denied for Grafana recording rules
body: useAllRulerRuleAbilities still enables ModifyExport for every Grafana-managed ruler rule (alerting and recording). useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities sets ModifyExport supported only when prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) is true. Recording rules rendered from the Prometheus list therefore lose Export even when the user has AlertingRuleRead, which is what the list-view menu uses.

title: $__range queries are interpolated before the no-split check
body: runSplitQuery now runs datasource.applyTemplateVariables on every target before querySupportsSplitting. That helper refuses to split expressions that still contain $__range, because the variable must be interpolated against each split window (the comment on querySupportsSplitting says backend interpolation of the split range is required). Template replacement consumes $__range using request.scopedVars for the full original range, so the check then sees a plain duration and splits the query anyway. Each chunk is executed with the full-range duration already baked in, so range-variable queries return wrong series. The $__range check has to happen on the raw expression, and $__range must not be replaced until each sub-range is known.

title: Shard splitting interpolates, then runSplitQuery interpolates again
body: runShardSplitQuery maps every target through applyTemplateVariables, then splitQueriesByStreamShard always delegates execution to runSplitQuery, which applies applyTemplateVariables a second time (the updated test even expects 5 calls for a single target). applyTemplateVariables also appends request.filters as ad-hoc matchers. The second pass therefore duplicates those matchers on an already rewritten expr, producing invalid or overly constrained LogQL and wrong results whenever ad-hoc filters are set. Interpolation for the shard path should happen once, and the inner runSplitQuery call must not template-replace targets that are already interpolated.

title: Empty-after-interpolation queries are no longer dropped
body: Previously interpolateVariablesInQueries ran before the expr/hide filters, so a target whose expression was only a variable that resolved to "" was removed and never queried. The new code filters on the raw expr first and only then calls applyTemplateVariables. A target like expr: "$query" that interpolates to an empty string now stays in the shard groups and is sent to Loki, which errors or returns unintended results. Filter again after interpolation, the same way the old interpolate-then-filter order did.

title: Interpolating before the $__range guard splits queries that must stay whole
body: runSplitQuery now runs datasource.applyTemplateVariables before querySupportsSplitting. That helper refuses to split expressions that still contain [$__range], [$__range_s], or [$__range_ms], because those macros must be resolved against the original request range (the comment says backend interpolation on a split range is wrong). templateSrv.replace, which applyTemplateVariables uses, substitutes $__range* from the parent request before that check, so isQueryWithRangeVariable no longer matches and the query is day-split. Each chunk is then executed with the full-dashboard duration already baked in (for example [7d] on a 1-day window), which over-counts range aggregations and multiplies Loki load. The same substitution also happens in runShardSplitQuery before it delegates to runSplitQuery, so the shard path has the same hole.

title: Pre-interpolating range vars breaks stream-shard selector rewrite
body: runShardSplitQuery now expands variables with applyTemplateVariables before interpolateShardingSelector rewrites the stream selector (line 154). interpolateShardingSelector inserts the shard matcher and `| drop __stream_shard__` by replacing the `{...}` selector only. If a range like [$__auto] is still attached to that selector, the rewrite keeps a valid range vector; after this change [$__auto] is already `5m`, so the range is left behind the inserted pipeline. The new test locks in the result: `count_over_time({a="b", __stream_shard__=~"20|10"} | drop __stream_shard__[5m])`, which is invalid LogQL (count_over_time requires a range vector, and [5m] is bound to the drop stage). Sharded metric queries whose range or step is a variable will fail or return errors.

title: applyTemplateVariables runs again on already interpolated shard requests
body: runShardSplitQuery already maps every target through applyTemplateVariables(query, scopedVars, request.filters) and then calls runSplitQuery on each shard subrequest. runSplitQuery applies the same function again, still passing request.filters. applyTemplateVariables is not idempotent when filters are present: ad-hoc matchers are appended to expr on every call, so each sharded subquery gets duplicate label matchers and can be rejected by Loki. The updated shard test expects applyTemplateVariables to be called 5 times (once up front plus once per group inside runSplitQuery), which confirms the re-entry, but nothing asserts that filters or escaped matchers survive a second pass.

title: $__range queries are interpolated before the no-split guard
body: runSplitQuery now calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables on every target before querySupportsSplitting(). That helper intentionally refuses to split expressions containing $__range / $__range_ms / $__range_s because those macros must be interpolated against each chunk's time range (the comment at the guard says the backend does that with the split range). After this change the macro is replaced using the original full request range, so isQueryWithRangeVariable() no longer matches and the query is time-split anyway. Each chunk then runs with a range duration for the whole query, producing wrong rates/counts (and the same path is hit again from runShardSplitQuery, which interpolates before delegating to runSplitQuery). The new tests only cover $__auto and $step, so this regression is untested. Preserve the range-variable check on the pre-interpolation expression and do not split those queries.

title: Completion logs no longer record unsampled trace IDs
body: LoggerMiddleware used to attach traceID from tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false), which includes unsampled spans. That field was removed and the line now only calls m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info. Infra FromContext only adds traceID for sampled spans (TraceIDFromContext with requireSampled=true). Plugin Request Completed logs for unsampled requests therefore lose traceID, so those requests can no longer be correlated from the egress log.

title: TestLogger.FromContext drops the fake and the context
body: FromContext ignores both the receiver and the context and returns NewTestLogger(). LoggerMiddleware now logs via logger.FromContext(ctx).Info, so any test that injects *TestLogger will record nothing on the instance under assertion: Calls, Message, and Ctx stay on a discarded logger. Contextual attributes also cannot be observed. The fake must return itself (or a child that shares the same Logs) and retain the context key/values.

title: No test that contextual fields still reach the completion log
body: pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName, and dsUID were removed from LoggerMiddleware's explicit log params and now depend on ContextualLoggerMiddleware calling log.WithContextualAttributes before LoggerMiddleware's FromContext. Nothing in this PR tests that middleware, a nil-safe request, or that Plugin Request Completed still contains those fields when the two middlewares are stacked as in CreateMiddlewares. A reversed wrap order or a FromContext that does not merge contextual attributes would silently drop datasource and plugin identity from egress logs.

title: Plugin completion logs drop traceID
body: logRequest no longer appends traceID from tracing.TraceIDFromContext, and ContextualLoggerMiddleware only puts endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, and uname on the context. The "Plugin Request Completed" / grafana-data-egress line therefore no longer carries a trace id, so those logs can no longer be correlated with the request trace. Put traceID back on the log params (or into the contextual attributes) before relying on FromContext.

title: TestLogger.FromContext drops recorded logs
body: FromContext ignores the receiver and returns NewTestLogger(). LoggerMiddleware now logs via logger.FromContext(ctx).Info, so any test that injects a TestLogger and asserts InfoLogs will see zero calls: the Info lands on a different instance. FromContext should return the same TestLogger (or a child that still records into it).

title: Nil plugin requests panic before logger nil-guards
body: ContextualLoggerMiddleware.QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, and CollectMetrics dereference req (req.PluginContext) with no nil check before calling next. LoggerMiddleware, which now sits inside this middleware, explicitly handles a nil request by skipping logging and forwarding the call. A nil QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics request that previously passed through the stack now panics in instrumentContext's caller, so the request never reaches the plugin client.

title: Request-completed logs no longer include traceID
body: LoggerMiddleware used to append traceID from tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false) on every "Plugin Request Completed" (grafana-data-egress) line, along with pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName, and dsUID. Those fields were removed in favor of m.logger.FromContext(ctx), but instrumentContext only stores endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, and uname via log.WithContextualAttributes. Nothing puts traceID into that attribute set, so completion logs lose the trace correlation field even when a trace ID is present on the context.

title: TestLogger.FromContext drops recorded logs
body: TestLogger.FromContext ignores the receiver and returns NewTestLogger(). LoggerMiddleware now emits "Plugin Request Completed" via logger.FromContext(ctx).Info, so any test that injects *TestLogger and asserts InfoLogs will see zero calls: the Info is written to a discarded logger. The fake also fails the new interface contract that FromContext returns a logger carrying this logger's context.

title: Device-limit denial is cached, so a retry bypasses the limit
body: tagDeviceUI writes the device key into localCache before CreateOrUpdateDevice returns. When the store rejects a new device with ErrDeviceLimitReached, that key stays cached for the default 29 minutes and the error is returned only for the current call. Authenticate treats that error as a hard failure, but the next anonymous request for the same X-Grafana-Device-Id hits the cache, returns nil, and is issued an anonymous identity without ever being inserted or counted. Refreshing once therefore bypasses the configured device limit, and those sessions never appear in the 30-day count, so the cap stays artificially low. Clear the cache entry (or set it only after a successful write) when tagging fails.

title: Device limit check is not atomic with insert
body: CreateOrUpdateDevice counts active rows and, only if count < deviceLimit, runs a separate INSERT. Those steps are not in one transaction and take no lock, so concurrent anonymous logins can all observe the same count below the cap and all insert. The configured limit can be exceeded under parallel traffic (multiple Grafana instances make this worse). Enforce the cap in the same transaction as the insert, or with a row/advisory lock, so the count and write cannot race.

title: Wire provider signature changed but generated injector was not updated
body: ProvideAnonymousDeviceService no longer accepts anonstore.AnonStore and now requires db.DB, and ProvideAnonDBStore gained a deviceLimit argument. Grafana constructs this service from the checked-in Wire injector (pkg/server/wire_gen.go), which is not in this PR. The existing injector still calls the old signature, so the OSS server package will not compile until wire is regenerated and any other call sites are updated.

title: New auth.anonymous device_limit setting is undocumented
body: AnonymousDeviceLimit is read from [auth.anonymous] device_limit (default 0 = unlimited) but this PR does not add the key to conf/defaults.ini or the auth configuration docs. Operators have no documented name, default, or meaning for the limit, so the feature cannot be configured from the shipped sample config.

title: Device limit is bypassed after the first request
body: tagDeviceUI writes the device cache key before CreateOrUpdateDevice returns. When the store is at the limit, a new device's first TagDevice call fails with ErrDeviceLimitReached (so Authenticate denies that request), but the key is already cached for 29 minutes. Every later request for that device ID hits the cache and returns nil without touching the database, so anonymous authentication succeeds and the device is never counted. The configured limit therefore only fails a single attempt per device per cache TTL and does not actually cap anonymous access.

title: Device limit check is not atomic with the insert
body: CreateOrUpdateDevice reads CountDevices and, only if the count is still under deviceLimit, performs a separate INSERT. Those steps are not in one transaction and are not serialized with the existing server lock, so concurrent anonymous requests (including across Grafana replicas sharing the database) can all observe count < limit and all insert. The configured cap can be exceeded by the number of in-flight creates, and nothing in the schema enforces the limit.

title: New auth.anonymous device_limit setting is undocumented
body: AnonymousDeviceLimit is read from auth.anonymous device_limit (default 0, meaning unlimited), but this change does not add the key to defaults.ini / sample.ini or any docs. Operators have no documented way to discover the setting, its default, or that 0 disables enforcement, so the feature cannot be configured as intended.

title: Cache is set before the limit check, so a rejected device is allowed on retry
body: tagDeviceUI writes the device cache key before CreateOrUpdateDevice returns. When the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, Authenticate fails once, but the key stays cached for 29 minutes. The next request for that device hits the cache, TagDevice returns nil, and anonymous authentication succeeds without ever recording the device. The configurable limit is therefore bypassed by any client that retries within the cache TTL. Set the cache only after a successful write, and do not treat a cached rejection as success.

title: Device limit check and insert are not atomic
body: CreateOrUpdateDevice counts recent devices and, if the count is under AnonymousDeviceLimit, inserts in a separate session with no transaction or row lock. Concurrent first-time devices can all observe count < limit and all insert, so the stored device count exceeds the configured cap and anonymous auth is granted past the limit. The count and the insert/upsert need to be serialized (single transaction with a lock, or an insert that fails when the cap is already reached).

title: Wire providers changed but generated injectors are not updated
body: ProvideAnonymousDeviceService no longer takes anonstore.AnonStore and now takes db.DB, and ProvideAnonDBStore gained an int64 deviceLimit argument. Grafana builds this graph with Google Wire and commits wire_gen.go; this PR does not update wire.go or wire_gen.go. Wire cannot provide a bare int64 to ProvideAnonDBStore, so regeneration will fail and the current generated injector will not compile against the new signatures.

title: device_limit is not added to defaults.ini
body: auth.anonymous device_limit is read via MustInt64(0) (0 means unlimited) but conf/defaults.ini and sample config are unchanged. Operators have no documented key, default, or meaning, and Grafana config docs are generated from defaults.ini, so the new limit cannot be discovered or set from the shipped configuration.

title: Cleanup debug logs left at Error level with full ID lists
body: CleanAnnotations and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags call r.log.Error on every batch (lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, and 579), including the successful path where err is nil. Each line dumps the full ids slice and the SQL condition. With a configured batch size in the tens of thousands this writes enormous error-level log records on every cleanup cycle even when nothing is wrong, flooding logs and adding allocation/IO cost to the job the PR is trying to make safer. These should be removed or reduced to debug without the ID list.

title: Cleanup ticker shortened from 10 minutes to 1 minute
body: Run now starts the background cleanup ticker at 1 minute instead of 10. Nothing in the PR description or the deadlock fix requires this, and it looks like leftover debugging next to the new Error logs. clean() uses a 9-minute timeout and runs synchronously, while time.Ticker buffers one tick, so a job longer than a minute will be re-entered immediately and the whole cleanup suite (annotations, snapshots, dashboard versions, images, invites, short URLs, query history) can run nearly continuously. That multiplies database load and can recreate the write contention this change is meant to avoid.

title: SQLite ID list built with quadratic string concatenation
body: When the SQLite fallback inlines IDs because AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize exceeds 999, deleteByIDs grows the IN-list with fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v) on every element. That copies the whole string each iteration. The new integration test exercises this path with a batch of 32767, so a single DELETE statement build is quadratic in the batch size and can stall the cleanup goroutine for a large annotation table. Build the list with strings.Builder or strings.Join instead.

title: Cleanup job interval accidentally reduced from 10 minutes to 1
body: Run() now starts the cleanup ticker at 1 minute instead of 10. Nothing in this change describes or tests a schedule change, and clean() still uses a 9-minute timeout, so this looks like leftover debug. After merge, annotation cleanup (and every other cleanup job) runs about 10x more often, increasing DB load and lock contention—the opposite of the deadlock fix—and a slow run can still be in progress when the next tick is due.

title: Leftover Error logs dump every cleanup batch, including all IDs
body: CleanAnnotations and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags log successful fetch/delete steps with log.Error, including the full ID slice and SQL condition (lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, and 579). These fire on every batch, even when nothing is deleted. In production that spams error-level logs and can serialize tens of thousands of IDs per batch (the new test uses a batch size of 32767), adding load and drowning real errors. These should be removed or dropped to debug without the ID list.

title: Cleanup logs full ID batches at Error level
body: CleanAnnotations and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags call r.log.Error on every batch for both the ID fetch and the delete (lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, and 579), including the full ids slice and the SQL condition. These run on the success path (err is nil) and again when a batch finds nothing. With AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize in the thousands, each line can dump tens of thousands of IDs. That floods production logs, trips error-based alerts, and allocates large log payloads on every cleanup cycle. These should be removed or dropped to debug without the ID list before merge.

title: Cleanup ticker shortened from 10 minutes to 1 minute
body: Run now uses time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 1) instead of 10 minutes. The PR is only about splitting annotation cleanup queries to avoid MySQL deadlocks; nothing in the description changes the job cadence. clean() still uses a 9-minute timeout that was sized for a 10-minute period, so a slow cycle now finishes and immediately starts another. Annotation cleanup is exactly the workload that was deadlocking writers, so running it about 10x more often increases DB load and makes that failure mode more likely. Restore the 10-minute interval unless the schedule change is intentional and the timeout is updated to match.

title: SQLite ID list is built with quadratic string concatenation
body: When the dialect is SQLite and AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize is above 999, deleteByIDs builds the IN-list with values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v) once per ID. Each iteration copies the entire growing string. The new test uses batch size 32767, so this path copies on the order of hundreds of megabytes to gigabytes of intermediate strings per DELETE and can stall or time out cleanup (and CI) for a batch that was supposed to be a simple workaround for SQLite's parameter limit. Build the list with strings.Builder or strings.Join instead.

title: Async legacy writes inherit the request context and are cancelled when the handler returns
body: Create, Delete, Update, and DeleteCollection start the legacy write in a goroutine via context.WithTimeoutCause on the incoming request context (lines 51, 110, 135, and 163). That child context is cancelled as soon as the apiserver finishes the request and cancels the parent, which is normally before the 10s timeout. The legacy write that mode 3 is supposed to perform as a safety copy therefore fails immediately with context canceled, so legacy storage silently diverges from unified storage.

title: Legacy create/update replay the caller's object instead of the unified result
body: After Storage.Create returns, the goroutine calls Legacy.Create with the same obj pointer the storage implementation just mutated (UID, resourceVersion, timestamps). Legacy.Update (line 139) likewise reuses the original UpdatedObjectInfo instead of writing the object Storage.Update already produced. The previous mode 3 update path wrapped that result so both stores stored the same bytes. Legacy optimistic concurrency then sees the unified resourceVersion, rejects or no-ops the write, and the two stores diverge. Failures are not logged, only counted, so the mismatch is invisible.

title: Storage failures and legacy delete-collection are recorded on the wrong metric series
body: On Storage.Create failure the code calls recordLegacyDuration (line 45) instead of recordStorageDuration; Storage.Update failure does the same at line 129. Successful Delete records the object name as the kind label (line 106: recordStorageDuration(..., name, ...)) instead of options.Kind, so the kind cardinality is object names. The legacy DeleteCollection goroutine calls recordStorageDuration (line 166) rather than recordLegacyDuration, so legacy latency and errors are attributed to unified storage. Mode 3 dashboards and alerts will mis-attribute failures and cannot tell whether the safety write succeeded.

title: Mode 3 unit tests mock the wrong store and never wait for the legacy goroutine
body: The create/update/delete error cases set expectations on Legacy (or none on Storage) even though the implementation returns the Storage error and only then calls Legacy. An unmocked Storage.Create returns a nil error, so the wantErr cases do not exercise the path they name. Success cases start an unsynchronized goroutine that calls Legacy after the test function returns and never assert that the legacy call happened or that its error was recorded. These tests will flake or panic on the mock after the test ends and do not lock in the dual-write contract.

title: Mode 3 playlist integration test reads legacy immediately after an async write
body: The new mode 3 file/unified/etcd cases call doPlaylistTests, which creates, updates, and deletes through the Kubernetes API and then immediately lists and gets the same objects on the legacy /api/playlists endpoints (around lines 522-531 and getFromBothAPIs). Mode 3 only copies to legacy asynchronously and does not wait for that copy, so those assertions race the goroutine and will flake or fail even when the async write would eventually succeed.

title: Async legacy writes inherit the request context and are cancelled on return
body: Create, Delete, Update, and DeleteCollection start the legacy write in a goroutine with context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, 10s). That child is still cancelled as soon as the incoming request context is cancelled, which happens when the handler returns the unified-storage result. The 10s timeout never applies. The legacy "safe measure" write is therefore raced against request completion and will usually fail with context.Canceled, so legacy storage diverges from unified storage with no retry. Derive the background work from context.WithoutCancel (then apply the timeout), and log the legacy error instead of only recording a metric.

title: Legacy Update reuses the same UpdatedObjectInfo concurrently
body: After Storage.Update returns, the goroutine calls Legacy.Update with the same objInfo value. UpdatedObjectInfo implementations typically cache the computed object or mutate internal state on the first UpdatedObject call, and Storage.Update may still be using that state. Running both updates at once races on that shared object and no longer writes the unified-storage result into legacy (the previous code snapshotted the updated object and applied that exact object to legacy). Legacy can fail optimistic concurrency, apply a different patch, or panic, so the two stores diverge.

title: Successful Delete records the object name as the metric kind label
body: On the Delete success path, recordStorageDuration is called with name (the object name) where every other call passes options.Kind. If that argument is a Prometheus label, each deleted object creates a new series and cardinality grows without bound. The error path on the previous line correctly uses options.Kind, so success and failure are also not comparable.

title: Storage failures and legacy delete-collection are recorded on the wrong histogram
body: Create and Update record a storage error with recordLegacyDuration (lines 45 and 129), so a unified-storage failure is counted as a legacy-storage failure and is missing from the storage histogram.
