DeleteCollection's async legacy call (line 166) uses recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, so legacy delete-collection latency and errors are attributed to unified storage. Mode 3 latency/error dashboards will be wrong and can hide a broken legacy backfill.

title: Destroy does not wait for in-flight legacy goroutines
body: Destroy closes Storage and Legacy immediately while Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection may still be running legacy writes in detached goroutines. Those calls can hit a destroyed backend (panic or lost write) during shutdown or mode switch, and there is no way for the caller to know the backfill finished.

title: Mode 3 tests never observe the async legacy write and mock the wrong store on errors
body: The Create error case is named as a unified-storage failure but only stubs Legacy.Create, and Storage.Create has no expectation, so the test does not exercise the path it claims. Success cases start legacy work in a goroutine and return without AssertCalled, a wait, or AssertExpectations, so a missing or panicked legacy write still passes. The playlist mode 3 integration test then reads the legacy API immediately after a k8s write, which will flake or fail for the same unsynchronized async path.

title: Async legacy writes are cancelled with the request
body: Create, Update, Delete, and DeleteCollection start the legacy write in a goroutine using context.WithTimeoutCause on the incoming request context. That child is cancelled as soon as the parent request context is cancelled, which the apiserver does when the handler returns—before the 10s timeout can matter. The legacy write that mode 3 relies on as a safety copy therefore fails with context.Canceled (or never runs to completion), so legacy storage diverges from unified storage while the API still returns success. The goroutines also drop the legacy error instead of logging it, so the failure is silent. Detach from cancellation (for example context.WithoutCancel) before applying the timeout, and log legacy failures.

title: Legacy update no longer applies the same object snapshot
body: Update now passes the original objInfo into both Storage.Update and the async Legacy.Update. The previous implementation resolved UpdatedObject once and wrapped that snapshot so both stores wrote the same object. UpdatedObjectInfo is often single-use or not concurrency-safe (patch/apply transformers mutate state and are applied against each store's own current object). Calling it again from the goroutine, concurrently with the in-flight request, can write a different object to legacy, double-apply a patch, or panic. Snapshot the object produced by the unified update and give legacy a fixed UpdatedObjectInfo.

title: Legacy create receives the object mutated by unified create
body: After Storage.Create returns, the same obj pointer is passed to the async Legacy.Create. Unified/etcd create fills in resourceVersion, UID, and timestamps on that object. Kubernetes create requires an empty resourceVersion, so the legacy create will be rejected or persist unified-storage metadata. Copy the object before the storage create (or deep-copy the pre-create input for legacy) so the safety write is a real create of the client's object.

title: Dual-writer metrics record the wrong store or label
body: On Storage.Create failure the duration is recorded with recordLegacyDuration (line 45); Storage.Update failure does the same (line 129). Delete success records recordStorageDuration with the object name as the kind label (line 106) instead of options.Kind. DeleteCollection's legacy goroutine records recordStorageDuration (line 166) instead of recordLegacyDuration. Failure and latency dashboards for mode 3 will attribute unified-storage errors to legacy, legacy delete-collection latency to storage, and delete metrics to a per-object series, so the safety-write signal this mode depends on is wrong.

title: Destroy does not wait for in-flight legacy goroutines
body: Destroy closes Storage and Legacy immediately while Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection may still be running legacy writes in unbounded goroutines. Shutdown or mode switches can destroy a store underneath those calls, dropping the safety write or racing use-after-close. Track the goroutines and wait for them (with the existing timeout) before Destroy returns.

title: Mode 3 playlist tests assume synchronous legacy writes
body: The new mode 3 integration cases reuse doPlaylistTests, which immediately lists and gets playlists through the legacy /api/playlists endpoints after k8s create, update, and delete (around the legacy search at line 522 and getFromBothAPIs). Mode 3 returns as soon as unified storage succeeds and only then writes legacy in the background, and that background context is cancelled when the request ends. Those assertions will flake or fail, and they never wait for the legacy write. The unit tests in dualwriter_mode3_test.go have the same gap: they return without waiting for or asserting the legacy mock calls, so a missing or cancelled legacy write still passes.

title: Cache fill is not rechecked under the write lock
body: GetWebAssets snapshots entryPointAssetsCache under a read lock, drops that lock, and only then takes the write lock and always reloads and assigns entryPointAssetsCache. Two callers that both observe a nil cache can both enter the write section. If the first finishes and publishes a good manifest, the second still overwrites it—including with nil when its read fails—so a successful fill is discarded and later non-dev callers miss the cache or all redo the load. After Lock, re-read the cache and return it when non-nil and not in dev, and do not assign a failed result over an existing entry.

title: Write path never rechecks cache and can wipe a good value
body: GetWebAssets drops the read lock, then later takes the write lock and always reloads and assigns entryPointAssetsCache = result (line 69), including when the load fails and result is nil. There is no second check of entryPointAssetsCache under the write lock. Two callers can both observe a nil cache; the first populates it successfully and the second then overwrites that pointer with nil (or a redundant load) if its file read fails. Later non-dev requests miss the cache and fail until a later load succeeds. After Lock(), return the existing cache when Env is not Dev and it is already non-nil, and do not store a nil/error result over a successful one.

title: Cache fill is not rechecked under the write lock
body: GetWebAssets drops the read lock and then takes the write lock without checking entryPointAssetsCache again. Concurrent cold calls (and any Dev reload) all proceed to read the manifest and then unconditionally assign entryPointAssetsCache = result, including when result is nil because the read failed. A failing caller can therefore wipe a cache that another goroutine just populated, and return an error even though a valid snapshot already existed. Later non-Dev requests miss the cache and stampede on disk again. Re-read the pointer after Lock and return the existing value when Env is not Dev and the cache is already non-nil; only publish a new pointer on success.

title: SQL kill-switch reported as invalid SQL
body: The legacy expression path still builds a SQLCommand via NewSQLCommand, which calls sql.TablesList. That now always fails because pkg/expr/sql/db.go RunCommands returns "not implemented" after DuckDB was removed. NewSQLCommand maps every such failure to a BadRequest (sql-invalid-sql / "error reading SQL command") and logs "invalid sql query". Previously valid SQL expressions are therefore rejected as malformed user SQL, not as a disabled feature. ExpressionQueryReader is a second entry point and returns a different error, "sqlExpressions is not implemented" (pkg/expr/reader.go), while enableSqlExpressions ignores FlagSqlExpressions and always returns false. Clients and the UI cannot tell a security disable (CVE-2024-9264) from a bad query, and the still-documented feature flag does not change either outcome.

title: No test that SQL expressions stay disabled
body: This change removes the DuckDB engine and is meant to close RCE/LFI via SQL expressions, but it adds no test that a SQL expression is rejected on both entry points (ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery and UnmarshalSQLCommand/Execute) and that no query is executed. The only enforcement on the legacy path is a stub whose errors are labeled "not implemented", and enableSqlExpressions is an inverted flag check that happens to return false on every branch. A regression that fills in the stub or "fixes" that helper would restore execution with no CI failure. The PR description records only manual checks.

title: SQL disable is a dead flag check that always returns false
body: enableSqlExpressions reads FlagSqlExpressions, inverts it, and then returns false from both branches. SQL expressions are therefore always rejected, but the check does not implement a real allow/deny policy and looks like a mistaken edit. A later cleanup that “fixes” the inversion (return the flag, or return true when the flag is on) would re-open the DuckDB SQL expression path that this change is meant to kill for CVE-2024-9264. The disable should be an obvious unconditional false (or the SQL command type removed), not a flag read whose result is discarded.

title: Rejection error says SQL expressions are unimplemented
body: When a SQL expression is parsed, ReadQuery returns fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented"). That text is wrong: the type was implemented and is being hard-disabled because DuckDB evaluation allowed RCE/LFI. Operators and the still-documented feature flag will treat this as a missing feature to turn back on, not as an intentional security shutdown. The error should say SQL expressions are disabled.

title: No regression test that SQL expressions cannot run
body: The security fix only stubs sql.DB and adds a gate in ExpressionQueryReader. UnmarshalSQLCommand still builds a SQLCommand and Execute still calls QueryFramesInto; both fail only because the new stubs return "not implemented". Nothing in this change asserts that a SQL expression query is rejected on the reader path and on UnmarshalSQLCommand/Execute, or that no DuckDB/process call is made. A partial revert that restores a real TablesList or QueryFramesInto would ship without a failing test.

title: SQL kill switch inverts the flag and always returns false
body: enableSqlExpressions sets enabled to the negation of FlagSqlExpressions and then returns false from both branches, so the flag is never honored and the control flow does not match the function name. This is the only gate on the ExpressionQueryReader SQL path (the error "sqlExpressions is not implemented" at the call site). A reviewer "correcting" the obvious inversion so the fall-through returns true would turn SQL expressions back on whenever the documented feature flag is enabled, which is exactly the CVE-2024-9264 surface. The disablement should be an explicit return false with a comment that SQL expressions are hard-disabled because of that CVE, and it should not read the flag with a negated condition.

title: Disabled SQL expressions report "not implemented"
body: When a SQL expression is rejected, ReadQuery returns fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented"). The feature was implemented and is being turned off to stop RCE/LFI (CVE-2024-9264); the feature flag and its docs are intentionally left in place. Operators who enable that flag, or clients that already send type=sql, will treat this as a missing feature or a bad deploy rather than a security disablement, and may try to turn the flag on or restore DuckDB. The error should say SQL expressions are disabled.

title: No test that SQL expressions cannot reach DuckDB
body: The CVE fix removes go-duck and stubs DB.RunCommands, DB.QueryFramesInto, and DB.TablesList, and rejects QueryTypeSQL in ExpressionQueryReader. Nothing in the change asserts either entry point. UnmarshalSQLCommand/NewSQLCommand still calls sql.TablesList, which still interpolates the user query into SELECT json_serialize_sql('...') and only fails because the stub returns an error; Execute still calls QueryFramesInto. A regression that restores a real in-memory DB, or that drops the reader check, would not be caught. Add a test that both ReadQuery and UnmarshalSQLCommand/Execute reject SQL expressions and never invoke a real engine.

title: Concurrent index init races on shared err
body: searchSupport.init launches one errgroup goroutine per namespace and each one does `_, _, err = s.build(...)` plus `totalBatchesIndexed++` on variables declared outside the loop. Those are unsynchronized shared writes. With BuildIndex no longer holding a process-wide lock, these goroutines actually run together, so a failed build can have its error overwritten by a later successful one (startup proceeds with a missing index) or a finished success can be overwritten by another goroutine's error (startup fails spuriously). The counter read for the trace event is likewise racy.

title: Same-key index builds no longer serialized
body: BuildIndex used to hold cacheMu for the whole build, which at least serialized bleve.New and cache publication. The lock is now taken only to assign b.cache[key]. getOrCreateIndex still does check-then-act (GetIndex, then build) with no per-key singleflight, and init can build many namespaces at once. Two callers for the same NamespacedResource can both pass GetIndex, both call bleve.New on the same directory (file indexes fail or corrupt the on-disk index), and the last cache write wins while the other caller keeps using the orphaned index. Searches and watch updates then diverge.

title: TotalDocs iterates the cache map without the mutex
body: TotalDocs ranges over b.cache with no cacheMu held, while BuildIndex writes that map under cacheMu. searchSupport.init now starts the watch goroutine (which can BuildIndex a namespace that was below the init threshold) and then calls TotalDocs for the new startup log. A concurrent map write during that iteration panics the process.

title: Failed constructor Init leaks lifecycle and in-flight builds
body: NewResourceServer now calls s.Init and, on error, returns nil without s.cancel() or lifecycle.Stop. Init runs lifecycle.Init (SQL backend opens the DB) before search.init. If index build fails, the caller has no server handle to stop the backend, so the DB pool is leaked. The cancelable context passed into the errgroup is also dropped, so in-flight namespace builds keep running after the constructor has already failed. Previously Init errors were returned on the live server, which could still be stopped.

title: Search watch loop panics when the event channel closes
body: After the index build, init always starts `for { v := <-events; s.handleEvent(watchctx, v) }` on context.Background(), not the server context. WatchWriteEvents' poller closes that channel when the SQL backend is stopped. A receive on a closed channel yields a nil *WrittenEvent, and handleEvent immediately reads evt.Type, which panics. Because init now runs inside NewResourceServer, every storage server starts this goroutine, and shutdown (server.Stop / backend cancel) will crash it. The goroutine also cannot be cancelled independently of the SQL poller.

title: Storage-server startup test skipped on postgres
body: TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer is the integration test that constructs and runs a storage-server target, which now builds the unified index inside NewResourceServer/InitializeModuleServer. The change skips that test whenever GRAFANA_TEST_DB=postgres, with a TODO that it fails in Drone. Postgres startup regressions from eager index init (the failure mode this PR is fixing) will not be caught in CI.

title: BuildIndex span context is still discarded
body: The PR's stated trace fix is to pass the span context into child work (`ctx, span := tracer.Start`). BuildIndex, which this change edits, still does `_, span := b.tracer.Start(...)`. The builder callback and SQL list work started from the incoming ctx are not children of the BuildIndex span, so the index-build trace stays disconnected from the work it wraps.

title: BuildIndex no longer serializes builds of the same key
body: BuildIndex used to hold cacheMu for the whole build, which also prevented two callers from indexing the same NamespacedResource at once. The lock is now taken only to insert the finished index. getOrCreateIndex is still check-then-act (GetIndex nil, then build), and init runs builds with an errgroup, so two builds of one key can overlap. The later insert overwrites the cache: the discarded index may already have watch updates applied, and the winner is a stale snapshot, so search silently misses writes. For file indexes, a second bleve.New on the same directory can also fail or corrupt the on-disk index. Per-key singleflight (or a lock held from the nil check through cache insert) is required; a shorter global lock alone does not fix the lost-update window.

title: Startup watch starts at latest RV and drops events written during index build
body: init lists each namespace via build(), which returns the resource version observed by that list, then ignores it. Only after every namespace has been indexed does it call WatchWriteEvents, which records listLatestRVs at that later moment and polls strictly after those versions. Any write committed after a namespace's list snapshot and before the watch baseline (other storage-server replicas, or the main Grafana process writing the same DB while this process is still starting) is neither in the built index nor replayed. Moving this work into NewResourceServer makes that window the entire startup index build. The watch must resume from the RV returned by each build, not from the RV at the end of all builds.

title: Index init goroutines race on shared err and counter
body: The errgroup workers in init all assign the outer err from build() and increment totalBatchesIndexed with no synchronization. With WorkerThreads > 1 (the concurrency this change is trying to use), that is a data race: a worker can return another worker's nil and hide a failed namespace build, so Init succeeds while that index was never built. The span attribute namespaced_indexed is also racy. Each worker needs its own error variable, and the counter needs atomic increment or a post-Wait tally.

title: TotalDocs ranges the index cache without cacheMu
body: TotalDocs iterates b.cache with no lock. search.init now starts the watch goroutine and then immediately calls TotalDocs for the new startup log. That goroutine can handle a write for a namespace that was not prebuilt and call BuildIndex, which writes b.cache under cacheMu. Concurrent map iteration and write panics the process during startup. TotalDocs must take cacheMu.RLock (and BuildIndex must keep the write lock around the map update).

title: Startup index watch skips writes that happen during build
body: searchSupport.init builds each namespace with ListIterator, then discards the resource version build returns and only afterwards calls WatchWriteEvents. That watch snapshots the latest RV and polls only events newer than that snapshot. Any write committed after a namespace was listed but at or before the watch snapshot is neither in the index nor replayed. build's own comment says watching must resume from the RV just read. Because Init now runs once at process start and is no longer retried on later RPCs, those documents stay missing from search until another write to the same key.

title: Index init goroutines share err and can hide build failures
body: The errgroup workers in searchSupport.init all assign the outer err from s.build and then return that same err, and they also increment totalBatchesIndexed with no synchronization. Another worker can overwrite err between the assignment and the return, so errgroup.Wait can observe nil even though a build failed (or a spurious error). Init is now synchronous in NewResourceServer and once.Do never retries, so a lost failure starts the server with a partial search index and no error to the caller.

title: BuildIndex no longer serializes same-key builds
body: cacheMu used to be held for the entire BuildIndex. It is now taken only to publish the finished index. getOrCreateIndex is check-then-build with no per-key lock, so two callers for the same NamespacedResource can both see a cache miss and both call bleve.New on the same deterministic directory (Root/namespace/resource.group) or both allocate a memory index. Concurrent bleve.New on one path fails or corrupts the on-disk index; the loser is leaked, and the cache keeps whichever build finishes last, which may not be the one already returned to an in-flight search.

title: TotalDocs ranges the index cache without the mutex
body: TotalDocs iterates b.cache with no cacheMu, while BuildIndex writes b.cache[key] under that lock. The new init log calls TotalDocs immediately after starting the search watch goroutine, which can getOrCreateIndex and BuildIndex for namespaces below InitMinCount as soon as the first poll arrives. Concurrent map read and write panics the process during startup.

title: Postgres storage-server integration test is now skipped
body: TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer is the integration coverage for the storage-server target, and this PR skips it entirely when GRAFANA_TEST_DB=postgres, with a TODO that it fails in Drone. Eager Init inside NewResourceServer is exactly what that test exercises via InitializeModuleServer. Skipping it removes the signal for a postgres startup regression instead of fixing it, so this change can merge while unified storage fails to come up on postgres in CI.

title: UsernameForm calls a method that does not exist
body: UsernameForm.authenticate now calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only method added on UsernamePasswordForm is isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel). UsernameForm does not define a no-arg overload, so this class does not compile and the re-authentication skip change cannot be built or shipped. The call needs to pass the user (or a real no-arg helper) or the authenticator factory will fail to compile.

title: Conditional passkeys UI is skipped when the user is not yet known
body: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires a non-null user, and both authenticate() (around line 115) and the error challenge (around line 137) only call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm when that returns true. Previously the WebAuthn conditional UI (challenge, rpId, ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI) was filled exactly when the user was not already selected, which is the discoverable-credential / passkey login page. After this change that initial form is no longer prepared, so realm passkeys login from the username or username/password page stops working, and a user-not-found error page also loses the passkey form. Re-authentication needs the fill to run when the user is already set; it should not replace the unidentified-user case. Gate on passkeys being enabled, not on user != null.

title: UsernameForm calls a method that does not exist
body: UsernameForm.authenticate now calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only method added on UsernamePasswordForm is isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel). Nothing in the hierarchy defines a no-arg overload, so this class does not compile and the re-authentication skip change cannot be built or deployed.

title: Conditional passkeys no longer set up when the user is unknown
body: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires a non-null user, and both authenticate() and the error challenge() now call fillContextForm only through that helper. Previously webauthn/passkey form data was filled when the user was not yet selected, which is the conditional-UI login path. With this change, the first username/password (and username-only) page omits the challenge, RP ID, and conditional-UI flag whenever context.getUser() is null, so discoverable passkey login on the initial form no longer works. Re-authentication (user already set) is the only path that still gets passkey data. The existing tests that expect //form[@id='webauth'] on the first login page will fail.

title: Call to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not compile
body: UsernameForm.authenticate() calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only method added on UsernamePasswordForm is isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel). There is no no-arg overload in this class or its parents, so this change does not compile and the passkeys re-authentication path cannot be built or tested.

title: Conditional passkeys UI dropped on initial login
body: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) returns true only when the user is already non-null, and both authenticate() (line 115) and the error challenge() (line 137) use that check before fillContextForm(). Previously the WebAuthn conditional UI (challenge, rpId, ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI) was filled when no user was selected yet, which is the username-less/discoverable passkey login. Now the first username/password page and invalid-user error pages never set up passkeys, so conditional passkey login on a fresh authentication no longer works. The user != null requirement should not gate form setup; passkeys-enabled alone should.

title: Login-cache invalidation uses org-wrapped isEnabled and can skip
body: update() loads the pre-image with getById(), which returns the organization-aware wrapper whose isEnabled() is false when the IdP is linked to a missing or disabled organization (or when the organization provider is disabled), even if the stored enabled flag is true. registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate treats that wrapper as "not a login IdP". If the update also makes the raw model ineligible (enabled=false, hideOnLogin, link-only, or broker-public cleared), both predicate checks fail and the method returns without invalidating the getForLogin list keys. Those lists were built from the JPA enabled/hide/link/public filters, so they still contain the IdP. After the org is enabled again, getForLogin keeps returning it, and OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean only re-checks isEnabled(), not hideOnLogin/linkOnly/broker-public, so a hidden or link-only broker can show up on the login page until some other event drops the cache. Compare against the delegate/raw model (or always invalidate login keys on update).

title: getForLogin cache drops provider order
body: Delegate getForLogin results are collected with Collectors.toSet() and then copied into a HashSet before the stream is returned. That discards the stable order previously produced by getAllStream (typically alias or creation order). Login pages sort with a comparator that is usually guiOrder, and the default guiOrder is the same for every broker, so the stable sort keeps HashSet iteration order. Brokers therefore shuffle between requests. Preserve encounter order (for example LinkedHashSet) when caching ids and when building the result stream.

title: Login-cache test cleanup targets alias "alias"
body: testCacheIDPForLogin creates idp-alias-0..20 but registers cleanup as testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove (also at the idp-alias-20 create). That resource is not one of the created providers, so the 21 brokers are left in the shared test realm. Later tests that count or list identity providers can fail or see extra login IdPs, and the new assertions never check that the cached ids are the expected aliases rather than only a size.

title: Login-cache invalidation uses wrapped isEnabled and skips real membership changes
body: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate treats the pre-update model from getById as the source of truth for whether the IdP is a login IdP. With the organization feature on, getById returns a wrapper whose isEnabled() is false whenever the linked organization is missing, disabled, or the organization provider is disabled, even if the stored IdP is enabled. LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate uses that isEnabled(). The getForLogin cache, however, is filled from the JPA query, which only checks the IdP's own enabled, link-only, hide-on-login, and broker-public flags. If the org is disabled (so the wrapped original already fails the predicate) and the update also fails the predicate — for example hide-on-login or link-only is set, broker-public is cleared, or the IdP enabled flag is turned off — both sides fail and the method returns without invalidating the login list caches. Those lists still contain the IdP. After the organization is enabled again, getById shows the updated flags, but OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean only re-checks isEnabled(), not hide-on-login or link-only, so a hidden or link-only broker can be offered on the login page until the cache expires.

title: getForLogin cache drops result order
body: Cached login results are stored in a Set of internal ids and returned from a HashSet. The previous getForLogin implementation returned the delegate stream order (stable storage order, typically alias or guiOrder). HashSet iteration order is undefined and can change between calls even when the membership is unchanged. Callers that do not sort, unlike OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean, will show identity-provider buttons in a shuffling order.

title: Login-cache test cleanup deletes the wrong IdP alias
body: testCacheIDPForLogin registers cleanup with testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove (also at the hide-on-login provider created later in the same test). The providers are actually created as idp-alias-0 through idp-alias-20, so cleanup issues DELETE for a non-existent alias "alias" and leaves every created broker in the shared test realm. Later tests that count identity providers, including testCacheIDPByOrg's expectation of 6 providers for an organization, can fail or become order-dependent, and the new test does not isolate its data.

title: Login-cache invalidation uses org-wrapped isEnabled()
body: update() passes the model from getById() into registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(). With organizations enabled, getById() returns an anonymous IdentityProviderModel whose isEnabled() is false when the organization is missing, disabled, or the organization provider is off, even if the stored IdP is enabled. LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() calls that override. If the organization is disabled, an IdP that is already in the getForLogin cache looks ineligible, and an update that also fails the predicate for a real reason (hideOnLogin, linkOnly, or kc.org.broker.public set to false) hits the early return and does not invalidate .idp.login.*. Organization enable/disable does not invalidate those keys either, and OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean only rechecks isEnabled(), not hide-on-login, link-only, or broker-public. After the organization is enabled again, getForLogin still returns that IdP and the login page can show a link-only or non-public organization broker. Compare storage flags (or always invalidate when the stored IdP is or was login-eligible), and re-apply the login predicate when serving cached ids.

title: Login-cache test never deletes the IdPs it creates
body: testCacheIDPForLogin registers cleanup with testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove (same mistake again at the hide-on-login IdP around line 425). The providers are created as idp-alias-0 … idp-alias-20, so this resource does not refer to them and they are left in the shared test realm. A second run, or any later test that counts realm or login IdPs, will see the leaked brokers and the exact size assertions (5, 6, 10, 11) will fail.

title: order() is abstract and breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: order() was added as a new abstract method on the public CryptoProvider SPI. Existing compiled implementations that are not in this PR (custom or older provider jars) no longer satisfy the interface. CryptoIntegration.detectProvider instantiates every provider via ServiceLoader and immediately calls order() to sort, so those implementations fail at startup with AbstractMethodError instead of being ignored. A default method (for example returning 0) would keep old providers loadable and still let the new authz provider lose to explicitly higher-order ones.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns the JDK keystore provider, not BC
body: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider(), which is the platform keystore provider (typically SunJSSE), not BouncyCastle and not null. Elytron's provider returns null so callers skip BC-specific setup. Callers that do Signature/Cipher.getInstance(alg, provider) with this result look up algorithms only in that provider, which does not implement SHA256withECDSA or the BC padding names Keycloak uses, so ECDSA/JWE operations fail with NoSuchAlgorithmException even though the JDK can perform them. If BouncyIntegration records this provider's name as the crypto provider, later lookups are pinned to the wrong provider for the life of the process.

title: FIPS, Elytron, and default providers share the same order
body: FIPS1402Provider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and DefaultCryptoProvider all return order 200, while detectProvider now keeps the first provider after a stable sort instead of failing when more than one CryptoProvider is on the classpath. Equal order preserves ServiceLoader/classpath order, so a deployment that contains both the FIPS provider and the default (or Elytron) provider silently runs whichever jar appears first. That can disable FIPS mode without an error. FIPS needs a strictly higher order than the non-FIPS providers now that multiple providers are allowed.

title: ECDSA integer conversion silently truncates oversized components
body: integerToBytes, used by asn1derToConcatenatedRS, copies the low qLength bytes whenever BigInteger.toByteArray() is longer than the curve field size and never checks that the discarded prefix is a single 0x00 sign byte. A non-canonical or oversized ASN.1 INTEGER is therefore rewritten into a different in-range R or S instead of being rejected. Signature conversion then succeeds with a value that is not the one that was signed, so verification can fail closed only by chance, or accept a rewritten component, instead of raising IOException on malformed DER.

title: ECDSA tests use one P-256 key and never check JDK verification
body: The suite generates a single KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC") key, which is P-256, and uses it for ES256, ES384, and ES512. It only asserts that asn1derToConcatenatedRS and concatenatedRSToASN1DER round-trip through this provider's own decoder. It never calls Signature.verify on the DER produced by concatenatedRSToASN1DER, and ES384/ES512 never see 48-byte or 66-byte R/S values from a matching curve. A DER encoding that Java's strict verifier rejects, or a high-bit padding bug that only shows up at the real ES384/ES512 sizes, still passes.

title: Equal-order crypto providers are no longer rejected
body: detectProvider used to fail startup when more than one CryptoProvider was on the classpath. It now sorts by order() descending and silently keeps the first winner, logging the rest only at debug. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider all return order 200, so a deployment that accidentally has two of those modules (the case the old check existed for) now boots with whichever ServiceLoader returns first. A FIPS provider can be ignored in favor of the non-FIPS default, or the reverse, with no error. Tie on order should still be a hard failure; only a strictly lower order (the new authz-client provider at 100) should be ignored.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns the default keystore provider
body: getBouncyCastleProvider is documented and used as the BouncyCastle (or BCFIPS) JCA provider. This implementation returns KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider(), which is the JDK keystore provider (typically SUN), not BouncyCastle. WildFlyElytronProvider correctly returns null when BC is absent. When this provider is the one CryptoIntegration selects, callers that register or use getBouncyCastleProvider() will treat a non-BC provider as BouncyCastle and either register the wrong provider or invoke BC-only algorithms against it and fail. Return null if no BC provider is available.

title: New abstract order() breaks existing CryptoProvider implementors
body: order() was added as an abstract method on the public CryptoProvider SPI with no default. Any out-of-tree or not-yet-updated CryptoProvider implementation no longer compiles or loads. A default such as order() returning 0 would keep old providers working and still let the in-tree providers (200) and AuthzClientCryptoProvider (100) win via the new sort.

title: ECDSA tests use one P-256 key and only check a symmetric round trip
body: The suite generates a single KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC") key (platform default, P-256) and reuses it for ES256, ES384, and ES512. R and S are therefore always ~32-byte P-256 integers, then padded to 48 or 66 bytes. The only assertion is that asn1derToConcatenatedRS(concatenatedRSToASN1DER(rs)) equals rs. A conversion that drops high bytes, mishandles the DER sign byte, or emits unverifiable ASN.1 still passes, and ES384/ES512 are never exercised at their real coordinate sizes. Generate a key on the matching curve (P-256/P-384/P-521) and check Signature.verify on the DER form produced by concatenatedRSToASN1DER.

title: Equal-priority crypto providers are chosen nondeterministically
body: detectProvider now sorts CryptoProvider implementations by order() and always returns the first entry, only debug-logging the rest. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider all return the same order (200), and Stream.sorted is only stable with respect to ServiceLoader iteration order, which is classpath-dependent. Previously more than one provider on the classpath was a hard failure. A deployment that accidentally has both the default and FIPS (or Elytron) providers will now start with whichever ServiceLoader yields first, so FIPS mode can silently run non-FIPS algorithms or the reverse, with no error and no warning above debug. Lower-priority providers such as AuthzClientCryptoProvider (order 100) should be ignored, but a tie for the highest order must still fail startup.

title: New order() method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementors
body: order() was added as an abstract interface method with no default. CryptoProvider is a public ServiceLoader SPI. Any out-of-tree or older compiled implementation that is not rebuilt against this change will throw AbstractMethodError as soon as CryptoIntegration.detectProvider calls CryptoProvider::order during startup, and source builds of those providers will fail to compile. A default such as default int order() { return 0; } would keep existing providers loadable while still letting in-repo providers override preference.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns the default keystore provider
body: When this provider is the one selected (standalone authz-client, where no order-200 provider is present), getBouncyCastleProvider() returns KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider(), which is the JDK keystore provider (typically SUN), not BouncyCastle. WildFlyElytronProvider returns null for the same method so callers can skip BC registration. Callers that register or look up algorithms on this Provider object will use the wrong JCA provider, so BC-only algorithms and provider-name checks fail or run against SUN instead of failing fast with UnsupportedOperationException like the other unimplemented methods on this class.

title: All-clients fallback NPEs when the Clients resource is missing
body: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) treats a missing per-client resource as an all-clients check, then calls PolicyStore.findByResource with whatever getResourceTypeResource returns. That helper returns null when the admin-permissions client has no "Clients" resource (schema not initialized, or an already-enabled realm that never received the new type). findByResource(server, null) then throws, so a normal manage/view/configure check becomes a 500 instead of a deny. The same null is later passed into ResourcePermission if the empty-policy guard is skipped.

title: getClientsWithPermission returns the type resource name, not client ids
body: getClientsWithPermission searches resources of type "Clients" and adds resource.getName() for every granted scope. The all-clients resource created by the schema is itself typed "Clients" and named "Clients", so a realm-wide grant inserts the literal "Clients" into the result and does not expand to actual client ids. Callers that filter client lists or role-mapping targets by this set will either hide every real client or treat a non-client id as granted. Per-client resources are only present after a specific permission was created, so an all-clients MAP_ROLES/VIEW grant cannot be applied through this API.

title: Existing admin-permissions clients never get the Clients type or scopes
body: init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already set, and nothing else in this change creates the new Clients resource or the configure, map-roles-client-scope, and map-roles-composite scopes. Realms that already enabled fine-grained admin permissions V2 therefore keep a schema that only has Users. Creating a Clients permission then fails scope validation ("No scopes found" / "Scope was not found for resource type"), and evaluation cannot fall back to an all-clients resource that was never stored.

title: Client permission resources are not resolved to a display name
body: getResourceName now has a Clients resource type whose stored name is the client UUID, but the method only special-cases Users and otherwise returns resource.getDisplayName(). Client resources are created with name set to the internal id and no display name, so admin permission listings show null (or a raw id) instead of the clientId. Deleting or renaming the client also has no equivalent of the user-not-found check, so stale client resources stay unlabeled.

title: V2 client permission hooks throw instead of denying
body: MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() now always returns ClientPermissionsV2 when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is on, but isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, canExchangeTo, resource, getPermissions, and the Policy accessors throw UnsupportedOperationException. Those methods are on the live admin evaluator path (client removal, permissions UI, token exchange). A caller that previously got false/null from the V1 evaluator now fails the request with 500, including for admins who only have realm roles and never opted into per-client policies.

title: Client removal no longer cleans permissions when only V2 is enabled
body: The removal listener is now skipped unless ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) is enabled. With only V2 enabled, ClientRemovedEvent does not run, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws anyway, so there is no cleanup of the authz resource named with the deleted client's id. A later permission evaluation can still grant scopes on that orphan id, and resource listings keep growing after clients are deleted.

title: requireView javadoc describes a boolean return
body: The new comments on requireView and requireViewClientScopes say they return true when canView()/canViewClientScopes() is true. Both methods are void and are documented elsewhere as throwing ForbiddenException. Implementors and callers reading only these comments will treat a failed check as a boolean instead of an authorization failure.

title: Map-role checks ignore manage-clients admins
body: canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles, and canMapClientScopeRoles only call hasPermission and never root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS) or canManage(client). When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is on, MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() always returns this class, so realm admins who only have the manage-clients role are denied mapping client roles, composite roles, and client-scope roles unless a separate FGAP policy exists. Those operations 403 for users who are allowed to manage the client.

title: Missing all-clients resource causes NPE
body: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource when no per-client resource exists, then immediately calls PolicyStore.findByResource(server, resource) and later evaluatePermission without a null check. getResourceTypeResource returns null when the "Clients" resource was never created (see init() early return on an existing admin-permissions client). A view/manage/configure check then throws NullPointerException instead of returning false, so admin API calls 500 rather than 403.

title: Existing admin-permissions client is not migrated
body: init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already set and never adds the new Clients resource type or the configure, map-roles-client-scope, and map-roles-composite scopes. Realms that initialized FGAP V2 when only Users existed keep the old resource server. Creating or evaluating a Clients permission then fails in getScope with "Scope [configure] does not exist" (or the equivalent for the other new scopes), so the feature does not work after upgrade.

title: Per-client resources are created without a type
body: getOrCreateResource creates the client resource with resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, owner) and only updateScopes. It never sets the resource type to CLIENTS, unlike init() which calls resource.setType(type) for the all-clients resource. ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission lists candidates with resourceStore.findByType(..., CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE). Per-client grants are therefore omitted from that set, so admin list/filter paths that rely on getClientsWithPermission drop clients the caller is actually allowed to see. The same query can also include the all-clients resource whose name is the literal "Clients", which is not a client id.

title: Client resource names are not resolved
body: getResourceName only special-cases the Users resource type. Client resources are stored under the internal client id and typically have a null display name, so the method returns null (or a blank display name) for Clients policies. Admin permission APIs and the console therefore show an empty resource name instead of the clientId for client-scoped permissions.

title: V2 client permission methods throw instead of denying
body: canExchangeTo, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, and the permission-policy accessors throw UnsupportedOperationException. With the V2 feature enabled, every clients() call uses this class. Token-exchange checks and the client management-permissions admin endpoints therefore 500 instead of returning false or a disabled permissions representation. The removal listener was gated to the V1 feature, but these other callers were not.

title: Map-roles checks ignore manage and admin roles
body: canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles, and canMapClientScopeRoles only call hasPermission for that one scope. They do not treat AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS or a granted MANAGE permission as sufficient, unlike canManage/canConfigure/canView. With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled, a realm admin or anyone granted manage-clients (or an all-clients manage permission) is denied mapping client roles, composites, and client-scope roles unless a separate map-roles* permission is also granted. That is an authorization regression versus the V1 evaluator and versus the transitive manage behavior already expected for users.

title: Per-client resource hides all-clients permissions
body: hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) loads the resource named by the client id and, if that resource exists, evaluates only that resource. The all-clients resource is consulted only when no per-client resource exists. A client that already has a narrower permission (for example view or configure) will therefore never receive an all-clients manage, view, or map-roles grant, and a negative permission on the type resource will not apply either. Admins who are allowed to manage every client can be forbidden from managing the one client that also has an object-level permission, and the fallback comment in this method is wrong for that case. If getResourceTypeResource returns null, the following findByResource(server, resource) can also NPE instead of denying.

title: Existing admin-permissions clients are not migrated
body: init returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already set, and nothing else in this change creates the new Clients resource type or the configure, map-roles-client-scope, and map-roles-composite scopes. Realms that already enabled fine-grained admin permissions (Users only) keep the old schema. Creating or evaluating a Clients permission then fails in getOrCreateResource ("No scopes found" / missing type resource) or getScope (scope not in the resource server). Upgraded deployments cannot use the new client permissions without a manual re-init.

title: Client id filter includes the type resource name
body: getClientsWithPermission adds resource.getName() for every Clients-typed resource that grants the scope, including the schema resource whose name is "Clients" rather than a client UUID. Callers that filter the client list by this set will either look up a non-existent client id or, when only an all-clients permission exists, return no clients at all. All-clients access is not expanded to real client ids, so partial-list and query paths that depend on this method are wrong.

title: Client resource names are not resolved
body: getResourceName only special-cases the Users type. Client resources created by resolveClient are stored under the internal client id and typically have no display name, so the method falls through to resource.getDisplayName() and returns null. Admin permission APIs and the UI will show a blank name for a client permission instead of the clientId, and a deleted client is not reported as missing the way a missing user is.

title: V2 does not clean up permissions when a client is removed
body: The removal listener now runs only when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) is enabled. Under V2, management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 and clients().setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, so the V1 branch cannot be reused, and no V2 branch deletes the authorization resource named by the removed client id. After a client is deleted, orphaned Clients resources and policies remain on the admin-permissions client and can be matched again if that id is reused or shown as dangling permissions.

title: requireView javadoc describes a boolean return
body: The new javadoc on requireView says it returns true if canView() returns true, and requireViewClientScopes is documented the same way. Both methods are void and are specified elsewhere to throw ForbiddenException. Callers reading only these comments will treat a failed check as a boolean result instead of an authorization failure.

title: Default update-strategy tests never enable rolling-updates
body: createInitialDeployment returns immediately when updateStrategy is null, before the new FeatureSpec setup that enables rolling-updates. Both parameterized tests (testImageChange and testCacheMaxCount) include that null case, which is the documented default strategy. The operator guide in this PR states the preview feature must be enabled or the operator fails, so these cases deploy a CR without the feature and will not exercise (or will fail) the default upgrade path the test is meant to cover. Enable the feature before that return so every strategy, including the default, runs with rolling-updates.

title: Enabling rolling-updates replaces any existing enabled features
body: setEnabledFeatures(List.of(ROLLING_UPDATES)) overwrites the CR's entire enabled-features list instead of appending. If getTestKeycloakDeployment (or a future caller) already set spec.features.enabled, those features are dropped whenever a non-default UpdateStrategy is applied. The server then starts with a different feature set than the rest of the operator suite, so upgrade assertions can pass or fail for the wrong reason. Add rolling-updates to the existing list rather than replacing it.

title: Feature-disabled test does not assert exit code 4
body: testFeatureNotEnabled only checks the error string. This PR makes exit code 4 the contract for a disabled rolling-updates feature (and moves the recreate-upgrade code from 4 to 3). A regression that still prints the message but exits 1, or that leaves recreate on 4, would not be caught. The test should assert exit code 4, and the check subcommand should be covered the same way as metadata.

title: Default update-strategy tests never enable rolling-updates
body: createInitialDeployment returns immediately when updateStrategy is null, and the new spec.features.enabled: rolling-updates assignment is only reached for an explicit strategy. The parameterized cases include null, which is the default "mimic 26.1" path: testImageChange(null) and testCacheMaxCount(null) deploy a CR without the feature. The operator guide added in this PR says the operator fails unless rolling-updates is enabled, and those tests still assert recreate/rolling status. As written, the default-strategy cases either fail reconciliation or only pass because some other image build happens to bake the feature in, so they do not actually cover the configuration users are told to use.

title: Exit-code contract is not asserted
body: This change makes exit status the public contract: recreate incompatibility moves from 4 to 3, and a disabled rolling-updates feature must exit 4. testFeatureNotEnabled only checks the error string, and testWrongVersions only checks the incompatibility message. Neither asserts result.exitCode(). That gap already hid the previous mismatch (code returned 4 while the guide documented 3), so a regression of 0/3/4 will still leave CI green and break scripts that branch on the exit code.

title: Default update-strategy tests never enable rolling-updates
body: createInitialDeployment returns immediately when updateStrategy is null, before enabling Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES. Both parameterized tests include null (the documented default strategy), and testCacheMaxCount(null) expects a successful rolling update. The new operator guide states that while this is preview the rolling-updates feature must be enabled or the Operator fails. Those cases therefore either fail reconciliation or never exercise the feature the PR says is now required.

title: Enabling rolling-updates wipes other CR features
body: When an update strategy is set, the helper replaces the entire enabled-features list with List.of(rolling-updates) instead of appending to any features already on the FeatureSpec. If getTestKeycloakDeployment (or a future caller) has already enabled features, they are dropped on the CR. The server then starts without those features, so upgrade tests can fail or pass for the wrong reason.

title: Disabled-feature test never checks exit code 4
body: testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the stderr text. The contract added in this PR is that metadata/check exit 4 when rolling-updates is disabled (and recreate was moved to 3 so 4 is no longer 'recreate'). Automation is documented to branch on that code. A regression that prints the message but exits 0, 1, or 3 would still pass this test.

title: All-groups VIEW satisfies canManage()
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE) succeeds, so a caller who only has the all-groups view scope is treated as allowed to manage groups. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup (and any other requireManage() gate) therefore lets a view-only admin create groups. canManage(GroupModel) correctly checks only MANAGE, so the no-arg method is inconsistent with the per-group check and with V1, which required MANAGE_USERS. A view permission must not authorize mutations.

title: View-members group filter uses authz resource ids
body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() walks resources with findByType(GROUPS) and, on a match, calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) and adds groupResource.getId() to the set later passed to user search/count as UserModel.GROUPS. FGAP group resources are stored by name equal to the group id (resolveGroup returns group.getId()), while getId() is the authorization resource primary key. The permission lookup therefore searches by the wrong name, misses the group policy, and falls back to the all-groups resource; the ids handed to getUsersCount/searchForUserStream are not group ids. Admins who only have view-members or manage-members on specific groups get an empty or wrong membership filter, so user search and counts omit those members (pagination is applied in the DB before the canView post-filter). The type resource named "Groups" is also included by findByType and must be skipped. Use the resource name (the group id) and evaluate that resource directly.

title: Per-group FGAP resources are created without type
body: getOrCreateResource creates a resource named with the group id and sets scopes, but never calls setType(GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE). The all-groups resource created in init() does set type. GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission relies on resourceStore.findByType(..., GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE), so individually permissioned groups are invisible to that scan even after the id/name bug is fixed. Set the type when creating the resource (same as the type-level resource).

title: Existing admin-permissions clients never get Groups schema
body: init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already set, and this PR adds the Groups resource type plus manage-membership, manage-members, and view-members scopes only on that first-time path. Realms that already enabled admin permissions V2 keep a client whose resource server has neither the Groups type resource nor the new scopes. Creating a group permission then fails in getOrCreateResource (ModelException "No scopes found") or scope validation, so the feature does not work on upgrade. init (or a migration) must add missing schema scopes and the Groups type resource to an existing admin-permissions client.

title: Group removal calls V2-unsupported permission teardown
body: registerListener still handles GroupModel.GroupRemovedEvent by calling management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false) whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled. This PR makes management() return MgmtPermissionsV2 when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, and GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException. If both features are on, deleting a group fails the admin event listener and can abort the removal. The listener must no-op (or use a V2 cleanup) when the V2 evaluator is active.

title: requireManageMembers javadoc cites the wrong check
body: The javadoc on requireManageMembers says it throws if canManageMembership(GroupModel) is false. The implementation throws when canManageMembers is false. Callers reading the contract will enforce the wrong scope (manage-membership vs manage-members).

title: Group canManage() treats VIEW as manage
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE) succeeds, so a caller who only has the Groups VIEW scope is treated as allowed to manage every group. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() (and any other requireManage() caller) therefore lets a view-only fine-grained admin create groups. V1 canManage() only checks MANAGE_USERS, and canManage(GroupModel) correctly checks only MANAGE. The VIEW scope must not satisfy canManage(); the interface comment that lists VIEW looks copied from canView().

title: View-members group filter uses authz resource ids
body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() walks resources with findByType and then calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) and granted.add(groupResource.getId()). V2 group resources are stored under the group id as the resource name (resolveGroup returns group.getId()), while getId() is the authorization resource UUID. hasPermission looks that value up with findByName, so the per-group permission check misses and falls back to the all-groups resource. The set passed to UserModel.GROUPS / getUsersCount is therefore not a set of group ids. User search and user counts for admins who can only view members of specific groups (UsersResource, BruteForceUsersResource) will drop those users or match the wrong groups.

title: Created group resources never get type Groups
body: getOrCreateResource() creates a resource and updates scopes but never calls resource.setType(resourceType). V1 group resources were typed "Group". GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() only discovers groups via resourceStore.findByType(..., GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE). Without the type, individual group permission resources are invisible to that scan, so membership-based user visibility cannot be computed even after the id/name mix-up is fixed. The all-groups resource created in init() does set the type; per-object resources must do the same.

title: Existing admin-permissions clients are not upgraded for Groups
body: init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already non-null, and that is the only place scopes and the "Groups" resource type are created. Realms that already enabled FGAP V2 (client created with only Users/Clients) never receive GROUPS, manage-membership, manage-members, or view-members. Creating a group permission then fails in getOrCreateResource with ModelException "No scopes found", and GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission() NPEs when getResourceTypeResource() returns null and that null is passed to policyStore.findByResource / resource.getScopes(). Schema init needs an idempotent update path for new resource types and scopes.

title: requireManageMembers javadoc cites the wrong check
body: The javadoc on requireManageMembers says it throws if canManageMembership(GroupModel) is false. The implementation throws when canManageMembers is false. Callers reading only the interface will enforce or test the wrong scope (manage-membership vs manage-members).

title: All-groups VIEW permission grants realm-wide group manage
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE) succeeds, so an admin who only has the Groups VIEW scope on the all-groups resource is treated as allowed to manage every group. requireManage() is the gate for creating top-level groups (GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup) and other mutations that call canManage() with no group. A view-only fine-grained permission therefore authorizes group creation and other manage operations. canManage() must require MANAGE (or MANAGE_USERS), not VIEW.

title: Group member search uses authorization resource ids, not group ids
body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() walks resources with findByType and then calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId()) and granted.add(groupResource.getId()). In the V2 schema the group id is the resource name (resolveGroup returns group.getId(), and getOrCreateResource stores that as the name); getId() is the authorization resource UUID. hasPermission looks that UUID up with findByName, misses the group resource, and either skips the permission or falls back to the all-groups resource. The set stored on the session as UserModel.GROUPS (UsersResource and BruteForceUsersResource searches, and getUsersCount) therefore does not contain group ids. Admins granted view-members or manage-members on specific groups get empty user searches and zero counts, or a filter on ids that match no groups.

title: Per-group authorization resources are created without the Groups type
body: getOrCreateResource creates a resource named with the group id and updates scopes, but never calls setType(GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE). Only the schema all-groups resource created in init() has type Groups. GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() discovers candidates solely via resourceStore.findByType(..., GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE). Individual group resources are invisible to that scan, so view-members and manage-members permissions on a single group never contribute group ids to user search or user counts. V1 set the type explicitly ("Group"); V2 needs the same when creating the resource.

title: Existing admin-permissions clients never gain Groups scopes or resources
body: init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already set, and this change only adds Groups (and manage-membership, manage-members, view-members) to the schema used at first creation. Realms that already enabled fine-grained admin permissions V2 keep a client with no Groups resource type and no new scopes. Creating a group permission then hits getOrCreateResource, which throws ModelException("No scopes found.") when scopeStore.findByName cannot resolve the new scope names. Permission checks that fall back to getResourceTypeResource also get null and then NPE in GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission on policyStore.findByResource(server, null) or resource.getScopes(). Enabling the feature must migrate an existing admin-permissions client, not only bootstrap a new one.

title: Group permission resources have no display name
body: getResourceName() only special-cases the Users resource type and otherwise returns resource.getDisplayName(). Group resources are created with the group id as the name and no display name, and this PR never teaches getResourceName to resolve GROUPS the way it resolves users to usernames. Admin APIs and the UI that list fine-grained permissions will show a null name for every group resource instead of the group name or path.

title: requireManageMembers javadoc cites the wrong check
body: The new javadoc on requireManageMembers says it throws if canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false. The method is required to enforce canManageMembers. Callers and implementors following the comment will apply the membership scope instead of manage-members.

title: Account UI error uses Java MessageFormat, not i18next placeholders
body: error-invalid-multivalued-size was changed from i18next placeholders ({{0}}, {{1}}, {{2}}) to Java MessageFormat ({0} and a {2,choice,...} pattern). Every other string in this account-ui bundle still uses {{name}} / {{0}}. The account console does not run these strings through MessageFormat, so the attribute name and limits are never substituted and the raw choice pattern is shown. The same 1<values fragment can also be parsed as an i18next/Trans tag and break rendering of the validation error.

title: Admin UI error switched to Java MessageFormat placeholders
body: error-invalid-multivalued-size in the React admin UI bundle was rewritten from {{0}}/{{1}}/{{2}} to Java MessageFormat {0} plus a ChoiceFormat clause. Admin UI interpolates {{ }} (i18next), not java.text.MessageFormat, so this validation message will display literal {0}, {1}, and {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values} instead of the attribute name and limits. The embedded <values> can also be treated as a translation component tag.

title: Lithuanian login TOTP step replaced with Italian
body: loginTotpStep1 was replaced with "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:", which is Italian, not Lithuanian. Users with the lt locale will see the wrong language on the authenticator setup step, and the previous Lithuanian wording (including the FreeOTP/Google Play links) is gone.

title: Lithuanian account TOTP step replaced with Italian
body: totpStep1 in the Lithuanian account theme was overwritten with the Italian sentence "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:". The account console will show Italian to Lithuanian users for the OTP setup instruction.

title: Simplified Chinese account string replaced with Traditional Chinese
body: totpStep1 in messages_zh_CN.properties was replaced with "在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：", which uses Traditional characters (手機, 安裝, 應用程式). The zh_CN login bundle and the rest of this file use Simplified Chinese, so mainland Chinese users get the wrong script for this OTP step.

title: Missing English bundle aborts the verifier with RuntimeException
body: verifySafeHtml() derives an English properties path and, on any IOException (file missing, unreadable, or path rewrite wrong), throws an unchecked RuntimeException. verify() only catches IOException from Files.readString, so a single translation whose English counterpart cannot be opened fails the whole Maven plugin instead of recording a message and continuing. That also skips duplicate-key and HTML results already collected for that file.

title: Account UI message switched to Java MessageFormat placeholders
body: error-invalid-multivalued-size was changed from i18next placeholders ({{0}}, {{1}}, {{2}}) to Java MessageFormat ({0} and a {2,choice,...} pattern). Every other string in this account-ui bundle still uses {{0}}-style interpolation. The account UI will not substitute the attribute name or limits, and users will see the raw choice-format pattern, including the '<' selector, instead of a readable validation error.

title: Admin UI message switched to Java MessageFormat placeholders
body: error-invalid-multivalued-size in the React admin console bundle was changed from {{0}}/{{1}}/{{2}} to a Java MessageFormat choice pattern. This bundle is not formatted with java.text.MessageFormat; the admin UI will show the literal '{0}' and '{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}' text instead of the attribute name and value counts.

title: Diff highlighter throws when prefix and suffix overlap
body: When sanitized and original differ, the report trims a shared prefix and suffix and then calls substring(start, length - end) with no check that start <= length - end. If the common prefix and suffix overlap (for example original 'aaa' vs sanitized 'aa'), length - end is less than start and String.substring throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. verify() does not catch RuntimeException, so one illegal message aborts the whole theme-verifier run instead of reporting the violation.

title: Message bundles are decoded as ISO-8859-1
body: verifySafeHtml loads files with PropertyResourceBundle(InputStream), which always decodes as ISO-8859-1. Keycloak theme message files are UTF-8 (the same files contain raw Chinese, Arabic, and other non-Latin text). The sanitizer therefore runs on mojibake, not the strings that are shipped, so it can fail the build on legitimate translations or miss HTML that only differs after a UTF-8 decode. Use a UTF-8 Reader (PropertyResourceBundle(Reader) or an InputStreamReader).

title: Lithuanian login string replaced with Italian
body: loginTotpStep1 in the Lithuanian login bundle was replaced with 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' which is Italian, not Lithuanian. Users with locale lt will see an Italian TOTP setup instruction.

body: totpStep1 in the Lithuanian account bundle was replaced with the same Italian sentence ('Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'). The previous Lithuanian text was removed, so the account theme shows the wrong language for this step.

title: Simplified Chinese account string written in Traditional Chinese

Every other string in this file uses {{...}}. The account UI will not substitute the attribute name or limits and will show the literal choice pattern to users when a multivalued attribute fails size validation.

Admin UI messages are interpolated with the {{ }} syntax, not java.text.MessageFormat, so this validation error will render unsubstituted placeholders and the raw choice pattern in the admin console.

title: Illegal-HTML report can throw and abort the build
body: When sanitized text differs from the original, the prefix/suffix trim can overlap (for example value "xx" and sanitized "x", or any case where the removed span is made of the same characters as the surrounding text). start + end then exceeds the string length and value.substring / sanitized.substring throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. That RuntimeException is not caught by verify(), so the theme verifier crashes instead of recording the HTML violation.

title: Lithuanian TOTP step replaced with Italian

body: totpStep1 in the Lithuanian account bundle was replaced with the same Italian sentence ("Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:") rather than Lithuanian. The account console will show Italian setup instructions to Lithuanian users.

title: Null-check verifies grantType twice, not rawTokenId
body: The AccessTokenContext constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) and then Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") instead of checking rawTokenId. A null raw token id is therefore accepted. encodeTokenId later concatenates it, so the jti becomes a string ending in ":null" rather than failing fast, and any later lookup or event correlation using that id is wrong.

title: Access-token id matcher checks the wrong slice and inverts the grant check
body: isAccessTokenId is what CODE_TO_TOKEN, refresh, device, and CIBA event assertions now use for Details.TOKEN_ID. Encoded ids are session(2) + tokenType(2) + grant(2) + ':' + uuid, so the grant shortcut is substring(4, 6). The matcher uses substring(3, 5) (last character of the token-type shortcut plus the first grant character) and returns false when that slice equals the expected shortcut. For a normal id such as onrtac:<uuid> the slice is "ta", which is not "ac", so the condition does not fail and only the UUID half is checked. Tests therefore pass even if the grant (or the whole prefix) is wrong, and a prefix shorter than 5 characters throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of a matcher mismatch.

title: getShortcut is abstract, documented as 3 letters, and never length-checked
body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() was added with no default, so every existing custom grant factory fails with AbstractMethodError when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit calls it, which prevents server startup. The javadoc says the shortcut is usually 3 letters, but the encoder requires exactly 2 characters: encodeTokenId concatenates the shortcut as-is, and getTokenContextFromTokenId rejects any prefix whose length is not 6. A grant that follows the javadoc (or returns any non-2-character shortcut) will issue access tokens that cannot be decoded, and postInit only compares map sizes, so it does not reject a bad length before those tokens are minted.

title: Duplicate grant shortcuts are not reliably rejected
body: postInit inserts every grant shortcut into grantsByShortcuts without checking that the shortcut is unique or exactly two characters, then only compares the two map sizes. That comparison misses the case where a shortcut collision is paired with an id collision (both maps shrink by the same amount) and is not repeated on the lazy refresh path in getShortcutByGrantType / getGrantTypeByShortcut. A colliding shortcut silently overwrites the other grant, so a token can be encoded as one grant and decoded as another, which breaks the session-lookup and token-exchange optimizations this id format is meant to support.

title: Constructor never rejects a null raw token id
body: AccessTokenContext's constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") instead of checking rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted, and encodeTokenId concatenates it into a jti ending in ":null". Those token ids are not unique and cannot be correlated with the generated id, while a genuinely null grantType is the only case that throws.

title: Access-token id matcher rejects the expected grant and checks the wrong characters
body: isAccessTokenId returns false when items[0].substring(3, 5) equals the expected grant shortcut, and that slice is not the grant shortcut anyway. The encoded prefix is session(0-1) + token type(2-3) + grant(4-5), so grant must be substring(4, 6), and a match must succeed rather than fail. As written, expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken accept any 6-char prefix plus a UUID and never verify the grant that was just added to the jti, so a wrong or missing grant encoding will not fail those tests.

title: New getShortcut() has no default and is invoked for every grant at startup
body: getShortcut() was added as an abstract SPI method. DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit enumerates every OAuth2GrantTypeFactory and calls it. A custom grant factory compiled against the previous interface will throw AbstractMethodError during provider postInit, which fails Keycloak startup rather than only disabling that grant. A default that yields the unknown shortcut (and is null-safe) is required for compatibility.

title: Shortcut contract says 3 letters but the encoder requires exactly 2
body: The new getShortcut() javadoc tells implementors to return a usually 3-letter shortcut. Decoding in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId requires the context prefix to be exactly 6 characters (2+2+2) and throws IllegalArgumentException otherwise, and neither postInit nor encodeTokenId checks shortcut length. A grant that follows the javadoc will mint access-token ids that cannot be decoded, so later introspection/session lookup using this context will fail for those tokens.

title: Malformed jti with a colon throws instead of degrading
body: getTokenContextFromTokenId treats a missing colon as a legacy id and returns UNKNOWN, but any id that contains a colon whose prefix is not exactly 6 known shortcuts throws IllegalArgumentException (and the exception text includes the raw token id). Callers that will use this on tokens presented to introspection, userinfo, or admin APIs must catch that or a non-conforming, legacy, or custom jti becomes a 500 instead of the same unknown-context fallback.

title: Access-token ID matcher rejects valid refresh tokens
body: isAccessTokenId splits the jti on ':' and then treats items[0].substring(3, 5) as the grant shortcut, returning false when that slice equals the expected shortcut. The encoded prefix is six characters: session type [0,2), token type [2,4), grant type [4,6). substring(3, 5) is therefore the last character of the token type plus the first character of the grant, not the grant shortcut. For a normal refresh access token the prefix is like "onrtrt", so substring(3, 5) is "rt", the condition matches RefreshTokenGrantTypeFactory.GRANT_SHORTCUT, and the matcher returns false. expectRefresh() will fail every regular refresh-token event assertion. The same slice also does not actually check authorization-code, device, or CIBA shortcuts ("onrtac" yields "ta"), so those expectations pass even when the grant shortcut is wrong. Compare items[0].substring(4, 6) and fail when it does not equal the expected shortcut (and when the prefix length is not 6).

title: Constructor null-check validates grantType twice, not rawTokenId
body: The fourth requireNonNull call passes grantType again with the message "Null rawTokenId not allowed". A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted and stored. encodeTokenId then concatenates it, producing a jti ending in ":null" (or an NPE later if a caller assumes the id is present). The check must be Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...).

title: New getShortcut() breaks existing grant factories and is not length-checked
