body: getShortcut() was added to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory with no default implementation. Every existing custom grant factory fails to compile, and a deployed one throws AbstractMethodError when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit calls getShortcut(), which aborts server startup. The javadoc also says the shortcut is "usually like 3-letters", but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId requires the whole context prefix to be exactly 6 characters (2+2+2) and throws IllegalArgumentException otherwise. Nothing in postInit or the hot-deploy refresh path checks that the shortcut is exactly two characters or that it does not collide with another grant after dynamic registration. A 3-character shortcut, which the new contract text encourages, is written into access-token jtis that can never be decoded.

title: Exhausted user-storage recovery codes are not removed
body: After a successful recovery-code login, the authenticator now loads the credential via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential, which prefers the user-storage credential. If that model reports all codes used, it still calls credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById. That API only deletes credentials stored in Keycloak's local credential store, not a credential owned by a user storage provider. The storage credential therefore stays configured, isConfiguredFor remains true, and the next login still demands a recovery code even though none are left. If recovery codes are the only second factor, the user cannot get back in to satisfy the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES action that is added on the same path. Disable or update the credential through the storage SPI (disableCredentialType / updateCredential) when the federated credential is exhausted.

title: Login form assumes storage returns a hashed recovery-code model
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential writes the user-storage credential as a UserCredentialModel whose value is a JSON array of plaintext codes, not RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialData/SecretData. The login bean (and the authenticator after a successful check) then calls RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel on whatever getFederatedCredentialsStream returns. A storage provider that persists and returns the value it was given has null or non-model secretData, so createFromCredentialModel throws and the recovery-code page fails with a server error before the user can sign in. Only the test provider hides this by rebuilding a model with createFromValues inside getCredentials. Keycloak needs a defined, converted representation (or must not parse storage credentials as local secret data) or user-storage recovery codes cannot be challenged.

title: Storage recovery codes are reusable and never advance
body: isValid deserializes the stored JSON list and returns true if any code equals the input. It does not require the next code in sequence, remove the used code, or update the stored credential. getCredentials then calls createFromValues on the original list, which hashes every code, resets the next index to the first code, and assigns a new credential id on every read. disableCredentialType also ignores recovery-authn-codes, so the credential cannot be turned off. The new login test only submits code 0 once, so it stays green while this provider treats backup codes as a reusable shared secret and cannot drive the all-codes-used path. Consume the matched code in isValid, return a stable id and the remaining sequence from getCredentials, and clear the credential in disableCredentialType.

title: Exhausted user-storage recovery codes are never removed
body: After a successful recovery-code login, if RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential reports every code used, the authenticator calls credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById. That API only deletes credentials stored in Keycloak's database. A credential that was created in user storage (the new path in CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential) is left in place, so isConfiguredFor stays true and the same codes remain available to the storage provider's isValid. The required action is still added, but the old federated credential is not cleared, so reconfiguration does not actually retire the codes the user just finished.

title: User-storage write format cannot drive the recovery-code login UI
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential hands user storage a UserCredentialModel whose value is a JSON array of raw codes, then returns. The login form (RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean) and the post-login check in RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator load that credential via getFederatedCredentialsStream and immediately call RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel / getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get(). Those calls require Keycloak secretData (hashed codes plus used flags) and credentialData (next index). A provider that persists the payload it was given has neither, so createFromCredentialModel throws or the next-code Optional is empty and the login page fails. Nothing in the helper writes the hashed model, passes the expected code index into isValid, or tells storage to consume a code, so sequential one-time use cannot work unless every storage provider reverse-engineers Keycloak's internal credential format.

title: Storage test accepts any code and never consumes it
body: The new user-storage isValid treats recovery codes as a reusable set: it deserializes the cleartext JSON list stored in credentialData and returns true if the submitted value equals any entry. It does not require the next index, does not mark a code used, and does not delete the credential when the list is exhausted. updateCredential also stores the raw codes rather than hashes. testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin only submits code 0 once and checks that the field is non-null, so it passes even though reuse, out-of-order codes, and the all-codes-used removal path are broken. The suite therefore does not lock in the one-time semantics this change is supposed to provide for federated users.

title: Login bean assumes a fully populated recovery-code model
body: RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean now calls RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential and unconditionally uses credentialModelOpt.get() plus getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get(). getCredential prefers the first federated credential of type recovery-authn-codes, which may be absent, metadata-only (type and id, no secretData), or a storage model that is not a RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel. Any of those cases throws NoSuchElementException or a deserialization error while rendering the recovery-code form, so a user who is configuredFor the type in user storage cannot open the login challenge. The previous code at least read a locally stored model that createCredential had fully populated.

title: Federated recovery codes are never consumed and can be replayed
body: isValid for recovery-authn-codes accepts a submitted code if it equals any value in the stored JSON list and then returns true without removing that code. Combined with getCredentials, which rebuilds the credential via createFromValues from the original full list (all codes unused), a code that has already been used still validates on every later login. Recovery codes are single-use bearer credentials; this storage, which is the implementation the new test relies on, leaves them reusable indefinitely. The new test only logs in once with the first code, so it does not catch the replay.

title: Successful federated recovery-code login does not retire the credential
body: After credentialManager().isValid succeeds, the authenticator loads the credential and, when all codes are used, calls removeStoredCredentialById. That API only deletes a credential stored in Keycloak's local credential store. A recovery-code credential created through CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential lives in the user-storage provider when updateCredential returns true, and nothing in this path calls the storage's updateCredential or disableCredentialType to drop or rewrite the used code. The local RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider used to mark the code used inside isValid; that provider is skipped once user storage owns the credential. Exhausted or already-used federated codes therefore stay valid, and the required-action fallback never sees allCodesUsed() if the storage returns a freshly rebuilt unused model.

title: User storage is given every recovery code in plaintext
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes the raw generated codes with JsonSerialization and passes that string as the UserCredentialModel challenge response. Local storage stores only hashes (RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues / hashRawCode). Any user-storage provider that persists challengeResponse, as the new backwards-compatibility storage does in credentialData, keeps the full set of unused backup codes in cleartext. A compromise of that store exposes codes that can be submitted directly to isValid.

title: Concurrent group test asserts before the reader thread finishes
body: createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti starts a background thread that lists groups and records exceptions, then the main thread deletes the groups, sets deletedAll, and immediately asserts that caughtExceptions is empty. The reader is never started-before-delete, never joined, and has no timeout. The assertion can therefore run before the reader has executed a single request, or while a request that began before deletedAll was set is still in flight and has not yet recorded its exception. A regression of the concurrent NPE can pass this test, and the thread can keep using managedRealm.admin() after the test method returns and realm cleanup starts, which is also racy against the admin client.

title: Concurrent group deletion still NPEs on subgroup streams
body: getSubGroupsCount() now treats a missing delegate as null, but the three filtered/paginated getSubGroupsStream overloads still do modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) with no null check (lines 256, 262, and 268). modelSupplier is the same lazy loader and returns null once the group has been deleted out from under a cached GroupAdapter. Any concurrent subgroup query on that adapter still throws NullPointerException, so the failure this change is meant to stop remains on those APIs. Null-check the delegate the same way, or otherwise fail consistently, before calling through.

title: Concurrent group test neither overlaps nor observes the reader
body: createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti starts a non-daemon reader and then deletes groups and asserts caughtExceptions is empty without waiting for the reader to start, join, or finish its in-flight call. deletedAll is set only after deletes, and the reader checks that flag only between requests, so the assertion can run before any read overlaps a delete and before an exception from the last call is added to the list. The regression can pass without ever hitting the race, a real NPE can be missed, and the leftover thread keeps using the shared admin client into later tests.

title: Deleted-group race still NPEs, and null count is unsafe
body: getSubGroupsCount() now avoids NPE when the cached group is already gone from the database, but it returns null. GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() is otherwise a numeric count, and callers such as GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount pass that value straight through; any unboxing (long, comparisons, arithmetic) turns the original server NPE into a client or later-server NPE, and a brief group listing can emit a group with a null subGroupCount. The same race is unfixed on the other paths that dereference modelSupplier.get() with no null check: getSubGroupsStream(search, first, max), getSubGroupsStream(first, max), and getSubGroupsStream(search, exact, first, max) at lines 256, 262, and 268. Those still throw NullPointerException if the delegate was deleted between cache hit and load. Return 0 (or omit the group) when the delegate is missing, and null-check those streams the same way.

title: Concurrent group test asserts before the reader finishes
body: createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti starts a non-daemon reader thread that calls groups() in a loop, then the test thread deletes groups, sets deletedAll, and immediately asserts caughtExceptions is empty. The reader is never joined or otherwise waited on, so the assertion runs while groups() may still be in flight. An NPE (or 500) that the test is meant to catch can be recorded after the assert, so the test passes even when the race still fails. The overlap is also not guaranteed: deletedAll can become true before the reader issues a single request. Join the reader (with a timeout) after deletions, and fail if it is still running or if it recorded any exception.

title: Optimized paginator cannot key datetime audit logs
body: When optimized_pagination=true, OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint paginates AuditLogEntry with OptimizedCursorPaginator and order_by="-datetime". That paginator's get_item_key (paginator.py) does math.floor/ceil on the order-by attribute and value_from_cursor returns the raw numeric cursor. DateTimePaginator exists specifically because datetime values are not numbers: after the first page returns rows, build_cursor calls get_item_key on a datetime and raises TypeError, so the new path 500s whenever the queryset is non-empty. A follow-up request with a numeric cursor would also emit SQL comparing the datetime column to an integer instead of DateTimePaginator's timestamp conversion, so pages would be wrong even if the TypeError were avoided. Keep DateTimePaginator, or implement the same datetime key encoding before using this class on audit logs.

title: Negative cursor offsets break or silently rewrite pagination
body: BasePaginator.get_result now does start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset and slices the queryset with that start. This runs for every Paginator and DateTimePaginator, not only the new audit-log path. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing (ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported) and PostgreSQL rejects a negative OFFSET, so a previous-page cursor whose offset is negative becomes a 500. Cursor.from_string already accepts a negative middle field (for example "1:-5:1"), so clients can trigger that. For a forward cursor, a negative offset is clamped to 0 and the first page is returned instead of rejecting the cursor, which changes results for every existing cursor-paginated endpoint. The same slice is repeated in OptimizedCursorPaginator when enable_advanced_features is set and cursor.offset < 0 (around line 880); the comments claiming the ORM handles negative slices and that this reaches data "beyond normal pagination bounds" are incorrect. Reject offset < 0 with BadPaginationError, as OffsetPaginator already does, and do not change BasePaginator slicing.

title: No tests for optimized pagination or negative offsets
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator and the organization audit-log branch that selects it (including enable_advanced_features and cursors with a negative offset) are added with no tests. The first successful page of audit logs would have shown the datetime TypeError, and a cursor such as "0:-1:0" would have shown the queryset slice failure and the global BasePaginator clamp. Without those cases, the broken path can ship while the default DateTimePaginator tests still pass.

title: Optimized paginator cannot key or filter datetime audit rows
body: When optimized_pagination=true, the audit-log endpoint paginates AuditLogEntry with order_by="-datetime" using OptimizedCursorPaginator. That class's get_item_key does math.floor/math.ceil on getattr(item, self.key), and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor number. A datetime cannot be floored, and a numeric cursor value is compared in SQL against the datetime column. Any non-empty optimized page raises TypeError while building the cursor; a follow-up request with a cursor either 500s or filters the wrong rows. DateTimePaginator (still used on the other branch) is the implementation that encodes and decodes this field. There are no tests covering the new branch.

title: Negative cursor offsets are sliced into the queryset
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when enable_advanced_features is set and cursor.offset < 0, does queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start. Django QuerySet slicing rejects negative indexes (ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported), so the audit-log path that passes enable_advanced_features=True returns 500 for any client-supplied cursor whose offset is negative (Cursor.from_string already accepts that). The same unclamped prev-cursor offset is also applied in BasePaginator.get_result for every endpoint using that paginator. This does not skip the organization filter, but it does turn a crafted cursor into an unhandled error instead of a bounded page, and it does not implement the claimed reverse scan.

title: No tests for OptimizedCursorPaginator or the audit-log switch
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator and the organization audit-log branch that selects it (optimized_pagination plus superuser/global access) ship with no tests. A test that returns at least one AuditLogEntry through that paginator would fail immediately on datetime key extraction, and a cursor with a negative offset would show the queryset slice error. Without that coverage the broken path can merge while the default DateTimePaginator path still looks fine.

title: Optimized paginator treats datetime keys as numbers
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does math.floor/math.ceil on getattr(item, self.key), and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor integer. OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint wires this class to order_by="-datetime" (organization_auditlogs.py around the optimized self.paginate call). AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime, so the first page dies in build_cursor with TypeError, and any later cursor compares an int to a timestamp column in SQL. The endpoint should keep DateTimePaginator (or this class must use DateTimePaginator's multiplier and fromtimestamp conversion). As written, optimized_pagination=true always 500s for admins.

title: Negative queryset slices are invalid in Django
body: When enable_advanced_features is set (the audit-log path always passes True) and the cursor offset is negative, get_result slices the queryset with that negative start (queryset[start_offset:stop]). Django QuerySet slicing raises ValueError if start or stop is negative; it does not "handle negative slicing automatically" as the comment claims. A client-supplied cursor such as "0:-5:0" therefore 500s instead of paginating. The same false assumption was copied into BasePaginator.get_result (start_offset = offset when cursor.is_prev), so a negative prev offset now fails on every endpoint that uses BasePaginator, not only audit logs.

title: Shared paginator silently clamps negative forward offsets
body: BasePaginator.get_result previously sliced with the cursor offset unchanged. It now uses max(0, offset) whenever the cursor is not a previous-page cursor. A crafted or corrupt forward cursor with a negative offset used to error; it now returns the first page as if offset were 0, with Link headers computed from that wrong slice. This runs for every BasePaginator consumer (issues, events, etc.), not just the new audit-log flag, and can repeat or skip rows without the client knowing the cursor was rejected.

title: No tests for the new pagination branch
body: The optimized_pagination query-param branch and OptimizedCursorPaginator are untested. Existing audit-log tests still hit DateTimePaginator, so they will not catch the datetime key TypeError, the negative-offset ValueError, or the cursor format change (DateTimePaginator encodes milliseconds; the new class emits raw numeric keys). A request with optimized_pagination=true from a superuser or global-access member should be covered before this path is exposed.

title: Optimized paginator cannot order audit logs by datetime
body: When optimized_pagination=true and the caller is a superuser or has global access, this endpoint paginates AuditLogEntry with OptimizedCursorPaginator and order_by="-datetime". That class's get_item_key does math.floor/math.ceil on the raw attribute, and value_from_cursor returns the cursor integer unchanged. Audit log datetime values are datetimes, so the first page that returns rows raises TypeError in get_item_key, and any later page compares a datetime column to an integer. DateTimePaginator exists for this field. Org owners/managers who pass the new query flag get HTTP 500s on an otherwise working endpoint, and there is no test covering the new branch.

title: Negative cursor offsets are passed into queryset slices
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator, when enable_advanced_features is set, slices the queryset with a client-supplied negative cursor.offset (Cursor.from_string accepts it). Django QuerySet slicing raises ValueError for any negative start/stop, so this path 500s instead of paginating. The same change in BasePaginator.get_result (line 182) stops clamping offsets for previous-page cursors on every cursor paginator, not just this class. Comments claiming the ORM safely handles negative slices and that this reaches rows beyond normal bounds are wrong; it only breaks pagination or, if a backend ever accepted the slice, would turn an untrusted cursor into an unbounded offset.

title: Sorted-set commands are incompatible with existing span-buffer sets
body: add-buffer.lua and SpansBuffer switched segment storage from Redis sets (SADD/SCARD/SUNIONSTORE/SSCAN) to sorted sets (ZADD/ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZSCAN/ZPOPMIN) with no migration. Keys already written as sets remain until redis_ttl (default 3600s). The next ZADD or ZCARD against those keys returns WRONGTYPE, so process_spans fails, segments are not merged or flushed, and in-flight span data is stuck or dropped for up to an hour after deploy.

title: Eviction cap is hardcoded and the Python size guard was removed
body: After a merge, the script ZPOPMINs the segment down to a hardcoded 1000 members, using the lowest end_timestamp_precise scores, with no metric. SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans is 1001 and is no longer consulted: _load_segment_data dropped the check that skipped segments over that count. Caps can diverge, eviction is invisible, and any path that does not hit this Lua branch (or a WRONGTYPE failure) can now flush an unbounded segment that the old guard would have dropped.

title: Redirect walk limit cut from 10000 to 1000
body: The parent-redirect loop now stops at 1000 hops and the comment that this limit can fail to join deep segment trees was removed. Traces whose redirect chain is deeper than 1000 are no longer merged into one segment; spans stay on separate keys and are flushed as split or parentless segments. That is a silent correctness regression versus the previous script.

title: Missing end_timestamp_precise crashes the span batch
body: process_batch now requires val["end_timestamp_precise"] and stores it as the sorted-set score. The previous consumer did not read this field (tests had to be updated to add it). A span event that omits it raises KeyError inside the batch, which fails the whole batch and stalls the consumer instead of buffering the span. Use a safe default or skip/metric the span if the schema field is optional.

title: No test for sorted-set eviction or over-limit segments
body: The insert path now scores members by end_timestamp_precise and the Lua script drops members once a segment exceeds 1000 spans, and the flush-time span-count skip was deleted. Existing buffer tests only use four or five spans with identical timestamps, so they never exercise ZPOPMIN, score ordering, the 1000 cap, or a segment that used to be rejected for max_segment_spans. A wrong eviction count or a failure to trim would ship without a failing test.

title: Optimized paginator cannot order audit logs by datetime
body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint switches to OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime", but OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does math.floor/ceil on getattr(item, self.key) and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor integer. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime, so the first page raises TypeError when building the next cursor, and any later page emits SQL comparing a timestamptz column to an integer (PostgreSQL error). DateTimePaginator already converts via strftime and fromtimestamp; this class does not, so optimized_pagination=true is unusable for the only endpoint that enables it.

title: Negative-offset pagination raises on Django querysets
body: When enable_advanced_features is set and the client cursor offset is negative, get_result slices the queryset with a negative start (queryset[cursor.offset:stop]). Django QuerySet explicitly rejects negative indexes with ValueError, so the "advanced" path 500s instead of paginating. The same unclamped offset is also used for previous-page cursors in BasePaginator.get_result, so a crafted prev cursor can 500 any endpoint using that base class. Cursors are client-supplied via Cursor.from_string, which accepts a negative offset integer.

title: In-place SET to ZSET change breaks existing span-buffer keys
body: Span segment keys (span-buf:s:...) change from Redis sets (SADD/SUNIONSTORE/SSCAN) to sorted sets (ZADD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZSCAN/ZPOPMIN) without a new key prefix or migration. Keys written before deploy remain SETs until redis_ttl (default 3600s). Any Z* command against those keys returns WRONGTYPE, so process_spans and flush_segments fail for in-flight segments and those spans are dropped or stuck until TTL. A rolling deploy cannot safely mix old and new consumers on the same keys.

title: Segments over 1000 spans are silently truncated
body: After merge, the script ZPOPMINs span_count-1000 members (lowest end_timestamp_precise) with no metric or log. The flush path used to skip an oversized segment, increment spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded, and log; that check was removed from SpansBuffer._load_segment_data. Truncated segments are still flushed and produced as if complete, so spans are lost with no signal, and the cap is hardcoded at 1000 rather than SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans (1001). There is no test that a segment larger than the cap drops the oldest members and still flushes the rest.

title: ZUNIONSTORE sums scores and can evict the wrong spans
body: zunionstore is called without AGGREGATE MIN/MAX, so Redis defaults to SUM. If the same payload is already in both keys (retry, or the Python ZADD and a previous buffer both holding it), the merged score becomes the sum of end timestamps. zpopmin then treats that span as newest or oldest incorrectly and can drop a different span than the oldest one. sunionstore did not have scores, so this is a new failure mode of the set-to-zset conversion.

title: Redirect walk cap cut from 10000 to 1000
body: The parent-redirect loop now stops after 1000 hops (previously 10000, with a comment that deeper segment trees would not join). When the cap is hit, the span is attached to an intermediate set_span_id instead of the true segment root. Deep traces are flushed as multiple incomplete segments, and the warning comment that documented this limit was removed. No test covers a chain longer than the new cap.

title: Optimized paginator cannot order audit logs by datetime
body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint now pages with OptimizedCursorPaginator and order_by="-datetime" when optimized_pagination=true. OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does int(math.floor/ceil(getattr(item, key))) and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor number. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime, so the first successful page raises TypeError while building the next cursor, and any non-zero cursor is compared to the datetime column as an int. The optimized path 500s for every superuser or global-access member who passes the flag; DateTimePaginator is the type that actually converts datetimes.

title: Negative-offset pagination raises instead of slicing
body: When enable_advanced_features is set (the audit-log path always passes True), a cursor with offset < 0 is sliced as queryset[negative:stop]. Django QuerySet rejects negative slice bounds with ValueError ("Negative indexing is not supported") and does not clamp or wrap. The comment that the ORM handles this and that it reaches rows past normal bounds is wrong, so the new code path 500s on any such cursor and does not implement the pagination it claims.

title: SET segment keys are incompatible with the new ZSET commands
body: process_spans now ZADDs span payloads and _load_segment_data ZSCANs them, while add-buffer.lua switched from SCARD/SUNIONSTORE to ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZPOPMIN. Keys already written by the previous sadd/sunionstore path are Redis SETs. The first ZADD, ZUNIONSTORE, or ZSCAN on those keys returns WRONGTYPE, so in-flight segments cannot be merged or flushed and span ingestion fails until those keys expire. There is no new key prefix or migration.

title: Eviction count is not atomic with the ZADD and can over-delete
body: Payloads are ZADDed in a separate pipeline, then each span runs this script, which ZPOPMINs down to 1000 using a count read inside the script. Two overlapping batches can each observe a count above 1000 and each pop span_count-1000 members, deleting more than the excess (including spans just inserted by the other batch). The cap is also a hardcoded 1000, while SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans (1001) is no longer enforced, and the segment_span_count_exceeded metric/log was removed, so drops are silent and not configurable.

title: Redirect walk limit cut from 10000 to 1000 splits deep segments
body: The parent-redirect loop now stops after 1000 hops instead of 10000 and still HSETs the span onto whatever set_span_id it reached. Traces whose redirect chain is deeper than 1000 are no longer joined to the real segment root; those spans are stored and flushed as a separate segment. The previous comment that this limit breaks joining was removed rather than the walk being fixed.

title: No test covers insert-time eviction or zset merge
body: The buffer tests only add the new end_timestamp_precise field to existing small trees. Nothing asserts that a segment larger than 1000 spans ZPOPMINs the lowest scores, that the root span is kept, or that zunionstore still merges redirect keys. A WRONGTYPE against leftover SET keys and over-eviction across batches would not be caught.

title: Shared cache key uses process-randomized hash()
body: The eligibility cache key is built with Python's hash() on the project-id tuple. hash() is salted per process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so the same org/projects produce different keys on different web workers and after restart. A shared cache (Redis/memcache) therefore never hits across processes, and invalidate_upsampling_cache() deletes a different key than the one other workers wrote. Allowlist checks keep hitting options on every request, and a 60s entry cannot be invalidated reliably when the allowlist changes.

title: Upsampling decision uses the wrong dataset
body: is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects is called with the closed-over dataset from get(), not the scoped_dataset argument that _get_event_stats actually queries. Dashboard widget splitting calls this helper with discover or the metrics dataset while the outer dataset stays metrics_performance / metrics_enhanced_performance (or the reverse). The column rewrite can then be applied to a dataset that has no upsampled_count/sample_weight (query error) or skipped on an errors query that should be upsampled, so chart counts are wrong or the endpoint 500s.

title: Upsampled count sums sample_weight but ingest only sets sample_rate
body: upsampled_count() is toInt64(sum(sample_weight)). The new store_event helper only copies contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate onto normalized_data['sample_rate'] and never writes sample_weight or 1/sample_rate. Nothing in this change connects those fields. For allowlisted projects, count() therefore sums a missing or unpopulated column (null/0, or a Snuba error if the column is absent) instead of the intended 1/client_sample_rate. The new stats test expects a 0.1 client rate to become count 10, which this pipeline cannot produce.

title: Accidental gitlink added to the tree
body: This change adds a gitlink/subproject named sentry-repo pinned to a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a (the PR base). It is unrelated to error upsampling, is not a real source file, and will break checkout or pull in an unintended submodule if merged.

title: Cache invalidation helper is never called
body: invalidate_upsampling_cache is documented as required when the allowlist changes, but nothing in the PR calls it (no options subscriber, signal, or admin path). Combined with the 60s cache.set of the allowlist result, projects added to or removed from issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist keep the previous upsampling decision until TTL, so counts stay 1x or jump to sample_weight sums after a config change with no way to flush.

title: Upsampled count sums the wrong field and does not invert sample rate
body: transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling rewrites count() to upsampled_count(), and the new SnQL function is sum(sample_weight) cast to int. The only ingest change, _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling, writes contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate onto sample_rate and never sets sample_weight. A client_sample_rate of 0.1 means the stored event represents about 10 events, but nothing computes 1/sample_rate, and the aggregate does not read sample_rate. Allowlisted error stats will either query a missing/zero sample_weight column (query error or a count of 0) or, if that column happens to hold the rate, return a fractional rate instead of an upsampled count. The new stats test expects count == 10 for one event at rate 0.1, which this path cannot produce.

title: Error-query detection is a substring match and treats exclusions as errors
body: _is_error_focused_query lowercases the raw query string and returns true if it contains the substring "event.type:error". That also matches negated or unrelated clauses such as "!event.type:error" and "event.type:error OR event.type:transaction". Discover queries that exclude errors are then rewritten from count() to upsampled_count()/sum(sample_weight). Transactions and other non-error events do not have that column, so those stats requests fail or return inflated/zero counts. The same check misses the dashboard errors split, which uses "!event.type:transaction" rather than "event.type:error", so genuine error-only discover queries are not upsampled.

title: Upsampling eligibility uses the request dataset, not the dataset actually queried
body: _get_event_stats decides upsampling with the closed-over dataset from get_dataset(request), then runs the query on scoped_dataset. Dashboard widget splitting calls this with discover (and an errors-only or transactions-only query) while the outer dataset is still metrics_performance or metrics_enhanced_performance. _should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns false for those metrics datasets, so the errors split never rewrites count(). The opposite also holds: an errors/discover request dataset can rewrite columns on a scoped dataset that is not the errors dataset. Counts for split dashboard widgets will be wrong or the rewritten function will be invalid on the dataset that actually runs.

title: upsampled_count is only registered on the discover dataset
body: The new upsampled_count SnQL function is added only inside DiscoverDataset.function_converter. is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects returns true for the errors dataset with no query check, and the endpoint then sends yAxis/selected_columns of "upsampled_count() as count" to that dataset. Unless the errors dataset shares this exact converter, allowlisted errors-dataset stats queries will fail function resolution instead of returning an upsampled count. The integration tests only hit discover via event.type:error and do not cover dataset=errors.

title: Allowlist cache key is process-local and invalidation is never called
body: The eligibility cache key is built with hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))). Tuple hashing is salted per process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so workers do not share keys and invalidate_upsampling_cache deletes a different key than the one another process wrote. That helper is also never called when issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist changes, despite the docstring saying it must be. A False or True allowlist result is then reused for 60 seconds. After an allowlist change, stats keep using the old decision: either counts stay un-upsampled or count() is rewritten to sum(sample_weight) for projects that are no longer allowlisted. The new stats tests patch options.get but not the cache, so a later case with the same project ids can still see the first case's cached True and fail or pass for the wrong reason.

title: Accidental gitlink pins a nested copy of the repository
body: This change adds a gitlink/submodule named sentry-repo whose commit is the PR base (a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a). It is unrelated to error upsampling. Checking out the branch will try to materialize a nested repository (or fail if the gitlink has no .gitmodules URL), and it should not be merged.

title: Upsampled count sums sample_weight but events only get sample_rate
body: upsampled_count() is defined as toInt64(sum(sample_weight)), and transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling rewrites count() to that function. The only ingest/test path added in this PR, _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling, writes contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate onto sample_rate and never sets sample_weight. A client_sample_rate of 0.1 must become a weight of 10 (1/rate) to match the new stats test, which expects count == 10 for one stored error. As written, allowlisted error stats either sum a missing/null column (count collapses toward 0, or the query errors) or, if sample_weight were copied from sample_rate, would report 0.1 instead of 10. toInt64 also truncates any fractional weight. Error volume on the events-stats API would be wrong for every allowlisted project.

title: Error detection is a substring check on the original request, not the executed query
body: _is_error_focused_query returns true when the raw request.GET query string contains the substring event.type:error. That matches negated filters such as !event.type:error, so a discover query that explicitly excludes errors is still rewritten from count() to upsampled_count()/sum(sample_weight). The check also ignores the query string actually executed: _get_event_stats passes the closed-over request into is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects, not the query argument. Dashboard discover-split builds transactions_only_query / errors_only_query and still calls _get_event_stats with the original request, so a request whose query contains event.type:error will upsample the transaction-only split query (sample_weight is not valid for transactions), and an errors-only split of a query that does not contain that substring will not upsample. Counts will be wrong or the Snuba query will fail.

title: Upsampling decision uses the outer dataset, not the dataset that runs
body: is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects is called with the endpoint's outer dataset, while _get_event_stats runs scoped_dataset, which dashboard widget splitting can change to discover or back to the metrics dataset. _should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns true for the errors module unconditionally and false for transactions. If the outer dataset is errors but the executed dataset is discover/transactions (or the reverse), count() is rewritten, or not rewritten, for the wrong dataset. Transaction queries can then reference sample_weight, and error queries can keep a raw count() and under-report volume.

title: Eligibility cache key uses process-local hash and is never invalidated
body: The cache key is error_upsampling_eligible:{org}:{hash(sorted project ids)} with a 60s TTL. hash() is salted per process for non-int values, and even for ints it is not a stable cross-version key; workers will miss or collide, so the stated cross-request cache does not work. invalidate_upsampling_cache builds the same key but is never called when issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist changes, so a stale True remains for up to 60s and keeps rewriting count() after a project is removed from the allowlist (and a stale False keeps serving un-upsampled counts after it is added). Integration tests patch options.get but do not clear this cache, so a reused project id can make the allowlist tests assert the wrong count.

title: store_event copies client_sample_rate into sample_rate without inverting
body: _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling sets normalized_data['sample_rate'] = float(client_sample_rate) whenever the value is truthy. Sampling rate and sample weight are inverses: 0.1 means one stored event represents ten. Writing the rate into sample_rate (and not sample_weight) makes every later store_event path, not just these tests, persist the wrong magnitude. A rate of 0 is also dropped by the truthiness check, so a fully sampled client is stored with no sample_rate at all.

title: Table widget flag renders an empty table
body: When the `use-table-widget-visualization` flag is on, `tableResultComponent` ignores the loaded widget result and always mounts `TableWidgetVisualization` with `columns={[]}` and `tableData` set to empty `data`/`fields`/`units`. Every dashboard table widget behind that flag shows no columns and no rows, while the previous `StyledSimpleTableChart` path (which had `result.data`, fields, and metadata) is skipped. The flag cannot be turned on without blanking table widgets.

title: Error payloads are zipped against dict values, not ids
body: `fetch_error_details` builds node ids from `error_ids`, then pairs `zip(error_ids, events.values())`. `nodestore.backend.get_multi` returns a dict keyed by node id; missing keys are omitted and value order is not guaranteed to match `error_ids`. The resulting `ErrorEvent.id` can be attached to the wrong event, and a missing event shifts every subsequent id. Look up each node id explicitly (and skip missing keys) instead of zipping parallel lists.

title: Summarize never requests error_ids
body: Error context is taken from `process_raw_response(..., fields=request.query_params.getlist("field"))` and then `response[0].get("error_ids", [])`. This endpoint does not force `error_ids` into the Snuba field list, so a normal summarize GET (no `field` query param) gets no error ids, `fetch_error_details` is a no-op, and the new error-context logs are never sent to Seer. The field list should always include `error_ids` regardless of the caller.

title: Nodestore timestamps are not numeric
body: Error events copy `data.get("timestamp", 0.0)` straight into `ErrorEvent.timestamp`. Nodestore event payloads store `timestamp` as an ISO-8601 string, while replay segment events use unix floats. `get_request_data` sorts on that value and `gen_request_data` compares it with `event.get("timestamp", 0)`. A string-vs-float comparison raises TypeError, which is uncaught in `analyze_recording_segments`, so any replay that actually has stored errors fails the summarize request with 500 instead of merging error lines.

title: Reports with neither age nor timestamp are accepted
body: `age` and `timestamp` are both `required=False`, and the cross-field checks only run when that field is present. A report that omits both (or sends only the other required fields) passes `BrowserReportSerializer` and is counted as a valid browser report. The comments say both Reporting API specs must be supported; each spec requires exactly one of those time fields. `validate()` should reject payloads that have neither or both. `validate_timestamp` also uses `initial_data.get("age")`, so `age: 0` is treated as absent and will not fail the timestamp check.

title: Hidden span attributes are only filtered while searching
body: `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` (`is_segment`, `project_id`, `received`) is applied only inside the branch that runs when `searchQuery` is non-empty. With an empty search the full sorted attribute list is returned, so those fields still render in the default Attributes tree. When the user searches, the same names are dropped even if they match the query. The exclusion needs to apply before the search filter if those attributes are meant to be hidden.

title: Analytics recorded before feature and auth checks
body: `analytics.record(..., user_id=request.user.id)` runs before the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` feature check and before body validation. This endpoint allows org-auth-token callers (`is_org_auth_token_auth` later). If `request.user` is missing or is not a real user, `.id` raises and a disabled or token-authenticated assemble call 500s instead of returning 404/400. It also emits assemble analytics for requests that are immediately rejected as feature-disabled. Record only after the feature check, and pass `user_id` only when the request has an authenticated user.

title: Issue template truncates via the wrong class
body: `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` is defined on `CommitContextIntegration` but calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title`. `_truncate_title` is a staticmethod on `CommitContextIntegration`, not on `PRCommentWorkflow`. Generating a merged-PR comment therefore raises AttributeError unless `PRCommentWorkflow` happens to inherit that method, and GitHub/GitLab workflows call this helper as `self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template`. Call `CommitContextIntegration._truncate_title` (or `self._truncate_title`) so title truncation does not depend on a class that does not define it.

title: Error events are paired by dict order and compared with the wrong timestamp type
body: fetch_error_details zips error_ids with nodestore get_multi().values(). If the backend omits missing keys or does not return results in request order, titles/messages are attached to the wrong event ids (or dropped while a later id is kept). It also stores data.get("timestamp") as-is. Nodestore events normally have an ISO string timestamp, while breadcrumb timestamps in gen_request_data are numbers. Sorting and the `<` comparison then raise TypeError and the summarize endpoint 500s whenever error context is enabled. The new tests only cover events stored with a numeric timestamp, so they miss production nodestore payloads.

title: Assemble analytics runs before the feature gate and assumes a real user
body: analytics.record is called with user_id=request.user.id before the organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble check and before auth-token handling. This endpoint is used by org auth tokens (is_org_auth_token_auth later in the same method). AnonymousUser has no id, so request.user.id raises AttributeError and the assemble API 500s for the token clients it is meant to serve. The event is also recorded for requests that will immediately 404 because the feature is off.

title: Flagged table widgets render empty data instead of query results
body: When organization.features includes use-table-widget-visualization, tableResultComponent ignores result.data, result.meta, fields, and field renderers and mounts TableWidgetVisualization with columns={[]} and tableData data: []. Dashboards with that flag show a blank table even when the widget query succeeded. The previous StyledSimpleTableChart path, which actually binds the query result, is skipped entirely.

title: Hidden span attributes are only removed while searching
body: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES (is_segment, project_id, received) is applied only inside the search filter. The empty-query branch returns sortAttributes(attributes) unchanged, so those fields still render in the default Attributes tree. They disappear only after the user types a search string, which is the opposite of hiding them.

title: Saved-search conversion is no-op'd with no replacement migration
body: Both 0917 and 0920 now return immediately, and tests/sentry/migrations/test_0917_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views.py is deleted. The comment points at 0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py, but that migration is not in this PR. Environments that have not yet applied 0917/0920 will never copy organization SavedSearch rows into GroupSearchView, and nothing in this change still tests that conversion.

title: Merged PR comment helpers are on the wrong class
body: get_merged_pr_single_issue_template and get_environment_info were added to CommitContextIntegration, but GitHubPRCommentWorkflow and GitlabPRCommentWorkflow call them as self methods. Those workflows subclass PRCommentWorkflow, not CommitContextIntegration, so get_comment_body will raise AttributeError and suspect-issue PR comments will fail. The helper also calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title, while _truncate_title is defined only on CommitContextIntegration, so even a direct call would AttributeError.

title: Error timestamps from nodestore are not comparable to breadcrumb timestamps
body: fetch_error_details copies data.get("timestamp") straight into ErrorEvent. Nodestore event payloads store timestamp as an ISO string, not a float. gen_request_data then compares that value with segment event timestamps using <. A string-vs-number comparison raises TypeError inside the paginator callback and the summarize endpoint returns 500 whenever error context is enabled. Tests only pass because they store a numeric timestamp. The same loop also zips error_ids with events.values(), so a missing nodestore key drops alignment and attaches the wrong title/message/timestamp to an event id.

title: Table widget flag renders an empty table
body: When organizations:use-table-widget-visualization is on, tableResultComponent ignores result.data, fields, and metadata and renders TableWidgetVisualization with columns={[]} and tableData.data=[]. Every dashboard table widget becomes blank instead of showing the query result. The flag is a user-visible switch, not a dead code path.

title: Hidden span attributes are only removed while searching
body: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES (is_segment, project_id, received) is applied only inside the searchQuery branch. With an empty search the full attribute list is returned, so those fields stay visible. Typing a query then hides them even when the name matches, which is the opposite of a hide-always filter and makes search results inconsistent with the unfiltered tree.

title: 60s deadline can skip SSO identity refresh for a day
body: check_auth_identities now has processing_deadline_duration=60 but still refreshes up to chunk_size (100) identities sequentially, each via an external provider call. check_auth already stamps last_synced=now on the whole chunk before this task runs. If the worker hits the 60s deadline mid-chunk, the remaining identities are not refreshed and will not be selected again until the next AUTH_CHECK_INTERVAL (~24h), so SSO validity can stay stale.

title: Assemble analytics runs before auth/feature checks and can 500 the upload
body: analytics.record(..., user_id=request.user.id) now runs before the organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble feature check and before request body validation. This endpoint is used by org auth tokens (is_org_auth_token_auth later in the handler). If request.user is anonymous or has no id, accessing .id raises and CI assemble uploads fail with 500 even when the feature is enabled and the body is valid. Failures are also recorded as successful assemble events when the feature is off.

title: Installer identity check is skipped on first install
body: The new GitHub-user check never runs when Integration.DoesNotExist is raised: dispatch returns pipeline.next_step() immediately. OAuthLoginView only stores github_authenticated_user in pipeline state; build_integration never compares that login to the installer. GitHub's post-install redirect and the installation webhook are unordered, and installation ids are not secret, so an attacker who completes OAuth as themselves and supplies a victim installation_id before the Integration row exists binds that installation to their Sentry org with no sender check. The control the PR describes only runs on the narrow reinstall path where an ACTIVE Integration already exists and has no OrganizationIntegration. Fail closed until the installer identity is known (or compare against the installation record) before calling next_step().

title: Missing sender metadata crashes instead of failing the install
body: The mismatch check indexes integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] with no guard. Integrations created before this change, or created by build_integration when state has no sender, often have no sender key (or a non-dict sender). On the reinstall path where the Integration row exists but no OrganizationIntegration does, that raises KeyError and the request 500s instead of rendering the invalid-installation page. A missing or malformed sender should be treated as a failed authenticity check.

title: Installation-not-found test now fails on a bogus OAuth state
body: test_installation_not_found still stubs GET /app/installations/{id} as 404, but the follow-up request uses state ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05, which is not the pipeline signature asserted elsewhere (9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3). OAuthLoginView rejects that state and returns "Invalid installation request." before build_integration ever runs, so the test no longer covers the 404 path and would still pass if that error handling regressed. The same generic error string means test_github_user_mismatch also cannot tell a state mismatch from a real sender mismatch. Drive a matching state (and a distinct assertion) through the 404 and user-mismatch cases.

title: Installer identity is not checked on first link
body: The new GitHub-user check never runs when no Integration row exists yet. OAuthLoginView records github_authenticated_user, but GitHubInstallation catches Integration.DoesNotExist and calls pipeline.next_step(), which creates the integration and organization link from the caller-supplied installation_id with no comparison to metadata sender. GitHub installation ids are enumerable and the installation webhook can arrive after this request, so an attacker who finishes any OAuth login can win that race and attach someone else's app installation to their Sentry org. Once that OrganizationIntegration exists, the later "already installed" branch blocks the real installer. The mismatch check has to fail closed until the webhook sender is known, including on this create path.

title: Missing sender metadata crashes re-link
body: The new comparison reads integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] with no guard. build_integration only stores sender when pipeline state already has it, and older or webhook-incomplete Integration rows can be ACTIVE with zero OrganizationIntegrations — exactly the branch that reaches this line. A missing or non-dict sender raises KeyError instead of the installation-failed page, so a legitimate re-link 500s and cannot be completed.

title: Installation-not-found test no longer hits that path
body: test_installation_not_found stubs a 404 from /app/installations/{id} but then calls setup with state ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05, which is not the pipeline signature (9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3). OAuthLoginView rejects the state and returns "Invalid installation request." before build_integration or the 404 handler runs. The assertion matches that generic error, so a regression in the installation-not-found path would still pass, and the old "The GitHub installation could not be found." contract is no longer covered.

title: Installer identity is not checked on first link
body: The new GitHub-user check only runs after an Integration row already exists and has no OrganizationIntegration. If Integration.DoesNotExist, dispatch returns pipeline.next_step() immediately and build_integration links that installation_id to the current Sentry org with no comparison to github_authenticated_user. GitHub fires the installation webhook and the browser redirect in parallel, so an attacker who knows a victim installation_id can finish this pipeline before the webhook creates the Integration, attach the victim's GitHub App install to the attacker's org, and then block the real installer via the "already installed on another organization" path. The OAuth step therefore does not enforce the mismatch failure described in the PR for the claim-on-create path.

title: Reinstall crashes when metadata has no sender
body: After an Integration exists with no OrganizationIntegration, the code always evaluates integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]. build_integration only stores sender when pipeline state already has it, and this pipeline never binds sender, so installs created through the pipeline (and any older rows whose webhook payload did not write metadata.sender) have no sender. Re-attaching those installations raises KeyError instead of the integration error page, so a previously working reinstall 500s and never reaches next_step.

title: User-mismatch test cannot tell a state failure from the new check
body: test_github_user_mismatch (and the rewritten test_installation_not_found) only assert the generic "Invalid installation request." body. That same string is returned for a state/signature mismatch, a bad OAuth code, a missing login, and the sender comparison. The mismatch test also reuses the hardcoded state 9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3 after login_as(user_2) and a new org pipeline, so a state mismatch fails the request before GitHubInstallation ever compares logins. Nothing asserts that a matching installer is allowed, that a missing Integration is rejected, or that the 404 installation path still surfaces, so the security control can be bypassed or broken without these tests failing.

title: AssignmentSource datetime cannot be passed through Celery
body: sync_group_assignee_outbound always enqueues sync_assignee_outbound with assignment_source.to_dict(), and that dict includes queued as a datetime. Celery task kwargs are JSON-serialized; datetime is not JSON-serializable, so apply_async raises whenever an inbound webhook sets an AssignmentSource. That is exactly the path this PR adds. The same-integration skip happens only later, inside the worker after should_sync, so the exception fires before any outbound sync: other linked integrations never receive the assignee update, and the originating integration is not cleanly skipped either. from_dict also does not parse an ISO string, so converting queued to a string without a matching parser would drop the source (return None) and re-open the sync loop.

title: queued default is evaluated once at import
body: AssignmentSource.queued defaults to timezone.now() on the dataclass field. That call runs once when the class body is executed, not when each instance is created, so every AssignmentSource built via from_integration or from_dict without an explicit queued value shares the same timestamp from process import. The field is meant to record when the change was queued and is copied into the task payload; it will not reflect the actual assignment time and cannot order or expire rapid successive assignee webhooks.

title: No test that a different integration still syncs
body: The new test only covers the matching-integration case (outbound sync not called). The stated fix is that other issue-sync integrations must still receive the assignee update. Nothing asserts that path, so a regression that suppresses every outbound sync whenever any AssignmentSource is present would still pass.

title: queued timestamp is frozen at import time
body: AssignmentSource.queued uses a bare default of timezone.now(), which Python evaluates once when the class is defined, not on each instance. Every source built via from_integration() therefore shares the same import-time timestamp, and to_dict() persists that stale value into the Celery payload. Use field(default_factory=timezone.now) if queued is meant to record when the assignment was enqueued; as written the field cannot distinguish rapid successive assignee changes.

title: AssignmentSource dict is not safe to round-trip through Celery
body: sync_group_assignee_outbound passes assignment_source.to_dict() straight into sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async. asdict() includes queued as a datetime. A JSON task serializer either raises TypeError (so the outbound task is never enqueued, and other linked integrations never get the assignee update) or stringifies the datetime. from_dict() then does cls(**input_dict) and only recovers a source if construction does not throw; it never parses an ISO timestamp back into a datetime, and any TypeError/ValueError returns None. The worker then calls should_sync with no source and the originating integration is not skipped, so the sync cycle this PR is meant to stop still happens after a real queue hop. The new tests run under self.tasks() eager execution, which passes the dict in-process and does not catch this.

title: Cycle guard drops sync to every issue on the source integration
body: should_sync returns False for the whole installation when sync_source.integration_id matches org_integration.integration_id. Outbound fan-out is per ExternalIssue, but the guard has no external-issue key, so an inbound assignee change on one linked ticket suppresses outbound assignee sync for every other ticket on that same integration. A group linked to two Jira issues will leave the sibling ticket stale. It also still echoes the change to every other issue-sync integration, so two integrations with both inbound and outbound assignee sync enabled can ping-pong the assignee between themselves.

title: AssignmentSource.queued is a shared import-time datetime and is not task-serializable
body: AssignmentSource.queued uses timezone.now() as a dataclass default, which is evaluated once at import, so every source shares one timestamp instead of the time the webhook was handled. to_dict() then puts that datetime into assignment_source_dict, which sync_group_assignee_outbound passes as Celery kwargs. A datetime is not a JSON-safe payload; if the integrations queue serializes as JSON, apply_async raises and no outbound assignee task is enqueued. That drops sync to other integrations (the path this PR still wants) and can 500 the inbound webhook. from_dict also fail-opens: any TypeError/ValueError returns None, should_sync treats that as "no source", and the same-integration echo this PR is meant to stop is sent anyway. Use field(default_factory=timezone.now) and serialize queued to an ISO string (and parse it in from_dict) before enqueueing.

title: Outbound assignee sync always passes a new keyword implementations may not accept
body: sync_assignee_outbound now always calls installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source), including when the source is None. Previously this keyword was never passed. The abstract method accepts **kwargs, but concrete installations that declare (external_issue, user, assign=True) without **kwargs or assignment_source will raise TypeError on every outbound assignee sync, then retry up to 5 times. That breaks assignee propagation for those providers, not only the cycle-break path. Confirm every sync_assignee_outbound implementation accepts the keyword, or only forward it when the implementation supports it.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler cannot be constructed
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler and implements none of its abstract methods (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data). It is still assigned as MetricAlertFire.detector_handler. Detector.detector_handler instantiates that class, so any detector whose type slug resolves to MetricAlertFire raises TypeError instead of evaluating. Previously this handler was concrete and evaluate() returned an empty list.

title: Group-key evaluation test expects the wrong occurrence
body: TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds the expected IssueOccurrence via build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", 6, ...) but then calls evaluate_group_key_value("group_key", 10, ...). Production calls build_occurrence_and_event_data with group_key "group_key" and value 10, so the fingerprint (and any value-derived fields) will not match the expected result. The assertion is wrong and will fail if IssueOccurrence equality includes those fields, and it does not lock the new hook's arguments.

title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
body: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate now returns dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult], but its docstring still says it returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult. Callers reading the docstring will use the old contract that this PR intentionally removed.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler cannot be instantiated
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler and implements none of its abstract methods (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data). Instantiating an ABC with unimplemented abstracts raises TypeError. Detector.detector_handler does exactly that via group_type.detector_handler(self), and MetricAlertFire still sets detector_handler to this class. Previously this handler was concrete and evaluate() returned []. Any detector whose type resolves to metric_alert_fire will now crash when processed instead of no-opping.

title: Group-key evaluation test expects the wrong occurrence
body: TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds the expected IssueOccurrence with group_key "val1" and value 6, then calls evaluate_group_key_value with group_key "group_key" and value 10. build_occurrence_and_event_data uses that group_key in the fingerprint, so the occurrence the handler returns cannot equal the expected one (fingerprint "{detector_id}:val1" vs "{detector_id}:group_key"). This assertion fails, or if equality ignores fingerprint it does not actually check the occurrence the new hook produced.

title: evaluate() docstring still says it returns a list
body: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate now returns dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult], and process_detectors depends on .values(). The docstring still says it returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult. Callers following the docstring will iterate the dict keys (group keys) instead of the results and mishandle evaluation output.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler cannot be instantiated
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler and implements none of its abstract methods (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data). Detector.detector_handler instantiates group_type.detector_handler(self), so any Detector whose type is metric_alert_fire will raise TypeError instead of evaluating. Previously this handler implemented evaluate and returned an empty list, so process_detectors could skip it safely. The class is a registered GroupType (type_id 8001), so this is a live crash if that slug is ever loaded.

title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
body: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate now returns dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult], but the docstring still says it returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult. Callers that follow the docstring will treat the return value as a sequence of results and break (iterating a dict yields keys, not DetectorEvaluationResult objects).

title: Multi-group test builds group_2 expected occurrence with the wrong value
body: test_state_results_multi_group feeds group_2 the value 10, but the expected IssueOccurrence is built with build_mock_occurrence_and_event(..., "group_2", 6, ...). The helper ignores value, so the assertion still passes and never checks that evaluate passes the packet value into build_occurrence_and_event_data. A regression that forwarded the wrong value (or swapped group keys) would not fail this test, and updating the helper to include value would make the test fail for the wrong reason.

title: Monitor context sends raw config, not the display copy
body: get_monitor_environment_context copies monitor.config and, when schedule_type is present, replaces it with get_schedule_type_display() on that copy. The returned context then sets "config" to monitor_environment.monitor.config, the original dict, so the transformed copy is discarded. Issue occurrences therefore still carry the numeric schedule_type instead of the human-readable schedule type the code just computed, and any later mutation of the returned config mutates the in-memory model config.

title: Monitor context drops schedule_type display conversion
body: get_monitor_environment_context copies monitor.config and, when schedule_type is present, replaces it with get_schedule_type_display() on that copy. The returned context ignores the copy and sends monitor_environment.monitor.config instead. Occurrence events therefore keep the raw schedule_type (typically an integer enum) rather than the display string, and the conversion is dead code. Anything reading the monitor context (issue UI, consumers of the Kafka occurrence) will see the wrong schedule type.

title: Failure-reason text does not match intended wording
body: get_failure_reason builds each clause as "%(count)d %(status)s" (for example "2 missed") and then appends a single "check-ins detected". For more than one status that yields strings like "2 missed, 1 timeout and 1 error check-ins detected", not the documented "2 missed check-ins, 1 timeout check-in and 1 error check-in were detected". That string is stored as the important "Failure reason" evidence on the incident occurrence, so users see grammatically wrong, ambiguous failure summaries whenever the threshold window mixes statuses or the count is not the singular special case.

title: Schedule type display is computed then discarded
body: get_monitor_environment_context copies monitor.config and, when schedule_type is present, replaces it with get_schedule_type_display() so the occurrence context would show a human-readable schedule type. The returned dict ignores that copy and sets "config" to monitor_environment.monitor.config, the original mapping. The converted value is never sent, so issue occurrence monitor context keeps the raw schedule_type (typically an integer) instead of the display string the code just computed.

title: Join timeout leaves flusher processes running
body: SpanFlusher.join() sets the shared stopped flag, spends the entire timeout in next_step.join(), then breaks out of the process loop when remaining_time <= 0 before calling process.terminate(). Unlike the previous single-process join, a timed-out shutdown therefore does not signal or kill any flusher process that is blocked in Redis or Kafka future.result() and has not yet observed stopped. Those processes are not reaped on rebalance (the consumer process stays up; daemon exit only happens when the parent exits), so they keep flushing the same shards while the new assignment starts its own flushers. That races flush_segments/done_flush_segments and produces duplicate segments to the buffered-segments topic.

title: Restart starts a second flusher before the first is dead
body: _ensure_processes_alive() kill()s a hung SpawnProcess and immediately calls _create_process_for_shards without join() or any wait until exitcode is set. SIGKILL is asynchronous, and kill failures are swallowed, so the old process can still be inside flush_segments, produce, or done_flush_segments when the replacement process starts on the same shard list. Two flushers then mutate the same Redis segments and both emit Kafka payloads, duplicating spans. The replaced Process object is also dropped without join(), so each restart leaks a zombie until the consumer exits.

title: Flusher metric tags embed comma-joined shard lists
body: shard_tag is ",".join of every shard owned by the process, and it is sent as the statsd/metrics tag shard (and, on wait_produce, shards). With the CLI default of --flusher-processes 1, one process owns every assigned partition, so the tag value is a comma-separated list such as "0,1,2,...". DogStatsD encodes tags as comma-separated key:value pairs, so that value is parsed as extra tags and the timer is dropped or attributed wrong. It also makes the series cardinality depend on the partition assignment instead of a single shard id, and the same string is set as a Sentry SDK tag that will exceed the 200-character tag limit on large assignments.

title: Flusher wait in test_basic is patched out
body: test_basic monkeypatches time.sleep to a no-op, then calls time.sleep(0.1) to "give flusher threads time" after setting current_drift. That call hits the same patched sleep, so it does not yield. join() then sets stopped before the flusher thread is guaranteed to have observed the new drift and produced. The assertion (msg,) = messages can therefore fail intermittently, and the new test does not actually cover the multiprocess flush path it was adjusted for.

title: join() skips terminate when the deadline is already spent
body: SpanFlusher.join() gives the entire timeout to next_step.join(), then breaks out of the process loop as soon as remaining_time <= 0, before process.terminate(). The previous single-process join always called terminate() after the wait, even if the deadline had passed. Arroyo shutdown/rebalance uses a finite join timeout, so after this change every flusher process is left running. Those processes are only daemonized, not stopped, and the consumer process stays alive across rebalance, so the old flushers keep calling flush_segments/produce on the same Redis shards as the replacement consumer. That yields duplicate buffered-segments and concurrent Redis expiry/delete races.

title: Flusher metric tags are a joined shard list
body: Produce/wait timers tag metrics with shard_tag = ",".join(all shards owned by that process). --flusher-processes defaults to 1, so the common case is one process for every assigned partition and a single tag value like "0,1,2,...,N". That value changes with every assignment, blows past typical tag-length limits (metrics get dropped), and is a different key on the wait timer ("shards") than on the produce timer ("shard"). Per-shard flusher health and latency dashboards will not work.

title: Added flusher wait is a no-op under the sleep patch
body: test_basic monkeypatches time.sleep to a no-op, then calls time.sleep(0.1) to let the flusher observe the drift update before join(). That call is the patched no-op, so it does not yield. join() sets stopped immediately; if the flusher thread has not yet run flush_segments with drift 9000, the segment is never produced and the assertion on messages fails intermittently. The new test does not actually cover the race it was added for.

title: Spawn flusher processes are never killed or terminated
body: Processes are created with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, but restart and shutdown only call kill()/terminate() when isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process). On Linux the default context Process class is the fork implementation, and SpawnProcess does not subclass it, so the check is false in production. A hung or crashed flusher is therefore left running while _create_process_for_shards starts another daemon on the same shards, and join() never signals the extras to exit. Those overlapping flushers both call flush_segments and produce the same segments to Kafka until the restart cap crashes the consumer, duplicating span data.

title: Restart does not reap the old flusher before starting the next
body: After a failed kill(), or even after a successful asynchronous kill()/SIGKILL, the old process object is overwritten without join(). The previous flusher can still be inside flush_segments/produce/done_flush_segments while the replacement process starts on the same shard list and Redis keys. Two flushers then emit the same segments, and unreaped children accumulate as zombies across the up-to-10 restarts.

title: join() drops remaining flushers when the deadline hits
body: join() walks processes and breaks as soon as remaining_time <= 0, before terminate() for that process or any later ones. The previous single-process join always terminated after the wait. With multiple flushers, a timeout therefore leaves later processes running (and, combined with the SpawnProcess isinstance check, never terminates them at all). Shutdown can return while those processes are still flushing and producing.

title: Flusher metric tags are inconsistent and unbounded
body: produce and segment_size_bytes are tagged with key "shard", but wait_produce uses "shards", so the two timers cannot be joined in the same dashboards. The value is ",".join of every shard on that process. With the CLI default of one flusher process that string is the full partition assignment, and it changes on every rebalance, creating a new high-cardinality series (and a very long tag) per assignment instead of a stable per-shard tag.

title: Added sleep is a no-op under the time.sleep monkeypatch
body: test_basic replaces time.sleep with a lambda that returns immediately, then calls time.sleep(0.1) to "give flusher threads time to process" after setting current_drift. That call is the patched function, so it does not wait. The flush still races with join(), which sets stopped immediately, so the test can pass or fail depending on thread scheduling and does not actually cover the timing it was changed to fix.

title: Queues are unbounded, so there is no backpressure
body: FixedQueuePool creates each worker queue with queue.Queue() and submit() always put()s without a max size. The strategy docstring claims natural backpressure when queues fill, but an unbounded queue never blocks the Arroyo poll thread. If result handling is slower than ingest, every message is copied into process memory and the consumer keeps fetching. A slow subscription or DB stall can grow memory until the process is OOM-killed, and offsets still outstanding will be reprocessed after restart.

title: Kafka commits are issued from a background thread
body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy starts a daemon commit thread that calls the Arroyo commit callback about once a second. That callback is only safe on the strategy thread (poll/join); it mutates consumer offset state that the processor also touches. Committing from another thread can race with poll, rebalance, and shutdown, producing incorrect commits, exceptions in the consumer, or a commit that does not match what the processor believes is safe.

title: Strategy close kills the factory-owned worker pool
body: The queue pool and its threads are created once on ResultsStrategyFactory, but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() and terminate() call queue_pool.shutdown(), which sets worker.shutdown, calls Queue.shutdown(), and joins the workers. Arroyo closes the strategy on every partition revoke/rebalance and then calls create_with_partitions again on the same factory. The next strategy still holds the already-shut-down pool, so later submit() calls fail or drop work and the consumer cannot process after the first rebalance or restart of the assignment.

title: Submit failures are acknowledged and never retried
body: If decode, grouping, or queue put raises, submit() logs and immediately add_offset/complete_offset for that broker offset.
