The commit loop then treats the message as fully processed and commits past it. Unlike RunTask, this does not crash the consumer, retry, or DLQ. A transient error (DB blip during grouping, queue already shut down, codec glitch that escapes decode_payload) permanently skips the uptime result, so incidents derived from that check are never created.

title: Shutdown abandons queued work and can skip the final commit
body: close() stops the commit thread before pool.shutdown(). shutdown() sets worker.shutdown = True and then shuts the queues down. A worker blocked in get() may process one item and then exit because the flag is set, leaving the rest of the queue unprocessed. Those offsets stay outstanding, and because the commit thread has already been joined they are never committed. join() also ignores the timeout argument and close() joins each worker for up to 5s sequentially, so a 20-worker pool can block shutdown for over a minute and still drop the tail. After every deploy or rebalance those messages are redelivered, and any handler that is not idempotent can double-write.

title: Queue-depth test races the workers
body: test_stats_reporting submits 10 items and immediately asserts get_stats()["total_items"] > 0. Workers are already running and the processor is a no-op, so the queues can be empty before that assertion. The test will flake under load even though the pool is behaving correctly. The same pattern does not wait until in-flight work finishes: qsize() is 0 as soon as a worker has dequeued an item, so wait_until_empty can return while processing is still running.

title: Error-handling test asserts the opposite of the implementation
body: test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling says processing errors must not block commits, but it asserts that no offset was committed after a handler exception. OrderedQueueWorker catches that exception and complete_offset() still runs, so the commit thread will commit the partition within about a second. The test only sleeps ~0.2s after the queue drains, so it passes only when the commit loop has not fired yet and fails when it has. It neither locks the intended behavior nor is stable.

title: Queues are unbounded, so there is no backpressure
body: FixedQueuePool builds each queue.Queue() with the default maxsize (unlimited), and SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit always returns after put(). The class comment claims natural backpressure, but Arroyo will keep polling Kafka and enqueueing as fast as the broker allows. A single slow group blocks commits for its whole partition (offsets cannot advance past the oldest incomplete offset), while every later message on that partition is retained in memory. A hot or stuck subscription can therefore grow process memory without bound and turn the clog this PR is meant to avoid into an OOM, without ever pausing the consumer.

title: Strategy close kills the shared worker pool and stops commits before drain
body: The queue pool and its worker threads are created once on ResultsStrategyFactory and shared by every strategy from create_with_partitions. SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() sets the commit-loop shutdown event, joins that thread, then calls FixedQueuePool.shutdown(). shutdown() sets each worker's shutdown flag before Queue.shutdown(), so a worker blocked in get() exits on ShutDown and does not drain remaining items, and a worker between iterations leaves the loop immediately. Offsets finished only during that drain are never committed because the commit thread is already stopped. On partition revoke/rebalance Arroyo closes this strategy and calls create_with_partitions again; the new strategy reuses the already-shut-down pool, so later messages are not processed for the rest of the process lifetime. join() also ignores its timeout and can block about 5s plus 5s per worker.

title: Kafka commits are invoked from a background thread
body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy starts a daemon commit thread that calls commit_function (the Arroyo commit callback, which reaches the librdkafka consumer) every second. Every other strategy in this consumer commits from the processing thread. librdkafka consumers are not thread-safe, and that callback races with poll, submit, and close/terminate on the main thread. terminate() does not even join the commit thread, so a commit can run while the consumer is shutting down. This can crash the consumer, commit a torn offset map, or lose the in-flight commit.

title: Failed messages are acked and never retried
body: OrderedQueueWorker.complete_offset runs in a finally block, including after result_processor raises, and SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit also add+completes the offset when decode, grouping, or put fails. The strategy docstring says offsets are committed only after successful processing, but any exception is logged and then treated as done, with no DLQ on the uptime-results consumer. A transient DB or downstream failure is therefore committed (offset+1) and will not be redelivered, so an uptime check that failed to be handled can be dropped permanently. The new error-handling test asserts the opposite (no commit) and only sleeps 0.2s while the commit loop waits 1s, so it neither matches the code nor reliably checks it.

title: Queue-depth test races the workers and can flake
body: test_stats_reporting submits 10 items and immediately asserts get_stats()['total_items'] > 0. Workers are already running and the processor is a no-op, so the queues can be empty before that assertion. test_different_groups_distributed likewise requires 20 hashed keys to land in all 3 buckets, which is not guaranteed. Both can fail on a quiet CI run without a product bug.

title: Rebalance shuts down the shared pool, then failed submits are committed
body: FixedQueuePool is created once on ResultsStrategyFactory and reused by every SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy from create_with_partitions. Strategy.close/terminate (and factory.shutdown) call queue_pool.shutdown(), which shuts the queues and joins the workers. On the next assignment Arroyo builds a new strategy against that same dead pool. submit() then fails on Queue.put (queue.ShutDown), and the except Exception handler add_offset+complete_offset's the message. The new strategy's commit thread treats that as committable and commits offset+1. Those results are acknowledged and never processed, so uptime checks are dropped after the first revoke/rebalance or any close().

title: Queues are unbounded, so submit never applies backpressure
body: Each work queue is queue.Queue() with no maxsize, and FixedQueuePool.submit always put()s without blocking. The class docstring claims natural backpressure when queues fill, but the Arroyo consumer thread can keep polling and enqueueing forever while workers lag. A slow subscription (the case this mode is meant to isolate) or a dead worker grows memory without bound and can OOM the process. submit() needs a bounded queue and must block (or otherwise stall the consumer) when that queue is full.

title: Offsets are committed from a background thread
body: _commit_loop runs on a daemon thread started in SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy and calls the Arroyo commit callback directly. That callback commits through the Kafka consumer, which the processor is also using on the main thread for poll, assignment, and close. librdkafka consumers are not thread-safe; concurrent commit and poll/close can crash the consumer or corrupt the group offset. Commits need to be handed back to the processing thread (for example recorded in poll() and committed there).

title: Shutdown joins every worker for 5s and join() drops the timeout
body: FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets worker.shutdown then queue.shutdown, then joins each worker with timeout=5.0 in series. A worker blocked in result_processor (DB/HTTP) does not notice shutdown until the current item finishes, so N queues can block shutdown for about N*5 seconds (100s at the default 20). SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.join ignores the timeout Arroyo passes and always calls close(), which also joins the commit thread for another 5s before shutting the pool. A revoke or process shutdown can therefore exceed the Kafka session/max.poll interval and trigger another rebalance while workers are still running. join() must honor its timeout, and worker joins need a single shared deadline.

title: Graceful shutdown does not drain queued work before stopping commits
body: OrderedQueueWorker.run checks self.shutdown at the top of the loop, and FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets that flag before waking the workers. A worker that finishes the current item, or that is unblocked from get() with items still queued, exits without processing the rest of the queue. close() also stops and joins the commit thread before pool.shutdown(), so anything completed after the last commit iteration is never committed by this strategy, and anything still queued is abandoned. Arroyo's join contract is that submitted messages are finished or the timeout fires; here in-flight uptime results are dropped on the floor until a later replay, and a replay will not happen for any offset the commit thread already advanced past.

title: Queue stats test can pass or fail depending on worker timing
body: test_stats_reporting submits 10 items and immediately asserts get_stats()['total_items'] > 0. Workers are already running, so a fast result_processor can drain every queue before that assertion. The same file's test_different_groups_distributed asserts that 20 hashed keys always land on all 3 queues, which hash() does not guarantee. Both tests will flake under load or a different PYTHONHASHSEED.

title: Backup-code login skips the password when totpCode is set
body: Password verification runs only when `user.password` is set and `credentials.totpCode` is empty (the check around line 121). The new backup-code branch then logs the user in if the backup code matches and never validates `totpCode`. A request with the victim's email, any non-empty totpCode (for example "000000"), and a valid backup code therefore skips the password entirely, consumes that code, and creates a session. Backup codes are supposed to replace the authenticator only; the login UI still sends the password and clears totpCode, but the credentials callback must not trust the client to omit totpCode. Anyone who obtains a backup code (the downloaded cal-backup-codes.txt, a screenshot, a clipboard history) can take over the account without the password. Verify the password inside this branch whenever the user has one, and do not treat an unchecked totpCode as proof the password was already accepted.

title: One-time backup codes are consumed with a lost update
body: Redeeming a backup code decrypts the stored list, finds a match, sets that slot to null, and writes the whole blob back with a plain user.update keyed only by id. There is no transaction, row lock, or compare-and-swap on the previous ciphertext. Two overlapping logins can both read the same list and both succeed: the same code opens two sessions, and if the requests use two different codes the later write restores the code the earlier request consumed. The promise that each code works exactly once is therefore not enforced. Consume the code with a conditional update (or SELECT FOR UPDATE) that fails if backupCodes changed, and only then issue the session.

title: Backup code comparison is case-sensitive and unnormalized
body: Codes are generated as lowercase hex (crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex") in setup.ts) and login compares them with indexOf after only stripping "-". The same check is in apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts at the backupCode.replaceAll call. There is no toLowerCase() or trim, and spaces are left in place. The recovery input in apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx uses placeholder "XXXXX-XXXXX" and does not set autoCapitalize="none", so mobile keyboards and anyone following the placeholder submit uppercase hex. Those attempts always fail as an incorrect backup code, which blocks the recovery path when the authenticator is already lost. Normalize by trimming, removing dashes and spaces, and lowercasing on the server, and stop advertising uppercase in the field.

title: Closing the codes dialog does not finish 2FA setup
body: On a successful enable response the modal only moves to DisplayBackupCodes and no longer calls onEnable(). onEnable() runs solely from the footer Close button. Escape, the overlay, and the dialog's default close control go through onOpenChange and do not notify the parent, so the settings switch stays off while twoFactorEnabled is already true on the server. Clicking the switch again calls setup and gets TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled, so the user cannot finish or disable 2FA until a full reload. The codes themselves exist only in component state and a blob URL from the earlier setup response; nothing can fetch or regenerate them. Refreshing, closing the tab, or dismissing the dialog drops the only copy. The copy button makes this worse: navigator.clipboard.writeText is not awaited, and the success toast is shown even if the write fails, so the user can close thinking the codes were saved. Call onEnable() when enable succeeds (and on every close after that), require an explicit save acknowledgement, and do not toast success unless the clipboard write resolves.

title: missing_backup_codes points at a settings flow that does not exist
body: The new string says "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." This PR only creates codes inside the initial 2FA setup response and never adds a settings action to generate or rotate them. Users who enabled 2FA before the migration, or who dismissed the one-time codes screen, hit this error on "Lost access" and are told to do something the product cannot do. They can only get codes by disabling 2FA (which still requires the authenticator) and turning it on again. The message should not claim a generate-in-settings flow unless that flow exists.

title: Tests never log in or disable 2FA with a backup code
body: The new coverage only clicks download, copy, and close on the codes screen. Nothing submits a backup code at login, checks that a used code is rejected, or disables 2FA with a backup code (the TODO at the top of this file calls that out). The existing enable-and-login test was not updated for the new screen: after OTP it never clicks backup-codes-close, and expect(locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy() asserts on the Promise returned by isChecked(), which is always truthy, so it passes even when the switch is unchecked. A break in backup-code authentication, including the password bypass and the non-atomic consume, would not fail CI.

title: Backup code alone can log in if any TOTP value is also sent
body: The new backup-code branch in credentials authorize never checks the primary factor. Password verification only runs when credentials.totpCode is empty, and non-CAL users are rejected only when totpCode is empty. A caller who knows the email and one backup code can sign in by posting any non-empty totpCode (for example "000000") with that backup code and a wrong or empty password. The password check and the identity-provider check are both skipped, and a matching backup code creates a session. A backup code then replaces the password or the IdP login, not only the authenticator, which contradicts the UI copy. The disable endpoint does not have this hole: it verifies the CAL password before accepting a backup code. This branch must verify the primary factor even when totpCode is present, and a non-CAL account must not be able to finish credentials login with only a backup code.

title: Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write
body: After a backup code matches, the handler nulls that array slot and writes the re-encrypted list with a plain read-modify-write. The user row is not locked and the write is not conditional on the ciphertext that was just read. Two overlapping logins with the same code both see it as unused and both get a session, so the code is not single-use. Two overlapping logins with different codes can also lose an update: each write is based on a stale list, and the last write puts the other code back. Consume the code in a transaction that locks the user row, or compare-and-swap on the previous ciphertext, and only then issue the session.

title: Dismissing the backup-code step skips onEnable and loses the codes
body: A successful TOTP enable used to call onEnable() immediately. It now only moves to the backup-code step, and onEnable() runs only from the Close button. The dialog still takes onOpenChange, so Escape, the overlay, or the X control closes it without onEnable() or resetState(). Two-factor is already enabled on the server, but the parent is not notified, so the settings switch stays off and a later toggle tries to enable again and fails as already enabled. The codes live only in this component's state, are never shown again, and there is no regenerate action, so that dismiss also permanently drops the only copy. A refresh on this step has the same result. Block dismissal until the user finishes, or treat every close of this step as completion and call onEnable().

title: Download control nests a button in an anchor inside the enable form
body: The download control is a Button wrapped in an anchor with the blob URL, inside the form whose submit handler is handleEnable. Interactive content inside an anchor is invalid HTML, and browsers often do not follow the link when the click target is a button, so Download can save nothing. The button also does not set type="button". The copy and close buttons in this footer call preventDefault because a click submits the form; this control cannot do that without also cancelling the download. A click can therefore POST /api/auth/two-factor/totp/enable again after 2FA is already on, while the file may not download. Use a type="button" control that starts the blob download without wrapping a button in an anchor.

title: Lost-access button also submits the disable form
body: The new Lost access / Go back button is inside the disable Form and neither sets type="button" nor calls preventDefault. The real disable control in the same footer is type="submit", and the enable modal's non-submit actions call preventDefault because clicks in these forms submit. Clicking Lost access therefore also runs handleDisable. The click handler clears the code fields first, so the request is sent with an empty TOTP and backup code, the API returns a second-factor or incorrect-code error, and that error is shown just for switching modes. This disable path is untested. Set type="button" on the toggle.

title: Backup-code auth is untested and the enable assertion cannot fail
body: The enable-and-login test never closes the new backup-code step, so onEnable() does not run and the switch is not updated. It then asserts expect(locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy(). isChecked() returns a Promise, and a Promise object is always truthy, so the assertion passes without 2FA being enabled. The test can also log out before the enable request finishes. The new steps only check that a download is named cal-backup-codes.txt and that a success toast appears; they do not read the file or use a code. Nothing covers login with a backup code, single-use consumption, a password-less backup-code attempt, or disabling 2FA with a backup code. Those are the paths with the auth and race bugs.

title: Backup-code match is case-sensitive and only strips hyphens
body: Stored codes are lowercase hex from randomBytes(5).toString("hex"), but login compares credentials.backupCode with indexOf after replaceAll("-", "") only. The disable handler in apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts line 61 does the same. Uppercase letters, spaces, or a different dash fail the match and are reported as an incorrect code. The field placeholder is XXXXX-XXXXX, and the recovery path is typing a saved code after losing the authenticator. Lowercase and strip non-hex characters before comparing in both handlers.

title: Copy toast fires before the clipboard write succeeds
body: The copy handler calls navigator.clipboard.writeText without awaiting or catching it, then immediately shows a success toast. writeText rejects when permission is denied or the clipboard API is missing. The user is told the codes were copied, closes the dialog, and cannot view them again. Await the write and toast only on success; show an error if it fails.

title: Empty backup-code submit shows no error
body: The login form sets noValidate, and the zod schema only validates email and password before passthrough, so the BackupCode required and minLength attributes are not enforced. Submitting Lost access with an empty code sends a falsy backupCode. The server treats that as not using a backup code, requires a TOTP code, and returns SecondFactorRequired. This handler only sets twoFactorRequired and does not set an error, so the submit looks like it did nothing. Validate backupCode on that step and show an error for an empty submission.

title: Missing-backup-codes text points at a settings action that does not exist
body: missing_backup_codes says to generate codes in settings. Users who enabled 2FA before this column existed, and anyone with null backupCodes, see this on login and when disabling 2FA. There is no settings action to generate codes while 2FA is already on: setup returns two-factor-already-enabled, and codes are only created during enable. The instruction cannot be followed. Tell them to disable and re-enable 2FA with the authenticator, or add a real regenerate action and then point at it.

title: Backup code alone can log in if any TOTP field is sent
body: Password verification in credentials authorize runs only when `user.password` is set and `credentials.totpCode` is empty. The new branch then treats any non-empty `backupCode` as a full login: it decrypts the stored codes, and on a match it burns that code and returns a session. It never checks the password itself. A caller who knows only a backup code (the plaintext file this feature downloads as cal-backup-codes.txt, a clipboard copy, or the setup response) can POST email, `totpCode` set to any non-empty value such as "1", and that backup code, and get a session without the password. The normal UI often avoids this only because it clears `totpCode` before submit; the credentials endpoint does not. The code is also consumed on that request, so the attacker takes the account and destroys a recovery code. Verify the password inside this branch whenever the user has one, before accepting or burning the code. Do not rely on the earlier `!credentials.totpCode` gate.

title: One-time backup codes can be replayed or restored under concurrent logins
body: After a backup code matches, the handler nulls that array slot and writes the re-encrypted list with a plain `prisma.user.update` on user id. The read, check, and write are not in a transaction and the update is not conditional on the previous ciphertext. Two parallel logins with the same code can both see it as unused and both receive sessions. Two parallel logins with different codes can also lose an update: the later write is based on a stale array and can put a just-consumed code back. Backup codes are documented as single-use, but that is not enforced. Consume the code with a row lock or compare-and-swap on the stored ciphertext so only one request can spend a given code.

title: Valid backup codes are rejected unless they match lowercase hex exactly
body: Stored codes are lowercase hex from `crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`. Login compares with `indexOf` after removing only "-" characters. The same check is in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` at the `replaceAll("-", "")` / `indexOf` call. There is no `toLowerCase()` or trim. The entry field (`apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx`) uses placeholder "XXXXX-XXXXX", which reads as uppercase, and does not set `autoCapitalize="none"` or `autoCorrect="off"`, so mobile keyboards will capitalize the first character. Pasting a line from the downloaded file often includes a trailing newline or space; a code entered as uppercase or with whitespace will not match and the user gets "incorrect backup code" for a real code. Normalize by stripping whitespace and dashes and lowercasing before compare, on both login and disable.

title: Closing the backup-code dialog does not finish setup or keep the codes
body: TOTP enable is committed on the server before the backup codes are shown (`setStep(DisplayBackupCodes)` only after enable returns 200). The plaintext codes exist only in that earlier setup response and in React state; nothing in this PR can show them again, and `setup.ts` rejects another setup with TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled once 2FA is on. The dialog still uses the parent `onOpenChange` with no guard. Cancel is hidden on this step, but Escape, overlay click, and the dialog close control still dismiss it. Only the Close button calls `onEnable()` (and `resetState()`). The new e2e expects the security switch to become checked only after that Close click, so a dismiss leaves the settings UI showing 2FA off while the account has 2FA on. If the modal unmounts or the user leaves the page without using Copy/Download, the codes are gone and cannot be recovered without the authenticator. Block dismiss on this step until the user confirms the codes are saved, or call the same completion path as Close, and offer a way to regenerate codes while 2FA is already on.

title: Missing-backup-codes error points at a settings flow that does not exist
body: The new string is "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." Login and disable show it when 2FA is on and `backupCodes` is null (every account that enabled 2FA before this migration, and any account whose codes were never stored). There is no settings control or API in this PR to generate codes afterward: `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts` returns TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled if 2FA is already on, and codes are only returned during that setup call. A user who lost the authenticator and follows this message cannot generate codes and cannot sign in. The copy should not tell them to do something the product cannot do.

title: Copy toast claims success even if clipboard write fails
body: The Copy handler calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` and immediately shows the success toast without awaiting or catching the promise. `writeText` rejects when clipboard permission is denied, the document is not focused, or `navigator.clipboard` is unavailable, and that rejection is unhandled. The user is told "Backup codes copied!" and can close the only screen that shows the codes without a copy actually existing. Await the write, and show an error toast (and do not claim success) if it fails.

title: Tests never prove a backup code can log in or that it is single-use
body: The first enable test still ends by waiting on the 2FA switch after OTP submit and does not click `backup-codes-close`. After this PR that submit leaves the backup-code dialog open and does not run `onEnable`, so the switch is not updated; the assertion above is the one the new FIXME says passes even when the switch is unchecked. The second test only checks that a download is named cal-backup-codes.txt, that a success toast appears, and that Close checks the switch. It does not read the file or clipboard (those checks are TODOs) and never submits a backup code. Nothing covers login with a backup code, rejection of a wrong or reused code, or disabling 2FA with a backup code, which is the behavior this PR adds. A break in comparison, consumption, or the password check would still leave CI green.

title: Organization slug condition is inverted
body: The organization create payload changed `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` into `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. That drops the negation. With billing disabled, neither `slug` nor `requestedSlug` is saved, so the new org has no URL. With billing enabled, `slug` is written immediately and `requestedSlug` is still written, so the slug is claimed before payment instead of staying pending. This is unrelated to destination calendars and will break org creation in both modes.

title: Google Meet bookings crash when no destination calendar is set
body: The Cal Video fallback now does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` and then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` with no null check. If destinationCalendar is null, undefined, or [], that value is undefined and booking creation throws TypeError before the location can be switched. The old code used optional chaining, so Meet with no Google calendar fell back to Cal Video. Every caller that passes null or [] (new bookings with no destination calendar, confirmation, and payment webhooks) will 500 on Google Meet instead of booking.

title: Secondary host events are created against the first destination calendar
body: createAllCalendarEvents loops over every destination calendar and calls createEvent once per host credential, but it still passes the full destinationCalendar array. CalendarManager.createEvent forwards only credential.id into the service, not that destination's externalId. Office 365, Lark, and CalDAV/Apple all still read only the first array element: Office builds `/me/calendars/${firstExternalId}/events` with the other host's token, Lark creates on the first calendar id, and BaseCalendarService filters to the first externalId. If that id is not on the secondary account, CalDAV's filter matches nothing, Promise.all of an empty list is treated as success, and a booking reference is stored for an event that was never created. Google does look up calendarId by credentialId, but the organizer attendee email is still the first destination's externalId, so the secondary Google insert can 400 or list the wrong organizer. Hosts other than the first therefore do not reliably get a calendar event, which is the bug this PR is meant to fix.

title: Collective host calendars are dropped when the organizer has none
body: Team destination calendars are collected for COLLECTIVE hosts, then attached with `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)`. The evt is initialized to null when both the event type and the organizer have no destination calendar, so the optional push is a no-op and those host calendars are discarded. createAllCalendarEvents then takes the empty branch, whose fallback filters credentials with `type === "calendar"`. Real types are `google_calendar` and similar, so that fallback never matches either. A collective booking whose organizer has not set a destination calendar creates no per-host calendar events even when every other host has a calendar connected.

title: Cancelling remaining recurring bookings does not delete each host event
body: The new per-reference cancel loop wraps the recurring all-remaining branch unchanged. That branch ignores the reference it is iterating, loads only booking.user.credentials (the organizer, not other hosts, and with no DB lookup), and for each future instance deletes only the first reference whose type includes `_calendar`. Other hosts' events on those instances are never deleted, so their calendars keep the cancelled series. Because this sits inside the new for-loop, the same incomplete delete also runs once per calendar reference and hammers the first event. The non-recurring branch already deletes each reference with its own credentialId and a DB fallback; the recurring branch needs the same treatment over every updated instance's calendar references.

title: Payment and confirmation creates still use a single destination calendar
body: Only handleNewBooking appends the other collective hosts' destination calendars. Stripe payment_intent.succeeded calls EventManager.create with an evt whose destinationCalendar is at most `[booking.destinationCalendar || user.destinationCalendar]`. The same single-calendar evt is built in getBooking (used by setup_intent.succeeded around the eventManager.create call) and in paypal-webhook.ts handlePaymentSuccess. confirm.handler.ts builds the same one-element list from the booking relation or the session user and passes it to handleConfirmation, without loading event-type hosts. Booking.destinationCalendar can store only the first calendar (handleNewBooking connects evt.destinationCalendar[0]). Paid or requires-confirmation collective bookings therefore still create only the organizer's calendar event, so the other hosts never get invited.

title: Google update/delete fallback can never resolve a calendar id
body: updateEvent now does `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)`. When externalCalendarId is null, undefined, or empty, the find compares every calendar id to that same falsy value and always returns undefined. The previous fallback was the destination calendar's externalId. calendar.events.update is then called with calendarId undefined and the update fails. deleteEvent (around line 315) uses the same dead find and then substitutes "primary", so a missing externalCalendarId deletes on the primary calendar; a 404 is treated as success and the event remains on the calendar it was actually created on. Any reference stored without externalCalendarId, including the no-credentialId create branch and seated-attendee updates that pass a null externalCalendarId, hits this.

title: Video booking references no longer store credentialId
body: referencesToCreate used to set credentialId to result.credentialId for every non-calendar result. It is now `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`, so video (and any other non-calendar) references are always saved without a credential id. handleCancelBooking only calls deleteMeeting when bookingVideoReference.credentialId is set, and then looks that id up in the user's credentials. New bookings will leave Zoom/Daily/other video meetings in place on cancel, and later location updates cannot find the credential that created the meeting.

title: Location updates persist calendar references without ids
body: updateLocation now sets externalCalendarId from result.externalId and credentialId from result.credentialId only. CalendarManager.updateEvent does not return either field, and the previous fallbacks to evt.destinationCalendar.externalId and credentialId were removed. editLocation writes referencesToCreate onto the booking. Calendar update results have updatedEvent rather than createdEvent, so those new rows also get uid "". A later cancel treats them as legacy references and calls deleteEvent with an empty uid on every calendar credential, and the real calendar id needed to patch the existing event is gone.

title: One missing host credential fails every calendar update
body: The new per-reference update loop loads a credential from the DB, but if that row is missing or has no app.slug it still pushes updateEvent(undefined, ...). getCalendar then rejects. Unlike createAllCalendarEvents, there is no `if (credential)` guard. The shared catch (around line 591) also dropped the console.error, and it returns a synthetic failure for every calendar reference instead of the updates that already succeeded. With multiple host references, one deleted or unlinked credential makes reschedule, location change, and attendee updates report total calendar failure and hides the underlying error. The seated-merge delete just below also calls getCalendar on a findUnique result with no null check, so a missing old credential aborts the same way.

title: CRM other_calendar references are updated twice
body: calendar references are now every reference whose type includes `_calendar`. Types such as closecom_other_calendar match that filter, so they are updated in the new per-reference loop and again by the later pass that filters `type.includes("other_calendar")`. Previously find() handled only the first calendar reference, and the second pass was what updated CRM calendars. Duplicate updates can create duplicate CRM activities or fail the second call. The first loop should exclude other_calendar types.

title: Seat merge deletes only the first host calendar event
body: When newBookingId is set (rescheduling a seated attendee into an existing slot), the cleanup still does booking.references.find for a single `_calendar` reference and deletes only that event. The rest of this function was rewritten to walk every calendar reference, but this path was not. Other hosts keep a live event at the old time after the merge, so their calendars stay busy and still show the meeting.

title: Webhook destinationCalendar shape changed and is inconsistent
body: CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar changed from a single DestinationCalendar or null to an array or null, and that object is spread into webhook payloads. Subscribers reading destinationCalendar.integration or destinationCalendar.externalId will break, but the PR is marked as a non-breaking bug fix. Emitters also disagree on the empty value: handleNewBooking still sends null when no calendar is set, while confirm, cancel, reminders, and payment handlers send []. The e2e suite only changed BOOKING_REJECTED to expect [] and still expects null for BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED, so the new contract is neither documented nor consistently tested.

title: No test covers multi-host calendar create or cancel
body: This change rewrites create, update, and delete across every destination calendar, but the only test edit is an e2e webhook expectation for an empty destinationCalendar. There is no coverage that a collective booking writes one event per host credential, that Google Meet with no destination calendar still books, that Office/CalDAV/Apple hosts are not given the organizer's calendar id, or that cancelling all remaining recurring instances deletes every host event. The PR checklist notes that no such tests were added, so these regressions will not be caught before merge.

title: Google Meet booking throws when destinationCalendar is missing
body: EventManager.create now takes the first destinationCalendar and reads .integration with no null check. If the list is null, undefined, or [] (the value many callers now pass when nobody has a destination calendar), destructuring yields undefined and this throws TypeError before any video or calendar work. Previously optional chaining treated a missing calendar as not Google and replaced Meet with integrations:daily. Any Google Meet booking without a destination calendar, including confirmation and payment flows that pass [], now fails the whole create instead of falling back to Cal Video.

title: Video references no longer store credentialId
body: referencesToCreate used to persist result.credentialId for non-calendar results and now stores undefined whenever the result is not a calendar type. updateLocation in this same file still copies result.credentialId, so this is an accidental drop. handleCancelBooking only calls deleteMeeting when the video BookingReference has a credentialId, and there is no fallback lookup by integration type. New bookings will therefore not record the video credential, and cancelling them leaves the Zoom, Daily, or other video room in place.

title: Secondary hosts are written to the first destination calendar
body: createAllCalendarEvents loops each host destination and calls the provider with that host's credential, but it still passes the full destinationCalendar array. Only GoogleCalendarService picks the calendar by credentialId. Office 365 and Lark still use index 0, so a second host's token is aimed at the organizer's calendar id and the API call fails; that host never gets an event. CalDAV/Apple (BaseCalendarService) filters the host's calendars to the organizer's external id, matches nothing, and still returns success, so a booking reference is stored for an event that was never created. Google inserts also set the organizer attendee email from the first destination's externalId, so events written onto another host's calendar are attributed to the main calendar. Office 365 updateEvent and deleteEvent still always call /me/calendar/events/{id} and ignore the target calendar id, so a non-default Office event cannot be rescheduled or removed. Narrow the event to the destination currently being written before calling any provider.

title: Google update/delete fallback can never select a calendar
body: When externalCalendarId is missing, updateEvent and deleteEvent (same expression at line 317) search destinationCalendar for an entry whose externalId equals that missing value. That comparison is dead: if a calendar id had been passed, the first branch would already have used it. Previously the fallback was destinationCalendar.externalId. updateEvent then calls the Google API with calendarId undefined, so reschedule and location updates fail for any booking reference that has no externalCalendarId. deleteEvent falls through to primary, and a 404 is treated as success (line 335), so cancellation reports success while the event remains on the non-primary calendar.

title: Collective host calendars are dropped from the event
body: Other hosts' destination calendars are only appended with optional chaining. If neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, the field is null and the push is a no-op, so every other host is discarded. createAllCalendarEvents then falls back to credentials whose type is exactly "calendar", which never matches google_calendar, office365_calendar, and the rest, so nobody gets a calendar event. Separately, when the event type does have a destination calendar, that single calendar replaces the organizer's personal calendar, and only users.slice(1) are added, so the organizer's own calendar is never included. The stated goal that every collective host with a calendar app receives an event is not met in either case.

title: Only the first destination calendar is stored on the booking
body: Booking.destinationCalendar is a single relation and the create payload connects only evt.destinationCalendar[0]. The other hosts' calendars exist only on the in-memory event used for the immediate create. Stripe payment_intent.succeeded and setup_intent.succeeded, and PayPal handlePaymentSuccess, rebuild CalendarEvent from that one booking or user record and call EventManager.create. confirm.handler does the same and passes the evt to handleConfirmation. Collective bookings whose calendar events are created after payment or after organizer approval therefore only write the first calendar; every other host is skipped even if the initial assembly was correct.

title: Cancelling a recurring series leaves other hosts' events
body: The non-recurring branch deletes each calendar reference with that reference's credential. The all-remaining recurring branch was not updated: it still loads only the booking owner's calendar credentials and, for each instance, uses find() so only the first _calendar reference is deleted. It is also nested inside the new per-reference loop, so that incomplete deletion runs once per calendar reference. Other hosts' credentials are never loaded, Google 404s from the wrong token are treated as success, and the booking is already marked cancelled. After "cancel all remaining", secondary hosts keep the series on their calendars and stay busy.

title: Organization slug condition is inverted
body: This unrelated change flips slug assignment. Previously slug was set only when team billing was disabled, and requestedSlug only when billing was enabled. requestedSlug is still gated on IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED, but slug is now set in that same case and omitted otherwise. With billing off, new organizations are stored with neither slug nor requestedSlug, so the org subdomain cannot resolve. With billing on, the slug is published immediately and requestedSlug is also set, skipping the hold-for-billing gate.

title: Google create falls back to primary instead of the chosen calendar
body: createEvent selects the calendar only by matching destinationCalendar.credentialId to the credential used for the call. EventManager still has a legacy path for destination calendars with no credentialId, and that path calls createEvent without an external id. The find then misses, and the insert uses "primary" instead of the destination calendar's externalId, so the event is written to the wrong calendar and reported as success. The follow-up hangout-link patch at line 168 passes selectedCalendar with no primary fallback, so that patch runs with an undefined calendarId and the Meet link is never written into the description. The stored booking reference external id will not match the calendar that was actually written.

title: Location updates store calendar references without ids
body: updateLocation now sets externalCalendarId and credentialId from the EventResult. CalendarManager.updateEvent does not return either field (it also does not return externalId), and calendar updates populate updatedEvent rather than createdEvent. New booking references created by edit location therefore have an empty uid and no calendar credential or external calendar id. Previously those ids were copied from the destination calendar. The new multi-reference cancel path treats a missing credentialId as a legacy reference and calls deleteEvent on every calendar credential with a null external id, which no longer falls back to the real destination calendar.

title: Seat-merge reschedule deletes only the first old calendar event
body: updateAllCalendarEvents was changed to update every calendar reference, but the newBookingId merge path still does references.find() and deletes only the first _calendar reference. When a seated booking is moved onto an existing slot, every other host's old calendar event is left in place at the original time. Those hosts remain busy for a booking that has already been merged away.

title: Webhook destinationCalendar shape is a breaking, inconsistent change
body: destinationCalendar on CalendarEvent changed from a single object or null to an array or null, and that object is sent on booking webhooks. Consumers that read payload.destinationCalendar.externalId or .integration will now see an array (or crash). The PR is marked non-breaking, but this is a public payload change. Callers are also inconsistent: handleNewBooking sends null when there is no calendar, while confirm, payment webhooks, and cancel send []. The e2e suite only updated BOOKING_REJECTED to expect []; BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED still expect null, so the contract is not locked down.

title: No test covers multi-host calendar create or cleanup
body: The only test change is a webhook fixture expecting destinationCalendar: [] for BOOKING_REJECTED. Nothing books a collective event with two hosts on different calendar providers and asserts one successful write per host credential, and nothing asserts that cancel, reschedule, and payment-confirmation paths create or delete every stored booking reference. The checklist explicitly says no tests were added. The provider, recurring-cancel, and deferred-create bugs above would not be caught by CI.

title: Google Meet fallback throws when no destination calendar is set
body: The Meet-without-Google-Calendar fallback used to read destinationCalendar?.integration, so a missing calendar evaluated to undefined and was replaced with Cal Video. It now destructures the first element of the new array and reads .integration with no null check. handleNewBooking sets destinationCalendar to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has one, and confirm.handler sets []. Both become an empty array here, so mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined and booking creation throws TypeError before the fallback can run. Any Google Meet booking that has no destination calendar — the case this branch exists for — now fails instead of falling back to Cal Video.

title: Collective host calendars are discarded when the main calendar is null
body: Co-host destination calendars are collected into teamDestinationCalendars, then appended with evt.destinationCalendar?.push. The field is set to null when the event type and the organizer both lack a destination calendar, and optional push on null does nothing, so every co-host calendar just collected is dropped. createAllCalendarEvents then sees no destinations. Its empty-list fallback only keeps credentials whose type is exactly "calendar", which never matches real types such as google_calendar, so nobody gets a calendar event. Even when the array is non-null, a host is included only if user.destinationCalendar is already set and schedulingType is COLLECTIVE, so a connected calendar with no destination-calendar row, and dynamic multi-user bookings without that scheduling type, still never get events. Initialize an array before pushing, and do not rely on the null optional chain.

title: Each host create still targets only the first destination calendar
body: createAllCalendarEvents calls createEvent once per destination, but always passes the original event whose destinationCalendar array still lists every host. Lark (larkcalendar CalendarService.ts around line 129), Office 365 (office365calendar CalendarService.ts around line 75), and CalDAV (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts around line 162) only read index 0. Later iterations therefore use the co-host's token against the first host's calendar id. Office 365 and Lark fail that write; CalDAV filters to the foreign URL, matches nothing, and still returns a successful uid, so a booking reference is stored for an event that was never created. The no-credentialId branch at line 380 also calls createEvent without destination.externalId and for every credential of that integration type, which duplicates events and cannot reach other hosts' credentials. If a credential cannot be loaded or has no app.slug, that host is skipped with no error result, so the booking still succeeds. updateAllCalendarEvents (line 542) passes the same unsplit event into every update, so reschedule has the same index-0 problem whenever a service falls back to destinationCalendar[0]. This is the stated acceptance criterion (every host calendar app should receive the event) and it does not hold for non-Google calendars.

title: Google organizer email is always the first destination calendar
body: createEvent now picks the calendar to write by matching credentialId, but the organizer attendee email is still taken from destinationCalendar[0] (mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId). The same event object, containing every host, is passed on every call, so an event written onto a co-host's calendar lists the primary host's calendar externalId as organizer. updateEvent (line 228) does the same on reschedule and location updates. Google can reject a write whose organizer does not match the authenticated calendar, or save an event with the wrong organizer and guest list, so co-host Google events are wrong even when calendarId selection succeeds. Select the destination entry that matches the credential or externalCalendarId being written, or pass a one-element destinationCalendar for that host.

title: Cancelling a recurring series does not delete co-host calendar events
body: When all remaining instances of a recurring booking are cancelled, the new per-reference loop still uses the old recurring body. That body ignores the reference and credential just resolved (including a co-host credential loaded from the database) and instead walks only the booking owner's calendar credentials. For each instance it uses references.find, so only the first calendar reference is deleted, and that delete is repeated once per owner credential and once per outer reference. Co-host credentials are never used, so their events stay on their calendars and keep blocking availability after the series is cancelled. Delete every calendar reference of every updated instance with that reference's own credentialId, and do not nest that work inside the outer reference loop.

title: Organization slug is now set in the opposite billing case
body: This unrelated edit inverts when an organization slug is stored. Previously slug was written on the team when team billing was disabled, and only metadata.requestedSlug was stored when billing was enabled so the slug could be assigned after payment. The new condition sets slug only when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, and sets nothing when it is false. The requestedSlug line was not inverted, so billing-enabled creates now set both slug and requestedSlug. Self-hosted orgs (billing flag off) are created with no slug and cannot be resolved by subdomain. Billing-enabled orgs claim the slug immediately while still unverified, which conflicts with the deferred-slug flow. Restore slug when billing is disabled, and only requestedSlug when it is enabled.

title: New booking references drop video credentialId and some external calendar ids
body: referencesToCreate used to store evt.destinationCalendar.externalId for calendar results and result.credentialId for non-calendar results. It now stores result.externalId and, for anything that is not a calendar type, hardcodes credentialId to undefined. createAllCalendarEvents only passes destination.externalId into createEvent when destination.credentialId is set (line 370). The legacy branch at line 380 calls createEvent(c, event) with no external id, so those references are saved with externalCalendarId undefined. handleCancelBooking only calls deleteMeeting when the video reference's credentialId is set, so if the video EventResult carried credentialId — which this mapping used to persist — cancelling a booking no longer deletes the remote meeting. Calendar references missing externalCalendarId also cannot be updated or deleted on the right calendar, especially with the broken Google fallback.

title: Location change saves calendar references without calendar ids
body: updateLocation builds referencesToCreate from result.externalId and result.credentialId. Calendar updates come from updateEvent, whose EventResult does not set externalId, credentialId, or createdEvent (CalendarManager.updateEvent only returns updatedEvent). Previously this mapping copied evt.destinationCalendar.externalId and credentialId onto every new reference. editLocation.handler persists referencesToCreate with references.create, so each location edit now inserts calendar rows with an empty uid and no externalCalendarId or credentialId. Later cancel/update cannot target the calendar those rows refer to, and deleteEvent may be called with an empty uid. Copy the reference's existing externalCalendarId and credentialId (or return them from updateEvent) instead of reading fields update results do not populate.

title: Google update/delete fallback compares externalId to a missing id
body: When externalCalendarId is missing, updateEvent used to fall back to destinationCalendar.externalId. It now does destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId). That find only runs when externalCalendarId is already null or empty, so it looks for a calendar whose externalId is null and never matches. calendar.events.update is then called with calendarId undefined and the update fails. deleteEvent (line 317) has the same find, then falls back to "primary", so a cancellation of an event that lives on a non-primary calendar and whose booking reference has no externalCalendarId hits primary, gets a 404, and is swallowed — the event stays on the user's calendar and continues to block time. Fall back to the destination entry for this credential, or to destinationCalendar[0].externalId, not to a comparison against the missing id.

title: A missing calendar credential fails every calendar update
body: The new update loop loads a credential by reference.credentialId, but if it is still missing (deleted credential, or app.slug absent so the DB object is ignored) it still calls updateEvent(credential, ...) with credential undefined. createAllCalendarEvents guards with if (credential); this path does not. updateEvent then rejects, Promise.all rejects, and the catch treats every calendar reference as failed even if other updates already ran. The catch builds an error message and no longer logs it (console.error was removed), so the failure is silent in logs. Skip or record a per-reference failure when the credential cannot be loaded, and do not abort the rest of the batch.

title: Merging a reschedule deletes only the first old calendar event
body: When newBookingId is set, updateAllCalendarEvents now updates every calendar reference, but the following cleanup still uses booking.references.find for a single _calendar reference and deletes only that one, and only if it has a credentialId. Co-host events created by this PR are left on their calendars after a seated merge/reschedule, so those slots stay busy. If the first reference has no credentialId, none of the old events are deleted. Delete every old calendar reference, using each reference's credentialId.

title: Confirming a collective booking still schedules one calendar
body: confirmHandler builds the CalendarEvent passed to handleConfirmation with only booking.destinationCalendar or the confirming user's destinationCalendar, wrapped in a one-element array. Booking.destinationCalendar is a single relation (handleNewBooking connects only evt.destinationCalendar[0]), and this handler never loads the other hosts' destination calendars. handleConfirmation is not updated in this PR to expand hosts itself, so a collective event that requires confirmation still creates a calendar event only for that one calendar. Co-hosts do not get events on confirm, which is the bug this change is supposed to fix for any booking that is not immediately accepted.

title: PayPal confirmation creates events for only one calendar
body: On payment success this builds evt.destinationCalendar from booking.destinationCalendar or the booking owner's user.destinationCalendar only, then, when the booking is already accepted, calls eventManager.create(evt). That is a single calendar. The in-memory multi-host list from handleNewBooking is not stored on the booking (only the first destination calendar is connected), and this webhook does not load event-type hosts. Paid collective bookings whose calendar events are created here still invite only one host.

title: Stripe confirmation creates events for only one calendar
body: handlePaymentSuccess sets destinationCalendar from booking.destinationCalendar or the booking owner only, then calls eventManager.create(evt) when the booking is already accepted. getBooking (line 119) does the same, and handleSetupSuccess uses that evt to create events when confirmation is not required. Neither path loads other collective hosts' destination calendars, and the booking row only has the first destination calendar connected. Paid or setup-intent collective bookings therefore still create a calendar event for one host only.

title: Reschedule request deletes co-host events with the acting user's token
body: Requesting a reschedule cancels the booking and deletes calendar events, but credentials are keyed only by credential.type from the acting user (credentialsMap.set(credential.type, credential)), not by reference.credentialId. A co-host reference whose type the actor also has (for example google_calendar) is deleted with the actor's token and the co-host's event uid. Google treats the resulting 404 as success, so the co-host event is left in place and the slot stays busy. References whose type the actor does not have are skipped entirely, with no database credential lookup. handleCancelBooking was updated to delete each reference with its own credential; this path was not, so collective events created by this PR are not removed from co-host calendars when a reschedule is requested.

title: Webhook destinationCalendar changed from object to array
body: CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar is now DestinationCalendar[] | null, and webhook payloads spread that evt (the playwright BOOKING_* assertions include this field). Existing consumers that read payload.destinationCalendar.externalId or .integration will get undefined, because those fields are on the object, not the array. The PR describes this as a non-breaking bugfix, but it is a public payload break with no versioning. Producers are also inconsistent: handleNewBooking sends null when unset, while confirm and the payment webhooks send []. BOOKING_REJECTED in webhook.e2e.ts now expects [] and BOOKING_CREATED / BOOKING_REQUESTED still expect null, so clients cannot null-check the field reliably.

title: No test covers multi-host calendar create, update, or delete
body: The only test change rewrites the BOOKING_REJECTED webhook fixture from destinationCalendar null to []. There is no coverage that a collective booking writes an event to each host's calendar, stores a reference with that host's credentialId and externalCalendarId, updates those events on reschedule, and deletes all of them on cancel — including non-Google calendars, a missing organizer destination calendar, recurring cancel-all, and payment or confirmation flows. The PR checklist notes that no such test was added. The bugs in this change (null push dropping co-host calendars, services always using index 0, recurring cancel deleting only the first reference) would not be caught in CI.

title: Google token refresh stores the Zod wrapper as the credential
body: After refreshing, Google CalendarService passes the updated credential object to parseRefreshTokenResponse and writes the return value directly to credential.key. That helper returns the Zod safeParse result {success: true, data: {...}}, not the token object (Office 365 and Zoom read .data). The next GoogleCalendarService constructor runs googleCredentialSchema.parse on that wrapper, which no longer has access_token at the top level, and throws. This runs whenever the access token is expiring, including when credential sync is disabled, so existing Google Calendar connections break until the user reconnects. If the Prisma write throws, the catch treats any error other than invalid_grant as recoverable and returns the old client, so the new token is never stored either.

title: Missing refresh_token is overwritten with the literal "refresh_token"
body: After a successful parse, if refresh_token is missing the helper sets data.refresh_token to the string "refresh_token". This runs for the normal provider schema and the sync schema. Office 365 calendar then spreads tokenResponse.data onto the stored credential and writes it (office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts around line 264). Microsoft often omits refresh_token on refresh and expects the previous one to be kept; the Office 365 schema marks it optional for that reason. The next refresh sends grant refresh_token=refresh_token, Microsoft returns invalid_grant, and the connection stays dead until the user reconnects. In sync mode the minimum schema strips the real refresh_token first, so this always fires, and Zoom then saves that literal (zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts line 120) in place of the real refresh token.

title: Salesforce refresh calls prisma without importing it
body: The new getClient path calls prisma.credential.update after exchanging the refresh token, but this file never imports prisma. Reaching that line throws ReferenceError: prisma is not defined and fails typecheck. getClient runs from the SalesforceCalendarService constructor, so every Salesforce create, update, or availability check throws and no connection is returned. This is not gated on credential sync, so it breaks existing Salesforce installs on deploy.

title: Sync token schema drops every field except access_token
body: minimumTokenResponseSchema is used whenever credential sync and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set. The computed keys z.string().toString() and z.string().optional().toString() are not Zod wildcards; both become "[object Object]", so the second overwrites the first. The schema only requires access_token and z.object strips unknown keys by default (there is no passthrough). Expiry, refresh_token, scope, and instance_url are discarded. Office 365, Zoom, and Salesforce then persist that stripped object. Zoom also sets expiry_date from the missing expires_in, which becomes NaN. A sync refresh therefore corrupts the stored credential instead of updating it.

title: Sync refresh returns a fetch Response callers cannot read
body: When credential sync is on, refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response and never checks response.ok or parses JSON. Callers still expect the old provider return value. Google CalendarService reads res.data, which exists on the Gaxios result and not on a fetch Response, so token.access_token throws; the catch ignores anything other than invalid_grant and the access token is never updated. HubSpot treats the Response as a HubspotToken and reads camelCase accessToken/expiresIn. Zoho Bigin and Zoho CRM read axios response.data and throw or skip the update. Webex still validates with webexRefreshedTokenSchema, which requires a fixed scope, token_type "Bearer", refresh_token, and refresh_token_expires_in, so the documented access-token-and-expiry payload is always rejected. Office 365 video replaces the whole credential key with the parsed body and drops refresh_token and email if they are absent. Enabling CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT therefore breaks refresh for the apps this PR wires up.

title: Salesforce client keeps the pre-refresh access token
body: After a successful token response, getClient saves accessTokenParsed.data.access_token but returns a jsforce Connection still configured with credentialKey.access_token and credentialKey.instance_url from before the refresh. If the stored access token is already expired, the API call that triggered getClient uses that expired token and can 401 even though a fresh token was just fetched. The new token is only used on a later request, and only if the database update succeeded.

title: Zoho Bigin sends the credential id as calcomUserId
body: refreshAccessToken passes credentialId, which is credential.id, as the third argument to refreshOAuthTokens. That argument is the Cal.com user id and is sent as calcomUserId. With sync enabled, the parent looks up tokens by a credential primary key, not the user, and can return another user's tokens when a user id collides with this credential id. The following code expects an axios response and reads tokenInfo.data; a fetch Response has no data, so it throws before the local update today. Fixing response parsing without fixing this argument would then write the other user's Zoho tokens onto this credential. Other adapters pass credential.userId.

title: Salesforce refresh fails unless statusText is exactly "OK"
body: The new token request throws HttpError when response.statusText is not the string "OK", before reading the body. Node fetch/undici often leaves statusText empty, especially on HTTP/2, which login.salesforce.com supports. A 200 with an empty or different reason phrase is treated as failure, getClient never returns a connection, and Salesforce calendar operations fail. The check should use response.ok or response.status.

title: Salesforce refreshes the OAuth token on every client construction
body: getClient always POSTs to the Salesforce token endpoint before building the connection, with no check that the stored access token is still valid. Availability and booking construct SalesforceCalendarService often, so each call adds a token round trip and consumes Salesforce OAuth quota. Previously the connection was created from the stored token and jsforce refreshed only when Salesforce rejected it. This extra call is not limited to credential sync, so it regresses every Salesforce user, and a token-endpoint failure now breaks operations that still had a valid access token.

title: Outbound credential sync request is unauthenticated
body: The POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends only calcomUserId and appSlug. It does not send CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET, a signature, or an Authorization header, and it does not check response.ok. The inbound webhook that writes credentials requires the shared secret, but the call that returns live access tokens does not prove it came from this Cal.com instance. An endpoint implemented to match this client cannot tell Cal.com from any other caller, so anyone who can reach that URL can request access tokens for arbitrary user ids and app slugs.

title: Credential webhook can insert duplicate rows
body: The handler uses findFirst and then updates or creates, with no transaction, lock, or unique constraint on (userId, appId). userId and type are not unique on Credential (other OAuth callbacks already special-case duplicates). Two deliveries for the same user and app, including a retry, can both see no row and both insert. findFirst has no orderBy, so a later sync updates an arbitrary duplicate while calendar code that also uses findFirst can keep the stale key. The user ends up with two credentials and the integration may keep using outdated tokens.

title: Credential sync does not clear the invalid flag
body: The update path writes only key and does not set invalid to false. Google, Webex, and Zoom set invalid after invalid_grant and then skip that credential. If a self-hoster pushes a fresh key for that user, this endpoint still returns 200, but Cal.com keeps ignoring the row, so the integration stays disconnected until the flag is cleared or the user reinstalls the app.

title: Webhook turns bad bodies and ciphertext into unhandled 500s
body: appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse throws a ZodError on a missing or wrong-typed body, and JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) throws if the ciphertext, key, or plaintext is invalid. Nothing catches those errors, and the handler does not require POST. The parent sync client gets a 500 instead of 400, cannot tell a bad payload from an outage, and may retry indefinitely. A decrypt exception can also leak crypto library details in the error response.

title: Zoom sync slug is "zoomvideo" but credentials are stored as "zoom"
body: refreshOAuthTokens is called with appSlug "zoomvideo", but the Zoom callback creates the credential with appId "zoom", and the new webhook stores appId from the app metadata slug, which is "zoom" for this app. The parent platform is the source of truth keyed by slug. A sync or refresh using one of these strings will not find the credential written under the other, so Zoom tokens will not update, or a second credential will be created under the wrong slug and never used by the video adapter.

title: Lark deletes the credential before sync refresh can run
body: refreshAccessToken still deletes the credential and throws when the local refresh token is missing or refresh_expires_date has passed, and that check runs before refreshOAuthTokens. With credential sync enabled, the parent app holds the real tokens and the local refresh token may be expired or absent, which is exactly when the sync endpoint should be called. Instead the row is deleted, the sync URL is never hit, and the user must reconnect Lark. The sync branch has to run before this destructive local-token check.

title: No tests for credential sync or shared OAuth refresh
body: This PR changes token refresh for Google, Office 365, Zoom, HubSpot, Lark, Webex, Zoho, and Salesforce and adds a webhook that writes credential rows, but it adds no tests. The PR checklist says tests were not added and were not run. The sync-disabled path needs a test that a provider response without refresh_token does not overwrite the stored refresh token and that credential.key is the token object, not a Zod safeParse wrapper. The sync-enabled path needs tests that the outbound request is authenticated, sends the user id rather than the credential id, and that each adapter can read the response. Without that, the credential corruption in parseRefreshTokenResponse and Google CalendarService is not caught before deploy.

title: Google refresh persists the Zod result wrapper as the credential
body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the Zod safeParse object ({success, data}), not the parsed token. This call site used to store googleCredentialSchema.parse(...), but now writes that wrapper to credential.key (lines 97-100). The in-memory client is updated from googleCredentials, so the current request can still succeed, but the next load runs googleCredentialSchema.parse on {success, data} and throws. Every Google Calendar credential breaks after the first refresh (about an hour), with or without credential sync. If sync is on, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response with no .data, so token.access_token throws; the catch on line 108 treats any error other than invalid_grant as success and returns the expired client, so refresh fails silently and the credential is not marked invalid.

title: Salesforce token update calls prisma but never imports it
body: getClient now calls prisma.credential.update after refreshing the Salesforce token, but this file does not import prisma. The name is undefined, so the first Salesforce calendar operation throws ReferenceError once the token endpoint returns OK and never builds a jsforce Connection. Salesforce event create/update/delete is broken for every user as soon as this ships, including installs that never enable credential sync.

title: Refresh parser strips real tokens and writes a fake refresh_token
body: The minimum schema's computed keys are z.string().toString() and z.string().optional().toString(), not wildcards. Those are literal property names (both typically "[object Object]", so the second overwrites the first). They do not match expires_in or expiry_date. When CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set, every caller uses this schema, including team credentials that still hit the real provider (the switch does not check whether the sync fetch ran) and Salesforce, which never calls the sync endpoint. safeParse then keeps only access_token and strips refresh_token and expiry. Lines 25-27 set refresh_token to the literal string "refresh_token" whenever it is missing. Office 365 spreads that object over the stored credential (office365calendar CalendarService.ts around line 264) and saves it, replacing the real refresh token. Zoom assigns newTokens.refresh_token and does Date.now() + newTokens.expires_in * 1000, so expiry_date becomes NaN/null and the refresh token is destroyed. The same fake value is applied on the default path whenever the app schema leaves refresh_token optional, which Office 365 does, and the refresh request does not send offline_access, so a response that omits refresh_token permanently breaks reconnect-free refresh.

title: Salesforce now fails closed on an unconditional, wrong-host token refresh
body: getClient always POSTs to https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token before returning a connection, even when the stored access token is still valid. Sandbox and many My Domain orgs must refresh against test.salesforce.com or their own login host; login.salesforce.com rejects those refresh tokens. Failure is detected via statusText !== "OK" (not response.ok), the error body is discarded, and the credential is not marked invalid, so the throw aborts every Salesforce operation instead of falling back to the existing token. The Connection on lines 101-108 is still built with credentialKey.access_token and credentialKey.instance_url, not the token just fetched, so a successful refresh is not what the client uses. Adding the missing prisma import does not fix this.

title: Sync refresh returns a raw fetch Response callers cannot consume
body: When credential sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns the fetch Response and does not check response.ok or parse JSON. Callers were not updated to that contract, and the comment says the body should be only an access token and expiry, which none of them read. Google expects a gaxios response and reads res.data (throws, then swallowed). Hubspot expects a token object with expiresIn/accessToken and then prisma-updates that value as credential.key; a Response JSON-serializes to an empty or near-empty object, so a refresh can wipe the Hubspot credential. Zoho Bigin and Zoho CRM read axios .data and throw. Lark passes the Response to handleLarkError, which requires Lark's {code, data} envelope. Webex still validates with webexRefreshedTokenSchema (fixed scope, refresh_token, refresh_token_expires_in), so the documented minimal body is rejected. Office 365 video replaces the entire credential key with the parsed body, so a partial payload drops refresh_token and email. With the feature env vars set, token refresh for these apps fails or destroys stored credentials.

title: Token sync request is unauthenticated
body: The POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends only calcomUserId and appSlug. It does not send CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET, a bearer token, or a body signature, and the URL scheme is not required to be HTTPS. The inbound webhook is authenticated, but this outbound call is what returns live OAuth access tokens. The parent app cannot tell Cal.com from any other caller, and user ids are sequential, so anyone who can reach that URL can request access tokens for arbitrary users. A self-hoster cannot fix that without editing this shared helper.

title: Zoho Bigin sync sends the credential id as the user id
body: refreshAccessToken is only given credentialId (the credential primary key) and passes that value as the userId argument to refreshOAuthTokens. When sync is enabled the helper treats any truthy number as a user id and posts it as calcomUserId, so the parent looks up the wrong user (or nobody) and will not return this user's token. The normal axios refresh is skipped entirely in that mode. The caller also expects an axios response (tokenInfo.data on line 96); a fetch Response has no .data, so the refresh throws even if the endpoint responded.

title: Lark deletes the credential before credential sync can refresh it
body: The new sync call sits after the guard that deletes the credential when refresh_token is missing or refresh_expires_date is expired. Credential sync is the path that is supposed to obtain a new access token from the parent when Cal.com does not hold a usable refresh token (parseRefreshTokenResponse even fabricates refresh_token because sync responses may omit it). A webhook-created Lark credential without a still-valid refresh token is deleted on first use instead of being refreshed, and the user must reconnect. If a refresh token is present, the sync Response is still passed to handleLarkError, which requires Lark's envelope, so a normal token JSON body fails the refresh anyway.

title: Credential webhook updates an arbitrary row and leaves it invalid
body: The handler findFirsts on userId plus appId with no orderBy, then updates or creates outside a transaction. userId and appId are not unique: Google's callback always inserts a new credential, and calendar code later loads a specific credential id. findFirst can update a different row than the one in use, return 200, and leave the active token stale. Concurrent deliveries can both miss and insert duplicates. The update only writes key, so a row already marked invalid stays invalid and is skipped by calendar loading even after a successful sync. Decrypted keys are JSON.parsed and stored with no per-app schema check, so a payload that is not the shape that app expects is persisted and breaks the integration on next use.

title: Zoom sync asks for app slug zoomvideo instead of zoom
