body: refreshOAuthTokens is called with appSlug "zoomvideo", but the Zoom app id and installed slug are "zoom" (see zoomvideo/api/callback.ts, appId: "zoom"). Other integrations pass the app-store slug (google-calendar, msteams, office365-calendar). The webhook stores credentials under appMetadata.slug, so a parent that keys off the real slug will not find a Zoom credential when Cal.com posts appSlug=zoomvideo, and token refresh for Zoom sync will 404 or return the wrong app's tokens.

title: No tests for credential ingestion or the shared refresh path
body: The new webhook can overwrite any user's OAuth credentials, and parseRefreshTokenResponse / refreshOAuthTokens now run on Google, Office 365, Zoom, and Salesforce refresh. The PR checklist says tests were not added, and there are none for a missing or wrong webhook secret, decrypt failure, two credentials for one app, or a refresh that reloads the saved key. A round-trip that refreshes a Google credential and reads it back would have caught the safeParse wrapper being stored; an Office 365 refresh whose body omits refresh_token would have caught the literal "refresh_token" overwrite.

title: Google refresh persists the Zod wrapper and breaks the credential
body: GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken now saves the return value of parseRefreshTokenResponse as credential.key. That helper returns Zod's safeParse result, {success: true, data: ...}, not the token object. The previous code stored googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials). This runs on every expiry refresh whether or not credential sharing is enabled. After the first successful refresh (access tokens last about an hour), the row no longer matches googleCredentialSchema, which is parsed again in the constructor at the next GoogleCalendarService load. Availability, event create/update/delete, and Meet links then throw for that linked credential. Reconnecting creates a new credential row and does not repair the existing id already attached to destination calendars, so the broken row keeps being selected. When sharing is enabled the same function fails earlier: refreshOAuthTokens returns a Fetch Response with no .data, token.access_token throws, and the catch treats every error other than invalid_grant as success and returns the expired client without writing a new token.

title: Refresh parser invents refresh_token and strips real token fields
body: After a successful parse, parseRefreshTokenResponse sets data.refresh_token to the literal string "refresh_token" whenever the field is missing, and callers persist that object. Office365CalendarService spreads the parsed data over the stored credential. Its schema marks refresh_token optional, and Microsoft's token endpoint is allowed to omit a new refresh token while the previous one stays valid. The spread then replaces the real refresh token with "refresh_token", so the next refresh fails until the user reconnects. This is not limited to the new sync flag. When sharing is enabled the schema used instead is also wrong: the computed keys z.string().toString() and z.string().optional().toString() are one literal property (both are typically "[object Object]", so the second overwrites the first), not a wildcard, and Zod strips unknown keys. expires_in, expiry_date, refresh_token, scope, and instance_url are dropped, then the placeholder refresh token is added. Office 365 and Zoom write that result back; Zoom also sets expiry_date from a missing expires_in, which is NaN, and zoomTokenSchema rejects NaN on the next read. Salesforce would persist the stripped object once its missing prisma import is fixed. The comment that any numeric property is the expiry is not implemented.

title: Salesforce refresh calls prisma without importing it
body: The new getClient path calls prisma.credential.update, but this file never imports prisma. Every other adapter in the PR imports @calcom/prisma explicitly, so this is not a global. SalesforceCalendarService constructs this.conn by calling getClient, so the first Salesforce calendar operation throws ReferenceError before a jsforce connection is returned. Event create, update, delete, and contact sync fail for every Salesforce user as soon as this code runs, including deployments that never enable credential sync.

title: Salesforce always refreshes against production and then uses the old access token
body: getClient now always POSTs to https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token and throws unless statusText is exactly "OK", before it builds the connection. Sandbox orgs must refresh at test.salesforce.com, and My Domain orgs use their own token URL; those refreshes fail and abort the client even when the stored access token is still valid. Previously a valid access token was used directly. The jsforce Connection is then created with credentialKey.access_token, the pre-refresh value, not the access token just returned, so an already-expired token is what this request uses. The refresh also ignores refreshOAuthTokens, so CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is never consulted for Salesforce. The value written back is accessTokenParsed.data; with sharing enabled that object has been reduced to access_token plus a fabricated refresh_token, so instance_url and the other Salesforce fields are dropped from the saved key.

title: Sync refresh returns an unchecked Fetch Response that callers treat as a provider token
body: When sharing is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw Fetch Response and does not check response.ok, parse JSON, or set a timeout. Callers were not updated to that contract, and the comment says the body should only be an access token and expiry, which is not what they read. HubSpot, Zoho CRM, and Zoho Bigin expect an axios or HubSpot SDK object and read .data, .accessToken, or .expiresIn. HubSpot then passes that Response to prisma.credential.update as key; JSON serialization keeps only the own property expiryDate (NaN becomes null), so the stored HubSpot credential is wiped to {expiryDate: null}. Google reads res.data, throws, and its catch swallows every error except invalid_grant, leaving the expired token in place. MS Teams parses the body and replaces the entire credential key with it, dropping refresh_token and email. Lark, Webex, and Zoom feed the same response into handlers that require the provider envelope; a non-OK or invalid_grant-shaped sync error can mark the Zoom or Webex credential invalid. A hung sync URL blocks booking and availability indefinitely because fetch has no timeout.

title: Token sync request sends user id with no authentication
body: The POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends only calcomUserId and appSlug. It does not send CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET, an HMAC, or any other credential, and it does not require the URL to be https. That endpoint is expected to return OAuth access tokens. The parent app therefore cannot tell Cal.com from any other caller who can reach the URL, and a client that can reach it can request tokens for arbitrary user ids. An http:// endpoint value would also put bearer tokens on the wire in cleartext. Nothing in .env.example says the caller is unauthenticated. The response is trusted with no status check, so an error body can be stored as a credential.

title: Lark deletes the credential before the sync refresh can run
body: refreshAccessToken still deletes the credential and throws when the stored refresh token is missing or refresh_expires_date is expired. That check runs before the new refreshOAuthTokens call. With credential sync the parent is the source of truth, and the sync helper documents a response that only contains an access token and expiry, so the local refresh token may be absent or already expired. In that case Cal.com deletes the Lark row instead of asking CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT for a new access token. The connection is gone and later calendar calls fail until the user reconnects; a webhook replay cannot help if the row was removed and a later findFirst misses the replacement.

title: Zoho Bigin sync sends the credential id as the Cal.com user id
body: BiginCalendarService.refreshAccessToken passes credentialId, the Credential primary key, as the third argument of refreshOAuthTokens. That argument is posted as calcomUserId. Credential ids and user ids are independent sequences, so when sync is enabled the parent looks up tokens for the wrong person and can return another user's Zoho access token. The Bigin code then reads tokenInfo.data as if the result were an axios response. A Fetch Response has no .data, so refresh throws and Bigin calls fail. If the response parsing is fixed without fixing the id, the other user's token would be written onto this credential.

title: Zoom sync asks for app slug zoomvideo but credentials are stored as zoom
body: Zoom's refresh calls refreshOAuthTokens with appSlug "zoomvideo", but the OAuth callback in this PR stores the credential with appId "zoom" and the install path uses slug "zoom". When credential sync is enabled, the parent is queried for zoomvideo and will not find the Zoom tokens it stored or received under zoom. Refresh fails and Zoom meetings cannot be created for synced users even when the webhook wrote a valid credential.

title: Credential sync upsert is racy and can leave a stale duplicate
body: The webhook does findFirst({userId, appId}) and then either updates that id or creates a row. Those steps are not in a transaction, and Credential has no unique constraint on (userId, appId). The Lark callback in this PR already notes that userId and type are not unique, which is why that flow updates by credential id. Two concurrent deliveries, including a parent retry, can both see no row and both insert, or findFirst can update an arbitrary duplicate because there is no orderBy. Calendar code also uses findFirst, so it can keep using a stale credential while the webhook returns 200. A retried sync therefore does not reliably make the parent the source of truth.

title: Synced credentials are not unmarked invalid
body: When a credential already exists, the webhook updates only key. It does not set invalid to false. Google, Webex, and Zoom in this PR set invalid true so a failed refresh stops being used. A parent that pushes a replacement token for a credential Cal.com already marked invalid still gets 200, but loaders that skip invalid rows will ignore the new keys and the integration stays disconnected.

title: Webhook throws on bad input and stores decrypted keys with no shape check
body: The handler has no method check and no try/catch around zod parse, symmetricDecrypt, or JSON.parse. A non-POST, a missing body, a string userId (the schema is z.number(), not coerce), or a ciphertext that does not decrypt to JSON becomes an unhandled 500, and the crypto or parser message can be returned to the caller. The decrypted value is written straight into credential.key. An array, string, or unexpected object is accepted, so a buggy parent can persist a shape the app later casts and crashes on, with a 200 only if Prisma happens to accept it.

title: Privileged credential webhook uses a raw reusable secret
body: This route can replace any user's integration credential, including calendar, video, CRM, and Stripe payment keys, for any app slug. The only check is inequality against a static header value. The compare is not constant-time, the secret is the raw header rather than an HMAC over the body, and there is no timestamp or nonce. A captured request stays valid forever and also discloses the secret itself, so the holder can forge new writes for every userId, not only replay one body. Rolling a rotated token back is enough to keep using a stolen OAuth refresh token after the parent thought it had replaced it.

title: No tests for credential sync or the OAuth refresh persistence change
body: The diff adds a privileged webhook and changes token refresh for every major OAuth app, but there are no new tests, and the PR checklist says tests were not added. The manual plan only hits the webhook and a simulated sync refresh. A unit test that refreshes Google and Office 365 with sharing disabled and asserts the stored key is still the token object, with the previous refresh_token kept when the provider omits one, would have caught the universal credential corruption. The webhook also has no coverage for a wrong secret, a non-object decrypted payload, an invalid credential being cleared, or two concurrent creates.

title: Team admin/owner check can never succeed
body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner. Membership role is a single value, so a user is never both ADMIN and OWNER, and the && short-circuits. If isTeamAdmin matches only ADMIN, the check is always false; if it also treats OWNER as admin, only owners pass and admins still fail. Either way team admins cannot add guests unless they are also the booking organizer or an attendee, which contradicts the variable name and the permission gate. The bookings UI still shows Additional guests on confirmed rows, so those users hit FORBIDDEN. Use ||, and skip the lookup when eventType.teamId is null instead of querying team id 0.

title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials
body: EventManager is built from the signed-in user and getUsersCredentials(ctx.user). Calendar BookingReferences are tied to the organizer's credential id (and other hosts' credentials on collective events), not the caller's. The query already loads booking.user with credentials and destinationCalendar and never uses that user. When an attendee adds guests, the host calendar event is not updated. On collective events, other hosts' calendar copies cannot be updated either because only one user's credentials are supplied. Load decrypted credentials for the booking organizer (getUsersCredentials, not the raw Prisma credential rows) and include collective hosts.

title: Any attendee can invite unlimited guests on any booking
body: Authorization only checks organizer, attendee, or the broken team-admin flag. booking.status, end time, and list size are never validated, and ZAddGuestsInputSchema is an unbounded email array. Any logged-in attendee can therefore add as many addresses as they want to a cancelled, rejected, unconfirmed, or past booking. Each new address is sent AttendeeScheduledEmail, and the mailer hardcodes ICS status CONFIRMED. videoCallData (join URL and meeting password) is copied onto the event whenever a video reference exists, so those invites disclose meeting access for events that are not accepted upcoming meetings, and a participant can send unlimited calendar mail through the platform. Restrict this to accepted future bookings and cap the guest list.

title: Seated events are not capacity-checked
body: Guests are inserted as Attendee rows with no comparison to eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot, which is only copied onto the calendar payload later. If occupancy is the attendee count, this overbooks the slot and can block real bookers. If occupancy is BookingSeat / seatsReferences, these guests become attendees with no seat, so seat counts, the seats UI, and cancel/reschedule links diverge from the attendee list. seatsShowAttendees is also ignored: sendAddGuestsEmails and the ICS include every attendee, leaking participant emails on events configured to hide them. Enforce remaining capacity before insert, or reject add-guests for seated events, and honor seatsShowAttendees when emailing.

title: Guests stay saved when calendar or email updates fail
body: prisma.booking.update commits the new Attendee rows before translation loading, updateCalendarAttendees, and sendAddGuestsEmails. The calendar call is outside the try/catch, so a thrown calendar or translation error returns 500 after the insert. A retry then filters those addresses out as already present and throws emails_must_be_unique_valid, so the calendar update and invite emails are never retried and the user is told the addresses are invalid. Email failures are caught, logged as a static string with the error discarded, and the handler still returns success, so the dialog toasts Guests added when nobody was notified. Roll back or make the side effects retryable, and do not report success when notification failed.

title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive
body: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS values are lowercased but not trimmed, and the submitted address is not trimmed or lowercased before includes(). A blocked address with different casing, or a blacklist entry with a leading space after the comma, is stored and emailed. Duplicate detection uses case-sensitive equality, so A@x.com and a@x.com both become Attendee rows, and the organizer's own email is not excluded. The read of existing attendees is also outside a transaction, so two parallel requests can both pass the filter and insert the same guest. Normalize both sides with trim and lowercase, trim blacklist entries, and do not add the organizer as an attendee. Mixed requests currently drop blocked or duplicate addresses silently and still return success.

title: New guests are stored with a blank name
body: Every newly inserted guest is saved with name set to an empty string. Scheduled and add-guest mail payloads address the recipient as `${attendee.name} <${attendee.email}>`, so new guests, who are sent AttendeeScheduledEmail, get a blank display name (` <email>`). The same empty name is sent in the calendar attendee update. Use the email address, or its local part, when no name was collected.

title: Already-invited emails get a new booking confirmation
body: sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the raw guests input, not uniqueGuests, the addresses actually inserted. In that helper, any attendee whose email is in the list receives AttendeeScheduledEmail (a full new-booking confirmation with cancel and reschedule links) instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. If the request includes someone already on the booking plus a new guest, the existing person is not inserted again but still gets a fresh scheduled email and does not get the guests-added notice. The includes() check is also case-sensitive. Pass the normalized list of addresses that were actually added.

title: Add-guest emails ignore disabled standard emails
body: sendAddGuestsEmails always emails the organizer and every attendee. Other helpers in this file (sendScheduledEmails, sendLocationChangeEmails, sendCancelledEmails, and the rest) skip host or attendee mail when event-type metadata disables standard emails. This helper has no such check, and addGuestsHandler never passes eventType.metadata. Organizers who turned those emails off still get guest-added mail and full AttendeeScheduledEmail messages, including ICS and meeting links, when guests are added. Pass the metadata through and honor the same disable flags.

title: Collective co-hosts are never notified
body: The CalendarEvent built for notifications never sets team or team.members, even though eventType is already loaded. sendAddGuestsEmails only emails extra hosts when calendarEvent.team.members is present, so that loop never runs. On a collective event, only booking.user receives OrganizerAddGuestsEmail; the other hosts are not told that guests were added. Load the event-type hosts and set calEvent.team the same way other booking mail flows do.

title: Add-guests is offered on past bookings
body: The new additional-guests action is added to editBookingActions, which is included in bookedActions. bookedActions is not limited to upcoming meetings: past confirmed bookings and past pending bookings also render TableActions with that list. Using it still inserts attendees and sends AttendeeScheduledEmail plus an ICS REQUEST for a time that already passed. Only show this action for accepted upcoming bookings, and enforce the same rule in addGuestsHandler.

title: No tests for addGuests authorization or failure paths
body: The new mutation ships with no unit or integration tests. The inverted team-admin condition, access to cancelled or past bookings, seated overbooking, blacklist casing, and a calendar or email failure after the attendee insert would not be caught in CI. Cover organizer, team admin, team owner, attendee, and stranger; non-accepted bookings; seat capacity; and a side-effect failure after insert.

title: Team admin/owner check is AND and never matches a real role
body: isTeamAdminOrOwner requires isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner to both be true. Membership has a single role, so a team admin is not an owner and an owner is not an admin; the branch is dead for normal memberships. Team admins and owners therefore cannot add guests unless they are also booking.userId or an attendee. Collective co-hosts who are only on the event hosts/references (not booking.userId and not attendees) are rejected as well. The bookings UI treats admin and owner as alternatives (isUserTeamAdminOrOwner) and still shows the action, so those users get FORBIDDEN. The check needs to be OR, and other hosts on the booking need to be allowed.

title: Calendar update uses the actor's credentials, not the host's
body: The query loads booking.user with credentials and destinationCalendar, but updateCalendarAttendees is called with an EventManager built from ctx.user and getUsersCredentials(ctx.user). Calendar references store the host credential id. This handler explicitly allows attendees, and the booker is an attendee while booking.userId is the host, so the booker path — a primary use of "add guests" — does not have those credential ids. The host calendar event is then not updated (or the call throws). The same happens for a team admin acting on someone else's booking, and even the owner path only has one user's credentials, so other collective hosts' calendar references are skipped. Guests can be stored while the existing invites still list the old attendees.

title: Attendees are committed before calendar and email, with no recovery
body: prisma.booking.update createMany commits the new Attendee rows before updateCalendarAttendees and sendAddGuestsEmails. Only the email call is in try/catch, and that catch logs a fixed string, drops the error object, and then the handler still returns success. If the calendar update throws (wrong credentials, provider error), the mutation 500s after the rows exist, emails never run, and AddGuestsDialog does not invalidate the bookings query on error. A retry treats those addresses as already invited and throws emails_must_be_unique_valid, so the guests stay on the booking with no mail and no calendar update, and the user cannot retry. There is no compensation or idempotent resend.

title: Attendees can fan out meeting invites with no state or guest limits
body: The only gate is organizer, attendee email match, or the broken team-admin check. booking.status and endTime are never read, so guests can be added to CANCELLED, REJECTED, PENDING, and already-ended bookings. The new mailers always attach an ICS with status CONFIRMED (attendee-add-guests-email.ts line 15, organizer-add-guests-email.ts line 19) and the payload includes the video URL from booking references, so a pending or cancelled meeting's join link is emailed as a confirmed invite. eventType.disableGuests is never read, so this bypasses the public booking form's no-guests setting. ZAddGuestsInputSchema.guests (addGuests.schema.ts line 5) is an unbounded email array, and each new address gets AttendeeScheduledEmail. Newly added guests are stored as attendees, so anyone with a Cal.com account for that address can invite more people. This is an authedProcedure, not limited to the bookings page.

title: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is bypassed by case and spaces
body: The env list is lowercased but not trimmed, and the filter uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) on the raw input. Zod email() does not lowercase, so Banned@example.com is inserted and then mailed when the list contains banned@example.com. A space after a comma ("a@x.com, b@x.com") makes every entry after the first fail to match. Blacklisted addresses that do match are dropped silently; if any other address remains, the handler still returns success, so the client toasts that every submitted guest was added.

title: Guest dedup is case-sensitive, racy, and not applied inside the request
body: uniqueGuests only drops an address when guest === attendee.email against the pre-read attendee list. A@x.com versus a@x.com, the same address twice in one payload, and the organizer's own email are all inserted. Nothing in this path enforces uniqueness, and the check-then-act is not transactional, so two concurrent calls with the same new address both pass the filter and both create rows. Emails are stored with the original casing, so later exact-match checks keep missing them. When every address is filtered, the error is emails_must_be_unique_valid, which is wrong for "already on the booking".

title: Notification uses the raw guest list, so existing attendees get a new booking email
body: sendAddGuestsEmails is called with guests, the original input, not uniqueGuests. In email-manager.ts, any attendee whose email is in that list gets AttendeeScheduledEmail (a fresh confirmation plus an ICS REQUEST) instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. The dialog never receives the current attendee list, so submitting one already-invited address plus one new address is a normal case: the existing person is not inserted again, but they are still in guests, so they receive a second "you're scheduled" mail and a new calendar REQUEST, which can duplicate the event or reset RSVP. Only the filtered list should be treated as new guests.

title: Seated bookings get bare Attendee rows with no seat check
body: For event types with seatsPerTimeSlot, occupancy is tracked with BookingSeat rows tied to attendees. This update only createManys Attendee records. It never creates BookingSeat rows and never compares the result to seatsPerTimeSlot (that value is only copied onto the calendar payload at line 145). Seat counts and the attendee list diverge: availability that counts seats will ignore these people, while the bookings UI and the add-guest emails include them. seatsShowAttendees is not enforced before the full attendee list is emailed. Paid seated events can also gain people who never took or paid for a seat.

title: Add-guest emails ignore disableStandardEmails
body: sendAddGuestsEmails always emails the organizer, every team member, and every attendee. sendLocationChangeEmails just above, and the other senders in this file, return early when eventTypeDisableHostEmail or eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail is set (metadata.disableStandardEmails). The new function does not take event type metadata, and the handler loads the full eventType but does not pass it. Event types that turned standard emails off (workflows only, or privacy) still send booking details and ICS invites when a guest is added.

title: Add guests is shown for past bookings
body: The new additional_guests action is pushed into editBookingActions, which is nested in bookedActions. bookedActions is not only rendered for upcoming confirmed bookings; it is also rendered for past confirmed bookings (line 554) and past pending bookings (line 553). Those rows can open AddGuestsDialog and call addGuests. Combined with the handler not rejecting ended bookings, that sends confirmation mail and calendar updates for a meeting that already happened. The action should be limited to upcoming accepted bookings.

title: No tests for the new addGuests mutation
body: The PR adds an authenticated mutation that writes attendees, updates calendars, and sends mail, and it adds no tests. There is no coverage for the admin/owner/organizer/attendee/stranger matrix, blacklist and case-insensitive dedup, booking status and disableGuests, seated events, or the branch that chooses AttendeeScheduledEmail versus AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. The admin/owner condition is already wrong; a handler test with an admin who is not the host would have failed the merge.

title: Team admin/owner check requires both roles
body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner. A membership has a single role, so this is either always false (if the helpers check ADMIN and OWNER exclusively) or true only for owners (if isTeamAdmin already treats OWNER as admin). Team admins who are not the booking host and not an attendee are rejected with FORBIDDEN, even though the flag is named and used as an admin-or-owner grant and the bookings UI treats team admins/owners as managers. They cannot add guests to team bookings they otherwise manage. This should be ||, and it should not query team id 0 when eventType.teamId is null.

title: Cancelled, past, and no-guest events still accept new guests
body: After the permission check the handler never reads booking status, endTime, or eventType.disableGuests before inserting attendees and emailing invites. Any logged-in attendee (not only the host) may call this with a numeric booking id. disableGuests is on the included event type and is ignored, so a host who turned guests off can still have arbitrary addresses emailed a CONFIRMED invite that includes the video URL and meeting password from the booking references. The same path runs for CANCELLED, REJECTED, and PENDING bookings, and for meetings that already ended. The new ICS builders hardcode status CONFIRMED. The bookings menu also offers this action for past confirmed rows (BookingListItem bookedActions, rendered around line 554), so this is not only a raw-API issue. Reject anything that is not an upcoming accepted booking, and honor disableGuests.

title: Seated events are not capacity-checked and get no seat rows
body: createMany inserts plain Attendee rows and later copies seatsPerTimeSlot onto the calendar payload, but never compares current attendees plus new guests to seatsPerTimeSlot and never creates the per-attendee seat rows (reference UIDs) seated bookings use. Occupancy, the seats UI, and seat-scoped cancel/reschedule links will not include these people. Depending on whether availability counts attendees or seats, the slot is either overfilled with people who still have the meeting link, or marked full without usable seat records. Paid-per-seat events also skip payment for these extra people. Block this mutation when seatsPerTimeSlot is set, or add real seats through the seat booking path and enforce the cap.

title: Attendee insert is not rolled back if calendar sync fails
body: prisma.booking.update createMany commits the new attendees before eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees, with no transaction and no compensating delete. If the calendar call throws (revoked credential, provider error, or the wrong user's credentials), the mutation fails but the rows remain. A retry then filters those emails out as already attending and throws BAD_REQUEST emails_must_be_unique_valid, so the caller cannot finish calendar sync or notifications. The host sees an error while the booking already lists the guests, and the guests were never emailed because sendAddGuestsEmails runs only after the calendar call. Persist guests only after sync succeeds, or roll the insert back on failure.

title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials, not the host's
body: EventManager is constructed from ctx.user and getUsersCredentials(ctx.user), not from the booking host. The query already loads booking.user.credentials and never uses them. Calendar references on the booking are stored against the host credential. Attendees are explicitly allowed to call this mutation, and the team-owner branch is meant to allow non-hosts; those callers do not have the host credential, so updateCalendarAttendees cannot update the host event. It will throw (leaving the rows committed with no rollback) or skip. Either way the host calendar, and Meet/Zoom guest lists derived from it, do not gain the new guests. Build EventManager from the booking owner (and that user's calendar credentials), including co-host credentials for collective events.

title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive and racy
body: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is lowercased, but the filter uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) without lowercasing or trimming guest, and split(',') does not trim entries. Blocked@example.com bypasses blocked@example.com, and a space after a comma in the env var bypasses that entry. The same === comparison against existing attendees is case-sensitive, the input array is not deduped, and the organizer address is not excluded, so one request can createMany both a@x.com and A@x.com, the same address twice, or the host as their own guest. There is no unique (bookingId, email) constraint and the check-then-insert is not locked, so two concurrent calls can also insert the same guest twice. Duplicate rows break the attendee list and send duplicate invites. When every address is filtered, the error key emails_must_be_unique_valid is also used for blacklist hits, so the client shows 'Emails must be unique and valid' instead of a blocked-email error. If at least one address remains, dropped addresses are silent and the UI still toasts success.

title: Notifications use the raw address list and hide send failures
body: sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the original guests array, not the filtered uniqueGuests that were actually inserted. In email-manager, newGuests.includes(attendee.email) is what chooses AttendeeScheduledEmail (a new ICS REQUEST) versus the guests-added notice. The dialog only receives bookingId, so a user can retype an existing attendee plus a new address; the existing attendee is skipped in the DB but still matches newGuests and gets a fresh booking-confirmation invite, which can duplicate the event on their calendar. evt.team is never set (the query does not even load eventType.team or hosts), so the team-member loop in sendAddGuestsEmails is dead and collective/round-robin co-hosts are not notified. Send failures are caught, logged as a fixed string without the error, and the mutation still returns success, so the UI shows 'Guests added' when nobody was emailed.

title: Add-guest emails ignore event-type email opt-out
body: Every other sender in this file checks eventTypeDisableHostEmail and eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail before sending. sendAddGuestsEmails does not take event-type metadata and always emails the organizer, every existing attendee, and each new guest, including full calendar invites. Event types with standard emails disabled still emit these messages when a guest is added. The handler has booking.eventType loaded and should pass its metadata so the same opt-out applies.

title: One occurrence is updated but the event is marked recurring
body: The handler updates only the given bookingId, but evt.recurringEvent is set from booking.eventType.recurringEvent for every instance of a recurring type. That field is what scheduled emails and calendar updates use to treat a CalendarEvent as a series (RRULE / series update). The recurring tab hides this action, so it is used on a single upcoming occurrence, yet the invite and calendar payload still describe the whole series. A guest is then on every occurrence in Google/Outlook (or holds an RRULE invite) while only one Booking row lists them, so later instances disagree between Cal.com and the external calendar. Either omit recurringEvent and target that occurrence's calendar reference, or add the guest to every future booking in the recurringEventId group and update the series once.

title: New guests are stored with an empty name
body: guestsFullDetails sets name to an empty string for every new guest. New guests are emailed via AttendeeScheduledEmail, which addresses them as `${name} <${email}>`, so the To header is ' <guest@example.com>'. Some mailers reject or blank that address, and calendar attendees are created with an empty display name. OrganizerAddGuestsEmail also interpolates attendees[0].name into the subject with no fallback (organizer-add-guests-email.ts line 28), so a blank first attendee yields 'with ' and no name. Store the email (or its local part) as the name when the guest did not provide one.

title: Guest list has no upper bound
body: guests is an unbounded z.array of emails, and MultiEmail can append fields without a cap. Any authenticated host or attendee can submit thousands of addresses in one call. The handler insert them and fans out a calendar invite per address containing the meeting URL. OrganizerAddGuestsEmail also puts every attendee email in replyTo, so a large list can exceed header limits and fail the send after the rows are already committed. Cap and dedupe the array in the schema before any writes or sends.

title: No tests for add-guests authorization or side effects
body: The new mutation ships with no handler or UI tests. Permission (admin vs owner vs attendee vs stranger), blacklist and case-variant duplicates, cancelled and seated bookings, the single-occurrence recurring case, and calendar or email failure after the insert are all untested, so the authorization, seat, and rollback bugs above would not be caught in CI.

title: Retry cleanup deletes reminders of every method
body: The new deleteMany ORs the old past-due SMS cleanup with retryCount > 1, and that second predicate has no method, scheduled, or scheduledDate filter. WorkflowReminder is shared by EMAIL, SMS, and WHATSAPP. On the next run of this SMS cron, any row with retryCount greater than 1 is deleted, including email and WhatsApp reminders and SMS rows already marked scheduled with a Twilio referenceId. Deleting a scheduled row drops the referenceId used to cancel the queued text, so a later booking cancellation cannot stop the message. The comment above the query still says it only removes past SMS reminders, which is no longer true. Scope the retry branch to unscheduled SMS (method SMS and scheduled false).

title: Two failures of any kind permanently drop the SMS
body: retryCount is incremented both when scheduleSMS returns a falsy value and for every exception in the surrounding try, including template rendering, getBookerBaseUrl, and database lookups, not only Twilio rejections. The next cron then deletes the row once retryCount > 1. Permanent failures (invalid number) and transient ones (Twilio 5xx, rate limit, network, brief DB error) share that budget, with no backoff beyond the cron interval. Two failures close together therefore remove the reminder even if the event is still days away, so a short provider outage can silently drop every SMS reminder in the 7-day window. Only non-retryable errors should exhaust the counter; transient errors need more attempts or a delay before deletion.

title: Missing number or empty body never consumes retries
body: retryCount is only updated when scheduleSMS returns falsy or throws. If sendTo is missing or the message body is empty, the code skips the send and does not increment retryCount or delete the row. Those reminders stay scheduled=false and are loaded, and their templates rebuilt, on every cron run until scheduledDate is in the past. That is the unbounded retry this PR is meant to stop, for a permanent failure that will never succeed. Treat that skip as a failed attempt or delete the row.

title: Retry-count update in catch aborts the rest of the batch
body: The new workflowReminder.update inside the per-reminder catch is not guarded. If it throws — the row was already deleted because the booking was cancelled, or the database errors — the exception escapes the catch, the original scheduling error is never logged, and the for-loop stops. Every later reminder in this invocation is skipped. Previously a single reminder failure was logged and the handler continued. If scheduleSMS had already accepted the message and the follow-up update failed, this path also counts that as a retry failure without saving referenceId, so the queued text can no longer be cancelled. The retry update needs its own try/catch so one row cannot fail the batch.

title: Overlapping crons can delete a reminder Twilio already accepted
body: Failures write retryCount to the in-memory value plus one instead of an atomic increment, and the cleanup delete removes any row with retryCount > 1 even when scheduled is already true. The handler never claims the row before calling Twilio, so overlapping cron runs can interleave: one run fails and stores retryCount 2, while the other run's scheduleSMS succeeds and sets scheduled and referenceId without clearing retryCount. Partial updates do not reset the other field, so the next run deletes that row. The Twilio message stays queued, but the referenceId required to cancel it is gone. Use an atomic increment and only delete unscheduled SMS rows.

title: retryCount cleanup sequentially scans WorkflowReminder
body: Every cron invocation deletes rows with retryCount > 1, but the new predicate is not covered by the existing indexes on (method, scheduled, scheduledDate), bookingUid, workflowStepId, seatReferenceId, or (cancelled, scheduledDate). Postgres must sequentially scan WorkflowReminder on each run, even when almost no rows match. On a bookings-scale table that scan is repeated for the life of the cron. Add an index that matches the cleanup filter (for example method plus retryCount) if this delete stays.

title: No test locks the retry delete scope or threshold
body: The PR adds a destructive delete and a failure counter with no tests. Nothing asserts that an email or WhatsApp reminder with retryCount > 1 is kept, that an already scheduled SMS row is kept, that a missing phone number does not spin until the event date, or that an SMS reminder is removed only after two failures and not on the first. Those are the branches this change gets wrong, and a fixture test of the delete filter and the increment paths would have caught them.

title: retryCount cleanup is not limited to unscheduled SMS
body: The new deleteMany branch matches every WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1 and does not filter on method, scheduled, or cancelled. This table also holds EMAIL and WHATSAPP reminders, and a scheduled SMS stores the Twilio SID in referenceId so a booking cancellation can stop the message. Failure updates write retryCount from the value read at the start of the run and do not require scheduled = false, so an overlapping run of this cron (no lock, one Twilio call per reminder) can set retryCount to 2 on a row another run already marked scheduled and saved a SID. The next invocation then deletes that row only because retryCount > 1, the SID is gone, and a later cancellation cannot cancel the text. The same predicate will also delete any non-SMS row that exceeds one retry. Restrict this branch to method SMS and scheduled false. The comment above the query still says it only deletes past-due SMS, which is no longer what it does.

title: Any two errors permanently drop in-window SMS reminders
body: Every thrown error in the scheduling try, and every falsy scheduleSMS result, increments the same retryCount, and the next cron deletes the row once retryCount > 1. That includes transient failures (Twilio 5xx or rate limits, getBookerBaseUrl, profile lookup), not only permanent ones such as an invalid number. This job loads every unscheduled SMS reminder whose scheduledDate is within 7 days, so two failed ticks during a short outage delete that whole window. Deletion is irreversible and there is no backoff or Twilio error-code check, so those attendees never get the text even after the provider recovers. Count only permanent send failures toward this cap; leave transient errors retryable until the scheduled date.

title: Missing phone or empty body never hits the retry limit
body: retryCount is incremented only inside the branch that actually calls scheduleSMS. If sendTo is missing (SMS_ATTENDEE with a null booking.smsReminderNumber, or SMS_NUMBER with an empty step sendTo) or the rendered body is empty, the handler skips the send and leaves retryCount at 0 and scheduled false, as long as nothing earlier threw. Those rows stay in the unscheduled-within-7-days query and are fully reprocessed, including profile and booker-URL lookups, on every cron run until scheduledDate is past — the unbounded retry this change is meant to stop. Missing numbers are a common permanent failure and never reach Twilio, so they never reach the new delete. Increment retryCount or delete the row when there is nothing to send.

title: Catch-path retry update can abort the cron and orphan a sent SMS
body: The new catch updates retryCount and does not handle that update failing. The try also wraps the update that stores the Twilio SID after scheduleSMS returns a message. If that SID update throws, the catch still treats it as a scheduling failure: it increments retryCount and leaves scheduled false and referenceId empty even though Twilio already accepted the message. Later runs schedule more messages for the same reminder, and once retryCount > 1 the row is deleted, so none of those messages can be cancelled. Separately, if the catch update itself throws (Prisma P2025 when a concurrent run already deleted the row), the error escapes the catch, the for-loop stops, and every later reminder in the batch is skipped. Previously this catch only logged. Guard the retry update, and do not count a failure that happens after Twilio has already returned a message as 'not scheduled'.

title: retryCount is a lost update under overlapping crons
body: Both failure paths set retryCount to the in-memory reminder.retryCount + 1 instead of an atomic increment, and the same pattern is in the catch. This route has no lock and does a Twilio request per reminder, so a second invocation can overlap a slow run. Both read the same count, both call scheduleSMS, and both write the same next value, so the stop-after-two-failures cap is not enforced and the attendee can get duplicate texts. A failure write can also raise retryCount above 1 on a row the other run already marked scheduled, which the new deleteMany then removes along with its SID. Use an atomic increment and a conditional update that only matches scheduled false (and the id).

title: OR retryCount delete cannot use the existing reminder index
body: deleteMany now ORs an unindexed retryCount > 1 predicate with the scheduledDate predicate. WorkflowReminder's index is (method, scheduled, scheduledDate) and was not extended for retryCount in the schema change. An OR against a column with no index typically forces a sequential scan of the whole table on every cron tick, taking row locks for deleted tuples, including email and WhatsApp reminders this job does not own. Split the two cleanups into separate deletes and add an index that matches the retry predicate so this cron does not scan the full reminder table.

title: No tests for retry accounting or the delete predicate
body: This change deletes workflow reminders and adds no tests. Coverage needs to lock the intended contract: scheduleSMS returning null increments retryCount; a thrown error increments it; the row is removed only after retryCount exceeds 1 and only for unscheduled SMS; a successful schedule with a stored referenceId is not deleted; a missing phone or empty body does not remain in the cron until the event time. Without that, the unscoped deleteMany and the silent no-send path will not be caught before they drop reminders in production.

title: retryCount cleanup deletes reminders this job does not own
body: The new deleteMany ORs a bare retryCount > 1 predicate that is not limited to method SMS, scheduled false, or unsent rows. WorkflowReminder is shared by EMAIL, SMS, and WHATSAPP, and the comment above the query still claims it only removes past-dated SMS reminders. Any row whose retryCount exceeds 1 is hard-deleted, including future email/WhatsApp reminders and rows already marked scheduled that still store a Twilio referenceId. Today only this handler writes the column, so non-SMS rows stay at 0 unless another writer sets them, but a concurrent cron can already produce a bad row: both runs load the same unscheduled reminder, one sets scheduled true and referenceId after a successful scheduleSMS, and the other writes retryCount from the stale in-memory value without touching scheduled. The next run then deletes that live provider message, so booking cancellation can no longer look up the SID and stop it. Scope the predicate to unscheduled SMS reminders.

title: Two transient errors permanently wipe pending SMS reminders
body: Every exception in the per-reminder try, and every falsy scheduleSMS result, increments retryCount, and the next cron deletes all rows with retryCount > 1. That includes Twilio timeouts, rate limits, and failures while loading the organizer profile or rendering the template, not only permanent rejections such as an invalid number. There is no backoff, so two consecutive runs during a short provider or DB outage set retryCount to 2 on every unscheduled SMS reminder in the 7-day window. The following run's deleteMany removes all of them. Those reminders are not recreated, the delete is not logged per id, and attendees never get the SMS after the provider recovers. Only permanent send failures should count, or the limit needs backoff before rows are deleted.

title: Unsendable reminders never increment retryCount
body: retryCount is updated only when scheduleSMS returns a falsy value or throws. If there is no destination (SMS_NUMBER sendTo empty, or booking.smsReminderNumber null) or the rendered message is empty, the handler skips the row and leaves retryCount at 0. The earlier continue when workflowStep or booking is missing does the same. Those rows stay scheduled false with a future scheduledDate, so every cron run loads them again until scheduledDate is in the past. That is the unbounded reschedule loop this change is meant to stop, and a booking with no phone number never enters the Twilio path the new counter covers. Treat these terminal cases as failures, or delete them, so they are retired after the same limit.

title: Failed retry bookkeeping aborts the rest of the batch
body: The new catch block awaits workflowReminder.update and does not handle that update failing. Previously the catch only logged, so the loop always continued. If the update throws — the row was already removed by this cleanup in an overlapping run, the reminder disappeared mid-batch, or the DB blipped — the exception escapes the for-loop, the handler 500s, and every later reminder in the batch is left unscheduled. findMany has no orderBy, so which reminders sit behind the failing row is undefined, and a cron retry hits the same hole. The original scheduling error is also never logged when the bookkeeping update throws. Ignore a missing row (or otherwise guard the update) so one bookkeeping failure cannot stop the rest of the batch.

title: retryCount is a lost-update read-modify-write
body: Failures write retryCount to the value read at the start of the iteration plus one, instead of an atomic increment, and nothing claims the row (for example updateMany where id and scheduled false) before calling Twilio. This endpoint has no lock, and each reminder does several awaits, so a slow run overlaps the next cron tick. Both invocations can read the same retryCount, both call scheduleSMS, and both store the same next count. The new cap is then under-counted, so a reminder is attempted more than twice, and both runs can schedule a duplicate SMS. Use an atomic increment and a conditional update so a concurrent run cannot reset the counter or send twice.

title: OR SQL fragments are unsafe to AND with more predicates
body: Team and org authorization SQL is an OR of a team-booking predicate and a personal-booking predicate, joined as `(${left}) OR (${right})` in buildOrgAuthorizationCondition and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition. That groups each side only; it does not parenthesize the whole OR. When eventTypeId and memberUserId are absent, getBaseConditions returns that fragment unchanged. SQL binds AND tighter than OR, so a caller query `WHERE ${conditions} AND "startTime" >= ${from}` is parsed as team-booking-predicate OR (personal-booking-predicate AND startTime >= from). Every team booking for an authorized team is included even when it fails the date range or any other AND predicate the caller adds. The event-type filter has the same shape, `("eventTypeId" = id) OR ("eventParentId" = id)`, with no outer parentheses. Interpolating it as `WHERE ${auth} AND ${eventTypeFilter}` is parsed as (auth AND eventTypeId = id) OR (eventParentId = id), so any booking whose parent event type matches is returned even if authorization fails. getBaseConditions does wrap both sides when a filter is present, but the no-filter return value and the public getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions fragments are not embed-safe. The old Prisma where-objects were grouped by the query engine, so this is a regression of the raw-SQL conversion. Wrap every fragment in an outer pair of parentheses before returning it.

title: Prisma.sql toEqual checks do not match nested fragments
body: The team-scope assertion here, the org-scope assertion around line 332, and the combined-filter assertion around line 429 expect a single flat Prisma.sql template via toEqual. The service builds those conditions with Array.reduce, nesting Prisma.sql fragments, and Prisma.sql does not flatten nested fragments until execution. The actual object has inner Sql values; the expected object has raw ids and arrays in values. Deep equality fails even when the SQL text and parameters match, so these tests fail in CI and do not validate authorization or filter SQL. Compare a flattened statement and parameter list, or execute the SQL.

title: Team and org authorization SQL is never executed
body: The only database query in this file is the user-scope getBaseConditions case, which is userId equality AND teamId IS NULL. Team and org authorization, including teamId/userId = ANY(array) and the isTeamBooking OR groups, are only compared as objects. PostgreSQL array binding for Prisma raw parameters and AND/OR precedence are therefore untested. Execute those fragments with $queryRaw against rows that must be included and rows that must be excluded (another org's team, a non-member personal booking, a team booking versus a personal booking, and an extra AND predicate such as a date range).

title: Ungrouped OR fragments break AND composition and can skip authorization
body: Team and org authorization SQL is an OR of two branches with no surrounding parenthesis group: ("teamId" = … AND "isTeamBooking" = true) OR ("userId" = ANY(…) AND "isTeamBooking" = false), built at the reduce in buildOrgAuthorizationCondition (line 173) and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition (line 204). The event-type filter is the same shape: ("eventTypeId" = $id) OR ("eventParentId" = $id) at line 106, also returned without an outer group when it is the only filter. getBaseConditions wraps each side only when both auth and filters are present (line 73). With no service filters it returns the bare authorization fragment here. That is the common insights path: this service only filters eventTypeId and memberUserId, and findMany (which AND-merged arbitrary caller where-clauses inside Prisma, so grouping was safe) was removed. Callers must add the time window themselves. WHERE ${getBaseConditions()} AND "startTime" >= $from AND "status" = 'accepted' is parsed as (team branch) OR (personal branch AND startTime >= $from AND status = 'accepted') because AND binds tighter than OR. Every team booking for that team is included regardless of date or status, so team/org insights over-count and ignore caller predicates. A second composition, WHERE ${getAuthorizationConditions()} AND ${getFilterConditions()}, is the obvious translation of the old findMany AND and is also wrong: it parses as (auth AND eventTypeId = $id) OR eventParentId = $id, so any booking whose eventParentId matches is returned even when it fails the org/team/user authorization predicate. That leaks rows for child/managed event types outside the caller's scope. Wrap every returned fragment, including the final OR and this no-filter return, in parentheses (Prisma.sql`(${fragment})`) before it is embedded. The new tests expect the unparenthesized text, so they lock the unsafe shape in.

title: Team/org SQL is never executed; toEqual does not match nested Prisma.sql
body: The team-scope assertion here, the org-scope assertion around line 332, and the combined-filter assertion around line 429 compare getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions to a single flat Prisma.sql template via toEqual. Those service methods build the predicate with Array.reduce, so the returned Prisma.Sql values array holds nested Sql fragments; flattening happens only when a query is executed, not in the constructor. vitest deep-equality compares that structure, not rendered SQL, so these three tests fail even when the SQL text matches. NOTHING, user-scope, and single-filter cases are flat templates and can pass, which hides the failure mode. The only query actually sent to the database is the user-scope getBaseConditions case (line 481), which is a pure AND and does not use OR or ANY(array). A passing run therefore does not check team/org authorization, array binding for ANY(${ids}), or the operator-precedence bug when these fragments are AND-ed with a date or status predicate. Execute the team and org fragments with $queryRaw (including an extra AND predicate) and assert both included and excluded rows.

title: Unparenthesized OR fragment breaks caller AND filters
body: In packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts, getBaseConditions returns the authorization fragment as-is when there are no service filters (line 75). Team and org scope build that fragment as `(teamPredicate) OR (userPredicate)` with no parentheses around the whole OR (the reduce at lines 171-174 and 204-207). SQL AND binds tighter than OR, so the intended caller query `WHERE ${await service.getBaseConditions()} AND "startTime" >= ${start} AND "startTime" < ${end}` is parsed as team-bookings OR (personal-bookings AND date window). Every matching team booking is returned regardless of the date filter, and any other AND predicate appended by the caller (status, member, and so on) is skipped on the team-booking branch. That over-returns rows, ignores the insights time window, and can defeat caller-side restrictions. The same shape exists on the event-type filter at line 106 (`eventTypeId = X OR eventParentId = X`) if getFilterConditions is embedded directly. The old Prisma `AND: [...]` where input did not have this trap, and getBaseConditions already parenthesizes when it combines auth and filters (line 73) but not when it returns auth alone. Wrap every returned fragment, including the OR reduce result, in parentheses so external AND/OR composition is safe.

title: ANY() on a JS array is not a Postgres int array
body: In packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts, org and team authorization interpolate JavaScript number arrays into PostgreSQL ANY() at lines 164 (`"teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})`), 168 (`"userId" = ANY(${uniqueUserIds})`), and 201 (`"userId" = ANY(${userIdsFromTeam})`). Prisma `$queryRaw` / `Prisma.sql` does not encode a JS array as a PostgreSQL `int[]`; the array is one untyped parameter, typically sent as text. PostgreSQL then fails the statement with an error such as `operator does not exist: integer = text` or `op ANY/ALL (array) requires array on right side`. User scope only uses scalar binds, and the only test that executes SQL is user-scoped, so this is not caught. Team and org insights, the main authorization paths, will throw instead of returning bookings. Build the list with Prisma.join and an explicit cast, for example `"userId" = ANY(ARRAY[${Prisma.join(userIds)}]::int[])`, and keep the empty-list guard because Prisma.join([]) is invalid SQL.

title: toEqual on nested Prisma.sql fragments will fail
body: In packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts, the team-scope assertion at line 295, the org-scope assertion at line 332, and the combined-filter assertion at line 429 expect `toEqual` against one flat `Prisma.sql` template. The service does not build those fragments as a single template: buildTeamAuthorizationCondition, buildOrgAuthorizationCondition, and buildFilterConditions nest fragments with `Prisma.sql`(${acc}) OR/AND (${condition})``. Prisma stores nested `Sql` objects in `values` and only flattens them when the query runs, so Vitest deep equality fails even when the rendered SQL matches. The PR notes these tests were not executed. User-scope and single-filter assertions can pass only because those paths return one uncomposed template. Compare a flattened statement, or assert on rows from an executed query, instead of `toEqual` on the `Sql` object; otherwise CI fails and the team/org SQL is never actually checked.

title: Empty updateMany throws after cache is written
body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache now ends with SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}). Prisma Client rejects an empty updateMany data object (Argument data must not be empty) with PrismaClientValidationError, so the method throws after CalendarCache rows have already been upserted. unwatchCalendar in this same class awaits that call after it has already stopped Google watches, cleared channel fields, and deleted cache, so unwatch now fails even though the remaining calendars' cache was rewritten. Webhook-driven refresh uses this method too; a non-2xx response makes Google retry, re-query the Calendar API, and hit the same throw on every notification. An empty update would also not bump @updatedAt even if it were accepted, so the comment's intent is not met. This PR's UI reads CalendarCache.updatedAt, not SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, so the call looks unnecessary. Remove it, or if a touch is required pass { updatedAt: new Date() }. The new helper also types data as Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput, which is not the UpdateManyMutationInput updateMany accepts, so the helper can fail typecheck as well.

title: Cache delete never refreshes connected calendars
body: deleteCache.useMutation only toasts and calls the optional onSuccess prop. The disconnect mutation in the same component invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars and viewer.apps.integrations in onSettled; delete does not. SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper owns the connectedCalendars query and passes its optional onChanged through as onSuccess, without refetching that query. After a successful delete the menu still shows the previous cacheUpdatedAt and the Delete cached data action, so the UI contradicts the success toast. Delete also only runs calendarCache.deleteMany and leaves Google watch channels active, so a later webhook can insert a new row before the user reloads. Invalidate connectedCalendars in onSettled the same way disconnect does.

title: Existing cache rows all get the migration timestamp
body: updatedAt is added as NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(), so every existing CalendarCache row is stamped with the migration time instead of the last real cache write. getCacheStatusByCredentialIds returns MAX(updatedAt) and the new menu shows it as Last updated. Right after deploy, every Google credential with any cache row looks freshly synced, including expired rows, because the status query does not filter expiresAt. That makes the status feature wrong for all current data until the next upsert. The header comment is also false: it says a required column without a default cannot be added to a non-empty table, but the SQL does set a default, which can make an operator abort a production migrate. Backfill from a real proxy (expiresAt minus the 30-day CACHING_TIME used when writing the cache) and correct the comment. NOW() is not a constant default, so PostgreSQL must rewrite CalendarCache under AccessExclusiveLock rather than using the instant add-column path, which blocks cache reads and writes for the length of the rewrite.

title: UserWithCalendars requires fields this function never reads
body: UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt and googleChannelId on allSelectedCalendars and userLevelSelectedCalendars, but getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb never reads either field. The function is exported, including the legacy getConnectedDestinationCalendars alias documented for @calcom/platform-libraries, so callers that previously passed selected calendars with only externalId, integration, and eventTypeId no longer typecheck. The only caller updated here is UserRepository.findUnlockedUserForSession, which now selects googleChannelId (the internal Google push-channel id) into the session user on every authenticated load just to satisfy the wider Pick. Drop the new required fields and the session select unless something in this change actually consumes them.

title: Webhook script writes the wrong env file and breaks on Linux
body: ENV_FILE is ../.env relative to the process cwd, not the script directory. bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repo root therefore creates or edits a .env outside the repository and never sets GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL for the app, then prints success. The edit on line 68 uses sed -i '', which is BSD/macOS-only; GNU sed treats '' as the script and fails the substitution. set -e is off, and cleanup always exits 0, so a missing tunnel URL, the Tunnelmole rate limit, and a failed sed all look successful. Resolve the env path from the script directory and use a portable in-place edit.

title: Cache delete authorization has no tests
body: deleteCacheHandler is a new mutation whose only authorization is credential.findFirst({ id: credentialId, userId: user.id }) before calendarCache.deleteMany({ where: { credentialId } }). This PR adds no tests. Dropping or widening that filter would let any logged-in user wipe another user's calendar cache by credential id, and nothing checks that a non-owner is rejected, that only that credential's rows are removed, or that connectedCalendars actually attaches cacheUpdatedAt from getCacheStatusByCredentialIds. Add allow and deny handler tests before shipping the endpoint.

title: dev:cron switched to undeclared tsx via npx
body: dev:cron changed from ts-node cron-tester.ts to npx tsx cron-tester.ts. ts-node is a declared devDependency of @calcom/web; tsx is not. Under Yarn Berry, npx can skip the workspace install, prompt to download an arbitrary latest tsx, or fail non-interactively. This unrelated change regresses yarn dev:cron. Revert it, or add tsx as a dependency and run it through Yarn.

title: Cache timestamp is always formatted en-US
body: The only user-visible cache status value is formatted with new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" }). The component already calls useLocale(), but the timestamp ignores the active locale and the user's 12/24-hour time format, so every non-US user sees a US short date and a 12-hour clock in Last updated. Format with the current i18n locale and the user's time format instead of a hardcoded en-US formatter.

title: Empty updateMany throws after cache is written
body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache finishes by calling SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}). Prisma Client rejects updateMany when data is empty (Argument `data` is missing / at least one field required), and this check happens even on models with @updatedAt, so the call throws every time. The free/busy rows are already upserted before this line, with no transaction, so Google webhook and watch refresh callers see a failure and retry. Each retry hits the Google freebusy API again, rewrites the cache, and throws again, which can burn calendar API quota and mark sync as failed. Passing {} also does not achieve the comment's goal: the settings UI reads CalendarCache.updatedAt (already maintained by the upsert's @updatedAt), not SelectedCalendar.updatedAt. Remove this call, or if a touch is actually required set updatedAt: new Date() explicitly.

title: Deleting cache does not refresh cache status
body: deleteCache.useMutation only toasts and calls the optional onSuccess prop. It never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars, unlike the disconnect mutation in the same component which invalidates that query in onSettled. cacheUpdatedAt comes from that query, and SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper loads it with refetchOnWindowFocus: false. After a successful delete the dropdown still shows the old timestamp and the delete action, so the UI claims cache exists when the rows are gone. onChanged is optional and is not guaranteed to refetch this query, so the mutation itself needs to invalidate connectedCalendars.

title: Cache status treats expired rows as live
body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups every CalendarCache row for the credential and returns max(updatedAt), with no expiresAt >= now() filter. getCachedAvailability in the same repository only serves rows that have not expired, so the settings dropdown can show a last-updated time and a delete action for cache that availability lookups will ignore. The new migration also backfills updatedAt to NOW() for every existing row, including expired ones, so right after deploy those stale rows look freshly updated. Filter to non-expired rows (and treat no matching row as no cache) so the status matches what is actually served.

title: Expected auth failure is thrown as a generic Error
body: When the credential is missing or not owned by ctx.user, deleteCacheHandler throws new Error("Credential not found or access denied"). tRPC maps a plain Error to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, so a normal not-found/forbidden case becomes a 500, gets reported as an exception, and is not a TRPCError the client can distinguish. Use TRPCError with NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN instead.

title: Cache timestamp is always formatted en-US
body: The last-updated label is built with Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" }) even though useLocale() is already in this component and the string is translated. Non-English users see an English date format (and the key is not formatted with their locale), which is wrong for a new user-facing timestamp in an i18n app.

title: Webhook helper writes the wrong env file and is macOS-only
body: ENV_FILE is the CWD-relative path ../.env, and the script never cds to its own directory. Running bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repo root (the usual invocation) updates a .env outside the repo, so GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is never set for the app. The update also uses sed -i '' (line 68), which is BSD/macOS sed; GNU sed on Linux treats '' as a backup suffix and does not apply the substitution. cleanup() always exits 0, so a failed URL extract looks successful to a caller.

title: dev:cron now depends on undeclared npx tsx
body: dev:cron was changed from ts-node (declared in this package's devDependencies) to npx tsx, but tsx is not a dependency of apps/web. Under Yarn Berry, npx does not reliably resolve workspace binaries and may download an unpinned tsx or fail offline, so yarn dev:cron can break. This change is unrelated to calendar cache and should use a declared runner instead of npx.

title: Empty updateMany throws after cache is written
body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache ends by calling SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) to touch SelectedCalendar.updatedAt. Prisma Client rejects updateMany when data is an empty object (validation error: data needs at least one field), and updateMany does not apply @updatedAt anyway, so {} cannot bump the column. unwatchCalendar in this file calls fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache after deleting cache, and Google webhook/cron refresh uses the same method. Those flows now throw after CalendarCache rows have already been upserted, so a successful cache write is reported as a failure and retried. The new UI reads CalendarCache.updatedAt, not SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, so this call does not serve the feature; remove it, or if the touch is required pass { updatedAt: new Date() } using UpdateManyMutationInput (the new repository method is typed as SelectedCalendarUpdateInput, which allows relation ops updateMany cannot apply).

title: Delete cache leaves stale status in the UI
body: deleteCacheMutation's onSuccess only toasts and calls the optional onSuccess prop. Unlike the disconnect mutation in the same component, it never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper loads that query with refetchOnWindowFocus: false and passes onChanged through as an optional prop, so after a successful delete the dropdown still shows the old cacheUpdatedAt and the delete action. Users are told the cache was deleted while the page keeps offering to delete it until a full remount.

title: Cache status treats expired rows as live cache
body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups CalendarCache by credentialId and returns max(updatedAt) with no expiresAt filter. Availability reads (getCachedAvailability) ignore rows whose expiresAt is in the past, but those rows are not deleted. Any leftover expired row still yields a cacheUpdatedAt, and CredentialActionsDropdown treats a truthy cacheUpdatedAt as live cache. Google connections whose cache has expired still show "Last updated" and "Delete cached data" even though that cache is not served.

title: updatedAt backfill marks every existing cache as just written
body: The migration adds CalendarCache.updatedAt NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(). Every existing row, including stale or expired cache, receives the migration transaction time rather than when the cache value was actually written. The new UI displays that column as "Last updated", so after deploy every Google credential that has any CalendarCache row looks freshly synced until the next Prisma upsert. The leading comment is also wrong: it says the column is added without a default and cannot be applied to a non-empty table, but the SQL does add a default. Backfill from a real write time, or leave the column nullable so legacy rows show as unknown instead of a false timestamp.

title: In-memory delegation calendars cannot see or delete cache
body: Cache status is loaded only via connectedCalendars.map(cal => cal.credentialId) and getCacheStatusByCredentialIds. In-memory delegation credentials use negative credential IDs: calendar-cache.repository.ts treats credentialId < 0 as invalid for DB writes and reads those users' cache by userId plus key, not by the synthetic id. The status query therefore returns nothing for those connections, so the dropdown never shows cache. deleteCache.handler.ts (credential lookup where id = credentialId and userId = session user) also cannot find an in-memory delegation credential and throws "Credential not found or access denied". Org users on delegated Google Calendar cannot view or clear the cache this feature is meant to manage.

title: Webhook helper writes the wrong .env and fails on Linux
body: ENV_FILE is the relative path "../.env", resolved from the process cwd rather than the script directory. Running ./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repo root (the usual invocation) creates or edits a .env outside the repository and never sets GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL where the app reads it; it can also modify an unrelated project's env file. The update on line 68 uses sed -i '', which is BSD/macOS syntax; GNU sed on Linux errors and does not update the file. cleanup() then exits 0 even when URL extraction fails, so the failure is easy to miss.

title: No tests for deleteCache ownership check
body: deleteCache is a new mutation that deletes every CalendarCache row for a credential after a single findFirst on id plus userId, and the PR adds no tests. Nothing asserts that another user's credentialId is rejected, that a missing credential deletes zero rows, or that a negative in-memory delegation id is denied. That where clause is the only authorization control; a regression would wipe another user's calendar cache without the suite catching it.

title: Reminder cancellation is never awaited, so the cancelled flag can be dropped
body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are fired inside forEach and never awaited, then the handler awaits unrelated deletes and returns "Booking successfully cancelled." The email fix only persists if WorkflowReminder.cancelled is updated, and SMS cancellation only happens inside that discarded promise. The same un-awaited pattern is in handleNewBooking.ts around line 966, packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx around line 488, and packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx around lines 212, 376, 519, and 574. On serverless the isolate can freeze when the response is sent, so the update never commits and the reminder is still delivered. The try/catch around the reschedule forEach does not help: forEach does not await, and both helpers swallow their own errors. This replaces an awaited prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany. Callers must await every cancellation (Promise.all or for-of) before returning or deleting parent rows.

title: immediateDelete reintroduces the SendGrid 100-cap and drops the retry record
body: When immediateDelete is true the helper POSTs a SendGrid batch cancel and returns without setting cancelled and without deleting the WorkflowReminder. Callers pass true for reschedules (handleNewBooking.ts:968) and for workflow/step deletion (workflows.tsx:214 and workflows.tsx:521). That immediate POST is the usage this PR is trying to stop: cancelled batches stay in SendGrid scheduled_sends until the original send time, and the cap is 100 pending cancellations. Reschedules and workflow deletes fill that cap, later cancels fail, and those emails are still sent. Failures are caught inside the helper, so the caller continues as if cancellation worked. On reschedule the booking is kept, the row is left with cancelled unset, and the cron only cancels cancelled=true rows, so it will not retry. On workflow and step deletion the POST is not awaited and the following delete cascade-removes the reminder (WorkflowStep/Workflow onDelete: Cascade). If the POST has not finished or failed because of the cap, the batch id is gone and the cron cannot retry, so the email is sent. Far-future sends should only set cancelled and keep the row. A workflow or step must not cascade the reminder away until SendGrid cancel has succeeded.

title: All email cancels are deferred, so reminders due before the next cron are still sent
body: For any reminder that already has a referenceId, cancellation only sets cancelled=true and never calls SendGrid, no matter how soon scheduledDate is. The only follow-up is the scheduleEmailReminders cron (PR: every 15 minutes), which cancels batches whose scheduledDate is within the next hour. SendGrid will not cancel a scheduled send less than 10 minutes before sendAt. If the booking is cancelled after the last cron run that is still more than 10 minutes before send time, the next run either happens after scheduledDate — and that job first deletes every EMAIL reminder with scheduledDate <= now, so cancel is never attempted — or SendGrid rejects the late cancel. The reminder is delivered. This is the common case of cancelling shortly before a reminder. Deferral also does not protect the 100-cap for sends already inside the one-hour window, because those cancellations would be pending for under an hour either way. Reminders already inside that window should be cancelled immediately; only later sends should be flagged for the cron.

title: Past-due reminders are deleted before SendGrid cancellation is attempted
