body: The cron starts by deleting every EMAIL WorkflowReminder with scheduledDate <= now, including rows with cancelled=true, and only then loads reminders to cancel (lines 44-51). The row is the only copy of the SendGrid batch id. If an earlier run did not cancel that batch (downtime, a thrown cancel aborting the loop, or the booking being cancelled after the last pre-send run), SendGrid still has the scheduled mail and this delete makes a later cancel impossible. Past-due cleanup must not remove cancelled rows until a SendGrid cancel has been attempted and the outcome recorded. As written, any missed window permanently fails the fix.

title: One SendGrid cancel failure aborts the rest and skips DB cleanup
body: remindersToCancel is handled in a single try/catch. Each POST is awaited in order, and the prisma deletes are only executed after every request succeeds. Any rejection — the 100 pending-cancellation cap, SendGrid refusing a cancel inside its 10-minute cutoff, a null referenceId, or a network error — jumps to the catch, which only logs, then the handler goes on to schedule new mail. Later reminders in that run are not cancelled. Rows whose POST already succeeded are not deleted, so the next run must redo them. A row that fails every time stays in the result set until its scheduledDate passes and the earlier deleteMany removes it, and each run that hits it aborts the rest of the batch, so those other cancelled reminders are sent. The query also does not require method EMAIL or a non-null referenceId, so one bad row is enough to fail the POST. Handle each reminder independently, skip rows without a batch id, and delete a row only after its own cancel succeeds.

title: Paid booking cancellation returns before workflow reminders are cancelled
body: If the booking is paid, this branch refunds, sets status to REJECTED, and returns "Booking successfully cancelled." before the reminder block at line 484. That block is the only place this handler marks email reminders cancelled or deletes SMS reminders. The earlier return null when the payment app is missing (around line 437) skips it too. Paid event types can still have workflows, and bookingToDelete already loads workflowReminders, but they are ignored on this path. A cancelled paid booking therefore keeps its scheduled emails and SMS. If the reminder was not yet handed to SendGrid, the cron's unscheduled query does not check booking status and will schedule and send it; if it was already scheduled, the cron only cancels rows with cancelled=true, which was never set. Reminder cancellation has to run on this path before returning.

title: Every workflow save recreates reminders while old SendGrid batches stay live
body: An existing step is treated as edited when JSON.stringify(oldStep) !== JSON.stringify(newStep). oldStep is a Prisma WorkflowStep and always includes numberVerificationPending; newStep is the zod input and has senderName instead, so the comparison is always true even when nothing changed. The branch used to delete the WorkflowReminder row; that deleteMany was removed. It now only calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder (line 576), which sets cancelled and leaves the SendGrid scheduled send in place, and that call is not awaited. The same request then scheduleEmailReminder's a new batch for every future booking of that step. Every workflow save therefore leaves the previous batches live until the cron's one-hour window and adds another set. Near-term reminders can be delivered twice. All superseded batches become pending cancellations in the same hour, which can exceed SendGrid's 100-cap and cause the cron cancel loop to fail. Compare the actual editable fields, and do not create the replacement send until the previous batch is flagged or cancelled.

title: No tests for deferred cancel or the cron SendGrid cancellation loop
body: The PR replaces SendGrid cancellation and adds a cron path, but no test covers deleteScheduledEmailReminder, the cancelled flag, reschedule/workflow-delete behavior, or the scheduleEmailReminders cancellation loop. The previous fix used the wrong SendGrid endpoint and failed in production once 100 pending cancellations accumulated. Without a test that a far-future cancel only sets cancelled, that an imminent cancel actually stops the batch, and that one failed POST does not skip the remaining rows, the same production failure can regress unnoticed.

title: immediateDelete still hits SendGrid and never records cancellation
body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder's immediateDelete branch POSTs /v3/user/scheduled_sends with status cancel and then returns without setting WorkflowReminder.cancelled and without deleting the row. Reschedule in handleNewBooking.ts (the call that passes true), workflow deletion in workflows.tsx, and workflow-step deletion in workflows.tsx all use that branch. That reintroduces the failure this PR describes: each cancel stays in SendGrid's scheduled_sends list until the original send time, and once the pending-cancellation cap (stated as 100) is reached further cancels fail and the email is still sent. Failures are only logged inside the helper, and cancelled is never set, so the new cron cannot retry. Workflow and step deletion then cascade-delete the WorkflowReminder, which also removes any chance of a later retry; a bulk delete of more than 100 already-scheduled reminders therefore silently leaves the overflow emails queued. On reschedule the old booking is not deleted, so the row stays scheduled=true and cancelled=null: if the SendGrid call failed the old reminder is still delivered, and if it succeeded the stale row is only removed when scheduledDate passes.

title: Cron deletes due reminders before withdrawing them from SendGrid
body: scheduleEmailReminders begins by deleteMany-ing every EMAIL WorkflowReminder whose scheduledDate is at or before now, and only afterward loads cancelled=true rows to POST a SendGrid cancel. Any cancelled reminder whose send time has already arrived is removed from the database and never cancelled at SendGrid, so the email is still delivered. With the job running every 15 minutes, a cancellation made after the last tick before scheduledDate (or any run that starts at or after the send time, including a delayed cron) always hits this path. The new cancel query cannot see those rows because they are already gone. SendGrid withdrawal for cancelled=true reminders has to run before this cleanup, and the cleanup must not delete cancelled rows that have not yet been cancelled at SendGrid.

title: One SendGrid cancel error aborts the batch and drops successful deletes
body: The new cancel loop awaits every SendGrid POST inside a single try/catch, and only after the whole loop does it await the queued workflowReminder.delete calls. Prisma queries are lazy, so those deletes have not run yet. If any request throws (unknown or already-cancelled batch id, the pending-cancellation cap, a network error), the catch only logs and then the handler goes on to schedule other mail. None of the reminders already cancelled at SendGrid are deleted, and every reminder after the failure is skipped. Those rows stay cancelled=true and are retried on the next run. There is no orderBy and no per-item isolation, so one permanently failing row can be selected first every 15 minutes and block every other cancellation until scheduledDate passes. At that point the opening deleteMany removes the rows without a SendGrid cancel and the emails send. Each reminder needs its own error handling, and a successful cancel must be persisted immediately so it is not retried and cannot poison the queue.

title: Reminder cancellation is fire-and-forget after awaited deletes were removed
body: Cancel, reschedule, and workflow-update callers used to collect prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany promises and await them before returning. That awaited delete is gone. They now call async deleteScheduledEmailReminder / deleteScheduledSMSReminder inside forEach and never await the promises: handleCancelBooking.ts around the new reminder loop, handleNewBooking.ts reschedule (the try/catch there cannot observe async failures), bookings.tsx requestReschedule, and the workflow update/delete paths in workflows.tsx. For an already-scheduled email, the cancelled=true update inside that floating call is the only signal the cron uses to withdraw the SendGrid batch. For an unscheduled email or SMS (no referenceId), the helper's row delete is the only thing stopping the reminder cron from sending it; scheduleEmailReminders schedules every scheduled=false email inside 72 hours and does not check booking status. On a serverless invocation those promises can be frozen when the handler returns, so the booking is cancelled but the reminder is still sent. The calls have to be awaited, and failures surfaced, before the handler finishes.

title: Paid cancellations return before workflow reminders are cancelled
body: In handleCancelBooking a paid booking is refunded and then returns 'Booking successfully cancelled' before the new reminder-cancellation loop. The booking status is already CANCELLED or REJECTED, but its WorkflowReminder rows are left untouched. Before/after-event workflow emails and SMS for paid bookings are therefore neither marked cancelled, deleted, nor withdrawn from SendGrid/Twilio, which is the same production failure this PR is fixing. The cancellation loop has to run on this path as well, and be awaited, before the early return.

title: No regression test for deferred cancellation of scheduled reminders
body: The description says the previous SendGrid cancel fix did not work in production, but this change adds no test for the replacement contract. Nothing asserts that booking cancel sets WorkflowReminder.cancelled instead of POSTing scheduled_sends immediately, that reschedule does not use the immediate SendGrid cancel, that the cron withdraws cancelled batches before deleting past-due rows, or that one failed cancel is retried without dropping the rest of the batch. Those are the paths that still send reminders for cancelled and rescheduled bookings, and they will regress silently without a test.

title: immediateDelete refills the 100-slot SendGrid cancel cap and fails open
body: When immediateDelete is true and a referenceId exists, deleteScheduledEmailReminder only POSTs /v3/user/scheduled_sends with status cancel and then returns. It does not delete the WorkflowReminder and does not set cancelled=true. SendGrid keeps that cancellation in scheduled_sends until the original sendAt (up to 72 hours), and this PR exists because that queue is capped at 100 pending cancellations account-wide; once it is full, further cancels fail and emails still go out. The hot callers pass true for every already-scheduled reminder regardless of how far away the send is: reschedule in handleNewBooking.ts (line 968), workflow deletion in workflows.tsx (line 214), and step deletion in workflows.tsx (line 521). A single workflow delete can therefore enqueue one long-lived cancel per upcoming reminder and trip the cap for the whole platform. If the POST fails, the catch only logs, cancelled is never set, and the cron will not retry, so the email is still delivered. On success the row is left looking active, so nothing records that the batch was already cancelled.

title: Cron cancel can miss, drop, or poison reminder cancellations
body: The new cancel pass does not reliably stop SendGrid sends for cancelled bookings. Before it runs, the handler deleteMany's every EMAIL WorkflowReminder with scheduledDate <= now, including cancelled=true rows whose SendGrid send has not been cancelled yet. A cron invocation that starts at or after sendAt therefore destroys the only record that could still cancel the batch, and the email goes out. The new query only selects cancelled rows due within the next hour, and this job runs every 15 minutes, while SendGrid will not honor a cancel inside roughly the last 10 minutes before sendAt. A booking cancelled after the last successful tick (for example 10 minutes before the reminder) is not stopped, and the following run deletes the row instead of cancelling it. The loop at line 56 has no per-item try/catch and only awaits the Prisma deletes in Promise.all after every SendGrid call succeeds. Prisma deletes are lazy until awaited, so one failure (null referenceId, non-email referenceId, already-cancelled batch, or a reminder inside the 10-minute cutoff) skips those deletes. Batches that were already cancelled stay cancelled=true; the next run retries them, SendGrid returns 400 on a second cancel, and that throw aborts the rest of the batch until the poisoned row ages out and the leading deleteMany removes it. findMany has no orderBy, so one too-late reminder can be first and block reminders that are still cancellable. The unscheduled-send query below still does not exclude cancelled=true or CANCELLED/REJECTED bookings, so any reminder row that cancellation failed to delete is scheduled and sent anyway.

title: Cancel no longer awaits reminder cancellation
body: handleCancelBooking used to collect workflowReminder.deleteMany promises and await them with the other Prisma work. It now calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder inside forEach and never awaits or collects those promises. The email helper only sets cancelled=true, which is the only signal the cron uses to stop SendGrid; the SMS helper cancels Twilio and deletes the row, and there is no SMS cron to finish that job. On serverless the runtime can freeze as soon as the handler returns, so those writes often never commit, the cron never sees the email as cancelled, and both email and SMS for the cancelled booking are still sent. Even when the write does commit, email cancellation is deferred to a 15-minute cron that only acts in the last hour, so a reminder due before the next tick is not stopped. Errors inside the managers are swallowed, and the handler still returns success.

title: Paid cancellation returns before reminders are cancelled
body: If the booking is paid, handleCancelBooking refunds it, sets status to REJECTED, and returns at line 464. Workflow reminder cancellation is only reached at line 485, after that return. Paid cancellations therefore never set cancelled=true and never call Twilio or SendGrid. Already scheduled workflow emails and SMS for refunded bookings are still sent. The new cron cannot recover them, because it only cancels rows with cancelled=true, and this path never writes that flag. The booking is also REJECTED rather than CANCELLED, so a later status check for CANCELLED would miss it too.

title: Reschedule cancel is not awaited and immediately consumes SendGrid cancel slots
body: On reschedule, handleNewBooking walks the original booking's workflowReminders with forEach and calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder(id, referenceId, true) without awaiting. forEach does not return those promises, so the try/catch around it never sees async failures, and the handler can finish the response while the SendGrid calls are still in flight. Passing true takes immediateDelete, which POSTs a cancel for every reminder that already has a referenceId, including sends up to 72 hours away, and puts those entries back into SendGrid's 100-slot scheduled_sends queue — the cap this PR is trying to stay under. If that POST fails, the helper swallows the error and does not set cancelled, so the cron will not retry and the old booking's workflow email is still sent after the reschedule. Direct attendee reschedules only cancel reminders on this path.

title: Request-reschedule dropped the awaited reminder delete
body: requestReschedule marks the booking CANCELLED and then calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder from forEach without awaiting them. The previous code awaited prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany after starting the provider cancels. The email helper only persists cancelled=true inside that unawaited call, which is what the cron needs in order to stop SendGrid; the SMS helper cancels Twilio and deletes the row in the same unawaited call, and SMS has no cron fallback. If the mutation returns before those promises settle, reminders for the booking the user just asked to reschedule are still delivered, and the API has already reported success.

title: Workflow and step saves can lose the cancellation record
body: Workflow deletion calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., true) and deleteScheduledSMSReminder inside forEach, then immediately awaits workflow.deleteMany. Step removal does the same at line 521 and then deletes the WorkflowStep. Both deletes cascade to WorkflowReminder. The provider calls are not awaited, so the rows can disappear before SendGrid or Twilio cancel finishes. immediateDelete also does not set cancelled=true, and a failed or frozen provider call then has no row left for the cron to retry, so those messages are still sent. Because every scheduled reminder for the workflow is cancelled immediately, one delete can also fill SendGrid's 100 pending-cancellation slots until the original send times. The same mutation dropped awaited reminder deletes when an event type is removed (line 376) and when a step is edited (line 574): those used to await workflowReminder.deleteMany and now only start unawaited manager calls. If those calls do not finish, the old reminders stay scheduled while the mutation also creates new ones, so both the old and the new messages go out.

title: No tests for the new reminder-cancellation behavior
body: This change replaces the SendGrid cancel-then-DELETE sequence and the awaited reminder deletes with a cancelled flag, a deferred cron cancel, and an immediateDelete mode, but adds no tests. Nothing covers the cron selecting cancelled rows and POSTing scheduled_sends, skipping DELETE /v3/user/scheduled_sends/{id} (which clears the cancel and lets the email send), a cancel inside the 15-minute cron gap or SendGrid's 10-minute cutoff, the 100-slot immediateDelete path, or cancel, reschedule, workflow delete, and paid-booking cancel actually stopping both email and SMS. Those are the production paths this PR is supposed to fix.

title: Reschedule cleanup uses forEach(async) and never finishes
body: In packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts the calendar/video cleanup at line 125 was switched to bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) so it can await the now-async getCalendar. Array.forEach does not wait for async callbacks and drops their return values, so the try/catch around it never sees failures, and Reschedule still sends the reschedule email and returns true while deletion is in flight. This is a regression from the async app-store change: previously getCalendar was synchronous, so deleteEvent was at least invoked before the callback yielded, and deleteMeeting started the provider call before returning. Now the calendar path awaits getCalendar before deleteEvent, and deleteMeeting (videoClient.ts) awaits getVideoAdapters before calling the provider, and nothing awaits either promise. The old event can remain on the external calendar and the video meeting can stay up; on serverless the runtime often freezes that work after the handler returns, so the cleanup never runs. Replace forEach with for...of or Promise.all and await both getCalendar/deleteEvent and deleteMeeting inside the try.

title: Wipe-my-cal reschedule never awaits event deletion
body: In packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts the cleanup that is supposed to remove the previous calendar event and video meeting (line 125) uses forEach with an async callback and awaits getCalendar inside it. forEach ignores that promise, so the try/catch does not handle rejections, and the function sends the reschedule email and returns true without waiting. Making getCalendar and deleteMeeting async makes this worse than the old fire-and-forget: both now yield before the provider call (getCalendar before deleteEvent, and deleteMeeting before videoAdapter.deleteMeeting), and those promises are discarded. Wipe My Cal's reschedule path can therefore leave the previous event on the external calendar, so the slot stays busy and the app fails at the thing it exists to do. Use for...of or Promise.all and await getCalendar, deleteEvent, and deleteMeeting before returning.

title: Request-reschedule does not wait for calendar or video deletion
body: In the requestReschedule mutation in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx, the booking is already written as CANCELLED (around line 475) and then bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) at line 553 awaits getCalendar and returns calendar.deleteEvent / deleteMeeting. forEach does not await those callbacks, and this mutation has no try/catch around them, so a failure becomes an unhandled rejection rather than a failed mutation. The handler then awaits sendRequestRescheduleEmail and the BOOKING_CANCELLED webhooks and resolves successfully while external cleanup may not have started. getCalendar and deleteMeeting are now async and both yield before the provider request, so discarding the callback promise means the Google/Outlook event and the video meeting are often never deleted (especially once a serverless response is sent and pending work is frozen). Attendees are told to reschedule and the slot can be double-booked or left blocked on the calendar. Collect the work with Promise.all or for...of and await deleteEvent and deleteMeeting before sending email or webhooks.

title: Cancelling remaining recurring bookings drops calendar deletes
body: In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts, when all remaining instances of a recurring booking are cancelled, external calendar deletion is done with credentials.forEach(async ...) at line 460, and this PR added await getCalendar as the first line of that callback. forEach does not wait for the async callback, and apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent) runs only after await calendar.deleteEvent, so the later await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) (line 652) does not include these deletes and cannot observe their errors. Because getCalendar is now async, the callback yields before deleteEvent is even called; previously getCalendar was sync so the provider delete was at least started. The handler still marks the bookings CANCELLED and returns "Booking successfully cancelled." The non-recurring branch just below (line 480) was correctly rewritten to for...of and pushes the delete promise onto apiDeletes; the recurring branch needs the same treatment (push calendar.deleteEvent(...) without awaiting it inside an abandoned forEach, or await a Promise.all of those calls) or cancelling a series leaves every occurrence on the external calendar.

title: Top-level import() preloads every app and can crash on a failed one
body: packages/app-store/index.ts builds appStore with bare import() calls (applecalendar: import("./applecalendar"), and the same for every other integration starting at line 3). Those expressions run as soon as the module is evaluated, not when a key is used, so the first import of appStore — which booking, calendar, video, and payment code all do — starts loading every integration package even if the request needs only one. Cold start and memory do not improve versus the old static imports, and every app module's top-level side effects still run on unrelated requests. A rejected import is also unhandled unless that specific key is later awaited. On Node 15+ the default is to terminate the process on an unhandled rejection, so one broken unused app can crash the server during an unrelated booking. Store thunks (() => import("./applecalendar")) and call them at the existing await sites so only the requested app loads and the caller can catch a failure.

title: Vital reschedule drops calendar and video cleanup
body: Reschedule now awaits the async getCalendar inside bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...). Array.forEach never waits for async callbacks and discards their return values, so the try/catch around the loop cannot see failures. getCalendar suspends on a dynamic app import before calendar.deleteEvent is called, and the video branch only returns deleteMeeting, which itself now awaits getVideoAdapters before calling the provider. Nothing awaits those floating promises. The function then sends the reschedule email and returns true. Previously getCalendar was synchronous, so deleteEvent was at least issued before the function continued. After this change a serverless worker can finish the request and freeze before the import resumes, so the cancelled booking's calendar event and video meeting are never removed (the slot stays busy and attendees still see the old event). Rejections become unhandled promise rejections. Await the references with for...of or Promise.all, including both deleteEvent and deleteMeeting, before sending email.

title: WipeMyCal reschedule drops calendar and video cleanup
body: The WipeMyCal reschedule handler awaits getCalendar inside bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...). forEach does not await async callbacks and ignores what they return, so the surrounding try/catch never handles rejections. Because app modules are now dynamic imports, getCalendar yields before calendar.deleteEvent runs, and the video branch returns deleteMeeting without awaiting it even though deleteMeeting now waits on getVideoAdapters before deleting the meeting. The handler proceeds to send the reschedule email and returns true while that work is still suspended. Before this change getCalendar was sync, so the calendar delete was started before the function moved on. On serverless the process can exit when the handler returns, leaving the old calendar event and video room in place after the booking is marked cancelled. Use for...of or Promise.all and await both provider deletes before sending email.

title: requestReschedule does not wait for provider cancellation
body: requestReschedule awaits getCalendar inside bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...). forEach does not join those promises, so the mutation continues, sends the reschedule email and BOOKING_CANCELLED webhooks, and resolves while calendar deletion is still suspended on the app-store dynamic import. The video branch only returns deleteMeeting from that callback; deleteMeeting now awaits getVideoAdapters before it calls the provider, so that cleanup is deferred the same way and is also not awaited. The booking row is already set to CANCELLED before this loop. If the worker stops when the tRPC mutation returns, which is typical on serverless, the provider calls never run and the old calendar event and video room remain. There is no try/catch around the loop, so a rejection is unhandled rather than a failed mutation. Await the references with for...of or Promise.all, including deleteEvent and deleteMeeting, before email or webhooks.

title: Recurring cancel never joins calendar deletions
body: Cancelling all remaining instances of a recurring booking deletes external calendar events with credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(await calendar.deleteEvent(...)) }). forEach does not return those promises, and the push onto apiDeletes happens only after deleteEvent has already resolved, so the later await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) neither starts nor waits for this work. This change made getCalendar async (it now awaits a dynamic import) while leaving this loop in place; the non-recurring branch just below was correctly rewritten as a for...of that awaits getCalendar and pushes the in-flight deleteEvent promise. Previously getCalendar was synchronous, so deleteEvent was invoked before the callback's first await and the provider request was at least started. Now the callback suspends before deleteEvent is issued. The handler can mark the series CANCELLED, send the cancellation email, and return while those events are still on the external calendar; on serverless the continuations are often dropped. Failures are unhandled rejections. Replace the forEach with a for...of or Promise.all and include each deleteEvent promise in apiDeletes before awaiting them.

title: Reschedule cleanup is not awaited after getCalendar became async
body: After the booking is already updated to CANCELLED, calendar and video cleanup runs in bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...). forEach discards the promise returned by an async callback, so the await getCalendar and the subsequent calendar.deleteEvent / deleteMeeting are not part of Reschedule's completion. The try/catch around the forEach only catches synchronous throws, not rejections from those awaits, which become unhandled rejections. The function then sends the reschedule email and returns true. On a serverless runtime the invocation can finish or freeze before the external calls finish, and because the row is already cancelled this path will not retry. The original calendar event and video meeting can remain, so the slot stays busy and a live meeting is left for a cancelled booking. Await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...)) or use a for...of loop so both deletes are joined to the handler and failures are caught.

title: WipeMyCal reschedule uses forEach(async) and drops cleanup
body: WipeMyCal reschedule marks the booking CANCELLED, then starts cleanup with bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) / deleteMeeting(...) }). Array.forEach does not await async callbacks, and the surrounding try/catch cannot see their rejections. The handler continues to sendRequestRescheduleEmail and returns true while Google/Outlook deletion and video deletion are still in flight (or not started, if the runtime suspends first). Failures are unhandled rejections rather than logged errors. A cancelled booking can leave the external event and meeting in place, blocking the time slot. Replace forEach with an awaited Promise.all(map(async ...)) or a for...of loop.

title: requestReschedule does not wait for calendar or video deletion
body: requestReschedule sets the booking to CANCELLED, then calls bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) to await getCalendar and deleteEvent, or to call the now-async deleteMeeting. forEach ignores the callback promise, and nothing after the loop awaits those operations before sendRequestRescheduleEmail and the BOOKING_CANCELLED webhooks. There is no try/catch on this loop, so a rejected dynamic import or a failed deleteEvent/deleteMeeting is an unhandled rejection. The mutation still completes successfully. Because the booking is already CANCELLED, the UI will not offer this cancel/reschedule again, and the external calendar event or video meeting can be left behind (double-booking the slot, live meeting for a cancelled booking). Collect the promises with map and await Promise.all before sending email and webhooks.

title: Recurring cancel never joins per-calendar deletes to apiDeletes
body: When cancelling all remaining occurrences, calendar deletion is bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... const deletedEvent = await calendar?.deleteEvent(...); apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); }). forEach does not return those promises. The push happens only after deleteEvent has already settled, and it pushes the resolved value rather than the in-flight promise. The later await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) therefore does not wait for this work and cannot observe its failures. The handler still returns "Booking successfully cancelled." The non-recurring branch in the same function was converted to a for...of that pushes calendar.deleteEvent's promise before awaiting; this recurring branch was only given an inner await and still races the request lifetime. Recurring events can remain on connected calendars. Build an array of delete promises (per credential and per updated booking) and await them with the rest of apiDeletes.

title: Eager import() promises load every app and can reject unhandled
body: appStore calls import() for every integration while the module is evaluating, instead of exposing lazy thunks such as () => import("./applecalendar"). The first import of @calcom/app-store therefore starts loading every calendar, video, CRM, and payment package even when the caller only needs one (for example deletePayment or a single getCalendar). That keeps the cold-start and memory cost of the old static barrel and adds a burst of parallel module loads. Each import() promise is also stored with no .catch(). If any app module rejects and that key is not awaited, the rejection is unhandled; Node's default unhandledRejection behavior throws and can exit the process, including for an app the current request never uses. A failed optional app should not be able to crash the server. Lazy-load on first access and attach rejection handling so an unused or broken app degrades instead of rejecting in the background.

title: Failed app import throws out of booking and availability flows
body: getCalendar awaits appStore[calendarType] with no try/catch. A rejected dynamic import now throws, whereas a missing implementation previously returned null. CalendarManager.createEvent and updateEvent only catch errors from calendar.createEvent/updateEvent, not from getCalendar, so one broken app chunk fails the whole EventManager create/update instead of returning success: false for that credential. deleteEvent has the same gap. getCachedResults does Promise.all on every getCalendar call, so one rejected import fails busy-time lookup for every connected calendar. That can 500 availability, or, if an upstream caller treats the failure as no busy data, hide conflicts and allow double booking. Catch import failures in getCalendar and return null, which callers already handle as "calendar not implemented".

title: getCalendar promises are started and sometimes discarded
body: getCalendar is now async, but getCalendarCredentials still calls it synchronously inside flatMap, before the app.variant === "calendar" check. When the variant is not calendar (types ending in _calendar still enter this filter, including *_other_calendar apps), the returned promise is dropped. If that promise rejects — getCalendar awaits a dynamic import that can reject — nothing handles it, which is an unhandledRejection introduced by this change. When the promise is kept, the exported calendar field silently changed from a Calendar instance to Promise<Calendar | null> while getCalendarCredentials stayed synchronous. getConnectedCalendars was updated to await item.calendar, but any other caller that still invokes calendar.listCalendars() without awaiting will throw at runtime. Only call getCalendar when the result is retained, and attach a catch (or await it) on every promise that is started.

title: Override days skip busy checks and can be double-booked
body: In checkIfIsAvailable, if any date override falls on the slot's day and the slot is treated as inside that override, the function returns true immediately. That return is before the busy-interval loop, so Google Calendar conflicts and existing Cal.com bookings are never consulted. isFixed is true for every user when schedulingType is null and for every collective host, and the same helper is used for fixed and round-robin hosts, so this is not limited to the round-robin case. On any day that has a date override, the public schedule can offer times when that host is already busy, which is what the booking page presents.

title: Multiple override windows on one day remove all slots
body: The new override scan uses dateOverrides.find and treats a truthy callback as "this slot is unavailable". The callback returns true when the slot is entirely before or entirely after that one window, and find stops at the first such window. A normal split override (for example 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00 on the same date) therefore rejects every slot, because every slot lies outside at least one window, and the day shows no availability. The predicate is also too weak in the other direction: it only excludes slots that end at or before the window start or start after the window end, so a slot that starts before the window and ends inside it is treated as bookable. Availability should require the whole slot to sit inside at least one same-day window.

title: Working-hours recheck zeroes split schedules
body: The new working-hours fallback uses the same inverted find, and it runs for every fixed host whenever an override did not already return — including ordinary single-host events, because those users are marked isFixed. workingHours.find rejects the slot if any entry for that UTC weekday does not contain the slot start. Two intervals on the same day (a lunch break is the common case) therefore eliminate every slot, including times that fall inside one of the intervals, so those hosts get an empty booking page. Separately, end is computed from slotStartTime rather than slotEndTime, so a slot that starts inside the range but runs past workingHour.endTime is accepted. That shows up in round-robin, where aggregated hours can emit a slot another host can take after this host's hours have ended. A weekday present in no workingHours entry is not rejected either, so this check cannot enforce a fixed host's day off.

title: Blocked-day overrides are never recognized
body: A fully blocked date is stored as an override whose start and end are the same instant, and this function tries to treat that as unavailable for the whole day. The check is dayjs(...) === dayjs(...). Those are two different objects, so reference equality is never true, even when both instants match. The later before/after checks then only exclude slots that do not overlap that single point, leaving a bookable hole around the shifted timestamp. For a UTC−5 host blocked at 00:00, the instant is shifted to 05:00Z, and a slot that overlaps 05:00Z is reported available on a day the host marked unavailable. Compare with isSame (or the underlying timestamps) and, on a match, reject the whole day.

title: Override date match depends on the server timezone
body: Whether an override applies is decided by comparing dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD") to slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD"). slotStartTime is time.utc(), so its format is UTC. The left side is built with dayjs(date.start) in local mode, so format uses the Node process timezone. If that timezone is not UTC, an override whose shifted instant falls on a different local calendar date than its UTC date does not match the slot. US evening overrides, which land in the 00:00–04:00Z window, are the typical case: dateOverrideExist stays false and the override is silently ignored, so the fixed host is treated as on their normal hours. Both sides need to be formatted in UTC, or the day bounds compared as absolute instants.

title: Override timezone conversion drops the day and double-applies DST
body: Date overrides are stored as the organizer's wall-clock time encoded in a UTC timestamp (a 14:00 IST override is 14:00Z, which the existing tests rely on). The new code adds inviteeOffset − organizerOffset minutes and then keeps only .hour() and .minute(), so a result on the previous or next calendar day cannot be represented. A 20:00–23:00 organizer-UTC override viewed from UTC+3 becomes 23:00 and 02:00; end-minute 120 is less than start-minute 1380, buildSlots drops any range whose start is not before its end, and the host's normal hours for that day were already removed, so the attendee sees no slots instead of 23:00–02:00. A Tokyo 08:00 override is placed at 19:00 on the New York day that contains the raw 08:00Z value, which is the next New York date, not 19:00 the previous evening (the real instant, 08:00 JST). Those minutes are then passed through buildSlots's organizerDSTDiff − inviteeDSTDiff correction, which exists for values computed from today's offset; these minutes already used the offset at the override instant, so when the two zones are not in the same DST period versus today every override slot shifts by an extra hour. Offsets are read via dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone): Date#toString is implementation-defined, a failed parse yields NaN and the range is dropped, and a missing timeZone (optional on TimeRange) throws from .tz() and fails the whole schedule request. checkIfIsAvailable converts the same overrides a different way (subtract the organizer offset and compare absolute instants), so the two layers disagree and a cross-midnight override can be emitted by one and rejected by the other, blanking the day.

title: Fixed-host override behavior is untested
body: The only new assertion re-queries the same personal event — one host, one override window, no calendar busy time — in Asia/Dhaka and expects the same UTC instants as Asia/Kolkata. That does not cover fixed-host round-robin, which is the bug the PR says it fixes, nor two windows on one date, a blocked day (start equal to end), a busy conflict on an override day, a timezone gap that crosses midnight, or a DST boundary. createBookingScenario never attaches hosts to the mocked event type, and the host fixture is not the { isFixed, user } shape getSchedule reads, so the new fixed-host branch of checkIfIsAvailable cannot be exercised without harness changes. The new paths can drop all slots or ignore busy times while this test stays green.

title: Slots inside a date override skip busy checks and can double-book
body: checkIfIsAvailable now returns true as soon as a slot falls on a day with a date override and is treated as inside that override, before the busy-interval scan. That scan is the only place calendar conflicts and existing Cal bookings are applied to generated slots, and this function now runs for every fixed host — including ordinary personal and collective events, whose users are marked isFixed. On any day that has a date override, a slot inside the override is therefore shown as free even when the host is already booked, so the same time can be booked twice.

title: Working-hours gate frees non-working days and drops split shifts
body: The new working-hours check uses find() to look for a same-day window that does not contain the slot, and treats "no such window" as available. If a fixed host has no entry for that weekday, every callback is falsy, find returns undefined, and the slot is kept. That is the round-robin case this PR is meant to close: union slots from a rotating host stay bookable on days the fixed host does not work. The same predicate rejects valid slots when a host has two windows on one day (for example 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00): the window that does not contain the slot makes find succeed and the slot is removed, so lunch-break schedules disappear from the booking page for every fixed host, not only round-robin. end is also copied from slotStartTime (line 142) instead of slotEndTime, so a slot that starts inside the window but runs past endTime is still treated as inside. A single window that fully contains the slot start still passes, which is why the existing one-range tests do not catch this.

title: Override window test misses blocked days, partial overlaps, and extra ranges
body: A full-day block is stored as an override whose start equals its end, and this callback tries to reject the whole day in that case. The comparison uses === on two dayjs objects, which is reference equality and is never true, so that branch never runs. The following checks only mark a slot outside a window when the slot ends at or before the override start or starts strictly after the override end. A slot that merely overlaps the window — starts before it, ends after it, or straddles a zero-length block — is treated as inside. find() then stops at the first same-day range that does not contain the slot, so two override ranges on one day (a normal custom-hours override with a gap) reject a slot that sits inside the other range and the day shows no bookable override slots. The date match also uses only the adjusted start, so an override whose UTC interval crosses midnight does not cover slots on the second day. After a timezone shift, a midnight–midnight block can land on the previous UTC date and miss the intended day entirely, leaving a fixed host bookable on a day they marked unavailable.

title: Override date match compares server-local date to UTC date
body: Whether an override applies to a slot is decided by formatting the offset-adjusted start with a local-mode dayjs and comparing it to slotStartTime.format(), and slotStartTime is in UTC mode (time.utc()). format() on a local-mode instance uses the process timezone, not UTC. Whenever the server timezone is not UTC, the two calendar dates disagree for overrides near midnight and the override is applied to the wrong day or not applied at all, so fixed-host date overrides silently fail outside a UTC process.

title: Timezone-adjusted overrides drop the day and can wipe that day's hours
body: Override start/end are converted by adding the invitee-minus-organizer offset and then keeping only hour and minute. That throws away a day boundary. If the shift moves one end across midnight and not the other, endTime is less than startTime; buildSlots discards any range with start >= end. The caller has already deleted that user's normal working hours for the invitee day the raw UTC timestamp fell on, so the day is left with no slots. Even when both ends wrap to clock times on the same side of midnight, the activeOverrides filter (line 206) still selects the invitee day that contains the unadjusted timestamp, whose UTC clock is the organizer wall time rather than the real instant. For a non-zero organizer offset those are different instants, so an evening override viewed from a timezone ahead (US host, European booker) is attached to the wrong calendar day. The new +6 test only shifts IST 14:00–18:00 by 30 minutes and stays on the same day, so it does not catch this.

title: Already-adjusted override minutes are DST-shifted again in buildSlots
body: The new override minutes are computed from the override date's own organizer and invitee offsets, so they are already invitee-local minutes for that date. They are then pushed into computedLocalAvailability and passed through buildSlots, which adds organizerDSTDiff - inviteeDSTDiff. That correction exists for working hours converted with today's offset (dayjs.tz(dayjs(), timeZone)), not for values already adjusted to the target date. When today and the booking day sit on different sides of a DST transition and the invitee timezone does not have the same delta, override slots move by an hour. Asia/Kolkata and Asia/Dhaka do not observe DST, so the added test cannot see it.

title: Tests never exercise fixed-host overrides or a real timezone day shift
body: The only new assertion re-requests the existing personal-event IST override in Asia/Dhaka and expects the same UTC instants. That is a 30-minute shift that stays inside one calendar day and never hits checkIfIsAvailable's fixed-host path with a host who is actually isFixed. Nothing covers a round-robin event with a fixed host whose date override or weekday hours are narrower than the rotating host, a blocked day (start equal to end), a booking or calendar conflict on an override day, split windows, or an override that crosses midnight after timezone conversion. The scenario helper also never attaches eventType.hosts as {isFixed, user}, so the existing round-robin tests leave every user isFixed false and would not exercise this gate even if a case were added. The regressions above can merge green.

title: Date-override hit returns available and skips busy times
body: checkIfIsAvailable returns true as soon as any date override is considered to cover the slot (the dateOverrideExist branch around line 133), before the busy-interval loop. Busy times from calendars and existing bookings are the only conflict filter applied to slots generated from working hours, and this function is that filter. It runs for every fixed host, which includes ordinary 1:1 and collective events (non-round-robin users are marked isFixed), and again for round-robin non-fixed hosts. On any day a host has a date override, slots during meetings are shown as free and can be double-booked.

title: Working-hours check rejects split schedules and ignores duration
body: The new working-hours gate uses workingHours.find and treats a match as "outside hours" (lines 139-150). The callback returns true when the slot's UTC weekday is in an entry and the slot start is outside that one range. find therefore succeeds if any same-day window does not contain the slot. A normal lunch-break schedule (two rows such as 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00 on the same weekdays) rejects every slot, because each slot misses at least one window. This runs for all fixed hosts, including 1:1 events, so those users see no bookable times. The end minute is also copied from the slot start (line 142 uses slotStartTime for both start and end) instead of the slot end, so event length is never compared to the window end and a round-robin slot taken from a longer host can run past the fixed host's hours. A weekday with no matching entry is not rejected at all, so a fixed host with no hours that day is treated as free when the slot came from someone else.

title: Override containment is inverted for multiple ranges
body: Date overrides are scanned with find (lines 106-130), and a truthy callback is treated as "slot is not within the override", which makes checkIfIsAvailable return false. The callback returns true when the slot is outside a single range (ends at or before that range's start, or starts after that range's end). Two override windows on the same day, which is how a break is stored, therefore disqualify every slot: each slot is outside at least one range, so the fixed host has no availability that day. A slot is also treated as inside a range unless it is completely before or completely after it, so a slot that only partially overlaps (starts before the window and ends inside it, or starts inside and ends after it) is accepted and can extend past the override. The all-day block on line 114 compares two separately constructed dayjs objects with ===, which is reference equality and never succeeds, so a zero-length override is not reliably treated as an all-day block.

title: Override timezone shift keeps only clock time and can wipe the day
body: The new conversion adds inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset to the override instants and then stores only .hour() and .minute() (lines 219-223). Those minutes are applied to whichever invitee day contains the unadjusted override.start (the filter at lines 206-208), not the day of the shifted time. When the offset crosses midnight, the clock wraps onto the wrong day. Example: organizer Asia/Kolkata, override stored as 02:00Z-04:00Z meaning 02:00-04:00 local, attendee in UTC. The offset is -330 minutes, hour() becomes 20:30, and that is added to the UTC day of 02:00Z, so slots show at 20:30Z the same date instead of 20:30Z the previous day. If only the start wraps, startTime exceeds endTime. Organizer IST 09:00-18:00 viewed from America/New_York (offset -630 minutes) becomes start 22:30 and end 07:30. buildSlots drops any range with start >= end (line 68), but the override block has already removed that user's normal working hours (lines 228-245), so the attendee sees no slots on the override day.

title: Converted override minutes are shifted again for DST
body: Override bounds are converted to invitee-local minutes using utcOffset() of the override's own date (lines 212-223). buildSlots then runs every slot, including those override minutes, through getTime, which adds organizerDSTDiff - inviteeDSTDiff (lines 102-110). That term corrects working hours that were converted with today's offset rather than the booking date's offset. Override minutes are already based on the booking date, so the extra term moves them whenever today's DST offset differs from the booking day's and the organizer and invitee are not on the same DST schedule. Example: organizer America/New_York, attendee in UTC, today in July (EDT, utcOffset -240) and the booking in January (EST, utcOffset -300). organizerDSTDiff is 60 and inviteeDSTDiff is 0, so every override slot is shown one hour late. Asia/Kolkata and Asia/Dhaka have no DST, so the new test does not catch this.

title: Override day comparison mixes server-local and UTC dates
body: Whether an override applies to a slot is decided by comparing formatted calendar dates (lines 110-111). slotStartTime is time.utc(), so its format() is the UTC date. The override side is dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD") with no .utc(), so format() uses the Node process timezone. On any server whose TZ is not UTC, an adjusted override whose UTC date differs from the server-local date will not match the slot, and the fixed-host override is ignored or applied to the wrong day. Example: server in America/Los_Angeles, override adjusted to 02:00 UTC formats as the previous local evening while the slot formats as the UTC date. The check this PR adds then does not run.

title: Tests miss fixed-host overrides and timezone day boundaries
body: The only new assertion re-fetches a personal-event date override with the attendee in Asia/Dhaka (+6) instead of Asia/Kolkata (+5:30) and expects the same UTC slot list. A 30-minute offset does not cross midnight or a DST change, so it does not catch override slots landing on the wrong day, ranges with start after end being dropped, or the extra DST shift in getTime. There is no round-robin case with a fixed host and a date override, which is the behavior the PR says it fixes, and no case where an override day also has a booking or calendar busy time. createBookingScenario never installs the hosts/isFixed rows, so the new checkIfIsAvailable branches are not exercised and the double-book and split-window regressions would not fail CI.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category is missing or unmatched
body: The migration unconditionally does execute(...embed_category...)[0]['id'] before copying any hosts. On a default install there is no site_settings row named embed_category (the YAML default is an empty string and is not persisted), so the SELECT returns zero rows, [0] is nil, and nil['id'] raises NoMethodError. The same crash happens if the stored value is a slug, an id, a different case, or a deleted category name, because the join is an exact match on categories.name. The uncategorized_category_id fallback on line 15 never runs in that case, and it has the same unchecked [0] access if that row is absent. Every upgrade that hits this aborts the migration and blocks deploy, including sites that never used embedding.

title: Host backfill interpolates SQL and skips normalization
body: Existing embeddable_hosts values are inserted with execute "INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)", bypassing EmbeddableHost callbacks and quote escaping. The old allow check treated http://eviltrout.com and https://example.com/1234 as the hostname only (URI#host / scheme strip). Those strings are stored verbatim, while EmbeddableHost.record_for_host looks up uri.host (eviltrout.com), so previously working allowlist entries stop matching and embeds start failing with invalid referer after a migration that otherwise succeeds. A value containing a single quote breaks the statement and aborts the migration; because this runs as the migration DB role, a crafted setting can also inject SQL. Blank lines and trailing CR from split("\n") are inserted as-is and will not match either. Use a bound, normalized insert (strip scheme, path, whitespace, downcase) instead of raw interpolation.

title: Imports lose embed_category unless the URL host matches
body: TopicEmbed.import used to pass SiteSetting.embed_category into PostCreator for every imported topic. It now passes only EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url).try(:category_id). When that lookup returns nil or false, category is nil and the new topic is filed in uncategorized. The migration deletes the embed_category site setting and only copies it onto embeddable_hosts rows, so there is no remaining default. Feed polling (Jobs::PollFeed, triggered from TopicRetriever when feed_polling_enabled) imports article URLs that were never required to be iframe allowlist hosts. Sites that set embed_category for RSS/Atom embedding but had a blank embeddable_hosts list lose the category entirely, and any feed item whose host does not exactly match an EmbeddableHost row is created uncategorized. Existing topics are not moved; all future imports are.

title: Allow check does not match hosts the model accepts
body: record_for_host compares lower(host) to URI#host without downcasing the bind parameter, and before_validation does not downcase the saved host. The format validator is case-insensitive, so Example.com is valid and stored as-is, but a referer or embed URL whose host is example.com fails the query and host_allowed? returns false. The same method ignores the port, while the validator allows example.com:8080 and the callback only strips a scheme and a path, so a saved ported host never equals uri.host. Consequence: legitimate embeds and TopicRetriever fetches are rejected, and TopicEmbed.import assigns no category, for values the admin UI just accepted. Downcase on write and in the query, and decide explicitly whether port is part of the key.

title: Host regex rejects real hostnames the old setting allowed
body: validates_format_of requires a dotted hostname whose final label is [a-z]{2,5} and whose labels are separated by a single hyphen or dot. That rejects localhost, IP addresses, and any TLD longer than five characters (.museum, .photography, .international, and other gTLDs already in use), plus punycode labels that contain '--' (xn--…). The previous embeddable_hosts site setting was a free-form list and allowed those hosts. Admins cannot save them now, so embedding cannot be enabled for those origins. The optional path group in the regex is also unreachable because before_validation strips the path first.

title: before_validation crashes when host is nil
body: The before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! twice with no presence check. EmbeddableHost.new.valid? or save with a missing host (Admin::EmbeddableHostsController assigns params[:embeddable_host][:host], which can be nil) raises NoMethodError instead of failing validation and returning 422 via render_json_error. There is also no validates_presence_of :host or :category_id, so a record can be valid? with category_id nil even though the column is null: false, and save then raises StatementInvalid rather than a validation error.

title: Update and destroy 500 when the host id is missing
body: update and destroy load the row with where(id: params[:id]).first and immediately use it (save_host sets host.host, destroy calls host.destroy) with no nil check or 404. An unknown id raises NoMethodError and returns 500. save_host also assumes params[:embeddable_host] is present, so a request without that key 500s the same way. On update, a missing or blank category_id is silently replaced with uncategorized_category_id, so a partial update wipes the category relationship.

title: category_id is not checked and has no foreign key
body: save_host writes whatever category_id is posted, and the migration declares category_id integer null: false with no foreign key or index. A deleted, unknown, or non-numeric id is stored. Category#destroy is not wired to embeddable_hosts, so deleting a category leaves dangling ids. TopicEmbed.import then passes that id to PostCreator, which cannot find the category, and new embedded topics land in uncategorized while the admin UI still shows the host as assigned. belongs_to :category does not validate existence.

title: Hosts are not unique, so category lookup is arbitrary
body: embeddable_hosts.host has no unique index, and EmbeddableHost has no uniqueness validation (case-insensitive or otherwise). After normalization, http://example.com and example.com become the same string and both can be saved, with different category_ids. record_for_host uses where(...).first with no ORDER BY, so topic import and the allow check pick an arbitrary row. Two admins, a retried migration (the INSERT is not idempotent), or duplicate lines in the old setting produce conflicting category assignments for one origin.

title: Plural id hydration throws and drops unresolved ids
body: The new _ids branch in _hydrateEmbedded calls obj[k].map with no check that the value is an array, then always deletes the original key and assigns pluralize(subType), even when _lookupSubType returns undefined. This runs for every payload with __rest_serializer == "1", not only embedding. A null or non-array *_ids attribute throws during store.find/findAll and fails the load. Id lists that are not sideloaded under the naive plural (thing + "s") are replaced with an array of undefined entries and the original ids are discarded. The previous code only rewrote singular _id keys, and only when a match was found.

title: Category and embeddable-host fabricators are swapped
body: spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb no longer defines :category, :diff_category, :happy_category, or :private_category. Those definitions were moved into spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb, and Fabricator(:embeddable_host) was written into the category file. Autoloading every fabricator file may hide this, but any explicit load of category_fabricator.rb will not define categories, and putting the category fabricators back in the original file without removing the copy will raise a duplicate fabricator error. The files need to be swapped back before merge.

title: New admin endpoints and the migration are untested
body: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController and Admin::EmbeddingController specs only assert the class ancestry. They never POST/PUT/DELETE, so a missing id 500, a nil host, invalid category_id, and the uncategorized fallback are not exercised. There is no migration spec, so the empty embed_category crash and the un-normalized host INSERT would not be caught. EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? examples use only lowercase hosts and do not cover mixed-case referers, ports, or scheme-prefixed values of the kind the old site setting accepted.

title: Migration crashes unless embed_category exactly matches a category name
body: The migration always runs execute(SELECT ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category')[0]['id']. Site settings are written to the database only when they differ from the YAML default, and embed_category defaults to an empty string, so on a normal install that query returns no rows. [0] is nil and ['id'] raises NoMethodError, rolling the migration back. The later if category_id == 0 fallback never runs in that case, so it does not cover sites that never set embed_category or whose value is not an exact categories.name match (different case, whitespace, slug instead of name). The uncategorized lookup on line 15 has the same [0] crash if that setting row is absent. Production deploys and test DB setup fail before any hosts are copied.

title: Host import interpolates SQL, skips normalization, then deletes the old settings
body: Each legacy host is inserted with VALUES ('#{h}', ...). A single quote or backslash in the old embeddable_hosts value is a SQL syntax error that aborts the upgrade, or arbitrary SQL run as the migration database role. The insert also skips EmbeddableHost before_validation, so values the previous allow-check accepted are stored raw. SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? stripped an http:// or https:// prefix and compared the rest to URI#host; a stored value like http://eviltrout.com will not equal URI#host eviltrout.com, so those hosts stop being allowed after upgrade. split on newline also keeps a trailing carriage return and surrounding whitespace, and a line longer than the new varchar(255) host column fails the INSERT. Line 31 then deletes the embeddable_hosts and embed_category rows unconditionally. The migration uses change plus execute, so it is irreversible and rollback cannot restore the deleted settings.

title: Allow-check ignores host case and port
body: record_for_host binds URI#host and queries lower(host) = ? without downcasing the bound value. URI#host keeps the original case, so a referer or embed URL such as http://Example.com/post does not match a stored host of any case, host_allowed? is false, the comments iframe is rejected, and TopicRetriever skips import so the embed stays on the loading view. URI#host also drops the port, but the format validator allows a :port suffix and before_validation does not remove it, so a saved host example.com:8080 is compared to example.com and never matches. An admin can save a port-qualified host that can never embed or import topics, with no error at save time. Downcase the lookup host and compare a canonical form (include a non-default port on both sides, or strip it both when saving and when checking).

title: Host format rejects valid hostnames
body: The format regex requires the final label to be 2 to 5 letters. That rejects hosts an admin needs to allow: gTLDs and older long TLDs such as example.photography or example.museum, IP addresses such as 127.0.0.1, and localhost. Create and update fail validation, so those sites cannot be added, host_allowed? stays false, and their embeds are denied. The same pattern accepts a port and a path, which record_for_host does not treat as the matched host, so the string that can be saved is not the string that is compared. Accept real hostnames and IP addresses, and canonicalize before validating.

title: Nil host crashes in before_validation
body: before_validation calls self.host.sub! with no nil check. Admin::EmbeddableHostsController assigns params[:embeddable_host][:host], which is nil when the key is omitted, and any EmbeddableHost.create/save with a nil host hits the same callback. NoMethodError is raised before format validation, so the request returns 500 instead of a 422. Guard the callback and validate presence so a missing host is a normal validation error.

title: Duplicate hosts make embed category assignment non-deterministic
body: There is no uniqueness validation, and the new table has no unique index on host. record_for_host uses an unordered .first after a case-insensitive column comparison, so two rows for the same host, including case variants such as Example.com and example.com which both pass the format check, cause TopicEmbed.import to file new topics in an arbitrary category. The migration can also insert duplicate lines from the old setting. Normalize case on save and add a unique index on lower(host).

title: Missing host update or destroy returns 500
body: update and destroy load the row with where(id: params[:id]).first and never check for nil. destroy then calls host.destroy, and update calls save_host which assigns host.host, so an unknown or already-deleted id raises NoMethodError and returns 500 instead of 404. save_host also reads params[:embeddable_host][:host] without checking the nested hash, so a body without embeddable_host 500s the same way. The admin delete action has no ajax error handler, so the failure is silent in the UI. Use find so RecordNotFound becomes a 404, and return 400 when the nested parameters are missing.

title: Category is not validated and has no foreign key
body: belongs_to :category does not check that the category exists, and category_id is a required integer with no foreign key. The admin controller copies category_id from params and only substitutes SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id when the value is blank, so a nonexistent id is saved, as is -1 if the hidden uncategorized setting was never initialized. Deleting a category leaves embeddable host rows pointing at the old id. TopicEmbed.import passes that id to PostCreator, so embedded topics are created uncategorized or with a dangling category_id, which breaks category topic counts and permission lookups. Validate that the category exists and add a foreign key that restricts or nullifies on delete.

title: Removing embed settings drops the SiteSetting API with no shim
body: embeddable_hosts and embed_category are removed from site settings, and SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? is deleted, with no deprecated wrappers. In-repo callers were updated, but plugins, console scripts, and custom jobs that still call SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts, SiteSetting.embed_category, or SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? raise NoMethodError after deploy, including during boot if a plugin touches them at load time. The migration also deletes the stored values, so those callers cannot fall back to the old data. Delegate the old methods to EmbeddableHost for a deprecation period, or external embedding integrations will break on upgrade.

title: Category and embeddable-host fabricators are swapped
body: spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb now defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host), while the new spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains the :category, :diff_category, :happy_category, and :private_category fabricators. Fabrication loads every file in the directory, so the suite may still see both definitions, but the files are reversed. A later cleanup that drops or overwrites the misnamed file will remove category fabrication for the whole suite, and anyone editing category_fabricator.rb will not find the category definitions. Swap the contents back.

title: New admin endpoints and the data migration are untested
body: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController and Admin::EmbeddingController specs only assert that the class subclasses AdminController. They never request create, update, destroy, or show, so they would not catch a 500 on a missing id, a nil host, an invalid category, or a duplicate host. There is no migration spec, so the embed_category [0] crash and the lossy host import are invisible to CI. EmbeddableHost specs cover scheme and path trimming and a basic allow-check, but not mixed-case URLs, ports, rejected TLDs, or duplicate hosts. Add request specs and a migration example that starts from the old site settings before merging.

title: Migration crashes unless embed_category exactly matches a category name
body: The migration sets category_id from execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'] with no empty-result check. site_settings only stores overridden values, and the default embed_category is a blank string, so a normal install returns zero rows. PG::Result#[] then yields nil and nil['id'] raises NoMethodError, aborting db:migrate before the fallback. The same unguarded [0] is repeated on line 15 for uncategorized_category_id, so that fallback crashes too if the row is missing. The join also fails (and crashes) when the saved value is a category id, a different case, a renamed category, or blank, even though PostCreator previously accepted that setting. Because this runs for every upgrade, not only embedding sites, the migration cannot be applied as written.

title: Host allowlist is never copied, then the site settings are deleted
body: The import is gated on embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0 after a SELECT. PQcmdTuples returns an empty string for SELECT (use ntuples); the pg gem's to_i makes that 0, so the block that copies hosts never runs. Line 31 still deletes the embeddable_hosts and embed_category site_settings rows. On any database that gets past the category lookup (embed_category equal to a category name), a successful migration therefore drops the existing allowlist and leaves embeddable_hosts empty. Embedding then fails closed for every previously allowed host, and the old values are gone.

title: Copied hosts skip normalization and are interpolated into SQL
body: Even if the import loop runs, each host is inserted with raw SQL and the model callbacks never run. The old allowlist accepted lines like http://eviltrout.com and https://example.com/1234 (the removed SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? stripped the scheme before comparing to URI#host; the new model strips scheme and path in before_validation). record_for_host compares only URI#host (example.com) to the stored string, so those migrated rows never match and existing embeds stop working. The same statement interpolates the host in single quotes (VALUES ('#{h}', ...)). A quote in the value is a syntax error that aborts the migration, or arbitrary SQL if the value is crafted. Use a quoted/bound insert of a normalized hostname (scheme, path, port, whitespace, and case stripped) before deleting the old settings.

title: Host allow-check does not match ports or mixed-case referers
body: host_allowed? / record_for_host decide whether a page may iframe the forum and which category an imported topic uses. The query is lower(host) = ? with the bind value taken from URI#host, which has no port and is not explicitly downcased. before_validation only strips a lowercase http(s):// prefix and a path; it keeps :port and original case, and the format regex explicitly allows a port. Saving example.com:3000 (valid) therefore never matches a referer of http://example.com:3000/..., so the host is denied and TopicEmbed.import gets no category. A mixed-case referer host likewise fails to match a stored example.com because only the column is lowercased. Case variants of the same host can both be stored and .first then picks an arbitrary category.

title: Host regex rejects real hostnames the old setting allowed
body: validates_format_of requires a dotted name whose final label is [a-z]{2,5}. That rejects legitimate embed hosts: TLDs longer than 5 characters (forum.museum, site.photography, and other gTLDs), IPv4 addresses, and localhost. The previous embeddable_hosts setting was a host list compared as hostnames, not this pattern, so those values can no longer be saved from the admin UI and cannot be allow-listed. The same regex's port and path alternatives are misleading: before_validation strips the path but not the port, and a stored port never matches URI#host (see record_for_host).

title: before_validation raises if host is nil
body: The callback calls self.host.sub! without a nil guard. Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host assigns params[:embeddable_host][:host] directly, which is nil when the key is omitted, then calls save. nil.sub! raises NoMethodError, so the request is a 500 instead of the format validation error render_json_error would have returned for a blank host. Empty string is fine; only nil blows up. The callback also does not downcase, strip whitespace, or remove a port, so values that survive validation still fail host_allowed?.

title: Update and destroy 500 when the host is missing
body: update and destroy load the row with EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and immediately use it (save_host(host) / host.destroy) with no nil check. A stale or unknown id raises NoMethodError and returns 500 instead of 404. save_host also assumes params[:embeddable_host] is present, so a PUT/POST without that key 500s the same way. The new controller specs never hit these actions.

title: No uniqueness on host, so category assignment is nondeterministic
body: embeddable_hosts.host is not unique, and EmbeddableHost has no uniqueness validation (the format regex is case-insensitive, so Example.com and example.com are both valid). The admin UI can save the same host twice with different categories. record_for_host uses where(...).first with no ORDER BY, so topic import and the embed allow-check attach an arbitrary category. Add a unique index on lower(host) and a validation that returns a JSON error instead of a duplicate row.

title: Save paints category from the client id, ignoring the server default
body: After host.save resolves, the component sets host.category to Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')) and does not use the payload. New rows start with categoryId null, and cantSave only checks the host string, so saving without touching the category chooser is allowed. The server replaces a blank category_id with SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id and returns that id. findById(null) does not return the uncategorized category, so the row leaves edit mode with an empty category badge even though a category was stored. The same overwrite drops the badge whenever categoryId does not resolve, which is the default path for the host/category editor this PR adds.

title: Plural id hydration throws when the ids value is null
body: The new *_ids branch in _hydrateEmbedded calls obj[k].map without checking that the value is an array. This runs for every rest_serializer payload, not only embeddable hosts. A null embeddable_host_ids (or any other null *_ids key) raises TypeError and rejects store.find / findAll for the parent record. The singular _id branch already no-ops when lookup fails; the plural branch should treat null or a non-array as an empty list instead of throwing.

title: New controller and migration behavior are not tested
body: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController and Admin::EmbeddingController specs only assert the class is a subclass of AdminController. They never POST/PUT/DELETE, so a missing record 500, a nil host 500, invalid hosts, and duplicate hosts are untested. There is no migration spec, so the unguarded embed_category lookup, the cmd_tuples check that skips the copy, and the raw INSERT of scheme-prefixed hosts are not caught. EmbeddableHost specs cover scheme/path trimming on the model but not record_for_host with a port, mixed-case referer, or nil host. The topic expandable_first_post? example titled as failing when no embeddable host exists no longer sets that condition; the method only checks embed_truncate and has_topic_embed?, so the example passes for the wrong reason.

title: In-place downsize can corrupt the upload and strips animation
body: Auto-downsize calls OptimizedImage.downsize with the same path for source and destination (the open upload Tempfile). ImageMagick convert and gifsicle are not safe that way: the output open truncates the file before it is fully read, and many versions write a temp file then rename it over the destination. The Tempfile fd stays on the old inode, while tempfile.size (fstat on that fd) is what both the while condition and Upload.create_for use as the filesize. After a replace, the recorded size can be the original multi-megabyte size while the path holds the smaller image, or create_for can persist the pre-downsize bytes / a truncated file. The return value is ignored, so a failed convert is retried and the damaged file is still passed to create_for. The loop can also exit while the file is still over max_image_size_kb (five 80% passes are not guaranteed to hit the byte limit, and a no-op or failed pass does not abort), despite the comment claiming the image is reduced to the allowed size. Rack multipart tempfiles are created as Tempfile.new("RackMultipart") and have no suffix, but optimize only selects the animated pipeline when the source path matches /\.GIF$/i, and the still instructions always run convert ...[0]. A large GIF is therefore flattened to the first frame even when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, and ImageMagick keys the writer off the destination suffix, so an extension-less output can fail or be written in the wrong format while original_filename and content_type stay unchanged. If the path does end in .gif, downsize_instructions_animated forwards the "80%" geometry to gifsicle --resize-fit, which was built for a pixel WIDTHxHEIGHT box, so animated downsize fails instead of shrinking the file.
