title: Second downsize definition replaces the width/height API
body: Ruby does not overload methods. The new downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) at line 149 completely replaces downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) at line 145, so the width/height wrapper is dead and never runs. The previous public signature passed numeric width and height (and an optional opts hash) into optimize, which formatted "WxH". Existing callers that still use that shape now bind height to opts; optimize then evaluates opts[:allow_animation] and raises NoMethodError because an Integer has no []. Callers that also pass an options hash raise ArgumentError (5 arguments for arity 3..4). optimize itself changed from (operation, from, to, width, height, opts) to (operation, from, to, dimensions, opts), and OptimizedImage.dimensions was removed, so any external caller of those methods with separate width and height breaks the same way. The upload controller only works because it uses the string form that accidentally overwrote the compatibility wrapper.

title: Client size check hardcodes 10MB for every upload type
body: validateUploadedFile used to enforce Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so images and attachments each honored the admin setting. It now rejects every file larger than a hardcoded 10240 KB. Attachments are not downsized by this feature, so a site with max_attachment_size_kb under 10240 no longer gets a client-side rejection (the file is uploaded and fails later), and a site that allows attachments over 10 MB can no longer select them in the composer. Images are also blocked at 10 MB even when max_image_size_kb is higher, so previously valid images never reach the server. The 413 handler at line 246 uses the same literal, so the alert always says the maximum is 10240 KB, which is wrong when the configured limit or the proxy body limit is different. This number is a separate copy from the controller's 10.megabytes cap, so the client and server ceilings can drift.

title: Multipart images are converted with no size ceiling
body: The new loop runs OptimizedImage.downsize up to five times whenever an image is larger than SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb. Nothing in that condition caps how large the file may be. The 10 MB ceiling added in this change is only applied to API URL fetches (FileHelper.download) and the browser check; a normal multipart POST never goes through that helper, and the client check is bypassable. create only requires a logged-in user, and the convert runs inside the deferred upload job before Upload.create_for can reject the file. Any member can therefore force repeated ImageMagick decodes of whatever body the web server accepts, including decompression bombs whose pixel buffer is far larger than the file size. A failing downsize does not break the loop, so one bad file always costs five process spawns.

title: URL upload fetch limit no longer follows the site setting
body: API URL uploads used to be fetched up to SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes. They are now stopped at a hardcoded 10.megabytes, for every type, not only images that will be downsized. On a site whose max_image_size_kb is above 10240, URL uploads the setting still allows (this fetch cap has always applied to non-images as well) are no longer downloaded, so the new downsize path never sees them. The ceiling is not configurable and is a different literal from the client-side 10 * 1024 check, so the two limits can diverge.

title: No coverage for downsize or the new upload ceiling
body: This change adds an upload-time convert loop, a new OptimizedImage.downsize calling convention, and replaces site-setting size checks with a hardcoded 10 MB cap in the client, the 413 message, and FileHelper.download. No tests were added for success or failure of that loop, in-place Tempfile conversion, GIF/animation handling, files that stay over max_image_size_kb after five attempts, or attachments versus images under a non-default max_*_size_kb. Those paths can store a truncated image or ignore the configured limits, and nothing in the PR would fail if they did.

title: Second downsize definition discards the width/height API
body: Ruby has no overloading, so the second OptimizedImage.downsize at app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 replaces the width/height method just above it at line 145 (Ruby warns "method redefined; discarding old downsize"). The wrapper that would build a "#{max_width}x#{max_height}" geometry is therefore dead, and the previous public signature downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) no longer exists. This pull request does not update any other call sites. A caller that still passes an options hash as a fifth argument raises ArgumentError (5 for 4). A four-argument call such as downsize(from, to, 400, 300) binds 400 as the geometry string and 300 as opts, so ImageMagick shrinks to width 400 instead of 400x300, and opts[:allow_animation] raises TypeError because opts is an Integer. optimize was also changed from separate width and height arguments to a single dimensions string, so direct callers of optimize break the same way. Keep one method that accepts either a geometry string or numeric width and height, and update every caller.

title: In-place downsize runs on an extensionless tempfile
body: create_upload downsizes with OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails) at uploads_controller.rb:67. Input and output are the same path. ImageMagick does not support that: convert can truncate the destination before it finishes reading, leaving a zero-byte or corrupt image, and the original bytes are already overwritten so there is no fallback. The false return value is ignored, so Upload.create_for on line 72 stores the damaged file. The path is also the wrong file identity. Rack multipart tempfiles are named like /tmp/RackMultipart... with no suffix, and the URL download uses the prefix discourse-upload-#{type} rather than the real extension; the original name lives only in filename. ImageMagick picks the output coder from the destination suffix, so the write can fail with no encode delegate or emit bytes that do not match filename and content_type. Animation is dropped for the same reason: OptimizedImage.optimize (optimized_image.rb:155) adds the gifsicle path only when the path matches /\.GIF$/i. An extensionless tempfile never matches, so every oversized GIF goes through convert ...[0], which keeps only the first frame. allow_animated_thumbnails therefore cannot preserve animation. Even if the path ended in .gif, gifsicle --resize-fit (optimized_image.rb:120) expects pixel geometry such as 100x100, not ImageMagick's 80%, so that branch would fail too. Tempfile#size is an fstat of the still-open descriptor; if convert replaces the path by rename, the size loop and the filesize passed to create_for keep seeing the old inode. Downsize into a new tempfile that keeps the original extension, and only replace the upload if the command succeeds and the new file is non-empty.

title: Hardcoded 10MB cap ignores image and attachment settings
body: validateUploadedFile used to limit uploads with Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'] (max_image_size_kb for images, max_attachment_size_kb for everything else). Line 182 now hardcodes 10 * 1024 KB for both types. Attachments are not downsized, and UploadsController never reads max_attachment_size_kb, so the browser will accept attachments the admin setting forbids (they fail late, or are stored if nothing else checks) and will reject attachments larger than 10MB even when that setting allows them. Images are capped at 10MB even when max_image_size_kb is higher, so previously valid uploads never reach the server downsize path. If max_image_size_kb is already at least 10240, a browser upload can never exceed the server downsize threshold and this feature does not run for normal uploads. The same magic number is repeated in the HTTP 413 alert (utilities.js:246), which tells the user the limit is 10240 KB regardless of the web server or site setting, and in API URL fetches (uploads_controller.rb:55, FileHelper.download(..., 10.megabytes)), which used to stop at SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes and now always pulls up to 10MB, including non-images. The client cap, the 413 text, and the download ceiling need to come from site settings: a real pre-downsize image ceiling, and max_attachment_size_kb for other files.

title: Downsize loop can finish still over the limit
body: The loop at uploads_controller.rb:66 calls OptimizedImage.downsize up to five times and ignores a false return. convert_with returns false when ImageMagick or gifsicle exits non-zero or ImageOptim raises, and it throws away stderr (&> /dev/null), so a failed pass leaves the file unchanged or truncated while the loop only decrements attempt. It then always calls Upload.create_for with no check that the file is under SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb. Each pass is a relative 80% geometry shrink plus another lossy re-encode and ImageOptim run, not a resize aimed at the byte limit. Five passes leave about 33% of the linear dimensions (about 10% of the pixels), which is not enough when the upload is near the new 10MB client ceiling and max_image_size_kb is much smaller. The while condition uses tempfile.size, which will not change if the tool replaced the path and the open descriptor still stats the old inode, so all five attempts run anyway. Multipart uploads also have no upper bound before convert, unlike the 10MB URL download, so any logged-in user who can post a large body can force five ImageMagick plus ImageOptim runs on an arbitrarily large image (and on a small decompression bomb just over the setting) on the synchronous request thread or on Scheduler::Defer. Stop when downsize fails, return an error if the file is still over the limit, and refuse files above a hard maximum before invoking convert.

title: No tests for downsizing or the new size caps
body: The new downsize loop in UploadsController#create_upload and the client/API limit changes ship with no tests. Nothing covers an image over max_image_size_kb being stored under that limit, convert failing or still being over the limit after five passes, an animated GIF keeping or losing frames, attachments still honoring max_attachment_size_kb, or OptimizedImage.downsize accepting both a geometry string and numeric width/height. Those are the paths this change gets wrong, and they will not be caught before merge.

title: Downsize reads and writes the same tempfile path
body: OptimizedImage.downsize is invoked with tempfile.path as both the source and the destination. The convert command built by downsize_instructions opens the output path for writing before it finishes reading the input, so when those paths are identical ImageMagick truncates the upload and the result is an empty or corrupt image. Versions that special-case this by writing a temporary file and renaming it over the destination leave the already-open Ruby Tempfile descriptor on the old inode while the path points at the new file. Upload.create_for on line 72 is then given that Tempfile object and tempfile.size, so the bytes stored, the SHA1 (if taken from the path), and the recorded filesize can disagree, and the saved upload is not the image the user sent.

title: Downsize path has no image extension, so encoding and GIF detection fail
body: create_upload passes tempfile.path straight through and never copies the bytes to a file ending in the original filename's extension. Multipart uploads use Rack's Tempfile (Tempfile.new("RackMultipart")), which has no .jpg/.png/.gif suffix, and the URL branch asks FileHelper.download for a "discourse-upload-#{type}" prefix that also does not include filename's extension. ImageMagick chooses the output encoder from the destination extension, so this convert fails with no encode delegate or writes a payload that is not the format implied by original_filename. optimize only takes the gifsicle path when the source path ends in .gif, so the allow_animation flag passed here does not apply and a GIF is sent through convert's [0] selector, which keeps only the first frame.

title: Failed downsize is ignored and the file is still uploaded
body: The loop discards the false return from OptimizedImage.downsize. convert_with returns false when convert, gifsicle, or ImageOptim fails, but the only exit condition is tempfile.size. A convert that truncates the file makes size 0, the while condition ends, and the empty file is treated as small enough and passed to Upload.create_for. If conversion fails without shrinking the file, the loop retries up to five times and then still calls create_for even though the image is larger than SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb. downsize_instructions also sets no JPEG -quality, so a re-encode at ImageMagick's default quality can grow the file across attempts. The feature does not enforce the size limit and can persist a truncated or oversized upload.

title: No maximum size before repeated ImageMagick conversion
body: The new loop runs for every image larger than SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb and never rejects files above the 10MB ceiling added on the client and in the URL downloader. Multipart bodies are not size-capped in create_upload before this work, and the client check is bypassable by a direct POST or API call. Each attempt shells out to convert or gifsicle and then ImageOptim. Any logged-in user can submit a very large image, or a small decompression bomb whose name looks like an image, and force up to five full decodes on a defer thread or, for synchronous API uploads, on a web worker, exhausting CPU and memory before Upload.create_for can apply a filesize error.

title: Second downsize definition overwrites the width/height API
body: Ruby does not overload by arity, so def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) on line 149 replaces def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) on line 145 at load time and emits a method-redefined warning. The width/height implementation is dead. This class previously exposed downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts). Callers that still pass width, height, and an options hash now raise ArgumentError (5 arguments for a method that accepts at most 4). Callers that pass width and height only bind height to opts, and optimize then raises TypeError on opts[:allow_animation] because an Integer does not accept a Symbol index. The new uploads-controller call only works because it matches the surviving definition; definition order, not an overload, is what makes "80%" work.

title: Client size check hardcodes 10MB for every upload type
body: validateUploadedFile used to compare against Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so images and attachments honored separate admin limits. It now always uses 10 * 1024 KB. Attachments larger than max_attachment_size_kb but under 10MB pass the client and are not downsized by the new server loop; attachments that the admin allowed above 10MB are rejected. Images are capped at 10MB even if max_image_size_kb is higher, and a max_image_size_kb of 0 (which skips server downsize because the new guard requires > 0) still hits this fixed client cap. The 413 handler on line 246 repeats the same constant, so the user-facing file_too_large message always claims the maximum is 10240 KB even when the proxy or the site setting rejected the file for a different limit.

title: URL fetch limit ignores per-type size settings
body: FileHelper.download used to stop at SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes. It now always allows 10.megabytes, and this runs before the code knows whether the URL is an image. Non-image API uploads are not passed through the new downsize loop, so a remote attachment or other non-image is fetched up to 10MB even when max_attachment_size_kb or max_image_size_kb is lower. That raises the amount of data an API client can pull into the temp directory and no longer matches the configured per-type limit.

title: 80% geometry and thumbnail setting do not correctly downsize GIFs
body: The third argument is the ImageMagick percentage "80%", but when the path ends in .gif and allow_animation is true, optimize uses gifsicle --resize-fit with that string. --resize-fit is built for a pixel box such as 800x600 (resize_instructions_animated), not an ImageMagick percentage, so the animated shrink fails and, because the return value is ignored, the GIF is left over the size limit. allow_animation is also bound to SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails. When that thumbnail setting is off, the canonical upload goes through convert's [0] frame selector and the stored GIF silently loses every frame but the first, even though the setting is not supposed to rewrite originals.

title: No tests cover automatic downsize or the new size ceiling
body: The new behavior — image-only shrinking, a five-attempt 80% loop, what happens when convert fails or the file stays over max_image_size_kb, non-image uploads still bound by their own site setting, and the OptimizedImage.downsize signature change — has no tests in this pull request. A regression that stores a truncated tempfile or rejects a previously allowed attachment would not be caught.

title: Unsubscribe is a state-changing GET
body: TopicsController#unsubscribe is exposed as GET t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe and t/:topic_id/unsubscribe, and it writes topic_users.notification_level before rendering. Rails CSRF protection does not cover GET, and this app predates SameSite cookies, so a logged-in victim can be forced to change topic or PM notification level by an image, link prefetch, or other cross-site GET. The write is also not idempotent: a level above regular becomes regular, and regular becomes muted, so a refresh or a second full page load applies a second transition (watching becomes regular, then muted). The Ember unsubscribe route never performs the change itself, so the only implementation of the action is this GET side effect.

title: Unsubscribe leaves tracking and watching users notified
body: The email string says the link will stop notifications for this topic, and the new page says the user will stop receiving them, but unsubscribe only sets notification_level to muted when it is already regular (1) or lower. Tracking (2) and watching (3) are both written to regular (1). Tracking receives the same reply, mention, and quote emails as regular, so that click changes nothing about email. Watching stops every-post emails but still sends reply, mention, and quote emails. A second request then takes regular to muted, so the first confirmation is false and a refresh changes the result.

title: Raw save does not record an explicit notification choice
body: unsubscribe assigns notification_level and calls save! instead of TopicUser.change. change is what sets notifications_changed_at, sets notifications_reason_id to user_changed, and publishes the /topic/:id notification_level_change event. save! leaves the old reason in place. Rows created when an email is sent often have a nil reason, because TopicUser.change is called with only last_emailed_post_number. update_last_read in topic_user.rb then forces notification_level back to tracking when notifications_reason_id is null and the auto-track time threshold is met, and auto_track does the same for a nil reason. For those users the unsubscribe does not stick, and already-open clients never get the level-change event.

title: Missing TopicUser row 500s unsubscribe
body: unsubscribe loads TopicUser with find_by(user_id, topic_id) and immediately reads tu.notification_level. If there is no row, tu is nil and this raises NoMethodError, so the request 500s and nothing is saved. A topic_users row is not created for every user who can see a topic; the URL is predictable and any logged-in user who can see the topic can open it without having visited or been emailed. TopicUser.change already creates the row when it is missing; this action does not use it.

title: Unsubscribe template does not match its route
body: The router registers a top-level topicUnsubscribe route at /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe, and the route, controller, and view are all the topic-unsubscribe module. Ember looks up template topic-unsubscribe, i.e. templates/topic-unsubscribe. The template was added at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs, which is the name for a nested topic.unsubscribe route that was not registered, and there is no matching topic/unsubscribe controller. After the Rails shell boots, the transition fails with a missing template, so the confirmation text and the notification dropdown never render.

title: Per-topic unsubscribe link is not tied to the recipient
body: Topic#unsubscribe_url is only the public topic URL plus /unsubscribe, and UserNotifications puts that same link in every recipient's mail. TopicsController#unsubscribe is behind ensure_logged_in and always updates current_user, with no signed user or email token. Unlike the existing digest path email/unsubscribe/:key, a logged-out recipient opening the message from a mail client is not unsubscribed by the click. If someone else is logged in (forwarded mail or a shared browser), that account's notification level is changed instead of the recipient's.

title: render :show drops canonical URL on topic pages
body: perform_show_response is also used by TopicsController#show, which calls canonical_url only after perform_show_response returns. Previously the HTML format block did not render, so Rails deferred the template until the action finished and @canonical_url was already set for the layout. The new render :show inside format.html renders the layout immediately, before that call, so every topic HTML response loses its canonical link. Unsubscribe HTML has the same gap because it never sets a canonical URL either.

title: No coverage of unsubscribe behavior or the new link
body: The only spec change passes unsubscribe_url into Email::MessageBuilder so the new unsubscribe_link translation does not raise MissingInterpolationArgument, but the example still only checks that the user-preferences URL appears in the text body. It never asserts that the per-topic unsubscribe URL is present in the text or HTML part, or that List-Unsubscribe changed. There is no controller or request spec for TopicsController#unsubscribe, so the level transition, nil TopicUser crash, slug redirect, and session requirements are untested.

title: render :show runs before canonical_url is set
body: perform_show_response now calls render :show inside the HTML branch (topics_controller.rb:500). TopicsController#show only calls canonical_url after perform_show_response returns (line 87). Previously the HTML branch did not render, so Rails implicit render ran after the action finished and the layout still saw @canonical_url. render evaluates the show template and layout immediately, so @canonical_url is still nil and every topic HTML response loses its canonical link. This is a silent site-wide regression, not limited to unsubscribe. Move the render back out of the shared method, or set the canonical URL before rendering.

title: Unsubscribe mutates notification state on a cookie-authenticated GET
body: config/routes.rb registers topics#unsubscribe as GET (t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe and t/:topic_id/unsubscribe), and the action writes TopicUser.notification_level at topics_controller.rb:107-113 with no per-user token. Topic#unsubscribe_url (topic.rb:719) is only /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe, the same for every recipient, unlike the existing digest link email/unsubscribe/:key. Rails forgery protection does not cover GET, so any page can include that URL as an image or link and, for a logged-in victim, downgrade or mute the topic. Email prefetchers and link scanners that send the user's cookies will do the same without a click. Logged-out recipients are only redirected to login, so the link does not identify or unsubscribe the person who was emailed. The Ember route never calls an unsubscribe API; it only loads the topic. A safe design is a signed, user-specific token, or a GET confirmation page plus a POST that uses TopicUser.change.

title: Unsubscribe does not stop notifications for watchers and is not idempotent
body: If notification_level is above regular (tracking=2 or watching=3), unsubscribe sets regular (1); otherwise it sets muted (0). Watching is what causes an email on every new post, and the new copy promises a full stop: server.en.yml unsubscribe_link says "stop receiving notifications about this particular topic", and client.en.yml topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications says "You will stop receiving notifications". After one request those users are still at regular, so replies, mentions, and quotes still notify. The transition is also not idempotent: a second GET (refresh, duplicate fetch, or a scanner request plus the user's click) sees regular and mutes. Outcome depends on how many times the URL is hit, and mute hides the topic from the user's lists, which is stronger than stopping email and is never explained. Always set muted (or another single terminal level) through TopicUser.change, and make repeat requests a no-op.

title: Missing TopicUser 500s, and save! does not record an explicit choice
body: unsubscribe does TopicUser.find_by and immediately reads tu.notification_level. If the logged-in viewer has no topic_users row (the URL is not bound to the email recipient; any logged-in user who can see the topic can open it), tu is nil and this raises NoMethodError. tu.save! also bypasses TopicUser.change, which is what sets notifications_reason_id to user_changed, sets notifications_changed_at, creates a missing row, and publishes /topic/:id on MessageBus. The mailer creates the recipient row with TopicUser.change(last_emailed_post_number:) and does not set a reason, so reason often stays nil. update_last_read then auto-upgrades notification_level back to tracking when notifications_reason_id is null and view time exceeds the auto-track threshold, and TopicUser.auto_track does the same when reason is nil. The unsubscribe can be silently undone on a later visit, and other open tabs are not notified. Use TopicUser.change so a missing row is created and the user's choice is sticky.

title: Unsubscribe template name does not match the route
body: The route is registered as topicUnsubscribe at /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe (app-route-map.js.es6:13). The new controller, route, and view are all topic-unsubscribe, which Ember resolves as topicUnsubscribe / template topic-unsubscribe. This template lives at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs, which compiles to the name topic/unsubscribe (nested route topic.unsubscribe). No code renders that name, and there is no templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs. The view also does not set templateName. After the Rails shell loads, the confirmation screen is blank: the stop-notifications copy and topic-notifications-button never appear, so the user cannot see or correct the level the GET just wrote. Move the template to templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs, or nest the route under topic and move the controller and view to match.

title: No spec covers unsubscribe behavior or the new email link
body: The only test change passes unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe" so I18n can interpolate unsubscribe_link. The example at line 179 still only checks that the user-preferences URL is in the body; it never asserts the per-topic URL or the new "click here" sentence. There is no request/controller spec for TopicsController#unsubscribe: missing TopicUser, watching versus regular, a second GET, slug redirect, logged-out access, or CSRF. The broken level transitions and the nil TopicUser crash can ship without a failing test.

title: Unsubscribe 500s when the user has no TopicUser row
body: TopicsController#unsubscribe does TopicUser.find_by(user_id, topic_id) and immediately reads tu.notification_level. find_by returns nil when that logged-in user has no topic_users row for the topic (never opened it, a different account than the email recipient, or the row was removed). Calling notification_level on nil raises NoMethodError, so the new email link returns 500 instead of unsubscribing or rendering the page. Email delivery usually inserts a row via TopicUser.change, but this public route does not, and nothing here creates one. Use TopicUser.change (it inserts when missing) or handle a missing record, and still persist an explicit muted level.

title: Unsubscribe does not stop notifications for watching or tracking
body: The email string says the link will "stop receiving notifications about this particular topic", and the page string says "You will stop receiving notifications". The action does not do that. Levels are muted=0, regular=1, tracking=2, watching=3. If the level is above regular it is set to regular; only regular or muted is set to muted. Tracking and regular send the same reply, mention, and quote emails, so a tracking user who clicks the link is unchanged and keeps those emails. A watching user is only dropped to regular and still gets reply, mention, and quote mail for the topic. The GET is also not idempotent: a refresh or second fetch sees regular and then mutes, so the result depends on how many times the URL is hit, and neither the email nor the page describes a two-step downgrade. The client route never changes the level itself, so an in-app transition to /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe only shows that future-tense copy. To match the copy, one request should set the topic to muted.

title: Direct save lets auto-track undo the unsubscribe
body: The action assigns notification_level and calls save!. TopicUser.change is what records a user-chosen level: it sets notifications_changed_at, sets notifications_reason_id to user_changed when it is still nil, and publishes on MessageBus. save! does none of that. update_last_read's SQL and TopicUser.auto_track only auto-upgrade a topic to tracking when notifications_reason_id is null. A row created just to store last_emailed_post_number still has a null reason. After this sets muted or regular, the next read that crosses an enabled auto-track threshold (user auto_track_topics_after_msecs or the site setting >= 0) writes tracking back, so the unsubscribe does not stick and notifications resume. Other open tabs also keep the old level because MessageBus is not notified. Persist the change through TopicUser.change so it is stored as an explicit user choice.

title: Topic unsubscribe mutates notification level on GET
body: config/routes.rb exposes GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe and GET /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe, and the action writes notification_level before rendering. There is no per-user token and no CSRF token. The URL is predictable from the topic slug and id, and protect_from_forgery does not apply to GET. In this app's era, browsers send session cookies on cross-site GETs, so another site can change a logged-in user's topic level with an img, redirect, or top-level link. A prefetch that includes the session does the same without a click. Because the downgrade is not idempotent, two fetches can go from watching to regular and then to muted. Do not change state on GET; show a confirmation and mutate on POST, or require an unguessable one-time key plus an explicit confirm.

title: Shared render drops canonical URL on every topic page
body: show calls perform_show_response and only then calls canonical_url(...) with the topic canonical path, discarding the return value. That call exists to store the URL the layout emits (Discourse assigns @canonical_url for rel=canonical / og:url) before render. Rendering used to be implicit at the end of the action, after that call. This change adds render :show inside perform_show_response's HTML branch, which show and unsubscribe both use, so the topic template and layout run before canonical_url. Every normal topic HTML response is sent without its canonical link. That is an SEO regression for all topic pages, not just unsubscribe. Set the canonical URL before rendering, or render only from unsubscribe after show's post-setup has run.

title: Unsubscribe template path does not match the Ember route
body: app-route-map.js.es6 registers a top-level route named topicUnsubscribe at /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe. Ember resolves that route's template from the dasherized name topic-unsubscribe (underscore/dasherize of topicUnsubscribe, not a slash path). The new route, controller, and view files use that name (topic-unsubscribe.js.es6), but the template is templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs, which is registered as topic/unsubscribe — the name for a nested topic.unsubscribe route that was never defined. After the server handles the email link, the Ember app will not find a template and will error instead of showing the confirmation text and the topic-notifications-button. Put the template at templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs, or nest the route as topic.unsubscribe and move the controller and view to match.

title: No spec checks unsubscribe behavior or the new email link
body: The only spec change passes unsubscribe_url into MessageBuilder so the updated unsubscribe_link translation does not raise MissingInterpolationArgument, then still only asserts that the user-preferences URL is in the body. It never checks that the topic unsubscribe URL or the new "stop receiving notifications about this particular topic" sentence is present. There is no controller or request spec for TopicsController#unsubscribe: missing TopicUser, watching versus tracking versus regular, a second request stepping down again, the slug redirect, or notifications_reason_id being set. Those paths are currently untested and are where this feature fails.

title: Blocklist lookup is case-sensitive and does not trim
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? loads a row with BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first, and the model never normalizes email before the uniqueness check or save. Signup stores the address exactly as submitted (User.new_from_params assigns params[:email] with no downcase or strip), and the new client cache compares that same raw string via rejectedEmails.contains. On PostgreSQL the unique index and equality match are case-sensitive, so a block row for bad@spam.com does not match Bad@spam.com, BAD@spam.com, or bad@spam.com with leading or trailing whitespace. Those are the same mailbox in practice (UsersController#change_email already does Email.downcase(...).strip), so a blocked address can still register by changing case or padding spaces, and after one rejection the signup form will allow that variant through again. Downcase and strip on write and inside should_block? before the query, and enforce case-insensitive uniqueness so mixed-case duplicates cannot be stored.

title: should_block? writes during validation and double-counts
body: should_block? is not a pure predicate: on every hit it does match_count += 1, sets last_match_at, and calls record.save, and EmailValidator calls it from User validation. UsersController#create always evaluates user.valid? and then user.save, and save runs validations again, so one signup attempt invokes should_block? twice. The first save commits immediately. The second runs inside the user-save transaction: if the user is persisted (including action_type do_nothing, which still updates stats), both increments commit and match_count rises by 2; if validation fails, the inner increment rolls back and the count rises by 1. Paths that only save once, such as User.create_for_email, rise by 1. Any valid? call, including a check that never creates a user, also mutates the row. The read-modify-write is racy under concurrent signups, and a failure in that save (lock timeout, StatementInvalid) escapes the validator and is rescued in create as login.something_already_taken. Record the match with one atomic UPDATE that does not run validations, and do not write from inside validation on every valid?/save pass.

title: Domain allow/deny regex is unanchored and can be bypassed
body: email_in_restriction_setting? builds Regexp.new("@(#{domains})", true) after only escaping dots, then uses value =~ regexp, which succeeds on any substring. With email_domains_whitelist set to example.com, attacker@example.com.evil.com matches @example.com and is treated as allowed. Someone who controls that domain can receive the activation message and register even though the address is not on example.com. The same pattern does not cover subdomains on the blacklist: spam.com does not match user@mail.spam.com, so a subdomain of a blocked provider is accepted. Other metacharacters in the site setting are interpolated raw, so a value with an unmatched parenthesis makes Regexp.new raise and turns every email change into a 500. Compare normalized domains (anchor at the end of the address, or split the setting and test equality) instead of a substring regex.

title: Email change never consults the blocklist
body: The new block check only runs from EmailValidator when a User is validated with email_changed?. UsersController#change_email never assigns user.email or saves the user. It only rejects the address if User.where("email = ?", lower_email).exists?, then creates an EmailToken and enqueues an authorization mail to that address. A blocked address therefore passes this endpoint and a confirmation message is sent. Whether the address actually sticks depends on EmailToken.confirm later performing a validating save; this request path itself does not enforce BlockedEmail.should_block?, so the control added for signup is missing on the email-change flow. Reject blocked addresses here before creating the token, using the same normalization as lower_email.

title: rejectedEmails array is shared across controller instances
body: rejectedEmails: Em.A([]) is evaluated once when CreateAccountController is defined, so the array sits on the prototype. pushObject mutates that array in place rather than assigning a per-instance property. Every instance then shares one list: a second controller (tests, App.reset(), or another create()) already contains emails rejected elsewhere and will fail emailValidation for them via contains. Set a fresh array in init with this.set('rejectedEmails', Em.A()) so instances do not leak rejections into each other.

title: Validator specs stub the block check and miss bypasses
body: The EmailValidator examples stub BlockedEmail.should_block? and never insert a BlockedEmail, so they cannot catch a case or whitespace mismatch, a failed lookup, or the write inside should_block?. blocked_email_spec.rb only uses the exact address block@spamfromhome.org and calls should_block? once, so it stays green if Bad@spam.com or a trailing space is allowed, and if UsersController#create increments match_count twice. Domain whitelist and blacklist behavior was moved into EmailValidator with no regression example, including the unanchored match of attacker@example.com.evil.com against a whitelist of example.com. Add cases for normalized lookup, a single stat update on the signup path, and anchored domain restrictions.

title: BlockedEmail.actions calls Enum with the wrong constructor
body: BlockedEmail.actions does Enum.new(:block, :do_nothing). Enum in this application (lib/enum.rb) takes a single hash of name => stable integer, the same form used by every other enum (for example PostActionType). Passing two symbols raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments). actions is invoked from set_defaults on every BlockedEmail save, from should_block? once a matching row is loaded (both record.save's before_validation and the action_type comparison), and from the fabricator, where action_type BlockedEmail.actions[:block] is evaluated when fabricators load. Blocked emails cannot be created through ActiveRecord, the new specs error, and if a row is inserted another way any signup whose email matches that row 500s inside validation instead of returning the blocked-email error. Define it as Enum.new(:block => 1, :do_nothing => 2) so stored action_type values are explicit and do not change if symbols are reordered.

title: Blocklist lookup is case-sensitive and not normalized
body: should_block? loads BlockedEmail.where(email: email) with the raw address, and nothing downcases or strips email before the uniqueness validation or insert. The rest of this app already normalizes addresses with Email.downcase and strip (UsersController#change_email, User.find_by_username_or_email), and the domain allow/deny regex is case-insensitive, but this blocklist is an exact match. PostgreSQL's unique index on blocked_emails.email is case-sensitive as well, so Spam@evil.com and spam@evil.com are different rows. A blocked address such as spam@evil.com can register by changing case or adding surrounding whitespace; the client rejectedEmails list has the same exact-string hole because it stores and compares result.values.email unchanged. Normalize with Email.downcase and strip in a before_validation callback and again inside should_block? before the query, so the block cannot be bypassed and case-variants cannot both be inserted.

title: Match stats written during validation are rolled back or double-counted
body: should_block? increments match_count and last_match_at and calls save while User email validation is running. User#save wraps validation in a transaction that Rails rolls back when save returns false, and a nested BlockedEmail save joins that transaction. On paths that only call save or save! (User.create_for_email and any other creator), a blocked address fails validation and the statistic update is rolled back, so the attempt is never recorded. UsersController#create makes the count path-dependent: it always calls user.valid? first, outside a transaction, which commits one increment, then user.save validates again. If the address is blocked, the second increment is rolled back (net +1). If action_type is do_nothing and the user is otherwise valid, both increments commit (net +2 per signup). save's false return is also ignored, so a failed stat write is silent. Record the match with an explicitly committed atomic update after the allow/block decision, not as a side effect of validation.

title: match_count update is a lost-update race
body: The counter is updated by reading match_count, adding 1 in memory, and calling save, with no row lock and no atomic SQL increment. Two concurrent signups that both load the same blocked_emails row each write old+1, so one attempt is dropped; last_match_at can also be overwritten by the slower request. A burst of registrations against one blocked address silently undercounts. Use a single UPDATE ... SET match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ? WHERE id = ? (or increment_counter) so concurrent matches are not lost.

title: Domain allow/deny regex is unanchored and barely escaped
body: email_in_restriction_setting? builds a case-insensitive regexp of @(domain-list) after only replacing dots with backslash-dot, and the pattern is not anchored at the end of the address. A whitelist of company.com therefore matches user@company.com.attacker.example, and that signup is allowed. That defeats email_domains_whitelist as an access control: any host that merely starts with an allowed domain plus a dot is treated as allowed. The same prefix match makes a blacklist of spam.com also reject user@spam.com.legitimate.example. Only dots are escaped before interpolation, so a setting value that contains other regexp metacharacters (an unmatched parenthesis, +, *) either matches the wrong addresses or raises RegexpError during validation and 500s every signup and email change. This was moved unchanged from User#email_validator. Escape each domain and anchor the match at a domain boundary and at the end of the string before relying on these settings.

title: Block and domain checks are stubbed away, so the new rules are untested
body: The validator spec stubs BlockedEmail.should_block? and only asserts that some email error is present or absent. It never checks that the message is user.email.blocked, never exercises email_domains_whitelist or email_domains_blacklist (so the unanchored-domain bypass stays green), and never runs User validations, so a broken validates :email, email: true wiring would still pass. blocked_email_spec only looks up the exact casing it inserted, so Spam@evil.com bypassing a spam@evil.com block is not caught, and nothing asserts match_count across UsersController#create's valid?-then-save path. There is also no example that a failed create returns errors and values, which the signup UI now depends on. Those cases need real records, not stubs.

title: Every email error is cached as a permanent format failure
body: On a failed create, the client pushObjects result.values.email whenever result.errors.email is set. That key is present for every email validation failure (already taken, domain not allowed, or blocked), not only blocklist hits. emailValidation then fails that exact string with I18n.t('user.email.invalid') — the same copy used for a malformed address — and submit stays disabled until the address text changes. The flash is the only place the real server reason appears; afterward the field says the address is invalid, and it cannot be resubmitted even if the failure was transient or the conflicting account is removed. rejectedEmails is also a prototype Em.A([]) and is never cleared when the modal closes, so the rejection sticks for the life of the page. Only cache blocklist rejections, or show the server's error string, and do not reuse the format-invalid translation.

title: Blocked-email match is case-sensitive and does not trim
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? loads a row with an exact where(email: email) comparison, and nothing downcases or strips the address on write or lookup. Uniqueness is case-sensitive, and the unique index on blocked_emails.email is case-sensitive, so User@spam.com and user@spam.com can both be stored and only one of them matches. Signup assigns params[:email] unchanged (User.new_from_params) and EmailValidator passes that raw value in. Elsewhere this app treats addresses as case-insensitive: UsersController#change_email uses Email.downcase(...).strip, and the domain regexp is built ignore-case. A listed address can therefore be used to register by changing case or adding surrounding whitespace, so the block list does not stop the signup it is meant to stop. Normalize with the same downcase-and-strip helper on save and in should_block?, and enforce a case-insensitive unique index.

title: Match stats are written during validation and counted twice per signup
body: EmailValidator calls BlockedEmail.should_block? from validate_each, but should_block? is not a pure check: on any hit it increments match_count, sets last_match_at, and save the row, including when action_type is do_nothing (the method returns false and no error is added). UsersController#create calls user.valid? at line 168 and then user.save at line 172, and save runs validations again. One signup attempt against a screened address therefore records two matches. The same write runs for every other valid? or failed save, including attempts that never create a user. match_count and last_match_at, which the model spec treats as the record of how often an address was seen, will be inflated, and every anonymous signup POST that hits a screened address performs a database write as a side effect of validation. Record the match once, after a real attempt, with an atomic update outside the validator.

title: match_count update is a lost-update read-modify-write
body: should_block? loads match_count, adds 1 in Ruby, and save writes that absolute value back. Two concurrent requests that both read the same count will both persist count+1, so attempts are dropped. save also runs validations and callbacks and writes every dirty column, so a failure or delay on this row can turn a signup validation into an error, or overwrite a concurrent last_match_at. Increment with an atomic update (update_counters or increment_counter) and set last_match_at with update_column so concurrent matches are not lost and other columns are not rewritten.

title: Domain allow/deny regexp is unanchored and barely escaped
body: email_in_restriction_setting? interpolates the site setting into a regexp of the form @(domain-list) after escaping only dots, then matches with =~, which succeeds on any substring and is not anchored at the end of the address. A whitelist entry of company.com therefore accepts attacker@company.com.evil.com. A blacklist entry of spam.com does not match user@mail.spam.com, because the character before spam.com is a dot rather than @, so subdomain addresses bypass the blacklist. Other regexp metacharacters in the setting are not escaped, so an invalid fragment raises RegexpError during validation and registration returns 500 instead of a validation error. This is the domain check moved from User, and it is still wrong. Anchor the host to the end of the string, decide explicitly whether subdomains should match, and escape metacharacters before interpolation.

title: Specs miss case bypass, double-count, and domain rules
body: EmailValidator specs stub BlockedEmail.should_block? and never create a blocked row, and BlockedEmail specs only call should_block? with the exact stored string. Nothing asserts that User validation (validates :email, email: true) rejects a blocked address, that a case or whitespace variant is blocked, that UsersController#create increments match_count once, or that the whitelist/blacklist branches accept or reject the suffix and subdomain cases above. Those bugs would leave this suite green.

title: Embed highlights template is invalid Ruby and 500s
body: `<%- end if %>` is compiled as Ruby `end if`, which is a syntax error (a block `if` is closed with `end`, not `end if`). ERB turns the whole template into one method, so any render of `embed/best` raises SyntaxError before HTML is produced. The first visit can still show `loading.html.erb` and enqueue a retrieve; once a `topic_embeds` row exists, every later iframe load 500s and the discussion never appears. The new controller spec does not enable `render_views`, so it never compiles this template and stays green.

title: Imported HTML is stored raw and executed on the Discourse origin
body: RSS items and remotely fetched pages are saved with `cook_method: raw_html` and `skip_validations: true`. `Post#cook` then returns `raw` unchanged, and both the embed view (`raw post.cooked`) and the normal topic UI render `cooked` as HTML. Nothing runs the content through Sanitize. `ruby-readability` 0.5.7 does not honor the `tags:` / `attributes:` arguments passed in `import_remote` (those are Sanitize-style options and are ignored), so scripts, event handlers, and `javascript:` links from the remote page are kept. `PollFeed` also `CGI.unescapeHTML`s the feed body first, turning entity-encoded markup into live tags. Separately, line 13 interpolates the source URL into a single-quoted `href` and into the link text with no encoding; `absolutize_urls` reparses with Nokogiri, which preserves injected elements and handlers. A feed link or embed URL such as `http://example.com/' onclick='alert(1)` becomes an active handler in the stored post. A normal CMS feed that includes an embed script is enough; the script runs as the viewing user on the forum origin, including inside the embed iframe.

title: Feed polling crashes on ordinary RSS items
body: `i.content.scrub` assumes every item has a string `content` and that `String#scrub` exists. Standard RSS 2.0 only has `description` (SimpleRSS sets `content` from `content:encoded`), so `i.content` is nil and this raises NoMethodError on the first such item. `String#scrub` itself was added in Ruby 2.1, so on Ruby 2.0/1.9 the call fails even when content is present. There is no per-item rescue, and `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so one bad item aborts the rest of the feed until the next hour. `TopicRetriever` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute` inline before the HTTP fallback, so the same exception also skips `import_remote` for the URL the user actually asked to embed. `feed_key` is computed and never used, and `open` is not given a timeout or closed.

title: Resize postMessage never arrives in the parent
body: `parent.postMessage(..., request.referer)` passes the full referer URL (scheme, host, path, and query) as `targetOrigin`. Browsers of this era compare that argument to the parent's origin (`https://host`), not to the full page URL, and drop the message when they differ. `<%= request.referer %>` is also HTML-escaped, so a referer containing `&` is inserted as `&` and cannot match even in browsers that parse `targetOrigin` as a URL. `embed.js` creates the iframe with `scrolling="no"` and no height, and only grows it on `discourse-resize`. The message is discarded, so the iframe stays at the default ~150px and comments are clipped with no scrollbar.

title: Resize listener treats any prefix of the forum URL as a trusted origin
body: The check is `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`, i.e. whether the forum URL string contains the sender origin, not whether the sender equals the forum origin. Any origin that is a string prefix of `discourseUrl` is accepted. For a forum at `https://discuss.example.com`, an attacker origin of `https://discuss.example.co` matches because `"https://discuss.example.com".indexOf("https://discuss.example.co") === 0`. That window can set `iframe.height` to an arbitrary value. Combined with `scrolling="no"`, a huge height covers the embedding page with the iframe. The listener also does not require `e.source === iframe.contentWindow`.

title: import_remote fetches the embed URL with open-uri and follows redirects
body: `import_remote` does `open(url).read` with no `require 'open-uri'` in this file (only `poll_feed.rb` requires it), no read size limit, no timeout, and no close. Unless some other file has already loaded open-uri, `Kernel#open` treats the URL as a local path and raises Errno::ENOENT, so the non-RSS embed path never imports. When open-uri is loaded, it follows HTTP redirects. `TopicRetriever` only compares the original URL's host to `embeddable_host`, so `http://allowed-host/redirect` that 302s to `http://127.0.0.1`, link-local cloud metadata, or another internal service is fetched and then stored as a public topic via the raw_html path. The embed action enqueues that fetch for any client that can set `Referer` to the allowed host. The same method is also called from the Disqus importer with links taken from the XML, with no host allowlist. Failures are unrescued, so a 404, SSL error, or huge body fails the job.

title: embed_url is varchar(255) under a unique index
body: `t.string :embed_url` is a varchar(255) on PostgreSQL, and the unique index is on that column. Article URLs with long slugs or tracking query strings routinely exceed 255 characters. `TopicEmbed.create!` then raises a string-right-truncation error, the import transaction rolls back, and that article can never be embedded. The column needs to be `text` (or a much larger limit); a unique btree index on text is valid in PostgreSQL.

title: Disqus import drops threads when the live page cannot be fetched
body: Topic creation used to be a local `PostCreator` call with the export title, `created_at`, permalink body, and optional `-c` category. It now depends entirely on `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which GETs `t[:link]` and returns nil on any network, HTTP, or readability failure. The comment loop is inside `if post.present?`, so a dead or blocked link silently skips every comment on that thread. `import_remote` / `TopicEmbed.import` also have no `created_at` or category argument, and the `-c` / `--category` option was removed, so existing invocations that passed a category fail and imported topics are dated now in the default category instead of the original thread date and destination.

title: Bulk embed imports still hit create rate limiters
body: `skip_validations: true` only turns off ActiveRecord validations. `Post` still includes `RateLimiter::OnCreateRecord` (`rate_limit` / `rate_limit_create_post`, plus topic creation limits in `TopicCreator`), and those callbacks run on save. A feed or retrieve that creates more than a handful of topics in one run will raise `RateLimiter::LimitExceeded` or roll back mid-loop; `PollFeed` has no per-item rescue, so the rest of the feed is skipped until the limit window resets (`max_topics_per_day` is 20). The Disqus task in this same change calls `RateLimiter.disable` around its import loop; `PollFeed` and `TopicRetriever` do not. Updates pass `bypass_rate_limiter`, but that flag only skips `EditRateLimiter` inside `PostRevisor`, not create limits.

title: Every embed miss re-downloads and imports the entire feed
body: When `feed_polling_enabled?` is set, each cache miss calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute` synchronously inside the retrieve job, before the single-URL HTTP fetch. The Redis throttle key is per embed URL, not per feed, so ten different articles trigger ten full feed downloads and imports per minute, on top of the hourly schedule (this path does not take the scheduler lock, so it can overlap the hourly run). `PollFeed#feed_key` looks like a conditional-GET / already-seen short-circuit but is never read, and `poll_feed` always `open`s the feed URL and walks every item. One slow or huge feed blocks the worker and can create a topic for every item as a side effect of viewing a single embed.

title: Retrieve throttle can stick forever if expire does not run
body: `retrieved_recently?` does `SETNX retrieved:<url> 1` and only then `EXPIRE 60`. Those are not atomic. If the process dies, Redis errors, or expire is skipped between the two calls, the key has no TTL. `retrieved_recently?` then stays true for that exact URL forever (unless `no_throttle` is set for staff), so the article is never fetched again. Use a single `SET key 1 NX EX 60` (or set the TTL inside the same command the deployment's Redis supports). The same gap exists for every distinct embed URL.

title: Embed URLs are compared exactly, so the same article splits or is skipped
body: Lookup, uniqueness, and the import short-circuit all use the raw URL string (`where(embed_url: url)` and the unique index). There is no normalization: `http://host/a` and `http://host/a/`, a URL with a fragment or `utm_*` query, and the same path with a different scheme case are different rows, so one article becomes multiple topics. The allowlist check is also case-sensitive: `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` uses `URI(embed_url).host`, which preserves case (`Example.COM`), and compares it to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` with `!=`. `TopicEmbed.import` only accepts URLs matching `/^https?:\/\//`, so `HTTP://...` is dropped. `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` uses the same case-sensitive host compare on `Referer`. Mixed-case canonical URLs from a CMS or feed never import, and the loading iframe retries forever.

title: Deleting the topic or first post leaves a row that crashes embed and feed updates
body: `belongs_to :topic` / `:post` do not declare `dependent: :destroy`, and `Topic` is not given a matching association, so destroying a topic or its first post leaves `topic_embeds` in place (there is also no foreign key). The embed action then does `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` for a missing topic and 500s on every view instead of importing again. On the next feed change, `post = embed.post` is nil and `PostRevisor.new(post)` raises, which aborts the rest of `PollFeed`'s item loop. `import` also treats any in-memory `PostCreator` result as success (`post.present?` is true for an unsaved post after a rolled-back create) and will `create!` an embed pointing at a topic id that was never committed.

title: Anyone who can set Referer can enqueue unbounded outbound fetches
body: `ensure_embeddable` only compares `Referer`'s host to `embeddable_host`. That header is not a credential; any client can send `Referer: http://<embeddable_host>/` and GET `/embed/best?embed_url=...`. On a cache miss the action always `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic)` with the caller-supplied URL and no per-IP or global limit. The job's 60s Redis throttle is per exact URL, so many distinct paths on the allowed host become many Sidekiq jobs and many outbound requests (and, after redirects, internal ones). `loading.html.erb` reloads every 30 seconds and enqueues again. `TopicRetriever` returns quietly on host mismatch, blank `embed_by_username`, throttle, or fetch failure, but the UI has no error state, so a misconfiguration or attacker page keeps scheduling work forever. This is a GET that mutates server state (jobs and topics), so crawlers and prefetch can trigger it too when a matching referer is present.

title: absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs and skips other relative ones
body: The helper claims to absolutize relative URLs but only rewrites `a[href]` and `img[src]` that `start_with?('/')`. A protocol-relative URL such as `//cdn.example.com/a.png` matches that check, then `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both slashes, so it is rewritten to `http://<article-host>/cdn.example.com/a.png` instead of keeping the CDN host. Relative URLs that do not start with `/` (`images/a.png`, `../a.png`, `?page=2`) are left unchanged and later resolve against the Discourse origin, so images and links 404 or hit forum routes. Both forms are common in RSS and article HTML. Only root-relative paths like `/hello` work, which is the only case the new spec covers.

title: import mutates contents in place and crashes when the body is nil
body: `contents << footer` appends to the caller's string instead of copying it. `import_remote` passes `doc.content` through, and Readability returns nil when it cannot extract an article, so this raises NoMethodError and the retrieve job fails (the loading iframe then retries forever). A frozen string raises the same way. Callers that reuse the buffer also get a second footer and a different SHA1 on the next import. Build a new string (`"#{contents}#{footer}"`) after rejecting blank content.

title: Embed controller spec never renders the templates it claims succeed
body: The success examples do not call `render_views` (rspec-rails 2 stubs views by default), so they never compile `best.html.erb` and cannot catch the `end if` syntax error. The example that expects a topic view stubs `TopicView.new` without a return value; mocha yields nil, so `@topic_view` is nil and a real render would raise before the `after` hook's `response.should be_success`. `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` only stubs whether `execute` calls `poll_feed` and never parses a feed, so the nil-`content` crash and unsanitized import are also untested.

title: Embed template has a Ruby syntax error and cannot render
body: best.html.erb closes its first conditional with `<%- end if %>` (line 6). That compiles to `end if`, which is a Ruby syntax error, so ActionView raises when an existing embed topic is rendered and the iframe gets a 500. The new controller spec never renders views, so it still passes. On-demand and feed-imported embeds cannot display comments until this is a plain `end`.

title: Imported HTML is stored and rendered without sanitization
body: Post#cook returns the raw body unchanged when cook_method is raw_html, and TopicEmbed.import saves remote HTML with that cook method (skip_validations: true). PollFeed (poll_feed.rb:35) runs CGI.unescapeHTML on the feed body first, which turns escaped tags back into real markup, and never runs Sanitize. import_remote only whitelists a few tags/attributes and still allows javascript: href/src values. TopicEmbed.import also interpolates the source URL, unescaped, into an href (topic_embed.rb:13). Cooked HTML is treated as trusted in the forum UI, and best.html.erb:19 emits it with `raw`. A feed item or imported page can therefore store script or javascript: links that execute in the Discourse origin for every viewer of the topic or embed.

title: Public embed endpoint triggers unbounded server-side fetches
body: EmbedController#best is an unauthenticated GET. Its only gate is that the Referer host equals embeddable_host (embed_controller.rb:26), which any non-browser client can spoof. It then enqueues RetrieveTopic for the caller-supplied embed_url (embed_controller.rb:15). TopicRetriever only compares URI#host to that setting and does not restrict scheme or port (topic_retriever.rb:15). import_remote then calls open(url).read with no timeout or size cap. open-uri follows redirects, so a path on the configured host that 302s to a link-local or internal URL is fetched from the Discourse server, and the body is loaded entirely into memory. Distinct embed_urls each enqueue work, so this is also a job-queue and memory DoS, and a successful HTML response is imported as a topic posted by embed_by_username.

title: Resize postMessage uses the full referer as targetOrigin
body: The embed layout calls parent.postMessage(message, request.referer). The second argument must be an origin (scheme://host[:port]), but request.referer is a full URL with path and query. Browsers then throw or drop the message (target origin does not match the parent). ERB escaping also turns `&` in the referer into `&`, so the string would not match even without a path. embed.js only grows the iframe from that discourse-resize message and sets scrolling=no, so comments stay clipped at the default iframe height.

title: Loading embed never reliably advances to the topic
body: When no TopicEmbed exists, EmbedController renders loading and then calls discourse_expires_in 1.minute (embed_controller.rb:19), marking that response cacheable. The loading page reloads itself after 30 seconds via location.reload() with no cache-busting flag, so the browser may reuse the fresh cached loading document and never notice that the topic was created. If the reload does hit the server, authorization still requires the Referer host to be embeddable_host. A reload's Referer is often the iframe's own Discourse URL or empty, not the original parent page, so ensure_embeddable returns InvalidAccess and the iframe stays on the error or loading state.

title: Feed poll crashes on typical RSS items
body: poll_feed always calls i.content.scrub and CGI.unescapeHTML. SimpleRSS exposes standard RSS 2.0 bodies as description (and content:encoded as content_encoded), not content, so i.content is missing or nil and this raises NoMethodError. String#scrub itself only exists on Ruby 2.1+, so the same line crashes on Ruby 1.9/2.0 even when content is present. There is no per-item rescue, and the job sets retry: false, so one bad item aborts the rest of that hourly import. Titles and links are also used unchecked, so a blank title fails the same way.

title: Feed URL is passed to Kernel#open with no scheme check
body: poll_feed passes SiteSetting.feed_polling_url directly to open() after requiring open-uri. Nothing checks that the setting is an http or https URL. In Ruby, open('|...') spawns a shell and open('/path') reads a local file; open-uri only special-cases strings that look like URLs. A feed setting of a pipe command or filesystem path (admin UI, API, or script running as an admin) becomes command execution or local file read on the next poll. http URLs are also fetched with no timeout, redirect allowlist, or response size limit, so a slow or huge feed blocks a worker and can exhaust memory.

title: Host-spam check still blocks imports for a new embed user
body: TopicEmbed.import creates the topic with skip_validations: true, but PostCreator still runs rollback_if_host_spam_detected before save. has_host_spam? is skipped only for trust level basic and above, and newuser_spam_host_threshold defaults to 3. A newly created embed_by_username account is trust level 0, and imported HTML usually contains several links to the same host, so the create transaction is rolled back. import still treats the returned post object as present and TopicEmbed.create! then fails on a null post_id. Feed polling and on-demand retrieve both fail for ordinary articles unless the configured user is already TL1+.

title: embed_url is limited to 255 characters
body: embed_url is a Rails string column, created as varchar(255), with a unique index on that column. Article and tracking URLs often exceed 255 characters. PostgreSQL then raises a string-truncation error, the import transaction rolls back, and that page can never be embedded. There is no foreign key or dependent: :destroy on topic_id/post_id either, so deleting the topic leaves a topic_embeds row; topic_id_for_embed still returns the dead id, TopicView errors, and TopicRetriever skips the URL because the row exists, so the embed never heals.

title: Protocol-relative URLs are rewritten onto the article host
body: absolutize_urls treats every href and src that starts with `/` as a root-relative path and strips leading slashes before prefixing the article origin. Protocol-relative URLs such as //cdn.example.com/img.png start with `/`, so they become http://article-host/cdn.example.com/img.png. Relative links that do not start with `/` (img.png, ../img.png) are left untouched. Imported RSS and readability HTML commonly uses both forms, so images and links in the created topic are broken. The port logic also drops the port whenever it is 80 or 443, so https on port 80 or http on port 443 is rewritten to the wrong default port.

title: Retrieve throttle can lock a URL forever
body: retrieved_recently? claims the per-URL lock with SETNX and only then sets a 60 second TTL in a second command. If the process dies between those calls, retrieved:<url> is left with no expiry. Later retrieves treat the URL as recently fetched forever, unless the viewer is staff (no_throttle). The key is also set before a successful fetch, so a crash or a failed fetch in that window permanently prevents import of that embed URL. SET with NX and EX in one command would avoid the stuck key.

title: Every embed miss synchronously imports the entire feed
body: On a cache miss, perform_retrieve calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute inline before fetching the requested URL. That downloads the whole feed and runs TopicEmbed.import for every item, inside the RetrieveTopic worker that was enqueued just to import one page. One iframe view can occupy a Sidekiq thread for the full feed and create or revise every feed topic. The redis lock only lasts 60 seconds, so a slow poll overlaps the next retrieve and starts another full import. The scheduled job already polls hourly; this path should not repeat that work synchronously.

title: Disqus import now requires live fetches and drops category and dates
body: The importer used to create a local permalink topic with the XML thread's created_at and an optional --category. It now calls TopicEmbed.import_remote for t[:link] and the category option was removed, so every thread is fetched over HTTP, posted as the current time, and lands in the default category. import_remote is not rescued: one missing link, non-http link, timeout, or readability failure raises and aborts the rest of the export. The task can no longer import from the XML file alone.

title: Embeddable host comparison is case-sensitive
body: invalid_host? and EmbedController#ensure_embeddable compare SiteSetting.embeddable_host to URI#host with != and do not downcase either side. Hostnames are case-insensitive, but Ruby's URI#host keeps the original case, so a referer or embed_url of http://EvilTrout.com is rejected when the setting is eviltrout.com. The embed then 403s or never imports even though the host is the configured one.

title: Poll feed specs do not exercise the guards they name
body: The examples that claim execute requires feed_polling_url and embed_by_username never stub feed_polling_enabled? to true. That setting defaults to false, so execute returns before those checks and the examples pass even if the url or username guard is deleted. Nothing calls poll_feed, so nil content, non-http item links, Kernel#open behavior, and TopicEmbed.import failures are untested. The embed controller spec also does not render views, which is why the best.html.erb syntax error is invisible to CI.

title: Referer is interpolated into a script string (reflected XSS)
body: The embed layout writes request.referer into a single-quoted JavaScript string with <%= %>. On Rails 3.2 and 4.0 that helper escapes &, <, >, and double quotes, but not single quotes, and it is not a JavaScript escape. ensure_embeddable only checks that URI(referer).host equals SiteSetting.embeddable_host, and Ruby's URI parser allows ' and () in the query. A parent URL such as http://eviltrout.com/?x=';alert(document.domain);// therefore passes the host check and is rendered as parent.postMessage(..., 'http://eviltrout.com/?x=';alert(document.domain);//'); which runs in the Discourse origin. This layout wraps both the loading and best responses, and a normal blog page that includes the embed script sends the full parent URL (including query string) as Referer. Any logged-in user who opens a crafted link on the embeddable host executes attacker script in the iframe and can perform forum actions as that user. Pass a fixed origin (Discourse base URL) or JSON-encode the target origin; do not HTML-interpolate a request header into script.

title: Imported HTML is stored and rendered unsanitized (stored XSS)
body: TopicEmbed.import appends an attribution link by interpolating the raw URL into HTML (href='#{url}' and the link text), then PostCreator stores that string with cook_method raw_html and skip_validations. Post#cook (post.rb:133) returns raw unchanged for raw_html, skipping the markdown sanitizer and plugin filters. The embed view prints it with raw post.cooked (best.html.erb:19), and the normal topic page also treats cooked as HTML, so the payload runs on the Discourse origin for every viewer. The URL is attacker-controlled: /embed/best only checks a spoofable Referer host, then the retrieve job accepts any http(s) URL whose host equals embeddable_host. A URL Ruby will parse, such as http://eviltrout.com/?q='onmouseover='alert(1), still returns the real page on most blogs (query string ignored) and, after Nokogiri::HTML.fragment.to_html, becomes an anchor with an event-handler attribute. absolutize_urls does not strip script, on* attributes, or javascript: URLs. The RSS path is worse: PollFeed does CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content) and imports that with no allowlist at all, so a feed body of <script> becomes a live script tag. import_remote's readability tag list still keeps a[href] and img[src], so javascript: links survive. Escaping the footer URL is required but not sufficient; sanitize imported HTML before it is persisted as cooked, including on the update path.

title: Success template has invalid Ruby (`end if`) and cannot render
body: The header branch is closed with `<%- end if %>`, which is not valid Ruby. ERB compiles the template before running it, so every successful embed (topic already imported, TopicView assigned) raises a syntax/template error instead of showing comments. The loading template is valid, so the iframe sits on "Loading Discussion..." until retrieve finishes and then 500s. The matching closer must be `<% end %>`. spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb never enables render_views, so it still expects 200 and will not catch this.

title: RSS poll crashes because item content is often nil
body: poll_feed always does i.content.scrub and then CGI.unescapeHTML. SimpleRSS leaves content nil for ordinary RSS 2.0 items (body is description and/or content_encoded) and for Atom entries that only have a summary. nil.scrub raises NoMethodError. There is no per-item rescue, and the job sets sidekiq retry: false, so one such item aborts the rest of the feed and the same crash repeats every hour. String#scrub also does not exist before Ruby 2.1, so this line fails even when content is present on 1.9/2.0. Use description / content / content_encoded with a nil guard, rescue per item, and do not let one bad entry (nil body, nil/short title, URI error, rate limit) skip the remainder. open(feed_url) also has no timeout, so a hung feed blocks the scheduler indefinitely.

title: Spoofable Referer is enough to fetch URLs and create topics
body: best enqueues retrieve_topic for any embed_url when the Referer host matches embeddable_host. Referer is fully client-controlled, the route is an unauthenticated GET, and TopicRetriever only compares URI(embed_url).host to that setting (lib/topic_retriever.rb:15). It does not restrict scheme beyond what open accepts, port, path, or redirects. import_remote then calls open(url).read (topic_embed.rb:48). open-uri follows redirects to other hosts by default, so an open redirect on the embeddable host (or a 302 to link-local/metadata addresses) becomes server-side request forgery, including port probes such as http://embeddable-host:6379/. The 60s throttle key is per URL, so an attacker can enqueue a distinct job and create a distinct public topic for every query string that returns HTTP 200, all as embed_by_username, bypassing SpamRulesEnforcer because import passes skip_validations. There is no body size limit or timeout, so this is also a memory/job-queue DoS. Require a non-spoofable control (signed embed token), re-validate every redirect hop against an allowlist, cap response size, and rate-limit imports globally.

title: import_remote uses Kernel#open without requiring open-uri
body: import_remote fetches the article with open(url).read but never requires open-uri. Kernel#open only treats the argument as an HTTP URL after open-uri is loaded; otherwise it opens a local path and raises Errno::ENOENT, so no topic is created. poll_feed.rb requires open-uri at load time, and TopicRetriever calls PollFeed before fetch_http only when feed polling is enabled, so on-demand import accidentally depends on that file having been loaded in-process. The Disqus thor task calls import_remote without requiring open-uri either. The call also has no read timeout or byte limit, and a nil doc.content then crashes import via contents <<. Require open-uri (or use a dedicated HTTP client), set timeouts and a max size, and handle nil/failed fetches without raising.

title: Every cache-miss embed runs a full synchronous feed import
body: When feed polling is enabled, perform_retrieve calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) inline before the single-URL HTTP fetch. That downloads and imports every feed item on the retrieve job, even though feed_key is computed in PollFeed and never used (no conditional GET). If the feed is slow, invalid, or hits the nil-content crash, the exception aborts perform_retrieve and fetch_http never runs, so turning on feed polling breaks on-demand embeds whenever the feed errors. URL comparison is exact, so a feed link that differs by trailing slash, http/https, or tracking params will not satisfy the embed_url; the expensive poll still runs and fetch_http then creates a second topic for the same article. Fetch the one URL directly, and do not let a feed failure skip that fetch.

title: Embed lookup is a raw string match and ignores deleted topics
body: topic_id_for_embed plucks topic_id for an exact embed_url match and does not check that the topic or post still exists. http://host/post, http://host/post/, and the https or utm variants are different rows, so the iframe misses the feed-imported topic and import creates duplicates. After a moderator deletes the topic, the row still matches, EmbedController builds a TopicView for a missing topic instead of enqueueing retrieve, and the URL is stuck.
