On update (line 32), embed.post is nil once the post is trashed (Post includes Trashable), and PostRevisor.new(nil) raises. That exception is not rescued in PollFeed, so one deleted import stops the hourly feed. Normalize URLs before save/lookup, and treat a missing topic/post as "not embedded" (or destroy the embed row on delete).

title: Protocol-relative and non-root-relative URLs are rewritten wrong
body: absolutize_urls treats every href/src that start_with?('/') as a root-relative path and does href.sub(/^\/+/, ''), which strips every leading slash. A protocol-relative image or link such as //cdn.example.com/img.png, which is common in RSS, becomes http://original-host/cdn.example.com/img.png and breaks. Relative URLs that do not start with / (images/a.png, ../a.png) are left untouched, so the browser resolves them against the Discourse origin and they 404 in the topic and in the embed iframe. Only rewrite a single leading slash, leave // URLs as protocol-relative (or prefix the scheme only), and resolve other relative references against the article URL. The same logic is duplicated for img at line 70.

title: embed_url is varchar(255) but article URLs are often longer
body: embed_url is a Rails string column, so PostgreSQL stores it as varchar(255), with a unique index on that column. Real article URLs with query parameters routinely exceed 255 characters. TopicEmbed.create! then raises (string truncation / statement invalid), the import transaction rolls back, and the embed stays on the loading page forever because no row is written. Use a text column (and a unique index on text, which PostgreSQL allows) before this ships; a later migration cannot silently widen rows that already failed to insert.

title: Concurrent imports race and enqueue jobs before commit
body: import does a check-then-act (where embed_url is blank, then create) inside Topic.transaction. Two retrieve jobs or a poll overlapping a retrieve can both pass the blank check and both call PostCreator. The unique index makes the second TopicEmbed.create! raise, rolling back that savepoint, but PostCreator#create calls enqueue_jobs after its inner transaction returns and before the outer transaction commits. Those Sidekiq jobs are not transactional: they run against a post that is not committed yet or that the unique-violation rollback undoes. The RecordNotUnique exception is also unrescued, so a racing PollFeed aborts the remaining feed items. Rescue the unique violation, re-read the existing embed, and enqueue post-processing only after the outer transaction commits.

title: Creates do not bypass rate limits that the Disqus importer disables
body: import passes skip_validations, which only turns off post validations and, in PostCreator, SpamRulesEnforcer. It does not skip RateLimiter::OnCreateRecord on Post. The update path passes bypass_rate_limiter: true, and lib/tasks/disqus.thor calls RateLimiter.disable around the whole import, but PollFeed and TopicRetriever call TopicEmbed.import with the limiter still active. If the embed user is subject to create-topic/create-post limits, a feed larger than that allowance raises mid-loop. PollFeed does not rescue per item and sets retry: false, so the rest of the feed is dropped and the next hourly run fails the same way. Disable the rate limiter for embed/feed creation the same way the Disqus task does, or the hourly import cannot keep up with a normal feed.

title: Login-required forums redirect the embed iframe to the login page
body: EmbedController skips check_xhr and preload_json but not the application login_required filter (redirect_to_login_if_required). Comment embeds are loaded anonymously in a third-party iframe. When login_required is on, that request is redirected to the login page before ensure_embeddable runs. The login page is sent with the normal X-Frame-Options policy, so the iframe is blank rather than showing comments. Anonymous readers, which are the main audience for an embedded comment box, never see the discussion. Skip the login redirect for this action and keep the embeddable-host check as the access gate.

title: Disqus import now requires a live URL and drops category and date
body: The importer used to create the topic locally from the export (title, permalink body, thread created_at, and optional -c category) and then attach comments, so dead or private links still imported. It now calls TopicEmbed.import_remote, which HTTP-fetches t[:link] and parses it with Readability. A 404, timeout, or non-article page skips the entire thread (the comment loop is inside if post.present?). The -c/--category option was removed, and import does not accept category or created_at, so threads land in the default category with "now" as the topic timestamp instead of the Disqus thread date. import_remote also does not require open-uri (see topic_embed.rb). Keep a local fallback when the fetch fails, and pass category and created_at through to PostCreator.

title: postMessage origin check is an inverted substring test
body: postMessageReceived accepts the event when discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) is not -1, i.e. when the configured URL string contains the sender origin. That is the opposite of an origin allowlist and also ignores e.source, so it is not limited to this iframe. Any origin that is a prefix of discourseUrl is treated as trusted. If discourseUrl is http://forum.example.com:3000/, a page at http://forum.example.com (port 80) matches at index 0 and can set iframe.height. Compare parsed origins for equality and require e.source === iframe.contentWindow. The same file concatenates discourseUrl + "embed/best" with no slash normalization (line 7), so a discourseUrl without a trailing slash requests a non-existent host path and the embed 404s.

title: Rails 3 lockfile was not updated for the new embed gems
body: ruby-readability and simple-rss were added to the Gemfile and to Gemfile_rails4.lock only. RAILS3=1 still uses Gemfile.lock (see the dual-boot lockfile switch at the top of the Gemfile). bundle install --deployment on the Rails 3 path fails because the lockfile does not match the Gemfile, so feed polling and import_remote cannot be installed on that boot path. Update Gemfile.lock as well, or the gems are missing exactly where PollFeed and TopicEmbed require them.

title: Specs never render embed views or parse a feed
body: The success examples stub TopicView and do not enable render_views, then an after hook expects HTTP 200. They therefore never compile app/views/embed/best.html.erb, whose `end if` syntax error 500s every real success response. spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb only checks that execute sometimes calls poll_feed and never feeds an RSS document, so the nil i.content crash is untested. spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb asserts cooked == raw, which records the unsanitized raw_html behavior instead of asserting that script and event-handler markup is stripped. Add a render_views example and a fixture-based PollFeed/import test that includes a normal RSS item and a hostile HTML body.

title: Small-action flex conversion leaves action buttons off the right edge
body: .small-action is now a flex row, but the old full-width float layout was removed without a flex replacement. Direct children are flex items, so float on them is ignored, and .small-action-desc stays at the initial flex: 0 1 auto (no flex-grow / flex: 1), so it shrink-wraps to its text instead of stretching across the row. The previous padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em, which made that block full width and kept text clear of the floated 45px avatar, was replaced with padding: 0 1.5%. The action button is still only float: right (line 309). If the button is a flex item, that float is ignored and there is no margin-left: auto, so it sits in source order next to the text. If it is nested in the description, the float still applies but only to the content-sized description box, not the post row. Either way undelete/delete/edit controls that used to pin to the right edge of the small-action row now sit immediately after short action text ("closed", "deleted", and similar). Browsers that ignore the new display values still honor float: left on .topic-avatar, and with the 4em offset gone the description overlaps the icon.

title: Header panel is not pinned right under the legacy flex display values
body: .panel lost float: right and is now pinned with margin-left: auto, while .d-header .contents is turned into a flex container by the new flexbox() mixin (and .title { float: left } was removed). Auto margins absorb free space only in modern flexbox. The mixin also emits display: -webkit-box and display: -ms-flexbox before display: flex, and those are the values IE10 and old WebKit actually keep, because they do not understand display: flex. In the 2009 box model and in IE10's 2012 flexbox, margin-left: auto does not consume free space, and float does not apply to flex/box items, so the removed float is not a fallback. Login, signup, notification, and user-menu controls therefore stay in source order immediately after the logo (and topic title) instead of at the right edge of the header — the browsers those prefixes were added to support. Pin the panel with a growing sibling (-webkit-box-flex: 1 and -ms-flex: 1) or the prefixed pack/justify properties, not auto margin alone.

title: Header extra-info flex item can push controls off-screen
body: order: 2 on .extra-info-wrapper only works if that element is a flex item of .d-header .contents, which is the new flex container, alongside .panel at order 3. As a flex item it keeps the default min-width: auto, so it will not shrink below its content's minimum size, and this change never sets min-width: 0, overflow: hidden, or flex: 1. .panel's margin-left: auto only moves the controls to the right when free space remains after items are sized. A long topic title (min-content is the longest unbreakable word, or the whole title if it cannot wrap) plus the logo and the icon panel overflows the header; the auto margin collapses to zero and the notification/user controls are pushed past the viewport or the page scrolls horizontally. Docked-header titles need min-width: 0 and ellipsis, or the row cannot shrink.

title: order() mixin applies 0-based values to 1-based box-ordinal-group
body: @mixin order copies $val unchanged into -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group. Those 2009 properties are 1-based and default to 1; modern order, -ms-flex-order, and -webkit-order are 0-based and default to 0. Legacy declarations must be $val + 1 (what Autoprefixer and Bourbon emit). As written, order(0) becomes ordinal-group 0 (invalid or sorted before every default item) and order(1) ties the item with every sibling that does not set an ordinal, whose default is already 1, so those items tie or swap in old WebKit/Firefox box layout while modern browsers keep the intended order. The current call sites pass 2 and 3, which still sort after the legacy default of 1, so this header does not mis-order today, but this mixin is the shared helper the PR adds and the first use of the normal values 0 or 1 will disagree across the browsers the prefixes exist for.

title: align-items() mixin emits invalid and unmapped legacy values
body: @mixin align-items forwards $alignment unchanged to -webkit-box-align and -ms-flex-align, and also emits -ms-align-items, which is not a real property (IE10/11 only implement -ms-flex-align). The 2009/2012 properties accept start and end, not flex-start and flex-end. @include align-items(flex-start) therefore produces a working unprefixed align-items: flex-start and legacy declarations those engines drop as invalid, so items fall back to the default stretch in the browsers this mixin is meant to cover. center and baseline, the only current call sites, happen to be valid in both syntaxes, so header and badge alignment are not broken by this today. Map flex-start to start and flex-end to end on the legacy properties only, and delete the -ms-align-items line.

title: Header category bullet loses its vertical alignment offset
body: The nested &.bullet { margin-top: 5px } rule under .extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper was removed, and nothing replaces that offset. align-items: center on .d-header .contents only centers the whole extra-info wrapper against the logo and icons. The category bullet is still a float: left child of the wrapper (line 34), so its position relative to the topic title text is independent of the parent's flex alignment. line-height: 1.5 on the wrapper does not restore a 5px shift of the floated badge. The bullet in the docked header topic strip will sit about 5px higher than before relative to the title text.

title: Small-action button no longer stays on the right edge
body: .small-action is now a flex row (flexbox() and align-items(center) at the top of the rule), but its delete/recover button is still only positioned with float: right. Float does not apply to flex items, so a direct-child button (the usual Discourse small-action markup: avatar, description, then the times button) stays in source order instead of pinning to the row's right edge. Even if the button is nested in .small-action-desc, that description is a default flex item (flex: 0 1 auto, no flex-grow) and now has only padding: 0 1.5% instead of a full-width block with 4em left padding, so a float inside it aligns to the text, not the far side of the post. The X that used to sit at the right of closed/pinned/similar action rows now sits immediately beside the action text and is easy to mis-click next to the username. Browsers that ignore flexbox still honor .topic-avatar { float: left }, and the 4em padding that kept the description clear of that 45px icon is gone, so the text runs through the icon. Give the description flex: 1 and min-width: 0, put margin-left: auto and flex-shrink: 0 on the button, and stop using float for either child.

title: order mixin writes 0-based values into 1-based box-ordinal-group
body: @mixin order($val) copies $val unchanged onto -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group as well as the modern order property. The 2009 box-ordinal-group property is 1-based and defaults to 1; modern order is 0-based and defaults to 0. Those prefixed declarations therefore do not implement order (the usual fix, used by Autoprefixer, is $val + 1). order(0) emits an invalid box-ordinal-group: 0, and order(1) ties with unordered siblings instead of coming after them. The new call sites pass 2 and 3 (.d-header .panel and .extra-info-wrapper), which still sort after the default group, so those two values happen to keep the same sequence in old WebKit/Firefox — but the shared mixin is wrong for every other value and should not be merged as the compatibility layer.

title: Header panel right-alignment has no working legacy fallback
body: .d-header .panel was float: right and .d-header .title was float: left. Both floats were removed and the panel is now only pushed right with margin-left: auto, while .contents is a flex container via the new flexbox() mixin. Auto main-axis margins absorb free space only in the 2012+ flex model (display: flex / -webkit-flex / -ms-flexbox). flexbox() also emits display: -webkit-box. Browsers that honor that 2009 value and not the later display values (stock Android 4.1–4.3, older iOS) lay the header out as an old horizontal box: floats on the flex items are ignored and margin-left: auto does not push, so the logo and the icon/login cluster sit together on the left. Browsers with no flexbox at all ignore every display value in the mixin; margin-left: auto on a block with width: auto computes to 0, so title and panel stack as full-width blocks. Theme CSS that still right-aligns .panel with float stops working for the same reason. Do not emit 2009 display values unless a 2009 spacer (-webkit-box-flex) actually pins the panel, and keep the float rules as the non-flex fallback.

title: Flexbox on .small-action unpins the action button and shrink-wraps the description
body: .small-action is now a flex container (display:flex via the new flexbox mixin, align-items:center), and .small-action-desc is no longer a full-width block. Its padding changed from 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em to 0 1.5%, and it has no flex-grow, so it shrink-wraps to its text. The staff delete/recover control is positioned only by .small-action button { float: right }, which used to pin it to the right edge of that full-width row. Float does not apply to flex items, so a button that is a direct child stays in source order beside the label; a button nested in .small-action-desc only floats to the right of the shrink-wrapped description, not the post row. On short actions the control sits against or over the label instead of at the far right. Set flex: 1 and min-width: 0 on .small-action-desc so an inner float can still reach the row edge, or drop the float and push the button with margin-left: auto.

title: order() mixin is off by one for 2009 box-ordinal-group
body: order() writes $val straight through to -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group. Those 2009 properties are 1-based (initial value 1, legal values are integers >= 1); standard order is 0-based (initial value 0). The matching prefix is $val + 1. As written, order(0) emits box-ordinal-group: 0, which is invalid and dropped so the item stays in the default group; order(1) ties with unordered siblings instead of following them; a negative order, the usual way to pull an item to the front, is invalid and ignored. -ms-flex-order and -webkit-order correctly share order's numbering, so IE10 and 2012-spec WebKit are fine. Header callers pass 2 and 3, which still sort after default items in both systems, but the mixin does not implement order for any other value. Add 1 on the two box-ordinal-group declarations.

title: align-items() mixin emits an invalid property and skips old Firefox
body: align-items() copies one keyword into every prefix and emits -ms-align-items, which is not a CSS property (IE10 uses -ms-flex-align, already set above). Old Firefox, which flexbox() and inline-flex() target with display: -moz-box and display: -moz-inline-box, needs -moz-box-align, and that declaration is missing. Header .contents, .small-action, and .badge-wrapper.bullet therefore become 2009 boxes with no cross-axis alignment in that engine, so the vertical centering and bullet baseline alignment this PR adds do not apply. The 2009 and IE10 properties also do not accept modern keywords: flex-start and flex-end must be mapped to start and end for -webkit-box-align, -moz-box-align, and -ms-flex-align, while -webkit-align-items and align-items keep the modern names. center and baseline happen to be valid in all three syntaxes, so IE10 and old WebKit align for the current call sites, but the mixin is wrong for the other standard values.

title: Header panel is not pinned right in the 2009 flexbox the new mixin enables
body: .d-header .panel no longer has float: right, and .d-header .title no longer has float: left. The replacement is margin-left: auto on .panel inside a .contents flex container, plus order. Auto margins absorb free space in modern flexbox and in IE10 (-ms-flexbox), so current Chrome, Firefox, Safari 7+, and IE10 still pin the icons to the right. They do not in the 2009 model: display: -webkit-box and display: -moz-box, which the new flexbox() mixin emits, treat auto margins as 0 and only distribute space with box-flex / -webkit-box-flex, which is never set. Browsers that only understand those prefixes (Safari 6, iOS 6, Android 4.3 stock browser, Firefox 21 and older) pack the logo, topic info, and controls on the left instead of keeping the menu at the right edge. Browsers with no flexbox at all lose the float fallback and stack the logo and panel as normal blocks. Keep float: left / float: right as the non-flex fallback (a flex formatting context ignores float on the items) and drop the 2009 display values, or add a 2009 pack so those prefixes actually reproduce the header.

title: website_name bypasses the TL0 anonymous website restriction
body: website_name is derived from user_profile.website and added to the public attribute list, but it was not added to untrusted_attributes beside website. That list is what makes UserSerializer omit website, bio, and location when Guardian#restrict_user_fields? is true, i.e. an anonymous viewer looking at a trust level 0 user. Nothing AMS actually invokes applies that check to website_name: include_website_name does not call restrict_user_fields?, and it is not a valid include hook (no trailing ?), so include? defaults to true. Logged-out clients therefore receive the website host, and the path as well when the domain heuristic matches, in the user JSON. The profile template renders model.website_name whenever it is present, so the external URL is shown on the profile even though the raw website attribute is stripped. That undoes the control that kept new accounts from advertising links to anonymous visitors and API clients.

title: Same-site check shows paths for unrelated hosts and hides them for www
body: website_name appends URI#path only when it decides the website host is the same site as Discourse.current_hostname, but the comparison is incorrect. The branch at line 144 treats two hosts as the same whenever they have an equal label count greater than 2 and share every label after the first. For a forum at forum.co.uk, forum.com.au, name.github.io, or app.herokuapp.com that matches every other host under that public suffix, so http://unrelated.co.uk/secret is rendered as unrelated.co.uk/secret instead of unrelated.co.uk. The else branch only appends the path when the forum hostname string-ends with "." plus the website host, and the exact-match branch is case-sensitive while URI#host is lowercased. A forum hostname of Example.com with website http://example.com/user therefore fails every branch and the path is dropped. The usual www/apex pair also fails: forum example.com and website http://www.example.com/user displays www.example.com with no path, which is the case this change is supposed to improve. Profiles will expose paths of unrelated sites and still hide paths for the same site.

title: Profile link text stays stale after the website is edited
body: The visible label used to be a controller computed property of model.website (host taken with split, invalidated when website changed). The template now prints the server snapshot model.website_name while href stays bound to model.website. User#save sends the edited website but only copies bio_excerpt back from the PUT response, so the in-memory website_name is left unchanged. Preferences edit that same user model, and the profile reads it without another fetch, so after a website change the anchor text can still show the previous host and path while the link points at the new URL until a full reload.

title: include_website_name is never used as the serializer include hook
body: ActiveModel Serializers emits an attribute unless include_<attribute>? exists and returns false. This method is named include_website_name without the question mark, so it is never called and the website.present? guard is dead. Every UserSerializer payload therefore includes website_name, with null when the website is blank, unlike location and website which are omitted when blank. Renaming this method to include_website_name? without removing it would also override the include_website_name? defined earlier by untrusted_attributes, because the class-body method is defined later, and that would drop the anonymous TL0 check.

title: Specs never assert website_name is hidden or domain-safe
body: The TL0 anonymous example still only expects bio_raw, bio_cooked, bio_excerpt, location, website, profile_background, and card_background to be absent, so it stays green when website_name leaks. The new website_name examples only stub discourse.org, example.com, and forums.example.com against http://example.com/user. They never cover a public-suffix collision such as forum.co.uk versus http://other.co.uk/secret, or example.com versus http://www.example.com/user, which are the cases the matcher gets wrong. The added tests do not catch the bugs in this change.

title: website_name bypasses anonymous TL0 website hiding
body: website_name is computed from the profile website, but it is not subject to the same anonymous trust-level-0 restriction as website. untrusted_attributes only defines include_<attr>? for bio, location, website, and the background fields, and that guard is what stops anonymous viewers (and crawlers hitting /users/:username.json) from seeing a new user's website. The new include_website_name method is never called: this serializer, like ActiveModel Serializers 0.8, only invokes include_website_name? (question mark), which is how every other include hook in this file is named. Even if it were renamed, it only returns website.present? and never calls scope.restrict_user_fields?(object). Previously the client derived the label from model.website, so when website was omitted the globe link disappeared. Now an anonymous profile request for a TL0 user omits website but still receives website_name (host, and host+path when the comparison matches), and the template renders it. That restores the spam-visible website the restriction exists to hide. Put :website_name in untrusted_attributes and delete this include method; a later include_website_name? that only checks website.present? would override the macro and keep the leak. As written, users with a blank website also always get "website_name": null, because the include hook does not run.

title: Same-domain check mis-classifies hosts
body: website_name's host comparison does not match "same domain", so the path is added for unrelated sites and omitted for equivalent ones. Equality and ends_with? are case-sensitive, but Ruby's URI parser keeps host case and Discourse.current_hostname is lowercase: http://Example.com/user on a forum at example.com fails every branch and displays Example.com with no path. The sibling branch (same label count > 2, then compare everything after the first label) treats evil.co.uk and forum.co.uk, or a.github.io and b.github.io, as the same site because the shared suffix is a public suffix, and appends the path. The else branch's discourse_host.ends_with?("." + website_host) is true for any suffix, so a website host of com matches every *.com forum and the label becomes com plus the path. The parent check is one-way: example.com on a www.example.com forum includes the path, but http://www.example.com/user on an example.com forum does not, because the label counts differ and example.com does not end with .www.example.com. Profile labels will therefore show paths for unrelated domains and hide paths for the same site entered with different case or a www prefix.

title: Displayed website name drops non-default ports
body: website_name keeps only URI#host, which never includes the port, then optionally appends the path. The removed client label used website.split("/")[2], so http://example.com:8443/app was shown as example.com:8443. It is now shown as example.com when the host is unrelated, or example.com/app when the host comparison matches. The href is still the original URL, but the visible text identifies the default port. Any profile website on a non-default port is mislabeled, including links that are not on the forum domain.

title: Specs miss the TL0 leak and domain edge cases
body: The anonymous TL0 example still only asserts that bio, location, website, and background keys are absent, and it never sets a website. website_name is therefore free to appear in that JSON (as a host/path, or as null when the include hook does not run) without failing the suite. The new examples only stub current_hostname to discourse.org, example.com, and forums.example.com against an already-lowercased http://example.com/user, so they do not catch case-sensitive misses, port stripping, the www child case, or false matches such as another *.co.uk host or a website host of com. Those are the paths that produce the wrong label or the privacy leak, and the added specs still pass if they ship.

title: website_name bypasses TL0 anonymous website hiding
body: website_name is computed from the profile website and added as a public attribute, but it is not registered in untrusted_attributes, which is what suppresses website for anonymous viewers of trust-level 0 users. include_website_name also never calls scope.restrict_user_fields?. Previously the profile label was derived in the browser from model.website, so omitting website also omitted the label. After this change, an anonymous GET of a TL0 user still receives website_name (the hostname, and host plus path when the same-domain branch matches) even though website is withheld. That discloses the URL the serializer is supposed to hide; with the path appended, the withheld URL can be reconstructed. The profile template will render that text. The spec's TL0 example still only asserts that website is absent and never checks website_name, so the regression is untested. Adding the missing ? on the include hook is not enough: that method only checks website.present?, which is true in this case.

title: include_website_name is never called
body: ActiveModel::Serializers includes an attribute only if include_<name>? returns true. Every other hook in this serializer uses that form (include_email?, include_stats?, include_suspend_reason?, and the methods defined by untrusted_attributes). include_website_name has no question mark, so it is never invoked and the website.present? guard is dead code. website_name is therefore always serialized, including a null website_name when the user has no website or the host cannot be parsed. The omission the new method was written to provide cannot happen.

title: Same-domain check mismatches common hosts
body: The decision to append the URL path does not compare registrable domains, so it both over-matches and under-matches. The elsif treats hosts as the same site when they have the same label count greater than 2 and share every label after the first. That equates unrelated sites that only share a public suffix: a forum at forum.co.uk and a website of http://phishing.co.uk/login both reduce to co.uk, so the profile shows phishing.co.uk/login instead of phishing.co.uk. The same false positive applies to *.com.au, *.co.jp, *.blogspot.com, *.github.io, and similar. The else branch only checks discourse_host.ends_with?("." + website_host), so the path is added when the website is a parent of the forum, but not when the website is a subdomain of the forum. A forum at example.com with website http://www.example.com/docs or http://blog.example.com/users/jane displays only www.example.com or blog.example.com, which hides the path this change is meant to show. Comparison is also case-sensitive: URI#host is lowercased, but Discourse.current_hostname is not normalized here, so a mixed-case hostname fails the exact-match branch and drops the path. The new specs only cover an unrelated host, an exact match, and the website-is-parent direction; they never exercise the elsif or the www/subdomain cases.

title: Non-ASCII website URLs vanish from the profile
body: The host is parsed with URI(...).host rescue nil, and a nil host makes website_name return nil. The profile template now shows the globe and link only when model.website_name is present, with no fallback to model.website. Ruby's stdlib URI raises URI::InvalidURIError on non-ASCII input (for example http://例え.jp/path) and on URLs containing spaces; those errors are swallowed, so website_name is null and the link disappears even though website is still stored and is still serialized for viewers allowed to see it. The old client label used website.split("/")[2], which still displayed a hostname for those strings. Internationalized profile websites that previously appeared are now omitted until rewritten as ASCII or punycode.

title: Website label goes stale after website changes
body: The header used to label the site with a controller computed property that observed model.website and updated when the website changed. It now renders the server field model.website_name, which is copied onto the model only when the user payload is first loaded. User#save sends the new website but only copies bio_excerpt back from the PUT response, so it never refreshes website_name. The header lives in user.hbs outside {{outlet}} and stays visible on preferences and other child routes. After model.website changes, the anchor href is the new URL while the link text is still the previous website_name until a full reload, so the visible label can name a different host than the link destination.

title: Dark-theme notification badges put $secondary text on a near-$secondary background
body: .badge-notification sets color to $secondary (line 235, and again on &[href]) and this change sets the dark-theme background to scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%). $secondary is the page background, so that fill is only 30% of the way from the dark background toward white, while the label stays the same dark color. Even if $secondary is pure black the contrast is about 2.5:1; with a typical dark secondary such as #222 it is worse, so base notification counts are illegible in every dark theme. The old scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) stayed light in dark themes because $primary is already light there, which is why dark $secondary text was readable. new-posts/unread-posts override the background, but any badge that uses the base background does not. Keep a light pill in both themes, or switch the dark-theme text to $primary when the background is derived from $secondary.

title: Embedded-post author link lightness is swapped
body: .embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). Every other conversion in this PR keeps that lightness on $primary for light themes and uses the complement on $secondary for dark themes, which here would be 30% / 70%. This line instead emits dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). Light themes therefore render those author links much paler than before and paler than the same treatment in common/base/topic-post.scss, which correctly stayed at 30%. Dark themes get a color only 30% lighter than the dark background, so the names have poor contrast. The .arrow rule on the next line was converted correctly from 60% to 60%/40%, so this swap is not the mapping used elsewhere.

title: Mobile custom-message-length hint inverts the 70% lightness
body: .custom-message-length was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) and is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)). The light-theme branch must stay at 70%; the dark branch should be scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%). Desktop modal.scss converted the same hint correctly to 70%/30%. On mobile light themes the character-count hint becomes much darker than before and than desktop; on dark themes it becomes a light gray (70% toward white from $secondary) instead of the muted 30% color, so the hint no longer matches across viewports.

title: Mobile topic-map h3 lightness changed from 20% to 50%
body: .topic-map h3 was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%) and is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)). That changes the light-theme color and uses the wrong dark complement; the established mapping is 20% on $primary and 80% on $secondary. Desktop topic-post.scss converted the same h3 correctly to 20%/80%. Mobile topic-map headings become more washed out in light themes, and in dark themes they are a mid-gray instead of the stronger color. The h4 in this same block was already 50% and correctly stayed 50%/50%, so the h3/h4 emphasis difference is lost on mobile and mobile no longer matches desktop.

title: Group member name color changed from 30% to 50% lightness
body: .user-stream .group-member-info .name was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) and is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)). Light themes therefore render member names lighter than before. The dark complement of 30% is scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%), which is what common/base/user.scss uses for .user-small .name. The .title rule immediately below was already 50% and was correctly wrapped as 50%/50%, so names and titles that were intentionally different now share one color in both themes.

title: Mobile group member name color changed from 30% to 50% lightness
body: .user-stream .group-member-info .name was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) and is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)). That regresses the light-theme color and picks the wrong dark-theme value; a 30% source should stay 30% on $primary and use scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%), matching common/base/user.scss .user-small .name. The .title rule just below was already 50% and correctly stayed 50%/50%, so mobile group-member names and titles that used to differ now look the same.

title: Disabled composer textarea text and background collide in dark themes
body: .wmd-input:disabled now uses scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 25%) in dark themes, a dark gray only a quarter of the way from the dark background toward white. The textarea color on line 175 is darken($primary, 40%). In a dark theme $primary is the light text color, so darkening it by 40 points yields a mid-dark gray. For a typical scheme ($primary around #ddd, $secondary around #222) those two land near lightness 47% and 35%, about 1.6:1, so disabled composer text is unreadable. The previous scale-color($primary, $lightness: 75%) stayed near-white in dark themes because $primary is already light, and the same darkened text remained readable on that light field. This $secondary substitution is for muted foregrounds, not for a field whose text is a darkened $primary.

title: Category badge-notification color still scales $primary in dark themes
body: .topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification still sets color to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%) while the other 50% text colors in this same file (header cells, excerpts, education text) were wrapped as dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)). In a dark theme this still lightens the already-light $primary, so category notification counts stay brighter than the surrounding muted text instead of getting the dark-theme treatment this change applies everywhere else in the file.

title: Embedded author link lightness arguments are swapped
body: In .embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a, the color was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) and is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). Every other conversion in this PR keeps the original percentage on the light-theme branch and uses 100 minus that percentage on $secondary for the dark branch. Here those arguments are inverted, so light themes render embedded reply author names much lighter than before (70% toward white instead of 30%), and dark themes use a 30% scale of $secondary instead of the 70% complement, leaving the names too dark on a dark background. It should be dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)).

title: Mobile flag-modal hint lightness is inverted
body: .custom-message-length was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) and is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)). The light and dark branches are swapped relative to the rest of the migration. The same selector in desktop/modal.scss was converted correctly to 70% on $primary and 30% on $secondary. On mobile, light themes therefore show a much darker character-count hint than before, and dark themes get a 70% scale of $secondary (too light) instead of 30%. Swap the arguments so the light branch stays at 70%.

title: Mobile topic-map heading lightness changed from 20% to 50%
body: .topic-map h3 was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%) and is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)). The light-theme percentage was not preserved; it was replaced with the 50% value from the h4 rule immediately below. In the same block, .number and i were correctly kept at 20% / 80%, and desktop topic-post.scss keeps this heading at 20% on $primary and 80% on $secondary. Mobile topic-map headings will be much more washed out in light themes and will not match the desktop dark-theme color. Restore 20% and 80%.

title: Group member name color flattened from 30% to 50%
body: .user-stream .group-member-info .name was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) and is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)). The adjacent .title rule was already 50% and was converted correctly, so the name rule looks copied from it. Names lose the darker emphasis they had versus titles in light themes, and dark themes get a 50% scale of $secondary instead of the 70% complement of the original 30%. The light branch must stay at 30% and the dark branch must be scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%).

title: Mobile group member name color flattened from 30% to 50%
body: Mobile .user-stream .group-member-info .name was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) and is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)), the same values as the following .title rule which was already 50%. This is the same mistaken copy as in desktop/user.scss: the light-theme percentage changed, so member names no longer read darker than titles, and the dark-theme color is a 50% scale of $secondary instead of the 70% complement of 30%. Restore 30% on $primary and 70% on $secondary.

title: Default badge background no longer contrasts with its text
body: .badge-notification sets color to $secondary (and &[href] does the same) while its background was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). That complement formula is for muted text drawn on a $secondary surface. Here the text is $secondary, so the background must stay distinct from $secondary. In a dark theme $secondary is already the dark page background, and scaling it only 30% toward white produces a dark gray with the same dark text on top, so default count badges become unreadable. The old scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) stayed light in dark themes because $primary is light, which is what kept the badge readable. Do not derive this background from $secondary; keep a dark-theme fill that still contrasts with $secondary text.

title: Category badge count still scales only $primary
body: .topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification still sets color to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%) even though this file's other topic-list header, cell, icon, and excerpt colors were converted to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, ...), scale-color($secondary, ...)). In dark themes that count remains a further-lightened $primary, which is the exact failure this change is meant to fix, and it will not match the muted color now used by the surrounding list text. Convert it the same way, with 50% on $primary for light themes and 50% on $secondary for dark themes.

title: Notification badge fill no longer contrasts with its text on dark themes
body: .badge-notification keeps color: $secondary (and the same on &[href]), but its background is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). In a dark scheme $secondary is the dark page background, so the dark branch paints dark text on a background only 30% lighter than that same color, about 2:1, which is unreadable at 11px. The old scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) stayed near-white on dark themes because $primary is already light, and that light fill is what contrasted with $secondary text. The muted-text complement (lighten $secondary) is the wrong transform for a fill whose foreground is $secondary; dark themes need a light background here, or the text color has to move to $primary as well.

title: Embedded post author link lightness was inverted
body: .embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). Every other conversion in this change keeps the original lightness on $primary for light themes and uses the complement (100 minus that lightness) on $secondary for dark themes. Light themes therefore jump from a 30% lift (a readable dark gray, roughly 6:1 on white) to a 70% lift (about #bdbdbd, under 2:1), so author names in expanded and embedded posts wash out. Dark themes get only a 30% lift of the dark background instead of 70%, so those links are darker than intended. It should be dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)), matching .names a in common/base/topic-post.scss.

title: Disabled mobile composer text fails contrast on dark themes
body: .wmd-input:disabled background is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 75%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 25%)), while the .wmd-input color rule immediately below stays darken($primary, 40%). On a dark scheme $primary is light, so darkening it by 40% yields a mid-dark gray, and lightening dark $secondary by 25% is another dark gray (about 1.6:1). The previous background, scale-color($primary, $lightness: 75%), was near-white when $primary is light, so the same text was readable. Desktop already styles this disabled field with dark-light-diff($primary, $secondary, 90%, -60%) and composer text as $primary. The same dark-theme background is also applied to #reply-title:disabled at line 168, which has no theme-aware text color in this file.

title: Mobile topic-map h3 lightness changed from 20% to 50%
body: .topic-map h3 was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%) and is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)). That neither preserves the light-theme value nor applies the 80% complement used for a 20% source. Desktop .topic-map h3 in this same change was correctly converted to 20%/80%, and the mobile h4 immediately below was already 50% — this value looks copied from h4. Light-theme topic-map headings become much more muted than before and than desktop; dark themes use a 50% lift instead of 80%, so the heading is darker against the dark map background than the desktop rule.

title: Mobile flag-message length hint lightness was swapped
body: .custom-message-length was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) and is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)). The light and dark percentages are transposed. Desktop desktop/modal.scss converts the same hint to 70% on $primary and 30% on $secondary. Light themes therefore show a darker, more prominent character-count hint than before and than desktop; dark themes lighten $secondary by 70% instead of 30%, so the hint is far brighter than the muted treatment this change is supposed to produce.

title: Group member name color was given the title's lightness
body: .user-stream .group-member-info .name was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)), identical to the adjacent .title, which really was 50% and was converted correctly. Light-theme names become lighter than before and no longer darker than titles; dark themes get a 50% lift of $secondary instead of 70%, so names are darker than the complement of the original 30%. common/base/user.scss still maps the parallel .name to 30%/70%. This rule should be dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)).

title: Mobile group member name color was given the title's lightness
body: .user-stream .group-member-info .name was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) and is now 50%/50%, the same value applied to .title (which was already 50%). The conversion used everywhere else keeps the original lightness for light themes and uses 100 minus that lightness on $secondary for dark themes, so this should be 30%/70%. Light-theme group-member names become lighter and indistinguishable from titles; dark themes render them darker than the intended complement. The same mistake is in desktop/user.scss, while common/base/user.scss still uses 30%/70% for .name.

title: Category badge count still lightens $primary on dark themes
body: .topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification still sets color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%) on a transparent background. Every other positive scale-color($primary, $lightness: …) in this file was wrapped as dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, …), scale-color($secondary, …)). On a dark scheme $primary is already light, so a further 50% lightness scale pushes the count toward white instead of the muted gray used for topic-list headers and excerpts (50%/50%). Category notification counts stay brighter than the surrounding muted text this change is fixing.

title: Public group members page is silently capped at 50
body: Group.findMembers always requests limit 50 (the model default) and offset 0, and the public group members route only calls findMembers() with no pager. group/members.hbs iterates members and has no next/previous controls (those exist only on the admin group screen). GroupsController#members now applies that limit to every group and no longer returns the full list: non-automatic groups previously returned every member, and automatic groups defaulted to 200. Any group with more than 50 members now shows only the first page, with no indication the list is incomplete and no way to see the rest.

title: Page count is one too high when size is a multiple of the page size
body: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (including exactly 50, the default page size) that yields an extra page: 50 members render as 1/2, 100 as 3 pages, and so on. showingLast compares currentPage to that inflated total, so Next stays enabled on the last real page. next() then sets offset to user_count, findMembers returns an empty slice, and the admin sees a blank extra page of members.

title: Creating a group ignores the selected alias level
body: create sets name and visible but never assigns alias_level, while update in the same controller does (params[:alias_level].to_i when present). The admin form shows the alias-level combo box for new groups (it is outside the {{#if id}} block), and Group.asJSON sends alias_level on POST /admin/groups. The chosen level is discarded and the row keeps the default (0 / nobody). The client model still holds the unsaved value, so the dropdown looks correct until reload, when it reverts. The create spec only checks name stripping, so this is untested.

title: Update forces visible to false when the param is omitted
body: update sets group.visible = params[:visible] == "true" unconditionally, unlike alias_level and name which are applied only when present. Any PUT or PATCH that does not include visible=true therefore hides the group and still returns 200. resources :groups still routes PATCH to update, and the removed update_patch path used to change membership without touching visible. A leftover PATCH {changes: {add: ...}} (old admin JS or an API client) now adds nobody and silently sets visible to false. Partial updates that only rename the group do the same.

title: Adding members does not trim names and can commit a partial update
body: add_members splits usernames on commas and looks each piece up with User.find_by_username without stripping. A normal typed value such as "alice, bob" looks up " bob", matches nobody, and is skipped. Unknown names are ignored and the action still returns success, so the admin UI reloads an unchanged list and cannot tell the user who was not added. group.add on an already-persisted group inserts the join row immediately, and the loop is not wrapped in a transaction: if a later name raises (duplicate membership / RecordNotUnique), earlier adds stay committed while the request 500s. The new spec only posts already-clean comma-separated names, so none of this is covered.

title: Member removal bypasses Group#remove and 404s if already gone
body: remove_member calls group.users.delete(user_id) instead of Group#remove, which the previous membership path used. Passing an id makes ActiveRecord find the user inside the association first, so a user who is not currently a member raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound (404) rather than succeeding as a no-op. For a has_many :through with no :dependent option, delete then delete_alls join rows and skips GroupUser destroy callbacks. Adds go through group.add, which is what keeps user_count in sync (the index spec expects user_count == 1 after add). Removals can therefore leave user_count, titles, or primary-group side effects stale. The new spec only asserts users.count after a successful delete, so that drift would still pass. The admin client also has no error handler on this request, so a 404 leaves the member on screen with no message.

title: Members endpoint does not bound limit or offset
body: limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i and offset = params[:offset].to_i are passed straight into the query. There is no maximum, so anyone who can see a group (including anonymous users, for a visible automatic group such as trust_level_0) can pass limit=1000000 and force the process to load and serialize the entire membership. Negative values are also accepted: PostgreSQL rejects LIMIT -1 and OFFSET -1, so a request like limit=-1 returns 500. A zero limit is echoed back to the admin client, which then divides by zero in totalPages and renders a broken pager.

title: Out-of-range member offsets are echoed back as a blank page
body: offset is taken from params with to_i and returned unchanged in meta.offset, even when it is past the end of the list. After the admin removes the last member on a page, Group.removeMember calls findMembers without moving offset backward. The client clamp uses the pre-request user_count (still the old total), so it still requests the old offset. The server, now with fewer users, returns an empty members array and the same offset; the client stores that offset. The UI sits on a blank page (and, with the off-by-one page count, may show 2/2 for a list that now fits on one page) until the admin clicks Previous. Negative offsets are likewise not corrected and make PostgreSQL raise.

title: Enter in the group form activates Add instead of Save
body: The new form wraps the name field, the user selector, and the action buttons, but none of the buttons set type="button" and the form has no submit handler. In HTML the default button type is submit, and pressing Enter in a text field synthetically clicks the first submit button in the form. Once the group has an id, that button is Add, not Save. Enter in the name field therefore runs addMembers (re-adding whatever is still in the username box) and does not save the name, visibility, or alias level. If Ember's action helper does not preventDefault, the form also does a GET navigation of the current admin URL and discards the in-page state. On a new group the first button is Save, so Enter behaves differently before and after the first save.

title: Add and remove failures are silent and the username field is never cleared
body: addMembers posts the usernames and, on success, does not clear the field (the TODO on the previous line). removeMember and addMembers both ignore rejected promises. A 422 (automatic group), 404 (member already gone), 500 (duplicate add), or network error closes the confirm dialog or clicks Add and then changes nothing on screen, so the admin cannot tell failure from a no-op. Because the field stays filled, a second click resubmits the same names; if Group#add raises on a duplicate, that second click 500s. Newly added users are also only reloaded on the current offset, so someone who sorts onto another page never appears in the list even though the request succeeded.

title: Username box is not reset when switching groups
body: Admin group controllers are Ember singletons. setupController replaces the model and reloads members but does not clear controller.usernames. The add-members field is bound to that controller property, and addMembers never clears it after a successful add either. Navigating from group A to group B leaves A's pending (or just-added) usernames in the box; clicking Add then PUTs those names onto group B. Offset is stored on the group model so it does not leak, but usernames were left on the shared controller when membership was split out of the save payload.

title: Member reloads use the unsaved name from the text field
body: findMembers builds GET /groups/<name>/members.json from this.get('name'), and the admin name input is two-way bound to that property. Editing the name and then paging, adding, or removing a member fetches (or fails to fetch) the unsaved name before Save. Remove itself uses the numeric id and can succeed, but the follow-up findMembers 404s, so the list never refreshes and the removed user stays on screen. The name is also interpolated without encodeURIComponent, so a value that still contains spaces produces a broken URL. Pagination has already written the new offset before the request, so a failed reload leaves the page indicator and the member list out of sync.

title: Client keeps the unstripped name after create
body: create() only copies resp.basic_group.id from the POST response. The server strips the name before save and returns the stored name on BasicGroupSerializer, but the in-memory group keeps whatever was typed, including leading or trailing spaces. showGroup then navigates with that unsaved name, so a refresh looks the group up by the spaced name, misses the record named "bob", and the admin route sends the user back to the index. A later Save sends the spaced name to update, which assigns params[:name] with no strip (create strips, update does not). That either fails name-format validation or writes the spaces back over the cleaned name.

title: GET group members no longer returns a bare array
body: GroupsController#members used to render_serialized an array of GroupUserSerializer objects. It now returns {members, meta: {total, limit, offset}}. The in-repo Group.findMembers client was updated, but any other caller — plugins, API scripts, or a browser still running the previous JS that did result.map(...) — will throw because the top-level JSON is an object. The reverse is also true during a rolling deploy: new JS expects result.members and result.meta and crashes on the old array. There is no versioned path or compatibility shim, and no spec locks the new contract.

title: Overlapping member-page requests can land on the wrong page
body: next and previous write offset and call findMembers immediately, and the pager links are not disabled while a request is in flight. Two quick clicks start two GETs; findMembers applies whichever response arrives last via setProperties, including that response's offset. A slower response for the previous page overwrites a later click, so the list and the page indicator show a page the admin already left. Nothing ignores a stale response.

title: Automatic-group removal spec uses PUT, and the public members API is untested
body: The "cannot remove members from automatic groups" example calls xhr :put, :remove_member, but the route and the UI use DELETE (the success example in the same context correctly uses DELETE). Controller specs invoke the action directly, so this still hits remove_member and does not prove the DELETE route, the :group_id param, or that PUT /members is add_members. Separately, GroupsController#members was rewritten to a paginated {members, meta} payload and no spec in this pull request covers the new shape, limit/offset bounds, or the regression that non-automatic groups are no longer returned in full.

title: Public group members list is capped at 50 with no pagination
body: The public group members route now calls Group.findMembers(), which always requests limit 50 (Discourse.Group default, and GroupsController#members defaults to 50 and always applies limit/offset). The members template only renders that page and has no next/previous or load-more control, unlike the new admin UI. Non-automatic groups previously returned every member, and automatic groups previously returned up to 200. Groups larger than 50 now look complete while everyone after the first page is omitted, with no indication of the total.

title: totalPages is one too high when the member count is a multiple of the page size
body: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. That is correct only when the count is not divisible by the page size. For 50 members and limit 50 it yields 2 instead of 1; for 100 it yields 3 instead of 2. showingLast stays false on the real last page, so Next stays enabled. next() then sets offset to user_count, findMembers loads an empty page, and the UI shows a phantom last page (for example 2/2 or 3/3 with no members). Use ceil(user_count / limit), and do not treat offset == user_count as a valid page.

title: Creating a group drops the selected alias level
body: The new-group form shows the alias-level combo (it is outside the {{#if id}} block) and Group.asJSON posts alias_level, but Admin::GroupsController#create only assigns name and visible before save. alias_level stays at the database default (0 / nobody) no matter what the admin picked. The client only copies basic_group.id from the response, so the form still shows the unsaved choice until a full reload. A second Save happens to persist it via update, but leaving the page or refreshing loses the setting. Update already honors alias_level; create does not, and the create spec only checks name stripping.

title: Removing the last member on a page leaves a blank page
body: removeMember reloads via findMembers() without moving offset backward. findMembers clamps offset with the pre-delete user_count (Math.min(user_count, offset)), so an offset already on the last page is kept. The server echoes that offset even when it is past the new end (GroupsController#members does not clamp). Example: 51 members, limit 50, page 2 shows one user; after that user is removed the request still uses offset 50, the response is an empty list with total 50, and the admin stays on an empty page until they click Previous.

title: Group update treats a missing visible flag as false and ignores the old payload
body: update always does group.visible = params[:visible] == "true" and reads name/alias_level from top-level params. The previous API (and any cached admin JS, plugin, or script) sent a nested group hash and could PATCH incremental membership changes. Those requests no longer include top-level visible, so this saves visible=false and returns 200, hiding the group, while name, alias_level, and usernames in group[...] are ignored and PATCH add/remove is gone. A missing or old-format update therefore persists a visibility change the caller did not make. Reject the old shape or read both params[:visible] and params[:group], and do not default visibility to false when the key is absent.

title: GET /groups/:name/members JSON shape changed from an array to an object
body: members used to render_serialized an array of GroupUserSerializer objects, which the old client mapped directly. It now returns {members, meta: {total, limit, offset}} and always paginates (default 50). The in-repo Group model was updated, but any other client, plugin, or cached script that still expects a JSON array will throw when it calls .map (or will only see the first page if it adapts). This is an unversioned break of a public group endpoint; old and new payloads are not accepted together.

title: Add and remove member failures are silent, and the add field is never cleared
body: addMembers() ignores the promise from model.addMembers(), and removeMember() ignores removeMember()'s promise. There is no error callback, so a 422, 500, or network failure closes the dialog or clicks Add and leaves the list unchanged with no alert. On success the username field is not cleared (the TODO on the previous line), and findMembers() only reloads the current offset, so a new user who sorts onto another page never appears. The server also returns 200 when every username is unknown (add_members skips failed lookups and still saves), so a typo is indistinguishable from success. Admins cannot tell whether membership changed.

title: Member page changes race and can display the wrong page
body: next and previous update group.offset and call findMembers() with no in-flight guard, and the links stay clickable until the response updates showingFirst/showingLast. Two quick clicks issue overlapping requests. findMembers() writes members, user_count, and offset from whichever response settles last, not from the latest offset. A slower request for an earlier page can overwrite a later one, so the pager and the member list disagree until another navigation. The same pattern applies to previous().

title: Update does not strip group names, and create does not sync the stripped name back
body: create saves (params[:name] || '').strip, but the client only applies resp.basic_group.id and keeps the raw name (including leading/trailing spaces). update then does group.name = params[:name] with no strip. The admin list therefore shows the unstripped name after create. The next Save posts that raw name; the placeholder says names cannot contain spaces, so validation fails and the rest of the edit is discarded, or a spaced name is stored even though create had already normalized it. Apply the serialized name after create and strip on update the same way as create.

title: New members pagination and admin member routes are untested at the HTTP layer
body: GroupsController#members changed from a full (or 200-row) array to a paginated {members, meta} object, and there is no spec for the default limit, offset, total, or response shape, so the public 50-member truncation would not fail CI. Admin add_members/remove_member specs call the actions directly with group_id and never go through config/routes.rb. A member route that supplies :id instead of :group_id, or a path that does not match /admin/groups/:id/members, would 400/404 in the browser while these specs stay green. The automatic remove example even uses xhr :put against an action routed as DELETE.

title: Add/remove members require group_id the route never sets
body: add_members and remove_member (line 85) load the group with params.require(:group_id). The new routes in config/routes.rb are bare put/delete "members" inside resources :groups, which are member routes on /admin/groups/:id/members. That segment is params[:id], the same param this controller already uses for update and destroy. Elsewhere in routes.rb a non-default name is written into the path (delete "groups/:group_id"); these member routes do not do that, so group_id is never populated. The Ember client only interpolates the id into the path and posts usernames or user_id, not group_id. require(:group_id) raises ParameterMissing and every add or remove returns 400. Controller specs stay green because they pass group_id directly and never hit the router. Read params[:id], matching update/destroy.

title: Members action requires group_id but the route sets id
body: The rewritten members action still calls find_group(:group_id), and find_group does params.require on that key. The route is get "members" inside resources :groups, i.e. GET /groups/:id/members, so the group name arrives in params[:id]. show in this same controller correctly uses find_group(:id); posts and counts have the same mismatch. Group#findMembers requests /groups/:name/members.json and only sends limit and offset, not group_id. The action 400s before it can return the new members/meta payload, so both the admin member list and the public members page stay empty. Use find_group(:id).

title: remove_member passes an integer to association delete
body: remove_member calls group.users.delete(user_id) with a raw integer. On Rails 4, CollectionAssociation#delete type-checks its arguments and raises ActiveRecord::AssociationTypeMismatch (User expected, got Fixnum) instead of deleting the group_users join row. Once the group_id param bug is fixed, removing a member still 500s and the user stays in the group. The new spec expects 200 and a user count of 0, so it fails if run. Load the user and call group.remove(user), which is what the previous membership update path used, or pass a User record to delete.

title: Public members page cannot show past the first 50 users
body: The public members route only calls model.findMembers() once, and Group#findMembers always sends limit 50 (the model default). groups/members.hbs has no pager and does not show the new meta.total. GroupsController#members now applies that limit to every group. Previously non-automatic groups returned every member and automatic groups defaulted to 200. Anyone opening a group with more than 50 members sees a silently truncated list and has no way to load the rest. The admin screen has next/previous; this page does not. Either paginate here or request a limit large enough to preserve the old full list.

title: totalPages is one too high when count divides evenly
body: totalPages is Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is a positive multiple of limit (50, 100, and so on) that is an extra page: 50 members with limit 50 displays 1/2 and leaves Next enabled. next() then sets offset to user_count, findMembers returns no rows, and the admin lands on a blank member page. Math.ceil(user_count / limit) is the right count (0 stays 0).

title: Create ignores alias_level the form submits
body: create sets name and visible but never alias_level. The new-group form shows the alias-level combo outside the id check, and Group#asJSON posts alias_level on create. The column stays at the default 0 (nobody can mention the group). The client only copies resp.basic_group.id back onto the model, so the UI keeps the level the admin chose and then transitions to the group page. They have no reason to hit Save again; after a reload the mention permission has reverted. update does persist alias_level. The create spec only checks that the name is stripped.

title: Member reloads use the unsaved group name
body: findMembers requests /groups/ plus this.get('name') plus /members.json. In the admin form the name text field is two-way bound to that same property, and pagination, add, and remove all call findMembers before Save. An edited but unsaved name is sent to the server. If it matches no group the reload 404s and the member list fails with no error UI (next/previous have already moved offset). If it matches a different group, that group's members are shown on this group's screen while add/remove still target this group's numeric id, so the admin can change the wrong memberships. Fetch with the persisted name, not the in-progress field.

title: Enter in the group form activates Add instead of Save
body: The admin group editor is now wrapped in a form, but Add, Save, and Delete are button elements with no type attribute, so they default to submit. On an existing non-automatic group the first submit button is Add. Pressing Enter in the name field (or the user selector) activates Add rather than Save: members are added, or addMembers returns immediately because the username box is empty, and the name, visibility, and alias level are not saved. Delete is also a submit button. Set type="button" on these action buttons. If the action helper does not preventDefault, the browser will also GET-submit the form to the current URL and reload the page, dropping unsaved edits.

title: Spaced usernames are skipped and add still succeeds
body: add_members splits the usernames string on commas and calls User.find_by_username on each token without stripping. A space after a comma, which is normal when typing into the selector ("alice, bob"), does not match username_lower, so that user is not added. Unknown names are skipped the same way. If group.save then succeeds, the action still renders success_json even when nobody was added. The admin UI reloads the current page and does not clear the input (the controller has a TODO for that), so the add looks successful. Strip each username and report names that did not match instead of returning success unconditionally.

title: Add/remove failures are silent and desync the pager
body: addMembers and removeMember (line 56) ignore the promises returned by the model. Those model methods only call findMembers on success and have no failure path. save and destroy in this same controller show a bootbox alert. A 400, 422 from an automatic group, or 500 therefore leaves the list unchanged with no message, so the admin cannot tell a failure from a no-op. next and previous also write offset before findMembers resolves, so a failed page load leaves the pager on a page whose members were never fetched. Overlapping findMembers responses are applied unconditionally, so a slower earlier page can overwrite a newer one.

title: Members limit and offset are unbounded
body: limit and offset come from the query string with only to_i and no range check. The endpoint is available to anyone who can see the group. limit=1000000 loads and serializes every member of a large automatic group such as trust_level_0 in one response, which is a straightforward DoS. offset=-1 or limit=-1 makes PostgreSQL reject the statement (OFFSET/LIMIT must not be negative) and the action returns 500. Clamp offset to >= 0 and cap limit to a small maximum; the UI only requests 50.

title: Members JSON shape and default size break existing clients
body: GET /groups/:name/members.json used to return a top-level JSON array of users (the previous client called result.map on it). It now returns an object with members and meta. When limit is omitted the action also returns at most 50 rows instead of the full roster for custom groups or the previous default of 200 for automatic groups. In-repo callers in this PR were updated, but external API clients, scripts, and plugins that still expect an array will throw or stop listing members, and callers that omitted limit silently lose everyone past 50. There is no version flag or fallback to the old shape.

title: Membership specs bypass routing and skip the public members API
body: The new add_members and remove_member examples invoke the actions with group_id in the params hash. That never loads config/routes.rb, so they pass even when PUT/DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members does not set group_id, which is the URL the Ember client uses. The automatic-group remove example uses xhr :put while the route is DELETE. Nothing in this PR covers GroupsController#members: the switch from a JSON array to {members, meta}, the new default limit of 50, or invalid limit/offset. Those are the paths the admin pager and the public members page depend on, and they can be broken while this spec stays green.

title: Fallback bundles are not loaded on the translation path
body: I18n::Backend::Fallbacks resolves SiteSetting.default_locale and :en inside the backend, but the on-demand loader only runs for the active locale. I18n.translate (line 68) calls load_locale(config.locale) and never consults I18n.fallbacks, and backend fallback lookups do not go back through I18n.translate, so those YAML files stay unloaded. The new ensure_loaded! helper is only called from ApplicationController#set_locale. Mailers, jobs, rake tasks, console use, and I18n.with_locale / I18n.t(locale:) that never hit that filter therefore miss fallback strings and return a missing-translation result even when the site locale or English has the key. Argument-less lookups then store that failure in the process-wide LRU (line 74). Hot keys are not evicted, so one early lookup permanently poisons later requests in the same process even after ensure_loaded! has loaded the files.

title: Translation cache key ignores dynamic fallback locale
body: FallbackLocaleList#[] re-reads SiteSetting.default_locale on every lookup so the fallback language can change without a restart, but the accelerator cache key is only "#{key}#{config.locale}#{backend.object_id}". Nothing clears @cache when the site locale changes. Argument-less I18n.t results — including strings taken from the previous default locale and cached missing-translation placeholders — remain in the 300-entry LRU, and frequently used keys are never evicted. After an admin changes default_locale, users whose own locale lacks those keys keep seeing the old fallback language until the process is restarted. Interpolated calls skip the cache, so the same copy can also disagree with itself depending on whether it has interpolations.

title: No tests for fallback order, loading, or cache interaction
body: The new user-locale → SiteSetting.default_locale → :en chain, ensure_loaded!, and the accelerator cache have no coverage. Fallbacks are now installed in every environment (previously only production/profile), so tests that expected a missing non-English key to raise or return a missing-translation string will silently get English instead, and the job/mailer load gap and stale-cache-after-default-locale-change bugs above would not be caught. A controller example and a non-request I18n.t (after setting a non-English locale whose fallback files are not yet loaded) need to assert both the fallback order and that a miss is not cached before the fallback bundles are loaded.

title: Fallback locale YAML is never loaded outside set_locale
body: The new fallback chain (requested locale, then SiteSetting.default_locale, then :en) only works if those locale files have been loaded into the backend. On-demand loading still only calls load_locale for I18n.config.locale inside I18n.translate, and the new I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! is invoked only from ApplicationController#set_locale. Processes that never hit that filter — Sidekiq workers, mailers, rake tasks, the console — therefore never load the site-default or English YAML. A job that does I18n.with_locale(user.effective_locale) and translates will load only that user's locale; missing keys will not fall back to the site language or English even though the yml files define them. Calls with an explicit locale: option have the same gap, because translate preloads config.locale rather than the locale actually being resolved. Argument-less I18n.t results are also frozen into the 300-entry LRU. The default i18n missing-translation handler returns a "translation missing: ..." string, so one early lookup in a job process caches that string and later lookups never retry after a locale file is loaded. Fallback loading has to happen on the translate path for the locale being resolved, not only in the controller filter.

title: Translation LRU key ignores the fallback locale
body: Argument-less translations are cached under "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}" only.
