body: ECDSAAlgorithmTest imports org.keycloak.crypto.ECDSAAlgorithm and org.keycloak.crypto.JavaAlgorithm and calls ECDSAAlgorithm.getSignatureLength() and JavaAlgorithm.getJavaAlgorithm(). Those types live in keycloak-server-spi, not in keycloak-core. authz/client/pom.xml only depends on keycloak-core (plus logging, httpclient, and jackson); this PR adds junit and hamcrest but not keycloak-server-spi. Maven test-compile of keycloak-authz-client-tests will fail with cannot find symbol, so the only test of the new ECDSA ASN.1 conversion never runs. Add a test-scoped dependency on the module that contains org.keycloak.crypto, or stop referencing those types and hardcode the JCA algorithm names and signature lengths.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns the JDK keystore provider
body: CryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider() is specified to return the BouncyCastle or BCFIPS Provider. AuthzClientCryptoProvider instead returns KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider(), which is the platform keystore provider (SUN for the Java 8 default JKS keystore, and typically SUN for the Java 9+ default PKCS12 keystore). That provider is not BC and does not implement ECDSA (SHA256withECDSA and the other SHA*withECDSA algorithms are on SunEC). Callers that pass this object to Signature.getInstance or Cipher.getInstance, or that treat a non-null result as "BC is available" / compare the name to BC or BCFIPS, will throw NoSuchAlgorithmException or take a non-BC path. WildFlyElytronProvider returns null for the same method to mean there is no BC; a non-null wrong provider bypasses those null checks. Return null or throw; do not hand back the keystore provider.

title: order() is a new abstract method and breaks existing implementations
body: order() was added to the public CryptoProvider interface with no default body. In-tree Default, Elytron, and FIPS implementations were updated, but any already-compiled implementor (a downstream or older crypto provider jar, or a test double) has no order() method. CryptoIntegration.detectProvider loads every provider via ServiceLoader and then calls CryptoProvider::order. That invocation throws AbstractMethodError and aborts detection entirely, so init fails even if a valid newer provider is also on the classpath. Source compatibility for external implementors is broken as well. Give the method a default that is higher than AuthzClientCryptoProvider's 100 (for example default int order() { return 200; }) so existing providers still outrank the authz-client stub and do not crash provider detection.

title: ES384/ES512 tests use a P-256 key and never check DER with JCA
body: The suite builds one KeyPair with KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair() and no ECGenParameterSpec, so the JDK default curve (secp256r1) is used for testES256, testES384, and testES512. ES384 and ES512 therefore never produce 48-byte or 66-byte R and S values; those components stay about 32 bytes and are only zero-padded to 96 or 132. Every real ES512 DER signature uses a long-form SEQUENCE length (content longer than 127 bytes), so ASN1Encoder.writeLength and ASN1Decoder.readLength's long-form path is never executed. The only assertion is that asn1derToConcatenatedRS and concatenatedRSToASN1DER round-trip to each other. The DER from concatenatedRSToASN1DER is not passed to Signature.verify and is not compared to the original JCA signature, so an encoder that this decoder accepts but JCA or another JOSE stack rejects still passes, including for ES256. Initialize P-256, P-384, and P-521 for the matching algorithms and verify the converted DER with Signature.verify.

title: AuthzClient.create permanently latches the process-wide crypto provider
body: AuthzClient.create(Configuration) now calls CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader()) before building the client. init only runs detection while the static cryptoProvider field is null; later calls, including the server's own init, are ignored. Detection uses ServiceLoader on that classloader only, which does not see providers visible solely on a child or thread-context classloader. If this runs first in a JVM whose view of the classpath is the authz-client jar (AuthzClientCryptoProvider, order 100) without Default, Elytron, or FIPS (order 200), the stub is installed for the whole process and cannot be replaced. The stub throws UnsupportedOperationException for getSignature, getPemUtils, ciphers, certificate utilities, and truststore wrapping, so a later embedded server or in-process testsuite that expected its own CryptoProvider fails on ordinary crypto calls. Do not latch a lower-priority provider forever: also search the context classloader, and allow a later init to replace the current provider when a higher-order one is found.

title: Role-mapping checks drop manage-clients and master admins
body: canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles, and canMapClientScopeRoles only call hasPermission. They never short-circuit on root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS), unlike canManage(ClientModel). hasPermission then returns false immediately when the caller is not in the same realm. ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 installs MgmtPermissionsV2 for every realm, so this replaces the V1 evaluator: realm admins with manage-clients, and master-realm admins, can no longer map client roles, add composites, or map client-scope roles unless a fine-grained permission also grants it. V1 kept that role check inside its permission helper before any same-realm test. The new tests only use myadmin with no admin role, so they do not catch the regression. map-roles-client-scope has no test at all.

title: Null all-clients resource NPEs permission checks
body: If no per-client resource exists, hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) loads the type resource with getResourceTypeResource and immediately calls PolicyStore.findByResource(server, resource). getResourceTypeResource returns null when the Clients resource was never created, was deleted, or the schema is not supported for that server (admin permissions disabled while the admin-permissions client pointer remains). findByResource dereferences the resource, so the call throws NullPointerException. The no-argument hasPermission null-checks its lookup; this overload does not. View, manage, configure, and map-roles checks that reach this fallback then 500 instead of denying, for any caller who did not already pass an admin-role short-circuit.

title: Existing admin-permissions clients never get the Clients schema
body: init returns as soon as realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is non-null, and nothing in this change syncs an already created resource server. The Clients resource and the new scopes configure, map-roles-client-scope, and map-roles-composite are only inserted when that client is first created. Realms that already enabled fine-grained admin permissions for Users keep the old server: the Clients resource is missing and getScope fails with "Scope [configure] does not exist" (and the same for the other new scope names) when a client permission is created. Evaluation then falls through to a null type resource and can 500. Only freshly initialized realms work.

title: Client deletion throws when both FGAP features are enabled
body: The removal listener is gated on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ, but AdminPermissions.management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, even if the V1 feature is also on. ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled always throws UnsupportedOperationException. With both features enabled, ClientRemovedEvent calls that method and the exception propagates from the provider listener, failing or rolling back client deletion. Role and group removal still use the V1 evaluators, so only clients are broken. The listener must not call the V2 implementation, or setPermissionsEnabled must be a no-op under V2.

title: Runtime client permission methods throw instead of deciding
body: Turning on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 makes ClientPermissionsV2 the client evaluator for every realm, not only realms that opted into admin permissions. canExchangeTo, isPermissionsEnabled, and getPermissions unconditionally throw UnsupportedOperationException. canExchangeTo is the token-exchange authorization check (authorized client plus subject token) and used to return a boolean, including role-based allow or deny; a throw is a 500, not a deny. isPermissionsEnabled and getPermissions are still the client management-permissions API and are reachable from any parent method that was not overridden, so those calls 500 as well. Unimplemented V2 behavior needs to fail closed or keep the manage-clients role path, not throw. getEvaluationContext in this class is unused, so the exchange path was left unfinished.

title: Per-client resources are stored with no type
body: getOrCreateResource now resolves Clients, then resourceStore.create plus updateScopes, but never setType(resourceType). The all-clients resource created in init does set type to Clients. ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission discovers candidates only via findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE). Individual grants therefore create resources that name lookup can see (hasPermission uses findByName) but the type query cannot. Any admin listing or filter that uses getClientsWithPermission omits every specifically permitted client, while a direct check of that same client can still succeed.

title: All-clients permission is returned as the id Clients
body: getClientsWithPermission adds resource.getName() for every Clients-typed resource whose evaluation grants the scope. The schema resource created for "all clients" is named Clients and has that type, so a type-level grant puts the literal string Clients into the set. That is not a client UUID. Callers that keep clients where granted.contains(client.getId()) will not treat the grant as access to every client, and nothing expands the type resource into real client ids. There is no global canMapRoles() to compensate, so an all-clients map-roles or view permission does not show those clients in filters that rely on this method.

title: Client resources are returned with a null display name
body: getResourceName only special-cases Users: the type resource becomes "All users" and other names are resolved to usernames, throwing ModelIllegalStateException if the user is gone. Client resources are stored under the internal client id (resolveClient returns client.getId()) and are created without a display name, so they hit return resource.getDisplayName() and come back null. The all-clients resource is named Clients and is not labeled "All clients". Permission listings for the new type show blank names, and a deleted client does not surface the missing-object error used for users.

title: V2 client grants are not removed when the client is deleted
body: Per-client FGAP resources are named with the client id and are not foreign-keyed to the client, so deleting the client does not cascade them. The only hook added here is the ClientRemovedEvent listener, and the new feature gate skips that hook unless ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) is enabled. In the V2-only setup this work targets, client deletion leaves the admin-permissions resource and its scope permissions in place. Listings keep a grant for a client that no longer exists, and getResourceName returns null for it. setPermissionsEnabled cannot be used to clean this up because the V2 implementation throws.

title: Client tests rotate myclient's secret and do not restore it
body: testConfigureOnlyOneClient calls generateNewSecret and invalidateRotatedSecret on myclient and never puts the original secret back. realmAdminClient is injected for the class as client myclient; the sibling impersonation helper logs in with client secret mysecret. After rotation, refresh for that confidential client fails, so later methods in this class can 401 once the access token is no longer reused. testManageOnlyOneClient also renames myclient and removeDefaultClientScope without restoring either, and AfterEach only deletes scope permissions, so later methods share that leaked client state.

title: requireView javadoc says a void method returns true
body: The new javadoc on requireView says it returns true if canView() returns true, but the method is void and throws ForbiddenException when the check fails, same as requireManage. requireViewClientScopes (line 102) has the same error: it says it returns true if canViewClientScopes() returns true. Implementors reading only the contract will treat these as predicates instead of enforcing checks.

title: All-clients permissions ignored once any per-client resource exists
body: ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String) evaluates the schema-level "Clients" resource only when resourceStore.findByName finds no resource named with that client's internal id. As soon as any object-level permission has created that resource, the method evaluates only the object resource and never loads all-clients policies. Those policies are stored on the separate "Clients" resource, and evaluatePermission is invoked with a ResourcePermission for only one resource, so they are not applied implicitly. Consequence: a manage/view/map-roles grant on all clients stops applying to a client as soon as anyone has any object-level permission on it (even a different scope or a different user). For example, an admin with manage-all loses manage, configure, and view on client X after another user is granted view on X. The same helper backs canManage, canConfigure, canView, canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles, and canMapClientScopeRoles, and the new javadoc says those checks must also honor the all-clients scope. PermissionClientTest never combines an all-clients permission with an object-level permission on the same client, so this is untested.

title: Map-roles checks ignore manage-clients and cross-realm admins
body: canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles, and canMapClientScopeRoles only call hasPermission. Unlike canManage(ClientModel) in the same class, they never short-circuit on root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS). hasPermission then returns false immediately when root.isAdminSameRealm() is false, before any policy evaluation. ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 makes AdminPermissions.evaluator/management always return MgmtPermissionsV2, so this class handles every admin request while the feature is on. Realm-management users who only have manage-clients, and master-realm admins managing another realm, are therefore denied mapping that client's roles, adding composite client roles, and mapping client-scope roles unless a fine-grained policy also exists. Those are ordinary admin operations. Callers that enforce these methods directly (requireMapRoles / requireMapCompositeRoles / requireMapClientScopeRoles) will return 403. The new tests only use myadmin, who has no manage-clients role, so the regression is not covered.

title: canExchangeTo throws instead of returning a decision
body: canExchangeTo unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException. Token exchange decides whether the calling client may exchange for another client by invoking clients().canExchangeTo, and AdminPermissions.management returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, including for realms that have not turned on the new admin-permissions schema. The permission check therefore aborts the grant with an exception (typically a 500) instead of the boolean V1 returned. getEvaluationContext is implemented and unused, so the previous evaluation path was not wired up. A permission-check method must return false or delegate to super.canExchangeTo; it must not throw.

title: Client removal still calls V2 setPermissionsEnabled, which throws
body: ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled, isPermissionsEnabled, getPermissions, resource, and the Policy accessors all throw UnsupportedOperationException ("Not supported in V2"). This PR overrides MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() to return that class, and AdminPermissions.management prefers V2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled. The removal listener still calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) on ClientRemovedEvent when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is also enabled (the new guard only checks the V1 feature). Deleting a client then fails the transaction with UnsupportedOperationException instead of removing the client. If only V2 is enabled, the guard skips the listener and nothing deletes the per-client authorization resources this PR creates on the admin-permissions client (named by client id). Deleted clients leave orphaned resources and policies behind. setPermissionsEnabled should be a no-op under V2, and client removal should delete those V2 resources explicitly.

title: getClientsWithPermission does not return client ids
body: getClientsWithPermission is the allowlist API callers use to filter clients by scope. It adds resource.getName() for every type "Clients" resource whose evaluation grants the scope. The schema-level resource created in AdminPermissionsSchema.init is named "Clients", so an all-clients grant inserts the literal string "Clients" rather than every client id. Callers comparing the set to client.getId() or client.getClientId() will not treat that as access to all clients, and a clientId of "Clients" could be confused with the type resource. Object-level resources are named with the internal client id (resolveClient returns client.getId()), which already differs from V1, where this method returned clientId strings. In addition, AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource (line 104) creates those resources with create/updateScopes and never setType, so findByType(CLIENTS) will not see them unless some other layer sets the type. Object-level grants are then omitted entirely. The method cannot be used to build a correct client allowlist.

title: Existing admin-permissions clients never gain Clients scopes
body: init returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already non-null. Scopes and type-level resources are created only on that path, from SCHEMA. This change adds the Clients resource type and the configure, map-roles-client-scope, and map-roles-composite scopes, but does not reconcile a client that was initialized when the schema contained only Users. On those realms the Clients resource and new scopes are never created. Creating a client permission then fails in getScope with ModelValidationException ("Scope [configure] does not exist") or in getOrCreateResource with ModelException ("No scopes found") when a required scope row is missing. Fresh enables work; any realm that already turned admin permissions on does not.

title: getResourceName does not resolve client resources
body: getResourceName special-cases Users: the type resource becomes "All users" and an object resource is resolved from the user id stored in resource.getName() to a username. There is no Clients branch. Client object resources are created with the internal client id as the name and no display name (getOrCreateResource only sets name, owner, and scopes). For a Clients policy the method falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is null, instead of "All clients" or the clientId. Permission APIs that show which resource a policy applies to will return a null name for every client permission, and any caller that assumes a non-null display string can NPE. A missing client should be handled the same way a missing user is (ModelIllegalStateException), not silently omitted.

title: Missing Clients type resource NPEs the permission check
body: When no per-client resource exists, hasPermission loads the type resource and immediately calls PolicyStore.findByResource(server, resource) and later resource.getScopes() with no null check. getResourceTypeResource returns null if the Clients resource was never created (init bails out when the admin-permissions client already exists) or if supportsAuthorizationSchema is false. findByResource dereferences resource.getId() and the permission check throws NullPointerException instead of returning false. An admin API call that should be denied becomes a 500. The same null resource is then passed to ResourcePermission if the isEmpty check were skipped.

title: requireView javadoc describes a boolean return
body: The javadoc added on requireView says it "Returns true if canView() returns true", and requireViewClientScopes says it "Returns true if canViewClientScopes() returns true". Both methods are void. They throw ForbiddenException when the corresponding can* check is false; they do not return a boolean. The comments document the wrong contract for every implementor of ClientPermissionEvaluator.

title: All-clients view bypasses an explicit per-client view deny
body: ClientPermissionsV2.canView(ClientModel) returns true as soon as canView() is true. canView() is true not only for the view-clients/manage-clients admin roles, but also when a fine-grained permission grants the view scope on the Clients resource type (all clients). The per-client check is then skipped, so a Logic.NEGATIVE view permission for that same caller on one client is never evaluated. requireView(client) and every admin operation gated on canView(client) (client representation, protocol mappers, client scopes) still succeed for the client that was explicitly denied. Negative permissions are already part of this model (user FGAP tests use Logic.NEGATIVE on the same permission API). Short-circuit only on the admin-role helper (canViewClientDefault), then evaluate the per-client decision so an explicit deny overrides all-clients view. The new client tests never create a negative permission, so this bypass is untested.

title: A per-client resource suppresses all-clients permissions
body: hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) loads the authorization resource named with the client id and, if that row exists, evaluates only that resource. The Clients type resource (all clients) is consulted only when no per-client resource exists. A per-client resource is created for any permission that targets that client, including a permission for a different user or a different scope. An administrator granted manage, configure, view, or map-roles on all clients then loses that grant on the client, because their all-clients policy is attached to the type resource and is never evaluated; a per-client grant of scope A also hides an all-clients grant of scope B. Evaluate both resources, and let a per-client policy override all-clients only for the scopes that policy actually covers. PermissionClientTest only covers a lone per-client grant or a lone all-clients grant, never both.

title: Existing admin-permissions clients never receive the Clients schema
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already set, and that is the only place schema scopes and the per-type all-resource records are created. This change adds the Clients resource type and the configure, map-roles-client-scope, and map-roles-composite scopes, but realms that already enabled admin permissions V2 already have that client (created earlier with only Users). After upgrade those scopes and the Clients resource are never inserted, so creating a Clients permission fails with a missing-scope validation error and all-clients evaluation cannot find the type resource. init must add any schema scopes and resource types that are not already present instead of treating a non-null admin-permissions client as fully initialized.

title: Client deletion throws when v1 and v2 admin-permission features are both enabled
body: The removal listener runs when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (v1) is enabled and then calls management().clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException. The two flags are independent, so enabling v2 does not turn v1 off. Deleting a client then throws from the provider event listener and can roll back the removal. Guard the v1 cleanup with the same condition management() uses (v1 evaluator actually selected), or make the v2 removal path a no-op instead of throwing. Role and group removal in this listener call management() as well; clients() is the override that now throws.

title: Null Clients type resource NPEs permission checks
body: When no per-client authorization resource exists, hasPermission sets resource from AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource and immediately calls PolicyStore.findByResource(server, resource) with no null check. getResourceTypeResource returns null if the Clients type resource was never created (init skips existing admin-permissions clients) or was deleted. findByResource then dereferences null and the admin call fails with 500 instead of denying the permission. Treat a null type resource as no all-clients permission.

title: Client permission resources are returned with a null display name
body: getResourceName resolves Users policies to "All users" or the username, but has no Clients branch and falls through to resource.getDisplayName(). Per-client resources are stored with the client UUID as the name and no display name, and the all-clients resource is stored as name "Clients" without a display name, so the admin permissions API returns null. The console cannot show which client a permission applies to, unlike users in the same API. Resolve the stored id to the clientId, return a label such as "All clients" for the type resource, and fail clearly if the client no longer exists, matching the user path.

title: canExchangeTo throws instead of returning an authorization decision
body: ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException. AdminPermissions.evaluator installs this class whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, and token exchange calls clients().canExchangeTo to decide whether the caller may exchange into another client's audience. That call now fails the token request with an unhandled server error instead of allow or deny. The same class throws from isPermissionsEnabled, getPermissions, and setPermissionsEnabled; this PR only guards the removal listener, and only behind the v1 feature flag. A boolean permission check must not throw — return false until exchange is actually implemented (getEvaluationContext in this class is unused). Otherwise enabling v2 breaks token exchange and any client management-permissions endpoint that still reaches these methods.

title: Client tests rotate myclient's secret and leave realm mutations behind
body: testConfigureOnlyOneClient calls generateNewSecret and invalidateRotatedSecret on myclient and never restores the original secret. realmAdminClient is injected as client myclient using the secret from the realm config, and AbstractPermissionTest's @InjectRealm does not request a per-method lifecycle, so the realm is shared by every method in the class. The next test that must obtain a token authenticates with a secret that no longer exists and fails. The same class also leaves other shared state: testManageOnlyOneClient renames myclient and moves a default client scope to optional, and testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient creates myclient-role and myclient-subRole with no cleanup. AfterEach only deletes scope permissions. Restore the secret, name, and scopes, and delete the roles, or results depend on test order.

title: requireView javadoc claims a boolean result for void methods
body: requireView and requireViewClientScopes are void and throw ForbiddenException when the matching can* check is false, but the new javadoc says each "Returns true if canView()/canViewClientScopes() returns true". That describes the boolean methods, not these require* methods. Neighboring require* docs correctly say they throw ForbiddenException. Callers reading the interface will think these methods return a decision instead of aborting the request.

title: Default update-strategy tests never enable rolling-updates
body: createInitialDeployment returns immediately when the update strategy is null, and the new code that sets spec.features.enabled to rolling-updates runs only for a non-null strategy. The parameterized image-change and cache-max-count tests call this helper with both null (the default strategy) and Recreate. The operator guide in this PR says that while the feature is preview it must be enabled or the operator fails, including for the default strategy that still decides rolling vs recreate on image changes. The default-strategy cases therefore never put rolling-updates on the Keycloak CR, which is the configuration users are told to set. Those tests either fail when the compatibility command rejects a feature-disabled server, or they pass only because operator/scripts/Dockerfile-custom-image now bakes the feature into the test image and never cover the documented CR path. Enable the feature for every deployment this helper builds, before the null return. setEnabledFeatures(List.of(...)) also replaces any features already on the CR instead of appending rolling-updates, so a deployment that already enables features loses them in the Recreate cases.

title: Exit code 4 changed meaning from recreate to feature-disabled
body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was 4 and is now 3, and 4 is reused as FEATURE_DISABLED. The update-compatibility check exit code is the public contract the guide tells automation to branch on. After this change an incompatible deployment exits 3 instead of 4, and exit 4 means the preview feature is off and no compatibility decision was made. Callers that observed the previous implementation (exit 4 = shut the deployment down and recreate) will treat a disabled feature as recreate-required, and will not treat a real incompatibility (now exit 3) as recreate-required, which can allow a rolling update the tool rejected or cause a full shutdown when the user only needed to enable the feature. The guide already listed 3 for recreate before this PR, so the old constant disagreed with the guide; if that text is the shipped contract, aligning the constant is right, but nothing in this PR updates operator production code that may still compare the job status to a literal 4. UpdateCommandDistTest does not assert either code, so CI will not catch a regression to the old value.

title: New and renumbered compatibility exit codes are not asserted
body: The distribution tests never check the exit codes this PR defines. testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts that stderr contains the disabled-feature message, and it only launches the metadata subcommand; it does not assert exit code 4, and there is no equivalent case for check. testWrongVersions only asserts the incompatibility error text after RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE moved from 4 to 3, so a build that still exits 4 (now the feature-disabled code) would still pass. The guide tells automation to branch on these codes (0 rolling, 3 recreate, 4 feature disabled). Assert the process exit code for both subcommands when rolling-updates is off, and assert exit code 3 when the stored versions are incompatible.

title: Documented --features flag replaces other enabled features
body: The updatecompatibility doc macro now renders every example as bin/kc.sh update-compatibility <args> --features=rolling-updates. Keycloak gives CLI arguments precedence over KC_FEATURES and keycloak.conf, and features is a single list-valued option, not a set merged across sources. Copying the documented command therefore replaces any other explicitly enabled features with only rolling-updates. The same guide says every option from the real deployment must be present and that omitting options produces an incorrect rolling-versus-recreate outcome. The examples should tell users to add rolling-updates to their existing enabled-feature list rather than hard-coding a replacement --features value.

title: Default update-strategy tests never enable rolling-updates
body: createInitialDeployment returns immediately when updateStrategy is null, before the new code that enables Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES. upgradeStrategy() yields null as well as RECREATE, and both testImageChange and testCacheMaxCount deploy that CR. The operator guide added in this change says that while the feature is preview, rolling-updates must be enabled or the Operator fails, and the CR example enables it even when strategy is left unset. The null cases therefore never put rolling-updates on spec.features.enabled. deployKeycloak(..., true) will time out if reconciliation fails closed without the feature. If the operator instead shells out to update-compatibility, that command now exits 4 (FEATURE_DISABLED) before it can report compatibility, so testCacheMaxCount(null) cannot observe the rolling update it asserts. Enable the feature for every strategy before that return. On the explicit-strategy path, setEnabledFeatures(List.of(rolling-updates)) also replaces any enabled-feature list already on the spec instead of adding rolling-updates, so other features configured by the test deployment would be dropped.

title: Exit code 4 is documented as a rolling-upgrade incompatibility
body: The check-command exit-code table says exit code 4 means "Rolling Upgrade is not possible" because rolling-updates is disabled. That is not what the implementation does. Both update-compatibility check and update-compatibility metadata return CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED (4) before any version or config comparison, after printing "Unable to use this command. The preview feature 'rolling-updates' is not enabled." The deployment may still be rolling-compatible; the tool refused to run. Exit code 3 uses the same "Rolling Upgrade is not possible" headline and tells the operator to shut the deployment down first. Scripts that follow this table and treat 4 like 3 will take unnecessary downtime, and a metadata-generation step that exits 4 will be misread as an upgrade incompatibility. Document 4 as a precondition failure for both subcommands: enable rolling-updates and re-run; do not shut down the cluster.

title: Remapped compatibility exit codes are not asserted
body: This change moves the recreate result from exit code 4 to 3 and assigns 4 to FEATURE_DISABLED, and the guide tells automation to rely on those codes rather than log text. testFeatureNotEnabled only checks that stderr contains the feature-disabled sentence; it never asserts exit code 4, and it only launches the metadata subcommand, not check, which has the same gate. testWrongVersions asserts the incompatibility text but not exit code 3, and the check invocation in testCompatible does not assert exit code 0. A regression that still prints the expected line but exits 4 for an incompatible version (the previous recreate code) or exits 1 after the feature-disabled message would pass CI and break scripts that branch on the exit code.

title: Caution falsely says the Operator fails without rolling-updates
body: The new caution says that during preview the `rolling-updates` feature must be enabled or the Keycloak Operator will fail. That contradicts both the note later in this same section and the operator test added in this PR. UpgradeTest.createInitialDeployment returns immediately when the update strategy is null and does not set spec.features.enabled to rolling-updates. Those cases still call deployKeycloak with wait-for-ready, and a cache max-count change is expected to roll rather than fail. So a normal Keycloak CR reconciles, becomes ready, and applies the documented 26.1-compatible default (recreate only on image change, roll on other config) with the preview feature off. The feature is only enabled in that test when spec.update.strategy is set explicitly. As written, the caution tells every Operator user that an upgrade breaks unless they turn on a preview feature, which will cause unnecessary preview opt-in or blocked upgrades. Narrow the warning to explicit spec.update usage, or change the test if fail-closed is actually required.

title: Exit code 4 is documented as an upgrade decision
body: The new exit-code row says code 4 means "Rolling Upgrade is not possible" because `rolling-updates` is disabled. That is the same decision wording as exit code 3, and the paragraph above the table says these codes are how automation determines the upgrade type. The implementation does not decide compatibility: both update-compatibility check and update-compatibility metadata print "Unable to use this command. The preview feature 'rolling-updates' is not enabled." and exit 4 before reading metadata or comparing versions. The only other upgrade type this guide defines is recreate (shut the deployment down before applying config). A pipeline that treats "rolling is not possible" as that outcome will take an unnecessary outage when the flag was merely omitted. Describe code 4 as a precondition failure, state that the upgrade type was not determined, and note that the metadata subcommand returns 4 as well; the table currently sits only under the check command.

title: Changed exit codes 3 and 4 are never asserted
body: This PR changes CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 and adds FEATURE_DISABLED = 4, and the guide tells users to branch automation on those codes. testFeatureNotEnabled only checks that stderr contains the disabled-feature sentence and never asserts the process exit code is 4; it also covers only the metadata subcommand, not check. testWrongVersions only checks the incompatibility log line and never asserts exit code 3. CLIResult.assertError succeeds for any non-zero status, so leaving recreate at 4, or picocli.exit collapsing the custom code to 1, would still pass. That docs-vs-code mismatch (docs already said 3, the constant was 4) is exactly what this PR is fixing, and nothing locks the new contract.

title: Groups VIEW scope is treated as manage
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() passes both VIEW and MANAGE to hasPermission and returns true if either scope is granted. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup authorizes only with requireManage(), so an admin who was granted view-only on groups can create top-level groups and can move an existing group to the top of the tree by posting its id. canManage(GroupModel) correctly requires MANAGE, and UserPermissions.canManage() does not treat view as manage. The new GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage() javadoc repeats this incorrect contract and should be corrected with the implementation.

title: Member-view filter stores authorization resource ids, not group ids
body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() is the set UsersResource.getUsersCount, UsersResource.searchForUser, and BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser apply as the groups whose members the caller may see. The findByType callback passes groupResource.getId() (the authorization resource primary key) both into hasPermission() and into the returned set. hasPermission() looks up resources by name, and per-group resources are named with the group id, so the lookup misses the group, falls back to the all-groups resource, and ignores the per-group view-members/manage-members grant. The ids placed in the session UserModel.GROUPS attribute are not group ids, and the schema resource named "Groups" is itself included by findByType. User search then matches nobody, so paginated results omit users the admin is allowed to see; when the set is empty, the query is not constrained and getUsersCount returns 0 while the list path only filters later in memory. GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest only calls users().search and never checks counts, so it does not catch this.

title: Per-group authz resources are created without a type
body: getOrCreateResource() creates the per-object resource and updates scopes, but never calls setType(resourceType). V1 GroupPermissions.initialize did set the type. GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() discovers groups with resourceStore.findByType(server, "Groups"), so individual group resources are invisible to that scan and view-members/manage-members grants never contribute real group ids to the user-search filter. Only the schema-level resource created in init(), which does set type, is found. Because the type is also unset, an evaluator that applies resource-type policies only to typed resources will not apply all-groups policies to these rows either.

title: Group deletion hits unsupported V2 setPermissionsEnabled
body: AdminPermissions.registerListener still handles every GroupRemovedEvent by calling management().groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false) when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled. With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 also enabled, groups() is now GroupPermissionsV2, and setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException. The listener is invoked from realm.removeGroup with no catch, so deleting any group (not only groups that have permissions) fails with a 500 and rolls back. V1 fine-grained admin authz is commonly enabled together with V2. If only V2 is enabled, the listener is not registered at all because it checks the V1 feature, so authorization resources created for a group by getOrCreateResource are never removed when the group is deleted. The same throw breaks the V1 management/permissions admin endpoint, which calls setPermissionsEnabled after requiring ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ.

title: All-groups policies are skipped once a per-group resource exists
body: hasPermission() evaluates only the per-group resource when findByName finds one, and loads the Groups type resource only when that lookup returns null. getOrCreateResource creates that row as soon as any permission references the group, including a different admin or a different scope such as view-members. After that, GroupPermissionsV2 never consults all-groups allow or deny policies for that group: an admin with all-groups MANAGE loses update, delete, and membership checks on it, and a negative all-groups policy does not deny a scope granted by the specific resource. Group listing no longer short-circuits on canView(), so those groups also disappear from an admin who only has all-groups view. testManageAllGroups only updates a group that has no specific resource, so only the fallback path is tested.

title: Existing admin-permissions clients never receive the Groups schema
body: init() returns immediately when the realm already has an admin-permissions client, so upgrade does not add the Groups resource type, the "Groups" all-resource, or the new scopes manage-membership, manage-members, and view-members. On those realms, creating a group permission fails: getScope throws ModelValidationException because the scope does not exist, and getOrCreateResource throws ModelException ("No scopes found") when attaching scopes. GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission then gets a null type resource from getResourceTypeResource and passes it to policyStore.findByResource and resource.getScopes(), which are not null-safe, so group list and permission checks for fine-grained admins throw NullPointerException instead of denying. This pull request contains no migration.

title: Scope grants are accepted without matching the evaluated resource
body: After evaluatePermission, GroupPermissionsV2 returns true for any permission whose scopes intersect the requested scopes. UserPermissionsV2, which this evaluator copies, ignores permissions whose resource id is not the resource just evaluated, because the result is not guaranteed to contain only that resource. Omitting the check here can apply a scope granted on another resource to the group being checked, widening view, manage, view-members, manage-members, or manage-membership beyond that group's policies.

title: Group list runs a policy evaluation per group
body: V2 canView(GroupModel) does not reuse the no-arg canView() result, and GroupsResource.getGroups and GroupResource.getSubGroups dropped the previous canViewGlobal short-circuit. An admin whose access comes from an all-groups permission therefore runs a full authorization evaluation for every group on the page, even though each call falls back to the same Groups type resource. On realms with large group trees the groups admin API issues one policy evaluation, and several store queries, per group on every list request.

title: Group permission resources have no resolvable name
body: getResourceName() maps Users resources to the username, but a Groups resource falls through to resource.getDisplayName(). getOrCreateResource() stores the group id as the resource name and never sets a display name, so the authorization admin API shows a null name, or a raw id, for group permissions instead of the group name. After the group is deleted or renamed those resources stay unresolved, whereas a missing user at least throws ModelIllegalStateException.

title: requireManageMembers javadoc cites the wrong method
body: The javadoc on requireManageMembers says it throws ForbiddenException if canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false. The implementation throws when canManageMembers returns false. Those are different scopes (manage-membership versus manage-members), so the published contract on this permission interface is wrong.

title: All-groups VIEW permission is treated as manage
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() treats a grant of either VIEW or MANAGE on the all-groups resource as success. canManage(GroupModel) correctly requires only MANAGE, and V1 canManage() only checks the manage-users role, so this is not the intended scope model. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup calls requireManage() before creating a group and applying its attributes, so an admin who was given only Groups VIEW can create top-level groups. The new GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage() javadoc repeats the mistake (it says V2 manage is true for VIEW or MANAGE), and GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest never asserts that VIEW alone cannot create or update groups.

title: Member search filter uses authz resource IDs, not group IDs
body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() passes groupResource.getId() into hasPermission() and adds that same value to the returned set. hasPermission() looks the id up with resourceStore.findByName(), but per-group resources are stored with the realm group id as the name (resolveGroup returns group.getId()) and a different authorization-resource UUID as getId(). The lookup misses, falls back to the all-groups resource, and never evaluates that group's own policies. The IDs handed to UsersResource and BruteForceUsersResource via session attribute UserModel.GROUPS, and to getUsersCount(), are therefore not group ids. If the all-groups resource has view-members or manage-members, the filter is a nonexistent group and both search and count return nobody the admin should see. If it does not, the set stays empty: search skips the DB filter and then applies canView in memory (so the new tests pass on a tiny user set) while getUsersCount() is still called with an empty group set and returns 0, and paginated search drops members who are not in the first page of all users. The type resource named "Groups" is also included by findByType and must not be treated as a group id.

title: Per-group resources are created without a type
body: getOrCreateResource() creates the authorization resource for a group (name = group id) and sets scopes, but never calls setType(GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE). init() does set the type on the all-groups resource. GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() discovers candidates only via resourceStore.findByType(..., "Groups"), so individual group resources created for group permissions are invisible to that query. User search/count then cannot be restricted to the groups whose members the admin may view, even after the resource-id vs group-id mix-up is fixed. The same omission also leaves displayName unset, so permission listings have nothing to show for these resources.

title: Group deletion and V1 permission APIs throw under FGAP V2
body: GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(), isPermissionsEnabled(), and the other GroupPermissionManagement methods unconditionally throw UnsupportedOperationException. AdminPermissions.management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 feature is enabled, and MgmtPermissionsV2.groups() now returns this class. AdminPermissions.registerListener still calls groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false) on every GroupRemovedEvent when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled, and that publish is not caught, so deleting any group in any realm fails with 500 and rolls back while V2 is on. The same throw breaks the V1 GET/PUT group management/permissions endpoints, which still call these methods after requiring only the V1 feature. There is also no V2 cleanup of the authorization resource named with the group id, so those resources are left orphaned even if the exception is later swallowed.

title: Existing admin-permissions clients are not upgraded with Groups
body: init() returns immediately when the realm already has an admin-permissions client, and this change adds no migration to sync the schema. Realms that enabled FGAP V2 before Groups existed keep a client that has Users/Clients but not the Groups resource or the new scopes (manage-membership, manage-members, view-members). Creating a group permission then fails because the scope does not exist. Evaluating permissions calls getResourceTypeResource(), gets null, and GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission() passes that null to policyStore.findByResource() (implementations call resource.getId()) and, if that returned, to resource.getScopes() — a 500 on group view/list/manage checks instead of a deny. Fresh test realms hide this because init() creates the full schema only when the client is absent.

title: A per-group resource hides all-groups grants
body: hasPermission() evaluates the all-groups resource only when findByName() returns null. As soon as any permission has created a resource named with that group id, later checks for that group evaluate only that resource's policies and never the all-groups resource. An admin with MANAGE or VIEW on all groups therefore gets 403 on a group that also has a narrower permission (for example VIEW or view-members), because the all-groups policy is not consulted. The comment in this method shows all-groups permissions are supposed to be checked explicitly; the specific-resource branch skips that. GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest never combines an all-groups permission with a per-group permission, so it does not catch the deny.

title: Group resources are not resolved to a display name
body: getResourceName() special-cases only the Users type (username, or "All users"). Group resources created by this PR use the group id as the resource name and do not set a display name, so the fallback resource.getDisplayName() is null. Permission and policy listings for the new Groups resource type therefore show a blank name instead of the group name or path, including the all-groups resource unless its display name was set elsewhere.

title: requireManageMembers javadoc cites the wrong method
body: The javadoc on requireManageMembers says it throws if canManageMembership(GroupModel) is false. That is the contract of requireManageMembership, copied onto the next method. requireManageMembers actually throws when canManageMembers is false. Callers following the javadoc will enforce group membership changes instead of member management.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission contract does not match the method
body: The javadoc says the method returns a Stream of groups with view permission. The signature returns Set<String>, and both the V1 and V2 implementations collect groups that grant view-members or manage-members, not the group VIEW scope. UsersResource uses that set as the UserModel.GROUPS membership filter. An implementor following the javadoc would return the wrong ids and either hide members the admin may see or prefilter user search by groups whose members they cannot view.

title: All-groups VIEW is treated as permission to manage groups
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true if hasPermission finds either the VIEW or MANAGE scope on the all-groups resource. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup authorizes group creation with requireManage(), which calls this method, and any other caller of canManage()/requireManage() treats it as a write check. A fine-grained admin granted only view access to groups can therefore create top-level groups. That contradicts canManage(GroupModel) in the same class, which correctly requires only MANAGE, and contradicts V1, which only checks the manage-users role. The new javadoc on GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage repeats the same mistake by documenting VIEW as sufficient. canManage() must require the MANAGE scope only.

title: Group-scoped user search and counts use authorization resource ids, not group ids
body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission is what UsersResource and BruteForceUsersResource pass to the user store (session attribute UserModel.GROUPS, and getUsersCount) so that an admin who cannot view all users only sees members of groups they may view. The callback passes groupResource.getId() into hasPermission and stores that same value. hasPermission treats the argument as a group id and looks it up with resourceStore.findByName, but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource stores the group id as the resource name and the authorization store assigns a different resource id. The lookup therefore misses. findByType(GROUPS) also cannot see per-group resources, because getOrCreateResource never calls setType, so only the type resource named "Groups" (if present) is visited. The set ends up empty or filled with authorization UUIDs. User search pagination then either is not restricted to the permitted groups or is restricted to ids that match no membership, and the count API returns 0 or a count for a non-existent group. Return the group id (resource name), skip the type resource, and persist instance resources with type Groups.

title: Group deletion throws when FGAP V2 is enabled
body: GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException (as do the other GroupPermissionManagement methods). AdminPermissions.registerListener still handles GroupModel.GroupRemovedEvent by calling management(session, realm).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false) whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled. management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, and therefore GroupPermissionsV2, whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled. With both features on, which is the normal combination if V1 is a default feature and V2 is enabled for this work, realm.removeGroup and the admin delete-group API fail with that exception and the group is not removed. If only V2 is enabled, the listener is not registered at all, so the V2 authorization resource named by the group id is never deleted and remains orphaned on the admin-permissions client. Group removal needs a V2 cleanup path; the V1 listener must not call the throwing methods while V2 is active.

title: A per-group permission resource hides all-groups grants
body: hasPermission looks up the per-group resource by name and, if it exists, evaluates only that resource. The all-groups resource is used only when no per-group resource exists. Creating any permission on a group (including one for a different administrator) creates that resource, after which an admin who holds VIEW or MANAGE on all groups is denied for that group because their all-groups policy is never evaluated. canView, canManage, canViewMembers, canManageMembers, and canManageMembership all go through this helper. GroupsResource.getGroups and GroupResource.getSubGroups no longer short-circuit on global canView() and now depend entirely on canView(group), so listing is affected as well. The new tests never combine an all-groups grant with a specific grant for another user. Evaluation has to combine the instance resource and the resource-type resource under the schema decision strategy; preferring the instance resource drops legitimate grants and also drops all-groups denies when only the instance is evaluated.

title: Existing admin-permissions clients never gain the Groups schema
body: init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already set, and no other path creates the Groups resource type, the "Groups" all-resource, or the new scopes manage-membership, manage-members, and view-members. Realms that already enabled fine-grained admin permissions (the client was created when only Users and Clients existed) do not pick up this change, and turning admin permissions off and on does not help if the client row remains. Creating a group permission then fails in getScope with "Scope [view-members] does not exist". GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission also calls getResourceTypeResource, gets null, and invokes policyStore.findByResource and resource.getScopes() with no null check, so group admin calls from users without manage-users/view-users become 500s instead of a deny. Upgrade must add the missing scopes and the Groups type resource to existing admin-permissions clients, or init/getResourceTypeResource must create them lazily.

title: Group permission resources have no human-readable name
body: getResourceName resolves only the Users resource type ("All users" or the username) and otherwise returns resource.getDisplayName(). Group resources created by getOrCreateResource use the group id as the name and never set a display name, and the new Groups type is not handled here. Permission listings for group policies therefore show a null name or a raw id instead of the group name or path, and there is no "All groups" label for the type resource. A missing user already throws ModelIllegalStateException; a missing group is silently unlabeled. Resolve group resources the same way users are resolved.

title: requireManageMembers javadoc cites the wrong check
body: The javadoc on requireManageMembers says it throws ForbiddenException when canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false. The implementation enforces canManageMembers, which is the manage-members scope, not manage-membership. Those are different permissions (managing the users in a group versus changing a user's group membership). An implementor or caller following the javadoc will check or document the wrong scope.

title: Public group permission methods were removed and renamed
body: GroupPermissionEvaluator is public. This change deletes getGroupsWithViewPermission(GroupModel) and renames getGroupsWithViewPermission() to getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() with no bridge method. In-repo callers were updated, but any extension that implements the interface or calls the old methods will fail to compile or throw NoSuchMethodError at runtime. If this interface is part of the supported admin-permissions contract, keep the old methods as deprecated delegates; otherwise call the break out in the release notes.

title: Account UI error uses Java MessageFormat instead of i18next placeholders
body: error-invalid-multivalued-size was changed from i18next placeholders (Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).) to Java MessageFormat, including a ChoiceFormat subpattern: Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}. Every other string in this account-ui bundle uses {{name}} / {{0}} (and <0> Trans tags), and apostrophes are not doubled the way MessageFormat requires, so this file is not formatted by Java. i18next will not substitute {0}/{1}/{2} and will not evaluate {2,choice,...}. Users who hit the multivalued-size validator will see the raw format string, including the < in 1<values, instead of the attribute name and limits. The previous {{0}}/{{1}}/{{2}} wording did not need this change to satisfy the new HTML check.

title: Admin UI error uses Java MessageFormat instead of i18next placeholders
body: The same key in the React admin-ui bundle was rewritten from Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s). to Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}. That bundle is loaded by i18next (the previous value already used {{0}} interpolation). i18next will leave {0}, {1}, {2}, and the Java choice pattern as literal text, so administrators validating a multivalued user-profile attribute see an uninterpolated format string rather than the attribute name and min/max. ChoiceFormat is not an i18next plural form; keep the {{0}}/{{1}}/{{2}} placeholders (for example the old value(s) wording).

title: Choice-format pre-strip bypasses the HTML sanitizer
body: Before the OWASP policy runs, normalizeValue deletes every {n,choice,...} substring for error-invalid-multivalued-size and any key starting with linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit. Anything inside that substring, including tags, is never sanitized. A community translation can therefore ship active HTML such as {0,choice,0#<a href="https://evil.example">click|1#minute} and the new check will still pass. linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit.* values are interpolated into HTML emails, and error-invalid-multivalued-size is shown in the account and admin UIs, so this bypasses the control the PR adds. Replace only the ChoiceFormat limit marker (the N< in 1<values) or reject choice subformats that contain tags, instead of discarding the whole pattern before sanitize().

title: Choice-format strip hides HTML from the sanitizer
body: Before the OWASP policy runs, normalizeValue() deletes every `{n,choice,...}` subformat on `error-invalid-multivalued-size` and any key starting with `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit`, using `\{[0-9]+,choice,[^}]*}` which consumes arbitrary text up to the closing brace, including tags. A translation such as `{0,choice,0#minutes|1#minute|1<reset}` is reduced to `...` and passes the checker. Those time-unit strings are MessageFormat-formatted and substituted unescaped into HTML email bodies (verification, password reset, execute-actions), so a translator can inject links or markup into official mail. The same hole exists for `error-invalid-multivalued-size`. Only the choice-format `<` limit marker should be neutralized (or the subformat text itself sanitized), and a test should cover a tag hidden inside a choice branch.

title: Account UI validation message switched to Java MessageFormat
body: This account-ui bundle is loaded by i18next, which interpolates `{{0}}`, `{{1}}`, and `{{2}}`. Sibling keys in the same file still use that form (for example `error-invalid-length-too-short='{{0}}' must have minimal length of {{1}}.`). This change replaces `{{0}}`/`{{1}}`/`{{2}}` with Java MessageFormat `{0}` and a `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` plural, which i18next does not evaluate. Users who fail the multivalued-size check will see the literal string, including `{0}` and the choice pattern, with no attribute name or limits. Restore the `{{n}}` placeholders and a plain wording such as `value(s)`. The Java choice format is only valid in the server-side theme bundles.

title: Admin UI validation message switched to Java MessageFormat
body: The keycloak.v2 admin console reads this file through i18next, which only substitutes `{{0}}`/`{{1}}`/`{{2}}`. The previous value used those placeholders (`Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).`). It was rewritten to Java MessageFormat `{0}` plus `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}`, which the React admin UI will not format. The multivalued-size validation error will display the raw pattern and empty placeholders instead of the attribute name and bounds. Keep the `{{n}}` form and `value(s)` here. The choice-format wording in `themes/.../theme/base/admin/messages/messages_en.properties` is the copy that MessageFormat actually evaluates.

title: Illegal-HTML diff reporter can throw and abort the scan
body: When the sanitized string differs from the original, the reporter computes a common prefix (`start`) and a common suffix (`end`) independently, then calls `substring(start, length - end)` on both strings without checking that `start + end` is within each length. If those regions overlap, `substring` throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. That is a realistic sanitizer result: `test<script>test` is reduced to `test`, `start` and `end` are both 4, and `sanitized.substring(4, 0)` throws. `verify()` only catches IOException, so the RuntimeException aborts the file, the Illegal HTML message is never returned, and later keys in that file are not checked. Clamp the range or fall back to the full strings before calling substring.

title: Choice-format exemption skips HTML sanitizing
body: normalizeValue deletes every {n,choice,...} subformat (replaced with "...") before the OWASP sanitizer runs, for linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit* and error-invalid-multivalued-size. The comment says the intent is only to ignore the '<' ChoiceFormat operator, but the regex drops the entire subformat, so markup inside it is never compared to English and never sanitized. MessageFormat does not HTML-escape arguments, and those unit strings are substituted into HTML email bodies (the {3} expiration in messages such as emailVerificationBodyHtml and passwordResetBodyHtml). MessageFormat quotes are the documented way to emit a literal '<', so a translation like {0,choice,0#'reset'|1#minute|1

title: HTML check decodes UTF-8 messages as ISO-8859-1
body: verifySafeHtml loads both the translation and the English bundle with new PropertyResourceBundle(FileInputStream) (lines 68 and 77). That constructor decodes properties as ISO-8859-1. Keycloak theme message files are UTF-8 (these bundles contain raw Arabic, CJK, and other non-ASCII text) and are loaded at runtime with a UTF-8 reader. The checker therefore does not see the string that will be rendered. OWASP's sanitizer strips specific code points such as bidi overrides (U+202E and similar) only when they are real Unicode characters; read as Latin-1 those UTF-8 bytes are different characters and are not removed, so a translation can carry them and still compare equal after sanitize. Reported "Illegal HTML" snippets for non-English files will also be mojibake. Use PropertyResourceBundle(new InputStreamReader(fis, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)) for both files.

title: Illegal-HTML diff can throw and abort the plugin
body: When sanitized text differs from the message, the code trims the shared prefix and suffix and then calls value.substring(start, value.length() - end) and sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end). The suffix walk is allowed to overlap the prefix, so start can be greater than length - end. Example: value "aaa<x>aaa" becomes "aaaaaa" after a disallowed tag is removed; start is 3 and end is 4, and sanitized.substring(3, 2) throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. That exception is not caught in verify() (only IOException is wrapped in MojoExecutionException), so one offending message crashes the Maven plugin with a stack trace instead of recording the violation and continuing with the other keys and files. The new tests use short non-overlapping diffs, so they do not catch this.

title: Constructor null-check tests grantType instead of rawTokenId
body: AccessTokenContext's constructor is supposed to reject a null raw token id, but the second requireNonNull call checks grantType again (message says 'Null rawTokenId not allowed'). A null rawTokenId is stored. encodeTokenId then concatenates ':' with that value, and Java string conversion turns null into the literal 'null', so every such token gets the same jti suffix (for example onrtac:null). Distinct access tokens would share a JWT ID, which breaks uniqueness for revocation, replay detection, and event correlation. The current TokenManager caller passes KeycloakModelUtils.generateId(), so this is latent, but the constructor is the shared entry point for the new SPI and does not enforce the invariant it claims to enforce.

title: Access-token ID matcher checks the wrong characters and inverts the match
body: isAccessTokenId is now what expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken, and expectAuthReqIdToToken use for Details.TOKEN_ID. After splitting on ':', it treats items[0].substring(3, 5) as the grant shortcut and returns false (no match) when that slice equals the expected shortcut. Both parts are wrong. The wire format is 2-char session type, 2-char token type, 2-char grant type, so the grant is substring(4, 6): for onrtac the grant is ac, while substring(3, 5) is ta (last char of token type 'rt'/'lt' plus the first grant char). The equality test is also inverted, so a real match is rejected. For every built-in grant, substring(3, 5) is 't' plus the grant's first character, which is never the grant shortcut, so the check never fires and the matcher accepts any six-char prefix plus a UUID. These new assertions will not fail if authorization-code, refresh, device, or CIBA access tokens are encoded with the wrong grant (including the 'na' fallback). A prefix shorter than 5 characters throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of a failed assertion. The check should require a prefix of at least 6 characters and substring(4, 6) equal to the expected shortcut.

title: New getShortcut() method has no default and aborts server startup
body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is the extension point for custom grant types, and getShortcut() was added with no default implementation. DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit walks every OAuth2GrantType factory and calls getShortcut() unconditionally. A custom grant JAR compiled against the previous interface does not have that method, so the call throws AbstractMethodError during provider startup and Keycloak fails to boot. A recompiled factory that returns null also aborts startup, because the shortcut is inserted into a ConcurrentHashMap, which rejects null keys. A default method is required so existing providers keep the server up, and postInit must reject invalid shortcuts with an explicit error instead of an NPE or AbstractMethodError.

title: Grant shortcuts are not validated as 2-character unique codes
body: Access-token ids are a fixed 6-character prefix (session type, token type, grant shortcut, 2 characters each) plus ':' plus the raw id. The decoder rejects any other prefix length. postInit stores each grant shortcut with no check that it is non-null, exactly 2 characters, free of ':', or unique beyond a map-size comparison. OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut's javadoc says shortcuts are 'usually like 3-letters', which cannot be represented in this format. A custom grant that follows that javadoc still passes the size check, and encodeTokenId will issue ids such as onrtabc:<uuid>. Decoding those ids throws IllegalArgumentException, so the context this feature exists to recover is unreadable. The hot-deploy refresh in getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut (puts around lines 113 and 131) also overwrites grantsByShortcuts without re-checking length or uniqueness. Two grants that share a shortcut leave one decode mapping, so previously issued tokens of the overwritten grant are reported as the other grant type. Registration should reject anything other than a unique 2-character shortcut, and the javadoc must match that contract.

title: Decoder throws on unknown prefixes instead of falling back like legacy ids
body: getTokenContextFromTokenId returns an UNKNOWN session type, token type, and grant when the jti has no ':'. If the id contains ':' but the prefix is not exactly 6 characters, or any 2-character slice is missing from the in-memory maps, it throws IllegalArgumentException. The length error says the token id 'Expected length of 6', but the check is only on the prefix before the colon, so the message is wrong and will mislead operators. Unknown shortcuts are a normal compatibility case, not corruption: feature-gated grants are absent from the maps when that feature is disabled or not deployed on this node (CIBA 'ci', device 'dg', token-exchange 'te', pre-authorized code 'pc'), and another Keycloak version can mint shortcuts this node does not know. Introspection or session lookup that uses this method, which is the stated purpose of the encoding, will then fail a still-valid access token instead of falling back to the old online-then-offline lookup. Unsupported prefixes should return an UNKNOWN context, the same as colon-less legacy ids.

title: Non-standard token exchange issues access tokens with unknown grant
body: The encoded grant type is whatever was stored on the client-session attribute Constants.GRANT_TYPE. If that attribute is missing, DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider records 'na' (unknown). Token exchange does not go through OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse, which is why this provider had to set the attribute itself before generateAccessToken(). Only StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient was updated. TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory still turns on legacy TOKEN_EXCHANGE, TOKEN_EXCHANGE_FEDERATED_V2, and TOKEN_EXCHANGE_SUBJECT_IMPERSONATION_V2, and those providers are not in this change. StandardTokenExchangeProvider rejects requested_subject, so impersonation cannot be this method. Those other flows still call TokenManager to mint access tokens, so their jti grant shortcut is 'na' rather than 'te'. Follow-up token-exchange logic that branches on the encoded grant (the #37117 case described in the PR) will not recognize them. The new AssertEvents matcher does not actually verify the grant shortcut, so CI will not catch this.

title: Replacing form params leaves the cached grant type stale
body: grantType is captured once in the Context constructor from formParams.getFirst(grant_type) and is what OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse writes into the client session before the access token id is encoded. setFormParams replaces formParams but does not recompute grantType, so getGrantType() can disagree with the params the grant then processes. A caller that uses the existing setter to change the request after construction will encode the original grant type into the access-token id. The constructor also now dereferences formParams, so a null map NPEs, which the previous constructor accepted. This change also removes the public Context(Context) copy constructor, so extensions that cloned a context that way no longer compile and have no other way to rebuild grantType.

title: First offline access tokens are labeled as online sessions
body: Access-token ids are encoded inside createClientAccessToken/initToken, which createTokenResponse calls on line 110 while userSession is still the online session, so the jti prefix is "on". Only after that does generateRefreshToken() create the offline user session (Keycloak keeps the same session id) and, when AuthenticationProcessor.FIRST_OFFLINE_ACCESS is set, line 120 deletes the online session — before the token is signed in build() and returned. By the time the client uses the access token, that session id exists only in the offline store, but the prefix says online. ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType has the same ordering: generateAccessToken() at line 139 runs before line 145 removes the online session whenever the refresh token is offline (not only the first issuance). This prefix is meant to skip the online-then-offline session lookup. Trusting "on" for these tokens misses the session and rejects valid access tokens from offline login. Resolve the final session store before encoding the id (or rewrite the id before signing).

title: Access-token id matcher uses the wrong slice and inverted logic
body: isAccessTokenId is supposed to require the new jti to embed the expected grant shortcut, but it does not. The wire format is six characters SSTTGG before the colon, so the grant shortcut is substring(4, 6). The matcher uses substring(3, 5) (last char of the token-type shortcut plus the first char of the grant; for onrtac:... that is "ta", not "ac") and returns false when that slice equals the expected shortcut, so a real match would be rejected. For every built-in shortcut the wrong slice never equals the expected value (onrtrt yields "tr", not refresh shortcut "rt"), so the check is dead code: any prefix:uuid passes expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken, and expectAuthReqIdToToken even if the grant shortcut is wrong. A prefix shorter than 5 characters throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of failing the assertion. Require a 6-character prefix and accept only when substring(4, 6) equals the expected shortcut.

title: Constructor null-checks grantType instead of rawTokenId
body: The constructor intends to reject a null raw token id, but the fourth Objects.requireNonNull checks grantType again (already checked on the previous line) and the message falsely says rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is stored. encodeTokenId concatenates it, and Java turns null into the literal "null", producing a jti such as onrtac:null. Every token built with a null raw id shares that jti, so revocation/replay checks keyed by token id cannot tell them apart. Require rawTokenId to be non-null.

title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing grant factories
body: getShortcut() was added to the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory SPI with no default method. DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit calls it on every grant factory. A custom grant-type provider compiled against the previous interface has no such method and throws AbstractMethodError during startup, which fails deployment when that provider is installed. The javadoc also says the shortcut is "usually like 3-letters", but the encoder and decoder require exactly two characters; an implementation that follows the javadoc mints access-token ids the default decoder cannot parse. Add a default that returns a stable 2-character shortcut (or "na") and document the exact length.

title: Grant shortcuts are not checked against the fixed 2-character format
body: Encoded access-token ids are session(2)+tokenType(2)+grant(2)+':'+rawId, and getTokenContextFromTokenId throws if the prefix length is not 6. postInit stores OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() with no check that it is non-null, exactly two characters, free of ':', and unique. A shortcut of any other length (including the 3-letter form described on getShortcut) is accepted, encodeTokenId embeds it, and decoding later throws IllegalArgumentException, so those tokens cannot be interpreted. A null shortcut NPEs in ConcurrentHashMap.put during postInit and aborts startup with an unclear error. The lazy refresh in getShortcutByGrantType (around line 112) and getGrantTypeByShortcut (around line 130) also overwrites an existing shortcut without re-running the duplicate size check, so a newly deployed grant can steal another grant's shortcut and make already-issued tokens decode as the wrong grant. Validate length, charset, and uniqueness both at startup and on the lazy path, and name the conflicting grant ids in the error.

title: Public Context copy constructor was deleted
body: The line that captures grantType from form params replaced the public OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context) copy constructor instead of being added inside the primary constructor. That copy constructor is part of the grant SPI context type. Callers that clone a context with new OAuth2GrantType.Context(existing) no longer compile, including any in-repo use that this edit did not update. The deletion looks accidental. Restore the copy constructor and copy grantType as well; a clone that leaves grantType null causes access tokens to be encoded with grant shortcut "na" even when the original request had a grant.
