body: When topEvents is set, only timeseries_columns are rewritten to upsampled_count(). selected_columns from get_field_list and orderby from get_orderby are left as count(), and get_equation_list is passed through unchanged on the same call. The top-N query therefore ranks groups by raw event count while the chart plots upsampled weights. Issues or projects with different client sample rates will show the wrong top series, and the plotted values will not match the sort metric. An equation that still contains count() stays on the raw count in the same response as an upsampled count() y-axis. Rewrite orderby, selected aggregates, and equations the same way, or rank with the upsampled aggregate.

title: upsampled_count is exposed as a public function
body: The new upsampled_count SnQLFunction is registered without private=True, unlike the function immediately above it in function_converter. It is therefore a public events-search aggregate: a caller can request yAxis=upsampled_count() or use it in a query without the allowlist or error-dataset checks in is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects. That bypasses the gate and runs sum(sample_weight) on projects and datasets the helper explicitly refuses, which either errors or returns undercounts. Mark the function private so only the server-side column rewrite can use it.

title: Transaction upsampling test does not wait for Snuba
body: test_error_upsampling_with_transaction_events stores a transaction with store_event and immediately GETs events-stats at this line, without wait_for_event_count. setUp waits for the two error events before querying, which shows ingestion is asynchronous in this Snuba test class. The new transaction may not be visible yet, so the assertion that the first bucket count is 1 fails intermittently. Wait for the transaction to be queryable before asserting.

title: Accidental gitlink added as sentry-repo
body: This change adds a gitlink sentry-repo pinned to a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a, which is the PR base commit, not a dependency of the upsampling feature. Merging a submodule pointer will break clones and CI (missing submodule URL, or a recursive checkout of this same repo) and is unrelated to error upsampling. Remove sentry-repo before merging.

title: Upsampled count sums sample_weight but nothing stores that weight
body: upsampled_count is defined as toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) and is substituted for count() on allowlisted error queries. This change never writes sample_weight and never computes an inverse sample rate. The only data-path edit, _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling in the test factory, copies contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate (for example 0.1) onto the existing event field sample_rate, which is the server-side sampling rate, not a weight. ClickHouse sum skips nulls, and the aggregate does not use ifNull(sample_weight, 1), so events with a missing weight contribute nothing; toInt64 then truncates a fractional sum toward zero, so a stored rate of 0.1 becomes 0 rather than 10. OrganizationEventsStatsEndpoint only catches ValidationError, so if sample_weight is absent on the queried entity the chart request 500s instead of falling back to count(). The new stats test expects each 0.1-sampled event to contribute 10, which this code cannot produce. Once the allowlist is non-empty, error count charts for those projects will be zeroed, truncated, or failed.

title: Error detection is a substring match and treats negations as errors
body: _is_error_focused_query treats a discover query as error-only if the raw query string contains the substring event.type:error after lowercasing. That is true for negations and mixed filters: !event.type:error contains event.type:error, and so does event.type:error OR event.type:transaction. The helper says sample_weight must not be applied to transactions and that the check should err on the side of caution, but this match does the opposite of a parsed filter. For allowlisted projects, count() is then rewritten to sum(sample_weight) on a query that still includes transactions. That either fails in Snuba because the column is not on the transactions entity, or returns a meaningless sum. The stats endpoint does not catch SnubaError, so the chart 500s. The unit test only covers the exact strings event.type:error, event.type:transaction, and an empty query, so the false positive is untested.

title: Upsampling decision ignores the dataset and query actually executed
body: _get_event_stats decides whether to upsample by passing the closed-over request dataset and request.GET query into is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects, not scoped_dataset and the query argument this call actually runs. The dashboard widget split path in the same method invokes _get_event_stats with the discover dataset and a rewritten query such as (query) AND !event.type:transaction or AND event.type:transaction, while the closed-over dataset is metrics_performance or metrics_enhanced_performance (that branch only runs when metrics_enhanced is true). _should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns false for metrics datasets, so those error-event widget queries never upsample even when every project is allowlisted. The request query is also not the executed query: a request containing event.type:error would mark the transaction-only probe eligible, and a request without that substring would skip an errors-only split. Dashboard error charts for allowlisted projects keep showing sampled counts, and the eligibility bit can disagree with the query sent to Snuba.

title: Only an exact y-axis count() is rewritten; sort, equations, and filters stay raw
body: transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling replaces a column only when its text is exactly count() (case-insensitive, stripped). In the top-events branch that rewritten list is passed as timeseries_columns / y_axes, but orderby=self.get_orderby(request) is left unchanged, so a normal sort=-count() still ranks groups by the raw count() aggregate while the plotted series is upsampled_count() as count. Top-N groups are chosen by sampled volume, so a low sample rate and high true volume group can be omitted; if the builder treats ORDER BY count() as a different aggregate from the alias, the top-events query errors instead. Equations (equation|count() * 2 and get_equation_list) and aggregate conditions in the query string (count():>N) are not rewritten either, so filters and equation series do not match the upsampled count series. Other count-derived y-axes such as epm() and eps() stay sampled, so one response can show an upsampled count beside a sampled rate. Columns that are already aliased, such as count() as errors, also fail the exact match and silently skip upsampling.

title: Shared cache around an in-memory option read slows and can fail stats
body: is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects calls cache.get and cache.set on Sentry's shared cache (Redis in production) on every events-stats query, including each dashboard split subquery, to avoid options.get of issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist. That option read is already a process-local dict lookup, so the cache adds a network round trip on a hot endpoint instead of removing work. Cache errors are not caught here, and OrganizationEventsStatsEndpoint does not catch them either, so a Redis timeout fails the chart. Keys are one per organization plus hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))), which is high-cardinality, and Python hash() is not a collision-resistant digest, so a collision would reuse another project set's allowlist boolean and could enable sum(sample_weight) for a set that is not fully allowlisted. invalidate_upsampling_cache is never called and can delete only one exact key, so it does not flush eligibility after an allowlist change. The docstring on _are_all_projects_error_upsampled, which says each call reads the latest configuration, is false once this 60-second cache is in front of it.

title: upsampled_count is a public discover aggregate and bypasses the allowlist
body: upsampled_count is registered on Discover's function converter without private=True, unlike the neighboring function in the same list (private defaults to false). It therefore becomes a user-facing function on every discover endpoint that shares this converter, not only the allowlisted stats path. Clients can request yAxis=upsampled_count(), or use it in other discover and alert queries, for projects that are not allowlisted and for queries that include transactions. The aggregate itself has no allowlist or dataset guard and always emits sum(sample_weight), so a missing column becomes a Snuba error and the gate in organization_events_stats is bypassable. It also sets default_result_type to number while count() is an integer, so series metadata changes type. If private functions are rejected by the same column parser the stats rewrite uses, marking it private will 400 the rewrite; the weight sum should be applied inside the query builder under the allowlist check rather than exposed as a public function.

title: Accidental gitlink committed without .gitmodules
body: This pull request adds a gitlink at sentry-repo pointing at commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a, which is the PR base, and does not add a .gitmodules entry or URL. A submodule pointer without a URL cannot be checked out. git submodule update, CI jobs that clone recursively, and tools that reject unexpected gitlinks will fail, and the link is unrelated to error upsampling. Remove the gitlink before merge.

title: Upsampling tests assert a 10x count the fixtures never produce
body: test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects stores events with client_sample_rate 0.1 and asserts each bucket count is 10. The factory only sets sample_rate to 0.1 and never sets sample_weight to 10, and no test inspects the SnQL or the stored column, so the assertion does not prove upsampling and fails unless an out-of-diff processor inverts the rate. The unit tests never call is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects, never seed or clear the new cache, and never cover !event.type:error, mixed event.type:error OR event.type:transaction, dataset=errors (which the helper always rewrites), events missing sample_weight, or topEvents sorted by count(). Those are the paths that currently mis-apply or skip the rewrite.

title: Suspect-issue PR comments will crash with AttributeError
body: get_merged_pr_single_issue_template and get_environment_info were added as methods of CommitContextIntegration, but GitHubPRCommentWorkflow and GitlabPRCommentWorkflow (subclasses of PRCommentWorkflow, which does not inherit CommitContextIntegration) call them as self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(...) and self.get_environment_info(issue). That raises AttributeError before a comment body can be built, so merged-PR suspect-issue comments stop being posted. The helper also calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title, but _truncate_title is defined on CommitContextIntegration, not PRCommentWorkflow, so even a direct call on the integration class fails the same way. The updated GitHub/GitLab comment tests expect the new body and will fail on this AttributeError. Move the helpers onto PRCommentWorkflow (where the callers live) and truncate via that class.

title: Flagged table widgets render an empty table instead of query results
body: When organization.features includes use-table-widget-visualization, WidgetCardChart replaces StyledSimpleTableChart with TableWidgetVisualization passed columns={[]} and tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}}. The real result.data, result.meta, fields, and loading state are discarded. TableWidgetVisualization only falls back to meta.fields when columns is nullish, so an empty array also suppresses column extraction. Enabling the flag blanks every dashboard table widget (including during load) instead of showing the query.

title: Error context is paired by dict order, not event id
body: fetch_error_details builds node ids from error_ids, then does zip(error_ids, events.values()) on the dict returned by nodestore.backend.get_multi. That pairs by iteration order, not by node id. Backends that omit missing keys (the usual get_multi behavior) shift every later row: if the second id is absent, the third event's title, message, and timestamp are attached to the second id and the last id is dropped. The id field is not even used in the log line, so the Seer prompt gets the wrong errors and timestamps. The new test only stores one error, so it cannot catch this. Look up each node id in the dict instead of zipping values().

title: Error and breadcrumb timestamps are not on the same scale
body: gen_request_data interleaves errors and breadcrumbs with error["timestamp"] < event.get("timestamp", 0). Replay segment events are raw rrweb records whose timestamp is epoch milliseconds. fetch_error_details copies the nodestore event timestamp, which is epoch seconds (or sometimes an ISO string). Seconds are always less than millisecond breadcrumbs, so every error is emitted before the first breadcrumb and the summary chronology is wrong for real replays. An ISO-string timestamp raises TypeError on < or sort, and that exception is outside fetch_error_details's try/except, so the summarize request 500s. The new tests hide this by writing segment JSON with now.timestamp() seconds. Normalize both sides to the same numeric unit before comparing.

title: Error ids are queried with the page stats window, not the replay
body: Error context now depends on query_replay_instance(start=filter_params["start"], end=filter_params["end"]) from ProjectEndpoint.get_filter_params. The replay AI tab (static/app/views/replays/detail/ai/index.tsx) calls this endpoint with no start, end, or statsPeriod. The lookup therefore uses the generic project default stats window rather than the replay's own start/end. Replays outside that window return no row, error_ids stays empty, and the summary is produced without error context with no error to the user. Query the replay by id over its retention window, or pass the replay bounds from the client.

title: Hidden span attributes are only removed while searching
body: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES (is_segment, project_id, received) is applied only inside the searchQuery branch. When the search box is empty the code returns sortAttributes(attributes) unchanged, so those internal fields stay visible. Once the user types a query that would match them, they disappear. If the intent is to hide them, filter them out before the search check; otherwise search results disagree with the full list.

title: Feedback list is clipped after the summary is inserted
body: The list grid cell used to be a FluidHeight Container (height 100% of the stretched grid area). It is now SummaryListContainer, a column flex with no min-height: 0 or overflow handling, containing FeedbackSummary plus that same height-100% Container. The list's 100% height is the full cell, then the summary and gap are added on top, so the column overflows the grid row. Background and LayoutGrid both set overflow: hidden, so the bottom of the feedback list is clipped and no longer lines up with the details pane. Give the list container flex: 1 and min-height: 0 (and overflow: hidden) so it fills only the space under the summary.

title: Attribute-key hook returns undefined after a failed fetch
body: useTraceItemAttributeKeys used to always reduce the API payload to a TagCollection (empty object if data was missing) and return that once loading finished. It now returns useQuery's data directly: attributes is previous while isFetching, otherwise data. On error, isFetching is false and data is undefined, and there is no ?? {}. Explore callers that wait for !isLoading and then spread or Object.keys the result will throw, blanking the search builder, instead of seeing an empty tag set. Return data ?? {} (and keep the previous value only while refetching).

title: Feedback summary ignores the environment page filter
body: useFeedbackSummary reads usePageFilters().selection and sends normalized datetime plus project, but not selection.environments. The feedback list on the same page is scoped by the environment page filter. With an environment selected, the summary is computed from every environment in the projects and date range, so it can describe feedback the list is not showing. Pass environment (and any other page filters the summary API supports) in the query.

title: 60s deadline is too short for a 100-identity auth refresh
body: check_auth_identities now has processing_deadline_duration=60 while it still loops up to chunk_size (default 100) identities, each doing an org-membership RPC and provider.refresh_identity HTTP call. 100 sequential IdP calls routinely exceed 60s, so the taskworker kills the task mid-batch. check_auth already sets last_synced=now on those ids before enqueueing this task, and they are not selected again until the next ~24h window (AUTH_CHECK_INTERVAL). Identities not yet refreshed are skipped for a day, so SSO invalidation is delayed. Raise the deadline to match the chunk, or shrink the chunk to what 60s can finish.

title: Issue titles are interpolated into markdown links unsanitized
body: MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE is "* ‼️ [**{title}**]({url}){environment}\n" and _truncate_title only slices to 50 characters. Issue titles come from user-influenced error messages. A title containing ] or ) breaks out of the link, for example [**click here](https://evil.example)**](real-url), and is posted to GitHub/GitLab. Truncation does not stop that. Escape markdown metacharacters in the title (and backticks in the environment name) before formatting.

title: Report age/timestamp rules do not match the spec the serializer claims
body: age and timestamp are both required=False, and there is no object-level validate() requiring exactly one of them. A report with neither is accepted and counted. The field validators also use initial_data.get("age") / get("timestamp"), which treat 0 as absent, so a report with age=0 and timestamp=0 skips both mutual-exclusion checks (0 is a valid age and a valid timestamp). Use "age" in initial_data (and the same for timestamp) and reject payloads that do not have exactly one of the two fields.

title: Flagged table widgets render with empty columns and data
body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, `tableResultComponent` swaps the real table for `TableWidgetVisualization` with `columns={[]}` and `tableData` hardcoded to `{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}`. `columns ?? fallback` does not treat `[]` as missing, so columns are not derived from meta either. Query results, loading state, field headers, and custom cell renderers are all dropped, so every dashboard table widget for that org renders blank.

title: Error payloads are paired by dict order, not event id
body: `fetch_error_details` builds nodestore ids from `error_ids`, then does `zip(error_ids, events.values())`. `get_multi` returns a dict keyed by node id and omits missing keys; value order is not the request order. A missing or reordered event attaches another event's title, message, and timestamp to the wrong id and drops the last id, so the Seer summary describes the wrong errors. Index with `events.get(node_id)` per id. The new test only stores one present event, so it does not catch this.

title: Unnormalized error timestamps crash or mis-order summaries
body: Error context defaults on. Timestamps from nodestore are stored raw and then compared with `<` to each segment event's numeric `timestamp` (default 0) while merging logs. Ingested events persist `timestamp` as an ISO-8601 string; `str < float` raises TypeError outside `fetch_error_details`'s try/except, so any replay with error ids 500s the summarize endpoint instead of returning a summary. The new test passes a float into `store_event`, so it does not lock the production shape. Segment fixtures in this same file use small offsets like `0.0` while event timestamps are unix time, so even two numbers will not interleave. Coerce both sides to one numeric unit before sort/compare.

title: Error ids depend on the client's field allowlist
body: The endpoint always runs `process_raw_response(..., fields=request.query_params.getlist("field"))` and then reads `error_ids` from that projection. The replay AI tab calls this URL with no `field` param, and any caller that passes `field` for something else will not include `error_ids`. If that helper only emits requested keys, error context is silently empty in the UI this change is for. The new test also omits `field` while expecting exception text in the Seer body, so it only passes if an empty field list means "all fields". Force `error_ids` into the internal lookup instead of forwarding the client field list.

title: Each segment page is summarized with every remaining error
body: `error_events` is closed over the paginator `on_results` callback, but `gen_request_data` flushes every not-yet-emitted error after the current page's segments. `GenericOffsetPaginator` only supplies one page (a long replay is many more than one page of segments). The first page, which is all the AI tab loads, therefore appends later errors instead of interleaving them with later breadcrumbs, and later pages repeat those errors in their Seer requests. Only emit errors whose timestamps fall in the page being summarized.

title: Unescaped issue titles break or inject PR comment links
body: `MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE` puts the issue title inside a markdown link (`[**{title}**]({url})`) after only truncating to 50 characters. Titles often contain `]`. That character closes the link early, so the GitHub/GitLab suspect-issue comment points at the wrong URL. A title an attacker can set by sending an error, such as `Click me](https://evil.example)`, injects an arbitrary link into the bot comment developers read on the PR. Escape `]` (and other markdown link characters) before formatting.

title: Report validation rejects real browser URLs and ignores age 0
body: `url` is a DRF `URLField`, which only allows http(s)/ftp(s). Reporting API document URLs are often `about:blank`, `chrome-extension:`, or other non-http schemes. Those reports now 422 the entire batch; the previous dataclass accepted any string. `validate_timestamp` / `validate_age` also use `initial_data.get("age")` and `get("timestamp")`, which are falsy for 0, so a spec-valid `age: 0` combined with a timestamp skips the mutual-exclusion error (and the reverse). Allow the schemes browsers actually send, and test key presence rather than truthiness.

title: Hidden span attributes are still shown until the user searches
body: `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` (`is_segment`, `project_id`, `received`) is applied only in the search branch. An empty `searchQuery` returns `sortAttributes(attributes)` immediately, so those fields remain in the default attributes panel. The hide filter has to run before that early return; otherwise the new constant never affects the view users actually see.

title: Feedback summary ignores the environment page filter
body: The summary request sends only the normalized datetime and `selection.projects`. The list page is under `PageFiltersContainer`, so the feedback list is environment-scoped, but this query never sends `selection.environments` (or the active feedback search). With an environment selected, the summary above the list describes feedback from other environments than the rows the user is looking at.

title: 60s auth-check deadline skips SSO refresh after last_synced is bumped
body: `check_auth_identities` now has `processing_deadline_duration=60` and previously had none. It walks up to `chunk_size` (default 100) identities, each doing an organization RPC plus `provider.refresh_identity` HTTP. If the worker is killed at 60s, the trailing `check_auth.apply_async` that continues the chain never runs. `check_auth` already set `last_synced=now` for the whole id list before enqueue, so those identities are not selected again for about a day and their SSO validity is not refreshed. Raise the deadline to fit the batch, or set `last_synced` only after a successful check.

title: AI summary errors while the project list is still loading
body: The new guard treats `replayRecord.project_id && !project` as "Project not found". `useProjectFromId` is also undefined while the project store is still loading, not only when the id is missing. The first render shows an error alert and keeps the summarize query disabled (`project?.slug` is missing) until projects arrive, instead of the loading state. Only show that error after the project list has finished loading.

title: Trace waterfall wrapper lost height 100%
body: The waterfall root changed from a flex column with `flex-grow: 1` and `height: 100%` to `<Flex direction="column" flex={1}>`. `flex={1}` does not set height. If the parent lays this view out by height rather than as a stretched flex item, the waterfall no longer fills the trace viewer and scrolling breaks. Put an explicit `height`/`min-height: 100%` back on that container.

title: Suspect-issue PR comments call helpers that are not on the workflow class
body: `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` and `get_environment_info` are defined on `CommitContextIntegration` (the class that ends just before `OpenPRCommentWorkflow`), but `GitHubPRCommentWorkflow` and `GitlabPRCommentWorkflow` call them as `self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(...)` / `self.get_environment_info(issue)`. Those workflow classes subclass `PRCommentWorkflow`, which holds an integration rather than inheriting these methods. The static helper also does `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title)`, and `_truncate_title` is not defined on `PRCommentWorkflow`. Generating a merged-PR suspect-issue comment therefore raises AttributeError, so the GitHub/GitLab comment task fails and no comment is posted.

title: Flagged table widgets render an empty hardcoded table
body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, `tableResultComponent` ignores `result.data`, `result.meta`, column fields, aliases, and the loading state and instead renders `TableWidgetVisualization` with `columns={[]}` and `tableData.data: []`. An empty `columns` array is truthy, so the visualization will not infer columns from meta either. Any org with that flag on sees blank dashboard table widgets instead of the query results.

title: Replay error context reads title/message that stored events do not have
body: `fetch_error_details` builds the Seer log from `data.get("title")` and `data.get("message")` on the raw nodestore payload. Stored error events usually keep the exception under `exception.values` / `metadata` (`type` and `value`); `title` is computed on the Event model and is often absent, and `message` is frequently empty. The log becomes `User experienced an error: ': ' at ...`, so exception type and value never reach the summary. The new test expects `ZeroDivisionError` and `division by zero` in that log after storing an exception-only event, which this field choice does not produce.

title: Error events are not ordered against replay segment timestamps
body: Chronological merge compares nodestore `timestamp` (unix seconds, and sometimes an ISO-8601 string) with the raw segment event `timestamp`. Recording segments are rrweb payloads whose timestamps are milliseconds. A seconds value is always less than a millisecond timestamp, so every error is emitted before every breadcrumb; if the stored timestamp is a string, `str < float` raises TypeError and the summarize request 500s. That is a regression for replays that have linked errors, because this endpoint previously summarized breadcrumbs without this comparison. The unit test avoids it by fabricating segment timestamps in seconds.

title: Error IDs are queried with page-filter dates the AI tab never sends
body: Error IDs now come from `query_replay_instance` using `start`/`end` from `get_filter_params(request, project)`. Segment loading (`fetch_segments_metadata`) does not use that window. The replay AI tab calls `/replays/{id}/summarize/breadcrumbs/` with no `statsPeriod`, `start`, or `end`. Depending on the default stats period, either the request 400s (breaking an endpoint that previously did not need dates) or error lookup is limited to a window shorter than replay retention, so older replays are summarized with no error context while their breadcrumbs still load.

title: Hidden span attributes are only removed while searching
body: `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` (`is_segment`, `project_id`, `received`) is applied only inside the `searchQuery` branch. When the search box is empty the function returns `sortAttributes(attributes)` unfiltered, so those fields still render. When the user searches, the same names are excluded even if the query matches them. The hide list needs to apply before the search filter, not instead of the unfiltered list.

title: 60s deadline is too short for a 100-identity refresh batch
body: `check_auth_identities` now has `processing_deadline_duration=60`, but `check_auth` still enqueues up to `chunk_size` (default 100) identities and this task refreshes them sequentially via external IdP calls. That routinely exceeds 60s. `check_auth` already sets `last_synced=now` before the task runs, so if the worker kills the task and does not retry the same id list, the unfinished identities are skipped until the next ~24h cycle and SSO validity is not refreshed. If it does retry, the same chunk keeps timing out and hammering the IdP.

title: Report URL validation rejects real browser documents and aborts the batch
body: `url` is a DRF `URLField`, whose default validator only allows http(s)/ftp. Reporting API document URLs include `about:blank`, `blob:`, `chrome-extension:`, and `file:` URLs, so those reports fail validation. The handler then returns 422 on the first invalid item and does not record metrics for any later valid reports in the same array. Browsers post mixed batches, and the previous dataclass path accepted unknown types and non-http URLs and still counted them.

title: Feedback summary ignores the environment page filter
body: The summary request sends the normalized datetime and `selection.projects`, but not `selection.environments`. The feedback list page is wrapped in page filters, so the list and search respect the environment selector while the summary does not. A user filtered to one environment still gets a summary of feedback from every environment in the project/date range, which can contradict the list beside it.

title: Trace waterfall wrapper dropped height: 100%
body: The waterfall root was a flex column with `flex-grow: 1` and `height: 100%`. It is now `<Flex direction="column" flex={1}>`, which does not set `height: 100%`. The trace view sizes this pane with a height chain rather than only flex-grow, so the waterfall can collapse and the virtualized span tree no longer fills the viewport.

title: Custom cell renderers cannot return falsy nodes
body: Both head and body renderers treat any falsy return as "use the fallback" (`if (cell)`), but the documented contract is that only `undefined` means fallback. A custom renderer that returns `0`, `''`, or `null` (valid React output, and a reasonable way to blank a cell) is discarded and the default field renderer runs instead.

title: installation_id is persisted before the OAuth state check
body: OAuthLoginView copies installation_id from the query string into pipeline state before it verifies that state equals pipeline.signature. bind_state writes the session immediately (the happy path depends on that, because installation_id must survive the redirect to GitHub). A request that then fails the state check still returns the error page, but the overwritten installation_id remains. PipelineAdvancerView is CSRF-exempt and this endpoint is a top-level GET, so a cross-site navigation to /extensions/github/setup/?installation_id=<attacker>&state=invalid is enough to poison an in-progress install. The victim's later successful OAuth callback does not carry installation_id, and GitHubInstallation prefers the stored value. The victim's organization is then linked using the attacker's installation id.

title: Installer identity is not checked on first install
body: The new check that the OAuth login matches metadata['sender']['login'] runs only when an Integration row already exists and has no OrganizationIntegration. If Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id) raises DoesNotExist, dispatch returns pipeline.next_step() and never reads github_authenticated_user. That is the normal first-install path: the installation webhook that records sender is asynchronous and often loses the race with the browser redirect, and build_integration only copies state['sender'] — it never receives or compares github_authenticated_user. Supplying an attacker installation_id (setup URL or the poisoned pipeline state) before that row exists links it to the victim's Sentry organization with no user check. The guarantee in the PR — fail on a mismatch between the OAuth user and the user who installed the GitHub App — is not enforced for new installations. The new test posts the webhook first, so it never covers this path.

title: Re-link crashes when metadata has no sender
body: On the re-link path the code indexes integration.metadata['sender']['login'] with no guard. build_integration only stores sender when pipeline state already has it, and this flow never writes github_authenticated_user into metadata. An ACTIVE Integration without a sender dict — older rows, rows created only by build_integration, or a webhook that stored sender under a different shape — raises KeyError or TypeError instead of the installation error page. The setup popup 500s and the re-link cannot finish.

title: Non-active Integration rows can no longer be reinstalled
body: Previously, an Integration that existed but had no OrganizationIntegration always continued to pipeline.next_step(), which re-fetches the GitHub installation and reactivates the record. The new lookup requires status=ObjectStatus.ACTIVE and turns DoesNotExist into the generic authenticity error. ObjectStatus includes DISABLED, PENDING_DELETION, and HIDDEN, so a leftover non-active row with no org link — a normal uninstall leftover — now blocks reinstall. The message tells the user the request could not be verified and to restart, which cannot succeed until the row is deleted out of band.

title: Token exchange omits redirect_uri sent on authorize
body: The authorize redirect includes redirect_uri, but the code exchange posts only code, client_id, and client_secret. RFC 6749 section 4.1.3 requires the token request to repeat redirect_uri when it was included in the authorization request, and the values must be identical. GitHub's POST /login/oauth/access_token documents the same parameter and rejects mismatches (redirect_uri_mismatch or an invalid/expired code). The new tests stub that URL and return a token no matter the body, so they stay green if GitHub rejects the exchange and every real install stops on the generic error page. The authorize URL is also built by string interpolation rather than urlencode, so the redirect_uri GitHub records may not byte-match a later form-encoded value.

title: OAuth network failures skip the installation error page
body: safe_urlopen of the token endpoint and the following get_user_info call sit outside the try/except that maps a bad token body to the installation error page. A timeout, connection error, or ApiError from either call propagates as an unhandled 500 in the setup popup. This change is supposed to render github-integration-failed.html when GitHub cannot mint a token or the user cannot be identified; that page is only reached when body parsing fails or access_token/login is missing.

title: installation-not-found test no longer hits the GitHub 404 path
body: test_installation_not_found used to request setup_path with an installation_id and assert build_integration's 404 text "The GitHub installation could not be found." It now overwrites that response with a second request whose state is ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05, not the pipeline signature the other tests lock in (9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3), and asserts the generic "Invalid installation request." string. Unlike the updated happy-path tests it never calls init_path, so there is no session pipeline; PipelineAdvancerView redirects to / with "Invalid request.", which does not contain the new expected bytes. If a pipeline did exist, the wrong state is rejected in OAuthLoginView and the installations API is never called, so a regression in the 404 handling would not be caught.

title: User-mismatch test posts a webhook with a stale signature
body: test_github_user_mismatch changes INSTALLATION_EVENT_EXAMPLE (installation id and sender.login) but sends a static X-Hub-Signature of sha1=d184e6717f8bfbcc291ebc8c0756ee446c6c9486, the digest of the unmodified fixture. The webhook view HMACs the raw body, so this delivery is rejected and never creates an Integration whose sender is attacker; the assert resp.status_code == 204 fails when verification is enabled. The test then reuses state 9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3, captured for the default org, after login_as(user_2) and a new organization, and asserts the same "Invalid installation request." string that OAuthLoginView returns for a state mismatch. Neither a pass nor a fail shows that the sender comparison ran.

title: Installer identity check is skipped for new installations
body: GitHubInstallation.dispatch returns pipeline.next_step() as soon as Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id) raises DoesNotExist (integration.py around line 481). That is the normal install path: assert_setup_flow never creates a webhook Integration and still finishes successfully. It is also the race where GitHub's setup redirect arrives before the installation webhook. build_integration only reads installation_id (and optional sender); it never reads github_authenticated_user, so the OAuth login collected by OAuthLoginView is discarded. Linking then uses the GitHub App's own credentials. Anyone who knows a Sentry GitHub App installation_id (it is in the post-install redirect and in GitHub's installation settings URL) can attach that installation to their Sentry organization before an Integration row exists. After that, the real installer hits the existing "installed on another Sentry organization" error and is locked out. The new sender comparison only runs later, and only when an ACTIVE Integration already exists and has no OrganizationIntegration.

title: OAuth state is not unique per install attempt
body: OAuthLoginView sets the OAuth state query parameter to pipeline.signature (integration.py line 402) and later accepts the callback when that value matches (line 412). The new tests require this state to be exactly 9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3 for every fresh pipeline, including organization_2's pipeline in test_github_installed_on_another_org, which only reaches the "installed on another Sentry organization" error after the state check. So the value is not a per-flow nonce. PipelineAdvancerView has csrf_protect = False and auth_required = False, and the callback is a GET, so a top-level navigation still sends the session cookie under SameSite=Lax. Any user can start an install, copy state from their own authorize redirect, and send a victim who has an in-progress pipeline to /extensions/github/setup/?code=<attacker code>&state=<that value>&installation_id=<attacker installation>. The callback is accepted, github_authenticated_user becomes the attacker, and the sender check then passes because both sides are the attacker, linking the attacker's GitHub App installation to the victim's Sentry organization.

title: installation_id is stored before the callback is authenticated
body: OAuthLoginView copies request.GET installation_id into pipeline state (integration.py lines 397-399) before it checks state or exchanges the code. A request that only has installation_id still performs that write and then redirects to GitHub OAuth because state is missing (line 401). GitHub's OAuth callback does not include installation_id, so it will not clear the poisoned value. GitHubInstallation also prefers a query-string installation_id over the saved one (lines 448-450). The setup endpoint is an unauthenticated GET with CSRF disabled, so a user who already has an install pipeline and opens .../extensions/github/setup/?installation_id=<id> gets that id attached to their session. After they complete the OAuth step, the pipeline links that substituted installation. Together with the branch that skips the installer check when no Integration row exists, a malicious link during install attaches the attacker's GitHub App installation to the victim's Sentry organization.

title: Token exchange omits redirect_uri sent at authorize
body: The authorize redirect always includes redirect_uri (integration.py lines 404-408), but the access-token POST (lines 416-423) sends only code, client_id, and client_secret. GitHub's token endpoint, and OAuth 2.0 RFC 6749 section 4.1.3, require the same redirect_uri on the token request when it was included in the authorization request; otherwise GitHub returns an error and no access_token. This code treats a missing access_token as a failed install and shows "Invalid installation request." The new tests stub https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token to always return a token, so they never observe the rejection. The authorize URL is also built with string interpolation instead of urlencode, so redirect_uri is not percent-encoded and can fail to match a properly encoded value. Because every GitHub install now goes through this step, token exchange can fail for all users once it is live.

title: Installer check crashes when sender login is missing
body: When an ACTIVE Integration exists but has no OrganizationIntegration, the code compares the OAuth login to integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] (integration.py lines 501-504) with no existence check. build_integration only writes metadata["sender"] if state already contains sender, and test_basic_flow expects a pipeline-created integration to have no sender key at all. Hitting this branch for a row without that nested login (pipeline-created integration, older webhook data, or sender stored as a string) raises KeyError or TypeError. The user gets a 500 instead of the installation-failed dialog, and the security comparison never runs. A missing sender should fail closed through error().

title: New security checks are not actually asserted
body: test_installation_not_found still stubs the installation API as 404, but the follow-up request uses state=ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05, which is not the pipeline signature the other tests use (9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3). OAuthLoginView rejects that state and returns the generic invalid-installation page before build_integration or the 404 path runs. The assertion was changed from "The GitHub installation could not be found." to "Invalid installation request.", so the test stays green if 404 handling is removed. test_github_user_mismatch has the same blind spot: it only asserts that generic string, which is also what state mismatch and token failure return, so it does not prove the sender comparison ran. That test also changes installation id and sender.login on INSTALLATION_EVENT_EXAMPLE but keeps the original X-Hub-Signature (test_integration.py line 423). If webhook signature verification is enabled, the webhook is rejected and no Integration with sender "attacker" is created, so the mismatch path is never set up.

title: installation_id is saved before OAuth state is validated
body: OAuthLoginView writes installation_id into the pipeline with bind_state before it checks that state matches pipeline.signature and before the authorization code is exchanged. bind_state persists the session immediately, and PipelineAdvancerView leaves csrf_protect = False, so a cross-site GET to /extensions/github/setup/?installation_id=<attacker> overwrites an in-progress install even when state is missing or wrong and the view then returns the error page. The later legitimate OAuth callback usually has no installation_id, and GitHubInstallation falls back to that poisoned value (request.GET.get("installation_id", pipeline.fetch_state("installation_id"))). The victim's org is then attached to the attacker's GitHub App installation whenever the sender check is skipped, or their own install is broken if the check runs. Persist installation_id only after state validation succeeds, and do not update pipeline state on the failure path.

title: User-match check skipped when Integration does not exist
body: The new control is supposed to reject a mismatch between the OAuth GitHub login and the user who installed the app, but that comparison runs only after an Integration row is already loaded. On Integration.DoesNotExist, GitHubInstallation returns pipeline.next_step() with no check. build_integration never reads github_authenticated_user; it fetches /app/installations/{id} with the GitHub App JWT, which can see every installation of this app, not only ones the OAuth user owns. Webhook creation of the Integration races the browser redirect, and any installation whose Sentry row is missing or was deleted takes this path. Combined with installation_id coming from the query string, an attacker can link a chosen GitHub App installation to the current Sentry organization and inherit the app's access to that account's repositories. Fail closed unless the OAuth user is verified against the installing user, or against installations visible to that user's token, before the org link is created.

title: Token request drops redirect_uri sent on authorize
body: The authorize redirect includes redirect_uri, but the access-token POST only sends code, client_id, and client_secret. GitHub's token endpoint, following RFC 6749 section 4.1.3, requires the same redirect_uri on the token request when it was included in authorization; otherwise it returns an error instead of access_token. This handler then always shows the invalid-installation page, so every install fails after the user authorizes, and that page is the same one used for real verification failures, so a manual check of the error UI does not prove the happy path. The comment says this mirrors OAuth2CallbackView.get_token_params, which includes redirect_uri. Tests stub the token URL and ignore the POST body, so they stay green. Send the same redirect_uri used in the authorize request, build that URL with urlencode (the current f-string leaves redirect_uri unencoded), and accept both form and JSON token bodies the way the shared callback view does.

title: Missing sender crashes the re-link path
body: The match check indexes integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] directly. Integrations created before sender was stored, or created by build_integration when pipeline state has no sender, have no sender object. That raises KeyError, or TypeError if sender is null, and the install 500s instead of rendering the installation-failed page. This is exactly the re-link branch (Integration exists, no OrganizationIntegration), so those records cannot be reinstalled. The inequality also does not require both values to be non-empty strings, so a null sender login and a missing github_authenticated_user would compare equal and be allowed through. Read sender with a safe lookup and deny unless both logins are present and equal.

title: User-info fetch errors bypass the error page
body: After the token exchange, get_user_info(payload["access_token"]) is called with no try/except. HTTP errors, network failures, and a non-mapping response propagate as an uncaught exception and a 500, unlike a missing access_token or a bad state, which return the installation-failed page. A GitHub /user failure during install therefore aborts opaquely, and the exception can capture the request that carries the new user access token into error reporting. Catch API failures and treat a missing login the same as the other verification failures.

title: Security tests never reach the checks they describe
body: test_installation_not_found used to assert "The GitHub installation could not be found." when the installation API returned 404. It now calls the callback with state ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05, which is not the pipeline signature 9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3, so it fails the state check and never reaches build_integration. test_github_user_mismatch mutates the installation webhook body (installation id and sender login) but keeps HTTP_X_HUB_SIGNATURE sha1=d184e6717f8bfbcc291ebc8c0756ee446c6c9486 from the original fixture, so signature verification rejects it when enabled, and then it reuses that same hardcoded state for a second user while asserting only the generic "Invalid installation request." string. That string is also returned for a state mismatch, a bad code, and a missing token, so the test can pass without comparing octocat to sender "attacker" or showing that no OrganizationIntegration was created. The token stub returns access_token regardless of redirect_uri. Recompute the webhook signature, drive a callback whose state actually matches that pipeline, and assert the specific denial for user mismatch, missing sender, and Integration.DoesNotExist.

title: AssignmentSource.queued is fixed at import time
body: queued is declared as `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`. Dataclass defaults are evaluated once when the class body runs, not per instance, and datetime is not rejected as a mutable default. Every AssignmentSource built without an explicit queued value — including every AssignmentSource.from_integration() call on the inbound webhook path — therefore shares one timestamp captured when the worker process imported the module. to_dict() copies that value into the Celery payload, so the field does not record when the assignment was queued and cannot order or expire the rapid successive assignee updates this PR is about. Use field(default_factory=timezone.now).

title: Outbound assignee task payload embeds a raw datetime
body: sync_group_assignee_outbound passes assignment_source.to_dict() into sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async. to_dict() is dataclasses.asdict(), so assignment_source_dict contains a live datetime under queued. Standard JSON encoding of that payload raises TypeError: Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable. apply_async is called from GroupAssignee.assign and deassign, which sync_group_assignee_inbound now always reaches for integration-driven assignee changes, so a JSON task serializer fails the inbound webhook and never enqueues outbound sync to other integrations. Encoders that stringify datetimes do not raise, but AssignmentSource.from_dict only does cls(**input_dict) and does not parse ISO-8601, so queued arrives on the worker as a str. Store queued with isoformat() (or a numeric timestamp) and parse it in from_dict.

title: Unparseable assignment source fails open and restarts the loop
body: If assignment_source_dict is present but AssignmentSource.from_dict returns None, the task still calls should_sync("outbound_assignee", None) and, when outbound assignee sync is enabled, writes the assignee back to the external issue. from_dict returns None on any TypeError or ValueError (missing fields, unexpected keys, a queued value that cannot be constructed) and does not log. A source payload that fails to parse is then indistinguishable from a Sentry-originated assignment, which is exactly the path that updates the originating integration and restarts the sync cycle. When a source dict was supplied and cannot be reconstructed, outbound sync should be skipped rather than performed.

title: Cycle-break tests miss the inbound webhook path
body: The new test only calls GroupAssignee.objects.assign with an AssignmentSource and asserts that the same integration's sync_assignee_outbound is not invoked. Nothing calls sync_group_assignee_inbound, which is the webhook entry point that must attach AssignmentSource.from_integration. Removing that argument would restore the production loop and still pass CI. Deassign with a matching source is also untested, and there is no two-integration case proving a different linked integration still receives the outbound update. tests/sentry/integrations/services/test_assignment_source.py never round-trips to_dict() through JSON and never checks that two instances get different queued timestamps, so the shared default and the non-serializable task payload are invisible.

title: AssignmentSource.queued is fixed at import time
body: AssignmentSource.queued is declared as `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`. Dataclass defaults are evaluated once when the class body runs, not when each instance is created, and datetime is immutable so this does not raise the mutable-default error. Every AssignmentSource built by from_integration (the inbound webhook path) or by from_dict when queued is omitted therefore shares one timestamp: the moment this module was imported in that process, not when the assignment was queued. to_dict()/asdict() copies that stale value into the Celery kwargs for sync_assignee_outbound, so task payloads carry a misleading queue time. The cycle check does not read queued today, but the field cannot be used to order or drop the rapid assignee updates this change is about, and debugging those races from the payload will be wrong. tests/sentry/integrations/services/test_assignment_source.py only asserts queued is not None, so it does not catch this. Use field(default_factory=timezone.now). Also, to_dict() emits the raw datetime and from_dict() will not parse an ISO string back into a datetime, so the dict is only safe if the task serializer preserves datetime objects.

title: Inbound webhook cycle-break path is untested
body: The production fix attaches AssignmentSource inside sync_group_assignee_inbound on both assign (line 115) and deassign (line 98), then relies on the outbound task to skip the originating integration. The only new test, test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration, calls GroupAssignee.objects.assign directly with an AssignmentSource and never goes through sync_group_assignee_inbound. The existing inbound tests call that function but do not run tasks or assert that outbound sync is skipped. Deleting the new assignment_source arguments from the inbound entry point would leave CI green and the Jira echo loop intact. There is also no test that a second, different integration still receives the outbound update when the source matches only one of them; a check that skipped every outbound sync whenever any source was set would not be caught.

title: AssignmentSource.queued is frozen at import time
body: queued is declared as queued: datetime = timezone.now() on the dataclass. That expression is evaluated once when the class body runs, not when an instance is created. Every AssignmentSource.from_integration() call on the inbound webhook path therefore stores the same timestamp: the moment this module was first imported in the process. Long-lived web and worker processes make that value hours or days old, so the field cannot distinguish or order the rapid successive assignee changes this PR is about. Dataclass equality includes queued, so distinct events for the same integration also compare equal for the life of the process, and to_dict() writes that stale timestamp into every sync_assignee_outbound payload. This needs field(default_factory=timezone.now). The new test only checks that queued is not None, so it does not catch the shared value.

title: to_dict() embeds a datetime in Celery task kwargs
body: to_dict() returns asdict(self), so queued is a raw datetime. sync_group_assignee_outbound passes that dict straight to sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async as assignment_source_dict. A JSON task transport (Celery JSON serializer, or Sentry taskworker) cannot encode datetime and raises TypeError while enqueueing. That apply_async call is synchronous inside GroupAssignee.assign and deassign, so an inbound webhook can persist the assignee and then fail, and the change is never pushed to any other integration. from_dict only does cls(**input_dict) inside a ValueError/TypeError handler and does not parse ISO-8601 strings. If a serializer stringifies the timestamp, queued is left as a string; if construction raises, from_dict returns None. The outbound task treats a None source as "not an echo" and performs the sync anyway, which brings the assignee loop back. self.tasks() runs eagerly and does not round-trip the serializer, and no test calls from_dict(source.to_dict()), so CI will not catch this.

title: Echo guard drops every linked issue on the source integration
body: should_sync returns False for the entire integration whenever sync_source.integration_id matches org_integration.integration_id. AssignmentSource does not record the external issue key, and sync_group_assignee_outbound attaches that same source to every GroupLink on the Sentry issue. A group may be linked to multiple external issues on one integration; GroupLink uniqueness is on the external-issue id, not the integration. An assignee webhook from Jira ticket A therefore skips outbound sync for ticket A and also for ticket B on the same Jira integration, so ticket B's assignee stays stale even with outbound assignee sync enabled. sync_group_assignee_inbound already has external_issue_key, and the outbound task already loads the target ExternalIssue, so the guard should skip only the originating issue. Skipping that one key still stops the echo; GroupAssignee.assign does not enqueue outbound sync when the assignee is unchanged, so a follow-up webhook that maps to the same Sentry user will not bounce.

title: Inbound wiring and cross-integration sync are untested
body: The new test calls GroupAssignee.objects.assign directly with an AssignmentSource and only covers the matching-integration assign case. test_assignee_sync_inbound_assign and test_assignee_sync_inbound_deassign call sync_group_assignee_inbound, which is the production webhook entry point that must pass assignment_source into assign and deassign, but they never assert that outbound sync to the source integration is skipped. Removing those assignment_source= arguments in sync.py would leave both inbound tests green and restore the loop. There is also no test that a second integration still receives the outbound update, and no test that deassign with a matching source skips outbound (test_assignee_sync_outbound_unassign still expects assignment_source=None). A guard that dropped every sourced sync, or a deassign path that forgot the source, would pass CI.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract and crashes on use
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but implements none of its abstract methods (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the new build_occurrence_and_event_data). Instantiating it raises TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler. It is still assigned as MetricAlertFire.detector_handler, and Detector.detector_handler calls that class with no try/except. Any detector whose type slug is metric_alert_fire will therefore throw while process_detectors resolves the handler and abort the rest of the batch. The previous handler was a concrete DetectorHandler whose evaluate() returned an empty list, so this is a regression. The TODO above the class still says it will become a stateful detector later, which no longer matches the base class.

title: test_dedupe expects an occurrence for the wrong group key
body: TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds the expected occurrence with build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", 6, PriorityLevel.HIGH), then calls evaluate_group_key_value with group_key "group_key" and value 10. The helper sets IssueOccurrence.fingerprint from handler.build_fingerprint(group_key), so the expected fingerprint is "{detector_id}:val1" while the code under test builds "{detector_id}:group_key". DetectorEvaluationResult and IssueOccurrence compare by value, so the equality assertion fails and the later dedupe-skip assertion is never reached. The expected value 6 also does not match the evaluated value 10; that second mismatch is currently hidden only because the helper ignores value.

title: Occurrence fingerprint is not tied to the resolve fingerprint
body: A non-OK transition now stores whatever IssueOccurrence build_occurrence_and_event_data returns, including its fingerprint, and process_detectors publishes that occurrence. The OK transition in the same method always emits StatusChangeMessage(fingerprint=self.build_fingerprint(group_key), new_status=RESOLVED). The hook is not passed that fingerprint, the base class does not overwrite occurrence.fingerprint afterward, and the new abstract method does not require subclasses to call build_fingerprint. If those fingerprints differ, the later resolve cannot match the issue this detector opened, while detector state is still marked inactive. Tests do not lock the invariant: the mock happens to call build_fingerprint, and test_above_below_threshold hardcodes the resolve fingerprint instead of asserting it equals the firing occurrence's fingerprint.

title: Occurrence tests never check the measured value
body: build_mock_occurrence_and_event accepts value but never puts it on the IssueOccurrence or event_data, so result equality cannot tell whether build_occurrence_and_event_data received the measured value. Call sites also pass the wrong number and still pass: test_state_results_multi_group builds the group_2 expectation with 6 while the packet value is 10; TestEvaluate.test_results_on_change evaluates 100 but expects an occurrence built with 6; TestEvaluate.test_dedupe evaluates 8 but expects 6. A regression that forwarded the dedupe value, the threshold, or another group's value would not be caught.

title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
body: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate's docstring still says it returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult. The method now returns a dict keyed by DetectorGroupKey, and process_detectors iterates .values() on that dict. A caller that follows the docstring and iterates the return value will get group keys rather than evaluation results.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler can no longer be constructed
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler and only has `pass`, so it does not implement the abstract methods counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data. Instantiating that class raises TypeError. MetricAlertFire.detector_handler still points at it, and Detector.detector_handler constructs the handler with group_type.detector_handler(self). Any processing of a metric_alert_fire detector therefore crashes inside process_detectors (the exception is not caught, so the rest of the detector batch fails too). The previous handler was a concrete DetectorHandler whose evaluate() returned [] and could be instantiated safely.

title: test_dedupe expected occurrence uses the wrong group key
body: TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds the expected IssueOccurrence with build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", 6, ...) but calls evaluate_group_key_value with group_key "group_key" and value 10. build_mock_occurrence_and_event puts the group key into the occurrence fingerprint via build_fingerprint, and IssueOccurrence equality includes fingerprint, so the expected DetectorEvaluationResult cannot equal the value evaluate_group_key_value actually returns. That assertion fails and the dedupe-skip half of the test never runs.

title: Tests build expected occurrences with the wrong evaluated value
body: build_mock_occurrence_and_event ignores its value argument, and several assertions pass a value that is not the one being evaluated. test_state_results_multi_group feeds group_2=10 but builds the expected occurrence with 6 (line 191). TestEvaluate.test_results_on_change evaluates 100 but expects an occurrence built with 6 (line 490). TestEvaluate.test_dedupe evaluates 8 but expects 6 (line 510). Those tests still pass if build_occurrence_and_event_data is called with the wrong value, so the new hook's value argument is not actually checked.

title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
body: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate now returns dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult], but the docstring still says it "returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult". Callers that follow the docstring will treat the return value as a list (index it, iterate results rather than result objects, and so on) and break against the new contract.

title: Metric alert handler is abstract and crashes when constructed
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler and has an empty body. StatefulDetectorHandler still has abstract methods (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the new build_occurrence_and_event_data), so instantiating MetricAlertDetectorHandler raises TypeError. The class remains MetricAlertFire.detector_handler, and Detector.detector_handler constructs it for any detector whose slug is metric_alert_fire. Previously this was a concrete DetectorHandler whose evaluate() returned an empty list. process_detectors does not catch that TypeError, so one such detector aborts the whole batch instead of no-opping. Implement the abstract methods, or keep a concrete DetectorHandler until a real stateful implementation exists.

title: Fired occurrence fingerprint is not tied to the resolve fingerprint
body: On a non-OK transition, evaluate_group_key_value publishes whatever IssueOccurrence build_occurrence_and_event_data returns, and it never sets or checks occurrence.fingerprint. On the later OK transition it publishes a StatusChangeMessage whose fingerprint is always build_fingerprint(group_key) (`{detector_id}` or `{detector_id}:{group_key}`). Issue resolution matches on that fingerprint. The new hook is not given the fingerprint, and the abstract method does not require the subclass to use build_fingerprint, so an occurrence opened under any other fingerprint will not be resolved when the detector returns to OK. Pass build_fingerprint(group_key) into the hook or overwrite the returned occurrence's fingerprint before publishing.

title: Occurrences are published before dedupe and detector state are committed
body: process_detectors sends each result to Kafka via create_issue_occurrence_from_result and only then calls handler.commit_state_updates(), which is what persists the dedupe value and active/priority transition queued during evaluate. This PR is what starts attaching an IssueOccurrence to threshold breaches on that path. If publish raises on a later group key, or the process stops before the commit, the dedupe key and stored status are unchanged. The same packet is evaluated again as a new transition and another occurrence is emitted. Occurrence ids are chosen by the subclass and are not derived from detector id, group key, and dedupe value, so the retry is not idempotent and users can get duplicate issues.

title: Group-key unit test expects an occurrence for a different key
body: TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds the expected IssueOccurrence with build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", 6, ...) but calls evaluate_group_key_value with group_key "group_key" and value 10. The handler forwards that group key into build_occurrence_and_event_data, which puts it on the occurrence fingerprint (`{detector_id}:group_key` versus the expected `{detector_id}:val1`). DetectorEvaluationResult and IssueOccurrence compare by value, so this assertion fails. Build the expected occurrence with group_key "group_key" and value 10.

title: Occurrence tests never assert the measured value
body: build_mock_occurrence_and_event accepts value and never uses it, and MockDetectorStateHandler.build_occurrence_and_event_data only forwards to that helper. Assertions therefore stay green if evaluate passes the wrong measurement. Concrete mismatches already in the tests: test_state_results_multi_group has group_2=10 but builds the expected occurrence with 6; test_results_on_change evaluates 100 but expects an occurrence built with 6; TestEvaluate.test_dedupe evaluates 8 but expects 6. Put value on the occurrence (for example evidence_data) and pass the actual packet value, or the new hook argument is untested.

title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
body: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate's docstring says it returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult. This PR changes the return type to a dict keyed by DetectorGroupKey. Callers that follow the docstring will iterate keys or treat the result as a sequence of evaluation objects. Update the docstring to describe the dict.

title: Occurrence context drops the prepared schedule_type display
body: get_monitor_environment_context copies monitor.config and, when schedule_type is present, replaces it on that copy with monitor.get_schedule_type_display() so the issue occurrence can carry a human-readable schedule. The returned context ignores that copy and sends monitor_environment.monitor.config instead. The display conversion is discarded, so every monitor incident occurrence published to Kafka still has the raw schedule_type. The returned config is also the live in-memory model dict, so any later mutation of the occurrence context config mutates the monitor instance.

title: failure_issue_threshold does not require N consecutive failures
body: try_incident_threshold is what opens a monitor incident after failure_issue_threshold consecutive failures. The threshold==1 path correctly uses only the current failed check-in. For any larger threshold it loads at most that many latest check-ins of any status and returns without opening an incident only if one of them is CheckInStatus.OK. It never requires the window to contain failure_issue_threshold rows, and it never requires those rows to be ERROR, MISSED, or TIMEOUT. A monitor set to threshold 3 whose first check-in fails therefore has a one-row window with no OK, and this still sets the environment to MonitorStatus.ERROR, get_or_creates a MonitorIncident, emits issue occurrences, and sends monitor_environment_failed. An in-progress check-in in the window counts as one of the N slots the same way, so a single real failure can both pass this gate and be published as a failure occurrence. Users who raised the threshold above 1 still get incidents and issues immediately.

title: Failure threshold opens an incident without enough failures
body: try_incident_threshold only treats the failure_issue_threshold window as "not yet an incident" when one of the fetched check-ins is OK. It never requires that window to actually contain failure_issue_threshold failed check-ins. The query is sliced to that many rows and then, if none are OK, the environment is saved as MonitorStatus.ERROR, a MonitorIncident is created, and issue occurrences are emitted. A monitor configured with failure_issue_threshold=3 and only one failed check-in (typical for a new monitor, or any history shorter than the threshold) therefore fails immediately. Non-failure statuses other than OK, such as in-progress, also do not block this path and still occupy slots in the slice, so the real failure count can be below the threshold even when the slice is full. If the slice is empty, the same path still persists ERROR and then raises IndexError on previous_checkins[0], leaving the environment failed with no incident and later failures stuck on the already-ERROR branch, which does not create one. Before saving status or calling get_or_create, require a full window whose every status is a real failure (error, missed, or timeout).

title: Occurrence context drops the prepared schedule_type
body: get_monitor_environment_context copies monitor.config and, when schedule_type is present, replaces it with monitor.get_schedule_type_display() so the issue event gets a human-readable schedule. The returned context ignores that copy and sends monitor_environment.monitor.config instead. Every monitor incident occurrence therefore keeps the raw stored schedule_type (typically the integer choice value) rather than the display label just computed, and the event payload shares the model’s live config dict instead of a detached copy. Downstream mutation or display of that context will not match what this function prepared. Return the modified config dict.

title: Incident opens before failure_issue_threshold consecutive failures
body: In try_incident_threshold, when failure_issue_threshold is greater than 1, the code loads at most that many recent check-ins (ordered by date_added, then reversed) and returns early only if one of them is CheckInStatus.OK. It never requires the window to contain failure_issue_threshold rows. A shorter history has no OK row, so execution still sets MonitorEnvironment.status to ERROR, get_or_creates a MonitorIncident, emits issue occurrences, and sends monitor_environment_failed. A new or ACTIVE monitor with failure_issue_threshold of 3 therefore opens an incident on its first failed check-in, and stays in ERROR so later failures keep attaching occurrences, until a success resolves it. The configured consecutive-failure tolerance is ignored whenever fewer than N check-ins exist. An empty slice also falls through this check and then raises IndexError on previous_checkins[0], aborting failure processing instead of returning False. Require len(previous_checkins) >= failure_issue_threshold before transitioning.

title: Non-failure check-ins count toward the failure threshold
body: The threshold gate only tests whether any row equals CheckInStatus.OK. Every other status, including in-progress check-ins that are stored as MonitorCheckIn rows, is treated as part of the failure streak and also occupies a slot in the limited window. With failure_issue_threshold 2, a recent window of one in-progress check-in plus one error contains no OK row, so the environment is marked ERROR and an incident is opened after a single real failure. An in-progress row can also push an older OK check-in out of the N-row window so that success is ignored. Only error, missed, and timeout rows should count toward the consecutive-failure threshold.

title: Occurrence context drops the adjusted schedule_type
body: get_monitor_environment_context copies monitor.config and, when schedule_type is present, replaces it with monitor.get_schedule_type_display() so the issue event can show a human-readable schedule type. The returned dict ignores that copy and sends monitor_environment.monitor.config instead. The display conversion never reaches Kafka, so contexts.monitor.config.schedule_type stays the raw stored value (typically an integer) on every monitor incident occurrence. The payload also aliases the live config dict, so any later in-place mutation of the event context mutates the in-memory monitor. Return the adjusted copy.

title: Mixed failure-reason text does not match the documented message
body: get_failure_reason is shown as the Failure reason evidence on monitor issues. Its docstring specifies strings such as "2 missed check-ins, 1 timeout check-in and 1 error check-in were detected" and "A failed check-in was detected". For more than one failure it formats each status as "%(count)d %(status)s" using the bare words missed/timeout/error, joins them, and appends a single "check-ins detected". Mixed failures therefore render as "2 missed, 1 timeout and 1 error check-ins detected" (no per-status "check-in(s)", and a plural noun for the whole list). The singular path returns "An error check-in was detected" (or missed/timeout), not the documented sentence. The docstring also misspells the summary as "humam readible". The evidence copy users see for multi-status incidents is wrong relative to the function's own contract.

title: Hung spawn flushers are never killed, so restarts overlap
body: Workers are created with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, i.e. SpawnProcess. That class subclasses multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess, not multiprocessing.Process, so isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is always false for real flusher processes. The new guard therefore never calls kill() in _ensure_processes_alive, and the same check in join() never calls terminate(). Previously kill() was unconditional, so this is a regression on the default single-process path as well as the multi-process path. A hung worker is left running, the restart counter is incremented, and _create_process_for_shards overwrites self.processes and drops the only reference the strategy keeps. The orphan keeps calling flush_segments/produce/done_flush_segments on the same shards as the replacement, which can duplicate segments on the buffered-segments topic or delete Redis state the other worker is still producing. The replacement also resets process_healthy_since, so once it looks healthy the parent stops retrying and the orphan runs until the consumer process exits. join() likewise cannot SIGTERM a worker blocked in Redis or Kafka that never observes the stopped flag. Thread-mode restarts (produce_to_pipe) leak the same way because nothing stops the previous thread. Even after the type check is fixed (use BaseProcess, or skip only threading.Thread), kill() is asynchronous and the replacement is started immediately with no join; the old worker must be reaped before a new one is started.

title: Timed join returns while flusher processes are still running
body: join() sets a deadline, spends the full timeout in next_step.join(timeout), then walks flusher workers. If the deadline is already exhausted it breaks immediately; if it expires mid-loop the break skips every remaining worker. Those workers are neither waited on nor terminated. close() intentionally does not stop flushers (to avoid a Redis memory spike at rebalance start), so join() is the only shutdown barrier. A worker blocked in flush_segments or Kafka produce will not see stopped until that call returns, and after the break nothing signals it. Kafka rebalance then builds a new SpanFlusher for the same shards — in this process or another — while the old workers are still flushing, so both produce the same segments and race on Redis flush markers. The previous single-process join always fell through to terminate() after the wait; the early break is a regression. On the way out of join(), every worker that is still alive must be killed and joined, including when the timeout is already spent.

title: test_basic wait is a no-op, so the flush assertion is racy
body: test_basic monkeypatches time.sleep to a no-op, then after setting fac._flusher.current_drift calls time.sleep(0.1) to let the flusher thread observe the new clock. That call is the patched no-op, so it does not wait, and the extra step.poll() does not flush either: SpanFlusher.poll only forwards to the committer while flushing runs on the background thread. step.join() then sets the shared stopped flag before it waits for the thread. If the thread has not yet read the updated drift, it sees stopped and exits without producing, and (msg,) = messages fails. The race is intermittent and worse under CI load. Wait with a sleep that was bound before the patch, or poll messages until the payload appears, using a real timeout.

title: Flusher metric tag is comma-joined and inconsistently keyed
