The sibling customize pages (permalinks, colors, emojis, site texts) respond with an HTML page that boots the Ember admin app for non-XHR requests; this controller (and its missing view template) does not. Opening or refreshing `https://site/admin/customize/embedding` directly in a browser returns a raw JSON payload instead of the admin UI. Add `respond_to`/`format.html` handling plus the blank HTML view like the other admin customize controllers.

title: update/destroy 500 on unknown id instead of 404
body: `update` and `destroy` do `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` without checking the result. For a stale or invalid id (e.g. two admins, one deletes a host while the other's page still shows it), `save_host(nil)` calls `nil.host = ...` and `destroy` calls `nil.destroy`, both raising NoMethodError → 500. Additionally `save_host` dereferences `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `[:category_id]` without verifying the wrapper param exists, so any request missing the `embeddable_host` key also 500s. Raise `Discourse::NotFound` when the record doesn't exist and guard the params.

title: before_validation crashes with NoMethodError when host is nil
body: The `before_validation` callback calls `self.host.sub!(...)` twice. If `host` is nil (e.g. an API call to POST /admin/embeddable_hosts without a host value), this raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard with `self.host = self.host.to_s` or skip the substitutions when host is blank.

title: No uniqueness constraint on host
body: Neither the model nor the migration enforces uniqueness of `host`. The admin UI lets the same host be added multiple times with different categories, and `record_for_host` uses `.first`, so which category an embedded topic lands in becomes nondeterministic. Add `validates_uniqueness_of :host` and a unique index (the migration's data copy should also dedupe).

title: Hosts saved with a port can never match; input host not downcased for comparison
body: The format validation explicitly allows a port (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`) and `before_validation` strips scheme and path but keeps the port, so an admin can save `example.com:3000`. But `record_for_host` compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)` — `uri.host` never includes the port — so that row can never match any referer and the site silently can never embed. Also the bound value isn't downcased, so a mixed-case referer host won't match `lower(host)`. Either reject/normalize ports on save or include the port (and downcase the input) in the lookup.

title: Host validation regex rejects legitimate TLDs longer than 5 characters
body: The regex requires `\.[a-z]{2,5}` for the final label, so valid domains like `example.technology`, `example.international` or `example.museum` fail validation and can't be added as embedding hosts. The old free-text setting imposed no such restriction, so this is a new, undocumented limitation.

title: Fabricator file contents were swapped
body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while the newly added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the category fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`) that were deleted from the category file. The suite still passes only because Fabrication loads every file in the directory regardless of name, but the filenames are now actively misleading and the contents should be swapped back.

title: Test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' no longer tests what it claims
body: `Topic#expandable_first_post?` was changed to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` and no longer consults embeddable hosts at all. The spec still asserts that it "is false if embeddable_host is blank", but it passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false — it would pass identically if a host existed, so it guards nothing about the removed condition. The example should be renamed/rewritten to reflect the new contract (or removed).

title: New admin endpoints have no request specs
body: The specs for `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` (and `Admin::EmbeddingController`) only assert the class inherits from `Admin::AdminController`. All the actual behavior added in this PR — creating/updating a host, the fallback to `uncategorized_category_id` when category is blank, validation errors, unknown-id handling, destroy, and the embedding show payload — is completely untested, which is how the nil-record and nil-param crashes slip through.

title: OptimizedImage.downsize is defined twice; the first definition is dead code and its callers break
body: The file defines self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) at line 145 and then redefines self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) at line 149. In Ruby the second definition silently replaces the first, so the width/height variant can never be executed. Any existing caller still using the old signature breaks: a 5-argument call raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments), and a 4-argument call downsize(from, to, w, h) silently mis-binds so the integer height lands in opts, where optimize then calls opts[:allow_animation] on an Integer. Remove the leftover 145-147 definition and update any remaining callers instead of shipping two.

title: Large animated GIFs are silently flattened to their first frame
body: The new auto-downsize code calls OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...). OptimizedImage.optimize only selects the animated (gifsicle) instructions when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`, but uploaded tempfiles (e.g. /tmp/RackMultipart...) have no extension, so the check never matches the original filename or the file content. Large animated GIFs therefore go through `convert <path>[0] ...`, which keeps only the first frame; the upload then succeeds with a static image and the user's animation is silently destroyed (previously the file was rejected for size and the user kept their original). The allow_animation option passed here is effectively dead for direct uploads; detect the format from the original filename or image content instead of the tempfile path.

title: Client-side upload size check no longer honors max_image_size_kb / max_attachment_size_kb
body: validateUploadedFile used to enforce Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']; it now hardcodes 10 MB for every upload type. Letting images up to 10 MB through is the point of this feature (the server downsizes them), but attachments are not downsized by the new server code (it only touches FileHelper.is_image? files), so: (a) an admin who set max_attachment_size_kb below 10 MB loses client-side enforcement and nothing in create_upload re-validates attachment size, and (b) an admin who set it above 10 MB has users wrongly rejected by the client. Additionally the 413 handler at line 246 now always reports a 10 MB maximum in the error message, which is wrong whenever the web server or site setting has a different limit. The 10 MB cap should apply to images; attachments should still be validated against their own setting.

title: Downsize failures are ignored and the possibly-oversized original is uploaded anyway
body: The while loop stops after 5 attempts regardless of whether tempfile.size is now within SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, the boolean result of OptimizedImage.downsize is ignored, and nothing is logged when it returns false (e.g. when convert/gifsicle errors out). The possibly-still-oversized file then flows straight into Upload.create_for. A large image that resists reduction (very high resolution source, missing/broken ImageMagick) is therefore either silently stored far above the configured limit or fails later with an unrelated error. Check the size after the loop and log or reject when the attempts are exhausted.

title: Animated downsize passes "80%" to gifsicle --resize-fit, which only accepts WxH geometry
body: downsize_instructions_animated delegates to resize_instructions_animated, producing `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`. gifsicle's --resize-fit requires explicit WIDTHxHEIGHT pixel dimensions and does not understand ImageMagick-style percentages, so any animated downsize through this path exits non-zero and convert_with returns false without resizing. Previously the animated path only ever received "WxH" strings; the new percentage-based flow needs its own animated instructions (e.g. gifsicle --scale 0.8) or computed pixel dimensions.

title: Every 80% retry also runs the full ImageOptim pipeline on the intermediate file
body: Each loop iteration calls OptimizedImage.downsize -> convert_with, which runs ImageOptim.new.optimize_image! (jpegoptim/pngcrush/etc.) on the intermediate result, only for the next iteration to overwrite it. Worst case that is five full optimization passes per upload where one final pass would suffice; for multi-megabyte PNGs this adds tens of seconds of CPU in the deferred job and can push the synchronous API upload path (is_api? && params[:synchronous]) toward request timeouts. Resize without optimizing inside the loop and optimize once at the end.

title: No specs cover the new auto-downsize upload flow
body: The PR changes upload size enforcement on both client and server, adds a resize loop in create_upload, and changes OptimizedImage.downsize's signature, but no spec files are touched. Controller/model specs that upload an image larger than max_image_size_kb would catch the regressions visible here (animated GIFs flattened to one frame, the duplicate downsize definition, the loop storing oversized originals when attempts run out). The feature currently ships untested.

title: Duplicate definition of OptimizedImage.downsize silently replaces the width/height version
body: The file now defines self.downsize twice: at line 145 as downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) and again at line 149 as downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}). In Ruby the last definition wins, so the width/height version at line 145 is dead code, and any existing caller (including specs) that invokes OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, width, height) will now raise ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments, 5 for 3..4) at runtime. Keep a single signature: either delete the width/height variant, or have it build the dimensions string and delegate to the new one.

title: Downsize loop reads size from a stale file handle and ignores downsize failures
body: The loop condition `while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` uses Tempfile#size, which is fstat() on the already-open file handle. OptimizedImage.downsize -> convert_with runs ImageOptim.optimize_image!, which — when it improves the image (the common case) — replaces the file at tempfile.path by moving a newly written file over it, i.e. a new inode. The open handle keeps pointing at the old, unlinked inode, so tempfile.size stays frozen at the size captured after the first convert and never reflects further reductions. Consequences: (1) an image that needs more than one pass to get under the limit is downsized all 5 times — shrunk to 0.8^5 ≈ 33% of its dimensions and lossily recompressed/optimized five times, degrading quality and burning CPU; (2) the same stale tempfile.size is passed to Upload.create_for on line 72, so an image that was actually reduced below the limit can be stored with, and validated against, its old larger filesize and still be rejected. The loop also ignores OptimizedImage.downsize's return value, so a failing convert is retried identically five times. Check File.size(tempfile.path), pass that value to create_for, and break out of the loop when downsize returns false.

title: Client-side upload size check hardcodes 10 MB and ignores max_image_size_kb / max_attachment_size_kb
body: validateUploadedFile used to check file size against Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']; it now uses a hardcoded 10 * 1024 for every upload type. This breaks the attachment path: a forum with max_attachment_size_kb set above 10 MB (e.g. to allow zips or videos) now has legitimate uploads rejected in the browser, and a forum with a lower attachment limit lets oversized files through only to fail on the server after the upload. For images it also ignores the configured limit in both directions — sites that raised max_image_size_kb above 10 MB still block larger images client-side — and the file_too_large message always reports 10 MB regardless of the actual setting. The per-type site settings should remain the source of truth, with any extra headroom for server-side downsizing applied only to type 'image'.

title: API URL-download size cap hardcoded to 10 MB instead of max_image_size_kb
body: FileHelper.download for URL-based API uploads is now called with 10.megabytes rather than SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes. On sites where the admin raised the image size limit above 10 MB, downloads that used to succeed now exceed the hardcoded cap; FileHelper.download raises, the rescue sets tempfile to nil, and the code then hits the pre-existing nil-tempfile path (tempfile.size at line 72 raises NoMethodError), turning a previously valid upload into a 500. The cap should stay tied to the site setting (or a single shared constant) instead of a magic number that can drift from configuration.

title: 413 error message now always claims the upload limit is 10 MB
body: The 413 (entity too large) handler in displayErrorForUpload used to report Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb in the file_too_large message; it now hardcodes 10 * 1024. Whenever the site's configured limit, or the web server's actual body-size limit that produced the 413, differs from 10 MB, the user is shown the wrong maximum size. The message should use the site setting or the real configured limit.

title: No tests for the auto-downsize upload path
body: This PR adds a server-side resize loop to UploadsController#create_upload and changes OptimizedImage.downsize's signature, but no specs were added or updated (only these three files changed). There is no coverage for: an oversized image being downsized below max_image_size_kb and accepted, termination when the image cannot be reduced enough, the animated-GIF branch, or the new downsize signature. Given the subtleties involved (the downsize tool replacing the file vs. the open tempfile handle, and the duplicate method definition in optimized_image.rb), controller and model specs should be added before merging.

title: Unsanitized `type` param flows into a shell command via the tempfile path (command injection)
body: `type` comes directly from `params` and is embedded into the download tempfile name ("discourse-upload-#{type}") at line 55. This PR then passes `tempfile.path` to `OptimizedImage.downsize` (line 67), and `OptimizedImage.convert_with` executes the instructions with backticks (`` `#{instructions.join(" ")}` `` in optimized_image.rb) with no shell escaping. A caller who can use the API URL-upload branch (`is_api?` + `url` present, no file) can put shell metacharacters such as `$(...)` or backticks into `type`; hosting an image larger than `max_image_size_kb` at that URL makes the new downsize branch execute, running the injected command as the app server user. Previously this tempfile path never reached a shell, so this exposure is introduced by this PR. Validate `type` against a whitelist before using it in a filename, and/or stop interpolating paths into a shell string (use an argv-array form of exec instead of backticks).

title: self.downsize is defined twice; the 4-argument version is dead and old callers silently misbehave
body: The file now defines `self.downsize` twice: lines 145-147 (`from, to, max_width, max_height, opts`) and lines 149-151 (`from, to, dimensions, opts`). Ruby keeps only the last definition, so the first method is dead code. Worse, any existing or plugin caller still using the old 4-argument form `downsize(from, to, width, height)` gets no arity error: the width is used verbatim as the ImageMagick geometry string (e.g. `-resize 1920\>` with no height) and the height (an Integer) is used as `opts`, so `!!opts[:allow_animation]` in `optimize` raises TypeError (Integer#[] with a Symbol), which is not rescued because the rescue lives in `convert_with`. Remove the leftover 4-argument definition (or make it delegate to the new one correctly).

title: Large animated GIFs are silently flattened to their first frame
body: The downsize call passes `tempfile.path` as `from`, and `OptimizedImage.optimize` only selects the animated (gifsicle) code path when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. Upload tempfiles created by Rack (and the API download tempfile) do not carry the original file extension, so for normal composer uploads this check is always false and a large animated GIF is processed by `convert from[0] ...`, whose `[0]` selects only the first frame and writes a static image back over the user's original file — the animation is silently destroyed even when `allow_animation` is enabled. Additionally, even when the animated branch is reached, it is handed the geometry string "80%", but gifsicle's `--resize-fit` expects an explicit WxH geometry and does not accept percentages, so it would fail on every one of the 5 attempts (the loop also ignores `downsize`'s false return and just retries the identical command). Base the animation check on the original filename or content type rather than the tempfile path, and use gifsicle-compatible geometry.

title: Client upload size check hardcodes 10MB for all types, ignoring the per-type site settings
body: `validateUploadedFile` now caps every upload at `10 * 1024` KB instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. The server-side downsize added in this PR only applies to images; attachments are still validated against `max_attachment_size_kb`, so sites with a lower attachment limit now accept files client-side that the server then rejects (bad UX, wasted upload), and sites with a higher attachment limit (or `max_image_size_kb` above 10MB) now have legitimate uploads blocked client-side — a regression. The 413 error handler at line 246 likewise always reports a 10MB limit in the `file_too_large` message regardless of the actual configured limit. Keep the per-type setting for attachments and only raise the effective cap for images that the server can downsize.

title: API URL-download cap hardcoded to 10MB and nil tempfile still dereferenced
body: For API uploads by URL the download limit was changed from the configured `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a fixed `10.megabytes`. This branch also serves non-image uploads, so attachments larger than 10MB can no longer be pulled via the API even when `max_attachment_size_kb` permits them. When the cap is exceeded the `rescue nil` leaves `tempfile` as nil, and line 72 then calls `tempfile.size`, raising NoMethodError instead of returning a clean error to the API client. Use the per-type size setting and handle the nil tempfile case explicitly.

title: No tests for the new auto-downsize behavior
body: The new downsize loop in `create_upload` (lines 64-70) — a retry loop that shells out to ImageMagick/gifsicle and mutates the uploaded file before `Upload.create_for` — ships without any spec coverage. There are no tests verifying that an over-limit image is downsized and accepted, that an image still over the limit after 5 attempts returns a clean validation error, or that animated GIFs keep their animation (they currently do not). Add controller/model specs covering these cases.

title: unsubscribe mutates notification state on an idempotent-unsafe GET
body: topics#unsubscribe is wired to plain GET routes (config/routes.rb adds get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" and "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe") and it permanently writes the user's topic notification level before rendering the page. GET requests must not mutate state, and this one is not even idempotent: the first visit drops a watching/tracking user to regular, but simply reloading the confirmation page (or hitting back) executes the URL again and, because the level is now regular, falls into the else branch and fully mutes the topic — while the page still only claims 'You will stop receiving notifications'. It is also CSRF-able: any third-party page can embed and silently change a logged-in visitor's notification state, and any logged-in link prefetcher triggers it. The state change should happen via POST (the unsubscribe page already renders a topic-notifications-button the user can click), or the GET should render a confirmation without writing.

title: NoMethodError (500) when the visitor has no TopicUser row
body: tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) can return nil. Emailed users normally have a row because send_notification_email calls TopicUser.change, but the unsubscribe URL is reachable by any logged-in user — someone who never interacted with the topic, or whose topic_users row was later removed — and the very next line calls tu.notification_level, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 instead of the unsubscribe page. Guard the nil case or use TopicUser.change, which upserts.

title: Direct tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping, allowing silent re-subscription
body: Assigning tu.notification_level and calling tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change, so notifications_changed_at and notifications_reason_id are not updated and the notification_level_change MessageBus event is never published. One concrete consequence: TopicUser.update_last_read and TopicUser.auto_track only auto-subscribe users whose notifications_reason_id is null, and TopicUser.change would have stamped the reason as user_changed — because this code doesn't, a user who unsubscribes (set to regular) and later spends time reading the topic can be silently flipped back to tracking by the auto-track-on-view-time logic. Open browser tabs also won't reflect the new level in real time. Use TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...) instead.

title: unsubscribe_link now hard-requires %{unsubscribe_url}, breaking other add_unsubscribe_link callers
body: The unsubscribe_link site text now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url} ('To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, [click here](%{unsubscribe_url})'), but Email::MessageBuilder only provides unsubscribe_url when the caller passes it in opts. The in-tree caller in user_notifications was updated, but any other caller of build_email with add_unsubscribe_link: true that doesn't pass unsubscribe_url (plugins, custom mailers) will now raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument when building both the text body (MessageBuilder#body) and the HTML part (MessageBuilder#html_part), failing those emails entirely — the existing spec had to be changed for exactly this reason. Consider defaulting unsubscribe_url (e.g., to user_preferences_url) or making the second sentence conditional.

title: No specs for the new state-mutating topics#unsubscribe endpoint
body: The PR adds a new endpoint that mutates user state with several branches — watching/tracking → regular, regular/muted → muted, missing TopicUser row, slug-mismatch 301 redirect, login requirement — but adds no controller or request specs for it; the only spec change passes unsubscribe_url in message_builder_spec. Even basic coverage would have caught the nil-TopicUser 500 and the non-idempotent escalation to muted on repeat visits described above.

title: unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when the user has no TopicUser row
body: In TopicsController#unsubscribe, `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` returns nil whenever the user has no topic_users row for that topic (e.g., they never visited or interacted with it, or the row was removed). The very next line dereferences `tu.notification_level`, so such a request raises NoMethodError and returns a 500. This endpoint is the target of links sent in notification emails, so it must be robust for any logged-in user. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...)`, which creates the row when missing, or explicitly handle the nil case.

title: unsubscribe mutates notification state via an unauthenticated-format GET request
body: The new unsubscribe endpoint is routed as GET (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` in config/routes.rb) and is added to `skip_before_filter :check_xhr`, and it immediately changes `TopicUser.notification_level` (`tu.save!`) when the URL is fetched. Rails' CSRF protection does not cover GET requests, so the only guard is the session cookie: anyone can change a logged-in victim's topic notification state (mute the topic, or demote it from watching/tracking to regular) by getting their browser to request the URL, e.g. by embedding `` in a post, PM, or external page. It also violates safe-GET semantics, so browser prefetchers can trigger it. The mutation should require a POST (the unsubscribe page already renders a notification control that could perform it), or at minimum a confirmation step.

title: unsubscribe saves TopicUser directly, bypassing TopicUser.change side effects
body: Everywhere else in the app, notification level changes go through `TopicUser.change`, which also sets `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` (so the UI can explain why the level is what it is) and publishes a `notification_level_change` MessageBus event so the user's other open tabs/sessions update live. The new unsubscribe action instead assigns `tu.notification_level` and calls `tu.save!`, so those timestamps/reason stay stale and other browser sessions never learn the topic was muted. Calling `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: level)` would fix this and the nil-row crash in the same action.

title: No request/controller spec for the new state-changing unsubscribe endpoint
body: This PR adds a new public, state-changing endpoint (TopicsController#unsubscribe) but only touches spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb to pass the new unsubscribe_url option. There is no controller/request spec covering the unsubscribe action itself: the slug redirect behavior, the watching/tracking -> regular and regular -> muted transitions, and the no-existing-TopicUser-row case (which currently 500s). A spec would have caught the nil dereference before merge.

title: Topic unsubscribe mutates user state via an unprotected GET request
body: The new `topics#unsubscribe` action is routed as `GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` and `GET /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe`, and it changes the current user's TopicUser notification level (demoting tracking/watching to regular, or muting) as a side effect of a plain GET. Rails does not verify CSRF tokens on GET requests, and the controller also skips `check_xhr` for this action, so any content that causes a logged-in user's browser to request that URL will silently change their subscription state. Concretely: an attacker can embed `` in a post, PM, or external page and every logged-in viewer gets muted/unsubscribed from topic 123. Additionally, corporate email gateways and security link-scanners that fetch URLs found in incoming mail will trigger the unsubscribe without the user ever clicking. The GET should render a confirmation page only, with the actual change performed via a POST/PUT (protected by the CSRF token) or via a signed one-click-unsubscribe token.

title: Unsubscribe toggle is not idempotent — reloading the page changes state again
body: In `topics#unsubscribe`, the new level is computed by toggling off the current level: if `tu.notification_level > regular` it is set to `regular`, otherwise it is set to `muted`. Because the mutation runs on every GET of the unsubscribe URL, repeating the request keeps changing the user's state: a watching user is demoted to regular on first load and then fully muted if they simply refresh the confirmation page (or hit back/forward, or a prefetcher re-fetches the link). Meanwhile the page text says "You will stop receiving notifications for …", which no longer matches the state the user actually ends up in after a reload. The action should set a deterministic target level (e.g., always mute, or always regular) or defer the change to an explicit form submission, so repeated visits are harmless.

title: Unsubscribe crashes when no TopicUser row exists and bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping
body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil (the user may have no row for that topic — e.g., it was never created or was removed), and the very next line dereferences `tu.notification_level`, producing a NoMethodError and a 500 instead of unsubscribing. Separately, assigning `notification_level` directly and calling `save!` skips what `TopicUser.change` does: it does not set `notifications_reason_id`/`notifications_changed_at` and does not publish the MessageBus `notification_level_change` event. Because `notifications_reason_id` remains NULL, the auto-track SQL in `TopicUser.update_last_read` (`when tu.notifications_reason_id is null and total_msecs_viewed > threshold then :tracking`) will silently flip the user back to tracking the next time they read posts in that topic, undoing their explicit unsubscribe, and other open browser tabs will show stale notification state. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...)`, which upserts safely (no nil crash), records the reason, and broadcasts the change.

title: Client-side navigation to /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe claims the user was unsubscribed without unsubscribing them
body: The actual unsubscribe only happens server-side in `topics#unsubscribe` during a full page load. The new Ember route's model hook merely loads the topic (`PostStream.loadTopicView`) and never calls any unsubscribe endpoint, yet its template states "You will stop receiving notifications for <topic>". Discourse intercepts clicks on same-origin links (for example an unsubscribe URL posted inside a topic or PM) and transitions client-side without a server round-trip, so a user arriving that way sees a message asserting they were unsubscribed when nothing changed — the opposite result from opening the same URL in a new tab, which does unsubscribe them. The route should either perform the change (e.g., via the notifications endpoint) or the copy should not claim notifications have stopped.

title: No request specs for the new state-changing topics#unsubscribe endpoint
body: This PR adds a new public, state-changing controller action plus routes, but the only spec touched is `spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb` (passing an extra `unsubscribe_url` option). There is no controller/request coverage for: unsubscribing from each starting level (watching/tracking/regular/muted), behavior when no TopicUser row exists, the 301 slug redirect, or the login requirement. Given the non-idempotent toggle logic and the nil-handling risk in this action, the endpoint needs request specs before merge.

title: unsubscribe_link now requires an %{unsubscribe_url} interpolation argument, breaking other add_unsubscribe_link callers
body: The default `unsubscribe_link` text now embeds `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `Email::MessageBuilder#body` and `#html_part` render it via `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` for every email built with `add_unsubscribe_link: true`. All core notification mailers were updated to pass `unsubscribe_url`, but any other existing or future caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without also passing `unsubscribe_url` (e.g., plugin mailers) will now raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` and fail to send, where previously it worked. Consider putting the per-topic sentence in a separate optional translation key or defaulting `unsubscribe_url` (e.g., to the user preferences URL) inside MessageBuilder.

title: Blocked email lookup is case-sensitive, so a block is trivially bypassed
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? does an exact-match lookup: BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first. On PostgreSQL string equality is case-sensitive, and nothing normalizes case anywhere in the flow: User.new_from_params assigns params[:email] exactly as typed, BlockedEmail.set_defaults only sets action_type, and EmailValidator passes the raw value through. An admin who blocks spammer@example.com will not block Spammer@example.com or SPAMMER@example.com, even though those deliver to the same mailbox, so a blocked spammer can re-register simply by changing letter case. Normalize the address (e.g. strip + downcase) both when writing blocked_emails rows and when checking in should_block?, or query with a case-insensitive comparison such as lower(email) = lower(?). The added specs only exercise exact-case matches, so this gap is not covered by tests.

title: match_count is incremented per validation pass, so one signup attempt is counted twice
body: should_block? has a database write side effect (match_count += 1 and save) and is invoked from EmailValidator, meaning it runs every time a User is validated. UsersController#create validates the user twice per attempt: once explicitly in `if user.valid? && SiteSetting.call_discourse_hub?` (users_controller.rb line 168) and again inside `user.save` (line 172). Because the record is new and unsaved, email_changed? is true for both passes, so a single blocked signup attempt increments match_count by 2 and updates last_match_at twice. Any other code that calls user.valid? and then user.save (or calls valid? as a dry-run check) also mutates these statistics. Match tracking should live outside the validation cycle (e.g. in the controller after a failed save) or otherwise be per-attempt rather than per-validation, otherwise the match_count/last_match_at audit data this feature exists to collect is unreliable.

title: match_count increment is a non-atomic read-modify-write
body: should_block? does record.match_count += 1 followed by record.save. That is a read-modify-write: two concurrent requests matching the same blocked email can both read the same counter value, and one increment is silently lost. If these statistics are meant to be accurate, use an atomic update such as BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_counters(match_count: 1) plus an update of last_match_at, instead of incrementing an in-memory attribute and saving the whole record.

title: Blocked-email matching is case-sensitive, so blocks are trivially bypassed
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? does an exact `where(email: email)` lookup, and the signup flow stores emails exactly as typed: `User.new_from_params` assigns `params[:email]` raw, the User model has no email downcasing callback, and the email uniqueness validator plus the Postgres unique index on users.email are both case-sensitive. Blocking `spammer@example.com` therefore does nothing to stop `Spammer@example.com` or `SPAMMER@example.com` from registering — the lookup misses the row and a separate account is created. The block should normalize case (store emails lowercase and compare against `email.downcase`) to be effective as an anti-abuse control.

title: Validator performs DB writes during validation; match_count is double-counted per signup
body: validate_each calls BlockedEmail.should_block?, which as a side effect increments match_count and sets last_match_at on the blocked_emails row. Validation is normally read-only, and here it runs more than once per signup: UsersController#create calls `user.valid?` at line 168 (before the DiscourseHub check) and then `user.save` at line 172, which validates again — so one blocked signup attempt records two matches. Any other `user.valid?`/`save` with a changed email (including records that fail for unrelated reasons or are rolled back) also bumps the counters, so match_count cannot be trusted as a count of signup attempts. The stats update should happen once, at the point the signup is actually rejected, not inside the validator.

title: match_count increment is a read-modify-write and loses updates under concurrency
body: In BlockedEmail.should_block?, `record.match_count += 1` followed by `record.save` reads the counter into memory and writes it back. Two concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked email both read the same value, so one increment is silently lost. Use an atomic update instead, e.g. `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all("match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ...")` or `update_counters`, which also avoids re-running validations and callbacks for a stats update.

title: rejectedEmails array is defined on the prototype and shared across instances
body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` in the hash passed to `Discourse.Controller.extend` puts a single mutable array on the controller's prototype, shared by every instance. The app currently instantiates this controller once, but any second instantiation — in JS tests, or if the controller is torn down and recreated — inherits emails rejected during earlier usage, and mutations via `pushObject` leak between instances. Initialize it per-instance instead, e.g. in an `init()` override with `this.set('rejectedEmails', Em.A([]))`.

title: No test covers the new errors/values response contract the client depends on
body: The failed-signup JSON now includes `errors: user.errors.to_hash` and `values: user.attributes.slice("name", "username", "email")`, and the new client behavior — pushing `result.values.email` into `rejectedEmails` only when `result.errors.email` is present — depends on both keys existing with exactly these shapes. No controller/request spec (or JS test) was added for this contract, so a rename or a change in how errors are serialized would silently break the "prevent resubmitting a blocked email" flow without any failing test.

title: match_count is incremented twice per failed signup because should_block? has a side effect inside validation
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? writes to the database (match_count += 1, last_match_at = now, save) every time it runs, and it is invoked from EmailValidator, i.e. from user validation. UsersController#create (app/controllers/users_controller.rb) calls user.valid? on line 168 and then user.save on line 172, both of which run the full validation suite, so a single signup attempt with a blocked email increments match_count by 2 and updates last_match_at twice. Any other code path that calls valid? before save does the same. The match_count/last_match_at statistics (whose purpose is explicitly described in the specs) will therefore be wrong for the primary flow they were built for. The stats update should be separated from validation (e.g. done once in the controller when a block actually rejects the signup) or made idempotent per request. The specs call should_block? directly, so they never exercise this double-run.

title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive, so blocks are trivially bypassed by changing letter case
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? does an exact-match lookup: BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first. Nothing downcases the user's email before validation — User.new_from_params assigns params[:email] verbatim and the User model never normalizes case (unlike change_email, which uses Email.downcase). A blocked address spammer@example.com will therefore not match Spammer@example.com or SPAMMER@EXAMPLE.COM, letting a blocked user register by simply varying case. The unique index added in the migration is case-sensitive as well, so variants can coexist in the table. The lookup should compare downcased emails (and ideally the column should be normalized on write).

title: Any server email error (e.g. 'has already been taken') marks the address as rejected and mislabels it invalid
body: On account-creation failure the client pushes result.values.email into rejectedEmails whenever result.errors.email exists, and emailValidation then reports I18n.t('user.email.invalid') for that address. But errors.email is present for any email validation failure, not just blocking — most commonly the uniqueness validation (User validates :email, uniqueness: true), which produces 'has already been taken'. A user whose signup failed because the email is already registered (or who hits the ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid duplicate race after a retry) will see 'email is invalid' from then on and will be unable to re-validate that address for the rest of the session, with no hint that the real problem is a duplicate. The client should only track emails rejected specifically by the blocked-email rule (e.g. a dedicated error code from the server), not any email error.

title: match_count increment is a non-atomic read-modify-write and record.save can silently fail
body: should_block? loads the record, does record.match_count += 1, then record.save. Two concurrent signup attempts against the same blocked email both read the same match_count and one increment is lost. Additionally, the return value of record.save is ignored, so if the save fails (e.g. a validation error from a concurrent change) the statistics are silently dropped while the block decision still proceeds. Use an atomic update (e.g. update_counters or UPDATE ... SET match_count = match_count + 1) for the stats bump.

title: Blocked-email match statistics are not recorded when another email validation already failed
body: The blocked check is gated on record.errors[attribute].blank?, so BlockedEmail.should_block? is never called if the email already has an error from the presence/uniqueness validators (which run before this one in User) or from the domain whitelist/blacklist check above. That means a signup attempt using a blocked email that also trips another rule — for example re-registering an email that is both blocked and already taken — leaves no trace in match_count or last_match_at, undercounting abuse attempts. If the gate exists only to avoid duplicate error messages, the stats recording should still happen and only the errors.add should be conditional.

title: change_email does not check the blocked list before sending the authorization email
body: UsersController#change_email only checks that the new email is not already in use, then creates an email token and enqueues the authorize_email message. A logged-in user can therefore request an email change to a blocked address and have the system send mail to it; the block is only (silently) enforced later if EmailToken.confirm saves the user and triggers the model validation, at which point the email change fails with no feedback to the user. The blocked check should also run in change_email so the request is rejected up front with a clear error.

title: Feed HTML is stored and rendered completely unsanitized (stored XSS)
body: Feed item content is imported with no sanitization: poll_feed unescapes entities via CGI.unescapeHTML, then TopicEmbed.import stores the string as the post raw with cook_method raw_html, and Post#cook returns raw unchanged for raw_html posts. The result is rendered unsanitized both on the forum (the app renders post.cooked unescaped, trusting the normal cooking pipeline to have sanitized it) and in app/views/embed/best.html.erb via <%= raw post.cooked %>, which is served from the Discourse origin inside the iframe. Any <script> or event handler attribute in a feed entry — from a hostile or compromised blog/feed, a rogue author on a multi-author blog, or a MITM on a plaintext feed URL — becomes stored XSS executing in the forum origin as viewing users/admins. CGI.unescapeHTML makes it worse by converting the feed's safely entity-escaped markup into live tags. Imported content must be sanitized (e.g., with the already-bundled sanitize gem) before being stored as raw HTML.

title: Unescaped URL interpolated into a single-quoted href in the imported footer
body: TopicEmbed.import appends a footer to every imported post: #{url}. The only validation on url is a /^https?:\/\// prefix check, so a URL containing a single quote (e.g. from a malicious feed or a fetched page URL) breaks out of the attribute and injects arbitrary HTML into the post body, which is then rendered raw via the raw_html cook path. Because the footer is appended after Readability extraction, this vector bypasses even the limited tag/attribute filtering that import_remote applies to article content. The URL should be HTML/attribute-escaped before interpolation.

title: Unauthenticated endpoint triggers remote fetch and topic creation; referer check is trivially spoofable
body: GET /embed/best enqueues a RetrieveTopic job for any embed_url with no existing embed, with no authentication and no rate limiting. The only gate is that the Referer host matches embeddable_host, which any non-browser client can spoof (curl -H 'Referer: http://blog.example.com' ...). The 60-second Redis throttle in TopicRetriever is per-URL, so an attacker can supply unlimited distinct URLs on the embeddable host: each one makes the server fetch that page and create a forum topic as the embed_by_username user (topic spam, bandwidth/CPU amplification), and when feed_polling_enabled is on each request also triggers a synchronous full PollFeed run inside the job. Consider per-IP rate limiting and/or restricting which paths are importable.

title: i.content is nil for RSS items without content:encoded, crashing the hourly job
body: i.content.scrub raises NoMethodError when a feed item has no content:encoded/content element — plain RSS 2.0 feeds that only provide <description> are common, and SimpleRSS returns nil for absent elements. Because the job sets sidekiq_options retry: false, the exception kills the run silently until the next hour and any remaining items are never imported. Fall back to i.description (and/or i.summary) when content is absent. The new poll_feed_spec only exercises the site-setting gates and never parses a feed item, so this path is untested.

title: embed.js/embed.css are never added to config.assets.precompile — feature 404s/500s in production
body: The PR adds app/assets/javascripts/embed.js and app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss and references them via stylesheet_link_tag 'embed' (in the embed layout) and as the script embedding sites load, but no config change adds 'embed.js' or 'embed.css' to the asset precompile list. With the application's explicit precompile list and assets.compile disabled in production, /embed/best will raise AssetNotPrecompiledError and the embed snippet URL will 404, so the entire feature is broken in production. Add both assets to config.assets.precompile.

title: add_column with default on posts rewrites the whole table under an exclusive lock
body: add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false causes PostgreSQL (pre-11) to rewrite every row of the posts table to materialize the default, holding an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock for the duration. posts is typically the largest table in a Discourse database, so on busy installs this migration can block all writes to posts for minutes during deploy. Add the column without a default/NOT NULL, backfill in batches, then apply the default and constraint.

title: open(url) used without requiring open-uri on the retrieve path
body: TopicEmbed.import_remote calls open(url), but this file never requires 'open-uri' — only poll_feed.rb does. The HTTP-retrieve path (EmbedController → RetrieveTopic job → TopicRetriever#fetch_http → TopicEmbed.import_remote) therefore only works if Jobs::PollFeed happened to be loaded already; in lazy-loading environments (dev/test, or any process that never referenced PollFeed) Kernel#open treats the URL as a filename and raises Errno::ENOENT. Add require 'open-uri' to topic_embed.rb (or lib/topic_retriever.rb) so the dependency is explicit.

title: embeddable_host is compared as an exact string against URI#host with no normalization
body: The check URI(request.referer).host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host compares the parsed host against free-form admin text. Values admins commonly paste — 'http://example.com', 'example.com/', or 'example.com:8080' — never equal URI#host ('example.com'), so every legitimate embed is rejected with 'invalid referer host' and no diagnostics. The same strict comparison in TopicRetriever.invalid_host? also fails when the blog's canonical URL host differs from the page host (www vs apex), producing the infinite loading screen. Parse/normalize the setting (compare host and port explicitly, and consider allowing subdomains) or validate its format when saved.

title: X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL is not a valid header value
body: ALLOWALL is not a permitted X-Frame-Options value (the spec defines DENY, SAMEORIGIN, and ALLOW-FROM uri). Browsers currently ignore unrecognized values, which is why framing happens to work, but the behavior is undefined and stricter user agents or normalizing proxies may handle it differently. To allow cross-origin framing for this action, remove the X-Frame-Options header instead of setting an invalid value.

title: Edits an already-deployed migration and adds force: true, which silently drops the table
body: This changes 20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb — a migration that has already run in deployed environments — to create_table :top_topics, force: true. force: true issues DROP TABLE IF EXISTS before creating, so anywhere the table exists while the migration is considered pending (db:schema:load followed by migrate, restored backups, staging/dev databases) the existing top_topics table is silently dropped and recreated. Where the migration already ran, the edit has no effect at all, making it misleading. Old migrations should not be edited; the new create_topic_embeds migration also does not need force: true.

title: Blank embed_by_username silently no-ops, leaving an infinite reload/job loop
body: When SiteSetting.embed_by_username is blank, fetch_http looks up User.where(username_lower: '') and returns without creating anything or logging why. The embed controller then keeps rendering loading.html.erb, which reloads the iframe every 30 seconds and enqueues a new RetrieveTopic job on every reload — forever, for every open browser tab on the embedding site. The controller or retriever should fail fast with a clear error (or gate the embed on embed_by_username being configured) instead of looping silently.

title: RSS feed content is stored as raw, unsanitized HTML — stored XSS on the forum domain
body: PollFeed takes each feed item's HTML (CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)) and passes it to TopicEmbed.import, which creates the post with cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html] (app/models/topic_embed.rb:22). Post#cook returns `raw` unchanged for raw_html posts (app/models/post.rb:133), so `cooked` contains the feed markup verbatim with zero sanitization, and it is rendered unescaped (<%= raw post.cooked %> in app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19, and as cooked HTML in the main app). Any <script> or on* handler in a feed item becomes stored XSS executing on the forum domain for every visitor. The CGI.unescapeHTML makes this worse: the XML parser already decodes entities once, so content the feed author properly escaped (e.g. `<script>` in a code sample) is decoded a second time into live markup — even a fully trusted blog can inject live scripts. Note the import_remote path at least whitelists tags/attributes via Readability; the RSS path sanitizes nothing. Feed content should be run through Sanitize (or an equivalent whitelist) before being stored as raw_html.

title: Server-side fetch follows redirects to any host — SSRF past the embeddable_host check
body: TopicRetriever#invalid_host? only validates that URI(embed_url).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host, but TopicEmbed.import_remote fetches with `open(url)` (open-uri), which transparently follows HTTP redirects to arbitrary hosts. An open redirect on the allowed host (e.g. http://blog.example.com/out?u=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data or an intranet address) lets an external requester make the forum server fetch internal URLs; the response is then Readability-parsed and published as a public topic, exfiltrating the content. The fetch layer should validate every redirect target against the allowed host or disable cross-host redirects.

title: postMessage targetOrigin is the full referer URL — browsers throw and the iframe never resizes
body: The layout calls parent.postMessage({type: 'discourse-resize', height: ...}, '<%= request.referer %>'). The referer is a full URL with a path (e.g. http://blog.example.com/2013/02/post.html), but targetOrigin must be an origin (scheme://host[:port]); Chrome/Firefox throw a SyntaxError ('Invalid target origin') for anything else. As a result the discourse-resize message is never delivered to the parent page and the embed.js auto-resize feature simply never works. The code should post to the referer's origin only. Additionally, the referer is interpolated into a single-quoted JS string and html_escape does not escape apostrophes on all Rails versions this repo supports, so a referer containing a raw ' would also break the script.

title: Loading page self-reload fails the controller's referer check — embed gets stuck on 403
body: The loading page reloads itself every 30s via document.location.reload() so it picks up the topic once the RetrieveTopic job finishes. A programmatic reload sends the iframe's own URL (the /embed/best URL on the forum host) as the Referer, not the embedding page's URL. EmbedController#ensure_embeddable (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26) compares URI(referer).host to SiteSetting.embeddable_host and raises Discourse::InvalidAccess on mismatch, so the reload gets a 403 and the embed is permanently stuck on an error page instead of showing the newly imported topic. The referer check needs to also accept the forum's own embed URL (or the loading flow needs another mechanism, e.g. message-bus).

title: Feeds without content:encoded crash the hourly job (nil.scrub)
body: For RSS 2.0 feeds that don't provide <content:encoded> — many feeds only ship <description> — SimpleRSS returns nil for i.content, so `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError. The hourly PollFeed job dies partway through the feed and all remaining items are skipped every run. Use a fallback such as (i.content || i.description) and guard for nil before calling scrub.

title: absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs (//host/path)
body: The relative-URL rewrite treats any href/src starting with '/' as host-relative: a protocol-relative URL like //cdn.example.com/a.png matches `href.start_with?('/')` and is rewritten to http://blog.example.com/cdn.example.com/a.png, producing a broken link. Protocol-relative URLs are common in feed/article HTML. The check should exclude values starting with '//' (and ideally also absolutize paths that don't start with '/', which are currently left relative and break in the forum context).

title: URIs that pass the regex but are invalid crash the whole import run
body: URLs are only validated against /^https?:\/\// before URI(url) is called in absolutize_urls (and open(url) in import_remote). Feed links or embed URLs containing spaces or other characters illegal in URIs (e.g. 'http://example.com/my post.html') pass the regex but raise URI::InvalidURIError here, which is not rescued — in PollFeed this aborts the entire hourly run so no further feed items are imported, and in the RetrieveTopic job it causes repeated sidekiq retries. Validate with URI.parse in a begin/rescue and skip bad items instead of aborting.

title: ADD COLUMN with DEFAULT + NOT NULL rewrites the entire posts table and blocks writes
body: add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false forces PostgreSQL (< 11) to rewrite every row of the posts table while holding an AccessExclusiveLock. posts is the largest table in a Discourse install, so on any sizable forum this migration blocks all posting/reading for minutes during a deploy. Safer pattern: add the column without a default, backfill in batches, then set the default and the NOT NULL constraint.

title: Find-then-create race on embed_url unique index aborts concurrent import jobs
body: import does `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and later TopicEmbed.create! inside a transaction. Two concurrent jobs for the same URL (a RetrieveTopic job racing the hourly PollFeed, or two RetrieveTopic jobs for staff, who bypass the redis throttle) both see no existing embed and both build a topic and post; the second create! hits the unique index on topic_embeds.embed_url and raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, failing that job — and in PollFeed, aborting the rest of the feed items. Rescue RecordNotUnique/re-check inside the transaction or use an upsert-style create_or_find.

title: Non-atomic setnx + expire can permanently throttle an embed URL
body: retrieved_recently? does $redis.setnx(retrieved_key, '1') followed by a separate $redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60). If the process crashes (or expire raises) between the two calls, the key never expires and retrieve() will treat that embed_url as recently retrieved forever — the topic is never fetched. Use a single atomic SET with an EX option (supported by redis-rb) instead of the two-step dance.

title: Editing an already-released migration and adding force: true
body: This changes the shipped 20131223171005_create_top_topics migration to create_table :top_topics, force: true. Databases that already ran the migration will never re-run it, so the change is a silent no-op there; on fresh or restored setups, force: true will silently DROP and recreate the table (and any data) if it already exists. Released migrations shouldn't be modified — add a new migration instead. The new db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb uses force: true too, carrying the same silent-drop risk.

title: Gating tests for feed_polling_url / embed_by_username are vacuous
body: The tests 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' never enable the preceding conditions: feed_polling_enabled? defaults to false in the test env (and the URL is unset in the username test), so execute short-circuits at the first condition and `poller.expects(:poll_feed).never` passes regardless of the condition under test. These specs would still pass if the url/username presence checks were removed entirely. Each gating test should stub all the prior conditions to true so only the condition under test fails.

title: request.referer injected into a JavaScript string with only HTML escaping
body: The embed layout interpolates request.referer directly into a single-quoted JS string: parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>'). ERB output is HTML-escaped, which is the wrong escaping context for a JavaScript string — and in the Rails 3 boot mode this repo still supports, ERB's html_escape does not escape single quotes at all. A request to /embed/best with a Referer such as http://<embeddable-host>/';alert(1);// passes the ensure_embeddable host check (a single quote and semicolons are legal characters in a URI path) and breaks out of the JS string, executing arbitrary script inside the iframe on the forum's own origin. Use request.referer.to_json (or escape_javascript) when building the targetOrigin string.

title: Unescaped URL interpolated into href attribute of posts rendered as raw HTML
body: TopicEmbed.import appends an 'Imported from' footer built as "#{url}" with the URL inserted unescaped. The only validation is that the URL starts with http(s)://; a single quote is a valid URI character, so a feed item link or an embed URL like http://host/page'onmouseover='alert(1) breaks out of the href attribute and injects arbitrary attributes/markup into the post body. Because these posts are created with cook_method raw_html, Post#cook returns the raw string with no sanitization, and the embed view renders it via `raw post.cooked` (and the main site renders cooked verbatim), this becomes stored XSS on the forum origin for everyone who views the imported topic or embed. Escape the URL (e.g. ERB::Util.html_escape) before interpolating it into the attribute.

title: raw_html cook method renders remotely fetched content with zero sanitization
body: Post#cook now returns `raw` unchanged when cook_method is raw_html, bypassing PrettyText's sanitizer entirely. The content stored in these posts comes from remote sources: feed items via PollFeed (no filtering at all) and arbitrary pages on the embeddable host via TopicRetriever/import_remote (ruby-readability whitelists tags/attributes but still passes through href/src values such as javascript: URLs). Any script, event handler, or javascript: link in the source HTML is rendered verbatim on topic pages, in the embed iframe on the forum origin, in email digests, etc. Additionally, PostCreator now honors opts[:cook_method] for every caller (lib/post_creator.rb setup_post) — if request parameters ever flow into PostCreator opts, any user could create unsanitized raw-HTML posts, so this must be guarded against.

title: Feed items without content crash the polling job permanently
body: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` raises NoMethodError when an item has no content element. With simple-rss, RSS 2.0 items only expose #content when the feed includes <content:encoded>; a large number of feeds carry only <description>, and Atom entries may omit content too. One such item raises out of the each loop, aborting the whole poll (the job has retry: false), and since items are processed in feed order the same item crashes the job again on every hourly run, so no later items are ever imported. Fall back to i.description / to_s and wrap per-item processing so one bad item cannot kill the entire feed poll.

title: TopicEmbed row is created even when PostCreator rolled the post back, leaving a dangling reference
body: import only checks `if post.present?` before calling TopicEmbed.create!, but PostCreator#create returns the unsaved post object (with errors) when creation fails — for example when rollback_if_host_spam_detected fires, which happens for a trust-level-0 embed user importing an article that links several times to the same host (newuser_spam_host_threshold). In that case the inner Post transaction rolls back the topic and post inserts, but TopicEmbed.create! still commits a row whose topic_id/post_id point at records that no longer exist. Every subsequent /embed/best request for that URL then finds the dead topic_id and TopicView raises not-found/invalid-access, so the embed for that URL is permanently broken and the import is never retried. Check post.persisted? / post.errors.empty? instead of post.present?.

title: absolutize_urls mangles protocol-relative URLs
body: Both the and rewriting treat any value starting with '/' as root-relative and rewrite it to prefix + path. Protocol-relative URLs such as //cdn.example.com/image.png (common in feeds and CMS output) also start with '/', so they are rewritten to http://host/cdn.example.com/image.png, breaking the link or image. Values starting with '//' should be left alone.

title: Unauthenticated endpoint enqueues unbounded outbound-fetch jobs
body: Any GET to /embed/best whose Referer host matches embeddable_host (a header trivially forged by non-browser clients) and that carries a previously unseen embed_url enqueues a RetrieveTopic job, which performs an outbound HTTP fetch of that URL. The only throttle is a 60-second redis key per URL inside the job, so an attacker can enqueue unlimited jobs simply by varying the URL — exhausting sidekiq workers and directing a flood of fetches at the configured embeddable host. There should be a global or per-IP rate limit before enqueuing retrieval work.

title: Every new embed URL runs a full synchronous feed poll
body: When feed_polling_enabled? is on, perform_retrieve executes Jobs::PollFeed inline for each retrieval before falling back to direct HTTP fetch. The retrieval throttle is keyed per embed URL, so N distinct new embed URLs cause N full feed downloads/parses (and a re-import/revision pass over every feed item) inside RetrieveTopic jobs. The unused feed_key method on PollFeed suggests a per-feed throttle was intended but never wired up.

title: Missing Referer hard-fails embedding for legitimate visitors
body: ensure_embeddable raises Discourse::InvalidAccess when request.referer is blank. Visitors using referer-stripping privacy extensions, behind referer-removing proxies, or on an HTTPS page embedding an HTTP forum (browsers omit Referer on the HTTPS→HTTP downgrade) will get an error instead of the comment embed. The check only needs to reject referers from foreign hosts; a blank referer could be treated as allowed so these users still see comments.

title: Disqus import no longer preserves the thread's original creation date
body: Before this change the topic-opening post was created with created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]); the new code path calls TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title]), which provides no way to pass created_at, so every imported thread's opening post is timestamped at import time. Imported forums lose their original chronology (topic ordering, 'x days ago' dates, digest ordering). Add a created_at option to import/import_remote and pass the thread date through.

title: float: right on .small-action button is ignored now that .small-action is a flex container
body: This PR adds `@include flexbox()` to `.small-action`, but the `button` rule inside it still relies on `float: right` to pin the small-action undo/recover button to the right edge of the row. Floats have no effect on flex items, so the button will now render immediately after the `.small-action-desc` text instead of at the far right of the row whenever the description is short (e.g. "closed the topic"). The header change in this same PR solves the equivalent problem for `.panel` by adding `margin-left: auto`; the same fix (or `justify-content: space-between`) is needed here for the button.

title: margin-left: auto used to right-align .panel does not work in the 2009-spec flexbox fallback the new mixin emits
body: `.panel` is now pushed to the right edge of the header with `margin-left: auto` instead of `float: right`. The `flexbox()` mixin added in this PR emits `display: -webkit-box`/`display: -moz-box` as fallbacks, and in that 2009 flexbox spec (old iOS Safari, old Android stock browser) auto margins on box children are treated as 0, so on exactly the browsers those fallback lines exist for, the header panel (user menu / login / signup buttons) will sit immediately after the logo instead of at the right edge. At the same time the float fallbacks were removed (`.title { float: left }` deleted, `.panel { float: right }` deleted), so those engines get the degraded layout with no fallback. Either drop the old-spec prefixes or add a fallback such as `-webkit-box-pack: end` / keeping a float fallback.

title: align-items mixin passes standard keywords verbatim to legacy properties that use different value names
body: The new `align-items($alignment)` mixin copies its argument into `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`, but those legacy properties do not accept the standard `flex-start`/`flex-end` keywords — they expect `start`/`end`. The mixin compiles silently and the declaration is simply dropped by those engines, so the first time someone uses `@include align-items(flex-start)` (the most common value in real layouts) alignment will be silently broken in old WebKit and IE10. Current usages only pass `center`/`baseline`, which happen to be valid in both syntaxes, so this is latent rather than an active bug — but the mixin should map the values (or the limitation should be documented) since it is being introduced for codebase-wide reuse. Additionally, `-ms-align-items` on line 121 is not a property that exists in any browser (IE10's 2012 spec only has `-ms-flex-align`), so that line is dead code.

title: Bullet category badge in the scrolled header loses its 5px top offset with no replacement
body: This PR removes `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }`. That offset was what aligned the small inline-flex bullet badge with the topic title text in the header's extra-info (scrolled) state. The new `@include align-items(center)` is applied to `.d-header .contents`, which only centers the `.extra-info-wrapper` as a whole within the header bar; `.extra-info-wrapper` itself is not a flex container and the badge inside it still uses `float: left`, so nothing replaces the intra-wrapper alignment the 5px margin provided. In the scrolled header the category bullet badge will sit higher than the title text baseline. The added `line-height: 1.5` does not compensate for the badge-to-title alignment. This should be verified in the scrolled header and either kept or replaced with an equivalent adjustment.

title: `float: right` on `.small-action button` is silently ignored now that `.small-action` is a flex container
body: This PR makes `.small-action` a flexbox container (`@include flexbox()` / `@include align-items(center)`). Per CSS, floats have no effect on flex items, so the `button { float: right; }` rule inside `.small-action` stops working for any button that is a direct child of the `.small-action` row. Previously that button was pinned to the right edge of the post row; now it will be packed immediately after `.small-action-desc` on the left, because the container has no `justify-content: space-between` and the button has no `margin-left: auto`. If the button is a direct child (as the old float-based layout implies), this is a visible layout regression for small action posts (e.g. undo/expand controls). Either keep the button out of the flex flow or replace the float with a flex-appropriate right-alignment (`margin-left: auto` on the button or `justify-content: space-between` on the container).

title: `align-items` mixin omits `-moz-box-align`, so the `-moz-box` fallback gets no alignment
body: The `flexbox()` and `inline-flex()` mixins emit `display: -moz-box` / `display: -moz-inline-box` for old Gecko browsers, and the `order()` mixin emits `-moz-box-ordinal-group`, but the new `align-items()` mixin only emits `-webkit-box-align`, `-webkit-align-items`, `-ms-flex-align`, `-ms-align-items`, and `align-items` — there is no `-moz-box-align` line. Any browser that ends up using the `-moz-box` display fallback therefore gets the old box layout without the requested vertical alignment (e.g. the header `.contents` and `.small-action` rows will not be centered there). Either add `-moz-box-align: $alignment;` to the mixin or drop the `-moz-box` display fallbacks so the mixin set is self-consistent.

title: `-ms-align-items` is not a real property
body: The `align-items()` mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`, but no Microsoft flexbox implementation ever supported that property — IE10's 2012 'tweener' syntax uses `-ms-flex-align` (which the mixin already emits on the previous line). The `-ms-align-items` declaration is dead code that no browser will parse; it should be removed to avoid implying IE coverage that doesn't exist.

title: float: right on .small-action button is dead because the container is now flexbox
body: This PR makes .small-action a flex container (@include flexbox() at the top of the rule), but the nested button still relies on `float: right` for its position. The float property has no effect on flex items, so the button rendered in small-action posts (e.g. the staff edit/action button on 'topic closed'-style posts) will no longer be pinned to the right edge of the row — it will be laid out immediately after .small-action-desc, because neither the button nor .small-action-desc has margin-left: auto or flex-grow to push it right. Add `margin-left: auto` to the button (or let .small-action-desc grow) and remove the now-inert float.

title: margin-left: auto used to right-align .panel does not work in the legacy box syntax the flexbox() mixin emits
body: .panel lost `float: right` and is now pushed to the right edge solely by `margin-left: auto` inside the flex container .contents. The flexbox() mixin applied to .contents also emits the 2009-syntax `display: -webkit-box` / `display: -moz-box` fallbacks, and the 2009 flexbox model does not support auto margins (they compute to 0). So in exactly the legacy browsers those prefixes exist for, the header icon panel will sit immediately after the title instead of at the right edge — a regression from the previous float-based layout, which worked everywhere. Either drop the 2009 display fallbacks or provide a fallback (e.g. keep a float on .panel, or use -webkit-box-pack on the container).

title: align-items mixin omits -moz-box-align, inconsistent with the other new flexbox mixins
body: The new align-items mixin emits -webkit-box-align, -ms-flex-align and modern declarations but no -moz-box-align. Its sibling mixins flexbox() and order() both include the 2009 Mozilla syntax (-moz-box, -moz-box-ordinal-group), so on Gecko versions that only implement the legacy box model, an element using these mixins becomes a -moz-box with ordering applied while the requested alignment (center in the header/small-action, baseline on category bullets) is silently ignored — the mixin half-works in exactly the engines it claims to support. Add `-moz-box-align: $alignment;` for consistency (the 2009 spec accepts start/end/center/baseline/stretch).

title: website_name bypasses the untrusted_attributes restriction that hides website from anonymous viewers of TL0 users
body: This serializer deliberately strips profile fields like `website` for TL0 users viewed anonymously via `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111), which returns false when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true. The newly added `website_name` attribute is declared as a plain attribute and is not part of that mechanism, so for a restricted (e.g. spammy TL0) user the JSON payload still contains `website_name` with the website's host/path even though `website` itself is removed. That defeats the purpose of the restriction: anonymous viewers (and crawlers) still see the website domain. `website_name` should get the same guard — either add it to `untrusted_attributes` or make its inclusion conditional on `!scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`.

title: include_website_name is missing the trailing '?' so ActiveModelSerializers never calls it
body: AMS conditional-inclusion hooks must be named `include_<attribute>?`. The method defined here is `include_website_name` (no question mark), so it is dead code and `website_name` is always serialized — including as `null` for users with no website. Rename it to `include_website_name?` (and, per the related finding, have it also check `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` so the privacy behavior matches `website`).

title: Non-ASCII (IDN) website URLs make website_name nil, hiding the user's website entirely
body: Ruby's `URI()` only accepts ASCII; a website like `http://münchen.de/page` raises URI::InvalidURIError, which the inline `rescue nil` turns into a nil host, causing `website_name` to return nil. The template (`{{#if model.website_name}}`) then hides the website block completely. Previously the display name was computed client-side with `website.split('/')[2]`, which handled such URLs fine, so this is a display regression for users with internationalized domains. Consider a tolerant fallback (e.g. string splitting, or falling back to the raw website string) when URI parsing fails.

title: The sibling-subdomain branch of website_name (elsif) has no test coverage
body: The most intricate condition added in `website_name` — the `elsif` that strips the first DNS label of both hosts when they have the same label count (e.g. website `www.example.com` vs instance `forum.example.com`) — is not exercised by any spec. The three added tests only cover equal hosts, unrelated hosts, and the parent-domain suffix case. Add a test with `Discourse.current_hostname` returning 'forum.example.com' and website 'http://www.example.com/user' expecting 'www.example.com/user', plus a negative case (same label count, different parent, e.g. www.other.com) to lock in the comparison behavior.

title: website_name leaks the website of TL0 users whose profile fields are hidden from anonymous visitors
body: This serializer deliberately hides `website` (along with bio/location/etc.) for trust-level-0 users viewed by logged-out visitors, via `untrusted_attributes`, which defines `include_website?` to return false when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`. The new `website_name` attribute (declared at line 43) is not in the untrusted list and its include guard only checks `website.present?`, so for a TL0 spammer the JSON still contains `website_name` with the host/path of the website even though `website` itself is omitted — and the profile template renders that name next to the globe icon. This defeats the anti-spam measure that hides new users' links from anonymous viewers. Fix by adding `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` (or honoring `scope.restrict_user_fields?` in its include check) and add a spec covering an anonymous view of a TL0 user with a website.

title: include_website_name is missing the '?' suffix, so ActiveModelSerializers never calls it
body: ActiveModelSerializers decides whether to emit an attribute by calling `include_<attribute>?`. Every other guard in this file follows that convention (`include_email?`, `include_stats?`, `include_card_badge?`, etc.), but the new method is defined as `include_website_name` without the question mark. It is therefore never invoked, and `website_name` is always serialized — including `"website_name": null` for users who have no website set. Rename it to `include_website_name?`.

title: Same-length host comparison treats unrelated domains on a shared suffix as the same site
body: The `elsif` branch drops the first dot-separated label of both the website host and the instance host and compares the remainders whenever both hosts have the same number of labels (> 2). That works for the intended `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com` case, but it also matches completely unrelated sites that share a parent or public suffix: e.g. website `example.co.uk` with instance `another.co.uk` compares `co.uk == co.uk`, and `alice.github.io` vs `bob.github.io` compares `github.io == github.io`, causing the profile to display the full URL path of an unrelated website. Compare registrable domains (e.g. via PublicSuffix) instead of blindly stripping the first label.

title: website_name is stale after the user edits their website
body: Previously the displayed label was a computed property (`websiteName`) derived from `model.website`, so editing the website in preferences updated the profile display immediately. Now the label comes from the server as `website_name`, and the `save()` success handler only applies `bio_excerpt` from the PUT response, discarding the recomputed `website_name` even though the server returns it. After changing their website, the user keeps seeing the old label on their profile until a full page reload. Apply `data.user.website_name` (and ideally `website`) from the save response, or refetch the user.

title: website_name bypasses the TL0/anonymous restriction that hides website
body: The serializer deliberately hides `website` (along with bio, location, etc.) for trust-level-0 users viewed by anonymous visitors via the `untrusted_attributes` mechanism (`include_website?` returns false when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`).
