The new `website_name` attribute is not in the `untrusted_attributes` list, and its value is derived directly from `object.user_profile.website`, so anonymous visitors now receive `website_name` (the website's host, plus full path when it matches the instance domain) in the JSON for TL0 users even though `website` itself is withheld. This defeats the anti-spam purpose of restricting those fields. The existing spec 'doesn't serialize untrusted attributes' will not catch this because `website_name` isn't in its attribute list either. Fix by adding `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list (or checking `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` in its include guard) and extend the spec to cover it.

title: include_website_name is dead code — missing '?' so AMS never calls it
body: ActiveModelSerializers decides whether to serialize an attribute by calling `include_<attribute>?` (with a question mark), as used everywhere else in this file (`include_email?`, `include_stats?`, etc.). The added method is named `include_website_name` without the `?`, so it is never invoked and `website_name` is always included in the payload — serialized as explicit null for users who have no website — instead of being omitted when `website` is blank. Rename it to `include_website_name?` (or, better, add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` as noted in the other finding, which also defines the include predicate).

title: Websites Ruby's URI parser rejects (e.g. IDN/Unicode domains) disappear from the profile entirely
body: `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` returns nil for any stored website that Ruby's ASCII-only URI parser cannot handle, such as non-ASCII/IDN domains. `website_name` then returns nil, and since the template renders the globe icon and link only inside `{{#if model.website_name}}`, the user's website stops being displayed on their profile at all. The previous client-side code (`website.split("/")[2]`) still displayed the domain for such URLs, so this is a regression for affected users. Consider falling back to the raw `website` string when URI parsing fails instead of returning nil.

title: No test for the sibling-subdomain branch of website_name
body: The most complex branch of `website_name` — the `elsif` that compares parent domains when website and instance hosts have equal label depth greater than 2 (e.g. show the full path for `www.example.com` on a `forum.example.com` instance, but only the host for `www.other.com`) — has no test coverage. The three added examples only exercise the equal-host case and the website-domain-is-parent case, so a regression in the parent-domain comparison would not be caught.

title: Light/dark values swapped for embedded-post username link
body: The rule for `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` (the bold username shown in the expanded "in reply to" post above a reply) used to be `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new line is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))` — the light-theme argument changed from 30% to 70%, and the dark-theme argument is 30%. Every other conversion in this PR keeps the original percentage as the first (light) argument and mirrors it for dark (e.g. `.username.new-user a` in this same file correctly uses 70% light / 30% dark). Here the two appear swapped: light themes now render this prominent bold link at primary+70% (light gray on a light background) and dark themes get secondary+30% (dark gray on a dark background), both low-contrast. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

title: Light/dark values swapped for .custom-message-length on mobile
body: In mobile/modal.scss the `.custom-message-length` hint (character counter in the flag modal) was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The desktop counterpart (desktop/modal.scss line 94) for the same class correctly kept 70% for light and added 30% for dark. On mobile the arguments are reversed: light themes get primary+30% (much darker than the intended dimmed hint) and dark themes get secondary+70% (much lighter), i.e. the de-emphasis is inverted in both themes. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))` to match desktop.

title: Light-theme lightness for .topic-map h3 changed from 20% to 50%
body: In mobile/topic-post.scss, `.topic-map h3` was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The desktop version of the same rule (desktop/topic-post.scss line 321) kept 20% for light and added 80% for dark, which is the pattern this PR follows everywhere else. On mobile light themes the topic-map heading text is now significantly lighter than before, and dark themes get 50% instead of the mirrored 80%, so mobile and desktop render the same element differently. Unless the light-theme change was intentional, this should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`.

title: Light-theme lightness for .group-member-info .name changed from 30% to 50%
body: In desktop/user.scss, `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, changing the light-theme color (30% -> 50%, i.e. lighter) rather than only adding a dark variant. The parallel rule for usernames in common/base/user.scss (`.user-small .username a`, also originally 30%) was correctly converted to 30% light / 70% dark, so this looks like an accidental change. The same edit was made in mobile/user.scss line 497. If intentional (to match the sibling `.title` at 50%), it should be called out, since the PR's stated purpose is only adding dark-theme variants; otherwise use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

title: Light-theme lightness for .group-member-info .name changed from 30% to 50%
body: In mobile/user.scss, `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, which changes rendering on light themes (the name becomes lighter) instead of only adding the dark-theme variant. Other 30% instances in this PR (e.g. common/base/user.scss `.user-small .name`) were converted to 30% light / 70% dark. The same change exists in desktop/user.scss line 522. If not a deliberate light-theme restyle, this should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

title: Missed scale-color instance: category badge-notification still light-theme only
body: In _topic-list.scss, `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still uses `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`. Every other `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` occurrence in this file (th, td, topic-excerpt, etc.) was converted to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, so this one appears to have been overlooked. On dark themes the new-topic count badge on the categories list will get the light-theme treatment (an already-light $primary lightened a further 50%, near-white) instead of the dimmed secondary-based color used elsewhere, making it visually inconsistent with the surrounding converted text.

title: Light-theme color of embedded-post username accidentally changed from 30% to 70% lightness
body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a`, the original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The PR converted it to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. The first argument of `dark-light-choose` is the value used for light themes, so on light themes this text now renders at 70% lightness instead of the original 30% — the bold username in expanded 'in reply to' posts becomes far lighter and harder to read. Every analogous conversion in this PR preserves the original lightness in the first argument and uses the complementary value on `$secondary` for the dark branch (e.g. `.names span a` in common/base/topic-post.scss correctly became 30%/70%). The two lightness values here appear to have been swapped; it should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

title: Light-theme color of mobile .topic-map h3 changed from 20% to 50% lightness
body: In `.topic-map h3` (mobile), the original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`, but the PR changed it to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. Because the first argument of `dark-light-choose` applies to light themes, the topic-map heading on mobile light themes is now rendered at 50% lightness instead of the intended 20%, making it much fainter. The desktop version of the same selector was converted correctly to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`, so mobile is inconsistent. The light branch should remain at 20%: `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`.

title: Light-theme color of mobile .custom-message-length changed from 70% to 30% lightness
body: In `.custom-message-length` (mobile), the original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, but the PR changed it to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The first argument of `dark-light-choose` is the light-theme value, so on light themes the flag custom-message character counter now renders at 30% lightness instead of 70% — much darker than before. The desktop version of the same selector (desktop/modal.scss) was converted as 70%/30%, preserving the original light value, so mobile directly contradicts it. The values should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`.

title: Light-theme color of .group-member-info .name changed from 30% to 50% lightness
body: In `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` (desktop), the original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but the PR changed it to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. Since the first argument of `dark-light-choose` is the light-theme value, the member name in the group-members stream now renders at 50% lightness instead of 30% on light themes, making it noticeably fainter and identical to the `.title` below it. The analogous `.user-small .name` conversion in common/base/user.scss preserved the 30% light value (30%/70%), so this looks like a copy-paste slip. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

title: Light-theme color of .group-member-info .name changed from 30% to 50% lightness
body: In `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` (mobile), the original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but the PR changed it to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The first argument of `dark-light-choose` applies to light themes, so on light themes the member name now renders at 50% lightness instead of the original 30%, fainter than intended and identical to the `.title` rule beneath it. The analogous conversion in common/base/user.scss for `.user-small .name` kept the light value at 30% (30%/70%), so this deviates from the PR's stated goal of only changing the dark-theme branch. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

title: Swapped lightness values change the light-theme color of the embedded-post author link
body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a`, the original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The pattern used throughout this PR keeps the light-theme branch unchanged and adds a complementary dark-theme branch (100−X), i.e. this should have become `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))` — exactly as done for the same 30% case in common/base/topic-post.scss line 15 of this PR. Instead the committed line is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`: the two values are swapped. Light themes now render this link far lighter than before, and dark themes get a dark 30%-lightness gray instead of the intended 70% gray, hurting readability in both themes.

title: custom-message-length uses swapped lightness values, changing the light theme and conflicting with desktop
body: `.custom-message-length` was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. In this same PR the identical class in desktop/modal.scss (line 94) was correctly converted to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, but the mobile file was changed to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))` — the branches are swapped. Light-theme mobile now shows this hint text much darker than desktop/before, and dark-theme mobile shows it brighter than intended, so the flag-modal character-count hint is inconsistent between desktop and mobile.

title: topic-map h3 lightness changed from 20% to 50% in the light branch instead of adding a dark branch
body: `.topic-map h3` was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. Per this PR's conversion rule it should become `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))` — which is exactly what desktop/topic-post.scss line 321 (the same selector) was changed to. The mobile file instead committed `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, which lightens the heading in the light theme (a change this PR is not supposed to make) and gives dark themes a 50% gray where 80% was intended, diverging from desktop.

title: group-member-info .name light-theme color changed from 30% to 50% lightness
body: `.group-member-info .name` was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. Following the PR's rule it should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, but the committed line is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. This silently lightens the member name in light themes and gives dark themes a 50% gray instead of the correct 70% complement.

title: group-member-info .name light-theme color changed from 30% to 50% lightness
body: Same issue as desktop/user.scss: `.group-member-info .name` was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and should have been converted to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, but the committed value is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light theme now renders the name lighter than before and the dark theme gets the wrong complement (50% instead of 70%).

title: Missed conversion: category badge-notification still uses scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)
body: `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still reads `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`, the exact pattern this PR eliminates everywhere else (six other occurrences in this same file were converted). On dark themes, where $primary is near-white, this badge count stays blindingly bright instead of being dimmed to a gray derived from $secondary like the rest of the UI. It should be `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`.

title: Members endpoint now caps all groups at 50, but the public group members page has no pagination
body: Before this change, GroupsController#members returned every member for non-automatic groups and only applied limit/offset to automatic groups (default 200). Now every group is limited to 50 by default. The public group members page (discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6 calling model.findMembers() once, rendering templates/group/members.hbs) has no next/previous or load-more controls — only the admin template got pagination. As a result, any group with more than 50 members (and any automatic group with more than 50, previously 200) now only ever shows the first 50 alphabetically, and the remaining members are unreachable. Either keep returning the full roster for the public page or add pagination there.

title: PATCH /admin/groups/:id now silently ignores incremental membership changes and resets visible to false
body: The old update dispatched PATCH requests to update_patch, which applied params[:changes] (add/delete usernames) and touched nothing else. This PR removes that branch, so PATCH and PUT both run the single update action: params[:changes] is silently ignored while success_json is returned, and because visible is computed unconditionally as params[:visible] == "true", any legacy client sending an incremental membership PATCH without a visible param will silently flip the group to invisible. If the incremental API is being removed, the action should reject such requests rather than report success, and visible should not be forced to false when the parameter is absent.

title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
body: totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which yields an extra page when user_count divides evenly (e.g. 100 users with limit 50 gives 3 pages instead of 2). On the real last page "next" stays enabled (showingLast compares currentPage to the inflated totalPages); clicking it requests offset == user_count, the server returns an empty member list, and the admin sees an empty "3/3" page. Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit).

title: automatic does not resolve inside the member item view, so the remove link is rendered for automatic groups too
body: This template is rendered as the itemView of {{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}, so its scope is the member item view (which only has `member` set via the each keyword), not the adminGroup controller. `automatic` is a property of the group, so {{#unless automatic}} is always truthy and the × remove link renders even for automatic groups. Clicking it sends DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members; the server correctly returns 422, but Group#removeMember has no rejection handler, so the admin gets no feedback and the row simply stays. The group's automatic flag needs to be passed into the item view explicitly, and/or the failure should be surfaced.

title: remove_member automatic-group spec uses PUT although the route only accepts DELETE
body: The "cannot remove members from automatic groups" example issues `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42`, but config/routes.rb maps remove_member only for DELETE ("delete 'members'"); PUT members routes to add_members. Controller specs dispatch straight to the action, so the test passes anyway, but it no longer reflects real traffic and would not fail if the route/verb mapping were broken. Use `xhr :delete` here, matching the other remove_member example.

title: totalPages off-by-one when member count is a multiple of the page size
body: totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit this overcounts by one page (e.g. 100 members at limit 50 gives 3 pages instead of 2; 50 members gives 2 instead of 1). Because the next action is enabled until currentPage == totalPages, the admin can page to offset == user_count, and the server then returns an empty member list, rendering a phantom empty last page. This should be Math.ceil(user_count / limit).

title: Public group members page is silently truncated to 50 members
body: Previously #members returned the full member list for non-automatic groups (only automatic groups were limited, default 200). It now always paginates with a default limit of 50. The public-facing group members page (group-members route and group/members.hbs) calls findMembers() once and has no pagination controls — pagination UI was only added to the admin template — so any group with more than 50 members now shows only the first 50 on its public members page, with no way to view the rest.

title: remove_member raises RecordNotFound when the user is not a member
body: remove_member calls group.users.delete(user_id) with an Integer id. Rails resolves numeric arguments via find on the association, which raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound if that user is not in the group, producing a 404/500 instead of a successful no-op. This is easy to hit in practice (e.g. two admins removing the same user, or a retry after the member list was reloaded). Use a lookup that tolerates absence, e.g. delete the join record scoped by user_id, or find_by(id:) and skip when nil.

title: {{#unless automatic}} always true inside the item view, so remove link shows for automatic groups
body: This template is rendered by the group-member item view whose context is the member (a User), which has no `automatic` property, so {{#unless automatic}} always evaluates true and the remove (×) link is rendered even for members of automatic groups. Clicking it fires removeMember, which the server rejects with 422 can_not_modify_automatic, and the client-side removeMember promise has no rejection handler, so the admin gets no feedback at all. The automatic flag needs to come from the group/controller (e.g. passed into the item view) rather than being looked up on the member.

title: add_members does not strip whitespace around usernames and fails silently
body: add_members splits the usernames param on ',' but never strips the pieces, so input like "alice, bob" looks up the literal username " bob", finds nothing, and silently skips it — the action still returns success_json. An admin adding multiple users can get a success response while some users were never added. Strip each username (and/or report which names were not found) before the find_by_username call.

title: remove_member automatic-group spec uses the wrong HTTP verb
body: The example "cannot remove members from automatic groups" issues `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...`, but config/routes.rb only maps DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members to remove_member (PUT is mapped to add_members). Controller specs dispatch directly to the action regardless of verb, so this still passes, but the spec no longer exercises the verb the client actually uses and would not catch a broken or missing DELETE route. It should use `xhr :delete` like the neighboring remove_member example.

title: No spec coverage for the changed /groups/:group_id/members response contract
body: This PR changes GET /groups/:group_id/members from a bare serialized array to an object shaped {members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}} and introduces default pagination, but the spec changes only cover Admin::GroupsController — there is no request/controller spec asserting the new response shape, the meta values, or the default limit/offset behavior. Any pre-existing spec for #members would also now fail against the new shape. Add coverage for the new contract.

title: add_members/remove_member read params[:group_id] but the routes only provide params[:id]
body: The new routes in config/routes.rb (lines 49-50) are declared as bare `delete "members"` / `put "members"` inside `resources :groups`, which Rails turns into member routes of the form `/admin/groups/:id/members` — the group id arrives in `params[:id]`. However `add_members` (line 66) and `remove_member` (line 85) do `params.require(:group_id)`, and the Ember client (discourse/models/group.js removeMember/addMembers) puts the id only in the URL path, sending only `user_id`/`usernames` in the body. As a result every real request to add or remove a member raises ActionController::ParameterMissing and returns a 400, so both features are completely broken in production. The controller specs don't catch this because they bypass the router and inject `group_id` directly. Either the routes need to expose `:group_id` (e.g. nested/scope) or the controller should use `params.require(:id)`.

title: totalPages is off by one whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit
body: `totalPages` computes `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. For e.g. 100 members with limit 50 this returns 3, although only 2 pages exist (the correct formula is `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`). Because `showingLast` compares currentPage to this inflated totalPages, the "next" button stays enabled on the real last page; clicking it sets offset = user_count, and the server returns an empty list, so the admin lands on a phantom empty page (e.g. "3/3" with no members). This affects every group whose member count is an exact multiple of 50.

title: Public group members list is now truncated to 50 with no pagination UI
body: Previously `members` returned all members for non-automatic groups and only applied a limit (default 200) to automatic ones. The new code applies `limit` (default 50) to every group. The public group members page (discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6 calls findMembers with the model's default limit of 50, and discourse/templates/group/members.hbs has no next/previous controls) therefore now shows only the first 50 members of any larger group, with no way for users to see the rest — a regression from the previous behavior. Pagination support (or a higher cap) is needed on the public page, not just the admin page.

title: {{#unless automatic}} checks the member's automatic flag, so the remove link always renders
body: This template is rendered as the itemView of `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` in admin/templates/group.hbs, so its context is the member (a User), not the group. Users have no `automatic` property, so `automatic` is undefined and the `{{#unless automatic}}` guard always passes — the remove (×) link is rendered for members of automatic groups too. Clicking it triggers Admin::GroupsController#remove_member, which correctly rejects the request with a 422 (`can_not_modify_automatic`), and the client's `removeMember` action has no error handling, so the admin just gets a confusing failure. The template needs the group's flag (e.g. via the parent view/controller) instead of resolving `automatic` on the member.

title: limit parameter on public members endpoint is unbounded
body: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` accepts any value with no maximum, and this endpoint is reachable by any user who can see the group. A request with `limit=1000000` will load and serialize that many users in one request. The old code had the same flaw but only for automatic groups; it now applies to all groups. Clamp the limit (e.g. `[[limit, 200].min, 1].max`).

title: remove_member spec uses PUT although the route is DELETE, and specs never exercise the real routes
body: The spec calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...` but config/routes.rb wires `remove_member` to DELETE only. Controller specs bypass the router, so the test still passes — and for the same reason none of the add_members/remove_member specs detect that the actual routes supply the group id as `params[:id]` while the controller requires `params[:group_id]` (which makes the feature fail with a 400 in production). Use the correct verb and, ideally, add request/route-level specs that go through the router for these two endpoints.

title: Fallback locales are only loaded for HTTP requests; jobs, mailers and rake tasks cannot fall back
body: The fallback chain ([current locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en]) is only materialized on disk in ApplicationController#set_locale via the new I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! call. The translate accelerator loads translations lazily per locale: I18n.translate only calls load_locale(config.locale), and nothing outside the controller (Sidekiq jobs, ActionMailer such as notification/digest emails, rake tasks, console) ever loads the fallback locales. So when a key is missing in the user's locale in one of those contexts, the I18n::Backend::Fallbacks module iterates the fallback chain but the backend holds no data for the default locale or :en (their yml files were never read), and the output is "translation missing: ..." instead of the English text. This is exactly the case the feature is meant to fix, and emails are a primary surface for it. The ensure_loaded! call should live in the translation path itself (e.g. have I18n.ensure_loaded!/load_locale load the whole fallback chain for the locale) or be invoked from job/mailer entry points, not solely from ApplicationController.

title: Translation LRU cache key ignores SiteSetting.default_locale, which now affects resolved values
body: Translations are cached under a key of key + config.locale + backend.object_id, but with the new FallbackLocaleList the value returned by translate_no_cache also depends on SiteSetting.default_locale (the middle entry of the fallback chain). If an admin changes the site's default locale at runtime, entries already cached through the old chain are never invalidated — the accelerator's @cache is only cleared by I18n.reload!, which a site-setting change does not trigger — so users can keep seeing fallback text in the previous default language until the 300-entry LRU happens to evict those keys or the process restarts. Include the default locale in the cache key or clear the translation cache when default_locale changes.

title: No specs cover the new fallback resolution and loading behavior
body: This PR changes how every missing translation is resolved (custom FallbackLocaleList ordering user locale -> SiteSetting.default_locale -> :en, fallbacks now enabled in all environments instead of only production, and explicit per-locale loading via ensure_loaded!), yet adds no tests. At minimum there should be coverage that a key missing in the current locale resolves to the site default locale and then to English, and that ensure_loaded! loads each locale in the chain, since regressions here surface as user-visible "translation missing" strings across the site and in emails.

title: Fallback locales are only loaded during web requests, so fallbacks silently fail in mailers, background jobs, and other non-request code
body: Translations are loaded lazily per-locale by the translate accelerator: I18n.translate only loads config.locale, and the only place that loads the full fallback chain (current locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en) is this new before_filter via I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!. Any code that translates outside the request cycle (Sidekiq jobs, ActionMailer views, rake tasks, console, plugins) never runs set_locale, so in those processes only the active locale's yml file is ever loaded. When a key is missing in that locale, I18n::Backend::Fallbacks will dutifully try the site default and :en, but those locales' translations were never loaded into the backend, so the lookup raises MissingTranslationData and the output is a 'translation missing: ...' string instead of the English/default fallback this PR is meant to provide. The loading of the fallback chain should live in the accelerator itself (e.g., in I18n.translate/load_locale, iterate I18n.fallbacks[config.locale] and ensure each locale is loaded) rather than only in ApplicationController#set_locale.

title: No tests cover the new server-side fallback behavior
body: This PR changes translation lookup for every locale in every environment (fallback chain current locale -> SiteSetting.default_locale -> :en, lazy loading of that chain via FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!, and removal of config.i18n.fallbacks from the environment configs), but adds no specs. Nothing verifies that a key missing from the active locale falls back to the site default and then to :en, that FallbackLocaleList#[] builds the expected chain (including uniq/compact behavior when locale == default == :en), or that ensure_loaded! actually loads every locale in the chain. A regression here would surface as untranslated or 'translation missing' strings across the whole site, so coverage of this initializer and the set_locale integration is warranted before merging.

title: Translation LRU cache key ignores the site-specific fallback locale
body: The cache key for memoized translations is built only from the key, the current locale and the backend object id (`k = "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`). With this PR, the resolved value of a translation now also depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale` (via `FallbackLocaleList`), and that setting is per-site on multisite installs and can be changed at runtime — but it is not part of the cache key, and the cache itself (`@cache` on the I18n singleton) is process-global. Consequences: (1) on a multisite cluster sharing one process, a key missing in locale X is resolved through whichever site's default locale populated the cache first — e.g. a user on a site whose default is German can be served the French fallback string cached for another site, until the 300-entry LRU happens to evict it; (2) on a single site, after an admin changes `default_locale`, fallback strings in the old language keep being served from the cache until eviction. Previously (`config.i18n.fallbacks = true`) the fallback target was the global `I18n.default_locale`, so cached entries were consistent. Include `SiteSetting.default_locale` (or the resolved fallback chain) in the cache key, or clear `I18n`'s cache when the setting changes.

title: Fallback locale files are only loaded for controller requests, so fallbacks silently fail in jobs/mailers/rake
body: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is only invoked from the `set_locale` before_filter, i.e. only for HTTP requests through ApplicationController. The translate accelerator's `translate` only ever loads yml files for `config.locale` (`load_locale(config.locale)`); it never loads the fallback locales itself. Any server-side code that translates outside a web request — Sidekiq jobs, ActionMailer views, rake tasks, console — with `I18n.locale` set to a non-English locale will walk the fallback chain (locale → site default → :en), find that no translations were ever loaded for the fallback locales, and render "translation missing: xx.yyy" instead of the site-default/English string. So the feature this PR adds silently does not work in exactly the server-side contexts that don't pass through a controller. Load the fallback locales inside the accelerator instead (e.g. have `I18n.ensure_loaded!`/`translate` load every locale in `I18n.fallbacks[locale]`), or route jobs/mailers through the same ensure_loaded! step.

title: FallbackLocaleList#[] does a SiteSetting read and several array allocations on every interpolated translation
body: The i18n fallbacks backend calls `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` on every backend lookup, and `FallbackLocaleList#[]` performs a `SiteSetting.default_locale` read plus `[locale, ...].uniq.compact` (multiple array allocations) each time. The translate accelerator only memoizes argument-free lookups — every `I18n.t` call with interpolation options (the common case in this codebase, e.g. anything with `count:` or a username) bypasses the LRU cache and pays this cost per call, in a code path that exists specifically to make translation fast. Consider memoizing the computed list keyed by (locale, default_locale) and invalidating when the setting changes.

title: No tests for the new fallback semantics, which now apply to all environments
body: This PR rewrites how fallbacks are computed (new `FallbackLocaleList`, new `I18n.ensure_loaded!`, per-request `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`) and, as a side effect, enables fallbacks in every environment — previously they were only turned on via `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` in the production-like configs, so in development/test a key present in English but missing in the active locale now silently renders the English text instead of a "translation missing" message. No specs cover any of this. At minimum, add coverage that `I18n.fallbacks[:xx]` returns `[xx, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq`, that a key missing in the active locale resolves through the site default and then English, and that the fallback locale files are actually loaded (the `ensure_loaded!` path).

title: Denial cache can persist denials computed from stale data and is never invalidated
body: In Check, when the DB fallback still denies, the denial is stored in permDenialCache for shortCacheTTL (30s) and short-circuits all later checks for that (namespace, user, action, name, folder) tuple. Two problems follow: (1) The deny decision may depend on the cached folder tree (checkInheritedPermissions -> buildFolderTree uses folderCache, also 30s TTL), which the DB fallback does NOT refresh. If a teammate of a folder creator checks a dashboard inside a folder created seconds ago, the fresh permission re-query returns the same scopes (e.g. only folders:uid:<grandparent>) and the stale tree has no ancestors for the new folder, so the request is denied and that deny is now cached for another 30s — extending the deny window up to ~60s after folder creation, longer than before this change, for exactly the 'newly created folder' scenario this PR is meant to fix. (2) When the fallback re-fetch does update permCache with fresh scopes, any pre-existing denial entry for a resource covered by those fresh scopes is not deleted, so the stale denial still wins over fresher permission data. Consider refreshing/invalidating the folder tree (or skipping denial caching) when the deny relied on folder-tree evaluation, and/or keying denials so a fresh allow can supersede them.

title: Every denied check for a distinct resource name now triggers a full DB permission fetch
body: With the new fallback, whenever the cached permission map does not contain the requested scope, Check unconditionally re-queries the full permission set from the database (getIdentityPermissions -> getUserPermissions -> permissionStore.GetUserPermissions). The denial cache only deduplicates repeats of the exact same (user, action, name, parentFolder) tuple, so a caller that polls N distinct resources it cannot access (dashboard listing integrations, scanners, a user clicking through an org where most content is restricted) now issues N full permission queries per 30s window, where before this change the permission cache answered all of them with a single query per user/action. Singleflight only collapses concurrent identical user+action fetches, not sequential distinct names. Consider bounding the fallback (e.g., a short 'permissions fresh as of' marker per user/action so repeated denials on different names within a few seconds don't each hit the DB).

title: Deny-cache test does not actually prove the denial cache short-circuits
body: In TestService_CacheCheck/'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry', the permission cache is seeded with map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false} and the comment claims this 'allows access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked'. A scope-map value of false does not allow anything, so the test returns Allowed=false even if the denial-cache logic were removed entirely: the cached perms would deny, the DB fallback (empty fakeStore) would also deny, and the assertion would still pass. To prove the denial cache is consulted, the cached value must be true — then the test would fail if the permDenialCache check in Check were removed or bypassed.

title: Permission-cache hits that result in denial are recorded as cache misses
body: When getCachedIdentityPermissions returns a cached permission map (cache hit) but checkPermission returns allowed=false, execution falls out of the if-block and reaches s.metrics.permissionCacheUsage.WithLabelValues("false", ...) — recording a cache miss even though the permission cache was hit. Denied checks are precisely the traffic pattern this PR optimizes, so this mislabeling systematically skews the cache hit-rate metric downward and makes the new caching behavior look less effective than it is. The hit/miss label should be recorded based on whether the cache lookup succeeded, before evaluating the allow/deny outcome.

title: Denial cache is consulted before the permission cache, so a stale denial overrides fresher cached grants
body: In Check, the denial cache is checked first (lines 116-121) and returns Allowed=false immediately, before the cached permission set is consulted (line 123). Denial entries live for shortCacheTTL (30s) and are never invalidated. Consider: (1) a user is denied resource A after a DB requery, so a denial entry for A is cached; (2) the user is then granted A in the DB; (3) any other cache miss for the same user+action re-queries the DB and refreshes permCache, which now includes A; (4) a new Check for A hits the stale denial entry and returns false even though the server's own fresh permCache would allow it. This reintroduces the exact 'user can't access a resource they were just granted' problem this PR is meant to fix, for up to 30s after any denial. Checking the cached permissions first (allow on positive evidence, then consult the denial cache for the fast-deny path) would avoid contradicting fresher cached grants while keeping the denial fast path.

title: userPermDenialCacheKey concatenates name/parent with underscores, which they can themselves contain, allowing key collisions
body: The key is built as namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent with no escaping. Dashboard and folder UIDs may contain underscores, so two different (name, parent) pairs can produce the same key: e.g. (name="dash_1", parent="x") and (name="dash", parent="1_x") both yield "..._dash_1_x". A denial cached for one resource would then incorrectly deny a different resource/parent combination for up to the 30s TTL. Use a separator that cannot appear in UIDs, or otherwise unambiguously encode the fields.

title: Denial-precedence test caches a non-allowing permission, so it doesn't prove the denial cache wins over cached grants
body: In the subtest "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry", the comment says "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked", but the code stores map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false} in permCache. With a false value the cached permissions would deny the request anyway, so the test would still pass if the denial-cache branch in Check were broken or removed. The cached scope should be set to true so the test actually verifies that a denial entry takes precedence over an allowing cached permission set.

title: Stale denial-cache entry overrides fresher permission data already in the server's cache
body: In Service.Check, the permission-denial cache is consulted first and short-circuits the request, before the permission cache is checked for an allow. A denial entry is written only after a fresh DB lookup denies, but it then lives for shortCacheTTL (30s). Meanwhile, any DB re-query for the same user+action (triggered by a check on a different resource, or by cache expiry) rewrites the entire permCache scope map with fresh permissions, because getUserPermissions always calls permCache.Set after fetching. Concrete sequence: t0 Check(user, dashboards:read, dash1) denies and caches a denial for dash1; t1 the user is granted access to dash1 and dash2; t2 Check(user, dashboards:read, dash2) misses the cached scope map, re-queries the DB, allows, and repopulates permCache with permissions that now include dash1; t3 Check(user, dashboards:read, dash1) hits the stale denial entry and returns Allowed=false even though the server's own permission cache (and the DB) would allow it. The user stays denied for that resource until the denial entry expires. This partially undermines the PR's stated goal (a single check that races the permission write poisons the resource for 30s). Checking the permission cache for an allow before consulting the denial cache would preserve the fast-deny path while preventing stale denials from overriding fresher allow data the server already holds.

title: Denial-cache precedence test uses a non-allowing cache entry, so it passes even without the denial-cache code
body: The subtest "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" says it seeds the permission cache to "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked", but it actually sets s.permCache to map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false} — a value that does not grant the scope. With that value, checkPermission also denies via the normal cached path, and the subsequent DB fallback against the fake store (which has no permissions) denies as well, so assert.False(t, resp.Allowed) passes even if the entire permDenialCache branch in Service.Check were deleted. The comment contradicts the code, and the new denial-cache behavior — including the permDenialCache.Set after a DB denial in service.go — is effectively untested. Seed the cache with map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": true} so the test fails if the denial-cache check is removed or bypassed.

title: "Silence notifications" menu item is shown but does nothing in the new rule list
body: In the new list view, GrafanaRuleListItem renders RuleActionsButtons with only promRule (the `rule` prop is undefined). AlertRuleMenu now derives the Silence ability from the Prometheus rule via useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, so the "Silence notifications" menu item renders enabled and clicking it calls handleSilence -> setShowSilenceDrawer(true). However, the drawer is gated on `{rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer && <SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer rulerRule={rule} .../>}`; with `rule` undefined the drawer never mounts, so clicking the menu item is a silent no-op. The new GrafanaGroupLoader test only asserts that the Silence menu item exists, never that clicking it opens anything. The silence flow needs to be driven from the prom rule/identifier, or the item should be hidden when no ruler rule is available.

title: Delete and Pause actions no longer appear in the list view rule menu
body: AlertRuleMenu gates the Delete item on `canDelete && rulerRule` (line 165) and the Pause item on `canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` (line 123). The new list view (GrafanaRuleListItem -> RuleActionsButtons.V2) never passes a rulerRule, only a GrafanaPromRuleDTO, so even though canDelete/canPause can now be satisfied through useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, the Delete and Pause items never render. Previously the list passed the ruler rule and both actions were available. The updated GrafanaGroupLoader test codifies the regression by asserting exactly 4 menu items (silence, duplicate, copy link, export) with no delete. Users of the new list view can no longer delete or pause rules from it, which is a functional regression beyond the stated goal of removing ruler API requests.

title: Federated rule groups lose their edit/delete immutability protection
body: useAllAlertRuleAbilities (which backs useAlertRuleAbility/useAlertRuleAbilities used across the old list view and detail views) previously computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` and treated federated rules as immutable, hiding Update/Delete/Pause/Restore/DeletePermanently. This PR rewrites it to delegate to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which hardcodes `const isFederated = false` with a TODO. As a result, for Mimir/GEM federated (cross-tenant, source_tenants) rule groups, those actions now report as supported whenever permissions allow, rendering Edit/Delete/Pause buttons that were previously suppressed; attempted operations will fail at the ruler API or mutate a group the UI previously treated as read-only.

title: Duplicate menu item becomes enabled for data-source rules based on Grafana-internal create permission
body: canDuplicate now ORs the ruler-based ability with the result of useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities. For a non-Grafana (Mimir/Cortex/Loki) rule, promRule fails prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule so skipToken is passed, producing useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined). With rule undefined, loading=false makes duplicateSupported=true, and the allowed side is checked against getRulesPermissions('grafana').create (alert.rules:create). A user who has Grafana-managed rule create permission but lacks alert.rules.external:write will now see the "Duplicate" menu item on cloud rules; before this change only the ruler-based ability (which requires the external write permission) was consulted. The backend still enforces permissions, but the UI now advertises an action the user cannot complete.

title: GrafanaRuleListItem rendered without a key in the filtered rule list
body: In the rules.map switch, the 'grafana' branch returns `<GrafanaRuleListItem rule={...} .../>` without `key={key}`; the replaced GrafanaRuleLoader had key={key}, and the sibling 'datasource' and 'default' branches still pass key. React will emit a missing-key warning, and mixing keyed and unkeyed siblings in the same list can cause React to mis-associate per-item component state (e.g. RuleActionsButtons' silence drawer / delete modal state) when the list updates.

title: Grafana recording rules lose the Export menu item in the list view
body: The new prom-based ability gates ModifyExport on prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) (`[AlertRuleAction.ModifyExport]: [isAlertingRule, exportAllowed]`), whereas the ruler-based path used rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule), which also matches recording rules. In the new list view only the prom-based path runs (no rulerRule is fetched), so Grafana-managed recording rules no longer show the "Export / With modifications" menu entry even though they did before and modify-export is valid for recording rules.

title: Rule view link drops the returnTo parameter
body: The previous GrafanaRuleListItem (in the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx) built the href as createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo }) using createReturnTo(), so navigating back from the rule detail page returned the user to the filtered list. The new component uses createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`) with no returnTo, breaking return-to-previous navigation for rules opened from the new list and filter views.

title: JSDoc still claims the group is loaded from Prometheus and Ruler endpoints
body: The comment above GrafanaGroupLoader says "Loads an evaluation group from Prometheus and Ruler endpoints", but this PR removed the ruler query (useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery) — only the Prometheus endpoint is queried now. The expectedRulesCount prop comment also still references the ruler response. These stale comments misdescribe the component's behavior after the change.

title: Stale comment and variable name referring to ruler rule preloading
body: After removing the alertRuleApi getGrafanaRulerGroup prefetch, the comment "This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules, but it improves the UX..." and the variable name `cacheAndRulerPreload` are stale — the block now only upserts the Prometheus groups cache. The comment should be updated so readers don't think ruler preloading still happens here.

title: 'Silence notifications' menu item is shown in the ruler-less list view but clicking it does nothing
body: In the new list view, GrafanaRuleListItem renders RuleActionsButtons with only `promRule` (no `rule`/rulerRule). AlertRuleMenu still shows the 'Silence notifications' item because `canSilence` can now be satisfied by the new useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(promRule) check. However, `handleSilence` only sets `showSilenceDrawer=true`, and the drawer is gated on `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` (line 104), which is false when no ruler rule is passed — so SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer is never rendered and the click silently does nothing. The newly added GrafanaGroupLoader test only asserts that the menu item is visible, not that it works, so it doesn't catch this. Either render a silence drawer that works from prom-rule data or hide the menu item when no rulerRule is available.

title: GrafanaRuleListItem rendered without a React key in the filtered rule list
body: In the `rules.map(...)` switch, the 'grafana' branch returns `<GrafanaRuleListItem>` without the `key={key}` prop that the previous `<GrafanaRuleLoader>` had (the 'datasource' and default branches still set `key`). React falls back to index-based reconciliation for grafana rows, so as pages are appended by infinite scroll and the 20s polling refresh re-renders rows, per-item state (open dropdown menus, drawers) can become attached to the wrong rule, and React logs a missing-key warning. Add `key={key}` to the grafana branch.

title: Federated rule groups are no longer treated as immutable after the useAllAlertRuleAbilities refactor
body: Before this change, `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)`, which made rules in Mimir federated groups (groups with `source_tenants`) non-editable/non-deletable in the UI. It now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifierV2)`, which hardcodes `const isFederated = false` with a TODO because the group object is no longer passed in. All existing consumers of `useAlertRuleAbility`/`useAllAlertRuleAbilities` (e.g. RuleActionsButtons, RulesTable, rule details) will now offer Edit/Delete/Pause for federated rules, and those operations will fail at the ruler API. Pass the group (or an isFederated flag) into useAllRulerRuleAbilities so the check is preserved.

title: Duplicate/View abilities fall back to Grafana permissions for non-Grafana rules when rule is undefined (skipToken)
body: When the prom rule is not a Grafana rule, callers pass `skipToken`, and `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` runs with `rule === undefined`. With no rule, `loading` is false, so `MaybeSupported` becomes `AlwaysSupported` and `[AlertRuleAction.Duplicate]` evaluates to `[true, has-grafana-create-permission]` using `getRulesPermissions('grafana')` (same for View with grafana read permission). AlertRuleMenu and RuleActionsButtons OR these abilities with the ruler-based ones, so for a cloud (Mimir/Loki) rule, a user who only has Grafana-managed rule create permission — but not `alert.rules.external:write` — will now see the Duplicate menu item; the actual operation will fail server-side. When the rule is undefined the hook should return all-false abilities instead of evaluating grafana permissions.

title: Export (modify-export) and pause support dropped for Grafana recording rules in the list view
body: The ruler-based ability used `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)` — true for both Grafana alerting and recording rules — to gate `ModifyExport`, `Pause` and `Restore`. The new `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` gates these on `prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`, which is false for recording rules, even though modify-export and pausing are supported for Grafana recording rules elsewhere. Because the list view no longer fetches ruler rules, the OR fallback in AlertRuleMenu can't compensate, so Grafana recording rules lose the Export menu item in the list (and the Pause ability now reports unsupported). Use the recording-inclusive type guard where the ruler version used `grafana.rule`.

title: Rule view link lost the returnTo parameter
body: The removed GrafanaRuleLoader built the rule href with `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })` using createReturnTo(); the new GrafanaRuleListItem builds the same URL without `returnTo`. Navigating back from a rule to the list no longer restores the user's previous list location/filter state. Restore the `returnTo` query parameter.

title: Stale comment about preloading ruler rules after the prefetch was removed
body: The comment 'This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules, but it improves the UX…' and the variable name `cacheAndRulerPreload` still describe ruler preloading, but the `alertRuleApi.util.prefetch('getGrafanaRulerGroup', …)` call was removed in this PR. The comment/name is now misleading about what the code does and should be updated.

title: Silence drawer never opens in the new list view: clicking 'Silence notifications' does nothing
body: RuleActionsButtons now supports being called with only a promRule (no rulerRule), which is exactly how GrafanaRuleListItem uses it in the new ruler-less list view. In AlertRuleMenu the Silence menu item is shown based on the new prom-rule abilities (useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities returns Silence=[silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule]), so for a Grafana alerting rule the 'Silence notifications' item is visible and clickable (the updated GrafanaGroupLoader test even asserts its presence). However, clicking it only calls setShowSilenceDrawer(true), and the drawer itself is still gated on `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` where `rule` is the (now optional) rulerRule. With rulerRule undefined the drawer is never rendered, so the silence action silently does nothing. The drawer needs to be renderable from the prom rule (e.g. a prom-based silence drawer) or the menu item must be hidden when no rulerRule is available.

title: skipToken path returns enabled abilities, granting Duplicate on cloud rules based on Grafana permissions
body: useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities/useGrafanaPromRuleAbility translate skipToken into `undefined` and call useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined). With rule undefined, useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable returns loading:false, so MaybeSupported becomes AlwaysSupported, isPluginProvided/isProvisioned are false, and the abilities are computed with getRulesPermissions('grafana'): Duplicate becomes [true, ctx.hasPermission(AlertingRuleCreate)]. AlertRuleMenu passes skipToken whenever promRule is not a Grafana prom rule (i.e. for every cloud/Mimir rule), and computes canDuplicate as ruler || grafana. As a result a user who has the Grafana-managed rule create permission but NOT AlertingRuleExternalWrite will now see the Duplicate menu item on cloud rules (previously only the ruler-based ability, which checks the external-write permission for that data source, was used). The skipToken/undefined-rule path should yield all-disabled abilities instead of permission-evaluated ones.

title: Federated rule groups lose their immutable treatment after useAllAlertRuleAbilities refactor
body: Before this change, useAllAlertRuleAbilities (still used via useAlertRuleAbility by CombinedRule consumers such as the existing RulesTable) computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)`, which made Update/Delete/Pause unsupported for federated (cross-tenant) Mimir/GEM rule groups. The hook now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which only receives a RulerRuleDTO and hardcodes `const isFederated = false` with a TODO. Consequently, for rules in federated groups the Edit/Delete/Pause abilities become 'supported' again and the corresponding buttons/menu items reappear; attempting the operation will fail against the ruler or, worse, modify a group the UI intentionally treated as immutable. The federated check needs to be preserved somewhere in the new delegation chain.

title: Export (and Pause) abilities restricted to alerting rules, recording rules lose Export in list view
body: In useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, ModifyExport is computed as [isAlertingRule, exportAllowed] where isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule). The ruler-based equivalent uses isGrafanaManagedAlertRule = rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule), which matches both Grafana alerting AND recording rules, so recording rules currently expose the 'Export / With modifications' menu item (the modify-export flow supports recording rules). In the new ruler-less list view the rulerRule is absent, so canExport relies solely on the prom-based ability and recording rules lose the Export menu entry. The same narrowing applies to Pause/Restore (Grafana recording rules are pausable, but the prom-based ability requires an alerting rule), which will bite once the pause menu item is wired to prom rules.

title: GrafanaRuleListItem rendered without React key in the filtered rule list
body: In FilterViewResults the rules are rendered via rules.map(...). The previous code rendered <GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} .../>, and the 'datasource' and 'default' branches still pass key={key}, but the 'grafana' branch now renders <GrafanaRuleListItem rule={rule} groupIdentifier={...} ... /> with no key prop. This triggers React's missing-key warning and forces index-based reconciliation for Grafana rows; since these rows contain stateful children (AlertRuleMenu, silence drawer state, delete modal), any future reorder/removal of rows could attach that state to the wrong rule. Pass key={key} as before.

title: Rule link no longer carries the returnTo parameter
body: The previous GrafanaRuleListItem (in the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx) built the rule href as createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo }) using createReturnTo(), so navigating back from the rule detail view returned the user to the originating (possibly filtered) rule list. The new component builds `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` with no returnTo, so the detail view's back navigation falls back to the default alert list and loses the user's list context/filters. Re-add the returnTo parameter.

title: Stale comment about preloading ruler rules after ruler prefetch was removed
body: The diff removes the alertRuleApi prefetch('getGrafanaRulerGroup', ...) dispatch but leaves the comment 'This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules, but it improves the UX. Because the user waits a bit longer for the initial load but doesn't need to wait for each group to be loaded' and the variable name cacheAndRulerPreload. The comment now describes behavior that no longer exists and is misleading about what the remaining upsertQueryData does; update the comment and rename the variable.

title: Sharded queries are interpolated N+1 times: once in runShardSplitQuery and again in every runSplitQuery sub-request
body: runShardSplitQuery (shardQuerySplitting.ts:49-52) now maps every target through datasource.applyTemplateVariables before grouping by stream shard, and then executes each shard group by building a subRequest and calling runSplitQuery. With this change, runSplitQuery also maps every target through datasource.applyTemplateVariables (the new .map here), so in the shard-splitting flow each query is interpolated once up front plus once per shard-group sub-request. The updated test 'Interpolates queries before running' in shardQuerySplitting.test.ts now expects applyTemplateVariables to have been called 5 times for a single target (1 upfront + 4 shard batches), which bakes this redundancy into the test suite. Variable substitution ($var, $__auto, step) is effectively idempotent so this mostly wastes work, but request.filters is passed on both calls, so ad hoc filters are appended to the stream selector twice unless applyTemplateVariables dedupes them — producing duplicated label matchers in the LogQL selector sent to Loki. Consider interpolating in only one place (e.g. let runSplitQuery skip interpolation when the caller already interpolated, or have the shard path rely on a single interpolation point).

title: No test coverage for ad hoc filters (request.filters) through the split/shard query paths
body: This change newly threads request.filters into datasource.applyTemplateVariables in runShardSplitQuery (previously it called interpolateVariablesInQueries with only scopedVars, so ad hoc filters were never applied to sharded queries) and in runSplitQuery (which previously did not interpolate targets at all). None of the added or updated tests set request.filters and assert the resulting selector — they only cover replacement of variables in expr and step. Because the shard path now invokes applyTemplateVariables multiple times per target (the updated 'Interpolates queries before running' test expects 5 calls for one query), a duplication or loss of ad hoc matchers in the final LogQL selector would go unnoticed. A test passing request.filters through both splitting paths and asserting the final expr would close the gap.

title: Shard-splitting path now interpolates every target twice
body: runShardSplitQuery() now maps every target through datasource.applyTemplateVariables() (line 52), but the already-interpolated targets are then passed via subRequest into runSplitQuery() (line 163), which after this PR also maps every target through datasource.applyTemplateVariables() (querySplitting.ts line 299). So in the shard path each query is interpolated once per shard-group request plus once at entry. The updated test codifies this: 'Interpolates queries before running' now expects applyTemplateVariables to have been called 5 times for a single-target request (1 + 4 shard sub-requests). Re-running template expansion on already-interpolated text is a known source of query corruption in Grafana: if a variable's value contains '$'-syntax (e.g. a custom variable value containing '${other_var}' or a label value with a '$' token matching another variable), the second pass will expand tokens introduced by the first pass and silently change the query sent to Loki. Additionally, because subRequest spreads the original request, request.filters survives into runSplitQuery, so ad hoc filters are injected into the selector twice (once per interpolation pass), producing duplicated matchers in the generated LogQL. Consider interpolating only once, e.g. by having runShardSplitQuery pass a flag so runSplitQuery skips interpolation for already-interpolated sub-requests.

title: Empty-expr filter now runs before interpolation instead of after
body: Before this change, the shard path interpolated first (datasource.interpolateVariablesInQueries) and then filtered out queries with an empty expr, so a query whose expr was only a variable that expands to an empty string was dropped. The new code filters on the raw, uninterpolated expr (lines 50-51) and interpolates afterwards (line 52), so such a query now passes the filter and proceeds with an empty interpolated expr: it is grouped via getSelectorForShardValues(''), triggers a fetchLabelValues call with an empty stream selector, and is ultimately sent to Loki as an empty query, which will return a parse error to the user instead of being silently ignored. The same ordering exists in the updated runSplitQuery (querySplitting.ts lines 296-299). Move the empty-expr check to after the applyTemplateVariables map, or filter again after interpolation.

title: Interpolating before querySupportsSplitting defeats the $__range no-splitting guard
body: runSplitQuery now interpolates every target via datasource.applyTemplateVariables (line 299) before partition(queries, (query) => !querySupportsSplitting(query)) runs on the next line. applyTemplateVariables substitutes the built-in range variables ($__range, $__range_s, $__range_ms) from scopedVars, and dashboard/Explore requests always carry those scoped vars. querySupportsSplitting() decides a query must not be split by calling isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr), which searches for the literal text '$__range' — but by the time it runs, that text has already been replaced (e.g. count_over_time({a="b"}[$__range]) has become count_over_time({a="b"}[30d])). Consequence: queries using $__range are now time-split instead of being routed to nonSplittingQueries and executed once over the full range, which is exactly what the comment above the check says must not happen. Besides contradicting the documented intent, this is a real cost/correctness regression for large ranges: with a 30-day dashboard, each 1-day chunk evaluates count_over_time(...[30d]), re-scanning ~30 days of data per chunk (~30x the scanned volume of the previous single request). The existing unit tests do not catch this because the test requests carry no scopedVars, so $__range survives interpolation in tests but not in production. The isQueryWithRangeVariable check should run on the raw, pre-interpolation expr — or, if splitting such queries is now intentional, the dead check and its misleading comment should be removed.

title: Queries are now interpolated two to three times (runShardSplitQuery / runSplitQuery / runQuery)
body: Interpolation is now applied repeatedly to the same targets. LokiDatasource.runQuery — which the splitting code calls for every sub-request (runSplitGroupedQueries in querySplitting.ts, and splitQueriesByStreamShard here) — already maps targets through applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters). With the new .map(...) added here in runShardSplitQuery and the one added in runSplitQuery (querySplitting.ts), every sub-query in the time-splitting path is interpolated twice, and every sub-query in the shard-splitting path three times (runShardSplitQuery → runSplitQuery → runQuery), because sub-requests keep the original request.scopedVars and request.filters. Two concrete consequences: (1) ad hoc filters from request.filters are injected into the stream selector on every pass, so the LogQL selectors sent to Loki contain each ad hoc matcher two or three times (previously they were injected exactly once, in runQuery); (2) any variable value that itself contains template syntax (a constant/text variable holding a literal containing another variable's name, or a $-prefixed token) is interpolated again by the later passes, silently altering the query Loki executes. The updated shard-splitting test that expects applyTemplateVariables to have been called 5 times for a single-target request (1 call in runShardSplitQuery plus 1 per shard group in runSplitQuery, with runQuery mocked) shows the redundancy is being baked into the tests rather than eliminated. One of the interpolation layers should be removed (or the later passes skipped for already-interpolated targets).

title: traceID silently dropped from "Plugin Request Completed" log lines
body: The previous implementation of logRequest explicitly appended the trace ID to the log params via tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false). This PR removes that block and instead relies on m.logger.FromContext(ctx), which only picks up the contextual attributes stored by ContextualLoggerMiddleware.instrumentContext (endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname). instrumentContext does not add a traceID attribute, so the traceID field is silently lost from these log lines, breaking log-to-trace correlation for plugin requests. This is a behavioral regression in a PR described as a rename-only chore. Fix: add the trace ID back, either by including tracing.TraceIDFromContext in the attributes added by instrumentContext or by continuing to append it in logRequest.

title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh recorder, making contextual logs invisible to tests
body: TestLogger.FromContext ignores the receiver and returns NewTestLogger(), a brand-new instance with its own empty Logs fields. Code under test that logs via FromContext — notably the updated LoggerMiddleware, which now calls m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...) — will record calls on a throwaway instance, so any test passing a TestLogger and asserting on its InfoLogs/WarnLogs/ErrorLogs counters will observe zero calls and cannot verify log output. The fake should return the receiver itself (or a logger that shares the same recording state) so contextual logging remains observable in tests.

title: Doc comment on Logger.FromContext is a copy of New's and describes the wrong contract
body: The comment on FromContext reads "returns a new contextual Logger that has this logger's context plus the given context", which is copied verbatim from New(ctx ...any) and describes New's semantics. FromContext takes a context.Context and returns a logger enriched with the log attributes previously stored in that context (via infra/log.WithContextualAttributes), falling back to the base logger when none are present. As written the comment misleads implementers about what the method must do.

title: LoggerMiddleware now silently depends on ContextualLoggerMiddleware running earlier in the chain
body: logRequest no longer derives pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID and uname from the request's PluginContext; those fields only appear in the "Plugin Request Completed" log if NewContextualLoggerMiddleware was registered before NewLoggerMiddleware in the middleware stack. Both constructors are exported and nothing documents or enforces this ordering, so any other wiring that uses NewLoggerMiddleware without the new middleware (tests, alternate client decorators, downstream projects) will silently emit logs missing those fields. Consider documenting the dependency on both constructors or having the logger middleware fall back to the request's PluginContext when no contextual attributes are present.

title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware has no test coverage
body: The PR adds ContextualLoggerMiddleware (instrumentContext plus the four wrapped client methods) but adds no test for it. Nothing verifies that QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics attach the endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname attributes to the context, or that the nil DataSourceInstanceSettings and nil User branches behave correctly. Since LoggerMiddleware's log output now depends entirely on these attributes (the inline logParams were removed), a regression here would silently strip fields from plugin request logs without any test failing.

title: traceID field silently dropped from the "Plugin Request Completed" log line
body: Before this PR, logRequest explicitly extracted the trace ID with tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false) and appended it as a "traceID" log field. That code is removed, and the log line now relies entirely on m.logger.FromContext(ctx), which only picks up the contextual attributes injected by the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware.instrumentContext: endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, and uname. No trace ID is added there, and neither log.WithContextualAttributes nor the infra logger's FromContext injects a trace ID automatically (the metrics middleware still calls tracing.TraceIDFromContext explicitly for exemplars, confirming it isn't automatic). The result is that the grafana-data-egress "Plugin Request Completed" log loses its traceID field, breaking log-to-trace correlation that previously existed — a behavior change not mentioned in the PR description, which presents this as a pure rename/move. If the removal isn't intentional, re-add traceID either in logRequest via tracing.TraceIDFromContext or in ContextualLoggerMiddleware's attribute list.

title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a new instance, so logs via FromContext are unobservable in tests
body: TestLogger.FromContext returns NewTestLogger() rather than the receiver f. Since LoggerMiddleware now logs exclusively through m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), any test that builds the middleware with log.NewTestLogger() and then asserts on logger.InfoLogs.Calls/Message will observe zero calls — the log entry is recorded on a throwaway instance the test cannot access, producing silently misleading results. Because TestLogger is the provided fake for the plugins log.Logger interface, FromContext should return f so that logs emitted through a derived logger are captured in the same Logs structs.

title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware and its interaction with LoggerMiddleware have no test coverage
body: The PR adds ContextualLoggerMiddleware with no test file. instrumentContext has conditional branches (DataSourceInstanceSettings nil, User nil) that are unexercised, and more importantly the central behavior change of this PR — LoggerMiddleware emitting endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname by reading context attributes set by ContextualLoggerMiddleware — is untested: metrics_middleware_test.go only asserts prometheus metrics, and nothing wires the two middlewares together to verify the resulting log fields. A wiring regression (for example, swapping the middleware order in CreateMiddlewares so the logger no longer sees the attributes, or dropping one of the attribute keys) would not be caught by any test.

title: traceID field dropped from "Plugin Request Completed" log lines
body: Before this change, LoggerMiddleware explicitly appended a "traceID" field to every "Plugin Request Completed" log line via tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false). This PR removes that code (and the tracing import) and relies entirely on contextual attributes attached by the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware — but instrumentContext in contextual_logger_middleware.go only adds endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, and uname; it never adds traceID. Nothing else in the plugin client middleware chain attaches traceID via log.WithContextualAttributes, so these log lines lose the trace ID whenever an upstream HTTP middleware hasn't already put it into the context — e.g. plugin calls originating from background services such as alerting evaluations, where the trace exists only as a span in ctx. This breaks log-to-trace correlation that previously always worked. Fix by either keeping the explicit traceID param in LoggerMiddleware or adding traceID inside instrumentContext.

title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh instance, so logs via FromContext are never recorded
body: TestLogger.FromContext ignores the receiver and returns NewTestLogger(). This matters because the production code changed in this PR (LoggerMiddleware) now logs exclusively through m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...). Any test that injects a *TestLogger and then asserts on InfoLogs/ErrorLogs/etc. of the instance it holds will see zero recorded calls — tests expecting a log will fail confusingly, and tests asserting that nothing was logged will silently false-pass even though the code under test did log. The fake should return f (or record into shared state) so that logs written through FromContext are observable by the test.

title: LoggerMiddleware now silently depends on ContextualLoggerMiddleware running earlier in the chain
body: LoggerMiddleware previously built the pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName, and dsUID log fields itself from req.PluginContext, so it was self-contained. After this change those fields only appear if ContextualLoggerMiddleware ran earlier in the middleware stack and attached them as contextual attributes. The production wiring in CreateMiddlewares happens to order them correctly, but NewLoggerMiddleware is exported and can be composed into other middleware stacks (tests, other decorator constructions); in any stack without ContextualLoggerMiddleware ahead of it, the "Plugin Request Completed" lines lose all plugin-identifying fields with no error or warning. At minimum the ordering requirement should be documented on NewLoggerMiddleware (the old InstrumentationMiddleware had such a comment, and it was removed in the rename).

title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware has no test, and no test covers the moved log fields
