Consequently none of the 21 identity providers created by this test are removed afterwards; each cleanup targets a nonexistent provider named "alias" (a silent 404). The leftover brokers remain in the shared test realm and can pollute subsequent tests that count identity providers or render the login page. Register the cleanup with the actual alias, e.g. capture final String alias = "idp-alias-" + i; and use testRealm().identityProviders().get(alias)::remove.

title: Login-cache invalidation on update is computed against the org-aware wrapped model, so updates made while the org is disabled can leave stale login entries
body: In update(), the current state of the IDP is loaded via getById(model.getInternalId()), which returns the organization-aware wrapper produced by createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel. That wrapper's isEnabled() returns false whenever the linked organization is disabled, deleted, or the OrganizationProvider is unavailable. registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate then evaluates getLoginPredicate() on this wrapped original: while the org is disabled, test(original) is always false, so the first early-return (!test(original) && !test(updated)) fires for any update that also makes the updated model fail the predicate — e.g. an admin sets hideOnLogin=true, linkOnly=true, or disables the raw IDP on a broker belonging to a disabled org. However, the .idp.login.* caches are populated from idpDelegate.getForLogin(), which only filters raw attributes (enabled, hideOnLogin, linkOnly, org-public) and does not consider org enabled state, so the raw-eligible IDP's id is still in the cached set and the needed invalidation is skipped. When the organization is later re-enabled nothing invalidates the login cache, getById resolves the stale id as enabled, and OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean — which only re-checks isEnabled() on the ORG_ONLY/ALL paths — will render a broker the admin explicitly hid from the login page. The 'original' used for the login predicate should be the unwrapped model (e.g. idpDelegate.getById(...)) so the predicate reflects raw stored attributes.

title: testCacheIDPForLogin registers cleanup for literal alias "alias", so the ~21 created identity providers are never removed
body: In testCacheIDPForLogin the cleanup registered inside the provider-creation loops uses the literal string "alias": getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) (the same statement is repeated at line 425 for idp-alias-20). No provider with alias "alias" exists, so each cleanup call targets a non-existent resource (404) and, more importantly, the idp-alias-0 … idp-alias-20 providers created by the test are never cleaned up. That leaves over twenty stray brokers — eleven of them enabled, login-visible realm-level providers — in the test realm, which can skew any later test in the class or suite that lists or counts login identity providers. Capture the actual alias in an effectively-final variable and register cleanup with testRealm().identityProviders().get(alias)::remove (note the same copy-pasted mistake already exists in testCacheIDPByOrg at line 303 and is worth fixing too).

title: Multiple crypto providers no longer fail fast; ties in order() are resolved arbitrarily
body: Before this change, detectProvider threw IllegalStateException when more than one CryptoProvider was found on the classpath. Now it silently sorts by order() descending and takes the first. All built-in providers (DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, FIPS1402Provider) use order 200, so a misconfigured classpath containing, for example, both keycloak-crypto-default and keycloak-crypto-fips1402 — previously a clear startup error — now results in an arbitrary winner (stable sort keeps ServiceLoader/classpath discovery order, which varies by environment), with the losing provider only mentioned in a debug log. Consider restoring fail-fast behavior when the highest order is shared by more than one discovered provider.

title: New abstract order() method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: CryptoProvider gains a new abstract method order(). Any existing third-party or custom CryptoProvider implementation compiled against the previous version of this interface will now fail at runtime with AbstractMethodError, because detectProvider invokes order() on every discovered provider during sorting (even when only one provider is present), and implementations fail to compile against the new interface. Declaring it as a default method (e.g. 'default int order() { return 100; }') would preserve backward compatibility while still allowing ordering.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the JDK keystore provider, not BouncyCastle
body: The CryptoProvider contract documents this method as '@return BouncyCastle security provider. Can be either non-FIPS or FIPS based provider', but this implementation returns KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider(), i.e. whatever JDK provider implements the default keystore type (typically SUN/SunJSSE), never BouncyCastle. Consequently CryptoIntegration.getProvider().getBouncyCastleProvider() (and hence BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER) yields a non-BouncyCastle provider; any consumer that passes it to a JCA getInstance(..., provider) call for BC-only algorithms will fail, with no error pointing at the real cause. If this module intentionally ships without BouncyCastle, returning null (as WildFlyElytronProvider does) or explicitly documenting the deviation would be less misleading.

title: Dead leftover encoder writes in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
body: Lines 114-115 create two ASN1Encoder instances, write rBigInteger and sBigInteger into them, and then discard the results; the actual return statement immediately below builds brand-new encoders. This has no functional effect but performs pointless allocation and DER encoding on every signature conversion and looks like leftover scaffolding from development. The two statements should be deleted.

title: Round-trip test only proves the two converters are consistent inverses of each other
body: The test asserts only that asn1derToConcatenatedRS followed by concatenatedRSToASN1DER followed by asn1derToConcatenatedRS returns the same bytes (rsConcat equals rsConcat2). Both methods could be wrong in complementary ways and the test would still pass — in the extreme, if both were identity functions the assertion holds while every ES256/384/512 signature produced or verified through them would be invalid. The test should validate against an independent reference: e.g. check rsConcat has the expected raw length and content relative to the JDK-produced DER signature, verify the re-encoded DER with java.security.Signature.verify(), or use a known test vector.

title: Creating an AuthzClient now installs the minimal provider as JVM-global CryptoIntegration state
body: AuthzClient.create(Configuration) now calls CryptoIntegration.init(...), which sets the static JVM-global cryptoProvider if it is not already set. In an application that embeds the authz client and later calls CryptoIntegration.init(...) itself (expecting to install a fully functional provider), that later init is silently a no-op, and every CryptoIntegration.getProvider() caller in the JVM receives AuthzClientCryptoProvider, which throws UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported yet.") for nearly all methods (getSignature, getPemUtils, getKeyPairGen, getX509CertFactory, ...). If this global side effect is intentional, it should be documented; otherwise consider initializing lazily only when crypto is actually needed or scoping the provider to the client.

title: New abstract method order() breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: int order() is added to the public CryptoProvider interface as an abstract method with no default. CryptoIntegration.detectProvider now invokes CryptoProvider::order on every provider discovered via ServiceLoader, so any third-party CryptoProvider implementation compiled against the previous interface will throw AbstractMethodError at runtime as soon as provider detection runs, and will fail to compile when rebuilt. keycloak-common is consumed by client applications and custom crypto integrations (e.g. custom FIPS providers) implement this interface, so this is a binary- and source-incompatible change. Make it a default method, e.g. default int order() { return 0; }, so existing implementations keep working.

title: Ties between providers with equal top order are now silently resolved by classpath order
body: detectProvider now sorts providers by order() descending and returns the first one; for providers with equal order the stable sort keeps ServiceLoader (i.e. JAR/classpath) order. Previously, having more than one CryptoProvider on the classpath was a hard IllegalStateException with a clear message. All three server providers (DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, FIPS1402Provider) return order 200, so a misconfigured classpath containing e.g. both keycloak-crypto-default and keycloak-crypto-fips1402 no longer fails fast: one is picked based on opaque JAR ordering and the deployment can silently run with the wrong (possibly non-FIPS) crypto provider, with only a DEBUG-level message listing the ignored providers. Consider failing, or at least logging at WARN level, when more than one provider shares the highest order.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the JDK default keystore provider, not BouncyCastle
body: The interface contract states this method returns the BouncyCastle security provider (FIPS or non-FIPS). This implementation returns KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider(), which is the provider backing the JVM's default keystore type (typically the SUN provider) and has nothing to do with BouncyCastle. Any caller that relies on the contract — for example code that registers the returned provider or requests BC algorithms from it via BouncyIntegration — will fail with confusing NoSuchAlgorithm/NoSuchProvider errors or silently use the wrong provider. Since nearly every other method of this class throws UnsupportedOperationException, and WildFlyElytronProvider returns null for this same method, this method should do one of those instead of returning a misleading provider.

title: Dead code: two discarded ASN1Encoder writes in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
body: Lines 114-115 call ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger) and ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger) and immediately discard the results; the actual DER sequence returned is built from two separate, freshly created encoders in the return statement. These two calls are leftover dead code that serve no purpose and can confuse readers of signature-conversion code; they should be removed.

title: New abstract method order() on CryptoProvider breaks existing implementations
body: The PR adds `int order();` as a new abstract method to the public `CryptoProvider` interface. keycloak-common is a published artifact and `CryptoProvider` is a ServiceLoader-loaded SPI that can be implemented outside this repository. Any existing compiled implementation used with the newer keycloak-common will fail at runtime with `AbstractMethodError` as soon as `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider()` sorts via `CryptoProvider::order`, and any source implementation stops compiling until it implements the method. Declaring it as a default method (e.g. `default int order() { return 0; }`) would provide the new ordering capability without breaking API/binary compatibility in a shared module.

title: Same-order crypto providers are now silently picked by classpath order instead of failing fast
body: detectProvider() previously threw IllegalStateException("Multiple crypto providers loaded... Make sure only one cryptoProvider available on the classpath") whenever more than one CryptoProvider was found. Now it sorts by order() and unconditionally takes the first entry. Because DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return order 200, a misconfigured classpath containing two of them — exactly the situation the old exception guarded against — no longer fails: one provider is silently chosen based on ServiceLoader/classpath ordering, which can vary between environments, and the only trace is a debug-level "Ignored crypto providers" message. In the worst case a deployment intended to run with the FIPS 140-2 provider boots with the default non-FIPS provider without anyone noticing. Consider keeping a hard failure, or at least logging a warning, when the highest order is shared by more than one provider.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the default keystore's JCA provider instead of a BouncyCastle provider
body: The CryptoProvider contract documents this method as returning the "BouncyCastle security provider" (non-FIPS or FIPS). This implementation returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, i.e. whatever provider backs the JVM's default keystore type (typically SUN), which is not BouncyCastle and varies with JDK configuration. The value is exposed via BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER, which other Keycloak code uses as the provider name for JCA getInstance(algorithm, provider) lookups and which CryptoIntegration.init() logs as the "java security provider", so with this provider active those lookups resolve against an arbitrary default provider rather than the documented one. Each call also instantiates a KeyStore just to obtain a Provider. If no BouncyCastle is available, returning null (as WildFlyElytronProvider does) or documenting the deviation would be more correct.

title: Dead code: two discarded ASN1Encoder instances in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
body: Lines 114-115 create two ASN1Encoder objects and write rBigInteger/sBigInteger into them, but the results are never used — the returned DER sequence is built from fresh encoders in the return statement (lines 117-121). The two statements have no effect other than allocating throwaway objects and performing pointless serialization on every ES256/384/512 signature conversion, and they confuse readers about which encoders actually produce the output. They should be removed.

title: New test bypasses the ServiceLoader/order mechanism that is the point of the PR
body: The functional core of this PR is that AuthzClientCryptoProvider is registered via META-INF/services/org.keycloak.common.crypto.CryptoProvider and is selected by CryptoIntegration only when no higher-order provider is present (DefaultCryptoProvider et al. use order 200, this one 100). The added test instantiates `new AuthzClientCryptoProvider()` directly, so a broken or missing service registration file, or an order() value that wins/loses incorrectly against DefaultCryptoProvider, would not be caught by anything. A test that loads providers through ServiceLoader/CryptoIntegration — e.g. asserting AuthzClientCryptoProvider is discoverable on its own and that DefaultCryptoProvider still wins when both are on the classpath — would cover the mechanism the PR actually introduces.

title: No upgrade path adds the Clients resource type and its scopes to already-initialized admin-permissions resource servers
body: init() bootstraps the admin-permissions resource server (all schema scopes plus one 'all' resource per resource type) only when the realm's admin permissions client is first created; it returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null. Realms that already enabled fine-grained admin permissions v2 before this change have a resource server containing only the Users scopes (manage, view, impersonate, map-roles, manage-group-membership) and no 'Clients' resource, and nothing in this PR ever updates them. On such realms: creating a Clients permission fails (getOrCreateResource throws ModelException("No scopes found.") because scopeStore.findByName returns null for the new scopes configure/map-roles-client-scope/map-roles-composite, and getScope rejects them as not existing); all-clients evaluation in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(String) always returns false because findByName(server, "Clients") returns null; and per-client evaluation can hit a NullPointerException in ClientPermissionsV2's fallback. A migration/upgrade step that adds the missing scopes and the Clients all-resource to existing admin-permissions resource servers is needed, otherwise the new feature is broken (with 500s) for every realm that adopted v2 earlier.

title: Missing null check on the 'Clients' all-resource leads to NullPointerException in per-client permission checks
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no client-specific resource exists, the code falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and immediately calls authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) without checking the result. getResourceTypeResource can return null — it does so whenever the 'Clients' resource is absent from the resource server (e.g., realms whose admin permissions client was initialized before the Clients type was added to the schema, since init() never runs again for them) or when supportsAuthorizationSchema is false. findByResource then dereferences resource.getId() and throws a NullPointerException, so every per-client permission check (canView/canManage/canConfigure/canMapRoles for a specific client) performed by a delegated admin returns a 500 instead of denying or granting access. Guard the null (return false) and/or ensure the resource is created on upgrade.

title: Deleting a client fails when both ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ and ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 are enabled
body: The removal listener added here is guarded by Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) (v1), but AdminPermissions.management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever the v2 feature flag is on, and MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() now returns ClientPermissionsV2. If an operator enables both the v1 and v2 features, handling ClientRemovedEvent calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which resolves to ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled — a method that unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). Provider event listener exceptions propagate, so every client deletion in the realm fails with an error and the transaction rolls back. The guard needs to select the cleanup path based on which evaluator is actually active (or ClientPermissionsV2 must implement a no-op/real cleanup) instead of only checking the v1 flag.

title: No cleanup of FGAP v2 client resources and permissions when a client is deleted
body: setPermissionsEnabled here throws UnsupportedOperationException, and the AdminPermissions.registerListener cleanup hook that used to invoke it on ClientRemovedEvent is now skipped whenever the v1 feature flag is off — i.e., in the standard v2-only setup. As a result, deleting a client that has fine-grained permissions leaves the resource created for it in the admin-permissions resource server (named by the client's internal id, created via AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource when a permission targets that client) and all permissions referencing it orphaned. These stale entries remain visible in permission listings and are still returned by getClientsWithPermission, so callers that resolve the returned names via session.clients().getClientById get nulls for deleted clients. A v2 cleanup path for client removal (deleting the resource and its referencing permissions) is missing.

title: getResourceName not extended for the Clients resource type
body: getResourceName resolves friendly resource names only for the Users type (returning the username, or "All users" for the all-resource). Resources of the newly added Clients type fall through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is never set for resources created by getOrCreateResource, so REST/admin-console representations of client permissions will render an empty or null name instead of the client's clientId, and the 'Clients' all-resource gets no equivalent of the "All users" label. Mirror the Users branch for CLIENTS: return "All clients" for the all-resource and resolve the client via session.clients().getClientById(realm, resource.getName()) to return its clientId.

title: Deleting any client throws UnsupportedOperationException when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled
body: AdminPermissions.registerListener (AdminPermissions.java:90-91) handles every ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent by calling management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). With the v2 feature on, management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, whose new clients() override now returns ClientPermissionsV2, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). The new guard added to the listener checks Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (v1), which is also enabled whenever v2 is enabled (v2 presupposes v1), so it does not protect this path. Provider events are published synchronously inside the transaction, so the exception propagates out of the client-removal call, rolls back the transaction and returns a 500 — deleting a client (and any realm teardown that removes clients) is broken under v2. Before this PR the event was dispatched to the v1 ClientPermissions implementation, which successfully removed the client's v2 authorization resources (they live on the same admin-permissions resource server, named by client id), so this is a regression introduced by the clients() override. Either implement the disable/cleanup path in ClientPermissionsV2 or skip this event for v2 in the listener. None of the added tests exercise deleting a client with v2 enabled, which is why this is not caught.

title: canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles drop the manage/admin-role fallback, denying legitimate admins
body: The v1 ClientPermissions implementations of canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles and canMapClientScopeRoles all start with `if (canManage(client)) return true;`, i.e. a caller with the manage-clients admin role (or manage permission on the client) may map roles. UserPermissionsV2.canMapRoles keeps the same fallback (this PR's own testTransitiveUserPermissions asserts that all-users MANAGE implies map-roles for users). The new ClientPermissionsV2 overrides (lines 91-103) only evaluate the FGAP MAP_ROLES / MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE / MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE permissions. Consequence: as soon as the v2 feature flag is enabled, a realm admin holding the manage-clients role but no FGAP policies gets 403 from RoleMapperResource.addClientRoleMapping, addComposites, etc. — in every realm, including realms that never opted into admin permissions, because hasPermission() returns false when the realm has no admin-permissions resource server (root.realmResourceServer() == null). Note that AdminPermissions.evaluator() selects MgmtPermissionsV2 based on the profile flag alone, not on realm opt-in. Add `if (canManage(client)) return true;` to the three methods for parity with v1 and with users v2.

title: No upgrade path seeds the Clients resource type/scopes into existing admin-permissions resource servers; permission checks then NPE
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null, and this PR adds no migration, so realms that already enabled fine-grained admin permissions v2 before this change (their resource server contains only the Users type and the original scopes) never receive the "Clients" all-resource or the new scopes configure, map-roles-client-scope and map-roles-composite. Two concrete failures follow. (a) In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no client-specific resource exists, getResourceTypeResource(...) returns null in such realms and the null is passed straight into policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) at line 219, causing a NullPointerException → 500 on routine client admin operations for any caller without the manage-clients role. (b) Creating a Clients-typed permission fails because getOrCreateResource cannot resolve the missing scopes and throws ModelException("No scopes found."). A null guard is needed here, and an upgrade/migration step must add the new resource type and scopes to pre-existing admin-permissions resource servers.

title: getClientsWithPermission queries resources by type, but per-client resources are created without a type
body: ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission iterates resourceStore.findByType(server, "Clients", ...), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources via resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, owner) and only updates their scopes — it never sets the resource type. Only the all-resource entries receive a type (init() calls resource.setType(type)). As a result findByType never matches any per-client resource; the method can only ever return an empty set or the literal "Clients" all-resource name (a string that is not a client id), never the ids of the clients the caller actually holds the requested scope on. Any consumer that filters a client list using this set will silently get wrong results. Set the resource type in getOrCreateResource (which would also fix the same latent gap for Users) or look the resources up differently.

title: getResourceName has no branch for the Clients resource type
body: getResourceName resolves Users resources to the user's username and labels the all-users resource "All users", but nothing handles the new Clients type. Permission representations for client resources therefore fall through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is never populated for resources created by getOrCreateResource, so the admin API/console shows a null/empty name (or the raw internal client UUID) instead of the clientId, and the all-clients resource gets no friendly label analogous to "All users". Add a Clients branch that resolves ClientModel.getClientId() and an "All clients" label for the type resource.

title: Javadoc for requireView()/requireViewClientScopes() describes return values of void methods; v2 notes misdescribe the fallback
body: The newly added javadoc for the void methods requireView() (line 96) and requireViewClientScopes() (line 101) says "Returns true if canView()/canViewClientScopes() returns true" — copied from the can* methods; these methods return nothing and throw ForbiddenException when the check fails. In addition, the repeated "For V2 only: Also if the caller has a permission to <scope> for all clients" notes are inaccurate: the v2 implementation checks the specific client's resource first and only falls back to the all-clients resource when no client-specific resource exists, so a client-specific grant (not just an all-clients grant) also satisfies the check. The documentation should describe the actual contract for implementers of this interface.

title: UnsupportedOperationException in setPermissionsEnabled/isPermissionsEnabled breaks client deletion and the client management-permissions endpoint
body: ClientPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException from setPermissionsEnabled (line 193), isPermissionsEnabled (line 188), getPermissions, resource(), etc. These methods are reachable in normal operation: (1) AdminPermissions.registerListener handles ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent by calling management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). This PR makes MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() return ClientPermissionsV2, and the newly added Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) guard passes when V2 is enabled (the V2 feature pulls in V1), so every client removal on a server with the V2 feature enabled throws from the synchronous provider-event listener, rolling back the transaction — deleting a client fails with a 500 (and realm deletion, which removes all its clients, fails too). (2) The admin REST endpoint GET/PUT /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id}/management/permissions calls isPermissionsEnabled/getPermissions/setPermissionsEnabled (ClientResource's ManagementPermissionReference handling), so it now returns 500, breaking the admin console's client permissions handling under V2. Either implement these methods for V2 (e.g., on removal, clean up the client's FGAP resource and its policies) or make the listener and endpoints skip them gracefully. There is no test covering client deletion with the V2 feature enabled.

title: canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles lost the canManage(client) fallback, blocking manage-clients admins
body: In V1 ClientPermissions these methods are implemented as 'if (canManage(client)) return true; return hasPermission(...)'. The new V2 overrides only call hasPermission(client, MAP_ROLES / MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE / MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE) and drop the canManage short-circuit. Because AdminPermissions.evaluator returns MgmtPermissionsV2 for every realm when the V2 profile feature is enabled, an administrator holding the realm 'manage-clients' role — who can currently map client roles — will get 403 from the role-mapping endpoints (RoleMapperResource checks canMapRoles etc.) unless an explicit FGAP map-roles permission exists. It also breaks the intended transitivity that a MANAGE permission implies map-roles, which Users V2 explicitly supports (UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.testTransitiveUserPermissions asserts role mapping works with only the manage scope; note canView(ClientScopeModel) in this same file does include MANAGE). The three overrides should include canManage(client) (or include the MANAGE scope in the evaluated scopes, as the Users V2 implementation does via varargs).

title: Possible NPE when the 'Clients' resource-type resource is missing
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), when no per-client resource exists, the code does resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and immediately calls authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) without a null check. getResourceTypeResource returns null when the schema is not supported for the realm (e.g., admin permissions disabled on the realm while the admin-permissions client still exists) and when the 'Clients' resource simply does not exist — which is the case for realms that enabled admin permissions before this change, because init() early-returns when the client already exists. The result is a NullPointerException and a 500 on ordinary admin operations such as viewing or updating a client for any caller without the manage-clients role. The sibling method hasPermission(String) correctly returns false when the resource is null; this path should do the same.

title: getClientsWithPermission queries findByType("Clients") but per-client resources are created without a type
body: getClientsWithPermission iterates resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) to find per-client resources. However, per-client resources are created in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource via resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, owner) and setType is never called on them — only the all-type resources created in init() get a type (and removeOrphanResources discriminates per-object resources by name rather than type precisely because their type is unset). Since findByType matches on the resource's type column, per-client resources are never returned here: callers holding only per-client permissions get an empty set from partial client listing, and if the all-type resource matches, its name — the literal string "Clients", which is not a client id — is added to the returned set. Either set the resource type when creating per-client resources (V1 ClientPermissions.resource() sets type "kc.client.resource") or resolve per-client resource names from the permissions/policies the way the Users V2 flow does.

title: No upgrade path: realms that already enabled admin permissions never receive the new Clients scopes and resource
body: init() creates the schema scopes and the all-type resources only when the admin-permissions client does not exist yet, and returns immediately if it does. Realms that enabled admin permissions (V2) before this change already have that client, so they never get the new scopes (configure, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite) or the "Clients" resource-type resource. In such realms, creating a Clients permission fails in getOrCreateResource with ModelException("No scopes found.") when it looks up the missing scopes, and permission evaluation falls into the getResourceTypeResource() == null path in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission. A migration or repair step that adds newly introduced scopes and resource-type resources to existing admin-permissions resource servers is needed.

title: getResourceName has no Clients branch and returns null display names for Clients resources
body: getResourceName only resolves display names for the Users resource type and otherwise falls through to resource.getDisplayName(). Resources created for the admin-permissions schema (the all-type "Clients" resource and per-client resources) never have a display name set, so permission/resource representations for Clients resources come back with null names, and there is no "All clients" equivalent of the existing "All users" label. Add a CLIENTS branch that resolves the client (e.g., returning its clientId) for per-client resources and "All clients" for the type resource.

title: New and changed exit codes (3 and 4) are never asserted
body: This PR makes the exit code the documented, stable contract of the update-compatibility tool (the guide explicitly tells users to rely only on exit codes for automation), changes the recreate exit code from 4 to 3 in CompatibilityResult, and introduces a new exit code 4 for 'feature disabled' — but no test asserts any of these codes. testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the error message and never checks that the process exits with code 4; testWrongVersions never asserts exit code 3 for the recreate outcome; testCompatible asserts exit code 0 only for the metadata command, not for the subsequent check command; and the feature-disabled path of the check subcommand is not exercised at all. This contract was already wrong once (RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE returned 4 while the docs said 3), so a wiring mistake in picocli.exit(...) or a wrong constant would again ship undetected: CI would stay green while user automation and the operator, both of which consume these exit codes, would break.

title: CAUTION overstates when the rolling-updates feature must be enabled
body: The new CAUTION says: "While on preview stage, the feature `rolling-updates` must be enabled. Otherwise, the Keycloak Operator will fail." Read literally this tells every reader that any deployment without the preview feature will break, but that is only true when an explicit update strategy is configured. With the default (unset) `spec.update.strategy` the Operator mimics 26.1 behavior and never invokes the update-compatibility command, so it works fine without the feature — this PR's own UpgradeTest demonstrates it: `createInitialDeployment` returns early for the null strategy without enabling `rolling-updates`, and `testCacheMaxCount(null)` still expects a successful rolling-upgrade status. The statement should be scoped (e.g., "must be enabled when configuring `spec.update.strategy`"), otherwise users on the default strategy may wrongly conclude they must enable a preview feature to keep the Operator working.

title: New and changed update-compatibility exit codes are never asserted
body: This PR introduces a new exit code (FEATURE_DISABLED = 4, returned when `rolling-updates` is not enabled) and changes the recreate exit code from 4 to 3 in CompatibilityResult, and the update-compatibility guide explicitly tells users to build automation around these exit codes rather than log output. However, no test verifies them: `testFeatureNotEnabled` only asserts the stderr message (line 49) and never checks that the process exits with code 4, and `testWrongVersions`/`testCompatible` assert messages but never assert exit code 3 (recreate required) or 0 (rolling possible) for the `check` command. A future regression that swaps or drops these exit codes — the tool's documented scripting contract — would pass the test suite unnoticed. Please add exitCode assertions to these tests.

title: Exit code 4 silently repurposed from 'recreate upgrade required' to 'feature disabled'
body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was changed from 4 to 3, and 4 now means FEATURE_DISABLED. The update-compatibility tool is explicitly documented as 'fully scriptable' and its exit codes are the supported contract for CI/CD pipelines. Any automation written against the previous preview that branches on exit code 4 to decide that a recreate upgrade is required will now misinterpret that case: a 'recreate required' result returns 3 (which such a script would treat as an unknown error), and a 'feature disabled' result returns 4 (which it would treat as 'recreate required', potentially triggering an unnecessary full shutdown and downtime). The docs table is updated in this PR, but existing scripts get no warning. If this renumbering is intentional, it should at least be called out in the release notes/upgrading guide so adopters of the preview can update their pipelines.

title: Feature-disabled path tested only for 'metadata' and documented exit code 4 never asserted
body: The new testFeatureNotEnabled only launches 'update-compatibility metadata' and asserts only the stderr message. The check subcommand's feature-disabled branch (UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run) has no coverage, and neither test asserts the exit code, even though the documentation added in this PR advertises exit code 4 ('The feature rolling-updates is disabled') as part of the scripting contract. A regression where picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED) returns the wrong code (e.g., 0 or 1) would silently break the automation contract this PR documents. Add a feature-disabled test for 'check' and assert exitCode() == 4 in both tests.

title: Caution overstates requirement: operator only fails when an update strategy is configured without the feature
body: The new CAUTION states 'the feature rolling-updates must be enabled. Otherwise, the Keycloak Operator will fail.' as a blanket statement. The PR's own UpgradeTest demonstrates otherwise: createInitialDeployment returns early without enabling the feature when no update strategy is set (updateStrategy == null), and that deployment is expected to become ready and to handle an image change with the default recreate behavior. The feature is only required when spec.update.strategy is configured on the Keycloak CR. As written, users who never set an update strategy will be told they must enable a preview feature to keep the Operator from failing, which is not true. Reword to scope the requirement, e.g. 'When spec.update.strategy is configured, the preview feature rolling-updates must be enabled; otherwise the Operator will fail to process the update.'

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission collects authz resource IDs instead of group IDs and never evaluates per-group permissions
body: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission (lines 121-125) the findByType callback calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) and adds groupResource.getId() to the granted set. Both are wrong. hasPermission looks resources up by *name* (resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)), and for the Groups resource type each resource is named with the group's ID (see AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup/getOrCreateResource), so passing the authz resource ID never matches and every check silently falls back to the 'all-groups' resource — the per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions this method is meant to collect are never actually evaluated. Additionally, the returned set is documented and consumed as group IDs: UsersResource and BruteForceUsersResource put it into the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute and UsersResource.getUsersCount passes it to session.users().getUsersCount(realm, ..., groupIds), all of which compare against real group IDs, so an authz resource ID matches no group. Consequences: (a) an admin with an all-groups view-members/manage-members permission gets a non-empty set containing a bogus ID, so user search returns zero users even though they can view members of every group; (b) an admin with only per-group view-members permissions gets an empty set, so no DB-level group restriction is applied — users/count returns the count of ALL users instead of only visible ones, and user-search pagination is applied at the database before permission filtering. The method should evaluate the resource it already has (as V1 GroupPermissions does) and collect groupResource.getName(), which holds the group ID.

title: canManage() returns true for view-only permission, allowing group creation
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE), i.e. it is satisfied by the 'view' scope on the Groups resource type. canManage()/requireManage() is what guards GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup (POST /admin/realms/{realm}/groups), so an admin who was granted only view permission on groups can create top-level groups — a privilege escalation. It is also inconsistent with canManage(GroupModel) in the same class (MANAGE scope only), with UserPermissionsV2.canManage() (MANAGE only), and it inverts the scope hierarchy used everywhere else in this code (MANAGE implies VIEW, not the reverse). The javadoc added to GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage() documents the same incorrect contract ('permission to VIEW or MANAGE groups'). Only the MANAGE scope should satisfy canManage().

title: No upgrade path for existing admin-permissions clients: missing 'Groups' resource/scopes cause NPE and 500s
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init() creates the scopes and the per-type 'all resources' resources only when the realm has no admin-permissions client yet (it returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null), and nothing in this PR backfills the new 'Groups' resource or the manage-membership/manage-members/view-members scopes for realms that already enabled admin permissions (ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2) before this change. For such realms every V2 group permission check fails: GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission (lines 144-147) falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, "Groups"), which returns null because that resource was never created, and the next line calls policyStore.findByResource(server, null), throwing a NullPointerException — turning all group admin endpoints into 500s. Likewise AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource throws ModelException("No scopes found.") when a group permission is created, because the new scopes do not exist in the store. A migration/initialization path that adds the new scopes and the 'Groups' type resource to existing admin-permissions clients (plus a null guard before findByResource) is needed.

title: Tests never exercise the DB-level group filter or users/count for group-scoped admins
body: The new GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest never exercises the database-level group filter that UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource install via the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute populated from auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(). In the tested scenarios (per-group VIEW_MEMBERS / MANAGE_MEMBERS) that set comes back empty, so searchForUserStream runs unfiltered and the assertions pass only because of the in-memory usersEvaluator::canView post-filter — which is why the resource-ID bug in GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission slips through. There is also no test of users/count for a group-scoped admin (currently returns the count of all users) and no test of user search for an admin holding an all-groups view-members/manage-members permission (currently returns zero users). Adding tests for filtered counts and for the all-groups member-visibility scenario would catch this regression.

title: canManage() returns true for admins holding only the 'view' scope on the Groups resource type
body: In the no-arg canManage(), the fallback calls hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE), so a delegated admin who was granted a scope permission with only the 'view' scope on the all-groups resource passes this check. canManage()/requireManage() is what guards group creation in GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup (POST /admin/realms/{realm}/groups), so a view-only groups admin can create top-level groups. The sibling method canManage(GroupModel) correctly checks only the MANAGE scope. The new tests never assert that a view-only grantee is forbidden from creating groups. Remove VIEW from the scope list in canManage() (the GroupPermissionEvaluator javadoc for canManage() mirrors the same wrong VIEW-or-MANAGE text and should be corrected too).

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() evaluates and returns Resource.getId() instead of the group id (resource name)
body: In the V2 schema, per-group authorization resources are stored with the group id as the resource *name* (AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource -> resolveGroup returns group.getId()). The callback passes groupResource.getId() (the Resource entity UUID) to hasPermission, which looks it up with resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId) — that never matches, so evaluation silently falls back to the all-groups resource instead of each group's own resource, and per-group view-members/manage-members permissions are never detected. It then adds groupResource.getId() (again the wrong UUID) into the granted set; callers put this set into the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute (UsersResource.searchForUser, BruteForceUsersResource) and into getUsersCount, which filter by group ids. Consequences: (a) for per-group grants the DB-level group restriction is never applied, so user searches run unfiltered with pagination applied before the canView post-filter (wrong pages, wrong counts); (b) when an admin has view-members on ALL groups, the all-groups resource (name 'Groups', not a group id) matches the iteration and its resource UUID is added as a bogus group id, so user search returns nothing and count returns 0 for an admin who should see everyone. Use groupResource.getName() in both the hasPermission call and granted.add, and skip the resource whose name equals the type name.

title: Per-group resources created by getOrCreateResource have no type set, so findByType("Groups") never returns them
body: getOrCreateResource creates the per-group resource via resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId()) and updates its scopes, but never calls setType (compare V1 GroupPermissions.initialize, which explicitly calls groupResource.setType("Group")). GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission enumerates group resources with resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...); since resources created here have a null type, they are never enumerated — only the 'Groups' all-resource (whose type is set in init()) matches. Even after fixing the id/name confusion in getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, per-group view permissions would still be invisible to it. The same gap exists for per-user/per-client resources created through this method, but it only becomes observable with the new Groups findByType usage.

title: Group removal event now hits UnsupportedOperationException in V2, breaking group deletion or leaking orphaned authorization data
body: AdminPermissions.registerListener handles GroupModel.GroupRemovedEvent by calling management(session, realm).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false) whenever the admin-fine-grained-authz (v1) feature is enabled. Before this PR, MgmtPermissionsV2 inherited groups() from MgmtPermissions and returned the v1 GroupPermissions, whose setPermissionsEnabled was a harmless no-op against a v2 realm; now MgmtPermissionsV2.groups() returns GroupPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException. As a result, deleting any group fails with a server error (the exception propagates out of realm.removeGroup) when both admin-fine-grained-authz and admin-fine-grained-authz-v2 are enabled. Conversely, with only v2 enabled the listener is not registered at all (registration is gated on the v1 feature), so a deleted group's authorization resource and all scope permissions referencing it are left orphaned in the store. V2 needs a real cleanup implementation for group removal (and the v1-only management/permissions endpoint should degrade gracefully instead of throwing).

title: No migration path: realms that already enabled admin permissions never get the 'Groups' resource and the three new scopes
body: The 'Groups' resource-type resource and the manage-membership/manage-members/view-members scopes are only created in AdminPermissionsSchema.init(), which returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null. Realms that enabled admin permissions (FGAP v2 preview) before this change keep their existing admin-permissions client untouched, so the new schema objects are never created. Consequences: (a) creating a group permission fails in getOrCreateResource, where scope lookup by name misses and throws ModelException("No scopes found."); (b) GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission's fallback calls AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...), which returns null when the 'Groups' resource is absent, and then calls policyStore.findByResource(server, null), producing a server error on group admin endpoints for delegated admins. An update mechanism is needed that syncs schema scopes and resource-type resources for pre-existing admin-permissions clients.

title: getResourceName() has no handling for the Groups resource type
body: getResourceName is the mechanism that translates per-object authorization resources into human-readable names for display (for Users it returns "All users" for the type resource and the username otherwise). For Groups resources — whose resource name is the group's UUID — it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is null for resources created via getOrCreateResource, so group permissions will be displayed with a blank or raw UUID identifier in the admin console. It should resolve the group analogously to the Users branch ("All groups" for the type resource, group name otherwise).

title: Javadoc for requireManageMembers references the wrong check method
body: The newly added javadoc for requireManageMembers(GroupModel) says "Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canManageMembership(GroupModel)} returns false" — it should reference canManageMembers(GroupModel). Additionally, the javadoc for getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() says "@return Stream of IDs of groups with view permission" although the method returns a Set. Since these docs describe authorization checks, the wrong references are misleading to implementers.

title: canManage() grants manage rights to admins holding only the 'view' scope on groups
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() evaluates hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE), and hasPermission returns true when ANY of the listed scopes is granted. canManage()/requireManage() is the guard for GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup (POST /admin/realms/{realm}/groups), so an administrator who was granted only the 'view' scope on the Groups resource type (no manage-users role, no manage scope) can create arbitrary top-level groups. The per-group counterpart canManage(GroupModel) in the same class correctly checks only MANAGE, and the Users V2 equivalent only checks the manage scope, so including VIEW here is a privilege escalation, not intended semantics. The new javadoc on GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage() also documents the wrong behavior. The VIEW scope should be removed from this check.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses resource type/id incorrectly and returns wrong identifiers
body: This method is broken in three compounding ways. (1) It iterates resourceStore.findByType(server, "Groups", ...), but per-group resources created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource never have resource.setType() called (only the all-groups resource created in AdminPermissionsSchema.init() has a type), so specific group resources are never visited. (2) Inside the loop it calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...), but hasPermission looks resources up by NAME via resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId), so passing the resource UUID never finds the resource and the check silently falls back to the all-groups resource for every entry. (3) It adds groupResource.getId() (the authz resource UUID) to the result, while all callers (UsersResource.searchForUser, UsersResource.getUsersCount, BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser) need actual group IDs to restrict the user query via the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute. Consequences: an admin whose only access is view-members/manage-members on specific groups gets an empty set, so the DB-level group filter is never applied and /users/count returns 0 while pagination is computed on unfiltered results; and an admin granted view-members on the all-groups resource gets a set containing a non-existent 'group id' (the resource UUID), so the user search is restricted to a group that doesn't exist and returns zero users.

title: setPermissionsEnabled() throws UnsupportedOperationException but is still invoked by the GroupRemovedEvent listener
body: Because MgmtPermissionsV2.groups() now returns GroupPermissionsV2, any caller of the GroupPermissionManagement methods hits UnsupportedOperationException. One such caller runs on the normal group-deletion path: AdminPermissions.registerListener registers a ProviderEventListener whenever Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled (enabling the V2 feature also enables V1), and on every GroupModel.GroupRemovedEvent it calls management(session, realm).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false). With V2 enabled that call now throws, so deleting a group (DELETE /admin/realms/{realm}/groups/{id}, which fires GroupRemovedEvent synchronously via realm.removeGroup) fails with a 500 instead of completing. The same problem affects GroupResource's management/permissions endpoints, which call permissions.groups().isPermissionsEnabled(group)/setPermissionsEnabled(...) after ProfileHelper.requireFeature(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) — that check passes under V2, so those endpoints also 500. The V2 overrides should no-op (as the V1 implementation effectively does when no V1 resources exist) rather than throw.

title: Null 'Groups' type resource is dereferenced; no upgrade path creates it for realms that already enabled admin permissions
body: In hasPermission(), when no per-group resource exists, the code falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, "Groups") and immediately calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).getId() semantics — getResourceTypeResource returns null when the resource server has no resource named "Groups", and findByResource(server, null) NPEs inside the store, producing a 500 on any group admin endpoint (group list, view, manage checks). This state is reachable for any realm that enabled admin permissions (realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null) before this change was deployed: AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns immediately when the client already exists, and nothing in this PR migrates existing resource servers to add the new "Groups" resource or the manage-members/view-members/manage-membership scopes. Those realms also cannot create group permissions, since getScope() validation fails for the missing scopes. A null guard plus an upgrade/initialization path for existing resource servers is needed.

The previous value was a proper Lithuanian translation containing <a> links; while removing the links was needed for the sanitizer, the replacement text was apparently copied from the wrong language file. Lithuanian users setting up an authenticator app will now be shown Italian instructions. It should be a Lithuanian rendering of "Install one of the following applications on your mobile:".

body: The new value of loginTotpStep1 in the Lithuanian (lt) login bundle is "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:" which is Italian, not Lithuanian (it matches the Italian translation, likely copied from messages_it.properties). The surrounding entries (loginTotpStep2, loginTotpStep3) are Lithuanian, so users on the OTP setup page will see one step in Italian. It should be a Lithuanian rendering of "Install one of the following applications on your mobile:".

It looks like the line was copied from messages_zh_TW.properties. Simplified Chinese users will see mixed-script text on the authenticator setup page; the line should be rewritten in Simplified Chinese.

title: JS console bundles switched from i18next {{0}} to Java MessageFormat {0}/{2,choice,...} syntax
body: The keycloak.v3 account console and keycloak.v2 admin console localize server error keys in the browser with i18next, whose interpolation syntax is {{0}} — every sibling error key in this file uses it (e.g. error-username-invalid-character='{{0}}' contains invalid character., error-empty=Please specify value of '{{0}}'). This change switches error-invalid-multivalued-size to Java MessageFormat syntax ({0}/{1}/{2} plus a {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values} pattern) which i18next cannot evaluate. When multivalued-attribute size validation fails, these consoles will render the raw text "Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}." to end users instead of a formatted message. The identical change was made in js/apps/admin-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v2/admin/messages/messages_en.properties and has the same problem. The Java MessageFormat wording is correct for the server-rendered bundles (themes/src/main/resources/...), but the JS bundles should keep the previous {{0}} … value(s). wording, which the new verifier also accepts.

title: Diff-snippet computation can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of reporting the violation
body: In the "Illegal HTML" reporting branch, start (common prefix length) and end (common suffix length) are computed independently, so they can overlap: when the sanitizer output contains the entire input as a prefix and also shares its tail (e.g. input value "" that the sanitizer normalizes to "" yields start=3 and end=2), then value.substring(start, value.length() - end) is invoked with begin (3) > end (1) and throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. Instead of the intended "Illegal HTML in key …" message, the verification aborts with an unhandled exception and a bare stack trace, and no further keys/files are checked. Clamp the values so start + end never exceeds the string length for both strings, e.g. end = Math.min(end, value.length() - start) and end = Math.min(end, sanitized.length() - start).

title: Lithuanian totpStep1 replaced with Italian text
body: The PR replaces the Lithuanian translation of `totpStep1` (which previously contained HTML anchors and therefore failed the new HTML verification) with the sentence "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:". That sentence is Italian, not Lithuanian — it was apparently copied from the wrong locale's message file. Users running the account console with the Lithuanian locale will see Italian instructions on the multi-factor authentication setup page. It should be a Lithuanian rendering of the English source "Install one of the following applications on your mobile:".

title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 replaced with Italian text
body: Same defect as in the account theme: the Lithuanian `loginTotpStep1` value was replaced with "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:", which is Italian, not Lithuanian. Users with the Lithuanian locale will see Italian instructions on the OTP setup page of the login flow. It should be a Lithuanian translation of the English source "Install one of the following applications on your mobile:".

title: Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) file now contains Traditional Chinese text
body: The new value of `totpStep1` in the zh_CN (Simplified Chinese) account bundle is "在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：", which is written in Traditional Chinese characters (手機/安裝/應用程式 instead of 手机/安装/应用程序). The rest of the file, and the zh_CN locale generally, uses Simplified Chinese — compare the neighboring lines such as `totpStep2=打开应用扫描二维码输入验证码`. The string looks like it was pasted from a Traditional Chinese (zh_TW) source; it should use Simplified characters for consistency with the locale.

title: Anchor-mismatch error message does not say which key or file is affected
body: When a translation contains an anchor tag that does not match the English source, `santizeAnchors` records the message `Didn't find anchor tag <a ...> in original string` with no message key and no file path — even though the `key` parameter is passed to the method and `file` is available as a field. Every other diagnostic produced by this class (duplicate keys, illegal HTML) includes the file and the key. When the plugin scans the entire themes tree, this message gives maintainers no way to locate the offending entry without grepping all message bundles for the anchor text. Include `key` and `file` in the message.

title: Anchor check enforces identical anchor order, not just identical anchors
body: `santizeAnchors` walks the anchors of the translation and of the English value with two independent matchers and requires them to be equal pair-by-pair in sequence (`Objects.equals(matcher.group(), englishMatcher.group())`). This enforces that anchors appear in the same ORDER as in the English source, not merely that the same set of anchors is present. A legitimate translation that reorders two links because the target language has different word order will fail verification with "Didn't find anchor tag", blocking valid translations. Consider matching anchors as a multiset (e.g., remove each matched anchor from a list of English anchors) instead of pairwise by position.

title: Italian text inserted into the Lithuanian account messages (totpStep1)
body: The change to `totpStep1` replaced the old Lithuanian sentence (which contained outdated anchor links) with "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:" — that is Italian, not Lithuanian. Lithuanian users will now see an Italian sentence on the OTP setup page of the account console. The correct replacement should be a Lithuanian translation of the current English source ("Install one of the following applications on your mobile:"), as was done correctly for the fi, sk, sv and no bundles in this same PR.

title: Italian text inserted into the Lithuanian login messages (loginTotpStep1)
body: `loginTotpStep1` was changed from a Lithuanian sentence to "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:", which is Italian. Lithuanian users will see Italian text in the mobile authenticator setup step of the login flow. This should be a Lithuanian translation of the English source "Install one of the following applications on your mobile:" (compare with the correct Slovak, Swedish, Finnish and Norwegian replacements made in this PR).

title: Traditional Chinese text introduced into the Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) account bundle
body: The new value `totpStep1=在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：` uses Traditional Chinese characters (手機, 應用程式) in the Simplified Chinese `zh_CN` bundle. The rest of this file (and the zh_CN login bundle, which uses 在您的移动设备中安装以下任意一个应用) is Simplified Chinese, so users get an inconsistent script variant. It should read e.g. "在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：".

title: error-invalid-multivalued-size switched to Java MessageFormat choice syntax that the i18next-based admin console cannot render
body: This key was changed from `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. The keycloak.v2 admin console formats these messages client-side with react-i18next, whose interpolation syntax is `{{0}}` (which is why the previous value used it) and which has no support for Java's `{2,choice,...}` clause. When this error is displayed for a multivalued attribute validation failure, the console will show the raw pattern text instead of substituting the attribute name and bounds. The server-side bundles (themes/.../admin and themes/.../login messages_en.properties) can use this syntax because they are formatted with java.text.MessageFormat, but the React console bundles must keep `{{0}}`-style placeholders.

title: error-invalid-multivalued-size switched to Java MessageFormat choice syntax that the i18next-based account console cannot render
body: This key was changed from `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. The keycloak.v3 account console renders these messages with i18next (`{{0}}` interpolation, as used by the previous version of this key), and vanilla i18next cannot evaluate a Java `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` expression — the choice clause will be displayed literally and the `{0}`/`{1}`/`{2}` placeholders won't follow this file's interpolation convention. Users hitting this validation error will see the raw format string instead of a readable message.

title: Anchor validation requires identical anchors in identical order and stops at the first mismatch
body: In `santizeAnchors` the n-th anchor found in the translation is compared with the n-th anchor found in the English source using sequential `find()` calls. A translation that contains exactly the same anchors as the source but in a different order — legitimate when grammar or right-to-left mirroring reorders links in a sentence — is reported as "Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string" and fails the build. Additionally the `break` after the first mismatch means any further anchors in the same value are never validated. Comparing against the multiset/list of English anchors (membership instead of positional matching) would avoid these false positives.

title: verifySafeHtml throws bare RuntimeException when a properties file can't be read, bypassing the MojoExecutionException contract
body: `verify()` declares `MojoExecutionException` and converts IO failures of the primary file read into it, but the new `verifySafeHtml()` opens the target file and the derived English file again and throws plain `RuntimeException("unable to read file ...")` on failure (also at line 70). This happens, for example, when a community locale file has no English counterpart under `resources/`, so adding a new translation can crash the Maven plugin with an internal-error stack trace instead of a clean, file-named plugin error or a regular verification message. These exceptions should be wrapped in `MojoExecutionException` (or reported as verification messages) for consistent error reporting.

title: Access tokens issued together with an offline refresh token get the wrong ("online") session-type prefix in their ID
body: initToken() encodes the token ID, including the session-type prefix, from the user session that exists at token-creation time. For an authorization-code or direct-grant request with scope=offline_access that session is the ONLINE session, so the ID gets the "on" prefix. However, afterwards TokenManager.AccessTokenResponseBuilder.generateRefreshToken() creates the offline user session and re-points accessToken.sessionState to the offline session (OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse even removes the online session for first-time offline access, which only works because the access token has been re-bound to the offline session). The result is that an access token bound to an OFFLINE session carries the "on" (online) prefix until the next refresh (refresh-minted tokens correctly get "of"). This corrupts exactly the data this PR exists to provide: a consumer relying on the session-type prefix to pick the right session lookup (follow-up #37662) would search online sessions, miss the offline session, and either reject a valid token or need the old fallback lookup anyway. The session type must be determined after the offline-session switch, or the token ID re-encoded when generateRefreshToken() rebinds the token to the offline session.

title: New isAccessTokenId matcher never actually verifies the grant-type shortcut (inverted condition and wrong character offsets)
body: The matcher added in this PR contains two mistakes in one line: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. First, the condition is inverted: it returns false (no match) when the extracted shortcut EQUALS the expected one, instead of when it does not. Second, the offsets are wrong: in the 6-character prefix (2 chars session type, 2 chars token type, 2 chars grant type) the grant shortcut occupies indexes 4-5, so it should be substring(4, 6); substring(3, 5) takes the second token-type character and the first grant-type character. Net effect: for real token IDs the extracted two characters essentially never equal the expected shortcut, so the matcher degrades to only checking that the part after ':' is a UUID, and expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken pass regardless of whether the encoded grant type is correct. If someone later fixes only the offsets, every one of those assertions will start failing because of the inverted equals. The whole purpose of these updated event assertions — verifying the new encoded context — is therefore not tested at all.

title: New abstract getShortcut() method breaks existing custom OAuth2 grant providers with AbstractMethodError at server startup
body: Adding a non-default method to the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory interface is a hard breaking change for any deployment with a custom grant type: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() iterates ALL registered OAuth2GrantType factories and calls getShortcut() on each of them during server startup, so a custom factory compiled against the previous version of the interface will throw AbstractMethodError and prevent the server from booting. This should be a default method (e.g. deriving a shortcut from the factory id, or returning null that the encoder factory tolerates). Note also that a custom implementation returning null would currently kill startup as well, because ConcurrentHashMap.put() throws NullPointerException for the null shortcut in postInit().

title: Constructor validates grantType twice and never checks rawTokenId for null
body: The constructor has `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null grantType not allowed")` immediately followed by `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` — the second check was clearly meant to validate rawTokenId but re-checks grantType. As a result, an AccessTokenContext with a null rawTokenId is accepted despite the error message claiming otherwise, and DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId() will then silently concatenate null into the token ID, producing something like "onrtac:null" instead of failing fast. Change the second requireNonNull to check rawTokenId.

title: Context.setFormParams() leaves the cached grantType field stale
body: The Context constructor now derives the grantType field from formParams (`formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)`), but the existing public setter setFormParams() replaces the formParams map without recomputing grantType. Any caller that swaps the form parameters after construction will have getGrantType() return the value from the original params, and that stale value is exactly what OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse() stores into the ClientSessionContext under Constants.GRANT_TYPE and what ends up encoded into the access-token ID. Either recompute grantType in setFormParams() or drop the cached field and read it from formParams in getGrantType().

title: testIncorrectGrantType passes because of a NullPointerException, not the intended validation error
body: The test builds the factory by hand and never calls postInit(), so the factory's sessionFactory field is null. When decoding "ofrtac:5678", getGrantTypeByShortcut("ac") does not find "ac" in the hand-built map and falls through to sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...), which throws a NullPointerException. The test catches the broad RuntimeException, so it goes green for the wrong reason and never exercises the intended path (unknown grant shortcut -> IllegalArgumentException "Unknown value 'ac' for grant type"). Catch IllegalArgumentException specifically and provide a stub/empty KeycloakSessionFactory so the real validation logic is tested.

title: getShortcut() javadoc suggests 3-letter shortcuts, but the codec requires exactly 2 characters
body: The javadoc says the shortcut is "usually like 3-letters", yet every built-in implementation returns 2 characters and DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId() hard-codes a 6-character context prefix (2 chars each for session type, token type, grant type) and rejects anything else with "Expected length of 6". A grant implementation that follows the javadoc and returns a 3-character shortcut would produce token IDs that cannot be decoded later, and nothing in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() validates the shortcut length (it only checks uniqueness). The contract should state that shortcuts must be exactly 2 characters and postInit should enforce it, or the codec should be made length-agnostic.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher can never fail the grant check: inverted condition and wrong substring offsets
body: The new matcher is supposed to assert that an access-token ID like "onrtac:<uuid>" carries the expected grant shortcut. In the 6-char prefix the grant shortcut sits at indexes 4-5 (2 chars session type + 2 chars token type + 2 chars grant type), but the code reads items[0].substring(3, 5), i.e. the second token-type character plus the first grant character. On top of that the condition is inverted: it returns false (no match) when the extracted text EQUALS expectedGrantShortcut, so a token with the wrong grant type is always accepted and expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken now assert nothing about the grant. The check should be `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. Also, a prefix shorter than 5 characters makes substring(3,5) throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of cleanly reporting a non-match.

title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing custom OAuth2 grant type providers at server startup
body: Adding an abstract method to the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory interface means any existing third-party/custom grant-type provider compiled against the previous interface will throw AbstractMethodError as soon as getShortcut() is invoked on it. That invocation happens eagerly for every registered grant factory in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(), i.e. during server boot, so upgrading with an existing custom grant provider deployed makes Keycloak fail to start with an obscure error. A default method (for example returning the "na"/unknown shortcut, or deriving a shortcut from the provider id) would keep existing implementations working.

title: Javadoc suggests ~3-letter shortcuts but the token-id decoder hard-requires exactly 2 characters per field
body: The javadoc of getShortcut() says the shortcut is "usually like 3-letters", but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId() requires the encoded prefix before ':' to be exactly 6 characters and slices it as 2/2/2, throwing IllegalArgumentException otherwise. A grant factory that follows the documentation and returns a 3-letter (or 1-letter) shortcut will produce access-token IDs that the decoder later rejects, and the duplicate-shortcut validation in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() does not check shortcut length, so nothing catches this at startup. The contract should state that shortcuts must be exactly two characters and postInit() should validate that, or the encoding/parsing should be made length-agnostic.

title: Constructor null-checks grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId
body: The line `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` repeats the grantType check (with the rawTokenId message) instead of checking rawTokenId. As a result an AccessTokenContext can be constructed with a null rawTokenId, and encodeTokenId() will then silently produce a token ID ending in "...:null" via string concatenation instead of failing fast.

title: Only the standard token-exchange provider records the grant type; other exchange flows mint tokens with "na" grant
body: Constants.GRANT_TYPE is set on the client session context only in StandardTokenExchangeProvider. The legacy (V1) token exchange provider and the other V2 exchange providers (subject impersonation, federated) create access tokens through the same TokenManager paths without ever setting this attribute, so access tokens they issue are encoded with the "na" (unknown) grant shortcut instead of "te". Since a stated motivation of this PR is to reliably know the grant type for token-exchange use cases (#37117), the signal will be missing/misleading for those exchange flows.

title: testIncorrectGrantType passes via NullPointerException from the unwired factory, not via the intended validation
body: The test builds DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory by calling init() and hand-populating grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts, but never calls postInit(), so the sessionFactory field stays null. Decoding "ofrtac:5678" enters the lazy-refresh branch of getGrantTypeByShortcut(), which dereferences sessionFactory and throws NullPointerException; the broad catch (RuntimeException) then lets the test pass. The intended IllegalArgumentException path ("Unknown value 'ac' for grant type") and the lazy map-refresh logic in getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut are therefore never actually exercised, and the test would still pass if that logic were broken or removed.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher never validates the grant shortcut (inverted condition and wrong substring bounds)
body: In the newly added isAccessTokenId matcher, the line `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` is wrong twice: (1) the condition is inverted — it returns false (no match) when the grant shortcut *equals* the expected value, i.e. it would reject a correct token ID and accept an incorrect one; (2) the bounds are wrong — in an encoded token ID like `onrtac:<uuid>` the 2-char grant shortcut sits at indexes 4-5, so it should be `substring(4, 6)`; `substring(3, 5)` yields e.g. "ta" for `onrtac`. As written the check can essentially never fire, so the matcher degenerates to a UUID check on the part after the colon.
