As written, a slot that starts inside working hours but ends past the working-hours end (e.g. a 60-min slot starting 30 min before the end of availability) is treated as within working hours, so the fixed-host filter will not remove it — exactly the kind of over-booking this PR is trying to prevent.

title: Slot time compared in UTC against working hours defined in organizer's timezone
body: `slotStartTime` is `time.utc()`, and the new check computes `slotStartTime.hour()`/`.day()` in UTC, then compares them against `workingHour.startTime`/`endTime`, which are minutes-since-midnight in the organizer's (schedule) timezone. For any organizer not on UTC the comparison is shifted by their offset (e.g. an IST host's 9:30 start becomes 570, but a 9:30 IST slot is hour 4 in UTC), so slots will be incorrectly rejected or accepted for fixed hosts depending on timezone. The slot time should be converted to the organizer's timezone (organizerTimeZone is already passed in) before extracting hour/day.

title: Override start/end minute computation wraps across midnight instead of producing out-of-range minutes
body: The new override mapping computes `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour() * 60 + ...minute()`. Because `.hour()` wraps into 0-23, an override whose adjusted time crosses midnight (e.g. organizer override 22:00-23:00 with invitee offset +3h becomes 25:00, reported as 1:00) produces a startTime/endTime in the wrong part of the day rather than minutes > 1440 or < 0 that the range logic could handle or clip. Overrides near midnight for invitees in distant timezones will show slots at completely wrong times. Compute total minutes from the shifted time (e.g. diff against start of day) instead of hour()/minute().

title: dateOverrideExist flag makes a slot available whenever any override matches its day, even if slot is outside all overrides
body: When `dateOverrides.find(...)` runs, the callback returns true only for slots outside the matching override, which correctly leads to `return false`. But if the slot's day matches an override and none of the 'outside' conditions trigger, the find returns undefined and execution falls to `if (dateOverrideExist) return true` — bypassing the busy-time check entirely. A fixed host with a date override on that day who also has a conflicting booking or calendar busy time during the override window will be reported available, allowing double bookings. The busy check should still run for slots inside an override.

title: dayjs objects compared with === always evaluates to false
body: In checkIfIsAvailable, the condition `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two distinct dayjs object references with `===`, which is always false. This branch was meant to detect a blocked-day override (where start equals end, i.e. the host marked the whole day unavailable). Because the check never fires, the callback falls through and returns undefined; find() then yields nothing, but dateOverrideExist was already set to true, so `if (dateOverrideExist) return true` makes every slot on that day bookable — the exact opposite of the intended behavior. A fixed host who uses a date override to block a whole day on a round-robin event will still be shown as available. Use `.isSame()` to compare the two instants.

title: Slot end computed from slotStartTime, breaking working-hours check
body: In the new working-hours check inside checkIfIsAvailable, `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` is a copy-paste of the `start` line — it should use slotEndTime. As a result, `end > workingHour.endTime` can never be true when start is inside the working hours, so a slot that starts within working hours but ends after the end of the host's working day is treated as inside working hours and remains bookable, cutting into time the host has marked unavailable.

title: Working-hours minutes compared against slot's UTC wall clock
body: In the new working-hours check, `slotStartTime` is `time.utc()` and `start`/`end` are computed from `slotStartTime.hour()` — i.e. minutes since midnight UTC. `workingHour.startTime`/`endTime`, however, are minutes since midnight in the organizer's (schedule) timezone, as produced by getUserAvailability/getWorkingHours. Comparing the two directly only works when the organizer is in UTC; for any other timezone the check accepts or rejects slots at shifted times. For example an organizer with 9:00–17:00 IST availability (240–690 minutes UTC) compared against a slot's UTC wall clock will pass/fail on the wrong boundary, so fixed-host slots can be shown outside their actual working hours or wrongly hidden.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category setting is absent
body: The migration does `execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. On any site that never set the `embed_category` site setting (it defaulted to blank), the query returns zero rows, so `[0]` is nil and calling `['id']` on nil raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration. The same fragility exists on line 15 for `uncategorized_category_id`. This will block upgrades for sites that used embeddable_hosts but never picked an embed category. Guard with `.first`/`&.` and a fallback.

title: Migrated hosts are inserted raw, without the normalization the new model applies
body: The old `embeddable_hosts` setting explicitly accepted values like `http://eviltrout.com` (the old `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` stripped `http(s)://` before comparing, and the removed specs confirm that format worked). The migration copies each line verbatim into the new table via raw SQL, bypassing the model's `before_validation` that strips the scheme and path. After migration, `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `URI(referer).host` (e.g. `eviltrout.com`) against the stored value `http://eviltrout.com` with `lower(host) = ?`, which never matches — embedding silently stops working for those hosts. The migration should normalize each value (strip scheme/path) before inserting.

title: update/destroy raise NoMethodError for nonexistent host instead of 404
body: `update` and `destroy` look up the record with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then call `host.destroy` / `host.save` without a nil check. A request for a missing or stale id (e.g. a row deleted in another tab) returns a 500 NoMethodError instead of a 404. Use `find` or raise `Discourse::NotFound` when the record is nil.

title: before_validation calls sub! on possibly-nil host
body: The `before_validation` callback does `self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` unconditionally. If a record is saved without a host (or the admin client sends a blank value — the DB column is null: false but validation happens first), `self.host` is nil and `sub!` raises NoMethodError, producing a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard with `if self.host` (and rely on a presence/format validation to report the error).

title: Host comparison is not case-insensitive on the input side
body: `record_for_host` runs `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` but never downcases the `host` extracted from the URI, while the `before_validation` that stores records never downcases either (the format validation is case-insensitive). A stored host entered as `Example.COM` matches, but an incoming referer `HTTP://EXAMPLE.COM/path` yields `uri.host == "EXAMPLE.COM"`, which won't equal `lower(stored)`. Downcase both the stored value and the lookup value to make matching reliably case-insensitive.

title: No uniqueness validation or DB index on host
body: Nothing prevents two EmbeddableHost rows for the same host (with different categories), and there is no index on `host`. Duplicates make `record_for_host`'s `.first` nondeterministic — a host could resolve to either category for imported topics — and every embed check (`host_allowed?` runs on every embedded comments request) does a full table scan. Add `validates_uniqueness_of :host` and a unique (or at least plain) index on `host` in the migration.

title: Fabricator file contents are swapped between category and embeddable_host files
body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now defines the `:embeddable_host` fabricator, while the newly added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the `:category` fabricators. The contents were pasted into the wrong files. Fabrication happens to load every file in the directory so specs still pass, but the misnamed files will confuse future edits and any tooling that maps fabricator names to files — swap the contents back.

title: category_id is mass-assigned from params without existence check
body: `host.category_id = params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` accepts any integer. An invalid id is only silently replaced with the uncategorized category when blank, not when pointing to a nonexistent category, leaving an orphaned foreign key; the admin UI will then break when rendering the host's category. Validate that the category exists (e.g. `validates :category, presence: true` with a foreign-key constraint) before saving.

title: Embedded *_ids hydration can produce undefined entries
body: In `_hydrateEmbedded`, for plural `*_ids` keys the code maps ids through `_lookupSubType`, which returns `undefined` when the id isn't present in the root payload, and then assigns the array to the plural property (the `hydrated || []` fallback never triggers since `map` always returns an array). Any payload whose `foo_ids` references an id not included in the sideloaded collection yields an array containing `undefined`, which will crash consumers doing `array[0].get('id')`. Filter out undefined values before assigning.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category setting row is absent
body: `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` assumes the query returns at least one row. Site settings only have rows in the `site_settings` table once they've been changed from the default, so any site that never customized `embed_category` (the common case) will get an empty result set, and `[0]` will be `nil`, raising `NoMethodError: undefined method '[]' for nil` and aborting the migration. The same pattern is used for `uncategorized_category_id` on line 15. Both lookups need a nil-safe fallback.

title: Host values interpolated directly into SQL in migration
body: The migration builds `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` by interpolating `h`, which comes from the admin-editable `embeddable_hosts` site setting. A host entry containing a single quote (or any SQL metacharacters) will produce malformed SQL and abort the migration, and in general this is SQL injection into a migration. Use parameterized execution (e.g. `exec_insert` with binds) or at minimum `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h)`.

title: before_validation crashes when host is nil
body: The `before_validation` block calls `self.host.sub!(...)` unconditionally. If `host` is nil (e.g. the admin submits the create form with a blank host, so `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` is nil in `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`), this raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil:NilClass` instead of producing a validation error. Guard with `if self.host.present?`.

title: update and destroy crash on unknown id instead of 404
body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for a nonexistent id. `update` then calls `save_host(nil)` which raises NoMethodError on `host.host=`, and `destroy` calls `nil.destroy`. Both should raise `Discourse::NotFound` / return 404 when the record is missing.

title: No uniqueness validation on host
body: Nothing prevents creating two `EmbeddableHost` rows with the same host (the old site setting was a flat list where duplicates were harmless). Duplicates make `record_for_host` nondeterministic about which category an embedded topic lands in and clutter the admin UI. Add `validates_uniqueness_of :host` (case-insensitive) and ideally a unique index in the migration.

title: Case-sensitive host comparison against lower(host)
body: `record_for_host` queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` but never downcases the incoming `host`. A referer like `HTTP://EVILTROUT.COM/page` yields `uri.host == "EVILTROUT.COM"`, which won't match the lowercase stored value, so embedding is wrongly rejected. Use `host.downcase` in the comparison.

title: Fabricator file contents are swapped
body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while the newly added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` defines the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, and `:private_category` fabricators. The definitions happen to load globally so tests pass, but the files are named for the wrong fabricators, which will confuse anyone editing or looking up fabricators by filename and breaks the convention the test suite relies on. Swap the file contents back.

title: Redundant/duplicated authorization filters
body: Both new admin controllers declare `before_filter :ensure_logged_in, :ensure_staff`, but `Admin::AdminController` already enforces admin access, and the routes are additionally wrapped in `AdminConstraint`. More notably `ensure_staff` would allow moderators (staff but not admins) while `AdminConstraint` allows admins — the layering is inconsistent; the controllers should rely on the standard admin controller behavior.

title: Migration crashes when site_settings rows are missing
body: Both `execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` (line 11) and `execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'uncategorized_category_id'")[0]['value']` (line 15) index into the result with `[0]` and immediately call `['id']`/`['value']` on it without checking whether any rows were returned. On a fresh install or any site where the `embed_category` setting was never customized (so no row exists in site_settings — site settings only persist a row once changed from default), `[0]` is nil and the migration raises NoMethodError, aborting the entire deploy. Only the `embeddable_hosts` query below is guarded with `cmd_tuples > 0`; the other two need the same treatment.

title: Migrated host values are not normalized, breaking the new lookup
body: The old `embeddable_hosts` site setting accepted values with scheme and path (the removed specs used values like `http://eviltrout.com` and `https://example.com/1234`), and `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` stripped schemes when comparing. The migration inserts these raw strings directly into `embeddable_hosts.host`, but the new `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `lower(host) = ?` against the bare URI hostname. Any previously configured host stored with a scheme or path will silently stop matching after this migration, so embedding from those sites stops working until an admin re-saves each host (only the model's `before_validation` strips the scheme). The migration should normalize values the same way the model does.

title: SQL string interpolation of host values in migration
body: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"` interpolates the raw site-setting value straight into SQL. A host string containing a single quote will produce a SQL error (aborting the migration) or worse. Use `sanitize_sql_array` / quoted values instead of string interpolation.

title: update/destroy crash when host id does not exist
body: In both `update` and `destroy`, `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can return nil. `update` then calls `save_host(nil)` which does `host.host = ...` → NoMethodError, and `destroy` calls `host.destroy` on nil → NoMethodError. A request with a stale or invalid id returns a 500 instead of a 404. Both actions should raise `Discourse::NotFound` (or check `host.blank?`) when the record is missing.

title: Category and embeddable_host fabricator file contents are swapped
body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while the new `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` defines `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, and `:private_category`. The contents of the two files were swapped by mistake. Fabrication loads every file in the fabricators directory so tests may still pass, but the files are misleadingly named and any tooling or developer looking for the category fabricator in `category_fabricator.rb` (or relying on filename-to-fabricator conventions) will be confused; the definitions should live in their correctly named files.

title: Case-sensitive host lookup can miss valid hosts
body: `record_for_host` does `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` but passes `uri.host` unmodified. The model's format validation allows uppercase (`/i`) and `before_validation` never downcases `host`, so a row saved as `Example.COM` (or a referer URI whose host contains uppercase) will never match because one side is lowercased and the other is not. Downcase both the stored host (in `before_validation`) and the lookup value to make matching consistent.

title: No uniqueness constraint/validation on host
body: Nothing prevents duplicate `EmbeddableHost` rows for the same host (no unique index in the migration, no `validates_uniqueness_of`). Admins can create several rows for the same hostname pointing at different categories, and `record_for_host` uses `.first`, so which category embedded topics land in is nondeterministic. Add a unique index on `host` and a uniqueness validation.

title: Duplicate `downsize` definitions silently override each other
body: The file now defines `OptimizedImage.downsize` twice: once at line 145 with signature `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and again at line 149 with `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. Ruby does not support overloading; the second definition silently replaces the first. Any existing caller that passes width and height as separate arguments (the original 4-argument API, e.g. `downsize(from, to, 800, 600)`) will now raise `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (4 for 2..3)`. The overload must be removed or the signatures unified (e.g. accept *args and dispatch).

title: Downsize loop never breaks on failure and uploads oversized file anyway
body: In `create_upload`, the `while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > ...` loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize` but ignores its return value. If `convert` fails (returns false) or the image simply cannot be shrunk below the limit within 5 iterations, the code falls through and calls `Upload.create_for` with the still-oversized (or unchanged) tempfile anyway, retrying an identical failing operation up to 5 times and wasting CPU. If downsizing fails or the file is still over the limit after the attempts, the upload should be rejected with a clear error instead of proceeding.

title: Animated GIFs are destroyed or fail downsizing
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)` routes animated GIFs (when `allow_animation` is true) to `downsize_instructions_animated`, which delegates to `resize_instructions_animated` producing `gifsicle ... --resize-fit 80%` — gifsicle's `--resize-fit` expects geometry like `WxH`, not a percentage, so the command fails and the GIF is never reduced (and the loop retries the same failing command 5 times). When `allow_animation` is false, `downsize_instructions` uses `#{from}[0]`, which silently strips all but the first frame, turning users' animated GIFs into static images. Additionally the animated-vs-static decision keys off `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`, but the tempfile path (e.g. `discourse-upload-image...`) has no `.gif` extension, so animated handling never actually triggers. Note also that the `from` and `to` paths are identical, so `convert` reads and overwrites the same file each iteration with compounding quality loss.

title: Hardcoded 10MB client-side limit ignores per-type site settings
body: `validateUploadedFile` previously enforced `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` (different limits for images vs attachments); it now hardcodes 10MB for both. If an admin configures `max_attachment_size_kb` above or below 10MB, or `max_image_size_kb` above 10MB, the client-side validation no longer matches the server: users may be wrongly blocked from uploading valid files, or allowed to select files the server will reject — and the 413 error handler at line 246 also reports the hardcoded 10MB rather than the actual configured limit, producing misleading error messages.

title: API URL downloads now hardcode 10MB instead of the configured image size
body: `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` replaces `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`. Sites that set `max_image_size_kb` above 10MB (e.g. 15MB) will now have API-based URL image downloads truncated/rejected at 10MB even though the subsequent downsize step could have brought them under the limit, and sites with a limit below 10MB now download more data than configured. The download cap should stay tied to the setting (or a named constant larger than any supported limit).

title: Duplicate `downsize` definition silently replaces the (from, to, max_width, max_height) signature
body: The file now defines `self.downsize` twice: once at line 145 taking `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` and again at line 149 taking `(from, to, dimensions, opts)`. In Ruby the second definition wins, so the 4-positional-argument version no longer exists. Any existing caller that passes width and height (e.g. `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, w, h)`) will now raise `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments`, and there is no indication all callers were migrated. One of the two definitions must be removed/renamed.

title: Animated GIF downsize passes "80%" to gifsicle --resize-fit, which expects WxH
body: The uploads controller calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)`. For animated GIFs, `optimize` selects `downsize_instructions_animated`, which delegates to `resize_instructions_animated` and produces `gifsicle ... --resize-fit 80% ...`. gifsicle does not accept a percentage for `--resize-fit`; the command fails, `convert_with` returns false, and the retry loop in the controller burns all 5 attempts without shrinking the file. Animated GIFs over the size limit can therefore never be uploaded, and the failure is silent (`&> /dev/null`).

title: Downsize retry loop ignores failure and retries identical work
body: The loop `while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > limit` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize` but never checks its boolean return value. If the conversion fails (bad image, missing convert/gifsicle, unsupported format), the file size never changes and the same failing command is executed 5 times synchronously inside the deferred job before falling through to `Upload.create_for`, which will then fail validation anyway. The result is wasted CPU and a confusing generic error instead of surfacing that the image could not be processed. Break out of the loop when `downsize` returns false.

title: Client-side upload size limit hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring site settings
body: `validateUploadedFile` previously read `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, so images and attachments each respected their configured limits. The change replaces that with a hardcoded `10 * 1024`. Sites with `max_attachment_size_kb` above 10MB will now have the client reject attachments the server would accept, and sites with image limits above 10MB get a client-side rejection even though the server can now auto-downsize large images (which is the point of this PR — the client should not pre-emptively block oversized images anymore). The same hardcoding was applied to the 413 handler at line 246.

title: Download cap hardcoded to 10MB for API URL uploads
body: `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` replaces the previous `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`. While the intent is to allow downloading larger originals for downsizing, this also caps downloads for sites whose configured image limit is above 10MB (they could previously pull larger files), and it downloads full-size originals for non-image types too, with the size magic number duplicated between the controller and the JS client. This should derive from a single setting (e.g. a multiple of max_image_size_kb) rather than a literal.

title: Downsizing SVGs and other vector/odd formats with `convert -resize 80%` can corrupt or balloon them
body: The guard uses `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)`, which (matching the client-side list) includes SVG. Running ImageMagick `-resize 80%` on an SVG rasterizes it and writes the result over the original path with the `.svg` extension, producing a mislabeled raster file or a failure; repeated attempts can also grow the file, making the loop spin. SVGs (and potentially other formats that don't shrink meaningfully at 80% quality-agnostic resize) should be excluded from the auto-downsize path.

title: Dead first `downsize` overload: width/height form unreachable and resize/downsize now inconsistent
body: Beyond the duplicate-definition problem, the first `downsize` (line 145) builds `"#{max_width}x#{max_height}"` and forwards — but it is immediately overridden by the line-149 version that takes a raw `dimensions` string. Meanwhile `resize` still takes explicit width/height. The net effect is an API where `downsize(from, to, 100, 200)` compiles fine at call sites in other code but now treats `100` as the dimensions string and `200` as `opts`, silently producing `-resize 100` with a nonsense opts hash. Any caller using the old arity misbehaves rather than raising.

title: Duplicate self.downsize definition silently overrides the 4-argument version
body: The file now defines `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145 and then immediately redefines `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149. In Ruby the second definition wins, so the 4-positional-argument version is dead code. Any existing caller that invokes `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, width, height)` will now raise `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (4 for 3..4)` — worse, a call with width and height will be treated as `dimensions = width` and `opts = height`, producing garbage ImageMagick dimensions instead of an error. Either remove the old overload or keep only one signature.

title: Client-side upload size check hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring site settings
body: `validateUploadedFile` previously enforced `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`; this PR replaces it with a hardcoded `10 * 1024` KB. If an admin sets a smaller limit (e.g. 2MB images, or lower attachment limits), users get no client-side warning and only learn about the failure after the upload round-trips to the server; if they set a larger limit, the client still blocks at 10MB. The same hardcoding was applied to the 413 handler at line 246. The site setting lookup should be kept (and the error message will then report the correct limit).

title: API URL downloads now hard-capped at 10MB regardless of configured limits
body: The download limit for API-provided URLs was changed from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes`. Admins who raise max_image_size_kb above 10MB still cannot pull larger images via the API (download returns nil and the upload fails with a confusing error), and the magic number can drift from the client-side and server-side limits. The downsize logic added below makes the original intent (download up to some cap, then shrink) work, but the cap should be a setting-derived value, e.g. a multiple of max_image_size_kb, not a literal.

title: Downsize loop keeps shrinking in place and gives up silently on failure
body: The loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` up to 5 times without checking the return value. Two problems: (1) each iteration recompresses the already-downsized file at 80% of the previous dimensions, so an image that needs more than one pass ends up drastically smaller and more degraded than necessary (0.8^5 ≈ 33% of original dimensions) rather than being resized once to a target that fits the byte limit; (2) if `downsize` fails (e.g. ImageMagick error on a corrupt/unsupported file), it returns false, the file size never changes, the loop burns through all 5 attempts running convert 5 times for nothing, and the oversized file is passed on to `Upload.create_for` anyway. The return value should break the loop, and a single computed resize (or at least checking progress between iterations) would avoid the compounding quality loss.

title: Animated GIF downsizing reuses thumbnail resize-fit instructions and drops animation framing
body: For animated GIFs the `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` path routes to `downsize_instructions_animated`, which just delegates to `resize_instructions_animated` (gifsicle `--resize-fit 80%`). Passing a percentage to gifsicle's --resize-fit is not valid geometry (it expects WxH), so animated GIFs over the size limit will fail to downsize (convert returns non-zero, loop no-ops) and the upload then fails validation. Additionally, tying upload downsizing of animations to the `allow_animated_thumbnails` setting conflates two unrelated features — a site that disables animated thumbnails still wants animated originals downsized.

title: unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser row
body: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil — a user can receive a notification email (e.g. via a category watch or a mention) without ever having a topic_users row. The very next line calls `tu.notification_level`, producing a NoMethodError and a 500 for exactly the users most likely to click an unsubscribe link. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic.id, notification_level: ...)` or handle the nil case by creating the record.

title: Unsubscribe mutates state via a GET request
body: The new `unsubscribe` action is exposed via GET (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` in config/routes.rb) and immediately writes to topic_users (setting regular/muted). GET links in emails are followed by mail-client prefetchers, link scanners, and antivirus proxies, so a user's notification state can be changed without any intentional action; it also makes the endpoint CSRF-able via a simple tag for logged-in users. The GET should render a confirmation page that performs the change via POST, as the client-side unsubscribe template suggests was intended.

title: topicUnsubscribe client route is shadowed by topic.fromParamsNear
body: The `topicUnsubscribe` route (path `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe`) is declared after the `topic` resource, whose child route `fromParamsNear` has path `/:nearPost`. Ember matches routes in declaration order, so `/t/slug/123/unsubscribe` matches `topic.fromParamsNear` with nearPost="unsubscribe" before the new route is ever reached. The unsubscribe page will instead load the normal topic route and attempt to treat "unsubscribe" as a post number. The route needs to be declared before the topic resource or nested so it wins.

title: unsubscribe_link translation now requires unsubscribe_url but most callers don't provide it
body: The `unsubscribe_link` text now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`, and `Email::MessageBuilder#body`/`#html_part` call `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` whenever `add_unsubscribe_link` is true. Only `send_notification_email` was updated to pass `unsubscribe_url`; any other email built with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` and no `unsubscribe_url` will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and fail to send. The interpolation should be conditional on the URL being present (or all callers updated and a test added for the missing-arg case).

title: Unsubscribe sets notification_level directly, losing reason/changed-at bookkeeping and MessageBus notification
body: The action assigns `tu.notification_level` and saves the model directly instead of using `TopicUser.change`. That bypasses setting `notifications_changed_at`/`notifications_reason_id` and skips the MessageBus `notification_level_change` publish, so any other open browser tabs of the user will keep showing the old notification state for the topic until reload, and analytics/auditing of why the level changed is lost.

title: Unsubscribe mutates notification state on a plain GET request
body: The new `unsubscribe` action is exposed via GET (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`) and immediately changes the user's `notification_level` in the database before rendering. GET requests are issued without user intent by mail-client link prefetchers, virus scanners (e.g. Outlook SafeLinks), and browser prerendering, and they carry no CSRF protection. Any such automated fetch of the unsubscribe URL will silently mute/change the user's topic subscription. Unsubscribe-via-GET should either require a POST confirmation or at minimum not apply the state change until the user confirms on the rendered page.

title: TopicUser.find_by can return nil, causing a 500 on unsubscribe
body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` is not guaranteed to exist. Users can receive notification emails without ever having a topic_users row for the topic (e.g. mailing-list mode subscribers, or users notified via category watching where the row was never created). In that case `tu.notification_level` on line 107 raises NoMethodError and the unsubscribe link from the email returns a 500. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...)` which creates the row when missing.

title: Direct save bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping
body: The action mutates `tu.notification_level` and calls `tu.save!` directly instead of `TopicUser.change`. As a result `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` are not set, and no `notification_level_change` message is published on MessageBus, so any open browser tabs of that user keep showing the old notification state and reporting that relies on the changed-at/reason fields is wrong. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: ...)` for consistency with every other code path that changes notification levels.

title: ensure_logged_in blocks the email unsubscribe flow for logged-out users
body: `unsubscribe` is added to the `ensure_logged_in` filter list. The feature's entry point is a link in a notification email, and recipients frequently are not logged in (mobile mail clients, different browser). Those users are bounced to the login page and, even after logging in, are not taken back to the unsubscribe URL, so the one-click unsubscribe silently fails for exactly the audience it targets. Consider a signed token in the unsubscribe URL (like the existing digest unsubscribe key) instead of requiring a session.

title: Watching/tracking users are demoted to 'regular', still receiving notifications
body: The logic sets the level to `regular` when it is currently above regular, and only mutes when it is regular or below. A user watching a topic (the most common reason for getting email) who clicks 'stop receiving notifications about this topic' is moved to regular, under which they still receive reply/mention notifications. The email copy ('To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here') and the page text ('You will stop receiving notifications') then claim the opposite of what happened.

title: unsubscribe_link now requires %{unsubscribe_url} but not all callers pass it
body: The `unsubscribe_link` translation now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` in `Email::MessageBuilder#body` and `#html_part` is invoked for every email built with `add_unsubscribe_link: true`; any current or future caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link` without passing `unsubscribe_url` (e.g. plugins, or the spec's own builder which previously only used `add_unsubscribe_link: true`) will now raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` and the email will fail to send. Either make the per-topic sentence conditional on the URL being present or guard against the missing key.

title: No controller/request specs for the new unsubscribe endpoint
body: The PR adds a state-changing endpoint (`topics#unsubscribe`), new routes, and a mailer link, but the only spec change is adding an `unsubscribe_url` option to an existing message-builder test. There is no coverage for the redirect-on-slug-mismatch branch, the level-downgrade/mute logic, the nil TopicUser case, or the requirement that the user be logged in — all of which contain bugs noted above.

title: unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when no TopicUser row exists
body: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil, and the very next line calls `tu.notification_level`, producing a 500. Not every emailed user has a topic_users row: mailing-list-mode emails (`mailing_list_notify`) are sent to users who may never have visited the topic, so the per-topic unsubscribe link added to those emails (`unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url`) will 500 for exactly the users most likely to click it. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...)` which creates the row if missing, or handle the nil case.

title: unsubscribe bypasses TopicUser.change, skipping reason tracking and MessageBus notification
body: The action mutates `tu.notification_level` directly and calls `tu.save!` instead of `TopicUser.change`. `TopicUser.change` sets `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` (:user_changed) and publishes `notification_level_change` over MessageBus. Bypassing it means (a) other open browser tabs/devices never learn of the change in real time, and (b) because `notifications_reason_id` stays null, auto-track logic (`TopicUser.auto_track` and the auto-track branch in `update_last_read`) can silently flip the user's level back to tracking the next time they read the topic, undoing the unsubscribe.

title: State-changing unsubscribe performed on a plain GET request
body: The new `GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` route immediately mutes/regularizes the topic for the logged-in user as a side effect of rendering the page. GET links in emails are routinely pre-fetched by mail scanners and link-protection services (e.g. Outlook SafeLinks, corporate proxies), so a user can have a topic muted without ever clicking anything. Unsubscribe links should land on a confirmation page and perform the state change via POST/PUT (as the site's existing email unsubscribe flow does with a key + POST), or at minimum only apply the change after explicit user confirmation.

title: unsubscribe_url ignores relative_root / subfolder installs incorrectly in redirect
body: `unsubscribe_url` is built as `"#{url}/unsubscribe"` where `url` uses `Discourse.base_url` (no `Discourse.base_uri` path handling issue for emails, which is fine), but in `TopicsController#unsubscribe` it is also used for the 301 slug-redirect (`redirect_to @topic_view.topic.unsubscribe_url`). Redirecting to the absolute URL is acceptable, but the redirect condition `(!request.format.json? && params[:slug].blank?)` combined with this absolute URL means the no-slug route `/t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` issues a redirect on every email click before doing the work — harmless but an extra hop; more importantly the JSON-format branch never redirects even when the slug is wrong, so the state change happens on mismatched-slug API calls.

title: Blocked email match is case-sensitive and unnormalized, so it is trivially bypassed
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? does an exact string lookup (`BlockedEmail.where(email: email)`) against the raw email entered on the signup form. The rest of the codebase normalizes email via Email.downcase (which lowercases and strips dots/plus tags for gmail-style providers) before storing/comparing, but this lookup does not. A blocked address like bad@spammer.com can be evaded simply by signing up as Bad@Spammer.com, or with gmail dot/plus variants (b.ad+1@gmail.com). Since the entire purpose of the feature is to keep blocked users out, the lookup should normalize the incoming email the same way User emails are normalized, and the blocked_emails rows should be stored normalized.

title: match_count increment is a non-atomic read-modify-write
body: should_block? loads the record, does `record.match_count += 1`, and saves. Under concurrent signups/validations hitting the same blocked email, increments will be lost (last writer wins). Use an atomic update such as `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all("match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ...")` or update_counters so the statistics are accurate.

title: Blocked check is skipped whenever any other email error exists
body: The BlockedEmail.should_block? call is guarded by `record.errors[attribute].blank?`, and each User.save with a changed email runs this validator. The intent is fine, but note that should_block? has a side effect (incrementing match_count and last_match_at) — because it runs inside model validation, any save of a user whose email changed (including admin edits, seed scripts, etc.) mutates these statistics, while genuinely blocked attempts that also fail format validation are never counted. If the stats are meant to record blocked signup attempts specifically, the counting should happen at the controller/signup path rather than inside a model validator.

title: Blocked email check is case-sensitive and easily bypassed
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? does an exact `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` lookup, and the value passed here is the raw `user.email` attribute, which is stored as the user typed it (User.new_from_params assigns params[:email] directly, no downcasing). A blocked address like spammer@example.com can register as Spammer@Example.com and sail past the block list, since PostgreSQL string comparison is case-sensitive. The email should be normalized (e.g. Email.downcase) before the lookup, both here and wherever BlockedEmail records are created.

title: Blocked emails not enforced on change_email
body: The new BlockedEmail validation only runs via User's `email` validator, but `change_email` never saves the user with the new email — it only checks uniqueness and creates an email token; the token confirmation path (EmailToken.confirm) updates the address without going through the new validator. An existing account (or one created before an address was blocked) can switch to a blocked email address, defeating the feature. The block check should also be applied in the email-change flow.

title: Match statistics update is racy and performed inside a validation
body: should_block? reads the record, increments match_count in Ruby, and saves, which loses increments under concurrent signups; more notably it is called from EmailValidator#validate_each, so merely validating a User (not saving) performs a database write with `record.save`, whose failure is silently ignored. Use an atomic update (e.g. update_counters / UPDATE ... SET match_count = match_count + 1) and consider moving the stats update out of the validation path.

title: rejectedEmails comparison is exact-string and won't match case variants
body: After a failed signup the server echoes back result.values.email and it is pushed into rejectedEmails; the check `this.get('rejectedEmails').contains(email)` is an exact string comparison against the current accountEmail input. If the user retries with different casing (e.g. Bad@Spam.com vs bad@spam.com) the client-side rejection won't trigger and they'll get another full server round-trip each time. Compare lowercased values.

title: Blocked email lookup is case-sensitive, allowing trivial bypass
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? looks up records with `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` using the exact string passed in. User emails are matched case-insensitively elsewhere in the app (e.g. Email.downcase is used in UsersController#change_email), but a blocked entry for 'spammer@evil.com' will not match a signup with 'Spammer@Evil.com' or 'SPAMMER@evil.com', so anyone can bypass the block list just by changing letter case. The email should be normalized (downcased) both when the BlockedEmail record is created and when it is looked up.

title: should_block? performs a database write inside a validation
body: should_block? is called from EmailValidator#validate_each, which runs during user.valid? — i.e. on every signup attempt and every form retry — and it increments match_count and saves the BlockedEmail record each time. This has two problems: (1) a validation method should be side-effect free; the counter save happens even if the surrounding user save later rolls back, and any validation failure on the BlockedEmail record itself would silently fail to save, and (2) every failed signup attempt triggers an extra UPDATE query. The statistics update should be moved out of the validator (e.g. only recorded on actual blocked signup attempts in the controller), or done with update_counters to avoid running the record's full validations.

title: Domain restriction regex is not anchored at the end, so whitelist/blacklist can be evaded or misapplied
body: email_in_restriction_setting? builds the pattern `@(domains)` with no end anchor. With a whitelist of 'mycompany.com', an address like 'attacker@mycompany.com.evil.org' matches and is accepted; conversely a blacklisted domain matches any address whose domain merely starts with it. The regex should be anchored (e.g. `@(#{domains})$` or matching against the parsed domain) so the comparison is against the actual email domain.

title: Uniqueness validation plus unique index has a race with no exception handling
body: BlockedEmail validates uniqueness of email and the migration adds a unique index, but two concurrent inserts of the same email can both pass validation, and the second will raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique/StatementInvalid on save. Nothing rescues this, so any code path or admin console creating blocked emails concurrently will surface a 500. Either handle the exception or rely on the index with an upsert.

title: raw_html cook method renders un-sanitized HTML into posts, enabling stored XSS
body: The new `cook_method == :raw_html` path returns `raw` verbatim, completely bypassing the PrettyText/Sanitize pipeline. Feed/import content is user-controlled HTML from an external source (PollFeed does `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` with no sanitization, and TopicEmbed.import_remote passes Readability output straight through). `scrub` only fixes invalid byte sequences, it does not strip `<script>` or event handlers. The resulting post is then emitted with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb (and anywhere else cooked posts render on the forum domain), so any script in a feed item executes in the forum's origin for every viewer, including logged-in admins. The imported content must be sanitized before being stored/served.

title: postMessage targetOrigin uses the full referer URL including path, which browsers reject
body: `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')` passes the entire referer URL as the targetOrigin. Per the postMessage spec, targetOrigin must be only scheme://host[:port]; if it contains a path the browser throws a SecurityError (or silently fails in older browsers) and the message is never delivered. Since every real referer includes a path, the 'discourse-resize' message that app/assets/javascripts/embed.js relies on to size the iframe will never arrive, leaving the iframe at its default height. The referer should be reduced to its origin before being used as targetOrigin.

title: PollFeed crashes on feed items without content
body: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` calls `.scrub` on `i.content` without checking for nil. Many Atom/RSS items only provide a summary/description and no content element, in which case SimpleRSS returns nil and the scheduled job raises NoMethodError, aborting the entire poll (and with retry disabled, nothing is imported until the next run). Guard with something like `(i.content || i.summary || '').scrub`.

title: Origin check uses substring matching instead of strict origin comparison
body: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts any message whose origin appears anywhere inside discourseUrl. This is a fragile check: for example if discourseUrl lacks a trailing slash, an origin like 'https://discourse.example.com' matches even when discourseUrl is 'https://discourse.example.com.evil.tld'-style misconfigurations, and it also matches when the configured URL merely contains the origin as a substring (e.g. discourseUrl '//example.com/path' vs origin 'https://example.com' — inverted cases aside, substring matching is not an origin comparison). Parse both URLs and compare scheme/host/port strictly before resizing the iframe based on a message.

title: TopicEmbed.create! runs even when PostCreator failed to persist the post
body: `creator.create` returns `@post` even when post creation rolled back (e.g. validation or host-spam rollback leaves @post set but not persisted, and in the spam case create swallows the rollback). `post.present?` is then true, so `TopicEmbed.create!(topic_id: post.topic_id, post_id: post.id)` runs with `post_id = nil` against a `null: false` column (and a possibly nil/unsaved topic_id), raising ActiveRecord::NotNullViolation out of the import path instead of cleanly skipping. Check `post.persisted? && post.errors.blank?` before creating the TopicEmbed.

title: absolutize_urls misses relative URLs that don't start with '/'
body: Only href/src values starting with '/' are rewritten. Relative links like `href="page2.html"` or `src="images/pic.png"` are left untouched, so in imported topics they resolve relative to the forum's domain and produce broken links/images. Use URI.join(url, href) (or equivalent) for any non-absolute URL instead of only root-relative ones.

title: Embedding authorization relies solely on the Referer header host
body: `ensure_embeddable` grants framing based only on `URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. Direct loads (no referer) are rejected, but referer is client-supplied and can be forged by non-browser clients, and any page on the allowed host — including user-generated content on that host — can embed arbitrary `embed_url` parameters, each enqueueing a retrieve job. The 60s redis throttle in TopicRetriever mitigates volume, but the only thing binding the embed URL to the page is this header check; consider also validating that the embed_url's host matches and documenting that the referer check is not a strong security boundary.

title: i.content can be nil, crashing the hourly feed job
body: In poll_feed, `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every feed item has a `content` element. Plain RSS 2.0 feeds typically only have `description`, not `content`, so SimpleRSS will return nil and `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError, aborting the entire feed poll (and because `sidekiq_options retry: false`, nothing is retried and no items from that feed are imported until the next hour, which will crash the same way). Use `i.content || i.description` and guard for nil.

title: raw_html cook method stores and serves completely unsanitized HTML
body: `cook` returns `raw` verbatim when cook_method is :raw_html, so posts imported via TopicEmbed.import (feed polling or remote retrieval of the embeddable host) bypass PrettyText/Sanitize entirely and are served as-is (the embed view even does `raw post.cooked`). Any script/event-handler markup in a fetched article or feed item becomes stored XSS on the forum itself, visible in topic pages, digests, and embeds. The imported HTML should be run through Sanitize with an allowlist before storage.

title: postMessage origin check uses substring match
body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that merely appears as a substring of discourseUrl. An origin like `https://evil.com/redirect?https://forum.example.com` would pass if discourseUrl is configured correspondingly, and more simply the check never validates that e.origin actually equals the forum's origin. Any site able to get a message to the parent window can resize the iframe; the check should compare e.origin against a parsed expected origin.

title: Check-then-create on embed_url races and raises RecordNotUnique
body: import() does `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and then `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a transaction. The migration adds a unique index on embed_url, so two concurrent imports of the same URL (hourly PollFeed plus a RetrieveTopic job enqueued from embed#best, which explicitly runs PollFeed and then fetches HTTP itself) will both find no row and one will crash with ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique. Rescue RecordNotUnique and fall back to the update path, or use an upsert.

title: absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs
body: Any href/src starting with '/' is prefixed with the article's scheme+host. Protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/x.jpg` start with '/', so they are rewritten to `http://host/cdn.example.com/x.jpg`, breaking those links/images in every imported post. Check for a leading '//' and skip (or prepend only the scheme) before treating the URL as host-relative.

title: feed_key is dead code; job does no change detection
body: feed_key computes a redis key 'feed-modified:<sha>' but nothing ever reads or writes it, and poll_feed re-downloads the feed and re-hashes/re-imports every item every hour. Either wire the key up to skip unchanged feeds (e.g. via If-Modified-Since/ETag or content hash) or remove it; as-is every hourly run re-fetches all items and calls PostRevisor/sha comparisons for each.

title: Editing an already-shipped migration to add force: true
body: CreateTopTopics already ran in existing deployments; changing `create_table :top_topics` to `force: true` modifies history. Environments that haven't run it yet (or that replay migrations, e.g. some CI/staging rebuilds after a partially applied state) will silently DROP and recreate the top_topics table, losing all aggregated counts. New behavior should go in a new migration rather than editing an old one.

title: X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL is non-standard and unsupported
body: `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = 'ALLOWALL'` is not a valid X-Frame-Options value (ALLOW-FROM requires a URI and is unsupported in Chrome/Safari; ALLOWALL is ignored entirely by most browsers). The effect is only achieved because an invalid value happens to be ignored — better to explicitly remove the header so the intent is clear and future middleware adding a default DENY doesn't break embeds.

title: import mutates the caller's contents string
body: `contents << "\n<hr>..."` appends the 'imported from' footer directly to the string passed in. Callers that reuse the buffer (e.g. the Readability document content or anything comparing the original afterwards) get silently modified data, and the sha1 is computed over the mutated value. Duplicate the string (`contents = contents + ...` or `contents.dup`) before appending.

title: Throws if #discourse-comments element is missing
body: `comments.appendChild(iframe)` runs without checking that `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` found an element. Site owners paste this snippet into arbitrary templates; if the container is absent or renamed, the script throws and no iframe is created, with no useful error. Bail out early (or log a clear message) when comments is null.

title: raw_html cook method stores unsanitized HTML as cooked post
body: Post#cook now returns the raw text verbatim when cook_method is :raw_html, which means the cooked column contains completely unsanitized HTML imported from RSS feeds (PollFeed) and remote pages (TopicRetriever -> TopicEmbed.import_remote). That cooked HTML is then rendered unescaped in app/views/embed/best.html.erb via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (and anywhere else cooked posts are shown), so any feed entry or embedded page can inject arbitrary JavaScript — a stored XSS that executes in the browsers of visitors on the embedding site (via the iframe) and of forum users viewing the imported topic. The content is never passed through Sanitize/PrettyText, so there is no script stripping at any point.

title: postMessage origin check uses substring match and can be bypassed
body: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` does a substring check instead of an exact origin comparison. An origin like `https://forum.example.com.evil.com` (or any host whose origin string appears inside discourseUrl) passes the check, allowing a malicious page to send crafted `discourse-resize` messages. It should compare `e.origin` exactly against the parsed origin of discourseUrl.

title: postMessage targetOrigin is the full referer URL, so resize messages are never delivered
body: `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')` passes the entire referer URL (including path, e.g. `http://blog.example.com/2013/02/10/post.html`) as targetOrigin. Browsers only accept an origin (scheme + host + port) or '*' as targetOrigin; a URL with a path will not match the parent's origin, so the message is silently dropped and the iframe is never resized (the resize mechanism this whole feature depends on does not work). Use only the origin portion of the referer.

title: Editing an old migration to add force: true drops the existing top_topics table
body: The already-applied migration CreateTopTopics was changed from `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. On any environment where this migration re-runs (e.g. rebuilt databases, or deployments where migration state is reset), force: true will DROP and recreate the existing top_topics table, destroying all stored top-topic statistics. Old migrations should never be edited; unrelated 'force: true' additions to MigrateWordCounts/new migrations are fine, but this one alters a shipped migration.

title: Feed items without content element crash the hourly job
body: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every RSS/Atom item has a `content` element. Many RSS feeds only provide `description`, in which case SimpleRSS returns nil for content and `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError. Since the job runs hourly with retry disabled, one such feed item kills the entire polling run and no topics get imported until the offending item scrolls out of the feed.

title: Controller spec expects TopicRetriever but the controller enqueues a background job
body: The spec 'tells the topic retriever to work when no previous embed is found' sets `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)`, but EmbedController#best never instantiates TopicRetriever — it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`, and in the test environment jobs are not executed. This expectation can never be satisfied by the real code path, so the test either fails or was written against an older synchronous implementation; it should instead assert that the :retrieve_topic job is enqueued with the right arguments.

title: import mutates the caller's contents string with <<
body: `contents << "\n<hr>\n<small>..."` appends the 'imported from' footer directly to the string passed in by the caller. Any caller that reuses that string (e.g. a loop variable or a comparison against the original feed content) will see it unexpectedly modified. Duplicate the string before appending (e.g. `contents = contents.dup` or `contents +=`).

title: Float-based layout in .small-action breaks once it becomes a flex container
body: .small-action is now a flexbox container (@include flexbox()), but its children still rely on floats: .topic-avatar has float: left and the button has float: right. Floats are ignored on flex items, so the action button that previously sat at the far right of the row will now render inline immediately after .small-action-desc instead of being right-aligned. The .small-action-desc also lost its 'padding-left: 4em' which previously cleared the 45px-wide avatar; combined with the removed 'margin-top: 5px' and 'padding-top: 4px' this changes vertical alignment of the description text. Either convert the children to proper flex layout (e.g. margin-left: auto on the button) or keep the floats and don't make the container a flexbox.

title: align-items mixin emits invalid value for legacy -webkit-box syntax when 'baseline' is used
body: The new align-items mixin passes the value straight through to -webkit-box-align and -ms-flex-align. The old 2009 flexbox syntax (-webkit-box-align) only accepts start/end/center/baseline/stretch — actually 'baseline' is not valid for -webkit-box-align in old WebKit (it accepts start, end, center, stretch only). .badge-wrapper.bullet calls @include align-items(baseline), so on browsers using the legacy -webkit-box syntax the alignment declaration is invalid and dropped, silently changing rendering there. If legacy support matters (which the prefixes imply), the mixin should map values per-syntax.

title: Dead .valign-helper rule left behind after flexbox conversion
body: The .contents block was converted from float/inline-block vertical-centering to flexbox with align-items: center, which makes the .valign-helper element (an inline-block 100%-height shim used to vertically center siblings) unnecessary. The rule remains in the stylesheet; if the corresponding span is also still emitted in the markup it will now participate as an extra zero-width flex item. The leftover markup/CSS should be removed as part of this change.

title: float: right on .small-action button no longer works inside new flex container
body: The PR turns .small-action into a flex container (@include flexbox()), but the button inside it still relies on `float: right` (line ~309) to be pushed to the right edge. CSS floats are ignored on flex items, so the button will now render immediately after the .small-action-desc content instead of being right-aligned. The same applies to the leftover `float: left` declarations on .topic-avatar and .small-action-desc .avatar. The layout should be expressed with flex properties (e.g. margin-left: auto on the button) or the floats removed, otherwise the small-action row layout regresses.

title: align-items mixin emits non-existent -ms-align-items property
body: The new align-items mixin includes `-ms-align-items: $alignment;` (line 121). There is no such property: IE10/11 only support the 2012 syntax `-ms-flex-align`, which is already emitted on the previous line. The bogus declaration is silently ignored by browsers, so it is dead output in every compiled stylesheet that uses the mixin; it should be removed.

title: .valign-helper rule is now dead code after flexbox switch
body: .d-header .contents is now a flex container with align-items: center, which makes the .valign-helper element (display: inline-block; height: 100%; vertical-align: middle) — a hack for vertical centering in inline-block layouts — completely ineffective, since vertical-align has no effect on flex items and height: 100% inside a flex row behaves differently. The rule (and the corresponding markup, if any) should be removed to avoid confusion.

title: Button float:right inside new flex container no longer works
body: .small-action is now a flex container (@include flexbox()), but its child button still relies on `float: right` to be pushed to the right edge. Floats are ignored on flex items, so the button will now sit immediately after .small-action-desc instead of at the far right of the row. The same applies to `float: left` on .topic-avatar and .small-action-desc .avatar (avatar is not a flex item so that one still works, but the button and topic-avatar are direct flex items). The button rule needs `margin-left: auto` (as was done for .panel in header.scss) or the container needs justify-content to preserve the previous layout.

title: align-items mixin emits invalid -ms-align-items property and values incompatible with old box syntax
body: The align-items mixin emits `-ms-align-items`, which is not a real vendor-prefixed property in any browser, so it is dead output. More importantly, when called with `baseline` (badges.css.scss for .badge-wrapper.bullet), it emits `-webkit-box-align: baseline` and `-ms-flex-align: baseline`; the 2009 box syntax and IE10's -ms-flex-align only accept start/end/center/stretch, so those declarations are dropped. Browsers needing the prefixed fallbacks (old Safari, IE10) will get no alignment at all for the baseline case, changing badge rendering versus the previous unprefixed-only code path only in modern browsers is fine, but the mixin gives a false sense of compatibility.

title: Dead float rules remain on flex items in header
body: After making .d-header .contents a flex container, several children that are now flex items still carry float rules: .icons (float: left), .icons > li (float: left is on a non-flex child so still effective), and .login-button/.sign-up-button (float: left). Floats on direct flex items are ignored, so .icons and the login/sign-up buttons no longer float; they rely on flex source order plus .panel's margin-left:auto/order(3). Any markup where these elements are not in the expected DOM order, or any CSS that expected the float behavior (e.g., text wrapping around the floated icons list), will render differently. The stale float declarations should be removed or the layout verified for all header states (logged-in, anon with login/signup buttons, docked).

title: include_website_name is missing the `?` suffix so AMS never calls it
body: ActiveModelSerializers 0.8/0.9 (used by Discourse) only honors filter methods named `include_<attribute>?`. The method is defined as `def include_website_name` (no question mark), so it is never invoked and `website_name` is always serialized — including when `website` is blank, in which case `website_name` returns nil and clients see an explicit `website_name: null`. Rename it to `include_website_name?`.

title: website_name leaks the website domain for TL0 users seen by anonymous visitors
body: The `untrusted_attributes` list hides `website` (and other profile fields) from anonymous viewers of trust-level-0 users, but the new `website_name` attribute was not added to that list and has no `restrict_user_fields?` guard. As a result, an anonymous crawler can still read the domain (or full host+path) of a TL0 user's website via `website_name` even though `website` itself is suppressed, defeating the purpose of the restriction. Add `website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` or gate its inclusion on `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`.

title: website_name returns nil for URLs without a scheme
body: `URI(website.to_s).host` returns nil for scheme-less websites like `example.com/user` (which Discourse accepts and displays). The method then returns nil even though `website` is present, so the profile shows no website name at all for those users. Previously the client-side `website.split("/")[2]` had similar limitations, but the new server-side code should normalize the URL (e.g. prepend `http://` when no scheme) before parsing instead of silently returning nil.

title: Second-level-domain comparison treats unrelated subdomains as the same site
body: The branch comparing `website_host.split('.')[1..-1] == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1]` treats e.g. website `www.wordpress.com` and instance `forum.wordpress.com` (or any two customers of a shared hosting domain) as the same site and exposes the full URL path. The old behavior only showed the host; this change reveals path information for domains that merely share a suffix. Consider using an exact-suffix check (`website_host == discourse_host || website_host.ends_with?('.' + discourse_host) || discourse_host.ends_with?('.' + website_host)`) instead of comparing truncated labels, which also mishandles multi-part TLDs like `example.co.uk`.

title: include_website_name is missing the '?' suffix, so AMS never calls it
body: ActiveModelSerializers filters attributes via methods named `include_<attr>?`. The new method is defined as `def include_website_name` (no question mark), so it is never invoked and `website_name` is always serialized — including as `nil` when the user has no website. The intended guard (`website.present?`) has no effect. Rename it to `include_website_name?`.

title: website_name is not declared an untrusted attribute, leaking TL0 users' websites to anonymous viewers
body: The serializer hides `website` from anonymous viewers of TL0 users via `untrusted_attributes :website, ...`, but the newly added `website_name` attribute is not in that list. Since `website_name` is derived directly from `website`, an anonymous visitor can now read a TL0 user's website host (and path) from the `website_name` field even though `website` itself is correctly suppressed. Add `website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list (and fix the missing `?` on its include method).

title: website_name returns nil for websites without a scheme or with unparseable URLs
body: `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` returns nil for values like `example.com/user` (no scheme — URI parses it as a path, host is nil) or any malformed URL that survives profile validation, causing `website_name` to be nil and the template's `{{#if model.website_name}}` to hide the website link entirely even though `model.website` is present. Previously the client-side code displayed `website.split('/')[2]`, which also degraded, but the new serializer should fall back to the raw `website` string instead of returning nil so the link remains visible.

title: Query string and fragment are dropped from displayed website name
body: When the domains match, the display value is built as `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path`, discarding any query string or fragment. A user whose website is `http://example.com/page?id=5` on the same host will see it displayed as `example.com/page`, which no longer represents the actual URL. Include `URI#query`/`fragment` or use `request_uri` when constructing the display path.

title: String#ends_with? does not exist — NoMethodError when website host is parent of instance host
body: Ruby's String class defines `end_with?`, not `ends_with?`. In the else branch of `website_name` (e.g. website host `example.com` vs instance host `forums.example.com` — exactly the scenario covered by the new spec 'website domain is parent of instance domain'), calling `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` raises NoMethodError, so serializing such a user raises a 500. The new spec for that case would fail with this code; it must be `end_with?`.

title: include_website_name missing '?' suffix, so the inclusion guard never runs
body: ActiveModel::Serializers only consults predicates named `include_<attr>?`. The method is defined as `def include_website_name` (no question mark), so it is ignored and `website_name` is always serialized (as null when the website is blank). Rename it to `include_website_name?`.

title: website_name leaks the website of TL0 users to anonymous viewers
body: `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes`, which hides a TL0 user's profile fields from anonymous visitors (scope.restrict_user_fields?). The new `website_name` attribute is not added to that list and its include guard only checks `website.present?`, so anonymous viewers now receive the TL0 user's website host (and path) via `website_name` even though `website` itself is hidden — defeating the purpose of the restriction. `website_name` should be included in `untrusted_attributes`.

title: Host comparison is case-sensitive and ignores default ports
body: `URI(website.to_s).host` preserves the case of the entered URL (e.g. `http://EXAMPLE.com/user` yields `EXAMPLE.com`), which will not equal `Discourse.current_hostname` and will fall through to the 'different domain' branch, hiding the path. Downcase both hosts before comparing. Additionally `URI(...).host` raises URI::InvalidURIError for URLs without a scheme (e.g. `example.com/user` parses with nil host, so it silently returns nil — acceptable but means scheme-less websites never show a path), which may be worth handling explicitly rather than via a blanket rescue.

title: Light-theme color for embedded-post metadata link changed from 30% to 70% lightness
body: In the diff for .embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a, the old rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The replacement is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. The light-theme branch was changed from 30% to 70%, so on light themes this link becomes much lighter than before — dark-light-choose is supposed to preserve the existing light value and only add the dark variant. This looks like a copy/paste of the complementary values into the wrong branch and will visibly regress light themes.

title: topic-map h3 light-theme color changed from 20% to 50% lightness
body: The mobile .topic-map h3 rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme value changed from 20% to 50%, making the heading noticeably lighter on light themes; the conversion should have kept 20% for the light branch (e.g. paired with 80% on the dark branch, as done for .number/i a few lines below).

title: custom-message-length light-theme color changed from 70% to 30% lightness
body: .custom-message-length was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The light-theme branch went from 70% to 30%, so the character-count hint text becomes much darker on light themes. The two values appear to have been swapped; the desktop version of the same rule uses (70%, 30%) correctly.

title: group-member-info .name light-theme color changed from 30% to 50% lightness
body: In desktop/user.scss the .group-member-info .name rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme value changed from 30% to 50%, unintentionally lightening group member names on light themes (the mobile version of the same rule in mobile/user.scss has the same change). The light branch should have preserved the original 30%.

title: group-member-info .name light-theme color changed from 30% to 50% lightness
body: In mobile/user.scss the .group-member-info .name rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, changing the light-theme rendering rather than only adding a dark-theme alternative. The original 30% lightness should be kept for the light branch.

title: Light-theme color changed from 30% to 70% lightness for embedded post meta-data link
body: The original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The replacement is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, so on light themes the color shifts from a 30%-lightened $primary to a 70%-lightened $primary, making the bold poster-name link in expanded embedded posts much fainter than before. The dark arm (30% of $secondary) is the correct dark-theme counterpart of the original 30%; the light arm should have stayed 30%.

body: Original: `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. New: `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme arm should have remained 30% (with the dark arm derived from $secondary); instead the name in the group member list becomes noticeably lighter on light themes, inconsistent with the neighboring .title which was correctly left at its original 50%.

body: Same issue as the desktop user.scss change: the original `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, altering the light-theme rendering (30% -> 50% lightness) instead of only adding a dark-theme alternative.

body: Original: `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. New: `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme arm jumped from 20% to 50% lightness, so topic-map headings on mobile light themes are much fainter than before; the light arm should have stayed 20% (matching the `.number, i` rule changed a few lines below, which correctly kept 20%).

title: Light-theme color of embedded-post username changed from 30% to 70% lightness
body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a`, the original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The PR changed it to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. body: In mobile/topic-post.scss `.topic-map h3`, the original `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` was replaced with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. body: In mobile/modal.scss `.custom-message-length`, the original `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` was replaced with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. body: In desktop/user.scss `.group-member-info .name`, the original `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` was replaced with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme value changed from 30% to 50% lightness even though the PR only intends to add a dark-theme fallback, so group member names on the user page will render lighter than before on light color schemes.

title: Member routes pass :id but controller requires :group_id, breaking add/remove member
body: The new routes `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` and `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` are declared inside `resources :groups` without a `collection` block, so Rails treats them as member routes: the URL is `/admin/groups/:id/members` and the group id arrives as `params[:id]`. However both `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` and `#remove_member` do `params.require(:group_id)`, which will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` (HTTP 400) for every real request. The JavaScript in `discourse/models/group.js` calls `/admin/groups/<id>/members.json`, matching the member route, so adding or removing a member from the admin UI will always fail. The specs pass because they invoke the controller actions directly with `group_id:` and never exercise the routing. Either wrap the routes in `collection do ... end` (so the client sends `group_id` as a query/body param) or change the controller to use `params[:id]`, and add a request/route-level test.

title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
body: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. For a group whose membership is an exact multiple of the page size (e.g. 100 users with limit 50) this yields 3 pages instead of 2. The 'next' button is then enabled on the real last page; clicking it sets `offset = min(offset + limit, user_count)` = user_count, and `findMembers` fetches an empty page, showing the admin a blank member list with pagination '3/3'.
