If Run() ever returns nil, err.Error() panics in the goroutine and crashes the test binary rather than failing the test cleanly. It should check `if err != nil && err.Error() != ...` or use require.Error. (Not introduced by this PR, but the test is being modified here.)

title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, so passkeys are never offered on a fresh (unauthenticated) login
body: The new helper `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. Both call sites that replaced the old logic (`authenticate()` line 115 and `challenge(context, error, field)` line 137) previously filled the WebAuthn conditional-UI form data when the user was NOT yet set (`context.getUser() == null`) — that is the normal first-login case where passkey autofill (conditional UI) must be offered so the user can sign in with a discoverable credential. With the new condition, `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` only runs when a user is already set in the context (re-authentication), so on a fresh login the `webauth` form / challenge attributes are never rendered and users can no longer log in with passkeys at all. This is exactly the scenario covered by the updated tests asserting `//form[@id='webauth']` is present on the initial login page, which would now fail. The condition should allow the fresh-login case (user == null) as well as the re-authentication case, e.g. by not requiring `user != null` here.

title: Call to no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not match any declared method
body: `UsernameForm.authenticate` now calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the only declaration added by this PR is `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` in `UsernamePasswordForm`. There is no no-arg overload in any changed file, so this does not compile. Presumably the intent was `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` (or a passkeys-enabled check without the user requirement, since at this point `context.getUser()` is known non-null, making the `user != null` check in the helper trivially true).

title: Overridden shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators missing @Override annotation
body: The newly added `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(AuthenticationFlowContext)` overrides the protected method introduced in `WebAuthnAuthenticator` but lacks the `@Override` annotation, so a future signature change in the parent would silently turn this into an unused method instead of a compile error.

title: Conditional passkeys UI no longer rendered on fresh (no-user) login
body: In authenticate(), the new guard `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` requires the user to be non-null before calling `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)`. Previously the form was filled exactly in the opposite case — inside the `else` branch where `context.getUser() == null` (fresh login, no user selected yet). On a normal first login there is no user in the context, so the WebAuthn conditional UI attributes (challenge, rpId, ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI) are never set, the browser never triggers `navigator.credentials.get()` with conditional mediation, and passkey autofill / discoverable-key login on the initial login page silently stops working. The same regression exists in `challenge(context, error, field)` at line 137: for the user-not-found error path (user == null) the webauthn context (including the AUTH_CHALLENGE_NOTE auth note that the webauthn action later reads) is no longer populated, so a subsequent passkey attempt from that error page would fail with a null challenge. The user-null check should not be part of deciding whether to render conditional passkeys; it should only distinguish the re-authentication case.

title: Call to no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not match any declared method
body: UsernameForm.authenticate() now calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the only method added in this PR is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` in the parent class UsernamePasswordForm (line 160). No no-arg overload is declared in UsernamePasswordForm, AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator, or any other file changed in this PR. Unless an overload exists elsewhere, this is a compilation error; if one does exist elsewhere with different semantics, the call site needs to be verified against the new re-authentication behavior introduced here.

title: Absence assertions for webauthn form catch generic Exception
body: reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey verifies the webauthn form is absent with try { findElement(...); fail(); } catch (Exception nsee) { /* expected */ }. Catching generic Exception means any failure — including assertion errors from the MatcherAssert line itself or unrelated WebDriver errors — is silently treated as 'expected', so the test can pass even when the page is broken. Catch NoSuchElementException specifically (as done elsewhere in this same file via Assert.assertThrows).

title: Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() breaks compilation
body: UsernameForm.authenticate() calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the only definition of that method in the hierarchy is `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`, which takes one argument. Neither AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator nor UsernamePasswordForm declares a no-arg overload, so this file does not compile. The intended call was presumably `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`.

title: Conditional passkeys no longer initialized on fresh login (user == null)
body: In authenticate(), the `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` call was moved out of the else branch and is now guarded by `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, which returns false when the user is null. Previously the form was filled exactly in the user == null case (fresh login with no user in context). As a result, on an initial login (no re-authentication), the WebAuthn conditional UI attributes (challenge, rpId, ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI) are never set, so discoverable-key/passkey login on the first login page is broken. The same regression applies to challenge(context, error, field) at line 137: after a failed login attempt where the user was cleared from the context, the passkeys UI will no longer be rendered even though the old code explicitly re-filled it when `context.getUser() == null`.

title: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate evaluates predicate against org-aware wrapped model, skipping needed invalidation
body: In update(), the 'original' model is obtained via getById(), which returns the organization-aware wrapper whose isEnabled() returns false when the linked organization is disabled. The cached getForLogin lists, however, are built from the raw database state (raw enabled flag, BROKER_PUBLIC config), so an IDP of a disabled org is still a member of those cached lists. If such an IDP is then updated in a way that changes its cache membership — for example moving it from org A to org B while both orgs are disabled — getLoginPredicate() returns false for both original and updated, so registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate returns early and never invalidates the login caches. The stale cached lists will then keep serving the IDP for org A's login and omit it for org B (e.g. getForLogin(ORG_ONLY, orgAId) returns an IDP no longer linked to org A). The invalidation predicate should be evaluated against the raw model state, not the org-aware wrapper.

title: Cleanup registers removal of literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP alias
body: In testCacheIDPForLogin (and identically at line 425), the loop creates IDPs named "idp-alias-0" ... "idp-alias-19" but registers cleanup with getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) — the literal string "alias" rather than the loop variable alias. As a result the 20+ created identity providers are never cleaned up and leak into subsequent tests in the same realm (and the cleanup callback itself references a non-existent resource, which may fail at teardown). The same copy-paste defect exists in testCacheIDPByOrg at line 303.

title: No test coverage for ORG_ONLY/ALL with organizationId=null or for unlinking an IDP from an organization
body: The new getForLogin cache has distinct search keys for organizationId=null (empty string) versus a specific org, and the invalidation logic depends on organizationId transitions (null -> org, org -> null). The test only exercises searches with a concrete org id and only covers linking an IDP to an org (via update + addIdentityProvider); it never covers unlinking (org -> null) or cache hits for the null-organization ORG_ONLY/ALL searches, so regressions in those paths (e.g. the wrapped-predicate issue in registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate) would not be caught.

title: Cleanup registers removal of literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP
body: In testCacheIDPForLogin, the loop that creates 20 IDPs registers cleanup with getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) — the string "alias" is a literal, not the loop variable alias ("idp-alias-" + i). The same mistake is repeated at line 425 for "idp-alias-20". As a result the cleanup removes a non-existent IDP named "alias" and the 20+ created identity providers leak into subsequent tests in the class (e.g. testCacheIDPByOrg counts IDPs and can see these leftover brokers), making tests order-dependent and flaky.

title: Login IDP cache is not invalidated when an organization is removed or disabled
body: getForLogin caches IDP id sets per (FetchMode, organizationId), but unlike getByOrganization it never checks isInvalid(orgId), and no invalidation of the cacheKeyForLogin keys is registered when an organization is removed, disabled, or when an IDP is linked/unlinked through the organization API without going through IdentityProviderStorageProvider.update() (the invalidation in registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate only fires on the update() path and relies on the caller passing an updated model with the new organizationId). If an org is deleted or its broker link is changed outside update(), the cached ORG_ONLY/ALL login lists keep returning the old IDP ids, so the login page can show brokers for a removed/disabled organization until the entry is evicted. getByOrganization handles this exact case with the isInvalid(orgId) check; getForLogin should do the same (or org removal/unlink should register invalidation for all login cache keys).

title: getForLogin cache does not honor organization invalidations, unlike getByOrganization
body: In getForLogin, the only staleness check is `isInvalid(cacheKey)` on the realm+mode login key. The analogous cached query method getByOrganization (line 173) additionally checks `isInvalid(orgId)` because organization-level changes (org update, org removal, IDP link/unlink performed through the organization APIs) register invalidations under the organization id, not under IDP cache keys. Any IDP link/unlink or org removal that does not route through IdentityProviderStorageProvider.update() (and therefore never triggers registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate) will leave the cached getForLogin lists stale: e.g. after an organization is removed its formerly-linked IDPs become realm-level login IDPs, but the cached REALM_ONLY list will not contain them and the ORG_ONLY/ALL lists may still reference them, until some unrelated IDP change happens to invalidate the login keys. The method should also consult the organization invalidation (or register login-cache invalidation from the organization provider) before serving cached results.

title: Cleanup registers removal of literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP alias
body: In testCacheIDPForLogin the cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` — the literal string "alias" rather than the loop variable `alias`/"idp-alias-" + i. The same mistake exists for idp-alias-20 (line 425). As a result none of the 21 identity providers created by this test are actually cleaned up (the lookup for alias "alias" finds nothing), leaking IDPs into the shared test realm and potentially affecting other tests that run afterwards in the same class/suite.

title: New abstract method order() breaks all external CryptoProvider implementations
body: The PR adds `int order();` as a new abstract method to the public SPI interface `CryptoProvider`. Any third-party or downstream implementation of this interface (the interface is in keycloak-common and is loaded via ServiceLoader precisely so it can be implemented externally) will now fail to compile, and existing compiled implementations will throw `AbstractMethodError` at runtime when `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider` calls `CryptoProvider::order` during sorting. This should be a `default int order() { return 0; }` (or similar) method to remain backward compatible.

title: Multiple providers with equal order are now silently accepted, can select non-FIPS provider in FIPS setup
body: Previously, `detectProvider` threw an IllegalStateException when more than one CryptoProvider was on the classpath, which was a deliberate guard against misconfiguration. Now the code sorts by `order()` and silently picks the first. `DefaultCryptoProvider`, `WildFlyElytronProvider`, and `FIPS1402Provider` all return order 200, and `Stream.sorted` is stable, so ties are resolved by arbitrary ServiceLoader enumeration order. If both the default (non-FIPS) and the FIPS 140-2 crypto jars end up on the classpath (a realistic packaging mistake), Keycloak will now silently start with whichever provider the classloader happens to return first — potentially the non-FIPS one in a FIPS-required environment — instead of failing fast. The previously ignored providers are only logged at debug level, so this misconfiguration is easy to miss. At minimum, equal-order ties among distinct providers should still be an error (or the FIPS provider should have a strictly higher order and a warning logged at WARN level).

title: Indefinite-length encoding (-1) is not handled, causing silent empty results or NegativeArraySizeException on malformed input
body: `readLength()` returns -1 for BER indefinite-length encoding (0x80). Callers do not handle this: `readSequence()` does `while (length > 0)` and silently returns an empty list for a -1 length (so `asn1derToConcatenatedRS` later fails with the misleading 'Invalid sequence with size different to 2'), and `readNext()` computes `length += reset()` and calls `read(length)` with a negative value, throwing an unhelpful `NegativeArraySizeException` instead of an IOException. Since this decoder parses signature bytes that ultimately come from a remote server, malformed/hostile input should produce a clear IOException. The -1 case should be rejected explicitly in `readLength()` (DER forbids indefinite lengths anyway) or handled by callers.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the default keystore provider, not a BouncyCastle provider
body: `getBouncyCastleProvider()` is implemented as `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, which returns whatever JCA provider services the default keystore type (e.g. the SUN provider), not a BouncyCastle provider. Callers of `CryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider()` reasonably expect a BC/BCFIPS provider and may pass it into BC-specific APIs, which would fail or behave incorrectly in environments where this fallback provider is the one selected (i.e. standalone authz-client use). If no BouncyCastle provider is available, returning null (as WildFlyElytronProvider does) or throwing would be less misleading.

title: New abstract method order() breaks all external CryptoProvider implementations
body: The PR adds `int order();` as an abstract method to the public `CryptoProvider` interface in keycloak-common. Any third-party or downstream implementation of this interface (the interface is explicitly designed for pluggable crypto integrations, e.g. custom FIPS providers) will now fail to compile or throw AbstractMethodError at runtime when the new CryptoIntegration sorting calls order(). Making it a default method (e.g. `default int order() { return 100; }`) would preserve compatibility while still allowing the built-in providers to override it.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns an arbitrary JRE provider, not BouncyCastle
body: AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the provider of the JVM default keystore (typically the SUN provider). Callers of CryptoIntegration.getProvider().getBouncyCastleProvider() reasonably expect a BouncyCastle(-like) provider and pass it to JCE getInstance(..., provider) calls for BC-specific algorithms; with this implementation they will get NoSuchAlgorithmException or silently use a provider that lacks the expected algorithms. If this provider is selected (it wins whenever no other CryptoProvider jar is present, which is exactly the standalone authz-client scenario), any code path touching getBouncyCastleProvider() misbehaves instead of failing clearly. Returning null or throwing UnsupportedOperationException like the other unsupported methods would be safer.

title: readSequence() silently accepts indefinite-length encoding and returns incomplete data
body: ASN1Decoder.readLength() returns -1 for indefinite-length encoding (0x80), and readSequence() uses `while (length > 0)`, so an indefinite-length SEQUENCE is silently parsed as an empty sequence instead of being rejected. The caller in AuthzClientCryptoProvider.asn1derToConcatenatedRS then throws only a misleading 'Invalid sequence with size different to 2'. Since the decoder is only meant to handle DER (which forbids indefinite lengths), readSequence should throw an IOException when readLength() returns -1 to fail loudly on malformed input.

title: Dead code: two ASN1Encoder results discarded in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
body: In concatenatedRSToASN1DER, lines 114-115 create two ASN1Encoder instances and call write(rBigInteger)/write(sBigInteger) on them, but the results are thrown away; the actual encoding is redone in the return statement with fresh encoders. This dead code is confusing and should be removed.

title: Test uses a P-256 key for ES384/ES512 and only asserts round-trip
body: ECDSAAlgorithmTest generates a single default-curve (P-256) EC key pair in the constructor and reuses it for testES384 and testES512, so the signatures being converted were produced by a curve that doesn't match those algorithms' real key sizes. Additionally the test only asserts that derToRS(rsToDer(x)) == x; it never verifies the produced DER against a Signature.verify() or a known-good JWS vector, so a systematically wrong encoding that round-trips would go undetected. Verifying the re-encoded DER with java.security.Signature (initialized with the matching curve key) would make the test meaningful.

title: New abstract order() method breaks all external CryptoProvider implementations
body: The PR adds `int order();` as an abstract method to the public `CryptoProvider` interface in keycloak-common. Any third-party or downstream implementation of this interface (which is the documented SPI for plugging in custom crypto providers) will now fail to compile, and pre-compiled implementations will throw AbstractMethodError when `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider` calls `CryptoProvider::order` during sorting. Since the method is only needed for tie-breaking, it should be declared as a `default int order() { return 0; }` to remain backward compatible.

title: Multiple full providers with equal order() are now silently picked arbitrarily instead of failing
body: Previously, having more than one CryptoProvider on the classpath threw an IllegalStateException ('Multiple crypto providers loaded...'), which caught misconfigurations such as having both the default (BC) and the FIPS1402 provider present. After this change, the code sorts by order() and silently uses the first. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return order() == 200, so if two of them end up on the classpath (e.g. both BC non-FIPS and BC-FIPS jars present), the selected provider depends on ServiceLoader iteration order, which is unspecified. This can silently run the server with the wrong crypto backend (e.g. non-FIPS instead of FIPS), where previously it failed fast. The equal-order case among 'real' providers should still be treated as an error.

title: Dead code in concatenatedRSToASN1DER: two encoder results discarded
body: In `concatenatedRSToASN1DER`, lines 114-115 call `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger)` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger)` and discard the results; the actual encoding is redone below in the `writeDerSeq(...)` call. The discarded calls are confusing leftovers and should be removed (they have no effect other than allocating unused objects).

title: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the default keystore JCA provider, not a BouncyCastle provider
body: `getBouncyCastleProvider()` is documented in CryptoProvider as returning the BouncyCastle security provider (FIPS or non-FIPS). This implementation returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, which is whatever JCA provider implements the default keystore type (e.g. SUN). Any code path that calls this expecting BouncyCastle algorithms (e.g. BouncyIntegration) will get the wrong provider. It would be safer to throw UnsupportedOperationException like the other unsupported methods, or return null explicitly.

title: Client deletion breaks with V2: listener calls ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled which throws UnsupportedOperationException
body: The registerListener handler now runs whenever Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled (which V2 depends on). On ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent it calls management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, AdminPermissions.management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, whose clients() now returns the new ClientPermissionsV2, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled() unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). As a result, deleting any client in a realm with the V2 feature enabled will propagate a RuntimeException from the event listener and fail the client removal (and leave the client-specific authorization resources orphaned). The V2 path needs a no-op/cleanup implementation for client removal, or the listener must skip the clients() call for V2.

title: All-clients permission is ignored whenever a client-specific resource exists
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the all-clients ('Clients' resource type) fallback is only evaluated when resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), ...) returns null. If any client-specific resource exists for that client (e.g. another admin was granted a VIEW permission on that client, which creates the resource), the code evaluates only that resource's permissions and never considers permissions attached to the all-clients resource. An admin holding an all-clients MANAGE/VIEW/CONFIGURE permission would then be denied operations on that specific client, depending on which policies happen to reference the client-specific resource. Both the client-specific resource and the all-clients resource should be evaluated (granted if either matches), as in the V1 implementation where both the typed permission and the per-client permission are checked.

title: Possible null resource passed to policy store when all-clients resource is missing
body: When the client-specific resource is not found, the code calls AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and immediately passes the result to authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource). getResourceTypeResource returns null when the resource is not found by name (e.g. realms where the admin-permissions resource server predates this change and was never re-initialized with the 'Clients' resource, since init() returns early when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null). Existing deployments upgrading to a version with this schema change will not have the 'Clients' resource/scopes created, so this can produce a NullPointerException (or store-specific failure) on every client permission check instead of a clean deny, and the new Clients scopes/resources are never provisioned for existing realms.

title: Dead code: unused getEvaluationContext, logger and TOKEN_EXCHANGE import
body: ClientPermissionsV2 contains a private getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) method that is never called (the only caller would be canExchangeTo, which now throws UnsupportedOperationException), plus an unused static logger field and an unused static import of AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE. This dead code should be removed (or wired in when token exchange is implemented for V2) to avoid confusion about how token-exchange evaluation is supposed to work in V2.

title: Client removal event crashes when both FGAP v1 and v2 features are enabled
body: The event listener now wraps cleanup in `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` and calls `management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false)` on `ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent`. When the v2 feature (ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2) is also enabled, `AdminPermissions.management()` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2`, whose `clients()` now returns the new `ClientPermissionsV2`, and `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled()` unconditionally throws `UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. Because this runs inside a ProviderEventListener during client deletion, deleting any client in such a deployment will blow up with an UnsupportedOperationException (or leave the deletion inconsistent). The v2 path needs its own no-op/cleanup handling instead of routing through a method that always throws.

title: Per-client resource lookup uses resource server id as owner while resources are created with client id as owner
body: `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` looks up the per-client resource via `resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId())`, i.e. with owner = `server.getId()`. However `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource()` creates these resources with `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId())`, i.e. owner = the client's id (`resourceServer.getClientId()`), which is a different value from the resource server's id. If the store filters by owner when a non-null owner is passed, the per-client resource created for a specific Clients permission will never be found here, so evaluation silently falls back to the all-clients resource and per-client grants/denies (e.g. a negative permission on one client) are ignored. Either pass `null`/the same owner used at creation time, or make creation and lookup consistent.

title: Possible null resource dereferenced in findByResource for all-clients fallback
body: When no per-client resource exists, the code does `resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE);` and immediately calls `authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource)`. `getResourceTypeResource()` can return `null` (it returns null when the resource store has no resource named 'Clients', e.g. for a resource server created before this schema type existed or after a failed init), so `findByResource(server, null)` will throw an NPE instead of simply denying permission. Add a null check on the returned resource before querying policies.

title: getResourceName not extended for the new Clients resource type
body: `getResourceName()` only special-cases the Users resource type. For the newly added Clients type, per-client resources are stored with the client's UUID as the resource name (see `resolveClient` returning `client.getId()`), but the method falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`, which is typically null for these programmatically created resources. Any UI/API that renders permission resource names (e.g. the admin console permission list) will show nothing or a raw UUID instead of the client's clientId. Add a Clients branch resolving the client and returning its clientId, mirroring the Users branch.

title: Javadoc for requireView()/requireViewClientScopes() describes return values for void methods
body: The newly added Javadoc for `requireView()` says "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}" and `requireViewClientScopes()` similarly says "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}", but both methods are `void` and throw ForbiddenException on failure. The documentation is copy-pasted from the boolean accessors and misstates the contract; it should say it throws ForbiddenException if the corresponding can* method returns false, as done for the other require* methods.

title: setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException and breaks client deletion in V2
body: AdminPermissions.registerListener (unchanged in behavior, services/.../AdminPermissions.java line 91) calls management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) on every ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent whenever the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature is enabled. With this PR, when the V2 feature is on, MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled (and isPermissionsEnabled) unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). The exception is thrown from a ProviderEventListener during client removal, so deleting any client in a realm with admin fine-grained authz V2 enabled will fail/roll back. The V2 implementation should no-op these legacy methods instead of throwing.

title: Possible NullPointerException when the 'Clients' all-resource does not exist
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no per-client resource is found, the code falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE), which returns null when the resource named 'Clients' is absent from the resource server (getResourceTypeResource returns null if resourceStore.findByName finds nothing). The result is passed directly into authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) without a null check, which will NPE instead of returning false. Contrast with hasPermission(String) a few lines below, which does check for null before evaluating. A missing or corrupted 'Clients' resource therefore turns every client permission check into a 500 error.

title: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changed from 4 to 3, breaking existing automation
body: This PR redefines RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 and repurposes 4 as FEATURE_DISABLED. The update-compatibility command is already shipped (as preview) and the docs explicitly tell users to build automation around the exit codes ('consumers... should rely only on the exit code of the check command'). Any existing script or pipeline that treats exit code 4 as 'recreate upgrade required' will silently misbehave after this change: a real recreate situation now returns 3 (which their script may treat as an unknown/unexpected error, or worse, ignore), and a feature-disabled run returns 4, which old scripts would interpret as 'shut down the deployment for a recreate upgrade' even though nothing is actually incompatible. Even for a preview feature, silently remapping an already-documented contract value warrants an explicit release note / migration note, or choosing a new unused code for FEATURE_DISABLED instead of renumbering.

title: Caution claims the Operator fails without rolling-updates feature, contradicting default-strategy behavior
body: The new CAUTION block states: 'While on preview stage, the feature rolling-updates must be enabled. Otherwise, the Keycloak Operator will fail.' However, the default behavior (update strategy not set) intentionally mimics Keycloak 26.1 and works without the feature: the modified UpgradeTest.createInitialDeployment only enables the rolling-updates feature when an explicit update strategy is configured, and the null-strategy parameterized runs (testImageChange / testCacheMaxCount) deploy and roll successfully without the feature. As written, the doc tells users the operator will break unless they enable a preview feature, which is incorrect for anyone not using spec.update.strategy and will cause unnecessary enablement of a preview feature (or panic). The caution should be scoped to 'when spec.update.strategy is set' or reworded.

title: testFeatureNotEnabled does not assert exit code 4
body: The new test for the feature-disabled path only asserts the error message text. The PR introduces a dedicated exit code (CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED = 4) and documents it in update-compatibility.adoc as part of the scriptable contract, but no test verifies that the metadata/check commands actually exit with code 4 when the feature is disabled (nor that the check command exits with 3 on incompatibility in testWrongVersions). A regression that returns code 0 or the generic error code 1 in these paths would go unnoticed while breaking consumers that rely on the documented exit codes.

title: testCacheMaxCount(null) expects a rolling upgrade but never enables the rolling-updates feature
body: In UpgradeTest, createInitialDeployment returns early when updateStrategy is null (line 105-107), so the Keycloak CR for the null-strategy case never gets Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES added to spec.features.enabled. However, testCacheMaxCount expects eventuallyRollingUpgradeStatus when the strategy is null. With this PR, the update-compatibility check command now exits with code 4 (FEATURE_DISABLED) and prints 'The preview feature rolling-updates is not enabled' when the feature is off, so the operator can no longer report a rolling upgrade for that deployment. The null-strategy parameterized invocation of testCacheMaxCount will therefore fail/timeout waiting for a rolling-upgrade status that can never occur.

title: Feature-disabled test does not assert the new exit code 4
body: testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the error message. The PR introduces a new, documented exit code (CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED = 4) that automation is supposed to rely on (the docs tell users to rely only on exit codes), but no test verifies that the command actually exits with 4 when the feature is disabled. A regression that returns the wrong exit code would go unnoticed.

title: Feature check runs before CLI validation, masking usage errors with exit code 4
body: In `run()`, the `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES)` check executes before `validateConfig()`. As a result, an invocation with invalid usage (e.g. missing the required `--file` argument) made while the feature is disabled exits with code 4 (`FEATURE_DISABLED`) and never reports the actual usage problem, even though the documentation in `update-compatibility.adoc` states exit code 2 signals an invalid CLI option and exit code 1 an unexpected error. Scripts keying on exit codes cannot distinguish 'feature disabled' from 'you invoked the command wrongly'. The same ordering exists in `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()`. Consider running the feature check after CLI validation, or documenting that the feature check takes precedence.

title: Default (null) update strategy path deploys without rolling-updates feature, leaving new operator requirement untested
body: The docs added in this PR state that while `rolling-updates` is in preview, the Keycloak Operator will fail if the feature is not enabled. However, `createInitialDeployment(null)` returns early without enabling the feature, so the default-strategy test case runs with the feature disabled. If the operator's default path indeed requires the feature (as the docs caution implies), this test would fail against such an operator; if the default path deliberately does not require it, there is no test asserting the operator's failure behavior when `spec.update.strategy` is set without enabling `rolling-updates`. A test covering the 'strategy set but feature disabled' failure case is missing.

title: canManage() grants manage access to admins holding only the 'view' scope on Groups
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the fallback checks hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE), i.e. the VIEW scope alone satisfies canManage(). GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() guards group creation with auth.groups().requireManage(), so any admin who has been granted only the 'view' scope on the all-groups resource (or who matches a view permission) can create new top-level groups in the realm. canManage() should only check the MANAGE scope (compare canView() on line 52, which correctly checks VIEW and MANAGE).

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() mixes up authorization Resource IDs with group IDs
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), the callback passes groupResource.getId() (the authorization store Resource ID) into hasPermission(), which does resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId) — but per-group resources are named by the group ID (see AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup/getOrCreateResource), so findByName with the Resource ID finds nothing and silently falls back to the all-groups resource evaluation. Worse, granted.add(groupResource.getId()) adds the Resource store ID, not the group ID. Callers (UsersResource.searchForUser, BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser, UsersResource.getUsersCount) put this set into the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute / count queries to filter users by group membership, so the filter uses non-existent group IDs and a fine-grained admin with view-members/manage-members permission on a group will see zero users instead of that group's members.

title: Possible NPE when the all-groups resource does not exist
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission(), when no per-group resource is found, resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE) can return null (getResourceTypeResource returns null when the resource type resource is not found in the store, e.g. the admin-permissions client schema was not initialized for this resource server). The next line calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) without a null check, causing a NullPointerException instead of cleanly denying access. UserPermissionsV2 has the same pattern, but there the 'Users' resource is guaranteed by V1 initialization; for the newly added Groups type the all-groups resource may not exist on older realms that enabled admin permissions before this schema change.

title: canManage() grants manage access to admins holding only the view scope
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the fallback evaluation is `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, i.e. it returns true when the caller has only the 'view' scope on the all-groups resource. An admin granted a view-all-groups permission (but not manage) would therefore pass `requireManage()` and be allowed to create top-level groups via GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup, and any other code path relying on groups().canManage(). The scope list should only contain MANAGE.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
body: GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() adds `groupResource.getId()` to the returned set. The returned set is consumed by UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource as `UserModel.GROUPS` session attribute and passed to `session.users().getUsersCount(realm, ..., groupIds)`, where the values must be group IDs used to filter users by group membership. In the V2 schema the group ID is stored as the resource *name* (AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup returns group.getId() as the resource name), while resource.getId() is the internal UUID of the authorization resource. As a result, admins who should see users through group view-members/manage-members permissions will get empty user lists and zero counts because the membership filter uses non-existent group IDs. It should add `groupResource.getName()`.

title: findByType("Groups") matches no per-group resources because V2 resources are created without a type
body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() iterates `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)`. However, per-group V2 resources are created in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource(), which never calls `resource.setType(resourceType)` (unlike the V1 GroupPermissions.initialize() that sets type "Group", and unlike the all-resource entries created in init() where the type is set from the ResourceRepresentation). So per-group resources have a null type and findByType("Groups") will only ever return the single all-groups resource — individual group view-members/manage-members permissions are never discovered, breaking user listing for group-scoped admins. Either set the type when creating resources in getOrCreateResource, or look resources up differently.

title: Possible null resource passed to policyStore.findByResource when all-groups resource is missing
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission(), when no per-group resource exists, `resource` is set to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)`, which returns null when the 'Groups' all-resource has not been created (e.g. the admin-permissions client was initialized before this schema version, or the resource was deleted). The very next statement calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` with that possibly-null resource, and after that `new ResourcePermission(resource, resource.getScopes(), server)` would NPE as well. The same pattern exists in UserPermissionsV2, but this new code repeats it; it should null-check the type resource before using it.

title: canManage() grants manage on view-only permission
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the fallback check is `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)` — it treats the VIEW scope as sufficient for manage. An administrator who only has an all-groups permission with the `view` scope (and no manage-users role) will have canManage() return true. This is used by GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup (requireManage()) to authorize creating top-level groups, so a view-only admin can create (and, via the same check elsewhere, potentially modify) groups. The VIEW scope should be removed from this check; only MANAGE should satisfy canManage().

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses authz resource ID instead of group ID
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), the callback calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` and `granted.add(groupResource.getId())`. However, hasPermission(groupId, ...) looks the resource up with `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, and in the V2 schema the resource *name* is the group ID (set by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource), while resource.getId() is the internal authorization-resource UUID. Passing the UUID means findByName never matches the specific group resource (it silently falls back to the all-groups resource), and the returned set contains authz resource IDs rather than group IDs. This set is consumed by UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource as the UserModel.GROUPS filter and by getUsersCount, so admins whose user visibility comes from group view-members/manage-members permissions will get wrong (empty) user lists and counts. It should use `groupResource.getName()` in both places.

title: Per-group resources created without resource type
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() creates resources via `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, ...)` and updates scopes, but never calls `resource.setType(...)` (unlike the V1 group permissions which set type "Group", and unlike init() which sets the type on the all-resources). GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() queries `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)`; per-group resources created through this path have a null type and will never be returned by that query, so group-specific view-members permissions are ignored when computing the groups with view permission.

title: No upgrade path for realms that already have an admin-permissions client
body: The Groups resource type, its all-groups resource, and the new scopes (manage-membership, manage-members, view-members) are only created in AdminPermissionsSchema.init(), which runs only when the admin-permissions client is first created for a realm. Realms that enabled admin permissions before this change already have the client, so init() returns early and the "Groups" resource and group scopes never exist. In that state GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission() calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` with `resource` being null (getResourceTypeResource returns null), causing a NullPointerException on any group permission evaluation, and getOrCreateResource for a Groups resource would fail with ModelException("No scopes found."). A migration/update path for existing admin-permissions clients is needed.

title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
body: The key `totpStep1` in the Lithuanian (lt) account message bundle was changed from a Lithuanian sentence to `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian, not Lithuanian. Lithuanian users of the account console will see an Italian instruction during TOTP setup. This looks like the English source text ('Install one of the following applications on your mobile:') was machine-translated into the wrong target language. It should be replaced with an actual Lithuanian translation.

title: Lithuanian login translation replaced with Italian text
body: The key `loginTotpStep1` in the Lithuanian (lt) login message bundle was changed to `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian, not Lithuanian. Lithuanian users will see Italian text on the TOTP setup page of the login flow. It should be a Lithuanian translation of 'Install one of the following applications on your mobile:'.

title: Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) message replaced with Traditional Chinese text
body: The key `totpStep1` in the zh_CN (Simplified Chinese) account bundle was changed to `在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：`, which uses Traditional Chinese characters (手機, 安裝, 應用程式) while the rest of the file is Simplified Chinese (compare the login zh_CN file, which uses `在您的移动设备中安装以下任意一个应用：` for the same message). Simplified-Chinese users will see inconsistent, effectively wrong-locale text on the TOTP setup page.

title: Email-file detection uses fragile substring match on file path
body: `normalizeValue` strips ` style="direction: rtl;"` whenever `file.getAbsolutePath().contains("email")` is true. This matches any directory or file name containing the substring 'email' anywhere in the path (e.g., a theme directory named 'emails' or a custom path containing 'email'), not just the intended `theme/base/email/messages` location. In such a case the verifier would silently normalize away a legitimate style attribute and hide a real HTML mismatch. The check should match the path segment explicitly (e.g., a regex on `theme/base/email/` or a path component equals 'email').

title: error-invalid-multivalued-size switched to {0}/{choice} syntax in a JS bundle that uses {{ }} interpolation
body: All other messages in the admin-ui and account-ui property files use the i18next `{{0}}` placeholder syntax (e.g. `'{{0}}' must have maximal value of {{2}}.`). This change rewrites `error-invalid-multivalued-size` to Java MessageFormat syntax (`{0}`, `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}`). If the React apps render this message via i18next, the placeholders and the choice expression will not be interpolated and users will see the literal raw string, including the `{2,choice,...}` expression. The same change was applied to `js/apps/account-ui/.../messages_en.properties` (line 188). Unless the JS apps have explicitly added MessageFormat support for this key, the server-style choice format belongs only in the Java theme bundles under `themes/`, not in the JS bundles.

title: Lithuanian totpStep1 replaced with Italian text
body: In the Lithuanian message bundle, `totpStep1` was changed from a Lithuanian sentence (with legitimate anchor links) to the Italian sentence 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'. Lithuanian users will now see an Italian instruction on the TOTP setup page. The same wrong-language replacement was made for `loginTotpStep1` in `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties` (line 71). These should be proper Lithuanian translations of the new English source text.

title: Simplified Chinese bundle now contains Traditional Chinese characters
body: The zh_CN (Simplified Chinese) account bundle's `totpStep1` was changed to '在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：', which uses Traditional Chinese characters (手機/應用程式/安裝 instead of 手机/应用程序/安装). All other messages in this file use Simplified Chinese, so this introduces an inconsistent, wrong-script translation for mainland Chinese users.

title: Locale-stripping regex character class also matches [ \\ ] ^ _
body: The pattern `_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties` uses the character class `[a-zA-Z-_]`, where `Z-_` is a range that also includes the characters `[`, `\`, `]`, `^`, and `_`. On Windows, absolute paths contain `\` separators, so the greedy `*` can match across directory boundaries and produce a wrong English file path (e.g. consuming a backslash and parts of parent directories when a path segment contains an underscore followed by `.properties`). It would be safer to use an explicit class like `[a-zA-Z_-]` or to derive the English file name from the file name only rather than from the whole absolute path.

title: Missing English reference file crashes the build with an unhelpful RuntimeException
body: `verifySafeHtml()` computes the English counterpart path and opens it unconditionally; if it does not exist (e.g. a new translated properties file is added before its `_en` counterpart, or the path mapping above mis-resolves), a plain `RuntimeException("unable to read file ...")` is thrown instead of a `MojoExecutionException`. Unlike `verify()`, which wraps IO errors into `MojoExecutionException`, this escapes the mojo's error handling and aborts the build with a raw stack trace instead of a clean verification error message. The same applies to the target bundle read at line 67.

title: Locale-stripping regex matches from the first underscore, not the locale separator
body: The expression `replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")` searches for the leftmost match in the whole file name, and the character class `[a-zA-Z-_]` allows letters and underscores anywhere, including the base name. For a file like `changedAnchor_de.properties`, the leftmost `_` is the one before `Anchor`, so the match is `_Anchor_de.properties` and the derived English file becomes `changed_en.properties` — which does not exist. The same applies to the `noHtml_de.properties` fixture, which resolves to `no_en.properties`. As a result the new tests `verifyNoChangedAnchors` and `verifyNoHtmlAllowed` will fail with `RuntimeException: unable to read file ...` instead of asserting the intended message. It works for production files only because they are all named `messages_<locale>.properties`. The regex should anchor to the locale suffix at the end, e.g. `_[a-z]{2}([_-][A-Za-z]{2})?\\.properties$`, or strip the suffix via `lastIndexOf('_')`.

title: Lithuanian totpStep1 replaced with Italian text
body: In the Lithuanian account messages file, `totpStep1` was changed to `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian, not Lithuanian. Lithuanian users will see an Italian sentence in the TOTP setup instructions. The same wrong text was also written to the Lithuanian login file (`loginTotpStep1` in `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties`, line 71), so it looks like a copy-paste from the Italian translation. Both entries should be replaced with a proper Lithuanian translation of the new English source 'Install one of the following applications on your mobile:'.

title: zh_CN totpStep1 written in Traditional Chinese characters
body: In the Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) account messages file, the new `totpStep1` value `在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：` uses Traditional Chinese characters (手機, 裝, 應用程式) that are inconsistent with the rest of the file, which is written in Simplified Chinese (e.g. 打开应用扫描二维码输入验证码 directly below). Simplified Chinese readers will notice mixed scripts; the string should be rewritten in Simplified Chinese, e.g. 在您的手机上安装以下应用之一：.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted condition and wrong substring indices
body: The new isAccessTokenId matcher contains `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. Two problems: (1) the condition is inverted — it returns false (no match) precisely when the grant shortcut equals the expected one, so the matcher only passes for tokens with the WRONG grant shortcut; (2) the indices are wrong — the encoded prefix is 6 chars with the grant shortcut at positions 4-5, so it should be substring(4, 6), not substring(3, 5) (which captures the 2nd token-type char plus the 1st grant char). As written, every updated assertion (expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectAuthReqIdToToken) will fail against correctly encoded token IDs, breaking the tests that use them.

title: Constructor null-checks grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId
body: In the AccessTokenContext constructor, the fourth check is `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` — it re-checks grantType instead of rawTokenId. As a result, rawTokenId can be null, which later causes encodeTokenId() to produce token IDs ending in 'null' (string concatenation of a null rawTokenId) and getTokenContextFromTokenId('...:') to behave inconsistently. The check should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`.

title: Public copy constructor Context(Context) removed from OAuth2GrantType.Context
body: The PR deletes the public copy constructor `Context(Context context)` from OAuth2GrantType.Context and replaces it with a grantType field initialized in the main constructor. Any existing custom OAuth2GrantType provider (or internal caller) that wraps/decorates a context via `new Context(existingContext)` will fail to compile after upgrade. If the removal is intentional, note it as a breaking change; otherwise keep the copy constructor and have it also copy the grantType field.

title: Lightweight-token flag derived from session context client, not the token's client
body: initToken now calls DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext, which determines lightweight vs regular via AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session), reading `session.getContext().getClient()`. In flows where the context client differs from the client the token is issued for (e.g. token exchange sets the requester in the context), the encoded token-type flag can reflect the wrong client. Worth verifying and adding a test that a token issued for a lightweight-token client is encoded as 'lt' in these flows.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted grant check and wrong substring offsets
body: The new isAccessTokenId matcher is broken in two ways. First, the grant shortcut is at characters 4-5 of the 6-char prefix (e.g. "onrtac" -> "ac"), but the code uses items[0].substring(3, 5), which yields "ta" and never equals any grant shortcut. Second, the condition is inverted: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns false (no match) when the shortcut *does* equal the expected one. The combined effect is that the matcher accepts any token ID regardless of grant type (since the substring never matches, the inverted check never triggers), so expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectAuthReqIdToToken/expectDeviceCodeToToken no longer actually verify the encoded grant type. If someone later fixes only the offset, the inverted condition would make all these tests fail. The check should be `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

title: Constructor null-check validates grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId
body: In the AccessTokenContext constructor, the fourth check is `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` — it checks grantType again instead of rawTokenId. As a result, rawTokenId may be null, which would later produce token IDs like "onrtac:null" in encodeTokenId, or a null rawTokenId from getTokenContextFromTokenId without any error. The line should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`.

title: Token exchange sets GRANT_TYPE attribute after access token may already be built in other exchange paths
body: In StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient, `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE)` is set only here; however the TokenManager.initToken that encodes the grant type into the token ID runs inside responseBuilder.generateAccessToken(), which is fine for this path. But other token-exchange providers (e.g. AbstractTokenExchangeProvider subclasses such as the legacy/standard V1 exchange and subject-impersonation flows) also generate access tokens via the TokenManager without setting Constants.GRANT_TYPE on the client session context, so their tokens will be encoded with grant "na" instead of "te". Given the PR's stated goal (token-exchange use case #37117 relying on the grant type in the token ID), tokens issued by those exchange paths will carry the wrong/unknown grant. Also note the import of TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory added in this file is unused.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher rejects exactly the token IDs it should accept
body: The new matcher in `isAccessTokenId` has two defects. First, the condition is inverted: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns false (no match) when the grant shortcut IS the expected one, and falls through to match for any other grant. Every call site (expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectAuthReqIdToToken) passes the shortcut that will actually be present, so all of these event assertions will fail on valid tokens. Second, the offset is wrong: the 6-char context is sessionType(0-1) + tokenType(2-3) + grantType(4-5), so the grant shortcut is at substring(4, 6), not substring(3, 5). With the inverted logic fixed, the code as written would compare chars 3-4 (second char of token type + first char of grant shortcut) and never match any valid grant shortcut. It should be `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

title: Duplicate null-check on grantType leaves rawTokenId unvalidated
body: The constructor contains `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null grantType not allowed");` twice in a row (lines 72-73), and the second one has the message "Null rawTokenId not allowed" but still checks grantType. As a result, rawTokenId is never null-checked despite the intent, and a null rawTokenId would produce a token ID ending in "null" or cause a later NPE in encodeTokenId. The second check should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`.

title: Copy constructor Context(Context) removed without replacement
body: The diff removes the public copy constructor `public Context(Context context)` from OAuth2GrantType.Context and adds the grantType field only to the primary constructor. Any existing code (in Keycloak itself or in custom OAuth2GrantType provider implementations deployed by users) that wraps or re-creates a Context via `new Context(existingContext)` will no longer compile, and the new grantType field would also be lost by such a copy even if re-added manually. This is an SPI interface in server-spi-private, but the removal is a silent breaking change that should either be restored (copying grantType as well) or called out.

title: Token ID encoding applied to every AccessToken including paths where GRANT_TYPE context is never set
body: initToken now unconditionally encodes the token ID via the encoder, reading Constants.GRANT_TYPE from the ClientSessionContext. That attribute is only set in the OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse path, ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType, PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType, StandardTokenExchangeProvider, and refresh validation. Tokens created through other paths that call createClientAccessToken — e.g. the implicit/hybrid flow in AuthorizationEndpoint, or any custom protocol/token service calling TokenManager directly — will silently get grant type "na" baked into the token ID. That may be acceptable, but more critically, any AccessToken whose context yields an unknown grant type that is not in the encoder's shortcut map causes encodeTokenId to throw IllegalStateException, failing token issuance with a 500. If a deployment adds a grant-type-like flow that sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE to a value not registered as an OAuth2GrantType (or sets it before the factory's maps are populated/refreshed in a cluster where provider registration differs), token creation breaks entirely. The encoder should fall back to the "na" shortcut instead of throwing when encoding.

title: Recovery codes stored in user storage are never consumed and can be reused
body: When recovery codes are stored in local (Keycloak DB) storage, RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.isValid() removes the used code so each code is single-use. With this change, when the credential lives in a federated user storage, validation goes through user.credentialManager().isValid(), which only delegates to the storage provider's CredentialInputValidator.isValid() — a read-only check that cannot mutate or remove the used code. There is no subsequent updateCredential call to persist the consumption either. As a result, a recovery code backed by user storage remains valid forever and can be replayed indefinitely, defeating the one-time-use security property of recovery codes.

title: removeStoredCredentialById does not remove a federated recovery-codes credential when all codes are used
body: After the change, RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential() can return a credential coming from federated user storage. When allCodesUsed() is true, the code calls authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(...), which only removes credentials from Keycloak's local storage; for a federated credential this is a no-op (the id is not a locally stored credential). The exhausted credential therefore remains in the user storage and will keep being returned by getFederatedCredentialsStream(). To remove it from user storage the code would need disableCredentialType / a provider-side removal path.

title: Raw (unhashed) recovery codes are handed to user storage, unlike local storage which stores hashes
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes the raw generated codes (JsonSerialization.writeValueAsString(generatedCodes)) into a UserCredentialModel and passes it to user.credentialManager().updateCredential(). When the credential ends up in local storage, RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel stores each code hashed (RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.hashRawCode). When it ends up in user storage, the external provider receives and — as the updated BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage demonstrates — persists the plaintext codes, and validates them with plain string equality. Any user storage following this contract will hold recovery codes in cleartext, so a compromise of the external store exposes all valid recovery codes, a weaker security posture than the local-storage path with no documentation warning about it.

title: Optional.get() on credential lookup throws NoSuchElementException instead of a handled error when credential is absent
body: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) may return Optional.empty() (e.g., the credential was removed between configuredFor() and form rendering, or a federated provider's getCredentials() failed to deserialize and silently dropped the entry, as BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage does on IOException). Calling credentialModelOpt.get() then throws NoSuchElementException, producing an unhandled 500 error on the login page instead of a graceful authentication error. The code should handle the empty case explicitly.

title: removeStoredCredentialById cannot delete federated recovery-code credentials
body: The lookup was changed to RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(), which now also returns credentials from federated user storage (getFederatedCredentialsStream). However, when all codes are used the code still calls authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(...), which only removes credentials from Keycloak's local storage. For a user whose recovery codes live in a federated user storage, the removal silently does nothing: the 'all codes used' credential persists in the user storage, and every subsequent login will keep re-adding the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action while the stale credential remains. The deletion path needs to handle federated credentials (e.g., via disableCredentialType/updateCredential on the user storage) or skip removal when the credential is federated.

title: Used recovery codes in user storage are never consumed, allowing replay
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential stores the raw generated codes (JSON-serialized plaintext list) in the user storage via UserCredentialModel. Unlike the local keycloak-recovery-authn-codes provider, whose isValid() marks a code as used and persists the updated credential, a federated user storage only validates the presented code against the stored list (see BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid, which does anyMatch without removing anything). Because no updated credential is written back after a successful authentication, a recovery code stored in user storage remains valid forever and can be reused by anyone who has seen it, defeating the one-time-use semantics of recovery codes. Additionally, the codes are transmitted to and held by the user storage as plaintext rather than the hashed form used in local storage, which weakens the at-rest protection for federated stores.

title: Recovery codes stored in user storage are never consumed after successful use
body: When the recovery-codes credential lives in a federated user storage, validation goes through user.credentialManager().isValid(...), which delegates to the storage's CredentialInputValidator.isValid(). Unlike the local RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider (which removes the used code from the stored credential as part of isValid), a federated storage has no update hook here, so the used code remains valid forever. Consequences: the same recovery code can be replayed indefinitely, getNextRecoveryAuthnCode() always returns the first code, and allCodesUsed() never becomes true, so the cleanup/re-enrollment logic below never triggers for federated users. The PR's own test storage (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid) demonstrates this: it only checks membership in the stored list without removing the used code.

title: removeStoredCredentialById cannot remove a federated recovery-codes credential
body: When all codes are used, the code calls authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId()). For a credential that was found via getFederatedCredentialsStream() (the new RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential path), removeStoredCredentialById only operates on the local store, so the federated credential is never deleted. The storage would need disableCredentialType/updateCredential semantics instead; as written the exhausted credential silently persists in the user storage.

title: Raw (unhashed) recovery codes sent to user storage while local storage hashes them
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes the plaintext generatedCodes list into the UserCredentialModel challenge response sent to user.credentialManager().updateCredential(). Any user storage implementing CredentialInputUpdater will therefore persist the raw recovery codes, whereas the local RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider stores only hashed codes. This creates an inconsistent security posture (plaintext recovery codes in external stores) with no documentation or warning to storage implementers that they are expected to hash/protect the value themselves.

title: Reader thread is never joined, so the assertion races with in-flight reads
body: createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti() starts a background thread that loops until deletedAll is set, then the main thread sets deletedAll.set(true) and immediately asserts caughtExceptions is empty without joining the thread. The reader thread can still be inside groups() when the assertion runs; an exception thrown by that final in-flight iteration is added to caughtExceptions after the assertion has already passed, so the regression this test is meant to catch can be silently missed (false positive). The thread should be joined before asserting.

title: Shared admin client used concurrently from two threads can produce unrelated failures
body: The reader thread and the main thread both use managedRealm.admin() (the same injected admin client / realm resource) concurrently. Keycloak's admin client is not thread-safe with respect to token refresh, so this test can fail intermittently for reasons unrelated to the NPE being fixed (e.g., concurrent token refresh errors recorded in caughtExceptions), making it flaky in CI. Consider using a separate admin client instance in the reader thread.

title: getSubGroupsCount() now returns null for a deleted group, risking NPE in callers that unbox the Long
body: The fix replaces the NPE inside getSubGroupsCount() with 'return model == null ? null : model.getSubGroupsCount();'. While GroupRepresentation.setSubGroupCount accepts null, any other caller that unboxes the returned Long (e.g., arithmetic or comparison on getSubGroupsCount()) will now get a NullPointerException exactly in the concurrent-deletion scenario this PR is addressing. Other group model implementations never return null here (they return the actual count or 0), so returning 0 (or the cached subgroup set size) would preserve the contract more safely.

title: Reader thread is never joined before asserting on caughtExceptions, making the test racy and leaky
body: In createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti, after deletedAll.set(true) the test immediately asserts assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty()) without joining the reader thread. The reader thread may still be in the middle of a groups() request when deletedAll flips, so an NPE thrown by that in-flight request is added to caughtExceptions after the assertion has already passed — the very race this test is meant to catch can be missed, and the test can pass while the bug still reproduces. Additionally the raw thread is never joined or interrupted, so it keeps making admin requests after the test method (and possibly the class' realm) is torn down, which can cause flaky failures in later tests. The thread should be joined before asserting.

title: Concurrent-deletion NPE remains in the paginated getSubGroupsStream variants
body: The PR fixes the NPE in getSubGroupsCount by null-checking modelSupplier.get(), but the same race exists in the three adjacent methods: getSubGroupsStream(String, Integer, Integer) at line 256, getSubGroupsStream(Integer, Integer) at line 262, and getSubGroupsStream(String, Boolean, Integer, Integer) at line 268 all dereference modelSupplier.get() directly. modelSupplier is a LazyModel over getGroupModel(), which returns null when the group has been deleted concurrently (exactly the scenario of issue #40368). When that happens these methods still throw a NullPointerException, so the fix is incomplete for concurrent group deletion.

title: getSubGroupsCount now silently returns null on concurrent deletion instead of failing fast
body: With this change, getSubGroupsCount returns null when the underlying group has been concurrently deleted. Every other accessor in GroupAdapter that encounters a missing delegate either falls back to cached data or throws IllegalStateException("Not found in database") (see getDelegateForUpdate/isUpdated), while getRoleMappingsStream/getSubGroupsStream detect staleness and delegate to the DB. Returning a null Long here is inconsistent and will surface as a silently missing subGroupCount in GroupRepresentation (populated via GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount), which callers may not distinguish from a genuinely unknown count, and could NPE any code that auto-unboxes the result. Consider aligning the behavior with the rest of the adapter (throw or delegate) rather than returning null.

title: Reader thread is never joined, making the final assertion racy
body: In `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`, the background thread reading groups is started but never joined. After `deletedAll.set(true)`, the main thread immediately asserts `caughtExceptions` is empty, but the reader thread may still be in the middle of its last `groups(...)` call and can add an exception to `caughtExceptions` after the assertion has passed (a false negative), or the JVM may exit with the thread still running. The test should keep a reference to the Thread, set the flag, call `thread.join()` (with a timeout), and only then assert on `caughtExceptions`.

title: Reader thread spins in a tight loop and can leak if the test fails early
body: The background thread loops `while (!deletedAll.get())` with no sleep and no bound, and `deletedAll` is only set at the end of the happy path. If group creation or deletion throws (e.g. the `fail(...)` in the create loop), the thread runs forever, keeping the test JVM busy hammering the server with `groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)` requests. Wrapping the delete loop in try/finally to always set the flag (and joining the thread) would make the test robust.

title: getSubGroupsCount now silently returns null for a deleted group instead of failing
body: The change converts an NPE into a `null` return when the group has been concurrently deleted (`modelSupplier.get()` returns null). Callers such as `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount` then serialize `subGroupCount: null` for a group that no longer exists, masking the deletion rather than surfacing it (every other accessor in this class throws `IllegalStateException("Not found in database")` in that situation). If returning a representation for a deleted group is acceptable this is fine, but the inconsistency is worth a conscious decision — e.g. returning 0 or skipping the group would be clearer contract behavior.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate by datetime; it crashes on the first page
body: The audit log endpoint uses OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime", but OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does `math.floor(value)` / `math.ceil(value)` directly on the attribute value, which is a Python datetime object. math.floor/datetime raises TypeError (an integer is required). get_item_key is invoked by build_cursor on every result set (via _build_next_values/_build_prev_values), so the very first request using ?optimized_pagination=true will 500. This paginator needs the same epoch-milliseconds conversion DateTimePaginator performs (strftime('%s.%f') * multiplier).

title: value_from_cursor returns a raw integer that is compared against a datetime column
body: Even ignoring the crash, OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor returns cursor.value unchanged (an integer), and build_queryset injects it into `WHERE <table>.datetime <= %s`. For a datetime-ordered queryset the cursor value must be converted back to a datetime (as DateTimePaginator.value_from_cursor does with fromtimestamp(value/1000)); comparing a datetime column to an integer epoch value will either error at the database level or silently match nothing/everything depending on coercion, corrupting pagination results.

title: Negative cursor offsets are passed into queryset slicing, which Django rejects
body: The comment claims 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically', but Django QuerySets explicitly do not support negative indexing: queryset[-5:95] raises ValueError ('Negative indexing is not supported'). Cursor offsets come from the client-supplied cursor string (`value:offset:is_prev`), which Cursor.from_string parses with int() and no validation, so any user with the optimized_pagination flag can send a negative offset and get a 500. The 'advanced feature' is non-functional and only adds a new error path.

title: BasePaginator silently clamps negative forward-cursor offsets instead of rejecting them
body: The change to BasePaginator.get_result replaces `results = list(queryset[offset:stop])` with `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`. A negative offset on a forward cursor previously raised a clear error; it is now silently treated as 0, so a client repeating a malformed/rewound cursor gets the first page again, which can cause infinite loops in polling consumers that keep following next cursors. Additionally, for is_prev cursors the raw (possibly negative) offset is still used in slicing and in the `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` check, making that boundary check inconsistent with the clamped slice in the non-prev path.

title: organization_context.member may be None, causing AttributeError before the optimized branch
body: `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` dereferences organization_context.member unconditionally for non-superusers. Requests authenticated without an organization membership context (e.g., certain token-based or org-auth-token flows that ControlSiloOrganizationEndpoint permits) have member=None, so this raises AttributeError and 500s the endpoint even though the user was never going to use the optimized path. Guard with `organization_context.member is not None and ...` or getattr.

title: No tests cover OptimizedCursorPaginator or the optimized audit log path
body: The PR adds ~100 lines of new pagination logic plus a new endpoint branch gated by query param and permissions, but no tests. Basic coverage (first page, next/prev cursor round trip, negative offset handling, non-privileged user requesting optimized_pagination, datetime ordering) would have immediately caught the math.floor(datetime) crash and the negative-slicing ValueError.

title: Negative offset slicing of a Django QuerySet raises AssertionError
body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when `enable_advanced_features` is set and the incoming cursor has a negative offset (which any client can supply via a cursor string like `0:-5:0`, parsed by Cursor.from_string), the code does `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative `start_offset`.
