The code only works because production/test servers happen to run in UTC. Use `dayjs.utc(date.start)` (or `.tz(organizerTimeZone)`) consistently for this comparison.

title: Dayjs objects compared with === is always false
body: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes') === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, 'minutes')` compares two distinct dayjs object references and can never be true; the intended check for a full-day 'unavailable' override (start equals end) never fires. This is currently masked for 00:00-00:00 blocked days because the later `slotStartTime.isAfter(end)` check catches them, but a blocked-day override stored with any non-midnight equal start/end (or a slot spanning that point) will incorrectly be treated as available. Use `.isSame(...)` instead of `===`.

title: Override timezone shift wraps across midnight and lands on the wrong day/hours
body: The new conversion computes startTime/endTime as `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, 'minute').hour() * 60 + ...minute()`. When the organizer-to-invitee offset shift moves the override across midnight (e.g. organizer in UTC+5:30 with a 00:30-02:00 override, invitee in UTC: offset = -330 minutes, shifting to 18:30-20:00 of the previous day), `.hour()` silently wraps to the previous/next day's wall-clock hours while the `activeOverrides` filter on line 207 still applies the override to the invitee day matching the override's own date. Result: slots are generated at wrong times on the wrong invitee day (and in some cases startTime > endTime, producing no or inverted ranges) whenever a date override crosses midnight after timezone conversion.

title: override.timeZone is optional in the type but used unconditionally
body: packages/types/schedule.d.ts declares `timeZone?: string` as optional on TimeRange, but getSlots now calls `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` without a fallback. When a caller passes date overrides without a timeZone, dayjs falls back to the server's guessed local timezone, so `organizerUtcOffset` — and therefore the shifted startTime/endTime — is computed against the wrong zone and the override is applied at incorrect times. Either make timeZone required on the override type or default it (e.g. to organizerTimeZone) before computing the offset.

title: No test covers the fixed-host round-robin scenario the PR claims to fix
body: The PR description states its primary fix is that date overrides of fixed hosts are respected for round-robin events, and all of the new checkIfIsAvailable logic (date-override filtering per fixed host, working-hours bounds, organizerTimeZone plumbing) serves that path. The added test only extends the existing personal single-user event 'Check for Date overrides' test with a second invitee timezone; there is no scenario with a ROUND_ROBIN event type, hosts with isFixed, or a fixed host's date override. The bugs in that new code path (busy times skipped inside overrides, slot end never checked against working-hours end, hosts with no hours on a weekday treated as available) would not be caught by the current suite.

title: Busy times are ignored on days with a date override, allowing double bookings
body: In checkIfIsAvailable, when a date override exists for the slot's day and the slot falls inside the override range, the function hits `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` (line 133) before the busy-time check at the bottom of the function. This means that on any day where a fixed host has a date override, that host's existing bookings and calendar busy times are never consulted — the slot is reported as available even if the host is already booked at that exact time. Before this change, checkIfIsAvailable always evaluated `busy`, so this is a regression that can produce double bookings for fixed hosts (and for round-robin hosts via the looseHostAvailability path, which uses the same function). The new tests don't cover the combination of a date override plus an existing booking, so this passes the suite unnoticed.

title: Working-hours check computes `end` from slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
body: In the new working-hours validation inside checkIfIsAvailable, both `start` and `end` are computed as `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()` (lines 141-142). Because `end` equals `start`, the `end > workingHour.endTime` condition can never detect a slot that starts inside working hours but finishes after they end. For example, with working hours 09:00-17:00 and a 60-minute event, a slot starting at 16:30 (ending 17:30, outside availability) passes the check and the fixed host is treated as available. This undermines the very guarantee this PR is adding — that slots are only shown when fixed hosts are actually available.

title: Working-hours `find` logic is wrong both ways: valid slots rejected and non-working days accepted
body: The working-hours check uses `workingHours.find(...)` where the callback returns true only when a matching-day entry excludes the slot. Two failure modes follow. (1) If a host has split working hours on the same day (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-18:00), a slot at 10:00 is not excluded by the first block but IS excluded by the second block (`start 600 < 840`), and `find` short-circuits on that second block — so a slot genuinely inside working hours is reported unavailable. The logic needs to require that the slot is within at least one block, not that no block excludes it. (2) If none of the host's working-hour entries include the slot's day at all, `find` returns undefined and the slot falls through to the busy check as available — so for a round-robin event (where aggregated working hours union all hosts' days), a fixed host who doesn't work that day at all is still considered available and the event can be booked with them, which is exactly the class of bug this PR claims to fix.

title: `===` comparison of two Dayjs objects is always false (dead code for unavailable-day overrides)
body: Line 114 compares `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes') === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, 'minutes')`. These are two freshly created Dayjs object instances, so strict reference equality is always false and this branch never executes. The intent is clearly to detect full-day 'unavailable' date overrides (start == end, stored as 00:00-00:00). Because the branch is dead, detection relies on the later `slotStartTime.isAfter(end)` check, which misses a slot starting exactly at the override boundary time (e.g. midnight for a blocked day): such a slot makes the find callback return falsy, sets dateOverrideExist=true, and is then returned as available with busy checks skipped. Use `.isSame()` instead of `===`.

title: Slot starting exactly at a date override's end is treated as inside the override
body: The boundary check uses strict `slotStartTime.isAfter(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, 'minutes'))` (line 123). A slot that begins exactly when the override ends (e.g. override 14:00-18:00, slot 18:00-18:45) is not excluded by this condition nor by the earlier `slotEndTime.isBefore/isSame(start)` condition, so the find callback returns falsy, `dateOverrideExist` remains true, and the function returns 'available' — additionally skipping the busy check due to the early return at line 133. The condition should be `!slotStartTime.isBefore(end)` so a slot at the exact override end is excluded.

title: Override timezone conversion silently breaks when `timeZone` is absent
body: The new conversion computes `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()`, but `timeZone` is declared optional on TimeRange (packages/types/schedule.d.ts) and only the slots router's getSchedule populates it. Any other current or future caller of getSlots that passes dateOverrides without a timeZone gets an offset computed against a guessed/local timezone (or a dayjs.tz failure), silently shifting override hours and producing wrong slots — worse than the old behavior, which needed no timezone at all. Additionally, `override.start.toString()` is an unnecessary and lossy round-trip (drops milliseconds, relies on implementation-specific string parsing) since `override.start` is already a Date that dayjs can wrap directly.

title: No test covers the fixed-host round-robin scenario the PR claims to fix
body: The PR's primary stated fix is that date overrides of fixed hosts are respected in round-robin events, and its manual test plan describes a round-robin event with one fixed host with a date override. However, the only new automated test extends the single-user 'Check for Date overrides' case with a second timezone. There is no test with schedulingType ROUND_ROBIN, hosts (isFixed true/false), and a date override on the fixed host, and no test combining a date override with an existing booking — which is exactly why the double-booking regression in checkIfIsAvailable (busy check skipped when dateOverrideExist) is not caught. A test with a fixed host, a date override, and a conflicting booking should be added.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category site setting was never customized
body: The migration does `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. site_settings rows only exist in the database when an admin has changed the value from the default, and embed_category defaulted to blank, so on any site that never set it this query returns zero rows. Indexing `[0]` on an empty PG::Result raises IndexError, which aborts the migration and blocks the upgrade. The same pattern is used for uncategorized_category_id on line 15. Both lookups need to tolerate an empty result.

title: Migrated hosts are inserted verbatim, so entries with scheme/path or quotes break or never match
body: The migration inserts each line of the old embeddable_hosts setting directly into the table with `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` bypassing the model. Two problems: (1) the old SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? tolerated values like 'http://example.com/page' (the old specs used such values), but the new EmbeddableHost.record_for_host matches `lower(host) = uri.host`, so a migrated host stored as 'http://example.com' will never match and embedding from that host silently stops working after the upgrade — the model's before_validation normalization never runs on migrated rows; (2) the value is interpolated into SQL unescaped, so a host containing a single quote breaks the migration (and is a SQL injection vector). The migration should normalize each host (strip scheme/path) and use bound parameters.

title: Fabricator file contents were swapped between category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb
body: spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines the :category, :diff_category, :happy_category and :private_category fabricators. The fabricator definitions were placed in each other's files. Tests may still pass because Fabrication loads every file in spec/fabricators, but the filenames are now actively misleading and any tooling that maps fabricators to their expected files will break. The contents of the two files should be swapped back.

title: before_validation crashes with NoMethodError when host is nil
body: The before_validation callback calls `self.host.sub!(...)` unconditionally. The controller sets `host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host]` directly, so if the host param is missing or blank, `self.host` is nil and `nil.sub!` raises NoMethodError, producing a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard with `return unless self.host.present?` (and the controller should handle a missing params[:embeddable_host] hash, which would itself raise NoMethodError on nil).

title: record_for_host does not downcase the incoming host before comparing
body: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases the stored column but compares it against the raw host extracted from the referer URI. DNS names are case-insensitive and an uppercase referer host (e.g. 'HTTP://EVILTROUT.COM/...') will fail to match a stored lowercase entry, wrongly rejecting legitimate embed requests. Use `host.downcase` when building the query.

title: Host validation rejects valid TLDs longer than 5 characters and there is no uniqueness constraint
body: The format regex requires `\.[a-z]{2,5}` so legitimate hosts such as 'example.technology' or 'example.museum' can never be added, silently failing validation in the admin UI. Separately, there is no validates_uniqueness_of :host and no unique index in the migration, so duplicate host rows can be created; record_for_host then picks an arbitrary one (`.first`), making the effective category for that host nondeterministic.

title: update/destroy raise NoMethodError (500) for a nonexistent host id
body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can return nil, and both update (via save_host, which immediately does `host.host = ...`) and destroy (`host.destroy`) dereference it. A request with a stale or invalid id returns a 500 instead of a 404. Raise RecordNotFound (e.g. use find(params[:id])) or return an error when the record is missing.

title: Plural hydration can inject undefined entries when a related id is not found
body: In _hydrateEmbedded, the new plural branch maps `xxx_ids` through _lookupSubType and assigns the result unconditionally (`obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []`), unlike the singular branch which only assigns `if (hydrated)`. _lookupSubType returns undefined when the id isn't present in the root payload (and for the 'category' special-case when the category isn't loaded client-side), so the hydrated array can contain undefined elements, which downstream code (e.g. `{{#each}}` rendering or .get calls) will trip over. Filter out undefined results or skip assignment when nothing resolved.

title: Test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' no longer tests what it claims
body: The implementation of Topic#expandable_first_post? no longer checks whether any embeddable hosts exist (the SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? condition was removed), but this spec was kept and renamed to suggest it verifies blank-host behavior. It only passes because Fabricate.build(:topic) is unsaved so has_topic_embed? returns false — the host-blank condition is never exercised. Either the test should be removed or updated to reflect the new contract.

title: Migration crashes when the embed_category site setting has no DB row
body: The migration does `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']`. Site settings only have a row in the `site_settings` table when an admin has overridden the default; on any install where `embed_category` was never changed from its empty default (or was set to a blank/non-matching value so the join returns nothing), the result set is empty, `[0]` is nil, and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration and blocking the deploy. The result needs a nil check before indexing (the same pattern is repeated on line 15 for `uncategorized_category_id`).

title: Migrated hosts are inserted raw, keeping scheme/path that lookups will never match
body: The old `embeddable_hosts` setting explicitly supported values like `http://discourse.org` and `https://example.com/1234` (the old specs set exactly those values). The new `EmbeddableHost` model strips the scheme and path in a `before_validation` callback, but the migration inserts the old values with raw SQL, bypassing the model entirely. After migration, rows contain e.g. `https://example.com/1234`, while `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `uri.host` (`example.com`) against the stored value, so every previously configured host that included a scheme or path silently stops being allowed — existing embedded comment installs break until an admin manually re-saves each host.

title: Migration interpolates setting values directly into SQL without escaping
body: The migration builds INSERT statements with `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`. `h` comes from the `embeddable_hosts` site setting, which was free text; a host entry containing a single quote will produce invalid SQL and fail the migration mid-way (and in principle allows SQL injection). Use `sanitize`/`quote` or a bound parameter instead of string interpolation.

title: record_for_host does not downcase the incoming host and cannot match hosts saved with a port
body: `record_for_host` runs `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` where `host` is `uri.host`. Ruby's URI parser preserves the case of the host (it is only downcased by `#normalize`), so a referer like `http://EVILTROUT.COM/page` will not match the stored lowercase `eviltrout.com` — the comparison should be against `host.downcase`. Additionally, the host validation regex on line 2 permits an optional port (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`), so an admin can save `example.com:3000`, but `uri.host` strips the port, meaning such a record can never match and embedding from that host is always rejected. Either reject ports in validation or include the port in the lookup.

title: before_validation crashes with NoMethodError when host is nil
body: The `before_validation` block calls `self.host.sub!(...)` unconditionally. If an `EmbeddableHost` is built without a host (e.g. the admin controller receives a request missing `embeddable_host[host]`, or code does `EmbeddableHost.new.valid?`), `nil.sub!` raises NoMethodError, producing a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard with `return unless self.host` (or `self.host = self.host.to_s`) and add a presence validation.

title: update and destroy raise NoMethodError for an unknown host id instead of 404
body: `update` and `destroy` do `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then use the result without a nil check: `update` passes nil into `save_host`, where `host.host = ...` raises NoMethodError, and `destroy` calls `host.destroy` on nil. A request for a deleted or bogus id returns a 500. Both actions should raise `Discourse::NotFound` (or use `find`) when the record is missing.

title: No uniqueness constraint or validation on host
body: Neither the model nor the migration enforces uniqueness of `host`, so admins can create duplicate rows for the same host pointing at different categories. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` then uses `.first`, making the category chosen for imported embedded topics arbitrary, and the admin UI shows conflicting duplicate rows. Add a unique index plus `validates_uniqueness_of :host, case_sensitive: false`.

title: Contents of category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb are swapped
body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while the new `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` defines all the category fabricators (`category`, `diff_category`, `happy_category`, `private_category`). The Fabrication gem loads every file in the directory so the test suite still runs, but the file names no longer match their contents — the new file's content belongs in `category_fabricator.rb` and vice versa.

title: Plural *_ids hydration produces arrays of undefined and deletes the raw ids even when nothing was resolved
body: In `_hydrateEmbedded`, the new plural branch maps `foo_ids` through `_lookupSubType` and then unconditionally sets `obj[plural] = hydrated` and deletes `obj[k]`. Unlike the singular branch (which only assigns and deletes when a hydrated object was actually found), this branch assigns even when `_lookupSubType` returned undefined for some or all ids — producing e.g. `colors: [undefined, undefined]` and destroying the original `color_ids` data. Any payload containing a plural id array whose collection is missing from the root (or partially missing ids) is silently corrupted. It should skip the assignment when nothing resolved, and ideally compact/filter unresolved ids; the `|| []` on the map result is also dead code since `map` always returns an array.

title: New admin endpoints have no request specs
body: The specs added for `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` (and `Admin::EmbeddingController`) only assert the class is a subclass of AdminController. There is no coverage for create/update/destroy behavior — authorization (non-staff rejected), the default-to-uncategorized category fallback, validation error rendering, deleting a host, or the embedding show endpoint. These endpoints implement the core of the feature (including the nil-record crashes noted above) and currently have zero functional coverage.

title: Fabricator file contents were accidentally swapped
body: The file spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb now contains the `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` definition, while all four category fabricators (:category, :diff_category, :happy_category, :private_category) were moved into the newly added spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb. The contents of the two files are swapped: the category fabricators belong in category_fabricator.rb and the embeddable_host fabricator belongs in embeddable_host_fabricator.rb. The suite still passes because Fabrication loads every file in the directory, but any developer looking for the category fabricator in category_fabricator.rb will find the wrong definition, and future edits are likely to be applied to the wrong file.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category / uncategorized_category_id rows are absent
body: Line 11 does `execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']`. Site settings only exist as rows in the site_settings table when they have been changed from their YAML defaults, so on a fresh install (or any site that never set embed_category, or where the stored value is '' or doesn't match a category name) the query returns zero rows, `[0]` is nil, and the migration aborts with `NoMethodError: undefined method '[]' for nil`. The same crash exists on line 15 for the `uncategorized_category_id` lookup when that row doesn't exist. This makes `rake db:migrate` fail on exactly the databases this migration is supposed to upgrade. The code needs to handle empty result sets (e.g. `rows[0].try(:[], 'id')` with a fallback).

title: Migrated hosts are inserted without normalization and may never match again
body: The old `embeddable_hosts` setting was matched leniently: `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` stripped `http(s)://` prefixes before comparing, so entries like `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234` worked. The new lookup (`EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`) requires an exact match against `URI(...).host`, and the model only strips the scheme/path in a `before_validation` callback — which never runs because this migration inserts the raw setting values with a bare SQL INSERT. Any existing entry that includes a scheme or path will be copied verbatim into the table and will silently stop matching referers after the upgrade, breaking comment embedding for those sites. The migration should normalize each value (strip scheme, path, and whitespace) before inserting.

title: Migration interpolates host values into SQL without escaping
body: The INSERT is built with string interpolation: `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` where `h` comes from a free-form, admin-editable site setting that was never validated as a hostname. A value containing a single quote (or other SQL metacharacters) will produce a syntax error and abort the migration mid-way, leaving the site_settings rows already deleted on some paths. Use `quote(h)` / bound parameters or insert via the model instead of raw string interpolation.

title: update and destroy crash with NoMethodError when the host record doesn't exist
body: In `update`, `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can be nil, and `save_host(nil)` immediately calls `host.host = ...`, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500. `destroy` has the same problem: `host.destroy` on nil raises. Both actions should return a 404 (e.g. `raise Discourse::NotFound`) when the record is missing, as other admin controllers do.

title: before_validation crashes on a nil host instead of failing validation
body: The before_validation block calls `self.host.sub!(...)` unconditionally. If `host` is nil — for example a POST to /admin/embeddable_hosts with a missing or blank `embeddable_host[host]` param — this raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil` and the request 500s, rather than producing a validation error from the format validator. Guard with `if self.host` (or use `self.host = self.host.to_s.sub(...)`) so an empty value fails validation cleanly.

title: Host validation rejects valid TLDs longer than 5 characters
body: The format regex ends with `\.[a-z]{2,5}`, which rejects legitimate hostnames with longer TLDs such as `example.technology`, `blog.international`, or `site.photography`. Admins embedding from such domains will get a validation error and be unable to add the host. The TLD portion should be more permissive (e.g. `[a-z]{2,}`).

title: Hosts saved with a port can never match in record_for_host
body: The validation regex explicitly permits a port (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`), so an admin can save `example.com:3000`. But `record_for_host` compares the stored value against `URI(host).host`, which never includes the port, so `where("lower(host) = ?", "example.com")` will not match the stored `example.com:3000`. Any host entry with a port is accepted by the UI but embedding from that host will always be rejected with 'invalid referer host'. Either strip/disallow ports at save time or include the port in the comparison.

title: No uniqueness constraint on host allows duplicate, conflicting entries
body: There is no `validates_uniqueness_of :host` and no unique index in the migration, so admins can create multiple rows with the same host pointing at different categories. `record_for_host` then returns whichever row `.first` happens to load, making the category that embedded topics land in nondeterministic. Add a model-level uniqueness validation (ideally case-insensitive, since lookup is on `lower(host)`) and a unique database index.

title: New admin controllers have no functional test coverage
body: Both new controller specs (admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb and admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb) only assert that the controller is a subclass of Admin::AdminController. Nothing exercises create/update/destroy of embeddable hosts, host normalization on save, the default-to-uncategorized category behavior, missing-record handling, or staff-only access. Bugs like the nil-record NoMethodError in update/destroy would be caught by even a minimal request spec.

title: edit() throws when the host's category no longer exists
body: `this.set('categoryId', this.get('host.category.id'))` assumes `host.category` is always present. `EmbeddableHost` has no foreign-key or dependent handling, so if the referenced category is deleted, the serializer still emits the stale `category_id`, the client-side lookup in the store finds no category, and `host.category` is undefined — clicking the pencil button then throws `TypeError: Cannot read property 'id' of undefined` and the row can no longer be edited. Use a safe access (`this.get('host.category.id')` via `Ember.get` chain or `host.get('category.id')` which is null-safe in Ember) and consider clearing category_id when a category is destroyed.

title: Client-side upload size validation hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring site settings
body: validateUploadedFile previously read the limit from Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], which distinguishes max_image_size_kb from max_attachment_size_kb and respects admin configuration. The change replaces it with a hardcoded 10 * 1024. Consequences: sites that set a lower limit (e.g., 1MB images) will no longer block oversized files client-side, sites that set a higher limit will now wrongly reject valid uploads, attachments are incorrectly capped by the image-size logic, and the 'file too large' error message reports a max_size_kb that has no relation to the configured value.

title: 413 error handler reports a hardcoded 10MB limit instead of the configured max image size
body: displayErrorForUpload used to show Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb in the file_too_large message when the web server returns 413. It now shows a hardcoded 10MB, so users are told the wrong maximum whenever the admin has configured max_image_size_kb to anything else, making the error message misleading.

title: URL download limit hardcoded to 10MB, breaking API uploads for other limits and non-image files
body: FileHelper.download for API-provided URLs previously used SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes as the cap; it is now hardcoded to 10.megabytes. This download path is used for any file type, not just images, so attachment downloads via the API are now silently capped at 10MB regardless of max_attachment_size_kb, and sites with max_image_size_kb set above 10MB cannot fetch larger images even though the downsizing logic below was intended to shrink them.

title: Duplicate definition of OptimizedImage.downsize makes the width/height overload unreachable
body: The class now defines self.downsize twice: once as downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) at line 145 and again as downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts) at line 149. In Ruby the second definition silently replaces the first, so the four-argument form is dead code. Any existing or future caller that passes max_width and max_height (the established API of this method) will now raise ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (4 for 3). The two-APIs-in-one-method approach needs a different mechanism (e.g., a separate method name or a single signature).

title: Animated GIF path passes "80%" to gifsicle --resize-fit, which does not accept percentages
body: The new upload-downsizing code calls OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails). For GIFs with allow_animation set, optimize dispatches to downsize_instructions_animated, which delegates to resize_instructions_animated and emits `gifsicle ... --resize-fit 80%`. gifsicle's --resize-fit expects a WIDTHxHEIGHT geometry, not a percentage, so the command fails, convert_with returns false, and the controller's retry loop runs 5 times without shrinking the file. The result: animated GIFs larger than max_image_size_kb always fail to upload instead of being downsized, and the loop silently wastes 5 shell-outs before giving up.

title: Downsize retry loop ignores failure and silently gives up after 5 attempts
body: The while loop never checks the boolean returned by OptimizedImage.downsize. If conversion fails (corrupt image, missing delegate, gifsicle geometry error), the loop burns all 5 attempts shelling out to a command that cannot succeed, then proceeds to Upload.create_for with the original oversized file, which then fails validation with a generic size error. A failed downsize should break out immediately (or surface a meaningful error) rather than retrying an unchanged file.

title: Duplicate `self.downsize` definition makes the 4-argument version dead code and breaks its callers
body: The file now defines `OptimizedImage.downsize` twice: once at line 145 with the signature `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and again at line 149 with `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. Ruby has no method overloading — the second definition silently replaces the first, so the 4-argument version is unreachable. Worse, any existing or future caller using the old 4-argument form (`downsize(from, to, width, height)`) will now have `height` bound to `opts`, and `!!opts[:allow_animation]` in `optimize` will raise a TypeError (no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer) at runtime instead of resizing. The leftover dead definition also misleads readers about the real contract. One of the two definitions should be removed and all callers migrated to a single signature.

title: Downsizing large animated GIFs silently destroys their animation
body: The new downsize path calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`. Inside `OptimizedImage.optimize`, the animated branch is chosen only when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`, but `from` here is the upload tempfile path (e.g. `/tmp/RackMultipart...`), which has no file extension, so the regex never matches. The code therefore falls through to `downsize_instructions`, which runs `convert #{from}[0] ...` — the `[0]` selector flattens the image to its first frame. A user uploading a large animated GIF will have the animation permanently discarded with no warning, even though `allow_animation` was explicitly passed. The animated-detection should be based on the original filename/content type, not the tempfile path.

title: Downsize retry loop ignores conversion failures
body: The loop `while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` never checks the boolean return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize`. If the conversion fails (corrupt image, unsupported format such as SVG written to an extensionless tempfile path so ImageMagick cannot determine the output format, missing binary), each iteration simply re-runs the same failing `convert` plus `ImageOptim` up to 5 times, wasting CPU in the deferred job and logging nothing about the upload-level failure. The loop should break (and ideally log) when `downsize` returns false.

title: API download limit hardcoded to 10 MB ignores site settings and applies to all types
body: The URL-based upload path for API clients changed from `FileHelper.download(url, SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, ...)` to a hardcoded `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`. This branch handles any upload `type`, not just images, so an admin who raised `max_attachment_size_kb` above 10 MB still cannot pull larger files via the API URL flow (the download is silently truncated/rejected at 10 MB and `rescue nil` swallows it, yielding a confusing nil-tempfile failure), while an admin who lowered limits gets no benefit from the cap at this layer. If the intent was only to accommodate images that will later be downsized, the limit should still derive from a setting (or at least only relax for image types).

title: Client-side upload size validation hardcoded to 10 MB, ignoring configured per-type limits
body: `validateUploadedFile` previously enforced `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, so the composer blocked oversized files before upload using the admin-configured image/attachment limits. It now uses a hardcoded `10 * 1024`. On sites with lower configured limits, users pass client validation and only fail later with a server error; on sites with higher limits (e.g. large attachments allowed), users are incorrectly blocked at 10 MB. The error message also now interpolates the raw value 10240 as `max_size_kb`. The client should keep reading the site setting; the server-side downsizing added in this PR handles the oversized-image case.

title: 413 error message reports a hardcoded 10 MB limit instead of the actual configured limit
body: In `displayErrorForUpload`, the 413 handler now shows `I18n.t('post.errors.file_too_large', { max_size_kb: 10 * 1024 })` instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`. Users will be told the limit is 10240 KB even when the site setting (and the web server limit that actually produced the 413) is different, and the raw kilobyte number is shown unformatted. The message should use the real configured limit.

title: Client-side upload size validation ignores site settings, hardcodes 10MB for both images and attachments
body: The check previously used Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so images were validated against max_image_size_kb and attachments against max_attachment_size_kb. The change replaces this with a hardcoded 10MB regardless of type. For attachments this breaks validation in both directions: a site that configured max_attachment_size_kb below 10MB will let users select files the server will reject after upload, and a site that configured a limit above 10MB will now hard-block legitimate attachment uploads on the client. The configured limits should still drive validation (or at least attachments should keep using max_attachment_size_kb).

title: 413 error message now always claims a 10MB limit
body: The 'entity too large' handler previously displayed Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb in the file_too_large message; it now hardcodes 10MB. Whenever the actual configured upload limit (or the web server's limit, which is what typically produces a 413) differs from 10MB, the user is shown a wrong maximum size in the error dialog.

title: API URL download limit hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring max_image_size_kb
body: FileHelper.download for API URL uploads was limited to SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes and is now hardcoded to 10.megabytes. On sites with a configured image limit above 10MB, API uploads via URL that were previously accepted will now silently fail (tempfile is nil after the rescue). The server-side limit should remain consistent with the site setting rather than a magic constant.

title: Downsize is passed an extensionless tempfile path, so ImageMagick cannot determine the output format
body: For regular browser uploads, tempfile is the Rack multipart tempfile (e.g. /tmp/RackMultipart2014...), whose path has no file extension. OptimizedImage.downsize shells out to `convert <from>[0] ... <to>` and ImageMagick derives the output image format from the destination filename extension; with no extension the convert command fails, convert_with returns false, the retry loop spins 5 times, and the oversized file is uploaded unchanged — the feature does nothing for the primary upload path. The same missing extension also means the `from =~ /\.GIF$/i` check in OptimizedImage.optimize never matches, so the animated-gifsicle branch is dead for direct uploads. A temp file carrying the original extension should be used.

title: Oversized animated GIFs are silently de-animated during downsize
body: The downsize instructions use `convert #{from}[0]`, which takes only the first frame, unless the animated branch is chosen. The animated branch is gated on allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails — a setting meant for thumbnails, not originals — and on the source path ending in .GIF, which is never true for direct uploads (see the extensionless tempfile issue). The result is that a user uploading an animated GIF larger than max_image_size_kb gets a static first frame stored as their original image with no warning, destroying the animation.

title: In-place downsize can leave a truncated file that is then uploaded
body: convert is run with the same path as input and output, and the loop only re-checks tempfile.size. If a convert run fails partway through writing the destination, the file can be left truncated/corrupted with a smaller size; the loop condition then passes and Upload.create_for stores the corrupt file as the user's upload. The result of OptimizedImage.downsize is never checked before continuing.

title: Duplicate definition of OptimizedImage.downsize shadows the width/height signature
body: The file now defines self.downsize twice: once at lines 145-147 as downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) and again at lines 149-151 as downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts). In Ruby the second definition wins, so the four-argument version at line 145 is dead code and any existing caller that passes max_width/max_height will now raise ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments), with Ruby also emitting a 'method redefined' warning. The old definition should have been removed instead of adding an overload.

title: Animated downsize reuses gifsicle --resize-fit, which does not accept a percentage like "80%"
body: downsize_instructions_animated delegates to resize_instructions_animated, which builds `gifsicle --resize-fit #{dimensions}`. gifsicle's --resize-fit expects WxH pixel dimensions; when the new upload downsize code passes "80%", gifsicle will fail, convert_with returns false, and the animated GIF is never downsized. A scale factor (gifsicle --scale) or explicit dimensions are needed for percentage-based downsizing.

title: unsubscribe crashes when the user has no topic_users row
body: In TopicsController#unsubscribe, `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can legitimately return nil: users in mailing-list mode receive notification emails for topics they have never visited (the mailer itself handles this — `TopicUser.get` is used nil-tolerantly in send_notification_email), as do users emailed via a topic invite. The very next lines dereference `tu.notification_level`, so clicking the new per-topic unsubscribe link from such an email raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of unsubscribing. The action should handle the missing row, e.g. by creating it via `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic.id, notification_level: TopicUser.notification_levels[:muted])`.

title: GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe mutates state with no token or confirmation
body: The new unsubscribe endpoint is a plain GET route that immediately changes the user's topic notification_level before rendering any page. Because GET requests carry no CSRF token, any third-party page that causes a logged-in user's browser to request the URL (e.g., an embedded pointing at the unsubscribe link) can silently mute or downgrade that user's subscription. Additionally, antivirus link scanners and browser/email prefetchers that fetch links from incoming mail will unsubscribe users without them ever clicking anything. State-changing actions should require POST, or the link should land on a confirmation page / use a signed token like the digest unsubscribe key.

title: Unsubscribe downgrades watching/tracking users to 'regular', contradicting the 'stop notifications' copy
body: For users whose notification_level is watching or tracking, the unsubscribe action sets the level to regular rather than muted. At 'regular' the user still receives notifications — and notification emails — whenever someone replies to them or mentions them in that topic. Yet the email link text says 'To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here' and the landing page says 'You will stop receiving notifications for <topic>'. Users who click the link will keep receiving emails for the topic, which is both a functional and messaging bug: either mute unconditionally or change the copy to say notifications are only reduced.

title: Template path does not match the route name, so the unsubscribe UI will not render
body: The client route is registered as a top-level route named `topicUnsubscribe` in app-route-map.js.es6, and the controller and view are named `topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, so Ember resolves the template for that route under the name 'topicUnsubscribe'. The template added here lives at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs, which registers as 'topic/unsubscribe' — a name only a child route `topic.unsubscribe` of the topic resource would look up. The route will therefore render with no template (or raise a missing-template error in development). Move the file to templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs to match the route, controller, and view naming.

title: No request specs for the new unsubscribe endpoint
body: The only spec change in this PR adds an unsubscribe_url option to an existing message-builder test. There are no request specs for TopicsController#unsubscribe covering the notification-level transitions (watching/tracking → regular, regular → muted), the behavior when the user has no topic_users row, or the slug-mismatch redirect. A request spec for the missing-row case would have caught the nil-dereference crash on the primary path of this feature.

title: Unsubscribe mutates state on a GET request (CSRF / link-prefetch)
body: The new `unsubscribe` action is routed as GET (`get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` in config/routes.rb) and is added to `skip_before_filter :check_xhr`, so a plain browser GET with only the session cookie changes the user's TopicUser notification_level. This violates safe-GET semantics in two ways: (1) any third-party page can silently unsubscribe/mute a logged-in user from an arbitrary topic via `` since topic ids are enumerable; (2) mail clients and security scanners (Outlook SafeLinks, Gmail prefetch, corporate link checkers) routinely follow links in emails, so the unsubscribe link in the notification email can be triggered without the user ever clicking it, silently muting the topic. The mutation should require a POST/PUT with CSRF protection, with the GET page only rendering the confirmation UI.

title: unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when the user has no TopicUser row
body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil — any logged-in user can visit `/t/<id>/unsubscribe` for a topic they have never read, posted in, or been emailed about, in which case no topic_users row exists. The very next line calls `tu.notification_level`, raising NoMethodError and producing a 500. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic.id, notification_level: ...)` (which upserts) or handle the nil case explicitly.

title: topicUnsubscribe route is shadowed by topic.fromParamsNear wildcard
body: The new route `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', { path: '/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe' })` is declared after `this.resource('topic', { path: '/t/:slug/:id' }, ...)` whose child route `fromParamsNear` has path `/:nearPost`. Ember matches routes in declaration order, so `/t/some-slug/123/unsubscribe` matches `topic.fromParamsNear` with `nearPost = "unsubscribe"` and the topicUnsubscribe route is never reached. The client then runs topic-from-params' setupController with a garbage nearPost, loading the topic stream instead of the unsubscribe confirmation page. The route must be declared before the topic resource (or nested with an explicit path that takes precedence).

title: unsubscribe_link translation now requires unsubscribe_url; callers without it will raise
body: config/locales/server.en.yml changed `unsubscribe_link` to include `[click here](%{unsubscribe_url})`. MessageBuilder calls `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` (here and in html_part) whenever `add_unsubscribe_link` is true, but `unsubscribe_url` is only present in template_args if the caller passed it. Any existing or future caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url` will now raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and fail to build the email. Either make the interpolation optional (fall back to the old text when unsubscribe_url is absent) or guard it in MessageBuilder.

title: Direct TopicUser save bypasses bookkeeping done by TopicUser.change
body: The unsubscribe action sets `tu.notification_level` and calls `tu.save!` directly instead of using `TopicUser.change`. As a result `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` are not updated (so there is no audit trail of when/why the level changed) and no MessageBus `notification_level_change` event is published, leaving the user's other open browser tabs showing a stale notification state for the topic.

title: No request specs for the new topics#unsubscribe action
body: The PR adds a new state-changing controller action (notification level changes, slug-mismatch 301 redirect, nil-TopicUser case, login requirement) but the only spec change is adding an `unsubscribe_url` option to an existing message builder spec. There are no request/controller specs covering the unsubscribe flow, which is how the nil TopicUser crash and the GET-mutation behavior slipped through.

title: unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when the user has no TopicUser record
body: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil — for example users in mailing list mode who receive emails for topics they have never visited or interacted with, and therefore have no topic_users row. The very next line calls `tu.notification_level`, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 instead of unsubscribing. This is exactly the population most likely to click a per-topic unsubscribe link. The action should create the record (e.g. via `TopicUser.change`) or handle the nil case.

title: topicUnsubscribe route name does not match the template path, so the page renders nothing
body: The route is registered as a top-level `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', ...)`, which makes Ember look for the `topic-unsubscribe` template (and the `topic-unsubscribe` controller/view, which is where the new controller and view files are placed). However the new template was added at `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, which registers under the name `topic/unsubscribe` — i.e. the name a nested `topic.unsubscribe` route would use. Because the resolved template name doesn't exist for this route, visiting /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe will render an empty page and the `stopNotificiationsText` controller will never be used. Either nest the route under the topic resource or move the template to `templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs`.

title: Unsubscribing a watching/tracking user only drops them to 'regular', so notification emails continue
body: The unsubscribe logic sets the level to `regular` whenever the current level is above regular (tracking or watching), and only sets `muted` when the level is already regular or below. The most common case for someone clicking 'stop receiving notifications about this topic' is that they are watching or tracking it; after one click they are still at `regular` and will continue to receive notification emails (replies to their posts, mentions) for the topic, while the page displays 'You will stop receiving notifications for <topic>'. That message is now false. If the intent is a true unsubscribe, the level should be set to muted in one step; otherwise the copy must not claim notifications have stopped.

title: Direct tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping
body: The unsubscribe action mutates `notification_level` and calls `tu.save!` directly instead of using `TopicUser.change`. As a result `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` are not updated, the `UserActionObserver` after-save callbacks are not fired, and no MessageBus `notification_level_change` message is published — so other open browser tabs of the same user will show a stale notification level for the topic, and any reporting/auditing on when/why the level changed will be wrong.

title: No test covers the new %{unsubscribe_url} interpolation in unsubscribe_link
body: The `unsubscribe_link` translation in server.en.yml now requires an `%{unsubscribe_url}` interpolation argument, but the only spec change passes `unsubscribe_url` into the builder without asserting that the topic unsubscribe link actually appears in the text body or HTML part. There is also no test that `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` behaves safely when `unsubscribe_url` is absent — with the new translation, any caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url` will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and break email delivery. Tests should assert the rendered link and the missing-argument behavior.

title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive, so blocks are trivially bypassed
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? performs an exact-match query: BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first. The email passed in comes straight from the signup form via User.new_from_params (which does no downcasing), and the blocked_emails table stores whatever case the admin entered. A spammer blocked as 'bad@spam.com' can register successfully as 'BAD@spam.com' or 'Bad@Spam.com' because the lookup won't match, and the user's own email uniqueness check is also case-sensitive so it won't collide with an existing account either. The block list should normalize (strip + downcase) both the stored value and the queried value, or the query should be case-insensitive.

title: match_count increment in should_block? is a racy read-modify-write
body: When a blocked email matches, should_block? does record.match_count += 1; record.save. Under concurrent signups hitting the same blocked address (the exact scenario a block list exists for), two processes can read the same match_count and both write back the same incremented value, losing counts. Use an atomic update (e.g., update_counters or UPDATE ... SET match_count = match_count + 1) instead. Additionally, calling full record.save here re-runs validations on every match and silently drops the stat update if the save fails for any reason; the return value is still computed from the stale record, which is fine, but the statistics become unreliable without any signal.

title: should_block? writes to the database from inside a model validation
body: EmailValidator#validate_each calls BlockedEmail.should_block?(value), which increments match_count and saves the blocked_emails row as a side effect of running validations. This means any user.valid? call — including ones that never lead to a save, and repeated client-side-driven validation attempts — mutates persistent statistics, and the write happens outside the user's save transaction. If stats collection is intended, it would be safer to record the match only when a signup is actually rejected (e.g., in the controller or in an after-validation hook gated on the record being persisted), otherwise the counters can be inflated arbitrarily by repeatedly triggering validation without ever creating an account.

title: Moved whitelist/blacklist email validation has no specs in the new validator spec
body: The email_domains_whitelist / email_domains_blacklist logic was moved out of User#email_validator into the new EmailValidator class, but the newly added spec/components/validators/email_validator_spec.rb only covers the BlockedEmail branch — there are no tests exercising the whitelist or blacklist paths of the moved code. If no existing user specs cover those site settings, a regression there (e.g., in email_in_restriction_setting?) would go unnoticed; the spec file should include cases for whitelist-allowed, whitelist-rejected, and blacklist-rejected emails.

title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive, allowing trivial bypass
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? does an exact-match query (BlockedEmail.where(email: email)) against the raw email string passed in from the user record, and User.new_from_params assigns params[:email] without downcasing or stripping. The fabricator and any manually curated blocklist entries will be lowercase, so a signup with 'BAD@spammers.org' will not match a blocklist entry for 'bad@spammers.org', even though those are the same mailbox in practice. Anyone blocked can re-register (or re-attempt) by simply changing the case of their address, defeating the feature this PR adds. The email should be normalized (e.g., Email.downcase(email).strip) both when storing BlockedEmail rows and when looking them up.

title: Validator performs a database write, and signups double-count match statistics
body: EmailValidator.validate_each calls BlockedEmail.should_block?(value), which increments match_count, sets last_match_at, and saves the BlockedEmail record — i.e., running model validations now has a write side effect. This is fragile in itself (validations can run in contexts where writes are unexpected), and it produces incorrect statistics in the main signup flow: UsersController#create calls user.valid? (line 168, app/controllers/users_controller.rb) to decide whether to contact the Discourse hub, and then user.save runs validations again, so a single blocked signup attempt increments match_count twice. The stats update should be moved out of the validation path (e.g., done once in the controller) or de-duplicated.

title: Moved whitelist/blacklist domain logic has no test coverage
body: The PR moves the email_domains_whitelist / email_domains_blacklist restriction logic out of User#email_validator into the new EmailValidator class, and removes the old User model code. The new spec only exercises the BlockedEmail branch (stubbing BlockedEmail.should_block?); there are no tests asserting that a non-whitelisted domain is rejected, that a blacklisted domain is rejected, or that an allowed domain passes. If the moved logic broke (e.g., the elsif precedence between whitelist and blacklist, or regex construction in email_in_restriction_setting?), nothing in this PR's tests would catch it. Tests covering the whitelist and blacklist branches should be added (or the old user email-restriction specs kept/pointed at the new validator).

title: Blocked email matching is case-sensitive, so blocks are trivially bypassed
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? does an exact-match lookup: BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first. The value passed in from EmailValidator is the raw email as the user typed it, and User.new_from_params stores the email as entered (no downcasing before validation), so the blocked list entry 'spammer@spamclub.com' will not match a signup for 'Spammer@SpamClub.com'. A blocked spammer can re-register simply by changing letter case. The email should be normalized (e.g. Email.downcase(email).strip) both in should_block? and in a before_validation callback when BlockedEmail records are created; the uniqueness validation on the model should also be made case-insensitive for the same reason.

title: match_count increment is a read-modify-write that loses updates under concurrency
body: should_block? loads the record, does record.match_count += 1, and calls record.save. Two concurrent signups with the same blocked email both read the same match_count and the second save overwrites the first, so the counter under-counts. Additionally this save runs full validations and silently discards the stat if save returns false. Use an atomic update (e.g. BlockedEmail.update_counters(record.id, match_count: 1) plus update_column for last_match_at) to avoid the race and the extra validations.

title: Blank email gets a misleading 'not allowed from that email provider' error when a whitelist is configured
body: ActiveModel::EachValidator runs on nil values by default. When SiteSetting.email_domains_whitelist is present and the email is blank, email_in_restriction_setting? evaluates 'nil =~ regexp' (nil, falsy), so the validator adds I18n.t('user.email.not_allowed') — 'is not allowed from that email provider' — on top of the presence validator's 'can't be blank'. Users see a confusing message implying their provider is banned when they simply left the field empty. Return early when value is blank (or add allow_blank: true and let the presence validator handle it).

title: rejectedEmails array is defined on the controller prototype and never cleared
body: rejectedEmails: Em.A([]) is passed to Discourse.Controller.extend, which puts a single mutable array instance on the prototype shared by every instance of CreateAccountController (the classic Ember.extend footgun). Any rejected email pushed in createAccount (line 275) persists for the life of the controller and would leak across instances if the controller is ever recreated (e.g. in tests or container teardown), causing unrelated emails to show 'invalid'. Initialize the array in init() (this._super(); this.set('rejectedEmails', Em.A([]))) and consider clearing it after a successful account creation.

title: Any email error marks the address as 'invalid' in the UI, including 'already taken'
body: On account creation failure, the code pushes result.values.email into rejectedEmails whenever result.errors.email exists, and emailValidation then shows I18n.t('user.email.invalid') for that address. But errors.email is also present for failures unrelated to validity — most commonly the email already being registered (uniqueness). After one failed submit, a user trying an already-registered email is told the address is 'invalid', which is wrong and confusing. Either check the specific error message, or have the server distinguish blocked/invalid from taken.

title: raw_html cook method renders feed/imported HTML without any sanitization, enabling stored XSS
body: The new `cook` short-circuit returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, bypassing the entire rendering/sanitization pipeline. This content originates from external sources: `Jobs::PollFeed` stores RSS/Atom item bodies (`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) directly, and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` stores Readability output. Nothing sanitizes it, and it is rendered raw in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` (`<%= raw post.cooked %>`) and in the normal topic UI. A malicious or compromised feed/article can therefore inject `<script>` or event-handler attributes that execute for every forum reader (stored XSS). The imported HTML should be run through the sanitizer (with an appropriate tag/attribute whitelist) before being stored as cooked.

title: postMessage targetOrigin is a full referer URL, which browsers reject, so iframe resizing never works
body: The layout calls `parent.postMessage({type: 'discourse-resize', height: ...}, '<%= request.referer %>')`. The targetOrigin argument to postMessage must be an origin (scheme://host[:port]) or '*'; passing a full URL with a path (e.g. `http://blog.example.com/2013/02/10/post.html`, which is what the referer will always be) causes the browser to throw a SyntaxError ('Invalid target origin') and the message is never delivered. Since embed.js only sets the iframe height when it receives this message, the embedded comments iframe stays at the browser default height (~150px) and the comments appear cut off. The origin should be derived from the referer (or `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`), not the full referer URL.

title: i.content can be nil for feeds without content:encoded, crashing the hourly job
body: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every feed item has a `content` element. SimpleRSS only populates `content` when the feed includes `content:encoded`; many RSS 2.0 feeds only provide `description`, and some Atom entries lack content entirely. For those items `i.content` is nil and `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError, which aborts `rss.items.each` and kills the whole polling job (which has `retry: false`), so no topics are imported at all. Fall back to `i.description` or skip items with no content.

title: TopicEmbed.import mutates the caller's contents string
body: `contents << "\n<hr>\n<small>..."` appends the 'Imported from' footer directly to the string object passed in by the caller. If the same string object is ever reused (e.g. a caller importing twice with one buffer, or passing a frozen string), the footer is appended multiple times — which also changes the computed content_sha1 and triggers spurious post revisions — or raises a RuntimeError on frozen strings. Use `contents = contents + ...` or `contents.dup` before appending.

title: setnx followed by expire is not atomic; a crash leaves the throttle key with no TTL
body: `retrieved_recently?` does `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)` as two separate commands. If the process dies (or redis errors) between the two, the key is set with no expiry, and that embed URL is treated as 'retrieved recently' forever — `perform_retrieve` will never run for it again, so the topic for that URL is never imported. Use a single atomic command such as `$redis.set(retrieved_key, "1", ex: 60, nx: true)`.

title: embed_url is limited to 255 characters with no model-level length validation
body: The migration creates `t.string :embed_url, null: false` (255-char limit) with a unique index, while `TopicEmbed` only validates presence. Blog/feed URLs frequently exceed 255 characters (tracking parameters, long slugs). For such URLs, `TopicEmbed.create!` raises a database error (or RecordNotUnique-style failure) instead of a clean validation, and `EmbedController` will keep enqueueing retrieval jobs for a URL that can never be stored. Either use `text`/a larger limit or add a length validation and gracefully skip over-long URLs.

title: absolutize_urls raises URI::InvalidURIError for feed URLs that pass the loose scheme check
body: `TopicEmbed.import` accepts any URL matching `/^https?\:\/\//`, but `absolutize_urls` then calls `URI(url)`, which raises `URI::InvalidURIError` for strings with spaces, quotes, or other invalid characters that still match the prefix regex (feed-provided `link` values in `Jobs::PollFeed` are not otherwise validated). The exception is unrescued here, so one malformed feed item aborts the entire hourly `PollFeed` run (which has `retry: false`), preventing all other items from being imported. Validate with `URI.parse` up front and skip items that fail to parse.

title: RSS/feed HTML is stored and rendered without any sanitization (stored XSS)
body: poll_feed takes the raw HTML from each feed item (`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) and passes it to TopicEmbed.import, which creates the post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. Post#cook (app/models/post.rb) returns `raw` verbatim for raw_html posts, skipping the entire rendering and sanitization pipeline, and app/views/embed/best.html.erb renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (the main app also serves cooked HTML to clients). Nothing ever sanitizes this content, so a feed entry containing `<script>` or event-handler attributes becomes stored XSS executed for every forum visitor and embed viewer. The forum trusts the configured feed URL, but a compromised or hostile blog feed would fully compromise the forum. The imported HTML should be run through Sanitize (already a dependency) before being stored.

title: i.content is nil for feeds without content:encoded, crashing the hourly job
body: SimpleRSS only populates `item.content` when the feed entry has a `<content:encoded>` (or `<content>`) element. Plain RSS 2.0 feeds that only provide `<description>` — which is extremely common — will have `i.content == nil`, so `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError. The exception aborts the whole PollFeed run (and since it is raised inside the hourly scheduled job, every subsequent run fails the same way), so no topics are ever imported from such feeds. The code should fall back to `i.description` when `i.content` is blank.

title: Per-URL retrieval throttle is trivially bypassed, enabling unauthenticated fetch amplification
body: The anonymous-accessible GET /embed/best endpoint enqueues a RetrieveTopic job for any embed_url, which makes the server perform an outbound HTTP fetch of that URL (TopicRetriever -> TopicEmbed.import_remote -> open(url)). The only protection is a 60-second Redis throttle keyed on the exact URL string (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`). An attacker can bypass it indefinitely by appending unique query strings (e.g. ?r=1, ?r=2, ...) to the same page on the embeddable host, causing the forum to hammer the configured embeddable host with unbounded fetches — a denial-of-service amplification against the very site the forum operator embeds. The throttle should be normalized (e.g. keyed on host/path, or a global rate limit) and import_remote should have timeouts and size limits.

title: Editing an already-released migration to add force: true is ineffective and dangerous
body: This migration was already merged and run by existing installations; changing `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` will never execute for anyone who already migrated, so whatever problem the edit was meant to fix silently persists for them. Worse, `force: true` drops the existing table before recreating it — for any environment where this migration has not yet run but the table exists with data, running it will destroy that data. If the table needs to be recreated, that must be done in a new migration.

title: postMessage origin check accepts origins that merely start with the forum URL
body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring check, not an origin comparison. If discourseUrl is 'https://forum.example.com', then a message from origin 'https://forum.example.com.evil.com' passes the check (indexOf returns 0), so any site whose origin begins with the forum's origin string can send messages to the embed script. Today the only handled message resizes the iframe, so impact is limited to layout manipulation, but the check is wrong and will silently extend to any future message types. It should compare e.origin against the parsed origin of discourseUrl exactly.

title: Check-then-create race in TopicEmbed.import crashes concurrent jobs
body: import looks up `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, when absent, creates the topic, post, and TopicEmbed row inside a transaction. Two RetrieveTopic jobs (or a poll plus a retrieve) for the same URL running concurrently can both see no existing embed and both try to create; the unique index on topic_embeds.embed_url makes the loser's `TopicEmbed.create!` raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, rolling back the just-created topic/post and failing the Sidekiq job (with retries). The race should be handled, e.g. by rescuing RecordNotUnique and re-reading the existing embed.

title: absolutize_urls mangles protocol-relative URLs
body: URLs like `//cdn.example.com/img.png` start with '/', so they match the `href.start_with?('/')` branch and are rewritten to `http://<feed host>//cdn.example.com/img.png`, which is broken. Protocol-relative hrefs and srcs are common in feed content; they will all 404 after import. The rewrite should skip values starting with '//'.

title: Adding a column with a default rewrites and locks the posts table
body: `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` on PostgreSQL versions prior to 11 rewrites the entire posts table to materialize the default, taking an access-exclusive lock for the duration. On a large forum this can block all reads/writes to posts for a long time during deploy. The safer pattern for that era is to add the column without a default, backfill in batches, then set the default and NOT NULL constraint.

title: setnx + expire is not atomic; a crash between them permanently blocks retrieval of the URL
body: retrieved_recently? does `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)` as two separate commands. If the process crashes or the Redis connection drops between the two, the key is set with no TTL, and that embed URL will be treated as 'retrieved recently' forever — the topic will never be imported. A single atomic SET with EX (or setex) avoids the window.

title: RSS feed content is stored and rendered as unsanitized raw HTML (stored XSS)
body: poll_feed passes `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` directly to `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates the post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. The new `Post#cook` returns the raw string unchanged for such posts, so `post.cooked` contains the feed HTML completely unfiltered — including any `<script>` or event-handler attributes (unescapeHTML even turns `<script>` back into a live tag). That cooked HTML is rendered unsanitized on the forum and in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. A single malicious or compromised feed entry would therefore execute arbitrary JavaScript in the browsers of all forum visitors and staff. The feed URL being admin-configured does not make every item in a third-party feed trustworthy; the content should be run through a sanitizer/whitelist before import.

title: i.content can be nil, crashing the hourly feed job
body: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` calls `.scrub` on `i.content`, but SimpleRSS only populates `content` when the feed item has a content:encoded element. Plain RSS 2.0 items typically only have a `description`, and Atom items use `summary`/`content` differently, so for many real feeds `i.content` will be nil and the job will raise NoMethodError. Since the job declares `sidekiq_options retry: false`, the entire hourly poll silently fails and no topics are imported. The code should fall back to `i.description`/`i.summary` or guard against nil.

title: absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs
body: The absolutize logic checks `href.start_with?('/')` and prepends the site's scheme+host, which also matches protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/image.jpg`. Such a URL gets rewritten to `http://sourcehost.com/cdn.example.com/image.jpg`, producing a broken link/image. Protocol-relative URLs are common in feed content (especially for images/CDNs), so imported topics will contain dead links. The check should skip values starting with `//`.

title: postMessage origin validation uses substring match instead of equality
body: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts any message whose origin is a substring of discourseUrl, rather than comparing origins exactly. This is a fragile trust check for a cross-origin message handler; it should compare the event origin against the forum's origin (e.g. `e.origin !== discourseOrigin`) so that only the actual Discourse iframe can drive the resize behavior, and so the check doesn't silently misbehave when discourseUrl has unexpected forms (paths, ports, trailing slashes).

title: Retroactively editing an existing migration to add force: true
body: The PR modifies the already-released migration `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`, changing `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. Migrations that have already run in production should not be edited — environments at different migration states will now have drifted from the checked-in definition, and `force: true` silently drops and recreates the table if the migration is ever re-run (e.g. after a rollback or in a partially-migrated environment), destroying any data in top_topics. New behavior belongs in a new migration.

title: float: right on .small-action button is silently ignored inside the new flex container
body: This PR makes `.small-action` a flex container via `@include flexbox()`. CSS specifies that `float` has no effect on flex items, so the `float: right` on the direct-child `button` (line 309) no longer does anything. Previously the button was pinned to the right edge of the small-action row; now it will render inline immediately after `.small-action-desc`, breaking the intended layout of small action posts (e.g. the edit/expand controls). The same applies to `float: left` on `.topic-avatar` (line 271), which is harmless only by accident of source order. The fix is to replace the button's float with `margin-left: auto` (or add `flex` spacing) so it is pushed to the end of the flex row.

title: align-items mixin emits -webkit-box-align, which does not support the 'baseline' value used by bullet badges
body: The new `align-items` mixin unconditionally emits `-webkit-box-align: $alignment` for the 2009 flexbox spec, but that old property only accepts start/end/center/stretch — `baseline` is invalid and the declaration is dropped. `.badge-wrapper.bullet` in badges.css.scss calls `@include align-items(baseline)`, so on browsers that only understand the old `-webkit-box` model (e.g. older iOS Safari, which Discourse's `display: -webkit-inline-box` fallback in `inline-flex()` explicitly targets) the invalid declaration is ignored and items fall back to stretch alignment, vertically misaligning the bullet color swatch against the category text. If old-WebKit support matters (the mixin's prefixes imply it does), the mixin needs a value mapping or a fallback for `baseline`.

title: Header panel alignment now depends entirely on flexbox with no fallback for non-flex browsers
body: `.panel` previously used `float: right`, which worked in any browser. It now relies on `margin-left: auto` inside the `.contents` flex container. In any browser where none of the `display` values emitted by the `flexbox()` mixin are supported, `.contents` stays a block container, an auto left margin on a block-level `.panel` computes to 0, and the panel (user menu, search, hamburger icons) collapses against the logo on the left instead of staying on the right, breaking the header layout. If the supported-browser matrix includes any non-flexbox browsers (or engines with buggy partial flex support such as IE10, where auto margins inside `-ms-flexbox` containers are unreliable), this needs a fallback such as retaining `float: right` alongside the flex rules.

title: button float:right inside .small-action is ignored now that the container is flex
body: The PR makes .small-action a flex container (@include flexbox()). Floats have no effect on flex items, so the 'button { float: right; }' rule inside .small-action (and the leftover 'float: left' on .topic-avatar) is now dead. The button (the small-action undo/edit control) previously sat at the right edge of the row; after this change it renders as a normal flex item immediately after .small-action-desc instead of being right-aligned. To preserve the layout the button needs 'margin-left: auto' (or .small-action-desc needs flex-grow: 1). The 'clear: both' on .small-action and the float rules should also be cleaned up or verified.

title: Header .contents is now a non-wrapping flex row with no shrink/overflow handling
body: .d-header .contents now uses display:flex with align-items:center but no flex-wrap (defaults to nowrap) and no min-width:0 on the items. Previously .title floated left and .panel floated right, so on narrow viewports content could drop/reflow; as flex items, .title, .extra-info-wrapper (which contains the topic title text and can be long) and .panel cannot wrap, and modern flex items refuse to shrink below their min-content size without min-width:0. On narrow screens or with a long topic title shown in the docked header, this can cause horizontal overflow or squished/overlapping header elements instead of graceful reflow. Consider adding min-width:0 plus text-overflow handling to .extra-info-wrapper/.title, or an appropriate flex-wrap/flex-shrink strategy.

title: align-items mixin emits a nonexistent -ms-align-items property and mismatched old-box values
body: The new align-items mixin emits '-ms-align-items: $alignment', which is not a real CSS property in any browser (IE10 implements '-ms-flex-align', which the mixin already includes) — it is dead code that suggests IE support the mixin doesn't actually verify. Additionally, '-webkit-box-align' (2009 flexbox) only accepts start/end/center/baseline/stretch; it does not accept 'flex-start'/'flex-end', so any future caller passing those values will get no alignment at all in browsers that fall back to 'display: -webkit-box'. Similarly the flexbox mixin emits 'display: -moz-box' but there is no accompanying '-moz-box-align', so the old-Firefox fallback is only half implemented. Either trim the unsupported fallbacks or add the correct value mapping.

title: Leftover .valign-helper rule is meaningless inside the new flex container
body: .valign-helper (display:inline-block; height:100%; vertical-align:middle) was a hack for vertically centering header content under the old float layout. Now that .contents is a flex container with align-items:center, this element becomes a flex item: vertical-align does not apply to flex items and height:100% resolves against an indefinite container height (auto). The rule is dead weight from an incomplete refactor and should be removed along with the corresponding element in the header template if it is no longer needed.

title: float:right on .small-action button is ignored now that .small-action is a flex container
