body: The PR adds `@include flexbox()` and `@include align-items(center)` to `.small-action`, which makes all of its direct children flex items. Per the flexbox spec, `float` has no effect on flex items, so the `button { float: right; }` rule (lines 306-310) silently stops working: a button rendered inside a small-action post that was previously pinned to the right edge will now sit inline immediately after `.small-action-desc`. To preserve the old right-aligned behavior the button needs `margin-left: auto` (or `justify-content`/`order` adjustments) instead of `float: right`. The same applies to the leftover `clear: both` on line 312 and the `float: left` on `.topic-avatar` (line 270), which are now dead declarations under the flex layout.

title: Panel right alignment relies on margin-left:auto, which breaks in browsers that only support the legacy -webkit-box flex syntax
body: `.panel` previously used `float: right` to sit at the right edge of the header; it now relies on `margin-left: auto` plus `@include order(3)` inside the new flex container. The `flexbox()` mixin emits `display: -webkit-box` / `display: -moz-box` for legacy engines, but the 2009 flexbox spec does not honor auto margins for alignment (it used `box-pack`), and `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`/`order` behavior also differs. On any client that falls back to the legacy box display, the panel will no longer be pushed to the right. If supporting those engines is the reason the legacy prefixes were added, the panel needs a fallback (e.g. keep a float fallback or use box-pack: justify).

title: website_name leaks the website field for TL0 users viewed anonymously, bypassing untrusted_attributes
body: The serializer deliberately hides `:website` (via `untrusted_attributes`, which checks `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`) so that anonymous visitors cannot see a TL0 user's profile fields. The new `:website_name` attribute is declared in the plain `attributes` list (line 43), is derived directly from `object.user_profile.website`, and its inclusion check only tests `website.present?` — it never checks `restrict_user_fields?`. As a result, for a TL0 user viewed by an anonymous visitor, `website` is omitted from the JSON but `website_name` (containing the website host, and possibly path) is still serialized, leaking exactly the information the restriction is meant to hide. The existing 'TL0 user seen as anonymous' spec was not extended to cover `website_name`, so the test suite does not catch this. `website_name` should be added to `untrusted_attributes` or its include check should mirror `include_website?`.

title: include_website_name is missing the '?' suffix, so ActiveModelSerializers never calls it
body: ActiveModelSerializers filters attributes by calling `include_<attribute>?` (with a question mark) — every other filter in this file follows that convention (`include_email?`, `include_stats?`, etc.). The new method is defined as `def include_website_name` without the `?`, making it dead code: the `website.present?` guard never runs, and `website_name` is always serialized (as `nil` when the user has no website, and unconditionally in the restricted-TL0 case described above). Rename it to `include_website_name?`.

title: Sibling subdomains are treated as the same domain as the instance
body: The middle branch compares hosts of equal label count by stripping the first label from both sides: `www.anything.com` vs `forum.anything.com` are considered 'the same domain' and the full URL path is displayed. A sibling subdomain is not the instance's domain — on multi-tenant or shared-domain setups (e.g. instance at `forum.example.com`, user website at `evil.example.com/phishing-page`) the profile will render the full path as if the link belonged to the site's own domain, which is exactly the misleading display this feature is supposed to avoid. The comparison should only show the path when the website host equals the instance host or is a parent domain of it (the first and third branches), not when it is merely a sibling.

title: website_name leaks TL0 users' websites to anonymous viewers, bypassing untrusted attribute protection
body: The `website` attribute is deliberately hidden for TL0 users viewed by anonymous visitors via `untrusted_attributes :website` (which checks `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`), an anti-spam/privacy measure so new users can't use their profile website for link spam. The new `website_name` attribute computes its value from the same `object.user_profile.website` but is not added to `untrusted_attributes` and its inclusion check (`include_website_name`, which only tests `website.present?`) never consults the scope. As a result, an anonymous viewer of a TL0 user's profile JSON now receives the website host — and the full host+path whenever the host matches the instance domain — even though `website` itself is suppressed. This defeats the restriction; `website_name` must be gated by the same `restrict_user_fields?` logic as `website`.

title: include_website_name is missing the trailing '?' so ActiveModel::Serializer never calls it
body: ActiveModel::Serializer's conditional-inclusion hook must be named `include_<attribute>?` (with a question mark), as used elsewhere in this file (e.g. `include_email?`, `include_stats?`). The method defined here is `include_website_name` without the `?`, so AMS never invokes it and the guard is dead code: `website_name` is serialized unconditionally, appearing as an explicit `null` in the JSON for every user without a website (and, combined with the first issue, there is no effective scope check at all). Rename the method to `include_website_name?` for the filter to take effect.

title: String#ends_with? does not exist; NoMethodError in the else branch
body: In the `website_name` method, the fallback branch calls `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)`. Ruby's String method is `end_with?`; the `ends_with?`/`starts_with?` aliases were provided by old ActiveSupport versions and were removed in Rails 4, which this codebase runs on. Whenever a user's website host is a parent domain of the instance hostname (e.g. website `example.com` on instance `forums.example.com`), serializing the user will raise NoMethodError and the whole user JSON endpoint will 500. This also means the third new spec (`returns complete website path when website domain is parent of instance domain`) would fail if run, so the tests appear not to have been executed. Change to `end_with?`.

title: include_website_name is missing the `?` suffix, so the guard is never invoked
body: ActiveModelSerializers only honors inclusion guards named `include_<attribute>?`. The method here is defined as `def include_website_name` (no question mark), so it is never called and `website_name` is always serialized, including a `website_name: null` key for users with no website. If the intent is to suppress the attribute when the website is blank, rename it to `include_website_name?`.

title: website_name leaks the website of TL0 users to anonymous visitors
body: The serializer deliberately hides `website` (along with bio, location, etc.) from anonymous viewers of trust-level-0 users via `untrusted_attributes`, which checks `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`. The new `website_name` attribute is not added to that list, and its inclusion guard only checks `website.present?` — so an anonymous visitor requesting a TL0 user's JSON now receives `website_name` (the website's host, and when it matches the instance domain, the full path) even though `website` itself is suppressed. This defeats the purpose of hiding the website field. `website_name` should be included in `untrusted_attributes` (or its include guard should check `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`).

title: No test for the same-length subdomain branch of website_name
body: The new `website_name` logic has three branches, but the specs only cover two: different domains and exact/parent-domain matches. The middle branch (equal label counts greater than two, e.g. website `www.example.com` vs instance `forum.example.com`, comparing the domains after stripping the first label) is untested, including its negative case where the registrable domains differ (`www.other.com` vs `forum.example.com`) and only the host should be returned.

title: Light/dark branches swapped for embedded-post username link color
body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a`, the original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The PR replaces it with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))` — the first argument (light theme) should preserve the original 30%, with 70% as the new dark-theme value. As written, the values are inverted, so on light themes this username link changes from 30% to 70% lightness (much fainter than intended, hurting readability), which is a visual regression unrelated to the dark-theme goal.

title: Light/dark branches swapped for .custom-message-length color
body: The original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, but the replacement is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))` — the branches are swapped relative to the convention used everywhere else in this PR (original value in the light branch, new value in the dark branch). The desktop equivalent (`desktop/modal.scss`) correctly uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. On mobile light themes this text now renders at 30% lightness instead of 70%, making it far darker than before and inconsistent with desktop.

title: topic-map h3 light-theme color changed from 20% to 50% lightness
body: In `.topic-map h3`, the original `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` was replaced with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme branch should keep the original 20% (the desktop counterpart in `desktop/topic-post.scss` correctly uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`). On mobile light themes, topic-map headings now render noticeably lighter than before, and mobile/desktop render the same element with different colors.

title: group-member-info .name light-theme color changed from 30% to 50%
body: In `.user-stream .group-member-info .name`, the original `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` was replaced with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme branch should preserve the original 30% (compare `.user-small .name` in `common/base/user.scss`, which correctly became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`). title: group-member-info .name light-theme color changed from 30% to 50%
body: Same mistake as in desktop/user.scss: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` originally used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` but now uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light branch should retain the original 30% value (e.g. `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`); as written, light themes get a lighter name color than before.

title: Missed scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%) instance in categories badge-notification
body: `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still uses `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`, the exact pattern this PR converts everywhere else (including the visually identical `.badge-notification` rule in `common/base/header.scss`, which was converted to `dark-light-choose(..., scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`). On dark themes this leftover produces an over-brightened color inconsistent with the rest of the converted badge notifications.

title: Light-theme color of embedded-post author link changed from 30% to 70% lightness
body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a`, the original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The first argument should be `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`.

body: In `.group-member-info .name`, the original `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` was replaced with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. body: In `.group-member-info .name`, the original `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. On light themes this lightens the group member name from 30% to 50%, an unintended change to light-theme rendering. The light argument should stay at 30% to preserve existing appearance.

title: topic-map h3 light-theme lightness changed from 20% to 50%, inconsistent with desktop
body: `.topic-map h3` was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme value changed from 20% to 50%, making the topic-map heading significantly lighter on light themes. The desktop equivalent (`desktop/topic-post.scss` `.topic-map h3`) was converted as 20%/80%, so mobile now renders differently from desktop. The light argument should remain 20%.

title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
body: totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100 members, limit 50), this yields 3 pages when only 2 exist. Because showingLast compares currentPage to totalPages, the 'next' button stays enabled on the real last page; clicking it sets offset = min(offset + limit, user_count) = 100, and findMembers then fetches an empty page, leaving the admin looking at a blank 'page 3/3' of members with no way forward. The computation should be Math.ceil(user_count / limit) (with the zero case handled), and/or the next action should clamp offset to user_count - limit.

title: 'automatic' check resolves against the member, so the remove button always renders
body: This template is rendered as the itemView for each member in '{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}', so its context is the individual user, not the group. '{{#unless automatic}}' therefore looks up 'automatic' on a User, which is undefined, so the condition always passes and the remove (×) link is shown even for automatic groups (admins, moderators, etc.). Clicking it fires the DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members request, which the server correctly rejects with 422 (can_not_modify_automatic), but the client-side removeMember action in the admin-group controller and the Group model's removeMember have no error handling, so the click fails silently and the member just stays in the list. The automatic check needs to come from the group/controller (e.g. passed via the each or referenced through the controller), and the failure case should surface an error to the admin.

title: Group create silently ignores the alias_level chosen in the form
body: The client sends alias_level on creation: Discourse.Group.asJSON() returns {name, alias_level, visible} and create() POSTs it to /admin/groups, and the alias level combo box in admin/templates/group.hbs is shown for new (unsaved) groups too. However the create action only assigns name and visible — params[:alias_level] is never applied — so every new group is created with the default alias_level of 0 ('nobody') regardless of what the admin selected, with no feedback. The admin must save the group and then save it again via update (which does handle alias_level) to get the intended setting.

title: Public group members page now truncates to 50 members with no pagination UI
body: The members action now always applies limit/offset (default limit 50) to every group; previously non-automatic groups returned their full member list and only automatic groups were capped. The public-facing group members page (discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6 and discourse/templates/group/members.hbs) was updated to read 'members' off the group model but has no pagination or load-more controls — only the admin group page got next/previous. As a result, any group with more than 50 members now shows only the first 50 (alphabetically) on its public members page, with no way for a visitor to see the rest.

title: members endpoint accepts an unbounded limit parameter
body: limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i places no upper bound on the page size for this publicly accessible endpoint (anyone who can see the group can call it). A request such as /groups/mods/members.json?limit=1000000 forces a COUNT plus a full SELECT and JSON serialization of that many users in one request. The limit should be clamped to a sane maximum (e.g. 200).

title: remove_member 'automatic group' test uses PUT while the route is DELETE-only
body: The test 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' calls xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42, but the route added in config/routes.rb is delete "members" => "groups#remove_member" — PUT /admin/groups/:id/members is not routed (PUT maps to add_members). Rails controller tests bypass the router and dispatch directly to the action, so this test passes anyway, which means it would not catch a missing or misconfigured DELETE route. It should use xhr :delete like the companion test does.

title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of the page size
body: totalPages is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When the member count is an exact multiple of the limit (e.g. 100 members with limit 50), this yields 3 pages instead of 2. Because `showingLast` compares currentPage to this inflated totalPages, the 'next' button stays enabled on the real last page; clicking it sets offset to `Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)` = user_count, and the member list renders an empty extra page. It should be `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

title: Public group members page now truncated to 50 with no pagination UI
body: Previously, the members action only applied limit/offset for automatic groups (with a default limit of 200); non-automatic groups returned all members. Now every group is capped at `limit` (default 50). The public members template (`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs`) and its route have no pagination controls — pagination was only added to the admin UI — so for any group with more than 50 members, the remaining members are no longer visible anywhere on the public group page.

title: {{#unless automatic}} is never true in the member item view, so the remove icon shows for automatic groups
body: This template is rendered as the itemView of `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` in group.hbs, so its context is the individual member (a Discourse.User), not the group controller. Users have no `automatic` property, so `{{#unless automatic}}` always evaluates true and the remove (×) link is rendered even for automatic groups — the exact case it was meant to suppress (the sibling `{{#unless automatic}}` in group.hbs works because its context is the controller). Clicking it on an automatic group fires the confirm dialog and then the server correctly rejects with 422, but the failure is silently swallowed (removeMember's promise has no error handler), so the admin gets no feedback. The view should receive the group's automatic flag explicitly.

title: No upper bound on the limit parameter for the public members endpoint
body: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` accepts any client-supplied value. Since /groups/:id/members is a public endpoint, anyone can request `?limit=1000000` and force the server to serialize and return huge user lists in one response. The limit should be clamped to a reasonable maximum (e.g. 200).

title: remove_member spec uses xhr :put instead of xhr :delete
body: The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' example calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42`, but the remove_member route is DELETE (`delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` in config/routes.rb); PUT is wired to add_members. Controller specs dispatch directly to the action so the test still passes, but the verb is a copy-paste error from the add_members test above and would mislead anyone converting these to request/route-level specs.

title: add_members/remove_member require params[:group_id] but the routes only supply params[:id]
body: The new routes in config/routes.rb are declared directly inside the `resources :groups` block (`put "members" => "groups#add_members"`, `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`), which makes them member routes: the URL is `/admin/groups/:id/members` and the group id arrives as `params[:id]`. Both actions call `params.require(:group_id)`, which raises `ActionController::ParameterMissing` (rendered as a 400) on every real request, so adding or removing members from the admin UI is completely broken. The specs pass only because rspec controller specs bypass routing and inject `group_id` directly into the params hash. The controller should read `params[:id]` (or the routes should be changed to actually provide `:group_id`).

title: totalPages off-by-one shows an extra empty page when user_count is a multiple of limit
body: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. For a group whose member count is an exact multiple of the page size (e.g. 100 members with limit 50) this yields 3 pages even though only 2 exist. The admin can then click "next" from page 2 (showingLast is false), which sets `offset = Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)` = 100, and `findMembers` fetches offset 100 from the server, landing on a permanently empty page 3. The computation should be `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` and the next-page clamp should not allow offset == user_count.

title: Public group members page now silently truncates non-automatic groups to 50 members with no way to see more
body: Previously `members` returned every member of a non-automatic group (only automatic groups were paginated). Now `.limit(limit).offset(offset)` is applied unconditionally with a default limit of 50, but the public template `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` has no pagination controls — it just iterates `members` once. Any group with more than 50 members (a common case, and the reason the old code had a workaround for the 200-member truncation bug) will only ever display the first 50 members alphabetically, with no UI to access the rest.

title: Adding a user who is already a member raises a unique-violation 500
body: `add_members` calls `group.add(user)` for every username found, with no check for existing membership. `Group#add` does `self.users << user`, which immediately inserts a `group_users` row; the join table has a unique index on (group_id, user_id), so re-adding an existing member raises `PG::UniqueViolation`/`ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` and returns a 500 to the admin. This is easy to hit from the UI because the `addMembers` controller action deliberately does not clear the usernames input (see the TODO in admin-group.js.es6), so clicking "Add" a second time re-submits the same usernames. Duplicates should be skipped (e.g. `group.users.include?(user)` or rescue/ignore the conflict).

title: No upper bound on the limit parameter of the public members endpoint
body: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` accepts any client-supplied value, so `GET /groups/<name>/members.json?limit=1000000` will serialize and return every member of the group in a single request. This endpoint is visible to anyone who can see the group, so an unbounded limit is an easy way to force expensive queries and huge responses. The limit should be clamped to a sane maximum (e.g. 50–200).

title: add_members doesn't strip whitespace when splitting usernames
body: `usernames.split(",").each` looks up each entry verbatim. If the input contains spaces after commas ("alice, bob"), the lookup `User.find_by_username(" bob")` fails and that user is silently skipped while the response still reports success. Each username should be stripped before lookup.

title: `{{#unless automatic}}` in the member item view never sees the group's automatic flag
body: This template is rendered as an itemView for each member, so its context is the member user, not the admin group controller. `automatic` is not a property of the user, so the `{{#unless automatic}}` guard always passes and the remove (×) link is rendered even for automatic groups. Clicking it then fires `removeMember`, which the server rejects with a 422. The automatic check needs to be passed through explicitly (e.g. via the view) instead of relying on context lookup.

title: Member endpoint specs use the wrong verb and bypass routing, hiding the broken route params
body: The "cannot remove members from automatic groups" test issues `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but the actual route is `delete /admin/groups/:id/members`. More generally, both new endpoint specs pass `group_id` directly in the params, so they exercise the action in a way no real request can: the member routes deliver the group id as `params[:id]`, meaning `params.require(:group_id)` in the controller fails in production while the specs stay green. These should be request/integration specs that go through the router, using the correct DELETE/PUT verbs and URLs.

title: Fallback locales are only loaded for web requests; jobs, mailers, and console get "translation missing"
body: The translate accelerator (lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb) lazy-loads only `config.locale` inside `I18n.translate`; loading of the full fallback chain (current locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en) happens exclusively through `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`, which is only invoked here in `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Any translation done outside the web request cycle — Sidekiq/scheduled jobs, user mailers (which render via `I18n.with_locale(user.effective_locale)`), rake tasks, console — with a non-default locale will have only that locale's yml files loaded. When a key is missing, the newly included `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` walks to the site default locale and then :en, but those translations were never loaded, so the lookup returns "translation missing: ..." instead of the English text. For non-English sites this means notification emails and other background-rendered content can show raw missing-translation strings — the feature this PR adds silently does nothing there. Additionally, no-argument translations are memoized in the process-wide LRU cache, so a missing-translation result produced before fallback locales are loaded can be served from cache afterwards. The fallback chain should be loaded inside the accelerator itself (e.g., in `load_locale`/`translate` or an overridden `I18n.with_locale`), not only in the controller filter.

title: Fallbacks now enabled in development and test, masking missing translations
body: Previously `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` existed only in the production/profile environment files. This initializer sets `I18n.fallbacks` unconditionally, so fallbacks are now active in development and test as well. In those environments a missing translation in the working locale will now silently render the English fallback instead of surfacing as a missing translation, which makes untranslated keys harder to spot during development and can let tests pass against fallback text rather than the intended translation. If that is intentional it should be called out; otherwise gate the assignment to the environments that previously had it enabled.

title: No tests for the new fallback behavior
body: The PR introduces a custom fallback order (requested locale → SiteSetting.default_locale → :en via `FallbackLocaleList`) and new lazy-loading of fallback locales (`I18n.ensure_loaded!`, `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!`), but adds no specs. There is no coverage asserting that a key missing in e.g. `de` resolves first to the site default locale and then to `en`, that all fallback locale files actually get loaded, or that the lazy-loading accelerator and the Fallbacks backend interact correctly. A regression spec covering those cases would protect the feature, especially given the loading is split between the initializer, the freedom patch, and the controller filter.

title: Fallback locales are only loaded for controller requests, so fallbacks silently fail in jobs/mailers
body: Fallback loading is triggered solely by `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` in `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Because the translate accelerator lazy-loads only `config.locale` (see `translate` in lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb), any translation performed outside a web request — Sidekiq jobs, user notification emails, scheduled tasks — will have the current locale's file loaded but never the fallback chain (site default locale and :en). In those contexts a key missing from the user's locale will render as 'translation missing' instead of falling back to the default/English string, so the feature only works for HTTP requests and silently no-ops elsewhere. The fallback loading should happen inside the translation path (e.g., in `load_locale`/`translate` or `I18n.with_locale`) rather than in a controller before_filter.

title: Translation LRU cache key does not account for the fallback chain, so cached results go stale when default_locale changes or differs per site
body: The accelerator caches no-argument translations under `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`. Before this change, the translation for a given key+locale depended only on that locale's file; now it also depends on the fallback chain, which includes `SiteSetting.default_locale` (see `FallbackLocaleList#[]` in config/initializers/i18n.rb). The cache is only cleared by `I18n.reload!`, which a site-setting change does not trigger. Consequences: (1) after an admin changes the site default locale, keys missing in a user's locale keep serving strings from the old default locale until the process restarts; (2) on multisite installs where different sites share the process and backend but have different `default_locale` values, a fallback result cached for one site is served to another site with a different default locale, producing wrong-language output. The cache key needs to incorporate the effective fallback list (or the cache must be invalidated when `default_locale` changes).

title: FallbackLocaleList#[] recomputes the chain on every translation lookup
body: `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks#translate` calls `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` for every translation that reaches the backend (which is all translations with interpolation arguments, since the LRU cache only covers the no-args path). The overridden `[]` performs a `SiteSetting.default_locale` lookup, allocates a symbol via `to_sym`, allocates and `uniq`s an array on every call, even though the result only changes when `default_locale` changes. On translation-heavy pages this is pure per-call overhead. Consider memoizing the computed list and invalidating it when the default_locale setting changes.

title: No tests for the new fallback ordering and loading behavior
body: This PR introduces a custom fallback chain (user locale → site default locale → :en), replaces the global `I18n.fallbacks` object with a custom `FallbackLocaleList`, moves pluralization setup between initializers, and adds `ensure_loaded!` to the translation accelerator, but changes no spec files (the PR description is also just the placeholder 'Test 9'). There is no coverage verifying that a key missing in the user locale resolves to the default locale and then to English, that `FallbackLocaleList#[]` behaves correctly when the user locale equals the default locale, or that fallback locale files actually get loaded. A regression here would surface as untranslated UI strings and would be easy to miss without tests.

title: Fallback locales are only loaded for web requests, so fallbacks silently fail in jobs/emails/rake/console
body: The new `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` call lives only in `ApplicationController#set_locale`, so fallback locale files (site default locale and English) are only loaded during controller requests. In every other server-side context that translates — Sidekiq/scheduled jobs, user notification emails, rake tasks, console — the translate accelerator's `load_locale` only loads the current locale. When the Fallbacks backend then tries to fall back to e.g. :en for a key missing from the user's locale, the English translations were never loaded into the process, so instead of the English text users get a "translation missing" string (the MissingTranslationData exception is swallowed by I18n's exception handler). Since the stated purpose of the PR is server-side fallbacks, and emails/jobs are the main server-side translation surface, the fallback-chain loading should happen in the accelerator itself (e.g. in `load_locale`/`translate`) rather than in a controller before_filter.

title: Translation LRU cache key does not account for the fallback chain, leaving stale results when default_locale changes
body: Cached translations are keyed only by `key + config.locale + backend.object_id`. With the new FallbackLocaleList, a lookup for a key missing in the current locale resolves via `SiteSetting.default_locale` and then :en, and that resolved value is cached under the current locale's key. If an admin later changes `SiteSetting.default_locale`, nothing resets the I18n LRU cache (changing a site setting does not call `I18n.reload!`), so all previously cached fallback results continue to return text from the old default locale until the entries happen to be evicted (300-entry cache) or the process restarts. Consider including the effective fallback list (or default_locale) in the cache key, or clearing the cache when default_locale changes.

title: No tests cover the new fallback ordering or loading behavior
body: The PR introduces user-visible fallback semantics ([requested locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en]) via a custom Hash subclass plus a new per-request loading hook and a new `I18n.ensure_loaded!` API, but contains no spec changes at all. There is nothing pinning down the fallback order, the behavior when a translation exists only in English, or the interaction with the translate accelerator's on-demand loading (the exact area where this can silently break, e.g. in job contexts). At minimum, specs should cover that a missing translation in a non-default locale returns the English string and that the fallback list reflects changes to SiteSetting.default_locale.

title: Denial cache key is ambiguous: fields joined with '_' can collide for UIDs containing underscores
body: userPermDenialCacheKey builds the key by concatenating namespace, userUID, action, name, and parent with '_' separators and no escaping or length prefixing. Resource and folder UIDs in Grafana can contain underscores, so distinct (name, parent) pairs produce identical keys: e.g. name="dash_a", parent="fold_b" and name="dash_a_fold", parent="b" both yield the same key. Because a cached entry means 'deny', a denial recorded for one dashboard/folder combination will incorrectly deny access to a different, unrelated dashboard for up to 30 seconds (shortCacheTTL). Use a delimiter that cannot appear in UIDs, hash the individual fields, or encode lengths to make the key unambiguous.

title: Denial cache is checked before the new DB requery path, reintroducing stale denials for newly granted permissions
body: The stated goal of this PR is to let creators access dashboards/folders they just created by requerying the DB when cached permissions don't contain the resource. However, the denial cache is consulted first in Check and short-circuits before both the permission cache and the DB fallback. If a Check is evaluated and denied before the permission grant is visible (e.g. a check that races the permission write at creation time, or read-replica lag on the permission query), the denial is cached for shortCacheTTL (30s) and every subsequent check for that exact resource returns Allowed=false without ever hitting the DB requery logic added in this PR. The creator is then locked out of the resource they just created for up to 30 seconds — the same symptom this PR is meant to fix. Consider a much shorter TTL for denial entries, or falling through to the DB on denial-cache hit under a singleflight/throttle instead of returning immediately.

title: Denial-cache hits are counted as permission-cache hits in metrics
body: When the denial cache short-circuits a Check, the code increments s.metrics.permissionCacheUsage with label "true" (cache hit). This metric is meant to track usage of the permission cache (permCache); denial-cache hits are a different signal and will inflate the apparent permission cache hit ratio, making dashboards/alerts built on this metric misleading. Consider a separate metric or an additional label value (e.g. "denial") for this path.

title: Stale denial-cache entries take precedence over fresher positive permission data
body: In Check, the permission denial cache is consulted before the positive permission cache, and denial entries are never invalidated when the permission cache is refreshed. Sequence: (1) Check(user, dashboards:read, dash1) misses the perm cache, the DB requery denies, and a denial entry is cached (30s TTL). (2) The user is then granted read on dash1. (3) Any other Check for this user+action that falls through to the DB (e.g. for dash2) refreshes permCache via getUserPermissions with fresh data that now includes dash1. (4) A retry of Check(user, dashboards:read, dash1) hits the stale denial entry at line 117 and returns denied, even though the server's own freshly cached permission set says allow. The denial check should run after the positive cache check (allow on cached hit, then denial cache, then DB fallback), or denial entries for the user+action should be dropped when permCache is rewritten. As written, users can be denied access to just-granted resources for up to the full 30s TTL even when the server already holds fresh permissions proving the grant — which partially defeats the stated purpose of this PR (immediately accessing newly granted/created resources).

title: Denial-precedence test uses a non-allowing cache entry, so it doesn't prove what its comment claims
body: In TestService_CacheCheck/"Should deny on explicit cache deny entry", the comment says "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked", but the perm cache is seeded with map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}. Because checkPermission tests the truthiness of scopeMap[scope], a false value does not grant access, so this test would pass even if the denial cache were checked after the permission cache, or if the permission cache were consulted and simply found nothing allowing. To actually pin down the precedence behavior (denial cache wins over an allowing perm cache entry), the cached value must be true — which would currently fail and exposes the stale-denial-overrides-fresh-allow problem in Check.

title: permissionCacheUsage metric recorded as a miss on a permission-cache hit that didn't grant access
body: When getCachedIdentityPermissions returns a cached permission set but checkPermission does not allow the request (triggering the intended DB requery fallback), execution reaches line 137 and increments permissionCacheUsage with label "false" (miss), even though the permission cache was hit. Before this change the metric was incremented inside getUserPermissions/getAnonymousPermissions strictly according to cache hit/miss, so dashboards and alerts built on the hit ratio will now show a drop in hit rate that does not reflect actual cache effectiveness. The hit should be recorded before evaluating checkPermission, with a separate metric (or label) for the fallback-to-DB path.

title: Stale denial cache entries are never revalidated and take precedence over fresh allows
body: In Check, the permDenialCache is consulted before anything else and short-circuits the entire request, returning Allowed=false. Denial entries live for shortCacheTTL (30s) and are never invalidated or cross-checked against fresher data. Two concrete consequences: (1) a user who is granted permission (directly, via a team, or via a folder) within 30s of a denied check keeps being denied until the entry expires — unlike stale allows in permCache, which now trigger a DB requery on miss, a stale denial has no fallback path to correct itself; (2) deny-wins ordering means a stale denial entry overrides a newer allow already sitting in permCache (e.g. denial cached at t=0, grant at t=5, a DB fetch for another resource refreshes permCache with the allow at t=6, a check at t=7 still returns deny because the denial entry is hit first). This partially re-introduces, on the deny side, the exact staleness problem this PR is fixing for newly created resources. Consider checking the denial cache only after the cached-permission allow path, or validating a denial hit against the current cached permission set before returning it.

title: Denial-cache test would pass even if the denial cache were ignored
body: In TestService_CacheCheck/'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry', the comment says 'Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked', but the code seeds the permission cache with map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false} — a false value, which checkPermission treats as not allowed anyway. As a result the assertion resp.Allowed == false would hold even if the permDenialCache lookup were removed entirely, so the test does not actually prove that the denial cache short-circuits the check. The seeded value should be true so the test fails when the denial entry is not honored.

title: permissionCacheUsage metric recorded as a hit when only the denial cache was used
body: When a Check is answered from permDenialCache, the code increments s.metrics.permissionCacheUsage with label "true" (cache hit), even though the permission cache itself was never consulted. This inflates the apparent permission-cache hit rate and makes it impossible to distinguish permission-cache hits from denial-cache hits in monitoring, which matters when tuning the TTLs this PR introduces. A separate label value or metric for denial-cache usage would keep the signal accurate.

title: Silence menu item renders in the new list view but clicking it does nothing
body: In the new ruler-less list view, RuleActionsButtons is rendered with only `promRule` (no `rule`/RulerRuleDTO). AlertRuleMenu computes `canSilence` from `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(promRule, ...)`, which can be true, so the 'Silence notifications' menu item is shown and calls `handleSilence()` -> `setShowSilenceDrawer(true)`. However, the drawer is only rendered behind the guard `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer`, and `rule` is undefined in this context, so the SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer never appears. The user clicks Silence and nothing happens — a visibly broken action in the primary new list view.

title: Delete menu item can never render in the new list view despite prom-based delete ability
body: The Delete menu item is guarded by `{canDelete && rulerRule && (...)}`. This PR adds prom-based ability checks (`canDelete` can now be true via `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` even without a ruler rule), and RuleActionsButtons.V2's `handleDelete` only needs the identifier (`showDeleteModal(identifier, groupIdentifier)`), but in the new list view `rulerRule` is always undefined, so the `rulerRule &&` guard permanently hides Delete. Users cannot delete Grafana rules from the new alert list view even with full permissions. The same pattern at line 123 (`canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)`) also makes Pause unavailable in the list view.

title: Refactor of useAllAlertRuleAbilities drops the federated rule group check, enabling edit/delete on federated Mimir groups
body: Before this change, `useAllAlertRuleAbilities(rule: CombinedRule)` computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` and used it to disable Update/Delete/Pause/DeletePermanently for federated (cross-tenant Mimir) rule groups. The PR rewrites `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` to delegate to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifierV2)`, which hardcodes `const isFederated = false` (with a TODO). Since `useAlertRuleAbility`/`useAlertRuleAbilities` still route through `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` and are used by existing components (e.g. the old RulesTable / RuleActionsButtons), edit, delete and pause actions are now offered in the UI for federated rule groups where they were previously disabled. The backend may still reject the operation, but this is a UI-level permission regression.

title: GrafanaRuleListItem rendered in rules.map without a key prop
body: In the `rules.map(...)` switch in FilterViewResults, the 'grafana' branch now returns `<GrafanaRuleListItem rule={...} groupIdentifier={...} ... />` with no `key` prop — the previous code passed `key={key}` (the comment in this file explains the artificial `key` exists specifically to prevent key duplication). The 'datasource' and default branches still pass `key={key}`. React will log a missing-key warning and, more importantly, reconciliation of this infinitely-appended list can match/grafana list items incorrectly when the list grows or re-renders.

title: skipToken path computes Duplicate ability against Grafana permissions, wrongly enabling Duplicate for cloud rules
body: When `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`/`useGrafanaPromRuleAbility` is called with `skipToken` (e.g. in AlertRuleMenu and RuleActionsButtons.V2 for cloud/Mimir rules, where `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule)` is false), `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined)` still computes abilities: loading is false so `MaybeSupported = AlwaysSupported`, and `[AlertRuleAction.Duplicate] = toAbility(duplicateSupported=true, getRulesPermissions('grafana').create)`. AlertRuleMenu then ORs this with the ruler ability, so `canDuplicate` becomes true for a cloud rule whenever the user has the Grafana-internal rule create permission — even if they lack the external rule write permission that the ruler-based check requires. The Duplicate menu item appears and navigates to a clone flow that will fail.

title: Prom-based abilities use alertingRule check for ModifyExport/Pause, dropping support for recording rules
body: In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, ModifyExport, Pause and Restore use `isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` as the supported flag, whereas the ruler-based equivalent uses `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)` / `isGrafanaManagedAlertRule`, which matches both alerting and recording Grafana rules. In the new list view (promRule only, ruler abilities unavailable), Grafana recording rules therefore lose the Export menu item and pause support that they previously had. Modify-export and pausing are valid operations for Grafana-managed recording rules.

title: Rule link no longer includes the returnTo parameter
body: The deleted GrafanaRuleLoader's GrafanaRuleListItem built the view URL with `createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view', { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`, so navigating back from the rule detail view returned the user to the list. The new GrafanaRuleListItem (used by both GrafanaGroupLoader and FilterView) builds the href without `returnTo`, silently regressing the back-navigation behavior for the new list views.

title: Component doc comment still says it loads from Prometheus and Ruler endpoints
body: The JSDoc above GrafanaGroupLoader still reads 'Loads an evaluation group from Prometheus and Ruler endpoints' and the `expectedRulesCount` comment still says 'Ruler response might contain different number of rules', but this PR removed the `useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery` call and all ruler handling from the component. The comments now describe behavior that no longer exists and will mislead future maintainers.

title: Stale comment and variable name reference ruler rule preloading that was removed
body: The comment 'This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules, but it improves the UX / Because the user waits a bit longer for the initial load but doesn't need to wait for each group to be loaded' and the variable name `cacheAndRulerPreload` remain, but the `alertRuleApi.util.prefetch('getGrafanaRulerGroup', ...)` dispatch they described was deleted in this PR. The remaining code only upserts the Prometheus groups cache, so the comment/identifier are now incorrect.

title: GrafanaRuleListItem rendered without a React key in the filtered rules list
body: In the `origin === 'grafana'` branch of the rules map, `<GrafanaRuleListItem>` is returned without `key={key}`, while the previous code passed `key={key}` to `GrafanaRuleLoader` and the sibling branches (`datasource`, `default`) still pass their keys. The component computes a stable `key` per rule precisely to avoid key duplication in this list. Rendering list children without keys triggers React's missing-key warning and, more importantly, can mis-associate component state (e.g. the delete modal / silence drawer state held by `RuleActionsButtons`) with the wrong rule row when pages are appended or the list is re-rendered. Add `key={key}` to the `GrafanaRuleListItem` element.

title: Delete menu item can never appear in the rule list because it still requires a rulerRule
body: The Delete menu item is gated on `{canDelete && rulerRule && (...)}`. This PR computes `canDelete` from prom-rule-based abilities (`useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`) specifically so delete works in the list view where 'we have removed all requests to the ruler API', but in that context `rulerRule` is always `undefined`, so the item never renders even when `grafanaDeleteSupported && grafanaDeleteAllowed` is true. The delete flow itself does not need the ruler rule — `RuleActionsButtons.V2` implements `handleDelete` as `() => showDeleteModal(identifier, groupIdentifier)`, which only uses the identifier. Net effect: users with delete permission cannot delete Grafana rules from the new list view (the updated GrafanaGroupLoader test even codifies this by expecting only 4 menu items with no Delete). Either drop the `rulerRule` requirement from the render guard or pass the identifier through instead.

title: Silence menu item is shown in the list view but clicking it does nothing
body: The silence drawer is only rendered when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is truthy: `{rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer && (<SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer rulerRule={rule} .../>)}`. In the new list view only `promRule` is supplied (ruler API calls were removed), so `rule` is undefined. Meanwhile `AlertRuleMenu` now shows the 'Silence notifications' item based on prom-rule-based `canSilence`, and `handleSilence` sets `showSilenceDrawer(true)` — but no drawer ever mounts. The user clicks the menu item and nothing happens. Either gate the silence menu item on the presence of a ruler rule, or make the drawer work from the prom rule data.

title: Refactor of useAllAlertRuleAbilities drops the federated-rule-group immutability check
body: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` (still used by existing components such as the old list's RuleActionsButtons via `useAlertRuleAbility`) previously computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` and treated federated groups as immutable (no edit/delete). It now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, which hardcodes `const isFederated = false;` with a TODO, and the `isFederatedRuleGroup` import was removed. As a result, rules in federated Mimir rule groups (groups with `source_tenants`) are no longer marked immutable on this code path, so Edit/Delete buttons can be shown for rules that must not be modified through Grafana. Restore the federated check for the CombinedRule-based path or thread the group's `source_tenants` into `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`.

title: ModifyExport ability for Grafana prom rules excludes recording rules, removing Export from the list view
body: In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, `[AlertRuleAction.ModifyExport]: [isAlertingRule, exportAllowed]` uses `prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`, which is false for recording rules. The ruler-based equivalent used `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)` (`isGrafanaRulerRule`), which is true for both alerting and recording rules. In the list view (no ruler rule available), `canExport` therefore becomes false for Grafana-managed recording rules and the Export menu item disappears, whereas previously recording rules could be exported from the list. The same `isAlertingRule` gating on Pause/Restore also diverges from the old semantics (Grafana recording rules support pausing). Use a check that includes recording rules where the action legitimately applies to them.

title: Rule view link no longer carries the returnTo parameter
body: The previous implementation built the rule link as `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`; the new `GrafanaRuleListItem` drops the `returnTo` parameter. Users navigating from the list to a rule's detail page will lose the 'return to previous' context, so going back from the detail view no longer returns them to their filtered list position. If this was not an intentional product change, restore the `returnTo` query parameter.

title: Stale comment and variable name still reference ruler rule preloading
body: The comment above the cache-preload block still says 'This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules, but it improves the UX / Because the user waits a bit longer for the initial load but doesn't need to wait for each group to be loaded', and the variable is still named `cacheAndRulerPreload`, but the `alertRuleApi.util.prefetch('getGrafanaRulerGroup', ...)` call was removed in this PR. The comment now describes behavior the code no longer has and is misleading to future readers; update the comment and rename the variable to reflect that only the Prometheus groups cache is populated.

title: Silence menu item is shown in the list view but clicking it does nothing
body: In the new list view, RuleActionsButtons is called with only promRule (rule/rulerRule is undefined). AlertRuleMenu can compute canSilence=true from the new prom-based abilities (useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities returns a Silence ability for Grafana alerting rules), so the 'Silence notifications' menu item is rendered and calls handleSilence, which sets showSilenceDrawer=true. However, the drawer is only rendered behind `{rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer && <SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer rulerRule={rule} .../>}`, and rule is undefined in the list view, so no drawer ever appears. The user clicks Silence and nothing happens — a broken, dead menu action. Either the silence ability should not be granted without a ruler rule, or the drawer needs to work from the prom rule/identifier.

title: Delete menu item can never appear in the alert list view
body: The Delete menu item is guarded by `{canDelete && rulerRule && ...}`. In the list view (GrafanaRuleListItem -> RuleActionsButtons), only promRule is passed and rulerRule is undefined, so Delete is never rendered even when canDelete is true via the new prom-based abilities. This is a regression: users could previously delete Grafana rules from the list view. The guard appears unnecessary because RuleActionsButtons' handleDelete ignores the rulerRule argument entirely (`handleDelete={() => showDeleteModal(identifier, groupIdentifier)}`) and the delete modal works off the rule identifier, which is now derived from the prom rule. The updated GrafanaGroupLoader test codifies the regression by asserting the menu has exactly 4 items with no Delete.

title: Pause/unpause no longer available from the list view despite canPause being computed
body: The pause menu item requires `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)`, but in the list view rulerRule is always undefined now (ruler API was removed), so MenuItemPauseRule can never render there even when canPause is true via the new useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities path. The grafana-based pause ability is computed and OR'd in but can never result in a visible action, making that check dead code and silently dropping the pause/unpause feature from the list view. If dropping pause is intentional, the prom-based Pause ability should not be requested here; if not, MenuItemPauseRule needs a prom-rule-based variant.

title: Duplicate action can be wrongly enabled for cloud rules based on Grafana-rule permissions
body: For non-Grafana (cloud) rules, promRule is not a Grafana prom rule, so useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities is called with skipToken, i.e. useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined). With rule=undefined, duplicateSupported evaluates to true (not provisioned, not plugin-provided, not loading) and the 'allowed' side is getRulesPermissions('grafana').create — i.e. the Grafana-managed rule create permission. Because canDuplicate ORs the ruler-based and grafana-based abilities, a user who has the Grafana rule-create permission but lacks alert.rules.external.write will now see an enabled 'Duplicate' menu item on Mimir/Cortex/Prometheus rules, whereas before this PR the ability was purely ruler-based and correctly gated on the external write permission. The backend will still reject the save, but the UI now offers an action the user is not permitted to perform.

title: Federated rule group check lost for CombinedRule-based abilities
body: useAllAlertRuleAbilities was refactored to delegate to useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifierV2). The old implementation computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` and treated federated (Mimir cross-tenant) rule groups as immutable, blocking Update/Delete. useAllRulerRuleAbilities hardcodes `const isFederated = false` with a TODO. Since the still-widely-used useAlertRuleAbility hook goes through useAllAlertRuleAbilities, federated rule groups are now considered editable/removable in all consumers of that hook (e.g. the v1 list view RuleActionsButtons), letting users attempt edits/deletes on federated rules that the ruler API will reject.

title: Prom-based abilities wrongly restrict Export/Pause/Restore to alerting rules, excluding Grafana recording rules
body: In useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, ModifyExport, Pause, Restore and DeletePermanently are gated on `isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`. The ruler-based equivalent (useAllRulerRuleAbilities) gates these on `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`, which is true for both Grafana alerting AND recording rules. Grafana recording rules can be paused and can be exported via modify-export, so in the list view (which now only has the prom rule) recording rules lose the Export and Pause actions that they previously had. Use a check that covers both Grafana prom rule types instead of alertingRule.

title: GrafanaRuleListItem rendered without a React key in filtered results
body: In the rules.map switch, the 'grafana' branch returns <GrafanaRuleListItem .../> without key={key}, while the 'datasource' and default branches both pass key={key} (and the previous code passed key to GrafanaRuleLoader). Mixing keyed and unkeyed siblings in the same list triggers React's missing-key warning and makes reconciliation fall back to index-based identity for those items, which can cause state mixups as pages of results are appended.

title: Rule view link lost the returnTo parameter
body: The old GrafanaRuleListItem built the href as createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo }) using createReturnTo(), so navigating back from the rule detail view returned the user to the rule list. The new component builds the href without returnTo, so the 'back' navigation from a rule opened from the list (grouped view or filter view) no longer returns to the list — a small but concrete UX regression.

title: Stale comment and variable name reference removed ruler preloading
body: The ruler prefetch dispatch was removed from getGroupsAndProvideCache, but the comment above the block still says 'This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules, but it improves the UX. Because the user waits a bit longer for the initial load but doesn't need to wait for each group to be loaded', and the variable is still named cacheAndRulerPreload. The comment now describes behavior that no longer exists and is misleading to future readers.

title: Interpolating before querySupportsSplitting() defeats the $__range no-split guard
body: The new `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...))` runs before `partition(queries, querySupportsSplitting)` on line 300. `querySupportsSplitting` deliberately excludes queries containing `$__range` (lines 285-287) because the range variable must be resolved against the full, unsplit time range. Since `applyTemplateVariables` substitutes `$__range` with the full-range duration up front, by the time `isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` is evaluated the token is already gone, so the guard never fires. Queries using `$__range` — previously sent as a single unsplit request — will now be time-split into daily chunks with the full-range duration baked into every sub-query (e.g. `rate(foo[3d])` executed against each 1-day window), and each chunk's lookback extends well outside its own range, returning wrong/inflated results. The range-variable check needs to run against the uninterpolated expr, or `$__range` queries need to be excluded before interpolation is applied.

title: Shard-split queries are now interpolated twice, duplicating ad hoc filters and re-processing interpolated values
body: `runShardSplitQuery` interpolates every target via `datasource.applyTemplateVariables` (line 52), and each shard sub-request is then executed through `runSplitQuery` (line 163), which after this PR interpolates the same targets again (querySplitting.ts:299). The updated test asserting `applyTemplateVariables` is called 5 times (once here plus once per shard group) confirms the double pass. Consequences: (1) `applyTemplateVariables` also injects `request.filters` ad hoc matchers into the stream selector, so with ad hoc filters configured those matchers are appended twice to every selector sent to Loki; (2) any variable replacement value that itself contains a `$`-style token (e.g. `${...}`) will be re-processed and potentially mangled by the second pass. Before this PR each query was interpolated exactly once. Consider interpolating only in one place — e.g. drop the interpolation in `runShardSplitQuery` since `runSplitQuery` now handles it — while noting the shard-values fetch (`fetchLabelValues`) needs the interpolated selector, so the fetch path must still receive an interpolated expr.

title: Interpolating before the split decision defeats the $__range guard, so $__range queries are now split
body: runSplitQuery now maps every target through datasource.applyTemplateVariables before partition() calls querySupportsSplitting(). querySupportsSplitting (line 287) relies on isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr) matching the literal '$__range' in the raw expression to exclude those queries from time-based splitting — the comment above it states these queries must not be split because the range window would be computed incorrectly per chunk. Because applyTemplateVariables runs templateSrv.replace over the expression, '$__range' is resolved to a fixed duration (the full request range) before the check executes, so isQueryWithRangeVariable can never match anymore and queries like avg_over_time({a="b"}[$__range]) or topk(...)[$__range] are now split into per-day chunks, each chunk carrying the same pre-baked full-range window. This silently produces incorrect merged results for exactly the class of queries the guard was created to protect. The split/non-split decision must be made on the original uninterpolated expression (e.g., partition before applying template variables, or check isQueryWithRangeVariable on the pre-interpolation expr).

title: Ad hoc filters are now injected multiple times into split queries
body: applyTemplateVariables is now called with request.filters as the third argument, which injects the ad hoc filter matchers into the selector at split-preparation time. However, every split sub-request is still executed through datasource.runQuery, which applies the same request.filters to its targets again when it calls applyTemplateVariables. In the shard-splitting path it is even worse: runShardSplitQuery (shardQuerySplitting.ts line 52) applies the filters, then runSplitQuery applies them again, then runQuery applies them a third time. With ad hoc filters configured and query splitting enabled, the expression sent to Loki contains the filter matchers duplicated two or three times, e.g. {job="x", cluster="us", cluster="us"}. This is semantically redundant, changes the query text (and therefore cache keys/history) compared to before this PR, and stacks multiple string-level insertions through the naive addAdhocFilters replacement. Filters should be applied in exactly one place in the execution chain.

title: No test that $__range queries remain excluded from splitting
body: The new tests only cover the happy path (variables like $__auto and $step are replaced before execution). The behavior most at risk from moving interpolation to the start of runSplitQuery — that queries containing '$__range' are still routed to the non-splitting path via querySupportsSplitting — has no coverage, and in fact no longer works. A test with an expression such as avg_over_time({a="b"}[$__range]) asserting that only a single, unsplit request is executed would have caught the regression introduced by interpolating before the split decision.

title: Ad hoc filters are now injected multiple times because sub-requests are re-interpolated in runQuery
body: runSplitQuery now interpolates every target via datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters), which injects the request's ad hoc filters into the stream selector. However, the generated sub-requests still carry request.filters and are executed through datasource.runQuery, which interpolates the targets again with the same filters (runQuery/interpolateVariablesInQueries is unchanged by this PR). Variable replacement ($var, $__auto, step) is idempotent, but ad hoc filter injection is not: it appends matchers to the selector each time it runs, so every split sub-query is now sent to Loki with each ad hoc matcher duplicated (e.g. {a="b", env="prod", env="prod"}). In the shard-splitting path it is applied three times (runShardSplitQuery -> runSplitQuery -> runQuery); the updated shard test even bakes this in by expecting applyTemplateVariables to be called 5 times for a single query. The generated expressions are incorrect and progressively more bloated; consider stripping filters from sub-requests after the first application or making the filter injection idempotent.

title: Empty-expression filter moved to before interpolation, so queries whose expr interpolates to empty are no longer dropped
body: Previously runShardSplitQuery filtered query.expr AFTER interpolateVariablesInQueries ran, so a target such as { expr: '$selector' } whose variable expands to an empty string was excluded from shard splitting. The new code applies .filter((query) => query.expr) before applyTemplateVariables, so such a target now flows into groupTargetsByQueryType with an empty interpolated expr and is passed on to runSplitQuery in a sub-request. runSplitQuery filters the now-empty expr away, and if that leaves a group with no runnable targets the requests array is empty, in which case runSplitGroupedQueries throws on requests.filter(...)[0].partition (Math.max(...[]) is -Infinity, so index [0] is undefined). That exception is thrown synchronously inside the promise callback in splitQueriesByStreamShard, leaving the outer observable hanging without completing. Filter again after interpolation, or guard the empty-requests case.

title: FromContext never reads the context-bound logger, so Plugin Request Completed logs lose pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname
body: The new `FromContext` implementation calls the method `d.l.FromContext(ctx)` on the infra `*log.ConcreteLogger`. That method only derives a logger with the `traceID` from the trace span in the context; it does not return the logger that `log.WithContextualAttributes(ctx, p)` stores in the context. The new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` (contextual_logger_middleware.go) attaches the pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname attributes to a context-bound logger via `log.WithContextualAttributes`, and `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` now relies on `m.logger.FromContext(ctx)` to pick those attributes up (the explicit log params were removed from logger_middleware.go). Because the wrapper never retrieves the context-bound logger — it should call the package-level `log.FromContext(ctx)` — the "Plugin Request Completed" log line silently loses the pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID and uname fields that were logged before this change whenever backend request logging (`PluginLogBackendRequests`) is enabled.

title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a discarded instance, breaking log assertions
body: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()` instead of `f`. Any code under test that logs through `FromContext` — which the updated `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` now does — will record calls on a throwaway logger instance, so tests that inject a `TestLogger` and then assert on its `InfoLogs`/`ErrorLogs`/etc. will see zero calls and no captured messages. The fake should return `f` (or record on the shared instance) so log output through `FromContext` is observable in tests.

title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware added without any test coverage
body: This PR introduces a new middleware that moves the `instrumentContext` logic (which endpoint/datasource/user attributes get attached and under which conditions, e.g. nil `DataSourceInstanceSettings` or nil `User`) out of the old instrumentation middleware, but adds no test for it. The only test touched is the renamed metrics middleware test, which covers metrics collection, not the contextual attributes. A regression in which attributes are attached — or in the interaction with `LoggerMiddleware.FromContext` — would go unnoticed.

title: FromContext doc comment is a copy-paste of the New comment and misdescribes the method
body: The doc comment for the new `FromContext` interface method reads "FromContext returns a new contextual Logger that has this logger's context plus the given context.", which is a verbatim copy of the `New` method's comment. `FromContext` takes a `context.Context` and (per its implementations) extracts/derives a logger from it — it does not merge variadic key/value pairs into the logger's context. The comment misleads implementers and callers about the method's contract.

title: traceID field dropped from 'Plugin Request Completed' log line
body: The previous implementation of logRequest explicitly appended "traceID" to the log parameters via tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false), and the tracing import was removed along with that code. The replacement relies on m.logger.FromContext(ctx), which only picks up contextual attributes stored in the context via log.WithContextualAttributes — and the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware (instrumentContext) only sets endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, and uname; it never sets traceID. Nothing else in the middleware chain injects traceID as a contextual log attribute, so the traceID field that operators previously had for correlating these plugin request logs with traces silently disappears from the "Plugin Request Completed" log line whenever plugin_log_backend_requests is enabled. If traceID was intended to be kept, it should either be re-added explicitly to logParams or included in the contextual attributes by the ContextualLoggerMiddleware.

title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a new instance, discarding captured logs
body: TestLogger.FromContext ignores the receiver and returns NewTestLogger(), i.e. a fresh, empty TestLogger. Since LoggerMiddleware now logs through m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...) instead of calling the injected logger directly, any test that passes a TestLogger and then asserts on its InfoLogs/WarnLogs fields will see zero calls — the log entry is recorded on the discarded instance, so the assertion fails (or, worse, if written to tolerate absence, silently passes). The fake should return the receiver itself (return f) so logs emitted through the FromContext path are captured on the same object the test holds.

title: Test function still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware after rename
body: The middleware was renamed from InstrumentationMiddleware to MetricsMiddleware and the test file was renamed accordingly, but the top-level test function is still called TestInstrumentationMiddleware. This is a leftover of the rename and makes test output/searching refer to a type that no longer exists; it should be renamed to TestMetricsMiddleware for consistency with the rest of the PR.

title: LoggerMiddleware still constructed with logger name 'plugin.instrumentation'
body: CreateMiddlewares builds the LoggerMiddleware with log.New("plugin.instrumentation"). Since the InstrumentationMiddleware no longer exists (it is now MetricsMiddleware, plus a separate ContextualLoggerMiddleware), the 'plugin.instrumentation' logger name is a stale reference to the removed type and makes log source attribution misleading — log lines emitted by the LoggerMiddleware now appear to come from an 'instrumentation' component that was deliberately renamed. A name such as 'plugin.logger' or 'plugin.client' would reflect the new structure.

title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh logger, making FromContext log calls unobservable in tests
body: The new FromContext method on TestLogger ignores the receiver and returns a brand-new TestLogger instance. This PR changes LoggerMiddleware to emit its "Plugin Request Completed" log via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), so any test that constructs the middleware with plog.NewTestLogger() and then asserts on InfoLogs/ErrorLogs of that instance will see zero recorded calls — the log entry is written to an unreachable instance. Tests verifying plugin request logging will either fail or (if written against the new behavior) silently assert nothing. FromContext should return f (or record on f and return it) so log calls made through FromContext remain assertable.

title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware and the moved log attributes have no test coverage
body: This PR introduces ContextualLoggerMiddleware, which is now solely responsible for attaching endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname to the request context, and simultaneously removes those explicit fields from LoggerMiddleware's "Plugin Request Completed" log line. No test was added for the new middleware, and the renamed metrics_middleware_test.go only asserts prometheus metrics. Nothing verifies that the contextual attributes are actually injected or that the plugin egress log line still contains pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID, so a regression (middleware reordering, or a change in log.WithContextualAttributes / ConcreteLogger.FromContext behavior) would silently strip these identifying fields from plugin request logs.

title: LoggerMiddleware now silently depends on ContextualLoggerMiddleware running before it
body: Previously LoggerMiddleware derived pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName and dsUID itself from the request's PluginContext. After this change it relies on m.logger.FromContext(ctx) picking up attributes injected by the separate ContextualLoggerMiddleware, so the two middlewares are order-dependent: the stack in CreateMiddlewares must keep NewContextualLoggerMiddleware() before NewLoggerMiddleware(...). Neither constructor documents this coupling. Any other code path that builds its own middleware list (tests, alternate decorators, or a future reordering) will get "Plugin Request Completed" logs missing all plugin-identifying fields, with no error. The ordering requirement should be documented, or the fields kept in LoggerMiddleware.

title: Explicit traceID attribute removed from plugin request completion logs
body: The old logRequest implementation explicitly extracted the trace ID via tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false) and appended it as the "traceID" field on the "Plugin Request Completed" log line. That code was deleted and replaced with m.logger.FromContext(ctx), so trace-log correlation for plugin egress logs now depends entirely on whether infra/log's ConcreteLogger.FromContext adds the trace ID from the context — behavior outside this diff and not covered by any test in this package. If FromContext does not add it, plugin request logs lose traceID and can no longer be correlated with traces.

title: Local cache is populated before the DB write, so rejected devices bypass the limit on retry
body: In tagDeviceUI, the local cache entry for the device is set (a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})) BEFORE calling anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice. When the device limit is reached, CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, which now propagates up to Anonymous.Authenticate and rejects the request. However, the device's cache key has already been written, so for the next 29 minutes every subsequent request from that same device hits the cache and returns nil without ever touching the database — meaning authentication succeeds. The net effect is that a device over the limit is blocked exactly once and then freely allowed in on any retry, which defeats the feature. The cache entry should only be set after CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds.

title: Device limit check is racy: COUNT then INSERT is not atomic
body: CreateOrUpdateDevice enforces the limit by first running CountDevices and only inserting if count < deviceLimit, with no transaction or database-level constraint tying the two together. Two concurrent requests for distinct new devices can both observe count < limit and both insert, exceeding the configured limit. With multiple Grafana replicas each doing this independently (and per-instance local caches), the overshoot can be larger. If the limit is meant to be enforced (e.g., for licensing/abuse control), the check-and-insert needs to be atomic (single transaction with locking, or a conditional INSERT based on a subquery count).

title: Device-limit rejection surfaces as a raw error, producing HTTP 500 for end users
body: When TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, Authenticate now returns that plain error (return nil, err). The authn layer has no typed handling for this error, so anonymous users who exceed the device limit will get a generic HTTP 500 Internal Server Error with the message 'device limit reached' instead of a deliberate status such as 429 Too Many Requests (or 401) with a user-facing explanation. The error should be wrapped in a typed authn/response error that maps to an appropriate status code and message.

title: Device tagging moved onto the synchronous auth path without timeout or panic recovery
body: Previously TagDevice was invoked in a background goroutine guarded by recover() and a 2-minute timeout (timeoutTag), so a slow or panicking database call could not affect request authentication.
