The primary purpose of this PR is producing standard DER signatures for ES256/ES384/ES512 client authentication without BouncyCastle, so the test should additionally verify the DER output against an independent implementation (e.g. `Signature.verify` with the JCA Signature, or fixed known-answer test vectors comparing against BouncyCastle's encoding), and ideally cover the end-to-end AuthzClient-with-ES256-credentials path.

title: New abstract method order() breaks all existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: The PR adds `int order();` as a new abstract method on the public `CryptoProvider` SPI. Only the four implementations in this repository were updated. Any third-party or downstream implementation of this interface (this is the documented SPI for plugging in crypto providers, loaded via ServiceLoader in CryptoIntegration) will fail to compile against the new keycloak-common, and — worse — an existing compiled provider jar on the classpath will throw AbstractMethodError at runtime when `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider()` sorts providers by calling `order()`, breaking previously working deployments at startup. The method should be given a default (e.g. `default int order() { return 0; }`) to preserve backward compatibility, as was already done for other methods on this interface (`getSupportedKeyStoreTypes`, `getSupportedRsaKeySizes`).

title: Multiple same-order providers are now silently accepted instead of failing fast
body: Previously, having more than one CryptoProvider on the classpath caused a hard `IllegalStateException` ("Multiple crypto providers loaded... Make sure only one cryptoProvider available on the classpath"). Now `detectProvider` sorts by `order()` descending and silently uses the first one, merely logging the rest at debug level. DefaultCryptoProvider, FIPS1402Provider and WildFlyElytronProvider are all assigned order 200, so if two of them end up on the classpath together (exactly the misconfiguration the old error guarded against), the winner is decided by ServiceLoader/classpath iteration order. In particular, a FIPS deployment that accidentally also ships the default (non-FIPS) provider jar will silently run non-FIPS-compliant crypto instead of failing at startup. The fail-fast check should be retained for ties at the highest order, or the FIPS provider should be given a strictly higher order.

title: ECDSA test only round-trips through its own encoder/decoder and never validates the DER output
body: The test takes a JDK-produced DER signature, converts it to concatenated R||S, converts back to DER with the new ASN1Encoder, decodes again with the new ASN1Decoder, and asserts the two concatenated forms are equal. Because both conversions share the same new implementation, a systematic encoder bug that the matching decoder tolerates (e.g. swapped r/s integers, wrong integer sign/zero-padding handling) still passes the assertion. The test never checks that the re-encoded DER byte array is actually valid — e.g. by verifying `asn1Des` with `Signature.getInstance(...)` initialized with the public key, or by comparing it against the original JDK-produced `sign` bytes / a known-good implementation such as the existing BouncyCastle-based ECDSACryptoProvider. As written, the test would not catch an encoder that produces signatures no real verifier accepts.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the default keystore provider, not BouncyCastle
body: `getBouncyCastleProvider()` is implemented as `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, which returns whatever JCA provider supplies the default keystore type (typically the SUN provider) — it has nothing to do with BouncyCastle. Callers of this method (e.g. `BouncyIntegration.init()`, which registers the returned provider and then uses `BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER` as the provider name for `Cipher`/`KeyFactory`/`Signature.getInstance(alg, PROVIDER)` calls) will be handed the SUN provider under the assumption it is BouncyCastle, causing failures for algorithms/paddings only BC provides (e.g. "AES/CBC/PKCS7Padding") or silently using a different provider than intended. If there is no BouncyCastle on the classpath this method should return null (as WildFlyElytronProvider does) rather than a mislabelled unrelated provider.

title: Indefinite-length form returns -1 and later causes unchecked NegativeArraySizeException
body: `readLength()` returns -1 for the BER indefinite-length marker (0x80). Callers pass this straight into `read(int length)`, which does `new byte[length]` — so a signature blob containing a 0x80 length byte throws an unchecked `NegativeArraySizeException` instead of the `IOException` callers expect for malformed input. Since this decoder parses externally supplied signature bytes, malformed input should be rejected with a checked IOException (or the indefinite-length case explicitly disallowed, since DER never uses it).

title: Dead encoder instances created and discarded in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
body: Lines 114-115 call `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger)` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger)` and discard the results; the actual DER is built again immediately below in the `writeDerSeq(...)` call. The two discarded statements are leftover dead code and should be removed to avoid confusion about which encoding path is authoritative.

title: Client removal fails with UnsupportedOperationException when V1 and V2 fine-grained-authz features are both enabled
body: AdminPermissions.registerListener now gates the ClientRemovedEvent handler only on Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (the V1 flag), which can be enabled at the same time as ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. When both are on, the listener calls AdminPermissions.management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false); management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, clients() returns the new ClientPermissionsV2, and setPermissionsEnabled unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). The exception propagates out of the event listener during session.clients().removeClient(...), so deleting any client — and by extension deleting a realm, which removes its clients — returns a 500. The same landmine exists for isPermissionsEnabled/resource/getPermissions. Either make the V2 overrides graceful no-ops for these legacy management methods, or make the listener skip when the V2 feature is active.

title: Missing null check and no migration for the new Clients resource/scopes on existing realms
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no per-client resource exists the code loads the 'Clients' type resource via AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) and immediately calls authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) without checking for null. getResourceTypeResource returns null whenever the admin-permissions resource server was initialized before this change: AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns early when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() already exists, so realms that already had FGAP v2 enabled never get the new 'Clients' resource or the new scopes (configure, map-roles, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite). For such realms every client admin operation that reaches this fallback throws an NPE (500), and creating any Clients-typed permission fails with 'Scope does not exist'. Add a null check here (mirroring the no-arg hasPermission) and provide an upgrade path that adds the new schema objects to existing admin-permissions resource servers.

title: canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles ignore manage permission and MANAGE_CLIENTS role
body: These three methods only evaluate the explicit map-roles* scopes and, unlike canManage/canView in the same class, do not short-circuit on root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS) and do not treat a manage permission as implying map-roles. This is inconsistent with the rest of the class (canConfigure and canView both chain through canManage) and with UserPermissionsV2, where manage transitively grants map-roles (asserted by testTransitiveUserPermissions). Consequence: under V2, an admin holding the manage-clients role, or a manage permission on a specific client or on all clients, gets 403 when mapping client roles to users or adding composite roles — a regression compared to V1 behavior, where manage clients implied the ability to map its roles.

title: getResourceName does not resolve names for Clients-typed resources
body: getResourceName only special-cases the Users resource type, resolving the stored user id to the username. For the newly added Clients resource type it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is never set for FGAP-created resources (getOrCreateResource only sets name/scopes), so admin REST responses and the admin console will show a null/empty name for client-typed permission resources instead of the client's clientId. Add a Clients branch mirroring the Users one that resolves ClientModel.getClientId().

title: Javadoc on void require methods incorrectly says "Returns {@code true}"
body: The newly added javadoc for requireView() ("Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}.") and requireViewClientScopes() ("Returns {@code true} if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}.") describes a boolean return, but both methods are void and throw ForbiddenException on failure. This contradicts the otherwise consistent 'Throws ForbiddenException if ...' wording used for the other require* methods and misleads implementers of the interface.

title: setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, breaking client deletion when FGAP V2 is enabled
body: ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). However, AdminPermissions.registerListener (AdminPermissions.java, in the ClientRemovedEvent branch) calls management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false) on every client removal. When Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, AdminPermissions.management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 and clients() now returns this ClientPermissionsV2, so deleting any client fires the event and the listener throws. Provider event listeners run synchronously inside the transaction, so the exception propagates and rolls back client deletion entirely. The V2 variant should either no-op here (V2 cleans up via orphan-resource removal) or the listener should skip clients for V2.

title: canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, breaking token exchange whenever V2 feature is on
body: canExchangeTo(ClientModel, ClientModel, AccessToken) throws UnsupportedOperationException. The standard token exchange flow (AbstractTokenExchangeProvider) builds an evaluator via AdminPermissions.evaluator(session, realm, auth) and calls auth.clients().canExchangeTo(authenticatedClient, targetClient, token) for every client-to-client exchange, regardless of whether the realm uses fine-grained admin permissions. With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled, MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returns this class, so any token exchange to a different target client results in an unhandled UnsupportedOperationException (HTTP 500) instead of an allow/deny decision. The unused getEvaluationContext helper and unused TOKEN_EXCHANGE import suggest this method was left unfinished; at minimum it should fail closed with a proper denial rather than throwing.

title: canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles lack the manage fallback, denying role-based and manage-permission admins
body: The three canMap* overrides only check hasPermission(client, MAP_ROLES / MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE / MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE). In V1 (ClientPermissions) these methods short-circuit with a manage check (manage-clients admin role / manage permission on the client), and the V2 Users implementation follows the same rule — testTransitiveUserPermissions in this PR asserts that a manage permission on users implies map-roles. Here, an administrator holding the manage-clients realm role or an FGAP manage permission on a client (or on all clients) gets canManage(client) == true but canMapRoles(client) == false, so role mapping for that client is denied. This is an access-control regression versus V1 and is inconsistent with the Users V2 semantics; the tests only pass because they grant the map-roles scopes explicitly.

title: getClientsWithPermission can never return real client IDs
body: getClientsWithPermission(scope) iterates resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) and adds resource.getName() to the result. However, per-client resources are created in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource via resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, owner) which never sets the resource type — only the type-level "Clients" resource created in init() has type set. So findByType never matches per-client resources (their type is null), meaning clients the caller was explicitly granted per-client permissions on are never returned. The only possible match is the "Clients" type resource itself, whose name is the literal string "Clients" — not a client ID — so the returned set is either empty or contains a bogus entry that callers comparing against client IDs (e.g., client listing filters) cannot use. The method effectively never returns a valid client ID.

title: No migration for realms whose admin-permissions resource server was initialized with the Users-only schema
body: init() returns early when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null, so realms that enabled FGAP V2 before this change keep a resource server containing only the Users resource and the Users scopes. The new Clients scopes (configure, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite) and the "Clients" type resource are never created for them. Consequences after upgrade: creating a Clients scope-permission fails validation in getScope with ModelValidationException("Scope [configure] does not exist."); creating a client resource in getOrCreateResource throws ModelException("No scopes found.") because the new scopes can't be found; and ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission falls back to a null "Clients" resource. An upgrade/re-initialization path that adds the new scopes and the Clients type resource to existing admin-permissions resource servers is needed.

title: getResourceName does not handle the Clients resource type, returning null display names
body: getResourceName(session, policy, resource) only special-cases USERS resourceType (mapping to "All users" or the username). For a policy with resourceType "Clients" it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is never set for resources created via getOrCreateResource or init(), so the admin console/REST representation of client permissions shows blank resource names. It should mirror the Users handling (e.g., "All clients" for the type resource and the client's clientId for per-client resources).

title: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) may call findByResource with a null resource
body: In the fallback branch, resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) can return null (e.g., when the "Clients" type resource doesn't exist, or supportsAuthorizationSchema is false). The very next statement calls authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) without a null check, which can throw a NullPointerException in store implementations that dereference the resource (e.g., resource.getId()) instead of simply denying access. A null check returning false should guard this call.

title: Javadoc on requireView()/requireViewClientScopes() describes a boolean return for void methods
body: The new javadoc for requireView() says "Returns true if canView() returns true" and requireViewClientScopes() says "Returns true if canViewClientScopes() returns true". Both methods are void and their contract is to throw ForbiddenException when the corresponding can* check fails (as correctly documented on the other require* methods). The documentation is misleading about the method contract and should say it throws ForbiddenException if the check returns false.

title: Deleting a client throws UnsupportedOperationException in FGAP V2 realms
body: The ProviderEventListener registered in AdminPermissions.registerListener handles ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent by calling management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) (AdminPermissions.java line 91). When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled (which also enables the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature, so the new feature check in the listener passes), management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, whose clients() now returns ClientPermissionsV2, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). The exception propagates out of the event listener during the client-removal transaction, so deleting any client in a realm with FGAP V2 enabled fails with a server error. Additionally, because no V2 cleanup is implemented, the per-client authorization resources created in the admin-permissions resource server (via AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource) are never removed when a client is deleted, leaving orphan resources behind. setPermissionsEnabled should be implemented for V2 (removing the client resource and its permissions from the admin-permissions resource server) instead of throwing.

title: canExchangeTo and management/permissions endpoints now throw UnsupportedOperationException under V2
body: ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, but the token-exchange flow (StandardTokenExchangeProvider) invokes AdminPermissions.evaluator(session, realm, auth).clients().canExchangeTo(client, targetClient, token) for client-to-client exchanges. With FGAP V2 enabled this now resolves to ClientPermissionsV2, so every token exchange attempt produces a 500 instead of an allow/deny decision; before this change clients() returned the V1 implementation which evaluated or short-circuited normally. The same applies to the admin management/permissions endpoints (GET/PUT /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id}/management/permissions), which call getPermissions, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, mapRolesPermission, mapRolesClientScopePermission, mapRolesCompositePermission, exchangeToPermission, isPermissionsEnabled and resource() — all of which now throw under V2. If these paths are intentionally unsupported in V2 they should fail with a controlled 4xx rather than propagating UnsupportedOperationException as a 500.

title: Null 'Clients' type resource is dereferenced; existing V2 realms never get the new resource/scopes
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no per-client resource exists the code falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and immediately passes the result to authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) without a null check. getResourceTypeResource returns null when the 'Clients' resource does not exist, and passing null into the JPA-backed findByResource throws, yielding a 500 on any client admin operation (view/manage/configure) for such realms. This is reachable because AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns early whenever realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null, so realms that initialized admin permissions before this change never receive the new 'Clients' resource or the new scopes (configure, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite) — no migration/backfill is provided in this PR. Either add a migration that creates the new schema objects for existing admin-permissions resource servers, or at minimum guard the null resource before calling findByResource.

title: Unused imports, unused logger and dead code in ClientPermissionsV2
body: ClientPermissionsV2 contains an unused static import of AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE (line 46) and an unused import of org.keycloak.authorization.model.Scope (line 27), which will fail Keycloak's checkstyle UnusedImports rule and break the build. The declared logger field is never used, and the private method getEvaluationContext (lines 262-272) is dead code that also solely justifies the ClientModelIdentity/DefaultEvaluationContext/EvaluationContext imports. Remove the unused imports, the logger and the dead method, or wire getEvaluationContext into the evaluation path if it was meant to be used.

title: CAUTION overstates when the rolling-updates feature is required
body: The new CAUTION block states that the `rolling-updates` feature must be enabled, 'Otherwise, the Keycloak Operator will fail.' This is too broad. The companion test change in `UpgradeTest.createInitialDeployment` enables the feature only when `spec.update.strategy` is explicitly set; the default case (no update strategy) deliberately deploys the Keycloak CR without the feature and still expects rolling-upgrade behavior for configuration changes (`testCacheMaxCount` with a null strategy asserts `eventuallyRollingUpgradeStatus`). So the Operator only fails when `spec.update` is used without the feature, not in general. As written, the doc will scare users into enabling a preview feature they don't need for the default upgrade behavior. The caution should say the feature is required only when setting `spec.update.strategy`.

title: Feature-disabled exit code 4 and the check command path are not tested
body: This PR introduces a new exit code `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` (and renumbers the recreate exit code from 4 to 3), making the exit code the documented contract for automation ('they should rely only on the exit code of the check command'). However, `testFeatureNotEnabled` only asserts the error message text for the `metadata` subcommand; it never asserts that the exit code is 4, and it does not exercise the `check` subcommand with the feature disabled at all. A regression that returns exit code 0 or 1 when the feature is disabled — which would silently break GitOps pipelines that branch on this code — would not be caught. The test should assert `cliResult.assertError(...)` plus the exit code 4, and cover `update-compatibility check` without `--features=rolling-updates`.

title: Recreate-upgrade exit code changed from 4 to 3, breaking the documented scripting contract
body: The previous release documented and implemented exit code 4 as 'Rolling Upgrade is not possible, shut down the deployment before applying the new configuration' (RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE = 4). This PR reassigns 4 to FEATURE_DISABLED and changes the recreate signal to 3. The update-compatibility guide explicitly tells users not to rely on anything except the command's exit code, so existing CI/CD pipelines written against the old contract (e.g., 'if exit code == 4 then do a recreate upgrade') will silently misbehave after upgrade: a recreate-required check now returns 3 (which such scripts will treat as an unknown/error case, potentially aborting the pipeline or worse, proceeding as if rolling were possible depending on the fallback), and a disabled feature now returns 4 (which such scripts will interpret as 'recreate required'). If this renumbering is intentional, it needs an explicit callout in the release notes/upgrading guide so users can update their automation, not just a silent change in the command's own doc page.

title: No test asserts the exit codes that the documentation declares as the stable contract
body: The docs added in this PR (update-compatibility.adoc) present the exit code table (0 = rolling possible, 3 = recreate required, 4 = feature disabled) as the supported scripting interface, yet the tests only assert on log output. In particular, testFeatureNotEnabled asserts only the stderr message but never checks that the process actually exits with CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED (4), and testWrongVersions asserts the error text but never checks exit code 3. If picocli.exit(...) were skipped, mis-mapped, or a PropertyException (exit code 2) were thrown instead, all tests would still pass while the documented contract would be broken. Add assertions like assertEquals(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED, result.exitCode()) and assertEquals(3, ...) for the recreate case.

title: Exit code 4 silently changes meaning from 'recreate required' to 'feature disabled'
body: This change reassigns the `check` command's exit codes: `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` moves from 4 to 3, and 4 becomes `FEATURE_DISABLED`. The tool's own documentation (update-compatibility.adoc) explicitly tells consumers to rely only on the exit code for automation, so exit codes are the public contract of this command. Any pipeline written against the previously released behavior (exit 4 = rolling upgrade not possible, shut down the deployment) will now either misinterpret 'feature disabled' as 'recreate required' (causing unnecessary downtime) or, worse, fail to handle the new exit code 3 and potentially treat a required recreate upgrade as an error or even proceed with a rolling upgrade against an incompatible Infinispan/Keycloak version. Even for a preview feature, reusing a previously emitted exit code for a different meaning is risky; a safer approach would be to keep 4 as recreate and use a new, previously unused code (e.g., 5) for the feature-disabled case, or at minimum call out the renumbering explicitly in the docs/release notes.

title: CAUTION claims the Operator will fail without the rolling-updates feature, contradicting the documented default behavior
body: The new CAUTION block states: 'While on preview stage, the feature `rolling-updates` must be enabled. Otherwise, the Keycloak Operator will fail.' This contradicts the rest of the same section, which documents that with `update.strategy` unset the operator 'defaults to mimicking Keycloak 26.1 or older behavior' (scale down on image change, rolling for config changes) — behavior that does not require the feature. The updated `UpgradeTest` confirms this: `createInitialDeployment` with a `null` strategy deliberately does not enable the `rolling-updates` feature and the deployment/upgrade proceeds normally. As written, the warning tells users the operator will break unless they enable the feature, which will drive them to enable a preview feature unnecessarily (or panic when they don't). The caution should be scoped to 'when configuring `spec.update.strategy`' rather than claiming the operator fails outright.

title: New exit codes 3 and 4 are never asserted in tests
body: The docs for the update-compatibility tool explicitly instruct users to 'rely only on the exit code of the check command' for automation, making the exit codes the tool's stable contract. However, none of the tests verify the new codes: `testFeatureNotEnabled` only asserts the error message (never that the process exits with code 4 / `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED`), and `testWrongVersions` only asserts error messages (never that a recreate-incompatible result exits with code 3). Only the success path asserts `exitCode() == 0`. A regression that swapped or dropped these exit codes would break consumer automation without failing any test; assertions on the exit codes for both the feature-disabled and recreate-required paths should be added.

title: canManage() grants manage rights to admins holding only the view scope on all groups
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() the fallback permission check is `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, i.e. it returns true when the caller has either the VIEW or the MANAGE scope on the all-groups resource. This appears to be a copy-paste of canView() directly above it. As a result, an admin who is granted only a 'view' permission for all groups (e.g. via an all-groups scope permission with the view scope) is treated as being able to manage groups globally: the no-arg canManage()/requireManage() is what GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() uses to authorize creating top-level groups, so a view-only admin can create groups. Per-group manage (canManage(GroupModel)) correctly checks only MANAGE, so the no-arg variant should drop AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW from the expected scopes.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authz resource IDs instead of group IDs
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), the granted set is populated with `groupResource.getId()`, which is the authorization-store Resource UUID. In the V2 schema the group ID is stored as the resource *name* (AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup returns group.getId() and getOrCreateResource creates the resource with that name). Callers of this method — UsersResource.searchForUser, BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser and UsersResource.getUsersCount — feed the returned IDs into the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute / group-filtered count queries, which expect real group IDs. Concretely: an admin whose only user visibility comes from a view-members/manage-members permission on all groups will get a non-empty set containing a resource UUID, the GROUPS session attribute is set with it, and searchForUserStream filters by membership in a non-existent group, so the admin sees zero users. The method should add groupResource.getName() (the group ID), mirroring what the V1 implementation did by stripping the prefix from the resource name.

title: Per-resource permission check in getGroupIdsWithViewPermission looks up resources by ID as if it were a name, and per-group resources are never typed
body: Inside the findByType visitor in GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), the code calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), VIEW_MEMBERS, MANAGE_MEMBERS)`. However hasPermission(String groupId, ...) does `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, so it is passed a resource ID where a resource name is expected; the lookup returns null and evaluation silently falls back to the all-groups resource instead of evaluating the policies attached to that specific group resource. Additionally, resources created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource never have their type set (no setType call), so resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) will not even iterate per-group resources — only the 'all groups' resource created in init() carries the type. Net effect: view-members/manage-members grants on individual groups are never detected by this method, and (combined with the getId() bug) the group-ID set used to filter user searches is wrong or empty.

title: No upgrade path for realms that enabled admin permissions before the Groups resource type existed
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init() creates the 'Groups' all-resource and the group-specific scopes (manage-members, view-members, manage-membership) only when the admin-permissions client is first created for a realm. Realms that already have admin permissions enabled (resource server initialized by an earlier version) will never get the new resource type or scopes, and this PR adds no migration. Consequences for such realms: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource() returns null for 'Groups', and GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission then calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, null)`, which dereferences the null resource in the JPA store implementation and throws (500 on group admin endpoints); likewise creating any group permission fails because the scope lookups in getOrCreateResource find no 'manage-members'/'view-members' scopes and throw ModelException("No scopes found."). A migration/initialization step that adds the new resource type and scopes to existing admin-permissions resource servers is needed.

title: getResourceName does not resolve names for the new Groups resource type
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName() resolves human-readable names only for the Users resource type; for everything else it returns resource.getDisplayName(). Group resources created via getOrCreateResource are named by group ID and never have a display name set, so anywhere this method is used to present resources of a Groups-type policy (e.g. permission listings in the admin UI), the entry will show null/empty instead of the group's name or path. A GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE branch resolving the group (e.g. its name or path) should be added, analogous to the existing Users handling.

title: Deleting a group throws UnsupportedOperationException when FGAP V2 is enabled
body: AdminPermissions.registerListener registers a ProviderEventListener (registered whenever Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled, which V2 implies) that on GroupModel.GroupRemovedEvent calls management(session, realm).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false). With the V2 feature enabled, AdminPermissions.management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, whose groups() method (added in this PR) returns GroupPermissionsV2, and GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). Provider events are published synchronously during group removal, so deleting any group with V2 enabled propagates this exception, fails the DELETE request and rolls back the transaction. Before this PR, MgmtPermissionsV2 did not override groups(), so the V1 implementation handled the event without throwing. The V2 class should either implement the cleanup of the group's authorization resources/permissions or make these management methods no-ops instead of throwing on this path.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses the authorization resource UUID instead of the group id
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, the findByType callback calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) and granted.add(groupResource.getId()). Per-group resources are created in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource with the resource name set to the group id, whereas Resource.getId() is the internal UUID of the authorization resource entity. Two consequences: (1) hasPermission does resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId), so passing the resource UUID never finds the per-group resource and silently falls back to evaluating the "Groups" all-resource — per-group view-members/manage-members grants are never detected, or the wrong resource is evaluated; (2) the returned set contains resource UUIDs, but callers (UsersResource.searchForUser, UsersResource.getUsersCount, BruteForceUsersResource) store it in the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute / pass it to user-count queries that expect group ids, so user searches and counts for group-scoped admins are filtered by non-existent groups and return wrong (usually empty) results. The method should use groupResource.getName().

title: Per-instance resources are created without a resource type
body: getOrCreateResource creates per-instance resources (for a specific user, group, or client) via resourceStore.create(...) and updateScopes(...) but never calls resource.setType(resourceType). Only the "all resources" created in init() get a type. GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission enumerates per-group resources via resourceStore.findByType(server, "Groups", ...), so those resources are never returned there, and any type-based lookup/fallback in the policy engine will not see them either. The resource type should be set (resource.setType(resourceType)) when the resource is created.

title: canManage() is satisfied by the view scope, allowing group management with view-only permission
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE), i.e. an admin holding only the view scope on the Groups resource type is treated as able to manage groups globally. The no-arg requireManage() guards privileged operations — for example GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup calls auth.groups().requireManage() — so an admin with a view-only "all groups" permission can create top-level groups (privilege escalation). The per-group overload canManage(GroupModel) correctly requires only the MANAGE scope; the no-arg variant should do the same. The javadoc added to GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage() in this PR also documents VIEW as sufficient and should be corrected.

title: No upgrade path for realms whose admin-permissions client already exists
body: init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null, so realms where fine-grained admin permissions V2 were initialized before this change never receive the new group scopes (manage-membership, manage-members, view-members) or the "Groups" all-resource. In such realms, creating a group permission fails at runtime: getScope() throws ModelValidationException("Scope [...] does not exist.") and getOrCreateResource() throws ModelException("No scopes found."), while GroupPermissionsV2's fallback getResourceTypeResource(session, server, "Groups") returns null. A migration or schema-reconciliation step for existing resource servers is needed so upgraded realms can use the new Groups resource type.

title: getResourceName has no handling for Groups resources
body: getResourceName only resolves a human-readable name for the Users resource type; for every other type it returns resource.getDisplayName(), which is never set for resources created by getOrCreateResource. For a Groups-type policy the resource name is the group id, so permission listings in the admin console will render an empty/null resource name for group permissions. A GROUPS branch should resolve the group (e.g., to its name or path), or at minimum fall back to resource.getName() instead of the unset display name.

title: canManage() returns true for admins holding only the 'view' scope on Groups
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() the fallback permission check is `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)` — it accepts the VIEW scope as sufficient for a manage-level decision. The no-arg canManage()/requireManage() is the guard for creating top-level groups (GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup calls `auth.groups().requireManage()`), so an admin who has been granted only the `view` scope on the Groups resource type (an all-groups view permission) will pass requireManage() and be able to create groups. The per-group overload canManage(GroupModel) correctly checks only MANAGE, so this looks like a copy-paste of the canView() scope list. The new javadoc on GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage() repeats the same wrong claim ('Also if it has permission to VIEW or MANAGE groups'), suggesting the doc was written to match the bug. Fix by checking only AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE here.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission confuses authz resource IDs with group IDs
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission the callback does `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` and `granted.add(groupResource.getId())`. But per-group resources are created (AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource/resolveGroup) with the resource NAME equal to the group model ID, while resource.getId() is the separate authz resource entity ID. Two consequences: (1) hasPermission(String groupId, ...) resolves the resource via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, so passing the entity ID never finds the per-group resource and always falls back to the all-groups 'Groups' resource — per-group view-members/manage-members permissions are never actually evaluated here; (2) the IDs placed in the returned set are authz resource IDs, yet callers (UsersResource.searchForUser, UsersResource.getUsersCount, BruteForceUsersResource) feed them into `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)`, where the user provider treats them as group model IDs to restrict the user search by membership. When the set is non-empty (e.g. an all-groups view-members permission exists), the membership filter matches no real group and user search/count return empty results for an admin who should see users. The V1 implementation correctly derives the group ID from the resource name (`resource.getName().substring(...)`) and passes the Resource object directly. This should use groupResource.getName() both for the permission check and for the granted set (and skip the 'Groups' type resource itself). The new GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest does not catch this because the post-query `canView`/`canViewByGroup` filter masks the broken DB-level filtering and pagination/count behavior is never asserted.

title: Group deletion fails with UnsupportedOperationException when V2 is enabled
body: AdminPermissions.registerListener registers a ProviderEventListener (whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled, which V2 depends on) that on GroupModel.GroupRemovedEvent calls `management(session, realm).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false)`. With the V2 feature enabled, AdminPermissions.management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, and this PR adds the MgmtPermissionsV2.groups() override returning GroupPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled (and isPermissionsEnabled/resource/getPermissions, etc.) unconditionally throws `new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. The exception propagates out of realm.removeGroup(), so deleting any group via the admin API (GroupResource.deleteGroup) will fail with a 500 under V2. Before this PR, MgmtPermissionsV2 inherited the V1 GroupPermissions, whose setPermissionsEnabled(false) is a harmless no-op cleanup, so this is a regression introduced by the groups() override. The V2 class needs a non-throwing implementation for the removal listener path (e.g. delete the authz resource/permissions for the group, or a no-op), and the same applies to GroupResource.get/setManagementPermissionsEnabled which call isPermissionsEnabled/setPermissionsEnabled when the V1 management endpoint is hit with V2 active.

title: No upgrade path: existing admin-permissions realms never get the Groups resource type and group scopes
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null, and nothing else in this PR creates the newly added artifacts for realms that already enabled admin permissions before this change: the 'Groups' all-resource and the three new scopes manage-membership, manage-members, view-members. For such upgraded realms: (a) creating a group permission through the policy API fails because getScope() looks up scopes by name and throws ModelValidationException("Scope [...] does not exist.") for the group scopes that were never created; (b) GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)` which returns null (the 'Groups' resource was never created), and then calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and `new ResourcePermission(resource, ...)` with a null resource, risking a NullPointerException on every group permission evaluation (canView/canManage/canViewMembers/etc.). A migration/upgrade step (or lazy creation on first use) is needed to add the new resource type resource and scopes to pre-existing admin permissions clients.

title: Resources created by getOrCreateResource are never assigned their resource type
body: In getOrCreateResource the newly created resource gets a name and scopes but never `resource.setType(resourceType)` (unlike the all-resources created in init(), which do set the type). GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission relies on `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` to enumerate per-group resources, so resources created for individual groups through the permission API will not be found by that query even after the ID-vs-name issue is fixed. The V1 GroupPermissions.initialize() sets the type ("Group") on its resources for the same reason. Set the type when creating the resource in getOrCreateResource.

title: Javadoc errors on requireManageMembers and getGroupIdsWithViewPermission
body: The javadoc for requireManageMembers(GroupModel) says "Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canManageMembership(GroupModel)} returns {@code false}" but the method delegates to canManageMembers, not canManageMembership. Additionally, getGroupIdsWithViewPermission's javadoc says "@return Stream of IDs of groups with view permission" while the method returns a Set, and its opening sentence references UserPermissionEvaluator#canView() although the contract is about group view-members permissions. These misleading docs describe the wrong method contract for an authorization-sensitive interface.

title: Java MessageFormat syntax used in i18next-based account-ui bundle
body: The keycloak.v3 account console is a React app that renders this bundle with i18next, whose interpolation syntax is `{{0}}` (as used by all neighboring keys in this file, e.g. `error-invalid-length-too-short='{{0}}' must have minimal length of {{1}}.`). This change replaces `{{0}}/{{1}}/{{2}}` with `{0}/{1}/{2}` and appends a Java MessageFormat choice pattern `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}`. When the account UI displays `error-invalid-multivalued-size`, i18next will not substitute `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}` and will print the raw choice expression literally, so end users see `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.` instead of a formatted message. The Java MessageFormat variant belongs in the server-side bundles (base admin/login themes); this JS bundle should keep the i18next syntax (the previous `{{0}} ... value(s)` form, or i18next pluralization).

title: Java MessageFormat choice pattern used in i18next-based admin-ui bundle
body: The keycloak.v2 admin console renders this bundle with i18next, where positional interpolation is `{{0}}`. The previous i18next form (`Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).`) worked; the Java MessageFormat version should only be used in the server-rendered theme bundles.

title: Diff-trimming code can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException
body: When a sanitized value differs from the original, the code trims common prefix (`start`) and common suffix (`end`) independently. If the common prefix and suffix overlap — i.e. start + end exceeds the length of one of the strings — then `value.substring(start, value.length() - end)` or `sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end)` is called with beginIndex > endIndex and throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. For example value `helloaab` sanitized to `helloab` (or `ab` vs `aab`) yields start=6, end=2, so substring(6, 5) is invoked. This would crash the verifier with a confusing exception instead of reporting the illegal HTML. `end` should be capped, e.g. at min(value.length(), sanitized.length()) - start.

title: verifySafeHtml throws untyped RuntimeException instead of MojoExecutionException
body: verify() wraps IOErrors in MojoExecutionException with a clear message, but the newly added verifySafeHtml() re-opens the message file and the derived English file and throws RuntimeException on any IOException (e.g. a community translation whose computed English counterpart under `resources` does not exist). This aborts the Maven build with a raw RuntimeException stack trace rather than a proper mojo failure message, and is inconsistent with the error handling contract of verify(). These catches should throw MojoExecutionException (or add a clear violation message) instead.

title: No test asserts a clean file produces zero violations
body: All four tests only assert that a specific violation message is present (hasItem) in files crafted to be invalid. There is no test asserting that a valid translation (e.g. noHtml_en.properties, or a translation whose HTML exactly matches the English source) returns an empty message list. Since this verifier runs against every message file in the build, a false-positive bug in the sanitizer logic would fail the build for all locales and would not be caught by these tests. The switch from Matchers.contains to hasItem in verifyDuplicateKeysDetected also means extra unexpected messages no longer fail that test.

When the server-side multivalued-attribute validation error is displayed in the account UI, users will see the raw template text including the literal choice-format string instead of a formatted message.

title: Missing or unreadable English counterpart file throws a bare RuntimeException instead of a proper build error
body: `verify()` wraps file reading in a catch that converts IOException into a descriptive MojoExecutionException, but the new `verifySafeHtml()` catches IOException from reading the message file or the computed `_en.properties` counterpart and rethrows it as an unchecked RuntimeException (lines 66-80). If a translation file is processed whose English counterpart does not exist (e.g. a newly added locale, or a file outside the expected directory layout), the Maven build aborts with a raw RuntimeException stack trace rather than a clean verification message or MojoExecutionException, making failures harder to diagnose and bypassing the plugin's documented error handling.

title: Anchor check compares tags positionally and the pattern matches any tag starting with 'a', causing false positives
body: `santizeAnchors` matches the N-th anchor in the translation against the N-th anchor in the English source and requires exact string equality. A legitimate translation that reorders two links (common when target-language word order differs) is rejected with "Didn't find anchor tag" even though it contains exactly the same anchors. Additionally, the pattern `</?a[^>]*>` matches any tag beginning with 'a' (`<abbr>`, `<address>`, `<article>`, ...), so those tags are silently stripped from the compared value when they happen to positionally match an English 'anchor', or produce misleading "Didn't find anchor tag" messages instead of being validated by the HTML policy. Both cases produce false verification failures for valid translations.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted condition and wrong substring offset
body: In the new isAccessTokenId(String expectedGrantShortcut) matcher, matchesSafely does `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. Two bugs: (1) the condition is inverted — the matcher returns false exactly when the grant shortcut equals the expected one, and returns true (if the rest is a UUID) when it does NOT match; (2) the offset is wrong — in a token id like `onrtac:<uuid>` the 2-char grant shortcut occupies positions 4-5, so it should be substring(4, 6), not substring(3, 5) (which yields e.g. "ta"). The correct check would be `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. As written, every event assertion switched to this matcher (expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectAuthReqIdToToken) will fail against correctly-encoded token ids, breaking a large part of the integration test suite.

title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing custom OAuth2 grant type providers
body: getShortcut() is added as a new abstract method with no default implementation on the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory interface. Any existing custom OAuth2 grant type provider (compiled against the previous interface) will fail with AbstractMethodError at runtime — and it will be hit during server startup, because DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() unconditionally calls gtf.getShortcut() on every registered OAuth2GrantTypeFactory. A default method (e.g. returning null, or a shortcut derived from getId()) combined with null-handling in the encoder factory would keep backward compatibility for third-party grant providers.

title: Grant type only recorded for standard token exchange, not other exchange flows
body: The Constants.GRANT_TYPE attribute is set to the token-exchange grant type only inside StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient. Other token exchange providers built on AbstractTokenExchangeProvider (the legacy V1 token exchange behind the TOKEN_EXCHANGE feature, subject impersonation V2, federated exchange) never set this attribute, so access tokens minted through those flows will encode the grant type as "na" (unknown) even though they went through the token-exchange grant. Since recognizing the token-exchange grant is one of the stated goals of this PR (issue #37117), the attribute should be set in a shared place (e.g. TokenExchangeGrantType.process or AbstractTokenExchangeProvider) so all exchange variants are covered.

title: Constructor null-checks grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId
body: The constructor contains `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` — a copy-paste of the line above. It checks grantType a second time (with a misleading message about rawTokenId) and never null-checks rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId then silently propagates and would be rendered as the literal string "null" by DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId when concatenating the token id. The check should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`.

title: getShortcut() javadoc contradicts the mandatory 2-character format
body: The javadoc says the shortcut is "usually like 3-letters", but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId strictly requires the encoded context to be exactly 6 characters (2 per segment) and throws IllegalArgumentException otherwise, and the whole PR design assumes every shortcut is exactly 2 characters. A grant factory returning a 3-letter shortcut (as the javadoc suggests) would produce token ids that can never be decoded. The javadoc should state that the shortcut must be exactly 2 characters and unique, and ideally postInit should validate the length.

title: testIncorrectGrantType passes for the wrong reason (NPE from null sessionFactory)
body: In testIncorrectGrantType, the factory's postInit() is never called, so its sessionFactory field is null. Decoding "ofrtac:5678" reaches DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getGrantTypeByShortcut("ac"), which — not finding the shortcut in the manually populated map — calls sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...) and throws a NullPointerException. The test catches plain RuntimeException, so it passes on the NPE rather than on the intended IllegalArgumentException("Unknown value 'ac' for grant type"). The test should assert the specific exception type/message (and ideally initialize the factory via postInit with a real or mocked session factory) so it actually verifies the unknown-shortcut handling.

title: Public copy constructor Context(Context) removed from grant SPI class
body: The diff removes the public copy constructor OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context context). Nothing in the repository uses it anymore, but Context is a public static class of the OAuth2 grant type SPI, so any external custom grant implementation that built a derived context via this constructor will fail to compile or link after upgrade. Since the field set is otherwise identical, keeping the constructor (now also copying grantType) would avoid an unnecessary compatibility break for custom providers.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher never actually checks the grant shortcut
body: In the new isAccessTokenId matcher, the grant-type check is doubly wrong: (1) the condition is inverted — `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects the match when the shortcut EQUALS the expected one, instead of when it does not; (2) the indices are wrong — in a token ID like `onrtac:<uuid>` the grant shortcut occupies character indices 4-5 (`substring(4, 6)`), but `substring(3, 5)` grabs the 2nd char of the token-type shortcut plus the 1st char of the grant shortcut (e.g. "ta" for "onrtac"), which never equals any expected shortcut. Net effect: the matcher accepts any token ID of the form `<anything>:<UUID>` regardless of grant type, so expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken and expectAuthReqIdToToken do not actually verify the encoded grant type — the tests pass even if the encoding is wrong. Additionally, if the prefix before ':' is shorter than 5 characters, substring(3, 5) throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of returning a clean non-match.

title: Grant type is only encoded for the standard token-exchange provider, not for legacy/impersonation/federated exchanges
body: The PR's stated motivation includes knowing the grant type for token-exchange use-cases, but `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE)` was only added to StandardTokenExchangeProvider. Other token-exchange implementations that extend AbstractTokenExchangeProvider — the legacy token exchange (V1) provider, subject-impersonation, and federated token exchange — never set this attribute, so access tokens issued through those flows are encoded with the 'na' (unknown) grant shortcut even though they went through the token-exchange grant. Any follow-up logic that relies on the encoded grant type (e.g. #37117) will silently misidentify these tokens.

title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations at runtime
body: Adding `String getShortcut();` as a new abstract method to the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory interface means any existing third-party/custom grant-type factory compiled against the previous interface will throw AbstractMethodError at server startup, because DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit unconditionally calls `gtf.getShortcut()` for every registered OAuth2 grant factory — this aborts postInit and prevents the server from starting. Custom grant types are a documented extension point of this SPI. Providing a default method (e.g. returning a derived or null shortcut that is then handled) would avoid breaking existing deployments on upgrade.

title: Constructor null-checks grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId
body: In the AccessTokenContext constructor, the second requireNonNull call checks `grantType` again instead of `rawTokenId` (`Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`). As a result a null rawTokenId is silently accepted despite the message saying otherwise, and encodeTokenId would then produce a token ID ending in `...:null`. The check should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`.

title: testIncorrectGrantType passes via a masked NullPointerException, not the intended parse error
body: In the test setup, DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit is never called, so `sessionFactory` is null. When testIncorrectGrantType parses `ofrtac:5678`, the unknown shortcut 'ac' takes the lazy-refresh path in getGrantTypeByShortcut, which calls `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...)` and throws a NullPointerException. The test catches the overly broad `RuntimeException`, so it passes for the wrong reason and would not distinguish a real IllegalArgumentException from the production parse-validation path from an NPE caused by incomplete test setup. The test should either initialize the factory through postInit (or stub the maps so no lazy refresh is needed) and assert on IllegalArgumentException specifically.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher never verifies the grant type (wrong indexes and inverted condition)
body: The new matcher is meant to assert that an encoded access token ID (format `<2-char session><2-char token-type><2-char grant>:<uuid>`, e.g. `onrtac:1f65761e-...`) contains the expected grant shortcut. However the check reads `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. Two defects: (1) the grant shortcut occupies character indexes 4-5, so it should be `substring(4, 6)`, not `substring(3, 5)`; (2) the condition is inverted — it returns `false` (no match) when the substring EQUALS the expected shortcut, instead of when it does NOT equal it. Because token-type shortcuts are `rt`/`lt`, `substring(3,5)` is always `t` + first char of the grant shortcut, which never equals the currently used expectations (`ac`, `dg`, `rt`, `ci`), so the matcher silently reduces to just the UUID check: all the updated event assertions (`expectCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken`, `expectAuthReqIdToToken`) pass regardless of the encoded grant type, giving false confidence that the encoding works. Worse, if a grant shortcut starting with 't' were asserted (e.g. token-exchange `te`), the matcher would falsely reject valid tokens. The line should be `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

title: New abstract getShortcut() method breaks existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations at runtime
body: Adding `String getShortcut();` as an abstract method to the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` interface is a hard breaking change for any custom OAuth2 grant type provider compiled against the previous version. `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` calls `gtf.getShortcut()` on every registered `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` during server startup, so an existing third-party grant provider that does not implement the new method will throw `AbstractMethodError` during `postInit`, failing server startup. Providing a default implementation (e.g. returning a derived or null shortcut handled gracefully) would avoid breaking deployed custom providers.

title: Duplicated null check on grantType leaves rawTokenId unchecked
body: The constructor contains `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` immediately after the identical check for grantType with the correct message. As a result `rawTokenId` is never null-checked (a null rawTokenId would later produce encoded IDs like `onrtac:null`), and if grantType were null the first check fires anyway, making the second statement dead code with a misleading message. The second statement should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`.

title: Public copy constructor Context(Context) removed from grant SPI class
body: The diff removes the public `Context(Context context)` copy constructor from `OAuth2GrantType.Context`, a public static class in the server-spi-private module. Nothing in the main codebase references it anymore, but any external/custom grant type implementation that clones a context (a reasonable pattern when wrapping or delegating grants) will no longer compile. If removal is intentional it should be called out in upgrade notes; otherwise the copy constructor should be kept and extended to copy the new `grantType` field.

title: getTokenContextFromTokenId throws IllegalArgumentException on malformed IDs instead of returning UNKNOWN context
body: Decoding is asymmetric: a token ID without a colon (all pre-change tokens) is handled gracefully by returning an UNKNOWN `AccessTokenContext`, but any ID containing a colon that does not match the exact 6-character context format, or that contains unknown shortcuts, throws `IllegalArgumentException`. This method is intended to be used by endpoints (introspection, userinfo, account REST — per the follow-up issues #37662/#37117) that parse arbitrary, potentially attacker-supplied or older/foreign token IDs; an unhandled `IllegalArgumentException` there will surface as a 500 error. Consider returning an UNKNOWN context for undecodable IDs (or at least documenting the throws contract on `TokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId`).

title: getShortcut() javadoc says '3-letters shortcut' but the format requires exactly 2 characters
body: The javadoc states the shortcut is "usually like 3-letters shortcut of specific grants", but the actual encoding format implemented in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` requires every shortcut to be exactly 2 characters long (`encodedContext.length() != 6` is enforced when decoding, 2 chars per type), and all built-in implementations return 2-character shortcuts (`ac`, `cc`, `rt`, `te`, ...). A provider author following the javadoc and returning a 3-character shortcut would produce token IDs that fail to decode. The javadoc should state that the shortcut must be exactly 2 characters and unique across grants.

title: Recovery codes validated against user storage are never consumed and remain reusable
body: When the recovery-codes credential lives in local storage, the code that was just used is consumed as a side effect of validation (RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.isValid removes the used code and persists the credential). When the credential lives in user storage (the new path added by this PR), validation is delegated to the storage provider's CredentialInputValidator.isValid, and nothing afterwards marks the code as used: there is no updateCredential/disableCredentialType callback with the remaining codes. The test provider added in this PR demonstrates the gap — BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid only checks membership in the stored raw-code list and never removes the used entry, so the same recovery code can be presented again on every subsequent login. This silently weakens the one-time-use security property of recovery codes for exactly the scenario this PR enables, and the new test (testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin) never asserts that a used code is invalidated. Either Keycloak should push the remaining codes back via updateCredential after a successful user-storage validation, or the limitation should be explicitly handled/documented.

title: removeStoredCredentialById cannot remove a user-storage (federated) recovery-codes credential
body: After this change the credential looked up via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential may come from user storage (getFederatedCredentialsStream). If such a provider tracks used codes itself and returns a credential whose allCodesUsed() is true, the cleanup call authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(...) only removes credentials from the local store and silently does nothing for federated credentials — additionally, credential models built by a storage provider (as the test provider does with RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues) may carry a null or synthetic id, so the removal has no valid target. The exhausted credential then remains in user storage, isConfiguredFor keeps returning true, and the user continues to be challenged with recovery codes that can never succeed. Removal for federated credentials would need to go through the storage provider (e.g. updateCredential/disableCredentialType) instead of removeStoredCredentialById.

title: Recovery codes stored in user storage are never consumed and can be replayed
body: For locally stored recovery-code credentials, the credential provider's isValid() consumes the used code (removes it from the credential data), making each code one-time-use. With this PR, when the credential lives in user storage, validation via user.credentialManager().isValid() delegates to the storage provider's isValid(realm, user, input), which can only check membership and has no way to remove the used code (see the new BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid, which just does generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(...) without updating anything). As a result, a recovery code stored in federated user storage remains valid forever and can be replayed by anyone who captured it, defeating the one-time-use semantics that are the entire point of recovery codes. Additionally, the cleanup logic here never helps: allCodesUsed() will never become true because the credential data is never updated, and even if it were, removeStoredCredentialById() only removes locally stored credentials and silently does nothing for a federated credential.

title: Optional.get() crashes when user storage supports recovery codes but does not expose them via getCredentials
body: The bean now calls RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user), which looks at getFederatedCredentialsStream() and then local storage, and immediately calls .get() on the Optional. However, the authenticator's configuredFor() uses credentialManager().isConfiguredFor(TYPE), which for user storage delegates to the provider's isConfiguredFor()/supportsCredentialType(). A user storage provider can legitimately implement CredentialInputUpdater + CredentialInputValidator (so it reports the credential as configured and can validate it) without implementing the optional CredentialInputProvider interface that backs getFederatedCredentialsStream(). For such a provider, getCredential() returns Optional.empty() and credentialModelOpt.get() throws NoSuchElementException, producing a server error instead of the recovery-code login page. The same mismatch affects RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator's post-validation lookup. The code should handle the empty Optional instead of assuming presence.

title: No test that a used recovery code is invalidated, and no test for the local-storage fallback
body: The new testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin only verifies one successful login with a recovery code. It never attempts to reuse the same code, which is exactly the scenario that is broken for user-storage-backed recovery codes (the storage's isValid cannot consume the used code, so reuse currently succeeds). A test asserting that the second login attempt with the same code fails would have caught the replay flaw. Additionally, the fallback path in CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential (user storage's updateCredential returns false, credential is created in the Keycloak DB via the recovery-codes credential provider) is not exercised anywhere: the only modified test storage now always supports the recovery-codes type, so a regression in the local-storage path would go unnoticed.

title: Exhausted recovery-code credentials stored in user storage are never removed
body: After a successful recovery-code login, the authenticator now looks up the credential with the new federated-aware RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(), so the returned credential may live in user storage. However, when all codes are used it still calls authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(...), which only deletes credentials from Keycloak's local store. For a credential supplied by a user storage provider this call silently no-ops: the exhausted credential remains in the user storage, isConfiguredFor()/configuredFor() keep returning true, and getCredential() keeps returning the used-up credential. The only recovery path is the required action being added afterwards; if the user abandons that flow, the stale credential persists and there is no code path that ever cleans it up (the class never attempts disableCredentialType or updateCredential on the provider for the exhausted credential). The removal should handle the federated case (or the all-codes-used branch should be skipped/handled differently for credentials whose ID belongs to a user storage provider).

title: getCredential prefers federated over local, but isValid validates local credentials first
body: The new getCredential() checks getFederatedCredentialsStream() first and only falls back to locally stored credentials. UserCredentialManager.isValid(), however, validates against locally stored credentials before delegating to user storage. If a user ends up with both a local and a federated recovery-codes credential (e.g. had local codes and is later linked to a user storage that also reports the type), the code that validated successfully may be the local one, while the post-validation bookkeeping in RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator (allCodesUsed() check, removal of the exhausted credential, triggering CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES) operates on the federated credential. The exhausted local credential would then never be detected or removed. This is also a behavior change on upgrade: an existing local recovery-codes credential is now shadowed by any federated one, whereas before only local credentials were consulted.

title: New recovery-keys test does not verify one-time-use semantics or the exhausted-credential path
body: testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin only performs a single successful login with the first recovery code. It never asserts that reusing the same code fails, never requests a second code to verify the displayed code number advances, and never exercises the 'all codes used' branch (removal of the credential and re-triggering of the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action) for a user-storage-backed credential. Notably, the test storage provider's isValid() accepts ANY of the stored raw codes regardless of the number shown on the login page and never marks a code as used, so even a broken implementation that ignores the requested code number or never consumes codes would pass this test. Given that the all-codes-used cleanup is exactly the part that does not work for federated credentials (removeStoredCredentialById is local-only), this path should be covered.

title: getCredentials() dereferences myUser without null check
body: The newly added getCredentials(RealmModel, UserModel) calls getMyUser(user) and immediately accesses myUser.recoveryCodes and myUser.otp. getMyUser() can return null when the user is not present in the in-memory map (other methods in the same class, e.g. isConfiguredFor() and isValid(), explicitly guard against this). A call for an unknown user — e.g. from admin/account credential listing or UserCredentialManager.getFederatedCredentialsStream() during edge-case lookups — would throw a NullPointerException instead of returning an empty stream.

title: Reader thread is never joined, so the test can pass without ever exercising the race
body: In createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti, the background thread that repeatedly calls managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...) is started but never joined. The main thread deletes the 100 groups, sets deletedAll=true, and immediately asserts caughtExceptions is empty. Because there is no thread.join() (and no guarantee the reader thread has executed even a single iteration before the deletes finish), the test can pass vacuously on a slow or busy CI runner without ever reproducing the concurrent read-during-delete scenario this PR is fixing. Additionally, the reader thread performs one more iteration after deletedAll becomes true (the flag is only checked at the top of the loop), so any exception thrown in that final in-flight request happens after the assertion has already executed and is silently lost. The test should join the reader thread before asserting (and ideally ensure a minimum number of read iterations occurred).

title: Fix only covers getSubGroupsCount; other cached read paths still NPE on concurrent group deletion
body: getSubGroupsCount() now null-checks modelSupplier.get() before use, but the identical concurrent-delete race remains in the sibling read paths of the same adapter: getSubGroupsStream(String, Integer, Integer), getSubGroupsStream(Integer, Integer), and getSubGroupsStream(String, Boolean, Integer, Integer) (lines 254-269) all call modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) without a null check, and getAttributes/getFirstAttribute go through cached lazy loaders that dereference the supplied GroupModel. If the group is deleted from the database between cache read and delegate load, those paths still throw the same NullPointerException this PR set out to fix, so requests hitting them (e.g. paginated subgroup listing while a group is removed) remain broken. The behavior is also now inconsistent: when the adapter was invalidated, isUpdated() throws IllegalStateException("Not found in database") for a deleted group, while this method silently returns null for the same condition.

title: NPE fix is incomplete: three getSubGroupsStream overloads still dereference modelSupplier.get() without a null check
body: This PR fixes the concurrent-deletion NPE in getSubGroupsCount() by checking modelSupplier.get() for null (the supplier returns null when the group was deleted from the database after the cached entry was loaded). However, the exact same race exists in the three sibling methods getSubGroupsStream(String search, Integer firstResult, Integer maxResults) (line 256), getSubGroupsStream(Integer firstResult, Integer maxResults) (line 262), and getSubGroupsStream(String search, Boolean exact, Integer firstResult, Integer maxResults) (line 268): all three call modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) with no null check. If a group is deleted concurrently while one of these paginated sub-group endpoints is being served (the scenario from issue #40368), they still throw a NullPointerException. These methods should apply the same null handling as getSubGroupsCount (e.g., return Stream.empty() or delegate consistently).

title: Reader thread is never joined, so the assertion on caughtExceptions races with in-flight requests
body: In createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti, the spawned reader thread loops until deletedAll is set, but the test thread sets deletedAll (line 155) and immediately asserts that caughtExceptions is empty (line 157) without joining the reader thread. The reader may still be executing a request at that point; an exception it throws a moment later is added to caughtExceptions after the assertion has already passed, so the test can silently miss the very failure it was written to catch (making it both flaky and weak as a regression test). Conversely, the reader thread may also still be running when the test method ends. The test should keep a reference to the Thread and call join() before asserting on caughtExceptions.

title: Fix is incomplete: paginated getSubGroupsStream variants still NPE on concurrent group deletion
body: The PR fixes the NPE in getSubGroupsCount() by null-checking the lazily loaded delegate, but the same race still exists in the three sibling methods that also dereference modelSupplier.get() without a null check: getSubGroupsStream(String search, Integer firstResult, Integer maxResults) (line 256), getSubGroupsStream(Integer firstResult, Integer maxResults) (line 262), and getSubGroupsStream(String search, Boolean exact, Integer firstResult, Integer maxResults) (line 268). Each of these calls modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) directly, so if the group is concurrently deleted between the cache load and this call, the supplier returns null and a NullPointerException is still thrown. Since the PR's stated purpose is to fix NPEs when accessing a group concurrently, these paths need the same null handling (e.g., return Stream.empty() or delegate consistently) or the bug will simply resurface through the paginated subgroup endpoints.

title: Reader thread is never joined, so exceptions can be added after the assertion and silently missed
body: createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti starts a background thread that repeatedly lists groups and collects exceptions into caughtExceptions, sets deletedAll after the delete loop, and then immediately asserts caughtExceptions is empty (line 157). The thread is never joined: between deletedAll.set(true) and the assertion the reader thread can still be inside managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...), and an exception thrown there (the very NPE this PR is fixing) is added to the list only after the assertion has already passed, so the test can green-light a failure it was written to catch. Conversely, if the delete loop itself throws, deletedAll is never set and the non-daemon reader thread spins in a tight HTTP loop forever, hanging the test JVM. The thread should be stored, and after deletedAll.set(true) the test should join() it (with a timeout) before asserting on caughtExceptions, ideally in a finally block so the thread is always terminated.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes with TypeError when used with a datetime order_by key
