Combined with the new in-process downsize, any user (when `is_api?`) can submit a URL pointing to a 10MB payload, force a full download, and only then attempt downsizing. There is no rate limit, content-type check before download, or guard against repeated large fetches, so this widens the resource-exhaustion surface for the API. The download cap should remain bounded by `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` (with a configurable, smaller multiple) rather than a hardcoded 10MB, and/or the URL path should require admin privileges.

title: New automatic-downsize feature has no tests
body: The PR adds non-trivial logic (size reduction loop, animated handling, integration with `OptimizedImage.downsize`, the new dimension-string API, and the change to URL download limits) but the changed-files list contains only production source. There are no controller specs verifying that oversized images are actually reduced, that GIFs in `allow_animation` mode are handled, that failures surface as errors, that the loop terminates, or that URL-downloaded files are bounded correctly. At minimum: a spec that an oversized PNG is downsized and accepted; a spec for an oversized animated GIF; a spec for the case where the image cannot be reduced below the limit within 5 attempts; and a spec for the JS-side validation against the site setting.

title: Hardcoded 10MB client-side limit breaks max_attachment_size_kb for non-image uploads
body: validateUploadedFile is called for both images and attachments (type is 'image' or 'attachment'). The previous code used Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'] so attachment uploads respected SiteSetting.max_attachment_size_kb. The change to a hardcoded 10MB means any admin who has set max_attachment_size_kb to anything larger than 10MB will see those legitimate attachment uploads rejected client-side, even though the server side still allows them. The intended behavior of letting oversized images through for downsizing should only apply to images, not attachments, since attachments are not downsized in this PR.

title: FileHelper.download limit raised to 10.megabytes, allowing oversized URL fetches
body: The download cap was changed from SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes (e.g. 4MB) to a hardcoded 10.megabytes. The only motivation is to fetch a larger image so it can be downsized locally. As a side effect, the server will now happily fetch up to 10MB from any URL the API caller supplies (and then potentially store a 10MB file even if the configured max_image_size_kb is, say, 500KB, if the downsize loop fails to bring it down). For sites that intentionally keep max_image_size_kb small to limit storage, this widens both bandwidth and disk exposure. The cap should stay tied to (or be a multiple of) SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, not unconditionally 10MB.

title: Downsize loop silently proceeds if file cannot be reduced under max_image_size_kb
body: After up to 5 iterations of OptimizedImage.downsize at 80%, the loop only checks tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes. The return value of OptimizedImage.downsize (which can be false if convert/gifsicle fails) is ignored, so an unsupported/corrupt image produces no error. More importantly, if the loop exhausts attempts and the file is still above max_image_size_kb, the code falls through and calls Upload.create_for anyway, so an oversized file is stored with no feedback to the user. The user has spent bandwidth uploading a file that should have been rejected. Either surface an error if the loop ends without success, or break out and skip the upload.

title: OptimizedImage.downsize is invoked with source and destination pointing at the same tempfile path
body: OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, '80%', ...) reads from and writes to the same file. ImageMagick's convert typically needs to fully open the input before writing the output, and on many filesystems this fails or corrupts the source. Use a separate Tempfile for the destination and move it back over the original on success.

title: Duplicate def self.downsize redefines the public API and silently breaks 5-argument callers
body: The file now contains two def self.downsize definitions. In Ruby the second definition (line 149) completely replaces the first (line 145), so the 5-argument form downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) is now dead and unreachable. Any caller that still uses the 5-argument signature (plugins, jobs, or other internal code) will instead hit the 4-argument version downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}), which interprets the third positional argument as a dimensions string (e.g. "100") rather than a width, and the fourth as opts (so a hash expected for opts will receive an integer and crash on opts[:allow_animation]). Either remove the unused first definition, or keep the 5-argument form as the canonical signature and remove the new 4-argument overload.

title: Dead downsize definition left in place after refactor
body: After the refactor, the 5-argument def self.downsize on line 145 is unreachable because line 149 redefines the same method with a different signature. Keeping the dead body around invites future maintainers to call it (and get the broken behavior described in the API finding above) or to waste time understanding which form is active. Delete it.

title: NoMethodError when TopicUser record is missing
body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)` returns nil when the logged-in user has never interacted with the topic (no row in topic_users). The very next line `if tu.notification_level > ...` then dereferences nil and raises NoMethodError, turning a normal first-time visit into a 500. The code should either create a record via `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: ...)` (which already handles the insert path) or bail out cleanly when tu is nil.

title: GET request mutates notification state (CSRF + no confirmation)
body: `unsubscribe` is wired to `GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` (see config/routes.rb lines 440-441) and silently flips the caller's TopicUser.notification_level as a side effect of loading the page. There is no CSRF token check (Rails protects only non-GET by default), no confirmation step, and no redirect after save — so any cross-site link, image hot-link, or browser prefetch that a logged-in user triggers against a known topic_id will toggle their notification level without consent, and a simple F5 re-toggles it (muted→regular→muted). It should be a POST with a confirm form, or at minimum redirect to the canonical topic URL after writing so refresh is idempotent.

title: Refreshing the unsubscribe page re-applies the toggle
body: After `tu.save!` the action falls through to `perform_show_response`, which renders the `show` template while the browser URL is still `/t/.../unsubscribe`. Reloading the page re-enters `unsubscribe`, re-reads the (now changed) notification_level, and flips it again. There is no `redirect_to` after the write, so the side effect is not idempotent — a user who refreshes once after unsubscribing from a 'watching' topic ends up muted, and a second refresh is a no-op, but the level they see in the UI does not match what they expect.

title: No specs for TopicsController#unsubscribe
body: A new state-changing controller action is added (toggles notification_level, requires login, supports slug/id redirect, falls back to show template) but there are no corresponding request/controller specs covering: happy path toggle, idempotency/refresh, behavior when no TopicUser row exists, behavior for topics the user cannot see, and the redirect when slugs_do_not_match. Only a tiny tweak to message_builder_spec was added.

title: Toggle sends already-regular users to muted with no warning
body: The branch `if tu.notification_level > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular] ... else ... muted` means a single click of the per-topic unsubscribe link on an account that is already at 'regular' silently demotes them to 'muted'. The I18n copy in client.en.yml ('You will stop receiving notifications...') is shown only on the Ember page; the non-JS GET fallback never shows it and never asks. Combined with the GET/refresh issue above, this is the path users will actually hit from email clients without JavaScript.

title: Typo in computed property name: stopNotificiationsText
body: The computed property is named `stopNotificiationsText` (three i's, 'Notificiations'). Templates and any future callers have to match this misspelling; it should be `stopNotificationsText`. There is no second typo'd alias, so renaming is safe.

title: Triple-stash on interpolated I18n string is XSS-prone if title ever flows from user input without escaping
body: `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` is rendered unescaped because the I18n string embeds `<strong>`. The `title` interpolation currently comes from `model.fancyTitle`, which html_escapes in Topic#fancy_title, so today this is safe — but the pattern is fragile: any future change that lets the title (or the surrounding I18n string) include raw HTML from a less-trusted source will inject script. Prefer rendering the strong tags from the template and using `{{title}}` (double-stash) for the topic title.

title: No error handling if PostStream.loadTopicView rejects
body: The `model` hook returns `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id).then(...)` with no `.catch`. If the user cannot see the topic (deleted, secured category, PM they're not a participant in), the promise rejects and Ember shows the generic error route, which is jarring for what is supposed to be a friendly unsubscribe confirmation page. Also, `params.id` is the route param but the same value is read from `params.id` here and the controller uses `params[:topic_id]` — fine for routing but worth noting that the slug from the route is never validated against `topic.slug`, unlike the Rails side.

title: Unsubscribe spec passes unsubscribe_url but never asserts on it
body: The new spec passes `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"` to the builder but only asserts the existence of the `List-Unsubscribe` header and that the body contains `user_preferences_url`. There is no expectation that `unsubscribe_url` actually appears in the rendered body or HTML — which is the entire point of the new translation key in server.en.yml. Without that assertion a regression that drops the interpolation variable would still pass.

title: unsubscribe_url interpolation has no fallback and is silently dropped
body: The new line `To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, [click here](%{unsubscribe_url}).` references `%{unsubscribe_url}` but only the notification emails path (`send_notification_email` in user_notifications.rb) sets this key. All other callers of `build_email` with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` (e.g., signup, forgot_password, admin_login, signup_after_approval, authorize_email, account_created) do not pass `unsubscribe_url`, so I18n will raise MissingInterpolationArgument or leave a literal `%{unsubscribe_url}` in the email body depending on the I18n backend. Either guard the interpolation (`%{unsubscribe_url}` only when present) or make `unsubscribe_url` default to nil in Email::MessageBuilder.

title: unsubscribe_url points at GET endpoint that mutates state
body: `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url` is now embedded in every notification email body, but as noted above that URL is a GET handler that immediately toggles the user's notification level (no confirmation). Clicking it from an email preview pane, a link-checker, or any URL sanitizer that fetches links will silently change the user's settings. This should be a confirmation page, not the destructive endpoint.

title: Two competing /unsubscribe routes with no clear precedence doc
body: Routes `t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` and `t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` are both added to map to `topics#unsubscribe`. The non-slug form will match `/t/1234/unsubscribe` before the slugged form because it is listed first. The unsubscribe emails use `Topic#unsubscribe_url` which always includes the slug, so the slugged form is the one that actually fires — but the bare-id form silently swallows anything that looks like `t/<digits>/unsubscribe`, which could mask future routing bugs. Either remove the bare-id form or document why both are required.

title: Duplicate %{respond_instructions} placeholder rendered twice when context posts present
body: The template now contains two `%{respond_instructions}` placeholders — one inside the `if context_posts.present?` branch (line 6) and one after the closing `end` (line 19). `Email::MessageBuilder#html_part` calls `html_override.gsub!('%{respond_instructions}', respond_instructions)`, which substitutes both, so it works, but it means the instructions are rendered twice in long emails (once above the previous discussion, once at the bottom). Verify this is intentional; otherwise remove the inner one.

title: Unsubscribe action performs writes via GET (CSRF-vulnerable and prefetchable)
body: The new `def unsubscribe` action (lines 98-116) is wired to GET routes (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` in config/routes.rb), but it writes to the database by setting `tu.notification_level` and calling `tu.save!` (lines 107-113). Rails' CSRF protection only applies to non-GET requests, so any logged-in Discourse user who loads a third-party page embedding `` (or an iframe) will be silently unsubscribed from that topic. Modern email clients and link-previewers also auto-fetch links, so the unsubscribe can fire the moment the recipient opens the email, before they ever click. The action should either render a confirmation page with a POST form, or use a signed/tokenized link (mirroring the existing `email#unsubscribe` action), so the actual state change happens on a non-GET request.

title: NoMethodError crash when the caller has no TopicUser record
body: Line 105 reads `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])`. This can legitimately return nil — a user may have been emailed about a topic they never visited, so no `topic_users` row exists. Line 107 then calls `tu.notification_level`, which raises NoMethodError on nil and produces a 500 response for the person clicking the unsubscribe link. Either create the TopicUser row first (via `TopicUser.change`/`TopicUser.track_visit!`) or treat nil as the current regular level before comparing.

title: No guardian authorization check before mutating state
body: The action does not call `guardian.ensure_can_see!(@topic_view.topic)` (or any equivalent authorization). Although the TopicUser write is scoped to `current_user.id` so the user can only mutate their own row, the redirect uses `@topic_view.topic.unsubscribe_url` and the action is reachable for any topic the user can fetch. An explicit authorization check consistent with the rest of the controller is missing, and combined with the GET-mutation issue above it widens the surface for both information disclosure and unintended writes.

title: No assertion verifies the per-topic unsubscribe URL appears in the email body
body: The new `unsubscribe_url:` argument is plumbed through to the message builder but the test on lines 178-180 only asserts `match(builder.template_args[:user_preferences_url])`. There is no `expect(message_with_unsubscribe.body).to match('/t/1234/unsubscribe')` (or equivalent) to cover the new `%{unsubscribe_url}` interpolation in `server.en.yml`'s `unsubscribe_link` text. The PR's headline feature (the per-topic link in the email) has no automated coverage as a result.

title: No controller spec added for the new unsubscribe action
body: The PR adds a brand-new action (`def unsubscribe`, line 98) but ships no test for it in `spec/controllers/topics_controller_spec.rb` or anywhere else. Coverage is needed for: requires login, only mutates the caller's own TopicUser row, handles a missing TopicUser gracefully, redirects when the slug mismatches, toggles between regular and muted, and rejects the GET state-change concern (or asserts it is replaced by a POST).

title: Typo `stopNotificiationsText` (double 'i')
body: The property on line 5 is named `stopNotificiationsText` (`Notificiations` has two i's). The template `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs` (line 3) references the same misspelled identifier via `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}`, so the wire-up works, but the misspelling should be corrected to `stopNotificationsText` in both files for clarity.

title: ensure_logged_in before_filter breaks the email one-click unsubscribe flow
body: `:unsubscribe` is added to the `ensure_logged_in` before_filter list (line 28), so a recipient clicking the unsubscribe link delivered in an email — who by definition is not authenticated — is bounced to the login page before reaching the action. The entire purpose of the per-topic unsubscribe link is to give the user a single, friction-free way out from their mail client; forcing a login defeats that. The action either needs to be excluded from `ensure_logged_in` and instead authorised via a signed, expiring token (the RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribe pattern), or the link should not be sent to anyone who isn't already signed in. As shipped, the new email copy added in server.en.yml (`unsubscribe_link`) and the `unsubscribe_url` interpolation in user_notifications.rb route users into a flow that will not work.

title: TopicUser.find_by result used without a nil check, raising NoMethodError
body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` at line 105 may return nil — for example when the recipient has never visited the topic, when a `TopicUser` row was removed independently, or when the notification email was sent by a path that didn't go through `TopicUser.change` and so never created the row. The next two lines (`tu.notification_level > …`, `tu.notification_level = …`) and the subsequent `tu.save!` all dereference `tu` and will raise NoMethodError, surfacing a 500 instead of performing the unsubscribe. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: …)` (which creates a row when missing), or guard `tu` against nil and respond with a redirect or 404.

title: Per-topic unsubscribe is a GET with side effects, no CSRF token, and no per-user signature
body: Both unsubscribe routes are defined as `get` and the controller action mutates `TopicUser#notification_level`. There is no signed token in `topic.unsubscribe_url` (it is just `#{Discourse.base_url}/t/#{slug}/#{id}/unsubscribe`, which is guessable from the topic id alone) and Rails' request forgery protection only applies to non-GET verbs. Consequence is twofold: (1) any third-party page can CSRF a logged-in Discourse user into being silently demoted from a topic via `` or a similar tag; (2) combined with the `ensure_logged_in` issue above, the action also doesn't authorise the email recipient — once the recipient logs in, whoever's session that is has their preference for that topic changed, which is the wrong user. This should be either a POST endpoint protected by CSRF token, or a GET that requires a server-signed token tied to (user, topic) — the same pattern already used by `EmailUnsubscribeKey` in Discourse.

title: MessageBuilder spec does not assert that the per-topic unsubscribe URL reaches the email body
body: The test was updated to pass `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"` to MessageBuilder, but the only body assertion in the `add_unsubscribe_link true` context still only checks for the global `user_preferences_url`. There is no expectation that the supplied `unsubscribe_url` is interpolated into the rendered `body` (or `html_part`). A regression where the new `%{unsubscribe_url}` placeholder is silently dropped (e.g. a missing I18n interpolation variable, or a typo in the gsub) would not be caught. Add an assertion such as `expect(message_with_unsubscribe.body).to match("/t/1234/unsubscribe")` and one for `html_part` too.

title: New TopicsController#unsubscribe action has no controller spec
body: The `unsubscribe` action at lines 98-116 introduces nontrivial behaviour — slug-aware 301 redirect to `topic.unsubscribe_url`, conditional demotion of `TopicUser.notification_level` between `:regular` and `:muted`, mutation via direct `find_by` + `save!` rather than `TopicUser.change` (so it bypasses the `MessageBus` publish and `notifications_changed_at`/`notifications_reason_id` updates other code paths rely on), and rendering `show` via `perform_show_response` — yet the PR adds no controller request spec. The two bugs above (`ensure_logged_in` and the nil `tu` dereference) would both be caught by even a basic logged-in request spec.

title: unsubscribe_link translation silently requires unsubscribe_url with no contract enforcement
body: The `unsubscribe_link` translation was rewritten to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}` (line 1855), but `Email::MessageBuilder` (lib/email/message_builder.rb) does not enforce that the key is present in `template_args` — it just calls `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` and `gsub`s the result. Any caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without also passing `unsubscribe_url` will produce an email whose "click here" link has an empty `href` or a literal `%{unsubscribe_url}` placeholder. Today only `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` passes the new option, but there is nothing to stop the next mailer that copies the pattern from forgetting it. Either provide a default in the translation, document the requirement next to the `add_unsubscribe_link` keyword, or have MessageBuilder raise when the key is missing.

title: Email comparison is case-sensitive, so blocked emails can be bypassed by changing case
body: Both the `should_block?` lookup (`BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first`) and the model-level `validates :email, uniqueness: true` rely on PostgreSQL's default case-sensitive comparison. An admin who adds `Bad@Spammers.org` to the block list will not block a user signing up with `bad@spammers.org`, because `email = 'bad@spammers.org'` does not match a row stored as `Bad@Spammers.org`. The whole point of the feature is silently defeated for any address whose case differs from the stored row. Normalize on write (e.g. `before_validation { self.email = email.to_s.downcase.strip }`), change the column to `citext` (or add a functional unique index `ON blocked_emails (lower(email))`), and query with `where('lower(email) = ?', value.downcase)`. The same case-folding must be applied to the value passed in from `EmailValidator`.

title: should_block? does a non-atomic read-modify-write and is called twice per request, inflating match_count
body: `should_block?` loads the row, mutates `record.match_count += 1` / `record.last_match_at = ...` in memory, then calls `record.save`. Two issues follow. (1) Lost update under concurrency: two parallel signups for the same blocked email both read `match_count = N`, both set `N+1`, both persist, and the stored value ends at `N+1` instead of `N+2`. Use an atomic update such as `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all('match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?, updated_at = ?', Time.zone.now, Time.zone.now)` or `BlockedEmail.increment_counter(:match_count, record.id)`. (2) Double counting within a single request: `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` explicitly and then `user.save` (which runs validations again), so `EmailValidator#validate_each` runs twice and `match_count` is incremented twice for every blocked-email attempt, plus twice again for `:do_nothing` matches. Validation callbacks should be pure; if statistics must be tracked, do it in a dedicated counter (e.g. Redis `INCR`) and keep `should_block?` side-effect free.

title: Whitelist/blacklist regex is unanchored, producing false positives
body: `email_in_restriction_setting?` builds the regex as `@(#{domains})` with no start/end anchors. A whitelist entry of `gmail.com` will incorrectly accept (and a blacklist entry will incorrectly reject) addresses like `attacker@gmail.com.evil.com` and `attacker@gmail.comx`, because `String#=~` returns the position of the first substring match. Anchor it as `\A@(#{domains})\z` (or at minimum require a non-word boundary after the captured domain) so the listed domain must run to the end of the address. This bug was carried over from the original `User#email_in_restriction_setting?`, but it now lives in the shared validator and is applied to every model that uses `validates :email, email: true`.

title: EmailValidator spec only covers the blocked-email branch
body: The spec stubs `BlockedEmail.should_block?` and never exercises the whitelist/blacklist branches of `validate_each`, nor the `email_in_restriction_setting?` regex. Because this is the only test for the new validator class, the unanchored-regex bug above (false positives like `attacker@gmail.com.evil.com` against a `gmail.com` whitelist) and any future regressions in whitelist/blacklist handling will not be caught. Add cases that set `SiteSetting.email_domains_whitelist` and `SiteSetting.email_domains_blacklist` and assert both false-positive cases and legitimate match/mismatch cases.

title: Unique index on email is case-sensitive, allowing duplicate rows with different case
body: `add_index :blocked_emails, :email, unique: true` uses PostgreSQL's default case-sensitive collation, and the model's `validates :email, uniqueness: true` is also case-sensitive. Together they allow two distinct rows to be inserted for `Bad@Spam.com` and `bad@spam.com`, fragmenting the block list and producing unpredictable `should_block?` results (only the first row in storage order will ever match). Replace the column type with `citext` (enable the extension first) or drop the plain index and add a functional unique index, e.g. `execute "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX index_blocked_emails_on_lower_email ON blocked_emails (lower(email))"`.

title: should_block? swallows save failures and DB exceptions
body: `record.save` is called without checking the return value and without rescuing exceptions. If the update fails (DB connection lost, race with row deletion, future validation error), the function returns based on the in-memory record while no error surfaces to the caller, and any exception raised by `save` will propagate out of `EmailValidator#validate_each` and abort the surrounding `User` validation with an unhelpful `ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid` instead of a clear validation message. At minimum check the return value and log on failure; better, rescue the write so statistics tracking never breaks a real signup.

title: Missing trailing newline
body: The diff for `lib/validators/email_validator.rb` ends with `No newline at end of file`. POSIX text files should terminate with a newline; many editors, linters, and POSIX tools assume this.

title: Database write hidden inside validator via BlockedEmail.should_block?
body: EmailValidator.validate_each calls BlockedEmail.should_block?(value), which performs a write (increments match_count, sets last_match_at, calls record.save) as a side effect. Validators must be pure: this implementation causes an extra UPDATE on the blocked_emails table on every User validation. match_count is therefore inflated by every call to user.valid?, every save attempt (and the create flow calls valid? then save, so it is double-counted), admin edits in the console, test suites, and any code that calls .valid? on a User collection. Move the match-counting side effect out of the validator — e.g., call an explicit record_blocked_attempt! from UsersController#create after the block decision — and leave should_block? read-only.

title: Lost-update race on match_count / last_match_at
body: Lines 14–16 do a non-atomic read-modify-write: `record.match_count += 1` mutates the in-memory AR object, then `record.save` writes the row. Two concurrent signups for the same blocked email can both SELECT match_count=N, both compute N+1, and the second save overwrites the first, losing one increment (and possibly a concurrent last_match_at update). Replace this with a single atomic SQL statement, e.g.: `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all(['match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?', Time.zone.now])` so the increment and timestamp happen in one statement that the database serializes.

title: EmailValidator spec only covers the BlockedEmail branch
body: The spec stubs BlockedEmail.should_block? and never exercises the whitelist/blacklist code paths. It does not verify: (a) an email matching SiteSetting.email_domains_whitelist is accepted, (b) an email not matching the whitelist is rejected with user.email.not_allowed, (c) an email matching SiteSetting.email_domains_blacklist is rejected, (d) the precedence rule (whitelist takes priority over blacklist), or (e) the early-exit when record.errors[attribute] is already populated by an earlier validator. These are real production code paths and need direct coverage.

title: should_block? is misnamed — it has side effects
body: The method name should_block? reads as a pure predicate ('does this email get blocked?'), but the implementation performs a database write whenever a matching record is found. Any caller that reasonably expects a read-only check — including future code, integration tests, or the EmailValidator itself — will be surprised by writes. Either rename to make the side effect explicit (e.g., record_match_and_should_block!) or split responsibilities: keep should_block? as a pure lookup and add a separate record_match! that the caller invokes only when it actually wants to count the attempt.

title: BlockedEmail.should_block? has a lost-update race condition
body: should_block? performs a non-atomic read-modify-write: it loads the record via `where(email: email).first`, increments match_count in Ruby memory, and saves. Under two concurrent requests for the same blocked email, both callers can read the same match_count, both increment it to N+1, and both write back, losing one increment. The persisted match_count will be smaller than the actual number of attempts, and last_match_at will lag behind the true last occurrence. The increment must be atomic (e.g., `record.increment!(:match_count)` plus `update_column(:last_match_at, Time.zone.now)`, or a single SQL UPDATE statement), and ideally wrapped in a single statement that does not depend on a previously read row.

title: EmailValidator triggers DB writes on every validation via BlockedEmail.should_block?
body: validate_each calls BlockedEmail.should_block?, which writes to the blocked_emails table (match_count and last_match_at) on every match. ActiveRecord typically runs validators multiple times during a single save: the controller calls `user.valid?` before save, ActiveRecord re-runs validations inside save, and re-runs them again on retries after uniqueness/format errors. Each blocked-email signup therefore inflates match_count several times and adds several UPDATE queries to the request path. Worse, calling `record.valid?` (without saving) still updates persisted state, which is surprising for a validator. Statistics tracking should be moved out of the validator (e.g., to an after_validation hook on User, or a Redis counter incremented only on actual save) so validation remains side-effect free and counters are not inflated.

title: BlockedEmail lookup is case-sensitive, allowing blocklist bypass via email casing
body: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` is a case-sensitive comparison, so a blocklist row stored as `bad@spamclub.com` will not match `BAD@spamclub.com`, `Bad@spamclub.com`, or any other case variant. This is inconsistent with the rest of the user-facing email code: User.find_by_username_or_email calls Email.downcase before lookup, the regex built in EmailValidator#email_in_restriction_setting? matches regardless of case, and email comparisons elsewhere in the codebase are case-insensitive. An attacker registering with a case-variant email bypasses the block entirely. The lookup should normalize (e.g., `BlockedEmail.where(email: email.downcase).first`) or emails should be lowercased on insert (with a citext/case-insensitive column), and the matching test should explicitly assert case-variant behavior.

title: EmailValidator whitelist/blacklist logic is not covered by tests
body: The original User#email_validator implemented two branches (SiteSetting.email_domains_whitelist and SiteSetting.email_domains_blacklist) that were extracted into lib/validators/email_validator.rb. The new spec only stubs BlockedEmail.should_block? and never sets email_domains_whitelist or email_domains_blacklist, so the regex-based domain matching, the priority between the whitelist and the blacklist (if/elsif), and the email_in_restriction_setting? helper are completely untested. The .gsub('.', '\.') escaping, the @-anchored regex, and the if/elsif precedence are non-trivial and easy to silently regress, so each branch (whitelist match, whitelist mismatch, blacklist match, blacklist mismatch, both unset) needs at least one explicit test.

title: cook_method migration default misclassifies all posts as raw_html
body: The migration `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` sets a default of 1 for every existing post (and every new post that does not explicitly assign cook_method). In `app/models/post.rb`, `Post.cook_methods` is `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`. With the conventional 0-indexed enum used elsewhere in this file (`Enum.new(:regular, :moderator_action)`, `Enum.new(:flag_threshold_reached, ...)`), `:regular` is 0 and `:raw_html` is 1. The default therefore marks every existing post as raw_html, which combined with the new `Post#cook` behavior (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`) and the `before_save` callback `self.cooked = cook(raw, topic_id: topic_id) unless new_record?`, means that the next save of any existing post overwrites the previously rendered `cooked` HTML with raw markdown. New posts created via `PostCreator` without an explicit `:cook_method` opts become raw_html too, because `setup_post` only assigns the value when `@opts[:cook_method].present?`. The migration default should be 0 (or whatever value corresponds to `:regular`).

title: XSS via unescaped embed URL in import footer
body: Line 13 builds an HTML snippet by interpolating the caller-supplied URL twice into an attribute and text node: `#{url}`. URLs from RSS `i.link`, `i.id`, or `Readability::Document` derived content are not validated or escaped. A URL containing `'`, `<`, or `>` (e.g. `http://evil.com/'>

title: External content rendered as raw HTML in embed iframe
body: `raw post.cooked` renders the stored `cooked` value without HTML escaping. Posts created via `TopicEmbed.import` are stored with `cook_method: raw_html`, which causes `Post#cook` to return `raw` verbatim. The `raw` value originates from RSS feed items (`SimpleRSS`) or the unfiltered output of `Readability::Document.new(...).content` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which can contain arbitrary HTML, including `<script>` and event handlers. When that post is shown in the embed iframe hosted on `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, the malicious markup executes in the Discourse origin. Either sanitize `doc.content` (and the RSS content) before storing, or run `cooked` through the discourse sanitizer pipeline regardless of `cook_method` for the embed view. The current combination is a stored XSS that is reachable by anyone able to publish a feed entry or scrape a hostile page.

title: JavaScript injection via request.referer in postMessage targetOrigin
body: `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')` inserts the raw `Referer` header value into a JavaScript string literal inside a `<script>` tag. HTML ERB escaping does not apply within script blocks, so any `'` or `</script>` in the referer can break out of the string. An attacker controlling a page on `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (which passes the host check in `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`) can navigate to the embed URL with a Referer like `http://embeddable_host/x');malicious_code;//'` — that referer is a syntactically valid URL whose host still matches `embeddable_host`, so it satisfies the controller's check, and its path is then injected into the script. Use `j request.referer.to_s %>` (or `escape_javascript`) to JSON-encode/escape the value into the script, or read `document.referrer` in JS instead.

title: Race window between lookup and create in TopicEmbed.import
body: Two workers can both observe `embed.blank?` and enter the `Topic.transaction` branch simultaneously. The unique index on `embed_url` will cause one of the `TopicEmbed.create!` calls to raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`, which is not rescued here and will propagate out of the transaction, leaving the other worker's topic orphaned from the embed row (or vice versa). The `post.blank?` branch also still falls through to `post` without ensuring the embed row exists for the new topic. Wrap the `create!` in a rescue that re-fetches the embed (or upsert) so concurrent importers converge on a single TopicEmbed record.

title: PollFeed crashes on RSS items with nil content/title
body: Inside the loop, `i.content.scrub` and `i.title` are used unconditionally. Many real-world feeds omit `content` and/or `title` on items, which raises `NoMethodError` (nil.scrub) and aborts the rest of the poll. With `sidekiq_options retry: false`, the failure is logged and silently dropped each hour, so a single bad feed item stops all later items from being imported. Add nil guards for `i.content` and `i.title`, and wrap the parse/iteration in a rescue so one malformed item doesn't poison the whole run.

title: Multiple fetches can race past existing-embed guard
body: `return if TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?` followed by `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` followed by another `exists?` check then `fetch_http` is not atomic. Two workers can both pass the first check and then both run `PollFeed` (which itself iterates the entire feed) and `import_remote` for the same URL, producing duplicate topics for the same source. The 60-second Redis throttle in `retrieved_recently?` only protects a single user — jobs queued by different users, or staff with `no_throttle: true`, do not serialize. Either short-circuit with a Redis lock around the full `perform_retrieve` block, or make `TopicEmbed.import` idempotent (lookup-or-insert) and rely on the unique index.

title: Unbounded fetch from arbitrary URLs in import_remote
body: `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` has no timeout and no size cap. `Kernel#open` (open-uri) will happily read an arbitrarily large response body into memory before Readability parses it. An attacker serving huge `text/html` from a page on `embeddable_host` can use the embed pipeline to make Discourse allocate large amounts of memory (and occupy a worker for a long time) simply by triggering `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` from a controlled page. Pass `read_timeout`, `open_timeout`, and/or a content-length limit to `open` (e.g. `URI.parse(url).open(read_timeout: 5, open_timeout: 5) { |io| io.read(2.megabytes) }`).

title: Stray require_dependency 'email/sender'
body: The job requires `email/sender`, but the body of `execute` only uses `TopicRetriever` and `User`. The require is dead code that will load and initialize the email-sender module on every job execution (including during tests). It also misleads future maintainers about the job's responsibilities. Remove it.

title: Missing test for invalid-referer failure and XSS-vulnerable layout interaction
body: The spec covers missing host, no embed_url, and a successful happy-path, but it never exercises the `URI(request.referer).host` comparison with a referer that has the right host but a hostile payload (the case that enables the script-injection finding in `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb`). It also doesn't verify that a referer whose host doesn't match `embeddable_host` is rejected. Add tests for both: a referer on a different host (expect non-success) and an assertion that any unsafe characters in the referer are not echoed verbatim into the response body (e.g. `expect(response.body).not_to include(request.referer)` or assert that the postMessage target is JSON-escaped).

title: Stored XSS via URL interpolation in imported_from footer
body:
Line 13 interpolates the `url` parameter into HTML without escaping: `contents << "
#{I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")} "`. The `url` originates from RSS item `link`/`id` (poll_feed.rb) or the Disqus XML import (disqus.thor), and is then persisted as `post.raw` with `cook_method = :raw_html`. Because the cooking pipeline is bypassed for `:raw_html`, the raw HTML is stored verbatim and rendered with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in app/views/embed/best.html. A URL containing a single quote (e.g. `http://x.com/'>` attribute and injects arbitrary HTML/JS that executes inside the Discourse iframe origin. The XSS is persistent in a post authored by the configured `embed_by_username` (typically a privileged system user), giving the attacker the ability to act as that user against the Discourse API.

title: X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL is not a recognized value
body: Line 28 sets `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"`. ALLOWALL is not one of the standardized values (DENY, SAMEORIGIN, or the deprecated ALLOW-FROM). Browsers that don't recognize it fall back to treating the header as absent, which means the embed page can be framed by any origin on the web, not just `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. The intent of the referer check is undermined because the response is now freely embeddable anywhere. The recommended replacement is a `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors <embeddable_host>` header.

title: postMessage targetOrigin is set to request.referer, which can be empty
body: Line 11 passes `<%= request.referer %>` as the `targetOrigin` to `parent.postMessage(...)`. The HTTP Referer header is browser-controlled and frequently null (direct navigation, referrer policies, missing header). When it is nil the rendered output becomes `parent.postMessage(..., '')`, and an empty-string targetOrigin is treated as `*` (any origin) per the HTML5 spec, leaking the iframe height to any parent window. The targetOrigin must be a fixed, server-controlled value such as the configured `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` origin, not the per-request referer.

title: Origin check is a fragile substring comparison that mishandles ports
body: Line 17 validates incoming postMessage events with `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`. This requires `e.origin` to be a substring of `discourseUrl`, which is the wrong shape for an origin check. It silently rejects legitimate origins whenever the configured `discourseUrl` and the browser's `e.origin` differ by a port (e.g. `http://example.com` vs `http://example.com:8080`), and conversely accepts attackers whose origin happens to be a prefix of the configured URL. The check should compare parsed origins (e.g. `new URL(discourseUrl).origin === e.origin`) so it handles scheme/host/port correctly.

title: Scheduled PollFeed job is executed synchronously inside a per-request job
body: `perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline (line 41) before falling through to the HTTP fetch. PollFeed downloads the entire RSS feed and processes every item, so every embed retrieval blocks on a full feed poll. This is also a concurrency hazard: concurrent retrieves can each trigger an independent synchronous poll, the job runs without Sidekiq retry/visibility, and any failure in the feed poll propagates into the per-URL retrieve. The synchronous call should be removed (let the scheduled job do its work independently) or replaced with `Jobs.enqueue(:poll_feed)`.

title: Race condition between TopicEmbed existence check and create
body: Lines 15-30 do `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and then, if blank, `TopicEmbed.create!` inside `Topic.transaction`. The check and the create are not atomic: two concurrent `import` calls for the same URL both observe `embed.blank?` and both proceed to `create!`, at which point the second one raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` (the migration adds a unique index on `embed_url`). The exception is not rescued, so the post is rolled back but the caller (a job or a controller) sees an error and the user-visible 'Loading...' view loops forever. Use `find_or_create_by` with a rescue, or `TopicEmbed.lock` / an upsert to serialize the create.

title: embed_url column length is too small for many real URLs
body: Line 6 declares `t.string :embed_url, null: false`, which Rails maps to `varchar(255)` in PostgreSQL. embed_url is the lookup key used both to find the existing embed (TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed) and as the unique index target. Real-world embed URLs with tracking query parameters or deep paths routinely exceed 255 characters, so inserts will raise `value too long for type character varying(255)` and the import will be lost. Use `t.text` (and a btree index on a hash, or a length-bounded variant) so longer URLs are not truncated or rejected.

title: TopicEmbed.import mutates the caller's contents argument in place
body: `import` appends the `imported_from` footer to `contents` via `contents << ...` (line 13). This mutates the caller's string in place. In `poll_feed.rb` the argument is `i.content` from SimpleRSS, and in `import_remote` it is `doc.content` from Readability; both are inputs the caller may still be holding. Beyond being surprising, the mutation also changes the SHA-1 of `contents` (computed on line 16 from the now-augmented string), so the content_sha1 stored in the embed reflects the appended footer rather than the imported article body. Use `contents +` or assign to a local variable.

title: Stray require_dependency for unused email/sender
body: Line 1 has `require_dependency 'email/sender'`, but `email/sender` is not referenced anywhere in `Jobs::RetrieveTopic#execute`. It looks like a copy/paste leftover from another job. It forces Rails to load the mailer framework on every RetrieveTopic invocation for no reason; remove it.

title: NoMethodError if RSS items lack a content element
body: Line 35 calls `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` without a nil check. RSS and Atom feeds vary: some items expose the body as `description`, `summary`, or `content:encoded`, and `i.content` is nil for items that only have one of the others. When that happens `.scrub` raises NoMethodError, which aborts the entire scheduled poll and prevents any items in the feed (including valid ones already in the loop) from being imported. Guard with `content = i.content && CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` (and similarly for `i.title`).

title: cook_method column default is :raw_html, breaking all existing posts
body: The migration adds `cook_method` with `default: 1, null: false`, but in `app/models/post.rb` the Enum is declared as `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`, which follows the standard 0-indexed convention (`:regular` = 0, `:raw_html` = 1). Backfilling every existing row to 1 makes every pre-existing post look like `:raw_html`, and `Post#before_save` then sets `cooked = cook(raw, ...)`; for any subsequently edited post, `cook` returns `raw` (Markdown text) instead of the rendered HTML. The default should be `0` (regular), so existing posts continue to use the cooking pipeline until they are explicitly imported with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`.

title: NoMethodError on nil feed content crashes the scheduled job
body: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` calls `scrub` on `i.content` directly. `NilClass#scrub` does not exist, so whenever an RSS/Atom item is missing a `content` field (which is the common case for items that only carry a `<description>` or `<summary>`) the scheduled job raises `NoMethodError`. The job is `retry: false`, so the failure is permanent; the feed will never be importable. Guard with `i.content.to_s.scrub` (or check `i.content` first) before unescaping.

title: X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL is not a valid directive, browsers ignore it
body: The controller sets `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"`. `ALLOWALL` is not one of the standardized X-Frame-Options values (DENY / SAMEORIGIN / ALLOW-FROM uri) and browsers ignore unknown values, falling back to whatever default framing policy is in effect. If the host previously sent a stricter value, or modern browsers apply a stricter default, the embed iframe will be blocked cross-origin, defeating the purpose of the embed controller. Use a `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self' https://<embeddable-host>` header (or `ALLOW-FROM` plus that host) to actually permit cross-origin framing.

title: PollFeed is run synchronously on every embed retrieval
body: In `perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is on, the retriever invokes `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline for every embed page load. PollFeed fetches and parses the full RSS/ATOM feed and calls `TopicEmbed.import` on every item. A busy embeddable page can therefore trigger many redundant full-feed imports. The scheduled job should be allowed to run on its own cadence and the retriever should not invoke it inline; only an explicit per-URL RSS lookup should be performed here.

title: Unescaped URL interpolation in the imported_from link enables stored XSS
body: The string `"#{url}"` is interpolated into the stored raw HTML with no escaping. `url` comes from `i.link`/`i.id` in the RSS feed (or from `TopicEmbed.import_remote`). When it contains characters like `'` or `>`, the rendered `` breaks out of its attribute and any following text becomes new HTML, e.g. `https://x/?'>` produces `'>...`. Because the post is saved with `cook_method: :raw_html` and the embed view emits it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, the injected `

title: Concurrent imports on the same embed_url race past the blank? check
body: `self.import` first does `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` to decide whether to insert, and only then calls `TopicEmbed.create!`. The migration creates a unique index on `embed_url`, but nothing in `import` rescues the duplicate-key exception that arises if a second concurrent job (e.g. two simultaneous loads of the same embeddable URL while retrieve_topic jobs run in parallel) reaches the insertion point. The losing transaction raises, and since the `Topic.transaction` block already ran a real `PostCreator.create`, an orphan topic and first post are left behind with no `TopicEmbed` row. Either guard the insert with the unique index in a single upsert, or rescue `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` and re-read the existing record.

title: order(2) on .extra-info-wrapper has no effect — parent is not a flex container
body: The diff adds `@include order(2);` to `.extra-info-wrapper`. The `order` property only applies to flex/grid children, but the natural parent in this file, `.title-wrapper` (lines 3–16), is still `float: left; width: 90%;` and was not converted to a flex container in this PR. Therefore the `order` declaration is dead CSS and does nothing at runtime. If the intent was to reorder the topic header elements via flex, the wrapping container (likely `.title-wrapper` or a parent in another stylesheet) must also be set to `@include flexbox();` for `order` to take effect.

title: Children of the new flex container .contents still rely on float: left
body: `.contents` is converted to a flex container via `@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`, but its descendants still use `float: left` to lay out horizontally: `.icons` (line 54), `.icons > li` (line 60), and `.login-button, button.sign-up-button` (line 43). In a flex container, `float` is ignored by the layout engine, so these declarations become dead code and the visual arrangement may not match the developer's expectation. The floats should be removed (and `.icons > li` re-laid out via flex properties such as `display: flex`) so the layout actually flows as flex intends.

title: Avatar floats inside the new flex container .small-action are silently dropped
body: `.small-action` is now a flex container (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`), but its descendants `.topic-avatar` (line 270, `float: left;`) and `.avatar` inside `.small-action-desc` (line 298, `float: left;`) still rely on floats for horizontal positioning. In a flex container `float` is ignored, so the original float-based layout around the avatars may silently change. The avatar positioning intent should be re-expressed with flex properties (e.g. `flex: 0 0 auto; margin-right`) rather than left as `float`, and the now-obsolete `float: left` declarations removed.

title: Removing margin-top: 5px on .badge-wrapper.bullet may misalign the bullet badge
body: The diff removes `.badge-wrapper.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` (originally compensating for the surrounding line-height) and at the same time adds `line-height: 1.5;` to `.extra-info-wrapper`. The bullet badge previously relied on that 5px top offset to sit on the text baseline; with the offset removed and a larger line-height, the bullet may now sit visually misaligned within `.extra-info-wrapper` unless another mechanism (e.g. flex `align-items` on the new flex parent, once that exists) restores the alignment.

title: align-items mixin emits the non-standard `-ms-align-items` property
body: The new `@mixin align-items` emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment;` on line 121. `-ms-align-items` is not a recognized CSS property — the real Microsoft/IE10 alias is `-ms-flex-align` (already emitted on the preceding line 120). The `-ms-align-items` declaration is dead code that no browser honors and should be removed to avoid confusion. Line 120 also has trailing whitespace after `$alignment;` before the semicolon, which is harmless but should be cleaned up.

title: PR description is just "Test 5" — does not describe the change
body: The pull request description reads only "Test 5", which conveys nothing about intent (layout rework, perf experiment, bug fix, etc.) or scope (the diff touches header, topic, topic-post and badges SCSS plus new flexbox mixins). Maintainers and reviewers have to infer the purpose from the diff. A meaningful description (e.g. "Replace float-based header/small-action layout with flexbox via new mixins in mixins.scss") should be provided before merging.

title: Button float: right is ignored after flex refactor of .small-action
body: The `button` rule inside `.small-action` still sets `float: right`, but this PR turns `.small-action` into a flex container via `@include flexbox()` on line 264. Per the CSS spec, floats have no effect on flex items, so the `float: right` is ignored. The button will no longer be pushed to the right edge of `.small-action`; it will instead render in document order immediately after `.small-action-desc`. To preserve the original layout, the button needs a flex-based equivalent (e.g., `margin-left: auto` or a flex `order`/alignment rule), otherwise small-action posts will visibly regress.

title: align-items mixin emits non-existent -ms-align-items property
body: The `@mixin align-items` block contains `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`. No such CSS property has ever existed; the IE10 prefix for `align-items` is `-ms-flex-align`, which is already emitted on the line above. The `-ms-align-items` declaration is invalid CSS and dead output that should be removed.

title: order mixin emits non-existent -webkit-order property
body: The `@mixin order` block contains `-webkit-order: $val;`. There is no `-webkit-order` property in any spec or browser; the relevant WebKit declarations are `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` (already present) or the unprefixed `order` (already present). The `-webkit-order` line is invalid and outputs no-op declarations that should be removed (or replaced with `-webkit-flex-order` only if a real implementation is targeted).

title: order() applied to non-flex item has no effect
body: @include order(2) is added to .extra-info-wrapper at the top level of the selector, but the CSS in this file does not make .extra-info-wrapper (or any of its ancestors inside this PR) a flex container, and the property only takes effect on flex items. Consequence: the rule is dead code; the author appears to intend for this element to be reordered within a flex row, but the layout will not change at all, so the rendered topic header ordering is unchanged from before this PR. Either the parent (e.g. #topic-title) must be turned into a flex container, or the rule should be removed.

title: Invalid -ms-align-items property in align-items mixin
body: The align-items mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`, which is not a valid CSS property. The Microsoft/IE10 syntax for alignment is `-ms-flex-align`, which is already included on the preceding line. Browsers silently ignore unknown property names, so this line is harmless dead output, but it is misleading to future readers and clutters the compiled CSS. It should be removed.

title: website_name not in untrusted_attributes, leaks TL0 website hosts to anonymous viewers
body: The new :website_name attribute is added to the attributes list on line 43 but is not included in the untrusted_attributes macro on lines 105-111, whereas :website is. The whole purpose of untrusted_attributes is to hide TL0 user fields from anonymous viewers (scope.restrict_user_fields? returns true). After this change, a TL0 user with website 'http://example.com/user' seen by an anonymous user will still have website_name='example.com/user' present in the JSON even though website is omitted. Anonymous viewers can now recover the host (and often path) of TL0 users' websites, partially undoing the privacy protection the macro was meant to provide. The fix is to add :website_name to the untrusted_attributes list on lines 105-111, and to update the spec to match.

title: include_website_name is missing the trailing ?
body: ActiveModel::Serializer invokes include_<attribute>? to decide whether to emit an attribute. The new method is defined as `def include_website_name` (line 153), without the question mark, so define_method for include_website_name? does not exist and AMS falls back to always including the attribute. Every other inclusion method in this file (include_email?, include_stats?, include_suspend_reason?, include_user_fields?, include_topic_post_count?, include_card_image_badge_id?, include_edit_history_public?, include_private_message_stats?) ends with `?`. As written, the inclusion guard has no effect: the JSON always contains website_name (which will be null when website is blank). The method should be `def include_website_name?`.

title: website_name crashes with NoMethodError if Discourse.current_hostname is nil
body: On line 139, discourse_host is set from Discourse.current_hostname. If that returns nil (misconfigured site, missing host, or specific request edge cases), the elsif on line 144 evaluates `discourse_host.split('.').length`, which raises NoMethodError on nil and 500s the user serializer. The early return on line 140 only guards website_host, not discourse_host. A simple guard like `return if discourse_host.nil? || discourse_host.empty?` (or swapping the logic to compute website data once and using a single safe path) would prevent the crash.

title: URI(website.to_s) is parsed four times in the same method
body: Inside website_name, `URI(website.to_s)` is constructed and parsed four separate times (lines 138, 143, 146, 149). Each call re-parses the URL. The result should be hoisted into a local variable (e.g. `uri = URI(website.to_s) rescue nil`) and reused for `.host` and `.path` access. This also makes the code easier to read and centralizes the rescue.

title: TL0 anonymous test does not cover website_name, so the privacy regression slips through
body: The untrusted_attributes list at line 11 is `%i{bio_raw bio_cooked bio_excerpt location website profile_background card_background}`. The test on lines 13-15 iterates only over that list, so even if the serializer leaks website_name for TL0 users seen as anonymous, the assertion passes. Combined with the privacy finding above, this means the regression introduced by this PR will not be caught by the existing spec. The list should be extended with :website_name (and a website value should be set on user_profile so that website_name would otherwise be present), so the test enforces the intended privacy boundary.

title: Missing coverage for edge cases of website_name
body: The new examples on lines 77-90 only cover three host-shape scenarios (different domain, identical domain, parent domain). They do not exercise: nil Discourse.current_hostname (currently raises), nil/blank website (include guard relies on the broken method name), URLs whose path is empty ('http://example.com' yields website_host + ''), URLs with query/fragment (e.g. 'http://example.com/u?x=1' drops the query in the displayed name), URLs with ports (host strips port, but path concatenation behaviour should be locked in), and the 'www.example.com vs forum.example.com' second-branch path that is only indirectly covered. Add examples for these so the contract is pinned down.

title: include_website_name missing trailing question mark
body: The new inclusion guard is defined as `def include_website_name` (without `?`), but ActiveModel::Serializer looks for a predicate method named `include_#{attr}?` (with the `?`) to decide whether to include an attribute. Every other inclusion guard in this file uses the `?` suffix (e.g. `include_email?`, `include_card_image_badge?`, `include_stats?`, `include_suspend_reason?`, `include_suspended_till?`, `include_user_fields?`, `include_topic_post_count?`). Without the `?` the framework will not recognize this as an inclusion check, so `website_name` will be serialized whenever it is non-nil even when `website` is blank, and the `website.present?` check becomes dead code. This also contradicts the intent expressed in the new spec which expects `website_name` to be absent when there is no website.

title: URI(website.to_s) parsed repeatedly in website_name
body: `website_name` calls `URI(website.to_s)` up to three times (once for `.host`, and up to twice more for `.path` in the branches that append the path). `website` is also re-invoked via the `def website` method each time, which makes another user_profile lookup. This should be parsed once into a local variable (e.g. `uri = URI(website.to_s) rescue nil`) and reused, and `website` should be memoized, to avoid redundant parsing/property lookups on every user serialization.

title: Path used in display drops query string and fragment
body: `URI(website.to_s).path` returns only the path component; the query string and fragment are discarded. For a URL like `http://example.com/users?section=profile#bio` the displayed name will be `example.com/users`, losing information the user entered. If only the host/path is desired, that is fine, but it should be a deliberate choice; if the full URL minus scheme/userinfo is the goal then `request_uri` minus the scheme/host (or the original string with scheme stripped) would preserve the query/fragment. There is also no handling for non-ASCII/percent-encoded paths or trailing slashes (e.g. `http://example.com/` displays as `example.com/`).

title: Subdomain-vs-subdomain branch of website_name is not tested
body: The new `website_name` method in app/serializers/user_serializer.rb has three branches: exact host match, subdomain equality (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length && > 2), and the parent/child fallback. The added specs cover the exact-match branch ('example.com' == 'example.com') and the parent/child branch ('example.com' vs 'forums.example.com'), but the middle `elsif` branch — for example `forum.example.com` vs `blog.example.com` (both have 3+ segments with a shared suffix like 'example.com') — has no test. This is a meaningful logic path that should be covered; without it, regressions in subdomain matching could ship unnoticed.

title: URI(website.to_s) is parsed three times in website_name
body: The `website_name` method calls `URI(website.to_s)` three times (once for `host`, then twice more for `.path` in each reachable branch). The serializer runs per user and is invoked for user lists (e.g. user cards, directory), so this is per-request overhead on every user serialization. Parse once into a local variable and reuse `parsed_uri.host` / `parsed_uri.path`.

title: website_name silently drops URL port, query, and fragment
body: `website_name` returns only `URI(...).host + URI(...).path`. For a user-supplied website such as `http://example.com:8080/users/123?ref=foo#bar`, the displayed link text becomes `example.com/users/123`, losing the port, query string, and fragment. The PR title says 'show complete URL path' but the implementation never defines what 'path' includes (path-only vs full-URL). At minimum this behavior should be documented in a comment on `website_name`, and ideally the intent (e.g., always show full URL via `URI#to_s` minus scheme, or only host+path) should be made explicit and tested.

title: Wrong lightness swapped on .topic-meta-data h5 a
body: The rule `.topic-meta-data h5 a` originally set color to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The PR replaces it with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, swapping the lightness values. In the light theme the color now becomes `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` (a much lighter gray than the original 30%) and the dark theme becomes `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)` instead of the intended `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)`. The correct fix is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. Consequence: the appearance of every embedded-post meta header link changes (light theme) and the dark theme gets the wrong contrast.

title: Wrong lightness on .topic-map h3
body: The rule `.topic-map h3` originally set color to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The PR replaces it with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, losing the original 20% lightness on the primary side. The intended mirror is 20% ↔ 80%, so it should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`. Consequence: mobile topic-map headings now render in mid-gray instead of the previous very-dark gray in the light theme, and mid-gray in the dark theme rather than near-white. Other selectors in the same `.topic-map` block (h4, span.domain, .number/i) were updated correctly with 50/50, 50/50 and 20/80, so this one stands out.

title: Wrong lightness on .custom-message-length
body: `.custom-message-length` originally used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The PR replaces it with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, swapping the two lightness values. The intended mirror is 70% ↔ 30%, so the correct call is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. Consequence: in light themes the flag-modal character-counter text is now a darker gray (30%) instead of the previous light gray (70%); the dark-theme branch is wrong too. The desktop counterpart `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/modal.scss` line 94 has the same selector and was correctly updated to 70/30, so this is a clear inconsistency between desktop and mobile.

title: Wrong lightness on .group-member-info .name
body: `.group-member-info .name` originally used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The PR replaces it with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, dropping the 30% lightness. The intended mirror is 30% ↔ 70%, so the correct call is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. Consequence: member-name text inside user-stream group-member-info is rendered in mid-gray on light themes instead of the original darker gray, and the dark-theme contrast is wrong. `.group-member-info .title` immediately below (also changed to 50/50) was correctly mirrored from its own original 50% lightness, so the two siblings end up with different colors in both themes despite originating from different lightnesses.

title: Wrong lightness on .group-member-info .name
body: Mirror of the desktop/user.scss issue. `.group-member-info .name` originally used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`; the PR replaces it with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The intended fix is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. Consequence: mobile group-member-info name text loses its darker emphasis versus the sibling `.title` rule (which legitimately stays 50/50) and the dark-theme color is wrong.

title: Lightness for $primary branch inverted from 70% to 30%
body: The conversion changed the primary branch's lightness from 70% to 30%, swapping the original and the complementary value. The light theme now renders .custom-message-length with the primary color at 30% lightness (dark/muted gray) instead of the intended 70% (light). Other files in this PR correctly preserve the original primary lightness and only add the secondary branch (e.g., admin_base.scss .badges .current-badge p.help keeps 40% on the primary branch). The expected fix is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`.

title: Primary branch lightness swapped (30% became 70%)
body: In .embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a, the primary branch's lightness was changed from 30% to 70%, inverting the original color. In the light theme this link is now a much lighter shade than before. The pattern used by other files in this PR keeps the primary branch lightness equal to the original `scale-color($primary, $lightness: ...)` value; only the secondary branch is added. Expected: `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The companion `.arrow` rule at line 294 is converted correctly (60% / 40%).

title: .group-member-info .name lightness changed from 30% to 50%
body: Original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`; the new value is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The primary branch lightness was changed during the edit, so the light theme renders the user name at 50% lightness (mid-gray) instead of 30% (dark text). Routing/controller param mismatch in add_members and remove_member
body: Both `add_members` and `remove_member` use `params.require(:group_id).to_i` to look up the group, but the routes declare `delete "members"` and `put "members"` at the top level of `resources :groups` (not inside a `collection do` block), so Rails generates member routes `DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members` and `PUT /admin/groups/:id/members` with the group id under `params[:id]`, not `:group_id`. Every real request from the frontend (which calls `Discourse.ajax('/admin/groups/' + this.get('id') + '/members.json', ...)`) will hit `ActionController::ParameterMissing: param not found: group_id` and return 400, making add/remove of members non-functional in production. The controller should use `params[:id]` (as the sibling `update` action does), or the routes should be wrapped in `collection do` and the group id passed in the body. The spec suite passes only because it injects `group_id:` directly into the params, bypassing the real routing.

title: Stray inside {{#each}} loop
body:
The template introduces ` ` inside the `{{#each m in members}}` block (line 19) with no matching opening `
`. This was added by this PR (visible as a `+` line in the diff). It will produce malformed HTML on the public group members page and may disrupt the surrounding table layout/browser rendering. The closing tag should be removed.

title: Specs bypass real routing and hide the add_members/remove_member param bug
body: Both `add_members` and `remove_member` specs pass `group_id:` directly in the request params (`xhr :put, :add_members, group_id: group.id, ...` and `xhr :delete, :remove_member, group_id: group.id, ...`). Because controller specs populate them straight into `params`, the tests succeed even though no route actually maps `:group_id` from the URL. They also exercise HTTP methods that partly disagree with the routes (e.g. the "cannot remove members from automatic groups" example uses `:put` against the `remove_member` action whose only declared route is DELETE). The suite should drive the actions through the real `/admin/groups/:id/members` URLs and methods so the routing/param mismatch in `groups_controller.rb` is caught.

title: Usernames are not trimmed before lookup
body: `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` splits the comma-separated string without stripping surrounding whitespace, so a payload like `"alice, bob"` produces `" bob"` and `User.find_by_username(" bob")` will not match the existing user `bob`. Either strip each element (`username.strip`) or rely on a username lookup that normalizes whitespace; otherwise users typed with accidental spaces silently fail to be added.

title: findMembers has no error handler and may silently drop pagination races
body: `findMembers` returns the `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` chain but never attaches a rejection callback, so a failed request (e.g. network error, 404, 500) is swallowed and the promise resolves to `undefined`. Callers like the `next`/`previous` admin actions and `setupController` of `group-members` invoke `return group.findMembers()` and get nothing useful on failure. In addition, two concurrent calls (e.g. rapid clicks on next) both write `user_count`/`offset`/`members` on the same record, so an earlier response can clobber a later one. Adding a `.catch` (or at least surfacing the error) and guarding against overlapping requests would make pagination reliable.

title: Stray closing inside {{#each}} loop with no matching opener
body:
The template contains a `` tag on line 19 inside the `{{#each m in members}}` block, but there is no corresponding opening `
` anywhere in the file (the only tag inside the loop is the ``). This produces invalid HTML and will cause the browser to insert an implicit `
` and may misrender rows in the group members table. The line should be removed.

title: delete/put "members" are member routes, but controller reads params[:group_id]
body: `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` and `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` are written directly inside the `resources :groups` block (not inside a `collection do`), so Rails treats them as member routes at `/admin/groups/:id/members` and only populates `params[:id]`. However, `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` (line 66) and `#remove_member` (line 85) both call `params.require(:group_id).to_i`, so every real browser request will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing: param is missing or the value is empty: group_id`. The RSpec tests pass only because the test invocation explicitly passes `group_id:` in the params hash, masking the bug. Fix either by moving the routes into a `collection do` block (so `group_id` is a query param) or by changing the controller to use `params[:id]`.

title: add_members does not strip whitespace from split usernames
body: `usernames.split(",")` yields entries like `" bob"` when a user types `"alice, bob"`, and `User.find_by_username(" bob")` returns nil (the DB stores usernames without surrounding whitespace), so the second user silently fails to be added. Strip each entry, e.g. `username.strip`, before looking the user up, and skip blanks. The existing happy-path spec uses `.join(",")` with no space, which is why this regression is not caught.

title: remove_member test sends PUT instead of DELETE
body: The spec at line 115 uses `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42`, but the `remove_member` action is now routed via `delete "members"` in `config/routes.rb`. The test should use `xhr :delete, :remove_member, ...` (mirroring the working "is able to remove a member" test below it). With the wrong verb the test either hits the wrong action or fails to route, and it does not exercise the DELETE branch at all.

title: Missing semicolon at end of addMembers
body: The `addMembers` function body ends with `})` on line 59 (closing the `.then` callback and the `Discourse.ajax` call) without a trailing semicolon. Every other method in the same file terminates statements with semicolons, so this is inconsistent and relies on ASI; it is a one-character fix.

title: Controller requires params[:group_id] but routes are member routes requiring :id
body: The `add_members` action (line 66) and `remove_member` action (line 85) both call `params.require(:group_id).to_i`. However, the routes `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` and `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` are written directly inside `resources :groups do ... end` in `config/routes.rb`, not inside a `collection do ... end` block. In Rails, direct routes at this nesting level are treated as member routes, producing URLs like `DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members` (where `:id` is the group ID). The JS client sends `DELETE /admin/groups/{id}/members.json` which matches the member-route pattern, but then `params[:group_id]` is never populated, so every call raises `ActionController::ParameterMissing: param is missing or the value is empty: group_id`. The admin group-member add/remove feature is therefore entirely broken. To fix, either move the routes into a `collection do ... end` block and have the client pass `group_id` as a query/body parameter, or change the controller to read `params[:id]`.

title: Test invokes remove_member with xhr :put but route is DELETE
body: At line 115, `it "cannot remove members from automatic groups"` does `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42`. The route for `remove_member` is defined as `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` (HTTP method DELETE). No PUT route exists for this action, so Rails cannot match the request and the test will fail with `ActionController::UrlGenerationError`. The HTTP verb in the spec must match the route verb.

title: Tests pass group_id but the member routes require :id in the URL
body: The `add_members` test (line 103) and `remove_member` tests (lines 115, 125) pass `group_id: group.id` as a request parameter. Because the routes are member routes that require `:id` in the URL path, Rails' URL generator cannot find `:id` in the parameters and will either raise `ActionController::UrlGenerationError` or substitute `group_id` for `:id` and produce an unintended URL. The tests must pass `id: group.id` (with the controller updated to read `params[:id]`), or the routes must be rewritten as collection routes.

title: Redundant group.save after users.delete and swallowed errors
body: In `remove_member`, `group.users.delete(user_id)` calls `ActiveRecord::Associations::CollectionAssociation#delete`, which directly issues a SQL DELETE on the join record and is already persisted. The subsequent `group.save` therefore has no unsaved changes to commit and cannot fail because of the deletion. The `if group.save / else render_json_error(group)` branching is misleading.
