Additionally, any DB-level error raised by `delete` (FK violations, lock timeouts, etc.) is not rescued, so the controller would 500 instead of returning a clean JSON error.

title: Silent failure on non-existent usernames in add_members
body: In `add_members`, when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns nil, the `if user = ...` branch silently skips that entry. The action still returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds, even if zero users were actually added. Admins therefore have no signal that a typo or non-existent account caused some (or all) intended members to be dropped. The action should accumulate the missing usernames and return them in the response, or return a non-success status when any username is unknown. The same applies to usernames that contain stray whitespace after splitting on commas (`"a, b"` produces `" b"`).

title: Stray closing with no matching opening tag
body:
Line 19 contains a `` inside the `{{#each m in members}}` block but there is no corresponding opening `
` anywhere in the template. This is invalid HTML and will produce browser parser warnings and an unexpected DOM tree (the browser will silently ignore the orphaned closer, or restructure siblings). Either remove the stray tag or wrap the rows in a matching element.

title: findMembers returns undefined instead of a resolved promise when name is empty
body: When `this.get('name')` is empty, the function executes `return ;` which yields `undefined`. The previous version returned `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])`. This violates the implicit promise-returning contract of a `find*` method: any caller that chains `.then(...)` will throw `TypeError: Cannot read property 'then' of undefined`. While the immediate callers in this PR (`admin_group_route.js`, `group-members.js.es6`, `admin-group.js.es6`) happen not to chain, future callers will. The function should return `Ember.RSVP.resolve()` (or at minimum `[]` so callers awaiting `.length` don't break) when name is blank.

title: Race condition: members load after the template has already rendered
body: `setupController` calls `model.findMembers()` but does not return its promise, so Ember does not wait for the AJAX request to finish before the template renders. The `{{#each m in members}}` block in `group/members.hbs` will therefore render with `members` undefined for a brief flash of empty content, then re-render when the promise resolves. The previous implementation used `afterModel` whose returned promise was awaited by the router before `setupController` ran, guaranteeing the data was ready. This is a UX regression and should be fixed either by returning the promise from `setupController` or by reverting to `afterModel` (or by toggling a loading flag in the controller until `findMembers` resolves).

title: FallbackLocaleList inherits from Hash but never reads or writes its storage
body: `FallbackLocaleList < Hash` overrides `#[]` to return a hardcoded array `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact` and never consults or updates the underlying Hash. This silently breaks the standard i18n `I18n.fallbacks` API: any code (including future plugin code, the Rails-generated `config.i18n.fallbacks`, or `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks#map=`) that sets a key via `fallbacks[locale] = ...` or calls methods like `each`/`map`/`merge` on `I18n.fallbacks` will get Hash-level behavior rather than the intended Fallbacks behavior, and the custom mapping will be completely ignored by `#[]`. Either don't subclass Hash, or implement the API of `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks` (including honoring a `map`) so that the object behaves like the fallback chain it replaces.

title: Critical load-order comment is not actually enforced
body: The file starts with the comment `# order: after 02-freedom_patches.rb`, but the filename is `config/initializers/i18n.rb` with no numeric prefix. Rails initializers are loaded by sorted filename, so whether this runs after `02-freedom_patches.rb` depends entirely on the other initializers in the directory. This initializer calls `I18n.ensure_loaded!` at runtime, which is defined by `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb`. If the accelerator patch has not been loaded yet, every request that hits `set_locale` will raise `NoMethodError: undefined method 'ensure_loaded!' for I18n:Module`. The ordering requirement should be made real (e.g. rename to `config/initializers/03-i18n.rb` and remove `config/initializers/02-freedom_patches.rb`'s require, or just `require_dependency` the accelerator from this file) rather than left as a comment.

title: ensure_loaded! takes LOAD_MUTEX once per fallback locale on every request
body: `set_locale` runs as a `before_filter` on every request, and now calls `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`, which iterates the fallback chain and calls `I18n.ensure_loaded! l` for each entry. Each call enters `LOAD_MUTEX.synchronize` in `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb` to re-check `@loaded_locales`. After the first request all locales are loaded, so the body of the synchronized block is a no-op, but the mutex is still acquired and released N times per request (3 by default). Under load this is pure contention overhead. A single `synchronize` that checks all needed locales once would be both faster and race-free.

title: ensure_loaded! checks @loaded_locales outside the mutex
body: The new `ensure_loaded!` does `@loaded_locales ||= []; load_locale locale unless @loaded_locales.include?(locale)`. The membership check happens without `LOAD_MUTEX`, so under contention many threads can race past it and pile up on `load_locale`'s mutex. `load_locale` does re-check inside the mutex and returns early, so this isn't a correctness bug, but it defeats the purpose of the outer check (which exists precisely to avoid the lock) and means the outer check is effectively dead code that only adds a racy read of `@loaded_locales`. Move the existence check inside the synchronized block, or use a concurrent set.

title: New fallback feature ships with no tests
body: This is a server-wide behavior change: every translation lookup now silently falls back to `SiteSetting.default_locale` and then to English, and `set_locale` triggers lazy loading of every fallback locale on every request. Despite being titled FEATURE and described as 'Test 9', the PR adds no specs for `FallbackLocaleList#[ ]` ordering, `ensure_loaded!` loading behavior, the interaction with `translate_accelerator`, the Fallbacks backend integration, or the removal of the explicit `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` from the environment files. There is no way to tell from this change whether the new fallback chain is correct (e.g. that `:en` is still reached when the site default is not English) or that the new initializer order won't break boot.

title: SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym raises NoMethodError when default_locale is nil
body: `FallbackLocaleList#[]` evaluates `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` on every call, and `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` (called from `ApplicationController#set_locale` on every request) also reaches this expression. If `SiteSetting.default_locale` is nil (e.g. before the site settings row exists, during a fresh install/seed, or in a misconfigured environment), `to_sym` raises NoMethodError and crashes the request. The trailing `.compact` does not guard this case, because the exception is raised before `compact` runs. Use a safe form such as `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale&.to_sym, :en].compact.uniq` and ensure there is at least one non-nil element.

title: FallbackLocaleList inherits from Hash but does not implement the I18n::Locale::Fallbacks contract
body: The class replaces the standard `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks` (which itself extends Hash) but only overrides `[]` and adds `ensure_loaded!`. The real class also defines `[]=`, `defaults`, and `defaults=`. With this replacement, any caller that does `I18n.fallbacks[locale] = [...]` or reads/writes `I18n.fallbacks.defaults` will silently use Hash defaults — our `[]` always recomputes from `SiteSetting.default_locale`, so any explicitly configured fallbacks are ignored without warning. Iterating `I18n.fallbacks.each` will likewise yield nothing because the underlying hash is empty. Either implement the missing methods (store explicit overrides and consult them before computing) or stop inheriting from Hash so the misleading API surface is removed and behaviour is explicit.

title: `compact` silently swallows a nil I18n.locale instead of surfacing the bug
body: `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact` relies on `compact` to drop a nil `locale`. A nil `I18n.locale` is an upstream problem (e.g. `current_user.effective_locale` returning nil in `ApplicationController#set_locale`) and translations will still resolve via `[default_locale, :en]`, hiding the misconfiguration. Either remove `compact` so the nil propagates as a real error, or replace it with an explicit guard that logs/warns when `locale` is nil and falls back intentionally.

title: No specs cover the new server-side localization fallback behaviour
body: The diff adds a non-trivial behaviour change (custom `FallbackLocaleList` with a `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en]` chain, eager loading via `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` from a `before_filter`, and a new `I18n.ensure_loaded!` patch in `translate_accelerator.rb`) but ships without any test files. At minimum there should be specs covering: the fallback order when user_locale, default_locale and `:en` are distinct; that a missing key in the user locale falls back to the default locale and then English; that `set_locale` preloads all three locales so the first `I18n.t` call after a switch does not return a missing translation; and the `uniq`/`compact` behaviour when `default_locale == :en` or `user_locale == default_locale`. Without these, regressions in fallback ordering or loading will not be caught.

title: Fallback array is rebuilt on every request and every translation lookup
body: `FallbackLocaleList#[]` allocates a fresh `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact` array on every call. After this PR, it is invoked once per request by `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` and again on every `I18n.t` lookup through the `Fallbacks` backend. The standard `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks` memoises the result per locale. Caching the array (e.g. with a `@cache = {}` keyed by `locale.to_sym`) avoids the per-call allocation and the repeated `SiteSetting.default_locale`/`to_sym` work in the hot path.

title: Mixed string/symbol in fallback list causes duplicate locale file loads
body: `FallbackLocaleList#[]` builds `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact`. `SiteSetting.default_locale` is a String (from the model) and `:en` is a Symbol, so the array mixes types. `Array#uniq` compares with `eql?`/`hash`, and `:en.eql?("en")` is `false`, so `["en", :en, :en].uniq` returns `["en", :en]` instead of one element. The result is then iterated by `ensure_loaded!`, calling `I18n.ensure_loaded!` for both `"en"` and `:en`. Each call ends up in `translate_accelerator.rb#load_locale`, where `Regexp.new("\\.#{locale}\\.yml$")` matches the same `*.en.yml` file for both the String and the Symbol, so the file is loaded and parsed twice on the first request from an English (or default-English) user. Fix by coercing consistently, e.g. `[locale.to_sym, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact`, and storing/comparing `@loaded_locales` as Symbols in `translate_accelerator.rb`.

title: FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but never uses Hash storage
body: `class FallbackLocaleList < Hash` only overrides `[]` and `ensure_loaded!`; no value is ever written to the underlying hash. This will silently drop any assignments made by `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` or callers that expect a real map (for example, an `I18n.fallbacks[locale] = [...]` override in a plugin or future Rails internal). Either drop the `Hash` superclass and just respond to `[]`, or actually populate the hash so callers can read the configured chain (e.g. for diagnostics or plugin overrides).

title: @loaded_locales ||= [] in ensure_loaded! is racy
body: `ensure_loaded!` does `@loaded_locales ||= []` outside of `LOAD_MUTEX`. Under MRI this is benign because of the GIL, but the assignment is not atomic and the subsequent `@loaded_locales.include?(locale)` is also unsynchronized. The actual file loading is protected by `load_locale`'s mutex, so correctness is preserved, but the pre-check is misleading: two threads can both fall through to `load_locale` and serialize on the mutex for no reason, and a `reload!` interleaved between the `||=` and the include? check could change the meaning of the check. Move the include? and load inside the mutex, or accept the duplication explicitly with a comment.

title: No test covers the new ensure_loaded! call in set_locale
body: The added `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` introduces a custom fallback chain (user locale → site default → English) and triggers translation loading on every request, but no controller or initializer test is included. In particular there is no coverage for: (a) anonymous users falling back to `SiteSetting.default_locale`, (b) a logged-in user whose `effective_locale` differs from the site default, (c) the dedup behaviour between `SiteSetting.default_locale` and `:en`. The PR description ("Test 9") does not point at any spec either.

title: PR description "Test 9" does not describe the change
body: The PR body is just "Test 9" and there are no specs in the diff, so reviewers and future archeology cannot tell what behaviour was intended to be exercised. At minimum the description should enumerate which fallback chains and which anonymous/logged-in locale combinations are being validated, and link to the relevant spec files.

title: requestCount metric mislabels denial cache hit as allowed
body: In the new denial cache hit branch, the code returns `&authzv1.CheckResponse{Allowed: false}` but increments `requestCount.WithLabelValues("false", "true", req.GetVerb(), req.GetGroup(), req.GetResource()).Inc()` with the hardcoded second label `"true"`. As a result, every denial served from the new denial cache is misreported in observability metrics as an allowed request. The second label should reflect the actual outcome (`"false"` or `strconv.FormatBool(false)`).

title: requestCount metric mislabels denied DB-sourced response as allowed
body: After the DB-backed `getIdentityPermissions` call, `allowed` may be `false`, but `requestCount.WithLabelValues("false", "true", req.GetVerb(), req.GetGroup(), req.GetResource()).Inc()` is still incremented with the hardcoded `"true"` second label rather than `strconv.FormatBool(allowed)`. The line itself is pre-existing (the diff shows it as unchanged context), but the PR adds the `if !allowed { ... }` block immediately above it and is the natural opportunity to fix it. Denied responses fetched from the DB are currently counted as allowed in metrics, distorting any dashboard or alert that aggregates this counter by the (error, allowed) label pair.

title: Test does not actually demonstrate denial cache priority
body: In `TestService_CacheCheck` -> `Should deny on explicit cache deny entry`, the comment on line 981 says "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked", but the cache value on line 982 is set to `false` (`map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}`). `checkPermission` returns false for an entry whose value is `false` (or that is missing) just the same as it would if the denial-cache branch were removed, so the assertion `assert.False(t, resp.Allowed)` only verifies that the response is false — it does not actually prove that the new denial cache branch overrides a permissive perm cache. The intended demonstration requires the value to be `true`; then removing the denial-cache check would make the test fail, while keeping it makes it pass. As written, the test cannot catch a regression where the denial-cache lookup is accidentally skipped when the perm cache holds an `Allowed: true` value.

title: Denial cache can return stale results when permissions change
body: The permDenialCache is only ever written (at line 154) and never invalidated when a user's permissions change. Because the denial-cache lookup at line 117 runs before the permission cache (line 123) and the DB requery, a stale denial entry will short-circuit the request and return Allowed=false even after the user has been granted access. With shortCacheTTL = 30s, any grant that lands within 30s of an earlier deny will be ignored. Concrete scenario: user is denied → denial entry written; admin grants access via role/team within 30s; next Check returns false even though both the DB and the (refreshed) permission cache would now allow it. The denial cache needs explicit invalidation (or at minimum must be invalidated when permissions for the user change), otherwise the new "fallback to DB" path added by this PR is bypassed exactly when it is most needed.

title: Denial cache key does not account for folder-tree moves
body: userPermDenialCacheKey only includes the resource's direct parent folder, not the folder-tree state used by checkInheritedPermissions (service.go line 581, which walks tree.Ancestors(req.ParentFolder)). If the parent folder is later moved under an ancestor that the user does have access to, a previously-cached denial for (user, action, name, parent) will keep returning false for up to 30s even though the inherited permission check would now succeed. Example: dashboard X in folder A (user lacks access) → denial entry written; folder A is moved under folder B (user has access); user checks X → denial hit → denied. The denial cache entry should either be invalidated when folder moves happen or include a tree-version component in the key.

title: Denial-cache precedence test does not actually set an allow
body: In 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry' the comment at line 981 says 'Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked', but the very next line sets the permission cache to map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}. With the value false, the cached-permission branch in Check would also have returned denied, so the test passes for the wrong reason and does not prove that the denial cache wins over an actual allow. To meaningfully exercise the precedence the cache should be set to {"dashboards:uid:dash1": true} (and ideally also assert that the permission store was never called).

title: Denial cache key omits group/resource, allowing cross-API collisions
body: userPermDenialCacheKey is keyed by namespace + userUID + action + name + parent, where action is derived from (group, resource, verb). Two distinct APIs that happen to translate to the same action (e.g. dashboard.grafana.app/dashboards:get and dashboard.example.com/dashboards:get both yielding dashboards:read) will share denial entries, so a denial cached for one API would incorrectly deny checks on the other for the same name+parent. The key should include the group (and ideally the resource) so that denials are scoped to the API that produced them.

title: Denial cache test does not actually verify precedence over perm cache
body: In TestService_CacheCheck/"Should deny on explicit cache deny entry", the permCache is seeded with map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}. Because the value is false (i.e. the positive cache already encodes a deny), the assertion assert.False(t, resp.Allowed) would pass even if the new permDenialCache early-return in Check were removed: getCachedIdentityPermissions would return the cached scope map, checkPermission would return false on its own, the code would fall through to the DB (which has no userPermissions set in this subtest), and the response would still be Allowed=false. To actually exercise the precedence that the PR introduces (denial cache consulted before positive cache, denial wins), the seeded scope must be true (e.g. map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": true}); with that value, removing the permDenialCache branch would make the test fail. The inline comment "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked" is also misleading because the value being written is false, not true. As written, the test passes trivially and does not cover the new code path it is meant to cover.

title: Negative cache for (user, action, name, folder) is never invalidated, producing a 30s stale-deny window after grants
body: s.permDenialCache.Set is called whenever a DB-backed check returns Allowed=false for a concrete (namespace, userUID, action, name, parentFolder) tuple, but there is no corresponding Delete anywhere in the changed files (or the surrounding code referenced by the diff). The same cache is consulted at the very top of Check, before the positive permCache or DB is read. Consequence: if a user has previously been denied access to a specific (name, parentFolder) for a given action (e.g. they were not in a role/team that had access, or a prior transient store error returned an empty permission set), a later grant of permission on that exact resource (role assignment, team membership change, fix of a misconfigured permission, or any path that flips the DB row to allow) will not be reflected for up to shortCacheTTL = 30s — the Check call will short-circuit at line 117 and return Allowed=false even though the DB would now allow it. The PR's stated goal (letting freshly-created dashboards/folders be accessible) is fine because for newly created resources no prior denial can exist, but for any other grant path this introduces a 30-second window in which authorized users are spuriously denied. Either the denial cache must be invalidated on every permission/role/team mutation path, or the per-resource denial entry should not be persisted at all (the positive permCache miss already forces a DB lookup on the second branch added in this PR).

title: requestCount metric labeled fromCache=true on the DB-resolved response path
body: The final response path of Check (reached when getCachedIdentityPermissions returned a hit whose permission check failed and the request was re-resolved via getIdentityPermissions / DB) increments s.metrics.requestCount with WithLabelValues("false", "true", ...). The second positional label is fromCache throughout the rest of the file (e.g. the permDenialCache-hit branch at line 119 and the cached-allow branch at line 133 use the same "false","true" pair). On this last code path the answer was not served from cache, so labeling it fromCache="true" misrepresents the metric and will understate the DB/hit-miss ratio in dashboards/alerts. This label pair was already present before the PR, but the PR added a new "false" path (the post-permissionCache miss branch) that reuses the same labels, so the misleading attribution now also applies to requests that genuinely went through the new fall-through-to-DB logic.

title: Pause action not rendered for Grafana rules in list view
body: The Pause menu item is gated by `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)`, which is false when `rulerRule` is undefined. After this PR the list view no longer passes a `rulerRule` for Grafana rules, so even though `canPause` (computed from `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`) is correctly true with proper permissions, the user cannot pause/resume Grafana rules from the list view. Either keep fetching the rulerRule just for this action, refetch it on click, or render the menu item with a GrafanaPromRuleDTO-aware pause component.

title: Delete action not rendered for Grafana rules in list view
body: The Delete menu item is gated by `canDelete && rulerRule && (...)`. With the list view no longer providing `rulerRule` for Grafana rules, `rulerRule` is undefined, so Delete is not rendered even though the new `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` check correctly reports `canDelete = true`. Users will lose the ability to delete Grafana rules from the list view. The component or its handler needs to support a path that does not require a `RulerRuleDTO`.

title: Silence drawer never opens for Grafana rules in list view
body: `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` is only mounted when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true, which is false when `rule` is undefined. In the new list view flow, `rule` is no longer passed to `RuleActionsButtons` (only `promRule`), so the Silence menu item appears in the dropdown (because `canSilence` is computed from `promRule`) but clicking it sets `showSilenceDrawer = true` and the drawer never mounts, silently doing nothing. Either gate the menu item on the same condition, or refactor the drawer to accept a `GrafanaPromRuleDTO`.

title: Missing `key` prop on GrafanaRuleListItem in FilterView switch
body: The previous code rendered `<GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} ...>` for the `grafana` case inside the `rules.map(...)`. After this change the new `<GrafanaRuleListItem ...>` is missing the `key` prop, while the sibling branches (`case 'datasource'` and the `default` case) still pass `key={key}`. Without a key on one branch React will fall back to array indices, which can cause incorrect component reuse, lost local state, and unnecessary remounts when the list is filtered, paginated or re-ordered.

title: Federated rule groups no longer detected as immutable
body: `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` now hard-codes `const isFederated = false;` with a TODO to re-add support. The previous implementation derived this from `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)`. Because this hook is still used for non-Grafana (cloud/Mimir) rules via `useAllAlertRuleAbilities`, federated rule groups will no longer be considered `immutableRule`, meaning Update/Delete/Pause/Restore abilities may report `supported=true` for rules that should be read-only at the federation level. Re-introduce the federated check or document that this is an intentional regression.

title: Removing Creating/Deleting state indicators is not covered by tests or docs
body: The old `GrafanaGroupLoader` rendered `RuleOperation.Creating` items for rules present in the Ruler but not yet in Prometheus, and `RuleOperation.Deleting` items for rules only in Prometheus (with a `logWarning`). Both the implementation and the corresponding tests (`should render rule with url and creating state when only ruler rule exists`, `should render delete rule operation list item when only prom rule exists`) have been removed. This is a user-visible UX regression (rules appear to vanish / reappear) but the change is not described in the PR description, nor in a changelog entry, and there is no test asserting the new behavior. Please document the intentional behavior change and add coverage.

title: Test asserting exactly 4 menu items encodes the missing Pause/Delete regression
body: The new test `should render correct menu actions when More button is clicked` asserts `expect(menuItems.length).toBe(4)` after granting all of `AlertingRuleUpdate`, `AlertingRuleDelete`, `AlertingRuleCreate`, etc. With those permissions the abilities hooks report `canPause = true` and `canDelete = true`, but the menu items for Pause and Delete are not rendered because of the `rulerRule`/`rule` gates in `AlertRuleMenu.tsx` (lines 123 and 165) and `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx` (line 104). The test currently passes because the bug is hard-coded into the expected count; once the Pause/Delete render bug is fixed, this test will fail unless updated.

title: Stale `// duplicate` comment
body: Inside `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` the line `const { isEditable, isRemovable, loading } = useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable(rule); // duplicate` carries a trailing `// duplicate` comment that does not explain anything (it doesn't say what is duplicated or why). It looks like a leftover TODO that should be removed or replaced with a meaningful comment.

title: Misleading `@deprecated` on `useAllAlertRuleAbilities`
body: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` is marked `@deprecated Use {@link useAllRulerRuleAbilities} instead`, but `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` is not a drop-in replacement: it has a different signature (`RulerRuleDTO | undefined` + `RuleGroupIdentifierV2` vs. `CombinedRule`). The wrapper itself (and `useAlertRuleAbility` / `useAlertRuleAbilities`) still calls `useAllAlertRuleAbilities`, so this deprecation is contradictory and will be confusing to readers. Either remove the deprecation, update the message, or finish migrating the `useAlertRuleAbility*` hooks.

title: `RuleActionsButtons` silently renders null for invalid props
body: `getEditableIdentifier` returns `undefined` and the component returns `null` whenever neither a `RulerRuleDTO` nor a Grafana `promRule` is supplied. Previously the prop `rule: RulerRuleDTO` was required and an identifier was always produced. The new permissive typing means a caller can pass `{}` (no rulerRule, no grafana promRule) and get an empty cell in the row instead of an obvious error. The TypeScript `RequireAtLeastOne` only narrows at the callsite, not at the place that actually uses both fields. At minimum, callers should be warned explicitly (a `logWarning` is logged but it does not propagate to the UI), and ideally a runtime error would be raised in development.

title: `useRulerRuleAbilities(undefined, ...)` still calls `useIsRuleEditable` from the list view
body: Even though `GrafanaRuleListItem` no longer provides a `rulerRule`, `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx` and `AlertRuleMenu.tsx` both still invoke `useRulerRuleAbility(s)` / `useRulerRuleAbilities` for every row, which in turn call `useIsRuleEditable(rulesSourceName, rule)` internally. If `useIsRuleEditable` issues a Ruler network call (as its name suggests), the goal of this PR — eliminating Ruler traffic from the alert list view — is not actually achieved for Grafana rules. Verify the implementation of `useIsRuleEditable` and short-circuit the hook when no `rulerRule` is provided (e.g., reuse the same `skipToken` pattern used for `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`).

title: GrafanaRuleListItem rendered inside .map() without a key prop
body: In FilterView.tsx the map over `rules` renders `GrafanaRuleListItem` for the `grafana` origin without a `key` prop, while the sibling `datasource` case still passes `key={key}`. The pre-existing code (deleted `GrafanaRuleLoader`) was passed `key={key}`; the replacement JSX drops that attribute. React relies on a stable key per list child to reconcile the list — without it React will warn in console and may reuse/mis-render state when rules are reordered, filtered, or partially updated. Add `key={key}` to the `GrafanaRuleListItem` JSX, mirroring the dataSource branch.

title: Tests mock the wrong ability hook for RuleActionsButtons (stale comment and mocks)
body:
The mock table and all assertions are built around `useAlertRuleAbility` (singular), with the comment 'RuleActionsButtons uses: useAlertRuleAbility (singular)'. After this PR, `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx` no longer calls `useAlertRuleAbility` — it calls `useRulerRuleAbility` for the ruler-side edit ability and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility` (with `skipToken`) for the prom-side fallback. As a result the per-test overrides of `useAlertRuleAbility` (e.g. for Update/Delete) have no effect on what is rendered, and the previous default `[false, false]` from `useRulerRuleAbility` is what actually drives `canEditRule`/`canDelete` etc. Concretely:

- The 'Should not render Delete button for users without the delete permission' test never sets `useRulerRuleAbility`/`useRulerRuleAbilities` for Grafana, so it appears to pass for the wrong reason (and only because the grafana-side plural hook is overridden); it does not exercise the OR-of-abilities logic in `AlertRuleMenu`.
- The 'Should render Delete button for users with the delete permission' test depends on the same gap.

Update the mocks and the explanatory comment so that the singular/plural ruler and grafana-prom hooks used by the V2 components are what is being stubbed, and assert against the actual hook calls. Otherwise a regression in `useRulerRuleAbility`/abilities OR'ing would go undetected.

title: Pause and Delete menu items are silently unavailable in the list view (rulerRule is now undefined)
body:
`AlertRuleMenu` still gates the Pause and Delete entries on the presence of the ruler-side data:

- Pause: `{canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) && groupIdentifier.groupOrigin === 'grafana' && (<MenuItemPauseRule rule={rulerRule} ... />)}`
- Delete: `{canDelete && rulerRule && (... onClick={() => handleDelete(rulerRule, groupIdentifier)} ...)}`

After this PR the grafana list view (`GrafanaRuleListItem`, `FilterView`) constructs the actions tree with only `promRule`, so `rulerRule` is `undefined` everywhere and both menu items disappear — not because the user lacks permissions (the abilities are still `[supported, allowed]` via the grafana-prom fallback) but because the underlying click handlers need the full ruler payload. This is a behavior regression vs. the previous list view and is not described in the PR description. Users will have to drill into each rule's detail page to pause or delete it, and any bulk operations built on the list will also break. Either plumb through enough ruler data (or use a prom-based delete path) so these actions keep working in the list, or call out this UX change explicitly and gate the entire removal behind a feature flag.

title: Dropping ruler fallback loses the 'Creating' / 'Deleting' rule states
body:
Before this change `GrafanaGroupLoader` fetched ruler data, paired it with the prom response via `matchRules`, and rendered outstanding rulers with `RuleOperation.Creating` and unmatched prom rules with `RuleOperation.Deleting`. After removing the ruler fetch (and `matchRules`/`RulerRuleLoadingError`), the component only renders `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules` directly. As a consequence:

- A rule that has been accepted by the ruler but not yet propagated to Prometheus (window of eventual consistency) disappears from the list instead of being shown with the 'Creating' badge.
- A rule that has been deleted from the ruler but is still in the prom response no longer appears as 'Deleting'.

Previously these intermediates were explicitly logged with `logWarning` because they are rare/expected; now they are silently absent, hiding the operation from the user. Either keep the ruler fetch + match (same call it makes today) just for status derivation, or update the prom API so the rule DTO carries a creation/in-flight marker that the list can render without a second query. This should be flagged in the PR description and either preserved or have tests covering the in-flight state.

title: Silence menu item silently does nothing in the alert list view
body: When GrafanaRuleListItem renders a rule from Prometheus data only, RuleActionsButtons receives promRule but no rulerRule. The Silence menu item in AlertRuleMenu is gated only by `canSilence` (it does NOT check `rulerRule`), so it is rendered. Clicking it triggers `setShowSilenceDrawer(true)`, but the SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer is conditionally rendered as `{rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer && <SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer rulerRule={rule} ... />}`. When `rule` is undefined this short-circuits to false, so the drawer never renders. The user clicks Silence in the menu, the menu closes, and nothing visible happens, with no error feedback. Either the Silence menu item must also be gated on `rulerRule` (matching Delete/Pause) or SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer must be updated to accept promRule-based data.

title: Delete menu item is no longer reachable in the alert list view (feature regression)
body: The Delete menu item is rendered as `{canDelete && rulerRule && (...)}`. In the alert list view, GrafanaRuleListItem passes only `promRule` to RuleActionsButtons, so `rulerRule` is undefined and Delete never appears, even when `canDelete` is true (which is now legitimately computed from `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`). Previously, the list view loaded the ruler rule for each Grafana rule and Delete was reachable. After this PR a user can view a Grafana rule in the list and edit it but cannot delete it from the list at all. Either remove `rulerRule &&` from the gate (and rework the onClick to not pass rulerRule) or document/handle the regression explicitly.

title: GrafanaRuleListItem returned from .map() is missing a `key` prop
body: Inside `rules.map((ruleWithOrigin) => { ... switch (origin) { ... case 'grafana': return (<GrafanaRuleListItem ... />); ... } })` the GrafanaRuleListItem element lacks a `key` prop, while the sibling cases (`DataSourceRuleLoader`, `UnknownRuleListItem`) correctly set `key={key}`. React will emit a 'Each child in a list should have a unique key' warning and state preservation for the rendered list item can be incorrect if the list reorders. Restore `key={key}` on the GrafanaRuleListItem to match the other branches.

title: GrafanaGroupLoader tests assert Silence menu appears but do not verify the click works in list view
body: The new tests in GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx assert that the Silence menu item is in the dropdown (`expect(ui.menuItems.silence().get()).toBeInTheDocument()`). They do not click Silence to verify a silence drawer actually opens. With the new render path, `rulerRule` is undefined so the SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer never mounts (see finding on RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx line 104), making the assertion misleading: the menu item is present but the feature is non-functional. Add a test that clicks Silence and verifies a drawer/silence creation flow actually opens (or assert the menu item is NOT present when rulerRule is unavailable).

title: New useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities family has no dedicated unit tests
body: The newly added hooks `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility`, `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, and `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable` (lines 287-406) are only exercised indirectly through RulesTable/AlertRuleMenu tests. Behavioral differences vs the ruler versions are subtle and untested: e.g. silence ability is `[silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule]` (recording rules can never be silenced), `isProvisioned` uses promRule.provenance, and `MaybeSupported` is hardcoded to AlwaysSupported (no `isRulerAvailable` flag). Without dedicated tests a regression in any of these branches (particularly the recording-rule silencing guard, which differs from the previous ruler behavior) could land unnoticed.

title: useAllAlertRuleAbilities is now deprecated but still exported and called from new code
body: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` is marked `@deprecated` in favor of `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`. The new AlertRuleMenu still computes abilities using both `useRulerRuleAbilities` AND `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` (an OR), and the new RuleActionsButtons.V2 follows the same pattern. There is no public hook that combines rule + groupIdentifier into a single OR of (ruler-based, prom-based) abilities for a CombinedRule. As written, every consumer has to manually call both hooks and OR the results, which is duplicated several times already (AlertRuleMenu does it 5 times). Consider exposing a combined `useAllAlertRuleAbilitiesFor(rule: CombinedRule | GrafanaPromRuleDTO, ...)` helper so the OR logic lives in one place and isn't re-implemented (and possibly desynchronized) at every callsite.

title: userEvent instance is shared across all tests instead of being recreated per test
body: `const user = userEvent.setup();` is created at module scope and shared by every test in the file. userEvent accumulates internal queues/state across tests; reusing the same instance across tests can lead to flakiness or interleaved events when tests run in parallel or share state. Standard practice is to call `userEvent.setup()` (or `render` returned `user`) inside each test or in `beforeEach` for a fresh setup.

title: Double interpolation of targets in sharded split path
body: runShardSplitQuery() now calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables() on every non-hidden target, then build sub-requests via interpolateShardingSelector and passes them to runSplitQuery(). runSplitQuery() then calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables() again on the same targets (querySplitting.ts line 299). Because variables such as $__auto and $step have already been substituted on the first pass, the second pass is a no-op string scan over every expr/step for every shard sub-request. While idempotent, this is wasted work proportional to (number_of_subqueries × targets_per_subquery). Consider detecting already-interpolated queries or pushing the interpolation responsibility to a single layer so the work is done once.

title: Brittle exact call-count assertion for applyTemplateVariables
body: The updated test 'Interpolates queries before running' asserts expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5). That count is tied to the current number of shard groups/requests produced by splitQueriesByStreamShard (currently 4 runSplitQuery sub-requests + 1 from runShardSplitQuery). Any future refactor that changes how shard groups are partitioned or merged - including the legitimate optimization of skipping the redundant second interpolation noted above - will break this test even when behavior is otherwise correct. Asserting on the final runQuery args, or checking the spy was called at least once per non-hidden target, would be more robust.

title: querySupportsSplitting check now operates on already-interpolated expr
body: applyTemplateVariables is called before querySupportsSplitting and partition. querySupportsSplitting() relies on isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr) returning true to keep $__range-bearing queries out of the split path (see the inline comment about backend interpolation with the split timeRange). Once $__range / $__range_s / $__range_ms have been substituted into numeric strings by applyTemplateVariables, isQueryWithRangeVariable can no longer recognise them and those queries will silently fall through into normalQueries and get split. The behavior change is benign for $__auto / $step but potentially incorrect for $__range queries, since the FRONTEND now substitutes them with the dashboard range while each sub-request still carries the chunk's range. Either guard the interpolation (skip applyTemplateVariables for queries that contain a $__range variable) or update querySupportsSplitting to detect the substituted form, and add a test covering a $__range expression.

title: applyTemplateVariables mock mutates input instead of returning a new object
body: The beforeEach mock for applyTemplateVariables does `query.expr = query.expr.replace(...); return query;`, i.e. it returns the SAME object reference with mutated fields. The real DataSource implementation in Grafana returns a fresh object via spread (`return { ...query, expr: ... }`), so the tests run against a fake implementation that mutates the caller's targets array. If someone fixes the mock to mirror the real implementation - or if the production code starts assuming the return is a new object - the test expectations (which look at the same query objects via runQuery mock.calls) can pass for the wrong reason. Recommend splitting the mock to return a new object so tests stay aligned with production semantics.

title: $__range queries no longer routed to non-splitting path because detection happens after interpolation
body: In `runSplitQuery`, `datasource.applyTemplateVariables` is now invoked on every kept target (line 299) BEFORE `partition(..., query => !querySupportsSplitting(query))` is evaluated (line 300). `querySupportsSplitting` relies on `isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` which uses `expr.includes('$__range')`. Because `templateSrv.replace` substitutes `$__range`/`$__range_s`/`$__range_ms` with numeric values, those strings are gone from `expr` by the time the check runs. As a result, queries such as `rate({app="frontend"}[$__range])` are now placed in `normalQueries` and get split across chunks instead of being routed to `nonSplittingQueries`. This is exactly the case the in-source comment on lines 285-287 warns against: when the chunk reaches the backend, `$__range` would be (re-)interpolated against the split timeRange and the result would be incorrect. Before this PR, `runSplitQuery` did not interpolate, so the `isQueryWithRangeVariable` check worked. The interpolation must be deferred until after the `$__range` / `querySupportsSplitting` classification, or the non-splitting partition must be computed from the original `request.targets`.

title: Mock `replace` does not handle built-in variables, masking the $__range regression
body: The new test `'Interpolates queries before execution'` (and the corresponding one in `shardQuerySplitting.test.ts`) override `replace` to substitute only `$__auto` and `$step`. They leave `$__range`/`$__range_s`/`$__range_ms` untouched. The real Grafana `templateSrv.replace` substitutes these built-ins. Because the mock preserves them, any future test using `$__range` will pass (the substring check finds the literal) while production silently drops them, so the regression described for `querySplitting.ts` cannot be caught by the current mock setup. The mocks should also replace built-in variables (e.g. `$__range` → `300s`) to reflect production, and a test asserting that a `$__range` query is not split should be added.

title: Queries are interpolated twice on the shard-splitting path
body: `runShardSplitQuery` (lines 49-52) maps every kept target through `datasource.applyTemplateVariables` and hands the resulting array to `splitQueriesByStreamShard`, which then constructs a `subRequest` whose `targets` are derived from those already-interpolated queries and passes that subRequest to `runSplitQuery` (line 163). `runSplitQuery` now also calls `applyTemplateVariables` on every kept target. So in the shard path each target is interpolated twice. Beyond wasted work, this is fragile: if `templateSrv.replace` (or a downstream format handler) is ever non-idempotent for any variable, the second pass would produce different output. The interpolation in `runShardSplitQuery` is redundant once `runSplitQuery` performs it itself; one of the two should be removed.

title: $__range check ineffective after interpolation breaks splitting logic for range queries
body: The change interpolates queries upfront via `applyTemplateVariables` (line 299), but the `querySupportsSplitting` check at line 282 is still applied to the interpolated queries via `partition` at line 300. The check `!isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` is intended to prevent splitting queries that contain `$__range`, but after `applyTemplateVariables` replaces `$__range` with a literal duration (e.g., `3d` or `259200000ms`), the check always returns true. As a result, queries like `count_over_time({a="b"}[$__range])` will now be split into sub-requests, but the `$__range` literal value baked into the query is the FULL range (since interpolation uses `request.range`), not the split range. This produces semantically incorrect results: each sub-request queries `[3d]` worth of data but only returns a window of 1d. The accompanying comment at lines 285-286 explicitly states that `$__range` queries should NOT be split. The `isQueryWithRangeVariable` check needs to be applied before interpolation (e.g., on the original `request.targets`), or `$__range` needs to be left uninterpolated and re-applied per sub-request.

title: No test covers $__range behavior after interpolation change
body: The new test 'Interpolates queries before execution' (line 75) only verifies `$__auto` and `$step` interpolation. There is no test for `$__range` queries after this change. A regression test should verify that queries containing `$__range` are still routed to the non-splitting path (i.e., they should not be split because the interpolated `$__range` value would be incorrect for split sub-requests). Without such a test, the `$__range` regression described in the primary finding could go undetected.

title: traceID field dropped from Plugin Request Completed log line
body: The old LoggerMiddleware.logRequest explicitly retrieved the trace ID via tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false) and appended it to the log params when non-empty. The new implementation calls m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...) with no equivalent step, and the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware (which now owns the contextual attribute injection) only adds endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname — it never adds traceID. As a result the "Plugin Request Completed" log line loses the traceID key that operators previously relied on to correlate plugin request logs with distributed traces. The traceID is still attached as a Prometheus exemplar in MetricsMiddleware, so the value is available in metrics, but it is no longer present in the request log.

title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware has no test file
body: The PR adds a brand-new middleware (NewContextualLoggerMiddleware / ContextualLoggerMiddleware) that is now responsible for enriching the request context with endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, and uname, and the LoggerMiddleware was changed to depend on that enrichment. Despite this, no contextual_logger_middleware_test.go is added. The existing tests only cover the renamed MetricsMiddleware. Without a test that exercises the four endpoints (QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) and verifies the contextual attributes are attached to the context, regressions in the enrichment logic (e.g. wrong field names, missing nil checks, or an endpoint that forgets to call instrumentContext) will not be caught.

title: LoggerMiddleware silently loses fields when ContextualLoggerMiddleware is absent
body: logRequest was changed from m.logger.Info(...) (self-contained: it explicitly appended pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName, dsUID, traceID) to m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...). The contextual attributes now come exclusively from ContextualLoggerMiddleware, which sits directly above LoggerMiddleware in CreateMiddlewares. If anyone reorders, removes, or conditionally skips ContextualLoggerMiddleware (the middleware is newly added and easy to miss), the "Plugin Request Completed" log line will lose endpoint, pluginId, uname, dsName, dsUID with no warning. The previous code was self-sufficient; the new code has a hidden ordering dependency. This should at minimum be documented on the function/middleware, or the fields should be re-added as fallbacks.

title: FromContext doc comment is incorrect
body: The comment "FromContext returns a new contextual Logger that has this logger's context plus the given context" implies FromContext merges additional context into the receiver, but the implementation (grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext in logger.go) actually extracts a *log.ConcreteLogger that was previously stored in ctx (via log.WithContextualAttributes) and rewraps it. The new logger is not "this logger's context plus the given context" — it is whatever the context already carries. The comment should describe that FromContext returns a Logger populated with the contextual attributes already present in ctx (returning a fresh logger if none are found). The same wording was previously used for New, where it is also inaccurate because New takes variadic any key/value pairs, not a context.

title: New doc comment misdescribes the parameter
body: The comment "New returns a new contextual Logger that has this logger's context plus the given context" was left unchanged, but New takes ctx ...any (key/value pairs) — not a context.Context. Combined with the newly added FromContext that does take a context.Context, the two methods are easy to confuse. The comment should be updated to describe New as taking key/value context attributes (e.g. "New returns a new contextual Logger that has this logger's context plus the given key/value pairs").

title: TestLogger.FromContext ignores its argument
body: TestLogger.FromContext(_ context.Context) Logger discards the context and returns a brand-new TestLogger, so any test that uses TestLogger to exercise code paths which now go through FromContext (notably the rewritten LoggerMiddleware.logRequest, which calls m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)) cannot assert that the contextual attributes placed in ctx by ContextualLoggerMiddleware actually reach the log call. The fake should at minimum capture the supplied context (or the contextual attributes derived from it) so tests can verify the propagation; otherwise the new dependency between LoggerMiddleware and ContextualLoggerMiddleware is untestable through this fake.

title: instrumentContext name is a leftover from the old InstrumentationMiddleware
body: The function is named instrumentContext, but it lives in ContextualLoggerMiddleware and only adds log key/value pairs to the context — it does no instrumentation in the metrics/tracing sense. The name was carried over verbatim from the old InstrumentationMiddleware. Renaming to e.g. addContextualAttributes or withPluginContextLogAttrs would make the new file self-describing.

title: traceID no longer attached to "Plugin Request Completed" log line
body: The old logRequest explicitly fetched the trace ID and appended it to the log params: `traceID := tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false); if traceID != "" { logParams = append(logParams, "traceID", traceID) }`. That code has been deleted in this PR and the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware.instrumentContext (pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/contextual_logger_middleware.go) only adds endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname — it never reads or forwards the trace ID via log.WithContextualAttributes. Nothing in the modified LoggerMiddleware recovers it either, so every "Plugin Request Completed" log line now loses its trace correlation. Unless pkg/infra/log's FromContext implementation silently injects a traceID (which the old explicit code suggests it does not), this is an observability regression: distributed tracing can no longer be joined back to the request completion log line.

title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware has no test coverage
body: A brand-new client middleware was added that mutates the request context with endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname via log.WithContextualAttributes on every QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth and CollectMetrics path. No contextual_logger_middleware_test.go was added, and the sibling metrics_middleware_test.go does not exercise this middleware. There is consequently no regression protection for: (a) the order in which contextual attributes are appended (the existing pCtx.DataSourceInstanceSettings / pCtx.User nil checks), (b) the assumption that downstream LoggerMiddleware actually picks the attributes up via FromContext, or (c) the still-missing traceID described in the related finding. A test should assert the expected key/value pairs on the context after each entrypoint, mirroring what the deleted instrumentContext tests would have caught.

title: Test function still named after the old middleware
body: The file was renamed from instrumentation_middleware_test.go to metrics_middleware_test.go and the helper references were updated (e.g. newMetricsMiddleware on line 78), but the top-level test func TestInstrumentationMiddleware was left unchanged. After this rename the test name no longer matches the production type it exercises; CI tooling, `--run` filtering and any coverage reports will keep advertising the obsolete name. Rename it to TestMetricsMiddleware for consistency with the rest of the rename.

title: Test function name not renamed to match the middleware
body: The test function is still named `TestInstrumentationMiddleware` even though the file and the middleware it tests were renamed to `MetricsMiddleware`. The diff only updates the internal call to `newMetricsMiddleware`, leaving the outer test name stale, which makes the test hard to find, breaks grep-based filtering (`-run TestMetricsMiddleware`), and signals that the rename was applied incompletely.

title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware has no test coverage
body: The new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` (and its `instrumentContext` helper, which builds the `endpoint`/`pluginId`/`dsName`/`dsUID`/`uname` attribute slice) is added with 69 lines of behavior but no accompanying `_test.go` file. The previous `instrumentContext` lived inside `instrumentation_middleware.go` and was likewise uncovered, but the move to a dedicated middleware is the right moment to add at least a basic test that verifies the contextual attributes are correctly populated (including the nil checks for `DataSourceInstanceSettings` and `User`) and are present on the downstream context.

title: LoggerMiddleware silently loses contextual fields if ContextualLoggerMiddleware is removed from the chain
body: The previous `logRequest` explicitly added `pluginId`, `endpoint`, `uname`, `dsName`, `dsUID`, and `traceID` as explicit log parameters. The new implementation strips all of those from `logParams` and relies on `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` to pick them up from the request context. That only works if `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` (which calls `log.WithContextualAttributes`) sits between `MetricsMiddleware` and `LoggerMiddleware` in the chain. Today this is true (see `pluginsintegration.go` lines 158-161), but the dependency is now implicit: any future refactor that reorders, conditionally registers, or removes the contextual-logger middleware will cause `Plugin Request Completed` log lines to silently lose identifying fields (plugin id, datasource uid, user, endpoint, trace id) with no compile-time or test-time signal. Either keep an explicit fallback that logs those fields if they are missing from context, or add a test that asserts the chain ordering.

title: FromContext falls back to a context-less logger when the type assertion fails
body: `grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext` does `d.l.FromContext(ctx).(*log.ConcreteLogger)`. If the type assertion ever fails (e.g. a future change in `pkg/infra/log` returns a different concrete type, or a test fakes the infra logger), the code falls back to `d.New()`, silently discarding every contextual attribute that `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` placed on the context. Since `LoggerMiddleware` now depends on this method to surface `pluginId`/`endpoint`/`uname` in production logs, a silent attribute drop here directly degrades log quality. Returning the asserted value (or logging/returning an error) is safer than constructing a fresh logger with no context.

title: Local cache set before DB call lets user bypass device limit on retry
body: In tagDeviceUI the local cache entry is written *before* a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice is invoked, and the same method returns nil on a subsequent cache hit without ever touching the database. Once the first CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, the cache still holds the key, so the very next request from the same device (within the 29 minute TTL) returns nil from tagDeviceUI, TagDevice returns nil, and Anonymous.Authenticate falls through to the success branch and admits the user even though they were never persisted to anon_device. In other words the device_limit enforcement only blocks the first attempt and is silently bypassed from then on. The cache write must be moved to after a successful CreateOrUpdateDevice, or only set on success.

title: TOCTOU race between CountDevices and the INSERT in CreateOrUpdateDevice
body: CreateOrUpdateDevice reads SELECT COUNT(*) and then conditionally issues an INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE, with no transaction or row lock around the pair. Two concurrent anonymous auths can both observe count == deviceLimit-1 and both succeed at the INSERT, leaving N+1 rows. With a small device_limit and any concurrent burst the advertised cap is silently exceeded. The check and the insert need to be done atomically (e.g. SERIALIZABLE transaction, SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on a sentinel row, or push the cap into a single INSERT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*)) < ?).

title: Anonymous authentication now blocks on a DB write per request
body: The previous implementation did the device tagging inside a goroutine with its own context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), timeoutTag), so anonymous auth never paid the cost of the INSERT/UPDATE. The new code calls a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice synchronously on the request context. Every anonymous request now waits on a database round trip (and a COUNT(*) when device_limit > 0) before issuing the authn.Identity, which is a clear latency regression under load. Consider preserving the async path for the happy case and only awaiting the result when the limit is actually close to being reached, or returning ErrDeviceLimitReached asynchronously.

title: Lost panic recovery on the synchronous tagging path
body: The old goroutine wrapped TagDevice in defer recover(){...} so a panic in the device tagging code only produced a log warning. The new synchronous call has no recovery, so any panic from a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice (or anything it calls) will now propagate up through Anonymous.Authenticate into the authn pipeline and crash the request handler. The recover() needs to be restored (e.g. with a named return) so a tagging panic cannot take down an anonymous auth request.

title: updateDevice silently locks out devices older than the 30 day window
body: The UPDATE statement only matches rows whose updated_at is BETWEEN (new UpdatedAt - anonymousDeviceExpiration) AND (new UpdatedAt + time.Minute). Devices that are older than 30 days but younger than the 61 day cleanup threshold still occupy a row but never count toward CountDevices and never match this WHERE. If the limit is reached (by fresh devices) and a previously active user returns after ~30 days, they hit ErrDeviceLimitReached even though they used to have a valid device, and there is no way for them to renew their slot until the cleanup job happens to run. The WHERE should probably match any existing row with the given device_id (or at least include the stale window) so users can refresh an old device instead of being permanently locked out.

title: device_limit setting is parsed but not documented anywhere
body: cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit is now read from auth.anonymous.device_limit, but the diff does not add the new key to the conf.ini spec file, the sample ini, or any docs page. Operators have no way to learn the option exists, what value 0 means (it disables the limit), or how the 30 day window interacts with the cap. Without documentation this feature is effectively invisible and any default a maintainer intends to ship will not be communicated.

title: No test exercises concurrent requests against the device limit
body: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only checks the single threaded flow: insert one device, then expect the second CreateOrUpdateDevice to return ErrDeviceLimitReached. It does not exercise the concurrent case that the new TOCTOU window in CreateOrUpdateDevice is most likely to fail in, and it does not exercise AnonDeviceService end to end (so the cache-bypass bug described in impl.go goes undetected). A goroutine based test that fans out more than device_limit parallel CreateOrUpdateDevice calls (and one that drives TagDevice through the service to verify the Authenticate behavior on limit hit) is needed.

title: Stale devices cannot be re-activated when limit is reached
body: In `CreateOrUpdateDevice`, when `count >= s.deviceLimit` the code delegates to `updateDevice`, which only matches rows whose `updated_at` is within the last 30 days (`BETWEEN device.UpdatedAt - anonymousDeviceExpiration AND device.UpdatedAt + time.Minute`). Because the active-count query already excludes rows older than 30 days, a device that has not been seen for >30 days does not count toward the limit; but `updateDevice` still treats it as 'not found' and returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, so a legitimate returning device is rejected. The same code path returns the same error for a truly new device, conflating the two cases and breaking device re-activation for users who have been away longer than the expiration window. Either the limit-saturated path should DELETE/INSERT stale rows (since they don't count toward the active count) or it should fall back to the regular upsert when no existing row matches the device ID, regardless of age.

title: TOCTOU race lets concurrent inserts bypass the device limit
body: `CreateOrUpdateDevice` does a `SELECT COUNT(*)` followed by an INSERT/UPSERT, with no transaction or row-level lock. Two simultaneous requests for distinct new device IDs can both observe `count < deviceLimit`, both fall through to the INSERT branch, and both succeed, pushing the active-device count above the configured `device_limit`. The same race exists between the count check and the subsequent UPDATE inside `updateDevice`. Wrap the count and the mutation in a single transaction (or otherwise serialize) so the limit is actually enforced under load.

title: Device tagging is now synchronous on every anonymous authentication
body: The previous implementation dispatched `TagDevice` in a goroutine with a `context.Background()` and a 2-minute timeout, so DB latency and DB errors did not block the auth path. The new code calls `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, httpReqCopy, ...)` inline using the request context. Every anonymous authentication now incurs an extra COUNT/INSERT/UPDATE round-trip plus, on Postgres/MySQL, the per-statement latency, and any transient DB error (or client disconnect that cancels `ctx`) will surface as a failed authentication even when no limit is configured. Consider keeping the fire-and-forget pattern (or a small bounded background context) for the no-limit case and only doing the synchronous, error-returning path when `AnonymousDeviceLimit > 0`.

title: Request context cancellation can lose device tags
body: `TagDevice` now uses the inbound request `ctx`. If the client disconnects mid-auth (a common case for an anonymous browser session that redirects away), the context is cancelled and the DB write is aborted, but the request handler then continues and returns success. The device is therefore neither in the DB nor counted for future requests until it is seen again. The previous implementation used `context.Background()` with its own timeout precisely to avoid this. The new design should derive a detached context (e.g., `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` or a fresh background context) for the device-tag DB write so client cancellation doesn't drop the write.

title: New device-limit path is not covered by tests beyond the obvious case
body: `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` only exercises the 'insert device A then reject new device B with limit=1' scenario. There is no test for the stale-but-existing device case (a device whose `updated_at` is older than 30 days that comes back when the active count is at the limit), nor for the TOCTOU race, nor for the `deviceLimit == 0` path confirming that the COUNT/UPDATE branch is fully bypassed. The stale-device case in particular hides a real bug (see separate finding); adding a regression test for it would have caught it.

title: Local cache is populated before the DB write, hiding failures
body: In `tagDeviceUI` the local cache is `SetDefault`ed *before* `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice` is called. If the DB write fails for any reason (DB blip, transient error, or the new ErrDeviceLimitReached that is returned for stale devices), the cache will continue to short-circuit writes for that device for the full 29-minute TTL, so the device will silently be absent from the DB even after the underlying problem clears. Set the cache entry only after a successful DB write, or pair it with a delete-on-error so retries can recover.

title: New `device_limit` setting is not documented in conf/defaults.ini
body: `readAuthSettings` now reads `auth.anonymous.device_limit`, but `conf/defaults.ini` (the canonical user-facing reference for Grafana configuration) is not in the change set. Operators have no way to discover the option, its key name, or the meaning of `0` (no limit) from the shipped configuration. Add a commented entry under `[auth.anonymous]` describing `device_limit`, its default, and the `0 = unlimited` semantics, and update any related docs (e.g., the anonymous-auth admin guide).

title: AnonymousDeviceLimit is exposed to unauthenticated clients
body: `AnonymousDeviceLimit int64` is added unconditionally to `FrontendSettingsDTO`, which is returned by `GET /api/frontend/settings` to every caller, including fully anonymous users. The value is also exposed via the matching `anonymousDeviceLimit` field in the runtime config. While the limit is not strictly secret, it is server-capacity information that helps an attacker probe the configured ceiling by attempting to register many fake `X-Grafana-Device-Id` values until `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is observed in the auth response. Consider omitting the field when `AnonymousEnabled` is false, or rounding/omitting it for non-admin sessions.

title: Test name and assertions don't verify that the first device was actually counted
body: `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` only asserts that the second `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. It does not assert on `CountDevices` before the second call to confirm the count actually reached the configured limit, so a regression that makes the limit check silently no-op (e.g., if `s.deviceLimit` were not threaded through) would still pass the test. Add an explicit `CountDevices` assertion between the two `CreateOrUpdateDevice` calls.

title: TOCTOU race allows exceeding device limit
body: In CreateOrUpdateDevice, the device count is read in one DB session (s.CountDevices) and the subsequent INSERT/UPDATE runs in a separate session. Under concurrent load, multiple requests can all observe count < limit and all proceed to INSERT, allowing the actual device count to exceed the configured limit by the number of in-flight requests. The check-then-act must be wrapped in a transaction with appropriate locking, or the limit enforced by a DB-level mechanism, to guarantee the cap.

title: TagDevice moved to synchronous request context
body: The previous implementation called TagDevice in a goroutine with an independent 2-minute context (context.Background() + WithTimeout). The new code calls TagDevice synchronously using the request context. Consequences: (a) every anonymous auth now pays the full DB latency (count + insert/update) on the hot path; (b) if the client cancels the request, the request context is cancelled and the device is never tagged, which both skews the usage stat 'stats.anonymous.device.ui.count' and lets a device avoid being counted against the limit. The async design should be retained for non-limit errors and only the limit-exceeded path needs to surface synchronously.

title: Extra COUNT(*) on every anonymous auth when limit is set
body: CreateOrUpdateDevice now issues a SELECT COUNT(*) ... WHERE updated_at BETWEEN ... AND ... on every call when deviceLimit > 0. There is no caching of the count and the check runs unconditionally on the auth hot path, adding a full table scan (or index scan) to every anonymous request even when the limit is nowhere near being reached.

title: Auth-flow behavior change for ErrDeviceLimitReached has no test
body: Anonymous.Authenticate now propagates anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached up so authentication fails when the limit is hit. The new integration test (TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit) only covers the store-level CreateOrUpdateDevice path; there is no test that exercises Anonymous.Authenticate to confirm (1) ErrDeviceLimitReached causes Authenticate to return an error rather than a successful identity, and (2) other errors from TagDevice are still swallowed with a warning. This is a behavior change that warrants a dedicated test, including asserting what HTTP status / message a real request would receive.

title: New device_limit setting has no user-facing documentation
body: The PR adds cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit read from [auth.anonymous] device_limit with default 0 (treated as unlimited), but no documentation file (e.g. docs/sources/setup-grafana/configure-grafana/_index.md or similar) is updated. Operators have no way to learn about the new key, its semantics (0 = unlimited, what happens at the limit, interaction with the 30-day cleanup window), or its env-var override name (expected GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT). The default sentinel of 0 and the rejection semantics (new devices rejected, existing devices continue to update) also need to be called out.

title: updateDevice query does not handle new vs expired-device distinction
body: When count >= deviceLimit the code routes to updateDevice, whose WHERE clause requires updated_at BETWEEN device.UpdatedAt-30d AND device.UpdatedAt+1m. A row that exists but whose updated_at is older than 30 days (still within the 61-day cleanup window) will be reported as 'no rows affected' and surface ErrDeviceLimitReached, indistinguishable from a genuinely new device. The caller cannot tell whether to retry later (e.g. after cleanup) or give up. Either the WHERE should also match such rows so they get refreshed, or the error should distinguish 'limit reached' from 'device expired/not found'.

title: Cleanup logs informational messages at Error level and will flood logs with the new 1-minute ticker
body: Lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, and 579 in xorm_store.go use r.log.Error for purely informational messages about cleanup progress (e.g., 'Annotations to clean by time', 'cleaned annotations by time', 'Tags to clean', 'cleaned tags'). These are not errors and should be logged at Debug level. With the cleanup ticker now firing every minute (see cleanup.go:77), these messages will be emitted at Error level on every cleanup cycle, flooding logs and potentially triggering false alerts on log-based monitoring. Additionally, the 'err', err field at lines 534, 554, and 576 is always nil at that point (the error from fetchIDs was already checked and the function returned earlier if it was non-nil), which is misleading. The 'ids', ids field also logs every annotation ID at Error level, which for large cleanups produces very large log entries.

title: Cleanup ticker frequency increased 10x (10 min -> 1 min) without justification in the PR description
body: The cleanup ticker was changed from `time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 10)` to `time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 1)`, a 10x increase in cleanup frequency. This significantly increases database load (more frequent SELECT and DELETE queries against the annotation and annotation_tag tables on every Grafana node). The change is not mentioned in the PR description and does not appear necessary for the deadlock fix itself (which is achieved by splitting the subquery into separate SELECT and DELETE statements that don't share a transaction). No server lock is visible in cleanup.go to prevent concurrent cleanups across multiple Grafana instances, so this much higher frequency raises the risk of overlapping cleanups in clustered deployments. This is a notable behavioral change that should be called out in the release notes and ideally discussed separately from the deadlock fix.

title: Cleanup loop terminates early when DELETE affects 0 rows, potentially leaving matching annotations uncleaned
body: untilDoneOrCancelled terminates its loop when batchWork returns an affected count of 0. With the new split SELECT/DELETE approach, batchWork returns the affected count from deleteByIDs. If fetchIDs returns IDs but deleteByIDs affects 0 rows (e.g., because a concurrent cleanup process or another transaction deleted those same IDs between the SELECT and the DELETE), the cleanup loop exits without checking whether more matching annotations exist. The original code used a single atomic DELETE with a subquery, so 'affected == 0' reliably meant there were no more matching rows. The correct termination condition for the new split approach is len(ids) == 0 (no more IDs to fetch), not affected == 0. This regression can cause annotations to be missed in deployments where concurrent cleanups are possible. The fix is to either change the termination check to use len(ids), or have batchWork return int64(len(ids)) instead of the affected row count.

title: Cleanup logs use Error level and log nil error on success
body: Lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, 579 use r.log.Error(...) for routine cleanup progress messages (e.g. 'Annotations to clean by time', 'cleaned tags'). The function already returns early on a non-nil error, so when execution reaches these log statements the err value is always nil, yet it is still passed as the 'err' key. The result is that every successful cleanup cycle emits Error-level log records containing a nil error. Combined with the cleanup ticker being moved to 1 minute in cleanup.go, this means an Error-level log is emitted on every pass of the cleanup job, polluting error monitoring and breaking any alerting/log filters that assume Error level indicates a real failure. The level should be Debug or Info, and the 'err' key should only be logged when non-nil (or moved into the error branch). Existing call sites in the same package use r.log.Info for routine ops (line 410: 'delete') and cleanup.go uses Debug for normal results (line 129), so this is also inconsistent with surrounding code.

title: Cleanup ticker shortened from 10m to 1m without justification
body: The Run loop's ticker was changed from time.Minute * 10 to time.Minute * 1. This is a 10x increase in cleanup job frequency that is unrelated to the deadlock fix described in the PR (which is in xorm_store.go). The change is not mentioned in the PR description and is bundled with the deadlock fix. With a 9 minute per-job timeout (line 89) and now a 1 minute tick, a slow cleanup cycle (e.g. while there are many annotations to remove) will cause the next tick to fire while clean(ctx) is still executing, leading to overlapping clean() invocations on the same shared parent context. This risk is amplified by the new 'fetchIDs then deleteByIDs' pattern, which performs two DB roundtrips per batch instead of one. The ticker value should either be reverted to 10 minutes or justified/handled separately, and the loop should track whether a clean cycle is in progress to avoid concurrent runs.

title: SQL and parameters are passed as separate args to session.Exec
body:
In deleteByIDs, the call is:

    res, err := session.Exec(append([]any{sql}, args...)...)

The first element of the variadic args slice is the statement text and the remaining elements are the bind parameters. xorm's Session.Exec expects (sql string, args ...interface{}); passing the SQL string as a positional argument via the args slice is unusual and depends on undocumented behavior of the dialect's Exec wrapper. Several xorm code paths treat the first element as a parameter and prepend the SQL separately, which can lead to the SQL being interpreted as part of the parameter list (e.g. on PostgreSQL where the driver receives the SQL as a query string only when calling Exec(sql, args...) directly). This should be called as session.Exec(sql, args...) to match the rest of the file (e.g. line 415, 419, 426, 430) and avoid silently malforming the query on some drivers.

title: cleanupWHERE clause is built from annotationType without an AND before created filter
body:
The condition built for the MaxAge branch is:

    cond := fmt.Sprintf(`%s AND created < %v ORDER BY id DESC %s`, annotationType, cutoffDate, r.db.GetDialect().Limit(...))

The annotationType argument (e.g. 'alert_id > 0 AND dashboard_id > 0' for dashboard annotations, or 'alert_id = 0 AND dashboard_id = 0' for API annotations) is concatenated directly.
