If `readLength()` returns -1 (BER indefinite-length encoding, which `readLength()` explicitly supports), the `while (length > 0)` test is false on entry and the method returns an empty list while leaving the end-of-contents marker and the entire sequence body unread. Callers will then see a zero-length list and either index out of bounds or silently accept an empty signature.
2. `readNext()` can in principle return more bytes than the declared remaining length (malformed input); in that case `length` underflows, the loop exits, and the leftover bytes are silently swallowed instead of being rejected as malformed.
The reader should either reject indefinite-length as not supported for DER or read until the 0x00 0x00 end-of-contents octets, and should validate that the consumed bytes never exceed the declared length.

title: logger.debugf called with a plain string and no format arguments
body: `logger.debugf(builder.toString());` passes a String with no `%` placeholders and no varargs to `debugf(String, Object...)`. This is misleading because the signature suggests a printf-style format string. If any discovered CryptoProvider class name ever contained a `%` (unlikely but not enforced), it would be interpreted as a format specifier and could throw. Use `logger.debug(builder.toString())` (or `logger.tracef` if formatting is desired) instead.

title: Test uses a single P-256 key for ES256/ES384/ES512
body: The constructor calls `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair()`, which on the standard SunEC provider returns a P-256 (secp256r1) key. That same key is then used to exercise ES256, ES384 and ES512, each of which expects a different curve and a different raw signature length (64, 96, 132 bytes respectively). With a P-256 key the SHA384withECDSA/SHA512withECDSA signatures still have only 32+32 byte components, so `getSignatureLength()` returns 96/132 while the real signature is 64 bytes; the test only round-trips the bytes through DER<->concatenatedRS and so happens to pass even though no ES384/ES512-shaped signature is ever produced. The test does not verify the conversion for genuinely larger curves and does not assert that a signature produced by `signature.sign()` round-trips to the original signature value for the expected length. Generate (or load) a key of the appropriate curve per algorithm and assert the round-tripped bytes actually equal the original `sign()` output.

title: NPE when the all-clients resource does not exist
body: In `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, when the per-client resource is absent, the code calls `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)`. That method returns null in several situations (e.g. when the resource type is unknown, when schema support is not active, or simply when the corresponding "Clients" resource row has not been created yet in the DB). The very next line passes that potentially-null resource to `authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource)`, which will throw a NullPointerException. The method must null-check the result before using it (and should not silently return false when the all-clients resource is missing - that is a real production scenario for any realm that enabled ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 before this PR was deployed, because the new resource type is added to the schema but never instantiated in the DB).

title: No migration to create the new "Clients" resource type resource for existing realms
body: `init(...)` early-returns whenever `realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null`, so it only runs the first time admin permissions are enabled on a realm. This PR adds a new resource type (`Clients`) to `SCHEMA` and to `init`, but it provides no upgrade path for realms that already enabled V2 admin permissions prior to this change: their authorization database will only contain the "Users" resource type resource (and scopes registered at the time), and the new "Clients" resource type resource will never be created. After upgrade, `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, "Clients")` returns null, causing the NPE described above in `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission`. A migration step (or at least a defensive null guard in the consumer) is required before this PR can be safely released to existing V2 users.

title: canMapRoles / canMapCompositeRoles / canMapClientScopeRoles ignore the MANAGE_CLIENTS realm role
body: `canManage(ClientModel)`, `canConfigure(ClientModel)`, `canManageClientScopes()` and `canView()` all explicitly fall back to the realm-level `MANAGE_CLIENTS` (and/or `VIEW_CLIENTS`) admin role via `root.hasOneAdminRole(...)` before consulting the FGAP scopes. `canMapRoles`, `canMapCompositeRoles` and `canMapClientScopeRoles` skip that fallback entirely and only call `hasPermission(client, ...)`. A realm administrator who has been granted the classic `MANAGE_CLIENTS` realm role (and not the equivalent FGAP scope) will pass `canManage(client)` but fail `canMapRoles(client)`, so they cannot add client roles/composites - which is a behavior break versus V1 and an inconsistent permission model across the evaluator. The methods should check `MANAGE_CLIENTS` first, matching the pattern used elsewhere in this class.

title: canView() ignores the FGAP MANAGE scope
body: `canView()` is implemented as `canViewClientDefault() || hasPermission(VIEW)`. `canView(ClientScopeModel)` on the other hand returns true for either VIEW or MANAGE, and `canView(ClientModel)` returns true whenever `canConfigure(client)` (which ultimately honors FGAP MANAGE) returns true. The asymmetry means an admin that was granted only the `manage` scope for all clients (a perfectly normal FGAP grant) can configure a specific client and view it via `canView(ClientModel)` / `canView(ClientScopeModel)`, but `canView()` and `canList()` - which the listing endpoints rely on - return false, so the admin cannot browse the clients list. The scope check for `canView()` should also accept `MANAGE` (and `canManageClientScopes()` should likewise accept VIEW), mirroring the way the per-resource variants behave.

title: Dead code in ClientPermissionsV2
body: The class contains several pieces of unused code that should be removed before merge: the `private static final Logger logger` (line 51) is never referenced, the helper `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken)` (line 262) has no callers in this file or the codebase, and the imports that exist solely to support that helper (`ClientModelIdentity`, `DefaultEvaluationContext`, `EvaluationContext`, `AccessToken`, `Scope`, plus `TOKEN_EXCHANGE` and `Arrays`) are dead as a consequence. Either wire `getEvaluationContext` into `hasPermission` so policies can match on `kc.client.id`, or delete it together with its imports.

title: Lazy initialization of clientPermissions is not thread-safe
body: `clients()` does a non-synchronized check-then-set on the `clientPermissions` field. If two threads invoke `mgmt.clients()` concurrently, both can observe `clientPermissions == null` and each builds its own `ClientPermissionsV2`, leaving one instance to be silently discarded. The same pattern is already present for `userPermissions`, but adding a second unsynchronized lazy cache makes the problem more likely to be hit. Make the field `volatile` and/or guard the assignment (`synchronized`, `AtomicReference`, or eager init in the constructors).

title: Listener gated by V1 feature flag disables cleanup in V2
body: The new `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ))` wraps the entire event body, so when only the V2 feature (`ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2`) is enabled the `RoleRemovedEvent`, `ClientRemovedEvent` and `GroupRemovedEvent` handlers are skipped entirely. Previously the handlers ran unconditionally, and `MgmtPermissionsV2.roles()` still has a real `setPermissionsEnabled` implementation that is no longer invoked, so role/group permission state will be left orphaned when those entities are removed in a V2-only realm. The check should be `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ || ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2`, or the per-handler calls must selectively skip the V2-unsupported `ClientPermissions.setPermissionsEnabled`.

title: getClientsWithPermission returns the literal string "Clients" as a client id
body: `getClientsWithPermission` iterates every resource whose type is "Clients", which includes the schema's "all-clients" resource (created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init` with name="Clients" and type="Clients"). If the all-clients resource has the requested scope granted, `hasGrantedPermission` returns true and the string `"Clients"` is added to the returned set. The contract of the method is a set of client ids; returning `"Clients"` causes callers (e.g. code that filters `realm.clients().get(...)`) to either crash trying to look up a client with that id or silently behave as if no clients matched. The handler must skip the resource whose name equals `CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE` (and, when that resource is granted, return the set of all client ids in the realm, not the literal "Clients").

title: Potential NPE when all-clients resource does not exist
body: In `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, when the per-client resource is null the code calls `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)`. That method returns null when admin permissions are disabled, when the type is unknown, or when the resource was never created. The next line then calls `authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource)` with a null resource, which will NPE inside the policy store. The fallback path must null-check the result of `getResourceTypeResource` and return `false` when null.

title: getResourceName has no case for the Clients resource type
body: `getResourceName` special-cases the `USERS` resource type (translating the all-users marker to "All users" and otherwise looking up the user to return the username). For the new `CLIENTS` resource type the method falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`, so client-typed resources will be displayed as the client UUID (the stored name) instead of a friendly label, and the all-clients resource will appear as the literal string "Clients" rather than "All clients". A symmetric branch for `CLIENTS.getType()` should be added.

title: Unused method and dead imports
body: `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken)` is defined but never referenced from anywhere in the class. The accompanying imports (`ClientModelIdentity`, `DefaultEvaluationContext`, `EvaluationContext`, `AccessToken`) and the `TOKEN_EXCHANGE` static import are also dead. The unused `logger` field is declared on line 51 as well. This is dead code introduced together with the new class and should be removed.

title: testManageOnlyOneClient assumes at least 2 default client scopes
body: After granting `MANAGE`, the test does `ClientScopeRepresentation clientScopeRep = defaultClientScopes.get(1);` (and again on line 174). If the realm configuration registers fewer than two default client scopes for `myclient` (the realm-admin permissions config in this PR adds new scopes that are stored on the admin-permissions client, not on the application client), `get(1)` throws IndexOutOfBoundsException and the test fails for reasons unrelated to the authorization logic. The test should either assert `defaultClientScopes.size() >= 2` or iterate by content rather than by hard-coded index.

title: No test exercises canMapClientScopeRoles, canManageClientScopes or canView(ClientScopeModel)
body: ClientPermissionsV2 implements `canMapClientScopeRoles` (backed by `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE`), `canManageClientScopes` (backed by the `MANAGE` scope) and `canView(ClientScopeModel)` (backed by `VIEW`/`MANAGE`), but PermissionClientTest only covers `MANAGE`, `CONFIGURE`, `VIEW`, `MAP_ROLES` and `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE`. The `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` scope is registered in the schema but is not exercised by any test, leaving the new authorization logic uncovered. A test mirroring `testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient` should grant `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` and verify that client-scope role mappings can and cannot be performed.

title: NPE risk in hasPermission when 'Clients' aggregate resource is missing
body: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when resourceStore.findByName returns null, the code falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...).getResourceTypeResource can legitimately return null (it does so when supportsAuthorizationSchema is false, or when the resource for the type is missing). The very next line calls authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) with that potentially null resource, which throws NullPointerException. The fallback path must null-check resource before calling findByResource (or simply return false if no 'Clients' aggregate resource exists), otherwise a missing resource will crash permission evaluation in production.

title: Listener gated on V1 feature flag will skip V2 cleanup
body: registerListener now wraps all event handlers in `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ))`. ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is the V1 flag; V2 is gated on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 elsewhere (in evaluator()/management()). If only the V2 flag is enabled, the listener body never runs, so RoleRemovedEvent/ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent will no longer trigger setPermissionsEnabled(...) cleanup on the corresponding permission resources. The original code ran unconditionally and let management() route to V1 or V2. Either the check should be `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ || ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` (or just the V2 flag), or the V2 implementations must actually be wired up so these events still get processed.

title: ClientRemovedEvent handler will throw UnsupportedOperationException in V2
body: The ClientRemovedEvent branch calls `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)`. When the V2 profile feature is on, management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, whose clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled is implemented as `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. The same goes for the role/group branches (no V2 implementation shown). So if the listener ever runs in V2 mode, it will propagate an UnsupportedOperationException out of the KeycloakSession event manager, surfacing as a 500/error during client/role/group deletion. Either the V2 implementations must provide real setPermissionsEnabled behavior, or the listener must explicitly skip V2 (the inverse of the bug above).

title: requireView / requireViewClientScopes Javadoc claims a return value
body: The newly-added Javadoc on requireView (around line 95) and requireViewClientScopes (around line 100) both start with "Returns {@code true} if ..." but the methods themselves return void (they throw ForbiddenException on failure). The Javadoc is wrong/misleading; it should describe that the method throws ForbiddenException when the corresponding canXxx() check is false, matching the style already used for requireManage, requireList, etc.

title: getClientsWithPermission leaks the 'Clients' aggregate name into the result
body: resourceStore.findByType(server, "Clients", ...) returns every resource whose type is "Clients" — that includes both per-client resources (named by client.getId()) and the schema's aggregate 'all-clients' resource (named "Clients"). The lambda then does `granted.add(resource.getName())`. When the caller has an all-clients permission that matches the requested scope, the string "Clients" ends up in the returned Set, mixed in with actual client UUIDs. Callers using this set (e.g., to filter what a user can manage or to look up clients by ID) will see a phantom "Clients" entry. The aggregate resource should be skipped (or its name normalized out) so only concrete client IDs are returned.

title: Unused private method and dead imports
body: getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) is defined but never called from anywhere in the class (canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, and no other call site uses it). The static import `AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE` and the import `org.keycloak.authorization.model.Scope` are likewise unused. These should be removed, or the helper should be wired into the permission evaluation if it is intended to provide kc.client.id attributes for policies.

title: findByName uses raw client.getId() with no null/empty guard
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), `resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId())` is called without verifying that client.getId() is non-null and non-empty. If the ClientModel has not been persisted yet (transient client during creation) or has been removed between the caller fetching it and this check, client.getId() can be null/blank, and the lookup will silently match a resource with an empty/null name (the all-resource aggregate has the name "Clients", but the default-find semantics for blank keys are implementation-defined). Guarding the lookup with a null check on client.getId() would prevent surprising false positives/negatives.

title: Feature-disabled branch is only covered for the metadata subcommand
body: The new testFeatureNotEnabled covers only UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.NAME, but the identical gating block was added to UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() (quarkus/runtime/.../UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java line 46-50). There is no test that verifies the `check` subcommand also prints 'Unable to use this command. The preview feature `rolling-updates` is not enabled.' and exits with code FEATURE_DISABLED (4). If someone removes or alters the feature check in UpdateCompatibilityCheck, this test suite will not notice. Add a sibling @Launch test (e.g. testFeatureNotEnabledCheck) that invokes the check subcommand without ENABLE_FEATURE and asserts both the error message and the exit code.

title: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE silently changed from 4 to 3
body: Before this PR, RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was 4, so external CI/GitOps scripts invoking `kc.sh update-compatibility check` would observe exit code 4 when a recreate upgrade was required. This PR redefines it to 3 and reassigns 4 to the new FEATURE_DISABLED case. Any automation that checks `if exit_code == 4 then recreate` will silently misinterpret the new exit code 4 as "recreate required" when in reality it now means "rolling-updates feature is disabled". The change is reflected in update-compatibility.adoc, but the docs do not call out the re-numbering of the previously documented exit code 4; users running older guides will not realize the semantics of 4 have changed. This deserves an explicit migration note (e.g., "previously 4 meant recreate; in this release 3 means recreate and 4 means feature-disabled") and should be flagged in the release notes / changelog so existing scripts can be updated.

title: CAUTION contradicts the documented default behavior and the operator tests
body: The new CAUTION block states: 'While on preview stage, the feature `rolling-updates` must be enabled. Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail.' Immediately below, the NOTE block (line 461-466) explains the default behavior ('the update strategy defaults to mimicking Keycloak 26.1 or older behavior') which works without enabling the feature. The accompanying test in UpgradeTest.createInitialDeployment deliberately does NOT enable ROLLING_UPDATES when updateStrategy is null, and testImageChange(null) asserts that the default recreate-on-image-change flow still works without the feature. So the operator does NOT fail without the feature when the user sticks to default behavior; it only fails when the user attempts to set spec.update.strategy. The CAUTION is misleading and contradicts both the NOTE and the test. It should be reworded to make it clear the feature is only required to use spec.update.strategy, not for the operator to function at all.

title: Enabled feature is not asserted to be actually applied to the running deployment
body: createInitialDeployment sets kc.getSpec().getFeatureSpec().setEnabledFeatures(List.of(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey())), but the tests (testImageChange and testCacheMaxCount) only assert on upgrade status conditions - they never verify that the rolling-updates feature is present in the CR that the operator processed (e.g. by asserting on the persisted CR or by checking that the StatefulSet was/wasn't recreated according to the documented semantics). If the operator ever silently drops the featureSpec on submit, these tests would still pass. Adding at least one assertion like `assertThat(currentKc.getSpec().getFeatureSpec().getEnabledFeatures()).contains("rolling-updates")` would close this gap and would also detect regressions in the CR schema mapping introduced by the FeatureSpec/UnsupportedSpec refactor in this PR.

title: picocli.exit() will not compile
body: The new code calls `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)`, but the only picocli import in this file is `import picocli.CommandLine;`. `picocli` is a package, not a class, so there is no static `exit(int)` method to call and the expression does not resolve to anything. The code will fail to compile. The author most likely intended `System.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)`, or to delegate back to the picocli CommandLine via `getCommandLine().get().setExecutionResult(...)` / throwing a `CommandLine.ParameterException`.

title: picocli.exit() will not compile
body: Same defect as in UpdateCompatibilityCheck: `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` is invoked, but the imports contain only `import picocli.CommandLine;`. `picocli` is a package name; there is no class named `picocli` with a static `exit` method to resolve. The new feature-disabled branch will not compile. Use `System.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` or the appropriate picocli mechanism (e.g. setting the CommandLine execution result).

title: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE silently changed from 4 to 3
body: The constant `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` was changed from `4` to `3`, and `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` now occupies the old slot. Any automation (CI/CD scripts, GitOps pipelines) that was already treating exit code `4` as "recreate upgrade required" will silently misclassify that condition as "feature disabled" after this change. Even though the surrounding tool is preview, the documentation still presents the exit codes as a stable contract for automation and the change is undocumented in the diff. The new value `3` also collides conceptually with the standard "recreate / must shut down" message, which is fine semantically, yet the previous mapping was different. At minimum this should be called out as a breaking change to the preview contract, and ideally the doc in update-compatibility.adoc should explicitly note that exit code `4` previously meant recreate and now means feature disabled.

title: testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts message, not exit code 4
body: The new `testFeatureNotEnabled` test verifies the user-facing error string but does not assert the exit code. The whole point of the new `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED = 4` constant and the matching doc table entry for exit code 4 is to give automation a reliable signal. The test should also `assertEquals(4, cliResult.exitCode())` (or the framework equivalent) so that a future regression where the command prints the message but returns a different exit code is caught.

title: updatecompatibility macro hardcodes --features=rolling-updates
body: The `updatecompatibility` macro now unconditionally appends ` --features=rolling-updates` to every rendered example, including usage that is meant to demonstrate the "feature not enabled" case (the very behavior asserted by `testFeatureNotEnabled`). Any documentation page that uses this macro will show users an example that explicitly turns the feature on, which makes it impossible to demonstrate the off-by-default behavior in docs. The macro should at most render the flag conditionally, or pages needing the negative example should be able to opt out.

title: Breaking change in exit code: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE moved from 4 to 3
body: The constant RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was changed from 4 to 3, and a new FEATURE_DISABLED constant with value 4 was added. Previously the command actually returned exit code 4 to signal 'recreate upgrade needed', even though the public documentation in docs/guides/server/update-compatibility.adoc always described exit code 3 as that case. While this PR brings the code into agreement with the documented contract, it is an observable behaviour change for any consumer that has scripted against the previously-returned exit code (e.g. CI pipelines checking for exit code 4 to detect that a recreate upgrade is required). Because the change to an already-documented/previewed command is made silently in a 'feature flag' PR, reviewers should explicitly call out the swap (4 -> 3 for recreate, 4 now means feature disabled) and ensure this is highlighted in release notes so existing automation can be updated.

title: YAML example contains literal 'Recreate|<not set>' which is not valid YAML
body: In the new Keycloak CR example the value 'strategy: Recreate|<not set>' is shown. The pipe-separated placeholder is a documentation convention indicating 'either Recreate or leave the field unset', but the surrounding block is fenced as [source,yaml] and the value is therefore syntactically invalid YAML (the literal string 'Recreate|<not set>' would be parsed as a strategy value if copy-pasted). A user following the example literally would either get a parse error or end up with the value 'Recreate|<not set>' as the strategy. The PR also re-numbers the callout (now <2>) but does not fix the placeholder. Replace the inline placeholder with a valid example (e.g. 'strategy: Recreate') and describe the default state in prose or in the existing table.

title: Exit-code comment only documents picocli codes 1 and 2, not the new 3 and 4
body: The comment block introduced above the constants reads '// see picocli.CommandLine.ExitCode // 1 -> software error // 2 -> usage error' followed by RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE = 3 and FEATURE_DISABLED = 4. The comment implies that 3 and 4 are also picocli exit codes, which they are not - they are now Keycloak-specific values that occupy the same numeric space as picocli-defined codes. Future readers may be confused about the source of these numbers. Either move the explanatory comment to only document the picocli slots (1 and 2) and add a separate note clarifying that 3 and 4 are tool-defined codes, or rename the comment to 'Tool exit codes' and list all four with their meanings.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses resource internal id instead of name
body: In `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` the lambda iterates `resourceStore.findByType(server, "Groups", ...)` and uses `groupResource.getId()` (the resource's own internal primary key) both as the argument to `hasPermission(...)` and as the value added to the granted set. The resource is created by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` -> `resolveGroup`, which sets the resource's NAME to `group.getId()`; the resource's internal id is a separate generated value. Downstream, `hasPermission(String groupId, ...)` does `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, i.e. it tries to look up a resource by NAME using the resource's own internal id. That lookup always misses, so the code falls through to the `AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE` (all-groups) placeholder resource and runs the scope evaluation there. The consequence: (a) when the admin has any policy on the all-groups placeholder, the placeholder's internal id is added to the granted set and then placed in `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` so the user search filters against a non-existent group id, potentially excluding users even when per-user `canViewByGroup` would grant visibility; (b) for per-group-only setups the function returns an empty set, silently disabling the `UserModel.GROUPS` pre-filter optimization (the `canView` per-user check is the only thing that carries correctness). The fix is to use `groupResource.getName()` for both the `hasPermission` argument and the value added to the granted set, and additionally skip the all-groups placeholder resource (`AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE.equals(groupResource.getName())`) so it isn't treated as a real group id.

title: Double semicolon in field initializer
body: `private final GroupRepresentation topGroup = new GroupRepresentation();;` has two semicolons after the constructor call. Harmless but worth fixing while the file is being touched.

title: V2 canManage() grants group-management privileges to VIEW-only admins
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (no-argument) falls back to `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, so an admin who only has the `view` scope on the 'Groups' all-resource is treated as if they can manage groups. This affects every admin endpoint guarded by `auth.groups().requireManage()` without a specific group argument, in particular GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup (POST /admin/realms/{realm}/groups) and the manage-only branches of GroupResource (updateGroup, deleteGroup, addChild, role-mappings). A user policy that grants only `view` on the `Groups` resource type now lets the holder create, rename, delete and reassign top-level groups, violating least privilege. The interface javadoc on GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage() even codifies this behavior. V1's canManage() correctly limits itself to the `manage-users` admin role; the V2 override should match that and check only `MANAGE` (or equivalently delegate to a per-group `canManage(GroupModel)` over an all-groups resource).

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses resource.getId() instead of resource.getName()
body: Inside `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` the iteration is `resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, groupResource -> { hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...); granted.add(groupResource.getId()); })`. In the V2 schema, per-group resources are created with `name == groupId` (see AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup / getOrCreateResource), so `groupResource.getId()` is the resource's own auto-generated UUID, not the group's id. Two concrete consequences: (a) `hasPermission` calls `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupResource.getId())` which never matches the per-group resource, so every per-group permission check falls back to the all-groups evaluation and ignores scope restrictions on the specific group; (b) the returned set is populated with resource UUIDs that the user search interprets as group ids (see UsersResource.searchForUser where the set is set as `UserModel.GROUPS`), so the user filter ends up matching no real groups and the entire view-by-group filter is broken. Both `getId()` calls should be `getName()` to mirror the V1 implementation that used `resource.getName().substring(RESOURCE_NAME_PREFIX.length())`.

title: NPE if AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource() returns null
body: In `hasPermission(String groupId, ...)`, when no per-group resource is found, the code does `resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` followed immediately by `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)`. `getResourceTypeResource()` can legitimately return null (it returns null whenever `supportsAuthorizationSchema` is false, when the resourceType argument is null, when the schema type is unknown, or when the 'Groups' resource has not yet been persisted in the resource store). Passing that null into `findByResource(server, null)` will NPE, crashing the admin REST call. Guard the lookup with a null check, mirroring the equivalent code in UserPermissionsV2 which has the same defect.

title: NPE if AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource() returns null
body: `hasPermission(UserModel user, ...)` performs the same fallback as GroupPermissionsV2: `resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE); if (policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()) return false;`. When `getResourceTypeResource` returns null (feature disabled, schema not yet initialized, or 'Users' resource missing), `policyStore.findByResource(server, null)` throws a NullPointerException. This affects every V2 canView/canManage/canImpersonate/canMapRoles/canManageGroupMembership call path. Add a null guard before `findByResource`.

title: Removed AdminRoles.ADMIN fallback may deny master-realm admins under FGAP V2
body: The pre-existing V2 overrides for canView(UserModel), canManage(UserModel), canMapRoles and canManageGroupMembership used to short-circuit on `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.ADMIN, AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS, ...)`. The new versions drop the `AdminRoles.ADMIN` role entirely. With AdminPermissionsEnabled + ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 on a child realm, a master-realm administrator holding only the `admin` role (no `manage-users`/`view-users` client role) will no longer satisfy the role check, and only the Authz policy engine will be consulted. Unless the realm admin has explicitly created a UserPolicy mapping the admin user to the 'Users' resource, every user-management call will fail with 403. This is a behavioral regression relative to V1 and the previous V2 implementation; either keep the ADMIN check or document/guarantee that ADMIN implies these scopes via policy.

title: Missing test that VIEW on Groups does not imply manage privileges
body: GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest grants a `view` scope on the `Groups` resource type in `testViewGroups` but only exercises the list endpoint. There is no test that asserts a VIEW-only admin cannot create, update, delete groups or add child groups. Given the canManage() privilege escalation introduced in GroupPermissionsV2 (see security finding), a regression test should be added that grants only VIEW scope and expects 403 on POST /groups, PUT /groups/{id}, DELETE /groups/{id}, and POST /groups/{id}/children. Without it the escalation can re-recur unnoticed.

title: canManage() javadoc misrepresents required scopes
body: The javadoc on `GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage()` says "Or if it has a permission to `AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW` or `AdminPermissionsSchema#MANAGE` groups". That text legitimizes the privilege-escalation behavior implemented in GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (a viewer should not be a manager). The doc should match V1 semantics: only `AdminPermissionsSchema#MANAGE` (or the `manage-users` admin role) grants manage; `view` should not.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses resource internal ID instead of group ID
body: In `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission`, the lambda iterates resources of type "Groups" and calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), …)`, then `granted.add(groupResource.getId())`. For V2 per-group resources created by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource`, the resource `name` is set to `group.getId()` (via `resolveGroup`), but the resource `id` is the auto-generated primary-key UUID assigned by `ResourceStore.create`. Consequently `findByName(server, groupResource.getId())` never matches the per-group resource, and `hasPermission` silently falls back to the "all-Groups" resource; if the admin has all-Groups scope granted they appear to have view-members/manage-members on every individual group, and the "group IDs" returned in the set are bogus internal UUIDs that the user-provider cannot match. The same logic is used by `BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser`, `UsersResource.searchForUser` (sets `UserModel.GROUPS`), and `UsersResource.getUsersCount`, so callers will see either empty result sets (because the ID does not match any real group) or count/list inconsistency (`getUsersCount` will return 0 while the search returns users via the post-filter fallback). The fix is to use `groupResource.getName()` (which equals `group.getId()` for per-group resources) and pass it into both `hasPermission` and the resulting `granted` set; additionally the all-Groups sentinel resource (where `getName()` equals the type string `Groups`) must be skipped, since it is not a real group ID. Mirroring the V1 implementation, which correctly uses `resource.getName().substring(RESOURCE_NAME_PREFIX.length())`, would resolve this.

title: Possible NPE in hasPermission when type resource is null
body: `hasPermission` assigns `resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE);` and immediately calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty();` without a null check. `getResourceTypeResource` can legitimately return null (when FGAP V2 is enabled but the "Groups" schema resource has not yet been created in the authz resource store, or when `supportsAuthorizationSchema` is false, etc.). The JPA `PolicyStore.findByResource` implementation dereferences `resource.getId()`, so calling it with a null `Resource` argument will throw a NullPointerException at runtime. The same pattern exists in `UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission` at the `findByResource(server, resource)` call. Add an explicit null guard before invoking `findByResource` (e.g., `if (resource == null || policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()) return false;`).

title: Possible NPE in hasPermission when type resource is null
body: Same defect as in `GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission`: after falling back to the all-Users schema resource via `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)`, the code calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()` without checking whether `getResourceTypeResource` returned null. The JPA `PolicyStore.findByResource` dereferences `resource.getId()` and will throw a NullPointerException for a null resource. Guard the call with a null check (e.g., `if (resource == null || policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()) return false;`).

title: Javadoc on canManageMembership contradicts V2 semantics
body: The interface Javadoc for `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` says it returns true if the caller has `MANAGE_USERS` "Or if it has a permission to `MANAGE` the group or `MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP` of the group." However `GroupPermissionsV2.canManageMembership` actually also delegates to `hasPermission(..., MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP)`, which corresponds to the documented behaviour (MANAGE or MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP). The V1 implementation, by contrast, accepts MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP only (via `hasPermission(group, MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP_SCOPE)`) and treats a `canManage(group)` match (which itself requires MANAGE on the specific group, not just MANAGE on all-groups) as a shortcut. The single Javadoc comment cannot describe both contracts accurately. Either split the behaviour or document that the V2 implementation effectively treats `MANAGE` of the group (anywhere) as sufficient to manage membership of that group, which is a broader grant than V1.

title: Javadoc on canViewMembers contradicts V2 semantics
body: The Javadoc for `canViewMembers(GroupModel)` describes the V1 contract (which was just `VIEW_MEMBERS`). Both the V1 (post-PR) and V2 implementations additionally accept `MANAGE_MEMBERS`. Either the comment should be updated to mention `MANAGE_MEMBERS` as well, or the implementations should only accept `VIEW_MEMBERS`. Note that accepting `MANAGE_MEMBERS` is a behaviour change relative to what the V1 implementation did before this PR (it used to return `hasPermission(group, VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE)` only), and the Javadoc does not warn administrators that a `manage-members` grant now implicitly grants view-members.

title: Build breaks if English source file is missing
body: In `verifySafeHtml()`, when no English file is found at the computed path (e.g. for any translation file in `resources-community/...` whose corresponding `resources/.../messages_en.properties` does not exist), the code wraps the `FileNotFoundException` from `new FileInputStream(englishFile)` into a `RuntimeException`, which propagates out of `verify()` and aborts the Maven build. The English lookup should be best-effort: either skip the HTML/anchor checks, fall back to treating the translation as the source of truth, or at minimum record a non-fatal message in the returned list. Currently any new language that lacks a committed English counterpart (or any test fixture that only ships `_xx.properties`) will crash the verifier.

title: Typo in method name `santizeAnchors`
body: The method is named `santizeAnchors` (missing the 'i' in 'sanitize'). The misspelling is also propagated to the only call site, so it does not affect behavior. It should be renamed to `sanitizeAnchors` so it reads correctly, matches the surrounding `verifySafeHtml()` naming style, and can be found by IDEs/refactoring tools.

title: HTML_TAGS pattern is case-sensitive, mismatching the sanitizer
body:
The pattern `HTML_TAGS = Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>")` only matches lowercase HTML tag names. The OWASP sanitizer used right after is case-insensitive (HTML tags are not case sensitive in the spec). Consequence: `containsHtml(englishValue)` returns `false` for English values containing only uppercase tags (e.g. ``/``), so `POLICY_NO_HTML` is selected even though the English string actually has HTML. For an English-only check this does not matter (the sanitizer still strips the tags), but the choice of policy governs whether `
`, `

`, ``, `` are allowed in the translation. If English ever ships uppercase variants, the corresponding translations would be incorrectly forced through the no-HTML policy. The regex should be case-insensitive (e.g. `]*>` with `Pattern.CASE_INSENSITIVE`).

title: Policy factories and regex are non-static instance fields
body: `POLICY_SOME_HTML`, `POLICY_NO_HTML`, and `HTML_TAGS` are instance fields even though they do not depend on any instance state and are constructed purely from constants. A new `PolicyFactory` and `Pattern` is allocated for every `VerifyMessageProperties` instance (i.e. once per message file). They should be `private static final` so they are compiled once and shared across all verifications, which is both faster and clearer about their immutability.

title: santizeAnchors couples mutable value with matcher bound to original
body: `santizeAnchors` creates `matcher = ANCHOR_PATTERN.matcher(value)` once before the loop, then inside the loop assigns `value = value.replaceFirst(...)`. The `matcher` keeps operating on the *original* string, but `replaceFirst` is invoked on the *mutated* `value`. In the common case the anchor tags appear in the same order in both strings and the algorithm accidentally works, but this is fragile: e.g. if the translation contains the same anchor tag multiple times or if `replaceFirst` removes a substring that affects positions of subsequent matches, `matcher.find()` will read positions in the original while `value` has shifted, leading to mismatches between `matcher.group()` and the substring actually being replaced. The matcher should be rebuilt from `value` after each replacement, or the anchors should be collected first and then stripped from the value.

title: No test for missing English source file
body: The new test suite only covers cases where an English file is present (`changedAnchor_en.properties`, `noHtml_en.properties`, `illegalHtmlTag_en.properties`, `duplicateKeys_en.properties`). The branch where `new FileInputStream(englishFile)` throws FileNotFoundException (the `catch (IOException e) { throw new RuntimeException(...) }` block at line 79) has no coverage. Add a fixture that ships only a translation without an English counterpart and assert either that `verify()` returns a graceful message in the list, or (if RuntimeException is intentional) document and assert that behavior, so future refactors do not silently change it.

title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 was replaced with Italian text
body: The Lithuanian translation for `loginTotpStep1` was changed from a proper Lithuanian sentence with embedded `<a>` tags to the Italian string `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`. The English source is `Install one of the following applications on your mobile:`. Users with Lithuanian locale now see an Italian sentence in the login UI instead of Lithuanian. This appears to be a copy/paste error from the Czech/Slovak/Swedish translations done in this PR. The original Lithuanian wording or a proper new Lithuanian translation should be used.

title: Lithuanian account totpStep1 was replaced with Italian text
body: Same issue as in the login theme: the Lithuanian `totpStep1` was changed to the Italian `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`. Lithuanian users of the account theme will see Italian text instead of Lithuanian. Replace with a proper Lithuanian translation (the previous Lithuanian text was removed because it contained `<a>` tags, but it should have been rewritten in Lithuanian, not in Italian).

title: Test fixture ends without a trailing newline
body: Several new test fixtures under `misc/theme-verifier/src/test/resources/` (`changedAnchor_de.properties`, `changedAnchor_en.properties`, `illegalHtmlTag_en.properties`, `noHtml_de.properties`, `noHtml_en.properties`) are missing the final newline. Some tooling (and `PropertyResourceBundle` / `Files.readString` consumers in stricter environments) behave inconsistently for files not terminated by a newline. Add a trailing newline to keep with POSIX text-file conventions.

title: Regex character class too broad due to '-' being treated as range operator
body: The regex `replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")` contains the character class `[a-zA-Z-_]`. In Java regex, the dash '-' that is not at the start or end of the class and not escaped is interpreted as a range operator. With the previous 'A-Z' range ending at 'Z' (0x5A), the '-_' is parsed as a range from 'Z' (0x5A) to '_' (0x5F), which silently adds '[', '\', ']', '^', and '_' to the matched character set. The author clearly intended `[a-zA-Z_]` (or `[a-zA-Z_-]` with '-' placed last so it is a literal). For typical locale codes (letters + underscore) this happens to work, but the regex is incorrect and could match unintended characters in path components containing '[', '\', etc. Fix by writing `[a-zA-Z_-]` (dash at the end of the class, making it literal) or `[a-zA-Z_]`.

title: Stale Matcher iterates over the original string while value is mutated
body: In `santizeAnchors`, `Matcher matcher = ANCHOR_PATTERN.matcher(value)` is created once against the original `value`, but `value` is reassigned inside the loop via `value = value.replaceFirst(...)`. Java's Matcher retains a reference to the original CharSequence and continues iterating from where it left off in that original buffer even after `value` now points to a newly-allocated string. Consequence: the matcher can 'find' anchors that have already been removed from the current `value`, and conversely can miss anchors that only exist in the modified string. With repeated anchors (e.g. translation `a b` vs English `x`), iteration will process the second `` against an exhausted EnglishMatcher and report "Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string", producing a false-positive. The fix is to either (a) re-create `matcher = ANCHOR_PATTERN.matcher(value)` after each `replaceFirst`, or (b) iterate via `Matcher.results()` and build a new string, or (c) tokenize the string with the matcher and rebuild.

title: replaceFirst only removes the first occurrence of a repeated anchor
body: `value.replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(englishMatcher.group()), "")` only replaces the FIRST match in `value`, not all matches. If a translation legitimately reuses the same anchor tag more than once and the English source only has one occurrence, only the first occurrence is stripped; the remaining occurrences are then passed to the OWASP sanitizer, which (with `POLICY_SOME_HTML` not allowing `<a>`) will escape them and produce a spurious "Illegal HTML" error. Combined with the stale-Matcher issue above, the second `<a href="X">` is also reported as "Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string". Use `replaceAll`, or iterate via the matcher and reconstruct the string, to handle repeated anchors correctly.

title: Comment mischaracterises '<1>' as a "numeric tag"
body: The comment states the sanitizer escapes 'numeric tags like `<1>`'. There is no concept of a numeric tag in HTML or in the OWASP sanitizer; the sanitizer simply treats the literal text `<1>` as an invalid HTML tag (because tag names must start with a letter per the policy) and escapes the '<' and '>' characters. `<1>` here is an i18next / React-Intl style indexed placeholder, not a numeric tag. The wording will mislead future maintainers about what the sanitizer is doing and why `<1>` survives the round-trip via `unescapeHtml4`.

title: Breaking change to i18next escape syntax in JS-side resource bundle
body: The value of `error-invalid-multivalued-size` was changed from `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. The double-brace form `{{0}}` / `{{1}}` / `{{2}}` is i18next's escape syntax for producing literal `{0}`/`{1}`/`{2}` text, which is what account-ui uses. After this change, i18next will interpret `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}` and the `{2,choice,...}` clause as placeholders / interpolation tokens. i18next does not implement Java MessageFormat choice format, and `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` is not valid i18next interpolation syntax, so the message will either fail to interpolate or be displayed verbatim with broken `{...}` text instead of the localized error. The previous value (`value(s)`) was a deliberate, working i18next-compatible rendering of the message; this PR regresses that. The new format belongs only on the Java side (e.g. `themes/src/main/resources/theme/base/login/messages/messages_en.properties`), where it does belong.

title: Same i18next breaking change in admin-ui resource bundle
body: Same regression as in the account-ui bundle: `error-invalid-multivalued-size` changed from `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` to Java MessageFormat syntax (`{0}`, `{1}`, `{2,choice,...}`). The admin-ui is also a React/i18next app, so the change replaces working placeholder-escaping with placeholders that i18next will try to interpolate, and embeds a Java MessageFormat choice clause (`{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}`) that i18next does not understand. Result at runtime: malformed interpolation and/or broken/untranslated text shown to the admin user.

title: No positive test that valid HTML in a translation is accepted
body: The four new tests only assert that illegal HTML is detected (`verifyIllegalHtmlTagDetected`, `verifyNoHtmlAllowed`, `verifyNoChangedAnchors`) and that duplicates are detected. There is no positive test that exercises the happy path of `verifySafeHtml`: e.g. an English value containing `bar` and a translation containing `bar` (or `bar`) that should NOT be reported. Without it, a regression in the sanitizer flow (e.g. always escaping ``) would not be caught by the test suite. Add a test resource pair (`allowedHtml_en.properties` + `allowedHtml_de.properties`) with matching allowed tags and assert that the message list does not contain "Illegal HTML".

title: No test for the `{2,choice,...}` normalization of `error-invalid-multivalued-size`
body: `normalizeValue` strips `{N,choice,...}` clauses for `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit.*` and `error-invalid-multivalued-size` specifically. This special case is central to the PR because that key was just rewritten across every bundle to use this Java MessageFormat choice syntax. There is no test fixture nor assertion that (a) a translation whose choice clause differs from the English (e.g. different `1#value|1<values` text) is still accepted, and (b) a translation with literal `<` outside a choice clause is rejected. The whole point of this PR is to make `error-invalid-multivalued-size` valid, but the only protection against regressing it is the production code itself, with no regression test in `VerifyMessagePropertiesTest`.

title: File is read and parsed twice per verification
body: `verify()` reads the file with `Files.readString(file.toPath())` for duplicate-key detection, and then `verifySafeHtml()` opens another `FileInputStream` and parses the same file as `PropertyResourceBundle`. The two reads produce no consistency guarantee (a file could change between reads) and double the I/O. Either parse once into a `PropertyResourceBundle` and reuse it for both checks, or read the bytes once and wrap them in two parsers. Not a correctness bug, but the verifier runs over hundreds of message bundles during a theme build, so the duplication is non-trivial.

title: Trailing newline stripped from `error-invalid-multivalued-size`
body: The unified diff shows the file ends with `\ No newline at end of file` after this change (the `-` line also had `\ No newline at end of file`). Many editors, linters, and POSIX text tools require files to end with a newline, and several Keycloak bundles historically did so. The fact that the previous version ended without a newline was already a minor smell, but the change also touches a line at the end of the file without restoring the newline. This will show up as a noisy diff in future PRs and may violate any project policy on POSIX file endings.

title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
body: The line `totpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` is Italian, not Lithuanian. The original Lithuanian text `Įdiekite FreeOTP arba Google Authenticator savo įrenginyje...` was removed because the sanitizer disallows `` in `totpStep1` (the English source for this key has no HTML). The replacement text should be a proper Lithuanian translation such as `Įdiekite vieną iš šių programų savo mobiliajame telefone:` instead of Italian. All Lithuanian users of the account theme will see an Italian sentence.

title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
body: The line `loginTotpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` is Italian, not Lithuanian. The original Lithuanian text with `<a>` tags was removed (correctly, because the English `loginTotpStep1` has no HTML), but the replacement is in Italian rather than Lithuanian. All Lithuanian users of the login theme will see an Italian instruction. The corrected text should be a proper Lithuanian translation (compare with the Slovak sibling file `messages_sk.properties`, which uses `Nainštalujte si do mobilu jednu z nasledujúcich aplikácií:` - actual Slovak).

title: Missing English file causes RuntimeException that aborts verification
body: In `verifySafeHtml()`, when the English counterpart file does not exist (e.g. a new locale added without an `_en.properties` base, or a typo in the locale suffix that prevents the regex from matching), the line `throw new RuntimeException("unable to read file " + englishFile, e)` is thrown. This is wrapped by no try/catch in `verify()`, so it propagates out of the verifier and aborts the whole Maven plugin run for any file that lacks an English counterpart, instead of gracefully skipping the HTML check (or emitting a non-fatal warning). At minimum a `MissingResourceException`/missing file should be turned into a skipped-or-warned result, not a fatal `RuntimeException`.

title: Locale regex character class does not include digits
body: The English-file lookup uses `.replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")`. The character class `[a-zA-Z-_]` excludes digits, so any locale code containing digits (e.g. `pt_BR_abc123` style variants, or future locale extensions) would not be matched and the English path would be computed incorrectly (likely left as the original locale suffix), causing the RuntimeException described above. The class should be `[a-zA-Z0-9-_]` to be robust against any locale suffix.

title: `<!-- -->` strip assumes a specific sanitizer output format
body: `sanitized = sanitized.replace("<!-- -->", "")` assumes the OWASP sanitizer inserts exactly the literal `<!-- -->` to escape stray braces (e.g. `{<!-- -->0}`). However, depending on the sanitizer version and the surrounding context, the inserted comment may not be exactly that literal (it can contain attributes or differ in whitespace, and the OWASP sanitizer in some versions emits nothing or emits different placeholders). Removing only that exact string and then comparing with `Objects.equals(sanitized, value)` makes the equality check fragile: legitimate curly-brace substitutions may be left as raw HTML-looking text in the comparison, and conversely the strip may be a no-op when it should not be. This should at least be guarded by checking the actual OWASP version's behavior, or the comment should be removed from the code path if no longer produced. Additionally the unescape step `org.apache.commons.text.StringEscapeUtils.unescapeHtml4` (deprecated in commons-text 1.x in favor of `escapeHtml4`/`unescapeHtml4`) is being applied even when the sanitizer did not produce HTML entities for this value, which can mask real diffs.

title: No test for missing English counterpart file
body: The test class only adds fixtures that always have a paired `*_en.properties` (illegalHtmlTag, noHtml, changedAnchor). There is no test that covers the realistic case where a translated file has no English counterpart (e.g. adding a new locale without `messages_en.properties`). Without such a test the `throw new RuntimeException` branch is uncovered and will surface for the first time as a build-breaking failure in production usage.

title: `POLICY_SOME_HTML` allows both `<b>` and `<strong>` but the comment/premise implies only one
body:
The policy allows `br`, `p`, `strong`, and `b`. OWASP's HtmlPolicyBuilder keeps the element name as written, so a translation using `...` will be compared against `...` (good), but the design is fragile: any future reordering or upstream policy default change (e.g. automatically rewriting `` to ``) will make every translated file containing `` report `Illegal HTML` even though it is on the allow-list. There is no test asserting that `` survives the sanitizer unchanged; the only HTML-related test fixtures are `illegalHtmlTag_en.properties` (`
`) and `noHtml_de.properties` (`` against a no-HTML English source).

title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic — event assertions no longer validate the grant type
body: The matcher `isAccessTokenId(String expectedGrantShortcut)` does: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false; return isUUID().matches(items[1]);`. The boolean is inverted: it returns FALSE when the grant shortcut matches, and returns TRUE when it does not (as long as the suffix is a UUID). Consequence: the four event assertions that now pass `expectedGrantShortcut` (AuthorizationCode "ac", Device "dg", RefreshToken "rt", Ciba "ci") will silently accept any non-matching grant as well, so tests like `expectCodeToToken`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh`, and `expectAuthReqIdToToken` never actually verify the grant-type portion of the encoded `Details.TOKEN_ID`. The PR author appears to have intended a positive match (`if (!... .equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`).

title: Wrong substring offset when extracting grant-type shortcut from the prefix
body: The encoded prefix is `sessionType(2) + tokenType(2) + grantType(2)`, so the grant-type shortcut is at positions 4–5 (substring(4, 6)). The matcher uses `items[0].substring(3, 5)` which instead extracts the last character of the token type plus the first character of the grant type (e.g. for "onrtac" it returns "ta", not "ac"). Combined with the inverted logic above, the matcher effectively never reads the grant shortcut. Fix is `items[0].substring(4, 6)`.

title: Copy-paste error in null check — rawTokenId is never validated
body: Line 73 is `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`. It re-checks `grantType` and shows a misleading message; the actual `rawTokenId` parameter is NOT null-checked, so a null `rawTokenId` flows through to `getRawTokenId()` and into `encodeTokenId`, producing a token ID ending with just `':'`. Replace with `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`.

title: postInit duplicate-detection only triggers on bijective collisions
body: The validation `if (grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size())` only fires when the number of unique shortcuts differs from the number of unique grant IDs, i.e. when a collision exists in BOTH directions (or in one direction such that sizes differ). A duplicate where two factories share the same `getId()` but have distinct shortcuts, or share the same shortcut but have distinct IDs, produces the same map sizes and is silently swallowed (the second `put` overwrites the first). Because this factory is created at boot in `postInit`, such misconfigurations silently produce token IDs that cannot be round-tripped. The fix is to verify cardinalities or, better, fail fast on the first detected duplicate with an informative error.

title: Javadoc claims shortcuts are "usually like 3-letters" but all implementations are 2-letter
body: The new contract documents the shortcut as "usually like 3-letters", yet every actual implementation ships 2-character shortcuts ("ac", "cc", "pg", "pc", "rt", "ci", "dg", "ro", "te") and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId` requires the 2-char layout. Update the javadoc to "2-character shortcut" so new grant authors do not introduce incompatible shortcuts.

title: Non-default SPI method — implementations are forced to provide getShortcut() with no fallback
body: `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` is added as a non-`default` method of the public factory interface. There is no default implementation and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId` throws `IllegalStateException` if the grant's shortcut is unknown. Any third-party `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` (Keycloak extensions or downstream products) that pre-dates this SPI will now throw at token-issuance time for that grant. This is an unavoidable contract break of an SPI used by external implementations; it should at minimum be a `default` returning a deterministic unique derivation (e.g. first two chars of the grant id, padded/truncated) and a doc note pointing at this breaking change.

title: Copy-paste error in Objects.requireNonNull null check
body: The fourth Objects.requireNonNull call passes `grantType` (not `rawTokenId`) but uses the message 'Null rawTokenId not allowed'. As a result: (1) a null `rawTokenId` is silently accepted and will later cause an NPE inside the encoder, and (2) a null `grantType` is reported with a misleading error message. The check should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`.

title: Matcher isAccessTokenId has inverted logic
body: In `isAccessTokenId`, the line `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns false (i.e. test FAILS) when the grant shortcut matches the expected one, and proceeds (i.e. test PASSES based only on the UUID check) when it does NOT match. The condition is backwards: it should be `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. Used in expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectAuthReqIdToToken, so any test asserting on the access-token id will give the opposite of the expected result.

title: Matcher isAccessTokenId slices wrong characters for the grant shortcut
body: The encoded prefix has layout [session 0-1][token 2-3][grant 4-5], so the grant shortcut is at indices 4-5. The matcher uses `items[0].substring(3, 5)`, which returns the last character of the token type and the first character of the grant type, not the grant type itself. It should be `substring(4, 6)`. Combined with the inverted logic, the matcher never actually verifies the grant type and accepts any 6-char prefix as long as the UUID part is valid.

title: TokenContextEncoderSpi marked internal, contradicts stated extensibility goal
body: `isInternal()` returns `true`, which in Keycloak restricts the SPI to a single implementation (the default). The PR description explicitly motivates the SPI by saying 'provider adds ability for someone to introduce his own provider'. To match that intent, `isInternal()` must return `false`, otherwise third parties cannot supply an alternative encoder.

title: Public copy constructor of OAuth2GrantType.Context removed without notice
body: The previous public `Context(Context context)` copy constructor is deleted by this PR. The constructor was on a public nested class of a public SPI, so any downstream code that created derived or copied Contexts will fail to compile. The PR description does not call out this removal, and there is no replacement, so this is an undocumented SPI breaking change.

title: Constant name GRANT_TYPE is misleading
body: `public static final String GRANT_TYPE = OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE;` resolves to the literal string `"grant_type"`, which is a key name used as a `ClientSessionContext` attribute key, not a grant-type value. The name suggests a grant type such as `authorization_code`. Either the constant should be renamed to make clear it is a session-context attribute key (e.g. `CLIENT_SESSION_CTX_GRANT_TYPE`) or the Javadoc should explain it is the OAuth2 parameter/attribute name, not a grant type value, to avoid misuse such as `ctx.getAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, OAuth2Constants.AUTHORIZATION_CODE)` style calls.

title: getTokenContextFromTokenId does not handle null encodedTokenId
body: `getTokenContextFromTokenId(String encodedTokenId)` immediately calls `encodedTokenId.indexOf(':')` with no null check. If a caller passes null (for example from `token.getId()` returning null), this throws an NPE instead of returning the UNKNOWN/UNKNOWN/UNKNOWN/encodedTokenId context the method otherwise provides for unencoded ids. It should guard against null and treat it the same as an old (unprefixed) id.

title: getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext NPEs on null userSession
body: `clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getUserSession()` is dereferenced for both `getPersistenceState()` and `isOffline()` without a null check. In some flows (e.g. when a client session is not yet bound to a user session, or in OID4VCI issuance paths that build a token without a persisted user session) this can be null, producing an NPE in the encoder. The provider should treat a null userSession as UNKNOWN rather than failing token issuance.

title: Dynamic grant-type insertion is racy and can corrupt the shortcut maps
body: Both `getShortcutByGrantType` and `getGrantTypeByShortcut` do a non-atomic check-then-put into the `ConcurrentHashMap`s. Two threads can simultaneously take the `null` branch and both write. More importantly, nothing prevents a new grant factory from registering with a shortcut that collides with an existing one after `postInit`, which silently overwrites the existing entry in `grantsByShortcuts` and corrupts lookups in both directions; the startup-only size check in `postInit` does not protect against this hot path.

title: Javadoc says 3-letter shortcut but implementation uses 2 letters
body: The new `getShortcut()` Javadoc reads 'usually like 3-letters shortcut of specific grants', but every built-in factory introduced by this PR (AuthorizationCode, ClientCredentials, Permission, PreAuthorizedCode, RefreshToken, ResourceOwnerPassword, TokenExchange, Ciba, Device) defines a 2-character shortcut. Either the Javadoc should be corrected to say '2-character shortcut' or the contract should permit variable length; otherwise implementers are likely to follow the comment and supply the wrong length.

title: testIncorrectGrantType catches RuntimeException instead of the specific type
body: The test catches bare `RuntimeException` and ignores the variable, so it would pass on any unexpected throw (e.g. NPE, IllegalStateException, ClassCastException) and would not catch a regression where the method silently returns instead of throwing. It should catch `IllegalArgumentException` (the type the implementation actually throws) and ideally assert the message, so the test specifically validates the documented behavior.

title: requireNonNull checks the wrong argument (rawTokenId is not validated)
body: The constructor does `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` instead of `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`. Since `grantType` was already validated on the preceding line, this duplicate call is a no-op and does NOT enforce the intended non-null constraint on `rawTokenId`. The instance will then be created with a null rawTokenId and the field assigned. Any subsequent use of `getRawTokenId()` will return null and break token ID encoding/decoding (e.g. a token could be encoded with an embedded null) or surface as a cryptic NPE later.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher has both an off-by-one and an inverted condition
body:
Two bugs in the new matcher body:
```
if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;
```
1. Off-by-one: the grant type is the last 2 characters of the 6-char prefix, i.e. indices 4 and 5. The call must be `items[0].substring(4, 6)`. The current call returns a mix of the second char of token type and the first char of grant type, not the grant type alone.
2. Inverted condition: the matcher is supposed to SUCCESS only when the grant type matches the expected shortcut, but the code returns false (no match) when the substring equals the expected shortcut. A correct version would be: `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.
As written, the matcher effectively accepts any well-formed encoded token ID regardless of which grant produced it, so integration tests that rely on it (expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectAuthReqIdToToken) will not be able to detect regressions in grant type encoding.

title: Public copy constructor on Context was removed without replacement
body: The diff deletes the `public Context(Context context)` copy constructor that was part of the public static nested class `OAuth2GrantType.Context`. Any external code (custom grant type providers) that currently uses this constructor will fail to compile against this SPI. The PR description does not mention this removal. If the constructor was genuinely unused, leave it intact or annotate it `@Deprecated` so existing implementations still compile.

title: New required method getShortcut() breaks external OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
body: `String getShortcut()` is added to the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` SPI without a default and without `@Deprecated` overloads. Any external implementation of this factory interface (custom grant providers) compiled against a previous Keycloak version will throw `NoSuchMethodError`/`AbstractMethodError` at startup because the bytecode references the missing interface method. Even when re-compiled, the change is not source-compatible unless each implementer explicitly returns a constant. Consider providing a default that returns a value derived from `getId()` (e.g. first two unique letters) so that existing implementations keep working, or document the upgrade requirement prominently.

title: Access token `jti` now encodes grant type, session type and lightweight flag visible to clients
body: `initToken` now sets `token.id(encoder.encodeTokenId(tokenCtx))`, which prepends a 6-character prefix (e.g. `onrtac:`) to the UUID used as the JWT `jti` and as `Details.TOKEN_ID`. The prefix reveals to any party that sees the access token (resource servers, browser-side apps, logs, error reports) the grant type that minted the token (including `pre-authorized_code`, `token-exchange`, etc.), whether the session is offline/online/transient, and whether the token is a lightweight access token. While not secret, this leaks behaviour (e.g. presence of offline sessions, use of token exchange) that is otherwise not conveyed to clients and that may not be desirable in all deployments (e.g. compliance, fingerprinting of Keycloak version/features, ability to distinguish realms/configurations). Consider making the SPI opt-in or at least allowing operators to disable it, and documenting the information disclosure in release notes.

title: Unused import TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory
body: The diff adds `import org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.grants.TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory;` but the new line uses `OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE` instead of any constant from `TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory`. The import is dead and should be removed to keep the file clean and avoid IDE warnings.

title: No tests for the new SPI wiring in production token issuance
body: The unit test `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest` only exercises the encoder's encode/decode logic with a manually-seeded factory map. There is no test that drives the full token issuance path (e.g. an authorization code, refresh, CIBA or device flow integration test) and asserts on the actual token ID prefix, nor is there a test that runs `postInit` against a real `KeycloakSessionFactory` to validate the shortcut-uniqueness assertion in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` (i.e. detecting duplicate shortcuts across grant factories). Combined with the broken AssertEvents matcher (#2), this means the PR can regress grant-type encoding in production without any test catching it.

title: Constants.GRANT_TYPE key collides with OAuth2 form parameter name
body: `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` is defined as `OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE`, which is the literal string `"grant_type"` (the standard OAuth2 form parameter name). It is used both as the form-parameter key to populate `OAuth2GrantType.Context.grantType` and as the attribute key on `ClientSessionContext`. Because session context attributes and form parameters are different objects, this is not a runtime bug, but the shared string is a sharp edge: any code that reads or writes `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` on the wrong object (e.g. on the form params) would be confused. Use a distinct namespaced key such as `Constants.GRANT_TYPE + ".attribute"` or move it to a session-context-specific constant to make the distinction explicit.

title: Recovery codes stored under wrong field; user storage will keep a credential with null credentialData
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential builds the input as `new UserCredentialModel("", credentialModel.getType(), recoveryCodesJson)`. The 3-arg `UserCredentialModel(String id, String type, String value)` constructor sets the `value` field and leaves `challengeResponse` as null (the parallel 4-arg constructor exists specifically to populate `challengeResponse`). The new BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential branch then reads `input.getChallengeResponse()`, so `recoveryCodesModel.setCredentialData(null)` is invoked and the JSON list of codes is silently dropped. Subsequent `getCredentials` will hit `JsonSerialization.readValue(null, List.class)` and the `isValid` branch will compare `input.getChallengeResponse()` against nothing, so the user can never authenticate with a recovery code stored in user storage. Either pass the JSON via the 4-arg constructor (e.g. `new UserCredentialModel("", type, recoveryCodesJson, null)`) or change the user storage provider to mirror OTP and use `input.getValue()` when populating `credentialData`. The added test testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin would fail today.

title: Recovery codes read from challengeResponse instead of value
body: The new `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE` branch stores the codes via `recoveryCodesModel.setCredentialData(input.getChallengeResponse())`. The credential is created in CredentialHelper with the 3-arg constructor, which populates `value`, not `challengeResponse`, so this field is null and the credentialData is never set. This is inconsistent with the OTP branch in the same method, which correctly reads `otpCredential.getValue()`. The branch should read `input.getValue()` (or, if challengeResponse semantics are desired, CredentialHelper must be changed to use the 4-arg constructor).

title: NoSuchElementException if user has no recovery codes credential
body: The bean calls `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel(credentialModelOpt.get())` without first checking `credentialModelOpt.isPresent()`. If the user no longer has a recovery-codes credential (e.g. the form is rendered while credentials are being recreated, after admin removal, or after `allCodesUsed()` already triggered `removeStoredCredentialById`), `Optional.get()` raises NoSuchElementException and the login page fails to render with a stack trace instead of a graceful error. A defensive null/empty check should be added (or the bean should not be instantiated when no credential is present).

title: Used-up recovery codes will not be removed when stored in user storage
body: When `recoveryCodeCredentialModel.allCodesUsed()` is true, the authenticator calls `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())`. BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage implements only `CredentialInputUpdater` and `CredentialInputValidator`; it does not implement `CredentialProvider` and therefore has no `removeCredential` hook. The default Keycloak path for `removeStoredCredentialById` only delegates to `CredentialProvider` instances, so removal silently fails for a user-storage credential. The user is left with a credential whose codes are all used and the required action to reconfigure will be added, but the stale credential entry remains in user storage forever.

title: disableCredentialType ignores recovery codes
body: The override only clears OTP when `credentialType` matches an OTP type. When admin REST or the account console calls disable with `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE` (now advertised via `supportsCredentialType` and visible through `getCredentials`), the method just logs `Unsupported to disable credential of type` and returns. Either reject the type in `supportsCredentialType`/`getDisableableCredentialTypesStream`, or clear `myUser.recoveryCodes` like it does for OTP. Otherwise the admin can list and view recovery codes as disableable but never actually disable them.

title: testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin does not verify code consumption
body: The test only logs in once with one recovery code and then logs out. It does not verify that the used code is actually consumed (i.e. that a second login attempt with the same code fails and that subsequent use of an unused code works) and does not verify that when all codes are used the credential is removed and `CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES` is added. This leaves the most important behavioural guarantees of the new feature uncovered.

title: getCredential javadoc is misleading
body: The Javadoc says the method "Checks the user storage for the credential. If not found it will look for the credential in the local storage". The implementation actually chains `user.credentialManager().getFederatedCredentialsStream()` with `getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream(...)`.
