title: Queue depth metric is not tagged by worker/queue
body: `OrderedQueueWorker.run` emits `remote_subscriptions.queue_worker.queue_depth` only with `tags={"identifier": self.identifier}`. With `num_queues=20` workers sharing the same identifier, all depth values are aggregated into one series and individual hot queues cannot be distinguished, defeating the purpose of the metric for diagnosing the very backlog problem the PR is meant to address. The worker_id (and ideally the queue index) should be in the tags.

title: wait_until_empty is dead code
body: `FixedQueuePool.wait_until_empty` is defined but never called by the strategy or factory. It also has subtle correctness issues if ever used (it polls `qsize()` rather than tracking completion, so it can race against in-flight items). Either remove it or document and test its intended use.

title: Backup code entropy is only 40 bits per code
body: Each backup code is generated as `crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`, producing a 10-character hex string with only 40 bits of entropy. Modern guidance (NIST SP 800-63B) recommends at least 64 bits of entropy for OTP secrets, and 128 bits is common. Because the code is the only thing standing between an attacker and account access (it bypasses the TOTP factor), 40 bits is brute-forceable in a realistic timeframe, especially since failed attempts do not consume the code and the API has no per-user rate limiting on the credentials provider beyond the existing email-based limiter.

title: Backup code is not consumed on failed attempt; timing-unsafe comparison
body: Two problems compound here: (1) `Array.prototype.indexOf` is not a constant-time comparison, so the time taken to find (or not find) a user-supplied backup code leaks information about how many leading bytes matched, enabling a timing side-channel that lets an attacker enumerate codes character by character. Use a constant-time comparison (e.g. compare each code with `crypto.timingSafeEqual` after length-checking). (2) The supplied code is only removed from the array after a successful match (`backupCodes[index] = null`), so failed attempts leave all 10 codes intact. Combined with the 40-bit entropy per code, this makes online brute force feasible: an attacker can submit unlimited guesses until one matches.

title: Timing-unsafe backup code comparison and missing password for non-CAL users
body: Same `backupCodes.indexOf(...)` timing leak as in the credentials provider: a constant-time comparison should be used. More importantly, the password check at line 40 is gated on `user.password && user.identityProvider === IdentityProvider.CAL`, so for SAML/Google users the only thing required to disable 2FA is a single valid backup code. A leaked backup code therefore gives an attacker the ability to log in via the credentials provider and then turn off 2FA entirely, reducing the account to a single factor. The credentials provider should still demand something only the legitimate user possesses (e.g. re-prompt for password, or require the SAML/Google re-authentication) before 2FA can be disabled.

title: Default export is named TwoFactor, not BackupCode
body: The file is `BackupCode.tsx` and consumers import it as `import BackupCode from "@components/auth/BackupCode"`, but the default export is declared as `export default function TwoFactor({ center = true })`. The mismatch is not a runtime error (default exports are not name-checked), but it is a clear copy/paste leftover that will confuse anyone reading the file or refactoring the codebase. Rename the function (and the display name / `displayName`) to `BackupCode`.

title: Label is not associated with the input
body: The `<Label>` renders `{t("backup_code")}` but has no `htmlFor` attribute, so screen readers do not announce it as the label for the backup-code input. Either pass an `htmlFor` matching the `id="backup-code"` on the `TextField`, or wrap the input with the label. The same `Label` import in `TwoFactor.tsx` has the same gap, so the new component was modeled on the existing bug.

title: Object URL for backup-codes download is never revoked on unmount
body: `URL.createObjectURL(textBlob)` is called whenever a user runs the setup, and the previous URL is revoked on the next setup, but the URL is not revoked when the component unmounts, when the modal is closed via the X / overlay, or when `onOpenChange(false)` fires. `resetState()` clears the state but does not call `URL.revokeObjectURL(backupCodesUrl)`. The blob stays in memory for the lifetime of the page, which is both a memory leak and a minor data exposure concern (the plaintext backup codes are still in the page's blob store). Revoke the URL in a cleanup effect and in `resetState`.

title: Backup-codes dialog buttons default to type="submit" and submit the TOTP form
body: The Close, Copy, and Download buttons inside the `<WithStep step={SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes}>` block do not specify a `type` attribute, so they default to `type="submit"`. They are rendered inside the `<Form handleSubmit={handleEnable} form={form}>` which targets the TOTP form. The `e.preventDefault()` call in each onClick does stop the default for that click, but: (a) the auto-submit effect (line 157-161) watches `totpCode`, so the moment a user pastes or types in the TOTP boxes on the same screen the form will submit; (b) relying on `preventDefault` on a submit button is fragile and a maintenance trap. Add `type="button"` to all three buttons (and to the `Continue` button at line 247, which has the same issue but at least is inside a different WithStep so is less likely to fire today).

title: formatBackupCode is used before it is declared
body: `handleSetup` (line 77) calls `formatBackupCode` at line 95, but `formatBackupCode` is declared with `const` at line 163, after `handleSetup` in the source. The const is in the temporal dead zone until the component body finishes executing, so any path that reaches the use before mount (e.g. an early return, a future refactor that calls `handleSetup` during render, or a test that calls the function directly) will throw `ReferenceError: Cannot access 'formatBackupCode' before initialization`. It works today only because the user has to click the button after mount. Move the helper above `handleSetup` (or extract it to module scope) so the dependency order matches the source order.

title: No e2e test covers backup-code login or backup-code disable
body: The new backup-codes test only exercises the display/copy/download UI on the setup flow. There is no test for the actual auth-critical paths the PR introduces: (1) logging in with a backup code after clicking "Lost access", (2) the login path when the backup code is wrong (expect `incorrect_backup_code`), (3) disabling 2FA using a backup code from the settings modal. The author flagged this in the TODO on line 12, but these are the security-relevant paths and should not ship untested. In particular there is no regression coverage for the credential flow that consumes a code and re-encrypts the array.

title: Download link is a plain <a> with no rel or sandboxing
body: The "Download" button is wrapped in `<a download="cal-backup-codes.txt" href={backupCodesUrl}>` with no `rel="noopener"` or `type` attribute. While `download` is set so navigation is not expected, an `href` that is a `blob:` URL still benefits from the standard hardening, and a future change that switches to a same-origin URL would silently introduce a tabnabbing vector. Add `rel="noopener noreferrer"` to be safe.

title: Race condition lets backup codes be reused / resurrected
body: The backup-code branch decrypts user.backupCodes, finds the matching index, sets the slot to null, and then writes the array back (lines 139-156). The read-decrypt-mutate-write cycle is non-atomic. If two concurrent authorize() calls hit it with the same backup code, both will decrypt the original array, both will find the match, and both will mark the slot null — so the same one-time code authenticates twice. With two different backup codes, each call mutates its own copy and the later write overwrites the earlier one, resurrecting the code that the first request already consumed. Because authorize() runs on every NextAuth credentials sign-in, a user with stolen credentials (or a session race) could keep re-using the same backup code. Replace the in-memory mutation with a single conditional Prisma update (e.g. a JSONB / array-element update that removes only the matched code) so the consumption is atomic at the database level.

title: Disable endpoint has no rate limiting on backup-code guesses
body: The disable endpoint verifies password (bcrypt-bounded) and then accepts a backup code by `backupCodes.indexOf(req.body.backupCode.replaceAll('-', ''))`. Unlike the NextAuth credentials authorize flow, this endpoint does NOT call `checkRateLimitAndThrowError`. An attacker who already has the user's password can therefore brute-force the ten 10-hex-char backup codes at full speed (only bcrypt on the password limits them, and that throttling is per user, not per attempt). The endpoint also never marks the consumed code, so even a correct guess leaves the rest usable. Add a rate limit per (userId, IP) and reuse the atomic consumption pattern from the credentials authorize flow.

title: All-codes-exhausted state is indistinguishable from a typo
body: When a user has consumed every backup code, `backupCodes` is `[null, null, ..., null]`. `user.backupCodes` is still a non-empty encrypted string, so the `if (!user.backupCodes) throw MissingBackupCodes` guard never fires. The user instead gets `IncorrectBackupCode` on every attempt, with no way to tell that they've actually run out of codes. After decrypt+parse, detect the case where every element is null/missing and throw `MissingBackupCodes` (or a new dedicated error) so the UI can surface a clear message and the user knows to re-enable 2FA and regenerate codes.

title: Backup-code login and disable paths are not end-to-end tested
body: The new e2e additions only exercise the backup-codes dialog (download/copy/close) after enabling 2FA. The two security-critical paths this PR introduces — logging in via backup code from `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx` (`twoFactorLostAccess` flow) and disabling 2FA via the 'Lost access' path in `DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx` — have no test at all. The PR description itself acknowledges 'I haven't added tests that prove my fix is effective'. For an authentication feature, both the happy path and the wrong-code / exhausted-code negative paths must be covered, and the consumed-once invariant should be asserted (e.g. login with the same code twice, second attempt must fail).

title: Blob URL leaks until next setup round-trip
body: `setBackupCodesUrl(URL.createObjectURL(textBlob))` is called on every setup response but the URL is only revoked when a *subsequent* setup response arrives. If the user reaches the backup codes screen and then closes the dialog (Cancel / Close) or the parent component unmounts without re-running setup, the latest object URL is never revoked. Combined with `resetState()` not clearing `backupCodesUrl`, opening the modal again can also bind to a stale URL. Revoke the previous URL inside `resetState` and on a `useEffect` cleanup that fires when the modal closes.

title: resetState leaves isSubmitting, backupCodes, secret and dataUri in place
body: `resetState()` only clears `password`, `errorMessage`, and `step`. It does not reset `isSubmitting`, `backupCodes`, `backupCodesUrl` (blob URL — see separate finding), `dataUri`, or `secret`. If the modal is closed and reopened, the next 'Continue' button can stay disabled (because `isSubmitting` may still be true from a previous round), and the stale `secret` / `dataUri` could be displayed against a brand-new secret if the user races the step transitions. Reset all transient state and revoke any pending blob URL inside `resetState`.

title: BackupCode component is named TwoFactor
body: `export default function TwoFactor({ center = true })` is the default export of `apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx`. The misleading function name makes the file confusing to navigate (especially since `TwoFactor.tsx` already exists in the same directory with a similar signature). Rename the function to `BackupCode` to match the file name.

title: body.backupCodes assumed to be present and a string array
body: Right after `await response.json()`, the code does `body.backupCodes.map(formatBackupCode)` with no guard. If the server ever returns an error body that lacks `backupCodes`, or returns it under a different key, or with non-string elements, the page crashes mid-setup and `setIsSubmitting(false)` runs but the user is left on a broken step. Validate the shape (Array.isArray and every element is a string) before using it, and fall back to the existing `something_went_wrong` error if it isn't.

title: Race condition lets a backup code be reused
body: The backup-code consumption path in authorize() reads user.backupCodes, decrypts it with JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)), nulls the matched slot, re-encrypts, and writes the result back via prisma.user.update with no atomicity guard. Two concurrent requests submitting different valid backup codes both read the same pre-image, each null a different index in their local copy, and whichever update commits last overwrites the other writer's null — restoring the slot the first request consumed. Consequence: a backup code can be used more than once, breaking the one-time-use guarantee the PR explicitly relies on (see the comment 'delete verified backup code and re-encrypt remaining'). Fix by making the update atomic, e.g. wrap read+write in prisma.$transaction, or include the expected pre-image in the WHERE clause so the second writer is rejected.

title: Backup-code login and disable flows are not tested
body: The TODO at the top of the file ('TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup') explicitly states the two main backup-code flows are not covered. The added e2e block only exercises the download/copy buttons in the setup screen and never actually submits a backup code during login or disable. The PR description also says 'I haven't added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works'. Without these tests, regressions in code matching, case normalization, the one-time-use guarantee, and the race condition in next-auth-options.ts would not be caught. The two inline TODOs ('check file content', 'check clipboard content') further leave the new UI assertions unchecked.

title: Disable endpoint logs a 'backup code login' error
body: The console.error inside the backup-code branch logs 'Missing encryption key; cannot proceed with backup code login.' This handler lives at /api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable, not a login endpoint. Operators reading server logs during a disable incident will be misled into believing a login attempt failed. The same wording is reused in packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:133, suggesting copy-paste rather than intent. Update the message to reflect the actual operation (e.g. 'cannot proceed with backup code verification while disabling 2FA').

title: Backup-codes Blob URL is never revoked when the modal closes
body: handleSetup calls URL.createObjectURL(textBlob) to produce the download link for the user's plaintext backup codes and stores it in backupCodesUrl. There is no URL.revokeObjectURL call when the modal closes — resetState() only clears password, errorMessage, and step, and the component has no unmount cleanup. The Blob keeps the user's plaintext backup codes alive in memory until either the next successful setup (which revokes the previous URL) or the page is unloaded. Revoke the URL inside resetState and in a useEffect cleanup that runs on unmount.

title: Default export is named TwoFactor instead of BackupCode
body: The new file apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx declares 'export default function TwoFactor(...)', yet consumers import it as 'import BackupCode from "@components/auth/BackupCode"' (see DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:8 and login.tsx:32). The symbol name in the file does not match the imported name. A developer greping for TwoFactor (e.g. while refactoring or deleting the existing apps/web/components/auth/TwoFactor.tsx) will edit the wrong file, and tools that flag mismatched export/import names may warn. Rename the export to BackupCode to match the file name and the import sites.

title: Google Calendar updateEvent selectedCalendar lookup is dead code
body: In `updateEvent`, the code is `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the only branch that would reach the `.find()`), the predicate `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` is `cal.externalId === undefined` and will never match any element. The result is always `undefined` in that branch, so the update will run with `calendarId: undefined`, which Google will reject or default to `primary` for the wrong account. The intent (per the comment in `createEvent`) is presumably to match by `credentialId` like the new `createEvent` logic does.

title: Google Calendar deleteEvent calendarId lookup is dead code
body: Same defect as in `updateEvent`: `const calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is undefined, `find` searches for `cal.externalId === undefined`, which never matches. Consequently the call falls through to `defaultCalendarId = 'primary'`, deleting the event from the organizer's primary calendar regardless of which host the reference actually belonged to. This silently destroys the wrong event on cancellation of a collective booking.

title: Calendar.createEvent signature change is not propagated to all implementations
body: The `Calendar` interface now mandates `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number): Promise<NewCalendarEventType>`, but only `GoogleCalendarService` and `BaseCalendarService` were updated. `LarkCalendarService.createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` and `Office365CalendarService.createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` still have the old single-argument signature, so they no longer satisfy the interface and any other third-party calendar app implementing `Calendar` will also be out of compliance. The change must either be made optional in the interface or every implementation must be updated.

title: teamMember objects carry unknown firstName/lastName properties
body: The new `teamMemberPromises` map returns `{ email, name, firstName: '', lastName: '', timeZone, language }`. Neither `Person` nor `TeamMember` (the element type of `CalendarEvent.team.members`) declares `firstName`/`lastName`, so these properties are excess and either cause a TypeScript error or are silently dropped. They serve no purpose in the subsequent code path (`team.members` is only iterated for `email`), and add confusion to the type. They should be removed.

title: loadUsers now throws on empty dynamicUserList, breaking dynamic bookings
body: The new `loadUsers` wrapper throws `HttpError(400, 'dynamicUserList is not properly defined or empty.')` when `!eventTypeId` and `dynamicUserList` is not an array or is empty. The previous behavior was a Prisma `findMany` that simply returned an empty array and let the caller proceed. For dynamic links/groups with no matching users (a realistic scenario, e.g. typos in slug or temporarily no active users), the booking flow now fails with a 400 instead of producing the previous, more graceful outcome. This is an unintended behavior change.

title: isTeamEventType uses string literals instead of enum
body: `isTeamEventType` was changed from `eventType.schedulingType === SchedulingType.COLLECTIVE || eventType.schedulingType === SchedulingType.ROUND_ROBIN` to `!!eventType.schedulingType && ['COLLECTIVE', 'ROUND_ROBIN'].includes(eventType.schedulingType)`. Using the enum values directly (as before) is type-safe; the new string-literal array silently breaks if the enum members are ever renamed and offers no compiler protection.

title: Fallback 'first connected calendar' filter never matches
body: When `event.destinationCalendar` is empty, the fallback is `const [credential] = this.calendarCredentials.filter((cred) => cred.type === 'calendar');`. Calendar credentials in this codebase have types like `google_calendar`, `office365_calendar`, etc. (all ending in `_calendar`), never a bare `'calendar'`, so the filter yields `[]`, `credential` is `undefined`, and no event is created. This is a pre-existing bug but is still present after this refactor and worth fixing while the code is being touched. A `cred.type.endsWith('_calendar')` check (matching the constructor filter) would work.

title: Only the first destinationCalendar is persisted on the Booking
body: The PR builds `evt.destinationCalendar` as an array (so the loop in `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` can create a Google event per host), but on persist only the first element is connected: `destinationCalendar: evt.destinationCalendar && evt.destinationCalendar.length > 0 ? { connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id } } : undefined`. The Prisma `Booking` model has a single `destinationCalendar` field, so subsequent code that rebuilds the array from the booking (e.g. `handleCancelBooking.ts` which does `[bookingToDelete?.destinationCalendar]`) will only see one calendar, even though the calendar event was actually created on multiple hosts' calendars. The PR does not include a schema change to support the array, so the asymmetry between 'events created' and 'what is stored' must be called out; downstream cancel/edit/reschedule flows will operate on the wrong subset.

title: Unrelated logic change to organization create handler
body: The diff inverts `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` (and the same for `requestedSlug`). This is a correct fix (the old condition produced a slug only when billing was disabled), but it has nothing to do with the destinationCalendar array refactor and changes organization creation behavior. It should ideally be split into its own commit/PR so it can be reviewed and reverted independently.

title: BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED tests still expect destinationCalendar: null
body: The BOOKING_REJECTED expectation was updated to `destinationCalendar: []` to match the new array contract, but the BOOKING_CREATED (line 119) and BOOKING_REQUESTED (line 373) tests still expect `destinationCalendar: null`. The corresponding code paths in `handleNewBooking.ts` set `destinationCalendar: ... ? [...] : null` (i.e. can return either an array or `null`). A test that books a collective event type where hosts do have destination calendars configured would actually exercise the array branch and is missing from this PR; the Loom shows the new behavior but no automated test was added.

title: updateEvent fallback always returns undefined
body: The new fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is reached only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the predicate searches for `cal.externalId === undefined`, which never matches. The previous behavior was `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` (a valid fallback). Now `selectedCalendar` is undefined when externalCalendarId is omitted, and there is no `'primary'` fallback like `createEvent` has — the update is sent to `calendarId: undefined`, which Google rejects. This breaks updates for any booking whose stored `externalCalendarId` is null (notably pre-refactor bookings created before references existed).

title: deleteEvent fallback always returns undefined
body: Same bug as in updateEvent: the find-against-undefined pattern guarantees no match, so `calendarId` falls back to 'primary' regardless of where the event actually lives. Result: deleteEvent targets a calendar that doesn't contain the event, returning 404, and the `if (err.code === 404) return resolve();` handler silently swallows the failure. Real deletion therefore never occurs for legacy bookings where `externalCalendarId` is null.

title: TypeError when MeetLocationType has no destination calendar
body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` produces `undefined` when the array is empty/absent. The very next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration`, which throws on `undefined`. Previously this was guarded by `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, so picking 'Google Meet' for any user without a destination calendar (a routine configuration) now 500s the booking instead of falling back to Cal Video.

title: Recurring cancellation uses booking owner's credentials only
body: Inside the recurring-event branch the code re-iterates `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(c => c.type.endsWith('_calendar'))` rather than the credential already resolved for the current reference. For collective bookings the booking owner is only one of several hosts; the other hosts' calendar credentials live elsewhere in the database (the if-branch already handles this by falling back to `prisma.credential.findUnique`). Only using the owner's calendars means other hosts' recurring instances never get deleted. The inner loop should be driven by `updBooking.references`/`reference.credentialId`, not by the owner's credentials.

title: Falls back to empty instead of user's destination calendar
body: `destinationCalendar: bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar ? [...] : []` lost the user-level fallback present everywhere else. Every other handler in this PR (confirm, editLocation, handleCancelBooking, deleteCredential, paypal-webhook, stripe webhook) falls back to `user.destinationCalendar` when the booking has none. Pre-reschedule bookings with no destination calendar will now be sent through reschedule emails and reschedule webhooks with `destinationCalendar: []`, and EventManager then has no host calendar to invite, which can produce no calendar events for the requester.

title: loadUsers refactor drops organization select
body: The new `loadUsers` removed `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the dynamic-user branch. Any downstream code that reads the user's organization slug from the loaded user (including the post-load flow that may construct event URLs / emails / org-aware flows) will receive `undefined`. The original select surfaced organization data so removing it is a silent regression, not a cleanup.

title: loadUsers error wrapping loses original status/context
body: Any error (including the new dynamicUserList-empty check) is rethrown as HttpError 500 'Unable to load users' unless it is already a Prisma error. This both changes observable behavior (a previously-silent empty dynamicUserList now turns into a 500 booking failure) and hides the real cause in logs. The empty-dynamicUserList guard should not be treated like a server failure.

title: Inconsistent empty destinationCalendar value across handlers
body: handleNewBooking emits `destinationCalendar: null` when both eventType and organizer have no destination calendar, while every other handler updated in this PR (confirm, editLocation, cancel, payment webhooks, deleteCredential, bookingReminder) emits `destinationCalendar: []` in the same case. Consumers (webhooks, emails, calendar services that do `[mainHost] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`) now have to handle both shapes for the same 'no calendar' semantic. Pick one (preferably `[]`) and apply it everywhere.

title: Booking create no longer persists per-host references when result.externalId is missing
body: In `create()` the new code sets `externalCalendarId: result.externalId` and `credentialId: result.credentialId` for calendar references. The `else` branch in `createAllCalendarEvents` (when `destination.credentialId` is undefined) calls `createEvent(c, event)` without the third `externalId` argument, so `result.externalId` is undefined, and the new reference is created with an undefined `externalCalendarId`. Later updates/deletes on those references will not target any specific calendar and will fall back to 'primary' / fail. With the new multi-host flow this branch is also reachable for brand-new collective bookings if any destination entry lacks a credentialId.

title: Unrelated logic change mixed into destinationCalendar PR
body: The diff inverts the original `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }` / `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { requestedSlug: slug }` into ternaries. This is a real bug fix (the original logic put `slug` on the org when billing was disabled, which is almost certainly wrong) but it is completely unrelated to the destinationCalendar array migration. It is a maintainability concern: bundling behavioral fixes in unrelated PRs makes bisecting and reverting harder, and this PR does not document or test the new behavior.

title: Booking-references loop runs delete logic serially before any awaits
body: The outer `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` does multiple sequential awaits per iteration: a Prisma `findUnique` for the credential, then possibly another to get a calendar, then `deleteEvent`. With multiple calendar references (collective bookings), this serializes N round-trips before any deletes actually fire. The deleteEvent calls themselves are collected as promises and awaited together later (`Promise.allSettled(...apiDeletes)`), so they are parallel, but the credential/calendar lookups preceding them are not. For a 5-host collective this turns into 5 sequential DB reads per cancellation. Hoist `prisma.credential.findUnique` lookups into a `Promise.all` and only await `getCalendar` after, or cache by id.

title: schedulingType added to CalendarEvent but unused
body: A new `schedulingType?: SchedulingType | null` field is added to `CalendarEvent`, and `handleNewBooking.ts` writes it onto `evt`. No consumer in this diff (or elsewhere in the codebase per the changes shown) reads it, and there is no documentation explaining which calendar integrations are expected to key off it. It is purely dead surface area — either remove it until a consumer exists or commit the consumer together with this PR.

title: BaseCalendarService.createEvent does not match new Calendar interface signature
body: The Calendar interface in packages/types/Calendar.d.ts now requires `createEvent(event, credentialId)`, but this class still implements `async createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` with no `credentialId` parameter. This is a TypeScript contract violation for any app that extends BaseCalendarService (e.g. caldav-style providers), and at runtime this implementation does not filter `event.destinationCalendar` by credential, so on a collective event whose first entry is a Google/Lark calendar it will request the wrong external id and likely fail.

title: Google updateEvent lookup compares externalId against externalCalendarId (broken)
body: `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` When `externalCalendarId` is falsy we then run `.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)`, i.e. search for an entry whose `externalId === undefined`. That never matches, so `selectedCalendar` is `undefined` and is passed straight to `calendar.events.update` as `calendarId`. The delete branch on line 315-317 has the same bug but without the `"primary"` fallback that the create branch uses, so deletion on the Google API will fail.

title: Google deleteEvent lookup always yields undefined
body: `const calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` The `.find` predicate requires `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`; since we are in the falsy branch of the ternary this becomes `cal.externalId === undefined`, never true. Result: an undefined `calendarId` is sent to `calendar.events.delete`, breaking deletions whenever a booking does not have a stored externalCalendarId.

title: updateEvent return is missing externalId/credentialId, breaking editLocation references
body: `EventResult` now declares `externalId?: string | null` and the `updateLocation` flow in EventManager.ts (lines ~200-211) reads `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId` to build `referencesToCreate`. But `CalendarManager.updateEvent` still returns only `{appName, type, success, uid, updatedEvent, originalEvent, calError, calWarnings}` without those two fields. As a result, every references row created by `updateLocation` will have `externalCalendarId: undefined`, losing the link to the underlying calendar event used by `deleteEvent`.

title: Lark createEvent always uses the first destination calendar regardless of credential
body: EventManager.create iterates over each destination and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` to drive the per-host booking. Lark's createEvent ignores the credential/externalId it was given and falls back to `event.destinationCalendar ?? []` (first element). In a collective event whose first destination belongs to a Google host, Lark will be asked to create the event under that Google external id and the request will fail or write to the wrong calendar.

title: Office365 createEvent ignores credentialId and may address the wrong calendar
body: Same pattern as Lark: the new Calendar interface and EventManager pass `credentialId` and `destination.externalId`, but Office365's implementation just takes `event.destinationCalendar[0]`. For a collective event the first destination is typically the main host's calendar (e.g. Google), so the Office365 call would attempt `https://graph.microsoft.com/.../calendars/<google-external-id>/events` and fail.

title: teamDestinationCalendars pushed without dedup; can create duplicate events on same calendar
body: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);` has no de-duplication by `credentialId`/`externalId`. Hosts that share a single connected destination calendar (a common case when multiple members point at the same Google account) will each contribute the same entry, leading EventManager.create to call `createEvent` twice for the same calendar+credential and create duplicate events in that calendar.

title: Cancellation only includes a single destination calendar, losing team calendars
body: The CalendarEvent built here wraps only `bookingToDelete.destinationCalendar` or the user destination in a single-element array and never collects other team hosts' destinations. handleNewBooking now aggregates host destination calendars into a multi-element array for new bookings; cancellation must do the same or cancellations on collective events will leak the secondary calendars (their events still exist because `deleteEvent` is called per reference, but emails/webhooks reflect only one calendar and the symmetry between create and cancel is broken).

title: destinationCalendar built without user.destinationCalendar fallback, inconsistent with other handlers
body: All sibling handlers (confirm, cancelBooking, editLocation, handleNewBooking, deleteCredential, paypal/stripe webhooks, bookingReminder) fall back to `user.destinationCalendar` when `booking.destinationCalendar` is null. This handler does not, so for users whose only destinationCalendar lives on the user (not the booking), the request-reschedule flow will silently go through with `destinationCalendar: []`, which EventManager.create interprets as 'no destination'.

title: When merging bookings, only first calendar reference of the old booking is deleted
body: `const oldCalendarEvent = booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"));` returns at most one reference. For a collective reschedule that produced multiple calendar references on the old booking, only the first one will be deleted on its provider. The remaining calendar events stay on the user's calendar and effectively become orphans.

title: loadUsers try/catch swallows programming errors and converts them to 500/400
body: The new wrapping of `loadUsers` in a try/catch that maps `Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError` to statusCode 400 and any other error to statusCode 500 masks real bugs (e.g. wrong select shape, missing relations). Also the `if (!Array.isArray(hosts)) throw` is unreachable: `hosts` was already set via `eventType.hosts || []`, so it is always an array. These added checks give a false sense of guarding a code path that cannot fail as written.

title: Main-host external id reused as organizer email even when event is created on another host's calendar
body: `email: mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId ? mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId : calEventRaw.organizer.email,` is taken from the FIRST destination calendar (the main host's calendar), but the actual insertion below happens on the calendar returned by `destinationCalendar?.find(c => c.credentialId === credentialId)`, which may be a different host. As a result, when a non-main host's Google calendar is the target, the organizer entry in that calendar's event will be the main host's externalId/email instead of the true calendar owner's.

title: PR makes no new tests for the multi-host collective booking flow it claims to fix
body: The change converts `destinationCalendar` from a single object to an array and rewires creation/cancellation across many files, fixing #7754 (collective events with multiple destination calendars per host). The PR description itself notes 'I haven't added tests that prove my fix is effective'. The existing `webhook.e2e.ts` update only changes the expected `destinationCalendar` literal in a single webhook assertion, which does not exercise the new per-host creation or per-host cancellation flow.

title: Credential key stored as the full safeParse result, not the parsed data
body: The new helper `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the `safeParse` envelope (`{ success, data }`). The Google Calendar service assigns that envelope directly to `key` and persists it: `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema); await prisma.credential.update({ where: { id: credential.id }, data: { key } });`. After the next refresh, `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` will be parsing an object of shape `{ success: true, data: { access_token, refresh_token, ... } }`, which fails every required field check, so the credential becomes permanently invalid. Other call sites (office365calendar, salesforce, zoom) correctly read `.data`; this is the lone regression. The function should return just the data, or the call site should be `data: { key: key.data }`.

title: Missing refresh token is replaced with the literal string "refresh_token"
body: When the parsed token response does not contain a `refresh_token`, the helper assigns `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` and stores the credential. The literal string "refresh_token" is not a valid OAuth refresh token, so on the very next refresh the provider will respond with `invalid_grant`, the credential will be invalidated, and (because it is now in the local DB) the user is stuck with a non-recoverable integration. The comment indicates the self-hoster's endpoint may return only `access_token` and `expiry_date`, in which case this branch is hit on every refresh. The function should refuse to mint a credential without a real refresh token, or fall back to the previously stored one.

title: minimumTokenResponseSchema computed keys both evaluate to the same literal string
body: `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()` use a Zod instance's default `Object.prototype.toString`, which returns the string `"[object Object]"` (zod does not override `toString` on ZodString / ZodOptional). Both expressions therefore evaluate to the same string. In an object literal the second property overwrites the first, so the schema collapses to `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), "[object Object]": z.unknown().optional() })`. The schema does not match the obvious intent ("any string key with a number value, plus any other properties"); it accepts any object that happens to have an `access_token` string and no other validation of the rest of the OAuth response. With this minimum schema in effect, callers will silently accept malformed token responses from the self-hoster's endpoint and store them, which then fails on subsequent use.

title: Time-of-check/time-of-use race in credential upsert
body: The handler does `prisma.credential.findFirst` and then either `update` or `create` based on the result. There is no unique constraint on `(userId, appId)` in the credential model (the comment at line 61 even acknowledges this), and nothing atomic here. Two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user/app can both see no existing credential and both attempt `create`, so one will fail with a unique-constraint / duplicate-key error (or succeed in creating a second row). The function does not wrap this in a transaction, does not use `upsert`, and does not catch the duplicate error and retry as an update. Result is a 500 for one of the two callers and/or duplicate credentials in the DB.

title: No HTTP method check; webhook accepts GET, HEAD, etc.
body: The handler does not check `req.method`. Anything other than POST will reach the body validation step, where `req.body` is typically undefined for GET, and `z.object({...}).parse(undefined)` will throw a ZodError, producing a 500 (and possibly leaking the expected schema in the response). The endpoint is a state-mutating webhook; it should explicitly `if (req.method !== 'POST') return res.status(405).json({ message: 'Method not allowed' })`.

title: symmetricDecrypt / JSON.parse failures are unhandled
body: The block `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""))` can throw in several ways: empty encryption key (falls back to `""`), wrong key, ciphertext tampered or not actually encrypted with this key, or successfully decrypted bytes that are not valid JSON. None of these are caught. A misconfigured self-hoster or any malformed payload will produce an unhandled 500, and the original ZodError from line 31 is similarly uncaught (would also 500 with the schema details). Both should be caught and returned as 4xx with a generic message, and the decryption/key-mismatch path should be logged.

title: Decrypted payload is stored as the credential key with no shape validation
body: After decrypting, the handler assigns `key: keys` to the credential, where `keys` is the result of `JSON.parse` (typed as `any`). There is no schema check that the decrypted value has the shape the downstream app expects (e.g. `{ access_token, refresh_token, expiry_date, ... }` for Google). Anyone holding the webhook secret and the encryption key can therefore overwrite an end-user's credential with arbitrary JSON. A compromised or buggy parent application could silently break a user's integration, and the next refresh would feed this malformed object into the per-app schemas (each of which has its own idea of the shape). Validate the parsed object against the target app's credential schema before persisting.

title: Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time string equality
body: The secret check is `req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, which short-circuits on the first differing byte. For a shared webhook secret the practical risk is low, but a remote attacker who can repeatedly send crafted requests and measure response times can in principle narrow down the secret byte-by-byte. Compare with a constant-time function such as `crypto.timingSafeEqual`.

title: Redundant prisma.app lookup; appStoreMetadata is the source of truth
body: The PR description states the parent's app store is the source of truth for apps, but this handler queries `prisma.app.findUnique({ where: { slug: reqBody.appSlug } })` and 404s if the local `app` row is missing. The `app` table is only populated by the app metadata sync (`CRON_ENABLE_APP_SYNC`, etc.), so a self-hoster whose env is fine but whose app sync has not run yet will see 404 for every valid slug. The very next line uses `appStoreMetadata[app.slug]`, which is the in-memory registry that the database is synced from, so the DB hit is unnecessary. Replace with `appStoreMetadata[reqBody.appSlug as keyof typeof appStoreMetadata]` and a single 404 if undefined.

title: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is a string, not a boolean
body: `export const APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED = process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY;` uses `&&` rather than `!!(...)`. The value is therefore the encryption-key string (a non-empty string is truthy, so the constant is the second operand's value), or `undefined` when either is missing. Every use site does a truthy check, so behaviour accidentally works today, but the type is wrong, the name is misleading, and a stricter consumer that does `=== true` or `Boolean(APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED)` would break. Should be `!!(process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY)`.

title: Outbound refresh request to self-hoster endpoint is unauthenticated
body: When credential sharing is enabled, the Cal.com server POSTs to `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the form body. There is no shared-secret header, no mTLS, no signature, and no per-user token; the only way the self-hoster can know the request is legitimate is by IP allowlist. The self-hoster's endpoint must return a valid access token to that Cal.com, so anyone able to reach the URL can mint tokens for arbitrary (calcomUserId, appSlug) pairs that the parent will then trust. Add an HMAC over the body using a shared secret (the same `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` already configured would be the natural fit), or otherwise authenticate the caller.

title: Outbound refresh fetch has no timeout and no error handling
body: The `fetch` to `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` has no `AbortController` / timeout, no try/catch, and no response-status check. If the self-hoster's endpoint is slow, the entire Cal.com request handler that triggered the refresh hangs (booking flow, calendar lookup, etc.); if it returns 5xx or fails DNS, the unhandled rejection bubbles up. Wrap in a timeout (e.g. 5–10s) and treat any non-2xx or network error as a refresh failure (which should invalidate the credential, the way direct-OAuth refreshes already do).

title: statusText-based HTTP check instead of response.ok
body: Salesforce's refresh path checks `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw new HttpError(...)`. `response.statusText` is an arbitrary reason phrase that the server may or may not send and that `fetch` does not always populate; the canonical way is `if (!response.ok)`. As written, a 4xx/5xx whose `statusText` happens to be `"OK"` (some proxies / Salesforce errors do this) would be treated as success and the response body parsed as a token, with `parseRefreshTokenResponse` then `reject`ing; in the opposite direction, a perfectly valid 200 with statusText `""` (HTTP/2, some servers) would always be rejected. Use `response.ok` and read the body for the real error.

title: Salesforce access token is refreshed on every API call
body: `getClient` is called from the constructor, before any expiry check, and unconditionally POSTs to the Salesforce token endpoint. There is no `isExpired` / `isTokenValid` short-circuit like the other integrations (Google, HubSpot, Lark, O365, Zoho) use. Every single Salesforce interaction (contact search, create event, update event, delete event) now incurs a synchronous network round trip to Salesforce, plus a credential-row write. Add the usual expiry check on `credentialKey.expires_in`/`expiry_date` and only call the refresh path when actually needed.

title: Helper returns the safeParse envelope, callers silently mis-use it
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the full `{ success, data }` object from `safeParse`, then performs a mutation (`refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = ...`) on the parsed result. Two of the four call sites correctly take `.data`, but the Google Calendar call site does not and the inconsistency already produced a high-severity regression there. The contract should be "return the data (after validation)", and the function should not be the place where the literal `refresh_token` is fabricated. Either return `data` directly or rename and document that callers must read `.data`.

title: Header name is documented as lowercase but the code does not normalize
body: The .env.example comment says "This is the header name that will be used to verify the webhook secret. Should be in lowercase." The handler reads `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"]`. In Next.js / Node, incoming HTTP header names are lower-cased, but the configured `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` is used as-is to index into `req.headers`. If a self-hoster sets it to anything but lower-case, the lookup silently fails and the request is rejected as 403 with no actionable message. Either enforce/document lowercase validation at startup, or normalize the configured name with `.toLowerCase()` before use.

title: New webhook endpoint and OAuth helpers have no tests
body: The PR description explicitly says "I haven't added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works". The two new endpoints (`/api/webhook/app-credential`), the two new helpers (`parseRefreshTokenResponse`, `refreshOAuthTokens`), and the new `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` constant together introduce a security-sensitive credential-syncing path. At a minimum: (1) webhook secret check accepts correct header and rejects wrong/absent; (2) Zod schema rejects malformed bodies and gives a 400; (3) symmetricDecrypt with wrong key is caught and is a 4xx, not a 500; (4) race against a concurrent identical webhook does not 500 (or returns idempotently); (5) `parseRefreshTokenResponse` does not silently fabricate a refresh_token; (6) `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is a boolean, not a string. None of these are covered.

title: Webhook handler accepts any HTTP method
body: The handler does not check `req.method` before processing. Combined with no CSRF protection and a single shared secret, this lets an attacker who learns the secret invoke the endpoint via GET (which Next.js does not JSON-parse by default, so `reqBody = z.parse(undefined)` will throw a 500), or submit via PUT/DELETE which could also expose side effects. The endpoint should explicitly require POST and reject other methods with 405.

title: Unprotected JSON.parse after decrypt can crash the request
body: `symmetricDecrypt` returns the raw decrypted bytes and the result is fed directly into `JSON.parse` with no try/catch. If the symmetric decrypt throws (bad key, tampered ciphertext, wrong padding) or the plaintext is not valid JSON, the handler crashes with an uncaught exception and returns a generic 500 instead of a 4xx. This also means the webhook secret check, user existence check, etc. cannot return a proper error. The decrypt and parse should be wrapped, and the result should be validated as an object before being assigned to `key`.

title: findFirst-then-create is racy and can duplicate credentials
body: The handler does `prisma.credential.findFirst({ userId, appId })` followed by `update` or `create` with no transaction. Two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same (userId, appId) can both observe no existing credential and both insert, leaving two `Credential` rows that downstream code (which does `findFirst` in e.g. office365video callback) cannot reliably deduplicate. Use `prisma.credential.upsert` with a unique compound key, or wrap the read/write in a transaction with appropriate isolation.

title: Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time equality
body: The webhook secret is compared with `!==`. Although the secret is shared and not user-derived, attackers can in principle exploit timing differences to recover the secret byte by byte. Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` against buffers of equal length (after a length check) to close this side channel.

title: Credential type sourced from app metadata, not the request
body: When creating a credential, the code uses `appMetadata.type` for `type` while the existing callbacks elsewhere in the codebase store values like `"google_calendar"`, `"hubspot_other_calendar"`, `"office365_video"`, etc. If `appStoreMetadata`'s `type` differs from the conventional string used elsewhere for the same app (or if the DB `app` row's slug does not match the metadata entry's slug), the new credential's `type` column will not match what CalendarService implementations later filter on, causing the freshly synced credential to be ignored.

title: Minimum token schema is malformed and does not validate anything
body: The schema is declared as `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional() })`. `z.string().toString()` evaluates to the literal string `"z.string()"` and Zod's `z.object` does not support arbitrary computed keys this way — it emits a warning at schema construction and the dynamic entries do not actually constrain any property. The resulting schema is effectively `{ access_token: string }` with an additional unknown catch-all, so `refresh_token`, `expiry_date`, `expires_in`, scopes, etc. are not enforced. The function should instead take the provider-specific `schema` argument when credential sharing is enabled (since the shared endpoint returns whatever format the host chose) or declare the real required fields.

title: Missing refresh_token is replaced with the literal string "refresh_token"
body: If the parsed response has no `refresh_token` field, the function sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. Downstream code in e.g. GoogleCalendarService and office365calendar persists `key` (or uses the value) as an actual OAuth refresh token. Storing the literal string "refresh_token" and later sending it to Google's/MS's refresh endpoint will cause the next refresh to fail with `invalid_grant`, which the Google service interprets as "unrecoverable, mark credential invalid". Instead, the existing refresh token should be preserved when the response omits one.

title: Outgoing credential-sync POST has no authentication
body: When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, this function POSTs `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` to the configured endpoint with no auth header. The receiving endpoint cannot verify the request came from this Cal.com instance, and a network attacker (or anyone who knows the endpoint URL) can impersonate arbitrary Cal.com users to obtain refreshed tokens. The same `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (and matching header name) that the incoming webhook requires should be sent on this outgoing request.

title: Missing Content-Type header and inconsistent return shape break every integration
body: Two issues: (1) The fetch sends a `URLSearchParams` body without `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, so the receiving endpoint that decodes the form will see empty fields. (2) The function returns either the original provider response (an axios/`googleapis` object with `.res.data`, `.access_token`, etc.) or a raw `fetch` `Response`. Every caller (googlecalendar, hubspot, larkcalendar, office365calendar, office365video, salesforce, webex, zoho-bigin, zohocrm, zoomvideo) immediately accesses fields like `res.data`, `response.json()`, `.accessToken`, `.access_token` etc. on the result. When credential sharing is enabled, those accesses will throw because the value is a `Response`, not the expected token object — so the feature breaks all integrations on the first refresh.

title: Saves SafeParseReturnType envelope instead of parsed data into credential.key
body: After the change, the code does `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema); await prisma.credential.update({ ..., data: { key } })`. `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the full Zod `SafeParseReturnType` (an object with `success`, `data`, and possibly `error`), not the parsed key. The credential row now stores `{ success: true, data: { ... } }` instead of the actual token object. The next time `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` runs it will throw and the credential will be unusable. Other integrations (`office365calendar`, `salesforce`, `zoomvideo`, `webex`) correctly do `...tokenResponse.data` or `...parsedToken.data` — only googlecalendar was updated incorrectly.

title: Salesforce getClient refreshes the OAuth token on every instantiation
body: `getClient` now unconditionally POSTs to the Salesforce token endpoint on every call, then writes the response to the DB. Previously Salesforce never did a refresh in this code path; every connection was constructed from the stored `credentialKey`. With the new code each `CalendarService` construction (and therefore each event create/update/getAvailability cycle that goes through the manager) makes an extra network round trip and a DB write. Add an expiry check before refreshing, matching the patterns used by googlecalendar / hubspot / webex.

title: Non-OK responses are detected via statusText === "OK"
body: The check `if (response.statusText !== "OK")` is fragile: HTTP status text is not guaranteed to be `"OK"` for 200 (it can be absent or empty in HTTP/2) and for many non-2xx responses `statusText` is still a non-empty string so the comparison misclassifies the response. Use `response.ok` (which checks 200–299) instead. With credential-sharing enabled the function will additionally return a `Response` rather than a parsed token, but the `statusText` check still has the bug described.

title: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is a string, not a boolean
body: `export const APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED = process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY;` evaluates to the encryption-key string when both env vars are set, or to `undefined`/`""` otherwise. Call sites use it in `if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED)` (truthy check), which works in practice, but it is documented/used as a boolean flag. Coerce explicitly: `Boolean(process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY)` so the type matches usage and an empty-string secret cannot accidentally enable sharing.

title: JSON.parse on req.query.state has no error handling
body: `JSON.parse(req.query.state)` will throw a SyntaxError if the state parameter is not valid JSON, turning the OAuth `add` endpoint into a 500. This code path is exercised only on path renames in this PR, but the file was moved and is part of the changed set; a `try`/`catch` returning `undefined` (matching the early-return for non-string state) would be safer. Same issue in `decodeOAuthState.ts`.

title: New webhook has no tests despite being the trust boundary for cross-instance credentials
body: The endpoint accepts encrypted credentials that fully overwrite a user's third-party OAuth tokens (potentially including refresh tokens) for any app, gated only by a single shared secret. The PR description acknowledges no tests were added. At minimum: tests for wrong/missing secret (403), unknown user (404), unknown app (404), invalid encrypted payload (4xx, not 500), missing/short encryption key, and concurrent writes for the same (userId, appId) should exist before merge.

title: refreshOAuthTokens returns incompatible types based on sync flag
body: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, this function calls fetch(...) and returns the fetch Response object. Otherwise it returns whatever refreshFunction() returns (which is provider-specific: a GaxiosResponse for googlecalendar, a HubspotToken for hubspot, an AxiosResponse for zoho-bigin/zohocrm, a fetch Response for office365calendar/office365video/webex/zoomvideo/larkcalendar). Callers then assume the returned value has the same shape as refreshFunction()'s return: e.g. googlecalendar does `res?.data` (GaxiosResponse.data) which is undefined on a fetch Response; hubspot reads `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` (does not exist on a Response); zoho-bigin reads `tokenInfo.data.error` (axios response shape). Whenever the sync flag is enabled, these integrations will throw at runtime and break OAuth flows. The function must either always return a normalized shape (e.g. parsed JSON) or be split into two functions so callers know which shape they get.

title: parseRefreshTokenResponse writes literal 'refresh_token' string into saved credentials
body: When `refresh_token` is missing from the parsed response the function does `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`, mutating the parsed object. Callers then persist this object back into the Credential row (see googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97-101, office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:263-273 which spreads tokenResponse.data over o365AuthCredentials). The literal string "refresh_token" is saved as the OAuth refresh token. The next refresh attempt will send that string to Google/Microsoft/etc. and fail, and users have no way to recover without manually editing the DB. The function should either leave refresh_token alone (and let the caller decide what to do) or reject the response as invalid.

title: minimumTokenResponseSchema's dynamic keys are no-ops in Zod
body: `z.object({ [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional() })` does not do what the comments claim. The bracketed expressions are evaluated once at schema creation time and resolve to the string `"ZodString"` (or similar), so this is effectively a single extra key "ZodString" on the object. It does not enforce "any property with a number is the expiry" nor does it allow arbitrary additional properties. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true the schema only requires `access_token` to be a string and otherwise accepts anything, so invalid/garbage token responses from the parent app will pass validation and be written into Cal.com's Credential table.

title: Salesforce Connection is built from the expired access token, not the freshly refreshed one
body: After the new refresh block saves `{...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: credentialKey.refresh_token}` to the DB, the immediately-following `new jsforce.Connection({ ... accessToken: credentialKey.access_token, refreshToken: credentialKey.refresh_token })` still passes the OLD access token from `credentialKey`. The connection is therefore used with the token that was just deemed expired enough to refresh. Salesforce API calls will be made with a stale token until the next request re-reads the credential from the DB, causing intermittent auth failures for bookings and contacts sync. Should be `accessToken: accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`.

title: Webhook handler accepts any HTTP method, including GET
body: The handler performs no `req.method` check, meaning GET, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, etc. all flow through the same code path and are capable of creating or updating credentials. This makes CSRF-style attacks and accidental re-triggering via browser prefetch / link previews much easier. Add an explicit check that the request method is POST (or whatever the documented method is) and return 405 otherwise.

title: Webhook secret compared with !==, vulnerable to timing attack
body: The secret check uses `req.headers[name] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. String equality short-circuits on the first differing byte, so an attacker with request-latency measurement capability (e.g. colocated on the same cloud region) can recover the secret byte-by-byte. Use a constant-time comparison such as `crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(headerValue), Buffer.from(process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET))` after length-checking.

title: Find-then-create/update is racy and will produce duplicate credentials
body: Between the `prisma.credential.findFirst` on line 62 and the subsequent `prisma.credential.create` on line 83 there is no transaction or unique constraint covering (userId, appId). Two near-simultaneous webhook deliveries for the same (userId, appSlug) will both observe no existing credential and both create one, producing duplicate credentials that later code paths (which use `findFirst`) silently ignore while the orphan still consumes app quota / shows in admin UIs. Use a single `prisma.credential.upsert` with a where clause on `(userId, appId)`, or wrap in `$transaction` with the proper unique constraint.

title: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is a string, not a boolean
body: `export const APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED = process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY;` is typed as `string | undefined` and the runtime value is either the second operand's string or the empty/falsy string `""` for the first operand. The codebase then uses `if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED) { return 403 }` and `if (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && ...)`. This works for the obvious cases but silently treats the literal string `"false"` as truthy, and is fragile if either env var is ever set to a non-empty placeholder. Coerce with `!!` (or compare against empty string) and ideally name it like a boolean.

title: Decrypt/JSON.parse failures are not caught
body: `symmetricDecrypt(...)` will throw if CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY is missing (the `|| ""` fallback produces an unusable key), and `JSON.parse` will throw on any non-JSON plaintext. Because this happens after the secret check, an unauthenticated-bypass-shaped input becomes an unhandled 500 (and in some Next.js handler configs may leak stack info). Wrap the decrypt + parse in try/catch and return 400 with a non-leaky message; also early-return 503 when CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY is unset.

title: redirectUri hardcodes 'zoho-bigin' instead of appConfig.slug
body: The diff replaces `WEBAPP_URL + \`/api/integrations/${appConfig.slug}/callback\`` with `WEBAPP_URL + \`/api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback\``. If appConfig.slug ever changes or the file is copied for another app, this diverges from the rest of the file (which still uses appConfig.slug elsewhere). Either keep using `appConfig.slug` or extract a constant.

title: parseRefreshTokenResponse result spread can clobber persisted refresh_token
body: `zoomTokenSchema.safeParse(oldCredential.key)` is the existing credential, then `key.access_token = newTokens.access_token; key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token;` overwrite key with the new tokens, then `prisma.credential.update(... data: { key })`. However `key` here came from `oldCredential.key` (a parsed copy) — but the file uses the same pattern as office365calendar where tokenResponse.data (returned from parseRefreshTokenResponse) is spread. In office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264 the line `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }` will overwrite the real refresh_token with the `"refresh_token"` literal if the OAuth provider omits a new refresh_token in its response (common for many providers). Combined with finding #2, this silently breaks refresh flows.

title: turbo.json lists CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY before CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET, breaking alphabetical order
body: Minor: in the new globalEnv block, `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` is added on line 205, then `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` on 206, then `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` on 207. The surrounding block was previously alphabetical (CALCOM_ENV, CALCOM_LICENSE_KEY, CALCOM_TELEMETRY_DISABLED, CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY, CI). The new entries are inserted out of order, which makes future diffs and merges noisier without affecting behavior.

title: Salesforce refresh check uses response.statusText !== 'OK' which is unreliable
body: `if (response.statusText !== "OK")` rejects any response whose status text differs from "OK". Many proxies / HTTP/2 responses return an empty statusText, and `response.ok` is the documented boolean for status 200-299. As written, a successful 200 refresh with an empty statusText will throw `HttpError(statusCode: 400, message: '')` and the credential will not be updated. Use `if (!response.ok)` instead.

title: Permission check uses && instead of ||, locking out team admins
body: The `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. With `&&`, a user has to be both a team admin AND a team owner to pass; team admins who are not owners are rejected, and the only way to be true is effectively to be an owner. The intent (matching `booking.isUserTeamAdminOrOwner` used elsewhere in the UI) is "admin OR owner", so this should be `||`. As written, team admins without ownership cannot add guests to a team booking, even though the UI lets them open the AddGuestsDialog.

title: Case-sensitive attendee dedup creates duplicate attendees and emails
body: `uniqueGuests` is filtered with `guest === attendee.email`, a strict (case-sensitive) equality against `booking.attendees[].email`. Submitting a guest email that differs only in case from an existing attendee (e.g. "John@Example.com" vs an existing "john@example.com") passes the filter, is inserted as a new attendee row, receives a fresh AttendeeScheduledEmail, and is added to the calendar invite — producing a duplicate attendee and a duplicate confirmation for the same person. Compare emails with `guest.toLowerCase() === attendee.email.toLowerCase()` (or normalize both sides).

title: Blacklist comparison is case-sensitive, allowing bypass via mixed case
body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is normalized with `.toLowerCase()`, but the `guest` value passed to `.includes(guest)` is the raw input. A blocked address can be submitted as e.g. "Bad@Email.com" and the check will miss it, so a blacklisted guest gets added to the booking and emailed. Normalize `guest` to lower case (or store a normalized form) before the includes check.

title: Unbounded guests array is a DoS / abuse vector
body: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.min` and no `.max`. Any authenticated user (organizer, attendee, or team owner) can submit a single mutation with thousands of emails; the handler will then create that many attendees, push them to the calendar via `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`, and dispatch that many emails. There is no per-booking cap, no rate limit, and no per-user rate limit. Add a sensible `.max(...)` (e.g. 20-50) and reject larger payloads at the schema layer.

title: Handler does not deduplicate the input array itself
body: The filter only drops entries that collide with an existing attendee or that are blacklisted; it does not collapse duplicates within the submitted `guests` list. Submitting `["a@x.com", "a@x.com"]` causes `createMany` to insert two attendee rows, send two confirmation emails, and add the same address twice to the calendar. Dedupe `guests` first (e.g. via `Array.from(new Set(guests.map(g => g.toLowerCase())))`) before filtering.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails is called with original `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`
body: After computing `uniqueGuests` (which drops duplicates vs. existing attendees and blacklisted entries), the handler still passes the original `guests` array to `sendAddGuestsEmails`. Inside `sendAddGuestsEmails` the predicate `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` then misclassifies pre-existing attendees as "new" guests whenever the user resubmitted their email, sending them an unnecessary `AttendeeScheduledEmail` rather than the intended `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. Pass `uniqueGuests` (the actually-added addresses) instead.

title: No transaction around attendee insert, calendar update, and emails
body: The handler performs `prisma.booking.update` (inserts new attendees), then `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`, then `sendAddGuestsEmails` outside any transaction and without a workflow that compensates on failure. If the calendar call throws, the DB already has the new attendees but no email goes out. If the email send throws (the only step wrapped in try/catch), attendees are still committed and the calendar already has them. The whole flow should be wrapped in `prisma.$transaction` or, at minimum, the email send failure should surface a non-success result instead of being swallowed by `console.log`.

title: Email-send failures are logged with console.log and otherwise swallowed
body: The catch block does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and returns success. The caller (UI) gets a `Guests added` toast even though the notifications never went out, and the only trace is a `console.log` (which is typically not captured). Use `logger.error(...)` with the error and either return a non-success status or surface a partial-success warning to the organizer so they can re-trigger notifications.

title: No check on booking status or end time; guests can be added to cancelled/past bookings
body: The handler does not inspect `booking.status` or compare `booking.endTime` against the current time. The UI in `BookingListItem` still surfaces the "additional_guests" action on past and on cancelled bookings (the `bookedActions` array is shown for `isBookingInPast && isConfirmed`, etc.), so an organizer (or attendee) can add new attendees and trigger `AttendeeScheduledEmail` to them for events that have already happened or were cancelled. Reject mutations when the booking is CANCELLED, REJECTED, or in the past (unless the event type explicitly allows it).

title: Recurring event instances are not propagated to the series
body: If the booking belongs to a recurring event, the new attendees are only added to this single `booking` row. The other instances of the series continue to point at the original attendee list, so a guest invited to one occurrence will not appear on the parent `recurringEventId`'s other instances. The original new-guests scheduling path (`handleNewBooking`/recurring helpers) handles this; this handler does not, and will leave the series inconsistent. Either add the guest to all future instances of the recurring series or restrict the action to non-recurring bookings and surface a clear error.

title: Error toast builds string with undefined code and ignores fallback
body: `const message = \`${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}\`; showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` — when `err.data` is missing, `err.data?.code` is the string "undefined", which is truthy, so the fallback to `unable_to_add_guests` never fires and the user sees "undefined: <key>". The error toast should fall back when either `code` or the translated message is missing/empty, and the rendered string should be cleaned up (e.g. only show the code when present).

title: Team admin permission check is inverted: requires being both admin AND owner
body:
The team permission check uses `&&` instead of `||`:

```ts
const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
    (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
    (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```

This means the user must be BOTH admin AND owner to be granted permission. A team admin (who is not an owner) is incorrectly denied. The variable name and intent clearly indicate either role should be sufficient. Compare with the rest of the codebase where similar checks use `||`. As written, almost no legitimate user passes this branch unless they happen to be both.

title: Any existing attendee can add arbitrary third parties to a booking
Case-sensitive comparison against existing attendee emails allows duplicates
Calendar update uses the requesting user's credentials instead of the booking organizer's
Guests persisted to DB before calendar/email side-effects, with no rollback
body: The flow is: `prisma.booking.update` (commits new attendees) -> `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` -> `sendAddGuestsEmails` (wrapped only in a `console.log` on error). There is no transaction and no compensation. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws (e.g., bad credentials, video provider error), the guests remain in the database but never receive an invite; the caller sees a TRPC error and may retry, creating duplicates. If email sending fails it is silently swallowed, so the UI reports success while the new guest never receives notification. Either wrap everything in a transaction with rollback, or reverse the order (validate-then-side-effect-then-persist) and surface failures properly.

title: Email-sending failure is silently logged, but the mutation still returns success
Allows adding guests to cancelled or already-completed bookings
body: After loading the booking there is no check on `booking.status`. A user can add guests to a `CANCELLED`, `REJECTED`, or past `ACCEPTED` booking. `sendAddGuestsEmails` will still send a 'guests added' notification and `updateCalendarAttendees` will still push an updated invite for an event that is no longer happening. Guard against `booking.status === BookingStatus.CANCELLED` (and arguably against bookings in the past).

title: New guests are inserted with empty name and the organizer's timezone/locale
body:
Each new guest row is created with:

```ts
{ name: "", email: guest, timeZone: organizer.timeZone, locale: organizer.locale }
```

An empty `name` will render as a blank attendee in the UI (booking list, emails, calendar) and confuses no-show/dropdown flows. Also forcing the organizer's timezone/locale means the new guest's localized email content and meeting-time display are wrong. Either ask for a name in the dialog (it currently does not), or at minimum leave name nullable/derive a placeholder, and use a sensible default locale (e.g., `en`).

title: Newly added guests receive the original 'meeting scheduled' confirmation instead of an 'added to meeting' notification
`booking?.userPrimaryEmail` is not a known Booking field
body: The calendar event uses `email: booking?.userPrimaryEmail ?? organizer.email`. The Prisma `Booking` model exposes `user` (relation) and `userId`, but I cannot find a `userPrimaryEmail` column on the Booking model in this diff's context. If it doesn't exist on `booking`, this will be `undefined` and the fallback `organizer.email` is used; otherwise the column may silently return `null` and bypass the intended primary-email selection. Verify the field exists; if not, drop the `??` or fetch from the user relation explicitly.

title: addGuests uses authedProcedure instead of bookingsProcedure
body: All sibling booking mutations in this router (`editLocation`) are wrapped with `bookingsProcedure` which presumably enforces booking-level authorization. `addGuests` uses the bare `authedProcedure`, leaving all access control to the handler. The handler has the permission bugs described above, so any logged-in user who can hit this endpoint relies entirely on a handler bug-free. Switch to `bookingsProcedure` for consistency and defense-in-depth.

title: Client-side uniqueness/email validation is misleading and not exhaustive
body: The schema is `z.array(z.string().email()).refine(... unique ...)`, and a failed parse just sets `isInvalidEmail` and shows the generic 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' message.
