Even without that, there is no timeout, no size cap, no redirect policy, and no URL validation, so the worker can be made to fetch internal addresses (SSRF: localhost, link-local IPs, AWS metadata endpoint `169.254.169.254`, etc.), or to hang on a slow peer. Replace with an HTTP client such as `Net::HTTP`/`Faraday` with an explicit timeout, an address whitelist, and an internal-IP blocklist.

title: Kernel#open on remote read URL enables shell injection and SSRF
body: `doc = Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` in `import_remote` has the same problems as the feed job: `Kernel#open` allows command execution via the `|` form, and any caller able to influence `@embed_url` (or the URL registered into `TopicEmbed.embed_url`) can reach this path. Add the same mitigations: use `Net::HTTP`/`URI.open` with an explicit timeout, an internal-IP blocklist, and a follow-redirects policy.

title: PollFeed executed inline, blocking the embed worker
body: `perform_retrieve` invokes `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously inside the worker handling `RetrieveTopic`. PollFeed downloads the full RSS feed and imports every item, which can take minutes; doing it inline blocks the worker and serialises all embed retrievals behind the feed poll. If `feed_polling_enabled?` is true, any number of concurrent embed retrievals will all race to call PollFeed in parallel (no lock), causing duplicate feed downloads. Either enqueue the poll as a separate Sidekiq job (and reuse the existing `feed_key` cache to coalesce) or drop the inline call and rely on the scheduled job to have populated the cache.

title: NoMethodError when feed item has no content
body: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` will raise `NoMethodError: undefined method scrub for nil` if any feed item omits `content` (or yields a nilable value depending on the feed shape). `i.title` is also passed straight into `TopicEmbed.import` and is rendered later as a topic title — a nil title causes a validation failure that propagates. Use `(i.content || '').scrub` and guard against nil titles.

title: feed_key helper is unused dead code
body: `feed_key` (memoising `"feed-modified:#{Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)}"`) is defined on `Jobs::PollFeed` but is never referenced anywhere in the codebase. Either delete it or wire it into the poll to actually skip duplicates (which would also help fix the inline-invocation problem in `lib/topic_retriever.rb`).

title: Stored XSS via unescaped embed_url interpolated into raw_html post
body:
TopicEmbed#import builds a trailing reference by interpolating the caller-controlled url directly into an HTML attribute and text node: `contents << "
#{I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")} "`. The url argument originates from arbitrary RSS items (PollFeed) or remote article fetches (import_remote), so an attacker controlling the feed/article can put characters like `'`, `>`, `"` into url to break out of the attribute or the link text. Because the contents are then stored as a post with `cook_method: raw_html` (which skips PrettyText/Markdown sanitization entirely, see app/models/post.rb#cook), the HTML is served verbatim to anyone rendering that post. Consequence: persistent XSS in Discourse via crafted RSS/ATOM items.

title: XSS in embed layout: HTML-escaped referer inside a JS string literal
body: The postMessage call interpolates `request.referer` into a single-quoted JS string with `<%= request.referer %>`, which only HTML-escapes output. Inside `<script>`, HTML entities such as `'` are unescaped by the JS parser back to `'` before execution, so a parent page can supply a referer like `https://x'); alert(1); //` and execute attacker JS in the embed iframe. The whole script must be emitted with JS-string-escaping (CGI.escape / json_escape or equivalent) rather than the default HTML escape, e.g. by using `j` and a JSON-encoded value or by replacing `'` with `\'`.

title: Migration backfills cook_method=1 (raw_html) for every post, breaking cooking pipeline
body: `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` sets the integer 1 as the default for all existing rows and for every future insert that omits cook_method. But `Post.cook_methods` is defined as `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` in app/models/post.rb, where the Enum assigns sequential indices starting at 0, so `:regular == 0` and `:raw_html == 1`. The migration therefore marks every existing post as raw_html. After deployment, `before_save` (`self.cooked = cook(raw, topic_id: topic_id) unless new_record?`) calls `Post#cook`, which now short-circuits to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, so the first edit on any previously-rendered post overwrites `cooked` with raw markdown and breaks rendering for that post and every post that quotes/redisplays it.

title: Post.cook short-circuits to raw_html because the migration default points at the raw_html enum value
body: `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` is gated on the raw_html enum value, but the DB default set by the new migration (default: 1) and every PostCreator call that does not explicitly pass `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:regular]` will land on raw_html. Combined with the migration defaulting all rows to 1, every legacy post and every default-created post loses its cooked HTML. The intent appears to be that `raw_html` is opt-in (only the embed/RSS import path sets it), so the enum value used for the column default must be `:regular` (0) and any feed/import caller should pass the raw_html value explicitly. Right now, both kinds of writes converge on raw_html, corrupting posts.

title: TopicRetriever invokes scheduled feed poll synchronously inside an embed job
body: `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` is called inline inside `perform_retrieve` whenever `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true. PollFeed is a recurring scheduled job that fetches the full configured RSS/ATOM feed and imports every item; running it synchronously inside an embed fetch blocks the worker for the full poll duration, doubles the load on the feed endpoint (once from the scheduled worker, once from each embed call), and re-imports items outside the dedup logic embedded in TopicEmbed.import. It should enqueue the scheduled job via Sidekiq or at minimum only check `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: ...)` without triggering a full re-poll.

title: NoMethodError when SiteSetting.embed_by_username is blank
body: `User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first` calls `.downcase` on the setting value without first verifying it is non-nil. PollFeed guards against this with the `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.present?` check, but `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` does not, so a missing setting raises NoMethodError, which propagates out of the retrieve_topic job. Guard with `return if SiteSetting.embed_by_username.blank?` like PollFeed does.

title: NoMethodError or encoding crash on RSS items missing content
body: `i.content.scrub` assumes `i.content` is a String that responds to scrub. SimpleRSS may leave `content` nil for entries without a `<content>` element, in which case the lookup raises NoMethodError on nil and aborts the entire poll (also no per-item rescue). On top of that, the surrounding code never validates the feed URL protocol, content type, or item count, and never catches network or parse errors, so a single malformed item or transient feed failure kills the whole job. Add nil guards (`i.content.to_s.scrub`) and per-item exception handling.

title: Referer-based authorization is fragile and bypassable
body: `ensure_embeddable` only checks `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. The Referer header is freely spoofable in many environments (browsers with privacy extensions, server-side fetchers, embedded webviews, curl), it can be wholly absent (in which case the empty string still passes URI parsing and compares mismatched, denying the request), and the comparison is a plain string match that ignores ports/scheme. An attacker able to set Referer (or to load the embed URL from a non-browser context) can pretend to come from any host. Authorization must not rely on a header that the configured embeddable host cannot enforce, and should additionally match scheme/port (e.g. compare `host_with_port` and `scheme`). At minimum, the current check must be paired with a signed/shared-secret or signed embed_url before the controller will fetch arbitrary content from the Discourse server.

title: force: true silently drops and recreates the top_topics table
body: Changing `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` makes the migration drop any pre-existing `top_topics` table before recreating it. The migration was previously already shipped to production; if any environment has a partially applied state, the next migration run will silently destroy data. Either drop the existing migration in favor of a new one that no-ops for upgrades, or document that this change must run on a clean DB only.

title: postMessage origin check uses indexOf substring match
body: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` checks whether `e.origin` appears anywhere inside `discourseUrl` rather than comparing the origin exactly. Even though discourseUrl is configured by the embedding site, a confused deployer can be tricked into rejecting legitimate messages or accepting unexpected ones if the configured URL embeds other origins as substrings. Use `discourseUrl.startsWith(e.origin + '/')` or compare origins directly.

title: Unused require_dependency 'email/sender'
body: The job requires `email/sender` but never references it (and TopicRetriever does not either). Remove the unused dependency to avoid loading unnecessary code paths and to prevent surprising coupling when email/Sender changes.

title: Tests do not cover the perform_retrieve (SSRF and dedup) paths
body: The spec only exercises the gated path through `retrieve` and asserts that `perform_retrieve` is or isn't called. There is no coverage of `perform_retrieve`, `fetch_http`, the `Jobs::PollFeed` invocation, or the duplicate-embed short-circuit. SSRF (fetching arbitrary URLs via `import_remote`) and the dedup queries are security-/data-integrity-sensitive and should have explicit specs covering the host check inside perform_retrieve, the user lookup, and the `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url:).exists?` early-return.

title: Embed URL injected raw into HTML, enabling XSS in the rendered embed view
body: The embed URL is interpolated unescaped into both the href attribute and the link text via I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}"). Imported posts are persisted with cook_method = :raw_html and the embed view renders their HTML through `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so the appended markup is emitted verbatim into the discourse origin. An embed URL containing a single quote, a newline, an `on*=` payload, or a `javascript:` scheme (originating from any RSS item, from a CMS at SiteSetting.embeddable_host, or from any direct caller of TopicEmbed.import) breaks out of the `` attribute and runs attacker-supplied HTML/JS. The call also mutates the caller's `contents` string in place via `<<`, which can break frozen-string inputs and corrupts the caller's data. Use Rails' link_to(url) (or html_escape) and build the suffix into a separate String instead of mutating `contents`.

title: <%- end if %> is a SyntaxError in Ruby ERB and will prevent the embed view from rendering
body: Line 6 closes the first if/else block with `  <%- end if %>`. Inside ERB that compiles to the literal Ruby `end if`, whose `if` modifier requires a condition expression. With no condition following `if`, Ruby's parser raises a SyntaxError the first time the view is compiled, so any request that reaches `best.html.erb` (i.e., any embedded topic that has been imported) will blow up instead of rendering. The other if/else in this same file (lines 11, 22, 29) closes with plain `<%- end %>`, confirming that this is a stray ` if` typo. Replace with `<%- end %>`.

title: X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL is not a recognized directive
body: The action unconditionally sets `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"`. The only valid X-Frame-Options values are DENY, SAMEORIGIN and the deprecated ALLOW-FROM <uri>. Browsers will silently ignore "ALLOWALL" and fall back to their default framing policy, so unless an equivalent Content-Security-Policy `frame-ancestors *` is set, the very framing that the embed feature was built to enable will be blocked in modern browsers. Use CSP `frame-ancestors *` (or remove this header and rely on CSP) instead.

title: postMessage origin check uses substring indexOf instead of a real origin comparison
body: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` only confirms that e.origin appears as a substring of discourseUrl. Any e.origin that is a substring of whatever `discourseUrl` is configured to (including future paths/queries/cached redirects) will pass the gate and be allowed to set `iframe.height` or drive other future message handlers. Use `new URL(discourseUrl).origin === e.origin` (or compare parsed origins via the postMessage API's own origin field) so the handler accepts only the configured Discourse origin.

title: PollFeed job aborts the entire hourly run on the first item or network failure
body: Inside the `rss.items.each` loop, `i.content.scrub` raises on a nil/Non-String item content, `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` raises on any transient network or HTTP error, and `TopicEmbed.import` raises on URL-regex mismatch or Nokogiri errors from `absolutize_urls`. Combined with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, one malformed item or one bad network response silently drops every subsequent item in the feed until the next hourly cron — and the exceptions are lost because the `feed_polling_enabled?` guard never runs around the loop. Wrap each item (and the open/parse) in begin/rescue, validate i.link/i.id/i.title/i.content up front, and log per-item errors so a single bad entry does not poison the entire run.

title: feed_key helper is dead code
body: The class defines `feed_key` (computing `"feed-modified:#{Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)}"`) but never references it. Either wire it into the poll path (e.g., a per-feed HTTP If-Modified-Since/last-modified check, or a rate-limit key to avoid re-importing unchanged items) or remove the unused method to avoid the impression that per-feed change detection exists.

title: request.referer is interpolated into a JS context without j/JS escaping
body: `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')` relies on Rails default HTML escaping inside a JavaScript string literal. While `'` happens to be escaped in a way that is inert inside a `<script>` block today, the correct helper for a value going into a JS string literal is `j request.referer` (or escaping explicitly for targetOrigin). The embed controller deliberately lets attacker-controllable URLs reach the referer header, so passing that value to postMessage's targetOrigin should be JS-escaped so that backslashes/control bytes produced by a hostile header cannot break the JS string or smuggle a different targetOrigin.

title: Throttle uses non-atomic SETNX + EXPIRE, which can leak a permanent key
body: `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)` leaves a brief window in which the key exists with no TTL. If the second command is lost (network blip, sidekiq preemption, Redis failover) the key has no expiry and permanently blocks retrievals for that URL. Use the atomic `SET key 1 NX EX 60` form instead.

title: TopicEmbed.import_remote (external URL fetch + ruby-readability) is not exercised
body: import_remote performs `open(url).read`, runs ruby-readability with the specific tags/attributes allowlist, and forwards the result into import. It is the highest-risk entry point in this PR (SSRF surface, hang on slow hosts, content that ends up as raw_html posts) and is reachable from both TopicRetriever#fetch_http and the disqus.thor import task. The new spec only covers import(), so any regression in the allowlist, the host contract, or the read/open behaviour would slip through.

title: poll_feed body (RSS item iteration, normalisation, TopicEmbed.import integration) is uncovered
body: The new spec only verifies the three guard conditions in execute() (feed_polling_enabled?, feed_polling_url present, embed_by_username present). The actual poll_feed body that parses the feed, falls back from i.link to i.id, runs CGI.unescapeHTML + i.content.scrub, and calls TopicEmbed.import per item is the section this review flagged as fragile (nil item fields, scrub failures, regex mismatch on id fallback) and is not tested at all.

title: Invalid CSS property -webkit-order in order mixin
body: The `order` mixin outputs `-webkit-order: $val;` on line 129, but no browser ever shipped an `-webkit-order` property. The 2009 WebKit flexbox spec used `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` (already emitted on line 126) and the 2012/modern spec uses the unprefixed `order` (emitted on line 130). The `-webkit-order` declaration is dead/invalid CSS and should be removed.

title: Invalid CSS property -ms-align-items in align-items mixin
body: The `align-items` mixin outputs `-ms-align-items: $alignment;` on line 121, but IE10/IE11 implement `align-items` as `-ms-flex-align` (already emitted on line 120). There is no `-ms-align-items` property in any CSS specification; the declaration is invalid and will be ignored by every browser. It should be removed.

title: Bullet badge vertical alignment likely broken in extra-info-wrapper
body: The change adds `line-height: 1.5` to `.extra-info-wrapper` and removes the `&.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` rule that previously compensated for the bullet badge's vertical positioning inside this wrapper. The bullet badge in `badges.css.scss` is an `inline-flex` element with `align-items: baseline`; with the new explicit `line-height: 1.5` on the parent, the baseline metric changes and the deleted 5px top margin will cause the bullet to sit visibly higher (or lower) relative to the surrounding text, producing a vertical misalignment regression for category bullets in the topic header.

title: .small-action-desc loses left indent that compensated for the avatar
body: The `.small-action-desc` padding was changed from `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em; margin-top: 5px;` to `padding: 0 1.5%`. While the parent is now a flex container and the floated 45px avatar no longer overlaps the text, removing the 4em left indent means the description text now starts directly against the avatar (separated only by the default 0px flex gap and the small 1.5% inner padding). The old 4em indent was visually meaningful; the new layout will look noticeably more cramped, and the 0 vertical padding combined with `align-items: center` removes all internal breathing room around the description text. This is a visual regression even if no overlap occurs.

title: Invalid CSS property `-ms-align-items` emitted by align-items mixin
body: The mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`, which is not a valid CSS property. The IE10 vendor prefix for align-items is `-ms-flex-align` (already included on the preceding line). Sass will compile this and ship it to the browser, where it is parsed as an unknown declaration and ignored. It also fails strict CSS validation and can produce warnings in tooling. The line should be removed.

title: `order: 2` applied to a non-flex child has no effect
body: `@include order(2)` is added to `.extra-info-wrapper`, but its parent `.title-wrapper` is styled in this same file as `float: left; width: 90%;` and is not a flex container. The `order` property only affects flex/grid items, so this declaration is dead CSS in the rendered output. If the intent was to reorder `.extra-info-wrapper` relative to the title, the author likely also needs `@include flexbox()` on `.title-wrapper` (and an explicit order for the other children). Otherwise the line should be removed because it implies a layout change that will not happen.

title: Invalid -ms-align-items property in align-items mixin
body: The new `align-items` mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`, which is not a valid CSS property. The only IE10-prefixed property for alignment is `-ms-flex-align` (already emitted on line 120). The invalid `-ms-align-items` declaration is silently ignored by browsers and is dead CSS.

title: Invalid -moz-inline-box value in inline-flex mixin
body: The new `inline-flex` mixin emits `display: -moz-inline-box;`, but Firefox never implemented an inline variant of its legacy `-moz-box` model — only the block-level `-moz-box` existed. The declaration is a no-op and adds noise; consumers of this mixin on legacy Gecko get neither the legacy flex nor a working inline-flex because `-moz-box` (the only Moz box value) is not emitted.

title: Invalid -webkit-order property in order mixin
body: The new `order` mixin emits `-webkit-order: $val;`, which is not a CSS property that any WebKit-based browser has ever shipped. The legacy WebKit property is `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` (already emitted on line 126). The `-webkit-order` declaration is dead CSS and should be removed.

title: Trailing whitespace inside align-items mixin
body: Line 120 (`-ms-flex-align: $alignment;  `) contains trailing whitespace after the semicolon. While cosmetic, it will appear verbatim in every compiled stylesheet that uses this mixin and is inconsistent with the rest of the file.

title: include_website_name method (without ?) is dead code; website_name not in untrusted_attributes
body: The serializer framework (ActiveModel::Serializer) looks for `include_website_name?` (with `?`) to determine if the attribute should be included. The manually defined `include_website_name` (without `?`) on line 153 is never called by the framework. It should either be renamed to `include_website_name?` (with `?`) or removed. Additionally, `website_name` is not in the `untrusted_attributes` list (line 105-111), so the auto-generated `include_website_name?` is not created. As a result, the `website_name` attribute is always included in the serialization (since `include_website_name?` is not defined, the framework includes it by default), which is inconsistent with the `website` attribute handling (which is in the `untrusted_attributes` list and hidden for TL0 users seen by anonymous). For TL0 users, the value would be nil, so it's not a privacy issue, but the inconsistency is a code quality concern.

title: URI(website.to_s) is parsed multiple times
body: The `URI()` parsing is done 2-3 times in the `website_name` method (lines 138, 143, 146, 149). It should be cached in a local variable to avoid redundant parsing on every serialization. For example: `uri = URI(website.to_s)` and then use `uri.host` and `uri.path`.

title: NoMethodError if Discourse.current_hostname is nil
body: The `elsif` condition on line 144 calls `discourse_host.split('.').length`, which would raise `NoMethodError` if `discourse_host` is nil (e.g., in a background job or rake task where `Discourse.current_hostname` is not set). The method should handle the case where `Discourse.current_hostname` is nil, e.g., by returning just the `website_host` or treating the nil case as a non-match.

title: Missing tests for edge cases in website_name
body: The tests only cover three cases: different domain (discourse.org vs example.com), same domain (example.com vs example.com), and parent domain (forums.example.com vs example.com). Missing tests include: URL with port (e.g., http://example.com:8080/user), URL with query string (e.g., http://example.com/user?foo=bar), URL with fragment (e.g., http://example.com/user#section), URL with encoded characters, URL with different protocol (https vs http), URL with subdomain of instance domain (e.g., blog.forums.example.com for forums.example.com), URL with subdomain of website domain (e.g., forums.example.com for blog.example.com), URL with nil website, and URL with invalid website.

title: Subdomain matching logic may not handle all valid cases
body: The `elsif` branch only matches when both hosts have the same number of parts AND more than 2 parts. This misses cases like `a.b.example.com` (4 parts) vs `b.example.com` (3 parts) where the website is a subdomain of the instance domain. The `else` branch's `ends_with?` check handles this case, but the logic is split across two branches in a non-obvious way. Consider simplifying the logic or adding a comment explaining the cases.

title: include_website_name predicate missing '?' suffix
body: The new predicate `def include_website_name` is defined without the trailing question mark, breaking the ActiveModel::Serializer convention used by every other include_* method in this file (include_email?, include_stats?, include_suspend_reason?, include_card_image_badge?, etc.). ActiveModel::Serializer looks specifically for `include_<attr>?` to gate attribute serialization. As a result the predicate is never invoked and `website_name` is always included in the serialized JSON whenever the attribute is defined, regardless of the intended `website.present?` check. This also defeats any future attempt to gate website_name exposure (e.g. for TL0 users via untrusted_attributes, since the predicate won't fire).

title: Missing test for the 'same suffix, equal part count > 2' branch
body: The new `website_name` implementation has three branches (exact match, `www.example.com == forum.example.com` style same-suffix with equal part count > 2, and parent-domain suffix). The spec only exercises the first and third (`Discourse.stubs(:current_hostname).returns('example.com')` and `...('forums.example.com')`); the elsif branch with two 3-part hosts sharing a suffix (e.g. `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`, both returning the full path) has no test, so a regression there would not be caught.

title: URI(website.to_s) parsed three times per call
body: `website_name` calls `URI(website.to_s)` three times to extract `.host` and `.path`. Since `website` is a method that reads `object.user_profile.website`, the value is stable across calls within one invocation, but parsing the URL three times is wasteful and makes the logic fragile: any future change that makes `website` non-deterministic (e.g., conditional computation) would cause `.host` and `.path` to be taken from different URLs. Hoisting `uri = URI(website.to_s)` (inside the existing `rescue`) into a local would fix both concerns.

title: include_website_name missing trailing question mark
body: The new method `def include_website_name` is missing the trailing `?`. ActiveModel::Serializer's inclusion check probes for `include_<attr>?`; because the method is named `include_website_name` (no `?`), the serializer never calls it and `website_name` is unconditionally included in the JSON payload even when `website` is blank (where it ends up as a noisy `null`). It should be `def include_website_name?`. The rest of the file (and the `untrusted_attributes`/`private_attributes`/`staff_attributes` macros) consistently use the `include_<attr>?` form, confirming the expected convention.

title: website_name leaks info that should be hidden for TL0 users
body: `website_name` is added to the public `attributes` list but is not registered as an `untrusted_attribute` next to `:website`. `untrusted_attributes` is what hides fields from anonymous viewers looking at TL0 (new) users via `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`. Because `website_name` is derived from `website` (it is exactly the host, and the path when domains match), hiding `website` while exposing `website_name` defeats the purpose of that filter: an anonymous visitor can still read `example.com/user` for any TL0 user. `:website_name` should be added to the `untrusted_attributes :bio_raw, :bio_cooked, :bio_excerpt, :location, :website, :profile_background, :card_background` list, and the matching spec assertion in `spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb` should be extended to assert `website_name` is absent for the TL0/anonymous context.

title: URI(...).path drops query string and fragment
body: `URI(...).path` returns only the path component, so any `?query` and `#fragment` parts of the user's stored website URL are silently discarded when building `website_name` (e.g. `http://example.com/user?ref=foo` becomes `example.com/user`). If the intent of the PR is to show the "complete URL path", `URI(...).request_uri` (or path + query + fragment) should be used so query parameters and anchors are preserved.

title: URI(website.to_s) parsed multiple times
body: `URI(website.to_s)` is parsed three separate times inside `website_name` (once for `host`, then again twice for `.path`). On a hot serializer called for every user payload, this is wasteful and harder to read. The URI object should be parsed once into a local variable and `host`/`path` (or `request_uri`) read from it.

title: Missing coverage for several branches of website_name
body: The new specs only exercise three cases (different 2-part host, identical host, subdomain/parent 3-part host). They do not cover: (a) the second branch where both hosts have the same number of parts greater than two (e.g. `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`) and a non-matching second-level label; (b) websites whose path includes a query string or fragment, to verify whether they are preserved or dropped; (c) websites with a non-default port; (d) websites whose scheme is missing or unparseable, to verify the `rescue nil` path doesn't leak garbage. None of these are covered by the existing TL0/untrusted test either, so the privacy regression on `:website_name` going through without `untrusted_attributes` is also untested.

title: $primary lightness changed from 30% to 70% (visual regression on light themes)
body: The PR pattern is to preserve the $primary lightness and only add a $secondary variant for dark themes, e.g. `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` → `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. This line breaks that pattern: `.topic-meta-data h5 a` originally was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` (a very dark color used for bold inline links inside topic meta data on the topic page). After the change it becomes `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, so on light themes the link is now a much lighter shade (lightness 70 instead of 30), making the bold link fade against light backgrounds — a clear visual regression. Should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

title: .group-member-info .name $primary lightness changed from 30% to 50%
body: Inside `.user-main .user-stream .group-member-info`, `.name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and was changed to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. This makes the user's name lighter on light themes than before (30% → 50%) and no longer matches the sibling `.title` (also 50/50) — the original intent was clearly to keep `.name` darker than `.title`. Should mirror the value, e.g. `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

title: .group-member-info .name $primary lightness changed from 30% to 50%
body: Same bug as the desktop counterpart: `.group-member-info .name` originally `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. On mobile light themes, group-member names are now lighter than they were, diverging from `.title` which remains 50/50. Should preserve the 30% lightness for the light theme branch.

title: .topic-map h3 $primary lightness changed from 20% to 50%
body: The mobile `.topic-map h3` rule originally `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%);` is converted to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The desktop equivalent in `desktop/topic-post.scss` correctly keeps the 20% primary value (`dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`). On mobile light themes, this header is now significantly lighter (50% vs 20%), reducing contrast against the light topic-map background. Should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))` to match desktop behavior.

title: .custom-message-length $primary lightness inverted (70% → 30%)
body: `.custom-message-length` originally `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%);` is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The desktop counterpart in `desktop/modal.scss` correctly preserves 70% for the primary branch (`dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`). On mobile light themes, the character-count hint becomes a very dark color (30%) instead of the original muted/lighter shade (70%), making it visually inconsistent with the desktop modal and harder to read as a hint. Should mirror the value rather than invert it: `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`.

title: Light theme color regression in .topic-meta-data h5 a
body: Original: `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);`. Changed to: `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%));`. The PR's stated goal is to add dark-theme support without altering light theme rendering, but here the light-theme branch now uses 70% lightness instead of 30%, producing a markedly lighter text in light mode (visual regression). The dark-theme branch is also wrong: with the original light value of 30% (a darker shade), the symmetric dark-theme value should be `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)`, not 30%, so dark mode will render the text too dim against a dark background.

title: Light theme color regression in .custom-message-length
body: Original: `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%);`. Changed to: `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%));`. The light-theme branch was changed from 70% to 30%, the inverse of the original. Compared with the desktop counterpart (`desktop/modal.scss` line 94) which correctly preserves 70% for the primary branch and uses 30% for secondary, this file has the values swapped: in light mode the text will now be much darker than before, and in dark mode it will be much lighter than intended.

title: Light theme color regression in .topic-map h3
body: Original: `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%);`. Changed to: `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));`. The light-theme value was changed from 20% to 50%, making the heading noticeably lighter in light mode. The matching desktop file (`desktop/topic-post.scss` line 321) keeps 20% for primary and uses 80% for secondary, which is the correct pattern. The dark-theme value is also wrong here (should be 80% to keep prominence on a dark background, not 50%).

title: Light theme color regression in .group-member-info .name
body: Original: `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);`. Changed to: `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));`. The light-theme value was changed from 30% to 50%, making the name text lighter in light mode. The dark-theme value should be 70% (to mirror the original 30% prominence on a dark background) but is 50%. The matching `.title` rule one block below correctly uses 50%/50% symmetric values because its original was already 50%.

title: Light theme color regression in .group-member-info .name
body: Original: `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);`. Changed to: `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));`. The light-theme value was changed from 30% to 50%, lightening the name text in light mode. The dark-theme value should be 70% (mirroring the original 30% prominence on dark backgrounds) but is 50%. This is inconsistent with the sibling `.title` rule directly below, which correctly uses 50%/50% because its original lightness was already 50%.

title: Light theme color regression in .group-member-info .name
body: Original: `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);`. Changed to: `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));`. The light-theme value was changed from 30% to 50%, lightening the name text. The dark-theme value should be 70% to maintain similar prominence on a dark background, but is 50%. Same pattern as the parallel bugs in desktop/user.scss line 522 and mobile/topic-post.scss line 497.

title: Primary lightness flipped from 70% to 30% in light mode
body: The change replaces `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The PR's intent (visible throughout the diff) is to keep the light-theme primary lightness the same and only add a complementary secondary for dark themes (e.g. desktop/modal.scss line 94 does 70%/30%). Here the primary value was flipped instead, so `.custom-message-length` text in light mode now renders at 30% lightness instead of the original 70%, producing a much darker color than before.

title: Primary lightness flipped from 30% to 70% in light mode
body: Inside `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a`, the change replaces `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. Following the convention used elsewhere in the PR (primary lightness preserved, secondary set to the complement, e.g. the next `.arrow` rule on line 294 does 60%/40%), this should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. In light mode the link color is now much lighter than before.

title: Group member name color: primary value altered from 30% to 50%
body: Inside `.group-member-info .name`, the change replaces `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. Every other transformation in this PR keeps the primary lightness identical to the original and uses the complement only for `$secondary` (e.g. `.title` immediately below correctly stays at 50%/50% on line 527 because its original was already 50%). Here the primary went from 30% to 50%, so group-member names on user pages render with a noticeably lighter color in light mode.

title: Topic-map h3 color: primary value altered from 20% to 50%
body: Inside `.topic-map h3`, the change replaces `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The PR's pattern (see the sibling `.topic-map h4` rule on line 190, which correctly keeps its 50% original) is to leave the primary lightness unchanged and pick the complement for `$secondary`. This one was copied from the h4 rule, so in light mode the topic-map h3 headings now appear far lighter (50%) than they were (20%).

title: Group member name color (mobile): primary value altered from 30% to 50%
body: Inside `.group-member-info .name`, the change replaces `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. This is the mobile counterpart of the same pattern bug in desktop/user.scss line 522; it appears the rule was copy-pasted from the sibling `.title` selector (whose original lightness really was 50%). Group-member names on mobile user pages now render at 50% lightness in light mode instead of the original 30%, making them visibly lighter.

title: add_members and remove_member read group id from a param the route never sets
body: The new routes are defined as `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` and `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` inside `resources :groups` but outside a `collection do` block, making them member routes that generate `/admin/groups/:id/members` with the group id in `params[:id]`. The controller actions, however, call `Group.find(params.require(:group_id).to_i)` (line 66 in add_members and line 85 in remove_member). The production client in `discourse/models/group.js` hits `/admin/groups/<id>/members.json` with no `group_id` body parameter, so `params.require(:group_id)` always raises `ActionController::ParameterMissing`, returning a 400. The actual add/remove logic in these actions never runs in production.

title: Spec test uses wrong HTTP verb for remove_member
body: The test `it "cannot remove members from automatic groups"` calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42`. The route is `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`, so a PUT to action `remove_member` does not match any defined route. Rails raises `ActionController::UrlGenerationError` (or returns 404), not 422, so the test cannot pass and gives no real coverage of the automatic-group behavior.

title: add_members/remove_member specs do not match the actual route URLs
body: All new specs invoke the action by name with body params, e.g. `xhr :put, :add_members, group_id: group.id, usernames: ...` (line 103) and `xhr :delete, :remove_member, group_id: group.id, user_id: user.id` (line 125). The routes are member routes with URL `/admin/groups/:id/members`, so the URL helper `member_admin_group_path(id)` requires `:id`. The tests only supply `group_id` in the body, so the helper cannot generate a URL and each request raises `ActionController::UrlGenerationError`. These tests do not exercise the routes the JS actually hits, and even fixing the controller to use `params[:id]` will not make them pass.

title: findMembers has no in-flight tracking and can clobber pagination state
body: findMembers reads `offset`/`user_count` from the model, fires an AJAX request, and on response overwrites those properties with the server-provided values. The new admin template wires prev/next actions directly to findMembers with no request token, last-write-wins check, or debouncing. If a user clicks "next" twice quickly, two requests are in flight and responses can arrive out of order: a slow first-page response that returns after the second-page response will overwrite the model back to the first page, leaving the UI inconsistent with what the user clicked.

title: add_members silently drops unknown usernames with no feedback
body: `usernames.split(",").each do |username| ... if user = User.find_by_username(username) ... end` skips any unresolved username silently, and the action returns `success_json` regardless of how many (zero, one, or all) usernames actually matched. The admin UI triggers this from an "Add" button with no per-user feedback, so an admin who types a typo (e.g. "jonh" instead of "john") gets a 200 response and an unchanged member count, with no signal that the input was invalid.

title: Stray closing div inside each loop produces malformed DOM
body: Inside `{{#each m in members}}`, line 19 contains a `` with no matching opening div in the loop body (the iteration body only contains `...`). The diff for this file only changes `model` to `members` on line 6, so the tag is pre-existing, but the file is part of this change set. It produces DOM that doesn't match the surrounding `` structure and should be removed.

title: Username selector not cleared after a successful add
body: The `addMembers` action carries a `// TODO: should clear the input` comment but never resets `usernames`. Membership changes used to flow through `saveWithUsernames`/`createWithUsernames`; now the only path that accepts usernames is this `addMembers` action, which leaves the typed names in the input. The next click on "Add" re-submits the same list unless the admin manually clears the field, and there is no client-side signal that the prior submission succeeded.

title: Admin group add_members/remove_member read :group_id but the router only sets :id
body: The new routes `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` and `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` are declared at the top level of `resources :groups, constraints: AdminConstraint.new do ... end` (i.e., not inside a `collection do` block), so Rails generates them as MEMBER routes `PUT/DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members`. The corresponding JS (`Discourse.ajax('/admin/groups/' + this.get('id') + '/members.json', ...)`) matches those URLs, so the param that holds the group id is `params[:id]`. However, both new actions read the group with `Group.find(params.require(:group_id).to_i)` (line 66 for add_members, line 85 for remove_member). Because `params[:group_id]` is never populated by the router, every real PUT/DELETE from the admin UI will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` and the add/remove member functionality will be completely broken in production. The controller specs pass because RSpec controller specs bypass routing and inject `group_id:` directly into the params hash, which is exactly the test gap that hides this bug. Either change the actions to read `params[:id]`/`params.require(:id)`, or add a `:group_id` segment to the routes.

title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
body: `totalPages` returns `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`. For any group whose member count is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 50 users with the default 50/page, or 100 users, etc.) this evaluates to one more page than actually exists. As a result `showingLast` stays false on the real last page and the "next" control is rendered enabled. Clicking it then sends `findMembers` with an `offset` that is clamped to `user_count` by `Math.min(group.get("offset") + group.get("limit"), group.get("user_count"))`, so the server returns zero rows and the user lands on an empty trailing page that the pagination arrows can never get them back out of. The intended formula is `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

title: addMembers never clears usernames and never reports errors
body: The action body just calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"))` and ignores the returned promise. The `// TODO: should clear the input` comment acknowledges the problem: after a successful add, the user-selector still contains the same text, so a second click re-submits the same usernames (silently de-duplicated server-side but still wasteful and confusing). Because no `.then`/`.catch` is wired up either, any failure from the underlying PUT (e.g. the parameter bug described above, or a validation error) is swallowed: the spinner clears, the input keeps the value, and the admin gets no feedback at all. The input should be cleared on success and any error should be surfaced.

title: add_members splits usernames on comma without trimming or rejecting blanks
body: `usernames.split(",").each do |username| ... User.find_by_username(username)` is called verbatim on each substring. If the user-selector ever produces a name with surrounding whitespace (e.g. `"alice , bob"` or stray trailing whitespace from an autocomplete suggestion), `User.find_by_username(" alice ")` returns nil and the entry is silently dropped — the request still returns `success_json`, the admin sees "added" and no user was actually added. The code should also explicitly skip blank entries instead of relying on `find_by_username("")` returning nil. Similar trimming is performed in other parts of the app (e.g. user creation) and would be expected here.

title: Stray closing inside {{#each}} block produces malformed HTML
body:
Inside `{{#each m in members}}` there is a literal `` on line 19 with no matching opening `
`, all of which sits inside a ``/`` structure. This is leftover from a previous container-based layout that survived the model refactor. Browsers will auto-correct the DOM in inconsistent ways and it is invalid markup, so any tooling that relies on the parse tree (a11y, sanitizers, etc.) can be confused. The `` should be removed.

title: save error handler crashes on non-JSON error responses
body: On failure the controller does `var message = $.parseJSON(e.responseText).errors;`. If the server returns a non-JSON body (e.g. an HTML 500 page from an unhandled exception, a maintenance page, or an empty body for a network failure), `$.parseJSON` throws a `SyntaxError`. That throw is swallowed by the promise chain, `disableSave` is reset to false in `.finally`, and the admin sees no error message at all — the save button just becomes clickable again with no indication that anything went wrong. The handler should guard against parse failure (try/catch or typeof check) and fall back to a generic error or `e.responseText` itself.

title: add_members/remove_member specs use group_id but production only exposes :id
body: Every new spec for the two actions passes the group identifier as `group_id:` (lines 94, 103, 115, 125). RSpec controller specs bypass Rails routing and inject that key directly into `params`, so the controller's `params.require(:group_id)` succeeds and the tests pass. In production the routes (`put "members"`/`delete "members"` under `resources :groups, constraints: AdminConstraint.new`) are member routes that expose the group id as `:id`, not `:group_id`, so the same actions will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` for every real request. Either rewrite the specs as request/integration specs that actually go through the router, or pass the param as `id: group.id` (and have the controller read `params[:id]`) so that the suite exercises the real contract. The `cannot remove members from automatic groups` example also uses `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but the route only accepts DELETE for that action — that mismatch is similarly masked by the controller-spec scope.

title: totalPages math is off by one for exact multiples
body: totalPages returns Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which yields 2 for user_count=50 with limit=50, 3 for 100 users with limit=50, etc. For exact multiples the result should be (50/50), (100/50)=2, etc. The correct formula is Math.ceil(user_count / limit). With the current code the pagination label displays e.g. "1/2" for a group that actually has only one page, and showingLast becomes true only after stepping into a non-existent page. Consequence: users see an extra phantom page and may be unable to reach later real pages on groups where the count happens to be a multiple of limit.

title: {{#unless automatic}} resolves to member.automatic instead of group.automatic
body: The template is rendered inside `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`, so `this` is the iterated User record. `{{#unless automatic}}` therefore evaluates `member.automatic`, which is undefined (User has no `automatic` attribute). The remove (×) button therefore appears for every member, including members of automatic groups, where the controller already forbids removal (remove_member returns 422 for automatic groups). The intended behaviour is to hide the remove link when the surrounding Group is automatic. The render context needs to expose group.automatic (e.g. via the itemView controller, a property pushed onto each member, or by checking the parent controller).

title: params[:visible] == "true" breaks when the client sends a JSON boolean
body: The admin UI sends `visible: !!this.get('visible')` via Discourse.ajax (JSON body), so Rails parses it to a boolean `true`/`false` rather than the string "true". `true == "true"` and `false == "true"` are both false in Ruby, so the assignment becomes `group.visible = false` regardless of what the checkbox shows. As a result the visibility checkbox in the group admin form does not stick. The same pattern appears in `create` on line 25. Use a comparison that handles both, e.g. `ActiveModel::Type::Boolean.new.cast(params[:visible])` or `params[:visible].to_s == "true"`.

title: remove_member spec uses wrong HTTP verb (PUT instead of DELETE)
body: The new route is `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` (see config/routes.rb), but this test calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...`. The companion test in the same context (line 125) correctly uses `:delete`. The test as written does not actually exercise the DELETE route; if someone later changed the route to PUT it would still pass and silently break the real endpoint. Change to `xhr :delete, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42` to match the route.

title: update action is under-tested after the refactor
body: The new `.update` context only covers one scenario: an automatic group ignoring a rename. It does not test that a non-automatic group can be renamed, that alias_level is updated from params[:alias_level], or that the new model asJSON contract (no `group:` wrapper, no `usernames`) round-trips correctly. The renamed `update` no longer touches usernames, so a regression in that decoupling would not be caught.

title: add_members silently drops unknown usernames with no error to the caller
body: `User.find_by_username(username)` returns nil for unknown names and the entry is skipped without feedback. The endpoint always renders success_json even when every requested username was invalid, so the admin UI has no way to surface a partial failure. Consider returning 422 with the list of unresolved usernames when at least one is not found.

title: addMembers does not clear the usernames input after submit
body: After a successful add the controller leaves `usernames` populated (a TODO comment on the line acknowledges this). `model.addMembers` does not reset it either. Clicking Add a second time re-submits the same string and re-issues a PUT for users already in the group, which the controller treats as a no-op but still triggers an extra AJAX round-trip and a full member-list reload.

title: Mixed Symbol/String types in fallback list cause stale-cache misses
body: self[locale] returns [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]. The first element is whatever locale was passed in (often a String, because set_locale assigns I18n.locale from SiteSetting.default_locale or current_user.effective_locale, both Strings), while the remaining two are Symbols. Array#uniq does not deduplicate across these types, so the resulting fallback list mixes Strings and Symbols. When ensure_loaded! iterates that list and stores entries into translate_accelerator's @loaded_locales, a later lookup with the same logical locale but the other type will miss and trigger a redundant load of the same yml file on subsequent requests.

title: FallbackLocaleList inherits Hash but [] returns Array, breaking Hash semantics
body: class FallbackLocaleList < Hash overrides [](locale) to return an Array of fallback locales instead of a Hash entry. While the standard I18n::Backend::Fallbacks class uses the same trick, this design makes Hash methods such as keys, values, each, merge, and empty? operate on the empty underlying Hash rather than the fallbacks, which is misleading and can break any caller that relies on Hash semantics. A plain class (or subclass of Object) with an explicit [] method would more honestly model what this object is.

title: No tests cover the new fallback behavior or the ensure_loaded! preload
body: The PR changes fallback behavior in several non-trivial ways: it introduces a custom FallbackLocaleList with a fixed [user_locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en] order, eagerly preloads all fallback locales for every request via I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! in ApplicationController#set_locale, removes config.i18n.fallbacks = true from three environment files (production.rb, profile.rb, cloud66 production.rb), and removes config/initializers/pluralization.rb (folding it into the new i18n initializer). No specs are added or updated, and the PR description is just 'Test 9' with no detail, so there is no automated verification that the fallback chain resolves as intended, that ensure_loaded! actually populates @loaded_locales, that background-job code paths still get translations, or that existing fallback-related tests still pass.

title: Fallback chain ignores current_user.effective_locale when site default differs
body: The [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en] chain puts the site-wide default before English but does not include the user's locale's natural parent (e.g. pt_BR users fall back to English rather than pt). While the inline TODO acknowledges this is a future enhancement, the current order also means that a user whose effective_locale happens to equal SiteSetting.default_locale still gets :en listed twice (uniq handles it, but the chain collapses to [default, :en] rather than [user, default, :en]), so any locale-specific translator for that user is silently lost. More importantly, for languages like zh_TW or sr_Latin whose site default may be a closely related variant, the user loses the more-specific fallback path entirely.

title: translate() loads only config.locale, not fallback locales, breaking fallbacks outside controllers
body: The patched translate() calls `load_locale(config.locale)` for the current I18n locale but never ensures the fallback locales (as defined by `I18n.fallbacks`) are loaded. ApplicationController#set_locale works around this by calling `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` on every request, but anything outside the controller request cycle (Sidekiq/background jobs, ActionMailer, rake tasks, the discourse console, plugin initialization, event handlers, etc.) does not run set_locale, so only config.locale's yml is loaded. When a key is missing in config.locale, I18n::Backend::Fallbacks#translate iterates `fallbacks[locale]` and calls Backend::Simple#translate for each fallback, but the yml files for those locales were never loaded, so the lookup misses and MissingTranslation is raised. The whole point of this PR is server-side fallbacks, so translate() itself should ensure the full chain is loaded, e.g. `ensure_loaded!(config.locale); I18n.fallbacks[config.locale].each { |l| ensure_loaded!(l) }`, rather than relying on a controller before_filter that is never invoked in those contexts.

title: SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym raises NoMethodError when default_locale is nil
body: FallbackLocaleList#[] builds the chain as `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact`. This initializer is loaded at boot, but `SiteSetting.default_locale` can legitimately be nil at that point (the setting is not yet populated from the DB, certain specs stub it, or it has been cleared). Calling `nil.to_sym` raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'to_sym' for nil:NilClass`, which propagates out of the initializer and prevents the app from booting. The trailing `.compact` does not protect against this because the exception is raised before compact runs. Guard against nil, e.g. `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale && SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact`, or coerce first.

title: No tests added for the new localization fallback feature
body: The PR introduces a non-trivial new class (FallbackLocaleList with custom [] and ensure_loaded!), a new I18n.ensure_loaded! method in the translate accelerator, and wires it into ApplicationController#set_locale, but the changed-files list contains no spec or test file. There are no specs covering: that missing keys in a user's locale fall back to SiteSetting.default_locale and then :en; that FallbackLocaleList#[] handles edge cases (nil default_locale, I18n.locale == :en, default_locale == :en, locale == default_locale); that ensure_loaded! loads every locale in the chain; or that translate() in translate_accelerator works correctly when fallbacks are exercised (both with and without options/args). Without these, regressions in fallback ordering or in the load_locale/ensure_loaded! interaction will be invisible.

title: FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but only overrides [], losing Hash semantics like []= and breaking plugin custom fallbacks
body: FallbackLocaleList < Hash overrides `[]` to always return a synthesized Array `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact` and never stores anything in the underlying Hash. The standard `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks` it replaces also implements `[]=` (and relies on Hash#keys / merge / etc. in places), which lets plugins add per-locale mappings like `I18n.fallbacks[:'zh-TW'] = [:'zh-TW', :'zh-CN']`. With this class, any such `[]=` write is silently ignored: the next `fallbacks[:'zh-TW']` recomputes the generic `[locale, default_locale, :en]` chain and the plugin's mapping has no effect. Either subclass `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks` to keep the extension contract, store computed chains in the Hash and read them back in [], or stop inheriting from Hash and only expose the methods actually consumed by I18n::Backend::Fallbacks.

title: No tests for the new fallback behavior
body: The PR introduces a new FallbackLocaleList class, a custom I18n.fallbacks implementation, the new I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! method, and a new I18n.ensure_loaded! method on the freedom patch. None of these changes have accompanying specs. There is no coverage verifying: that the fallback chain order is correct for users vs anonymous requests, that I18n.locale changes between requests trigger reloads, that SiteSetting.default_locale is honored as a fallback, that missing keys in a non-English locale correctly fall back to English, or that ensure_loaded! is idempotent. The PR description 'Test 9' does not indicate tests are present anywhere.

title: FallbackLocaleList inherits Hash but only overrides []
body: FallbackLocaleList < Hash redefines only the [] method. All other methods of I18n::Locale::Fallbacks that callers may rely on (e.g. defaults, defaults=, compute, map, each over configured fallbacks, []=) are left as plain Hash methods that operate on an always-empty Hash. Any plugin or piece of code that does I18n.fallbacks[:zh_TW] = [:zh_TW, :zh_CN, :en] will silently be ignored because lookup always goes through the overridden []. Methods like I18n.fallbacks.defaults will raise NoMethodError. Either stop inheriting Hash or implement the full Locale::Fallbacks contract so that per-locale configuration and other API consumers are not broken.

title: Fallback chain mixes String and Symbol locales
body: set_locale in application_controller.rb assigns I18n.locale from current_user.effective_locale or SiteSetting.default_locale, which return String values in Discourse. The fallback chain is [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en], so the chain can contain a String like 'fr' alongside Symbols :en. Array#uniq does not deduplicate values of different types, so 'en' and :en would both end up in the chain and load_locale would add both to @loaded_locales in translate_accelerator.rb. This results in wasted reloads and risks comparison surprises in i18n internals or third-party code. Coerce locale to a Symbol (e.g. locale.to_sym) so the chain is uniformly typed.

title: ensure_loaded! has a data race on @loaded_locales
body: ensure_loaded! initializes @loaded_locales ||= [] outside any mutex and then calls load_locale, which itself protects only the body via LOAD_MUTEX. Two threads that race on the first call can each observe @loaded_locales as nil, create separate Array instances, and the last write wins. Whichever instance is no longer referenced loses its additions, so subsequent calls into ensure_loaded!/load_locale can re-load already-loaded locales. The mutex currently held only by load_locale is not sufficient because @loaded_locales may flip between two arrays mid-flight. Initialize the ivar under the same LOAD_MUTEX (or use a Set guarded by the mutex) so the @loaded_locales reference itself is stable.

title: ensure_loaded! allocates per request in a before_filter
body: set_locale runs as a before_filter on every request, and the new line invokes I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!, which calls self[I18n.locale] and allocates a new Array every time, then iterates it calling I18n.ensure_loaded! for each fallback locale. The actual YAML loading is memoized via @loaded_locales, but the per-request Array allocation and Hash#[] invocation occur for every request, including API and XHR requests that never render translations. Consider calling ensure_loaded! only when the locale or SiteSetting.default_locale changes, or memoizing the resolved fallback chain on the FallbackLocaleList instance.

title: Fallback config silently moved without explanation
body: The PR removes config.i18n.fallbacks = true (and its explanatory comment) from config/environments/production.rb, config/environments/profile.rb, and config/cloud/cloud66/files/production.rb without leaving a comment noting that i18n fallbacks are now configured exclusively by config/initializers/i18n.rb. The two places previously disagreed in subtle ways and a future engineer may add the Rails-style line back, double-enabling the Fallbacks module, or assume the initializer is the only source of truth. Leave a one-line note in each environment file pointing at the initializer, or document the migration in the initializer itself.

title: Denial cache key uses raw subject UID while permission cache key uses resolved UID
body: In Check, the denial cache key is built with `userPermDenialCacheKey(checkReq.Namespace.Value, checkReq.UserUID, ...)`, where `checkReq.UserUID` is the raw value parsed from `req.GetSubject()` (e.g., "123" for subject `user:123`). However, `getCachedIdentityPermissions` (called shortly after) resolves the same user through `GetUserIdentifiers`, which can translate a numeric ID into the actual UID (e.g., "abc123") and then uses that for `userPermCacheKey`. The two caches therefore live under different namespaces for the same user: denial entries are stored under the raw input string, permission entries under the resolved UID. Consequences: (1) the denial cache will store duplicate entries for the same user depending on how the caller formats the subject, wasting memory; (2) more importantly, denial behavior becomes inconsistent — a denial cached for `user:123` will not be hit when the same user is checked via `user:<actualUID>`, so a user could be allowed on one path and denied on another for the same resource. The denial key should be derived from `userIdentifiers.UID` (after the lookup) the same way the permission cache key is.

title: Denial cache TTL will keep returning false for up to 30 s after a permission grant
body: `permDenialCache` is set with `shortCacheTTL = 30 * time.Second` and is consulted before any other source of truth. Once a denial is recorded for a (user, action, name, parent) tuple, the service will continue returning `Allowed: false` for that tuple for up to 30 seconds with no way to invalidate it on permission grant. The PR explicitly targets scenarios where a user gains a new permission (e.g. they just created a dashboard/folder) and immediately needs access; in the unhappy path where the same (name, parent) was previously checked and denied, the new grant will be invisible until the denial entry expires. There is no invalidation hook tied to permission changes and no `Delete` call on `permDenialCache` anywhere in the file. At minimum the key should be tied to a shorter TTL than the permission grant path, or the service should be invalidated whenever roles/permissions are mutated.

title: No test verifies the denial cache is populated when Check returns false
body: The new branch `if !allowed { s.permDenialCache.Set(ctx, permDenialKey, true) }` is the only place where `permDenialCache` is ever written to (other than the test's manual `Set` in `Should deny on explicit cache deny entry`). The existing `TestService_Check` "should deny user without permission" case asserts `resp.Allowed == false` but does not check `s.permDenialCache.Get(...)` afterwards. As a result, if a future change accidentally removes or breaks the `Set` call, the denial cache would silently stop being populated and no CI signal would fire. The test should explicitly read `s.permDenialCache` (e.g. via `userPermDenialCacheKey`) and assert the entry was written.

title: Denial-cache precedence test setup does not actually prove precedence
body: In `Should deny on explicit cache deny entry`, the perm cache is set with `map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}`. Because `checkPermission` only inspects the boolean via `if scopeMap[t.scope(req.Name)]`, a value of `false` is indistinguishable from a missing key — the check would return `false` even without the denial cache entry. To actually demonstrate that `permDenialCache` is consulted first and short-circuits a would-be allow, the perm cache should be set to `true` for `dashboards:uid:dash1` (matching folder inheritance), so that removing the denial entry would change the response from `false` to `true`.

title: List still serves stale permission cache, so newly created dashboards/folders can be invisible
body: The PR's stated goal is that "dash/folder creator can access the dashboard/folder that they've just created". The `Check` path now falls through to the DB when the cached permission map does not contain the requested resource. `List`, however, was only changed to use `getCachedIdentityPermissions` first; it still returns whatever the cache holds when there is a hit, with no equivalent "cache hit but resource not present -> requery" step. For a user whose cached permission scope map predates the new dashboard/folder, `List` will silently omit the newly created item until the cache expires (`shortCacheTTL`, 30 s). The same `cachedPerms` -> DB fallback used in `Check` needs to apply when the List is asked about a name/folder that is not present in the cached scope map.

title: Denial cache blocks fallback for 30s after permission grants or folder-permission grants
body: The new permDenialCache is keyed by (namespace, userUID, action, name, parent) with a 30s TTL and is consulted BEFORE the permCache check and the new DB-fallback path. Trace for the regression scenario: (T=0) user denied -> permDenialCache.Set(("dash1", "fold1")) and permCache holds empty data; (T=10) admin grants permission on dash1, or grants permission on fold1 which gives inherited access via checkInheritedPermissions; (T=15) user retries -> permDenialCache.Get HITS and returns Allowed=false, so neither permCache nor getIdentityPermissions is consulted. The very same PR adds a fallback that would otherwise have allowed this request immediately. Result: a user who was previously denied (directly OR via folder inheritance that has since been granted) stays denied for up to 30s, despite the freshly persisted grant. This is the same window the fallback was designed to eliminate, so the new denial cache directly negates the PR's own improvement for the permission-grant case. The PR should either (a) invert the check order so permCache/fallback runs first, (b) invalidate the denial entries on role/permission changes, or (c) at minimum document this trade-off.

title: Server-side fix only applies in-proc; remote mode still hides newly created dashboards behind 30s client cache
body: The PR removes the authlib client cache for the in-proc case by passing NoopCache (lines 101-105) so every request reaches the server-side Check (which now has the cache-fix logic). But the remote branch at lines 160-167 still wires authzlib.WithCacheClientOption with cache.NewLocalCache{Expiry: 30s}. Because the client caches the whole CheckResponse, the bug the PR is fixing ("dash/folder creator can't access the dashboard/folder that they've just created") is NOT fixed for remote deployments: a creator's first Check on their new dashboard will be served from the 30s client cache, not from the server. Either the in-proc change should be applied symmetrically to remote, or the 30s TTL should be reduced to ~0 with explicit invalidation when permissions change.

title: No test covers the "user is granted access to a previously denied resource" scenario
body: TestService_CacheCheck exercises: cache-hit allow, cache-miss DB fallback, outdated-cache DB fallback, and explicit denial-cache hit. None of these exercise the precise regression introduced by permDenialCache: deny a user at T=0 (sets denial cache), then grant the permission (or grant the parent folder), then issue another Check and assert it is allowed. Adding such a test would currently FAIL against the new code, surfacing the regression described in the first finding. Without it, the trade-off between denial cache and the DB-fallback fix is not pinned down and could silently regress in future.

title: Test stores map[string]bool{"...": false} but comment claims it "Allow[s] access"
body: In the subtest "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry", the comment "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked" sits above s.permCache.Set(..., map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}). The value false is falsy, so in checkPermission the truthiness check scopeMap[t.scope(req.Name)] returns false and the lookup behaves identically to the key being absent. The comment is therefore wrong: the entry is not an "allow" entry. If the intent of the test is to show that the denial cache overrides an allow decision from permCache, the cached value should be true (e.g., map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": true}) so the contrast with the denial cache is unambiguous.

title: Test "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" does not actually verify denial cache precedence
body: The sub-test "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" in TestService_CacheCheck seeds the permission cache with map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false} alongside an entry in permDenialCache. Because the permCache entry is already a denial for the requested resource, the test returns Allowed=false regardless of whether the denial cache branch is ever executed. If someone removed the permDenialCache check (or made the denial cache never match), the assertion would still pass because checkPermission would deny via permCache. To genuinely exercise denial-cache precedence over permCache, the permCache entry should be {dashboards:uid:dash1: true} (or another scope that grants the request) so that only the denial cache can explain the observed denial. As written, the test is a tautology that does not cover its claimed scenario, leaving the new code path untested.

title: Denial cache key collides between anonymous and any identity with userUID "0"
body: userPermDenialCacheKey(namespace, userUID, action, name, parent) is built solely from the parsed userUID. validateSubject parses "anonymous:0" to userUID "0" with identityType TypeAnonymous, but for any other identity whose UID is also "0" (e.g. a service-account or a user with numeric id 0 if such a record ever exists) the key namespace + ".perm_0_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent is identical. Consequently, an anonymous denial will incorrectly deny a same-UID user (and vice versa) for up to 30s. The key should include the identity type or use distinct prefixes per identity (e.g. anon.perm_..., user.perm_...) like permCache already does via anonymousPermCacheKey vs userPermCacheKey. The current naming userPermDenialCacheKey also misleads readers into thinking it only applies to real users.

title: Permission-denial cache can mask newly granted access for up to 30s
body: In Service.Check, when the DB lookup returns !allowed, the (namespace, userUID, action, name, parent) tuple is written to permDenialCache with shortCacheTTL (30s). On any subsequent request for that exact tuple within the TTL, the denial cache short-circuits and returns Allowed=false without consulting permCache or the DB. This means workflows where a user gains access to a previously denied resource (e.g., an admin assigning a role that grants dashboards:read on a specific dashboard, or a service account being granted a folder) will be incorrectly denied for up to 30 seconds after the grant, despite the PR's stated goal of letting newly created dashboards/folders be accessible. Either the TTL needs to be much shorter, the denial cache must not be consulted before the permCache/DB for the freshly granted case, or some form of invalidation is required when permissions change.

title: permissionCacheUsage "false" label means "went to DB", not "cache unused"
body: The new permissionCacheUsage.WithLabelValues("false", action).Inc() call in Service.Check is reached both on a permCache miss (err != nil from getCachedIdentityPermissions) AND on a permCache hit that denies the request. In both cases we fall through to a getIdentityPermissions DB query. So the metric really tracks "did we have to query the DB", not "was the cache hit/missed". Combined with the symmetric requestCount.WithLabelValues(..., "true", ...) which is incremented on every code path after validateCheckRequest succeeds (cache hits, cache misses that went to DB, and errors during/after the DB call), the label "cached" is misleading. Either rename the labels (e.g., "served_from_db") or restrict "true" to genuine cache-hit responses so dashboards and alerts derived from these counters are meaningful.

title: Existing "should deny user without permission" test does not verify the new denial cache population
body: TestService_Check "User permission check" / "Anonymous permission check" already exercises the path that should populate permDenialCache (a Check that returns Allowed=false after going through getIdentityPermissions), but the assertions only check idCache and permCache, never permDenialCache. With the new code, a successful denial on the slow path must result in an entry under userPermDenialCacheKey(ns, userUID, action, name, parent); the test should assert that presence so that any future regression that drops the Set call is caught.

title: "Fallback to the database on outdated cache" test does not verify the cache was refreshed
body: The sub-test pre-seeds permCache with an outdated entry for dashboards:read (only dash1) and a DB that grants dash2, expecting Allowed=true via the fallback path. It does not assert that permCache was updated with the freshly fetched scopes including "dashboards:uid:dash2". Since the whole point of the fallback path is to keep permCache fresh, this should be asserted (e.g. require.Contains on s.permCache.Get for the new key).

title: NoopCache methods have unused ctx parameter and unused receiver name
body: The new NoopCache.Get/Set/Delete all declare ctx context.Context but never reference it, and the receiver is named lc (a leftover from LocalCache). Pass-though no-op types typically either omit the parameter (using the cache.Cache contract that doesn't require it) or use _ = ctx; the current shape will trigger unused-parameter linters and obscures the intent that these are pure no-ops. A short doc comment on the type explaining why this exists (in-proc client wants to skip the authlib local cache because the in-process server is already caching) would also help reviewers.

title: Missing key prop on GrafanaRuleListItem causes React warnings and list update issues
