Should be d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage). The matching success call on line 48 uses recordStorageDuration, so the error branch is clearly wrong.

title: Update error path records legacy metric instead of storage metric
body: In Update, when d.Storage.Update returns an error the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage). This is the same kind of mislabel as in Create: the storage call failed but a legacy metric is being recorded. Should be d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage) to match the success path on line 132.

title: Storage duration label uses object name instead of Kind
body: On the successful storage Delete path the code calls d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage), passing the object's name as the kind label. The error branch on line 103 correctly uses options.Kind, and every other storage/legacy recording in the file uses options.Kind. This will produce mislabeled metrics (e.g. kind=foo-uid-1234 instead of kind=Playlist) and break grouping/filtering for storage duration dashboards.

title: Legacy DeleteCollection result recorded as storage metric
body: In the DeleteCollection async goroutine, the legacy call's result is recorded with d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy). All other legacy paths in this file (Create line 56, Delete line 113, Update line 140) use d.recordLegacyDuration. This mislabels legacy failures as storage failures and inflates storage duration histograms; should be d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy).

title: Update no longer ensures legacy receives the same object as storage
body: The previous Mode3.Update computed `updated` from objInfo.UpdatedObject(ctx, old_storage), then wrapped objInfo via updateWrapper so that the legacy store received the same updated object storage did. The new implementation just passes the original objInfo to both d.Storage.Update and d.Legacy.Update. Each store will now call objInfo.UpdatedObject with its own view of `old`, so storage and legacy can compute different updated objects (e.g. when objInfo.UpdatedObject depends on `old`, when the underlying stores have diverged, or when update validation adjusts the payload). For Mode3 where legacy is meant to be a safety-net copy of storage, silently writing different payloads defeats the purpose and can corrupt the legacy store. The wrapper pattern (or equivalent) should be preserved.

title: Mode3 doc comment no longer matches behavior after async change
body: The comment `// Mode 3 represents writing to LegacyStorage and Storage and reading from Storage.` is now stale: this PR made the legacy write asynchronous and described in the PR description as a `safety measure` backup, but the comment says nothing about ordering or that legacy is best-effort. Update the comment (or add a package/struct-level doc) to explain that writes go to Storage synchronously and to Legacy asynchronously as a safety net, and that reads come only from Storage.

title: TestMode3_Create error case never triggers an error
body: In the `error when creating object in the unified store fails` case, only setupLegacyFn is provided; setupStorageFn is nil. d.Storage.Create is the first call in Mode3.Create; with no expectation set on the mock the call returns zero values (nil, nil). The function therefore does not return early, fires the legacy goroutine, and returns (nil, nil) to the test. assert.Error(t, err) then fails. To actually exercise the storage-error path this case needs a setupStorageFn that returns an error.

title: TestMode3_Delete error case never triggers an error
body: Same defect as TestMode3_Create: the `error when deleting an object in the unified store` case has no setupStorageFn, so d.Storage.Delete is called on an unconfigured mock and returns (nil, false, nil). dw.Delete returns no error and assert.Error(t, err) fails. Add a setupStorageFn that returns an error from Delete.

title: TestMode3_DeleteCollection error case never triggers an error
body: Same defect as TestMode3_Create: the `error deleting a collection in the unified store` case has no setupStorageFn, so d.Storage.DeleteCollection returns (nil, nil). dw.DeleteCollection returns no error and the wantErr assertion fails. Add a setupStorageFn that returns an error from DeleteCollection.

title: Mode3 write tests never assert that legacy was also called
body: Mode3's whole point is that writes go to both Storage and Legacy. None of the TestMode3_Create / Delete / Update / DeleteCollection tests assert that the legacy store's method was invoked (e.g. via ls.AssertCalled or AssertExpectations on the legacy mock). Because the legacy call is in a goroutine the tests also need to wait for it (sync.WaitGroup, channel, or a goroutine hook in the mock) before asserting, otherwise the assertions race the goroutine and become flaky. Without these assertions the tests would still pass even if the async legacy write were silently removed.

title: Double-checked locking is incomplete; concurrent callers may redundantly re-read the manifest
body: After acquiring the write lock at line 48, the code does not re-check `entryPointAssetsCache`. If multiple goroutines call GetWebAssets concurrently before the cache is populated (e.g., during startup in non-dev mode), each will serialize on the write lock and redundantly read assets-manifest.json from disk and re-decode it. The proper double-checked locking pattern requires a second check of `entryPointAssetsCache` after acquiring the write lock (gated on `cfg.Env != setting.Dev`, since dev mode intentionally bypasses the cache), so that only the first caller does the I/O and subsequent callers return the cached value. As written, every concurrent caller that arrives between the RUnlock at line 43 and the Lock at line 48 pays the full disk-read cost.

title: No test exercises the concurrent path; the race fix is not regression-protected
body: The PR adds synchronization to fix a data race on the global `entryPointAssetsCache`, but no test file is added or modified (the changed-files list contains only `pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go`). Without a concurrent test run under `go test -race` that exercises GetWebAssets from multiple goroutines, future refactors could easily reintroduce the race — for example by reverting to a bare read of the global, by moving the `defer entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Unlock()` above the assignment on line 70, or by replacing the RWMutex with a non-sync primitive. A test that spawns N goroutines all calling GetWebAssets and waits on a sync.WaitGroup would have caught the original race and will catch any regression.

title: Thundering herd: no re-check of cache after acquiring write lock
body: After acquiring the write lock at line 48, the function does not re-check whether entryPointAssetsCache has been populated by another goroutine that passed the fast-path check (lines 41-47) while the cache was still nil. As a result, every concurrent goroutine that observes a nil cache in the fast path will acquire the write lock in turn and each redundantly re-read the manifest file and re-parse the JSON. This is the classic double-checked-locking pitfall: the fast-path RLock/RUnlock check at lines 41-43 is not mirrored inside the Lock-held critical section. At Grafana startup, where many HTTP handlers can call this function concurrently, this causes N redundant file reads and JSON decodes instead of one. The fix is to add a re-check inside the write-lock critical section, e.g. by inserting `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }` immediately after `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()` on line 48.

title: No regression test added for the race fix
body: The PR fixes a data race on the entryPointAssetsCache package variable by adding a sync.RWMutex around its reads and writes. However, no test file is added or modified alongside this change. A regression test that calls GetWebAssets concurrently from multiple goroutines (e.g. via sync.WaitGroup) and runs under `go test -race` would have caught the original race and now guards against future refactors reintroducing it. Without such a test, the fix is unverified by CI and can silently regress.

title: Missing re-check of cache after acquiring write lock causes redundant recomputation under concurrent first-time load
body:
After taking the write lock at line 48, the function does not re-check whether another goroutine has populated `entryPointAssetsCache` while this goroutine was waiting for the lock. In non-Dev mode with an initially empty cache, multiple concurrent first-time callers will all see `nil` under the read lock, enter the write path, serialize on the write lock, and each independently re-read and re-parse the manifest and overwrite the cache. The consequence is wasted I/O and CPU at startup. Add a second check under the write lock so only the first caller does the work:

entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()
defer entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Unlock()
if entryPointAssetsCache != nil && cfg.Env != setting.Dev {
    return entryPointAssetsCache, nil
}

Additionally, the write path unconditionally overwrites the cache with `result` even when `readWebAssetsFromFile` returns an error (result == nil, err != nil). This pre-existing cache-poisoning bug is now reachable from concurrent requests: one goroutine's transient failure can evict a previously valid cache value, forcing every subsequent caller to retry the file read. The error path should leave the previous cache value intact.

title: Confusing logic in enableSqlExpressions that always returns false
body: The new `enableSqlExpressions` function uses unnecessarily complex logic to always return false. The variable `enabled` is assigned `!h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`, meaning `enabled` is true when the flag is OFF — the opposite of what the name suggests. Both branches then return `false`, so the feature flag value is completely ignored. This is confusing and error-prone: a future maintainer may attempt to 'fix' what looks like an inverted boolean bug and inadvertently re-enable SQL Expressions, reintroducing CVE-2024-9264. A safer implementation would simply be `return false` with a comment explaining that SQL Expressions are permanently disabled due to CVE-2024-9264, making the intent unambiguous and removing any appearance that the feature flag is consulted.

title: Dead reference to FlagSqlExpressions feature toggle
body: The function `enableSqlExpressions` queries `featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions` but the result is never used — both code paths return `false`. Either the feature toggle and its documentation should be removed (since SQL Expressions are now hard-disabled regardless of the flag), or the function should be simplified to make clear the flag is intentionally ignored. Leaving a feature toggle that appears to gate behavior but actually does nothing is misleading for operators and future developers.

title: No tests verifying SQL Expressions are disabled
body: This is a security fix (CVE-2024-9264) that hard-disables SQL Expressions, but no tests are added to `pkg/expr/reader_test.go` (or any new test file) to verify that a `QueryTypeSQL` query now returns the expected 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' error. Without a regression test, a future change could re-enable the SQL code path silently. At minimum, a test that constructs an `ExpressionQueryReader`, calls `ReadQuery` with a `QueryTypeSQL` JSON payload, and asserts the returned error would lock in the security fix.

title: SQL command construction path still reachable if reader check is removed
body: `NewSQLCommand` in `pkg/expr/sql_command.go` still calls `sql.TablesList` which constructs a DuckDB command via `fmt.Sprintf("SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')", rawSQL)`. Currently this is unreachable because `reader.go` rejects `QueryTypeSQL` upfront, but the code path remains live and `TablesList` is still an exported function in `pkg/expr/sql`. If the `enableSqlExpressions` gate in `reader.go` is later weakened or removed (e.g., because someone misreads the confusing boolean logic in `enableSqlExpressions`), the original DuckDB-based command construction — including the string interpolation that contributed to CVE-2024-9264 — would be reachable again. Consider making `TablesList` and `NewSQLCommand` return an 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' error directly rather than relying solely on the reader-level gate, so the vulnerable code path cannot be reached even if the reader check is bypassed.

title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false despite appearing conditional
Unsafe SQL formatting pattern retained as dead code
body: `TablesList` still constructs a SQL command with `fmt.Sprintf("SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')", rawSQL)` after only escaping single quotes. Although the new stub DB returns `"not implemented"` before any statement is actually evaluated, the vulnerable code path is still reachable via `UnmarshalSQLCommand` / `NewSQLCommand`, which are not gated by the new `enableSqlExpressions` check in `reader.go`. More importantly, this retains the exact pattern that made CVE-2024-9264 exploitable; if anyone later restores DuckDB to "re-enable" SQL expressions, the injection re-emerges immediately. Since `TablesList` now always returns the stub error and is never useful, the entire function (and the unsafe `Sprintf`/`Replace`/`RunCommands` calls) should be deleted rather than preserved in a half-disabled form.

title: Error message claims SQL expressions were never implemented
body: When `enableSqlExpressions` returns false, the reader returns `fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")`. This message is misleading for two reasons: (a) SQL expressions were shipped and used in dashboards before this PR, so users with existing panels will hit this error and have no way to understand why a previously working feature now fails; (b) the message obscures the actual reason — a security fix for CVE-2024-9264. The error should at minimum mention that the feature has been disabled for security reasons and link to the blog post / release notes, so dashboards that previously used SQL expressions don't silently look like an unimplemented feature. The same misleading message would also be surfaced from `UnmarshalSQLCommand` if `sql.TablesList` is reached.

title: Stub DB has no explanation that this is a CVE-2024-9264 mitigation
body: `pkg/expr/sql/db.go` introduces an empty `DB` struct whose three methods all return `errors.New("not implemented")`, and is wired into `parser.go` and `sql_command.go`. There is no package- or type-level comment explaining that this file exists solely as a CVE-2024-9264 mitigation, that callers must gate usage through `enableSqlExpressions`, or that the methods are deliberately inert. Future maintainers may reasonably assume this is a working SQL backend and try to fill in the methods to re-enable the feature, reintroducing the vulnerability. Add a comment such as `// Stub DB used after CVE-2024-9264 to make SQL expressions return errors; do not implement.`

title: No regression test that SQL expressions are rejected
body: This is a security-driven removal of a feature, but the diff contains no test changes. Existing tests for `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery` (and for `UnmarshalSQLCommand`) will continue to pass only if they don't exercise the `QueryTypeSQL` branch; there is nothing pinning the new behavior. At minimum, add a test that asserts (a) `ReadQuery` with `QueryTypeSQL` returns an error mentioning SQL expressions are disabled, and (b) `UnmarshalSQLCommand` / `NewSQLCommand` rejects any input. Without this, a future refactor could silently re-enable SQL expressions (e.g. by "simplifying" `enableSqlExpressions`) and re-open CVE-2024-9264.

title: enableSqlExpressions has dead logic that always returns false
body: The function `enableSqlExpressions` takes `*ExpressionQueryReader` and reads `h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`, but both branches of the conditional return `false`. The feature toggle is referenced but its value has no effect on the outcome; the function unconditionally returns `false`, making the parameter `h`, the `features` field access, and the conditional dead code. A future maintainer who wants to re-enable SQL expressions by toggling `FlagSqlExpressions` will be misled into thinking the flag works, when in fact the function must be rewritten. The intended behavior could be expressed simply as `return false` (or, if the flag should still control the feature, `return h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`). Leaving the bogus intermediate variable `enabled` and unreachable branch will confuse future readers and any tooling (linters, dead-code detectors) that flags `h` as unused.

title: Vulnerable SQL-interpolation pattern preserved in dead code
body: The line `cmd := fmt.Sprintf("SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')", rawSQL)` is the exact vulnerable pattern behind CVE-2024-9264. It builds a DuckDB SQL statement by interpolating user-controlled `rawSQL` after only escaping single quotes (`strings.Replace(rawSQL, "'", "''", -1)`), which is an incomplete sanitizer (e.g. backslash escapes, Unicode, or comment sequences can still break out). It is currently unreachable because the stubbed `RunCommands` returns "not implemented" and because `ReadQuery` blocks SQL queries via `enableSqlExpressions`, but this function and its file are left in place for easy re-enabling. If anyone later swaps the stub back for the real DuckDB backend or removes the `enableSqlExpressions` guard, the original RCE/LFI vulnerability returns with no review trigger. Either delete the entire `pkg/expr/sql/parser.go` body (since it is unreachable) or replace the format-string concatenation with proper DuckDB parameter binding / parser API usage before the code can be re-enabled.

title: Misleading user-facing error message for disabled feature
body: When a user submits a SQL expression query they get `fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")`. This phrasing suggests the feature simply has not been built yet, which contradicts reality: the feature was shipped, then deliberately disabled because of CVE-2024-9264. Users filing a request to "implement SQL expressions" or assuming it will arrive in a future release is a foreseeable miscommunication. Consider wording such as "sqlExpressions are disabled for security reasons (see CVE-2024-9264)" or, at minimum, "sqlExpressions are not supported in this version" so users understand this is an intentional, security-driven removal and not a missing feature.

title: No automated test verifies the SQL-expressions kill switch
body: The patch is a security mitigation that introduces a new behavior (any `QueryTypeSQL` request must be rejected with "sqlExpressions is not implemented" before any SQL parsing happens, and the `enableSqlExpressions` helper must return `false` unconditionally), yet no test file is modified or added. The PR description relies on a manual verification by one engineer. For a CVE fix this should be covered by an automated unit test in `pkg/expr/reader_test.go` (or equivalent) that asserts: (1) a `QueryTypeSQL` query returns the expected error and never reaches `NewSQLCommand`/`sql.TablesList`, and (2) `enableSqlExpressions` returns `false` regardless of the feature toggle state. Without that test, a future refactor that "restores" the feature-flag branch or accidentally wires `enableSqlExpressions` to `true` will not be caught by CI.

title: Race condition introduced by removing BuildIndex global lock
body: The diff removes `b.cacheMu.Lock()` at the start of `BuildIndex` and only acquires it around the final `b.cache[key] = idx` assignment. As a result, two concurrent calls for the same key can both pass through `GetIndex` (which takes only an RLock and returns nil for a missing entry) and concurrently execute `BuildIndex` for the same key. Both will then race on `b.cache[key] = idx` with last-writer-wins. At startup this is reachable whenever a gRPC request lands while `searchSupport.init` is still building a namespace, and at runtime it is reachable whenever a search request races with `getOrCreateIndex`. Previously the lock held for the whole build prevented this entirely; now the cache can contain stale indexes, and the second build allocates a whole new bleve index (potentially on disk under `b.opts.Root`) that is then orphaned. The fix in `getOrCreateIndex` only acquires the index after the build returns, so callers that retrieved the earlier index write to an index that is no longer the cached one. A per-key mutex, singleflight.Group, or sync.Map with double-checked loading is needed to make this safe.

title: Reordering search.init before initWatcher loses events written in the gap
body: The diff reorders `Init` to call `s.search.init(ctx)` first and then `s.initWatcher()`. Previously the broadcaster/stream was attached before the search index was built. `searchSupport.init` builds the index from a snapshot taken via `GetResourceStats`/`ListIterator` that returns when its last `ListIterator` completes. Any writes that hit the SQL backend between that point and when `s.initWatcher` starts (and calls `WatchWriteEvents` -> `listLatestRVs` to compute its `since`) are NOT in the search index snapshot AND are NOT yet visible to the watcher, so they are silently dropped from the search index. With the old order, the watcher (poller) was already running, so its `since` was at or after the build's last read RV. The fix is either to keep the original order or to pass an explicit `since` (the last RV read by `searchSupport.init`) into `initWatcher` so its polling starts at that RV.

title: NewResourceServer now fails if init fails, breaking callers that relied on lazy init
body: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` synchronously and returns `(nil, err)` on any init failure (lifecycle hook, search init, or watcher startup). Previously, init was deferred to the first RPC and a server object was always returned. Callers (e.g., the storage server module wiring) that construct the server, register it, and then serve traffic will now fail at construction time on any transient init failure. The PR description explicitly flags this as a question for the reviewer ("Does anything else depend on initializing US lazily?") but the chosen behavior change is significant: a slow/unhealthy database at startup, a corrupt bleve index directory, or any failure in `s.lifecycle.Init` / `s.search.init` will now prevent the storage server module from starting at all. Either keep the lazy path (with a context that isn't the per-RPC deadline) or ensure every caller of `NewResourceServer` is updated and tested for the eager-failure case.

title: NewResourceServer leaks backend resources when Init fails
body: When `s.lifecycle.Init(ctx)` succeeds (which is what opens the SQL database connection in the SQL backend's `initLocked`) but a later step in `s.once.Do` (search init or `initWatcher`) fails, `NewResourceServer` returns `(nil, err)` without calling `s.Stop`. There is no `defer` to call `s.cancel()` or to call `s.lifecycle.Stop`. The SQL backend's database handle (`b.db`), open bleve file indices on disk under `b.opts.Root`, and any goroutines started during partial init are left running. A successful subsequent `NewResourceServer` call for the same backend then races against the leaked resources. Add a cleanup path on the failure branch.

title: Data race on outer `err` variable inside errgroup goroutine
body: Inside `searchSupport.init`, the errgroup goroutine does `_, _, err = s.build(...)` and then `return err`, where `err` is the outer named variable declared just above the `for` loop. With `group.SetLimit(s.initWorkers) > 1`, multiple goroutines write to the same outer `err` concurrently. The race is benign here because the goroutines also `return err` and `group.Wait()` is reassigned to `err` immediately after, but it is still a data race per the Go memory model and a race detector run will flag it. Use `_, _, buildErr := s.build(...)` and return `buildErr`.

title: BuildIndex still discards the traced context
body: This PR's stated goal is to "fix trace propagation by passing span contexts down". `searchSupport.init`, `searchSupport.build`, and `backend.GetResourceStats` were all updated from `_, span := ...` to `ctx, span := ...` so the new context flows into downstream calls. `bleveBackend.BuildIndex` is the only other function touched in this PR that still uses `_, span := b.tracer.Start(ctx, tracingPrexfixBleve+"BuildIndex")`. The span exists but the returned context is dropped, which is the same bug the PR claims to fix. Apply the same `ctx, span :=` change here for consistency, even though the builder closure currently captures its own context from the caller.

title: Trace propagation fix is incomplete in backend.go
body: The PR description says "Fixes trace propagation by passing span contexts down" and updates `GetResourceStats` from `_, span := ...` to `ctx, span := ...`. Other methods in the same file (`WriteEvent` at line 158, `ReadResource` at line 353, `ListIterator` at line 388, `poll` at line 664, `resourceVersionAtomicInc` at line 718) still use `_, span := b.tracer.Start(ctx, ...)`, discarding the returned context. Downstream DB calls made with the outer `ctx` (not the traced context) therefore do not appear as children of these spans. Either the fix is intentionally scoped (in which case the PR description is misleading) or these should all be updated to `ctx, span :=`.

title: Postgres support in the storage-server integration test is skipped rather than fixed
body: The diff adds a `t.Skip` for `dbType == "postgres"` with a TODO to fix the test. This PR changes the most fundamental part of the storage server lifecycle (where initialization runs) but provides no new test coverage for that change, and the only integration test that exercises `InitializeModuleServer` with `modules.StorageServer` is now skipped on the very backend the storage server is required to support. Combined with the eager-init behavior change in `NewResourceServer`, this leaves a regression in postgres untested. Either unblock the test or add a dedicated test that exercises `NewResourceServer` -> eager init -> a Search gRPC call end-to-end on a real backend.

title: successful index build still logs duration but index size is constant
body: The new `s.log.Info("search index initialized", "duration_secs", end-start, "total_docs", s.search.TotalDocs())` reports `total_docs` from `bleveBackend.TotalDocs()`, which iterates `b.cache` at the moment init's search goroutines return. Because `searchSupport.init` uses `errgroup.Group` with `group.SetLimit(s.initWorkers)`, multiple `BuildIndex` calls may still be in flight when init's group.Wait() returns only the FIRST error; if no error occurred, `group.Wait` returns nil and the cache may not yet contain every index that was being built (the cache assignment happens inside `bleveBackend.BuildIndex`, after `builder(idx)` and `idx.Flush()`, and is only protected by `cacheMu`). Worse, if any one of those last in-flight builds fails after some succeed, the log line is never reached but partial state is reported earlier. This is a minor observability concern, but combined with the bleve lock-removal race it understates how many indexes were actually built.

title: Postgres skip added — hides eager-init regression
BuildIndex no longer serializes per key — duplicate indexes possible
body:
The previous version held `b.cacheMu` for the entire BuildIndex call, so concurrent calls for the same key were serialized and the cached index was consistent. The new version only locks when assigning `b.cache[key] = idx`. Two concurrent calls to `BuildIndex` for the same `NamespacedResource` (for example, two simultaneous `Search` requests that both find the cache empty via `getOrCreateIndex`, or the init goroutine racing with an incoming search) will both:
  1. Open separate bleve indexes (file or memory),
  2. Run the builder to write all documents,
  3. Flush,
  4. Race to write `b.cache[key]` — last writer wins, the loser's index is orphaned in memory and the work is wasted.
The PR description frames this as "finer grain locking", but the same-key duplication problem is exactly the TODO called out in `searchSupport.getOrCreateIndex` ("We want to block while building the index and return the same index for the key … simple mutex not great … we don't want to block while anything in building, just the same key"). A per-key lock (e.g. a `sync.Map` of in-progress builds, or a sharded mutex keyed by `NamespacedResource`) is needed to actually fix the duplicate-build race while keeping different-key concurrency.

title: Eager Init inside NewResourceServer changes the constructor's contract
body:
`NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` synchronously before returning. The constructor will now block for the full duration of search-index build (potentially many seconds for large installations) and return an error if init fails. Previously the same errors would surface on the first RPC and the constructor returned quickly.
This breaks any caller that expected the constructor to be cheap (tests, callers that wire up dependencies lazily, callers that want to surface a degraded server, callers that explicitly rely on `server.Init` being invoked separately). The PR description itself flags this concern ("Does anything else depend on initializing US lazily? What could this break?") without answering it. Verify all callers of `NewResourceServer` and the SQL `NewBackend` (which now also returns only after `Init` succeeds, since its backend implements the resource LifecycleHooks path) before merging — at minimum, document the contract change on the function and make sure module startup won't now fail outright where it previously degraded.

title: Event-pump goroutine in search.init panics on channel close
BuildIndex no longer serializes same-key builds; risk of corrupted file index
body: The diff removes the outer `b.cacheMu.Lock(); defer b.cacheMu.Unlock()` that wrapped all of `BuildIndex` and replaces it with a narrow lock around only the `b.cache[key] = idx` assignment. `getOrCreateIndex` calls `s.search.GetIndex` and then `s.build`, so the cache read and the cache update are not atomic. The OLD code at least serialized any two concurrent `BuildIndex` calls for the same key via the global write lock; the NEW code allows them to run in parallel. For file-based indices this is dangerous: `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` opens the same on-disk directory (`filepath.Join(b.opts.Root, key.Namespace, fmt.Sprintf("%s.%s", key.Resource, key.Group))`) in two goroutines, and bleve (bolt/badger-backed) does not safely tolerate concurrent openers/writers on the same path, so the on-disk index can be corrupted and subsequent reads will fail or return garbage. For memory-backed indices, both goroutines still build a full index and the loser is orphaned (CPU + memory leak). The intended concurrency win is for different keys; same-key concurrency needs per-key serialization (e.g. a `sync.Map` of per-key mutexes) before opening the bleve index.

title: TotalDocs reads cache without holding the cache lock
body: `TotalDocs` does `for _, v := range b.cache { ... }` with no lock acquisition, while `BuildIndex` (now able to run concurrently with other builds and with any caller of `TotalDocs`) writes to `b.cache` under `b.cacheMu`. Iterating a Go map while it is being written to is a data race and is documented as able to panic with "fatal error: concurrent map read and map write" or "concurrent map writes". `TotalDocs` is part of the `SearchBackend` interface and is called from `searchSupport.init` via `s.search.TotalDocs()` immediately after `group.Wait()`, but it may also be invoked from elsewhere (metrics endpoints, future callers). It should at least take `b.cacheMu.RLock()` for the duration of the iteration. Previously this was masked because the lock was held during the whole `BuildIndex`; with the finer-grained locking the race window is now larger.

title: Init triggers two WatchWriteEvents calls; SQL backend spawns two pollers
body: `(*server).Init` is now called from `NewResourceServer` and unconditionally runs both `s.search.init(ctx)` and `s.initWatcher()`. `search.init` itself calls `s.storage.WatchWriteEvents(watchctx)` and starts a long-lived goroutine that consumes from that channel. `initWatcher` then constructs a `Broadcaster` whose subscriber-setup callback also calls `s.backend.WatchWriteEvents(s.ctx)` the first time a client subscribes via `Watch`. For the SQL backend, `WatchWriteEvents` is implemented as `go b.poller(ctx, since, stream)` (pkg/storage/unified/sql/backend.go:566), so every call spins up a new poller goroutine that polls the database every 100ms. After this PR, every Grafana process with unified storage enabled runs two such pollers against the same database and reads the same history rows, doubling query load and (for `search.init`'s consumer) processing events from a completely separate stream than the `Broadcaster`. The PR explicitly reorders the init code but does not address this; the right fix is to have `search.init` subscribe to the existing `Broadcaster` instead of opening a second watcher. This was pre-existing but is directly within the scope of the init restructuring and should be resolved in the same change.

title: NewResourceServer now blocks on full index build and leaks partial state on Init failure
body: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` synchronously and returns `(nil, err)` if it fails. There are three consequences a maintainer should be aware of: (1) every caller of the constructor now blocks for as long as it takes to build every search index, which is a contract change from the previous "return fast, build on first gRPC call" behavior; this can affect test fixtures, alternate startup paths, and any code that constructs a `ResourceServer` and expects immediate return. (2) If `search.init` fails partway through, indexes that were successfully built remain in the bleve cache and any partially-started watcher goroutine is not torn down, because `Stop` is not called when returning `(nil, err)`. (3) The internal `ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(...)` pair is created on the success path of construction but on the failure path the `cancel` function (held in `s.cancel`) is never invoked and the context has no parent cancellation. The constructor should either run init with a `defer cancel()` so failure cleans up, or document the new contract explicitly. Note also that `pkg/server/module_server_test.go` now skips postgres for the storage server target — likely a symptom of this new blocking init interacting with the test harness, which suggests the contract change is observable from outside the unified storage package.

title: Compile error: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() called with no arguments
body: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), the new code calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with zero arguments. However, the only method that exists in UsernamePasswordForm (which UsernameForm extends) is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. There is no zero-argument overload, so this is a compile error and the PR cannot be built. The intended call is almost certainly `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` — without the argument the method body would have referenced an undefined symbol, and even if it compiled it would still need the UserModel to check `user != null` correctly.

title: Awkward try/catch/fail pattern instead of assertThrows
body: In the new `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` test, the assertions that no `form[@id='webauth']` element exists use an inverted try/catch/fail pattern: `MatcherAssert.assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue()); fail(...)`. This catches any Exception (including NoSuchElementException, AssertionError, runtime errors) and treats them all as success. If the page happens to change in the future so that findElement throws something else, or returns a non-null WebElement that fails the null check, the test silently swallows it. The existing project convention (e.g. PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest line 202, PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest before the change) is to use `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, () -> driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']")))`. The same issue appears at line 313 in this file.

title: Public/protected API surface: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled signature is unusual
body: The new helper `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` mixes responsibilities: the method name suggests a configuration check, but its body also requires the user to be non-null. Callers must always pass `context.getUser()` rather than the more natural `null` when querying the realm-level toggle. This will cause subtle bugs in future callers (e.g. someone calling `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(null)` to ask "are passkeys enabled in this realm?" will get false even when they are). Consider splitting into two methods (e.g. `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` for the realm-level check and `isConditionalPasskeysAvailableFor(UserModel user)` for the combined check) or rename to make the semantics clear.

title: Stale inline comment after refactor
body: The comment on the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH field still reads "In this case we skip clearing of the user after unsuccessful password authentication", which is fine, but the inlined `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)` call in `badPasswordHandler` no longer carries its own explanatory comment. Given that the helper now also affects the re-authentication form layout (USERNAME_HIDDEN/REGISTRATION_DISABLED), callers may not realize the side-effect. A short Javadoc on `setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError` documenting what form attributes it sets and why would help — currently the Javadoc is just an implementation comment.

title: Compile error: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() called without required argument
body: UsernameForm.authenticate() invokes isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only definition in the parent class UsernamePasswordForm (line 160-162) requires a UserModel parameter. There is no no-arg overload in UsernameForm, UsernamePasswordForm, or AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator. The change in UsernameForm.java is `if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())` — this will not compile. The fix is either to add a no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() to UsernamePasswordForm (returning the realm passkeys-enabled state without requiring a user) or to pass context.getUser() into the existing method.

title: Regression: webauthn conditional UI form no longer rendered on fresh login
body: The new helper isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requires user != null (line 161). In authenticate() it is now called unconditionally with context.getUser(), so when the user has not yet been identified (the fresh-login branch where context.getUser() == null), webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) is never invoked. The previous code invoked fillContextForm inside the else branch when user was null and passkeys were enabled. As a result the conditional-UI challenge/RP ID/timeout/uv attributes are not populated on the initial login form, breaking discoverable-credential login and the existing tests PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey (asserts webauth form is present on fresh login) and webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey (expects automatic login via discoverable key). The test webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication added in this PR also fails because its initial-login prerequisite depends on the same conditional UI.

title: Regression: webauthn form no longer rendered on error when user is null
body: The overridden challenge(AuthenticationFlowContext, String error, String field) now guards fillContextForm behind isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), which is false when context.getUser() is null. Previously the guard was `context.getUser() == null && webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` — i.e. fillContextForm ran on the user-not-found path. After the change, a USER_NOT_FOUND error during a fresh login no longer repopulates the webauthn form, so the conditional UI is broken on the error retry. This is a behavior reversal of the prior intent, not a fix.

title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled parameter is dead — user != null check defeats the call sites
body: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) is defined as `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. The `user != null` clause makes the parameter useless (the result does not depend on any user attribute — isPasskeysEnabled() is realm-level). All three callers (authenticate, error-challenge, and the broken UsernameForm call) would be more correct as a no-arg method that simply returns the realm passkeys state. The redundant `user != null` term is what causes the two regressions above. Either drop the parameter and the null check, or remove the `user != null` term so user=null still yields true when passkeys are realm-enabled.

title: Compilation error: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called with no arguments but only the UserModel-taking overload is defined
body: Line 47 reads `if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()) {`. The only definition added by this PR is `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` in UsernamePasswordForm.java line 160. There is no no-arg version defined anywhere in the class hierarchy (UsernameForm extends UsernamePasswordForm extends AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator). The call therefore does not resolve and the module will not compile. The intended logic was likely `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, mirroring the other call sites in UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate (line 115) and UsernamePasswordForm.challenge (line 137), which both pass `context.getUser()`.

title: IS_USER_IDENTIFIED attribute now depends on shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators instead of user != null
body: Previously, `isUserIdentified` was set to true whenever `context.getUser() != null`. The refactor moved the assignment inside `if (shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)) { ... isUserIdentified = true; ... }`. WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator overrides shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators to always return false (added in this PR), so IS_USER_IDENTIFIED is always sent as "false" to the form template, including re-authentication scenarios where the user IS identified and a UsernameForm or UsernamePasswordForm authenticator has already hidden the username via USERNAME_HIDDEN. Any template logic that switches on IS_USER_IDENTIFIED (e.g., to label the page, scope the listed passkeys, or render a 're-authenticate as X' state) will behave as if no user is identified. A cleaner fix is to compute `boolean isUserIdentified = user != null;` once and keep the authenticator-list gating inside the if-block, so the two concerns are not coupled.

title: try/assertThat/fail/catch pattern is misleading and contains dead `fail()` call
Unused import NoSuchElementException after Assert.assertThrows calls were replaced
body: The diff replaces the two `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` assertions with `MatcherAssert.assertThat(driver.findElement(...), Matchers.notNullValue())`, but the import `import org.openqa.selenium.NoSuchElementException;` at line 51 was left behind. NoSuchElementException is no longer referenced anywhere in the file; remove the import.

title: Login cache is over-invalidated because wrapped isEnabled() on idpById returns false whenever the linked org is currently disabled
body: In registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(original, updated), the `original` argument is `idpById` from getById(model.getInternalId()), which is wrapped via createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel(...) and overrides isEnabled() to additionally check the linked organization's runtime status (provider.isEnabled() && org.isEnabled() && super.isEnabled()). The `updated` argument is the raw model passed to update(...), whose isEnabled() only reflects the model's ENABLED field. When the IDP is linked to an org that is currently disabled or removed, getLoginPredicate().test(original) returns false (wrapped isEnabled returns false because of the org status), while getLoginPredicate().test(updated) returns true (raw isEnabled is true). Neither early-return branch matches, so the login cache is invalidated even though the update did not change the IDP's static login configuration. The cache state would still be functionally correct (the wrapped isEnabled at read time filters out the IDP), so the impact is wasted work rather than incorrect results, but the optimization described in the Javadoc ('IDP is currently a login IDP' vs 'currently NOT a login IDP') is undermined for org-linked IDPs. Consider obtaining the underlying model for the comparison (e.g., look up cached via realmCache.getCache().get(internalId, CachedIdentityProvider.class) or idpDelegate.getById) rather than the org-aware wrapped instance.

title: Misleading comment in remove(): comment refers to a cache lookup that actually goes to the JPA delegate
body: The comment '//lookup idp by alias in cache to be able to invalidate its internalId' sits next to the use of `storedIdp`, which is populated from idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) — i.e. a JPA delegate lookup, not a cache lookup. The refactor hoisted idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) out of the `if (isInvalid(cacheKey))` branch into a local variable used by both branches of the if/else, but the wording still implies a cache read. The lookup never consults the cache.

title: testCacheIDPForLogin registers removal of an IDP with alias 'alias' (literal) instead of the alias variable
body: In the loop creating IDPs the cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)`. The argument is the literal string "alias", not the loop variable (e.g. `alias`). This will attempt to remove an IDP with alias "alias" at cleanup time, which does not exist. The pattern is pre-existing in testCacheIDPByOrg, but the PR copies it into the new test instead of fixing it. The fix is to use `alias` (the variable) rather than the literal string.

title: testCacheIDPForLogin does not cover organization-level changes that affect login availability
body: The new test exercises IDP create/remove/update and the cache invalidations they cause. It does not exercise organization-level changes that affect IDP login availability: disabling an organization, removing an organization, or unlinking an IDP from its organization. None of these trigger registerIDPLoginInvalidation/OnUpdate, so the login cache may stay stale until some unrelated IDP change triggers an invalidation. The wrapped isEnabled() at read time filters out IDPs whose org is disabled, so correctness is preserved, but the cache freshness behavior in those scenarios is untested.

title: remove() unconditionally hits the DB to fetch the IDP
body: The diff hoists `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` out of the `if (isInvalid(cacheKey))` branch so the result can be passed to the new `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)` call. As a consequence, every `remove(alias)` now performs a JPA `getByAlias` lookup, even when the IDP is fully cached in `CachedIdentityProvider`. Previously the DB was only hit on the invalidation path or on a cache miss; the cache-hit path was DB-free. The login-eligibility check can be satisfied by reusing the cached model (e.g. `cached != null ? cached.getIdentityProvider() : idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)`), so this regression is avoidable without losing the new invalidation behaviour.

title: searchKey for REALM_ONLY mode varies with organizationId unnecessarily
body: In `getForLogin`, `String searchKey = organizationId != null ? organizationId : "";` is used for every `FetchMode`, but `FetchMode.REALM_ONLY` does not depend on `organizationId` (the default implementation always sets `ORGANIZATION_ID` to null for that mode, so the result set is identical regardless of the orgId parameter). Calls to `getForLogin(REALM_ONLY, ...)` with different non-null organizationIds will miss the searchKey inside the cached `IdentityProviderListQuery`, fall into the `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)`/re-query path, and accumulate redundant searchKeys in the same cached entry. The searchKey for `REALM_ONLY` should be a constant (e.g. always `""`) so all REALM_ONLY lookups share one cached entry.

title: getLoginPredicate() semantics changed: org-linked IDPs now require BROKER_PUBLIC=true
body: The static predicate returned by LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() is a public server-spi API. Before this change it only checked ENABLED, not LINK_ONLY, and not HIDE_ON_LOGIN; now it additionally requires that if the IDP has a non-null organizationId then idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC) must parse as true. Concretely, an enabled, non-link-only, not-hide-on-login IDP that is linked to an organization with BROKER_PUBLIC=false used to satisfy the predicate but no longer does. Any caller in server-spi (or downstream extensions) that uses this predicate to decide whether an IDP is a login candidate will observe a behavior change. The new semantics are consistent with what getForLogin actually returns, so it is arguably a correctness fix, but it is still a public-API behavioral change that should be called out explicitly (e.g. in release notes / javadoc) so that downstream code relying on the old behavior can be reviewed.

title: testCacheIDPForLogin cleanup never removes the created IDPs (literal "alias" instead of variable)
body: The line `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` passes the literal string "alias" rather than the loop variable `alias`. There is no IDP with alias "alias" in this test, so `get(...)` returns null and a `null::remove` method reference is registered. When the cleanup is executed it will throw NPE and the IDPs that were just created (idp-alias-0..19 in the first loop plus idp-alias-20 created later) are never removed. The same bug is already present in testCacheIDPByOrg (line 303); this PR replicates and extends it by 21 leaked IDPs per run. Consequence: IDP state leaks across tests within the same class/suite, which can cause ordering-dependent failures in unrelated tests that assume an empty IDP set. Fix is to use `alias` (the variable) instead of the literal "alias", or simply not register per-iteration cleanups.

title: testCacheIDPForLogin only inspects the cache; it never verifies the IDPs returned by getForLogin
body: Throughout the test, every call to `session.identityProviders().getForLogin(...)` discards the returned stream and only asserts on `IdentityProviderListQuery.getIDPs(searchKey).size()` in the cache. As a result, a regression in which `getForLogin` returns the wrong set of IDPs (e.g. due to a bug in the search-key resolution, in the createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel wrapping, in set membership, or in the fallback path where `idp == null` triggers a re-fetch) would not be caught here. The test should also materialize the stream and assert the alias/internal-id set returned matches expectations (e.g. with Assert.assertEquals on a sorted list of aliases for each FetchMode). It should also cover `FetchMode.ORG_ONLY`/`ALL` with `organizationId == null` (searchKey = ""), which is a branch the new cache explicitly takes but is not exercised anywhere in this PR.

title: integerToBytes returns wrong array in left-padding branch
body: In the `qLength > bytes.length` branch of `integerToBytes`, the method allocates a left-padded `tmp` array of `qLength` bytes and copies `bytes` into it, but then returns `bytes` (the original shorter array) instead of `tmp`. The left-padding is therefore never applied. This causes `asn1derToConcatenatedRS` to call `System.arraycopy(r, 0, concatenatedSignatureValue, 0, len)` with `r.length < len`, which throws `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` whenever the BigInteger R or S value happens to be shorter than `qLength` (e.g. when the high byte of the value is 0, which is statistically possible for ECDSA signatures). The fix is to return `tmp` on line 160.

title: Dead code in concatenatedRSToASN1DER discards encoder results
body: The two statements `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` create encoders, write to them, and immediately discard the results. The actual encoding used for the return value is produced by the subsequent `writeDerSeq(...)` call. The dead code is confusing and wasteful, and should be removed.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider does not return a BouncyCastle provider
body: `AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider()` returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, which is the provider backing the default JCA keystore (typically SunJCE on a standard JDK, or the BC provider only if it has been registered globally). The method is named `getBouncyCastleProvider` and the interface contract in `CryptoProvider` documents it as returning the BouncyCastle security provider, so any caller that relies on this method to obtain BouncyCastle (e.g. to invoke BC-specific APIs) will silently get the wrong provider. Since the authz-client is intended to avoid the BouncyCastle dependency, the method should return `null` or the implementation should be renamed/document so the contract is not violated.

title: Indefinite-length encoding returned as -1 but not handled by callers
body: `readLength()` returns `-1` for indefinite-length encoding (length byte 0x80). Callers like `readSequence()` then evaluate `while (length > 0)`, which immediately exits and returns an empty list, while `readInteger()` would pass `-1` to `read(int)`, which throws an `IOException` with a misleading 'EOF found reading -1 bytes' message. Indefinite-length encoding is not legal in DER and should be rejected explicitly (e.g. throw an `IOException` for `0x80`) instead of being silently passed through.

title: Test does not cover the case where R/S is shorter than the curve length
body: The test only exercises the round-trip with default JDK-generated EC keys and a fixed message. For typical ES256 signatures the BigInteger byte arrays of R and S are 32 or 33 bytes long, so the `qLength > bytes.length` branch of `integerToBytes` is never entered and the `return bytes` bug on line 160 of `AuthzClientCryptoProvider` is not detected. A test that explicitly constructs DER signatures where R or S is shorter than `algorithm.getSignatureLength() / 2` (e.g. by zero-padding the high byte) would trigger the `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` described above. Without such a test the bug will not be caught by CI.

title: Adding order() to CryptoProvider is a binary-incompatible API change
body: A new abstract method `int order()` has been added to the `org.keycloak.common.crypto.CryptoProvider` interface. This is part of the public `keycloak-common` artifact: any out-of-tree implementation of `CryptoProvider` (extensions, integrators, third-party crypto providers) will fail to compile/link against the new interface. This should be called out in the release notes / migration guide so downstream users know they must add an `order()` method to their implementation. Additionally, consider providing a `default` implementation (e.g. `return 0;`) to make the change source-compatible for the common case.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns default JCE provider, not BouncyCastle
body: The implementation returns KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider(), which is the JDK provider that happens to supply the default keystore type (typically SUN/SunJCE), not BouncyCastle. Every other CryptoProvider implementation returns a BouncyCastle/FIPS provider here (DefaultCryptoProvider returns bcProvider, FIPS1402Provider returns bcFipsProvider), and the interface Javadoc on CryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider() explicitly states 'BouncyCastle security provider'. Callers that rely on this getter to obtain a BC-backed Provider will silently receive the JDK provider instead, which can cause missing algorithms, wrong defaults (e.g., signature/padding), or NPEs in downstream code that assumed non-null BC.

title: Dead code allocates and discards two ASN1Encoders in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
body: Lines 114-115 ('ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger); ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);') create two encoders, allocate ByteArrayOutputStream buffers, write the BigIntegers, and immediately discard the results. They are not stored and not part of the DER sequence produced below. They are pure waste (two extra BigInteger.toByteArray() calls and allocations on every ECDSA sign/verify) and clearly look like a leftover from refactoring. They should be removed.

title: order() added as non-default method breaks third-party CryptoProvider implementations
body: CryptoProvider is a public interface in org.keycloak.common.crypto that is implemented by external modules (default/elytron/fips1402) and is part of the published keycloak-common artifact. Adding 'int order();' as an abstract method (instead of a default method) is an ABI break: every third-party or downstream implementation of CryptoProvider will fail to compile against the new release. Since the only purpose of order() is to pick between multiple implementations on the classpath, it should be 'default int order() { return 0; }' (or similar) so existing implementations keep working and the new AuthzClientCryptoProvider can opt in to a lower priority.

title: logger.debugf used with a preformatted message and no parameters
body: The new debug branch builds a StringBuilder of ignored provider names and then calls 'logger.debugf(builder.toString())'. debugf is the parameterized-format API; passing a plain string with no parameters means the string is treated as a format and any stray '%' would throw. It should be 'logger.debug(builder.toString())' (or 'logger.debugf("Ignored crypto providers: %s", joined)'). Same anti-pattern is present on line 63 which is pre-existing but worth aligning.

title: ECDSA conversion test only round-trips, does not validate against known vectors or wrong-key cases
body: ECDSAAlgorithmTest always generates a default-curve (P-256) EC key and runs the same round-trip (DER -> RS -> DER -> RS, equality) for ES256/ES384/ES512. This will pass even if the converter silently produces wrong-length outputs, drops leading bytes incorrectly for edge cases (r or s near q/2, r with high bit set, leading 0x00 from DER INTEGER), or works only because the specific test key avoids boundary values. There is also no test asserting the size of the produced concatenated/DER output, no negative-case test (truncated, malformed), and no test that exercises getBouncyCastleProvider/getKeyStore (whose implementation is actually wrong, see separate finding). Tests against a known signature vector per curve would catch real conversion bugs.

title: Breaking API change: order() added as abstract method
body: The new int order() method is added to the CryptoProvider interface as an abstract method with no default implementation. Any third-party implementation of CryptoProvider will fail to compile against this SPI. A default (e.g., `default int order() { return 100; }`) would preserve existing implementations while letting the in-tree providers (Default/FIPS/Elytron at 200, AuthzClient at 100) override it as needed. As-is, every external CryptoProvider consumer must be updated simultaneously.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns the default JDK provider, not BouncyCastle
body: The implementation returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, which on a stock JVM is SUN/SunJSSE/SunPKCS11 — not BouncyCastle. The method is named `getBouncyCastleProvider()` and the other implementations (DefaultCryptoProvider, FIPS1402Provider) genuinely return a BC-based provider, so callers expecting BC algorithms/properties on the returned Provider will silently get something else. Either return null (matching WildFlyElytronProvider) or add a BC provider lookup, and document the contract.

title: Dead code: ASN1Encoder instances are created and discarded
body: Lines 114-115 invoke `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger)` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger)` but never call `toByteArray()` nor capture the return value. The actual conversion happens in the immediately following `writeDerSeq(...)`, which constructs two brand-new encoders from the same BigIntegers. The two discarded encoder allocations plus two BigInteger-to-byte-array serializations are pure waste and look like a copy-paste mistake; they should be removed.

title: readSequence silently returns empty for indefinite-length encoding
body: If `readLength()` returns -1 (the indefinite-length form per X.690), the loop condition `while (length > 0)` is never entered (since -1 > 0 is false) and an empty `List` is returned without raising an error. DER forbids indefinite-length encoding, so encountering it indicates a malformed or non-DER input — silently returning an empty list masks the bug and lets the caller continue processing a bogus signature. The method should throw IOException when `length == -1`.

title: Test only verifies round-trip conversion, not signature correctness
body: The test signs data with the JDK provider, converts DER → RS → DER → RS via AuthzClientCryptoProvider, and asserts the two RS arrays match. It never checks that the resulting R/S actually correspond to the signature's real R and S components — a bug that swaps R/S, off-by-ones a byte, or always returns zeros would pass this test. Add an assertion that re-assembles a Signature from the converted bytes and runs `signature.verify()` against the original data and public key; also test negative cases (tampered DER, wrong length).

title: NPE risk when all-clients resource is missing
body: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when there is no resource for the specific client, the code falls back to loading the type-level resource via AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource(...). That method can return null (e.g., when supportsAuthorizationSchema is false, the type is unknown, or no resource has been created for the type yet). The subsequent authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty() call then dereferences a null resource and throws NullPointerException. The code should guard against a null 'resource' before passing it to findByResource, returning false instead.

title: getClientsWithPermission can return the resource type name as a client id
body: ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission iterates all resources whose type is 'Clients' and adds resource.getName() to the returned set for each resource the admin has the scope on. This includes the 'all-clients' resource whose name is the literal string 'Clients' (set in AdminPermissionsSchema.init). So when an admin has the scope for all clients, the returned set contains the entry 'Clients', which is not a client internal id. Callers expecting a Set<String> of client ids will then attempt to look up a client with id 'Clients' and fail. The method should skip the type-level resource (or filter its name) so only actual client ids end up in the set.

title: Listener no longer cleans up authz data for V2-only realms
body: The event listener for RoleRemovedEvent/ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent is now wrapped in a check for Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (the V1 feature). For realms that enable only ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2, the listener never runs at all, so on client/role/group removal no cleanup of the corresponding resources in the admin-permissions client occurs. Resources representing deleted clients (and any scope-based policies referencing them) become orphans in the authorization store. The change is needed to avoid UnsupportedOperationException from ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled, but the V2 side does not implement equivalent cleanup, so data integrity is now degraded. Either a V2 path that deletes the orphaned resources in the admin permissions client should be added, or the wrapper should also include the V2 feature and dispatch to a V2 cleanup.

title: canMapRoles / canMapCompositeRoles / canMapClientScopeRoles skip the admin-role check
body: Other V2 overrides such as canManage(ClientModel) and canManageClientScopes() first short-circuit on root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS), then fall back to the schema permission. canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles, and canMapClientScopeRoles only call hasPermission(client, ...) and never consult the admin roles. As a result, a caller that holds the MANAGE_CLIENTS realm role can manage/configure/view a client (and the V2 canView chains through canConfigure which calls canManage) but cannot map roles on it. This is inconsistent with the rest of the V2 evaluators and may surprise administrators; verify whether the V1 canMapRoles also gated on the admin role and, if so, restore the hasOneAdminRole short-circuit.

title: Unused imports, unused logger, and dead private method
body: ClientPermissionsV2 imports org.keycloak.authorization.model.Scope (line 27) and the static AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE (line 46) but neither symbol is referenced anywhere in the file. It also declares 'private static final Logger logger = Logger.getLogger(ClientPermissionsV2.class);' (line 51) and a private getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) method (lines 262-272) which is never called. These should be removed to keep the new file clean; if getEvaluationContext is intended for later use it should be marked as such or actually wired into the permission evaluation.

title: Mixed JUnit 4 / JUnit 5 imports in same test
body: PermissionClientTest imports 'static org.junit.Assert.fail' (JUnit 4) while every other fgap test in this PR (e.g. UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest) imports 'static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.fail' (JUnit 5), and the rest of PermissionClientTest already uses JUnit 5 annotations (@Test, @AfterEach from org.junit.jupiter.api). The mixed import is inconsistent and can lead to confusing failure signatures if the wrong Assert is ever picked up; switch to org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.fail to match the surrounding test suite.

title: Event listener feature-flag mismatch causes UnsupportedOperationException when both V1 and V2 FGAP are enabled
body: The event listener body is wrapped in `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ))`, but inside it calls `management(...)` which dispatches to MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is enabled. With the new `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` override, that path returns `ClientPermissionsV2`, whose `setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean)` now throws `UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. Before this PR, `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` inherited V1's implementation and the call worked. As a result, in a realm where both `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` and `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` are enabled, any `ClientRemovedEvent` (or `RoleRemovedEvent`/`GroupRemovedEvent` whose management path is also impacted) will raise `UnsupportedOperationException`. The check should be either `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ && !ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2`, or the calls into the V2 evaluator should be guarded so that the unsupported operation is not invoked when V2 is in effect.

title: Possible NPE in hasPermission when the "all-clients" resource does not exist
body: In `hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)`, when no per-client resource exists, the code falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)`. That method can return null (e.g., schema not yet initialized, `supportsAuthorizationSchema` returns false, unknown resource type, or `findByName` returns no row). The result is then passed unchecked to `authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource)`, which dereferences the resource (e.g., to read its id) and will throw NullPointerException. A null check is required before invoking `findByResource`.

title: getClientsWithPermission only enumerates the "all-clients" resource and misses individual client resources
body: `getClientsWithPermission(String scope)` iterates with `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)`. Only the type-resource created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init` (with type "Clients") matches this query, because `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` creates per-client resources without setting the `type` field (the `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId())` call never sets a type). Therefore (a) when a user has permission only via a per-client resource, `getClientsWithPermission` returns an empty set, and (b) when the user has an "all-clients" grant, the result contains the literal name "Clients" instead of the actual client IDs in the realm. Either the per-client resources must be created with `type = CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE`, or the enumeration should iterate all client resources (e.g., `resourceStore.findByName(server, ...)` for each client, or by a different store query).

title: No test exercises the MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope for clients
body: The new `ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel)` (and its corresponding schema scope `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE`) is declared on the interface and implemented, but `PermissionClientTest` does not contain a test case that grants `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` and verifies the associated behavior is allowed, nor a negative case. Only `MAP_ROLES` and `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE` are exercised through `testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient`. A dedicated test should be added so the new scope is covered by the test suite.

title: Several imports and a private helper are unused
body: The imports `org.jboss.logging.Logger`, `org.keycloak.authorization.common.ClientModelIdentity`, `org.keycloak.authorization.common.DefaultEvaluationContext`, `org.keycloak.authorization.model.Scope`, `org.keycloak.models.RealmModel`, `org.keycloak.representations.AccessToken`, the static import `org.keycloak.services.resources.admin.permissions.AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE`, and the private method `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken)` (plus the `Map`, `Collection`, `List` transitive uses it drags in) are not referenced anywhere in the file. The unused `private static final Logger logger` field and the dead `getEvaluationContext` helper should be removed to keep the class focused on the implementation that is actually wired up.

title: getClientsWithPermission includes the "Clients" all-resource name in result set
body: resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) iterates over every resource of type "Clients", which includes both per-client resources (named client.getId()) and the all-clients resource created in AdminPermissionsSchema.init() with the name "Clients". When the caller holds an all-clients scope permission, hasGrantedPermission returns true for that all-clients resource and the literal string "Clients" is added to the returned set alongside any real client UUIDs. Callers using this set to filter or load clients will misinterpret the resource-type string as a client ID (lookups will fail) and the absence of a distinct "all" indicator means the all-clients case is silently lost. The loop must either skip the all-clients resource (compare resource.getName() to AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) or model the all-clients case as a separate sentinel.

title: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) can NPE when all-clients resource is missing
body: When no per-client resource exists, the code loads the all-clients resource via AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...). If the schema resource server has not been initialized (or the resource was otherwise removed), getResourceTypeResource returns null, and the subsequent authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) is invoked with a null resource and throws a NullPointerException. This path is reached on every per-client permission check when no all-clients policy has been created yet, so it is reachable in production during early realm setup. Add a null check on the resource returned from getResourceTypeResource before calling findByResource.

title: registerListener gates V2-only deployments off event-driven cleanup
body: The new wrapper uses Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) (the legacy V1 flag), but the listener body delegates to management(...) which dispatches on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 and can return MgmtPermissionsV2. When a realm runs with only V2 enabled and V1 disabled, the entire listener body is now skipped, so ClientRemovedEvent, RoleRemovedEvent, and GroupRemovedEvent will not trigger any cleanup of the V2 resources/scopes/policies those objects back. The check needs to consider ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 (either in addition to or instead of the V1 flag) so that pure-V2 realms still receive the event-driven cleanup.

title: Javadocs on several interface methods omit V2 behavior notes
body: Methods such as canList(), requireList(), canViewClientScopes(), requireViewClientScopes(), canListClientScopes(), requireListClientScopes(), and requireView() are newly documented in this PR but, unlike canManage/canView/canView(ClientModel)/canConfigure(ClientModel)/canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles, do not include the "For V2 only: ..." clause that explains the FGAP fallback used by ClientPermissionsV2. Because ClientPermissionsV2 does not override any of these (canList/canViewClientScopes/canListClientScopes all fall through to the V1 implementation), readers cannot tell how these methods behave under ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Add the missing "For V2 only" notes (or note explicitly that they inherit V1 behavior unchanged) so the contract is clear.

title: No integration test for VIEW-per-client or all-clients CONFIGURE / MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE in V2
body: PermissionClientTest adds coverage for MANAGE per-client (testManageOnlyOneClient), CONFIGURE per-client (testConfigureOnlyOneClient), MANAGE all-clients (testManageAllClients), VIEW all-clients (testViewAllClients), and MAP_ROLES+MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE per-client (testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient). It never exercises VIEW scoped to a single client, CONFIGURE granted on the all-clients resource, or MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE at all. Since ClientPermissionsV2.canView(ClientModel), canConfigure(ClientModel) (all-clients branch in hasPermission) and canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel) are brand new code paths, at least one positive and one negative test for each is needed to lock in behavior; without them, regressions in those branches (for example the "Clients" leak in getClientsWithPermission, or the NPE in hasPermission) will not be caught.

title: Exit code 4 description is misleading
body: The documentation for exit code 4 says 'Rolling Upgrade is not possible. The feature `rolling-updates` is disabled.', but the actual behavior (see `printFeatureDisabled()` in `AbstractUpdatesCommand.java` and the new `testFeatureNotEnabled` in `UpdateCommandDistTest.java`) is that the command never runs at all and prints 'Unable to use this command. The preview feature `rolling-updates` is not enabled.' Scripts that rely on exit code 4 to decide between rolling and recreate will be misled: the deployment may be perfectly eligible for a rolling upgrade; the code only signals that the user must enable the feature first. The row should describe 'Command unavailable: preview feature `rolling-updates` is not enabled' (or similar), not 'Rolling Upgrade is not possible'.

title: Caution claim that the Operator will fail is inaccurate
body: The CAUTION block states: 'While on preview stage, the feature `rolling-updates` must be enabled. Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail.' But the very next NOTE in the same section documents a default behavior that works without the feature: 'the update strategy defaults to mimicking Keycloak 26.1 or older behavior'. The Operator does not 'fail' when the feature is disabled; it only fails if the user supplies the new `spec.update.strategy` field without enabling the feature. The wording should be tightened to make that conditional explicit (e.g., '...must be enabled if you set `spec.update.strategy`').

title: Breaking change of exit code for recreate upgrade (4 -> 3)
body: `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` was changed from 4 to 3, and a new `FEATURE_DISABLED` constant took the value 4. Any external automation (CI/CD scripts, GitOps pipelines) that key off exit code 4 to detect 'recreate upgrade needed' will now interpret it as 'feature disabled' instead, taking the wrong branch. The previous public exit-code contract (4 == recreate, per the prior docs and code) is broken without a migration note. Either keep 4 as recreate and pick a new value for FEATURE_DISABLED, or call out the breaking change explicitly so downstream users can update their scripts.

title: No test for `check` subcommand with feature disabled
body: The new `testFeatureNotEnabled` only exercises the `metadata` subcommand (line 48: `@Launch({UpdateCompatibility.NAME, UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.NAME})`). The same feature gate was added to `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` (UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java lines 46-50), but there is no equivalent test for the `check` subcommand to confirm it also prints 'Unable to use this command. The preview feature `rolling-updates` is not enabled.' and exits with code 4. A symmetric test (e.g., `testFeatureNotEnabledForCheck`) should be added.

title: testFeatureNotEnabled does not assert exit code 4
body: The new `testFeatureNotEnabled` only asserts the stderr error message; it does not verify that the process actually exits with `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED` (4). If a future change accidentally leaves the default 0 exit code, this test would still pass. The other tests in this file (e.g., `testCompatible` at line 75) do call `assertEquals(0, result.exitCode())`, so adding a similar exit-code assertion here would be consistent and catch regressions in the exit-code wiring in `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()`.

title: YAML example uses non-YAML placeholder `Recreate|<not set>`
body: The CR example shows `strategy: Recreate|<not set>`, which is not a valid YAML scalar and will be rejected (or stored as the literal string 'Recreate|<not set>') if a user copies the snippet verbatim. The pre-existing doc had the same issue and the PR was a natural place to fix it. The placeholder should be replaced with a valid value (e.g., a separate example with `strategy: Recreate` and a NOTE explaining that omitting the field means default behavior).

title: printFeatureDisabled hard-codes the feature name in the error message
body: `printFeatureDisabled()` hard-codes the literal string 'rolling-updates' in the message: `printError("Unable to use this command. The preview feature 'rolling-updates' is not enabled.");`.
