The method is now a reusable helper in `AbstractUpdatesCommand` and other preview-gated commands may follow the same pattern; if any of them is gated on a different feature, the message will be wrong. Either parameterize the method with the feature name, or rename it to something feature-specific (e.g., `printRollingUpdatesDisabled()`) so misuse is obvious.

title: picocli.exit() does not halt execution; rely on `return` only
body: In `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` (and the identical block in `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()` at lines 46-50), the disabled-feature branch uses `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED);` followed by `return;`. picocli's `CommandLine.exit(int)` only stores the requested exit code; it does not terminate the JVM or the run() method. The `return` is what actually prevents `validateConfig()` and the rest of the body from running. The code is correct, but the chosen API is misleading and a future refactor that drops the `return` (or calls `picocli.exit()` from a helper) would silently execute the rest of the command. Consider using `throw new ParameterException(...)` or letting the framework short-circuit, so the early-return contract is enforced rather than incidental.

title: Exit code 4 silently reassigned, breaking scripts that check for recreate upgrade
body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was 4 and is now 3; the new FEATURE_DISABLED constant takes the previous value of 4. Any consumer that was scripting against `update-compatibility check` and matching exit code 4 to detect a recreate-upgrade outcome will now silently treat a 'feature disabled' failure as a recreate upgrade. The error messages differ but the exit code, which is what the docs recommend scripts rely on ('they should rely only on the exit code of the `check` command'), has changed. Even for a preview feature this is a contract break worth calling out in the release notes; alternatively, reserve a new code (e.g., 5) for FEATURE_DISABLED and leave RECREATE at 4 to preserve backward compatibility.

title: Exit code 4 description is misleading
body: The exit-code table describes code 4 as 'Rolling Upgrade is not possible. The feature `rolling-updates` is disabled.', but in this case the command does not actually determine whether a rolling upgrade is possible — `AbstractUpdatesCommand.printFeatureDisabled()` short-circuits the command and prints 'Unable to use this command. The preview feature `rolling-updates` is not enabled.' before any compatibility analysis. The wording should make it clear that the command itself could not run (e.g., 'The command cannot run. The feature `rolling-updates` is disabled.') rather than implying a compatibility verdict was reached.

title: testFeatureNotEnabled does not assert exit code 4
body: The test only verifies the stderr error message produced by `printFeatureDisabled()`, but the contract introduced by this PR is also that the command exits with CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED (4). The PR description and the docs explicitly state 'they should rely only on the exit code of the `check` command', so the test for the new exit code should assert `cliResult.exitCode() == 4` (and ideally `assertExitCode`-style). Without it, an implementation that returned exit code 0 (or any other value) while still printing the message would not be caught.

title: No coverage for UpdateCompatibilityCheck with feature disabled
body: `testFeatureNotEnabled` only exercises `update-compatibility metadata` when the feature is disabled. `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` has the same feature gate added (see quarkus/runtime/.../UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java) and is the more important subcommand for users (per docs: 'they should rely only on the exit code of the `check` command'). A symmetric test launching `update-compatibility check` without `--features=rolling-updates` and asserting both the error message and exit code 4 is needed to prevent regressions in the check subcommand.

title: Breaking change: recreate-upgrade exit code changed from 4 to 3
body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was changed from 4 to 3 to free up exit code 4 for the new FEATURE_DISABLED case. This silently changes the public CLI contract of `kc.sh update-compatibility check` for any existing user. Pipelines/scripts that detect a required recreate upgrade by checking `if [ $? -eq 4 ]` will no longer match and will incorrectly conclude the deployment succeeded or that the feature was disabled. Because the PR description does not call this out as a breaking change and the docs are updated as if the new mapping was always in effect, users upgrading will be broken without warning. The change should either be reverted (keep 4 for recreate and pick another code for FEATURE_DISABLED, e.g. 5) or prominently documented as a breaking change in the release notes.

title: No test for `update-compatibility check` when the rolling-updates feature is disabled
body: The new `testFeatureNotEnabled` only exercises `update-compatibility metadata` without enabling the feature. The matching code path in `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` that prints `printFeatureDisabled()` and exits with `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED` (=4) is left uncovered. A symmetric test such as `@Launch({UpdateCompatibility.NAME, UpdateCompatibilityCheck.NAME})` asserting the same error message would lock in the contract for both subcommands and prevent one of them silently regressing.

title: CAUTION overstates behavior: operator does not fail when feature is disabled unless spec.update.strategy is set
body: The CAUTION says "While on preview stage, the feature `rolling-updates` must be enabled. Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail." This is misleading: the operator still functions with the default (legacy) update strategy when the feature is not enabled, as demonstrated by `UpgradeTest.createInitialDeployment` whose `updateStrategy == null` branch returns the Keycloak CR without enabling the feature and the test still passes. The wording should clarify that the feature is only required when the user sets `spec.update.strategy`; otherwise readers may believe enabling rolling-updates is mandatory for any Keycloak deployment.

title: CAUTION removed the prior TODO without leaving context for readers
body: The diff replaces a one-line `// TODO Link to discussion?` comment with a CAUTION block. While the new CAUTION is informative, it does not link to or mention the discussion referenced by `previewDiscussionLink` (keycloak/keycloak#36785), even though the discussion is the canonical place for users to give feedback while the command is preview. Either keep a pointer to the discussion or rely on `previewDiscussionLink` already being rendered at the top of the page, but ensure the CAUTION does not inadvertently hide the feedback channel from users experimenting with the tool.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission passes resource UUID where group ID is needed
body: Inside the lambda passed to resourceStore.findByType(), the code calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) and adds groupResource.getId() to the granted set. However, hasPermission(String groupId, ...) does findByName(server, groupId), which looks up the resource by NAME (the group's ID), not by the resource's database UUID. In V2 per-group resources are named with the group ID, but getId() returns the resource's own UUID - these are different. findByName will always return null for these lookups, and hasPermission will fall back to the schema (all-groups) resource for every iteration. Consequences: (1) An admin with VIEW_MEMBERS permission only on a specific group will get an empty granted set, so the user search will not filter by groups and no users will be visible (in V2 mode, testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers and testCanViewUserByManageGroupMembers in the new test class would fail). (2) When the admin has the VIEW_MEMBERS scope on the all-groups schema resource, the granted set is populated with the resource UUIDs instead of group IDs, making the value unusable downstream. The V1 analogue in GroupPermissions correctly passes the Resource object directly and strips the name prefix; the V2 version should use groupResource.getName() both in the hasPermission call and when adding to the granted set.

title: canManage() in V2 treats VIEW permission as sufficient for MANAGE actions
body: canManage() returns true when the caller has either VIEW or MANAGE permission on the all-groups schema resource: return hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE). This means an admin with only VIEW permission on Groups can call requireManage() (no-arg) at GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup and successfully create new top-level groups, even though they explicitly lack MANAGE. This is also inconsistent with canManage(GroupModel group) in the same file (lines 73-80), which only permits MANAGE, not VIEW. In V1, canManage() required only the MANAGE_USERS admin role, so VIEW_USERS-like capabilities were correctly excluded. The docstring was updated to mention VIEW, but the behavior contradicts least-privilege and makes 'has VIEW on all groups' grant more capability than 'has MANAGE on a specific group'. The new testManageAllGroups test grants MANAGE explicitly and therefore does not cover or detect this case.

title: resolveGroup only resolves by ID, not by name/path
body: resolveGroup just calls session.groups().getGroupById(realm, id) and returns null when the group is not found. In contrast, resolveUser additionally falls back to getUserByUsername and resolveClient falls back to getClientByClientId. If the id passed to getOrCreateResource is a group name or path (which can happen if a caller misinterprets the field, or if group representation identifiers evolve), getOrCreateResource will fail with 'Could not map resource object with type [Groups] and id [name]'. While the current code paths pass group.getId() (a UUID), the asymmetry with users and clients is worth a comment or alignment so a future caller is not surprised by the silent null.

title: GroupResource.getManagementPermissions/setManagementPermissionsEnabled will crash if invoked under V2
body: GroupPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException for isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, viewPermission, managePermission, viewMembersPermission, manageMembersPermission, manageMembershipPermission, and getPermissions. The REST endpoints GroupResource.getManagementPermissions and setManagementPermissionsEnabled (lines 321-365 of GroupResource.java) call these methods after only gating on Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ. If a deployment enables ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 together with (or instead of) V1 such that the endpoint is reachable but mgmt() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, the endpoint will throw UnsupportedOperationException on the first request. The endpoints should at least be gated on Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 being absent (i.e., only callable when V1 is the active mode), or V2 should provide a meaningful non-throwing implementation that returns the resource representation for the V2 resource-type resource.

title: New V2 group permissions behavior is not exercised in V2 mode
body: The five new tests in GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest rely on the V1 path: they create permissions via createPermission/createAllPermission scoped under the FGAP-managed client. If the same test is run with ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled, the implementations in GroupPermissionsV2 (canView, canManage, canViewMembers, canManageMembers, canManageMembership, getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, etc.) will be invoked, and - given the bug in getGroupIdsWithViewPermission - several tests (notably testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers and testCanViewUserByManageGroupMembers, where the search filter depends on UserModel.GROUPS being set from getGroupIdsWithViewPermission) will fail. Add a parallel V2 test class (or a parameterized config that also enables ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2) to cover the new V2 code paths before merging.

title: V2 getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses resource UUID instead of group name
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() (line 122), the lambda iterates over resources of type "Groups" and calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) while also adding groupResource.getId() to the granted set. groupResource.getId() is the resource's internal UUID (a system-generated identifier), but the contract of getGroupIdsWithViewPermission requires group IDs (GroupModel.getId()), which are stored as the resource's name. Two consequences follow: (1) hasPermission does findByName(server, groupId) with the resource UUID, so per-group resources (which are named with the group ID) are never matched and the code always falls through to the all-groups resource check. As a result per-group V2 permissions are effectively ignored when computing the visible-group set. (2) The set returned to callers contains resource UUIDs, not group IDs, so downstream consumers (UsersResource.searchForUser / getUsersCount and BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser) end up storing nonsense values in session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, ...) and passing them to user search/count queries, producing wrong results and silent functional regressions whenever an admin has any level of V2 group VIEW_MEMBERS / MANAGE_MEMBERS permission. The fix should be hasPermission(groupResource.getName(), ...) and granted.add(groupResource.getName()). Existing GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest cases do not exercise the all-groups-level permission path, so they do not detect this regression.

title: Potential NPE when all-groups resource cannot be resolved
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission (lines 144-150), when groupId-specific lookup returns null the code falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...).getResourceTypeResource can return null (e.g. when supportsAuthorizationSchema is false, the resourceType is unknown, or the all-groups resource was never created). That null value is then passed unchecked to policyStore.findByResource(server, resource), which on the common JPA/in-memory store implementations will NPE. A simple null check on the result of getResourceTypeResource, or treating a null return as "no all-groups resource -> no permission", would make the code robust.

title: JavaDoc says getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns a Stream
body: The JavaDoc on GroupPermissionEvaluator.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission (added in this PR, line 144-147) reads "@return Stream of IDs of groups with view permission." but the declared return type (and the implementations in both GroupPermissions and GroupPermissionsV2) is Set<String>. Either the wording "Stream of IDs" is a leftover that should be "Set of IDs", or the return type was meant to be a stream. This is the only contract documentation of a method that several other files depend on, so it should be accurate.

title: NPE potential when all-groups resource lookup returns null
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission, when the per-group lookup fails the code calls `resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE);` and on the next line dereferences it directly with `if (policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty())`. getResourceTypeResource can return null when supportsAuthorizationSchema is false or when the synthetic all-groups resource has not been created. The missing null check will throw NullPointerException on the first FGAP V2 group-evaluation call that hits this path. The guard must be `resource == null || policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()` (or equivalent) before evaluating permissions.

title: Same NPE pattern in UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission fallback
body: UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission assigns `resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE);` and immediately dereferences it on the next line in `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()`. If the all-users resource does not exist (e.g., schema not yet initialised) this throws NullPointerException, breaking V2 per-user evaluations (canView/canManage/canMapRoles/canImpersonate/canManageGroupMembership on a specific user). A null guard before the policy lookup is required.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission only sees the all-groups resource, ignoring individual group permissions
body: The implementation iterates `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, …)`, but `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` never sets the resource type on the per-entity resources it creates (see AdminPermissionsSchema.java around line 121), so `findByType("Groups", …)` returns only the synthetic all-groups resource created during `init()`. In addition the lambda calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), …)` (a UUID produced by the resource store) while `hasPermission` resolves resources by `findByName` against the group UUID, and then `granted.add(groupResource.getId())` adds the resource UUID into a set that callers (UsersResource.searchForUser and BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser) treat as group IDs to populate `UserModel.GROUPS`. The net effect is that group-specific VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions are completely ignored; only a permission on the all-groups resource can populate the set. As a consequence, an admin whose only permissions are scoped to a specific group will not be filtered to members of that group when listing users, and the new test `testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers` cannot pass under FGAP V2.

title: Individually-created resources are not tagged with their resource type
body: In `getOrCreateResource` the path that creates a missing per-entity resource (`resource = resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId()); … resource.updateScopes(…)`) never calls `resource.setType(resourceType)`. By contrast `init()` does set the type when it pre-creates the all-groups/all-users/all-clients resources. Anything that relies on `ResourceStore.findByType` (such as GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, which iterates `findByType("Groups", …)`) will therefore only see the synthesised resources and miss the per-entity ones. Add `resource.setType(resourceType);` after `updateScopes` so that later type-filtered lookups see per-entity resources.

title: HTML_TAGS regex misses closing tags and uppercase tags
body:
The regex `Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>")` only matches opening tags whose name consists of lowercase ASCII letters. Closing tags like `

` and uppercase tags like `
` will not be detected. The `containsHtml` decision gates whether POLICY_SOME_HTML or POLICY_NO_HTML is applied to translations, so any English source that contains only closing tags or uppercase tags will be treated as having no HTML. The translation will then be sanitized with POLICY_NO_HTML, which will escape those tags (e.g., `

` becomes `</p>`), making them appear as literal text in the rendered UI.

title: Method name typo `santizeAnchors`
body: The method is named `santizeAnchors` (missing 'i'). Should be `sanitizeAnchors`. This is cosmetic but reflects on code quality.

title: Missing English file throws RuntimeException, crashing the verifier
body: When the English counterpart file cannot be found (e.g., for a brand new translation that has no `_en.properties` source yet, or for a locale like `es_419` whose suffix contains digits and so does not match the locale-detection regex on line 75), the FileInputStream constructor throws FileNotFoundException, which is caught and rewrapped as `new RuntimeException("unable to read file " + englishFile, e)`. Because `verifySafeHtml` does not declare any checked exceptions and `verify()` only catches `IOException`, this RuntimeException propagates out of the Mojo, bypassing the normal MojoExecutionException error path. The result is that any file whose English source is missing will abort the entire verification, instead of producing a clean message.

title: Locale-suffix regex doesn't accept digits, blocking non-Latin locale files
body: The path translation `replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")` only matches locale suffixes that consist entirely of ASCII letters, hyphen and underscore. BCP-47 derived locales that include digits (e.g. `es_419`, `en_US_POSIX`, or numeric region sub-tags) will not match the regex, so `replaceAll` is a no-op and `englishFile` equals `file`. The code then tries to load the same file as its own English source and either crashes (because the regex `_[a-zA-Z-_]*` excludes digits) or silently validates a translation against itself. The character class also includes the underscore, which is fragile when suffixes themselves contain underscores (e.g. `zh_CN`).

title: Magic string `<!-- -->` removed unconditionally from sanitized output
body: After `policy.sanitize(value)` and `unescapeHtml4`, the code does `sanitized = sanitized.replace("<!-- -->", "")`. This hardcoded string is presumed to be what the OWASP sanitizer inserts to disambiguate content, but the OWASP library is not part of the project's source, so this is an undocumented and version-dependent contract. If a future OWASP release inserts a different placeholder (e.g. `<!---->` without space, `<!---->`, or HTML-escaped form), the replacement will silently stop working and the sanitizer output will be reported as illegal HTML for any translation containing double curly braces. Worse, the replacement is applied unconditionally even when the original `value` legitimately contains the substring `<!-- -->`, in which case legitimate comments are silently stripped and the comparison will erroneously consider the value 'clean'.

title: replaceFirst in santizeAnchors operates on a value mutated by previous iterations
body: In `santizeAnchors`, the Matcher is constructed from the original `value`, so `matcher.find()` continues to identify anchors at their original positions even after the body of the loop has replaced earlier occurrences in `value`. When the value contains the same anchor twice (e.g. two `<a href="X">`), the first iteration replaces the first occurrence in the (still identical) value, but the second iteration tries `value.replaceFirst(englishMatcher.group(), "")` on the already-shortened string, which no longer contains that anchor at that position. The replacement becomes a no-op, the loop advances to the next match in the original string, and the second anchor ends up compared against the next English anchor (or causes a spurious 'did not find anchor tag' message). The logic should either rebuild the Matcher after each replacement or use indices rather than `replaceFirst` to align modifications.

title: POLICY_SOME_HTML and POLICY_NO_HTML should be static final
body: `PolicyFactory POLICY_SOME_HTML = new org.owasp.html.HtmlPolicyBuilder()...toFactory();` and the corresponding `POLICY_NO_HTML` are declared as instance fields on a class that has only instance state (`file`, `messages`). They should be `private static final` so they are constructed once per JVM rather than per VerifyMessageProperties instance and so that the class clearly expresses they are constants.

title: Comment about `<!-- -->` placement is unclear and possibly wrong
body: The block comment on lines 96-97 reads `// Sanitizer will add them when there are double curly braces`, where 'them' is ambiguous (HTML comments? entities?). The actual rationale is that the OWASP policy inserts an HTML comment to separate ambiguous sequences, not specifically 'when there are double curly braces'. Anyone reading this code in the future will not understand the dependency on OWASP's exact placeholder format. A short, accurate comment (and ideally an OWASP API that exposes skipped content) would prevent future breakage.

title: No test coverage for closing/uppercase HTML tags or English missing file
body:
The new tests cover duplicate keys, illegal HTML tags in an English file (`illegalHtmlTag_en.properties`), a non-English file with `` (noHtml_de.properties) and a changed anchor (`changedAnchor_de.properties`). They do not cover the scenarios where the English source contains only a closing tag (e.g. `

`), only uppercase tags, a translation that is missing keys present in the English source, an English source file that is missing entirely, or translations where the order of identical anchors differs. Given that the verifier's correctness depends on these edge cases, at least one negative test for 'English has only closing tags -> POLICY_NO_HTML is wrongly applied' should be added.

title: verifySafeHtml throws RuntimeException on missing English file, crashing the Maven build
body: When the English counterpart file (computed via `file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll("resources-community","resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties","_en.properties")`) does not exist, the catch block wraps the `FileNotFoundException` as `new RuntimeException("unable to read file " + englishFile, e)`. The caller `verify()` only catches `IOException` (line 52), so the `RuntimeException` propagates and aborts the Maven build with an uncaught-exception stack trace instead of a clean Mojo-level error. For any property file under `resources-community` whose English sibling is missing or whose path does not match the assumed layout, the theme-verifier plugin will crash. The fix is to declare `throws MojoExecutionException` on `verifySafeHtml` (or wrap the call into `try { … } catch (IOException|RuntimeException e) { throw new MojoExecutionException(..., e); }` in `verify()`).

title: Lithuanian totpStep1 was replaced with Italian text
body: The line was changed from the Lithuanian string `totpStep1=Įdiekite FreeOTP arba Google Authenticator savo įrenginyje. …` to `totpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`. The new value is Italian, not Lithuanian, so users with the Lithuanian locale will see Italian text in the account UI. The sanitizer does not detect this because it only checks HTML structure, not translation correctness, and the corresponding English source (`Install one of the following applications on your mobile:`) has no HTML so POLICY_NO_HTML is used. The right value should be a Lithuanian translation of the English source.

title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 was replaced with Italian text
body: Same regression as in the account bundle: `loginTotpStep1=Įdiekite FreeOTP arba Google Authenticator savo įrenginyje. …` was replaced by `loginTotpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`. Lithuanian users will see Italian text on the login TOTP step-up page.

title: Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) bundle uses Traditional Chinese characters
body: The new `totpStep1=在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：` mixes Traditional-only characters (`機`, `裝`, `應用`, `程式`) into the zh-CN resource bundle, which is supposed to be Simplified Chinese. The rest of the file is Simplified. Mixing scripts causes inconsistent rendering depending on the viewer's font fallback chain and breaks the zh-CN/zh-TW separation. The expected translation should use Simplified forms (手机, 安装, 应用, 程序).

title: HTML_TAGS regex is case-sensitive and misses uppercase tags
body:
`Pattern HTML_TAGS = Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>");` only matches lower-case tag names. Real-world translations can use mixed-case or upper-case tags (e.g., `
`, `

`). When the English source uses such tags, `containsHtml` returns false, `POLICY_NO_HTML` is selected instead of `POLICY_SOME_HTML`, and legitimate allowed elements such as `
` in the translation get stripped, producing a false "Illegal HTML" error. Either compile the pattern with `Pattern.CASE_INSENSITIVE` or use `[a-zA-Z]+`.

title: Locale-matching regex includes unintended characters due to misplaced `-`
body: The pattern `"_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties"` contains the character class `[a-zA-Z-_]`. Java's regex interprets the `-` between `Z` and `_` as a range, so the class actually matches `a-z`, `A-Z`, `[`, `\\`, `]`, `^`, `_`. For typical locale codes (`de`, `zh_CN`, etc.) this happens to work, but a malformed locale segment could be accepted. Move the `-` to the end of the class to make it literal: `_[a-zA-Z_-]*\\.properties`.

title: PolicyFactory instances are not static final
body: `POLICY_SOME_HTML` and `POLICY_NO_HTML` are non-static instance fields initialized in each `VerifyMessageProperties` instance, and are declared after the constructor and `verify()` method. They are immutable and shared between instances, so they should be `private static final`. This avoids rebuilding the OWASP policies for every file checked and makes the intent explicit.

title: Typo in method name: 'santizeAnchors' should be 'sanitizeAnchors'
body: The helper that strips matching anchor tags is misspelled `santizeAnchors` (missing the second `i`). Rename to `sanitizeAnchors`.

title: getEnglishValue silently swallows MissingResourceException
body: If a key is present in the translation bundle but missing from the English bundle, `getEnglishValue` catches `MissingResourceException` and returns the empty string. The sanitizer then evaluates the translation against `englishValue=""`: `containsHtml` is false so `POLICY_NO_HTML` is used, which strips any HTML the translation has and produces a spurious "Illegal HTML" error. A missing English key should be reported as a separate problem (out-of-sync bundles) rather than masked as if English had no HTML for that key. Either rethrow `MissingResourceException` as a dedicated message or treat the missing-English-key case explicitly.

title: verifySafeHtml is under-tested
body:
The new test class only covers four scenarios: duplicate keys, an illegal tag in an English file, a German `` translation whose English has no HTML, and a changed-anchor URL. Important paths of `verifySafeHtml` are not exercised: (a) translation with `
`/`` when English has HTML (allowed-element case), (b) translation containing a `

title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
body: The `totpStep1` key previously held a Lithuanian translation (`Įdiekite <a href="https://freeotp.github.io/"...`) that was replaced with Italian text (`Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`). The neighboring keys `totpStep2` and `totpStep3` remain in Lithuanian, so the file becomes internally inconsistent. This is a translation regression: the original Lithuanian content is lost and a wrong-language string is now displayed to Lithuanian users. The new HTML sanitizer cannot catch this since it only validates HTML safety, not language correctness.

title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
body: The `loginTotpStep1` key previously held a Lithuanian translation (`Įdiekite <a href="https://freeotp.github.io/"...`) and was replaced with the Italian string `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`. Surrounding `loginTotpStep2` and `loginTotpStep3` are still Lithuanian, making the file internally inconsistent. The Lithuanian translation is now lost to users. The new sanitizer does not verify language matches and therefore will not detect this regression.

title: Simplified Chinese translation replaced with Traditional Chinese
body: The `totpStep1` key in this Simplified Chinese file (zh_CN) was changed from Simplified Chinese text (`在你的设备上安装 ... Google Authenticator.两个应用可以从 ...`) to Traditional Chinese text (`在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：`). Characters like `您`, `手機`, `安裝`, `程式` are Traditional; the file should use Simplified forms. zh_CN users will now see Traditional Chinese on this screen, breaking locale expectations.

title: English source `templateHelp` typo `<NAME >` not fixed
body: The English source string `templateHelp` contains `CLAIM.<NAME > ...` with a stray trailing space inside the angle brackets (`<NAME >` instead of `<NAME>`). The Chinese translation in `messages_zh_CN.properties` was corrected to `CLAIM.<NAME>`, but the English source on which all other translations are based still contains the typo. Any future translation that copies the English literally will reintroduce the typo. The verifier handles this for `templateHelp` via `normalizeValue`, but only for that specific key; the underlying source string is inconsistent with the rest of the translations.

title: HTML_TAGS regex is too restrictive for HTML detection
body: `HTML_TAGS` is defined as `Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>")`. This only matches tags whose first character after `<` is a lowercase ASCII letter, so `<DIV>`, `<H1>`, `<h1>`, `<a1>` and any tag name containing a digit or uppercase letter will not be detected. The OWASP sanitizer is case-insensitive and HTML spec tags are case-insensitive, so this leads to false negatives in `containsHtml()` and inconsistent classification between POLICY_SOME_HTML and POLICY_NO_HTML. In practice this can produce false positives (e.g. English `<H1>` falls through to POLICY_NO_HTML, the sanitizer strips the tag, and the verifier reports `Illegal HTML` for the translation even though both sides are identical). Fix by using a case-insensitive pattern or by parsing via the sanitizer itself.

title: verifySafeHtml throws RuntimeException, not MojoExecutionException
body: `verifySafeHtml()` is called from `verify()` which declares `throws MojoExecutionException`. However `verifySafeHtml()` catches `IOException` and rethrows it as `new RuntimeException(...)`. A `RuntimeException` is not caught by the surrounding `catch (IOException e)` block in `verify()`, so it propagates unchecked and aborts the build with an unhandled exception instead of being wrapped into a `MojoExecutionException` with the existing error formatting. Either rethrow as `MojoExecutionException` (and declare it) or add the message to the `messages` list so the build produces a useful diagnostic.

title: Method name `santizeAnchors` is misspelled
body: `santizeAnchors` should be spelled `sanitizeAnchors`. This is a public-facing method name (well, package-private, but reachable as a Java identifier in the codebase), so the typo propagates to anyone reading or extending the code.

title: Limited test coverage of HTML sanitizer behavior
body: The added tests cover only the simplest cases: duplicate keys, illegal HTML tag, HTML where the English has none, and changed anchor URL. They do not cover: (1) the legitimate-translation case where English has HTML and target has the same HTML (which should pass); (2) case-insensitive HTML in the English source; (3) HTML-like placeholders such as `<NAME>` or `<USERNAME>` in messages that are not whitelisted in `normalizeValue`; (4) multiple anchors; (5) anchors that differ only in inner text but keep the same URL (legitimate translations of link text); (6) `errorTitleHtml`-style keys where the English contains `<strong>` and the translation must keep it. Adding these tests would catch regressions in the sanitizer logic and the normalization rules.

title: normalizeValue special-cases only a few keys, risking false positives
body: `normalizeValue` strips HTML-looking content only for `templateHelp`, `optimizeLookupHelp`, `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*`, and `error-invalid-multivalued-size`. Any other message that legitimately contains text resembling an HTML tag (e.g., `<NAME>`, `<USERNAME>`, `<EMAIL>`, or any other MessageFormat placeholder that the translator chose to write with angle brackets) will be stripped by the OWASP sanitizer under POLICY_NO_HTML and the verifier will incorrectly report `Illegal HTML`. For example, any key like `fooBarTemplate=Hello <NAME>` will fail verification because `<NAME>` is not an allowed tag. Either broaden the placeholder normalization or detect via the sanitizer whether the English contains any disallowed HTML before applying POLICY_NO_HTML (i.e., compare normalized values against sanitized English, not against the raw translation).

title: Constructor null-check uses wrong argument for rawTokenId
isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic
Shortcut-collision validation does not catch duplicate shortcuts
Unchecked cast to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory in postInit
body: `postInit` performs `(OAuth2GrantTypeFactory) factory1` for every factory returned by `getProviderFactoriesStream(OAuth2GrantType.class)`. The stream type only guarantees `ProviderFactory<OAuth2GrantType>`, not `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory`. Any third-party extension that registers an `OAuth2GrantType` without implementing `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` will cause a `ClassCastException` at server startup. Either filter on `instanceof OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` or guarantee the relationship contractually.

title: Adding abstract method to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory breaks existing implementations
body: `getShortcut()` is added to `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` without a default implementation. Although the interface lives in `server-spi-private`, external grant-type extensions routinely implement it (every Keycloak extension that adds a custom grant does so). Adding a non-default method is a compile-time breaking change for any such extension and a runtime ClassCastException/NoSuchMethodError for those loaded by reflection before recompilation. Consider providing a default (e.g. returning the first two characters of `getId()`, or `UNKNOWN`) so that existing custom factories keep working.

title: Removed Context copy constructor
body: The `Context(Context context)` copy constructor that was previously on `OAuth2GrantType.Context` is deleted. The diff message is misleading - the constructor was not just unused inside these files, but is part of a private SPI that custom grant extensions may rely on (e.g. to clone context to a sub-task or to wrap it for retries). The deleted constructor also closes the door on the previously available pattern of reusing one `Context`. Either keep it, deprecate it, or document clearly that this SPI is consumed by external extensions.

title: getShouldUseLightweightToken widened from package-private to public
body: `getShouldUseLightweightToken` is changed from package-private to `public static`. This is required for the new encoder to reach it, but it is also expanding the public surface of an unrelated class in ways not strictly required by the PR (a small package-private helper on a wrapper class would have been enough). Either keep it package-private and move the lightweight-token resolution into `AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper` itself, or accept the API widening and document it.

title: Test relies on NPE rather than the intended IllegalArgumentException
body: `testIncorrectGrantType` exercises the unknown-shortcut path (`ac` is not in the manually populated map) but never calls `factory.postInit(...)`, so `getGrantTypeByShortcut` ends up dereferencing the null `sessionFactory` and throws NullPointerException, which is then swallowed by the `catch (RuntimeException)` clause. The test passes only because NPE happens to extend `RuntimeException`. The test should populate the maps explicitly (as it already does), or use `assertThrows(IllegalArgumentException.class, ...)` once the method is fixed to throw a documented exception, instead of implicitly relying on a side-effect NPE.

title: No integration coverage for the encoded access-token format
body: The PR introduces a new on-the-wire format for `jti` (e.g. `onrtrt:<uuid>`) and changes every test helper that asserts on `Details.TOKEN_ID`. There is no integration test that round-trips through `createClientAccessToken` -> JWT signing -> token manager decode to confirm that `TokenManager` and the introspection / UMA / account endpoints all still recognise tokens minted under the new format. Because the matching helper in `AssertEvents` is also broken, the existing tests cannot act as a safety net for this either. At least one integration test exercising a token-end-to-end (login + introspection + refresh) is needed.

title: Stale comment about clientSession note remains
body: The diff `sessionContext.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, ...)` is added next to the unchanged `clientSession.setNote(VC_ISSUANCE_FLOW, ...)`. There is no comment explaining why both are needed (the note stores the VC flow marker, the attribute stores the grant type for the encoder). The PR would benefit from a single-line comment indicating the dual-purpose nature of these two assignments so the next reader does not delete the attribute thinking it duplicates the note.

title: Refresh path double-lookups the map
body: `getShortcutByGrantType` first does `grantsToShortcuts.get(grantType)`, and if null, then potentially recomputes the entry and then does a second `grantsToShortcuts.get(grantType)`. For an unknown grant type this is two map lookups; for a known one it's also two if you count the assignment on line 116. Minor, but more importantly the asynchronous refresh logic in `getGrantTypeByShortcut` walks the entire `OAuth2GrantType` factory stream every time the cached map misses - on a server with many grant types this is wasteful, especially as `findFirst` after `filter` could short-circuit earlier. Consider caching the per-shortcut lookup result the first time it is computed.

title: Constructor requireNonNull checks wrong variable for rawTokenId
body: The fourth argument of the constructor is `String rawTokenId`, but the validation reads `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`. The check uses `grantType` (already validated on the previous line) and so cannot fail. As a result `rawTokenId` is never validated and a null raw token id silently passes the constructor and is later encoded into the produced token id. It should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic and wrong substring range; does not actually verify the grant shortcut
body:
The body asserts: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false; return isUUID().matches(items[1]);`. Two defects combine to make the filter useless:
1) The negation is missing - the substring must equal the expected shortcut for the match to succeed, but the code rejects matches instead.
2) The indices are wrong - the grant-type shortcut occupies positions 4-5 of the prefix (session[0..1], token[2..3], grant[4..5]), so extracting `substring(3, 5)` returns the second character of the token-type shortcut and the first character of the grant shortcut (`ta` for `onrtac`), never the two-char grant shortcut the test expects.

Concretely, for `AuthorizationCodeGrantTypeFactory.GRANT_SHORTCUT = "ac"`, the encoded prefix `onrtac` produces substring `"ta"`, which never equals `"ac"`, so the test falls through to the UUID check and the matcher matches every well-formed id regardless of grant type. For refresh tokens the substring `(online/offline, regular, refresh)` becomes `"rt"`, which DOES equal the expected shortcut and incorrectly FAILS the match. Fix to `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

title: Converting getShouldUseLightweightToken from instance method to public static is a behavioral break for subclasses
body: `getShouldUseLightweightToken` was previously a package-private instance method. The change turns it into `public static boolean getShouldUseLightweightToken(...)`. Any custom subclass outside the tree (or within) that overrode this method to influence which token type is chosen will silently stop being called - static methods are not dispatched virtually, and their overrides no longer compile cleanly. The PR description does not call this out as an API/SPI change. If the method is meant to be part of an extension contract it should be made `public` only while staying an instance method (or factored into a separate strategy class).

title: No null check on getShortcut() before using shortcut as map key and in token id encoding
body: `getShortcutByGrantType` invokes `factory.getShortcut()` and uses the result as both a map key (`grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType)`) and as part of the produced token id (`+ grantShort +` in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId`). The interface contract `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` does not forbid null. A custom or future factory returning null would either corrupt the `grantsByShortcuts` map (ConcurrentHashMap rejects null keys, throwing NullPointerException) or cause `encodeTokenId` to concatenate a null piece into the encoded token id (also raising NPE). Add a null-check or document that implementations must return a non-null 2-character shortcut.

title: Pair of map updates not atomic; transient inconsistency possible under concurrent refresh
body: `getShortcutByGrantType` performs `grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType); grantsToShortcuts.put(grantType, shortcut);` as two separate operations. Concurrent callers loading a brand new grant type can leave the cache in a window where one direction (shortcut -> grant type) is populated and the other (grant type -> shortcut) is not yet visible. A concurrent reader doing the opposite lookup at that moment will not find the entry and may either retry (incurring an extra `getProviderFactoriesStream` enumeration) or - in the `encodeTokenId` path - throw IllegalStateException("Cannot encode token with unknown grantType") despite the grant being known moments later. Although very unlikely in practice, the two maps are mutated independently under contention; an `AtomicReference<Map<...>>` swap or populating both into temporary maps and then performing atomic `putAll` would be safer.

title: grantType field is cached from form params at construction but not refreshed when setFormParams is called later
body: The Context constructor takes the grant type from `formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)` and stores it in `this.grantType`. The class also exposes `setFormParams(...)` which replaces `this.formParams` but does not update `this.grantType`. If a grant flow modifies form parameters after construction, `context.getGrantType()` (now used by `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse` and `ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType.process` to populate `Constants.GRANT_TYPE`) will return the stale value, causing the encoded `grantType` shortcut in the access token id to be wrong. Update `setFormParams` to recompute `grantType` from the new params or document that the value is intentionally fixed at construction.

title: SpI is marked internal but the PR description advertises extensibility for custom encodings
body: `TokenContextEncoderSpi.isInternal()` returns `true`, meaning no custom `TokenContextEncoderProviderFactory` implementations can be registered through the normal Spi lookup. The PR description states the SpI was introduced so that "someone (can) introduce his own provider ... and eventually encode some more info or encode stuff in the different way etc." These two statements are mutually exclusive: if the SpI is internal, downstream implementations cannot plug in. Either the SpI should be public (and `isInternal()` should return `false`), or the PR description should be corrected and the indirection justified purely for testability - in which case the `TokenContextEncoderProvider`/`...Factory` types could live in a single class without an SpI.

title: Copy-paste error in requireNonNull message
body: Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") reuses the previous line's check on grantType and labels the message as if it were for rawTokenId. The intended line is almost certainly Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed"). With this typo, if a caller passes a null rawTokenId, the failure message says "Null rawTokenId not allowed" but does so from the grantType check, while the rawTokenId is never validated at all and is allowed to be null.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher does not actually verify the expected grant type
body: In the new isAccessTokenId(String expectedGrantShortcut) matcher: (a) the condition is inverted ('return false' when the substring equals the expected grant), and (b) the offset is wrong. The token id format produced by encodeTokenId is ST(2) + TT(2) + GT(2) + ':' + rawId, so the grant shortcut occupies characters at 0-indexed positions 4 and 5 (substring(4,6)). The matcher uses substring(3,5), which is the last char of the token type and the first char of the grant type ("ta" for the example in the PR description, "ac" would actually be at substring(4,6)). Because of the offset, the substring will never equal the expected grant, and because of the inversion the branch returns false instead of true even if it did. As a result, every call site that now uses isAccessTokenId(...) (expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectAuthReqIdToToken) effectively only checks that the token id has the form 'XXXXXX:UUID' and does not actually verify the grant type. The whole point of these test changes - to detect wrong grant shortcut mapping after this PR - is silently lost.

title: New abstract method on the grant SPI breaks every external implementation
body: Adding String getShortcut() as an abstract method on OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is a binary- and source-incompatible change for every third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementation (including in the many extensions Keycloak ships). Any out-of-tree impl compiled against the previous version will fail to load at runtime with AbstractMethodError and any extension maintainer will fail to compile against the new version. The field is internal SPI (server-spi-private), but it is still on an interface implemented by SPIs in extension points (Ciba, Device, TokenExchange, UMA Permission, etc.). At a minimum the new method needs a default implementation (e.g. default returning getId()) and the existing built-in factories should override it.

title: Removed public Context copy constructor
body: The diff removes the public Context(Context context) copy constructor from OAuth2GrantType.Context (the rest of the constructors remain). Even for 'internal' SPI in the server-spi-private module, this is a binary-incompatible removal: existing compiled callsites and any extension using that constructor will fail with NoSuchMethodError at runtime. If a copy constructor was no longer needed, that should be confirmed; if it was, it should be retained.

title: getShouldUseLightweightToken promoted from package-private instance to public static
body: The method signature was changed from 'boolean getShouldUseLightweightToken(KeycloakSession session)' (package-private instance) to 'public static boolean getShouldUseLightweightToken(KeycloakSession session)'. Subclasses outside this package that overrode the package-private instance version will now have two distinct methods (the inherited one and their override) and call sites using their subclass reference would still hit the parent's version. It would be safer to keep an instance-method shim (e.g. protected boolean getShouldUseLightweightToken(...) that delegates to a public static) so that subclasses continue to work, or document and version the change explicitly.

title: Duplicated-grant-shortcut validation fires after entries already overwritten, error message misleading
body: In postInit the loop does grantsByShortcuts.put(grantShortcut, grantName) for each grant. If two factories return the same shortcut, the later entry silently overwrites the earlier one in grantsByShortcuts, but grantsToShortcuts still contains both grant ids. The only validation is the post-loop size check, which catches it but the exception message just says 'Make sure there is no OAuth2GrantType implementation with same ID or shortcut like other grants' and does not identify which shortcut collided. The same race exists in getShortcutByGrantType (lazy refresh path), which does grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType) and grantsToShortcuts.put(grantType, shortcut) without any uniqueness check on the shortcut. If a misbehaving third-party provider returns a shortcut that collides with an existing one, this will silently corrupt the cached mapping at runtime.

title: Constants.GRANT_TYPE is only set on the refresh path, not consistently on all token-issuance paths
body: The grant-type attribute is set in OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse, ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType.process, StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient, PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType.process, and (for refresh) TokenManager.validateToken. Any future caller of TokenManager.createClientAccessToken / initToken that does not first call one of these will silently fall back to the 'na' (unknown) shortcut in the encoded JTI. Constants.GRANT_TYPE is documented as the canonical key, but the responsibility for populating it is spread across many call sites with no guard. This should either be enforced inside createClientAccessToken/initToken (refuse to issue without a known grant type) or documented; otherwise the encoding will appear to work yet the encoded grant type will be 'na' for missed paths.

title: getTokenContextFromTokenId will NPE on null input and does not validate token id length when no colon
body: getTokenContextFromTokenId(encodedTokenId) calls encodedTokenId.indexOf(':') without a null check. If it is called with a null token id (e.g. a token whose jti claim ended up null/unset, which is possible when no raw id was supplied), it will throw NullPointerException instead of returning the UNKNOWN context. Also, the decoder accepts 'no colon' strings of any length (including empty string) and treats the whole input as the raw id, which means a malformed token id that contains a colon later in the string (rather than as separator) could be parsed incorrectly because indexOf only finds the first ':'.

title: OAuth2GrantType.Context.grantType is captured at construction time but setFormParams can replace the params later
body: The new grantType field is initialized once in the constructor from formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE), but the class still exposes setFormParams(...) which replaces the entire formParams map without updating grantType. Any flow that calls setFormParams after construction (the existence of that setter suggests it happens) will leave grantType pointing at the original form value, while getFormParams() returns the new one. The downstream constant Constants.GRANT_TYPE will then be the stale value, and the encoded JTI will carry the wrong grant shortcut.

title: Reconstructed recovery-codes credential loses its ID, breaking removeStoredCredentialById downstream
body: In getCredentials() the stored CredentialModel myUser.recoveryCodes (created in updateCredential with setId(KeycloakModelUtils.generateId())) is discarded and replaced with a brand-new RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel built via RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...). createFromValues only accepts the raw codes, createdDate and userLabel, so the ID of the credential actually sitting in MyUser.recoveryCodes is not propagated to the returned model. RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator then does authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId()) using that ID. Because the ID no longer matches what was stored, and BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage does not implement removeStoredCredentialById/getStoredCredentialById anyway, the credential cannot be removed once all of the codes are consumed, leaving a stale 'all codes used' credential in federated storage.

title: All-used recovery code credential is never removed when it lives in user storage
body: After a successful recovery code match, the authenticator looks up the credential via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) which prefers getFederatedCredentialsStream(). If the credential is federated and allCodesUsed() is true, the code calls authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId()). CredentialManager.removeStoredCredentialById only operates on locally-stored credentials; the federated provider BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage does not implement removeStoredCredentialById at all. The credential therefore remains in the user storage with all codes consumed, and any subsequent regeneration depends on updateCredential overwriting it. Combined with the ID-mismatch in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials, the cleanup path is doubly broken for the very flow this PR introduces.

title: Recovery codes are persisted in plaintext (raw unhashed) in credentialData
body: updateCredential for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE stores input.getChallengeResponse() verbatim as credentialData, where getChallengeResponse() is the JSON array of raw generated codes that CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes. The standard keycloak-recovery-authn-codes provider hashes the codes before storing them in credentialData, so user-federated recovery codes now bypass that hashing. Anyone with read access to the credential metadata (admin REST /account/credentials, exports, debug logs, etc.) sees the usable plaintext recovery codes. Either hash them in the user-storage provider before storing or delegate to the standard provider for serialization while still returning a stored/federated credential model.

title: Bean crashes with NoSuchElementException when user has no recovery-codes credential
body: The constructor calls RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user).get() unconditionally. Before this PR the same .get() was already present, but the PR changes RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential to also fall back to federated credentials via getFederatedCredentialsStream. For federated users that have never configured recovery codes, getFederatedCredentialsStream still returns the provider's getCredentials() result; when MyUser.recoveryCodes is null the stream is empty and getCredential returns Optional.empty(), causing credentialModelOpt.get() to throw NoSuchElementException and break the login page. Guard with isPresent() and fall back to a sane default (or render no code-number UI) when no credential exists.

title: hasRecoveryCodes does not normalize username but the map keys are lowercased
body: addUser stores entries with users.put(translateUserName(username), new MyUser(username)) and translateUserName lowercases the username. hasRecoveryCodes looks up userPasswords.get(username) directly, so a caller passing a mixed-case username will always get false even when the user and their recovery codes exist. hasUserOTP has the same flaw; the new code copies it instead of fixing it. Pass the username through translateUserName (or use a case-insensitive lookup) so the assertion in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.assertUserHasRecoveryKeysCredentialInUserStorage works regardless of how the username is supplied.

title: NPE / NumberFormatException on missing or malformed form params in processAction
body: processAction reads generatedAtTimeString and generatedCodesString via formParamsMap.getFirst(...) and immediately compares them with .equals(...). If either parameter is missing, .getFirst returns null and the .equals call throws NullPointerException. The subsequent line uses Long.valueOf(generatedAtTimeString), which throws NumberFormatException if the value is present but not a valid long. This code is touched by the PR and is now invoked from the user-storage path too, so a tampered/missing form will throw before any attempt to clean up the generated auth-notes. Validate parameters first (treat null/blank as 'tampered' and re-issue via requiredActionChallenge).

title: Test only exercises the happy path for recovery codes in user storage
body: testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin only verifies create-in-user-storage + single successful login. It does not cover: regenerating codes (multiple updateCredential calls - which currently overwrites and changes the credential ID); using all codes until allCodesUsed() and observing what happens to the stored credential; disabling recovery codes through admin REST or account mgmt; account mgmt listing of credentials (which will show credentialData containing plaintext codes due to the hashing gap); and confirming that the credential is removed once all codes are used (which the production code path does not handle for federated storage). At minimum add a test that consumes every recovery code and asserts that the credential is actually gone, otherwise regressions in the cleanup path will not be caught.

title: Recovery codes stored unhashed
body: In `createRecoveryCodesCredential`, the generated recovery codes are serialized to JSON as raw strings (`recoveryCodesJson = JsonSerialization.writeValueAsString(generatedCodes)`) and passed as the credential value to both user storage (`UserCredentialModel`) and local storage (`RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel`). `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils` already provides `hashRawCode`/`verifyRecoveryCodeInput` for hashing codes with `Algorithm.RS512`, but they are not used anywhere in this code path. Anyone with read access to the federated user storage or to the Keycloak DB can read the recovery codes in plaintext and reuse them to bypass 2FA. The codes must be hashed before persistence (e.g., via `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.hashRawCode`) and verified by hashing the user input, as the existing helpers already support.

title: Recovery codes can be reused indefinitely in federated storage
body: `isValid` for `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE` only does `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))` and never updates the stored credential data to mark the consumed code. The corresponding local-storage behaviour (see `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.isRecoveryAuthnCodeInputValid` which checks `recoveryCodeCredentialModel.allCodesUsed()` and removes the credential) has no counterpart in the user-storage path, so a single recovery code stays valid forever and `allCodesUsed()` will never trigger for federated users.

title: NoSuchElementException when user has no recovery codes
body: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` returns `Optional<CredentialModel>`, but the constructor immediately calls `credentialModelOpt.get()` and then `recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get().getNumber()`. If the user has no recovery-codes credential (e.g., the authenticator is reached before the credential is created, or the federated storage returns nothing), this throws `NoSuchElementException` and breaks the login form rendering. The constructor should handle the empty Optional (skip rendering, throw a meaningful exception, or the calling site must guard creation).

title: removeStoredCredentialById does not work for federated credentials
body: When all codes are used, the authenticator calls `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())`. `removeStoredCredentialById` only removes locally stored credentials; for a federated credential (which is exactly the case the PR is enabling) this call is a no-op or an error, so a federated user whose recovery codes are exhausted will never have the credential removed and `allCodesUsed()` will never remove the required action either.

title: disableCredentialType silently ignores recovery-authn-codes
body: `disableCredentialType` only handles OTP types and logs an 'Unsupported to disable credential of type' message for everything else. With the new `supportsCredentialType` accepting `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE`, an admin call to disable recovery codes for a federated user will silently fail and leave the credential active. The recovery-codes branch must clear `myUser.recoveryCodes` (and likewise `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream` must include the type when present).

title: Federated credential ID is dropped when exposing recovery codes
body: `getCredentials` reconstructs the recovery-codes credential via `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...)`, which does not set `id` from `myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()`. The credential returned through `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` therefore has a different (likely null) id than the one stored in `myUser.recoveryCodes`. Any caller that subsequently operates on this id (e.g., `removeStoredCredentialById` in `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator`, or admin REST `DELETE /credentials/{id}`) will target the wrong record. The credential id must be copied into the reconstructed model.

title: getCredentials no longer returns the password credential
body: The new `getCredentials` implementation builds the result list only from `myUser.recoveryCodes` and `myUser.otp`. It never adds `myUser.hashedPassword`. Since the credential manager's federated stream is built from `UserStorageProvider.getCredentials`, the federated user's password will disappear from `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` and from any account/admin REST listing. The pre-existing password handling must be preserved alongside the new recovery-codes entry.

title: Recovery-codes test only covers the happy path
body: `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` only exercises setup + a single successful login with the first code. It does not verify: an incorrect/wrong-format code is rejected, that a consumed code cannot be reused, that an exhausted credential triggers `CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES` and removes the credential for the federated user, or that recovery codes are not also written to the local DB. Given the data-integrity concerns introduced by this PR (hashing, consumption tracking, removal), at least negative-path and exhaustion assertions are required.

title: Potential NullPointerException on tampered/missing form fields
body: `httpReqParamsMap.getFirst(FIELD_GENERATED_AT_HIDDEN)` and `getFirst(FIELD_GENERATED_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES_HIDDEN)` can return `null` (e.g., form tampering or a stale POST). The code then calls `.equals(...)` on the result and `Arrays.asList(generatedCodesString.split(","))` later, both of which throw NPE on null. A null check (or `Objects.equals` with the auth-note value) is needed before the equality test.

title: Federated recovery-codes credential never removed when all codes are used
body: When a user has recovery codes stored in federated storage and all codes have been consumed, the code calls `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())`. `removeStoredCredentialById` only acts on credentials in local Keycloak storage, not on federated credentials returned via `getFederatedCredentialsStream()`. The result is that the (now exhausted) credential remains in the user storage and is still picked up by `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential()` on subsequent logins, so the user is repeatedly asked to re-configure while the stale credential is never cleaned up. There must be a separate path (or a fallback to a federated-credential delete) when the credential was returned from the user storage.

title: RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean crashes if user has no recovery codes
body: The constructor does `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel(credentialModelOpt.get())` directly on the result of `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)`, which returns `Optional<CredentialModel>`. If the user has never configured recovery codes (e.g. the bean is rendered for a user in any context where they don't exist), `get()` throws `java.util.NoSuchElementException` and the login template fails to render. This was safe before the change because the previous code used `findFirst().get()` on the local-credentials stream and would throw a similar error, but the new code now also considers federated credentials and the same fragility remains; an explicit `isPresent()` check (and a sensible fallback when absent) is required.

title: Recovery codes stored and compared in plaintext in user storage
body: `updateCredential` stores `input.getChallengeResponse()` (the raw codes JSON) directly in `credentialData`, and `isValid` reads it back and does `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))`. Recovery codes are intended to be one-time, low-trust-secret recovery material and the local Keycloak provider stores them hashed (via `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.hashRawCode`). Storing them as plaintext and comparing raw-vs-raw in the user-storage SPI means a breach of this user storage yields every still-valid recovery code in cleartext, and provides a copy-paste template that propagates this insecure pattern to real user-storage implementations. The `isValid` path should normalize through the same hash used by the local provider, and the stored credential data should be hashed at rest.

title: getCredentials returns a RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel with a regenerated id
body: `getCredentials` constructs the returned `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` via `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(rawCodes, createdDate, userLabel)`, which does not take the existing `myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()`. Every time the credential is listed, a new id is generated. Downstream consumers that try to manage the credential by id — including the new `removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())` in `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` — then operate on a non-existent local-storage id, so any per-id operation (remove, update, disable) against the federated credential silently no-ops. `getCredentials` should return a model whose `getId()` equals `myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()`.

title: New recovery-codes integration test covers only one happy path
body: `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` exercises exactly one successful login with the first requested recovery code. It does not cover: (a) reusing the same code a second time (must fail), (b) entering an invalid code (must fail with the configured error), (c) using every code in sequence until `allCodesUsed()` triggers the required action and removes the credential (the path the diff actually changed), or (d) disabling the recovery-codes credential via the admin REST. The cleanup/id-mismatch bug noted above would not be caught by this test because the all-codes-used branch is never reached.

title: Test reader thread is not joined before assertion
body: The new test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti` starts a background reader thread with `new Thread(...).start()` but never joins it. After the main thread deletes all groups it sets `deletedAll.set(true)`, but the reader may still be inside a `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...)` call when the assertion runs. Any exception raised by that in-flight call (or by a subsequent loop iteration before the thread observes `deletedAll`) will be appended to `caughtExceptions` AFTER `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` has already executed, so the test will silently pass even when the bug it is meant to catch is still present. The reader thread should be stored in a local, joined (with a timeout) before the assertion, and `deletedAll` should not be set until after the reader is observed to have exited the read loop.

title: Same NPE pattern remains on getSubGroupsStream overloads
body: The PR only adds a null guard to `getSubGroupsCount()`, but the three `getSubGroupsStream(...)` overloads immediately below (lines 256, 262, 268 in the head file) still use the exact pattern that was reported as NPE: `return modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)`. When the underlying delegate group has been deleted concurrently, `modelSupplier.get()` returns null and these methods will dereference null just like the original `getSubGroupsCount()` did. If the regression test is meant to prove the NPE is gone, it should cover these methods too, or the fix should be applied to all four methods (e.g. extracting the cached-load into a helper that returns null safely).

title: getSubGroupsCount silently returns null instead of invalidating cache
body: Before the change, `getSubGroupsCount()` would NPE on a missing underlying group. After the change it returns `null` without invalidating the cached entry, without going through `getDelegateForUpdate()`, and without calling `registerGroupInvalidation`. The other 'updated' paths in this class (`getDelegateForUpdate`, `isUpdated`) consistently treat 'group missing in DB' as `IllegalStateException("Not found in database")`, so this method now diverges from the rest of the contract: callers (e.g. `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount`, which calls `representation.setSubGroupCount(group.getSubGroupsCount())`) silently receive a `null` Long that may surface as a `null` field in the serialized representation. Either the cache should be invalidated and an empty/0 count returned, or an `IllegalStateException` should be raised like the sibling methods do.

title: Regression test does not exercise the fixed code path
body: The test only calls `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)`, which lists top-level groups. The fix targets `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount()`, which is reached through subgroup-count population (`GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount`, only invoked when `subGroupsCount=true` is passed down). The listing call used here may not traverse the subgroup-count code path, so even if the fix were reverted the test could still pass by exercising only the un-fixed `getSubGroupsStream` paths. The test should either pass `false` for brief representation and use a parent group with subgroups, or directly invoke the admin endpoint that returns `subGroupCount` (e.g. fetching a single group with `?subGroupsCount=true`) to actually exercise the patched line.

title: Reader thread is a non-daemon Thread without a name
body: The reader thread is created with `new Thread(() -> {...})` and is not marked as a daemon. If the test fails or the thread is not joined (see previous finding), it can outlive the test method and keep issuing admin REST calls against the server after the test reports its result, polluting subsequent tests' state. The thread should be created as a daemon thread (or joined) and given a descriptive name so failures show up in stack traces.

title: Fix is incomplete: other GroupAdapter methods still NPE on concurrently deleted groups
body: The null guard is added only to getSubGroupsCount (line 274). Other GroupAdapter methods that delegate to the cached model via cached.getX(keycloakSession, modelSupplier) still throw NPE when the underlying group is deleted from the database. After isUpdated() returns false, modelSupplier.get() can return null and the DefaultLazyLoader invokes its function with a null source (e.g., source -> source.getSubGroupsStream().map(...).collect(...)). Affected call sites in this file: getFirstAttribute (line 149), getAttributeStream (line 155), getAttributes (line 163), hasDirectRole (line 182), hasRole (line 188), getRoleMappingsStream (line 204), getSubGroupsStream (line 240). CachedGroup.getAttributes (line 66) and CachedGroup.getSubGroups (line 90) likewise lack the null guard. The same defensive null check applied to getSubGroupsCount should be applied consistently.

title: getRoleMappings null check guards the wrong variable
body: The check `if (group == null)` verifies that the Supplier<GroupModel> parameter itself is null, but modelSupplier in GroupAdapter is set in the constructor and is never null. The comment indicates the intent was to handle the case where the loaded GroupModel is null, but the implementation checks the wrong variable. As a result, getRoleMappings still invokes the loader function on a null source whenever supplier.get() returns null. Any GroupAdapter method that calls cached.getRoleMappings (hasDirectRole line 182, hasRole line 188, getRoleMappingsStream line 204) remains vulnerable to NPE under the same concurrent-delete scenario that the PR is trying to address. The guard should check the result of group.get() being null.

title: Reader thread is never joined; assertion can race the reader
body: createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti starts an anonymous reader thread (line 139) that loops until deletedAll is true, then asserts caughtExceptions is empty immediately after setting deletedAll.set(true) (line 155). The reader thread is never joined. If the reader is mid-request when the main thread asserts, an exception thrown by that request after the assertion is added to caughtExceptions without being observed by the test. As written, the test can pass even when the bug is present (reader thread throws after the assertion completes) and can be flaky. The Thread should be captured into a local variable and thread.join() called before the assertThat.

title: Cache entry is not invalidated when group is missing from DB
body: When modelSupplier.get() returns null because the group was concurrently deleted from the database, getSubGroupsCount now returns null but the cache entry remains in place. Every subsequent call on the same GroupAdapter will repeat the failed DB lookup and return null again. The fix should also call cacheSession.registerGroupInvalidation(cached.getId()) (as getDelegateForUpdate does at line 59) when the model turns out to be missing, so the cached entry is removed and subsequent requests reload correctly instead of repeatedly hitting a known-missing group.

title: Same NPE remains in three getSubGroupsStream overloads
body: The PR fixes the NPE in getSubGroupsCount() (line 275) where modelSupplier.get() could return null. However, three other methods on lines 256, 262, and 268 still have the identical vulnerable pattern: `return modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)`. The Supplier can return null when the underlying group has been deleted concurrently (this is the same race condition that motivated the fix). If a caller invokes any of these overloaded variants while the group is being deleted, an NPE will still be thrown from the auto-unboxing/inner method call. The fix is therefore incomplete and leaves the same crash reachable via subgroup listing code paths.

title: Same NPE remains in getSubGroupsStream(Integer,Integer)
body: Same root cause as the line 256 finding. `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(firstResult, maxResults)` will NPE if modelSupplier.get() returns null, which happens when the group is no longer in the database due to concurrent deletion.

title: Same NPE remains in getSubGroupsStream(String,Boolean,Integer,Integer)
body: Same root cause as the line 256 finding. `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(search, exact, firstResult, maxResults)` will NPE if modelSupplier.get() returns null under the same concurrent-deletion scenario the PR is trying to fix.

title: Reader thread is not joined before asserting caughtExceptions
body: In createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti, the reader thread is started with `new Thread(() -> {...}).start()` without storing the reference, and the main thread sets `deletedAll.set(true)` and then immediately asserts `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())`. There is no `thread.join()` (or CountDownLatch) between flipping the flag and the assertion. If the reader thread is still executing a `groups(...)` call when the assertion runs, any exception it subsequently catches is written to caughtExceptions after the assertion has already been evaluated, causing the test to silently miss failures. This makes the test flaky and unreliable as a regression test for the concurrency bug it is meant to cover.

title: Test does not exercise the actual getSubGroupsCount code path that was fixed
body: The new test createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti only calls `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)` which loads brief representations.
