The NPE that this PR fixes lives in GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount(), which is only invoked when the subgroup count is populated (e.g. via GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount, which is only triggered for non-brief representations or when subGroupsCount=true in the admin hierarchy API). As written, the test exercises a different read path and is unlikely to reproduce the original issue 40368, so even if it passes it does not prove the fix is effective.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key crashes on datetime fields
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does `int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))` after `value = getattr(item, self.key)`. The endpoint wires this paginator in with `order_by="-datetime"`, so `self.key` is `"datetime"` and `getattr(item, "datetime")` returns a `datetime.datetime` object. `math.floor(datetime)` raises `TypeError: a float is required`, so every call through the new path (including the very first request, because `build_cursor` calls `key(...)` to seed the next/prev cursor) will raise 500. The optimized paginator should subclass `DateTimePaginator`'s key conversion (multiplier + strftime) or be otherwise datetime-aware.

title: Negative-offset slicing crashes Django QuerySet
body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, the advanced-features branch sets `start_offset = cursor.offset` (which can be negative) and then does `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])`. Django QuerySet slicing explicitly disallows negative indices and raises `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported` (or the equivalent TypeError on newer Django). The "negative offset support" advertised by the new class therefore crashes the request whenever a client sends a cursor with a negative offset. There is no defensive clamp (`max(0, ...)`) and no fallback, so the feature is non-functional in practice.

title: BasePaginator.get_result now passes negative offsets to QuerySet slicing
body: The new line `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` deliberately lets a negative `offset` flow into `queryset[start_offset:stop]` when the cursor is a prev cursor. Cursor offsets are parsed straight from the URL via `int(bits[1])` in `Cursor.from_string`, so any client (or buggy prior response) that produces a negative offset will now hit Django's negative-indexing AssertionError. The accompanying comment ("This is safe because the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions") is factually wrong: Django does NOT handle negative slicing and the previous code did not claim to. This change advertises a behavior that does not work.

title: Comment falsely claims QuerySet handles negative offsets
body: The comment block above the new offset calculation says "This is safe because the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions." Django's QuerySet raises on negative slicing (see the related finding at line 182/882). The comment is misleading and should either be removed or replaced with a real explanation of the intent plus a real guard, e.g. clamping to `>= 0` like the not-is_prev branch.

title: No tests cover the new optimized pagination path
body: The PR introduces a new request gate (`optimized_pagination=true`) and a new paginator class but does not add any tests for the new code path in `organization_auditlogs.py` or `paginator.py`. Given that the new path currently 500s on any non-trivial cursor (see other findings), tests would have caught the regression. At minimum, a test should cover (a) that `optimized_pagination=true` for an admin uses `OptimizedCursorPaginator` and succeeds end-to-end on `order_by="-datetime"`, and (b) that bad/negative cursors do not crash the endpoint.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates BasePaginator.get_result without a real perf win
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result is a near-verbatim copy of BasePaginator.get_result; the only behavioral difference is the negative-offset branch (which is itself broken — see other findings). The endpoint always passes `enable_advanced_features=True` when it opts in, so the flag is effectively dead. There is no documented or measurable performance improvement over DateTimePaginator/BasePaginator: the same queryset is built, sliced, and `build_cursor` is invoked identically. Either delete the class and the gating code, or implement the actual optimization (e.g. a keyset pagination scheme or a bounded lookup) and benchmark it.

title: Negative queryset slicing will raise AssertionError in Django
body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset is negative, the code does `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` with start_offset = cursor.offset (negative). Django QuerySet.__getitem__ explicitly raises AssertionError('Negative indexing is not supported.') when the start of a slice is negative (django/db/models/query.py). The in-code comment 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is therefore false. Because Cursor.from_string parses `int(bits[1])` without clamping, and the endpoint gates this branch on superuser/global-access + the query param `optimized_pagination=true`, any such user can craft a cursor with a negative offset and crash the audit log endpoint with a 500 (AssertionError, not a BadPaginationError). The intended 'high-performance bidirectional pagination' feature is unreachable in any working form.

title: Comment falsely asserts permissions are checked for negative offsets
body: The comment 'This is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level' next to the negative-offset branch implies that negative slicing is gated by some access control. No such check exists: the only gate is `self.enable_advanced_features`, which is set from the endpoint for any superuser or member with `org:global_access`. The endpoint's permission_classes (OrganizationAuditPermission) and the query filter on `organization_id` already apply to both code paths identically, so the claim is both misleading and irrelevant to the new behavior. A reviewer relying on this comment to evaluate risk would be misled about the actual attack surface.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates BasePaginator logic
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result is an almost-verbatim copy of BasePaginator.get_result (lines 136-215), differing only in the extra branch that allows a negative start_offset. This duplication means any future fix, security patch, or bug fix applied to BasePaginator.get_result will silently not apply to the new paginator. Given the new class is only ever selected from one endpoint and one branch, the simpler and safer design is to add an `enable_advanced_features` flag on BasePaginator (or a small subclass that only overrides the slicing step), rather than copy the full state machine including cursor building, prev-page filtering, and post_query_filter handling.

title: 'Performance optimization' comment describes a no-op change
body: The diff replaces `stop = offset + limit + extra; results = list(queryset[offset:stop])` with `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset; stop = start_offset + limit + extra; results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])`. For any non-negative offset (the normal case) `max(0, offset) == offset`, so this is functionally identical to the prior code; the comment 'For high-traffic scenarios, allow negative offsets to enable efficient bidirectional pagination without full dataset scanning' therefore misrepresents a no-op as a performance optimization. For prev cursors with a negative offset the behavior is also unchanged (still crashes in Django; see the related critical finding). Either remove the misleading comment or implement the actual optimization.

title: Comment suggests new behavior that the code does not add
body: The Cursor.__init__ change is comment-only: `self.offset = int(offset)` already accepted negative integers before this PR. The new comment 'Performance optimization: Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination scenarios. This enables efficient reverse pagination from arbitrary positions in large datasets' implies the constructor was modified to permit this, but `int(offset)` was unchanged. This is misleading documentation in a security-sensitive area; reviewers and future maintainers may infer that negative offsets are officially supported when in fact the only consumer (OptimizedCursorPaginator) is broken and no other cursor parsing path validates bounds.

title: 'authorized administrators' mislabels org:global_access
body: The variable is named `enable_advanced` and the comment says 'for authorized administrators', but the condition is `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`. `has_global_access` corresponds to the `org:global_access` scope, which is granted to Sentry employees (staff) for cross-org support, not to organization administrators. Conflating the two is a documentation/UX defect: org owners/admins will not see this code path even if they set `optimized_pagination=true`, while Sentry staff can. The branch's purpose should be described accurately (e.g. 'enable for Sentry staff and superusers') and, if intended for staff, the flag should probably not be exposed at all to non-staff.

title: New query parameter and paginator branch have no tests
body: The diff introduces a new query parameter `optimized_pagination`, a new permission-derived branch, and a new paginator class (OptimizedCursorPaginator) with non-trivial behavior (negative offsets, a duplicate state machine, and a feature flag). The PR does not modify or add any tests in the diff (no files under tests/ are listed). At minimum there should be tests covering: (1) the endpoint dispatches to OptimizedCursorPaginator only when both the flag and the permission gate are set; (2) the standard DateTimePaginator path is used otherwise; (3) cursor encoding/decoding round-trips for the new path; (4) the failure mode for negative offsets (which currently is an uncaught AssertionError, see critical finding). Without tests, the 'Test 1' description and the silent code duplication are the only signals of correctness.

title: Django QuerySet does not support negative slicing
body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset is negative, the code executes `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` with a negative start_offset. Django QuerySets explicitly disallow negative slicing — the __getitem__ implementation raises `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported.` whenever k.start or k.stop is negative. Every request that takes this branch will crash with 500 instead of paginating. The adjacent comment 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is factually wrong; the framework does no such thing.

title: Comment falsely asserts queryset-level permission enforcement
body: The comment 'This is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level' preceding the negative-offset branch is incorrect. No queryset-level filtering is added in this code path; the same queryset is sliced. If the slice were ever accepted by the ORM, it would let the caller view arbitrary rows beyond the cursor without any extra scoping. The justification does not match the code, and given the surrounding logic, the author appears to have meant it as a permission guarantee that the patch does not actually provide.

title: Permission gate does not match its 'authorized administrators' comment
body: The new branch is gated by `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`, but the comment immediately above says 'authorized administrators'. `has_global_access` is granted to Sentry staff who can read every org; it does not imply administrative rights in the calling organization. The PR title and comments talk about admins, while the code quietly extends access to any global-access member (e.g., support engineers). Either the comment is wrong or the gate is wrong; the mismatch should be resolved before merging, especially given the buggy 'advanced feature' being enabled.

title: No tests for the optimized-pagination code path
body: The PR introduces a new query parameter (optimized_pagination), a new paginator class (OptimizedCursorPaginator), and a new kwarg (enable_advanced_features) plumbed through self.paginate, but no tests are added for any of these. Given that the underlying behavior crashes due to Django's negative-indexing restriction, the absence of a test is what allowed the bug to ship. A test exercising the new branch (and the negative-offset path it claims to enable) would have caught this immediately.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates BasePaginator.get_result
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result is an almost-verbatim copy of BasePaginator.get_result (lines 136–215) with only the negative-offset branch swapped in. This duplicates ~70 lines and means any future fix to BasePaginator.get_result (correctness, edge cases, the post_query_filter ordering, the extra-row trimming, etc.) must be re-applied here. If the feature is meant to ship, it should override only the offset calculation (e.g., a small helper) and delegate the rest to super().get_result, or use a flag on BasePaginator itself.

title: Cursor comments claim a behavior change that doesn't exist
body: The added comments in Cursor.__init__ state 'Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination scenarios' and 'This enables efficient reverse pagination from arbitrary positions in large datasets', but the code is unchanged — `self.offset = int(offset)` already accepted negative ints before this patch. The comments misrepresent a no-op as a deliberate performance/feature change and tie the Cursor abstraction to a feature (negative offsets) that the rest of the system cannot actually consume.

title: Django ORM raises AssertionError on negative slice indices
body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0, the code does `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` with start_offset set to a negative value. Django's QuerySet.__getitem__ asserts that slice indices are non-negative and raises `AssertionError('Negative indexing is not supported.')` when they are not. The in-line comment claims 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically', which is false. Any superuser or global admin who sends a cursor URL parameter like `cursor=0:-1:0` to the audit logs endpoint (which unconditionally sets enable_advanced_features=True for those users) will cause an unhandled AssertionError, producing a 500 response.

title: Negative offset still crashes BasePaginator for is_prev=True
body: The BasePaginator.get_result change `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` only clamps negative offsets for the non-prev branch. When cursor.is_prev is True and cursor.offset is negative, start_offset stays negative and the subsequent `queryset[start_offset:stop]` triggers Django's 'Negative indexing is not supported' AssertionError. The accompanying comment ('This is safe because the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions') is incorrect; Django explicitly disallows negative slice indices on querysets.

title: Endpoint unconditionally enables broken advanced pagination path
body: When the user is a superuser or has global access, the endpoint passes `enable_advanced_features=True` to OptimizedCursorPaginator. Combined with the fact that `Cursor.__str__`/`from_string` round-trip a user-supplied integer offset verbatim, any such user can craft a cursor with a negative value (e.g. `?cursor=0:-1:0`) to crash the endpoint with AssertionError. There is no validation, no length/offset bound check, and no fallback; the new paginator code path is a denial-of-service for the most privileged users. The gating mechanism is also confused: `optimized_pagination=true` from the request is checked but plays no role, while the actual crash vector (cursor.offset) is unvalidated.

title: Silent per-span data loss replaces whole-segment drop
body: When the post-union ZSET cardinality exceeds 1000, the script executes `zpopmin` to drop the oldest (lowest end_timestamp_precise) members. This is a fundamental semantic change from the previous consumer-side check in buffer.py (which dropped the entire segment via `del payloads[key]`) to silently dropping individual members during insertion. For traces where the root span arrives late, child spans already buffered can be evicted before the root arrives, producing incomplete segments that are still flushed downstream with no error. There is no metric for evicted spans, no test coverage, and the eviction strategy (lowest end_timestamp_precise) is not justified.

title: Redirect chain depth limit silently lowered 10x
body: The redirect-resolution loop cap was reduced from 10000 to 1000, removing the previous safety comment about depth 10k. The PR description provides no rationale for this change. Any trace whose segment tree has a redirect chain between 1001 and 10000 deep will now exit the loop before resolving to the final set_span_id, leaving the new span attached to a stale set and producing a split/broken segment instead of one correctly-merged segment. This change affects production correctness for deeply nested traces and is not covered by tests.

title: KeyError if end_timestamp_precise is missing from event
body: The factory reads `end_timestamp_precise=val["end_timestamp_precise"]` with direct subscript access. Unlike `parent_span_id`, which is read via `val.get(...)`, this field is treated as required. The SpanEvent schema may evolve or upstream producers (older relays, batched ingest) may omit it; any such event will raise KeyError inside the consumer, killing the batch and potentially stalling the partition. The newly added test only covers the happy path where the field is present.

title: ZUNIONSTORE default SUM aggregation distorts end_timestamp_precise scores
body: Both unions use the default `AGGREGATE SUM` semantics: when the same member is present in both the destination set_key and the incoming source (parent_key on the second union, span_key on the first if a previous batch had landed it there), the resulting score becomes `original_score + new_score` instead of staying at `end_timestamp_precise`. This makes scores meaningless sums of microsecond-precision timestamps, which silently changes the ordering produced by `zscan` and biases `zpopmin` eviction (summed members get higher scores, making them less likely to be evicted). It is also undocumented and not tested.

title: max_segment_spans parameter no longer enforced
body: SpansBuffer still accepts `max_segment_spans: int = 1001` in __init__ but the consumer-side enforcement that used this limit in _load_segment_data was deleted without removing the parameter. The limit is now controlled entirely by the hardcoded 1000 in add-buffer.lua. Any caller that tuned max_segment_spans is silently overridden by a magic number in the Lua script; the parameter is dead config.

title: zscan on legacy SET keys will raise WRONGTYPE during deploys
body: The consumer now issues `p.zscan(key, ...)` against every segment key, but the on-disk format previously used Redis SETs. On rolling deploys where new consumer instances coexist with old data, or after a partial rollback, zscan against a SET key returns `WRONGTYPE Operation against a key holding the wrong kind of value`. There is no version/key-type check, no migration step, and no metric for this condition, so segments will silently fail to load and the consumer will lose data for the affected trace until the keys TTL out.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates Paginator almost verbatim
body: The new OptimizedCursorPaginator re-implements get_item_key and value_from_cursor exactly as Paginator does (Paginator already inherits these from BasePaginator), and re-implements get_result as a near-copy of BasePaginator.get_result. The only meaningful difference is the `enable_advanced_features` branch that itself crashes. This is dead code masquerading as a feature; it is brittle (any future change to BasePaginator.get_result will need to be mirrored) and the misleading docstring advertises capabilities (negative offsets) that don't actually work.

title: Cursor accepts arbitrary int offset with no validation
body: Cursor.__init__ now advertises 'Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination scenarios' but accepts any integer without bound or sign validation. Combined with the broken negative-offset handling downstream, this lets any caller of Cursor.from_string feed extreme or malicious values (e.g. -2**31) into the paginator. Even with negative-offset slicing eventually corrected upstream, an attacker can still trigger expensive queries via large positive offsets (which are also unbounded).

title: No tests cover the new >1000-span eviction behavior
body: The Lua script's `zpopmin`-based eviction when span_count > 1000 is a new behavioral guarantee with data-integrity implications, but no test inserts more than a handful of spans per segment. There is no test for: (a) which spans get evicted (oldest by end_timestamp_precise?); (b) that the eviction actually caps cardinality at 1000; (c) that segments exceeding 1000 spans still flush correctly and don't get dropped; (d) that the metric/observability for evictions exists. The PR therefore lacks coverage of its headline feature.

title: Test payloads omit end_timestamp_precise validation
body: Existing tests were retrofitted to add `end_timestamp_precise=1700000000.0`, but the only new test value is a constant used uniformly. There is no test asserting that missing end_timestamp_precise produces a clear error (vs. the KeyError that the current code raises), no test for non-finite or negative values, and no test verifying that two spans with the same end_timestamp_precise are still both retained (zadd behavior on score collision is not asserted).

title: Comments describe a feature that does not exist
body: The added inline comments describe 'Performance optimization for high-volume audit log access patterns', 'optimized paginator for high-performance audit log navigation', and 'enhanced cursor support' — but the OptimizedCursorPaginator it routes to is a copy of Paginator with a feature (negative offsets) that crashes Django. The `optimized_pagination=true` query parameter is checked but does not influence which features are actually exposed. The comments mislead future maintainers about what the code does and why.

title: Comments falsely claim queryset handles negative slicing
body: Both the BasePaginator change at line ~179 and the OptimizedCursorPaginator comment at line ~876 assert 'the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions' / 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically'. This is incorrect: Django raises AssertionError on negative slice indices. Comments that document safety properties that are not true make future debugging harder and may cause contributors to rely on a guarantee that does not exist.

title: Redirect-follow loop limit reduced 10x without justification
body: The loop bound `for i = 0, 1000 do` was lowered from 10000. The original comment explicitly warned that this limit is the maximum depth of redirect chains that get joined; depths above it leave segment trees unjoined. Cutting the limit to 1000 means 10x more chains (especially long, deep spans trees common in distributed traces with many ancestor pointers) will silently fail to be merged, producing orphaned/incomplete segments flushed on the no-root timeout. The PR description ("Test 2") does not justify this regression.

title: Eviction silently drops spans with no metric or log
body: When `span_count > 1000` the script calls `zpopmin set_key, span_count - 1000`. Because the score is `end_timestamp_precise`, ZPOPMIN evicts the OLDEST ones in time. This is silent data loss: spans are permanently removed from the segment, no metric is incremented, no log is emitted, and the segment will be flushed incomplete with no way for operators to detect the loss. Even the prior Python-side metric `spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded` is no longer reachable (see buffer.py finding). At minimum, emit a `redis.call`/server-side metric (e.g. `INCR spans.buffer.add_buffer.evicted`) so this is observable.

title: KeyError on messages missing `end_timestamp_precise`
body: `end_timestamp_precise=val["end_timestamp_precise"]` raises KeyError if the field is absent. This field is not part of the original schema validated for `SpanEvent`, and any messages produced before this rollout (including in-flight backlog topics, retained Kafka segments, and relays that have not been updated) will crash the consumer's `process_batch` for every message. Use `val.get("end_timestamp_precise", 0.0)` (and consider how `0.0` interacts with zset ordering) or reject/log with a metric instead of hard-crashing.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator passes negative offset to Django queryset
body: When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code does `results = list(queryset[cursor.offset:stop])`. Django querysets do NOT support negative slice starts (the QuerySet.__getitem__ implementation raises `AssertionError("Negative indexing is not supported.")`). The accompanying comment ("The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically") is factually wrong. Any cursor with a negative offset routed through this branch (which the audit-logs endpoint now creates whenever a superuser/global-access admin sends `optimized_pagination=true`) will produce a 500.

title: Negative offset clamp only applied for non-prev cursors
body: The defensive change is `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`. For `cursor.is_prev=True` with a negative offset (still reachable through legitimate cursor strings), `offset` is used directly as a slice start and Django will still raise AssertionError. Either always clamp (`start_offset = max(0, offset)`) or validate at the Cursor layer.

title: max_segment_spans check removed without replacement
body: The previous loop had `if len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans: metrics.incr("spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded")` which deleted oversized segments and emitted a metric. This guard is removed; the Lua-side eviction (see add-buffer.lua finding) is the only cap on count. But eviction happens at insert time and is bounded at 1000, while `max_segment_spans` defaults to 1001 — leaving no headroom and removing the only operator-visible signal. Either restore the check or delete the dead constructor parameter and update the docstring.

title: max_segment_spans constructor parameter is now unused
body: `max_segment_spans: int = 1001` is still accepted by `SpansBuffer.__init__` and stored on `self`, but never read after this change. It also appears in no test or call site (factory.py constructs SpansBuffer without it). Either remove it or wire it back in as a safety net alongside the Lua eviction.

title: organization_context.member may be None for superusers
body: `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` evaluates the right-hand side unconditionally. `organization_context.member` is typed as `RpcOrganizationMember | None`; a superuser who is not a member of this organization (which is exactly the case where the first disjunct is what protects the call) will hit AttributeError on `None.has_global_access`. Use short-circuit-friendly access: `organization_context.member.has_global_access if organization_context.member else False`.

title: No test for new eviction / ZSET path
body:
The behavioural change in this PR — switching from sets to sorted sets, evicting oldest spans above 1000, and tracking `end_timestamp_precise` as score — has zero test coverage. There is no test that:
  - feeds more than 1000 spans into one segment and verifies the resulting cardinality is bounded,
  - verifies that the evicted members are the ones with the lowest score (and therefore that this is observable as data loss),
  - verifies ZUNIONSTORE merge ordering preserves spans by end_timestamp.
Add an explicit regression test before merging; otherwise the eviction rule can change silently.

title: No tests for OptimizedCursorPaginator or negative-offset branch
body:
`OptimizedCursorPaginator` (a new class) and the new `enable_advanced_features` flag have no test coverage. The audit-logs endpoint change that wires it in (superuser OR has_global_access) is similarly untested. Add at least:
  - tests that the new paginator is selected for the documented inputs,
  - tests for the negative-offset code path (and document the expected 500 if/until the Django-slice bug is fixed).
Currently the only signal these paths work is manual QA.

title: Misleading comment about Django ORM negative slicing
body: Comment claims: "The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" and "This is safe because the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions". This is incorrect: `QuerySet.__getitem__` raises `AssertionError("Negative indexing is not supported.")` for any negative slice start. The comment should be removed and the code actually fixed (or replaced with reverse-window logic using `reversed(queryset)` / LIMIT + OFFSET + explicit ordering).

title: KeyError on spans missing end_timestamp_precise
body: The new code uses `end_timestamp_precise=val["end_timestamp_precise"]` with subscript access, while every other optional field in the same Span constructor (parent_span_id, is_remote) uses `.get()`. Any span payload already buffered in the ingest-spans Kafka topic (or coming from a producer that has not yet been upgraded) that lacks this key will raise KeyError and crash the consumer batch. Use `val.get("end_timestamp_precise")` (or fall back to a sentinel such as 0.0) for forward compatibility with in-flight messages.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator negative slicing will raise AssertionError
body: The new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` does `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` with `start_offset = cursor.offset` (a negative integer) when `enable_advanced_features` is True and `cursor.offset < 0`. Django QuerySets explicitly do not support negative indexing; `QuerySet.__getitem__` asserts `int(k.start) >= 0` and raises `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported.` The inline comment "The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is false. Any admin-supplied cursor string like `"0:-10:0"` (Cursor.from_string parses the second token via `int(bits[1])`) will crash the endpoint with a 500. This also contradicts the docstring claim that the feature is "safe" — it is not even reachable without a server error. Either remove the negative-offset branch or fetch a count first and translate the offset to a positive LIMIT/OFFSET in SQL.

title: max_segment_spans protection silently removed from flush path
body: `_load_segment_data` previously guarded against runaway segments by deleting any key whose accumulated span count exceeded `self.max_segment_spans` (default 1001) and emitting the `spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded` metric. The diff deletes that branch entirely and the constructor parameter `max_segment_spans` is now dead — no code reads it. The new in-Lua `zpopmin` eviction runs on the insert path, but it does not protect against (a) segments populated before this rollout, (b) sets that exceed 1000 entries between two insert calls, or (c) the case where `zcard(set_key)` after `zunionstore` returns 0 because both source sets were empty (so eviction is skipped even though `zcard` afterward would still report >1000). Without the flush-time guard a single oversized segment will now be loaded into memory and serialized, which is exactly what the old check prevented.

title: zpopmin eviction key is not actually oldest spans
body: Eviction uses `zpopmin` against `end_timestamp_precise` scores. When many spans in a segment share the same `end_timestamp_precise` (which is the common case for spans belonging to the same transaction), Redis sorted-set ordering for ties is lexicographic on the member bytes, i.e. on the JSON payload. The "evict oldest" policy therefore degenerates to "evict whichever serialized payload sorts first," which is essentially arbitrary and may preferentially drop small/different payloads. The score should include a deterministic tiebreaker (e.g. span_id) so eviction order is reproducible.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator added with no test coverage
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator is a near-copy of BasePaginator.get_result with a security-relevant behavior change (allowing negative offsets when `enable_advanced_features=True`). It is wired into the audit-logs endpoint and gated only by `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`, but there are zero tests for the class itself, for `enable_advanced_features=True` path, for negative offsets, or for the auditlog endpoint's new `optimized_pagination=true` branch. A paginator that silently changes the cursor contract for admins deserves its own tests in tests/sentry/api/test_paginator.py and tests/sentry/api/endpoints/test_organization_auditlogs.py.

title: Pre-existing typo order_b still present in BasePaginator.build_queryset
body: In `BasePaginator.build_queryset` the branch that flips `-key` ordering back to ascending writes `queryset.query.order_b = tuple(new_order_by)` — `order_b` is not an attribute of `Query` (the correct attribute is `order_by`). As a result, the reversed ordering is silently dropped and the queryset is left ordered by `-key` even though the code intended `+key`. This is in the same file the diff touches and is exercised by every caller using a descending order_by with a `is_prev=True` cursor that has a cursor value. It must be fixed before this PR lands; the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` inherits from `BasePaginator` and inherits the bug.

title: Endpoint change misrepresented as performance optimization
body: The endpoint change is labeled "Performance optimization for high-volume audit log access patterns" and the new query parameter is named `optimized_pagination`, but `OptimizedCursorPaginator` produces the same SQL plan as `DateTimePaginator` for the normal (forward, non-negative offset) case; the only functional difference is that it permits negative cursor offsets. There is no benchmark, no documentation in `api-docs/` (Sentry typically gates new query params), and no mention that the new branch is only active for superusers/org members with global access — `enable_advanced_features=True` is silently enabled based on `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`, which is not the same permission check used elsewhere in this endpoint (`OrganizationAuditPermission`). Either rename the parameter to reflect what it actually does (e.g. `allow_negative_offset`) and document it, or drop the class.

title: Upsampling eligibility check uses outer `dataset` instead of the dataset actually being queried
body: Inside `_get_event_stats`, the helper is invoked with the closure-captured `dataset` (the dataset requested by the client) rather than the function's `scoped_dataset` argument, which is the dataset actually executed against. In `get_event_stats_factory`, widget-splitting can pass a different `split_dataset` (e.g. `discover` when the original requested dataset is `transactions`), and `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` then evaluates `dataset == errors/transactions/discover` against the wrong dataset. The result is that upsampling is silently skipped (or wrongly applied) for any query where the requested dataset and the executed dataset differ, including the widget split path. Pass `scoped_dataset` (or both) to `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` so the decision is based on the dataset that will actually run.

title: Only the literal token `count()` is rewritten; other common count-style aggregations are silently left as raw counts
body: `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` only rewrites columns whose stripped/lowercased form is exactly the string `"count()"`. Any column with arguments (`count_if(...)`, `count_unique(...)`, `count_distinct(...)`), aliased forms (`count() AS total`), whitespace inside the parens (`count(  )`), or counts appearing inside an `equation` expression is left untouched and will be executed against `sample_weight` semantics on some datasets and raw event semantics on others. The docstring says it "transforms aggregation functions to use sum(sample_weight) instead of count()" implying plural coverage; in reality it is a single literal-string match. Either expand the matcher to cover the realistic variants or document the limitation clearly and reject unhandled inputs so callers cannot get silently-mixed semantics.

title: _is_error_focused_query misses queries that target errors by exclusion
body: The check only looks for the substring `event.type:error` in the raw `query` parameter. Common Sentry search syntax that targets errors by negating the transaction type (e.g. `!event.type:transaction`, or `event.type:error OR ...`) is missed — `!event.type:transaction` will return False even though it is an errors-only query, so upsampling is skipped for those queries. Worse, the substring match is naive: a query like `event.type:errorcount` (an unknown tag name in user queries) would also pass. Use the parsed token list from `event_search.parse_search_query` (the same parser the rest of this endpoint uses) and inspect the `event.type` clause's value rather than substring-matching on the raw query string.

title: Upsampling integration tests assert an upsampled value that requires `sample_weight` to be populated by ingest
body: `OrganizationEventsStatsErrorUpsamplingTest.test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects` asserts `data[0][1][0]["count"] == 10`, deriving that 10 from the stored `client_sample_rate=0.1` and the Snuba `upsampled_count() = sum(sample_weight)` definition in `discover.py`. In `SnubaTestCase` no Relay pipeline runs and `sample_weight` is not populated from the `sample_rate` set by `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling`; `sum(NULL)` over the column will be NULL/0 and the assertion will fail, or — even worse — pass only by accident and silently never validate the upsampling transformation. Either populate `sample_weight` in the test fixture (or wrap the assertion in a mock that returns the expected sample_weight), or split the test so that it verifies (a) the SQL emitted by `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` and (b) the upsampled result via a controlled sample_weight fixture.

title: Integration tests do not invalidate the upsampling eligibility cache, so order-dependent failures are likely
body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` writes `is_eligible` to the shared cache under a key derived only from `organization.id` and the sorted project IDs. The new test class exercises four different allowlist configurations against the same `(organization, [project, project2])` tuple. Without invalidating the cache (e.g. by calling the exposed `invalidate_upsampling_cache` helper or clearing the cache backend in `setUp`/`tearDown`), the first test that runs caches its result and subsequent tests will read that stale value and silently skip the upsampling path they are trying to exercise. Add cache cleanup in `setUp`/`tearDown`, or assert on the emitted SnQL instead of the response value to make the tests order-independent.

title: The main public entry point `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` and `invalidate_upsampling_cache` have no direct tests
body: The unit test file only exercises the private helpers `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`, `_is_error_focused_query`, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`, and `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling`. It does not test the actual public entry point `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` (including its caching behavior, short-circuit when the allowlist is missing, or that it combines the allowlist check with the dataset/query check correctly), nor does it test `invalidate_upsampling_cache`. Given that the function is the one wired into the request hot-path and contains the non-trivial cache logic flagged in other findings, it deserves direct unit tests.

title: Cache value caches only the allowlist result; the transform check still runs on every cache hit
body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` caches only the boolean returned by `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`. On a cache hit the function still executes `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform(dataset, request)`, which performs module-identity comparisons, parses the query string, and runs lazy imports of `sentry.snuba.discover/errors/transactions` on every call. To make the 60 s TTL actually pay off, include the relevant decision inputs (or the combined boolean) in the cache value so cache hits short-circuit the full check. At minimum, hoist the `from sentry.snuba import …` statements to module scope so a cache hit is genuinely cheap.

title: _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling accepts arbitrary floats including invalid sample rates
body: The helper writes `normalized_data["sample_rate"] = float(client_sample_rate)` whenever `client_sample_rate` is truthy and converts cleanly. It does not validate the resulting value: 0 (everything dropped → sample_weight = ∞), negative values, or values > 1 are all accepted. A client (or a misbehaving test fixture) can supply `client_sample_rate=0.0` and silently produce divide-by-zero / infinity in the server-side upsampling, or supply `client_sample_rate=-1.0` and corrupt aggregated metrics. Validate the value is in the open interval (0.0, 1.0] before assigning.

title: Overly broad `except Exception: pass` in _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling hides real bugs
body: Two nested `try/except Exception: pass` blocks silently swallow everything, including programming errors like the `normalized_data` object not being a `MutableMapping` at all (e.g. someone refactors `store_event` and passes the wrong value). The first block only needs to handle the case where `contexts` is not a mapping (AttributeError / TypeError), and the second only needs to handle `ValueError` from `float()`. Narrow the exception types so genuine bugs surface instead of being papered over.

title: Repeated in-function imports of sentry.snuba modules on every call
body: `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` does `from sentry.snuba import discover, errors` and `from sentry.snuba import transactions` inside the function body, executing those imports on every invocation (including every cache-hit path from `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`). There is no circular-import reason to defer them — `sentry.snuba` does not import this helper. Move the three imports to module top-level so each call is a constant-time identity comparison.

title: _is_error_focused_query uses naive substring matching that yields wrong upsampling decisions
body:
The check `"event.type:error" in query` is a raw substring test on the lowercase query string. As a result it returns True (and therefore triggers error upsampling on the discover dataset) in cases where the query is actually not error-focused, e.g.:

- Negated clauses: `!event.type:error` still contains the substring `event.type:error`.
- Compound queries mixing transactions and errors: `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`, `event.type:error something else`, etc.
- Look-alike values: `event.type:errors`, `event.type:error_handled`, any custom tag named `event.type:error*`.

When upsampling is applied in any of these cases, `count()` is rewritten to `upsampled_count()` (= `sum(sample_weight)`) but the result set includes rows without `sample_weight` (transactions, non-error events), so the returned counts are mathematically wrong and silently inflated/deflated. The docstring claims this check "errs on the side of caution" — in reality it is more permissive than just `event.type:error`. The function should parse the query and require an un-negated, standalone `event.type:error` predicate.

title: invalidate_upsampling_cache is defined but never called, so the 60s allowlist cache is ungovernable
body: `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is added with a docstring that explicitly says it "should be called when the allowlist configuration changes to ensure cache consistency across the system", but nothing in the PR (or in any of the modified files) calls it. The 60-second cache in `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` therefore becomes stale any time `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` is updated: projects added to the allowlist will not be upsampled for up to 60s, and projects removed will continue to be upsampled (returning inflated counts) for up to 60s. This is a correctness hazard for an opt-in metric that drives billing/usage reporting numbers. Either wire up the invalidation in the option-change signal handler or drop the cache and accept the option lookup cost.

title: upsampled_count SnQLFunction is only registered on the discover dataset but is also injected into errors-dataset queries
body: `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns True for the `errors` dataset unconditionally, and the endpoint rewrites `count()` to `upsampled_count()` whenever that check passes. The new `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction is, however, only registered on the discover dataset's function map in this PR. So a top-events or non-RPC query routed to the `errors` dataset (which is in the dataset whitelist at lines ~172-188 of `organization_events_stats.py`) will be sent down with a `upsampled_count()` aggregate that the errors dataset's function_converter does not know about, causing a query build/runtime error at request time. If upsampling is meant to work on `errors` as well, register the SnQLFunction on that dataset too; otherwise gate the rewrite so it only applies when the scoped dataset is `discover`.

title: transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling ignores aliased count()
body:
The transformer compares `column_lower == "count()"` exactly, so any column expression that contains `count()` but is not literally that string is left untouched. In practice that includes:

- Aliased forms: `count() as my_count`, `count() AS count`.
- Annotated forms: `count()` followed by other tokens, e.g. `count(), other_col` (already split into separate items so OK), but also `count(error_count)` if it ever appears bare.
- Aggregations wrapped by other functions: `topK(1)(count())`.

The result is that for the same query, some y-axes are upsampled and others are not, mixing weighted and unweighted counts in the same response and producing nonsense totals / charts in the dashboard. The match should be against the leading aggregate token rather than the whole trimmed string.

title: _are_all_projects_error_upsampled does not validate the allowlist option type
body: `options.get("issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist", [])` is used directly with `project_id in allowlist`. If the option is ever misconfigured (set to a string, tuple, generator, etc.), `in` falls back to iteration/substring semantics — for a string allowlist, `123 in "1234"` returns True and arbitrary project IDs will be considered allowlisted, silently enabling upsampling (and inflated counts) for the wrong tenants. There is no schema/option validator in this PR and no isinstance(list)/set coercion in the consumer. Coerce `allowlist` to a `set` (and assert the type) before the membership check.

title: _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling swallows all exceptions with bare except Exception
body: Both `try: ... except Exception: pass` blocks around the `contexts.error_sampling` lookup and the `float(...)` conversion in `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` silently discard every error. Because this runs on every `store_event` call in tests (and could be wired into production ingestion), any structural change to the event dict (renamed contexts, different nesting, AttributeError on a non-dict `contexts`, etc.) will fail silently and leave `sample_rate` unset with no log/raise. The function should narrow the catch (e.g. `(AttributeError, TypeError, ValueError)`) and at minimum `logger.warning` on unexpected shapes so misconfiguration is debuggable.

title: Docstring/comment claims caution while the implementation is permissive
body: The docstring for `_is_error_focused_query` says "Reduced to only check for event.type:error to err on the side of caution", and the surrounding module comment on line 86 likewise claims sample_weight is guaranteed by the schema so no checks are needed. The actual substring check is more permissive than just `event.type:error` (it also matches `!event.type:error`, `event.type:errors`, compound OR queries with transactions), and the sample_weight assumption is not enforced anywhere visible in this PR. These comments will mislead future maintainers into trusting the function's output. Either tighten the implementation to match the comments or update the comments to describe the real behavior.

title: upsampled_count SnQLFunction not marked private
body: The newly added `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction is registered without `private=True`, unlike the surrounding private helpers (e.g. `thing_expression`, `count_at_least`). Without that flag the function becomes part of the user-exposed SnQL/Discover function surface, so end users could write `upsampled_count()` in their own queries. The function is only meaningful in conjunction with the project allowlist/sampling-rate pipeline, and emits `sum(sample_weight)` which has different semantics (and potential NULL-handling) from `count()`. Users invoking it directly outside of `organization_events_stats` will get counts that silently diverge from what they expect.

title: sum(sample_weight) silently drops NULL sample_weight rows
body: `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` rewrites `count()` to `upsampled_count()` which is implemented as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`. ClickHouse/SnQL `sum` ignores NULL arguments entirely, so any allowlisted-project event that has `sample_weight IS NULL` is silently omitted from the result, undercounting errors. The comment claims the schema guarantees `sample_weight` is non-null for allowlisted projects, but nothing in this helper (or in `discover.py`) enforces or even validates that invariant. There should be at minimum a guard that rejects the transformation (or coalesces `sample_weight` to a fallback) when the project list could contain NULL-weight events, otherwise dashboards/alerts that switch to upsampled counts will report numbers lower than the truth with no warning.

title: transform only matches literal count(), misses aliased and surrounded variants
body: `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` compares `column.lower().strip() == "count()"`. This single-equality test misses common variants that should still be upsampled: `count() as my_count`, `count() AS errors`, `count("id")` (counting a specific column), or `count()` surrounded by extra inner whitespace. As a result, a column written as `count() as count` (with explicit alias) will be passed through unchanged while the same column written as `count()` will be replaced with `upsampled_count() as count`, giving two clients querying the same metric different aggregations. The transform should at least recognise `count()` with a trailing `as <alias>` clause.

title: _is_error_focused_query uses substring match on query string
body: `_is_error_focused_query` decides based on `"event.type:error" in query`. The check is a raw substring match, so queries like `event.type:error_handled` (if such an alias is ever introduced) or any token that begins with `event.type:error` would be treated as error-focused and force the upsampled transformation on a dataset that may include non-error rows. A safer check parses the query tokens (e.g. via `event_search.parse_search_query`) and inspects the actual `event.type` value rather than doing a substring `in`.

title: Error message wording regression adjacent to top_events validation
body: The diff changes the response message from `"If topEvents needs to be at least 1"` to `"topEvents needs to be at least 1"`. The new wording is grammatically cleaner, but it is bundled into a commit titled `feat(upsampling)` with no mention of an API/UX message change. Because this is a public 400 response body on `organization-events-stats`, any client that does an exact-string match on this `detail` value (e.g. localised tooling) will break. The change should either be split into its own commit or called out in the description.

title: Unnecessary try/except around safe dict lookups
body: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` wraps the chained `.get(...).get(...).get(...)` in a `try/except Exception: pass` and the `float(...)` conversion in another one. `dict.get` cannot raise for missing keys, and a malformed `client_sample_rate` string is the only realistic failure mode, which the second `try` already handles. The first try/except hides real bugs (e.g. `AttributeError` from a malformed contexts payload) and should be removed; only the `float()` conversion needs to be defensive.

title: setUp reassigns self.user after login_as, breaking auth identity
body: In `OrganizationEventsStatsErrorUpsamplingTest.setUp`, the test calls `self.login_as(user=self.user)` with the user that `APITestCase.setUp` created, then immediately overwrites `self.user = self.create_user()`. From that point on, `self.user` no longer refers to the authenticated user, and any tag, audit log entry, or future test that reads `self.user` will silently use the wrong identity. In particular the events stored right below use `self.user.email` / `self.user2.email` as the `sentry:user` tag, which means the test is asserting counts against events whose owner does not match the calling API user; if any later assertion (or downstream test) compares user identity this will fail.

title: Stale upsampling eligibility cache has no invalidation hook
body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` caches the all-projects-in-allowlist result for 60 seconds, and `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is provided but never called from anywhere in the diff (no admin signal, option listener, or tests cover invalidation). If a project is added to or removed from `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist`, requests for the next minute will continue to use the previous decision. In the worst case (allowlist shrinks while cache still says eligible) the endpoint will issue `sum(sample_weight)` queries for projects that no longer guarantee non-null `sample_weight`, potentially producing the silent undercount called out above. There should be an explicit invalidation call (or a much shorter TTL, or no cache) wired up before merging.

title: Tests do not cover caching, invalidation, aliased count(), or NULL sample_weight
body: The new test file covers the allowlist membership, the basic `count()` transform, the `event.type:error` substring check, and the dataset dispatch, but misses the most failure-prone paths: (1) `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` is never tested, so the cache key construction (`hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`), cache-hit fast path, and 60s TTL behaviour are entirely uncovered; (2) `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` is never given aliased inputs (`count() as my_count`) so the limitation called out above is not pinned by a test; (3) there is no test asserting behaviour when a project in the allowlist emits events without `sample_weight`. Adding at least one cache-hit/miss test and an aliased-count test would prevent the cache and transform edge cases from regressing unnoticed.

title: Cache key uses hash() of project_ids tuple
body: The cache key is built as `f"error_upsampling_eligible:{organization.id}:{hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))}"`. While `hash(int)` is deterministic in CPython, mixing `hash()` of a derived structure into a cache key is fragile (it depends on tuple-hash internals and any future changes to them) and produces opaque keys that are hard to inspect/grep in Redis. A deterministic, explicit key like `f"error_upsampling_eligible:{organization.id}:{','.join(map(str, sorted(project_ids)))}"` (or a sha1 prefix) would be safer, debuggable, and immune to future interpreter changes.

title: TableWidgetVisualization rendered with hard-coded empty data when feature flag is on
body: In `tableResultComponent`, when the `use-table-widget-visualization` feature flag is enabled, `TableWidgetVisualization` is rendered with `columns={[]}` and a hard-coded empty `tableData` object (`data: []`, `meta: { fields: {}, units: {} }`). The actual result data (`result.data`, `result.meta`), `fields`, `getFieldHeaderMap`, `getCustomFieldRenderer`, and `minTableColumnWidth` are all available in the surrounding scope but are not forwarded. Any organization with the feature flag enabled will see fully empty tables in every dashboard widget, which is a functional regression vs. the existing `StyledSimpleTableChart` branch.

title: Object.keys on possibly undefined meta throws TypeError
body: The fallback column extraction does `Object.keys(tableData?.meta.fields).map(...)`. Optional chaining on the `?.` only protects `tableData`; if `tableData.meta` is undefined (e.g. when called with `{data: []}` and no `meta`), this throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'fields')`. The type says `meta` is always present, but the chart.tsx integration actually passes a hard-coded tableData whose meta is present in this PR but the contract is not enforced at runtime. Should be `Object.keys(tableData?.meta?.fields ?? {})` or equivalent.

title: Bare `except Exception` logged at INFO swallows real errors in get_environment_info
body: `CommitContextIntegration.get_environment_info` wraps the whole body in `except Exception as e:` and then logs at INFO level (`logger.info("get_environment_info.no-environment", extra={"issue_id": issue.id, "error": e})`). Catching the bare `Exception` base class will silently swallow programming errors, `DatabaseError`, `ObjectDoesNotExist`, etc., and logging them at INFO hides them from alerting/dashboards. Should narrow to the specific exceptions that are expected (e.g. `Group.DoesNotExist`, `Environment.DoesNotExist`) and log unexpected exceptions at `WARNING` or `EXCEPTION`.

title: Analytics event recorded before feature-flag check, polluting analytics with disabled usage
body: `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` is invoked on every request, before the `features.has("organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble", ...)` check that returns 404 for orgs without the flag enabled. This will record an analytics event for every caller — including unauthorized clients and orgs without the feature — biasing usage metrics. The recording should be moved after the feature flag check (and ideally after successful validation) so it only reflects real usage of the endpoint.

title: Analytics event registration relies on side-effect import that may not run before endpoint usage
body: `src/sentry/preprod/__init__.py` does `from .analytics import *` purely for the side effect of `analytics.register(PreprodArtifactApiAssembleEvent)`. The endpoint `organization_preprod_artifact_assemble.py` only imports from `sentry.preprod.tasks`, not from `sentry.preprod`. If nothing else imports the `sentry.preprod` package during process startup, the event class will never be registered and `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` may fail or be dropped. There is no Django AppConfig / `ready()` hook in the PR to guarantee registration. Either register the event at module import inside `analytics.py` (it already self-registers) and ensure the package is imported, or add an explicit `default_app_config` so `preprod.apps.PreprodConfig.ready()` runs the registration.

title: Migrations 0917/0920 neutered to no-ops with no test coverage for the deferred migration
body: Both `0917_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views.py` and `0920_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_revised.py` were reduced to `return` with a comment pointing to `0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py`. The corresponding test `tests/sentry/migrations/test_0917_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views.py` was deleted in the same PR, and there is no test for `0920`. If `0921` does not exist in the repo, or if it fails to migrate the `SavedSearch -> GroupSearchView` rows correctly, the saved-search-to-view conversion that this migration sequence was supposed to perform will not happen on any environment that runs migrations sequentially — and there is no test guarding against the wrong file being referenced. Verify that 0921 exists and add a migration test (or `TestMigrations`) that exercises the full path the comment references.

title: Migration references non-existent file name in docstring
body: The migration docstring says `See 0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py for the correct migration.` but no file with that name appears in the PR or in `src/sentry/migrations/` paths shown. If the intended successor migration is `0921_*` with a different suffix, both migration docstrings are wrong and a future engineer will look for a file that does not exist. Verify the correct migration name and fix the docstring, or add the referenced migration if it really is missing.

title: Dead `_handle_regex_match` left behind in parametrize_w_experiments
body: After removing `ParameterizationRegexExperiment`, the inner function `_handle_regex_match` inside `parametrize_w_experiments` (lines ~335-343) is no longer called from the for-loop (which now unconditionally calls `experiment.run(content, _incr_counter)`). The unused closure is dead code, but it still holds a reference and is misleading to future readers who may think experiments can be regex-based.

title: Renamed analytics event `replay.view_html` -> `replay.view-html` is a silent breaking change
body: `trackAnalytics('replay.view_html', ...)` was changed to `trackAnalytics('replay.view-html', ...)`. The corresponding entry in `static/app/utils/analytics/replayAnalyticsEvents.tsx` was updated and the old `replay.view_html` key was removed entirely from `ReplayEventParameters` and `replayEventMap`. Any external dashboard, alert, or query filtering on the literal `replay.view_html` event name will silently stop receiving data. The PR description does not call this out; the rename should be flagged in changelog / product docs, or the old key should be kept as an alias for at least one release.

title: Removed `grouping.experiments.parameterization.traceparent` option not asserted by tests
body: The `grouping.experiments.parameterization.traceparent` option was deleted from `src/sentry/options/defaults.py`. There are no tests in the PR asserting that no code reads this option key, and `tests/sentry/grouping/test_parameterization.py` continues to test traceparent parameterization behavior. If any deployed instance still has the option persisted in DB / Redis from before this removal, lookups for it will now fail validation when callers pass an unrecognized key — worth grepping for any remaining `options.get("grouping.experiments.parameterization.traceparent")` references and adding a deprecation removal test.

title: PR description "Replays Self-Serve Bulk Delete System" does not match the diff contents
body: The PR title and description focus on a replays bulk-delete system, but the diff includes large, unrelated changes to grouping parameterization, browser reporting collector, GitHub/GitLab PR templates, autofix defaults, dashboards table widget, explore Visualize refactor (yAxes -> yAxis), feedback AI summaries, integrations, and two migrations that are turned into no-ops. None of these are described in the description. This makes the PR very hard to review and reason about; either split into focused PRs or update the description to enumerate the actual change set so reviewers know what they are signing off on.

title: No test covers the new `use-table-widget-visualization` branch in chart.tsx
body: There is a `tableWidgetVisualization.spec.tsx` testing the new component in isolation, but there is no test exercising the wiring in `chart.tsx` that chooses `TableWidgetVisualization` when the feature flag is on. Given the bug above (empty hard-coded data), this integration test would have caught it. Add an APITestCase / jest test that asserts the new component is rendered with the actual `result.data` / `result.meta` when the flag is on.

title: TableWidgetVisualization is rendered with hardcoded empty data when feature flag is on
body: When the `use-table-widget-visualization` feature flag is enabled, the new `TableWidgetVisualization` is rendered with hardcoded `columns={[]}` and `tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}}`. All the real `result.data`, `result.meta`, `fields`, etc. that are passed to the original `StyledSimpleTableChart` are discarded. This means any organization with the flag enabled will see an empty table widget with no rows and no columns. The implementation appears to be an incomplete placeholder; it should pass through `fields`, `result.data`, `result.meta`, and a derived `columns` array rather than constant empty values.

title: Exception handler swallows all errors at info level
body: `get_environment_info` catches bare `Exception` and logs it at `logger.info` (`get_environment_info.no-environment`). Unexpected errors like database failures, N+1 query explosions, or programming errors are silently downgraded to an info-level event with no stack trace, making them invisible in standard error monitoring. Either catch the specific expected exceptions (e.g. `Group.DoesNotExist`) or log at `logger.warning`/`logger.exception` so the failure shows up in Sentry's own error tracking. The current behavior risks hiding real production issues while a comment marks it as `intentional`.

title: Analytics event recorded before feature flag check
body: The `preprod_artifact.api.assemble` analytics event is emitted at the very top of `post()` and runs unconditionally — before the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` feature flag check, schema validation, and chunk verification. As a result, every unauthorized or invalid request still generates an analytics record, polluting the metric with traffic that did not actually assemble an artifact and inflating `preprod_artifact.api.assemble` counts. The analytics call should be moved to after the feature flag and validation checks so it only fires for successful/meaningful requests.

title: Unescaped markdown title injection
body: `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` formats issue titles into the markdown template `* ‼️ [**{title}**]({url}){environment}\n` without escaping markdown control characters. A title containing characters like `*`, `_`, `[`, or `]` will be interpreted by markdown renderers and can break the comment formatting (or be used to inject unintended markdown). Consider sanitizing or escaping the title before substituting it into the template.

title: Organization-type actors silently become owner-less
body: `create()` only sets `owner_user_id`/`owner_team_id` when the actor is a user or team. The `ActorField` it depends on accepts organization actors as well; if such an actor is passed, the Detector is silently created with both owner ids set to `None`, giving no error and no diagnostic. Either reject organization actors in validation, or document/encode that organization ownership is not supported. The added tests only cover user and team owners, so this gap isn't caught.

title: Migrations silently no-op; relies on unverified external migration
body: Both 0917 and 0920 were turned into `return`-only no-ops with a comment pointing to `0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py` as the migration that actually performs the data conversion. If 0921 does not exist in the codebase (it is not in the diff for this PR), then on any environment that previously had data in `sentry_savedsearch` with `visibility=ORGANIZATION`, no migration will ever convert those saved searches to `GroupSearchView`. A maintainer should verify that 0921 is present and has run in production before merging, otherwise this PR silently breaks a previously-working data migration.

title: New `equations` parameter added to `run_top_events_timeseries_query` without tests
body: `run_top_events_timeseries_query` now accepts and forwards an `equations` parameter through to `rpc_dataset_common.run_top_events_timeseries_query`, but no test exercises the new parameter. The other files changed in the explore area (`visualizes.tsx`, `aggregateFields.tsx`, etc.) update test fixtures to match the `yAxes -> yAxis` rename but nothing verifies the equations path. Add at least one test covering the equations parameter.

title: Null summary can render in the UI when API returns `success=false` with used feedbacks
body:
`tooFewFeedbacks` is only true when `numFeedbacksUsed === 0 && !data.success`. The `FeedbackSummary` component checks `tooFewFeedbacks` and `isError` to decide whether to render, but it does not check whether `summary` is null. If the API returns `success: false, summary: null, numFeedbacksUsed > 0`, the component renders the title plus an empty `

null

`. Either also bail out when `summary == null`, or have the hook set `tooFewFeedbacks` more conservatively.

title: Empty error_ids returned from snuba can cause validation errors in log assembly
body: `error_ids = response[0].get("error_ids", []) if response else []` assumes `response[0]` exists. In tests where `query_replay_instance` is not set up, the endpoint relies on the integration being mocked. In production, if the snuba call returns no rows (but does return a `[]` array), `response[0]` is `undefined` and the optional chaining would handle that, but then `error_events` is `[]` — fine. However, when `disable_error_fetching` is false and `error_ids` contains ids that no longer resolve in nodestore (a normal race after deletion), the `fetch_error_details` wrapper currently swallows exceptions silently with `sentry_sdk.capture_exception`, but the test `test_get_with_error` does not exercise the empty-error-ids path. Worth adding a regression test for the case where `error_ids` is present but all ids miss in nodestore.

title: Falsy custom cell returns treated as 'no custom renderer'
body: `renderTableBodyCell` is typed as `React.ReactNode | undefined`. The implementation uses `if (cell) { return cell }` to decide whether to fall back to the default renderer, which treats falsy ReactNodes (`0`, `false`, empty string) as 'no custom renderer'. In practice custom renderers typically return JSX or `undefined`, but the contract should use `cell !== undefined` to avoid a future footgun when a renderer intentionally returns `false` to render nothing.

title: Renaming inner parameter `organization` to `org` may obscure the dead-data branch
body: The diff renames the inner parameter in `getCustomFieldRenderer` from `organization?: Organization` to `org?: Organization` to avoid shadowing the prop. The intent is fine, but combined with the fact that the parameter is never actually used (the previous code passed it to `datasetConfig.getCustomFieldRenderer` and the new code still does not), it confirms that this function takes a parameter it never consumes. Recommend dropping the parameter entirely from the signature so callers don't have to pass it.

title: TableWidgetVisualization rendered with empty data when feature flag is enabled
body: When the feature flag `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, the code renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{ data: [], meta: { fields: {}, units: {} } }} />` with hardcoded empty data, completely ignoring the computed `tableResults` and `result` variables that contain the actual table data. Any organization with this feature flag enabled will see empty tables in their dashboard widgets instead of the actual query data. The component should receive the real `tableResults` data (likely mapped to the `TabularData` format that `TableWidgetVisualization` expects).

title: Default autofix automation tuning silently changed from 'low' to 'off'
body: `DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT` was changed from `"low"` to `"off"` without any indication in the PR description. This changes the default behavior for new projects: autofix will no longer run automatically on new issues by default. The corresponding project option default in `src/sentry/projectoptions/defaults.py` (line 205) was also changed. This is a user-facing behavior change that should be called out explicitly in the PR description and potentially coordinated with documentation/release notes, as existing projects that rely on the default will not be affected, but new projects will have a different experience.

title: Analytics recorded before feature flag check
body: The `analytics.record(...)` call for `preprod_artifact.api.assemble` is placed before the `features.has(...)` check. This means analytics events are recorded for every request to this endpoint, including requests from organizations where the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` feature is disabled (which return 404). This inflates analytics metrics with requests from users who can't actually use the feature. If the intent is to track actual usage, the analytics call should be moved after the feature flag check.

title: dcg_to_slow_conditions source changed from dcg_to_groups.keys() to dcg_ids
body: Previously, `get_condition_query_groups` computed `dcg_to_slow_conditions` from `list(event_data.dcg_to_groups.keys())`, while `get_groups_to_fire` computed it from `list(event_data.dcg_ids)`. The refactoring unifies both to use `list(event_data.dcg_ids)` (computed once in `process_delayed_workflows`). If `event_data.dcg_ids` and `event_data.dcg_to_groups.keys()` contain different sets of DCG IDs, this changes which DCGs have their slow conditions fetched and could alter workflow firing behavior. The behavioral difference should be verified and tests should cover the case where these two sets differ.

title: Broad except in get_environment_info swallows all errors silently
body: `get_environment_info` catches a bare `Exception` and only logs at info level via `logger.info(...)`. This swallows all errors including programming errors (AttributeError, TypeError, etc.) silently, making debugging difficult. The intent seems to be to gracefully handle cases where the environment can't be determined, but catching all exceptions is too broad. At minimum, the exception type should be narrowed (e.g., `Event.DoesNotExist`, `NodeData.DoesNotExist`) or the bare except should log at warning/error level for unexpected exceptions.

title: Feedback separator changed from list format to raw join
body:
The separator for joining feedback entries changed from `"
".join(f"- {msg}" for msg in feedbacks)` (which produced a bulleted list) to `"
------
".join(feedbacks)` (which produces raw separator-delimited entries). This is a significant change in how feedback is presented to the LLM. If any feedback message contains the substring `------`, it could be confused with a separator. Additionally, the new format doesn't provide visual structure (no bullet points), which may affect LLM summarization quality. This should be tested to ensure the LLM still produces good summaries with the new format.

title: KeyError when integration.metadata lacks 'sender' field
body: In GitHubInstallation.dispatch, the user-mismatch check reads `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` directly. The `sender` key is populated only by the GitHub installation webhook handler — not by build_integration (which only sets sender from state if present) — so any path where the webhook has not yet been processed, has failed, or otherwise did not set `metadata["sender"]` will raise KeyError and 500. This is reachable in normal operation: the first user that installs via OAuth creates the Integration before the webhook lands, and any subsequent install on that installation_id will crash. Should be `integration.metadata.get("sender") or {}).get("login")` and treat None as a mismatch.

title: get_user_info() exception not handled, can cause 500
body: `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` makes an authenticated call to GitHub's /user endpoint. If this call raises (network failure, DNS error, GitHub 5xx, rate-limit response, ApiError, etc.) the view returns 500 to the user instead of the graceful `error()` page shown for all other failure modes. The surrounding OAuth token-exchange path already wraps everything in `try/except Exception`, so for consistency (and to avoid leaking a stack trace on a transient GitHub failure) this should be wrapped the same way and a missing/invalid `login` should also fall back to `error()`.

title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the 404 path
body: After the change the test does two GETs: first `setup_path?installation_id=...`, then `setup_path?code=...&state=ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05`. Because the second GET uses a state value that does not match `pipeline.signature`, the view short-circuits with the state-mismatch branch and returns the generic `Invalid installation request.` error before `build_integration` (which is what actually calls the 404-stubbed `/app/installations/<id>` endpoint) ever runs. The 404 stub is therefore dead code in this test. The assertion was also weakened from `b"The GitHub installation could not be found."` to the generic error string, so a regression that silently swallows the 404 would not be caught. Either use the correct state so the test reaches build_integration and assert the specific 404 message, or rename the test to reflect what it now covers (state mismatch).

title: Hardcoded webhook signature does not match the modified payload
body: `test_github_user_mismatch` mutates the JSON loaded from `INSTALLATION_EVENT_EXAMPLE` (changes `installation.id` and `sender.login`) before POSTing to `/extensions/github/webhook/`, but reuses the signature `sha1=d184e6717f8bfbcc291ebc8c0756ee446c6c9486` that was computed for the original (unmodified) fixture body. With signature verification enabled the webhook handler will refuse the event and no Integration with `sender.login == "attacker"` will be created, so the subsequent assertion that `GitHubInstallation` correctly rejects the second install does not actually exercise the mismatch branch — it would behave identically with or without the new check. The signature should be recomputed for the modified body (or the test should bypass signature verification explicitly).

title: installation_id bound to pipeline before CSRF state is validated
body: In OAuthLoginView.dispatch the very first action is `pipeline.bind_state("installation_id", installation_id)`, which executes before the `if request.GET.get("state") != pipeline.signature` CSRF/state check on the OAuth callback path. So a request that supplies a forged `state` (e.g. forged-state scenario) will still mutate pipeline state in Redis before being rejected. This is low impact because the next legitimate request will re-bind or the error returns immediately, but defensively the state validation should run before any side effects on the pipeline.

title: safe_urlopen() not wrapped in try/except
