Every other handler in the PR (confirm.handler.ts:175, editLocation.handler.ts:85, handleCancelBooking.ts:251, deleteCredential.handler.ts:290, handleNewBooking.ts:1063) falls back to `user.destinationCalendar` when the booking has none. Here that fallback was removed (it was a typo'd duplicate in the old code), so reschedule webhooks and the reschedule email are now sent with `destinationCalendar: []` even when the booking's owner has a destination calendar configured. This is inconsistent and may mislead recipients about which calendar will be updated.

title: No test covers the core multi-host destinationCalendar fix
body: The PR author checked the box "I haven't added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works." The only test change in the whole PR is updating the expected `destinationCalendar` value from `null` to `[]` in `apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts`. There is no integration or unit test exercising the new collective-event path: building the `evt.destinationCalendar` array with organizer + team host destinations, persisting it through `handleNewBooking`, or verifying that `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` fans out to all host calendars. Given the size of the refactor (signatures changed, persistence narrowed, multiple CalendarService adapters updated), this is a significant test gap and the regressions called out above (e.g. TypeError on Meet bookings, dropped team destinations, broken Google update/delete) are likely to pass through CI because nothing in the suite exercises the scenario.

title: hosts.map users lack destinationCalendar, so teamDestinationCalendars stays empty
body: In the new loadUsers(), when the event has hosts, `users` is built via `hosts.map(({ user, isFixed }) => ({ ...user, isFixed }))`. The `user` record on each host is whatever Prisma returned for the relation; no explicit `select`/`include` is added, so relation fields like `destinationCalendar` are not present on those `user` objects. Downstream, `teamMemberPromises` does `if (isTeamEventType && eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE" && user.destinationCalendar)` and pushes to `teamDestinationCalendars` — this will always be undefined for host-loaded users, so `teamDestinationCalendars` ends up empty for COLLECTIVE team events. The whole point of this PR (multiple hosts receiving calendar events) silently fails whenever hosts come from the `eventType.hosts` relation.

title: evt.destinationCalendar?.push silently no-ops when null
body: Right above, `destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` is set. The follow-up `if (isTeamEventType && eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE") { evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars); }` uses optional chaining on a potentially null array — `null?.push` is just `undefined`, it does nothing and does not warn. For any COLLECTIVE event without an event-type or organizer destination calendar, no team members' destination calendars are attached to `evt`, even though they were collected into `teamDestinationCalendars`. Replace `?.push(...)` with an explicit `evt.destinationCalendar ??= []; evt.destinationCalendar.push(...)` (or build the final array once and assign it).

title: Only first destination calendar is persisted on the booking
body: The booking `data` block writes `destinationCalendar: evt.destinationCalendar && evt.destinationCalendar.length > 0 ? { connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id } } : undefined`. The Booking schema has a single `destinationCalendar` relation, so only the first entry in `evt.destinationCalendar` is persisted. The PR’s stated goal is to invite every host to their own calendar, but on any later operation (reschedule, cancel, edit-location, request-reschedule) the booking record exposes only one destination. The other per-host calendar references survive only as BookingReference rows; deleting the booking.destinationCalendar connect for the event-type even on first creation breaks the previously persisted id reference for non-collective callers and silently drops the per-host mapping for re-runs. Either the schema needs to become a join table, or the booking should record which host’s calendar it was set under and consumers must be updated accordingly — this PR ships neither.

title: updateEvent fallback finds by externalId === externalCalendarId (its own falsy arg)
body: In `updateEvent`: `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. The branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, but then `.find` compares each calendar’s `externalId` against that same falsy value — it can essentially never match, so `selectedCalendar` will always be `undefined` in the fallback path and the update will fall back to whatever `calendarId` ends up being (`undefined` here, since the destructuring doesn’t define one). This is a regression vs. the old line `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`, which at least returned the first calendar’s externalId. The intended fallback was almost certainly `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId` (or matching by `credentialId`). Effect: any Google calendar update that reaches this code without a non-empty `externalCalendarId` will misroute or attempt to operate against `calendarId: undefined`.

title: deleteEvent fallback also searches by externalId === externalCalendarId
body: Same defect as in `updateEvent`. `const calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` — when `externalCalendarId` is null/empty the `find` predicate compares each calendar’s externalId against that same null/empty value, so the find never matches and the fallback always yields `undefined`. The eventual ternary `calendarId ? calendarId : defaultCalendarId` then drops to `"primary"`, which is the wrong calendar for multi-host events and can delete from the wrong account or simply 404. Either use `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId` for the fallback or restrict the lookup to a credentialId-keyed match.

title: Calendar.createEvent signature requires credentialId; other implementations still take one arg
body: The `Calendar` interface now declares `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number): Promise<NewCalendarEventType>`, but the other concrete implementations were not updated: `BaseCalendarService.createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` in packages/lib/CalendarService.ts (line 125), `LarkCalendarService.createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` in packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts (line 125), and `Office365CalendarService.createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` in packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts (line 72) all declare `implements Calendar` and define `createEvent` with a single parameter. This is an interface/implementation mismatch that TypeScript will reject on build; every consumer of these apps (e.g., `createAllCalendarEvents` in EventManager) currently calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent)` without the new `credentialId`, so those code paths will not compile against the interface. Either make `credentialId` optional in the interface and update only Google, or update the three other services and all call sites to pass the credential id.

title: Organization slug/requestSlug logic is inverted and out of scope
body: This PR is supposed to change only the destinationCalendar handling, but this file was modified and the change inverts behavior: previously `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` set the org slug when billing was disabled, and `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { requestedSlug: slug })` set the metadata requestedSlug when billing was enabled. The new code is `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` (slug now set when billing is enabled — opposite of before) plus `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { requestedSlug: slug } : {})` (requestedSlug now conditional, where it used to also be set unconditionally on the top-level create). Organizations created while billing is disabled will now have no slug at all instead of the previous behavior, which breaks subdomain routing for non-billing orgs. This deserves to be a separate PR with proper justification and migration handling, not a drive-by change hidden inside a calendar refactor.

title: loadUsers aggressively throws on empty dynamicUserList and is no longer required to return users
body: The new `loadUsers` wraps everything in try/catch and throws HttpError(500, "Unable to load users") for any non-HttpError/non-Prisma error, and adds new preconditions that the previous version lacked: `if (!Array.isArray(dynamicUserList) || dynamicUserList.length === 0) throw new Error("dynamicUserList is not properly defined or empty.")` and `if (!Array.isArray(hosts)) throw new Error("eventType.hosts is not properly defined.")`. Empty `dynamicUserList` was previously allowed to fall through to a normal empty result; a route that legitimately resolves no users (e.g., data issues) will now return 500/400 instead of being handled by upstream `ensureAvailableUsers` guards. Also, `return users.length ? users : eventType.users` evaluates eventType.users only after spreading hosts — for a non-host regular event this works, but for a team event with `eventType.schedulingType=ROUND_ROBIN` and no hosts it now returns the legacy `eventType.users` array and silently bypasses the host semantics the rest of the code expects.

title: Team member shape adds unknown firstName/lastName empty fields
body: `teamMemberPromises` returns `firstName: "", lastName: ""` for every team member, but the `Person` type in `@calcom/types/Calendar` has no such keys (only `name`, `email`, `timeZone`, `language`, `username`, `id`, `bookingId`, `locale`, `timeFormat`, `bookingSeat`). Any strict object-literal usage would fail, and email/SMS renderers that iterate the object will get the empty strings. This was added without updating the type definition or any consumer — either the fields need to be added to `Person` and used by templates, or the spread of dead keys should be removed.

title: TypeError crash when destinationCalendar is empty and location is Google Meet
body: After the destinationCalendar is converted to an array, this fallback uses `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without an optional chain. When `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` or `[]` (which is a common case handled by every caller of this function, e.g. when the user selected Google Meet as the location but has no Google Calendar configured on Cal, which previously was a soft "fallback to Cal Video" path), `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = ... ?? []` yields `undefined`, and the next expression `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')`. The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"` and would safely fall back to Cal Video; the new code crashes before the fallback can occur. This regression breaks the entire Meet-location code path for any booking without a Google destination calendar.

title: Team destination calendars not added when no event-type or organizer calendar exists
body: The event's `destinationCalendar` is set by the chain to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` is set. The subsequent line `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);` uses optional chaining and silently no-ops on `null`. As a result, in the very scenario the PR is meant to fix — a COLLECTIVE event where the event-type has no destination calendar and the organizer (first host) has no destination calendar but other team members do — the team members' `destinationCalendar` values are never attached to `evt.destinationCalendar`, and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` falls back to "the first connected calendar" instead of creating the event in each host's calendar. The push should be a normal assignment that initialises the array if needed, e.g. `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`. Also note that if `eventType.destinationCalendar` is set, pushing team members onto the same array may create duplicate references for the same DestinationCalendar record.

title: Broken fallback for updateEvent when externalCalendarId is missing
body: In `updateEvent`, the fallback for when `externalCalendarId` is not provided is now `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When `externalCalendarId` is `null`/undefined (which happens for legacy bookings stored before this PR that do not have `BookingReference.externalCalendarId` populated), the predicate compares `cal.externalId === undefined` and never matches, so the result is `undefined`. The previous code `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` correctly fell back to the first destination calendar's externalId. With this change, update calls that previously succeeded now hit Google with `calendarId: undefined` and fail. The intent appears to be "pick the destination calendar for this credential", so the find should compare against `credentialId` (or the caller should pass it through), not against the already-undefined `externalCalendarId`. The same broken pattern is present in `deleteEvent` (see next finding).

title: Broken fallback for deleteEvent when externalCalendarId is missing
body: The deleteEvent fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` exhibits the same bug as updateEvent: when `externalCalendarId` is undefined/null, the predicate cannot match, so `calendarId` ends up `undefined` and Google receives a delete call without a `calendarId` (only the `defaultCalendarId = "primary"` ternary saves it when `calendarId` is falsy). For legacy bookings that don't store an externalCalendarId on the reference, this silently routes deletions to "primary" instead of the correct destination calendar. The fallback was `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` before this PR, and the rewrite removes that legitimate fallback without providing a working one.

title: Team members may be excluded when first user in array is not the organizer
body: The new `teamDestinationCalendars` is built from `users.slice(1)`, i.e. it always excludes whichever user happens to be at index 0 in the `users` array. For dynamic events `users` is populated from `prisma.user.findMany({ where: { username: { in: dynamicUserList } } })` with no `orderBy`, so the index-0 user may not be the organizer. If the actual organizer happens to be at index 0 they are correctly excluded (their calendar is taken from `organizerUser.destinationCalendar`), but if they are not, their `destinationCalendar` is lost from `teamDestinationCalendars` because `.slice(1)` indiscriminately cuts the first element. The exclusion should be keyed on whether the user is the organizer (e.g. by id/username), not on array index.

title: Refresh token overwritten with literal string "refresh_token"
Zod schema is invalid - computed property syntax used incorrectly
Returns fetch Response object, callers expect axios-style response with .data
body:
When credential sharing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch` `Response` object instead of calling the refresh function and returning its resolved value. Several integrations then treat the result as the original axios response:

- `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177,192`: does `hubspotRefreshToken.expiryDate = Math.round(...)`. A fetch `Response` has no `expiryDate`; this throws and the token is never saved.
- `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:96`: does `if (!tokenInfo.data.error)`. A `Response` has no `.data`, so this throws and the credential update is skipped.
- `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94-96`: does `res?.data` and then `token.access_token`/`token.expiry_date`. With sync enabled `res.data` is `undefined` and the next lines throw.
- `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:84`: passes the `Response` to `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>`, which will not produce a `RefreshTokenResp` shape.
- `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:262-264`: passes the `Response` through `handleErrorsJson(response)`; even if it parses, the body will not match `refreshTokenResponseSchema`.

Either the helper should `await refreshFunction()` (i.e. only short-circuit when syncing) or every caller must be updated to consume a `Response`.

title: No HTTP method check - GET/HEAD/OPTIONS can mutate credentials
body: The handler does not verify `req.method` and proceeds to write to the database for any HTTP verb. Because the only authentication is a shared webhook secret read from a header (not a session/CSRF token), a cross-origin GET/POST sent by an attacker's page that the victim visits can cause credential create/update calls if the secret leaks or is guessable. The handler must reject non-POST requests with 405.

title: Uncaught exceptions on invalid payload / bad decryption can crash the handler
body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a ZodError on bad input, and `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, ...))` throws if decryption returns a non-JSON string (e.g. wrong key). Neither call is wrapped in try/catch, so a single bad request from a self-hoster returns a generic 500 with a stack trace and no structured error message, and the response never goes out cleanly. Wrap them and respond with 400 on validation/decryption failures.

title: Webhook secret comparison is not constant-time
body: `req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` short-circuits on the first differing byte, so a network attacker measuring response latency can recover the secret byte by byte. Use a constant-time comparison (e.g. `crypto.timingSafeEqual`) since the secret is high-value.

title: Race condition between findFirst and update/create
body: Two concurrent webhook calls for the same `userId`/`appSlug` can both run `findFirst` returning nothing, then both call `credential.create`, producing duplicate credential rows (the schema does not enforce a unique constraint on `(userId, appId, type)`). There is no transaction wrapping the find-then-write, and no idempotency key on incoming webhooks. Wrap the lookup-and-write in a Prisma transaction (or upsert with a unique key) and consider de-duplicating webhooks.

title: Token refresh POST sent without authentication to user-controlled URL
body: When sharing is enabled, Cal.com POSTs the user's Cal.com ID and app slug to `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with no webhook secret / signature header. If the env var is ever set to an attacker-controlled URL (mistakenly, via env injection, or via a malicious admin in a multi-tenant setup), the attacker can observe every refresh attempt and correlate users -> apps -> Cal.com IDs, and respond with whatever token they want Cal.com to use next (giving them access to every user's calendar/video data). The sync endpoint should authenticate Cal.com with a shared secret header, and the response should be authenticated/signed too. Also, `calcomUserId` is sent in the URL body - consider sending it in a signed payload.

title: fetch() has no timeout - hangs forever on slow sync endpoint
body: `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` has no `signal`/timeout, so if the sync endpoint is unresponsive Cal.com's token refresh path blocks indefinitely, which in turn blocks every booking/Calendar availability check for that user. Pass `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(...)` or wrap in a race.

title: Salesforce bypasses refreshOAuthTokens - credential sharing never engages
body: The new Salesforce refresh code (lines 75-99) calls `fetch` directly to `login.salesforce.com/.../token` and never goes through `refreshOAuthTokens`. So while the PR description claims every supported app participates in credential syncing, Salesforce will silently ignore `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` / `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` and keep hitting Salesforce directly. Either route Salesforce through the helper or document the deviation.

title: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is misnamed and a non-boolean
body: `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is the value of `process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (or that of `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`) when both are truthy - i.e. it returns a string like `"abc..."`, not a boolean. Callers such as `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` use it in an `if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED)` test, which works, but the name suggests a boolean and the value leaks the env var into logging paths. Also, the constant does not require `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, even though `refreshOAuthTokens` requires it before sharing actually happens - rename and normalize (`!!`) so it is a true boolean and reflects all three required env vars.

title: Broken Zod schema for minimum token response
body: The `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` as computed property keys. Calling `.toString()` on a Zod schema returns a fixed string like `"ZodString"`, not a property name pattern. This does not create a schema that accepts any string key with a number value (as the comment suggests); instead it creates a single hardcoded key with an arbitrary name. When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, every call to `safeParse` will validate against this broken schema, likely rejecting all valid sync responses (or accepting them with wrong types). The intent was probably `z.record(z.string(), z.number()).optional()` or similar. All sync-path token refreshes will fail validation and throw "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned".

title: Missing refresh_token overwritten with literal string "refresh_token"
body: When `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token` is falsy, the code sets it to the literal string `"refresh_token"`. This is clearly placeholder/debug code that was never completed. When the sync endpoint returns a response that omits `refresh_token` (which is the expected case — the sync endpoint only returns access_token and expiry), the credential will be saved with `refresh_token: "refresh_token"`, permanently breaking token refresh for that user. Even in the non-sync path, any schema that doesn't require `refresh_token` (e.g., the Salesforce schema) will have its existing refresh_token overwritten by this literal string before the spread in the caller, unless the caller explicitly re-overwrites it (as Salesforce does, but Google Calendar and Office365 do not).

title: Sync branch returns fetch Response, callers expect incompatible shapes
body: When the sync endpoint is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch` `Response` object. The callers expect completely different shapes: googlecalendar expects `{ res: { data: { access_token, expiry_date } } }` (from googleapis' `refreshToken`), hubspot expects a `HubspotToken` object (from `@hubspot/api-client`), zohocrm and zoho-bigin expect an axios response with `.data`. When sync is enabled, googlecalendar will do `res?.data` on a `Response` object (undefined), then `token.access_token` throws TypeError. Hubspot, zohocrm, and zoho-bigin will have similar shape mismatches. The function needs to normalize the sync endpoint response into the shape each caller expects.

title: Race condition: no transaction around findFirst + create/update
body: The handler does `findFirst` then `create` or `update` in separate queries without a transaction. Two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same `(userId, appSlug)` can both find no existing credential, both attempt `create`, and either violate a unique constraint or produce duplicate credentials. The comment says "Can't use prisma upsert as we don't know the id of the credential", but the solution is to wrap the findFirst+create in `prisma.$transaction`, or use a composite unique key on `(userId, appId)` and catch the unique violation to fall back to update.

title: No error handling around decryption and JSON parse
body: `symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "")` will throw if the key is missing, wrong, or the ciphertext is malformed. The subsequent `JSON.parse` will throw if the decrypted plaintext is not valid JSON. Neither is wrapped in try/catch, so an invalid payload causes an unhandled exception and a 500 response, and the error details may leak. An attacker can probe the endpoint with random ciphertexts to enumerate behavior. Wrap in try/catch and return a 400 on decryption/parse failure.

title: Non-constant-time webhook secret comparison and header case bug
body: Two issues in the secret check: (1) `!==` on the header value is not constant-time, allowing timing side-channel attacks to recover the secret byte-by-byte. Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers. (2) `req.headers` keys are lowercased by Node, but the code looks up the header using `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` as-is. If a self-hoster sets the env to a mixed-case name, the lookup silently fails (the comparison becomes `undefined !== secret` which is always true), and the endpoint returns 403 for legitimate requests. Normalize the env var to lowercase before lookup, or always lowercase the key.

title: No HTTP method check and no rate limiting
body: The handler processes any HTTP method (GET, PUT, DELETE, etc.) without checking `req.method`. It should explicitly accept only POST. Additionally, the endpoint has no rate limiting or brute-force protection beyond the shared secret. Combined with the non-constant-time comparison, an attacker who discovers the endpoint can attempt to brute-force the secret or flood it with requests.

title: Outgoing request to sync endpoint has no authentication
body: The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the body. There is no shared secret, HMAC signature, or mutual TLS to authenticate the Cal.com instance to the self-hoster's endpoint. If the endpoint URL is discovered (e.g., via DNS enumeration or logs), an attacker can request refreshed tokens for arbitrary `calcomUserId` values, receiving valid access tokens for victims' third-party integrations. Add a signed payload (e.g., HMAC with a shared secret) or a bearer token header.

title: No timeout on sync endpoint fetch
body: The `fetch` to the sync endpoint has no timeout. If the endpoint hangs or is slow, every token refresh in Cal.com will block on it, cascading into stalled calendar/video operations. Add an `AbortController` with a reasonable timeout (e.g., 10s).

title: Salesforce token refreshed on every service instantiation
body: The newly added block in `getClient` unconditionally fetches a new access token from Salesforce every time the method is called. Since `getClient` is invoked in the constructor (`this.conn = this.getClient(credential).then(c => c)`), every `new SalesforceCalendarService(credential)` — which happens for every booking/event involving Salesforce — triggers a token refresh request to Salesforce. This is a significant performance regression and risks hitting Salesforce API rate limits. The refresh should only happen when the existing token is expired or near expiry, matching the pattern used in other CalendarServices.

title: Unreliable response check and missing error handling
body: Two issues: (1) `response.statusText !== "OK"` is unreliable — `statusText` may be empty for HTTP/2 or some responses. Use `!response.ok` or check `response.status`. (2) The entire new fetch block has no try/catch. If the network request fails (DNS error, connection refused, timeout), the rejection propagates unhandled from the constructor's promise chain, leaving `this.conn` in a rejected state and breaking all subsequent Salesforce operations with no clear error.

title: Google calendar token refresh broken when sync endpoint is enabled
body: When `refreshOAuthTokens` takes the sync branch, it returns a raw `fetch` `Response` object. The next line does `const token = res?.data;` — on a `Response`, `.data` is undefined. Then `token.access_token` throws TypeError, which is caught by the outer try/catch and causes the credential to be marked invalid (via the `invalid_grant` path... actually the error message won't be "invalid_grant", so the catch just returns the unrefreshed auth, but the root cause is a shape mismatch in the sync path that will silently break Google Calendar for all self-hosters using this feature).

title: Zoom refresh_token lost when sync endpoint returns minimal response
body: In the sync path, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` uses the broken `minimumTokenResponseSchema` (see finding on parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts). Even if validation passes, the helper then overwrites `refresh_token` with the literal string `"refresh_token"` when it's missing. Downstream, `key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token` sets the stored credential's refresh token to that literal string. The next refresh attempt will send `"refresh_token"` as the actual refresh token to Zoom, which will reject it with `invalid_grant`, permanently breaking the integration.

title: Redirect URI hardcoded, inconsistent with callback.ts
body: The `add.ts` handler hardcodes `redirectUri = WEBAPP_URL + "/api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback"`, while the corresponding `callback.ts` (line 36) still uses `WEBAPP_URL + "/api/integrations/${appConfig.slug}/callback"`. If `appConfig.slug` is ever changed, the add and callback endpoints will use mismatched redirect URIs and OAuth will fail with a redirect_uri_mismatch error. Both files should use the same expression (preferably the config-based one).

title: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED name is misleading
body: The constant is defined as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, but the token refresh sync path additionally requires `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`. Each call site that needs the sync path checks the constant AND the endpoint separately (e.g., in `refreshOAuthTokens.ts`), which is correct but error-prone. Consider either including the endpoint check in the constant or renaming it to reflect what it actually gates (e.g., `APP_CREDENTIAL_WEBHOOK_ENABLED`).

title: Encryption key length comment is wrong
body: The comment for `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` says "must be 32 bytes for AES256 encryption algorithm" and recommends `openssl rand -base64 24`. Base64-encoded 24 bytes decodes to 18 bytes, which is less than the 32 bytes (256 bits) required by AES-256. The correct command for 32 raw bytes is `openssl rand -base64 32` (which produces ~44 characters of base64). The `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` comment on line 91 has the same mistake but was not introduced by this PR.

title: Sync path silently bypassed for team credentials without logging
body: The condition `... && userId` means that for team credentials (where `credential.userId` is null), the sync path is silently skipped and the normal refresh is used, even when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set. This means team-installed apps on self-hosted instances will continue refreshing against the self-hoster's OAuth client, not the parent's, which may be the intended behavior but is undocumented and surprising. At minimum, a log message should indicate that the sync path was skipped due to missing userId.

title: minimumTokenResponseSchema does not declare an index signature, validation will always fail
body: The schema uses `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()`, but those are computed property names that evaluate to the strings "ZodString" and "ZodOptional" at runtime, not TypeScript index signatures. As a result the parsed object must contain a literal `ZodString: number` property in addition to `access_token`, which OAuth token responses never have. Whenever the credential-sync flow is active, `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(response)` returns `{success: false}` and `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned", so every credential refresh attempted via the sync endpoint will fail.

title: Returns SafeParseResult instead of parsed data; Google Calendar persists the wrapper
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the full `safeParse` result object (`{success: true, data: ...}`), but `googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` consumes it as if it were the parsed key: `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema); await prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. This causes the database row to be overwritten with `{success: true, data: {…token fields…}}` rather than the token fields themselves. On the next request `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` will fail and the credential becomes effectively unusable.

title: Mutates parsed result by setting refresh_token to the literal string "refresh_token"
body: If the parsed response has no `refresh_token`, the helper does `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. The string "refresh_token" is not a valid OAuth refresh token; any caller that persists this object (directly or via spread) will end up storing a placeholder value, causing the next refresh attempt to fail with invalid_grant. This affects the standard schemas (e.g. `refreshTokenResponseSchema`, `googleCredentialSchema`) that mark `refresh_token` optional. The mutation also has no TypeScript escape hatch – the helper writes a property that may not exist on the inferred type.

title: Sync endpoint returns a fetch Response while callers expect axios / typed token objects
body:
When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch` `Response`. Several callers assume their original axios / jsforce shape:
- `hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`: treats the return value as `HubspotToken` and reads `hubspotRefreshToken.expiryDate` and `.expiresIn` (undefined on a Response) and writes back `expiryDate = Math.round(Date.now() + undefined * 1000)` → NaN persisted as the expiry.
- `zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts` and `zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts`: read `tokenInfo.data.error`, `tokenInfo.data.expiryDate`, etc. on what is now a `Response` object – `undefined.error` throws.
- `googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`: reads `res?.data.access_token` – undefined, throwing on `.access_token`.
The sync path therefore crashes the refresh for several integrations instead of delegating to the user's endpoint.

title: zoho-bigin passes credential.id where user.id is expected
body: `refreshAccessToken(credentialId, credentialKey)` calls `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)`. `refreshOAuthTokens` then POSTs `calcomUserId=${credentialId}` (the `Credential.id`, not `User.id`) to the self-hoster's sync endpoint, so the parent cannot resolve the user. Every other caller (Hubspot, Office365 video, Lark, Webex, Zoom, ZohoCRM) correctly forwards `credential.userId`.

title: Webhook secret comparison is not constant-time
body: `req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` performs a non-constant-time string comparison, exposing the webhook secret to timing attacks. Anyone able to observe response latencies could recover the secret character by character. Because this single shared secret authorizes writes of OAuth credentials for arbitrary `userId` values (see below), a leaked secret enables full impersonation of any user via injected tokens. Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` over equal-length buffers.

title: Webhook allows writing OAuth tokens for any user with no per-user authorization
body: The endpoint authenticates the caller only via the shared `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` header; the request body supplies `userId` directly. There is no binding between caller identity and the target user (no signature of the userId, no per-user secret, no replay protection/nonce, no rate limit). Anyone in possession of the secret can therefore upsert OAuth credentials for any userId, including admin accounts, and effectively impersonate them. Because the secret is also required to be 32 bytes for AES-256, a leak is catastrophic for the instance.

title: findFirst + create/update upsert is racy
body: The handler does a `findFirst` followed by separate `update`/`create` calls rather than a single `upsert`/transaction. Two concurrent webhook calls for the same `(userId, appSlug)` can both observe `appCredential === null` and both insert, leaving duplicate `Credential` rows for the same user/app and breaking the assumption made elsewhere in the codebase (larkcalendar, office365video, webex, zoom callbacks) that there is at most one credential per `(type, appId, userId)`.

title: Unnecessary database round-trip before appStoreMetadata lookup
body: The handler queries `prisma.app.findUnique({ where: { slug: reqBody.appSlug } })` and then immediately re-resolves the same slug against the in-memory `appStoreMetadata` map. The DB call adds latency to a public webhook and is redundant: validating against `appStoreMetadata` directly (and 404ing if absent) gives the same behaviour without hitting Postgres.

title: Header lookup uses env var verbatim, but Node lowercases request headers
body: `req.headers` in Node stores header names in lowercase. The handler looks up `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"]`. If an operator sets `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` to any mixed/upper-case value, the lookup is `undefined` and every request is rejected with 403, even when the secret itself is correct. The constant should be lowercased before use, or compared against `req.headers[name.toLowerCase()]`.

title: Body validation throws and bubbles as 500 instead of returning 400
body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a Zod error when the body is malformed. Next.js converts that into a generic 500, while the rest of the handler consistently returns structured 400/403/404 JSON. Callers (the self-hoster's parent app) will not be able to distinguish malformed payloads from server errors.

title: Salesforce refresh bypasses refreshOAuthTokens entirely
body: `getClient` issues the refresh POST directly to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` and then runs it through `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, but it never routes through `refreshOAuthTokens`. The result is that for self-hosters that turn on `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, Salesforce refresh tokens continue to be exchanged against Salesforce directly instead of being fetched from the configured parent service – inconsistent with every other calendar/video integration modified here, and undermining the purpose of the feature for Salesforce users.

title: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED combines two unrelated flags and yields a non-boolean
body: `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`. With an empty string for either env var this evaluates to the empty string (or the other env var), not `false`, and downstream code uses it as a truthy check (`if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED)`) – empty string is falsy so it happens to work, but `parseRefreshTokenResponse` later does `if (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT)`, so the semantics depend on whether the env var is the literal `"false"`/`"0"` or empty. Coerce to a boolean explicitly and either include `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` in the gate or document the partial activation mode.

title: Team admin/owner check uses && instead of ||
body: The authorization gate `const isTeamAdminOrOwner = (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...));` requires the user to be BOTH admin AND owner. The intent is admin OR owner (typical permission check). Using `&&` means an admin who isn't an owner (or vice-versa) cannot add guests, and only true owners who are also admins ever satisfy it. This is a high-impact auth regression for team bookings.

title: Email deduplication is case-sensitive, lets same data form differently-typed duplicates through
body: `uniqueGuests` filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails with case-sensitive string comparison (`guest === attendee.email`, `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). The blacklist is lowercased, but incoming `guest` strings are not. RFC 5321 in practice treats the domain as case-insensitive and most providers treat the local part as case-insensitive too. Submitting `Foo@Bar.com` and an existing attendee `foo@bar.com` (or a blacklisted `FOO@bar.com`) is treated as a new guest, allowing duplicates and bypassing the blacklist. Same issue exists in `apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx` (Set-based uniqueness on the raw values) and in `packages/emails/email-manager.ts` (`newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`), which causes newly added guests to receive the wrong email variant.

title: No transaction around DB update and external calendar call
body: `prisma.booking.update` adds the new attendees to the DB, and only then `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` is called against external calendars with no try/catch or transaction wrapper. If the calendar sync throws (network failure, auth, daily/zoom error), the booking now has new attendees persisted while the underlying video/calendar provider never received them, and the user sees no error and no rollback. Wrap the DB update and the external calendar update in a compensating action (or catch and roll back attendees) so failures don't leave the system in an inconsistent state.

title: Emails sent to blacklisted guests because original `guests` array is used
body: The handler filters blacklisted emails into `uniqueGuests`, but then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the unfiltered input. If a user submits a mix containing at least one valid guest, blacklisted addresses in the same submission still get email notifications (and may even receive a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` depending on how `attendees.includes(attendee.email)` resolves). Send notifications to `uniqueGuests` (or at minimum exclude blacklisted ones) and consider lowercasing before comparison.

title: Existing attendees can add arbitrary guests to someone else's meeting
body: `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find(a => a.email === user.email)` makes any person on the original booking authorized to add guests. There is no restriction on which guests (e.g., it could be anyone on the internet, including the organizer's competitors, third parties unrelated to the event, or used for spam/phishing). This is a privilege escalation: invitees are not the booking owner. If attendees adding guests is intentional, it should at least be limited (e.g., max count, requires confirmation, recorded in audit log, etc.); otherwise the authorization model should be reduced to organizer/team-admin/owner only.

title: Misleading TRPCError message for empty uniqueGuests
body: When `uniqueGuests.length === 0`, the handler throws `BAD_REQUEST` with message `emails_must_be_unique_valid`. The real cause is that all submitted addresses were either duplicates of existing attendees or blacklisted (or the list was empty). The message implies a format/duplicate validation problem to the caller and to the toast in the dialog, which is misleading. Use a message that reflects the actual condition (e.g., `no_new_guests_to_add`) and return a more accurate HTTP/UI message.

title: No booking state check (cancelled, past, recurring) before mutating
body: The handler never inspects `booking.status` or `booking.endTime`. This allows adding guests to CANCELLED, REJECTED, or already-finished bookings (and to recurring-event members without scoping). The action should be restricted to upcoming, non-cancelled bookings; if recurring, the implementation should either disallow or apply to the full series intentionally. Otherwise users can add guests to events that already occurred.

title: Subject uses attendees[0].name, crashes if attendees is empty and ignores others
body: `name: this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` will throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined` if `attendees` is empty (and the catch in the handler swallows the email error so the failure is silent). Additionally, only the first attendee's name is used even when many are present; the booking confirmation pattern elsewhere usually renders a multi-attendee list. Defensively handle an empty array and consider using a list of attendee names or the organizer/team context.

title: Newly added attendees may receive AttendeeAddGuestsEmail instead of confirmation
body: `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` is case-sensitive, but `attendee.email` (from DB, typically lowercased) and the submitted `newGuests` strings can differ in case. A newly added guest whose email case does not exactly match will be sent the "guests added" notification instead of the full booking confirmation email — which is the opposite of what they need. The whole check, plus the client/server dedup, must be case-insensitive (lowercase before compare) so the correct email goes to each.

title: Validation schema rebuilt each render; dedup is case-sensitive; error never clears on edit
body: `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` is constructed inside the component on every render (also: the inner `refine` deduplicates with a case-sensitive `Set`). Beyond perf, the dedup allows case-variant duplicates through. More importantly, when validation fails, `isInvalidEmail` is set to true and only reset on Cancel; subsequent keystrokes that fix the input don't clear the red error banner, so the user sees a stale failure even after correcting the email. Clear the error in `setValue`/`MultiEmail` change handler and lowercase before comparing.

title: Submits empty-string entries if user clicks Add without filling the seeded input
body: Initial state is `[""]` and the validation runs on the full array (including empty entries). The zod `.email()` rejects empty strings, so the user gets a generic "emails must be unique and valid" error and can't tell that the cause is the blank seeded input. Strip empty strings before validation, or include a clear inline message that distinguishes empty/invalid/duplicate.

title: "add_members" action is shown unconditionally for every editable booking
body: The new action is added to `editBookingActions` for all bookings shown through the Edit menu, regardless of booking status, start time, or whether the viewer is organizer/admin/owner. While the server enforces permissions, the UI still surfaces a "Add guests" action that, for past or cancelled bookings, will fail (since the new handler doesn't guard against these states). Also, the action id `add_members` is misleading — it adds guests, not members.

title: Component mutates its `value` prop directly
body: `value = value || [];` reassigns the incoming prop. In React this silently breaks the source state contract (e.g., parent state can diverge from what the component is rendering, effects/memos based on `value` may not fire correctly, and linters/Hooks rules flag it). Use a local alias (`const safeValue = value ?? [];`) and never reassign props.

title: Hardcoded `required` on every email input
body: Every rendered `EmailField` passes `required` unconditionally. This makes form-level validation impossible (HTML form submission will always be blocked) and is also misleading for the "add another" UX where users can intentionally leave the new field blank while editing another. Drop the hardcoded `required`, or scope it to form contexts.

title: No max length on guests list, enables unbounded inserts/emails
body: `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` allows `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(...)`. A caller can submit arbitrarily large arrays, triggering many DB inserts, many calendar API calls inside `updateCalendarAttendees`, and many emails. Add a reasonable max (e.g., 20-50) in the schema and a per-user rate limit on the mutation.

title: Email sending errors silently swallowed, user told "Guests added"
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails` is wrapped in try/catch with only `console.log`. On failure the dialog still shows the success toast and the mutation returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`, so the organizer believes every attendee was notified when in fact some may not have been. Either surface the error or only show success after both DB and email pipelines succeed.

title: No tests for the new addGuests handler/schema/dialog
body: The PR adds a new TRPC mutation (`addGuests`) with non-trivial authorization logic (team admin/owner, organizer, attendee), email blacklist filtering, case-sensitivity, calendar sync, and two new email templates, plus a new dialog component — and ships no tests. Given the auth/duplicate/blacklist bugs visible above, this is a substantial test gap. Add unit tests for the handler (authorization matrix, blacklist, duplicates, case-insensitivity, cancelled/past bookings) and integration/component tests for `AddGuestsDialog` validation paths.

title: Team admin/owner permission check uses && instead of ||
body: The `isTeamAdminOrOwner` flag is built with a logical AND of `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner`, but the variable name and intent (`AdminOrOwner`) clearly indicates OR. As written, a team admin who is not also an owner fails the check (the only users who pass are owners, since being an owner typically implies being an admin). Any non-owner team admin (e.g. a delegated team manager) is silently denied permission even though the UI label and code path assume they can add guests.

title: Blacklist comparison is case-sensitive while blacklist is lowercased
body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased via `.toLowerCase()` on line 71, but the subsequent filter compares raw user input: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. A guest like `Bad@Example.com` is not matched against a blacklist entry `bad@example.com`, so any address whose case differs from the configured blacklist bypasses it entirely. Normalize the guest email (and ideally emails throughout the handler) to lowercase before comparing.

title: No transaction / no error handling around calendar sync after DB update
body: `prisma.booking.update` writes the new attendees to the database first. `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` is then awaited with no try/catch. If the calendar integration throws (rate limit, expired token, network, etc.), the function rejects with a 500, but the database already has the new attendees persisted. Result: the Cal.com booking now lists guests that are NOT on the linked Google/Outlook calendar, and the user has no way to roll back. The whole flow should be wrapped in a transaction or, at minimum, the calendar sync should happen first so a failure leaves the system consistent.

title: Any attendee can add arbitrary guests without organizer consent
body: Permission grants the addGuests capability not only to organizers and team admins/owners but also to any attendee (`isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find(a => a.email === user.email)`). Combined with the lack of rate limiting, any invitee can enumerate or spam-add external email addresses to someone else's meeting. There is no confirmation from the organizer, and the organizer is only informed after the fact via `OrganizerAddGuestsEmail`. Either remove the attendee branch or require organizer approval.

title: No check on booking status before mutating
body: The handler never inspects `booking.status` or `booking.endTime`. It will happily persist new attendees onto CANCELLED, REJECTED, or already-finished bookings, and `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` will then either fail or silently modify a calendar event for a meeting that no longer exists. The handler should reject mutations on non-ACCEPTED or past bookings.

title: Email send uses raw input guests instead of filtered uniqueGuests
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is called with the original input list rather than `uniqueGuests` (which excludes already-attending emails and blacklisted addresses). In `email-manager.ts` the recipient loop checks `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` to decide between sending a fresh `AttendeeScheduledEmail` vs. an `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. As a result, an existing attendee whose email is also present in the input gets a full "you're scheduled" confirmation email (with ICS file) instead of a "guests added" notification, and any email in the input that wasn't actually added is still considered "new" for routing. Pass `uniqueGuests` to `sendAddGuestsEmails` instead.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores disableStandardEmails settings
body: Every other send* function in this file honors `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` and `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` (read from the event type metadata). `sendAddGuestsEmails` accepts no metadata and never checks these flags, so it always sends the organizer and attendee notifications regardless of how the event type is configured. Either thread the metadata through from the handler or look it up via the booking's eventType.

title: attendees[0].name accessed without null check in email subject
body: The subject template reads `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name`. If `attendees` is empty this throws a TypeError that aborts the email; if `attendees[0].name` is null/undefined the subject renders as "Guests Added: <eventType> with  at <date>". Add a guard or fall back to the organizer/team name.

title: isInvalidEmail flag is not cleared after a successful mutation
body: On validation failure `setIsInvalidEmail(true)` is called, but neither `onSuccess` nor `handleAdd` ever resets it back to false. A user who first submits invalid emails, then fixes them and successfully adds guests, will continue to see the red "Emails must be unique and valid" banner in the dialog (and after reopening the dialog for the same booking) until the Cancel button is clicked. Reset the flag at the start of `handleAdd` and inside `onSuccess`.

title: Initial state seeds an empty string, so the first Add always fails validation
body: `useState<string[]>([""])` initializes the input with one empty email. The zod schema `z.array(z.string().email())` rejects empty strings, so clicking "Add" with the default state always shows the error banner before the user has even had a chance to type. Initialize with an empty array (matching `MultiEmail`'s empty-state branch) and add the empty input only after the user clicks "Add Emails".

title: addGuests uses authedProcedure instead of bookingsProcedure
body: Sibling mutations that touch a booking (`editLocation`, `confirm`, etc.) use `bookingsProcedure`, which typically enforces booking-level permission middleware. `addGuests` is wired with the looser `authedProcedure`, so any authenticated user can hit the endpoint and the only authorization is the handler's own checks (which have the bugs noted above). Use `bookingsProcedure` for consistency and to inherit the centralized guards.

title: Email-send errors are swallowed with console.log
body: `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` discards the error object entirely (notice `console.log` rather than `console.error`, and `err` is not used). Use `logger.error(...)` from `@calcom/lib/logger` like the rest of the file, and include `err` so the failure is diagnosable in production.

title: Direct reassignment of a prop
body: `value = value || [];` mutates the `value` prop in place. While React does not re-render on prop mutation, this is misleading code and means subsequent reads use the mutated object reference. Use a default parameter (`value = []` in the signature) or a local `const emails = value ?? []`.

title: Using array index as React key in the email list
body: `value.map((field, index) => <li key={index} ...)` reuses keys when emails are added/removed, which causes React to reuse input components and can lose focus/caret position or render stale values for the newly inserted empty input. Use a stable id (e.g. include the email value or a counter ref).

title: Team admin permission requires user to be both admin AND owner
body: The permission check `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))` requires the caller to be BOTH a team admin and a team owner. Since `isTeamAdmin` typically already returns true for owners, the AND collapses the check to "owner only" — team admins lose the ability to add guests. The operator should be `||` (or the `isTeamAdmin` call should be dropped, as it already covers owners). With the current code, only team owners can use the new feature even though the UI claims any admin/owner can.

title: Team bookings crash with Prisma RecordNotFound
body: For team/round-robin bookings, `booking.userId` is often null. The handler does `where: { id: booking.userId || 0 }` when looking up the organizer, so it issues `findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: 0 } })`, which throws an unwrapped `Prisma.RecordNotFound` error and returns a 500 to the client instead of a meaningful error. The lookup needs to handle `booking.userId == null` explicitly (e.g. resolve the organizer from `eventType.team` or return a clean `NOT_FOUND`/`BAD_REQUEST`).

title: Deduplication is case-sensitive, allowing near-duplicate attendees
body: Both the existing-attendee check (`guest === attendee.email`) and the email format assumed by the rest of the app treat emails as case-sensitive, but emails are case-insensitive by RFC. A caller can submit `Alice@Example.com` while an existing attendee is `alice@example.com` and the new one will be added as a separate row, creating duplicate attendees in `Booking.attendees` and duplicate calendar invites. All comparisons should lowercase both sides before comparing, and the schema should normalize input.

title: Blacklist check is case-sensitive
body: `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` is lowercased on parse, but the input `guest` is not lowercased before `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. Submitting `BLOCKED@example.com` against a blacklist entry `blocked@example.com` will bypass the block. The guest value must be lowercased before being checked against the blacklist.

title: Server-side schema does not enforce uniqueness, allowing duplicate rows
body: `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only validates email format; uniqueness is only enforced in the client `AddGuestsDialog`. A malicious or buggy client can POST `["a@x.com", "a@x.com"]` and the handler will create two `Attendee` rows for the same address. The server schema should `.refine` for uniqueness (ideally after lowercasing) and the handler's `uniqueGuests` filter should also be the source of truth for the DB write — currently `prisma.booking.update(... createMany: data: guestsFullDetails)` uses `uniqueGuests`, but the email pass later (`sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`) uses the raw `guests` input, which can still mis-trigger the duplicate `AttendeeScheduledEmail` branch in `email-manager.ts`.

title: No transactional boundary between DB write and calendar/email side effects
body: `prisma.booking.update` runs first, then `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, then `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`. None of this is in a transaction. If the calendar call or email send throws, the DB is left with attendees added but the connected calendar/videocall still missing them, and the user sees a 500 even though the mutation was half-applied. The whole flow should be wrapped (DB update + calendar update + email send) so a failure leaves no partial state, or the email/calendar steps should run before the DB write with a compensating delete on failure.

title: Email send failure is silently swallowed
body: The `sendAddGuestsEmails` call is wrapped in `try { ... } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`. The DB has already been mutated and the calendar has already been updated, so the API returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` and the UI shows the success toast even when no emails went out. Either surface the error (so the UI can retry/notify) or skip the DB write until emails have been queued.

title: Cancelled/rejected/past bookings can have guests added
body: After loading the booking, the handler never checks `booking.status`. A caller can add guests to a CANCELLED, REJECTED, or already-past booking, which will create new attendees, push them to the connected calendar, and send "guests added" emails about an event that is no longer happening. The handler must reject when the booking is not in an `ACCEPTED` (or `PENDING`) state, and ideally also when `booking.endTime < now()`.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails sends AttendeeScheduledEmail to new guests using raw input emails
body: The handler passes the raw `guests` input (which may contain case variants or duplicates) as `newGuests`, and `sendAddGuestsEmails` does `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` to decide between `AttendeeScheduledEmail` and `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. Because the match is case-sensitive and the input was not deduplicated/normalized, the wrong email template is sent in the obvious cases (e.g. `Alice@x.com` vs `alice@x.com`) and a duplicate email is sent if the same address was submitted twice with different casing. The list of "new" guests should be built from the normalized `uniqueGuests` and lowercased before comparison.

title: Dialog sends empty email rows through validation and fails with a misleading message
body: `MultiEmail` initializes `value` with `[""]` and the "Add Another" button pushes another `""`. The dialog validates the raw `multiEmailValue` array, so leaving any field blank (e.g. `["a@x.com", "", "b@x.com"]`) or submitting immediately on open fails `z.array(z.string().email())` and shows "Emails must be unique and valid", which does not describe the actual problem (blank fields). The handler should `.transform`/filter out empty strings (and lowercase + trim) before parsing, and surface a more specific message — otherwise users will repeatedly hit this confusing error.

title: Error toast displays raw TRPC code instead of a useful translation key
body: On error the toast uses `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`. For zod-input failures `err.message` is a generic zod string (e.g. the literal string `"BAD_REQUEST"` is not a translation key), so users see `BAD_REQUEST: BAD_REQUEST` or a missing-translation key. The handler should throw `TRPCError`s with translation-key messages (like the existing `emails_must_be_unique_valid`/`you_do_not_have_permission`), and the client should prefer `t(err.message)` only when the key exists, falling back to `unable_to_add_guests` otherwise.

title: userPrimaryEmail is always undefined, silently falling back to organizer.email
body: The Prisma `booking` query does not select `userPrimaryEmail`, so `booking?.userPrimaryEmail ?? organizer.email` always resolves to `organizer.email`. This is unlikely to be a security issue (the booking's organizer email is also pulled from the same user record), but the misleading fallback hides the intent. If the original design is to honor the organizer's primary email for calendar invites, the field needs to be added to the `select`/`include`; otherwise the dead branch should be removed.

title: No upper bound on guests array length
body: The schema accepts an unbounded array of emails and the handler will happily create that many attendees, update the calendar, and fan out N emails. A malicious caller can submit thousands of addresses to cause resource exhaustion and email bombing. Add `z.array(...).min(1).max(N)` (with N chosen to match the event type's `seatsPerTimeSlot` / max attendees setting) and consider reusing `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` plus rate limiting.

title: {...props} spread after named props allows caller to silently override intended fields
body: `{...props}` is spread after `title`, `headerType`, `subject`, and `callToAction`, so if any caller (including `organizer-add-guests-email.ts` if extended) ever passes one of those keys, the intended value is silently overridden. Move `{...props}` before the named props, or destructure them out of `props` before spreading. The same pattern exists in `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail.tsx`.

title: AddGuestsDialog is always mounted for every booking row
body: The `<AddGuestsDialog>` is rendered unconditionally for every `BookingListItem` (and the BookingListItem table can render hundreds of rows). The dialog content is always in the DOM, registering tRPC mutation hooks for every row. The dialog should only be mounted when `isOpenAddGuestsDialog` is true (the same pattern other dialogs in this file already use), to avoid hundreds of stale mutation handles and extra DOM nodes on the bookings list page.

title: retryCount never incremented when message or sendTo is empty, so the new retry/delete mechanism is bypassed
body: The new retry/delete behavior only fires inside the branches that actually attempt scheduling. When `message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo` is falsy (e.g. SMS template evaluates to an empty string, attendee has no phone number, etc.) the entire `if` block is skipped, no `twilio.scheduleSMS` call is made, and neither the `else` (line 179) nor the `catch` (line 190) path runs. The reminder therefore never has its `retryCount` incremented and will be picked up again on every cron run until its `scheduledDate` passes, exactly the bug this PR claims to fix. The PR description's stated goal is to delete reminders that fail to schedule after two attempts, so empty message / missing recipient must also drive `retryCount` (e.g. increment in an `else` for the outer guard) or be deleted immediately.

title: Cleanup deleteMany applies retryCount > 1 to non-SMS reminders too
body: The new cleanup `deleteMany` uses an `OR` whose second branch is `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` with no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, unlike the first branch. The first branch is correctly scoped to SMS, but the second branch will delete any `WorkflowReminder` row (including EMAIL and WHATSAPP) whose `retryCount` exceeds 1, regardless of scheduledDate. Today only this SMS path increments `retryCount`, but any future change that bumps the counter for email/whatsapp (or a stray backfill) will silently delete those reminders too. The retryCount clause should be `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, retryCount: { gt: 1 }` to keep semantics consistent with the rest of the handler.

title: retryCount increment is read-modify-write and not atomic
body: The update uses `data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 }`, where `reminder.retryCount` was read earlier in `findMany`. If two cron invocations (or any concurrent process) process the same reminder, both will read the same value and both will write `value + 1`, silently losing one retry attempt and possibly keeping a failing reminder alive beyond the intended two attempts. Use Prisma's atomic `increment` operation (e.g. `update({ where: { id }, data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } } })`) in both the `else` branch (line 179-186) and the `catch` branch (line 190-197).

title: SMS scheduling errors are logged with console.log instead of console.error
body: The catch block at line 198 uses `console.log(`Error scheduling SMS with error ${error}`)`. Failure logs should use `console.error` so they are routed to error streams/aggregators and don't get buried in routine info output; otherwise on-call engineers triaging SMS delivery issues have to grep for the string "Error scheduling" in info-level logs.

title: No tests added for the new retryCount / cleanup behavior
body: The PR introduces a new `retryCount` column, a new cleanup branch in `deleteMany` (`retryCount > 1`), and new increment paths in both the `else` and `catch` branches. None of these are covered by automated tests. Given there are several failure paths (twilio returns falsy, twilio throws, message empty, sendTo missing) and a non-trivial boundary (`gt: 1` rather than `gte: 1`), this is a regression risk. Tests should at minimum cover: SMS scheduled successfully -> `scheduled: true` set; twilio returns falsy -> `retryCount` becomes 1, reminder still present; twilio throws -> `retryCount` becomes 1; reminder with `retryCount >= 2` is deleted by the cleanup `deleteMany`; the empty message / missing sendTo case actually increments `retryCount` (or is fixed to do so per the other finding).

title: retryCount-based deletion is method-agnostic
body: The new `deleteMany` clause `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` is placed in the top-level `OR` without any `method` filter, so it will delete EMAIL and WHATSAPP `WorkflowReminder` rows in addition to SMS ones. The rest of the handler only processes SMS (the `findMany` is restricted to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`), and only the SMS path increments `retryCount`, so today this is latent — but the schema field is shared and the next contributor who increments `retryCount` for, say, WhatsApp will silently start dropping those rows here. The retry-clause should be scoped to SMS (e.g. `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, retryCount: { gt: 1 }`) so the deletion rule matches the rule that produces the counter.

title: Retry-based deletion ignores `scheduled` and may drop already-scheduled reminders
body: The `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` branch in the top-level `OR` of the `deleteMany` runs without checking `scheduled` or `referenceId`. Today only the failure path increments `retryCount`, so this is latent — but if any future change ever bumps `retryCount` after a successful schedule (for example as part of a send-status callback, or by an SMS_RECEIVED/RECEIPT webhook reconciliation that double-writes), reminders that were already handed off to Twilio will be deleted here while the provider still has a live scheduled message, producing a phantom-delivery bug with no audit row. The retry-deletion should also require `scheduled: false` (or only apply to rows with no `referenceId`) so it cannot tear out rows whose SMS is already in flight.

title: retryCount update uses stale in-memory value (lost-update race)
body: Both the `else` branch (line 179) and the `catch` block (line 190) write `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`, where `reminder.retryCount` is the value returned by the `findMany` at the top of the handler. If two cron invocations overlap, or the same reminder is picked up twice within one run, both workers read the same starting value and both write `start + 1`, so the counter only advances by one instead of two. That means under overlap a reminder can take 3–4 actual attempts to reach `retryCount > 1` and be deleted, breaking the "after two failures" guarantee stated in the PR description. The update should be a relative increment (e.g. `{ retryCount: { increment: 1 } }`) so concurrent workers compose correctly.

title: No tests cover the new retry/delete behavior
body: The PR adds a new column, changes the deletion predicate, and introduces two new update sites, but ships no tests for the new behavior. Specifically there is no test covering: (a) `retryCount` increments on `twilio.scheduleSMS` returning a falsy value, (b) `retryCount` increments in the catch block, (c) reminders with `retryCount > 1` are deleted by the next run, (d) reminders with `retryCount <= 1` are not deleted. Without these, a future refactor of the OR/deleteMany/findMany queries could regress the cap without being caught.

title: Error log drops reminder context
body: The catch block only logs `Error scheduling SMS with error ${error}`. It does not include the `reminder.id`, `bookingUid`, `workflowStepId`, or the `sendTo`/recipient, so when the new retry path deletes a reminder after two failures there is no trail in logs tying the deletion back to a specific booking or recipient. For a feature whose entire purpose is to stop silently retrying bad recipients, the error log should at minimum include the reminder id and recipient so on-call can correlate the eventual deletion with the original failure.

title: Catch block increments retryCount for non-SMS errors
body: The catch block added in this PR wraps the entire try block, so it catches errors from `prisma.profile.findFirst` (line 111), `getBookerBaseUrl` (line 119), and `customTemplate` (line 138) — none of which are SMS scheduling attempts. If any of these fail (e.g., a transient DB connection issue when looking up the organizer profile), `retryCount` is incremented even though `twilio.scheduleSMS` was never called. After two such unrelated failures, the reminder will be permanently deleted by the `deleteMany` at line 29, losing a perfectly valid SMS reminder that should have been scheduled. The retry-counting logic should only fire when the actual SMS scheduling attempt fails.

title: deleteMany cleanup is not scoped to SMS method
body: The new `OR` branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` added to the `deleteMany` has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, unlike the original condition it was combined with. The cron job at `scheduleSMSReminders.ts` is specifically the SMS-scheduling cron, but it now deletes any `WorkflowReminder` row (EMAIL, WHATSAPP, etc.) whose `retryCount` exceeds 1. Today only this file increments `retryCount`, so nothing breaks yet, but this couples the SMS cron to a global invariant and will silently delete non-SMS reminders the moment any other code path starts writing to `retryCount`. The `OR` branch should be scoped to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (or the responsibility split should be revisited).

title: Retry-count logic has no test coverage
body: The PR introduces non-trivial new behavior: incrementing `retryCount` on scheduling failure (both the `else` branch at line 179 and the `catch` branch at line 190), and using `retryCount > 1` to delete reminders. This is the only mechanism that prevents the SMS scheduler from infinitely retrying bad numbers, so it is reliability-critical. There are no tests added or modified for `scheduleSMSReminders.ts`. The behavior should be covered by tests: e.g., a failing `twilio.scheduleSMS` increments `retryCount`, a second failure leads to deletion on the next run, and a successful scheduling does not touch `retryCount`.

title: retryCount update is a non-atomic read-modify-write
body: Both new `prisma.workflowReminder.update` calls (line 184 in the `else` branch and line 195 in the `catch`) compute `reminder.retryCount + 1` from the value that was loaded at the start of the loop iteration. If two instances of this cron run concurrently (e.g., a manual trigger overlapping a scheduled run, or two pods picking up the same scheduled task), both can read the same `retryCount` value and both write `value + 1`, causing one increment to be lost. The reminder would then survive one extra cron run before being deleted. This is a minor concurrency hazard under the current deployment model but should use an atomic increment (e.g., `prisma.workflowReminder.update({ data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } } })`) to be safe.

title: findMany method removed without migration path
body: The previously-public `findMany(findManyArgs: Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedFindManyArgs)` method has been deleted and replaced with `getBaseConditions()`. Any existing caller (other modules, route handlers, etc.) that previously invoked `service.findMany({ select, where, orderBy, take, ... })` will now fail to compile, and the README/PR description does not document this as a breaking change nor provide a migration shim. A search for other consumers should be done before merging and any callers must be updated to use `prisma.$queryRaw` with the returned conditions.

title: Loss of where-clause merging capability
body: The previous `findMany` merged a caller's `findManyArgs.where` into the final Prisma where (via `...findManyArgs.where, AND: [auth, filter]`). The new `getBaseConditions()` only returns the authorization + filter SQL fragment and provides no way for a caller to layer additional predicates. Any caller that relied on passing extra `where` (date ranges, status filters, paging cursor, etc.) will silently lose those filters. The integration test now hard-codes a `SELECT id FROM "BookingTimeStatusDenormalized"` query and the call sites have no documented API to add their own conditions.

title: Caching behaviour no longer covered by tests
body: The previous test file contained a `describe("Caching", ...)` block with two tests that verified `getAuthorizationConditions` / `getFilterConditions` returned identical objects on repeated calls (proving the internal cache works). The new diff silently removes that entire describe block while the cache (`this.cachedAuthConditions`, `this.cachedFilterConditions`) is still implemented in the service. There is no replacement test, so regressions to the cache (e.g. accidental double work, or cache not invalidating after construction) would not be caught. The PR description does not mention removing this coverage.

title: Integration test depends on BookingTimeStatusDenormalized being synchronously populated
body: The integration test inserts rows via `prisma.booking.create` / `prisma.eventType.create` and immediately runs `SELECT id FROM "BookingTimeStatusDenormalized" WHERE ${baseConditions}`, expecting the just-inserted booking to appear. This relies on `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized` being kept in sync with `Booking` synchronously (via trigger or denormalization job at insert time). If it is a materialized view or is only refreshed by a background job, this test will be flaky in CI. The PR description even acknowledges that the test runner had configuration issues and asks for manual verification. There is no setup/teardown that guarantees the denormalized table reflects the freshly created booking, and no assertion that the table is non-empty before running the test.

title: Prisma.Sql equality assertions are fragile and not validated
body: Every assertion in the rewritten test compares the service output with a literal `Prisma.sql\`...\`` template using `expect(...).toEqual(...)`. `Prisma.Sql` is an object whose internal `strings` / `values` arrays are sensitive to whitespace, parenthesis placement, and the order of interpolation. Several assertions in the diff (e.g. line 273, 296-298, 333-343) embed `${[array]}` exactly matching the implementation's array order; if the implementation ever produces a different equivalent SQL (e.g. `("teamId" = ANY($1))` vs `("teamId" = $1)` for a single element, or different spacing) the tests will fail even though the SQL is semantically identical. There is no helper that compares the rendered SQL structurally, and the PR description explicitly flags that the tests were not actually run (`test runner configuration issues`) so the equality assumptions are unverified.

title: Constructor type widened without enforcing teamId for team scope
body: The constructor parameter type changed from `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` (discriminated union that requires `teamId` when `scope === "team"`) to `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` where `teamId` is optional. `safeParse` then sets `this.options = null` on any validation failure, which silently downgrades the user to `NOTHING_CONDITION` (no results) instead of throwing. A caller that passes `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` without `teamId` will get a service that returns nothing with no error. This is a behaviour change: previously TypeScript would reject the call at compile time; now it silently produces empty results, which is a security/visibility concern since it may mask authorization bugs.

title: PR description mislabels the scope of the change
