body: The PR title and description say this only "updates the integration tests for the Prisma.sql format that was previously converted in the service implementation", but the diff also substantially rewrites the service itself: deletes `findMany`, changes return types from `Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedWhereInput` to `Prisma.Sql`, widens the constructor options type, removes the `NOTHING = { id: -1 }` sentinel, and adds `getBaseConditions()`. Reviewers reading the description would not expect these breaking service-level changes. The description should be updated to call out the API break and the removal of cache tests.

title: Org-scope authorization silently skips direct org members when there are no child teams
body: In `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition`, the user membership lookup is gated on `teamsFromOrg.length > 0`, even though `teamIds` always contains the org's own ID (`[options.orgId, ...teamsFromOrg.map(t => t.id)]`). When an organization has zero child teams but has direct members (a realistic configuration, e.g., a small org that hasn't created sub-teams), `userIdsFromOrg` is forced to an empty array. As a result, personal (non-team) bookings made by those direct org members will not match the authorization SQL: the first branch only matches `isTeamBooking = true`, and the second branch is excluded entirely. Those users effectively disappear from org-scope insights. The user lookup should be performed whenever `teamIds` is non-empty, not based on `teamsFromOrg.length > 0`. The PR is the right moment to fix this since the file is being rewritten anyway; preserving the bug in raw SQL form just locks it in.

title: `findMany` removed without documenting the migration for external callers
body: The class previously exposed `async findMany(findManyArgs)`, which built a Prisma `bookingTimeStatusDenormalized.findMany` query using the constructed auth/filter conditions. That method is gone and has been replaced with `getBaseConditions(): Promise<Prisma.Sql>`, forcing every caller to switch to `prisma.$queryRaw` and to hand-write the SELECT clause themselves. This is a breaking change for any in-repo caller that imports `InsightsBookingService` (the file is in `packages/lib/server/service`, which is a shared library package). The PR description only discusses the test changes and does not call out this API break or describe the migration. A grep for `InsightsBookingService` consumers should be done and they should be updated in the same change, or at minimum the PR description should list them.

title: Caching tests removed with no replacement
body: The diff deletes the entire `describe("Caching", ...)` block (two tests: "should cache authorization conditions" and "should cache filter conditions") without adding equivalent coverage. The implementation still caches via `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions` (lines 84 and 91 in `insightsBooking.ts`), so a future refactor that accidentally re-builds conditions on every call (e.g., removing the `=== undefined` guard) would not be caught. At minimum one test should be added that asserts a second call returns the exact same `Prisma.Sql` instance / deep-equal structure as the first.

title: Tests have not been executed for a HIGH RISK SQL/authorization PR
body: The PR description itself states that the author "encountered test runner configuration issues" and explicitly asks reviewers to manually run `TZ=UTC yarn test packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts`. For a change that the author flags as HIGH RISK and that touches authorization conditions built with `Prisma.sql` template literals, this is not acceptable. Several non-obvious things need to actually execute and return correct rows: (a) JS arrays interpolated into `Prisma.sql` are correctly serialized for PostgreSQL `ANY()` (see line 296 for the single-element case and lines 333-342 for the multi-element case — if Prisma emits them as `'{}'` or as a comma list rather than a proper array, the query fails); (b) the `(isTeamBooking = true)` / `(isTeamBooking = false)` predicates produce correct row matching against the `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized` table; (c) the cached conditions actually short-circuit; (d) the org-scope test's expected array order matches the order returned by `findAllByParentId`. None of this has been verified by the author. The merge should be blocked until CI proves these tests pass against a populated database.

title: findMany method removed (public API break)
body: The previous public method `findMany(findManyArgs)` has been replaced with `getBaseConditions()` returning a raw `Prisma.Sql` fragment. Any external/internal caller that previously invoked `service.findMany({...})` will no longer compile or will silently break at runtime. This is a breaking change but is not mentioned in the PR description, and the migration path (callers must now build their own `$queryRaw` queries and embed `baseConditions` themselves) is not documented. Please confirm no other callers exist in the repo or provide a shim.

title: Caching behaviour tests removed alongside implementation
body: The 'Caching' describe block (previously covering `getAuthorizationConditions` / `getFilterConditions` caching) was deleted in this PR. The service still has `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions` fields and still uses the same cache-on-first-call pattern, but there is now zero test coverage for it. A future refactor that breaks caching (e.g. invalidating on filter mutation, key collisions across scopes, or accidental mutation of the cached SQL) will not be caught.

title: getBaseConditions integration test only covers 'user' scope
body: The new `$queryRaw`-based integration test in the 'getBaseConditions' describe block only exercises the `scope: 'user'` path against the real database. The `scope: 'team'` and `scope: 'org'` branches (which are the most complex, with nested AND/OR and `ANY()` arrays) are only compared by stringified SQL and never actually executed against `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized`. Authorization regressions in those branches (e.g. wrong parenthesization, missing `teamId`/`isTeamBooking` clauses, leak across org boundaries) will not be caught by this suite.

title: Dead branches in getBaseConditions
body: `getAuthorizationConditions` is typed `Promise<Prisma.Sql>` and is never null (it always returns either `NOTHING_CONDITION` or a real SQL fragment), so the `else if (authConditions)` branch in `getBaseConditions` is unreachable — `Prisma.Sql` is an object and therefore always truthy. The fallback `else { return NOTHING_CONDITION; }` branch is similarly unreachable. This is harmless dead code but it misleads readers about what can be returned and what combinations are possible.

title: Org scope user list excludes users only on the org membership
body: `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` derives `userIdsFromOrg` from `MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds({ teamIds })` where `teamIds` is `[orgId, ...childTeamIds]`. In practice this only returns users who have a membership in the org *or* one of its child teams — but anyone whose membership row points directly at the org but who has no child-team membership is still included, and conversely users who only sit on sub-teams are included. The more subtle problem is the inverse: a user who is *only* an org member via a direct org membership row with no team-level membership is included only because `orgId` is in `teamIds`. If the data ever drifts so the org itself is excluded from `teamIds` (or if the query is later changed to fetch only sub-team memberships to optimize), those users' non-team bookings will silently disappear from org-scope insights. The pre-existing object-based version had the same shape, so this is not a regression, but the SQL rewrite is a good opportunity to make the intent explicit (and to add an integration test for an org member without any sub-team membership).

title: Team scope does not deduplicate userIdsFromTeam
body: `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` deduplicates `userIdsFromOrg` via `Array.from(new Set(userIdsFromOrg))` before binding into `ANY(${uniqueUserIds})`. `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` does the equivalent operation but skips the deduplication step (`const userIdsFromTeam = usersFromTeam.map((u) => u.userId);` is used directly). For a team with many members who happen to share membership rows the resulting `ANY(...)` array can balloon, growing the bound parameter size and the SQL plan unnecessarily. Make the two paths consistent.

title: No afterEach cleanup; failing tests leak database rows
body: Cleanup is implemented as a returned `cleanup()` function that each test must remember to call at the end of its body. If a test fails or throws before reaching the `await testData.cleanup()` line (and there is at least one such path — e.g. the new `$queryRaw` assertion in the `getBaseConditions` describe block, which calls cleanup only after the expect), the user/team/membership/booking/eventType rows it created persist in the shared database, polluting subsequent runs. Wrap `createTestData` in a `try/finally` or use `afterEach(() => testData?.cleanup())` to guarantee cleanup.

title: Integration test does not assert query column shape or count edge cases
body: The only end-to-end `$queryRaw` assertion in the suite (`expect(results).toEqual([{ id: userBooking.id }])`) verifies that *exactly one* row is returned for a user-scoped, single-eventType filter. It does not assert that (a) a booking owned by the same user on a *different* eventType is excluded, (b) a *team* booking for this user is excluded by the `teamId IS NULL` clause, or (c) that the booking row is actually selected from `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized` (not just any table that happens to have an `id` column). Adding these assertions is the only way the user-scope SQL is meaningfully exercised.

title: isOrgOwnerOrAdmin replaced .includes with two == comparisons without behavioral justification
body: `isOrgOwnerOrAdmin` was changed from `([MembershipRole.OWNER, MembershipRole.ADMIN] as const).includes(membership.role)` to `(membership.role === MembershipRole.OWNER || membership.role === MembershipRole.ADMIN)`. The two are functionally identical for the enum values in use today, but the new form silently breaks if `MembershipRole` is ever extended with another privileged role — `includes` makes it trivial to add a role to the array, whereas the `||` chain has to be edited in two places. Either keep `.includes` or add a comment explaining the choice.

title: updateManyByCredentialId called with empty data
body: The new call `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` passes an empty `data` object. Prisma's `updateMany` either rejects empty data with a validation error (which would break the unwatchCalendar flow that invokes this) or silently performs no update. In neither case does it update `updatedAt` as the preceding comment claims, so `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is never set by this code path. The intended behavior must be achieved by passing an explicit field, e.g. `{ updatedAt: new Date() }`.

title: Comment misrepresents code behavior
body: The comment `// Update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt for all calendars under this credential` directly precedes a `updateManyByCredentialId` call with empty `data`. The call does not update `updatedAt`, so the comment is inaccurate and misleading to anyone reading the code.

title: macOS-only sed syntax breaks script on Linux
body: Line 68 uses `sed -i '' -E "..."` which is BSD/macOS sed syntax. On Linux, `sed -i` requires either no argument or a suffix as an extension (e.g. `sed -i.bak -E`). As written, the script will fail with a usage error on any non-macOS developer machine or CI runner, silently leaving `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` stale and breaking local webhook testing.

title: Cache timestamp hardcoded to en-US locale
body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` is used to format `cacheUpdatedAt`, ignoring the user's locale even though `useLocale()` is already invoked in the same component. Non-English-speaking users will see US-formatted dates (e.g. `12/31/2025, 4:30 PM`) instead of their own regional convention. The date-time key in common.json (`cache_last_updated`) is also a non-interpolated template, so the format cannot be easily localized downstream.

title: Cache status query ignores expiresAt
body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` calls `prisma.calendarCache.groupBy({ where: { credentialId: { in: credentialIds } } })` without filtering by `expiresAt`, unlike `getCachedAvailability` which only returns non-expired rows. A credential with only stale (expired) cache entries will still show a `cacheUpdatedAt` in the UI, causing users to see a 'Last updated' timestamp for cache that is no longer being served — and they may delete it under the mistaken assumption it is currently in use.

title: No tests for new deleteCache tRPC handler
body: The new `deleteCache` mutation is a destructive operation against `CalendarCache` keyed by a user-owned credential, yet no unit or integration tests are added covering ownership validation (e.g. missing credential, credential owned by another user) or successful cache deletion. This is the kind of authorization-sensitive path that warrants explicit test coverage before merging.

title: No tests for new getCacheStatusByCredentialIds repository method
body: The newly added `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` method is the data foundation for the new UI cache-status feature, but no tests were added (including the mock implementation in `calendar-cache.repository.mock.ts`). A test verifying that the method correctly groups by credentialId and returns null for credentials with no cache rows is missing.

title: No tests for new CredentialActionsDropdown component
body: The newly introduced `CredentialActionsDropdown` component (which replaces `DisconnectIntegration` and is rendered in the installed-calendars list) has no unit or e2e tests. The conditional render guard (no dropdown if neither disconnect is permitted nor a Google Calendar cache exists), the cache-status display, the confirmation dialogs, and the tRPC mutation success/error paths all lack coverage.

title: deleteCacheMutation does not invalidate connectedCalendars query, leaving stale cacheUpdatedAt in UI
body: After a successful cache deletion, the user's dropdown still shows the old 'Last updated' timestamp because the `deleteCacheMutation` only calls `onSuccess?.()` and shows a toast, but unlike `disconnectMutation` (lines 53-65) it never invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. Since `connectedCalendarsHandler` maps `cacheUpdatedAt` from the DB on each query, the displayed status will remain stuck on the pre-deletion value until the user manually reloads. Either invalidate the query (mirroring `disconnectMutation`'s `onSettled`) or refetch the calendars query on success so the cache status reflects reality.

title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds ignores expiresAt, surfacing expired cache rows
body: `getCachedAvailability` (lines 121-129) explicitly filters on `expiresAt: { gte: new Date(Date.now()) }` so lookups refuse to serve stale entries, but the new `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` only groups by `credentialId` with no `expiresAt` filter. Result: once a row's `expiresAt` is in the past, `getCachedAvailability` returns null yet the UI still displays a 'Last updated' timestamp from that expired row, giving the user the misleading impression that their cache is fresh. Add the same `expiresAt: { gte: new Date(Date.now()) }` (or filter out expired entries in the `Map` mapping) so the UI status matches the lookup behavior.

title: updateManyByCredentialId called with empty data {} may be a no-op
body: `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` is invoked with an empty update payload under the comment 'Update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt for all calendars under this credential'. Depending on Prisma's behavior with `data: {}` (some Prisma versions reject it or skip generating the SET clause, in which case the auto-managed `@updatedAt` is not refreshed), this can silently do nothing. Either set the field explicitly (`updatedAt: new Date()`) or remove the call if updating `updatedAt` is intentionally handled elsewhere (the PR notes themselves flag this as a candidate for removal since the UI uses `CalendarCache.cacheUpdatedAt` instead).

title: Migration warnings comment contradicts the SQL default
body: The header comment generated by Prisma reads 'Added the required column `updatedAt` to the `CalendarCache` table without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty.' but the SQL right below uses `NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()`. The comments are misleading and will confuse anyone reviewing the migration history; update the warning so it matches the actual change ('with default `NOW()` for legacy rows').

title: BSD-only sed syntax makes script fail on Linux
body: `sed -i '' -E ...` is BSD sed (macOS) syntax where the empty argument after `-i` disables backup file creation. On GNU sed (Linux/Ubuntu/etc. CI runners and most dev containers) this is interpreted as a backup suffix and produces an error or an unexpected backup file. Either detect the platform and dispatch to `sed -i.bak` followed by `rm`, or use a portable idiom such as `sed -i.bak -E "..." "$ENV_FILE" && rm "$ENV_FILE.bak"`.

title: No tests for deleteCacheHandler, getCacheStatusByCredentialIds, or CredentialActionsDropdown
body: Three new pieces of behavior ship with the PR (deleteCache tRPC handler with ownership check, getCacheStatusByCredentialIds repository method, and the deleteCachedData flow in CredentialActionsDropdown), but no unit/integration tests are added. The PR review checklist itself called this out as a known limitation. At minimum, add a handler test that covers the cross-user denial path (requesting a credential belonging to another user) and the success path, plus a UI test for the dropdown rendering and invalidation behavior.

title: updateManyByCredentialId called with empty data; @updatedAt is not bumped
body: The new call `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` is preceded by the comment `// Update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt for all calendars under this credential`, but the `data` argument is an empty object. Prisma does not update any column (including `@updatedAt`) when `data` is empty, so this is effectively a no-op (or, depending on the Prisma version, throws) while pretending to refresh the timestamp. Either remove the call (the author notes the webhook handler already updates this field) or pass `{ updatedAt: new Date() }` so the intent matches the behavior.

title: deleteCache success path does not invalidate connectedCalendars; UI stays stale
body: The `deleteCacheMutation` only fires `onSuccess?.()` on success. The companion `disconnectMutation` immediately below (lines 53-65) explicitly invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` and `utils.viewer.apps.integrations` via `onSettled`. After the user clicks "Delete cached data", the `CalendarCache` rows are deleted server-side but `connectedCalendar.cacheUpdatedAt` in cache keeps showing the old value, so the dropdown keeps displaying the same `Last updated: ...` line and the destructive action appears to have done nothing. Add the same `async onSettled` invalidation block (or an `onSuccess`-side invalidate) to `deleteCacheMutation` so the UI reflects deletion.

title: Cache timestamp hard-coded to en-US locale
body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" }).format(new Date(cacheUpdatedAt))` ignores the user's locale and uses month/day/year, which is incorrect and confusing for users on non-en-US locales (e.g., users with `de`, `fr`, `ja`). Use the locale-aware helper exposed by `useLocale`/i18n (e.g., `formatInTimeZone` from `date-fns-tz` or `Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale)`) so the display matches the rest of the app.

title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds ignores expiresAt, returns expired caches
body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups all rows for the credential and returns the max `updatedAt` regardless of `expiresAt`. Cache rows live for `CACHING_TIME = ONE_MONTH_IN_MS`; once they all expire, this still returns the last write timestamp and the dropdown will keep displaying `Last updated: <30+ days ago>` even though no live cache exists. Filter the `groupBy` with `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` (or join/max only non-expired rows) so the UI only shows status for currently valid cache entries.

title: dev:cron switched to npx tsx without declaring tsx
body: The script changes from `ts-node cron-tester.ts` to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`. `tsx` is not declared in `dependencies` or `devDependencies`, while `ts-node` is still a devDependency (line 196) and is still used by `check-changed-files` and `translate-locales` (lines 24-25). Either add `"tsx": "..."` to devDependencies (preferred) so the version is pinned, or revert to `ts-node` for consistency. Relying on `npx` to fetch `tsx` on demand risks version drift, slower startup, and silent failures in offline/CI environments.

title: macOS-only sed -i '' syntax breaks on Linux
body: `sed -i '' -E "s|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=.*|GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=$TUNNEL_URL|" "$ENV_FILE"` uses BSD/macOS in-place edit syntax. On GNU sed (Linux) `-i` requires an extension argument, so this either errors or creates a literal backup file named `''`. Detect the platform (e.g., `[[ "$(uname)" == "Darwin" ]] && sed -i '' ... || sed -i ...`) or use a portable approach (perl in-place, or write to a temp file and rename) so the script works for non-macOS developers and CI runners.

title: Prisma warning contradicts the actual SQL (default IS supplied)
body: The auto-generated warning at the top says: "Added the required column `updatedAt` to the `CalendarCache` table without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty." But the migration itself uses `DEFAULT NOW()`, which is exactly the safe-handling approach that contradicts the warning. Either delete the stale warning block or rewrite it to reflect that a default was added (e.g., "Added required column `updatedAt` with a default of `NOW()` so existing rows are populated"). As shipped, the comment misrepresents the migration and would mislead a reviewer auditing why the migration is safe on a non-empty table.

title: Reschedule still uses immediate SendGrid cancellation
body: The newly added reschedule path calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)`, passing `immediateDelete=true`. The PR description and design (move cancellation to the CRON to avoid SendGrid's 100 pending cancellations limit) only makes sense with the deferred approach. Calling SendGrid synchronously here reintroduces the exact bug being fixed: a reschedule flurry can hit the 100-pending-cancellations cap, leaving previously scheduled email reminders un-cancelled. Should be `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` (no third arg) to mark `cancelled=true` and let the CRON do the SendGrid call, matching the approach used in `handleCancelBooking.ts` and elsewhere.

title: Use of private Prisma client type
body: `const workflowRemindersToDelete: Prisma.Prisma__WorkflowReminderClient<WorkflowReminder, never>[] = [];` references a private/internal Prisma generated type (`Prisma__WorkflowReminderClient`). Such types are not part of Prisma's public API and are subject to change between Prisma versions, which can silently break compilation. Use a public type such as `Prisma.PrismaPromise<WorkflowReminder>` or simply `Promise<WorkflowReminder>`.

title: Cancellation query missing method filter
body: The new cancellation query only filters by `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate`, with no `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL` filter. The same `workflowReminder` table also holds SMS reminders, and although the current SMS code hard-deletes rows, a future code path that sets `cancelled=true` on SMS rows (or a manual DB edit) would cause this CRON to attempt to POST `batch_id: null` to SendGrid's scheduled_sends endpoint and crash on null. Adding `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL` to the where clause makes the logic self-contained and consistent with the `deleteMany` block above it.

title: immediateDelete=true leaves orphan DB rows
body: When `immediateDelete` is true, the function calls SendGrid to cancel and `return`s without ever updating or deleting the `workflowReminder` row. The row therefore remains in the DB with `cancelled = null`, so the new CRON will not pick it up and there is no follow-up cleanup. The SMS path always hard-deletes its row regardless; the email path should at least mark `cancelled: true` (or delete) after the SendGrid call so the row is not orphaned, particularly since these callers (workflow delete, step delete, reschedule) may not cascade-delete the reminder row.

title: Async functions in forEach are not awaited
body: `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach((reminder) => { deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...); deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...); })` invokes async functions without awaiting. The surrounding `try/catch` cannot capture rejections from these calls; any failure (e.g., SendGrid 4xx, Prisma error) becomes an unhandled rejection and the error handler `log.error("Error while canceling scheduled workflow reminders", error)` will never be executed. Use `await Promise.all(reminders.map(...))` inside the try/catch (or a `for/await`) so cancellations complete and errors are observable.

title: Reminder cancellations fired from forEach without awaiting
body: `updatedBookings.forEach((booking) => booking.workflowReminders.forEach((reminder) => { deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...); deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...); }))` does not await the async reminder calls. The handler returns the success response while cancellations are still in flight. Errors from the internal `try/catch` of those helpers are merely logged via `console.log` and the caller never learns if a cancellation failed. Combined with the immediateDelete semantics, a failure means the cancelled booking can still trigger an outgoing workflow reminder. Convert to `await Promise.all(...)` or sequential `for/await`.

title: Reschedule reminder cancellation not awaited
body: In `requestReschedule`, `bookingToReschedule.workflowReminders.forEach((reminder) => { deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId); deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId); })` does not await the async deletion calls. Failures are only logged by the helpers' internal catch and never propagated to the caller, so a SendGrid/Prisma error leaves the reminder in place. With no surrounding try/catch, even logging of these errors disappears at this layer. Use `await Promise.all(...)`.

title: Multiple reminder cancellation blocks fire-and-forget
body: Several blocks in the `update` and `delete` mutations (`scheduledReminders.forEach`, `remindersToDelete.flat().forEach`, `remindersFromStep.forEach`, `remindersToUpdate.forEach`, `steps.forEach` calling `scheduleEmailReminder`/`scheduleSMSReminder`) iterate with `forEach` over async functions that are never awaited. Errors from SendGrid/Twilio/Prisma are swallowed inside the helpers' catch blocks. Use `await Promise.all(...)` (or sequential `for/await`) so failures are observable and cancellations actually complete before the workflow state changes.

title: Cancellation loop is sequential
body: Reminders are cancelled one at a time using `await client.request(...)` inside a `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop. With many reminders to cancel (the whole reason for deferring to a CRON), serializing SendGrid calls slows the CRON. The SendGrid cancel calls are independent, so they can run in parallel via `Promise.allSettled` to keep the request window short and reduce the chance that one slow call blocks the run. DB deletes can then be awaited in another `Promise.all`.

title: Past-dated reminders deleted before cancellation runs
body: The first block deletes every EMAIL reminder with `scheduledDate <= now()` regardless of `cancelled` or `scheduled` state, and the cancellation block runs after. A reminder that was just marked `cancelled=true` while its `scheduledDate` is still in the future (within ~1 hour) is fine, but the unconditional past-date delete means a reminder with `scheduled=false`, `cancelled=true`, and a `scheduledDate` that briefly slipped into the past (e.g., race during reschedule) will be silently deleted before the cancellation CRON ever tries to SendGrid-cancel it. Filter by `scheduled: true` (and/or `referenceId: { not: null }`) so unscheduled/cancelled reminders are not lost.

title: New column is nullable with no default
body: `ALTER TABLE "WorkflowReminder" ADD COLUMN "cancelled" BOOLEAN;` leaves the column nullable with no default. The CRON relies on `cancelled: true` (strict match) to pick up rows, so existing rows with `NULL` will never be processed. While intentional for new rows, any rows that were already scheduled in SendGrid for cancelled bookings prior to this migration will remain pending in SendGrid forever (the very bug this PR addresses). Either set a default of `false`, backfill, or add a one-off cleanup for legacy scheduled reminders.

title: Workflow delete uses immediateDelete inconsistently
body: In `delete` and the deleted-step branch of `update`, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` is used (`immediateDelete=true`). Other branches in the same file (e.g., `activeOn` change block at line 376 and edited-step block at line 569) call without `immediateDelete`. Deleting a workflow with many active bookings could therefore hit SendGrid's 100-pending-cancellations limit. Either drop `immediateDelete=true` everywhere for consistency with the PR's stated design, or document the choice explicitly.

title: Outer try/catch abandons the cancellation loop and orphans DB deletes on first SendGrid failure
body: The try block wraps both the `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop and the final `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)`. If any `client.request({...status:"cancel"})` call rejects mid-loop, control jumps straight to the catch and the function returns. Two consequences: (a) every reminder after the failing one is never sent to SendGrid and will still be delivered, and (b) the `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` promises already pushed into `workflowRemindersToDelete` are never awaited — they become orphaned microtasks (also a memory leak) and any subsequent cron run will not see them cleaned up. The catch only logs and returns. Move the try/catch inside the loop (or use `Promise.allSettled`) so each cancellation is independent and all DB deletes are processed.

title: remindersToCancel query is missing the EMAIL method filter
body: `prisma.workflowReminder.findMany({ where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: dayjs().add(1, "hour").toISOString() } } })` does not filter by `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL`. SMS reminders don't currently reach `cancelled=true` (because `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` always deletes the row), but the only thing this query feeds is a SendGrid `/v3/user/scheduled_sends` POST with the `referenceId`, which is a SendGrid batch id. If anything ever marks an SMS reminder `cancelled=true`, the code would call SendGrid's email API with a Twilio SID. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL`.

title: deleteScheduledEmailReminder with immediateDelete=true has no fallback when the SendGrid cancel fails
body: When `immediateDelete` is true and `client.request({ url: "/v3/user/scheduled_sends", method: "POST", body: { batch_id: referenceId, status: "cancel" } })` throws (e.g. SendGrid's 100-pending-cancellation limit described in the PR, or a transient HTTP error), the function catches the error, logs it, and returns without writing anything to the database. The `WorkflowReminder` row stays at `scheduled=true` with `cancelled=null`, so the new cron logic in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` (which only matches `cancelled: true`) will never pick it up, and the email remains scheduled in SendGrid — i.e. the very bug the PR is supposed to fix. Fall back to setting `cancelled: true` when the immediate cancel fails so the cron will retry.

title: Reschedule in handleNewBooking passes immediateDelete=true, defeating the PR's fix for the SendGrid 100-cancellation limit
body: The PR's stated root cause for the original bug is that SendGrid caps pending cancellations at 100 and any new cancellation request beyond that silently fails, leaving the scheduled email in place. The new `cancelled`/cron approach in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` exists precisely to avoid that cap. But here, on every successful reschedule, the code still calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)`, which goes straight to SendGrid's cancel API. Under any volume of reschedules this hits the same 100-pending-cancellations ceiling and rescheduled bookings will again leak their reminders. Use the same delayed-mark-cancelled approach as `handleCancelBooking.ts` (no `immediateDelete`) so the cron job, not the synchronous call, drives the actual SendGrid cancel.

title: Reschedule in handleNewBooking cancels immediately, but requestReschedule in bookings.tsx does not — same operation, different behavior
body: `handleNewBooking.ts` line 968 calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` when an attendee reschedules, while `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx` lines 488-494 in the `requestReschedule` mutation call `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` (no `immediateDelete`). Both code paths cancel the reminders of the same kind of booking (a cancelled-and-rebooked booking), so the resulting behavior — whether the email is gone immediately or up to a cron cycle later, and whether SendGrid is hit synchronously at all — should be identical. Pick one strategy and apply it in both places. The `handleNewBooking.ts` choice is also the one that reintroduces the 100-limit bug above.

title: Workflow step deletion uses immediateDelete=true while step editing does not — inconsistent with the PR's approach
body: In the `update` mutation, when a step is deleted (line 521) the code calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` (immediate delete), but when a step is merely edited (line 576) it calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` (deferred to the cron). Deleting and editing a workflow step both end with the old reminders no longer matching the workflow definition, so they should use the same cancellation strategy. As written, deleting a workflow on a high-traffic account still synchronously calls SendGrid's cancel API and risks the 100-pending-cancellations cap the PR is meant to work around.

title: First deleteMany runs before cancelled-reminder processing, racing SendGrid's send window
body: The handler first runs `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany({ where: { method: EMAIL, scheduledDate: { lte: dayjs().toISOString() } } })`, then finds `cancelled: true` reminders whose `scheduledDate <= now + 1h` and only then calls SendGrid's cancel API. A `cancelled=true` row whose `scheduledDate` is in the past (e.g. the cron was delayed and SendGrid has not yet processed `sendAt`) is wiped by the first deleteMany before it can be cancelled, and the email will be delivered. Process the `cancelled=true` cancellation loop before the past-dated cleanup deleteMany (or scope the cleanup deleteMany to `cancelled: { not: true }`).

title: Error in cancel-reminder catch is logged with console.log instead of console.error
body: Line 76 uses `console.log(\`Error cancelling scheduled Emails: ${error}\`)` while every other failure path in this file (lines 22, 29, 222) uses `console.log` for non-errors too, but this branch is explicitly an error case from the new cancellation loop. Use `console.error` so log-shipping and alerting can distinguish operational failures from normal output.

title: forEach with async callbacks, fire-and-forget; outer try/catch is dead code
body: The newly added block at lines 963-975 wraps `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach(...)` in a try/catch, but Array.prototype.forEach does not await async callbacks. The calls to `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)` (with `immediateDelete: true`, so it does a SendGrid HTTP request) and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)` return promises that are discarded. Any rejection from them is not delivered to the outer `catch` and is only logged (or lost) inside the deletion functions' own try/catch. The subsequent `eventManager.reschedule(...)` and rest of the booking flow proceeds without waiting, so the reschedule response can return to the client while the old reminders are still being (or never) cancelled. Fix by awaiting each call (`for...of` loop) or using `Promise.all(reminders.map(...))` with the try/catch inside the async iteration.

title: Sequential for-await loop aborts whole batch on first SendGrid error; pending delete promises are never awaited
body: In the new block (lines 53-77) the loop calls `await client.request(...)` for every reminder and only after success builds a `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` and pushes it into `workflowRemindersToDelete`. When `client.request` throws (e.g. SendGrid's documented limit on pending cancellations is reached, batch_id not found, or transient API error), the throw escapes the for-loop into the outer try/catch which only logs and returns. Consequences: (1) every reminder after the first failure is silently skipped in this run; (2) the deletes already pushed for the successful iterations are never executed because `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` is skipped after the throw — they become dangling promises that may or may not resolve in the background with no observability. The retry-on-next-run strategy is undermined if the first failure always happens early. The loop should isolate each reminder's cancel+delete (try/catch per iteration, push successes only) and always `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` before returning.

title: forEach with async deletion functions; workflow reminder cancellation is fire-and-forget
body: The new code at lines 484-493 iterates over `updatedBookings`/`workflowReminders` with `forEach` and invokes `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)` without awaiting. These functions perform real side effects (DB update to set `cancelled: true`, Twilio HTTP call, DB delete). Because they aren't awaited, the handler reaches `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` and `await sendCancelledEmails(evt)` and returns successfully even if every cancellation silently failed inside the deletion helpers' inner try/catch. For EMAIL reminders specifically, if the `prisma.workflowReminder.update` to set `cancelled: true` fails, the CRON job in scheduleEmailReminders will never know to cancel that send and the email will still be delivered. Use `for...of` with `await` (or `Promise.all([...].map(...))`) so failures surface and the row is reliably marked before the request resolves.

title: forEach with async deletion functions in requestReschedule mutation
body: In the `requestReschedule` mutation (lines 487-494) `bookingToReschedule.workflowReminders.forEach(...)` calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` without awaiting. The mutation returns before those calls complete (or have any chance of failing). For EMAIL reminders, a failure to set `cancelled: true` in the DB means the CRON-driven SendGrid cancellation never happens and the attendee receives the old reminder email. Use `for...of` with `await`, or `await Promise.all(reminders.map(async r => ...))`, so the DB row is reliably marked (and the Twilio call observed) before the mutation responds.

title: Reschedule path bypasses the deferred-cancellation fix and re-introduces the 100-pending-cancellations bug
body: In the new reschedule block, the call is `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` — passing `immediateDelete: true` causes an immediate SendGrid POST to /v3/user/scheduled_sends with status:'cancel' for every workflow reminder of the previous booking. This is inconsistent with the cancellation path in `handleCancelBooking.ts` and `bookings.tsx` (both use the default `immediateDelete: false`, which marks `cancelled: true` and lets the cron in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` do the SendGrid call in a controlled window). The whole purpose of the PR is to avoid SendGrid's 100-pending-cancellations limit; the reschedule path here still hits it directly. Under any burst of simultaneous reschedules the limit will be reached and old reminders will be delivered (the exact bug being fixed). Pass `false` (or omit) to be consistent with the cancel path.

title: forEach(async) in recurring-cancellation branch loses calendar deleteEvent calls
body: In the recurring-cancellation branch (bookingToDelete.eventType?.recurringEvent && bookingToDelete.recurringEventId && allRemainingBookings) the code uses `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { ... })`. Array.prototype.forEach does not await async callbacks, so the inner `await getCalendar(credential)` and `await calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` invocations are fire-and-forget and the pushes to `apiDeletes` happen asynchronously. By the time control reaches `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` at line 652, `apiDeletes` will normally be empty for the recurring branch, so those `deleteEvent` calls are never awaited. Consequence: when an attendee (or organizer) cancels a recurring booking with `allRemainingBookings=true`, the response returns success but the underlying calendar events are not actually deleted on the external provider. Use `for (const credential of ...) { ... }` (as already done at lines 480-483 in the non-recurring branch) or `await Promise.all(calendarCredentials.map(...))` so the deletes are collected and awaited before the request resolves.

title: forEach(async) in requestReschedule drops calendar/video cleanup
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })` does not await its async callback, so the `await getCalendar(...)` + `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` and the `deleteMeeting(...)` calls for each booking reference are started but never awaited. The function then proceeds to send the reschedule email/webhook and returns to the client, meaning external calendar events and video meetings from the original booking are not reliably cleaned up when a booking is rescheduled. This was an existing latent issue (deleteEvent was already async) but the conversion to async `getCalendar` makes the missing await even more important. Replace the forEach with a for-of loop or Promise.all so all cleanup promises are awaited before returning.

title: forEach(async) drops calendar cleanup on vital reschedule
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })` does not await its callback. The `await getCalendar(credentialsMap.get(bookingRef.type))` and subsequent `calendar?.deleteEvent(bookingRef.uid, builder.calendarEvent)` invocations are untracked promises. The function returns `true` without waiting for these deletes, so a vital-related reschedule can complete without actually removing the previous calendar/video events on the external provider. The conversion from sync to async `getCalendar` makes this dependency concrete. Use `for (const bookingRef of bookingRefsFiltered) { ... }` (with await inside) or wrap in `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))`.

title: forEach(async) drops calendar cleanup on wipemycalother reschedule
body: Same pattern as in vital/lib/reschedule.ts: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })` does not await its async callback, so the `await getCalendar(...)` + `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` calls run detached from the request lifecycle. The reschedule returns success without guaranteeing the prior calendar events are deleted. Use a sequential for-of or Promise.all to await the deletes before resolving.

title: getCalendarCredentials now returns Promise<Calendar> but types still say Calendar
body: `getCalendarCredentials` now constructs each `calendar` entry via `getCalendar(credential)`, which is async. The returned objects therefore have `calendar: Promise<Calendar | null>` at runtime, but there is no explicit return type or `.d.ts` update, so TypeScript still infers/asserts `calendar: Calendar | null`. This is an implicit API/contract break: any new or existing consumer that forgets to `await item.calendar` will call `.listCalendars()`/`.createEvent(...)`/`.deleteEvent(...)` on a Promise object and fail with a cryptic runtime error (e.g. `calendar.deleteEvent is not a function`). Either update the return type to reflect the Promise and rename the field (e.g. `calendarPromise`), or wrap the synchronous-style list construction with a single `Promise.all` inside `getCalendarCredentials` so callers see a real `Calendar` instance and existing call sites like `getConnectedCalendars` can drop their per-item await.

title: Calendar deletes serialized by for-of instead of Promise.all
body: The PR replaces the previous `forEach((credential) => { ... apiDeletes.push(calendar?.deleteEvent(...)); })` with a sequential `for (const credential of calendarCredentials) { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); apiDeletes.push(calendar?.deleteEvent(...)); }`. This now awaits each `getCalendar` and each `deleteEvent` one credential at a time. For users connected to many calendars (or with `_other_calendar` integrations) this serializes what used to run in parallel and noticeably slows cancellation latency. Preserve the new await-semantics but parallelize with `const calendars = await Promise.all(calendarCredentials.map(getCalendar)); apiDeletes.push(...calendars.map(c => c?.deleteEvent(uid, evt, externalCalendarId)));` (or equivalent `.flatMap`).

title: Outer `calendar` variable unused after refactor
body: `const calendar = await getCalendar(calendarCredential);` is now declared unconditionally but is only consumed in the `else` branch. In the `if (recurring && allRemainingBookings)` branch the code creates its own (shadowed) `calendar` inside the forEach callback, making the outer value dead. Either remove the outer declaration and move it into the `else` branch, or move the recurring-branch delete logic out so the outer calendar is actually used. As-is this is dead-await work and visual confusion about which calendar is being used.

title: forEach with async callback loses error handling and never waits
body: At packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts:125, the code runs `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })` inside a try/catch (lines 124-139). Array.prototype.forEach does not await async callbacks, so the Promise returned by the async arrow is discarded, and the await on getCalendar (line 128) and the returned `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` Promise are fire-and-forget. With getCalendar now async, the dynamic import inside it can reject, and that rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection - the surrounding try/catch cannot see errors thrown after the first await inside the callback. Consequence: when a calendar integration fails to load or delete an event during a reschedule, the error is silently dropped (only Node's unhandledRejection handler sees it), the try/catch's logger.error is never invoked, and the user may see a booking marked as rescheduled while the old event remains on their calendar. Replace forEach by `Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (ref) => { ... }))` (or a for-of loop with await), and move any try/catch inside the async function so rejections can be caught.

title: forEach with async callback loses error handling and never waits
body: Same bug pattern as the vital reschedule file: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })` at line 125 is wrapped in a try/catch (lines 124-139), but forEach does not await the async callback, so rejections from `await getCalendar(...)` (line 128) and from `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` are not caught by the surrounding try/catch and become unhandled promise rejections. The `await getCalendar` added by this PR is a new place where async errors can occur (dynamic import rejection), and the try/catch is now actively misleading because it looks like errors will be logged but they will not be. Use Promise.all + an inner try/catch (or for-of with await) instead of forEach.

title: forEach with async callback never awaits and there is no error handling
body: In the requestReschedule mutation at packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:553, `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); })` fires off calendar deletions without awaiting. There is no try/catch around it. The mutation proceeds to await sendRequestRescheduleEmail and to await the webhook promises, then returns - the deletions may still be in flight or have failed silently. With getCalendar now async, a rejection from the dynamic import (e.g., app module missing or throwing on evaluation) becomes an unhandled promise rejection. Consequence: reschedule can be marked successful in the DB and the user notified, while the old calendar event is never deleted and the error is silently lost. Replace the forEach with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (ref) => { ... }))` (or a for-of with await) and add per-iteration error handling so failures are at least logged.

title: forEach with async callback in recurring-event cancellation never awaits and lacks error handling
body: In the recurring-event branch of handleCancelBooking at packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:460, `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { ... await getCalendar(credential); ... await calendar?.deleteEvent(...); ... })` is fire-and-forget: forEach does not await async callbacks. There is no try/catch around this code. The await on getCalendar (added by this PR, now an async function whose dynamic import can reject) and on deleteEvent produce unawaited promises. Consequence: recurring-event cancellations can leave orphan events on user calendars, and any rejection from a missing/broken app module is an unhandled rejection with no logger entry. Replace with `await Promise.all(calendarCredentials.map(async (credential) => { ... }))` and add a try/catch inside the callback to log failures.

title: getVideoAdapters awaits each dynamic import sequentially
body: In packages/core/videoClient.ts:21-36, getVideoAdapters is implemented as `for (const cred of withCredentials) { ... const app = await appStore[appName as keyof typeof appStore]; ... }`. Previously this was a synchronous reduce over already-bundled modules; the PR conversion to async made every iteration await the dynamic import in series. For a user with multiple video integrations (e.g. zoom + daily + googlemeet) the dynamic imports are done sequentially when they could run concurrently via `Promise.all(withCredentials.map(async (cred) => { ... }))`. While each individual import is typically fast, this is a clear performance regression introduced by the refactor and is worth parallelizing.

title: getCalendarCredentials keeps a sync signature but returns objects with unawaited Promises
body: At packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:23-36, getCalendarCredentials is still declared as a synchronous function but now stores the result of `getCalendar(credential)` (which became async and returns `Promise<Calendar | null>`) in each item's `calendar` field (line 28). The caller must remember to `await item.calendar` individually. The diff updates getConnectedCalendars to do this (line 48), but the API contract is unsound: any other caller (existing or future) that uses the returned items expecting `calendar` to be a Calendar (or just checks `if (!calendar)` to short-circuit) will be wrong - a Promise is always truthy. Either make getCalendarCredentials async and await getCalendar inside, or memoize a synchronous module loader so getCalendar can stay sync and the field type is preserved.

title: forEach(async) does not await calendar/video deletions before sending reschedule email
body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... }) at line 125 is the classic forEach-doesn't-await-async-callbacks anti-pattern. The function reaches line 143 (await sendRequestRescheduleEmail) and then returns while the awaited getCalendar/deleteEvent/deleteMeeting calls inside the forEach are still in flight. The reschedule email is sent before the previous calendar/video events are actually deleted, so users can get a "please reschedule" email with the original time still marked busy on the calendar. Additionally, the surrounding try/catch (lines 124 and 135-139) silently breaks: pre-PR getCalendar was synchronous so its thrown errors reached this catch, but now getCalendar returns a rejected promise from inside the async callback, so rejections become unhandled promise rejections and are never logged via logger.error.

title: forEach(async) does not await calendar/video deletions before sending reschedule email
body: Same bug as packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... }) does not await its async callback. The function proceeds to await sendRequestRescheduleEmail (line 143) and returns while the calendar/video deletions are still pending. The pre-existing try/catch on lines 124/135-139 also loses its ability to catch errors thrown from getCalendar, since those errors are now inside rejected promises returned by the async callback rather than synchronous throws.

title: forEach(async) for recurring calendar deletions races with Promise.all(apiDeletes)
body: In the recurring cancellation branch, bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { ... }) is used. Each iteration awaits getCalendar and calendar.deleteEvent and pushes the resolved result into apiDeletes. forEach does not await these async callbacks, so when the later Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) at line 652 runs, the array may not yet contain all the entries (or any of them). Even when entries are eventually pushed, they are the already-resolved values from `await calendar?.deleteEvent(...)`, not pending promises, so Promise.all provides no concurrency waiting. This means recurring calendar cancellations can be silently dropped and apiDeletes can be resolved before the actual deletions occur.

title: forEach(async) does not await calendar/video deletions before reschedule email and webhook
body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... }) at line 553 starts calendar and video deletions but does not wait for them. The mutation immediately proceeds to await sendRequestRescheduleEmail (line 570) and then runs sendWebhooks via Promise.all (line 618). Recipients can receive the reschedule email and webhook while the original calendar/video event is still active. Errors from getCalendar or deleteEvent/deleteMeeting inside the async callback also become unhandled promise rejections because there is no try/catch and the forEach ignores the returned promises.

title: getCalendarCredentials now leaks Promise<Calendar|null> in its return values without being async
body: getCalendarCredentials (line 23) is still declared synchronous, but inside it calls the now-async getCalendar and stores the returned Promise<Calendar | null> in each result's `calendar` field (line 28). The only caller, getConnectedCalendars, happens to do `const calendar = await item.calendar;` so it works at runtime, but the function's signature and ReturnType no longer reflect the new shape. Any future caller that forgets to await `item.calendar` will silently get a Promise where it expects a Calendar. The function should either be marked `async`, or resolve the calendars up front with `await Promise.all(...)` before returning, so the contract matches the name.

title: Copy-paste bug in working-hours end calculation
body: In the newly added working-hours check inside `checkIfIsAvailable`, `end` is computed from `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`: `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();`. As `start === end`, the guard collapses to `slotStartTime < workingHour.startTime || slotStartTime > workingHour.endTime`, which never detects slots whose duration crosses the end of the working window. For any event longer than the gap between the slot start and the day's working-hour end (e.g. a 60-minute slot starting at 17:30 with working hours 9-17), the slot is treated as inside working hours and forwarded to the busy check, so it can be booked outside availability.

title: Working-hours comparison uses UTC time/day against organizer-local working hours
body: The working-hours guard compares `workingHour.days.includes(slotStartTime.day())`, `slotStartTime.hour()` and `slotStartTime.minute()` against `workingHour.startTime/endTime`. `WorkingHours.startTime/endTime` are minutes since midnight and `days` is the organizer/day-local day-of-week (as produced by `getAggregateWorkingHours`/`getWorkingHours`), while `slotStartTime` was produced by `time.utc()`, so `.day()/.hour()/.minute()` are in UTC. The comparison only works when organizer TZ is UTC; for any other organizer timezone the day-of-week and time-of-day values do not line up and slots can be classified as in/out of hours purely based on the UTC clock. The slot must be converted to the organizer's timezone (or, in `checkIfIsAvailable`, to `organizerTimeZone`) before these comparisons.

title: Date-override day comparison formats in the server's local timezone
body: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` formats the shifted instant using the dayjs instance's default (server-local) timezone, not `organizerTimeZone`. The right-hand side `slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")` is also in the server's local zone, so the two sides happen to match each other but not necessarily the organizer. When an organizer whose timezone is east of UTC enters an early-morning override (e.g. 06:30 IST = 01:00 UTC), `add(-330)` crosses midnight and the formatted day is the previous UTC day, so slots on the correct organizer day are rejected as outside the override. Use `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).format("YYYY MM DD")` and `slotStartTime.tz(organizerTimeZone).format("YYYY MM DD")` to compare days in the organizer's timezone.

title: `===` on dayjs instances never matches, breaking zero-length override handling
body: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` is reference equality of two distinct dayjs objects, which is always false. The branch that returns `true` (treating the slot as outside the override because the override has no duration) is therefore unreachable. Use `.isSame()` or compare `.valueOf()` if the intent is a value comparison. As written, a zero-length override (or "all-day" override with equal start and end) cannot be matched and falls into the same path as ordinary ranges.

title: Multi-override semantics: first non-covering override incorrectly blocks the slot
body: The `dateOverrides.find(...)` loop returns the first override whose day matches and for which the slot is outside that override's range; the outer `if` then returns `false` (slot unavailable) regardless of whether another override for the same day does cover the slot. With several date overrides on the same day (e.g. 09-11 and 14-16), a slot at 09:30 is inside the first override but not the second, the find returns the second, and the slot is rejected. The semantic should be ANY (available if any override covers), not ALL. The simplest fix is to break out as soon as a covering override is found, and only return `false` if every override for that day fails to cover.

title: `dayjs.tz(date.start, override.timeZone)` used without guarding undefined
body: `override.timeZone` was just made optional on `TimeRange`, but `slots.ts` calls `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()` unconditionally. `dayjs.tz(..., undefined)` does not throw on every code path but yields the host-local offset, which silently corrupts the offset math (`organizerUtcOffset`) and therefore every converted override time, producing wrong `startTime`/`endTime` minutes and wrong slots. Either require `timeZone` on the input, default it to `organizerTimeZone`/`timeZone`, or assert/throw when it is missing so the failure is not silent.

title: Convoluted offset arithmetic obscures intent and is easy to break under DST
body: `const utcOffset = dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1;` followed by `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` is a non-standard way to express "view `date.start` in `organizerTimeZone`". It also relies on the offset at the exact instant `date.start`, so for multi-day date overrides that span a DST transition the start and end can be shifted by different amounts and the resulting window can be subtly incorrect. Replacing this with `dayjs(date.start).tz(organizerTimeZone)` (and equivalent on the slot) eliminates the manual offset handling.

title: No test for the round-robin fixed-host date-override fix
body: The PR description and linked issues (#8207, #8329) state the change makes fixed hosts' date overrides count toward round-robin availability, but the new test only covers a single user with a date override at two different invitee timezones. There is no scenario that exercises a round-robin event with a fixed host plus a round-robin host where the fixed host has a date override restricting availability on a day; that is precisely the behaviour being fixed and currently has no regression test.

title: New `workingHours` branch in `checkIfIsAvailable` has no coverage
body: The PR adds a `workingHours`-based availability check inside `checkIfIsAvailable` (slots.ts lines 138-151). None of the tests in `getSchedule.test.ts` cover that branch (no test sets up a schedule with a normal-hours entry and then exercises a slot that crosses or falls outside those hours, and none cover the UTC-vs-organizer-tz interaction). Given the day/time-of-day handling bugs above, this is the branch most likely to regress silently and is exactly where a regression test belongs.

title: Duplicate start/end computation in working hours check
body: Inside the working-hours check in `checkIfIsAvailable`, both `start` and `end` are computed from `slotStartTime`, making them identical. As written, the upper-bound check `end > workingHour.endTime` is the same as `start > workingHour.endTime`, so a slot that starts inside the working window but whose `slotEndTime` extends past `workingHour.endTime` is never rejected here. The intent is clearly to compare the slot's end against `workingHour.endTime`; `end` should be `slotEndTime.hour() * 60 + slotEndTime.minute()`. While `getTimeSlots` generally generates slots that fit, this validator is supposed to be a defense-in-depth check and is currently incorrect for any case where a slot can extend past working hours (e.g., events that cross the boundary).

title: slotStartTime.day() is UTC but workingHour.days is organizer's local day
body: `slotStartTime = time.utc()` is converted to UTC before the check, so `slotStartTime.day()` returns the day-of-week in UTC. `workingHour.days` represents the organizer's local days (the schedule is defined in the organizer's timezone). At day boundaries this mismatches: a slot at, say, 23:30 UTC on Monday is Tuesday 05:00 in Kolkata (UTC+5:30), so `workingHour.days.includes(1)` looks for Monday entries that don't apply, and Tuesday entries that do apply are never consulted. The slot will be incorrectly treated as outside working hours. The day lookup should use `slotStartTime.tz(organizerTimeZone).day()`.

title: Date override day comparison depends on server's local timezone
body: The check `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').format('YYYY MM DD') === slotStartTime.format('YYYY MM DD')` mixes two different reference frames: the left side is computed in the dayjs instance's local timezone (i.e. the Node server's TZ) after a numeric offset shift, and the right side is UTC because `slotStartTime = time.utc()`. If the server runs in any timezone other than the organizer's, the comparison produces wrong results near day boundaries, so a date override can fail to match a slot that occurs on the same calendar day in the organizer's timezone. The correct comparison is `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).format('YYYY MM DD') === slotStartTime.tz(organizerTimeZone).format('YYYY MM DD')`. The current code is also semantically fragile - the `utcOffset * -1` arithmetic is not doing what the variable name suggests.

title: Working-hours find returns the wrong boolean for split/missing schedules
body: `workingHours.find(...)` returns truthy as soon as any single working-hour entry reports the slot as outside its range, then the slot is rejected. This is inverted: a slot should be considered inside working hours if it fits inside ANY entry, not outside if it doesn't fit every entry. For a user with split shifts (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-17:00) the first entry's 'outside' will incorrectly mark a 15:00 slot as unavailable. Likewise, when no workingHour entry covers the slot's day at all, every callback returns falsy, the find returns undefined and the slot is treated as available even though the user has no working hours that day. The logic needs `find` to return when the slot is INSIDE a working hour (or no entries match at all → unavailable).

title: No regression test for the round-robin fixed-host date-override fix
body: The PR description and the linked issue (#8207) call out that round-robin events were being booked when fixed hosts were unavailable due to a date override. The `checkIfIsAvailable` call site for `fixedHosts` is precisely what addresses this. The only new test added in this PR is the 'different timezone' variant of the existing personal-event date-override test; nothing exercises a `ROUND_ROBIN` event type with a `hosts: [{ isFixed: true }, { isFixed: false }]` setup plus a date override on the fixed host. Without such a test, the very behavior this PR is supposed to fix can silently regress.

title: Test fixture name and stored times disagree on the override's timezone
body: The schedule description for `IstWorkHoursWithDateOverride` says 'Date Override for 2PM to 6PM IST (in GST time it is 8:30AM to 12:30PM)' which corresponds to 08:30-12:30 UTC, but the fixture stores `startTime: '1970-01-01T14:00:00.000Z'` and `endTime: '1970-01-01T18:00:00.000Z'` (14:00-18:00 UTC, i.e. 19:30-23:30 IST). The expected slot list ('08:30:00.000Z', '09:30:00.000Z', ...) corresponds to the description, not to the stored UTC values. Either the fixture should store 08:30/12:30 UTC or the description should be corrected, otherwise a future maintainer cannot tell which interpretation the system relies on.

title: selectedSlots branch silently skips working-hours/date-override checks
body: In the final `if (selectedSlots?.length > 0)` branch, `checkIfIsAvailable` is called with `busy` (from selectedSlots) but without passing `dateOverrides` or `workingHours` from `userSchedule`, so the parameter defaults `[]` apply. If a host's availability changed between when the slot was generated and when the reservation was checked, or if a previous filter was bypassed by some future refactor, the slot could pass this check while being outside the host's availability. At minimum it is inconsistent with the other two call sites which do pass these fields; the comment explaining why this branch intentionally omits them is missing.

title: Working-hours check sets end equal to start, ignoring event length
body: In the newly added working-hours branch of `checkIfIsAvailable`, the local `end` variable is computed as `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`, which is identical to `start`. The intent (from the variable names and the surrounding comment `slot is outside of working hours`) was clearly to compare the slot's end time against `workingHour.endTime`. With `end === start` the predicate reduces to `if (start < workingHour.startTime || start > workingHour.endTime)`, so any slot whose start is still within working hours is treated as available even when the booking length pushes the slot past `workingHour.endTime`. Concretely: a 60‑minute event starting at 16:30 with working hours 9:00–17:00 (the slot ends at 17:30, past the working hours) would be returned as bookable.

title: Date-override day comparison mixes local-mode and UTC-mode dayjs objects
body: The comparison `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD") === slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")` is incorrect: `dayjs(date.start).add(...)` returns a Dayjs in the default (system local) timezone, so its `.format("YYYY MM DD")` is rendered in the server's local timezone, while `slotStartTime = time.utc()` is explicitly in UTC mode and formats in UTC. As a result the comparison only matches when the server happens to run in UTC (or in the same offset as the override), and silently fails in any other deployment timezone, causing date overrides to be missed entirely or applied on the wrong day. Both sides must use `.tz(organizerTimeZone)` (e.g. `dayjs(date.start).tz(organizerTimeZone).format("YYYY MM DD") === slotStartTime.tz(organizerTimeZone).format("YYYY MM DD")`), or both must be forced to UTC with `.utc()`.

title: Date-override offset formula does not compute wall-clock time in invitee tz
body: The new block computes `const offset = inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset;` and then `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour() / .minute()` to derive `startTime`/`endTime`. This does not produce the minute-of-day in the invitee's timezone. Worked example: override at 14:00 IST is stored as `override.start = 1970-01-01T08:30:00.000Z`. With invitee in Asia/Dhaka (+06:00) the code gives `offset = 30`, then `dayjs(08:30Z).utc().add(30m).hour() = 9`, so `startTime = 540` (09:00), i.e. slots appear at 09:00 Asia/Dhaka = 03:00 UTC. The correct value is `14:30 Asia/Dhaka = 08:30 UTC`, which would come from `dayjs(override.start).tz(timeZone).hour()*60 + .minute()`. As a result, for the production data shape (UTC moment encoding the organizer's wall clock) the PR silently shifts all date-override slots by the full timezone offset between organizer and invitee (e.g. 5h30m for IST→UTC, 5h for IST→EST).

title: Date-override test uses literal-UTC times instead of organizer wall-clock times
body: The `IstWorkHoursWithDateOverride` fixture stores the override as `{ startTime: "1970-01-01T14:00:00.000Z", endTime: "1970-01-01T18:00:00.000Z" }` and a schedule timeZone of `+05:30`, but the test's own name comment says the override is "2PM to 6PM IST". In production a Cal.com date override is the UTC moment that represents the organizer's local wall clock, so a 14:00 IST override is stored as `1970-01-01T08:30:00.000Z`. The fixture instead stores the literal UTC time 14:00, which happens to make the buggy `offset = inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset` formula in `packages/lib/slots.ts` produce the right UTC slots by accident (both IST and Asia/Dhaka invitees see `08:30Z`). The new "different timezone" sub-assertion only verifies that the two invitees see the same UTC slot list; it does not exercise the real production shape where the stored Date represents the organizer's wall clock. With the production shape the PR's formula would emit slots shifted by the full organizer↔invitee offset and the tests would fail, so this gap is hiding the high-severity timezone bug above.

title: SQL injection in migration via string interpolation
body: The migration interpolates the host value directly into SQL: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. The `h` value comes from splitting the `embeddable_hosts` site setting, which an admin can populate. A value containing a single quote (e.g. `evil.com'); DROP TABLE embeddable_hosts; --`) will break out of the string and execute arbitrary SQL. Use parameterized queries or at minimum escape the value (e.g. `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h)`).

title: before_validation crashes when host is nil
body: The `before_validation` callback calls `self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` and `self.host.sub!(/\/.*$/, '')`. If `host` is nil (which happens when the API receives a request without a host param, or when the record is built in tests without a host), this raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil`. The callback should guard with `return unless host.present?` or use non-bang `sub` and assign back.

title: update action crashes when host id not found
body: `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for an unknown id. The code then calls `save_host(host)`, which executes `host.host = ...` on nil, raising `NoMethodError` and returning a 500. The controller should return 404 (e.g. `raise Discourse::NotFound` or `render status: 404`) when the lookup fails.

title: destroy action crashes when host id not found
body: `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can be nil, but `host.destroy` is then called on nil, raising `NoMethodError` and producing a 500. Should return 404 when the host doesn't exist.

title: Missing index on embeddable_hosts.host
body: The migration creates the `embeddable_hosts` table with a `host` column but no index. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` runs `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` on every embed request. As the table grows, this will become a sequential scan. Add `add_index :embeddable_hosts, :host` (or a unique index to also prevent duplicate hosts).

title: expandable_first_post? no longer requires any embeddable hosts
body: The old check `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` was replaced with `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`. Since `embeddable_hosts` was removed as a site setting, the check now passes whenever `embed_truncate?` is true and there's a topic embed, even if no embeddable hosts exist in the new `embeddable_hosts` table. The method should check `EmbeddableHost.any?` (or equivalent) to preserve the original semantic that embedding is only expandable when at least one host is configured.

title: category_fabricator.rb contains the wrong fabricator
body: The diff swapped the contents: `category_fabricator.rb` now defines only `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while the category fabricators were moved into `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. Although Fabricator looks up by symbol so the tests will run, this is confusing and fragile: anyone reading the file will think it fabricates categories, and any test that needs both will pull from the wrong file. The two files should be swapped back so each filename matches its contents.

title: Combined @on and @observes decorators on same method
body: `_focusOnInput` is decorated with both `@on('didInsertElement')` and `@observes('editing')`. The `@observes` decorator registers the method as a property observer, while `@on('didInsertElement')` registers it as a one-shot insert listener. Using both is redundant and fragile across Ember versions; the observer semantics differ from the event-listener semantics, and the focus call may not run when expected (or may run when not expected). Use only `@observes('editing')` or only `@on('didInsertElement')`.

title: deleteHost action passed as a string
body: The template passes `deleteHost="deleteHost"` (a quoted string) to the component. In Ember this is a literal string, not a reference to the controller's action. The component's `sendAction('deleteHost', host)` will fail to find the action and the host will not be removed from the list after deletion. The attribute should be `deleteHost=(action "deleteHost")` or the equivalent binding that resolves to the controller action.

title: saveChanges action is unreachable
body: `saveChanges` is defined on the controller but no UI element in `embedding.hbs` triggers it (only `addHost` is wired to a button). The corresponding PUT /admin/customize/embedding route and `update` action in `EmbeddingController` are also unused. Either remove the dead code or add a Save button to the template.

title: Category referenced only by id, never re-hydrated in client store
body: EmbeddingSerializer declares `has_many :embeddable_hosts, embed: :ids`, and EmbeddableHostSerializer exposes only `category_id`. The Ember side hydrates `category_id` into a `category` object only when the response has `__rest_serializer: "1"` and a `categories` collection in the root. `EmbeddingController#show` passes `rest_serializer: true` but does not include a `categories` collection, so `category` may be undefined on the client even though the controller template renders `{{category-badge host.category}}`. Verify the categories collection is included in the embedding payload, or have the client fetch the category separately.

title: Uncategorized fallback is silently forced for blank category_id
body: `host.category_id = SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id if host.category_id.blank?` overwrites an explicitly blank choice with the uncategorized bucket, which may not be what the admin intended. If `SiteSetting.allow_uncategorized_topics` is false (and an admin chose none), this still creates a host pointing at the uncategorized category and the embedded topic will be rejected by the topic validation. Should reject the request with a validation error instead, or require a non-blank category.

title: Controller spec has no coverage of create/update/destroy
body: The only assertion is `expect(Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController).to eq(true)`. There is no test exercising the create, update, or destroy actions, the `ensure_staff` before filter, the SQL-injection-prone `host.host = params[:...]` mass-assignment, or the not-found path. Given the bugs in those actions (nil host on update/destroy), a regression here would not be caught.

title: Embedding controller spec has no coverage of show/update
body: Same as the embeddable_hosts controller: only a parent-class check. No tests verify the serialized payload, staff enforcement, or the `fetch_embedding` ordering.

title: resources :embeddable_hosts exposes undefined show and index actions
body: `resources :embeddable_hosts, constraints: AdminConstraint.new` generates index, show, create, update, and destroy routes. The controller implements only create, update, and destroy. Requests to GET /admin/embeddable_hosts or GET /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id will hit `index`/`show` and raise `ActionController::UrlGenerationError` or `UnknownAction`. Either add `only: [:create, :update, :destroy]` to the route or implement the missing actions.

title: Removal of SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? breaks plugins/clients
body: The `allows_embeddable_host?` class method was deleted in this PR. Any plugin, theme, or external integration that called it (it is a public class method on a widely used model) will get `NoMethodError` after upgrade.
