title: include_website_name missing question mark — dead code
body: The new `include_website_name` method is defined without the trailing `?`. Throughout this file (and AMS conventions used by Discourse), every include predicate is named `include_<attr>?` (e.g., `include_email?`, `include_card_image_badge?`, `include_stats?`). Without the `?` the serializer never calls this method, so it has no effect and `website_name` will be included in the JSON whenever its computed value is non-nil. It should be `def include_website_name?`.

title: TL0 users' website_name leaks to anonymous viewers
body: `:website` is registered with `untrusted_attributes`, which auto-generates `include_website?` to return `false` when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` (i.e., a TL0 user viewed by an anonymous/staff-with-restriction visitor). The new `include_website_name?` predicate (or the existing `include_website_name` if it's a typo) only checks `website.present?` and never calls `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`. As a result, even when `website` is suppressed from the payload for a TL0 user, `website_name` (which still reveals the host and path the user has set) can still be serialized, bypassing the same privacy gate. Either add `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` call (lines 105–111) or have the include predicate return `false if scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`.

title: website_name drops query string and fragment
body: `website_name` concatenates `URI(website).host` with `URI(website).path`, but never appends `.query` or `.fragment`. A user whose website is, e.g., `http://example.com/users/bob?tab=posts#about` will be displayed as `example.com/users/bob`, losing information the PR title advertises ('show complete URL path'). If the intent really is to mirror the original full URL when on the same domain, `URI(website).request_uri` (or host + path + query + fragment) should be used instead of just path.

title: No coverage that website_name is hidden from anonymous viewers of TL0 users
body: The 'with a TL0 user seen as anonymous' context asserts that `untrusted_attributes` (`:bio_raw`, `:bio_cooked`, `:bio_excerpt`, `:location`, `:website`, `:profile_background`, `:card_background`) are absent from `json`. After this change `:website_name` carries the same private information as `:website` and must be excluded by the same `restrict_user_fields?` gate, but the existing assertion was not extended and no new test exercises this case. Without such a test the privacy regression described above can be reintroduced unnoticed.

title: URI(website.to_s) parsed up to three times per call
body: `URI(website.to_s)` is invoked three times inside `website_name` (once for `.host`, then again for `.path` in each branch that includes the path). Each call constructs and parses a URI object. The value should be assigned to a local once (e.g., `uri = URI(website.to_s) rescue nil`) and reused. The method is called for every user serialization, so this multiplies unnecessarily.

title: Drive-by doc comment change unrelated to PR
body: This PR is about changing the website display behaviour. The diff also edits the JSDoc above `profileBackground` from `@property websiteName` to `@property profileBackground` in `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/user.js.es6`. The fix is correct, but it's an unrelated drive-by change that should be in its own commit/PR so the website-domain UX change stays focused and reviewable.

title: Subdomain check uses brittle two-segment suffix test
body: The `elsif` branch only fires when `discourse_host` and `website_host` have the same number of dot-separated segments and that count is `> 2`. A case such as `Discourse.current_hostname` returning `example.com` (2 segments) while `website_host` is `forums.example.com` (3 segments) skips the `elsif`, drops into `else`, and `discourse_host.ends_with?('.' + website_host)` is false, so the user sees just `forums.example.com` with no path even though the discourse host is a parent suffix of the website host. The condition that decides whether to show the path should be based purely on suffix relationship (e.g., one host ends with `.` + the other, or they are equal), not on equal segment counts, otherwise same-domain path display is missed in mixed-depth subdomain setups.

title: include_website_name missing ? suffix breaks AMS include check
body: The new `def include_website_name` method at line 153 is missing the `?` suffix: it should be `def include_website_name?`. ActiveModel Serializers discovers conditional include logic by looking for predicate methods named `include_<attr>?` on the serializer. Without the `?`, this method is not recognized as an include check, and `website_name` will be included in the serialized JSON whenever the attribute method exists, regardless of whether `website` is set. This contradicts the design intent shown by the body `website.present?` and is inconsistent with every other `include_*?` method in the same file (e.g., `include_email?` at line 117, `include_stats?`, `include_suspend_reason?`, `include_user_fields?`, `include_topic_post_count?`), all of which correctly use the predicate form. Fixing this is a one-character change (`def include_website_name?`) and matches the established convention in the file.

title: Missing test for same-segment-count subdomain (elsif) branch
body: The `website_name` method has three branches: (1) exact host match `if website_host == discourse_host`, (2) same-segment-count subdomain match `elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2`, and (3) parent-domain match `else`. The three tests added in this PR only cover branches (1) and (3); the elsif branch (the `www.example.com == forum.example.com` case) is not exercised at all. That branch contains the most complex logic in the method — `website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') ? website_host + URI(website.to_s).path : website_host` — and has both a true and false outcome that should be verified, e.g., `Discourse.current_hostname = 'forum.example.com'` with website `http://www.example.com/user` (should yield `www.example.com/user`) and with website `http://www.other.com/user` (should yield `www.other.com`, no path).

title: Missing edge case tests for URL parsing in website_name
body: The new `website_name` method uses `URI(website.to_s).host` (with `rescue nil`) and `URI(website.to_s).path`, which behave inconsistently at the boundary. No tests cover: (1) a malformed URL such as `'not a valid url'` where `URI(...).host` raises (handled by `rescue nil`), (2) a URL with no path such as `http://example.com` where `URI().path` is `''`, producing `'example.com'`, or (3) a URL with a trailing slash such as `http://example.com/` where `URI().path` is `'/'`, producing `'example.com/'`. The trailing-slash inconsistency in particular means two visually identical URLs (one with, one without `/`) render different display text on the profile, which would surprise users and is worth either a test or explicit normalization in the serializer.

title: include_website_name conditional missing trailing question mark
body: The method at line 153 is `def include_website_name` (no `?`). ActiveModel::Serializer only recognizes `include_<attr>?` (with the question mark) as a conditional inclusion method; every other `include_*?` method in this file (e.g. `include_email?`, `include_suspend_reason?`, `include_card_image_badge_id?`, `include_card_image_badge?`, `include_user_fields?`, `include_topic_post_count?`) follows that convention, and the `untrusted_attributes` / `staff_attributes` / `private_attributes` macros at the top of the file all build the method name with `?`. Because the `?` is missing here, AMS treats `website_name` as an attribute that is always serialized: when `user_profile.website` is blank, `json[:website_name]` will appear in the payload with a `nil` value instead of being omitted, and no automated test would catch it because none of the new examples exercise the blank-website case. Rename to `def include_website_name?`.

title: website_name is not gated by untrusted_attributes and leaks for TL0 users seen by anonymous
body: Line 43 declares `:website_name` as a regular attribute, but the implementation at line 137 derives the value from `user_profile.website`, which is gated for TL0 users via `untrusted_attributes` (see line 109). The TL0/anonymous context in the spec at lines 6–16 was not updated, and the value list at line 11 still does not include `:website_name`. Consequence: for a TL0 user whose `user_profile.website` is set, `website` itself is hidden from anonymous viewers, but the derived `website_name` (which exposes the host and, when the host matches Discourse, the URL path) is still emitted. The current `include_website_name` (without `?`) at line 153 also fails to consult `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`. Add `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list (which will generate a properly-named `include_website_name?` that respects the TL0 restriction) instead of keeping a hand-rolled conditional.

title: URI(website.to_s) is parsed up to three times in website_name
body: Inside `website_name`, `URI(website.to_s)` is built once for `.host` on line 138 and then twice more for `.path` on lines 143, 146 and 149. Parse the URL once into a local variable and reuse it (e.g. `uri = URI(website.to_s) rescue nil; return if uri.nil? || uri.host.nil?`), which also makes the method shorter and easier to follow.

title: Domain comparisons are case-sensitive while URI#host is already lowercased
body: `URI(website.to_s).host` always returns a lowercase host (RFC 3986 §3.2.2), but the comparisons on lines 141, 144, 146 and the `ends_with?` on line 149 compare against `Discourse.current_hostname` verbatim. If an instance is configured with a mixed-case hostname (`Example.com`), a user whose website is `http://example.com/...` will not be recognized as same-domain, so the full path will not be shown even though the two hosts are equivalent per the URL spec. Normalize the instance hostname once (e.g. `discourse_host = Discourse.current_hostname.to_s.downcase`) or use case-insensitive comparison.

title: TL0 privacy test does not cover website_name and there is no blank-website case
body: The `untrusted_attributes` list at line 11 (`bio_raw bio_cooked bio_excerpt location website profile_background card_background`) was not extended with `:website_name`, so the assertion at lines 13–15 never verifies that `website_name` is excluded for a TL0 user seen by anonymous. There is also no example exercising `website_name` when `user_profile.website` is nil/blank, which is exactly where the `include_website_name` (no `?`) bug at user_serializer.rb:153 would surface — the key would be present with a `nil` value rather than being omitted. Add `website_name` to the untrusted list and add a blank-website expectation.

title: The sibling-subdomain branch in website_name has no test coverage
body: The `elsif` at user_serializer.rb:144–146 (the 'www.example.com / forum.example.com' heuristic that matches sibling subdomains with the same segment count) is reachable but not covered by any of the three new examples. The three added scenarios are (a) completely different domain, (b) identical host, and (c) subdomain via the `ends_with?` else branch — none of them exercises the segment-count branch, so a regression there would not be caught.

title: Wrong lightness on light-theme branch
body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a`, the original light-theme rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` (a darker shade suitable for bold usernames in light themes). The conversion replaced it with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, which makes the light-theme branch `lightness: 70%` instead of 30%. The PR's stated intent is to add a dark-theme branch while preserving the existing light-theme appearance, so the light branch's `70%` is wrong: it should be `30%`. In light themes, embedded-post meta-data usernames will visibly appear much lighter than before.

title: Wrong lightness on light-theme branch (.group-member-info .name)
body: In `.user-main .user-stream .group-member-info .name`, the original light-theme rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The conversion became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, so the light-theme branch now uses `lightness: 50%` instead of the original `30%`. The neighbouring `.group-member-info .title` selector in the same block kept its `50%` lightness correctly; only `.name` got its first-argument lightness changed, making the two siblings inconsistently colored and clearly different from before in light themes.

title: Wrong lightness on light-theme branch (.group-member-info .name)
body: In `.user-main .user-stream .group-member-info .name`, the original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new rule is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme branch should have stayed at `30%` (as the sibling `.group-member-info .title` did) but was changed to `50%`, producing a lighter, visibly different color in light themes and breaking the relative contrast between `.name` and `.title` that the original defined.

title: Wrong lightness on light-theme branch (.topic-map h3)
body: In `.topic-map h3`, the original light-theme rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. It was converted to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, making the light-theme branch `50%` instead of `20%`. The corresponding desktop rule (`desktop/topic-post.scss` for the same `.topic-map h3`) correctly preserves `lightness: 20%` in the light branch and `80%` in the dark branch, so this is an inconsistency between desktop and mobile and an unintended visual change in light themes: topic-map headings will appear much lighter on mobile.

title: Inverted lightness on light-theme branch (.custom-message-length)
body: In `.custom-message-length`, the original light-theme rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The conversion became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, swapping the light/dark arguments. The light-theme branch is now `lightness: 30%` (the dark shade), and the dark-theme branch is `lightness: 70%` (the light shade) — the exact opposite of every other conversion in this PR. The matching desktop rule in `desktop/modal.scss` correctly uses `70%` / `30%`. In light themes on mobile, the custom-message hint text will appear as a dark shade instead of the intended lighter grey, hurting readability.

title: Lightness values transposed for .topic-meta-data h5 a
body: Inside `.topic-meta-data h5 a` the original CSS was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);` (a darker shade used for bold meta text). The patch changed it to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%));`. Because `dark-light-choose(A, B)` returns `A` in the light theme, the rendered color in the default (light) theme is now `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` instead of the original 30%, making this bold link much lighter than intended in light mode. The light branch should still be `$primary` at 30%, e.g. `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

title: .group-member-info .name color regressed in light theme
body: Inside `.group-member-info .name` the original CSS was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);` (a dimmer shade of primary text). The patch changed it to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));`. Since `dark-light-choose` evaluates to its first argument in the light theme, the rendered color is now `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` rather than 30%, visibly lightening group-member names on user pages in the default theme. Should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))` to preserve the original light-theme color.

title: .custom-message-length color regressed in light theme
body: Inside `.custom-message-length` the original CSS was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%);` (a lighter, less prominent helper text in modals). The patch changed it to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%));`. Because `dark-light-choose(A, B)` returns `A` in the light theme, the rendered color is now `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` instead of the original 70%, making the “characters remaining” helper much darker / more prominent than intended on mobile. Should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))` to preserve the original light-theme color.

title: .topic-map h3 color regressed in light theme
body: Inside `.topic-map h3` the original CSS was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%);` (a very dark, prominent heading). The patch changed it to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));`. Since `dark-light-choose(A, B)` returns `A` in the light theme, the rendered color is now `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` instead of the original 20%, dramatically lightening the topic-map headings on mobile. Should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))` to preserve the original light-theme color.

title: .group-member-info .name color regressed in light theme
body: Inside `.group-member-info .name` the original CSS was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);` (a darker shade for muted group member text). Since `dark-light-choose` resolves to its first argument in the light theme, the rendered color is now `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` instead of the original 30%, lightening group-member names on the mobile user page in the default theme. Should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))` to preserve the original light-theme color.

title: Lightness value swapped: 30% became 70% for $primary
body: The original rule `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` was changed to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. The fix is to swap the lightness arguments: `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

title: Lightness value changed: 20% became 50% for $primary
body: The original rule `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` for `.topic-map h3` was changed to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The $primary lightness went from 20% to 50%, so the light-theme topic-map heading (an element with intentionally darker text against a light background) becomes much lighter than before, hurting contrast. The intent of the PR was to add a dark-theme branch, not to alter the light-theme color.

body: Inside `.user-main .user-stream .group-member-info .name`, the original `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` was replaced with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme branch now uses 50% lightness instead of 30%, lightening the group-member name text in the light theme. The $primary lightness should be preserved (30%) and only the dark-theme branch ($secondary) should be added.

title: Lightness value swapped: 70% became 30% for $primary
body: The original rule `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` for `.custom-message-length` was replaced with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. title: Lightness value changed: 30% became 50% for $primary
body: Inside `.user-main .user-stream .group-member-info .name` (mobile), the original `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` was replaced with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. title: totalPages off-by-one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
body: The totalPages computed property uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100 members with limit 50) this returns 3 instead of the correct 2, so showingLast stays false on the real last page and the admin can navigate to an empty trailing page (page 3 of 2). Replace with Math.ceil(user_count / limit) (keeping the user_count == 0 guard) so the pager reflects the actual number of pages.

title: Stray inside the group members table
body:
There is a stray closing tag inside the , sitting between and {{/each}}. A cannot be a direct child of a table outside cell context, so this is invalid HTML; browsers will attempt to repair the DOM, which can shift rendered elements and break the table styling that this PR is also touching. The tag is clearly leftover from an earlier template shape (the surrounding
wrapper was removed in this diff but the close tag was not). Remove the
.

title: add_members silently drops unknown or whitespace-padded usernames and still reports success
body: In the add_members action the usernames.split(",").each loop silently ignores names that don't resolve via User.find_by_username, and the split does no whitespace stripping, so an entry like " bob" (with a leading space) won't match the stored username and is also dropped. The action then renders success_json regardless of how many names were actually accepted, so the admin sees success even when every supplied username was invalid. Strip each username before lookup, and either reject the request or include the not-found names in the response so the caller can tell which entries failed.

title: add_members crashes with NoMethodError when usernames is sent as an array
body: params.require(:usernames) accepts whatever shape is sent; if a client posts usernames[]=alice&usernames[]=bob (the standard Rails array-param convention), params[:usernames] is an Array. The subsequent usernames.split(",") then raises NoMethodError because Array has no split method, returning a 500 to the caller. Coerce the param to a string before splitting (e.g. Array(params[:usernames]).flatten.join(",")) or return a 400 when the value is not a String.

title: save error handler throws when the server returns an empty or non-JSON error body
body: The save action's rejection handler does var message = $.parseJSON(e.responseText).errors; with no guard. When the server returns an empty body, an HTML error page from a proxy (502/504), or any non-JSON content, $.parseJSON throws. The throw escapes the rejection handler and surfaces as an unhandled promise rejection, the bootbox alert is never shown, and the failure is invisible to the admin. Wrap the parse in a try/catch (or check that e.responseText is non-empty and parseable) and fall back to a generic message such as I18n.t('generic_error') when parsing fails.

title: addMembers action carries an unresolved TODO to clear the input
body: The addMembers action still contains the comment // TODO: should clear the input but does not implement it. After a successful add the user-selector continues to show the just-typed usernames, so an admin who wants to add more members has to manually delete the previously typed list. Either reset this.set('usernames', null) (and the bound input) after the AJAX call resolves, or remove the TODO comment.

title: Admin member routes put :id in params but controllers expect :group_id
body: The new routes `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` and `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` are declared inside `resources :groups, constraints: AdminConstraint.new do ... end`. With that placement Rails treats them as member actions, so the URLs are `DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members` and `PUT /admin/groups/:id/members` and the group id is exposed as `params[:id]`. However, `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` (line 66) and `#remove_member` (line 85) both call `params.require(:group_id).to_i`, and the routes never populate `params[:group_id]`. Every AJAX call from the new admin UI to add or remove a member will therefore raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing: param not found: group_id` and return a 400 error, so the new add/remove member functionality does not work. The controller specs pass because `xhr :put/:delete, :add_members/:remove_member, group_id: ...` bypasses routing and injects `group_id` directly into params. Fix by changing the controllers to read `params[:id]`, or by wrapping the routes in `member do ... end`, or by naming the resource param explicitly (e.g. `param: :group_id`).

title: totalPages formula overcounts when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
body: The `totalPages` computed property returns `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. For `user_count = 50` and `limit = 50` this yields `1 + 1 = 2`, but there is only a single page of members. As a result `showingLast` is `false` while the admin is on the only existing page, so the "next" anchor stays enabled. Clicking it sets `offset = user_count` and triggers `findMembers`, which then requests a page that returns `members: []`. The page indicator shows "1/2" with no members and the admin must click "previous" to see them. The correct formula is `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

title: add_members does not strip whitespace, so usernames with surrounding spaces are silently dropped
body: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` does not strip whitespace before calling `User.find_by_username(username)`. If the admin types "alice, bob" (note the space after the comma) or pastes a comma-separated list with spaces or line breaks, `User.find_by_username(" bob")` returns nil and that user is silently skipped. The endpoint still returns `success_json`, so the admin sees a green success state even when only some (or none) of the listed users were added, with no indication that anything was missed. Strip whitespace (and skip blank entries) before the lookup, e.g. `username.strip` and `next if username.empty?`.

title: remove_member deletes the join record before group.save, leaving validation errors in an inconsistent state
body: `group.users.delete(user_id)` on a `has_many :through` association deletes the join record from the database immediately. The subsequent `group.save` only persists Group-model attribute changes, not the membership change. If Group validation fails (e.g. a uniqueness validator on `name`), the controller responds with `render_json_error(group)`, but the membership removal has already been committed. The client therefore sees an error response while the member has actually been removed from the group. Either drop the `group.save` (the membership change already succeeded) or perform the deletion and the save inside a single transaction so they commit or fail together.

title: add_members reads params[:group_id] but route only exposes :id
body: The new add_members action does `Group.find(params.require(:group_id).to_i)`, but the route in config/routes.rb defines `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` as a member route inside `resources :groups`, which only populates `params[:id]`, not `params[:group_id]`. The client in app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js sends `PUT /admin/groups/${group.id}/members.json`, so `params[:group_id]` will be nil and `params.require(:group_id)` will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` in production. The action should read `params[:id]` (or the route should be expressed so that the ID arrives as `group_id`).

title: remove_member reads params[:group_id] but route only exposes :id
body: Same root cause as the add_members finding above: `remove_member` reads `params.require(:group_id)`, while the DELETE member route only sets `params[:id]`. The JS sends `DELETE /admin/groups/${group.id}/members.json?user_id=...`, so `params[:group_id]` is nil and the action will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` in production, breaking member removal.

title: totalPages off-by-one for exact multiples, exposing an empty last page
body: `totalPages` returns `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. For user_count=50, limit=50 it returns 2 instead of 1; for user_count=100, limit=50 it returns 3 instead of 2. The `next` action uses `showingLast = propertyEqual(currentPage, totalPages)` to decide when to stop, so with the inflated totalPages the user can click Next past the last real page and `findMembers` will be invoked with `offset == user_count`, returning an empty result page that is still displayed. Should use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (or `Math.floor((user_count - 1) / limit) + 1`).

title: remove_member test uses wrong HTTP verb (PUT vs DELETE)
body: The test 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' uses `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42`, but the route is defined as `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`. RSpec controller specs invoke actions directly and largely ignore the verb, so this test happens to pass via the automatic-group short-circuit, but it does not exercise the real DELETE route and would not catch the param-name mismatch above. Use `xhr :delete, :remove_member, ...` (and ideally drive the test through routing).

title: Tests pass group_id directly, bypassing routing and hiding the route bug
body: Every new test passes `group_id: <id>` (or `:user_id`) directly as a hash parameter, so RSpec never goes through the route table and `params[:group_id]` is supplied even though the route only sets `params[:id]`. That is why the `params.require(:group_id)` bug appears to work in the controller spec but will fail in production. Switch to `id:` and/or add a request/integration spec that hits the real URL.

title: group.users.delete(user_id) replaces the safer group.remove(user) pattern
body: The previous implementation used `group.remove(user)` to drop just the membership. The new code calls `group.users.delete(user_id)` with a raw integer. Behaviour depends on the association: for `has_many` without `through` Rails may resolve the id and destroy the User record; for `has_many :through`/`HABTM` only the join row is removed, but the internal lookup raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` if the id does not exist — losing the previous silent no-op for unknown users and risking a 500. Prefer `group.users.find_by(id: user_id)&.delete` (or rescue membership), and keep the pattern consistent with `add_members` which still uses `group.add(user)`.

title: add_members silently drops stripped or unknown usernames
body: `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` neither strips whitespace nor skips blanks, so a value like `"alice, bob,carol"` (space after the first comma) tries `User.find_by_username(" bob")` and silently fails to add that user. Additionally, unknown usernames are silently ignored with no error in the response, so the admin gets a 200 success even when none of the supplied names were applied. At minimum strip each entry and skip blanks, and consider returning the list of unrecognised names so the UI can warn.

title: findMembers returns undefined when group has no name
body: `if (Em.isEmpty(this.get('name'))) { return ; }` returns `undefined` rather than a resolved promise. The two current callers (admin_group_route and group-members route) ignore the return value, but any future caller chaining `.then(...)` would throw `TypeError: Cannot read property 'then' of undefined`. Return `Ember.RSVP.resolve()` for consistency with the previous version that returned `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])`.

title: Group#addMembers / #removeMember have no error handler
body: The `Discourse.ajax` call in `addMembers` (and `removeMember`) registers only a `.then` success handler that triggers `self.findMembers()`. There is no rejection handler, so a 4xx/5xx response (group validation failure, network error, or the route bug above) is swallowed and the admin sees no feedback that the operation actually failed. Add a second argument to `.then` (or `.catch`) that surfaces a `bootbox.alert` like the save action does.

title: FallbackLocaleList inherits from Hash but only overrides []
body: FallbackLocaleList extends Hash and overrides only []. Other Hash methods (keys, values, each, merge, empty?, etc.) inherited from Hash return empty-Hash behavior, which is inconsistent with [] returning a non-empty array for any locale. If any other code (including future changes or plugins) inspects I18n.fallbacks via these methods, it will get unexpected results. A plain object exposing only the methods actually used (or delegation) would be safer than inheriting from Hash.

title: Translation cache key omits the fallback chain
body: The translate cache key is "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}". It does not include the fallback chain used by I18n::Backend::Fallbacks. With localization fallbacks now in effect, a translation that is missing in config.locale will be resolved through FallbackLocaleList#[] (which incorporates SiteSetting.default_locale). If SiteSetting.default_locale changes at runtime (it is admin-editable), entries cached under the previous fallback chain will continue to be served for the new chain, returning stale translations. The cache key should incorporate the resolved fallback locales (e.g. I18n.fallbacks[config.locale]) so changes to default_locale or any other fallback source invalidate the relevant entries.

title: No tests for new localization fallback feature
body: This PR adds a new server-side localization fallback mechanism (custom FallbackLocaleList, ensure_loaded! chain, integration with the patched I18n translate accelerator), but no specs are included in the diff. Regression risks include: (1) FallbackLocaleList#[] ordering/duplication with current_user.effective_locale vs SiteSetting.default_locale vs :en; (2) Pluralization/Fallbacks module composition when both are mixed into I18n::Backend::Simple; (3) thread-safety of ensure_loaded! running inside a per-request before_filter that touches @loaded_locales and LOAD_MUTEX; (4) cache key stability under fallback (translate_no_cache returning fallback-locale values while the LRU cache is keyed only by config.locale). A feature of this scope touching the I18n initialization order needs explicit coverage before merge.

title: FallbackLocaleList#[] crashes if SiteSetting.default_locale is nil
body: FallbackLocaleList#[] unconditionally calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym and embeds the result in the fallback chain. If SiteSetting.default_locale is nil or an empty string (e.g. a half-applied migration, a misconfigured SiteSetting row, or a unit test that stubs the setting), this raises NoMethodError or returns [:en] without the site locale, silently degrading fallback behavior for every request that goes through the before_filter. The method should defend against nil/blank values (treat them as :en or skip), or the initializer should validate SiteSetting.default_locale at boot.

title: FallbackLocaleList is a Hash subclass but only [] is overridden
body: FallbackLocaleList < Hash overrides [] to return an Array, but inherits Hash semantics for everything else (keys, each, merge, []=, store, dig, etc.) while the underlying hash stays empty. I18n::Backend::Fallbacks and other code may call e.g. I18n.fallbacks[locale] = [...] or iterate keys; those calls will silently no-op or return empty results, masking configuration mistakes. Additionally, since the override is not synchronized, two threads can compute the fallback list concurrently while reading SiteSetting.default_locale - benign today but a footgun if the override ever grows. Either delegate to a plain object exposing only the contract Fallbacks needs, or override the full Hash surface and freeze the per-locale list.

title: Fallback locales are force-loaded on every request via before_filter
body: ApplicationController#set_locale ends with I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!, which calls I18n.ensure_loaded! for every locale in the user's fallback chain on every request. While @loaded_locales.include? short-circuits after the first request, the very first request after boot (and after each I18n.reload!) must parse all fallback yml files inside the request path, inflating TTFB and competing for LOAD_MUTEX with concurrent requests. The fallback translations only need to be loaded once at boot (or lazily before the first translate for that locale); the before_filter should not be the trigger. Consider moving ensure_loaded! out of the request path or gating it behind a once-per-process flag.

title: ensure_loaded! reads @loaded_locales outside LOAD_MUTEX
body: The new ensure_loaded! does @loaded_locales ||= [] and @loaded_locales.include?(locale) without holding LOAD_MUTEX, then delegates to load_locale which does take the mutex. If I18n.reload! is called concurrently with ensure_loaded!, the include? check can race against @loaded_locales = [], causing ensure_loaded! to skip loading translations that reload! just cleared. Functionally load_locale will still reload inside the mutex, but the pattern is racy and the dedicated ensure_loaded! wrapper is the obvious place to add a guard if it ever becomes load-bearing. Worth tightening before this method is used per-request.

title: Fallback ensure_loaded! runs on every request
body: The new `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` call in `set_locale` runs for every action via the `before_filter`. It allocates a new fallback array via `FallbackLocaleList#[]` on each call and then invokes `I18n.ensure_loaded!` for each entry, which performs an unsynchronized `Array#include?` against `@loaded_locales` inside the I18n translation path. For the common case where the user locale equals the default (and `:en` is already loaded), this allocates an array and does redundant checks on a hot path that runs for every request. Consider memoizing the resolved fallback list per locale or skipping the call when all entries are known to be loaded.

title: New i18n fallback behavior added without any specs
body: The PR introduces a new `FallbackLocaleList` class with custom `[]` and `ensure_loaded!` methods, deletes the standalone `pluralization.rb` initializer, replaces the default Rails fallback chain, and changes fallback semantics for every translated string on the server — yet no test files appear in the diff. This change deserves specs covering: fallback list contents and ordering for combinations of user locale / `SiteSetting.default_locale` / `:en`; deduplication when `locale` equals the default or is itself `:en`; `ensure_loaded!` idempotency; and that translations still resolve correctly through the custom list (including missing-key fallback to English).

title: ensure_loaded! check is outside LOAD_MUTEX
body: The newly added `ensure_loaded!` does `@loaded_locales.include?(locale)` outside any mutex and then calls `load_locale`, which acquires `LOAD_MUTEX`. While `load_locale` re-checks `@loaded_locales.include?(locale)` under the mutex (so correctness is preserved), the outer include check is a TOCTOU pattern: multiple concurrent threads can race past it and redundantly contend on `LOAD_MUTEX`, doing duplicate Array scans and (in the worst case) holding the mutex while reading translation files. The `@loaded_locales ||= []` initialization is also unsynchronized (harmless here since both branches would assign empty arrays). Move the include check inside `LOAD_MUTEX.synchronize` (e.g., inline the load logic) to avoid wasted work under contention.

title: FallbackLocaleList extends Hash unnecessarily
body: `class FallbackLocaleList < Hash` inherits from Hash but the overridden `[]` never reads from Hash storage and no entries are ever written via `store=`/`[]=`. As a result, Hash methods such as `keys`, `values`, `each`, `empty?`, and `fetch` expose the empty underlying Hash state while `[]` returns a generated array — two contradictory views of the same object that will surprise future maintainers. The class also accepts only a single positional `locale`, whereas `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks#[]` accepts splat locales; if any plugin or i18n version ever passes multiple locales here it will raise `ArgumentError`. A plain class (or one whose `[]` takes `*locales`) would be both clearer and safer.

title: Stale denial cache can block legitimate access for up to 30s after a permission grant
body: The newly introduced permDenialCache is consulted at the very start of Service.Check (lines 116-121) and short-circuits to Allowed=false before the permCache or the database are touched. There is no invalidation tied to permission changes (grants, role/team membership changes, deletions). Once any (namespace, userUID, action, name, parent) tuple has produced a deny response, that deny is cached for shortCacheTTL (30s) and will be returned for every subsequent request, even if the underlying database now grants the permission. This is a regression introduced by the PR and works against its stated goal of letting users access newly created resources: any prior deny that happened to land in the cache for the same (name, parent) tuple will hold the new permission back for up to 30s. Consider invalidating the denial entry whenever a permission grant or revocation affects the cached tuple, or use a much shorter TTL so the cache behaves as a brief burst guard rather than a 30s negative answer.

title: Test does not actually verify that denial cache overrides a permissive permCache
body: In TestService_CacheCheck / 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry', the permCache is seeded with map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false} and the comment says 'Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked'. With the value false, checkPermission already returns false for that scope, so the subtest passes whether or not the permCache is consulted and does not demonstrate the precedence it claims. To actually verify that the denial cache overrides an otherwise-permissive permCache, the seeded value should be true (e.g. map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": true}).

title: No test covers a stale denial cache blocking access after a permission grant
body: The denial cache can hold a deny entry for up to 30s after a user was last denied for a (name, parent, action) tuple. There is no test that asserts (and therefore no guard against) the regression scenario: a prior deny is cached for the user, but the underlying store now grants the permission, and Service.Check still returns Allowed=false because the denial cache short-circuits before the new fallback-to-DB path. Adding such a test would either confirm the 30s window is acceptable, or catch it if invalidation is later added.

title: PermDenialCache can block legitimate access after permission grant or resource recreation
body: The permDenialCache is consulted at the very start of Check() (lines 116-121) and short-circuits to Allowed:false without ever touching the DB or the permCache. The denial is written at lines 153-155 whenever checkPermission returns false, with a 30-second TTL (shortCacheTTL). Because the denial entry is never invalidated when permissions change or resources are created, the following scenarios keep a freshly-authorised user locked out for up to 30 seconds: (1) user A previously failed a check on resource X (e.g. before X existed or before the grant), the entry is cached, then X is created with A as owner / A is added to a team that grants access — the next Check still hits the denial key and denies; (2) the same happens when a resource is deleted and later recreated with the same UID under new ownership; (3) a race where A asks for X before the create-grant transaction commits — A is denied, the denial is cached, and once the transaction commits A still cannot access X until the entry expires. This re-introduces precisely the 'creator cannot access the dashboard/folder they just created' symptom this PR is supposed to fix. Consider only caching denials for resources known to exist, invalidating the entry on permission change, or dropping the TTL drastically.

title: List does not fall back to DB when the permCache is stale, leaving newly created items invisible
body: In the new List() the only DB fallback is on a complete cache miss (getCachedIdentityPermissions returns cache.ErrNotFound). If the user already has a populated permCache for the action, List trusts it as-is and never requeries. Compare with Check() (lines 123-136) which now requeries when the cached scopeMap does not contain the requested name/folder. The PR's stated goal — 'dash/folder creator can't access the dashboard/folder that they've just created' — is therefore only fixed for Check; a user who navigates to the dashboards list immediately after creating a dashboard will not see the new entry until the permCache expires (30s). Either List should also requery when the requested name/folder is absent from the cached scopes, or at minimum the dashboard/folder create path should invalidate or refresh the relevant permCache entries.

title: Test comment claims 'allow access' but the value is set to deny
body: In TestService_CacheCheck / 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry' the comment reads '// Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked' immediately above `s.permCache.Set(ctx, userPermCacheKey(...), map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false})`. The map value is false, so the permCache entry would deny access if it were consulted (the check is `if scopeMap[t.scope(req.Name)]`). The test still passes because the denial cache is hit first, but the comment misrepresents what the permCache entry contains and could mislead anyone reading it. Either set the value to true (to match the comment) or rewrite the comment to say something like '// permCache entry that would allow access — never consulted because the denial cache wins'.

title: Denial cache entries are never invalidated, so previously-denied resources stay denied for up to 30s after a permission grant
body: After a Check returns Allowed=false, the code calls s.permDenialCache.Set(ctx, permDenialKey, true). Nothing in this PR (or anywhere else visible in the diff) ever calls Delete on permDenialCache, so entries only expire via the 30-second TTL. Once a (namespace, user, action, name, folder) tuple has been denied, the user will keep receiving Allowed=false on that exact tuple for up to 30 seconds — even after a permission grant (role assignment, dashboard share, etc.) makes them eligible. This is a regression relative to the pre-PR flow, where a re-check after a grant would consult the DB and return the updated permission; the new denial cache short-circuits that re-check. As a consequence, the same user with the same role can see inconsistent behavior: a brand-new dashboard they have never asked about returns Allowed=true (no prior denial entry), while a dashboard they queried once before the grant returns Allowed=false until the entry expires. The denial cache should be invalidated (e.g., on role/permission changes or dashboard creation/sharing) so grants take effect promptly.

title: Denial cache key uses raw userUID while permission cache uses the resolved UID
body: The denial cache key is built from checkReq.UserUID, the raw identifier parsed from the request subject by validateSubject. The permission cache key in getCachedIdentityPermissions is built from userIdentifiers.UID, the value returned by GetUserIdentifiers. GetUserIdentifiers treats a purely-numeric userUID as a user ID and resolves it to the user's canonical UID (typically a non-numeric string). For the same user, denial cache entries therefore live under one identifier and permission cache entries under another, so the two caches never share state. Concretely, if a user is identified by numeric ID '123' the denial cache is keyed by '123', while the permission cache is keyed by the resolved UID (e.g., 'abc456'); a denial cached under '123' will never block a request that arrives with subject 'user:abc456' (and vice versa). The denial cache key should be built from the same resolved UID that the permission cache uses.

title: permissionCacheUsage metric conflates denial-cache hits with permission-cache hits
body: When the denial cache hits, Check increments permissionCacheUsage with label value 'true'. The same metric and label are used later for genuine permission-cache hits (line 132). The 'true' label therefore no longer means 'permission cache hit' — it means 'either permission cache or denial cache hit'. Existing dashboards/alerts built on this metric will silently change meaning after this PR. The denial cache hit should be recorded under a distinct metric name or a distinct label (e.g., cache='denial' vs cache='permission').

title: No regression test for a stale denial cache entry after a permission grant
body: TestService_CacheCheck covers a denial cache hit that has just been written (subtest 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry'), but it does not cover the regression scenario where a denial cache entry sits for the full 30-second window while the underlying permission is granted (e.g., via role assignment or dashboard share). Given that permDenialCache has no invalidation path anywhere in the change, a test should pin down what happens when a previously-denied Check is re-run after the DB now grants the permission; with the current code the response is still Allowed=false for up to 30 seconds, and there is no test that would catch the resulting regression.

title: Test 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry' uses a scope value of false but its comment claims it allows access
body: The new subtest primes permCache with map[string]bool{'dashboards:uid:dash1': false} and the inline comment says this 'allow[s] access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked'. A scope map entry with value false does not represent a granted scope — the map is effectively empty for the requested resource, so it does not actually demonstrate the intended precedence (denial cache over an allowed scope). To demonstrate that the denial cache takes precedence over a granted scope, the entry should be set to true (map[string]bool{'dashboards:uid:dash1': true}); otherwise the test would pass even if the permCache lookup was silently dropped from the Check path.

title: Missing key prop on <GrafanaRuleListItem> in mapped list
body: In the `.map((ruleWithOrigin) => { ... })` body of FilterViewResults, the `case 'grafana'` branch renders <GrafanaRuleListItem> without a `key` prop, while the sibling branches (`case 'datasource'` and the default branch) set `key={key}`. Because the result is returned from inside a switch inside a `.map()` callback returning JSX, React requires a stable key on each top-level list item. Without it React will emit 'Each child in a list should have a unique key' warnings at runtime, and worse, the component instances/state for reordered/added/removed Grafana rules may be reused incorrectly, leading to stale UI (e.g. wrong rule metadata or stale expansion/popover state) when the filtered list changes. Fix: add `key={key}` to the <GrafanaRuleListItem> element so it matches the other branches.

title: useAllRulerRuleAbilities hardcodes isFederated=false, regressing federated rule immutability
body: In `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` (line ~246) the federation check was changed from `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` to a hardcoded `const isFederated = false;` with a TODO. This hook is still used by `useRulerRuleAbility(s)` and therefore consumed outside the list view (e.g. RuleDetails/RuleViewer via RuleActionsButtons/AlertRuleMenu) where `rulerRule` IS defined. Federated rule groups (a Mimir feature) are supposed to be treated as immutable: their rules cannot be removed or edited by a tenant. With `isFederated=false`, federated rules now report Update/Delete abilities as supported and (depending on permissions) allowed, so the Delete menu item in AlertRuleMenu can render for federated Mimir rules and may cause DELETE requests that the API rejects. At minimum the rule is shown as editable/removable when it should not be, breaking existing RBAC guarantees of the rule details/viewer pages.

title: canPause is computed via OR but Pause menu item is gated on rulerRule being defined
body: AlertRuleMenu now computes `canPause = (pauseSupported && pauseAllowed) || (grafanaPauseSupported && grafanaPauseAllowed)`, so for a Grafana rule in the new list view (where `rulerRule` is undefined) canPause is correctly driven by the GrafanaPromRule abilities. However the Pause <MenuItemPauseRule> is rendered behind the additional expression `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) && groupIdentifier.groupOrigin === 'grafana'`, both of which are false when rulerRule is undefined. Result: the Pause menu item is never shown in the list view even though the ability system reports the user can pause. Either the render gate needs to be updated (e.g. use the grafana prom rule) or the gate should be removed if Pause cannot actually be performed from the list view; otherwise ability/capability state and UI will diverge.

title: Brittle exact menu-item count assertion in menu visibility test
body: The 'should render correct menu actions when More button is clicked' test asserts `expect(menuItems.length).toBe(4)` exactly. Because menu contents depend on abilities (Pause, Silence, Declare Incident, Duplicate, Copy link, Export, Delete, extension links, sub-menu children, dividers), any future addition of a menu item (e.g. re-enabling Pause without a ruler rule, declaring incident in dev, or restoring an extension link) will silently break the test or mask real regressions. Prefer asserting presence/absence of each expected item individually and omit the exact-count check, or factor the assertion via a helper that enumerates expected vs forbidden items.

title: Stray '// duplicate' comment with no meaning
body: Line 289 contains `const { isEditable, isRemovable, loading } = useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable(rule); // duplicate`. The trailing `// duplicate` does not document anything specific (it isn't a TODO, doesn't reference an issue, and isn't a useful annotation) and reads as dev noise. Remove or replace it with a meaningful comment to avoid future confusion.

title: Delete menu item never renders in the list view
body: The Delete menu is gated by `canDelete && rulerRule && (...)`. In the list view the consumer (`GrafanaRuleListItem`/`RuleActionsButtons.V2`) only passes `promRule`, so `rulerRule` is `undefined`. The new `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` evaluates `canDelete` to `true` for users with delete permission on Grafana folders, but the render guard short-circuits to `false` and the Delete option is hidden anyway. Effectively users will not be able to delete Grafana-managed rules from the list view even though the abilities hook reports they can.

title: Pause menu item never renders in the list view
body: The Pause menu item is gated by `canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) && groupIdentifier.groupOrigin === 'grafana'`. In the list view `rulerRule` is `undefined`, so `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(undefined)` returns `false` and the Pause option is hidden even though `canPause` (computed via `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`) may be true. Users lose the ability to pause Grafana-managed rules from the list view.

title: Silence action does nothing in the list view
body: When the user clicks Silence, `handleSilence` sets `showSilenceDrawer=true`. The drawer is rendered only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer`, but `rule` is `undefined` in the list view. So `showSilenceDrawer` flips to `true` and nothing visible happens. The grafana-only `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` was never made to accept `promRule`, so silence is silently broken for the list view, despite `canSilence` evaluating `true` via the new abilities.

title: Missing React key prop on <GrafanaRuleListItem>
body: When migrating from `GrafanaRuleLoader` to `GrafanaRuleListItem`, the `key={key}` prop was dropped from the Grafana branch of the list switch (the datasource branch still passes `key={key}`). React will warn about missing keys in the filtered list and, more importantly, component state (e.g. menu open/close, hook subscriptions) will not be preserved correctly across reorders and unmounts because React falls back to using array index.

title: Creating and Deleting transient states no longer rendered
body: The previous version fetched both Prometheus and Ruler groups and used `matchRules` to distinguish three cases: rules present in both (normal), rules only in ruler (rendered with `RuleOperation.Creating`), and rules only in Prometheus (rendered with `RuleOperation.Deleting`). This PR removes the Ruler fetch and the entire matching logic, so rules that are in the middle of being created/deleted will silently appear as ordinary active rules, with no Creating/Deleting badge. The `operation={RuleOperation.Creating}` and `RuleOperationListItem` props are still accepted by `GrafanaRuleListItem` but nothing ever computes them now.

title: Tests for Creating/Deleting transient state were deleted
body: The original `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx` covered `should render rule with url and creating state when only ruler rule exists` and `should render delete rule operation list item when only prom rule exists`, plus three unit tests for `matchRules`. All have been removed in this PR. Since the deletion of those behaviors is a regression risk (see the previous finding), these tests should be retained (or replaced with new tests asserting the new equivalent behavior) to prevent re-introducing the bug.

title: Stale `// duplicate` comment in useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities
body: Line 289 in `useAbilities.ts` reads: `const { isEditable, isRemovable, loading } = useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable(rule); // duplicate`. The trailing `// duplicate` looks like a leftover TODO/scratchpad marker. It is meaningless to future readers and should be removed or replaced with an explanatory comment.

title: Redundant triple mock reset in beforeEach
body: The `beforeEach` block calls `jest.clearAllMocks(); jest.restoreAllMocks(); jest.resetAllMocks();` sequentially. Calling all three is redundant (each fully resets call/spy state) and can mask the intent of which reset is actually needed. Pick the single appropriate call. Also, because the mocks are then re-set up immediately with default returns, the order/selection matters: if `clearAllMocks` is removed, the previously installed `mockImplementation` from the previous test would persist for unwired mocks, potentially producing subtle cross-test contamination.

title: Missing `key` prop on GrafanaRuleListItem inside rules.map()
body: Inside `rules.map(...)`, the `case 'grafana'` branch now renders `<GrafanaRuleListItem .../>` without a `key` prop, while `case 'datasource'` and the `default` branch both pass `key={key}`. The pre-PR code wrapped `GrafanaRuleLoader` with `key={key}`; that key was dropped in the rewrite. This triggers React's "each child in a list should have a unique key prop" warning in production and can cause incorrect list diffing when items are added, removed or reordered. Fix by passing `key={key}` to the `GrafanaRuleListItem` element.

title: Pause/Delete menu items in list view never render even when permission exists
body: `AlertRuleMenu` now computes the abilities as `(ruler ok) || (grafana prom ok)`, with a comment that says this is precisely to support the alert list view where ruler requests are removed. However the actual rendering of Pause and Delete is still gated on a defined `rulerRule`: `{canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) && groupIdentifier.groupOrigin === 'grafana' && <MenuItemPauseRule rule={rulerRule} .../>}` and `{canDelete && rulerRule && ... onClick={() => handleDelete(rulerRule, ...)}}`. In the list-view flow (`FilterView` → `GrafanaRuleListItem` → `RuleActionsButtons.V2` → `AlertRuleMenu`) `rulerRule` is `undefined`, so even when `canPause`/`canDelete` are correctly `true` via the new grafana-prom path, neither menu item renders. This is an incomplete refactor and a real functional regression for pause/delete of Grafana-managed rules from the list view.

title: Silence drawer in the V2 buttons component cannot open from the list view
body: The Silence drawer is rendered as `{rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer && <SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer rulerRule={rule} .../>}`. In the list-view flow `GrafanaRuleListItem` passes only `promRule` (no `rule` / `RulerRuleDTO`) to `RuleActionsButtons.V2`, so `rule` is `undefined` and the `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule` type guard returns false. The corresponding Silence menu item inside `AlertRuleMenu` is similarly gated on a defined `rulerRule`, so the user has no path to silence a Grafana rule from the alert list/group view. Either provide an API path that can act on a `GrafanaPromRuleDTO` alone, or remove the Silence entry and explicitly document the limitation, before merging.

title: Rule view link no longer carries a `returnTo` URL parameter (behavior change vs old loader)
body: The deleted `GrafanaRuleLoader` built the rule's href with `createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view', { returnTo })`, using the `createReturnTo()` helper, so the detail view could breadcrumb back to the list/folder and persist the navigation context. The new `GrafanaRuleListItem` builds it as `createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view')` with no options, dropping `returnTo` entirely. Users entering the rule view from the new list/group view lose the prior back-navigation behavior. If returnTo is no longer needed (because of a new navigation model), say so explicitly and audit other callers; otherwise preserve it here for parity with the previous behavior.

title: Tests do not exercise the V2/list-view abilities path that loses Pause/Delete/Silence
body: All delete/duplicate/edit/per-menu tests in `RulesTable.test.tsx` (and the `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx` 'should render correct menu actions' test) drive the abilities through `RulesTable` / `GrafanaGroupLoader`, which still forwards a `RulerRuleDTO` to the menu/buttons. That means the `rulerRule` / `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` rendering gates are still satisfied in those tests, so the regression documented in the AlertRuleMenu and RuleActionsButtons.V2 findings is not exercised at all and the menu-item counts happen to pass for the wrong reason. Add a focused test that mounts `GrafanaRuleListItem` (or `RuleActionsButtons.V2`) with only `promRule` set, and assert whether Pause/Silence/Delete should or should not appear — before this is merged, the question is currently unverified.

title: $__range queries are no longer excluded from splitting
body: The new `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...))` runs before the `partition(... , query => !querySupportsSplitting(query))` step. `querySupportsSplitting` relies on `isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` to keep queries that contain `$__range` out of the time-split batches (the existing comment even explains that splitting such queries is incorrect because `$__range` would then be resolved against a sub-range). Because `applyTemplateVariables` resolves template variables and global variables (including `$__range`/`$__range_s`/`$__from`/`$__to`) on the frontend with the FULL time range, the `$__range` token disappears from `expr` before the check runs. The `isQueryWithRangeVariable` predicate then returns false and the query gets partitioned into `normalQueries` and split into 1-day chunks, each chunk receiving the full range baked into the previously-interpolated `$__range`. The result is wrong data: e.g. `count_over_time({a="b"}[$__range])` over a 2-day dashboard range becomes `count_over_time({a="b"}[2d])` applied to a 1-day sub-range. The check needs to run on the original (pre-interpolation) expression, or `$__range` must be excluded from this frontend interpolation.

title: Stale comment about $__range interpolation location
body: The comment in `querySupportsSplitting` says `$__range` is "interpolated on the backend with the split timeRange". After this PR the variable is interpolated on the frontend (`datasource.applyTemplateVariables`) with the full timeRange before the splitting decision, so the justification given in the comment no longer matches the code path. If the exclusion is still intended, the comment should be updated to describe the new ordering (check pre-interpolation expr, or skip `$__range` in the interpolation step); otherwise the check should be removed entirely.

title: Templates are interpolated once in runShardSplitQuery and again inside every nested runSplitQuery call
body: `runShardSplitQuery` now calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables` on every non-hidden, non-empty target and passes the interpolated list to `splitQueriesByStreamShard`. Each shard group later builds a `subRequest` from these already-interpolated targets and calls `runSplitQuery(datasource, subRequest, ...)`. Inside `runSplitQuery`, the new `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters))` re-runs template interpolation on the same queries. The test `'Interpolates queries before running'` codifies this by asserting `applyTemplateVariables` is called 5 times for a single-target request (1 + 4 shard groups). Beyond the wasted work, if `applyTemplateVariables` is not strictly idempotent (e.g. it touches scopedVars, fires telemetry, mutates caches, or escalates unknown variables to errors) the second pass can change behavior or throw. Either `runSplitQuery` should be told the targets are already interpolated (skip flag / do not re-apply), or `runShardSplitQuery` should defer interpolation to the inner `runSplitQuery` call.

title: No regression test for $__range queries being excluded from splitting
body: The new `'Interpolates queries before execution'` test only covers `$__auto` and `$step` interpolation. There is no test asserting that a query containing `$__range` (or `$__range_s`) is still routed into `nonSplittingQueries` and never time-split. Given that this PR moves the `querySupportsSplitting` decision to after interpolation, this is exactly the regression a test should pin down. Without it, the existing exclusion documented by the `querySupportsSplitting` comment can silently break (see the corresponding finding in `querySplitting.ts`).

title: Assertion bakes in the redundant interpolation count
body: The updated `'Interpolates queries before running'` test asserts `expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` for a single-target request, which is exactly the count produced by interpolating once in `runShardSplitQuery` and then once per nested `runSplitQuery` shard-group call (1 + 4). Hard-coding this number hides the redundant work (see finding in `shardQuerySplitting.ts`) and will need to be changed if/when the duplication is removed. A test that asserts the final `runQuery` payloads contain correctly interpolated `expr`/`step` (which it already does for the shard splitting test) is sufficient; asserting the call count of an internal helper locks in the current inefficiency and the $__range regression.

title: Queries are interpolated twice in the shard-splitting flow
body: runShardSplitQuery now interpolates each query (line 49-52), then passes the already-interpolated targets into splitQueriesByStreamShard. For every shard group, runNextRequest (line 163) calls runSplitQuery(datasource, subRequest, ...) with that subRequest, and the new runSplitQuery in querySplitting.ts (line 296-299) re-applies datasource.applyTemplateVariables to the same queries. The result is 1 + N interpolations of the same queries (N = number of shard groups). The test on line 112 of shardQuerySplitting.test.ts even pins this in place with expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5). It works only because the template-service replacement is idempotent on the substituted values, but it is wasted work on every shard group iteration, and any future interpolation that is not strictly idempotent (e.g. counters, suffixes, timestamps) will silently produce wrong results or repeated side effects on the same query objects.

title: Brittle call-count assertion masks the duplicate-interpolation waste
body: The test pins expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5), which depends on the exact number of shard groups produced by the specific fetchLabelValues fixture plus the 1+N pattern above. Any change to grouping size, fetchLabelValues results, or the runSplitQuery call sites will break this test even when the user-visible behavior is correct. The assertion exists only to document the redundant call from runShardSplitQuery through runSplitQuery; it should instead verify the intended contract (e.g. that queries are interpolated exactly once before the first runQuery call) so a regression that introduces or removes duplicate interpolation is caught.

title: applyTemplateVariables is invoked twice for every shard-group sub-request
body: runShardSplitQuery (shardQuerySplitting.ts line 52) calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables once per query to produce the interpolated `queries` array that is then handed to splitQueriesByStreamShard. splitQueriesByStreamShard calls runSplitQuery (line 163) once per shard group, and runSplitQuery (this file line 299) again calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables on the already-interpolated targets. The shard-splitting test now demonstrates this: a request with one query produces 4 shard groups, so applyTemplateVariables is invoked 5 times for the same set of targets when only 1 call is needed. applyTemplateVariables is non-trivial (it walks the template substitution pipeline, including ${var}, $var, [[var]] and built-ins like $__range/$__interval, plus ad-hoc filters), so the extra calls are wasted CPU on every sharded request and scale with the number of groups. Consider either moving the interpolation out of the per-group loop (so it happens exactly once in runShardSplitQuery) or adding an option like `skipInterpolation` to runSplitQuery so the delegation from runShardSplitQuery does not re-interpolate the already-interpolated queries.

title: Filter order changed: queries that interpolate to an empty expression are no longer filtered out
body: The new code filters `request.targets` by `query.expr` and `!query.hide` BEFORE calling applyTemplateVariables, while the previous implementation invoked `interpolateVariablesInQueries` first and then filtered. With the previous order, a target whose template variables resolved to an empty string (for example `${var}` where `var` is unset or empty, or `{label="${var}"}`) became empty after interpolation and was filtered out by the `query.expr` check. With the new order, the filter inspects the ORIGINAL, pre-interpolated expression, so those targets now pass through the filter and reach the shard splitter and ultimately the backend as malformed queries (e.g. `count_over_time([5m])` or `{label=""}`), which will error out instead of being silently skipped as before. This is a behavior regression for the small set of dashboards that rely on variable values resolving to empty.

title: Test pins the redundant 5x interpolation as expected behavior
body: The test 'Interpolates queries before running' was changed from expecting `interpolateVariablesInQueries` to be called 1 time to expecting `datasource.applyTemplateVariables` to be called 5 times. The expected count of 5 is exactly the redundant-interpolation pattern introduced by this PR (1 call in runShardSplitQuery + 1 call inside runSplitQuery for each of the 4 sub-requests). Hard-coding 5 in the assertion makes the wasteful double-interpolation the contract of the test and will silently block any future refactor that avoids re-interpolating the already-interpolated targets inside runSplitQuery. The assertion should instead verify that the queries sent to runQuery are correctly interpolated (or that interpolation is called once per distinct query), without coupling the test to the current call count.

title: Stale test function name after type rename
body: The test function is still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware on line 21 even though the type was renamed to MetricsMiddleware. The test name should be updated to TestMetricsMiddleware to match the renamed type and avoid confusion for future maintainers.

title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware has no test coverage
body: The newly added ContextualLoggerMiddleware (NewContextualLoggerMiddleware at line 14, with the underlying ContextualLoggerMiddleware type at line 22) has no associated test file. This middleware is responsible for adding endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, and uname to the request context via log.WithContextualAttributes. The LoggerMiddleware now relies on this behavior to produce logs with those fields. Without tests, there is no verification that these attributes are correctly added, and a future change to instrumentContext could silently break the logger output without any test failure.

title: TestLogger.FromContext silently discards context
body: TestLogger.FromContext (line 46) ignores the context argument and returns a fresh NewTestLogger() instance, dropping any contextual attributes set via log.WithContextualAttributes. With LoggerMiddleware now using m.logger.FromContext(ctx) instead of m.logger, tests that use TestLogger can no longer verify that contextual attributes (endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname) added by ContextualLoggerMiddleware are actually retrieved by the logger. A test that asserts these fields appear in a log message will fail to do so through this fake, so the new context-propagation logic is effectively untestable.

title: Logger name 'plugin.instrumentation' is misleading after rename
body: The logger is created with the name 'plugin.instrumentation' on line 161 (log.New('plugin.instrumentation')). After renaming InstrumentationMiddleware to MetricsMiddleware and splitting out the contextual logger middleware, this logger name no longer aligns with the new terminology and will be confusing to operators searching logs by component name. Consider updating to 'plugin.logger' or 'plugin.request'.

title: Trace ID silently dropped from Plugin Request Completed log
body: The previous logger_middleware.go explicitly extracted the trace ID from the request context and appended it to the log parameters: `traceID := tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false); if traceID != "" { logParams = append(logParams, "traceID", traceID) }`. This extraction was removed in this PR and the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware only adds endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname to the context logger, not the trace ID. As a result, the 'Plugin Request Completed' log emitted by LoggerMiddleware no longer carries a traceID field unless pkg/infra/log transparently correlates with the OpenTelemetry trace context. This regression is not described in the PR description and removes an important field used for correlating plugin request logs with traces. The author should either restore the explicit extraction in LoggerMiddleware or verify (and document) that the infra/log context logger includes the trace ID automatically.

title: Test function name not updated after rename
body: The file was renamed from instrumentation_middleware_test.go to metrics_middleware_test.go and the type/constructor were renamed to MetricsMiddleware/newMetricsMiddleware/NewMetricsMiddleware, but the top-level test function is still declared as `func TestInstrumentationMiddleware(t *testing.T)`. This is inconsistent with the rename and the test name will be misleading in test output and any -run filters. It should be renamed to TestMetricsMiddleware.

title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware has no test file
body: The PR introduces a brand new middleware file pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/contextual_logger_middleware.go containing the instrumentContext helper plus four RPC entry points (QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) that propagate a contextual logger through the request context. No corresponding contextual_logger_middleware_test.go is added, so the behavior of instrumentContext (including the conditional dsName/dsUID/uname branches) and the context propagation through the middleware chain is entirely untested. The metrics_middleware_test.go rename only exercises the metrics side; nothing verifies that the new middleware actually enriches the context as advertised, or that the LoggerMiddleware downstream receives the expected attributes.

title: Updated logRequest behavior is not covered by any test
body: The logRequest method was reworked from passing an explicit logParams slice (with pluginId, endpoint, pluginCtx.User.Login, dsName, dsUID and traceID explicitly appended) and calling m.logger.Info(...) to instead calling m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...) with a slimmed-down logParams. This is a meaningful behavioral change: the pluginId/endpoint/user/ds/traceID fields now come from the contextual logger rather than from explicit key/value pairs, which means the log payload silently loses those fields unless ContextualLoggerMiddleware is wired into the chain ahead of LoggerMiddleware. There is no test that verifies either the resulting log structure or the implicit ordering contract between these two middlewares, so a future reordering or refactor of CreateMiddlewares could regress the log output without any test failure.

title: Test function name still references the old InstrumentationMiddleware
body: The file was renamed from instrumentation_middleware_test.go to metrics_middleware_test.go and the only internal change is renaming newInstrumentationMiddleware to newMetricsMiddleware, but the top-level test function is still TestInstrumentationMiddleware. After the public type/constructor rename this name is misleading and makes the test harder to locate and reason about (it now looks like it tests a type that no longer exists). It should be TestMetricsMiddleware.

title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a new instance, breaking the standard TestLogger assertion pattern
body: The newly added TestLogger.FromContext returns NewTestLogger() (a brand-new TestLogger) instead of returning the receiver f. The LoggerMiddleware.logRequest now invokes m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), so any test that hands a TestLogger into LoggerMiddleware (or any other component that calls FromContext on it) and then inspects the original instance's InfoLogs/WarnLogs/etc. will see zero calls because the log was recorded on a different TestLogger instance that the test never references. To keep the established pattern (pass a TestLogger, assert on its fields) TestLogger.FromContext should return f (or a thin wrapper that delegates to f) so assertions against the original instance still work.

title: Local cache is set before DB write, bypassing the device limit on subsequent requests
body: In tagDeviceUI, the local cache entry is set before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice. When the limit is reached, CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, but the cache key remains set.
