Because `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel)` short-circuits to false when the user argument is null, fillContextForm is now never invoked on a user's first visit to the username+password form. This means the CHALLENGE/RP_ID/conditional-UI attributes are never set on the initial login page, breaking discoverable-credential auto-login and the conditional webauthn button on first paint. The same swap is repeated in `challenge(context, error, field)`, so the conditional UI also disappears from initial-login error pages (invalid username/password). Existing tests `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey` in all three test classes plus the first-page assertions of `passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey`, `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication`, and `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey` rely on `//form[@id='webauth']` being present and `getUsernameAutocomplete() == "username webauthn"` after `oauth.openLoginForm()`; those assertions will fail. The fix is to call fillContextForm for the initial-login case as well (e.g., drop the `user != null` part of `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` for this caller, or invoke fillContextForm separately whenever `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` regardless of whether the user is set).

title: Compile error: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() called with no args
body: The method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is invoked with no arguments, but the only definition in the parent class UsernamePasswordForm is `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` which requires a UserModel parameter. There is no no-arg overload anywhere in the class hierarchy. This will prevent the project from compiling. Likely intended to be `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, or a separate no-arg overload was forgotten.

title: WebAuthn form no longer filled on initial login (conditional UI regression)
body: Before this change the call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` lived inside the `else` branch where `context.getUser() == null`, i.e. it ran on the initial login page so conditional UI passkeys worked for users without a session. The new code hoists it out and gates it on `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, which requires `user != null`. As a result the WebAuthn challenge, RP ID, allowed authenticators, and ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI attribute are never set on the initial login form, so navigator.credentials.get() cannot auto-discover passkeys. The existing test `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey` still asserts `driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']"))` is present immediately after `oauth.openLoginForm()` (before any submission), which this change makes impossible. The fill must also happen in the `user == null` branch (or in both branches).

title: Awkward try-fail pattern to assert element absence
body: In `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey`, the test uses `try { assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue()); fail(...); } catch (Exception nsee) {}` to assert that the webauthn button is not rendered. `WebDriver.findElement` throws `NoSuchElementException` when the element is missing and never returns null, so `assertThat(element, nullValue())` would always fail with an AssertionError if the element exists, making the subsequent `fail()` unreachable. The cleaner pattern already used elsewhere in this package (`PasskeysUsernameFormTest` line 202) is `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, () -> driver.findElement(...))`. The same anti-pattern is repeated at line 312.

title: remove() always hits DB to fetch storedIdp even when cache is valid
body: The modified `remove(alias)` method now unconditionally calls `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` at the top of the method to obtain `storedIdp` for `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)`. The previous code only invoked `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` when `isInvalid(cacheKey)` was true (the common-case fast path used the cached `CachedIdentityProvider`). After this change, every `remove` performs a DB lookup even when the alias is fully cached, turning what was an O(1) cache hit into an extra JPA roundtrip on the hot path for IDP removal.

title: registerIDPLoginInvalidation invalidates all FetchMode caches unnecessarily
body: `registerIDPLoginInvalidation` registers invalidation for every `FetchMode` (REALM_ONLY, ORG_ONLY, ALL) whenever the affected IDP passes the login predicate. However, a realm-only login IDP can only appear in the REALM_ONLY and ALL caches, and an org-bound login IDP can only appear in the ORG_ONLY and ALL caches. Invalidating the third cache (e.g. wiping ORG_ONLY results when creating a realm-only IDP) discards valid cached entries that have no relationship to the change, forcing the next call in that mode to repopulate from the DB unnecessarily. The predicate already exposes whether the IDP has an organizationId, so a targeted invalidation per affected mode would be straightforward.

title: New isEnabled() re-check in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean has no test
body: The PR adds `idp.isEnabled() && ...` filters to both the `ORG_ONLY` and `ALL` branches of `searchForIdentityProviders`, with a comment explaining that the re-check is needed because the cached IDP model is wrapped and `isEnabled()` may return false when the bound organization is disabled. There is no test in `OrganizationCacheTest` (or elsewhere in the diff) that exercises this re-check path - e.g. a test that disables the organization bound to a cached IDP and verifies the login page no longer shows the IDP. Without such a test, a future refactor that removes the re-check (thinking the cached wrapper already handles it) would silently regress this behavior.

title: searchKey collapses null and empty-string organizationId but they yield different DB results
body: `String searchKey = organizationId != null ? organizationId : "";` maps both `null` and `""` to the same cache index. In the default `getForLogin`, for `FetchMode.ORG_ONLY`/`FetchMode.ALL` the `organizationId == null` branch does NOT add an `ORGANIZATION_ID` filter (returning every org-linked login-eligible IDP), while `organizationId == ""` adds `ORGANIZATION_ID=\"\"` to the search options (returning only IDPs whose org id is the empty string, typically none). A subsequent call with `""` after a successful `null` call will return the cached set for the wrong query. Although the current callers all pass `null` or a real id, the cache key does not preserve the distinction the delegate makes.

title: searchKey for REALM_ONLY uses organizationId even though the default impl ignores it
body: The default `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin` ignores the `organizationId` parameter when `mode == REALM_ONLY` (it always sets `ORGANIZATION_ID` to `null`). Using `organizationId` as part of `searchKey` for `REALM_ONLY` causes separate cache entries (and extra DB queries) for what is logically the same result, e.g. `getForLogin(REALM_ONLY, null)` and `getForLogin(REALM_ONLY, \"org1\")` produce identical IDP sets but populate two distinct entries. The `searchKey` for `REALM_ONLY` should be a constant (e.g. the empty string) regardless of `organizationId`.

title: remove() now performs an extra unconditional JPA getByAlias() on every delete
body: The diff hoists `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` above the cache check, so the JPA delegate is hit on every `remove(...)` even when the cache is not invalid and `storedIdp` is only used later by `registerIDPLoginInvalidation`. Previously the DB lookup happened only in the `isInvalid(cacheKey)` branch. The new lookup can be guarded, or `storedIdp` can be fetched lazily before `registerIDPLoginInvalidation`, to avoid the extra DB round-trip on the common path.

title: testCacheIDPForLogin registers cleanup with hard-coded alias "alias"
body: Inside the create loop, `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` is called for every created IDP. `get("alias")` looks up an IDP with the literal alias `"alias"`, which does not exist; the method reference will be evaluated at teardown and fail. The intent is clearly `get("idp-alias-" + i)::remove`. (The same broken pattern appears in the older tests in this file but is perpetuated here.)

title: testCacheIDPForLogin only asserts cache size, not the IDPs returned by getForLogin
body: The test only verifies the size of the cached set of internal IDs in `IdentityProviderListQuery.getIDPs(searchKey)`. It does not consume `session.identityProviders().getForLogin(...)` and assert the alias/enabled/disabled state of the returned streams, nor does it verify that an IDP that was just removed no longer appears. A regression in the mapping from cached internal IDs to returned models (e.g. a stale entry that should have been invalidated) would go undetected.

title: getForLogin does not honor organization invalidation the way getByOrganization does
body: `getByOrganization` explicitly bypasses the cache when either `cacheKey` or `orgId` is invalidated (`isInvalid(cacheKey) || isInvalid(orgId)`). The new `getForLogin` only checks `isInvalid(cacheKey)`. If the organization itself is invalidated (e.g. disabled or removed) in the current session, the login cache can continue to serve its internal-id set, and the wrapper's per-IDP `isEnabled()` only filters out one IDP at a time; this can leave stale results that diverge from what `idpDelegate.getForLogin` would return.

title: Test cleanup uses literal alias "alias" instead of the variable, leaking IDPs across runs
body: Inside the new `testCacheIDPForLogin` (and also the pre-existing `testCacheIDPByOrg` at line 303), the cleanup is registered with `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)`. The string `"alias"` is a literal, not the per-iteration variable `alias`. Each cleanup therefore resolves to an IDP lookup of a non-existent alias and ends up being a no-op (or NPE when invoked on the null resource). All 20 IDPs created in the loop (and the 10 in testCacheIDPByOrg) remain in the realm after the test, which will cause `idp-alias-0` creation to fail on a subsequent run and pollutes the realm state used by other tests. The cleanup should reference the iteration's alias (e.g., `final String alias = "idp-alias-" + i; ... addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get(alias)::remove);`).

title: remove() always calls idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) even when the cached entry is available
body: The new code unconditionally fetches `storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` at the top of `remove()` solely so it can pass it to `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)`. In the `else` branch the cache already holds a `CachedIdentityProvider` whose model could supply the same information, so the DB round-trip is unnecessary on the common (warm cache) path. Reuse the cached model when available, e.g.: if invalid, fetch from DB; otherwise use `cached.getIdentityProvider()` (and still null-check, since the alias may genuinely not exist).

title: LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() rebuilds the Predicate on every invocation
body: `getLoginPredicate()` constructs a fresh `Predicate<IdentityProviderModel>` (stream of `LoginFilter.values()`, reduce, several `and()` chains) every time it is called. `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` invokes it four times per update, and `registerIDPLoginInvalidation` invokes it once per create/remove, so the same chain is reconstructed repeatedly on hot paths. Cache the composed predicate in a `private static final Predicate<IdentityProviderModel> LOGIN_PREDICATE = ...` and have the method simply return that field.

title: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate() calls getLoginPredicate().test(...) four times per update
body: Both branches of the invalidation guard re-invoke the (already expensive) predicate twice on each of `original` and `updated`, i.e. four predicate evaluations per IDP update. Store the booleans once: `boolean wasLogin = getLoginPredicate().test(original); boolean isLogin = getLoginPredicate().test(updated);` and use those locals in the two `if` conditions.

title: Duplicate junit and hamcrest test dependencies
body: The diff adds a second block declaring junit and hamcrest as test dependencies, but the original pom.xml already declares the exact same junit and hamcrest dependencies a few lines above (originally at the existing test scope block). Maven will accept this but the file now has the same dependency declared twice with identical scope, groupId, and artifactId. This is an obvious copy/paste mistake; one of the two blocks must be removed before merging.

title: Dead encoder instances created and discarded in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
body: In the ECDSA `concatenatedRSToASN1DER` method, the two calls `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` immediately after computing the BigIntegers create new ASN1Encoder instances, write into them, and discard the result. Only the second pair inside `writeDerSeq(...)` is actually used to build the DER output. The discarded calls are dead code (wasted allocations and a misleading read of the code) and must be removed.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns the JDK default provider, not BouncyCastle
body: `getBouncyCastleProvider()` is implemented as `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, which returns the provider that supplies the default keystore type (typically SunJCE on a standard JDK), not BouncyCastle. The interface contract and the method's name promise a BouncyCastle provider, and the existing `DefaultCryptoProvider`/`FIPS1402Provider` actually return a BC/BCFIPS instance. Any caller (now or in the future) that relies on BC-only algorithms or extensions (e.g., for `getKeyFactory`, `getSignature`, `getCertificateUtils` if they are later implemented) will silently get the JCE provider and either fail with `NoSuchAlgorithmException` or produce incorrect results. The implementation must return an actual BouncyCastle provider (or the documented behaviour must be revised and the contract clarified).

title: Silent behavior change when multiple CryptoProviders are on the classpath
body: Previously `detectProvider` threw an `IllegalStateException` when more than one `CryptoProvider` was found, forcing a clean classpath. The new code silently picks the highest-`order()` one and downgrades the warning to `logger.debugf`, only logging a generic "Ignored crypto providers:" message. Several built-in providers (`DefaultCryptoProvider`, `WildFlyElytronProvider`, `FIPS1402Provider`) all return `order() == 200`, so when more than one is accidentally on the classpath (e.g., during testsuite setups that pull in both non-FIPS and FIPS BC) the chosen provider becomes non-deterministic and the misconfiguration is hidden from operators because the message is at DEBUG level. At a minimum the message must be emitted at WARN/INFO, and the previous hard-fail behaviour for genuinely ambiguous setups should be considered. The new `logger.debugf(builder.toString())` call also passes a pre-built string with no format specifiers to a `*f` method, which is misuse.

title: readSequence can loop forever on indefinite-length encoded sequences
body: `readSequence` uses `while (length > 0)` where `length` comes from `readLength()`. `readLength` returns `-1` for indefinite-length encoding (the `0x80` byte) without throwing. An indefinite-length outer sequence would therefore cause an infinite loop. ECDSA signatures use DER (no indefinite length), so this is latent, but the class is a general ASN.1 reader and this is a clear bug. Either throw on indefinite length in `readSequence` or handle it properly (look for the end-of-contents octets 0x00 0x00).

title: EC key generated in constructor instead of @Before, and uses platform-default curve
body: The test generates the `KeyPair` in the constructor using `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair()`, which relies on the platform-default EC parameters (P-256 on most modern JDKs but not guaranteed everywhere). The same key is then used to sign with SHA256withECDSA, SHA384withECDSA and SHA512withECDSA, producing signatures of mixed validity; the test only verifies the round-trip of the RS<->ASN1 conversion, never that the conversion matches what a real verifier would expect for ES256/ES384/ES512. Generating the key in a `@Before` method and using a deterministic curve (e.g., `ECGenParameterSpec("prime256v1")`) would make the test more reliable across JDKs and the suite more informative.

title: order() added as abstract method on CryptoProvider is a breaking change
body: `int order()` was added to the `CryptoProvider` interface as an abstract method (not a `default`). Any external implementation of `CryptoProvider` that existed before this PR will fail to compile until it provides an implementation. This is acceptable for an internal SPI but worth noting that the order chosen (`AuthzClientCryptoProvider`=100, all built-in providers=200) makes the built-in providers always win, which is the intended behaviour but is not enforced by tests. Also consider documenting the chosen ordering semantics (higher number wins, what to choose if equal) on the interface.

title: No bounds check on signature length and signLength in ECDSA converters
body: `concatenatedRSToASN1DER` and `asn1derToConcatenatedRS` assume that `signature.length == signLength` and that `signLength` is even. If a caller passes a shorter signature or an odd `signLength`, the code will either throw `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` from `System.arraycopy` or silently produce a truncated `s` half. A simple length check up-front would prevent surprising failures when this code is reused beyond the current authz-client wiring.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns the default JCE provider, not BouncyCastle
body: The implementation calls `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, which returns the provider of the JVM's default keystore type (typically SUN for JKS or SunJSSE for PKCS12), not BouncyCastle. The interface contract in CryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider documents that it must return a BouncyCastle security provider (non-FIPS or FIPS). When this provider is selected by CryptoIntegration (which happens whenever authz-client is used standalone, since DefaultCryptoProvider is not on that classpath), any caller that does `Signature.getInstance(alg, prov)` or similar expecting BC will silently get a different provider. That breaks the contract and can cause ECDSA verification to fall back to SunEC/SUN (or fail outright if BC is required for the curve/algorithm), defeating the purpose of this class for the standalone 3rd-party use case.

title: Test only verifies round-trip consistency, not correctness against a reference
body: The test asserts `rsConcat2 == rsConcat` after running `sign -> asn1derToConcatenatedRS -> concatenatedRSToASN1DER -> asn1derToConcatenatedRS`. This is an idempotency property test, not a correctness test: if both converters are biased the same way (e.g., they swap r and s, off-by-one the padding, or always strip the leading zero byte) the round-trip still matches and the assertion passes. The test never checks that the produced `rsConcat` actually equals the raw r||s bytes that the JDK signature produced, nor compares against BouncyCastle's BCECDSACryptoProvider output. A reference comparison (or parsing the original DER signature with java.security and comparing the integers byte-for-byte) is needed to actually validate the conversion.

title: Two ASN1Encoder instances are created and discarded on every call to concatenatedRSToASN1DER
body: Lines 114-115 call `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` and throw away the returned encoders. They have no effect on the result (the real encoding is produced by the two encoders passed into `writeDerSeq` on lines 119-120). These are dead allocations executed on every signature verification; they should be removed.

title: Test uses default EC key for all algorithms, masking wrong-size behavior for ES384/ES512
body: The constructor generates a single key with `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair()`, which on most JDKs produces a P-256 key (32-byte components). `ECDSAAlgorithm.ES384` and `ES512` expect 48-byte and 66-byte components respectively, but the JDK's Signature returns ~32-byte r/s for a P-256 key regardless of the requested algorithm name. `asn1derToConcatenatedRS(sign, 96)` then pads the 32-byte components with leading zeros to 48 bytes, and the subsequent RS->DER->RS round-trip is consistent because the same padding is applied again. The test passes, but `asn1Des != sign` and the resulting signature cannot be verified against the data. Each `test*` method should generate a key with the matching curve (P-256 for ES256, P-384 for ES384, P-521 for ES512), e.g. via `ECGenParameterSpec` and `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC")` initialized appropriately.

title: Test only verifies round-trip consistency, not absolute correctness of concatenatedRSToASN1DER
body: The assertion `Assert.assertArrayEquals(rsConcat, rsConcat2)` only proves that `asn1derToConcatenatedRS` is idempotent over its own output, which is essentially a property of the decoder. A buggy `concatenatedRSToASN1DER` that, for example, swapped r and s, added a spurious leading zero, or used the wrong tag/byte order, could still satisfy this equality. The test should additionally assert `Assert.assertArrayEquals(sign, asn1Des)` and, more importantly, verify the produced signature against the data with the public key (`Signature.initVerify(...); signature.update(data); Assert.assertTrue(signature.verify(asn1Des));`). Without that, a real conversion bug would not be caught.

title: Dead `ASN1Encoder.create().write(...)` calls in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
body: Lines 114-115 call `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger)` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger)` and then immediately discard the returned instances (no assignment, no `toByteArray()`). The encoders' internal `ByteArrayOutputStream`s accumulate the encoded bytes that are then thrown away. The actual return value is built only by the subsequent `ASN1Encoder.create().writeDerSeq(...)` call. The two lines are dead code that waste allocations and obscure intent; they should be deleted.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the default JCA provider, not BouncyCastle
body: The implementation does `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, which on a stock JDK returns the SUN provider (for JKS) - not BouncyCastle. The contract on `CryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider()` (documented as "BouncyCastle security provider") is violated, and any authz-client code path that uses this provider for BC-only algorithms (e.g. certain Signature/Cipher/KeyFactory lookups requested without an explicit provider name) will fail with `NoSuchAlgorithmException` or get a non-BC implementation. The authz-client explicitly advertises itself as a self-contained CryptoProvider, so this method should return a real BouncyCastleProvider (matching what the other CryptoProvider implementations do), or the doc/comment on the class should be updated to state that BC algorithms are unsupported and `getBouncyCastleProvider()` is intentionally a stub.

title: Adding `int order()` as a non-default abstract method is a binary-incompatible API break
body: `order()` is declared without a `default` body, so every external implementation of `CryptoProvider` (third-party SPIs registered via `META-INF/services/org.keycloak.common.crypto.CryptoProvider`) will fail to load with `NoSuchMethodError` / `AbstractMethodError` at `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider` time. Before this PR such implementations would be the only ones on the classpath (no ordering needed); afterwards they are still detected by `ServiceLoader` and either shadow the bundled providers or get shadowed by them, but every call site that compiled against the old interface breaks at runtime. Either provide a sensible `default int order() { return 0; }` (or `Integer.MIN_VALUE`) so existing implementations keep working, or document this as an intentional breaking change and bump the module's major version. Without a default, downstream Keycloak extensions and forks will start crashing on startup.

title: Tie-breaking by ServiceLoader iteration order is non-deterministic when orders are equal
body: When two providers share the same `order()` value (e.g. `DefaultCryptoProvider`, `WildFlyElytronProvider` and `FIPS1402Provider` all return 200 here), `Comparator.reversed()` is stable, so the winner is whichever provider ServiceLoader happens to iterate first. JAR ordering on the classpath is not specified by the JLS, and tools/builds can produce different orders, so the chosen CryptoProvider can differ between environments with the same dependency set. This previously threw a clear error; now it silently picks an implementation. The log line also leaks a format string into `logger.debugf(builder)` (class names contain no `%` so it's safe today, but it should be `logger.debugf("%s", builder.toString())`). Either reject equal orders with an informative error, or sort by a secondary deterministic key (class name) and document the precedence.

title: CryptoIntegration.init is called from create(Configuration) but not from create() / create(InputStream) entry points
body: `CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader())` is added only to the `create(Configuration)` overload. Although `create()` and `create(InputStream)` both delegate to `create(Configuration)` and so transitively initialize the provider, the contract of `CryptoIntegration.init` is that callers invoke it explicitly with their own classloader, and double-checked init inside `init` records the *first* classloader it sees. Any caller that constructed an `AuthzClient` via a non-default classloader (e.g. inside an OSGi bundle, a JEE lib isolation, or an app-server deployment that also exposes `keycloak-authz-client`) will have the choice of CryptoProvider pinned to the AuthzClient class's loader, even though a more appropriate provider exists on their loader. The init should happen in every public `create(...)` overload, or be done once eagerly in a static initializer / `ServiceLoader` lookup that does not depend on which API the user calls first.

title: Individual client/user resources are created without a type
body: `getOrCreateResource` creates the resource via `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId())` and never calls `resource.setType(resourceType)`. The all-resource created in `init` has its type set explicitly via `resource.setType(type)`, but the per-instance resources produced here are stored with a null/empty type. Downstream consumers that filter by type will silently skip them. In particular, `ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission` calls `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, …)`, so it only sees the all-resource (`"Clients"`) and never the individual client resources. The returned set therefore contains only the all-resource name and never any individual client IDs, so callers that filter clients shown to an admin will see no per-client entries. Set the type on the resource in `getOrCreateResource` (e.g. `resource.setType(resourceType)` right after `resourceStore.create`) so that individual resources are discoverable by type.

title: Potential NPE when the all-clients resource does not exist
body: In `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, when no resource is found by name the code falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)`. That method can legitimately return `null` (it returns null when the schema is not supported, when `resourceType` is null, when the type is not registered, or when the resource is not in the store). The result is then passed to `authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()` without a null check, which will throw a NullPointerException. Add a null check before calling `findByResource` and return false if the all-clients resource is missing.

title: Dead code: getEvaluationContext is never called
body: `ClientPermissionsV2.getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken)` is defined as a private method but is not referenced anywhere in the file. It builds a `DefaultEvaluationContext` with a `kc.client.id` attribute but is never used by `hasPermission`, `hasGrantedPermission`, or any other code path. Either delete it or wire it into the actual evaluation paths that need a client-aware context.

title: getResourceName does not handle the Clients resource type
body: `getResourceName` only has a branch for `USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE`. For a policy whose resource type is `CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE`, the method falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`. The resources created for individual clients by `getOrCreateResource` are named with the client's internal UUID (`resolveClient` returns `client.getId()`), and `getDisplayName()` returns that same UUID. So when an admin views a client-targeted permission in the UI, the resource is shown as the UUID rather than the human-readable client name. Add a `Clients` branch that resolves `resource.getName()` via `session.clients().getClientById(...)` and returns `client.getClientId()` (or the client's display name) for individual resources, and "All clients" for the all-resource, matching the existing `USERS` pattern.

title: getClientsWithPermission and per-client filtering are not tested
body: The new `ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission(String)` and the per-client resource lookup path in `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` are not exercised by any test in `PermissionClientTest`. The tests only cover scenarios where the specific resource exists. There is no test that verifies a caller with a per-client scope permission (no all-clients permission) is correctly identified via `getClientsWithPermission`, nor one that exercises the all-clients fallback when a per-client resource exists with a different scope than the one being checked. Adding such tests would have caught the missing `setType` bug.

title: getResourceName does not handle the new CLIENTS resource type
body: getResourceName was extended to add a CLIENTS resource type and scopes, but the existing getResourceName() method only resolves resource names for the USERS resource type. For policies with resourceType "Clients", the method falls through to `return resource.getDisplayName()`, which for schema-created resources is null (display name is never set in getOrCreateResource). For individual client resources whose name is the client UUID, this returns an unhelpful UUID rather than the clientId/username-style identifier. The method should be extended with an `else if (CLIENTS.getType().equals(resourceType))` branch that handles `resource.getName().equals(CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` (returning "All clients") and resolves individual clients via session.clients().getClientById(realm, resource.getName()), analogous to the USERS handling.

title: Potential NPE when the all-clients resource does not exist
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when resourceStore.findByName returns null the code calls AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...). That helper returns null if no resource of that name exists in the store. The result is passed unconditionally to authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource), which will throw NullPointerException on `resource`. A null check is needed before calling findByResource. While init() always creates the all-clients resource in a fresh realm, this is a robustness hole for realms where the admin-permissions client exists without the schema resource (e.g., migration edge cases).

title: Dead code: unused Logger field, TOKEN_EXCHANGE import, and getEvaluationContext helper
body: The class declares `private static final Logger logger = Logger.getLogger(ClientPermissionsV2.class);` (with the corresponding org.jboss.logging.Logger import) but never references logger. It also imports `org.keycloak.services.resources.admin.permissions.AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE` without using it. The private method `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken)` (lines 262-272) is defined but never invoked anywhere in this class. These should be removed to keep the new file clean.

title: requireView() JavaDoc says "Returns true" for a void method
body: The JavaDoc added by this PR for `void requireView();` reads `Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}.` Since the method is void and explicitly named `require*`, the doc should describe the exception it throws, e.g., `Throws ForbiddenException if canView() returns false.` The same issue affects `requireList()` and `requireListClientScopes()`, which were re-documented in this PR but copy the correct pattern, so they read correctly. Only `requireView()` was mis-described.

title: No test coverage for the new MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS now includes the MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope, ClientPermissionsV2 implements canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel) using it, and the ClientPermissionEvaluator interface documents it. However, PermissionClientTest does not exercise this scope or canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel) at all (it covers MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE together in testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient, but never MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE). A test similar to testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient, but verifying client-scope role mapping with MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE, should be added so that the scope and the canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel) implementation have real coverage.

title: getClientsWithPermission includes the literal string "Clients" as if it were a client id
body: `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` returns every resource whose type is "Clients", which includes both per-client resources (whose names are client UUIDs) AND the aggregate all-clients resource whose name is literally the string "Clients". When the caller has permission via the all-clients resource, hasGrantedPermission returns true and `granted.add(resource.getName())` puts "Clients" into the returned set. Callers treat the result as a set of client ids and will try to resolve "Clients" as a client, which is not a valid client id. The aggregate resource must be skipped (e.g., by checking `resource.getName().equals(AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` and continuing), or callers must be told separately that "all clients" permission applies.

title: canView() is inconsistent with canView(ClientScopeModel) regarding MANAGE permission
body: `canView()` only checks VIEW via `hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)`, but `canView(ClientScopeModel)` checks BOTH VIEW and MANAGE via `hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW) || hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. A user with only MANAGE permission on all clients can pass canView(ClientScopeModel) but fails canView(). This asymmetry is inconsistent within the same class and may break listing/filtering paths that consult canView() without per-client evaluation, contradicting the V2 contract that MANAGE implies VIEW. canView() should also accept MANAGE permission, matching the canView(ClientScopeModel) behavior.

title: canManageClientScopes() ignores per-client MANAGE permission
body: `canManageClientScopes()` and `canManage(ClientScopeModel)` only consult `hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)` against the all-clients resource, never the per-client resource. In testManageOnlyOneClient a user is granted MANAGE only on a specific client and is then expected to be able to removeDefaultClientScope on that same client; this only works if the admin endpoint happens to call canManage(client) instead of canManage(clientScope). Any caller that does consult canManage(ClientScopeModel) for a scope attached to a single specific client will incorrectly deny the operation even when the user clearly manages that client. canManage(ClientScopeModel) should accept a ClientModel context (or canManageClientScopes should also be parameterized) so the per-client permission is honored.

title: getClientsWithPermission adds the literal resource type name to the granted set
body: In ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission, the lambda passed to resourceStore.findByType iterates over every resource with type "Clients", including the "Clients" resource itself (the all-clients resource whose name is the string "Clients"). When the caller has any scope permission on that all-clients resource, hasGrantedPermission returns true and the code does granted.add(resource.getName()), which inserts the literal string "Clients" into the set. "Clients" is not a valid client internal id (UUID), so any consumer that uses the returned set to look up or filter clients (e.g. comparing against ClientModel.getId()) will get an empty result and silently break filtering for callers who have only the all-clients permission. The "Clients" resource itself must be excluded (e.g. skip when resource.getName().equals(AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)).

title: Event listener gate allows V1 path to call V2 code that throws
body: The listener is wrapped in `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ))`, but inside it the code calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(...). The static management() helper returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, regardless of the V1 flag. After this PR, MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled now throws UnsupportedOperationException. So when both V1 and V2 feature flags are enabled and a client is removed, the listener still fires (V1 gate passes) and the call into ClientPermissionsV2 throws. Roles/groups don't have this problem because MgmtPermissionsV2 inherits their V1 implementations, but the client branch does. The gate needs to be "V1 enabled AND V2 not enabled", or the listener must dispatch through a V1-only helper, otherwise client deletion can blow up at runtime in deployments with both flags on.

title: getResourceName ignores the new Clients resource type
body: getResourceName handles USERS specially: it resolves the resource to "All users" for the type resource and to user.getUsername() for individual user resources. There is no branch for the new CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, so the method silently falls through to return resource.getDisplayName(). Because clients are stored with resource.getName() == client.getId() (the internal UUID produced by resolveClient), the value returned for any client-related policy/resource will be an opaque UUID rather than the human-readable clientId (e.g. "myclient"). UI/admin displays that rely on getResourceName will show UUIDs for clients while showing usernames for users, which is inconsistent and not user-friendly. Add an else-if branch for CLIENTS that returns "All clients" for the type resource and client.getClientId() (looked up from session.clients()) otherwise.

title: getClientsWithPermission is not covered by tests
body: The PR introduces the override ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission(String), but no test exercises it. The closest coverage (testViewAllClients) only checks findAll() visibility, which can succeed via the all-clients role check without ever calling getClientsWithPermission. Without a dedicated test that calls getClientsWithPermission("view"/"manage") for an admin who has only the all-clients permission and asserts that the returned set contains the right client ids and does not contain the literal "Clients", the bug at ClientPermissionsV2.java:138 (the all-clients resource being included in the result) cannot be caught by CI.

title: Potential NullPointerException when "all-clients" resource is missing
body: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...). getResourceTypeResource returns null in two cases: when supportsAuthorizationSchema(...) is false, and when the ResourceStore has no row with name == resource type (e.g. if AdminPermissionsSchema.init() never ran for this realm, or was upgraded in an unexpected order). The very next statement, authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource), then dereferences the possibly-null resource. This is reachable on any code path that asks for permission on a client before the schema initialization has produced the "Clients" resource. Guard with a null check (return false) before calling findByResource.

title: testFeatureNotEnabled does not cover UpdateCompatibilityCheck
body: The new testFeatureNotEnabled only exercises the 'metadata' subcommand. The same feature gate (Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES check) was added to UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run(), but there is no equivalent test that runs `update-compatibility check` without `--features=rolling-updates` and asserts the 'preview feature rolling-updates is not enabled' error. A future regression that drops the check in UpdateCompatibilityCheck would not be caught.

title: testFeatureNotEnabled does not assert the FEATURE_DISABLED exit code
body: The test only asserts the stderr message via cliResult.assertError(...). The new CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED = 4 contract (and the doc in update-compatibility.adoc which promises exit code 4 for this case) is not asserted. Compare with testCompatible which does assertEquals(0, result.exitCode()). Without an exit-code assertion the documented contract is not actually enforced by tests.

title: Breaking change of RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3
body: Previously exit code 4 meant 'Rolling Upgrade is not possible'. After this PR that meaning moves to exit code 3 and exit code 4 is reused for 'feature rolling-updates disabled'. Any external automation / GitOps pipeline / scripts that branched on the old exit-code 4 to detect a recreate upgrade will now take the new FEATURE_DISABLED branch instead, which is unrelated. Although this is documented in update-compatibility.adoc, this is a silent, behavior-affecting change for consumers of the CLI and should at least be called out in release notes / upgrade guide.

title: Exit-code 4 row in the table is misleading
body: The table row for exit code 4 reads 'Rolling Upgrade is not possible. The feature `rolling-updates` is disabled.' In reality, when the feature is disabled the command bails out via printFeatureDisabled() / CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED and never performs any rolling-upgrade analysis. The wording makes the user think a rolling-upgrade decision was made; in fact the command cannot run at all. The row should describe this as 'The feature `rolling-updates` is disabled; the command cannot determine upgrade compatibility.' (The stderr from AbstractUpdatesCommand.printFeatureDisabled already says 'Unable to use this command', which is the accurate phrasing.)

title: Misleading 'Operator will fail' warning when the feature is disabled
body: The CAUTION block states: 'While on preview stage, the feature `rolling-updates` must be enabled. Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail.' The operator does not fail; in the same PR, UpgradeTest.createInitialDeployment deliberately runs scenarios with `updateStrategy == null` and the feature NOT enabled, and expects the operator to still deploy and apply the old/recreate behavior. So the operator continues to work (using the Keycloak 26.1-or-older behavior) but does not recognize the new `update.strategy` field. The warning overstates the consequence and should be reworded to reflect that only the new update-strategy behavior is unavailable.

title: YAML example contains an invalid placeholder value
body: The example shows `strategy: Recreate|<not set> # <2>`, which is not valid YAML and cannot be applied as-is. The intent (that strategy may be either 'Recreate' or unset) is not obvious from a copy/paste. Either split it into two examples or use a non-YAML block to list the allowed values.

title: Breaking change in exit code for recreate upgrade
body: The constant RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was changed from 4 to 3, freeing up exit code 4 for the new FEATURE_DISABLED constant. Any existing user/operator script that checks for exit code 4 to detect "recreate upgrade is needed" will now incorrectly classify that result as a feature-disabled error. Even though the feature is preview, this is a backward-incompatible change to a public CLI contract documented in update-compatibility.adoc. Consider using a different value (e.g. 5) for FEATURE_DISABLED, or clearly call out the breaking change.

title: testFeatureNotEnabled does not assert the new FEATURE_DISABLED exit code
body: The new testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the stderr message but never verifies the process exit code. The whole point of the new CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED = 4 path is to expose a stable exit code (as documented in update-compatibility.adoc, exit code table). Without an assertEquals(4, cliResult.exitCode()) (or equivalent) the contract is untested and could silently regress (e.g. if the early-return path is removed or if picocli.exit is no longer reached).

title: FEATURE_DISABLED path not covered for the 'check' subcommand
body: The PR adds the same ROLLING_UPDATES feature gate in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() (UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java:46-50), but the new feature-disabled test only exercises UpdateCompatibilityMetadata. The 'check' subcommand's feature-disabled branch has no coverage, so a regression there (e.g. wrong exit code, swallowed error message) would not be caught.

title: 'Rolling Updates' strategy not documented in the possible field values table
body: The 'Supported Updates Types' section lists both 'Rolling Updates' and 'Recreate Updates' as supported strategies, but the 'Possible field values' table only documents '<not set>' and 'Recreate'. The YAML example uses 'strategy: Recreate|<not set>' as if those were the only options, leaving users no documented way to opt into the Rolling Updates strategy. Either the table is missing a 'Rolling' / 'RollingUpdate' row, or the prose is misleading and the strategy is implicit (in which case the prose should say so explicitly).

title: YAML example shows literal 'Recreate|<not set>' as a strategy value
body: The example YAML contains `strategy: Recreate|<not set>` as if it were a real value. The `|` is a YAML block-scalar indicator, so the strategy would be parsed as the literal string "Recreate|<not set>", which will not match either of the documented enum values and will be rejected (or silently treated as invalid). The intent is presumably to show "either Recreate or leave unset"; this should be expressed as prose or as two separate example snippets, not as a YAML value.

title: Custom-image template unconditionally enables a preview feature
body: The example Dockerfile used by the operator's custom-image flow now bakes in `--features=rolling-updates`. rolling-updates is a PREVIEW feature (Profile.java line 136) and the docs state the operator itself requires it to be enabled, but this file is a template that downstream users may copy. Unconditionally enabling a preview feature in a template can surprise users who expect a vanilla Keycloak image and makes it harder to turn the feature off later. Consider leaving the template without the flag and letting the operator enable it at deploy time, or clearly comment that this is required for the operator.

title: Breaking change: recreate-upgrade exit code changed from 4 to 3
body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is changed from 4 to 3, and the new FEATURE_DISABLED constant takes the old value 4. This is a behavior change for any user/automation that relies on the previous exit code 4 to detect a recreate upgrade. The previous docs (update-compatibility.adoc) already listed 3 as the recreate code, so this PR brings the code in line with the documented contract, but it is still a silent behavior change for existing callers that depended on the buggy value. Consider calling this out in release notes or, since the tool is preview, leave the old code path with a deprecation alias.

title: Tests assert error messages but never assert exit codes
body: testCompatible only asserts `assertEquals(0, result.exitCode())` for the OK case, while testWrongVersions and the new testFeatureNotEnabled only assert on the printed error/message text, never on the numeric exit code. This is exactly the gap that allowed the previous `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE = 4` bug to exist while the docs claimed exit code 3. Without exit-code assertions, a future regression that swaps 3 and 4 (or assigns the wrong constant) will not be caught. Add `assertEquals(CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE, result.exitCode())` (and the corresponding FEATURE_DISABLED assertion) so the contract is enforced.

title: testFeatureNotEnabled only covers the metadata subcommand
body: The new feature-gate branch was added to both UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run(), but testFeatureNotEnabled only exercises UpdateCompatibilityMetadata. The check subcommand has identical feature-flag logic and is left untested for the disabled case, so a future regression that, for example, removes the guard from one of the two run() methods will go unnoticed. Add a symmetric test for `UpdateCompatibility.NAME, UpdateCompatibilityCheck.NAME` that asserts both the 'feature disabled' error and exit code 4.

title: Error message references generic 'this command' instead of the actual command
body: printFeatureDisabled() emits "Unable to use this command. The preview feature 'rolling-updates' is not enabled." Both subcommands have a clearer name (update-compatibility check / metadata) and the message will be displayed to operators running the CLI. The generic wording also doesn't match the more specific phrasing used in the docs (`docs/guides/server/update-compatibility.adoc` says "the commands will fail"). Consider naming the command or, at minimum, matching the doc wording so the user immediately knows which command failed.

title: V2 canManage() (no-arg) treats VIEW scope as sufficient for MANAGE operations
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (lines 64-71) the body returns true if hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE) holds. That call lets any caller with the VIEW scope on the all-groups resource pass the check. Operations that gate on the no-arg canManage (e.g. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup -> requireManage()) will then allow callers to create/modify/delete groups even though they only have view permission. The interface JavaDoc on GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage() codifies this as the intended V2 behavior, but it is an explicit regression relative to V1 (GroupPermissions.canManage() is gated strictly on the MANAGE_USERS admin role) and the testViewGroups test grants Set.of(VIEW) yet does not assert that group management remains denied, so the regression is not caught. A maintainer should confirm whether 'VIEW implies MANAGE on groups' is really desired.

title: Possible NullPointerException when getResourceTypeResource returns null
body: In the private hasPermission(String groupId, String... scopes) method (around line 144), when the per-group resource lookup returns null the code falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and immediately calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty(). AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource() explicitly can return null (when supportsAuthorizationSchema is false, when the resourceType is unknown, or when the all-groups resource has not been created yet). Passing null to policyStore.findByResource(...) is not null-guarded and throws NPE in the JPA implementation. Because canView() (no-arg) and canManage() (no-arg) both call hasPermission(null, ...) for any caller without MANAGE_USERS, this NPE can be hit during normal V2 permission evaluation whenever the GROUPS type resource has not been created.

title: Same NPE risk in UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission when the all-users resource is missing
body: The private hasPermission(UserModel, EvaluationContext, String...) method has the same structure: when the specific user resource is missing it calls AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and then policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty() without a null check. When the USERS type resource does not exist (resourceTypeResource returns null) this will pass null to policyStore.findByResource and raise NPE. Every canView/canManage/canImpersonate/canMapRoles/canManageGroupMembership path can trigger this, so the risk surface is large.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission stores Resource DB IDs instead of group IDs
body: Inside the lambda passed to resourceStore.findByType(...) (around line 121) the code uses groupResource.getId() both as the argument to hasPermission and as the value added to the granted set. The Resource model's id is the database primary key (a UUID), but hasPermission does resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId) (lookup by name, not by id) and the all-V2 group resources are named with the group id (see AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup which returns group.getId()). A UUID never matches a resource name, so hasPermission always falls through to the all-groups fallback for every individual group, and the granted set is filled with Resource DB UUIDs rather than group ids. As soon as a caller only has the all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS / MANAGE_MEMBERS permission (no per-group grants), getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns a non-empty set of UUIDs that no real group matches, UsersResource.searchForUserStream filters by these bogus ids and returns zero users even though the caller should see members of every group. The bug is latent because the test scenarios always grant per-group permissions (so the fallback policyStore.isEmpty() short-circuits to false and the granted set stays empty), but in production this manifests as 'admin has all-groups permission yet sees no users'.

title: getResourceName is not taught the Groups resource type
body: getResourceName (around line 332) only special-cases USERS.getType() and falls through to resource.getDisplayName() for everything else. With the new GROUPS resource type the all-groups resource will report its raw name 'Groups' (or whatever getDisplayName returns on top of that), and per-group resources will report their UUID name (because individual group resources are created with name = group.getId() and no displayName is set). It should mirror the Users branch and return 'All groups' / the resolved GroupModel.getName() for the new resource type so error messages, evaluation logs and admin UIs show meaningful labels.

title: Stray double semicolon on the topGroup field initializer
body: Line 68 declares `private final GroupRepresentation topGroup = new GroupRepresentation();;` with two semicolons. It compiles but is a typo worth cleaning up since the rest of the file uses single semicolons consistently.

title: testManageGroupMembership does not verify that joinGroup actually linked the user
body: The last action of testManageGroupMembership (line 306) is `realmAdminClient.realm(realm.getName()).users().get(bobId).joinGroup(topGroup.getId());` without any assertion or follow-up read. The test only distinguishes 'threw' from 'returned cleanly', but if the implementation silently returned a non-error response (e.g. a 404 swallowed by the admin client) the test would still pass even though Bob was never actually joined to topGroup. Add an explicit assertion that lists Bob's group memberships afterwards and contains topGroup.getId().

title: V2 canManage() grants management from VIEW scope
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() the V2 permission fallback uses hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE). Because the implementation returns true when the caller has the VIEW scope on the all-groups resource, an admin who was granted only view on all-groups will pass canManage() and therefore requireManage(). The only call site in this PR is GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup, which would then let a view-only admin create new top-level realm groups, even though they are not allowed to update or delete groups (per-group requireManage(group) correctly checks only MANAGE). canManage() must check only the MANAGE scope, not VIEW. The per-group counterpart canManage(GroupModel) is implemented correctly and only requests AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE.

title: Javadoc for canManage() documents the buggy behavior
body: The new Javadoc on GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage() states 'For V2 only: Also if it has permission to AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW or AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE groups.' This was added in this PR and matches the buggy GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() implementation, but the documented contract is wrong: VIEW on all-groups must not imply management. The contract for canView() right below it is correct (VIEW or MANAGE), reinforcing that canManage() should only require MANAGE. The Javadoc should be corrected to 'Also if it has a permission to AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE groups' so it does not codify the privilege escalation.

title: No test for view-only on all-groups being denied for management
body: The new GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest only covers granting MANAGE on all-groups (testManageAllGroups) and granting MANAGE/VIEW on individual groups. It never grants only the VIEW scope on all-groups and asserts that POST /admin/realms/{realm}/groups is forbidden. Because of the canManage() bug described above, that assertion would currently fail, so the test gap is what allowed the regression to slip in. A test granting only the all-groups VIEW scope and then calling add(new GroupRepresentation()) and expecting 403 would both document the intended contract and catch this bug.

title: resolveGroup() never resolves by name/path while resolveUser() does
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() dispatches the GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE case to resolveGroup(), which only attempts session.groups().getGroupById(realm, id) and returns group.getId() verbatim. The sibling resolveUser() also falls back to session.users().getUserByUsername(realm, id) and resolveClient() falls back to getClientByClientId(...). The asymmetric handling means that if a caller passes a group name or path instead of the internal id (a plausible mistake when constructing policies), resolveGroup() will return null and getOrCreateResource() will throw IllegalStateException('Could not map resource object ...'). At minimum the method should attempt the by-name lookup for symmetry, or this limitation should be called out in the class Javadoc.

title: canManage() lost its 'for V1 only' admin default fallback when V2 was added
body: The diff replaced 'return root.users().canManageDefault()' in GroupPermissions.canManage() with 'return root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS)'. canManageDefault() was removed from UserPermissions in the same PR. The change is semantically equivalent for the remaining caller, but it means GroupPermissionsV2 can no longer be re-entered through the old canManageDefault() hook. More importantly, callers that were updated to use root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS) directly (e.g. RolePermissions.canMapRole) no longer go through any wrapper that can be changed centrally. This is a minor maintainability concern, but it also means the previous 'canManageDefault' abstraction (which could one day include V2 logic) was removed in the same commit that added V2. Worth keeping in mind if V2 is later extended to model 'can manage users' differently.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission stores resource UUIDs instead of group IDs
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() the code iterates resources of type "Groups" and adds `groupResource.getId()` to the granted set. Resource IDs are UUIDs and are NOT real group IDs. Because V2 builds all-groups authorization on a single schema-typed resource rather than per-group resources, `findByName(server, groupResource.getId())` always returns null and execution falls back to `getResourceTypeResource(...)`. Any scenario where `hasPermission` succeeds (e.g. an admin granted VIEW_MEMBERS on the all-groups resource directly) results in the all-groups resource's UUID being added. Downstream consumers (UsersResource.getUsersCount, BruteForceUsersResource/UsersResource.searchForUser, which set `UserModel.GROUPS` to this set and pass it to `session.users().getUsersCount(..., groupIds)`/`searchForUserStream(..., GROUPS=...)`) treat these strings as group IDs. As a result, for an admin who only has VIEW_MEMBERS on all-groups, user search returns zero users and the count endpoint reports zero even though the admin should see users of all groups. V1's equivalent uses `resource.getName().substring(RESOURCE_NAME_PREFIX.length())`; V2 needs to either return group IDs (resource names) or adopt a sentinel "all groups" semantics understood by callers, plus the search/count code must be consistent with the chosen semantics. This is not covered by the existing tests, which only grant view-members on specific groups.

title: NullPointerException risk in hasPermission when getResourceTypeResource returns null
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission, after `resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)` the code immediately calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()`. However, AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource returns null when `supportsAuthorizationSchema(session, resourceServer)` is false (e.g. the admin permissions client lookup fails or the schema resource has not yet been initialized at very early lifecycle stages). Calling `policyStore.findByResource(server, null)` will pass null into the policy store, which throws NullPointerException. Add a null check on the result of `getResourceTypeResource` before the findByResource call and return false if null. The same pattern exists in UserPermissionsV2.java at line 111.

title: Same null-deref risk as in GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission
body: The UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission method assigns the result of `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` to `resource` and then unconditionally passes it to `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()`. If `getResourceTypeResource` returns null (it can, per AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource when supportsAuthorizationSchema is false), this throws NPE. Add a null check.

title: getResourceName ignores GROUPS resource type
body: getResourceName only contains a branch for `USERS.getType().equals(resourceType)`. With GROUPS now a first-class resource type in SCHEMA, policies for groups fall through to `return resource.getDisplayName();`. For specific group resources the `getName()` is the group's ID (per `resolveGroup`) and the display name is typically unset, so the admin UI and policy listings will show an empty string or the group id rather than the group's actual name. Add a parallel branch similar to the users branch that resolves the GroupModel by `resource.getName()` and returns `group.getName()` (and for the "all-groups" schema resource return a label such as "All groups"). This is a function gap introduced by adding the GROUPS resource type without updating this method.

title: Missing permission.getResourceId() filter, inconsistent with UserPermissionsV2
body: GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission iterates returned permissions checking only the scope names, without verifying `permission.getResourceId().equals(resource.getId())`. The corresponding UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission does include this check. If `root.evaluatePermission(...)` ever returns a permission whose resource is not the one we are evaluating (e.g. due to policy inheritance or shared scope names across resource types), GroupPermissionsV2 would grant access based on that foreign permission. For parity with UserPermissionsV2 and to avoid potential cross-resource grants, add `if (permission.getResourceId().equals(resource.getId()))` around the inner scope loop.

title: Double semicolon on field initializer
body: `private final GroupRepresentation topGroup = new GroupRepresentation();;` contains a stray second semicolon. It is legal Java but is a lint-grade mistake worth fixing.

title: registerListener now only registers when FGAP V1 feature is enabled at startup
body: The previous behavior registered a ProviderEventListener unconditionally and gated the handler body with a `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` check at every event. The change moves the check outside so the listener is only registered when the V1 feature is enabled. This is functionally equivalent for static feature flags, but it is a behavioral contract change: callers that rely on registering then toggling the feature flag, or that replay events captured before the flag was disabled, will not see the old gating. Either keep registration unconditional (for runtime-toggle safety) or document the new behavior. Not a bug per se but worth a note in commit message / release notes.

title: Method name typo 'santizeAnchors' instead of 'sanitizeAnchors'
body: The new method is named `santizeAnchors`, missing the 'i'. This typo will propagate to any logs, error messages, or future callers, and makes the code harder to maintain. It should be `sanitizeAnchors`.

title: Narrow literal removal of '<!-- -->' may miss sanitizer variants
body: The code unconditionally does `sanitized = sanitized.replace("<!-- -->", "");` to strip the comment separator that the OWASP sanitizer inserts between adjacent text blocks. However, the sanitizer emits comments with varying internal whitespace (e.g. `<!--  -->`, `<!--->`), so this literal replacement leaves artifacts behind. As a result, when the sanitizer splits adjacent text blocks the verifier can still register a spurious difference and incorrectly flag the translation as containing illegal HTML. A regex such as `<!--\s*-->` should be used.

title: IOException from missing English counterpart is wrapped as RuntimeException
body: In `verifySafeHtml`, when the English counterpart file cannot be opened, the IOException is caught and rethrown as `new RuntimeException("unable to read file " + englishFile, e)`. The other I/O failure paths in the class surface errors via `MojoExecutionException` (declared on the public `verify` method) so this RuntimeException is inconsistent and bypasses the standard failure reporting of the Maven plugin. Additionally, if a translation is added before its English source lands (e.g. a brand-new locale) the verification will crash instead of skipping or warning. There is also no test for this scenario.

title: English-file path derivation uses a regex that can map unrelated locales to _en
body: The expression `file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll("resources-community", "resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")` matches any underscore-prefixed locale segment (the inner character class includes `-` and `_` so the suffix can contain hyphens too). It will therefore map, for instance, `messages_zh_TW.properties` to `messages_en.properties` instead of `messages_zh_Hant.properties`/etc., and will silently turn `messages_.properties` into `messages_en.properties`. There is no test that asserts the English counterpart is selected correctly for non-`_en` locales.

title: HTML_TAGS regex only matches lowercase HTML tags
body:
`Pattern HTML_TAGS = Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>")` only matches tags whose name begins with one or more ASCII lowercase letters, so `containsHtml` returns false for tags such as `
`, `

`, `
`, or attributes-only constructs. When the English source happens to use uppercase tags, POLICY_NO_HTML is incorrectly selected and the OWASP sanitizer is then forced to make a structural decision that POLICY_SOME_HTML was meant to handle, producing false positives. Case-insensitive matching (`(?i)<[a-z]+[^>]*>`) or explicit handling of uppercase letters is needed.

title: Anchor sanitizer can incorrectly flag repeated/misordered anchors
body: In `santizeAnchors` the local `Matcher matcher` is created from the original `value`, while the loop also reassigns `value = value.replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(englishMatcher.group()), "")`. The Matcher still searches the unstripped original, but its `find()` advancement combined with `englishMatcher.find()` advancement causes two false-positive scenarios: 1. If the translation legitimately repeats the same anchor (e.g. `link ... link`) while English has only one, the second translation anchor finds no remaining English anchor and the method reports "Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string" even though no malicious anchor was added. 2. If a translation reorders two anchors relative to English, the first match succeeds and removes the first anchor from `value`, then the second translation anchor is compared against the (now second) English anchor and is flagged as missing. Both cases will be reported as illegal anchor use even when the resulting sanitized HTML is identical to the English source. The matcher state should be re-derived from the modified `value` after each successful replacement, or the comparison should be done on the anchor sets rather than positionally.

title: No test coverage for missing English source file
body: There is no test that exercises the case where a translation file's English counterpart is absent or unreadable. `verifySafeHtml` will throw a `RuntimeException` (wrapping a `FileNotFoundException`) in that case, crashing the whole verification rather than reporting a clean error. A regression test calling `verify()` on a translation whose derived `_en` path does not exist should be added and the method should translate the IOException into `MojoExecutionException` to match the rest of the class.

title: No test exercises the new anchor path on real translations
body: The anchor sanitizer is the only defense against a translator pointing an existing English anchor at a malicious URL (the test fixture does cover that), but there is no test that verifies the case where a translation uses the same anchor as English and is therefore silently stripped without error. Likewise there is no test for the `<0>...</0>`/`<1>...</1>` style parameterized placeholders that many `messages_*.properties` files use (e.g. `resourceSharedWith_one`). Because `HTML_TAGS` does not match `<0>` etc., the verifier will select POLICY_NO_HTML for those values, and the OWASP sanitizer (which treats `<0>` as an unknown tag) will strip them, causing the verifier to flag legitimate translations as illegal HTML. This should be tested explicitly and either the policy decision or the normalize step needs to handle `<n>` placeholders.

title: Lithuanian totpStep1 translated into Italian instead of Lithuanian
body: The value of totpStep1 was changed from a valid Lithuanian sentence containing FreeOTP/Google Play anchor tags to Italian text 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'. Lithuanian users will see a message in the wrong language. The new value is also identical to the login theme's loginTotpStep1, suggesting the author copy-pasted the wrong source translation.

title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 translated into Italian instead of Lithuanian
body: The value of loginTotpStep1 was changed from a valid Lithuanian sentence containing FreeOTP/Google Play anchor tags to Italian text 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'. Lithuanian users will see a login message in the wrong language.

title: verifySafeHtml throws RuntimeException instead of MojoExecutionException for IO errors
body: When the properties file cannot be read, verifySafeHtml throws a plain RuntimeException. The enclosing verify() method declares throws MojoExecutionException and the sibling verifyNoDuplicateKeys uses MojoExecutionException. A RuntimeException here causes the Maven build to fail with a confusing stack trace instead of the standard 'MojoExecutionException: Can not read file ...' error, and it bypasses Mojo error reporting. The same problem exists on line 79 for the English file.

title: PolicyFactory and HTML_TAGS Pattern are instance fields but immutable
body: POLICY_SOME_HTML, POLICY_NO_HTML, and HTML_TAGS are declared as instance fields but are created from constants (no per-instance state). They should be static to avoid rebuilding the OWASP PolicyFactory and compiling the regex for every VerifyMessageProperties instance. The ANCHOR_PATTERN on line 145 is correctly static; the others should be too.

title: Typo in method name santizeAnchors
body: The helper method is named 'santizeAnchors' (missing the 'i'). It should be 'sanitizeAnchors' to be consistent with the other spelling in the same class (sanitized, sanitize). This is a public-ish helper used from verifySafeHtml and is easy to fix before merge.

title: verifyDuplicateKeysDetected assertion relaxed from contains to hasItem
body: The duplicate-key test was changed from 'Matchers.contains(...)' (exact list match) to 'Matchers.hasItem(...)' (only checks one item is present). This is a regression in test strictness: additional error messages for the same key (e.g., a future Illegal HTML detection on the same fixture) would no longer cause the test to fail, masking real regressions. The original stricter assertion should be retained, possibly by asserting the list size or by separating the duplicate-key case into its own fixture.

title: Italian text placed in Lithuanian translation file (loginTotpStep1)
body: The loginTotpStep1 value was changed from a Lithuanian sentence beginning with 'Įdiekite' to Italian 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'. This is the wrong language for the lt (Lithuanian) messages file. Lithuanian users of the login UI will see the Italian sentence instead of a localized one, which is a regression versus the prior Lithuanian content (e.g. a proper translation would start with 'Įdiekite').

title: Italian text placed in Lithuanian translation file (totpStep1)
body: The totpStep1 value was changed from a Lithuanian sentence beginning with 'Įdiekite' to Italian 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'. This is the wrong language for the lt (Lithuanian) messages file. Lithuanian users of the account UI will see the Italian sentence instead of a localized one.

title: RuntimeException on missing English reference aborts whole verification
body: verifySafeHtml() computes the English reference path by replacing 'resources-community' with 'resources' and the language suffix with '_en.properties'. When the resulting English file does not exist (for example, when only a translations file exists in resources-community and no English counterpart lives in resources/), new FileInputStream(englishFile) throws IOException which is wrapped in a RuntimeException. This RuntimeException is not caught by the try-catch in verify() (which only handles IOException), so it propagates out of verify() and aborts the Maven build entirely - including the duplicate-key checks that already ran successfully for that file. The sanitizer should at minimum catch this and record a message rather than failing the build.

title: Matcher state is stale after value is reassigned in santizeAnchors
body: In santizeAnchors(), the matcher is created against the value at method entry: `Matcher matcher = ANCHOR_PATTERN.matcher(value)`. Inside the while loop, `value = value.replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(englishMatcher.group()), "")` reassigns the local `value` variable, but the matcher continues to operate on the ORIGINAL character sequence it was bound to at construction time. On the next iteration, matcher.find() continues scanning the ORIGINAL value while value.replaceFirst(...) acts on the (already-modified) current value. This divergence can cause: (a) the wrong occurrence of an anchor being removed when value contains multiple copies of the same anchor, (b) stale positions when anchors shift after previous removals, and (c) the loop iterating past anchors that were already removed from the current value. The matcher needs to be recreated (or `value` re-assigned to a freshly-built matcher) after each replaceFirst.

title: Typo in method name 'santizeAnchors'
body: The method name is spelled 'santizeAnchors' (missing the 'i' in 'sanitize'). It should be 'sanitizeAnchors'.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher is broken: reversed logic and wrong substring indices
body: The new `isAccessTokenId` matcher is supposed to verify that an access token id has the form `<sessionType 2><tokenType 2><grantType 2>:<uuid>` and that the grant shortcut equals `expectedGrantShortcut`. Instead, `items[0].substring(3, 5)` extracts index 3 (last char of token type) and index 4 (first char of grant type), so it never matches any real 2-char grant shortcut — for the existing grants it virtually never equals `expectedGrantShortcut`, so the `if (...) return false;` early-out is never taken. And the logic is inverted: to require equality one must write `if (!substring.equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`, not `if (substring.equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. The correct read should be `items[0].substring(4, 6)`. As a result every newly updated `expectCodeToToken`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh` and `expectAuthReqIdToToken` event assertion silently degrades to a plain UUID check on the suffix, so the integration tests do not actually validate the grant type encoded into the access token id by the new SPI. A regression in the encoding (wrong prefix, wrong grant mapping) would slip through CI undetected.

title: AccessTokenContext constructor never validates rawTokenId for null
body: Line 73 reads `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` — a copy-paste of the previous line: it again checks `grantType` and uses a wrong error message. The intended `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` is missing. The promised non-null contract on `rawTokenId` is therefore not enforced. `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId` then happily appends `'null'` after the ':' producing malformed ids (e.g. `onrtac:null`), and `getTokenContextFromTokenId` on the receiver side gets back `null` for `rawTokenId`, breaking the round-trip and any later lookup logic that depends on the real jti.

title: getShortcut() Javadoc says "3-letters" but codec uses a fixed 2-char position
body: The new method's Javadoc reads "usually like 3-letters shortcut of specific grants", but `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` always splits the encoded id at fixed 2-char positions (`substring(4, 6)` for grant type) and `getTokenContextFromTokenId` enforces `encodedContext.length() != 6`.
