The real problem: the client-side length validation does not normalize the input — a user could enter `XXXXX-XXXXX` but also `XXXXXX-XXXX` (still 11 chars) which the server would strip to 10 chars and reject. More importantly, there is no `pattern` validation restricting to hex characters, so non-hex input of the right length passes client validation and fails server-side with a generic error. Add a `pattern="[0-9a-fA-F-]{10,11}"` (or normalize on submit) and ensure the registered value is normalized (dashes stripped) before submission.

title: formatBackupCode is used before its declaration (temporal dead zone risk) and defined inside component body
body: `formatBackupCode` is referenced at line 95 inside `handleSetup` (`body.backupCodes.map(formatBackupCode)`) but is declared with `const` at line 163, AFTER the `handleSetup` function definition. Because `handleSetup` is only invoked at runtime (after the component has fully rendered and `formatBackupCode` is initialized), this works due to closure semantics — but it is fragile and confusing. If `handleSetup` were ever called during render or if the declaration order changed, it would throw a ReferenceError. Move `formatBackupCode` above `handleSetup` (or to module scope) for clarity and safety.

title: backupCodes state is untyped (never[]) causing implicit any in map
body: `const [backupCodes, setBackupCodes] = useState([])` infers type `never[]`. When `setBackupCodes(body.backupCodes)` is called with `any` (from `response.json()`), TypeScript does not error because `any` is assignable, but `backupCodes.map((code) => ...)` at line 203 has `code` implicitly typed. This loses type safety — if the API shape changes, no compile error will catch it. Type the state as `useState<string[]>([])`.

title: Object URL for backup codes download is never revoked on unmount
body: `URL.createObjectURL(textBlob)` creates `backupCodesUrl`, and it is revoked only when a NEW setup creates another URL (`if (backupCodesUrl) URL.revokeObjectURL(backupCodesUrl)`). If the user closes the modal without re-running setup, or the component unmounts, the object URL is never revoked, leaking memory. Add a `useEffect` cleanup that revokes `backupCodesUrl` on unmount.

title: Backup code and TOTP code are both registered in the same form and both submitted, allowing ambiguous server-side branch selection
body: The login form registers both `totpCode` (via TwoFactor's hidden input) and `backupCode` (via BackupCode's TextField) in the same react-hook-form. When the user switches between TOTP and backup-code modes (via the 'Lost access' / 'Go back' buttons), the code clears the other field with `methods.setValue("totpCode", "")` or `methods.setValue("backupCode", "")`, but `setValue` does not trigger re-validation or necessarily clear the DOM input value for uncontrolled inputs. On submit, `signIn` sends ALL form values including `email`, `password`, `totpCode`, `backupCode`, and `csrfToken`. The server-side logic in `next-auth-options.ts` checks `credentials.backupCode` FIRST — so if a stale `totpCode` value remains in the form state (e.g. user typed a TOTP, switched to backup code, the setValue didn't clear the hidden input's value), the server may receive both and take the backup-code path even though the user intended TOTP, or vice versa. The form should unregister the unused field when switching modes (`methods.unregister("totpCode")` / `methods.unregister("backupCode")`) or the submit handler should explicitly send only the relevant field.

title: Zod schema makes password optional when totpEmail is present, but backup-code login still requires password on server
body: The form schema sets `password: !!totpEmail ? z.literal("") : z.string().min(1)`. When arriving via the TOTP JWT flow (`totpEmail` set), the password field is hidden and empty. However, the server-side authorize() in `next-auth-options.ts` still verifies the password when `user.password && !credentials.totpCode` — and when using a backup code, `credentials.totpCode` is empty, so the server WILL attempt password verification with an empty string and reject with `IncorrectEmailPassword`. This means the 'Lost access' backup-code flow is BROKEN for users arriving via the `totp` JWT redirect (external TOTP flow), because no password is collected but the server demands it. The backup-code branch on the server must either skip password verification when arriving via the TOTP JWT flow (trusting the JWT), or the login page must collect the password in backup-code mode. As written, a user who clicks 'Lost access' on the TOTP screen cannot log in with a backup code.

title: E2E test uses prisma without importing it; test will fail at runtime
body: The test references `prisma?.user.findFirst(...)` at lines 64 and 141, but there is no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"` (or similar) at the top of the file. The imports only include `@playwright/test`, `otplib`, `@calcom/lib/crypto`, `@calcom/lib/totp`, and `./lib/fixtures`. This will cause a ReferenceError at runtime when the 'Login with 2FA enabled' or 'Disable 2FA' steps execute. Add the missing prisma import.

title: No test coverage for backup-code login or backup-code disable flows despite being the core feature
body: The PR description says 'enable their use during 2fa login flow' and the test file even has a TODO: 'add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup'. The only backup-code-related test additions are UI checks for the download/copy/close buttons during setup. There is NO test that: (1) logs in using a backup code via the 'Lost access' flow, (2) verifies a used backup code cannot be reused, (3) disables 2FA using a backup code, or (4) verifies the backup-code branch in the disable endpoint. These are the primary new security-sensitive paths and they are completely untested. Add e2e tests that exercise backup-code login (including reuse rejection) and backup-code-based 2FA disable.

title: Toggle button lacks type="button" and is inside a form, causing accidental form submission
body: The 'Lost access' / 'Go back' toggle Button at line 113-121 is rendered inside a `<Form>` (which wraps a `<form>` element). The Button component likely defaults to `type="submit"` (common in this codebase's Button). Clicking 'Lost access' would submit the form, triggering `handleDisable` with empty/partial values instead of just toggling the state. Add `type="button"` to this Button to prevent implicit form submission.

title: Download link wraps a Button in an anchor without preventing default or ensuring href is set before render
body: The download `<a download="cal-backup-codes.txt" href={backupCodesUrl}>` wraps a `<Button>`. On the DisplayBackupCodes step, `backupCodesUrl` is set during `handleSetup` before `setStep(SetupStep.DisplayQrCode)`, so by the time the user reaches DisplayBackupCodes it should be populated. However, if the component re-renders before the state update completes, or if `backupCodesUrl` is empty string, the anchor has `href=""` and clicking it navigates to the current page. Additionally, nesting a `<button>` inside an `<a>` is invalid HTML (interactive content cannot be nested). Use a Button with `onClick` that programmatically triggers the download (e.g. creating a temporary anchor), or use an `<a>` styled as a button without a nested Button component.

title: Setup endpoint returns plaintext backup codes in the API response and stores them encrypted as a single blob
body: The setup endpoint returns `{ secret, keyUri, dataUri, backupCodes }` where `backupCodes` is the plaintext array. While this is necessary to display them once to the user, the codes are also persisted in the DB as `symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes))` — a single encrypted blob containing all plaintext codes. This means: (1) the API response exposes all codes to anyone with a valid session (acceptable for setup, but should be rate-limited and ideally one-time), (2) the DB stores recoverable plaintext codes (encrypted at rest, but the encryption key is in env and the codes are not individually hashed), so a DB+env compromise reveals all backup codes. The endpoint also has no rate limiting — an authenticated user could call setup repeatedly (after disabling 2FA) to enumerate codes, though this is low risk. More importantly, the codes should be hashed before storage (store only hashes, return plaintext once), so that DB leaks do not expose usable backup codes.

title: Third-party identity provider check is bypassed when backupCode is supplied
body: The check `if (user.identityProvider !== IdentityProvider.CAL && !credentials.totpCode)` throws `ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled` only when `totpCode` is absent. If a user has a Google/SAML identity provider AND 2FA enabled (possible via the `loginWithTotp` flow for OAuth users), and an attacker supplies a `backupCode` (without `totpCode`), this check is skipped because `credentials.totpCode` is empty — wait, actually `!credentials.totpCode` is true when totpCode is empty, so the check WOULD throw. But then the next check `if (!user.password && user.identityProvider !== IdentityProvider.CAL && !credentials.totpCode)` also throws `IncorrectEmailPassword`. However, if a backupCode is supplied, `credentials.totpCode` is empty, so both checks trigger and reject. The real issue: for OAuth users with 2FA, the backup-code flow requires `credentials.totpCode` to be empty (to pass the identity provider checks), but then the backup-code branch runs. This is actually consistent. The subtle bug: the condition `!credentials.totpCode` is used as a proxy for 'this is a first-factor-only attempt', but when a backupCode is supplied, totpCode is empty, so the identity-provider checks run — which is correct. However, the password check at line 121 `if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)` runs for backup-code attempts, meaning OAuth users (no password) with 2FA cannot use backup codes because `user.password` is null and the check is skipped, but then the backup-code branch runs without any first-factor verification. An OAuth user with 2FA enabled who arrives via `loginWithTotp` JWT has already proven identity via the JWT, so this is acceptable — but the logic is convoluted and fragile. The conditions should be restructured to explicitly handle the three cases: (1) first-factor only (email+password), (2) TOTP second factor, (3) backup code second factor, each with clear preconditions.

title: Nested form element inside DialogContent Form creates invalid HTML and double submission handlers
body: The `ConfirmPassword` step renders a `<form onSubmit={handleSetup}>` (line 172) INSIDE the outer `<Form handleSubmit={handleEnable} form={form}>` (line 209). This nests a `<form>` inside a `<form>`, which is invalid HTML — browsers will typically drop the inner form tag, causing `handleSetup` to never fire via form submission. The 'Continue' button at line 233 has `onClick={handleSetup}` AND `type="submit"`, so it works via the onClick, but pressing Enter in the password field may submit the outer form (triggering `handleEnable` with an empty totpCode) instead of `handleSetup`. This is a real UX bug: pressing Enter in the password field may trigger the wrong handler. The inner `<form>` should be removed and the password field should be part of the outer form, or the steps should be restructured to avoid nested forms.

title: callbackUrl slash stripping regex is incorrect and can mangle valid URLs
body: `if (/"\//.test(callbackUrl)) callbackUrl = callbackUrl.substring(1);` — the regex `/"\//` tests for a literal double-quote followed by a forward slash (`"/`), not just a leading slash. This was likely intended to be `/^\//` (leading slash). As written, it only strips the first character if the URL contains a `"/` sequence anywhere, which is wrong. A callbackUrl like `/booking` (leading slash, no quote) will NOT be stripped, then the next check `if (!/^https?:\/\//.test(callbackUrl))` prepends WEBAPP_URL, producing `https://app.cal.com//booking` (double slash). This is a pre-existing bug but is in the changed file and affects the login flow with backup codes. Fix the regex to `/^\//`.

title: Null-dereference when destinationCalendar is empty: mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration throws
body: In EventManager.create(), the code does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then immediately accesses `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without a null check. When destinationCalendar is an empty array (which is now a valid, explicitly constructed value in many call sites, e.g. handleNewBooking.ts sets `destinationCalendar: ... : null` but other call sites pass `[]`), destructuring yields `undefined` and `.integration` throws a TypeError, crashing event creation for any booking with no destination calendar. The guard must be `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

title: updateEvent/deleteEvent look up destination calendar by externalId === externalCalendarId, which is always undefined when externalCalendarId is falsy
body: In updateEvent (line 254-256) and deleteEvent (line 315-317), the fallback when `externalCalendarId` is not provided is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. Since the branch is only taken when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` compares a string to `undefined`/`null`/`""` and never matches, so `selectedCalendar`/`calendarId` is always undefined and the code silently falls back to "primary" (updateEvent) or "primary" (deleteEvent). For events stored on a non-primary destination calendar, updates and deletes will target the wrong calendar (or fail with 404), leaving stale events on the real calendar. The lookup should match by `credentialId` (as createEvent does) or use the first destination calendar entry.

title: Hangout-link patch uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar` which may be undefined, breaking the Meet link update
body: In createEvent, after `calendar.events.insert` succeeds with `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`, the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` (line 166-168) passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar` without the `|| "primary"` fallback. When no destination calendar matches the credential (selectedCalendar is undefined), the patch is sent with `calendarId: undefined`, so Google's API will reject or misroute it and the event description will never be updated with the Meet hangout link. This is a regression from the previous code which used the same resolved `selectedCalendar` variable that already included the "primary" fallback.

title: createAllCalendarEvents: when destination has no credentialId, createEvent is called without externalId, so per-destination calendar selection is lost
body: In the `else` branch of createAllCalendarEvents (line 375-382), for a destination calendar entry without a `credentialId`, the code calls `createEvent(c, event)` without passing `destination.externalId`. The `createEvent` signature in CalendarManager now accepts `externalId` and the GoogleCalendarService uses it (via credentialId matching) to pick the right calendar, but here it is omitted, so every credential of that integration type will create the event on its own primary/first calendar rather than the specific destination calendar the host selected. For collective events with multiple hosts each having their own calendar app, this creates events on the wrong calendars. The call should be `createEvent(c, event, destination.externalId)`.

title: updateAllCalendarEvents: updateEvent may be called with an undefined credential, causing a crash or failed update
body: In updateAllCalendarEvents, when `reference.credentialId` is set, the code looks up the credential in `this.calendarCredentials` and, if not found, fetches it from the DB. But if the DB fetch also fails (credential deleted, or belongs to another host not in this EventManager instance), `credential` remains `undefined` and line 542 still calls `updateEvent(credential, event, bookingRefUid, calenderExternalId)`. `updateEvent` in CalendarManager immediately does `getCalendar(credential)` / `credential.id`, which will throw on undefined. For collective events where the EventManager is constructed with only the organizer's credentials, references belonging to other hosts' credentials will hit this path and throw, aborting the whole update loop (caught by the outer try/catch which then returns failure results for ALL references). The code must skip the reference (or push a failed result) when `credential` is undefined.

title: Only the first destination calendar is persisted on the booking; additional hosts' destination calendars are dropped
body: When creating the booking record, the code does `destinationCalendar: evt.destinationCalendar && evt.destinationCalendar.length > 0 ? { connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id } } : undefined`. The Booking model has a single `destinationCalendar` relation, so only the organizer's (first) destination calendar is stored. The additional team hosts' destination calendars that were pushed into `evt.destinationCalendar` (teamDestinationCalendars) are used for event creation but are not persisted anywhere on the booking. On reschedule/cancel, the code rebuilds `destinationCalendar` from `booking.destinationCalendar || user.destinationCalendar`, so the other hosts' calendars are lost and their calendar events will not be updated/deleted correctly. This is a data-integrity gap: the PR's stated goal (hosts get invited correctly on reschedule/cancel) is only partially achieved because the multi-host destination info is not stored.

title: teamDestinationCalendars only collects destination calendars for COLLECTIVE scheduling, but evt.destinationCalendar push is also gated on COLLECTIVE while round-robin hosts are silently dropped
body: The collection of team hosts' destination calendars (line 987-991) and the push into evt.destinationCalendar (line 1075-1077) are both gated on `eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE"`. For ROUND_ROBIN team events, only one host is booked per slot, but that host may not be users[0] (the organizer); the code only ever uses `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` (or eventType.destinationCalendar) and never the selected round-robin host's destination calendar. The chosen host's calendar app therefore does not receive the event. At minimum this is inconsistent with the PR's goal; the destination calendar should be resolved from the actually-booked host(s).

title: Recurring-event cancellation deletes events for ALL of the organizer's calendar credentials, not just the reference's credential
body: In the recurring + allRemainingBookings branch (lines 444-468), for each booking reference the code iterates over `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(type.endsWith("_calendar"))` and deletes the event from every one of the organizer's calendar credentials. For collective events with multiple hosts, `bookingToDelete.user` is only the organizer, so this loop deletes from the organizer's calendars repeatedly (once per reference) and never touches the other hosts' calendars, whose events are instead handled by the outer per-reference loop — but the outer loop only handles the non-recurring path correctly. The net effect: duplicate delete calls against the organizer's calendars and no deletion on other hosts' calendars for recurring collective bookings. The inner loop should use the specific `calendarCredential` resolved for the reference (as the non-recurring path does), not all of the user's credentials.

title: Cancel path builds destinationCalendar from only booking/user destinationCalendar, losing other hosts' calendars
body: The `evt.destinationCalendar` built for cancellation (lines 251-255 and 528-532) is `[bookingToDelete.destinationCalendar] || [bookingToDelete.user.destinationCalendar] || []`. For collective events with multiple hosts, only the organizer's destination calendar is included. The calendar services use `destinationCalendar[0]` (e.g. LarkCalendarService, BaseCalendarService, GoogleCalendarService's mainHostDestinationCalendar) to decide which calendar to delete/update from, so for cancellations the delete may be attempted against the organizer's calendar with an event uid that lives on another host's calendar, causing 404s (silently resolved in Google's deleteEvent) and leaving events on other hosts' calendars undeleted. The booking's references (which do store per-credential externalCalendarId) are the correct source; the evt should include all destination calendars or the delete should rely on reference.externalCalendarId (which it does pass, but Google's deleteEvent ignores externalCalendarId when it doesn't match a destinationCalendar entry — see the find-by-externalId bug).

title: Inverted IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED condition drops organization slug when billing is enabled
body: The diff flips `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` (and correspondingly for requestedSlug). This is unrelated to the destinationCalendar change and inverts the original logic: previously the slug was set when team billing was DISABLED; now it is only set when team billing is ENABLED. On instances where IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is false (the common self-hosted configuration), organizations will now be created without a slug, breaking organization subdomain routing. This looks like an accidental logic inversion introduced in this PR and should be reverted.

title: Calendar.createEvent signature now requires credentialId, but several implementations don't accept it — contract break for third-party/other calendar apps
body: The `Calendar` interface changed `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` to `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number)`. Only GoogleCalendarService was updated to accept and use `credentialId`. LarkCalendarService, Office365CalendarService, and BaseCalendarService (caldav/ical) still declare `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` with a single parameter. TypeScript structural typing permits implementations with fewer parameters, so this compiles, but the contract is now inconsistent: CalendarManager.createEvent always calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`, and any calendar service that needs to select a calendar per credential (as Google now does) cannot do so because the interface consumers other than Google ignore the second argument. More importantly, any external app implementing the old interface and relying on positional args is fine, but the interface no longer documents which implementations actually support per-credential selection. The interface and all implementations should be updated consistently (either all accept credentialId or the param should be optional).

title: createEvent passes credential.id as the second argument, but the Calendar interface's second parameter is named/typed as credentialId while GoogleCalendarService matches destinationCalendar by credentialId — semantics mismatch with externalId usage in EventManager
body: CalendarManager.createEvent calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` and also returns `externalId` (the third param passed from EventManager, which is `destination.externalId`). GoogleCalendarService.createEvent uses the second param (`credentialId`) to find the matching destination calendar: `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`. This works only if `destinationCalendar` entries carry a `credentialId`. However, `DestinationCalendar` (the Prisma model) does NOT have a `credentialId` field — it has `integration`, `externalId`, `userId`/`eventTypeId`. The `credentialId` only exists on `IntegrationCalendar`/`SelectedCalendar`. So `cal.credentialId === credentialId` will be `undefined === number` → false for all entries, `selectedCalendar` will be undefined, and every Google event falls back to "primary" — silently defeating the entire purpose of the PR for Google Calendar. The matching key must be something present on DestinationCalendar (e.g. match by `integration` type against `credential.type`, or look up the credential's calendars).

title: createAllCalendarEvents matches destination.credentialId against calendar credentials, but DestinationCalendar has no credentialId field
body: In createAllCalendarEvents, the code checks `if (destination.credentialId)` and then finds the credential by `c.id === destination.credentialId`. The `destinationCalendar` array on CalendarEvent is typed as `DestinationCalendar[]` (Prisma model), which has no `credentialId` column (only `integration`, `externalId`, `userId`, `eventTypeId`, `eventTypeId`). Therefore `destination.credentialId` is always `undefined` at runtime, the `if` branch is never taken, and the code always falls into the `else` branch which matches by `destination.integration` against `credential.type`. This means: (a) the DB-fetch fallback for credentials not in the EventManager's list is dead code, and (b) for collective events where the organizer's EventManager only holds the organizer's credentials, other hosts' destination calendars (whose credentials are not in `this.calendarCredentials`) result in an empty `destinationCalendarCredentials` filter and NO event is created on the other hosts' calendars — the exact scenario the PR claims to fix. The credential resolution must be based on fields that actually exist (integration type + user/host), or the destination calendar entries must carry the credential id.

title: Webhook e2e expectations for destinationCalendar are inconsistent (null vs []) and don't cover the new array shape
body: The BOOKING_CREATED test still expects `destinationCalendar: null` (line 119) while the BOOKING_REJECTED test was changed to expect `destinationCalendar: []` (line 249), and BOOKING_REQUESTED still expects `null` (line 373). With the type change to `DestinationCalendar[] | null`, the webhook payload will now be an array (possibly empty) rather than null in most paths. The tests are inconsistent with each other and likely with actual behavior; at least one of them will fail or is already masking a regression. The expectations should be unified to the actual serialized value (likely `[]`) and ideally a collective-event webhook test should be added to verify multiple destination calendars are serialized.

title: evt.destinationCalendar may be null when pushed to, causing a TypeError for collective events without any destination calendar
body: The code sets `destinationCalendar: eventType.destinationCalendar ? [eventType.destinationCalendar] : organizerUser.destinationCalendar ? [organizerUser.destinationCalendar] : null` (line ~1063), then unconditionally does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` (line 1075). The optional chaining protects against undefined, but if `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` (the explicit `: null` branch), `null?.push(...)` evaluates to `undefined` without throwing — so no crash, but the team destination calendars are silently dropped when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, even though team members do. The intent (fallback to normal behaviour but also support multiple) is not met in that case. The initial value should be `[]` instead of `null` so pushes always work.

title: Lark createEvent now throws when destinationCalendar is empty, whereas before it fell back to the primary calendar
body: Previously `const calendarId = event.destinationCalendar?.externalId;` yielded `undefined` when no destination calendar was set, and the code threw `new Error("no calendar id")` — so behavior is the same in the empty case. However, the new code `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` combined with the existing `if (!calendarId) throw` means that for collective events where the FIRST destination calendar entry is not the one matching this credential (Lark's createEvent has no credentialId parameter to select among multiple destinations), the event is created on the first host's calendar only, and other hosts' Lark calendars never get the event. Since the Calendar interface now passes credentialId but Lark ignores it, multi-host Lark support is incomplete. At minimum this is a functional gap versus the PR's stated goal; the credentialId parameter should be used to select the matching destination calendar.

title: BaseCalendarService (CalDAV/iCal) only creates the event on the first destination calendar, not on all hosts' calendars
body: In BaseCalendarService.createEvent, `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then the calendars list is filtered to only those matching `mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` (or all calendars if none set). For a collective event with multiple hosts each having a CalDAV calendar, only the first host's calendar receives the event; the other hosts' calendars are filtered out. Since CalDAV credentials are per-user and the EventManager creates one BaseCalendarService per credential, the correct behavior would be to create the event on the calendar matching the current credential (like GoogleCalendarService attempts via credentialId), not just the first destination calendar entry. As written, collective events with multiple CalDAV hosts only block/create on one host's calendar.

title: BrokenIntegrationEmail only reports the first destination calendar; multi-host breakage is misreported
body: The email template takes `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = calEvent.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and builds the message from only that entry. For collective events where a non-first host's calendar integration is broken, the email will name the wrong calendar (the first host's) or fall back to the generic "calendar" string. This is a minor UX/reporting issue but misleading. The email should list all destination calendars or the specific failing one (the caller knows which credential failed).

title: requestReschedule drops the user's destinationCalendar fallback that other handlers kept
body: The original code was `destinationCalendar: bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar || bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar` (a no-op fallback to itself, clearly a pre-existing bug). The new code is `bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar ? [bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar] : []`, which removes even the (broken) intent and never falls back to the user's destination calendar, unlike confirm.handler.ts, editLocation.handler.ts, and handleCancelBooking.ts which all fall back to `user.destinationCalendar`. For bookings without a booking-level destination calendar, the webhook payload and any downstream calendar operations will see an empty array instead of the organizer's calendar. The fallback to the organizer's destination calendar should be restored for consistency.

title: buildUIDCalendarEvent has an inverted guard that makes it always throw when users are set
body: The method reads `if (this.users && this.users.length > 0) { throw new Error("call buildUsers before calling this function"); }` — the condition is inverted. It should throw when users are NOT set (`!this.users || this.users.length === 0`), because the very next lines destructure `const [mainOrganizer] = this.users;` and use `mainOrganizer.username`, which crashes on an empty array. As written, calling buildUIDCalendarEvent after buildUsers (the correct order) always throws, and calling it before buildUsers crashes on `mainOrganizer.username`. This is a pre-existing bug unrelated to the PR but it directly affects the reschedule-email builder path touched by this change (requestReschedule.handler.ts uses CalendarEventBuilder/Director).

title: updateEvent/deleteEvent look up destination calendar by externalId instead of credentialId, always yielding undefined
body: In updateEvent (line 254-256) and deleteEvent (line 315-317), the fallback when externalCalendarId is not provided is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. Since externalCalendarId is falsy in that branch, `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` compares a string to undefined/null and can never match, so selectedCalendar/calendarId is always undefined and the code silently falls back to "primary" (update) or "primary" (delete). For collective events where the event lives on a host's non-primary calendar, reschedule/cancel will target the wrong calendar (or fail with 404 which is swallowed in deleteEvent), leaving stale events on the real calendar. The lookup should match by credentialId (as createEvent does at line 147-149) or the caller should always pass externalCalendarId.

title: Hangout-link patch uses possibly-undefined selectedCalendar as calendarId
body: In createEvent, after `calendar.events.insert` succeeds, the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` (line 166-177) uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar` directly. selectedCalendar is `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`, which is undefined when no destination calendar matches the credential (the insert then correctly used `selectedCalendar || "primary"` at line 154). Passing `calendarId: undefined` to the patch call will make the Google API request fail or hit an invalid endpoint, so the Meet hangout link is never written into the event description for hosts whose destination calendar entry doesn't carry a matching credentialId. It should use `selectedCalendar || "primary"` like the insert does.

title: Google Meet fallback check crashes or misfires because mainHostDestinationCalendar may be undefined
body: In EventManager.create, line 118-120: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` then `if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")`. When `evt.destinationCalendar` is null/undefined or an empty array, mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined and accessing `.integration` throws a TypeError, aborting event creation entirely for any Google Meet booking without a destination calendar. Even when defined, checking only the first destination calendar means a collective event whose first host uses Office365 but a later host uses Google Calendar will be incorrectly downgraded to Cal Video. The check should be `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"` (optional chaining) and ideally check whether ANY destination calendar is google_calendar.

title: createAllCalendarEvents only creates events for destination calendars, dropping other hosts' calendars and other_calendar integrations for collective events
body: The rewritten createAllCalendarEvents iterates `event.destinationCalendar` and creates one event per destination entry. However, for collective team events the PR's own handleNewBooking change pushes each host's destinationCalendar into evt.destinationCalendar, but the EventManager is constructed with only the organizer's credentials (`new EventManager(user)` in handleNewBooking). Inside the loop, when `destination.credentialId` is set, the code looks up the credential in `this.calendarCredentials` and, if not found, fetches it from the DB — that part is OK. But when `destination.credentialId` is NOT set (DestinationCalendar rows always have credentialId in the Prisma schema, but the type allows it to be absent), the else branch filters `this.calendarCredentials` by `destination.integration` — the organizer's credentials only — so a non-organizer host's calendar type won't be found and no event is created for that host. Additionally, the trailing block that creates events for all `other_calendar` credentials runs regardless, which is fine, but the primary per-host creation depends on the organizer's credential list containing every host's calendar credential, which it does not. The net effect: for collective events, hosts other than the organizer may never get calendar events created, which is exactly what issue #7754 is about.

title: Fallback when no destinationCalendar filters by type === "calendar" which matches no real credential type
body: In createAllCalendarEvents, the else branch (no destinationCalendar) does `this.calendarCredentials.filter((cred) => cred.type === "calendar")`. Real credential types are values like "google_calendar", "office365_calendar", "caldav_calendar" — none equals the literal "calendar". So when a user has no destination calendar configured, no calendar event is created at all (previously the code had the same filter, but combined with the destinationCalendar branch this means users without a destination calendar silently get no calendar event). The fallback should pick the first calendar credential (e.g. `[0]`) or filter by `cred.type.endsWith("_calendar")`.

title: updateAllCalendarEvents pushes promises into result array inside a for-loop without awaiting, mixing awaited and pending promises
body: In updateAllCalendarEvents, the loop `for (const reference of calendarReference) { ... result.push(updateEvent(credential, event, bookingRefUid, calenderExternalId)); ... }` pushes unawaited promises, and `return Promise.all(result)` at line 590 awaits them — that part is fine. However, when `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found in `this.calendarCredentials` and the DB fetch also fails (credentialFromDB null or app slug missing), `credential` remains undefined and `updateEvent(undefined, ...)` is called, which will throw inside updateEvent when it does `getCalendar(credential)` / accesses credential properties. The catch block at line 591 then converts this into a generic failure for ALL references, marking every calendar update as failed even though other references may have succeeded. A missing/deleted credential for one host should fail only that reference, not abort the whole batch.

title: Booking.destinationCalendar connect only persists the first destination calendar, dropping additional hosts' calendars for collective events
body: When creating the booking record, the code does `destinationCalendar: evt.destinationCalendar && evt.destinationCalendar.length > 0 ? { connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id } } : undefined`. The Booking model has a single destinationCalendar relation, so only the organizer's (first) destination calendar is persisted on the booking. The additional team hosts' destination calendars that were pushed into `evt.destinationCalendar` (teamDestinationCalendars) exist only on the in-memory CalendarEvent. On reschedule/cancel, handlers like handleCancelBooking build `destinationCalendar` from `bookingToDelete.destinationCalendar` (single) or `user.destinationCalendar`, so the extra hosts' calendars are lost and their calendar events won't be updated/deleted correctly. This is a data-integrity gap: the multi-host support only works at creation time, not on reschedule/cancel, unless references (which do store per-credential externalCalendarId/credentialId) are used — but handleCancelBooking's evt construction ignores references for destinationCalendar.

title: teamDestinationCalendars only collected for COLLECTIVE scheduling, silently dropping host calendars for ROUND_ROBIN
body: The code `if (isTeamEventType && eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE" && user.destinationCalendar) { teamDestinationCalendars.push(user.destinationCalendar); }` and later `if (isTeamEventType && eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE") { evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars); }` restricts multi-host destination calendars to COLLECTIVE events only. For ROUND_ROBIN team events (where a single host is chosen per booking), the chosen host may not be the organizer (users[0]), so the event is created on the organizer's calendar instead of the assigned host's calendar. The PR description says "supports multiple so host can get invited correctly" — round-robin hosts are equally affected. Either include ROUND_ROBIN here or ensure the round-robin-selected host's destination calendar is used.

title: Cancellation loops over all calendar references but deletes using each reference's uid against every user calendar credential, causing wrong/extra deletions for collective events
body: The new cancellation logic iterates `bookingCalendarReference` (all references with type containing "_calendar"). For each reference with a credentialId, it resolves the calendar and calls `calendar?.deleteEvent(uid, evt, externalCalendarId)` — that's correct per-reference. But in the recurring branch (lines 449-461) and in the no-credentialId branch (lines 473-482), it iterates ALL of `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` filtered by `_calendar` and deletes `bookingRef.uid` from each — for a collective booking with 2 hosts, the organizer's credential list only contains the organizer's calendars, so the second host's calendar event is never deleted (stale event remains). Conversely, for a single user with multiple calendar credentials connected, the same uid is deleted from every connected calendar, which may delete events that were never created (harmless due to 404 handling, but noisy). The deletion should be driven by the booking references (which store credentialId + externalCalendarId per calendar event), not by the organizer's full credential list.

title: Cancel evt.destinationCalendar only includes booking/user destination calendar, not all hosts' calendars, so calendar services pick the wrong calendar for collective events
body: The evt built for cancellation sets `destinationCalendar: bookingToDelete?.destinationCalendar ? [bookingToDelete?.destinationCalendar] : bookingToDelete?.user.destinationCalendar ? [bookingToDelete?.user.destinationCalendar] : []`. For collective events with multiple hosts, only one destination calendar is present. Calendar services like GoogleCalendarService.deleteEvent use `event.destinationCalendar?.find(...)` fallbacks and BaseCalendarService filters by the first entry — so deletion/update may target the organizer's calendar rather than the calendar where the event actually lives. The evt should aggregate destination calendars from all booking references (each reference has externalCalendarId + credentialId) or the booking should store all destination calendars. As written, cancel/reschedule for collective events can miss the second host's calendar event.

title: Inverted IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED condition drops organization slug when billing is enabled and sets it when disabled
body: The diff changed `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` and `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { requestedSlug: slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { requestedSlug: slug } : {})`. Wait — re-reading: original was `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }` (slug set when billing DISABLED) and new is `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}` (slug set when billing ENABLED). These are opposite semantics. Combined with the metadata line which kept `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { requestedSlug: slug } : {}`, the new code sets `slug` exactly when `requestedSlug` is set. On self-hosted instances without team billing (IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED=false), organizations would now be created WITHOUT a slug, breaking org subdomain routing (orgDomains relies on team.slug). This looks like an accidental logic inversion unrelated to the destinationCalendar change and will break organization creation on non-billing deployments.

title: buildUIDCalendarEvent throws when users exist instead of when they don't, and then dereferences possibly-undefined mainOrganizer
body: The method `buildUIDCalendarEvent()` starts with `if (this.users && this.users.length > 0) { throw new Error("call buildUsers before calling this function"); }` — the condition is inverted: it throws precisely when users HAVE been built (the correct precondition), and proceeds to `const [mainOrganizer] = this.users;` when users is empty/undefined, making mainOrganizer undefined and causing `mainOrganizer.username` to throw a TypeError. The guard should be `if (!this.users || this.users.length === 0)`. As written, any caller that correctly builds users first will get the error, and any caller that doesn't will crash on the next line.

title: Lark createEvent throws when no destination calendar is set, breaking bookings for users without a destination calendar
body: createEvent does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId; if (!calendarId) { throw new Error("no calendar id"); }`. Unlike Google/Office365 services which fall back to the primary calendar, Lark hard-fails when destinationCalendar is empty. Previously the code was `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` which also yielded undefined, but the previous behavior may have been to use a default; regardless, with the new array type, any Lark user without a destination calendar configured (destinationCalendar = []) will now get a thrown error on every booking creation, failing the whole event creation. It should fall back to the primary calendar (e.g. via listCalendars and picking primary) instead of throwing.

title: Calendar interface createEvent signature changed to require credentialId, breaking all other Calendar implementations that don't accept it
body: The `Calendar` interface now declares `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number): Promise<NewCalendarEventType>`. TypeScript method parameters are bivariant for method declarations, so implementations with fewer parameters (e.g. `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` in LarkCalendarService, Office365CalendarService, BaseCalendarService in packages/lib/CalendarService.ts) still satisfy the interface — but at runtime, CalendarManager.createEvent (packages/core/CalendarManager.ts line 236) calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`. For implementations that ignore the second argument, the destination calendar selection inside those services relies on `event.destinationCalendar[0]` (the organizer's), NOT the credential being invoked. This means for collective events, when EventManager iterates destination calendars and calls createEvent with host B's credential, the Lark/Office365/Caldav services will still create the event on the FIRST destination calendar (host A's) rather than the calendar matching the credentialId passed. The interface change is not honored by these implementations, so multi-host support silently degrades to "create N duplicate events on host A's calendar" for non-Google providers. Each implementation must use the credentialId to select the matching destination calendar entry (as GoogleCalendarService now does).

title: createEvent in CalendarManager accepts externalId but passes it into the result instead of using it to select the calendar
body: The new signature is `createEvent(credential, calEvent, externalId?)` and it calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` — passing credential.id, not externalId. The externalId is only attached to the returned EventResult. For GoogleCalendarService this works because it finds the destination calendar by credentialId. But the externalId parameter (destination.externalId from EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents line 370) is the specific calendar on that credential that should receive the event; by not passing it to the calendar service, services that support multiple calendars per credential (Google, Office365) will always pick the first destinationCalendar entry matching the credentialId, which may not be destination.externalId if a user has multiple destination calendar rows for the same credential. The externalId should be threaded through (e.g. as an additional parameter or by ensuring event.destinationCalendar contains the right entry) so the event lands on the intended calendar.

title: loadUsers rewrite changes behavior for dynamic group bookings and swallows errors into generic 500s
body: The loadUsers function was rewritten with a try/catch that throws `HttpError({ statusCode: 500, message: "Unable to load users" })` for any non-HttpError/non-Prisma error, and it removed the `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the dynamic user query. Downstream code that relied on `user.organization?.slug` for org-aware availability/booking will now see undefined. Also, for the eventTypeId branch, the original code returned `eventType.hosts?.length ? hosts.map(...) : eventType.users || []`; the new code returns `users.length ? users : eventType.users` — when hosts exist but map to an empty array (shouldn't happen, but), behavior differs subtly. More importantly, wrapping everything in a 500 masks real errors (e.g. translation failures) and the removed organization select is a functional regression for organization bookings. These changes are unrelated to the destinationCalendar array migration and should be reverted or justified.

title: isTeamEventType computed with string literals instead of SchedulingType enum
body: `const isTeamEventType = !!eventType.schedulingType && ["COLLECTIVE", "ROUND_ROBIN"].includes(eventType.schedulingType);` uses hardcoded strings instead of the imported SchedulingType enum (SchedulingType.COLLECTIVE / SchedulingType.ROUND_ROBIN). This works only because the enum values are those exact strings, but it's fragile and inconsistent with the rest of the codebase (e.g. confirm.handler.ts uses SchedulingType.COLLECTIVE). If the enum values ever change, this silently breaks. Use the enum.

title: Webhook e2e expectations for destinationCalendar are inconsistent (null vs []) and only one case was updated
body: The BOOKING_REJECTED test was updated to expect `destinationCalendar: []` (line 249), but the BOOKING_CREATED test still expects `destinationCalendar: null` (line 119) and the BOOKING_REQUESTED test still expects `destinationCalendar: null` (line 373). With the new array type, the webhook payload will contain `destinationCalendar: []` (empty array) when no destination calendar is set — `toMatchObject` with `null` will fail because `[]` does not match `null`. These two assertions need to be updated to `[]` as well, otherwise the e2e suite will fail (or the payload actually sends null, which would indicate the evt construction in some paths still produces null and violates the new type). Either way the inconsistency must be resolved.

title: requestReschedule evt.destinationCalendar drops the user's destination calendar fallback
body: The new code is `destinationCalendar: bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar ? [bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar] : []`. The original code was `bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar || bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar` (a no-op fallback to itself, likely a bug, but the booking query at line 60 selects destinationCalendar and the user's destinationCalendar is not selected). Other handlers (handleCancelBooking, confirm.handler) fall back to `user.destinationCalendar` when the booking has none. Here, when the booking has no destinationCalendar, the evt gets an empty array, so downstream calendar deletion (which uses evt.destinationCalendar to locate the calendar) may fail to find the right calendar. The booking query should also select `user: { select: { destinationCalendar: true } }` and the fallback should mirror the other handlers.

title: BrokenIntegrationEmail calendar name derivation can produce "undefined undefined" or crash when integration has no underscore
body: The code does `let calendar = mainHostDestinationCalendar ? mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration.split("_") : "calendar";` then `if (Array.isArray(calendar)) { const calendarCap = calendar.map(...); calendar = calendarCap[0] + " " + calendarCap[1]; }`. If `integration` is a string without an underscore (e.g. "caldav"), split returns a single-element array and `calendarCap[1]` is undefined, producing "Caldav undefined" in the email. If mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined, calendar stays the string "calendar" and the Array.isArray branch is skipped — OK. But the undefined-second-element case produces broken user-facing text. Should guard `calendarCap[1] ?? ""` or use a proper display name.

title: BaseCalendarService (CalDAV/Apple) createEvent only creates the event on the first destination calendar, ignoring additional hosts' calendars
body: In BaseCalendarService.createEvent, `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` then the calendars filter matches only `c.externalId === mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` (or all calendars if no externalId). For a collective event with multiple hosts each having their own CalDAV/Apple calendar credential, EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents calls createEvent once per destination entry with a different credential — but each BaseCalendarService instance is constructed with ONE credential (the host's), and `this.listCalendars(event)` returns that host's calendars. The filter then picks only the calendar matching the FIRST destination calendar's externalId, which belongs to a different host/credential. So for host B's credential, the event is either created on no calendar (if externalIds don't match) or on host A's calendar URL using host B's credentials (auth failure). The filter should match by the credential's own calendars (i.e. create on the primary calendar of THIS credential) rather than by the first destination calendar's externalId. This breaks collective events for CalDAV/Apple Calendar users.

title: referencesToCreate externalCalendarId/credentialId now come from result, but for non-calendar results they are undefined, and for calendar results the externalId is the passed-in destination.externalId which may be undefined
body: In create(), referencesToCreate maps `externalCalendarId: isCalendarType ? result.externalId : undefined` and `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`. result.externalId is the `externalId` param of CalendarManager.createEvent, which EventManager passes as `destination.externalId` (line 370) — but only in the `destination.credentialId` branch. In the else branch (line 380) and the no-destinationCalendar fallback (line 391) and the other_calendar branch (line 403), createEvent is called WITHOUT externalId, so result.externalId is undefined. The booking reference then stores externalCalendarId = undefined, meaning on update/delete the calendar service cannot locate the specific calendar and falls back to primary — which may be wrong for users with multiple calendars. Previously the code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId` which had the same issue but at least was consistent. The reference should store the actual external calendar id returned by the calendar service (creationResult) or the destination.externalId in all branches.

title: PayPal webhook evt.destinationCalendar ignores team hosts' calendars, only organizer/booking calendar is used when creating calendar events post-payment
body: In handlePaymentSuccess, the evt is built with `destinationCalendar: booking.destinationCalendar ? [booking.destinationCalendar] : user.destinationCalendar ? [user.destinationCalendar] : []` and then `new EventManager(user)` + `eventManager.create(evt)` is called when the booking was already confirmed. For collective team bookings paid via PayPal, only the organizer's destination calendar is included; other hosts' calendars are not, so calendar events are only created for the organizer. The booking query (lines 57-86) doesn't fetch eventType hosts or their destination calendars. This is the same multi-host gap as handleNewBooking but in the payment-confirmation path — collective paid bookings confirmed via PayPal webhook will miss host calendar events.

title: Stripe webhook evt.destinationCalendar only includes booking/user calendar, missing team hosts for collective paid bookings
body: Both getBooking (line 101-119) and handlePaymentSuccess (line 207-229) build evt.destinationCalendar from only `booking.destinationCalendar || user.destinationCalendar`. For collective team bookings where the organizer is not the only host, the other hosts' destination calendars are not included, so when `eventManager.create(evt)` runs (lines 242, 331), only the organizer's calendar receives the event. The booking query selects `eventType: true` but the hosts' destination calendars are not fetched. Same gap as the PayPal webhook; collective paid bookings confirmed via Stripe will not create calendar events on all hosts' calendars.

title: confirmHandler evt.destinationCalendar only includes booking/user calendar, missing other hosts for collective bookings
body: The evt built in confirmHandler sets `destinationCalendar: booking?.destinationCalendar ? [booking.destinationCalendar] : user.destinationCalendar ? [user.destinationCalendar] : []`. For collective team bookings requiring confirmation, when the organizer confirms, handleConfirmation → EventManager.create runs with only the organizer's destination calendar. Other hosts' calendars are not included, so their calendar events are not created upon confirmation. The booking query (lines 38-91) doesn't fetch eventType hosts or users with their destination calendars. This breaks the multi-host support for collective events that require confirmation.

title: bookingReminder evt.destinationCalendar only includes booking/user calendar, not team hosts
body: The reminder cron builds `selectedDestinationCalendar = booking.destinationCalendar || user.destinationCalendar` and wraps it in an array. For collective team bookings, only one calendar is included. The reminder email itself (sendOrganizerRequestReminderEmail) may not create calendar events, so impact is limited to email content/links, but if any downstream consumer uses evt.destinationCalendar to schedule or display calendar info, hosts are missing. Low impact but inconsistent with the multi-host goal.

title: updateAllCalendarEvents calls updateEvent with possibly-undefined credential when DB lookup fails
body: In the loop over calendarReference (line 504-551), when `reference.credentialId` is set, the code looks up the credential in this.calendarCredentials and falls back to a DB fetch. If both fail (credential deleted, or app slug missing), `credential` stays undefined and line 542 `result.push(updateEvent(credential, event, bookingRefUid, calenderExternalId))` calls updateEvent with undefined. updateEvent (CalendarManager.ts line 272) does `getCalendar(credential)` and `credential.appName` — wait, it accesses `credential.appName` only in the return, but `getCalendar(credential)` with undefined will throw. The throw is caught by the outer try/catch (line 591), which then returns failure results for ALL references, discarding any successful updates from other references in the same batch. A single missing credential should only fail that one reference.

title: Office365 createEvent only targets the first destination calendar; multi-host collective events create duplicate events on the organizer's calendar
body: Office365CalendarService.createEvent uses `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and builds the URL from `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId`. When EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents calls createEvent once per destination calendar entry (each with a different credentialId), the Office365 service ignores the credentialId parameter (the interface now requires it but this implementation's signature is still `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` — it doesn't even declare the second parameter). So for host B's credential, the service still uses the FIRST destination calendar's externalId (host A's calendar) with host B's access token — either failing auth or creating the event on the wrong calendar. The service must use the credentialId to find the matching destination calendar entry, like GoogleCalendarService does.

title: Office365 updateEvent and deleteEvent ignore externalCalendarId and destinationCalendar entirely, always using /me/calendar/events
body: Office365CalendarService.updateEvent (line 94-109) always uses `/me/calendar/events/${uid}` and deleteEvent (line 111-123) always uses `/me/calendar/events/${uid}`, ignoring both the `externalCalendarId` parameter and `event.destinationCalendar`. For users who have their events on a non-default calendar (which is exactly what destinationCalendar is for), updates and deletes will 404 or hit the wrong calendar. This was pre-existing behavior but becomes more impactful with the multi-destination-calendar change: for collective events, the event may live on a host's non-default Office365 calendar, and update/delete will silently fail to find it. The methods should use externalCalendarId when provided: `/me/calendars/${externalCalendarId}/events/${uid}`.

title: CalendarEventClass.destinationCalendar typed as DestinationCalendar[] but Prisma DestinationCalendar type includes relation fields that may not be present at runtime
body: The class declares `destinationCalendar?: DestinationCalendar[] | null;` using the Prisma model type. However, in many call sites the destination calendar objects come from partial selects (e.g. `user.destinationCalendar` selected without `credential` include, or `booking.destinationCalendar` selected as a scalar relation). The Prisma `DestinationCalendar` type includes all scalar fields, which is fine, but code that does `destination.credentialId` (EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents line 340) relies on credentialId being present — it is a scalar on the model so it's fine. The concern is that `IntegrationCalendar` (used in CalendarManager.getConnectedCalendars) is a different shape, and some code mixes them. The type is technically correct for the Prisma relation but the class is also used with IntegrationCalendar-like objects in places; consider using a narrower type like `Pick<DestinationCalendar, "id" | "externalId" | "integration" | "credentialId">[]` to make the contract explicit. Low severity — more of a type-safety improvement.

title: Only evt.destinationCalendar[0] is connected to the booking; additional hosts' destination calendars are not persisted anywhere on the booking
body: At booking creation, `destinationCalendar: evt.destinationCalendar && evt.destinationCalendar.length > 0 ? { connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id } } : undefined`. The Booking model has a single `destinationCalendarId` foreign key, so only the first (organizer's) destination calendar is stored. The additional team hosts' destination calendars pushed into evt.destinationCalendar (teamDestinationCalendars) are used during event creation (EventManager.create) but are NOT persisted on the booking. On reschedule or cancel, handlers reconstruct evt.destinationCalendar from `booking.destinationCalendar` (single) — the other hosts' calendars are lost. This means the multi-host calendar support works only for the initial creation; reschedule/cancel will not update/delete events on the other hosts' calendars (unless references are used, but handleCancelBooking's evt construction doesn't aggregate from references). This is a fundamental data-model limitation that the PR does not address — either the Booking model needs a many-to-many relation to DestinationCalendar, or reschedule/cancel must rebuild the destination calendar list from booking references + eventType hosts.

title: updateEvent/deleteEvent look up destination calendar by externalId instead of credentialId, always yielding undefined
body: In updateEvent (line 254-256) and deleteEvent (line 315-317), the fallback when externalCalendarId is not provided is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. Since externalCalendarId is falsy in that branch, `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` compares a string to undefined/null and can never match, so selectedCalendar/calendarId is always undefined and the code silently falls back to 'primary' (update) or 'primary' (delete). For collective events where the event lives on a non-primary calendar of a host, rescheduling or cancelling will update/delete the wrong calendar (or fail with 404 which is swallowed in deleteEvent). The lookup should match on `cal.credentialId === credentialId` (as createEvent correctly does at line 147-149) or the caller must always pass externalCalendarId.

title: Google Meet fallback crashes when destinationCalendar is empty (undefined.integration)
body: Line 118-119: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []; if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")`. When evt.destinationCalendar is an empty array (which many call sites now produce, e.g. handleCancelBooking, confirm.handler, requestReschedule.handler), mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined and accessing `.integration` throws a TypeError, breaking event creation for any Google Meet booking that has no destination calendar configured. It should be `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

title: Fallback path filters credentials by type === "calendar" which matches no real credential type
body: In createAllCalendarEvents, the else branch (no destinationCalendar) does `this.calendarCredentials.filter((cred) => cred.type === "calendar")`. Credential types are app slugs like "google_calendar", "office365_calendar", "caldav_calendar" — none equals the literal "calendar" — so the fallback never creates any calendar event when destinationCalendar is empty. Previously the code relied on destinationCalendar being set; now that many call sites pass `[]` instead of null/undefined (e.g. bookingReminder.ts line 130, webhook.ts, confirm.handler.ts), bookings without a configured destination calendar will silently get no calendar event created. The fallback should use `cred.type.endsWith("_calendar")` (excluding "other_calendar" which is handled separately below) or pick the first calendar credential.

title: createEvent called without externalId in the no-credentialId branch, losing per-destination calendar selection
body: In createAllCalendarEvents, when a destination entry has no credentialId (line 375-382), the code calls `createEvent(c, event)` without passing `destination.externalId`. The CalendarManager.createEvent signature now accepts externalId and GoogleCalendarService.createEvent uses credentialId to find the matching destination calendar (`calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`). Without the externalId being threaded through, and since the destination entry lacks credentialId, the Google service cannot match the destination to the credential and falls back to "primary", so team hosts' events may be created on the wrong calendar. The call should be `createEvent(c, event, destination.externalId)`.

title: Booking.destinationCalendar connect only persists the first destination calendar, dropping additional hosts' calendars
body: The evt.destinationCalendar array is correctly built with the organizer's calendar plus all collective team members' calendars (teamDestinationCalendars pushed at line ~1074), and EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents creates calendar events on each host's calendar. However, when persisting the booking (line ~1871-1877), only `evt.destinationCalendar[0].id` is connected to the booking: `destinationCalendar: evt.destinationCalendar && evt.destinationCalendar.length > 0 ? { connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id } } : undefined`. The Booking model has a single destinationCalendar relation, so on reschedule/cancel the code reconstructs evt.destinationCalendar from booking.destinationCalendar (single) or user.destinationCalendar — the additional hosts' destination calendars are lost. Consequences: (1) reschedule/cancel flows (handleCancelBooking, EventManager.reschedule) will only update/delete events on the first host's calendar reference; other hosts' calendar events are updated only via booking.references (which do include all created references), but the destinationCalendar-based lookups in calendar services (e.g. GoogleCalendarService update/delete fallbacks) will target the wrong calendar; (2) the DB state no longer reflects which calendars the event was created on. This needs either a schema change (booking-to-destinationCalendar many-to-many) or at minimum ensuring all created references carry correct credentialId/externalCalendarId so updates/deletes don't depend on destinationCalendar.

title: teamDestinationCalendars only collected for COLLECTIVE scheduling, but pushed for any isTeamEventType check that also matches ROUND_ROBIN incorrectly
body: At line ~987-1000, team members' destination calendars are pushed into teamDestinationCalendars only when `eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE"`. At line ~1074, they are appended when `isTeamEventType && eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE"`. isTeamEventType was changed (line ~689) to `!!eventType.schedulingType && ["COLLECTIVE", "ROUND_ROBIN"].includes(eventType.schedulingType)`. For ROUND_ROBIN events, only one host is booked per slot, but the code path at line 1074 checks schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE" so ROUND_ROBIN is excluded from pushing — that part is consistent. However the deeper issue: for ROUND_ROBIN, `users` contains all hosts, and `users.slice(1)` team members are added to evt.team/attendees, and EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents will create calendar events for destinationCalendar entries — but for round robin only the booked host's calendar should receive the event. Since destinationCalendar for round robin only contains the organizer's calendar (eventType.destinationCalendar || organizerUser.destinationCalendar), only one event is created — OK. But the organizerUser for round robin is chosen per-slot; verify organizerUser.destinationCalendar corresponds to the actually booked host. If organizerUser is the event-type owner rather than the assigned host, the event lands on the wrong host's calendar. This needs verification; at minimum the collective-only gating means round-robin multi-calendar support is absent, which may be intended but should be confirmed against issue #7754.

title: destinationCalendar set to null instead of [] when neither eventType nor organizer has one, inconsistent with other call sites
body: Line ~1060-1064: `destinationCalendar: eventType.destinationCalendar ? [eventType.destinationCalendar] : organizerUser.destinationCalendar ? [organizerUser.destinationCalendar] : null`. Other call sites in this PR use `[]` as the empty value (e.g. handleCancelBooking, confirm.handler, paypal-webhook). EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents checks `event.destinationCalendar && event.destinationCalendar.length > 0`, so null and [] behave the same there, but downstream code like `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` (EventManager line 118) handles both. The inconsistency itself is benign, but combined with the fallback bug (filter `cred.type === "calendar"` matching nothing), a null/[] destinationCalendar means NO calendar event is created at all for users without a configured destination calendar — a regression from the previous behavior where `eventType.destinationCalendar || organizerUser.destinationCalendar` being undefined still resulted in createAllCalendarEvents falling through to the (broken) fallback. Actually previously the fallback had the same `cred.type === "calendar"` bug? No — previously the else branch was only reached when destinationCalendar was falsy, and it had the same filter. So the regression risk is equal; the real issue is the fallback filter (reported separately). This finding is about consistency: use [] to match the type `DestinationCalendar[] | null` and other call sites.

title: referencesToCreate externalCalendarId/credentialId now come from result, but createEvent's externalId param is destination.externalId while result.externalId is set from the same — verify consistency for non-Google providers
body: In EventManager.create, referencesToCreate now uses `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId` (lines 169-170), which CalendarManager.createEvent populates from its new `externalId` parameter and `credential.id`. In createAllCalendarEvents, createEvent is called with `destination.externalId` only in the credentialId branch (line 370); in the else branch (line 380) it's called without externalId, so result.externalId is undefined and the created booking reference will have externalCalendarId undefined even though the event was created on destination.externalId's calendar (if the service honored it). For Google this is partially mitigated by credentialId matching, but for CalDAV (BaseCalendarService.createEvent filters calendars by mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId — the FIRST destination only) and Office365 (uses first destination's externalId), events for secondary hosts are created on the first host's calendar, and references record no externalCalendarId. This means updates/deletes for secondary hosts' events cannot locate the correct calendar. The else branch must pass destination.externalId.

title: Lark createEvent throws when destinationCalendar is empty, breaking bookings without a destination calendar
body: createEvent (line 128-132) does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId; if (!calendarId) { throw new Error("no calendar id"); }`. Previously the code was `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` with the same throw, so behavior is unchanged for missing calendar — but now that many call sites pass `[]` instead of a populated object, and EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents calls createEvent for every destination entry AND for all "other_calendar" credentials unconditionally (line 399-405), a Lark "other_calendar" credential will throw whenever destinationCalendar is empty, causing Promise.all in createAllCalendarEvents to reject... actually createEvent in CalendarManager catches errors per-credential (line 236-254), so it logs and returns success=false. Still, for the primary destination path, an empty destinationCalendar array now reaches createEvent (via the else fallback branch which is broken anyway). The throw on missing calendarId is pre-existing behavior; the new risk is that `event.destinationCalendar ?? []` destructuring silently produces undefined and the error message is misleading. More importantly, updateEvent/deleteEvent have the same pattern. This is a pre-existing design (Lark requires a calendar id), so severity is medium: ensure callers don't invoke Lark createEvent without a destination calendar — EventManager's unconditional "other_calendar" loop (line 399-405) does exactly that.

title: Unconditional creation of "other_calendar" events ignores destinationCalendar and can create duplicate/wrong events for collective bookings
body: At the end of createAllCalendarEvents (lines 398-405), the code unconditionally creates events for all credentials whose type includes "other_calendar" (e.g. CRM pseudo-calendars like closecom_other_calendar), regardless of destinationCalendar. For collective events with multiple hosts, each host's EventManager instance... actually EventManager is constructed per-user (organizer), so this runs once. But the destinationCalendar loop (lines 338-383) iterates over ALL destination calendars (organizer + team members) and for entries without credentialId it creates events on ALL credentials matching destination.integration — meaning for a collective event with 2 hosts each having google_calendar, if the destination entries lack credentialId, events are created on both hosts' Google calendars for each destination entry, potentially creating duplicates (2 destinations × 2 credentials = 4 events, when 2 are expected). The destination entries built in handleNewBooking come from Prisma DestinationCalendar objects which DO have credentialId? DestinationCalendar model has credentialId? Let me check: the Prisma DestinationCalendar has `credentialId Int?` — in handleNewBooking, teamDestinationCalendars are user.destinationCalendar objects which include credentialId if set. If users set destinationCalendar without credentialId (possible?), the else branch creates events on all matching credentials — for collective with 2 google hosts, destination[0] (organizer, no credentialId) → creates on both hosts' google credentials; destination[1] (member, no credentialId) → creates on both again → 4 events. This is a real duplication risk when credentialId is absent on destination entries.

title: Recurring-event cancellation deletes events using ALL of the booking user's calendar credentials instead of the reference's credential
body: In the recurring + allRemainingBookings branch (lines 444-468), for each calendar credential of `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` (ALL calendar credentials of the organizer, not the credential that owns the reference), the code iterates updatedBookings and deletes the first `_calendar` reference found (`updBooking.references.find(...)`) using that credential's calendar service. For collective events where the reference belongs to a different host's credential, `calendar?.deleteEvent(uid, evt, externalCalendarId)` is called with the wrong credential — the externalCalendarId belongs to another user's calendar, so deletion will 404 (silently resolved in Google deleteEvent) or delete nothing. The outer loop already has the correct `calendarCredential` for the reference (line 428-441); the inner recurring loop should use that same credential/calendar, not re-iterate all user credentials. This leaves stale events on secondary hosts' calendars when cancelling recurring collective bookings.

title: Cancellation evt.destinationCalendar only includes booking/user destination calendar, not team hosts' calendars
body: When building evt for cancellation (lines 251-255), destinationCalendar is `[bookingToDelete.destinationCalendar]` or `[bookingToDelete.user.destinationCalendar]` — a single calendar. For collective events with multiple hosts, the calendar services' deleteEvent fallback (`event.destinationCalendar?.find(...)`) uses this array; since booking.destinationCalendar only stores the first destination (see handleNewBooking connect), secondary hosts' calendars are not represented. However, deletion primarily uses `externalCalendarId` from the reference (passed explicitly), so the impact is limited to the fallback paths in GoogleCalendarService.deleteEvent (line 315-317) which are broken anyway (see separate finding). Still, for correctness the evt should include all destination calendars of the team members, or the deletion logic should rely solely on references (which it mostly does via bookingCalendarReference loop). The current code does iterate all references (line 422-483), so deletion per-reference is attempted; the evt.destinationCalendar is only used as fallback. Medium severity because the broken fallback in Google service makes this matter.

title: destinationCalendar fallback to user.destinationCalendar was removed, and the original code was self-referential (bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar || bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar)
body: The diff shows the old code was `destinationCalendar: bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar || bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar` (a self-OR, clearly a pre-existing bug — probably meant `bookingToReschedule?.user?.destinationCalendar`). The new code is `bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar ? [bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar] : []`. The booking query (line 43-74) does not select `user.destinationCalendar`, so the user fallback is impossible here without a query change.
