The evt is used for webhooks (BOOKING_CANCELLED payload) — the webhook payload's destinationCalendar will now be [] when the booking has no destinationCalendar, whereas other handlers (handleCancelBooking) fall back to user.destinationCalendar. This changes the webhook payload contract for consumers. Either include user.destinationCalendar in the query and fall back, or accept the change deliberately. Also note the webhook.e2e.ts test expects `destinationCalendar: []` for BOOKING_REJECTED and `null` for BOOKING_CREATED/BOOKING_REQUESTED — the null expectations at lines 119 and 373 were NOT updated (only line 249 was changed to []), meaning those tests will now fail because the payload will contain [] not null. Wait — line 119 `destinationCalendar: null` and line 373 `destinationCalendar: null` remain unchanged in the test file. The actual payloads: BOOKING_CREATED comes from handleNewBooking where destinationCalendar is now an array (possibly [] or [cal]) — never null. So `toMatchObject({ destinationCalendar: null })` will fail. This is a test gap/bug.

title: BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED webhook tests still expect destinationCalendar: null but the payload is now an array
body: The PR changed the CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar type to an array and updated the BOOKING_REJECTED expectation (line 249) from null to [], but left `destinationCalendar: null` at line 119 (BOOKING_CREATED) and line 373 (BOOKING_REQUESTED). The webhook payload is built from the CalendarEvent, where destinationCalendar is now always an array (e.g. handleNewBooking sets `[eventType.destinationCalendar]` or `[organizerUser.destinationCalendar]` or null — actually handleNewBooking can set null at line ~1064). Hmm, handleNewBooking sets `destinationCalendar: ... : null` — so BOOKING_CREATED payload could be null if neither eventType nor organizer has a destination calendar. In the e2e test, the user is created via fixtures — does the fixture user have a destinationCalendar? Typically not by default. So the payload would be null for BOOKING_CREATED (matching the test), but for BOOKING_REJECTED (confirm.handler) the code now always produces an array ([]), hence the test update at line 249. For BOOKING_REQUESTED — which handler produces it? handleNewBooking with requiresConfirmation — same evt as BOOKING_CREATED, so null is still expected and correct. So lines 119 and 373 may still pass. BUT the inconsistency: handleNewBooking produces null while confirm.handler produces [] for the same conceptual field — the webhook contract is now inconsistent across trigger events (null vs []). This is an API contract break for webhook consumers. The type is `DestinationCalendar[] | null` so both are valid, but consumers must handle both. This should be standardized to always [] (or always null) — recommend making handleNewBooking produce [] instead of null.

title: Inconsistent empty value for destinationCalendar (null vs []) across webhook payloads breaks consumer contract
body: handleNewBooking sets `destinationCalendar: ... : null` when no calendar is configured (line ~1063), while confirm.handler, handleCancelBooking, bookingReminder, and the payment webhooks all use `[]`. The CalendarEvent type allows both (`DestinationCalendar[] | null`), but webhook consumers receive BOOKING_CREATED/BOOKING_REQUESTED payloads with `destinationCalendar: null` and BOOKING_REJECTED/BOOKING_CANCELLED payloads with `destinationCalendar: []`. This is an inconsistent API contract introduced by the PR. Standardize on `[]` (matching the new array type semantics) in handleNewBooking.

title: Calendar.createEvent interface now requires credentialId, but not all Calendar implementations were updated (CalDAV/BaseCalendarService, Office365, Lark)
body: The `Calendar` interface in packages/types/Calendar.d.ts (line 221) was changed to `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number): Promise<NewCalendarEventType>`. CalendarManager.createEvent now calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` (line 236). However, the implementations in packages/lib/CalendarService.ts (BaseCalendarService.createEvent, line 125: `async createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)`), packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts (line 72: `async createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)`), and packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts (line 125: `async createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)`) were NOT updated to accept credentialId. TypeScript structural typing allows implementations with fewer parameters, so this compiles, but at runtime `credentialId` is simply ignored by these services — they always use the first destination calendar (BaseCalendarService line 156, Office365 line 73, Lark line 128). For collective events with hosts on CalDAV/Office365/Lark, events will be created on the wrong host's calendar (the first destination's calendar) because these services cannot select the calendar matching the credential. This defeats the PR's purpose for non-Google providers. Each service should accept credentialId and use `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` like GoogleCalendarService does.

title: Office365 createEvent ignores credentialId and always uses the first destination calendar, breaking collective events
body: Office365CalendarService.createEvent (line 72-92) only reads `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` and uses its externalId. It does not receive or use credentialId (the interface change added credentialId but this implementation wasn't updated). In a collective event with two Office365 hosts, EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents calls createEvent once per destination with the corresponding credential, but the service always picks destinationCalendar[0].externalId — the organizer's calendar — so the second host's event is created on the organizer's calendar using the second host's credential (which will fail with 403/404 since the credential doesn't own that calendar), or if it succeeds it's on the wrong calendar. The service must accept credentialId and select `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`, falling back to the first entry or the default calendar.

title: BaseCalendarService (CalDAV/Apple) createEvent uses only the first destination calendar, ignoring which credential is being used
body: BaseCalendarService.createEvent (line 125-198) destructures `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` (line 156) and filters calendars by that single externalId. It does not accept credentialId (signature unchanged at line 125). For collective events with multiple CalDAV hosts, EventManager calls createEvent once per host credential, but each call creates the event on the FIRST destination's calendar URL using each host's own credentials/headers — the second host's credentials will fail to write to the first host's CalDAV calendar (auth error), or worse, if calendars are shared, create duplicates. The service must accept credentialId and select the destination calendar whose credentialId matches, like GoogleCalendarService does.

title: updateAllCalendarEvents: updateEvent called with possibly-undefined credential when DB lookup fails
body: In updateAllCalendarEvents, when `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is neither in this.calendarCredentials nor found in the DB (credentialFromDB null or app.slug missing), `credential` remains undefined (or retains the value from a previous loop iteration — it's declared with `let credential;` outside the try and reused across iterations of the for loop at line 504!). Then `result.push(updateEvent(credential, event, bookingRefUid, calenderExternalId))` is called with undefined credential. updateEvent (CalendarManager line 272) does `getCalendar(credential)` with undefined — likely throws, caught by the outer try/catch which returns failure results. But worse: `credential` is declared outside the for loop (line 480: `let calendarReference..., credential;`), so if iteration 1 sets credential and iteration 2's lookup fails, iteration 2 reuses iteration 1's credential — updating the WRONG calendar with the wrong credential. This is a real bug: the credential variable must be scoped inside the loop (const per iteration).

title: Shared `credential` variable across loop iterations in updateAllCalendarEvents causes cross-reference credential leakage
body: `credential` is declared once outside the `for (const reference of calendarReference)` loop (line 480: `let calendarReference: PartialReference[] | undefined = undefined, credential;`). Inside the loop (lines 511-542), when `reference.credentialId` is set, credential is assigned from this.calendarCredentials or DB. If a reference has no credentialId (else branch, line 543-550), credential is NOT reassigned — but the else branch uses a local `credentials` variable, so that's fine. However, if the credentialId branch's DB lookup fails (credentialFromDB null), credential retains the PREVIOUS iteration's value, and `updateEvent(credential, ...)` at line 542 uses the wrong credential for the current reference — updating a calendar event on the wrong user's calendar with the wrong credentials. This can modify another user's calendar event (data integrity/security issue). Fix: declare `let credential` inside the loop body (per-reference scope), and skip/throw when the credential cannot be resolved.

title: Sequential await in destination loop creates calendar events one-by-one, slow for collective events with many hosts
body: createAllCalendarEvents iterates `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` with `await createEvent(...)` inside (lines 339-383), making calendar event creation sequential per destination. For collective events with N hosts, this serializes N external API calls. The previous code used Promise.all for the no-credentialId branch. The credentialId branch also does a potential DB fetch per destination (line 344). This is a performance regression for collective events — should use Promise.all over destinations (with per-destination credential resolution). Severity medium since collective events typically have few hosts, but with the DB fetch inside the loop it's N sequential round trips.

title: Team members' destination calendars collected via users.slice(1) but users ordering/host assignment for ROUND_ROBIN may include unbooked hosts
body: teamDestinationCalendars is built from `users.slice(1)` — all users except the first. For COLLECTIVE, all users attend, so this is correct. But `users` comes from loadUsers which for hosts-based event types returns `eventType.hosts.map(...)` — ALL hosts, not just available/booked ones. For COLLECTIVE, ensureAvailableUsers filters to available users before this point? The teamMemberPromises at line ~990 uses `users` — need to verify `users` at that point is the filtered available users (after ensureAvailableUsers). Looking at the flow: ensureAvailableUsers returns availableUsers, and `users` is reassigned? The diff context doesn't show the reassignment. If `users` still contains all hosts (not just available ones), then for a collective event where only 2 of 3 hosts are available, the third host's destinationCalendar would be included and EventManager would try to create a calendar event on their calendar using their credential — but the EventManager is constructed with only the organizer's credentials (`new EventManager(organizerUser)` or similar), so createAllCalendarEvents' DB fallback (line 344) would fetch the third host's credential from DB and create an event on their calendar even though they're not part of the booking. This would be wrong. Need to verify that `users` at line 990 is the availability-filtered list. The variable `users` is declared earlier and ensureAvailableUsers is called with users — the result should be assigned back. If not, this is a bug. Given the diff shows `const teamMemberPromises = users.slice(1).map(...)` without visible reassignment of users after ensureAvailableUsers in the shown context, this is suspicious. At minimum, the code should use the same filtered user list used to build attendees/teamMembers.

title: buildUIDCalendarEvent has inverted guard: throws when users exist instead of when they don't
body: Line 179-181: `if (this.users && this.users.length > 0) { throw new Error("call buildUsers before calling this function"); }`. The error message says "call buildUsers BEFORE calling this function", but the condition throws when users ARE present — the guard is inverted. It should be `if (!this.users || this.users.length === 0)`. As written, buildUIDCalendarEvent throws whenever users have been set (the correct precondition), and proceeds to `const [mainOrganizer] = this.users` (line 182) when users is undefined — which would throw a different error (Cannot read properties of undefined). This is a pre-existing bug (not introduced by this PR — the diff only shows the import change), but it's in a changed file and the PR touches this builder's destinationCalendar handling. Worth fixing while here, but since it's pre-existing and unrelated to the destinationCalendar change, severity is low.

title: Inverted IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED conditionals break organization slug assignment
body: The diff changed `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` and `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { requestedSlug: slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { requestedSlug: slug } : {})`. The first change is a semantic inversion: previously, when team billing was NOT enabled, the slug was set directly on the organization; now it's only set when billing IS enabled. The second change is equivalent (&& → ternary). The first change alters behavior: with IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED=false (self-hosted default), organizations no longer get their slug set at creation — `slug` will be null, breaking organization subdomain routing. This looks like an accidental inversion unrelated to the destinationCalendar PR (possibly a bad merge or drive-by change). It must be reverted to `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` or justified. This is a critical regression for self-hosted org creation.

title: evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars) mutates the array that may be shared with eventType.destinationCalendar or organizerUser.destinationCalendar
body: Line ~1060-1064: `destinationCalendar: eventType.destinationCalendar ? [eventType.destinationCalendar] : organizerUser.destinationCalendar ? [organizerUser.destinationCalendar] : null` — this creates a NEW array containing the Prisma object, so pushing to it (line 1074: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`) does not mutate the Prisma objects themselves, only the new array. So no shared-state mutation of Prisma results. However, the array now contains a mix of the eventType/organizer destination and team members' destinations — when persisted (line ~1871), only [0] is connected. Already reported. Additionally, if the same DestinationCalendar object appears twice (e.g. two hosts share the same destination calendar row — unlikely since destinationCalendar is per-user), duplicates could cause duplicate event creation in createAllCalendarEvents (the loop doesn't dedupe by credentialId). Low risk. Not reporting separately — covered by the persistence finding.

title: MeetLocationType fallback check uses mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration but DestinationCalendar.integration is the app slug like 'google_calendar' — verify field semantics
body: Line 119: `if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")`. The Prisma DestinationCalendar model has an `integration` field (string) — its values are app slugs like "google_calendar", "office365_calendar". The check `!== "google_calendar"` is correct for detecting absence of Google Calendar. But when destinationCalendar is empty (now common — many call sites pass []), mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined and `.integration` throws (already reported as the crash finding). The fix `?.integration` would make the condition true (undefined !== "google_calendar") → falls back to Cal Video, which is the correct behavior for no Google Calendar. So the optional chaining fix is correct and necessary.

title: BrokenIntegrationEmail calendar name parsing can produce 'undefined undefined' or wrong name when destinationCalendar is empty
body: Line 88-96: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = calEvent.destinationCalendar ?? []; let calendar = mainHostDestinationCalendar ? mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration.split("_") : "calendar"; if (Array.isArray(calendar)) { const calendarCap = calendar.map(...); calendar = calendarCap[0] + " " + calendarCap[1]; }`. If integration is e.g. "google_calendar", split gives ["google","calendar"], calendarCap[0]="Google", calendarCap[1]="Calendar" → "Google Calendar" — OK. But if integration has only one segment (e.g. "caldav"), calendarCap[1] is undefined → "Caldav undefined". If integration is undefined (destination entry without integration), split throws. Pre-existing fragility, now more likely because destinationCalendar entries may be partial. Low severity since this email is only sent on broken integrations (and the send is currently commented out in CalendarManager).

title: Google Calendar hangoutLink patch uses selectedCalendar which may be undefined, causing patch to target wrong calendar
body: In createEvent, after insert, if the event has a hangoutLink, the code calls `calendar.events.patch({ calendarId: selectedCalendar, ... })` (line 166-177). selectedCalendar is `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` — which is undefined when no destination matches the credential (line 147-149), even though the insert used `selectedCalendar || "primary"` (line 154). So the patch targets calendarId=undefined while the insert went to "primary" — the patch will fail (Google API error) or hit the wrong calendar, leaving the event description without the Meet link. The patch should use `selectedCalendar || "primary"` consistently. Same pattern in updateEvent (line 277: `calendarId: selectedCalendar` where selectedCalendar could be undefined when externalCalendarId is falsy and the find fails — see the broken find at line 254-256).

title: Booking destinationCalendar connect uses evt.destinationCalendar[0].id — but for collective events the first entry may be a team member's calendar if organizer has none
body: Line ~1871-1877: `destinationCalendar: evt.destinationCalendar && evt.destinationCalendar.length > 0 ? { connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id } } : undefined`. evt.destinationCalendar[0] is eventType.destinationCalendar or organizerUser.destinationCalendar (the organizer's), and team members' calendars are appended after. So [0] is the organizer's — correct for the primary. But if the organizer has NO destination calendar and eventType has none, evt.destinationCalendar starts as null and teamDestinationCalendars are pushed only if `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)` — wait, line 1074: `if (isTeamEventType && eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE") { evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars); }` — if evt.destinationCalendar is null (no organizer/eventType calendar), the push is skipped (optional chaining), so team members' calendars are NOT included! For a collective event where the organizer has no destination calendar but team members do, the event would only be created on... createAllCalendarEvents: destinationCalendar is null → else branch → broken fallback (filter type === "calendar") → no events created, OR if the fallback worked, only one. The team members' calendars are silently dropped because the push is conditional on evt.destinationCalendar being non-null. Fix: initialize evt.destinationCalendar to [] and push team calendars unconditionally for collective, or build the array as [...(organizer ? [organizer] : []), ...teamDestinationCalendars].

title: Collective team destination calendars are dropped when organizer has no destination calendar (null?.push no-op)
body: Line ~1060: `destinationCalendar: eventType.destinationCalendar ? [eventType.destinationCalendar] : organizerUser.destinationCalendar ? [organizerUser.destinationCalendar] : null`. Line ~1074: `if (isTeamEventType && eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE") { evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars); }`. When neither eventType nor organizerUser has a destinationCalendar, evt.destinationCalendar is null, and `null?.push(...)` is a no-op — the team members' destination calendars (collected in teamDestinationCalendars at line ~990) are silently discarded. EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents then sees destinationCalendar as null/empty and falls into the broken fallback branch (filter `cred.type === "calendar"` matches nothing), so NO calendar events are created for any host — the booking exists but no one gets a calendar invite. This is a regression for collective events where the organizer lacks a destination calendar but hosts have them. Fix: build the array as `[...(eventType.destinationCalendar ? [eventType.destinationCalendar] : organizerUser.destinationCalendar ? [organizerUser.destinationCalendar] : []), ...(isTeamEventType && eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE" ? teamDestinationCalendars : [])]`.

title: Fallback branch credential filter `cred.type === "calendar"` never matches; should be endsWith("_calendar") excluding other_calendar
body: Line 389: `const [credential] = this.calendarCredentials.filter((cred) => cred.type === "calendar");`. No credential has type exactly "calendar" — types are "google_calendar", "office365_calendar", "apple_calendar", "caldav_calendar", etc. This fallback (used when event.destinationCalendar is empty/null) therefore never creates a calendar event. With the PR making empty arrays the norm (many call sites now pass [] instead of a populated object), bookings for users WITHOUT a configured destination calendar will get NO calendar event created — a silent regression. The filter should be `cred.type.endsWith("_calendar") && !cred.type.includes("other_calendar")` (other_calendar is handled separately below at line 402), or simply pick the first calendar credential.

title: Cancellation iterates all calendar references but uses bookingToDelete.user.credentials (organizer only) — team hosts' credentials fetched from DB individually, but recurring branch uses all user credentials indiscriminately
body: The non-recurring branch (lines 422-483) correctly resolves each reference's credentialId against bookingToDelete.user.credentials first, then falls back to a DB fetch (lines 428-441) — good, this handles team hosts whose credentials aren't in bookingToDelete.user.credentials. But the recurring branch (lines 444-468) ignores the reference's credentialId entirely: it iterates ALL of `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` filtered by `type.endsWith("_calendar")` and for each, deletes the first `_calendar` reference found in each updated booking. For collective recurring events, references belong to different hosts' credentials; using the organizer's credentials to delete events on other hosts' calendars will fail (404, silently resolved) leaving orphaned events. The recurring branch should use the same per-reference credential resolution as the non-recurring branch.

title: Calendar interface createEvent signature change (added credentialId) is a breaking change for third-party/custom calendar app implementations
body: The `Calendar` interface's createEvent was changed from `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` to `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number)`. TypeScript allows implementations with fewer parameters, so existing implementations compile, but the semantic contract changed: implementations that don't use credentialId will create events on the wrong calendar for collective events (as detailed in the BaseCalendarService/Office365/Lark findings). For app-store apps shipped in this repo, the implementations should be updated. For any external/custom apps (Cal.com supports custom apps via the app store structure), this is a behavioral breaking change. The PR should update ALL in-repo implementations (BaseCalendarService, Office365, Lark — currently not updated) to accept and honor credentialId.

title: updateLocation referencesToCreate uses result.externalId/credentialId which are not populated by CalendarManager.updateEvent
body: In updateLocation (lines 201-211), referencesToCreate maps `externalCalendarId: result.externalId, credentialId: result.credentialId ?? undefined`. But CalendarManager.updateEvent (lines 272-323) does NOT set externalId or credentialId on its returned EventResult — looking at the return object (lines 313-322), it returns appName, type, success, uid, updatedEvent, originalEvent, calError, calWarnings — no externalId, no credentialId. So result.externalId and result.credentialId are always undefined here, and the references created by updateLocation will have externalCalendarId undefined and credentialId undefined. Previously the code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId` and `result.credentialId ?? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId` — also mostly undefined for the array case. The consequence: after a location change (editLocation.handler), the booking's references are recreated (prisma.booking.update with references: { create: updatedResult.referencesToCreate }) — wait, editLocation.handler line 119-121 does `references: { create: updatedResult.referencesToCreate }` — this ADDS new references without deleting old ones? Actually it creates new references alongside existing ones. The new references lack externalCalendarId/credentialId, so future updates/deletes (which rely on reference.credentialId and reference.externalCalendarId) will not find the right calendar — updateAllCalendarEvents falls to the else branch (filter by type) and deleteEvent gets externalCalendarId undefined. This breaks subsequent reschedule/cancel for the booking. CalendarManager.updateEvent should populate externalId (from the externalCalendarId param) and credentialId (from credential.id) in its return value.

title: updateEvent does not return externalId/credentialId in EventResult, breaking reference tracking for location updates
body: CalendarManager.updateEvent (lines 272-323) returns an EventResult without `externalId` or `credentialId` fields, even though it receives `externalCalendarId` and `credential` as parameters. EventManager.updateLocation builds referencesToCreate from `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId` (EventManager.ts lines 208-209), which are therefore always undefined. The references persisted after a location change (editLocation.handler.ts line 119-121: `references: { create: updatedResult.referencesToCreate }`) will lack externalCalendarId and credentialId. Subsequent reschedule/cancel operations rely on these fields (EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents line 505-509 reads reference.externalCalendarId; handleCancelBooking reads reference.credentialId) — with them missing, updates fall back to type-based credential matching (may pick wrong credential for users with multiple calendar apps) and deletes get externalCalendarId undefined (hitting the broken fallback paths). Fix: add `externalId: externalCalendarId, credentialId: credential.id` to updateEvent's return object.

title: Location update creates new booking references without deleting old ones, causing duplicate references
body: Line 113-123: `prisma.booking.update({ where: { id: bookingId }, data: { location, references: { create: updatedResult.referencesToCreate } } })`. This CREATES new references but does not delete the existing ones. After a location change, the booking will have both old references (with old uids/externalCalendarIds) and new references. EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents filters references by type and iterates ALL of them — so subsequent reschedule/cancel will attempt to update/delete BOTH the old and new calendar events, causing errors (old event may already be deleted or belong to a different location's video meeting) and potentially updating stale calendar entries. The old references should be deleted first (or use upsert). This may be pre-existing behavior (the diff doesn't show changes to this logic), but combined with the new externalId/credentialId population issues, it's worth flagging. Actually checking the diff — this file's only change is the destinationCalendar array wrapping. So the duplicate-reference issue is pre-existing. Downgrade to low/speculative? The PR's changes to EventManager.updateLocation (externalId/credentialId now from result, which are undefined) make the newly created references LESS useful than before (previously they carried evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId). So the PR regresses this path. Keep as medium with focus on the regression.

title: isTeamEventType check changed from enum comparison to string array includes — verify SchedulingType import and values
body: Line ~689: changed from `eventType.schedulingType === SchedulingType.COLLECTIVE || eventType.schedulingType === SchedulingType.ROUND_ROBIN` to `!!eventType.schedulingType && ["COLLECTIVE", "ROUND_ROBIN"].includes(eventType.schedulingType)`. The string literals must match the Prisma enum values exactly. SchedulingType enum in Prisma is COLLECTIVE, ROUND_ROBIN, MANAGED. The string comparison works if eventType.schedulingType is the enum string. But the import of SchedulingType may now be unused (check). Also, the CalendarEvent type now includes `schedulingType?: SchedulingType | null` (added in Calendar.d.ts line 182) and handleNewBooking sets `schedulingType: eventType.schedulingType` on evt (line ~1071) — this is a new field in the webhook payload. This is an additive change, fine. The isTeamEventType change is semantically equivalent. Low severity — just verify no unused import lint error and that the enum values match.

title: EventManagerUser type still has destinationCalendar: DestinationCalendar | null (singular) but the class no longer uses it
body: Line 62-65: `export type EventManagerUser = { credentials: CredentialPayload[]; destinationCalendar: DestinationCalendar | null; };`. The constructor (lines 78-87) only uses user.credentials — destinationCalendar is not used. Callers construct EventManager with `{ ...user, credentials }` where user may have destinationCalendar (singular, from Prisma). This type is now misleading since CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar is an array. The EventManagerUser type should either drop destinationCalendar or change to DestinationCalendar[]. Since it's unused in the constructor, dropping it would be cleanest, but callers pass it — TypeScript allows extra properties in spread. Low severity (type hygiene), but could confuse future maintainers.

title: Organizer email overridden with mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId (calendar ID, not email) for Google Calendar events
body: Lines 122-124 (createEvent) and 228-230 (updateEvent): `email: mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId ? mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId : calEventRaw.organizer.email`. For Google Calendar, externalId IS the calendar ID which for primary calendars is the user's email, but for secondary calendars it's a calendar ID (like abc123@group.calendar.google.com), not an email. Setting the organizer attendee's email to a calendar ID is invalid — Google may reject the event or misattribute the organizer. This was pre-existing behavior (the old code did `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.externalId ? calEventRaw.destinationCalendar.externalId : calEventRaw.organizer.email`), so not a regression, but it's wrong and now more impactful because destinationCalendar is an array and the first entry may be a secondary calendar. The organizer email should remain calEventRaw.organizer.email; the calendar selection is handled by calendarId. This is a pre-existing bug worth fixing but not introduced by this PR — low severity in the context of this review.

title: teamDestinationCalendars collected from users.slice(1) but for collective events the organizer is users[0] — verify users[0] is always the organizer/booking user
body: Line ~990: `const teamMemberPromises = users.slice(1).map(async (user) => { if (isTeamEventType && eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE" && user.destinationCalendar) { teamDestinationCalendars.push(user.destinationCalendar); } ... })`. This assumes users[0] is the organizer (whose destinationCalendar is used as the primary at line ~1060 via organizerUser.destinationCalendar). But `organizerUser` is a separate variable — is it guaranteed to be users[0]? For collective events, users comes from eventType.hosts or eventType.users. The organizerUser is determined elsewhere (likely the event type owner or the first user). If organizerUser !== users[0], then users.slice(1) might include the organizer (duplicate) or exclude a team member. Also, for collective events, ALL users attend, so all their destination calendars should be included — but the code excludes users[0] from teamDestinationCalendars and uses organizerUser.destinationCalendar as primary. If users[0] !== organizerUser, the organizer's calendar might be pushed as a team member AND used as primary (duplicate), or users[0]'s calendar is dropped. Need to verify organizerUser === users[0]. The diff doesn't show organizerUser assignment. This is a potential correctness issue for collective events — flagging for verification.

title: createAllCalendarEvents mixes sequential and parallel creation; DB credential fetch inside loop is a bottleneck and potential N+1
body: The destination loop (lines 339-383) is sequential (`for...of` with `await`), and inside it, when the credential isn't in this.calendarCredentials, a `prisma.credential.findUnique` DB query is executed (line 344) — one query per destination per booking creation. For collective events with many hosts whose credentials aren't pre-loaded, this is N sequential DB round trips + N sequential external API calls. The credentials could be batch-fetched with `findMany({ where: { id: { in: destinationCredentialIds } } })` before the loop, and event creation parallelized with Promise.all. Performance issue for collective bookings — medium severity.

title: Recurring cancellation inner loop shadows `uid` and `externalCalendarId` from outer reference destructuring
body: Lines 423-424: `const { credentialId, uid, externalCalendarId } = reference;` (outer scope). Lines 453-456: inside the recurring branch, `const bookingRef = updBooking.references.find(...); if (bookingRef) { const { uid, externalCalendarId } = bookingRef; ... }` — the inner destructuring shadows the outer uid/externalCalendarId. This is intentional (using the per-booking reference's uid), but the shadowing is confusing and error-prone. More importantly, the inner loop uses `calendar` from the OUTER credential (the reference's credential), iterating over ALL user calendar credentials in the outer `promises` map (line 449-461: `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).map(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... })`) — wait, re-reading: the recurring branch is INSIDE the `if (calendarCredential)` block (line 442), and the `promises` map at line 449 iterates `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` (ALL calendar credentials), creating a calendar service for each and deleting the bookingRef's event with EACH credential. So for a recurring booking with 2 calendar credentials, each updated booking's event is deleted twice (once per credential) — the second delete will 404 (silently resolved in Google). For collective recurring events, the reference belongs to a specific host's credential, but deletion is attempted with ALL of the organizer's credentials — wrong credentials will fail, and if the organizer has a credential of the same type as the host, it might delete from the wrong calendar (if externalCalendarId matches, which it won't across users). The net effect: redundant API calls and potential confusion, but the correct credential's delete should succeed. The logic should use the specific `calendar` (from calendarCredential) rather than iterating all user credentials. This is the same issue as finding #18 but worth emphasizing the shadowing and the all-credentials iteration.

title: Merge-delete of old calendar event uses getCalendar(calendarCredential) which may be null, then optional-chains deleteEvent — silently skips deletion
body: Lines 553-565: when newBookingId is provided (merge scenario), the old calendar event is deleted: `const calendarCredential = await prisma.credential.findUnique(...); const calendar = await getCalendar(calendarCredential); await calendar?.deleteEvent(...)`. If calendarCredential is null (deleted credential) or getCalendar returns null (unknown app type), `calendar?.deleteEvent` is a no-op — the old calendar event is silently left on the user's calendar. This is pre-existing behavior (the diff shows this block was moved but not fundamentally changed). Low severity — silent failure, but pre-existing.

title: Duplicate destination calendars not deduplicated — same calendar pushed twice creates duplicate events
body: If two collective hosts share the same destination calendar (same DestinationCalendar row — possible if they share a team calendar or the same credential+externalId), teamDestinationCalendars will contain duplicates, and evt.destinationCalendar will have duplicate entries. EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents iterates destinations and calls createEvent per destination — for entries with the same credentialId, two events are created on the same calendar (duplicate calendar events). The loop should dedupe by credentialId (or externalId+integration). Medium severity — edge case but real for teams sharing calendars.

title: Lark updateEvent error path calls deleteEvent(eventId, event) without calendarId, which will throw 'no calendar id'
body: Line 224-228: in updateEvent's catch block, `await this.deleteEvent(eventId, event)` is called without the third `externalCalendarId` argument. deleteEvent (line 236-242) computes `calendarId = externalCalendarId || mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId` — if the event has no destinationCalendar (or the first entry has no externalId), it throws "no calendar id provided in deleteEvent". So the error-recovery path (delete the partially-updated event) will itself throw, masking the original error. The catch should pass the resolved calendarId: `await this.deleteEvent(eventId, event, calendarId)`. Pre-existing pattern but exposed by the array change.

title: PayPal webhook evt.destinationCalendar doesn't include team hosts' calendars for collective paid events
body: Line 152-156: `destinationCalendar: booking.destinationCalendar ? [booking.destinationCalendar] : user.destinationCalendar ? [user.destinationCalendar] : []`. For collective paid events, this only includes the booking's (first) destination calendar. When EventManager.create is called (line 170) for an already-confirmed booking, createAllCalendarEvents will only create events for this single destination — team hosts' calendars are not included, so hosts won't get calendar events when a paid collective booking is confirmed via PayPal webhook. The booking.destinationCalendar only stores the first destination (per the persistence finding). This means the PayPal confirmation path creates fewer calendar events than the initial booking path. For Stripe (webhook.ts handlePaymentSuccess, line 229), same issue. These webhook paths reconstruct evt from the booking and lose the multi-destination information. Since booking.destinationCalendar is a single relation, the information is lost at persistence time — the webhook handlers cannot recover it. This is a consequence of the schema limitation (single destinationCalendar on Booking). High-level issue: paid collective bookings confirmed via webhook will not create calendar events on all hosts' calendars.

title: Stripe webhook evt.destinationCalendar doesn't include team hosts' calendars for collective paid events
body: Same issue as PayPal webhook: line 229 `destinationCalendar: selectedDestinationCalendar ? [selectedDestinationCalendar] : []` where selectedDestinationCalendar is booking.destinationCalendar || user.destinationCalendar (single). For collective paid events confirmed via Stripe webhook, EventManager.create (line 243) will only create calendar events for this single destination — team hosts' calendars are excluded. Combined with the booking persistence storing only the first destination, the webhook confirmation path cannot create events on all hosts' calendars. This is a data-model limitation exposed by the PR's multi-destination feature.

title: confirm.handler evt.destinationCalendar doesn't include team hosts' calendars for collective bookings requiring confirmation
body: Line 175-179: `destinationCalendar: booking?.destinationCalendar ? [booking.destinationCalendar] : user.destinationCalendar ? [user.destinationCalendar] : []`. When a collective booking requiring confirmation is confirmed (line 225: handleConfirmation → EventManager.create), the evt only has the booking's single destination calendar. Team hosts' calendars are not included, so handleConfirmation's EventManager.create will only create calendar events for the organizer's calendar — hosts won't receive calendar invites when the booking is confirmed. The booking.destinationCalendar stores only the first destination (per persistence finding), and the confirm handler doesn't have access to the original multi-destination array. This is a functional gap for collective + requiresConfirmation flows: hosts are added as attendees (via evt.team?) but their calendars don't get events. Actually, handleConfirmation calls EventManager.create which uses evt.destinationCalendar — with only one entry, only one calendar event is created. The other hosts are in evt.team.members (if set) and would be invited as attendees to the organizer's calendar event, but won't have the event on their own calendars. This matches the PR's goal ("host can get invited correctly") — invited as attendees, yes, but not getting their own calendar event. Depending on interpretation, this may be acceptable (hosts get the event via attendee invitation on the organizer's calendar), but the PR title says "handle collective multiple host on destinationCalendar" implying each host's calendar should get the event. The confirm path doesn't achieve that.

title: TypeError when destinationCalendar is empty array: mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration on undefined
body: Line 118-119: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []; if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")`. When evt.destinationCalendar is `[]` (now produced by many call sites: bookingReminder.ts:130, webhook.ts:119/229, confirm.handler.ts:175-179, editLocation.handler.ts:85-89, requestReschedule.handler.ts:240-242, deleteCredential.handler.ts:290-294, handleCancelBooking.ts:251-255/528-532, paypal-webhook.ts:152-156), `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined`, and `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')`. This crashes EventManager.create for ANY Google Meet booking where destinationCalendar is empty — i.e., users without a configured destination calendar who use Google Meet. The optional chaining `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"` is required; with it, undefined !== "google_calendar" is true, correctly falling back to Cal Video.

title: CalendarEventClass.destinationCalendar type uses Prisma DestinationCalendar[] but CalendarEvent interface allows null — class should match
body: Line 26: `destinationCalendar?: DestinationCalendar[] | null;` — matches the interface. OK, no issue. Skip.

title: bookingReminder evt.destinationCalendar uses booking.destinationCalendar || user.destinationCalendar — single calendar, no team hosts
body: Line 107: `const selectedDestinationCalendar = booking.destinationCalendar || user.destinationCalendar;` and line 130: `destinationCalendar: selectedDestinationCalendar ? [selectedDestinationCalendar] : []`. This is only used for sendOrganizerRequestReminderEmail (line 133) — an email, not calendar event creation. So the destinationCalendar in the evt is only used for email content (if at all). Low impact — the reminder email doesn't create calendar events. No fix needed beyond consistency.

title: evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars) — optional chaining on possibly-null array silently skips team calendars
body: Line ~1074: `if (isTeamEventType && eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE") { evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars); }`. When evt.destinationCalendar is null (no eventType.destinationCalendar and no organizerUser.destinationCalendar — line ~1063 sets null in that case), the `?.push` is a no-op and teamDestinationCalendars are silently dropped. This means collective events where the organizer has no destination calendar configured will not create calendar events on team members' calendars either — the entire multi-host destination feature is defeated in this case. The array should be initialized to include team calendars regardless: `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]` for collective events.

title: createEvent in no-credentialId branch doesn't pass destination.externalId, losing calendar selection for Google
body: Line 376-382: when a destination entry has no credentialId, the code finds all credentials matching `destination.integration` and calls `createEvent(c, event)` — WITHOUT passing `destination.externalId` as the third argument. CalendarManager.createEvent's third param `externalId` is then undefined, and the returned EventResult.externalId is undefined. GoogleCalendarService.createEvent uses `credentialId` (second param, correctly passed as `credential.id` by CalendarManager) to find the matching destination calendar — so for Google, the calendar selection still works via credentialId matching. BUT the returned reference's externalCalendarId will be undefined (since result.externalId is undefined), so future updates/deletes that rely on reference.externalCalendarId will fall back to the (broken) destinationCalendar lookup. The call should be `createEvent(c, event, destination.externalId)` to thread the externalId through.

title: createEvent's externalId parameter is optional but GoogleCalendarService relies on credentialId matching — inconsistent selection mechanisms
body: CalendarManager.createEvent (line 218-270) accepts `externalId?: string` and passes it through to the result. GoogleCalendarService.createEvent (line 87) accepts `credentialId: number` and uses `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` — it does NOT use the externalId param passed by CalendarManager (CalendarManager doesn't even pass externalId to calendar.createEvent — it only puts it in the result!). Wait, let me re-read: CalendarManager.createEvent line 236: `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` — it passes credential.id as the second arg (credentialId), NOT externalId. The externalId param of CalendarManager.createEvent is only used in the return value (line 267: `externalId`). So GoogleCalendarService receives credentialId and finds the destination by credentialId — correct. But the externalId param of CalendarManager.createEvent (passed by EventManager as destination.externalId) is IGNORED by the calendar service — it's only recorded in the result. For Google, credentialId matching works. For other services that don't use credentialId (Office365, CalDAV, Lark — which don't even accept the param), the externalId is not used for calendar selection. So the externalId param is effectively dead for calendar selection — it's only metadata. This is a design inconsistency: either services should accept and use externalId for selection, or the param should be removed. Currently, Google works via credentialId; others are broken for multi-destination (as reported).

title: Only first destination calendar persisted on booking — multi-host destination info lost for reschedule/cancel/confirm flows
body: Line ~1871-1877: `destinationCalendar: evt.destinationCalendar && evt.destinationCalendar.length > 0 ? { connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id } } : undefined`. The Booking Prisma model has a single `destinationCalendar` relation (one-to-one). The evt.destinationCalendar array contains the organizer's calendar plus all collective team members' calendars (built at lines ~1060-1074). Only the FIRST entry's id is connected to the booking. All subsequent flows that reconstruct evt.destinationCalendar from the booking (handleCancelBooking line 251-255, confirm.handler line 175-179, requestReschedule.handler line 240-242, editLocation.handler line 85-89, payment webhooks) will only see the organizer's calendar — team hosts' destination calendars are lost. While calendar event updates/deletes primarily use booking.references (which do capture all created events with their credentialIds), the destinationCalendar-based fallbacks in calendar services and the evt passed to emails/webhooks will be incomplete. For the PR's stated goal ("host can get invited correctly"), the critical paths (create) work via references, but reschedule/cancel rely on references too (EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents iterates references). The main risk is the broken fallback paths in GoogleCalendarService (update/delete find by externalId) and the evt.destinationCalendar used for email content. A proper fix requires a schema migration to support multiple destination calendars on Booking (many-to-many), or ensuring all flows rely exclusively on references (which have credentialId + externalCalendarId per event).

title: Webhook secret comparison is not constant-time and fails open on missing env vars
body: The webhook secret check uses a plain `!==` string comparison between `req.headers[...]` and `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. This is vulnerable to timing attacks, and worse: if `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset (empty string) and the attacker sends an empty/missing header value, `undefined !== undefined` is false, so the check passes and the endpoint proceeds. Although `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` (packages/lib/constants.ts:103) requires both `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` to be truthy, the header lookup `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"]` can still be `undefined` while the env var is set, and `undefined !== "secret"` correctly rejects — but the comparison should use a constant-time comparison (e.g. crypto.timingSafeEqual) and explicitly reject when either side is missing. Additionally, the endpoint does not restrict `req.method` to POST, so any HTTP method (GET, etc.) is accepted.

title: Unhandled Zod parse error returns a 500 with stack details instead of a 400
body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a ZodError when the body is invalid. In a Next.js API route, an uncaught throw results in a 500 response and potentially leaks validation error details (including the shape of expected fields) to the caller. It should be wrapped in `safeParse` and return a 400 with a generic message. The same applies to the `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` on line 57, which throws on malformed ciphertext or invalid JSON, producing an unhandled 500.

title: Decryption uses an empty-string fallback key and stores arbitrary attacker-controlled JSON as credential key
body: `symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "")` falls back to an empty string if the env var is missing. Depending on the implementation of `symmetricDecrypt` in @calcom/lib/crypto, an empty key may either throw or (worse) be accepted, and the decrypted value is passed to `JSON.parse` with no schema validation before being written directly into `prisma.credential.key` (lines 78 and 85). A caller with the webhook secret could store arbitrary JSON structures as a credential, corrupting app behavior (e.g. missing `access_token`/`refresh_token` fields, wrong types). The decrypted `keys` should be validated against a zod schema (e.g. requiring `access_token: string`, `refresh_token: string`, `expiry_date: number`) before persisting, and the encryption key must be required (fail closed) rather than defaulting to `""`.

title: TOCTOU race between findFirst and create can create duplicate credentials
body: The handler does `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId } })` and then either `update` or `create` based on the result. Two concurrent webhook calls for the same user+app can both observe no existing credential and both execute `create`, producing duplicate credentials for the same user/app pair. Several app services assume a single credential per user (e.g. office365video callback deletes duplicates because 'when creating a video room we only do findFirst so if they have more than 1 others get ignored'), so duplicates silently break token refresh for the ignored rows. The lookup+write should be atomic (e.g. a transaction with serializable isolation, or a DB-level unique constraint plus upsert-style retry).

title: Credential sync endpoint is called over plain fetch with no authentication, TLS validation is implicit, and the response is trusted blindly
body: When `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set, `refreshOAuthTokens` POSTs `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` to that endpoint and returns the raw `Response`. There is no authentication on this outbound call (no shared secret header), so any party that can influence DNS/network could impersonate the endpoint; conversely the endpoint receives the userId in plaintext. More importantly, callers then treat the response body as valid OAuth tokens. In `parseRefreshTokenResponse` the `minimumTokenResponseSchema` only requires `access_token: z.string()` plus a numeric field — it does not require an expiry field, and `parseRefreshTokenResponse` then fabricates `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` (line 26) when absent. The fabricated refresh token is persisted to the DB (e.g. googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97-101 writes `key` including the fake refresh_token), which will permanently break future refreshes for that credential. The schema should require a real expiry and the code should refuse to persist a placeholder refresh token.

title: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses invalid zod index-signature syntax and does not validate what callers need
body: The schema declares `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()`. In zod, computed keys in object literals are not index signatures — `[z.string().toString()]` evaluates to the literal string `"string"` (the result of `z.string().toString()`), so the schema effectively becomes `{ access_token: string, string: number, string: unknown }`, which is almost certainly not the intent and will mis-validate token responses (e.g. it may strip or reject real fields like `expires_in`). The intent was likely `.catchall(z.unknown())` or `z.object({ access_token: z.string() }).passthrough()`. As written, when credential sharing is enabled the strict per-app schemas (e.g. `zoomRefreshedTokenSchema` requiring `refresh_token`, `expires_in`, `token_type`) are bypassed entirely, so malformed sync-endpoint responses are accepted and persisted.

title: Missing refresh_token is silently replaced with the literal string "refresh_token" and persisted
body: When the parsed response has no `refresh_token`, the code sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` — a placeholder string, not a token. Callers (e.g. packages/app-store/zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:118-124, packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:95-101) write this into `prisma.credential.key` and future refresh attempts will send `refresh_token="refresh_token"` to the provider, which will always fail with invalid_grant, permanently breaking the credential until the user reconnects. The correct behavior is to preserve the existing refresh token from the stored credential (OAuth providers typically omit refresh_token on refresh responses) or reject the response; writing a literal placeholder is a data-integrity bug.

title: Token refresh reads `res?.data` but refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response whose body is never parsed in the sync path
body: In the non-sync path, `refreshFunction` returns `fetchTokens.res` (a GaxiosResponse) and `res?.data` is the token JSON. But when credential sync is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `Response` object from `fetch(CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT)` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-15) — a `Response` has no `.data` property, so `token` is `undefined` and `token.access_token` on line 95 throws a TypeError. The sync path is therefore completely broken for Google Calendar: the code needs to `await response.json()` (and check `response.ok`) before reading `access_token`/`expiry_date`. The same mismatch affects every caller that expects the provider-shaped object: hubspot (expects a HubspotToken with `expiresIn`), lark (passes the Response into `handleLarkError` which calls `.json()` — that one works), office365 (`handleErrorsJson(response)` works), zoom/webex (`handleZoomResponse`/`handleWebexResponse` call `.json()` — work), but googlecalendar and hubspot and zoho-bigin and zohocrm and salesforce read `.data` directly and will crash or misbehave.

title: HubSpot refresh treats a fetch Response as a HubspotToken, then reads `.expiresIn` off it
body: When credential sync is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `Response` object, but the code assigns it to `hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken` and immediately reads `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` (line 192) and `hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken` (line 202). A `Response` has neither property, so `expiryDate` becomes `NaN` (`Math.round(Date.now() + undefined * 1000)`) and `setAccessToken(undefined)` is called, corrupting the stored credential with `expiryDate: NaN` and breaking all subsequent HubSpot calls. The response body must be parsed (`await response.json()`) and validated before use.

title: zoho-bigin passes credentialId (a number) as the userId argument to refreshOAuthTokens
body: `refreshOAuthTokens(refreshFn, "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes `credential.id` (the credential's primary key) where the function's third parameter is documented/used as `userId: number | null` and is sent to the sync endpoint as `calcomUserId` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:11). The sync endpoint will therefore receive a credential ID instead of a Cal.com user ID, so the self-hoster's app store cannot map it to the right user and token refresh via sync will target the wrong (or no) user. It should pass `credential.userId` like every other integration does.

title: Salesforce getClient performs a token refresh on every instantiation and never uses refreshOAuthTokens, and the new code has a logic bug in the error check
body: The diff adds an unconditional `fetch` to Salesforce's token endpoint inside `getClient` (which runs in the constructor path for every calendar operation), so every Salesforce API call now triggers a refresh-token request — a performance regression and a behavioral change (Salesforce rotates refresh tokens; doing this per-request can invalidate tokens concurrently). Additionally, the guard `if (response.statusText !== "OK")` is wrong: `statusText` for a 200 response is typically `"OK"` but for many HTTP clients/proxies it can be empty; the correct check is `!response.ok`. As written, a successful response with an empty statusText would throw, and a failed response whose statusText happens to be "OK" would be treated as success. Also, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` is called but its result is checked with `accessTokenParsed.success` — however `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws on failure and returns the safeParse result object on success, so `.success` works, but the earlier `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)` after a throw is dead code; and the whole block ignores the credential-sync path entirely (no `refreshOAuthTokens` call), so Salesforce is not actually integrated with the sync feature despite the PR title.

title: Salesforce credential update drops fields and uses prisma without import
body: The added code calls `prisma.credential.update(...)` at line 96, but `prisma` is not imported in this file (the imports at the top only include `@calcom/lib/*`, `@calcom/types/*`, and relative utils). This will be a `ReferenceError` at runtime (or a TS compile error) the first time a Salesforce client is constructed. Additionally, the update writes `key: { ...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: credentialKey.refresh_token }`, discarding `instance_url` and other fields from the original credential that jsforce needs (the `new jsforce.Connection` below still reads `credentialKey.instance_url`, but the stored credential loses it on subsequent loads).

title: Office365 refresh merges parsed token data but parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a safeParse result, and the old error logging was removed
body: The code does `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }`. `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the zod safeParse result object (with `.success`/`.data`), so this spread is correct in shape — but note that when credential sync is enabled, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` validates against `minimumTokenResponseSchema` (which, per the schema bug, may strip fields) and fabricates `refresh_token: "refresh_token"`, which would overwrite the real refresh token in the stored credential. Also, the previous `console.error` logging of zod errors and the MS response was removed, so failures are now silent. And `refreshTokenResponseSchema` transforms `expires_in` into an absolute `expiry_date`-style value but the field is still named `expires_in` and `getToken` checks `isExpired(o365AuthCredentials.expires_in)` — mixing semantics.

title: MS Teams refresh computes expiry_date in milliseconds while isExpired compares against seconds-since-epoch elsewhere
body: `responseBody.expiry_date = Math.round(Date.now() + (responseBody?.expires_in || 0) * 1000)` produces milliseconds, and `isExpired = (expiryDate: number) => expiryDate < Math.round(+new Date())` compares against milliseconds too — so within this file it is consistent. However the credential is also written by `office365calendar/api/callback.ts` which sets `expiry_date = Math.round(+new Date() / 1000 + responseBody.expires_in)` (seconds). The two Office365 apps share the `msteams` app keys and the same `office365_video`/`office365_calendar` credential types are distinct, but any code path or future change that reads `expiry_date` with the other convention will misjudge expiry by a factor of 1000. At minimum this inconsistency between the two Office365 adapters (seconds in calendar callback/CalendarService, milliseconds in video adapter) is a latent bug; the units should be normalized and documented.

title: isTokenValid logic is inverted
body: `const isTokenValid = (token: ZoomToken) => (token.expires_in || token.expiry_date) < Date.now();` returns true when the token is expired (this is pre-existing code, unchanged by the diff, but the PR touches this file and the surrounding refresh logic). Combined with `getToken` returning the access token when `!isTokenValid(...)` is false, the naming/logic is inverted: `isTokenValid` actually means "is expired". This is confusing but functionally the refresh path triggers correctly; it is worth flagging because the PR modifies the refresh flow and a future refactor could easily flip it. (Pre-existing, but adjacent to changed lines 79-125.)

title: parseRefreshTokenResponse result misused: it returns a safeParse result but the sync path bypasses zoomRefreshedTokenSchema
body: When credential sync is enabled, `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseBody, zoomRefreshedTokenSchema)` validates against `minimumTokenResponseSchema` instead of `zoomRefreshedTokenSchema`. The minimum schema only requires `access_token` and fabricates `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when missing. Zoom's refresh response always includes a new `refresh_token`; if the sync endpoint omits it, the placeholder is persisted (line 120: `key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token`), permanently breaking Zoom token refresh. The code then reads `newTokens.expires_in` (line 122) which the minimum schema does not guarantee is present (its numeric catch-all is broken — see the parseRefreshTokenResponse finding), so `key.expiry_date` can become `NaN`.

title: Webex isTokenValid logic is inverted (pre-existing, adjacent to changed refresh code)
body: `const isTokenValid = (token: WebexToken) => token.expiry_date < Date.now();` returns true when the token is expired, and `getToken` uses `!isTokenValid(credentialKey) ? Promise.resolve(credentialKey.access_token) : refreshAccessToken(...)`. Functionally this still refreshes when expired, but the inverted naming is a trap; the PR rewires the refresh path (lines 62-78) and any cleanup of this function could silently break refresh. Flagging because the changed code depends on this predicate.

title: Zoho CRM isTokenValid logic is inverted (pre-existing, adjacent to changed refresh code)
body: `const isValid = token && token.access_token && token.expiryDate && token.expiryDate < Date.now();` — this returns truthy when the token IS expired (expiryDate in the past), and `getToken` resolves without refreshing when `isTokenValid(credentialKey)` is true. So an expired token is treated as valid and the stale access token is used; a valid (unexpired) token triggers a refresh. This is inverted and will cause Zoho CRM calls to fail with 401 until the token happens to be refreshed by the other branch. The PR modifies the refresh function this predicate gates (lines 204-216), so the bug is directly in the changed feature's path.

title: zoho-bigin expiryDate computed in milliseconds while BiginToken.expiryDate convention elsewhere is milliseconds — but isTokenValid compares to Date.now(), and the sync path returns a Response whose .data is undefined
body: When sync is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `Response`; the code then reads `tokenInfo.data.error` (line 96) — a `Response` has no `.data`, so `tokenInfo.data` is `undefined` and `tokenInfo.data.error` throws a TypeError inside `refreshAccessToken`, which is not caught here (the function has no try/catch), so the whole auth fails. The non-sync path returns an axios response where `.data` is correct. The sync path must `await response.json()` first. (Same class of bug as the Google/HubSpot findings: callers assume provider-shaped objects but receive a fetch Response.)

title: Lark refresh passes a fetch Response into handleLarkError which expects a Response — OK — but the sync path response is not JSON-validated and refresh token rotation is mishandled
body: In the sync path, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `Response` from the sync endpoint; `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>(resp, this.log)` presumably calls `resp.json()` and checks Lark's `code !== 0` envelope. A self-hoster's sync endpoint returning `{ access_token, expires_in, refresh_token, refresh_expires_in }` (flat, no Lark envelope) would fail the `code === 0` check or produce `data.data` undefined, throwing. The sync contract (flat token response) is incompatible with Lark's envelope expectations unless handleLarkError is tolerant. Additionally, when the sync endpoint does not return a new `refresh_token`, `newLarkAuthCredentials.refresh_token` becomes `undefined` and overwrites the stored refresh token (line 92), breaking future refreshes — the existing refresh token should be preserved when the response omits one.

title: No timeout, no retry, and no Content-Type header on the sync endpoint request; response.ok is never checked
body: The `fetch` to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` has no `AbortController`/timeout, so a hung sync endpoint will block token refresh indefinitely (calendar operations hang). There is no `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded` header even though the body is `URLSearchParams` (some servers reject or misparse the body without it). And the returned `Response` is never checked for `ok`/status — a 500 from the sync endpoint is treated the same as a success and its body is parsed as tokens by callers, persisting garbage (e.g. an HTML error page fails JSON.parse, or a JSON error object is partially accepted by the broken minimum schema).

title: Credential creation does not set `invalid: false` explicitly and does not validate that appMetadata.type matches the app's expected credential type
body: When creating a credential, the handler uses `type: appMetadata.type` from `appStoreMetadata`. If the appSlug maps to an app whose metadata `type` differs from what the app's services expect (e.g. a slug collision or a misconfigured app store entry), the credential is created with a wrong `type`, and services that look up credentials by `type` (e.g. `findFirst({ where: { type: "zoom_video" } })`) will not find it. There is also no validation that the decrypted `keys` object contains the fields the app requires (access_token, refresh_token, expiry). The webhook should validate the payload shape per app type or at least a minimal common shape.

title: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is a string-or-empty value, not a boolean, and is used in boolean contexts
body: `export const APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED = process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY;` evaluates to `string | undefined` (the value of the last truthy env var, or `undefined`). It is used as a boolean in `if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED)` (works) and in `if (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT)` (works), but exporting a truthy string as a flag named `..._ENABLED` is misleading and will break if anyone does strict `=== true` checks or serializes it. It should be wrapped in `Boolean(...)` or `!!(...)`.

title: Unrelated hardcoded redirect URI change slipped into the diff
body: The diff changes `const redirectUri = WEBAPP_URL + `/api/integrations/${appConfig.slug}/callback`` to a hardcoded `` `/api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback` ``. If `appConfig.slug` is `"zoho-bigin"` this is a no-op, but if the config slug ever differs (e.g. a renamed app), the OAuth redirect URI registered in Zoho would silently mismatch. This change is unrelated to the credential-sync feature and should either be reverted or justified.

title: No tests for the new webhook endpoint or the sync/refresh helpers
body: The PR adds a new public API endpoint (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`) and two new shared helpers (`refreshOAuthTokens`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse`) that alter the token-refresh path of ~10 integrations, but the PR description's checklist explicitly states "I haven't added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works". There are no unit tests covering: webhook secret validation, the disabled-feature 403, user/app lookup, decrypt+create/update, the sync-vs-direct branch in refreshOAuthTokens, or the placeholder refresh_token behavior in parseRefreshTokenResponse. Given that the refresh path is security-critical (OAuth tokens), tests are needed before merge.

title: Inconsistent app slug values passed by different integrations ("zoomvideo" vs "zoom", "msteams" vs "office365-calendar")
body: Callers pass different slug strings for the same underlying app: zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts passes `"zoomvideo"` while zoomvideo/api/callback.ts creates the credential with `appId: "zoom"`; office365video passes `"msteams"` while office365calendar passes `"office365-calendar"`. The sync endpoint receives `appSlug` and must map it to the self-hoster's app store; inconsistent slugs between the credential's `appId` and the sync request's `appSlug` will cause lookups to fail on the self-hoster side. The slug sent to the sync endpoint should match the credential's `appId` (i.e. `credential.appId`) rather than a hardcoded per-call-site string.

title: parseRefreshTokenResponse return value used as the credential key, discarding the original credential fields
body: `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` — `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the zod safeParse result object (`{ success, data }`), not the parsed data. This `key` is then written to `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })` (line 100). So the stored credential key becomes `{ success: true, data: { ...tokens } }` instead of the token object itself — the credential is corrupted and `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` on next load will fail (the stored object has no `access_token` at the top level). It should be `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...).data` (after checking `.success`). This is a direct data-corruption bug in the changed lines.

title: parseRefreshTokenResponse return value spread includes the `success` flag into the credential key
body: `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }` — this correctly spreads only `.data`, so this call site is fine; however note that `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws on failure, so `tokenResponse.success` is always true here and the `&&` guard is dead. Not a bug per se, but combined with the googlecalendar misuse of the same helper (returning the whole result object), the helper's return type (`SafeParseReturnType`) is error-prone: callers must remember to unwrap `.data`. The helper should either return the parsed data directly (throwing on failure, which it already does) or be renamed/typed to make the unwrapping explicit.

title: Stray empty JSDoc comment `/** */` above the handler
body: Line 16 contains `/** */` — an empty JSDoc block left over from development. It should be removed or replaced with a real description of the endpoint (method, auth, payload).

title: Webhook secret comparison is not timing-safe and fails open when env vars are unset
body: The webhook secret is compared with `!==` (non-constant-time, enabling timing attacks) and, more importantly, when `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset the comparison becomes `header !== undefined`. If the attacker sends a request without the configured header, `req.headers[...]` is `undefined`, so `undefined !== undefined` is false and the check passes — the endpoint is then only protected by `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED`, which is truthy whenever both env vars are set... but note `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is computed as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, so if the secret is unset the feature flag is falsy and the endpoint returns 403. However, if `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is set to an empty string (as in the shipped `.env.example`: `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET=""`), the flag is falsy too. The real risk: if an operator sets `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` and `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` but the header name env var (`CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME`) is misconfigured or the secret is an empty string while the flag logic changes, any request without that header passes authentication. Additionally, `req.headers[...]` is `string | string[] | undefined`; comparing an array to a string with `!==` always passes for array-valued headers, and the value is never validated to be a string. Use a constant-time comparison (e.g. `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on hashed buffers) and explicitly reject when either env var is missing or empty.

title: Unhandled Zod parse error returns a 500 with a stack-trace-bearing error instead of a 400
body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a `ZodError` on invalid input. Because the handler does not catch it, Next.js returns a 500 and the raw Zod error (including the received payload shape) leaks to the caller. The endpoint should use `safeParse` and return a 400 with a generic message. The same applies to the `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` on line 57, which throws on malformed/undecryptable payloads, producing an unhandled 500.

title: Decryption uses an empty-string key fallback and stores attacker-controlled JSON verbatim as the credential key
body: `symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "")` silently falls back to an empty key. Depending on the implementation of `symmetricDecrypt` in `@calcom/lib/crypto`, an empty key may either throw or — worse — decrypt with a predictable key, letting an attacker who knows the code forge `keys` payloads. The handler must verify `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is set (and of the expected length) before decrypting and return 500/403 otherwise. Additionally, the decrypted `keys` value is `JSON.parse`d with no schema validation and written directly into `prisma.credential.key` (lines 78 and 85). A valid webhook caller (or anyone if the secret check is bypassed) can store arbitrary JSON — including a `refresh_token`/`access_token` of their choosing for any user and any app — which is then used by the calendar/video services to act against third-party APIs. The decrypted payload should be validated against a per-app credential schema before persisting.

title: findFirst-then-update/create race allows duplicate credentials and lost updates
body: The handler does `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId } })` and then either `update` or `create` based on the result. Two concurrent webhook calls for the same user/app both see no credential and both `create`, producing duplicate credentials for the same user+app (the schema does not enforce uniqueness on `(userId, appId)` — other callbacks in this codebase, e.g. zoomvideo/webex/tandem, explicitly `deleteMany` existing credentials first, confirming duplicates are possible). Concurrent updates can also overwrite each other. The write should be atomic — e.g. a transaction, or `upsert` on a unique constraint, or `updateMany`/`create` guarded by a transaction with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` semantics.

title: Endpoint does not restrict HTTP method or content type
body: The handler responds to any HTTP method (POST, GET, PUT, ...) and never checks `req.method`. A GET request with a query-string body would still be parsed by Next.js into `req.body` for some content types, and more importantly there is no method gate, so the endpoint's behavior is not constrained to the documented webhook POST. It should return 405 for non-POST methods. Relatedly, `req.body` may be a string if the content type is not JSON, which would make the Zod parse fail with a 500 (see the parse finding).

title: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses invalid zod index-signature syntax and will not validate as intended
body: The schema is written as `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional() })`. Computed keys with zod schemas are not valid index signatures — zod index signatures must be created with `z.record(...)` or `.catchall(...)`.
