ActiveModel::Serializers' `has_many` with `embed: :ids` calls `object.embeddable_hosts` (works on OpenStruct via method_missing) and then maps to ids — this likely works, but `embed: :ids` means the response only contains `embeddable_host_ids: [...]` and NOT the embedded host objects. The Ember route does `this.store.find('embedding')` and the template iterates `embedding.embeddable_hosts` expecting full host objects with `host.host` and `host.category`. With `embed: :ids`, the store's `_hydrateEmbedded` (store.js.es6) looks up `root['embeddable_hosts']` (plural collection) in the payload — which is absent because ids-only embedding produces `embeddable_host_ids`. The `_lookupSubType` for the `embeddable_host_ids` key (matching `/(.+)_id(s?)$/`) will try to find each id in `root['embeddable_hosts']`, which is undefined, so `hydrated` will be `[undefined, ...]` and `obj['embeddable_hosts'] = [undefined...]`. The admin UI will render broken/empty rows. The serializer should use `embed: :objects` (or embed the objects with their serializer) so the payload contains an `embeddable_hosts` array, matching what the Ember store and template expect.

title: save() sends only the 'host' property, dropping category_id from the buffered changes and never persisting category edits
body: `const props = this.get('buffered').getProperties('host');` fetches only the `host` key from the buffer, then `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')` is set on the props object. But `categoryId` is a separate component property bound to the `category-chooser`, and it is only initialized in the `edit()` action (`this.set('categoryId', this.get('host.category.id'))`). For a NEW host (created via `addHost`), `edit()` is never called, so `categoryId` stays `null`; when saving, `props.category_id = null` is sent, and the server-side `save_host` then defaults it to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` (controller line 25). So a newly added host can never be assigned a non-default category through the UI — the category chooser selection is silently discarded on create. Additionally, `getProperties('host')` returns the buffered host string, and assigning `props.category_id` mutates that plain object correctly, but if the buffer contained more keys they'd be dropped. The fix: build props explicitly, e.g. `const props = { host: this.get('buffered.host'), category_id: this.get('categoryId') }`, and initialize `categoryId` for new records (or bind the chooser directly to `buffered.category_id`).

title: After save, category is set from a possibly-null categoryId, desyncing the model from the server response
body: After a successful save, the code does `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')))`. If `categoryId` is null (new host saved without choosing a category — see related finding), `findById(null)` returns undefined and the host's `category` is set to undefined even though the server defaulted `category_id` to the uncategorized category. The server response (serialized with `rest_serializer: true`) contains the authoritative `category_id`, but it is ignored. The component should rely on the save response / `host.reload()` or at least fall back to the server-provided `category_id` rather than the possibly-stale local `categoryId`.

title: saveChanges action calls update({}) with no attributes and has no UI trigger
body: `saveChanges()` calls `this.get('embedding').update({})` — an empty attribute hash. The `embedding` model is an OpenStruct-backed singleton with only `id` and `embeddable_hosts`; there are no editable scalar attributes on the embedding itself (all settings like embed_truncate remain site settings). The template (embedding.hbs) has no button wired to `saveChanges`, so this action is dead code that would issue a pointless PUT /admin/customize/embedding with an empty payload if ever invoked. Either remove the action or wire it to actual embedding-level settings; as written it is misleading dead code.

title: basePath type normalization breaks existing admin models whose type key uses underscores
body: `basePath` now does `ADMIN_MODELS.indexOf(type.replace('_', '-'))`. `String.replace` with a string pattern replaces only the FIRST occurrence, and more importantly the check is applied to the raw `type` passed from the store. For the existing admin model `site-customization`, the store type key is `site-customization` (already dashed) so it still matches. But for `plugin` it matches. The new `embeddable-host` type is dashed, so it matches. However, if any caller uses the underscored form `embeddable_host` (e.g. `store.createRecord('embeddable_host')` as done in admin-embedding.js.es6 line 10!), `type.replace('_', '-')` converts it to `embeddable-host` and it matches — OK. But `Ember.String.underscore(store.pluralize(type))` in `pathFor` will pluralize `embeddable_host` to `embeddable_hosts` and underscore to `embeddable_hosts`, producing `/admin/embeddable_hosts` — while the Rails route is `resources :embeddable_hosts` under the admin namespace, which by default maps to `/admin/embeddable_hosts` — that matches. The subtle break: `type.replace('_', '-')` only replaces the first underscore; a type like `foo_bar_baz` becomes `foo-bar_baz` and won't match a dashed ADMIN_MODELS entry. This is fragile; use `type.replace(/_/g, '-')` or `Ember.String.dasherize(type)` for correctness.

title: _hydrateEmbedded maps plural _ids keys without guarding against non-array values, producing [undefined] entries
body: The new plural branch does `obj[k].map(...)` whenever the key matches `/(.+)_id(s?)$/` with the `s` group. If a serializer sends `category_ids: null` or a non-array (e.g. a single id, or an empty string), `.map` either throws (null) or iterates characters (string), corrupting the hydrated object. There is no `Ember.isArray(obj[k])` guard. The single-id branch guards with `if (hydrated)`, but the plural branch assigns `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []` where `hydrated` is the result of `.map` — if `_lookupSubType` returns undefined for a missing id, the array contains `undefined` entries rather than being filtered. This affects the new `embeddable_host_ids` embedding path (see EmbeddingSerializer finding): when the payload contains `embeddable_host_ids` but no `embeddable_hosts` collection, `_lookupSubType` returns undefined for each id and the model ends up with `embeddable_hosts = [undefined, undefined, ...]`. Add an `Ember.isArray` check and filter out undefined lookups.

title: Serializer exposes only category_id, but the Ember component reads host.category (object) for display and editing
body: `EmbeddableHostSerializer` emits `id, host, category_id`. The Ember component `embeddable-host.js.es6` reads `this.get('host.category.id')` in `edit()` and the template renders `{{category-badge host.category}}`. With only `category_id` serialized (and the embedding payload using `embed: :ids` per the EmbeddingSerializer), the store's `_hydrateEmbedded` will attempt to resolve `category_id` via `_lookupSubType('category', ...)`, which special-cases categories via `Discourse.Category.findById(id)` — this works only if the category is already loaded client-side. For an admin page where categories may not be preloaded, `host.category` will be undefined and the badge renders blank, and `edit()` sets `categoryId` to undefined. The serializer should include the category object (e.g. `has_one :category` or a `category` attribute with BasicCategorySerializer) when `rest_serializer` is used for the embedding payload, or the component should use `host.category_id` directly with the category-chooser.

title: Category fabricators were moved into the wrong file, leaving category_fabricator.rb containing only the embeddable_host fabricator
body: The diff shows `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` was gutted: all category fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`) were deleted from it and now that file contains ONLY `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`. Meanwhile `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` was created containing the category fabricators (and NOT the embeddable_host fabricator). The two files' contents are swapped. This means: (1) `Fabricate(:embeddable_host)` is defined in `category_fabricator.rb` — it will load, but the file name is wrong and confusing; (2) more critically, the `:embeddable_host` fabricator references `category` (line 3: `category`), which requires the `:category` fabricator — that now lives in `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. Fabrication loads all files in spec/fabricators, so both will be loaded and it may work by accident, but the file naming is inverted: `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` should contain the embeddable_host fabricator and `category_fabricator.rb` should contain the category fabricators. This is clearly a copy-paste/file-swap mistake that will confuse maintainers and risks load-order issues.

title: embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains category fabricators instead of the embeddable_host fabricator
body: This file is named `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` but its entire content is the category fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`) — the exact content that was removed from `category_fabricator.rb`. The actual `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` block (host "eviltrout.com", category) was placed in `category_fabricator.rb` instead. The two files have been swapped. Every spec that does `Fabricate(:embeddable_host)` (embed_controller_spec, topic_embed_spec, topic_spec, embeddable_host_spec) depends on this fabricator being correctly defined and associated with a category; while Fabrication loads all fabricator files so it may resolve, the misplacement is a clear defect: the embeddable_host fabricator belongs in embeddable_host_fabricator.rb, and the category fabricators belong in category_fabricator.rb. Fix by swapping the file contents back.

title: Authorization relies on redundant before_filter in addition to Admin::AdminController and route constraint
body: `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` inherits from `Admin::AdminController` (which already enforces staff access) and the route is declared with `constraints: AdminConstraint.new` (admin-only, routes.rb line 153). The explicit `before_filter :ensure_logged_in, :ensure_staff` on line 3 is redundant — it downgrades the effective protection from admin-only (route constraint) to staff-only (moderators) at the controller layer. A moderator hitting the controller directly (if the route constraint were ever relaxed or bypassed) would pass `ensure_staff` but should not manage embeddable hosts. Other admin controllers in this codebase (e.g. permalinks, emojis) rely on the AdminConstraint route constraint and Admin::AdminController without re-declaring ensure_staff. Remove the redundant filter or change it to `ensure_admin` for defense in depth consistent with the AdminConstraint.

title: TopicEmbed.import silently creates topics in the uncategorized category when no EmbeddableHost matches the URL
body: `TopicEmbed.import` now does `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` and passes `category: eh.try(:category_id)` to PostCreator. `record_for_host` returns `false` (not nil) when the URL is unparseable or has no host, and returns `nil` when no DB row matches. `eh.try(:category_id)` on `false` returns nil (false doesn't respond to category_id, try returns nil), and on nil returns nil. So for any embed URL whose host is not in the allowlist, `category` is nil and PostCreator falls back to the default/uncategorized category. Previously the category came from the `embed_category` site setting, which was a single global default. Now, if an admin has not configured an EmbeddableHost for a feed URL, imported topics silently land in uncategorized instead of the configured embed category — a behavior regression for existing sites upgrading (the migration only creates EmbeddableHost rows from the old `embeddable_hosts` setting, and deletes `embed_category`; sites that relied on `embed_category` without listing every feed host in `embeddable_hosts` lose their category assignment). The import path should either reject URLs without a matching EmbeddableHost (since TopicRetriever already gates on `host_allowed?`) or fall back to a sensible default explicitly.

title: expandable_first_post? no longer checks that any embeddable host exists, changing behavior for sites with no hosts configured
body: `expandable_first_post?` was changed from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`. The `embeddable_hosts.present?` guard was removed because the setting no longer exists. But the semantic of that guard was: only offer the 'expand embed' UI when embedding is actually enabled on the site (at least one allowed host). Now, on a site with zero EmbeddableHost rows, any topic that has a TopicEmbed (e.g. created via feed polling before hosts were removed, or imported by other means) will show the expandable first-post UI even though no external site is allowed to embed it. The correct replacement guard is `EmbeddableHost.exists?` (or checking that the topic's embed_url host is allowed). The spec was updated to fabricate an embeddable_host in the 'with an embeddable host' context, confirming the intent, but the production code lost the check entirely.

title: Controller spec only checks inheritance; no tests for create/update/destroy behavior or authorization
body: The entire spec for Admin::EmbeddableHostsController is a single assertion that the class is a subclass of Admin::AdminController. There are no tests for: creating a host (happy path + validation failure), updating a host, destroying a host, the nil-record 500 bug (see controller finding), authorization (non-staff/non-admin rejected), or the category_id defaulting to uncategorized when blank. Given this controller performs writes against a security-sensitive allowlist (embeddable hosts control which external sites can iframe the forum), the absence of any behavioral or authorization test is a significant gap. At minimum, add tests mirroring other admin controller specs: admin can create/update/destroy, moderator is denied (route constraint is AdminConstraint), invalid host returns 422, missing id returns 404 (once fixed).

title: Embedding controller spec only checks inheritance; show/update serialization untested
body: Like the embeddable_hosts spec, this spec contains only `expect(Admin::EmbeddingController < Admin::AdminController).to eq(true)`. The `show` action's serialization (EmbeddingSerializer with the OpenStruct, embed: :ids behavior) and the `update` action are completely untested. Given the serializer/store contract concerns around `embed: :ids` vs the Ember client expecting embedded objects (see EmbeddingSerializer finding), a serialization spec asserting the JSON shape of GET /admin/customize/embedding is essential. Add a test that GETs the show action as admin and asserts the response contains the expected structure (embeddable_hosts with id/host/category_id), and that non-admins are rejected.

title: update action is a no-op that re-renders show; PUT /admin/customize/embedding accepts and ignores any payload
body: `update` simply re-renders the embedding serializer without reading or applying any params. The route `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"` (routes.rb line 139) accepts a PUT with an arbitrary body and returns 200 with the current embedding state, silently discarding whatever the client sent. The Ember adapter's `update` (rest.js.es6 line 56) sends `data[typeField] = attrs` and expects `json[typeField]` back. This is a misleading API: clients may believe settings were saved. Either implement actual update semantics (e.g. accept embed_truncate and other embedding settings) or remove the PUT route and the `saveChanges` controller action to avoid a dead, misleading endpoint.

title: resources :embeddable_hosts generates an index/show route that has no controller action
body: `resources :embeddable_hosts, constraints: AdminConstraint.new` generates all RESTful routes including GET /admin/embeddable_hosts (index) and GET /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id (show). `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` only defines `create`, `update`, and `destroy` — there are no `index` or `show` actions. A request to those routes will raise AbstractController::ActionNotFound (or UnknownFormat) → 500/404. Since the Ember client fetches hosts via the embedding endpoint (GET /admin/customize/embedding), the index/show routes are unnecessary. Restrict the resource: `resources :embeddable_hosts, only: [:create, :update, :destroy], constraints: AdminConstraint.new`.

title: Template hides the entire hosts table (and shows nothing) when there are zero hosts, with no empty-state message
body: `{{#if embedding.embeddable_hosts}}` wraps the whole table. When no hosts exist, the admin sees only the 'Add Host' button with no explanation, and — combined with the EmbeddingSerializer `embed: :ids` issue — `embedding.embeddable_hosts` may be undefined or an array of undefined entries even when hosts exist, causing the table to render with broken rows or not at all. Add an `{{else}}` branch with an empty-state message (e.g. i18n 'admin.embedding.no_hosts'), and ensure the serializer actually embeds host objects so the `if` evaluates correctly.

title: @on('didInsertElement') combined with @observes('editing') refocuses the input on every edit toggle, fighting user interaction
body: The `_focusOnInput` method is decorated with both `@on('didInsertElement')` and `@observes('editing')`. The observer fires whenever `editing` changes (i.e., when entering AND leaving edit mode). When leaving edit mode (editing becomes false), the observer still schedules `this.$('.host-name').focus()` in afterRender — but by then the input may no longer exist (the `{{#if editing}}` block has been torn down), so `this.$('.host-name')` is an empty jQuery set and `.focus()` is a no-op; harmless but sloppy. More importantly, the observer firing on `editing` becoming false is unintended. The intent is clearly to focus only when entering edit mode. Use `@observes('editing')` with a guard `if (this.get('editing'))`, or better, drop the observer and call the focus logic explicitly from the `edit()` action and `didInsertElement` when `host.isNew`.

title: destroyRecord failure leaves the host in the list and gives no feedback beyond the generic ajax error popup
body: In the `delete` action, `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { this.sendAction('deleteHost', this.get('host')); })` only removes the host from the controller's list on success. There is no `.catch(popupAjaxError)` (unlike `save`), so if the DELETE request fails (e.g. the nil-record 500 from the controller, or a network error), the promise rejection is unhandled — no error is shown to the admin and the row stays. The user gets no feedback that deletion failed. Add `.catch(popupAjaxError)` to match the `save` action's error handling.

title: No test for blank/nil host (the before_validation nil crash) and no uniqueness validation test
body: The spec tests trimming of http/https/paths and host_allowed? matching, but does not test: (1) `EmbeddableHost.new(host: nil).valid?` or `EmbeddableHost.new(host: '').valid?` — which currently crashes with NoMethodError in before_validation (see model finding); (2) duplicate host rejection (case-insensitive) — the model has no uniqueness validation; (3) that `record_for_host` returns false for nil/blank/unparseable input (the security-critical path used by EmbedController#ensure_embeddable and TopicRetriever). Adding these tests would pin down the nil-crash bug and the case-insensitive duplicate issue.

title: count action renders JSONP with unvalidated callback parameter (pre-existing, but now more exposed without host gate context)
body: `render json: {counts: by_url}, callback: params[:callback]` reflects the `callback` query parameter directly into a JSONP response. While this is pre-existing code and not changed by this PR, the PR removes the `embeddable_hosts` blank-check from `ensure_embeddable` (which also gates `count`), meaning the JSONP reflection is now reachable in configurations where previously a blank setting would have blocked it. A malicious `callback` value could be used for reflected content injection in browsers that render the response as HTML (JSONP callback injection). This should be validated against a whitelist regex (e.g. `/\A[a-zA-Z_$][a-zA-Z0-9_$]*\z/`) or removed in favor of CORS. Flagging because the PR's change to `ensure_embeddable` alters the exposure of this endpoint.

title: category-chooser bound to categoryId which is not initialized for new records, so new hosts cannot pick a category
body: The `{{category-chooser value=categoryId}}` binds to the component's `categoryId` property, which is initialized to `null` (component line 9) and only set in the `edit()` action. For a new host row (created via `addHost` → `store.createRecord('embeddable-host')`), `edit()` is never invoked (the row starts in editing mode because `host.isNew` is true), so `categoryId` remains null. The chooser shows no selection, and on save `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')` sends null, which the server replaces with the uncategorized category. The admin's category selection for a new host is therefore always ignored. Initialize `categoryId` when the host is new (e.g. in `didInsertElement` if `host.isNew`, set it to the default/uncategorized category id) or bind the chooser to `buffered.category_id` so it participates in the buffer lifecycle.

title: Migration reads embed_category by joining site_settings.value to categories.name, which fails for renamed categories or non-default locales
body: The migration resolves the target category with `SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'`. This joins the site setting's value (a category NAME) to `categories.name`. If the category was renamed after the setting was configured, or if the setting holds a slug rather than a name, or if multiple categories share a name (possible in different parents), the join returns zero or multiple rows. `[0]['id']` on an empty result raises NoMethodError (nil['id']), aborting the migration. The fallback to `uncategorized_category_id` only triggers when `category_id == 0`, not when the query crashes. More robust: look up by name with `Category.where(name: value).first` semantics, or rescue and default. Also, the migration deletes the `embed_category` and `embeddable_hosts` settings at the end (line 31) — if the INSERT loop fails midway (e.g. SQL injection crash or constraint violation), the settings are NOT deleted (good), but partial embeddable_hosts rows may already be inserted, and re-running the migration will duplicate them (no uniqueness constraint). Consider wrapping in a transaction (migrations are transactional by default in Rails, but `execute` DDL/DML is fine) and adding a uniqueness guard.

title: Plural _ids hydration assigns undefined entries instead of filtering missing lookups
body: In the new plural branch of `_hydrateEmbedded`, `obj[k].map(function(id) { return self._lookupSubType(subType, type, id, root); })` — when `_lookupSubType` returns undefined (id not found in the root collection), the resulting array contains `undefined` holes. The subsequent `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []` keeps those holes. Downstream code iterating `embeddable_hosts` (e.g. the `{{#each}}` in embedding.hbs) will render rows for `undefined` entries, causing template errors (`Cannot read property 'host' of undefined`). The single-id branch guards with `if (hydrated)`, but the plural branch has no equivalent filter. Add `.filter(function(h) { return !!h; })` or use `Ember.A()` with compact semantics.

title: Locale string 'Allowed Hosts' is used as a table column header for a single host value
body: The locale key `admin.embedding.host: "Allowed Hosts"` (plural) is used in embedding.hbs line 4 as the column header for the host column (`{{i18n "admin.embedding.host"}}`). A column listing individual hostnames should be singular ("Host" or "Allowed Host"), not plural "Allowed Hosts". The plural reads incorrectly as a section title. Change to `host: "Host"` (or "Allowed Host") for the column header.

title: Silent fallback to uncategorized_category_id when category_id is blank may hide admin configuration errors
body: `host.category_id = SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id if host.category_id.blank?` silently substitutes the uncategorized category whenever the client sends a blank/nil category_id. Combined with the Ember component bug (categoryId not initialized for new hosts), this means a new host created without explicitly choosing a category is silently assigned to uncategorized — the admin may believe they set a category that was never sent. While the fallback prevents a NOT NULL violation (category_id is null: false in the migration), it masks client/server contract mismatches. Consider returning a validation error when category_id is blank on create (forcing the UI to send a valid category), or at minimum ensure the UI always sends a valid category_id (see component finding).

title: SQL injection in data migration via string interpolation of site setting values
body: The migration builds an INSERT statement by interpolating the raw `embeddable_hosts` site setting value directly into SQL: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. The value comes from the `site_settings` table (previously admin-editable free text, one host per line). Any quote or SQL metacharacter in that setting (e.g. a host line containing `'); DROP TABLE ...;--`) is executed verbatim against the database during `rake db:migrate`. This is a critical SQL injection / data-integrity risk on every deployment that has the old setting populated. Use parameterized queries (`execute` with bind params, or `sanitize_sql_array`, or ActiveRecord inserts) instead of string interpolation.

title: update/destroy crash with NoMethodError when the host id does not exist
body: `update` and `destroy` do `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then call `save_host(host)` / `host.destroy` without a nil check. If the id is missing or stale (e.g. the record was deleted in another tab, or a crafted request), `host` is nil and the request raises `NoMethodError` (500 error) instead of returning a 404. `save_host` also dereferences `host.host = ...` on a possibly-nil object. Add a `raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` (or render 404) when the record is not found.

title: Mass-assignment of arbitrary params into EmbeddableHost attributes
body: `save_host` assigns `host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `host.category_id = params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` directly from params. While the model only has `host` and `category_id` columns, this pattern bypasses strong-parameter protection and will silently accept and persist any future attribute added to the model (e.g. if a column is later added), and it does not validate that `category_id` refers to an existing category — a bogus category_id is stored, violating referential expectations (the column is `null: false` but there is no FK/validation), leaving orphaned hosts whose category badge renders nothing. Use explicit permitted params and validate the category exists.

title: before_validation mutates nil host, crashing validation when host is blank
body: The `before_validation` block calls `self.host.sub!(...)` unconditionally. When `host` is nil (e.g. a create/update request with a missing `embeddable_host[host]` param, which the controller does not guard against), `nil.sub!` raises `NoMethodError`, turning a simple validation failure into a 500 error. Guard with `self.host = host.to_s` or `if host.present?` before calling `sub!`, and add a presence validation on `host` (currently only a format validation exists, which is skipped for nil/blank values depending on configuration).

title: Host format regex is too permissive and allows path/port tricks that break referer matching
body: The validation regex `/\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i` allows an optional port and an arbitrary path suffix (`(\/.*)?`). However `record_for_host` compares only `uri.host` (no port) against the stored value with `lower(host) = ?`. Consequences: (1) a stored host of `example.com:8080` will never match a referer from `example.com` (port stripped by URI parsing), so the admin-configured host silently does not work; (2) a stored host with a path (`example.com/foo`) is stripped by `before_validation` (`self.host.sub!(/\/.*$/, '')`) so the path part of the regex is dead code; (3) the regex permits uppercase via `/i` but matching is done with `lower(host) = ?` against `uri.host` which is not downcased — `URI('http://EXAMPLE.com').host` returns `EXAMPLE.com` in some Ruby versions, causing a case-sensitivity mismatch and a stored `example.com` failing to match referer `http://EXAMPLE.com/...`. Normalize with `host.downcase` in both the callback and `record_for_host`, and decide whether ports are supported; if not, reject them in validation.

title: Referer host matching is case-sensitive and does not downcase the incoming host
body: `record_for_host` does `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` where `host = uri.host`. The stored column is lowered by the DB comparison, but the incoming `uri.host` is NOT downcased. `URI.parse('http://EVILTROUT.COM/x').host` preserves case, so a referer from `http://EVILTROUT.COM` will not match a stored `eviltrout.com`, and conversely the check is inconsistent with the model's own normalization. Downcase the parsed host (`host = uri.host.to_s.downcase`) before the query so matching is deterministic regardless of referer casing.

title: Removing the 'embeddable hosts not set' check changes behavior: embeds are now allowed with zero configured hosts in some paths
body: The old code raised `Discourse::InvalidAccess.new('embeddable hosts not set') if SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.blank?` before checking the referer. The new code only calls `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)`. `host_allowed?` returns `record_for_host(host).present?`, and `record_for_host` returns `false` when the referer is nil/unparseable — so with no hosts configured the behavior is equivalent (denied). However, the explicit 'not set' guard also protected against a nil/blank referer edge case and made the failure mode explicit; more importantly, `Topic#expandable_first_post?` (app/models/topic.rb line 869) had its `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` condition removed, so the 'expand embed' UI is now shown whenever any `TopicEmbed` exists for the topic, even if no `EmbeddableHost` rows exist at all — meaning content can be expanded/retrieved for hosts that were never approved. The gating condition should be `EmbeddableHost.exists?` (or equivalent) rather than removed entirely.

title: expandable_first_post? no longer checks that any embeddable host is configured
body: `expandable_first_post?` was changed from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to just `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`. The first condition existed to ensure embedding was enabled (at least one allowed host configured). With it removed, any topic that has a `TopicEmbed` row (e.g. created before hosts were reconfigured, or via feed polling) will show the 'expand embed' affordance even when the site has zero `EmbeddableHost` records, exposing embedded content to visitors on disallowed origins. The check should be replaced with `EmbeddableHost.exists?` (or a cached equivalent), not deleted.

title: EmbeddingSerializer embeds only ids but the client expects hydrated host objects with category
body: `EmbeddingSerializer` declares `has_many :embeddable_hosts, serializer: EmbeddableHostSerializer, embed: :ids`, so the JSON payload contains `embeddable_hosts: [1,2,3]` plus a side-loaded `embeddable_hosts` array. The Ember admin route does `this.store.find('embedding')`, and the store's `_hydrateEmbedded` (store.js.es6) maps `embeddable_host_ids` → `embeddable_hosts` only when the payload uses the `_ids` suffix convention with `__rest_serializer: "1"`. The serializer emits `embeddable_hosts` (already plural, ids) rather than `embeddable_host_ids`, so the client-side hydration in `_hydrateEmbedded` (which matches `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/`) will NOT fire for this key, and `embedding.embeddable_hosts` in the controller will be a plain array of integers, not model objects — the `embeddable-host` component's `host.host`, `host.category`, `host.isNew` bindings will all break. Either emit `embeddable_host_ids` with side-loaded objects (matching the rest_serializer convention used elsewhere), or embed objects directly (`embed: :objects`).

title: save() sends buffered 'host' property but the server expects the 'host' attribute inside embeddable_host params
body: In `save()`, `const props = this.get('buffered').getProperties('host')` fetches the buffered value of the `host` attribute (a string like 'example.com'), then `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')` and `host.save(props)`. The REST adapter's `update`/`createRecord` wraps attrs as `data['embeddable_host'] = attrs`, so the request body becomes `embeddable_host[host]=example.com&embeddable_host[category_id]=...` — this part is actually correct. However, `getProperties('host')` returns `{host: <string>}` only if the buffered content mixin exposes it that way; if the buffer stores the whole record, `props` could be the record itself and `props.category_id = ...` would mutate the record. More concretely: after a successful save the code does `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')))` but never calls `this.rollbackBuffer()` / `this.set('buffered.host', ...)`, so the buffered (dirty) state persists and `cantSave` (which depends on `buffered.host`) keeps the old value; on the next edit the stale buffer is shown. The buffer must be committed/rolled back after a successful save.

title: edit() reads host.category.id but the serializer only provides category_id, so category is undefined and categoryId becomes undefined
body: `edit()` does `this.set('categoryId', this.get('host.category.id'))`. The `EmbeddableHostSerializer` only emits `id, host, category_id` — there is no embedded `category` object on the client model unless the store hydrates `category_id` into a `category` property. The store's `_hydrateEmbedded` does map `category_id` → `category` via `Discourse.Category.findById(id)` (store.js.es6 `_lookupSubType` special-cases 'category'), but only when the payload is marked `__rest_serializer: "1"` AND the key matches `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/` — the host serializer emits `category_id`, which matches, so hydration may occur. However, the `EmbeddingSerializer` uses `embed: :ids` for hosts, so host objects are side-loaded under an `embeddable_hosts` key; whether each side-loaded host object gets `_hydrateEmbedded` applied depends on the root payload having `__rest_serializer: "1"` (the controller passes `rest_serializer: true`, which should set it). If hydration does not run (e.g. the side-loaded array isn't processed through `_hydrate` with the root), `host.category` is undefined and `this.get('host.category.id')` returns undefined, so `categoryId` is undefined and the category chooser starts blank on edit — the admin cannot see the current category and saving would send `category_id=undefined`, which the server treats as blank and resets to uncategorized. This needs verification/fix: prefer `this.get('host.category_id')` which is always present on the model.

title: addHost pushes a new record into embedding.embeddable_hosts but the array may be a plain JS array of ids, not an Ember array of models
body: Depending on whether the store hydrates the `embeddable_hosts` relationship (see the EmbeddingSerializer finding), `this.get('embedding.embeddable_hosts')` may be a plain array of integer ids rather than an Ember.Array of `embeddable-host` models. `pushObject` is an Ember.Array method; on a plain array it throws `pushObject is not a function`, breaking the 'Add Host' button. Even when it is an Ember array, pushing a `createRecord('embeddable-host')` with no attributes creates a record with `host: undefined`; the component's `cantSave` checks `Ember.isEmpty(host)` on the buffered host string, which is correct, but the new record is immediately rendered in `editing` mode (because `host.isNew` is true) with an empty host input — acceptable — yet if the user cancels, `deleteHost` removes it from the array but the record remains in the store's identity map as a new record; this is minor. The primary risk is the type mismatch of `embeddable_hosts`.

title: _hydrateEmbedded plural branch maps ids but does not handle missing/undefined entries and mutates obj while iterating
body: The new plural branch `obj[k].map(function(id) { return self._lookupSubType(subType, type, id, root); })` assumes `obj[k]` is always an array. If a serializer emits `color_ids: null` or omits entries, `obj[k].map` throws. Additionally, `_lookupSubType` can return `undefined` (when the id isn't found in the side-loaded collection), producing an array full of `undefined` holes assigned to `obj[self.pluralize(subType)]` — downstream code doing `colors[0].get('id')` (as the new store test does) will crash. The singular branch guards with `if (hydrated)`, but the plural branch does not filter out unresolved ids. Filter out falsy results: `obj[k].map(...).filter(function(x){ return !!x; })` or similar, and guard `if (!obj[k]) { return; }`.

title: basePath type normalization only replaces the first underscore, breaking multi-word admin model types
body: `type.replace('_', '-')` (without a global flag) replaces only the FIRST underscore. The `ADMIN_MODELS` list contains `'embeddable-host'` (single word, fine), but any future admin model with two underscores (e.g. `site_customization_field` → expected `site-customization-field`) would only become `site-customization_field` and fail the `indexOf` check, silently routing an admin model's requests to the non-admin base path `/` instead of `/admin/`. Use `type.replace(/_/g, '-')` for correctness and robustness.

title: Category fabricators were moved into the wrong file: category_fabricator.rb now defines the embeddable_host fabricator and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines categories
body: The diff shows `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` was overwritten to contain ONLY the `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` block, deleting the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, and `:private_category` fabricators. Meanwhile `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` (new file) contains the category fabricators. The file names are swapped relative to their contents: every spec that does `Fabricate(:category)` relies on the category fabricators being loaded (Fabrication auto-loads all files under spec/fabricators, so loading may still work), but this is a serious maintainability/correctness defect — the file named `category_fabricator.rb` no longer defines a `:category` fabricator, and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` does not define `:embeddable_host`. Any tooling, generator, or developer that expects fabricators to live in the file matching their name (and any `require` of a specific fabricator file) breaks. The contents of the two files must be swapped back so each file defines the fabricator matching its name.

title: update action is a no-op that just re-renders, giving a false sense that embedding settings can be saved
body: `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` simply re-renders the embedding serializer without reading or persisting any params. The route `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"` and the admin controller's `saveChanges` action (`this.get('embedding').update({})`) both target it. Since hosts are created/updated/deleted through `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`, the embedding `update` endpoint is misleading dead code: a client PUTing embedding-level settings (if any are ever added) would silently succeed without persisting anything. Either implement it to accept and persist embedding-level attributes, or remove the route/action to avoid a misleading API surface.

title: Authorization relies on redundant before_filter in addition to route constraint; ensure_staff allows moderators, route allows only admins — verify intended privilege level
body: The routes declare `resources :embeddable_hosts, constraints: AdminConstraint.new` (admin-only), but the controller adds `before_filter :ensure_logged_in, :ensure_staff` (staff = admins + moderators). The effective access is the intersection (admin-only via route), so moderators get 404 rather than 403. This is not a vulnerability per se, but the controller's `ensure_staff` is misleading dead weight and inconsistent with sibling admin controllers that rely on the route constraint alone (e.g. `Admin::EmbeddingController` uses `ensure_staff` too but its routes also use `AdminConstraint`). More importantly, the `create`/`update`/`destroy` actions mutate which external sites can embed and iframe forum content (a security-sensitive setting affecting X-Frame-Options / referer allowlisting); confirm admin-only is intended and remove the redundant/misleading `ensure_staff` filter, or document why moderators are filtered at the controller level but blocked at the route level.

title: Serializer defines trivial attribute methods that just delegate to the object; also missing category object for the client
body: The explicit `def id; object.id; end` etc. methods are redundant — `attributes :id, :host, :category_id` already generates them. More importantly, the admin UI (`embeddable-host.hbs`) renders `{{category-badge host.category}}`, which requires a `category` object on the client model, but the serializer only emits `category_id`. The client store can hydrate `category_id` → `category` via `Discourse.Category.findById` only when the payload is processed as a rest_serializer payload with the root containing categories; the `EmbeddingSerializer` side-loads hosts but does not include a `categories` array, so `Discourse.Category.findById` may return undefined if categories aren't already loaded in the client. The serializer should either embed the category (`has_one :category` / `embed: :objects`) or the embedding payload should side-load categories, otherwise the category badge column renders blank.

title: Controller specs only assert inheritance; no tests for create/update/destroy behavior, authorization, or validation errors
body: Both new controller specs (`Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` and `Admin::EmbeddingController`) contain a single test asserting the class is a subclass of `Admin::AdminController`. There are no tests covering: successful host creation/update/destroy, rejection of non-staff users, handling of missing/invalid host params (which currently 500 due to the nil-host bug in the model), the nil-record 404 path in update/destroy, or the embedding show/update serialization shape. Given these endpoints mutate security-sensitive embed allowlisting, the test coverage is inadequate — the existing bugs (nil host crash, missing record crash) would not be caught.

title: No test for blank/nil host (which crashes before_validation) and no test for case-insensitive referer matching
body: The spec covers trimming http/https/paths and `host_allowed?` for exact hosts, but does not test: (1) `EmbeddableHost.new(host: nil).valid?` — which currently raises `NoMethodError` on `nil.sub!` in `before_validation` (the bug noted in the model finding); (2) case-insensitive matching (`host_allowed?('http://EVILTROUT.COM')` vs stored `eviltrout.com`) — which the current `record_for_host` implementation gets wrong because it doesn't downcase `uri.host`; (3) uniqueness — two hosts differing only by case (`Example.com` vs `example.com`) can both be saved because there is no uniqueness validation, and `lower(host) = ?` matching means they are duplicates functionally. Add a uniqueness validation (scoped with `lower`) and tests for these cases.

title: No uniqueness validation on host — duplicate/case-variant hosts can be created
body: `EmbeddableHost` validates only the format of `host`. There is no `validates_uniqueness_of :host` (case-insensitive). Because `record_for_host` matches with `lower(host) = ?`, storing both `Example.com` and `example.com` creates functionally duplicate rows that both match the same referers; the admin UI will show two rows for the same site, and deleting one still leaves embedding enabled. Add `validates_uniqueness_of :host, case_sensitive: false` (and ideally a unique index in the migration) to prevent duplicate allowlist entries.

title: Migration lacks a unique index on host and does not downcase migrated values
body: The migration creates `embeddable_hosts` with `host` and `category_id` but no unique index. Since `record_for_host` matches case-insensitively (`lower(host) = ?`), duplicate rows (including case variants) will silently coexist and all match — there is no DB-level guard. Also, the migrated values from the old `embeddable_hosts` site setting are inserted verbatim (`'#{h}'`) without stripping `http://` prefixes or paths (the model's `before_validation` normalization is bypassed because raw SQL INSERT is used), so a legacy value like `http://example.com/path` becomes a stored host of `http://example.com/path`, which will never match a referer (referer matching compares only `uri.host`). The migration should normalize each host (strip scheme/path, downcase) before insert and add a unique index on `lower(host)`.

title: Blank category_id silently falls back to uncategorized, masking client errors
body: `host.category_id = SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id if host.category_id.blank?` silently converts a missing/invalid category selection into the uncategorized category. If the admin UI sends `category_id` as an empty string (e.g. the category chooser not initialized — see the `edit()` finding where `categoryId` can be undefined), the host is saved pointing at uncategorized without any error, so embedded posts land in the wrong category with no feedback. This should either be a validation error when `category_id` is blank on create, or at minimum the fallback should only apply when the param is absent, not when it's an invalid/nonexistent id. Also, `uncategorized_category_id` is typically a negative sentinel (-1) that may not correspond to a real Category row, so `belongs_to :category` will be nil and the badge renders blank.

title: Table is only rendered when embeddable_hosts is non-empty, so a new host cannot be added when the list is empty
body: `{{#if embedding.embeddable_hosts}}` wraps the entire `<table>` including the `{{embeddable-host}}` rows. When there are zero hosts, the table (and its header row) is not rendered at all — only the 'Add Host' button shows. When the admin clicks 'Add Host', `addHost` pushes a new record into `embedding.embeddable_hosts`, which makes the `{{#if}}` become true and the table appears — so functionally it works. However, the `{{#each}}` over a possibly plain array (see controller finding) and the conditional table mean the header only appears after the first add; more importantly, if `embeddable_hosts` is a plain array of ids (not models), `{{#if}}` is truthy for `[1,2]` but `{{embeddable-host host=host}}` receives an integer, breaking rendering. The template should render the table header unconditionally and iterate safely.

title: @on('didInsertElement') combined with @observes('editing') refocuses the input on every edit toggle and on insert, stealing focus unexpectedly
body: The `_focusOnInput` method is decorated with both `@on('didInsertElement')` and `@observes('editing')`. The observer fires whenever `editing` changes (becoming true when entering edit mode, and again when leaving), and `didInsertElement` fires on render. When `editing` becomes false after save/cancel, the observer still runs and schedules `this.$('.host-name').focus()` — but by then the input is gone (the `{{#if editing}}` block rendered the read-only view), so `this.$('.host-name')` is empty and focus is lost (or, in a race, focus may be applied to a removed element). This causes the page focus to jump to the body after saving. The `@observes('editing')` should be guarded to only focus when entering edit mode (`if (this.get('editing'))`), or the observer should be removed in favor of focusing only on `didInsertElement` when `isNew`.

title: Locale string 'Allowed Hosts' is used as a table column header for a single host value, and 'Post to Category' is ambiguous
body: The new `admin.embedding` locale block defines `host: "Allowed Hosts"` (plural) which is used in `embedding.hbs` as the column header for an individual host value (`{{i18n "admin.embedding.host"}}` above a column of single hostnames). A column listing individual hosts should be labeled "Host" or "Allowed Host", not "Allowed Hosts". Similarly `category: "Post to Category"` describes the category that embedded topics are posted into — it is used as a column header for the category badge, so "Category" would be clearer. These are user-facing admin strings; the plural/ambiguous wording will confuse admins managing the allowlist.

title: X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL is set even when the referer check fails (header set before the raise propagates in some paths)
body: In `ensure_embeddable`, `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"` is set AFTER the `raise Discourse::InvalidAccess` guard inside the `if` block, but the `rescue URI::InvalidURIError` re-raises a new `Discourse::InvalidAccess`. When the referer is invalid, `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` returns false and `raise` executes before the header line — so the header is not set on denial (good). However, the header is set unconditionally for ANY request that passes the referer check, including the `count` action which returns JSON counts for arbitrary embed_urls — this is fine. The actual concern: `ALLOWALL` is a non-standard value (browsers ignore invalid X-Frame-Options values, falling back to default framing protections, but some older/other implementations may treat it permissively). More importantly, setting `ALLOWALL` (rather than removing the header or using CSP frame-ancestors) means any site can frame the content IF the referer check passes — but the referer check is the only gate, and browsers can suppress referers (privacy settings, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`), in which case `request.referer` is nil, `host_allowed?(nil)` returns false, and access is denied — which is safe but breaks legitimate embeds for users with strict referrer policies. This is a known tradeoff; the finding is that the code sets a non-standard header value `ALLOWALL` which is not a valid X-Frame-Options directive (valid values are `DENY` and `SAMEORIGIN`); modern browsers ignore it, so the protection relies entirely on the referer check, and the header provides no real defense. Consider using CSP `frame-ancestors` with the allowlisted hosts instead.

title: Embedded topic category now comes from EmbeddableHost, but when no host matches, category is nil and PostCreator may create an uncategorized topic or fail
body: `TopicEmbed.import` now does `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` and passes `category: eh.try(:category_id)` to `PostCreator`. When the URL's host is not in the allowlist (which can happen because `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` gates retrieval, but `TopicEmbed.import` is also called directly from feed polling `Jobs::PollFeed` and potentially other paths that may not check the allowlist first), `eh` is nil/false and `category` is nil. `PostCreator` with a nil category will create a topic in the uncategorized category (or fail validation if `allow_uncategorized_topics` is false and the user is not staff). Previously the category came from the global `SiteSetting.embed_category` which always had a value. The behavior change means feed-polled or directly-imported embeds without a matching host silently land in uncategorized (or error). The import path should either skip import when no host matches (return nil) or fall back to a configured default category, and this should be tested.

title: invalid_host? now depends on EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? which returns false for nil referer, but the retriever is initialized with an embed_url, not a referer — semantics changed
body: `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` calls `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(@embed_url)`. `host_allowed?` → `record_for_host(host)` does `URI(host)` and extracts `uri.host`. The `@embed_url` is the URL of the external page being embedded (e.g. `http://eviltrout.com/2013/02/10/why-discourse-uses-emberjs.html`), so `uri.host` is `eviltrout.com` — this is correct and matches the old `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` behavior. However, `record_for_host` returns `false` (not nil) when URI parsing fails, and `host_allowed?` returns `record_for_host(host).present?` → `false.present?` → `false`, so `invalid_host?` returns `!false` = `true` — correct. The semantics are preserved. The only concern is that `record_for_host` returns `false` or a record, and `.present?` on `false` is `false` — fine. No bug here; this finding is withdrawn as it is a restatement. (Not reporting.)

title: SQL injection in migration via interpolated host value
body: The migration builds an INSERT statement with string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. The value `h` comes directly from the `embeddable_hosts` site setting (line 18-24), which is admin-controlled free text. A host value containing a single quote (e.g. `evil.com'); DROP TABLE users;--`) breaks out of the string literal and executes arbitrary SQL during `rake db:migrate`. This must use parameterized queries, e.g. `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (?, ?, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)", [h, category_id]` (or `sanitize_sql_array`).

title: update/destroy actions crash with NoMethodError when host id does not exist
body: `update` does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then passes the result to `save_host(host)`, which immediately calls `host.host = ...`. If no EmbeddableHost matches the id, `host` is nil and the request raises NoMethodError (500 error) instead of returning a 404. Same problem in `destroy` at line 15-16: `host.destroy` on nil raises. Both actions should return `render json: not_found_json` (or raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound) when the record is missing.

title: before_validation callback crashes on nil host
body: The `before_validation` block calls `self.host.sub!(...)` unconditionally. If `host` is nil (e.g. a create/update request that omits the `host` param, which the controller at app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:23 allows since it just assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]`), `nil.sub!` raises NoMethodError and the request 500s instead of returning a validation error. The callback should guard with `self.host.sub!(...) if self.host.present?` (or use `self.host = host.to_s.sub(...)`).

title: Host validation regex allows paths but before_validation strips them, and does not enforce uniqueness
body: The format regex `/\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i` permits an optional path (`(\/.*)?`), but the `before_validation` callback strips everything after the first `/` (line 7), so two different submitted hosts like `example.com/foo` and `example.com/bar` both normalize to `example.com`. There is no `validates_uniqueness_of :host`, so the admin UI can create duplicate rows for the same host (the old SiteSetting-based implementation was a set of lines, so duplicates were impossible). Duplicate rows make `record_for_host` return an arbitrary one and let two categories compete for the same host. Add `validates_uniqueness_of :host, case_sensitive: false` (the lookup at line 17 already uses `lower(host) = ?`).

title: Removal of the 'embeddable hosts not set' check changes behavior when no hosts are configured
body: The old code raised `Discourse::InvalidAccess.new('embeddable hosts not set')` when `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` was blank, and only then checked the referer. The new code only calls `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)`, which returns false when the table is empty, so the behavior is equivalent in outcome (request rejected) — but note that `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` performs a DB query on every embed request with no caching, and more importantly the error message/behavior for a completely unconfigured install is now the generic 'invalid referer host'. More significantly: `record_for_host` uses `URI(host) rescue nil` — if `request.referer` is nil (no Referer header), `URI(nil)` raises, is rescued to nil, and `host_allowed?` returns false, which is correct. However, if the referer is a malformed URI the rescue also returns false — fine. The real issue is that this is a per-request unindexed `lower(host) = ?` query; there is no index on `embeddable_hosts.host` in the migration (line 3-7 of db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb creates the table with no indexes), so every embed comment request does a sequential scan. Add an index (ideally a unique index on `lower(host)` via `add_index :embeddable_hosts, 'lower(host)', unique: true`).

title: EmbeddingSerializer embeds host ids but the client store expects embedded objects for category hydration
body: The serializer declares `has_many :embeddable_hosts, serializer: EmbeddableHostSerializer, embed: :ids`, producing JSON like `{ embedding: { id: 'default', embeddable_host_ids: [1,2] } }`. The Ember store's `_hydrateEmbedded` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:189-212) handles `*_ids` keys by looking up each id via `_lookupSubType` in the root payload's `embeddable_hosts` collection — but with `embed: :ids` the root payload contains no `embeddable_hosts` array of objects, only the id list, so `_lookupSubType` finds nothing and `host.category` / the host objects themselves are never hydrated. The admin embedding template (`embedding.hbs`) iterates `embedding.embeddable_hosts` and renders `{{host.host}}` and `{{category-badge host.category}}`, which will be empty/broken. Either the serializer must embed objects (`embed: :objects` with the hosts array in the root payload) or the controller must render the hosts collection alongside. As written the admin page cannot display existing hosts.

title: save() sends only the 'host' property, dropping category_id from the buffered changes and always sending category_id separately
body: `const props = this.get('buffered').getProperties('host');` fetches only the `host` attribute from the buffer, then `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')` is set on the props object. That part is OK, but the `categoryId` is initialized only in the `edit()` action (line 26: `this.set('categoryId', this.get('host.category.id'))`). For a newly created host (`addHost` in admin-embedding.js.es6 creates a record with no attributes), `categoryId` stays null, so `props.category_id` is null and the server falls back to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` (embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:25). Also, after a successful save the component sets `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')))` — if `categoryId` is null, `findById(null)` returns undefined and the badge renders blank. The category chooser should default to a sensible value and the save should be blocked (cantSave) when no category is selected, since category_id is `null: false` in the migration.

title: cantSave computed property only checks the host string, not category selection
body: `cantSave` returns `isSaving || Ember.isEmpty(host)` where `host` is `buffered.host` — it validates only the hostname. A user can save a host with no category selected (categoryId null), which the server silently coerces to the uncategorized category (embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:25), an action the admin may not have intended. The save button should also be disabled when `categoryId` is empty.

title: _hydrateEmbedded plural branch crashes when an *_ids key has a null/undefined value
body: The new plural branch does `obj[k].map(...)` without checking that `obj[k]` is an array. The regex `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/` matches any key ending in `_id` or `_ids`, including scalar attributes that happen to end in `_id` (e.g. a model with a `parent_id` that is null, or any `*_ids` field sent as null). If `obj[k]` is null or undefined, `.map` raises TypeError and the whole hydration fails. The singular branch guards with `if (hydrated)`; the plural branch needs `if (obj[k]) { ... }` or `Ember.makeArray(obj[k]).map(...)`. This is a regression risk for any existing serializer that emits a nullable `*_ids` field.

title: basePath type normalization only replaces the first underscore
body: `type.replace('_', '-')` uses a string argument, which in JavaScript replaces only the first occurrence. A model type like `embeddable_host` works (one underscore), but any future admin model with two underscores (e.g. `site_customization_setting`) would only get its first underscore replaced and would not match the ADMIN_MODELS list, silently routing admin requests to the non-admin base path. Use `type.replace(/_/g, '-')` for correctness.

title: Category fabricators were deleted from category_fabricator.rb and moved into embeddable_host_fabricator.rb, breaking the fabricator file naming convention
body: The diff shows all four category fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`) were removed from `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` (leaving it containing only the `:embeddable_host` fabricator) and re-added verbatim into `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. Two problems: (1) `category_fabricator.rb` now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` — a file named after categories contains an unrelated fabricator, and the embeddable host fabricator is defined in two places conceptually (the file `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains only category fabricators, so its name is wrong too). (2) More concretely, Fabrication loads fabricator files by convention; having the `:embeddable_host` fabricator in `category_fabricator.rb` and the category fabricators in `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` is confusing and error-prone — if any tooling or future refactor deletes 'unused' fabricator files by name, all category fabricators (used by hundreds of specs, e.g. spec/models/topic_spec.rb) would vanish. The `:embeddable_host` fabricator belongs in `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` and the category fabricators belong in `category_fabricator.rb`.

title: Authorization relies on redundant before_filter instead of AdminConstraint used by sibling admin controllers
body: The controller declares `before_filter :ensure_logged_in, :ensure_staff` while the routes already wrap `resources :embeddable_hosts, constraints: AdminConstraint.new` (config/routes.rb:153). `ensure_staff` allows moderators, whereas `AdminConstraint` restricts to admins — so a moderator can reach these controller actions directly (the route constraint only applies to route recognition; if the controller is reachable the before_filter is the only guard, and `ensure_staff` passes for moderators). Every other admin resource controller in this codebase relies on AdminConstraint at the route level and does not add `ensure_staff`. Either drop the before_filter (route constraint is sufficient and stricter) or change it to `ensure_admin` for defense in depth. As written, moderators can create/update/destroy embeddable hosts, which is an admin-only settings change.

title: TopicEmbed.import silently falls back to no category when the embed URL's host is not registered
body: `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` returns `false` (not nil) when the host is not found or the URI is invalid (app/models/embeddable_host.rb:11-12). The code then does `category: eh.try(:category_id)` — `false.try(:category_id)` returns nil, so PostCreator receives `category: nil`. Previously the category came from `SiteSetting.embed_category`, which had a configured default. Now, any import whose URL host has no EmbeddableHost row (e.g. a feed item from a newly added feed URL, or a host row deleted by an admin) creates a topic with no category, which lands in uncategorized (or fails validation if `allow_uncategorized_topics` is false and the user is not staff). This is a silent behavior change for the RSS/feed polling path (Jobs::PollFeed → TopicEmbed.import). The import should either skip/flag such URLs or fall back to a configured default category.

title: update action is a no-op that just re-renders show
body: `update` simply re-renders the embedding serializer without reading or applying any params. The route `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"` (config/routes.rb:139) and the client controller's `saveChanges` action (`this.get('embedding').update({})` in admin-embedding.js.es6:6) imply that settings can be saved through this endpoint, but nothing is persisted — the OpenStruct built in `fetch_embedding` is rebuilt from the DB on every request and no attributes are ever assigned. Either implement actual update semantics (e.g. accept and persist embedding-level settings) or remove the PUT route and the `saveChanges` action so the UI does not imply a save that silently does nothing.

title: Controller specs only assert inheritance; no coverage of create/update/destroy, authorization, or validation
body: Both new controller specs (this file and spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb) contain a single test asserting the controller is a subclass of Admin::AdminController. There are no tests that: a non-admin/non-staff user is rejected; an admin can create a host with a valid host+category; invalid hosts are rejected with a 422; updating a nonexistent id returns an error rather than 500 (see the nil-host bug in the controller); destroying a host works. Given that the controller has real logic (save_host, nil-record handling, category fallback), the specs should exercise the HTTP endpoints with `sign_in(Fabricate(:admin))` etc.

title: Model spec does not test nil host, duplicate hosts, or invalid formats
body: The spec covers http/https/path trimming and host_allowed? lookups, but does not test: (1) `EmbeddableHost.new(host: nil)` — which currently crashes in before_validation (nil.sub!), so a regression there would not be caught; (2) duplicate hosts — there is no uniqueness validation and no test pinning down the desired behavior; (3) invalid formats (e.g. `host` with spaces, `http://`, uppercase, port-only) to confirm the regex rejects them. Adding these would lock in the intended contract.

title: Template renders nothing (not even the Add Host button) when there are no hosts, due to {{#if}} wrapping only the table
body: The `{{#if embedding.embeddable_hosts}}` block wraps only the table; the `{{d-button ... action="addHost"}}` at line 14 is outside it, so the button does render. However, when the serializer uses `embed: :ids` (see the EmbeddingSerializer finding), `embedding.embeddable_hosts` will be an empty/undefined array on first load, so the table is hidden — which is correct — but combined with the hydration bug the page will appear permanently empty with no way to tell the admin why. More importantly, there is no empty-state message; a fresh install shows only an 'Add Host' button with no explanation. Minor UX issue, but the empty table header (Host / Post to Category) is also hidden, so the user gets no column context. Consider an explicit empty-state row.

title: expandable_first_post? no longer checks that any embeddable host exists, changing behavior for sites with no hosts configured
body: The method changed from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`. The old check ensured the expand-embed UI was only offered when the site actually had embed hosts configured. The new version returns true for any topic that has a TopicEmbed row, regardless of whether any EmbeddableHost exists. The spec at spec/models/topic_spec.rb:1403 ('is false if embeddable_host is blank') now passes only because no host is fabricated in that example — but the method itself no longer consults the hosts table at all, so the test name is misleading and the guard is gone. If the intent was to drop the setting check because hosts are now per-embed, the method should instead verify the topic's embed URL host is registered (e.g. via `TopicEmbed` + `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`), otherwise the 'expand embed' affordance can appear on sites that have disabled embedding entirely (all hosts deleted).

title: embeddable_hosts resource routes are not scoped under /customize, producing a top-level /admin/embeddable_hosts REST API
body: `resources :embeddable_hosts, constraints: AdminConstraint.new` is declared at the admin namespace root (line 153), so it generates `/admin/embeddable_hosts` (index/create) and `/admin/embeddable_hosts/:id` (show/update/destroy). The Ember adapter for `embeddable-host` (app/assets/javascripts/admin/adapters/embedding.js.es6 is for the embedding model; the host model uses the default rest adapter with ADMIN_MODELS prefix `/admin/`) will call `/admin/embeddable_hosts` — consistent. But this exposes a full REST resource (including index and show, which the controller does not define — those will 404/raise AbstractController::ActionNotFound) at a top-level admin path, unlike sibling resources (site_texts, user_fields, emojis) which are scoped under `/customize`. The controller only implements create/update/destroy; index/show are missing. Either scope the resource (`scope "/customize" do resources :embeddable_hosts ... end`) to match siblings, or restrict with `only: [:create, :update, :destroy]`.

title: Downsize loop uses file size in bytes compared against kilobytes setting, causing incorrect comparison
body: The condition `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` compares the tempfile size (in bytes) against `max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` (which converts KB to bytes). However, `tempfile.size` returns bytes, and `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` also returns bytes (e.g., 1024 * KB value). This comparison is actually correct for bytes vs bytes. BUT the real bug is on line 67: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` passes "80%" as the dimensions parameter. Looking at `downsize_instructions`, this becomes `-resize 80%\>` which is a percentage resize, not a size-based downsize. The loop condition checks if file size exceeds the limit, but the downsize operation only reduces dimensions by 20% each iteration (80% of current size). For a very large image (e.g., 50MB), 5 iterations of 80% reduction only gets to ~32% of original dimensions, which may still result in a file larger than the limit. More critically, if the image is already small in dimensions but large in file size (e.g., uncompressed PNG), resizing won't help reduce file size proportionally. The loop may exit with `attempt == 0` while the file is still over the size limit, and the upload proceeds anyway with an oversized file.

title: Downsize writes to same path as input, risking data corruption if ImageMagick fails
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` passes the same path for both `from` and `to` parameters. The `downsize_instructions` generates a command like `convert /tmp/file.png[0] -gravity center -background transparent -resize 80%\> /tmp/file.png`. ImageMagick's `convert` command reads the input file completely before writing output, so this usually works, but if the process is interrupted, crashes, or runs out of disk space during the write, the original file is corrupted/truncated. The tempfile would then contain a partial or corrupt image, and `Upload.create_for` on line 72 would create an upload record for a corrupted file. This is a data integrity risk. The code should write to a separate temporary file and then replace the original only on success.

title: Downsize loop doesn't verify success of downsize operation before continuing
body: The while loop on lines 66-69 calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` but ignores the return value. `downsize` (via `convert_with`) returns `false` if the ImageMagick command fails or if `ImageOptim` optimization fails. If downsize fails (e.g., corrupt image, missing ImageMagick, unsupported format), the loop continues decrementing `attempt` and retrying 5 times on the same unchanged file, wasting CPU and time, then proceeds to create an upload with the original oversized file. The code should check the return value and break or handle the error appropriately.

title: API URL download limit increased from max_image_size_kb to 10MB, bypassing size restrictions
body: The change from `FileHelper.download(url, SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, ...)` to `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` increases the maximum download size for API-provided URLs from the configured `max_image_size_kb` (which could be e.g., 1MB or 2MB) to a hardcoded 10MB. This allows API clients to make the server download much larger files than the site's configured image size limit. While the subsequent downsize loop attempts to reduce the size, this still allows: (1) temporary disk usage of up to 10MB per request, (2) network bandwidth consumption downloading 10MB files, (3) potential DoS if many API requests are made with URLs pointing to large files. The original limit was tied to the site setting; the new hardcoded 10MB removes that protection. The download limit should remain tied to a configurable maximum, or at least be documented as a deliberate security tradeoff.

title: content_type is nil for API URL uploads, potentially causing incorrect MIME type detection
body: When uploading via API URL (line 54-56), `content_type` is never set (it's only set in the `else` branch on line 60). The downsize block on lines 64-70 runs before `Upload.create_for` on line 72, which receives `content_type: content_type` (nil for URL uploads). While this may have been the case before this PR, the new downsize logic specifically processes images, and having `content_type` nil means the upload record may not have the correct content type set. This could affect how the file is served later (Content-Type header) and whether it's treated as an image for thumbnail generation. The `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` check on line 64 uses the filename extension, but the actual content_type stored in the upload may be nil or incorrectly detected.

title: Client-side file size validation hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring site settings for max image/attachment size
body: The change from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB) removes the client-side validation against the actual configured site settings. If an admin sets `max_image_size_kb` to 1MB (1024 KB), the client will still allow uploads up to 10MB before the server rejects them or attempts to downsize them. This creates a poor user experience: users can select and upload files up to 10MB that will then be processed server-side (potentially downsized or rejected), wasting bandwidth and time. The client-side check should use the actual site setting value to provide immediate feedback. The same issue exists on line 246 for the 413 error handler.

title: Error message for 413 uses hardcoded 10MB instead of actual configured limit
body: When the server returns a 413 (Payload Too Large) error, the client displays `I18n.t('post.errors.file_too_large', { max_size_kb: maxSizeKB })` where `maxSizeKB` is hardcoded to `10 * 1024`. If the site has configured a smaller limit (e.g., `max_image_size_kb = 2048` for 2MB), the error message will incorrectly tell the user the limit is 10MB, confusing users about why their 3MB file was rejected. The message should reflect the actual configured limit from `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` or `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_attachment_size_kb` depending on the upload type.

title: Animation detection uses case-sensitive .GIF regex, missing .gif files
body: The line `method_name += "_animated" if !!opts[:allow_animation] && from =~ /\.GIF$/i` uses `/\.GIF$/i` which has the `i` flag for case-insensitive matching, so this actually works correctly for `.gif`, `.GIF`, `.Gif`, etc. However, this is inconsistent with the rest of the codebase which typically uses `/\.gif$/i` (lowercase). More importantly, this regex only matches files ending in `.GIF` (case-insensitive), but animated images can also be `.webp` or other formats. The `allow_animation` option is specifically for animated GIFs, so this may be intentional, but the uppercase `GIF` in the pattern is unusual and could be a typo that happens to work due to the `i` flag.

title: Downsize loop runs synchronously in web request, blocking for potentially long ImageMagick operations
body: The downsize loop (lines 64-70) runs synchronously within the `create_upload` method, which is called either directly (synchronous API) or via `Scheduler::Defer.later` (line 19). For non-API uploads, this runs in a background job, which is acceptable. However, for synchronous API requests (line 15-17), this blocks the web worker for the duration of up to 5 ImageMagick `convert` operations plus `ImageOptim` optimization. Each operation can take several seconds for large images, potentially causing request timeouts and tying up web workers. Large image processing should be moved to a background job even for API requests, or the synchronous API path should have a separate, shorter timeout. The current implementation risks worker exhaustion under load.

title: Downsize uses fixed 80% reduction rather than calculating required reduction to meet size target
body: The downsize loop uses a fixed "80%" dimension reduction each iteration. This is inefficient: for a 50MB image with a 2MB limit, reducing dimensions by 20% each time reduces file size roughly by 36% (area scales with square of linear dimensions), so 5 iterations get to ~32% of original dimensions (~5MB file), still over the limit. The loop exits after 5 attempts regardless. A more efficient approach would calculate the target dimensions based on the ratio of current size to target size, or use ImageMagick's `-define jpeg:extent` or similar to target a specific file size directly. The current approach wastes CPU on multiple iterations that may not achieve the goal.

title: Downsize loop uses file size as proxy for image dimensions, causing infinite/ineffective resizing for already-small large files
body: The condition `while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` downsizes based on file size, but `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` reduces dimensions by 80%, not file size proportionally. A high-resolution but already-compressed image (e.g., a 9MB JPEG that is 2000x2000) will be resized to 1600x1600, which may still be > max_image_size_kb in bytes, causing repeated downsizing up to 5 attempts (down to ~33% of original dimensions) even though the image dimensions are already reasonable.
