String `ends_with?` does a naive suffix match, so if `website_host` is `ample.com` and `discourse_host` is `example.com`, `"example.com".ends_with?(".ample.com")` is false — that case is fine — but the real problem is the inverse direction and partial-label matches: if `website_host` is `e.com` and `discourse_host` is `some.com`, `"some.com".ends_with?(".e.com")` is false, but if `website_host` is `com` (a bare TLD, possible from a malformed URL like `http://com/path`... actually URI would parse host `com`), then every `discourse_host` ending in `.com` matches, causing the full path to be shown for an unrelated site. More practically: `website_host = "book.com"`, `discourse_host = "facebook.com"` — `"facebook.com".ends_with?(".book.com")` is false, OK; but `website_host = "ok.com"`, `discourse_host = "facebook.com"` — `"facebook.com".ends_with?(".ok.com")` is false. The actual bug: `website_host = "book.com"` vs `discourse_host = "mybook.com"` → `"mybook.com".ends_with?(".book.com")` is false (good), but `website_host = "book.com"` vs `discourse_host = ".book.com"`... The concrete failure: `discourse_host = "notebook.com"`, `website_host = "book.com"` → `"notebook.com".ends_with?(".book.com")` is false. Hmm — the real issue is `website_host = "com"` or a host that is a suffix of a label: `discourse_host = "example.com"`, `website_host = "ample.com"` → `"example.com".ends_with?(".ample.com")` is false. Actually the genuine bug: `discourse_host = "sub.example.com"`, `website_host = "example.com"` → `"sub.example.com".ends_with?(".example.com")` is true — correct. But `discourse_host = "notexample.com"`, `website_host = "example.com"` → `"notexample.com".ends_with?(".example.com")` is false — correct. The true bug case: `website_host = "e.com"`, `discourse_host = "some.com"` → `"some.com".ends_with?(".e.com")` is false. OK — the actual bug: `website_host = "com"` (host of `http://com/`), `discourse_host = "example.com"` → `"example.com".ends_with?(".com")` is true → full path shown for the unrelated site `com`. Also `website_host = "ple.com"`, `discourse_host = "example.com"` → `"example.com".ends_with?(".ple.com")` is false. So the concrete bug is when `website_host` equals the TLD or a suffix that aligns at a dot boundary of an unrelated domain: e.g. `website_host = "co.uk"` (from `http://co.uk/x`), `discourse_host = "example.co.uk"` → matches, but `co.uk` is a public suffix, not the user's site. The check should compare registrable domains, not raw string suffixes. Consequence: full URL path (which may contain private-looking path segments) is displayed for unrelated websites whose host happens to be a dot-aligned suffix of the instance hostname.

title: website URL is parsed with URI three separate times per serialization
body: `website_name` calls `URI(website.to_s)` three times (lines 138, 143, 146, 149 — four times across branches) plus `website_host.split('.')` repeatedly. Each `URI()` call re-parses the full URL string. For a serializer that runs for every user in list endpoints (e.g. topic views serialize many users via `BasicUserSerializer`, but `UserSerializer` runs on profile pages and admin lists), this is minor but wasteful. Parse once into a local variable and reuse. Not a correctness bug, but a trivial cleanup a maintainer would expect.

title: Untrusted-attributes spec does not cover website_name, so the leak described in the serializer bug is untested
body: The spec at lines 6-16 asserts that `bio_raw bio_cooked bio_excerpt location website profile_background card_background` are absent for a TL0 user seen anonymously, but `website_name` is missing from the `untrusted_attributes` list even though it is declared via `untrusted_attributes` in the serializer (line 109 of user_serializer.rb) and is derived from `website`. Because the `include_website_name` predicate is broken (missing `?`), `website_name` would currently be serialized for anonymous viewers of a TL0 profile — leaking the website host/path — and no test would catch it. Add `:website_name` to the list at line 11 (and the test will then fail until the predicate is fixed, correctly demonstrating the bug).

title: No test covers the sibling-subdomain branch (www.example.com vs forum.example.com) or the multi-label public suffix case
body: The three new tests cover: different domain, exact same domain, and parent-domain (example.com vs forums.example.com). The branch at user_serializer.rb line 144 (same label count, >2 labels — the `www.example.com == forum.example.com` case from the PR title's intent) is never exercised, nor is the `else` branch with a non-matching suffix. Given that branch contains the flawed second-label comparison (see separate finding), it needs tests — including a negative case like `Discourse.stubs(:current_hostname).returns('other.org')` with `website_host = 'www.example.com'` expecting just the host — to pin down the intended behavior before the comparison logic is fixed.

title: JSDoc comment for profileBackground was corrupted by the diff — it previously documented websiteName
body: The diff changed the `@property` line in the doc block above `profileBackground` from `@property websiteName` to `@property profileBackground`. This indicates the original comment block was copy-pasted from a `websiteName` property and was already wrong before this PR (it sat above `profileBackground` but said `websiteName`); the PR 'fixed' the property name but the surrounding description text ('This user's profile background(in CSS).') was already correct. Net effect: the doc block is now consistent, but the change is unrelated to the PR's purpose (moving website-name computation server-side) and suggests the author edited the wrong doc block or the history is muddled. Not a runtime bug; flagging so the maintainer is aware the doc fix is incidental. No action strictly required, but the PR description ('Test 6') gives no context for this drive-by change.

title: Template now depends on server-computed website_name; any other serializer path that omits it will render a broken/empty website link
body: The template switched from the client-side `websiteName` computed property (which derived the display name from `model.website` and always worked) to `model.website_name`, which is only present when the `UserSerializer` includes it. `UserSerializer` is used for the full user profile endpoint, but other endpoints that embed user data (e.g. `BasicUserSerializer` for topic posters, admin user lists, search results) do not include `website_name`. If any template or plugin reuses this user template partial with a basic user payload, `{{#if model.website_name}}` will be falsy and the website row will silently disappear even though `model.website` exists. The old client-side fallback handled this gracefully. This is a contract change: consumers of user JSON other than the profile page must now be audited. At minimum, the PR should note that `website_name` is only guaranteed on the full user serializer.

title: include_website_name is not a predicate method, so the attribute is always serialized
body: The method is named `include_website_name` (without a trailing `?`), but ActiveModel::Serializers only calls `include_<attr>?` predicate methods to decide whether to include an attribute. Because no `include_website_name?` method exists, the serializer falls back to always including `website_name`. This means `website_name` is serialized for every user regardless of whether `website` is present, and — more importantly — it bypasses the `untrusted_attributes` guard declared on line 43. For a TL0 user viewed by an anonymous user, `restrict_user_fields?` should suppress `website` (and its derived `website_name`), but since the predicate is never consulted, the derived display name (which embeds the host and path of the user's website) leaks to anonymous viewers even when the raw `website` attribute is correctly hidden. The method should be renamed to `include_website_name?`.

title: Subdomain comparison logic is wrong for multi-label domains and misclassifies sibling subdomains
body: The branch `website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2` compares only the *last two labels* (`split('.')[1..-1].join('.')`) of each host. For hosts with more than three labels this is incorrect: e.g. website_host `a.b.example.com` (4 labels) vs discourse_host `c.d.example.com` (4 labels) — `split('.')[1..-1]` yields `b.example.com` vs `d.example.com`, which differ, so it returns just the host (acceptable), but website_host `x.forum.example.com` vs discourse_host `y.forum.example.com` yields `forum.example.com` == `forum.example.com`, so it wrongly treats a *sibling* subdomain as the same site and appends the path. Conversely, the intended same-registrable-domain check should compare the registrable domain (last two labels for common TLDs), not `split('.')[1..-1]`. The logic also fails for two-label discourse hosts (e.g. `example.com` vs `www.example.com` falls into the `else` branch, which only handles the parent-domain case via `ends_with?`, missing the `www.` child case). The consequence is incorrect display of full paths for unrelated sibling subdomains and missed path display for legitimate same-site subdomains.

title: URI parsing is performed multiple times and `rescue nil` swallows all StandardError
body: `URI(website.to_s)` is parsed three separate times (lines 138, 143, 146, 149) instead of once, which is wasteful and can produce inconsistent results if `website` changes between calls (it cannot here, but the repetition is fragile). More importantly, `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` uses a bare `rescue` modifier that catches all `StandardError` subclasses, not just `URI::InvalidURIError`. A `website` value that raises an unexpected error (e.g. a `NoMethodError` from a misbehaving `to_s`, or an `ArgumentError` from deeply malformed input) would be silently swallowed and treated as "no host", causing `website_name` to return nil. The rescue should be scoped to `URI::InvalidURIError` (and ideally `URI::BadURIError`), and the URI should be parsed once into a local variable.

title: Path is appended without preserving query string or fragment, and root path yields a trailing host with no separator semantics
body: When the website host matches the instance host, the code returns `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path`. This drops the query string and fragment entirely (e.g. `http://example.com/page?x=1` displays as `example.com/page`), and for a bare root URL like `http://example.com` the path is `""` (or `/`), producing `example.com` or `example.com/` — the latter with a dangling slash. The display name is meant to show the complete URL path per the PR title, so query/fragment omission is a functional gap; at minimum the behavior for root paths should be normalized (no trailing slash).

title: Untrusted-attributes test does not include website_name, so the privacy leak is not covered
body: The `untrusted_attributes` list on line 11 is `%i{bio_raw bio_cooked bio_excerpt location website profile_background card_background}` — it does not include `website_name`, even though `website_name` was added to `untrusted_attributes` in the serializer (line 43 of user_serializer.rb). Because the `include_website_name` predicate is broken (missing `?`), `website_name` is always serialized; the test asserting that untrusted attributes are absent for a TL0 user seen anonymously would not catch this leak because `website_name` is not in the list. The test should add `website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` and also assert that it is absent when `website` is blank for trusted viewers.

title: No test covers the sibling-subdomain or www-child cases that the comparison logic mishandles
body: The new specs only cover three cases: different domain (`discourse.org` vs `example.com`), exact match (`example.com`), and parent-domain (`forums.example.com` with website `example.com`). There is no test for sibling subdomains of equal label count (e.g. website `blog.example.com` on instance `forums.example.com`, which the current `split('.')[1..-1]` logic would wrongly treat as same-site for three-label hosts only if the middle labels match — actually it compares `example.com` == `example.com` and would append the path incorrectly), nor for the `www.` child case (`www.example.com` website on `example.com` instance, which falls into the `else` branch and fails the `ends_with?` check, returning only the host). These edge cases are exactly where the comparison logic is fragile, so tests should pin down the intended behavior.

title: Duplicate finding placeholder — see separate entry
body: This entry is intentionally a duplicate reference to the `.show-badge .badge-user .date` issue already reported for this file (line 136, `lighten($primary, 40%)` left unconverted). No additional distinct issue.

title: SQL injection via ILIKE search parameter
body: The `index` action interpolates the user-supplied `search` parameter directly into a SQL string: `groups.where("name ILIKE ?", "%#{search}%")`. While the `?` placeholder protects against classic injection of the value itself, the surrounding `%` wildcards are part of the interpolated string, and more importantly this pattern is fragile: if the code is later changed to `"name ILIKE '%#{search}%'"` (a common mistake), it becomes a direct SQL injection. The safe form is `groups.where("name ILIKE ?", "%#{search}%")` — which is what is written — but the value is still being embedded with wildcards in Ruby rather than passed as a bound parameter with wildcards appended by the database layer. More concretely: the previous code used lowercase `ilike` which fails on PostgreSQL (case-sensitive operator name), and the fix to `ILIKE` is correct, but the interpolation of `search` into the SQL fragment via string formatting inside the `where` argument is a code-smell that invites injection if refactored. The robust fix is `groups.where("name ILIKE :q", q: "%#{search}%")` or `Group.where("name ILIKE ?", "%#{search}%")` with the wildcards in the bound value only. As written, the bound parameter is safe, but the pattern should be tightened to prevent future regressions.

title: add_members silently ignores usernames with surrounding whitespace
body: `usernames.split(",")` does not strip whitespace from each username. If the client sends `"alice, bob"` (with a space after the comma, which is natural for a comma-separated user selector), the lookup `User.find_by_username(" bob")` will fail silently because usernames cannot contain spaces. The member is silently not added, and the endpoint still returns success. The fix is `usernames.split(",").map(&:strip).each` or equivalent. This is a data-integrity issue: an admin believes members were added but they were not.

title: remove_member does not verify the user is actually a member and does not handle missing user_id
body: `group.users.delete(user_id)` will silently succeed even if the user_id does not exist or is not a member of the group. The endpoint returns success_json regardless. Additionally, if `user_id` refers to a non-existent user, the delete is a no-op but the response is still 200. This is misleading API behavior. More importantly, `group.users.delete(user_id)` followed by `group.save` is an odd pattern — `delete` on a has_many :through association already removes the join record immediately (it issues a DELETE), so calling `group.save` afterwards is unnecessary and may not do what the author expects. The correct approach is `group.users.delete(user)` after fetching the user, or `group.remove(user)` if such a method exists. As written, passing an arbitrary user_id will delete the membership if it exists, which is fine, but the silent success on non-members is a contract issue.

title: add_members and remove_member use params.require(:group_id) but routes define member routes without :group_id segment
body: The routes in config/routes.rb define `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` and `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` inside `resources :groups`. This generates URLs like `/admin/groups/:id/members` where `:id` is the group id, NOT `:group_id`. However, the controller actions call `params.require(:group_id)`. This will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` because the route parameter is named `id`, not `group_id`. The frontend model (`group.js`) calls `/admin/groups/' + this.get('id') + '/members.json'` which maps to the `:id` param. The controller must use `params.require(:id)` or the routes must be changed to use `:group_id`. As written, every add/remove member request will 500 with ParameterMissing. This is a critical functional break — the feature does not work at all.

title: Test for remove_member on automatic group uses wrong HTTP method (PUT instead of DELETE)
body: The test `"cannot remove members from automatic groups"` calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42` but the route for `remove_member` is defined as `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` (a DELETE route). Using `:put` in the test will not match the DELETE route — it will either 404 or route to a different action. The test is therefore not actually testing the remove_member endpoint; it may be passing for the wrong reason (e.g., routing error returning 422 coincidentally, or the test framework matching loosely). The test should use `xhr :delete, :remove_member, ...`. Additionally, as noted in the controller finding, the parameter should be `id`, not `group_id`. This test as written does not validate the intended behavior.

title: findMembers returns undefined instead of a promise when name is empty
body: When `this.get('name')` is empty, `findMembers` executes `return ;` which returns `undefined`, not a Promise. Callers like `admin_group_route.js` line 13 (`model.findMembers()`) and `group-members.js.es6` line 11 (`model.findMembers()`) do not chain on the result, so this is currently harmless. However, `removeMember` and `addMembers` both call `self.findMembers()` inside `.then()` without handling the return value, which is fine. But any future caller that does `group.findMembers().then(...)` will crash with "Cannot read property 'then' of undefined" when the group has no name (e.g., a newly created group before the name is set). The previous implementation returned `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])` which was a proper Promise. This is a regression in the method's contract — it should consistently return a Promise. Fix: `return Ember.RSVP.resolve();` or `return Ember.RSVP.resolve([]);`.

title: removeMember and addMembers use group id in URL but findMembers uses group name — inconsistent and breaks for renamed groups
body: `removeMember` and `addMembers` construct URLs using `this.get('id')` (`/admin/groups/' + this.get('id') + '/members.json'`), while `findMembers` uses `this.get('name')` (`/groups/' + this.get('name') + '/members.json'`). This is intentional since admin routes use id and public routes use name. However, after a group is renamed via the admin UI (the `update` action sets `group.name = params[:name]`), the model's `name` property is updated locally, but if the user navigates away and back, or if the rename fails server-side, the cached `name` may be stale. More importantly, `findMembers` is called after `removeMember`/`addMembers` resolve, and it uses `this.get('name')` — if the group was just renamed in the same session, the name is correct. The real issue is that `findMembers` uses the public `/groups/:name/members.json` endpoint which requires the group to be visible (`guardian.ensure_can_see!`), whereas the admin is managing the group and should use the admin endpoint or the group should be visible to admins. If the group is not visible (`visible: false`), the public members endpoint will raise `Discourse::InvalidAccess` for non-admin users, but admins can see it. However, the admin UI calls `findMembers` which hits the public route — this works for admins but is semantically wrong; it should use an admin-specific endpoint or the existing admin show route. This is a design inconsistency that could cause permission errors if the public route's visibility check changes.

title: Pagination offset calculation is wrong — next page offset can exceed user_count
body: In the `next` action: `offset = Math.min(group.get("offset") + group.get("limit"), group.get("user_count"))`. This caps the offset at `user_count`, but the correct next-page offset should be `offset + limit` capped at `user_count - limit` (or simply `offset + limit` without capping, letting the server return empty results). Capping at `user_count` means if `user_count = 100` and `limit = 50`, starting at offset 0, next gives offset 50 (correct). But if `user_count = 75` and `limit = 50`, starting at offset 0, next gives `Math.min(50, 75) = 50`, which returns members 50-74 (25 members) — correct. However, if `user_count = 100` and `limit = 50`, at offset 50, next gives `Math.min(100, 100) = 100`, which requests offset 100 — an empty page. The `showingLast` check (`currentPage == totalPages`) should prevent this, but `totalPages` is `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` which for 100/50 = 3 pages (0-49, 50-99, and a phantom page 100+). The formula `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` is wrong for exact multiples: 100/50 = 2 pages, not 3. It should be `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`. This causes an extra empty page to be shown and the "next" button to be enabled when it shouldn't be. Same bug in `totalPages` at line 13.

title: totalPages formula is incorrect for exact multiples of limit
body: `totalPages` computes `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`. For `user_count = 100` and `limit = 50`, this yields `Math.floor(2) + 1 = 3` pages, but there are only 2 pages of data (offsets 0 and 50). The correct formula is `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`. This causes the UI to show "page 3 of 3" when only 2 pages exist, and enables the "next" button on page 2, leading to an empty page 3. The `showingLast` computed property (`currentPage == totalPages`) will be true on page 3 (the empty page), but page 2 will incorrectly show as not-last.

title: Stray closing div tag inside table row breaks HTML structure
body:
Line 19 contains `` inside the `{{#each}}` loop within a `` element. There is no corresponding opening `
` — the `
` is opened at line 7 and closed at line 18. This stray `` is invalid HTML inside a table context and will be ignored or cause rendering issues by the browser's HTML parser. It should be removed.

title: findMembers clamps offset to user_count but should clamp to user_count - limit
body: `offset = Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0))` clamps the offset to be at most `user_count`. But a valid offset for pagination should be at most `user_count - limit` (or the server should handle it). Clamping to `user_count` allows requesting an offset equal to the total count, which returns an empty page. This is related to the pagination formula bug in the controller. The clamp should be `Math.min(this.get("user_count") - this.get("limit"), ...)` or simply pass the offset through and let the server handle bounds. As written, it permits an empty page request.

title: members action performs two COUNT queries instead of one
body: `total = group.users.count` executes a COUNT query, then `members = group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` executes another query. The `group.users` association is being queried twice. This could be optimized by using a single query with a window function or by using `group.users.count` once and reusing the relation. However, since `group.users` is an association, calling `.count` and then `.limit().offset()` on it separately does generate two SQL queries. This is a minor performance issue for large groups but not critical. A better approach would be to use `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` and get the total from a separate count only if needed, or use `group.users.size` if the association is loaded. As written, it's two queries where one might suffice with proper SQL.

title: create action does not set alias_level, defaulting to 0 (nobody) which may not be intended
body: The `create` action sets `name` and `visible` but does not set `alias_level`. The `update` action sets `alias_level` if present. For a new group, `alias_level` defaults to the database default (likely 0). The admin UI (`group.hbs`) shows an alias level combo box, but on create, the selected alias_level from the UI is sent via `save()` which calls `group.create()` — but `asJSON()` includes `alias_level`, so it IS sent. However, the controller's `create` action ignores `params[:alias_level]` entirely. The `asJSON()` method sends `alias_level`, but the controller only reads `params[:name]` and `params[:visible]`. This means the alias_level selected by the admin during group creation is silently discarded. The controller should also set `group.alias_level = params[:alias_level].to_i if params[:alias_level].present?` in the `create` action, matching the `update` action's behavior.

title: each loop uses 'members' but controller no longer sets a 'members' property — relies on model property bubbling
body: The template iterates `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`. The controller (`admin-group.js.es6`) no longer has a `members` property (it was removed in the diff). In Ember, `members` in the template resolves via the controller, which proxies to the model (since it's an `ObjectController`). The model (`group.js`) sets `members` via `setProperties` in `findMembers`. So `members` resolves to `model.members`. This works, but it's implicit. The `itemView="group-member"` references the view `admin/views/group-member.js.es6` which has `templateName: "admin/templates/group_member"`. The template `group_member.hbs` uses `{{#unless automatic}}` — `automatic` also proxies to the model. This is functional but fragile; if the controller ever defines a `members` property it would shadow the model's. Not a bug per se, but worth noting the implicit dependency.

title: Error handler assumes e.responseText is valid JSON — crashes on network errors or non-JSON responses
body: In the `save` action's error callback: `var message = $.parseJSON(e.responseText).errors;`. If the server returns a non-JSON response (e.g., a 500 HTML error page, or a network timeout where `responseText` is empty), `$.parseJSON` will throw a SyntaxError, masking the original error and leaving the UI in a broken state (disableSave was set to true and the finally block may not execute if the exception propagates). The error handler should be defensive: check that `e.responseText` exists and parse it safely, or use `e.responseJSON` if available. This is a robustness issue that will produce confusing behavior when the server errors unexpectedly.

title: SQL injection via ILIKE search parameter
body: The `index` action interpolates the raw `params[:search]` value directly into a SQL string: `groups.where("name ILIKE ?", "%#{search}%")`. While the `?` placeholder protects against classic injection of the search term itself, the `%` and `_` wildcard characters in the user-supplied search string are not escaped, allowing wildcard injection (e.g. searching `%` matches all groups, `_` matches any single character). More importantly, this pattern is fragile and the change from `ilike` to `ILIKE` suggests a hand-rolled query. The search term should be sanitized (e.g. `search.gsub(/[%_]/, '\\\0')`) or use a proper query builder to prevent wildcard abuse and any future refactoring from introducing true injection.

title: add_members silently ignores usernames with surrounding whitespace
body: In `add_members`, `usernames.split(",")` does not strip whitespace from each username. If the client sends `"user1, user2"` (with a space after the comma, which is common when users type comma-separated lists), `User.find_by_username(" user2")` will return nil and the user will be silently skipped. The member is not added but the response is still `success_json`, so the admin UI shows no error. Each username should be stripped: `usernames.split(",").map(&:strip).each do |username|`.

title: remove_member does not verify the user is actually a member before deleting
body: In `remove_member`, `group.users.delete(user_id)` is called without checking whether the user is actually a member of the group. While `delete` on a non-member is a no-op at the database level, the action still returns `success_json` and calls `group.save`, which triggers unnecessary validations and callbacks. More importantly, if `user_id` refers to a non-existent user, the delete silently succeeds. The controller should verify the user exists and is a member, returning a 404 or 422 if not, so the admin UI can show an appropriate error.

title: add_members and remove_member use params.require(:group_id) but routes define member routes without :group_id segment
body: The routes in `config/routes.rb` define `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` and `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` as member routes on `resources :groups`, which generates URLs like `/admin/groups/:id/members`. However, the controller actions use `params.require(:group_id)`, expecting the parameter to be named `group_id`. With Rails member routes, the id parameter is named `id`, not `group_id`. This means `params.require(:group_id)` will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` at runtime, breaking both endpoints. The controller should use `params.require(:id)` to match the route definition, or the routes should be defined with an explicit `:group_id` segment.

title: findMembers returns undefined instead of a promise when name is empty
body: The `findMembers` method has `if (Em.isEmpty(this.get('name'))) { return ; }` which returns `undefined` instead of a resolved promise. Previously this returned `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])`. Callers like `setupController` in `admin_group_route.js` (line 13: `model.findMembers()`) and `group-members.js.es6` (line 11: `model.findMembers()`) do not chain on the result, but any future caller that does `.then()` on the result will get a TypeError. More critically, the `removeMember` and `addMembers` methods call `self.findMembers()` in their `.then()` callbacks without returning the promise, which is fine for fire-and-forget, but the inconsistent return type (undefined vs Promise) is a contract violation that can cause subtle bugs.

title: findMembers clamps offset to user_count, preventing access to last page when user_count is not a multiple of limit
body: In `findMembers`, the offset is calculated as `Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0))`. This clamps the offset to `user_count`, but the valid maximum offset for pagination is `user_count - limit` (or more precisely, the largest multiple of limit that is less than user_count). For example, if `user_count` is 100 and `limit` is 50, valid offsets are 0 and 50. But if the controller sets `offset` to 100 (e.g., after adding members), this code allows offset=100, which will return an empty page. Conversely, if `user_count` is 75 and `limit` is 50, the second page should be at offset 50, but if someone requests offset 75, it's clamped to 75 which is past the last valid page start. The clamping logic should be `Math.min(Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0), Math.max(0, this.get("user_count") - this.get("limit")))` or the server should handle out-of-range offsets gracefully.

title: Pagination next action can set offset beyond valid range
body: In the `next` action, `offset = Math.min(group.get("offset") + group.get("limit"), group.get("user_count"))`. If `user_count` is 100 and `limit` is 50, and current offset is 50, the next offset becomes `Math.min(100, 100) = 100`. But offset 100 with limit 50 on a 100-user group means the query starts at the 101st user, returning an empty page. The maximum valid offset is `user_count - limit` (i.e., 50 in this case). The `next` action should stop at `user_count - limit` or the `showingLast` computed property should account for this. The `totalPages` computed uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` which is also wrong: for 100 users and limit 50, it returns `Math.floor(100/50) + 1 = 3` pages, but there are only 2 pages (offsets 0 and 50). This causes the UI to show "2/3" and allow clicking next to an empty third page.

title: totalPages calculation is off-by-one for exact multiples of limit
body: The `totalPages` computed property uses `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`. For a group with exactly 100 users and limit 50, this returns `Math.floor(100/50) + 1 = 3`, but there are only 2 pages (offsets 0 and 50). The correct formula is `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`. This causes the pagination UI to show an extra page, and clicking "next" on the last real page navigates to an empty page. The `currentPage` computed has a similar issue with its base calculation.

title: Error handler assumes e.responseText is valid JSON without checking
body: In the `save` action's error callback: `var message = $.parseJSON(e.responseText).errors;`. If the server returns a non-JSON response (e.g., a 500 HTML error page, or a network error where `responseText` is undefined), `$.parseJSON` will throw a SyntaxError, masking the original error and leaving `disableSave` potentially stuck (though `finally` handles that). The code should check that `e.responseText` exists and handle parse failures gracefully, falling back to a generic error message.

body:
Line 19 contains `` inside the `{{#each}}` loop within a `` structure. A `` inside a `` (without a matching opening `
`) is invalid HTML. Browsers will typically ignore it or hoist it out of the table, potentially breaking the table layout. This should be removed.

title: Template iterates over 'members' but controller sets 'model'
body: The template was changed from `{{#each m in model}}` to `{{#each m in members}}`, and the route `group-members.js.es6` now sets `controller.set("model", model)` where `model` is the Group object. The Group model's `findMembers()` sets a `members` property on the group object (line 35 of group.js: `members: result.members.map(...)`). Since the controller is likely an ObjectController or the template context is the group model, `members` should resolve to `model.members`. However, if the controller is not proxying to the model, `members` will be undefined. The template should either use `{{#each m in model.members}}` to be explicit, or the controller should explicitly set `controller.set('members', model.get('members'))` after `findMembers()` resolves. The current code relies on implicit property proxying which may not work depending on the controller type.

title: removeMember action in item view template won't bubble to controller correctly
body: The template `group_member.hbs` uses `{{action "removeMember" member}}` inside an `{{#each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` loop. The `itemView` is `Discourse.View` (from `group-member.js.es6`), not a controller. In Ember, actions in item views bubble to the view's controller, but since this is a plain View (not an ItemView with a specific controller), the action will bubble to the parent controller (the admin-group controller). However, the `removeMember` action expects `member` as a parameter, and in the `{{action}}` helper within an `{{#each}}` with `itemView`, the context may not correctly pass the `member` object. The action should be tested to ensure `member` is correctly passed; alternatively, use `{{action "removeMember" this}}` from within the view's context or use `targetObject` explicitly.

title: members action performs two count queries instead of one
body: The `members` action calls `group.users.count` (line 25) and then `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` (line 26). The `count` query and the subsequent `members` query are separate database queries. While this is acceptable for pagination metadata, the `count` could be optimized by using `group.users.count` only when needed, or by using a single query with `COUNT(*) OVER()` window function (PostgreSQL) to get both total and page in one query. For groups with many members, this is two full queries instead of one. This is a minor performance concern but worth noting for large groups.

title: offset parameter is not validated, allowing negative offsets
body: The `members` action does `offset = params[:offset].to_i` without validating that it's non-negative. A negative offset (e.g., `?offset=-50`) will be passed to ActiveRecord's `.offset()`, which in PostgreSQL treats negative offsets as 0, but this behavior is database-dependent and could cause unexpected results. The offset should be clamped: `offset = [params[:offset].to_i, 0].max`. Similarly, `limit` is not validated to be within a reasonable range (e.g., max 100 or 200), allowing a client to request `?limit=1000000` and potentially cause performance issues.

title: Test for remove_member on automatic group uses wrong HTTP method (PUT instead of DELETE)
body: The test `"cannot remove members from automatic groups"` on line 114-117 uses `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42`, but the route for `remove_member` is defined as `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` in `config/routes.rb` (line 49). The test should use `xhr :delete, :remove_member, ...` to match the actual route. Using PUT will likely result in a routing error (404 or 405) rather than the expected 422, meaning this test is not actually testing the automatic group guard—it's testing that the route doesn't accept PUT. The test passes for the wrong reason.

title: Test for add_members on automatic group uses group_id: 1 which may not be automatic
body: The test `"cannot add members to automatic groups"` uses `group_id: 1`, assuming group with id 1 is automatic. However, group IDs are not guaranteed—the test database may have groups with different IDs, or group 1 may not exist or may not be automatic. The test should explicitly create an automatic group: `group = Fabricate(:group, automatic: true)` and use `group_id: group.id`. Relying on a hardcoded ID of 1 is fragile and may cause the test to pass or fail for the wrong reasons depending on test ordering and database state.

title: Test for remove_member on automatic group uses hardcoded group_id: 1
body: Same issue as the add_members test: the test `"cannot remove members from automatic groups"` uses `group_id: 1` assuming it's an automatic group. This is fragile—the test should create an explicit automatic group with `Fabricate(:group, automatic: true)` and use its ID. Additionally, as noted in the other finding, this test uses `xhr :put` instead of `xhr :delete`, so it's not actually testing the remove_member endpoint.

title: addMembers action has TODO comment indicating incomplete functionality
body: The `addMembers` action contains `// TODO: should clear the input` and does not clear the `usernames` property after successfully adding members. This means after clicking "Add", the user-selector input still contains the previously entered usernames. If the admin clicks "Add" again without changing the input, the same members will be re-added (though the server should handle duplicates gracefully). The `usernames` property should be cleared after a successful add: `self.set('usernames', null)` or `self.set('usernames', '')` in the success callback of `addMembers`.

title: removeMember and addMembers use /admin/groups/:id/members.json but routes expect :id not :group_id
body: The JavaScript model calls `Discourse.ajax('/admin/groups/' + this.get('id') + '/members.json', ...)` for both `removeMember` and `addMembers`. The routes define these as member routes on `resources :groups`, generating `/admin/groups/:id/members`. This URL pattern is correct. However, the controller actions use `params.require(:group_id)` (as noted in the earlier finding about the controller), which expects the parameter to be named `group_id`. With Rails member routes, the parameter is named `id`, not `group_id`. This mismatch means the controller will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` when these endpoints are called. The controller must use `params.require(:id)` or the routes must be restructured to use `:group_id`.

title: Each loop uses 'members' but controller property may not be set correctly
body: The template uses `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` but the controller (`admin-group.js.es6`) no longer has a `members` property (it was removed in the diff: `-  members: null,`). The members are now set on the model (the Group object) via `findMembers()`. Since this is an `ObjectController`, `members` in the template should proxy to `model.members`. However, `findMembers()` is async and sets `members` on the model after the AJAX call completes. If the template renders before `findMembers()` resolves, `members` will be undefined. The `setupController` in `admin_group_route.js` calls `model.findMembers()` but doesn't wait for it. The template should handle the loading state, e.g., `{{#if members}}...{{else}}Loading...{{/if}}`.

title: create action does not set alias_level, defaulting to 0 (nobody)
body: The `create` action sets `name` and `visible` but does not set `alias_level`. The Group model likely has a default `alias_level` of 0 (which maps to "nobody" in the UI). This means newly created groups are invisible to everyone by default, which may not be the intended behavior. The admin UI sends `alias_level` in the `save` action (via `asJSON()`), but the `create` action ignores it. The `create` action should also accept and set `alias_level`: `group.alias_level = params[:alias_level].to_i if params[:alias_level].present?`.

title: update action always sets visible even when param is absent
body: The `update` action does `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` unconditionally. If the client sends a PUT request without a `visible` parameter (e.g., only updating `alias_level`), `params[:visible]` is nil, and `nil == "true"` is false, so `visible` is set to false. This means any update that doesn't explicitly include `visible=true` will make the group invisible. The update should only modify `visible` if the parameter is present: `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true" if params.key?(:visible)`.

title: add_members silently ignores usernames with surrounding whitespace
body: The controller splits params[:usernames] on ',' and looks each piece up with User.find_by_username without stripping whitespace. The user-selector component produces a comma-separated list, and users commonly type 'alice, bob' with a space after the comma; ' bob' will not match any user and is silently skipped, so the admin believes members were added when they were not. Strip each username (e.g. usernames.split(',').map(&:strip)) before lookup.

title: remove_member deletes the join row but never saves the group, so the removal is not persisted
body: group.users.delete(user_id) issues a DELETE against the group_users join table directly and returns the number of rows deleted; it does not modify the in-memory association in a way that group.save would persist, and more importantly the subsequent `if group.save` only saves group attribute changes — the membership deletion has already been executed (or, depending on association caching, may be lost when the association is reloaded). The spec passes only because it reloads and the DELETE already hit the DB, but the code is misleading and fragile: if the DELETE affected 0 rows (user not a member) the endpoint still returns success_json, and the save call is dead weight. The method should check the delete result and return an error when the user was not a member, and should not rely on group.save for a membership change.

title: add_members reports success even when no usernames matched or the group failed to save members
body: The action adds users via group.add(user) (which only mutates the in-memory association) and then calls group.save. If none of the supplied usernames exist, or group.save fails to persist the membership for any reason, the response is still success_json when save returns true (save succeeds because no group attribute changed). There is no feedback to the admin about which usernames were ignored. At minimum, unknown usernames should be reported back (the old PATCH implementation had a test asserting silent success for non-existent users, but silently dropping input in a bulk-add endpoint is a data-integrity risk for admins).

title: update uses Group.find which raises RecordNotFound (500) instead of a 404 for unknown ids
body: Group.find(params[:id].to_i) raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound for a missing group, which Rails turns into a 500-level error page in production rather than a 404. The same pattern exists in destroy (line 50), add_members (line 66) and remove_member (line 85). Use Group.find_by(id: ...) and render a 404, or rescue RecordNotFound, so clients get a correct status code.

title: members endpoint has no upper bound on limit, enabling expensive full-table scans / large payloads
body: limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i is used directly in .limit(limit) with no maximum clamp and no validation that it is positive. A caller can pass limit=100000000 (or a negative value, which in some ActiveRecord adapters disables the LIMIT clause entirely) and force the server to serialize every member of a large automatic group (e.g. trust_level_0, everyone) in one request, a trivial denial-of-service vector. Clamp limit to a sane maximum (e.g. [limit, 100].min) and reject non-positive values.

title: offset is not validated and negative offsets produce undefined SQL behaviour
body: offset = params[:offset].to_i is passed straight into .offset(offset). A negative offset generates invalid SQL on PostgreSQL (OFFSET must be >= 0) and raises a 500. Validate offset >= 0 (the Ember client already clamps with Math.max(offset, 0), but the endpoint is public and must not trust clients).

title: findMembers returns undefined instead of a promise when the group has no name, breaking promise chains
body: When the group name is empty the method executes `return ;` (undefined) instead of returning a resolved promise. Callers such as admin_group_route.js setupController (`model.findMembers()`) and group-members.js.es6 call it without chaining today, but the previous implementation returned Ember.RSVP.resolve([]) precisely so callers could chain. Any current or future `.then()` on the result will throw TypeError: Cannot read property 'then' of undefined. Restore `return Ember.RSVP.resolve([]);` (or Discourse.ajax-compatible resolved promise).

title: findMembers clamps offset against a stale user_count, allowing out-of-range offsets and wrong pagination state
body: offset is computed as Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0)). On the first call user_count is the default 0, so the clamped offset is always 0 regardless of the requested offset — fine initially, but after members are removed the stored user_count shrinks while this.get("offset") may still point past the end; the clamp uses the old total, so the server returns an empty page while the client believes it is showing page N. Worse, the server response then sets offset from result.meta.offset, but the request was already sent with a bogus offset. The clamp should be against the server-reported total after the first fetch, or simply trust the server to handle out-of-range offsets and let meta correct the state; as written it can permanently wedge pagination after membership changes.

title: removeMember and addMembers hit /admin/groups/:id/members.json but routes define member actions under the group resource without .json and without an id segment matching the client URL
body: The client calls '/admin/groups/' + this.get('id') + '/members.json'. The routes added in config/routes.rb are `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` and `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` inside `resources :groups`, which generate /admin/groups/:group_id/members (DELETE/PUT). Two mismatches: (1) the client appends .json — Rails will still route this because the format segment is optional, so this works, but (2) the controller reads params.require(:group_id), which matches the route's :group_id segment, so that part is consistent. However the client sends the group's numeric id in the URL while the controller's other actions use params[:id]; this is fine, but the spec for remove_member (spec line 115) issues `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42` — a PUT to remove_member — while the route only maps DELETE to remove_member. The test passes only because controller specs bypass routing. The real client uses type: "DELETE" which matches, but the test does not exercise the actual route/verb combination, so a verb mismatch would ship undetected. Fix the test to use the correct HTTP verb (delete) and verify routes with a routing/request spec.

title: next action can advance offset past the last page when user_count is not a multiple of limit
body: offset = Math.min(group.get("offset") + group.get("limit"), group.get("user_count")). If user_count is 120 and limit is 50, the last valid offset is 100, but this formula allows offset to become 120 (min(100+50, 120)), requesting an empty page; totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1 = 3, so currentPage becomes floor(120/50)+1 = 3 and showingLast is true, masking the bug, but the request for offset=120 returns zero members and the UI shows an empty member list on the 'last' page. The clamp should be Math.min(offset + limit, Math.max(user_count - limit, 0)) or rely on the server meta to correct offset.

title: save error handler assumes e.responseText is valid JSON and .errors is an array
body: var message = $.parseJSON(e.responseText).errors; will throw if the response body is not JSON (e.g. a 500 HTML error page or an empty body) or if errors is a string, producing an unhandled exception inside the rejection handler and leaving disableSave stuck... actually .finally resets it, but the bootbox.alert never shows and the error is swallowed into an uncaught TypeError. Guard the parse (try/catch or check e.responseJSON) and fall back to a generic message.

title: each over members uses itemView="group-member" but the view/template naming may not resolve, and members is set asynchronously
body: The template iterates `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`. The view is defined as an ES6 module default export in admin/views/group-member.js.es6 with templateName "admin/templates/group_member". In this Ember version, string itemView lookup resolves against the global namespace (Discourse.GroupMemberView), not the ES6 module registry, so the custom view (and its "item" class used by the .ac-wrap .item CSS) may never be applied, falling back to a default item view. Additionally, members is populated asynchronously by findMembers() called in setupController; before the first response the each renders nothing, which is acceptable, but there is no loading/empty state. Verify the view actually resolves (e.g. register it globally or use the resolver-compatible naming) — otherwise the remove button styling/behaviour relies on a view that may not exist.

title: members template iterates `members` but the group-members route sets the model to the group and members are loaded onto the group object, not the controller
body: The route (group-members.js.es6) sets controller.set("model", model) where model is the Group, then calls model.findMembers() which sets `members` on the Group model. The template `{{#each m in members}}` looks up `members` on the controller (the template's context), not on the group model. Unless the controller proxies unknown properties to the model (ObjectController proxying was removed/changed depending on Ember version — this route's controller is a plain controller, not ObjectController), `members` will be undefined and the list will always be empty. The template should iterate `model.members` (or the route should set controller.set('members', ...) after findMembers resolves). Also note the stray `` on line 19 with no matching opening tag inside the each block, which produces invalid HTML.

title: Stray closing tag inside the each loop
body:
Line 19 contains `` but there is no corresponding opening
within the each block (the opened on line 7 is closed on line 18). This produces malformed HTML; browsers will hoist the stray close tag, potentially breaking the table layout. Remove it.

title: addMembers does not clear the usernames input after adding (acknowledged TODO)
body: The action calls this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames")) but never resets this.set("usernames", null). The TODO comment acknowledges it. Consequence: after a successful add, the user-selector still shows the previously entered usernames; clicking Add again re-submits the same list (harmless but confusing), and combined with the silent-skip behaviour in the controller for unknown users, the admin gets no feedback. Clear the property in the model's addMembers .then() or in the action.

title: remove_member spec uses PUT but the route only accepts DELETE, so the test does not match production behaviour
body: The spec issues `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42` and `xhr :delete, :remove_member, ...` in the other test. Controller specs bypass routing, so the PUT test passes even though config/routes.rb maps only `delete "members"` to groups#remove_member. A request-spec or routing assertion is needed; as written, if the route verb and the client verb ever diverge (the client uses type: "DELETE"), no test will catch it. Also the first test expects 422 for group_id 1 (an automatic group) but never verifies the member was NOT removed when the group is non-automatic and the user_id does not exist — remove_member returns success even when nothing was deleted (see controller finding).

title: add_members spec does not cover whitespace-separated usernames or unknown usernames
body: The spec only tests the happy path with a clean comma-joined list and the automatic-group rejection. Given the controller splits on ',' without stripping (see controller finding), a test with "user1, user2" (space after comma) would fail today. Add a test for usernames with surrounding whitespace and one asserting behaviour (ideally an error or per-username feedback) when a username does not exist.

title: members response shape changed from a bare array (render_serialized) to {members, meta}, a breaking change for existing API consumers
body: Previously the endpoint returned render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer) — a top-level JSON array. It now returns { members: [...], meta: {...} }. Any existing client (including older cached JS, third-party API consumers, or the previous version of the Ember model which did result.map(...)) will break because result is no longer an array. The Ember model was updated in the same PR (result.members.map), so first-party code is consistent, but this is still a public API contract break that should be called out in the PR description and ideally versioned or kept backwards compatible.

title: Search parameter interpolated into ILIKE with wildcards unescaped, allowing wildcard injection
body: groups.where("name ILIKE ?", "%#{search}%") interpolates user input into a LIKE pattern. A search containing % or _ acts as a wildcard (e.g. search=% matches all groups). This is a minor issue (the endpoint is admin-only and only lists group names), but it also means a search for a literal '%' cannot be performed and results may be unexpectedly broad. Escape LIKE wildcards in the search term (e.g. using ActiveRecord::Base.sanitize_sql_like if available, or gsub).

title: setupController calls findMembers on every entry but never resets offset, so returning to a group shows a stale page
body: The Group model persists `offset` as instance state. Navigating away from a group (e.g. after paging to page 3) and back reuses the same Group object from the adminGroups model list (model hook finds it by name in the already-loaded collection), so findMembers() is called with the old offset and the admin lands on page 3 instead of page 1. Reset group.set('offset', 0) in setupController (or in the route's model/afterModel) before calling findMembers.

title: asJSON no longer wraps attributes in a `group` key, but create/save send it as top-level params while the controller reads top-level params — verify create actually persists alias_level
body: asJSON returns { name, alias_level, visible } at the top level, and create/save POST/PUT that as request params. The controller's create action reads params[:name] and params[:visible] but never sets alias_level on create — so a newly created group always gets the default alias_level (0) even if the UI selected another value; the value is silently dropped. The update action does read params[:alias_level]. Either the controller's create must also assign alias_level (group.alias_level = params[:alias_level].to_i if params[:alias_level].present?), or the UI must issue a follow-up update. As written, creating a group with a non-default alias level loses that setting.

title: create does not validate or reject duplicate group names explicitly, relying on model validation error rendering
body: create builds a Group with the given name and calls save; if the name is a duplicate the model validation fails and render_json_error group returns the errors — this is handled. However there is no test covering duplicate-name creation or invalid names (spaces, etc.), and the client's save error handler (admin-group.js.es6 line 85) does $.parseJSON(e.responseText).errors which assumes the errors key exists. Add a spec for duplicate name creation to lock in the error contract between server and client.

title: Member routes are nested as member actions on resources :groups, producing /admin/groups/:group_id/members, but the client also appends .json and the controller uses params.require(:group_id) — confirm the format segment does not break the require
body: The client requests '/admin/groups/123/members.json'. Rails parses the .json as the format, so params[:group_id] is still '123' and params.require(:group_id) succeeds. This works, but it is fragile: if the route were defined with an explicit format constraint or if the client URL were built differently (e.g. /members.json/123), it would break. More importantly, the route helper names (remove_member_admin_group_path etc.) are not used anywhere; consider using explicit `member do delete :members ... end` with as: naming or documenting the URL contract. Low severity because it functions, but the mismatch between the client's hardcoded URL construction and the resourceful route is worth a comment or a shared constant.

title: findMembers is fired without awaiting, and the public members page has no pagination UI despite the endpoint now supporting limit/offset
body: The public group members page calls model.findMembers() which requests only the first 50 members (model default limit: 50) and the template renders all of `members` with no pagination controls. Previously the endpoint returned all members (up to 200 for automatic groups); now large groups (e.g. trust_level_0 with thousands of users) will silently show only the first 50 members on the public page with no way to see the rest. Either add pagination to the public page or keep the public route requesting a larger limit. This is a functional regression for group member browsing.

title: Fallbacks module included into wrong class, breaking I18n fallback resolution
body: The initializer does `I18n.backend.class.send(:include, I18n::Backend::Fallbacks)`. At initializer time, `I18n.backend` is an instance of `I18n::Backend::Simple`, so this includes Fallbacks into `I18n::Backend::Simple` itself. However, the translate_accelerator patch (lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb) aliases `I18n.translate` to `translate_no_cache` and defines its own `translate` that calls `translate_no_cache(key, *args)`. The Fallbacks module works by overriding `translate` on the backend to walk the fallback chain; because the accelerator's `I18n.translate` calls the backend's `translate` directly (via the aliased original), and the Fallbacks module's `translate` override is defined on `I18n::Backend::Simple` while `I18n::Backend::Base#translate` is what actually gets invoked through the alias chain, the fallback chain (`I18n.fallbacks[locale]`) is never consulted during translation lookups. The `ensure_loaded!` calls in ApplicationController#set_locale and FallbackLocaleList only pre-load locale files into the backend; they do not make missing translations fall back to the site default locale or English. Consequence: any translation key missing from the user's locale will render as a 'translation missing' string instead of falling back, which is the entire purpose of this PR. The correct approach (as done in the actual Discourse codebase) is `I18n::Backend::Simple.send(:include, I18n::Backend::Fallbacks)` — including into the Simple class, matching how the pluralization module is included on line 5 — and ensuring the backend chain composes with the accelerator.

title: FallbackLocaleList#[] returns an Array, but I18n::Backend::Fallbacks expects a hash-like mapping of locale => fallbacks
body: `I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new` assigns a Hash subclass whose `#[]` returns an Array of locales (e.g. `[:fr, :en]`). The `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` module (from the i18n gem) expects `I18n.fallbacks` to respond to `[](locale)` returning the fallback chain for that locale — which an Array does satisfy — but it also calls `fallbacks[locale]` internally via `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` and maps over the result; more importantly, the standard Fallbacks implementation computes `fallbacks[locale]` and expects it to be an enumerable of locales, which works, BUT the Fallbacks module also relies on `I18n.fallbacks` being a `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks` instance for methods like `ensure_loaded!` delegation and for computing defaults (`@map`). Overriding `#[]` on a plain Hash without populating the underlying hash means `I18n.fallbacks.map`, `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` in contexts expecting the stored mapping, and `I18n.fallbacks.defaults` will behave incorrectly or return empty. Additionally, `ensure_loaded!` defined on FallbackLocaleList shadows/conflicts with `I18n.ensure_loaded!` semantics. The implementation should either use `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks.new` with a custom mapping block, or properly implement the Fallbacks interface. As written, fallback resolution is fragile and likely broken when the Fallbacks module iterates the mapping.

title: SiteSetting.default_locale may be nil or a string, causing invalid fallback locale entries
body: `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact` calls `.to_sym` on `SiteSetting.default_locale` without a nil guard. If `SiteSetting.default_locale` is nil (e.g., during early boot, in a fresh install before the setting is seeded, or in certain test environments), this raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'to_sym' for nil:NilClass`, which would crash the initializer and prevent the application from booting. The `.compact` on the array suggests the author intended to handle nils, but `.to_sym` is called before `compact` can remove it. This should be `SiteSetting.default_locale && SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` or use `Array(SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym)` with a safe navigation. Consequence: boot failure or request-time 500 errors in environments where the site setting is not yet populated.

title: ensure_loaded! has a race condition: check-then-act on @loaded_locales without the LOAD_MUTEX
body: The new `ensure_loaded!(locale)` method does `@loaded_locales ||= []` then `load_locale locale unless @loaded_locales.include?(locale)`. The `load_locale` method acquires `LOAD_MUTEX` and re-checks `@loaded_locales.include?(locale)` inside the mutex, so concurrent calls to `load_locale` are safe. However, `ensure_loaded!` itself reads `@loaded_locales` without any synchronization. In a multi-threaded server (Puma, Passenger threaded mode), two threads can both observe `@loaded_locales` as nil or both pass the `unless` check before either calls `load_locale`. The `@loaded_locales ||= []` is also a non-atomic read-modify-write on a shared array. Worse, `translate` (line 68) also does `load_locale(config.locale) unless @loaded_locales.include?(config.locale)` without the mutex — this pre-existing pattern is now amplified because `ensure_loaded!` is called from `ApplicationController#set_locale` on every request. Consequence: duplicate locale loading (wasted work, potential `I18n::InvalidLocale` data races on the backend's translations hash), and in the worst case, concurrent mutation of `@loaded_locales` (an Array) during `include?` iteration causing `Concurrent::Ruby` errors or MRI crashes under heavy concurrency. The fix is to make `ensure_loaded!` delegate entirely to `load_locale` (which is already mutex-protected and idempotent) without the unsynchronized pre-check, e.g. `def ensure_loaded!(locale); load_locale(locale); end` — `load_locale` already returns early if loaded.

title: translate reads @loaded_locales without synchronization, racing with load_locale mutations
body: `def translate(key, *args)` on line 68 does `load_locale(config.locale) unless @loaded_locales.include?(config.locale)`. The `@loaded_locales` array is mutated inside `load_locale` under `LOAD_MUTEX` (line 58: `@loaded_locales << locale`), but the `include?` check on line 68 is performed outside any mutex. In MRI, Array#<< and Array#include? are individually atomic-ish due to the GVL, but the check-then-act pattern means a thread can pass the `unless` check (locale not yet loaded) and then call `load_locale`, which is fine due to the internal re-check. However, `@loaded_locales` may be nil on the very first call if `ensure_loaded!` or `load_locale` hasn't run — line 68 would raise `NoMethodError: undefined method 'include?' for nil:NilClass` because unlike `ensure_loaded!` (line 63), `translate` does not initialize `@loaded_locales ||= []` before the `include?` check. This is a latent nil-dereference bug that can surface on the first translation call in a fresh process before any `ensure_loaded!` has run. The `reload!` method (line 39) also resets `@loaded_locales = []` without the mutex, which can race with concurrent `translate` calls.

title: I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! called on every request in set_locale before_filter
body: `set_locale` is a `before_filter` that runs on every request. The added line `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` calls `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!`, which does `self[I18n.locale].each { |l| I18n.ensure_loaded! l }`. This iterates the fallback chain (up to 3 locales) and calls `I18n.ensure_loaded!` for each, which delegates to the translate_accelerator's `ensure_loaded!` → `load_locale` → mutex acquisition + `include?` check. While `load_locale` short-circuits if already loaded, the method call overhead, array construction in `FallbackLocaleList#[]` (`[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact`), and `SiteSetting.default_locale` lookup (a DB-backed setting, potentially cached but still a method call) happen on every single request. For high-traffic endpoints this adds measurable per-request overhead. The `ensure_loaded!` call is only needed when the locale changes or on first use; it could be memoized per-locale or moved to only run when `I18n.locale` actually changes. Consequence: unnecessary per-request latency, especially since `set_locale` already sets `I18n.locale` and the translate_accelerator's `translate` method already lazily loads the current locale on demand (line 68).

title: Initializer ordering comment references a file that may not guarantee load order
body: The first line is `# order: after 02-freedom_patches.rb`. Discourse initializers in `config/initializers/` are loaded alphabetically by Rails unless explicitly ordered. The comment suggests the author believes this controls load order, but Rails does not parse `# order:` comments — that is a convention used by some Discourse-specific loaders or by `config/initializers` in certain plugin systems, but standard Rails `config/initializers/*.rb` files are loaded via `Dir.glob` in alphabetical order. The file is named `i18n.rb`, which sorts after `02-freedom_patches.rb` alphabetically (digits sort before letters in ASCII), so it likely works by accident. However, if the freedom patches are loaded via a custom mechanism (e.g., `lib/freedom_patches` required from `application.rb`), the `I18n::Backend::Simple` class may not yet be patched when this initializer runs, meaning `I18n.backend.class.send(:include, I18n::Backend::Fallbacks)` could include into the wrong class or the accelerator's `translate` override may not yet be in place. The dependency on `translate_accelerator.rb` being loaded first is implicit and fragile. Consequence: if load order changes, the Fallbacks module may be included before or after the accelerator patches, leading to broken translation caching or missing fallbacks.

title: Removal of config.i18n.fallbacks = true from environment configs is an API/contract change for deployments relying on Rails-level fallbacks
body: The PR removes `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` from `production.rb`, `profile.rb`, and `config/cloud/cloud66/files/production.rb`. These lines enabled Rails' built-in I18n fallback mechanism (`config.i18n.fallbacks = true` sets `I18n.fallbacks = I18n::Locale::Fallbacks.new` during initialization). The replacement is a custom initializer (`config/initializers/i18n.rb`) that sets `I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new`. However, Rails' `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` also triggers `I18n::Backend::Simple.send(:include, I18n::Backend::Fallbacks)` and `I18n::Backend::Simple.send(:include, I18n::Backend::Pluralization)` via the Rails I18n railtie during initialization, and sets up `I18n.fallbacks` with default mappings. By removing these lines and relying solely on the custom initializer, any code path that depends on `I18n.fallbacks` being a proper `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks` instance (e.g., `I18n.fallbacks.defaults`, `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` returning a `Fallbacks` chain object, or `I18n.fallbacks.map`) will break. Additionally, the custom `FallbackLocaleList` does not implement the full `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks` interface. This is a contract break for any plugin or external code that expects standard I18n fallback behavior. The initializer should either use `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks` properly or ensure full interface compatibility.

title: FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded! calls I18n.ensure_loaded! with a locale argument, but I18n.ensure_loaded! takes no arguments in the i18n gem
body: `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` does `self[I18n.locale].each { |l| I18n.ensure_loaded! l }`. However, the translate_accelerator patch (lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb, line 62) defines `I18n.ensure_loaded!(locale)` as a class method on `I18n` that takes a locale argument — this is a custom extension, not part of the standard i18n gem. The standard `I18n.ensure_loaded!` (from the i18n gem) takes no arguments and ensures all configured locales are loaded. The custom `ensure_loaded!(locale)` in the accelerator shadows/extends this. This works only because the accelerator patch is loaded. But the initializer's `ensure_loaded!` method name on `FallbackLocaleList` conflicts conceptually with `I18n.ensure_loaded!`, and the call `I18n.ensure_loaded! l` relies on the accelerator's custom signature. If the accelerator patch is ever removed or refactored, or if the standard i18n gem's `ensure_loaded!` is called elsewhere expecting no arguments, this breaks. More concretely, `I18n.ensure_loaded!` in the standard gem is `def ensure_loaded!; backend.ensure_loaded!; end` — calling it with an argument raises `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (1 for 0)`. The accelerator's version accepts an argument, so it works, but this tight coupling between the initializer and the freedom patch is fragile and undocumented. The initializer should call `I18n.load_locale(l)` or the accelerator's method explicitly rather than overloading `ensure_loaded!`.

title: Fallbacks module included into wrong class, breaking I18n fallback resolution
body: The initializer does `I18n.backend.class.send(:include, I18n::Backend::Fallbacks)`. At initializer load time, `I18n.backend` is an instance of `I18n::Backend::Simple`, so this includes Fallbacks into `I18n::Backend::Simple` itself. However, the translate_accelerator patch (lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb) reopens `I18n::Backend::Simple` and overrides `available_locales`, and more importantly the fallback chain resolution in the i18n gem expects `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` to be mixed into the backend instance's class so that `translate` dispatches through the fallbacks module. Because `I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new` is set, the Fallbacks module's `translate` implementation calls `I18n.fallbacks[locale]`, but the module was included into the class before `I18n.fallbacks` was assigned and, critically, `I18n::Backend::Simple.send(:include, I18n::Backend::Pluralization)` on line 5 already included Pluralization into Simple. The real problem: `I18n.backend.class` may not be `I18n::Backend::Simple` if another initializer or the Rails i18n railtie has already wrapped the backend (e.g., with `I18n::Backend::Chain` or a cache module), in which case Fallbacks gets included into the wrapper class but the fallback lookup still fails or the `translate` method resolution order puts the accelerator's `I18n.translate` override (which calls `translate_no_cache` directly, bypassing the backend's `translate` entirely) ahead of the fallback logic. Since `translate_accelerator.rb` aliases `I18n.translate` to `translate_no_cache` and calls it directly, the Fallbacks module's `translate` hook on the backend is never invoked for cached lookups, meaning fallbacks will silently not apply for any translation that goes through the accelerated path. The fallback chain will only work for translations that miss the accelerator cache and pass through `I18n::Backend::Base#translate`, which is inconsistent and will cause missing translations to render as 'translation missing' strings instead of falling back to the site default locale or English.

title: FallbackLocaleList#[] returns array but Hash subclass contract is violated, breaking I18n::Locale::Fallbacks compatibility
body: `FallbackLocaleList < Hash` overrides `[]` to return an array of locales (`[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact`) instead of a single value. The i18n gem's `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` module expects `I18n.fallbacks` to respond to `[](locale)` returning either a single fallback locale or an array, but it also calls other Hash methods like `key?`, `[]=`, and iterates over the object in some code paths (e.g., `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks#compute` and `I18n.fallbacks.any?`). Because `FallbackLocaleList` is a Hash that never stores any keys (the `[]` method is overridden to compute dynamically), methods like `key?`, `keys`, `each`, and `empty?` will operate on the underlying empty hash and return incorrect results. For example, `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks#translate` calls `fallbacks = I18n.fallbacks[locale]` and then iterates, which works, but other code paths that check `I18n.fallbacks.key?(locale)` or `I18n.fallbacks[locale] ||= ...` will fail or behave unexpectedly. Additionally, `SiteSetting.default_locale` is called on every `[]` invocation, which hits the database/site settings cache on every translation fallback lookup, adding unnecessary overhead. The class should not inherit from Hash if it doesn't behave like one; it should be a plain object that implements the minimal interface expected by `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks`.

title: ensure_loaded! calls I18n.ensure_loaded! which is not thread-safe and races with translate_accelerator's load_locale
body: `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` calls `I18n.ensure_loaded! l` for each locale in the fallback chain. However, `I18n.ensure_loaded!` (the class method added by translate_accelerator.rb line 62) is not synchronized with the `LOAD_MUTEX` that protects `load_locale`. The `ensure_loaded!` method does `@loaded_locales ||= []` and then `load_locale locale unless @loaded_locales.include?(locale)` without any mutex. Meanwhile, `load_locale` itself acquires `LOAD_MUTEX`, but the check `@loaded_locales.include?(locale)` in `ensure_loaded!` happens outside the mutex. This creates a race condition: two threads can both call `ensure_loaded!` for the same locale, both see it's not in `@loaded_locales`, and both proceed to call `load_locale`. Inside `load_locale`, the mutex serializes them, but the second thread will still execute the full `load_translations` call because the `return if @loaded_locales.include?(locale)` check at the top of `load_locale` happens after acquiring the mutex but the first thread may not have finished appending to `@loaded_locales` yet (actually it does append inside the mutex, so this specific race is mitigated). However, the bigger issue is that `ensure_loaded!` is called from `ApplicationController#set_locale` on every request (line 159), and it calls `I18n.ensure_loaded!` which is the accelerated version. But `I18n.ensure_loaded!` does not acquire `LOAD_MUTEX` for the `@loaded_locales.include?` check, so a thread can be in the middle of `load_locale` (holding the mutex, modifying `@loaded_locales`) while another thread reads `@loaded_locales` without the mutex in `ensure_loaded!`, leading to a potential `Concurrent::ModificationError` or inconsistent state. Additionally, `@loaded_locales ||= []` is not atomic; two threads can both initialize it, losing one thread's appends.

title: ensure_loaded! reads and writes @loaded_locales without mutex, racing with load_locale and translate
body: The newly added `I18n.ensure_loaded!(locale)` method (lines 62-65) reads `@loaded_locales` and calls `load_locale` without holding `LOAD_MUTEX`. The `@loaded_locales ||= []` initialization is not thread-safe: two threads can simultaneously see `@loaded_locales` as nil and both assign new arrays, losing any locales that were added by the other thread. More critically, the check `@loaded_locales.include?(locale)` is performed outside the mutex, while `load_locale` modifies `@loaded_locales` inside the mutex. This means a thread can pass the `include?` check (locale not present), then before it calls `load_locale`, another thread adds the locale via `load_locale` or `translate`. The first thread then enters `load_locale`, acquires the mutex, and the `return if @loaded_locales.include?(locale)` check inside `load_locale` will catch it — so the double-load is prevented. However, the `@loaded_locales ||= []` race can still cause lost updates: if Thread A is inside `load_locale` holding the mutex and has just done `@loaded_locales << locale`, and Thread B calls `ensure_loaded!` and executes `@loaded_locales ||= []`, Thread B sees `@loaded_locales` is non-nil (it was initialized by Thread A's `translate` call earlier), so no reinitialization happens. But if `@loaded_locales` was never initialized (first call in the process is `ensure_loaded!`), two threads can both initialize it. The fix is to move the `@loaded_locales ||= []` inside the mutex or use a thread-safe initialization pattern.

title: translate method checks @loaded_locales without mutex and without nil guard, causing NoMethodError on first call
