body: UserPermissionsV2 extends UserPermissions which implements UserPermissionEvaluator and UserPermissionManagement. UserPermissionsV2 overrides isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, getPermissions, resource, managePermission, viewPermission, manageGroupMembershipPermission, mapRolesPermission, adminImpersonatingPermission, userImpersonatedPermission to throw UnsupportedOperationException. The realm-level users management/permissions endpoints (GET/PUT /admin/realms/{realm}/users/management/permissions) call these methods. When V2 is active, these endpoints return 500 errors. The V2 implementation should provide these methods or the endpoints should be guarded.

title: FINAL CONFIRMATION: canManage() line 70 accepts VIEW scope — critical privilege escalation
body: This is the most critical finding. GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() at line 70: `return hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE);`. The method is named canManage() and is used to check global manage permission for groups. It accepts the VIEW scope as sufficient. Consequences: (1) GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup (POST /admin/realms/{realm}/groups) calls `auth.groups().requireManage()` which calls canManage() — a view-only admin can create groups. (2) GroupPermissions.canManage(GroupModel) (inherited, line 234) calls `if (canManage()) return true;` — a view-only admin can manage (update, delete) ANY group. (3) GroupResource.deleteGroup calls `this.auth.groups().requireManage(group)` → canManage(group) → canManage() → true — view-only admin can delete any group. (4) GroupResource.updateGroup, addChild, getRoleMappings (manageCheck) — all gated by requireManage(group) → canManage() → true. This is a complete escalation from view to manage for the Groups resource type. The fix is a one-line change: `return hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE);`.

title: canManage() checks VIEW scope instead of MANAGE scope
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (line 70), the fallback permission check is `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, which grants manage rights to any admin holding only the VIEW scope on the Groups resource type. The per-group variant canManage(GroupModel) on line 79 correctly checks only MANAGE, and the interface javadoc for canManage() states it should return true for a permission to MANAGE groups. Consequence: an admin granted only 'view' on all groups (or on the Groups resource type) can create, update, and delete groups, a privilege escalation. The same copy-paste error exists in UserPermissionsV2? No — UserPermissionsV2.canManage(UserModel) correctly uses MANAGE only; only this group-level canManage() is wrong.

title: hasPermission looks up group resource by raw group id as resource name, but V2 resources are keyed differently
body: GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission(String groupId, ...) does `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` (line 141). In the V2 schema (AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource), per-group resources are created with the group id as the resource *name* via resolveGroup(), so findByName(server, groupId) is consistent with that. However, getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() (line 121-125) iterates resources of type GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE and calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` — passing the resource's internal store id, not the group id that is used as the resource name. findByName(server, resource.getId()) will therefore not find the resource, the code falls back to the all-groups resource, and the per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS evaluation is performed against the wrong resource. Consequence: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns incorrect group id sets (it adds resource.getId() — the authz resource id, not the group id — to the returned set), which UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource then pass to session.users().searchForUserStream via UserModel.GROUPS, filtering users by group ids that do not match actual group ids. This breaks fine-grained user visibility for admins with only group-scoped view-members permissions and returns wrong/empty user lists.

title: Null resource from getResourceTypeResource is dereferenced without a null check
body: In hasPermission(), when the per-group resource is not found, the code calls `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` (line 144) and immediately calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` on line 147 without checking whether resource is null. getResourceTypeResource returns null when the resource type resource does not exist (e.g., admin permissions enabled but schema not initialized, or supportsAuthorizationSchema false). A NullPointerException would then be thrown instead of returning false, turning a 'no permission' situation into a 500 error. The analogous code in UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission (line 109-113) has the same pattern, but there the resource lookup is equally unchecked; at minimum GroupPermissionsV2 should null-check before findByResource.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission in V1 base class still queries V1 resource type 'Group' and strips a prefix that no longer matches
body: GroupPermissions.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() (lines 298-320) iterates `resourceStore.findByType(server, "Group", ...)` and extracts group ids via `resource.getName().substring(RESOURCE_NAME_PREFIX.length())` where RESOURCE_NAME_PREFIX = "group.resource.". This is the V1 implementation and remains correct for V1. However, GroupPermissionsV2 overrides this method but its override (GroupPermissionsV2 lines 106-128) iterates type AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE ("Groups") and adds `groupResource.getId()` — the authorization resource id — to the returned set, while callers (UsersResource.searchForUser, BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser, UsersResource.getUsersCount) treat the returned set as group ids (they are passed to session.users().getUsersCount(realm, ..., Set<String> groupIds) and set as UserModel.GROUPS for searchForUserStream, both of which expect group ids). Since V2 group resources are named with the group id (AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup returns group.getId() and getOrCreateResource uses it as the resource name), the override should add `groupResource.getName()` (the group id), not `groupResource.getId()`. As written, user search/count filtering by group membership is broken under V2 for admins without global view-users.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission passes resource id instead of group id (resource name) to hasPermission
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() (lines 121-125), for each group resource found by type, it calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), VIEW_MEMBERS, MANAGE_MEMBERS)`. But hasPermission(String groupId, ...) resolves the resource with `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, i.e., it expects the resource *name*, which for V2 group resources is the group id (see AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource / resolveGroup). Passing the internal resource id means findByName fails, the code falls back to the all-groups resource, and the per-resource permission check is evaluated against the wrong resource — so the set of group ids collected does not reflect per-group view-members permissions. Additionally the collected value `granted.add(groupResource.getId())` adds the authz resource id rather than the group id, which downstream consumers (UsersResource.searchForUser sets UserModel.GROUPS to this set; getUsersCount passes it as group ids) interpret as group ids. Both issues together make group-scoped user visibility incorrect under V2.

title: searchForUser now sets UserModel.GROUPS session attribute even when the admin has global view-users, changing downstream semantics
body: The diff removes the `if (!auth.users().canView())` guard around setting the session attribute UserModel.GROUPS in searchForUser (lines 448-451). Previously the attribute was only set when the admin lacked global view permission. Now `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is always called and, if non-empty, the attribute is set. In GroupPermissions.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission (V1) the method returns an empty set when root.users().canView() is true, so V1 behavior is preserved; but in GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission the same guard exists (line 107). The behavioral change is that toRepresentation's `usersEvaluator.grantIfNoPermission(session.getAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS) != null)` (line 459) now sees a non-null attribute whenever the admin has any group with view-members permission, even if the admin also has global view-users — grantIfNoPermission then grants view on all users in UserPermissions.hasPermission when the Users resource is missing (line 501: `grantIfNoPermission && expectedScopes.contains(MANAGE_SCOPE) && expectedScopes.contains(VIEW_SCOPE)`), which can over-grant. More importantly, setting UserModel.GROUPS unconditionally causes searchForUserStream to filter users by group membership even for admins who have global view-users but happen to have view-members on some group, hiding users not in those groups — a regression in user listing for admins with mixed permissions.

title: canMapRoles and canManageGroupMembership now accept MANAGE scope as sufficient, weakening the permission model
body: The diff changes UserPermissionsV2.canMapRoles(UserModel) from `hasPermission(user, null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES)` to `hasPermission(user, null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE, AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES) || canManageByGroup(user)` (lines 77-83), and similarly canManageGroupMembership from MANAGE_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP only to `MANAGE, MANAGE_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP` (lines 85-92). The interface javadoc (UserPermissionEvaluator lines 137-145 and 153-161) documents that map-roles requires the MAP_ROLES scope (or MANAGE of the user), and manage-group-membership requires MANAGE_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP (or MANAGE of the user). By also accepting the user-level MANAGE scope for these operations, an admin with only 'manage' on a specific user (but not map-roles) can now map roles to that user, and an admin with only 'manage' can manage group membership — exceeding the documented scope semantics. Note the base class UserPermissions.canMapRoles already returns true when canManage(user) is true, so the V2 change makes per-user MANAGE a sufficient condition, which contradicts the FGAP V2 design where map-roles is a distinct scope (the tests in UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.testMapRoles explicitly create a MAP_ROLES-only permission and expect it to be required).

title: Removal of AdminRoles.ADMIN from role checks in V2 user permission methods
body: The diff removes AdminRoles.ADMIN from the hasOneAdminRole checks in canView(UserModel) (line 48: was `AdminRoles.ADMIN, AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS, AdminRoles.VIEW_USERS`, now only MANAGE_USERS/VIEW_USERS) and canManage(UserModel) (line 57: was `ADMIN, MANAGE_USERS`, now only MANAGE_USERS). AdminRoles.ADMIN is the realm-admin composite role; in V1 code paths (e.g., MgmtPermissions.hasOneAdminRole usage elsewhere) realm admins are expected to retain full access. If ADMIN no longer implies manage-users/view-users membership in the V2 evaluation path (hasOneAdminRole checks direct role assignment, and realm-admin is a composite role that may not be expanded depending on implementation), realm admins could lose access to user operations under V2. This needs verification against how hasOneAdminRole resolves composite roles; if composites are resolved it is harmless, otherwise it is an access regression for realm admins.

title: canList() logic change drops VIEW_USERS/MANAGE_USERS as sufficient for listing groups
body: The diff changes GroupPermissions.canList() from `canView() || root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.VIEW_USERS, AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS, AdminRoles.QUERY_GROUPS)` to `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.QUERY_GROUPS) || canView()` (line 148-149). Since canView() itself checks `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS, AdminRoles.VIEW_USERS)` (line 287), the net effect is equivalent for V1. However the reordering changes evaluation cost only; no functional change. Not a defect — but note the interface javadoc for canList() (GroupPermissionEvaluator lines 32-39) says 'at least one of QUERY_GROUPS, MANAGE_USERS or VIEW_USERS', which matches. No issue; disregard.

title: canViewMembers now also accepts MANAGE_MEMBERS scope in V1, broadening member visibility
body: The diff changes GroupPermissions.canViewMembers(GroupModel) from `hasPermission(group, VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE)` to `hasPermission(group, VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE, MANAGE_MEMBERS_SCOPE)` (line 340). This means an admin with only manage-members permission on a group can now view the group's members. The interface javadoc (GroupPermissionEvaluator lines 119-125) documents canViewMembers as true for VIEW_MEMBERS or MANAGE_MEMBERS, so this aligns with the documented contract; however it is a behavioral broadening of the V1 permission model: previously manage-members did not imply view-members. If V1 semantics intentionally separated these (manage-members to add/remove members without listing them), this change leaks the member list to admins who should only be able to modify membership. The same broadening exists in GroupPermissionsV2.canViewMembers (line 86). This should be confirmed as intended; otherwise it is a confidentiality regression for group member listings.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission V1 implementation returns empty set when users().canView() but not when users().canManage()
body: The diff changes the guard in GroupPermissions.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() from `if (root.users().canView() || root.users().canManage()) return Collections.emptySet();` to `if (root.users().canView()) return Collections.emptySet();` (line 299). Since canView() in UserPermissions returns true when the admin has MANAGE_USERS or VIEW_USERS roles (line 298 of UserPermissions), and canManage() is subsumed, the change is behaviorally equivalent for role-based admins. For V1 fine-grained permissions, an admin with a manage permission on Users (but no view permission) would previously get an empty set (meaning 'no group filtering — see all users'), and now would get the group-filtered set. In UsersResource.toRepresentation, `usersEvaluator.grantIfNoPermission(session.getAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS) != null)` — with the attribute now set for manage-only admins, grantIfNoPermission becomes true, and UserPermissions.hasPermission line 501 grants view when the Users resource is missing and both MANAGE and VIEW scopes are expected. This could grant view on all users to a manage-only admin when the Users resource is absent — a subtle over-grant. The change appears intentional for V2 alignment but alters V1 behavior for manage-only admins.

title: getSubGroups filter change removes global canView bypass, but relies on per-group canView which in V2 falls back to all-groups resource
body: The diff changes the subgroup filter in GroupResource.getSubGroups from `.filter(g -> canViewGlobal || auth.groups().canView(g))` to `.filter(auth.groups()::canView)` (lines 176-180), removing the cached `canViewGlobal` boolean. This is functionally equivalent only if canView(g) returns true whenever canView() (global) is true. In GroupPermissions (V1), canView(GroupModel) checks `canView() || canManage()` first (line 255), so equivalence holds. In GroupPermissionsV2, canView(GroupModel) checks admin roles then `hasPermission(group.getId(), VIEW, MANAGE)` — and hasPermission falls back to the all-groups resource when the per-group resource is missing, so a global view permission still grants per-group view. Equivalence holds, but the removal of the cached boolean means canView() is no longer evaluated once; each subgroup now triggers a full permission evaluation (role check + resource lookup + policy evaluation), a performance regression for large group hierarchies. Not a security bug, but a perf concern; more importantly, if any future canView(GroupModel) implementation diverges from canView() the bypass is lost silently.

title: getGroups non-hierarchy path drops cached canViewGlobal, causing per-group full permission evaluation
body: The diff changes the non-hierarchy branch of GroupsResource.getGroups from `.filter(g -> canViewGlobal || groupsEvaluator.canView(g))` (with canViewGlobal cached once) to `.filter(groupsEvaluator::canView)` (lines 113-114). For admins with global view permission, every group now triggers a full canView(g) evaluation (role checks plus, in V2, a resource lookup and policy evaluation per group) instead of a single cached check. For large realms this is a performance regression on the group listing endpoint. The populateHierarchy=true path (GroupUtils.populateGroupHierarchyFromSubGroups) is unaffected.

title: getScope throws NullPointerException when resourceType is not in the schema
body: In AdminPermissionsSchema.getScope (lines 229-244), when supportsAuthorizationSchema is true, the code does `SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType).getScopes()` (line 238) without null-checking the result of get(resourceType). If a caller passes a resourceType that is not one of Clients/Groups/Users (e.g., a legacy or custom type, or null), get() returns null and a NullPointerException is thrown instead of the intended ModelValidationException. The method already validates the scope name against the resource type's scopes, so it clearly expects resourceType to be a schema type, but there is no guard. Callers that pass arbitrary resourceType values (e.g., policy evaluation paths that pass policy.getResourceType()) would get an NPE (500 error) rather than a validation error.

title: getResourceName only handles Users resource type; Groups resources fall through to display name
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName (lines 328-350) resolves a human-readable name only for the USERS resource type (returning 'All users' or the username). For GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE resources it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()` (line 349), which for V2 group resources is typically null/empty since resources are created with only a name (the group id) and no display name (see init(), lines 271-276, which creates ResourceRepresentation without displayName). UI/policy listings that call getResourceName for group resources will show blank or null names instead of the group name. A GROUPS branch resolving the group name via session.groups().getGroupById (mirroring the USERS branch) is missing.

title: registerListener feature check moved outside the listener changes V1 behavior when feature is toggled at runtime
body: The diff moves the `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` check from inside onEvent to the registration site (lines 73-98). Previously the listener was always registered and the feature check was evaluated per event; now the listener is only registered when the feature is enabled at startup. Since Profile features are static for the server lifetime this is behaviorally equivalent in practice, but if the check was previously per-event to support dynamic feature toggling (some Keycloak features can be re-checked), this is a subtle change. More relevant: the indentation of the moved block is inconsistent (the if-body is indented as if still inside a method), a cosmetic defect. Not a functional bug; flagging only because the restructure adds no value and obscures the diff.

title: canMapRole now requires MANAGE_USERS role directly instead of canManageDefault(), changing V1 fine-grained behavior
body: The diff changes RolePermissions.canMapRole from `if (root.users().canManageDefault()) return checkAdminRoles(role);` to `if (root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS)) return checkAdminRoles(role);` (line 302). canManageDefault() was exactly `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS)` (removed from UserPermissions in this same PR), so for role-based admins the behavior is identical. However, in V1 fine-grained authz, an admin could have the 'manage' scope permission on the Users resource (via UserPermissions.canManage() returning true through hasPermission(MANAGE_SCOPE)) without holding the MANAGE_USERS role; previously canMapRole's first check used canManageDefault() (role only), so this is equivalent. But other V1 paths relied on users().canManage() (which includes fine-grained permissions) for role mapping; the new check bypasses fine-grained user permissions entirely, so an admin granted manage-users via FGAP V1 permissions (not the role) can no longer map roles. This is a functional regression for V1 FGAP deployments unless V2 is enabled (MgmtPermissionsV2 path). The same pattern appears in GroupPermissions.canManage()/canView() where canManageDefault/canViewDefault were replaced by direct role checks — those are in the V1 class GroupPermissions, so V1 fine-grained group permissions (manage/view scope on group resources) are still checked via hasPermission in canManage(GroupModel)/canView(GroupModel), but the global canManage()/canView() no longer consider FGAP permissions, affecting requireManage()/requireView() global checks (e.g., GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup calls auth.groups().requireManage()).

title: V1 GroupPermissions.canManage()/canView() no longer consider fine-grained group permissions, breaking V1 FGAP global group operations
body: The diff replaces GroupPermissions.canManage() from `root.users().canManageDefault()` to `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS)` (line 274-276) and canView() from `root.users().canViewDefault()` to `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS, AdminRoles.VIEW_USERS)` (line 286-288). In V1 fine-grained admin permissions (ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature, MgmtPermissions/GroupPermissions path), an admin could be granted the 'manage' or 'view' scope on a group resource (via GroupPermissions.initialize/hasPermission) without holding realm-management roles. The per-group methods canManage(GroupModel)/canView(GroupModel) still check hasPermission, but the global canManage()/canView() — used by requireManage()/requireView() for realm-wide operations such as GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup (auth.groups().requireManage()) and by canList() — now ignore FGAP permissions entirely. Consequence: in V1 FGAP deployments, admins who previously could create top-level groups via a view/manage permission on the Groups resource (or via the old users().canManageDefault() semantics) are now denied; conversely the change removes the V1 FGAP evaluation from these global checks. This is a behavioral/API break for V1 fine-grained authorization unless the intent is that V1 group permissions are only per-group. The same replacement was done in UserPermissions.canManage()/canView() (lines 233-243, 297-307) where the fine-grained hasPermission fallback is retained, so the group change is inconsistent with the user change.

title: canViewByGroup changed from getGroupsWithViewPermission(group) to canViewMembers(group), altering V1 semantics
body: The diff changes UserPermissions.canViewByGroup from `evaluateHierarchy(user, (group) -> root.groups().getGroupsWithViewPermission(group))` to `evaluateHierarchy(user, root.groups()::canViewMembers)` (line 587-590). The old V1 method getGroupsWithViewPermission(GroupModel) (removed from the interface) returned true when `root.users().canView() || root.users().canManage()` OR the admin had VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permission on the group. The new canViewMembers(GroupModel) in GroupPermissions returns true when `root.users().canView()` OR hasPermission(group, VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE, MANAGE_MEMBERS_SCOPE) (line 330-341). The difference: the old check also returned true when root.users().canManage() (manage-users role or manage permission) even without view permission on the group; the new canViewMembers only checks users().canView(). However, canView(UserModel) in UserPermissions is `canView() || canViewByGroup(user)`, and canView() already covers MANAGE_USERS/VIEW_USERS roles and the manage/view scopes, so for role-based admins the outcome is the same. For V1 FGAP admins with only a 'manage' permission on Users (not view), the old code granted view-by-group via users().canManage(); the new code does not (canViewMembers requires users().canView()). This narrows V1 FGAP behavior: a manage-only admin can no longer see users through group membership. Whether this is intended is unclear; it is a behavioral change to V1 permission evaluation.

title: searchForUser sets UserModel.GROUPS session attribute unconditionally, affecting brute-force user listing for admins with global view
body: The diff removes the `if (!auth.users().canView())` guard in BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser (lines 147-150), so `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is always called and UserModel.GROUPS is set whenever the set is non-empty. For an admin with global view-users plus view-members on some group, the session attribute is now set, causing searchForUserStream to filter users by group membership and hiding users outside those groups from the brute-force user search — a regression for admins who should see all users. Additionally, toRepresentation's `usersEvaluator.grantIfNoPermission(session.getAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS) != null)` (line 159) now evaluates true for such admins, which in UserPermissions.hasPermission (line 501) grants view on all users when the Users resource is missing — over-granting. The same unconditional pattern was introduced in UsersResource.searchForUser.

title: Test cleanup in @BeforeEach uses response after try-with-resources closes it
body: In GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.onBefore (lines 71-79), the code does `try (Response response = realm.admin().groups().add(topGroup)) { ... topGroup.setId(ApiUtil.handleCreatedResponse(response)); ... }`. ApiUtil.handleCreatedResponse now uses try-with-resources internally (per the ApiUtil change), closing the response; the outer try-with-resources then closes it again (harmless), but more importantly the assertion and id extraction happen inside the outer try block before the outer close — this is fine. However, the pattern of calling handleCreatedResponse (which closes the response) inside an outer try-with-resources is redundant and confusing; if handleCreatedResponse's internal close throws or the outer close is reached after the inner close, behavior is still safe (Response.close is idempotent). Not a functional bug; flagging as a test code smell. More significant: the test class lacks a test verifying that an admin with only view-members on a group cannot list groups (negative case for group listing), and lacks a test for manage-membership on a subgroup granting membership management on parent/child hierarchies — coverage gaps for the new Groups resource type scopes.

title: testManageAllGroups creates a group without name, expecting FORBIDDEN, but the assertion only checks status code inside try-with-resources
body: In testManageAllGroups (lines 141-143), `realmAdminClient.realm(realm.getName()).groups().add(new GroupRepresentation())` sends a group with no name. The expected FORBIDDEN is asserted, but the test does not verify that no group was actually created (a 403 could theoretically be returned after partial creation, though unlikely). More importantly, the test relies on the permission check happening before validation; if the implementation order changes (validation before authz), the test would get 400 instead of 403 and fail — a brittle test. Similarly testManageGroup line 207 updates topGroup with myGroup representation (different id) expecting ForbiddenException; this tests that per-group manage on myGroup does not grant manage on topGroup, which is good coverage. The broader gap: no test verifies that getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns group ids (not resource ids) — the bug identified in GroupPermissionsV2 would not be caught by these tests because testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers only checks user search results, and if the group id set were wrong the search would return empty and the test would fail — actually it would catch it. OK, this is adequate; downgrading to a note about brittle status-code-only assertions.

title: GroupPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException for management methods still called from V1 code paths
body: GroupPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException for isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, viewMembersPermission, manageMembersPermission, manageMembershipPermission, viewPermission, managePermission, resource, and getPermissions (lines 168-210). However, GroupResource.getManagementPermissions (line 321-330) and setManagementPermissionsEnabled (line 354-365) call `AdminPermissions.management(session, realm)` which returns MgmtPermissionsV2 when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, and then call permissions.groups().isPermissionsEnabled(group) / setPermissionsEnabled / resource / getPermissions. These endpoints are guarded by `ProfileHelper.requireFeature(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` (V1 feature), not V2 — so if both features are enabled (or V2 enabled while the V1-guarded endpoint is invoked), the call reaches GroupPermissionsV2 and throws UnsupportedOperationException, producing a 500 error on GET/PUT /admin/realms/{realm}/groups/{id}/management/permissions. Either the endpoints need a V2 guard/feature check, or GroupPermissionsV2 must implement these methods (e.g., returning a V2-appropriate ManagementPermissionReference). This is a runtime API break for the group management-permissions endpoint under V2.

title: UserPermissionsV2.isImpersonatable throws UnsupportedOperationException but is called from V1 code paths
body: UserPermissionsV2.isImpersonatable(UserModel, ClientModel) and isImpersonatable(UserModel) throw UnsupportedOperationException (lines 142-149). The base class UserPermissions.canImpersonate(UserModel, ClientModel) (line 356-362) calls `canImpersonate()` then `isImpersonatable(user, requester)`, and canClientImpersonate (line 340-353) calls `canImpersonate(context) && isImpersonatable(user)`. In V2, canImpersonate(UserModel, ClientModel) is overridden (line 65-74) and does not call isImpersonatable, and canClientImpersonate is overridden to delegate to canImpersonate(user, client) (line 137-139). However, any other caller of isImpersonatable (e.g., UserResource impersonation endpoints that check isImpersonatable directly, or the deprecated interface method used elsewhere) will hit UnsupportedOperationException under V2. The interface UserPermissionEvaluator still declares isImpersonatable as @Deprecated but not removed; if any V2-active code path (e.g., UserResource.impersonate) calls auth.users().isImpersonatable(...), it will throw. This should be verified; if UserResource only uses canImpersonate, the risk is limited to external/other callers, but the UnsupportedOperationException pattern for interface methods that remain on the public evaluator interface is fragile.

title: canView() and canManage() fall back to all-groups resource but do not check per-resource permission existence correctly when resource is null
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission, when groupId is null (global checks from canView()/canManage()), resource is set to null initially (line 141: `groupId == null ? null : ...`), then the `if (resource == null)` block fetches the all-groups resource type resource and checks `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()`. If getResourceTypeResource returns null (schema not initialized), findByResource(server, null) behavior is undefined/likely NPE. Also, for the global canView()/canManage() path, the check `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()` returns false (deny) when there are no policies on the all-groups resource — correct — but when groupId is null and the all-groups resource exists with policies, evaluation proceeds on the all-groups resource, which is correct. The null-resource NPE risk (line 147) applies to both global and per-group paths when the schema resource is missing. This is the same finding as the earlier NPE note but specifically for the global canView/canManage path where groupId is null and the resource type resource may not exist if init() was not called.

title: getOrCreateResource throws generic ModelException('No scopes found.') without identifying the missing scope
body: In AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource (lines 123-127), when a scope defined in the resource type is not found in the scope store, the code throws `new ModelException("No scopes found.")` without including the scope name or resource type. This makes diagnosing initialization/ordering problems (e.g., scopes not yet created when a per-group resource is being created) difficult in logs. The message should include the scope name and resource type, similar to the validation messages in getScope (lines 234, 239). Low severity operational/diagnosability issue.

title: MgmtPermissionsV2.groups() returns GroupPermissions (declared type) but field is GroupPermissionsV2 — type mismatch with base class contract
body: MgmtPermissionsV2 overrides `public GroupPermissions groups()` (line 58) with return type GroupPermissions (the V1 class), while the field is GroupPermissionsV2 and the instance created is GroupPermissionsV2. The base class MgmtPermissions.groups() presumably returns GroupPermissions; the override narrows the instance but not the declared type. This compiles because GroupPermissionsV2 extends GroupPermissions, but callers typed against MgmtPermissions.groups() get the V1 type and cannot access V2-specific behavior without casting. More importantly, the override signature `public GroupPermissions groups()` matches the base, so it is a valid override; the concern is only API clarity. However, if the base class method is declared to return the interface GroupPermissionEvaluator or a different type, this could be a compile issue — since the PR compiles, it is fine. Downgrading to a note: the declared return type should ideally be GroupPermissionEvaluator or GroupPermissionsV2 for clarity, but this is a style/API-design preference, not a bug. Disregard as a finding per instructions (style preference).

title: Fields changed from private to protected for V2 subclassing — acceptable but widens encapsulation
body: The diff changes GroupPermissions fields root, resourceStore, policyStore from private to protected (lines 55-58) to allow GroupPermissionsV2 access. This is a common pattern but widens the class's encapsulation boundary; since GroupPermissionsV2 is in the same package, package-private would suffice. Not a defect; disregard per instructions (style preference).

title: Indentation change in getUsers else-if branch is inconsistent (cosmetic but obscures diff)
body: The diff shows the `} else if (last != null || ...)` block in getUsers (lines 298-336) re-indented with extra spaces (the whole block shifted right by 4 spaces relative to the surrounding code), while the logic is unchanged. This is a formatting inconsistency introduced by the diff (likely a merge artifact) that makes the code harder to read and the diff noisier. Not a functional issue; flagging as a doc_defect/cleanup item since it affects readability of the changed file.

title: handleCreatedResponse try-with-resources closes response before caller can use it in outer try-with-resources, causing double-close and potential confusion
body: ApiUtil.handleCreatedResponse now wraps its body in try-with-resources (lines 8-14), closing the Response before returning the id. Callers like GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.onBefore (line 73-77) and UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest (line 146) use the pattern `try (Response response = ...create(...)) { String id = ApiUtil.handleCreatedResponse(response); ... }` — the response is closed inside handleCreatedResponse, then the outer try-with-resources closes it again. Response.close() is idempotent in RESTEasy, so no resource leak, but the pattern is misleading: callers that rely on the response remaining open after handleCreatedResponse (e.g., reading the entity) would break. The refactor changes the method's contract (it now consumes/closes the response) without updating the method name or javadoc, and without updating all callers to remove their now-redundant outer try-with-resources. This is a test-framework API contract change that should be documented or the callers simplified.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns empty set when users().canView() is true, but callers use the set to decide grantIfNoPermission — combined with unconditional attribute setting this can grant view on all users
body: GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission (line 107) returns an empty set when root.users().canView() is true. In UsersResource.searchForUser (line 448-451), the set is fetched unconditionally (the `if (!auth.users().canView())` guard was removed) and `if (!groupIds.isEmpty()) session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)`. When the admin has global view-users, getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns empty, so the attribute is not set — correct. But when the admin does NOT have global view-users and has view-members on some groups, the set is non-empty and the attribute is set; then toRepresentation calls `usersEvaluator.grantIfNoPermission(session.getAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS) != null)` (line 459), setting grantIfNoPermission=true. In UserPermissions.hasPermission (line 501), when the Users resource is missing, `grantIfNoPermission && expectedScopes.contains(MANAGE_SCOPE) && expectedScopes.contains(VIEW_SCOPE)` grants view. This is the intended V1 fallback behavior. However, under V2, UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission (line 94-133) does NOT consult grantIfNoPermission at all — it returns false when the resource is missing (after the all-users fallback check). So the grantIfNoPermission mechanism is V1-only, and the unconditional attribute setting in searchForUser combined with V2's getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returning resource ids (not group ids, per earlier finding) means the UserModel.GROUPS filter uses wrong ids. The net effect under V2: user search filtering by group membership is broken (wrong ids), and the grantIfNoPermission flag is set but ignored by V2 evaluation — inconsistent state.

title: canView(GroupModel) passes group.getId() as resource name, but if the group resource was not created yet, falls back to all-groups — a group with no resource inherits all-groups permissions (intended), but a group with a resource that has no policies gets denied even if all-groups grants view (policy evaluation on wrong resource)
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.canView(GroupModel) (line 56-62), hasPermission(group.getId(), VIEW, MANAGE) is called. In hasPermission (line 141), `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` looks up the per-group resource by name (group id). If found, evaluation proceeds on that resource only — the all-groups fallback is NOT consulted. This means if an admin has a view permission on all-groups (the Groups resource type resource) but the specific group has its own resource (created when a per-group permission was defined) with no policies granting view, canView(group) returns false even though the all-groups permission should apply (resource-type permissions are meant to apply to all resources of that type unless overridden). In the V2 FGAP model (per AdminPermissionsSchema and UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission), when a per-resource permission exists, evaluation is on that resource; the all-groups resource is only a fallback when no per-resource exists. This matches UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission behavior (line 105-114), so it is consistent with the V2 design. However, the semantics depend on whether per-group resources are auto-created: AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates a per-group resource when a permission references it. If a permission is created for group A (creating resource A), and another permission exists on all-groups granting view, then for group B (no resource), the all-groups fallback applies — correct. For group A, only resource A's policies apply — the all-groups permission does NOT cascade. This is the standard FGAP V2 semantics (resource-type permissions apply to the type resource; per-resource permissions override). So this is consistent; not a bug. Disregard.

title: canList() reordering changes short-circuit evaluation order — canView() now evaluated after role check, no functional change but javadoc mismatch
body: The diff changes canList() from `canView() || root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.VIEW_USERS, AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS, AdminRoles.QUERY_GROUPS)` to `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.QUERY_GROUPS) || canView()` (line 148-149). Functionally equivalent (both are OR of the same conditions since canView() covers MANAGE_USERS/VIEW_USERS). The interface javadoc (GroupPermissionEvaluator lines 32-39) lists QUERY_GROUPS, MANAGE_USERS, VIEW_USERS — consistent. No issue; disregard.

title: getOrCreateResource switch statement throws IllegalStateException for unknown resource types, but callers may pass null resourceType
body: The new switch statement in getOrCreateResource (lines 107-112) uses `switch (resourceType)` with cases for the three known types and a default that throws IllegalStateException. If resourceType is null, a NullPointerException is thrown (switch on null) rather than the IllegalStateException with a meaningful message. The previous code used if/else with USERS.getType().equals(resourceType) which was null-safe. Callers that pass null resourceType (e.g., when creating a permission without a resource type) would now get an NPE instead of a clear error. The method is called from policy/permission creation paths where resourceType may be optional for non-schema resource servers; supportsAuthorizationSchema guards the schema path, but within the schema path a null resourceType should produce a validation error, not an NPE.

title: English reference file path is computed with a regex that does not match real locale suffixes, causing the verifier to fail or compare against the wrong file
body: The English bundle path is derived with `file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll("resources-community", "resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")`. The character class `[a-zA-Z-_]` does not include digits, so locale suffixes containing digits such as `_zh_CN`, `_zh_TW`, `_pt_BR` are not matched and the path is left unchanged (pointing at the translated file itself). Additionally, for files already named `messages_en.properties` the regex matches `_en` and rewrites it to `_en.properties` (harmless), but for any file whose locale suffix contains a digit the verifier will read the translated file as the 'English' source. Consequence: the HTML policy decision (`containsHtml(englishValue)`) is made against the translated value instead of the English source, so translations can be wrongly allowed or wrongly rejected, and the anchor-tag comparison compares a translation against itself. The regex should be something like `_[a-zA-Z]{2}(_[A-Za-z0-9]+)?\\.properties` or, more robustly, the locale should be parsed from the file name.

title: Missing English properties file causes an uncaught RuntimeException instead of a proper verification message
body: When the computed English file does not exist (which, per the path bug above, happens for every locale whose suffix contains digits, and also for any key present only in a translation), `new FileInputStream(englishFile)` throws FileNotFoundException which is wrapped in a `RuntimeException` and propagates out of `verify()`. `verify()` only catches `IOException` around `Files.readString`, so this RuntimeException escapes the declared `MojoExecutionException` contract and will crash the build with a stack trace rather than reporting a verification problem. The English bundle load should tolerate a missing file (treat as empty bundle, as `getEnglishValue` already does for missing keys) or report a proper message.

title: Anchor sanitization removes the English anchor from the translated value at the wrong position and can loop forever / corrupt the value
body: `santizeAnchors` iterates over anchors in the translated value and, for each match, calls `value.replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(englishMatcher.group()), "")`. `replaceFirst` removes the first occurrence of the English anchor text anywhere in the translated string, not the occurrence at the translated matcher's position. If the translated value contains the same anchor text earlier (e.g. repeated links, or text identical to the tag), the wrong occurrence is removed and the remaining anchors shift, so subsequent iterations compare mismatched anchors and report false 'Didn't find anchor tag' errors. It also mutates `value` while iterating with a Matcher created from the original string, which can cause the loop to never terminate or to skip anchors when the removal shortens the string (Matcher indices become stale). The method should rebuild the string by removing the exact matched region (e.g. using `matcher.start()/end()` with a StringBuilder) instead of `replaceFirst` on the whole value.

title: HTML detection regex only matches lowercase single-word tags, so uppercase or attribute-bearing tags in the English source disable HTML allowance for translations
body:
`HTML_TAGS = Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>")` is used by `containsHtml` to decide whether the English source contains HTML and therefore whether `POLICY_SOME_HTML` (allowing br/p/strong/b) is applied to the translation. The pattern requires the tag name to start with a lowercase letter and contain only lowercase letters, so English values containing uppercase tags (`
`, `

`), self-closing or attribute forms like `
` (actually matched by `[^>]*` after `br`, but `
` is not), or tags with uppercase names will be classified as 'no HTML'. A translation that legitimately mirrors an uppercase English tag (e.g. `
`) would then be sanitized with `POLICY_NO_HTML`, stripping the tag and producing a false 'Illegal HTML' failure. The pattern should be case-insensitive (`Pattern.CASE_INSENSITIVE`) and should match the tags actually allowed by the policy.

title: HTML policy allows only br/p/strong/b but the verifier's anchor handling strips <a> tags before sanitization, so the check does not actually validate that translations only use the allowed elements
body: `POLICY_SOME_HTML` allows only `br`, `p`, `strong`, `b`, yet `santizeAnchors` removes anchor tags from the translated value before `policy.sanitize(value)` runs (line 88 runs before line 92). This means an `<a href="javascript:...">` or any other anchor in a translation is never seen by the sanitizer: it is either silently removed (when it matches the English anchor) or reported only as 'Didn't find anchor tag' (when it doesn't). The sanitizer therefore never validates the attributes of anchors that translations are allowed to contain (email templates legitimately contain `<a href="{0}">`), and a translation containing a malicious anchor that happens to textually match the English anchor is accepted without any attribute checking. The anchor handling should instead let the sanitizer process the value with a policy that allows `a` with safe URL schemes (e.g. `allowAttributes("href").matching(...)` on the policy), and only afterwards compare the surviving anchors with the English ones.

title: Unconditional unescapeHtml4 on the sanitized value corrupts legitimate HTML entities in message values
body: After sanitizing, the code unconditionally applies `StringEscapeUtils.unescapeHtml4(sanitized)` (line 95) and also unescapes the original value in `normalizeValue` (line 130). The OWASP sanitizer escapes text content (e.g. `&` becomes `&`, `'` becomes `'`), and the comparison then unescapes both sides. However, unescaping the sanitized output also unescapes entities that were present verbatim in the source value and were intentionally double-escaped by the sanitizer, and it will turn a literal `&amp;` in the source into `&` on both sides, masking real differences. More importantly, a value that legitimately contains the text `<script>` (escaped HTML shown to the user) is unescaped to `<script>` on the value side, then re-sanitized... actually the sanitize happens before unescape, so the unescape happens after sanitize and can reintroduce `<` characters into `sanitized` that are then compared against the unescaped original; any value whose sanitized form differs only by entity encoding will be compared after both sides are unescaped, which can both hide real differences (a translation that adds `<` where English has `<`) and create false positives. The unescape should only be applied to compensate for the sanitizer's own escaping of characters that were not entities in the source, not as a blanket unescape of the whole string.

title: templateHelp normalization regex only strips uppercase claim names, leaving lowercase or mixed-case placeholders to fail verification
body: `normalizeValue` special-cases the key `templateHelp` with `value.replaceAll("CLAIM\\.<[A-Z]*>", "")`. The comment says it allows `CLAIM.<NAME>`, but the regex only matches uppercase letters. A translation using `CLAIM.<name>` or `CLAIM.<sub>` (lowercase claim names are common, e.g. the zh_CN admin message references `${CLAIM.sub}`) will not be stripped, the `<name>` will be treated as an HTML tag by the sanitizer, and the verifier will report a false 'Illegal HTML' error. The regex should be case-insensitive or match any non-`>` characters: `CLAIM\\.<[^>]*>`.

title: Choice-format normalization regex does not handle nested braces, breaking verification of messages with nested choice/format patterns
body: For keys starting with `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit` and `error-invalid-multivalued-size`, the code replaces `\{[0-9]+,choice,[^}]*}` with `...`. The character class `[^}]*` stops at the first `}`, so a choice pattern containing a nested brace (e.g. `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<{2,number}}` or the new `error-invalid-multivalued-size` value `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` combined with other placeholders on the same line) will only be partially replaced, leaving a dangling `{` or `}` that the sanitizer treats as text and that will mismatch the sanitized output, producing false 'Illegal HTML' reports. The replacement should consume balanced braces or the whole `{n,choice,...}` construct including nested groups.

title: Tests for HTML verification rely on an English fixture that the buggy path computation never actually locates, so the tests do not exercise the intended code path
body: The new tests load fixtures from the classpath (e.g. `illegalHtmlTag_en.properties`, `noHtml_de.properties` + `noHtml_en.properties`). `VerifyMessageProperties` computes the English file path from the translated file's absolute path using `replaceAll("resources-community", "resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")`. The test resources live under `target/test-classes` (or `src/test/resources`), which contains neither `resources-community` nor a `resources` directory, so for `noHtml_de.properties` the computed 'English' path is `.../noHtml_en.properties` only if the regex matches `_de` — it does match `_de`, so the fixture works by accident. But the tests never cover a locale with digits (e.g. `zh_CN`), never cover a file in a `resources-community` tree, and never cover the case where the English file is missing. As a result the path-computation bug (finding #1) and the missing-file crash (finding #2) are not caught. Tests should include a fixture pair with a digit-containing locale and a test for a translation whose English file does not exist.

title: Account UI error-invalid-multivalued-size changed from {{0}}/{{1}}/{{2}} (i18next interpolation) to {0}/{1}/{2} with a MessageFormat choice pattern, which i18next will not interpolate correctly

With the new value, i18next will render the literal text `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` instead of the attribute name and counts, so users will see a broken error message. The account UI file should keep the i18next `{{0}}`/`{{1}}`/`{{2}}` syntax (and plural handling via i18next's own `_one`/`_other` suffixes if needed), not the Java MessageFormat syntax used by the FreeMarker themes.

title: Chinese admin templateHelp still contains a full-width space inside `<NAME >` that the verifier's templateHelp normalization does not strip

However, the verifier's regex remains ASCII-only; any future translation using lowercase claim names or non-ASCII characters inside `CLAIM.<...>` will false-positive. This is a robustness gap in the verifier (see related finding on the templateHelp regex).

title: owasp-java-html-sanitizer 20240325.1 is used without a stated policy for URL schemes on allowed elements; combined with the anchor-stripping logic this leaves anchor validation entirely to string comparison
body: The PR adds `com.googlecode.owasp-java-html-sanitizer:owasp-java-html-sanitizer:20240325.1` to verify message HTML. The `POLICY_SOME_HTML` policy allows `br`, `p`, `strong`, `b` with no attributes and no URL policy, and `POLICY_NO_HTML` allows nothing. Because `santizeAnchors` removes all `<a>` tags from the value before sanitization (see the anchor finding), the sanitizer never gets the chance to validate `href` values (e.g. reject `javascript:` URLs) in translations. The version 20240325.1 is recent enough, but the design means the sanitizer dependency is effectively only used to strip non-whitelisted tags, and all anchor safety relies on exact string equality with the English source. If a translation's anchor matches the English anchor textually, its `href` is never checked by the sanitizer. The policy should allow `a` with `href` restricted to safe schemes (e.g. `allowAttributes("href").matching(uris().withSchemes("http","https","mailto"))`) and the anchor comparison should happen after sanitization.

title: Difference-highlighting substring logic can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when one string is a prefix of the other
body: When `sanitized` and `value` differ, the code computes `start` as the length of the common prefix and `end` as the length of the common suffix, then calls `value.substring(start, value.length() - end)` and `sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end)`. If one string is a strict prefix of the other (e.g. value = 'abc', sanitized = 'abcd'), then start = 3 and end = 0, and `value.substring(3, 3)` is fine, but if the strings share both a prefix and a suffix that overlap (e.g. value = 'aa', sanitized = 'a'), start can exceed `value.length() - end`, causing `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` (begin > end). Example: value = 'aba', sanitized = 'aa': common prefix 'a' (start=1), common suffix 'a' (end=1), then `value.substring(1, 3-1=2)` = 'b' and `sanitized.substring(1, 2-1=1)` → begin 1 > end 1 is OK (empty), but value='aa', sanitized='a': start=1, end=1, `sanitized.substring(1, 1-1=0)` → begin 1 > end 0 → StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. The verifier would crash with an unhelpful exception instead of reporting the illegal HTML. The code should clamp `start`/`end` so that `start + end <= min(value.length(), sanitized.length())`.

title: Email RTL style stripping uses a hardcoded English attribute string that will not match translations that reorder or translate the style attribute
body: `normalizeValue` strips ` style="direction: rtl;"` (with an English attribute name and value) from values in files whose path contains 'email'. The OWASP sanitizer would otherwise escape or strip the `style` attribute (it is not allowed by either policy), causing a false 'Illegal HTML' report for RTL email templates. However, the strip is a literal string match: any translation that writes the attribute differently (e.g. `style='direction: rtl;'`, `style="direction:rtl;"`, or with extra spaces) will not be stripped and will false-positive. More importantly, the check `file.getAbsolutePath().contains("email")` is a heuristic on the path; the same RTL style may legitimately appear in non-email themes. The normalization should use a regex tolerant of quoting/spacing, or better, the policy should allow the `style` attribute with a strict `direction: rtl` value matcher for email templates.

title: PolicyFactory instances are non-static mutable-looking fields initialized inline; should be static final
body: `POLICY_SOME_HTML` and `POLICY_NO_HTML` are declared as instance fields (`PolicyFactory POLICY_SOME_HTML = ...`) without `static` or `final`. They are immutable and thread-safe, and re-creating them per `VerifyMessageProperties` instance is wasteful. They should be `private static final`. This is a minor style/performance point, not a correctness bug.

title: Czech error-invalid-multivalued-size choice pattern uses an incomplete set of plural forms
body: The Czech login file ends with `error-invalid-multivalued-size=Atribut {0} musí mít nejméně {1} {1,choice,0#hodnot|1#hodnotu|1<hodnoty|4<hodnot} a nejvíce {2} {2,choice,0#hodnot|1#hodnotu|1<hodnoty|4<hodnot}.` Czech has three plural forms (1 → hodnota/hodnotu, 2-4 → hodnoty, 0/5+ → hodnot). The choice pattern `0#hodnot|1#hodnotu|1<hodnoty|4<hodnot` maps: 0 → 'hodnot', 1 → 'hodnotu', 2-4 → 'hodnoty', 5+ → 'hodnot'. This is actually a reasonable Czech plural mapping (0 and 5+ use genitive plural 'hodnot', 1 uses accusative singular 'hodnotu', 2-4 use nominative plural 'hodnoty'). However, the English source uses `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` — the choice is on `{2}` (the maximum), not `{1}` (the minimum). The Czech translation attaches a choice to `{1}` as well, which diverges from the English structure and will produce grammatically correct but structurally different output. The Czech value should mirror the English: `Atribut {0} musí mít nejméně {1} a nejvíce {2} {2,choice,0#hodnot|1#hodnotu|1<hodnoty|4<hodnot}.` (choice only on `{2}`).

title: changedAnchor test fixture has no trailing newline and the English fixture does, which may affect PropertyResourceBundle parsing edge cases but is not itself a defect; however the test only covers a changed href, not a changed tag structure
body: The `changedAnchor_de.properties` fixture ends without a newline (`\ No newline at end of file`) while `changedAnchor_en.properties` also has no trailing newline. The test `verifyNoChangedAnchors` checks that a translation with `<a href="http://malicious.com">` against an English `<a href="http://example.com">` produces 'Didn't find anchor tag'. This covers the changed-href case. It does not cover: (a) a translation with an extra anchor not present in English, (b) a translation missing an anchor present in English, (c) a translation with a self-closing or differently-structured anchor. The `santizeAnchors` loop breaks on the first mismatch, so case (a) with multiple anchors where the first matches but the second doesn't is partially covered, but case (b) (missing anchor) is not tested at all — a translation that drops an anchor entirely will pass `santizeAnchors` silently (the while loop simply doesn't execute for the missing anchor) and then the sanitizer will not complain because there is no extra HTML. A missing anchor in a translation is a real defect (broken link) that the verifier should catch but currently does not. This is a functional gap in the new verifier.

title: Verifier does not detect translations that omit an anchor tag present in the English source
body: `santizeAnchors` only iterates over anchors found in the *translated* value (`matcher = ANCHOR_PATTERN.matcher(value)`) and checks each against the English anchors. If a translation simply omits an `<a>` tag that exists in the English source (e.g. the English has two links and the translation has only one), the loop runs once for the single translated anchor, matches it against the first English anchor, removes it, and returns without ever noticing that the second English anchor has no counterpart. The subsequent sanitization also passes because there is no extra HTML in the translation. The result is a silently broken translation (missing link) that the verifier — whose stated purpose is to catch changed anchors — does not report. The method should also iterate over the English anchors and verify each has a matching counterpart in the translation (i.e. compare counts and sequences in both directions).
