Existing columns may have labels 'A', 'B', etc. The new column gets no label. When applied, the labels are not reassigned (handleApply just converts to JSON). This means the new column has an empty label in the URL/state, which may cause issues downstream (e.g., chart labels, analytics). Labels should be reassigned sequentially after add/delete operations.

title: FeedbackSummary rendered inside SummaryListContainer but the container has no defined height — layout may collapse
body: The FeedbackSummary component is placed inside SummaryListContainer (a flex column with gap) above the Container (FluidHeight) that wraps FeedbackList. The SummaryListContainer has style={{gridArea: 'list'}}. The grid row for 'list' is '1fr' (from grid-template-rows: max-content 1fr). The SummaryListContainer is a flex column containing FeedbackSummary (which may render null, a Placeholder, or the summary box) and Container (FluidHeight). If FeedbackSummary renders null (feature disabled, error, or too few feedbacks), the SummaryListContainer just contains the Container. If it renders content, the summary box appears above the list. The layout should work, but the SummaryListContainer doesn't have overflow handling — if the summary is very long (55 words max per the prompt), it could push the list down. Minor layout concern.

title: referrer added to getAlertsUrl but not to exploreUrl — inconsistent analytics tracking
body: The diff adds referrer to getAlertsUrl({..., referrer}) but the exploreUrl (getExploreUrl) already had referrer passed (it was in the original code at line 56). So the change adds referrer to the alert URL generation. This is correct — the alert creation URL now includes the referrer for analytics. The exploreUrl already had it. Not a bug, just confirming the change is intentional and correct.

title: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES filtering only applied when searchQuery is non-empty — hidden attributes shown when search is empty
body: The sortedAndFilteredAttributes useMemo: if (!searchQuery.trim()) return sorted; — returns ALL sorted attributes without filtering HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES when there's no search query. The HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES filter (!HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(attribute.name)) is only applied in the search branch. This means when the search box is empty (the default state), hidden attributes (is_segment, project_id, received) ARE displayed. They are only hidden when the user types a search query. This is backwards — hidden attributes should always be hidden, regardless of search state. The filter should be applied unconditionally, with the search filter applied additionally when searchQuery is non-empty.

title: getTraceAttributesTreeActions uses findSpanAttributeValue(attributes, 'project_id') but project_id is in HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES
body: The component hides 'project_id' from display (HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES) but still uses findSpanAttributeValue(attributes, 'project_id') to get project IDs for getTraceAttributesTreeActions. This is fine — the attribute is hidden from the UI but still used internally for actions. Not a bug, just noting the attribute is used despite being hidden.

title: PercentInput disabled when bulk edit enabled but not active — but onBlur still fires onBulkEditChange(false)
body: The PercentInput is disabled when !hasAccess || (isBulkEditEnabled && !isBulkEditActive). When disabled, the input can't be focused or blurred normally, so onBlur={() => onBulkEditChange?.(false)} won't fire from user interaction. However, if the input was active (isBulkEditActive=true) and then isBulkEditActive becomes false (e.g., parent state change), the input becomes disabled while focused — the blur event may or may not fire depending on browser behavior. If it doesn't fire, onBulkEditChange(false) is never called, leaving the parent in a stale bulk-edit-active state. The disabled logic and blur handler interaction is fragile.

title: Enter key handler only works when isBulkEditActive — but input may not be in bulk edit mode
body: The onKeyDown handler checks if (event.key === 'Enter' && isBulkEditActive) before blurring. If the input is not in bulk edit mode (isBulkEditActive is false), pressing Enter does nothing (no blur, no submit). This may be intentional (Enter only confirms bulk edit), but if the input is used in non-bulk-edit mode, Enter should still trigger blur or form submission. The handler is a no-op for non-bulk-edit usage.

title: Removal of 'Type' rows from grouping variant display — information loss
body: The diff removes the 'Type' data rows for COMPONENT, CUSTOM_FINGERPRINT, BUILT_IN_FINGERPRINT, SALTED_COMPONENT, and PERFORMANCE_PROBLEM variant types. These rows displayed the variant.type value with a QuestionTooltip explaining what each type means (e.g., 'Uses a complex grouping algorithm taking event data into account'). Removing them loses educational context for users trying to understand how their events are grouped. If this is intentional (UI simplification), it should be confirmed; otherwise it's a regression in user-facing documentation.

title: serverSidePct uses toFixed() without radix — returns string, then Number() conversion for clientSidePct
body: const serverSidePct = ((httpDuration / totalDuration) * 100).toFixed(); — toFixed() without arguments defaults to 0 decimal places, returning a string like "75". Then const clientSidePct = 100 - Number(serverSidePct); — converts back to number. This works but is convoluted. More importantly, toFixed() rounds, so serverSidePct and clientSidePct may not sum to exactly 100 (e.g., 75.5 rounds to "76", clientSidePct = 100 - 76 = 24, but actual client is 24.5). The displayed percentages may be off by 1 and won't sum to 100. Should use toFixed(0) consistently or Math.round for both, or display one decimal place.

title: totalDuration could be zero or negative — division by zero produces Infinity/NaN percentages
body: const totalDuration = rootEvent.endTimestamp - rootEvent.startTimestamp; If endTimestamp equals startTimestamp (zero-duration transaction) or is less (clock skew), totalDuration is 0 or negative. Then ((httpDuration / totalDuration) * 100) produces Infinity, -Infinity, or NaN. toFixed() on Infinity returns "Infinity", on NaN returns "NaN". These would be displayed as percentages in the UI. Should guard against totalDuration <= 0.

title: Flex wrapper without gap — icon and text spacing relies on StyledIconClock margin
body: The Flex component wraps the icon and TimeSince components. The StyledIconClock has margin-right: ${space(0.5)} for spacing. But the separator span ( — ) and the second TextOverflow don't have explicit gap handling. The Flex component with align="center" but no gap prop means spacing between the separator and text elements relies on the   entities in the separator span. This works but is fragile. The previous FlexWrapper had the same structure. Not a regression, just noting the layout relies on non-breaking spaces for spacing.

title: maxScale defaults to 10 when durationMs is undefined — zoom in disabled at wrong threshold
body: const maxScale = durationMs ? Math.ceil(durationMs / 60000) : 10; When durationMs is undefined (replay not loaded), maxScale is 10. The zoom in button is disabled when timelineScale === maxScale. If the replay loads later with a duration that implies maxScale < 10 (e.g., 5 minutes → maxScale=5), and the user had zoomed to 10 before load, the scale would be out of bounds. But since the component re-renders when replay loads, timelineScale state persists (from useTimelineScale context). If timelineScale was set to 10 (the default max) and the real maxScale becomes 5, the zoom in button is disabled (10 === 5 is false, so it's enabled), but zooming in would set scale to 11 which exceeds maxScale=5. The handleZoomIn uses Math.min(timelineScale + 1, maxScale) so it clamps correctly. But the disabled check timelineScale === maxScale would be false (10 !== 5), so zoom in is enabled and clicking it sets scale to min(11, 5) = 5, which is LESS than current 10 — zooming in actually zooms out. This is a bug: stale timelineScale from before load can exceed the real maxScale, and the zoom in button incorrectly adjusts.

title: Analytics event name changed from 'replay.view_html' to 'replay.view-html' — breaking analytics continuity
body: trackAnalytics('replay.view-html', ...) was changed from 'replay.view_html'. The replayAnalyticsEvents.tsx file defines 'replay.view-html' as a key. If historical analytics data uses 'replay.view_html' (with underscore), this change breaks trend continuity — dashboards and funnels tracking the old event name will see a drop to zero. The event name should be consistent with historical data, or a migration/alias should be set up in the analytics pipeline. The replayEventMap has 'replay.view-html' mapped to 'Clicked "View HTML" in Replay Breadcrumb', confirming the new name is intentional, but the historical data continuity concern remains.

title: New analytics events 'replay.timeline.zoom-in'/'zoom-out' use Record<string, unknown> — no type safety for parameters
body: The new event parameters 'replay.timeline.zoom-in' and 'replay.timeline.zoom-out' are typed as Record<string, unknown>, meaning any parameters can be passed without type checking. The trackAnalytics calls in timeAndScrubberGrid.tsx pass {organization} which is not a defined parameter. This is inconsistent with other events that have explicit parameter types. The events should define their expected parameters (e.g., organization slug) for type safety and documentation.

title: teamId extracted with non-null assertion — crashes if assignee format is unexpected
body: const teamId = assignee?.split(':')[1]!; — if assignee is set but doesn't contain ':', split(':')[1] is undefined, and the ! assertion hides this. teamId would be undefined. Then filteredProjectTeams.find(team => team.id === teamId) returns undefined, and teamName is undefined. Later, assigneeTeamActor = assignee && {type: 'team', id: teamId, name: ''} — id is undefined. ActorAvatar with actor.id undefined may crash or render incorrectly. The assignee state is initialized to '' and set via handleOwnerChange which receives values like 'team:123' or '' (unassigned). If the value format is ever different, this breaks. Should validate the split result.

title: aria-label uses teamName?.name but teamName is a Team object — should be teamName?.slug
body: triggerProps={{'aria-label': assignee ? `Assigned to #${teamName?.name}` : t('Unassigned'), ...}}. teamName is a Team object from filteredProjectTeams.find(...). Team objects have a `slug` property, not `name` (or name may be the display name). The aria-label would show "Assigned to #undefined" if teamName.name is undefined, or the team's display name instead of slug. Should use teamName?.slug for consistency with the dropdown labels which use #{team.slug}.

title: Threshold display logic is convoluted and may show wrong threshold
body: The threshold display: `${thresholdTypeText} ${rule.latestIncident || (!rule.latestIncident && !resolvedTrigger) ? trigger?.alertThreshold?.toLocaleString() : resolvedTrigger?.toLocaleString()}`. The condition `rule.latestIncident || (!rule.latestIncident && !resolvedTrigger)` simplifies to `rule.latestIncident || !resolvedTrigger`. When there's no active incident and no resolvedTrigger, it shows trigger?.alertThreshold (the critical/warning trigger threshold). When there's no active incident but there IS a resolvedTrigger, it shows resolvedTrigger. This logic is hard to follow and may display the wrong threshold in edge cases (e.g., active incident with no matching trigger). The original code before this PR may have been clearer; this ternary should be refactored for readability.

title: Hardcoded full token displayed in UI — real-looking token committed to source
body: const FULL_TOKEN = '91b57316-b1ff-4884-8d55-92b9936a05a3'; — this is a hardcoded UUID that looks like a real token. The comment says "HARDCODED VALUES FOR TESTING" but this is in a production component (static/app/views/codecov/tests/onboardingSteps/addUploadToken.tsx), not a test file. If this is a real token (e.g., from a test environment that was accidentally committed), it should be revoked. Even if it's fake, displaying a full token in the UI (even for testing) trains users to expect tokens to be shown, and the "Regenerate" button suggests this is a real flow. The component should use a clearly fake placeholder like 'xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx' or fetch from an API mock. The truncated token '********05a3' reveals the last 4 chars of the full token, which is a partial secret disclosure pattern.

title: Link to GitHub with hardcoded test repo URL — placeholder not replaced
body: <Link to="https://github.com/codecov/codecov-test-repo"> — this is a hardcoded placeholder URL in a production component. The TODO comment says "replace with actual link". If this ships, users will click a link to a non-existent or unrelated GitHub repo. The component is in views/codecov/tests/onboardingSteps/ which suggests it's for testing, but it's a real component that could be rendered. Should use a proper docs URL or be gated behind a feature flag.

title: CodeSnippet shows 'SENTRY_PREVENT_TOKEN' as the token name — likely wrong env var name
body: <CodeSnippet dark>SENTRY_PREVENT_TOKEN</CodeSnippet> — the token name 'SENTRY_PREVENT_TOKEN' looks like a typo or placeholder. It should likely be 'SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN' or 'CODECOV_TOKEN' or similar. 'PREVENT' is suspicious — possibly a typo for 'PRESENT' or a placeholder that wasn't replaced. Users following these instructions would set the wrong environment variable.

title: Placeholder links with to="placeholder" — broken navigation
body: The OrgFooterMessage component has <Link to="placeholder">Integrated Organization</Link> and <Link to="placeholder">GitHub identity</Link>. These are placeholder links that will navigate to a route literally called "placeholder" which doesn't exist, resulting in a 404 or broken page. These should be real documentation URLs or removed before shipping.

title: MenuFooter receives hardcoded 'placeholder' repoAccessLink
body: <MenuFooter repoAccessLink="placeholder" /> — the repoAccessLink is hardcoded to the string "placeholder". The MenuFooter renders <Link to={repoAccessLink}>repo access</Link>, which will navigate to a route called "placeholder". This is a broken link in production UI. Should be a real GitHub settings URL or fetched from the backend.

title: SyncRepoButton onClick is a no-op — button does nothing
body: The SyncRepoButton has onClick={() => {}} with a TODO comment "Adjust when sync endpoint is ready". This is a dead button that appears in the UI but does nothing when clicked. Users will click "sync now" and nothing happens, which is a poor UX. The button should be hidden or disabled until the endpoint is ready, or show a "coming soon" message.

title: SAMPLE_BRANCH_ITEMS hardcoded — shows fake branches in production
body: const SAMPLE_BRANCH_ITEMS = ['main', 'master']; — these are hardcoded sample branches that appear in the branch selector dropdown alongside the real branch. The comment pattern (similar to CODECOV_PLACEHOLDER_REPOS in repoSelector) suggests these are placeholders. If the real branch list API isn't ready, showing 'main' and 'master' as options may confuse users (selecting them may not work). Should be gated or removed until the API is ready.

title: SAMPLE_ORG_ITEMS hardcoded — shows fake orgs in production
body: const SAMPLE_ORG_ITEMS = ['codecov', 'getsentry']; — hardcoded sample integrated organizations. Same issue as SAMPLE_BRANCH_ITEMS — these appear in the dropdown as selectable options but are not real data. Should be removed or gated until the API provides real data.

title: CODECOV_PLACEHOLDER_REPOS hardcoded — shows fake repos in production
body: const CODECOV_PLACEHOLDER_REPOS = ['gazebo', 'sentry']; — hardcoded placeholder repos. The TODO says "When API is ready, replace placeholder w/ api response". These fake repos appear in the repo selector dropdown. Selecting them would set the repository filter to a non-existent repo, likely resulting in empty data. Should be removed until the API is ready.

title: renderHeadCell cast to GridColumnOrder signature — type mismatch with TabularColumn
body: renderHeadCell: renderDefaultHeadCell({renderTableHeadCell}) as (column: GridColumnOrder, columnIndex: number) => React.ReactNode. The renderDefaultHeadCell returns a function taking TabularColumn<keyof TabularRow>, but it's cast to a function taking GridColumnOrder. TabularColumn and GridColumnOrder have different shapes (TabularColumn has key, name, type, width; GridColumnOrder has key, name, width). The cast hides a potential type mismatch. If GridEditable passes a GridColumnOrder that lacks the `type` field, renderDefaultHeadCell's fieldAlignment(column.name, column.type as ColumnValueType) would get undefined type. The cast should be verified or the types aligned.

title: GridEditable data prop receives tableData?.data ?? [] — but columnOrder may reference keys not in data
body: The component passes data={tableData?.data ?? []} and columnOrder={columnOrder} to GridEditable. If columns prop is provided with keys that don't exist in tableData.data rows, the body cell renderer will get undefined values. The renderDefaultBodyCell handles this via fieldRenderer which should handle undefined gracefully, but the raw fallback (dataRow[column.key]) would return undefined. GridEditable may render empty cells or crash depending on its implementation. Should validate that column keys exist in data or handle missing keys.

title: LoadingPlaceholder renders GridEditable with empty columnOrder and data — may show empty table instead of loading state
body: TableWidgetVisualization.LoadingPlaceholder renders <GridEditable isLoading columnOrder={[]} columnSortBy={[]} data={[]} grid={{}} />. With empty columnOrder and data, GridEditable with isLoading should show a loading skeleton. But if GridEditable doesn't handle empty columnOrder well (e.g., renders no columns), the loading state may appear as an empty table rather than a skeleton. Should verify GridEditable's loading rendering with empty props.

title: fieldAlignment called with column.type as ColumnValueType — but TabularColumn.type is AttributeValueType which includes null
body: const align = fieldAlignment(column.name, column.type as ColumnValueType); — column.type is AttributeValueType | undefined (from TabularColumn type: type?: AttributeValueType). AttributeValueType includes null. The cast to ColumnValueType doesn't handle null/undefined. fieldAlignment may not handle null type gracefully. Should be column.type ?? undefined or handle null explicitly.

title: getFieldRenderer called with tableData.meta.fields but column.key may not be in fields — returns fallback renderer that may not handle the value
body: const fieldRenderer = getFieldRenderer(columnKey, tableData.meta.fields, false); — if columnKey is not in tableData.meta.fields (e.g., a custom column added via the columns prop that doesn't exist in the data), getFieldRenderer returns a default/fallback renderer. The fallback renderer may render the raw value without formatting, or may expect a specific type. The third argument `false` is likely `isColumn` or similar. If the column key is not in meta.fields, the renderer won't have type information and may render incorrectly. Should check if columnKey is in meta.fields and fall back to raw value rendering if not.

title: unit extracted with `as string` cast — may be null from meta.units
body: const unit = tableData.meta.units?.[columnKey] as string; — meta.units values are TabularValueUnit = DataUnit | null. The `as string` cast hides the possibility of null. If the unit is null, fieldRenderer receives unit=null (cast to string). fieldRenderer should handle null unit, but the cast is misleading. Should be `as string | undefined` or handle null explicitly.

title: Sample data includes 'id' field with empty string but 'id' is not in meta.fields
body: The sample data rows include id: '' but meta.fields only has 'http.request_method' and 'count(span.duration)'. The 'id' field is not declared in meta.fields. When rendered, the table will only show columns from meta.fields (or the columns prop), so 'id' won't be displayed. But if someone uses this fixture and expects 'id' to be a column, it won't appear. The fixture is inconsistent — either add 'id' to meta.fields or remove it from the data rows.

title: Test 'Table applies custom order and column name if provided' is not async but uses getAllByTestId synchronously
body: The test function is not declared async but uses screen.getAllByTestId('grid-head-cell') synchronously. If GridEditable renders asynchronously (e.g., due to ResizeObserver or virtualization), the headers may not be in the DOM yet when getAllByTestId runs, causing a flaky test. Should use await screen.findAllByTestId to wait for rendering. The first test ('Basic table renders correctly') correctly uses await findByText, but this test doesn't await anything.

title: Header text assertion uses children[0]?.textContent — fragile DOM traversal
body: expect(headers[0]?.children[0]?.textContent).toEqual(columns[0]?.name); — this assumes the header cell's first child contains the column name text. If the Tooltip wrapper adds extra DOM elements (which it does — StyledTooltip wraps the text), the textContent may include tooltip content or be nested differently. The test should use a more robust query like within(headers[0]).getByText(columns[0].name) or check textContent of the header directly.

title: Storybook story uses width: -1 for columns — negative width is unusual
body: The customColumns in the story use width: -1. The TabularColumn type has width?: number. A negative width is unusual — typically width is a positive pixel value or undefined for auto. The GridEditable component may interpret -1 as "auto" or "flex", but this should be documented. The default columnOrder in tableWidgetVisualization.tsx also uses width: -1. If -1 is a magic value for "auto width", it should be a named constant or documented.

title: Storybook CodeSnippet embeds JSON.stringify of data with template literal indentation — may produce malformed JSON display
useGetTraceItemAttributeValues called without attributeKey — hook signature changed but the hook fetches values per-tag at call time
body: The hook useGetTraceItemAttributeValues is called with {traceItemType, type: 'string', projectIds: projects} — no attributeKey. The hook's getTraceItemAttributeValues function takes (tag: Tag, queryString: string) and uses tag.key as the attributeKey. This is correct — the hook returns a function that fetches values for any given tag. The old hook required attributeKey at hook level; the new one defers it to call time. This is a better design. Not a bug.

title: findAllFieldRefs filters writablePageParams.aggregateFields with isBaseVisualize but readablePageParams uses isVisualize — inconsistent filtering
body: In findAllFieldRefs: readableVisualizeFields uses aggregateFields.filter<Visualize>(isVisualize) (filters for Visualize class instances with yAxis), but writableVisualizeFields uses writablePageParams.aggregateFields?.filter<BaseVisualize>(isBaseVisualize) (filters for BaseVisualize objects with yAxes array). The readable params contain Visualize instances; the writable params contain BaseAggregateField (GroupBy | BaseVisualize). This is correct — readable params have Visualize objects, writable params have plain JSON objects. The different filters are appropriate for the different data shapes. Not a bug, but the asymmetry is confusing and should be documented.

title: defaultPageParams maps visualizes to yAxis for sortBys — but defaultSortBys expects yAxes array
body: defaultSortBys(mode, fields, aggregateFields.filter(isVisualize).map(visualize => visualize.yAxis)) — the third argument is string[] (yAxes). defaultSortBys signature is (mode: Mode, fields: string[], yAxes: string[]). This is correct — it passes an array of yAxis strings. Not a bug.

title: Sort validation checks visualize.yAxis === sortBy.field — but sortBy.field may be an aggregate alias
body: In getSortBysFromLocation: visualizes.some(visualize => visualize.yAxis === sortBy.field). The sortBy.field from the URL may be an aggregate alias (e.g., 'count' instead of 'count(span.duration)') depending on how the sort was encoded. formatSort uses getAggregateAlias(sort.field) when writing to URL. If the URL contains an alias, the validation visualize.yAxis === sortBy.field would fail (yAxis is the full expression, field is the alias), causing the sort to be rejected and replaced with default. This could silently drop user-specified sorts. Should compare against both the full expression and the alias.

title: parseBaseVisualize uses Number(parsed.chartType) — ChartType enum values may be strings
body: const chartType = Number(parsed.chartType); if (Object.values(ChartType).includes(chartType)). ChartType is likely a numeric enum (from insights/common/components/chart). Number(parsed.chartType) converts the JSON value to a number. If ChartType is a string enum, Number() would produce NaN and the check would fail. If ChartType is a numeric enum, this works. The existing code used the same pattern, so this is not a regression. But if ChartType is ever changed to a string enum, this breaks silently (chartType would never be set from URL).

title: determineDefaultChartType reduce starts with ChartType.AREA as initial accumulator — ties broken toward AREA
body: return [ChartType.AREA, ChartType.BAR, ChartType.LINE].reduce((acc, ct) => (counts[ct] >= counts[acc] ? ct : acc), ChartType.AREA); — the reduce starts with AREA as the initial value. The reduce iterates [AREA, BAR, LINE]. For each, if counts[ct] >= counts[acc], acc becomes ct. Starting with AREA: if counts[AREA] >= counts[AREA] (always true), acc stays AREA. Then if counts[BAR] >= counts[AREA], acc becomes BAR. Then if counts[LINE] >= counts[BAR], acc becomes LINE. The >= means ties go to the later element. So if all counts are 0 (no recognized functions), acc stays AREA (initial). If BAR and LINE tie, LINE wins (>=). If AREA and BAR tie, BAR wins. The initial AREA is effectively overridden by the first iteration (AREA >= AREA is true, so acc stays AREA). The logic is correct but the initial value is redundant since the first element is AREA. Not a bug.

title: getEventView uses visualizes[visualizeIndex]!.yAxis — non-null assertion on array access
body: const yAxis = visualizes[visualizeIndex]!.yAxis; — the ! assertion assumes visualizes[visualizeIndex] exists. If visualizeIndex is out of bounds (e.g., stale index after visualizes change), this crashes. The addToDashboard callback receives visualizeIndex from chartOptions which is built from visualizes.map((chart, index) => ...), so the index should be valid at click time. But if visualizes changes between render and click (e.g., user removes a chart), the index could be stale. Should validate visualizes[visualizeIndex] exists.

title: Field deduplication uses allFields.includes() — O(n²) for large field lists
body: The fields useMemo iterates aggregateFields and for each, checks if (allFields.includes(aggregateField.yAxis)) continue; then allFields.push(...). This is O(n²) where n is the number of aggregate fields. For typical usage (a few groupBys and visualizes), this is fine. But if there are many fields (e.g., 50+), the quadratic behavior is noticeable. Should use a Set for O(n) deduplication. Minor performance issue.

title: canUsePreviousResults uses usePrevious(options) but options is a new object every render — previousOptions comparison may always be false
body: const previousOptions = usePrevious(options); — options is built with useMemo with dependencies [query, yAxes, interval, fields, orderby, topEvents, enabled, queryExtras]. If all dependencies are stable, options is referentially stable and usePrevious works correctly. But if any dependency changes identity every render (e.g., queryExtras is a new object each render), options changes every render, and previousOptions would always be the immediately preceding options (not the "previous query's" options). The isEqual checks (isEqual(options.interval, previousOptions.interval), etc.) compare individual fields, so even if options identity changes, the field-level comparisons work. But the initial check isEqual(query, previousQuery) — if query is stable, this is fine. The logic is correct but fragile — it relies on field-level isEqual rather than object-level comparison.

title: Attribute key regex validation is duplicated and inconsistent — second regex is a subset of the first
body: The validation: if (!/^[a-zA-Z0-9_.:-]+$/.test(attribute.key) && !/^tags\[[a-zA-Z0-9_.:-]+,number\]$/.test(attribute.key)) continue;. The first regex allows keys with dots, colons, hyphens, underscores, alphanumerics. The second regex allows tags[...] with number type. But the first regex would also match 'tags[foo,number]' if brackets were allowed — they're not (no [ or ] in the first regex). So the two regexes are for different formats. However, the comment says "EAP spans contain tags with illegal characters. SnQL forbids `-` but is allowed in RPC. So add it back later" — but the regex INCLUDES `-` in the character class [a-zA-Z0-9_.:-]. The `-` at the end of the character class is a literal hyphen. So hyphens ARE allowed by the regex. The comment is misleading — the regex allows hyphens, which SnQL forbids. The comment says "add it back later" but the regex already allows it. This is confusing and may indicate the validation is wrong.

title: isKnownAttribute filters sentry.* but allows sentry.message.* — inconsistent with comment
body: isKnownAttribute returns false (i.e., NOT known, so it's included) for keys starting with 'sentry.message.' or 'tags[sentry.message.'. For all other 'sentry.' or 'tags[sentry.' keys, it returns true (known, so skipped). The comment says "For logs we include sentry.message.* since it contains params etc." This is intentional — sentry.message.* attributes are included because they contain useful log message params. Not a bug, but the function name isKnownAttribute is confusing because it returns true for attributes to SKIP (known/internal), not for attributes that are "known" in the general sense.

title: useQuery queryFn returns getTraceItemAttributeKeys() but queryKey includes queryOptions — cache key doesn't include search substring
body: The queryKey is ['use-trace-item-attribute-keys', queryOptions] where queryOptions includes substringMatch: search. But the queryFn calls getTraceItemAttributeKeys() without passing a search string — it always fetches ALL keys (no substring filter). The queryOptions includes substringMatch: search (from makeTraceItemAttributeKeysQueryOptions), but the queryFn ignores it. So the cache key varies by search string, but the actual data fetched is always the full list. This means typing in a search box creates new cache entries with identical data — cache pollution. The queryFn should pass the search string to getTraceItemAttributeKeys(search) to actually filter, or the queryKey should not include substringMatch.

title: dedupeArray import removed but dedupedYAxes is now just [visualize.yAxis] — no deduplication needed
body: The code changed from const dedupedYAxes = dedupeArray(visualize.yAxes) to const dedupedYAxes = [visualize.yAxis]. Since Visualize now has a single yAxis, the array has one element and no deduplication is needed. The dedupeArray import was correctly removed. Not a bug.

title: expectRows helper uses parseFunction(field.yAxis)! with non-null assertion — test crashes if yAxis is not a function
body: const parsedFunction = parseFunction(field.yAxis)!; — if field.yAxis is not a valid function expression (e.g., a plain column name), parseFunction returns null and the ! assertion hides it. The next line expect(parsedFunction).not.toBeNull() would fail, but the crash happens before that if parseFunction returns null and the code tries to access parsedFunction.arguments. Actually, the ! is a TypeScript assertion, not runtime — at runtime, parsedFunction would be null and parsedFunction.arguments would throw. The test should check for null before accessing properties.

title: Tests updated for Visualize constructor change but don't test label assignment for added charts
body: The tests were updated to use new Visualize('count(span.duration)', {label: 'A'}) instead of new Visualize(['count(span.duration)'], {label: 'A'}). The test 'allows changing visualizes' checks that adding a chart creates new Visualize('count(span.duration)', {label: 'B'}) — so label assignment IS tested. But the toolbarVisualize.tsx addChart creates new Visualize(DEFAULT_VISUALIZATION) without a label (label defaults to ''). The test expects label 'B' for the added chart. This means either the test is wrong (the actual code produces label '') or there's label reassignment logic elsewhere. Looking at the test: after clicking 'Add Chart', it expects visualizes to equal [new Visualize('avg(span.self_time)', {label: 'A'}), new Visualize('count(span.duration)', {label: 'B'})]. But addChart creates new Visualize(DEFAULT_VISUALIZATION) with no label. So the test would FAIL unless there's label reassignment. This is a test gap — the test expects behavior that the code doesn't implement (see related finding about addChart not setting labels).

title: addChart doesn't assign sequential labels — test expects 'B' but code produces empty label
body: The test 'allows changing visualizes' in index.spec.tsx expects that clicking 'Add Chart' produces a new visualize with label 'B'. But addChart in toolbarVisualize.tsx creates new Visualize(DEFAULT_VISUALIZATION) without a label option, so label defaults to ''. The test would fail. Either the test is wrong (should expect label '') or the code should assign labels. Looking at the test expectation: new Visualize('count(span.duration)', {label: 'B'}) — this expects label 'B'. The code doesn't do this. This is a real bug: new charts get empty labels, breaking the chart label badges (A, B, C...) that appear when multiple charts exist.

title: shouldHighlightSaveButton compares visualizes.toJSON() with singleQuery?.visualize using valueIsEqual with third arg true
body: !valueIsEqual(visualizes.map(visualize => visualize.toJSON()), singleQuery?.visualize, true) — the third argument true to valueIsEqual likely means "strict" or "deep". The saved query's visualize field is an array of BaseVisualize objects (from the backend). visualizes.map(v => v.toJSON()) produces BaseVisualize objects. The comparison should work if the shapes match. But the saved query's visualize may have a different shape (e.g., stored as a different format in the database). If the shapes don't match exactly, valueIsEqual returns false, and the save button is always highlighted (indicating unsaved changes) even when nothing changed. This could be a false-positive "unsaved changes" indicator.

title: useSortByFields receives yAxes as string[] but the hook may expect a different type
body: useSortByFields({fields, yAxes: visualizes.map(v => v.yAxis), groupBys, mode}) — yAxes is string[]. The hook's expected type for yAxes should be verified. Previously it was visualizes.flatMap(v => v.yAxes) which also produced string[]. So the type is the same. Not a bug.

title: ColumnCompactSelect disabled when fieldOptions.length === 1 — but the single option may be the current value
body: The ColumnCompactSelect (field/argument selector) is disabled={fieldOptions.length === 1}. When there's only one option, the select is disabled. This is intentional (no choice to make). But if the single option is NOT the current value (e.g., the current yAxis uses a field not in the options), the select shows the current value but is disabled, and the user can't change it. This could happen if the current visualize's argument is not in the available fields (e.g., a custom field). The disabled state prevents fixing this. Should allow selection even with one option, or ensure the current value is always in the options.

title: UseTraceItemAttributeBaseProps docstring says 'currently only supports LOGS' but TraceItemDataset has SPANS too
body: The docstring for traceItemType says "The trace item type supported by the endpoint, currently only supports LOGS." But TraceItemDataset enum has both LOGS = 'logs' and SPANS = 'spans'. The hooks (useGetTraceItemAttributeValues, useGetTraceItemAttributeKeys) are used with TraceItemDataset.SPANS in transactionNameSearchBar.tsx and traceItemSearchQueryBuilder.tsx. The docstring is outdated — it should say "supports LOGS and SPANS" or be removed.

title: viewSamplesTarget visualize argument extraction uses continue inside for...of — skips rest of loop body correctly but the outer loop structure is nested
body: The visualize argument extraction: for (const visualize of visualizes) { const parsedFunction = parseFunction(visualize.yAxis); if (!parsedFunction?.arguments[0]) { continue; } ... }. The continue skips to the next visualize. This is correct. Previously it was a nested for loop over visualize.yAxes. The flattening is correct. Not a bug.

title: getSuggestedTransactions passes a Tag-like object without kind — hook checks tag.kind === FieldKind.FUNCTION
body: The hook getTraceItemAttributeValues is called with {key: SpanFields.TRANSACTION, name: SpanFields.TRANSACTION} as the tag. The hook checks if (tag.kind === FieldKind.FUNCTION || type === 'number') return []. Since the tag object doesn't have a `kind` property, tag.kind is undefined, so the check passes (not a function). This is fine — the tag is treated as a string tag. But the Tag type requires a `kind` field. Passing an object without `kind` is a type error that TypeScript should catch. The object should include kind: FieldKind.TAG or the hook should handle missing kind.

title: getSuggestedTransactions throws Error inside catch but the error is swallowed by debounce
body: In getSuggestedTransactions (a debounced function), the catch block does: throw new Error('Unable to fetch event field values'). But this throw happens inside an async function called by debounce. The debounced function's return value (a Promise) is not awaited or caught by the caller (handleSearchChange calls getSuggestedTransactions(query) without await/catch). So the thrown error becomes an unhandled promise rejection. The error message is never shown to the user, and the loading state may remain true (setLoading(true) was called, but setLoading(false) in finally should still run). Actually, the finally block runs setLoading(false), so loading is reset. But the thrown error is an unhandled rejection. Should log the error or show a user-facing message instead of throwing.

title: decodeValueToItem uses lastIndexOf(':') — breaks for transaction names containing colons
body: const decodeValueToItem = (value: string): DataItem => { const lastIndex = value.lastIndexOf(':'); return { transaction: value.slice(0, lastIndex) }; }. If a transaction name contains a colon (e.g., "GET /api/v1/users:export"), lastIndexOf(':') finds the last colon, and slice(0, lastIndex) would cut off part of the transaction name. For "GET /api/v1/users:export", lastIndexOf(':') finds the colon before "export", and slice(0, lastIndex) returns "GET /api/v1/users" — losing ":export". The function assumes the value format is "transaction:something" but the value comes from search results which are transaction names (from getTraceItemAttributeValues). If the value IS just the transaction name (no suffix), lastIndexOf(':') finds a colon within the name and truncates it. This is a bug — the function should not parse the value at all if it's just a transaction name, or the value format should be documented.

title: Trend calculation uses dataRow['user_misery()'] and weekRow['user_misery()'] with type assertion — may be undefined
body: const trend = weekRow ? ((dataRow['user_misery()'] as number) - (weekRow['user_misery()'] as number)) * 100 : null; — the values are cast to number but may be undefined or null if the API doesn't return user_misery() for a row. undefined - undefined = NaN, NaN * 100 = NaN. The filter .filter(x => x.trend !== null) doesn't filter NaN (NaN !== null is true). So rows with NaN trend pass through. Later, Math.abs(b.trend) - Math.abs(a.trend) with NaN produces NaN, and the sort is unstable. Math.round(Math.abs(trend)) with NaN produces NaN, displayed as "NaN%". Should check for undefined/null/NaN values.

title: Early return null inside map callback — React key warning and inconsistent rendering
body: Inside groupedData.map((dataRow, idx) => { ... if (!weekRow || trend === null) { return null; } ... return (<Fragment key={idx}>...</Fragment>); }). Returning null from a map callback is valid in React, but the key is on the Fragment inside the return, not on the null. React may warn about missing keys for the null entries. Also, the idx >= COLLAPSE_COUNT check returns null AFTER the weekRow check, so the order of checks matters. If a row is filtered out by the weekRow check, the idx-based collapse count may be off (collapsed rows are counted differently). Minor React best-practice issue.

title: ResizeObserver cleanup in setRef unobserves containerRef.current but doesn't disconnect — observer leak
body: In setRef: if (resizeObserverRef.current && containerRef.current) { resizeObserverRef.current.unobserve(containerRef.current); } — this unobserves the old element but doesn't disconnect the observer. Then a new ResizeObserver is created and assigned to resizeObserverRef.current, overwriting the old reference. The old observer is never disconnected, so it leaks (continues to exist, though unobserved). The useEffect cleanup on unmount does disconnect, but if setRef is called multiple times (e.g., re-render with different node), each call creates a new observer without disconnecting the old one. Should call resizeObserverRef.current.disconnect() before creating a new one.

title: Unmount cleanup checks containerRef.current but it may have been set to null by setRef cleanup
body: The useEffect cleanup: if (resizeObserverRef.current && containerRef.current) { resizeObserverRef.current.unobserve(containerRef.current); resizeObserverRef.current.disconnect(); }. If setRef was called with null (React ref cleanup), containerRef.current is null, and the cleanup skips disconnect. But resizeObserverRef.current may still hold an observer. The cleanup should disconnect resizeObserverRef.current regardless of containerRef.current. Should be: if (resizeObserverRef.current) { resizeObserverRef.current.disconnect(); }

title: Flex component with direction="column" flex={1} — flex prop may not be a valid Flex prop
body: The change replaces <FlexBox> (a styled div with display: flex, flex-direction: column, flex-grow: 1, height: 100%) with <Flex direction="column" flex={1}>. The Flex component from sentry/components/core/layout — does it accept a `flex` prop? The Flex component typically accepts direction, align, justify, gap, wrap props. A `flex` prop may not be supported and would be passed as a DOM attribute (flex="1") which is invalid HTML. The original FlexBox had flex-grow: 1 and height: 100%. The new Flex with flex={1} may not apply flex-grow correctly. Should verify Flex supports the flex prop, or use style={{flex: 1}} or a styled wrapper.

title: Type annotation change from ((frame: Frame) => boolean) | undefined to (frame: Frame) => boolean — removes undefined possibility
body: The flamegraphFrameFilter type changed from ((frame: Frame) => boolean) | undefined to (frame: Frame) => boolean. The useMemo always returns a function (never undefined), so the new type is more accurate. The old type included undefined but the code never returned undefined. This is a type accuracy improvement, not a bug. The explicit (frame: Frame) parameter type annotations on the returned arrow functions are also improvements.

title: chapterData breadcrumbs filter uses breadcrumb.timestampMs but getChapterFrames() may return frames without timestampMs
body: const chapterData = summaryData?.data.time_ranges.map(({period_title, period_start, period_end}) => ({ ..., breadcrumbs: replay?.getChapterFrames().filter(breadcrumb => breadcrumb.timestampMs >= period_start * 1000 && breadcrumb.timestampMs <= period_end * 1000) ?? [] })); — getChapterFrames() returns ReplayFrame objects. If a frame doesn't have timestampMs (undefined), the comparison undefined >= number is false, so the frame is excluded. This is safe (excluded, not crash). But if getChapterFrames() returns frames with timestampMs as a string (not number), the comparison would be string >= number which is false (type coercion). Should verify timestampMs is a number.

title: TimestampButton startTimestampMs uses replay?.getStartTimestampMs() ?? 0 — but breadcrumb timestamps are absolute, start should be replay start
body: In the chapter rendering: <TimestampButton startTimestampMs={replay?.getStartTimestampMs() ?? 0} timestampMs={start} />. The start is period_start * 1000 (from the summary data). The TimestampButton likely computes a relative time from startTimestampMs. If replay is undefined, startTimestampMs is 0, and the relative time calculation would be wrong (timestampMs - 0 = huge number). Should ensure replay is defined before rendering chapters, or handle the undefined case.

title: BreadcrumbRow onClick and onInspectorExpanded are no-op functions — breadcrumbs are not interactive
body: The BreadcrumbRow components in the AI summary chapters have onClick={() => {}} and onInspectorExpanded={() => {}} — no-op handlers. The breadcrumbs are displayed but clicking them does nothing (no seek to timestamp, no expansion). This is intentional (the AI summary is a read-only overview), but the BreadcrumbRow component may show interactive affordances (hover states, click cursors) that mislead users into thinking they're clickable. Should either make them seek to the timestamp or use a non-interactive breadcrumb display.

title: onEventSelect called with options?.value but Select onChange may pass the option object directly
body: onChange={(options: any) => { onEventSelect(options?.value); }} — the Select component's onChange signature may pass the selected option directly (not an object with .value). The `options: any` and `options?.value` pattern assumes the callback receives an object with a value property. If Select passes the value directly (e.g., a string), options?.value would be undefined (strings don't have .value). Should verify the Select component's onChange signature. The `any` type hides this potential bug.

title: TabList.Item textValue uses getTabDisplay ? getTabDisplay(tab) : tab — but renderTab already defaults to identity
body: textValue={getTabDisplay ? getTabDisplay(tab) : tab} — this duplicates the default logic in renderTab (which is getTabDisplay ?? ((tab) => tab)). If getTabDisplay is provided, both use it. If not, textValue uses tab directly and renderTab uses the identity function. This is correct but redundant — could just use renderTab(tab) for textValue since renderTab already handles the default.

title: handleSync sends date_updated as new Date().toISOString() — server may reject client-provided timestamp
body: In handleSync: data: {raw: codeownerFile.raw, date_updated: new Date().toISOString()}. The client is setting date_updated to the current time. This is a client-controlled timestamp sent to the server. The server should set date_updated itself (e.g., auto_now=True) rather than trusting the client. If the server accepts this field, a malicious client could set arbitrary dates. More likely, the server ignores it or the field name is wrong. Should verify the API contract — the client should probably not send date_updated at all.

title: response.allowedOrigins.join(' ') crashes if allowedOrigins is null or not an array
body: setClientDetails({ ..., allowedOrigins: response.allowedOrigins.join(' '), ..., redirectUris: response.redirectUris.join(' '), ... }). If the API returns allowedOrigins or redirectUris as null (e.g., no origins configured), .join(' ') throws TypeError. The ClientDetails type says allowedOrigins: string | null, but the code assumes the API response has arrays. Should be (response.allowedOrigins ?? []).join(' ') or similar null-safe handling.

title: ApiForm onSubmitSuccess reloads entire page — loses form state and is heavy-handed
body: onSubmitSuccess={() => window.location.reload()} — after a successful form submission, the entire page reloads. This is a poor UX (full page flash, lost scroll position) and suggests the form doesn't properly update local state after save. The component should update clientDetails state from the response instead of reloading. window.location.reload() is a code smell indicating the developer didn't wire up proper state management.

title: assert_invalid_report_data helper defined but test for non-list body (422 without details) is missing
body: The endpoint returns 422 without a JSON body (just status) when the request body is not a list (line 104 of browser_reporting_collector.py: return Response(status=HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY)). But the tests only test invalid report data WITHIN a list (using assert_invalid_report_data which expects response.json() with error/details). There's no test for the non-list case (e.g., posting a dict or string instead of an array). The test_rejects_invalid_content_type tests 415 but not the non-list 422 case. Missing test coverage for the non-list rejection path.

title: test_mixed_fields expects both age and timestamp errors but the serializer may only report one
body: The test expects both {"age": ["If age is present, timestamp must be absent"], "timestamp": ["If timestamp is present, age must be absent"]}. The serializer has validate_timestamp and validate_age methods that check each other. When both are present, validate_timestamp raises (because age is present) and validate_age raises (because timestamp is present). DRF runs all field validators and collects errors, so both errors should appear. But the order of validation and whether both run depends on DRF internals. The test asserts both, which is correct if DRF runs both validators. This is fine but worth noting the test depends on DRF running both field-level validators even when both fail.

title: Removal of ParameterizationRegexExperiment tests leaves no coverage for regex-based experiments
body: The tests test_parameterize_regex_experiment and test_parameterize_regex_experiment_cached_compiled were removed along with the ParameterizationRegexExperiment class. If regex-based experiments are re-introduced in the future (or exist in downstream code), there's no test coverage for the pattern. The comment in the original test said "We don't have any of these yet, but we need to test that they work" — so the tests were forward-looking. Removing them removes the safety net for future regex experiments.

title: Expected comment format changed to include blank lines between items — test asserts exact format with trailing newlines
body:
The expected_comment now has blank lines between each issue item (* ‼️ [**issue 1**](...) in `dev`

* ‼️ [**issue 2**](...)

* ‼️ [**issue 3**](...) in `prod`

). The MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE is "* ‼️ [**{title}**]({url}){environment}
" — note the trailing 
. When joined with "
".join(...), each item ends with 
 and they're joined with 
, producing item1

item2

item3
. This creates blank lines between items. The test asserts this exact format. If the template's trailing 
 is intentional (for markdown rendering), fine. But the double newline between items may render as extra spacing in GitHub. The test is correct for the current implementation but the format should be verified as intentional.

title: GitLab expected comment uses ev1.group.title instead of hardcoded 'issue 1' — inconsistent with GitHub test
body: The GitLab test's expected_comment uses {ev1.group.title} (dynamic) while the GitHub test uses hardcoded 'issue 1'. The GitLab test is more robust (uses actual group titles), but the inconsistency between the two test files is notable. The GitHub test hardcodes 'issue 1', 'issue 2', 'issue 3' which matches the event data messages. Both are correct but the GitLab approach is better practice. Not a bug, just an inconsistency.

title: GitLab test_comment_workflow expected comment uses self.another_organization.slug for second issue — but the URL hardcodes 'foobar'
body: The expected comment in test_comment_workflow uses: * ‼️ [**{titles[1]}**](http://testserver/organizations/{self.another_organization.slug}/issues/{groups[1]}/?referrer=gitlab-pr-bot). But the original test (before this PR) hardcoded 'foobar' in the URL: http://testserver/organizations/foobar/issues/{groups[1]}/. The new test uses self.another_organization.slug. If self.another_organization.slug is 'foobar', this is equivalent. But the test now depends on the organization slug being 'foobar'. If the test setup changes the slug, the test breaks. The original hardcoded 'foobar' was fragile; the new dynamic version is better but should be verified that another_organization.slug is indeed 'foobar'.

title: Migration test deleted but no replacement test for the no-op migration or the 0921 migration
body: The test file test_0917_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views.py was deleted entirely. The migration 0917 is now a no-op (just returns). There's no test verifying that the no-op migration runs without error, and no test for migration 0921 (the "rerevised" migration that supposedly does the real work). Since 0921 is not in the changed files list, there may be no test coverage for the actual data migration. This is a critical test gap — the data migration that converts org saved searches to views has no test coverage in this PR.

title: Test changed max_segment_id from 0 to None but doesn't test the actual None handling in _make_recording_filenames
body: The test test_run_bulk_replay_delete_job_completion changed the mock data to use max_segment_id: None instead of 0. This tests that the job handles None max_segment_id. But the actual None handling is in _make_recording_filenames (src/sentry/replays/usecases/delete.py) which returns [] when max_segment_id is None. The test mocks delete_matched_rows, so it doesn't test that _make_recording_filenames correctly returns [] for None. The unit test for _make_recording_filenames with None input is missing. The integration test (test_run_bulk_replay_delete_job_chained_runs) uses real data but doesn't specifically test the None case.

title: test_get_request_data is a standalone function (not in a class) — may not have access to test fixtures
body: test_get_request_data is defined as a standalone function at module level, outside the ProjectReplaySummarizeBreadcrumbsTestCase class. It tests get_request_data directly with mock data. This is fine for a pure function test. But it's placed after the class definition, which is unconventional. Not a bug, just noting the structure.

title: @requires_snuba decorator added but tests use TransactionTestCase — snuba requirement may be for store_replays
body: The @requires_snuba decorator was added to the test class. The store_replays method posts to settings.SENTRY_SNUBA + "/tests/entities/replays/insert" which requires a running Snuba instance. The decorator is appropriate. But the test_get and test_get_feature_flag_disabled tests don't call store_replays — they only save recording segments. These tests don't need Snuba. Only test_get_with_error and test_get_with_error_context_disabled call store_replays. The @requires_snuba on the class means ALL tests are skipped without Snuba, even those that don't need it. Should be on individual tests or the class should be split.

title: Owner update tests don't verify that the owner is a member of the organization
body: The tests test_update_owner_to_user, test_update_owner_to_team, and test_update_clear_owner verify that the owner is set correctly. But they don't test the negative case: setting an owner who is NOT a member of the organization (should be rejected). The test_organization_detector_index.py has test_owner_not_in_organization for the create endpoint, but the update endpoint (PUT) has no such test. If the update endpoint doesn't validate organization membership (see related security finding), this test gap means the vulnerability is untested.

title: test_owner_not_in_organization creates other_user but doesn't verify the error message content
body: The test asserts response.status_code == 400 and "owner" in response.data. But it doesn't verify the specific error message (e.g., "User is not a member of this organization"). If the validation is missing (see related security finding), the test would fail with a different error or no error. But the test only checks that "owner" is a key in the response data, which is a weak assertion. Should assert the specific error message to ensure the validation is actually happening.

title: test_get_condition_query_groups now computes dcg_to_slow_conditions inline — duplicates setup logic
body: The test computes dcg_to_slow_conditions = get_slow_conditions_for_groups(list(dcg_to_groups.keys())) inline before calling get_condition_query_groups. This duplicates the logic that process_delayed_workflows now does. If the setup changes, the test needs to be updated in sync. Could be a fixture or helper. Minor test maintainability issue.

title: OrganizationEventsStatsTopNEventsLogs test class name suggests logs but uses SnubaTestCase not OurLogTestCase-specific assertions
body: The class OrganizationEventsStatsTopNEventsLogs extends APITestCase, SnubaTestCase, OurLogTestCase. It uses self.create_ourlog and self.store_ourlogs from OurLogTestCase. The test test_simple_top_events queries the events-stats endpoint with dataset=ourlogs. The test is a sanity check (as noted in the comment). It verifies top events for logs. title: Renamed OrganizationEventsStatsTopNEvents to OrganizationEventsStatsTopNEventsSpans — existing test references may break
body: The class OrganizationEventsStatsTopNEvents was renamed to OrganizationEventsStatsTopNEventsSpans. If any CI configuration, test runner, or documentation references the old class name (e.g., pytest -k OrganizationEventsStatsTopNEvents or test selection by class name), it would no longer match.
