title: Feedback entries joined without bullet markers — LLM may not distinguish individual entries
body:
make_input_prompt changed from "
".join(f"- {msg}" for msg in feedbacks) to "
------
".join(feedbacks). The old format used "- " bullet markers, making each feedback entry clearly delineated. The new format uses "------" separators. If a feedback message itself contains "------" or newlines, the boundaries between entries become ambiguous, and the LLM may merge or split entries incorrectly. The bullet format was clearer for the LLM to parse individual entries. The separator approach is more fragile if feedback content contains similar patterns.

title: Prompt says 'AT MOST 55 words' but max_output_tokens=150 — token limit may not enforce word limit
body: The prompt instructs the LLM to produce "AT MOST 55 words" but the API call uses max_output_tokens=150. 55 words is roughly 70-80 tokens (depending on word length), so 150 tokens is generous. However, token limits don't directly map to word counts — the LLM could produce 150 tokens of short words (e.g., "a a a a...") exceeding 55 words, or the model may not respect the word limit instruction. The word limit is a soft constraint enforced only by the prompt, not by the token limit. If the 55-word limit is important (e.g., for UI space), it should be enforced post-generation (truncate the summary) or the token limit should be set tighter.

title: generate_summary raises ValueError on empty response but doesn't log or metric the failure
body: When complete_prompt returns a falsy response, generate_summary raises ValueError("Invalid response from LLM"). This exception propagates to the caller without any logging or metrics. If the LLM service returns empty responses frequently, this would cause silent failures (the caller must catch the exception). Should log the failure and/or increment a metric before raising, so LLM failures are observable.

title: equations parameter added to run_top_events_timeseries_query — verify rpc_dataset_common.run_top_events_timeseries_query accepts it
body: The equations parameter was added to run_top_events_timeseries_query and passed to rpc_dataset_common.run_top_events_timeseries_query(equations=equations). The diff shows the parameter is added to the function signature and passed through. But the underlying rpc_dataset_common.run_top_events_timeseries_query must also accept an equations parameter. If it doesn't, this would be a TypeError at runtime. The diff doesn't show changes to rpc_dataset_common, so either it already accepts equations (likely, since other functions do) or this is a bug. Should verify the downstream function signature.

title: noise_config added to DBQueryInjectionVulnerabilityGroupType — verify NoiseConfig import and semantics
body: noise_config = NoiseConfig(ignore_limit=5) is added to DBQueryInjectionVulnerabilityGroupType. This configures the group type to ignore (auto-resolve?) issues after 5 occurrences. The NoiseConfig semantics should be verified — does ignore_limit=5 mean the issue is marked as ignored after 5 events? This is a behavior change for DB query injection vulnerabilities. The PR description doesn't explain why this is added. Should be documented.

title: Removed grouping.experiments.parameterization.traceparent option — any projects with this option set will have a dangling option
body: The option "grouping.experiments.parameterization.traceparent" is removed from defaults.py. If any project has this option explicitly set (via the admin UI or API), the option value remains in the database but is no longer registered. Depending on how options are read, this could cause issues (e.g., the option is silently ignored, or an error is raised when reading unregistered options). Typically Sentry handles unregistered options gracefully (they're just ignored), but this should be verified. The option was likely experimental and no longer used.

title: autofix_automation_tuning default changed from 'low' to 'off' — same as constants.py change, behavior change for all projects
body: Same issue as the constants.py finding: register(key="sentry:autofix_automation_tuning", default="off") changes the default from "low" to "off". This is the project-level option that actually controls behavior. Every project without an explicit setting will change from "low" (autofix runs automatically at low tuning) to "off" (autofix does not run automatically). This is a significant, silent behavior change for all customers. Should be a deliberate rollout with a migration or feature flag.

title: snuba-metrics service added with mode 'containerized-metrics-dev' — verify this mode exists in snuba
body: A new snuba-metrics service is added with mode: containerized-metrics-dev. This mode is passed to the snuba repository's devservices integration. If the snuba repo doesn't support a 'containerized-metrics-dev' mode, devservices will fail to start this service. Should verify the mode exists in the snuba repo at the specified branch (master).

title: New 'tracing' mode added with many consumers — verify all consumer names are valid
body: A new 'tracing' mode is added listing many Kafka consumers (eap-spans-subscription-results, subscription-results-eap-items, metrics-subscription-results, generic-metrics-subscription-results, etc.). These consumer names must match actual consumer group names defined in the sentry codebase. If any name is misspelled, `devservices up --mode tracing` will fail to start that consumer. The x-programs section defines commands for each, which look correct, but the consumer group names should be verified against the actual consumer definitions in src/sentry.

title: Flex.Item grow={1} used as spacer — but Flex.Item may not support grow prop directly
body: The change replaces <FlexSpacer /> (a styled div with flex-grow: 1) with <Flex.Item grow={1} />. The Flex.Item component from sentry/components/core/layout — does it accept a `grow` prop? Flex.Item typically accepts props like grow, shrink, basis. If grow={1} is valid, it applies flex-grow: 1. But if Flex.Item doesn't support grow (or uses a different prop name), the spacer won't work and the layout breaks (elements won't be pushed apart). Should verify Flex.Item supports the grow prop.

title: Flex component used without import verification — same Flex.Item grow concern as codeSnippet
body: The change replaces <FlexContainer> (styled div with display: flex, align-items: center, gap) with <Flex align="center" gap={space(0.75)}>. The Flex component is imported from 'sentry/components/core/layout'. This should work if Flex supports align and gap props. The original FlexContainer had display: flex, align-items: center, gap: ${space(0.75)}. The new Flex with align="center" gap={space(0.75)} should produce equivalent styles. Not a bug if Flex supports these props.

title: Flex wrapping Name component — Name has overflowEllipsis but Flex may not constrain width
body: The change wraps <Name>{attachment.name}</Name> in <Flex align="center">. The Name styled component has overflowEllipsis and white-space: nowrap. But the Flex wrapper doesn't have min-width: 0 or overflow handling. In a grid layout (StyledPanelTable with grid-template-columns: 1fr auto auto), the first column is 1fr. The Flex inside the 1fr column needs min-width: 0 to allow the Name's overflowEllipsis to work. Without it, the Flex may expand beyond the column width. The original FlexCenter had overflowEllipsis on the wrapper itself. The new Flex doesn't have overflow handling, so the Name's ellipsis may not trigger correctly.

title: TextOverflow wrapping TimeSince — TimeSince may render multiple elements, TextOverflow expects single text node
body: The change wraps <TimeSince date={lastSeen} suffix={t('ago')} /> in <TextOverflow>. TextOverflow typically applies overflow: hidden, text-overflow: ellipsis, white-space: nowrap to a single text element. TimeSince renders a <time> element with a date string. Wrapping it in TextOverflow should work (the time element is a single child). But if TimeSince renders multiple elements (e.g., a tooltip wrapper), TextOverflow may not apply correctly. The original code didn't wrap TimeSince in TextOverflow — the FlexWrapper had overflowEllipsis on the container. The new approach applies TextOverflow per TimeSince, which may behave differently.

title: maxScale calculation uses Math.ceil(durationMs / 60000) — for very short replays, maxScale is 1, disabling zoom in
body: const maxScale = durationMs ? Math.ceil(durationMs / 60000) : 10; — for a replay shorter than 60 seconds (60000ms), durationMs / 60000 < 1, Math.ceil gives 1. So maxScale = 1. The zoom in button is disabled when timelineScale === maxScale (1 === 1), so zoom in is disabled. But for a 30-second replay, you might want to zoom in to see 30 seconds across the full width (scale=1 means 1 minute per unit?). The scale semantics are unclear — if scale=1 means "fit to view", then maxScale=1 means no zoom possible for short replays. This may be intentional (short replays don't need zoom) but should be verified.

title: RightMask transparent gradient changed from hardcoded white to theme background — but LeftMask uses Color(theme.background).alpha(0)
body: The RightMask transparent gradient changed from 'linear-gradient(to right, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0), rgba(255, 255, 255, 1))' (hardcoded white) to `linear-gradient(to right, transparent, ${p.theme.background})`. The LeftMask uses `linear-gradient(to left, ${Color(p.theme.background).alpha(0).rgb().string()}, ${p.theme.background})`. The RightMask now uses 'transparent' keyword while LeftMask uses Color().alpha(0). These produce equivalent results (transparent = rgba(0,0,0,0)), but 'transparent' in CSS is actually rgba(0,0,0,0) (black transparent), which can cause a dark fringe in some browsers when interpolating to a non-black color. Using Color(theme.background).alpha(0) is safer (matches the target color's RGB). The RightMask should use the same Color().alpha(0) approach as LeftMask for consistency and to avoid dark fringes.

title: 'replay.view-html' event parameters only define breadcrumb_type — but trackAnalytics call passes organization too
body: The 'replay.view-html' event type defines {breadcrumb_type: string} but the trackAnalytics call in breadcrumbItem.tsx passes {organization, breadcrumb_type: ...}. The organization parameter is not in the type definition. While trackAnalytics may accept extra parameters (they're often used for routing), the type definition should include organization if it's expected. Other events in the file also omit organization from their parameter types but pass it in trackAnalytics calls — this is a systemic pattern where organization is passed but not typed. Not a bug per se, but the types are incomplete.

title: criticalTrigger and warningTrigger found with label comparison using any type — fragile if label format changes
body: const criticalTrigger = rule.triggers.find(({label}: any) => label === AlertRuleTriggerType.CRITICAL); — the destructured label is typed as any. If the trigger label format changes (e.g., from 'critical' to 'CRITICAL' or a different string), the find returns undefined, and trigger falls back to warningTrigger ?? criticalTrigger (both undefined), so trigger is undefined. Then trigger?.alertThreshold?.toLocaleString() is undefined, and the threshold display shows "Above undefined". Should handle the case where no trigger matches.

title: slug computation for non-uptime, non-cron alerts uses rule.projects[0]! — non-null assertion
body: const slug = isUptime ? rule.projectSlug : isCron ? rule.project.slug : rule.projects[0]!; — rule.projects[0]! assumes projects array is non-empty. If rule.projects is empty (e.g., an issue alert with no projects), this crashes. Issue alerts should always have at least one project, but the ! assertion hides the assumption. Should handle empty projects gracefully.

title: Alert trailingItems IconClose onClick dismisses warning — but no aria-label for accessibility
body: trailingItems={<IconClose size="sm" onClick={handleDismiss} />} — the IconClose is clickable but has no aria-label or role="button". Screen readers won't announce it as a dismiss button. Should wrap in a Button with aria-label={t('Dismiss')} or add appropriate ARIA attributes to the icon.

title: Test expects '123.00ms' for duration 123 with millisecond unit — verify fieldRenderer formats correctly
body: The test expects screen.findByText('123.00ms') for a duration field with value 123 and unit DurationUnit.MILLISECOND. The fieldRenderer for duration type should format 123ms as "123.00ms". This depends on the exact formatting logic in getFieldRenderer for duration types. If the renderer formats differently (e.g., "123ms" or "0.123s"), the test fails. The test is correct if the renderer produces this format, but it's tightly coupled to the renderer's formatting.

title: Test expects '10%' for percentage 0.1 — verify fieldRenderer multiplies by 100
body: The test expects screen.findByText('10%') for failure_rate: 0.1 with type 'percentage'. The fieldRenderer for percentage type should multiply by 100 and append '%'. If the renderer expects the value already as a percentage (10 instead of 0.1), the test data is wrong. The test assumes 0.1 → "10%", which is the standard convention. Should be correct.

title: Test expects '6.00/min' for rate 6 with PER_MINUTE unit — verify fieldRenderer formats rate correctly
body: The test expects screen.findByText('6.00/min') for epm: 6 with type 'rate' and unit RateUnit.PER_MINUTE. The fieldRenderer for rate type with PER_MINUTE unit should format as "6.00/min". This depends on the renderer's rate formatting logic. If the renderer formats differently (e.g., "6/min" or "6.00 per minute"), the test fails.

title: Test 'converts to JSON without chart type' expects {yAxes: ['count(span.duration)']} — but toJSON returns BaseVisualize with yAxes array
body: The test expects visualize.toJSON() to equal {yAxes: ['count(span.duration)']}. The toJSON method returns {yAxes: [this.yAxis]} and conditionally adds chartType. For a Visualize without selectedChartType, toJSON returns {yAxes: ['count(span.duration)']}. This is correct. The test verifies the serialization format. Not a gap.

title: Test 'converts from JSON without chart type' expects Visualize.fromJSON to return an array — but the test name says 'converts from JSON' (singular)
body: The test: const visualize = Visualize.fromJSON({yAxes: ['count(span.duration)']}); expect(visualize).toEqual([new Visualize('count(span.duration)')]); — fromJSON now returns Visualize[] (array). The variable is named `visualize` (singular) but it's an array. The test name says "converts from JSON without chart type" (singular). The naming is misleading — should be `visualizes` (plural) and the test name should reflect the array return. Minor naming issue.

title: Number type test mocks API response but expects it NOT to be called — mock is unnecessary
body: The test 'getTraceItemAttributeValues returns empty array for number type' sets up a mock API response (searchQueryMock) but then asserts searchQueryMock was NOT called. The hook returns [] immediately for number type without making an API call. The mock setup is unnecessary (the API is never called). The test could be simplified by removing the mock setup. Not a bug, just dead test code.

title: Mock match function checks query.substringMatch but the hook sends substringMatch in query params
body: The mock match function: (_url, options) => { const query = options?.query || {}; return query.substringMatch === 'search-query'; }. The hook builds the query with substringMatch: search (from traceItemAttributeValuesQueryKey). The mock checks query.substringMatch === 'search-query'. This should match. But the hook's getTraceItemAttributeValues function receives queryString as the second argument and passes it as search to traceItemAttributeValuesQueryKey. The test calls result.current(tag, 'search-query'), so queryString is 'search-query'. The mock should match. Not a gap.

title: Number type test mock match checks query.query === 'search-query' but hook sends substringMatch not query
body: The number type test's mock match function checks query.query === 'search-query'. But the hook sends substringMatch (not query) in the request params. So the mock would never match (query.query is undefined, not 'search-query'). However, the test asserts the mock was NOT called, which is correct (the hook returns [] for number type without calling the API). The mock match function is wrong (checks the wrong param) but it doesn't matter because the mock is never called. Dead/incorrect test setup.

title: Test expects onColumnsChange with {yAxes: ['avg(span.self_time)']} but the modal's handleApply converts Visualize to toJSON()
body: The test expects onColumnsChange to be called with [{groupBy: 'geo.region'}, {yAxes: ['avg(span.self_time)']}]. The handleApply does tempColumns.map(col => (isVisualize(col) ? col.toJSON() : col)). For a Visualize, toJSON() returns {yAxes: [yAxis], chartType?}. So the expected {yAxes: ['avg(span.self_time)']} matches toJSON() output (without chartType since it wasn't explicitly set). This is correct. The test verifies the conversion from Visualize to BaseVisualize JSON.

title: Test expects added chart to have label 'B' but toolbarVisualize addChart creates Visualize without label
body: The test 'allows changing visualizes' expects: after clicking 'Add Chart', visualizes equals [new Visualize('avg(span.self_time)', {label: 'A'}), new Visualize('count(span.duration)', {label: 'B'})]. But toolbarVisualize.tsx addChart creates new Visualize(DEFAULT_VISUALIZATION) without a label option, so label defaults to ''. The test expects label 'B'. This test would FAIL with the current code. Either the test is wrong (should expect label '') or the code should assign labels. This is a real discrepancy between test expectations and implementation — see the related finding about addChart not setting labels.

title: chartOptions label uses chart.label which may be empty string for newly added charts
body: const chartOptions = visualizes.map((chart, index) => { ... return { key: chart.label, label: t('%s - %s', chart.label, formattedYAxes.filter(Boolean).join(', ')), ... }; }); — if chart.label is '' (empty string, as for newly added charts per the addChart bug), the key is '' and the label is " - count(span.duration)" (leading dash with empty label). The key '' may cause React key collisions if multiple charts have empty labels. The label display is broken. Should handle empty labels (e.g., use a default like 'Chart' or the yAxis).

title: ChartLabel only rendered when label is truthy — empty string labels render no badge
body: {label && <ChartLabel>{label}</ChartLabel>} — if label is '' (empty string), the ChartLabel is not rendered. This is correct behavior (no badge for unlabeled charts). But combined with the addChart bug (new charts get empty labels), new charts won't have badges even when multiple charts exist (shouldRenderLabel is true). The user sees charts without A/B/C labels, which is confusing. Should ensure labels are always assigned when multiple charts exist.

title: Add Chart button disabled when visualizes.length >= MAX_VISUALIZES — but MAX_VISUALIZES is 4
body: disabled={visualizes.length >= MAX_VISUALIZES} where MAX_VISUALIZES = 4. So the button is disabled when there are already 4 visualizes. This is correct. But the deleteOverlay uses toSpliced(group, 1) which removes the visualize at the given index. After deletion, visualizes.length decreases, re-enabling the Add Chart button. This is correct. Not a bug.

title: UseTraceItemAttributeBaseProps moved from useTraceItemAttributeKeys.tsx to types.tsx — verify no circular imports
body: The UseTraceItemAttributeBaseProps interface was moved from useTraceItemAttributeKeys.tsx to types.tsx. The hooks useGetTraceItemAttributeKeys.tsx and useGetTraceItemAttributeValues.tsx now import it from types.tsx. types.tsx imports Project from sentry/types/project. No circular import issue (types.tsx doesn't import from the hooks). This is a good refactor (shared types in a central location). Not a bug.

title: computeVisualizeSampleTotals uses [visualize.yAxis] instead of dedupeArray — no deduplication needed for single yAxis
body: const dedupedYAxes = [visualize.yAxis]; — since Visualize now has a single yAxis, the array has one element. dedupeArray is no longer needed. The import was removed. This is correct. Not a bug.

title: LayoutGrid grid-template-columns changed from minmax(1fr, 195px) to minmax(195px, 1fr) — column width semantics reversed
body: The medium breakpoint grid-template-columns changed from minmax(1fr, 195px) 1fr to minmax(195px, 1fr) 1.5fr. The original minmax(1fr, 195px) means the first column is at least 1fr (flexible) and at most 195px — so it shrinks to content but caps at 195px. The new minmax(195px, 1fr) means at least 195px and at most 1fr — so it's at least 195px wide and can grow. This is a significant layout change: the filters column is now guaranteed to be at least 195px wide (previously it could shrink below 195px if content was narrow). The second column also changed from 1fr to 1.5fr (wider). This changes the dashboard layout proportions. Should be verified as intentional.

title: getExploreUrl visualize uses yAxes array — but the Explore page now expects single yAxis per visualize
body: const exploreUrl = getExploreUrl({ ..., visualize: [{ chartType, yAxes }], ... }); — the visualize object uses yAxes (array). The Explore page's getVisualizesFromLocation parses BaseVisualize objects with yAxes arrays and expands them into individual Visualize instances (one per yAxis). So passing yAxes as an array is correct for the URL format — the Explore page will expand it. This is the BaseVisualize format, which is what the URL expects. Not a bug.

title: handleSearchChange parameter typed as `any` — should be string
body: const handleSearchChange = (query: any) => { — the query parameter is typed as any. It's passed to setSearchString(query) (expects string) and getSuggestedTransactions(query) (expects string). The BaseSearchBar onChange likely passes a string. The `any` type is unnecessary and hides potential type errors. Should be (query: string).

title: miseryRenderer created from periodTableData?.meta — but weekMisery uses same renderer with weekRow data
body: const miseryRenderer = periodTableData?.meta && getFieldRenderer('user_misery()', periodTableData.meta, false); — the renderer is created from periodTableData.meta. Then weekMisery = weekRow && miseryRenderer?.(weekRow, {organization, location, theme}). The renderer is used with weekRow data but created from periodTableData.meta. If the meta differs between period and week data (e.g., different units or types), the renderer may format weekRow incorrectly. Should create a separate renderer from weekTableData.meta or verify the metas are identical.

title: getTraceAttributesTreeActions receives projectIds from findSpanAttributeValue(attributes, 'project_id') — but attributes is the full list, not filtered
body: getCustomActions={getTraceAttributesTreeActions({ location, organization, projectIds: findSpanAttributeValue(attributes, 'project_id') })} — `attributes` is the full attributes prop (not sortedAndFilteredAttributes). This is correct — the actions should have access to all attributes, not just the filtered/searched ones. Not a bug.

title: Flex component with ref={setRef} — Flex may not forward ref to DOM element
body: <Flex ref={setRef} justify="space-between"> — the Flex component from sentry/components/core/layout must forward the ref to the underlying DOM element for the ResizeObserver to work. If Flex doesn't use React.forwardRef, the ref would be null and the ResizeObserver would never be set up. Should verify Flex forwards refs, or use a plain div with display: flex styles.

title: Flex with direction="column" flex={1} — flex prop may not be supported, and height: 100% from original FlexBox is lost
body: The original FlexBox had height: 100%. The new <Flex direction="column" flex={1}> doesn't have height: 100%. If the parent container has a defined height, flex={1} (flex-grow: 1) would make the Flex fill available space. But without height: 100%, if the parent's height is determined by content (not a fixed/flex parent), the Flex may not fill the full height. The original height: 100% ensured the Flex fills its parent. The new version relies on flex-grow, which requires the parent to be a flex container with a defined height. Should verify the parent is a flex container or add height: 100% via style prop.

title: Type annotation improvement — no functional change
body: The flamegraphFrameFilter type changed from ((frame: Frame) => boolean) | undefined to (frame: Frame) => boolean, and the returned arrow functions now have explicit (frame: Frame) parameter types. This is a type accuracy improvement with no runtime change. Not a bug or issue.

title: Project lookup changed from URL query param to replayRecord.project_id — but replayRecord may be undefined initially
body: The project lookup changed from useLocationQuery({fields: {project: decodeScalar}}) to useProjectFromId({project_id: replayRecord?.project_id}). If replayRecord is undefined (still loading), project_id is undefined, and useProjectFromId returns undefined. The query is disabled (enabled checks project?.slug), so no request fires. But the "Project not found" check (replayRecord?.project_id && !project) would be false (replayRecord?.project_id is undefined), so the error message doesn't show. When replayRecord loads, project_id becomes defined, and if the project isn't found, the error shows. This is correct behavior. But if replayRecord is undefined, the component falls through to isPending check — the useApiQuery isPending would be true (query disabled but still pending?), so the loading indicator shows. This is correct.

title: PercentInput disabled when bulk edit enabled but not active — but the input is still rendered and may be focusable
body: The PercentInput is disabled when !hasAccess || (isBulkEditEnabled && !isBulkEditActive). When disabled, the input has disabled attribute. But the Tooltip wrapper around it: <Tooltip disabled={hasAccess} title={...}><PercentInput disabled={...} /></Tooltip>. If hasAccess is false, the Tooltip is enabled (shows "You do not have permission..."). The disabled input inside a Tooltip — the Tooltip may not trigger on a disabled input (disabled elements don't fire mouse events in some browsers). The tooltip may not show for users without access. Should wrap the Tooltip around a span or use a different pattern for disabled elements.

title: EventSelector onChange uses options?.value but Select may pass the value directly
body: Same issue as previously noted: onChange={(options: any) => { onEventSelect(options?.value); }}. The Select component's onChange signature should be verified. If it passes the selected value directly (string), options?.value is undefined. The `any` type hides this. Should check the Select component's API.

title: Flex.Item grow={1} used to replace FlexContainer — verify Flex.Item supports grow prop
body: The change replaces <FlexContainer> (styled div with flex: 1) with <Flex.Item grow={1}>. Same concern as codeSnippet.tsx — Flex.Item must support the grow prop. If it does, flex-grow: 1 is applied. If not, the layout breaks (the description won't take available space, and the Metadata will not be pushed to the right).

title: codeOwnersUrl === 'unknown' check — string comparison with magic value
body: {codeowner.codeOwnersUrl === 'unknown' ? null : (<StyledExternalLink href={codeowner.codeOwnersUrl}>...)}. The magic string 'unknown' is used to indicate no URL. This is fragile — if the API returns a different sentinel (e.g., null, empty string, or 'N/A'), the check fails and a broken link is rendered. Should check for falsy values or a proper null/empty check.

title: response.allowedOrigins.join(' ') and response.redirectUris.join(' ') — same null safety issue as previously noted
body: Same issue: if the API returns null for allowedOrigins or redirectUris, .join(' ') throws. Should use (response.allowedOrigins ?? []).join(' ') or (response.redirectUris ?? []).join(' ').

title: TabularColumnFixture default type is 'string' — but TabularColumn.type is AttributeValueType which includes null
body: The fixture returns type: 'string' as default. TabularColumn.type is AttributeValueType | undefined. 'string' is a valid AttributeValueType. The fixture is correct. Not a gap.

title: TabularColumnsFixture maps params to TabularColumnFixture — straightforward, no issues
body: The fixture is a simple mapper. No issues. Not a gap.

title: Test updated to expect 'off' default — but doesn't test migration of existing 'low' values
body: The test asserts the default is now "off" instead of "low". But there's no test verifying that existing projects with "low" explicitly set retain their value, or that projects without explicit setting get "off". The default change is tested, but the migration/rollout behavior (how existing projects are affected) is not tested. Should add a test for a project with no explicit option (gets "off") vs a project with explicit "low" (retains "low").

title: Test updated to expect 'off' default — same gap as test_project_details.py
body: The serializer test asserts autofixAutomationTuning == "off" by default. Same gap: no test for existing projects with explicit "low" value retaining it. The default change is tested but the backward compatibility is not.

title: test_get_with_error stores event and replay but doesn't test the case where nodestore returns None for an error_id
body: The test test_get_with_error verifies that error details are included in the Seer request. But it doesn't test the case where nodestore returns None for an error_id (event not found). The fetch_error_details function filters out None data (if data is not None), but the zip misalignment bug (see related finding) means the test might pass even with misaligned data. Should add a test with a missing event to verify the filtering works correctly.

title: Owner tests don't verify audit log entry is created for owner changes
body: The update() method in detector.py creates an audit entry (create_audit_entry) after saving. The owner tests verify the owner is set correctly but don't verify that the audit log entry includes the owner change. Should assert that the audit log data reflects the owner change.

title: test_simple and other get_groups_to_fire tests now pass dcg_to_slow_conditions — but don't test the case where slow conditions change between calls
body: The tests pass self.dcg_to_slow_conditions computed in setUp. But the refactor moved the computation from inside get_groups_to_fire to the caller (process_delayed_workflows). The tests verify get_groups_to_fire works with pre-computed slow conditions. But they don't test that process_delayed_workflows correctly computes and passes the slow conditions. The integration of the refactor is not tested — only the individual functions with manually provided inputs.

title: OrganizationEventsStatsTopNEventsLogs only has one test — minimal coverage for logs top events
body: The comment says "This is implemented almost exactly the same as spans, add a simple test case for a sanity check". One test is provided. But the spans version (OrganizationEventsStatsTopNEventsSpans) has many tests (test_simple_top_events, test_top_events_with_groupby, etc.). The logs version only has test_simple_top_events. If the logs implementation diverges from spans in the future, the lack of tests would hide regressions. Should add more test cases mirroring the spans tests, or at least test with groupby and multiple yAxes.

title: Unauthenticated endpoint logs full request bodies, enabling log injection and sensitive data leakage
body: The endpoint has `permission_classes = ()` and is CSRF-exempt, so any anonymous caller can POST arbitrary JSON. Line 93 does `logger.info("browser_report_received", extra={"request_body": request.data})`, logging the entire unvalidated request body (which can be arbitrarily large and attacker-controlled) at INFO level. This is a log-injection / log-flooding vector (attacker-controlled content written to application logs, potentially breaking log parsers or filling disk) and a sensitive-data exposure risk (any data a browser or attacker sends is persisted to logs). The raw body is also logged again at line 102 (`extra={"data_type": ..., "data": raw_data}`) for non-list payloads. The endpoint should not log full request bodies; it should log only counts/types or a size limit, and should enforce a maximum request size.

title: Unbounded array of reports validated and processed per request enables DoS
body: The endpoint accepts a JSON array of reports with no limit on the number of items (`raw_data` is checked only with `isinstance(raw_data, list)`). It then constructs a `BrowserReportSerializer` for every element (lines 108-120) and iterates all validated reports to emit metrics (lines 123-128). A single request with millions of tiny report objects forces millions of serializer instantiations and metric emissions, allowing an anonymous caller (the endpoint has `permission_classes = ()`) to exhaust CPU/memory. There should be a maximum report count per request (e.g. reject arrays larger than N with 422/413) and ideally a request body size limit.

title: zip() pairs error_ids with events.values() in arbitrary dict order, mis-associating errors with IDs
body: In `fetch_error_details`, `node_ids` is built in the order of `error_ids`, but `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a dict whose iteration order is not guaranteed to match the input order. The list comprehension then does `zip(error_ids, events.values())`, so each `event_id` may be paired with a different event's data. The resulting `ErrorEvent` objects would carry the wrong `id` (and wrong title/message/timestamp), corrupting the error context sent to Seer and producing misleading summaries. The code should look up each event by its own node id, e.g. `[... for event_id in error_ids if (data := events.get(Event.generate_node_id(project_id, event_id))) is not None]`.

title: response[0] indexing assumes a replay row exists; crashes with IndexError when the replay is not found
body: `error_ids = response[0].get("error_ids", []) if response else []` guards against an empty list, but `process_raw_response` may return a list whose first element is not a dict containing `error_ids` (e.g. when the requested fields don't include `error_ids`, or the replay_id doesn't match any row but a row is still returned). If `response[0]` lacks `error_ids`, `.get` returns `[]` which is fine, but if `response` is a non-empty list of unexpected shape (or `response[0]` is `None`), this raises an unhandled exception and returns a 500. More importantly, when the replay does not exist, the code proceeds to fetch segments and call Seer instead of returning 404, wasting resources. The code should explicitly check that the replay was found (e.g. `if not response or not response[0].get("error_ids")`) and return a 404/empty result.

title: delete_matched_rows deletes only the last replay_id due to loop variable reuse
body: In `delete_matched_rows`, the loop `for row in rows: delete_replay_recordings(project_id, row)` is followed by `delete_replays(project_id, [row["replay_id"] for row in rows])`. The second comprehension reuses the name `row`, which in Python 3 does NOT leak the loop variable... however, the actual bug is different: the list comprehension `[row["replay_id"] for row in rows]` is correct. Re-examining: the real issue is that `delete_replay_recordings` is called per-row (fine), but `delete_replays` publishes archive events for all replay_ids — that part is correct. The actual defect: `delete_matched_rows` returns `None` always and the function deletes recordings row-by-row, but if `rows` is empty it returns early — OK. The genuine bug: the comprehension variable `row` shadows nothing harmful. After careful review, the concrete defect is that `delete_replay_recordings` spawns a `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=100)` per row (line 74), so for a batch of N rows it creates N thread pools of 100 threads each — up to 100*N threads — exhausting resources. This is a performance/concurrency bug: the thread pool should be created once for the whole batch.

title: A ThreadPoolExecutor with 100 workers is created per matched row, causing thread explosion
body: `delete_replay_recordings` creates `cf.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=100)` inside the function, and `delete_matched_rows` calls it once per row in a loop. For a batch of 100 rows, this creates 100 thread pools × 100 threads = up to 10,000 threads (though pools are closed after each call, they are created and destroyed serially, so peak is 100 threads at a time but with heavy churn). More importantly, `pool.map` results are not consumed for exceptions — if `_delete_if_exists` raises a non-NotFound exception (e.g. a transient GCS error), `pool.map` will re-raise it only when iterating results, but the results iterator is never consumed, so exceptions are silently swallowed and the `with` block exits without waiting properly... actually `with` calls shutdown(wait=True). The concrete issue: exceptions from `pool.map` are never retrieved because the returned iterator is discarded, so storage deletion failures (other than NotFound) are silently ignored, leaving orphaned blobs while the replay is still marked archived. The code should consume the iterator (e.g. `list(pool.map(...))`) to surface errors, and the pool should be shared across rows.

title: get_merged_pr_single_issue_template calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title which does not exist on that class
body: The new static method `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` (line 596) calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title)`, but `_truncate_title` is defined as a `@staticmethod` on `CommitContextIntegration` (line 577), not on `PRCommentWorkflow`. `PRCommentWorkflow` is a separate class defined later in the same file and has no `_truncate_title` attribute. This will raise `AttributeError` at runtime whenever a merged-PR comment is generated, breaking the GitHub/GitLab PR comment workflow. The call should be `CommitContextIntegration._truncate_title(title)` (or the method should be moved/duplicated onto `PRCommentWorkflow`).

title: _truncate_title is defined on CommitContextIntegration but used as if on PRCommentWorkflow
body: The truncation helper `_truncate_title` is placed on `CommitContextIntegration` (an integration-level class) but is only used by `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template`, which is also on `CommitContextIntegration` yet references `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title`. Beyond the AttributeError (reported separately), the design is confusing: the helper belongs with the PR comment workflow code. Consider moving `_truncate_title` and `ISSUE_TITLE_MAX_LENGTH` next to `PRCommentWorkflow`/`MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE` and calling it directly.

title: Detector owner can be set to any user or team without verifying membership in the organization/project
body: The `owner` field uses `ActorField`, and both `create` (lines 120-127) and `update` (lines 67-79) blindly assign `owner_user_id`/`owner_team_id` from the validated actor without checking that the user is a member of the organization or that the team belongs to the organization/project. A user with detector-edit permission could assign a detector to an arbitrary user ID or team ID (e.g. by crafting `"owner": "user:<id>"` or `"team:<id>"`), causing notifications/ownership to be routed to principals outside the organization, or to nonexistent IDs. The validator should resolve the actor and verify organization membership (and team-in-organization) before persisting, returning 400 otherwise. The new tests (`test_owner_not_in_organization`) suggest this validation is expected but the validator does not implement it.

title: update() reads validated_data["detector_type"] but the serializer field is named "type"
body: In `update`, line 64 does `instance.type = validated_data.get("detector_type", instance.group_type).slug`. The serializer declares the field as `type = serializers.CharField()` (line 35) and `validate_type` returns the GroupType class, so the validated data key is `"type"`, not `"detector_type"`. As written, `validated_data.get("detector_type", ...)` always falls back to `instance.group_type`, meaning a detector type change via PUT is silently ignored. It should be `validated_data.get("type", instance.group_type).slug` (the value being the GroupType class returned by `validate_type`).

title: dcg_to_slow_conditions is computed inside a conditional block, causing NameError when the feature flag is off
body: In `process_delayed_workflows`, `dcg_to_slow_conditions = get_slow_conditions_for_groups(...)` (line 652) is inside an `if` block (guarded by a feature flag, based on the diff context). Later, `get_condition_query_groups(..., dcg_to_slow_conditions)` (line 675) and `get_groups_to_fire(..., dcg_to_slow_conditions)` (line 702) reference the variable unconditionally. When the feature flag is disabled, the assignment never executes and the later references raise `NameError` (or `UnboundLocalError`), crashing delayed workflow processing. The computation should be moved out of the conditional so it always runs.

title: Log message references undefined variable event_data in fire_actions_for_groups
body: The diff changes the logged `extra` from `"event_data": event_data` to `"event_data": workflow_event_data` inside `fire_actions_for_groups`. If `workflow_event_data` is only defined in a narrower scope (e.g. inside a loop or conditional) while the log statement is outside that scope, this raises `NameError`. Based on the diff, the log statement at line ~580 is inside a loop where `workflow_event_data` may be the loop variable — need to verify it is always bound before the log call. If `workflow_event_data` is defined per-iteration and the log is also per-iteration, it's fine; otherwise it's a NameError. Flagging for verification because the rename from `event_data` to `workflow_event_data` suggests a scoping change that could break logging.

title: Removing ParameterizationRegexExperiment breaks the public __all__ contract and any external users
body: The diff removes `ParameterizationRegexExperiment` from `__all__` and deletes the class entirely, and narrows `ParameterizationExperiment` from `ParameterizationCallableExperiment | ParameterizationRegexExperiment` to just `ParameterizationCallableExperiment`. This is a breaking API change: any code (including getsentry or plugins) that imports `ParameterizationRegexExperiment` or passes a regex-based experiment to `Parameterizer(experiments=...)` will now fail at import time or at runtime. Additionally, `parametrize_w_experiments` no longer handles the regex-experiment branch, so if any caller still constructs one it will break. If this removal is intentional, it should be called out as a breaking change and downstream repos (getsentry) must be updated in lockstep; otherwise the class should be retained (deprecated) rather than deleted.

title: Analytics event is recorded before the feature-flag check, inflating metrics for unauthorized requests
body: `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` is called at the top of `post()` (lines 81-86), before the `features.has("organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble", ...)` check (lines 88-91) that returns 404. This means every request from an organization without the feature flag — including unauthenticated probing — is counted as an "assemble" event, polluting analytics and potentially triggering alerts on abuse. The analytics event should be recorded only after the feature check passes (and ideally after the request is validated), or a separate `denied` event should be used.

title: request.user.id will raise AttributeError for org-auth-token authentication
body: The endpoint supports org auth tokens (`is_org_auth_token_auth(request.auth)` is checked at line 137), but line 85 does `user_id=request.user.id`. For token-based authentication, `request.user` may be an `AnonymousUser` (which has `id = None`, so no crash) — but depending on the auth backend, `request.user` could be unset or the token auth path may not populate `request.user` at all, causing an `AttributeError`. The analytics event definition marks `user_id` as `required=False`, so the code should use `getattr(request.user, "id", None)` to be safe.

title: Migration body replaced with a no-op return, but the migration is marked is_post_deployment and may already be recorded as applied
body: The migration previously contained a data migration that converted org-level `SavedSearch` rows into `GroupSearchView` rows. The new body is just `return` with a comment "This migration had an error and was never run. See 0921_...". This is dangerous: if migration 0917 was already recorded as applied in any environment (e.g. because the migration runner marked it complete even though the function errored, or because it ran partially before failing), replacing the body with a no-op means those environments will never perform the conversion, and the data will be permanently lost/inconsistent. The correct approach for fixing a broken data migration is to keep the original migration immutable and add a new corrective migration (which 0921 appears to be), NOT to rewrite the body of an already-shipped migration. Rewriting history of a migration that may have been applied breaks migration consistency. The original body should be restored (or the migration should be squashed/replaced via a proper migration operation), and the fix should live only in 0921.

title: Second revised migration is also a no-op, so the data conversion never actually runs anywhere
body: Migration 0920 (the "revised" migration) also had its body replaced with `return` and the same comment pointing to 0921. Combined with the same change to 0917, this means neither 0917 nor 0920 performs any data conversion. If 0921 is the intended corrective migration, then 0917 and 0920 should retain their original (fixed) logic or be squashed away — but as written, any environment that runs 0917/0920 gets a silent no-op, and if 0921 is the only one with logic, environments that already passed 0917/0920 will still run 0921 (good), but the comments claim the earlier migrations "had an error and were never run" which is an assumption that may not hold. More critically, the test file `tests/sentry/migrations/test_0917_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views.py` was deleted, so there is no test coverage verifying the conversion actually happens. The migrations should be restored to perform the conversion (with the bug fixed), or the no-op should be clearly justified and a test added for 0921.

title: Deleting the migration test removes all coverage for the saved-search-to-view conversion
body: The test file for migration 0917 was deleted entirely. Since the migration body was also turned into a no-op, there is now zero test coverage verifying that org-level SavedSearch rows are converted to GroupSearchView rows. If migration 0921 is the real conversion, a test for 0921 should exist; if not, the deletion of this test leaves the data migration completely unverified. A test should be added for the migration that actually performs the conversion.

title: New table widget branch renders TableWidgetVisualization with empty columns and empty data, discarding all query results
body: In `tableResultComponent`, when the `use-table-widget-visualization` feature flag is on, the code renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />` — hardcoded empty columns and empty data. This completely discards the actual `result.data` and `result.meta` that were just fetched, so every table widget in dashboards would render an empty table for any organization with this feature flag. The props should be wired to the real data: `columns` derived from `fields`/`result.meta` and `tableData={{data: result.data, meta: result.meta}}`. As written, enabling the flag breaks all dashboard table widgets.

title: Visualize.fromJSON now returns an array, breaking the static method's contract and all callers expecting a single Visualize
body: `Visualize.fromJSON` previously returned a single `Visualize`; it now returns `Visualize[]` (line 78-82). The only in-repo caller updated is `aggregateFields.tsx` (`updateLocationWithAggregateFields`), which now does `Visualize.fromJSON(aggregateField)` and maps over the result. But `fromJSON` is a public static method on an exported class; any other caller (including getsentry or code not shown in this diff) that does `const v = Visualize.fromJSON(json)` and then `v.yAxis` will now get `undefined` (since `v` is an array). This is a silent API break. The method should either keep returning a single `Visualize` (when `yAxes` has one element) or be renamed (e.g. `fromJSONMulti`) to make the breaking change explicit.

title: updateLocationWithAggregateFields drops the label when serializing a Visualize via fromJSON
body: In `updateLocationWithAggregateFields`, for a `BaseVisualize` the code does `const visualizes = Visualize.fromJSON(aggregateField); return visualizes.map(visualize => JSON.stringify(visualize.toJSON()))`. `Visualize.fromJSON` constructs each `Visualize` with `label: ''` (hardcoded in `fromJSON`), so the original label (e.g. 'A', 'B') is lost when the location query is updated. Since `getAggregateFieldsFromLocation` re-assigns labels sequentially (`String.fromCharCode(65 + i)`), the labels may be regenerated consistently — but if the input `aggregateFields` contains `Visualize` instances with custom labels (e.g. from the writable page params), those labels are silently discarded. The serialization should preserve the label, e.g. by using the original `Visualize` objects directly rather than round-tripping through `fromJSON`.

title: Attribute key regex rejects keys containing hyphens even though the comment says hyphens are allowed
body: The comment at lines 95-96 says "EAP spans contain tags with illegal characters. SnQL forbids `-` but is allowed in RPC. So add it back later", implying hyphenated keys should be kept. But the validation regex `/^[a-zA-Z0-9_.:-]+$/` includes `-` only inside the character class at the end (`_.:-`), which does allow hyphens... however the second regex `/^tags\[[a-zA-Z0-9_.:-]+,number\]$/` also allows hyphens. Re-checking: the character class `[a-zA-Z0-9_.:-]` — the `-` at the end is a literal hyphen, so hyphens ARE allowed. The actual bug: keys with hyphens pass the regex but the comment says they need to be "added back later" — if the downstream search query builder doesn't re-add the hyphen handling, these keys will produce invalid SnQL. This is more of a latent inconsistency. A more concrete issue: the regex allows `:` and `.` and `_` but rejects keys with other common characters like `/` or spaces, silently dropping valid attributes. This is a data-completeness issue rather than a crash. Flagging as low-confidence; the maintainer should verify the regex matches the actual set of valid EAP attribute keys.

title: API request uses queryKey[0] as URL but spreads queryKey[1].query, fragile to queryKey shape changes
body: `api.requestPromise(queryKey[0], {method: 'GET', query: {...queryKey[1]?.query}})` assumes `queryKey` is a 2-tuple `[url, {query}]`. This works but is fragile; if `traceItemAttributeValuesQueryKey` is ever changed to include additional options (e.g. a third element for `retry`), this breaks silently. More importantly, spreading `{...queryKey[1]?.query}` creates a shallow copy which is fine, but if `query` contains arrays (e.g. `project: string[]`), the spread preserves references — acceptable. This is a minor robustness note, not a functional bug. Downgrading to low.

title: tooFewFeedbacks logic is inverted: shows summary UI when zero feedbacks were used and generation failed
body: `tooFewFeedbacks: data.numFeedbacksUsed === 0 && !data.success` — this is true when zero feedbacks were used AND the request was not successful. The intent (per the name and the component's `tooFewFeedbacks` early-return) is to hide the summary when there isn't enough feedback to summarize. But the condition `!data.success` means: if the API succeeded with 0 feedbacks used (e.g. an empty feedback list), `tooFewFeedbacks` is false, so the component proceeds to render `summary` (which would be `null`), showing an empty summary box. Conversely, if the API failed, `isError` would also be true (depending on status code) and the component returns null anyway. The logic should likely be `data.numFeedbacksUsed === 0` (regardless of success) or `!data.success || data.numFeedbacksUsed < MIN_FEEDBACKS`. As written, the guard does not reliably hide the summary when there are too few feedbacks.

title: Project lookup switched from URL query param to replayRecord.project_id, but the query is enabled before project resolves
body: The code changed from reading `project` from the URL query (`useLocationQuery`) to `useProjectFromId({project_id: replayRecord?.project_id})`. The `useApiQuery` `enabled` condition (line 71-75) requires `project?.slug` to be truthy, so the query won't fire until the project loads — that's fine. However, the new early-return at line 90 (`if (replayRecord?.project_id && !project)`) renders an error "Project not found" — but `useProjectFromId` returns `undefined` while loading, not just when not found. So during the initial loading period, the component will briefly show "Project not found. Unable to load AI summary." before the project resolves, causing a flash of an incorrect error message. The check should distinguish loading from not-found (e.g. use `isLoading` from `useProjectFromId` if available, or check `projects` store).

title: createAISummaryQueryKey called with empty string replayId/projectSlug when data is missing, producing a malformed query key
body: `createAISummaryQueryKey(organization.slug, project?.slug, replayRecord?.id ?? '')` is called unconditionally during render, even when `replayRecord?.id` is undefined or `project?.slug` is undefined. This produces a query key like `/projects/org/undefined/replays//summarize/breadcrumbs/`. Although the query is disabled (`enabled: Boolean(...)`), the malformed key is still constructed and could be used for cache lookups or devtools. It's better to return a stable disabled key or guard the call. Low severity since `enabled` prevents the request.

title: delete_matched_rows deletes recordings row-by-row but only archives the last row's replay_id set — actually archives all, but the per-row recording deletion is inefficient and the function returns None always
body: Re-examining `delete_matched_rows`: it loops `for row in rows: delete_replay_recordings(project_id, row)` then calls `delete_replays(project_id, [row["replay_id"] for row in rows])`. The list comprehension correctly collects all replay_ids (the loop variable `row` in a comprehension has its own scope in Python 3). So all replays are archived. The real issues: (1) `delete_replay_recordings` is called once per row, each creating a ThreadPoolExecutor — inefficient; (2) the function always returns `None` even when `rows` is non-empty, so callers cannot know how many rows were processed; (3) there is no transactional consistency — if recording deletion fails partway, the replay is still archived (marked deleted) but blobs remain, and vice versa. The function should batch the recording deletions and ideally report counts/failures.

title: check_auth_identities unconditionally reschedules check_auth even when called for a single identity
body: `check_auth_identities` always calls `check_auth.apply_async(...)` at line 99, even when invoked directly with a single `auth_identity_id` (the deprecated `check_auth_identity` path delegates to `check_single_auth_identity`, not this, so that's fine). But when called with `auth_identity_ids` from `check_auth`, rescheduling is correct. The issue: if `check_auth_identities` is invoked manually or via the deprecated path with a specific ID, it still enqueues a full `check_auth` scan, causing unnecessary work. This is a minor inefficiency, not a correctness bug. Low severity.

title: processing_deadline_duration added to schedule_webhook_delivery may be too short for large batches
body: `schedule_webhook_delivery` now has `processing_deadline_duration=30` (seconds). If this task iterates over many pending webhook deliveries, 30 seconds may be too short, causing the taskworker to kill the task mid-processing and potentially redeliver/retry, leading to duplicate processing. Without seeing the task body, this is a risk: the deadline should be validated against the expected batch size, or the task should be chunked. Flagging for verification.

title: findAllFieldRefs filters writable aggregateFields with isBaseVisualize but then accesses .yAxes — correct, but the readable branch uses isVisualize and accesses .yAxis; verify consistency
body: In `findAllFieldRefs`, the readable branch (line 358-360) filters with `isVisualize` and maps `visualize.yAxis` — correct for the new single-yAxis `Visualize`. The writable branch (line 375-377) filters with `isBaseVisualize` and flatMaps `visualize.yAxes` — correct for `BaseVisualize`. This is consistent. However, the function name and dual handling suggest complexity; no concrete bug found. Skipping — not reporting.

title: addChart maps over visualizes including the new one, but the new Visualize has no label assigned
body: In `addChart`, `new Visualize(DEFAULT_VISUALIZATION)` is created without a `label` option, so `label` defaults to `''`. The existing visualizes have labels 'A', 'B', etc. The new chart gets an empty label, so `shouldRenderLabel` (visualizes.length > 1) will render an empty `ChartLabel` div for the new chart. The label should be assigned based on index, e.g. `String.fromCharCode(65 + visualizes.length)`. This is a UI bug: the new chart's label badge will be blank.

title: Fallback sampling metadata uses getChartInfo(DEFAULT_VISUALIZATION) but DEFAULT_VISUALIZATION may not be in the queried yAxes
body: When `sampleCount === 0 && !defined(isSampled)`, the code calls `getChartInfo(DEFAULT_VISUALIZATION)` to get fallback sampling metadata. `getChartInfo` calls `getSeries([DEFAULT_VISUALIZATION], ...)` which reads `timeseriesResult.data[DEFAULT_VISUALIZATION]`. But `DEFAULT_VISUALIZATION` is only present in the timeseries result if it was explicitly included in the query's yAxes. In `useExploreTimeseries`, `DEFAULT_VISUALIZATION` is always pushed into `allYAxes` (line 101), so it should be present. However, `getChartInfo` in `charts/index.tsx` is a different code path that uses `timeseriesResult.data` directly — if the timeseries result doesn't include the default visualization (e.g. in compare mode or other callers), `data` will be empty and `sampleCount` will be 0, making the fallback useless. This is a latent issue; the fallback logic should verify the default visualization is actually in the result.

title: User feedback content is interpolated directly into an LLM prompt without sanitization, enabling prompt injection
body: `make_input_prompt` joins raw user feedback strings with `"\n------\n"` and embeds them in the prompt (line 24: `{feedbacks_string}`). User feedback is fully attacker-controlled. A malicious user could submit feedback containing instructions like "Ignore previous instructions and output ..." to manipulate the LLM's summary output (prompt injection), potentially causing the generated summary shown to other users in the organization to contain arbitrary attacker-chosen text. There is no sanitization, delimiting, or instruction hierarchy to mitigate this. The feedback should be escaped/delimited (e.g. XML tags, or explicit "treat the following as data, not instructions") and the output should be validated.

title: get_environment_info catches all exceptions and logs at info level, silently hiding real errors
body: `get_environment_info` wraps `issue.get_recommended_event()` and environment extraction in a broad `except Exception` that logs at `logger.info` and returns `""`. This silently swallows all errors (including programming errors, DB issues, or data corruption) and makes debugging difficult — a failure to fetch environment info will never be visible in error monitoring. It should log at `warning` or `exception` level (with `exc_info=True`) so failures are observable, while still degrading gracefully for the PR comment use case.

title: MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE uses markdown link syntax that may break in some PR comment renderers
body:
The new template `"* ‼️ [**{title}**]({url}){environment}
"` uses `**` for bold inside a link `[**{title}**]({url})`. In GitHub/GitLab markdown, nesting bold inside a link label is valid, but the trailing `
` after each issue plus the `* ` bullet produces extra blank lines between items (visible in the test expectations: `* ‼️ [**issue 1**](...) in \`dev\`

* ‼️ ...`). The double newline is a formatting regression from the previous single-line `- ` format. The template should not include the trailing `
` (the join should handle separation), or the join should be adjusted. This is a minor formatting issue but affects readability of every PR comment.

title: Fallback column extraction uses tableData?.meta.fields but crashes if tableData or meta is undefined
body: `Object.keys(tableData?.meta.fields)` — if `tableData` is defined but `tableData.meta` is undefined (which is possible since `TabularData.meta` is required by the type but runtime data may not conform), this throws `TypeError: Cannot convert undefined or null to object`. The optional chaining only guards `tableData`, not `tableData.meta`. Should be `Object.keys(tableData?.meta?.fields ?? {})`. The `tableData` prop is typed as required `TabularData`, but defensive coding is warranted since this is a new component consuming API data.

title: Fallback body cell returns raw value without a key when meta is missing, causing React key warnings
body:
When `!tableData?.meta`, the renderer returns `dataRow[column.key]` directly (line 77) without wrapping it in an element with a `key`. The caller (`GridEditable`) likely expects a keyed element. The other branch wraps in a `
`. The fallback should also be wrapped: `return
{dataRow[column.key]}
` or the raw value should be returned with a key. Low severity but will cause React reconciliation warnings.

title: Changing DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT from "low" to "off" changes behavior for all existing projects without migration
body: The default for `sentry:autofix_automation_tuning` changed from `"low"` to `"off"` in both `constants.py` and `projectoptions/defaults.py`. This is a behavioral change: projects that have never explicitly set this option will now default to `"off"` instead of `"low"`, meaning autofix automation that previously ran at low frequency will stop running entirely. This silently disables a feature for existing customers. If this is intentional, it should be communicated as a breaking change and ideally gated behind a feature flag or a migration that sets the option explicitly for existing projects. The tests were updated to expect `"off"`, confirming the change is deliberate, but the impact on existing projects is significant.

title: Removing the grouping.experiments.parameterization.traceparent option registration may break projects that have it set
body: The option `grouping.experiments.parameterization.traceparent` was removed from `defaults.py`. If any project has this option set in the database, reading it via `options.get(...)` will now return the default (0.0) instead of the stored value, silently changing grouping experiment behavior. Options should generally be deprecated (kept registered with default 0.0) rather than removed, unless a migration cleans up stored values. Verify that no code still reads this option, or keep the registration with a zero default.

title: run_top_events_timeseries_query now accepts equations but the underlying rpc_dataset_common function signature must support it
body: The new `equations` parameter is passed through to `rpc_dataset_common.run_top_events_timeseries_query`. If that function doesn't accept an `equations` keyword, this will raise `TypeError` at runtime. The diff shows the parameter is added and forwarded, but the callee's signature isn't shown. Verify that `rpc_dataset_common.run_top_events_timeseries_query` accepts `equations`; otherwise this is a crash for any caller using the ourlogs top-events path.

title: makeTraceItemAttributeKeysQueryOptions omits environment intentionally but the comment is misleading
body: The comment says "environment left out intentionally as it's not supported" — but the previous implementation (in the old `useTraceItemAttributeKeys`) DID include `environment: selection.environments` in the query. Removing it changes behavior: attribute keys will now be fetched across all environments instead of the selected ones, potentially returning different (broader) results and breaking environment-scoped search. If the backend endpoint doesn't support environment filtering, that's a backend limitation, but the frontend should either pass it (if supported) or clearly document the behavior change. This is a functional regression for users who rely on environment-scoped attribute suggestions.

title: Regex for attribute keys allows hyphen but the second alternative for tags[...,number] has the hyphen in a different position, potentially inconsistent
body: The two regexes are `/^[a-zA-Z0-9_.:-]+$/` and `/^tags\[[a-zA-Z0-9_.:-]+,number\]$/`. In the first, the character class is `[a-zA-Z0-9_.:-]` where `-` at the end is literal. In the second, same class. They are consistent. However, the first regex allows `:` and `.` and `_` but the `tags[...]` form requires the key inside brackets to match the same class — a key like `foo-bar` matches both. No bug found; skipping.

title: Removing the 'Type' row from grouping variant display loses information about the variant type
body: The diff removes the `Type` row (with explanatory tooltips) from all variant cases (COMPONENT, CUSTOM_FINGERPRINT, BUILT_IN_FINGERPRINT, SALTED_COMPONENT, PERFORMANCE_PROBLEM). This removes the `variant.type` value and its helpful tooltip from the UI. If this is intentional (the title already shows the description), fine; but the tooltips contained useful explanations of what each variant type means. Verify this is a deliberate UX decision and not an accidental deletion.

title: Visualize constructor always sets stack='all', removing the previous behavior of unstacked bars for multi-yAxis visualizes
body: Previously, `this.stack = this.chartType === ChartType.BAR && this.yAxes.length > 1 ? undefined : 'all'` — multi-yAxis bar charts were unstacked. Now `this.stack = 'all'` unconditionally (line 49). Since `Visualize` now always has a single yAxis, `yAxes.length > 1` is never true, so the condition would always be `'all'` anyway. But the test `uses unstacked bar graph` was removed, confirming the behavior change. For single-yAxis bar charts, stacking is irrelevant (one series), so this is fine. However, if multiple `Visualize` instances are rendered on the same chart (overlays), they will now all have `stack='all'`, which may cause them to stack when they previously wouldn't. Verify that multiple bar-chart visualizes on the same chart should stack.

title: Removing the multi-yAxis check from useTopEvents may enable top-N for queries that previously didn't support it
body: The check `if (visualizes.some(visualize => visualize.yAxes.length > 1)) return undefined;` was removed. Since `Visualize` now always has a single yAxis, this check would never trigger anyway. But the semantic was: top-N is disabled when a single visualize had multiple yAxes (which no longer exists). With the new model, each visualize is a separate chart, so top-N per chart is fine. No bug; the removal is correct given the refactor.

title: isVisualize type guard checks for 'yAxis' but BaseVisualize uses 'yAxes'; a BaseVisualize with yAxes will fail isVisualize, which is correct, but the naming is confusing and the guard may misclassify
body: `isVisualize` checks `'yAxis' in value && typeof value.yAxis === 'string'` — this correctly identifies the new single-yAxis `Visualize` and rejects `BaseVisualize` (which has `yAxes`). `isBaseVisualize` checks `Array.isArray(value.yAxes)`. These are mutually exclusive and correct. However, in `getAggregateFieldsFromLocation`, the loop checks `isGroupBy` then `isBaseVisualize` — a `Visualize` instance (which has `yAxis`, not `yAxes`) will fail `isBaseVisualize` and be silently dropped from `aggregateFields`! If `rawAggregateFields` contains a serialized `Visualize` (with `yAxis` instead of `yAxes`), it won't match `isBaseVisualize` and won't be added. But `parseGroupByOrBaseVisualize` only returns `GroupBy | BaseVisualize | null`, and `parseBaseVisualize` requires `Array.isArray(parsed.yAxes)`, so a `Visualize.toJSON()` (which produces `{yAxes: [yAxis]}`) is a valid `BaseVisualize`. So the round-trip is consistent. No bug found; skipping.

title: handleApply serializes Visualize via toJSON() but the onColumnsChange type expects BaseAggregateField[]; GroupBy objects are passed through unchanged — verify the consumer handles both
body: `onColumnsChange(tempColumns.map(col => (isVisualize(col) ? col.toJSON() : col)))` — `isVisualize` checks for `yAxis`, and `Visualize.toJSON()` returns `{yAxes: [yAxis], chartType?}` which is a `BaseVisualize`. `GroupBy` objects are passed as-is. The `onColumnsChange` prop type is `(columns: BaseAggregateField[]) => void` where `BaseAggregateField = GroupBy | BaseVisualize`. This is correct. No bug.

title: Compare Queries link uses visualizeYAxes[0]! which may be undefined if visualizes is empty
body: `yAxes: [visualizeYAxes[0]!]` — if `visualizes` is empty, `visualizeYAxes[0]` is `undefined`, and the non-null assertion `!` only suppresses the TypeScript error, not the runtime value. The resulting query would have `yAxes: [undefined]`, producing a malformed compare URL. There should be a guard (e.g. disable the button or return early if `visualizes.length === 0`).

title: DEFAULT_VISUALIZATION is pushed into allYAxes unconditionally, but if visualizes already contains it, dedupeArray handles it; however the sort() may reorder it unexpectedly
body: `allYAxes.push(DEFAULT_VISUALIZATION); return dedupeArray(allYAxes).sort();` — the `.sort()` sorts alphabetically, so DEFAULT_VISUALIZATION may not be first. This is fine for the query (order doesn't matter for yAxes), but consumers that assume `yAxes[0]` is the default may break. In `useExploreTimeseries`, the result is passed to `useSortedTimeSeries` which returns data keyed by yAxis, so order doesn't matter. No bug.

title: viewSamplesTarget iterates visualizes and extracts parsedFunction.arguments[0] but no longer iterates yAxes; for a Visualize with an equation (no arguments), the field is skipped — correct, but verify equations are handled
body: The loop `for (const visualize of visualizes)` now does `parseFunction(visualize.yAxis)` once. If `visualize.yAxis` is an equation (e.g. `count() / count()`), `parseFunction` returns null and the field is skipped — correct, since equations don't have a single argument field. No bug.

title: Adding referrer to getAlertsUrl is correct, but the exploreUrl does not include referrer in the same way — verify consistency
body: The diff adds `referrer` to `getAlertsUrl` but `getExploreUrl` already had `referrer` passed (line 56). This is consistent. No bug.

title: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES are only filtered when a search query is present; without a search they are still shown
body: The filter `!HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(attribute.name)` is only applied inside the `if (searchQuery.trim())` branch (line 65-69). When there is no search query, `sortedAndFilteredAttributes` returns `sorted` (all attributes), including `is_segment`, `project_id`, and `received`. So the hidden attributes are shown by default and only hidden when the user searches. The intent (per the constant name `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES`) is clearly to always hide them. The filter should be applied unconditionally: `sorted.filter(attr => !HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(attr.name))` and then additionally filter by search query if present.

title: chapterData maps over summaryData?.data.time_ranges but summaryData is already checked non-null above; optional chaining is redundant but harmless
body: Line 122 uses `summaryData?.data.time_ranges.map(...)` but `summaryData` was already checked at line 114 (`if (!summaryData)`). The optional chaining is redundant. More importantly, `summaryData.data` could be undefined if the API returns `{data: null}`, causing a crash. Should be `summaryData.data?.time_ranges?.map(...) ?? []`. Low severity.

title: Placeholder shown during isPending but the hook returns isPending=true only when data is undefined; after error, isPending is false and isError is true, so the error branch returns null — correct, but the loading state may flash
body: The component checks `isError` before `isPending`, so on error it returns null (no flash). On pending, it shows a Placeholder. This is correct. No bug.

title: Entire request payload is buffered in memory as a JSON string before sending to Seer
body: `analyze_recording_segments` builds `request_data = json.dumps({"logs": get_request_data(...)})` (line 177), which materializes the entire list of log messages (all breadcrumbs + errors for the whole replay) in memory as a single JSON string. For long replays with many breadcrumbs, this can be very large (tens of MB), causing high memory usage and slow serialization. The comment at line 185 acknowledges "Request isn't streaming. Limitation of Seer authentication." This is a known limitation but still a real performance/memory risk for large replays. Consider chunking or streaming if Seer supports it, or at least capping the number of breadcrumbs sent.

title: error_events.sort mutates the caller's list in place, which may be unexpected
body: `get_request_data` does `error_events.sort(key=lambda x: x["timestamp"])` (line 138), mutating the list passed in. The caller (`analyze_recording_segments` via `functools.partial`) passes the same list to the paginator's `on_results`, which may be called multiple times or the list may be used elsewhere. In-place mutation is a side effect that could cause issues if the list is reused. Should use `sorted(error_events, key=...)` instead.

title: Error events are interleaved with breadcrumbs by timestamp comparison, but breadcrumb timestamps are in seconds while error timestamps may be in a different unit
body: In `gen_request_data`, the comparison `error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"] < event.get("timestamp", 0)` assumes both are in the same unit. `ErrorEvent.timestamp` comes from `data.get("timestamp", 0.0)` (line 115), which is the event's timestamp (typically seconds since epoch as a float). Breadcrumb `event.get("timestamp", 0)` is the replay breadcrumb timestamp (also seconds since epoch, relative to replay start or absolute?). If breadcrumb timestamps are relative (e.g. milliseconds since replay start) and error timestamps are absolute (epoch seconds), the comparison is meaningless and errors will be interleaved incorrectly. The test `test_get_request_data` uses small floats (1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0) for both, so it passes, but real data may have mismatched scales. Verify the units match.

title: get_slow_conditions_for_groups is now called once in process_delayed_workflows but the functions still accept it as a parameter; verify no double-fetching
body: Previously, `get_condition_query_groups` and `get_groups_to_fire` each called `get_slow_conditions_for_groups` internally. Now the caller computes it once and passes it in. This is an improvement (avoids duplicate DB queries). However, the diff shows the computation is inside a feature-flag conditional (see separate finding about NameError). If the flag is on, the computation happens once — good. If off, NameError. The performance fix is correct; the scoping bug is reported separately.

title: Logger switched from logging.getLogger to log_context.get_logger — verify log_context is properly initialized in all task contexts
body: The logger was changed from `logging.getLogger(__name__)` to `log_context.get_logger(__name__)`. `log_context` is a workflow-engine-specific context logger that relies on `log_context.root()` / `WorkflowEventContext` being set. If `process_workflows` is called from a context where `log_context` isn't initialized (e.g. a task that doesn't use `@log_context.root()`), the logger may not emit or may raise. Verify that all entry points to `process_workflows` set up the log context.

title: defaultSortBys receives visualizes.map(v => v.yAxis) but the function signature expects yAxes: string[] — correct, but the mode check uses fields.includes('timestamp') which may not be populated yet
body: In `defaultPageParams`, `defaultSortBys(mode, fields, aggregateFields.filter(isVisualize).map(visualize => visualize.yAxis))` — `fields` here is the raw fields list which may not include 'timestamp' yet (it's populated later). If `fields` is empty, `defaultSortBys` returns `[]` for SAMPLES mode, meaning no default sort. This may be intentional. No concrete bug.

title: else branch assumes aggregateField is a Visualize with yAxis, but the type is AggregateField = GroupBy | Visualize; isGroupBy was checked, so the else is Visualize — correct
body: The `else` branch (line 77-82) assumes the field is a `Visualize` and accesses `.yAxis`. Since `isGroupBy` was checked first, the else is indeed `Visualize`. Correct. No bug.

title: visualizes analytics field changed from raw Visualize[] to visualizes.map(v => v.toJSON()) — verify the analytics schema expects the serialized form

But if consumers try to invalidate by API URL (e.g. `queryClient.invalidateQueries(['/organizations/.../trace-items/attributes/'])`), it won't match. This is a minor cache-invalidation concern. The previous implementation used `useApiQuery` with the API path as the key, which is more conventional. Consider using the API path as part of the query key for consistency.
