The second branch has no method: SMS filter, so any WorkflowReminder with retryCount>1 is deleted regardless of method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) and regardless of scheduled/scheduledDate. The comment and intent is SMS-only cleanup. This causes data loss for other channels if they ever use retryCount and can delete future scheduled reminders. Fix by AND-ing method SMS (and scheduled:false) into the retryCount branch.

title: Non-atomic retryCount increment loses retries
body: In scheduleSMSReminders.ts both failure paths do data: {retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1} using the value read at the start of the cron run. If two cron invocations overlap or the same reminder is processed concurrently, both read the same value and write back the same increment, losing one retry. The reminder can then never reach the >1 threshold and be retried forever. Use atomic Prisma update data: {retryCount: {increment: 1}} instead of read-modify-write.

title: Missing number / empty message never counts as retry
body: In scheduleSMSReminders.ts the send is guarded by if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo) with no else. When sendTo is missing/empty (e.g. invalid or absent smsReminderNumber, the exact case this PR claims to fix) or message is empty, the loop does nothing: no scheduled flag, no retryCount increment. The same row is fetched again on every cron tick until scheduledDate passes, defeating the 2-strike retry limit. The same applies to the continue when workflowStep/booking is missing. Increment retryCount or delete in those no-op paths.

title: Retry-count cleanup deletes non-SMS reminders
body: The deleteMany uses OR: [SMS + past scheduledDate, retryCount > 1]. The second branch has no method filter, so any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1 will be deleted regardless of method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP, SMS). Today only the SMS path increments the column so the blast radius is limited, but the predicate is wrong and will delete unrelated reminder types as soon as they ever use retryCount. It should be ANDed with method: SMS.

title: Missing sendTo/message never increments retryCount, infinite retry remains
body: Retry increment only happens inside if (message?.length && sendTo) in the else branch, or in the catch block. If sendTo is empty (e.g. missing smsReminderNumber / sendTo number) or message is empty, the loop iteration does nothing - no scheduled flag, no retryCount increment, no delete. That reminder will be re-fetched by every cron run until its scheduledDate passes, which is exactly the endless rescheduling for invalid/missing numbers this PR claims to fix.

title: Non-atomic retryCount increment from stale read
body: The code updates retryCount with data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 } using the value read earlier in findMany. If two cron instances / overlapping runs process the same reminder, one increment is lost. Use an atomic increment operation instead of read-modify-write so retries are counted correctly.

title: Retry-count cleanup deletes non-SMS reminders
body: The deleteMany uses OR: [{method:SMS, scheduledDate lte now}, {retryCount gt 1}]. The second branch has no method filter and no scheduled:false filter, so any WorkflowReminder with retryCount>1 is deleted even if method is EMAIL/WHATSAPP or even if scheduled:true with a future scheduledDate and valid Twilio referenceId. That causes data loss and orphaned scheduled sends that can no longer be cancelled. It should be ANDed with method: SMS and scheduled:false.

title: Non-atomic retryCount increment loses counts
body: Both failure paths do data:{retryCount: reminder.retryCount+1} using the value read at the start of the cron run (lines 184 and 195). Overlapping cron executions read the same stale value and overwrite each other, losing a retry and allowing infinite retries. Use atomic update data:{retryCount:{increment:1}} instead.

title: Missing sendTo/message never increments retryCount
body: If message is empty or sendTo is falsy the if (message?.length && sendTo) block does nothing and falls through without updating retryCount or scheduled. Such reminders, e.g. missing/invalid smsReminderNumber, are refetched every cron run until scheduledDate passes, defeating the stated goal of deleting after 2 failures. The failure/skip path must also increment retryCount or otherwise resolve the reminder.

title: Public findMany method deleted without migration
body: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts previously exposed findMany(findManyArgs) that applied authorization and filter conditions via a Prisma where clause. This PR deletes that method and only exposes getBaseConditions() returning Prisma.Sql for manual $queryRaw use. Any existing caller that still calls service.findMany() will fail at compile time / throw TypeError: service.findMany is not a function at runtime. Deleting a public service method in the same change that converts internals to raw SQL is a breaking contract change and requires updating all call sites in the same PR.

title: toEqual on Prisma.Sql compares template segmentation, not SQL semantics
body: The test at packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:295 expects team/org/combined conditions with expect(conditions).toEqual(Prisma.sql`...flat template...`). The service builds the same SQL text via nested interpolation, e.g. Prisma.sql`(${acc}) OR (${condition})` and Prisma.sql`(${acc}) AND (${condition})` in buildOrgAuthorizationCondition, buildTeamAuthorizationCondition and buildFilterConditions. Prisma.Sql stores strings[] plus values[]; nested Sql values are flattened by splicing, so the resulting strings[] segmentation differs from a hand-written flat template even when the final SQL text and bound values are identical. toEqual therefore fails on false negatives, making the authorization/filter tests red while the query is semantically correct. Tests should compare rendered SQL plus values or execute the query instead of deep-equaling Sql objects.

title: Org-scope expectation assumes deterministic DB row order
body: The org-scope test at packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:333 expects teamIds = [org.id, team.id, team2.id, team3.id] and userIds = [user.id, user2.id, user3.id] in that exact order. The service builds those arrays from TeamRepository.findAllByParentId and MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds with no ORDER BY. Database return order is undefined, so the ANY(...) arrays can come back in any order. The test will flake or fail when Postgres returns rows in a different order even though authorization is correct. The test must sort both expected and actual arrays or assert order-insensitively.

title: Public findMany method removed without caller migration
body: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts replaces the public findMany(findManyArgs) method that queried bookingTimeStatusDenormalized with getBaseConditions() returning Prisma.Sql. The diff deletes findMany and no other file in this PR updates callers. Any existing caller using service.findMany({ select, where }) will fail to compile or throw at runtime, which is a breaking contract change.

title: Org/team ANY() SQL never executed against database
body: packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts only executes user-scope conditions via prisma.$queryRaw. Team-scope and org-scope authorization uses teamId = ANY(array) and userId = ANY(array) raw SQL, but those tests only compare Prisma.sql objects with toEqual and never run them. A syntax, type-cast, or array-binding error in the ANY queries would pass tests and fail in production with over- or under-authorization.

title: Org scope drops personal bookings when org has no child teams
body: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts in buildOrgAuthorizationCondition only loads memberships when teamsFromOrg.length > 0. When an organization has no child teams, teamIds is still [orgId] but userIdsFromOrg is forced to []. The resulting org condition then contains only teamId = ANY(...) AND isTeamBooking = true and omits the userId = ANY(...) AND isTeamBooking = false branch, so org admins see zero personal bookings instead of org members personal bookings.

title: Public findMany() removed without migrating callers
body: insightsBooking.ts replaces the public findMany(findManyArgs) method that wrapped prisma.bookingTimeStatusDenormalized.findMany with where AND [auth, filter] with a new getBaseConditions() that returns Prisma.Sql for use with $queryRaw. The PR only changes the service and its test. Any existing production caller that imports InsightsBookingService and calls findMany will fail TypeScript compilation or throw at runtime, and any extra where/select logic previously merged by findMany is now silently dropped unless every caller is rewritten to compose raw SQL.

title: Event-type filter OR fragment lacks parentheses
body: buildFilterConditions pushes Prisma.sql `("eventTypeId" = id) OR ("eventParentId" = id)` with no surrounding parentheses. getFilterConditions is public and returns that fragment directly. If a caller interpolates it as WHERE X AND <fragment> without adding its own parentheses, SQL AND binds tighter than OR, turning (A OR B) AND C into A OR (B AND C) style logic. That changes which bookings match and can return rows that should have been filtered out. The fragment itself should be parenthesized.

title: ANY() org/team SQL never executed against the database
body: The only test that executes SQL via prisma.$queryRaw SELECT id FROM BookingTimeStatusDenormalized WHERE baseConditions uses scope user, whose auth SQL is scalar userId equality plus teamId IS NULL. The org-scope and team-scope branches that use teamId = ANY(array) and userId = ANY(array) are only compared with toEqual against Prisma.sql objects and never run against Postgres. Parameter binding, array serialization, type casts, NULL handling, and quoted identifier errors in those high-risk branches would still pass the suite.

title: Org/team SQL expectations depend on nondeterministic DB order
body: The org-scope test expects teamIds = [org, team, team2, team3] and userIds = [user, user2, user3] in creation order via toEqual on Prisma.Sql values. The service builds those arrays from TeamRepository.findAllByParentId and MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds with no ORDER BY, so return order is undefined. The test is order-sensitive while = ANY() semantics are order-insensitive, making the test flaky and unable to distinguish a real logic error from a different row order.

title: updateMany with empty data throws / never bumps updatedAt
body: CalendarService.ts calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) with an empty data object. Prisma rejects updateMany when data is empty (Argument `data` must not be empty), so fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache will throw after it just wrote the cache, breaking watch/subscribe flow. Even if accepted, an empty update does not explicitly set updatedAt, so the intended 'touch SelectedCalendar.updatedAt' does not happen. Pass an explicit timestamp e.g. { updatedAt: new Date() } or remove the call.

title: Delete-cache success never refreshes cache status
body: CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx defines deleteCacheMutation with only showToast + onSuccess callback, while the disconnectMutation in the same file invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars and viewer.apps.integrations onSettled. After deleting calendarCache rows the connectedCalendars query still holds the old cacheUpdatedAt, so the dropdown continues to show stale Last updated and Delete option until a full reload. Invalidate connectedCalendars after deleteCache settles.

title: Cache status ignores expiry, shows dead cache as active
body: calendar-cache.repository.ts getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups by credentialId with no expiresAt filter, while getCachedAvailability in the same file only returns rows with expiresAt >= now. Expired rows therefore still produce a max(updatedAt) that the UI renders as Cache Status / Last updated, misleading users into thinking live cache exists and offering delete for inert data. Add expiresAt: { gte: new Date() } to the status query.

title: Throws generic Error instead of TRPCError for auth failure
body: deleteCache.handler.ts throws new Error("Credential not found or access denied") when the credential is not owned by ctx.user. A generic Error surfaces as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN, conflates missing vs forbidden, and breaks client error handling conventions used by other routers that throw TRPCError with a code. Use TRPCError with code NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN.

title: Cache timestamp hardcodes en-US locale
body: CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx formats cacheUpdatedAt with new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...) even though the component already has useLocale/t(). Users in other locales see US short date/time format inconsistent with the rest of the app. Use the active locale from useLocale instead of a hardcoded string.

title: macOS-only sed breaks script on Linux
body: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh runs sed -i '' -E to rewrite GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL. The empty backup-suffix argument is BSD/macOS syntax; on GNU/Linux sed it is parsed as an input file and fails, so the helper cannot update .env on Linux dev machines/CI. Detect OS or use a portable sed invocation.

title: updateMany with empty data will throw
body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) with empty data. Prisma rejects updateMany when data is empty (Invalid invocation: data must not be empty), so every cache warm-up will now throw after writing the cache. Pass an explicit field like { updatedAt: new Date() } or remove the call.

title: Delete-cache success never invalidates cache status query
body: deleteCacheMutation onSuccess only shows a toast and calls onSuccess?.(), while disconnectMutation invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars and viewer.apps.integrations onSettled. After deleting cached data the connectedCalendars query still holds the old cacheUpdatedAt, so the dropdown keeps showing a stale Last updated timestamp until a manual refetch.

title: Cache status ignores expiry, shows stale cache
body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups all CalendarCache rows by credentialId with no expiresAt filter, while getCachedAvailability only honors rows with expiresAt >= now. A credential whose rows are all expired will still report an updatedAt and the UI will offer Delete cached data for unusable cache.

title: macOS-only sed breaks script on Linux
body: The script uses sed -i '' -E to rewrite GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL. The empty backup-suffix argument is BSD/macOS syntax; on GNU/Linux sed it is parsed as an input file and fails, so the helper cannot update the env file on Linux/CI containers. Use a portable update or detect OS.

title: Auth failure throws generic Error instead of TRPCError
body: When the credential is not found or belongs to another user the handler throws new Error("Credential not found or access denied"). Other viewer routers use TRPCError with NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN codes, so clients cannot distinguish auth failure from an internal error and get a 500 instead of a coded error.

title: updateManyByCredentialId called with empty data throws
body: CalendarService.ts line 1024 calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) with an empty data object. Prisma rejects updateMany with empty data with a validation error ("data must not be empty"), so every execution of fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache will throw after writing the cache instead of touching SelectedCalendar.updatedAt. This breaks the cache-warming path that runs after watching calendars. Pass an explicit touch like { updatedAt: new Date() } or remove the call.

title: Delete-cache success never refreshes cache status
body: CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx defines deleteCacheMutation with onSuccess that only shows a toast and calls onSuccess?.(), but unlike disconnectMutation it never invalidates trpc.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. The cacheUpdatedAt prop comes from that query, so after deleting the cache the dropdown will keep showing the old "Last updated" timestamp until a manual refetch. Invalidate the connectedCalendars query on success/settled.

title: Cache status includes expired rows
body: CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups by credentialId with no expiresAt filter, while getCachedAvailability only honors rows with expiresAt >= now. A credential whose rows are all expired will still return a max(updatedAt) and the UI will show "Cache Status / Last updated" and offer deletion for a cache that is effectively unusable. Filter the groupBy to non-expired rows (expiresAt gte now) or otherwise distinguish no-valid-cache.

title: Generic Error instead of typed TRPC error for auth failure
body: deleteCache.handler.ts throws new Error("Credential not found or access denied") when the credential is not owned by the caller. Thrown as a generic Error this surfaces as an internal server error instead of NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN, loses the intended authorization semantics, and is inconsistent with tRPC error handling. Throw a TRPCError with code NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN.

title: Cache timestamp hardcoded to en-US locale
body: CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx formats cacheUpdatedAt with new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...), ignoring the user's locale from useLocale. Users in other locales will see a US-only date format inconsistent with the rest of the app. Use the active locale for formatting.

title: macOS-only sed breaks script on Linux
body: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh updates GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL with sed -i '' -E, which is macOS/BSD syntax. On Linux/GNU sed the empty '' is treated as a filename and the script fails to update ../.env. The script also uses a relative ENV_FILE ("../.env") that depends on cwd. Make the in-place edit portable (detect OS or use a temp file) and resolve the env path relative to the script.

title: dev:cron switched to tsx without dependency
body: apps/web/package.json changes dev:cron to "npx tsx cron-tester.ts" but tsx is not added to dependencies or devDependencies (only ts-node is). On clean installs, offline CI, or pinned environments npx may fail or fetch an unpinned version, while neighboring scripts still use ts-node. Add tsx as a devDependency or keep ts-node.

title: immediateDelete cancels SendGrid but never deletes DB row
body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder with immediateDelete=true (used for reschedule in handleNewBooking.ts and for workflow/step delete in workflows.tsx) POSTs batch cancel to SendGrid and then returns without deleting or updating the workflowReminder row. The row stays with scheduled=true and the old referenceId. For reschedule there is no cascade delete, so orphan rows accumulate, are never marked cancelled for the cron to pick up, and past-date cleanup is the only eventual removal. Fix must delete the reminder row after successful SendGrid cancel.

title: One SendGrid failure aborts all pending email cancellations
body: The cron wraps the entire for-loop of SendGrid cancel calls and the Prisma deletes in a single try/catch. If client.request throws for any one reminder, the loop aborts, remaining reminders are never attempted, and the workflowRemindersToDelete array built so far is never awaited because Promise.all is skipped on exception. One bad batch_id therefore leaves all other cancelled emails scheduled and they will still be sent. Handle each reminder independently.

title: Cancel query too broad and past-cancelled rows deleted without SendGrid cancel
body: remindersToCancel filters only on cancelled:true and scheduledDate, with no method=EMAIL, scheduled=true, or referenceId-not-null filter, so it can attempt SendGrid cancel with batch_id null and fail the whole batch. Worse, the earlier deleteMany at line 34 deletes all EMAIL reminders with scheduledDate in the past, including cancelled ones, without calling SendGrid. Those rows disappear from the cancel query so their scheduled sends are never cancelled. Filter the cancel query and run cancels before blind past-date deletes.

title: Paid bookings return before workflow reminders are cancelled
body: When booking.paid is true the handler refunds, updates status to REJECTED, awaits apiDeletes and returns at line 464. The workflow-reminder cancellation loop at lines 485-493 is below that return and never runs for this path. Paid cancelled bookings therefore keep their scheduled email/SMS workflowReminders and the reminders are still sent. Move reminder cancellation before the paid early-return or duplicate it there.

title: Async reminder cancellations fired without await
body: updatedBookings.forEach calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder, both async functions doing Prisma updates and SendGrid/Twilio calls, without awaiting or collecting promises. The same fire-and-forget forEach pattern is repeated in handleNewBooking.ts reschedule, bookings.tsx requestReschedule, and workflows.tsx. The request can finish and return success before the cancelled flag is persisted, errors are swallowed, and try/catch around forEach cannot catch them. Await with Promise.all.

title: immediateDelete cancels SendGrid but never deletes DB row
body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder with immediateDelete=true does client.request cancel then returns without deleting or marking the WorkflowReminder row. The SMS version deletes the row, and cascade only cleans workflow-delete cases. For the reschedule path in handleNewBooking.ts the old booking row remains scheduled:true with no cancelled flag, so it is never retried by the cron and lingers until past-date cleanup. If the SendGrid cancel fails the email can still be sent with no retry.

title: One SendGrid failure aborts all pending cancellations
body: The for loop awaits client.request for each reminder to cancel and only after the loop runs Promise.all of queued prisma deletes. Any throw jumps to the outer catch, skipping remaining reminders and discarding deletes already queued in workflowRemindersToDelete. One bad batch_id therefore prevents cancellation/deletion of all other cancelled reminders in that cron run, leaving them to be sent.

title: Workflow reminder cancels fire-and-forget in forEach
body: updatedBookings.forEach calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder / deleteScheduledSMSReminder which are async prisma/twilio/SendGrid operations, but forEach is not awaited and the promises are not added to prismaPromises. The handler can return and finish the request before cancelled=true is persisted or SMS is cancelled/deleted, so the cron can still see/schedule the reminder and the email/SMS is still sent.

title: Reschedule reminder cancels not awaited
body: bookingToReschedule.workflowReminders.forEach invokes async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder without awaiting or collecting promises. The DB update to cancelled=true or delete may not complete before subsequent calendar/email work, so a concurrently running scheduleEmailReminders cron can still schedule/send the old reminder.

title: Reschedule cleanup uses async forEach without await
body: originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach calls async delete functions inside a try/catch but never awaits them. Exceptions from the async callbacks become unhandled rejections not caught by the surrounding try, and the SendGrid cancel / DB delete may not finish before reschedule proceeds, leaving old reminders active.

title: SMS DB row leaked when Twilio cancel fails
body: deleteScheduledSMSReminder does await twilio.cancelSMS then prisma delete in the same try. If cancelSMS throws because the message was already sent, failed, or the SID is invalid, the delete is skipped and the catch only logs. The WorkflowReminder row remains forever as scheduled, leaking data and confusing later workflow edit/delete logic. The row should be deleted even if provider cancel fails.

title: Cron can schedule email after concurrent cancel
body: unscheduledReminders is fetched without excluding cancelled=true and booking status is never re-checked. The loop then calls sgMail.send before the prisma update. If a booking is cancelled between the findMany and the send, handleCancelBooking will delete/mark the row but the cron has already sent the email via SendGrid. The send should happen after re-validating the reminder still exists and is not cancelled, or the update should precede the external send.

title: immediateDelete path cancels SendGrid but never deletes DB row
body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder with immediateDelete=true POSTs status=cancel to SendGrid and then returns without deleting or updating the WorkflowReminder row. Callers in handleNewBooking reschedule path and workflows delete/step-delete paths rely on this to remove the reminder, so the row stays in the DB with scheduled=true and the same referenceId. For reschedule there is no cascade delete, so orphan scheduled rows accumulate and will later be cleaned only as past-due without ever being cancelled in some paths.

title: Bulk email cancel aborts and skips DB deletes on first failure
body: The cron loops with await client.request inside try, pushes prisma.workflowReminder.delete promises, and only after the loop does Promise.all. If any single SendGrid cancel throws, control jumps to catch, the Promise.all is never reached, so even reminders already cancelled in SendGrid are never deleted from the DB. They will be retried every 15 minutes and re-cancelled, and a single bad batch_id blocks all other cancellations in that run.

title: Unscheduled-reminder query can schedule cancelled reminders
body: unscheduledReminders finds method=EMAIL, scheduled=false, scheduledDate within 72h with no filter on cancelled. Any row with cancelled=true and scheduled=false would still be sent via SendGrid and then marked scheduled=true. The new design keeps cancelled rows in the DB until the cron cancels them, so the schedule path must exclude cancelled=true or a cancelled booking can still get emails.

title: Cancel query not scoped to EMAIL/scheduled reminders with referenceId
body: remindersToCancel selects only cancelled=true and scheduledDate, with no method=EMAIL, scheduled=true, or referenceId not null filter. SMS reminders use Twilio SIDs not SendGrid batch_ids and email rows without referenceId have nothing to cancel in SendGrid. If such a row ever has cancelled=true the job will POST a Twilio SID or null batch_id to /v3/user/scheduled_sends and then delete the row, which is wrong and hides the logic error.

title: Past-due delete runs before cancel and drops cancelled sends
body: The handler first deleteMany all EMAIL reminders with scheduledDate <= now without cancelling them in SendGrid, then queries cancelled reminders within the next hour. Past-due cancelled rows are deleted without ever attempting SendGrid cancel. If the cron was down or missed the 1-hour window, the email may already have been sent, but the ordering guarantees no cancel attempt is made.

title: Workflow reminder cancellations not awaited
body: updatedBookings.forEach calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder without await or Promise.all, and the same fire-and-forget forEach pattern is repeated in handleNewBooking, bookings.tsx requestReschedule, and workflows.tsx. The async Prisma update/cancel and external SendGrid/Twilio calls run in background, so the API can return before cancellation is persisted, errors become unhandled rejections only logged inside the helper, and process shutdown loses cancellations.

title: Recurring cancel deletions never awaited
body: In handleCancelBooking.ts the code iterates calendar credentials with `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... apiDeletes.push(await calendar?.deleteEvent(...)) })`. A `forEach` with an async callback is fire-and-forget; the outer function does not await the callbacks. Later the code does `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))`, but at that point `apiDeletes` has not yet been populated by the still-pending callbacks. Consequence: for recurring cancellations with `allRemainingBookings`, calendar deletions are lost or race with the response, leaving stale events on external calendars and incorrect availability.

title: Reschedule deletions fire-and-forget via async forEach
body: In bookings.tsx `requestReschedule` does `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { if (...) { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); } else ... return deleteMeeting(...) })` with no await on the loop and no `Promise.all`. The returned promises from `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` are also not awaited or collected. Consequence: the handler sends the reschedule email and webhooks before old calendar/video events are deleted, failures become unhandled rejections, and old time slots may never be freed, causing double-bookings.

title: Async forEach leaves calendar/video deletes unawaited
body: In vital/lib/reschedule.ts the code does `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); return deleteMeeting(...) })` inside a `try` block. `forEach` does not await async callbacks, so the `try/catch` cannot catch asynchronous rejections and the function proceeds to send email and `return true` immediately. Consequence: deletion errors are silently lost as unhandled rejections and reschedule can report success while external calendar/video events remain.

title: Async forEach leaves calendar/video deletes unawaited
body: In wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts the code does `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); return deleteMeeting(...) })` inside a `try` block. `forEach` does not await async callbacks, so the `try/catch` cannot catch asynchronous rejections and the function proceeds to send email and `return true` immediately. Consequence: deletion errors are silently lost as unhandled rejections and reschedule can report success while external calendar/video events remain.

title: getCalendarCredentials now returns promises in sync API
body: In CalendarManager.ts `getCalendarCredentials` is still a synchronous function but now does `const calendar = getCalendar(credential)` where `getCalendar` is async and returns `Promise<Calendar|null>`. The returned objects therefore contain `calendar: Promise` instead of `Calendar|null`. Only `getConnectedCalendars` was updated to `await item.calendar`. Any other consumer of this exported function expecting a truthy calendar instance or calling calendar methods directly will get a Promise object (always truthy) and fail. The contract change is invisible in the sync signature and breaks callers and type expectations.

title: Recurring calendar deletes lost by async forEach race
body: In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts line 460 the code does .filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); }). Because forEach does not await the async callback, the outer function continues immediately to await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) at line 652 while the callbacks are still suspended on await getCalendar. apiDeletes is therefore still empty or partial when it is concatenated, so calendar deleteEvent calls for recurring bookings (allRemainingBookings path) are never awaited and may never be pushed. Consequence is cancelled recurring bookings remain on external calendars (Google/Outlook) and orphaned events.

title: Reschedule calendar/video cleanup fire-and-forget
body: In packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts line 125 bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar ... return calendar?.deleteEvent ... return deleteMeeting ... }) is not awaited and its returned promises are discarded. The surrounding try/catch cannot catch async rejections, the function can return true and send reschedule email before deletions finish, and any rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection. Consequence is old calendar events/video meetings are not reliably deleted on reschedule, leaking bookings on providers.

title: Reschedule calendar/video cleanup fire-and-forget
body: In packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts line 125 bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar ... return calendar?.deleteEvent ... }) is not awaited and results are discarded. The try/catch around forEach only covers synchronous setup, not the async deletions. Consequence is reschedule returns before external calendar/video deletion completes and failures are silently lost, leaving stale events on providers.

title: requestReschedule deletions never awaited
body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx line 553 bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar ... return calendar?.deleteEvent ... return deleteMeeting ... }) fires async work without collecting promises. The mutation then sends reschedule email and webhooks without waiting for deletions. Consequence is previous time is not reliably freed on external calendars/video apps and errors are unhandled, same leak as other reschedule paths.

title: Dynamic imports are still eager, no lazy loading
body: In packages/app-store/index.ts lines 3-30 the store is built as { applecalendar: import("./applecalendar"), ... }. Each import() expression executes immediately when the index module is imported, starting load of all ~31 apps at startup. Awaiting later does not defer loading. Consequence is the PR does not achieve lazy/code-split loading; startup still pays cost of loading every calendar/video/payment app, and a single failing app rejects its stored promise for all future awaits.

title: One failed calendar import fails all availability
body: In packages/core/CalendarManager.ts line 142 const calendars = await Promise.all(calendarCredentials.map((credential) => getCalendar(credential))) awaits all dynamic imports together. Previously getCalendar was synchronous and returned null for unknown types; now a rejected import (missing module, load error) rejects the whole Promise.all. Consequence is getCachedResults throws and returns no busy times for any calendar when a single credential's app fails to load, instead of skipping that calendar.

title: Recurring cancel calendar deletes never awaited
body: In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts the recurring-cancel path does bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); for (...) { const deletedEvent = await calendar?.deleteEvent(...); apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); } }). forEach does not wait for async callbacks, so the outer handler continues to Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) while apiDeletes is still empty. The pushed deleteEvent promises are added after the Promise.all has already been constructed, so recurring booking cancellations leak events on external calendars and apiDeletes never reflects failures.

title: Async forEach fire-and-forget calendar/video deletes
body: In packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... return deleteMeeting(...) }) is not awaited and its returned promises are discarded. The surrounding try/catch cannot catch async rejections from forEach callbacks, and the function returns true and sends reschedule email without waiting for calendar.deleteEvent or video deleteMeeting to finish. Failed deletions are silently lost and previous time is not freed.

title: Async forEach fire-and-forget calendar/video deletes
body: In packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... }) is not awaited and its promises are discarded. The surrounding try/catch cannot observe async errors, and the function proceeds to send reschedule email and return true before deletions complete. Calendar and video cancellations can be skipped or fail silently.

title: Async forEach fire-and-forget reschedule deletes
body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx requestReschedule does bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... return deleteMeeting(...) }) without awaiting the callbacks or collecting promises. Deletion of the old calendar/video events runs detached from the mutation, errors are unhandled, and the reschedule email and webhook are sent regardless of whether the old slot was freed.

title: getCalendarCredentials now returns promises as calendar
body: In packages/core/CalendarManager.ts getCalendarCredentials still runs synchronously but now stores const calendar = getCalendar(credential) where getCalendar returns Promise<Calendar|null>. Its return value changed from {integration, credential, calendar: Calendar|null} to {integration, credential, calendar: Promise<Calendar|null>} without changing the function signature to async. Only getConnectedCalendars was updated to await item.calendar; any other caller expecting a sync Calendar instance will receive a Promise object, treat it as truthy, and call calendar methods on a Promise at runtime.

title: Dayjs objects compared with === never equal
body: In checkIfIsAvailable the code tests `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` to detect a zero-length date override (day marked unavailable). `dayjs()` returns an object, so `===` compares object identity and is always false. As a result a full-day block is never detected, `dateOverrideExist` stays true and the function later returns true (available). A day the host blocked off will still show bookable slots and can be booked.

title: Working-hours end check ignores event length
body: In checkIfIsAvailable both `start` and `end` are computed as `slotStartTime.hour()*60+slotStartTime.minute()`. `end` never adds `eventLength`. A slot that starts inside working hours but ends after `workingHour.endTime` (e.g. 60-min event starting 30 min before close) passes the check and is reported available, allowing bookings that overflow availability.

title: Working-hours check fails with split hours
body: In checkIfIsAvailable availability is rejected if `workingHours.find(workingHour => slot is outside that workingHour)` finds any entry. If a user has two intervals on the same weekday (e.g. morning and afternoon), a slot inside one interval is outside the other, so `find` always succeeds and every slot is marked unavailable. The correct test is that a slot is available if it is inside any interval, not that it is outside any interval. Fixed hosts with split hours will show no slots.

title: Date-override containment misses slots overflowing the override
body: In checkIfIsAvailable a slot is deemed outside a date override only if `slotEnd <= overrideStart` or `slotStart > overrideEnd`. A slot that starts inside the override but ends after `override.end` (e.g. override 10:00-11:00, slot 10:30-11:30) satisfies neither condition, so `find` returns undefined and the slot is treated as inside the override and returned as available. This allows bookings that extend beyond the override window. The same block also uses `isAfter` instead of same-or-after for the end boundary, so a slot starting exactly at override end is treated as inside.

title: Timezone offset computed from Date.toString()
body: In getSlots the offsets are computed as `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` and `.tz(timeZone)`. `Date.toString()` produces a locale-dependent string without explicit offset that dayjs must re-parse, which can lose the original instant, depend on server locale, and give the wrong `utcOffset()` around DST. The Date object should be passed directly to dayjs, e.g. `dayjs(override.start).tz(...)`, to preserve the instant.

title: Date-override timezone shift drops day rollover
body: In getSlots an override is converted to invitee minutes-since-midnight via `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset).hour()*60+minute`. Only hour/minute are kept and the result is applied to the original `startOfInviteeDay`. If the invitee-organizer offset moves the override across midnight, the portion belonging to the adjacent invitee day is still placed on the original day (or `start >= end` and skipped entirely). This creates slots on the wrong day or drops availability for timezones far apart.

title: Dayjs objects compared with === so full-day block never detected
body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts line 114 checkIfIsAvailable does `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` to detect a zero-length date override meaning unavailable all day. Dayjs objects are objects, so === is always false even when times are equal. The find callback therefore never returns true for that case, dateOverrideExist stays true, and the function later returns true meaning available. A full-day unavailable override will incorrectly show slots as bookable.

title: Slot ending after date-override end is treated as available
body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts checkIfIsAvailable only rejects a slot if slotEnd is before/same as override start or slotStart is after override end. It never checks if slotEnd is after override end. For example override 10:00-11:00 and slot 10:30-11:30 will not match either outside condition, so find returns falsy, dateOverrideExist is true and the function returns true. This allows bookings that extend past the override to be shown as available.

title: Multiple date overrides on same day require slot to be inside all overrides
body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts checkIfIsAvailable uses `dateOverrides.find(date => slot is outside date)` to decide unavailable. If a day has split overrides e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-18:00, a slot at 10:00 is inside the first but outside the second, so find matches the second and returns false. Correct logic is unavailable only if outside every override (inside none). This will incorrectly hide valid slots on split days.

title: Working-hours check ignores event length and fails on split hours
body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts lines 139-147 the working-hours guard computes `start` and `end` both as slotStart hour*60+minute, never adding eventLength, and uses `find` meaning any workingHours entry that does not contain the start rejects the slot. A 60-min slot starting at 17:45 with hours ending 18:00 passes even though it overruns, and a day with two intervals e.g. morning/afternoon will reject a slot valid in one interval because it is outside the other. This exposes out-of-hours slots and hides valid split-day slots.

title: Date-override comparison mixes server-local and UTC timezones
body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts checkIfIsAvailable builds `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset)` without utc() while slot times are `time.utc()`. dayjs(Date) renders in server local timezone, so format YYYY MM DD and isBefore/isSame/isAfter compare different zones. On a server not running UTC the day equality and boundary checks shift by the server offset, causing overrides to apply to the wrong day or allow/deny wrong slots.

title: Override offset uses toString parsing and may crash on missing timezone
body: In packages/lib/slots.ts lines 212-213 the code does `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()`. toString produces a locale-dependent string with server zone abbreviation which dayjs parsing can misinterpret, and override.timeZone is optional per schedule.d.ts. If undefined, tz(undefined) can throw or return wrong offset, breaking slot generation or shifting overrides by hours/DST. It should parse the Date as UTC instant e.g. dayjs.utc(override.start).tz().

title: No test for fixed-host round-robin date overrides
body: The PR description claims to fix round-robin fixed-host date overrides, but apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts only adds a timezone variant of the single-user date-override test. There is no scenario with schedulingType ROUND_ROBIN plus hosts with isFixed and differing overrides, so the main fixed-host regression has no coverage and could regress silently.

title: Date-override unavailable-day check uses reference equality and never matches
body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts checkIfIsAvailable compares two newly created Dayjs objects with ===. Two different objects are never ===, so the empty-override (start == end means day is unavailable) branch never returns true. Because dateOverrideExist is still set to true, execution falls through to if (dateOverrideExist) return true, marking slots on an unavailable day as available and allowing booking when the host blocked the whole day.

title: Working-hours end check ignores event length
body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts checkIfIsAvailable computes both start and end as slotStartTime.hour()*60+slotStartTime.minute(). The slot end time (start + eventLength) is never used. A slot starting inside working hours but ending outside (e.g. 30-min slot at 17:45 with hours ending at 18:00 for a 60-min event) is treated as inside, so events can be booked past the end of working hours.

title: Split working hours incorrectly marked unavailable
body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts checkIfIsAvailable uses workingHours.find(h => outside) to reject a slot. When a user has two intervals on the same day (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00), a slot at 10:00 is inside the first interval but outside the second, so find returns the second interval and the slot is rejected as outside working hours. Correct logic must accept if ANY interval for that day contains the slot, not reject if ANY interval does not contain it.

title: Date-override day matching uses server-local time and wrong date basis
body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts checkIfIsAvailable computes utcOffset from organizerTimeZone then does dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset).format('YYYY MM DD') compared to slotStartTime.format where slotStartTime is UTC. dayjs(date.start) without tz renders in the server local timezone, so the result depends on where the server runs, and the comparison is against UTC date instead of organizer-local date. An override at 00:30 organizer time (previous-day UTC) is attributed to the wrong calendar day, causing overrides to be ignored or applied to the wrong day.

title: Date-override timezone shift crashes on missing timezone and drops midnight crossover
body: In packages/lib/slots.ts getSlots does dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset() where TimeRange.timeZone is optional. When undefined, tz(undefined) throws/misbehaves. It also parses via toString() instead of the Date instant, uses only the start instant offset for both start and end, and reduces to hour()*60+minute. An override that shifts across midnight in invitee timezone (e.g. 00:30 organizer becomes previous/next day invitee) loses the day component and is placed on the wrong invitee day, and overrides spanning midnight get start > end and produce no slots.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category is unset
body: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration does execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name='embed_category'")[0]['id']. If the site never set embed_category (default blank) or has no matching category, [0] is nil and calling ['id'] raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration for fresh installs and most existing sites.

title: Migration SQL injection and unnormalized hosts
body: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration interpolates each raw site-setting value directly into SQL: "INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)". A host containing a single quote breaks the statement or injects SQL. It also bypasses EmbeddableHost normalization, so values like 'http://example.com/1234' are stored verbatim while runtime lookup compares only bare hostname, leaving migrated hosts non-matching.

title: before_validation crashes on nil host
body: In app/models/embeddable_host.rb the before_validation block calls self.host.sub! twice without checking presence. Creating an EmbeddableHost with nil/missing host raises NoMethodError instead of a validation error, turning a user error into a 500.

title: update/destroy dereference missing record
body: In app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb update and destroy do EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and then immediately call save_host(host)/host.destroy. For an unknown id host is nil, causing NoMethodError (500) instead of a 404. save_host also assumes params[:embeddable_host] is present.

title: No uniqueness constraint on host
body: In app/models/embeddable_host.rb there is only a format validation and in the migration there is no unique index on embeddable_hosts.host. Duplicate hosts (including case variants, since lookup is lower(host)=?) can be created, allowing ambiguous category mapping and duplicate admin rows.

title: Plural embedded ids assumed to be array
body: In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6 _hydrateEmbedded now calls obj[k].map for any key ending in _ids. If the payload has null, undefined, or a single value for such a key, .map throws TypeError and breaks hydration of the whole record (e.g. embedding). It also stores undefined entries for ids with no match instead of compacting.

title: before_validation crashes on nil host
body: In app/models/embeddable_host.rb the before_validation block calls self.host.sub! unconditionally. If host is nil or blank, this raises NoMethodError instead of failing validation. Any create/update with missing host param therefore 500s instead of returning a validation error.

title: update crashes on unknown id
body: In app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb update does EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first then calls save_host(host) without checking for nil. An unknown or deleted id causes NoMethodError on nil inside save_host instead of 404, resulting in a 500.

title: destroy crashes on unknown id
body: In app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb destroy does EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first then host.destroy without nil check. Requesting a non-existent id raises NoMethodError on nil instead of returning 404/success_json.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category is blank
body: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration does execute(... WHERE s.name='embed_category')[0]['id'].to_i. If embed_category setting is blank, missing, or does not match a category name, [0] is nil and the migration raises NoMethodError and cannot run. The fallback to uncategorized_category_id on line 14 is never reached.

title: SQL injection and unnormalized hosts in migration
body: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb line 25 interpolates raw site-setting value h directly into SQL: VALUES ('#{h}', ...). A host containing a quote breaks the statement or injects SQL; values should be quoted/escaped or inserted via ActiveRecord. It also inserts raw values with scheme/path intact, while EmbeddableHost normalizes to bare hostname, so migrated rows will not match EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? lookups.

title: Host lookup is case-sensitive and drops ports
body: In app/models/embeddable_host.rb record_for_host does where("lower(host) = ?", host) where host is uri.host without downcasing. Because only the column is lowered, lookups with uppercase letters miss, and because uri.host strips :port while the model validation allows and stores host:port, any host configured with a port can never match. Allowed referers are then incorrectly rejected.

title: Fabricator files are swapped
body: spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb now defines only Fabricator(:embeddable_host) while spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines Fabricator(:category) and related category fabricators. The contents are in the wrong files. It happens to load because all fabricators are required, but it breaks the file-to-fabricator convention and will confuse future maintenance or selective loading.

title: _hydrateEmbedded assumes *_ids is always an array
body: In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6 _hydrateEmbedded calls obj[k].map for any key matching *_ids. If the value is null/undefined or a single scalar, this throws TypeError. When individual ids have no matching embedded record, _lookupSubType returns undefined, so the resulting plural array contains undefined entries instead of filtering them out.

title: Migration interpolates host value into raw SQL
body: File db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb builds INSERT with string interpolation of the old site_settings value: VALUES ('#{h}', ...). A host containing a single quote breaks the migration and allows SQL injection. The value comes from user-controlled site settings and must be quoted/sanitized or inserted via ActiveRecord, not string interpolation.

title: Migration crashes if embed_category settings are missing
body: File db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb assumes SELECT queries always return a row and indexes [0]['id'] / [0]['value'] unconditionally. On a fresh install or when embed_category / uncategorized_category_id / embeddable_hosts rows are absent, [0] is nil and the migration raises NoMethodError, blocking db:migrate. Guard for empty results.

title: Update/destroy dereference nil when host not found
body: File app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb does EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first then calls save_host(host) or host.destroy without checking for nil. An unknown id causes NoMethodError and a 500 instead of 404. The same applies to destroy. Return not-found when the record is missing.

title: before_validation crashes on nil host
body: File app/models/embeddable_host.rb calls self.host.sub! twice in before_validation without guarding nil. If host is nil or blank, this raises NoMethodError before format validation can run, turning a validation error into an exception in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host.

title: Host lookup is case-sensitive and ignores port stripping
body: File app/models/embeddable_host.rb queries where("lower(host) = ?", host) with the raw URI host value. The column is lowered but the parameter is not downcased, so mixed-case referers fail to match. It also compares URI.host (no port) against a column that can contain a port, so hosts stored with :port never match. Downcase the parameter and normalize ports on both sides.

title: Only first underscore is normalized for admin check
body: File app/assets/javascripts/discourse/adapters/rest.js.es6 uses type.replace('_','-') which replaces only the first underscore. Any model type with multiple underscores will fail the ADMIN_MODELS check and use the wrong base path. Use a global replace.

title: Plural embedded ids crash on null or contain undefined
body: File app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6 in _hydrateEmbedded assumes any key ending in _ids is an array and calls obj[k].map directly. If the payload has null, missing, or singular values, this throws. Even when it is an array, failed lookups insert undefined entries without filtering. Guard for non-arrays and compact missing lookups.

title: Fabricator files have swapped contents
body: File spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb now defines only Fabricator(:embeddable_host) while spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines the category fabricators. The contents are swapped relative to filenames. It works only because all fabricators are loaded globally, but it is confusing and will break anyone requiring files by name. Put each fabricator in its matching file.

title: No coverage for new admin embedding endpoints
body: Files spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb and spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb only assert subclassing and never exercise create/update/destroy/show, validation errors, auth, or not-found paths. The new controllers and migration logic that replaces site settings are untested and regressions like nil handling would not be caught.

title: Duplicate `downsize` definition shadows 4-arg version
body: app/models/optimized_image.rb defines self.downsize twice: once as (from,to,max_width,max_height,opts) and again as (from,to,dimensions,opts). In Ruby the second definition overwrites the first, so any existing caller using the 4-argument max_width/max_height form will now raise ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments). This silently breaks backward compatibility while adding the new 3-argument form used for percentage downsizing.

title: Loop checks tempfile.size instead of path size, never sees shrink
body: In UploadsController#create_upload the retry loop checks tempfile.size while OptimizedImage.downsize overwrites tempfile.path in place via an external convert process. tempfile.size stats the open file descriptor, which still points to the old inode if the converter unlinks/recreates the path, so the size appears unchanged. The loop then always runs all 5 iterations and shrinks an image to ~0.8^5 (~33%) even when one pass would have sufficed. Use File.size(tempfile.path) to stat the path.

title: In-place downsize with unchecked return risks data loss
body: UploadsController calls OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...) using the same file as source and destination and never checks the return value. If convert/gifsicle fails it can truncate or corrupt the only copy of the upload, and the code retries the same failing command up to 5 times then proceeds to create the Upload from the corrupted/oversized file. Use a separate temp destination and abort/handle error if downsize returns false.

title: Animated downsize passes percentage to gifsicle resize-fit
body: OptimizedImage.downsize_instructions_animated just delegates to resize_instructions_animated, which builds gifsicle --resize-fit <dimensions>. The new upload flow passes "80%" as dimensions. gifsicle expects WxH for --resize-fit, not a percentage, so animated GIF downsizing will fail, return false, and large GIFs will never be reduced to SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.

title: Remote download hardcodes 10MB ignoring site settings
body: FileHelper.download for API-provided URLs was changed from SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes to a hardcoded 10.megabytes. Admins who configured a larger max_image_size_kb will have valid remote images rejected/truncated at 10MB, and the limit no longer tracks configuration. The cap should derive from site settings, e.g. max of image/attachment limits.

title: Client validation hardcodes 10MB and ignores type setting
body: validateUploadedFile replaced Discourse.SiteSettings['max_'+type+'_size_kb'] with hardcoded 10*1024. This ignores both max_image_size_kb and max_attachment_size_kb and breaks admins who raise limits above 10MB (client rejects files server would accept) or lower attachment limits below 10MB (client allows files server will reject). Keep per-type site-setting lookup; if large images are to be downsized server-side the image limit needs explicit handling, not a global hardcode.

title: 413 error message hardcodes 10MB
body: displayErrorForUpload for HTTP 413 replaced Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb with hardcoded 10*1024. The alerted max_size_kb will be wrong whenever the configured limit differs from 10MB, and it always reports the image limit even for attachment uploads. Read the message value from site settings.

title: Duplicate `downsize` definition removes width/height API
body: app/models/optimized_image.rb defines self.downsize twice: at line 145 as (from,to,max_width,max_height,opts) and again at line 149 as (from,to,dimensions,opts). In Ruby the second definition overwrites the first. Any existing caller using the 5-argument form will now get ArgumentError (5 for 3..4) and thumbnail generation breaks. The PR intended to add a new overload but instead deleted the old contract.

title: Stale filesize passed to Upload after in-place downsize
body: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb downsizes the file in place on disk but then calls Upload.create_for with tempfile.size captured from the original Ruby file object. If ImageMagick rewrites/replaces the path, the open Tempfile descriptor still reports the old large size. Validation in the Upload model that uses the passed size will then reject the upload as too large even though the file on disk is now small, defeating the feature, or store an incorrect filesize in the database.

title: In-place convert with same source/dest and unchecked failure
body: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb calls OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%"...) in a loop without checking the return value. Reading and writing the same path with `convert src[0] ... dst` risks truncating/corrupting the file if the converter truncates the output before reading completes. On failure the file size never shrinks but the loop still retries 5 times wasting CPU and then proceeds to create the upload with a corrupt/oversize file.

title: Client validation hardcodes 10MB ignoring site settings
body: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js replaced Discourse.SiteSettings['max_'+type+'_size_kb'] and max_image_size_kb with hardcoded 10*1024 in validateUploadedFile and displayErrorForUpload. Attachments and images now share the same 10MB client limit regardless of max_image_size_kb / max_attachment_size_kb settings. Admins who lowered limits will see client allow uploads the server rejects, and admins who raised limits above 10MB will see client incorrectly reject allowed files.

title: Animated downsize passes percentage to gifsicle --resize-fit
body: app/models/optimized_image.rb downsize_instructions_animated delegates to resize_instructions_animated which builds `gifsicle --resize-fit #{dimensions}`. The new caller in uploads_controller passes dimensions as "80%". gifsicle expects WxH geometry, not a percentage, so animated GIF downsizing will fail, return false, and the retry loop in the controller will spin 5 times without ever shrinking the GIF.

title: Client-side limit hardcoded to 10MB ignoring SiteSettings
body: validateUploadedFile in app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js now uses `10 * 1024` for both `image` and `attachment` types instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` (and displayErrorForUpload at line 246 does the same). This breaks admin configurability: attachments that should respect max_attachment_size_kb and images that should respect max_image_size_kb are both capped at 10MB, so larger allowed files are wrongly rejected client-side and smaller configured limits are not enforced, diverging from server-side validation.

title: Remote download capped at hardcoded 10MB
body: In app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb create_upload downloads API-provided URLs with a hardcoded `10.megabytes` limit instead of `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`. If an admin configures a larger max_image_size_kb, legitimate remote images larger than 10MB are truncated/rejected by FileHelper.download before the new downsize logic can run, so the feature does not work for URL uploads above 10MB.

title: In-place ImageMagick downsize corrupts original
body: In app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb line 67 calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` using the same path for source and destination. ImageMagick `convert` reading and writing the same file can truncate/corrupt the file, especially on failure. On failure the original upload bytes are lost and a partial/corrupt file is then passed to Upload.create_for.

title: Downsize loop ignores conversion failure
body: In app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb the `while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > limit` loop at lines 66-69 never checks the return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize`. A failed conversion still decrements `attempt` and re-stats the same (possibly corrupt/unchanged) file, wasting up to 5 converts and then proceeding to `Upload.create_for` with an still-oversized or corrupted tempfile instead of surfacing an error.

title: Duplicate downsize definition shadows width/height overload
body: In app/models/optimized_image.rb there are two `self.downsize` definitions back-to-back: line 145 `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` and line 149 `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts)`. Ruby has no overloading, so the second overwrites the first. Existing callers using the 5-argument form will have max_width bound to dimensions and max_height bound to opts, producing malformed geometry strings and wrong options and breaking thumbnail/downsize behavior.

title: Nil TopicUser crashes unsubscribe
body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb unsubscribe does TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) then immediately dereferences tu.notification_level. Users who have never entered the topic, who only have implicit regular state, or whose TopicUser was never created have no row, so tu is nil. Any such user clicking the email link gets NoMethodError on nil instead of unsubscribing. Must handle nil by creating/changing via TopicUser.change or defaulting to muted.

title: State-changing unsubscribe on GET
body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb TopicsController#unsubscribe mutates notification_level and calls tu.save! inside a GET action wired in config/routes.rb as get t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe. GETs are prefetched by email scanners, browsers, crawlers and are not CSRF-protected, so merely opening/scanning the email or link can silently change subscription state. State change must be POST/PUT/DELETE with CSRF/form token, or at minimum require confirmation.

title: Unsubscribe lacks visibility check and error handling
body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb unsubscribe builds TopicView.new(params[:topic_id], current_user) and then mutates TopicUser without guardian.ensure_can_see! and without rescuing Discourse::NotFound / Discourse::InvalidAccess the way show does. For private, deleted, secured-category or non-existent topics this raises unhandled 500 or leaks existence via redirect vs exception, and allows notification_level writes for topics the user cannot see. Must authorize visibility before mutating.

title: Unsubscribe only steps down one level, still subscribed
body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb unsubscribe does: if watching/tracking then set to regular else muted. A watching/tracking user clicking To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here from config/locales/server.en.yml ends up on regular and will still receive mentions/replies, contrary to the page copy You will stop receiving notifications and the email promise. Either always mute or fix copy to explain two clicks are required.

title: Email unsubscribe link requires login, fails logged-out
body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb unsubscribe is behind before_filter :ensure_logged_in with no email token, while the link post.topic.unsubscribe_url is sent in notification emails. A recipient opening the email in a logged-out browser, different device, or email client is redirected to login and the unsubscribe never executes, making the advertised per-topic unsubscribe unusable. Needs a signed one-click token like DigestUnsubscribeKey or explicit login-then-confirm flow.

title: Unsubscribe crashes when TopicUser row is missing
body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb TopicsController#unsubscribe does tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) and then immediately reads tu.notification_level. A user who was never tracked in TopicUser (the normal case for a user with default regular level) gets nil, so the request raises NoMethodError and returns 500 instead of unsubscribing. The code must handle nil by creating the row or using TopicUser.change.

title: State-changing GET allows CSRF/crawler unsubscribes
body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb the new TopicsController#unsubscribe is routed via GET in config/routes.rb and unconditionally mutates notification_level then saves. GETs are prefetched by browsers, crawlers, link scanners and can be embedded as an image, so an attacker can force a logged-in victim to be muted from a topic without consent. Mutating actions must not be GET; use POST/PUT with CSRF protection or make GET render-only.

title: Direct save bypasses notification-level side effects
body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb the unsubscribe action assigns tu.notification_level directly and calls tu.save!, instead of using TopicUser.change. TopicUser.change sets notifications_changed_at, notifications_reason_id, publishes MessageBus notification_level_change and runs observe_after_save_callbacks_for. The direct save leaves timestamps/reasons stale and connected clients out of sync.

title: Unsubscribe only steps down one level
body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb the logic is if tu.notification_level > regular then set to regular else set to muted. A watching/tracking user clicking the email Stop receiving notifications link is only demoted to regular and will still receive notifications, contradicting the email and locale text. Repeated visits further demote to muted, so the endpoint is non-idempotent and confusing.

title: New unsubscribe_link interpolation breaks emails without unsubscribe_url
body: In config/locales/server.en.yml unsubscribe_link now requires both %{user_preferences_url} and %{unsubscribe_url}. In lib/email/message_builder.rb MessageBuilder#body and #html_part call I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args) whenever add_unsubscribe_link is true. Any caller that sets add_unsubscribe_link without passing unsubscribe_url now raises I18n missing interpolation and fails to send email. The builder needs a default or fallback when unsubscribe_url is absent.

title: createRecord with existing id duplicates store record
body: In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6 model() does this.store.createRecord('topic', {id: params.id}) then PostStream.loadTopicView. If the topic is already in the Ember store, createRecord creates a second unsaved record with the same id, causing duplicate-record/identity-map conflicts and dirty-state issues. It should find/reuse the existing record, and the promise rejection from loadTopicView is unhandled, leaving a blank page on 404/forbidden.

title: Unsubscribe crashes when no TopicUser row exists
body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb the unsubscribe action does tu = TopicUser.find_by(...) then immediately reads tu.notification_level. A user who was never tracked in the topic (e.g. mentioned by email, first visit via email link) has no row, so find_by returns nil and the request raises NoMethodError on nil, returning 500 instead of unsubscribing.

title: State-changing unsubscribe exposed as GET
body: In config/routes.rb the new endpoints get t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe and get t/:topic_id/unsubscribe map to TopicsController#unsubscribe which mutates TopicUser.notification_level and saves. GETs are not CSRF-protected, are prefetched by email clients/crawlers, and are retried on refresh, so an attacker can force a victim's browser to load an image/URL to silently downgrade their subscription, and a refresh double-applies the downgrade.

title: Direct save bypasses notification-level side effects
body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb unsubscribe mutates tu.notification_level and calls tu.save! directly instead of TopicUser.change. That skips updating notifications_changed_at, notifications_reason_id, MessageBus notification_level_change publish and tracking-state handling done by the canonical path, leaving clients/stale caches out of sync.

title: Watching users need two visits to actually mute
body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb unsubscribe only steps down one level per hit: if level > regular it sets regular, else muted. A watching/tracking user clicking the email link advertised as stop receiving notifications ends up still on regular and still receives notifications, requiring a second visit to reach muted.

title: New unsubscribe_link interpolation breaks emails without unsubscribe_url
body: In config/locales/server.en.yml unsubscribe_link now requires both %{user_preferences_url} and %{unsubscribe_url}. In lib/email/message_builder.rb body and html_part unconditionally interpolate that key whenever add_unsubscribe_link is true. Any existing caller that sets add_unsubscribe_link without passing unsubscribe_url now raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and fails to send the email.

title: Client-side navigation never triggers server unsubscribe
body: In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6 model() only calls PostStream.loadTopicView (TopicsController#show JSON), never the new TopicsController#unsubscribe endpoint. The server downgrade only runs on full-page HTML load, so navigating to /t/slug/id/unsubscribe inside the Ember app shows the page without actually changing the notification level.

title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive, allowing trivial bypass
body: app/models/blocked_email.rb does BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first with the raw submitted value and neither BlockedEmail nor User downcases/normalizes email before this check. PostgreSQL string equality is case-sensitive, so if an admin blocks bad@spammers.org an attacker can register BAD@spammers.org or Bad@Spammers.org, miss the block list, pass EmailValidator, and create the account. The block feature is therefore defeatable by changing case.

title: Validation has DB write side effect, double-counts every signup
body: lib/validators/email_validator.rb calls BlockedEmail.should_block?(value) from validate_each, and should_block? increments match_count and updates last_match_at with save. UsersController#create calls user.valid? and then user.save, which validates again, so one signup attempt increments match_count twice and touches last_match_at twice. Any other valid?/invalid paths also mutate stats even when the user is never saved, making match_count/last_match_at unreliable for abuse monitoring.

title: Non-atomic read-modify-write on match_count loses updates
body: app/models/blocked_email.rb implements stats as record.match_count += 1; record.last_match_at = ...; record.save. Under two concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked email both threads read the same count, increment locally, and save, so one increment is lost. It also runs full validations/callbacks and touches updated_at for a stats counter. Use an atomic increment such as increment_counter/update_counters/update_all instead.

title: Wrong Ember dependent key means rejected email never shows invalid
body: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/create_account_controller.js declares emailValidation as .property('accountEmail', 'rejectedEmails.@each') but rejectedEmails is an array of plain strings. @each only observes properties on array members, not array membership, so pushObject in createAccount does not invalidate emailValidation. After the server rejects a blocked email the field keeps showing OK until the user edits the email text, defeating the purpose of the rejectedEmails cache.

title: Validator performs a database write on every validation
body: lib/validators/email_validator.rb line 13 calls BlockedEmail.should_block?(value) from inside validate_each, and should_block? increments match_count and saves the BlockedEmail record. Validation is supposed to be read-only but now does a write. UsersController#create calls user.valid? and then user.save which validates again, so a single blocked signup increments match_count twice, and validations that fail for unrelated reasons or are run multiple times also inflate statistics and add extra writes to the signup path.

title: Blocked email lookup is case-sensitive allowing bypass
body: app/models/blocked_email.rb line 12 looks up BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first with the raw value and validates uniqueness case-sensitively with no downcasing on write. Email addresses differing only in case or surrounding whitespace will miss the block list, so an attacker blocked as bad@spammers.org can sign up as BAD@spammers.org or with different casing and the validator will not reject them.

title: Non-atomic match_count increment loses updates
body: app/models/blocked_email.rb lines 14-16 do record.match_count += 1 followed by record.save. Under concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked address this read-modify-write races and one increment overwrites the other, so match_count and last_match_at statistics become inaccurate. An atomic counter update such as increment_counter or update_counters should be used.

title: change_email bypasses blocked/domain email checks
body: app/controllers/users_controller.rb line 265 change_email only checks whether the address is already taken and then creates an email token, without running the User EmailValidator whitelist/blacklist or BlockedEmail check that signup runs. A user can therefore change their account email to a blocked or disallowed domain even though new signups with the same address are rejected.

title: Wrong Ember dependent key prevents rejected email UI update
body: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/create_account_controller.js line 96 declares emailValidation dependent on rejectedEmails.@each, but rejectedEmails is an array of plain strings. @each only observes properties on array items, so pushObject of a string does not invalidate the computed property. After a server rejection the email field will not immediately show as invalid until accountEmail itself changes. The dependent key should observe array membership such as rejectedEmails.[] or length.

title: Moved whitelist/blacklist logic has no test coverage
body: spec/components/validators/email_validator_spec.rb only tests the new blocked-email branch. The whitelist/blacklist domain logic was moved verbatim from User#email_validator into EmailValidator but has no specs in this PR, so a regression in domain restriction behavior during the refactor would not be caught.

title: Validator performs DB writes on every validation
body: In lib/validators/email_validator.rb line 13, EmailValidator#validate_each calls BlockedEmail.should_block?(value), and BlockedEmail.should_block? increments match_count, sets last_match_at and calls save. Validation is supposed to be side-effect free and can run multiple times per User save, on any attribute change that leaves email_changed? true, and even on valid? checks that never save. Consequence: match_count/last_match_at are inflated, extra SELECT+UPDATE on every signup/email-change validation, and a failed User save still commits BlockedEmail stats in a separate transaction.

title: Non-atomic match_count increment loses updates
body: In app/models/blocked_email.rb lines 14-16, should_block? does record.match_count += 1; record.last_match_at = ...; record.save. This is read-modify-write with two separate queries. Concurrent blocked signup attempts for the same email will both read the same count and overwrite each other, losing counts. It also runs validations/callbacks and updates updated_at.
