Consequence: inaccurate blocking statistics under concurrency; should use atomic increment_counter / update_counters / update_columns.

title: Blocked email lookup is case-sensitive and bypassable
body: In app/models/blocked_email.rb line 12, BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first does an exact case-sensitive match, and EmailValidator passes the raw value without downcasing/normalizing. User emails differ in case (e.g., BAD@spammers.org vs bad@spammers.org). Consequence: an attacker can bypass a blocked-email entry simply by changing letter case, and BlockedEmail uniqueness validation also permits duplicate entries differing only by case.

title: Domain whitelist/blacklist regex is unanchored
body: In lib/validators/email_validator.rb lines 18-22, the check builds Regexp.new("@(#{domains})", true) with no end-anchor and only escapes dots. An email like user@allowed.com.evil.com contains substring @allowed.com and will pass a whitelist for allowed.com, and similarly blacklist entries can be evaded with suffix subdomains. Consequence: domain restrictions moved from User to EmailValidator remain bypassable for both whitelist and blacklist.

title: Wrong Ember dependent key for rejectedEmails
body: In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/create_account_controller.js line 96, emailValidation declares .property('accountEmail', 'rejectedEmails.@each') but rejectedEmails is an array of plain strings. @each observes properties of array items, not array membership; for primitive arrays the correct key is rejectedEmails.[] (or .length). Consequence: after createAccount pushes a server-rejected email via pushObject, emailValidation may not recompute, so the form still shows the blocked email as ok/submittable until the user edits the email field.

title: Whitelist/blacklist branches have no coverage
body: In spec/components/validators/email_validator_spec.rb, the only tests stub BlockedEmail.should_block? true/false and assert presence of errors. There are no tests for email_domains_whitelist, email_domains_blacklist, the interaction where whitelist errors should suppress the blocked check, nil/malformed values, or real BlockedEmail integration. Consequence: regressions in the moved restriction logic from User#email_validator and the new blocked-email branch will not be caught.

title: Reflected XSS via unescaped request.referer in postMessage
body: In app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb line 11 the raw request.referer is interpolated into a single-quoted JavaScript string: parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>'). Referer is attacker-controlled. A value containing ' , </script> or similar breaks out and executes arbitrary JS in the embed iframe origin. Fix by using escape_javascript / to_json for the origin and by passing only the origin (scheme://host:port), not the full URL.

title: raw_html cook path stores unsanitized HTML leading to stored XSS
body: Post#cook returns raw verbatim when cook_method is raw_html, skipping the entire rendering/sanitization pipeline. TopicEmbed.import sets cook_method to raw_html for RSS/readability content and app/views/embed/best.html.erb renders it with <%= raw post.cooked %>. Any <script>, on* handler, iframe or form in the feed or scraped article is stored and later served to all embed viewers. Fix by sanitizing on import or on cook.

title: SSRF and unhandled fetch in import_remote
body: TopicEmbed.import_remote calls open(url).read on a URL that ultimately derives from the embed_url query param via Jobs::RetrieveTopic -> TopicRetriever -> fetch_http. There is no timeout, size limit, error handling, or redirect restriction. TopicRetriever only checks the initial host equals embeddable_host, but open-uri follows redirects to any host and ignores ports, allowing port-scanning / internal network access and causing job exceptions / hangs when the remote site is down.

title: PollFeed crashes on feed items without content
body: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb line 35 the code does CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) unconditionally. SimpleRSS items often have only link/title/description and nil content, so i.content is nil and .scrub raises NoMethodError, aborting the whole hourly poll and preventing any items from importing. Fix by falling back to description, handling nil, and rescuing fetch/parse errors.

title: Invalid X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL breaks embedding
body: EmbedController sets response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL". ALLOWALL is not a defined directive. Browsers treat unknown values as DENY/SAMEORIGIN and will refuse to frame the content, defeating the embed feature. To allow framing the header must be removed, not set to ALLOWALL.

title: Unescaped URL interpolated into imported HTML
body: TopicEmbed.import builds "#{url}" with only a /^https?\:\/\// check. A URL like http://x/'>

title: content_sha1 updated even if revision fails
body: In TopicEmbed.import the update path calls revisor.revise! then unconditionally does embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1). If revise! returns false or the post is nil/deleted, the hash is still advanced, so the new content is lost and will never be retried because future imports compare equal. Fix by only updating the hash on successful revision and handling missing embed.post.

title: Non-atomic throttle key can leak permanently
body: TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently? does $redis.setnx(key,1) then $redis.expire(key,60) as two separate commands. If the process crashes between them the key never expires and that embed_url is throttled forever. It also creates one unbounded key per distinct URL. Fix by using a single atomic SETEX / SET NX EX.

title: EmbedController spec contradicts implementation
body: The spec expects EmbedController#best to call TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve when no embed exists, but the implementation enqueues Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic,...) and renders loading. The test will fail and does not cover the actual async path, the 1.minute expiry, or visibility of the TopicView. Fix the spec to expect the job enqueue.

title: Unsanitized feed/remote HTML stored as raw_html enables persistent XSS
body: In app/models/topic_embed.rb line 13, TopicEmbed.import appends "#{url}" with unescaped URL interpolation and stores attacker-influenced RSS/Readability HTML via Post with cook_method raw_html. In app/models/post.rb Post#cook returns raw verbatim for raw_html, bypassing the sanitization pipeline, and app/views/embed/best.html.erb renders it with `raw post.cooked`. A feed containing

title: Reflecting request.referer as postMessage targetOrigin breaks resize and risks XSS
body: In app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb line 11, request.referer (fully attacker-controlled header) is interpolated into a JS string as the second argument to parent.postMessage. postMessage requires an origin (scheme://host:port), not a full URL with path, so browsers throw and the resize message never delivers. It also reflects user input into script context; HTML-escaping does not make it safe inside <script>. Derive and validate the origin server-side from the allowlisted embeddable host instead of echoing Referer.

title: Reversed postMessage origin check accepts wrong senders
body: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js line 17, the check is `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) return`. This tests whether the configured discourseUrl string contains the message origin, instead of testing whether the message origin equals the expected Discourse origin. Any origin that happens to be a substring of discourseUrl passes, and legitimate origins with a path prefix can fail. An attacker iframe/window can then drive `iframe.height` resizing. Compare parsed origins for equality and validate height as a finite number.

title: Bare open() on admin-configured feed URL allows SSRF and pipe execution
body: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb line 29, `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses Kernel#open, not URI.open. If the value starts with `|` it can execute a local command, and http(s) URLs follow redirects, honor file-like wrappers, and have no timeout or size limit or error handling. A malicious or compromised feed URL can cause server-side request forgery, hang the scheduler, or execute commands. Use URI.parse + URI.open with explicit http/https allowlist, timeouts, size limits, and rescue network errors.

title: Unrestricted open(url).read in import_remote allows SSRF via embed URL
body: In app/models/topic_embed.rb line 48, import_remote does `open(url).read` on a caller-supplied embed_url with no timeout, size limit, scheme validation, redirect limit, or exception handling. TopicRetriever only checks the initial host equals embeddable_host, but open-uri follows cross-host redirects, so an attacker can make the server fetch internal metadata/cloud endpoints or large/slow resources and raise unhandled exceptions that fail the job. Restrict to http/https, disable/limit redirects, add timeouts, and handle failures.

title: PollFeed crashes when feed item has no content
body: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb line 35, `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every RSS/Atom item has non-nil content. Real feeds often omit content/encoded body or provide only summary/title. Nil raises NoMethodError, aborting the whole hourly poll so no items are imported. Guard for nil/empty content and title/url before calling TopicEmbed.import.

title: Non-atomic setnx + expire throttle can leak a permanent throttle key
body: In lib/topic_retriever.rb lines 27-28, throttling does `$redis.setnx(key,1)` then a separate `$redis.expire(key,60)`. If the process crashes between the two calls the key never expires and that embed_url is throttled forever (or until manual deletion). Concurrent processes can also interleave. Use a single atomic SET with NX+EX (setex/set with expire option) or Lua.

title: Invalid X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL header
body: In app/controllers/embed_controller.rb line 28, the filter sets `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL`. ALLOWALL is not a defined directive (valid values are DENY, SAMEORIGIN, ALLOW-FROM). Browsers ignore the invalid value and fall back to default behavior, so embed framing remains unpredictable/blocked instead of explicitly allowed. Delete the header to allow framing instead of sending an invalid value.

title: PostRevisor ignores validation/save failure and still reports success
body: In lib/post_revisor.rb line 85, `revise!` was changed to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` but the return value is discarded and `revise!` unconditionally returns true, advances draft sequence, and triggers post-processing. When validations are enabled and save fails, callers (including TopicEmbed.import update path) believe the revision succeeded and still update content_sha1. Check the save result and return false/propagate errors on failure.

title: Mutating caller contents string with << corrupts hash and causes duplicate footers
body: In app/models/topic_embed.rb line 13, `contents << "\n<hr>..."` mutates the caller's string in place. If the same string object is reused, the footer is appended repeatedly, changing the SHA and triggering spurious revisions, and surprising callers that retain the string. Use non-mutating concatenation (contents = contents + footer or dup) before hashing/storing.

title: Reflected XSS via unescaped request.referer in postMessage targetOrigin
body: File app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb line 11 interpolates <%= request.referer %> directly inside a single-quoted JavaScript string without JavaScript escaping. Referer is a fully attacker-controlled request header, so a value containing ' can break out and inject arbitrary script executed in the forum origin. Additionally the full referer URL (with path/query) is used as postMessage targetOrigin, which must be an origin; this breaks delivery and encourages a wildcard fix.

title: Stored XSS via unsanitized RSS/remote HTML stored as raw_html
body: File app/models/topic_embed.rb line 13 appends an unsanitized link built from feed-controlled url ("#{url}") and TopicEmbed.import stores feed/readability HTML verbatim with cook_method raw_html. Combined with app/models/post.rb bypass that returns raw without sanitization and app/views/embed/best.html.erb using raw post.cooked, an attacker who controls feed content or linked page content gets persistent script execution in forum and embedded contexts. absolutize_urls only rewrites leading-/ URLs and leaves script tags, event handlers, and javascript: URLs intact.

title: raw_html cook_method bypasses sanitization pipeline
body: File app/models/post.rb line 133 in Post#cook returns raw directly when cook_method is raw_html, skipping PrettyText cooking/sanitization and plugin filters. Any raw_html post content (from RSS polling or readability fetch) is then stored as cooked and rendered with raw in views, so unsanitized external HTML becomes stored XSS across topic pages, not just the embed iframe.

title: Reversed postMessage origin check accepts prefix origins
body: File app/assets/javascripts/embed.js line 17 checks discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1 instead of checking that e.origin equals the expected Discourse origin. This tests whether the attacker-controlled origin is a substring of the trusted URL, so any origin that happens to be a string prefix of discourseUrl would be accepted and can drive iframe resizing. Origin validation must be strict equality against the expected origin.

title: import_remote uses open without open-uri, enabling local file read
body: File app/models/topic_embed.rb line 48 calls open(url).read without requiring open-uri. When called via Jobs::RetrieveTopic / TopicRetriever (which never requires open-uri), Kernel#open treats the argument as a file path, so fetching fails for HTTP and can read local files. It also has no timeout, redirect limit, size limit, or error handling, allowing SSRF, hangs, and job crashes.

title: Feed polling crashes on nil content and leaks resources with unbounded work
body: File app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb line 29 does SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) with no rescue, timeout, or close, and line 35 does CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) without nil guards for content/title/link. A single malformed item, network error, huge feed, or missing field raises NoMethodError or network exception and aborts the hourly job, while iterating every item each hour can create unbounded topics.

title: Non-atomic setnx plus expire throttle can permanently block retrieval
body: File lib/topic_retriever.rb lines 27-28 implements the 60-second retrieval throttle as $redis.setnx followed by $redis.expire. If the process crashes between the two calls the key never expires, so that embed_url is throttled forever. Use an atomic SET with NX and EX (or setex) and normalize/hash the URL for the key.

title: Race on embed creation and wrong persisted check can raise duplicate key
body: File app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 20-28 checks embed.blank? then creates Topic/Post/TopicEmbed without handling concurrent creators. Two concurrent retrieve/poll jobs for the same embed_url both pass the check and the second hits the unique index on topic_embeds.embed_url with RecordNotUnique. Also the guard uses post.present? instead of post.persisted?, so a failed PostCreator result with errors still attempts TopicEmbed.create! with nil ids.

title: content_sha1 updated even when revision fails or post is missing
body: File app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 32-37 calls PostRevisor#revise! without checking its false return value or whether embed.post is nil (e.g., deleted post), then unconditionally does embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1). A failed or skipped revision permanently marks the new content as synced, so legitimate feed changes are never retried.

title: Invalid X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL header will not allow framing
body: File app/controllers/embed_controller.rb line 28 sets response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] to ALLOWALL to permit iframing. ALLOWALL is not a valid X-Frame-Options directive and browsers ignore or treat it as deny; to allow embedding the controller must delete the header or use ALLOW-FROM semantics, otherwise the embed iframe remains blocked when a default SAMEORIGIN/DENY is set.

title: Embed controller spec expects direct retriever but code enqueues job
body: File spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb lines 40-45 expects TopicRetriever.new and retrieve on a cache miss, while app/controllers/embed_controller.rb line 15 does Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic,...). The test does not verify actual behavior and would fail/pass for the wrong reason, leaving the enqueue path, user_id propagation, and loading render untested.

title: float:right on flex item is ignored so small-action button loses right alignment
body: In app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic-post.scss .small-action is now a flex container via flexbox(). Per CSS Flexbox spec, float has no effect on a flex item. The button rule still uses float: right to push the dismiss/close button to the far right, so after this change it will be laid out as the next flex item directly after .small-action-desc instead of at the right edge. The fix is margin-left: auto on the button or justify-content on the container.

title: order mixin off-by-one for legacy box-ordinal-group
body: In app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss the order($val) mixin emits -webkit-box-ordinal-group: $val and -moz-box-ordinal-group: $val. Legacy box ordinal-group is 1-based while modern order is 0-based, so the correct mapping is ordinal-group = order + 1. Emitting the same value orders legacy WebKit/Firefox differently than modern browsers, breaking the intended order(2) vs order(3) relationship used for .extra-info-wrapper and .panel in old browsers.

title: align-items mixin emits invalid -ms-align-items property
body: In app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss align-items() outputs -ms-align-items: $alignment. No such CSS property exists; IE10 flexbox only uses -ms-flex-align. The declaration is dead code that bloats every use of align-items(center/baseline) and can confuse future maintenance. It should be removed, leaving -ms-flex-align plus standard align-items.

title: float:right on flex item is ignored, button loses right alignment
body: In app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic-post.scss .small-action is now a flex container via flexbox() mixin, so its direct children (.topic-avatar, .small-action-desc, button) are flex items. Per CSS Flexbox spec, float and clear have no effect on flex items. The button rule still uses float: right to push the dismiss/close button to the far right, which will now compute to none and the button will render immediately after the description instead of at the right edge. Fix by using margin-left: auto or justify-content on the flex container instead of float.

title: order mixin off-by-one for legacy -webkit-box-ordinal-group
body: In app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss the order() mixin emits -webkit-box-ordinal-group: $val with the same value as order: $val. The 2009 box spec is 1-indexed (ordinal-group = order + 1, default 1 equals order 0), so order(2) and order(3) used in topic.scss and header.scss produce ordinal-group 2/3 which correspond to modern order 1/2. Modern browsers and legacy WebKit (Safari 6, iOS 6, old Android) will compute different orders, causing inconsistent header/extra-info/panel ordering. It should emit -webkit-box-ordinal-group: $val + 1 and -moz-box-ordinal-group accordingly.

title: margin-left:auto does not right-align in legacy -webkit-box fallback
body: In app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/header.scss .d-header .panel uses margin-left: auto to push the panel to the right inside .contents which now uses display: -webkit-box / flex via mixins. Auto margins only absorb free space in the modern flexbox spec; the 2009 -webkit-box implementation does not support pushing items with auto margins and has no box-pack set. Legacy WebKit that only understands display: -webkit-box will therefore left-align the panel next to the title instead of right-aligning it, breaking the header despite the prefixes.

title: Invalid -ms-align-items property in align-items mixin
body: In app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss align-items() emits -ms-align-items: $alignment which is not a real CSS property and is ignored by all browsers. IE10/11 only understand -ms-flex-align (already emitted) for this, so the extra declaration is dead code and suggests the prefix mapping was not verified. Remove it to avoid confusion and false confidence in IE alignment, especially for align-items(baseline) used by badges.

title: order() mixin off-by-one for legacy box-ordinal-group
body: In app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss the order() mixin sets -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group to the same value as order. The legacy 2009 box spec is 1-indexed while modern order is 0-indexed, so the correct mapping is ordinal-group = order + 1. As written, order(2)/order(3) used for .extra-info-wrapper and .d-header .panel produce ordinal-group 2/3 instead of 3/4, mis-ordering header items in old WebKit/Firefox and breaking any future use of order(0)/order(1) which will collide with the default group.

title: Invalid -ms-align-items property in align-items mixin
body: In app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss align-items() emits -ms-align-items, which does not exist. IE10/11 only understand -ms-flex-align. The invalid declaration is ignored, so IE gets only -ms-flex-align, and anyone relying on the second line for baseline/center alignment in IE is misled. Remove the -ms-align-items line.

title: float:right on flex item is ignored, button no longer right-aligned
body: In app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic-post.scss .small-action was changed to display:flex via flexbox(), but its button rule still uses float:right to push it to the far right. Per the flexbox spec float and clear have no effect on flex items, so the button becomes a normal row flex item placed directly after .small-action-desc instead of at the right edge. This is a visual regression versus the old block layout. Use margin-left:auto or justify-content instead of float for the flex case.

title: Conditional serializer hook misnamed so it never runs
body: In app/serializers/user_serializer.rb the method is defined as `include_website_name` without a trailing `?`. ActiveModel::Serializers looks for `include_<attr>?`, so this method is never called. As a result `website_name` is always serialized, even when `website` is blank (as nil), and any future filtering for trust/privacy is bypassed.

title: website_name bypasses TL0 untrusted-field hiding
body: In app/serializers/user_serializer.rb `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` so anonymous viewers do not see TL0 users' website/bio/location, but newly added `website_name` is only added to `attributes` and not to `untrusted_attributes`. Since `website_name` contains the website host plus path, it leaks the very URL that `website` hiding is meant to suppress for spam prevention.

title: Scheme-less websites return nil and hide profile link
body: In app/serializers/user_serializer.rb `website_name` is derived via `URI(website.to_s).host` which returns nil when the stored website has no scheme such as `example.com/user`. The method then returns nil early, and the profile template in user.hbs gates display on `model.website_name`, so a user with a valid scheme-less `model.website` shows no website link at all.

title: Query, fragment and port stripped from displayed path
body: In app/serializers/user_serializer.rb `website_name` is built as `website_host + URI(website).path` when domains match. That drops the query string, fragment, and non-default port, so `http://example.com/page?x=1#y` displays as `example.com/page` despite the PR goal of showing the complete path. Users cannot distinguish such URLs.

title: Untrusted-attributes test not updated for website_name
body: In spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb the TL0-anonymous test lists bio/location/website/profile backgrounds but omits the new `website_name`. The test therefore cannot catch the privacy regression where `website_name` remains visible while `website` is hidden.

title: Conditional-serialize hook misnamed so it never runs
body: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:153 defines `def include_website_name` without the trailing `?`. ActiveModel::Serializer only honors `include_<attr>?`, as used by every other hook in this file (e.g. `include_email?`, `include_stats?`). As a result the `website.present?` guard is dead code and `website_name` is always serialized, including a `website_name: null` key when there is no website.

title: website_name bypasses TL0 anonymous hiding for website
body: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:105 lists `website` in `untrusted_attributes` so TL0 profiles are hidden from anonymous via `restrict_user_fields?`, but the new `website_name` attribute (added at line 43) was not added there. Since `website_name` is derived directly from `website` (host plus path), an anonymous client can learn a TL0 user's website host/path from `website_name` even when `website` itself is correctly suppressed.

title: Unhandled nil current_hostname crashes user serialization
body: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:139 assigns `discourse_host = Discourse.current_hostname` with no nil guard, then calls `discourse_host.split('.')` at line 144 and `discourse_host.ends_with?` at line 149. If hostname is nil/unset, every UserSerializer render raises NoMethodError, breaking user profile JSON with a 500.

title: Same-domain display drops query, fragment and port
body: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:143 builds the same-domain display as `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path`. `URI#path` excludes query string, fragment, and `host` excludes an explicit port, so `http://example.com/user?x=1#y` or `http://example.com:8080/user` is truncated to `example.com/user`, contradicting the PR goal of showing the complete URL path and losing navigation-relevant information.

title: include_website_name missing ? so conditional never runs
body: In app/serializers/user_serializer.rb the method is defined as `def include_website_name` without a question mark. ActiveModel::Serializer checks `include_<attr>?` (as used for `include_email?`, `include_stats?` in the same file), so this method is never called. As a result `website_name` is always serialized even when `website` is blank, returning nil instead of being omitted.

title: website_name leaks website hidden for TL0 users
body: The serializer hides `website` for TL0 users seen by anonymous via `untrusted_attributes`, which returns false when `scope.restrict_user_fields?` is true. `website_name` was added to `attributes` but was not added to `untrusted_attributes`, and its include check only tests `website.present?`. An anonymous viewer of a TL0 profile will therefore still receive `website_name` containing the website host and path, defeating the hiding of `website`.

title: untrusted attributes test omits website_name
body: The spec's `untrusted_attributes` list in spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb does not include `website_name`, so the test that verifies TL0 attributes are hidden from anonymous users cannot catch the leak of `website_name` described above.

body: In app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/user.scss line 497 (.group-member-info .name) the original was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). It became dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)). The light-theme branch does not preserve the original 30% value, causing an unintended light-theme color shift and breaking the 30% / 70% pattern used for this element elsewhere. It should be 30% / 70%.

title: Swapped light/dark lightness in embedded meta link
body: In .embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a the old rule was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The change made it dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The light-theme branch should stay at 30% with dark branch at 70%, i.e. 30%/70% like every other 30% conversion. As written light themes get a 70% lightened color that is much too faint and dark themes get 30% instead of 70%.

title: Wrong lightness for custom-message-length on mobile
body: Old rule was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%). New rule is dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)). The light side changed from 70% to 30%. Desktop modal.scss for the same selector correctly uses 70%/30%. Mobile will now render much darker hint text in light themes and is inconsistent with desktop.

title: Wrong lightness for topic-map h3 on mobile
body: Old rule was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%). New rule is dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)). The light branch should be 20% with dark branch 80%, as desktop/topic-post.scss h3 correctly does with 20%/80%. As written mobile light themes get a 50% lightened heading instead of 20%, losing contrast and diverging from desktop.

title: Lost distinct color for group-member name
body: Old .group-member-info .name was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). New is dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)), identical to .title below it. It should be 30%/70% per the 100-minus convention used everywhere else and per common/base/user.scss which keeps 30%/70% for the same elements. Light themes get too-light names and the name/title distinction is lost.

title: Lost distinct color for group-member name on mobile
body: Old .group-member-info .name was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). New is dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)), identical to .title. It should be 30%/70% to preserve the light-theme value and match common/base/user.scss. As written mobile light themes render the name lighter than designed.

title: totalPages off-by-one when count divisible by limit
body: In app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6 totalPages is Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100 users, limit 50) this returns 3 instead of 2, so the pager shows a non-existent third page that renders empty and enables the next button past the end.

title: next pagination can seek to offset == user_count
body: In app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6 the next action clamps with Math.min(offset + limit, user_count). A valid offset is zero-based, so offset equal to user_count points past the last record and returns zero rows. It should clamp to the start of the last page, otherwise the admin can navigate to an empty page.

title: create ignores alias_level selected in UI
body: In app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb Admin::GroupsController#create only assigns name and visible, while #update assigns alias_level. The admin form exposes an alias-level combo-box for new groups, so the chosen value is silently dropped and every new group is created with the default level.

title: add_members does not trim usernames
body: In app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb add_members does usernames.split(",") and looks up each token verbatim with User.find_by_username. A normal list like "bob, alice" leaves a leading space on the second token, the lookup returns nil, and the user is silently skipped with a success response, so the admin thinks the add succeeded.

title: remove_member bypasses Group#remove logic
body: In app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb remove_member calls group.users.delete(user_id) directly, while add_members uses group.add(user). Direct association delete skips any cleanup encapsulated in Group#remove (primary-group reset, counters, callbacks) and passes a raw integer id instead of a User record. This risks leaving inconsistent user/group state compared to the normal removal path.

title: members limit/offset unvalidated
body: In app/controllers/groups_controller.rb GroupsController#members takes limit as (params[:limit] || 50).to_i and offset as params[:offset].to_i with no bounds. A client can request an unbounded limit causing a huge users load and DoS, or a negative/zero limit/offset causing empty results, division-by-zero in the pager, or database errors. The limit needs a maximum and non-negative clamping.

title: automatic check in member row resolves to wrong scope
body: In app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group_member.hbs the template rendered per-member with itemView checks {{#unless automatic}}. Inside that item context automatic resolves to the member User, not the group, so it is always falsy and the remove link is shown even for automatic groups where removal is prohibited. The backend rejects it, but the UI incorrectly offers deletion.

title: findMembers changed promise contract
body: In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js findMembers now returns undefined when the name is empty instead of Ember.RSVP.resolve([]) as before, and addMembers/removeMember do not return the inner findMembers promise. Callers that chain .then on findMembers will throw on undefined, and callers cannot wait for the reloaded member list after an add or remove.

title: add_members requires :group_id but route provides :id
body: In config/routes.rb the member routes are defined as delete/put "members" inside resources :groups, so the group id arrives as params[:id] (e.g. /admin/groups/:id/members). Admin::GroupsController#add_members does Group.find(params.require(:group_id).to_i) and #remove_member does the same. A real request from app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js which PUTs/DELETEs to /admin/groups/:id/members.json will raise ActionController::ParameterMissing for missing group_id. Controller specs pass only because they inject group_id directly, bypassing routing.

title: remove_member requires :group_id but route provides :id
body: Same mismatch as add_members: Admin::GroupsController#remove_member does Group.find(params.require(:group_id).to_i) while the route /admin/groups/:id/members supplies :id. DELETE requests from the admin UI will 400 with missing group_id, so member removal is broken in production despite the controller spec passing with an artificial group_id param.

title: Unbounded limit/offset in members endpoint
body: GroupsController#members does limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i and offset = params[:offset].to_i with no clamping, then group.users.order(...).limit(limit).offset(offset). An attacker can request limit=1000000 to load huge result sets into memory for DoS, or limit=0/negative or offset negative which can return empty sets or raise SQL errors. The previous code defaulted to 50/200 with limited use; the new code needs a max cap and offset >= 0 validation.

title: totalPages off-by-one creates empty last page
body: totalPages is Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is exactly divisible by limit (e.g. 50/50, 100/50) this reports 2 and 3 pages instead of 1 and 2. Combined with next using Math.min(offset+limit, user_count), the UI can navigate to an offset == user_count that returns zero members, showing an empty last page and a wrong currentPage/totalPages label.

title: add_members does not strip whitespace around usernames
body: add_members does usernames.split(",").each with no strip, then User.find_by_username(username). Input like "alice, bob" from the user-selector will look up " bob" with a leading space and silently skip it, so the second user is never added with no error. The action should strip each token and skip blanks.

title: findMembers returns undefined instead of promise
body: findMembers does if (Em.isEmpty(this.get('name'))) { return ; } whereas before it returned Ember.RSVP.resolve([]). Callers such as admin next/previous return group.findMembers() and routes rely on a thenable; returning undefined breaks promise chaining and error handling for empty-name groups. It should return a resolved promise.

title: addMembers/removeMember swallow reload errors
body: removeMember and addMembers do Discourse.ajax(...).then(function() { self.findMembers(); }) without returning the inner findMembers promise and without a rejection handler. The outer promise resolves before the list reloads so the UI cannot wait for fresh data, and failures from the reload or from the 422 automatic-group guard are silently ignored with no user feedback.

title: remove_member automatic-group test uses wrong verb
body: The test for cannot remove members from automatic groups does xhr :put, :remove_member while the route is delete members => groups#remove_member. Controller specs dispatch by action name so it passes, but it never verifies the real DELETE route or the :id vs :group_id param mismatch, masking the production routing bug.

title: Admin members actions read :group_id but route supplies :id
body: In app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb add_members (and remove_member at line 85) does Group.find(params.require(:group_id).to_i). In config/routes.rb the routes are declared as member routes inside resources :groups (delete "members", put "members"), so the URL /admin/groups/:id/members.json supplies params[:id], not params[:group_id]. The JS calls /admin/groups/<id>/members.json, so the controller will raise ActionController::ParameterMissing and adding/removing members via the UI will always fail with 400. Controller specs pass only because they inject group_id directly and bypass routing.

title: Unbounded limit/offset on group members endpoint
body: In app/controllers/groups_controller.rb GroupsController#members does limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i with no maximum and no validation of offset. A caller can request limit=1000000 (or negative values) causing order/limit/offset over a large users table, loading huge result sets into memory and serializing them. This is a denial-of-service / performance risk; the limit should be clamped to a sane maximum and negative/non-numeric values rejected.

title: totalPages off-by-one for exact multiples
body: In app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6 totalPages is Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50/50, 100/50) this reports one extra page (2 instead of 1, 3 instead of 2). Combined with next using Math.min(offset+limit, user_count), the admin can paginate to an empty last page and showingLast never becomes true on the real last page.

title: Adding members fails when usernames contain spaces
body: In app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb add_members does usernames.split(",").each with User.find_by_username(username) and no strip. The user-selector sends comma-separated values that commonly contain spaces after commas (e.g. "bob, alice"). The second lookup becomes " alice" with a leading space and will not match, so only the first user is added and the rest are silently ignored with a success response.

title: Update unconditionally clears visible when param omitted
body: In app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb update does group.visible = params[:visible] == "true" without checking presence. If a client updates only alias_level or name and omits visible, visible is forced to false and saved, unintentionally hiding the group. The assignment should only run when params[:visible] is present.

title: Spec uses wrong verb and masks routing param bug
body: In spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb the remove_member test does xhr :put, :remove_member while config/routes.rb defines delete "members" => "groups#remove_member". The specs also pass group_id directly, so they never exercise the real /admin/groups/:id/members route. The suite therefore cannot catch the :group_id vs :id mismatch or a verb mismatch, and gives false confidence that member add/remove works.

title: Translate only loads current locale, can cache missing translation
body: I18n.translate in lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb only calls load_locale(config.locale) before delegating to the backend, but the new fallback chain is [user locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en]. If the fallback locale files are not yet loaded the backend lookup misses and returns 'translation missing'. That result is stored in the global LRU cache. Any code path that did not run ApplicationController#set_locale (Sidekiq jobs, mailers, console, standalone backend calls) can therefore poison the cache, and later web requests that did preload fallbacks will still hit the cached missing string until LRU eviction or reload!.

title: Fallback lookup hits SiteSetting on every translation without normalization
body: FallbackLocaleList#[] in config/initializers/i18n.rb is called by the I18n fallbacks backend on every translated key and executes [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact. That means every I18n.t does a SiteSetting read plus allocation. With hundreds of translations per page this is significant overhead. It also never normalizes the incoming locale to a symbol, so a string 'en' and symbol :en are not deduped by uniq, producing duplicate chain entries, and string entries never match the symbol entries in @loaded_locales, causing repeated load_path scans.

title: Translation cache key ignores fallback chain
body: The LRU key in lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb is built only from key plus config.locale plus backend object_id. The rendered value now depends also on SiteSetting.default_locale, which is part of the fallback chain. Changing the site default locale or updating a fallback-locale translation does not invalidate existing entries, so users whose own locale misses will keep seeing the old fallback string until the entry is evicted, reload! is called, or the process restarts.

title: Fallback lookup hits DB on every translation and can crash
body: FallbackLocaleList#[] in config/initializers/i18n.rb calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym on every lookup. I18n::Backend::Fallbacks calls I18n.fallbacks[locale] for every missing translation, so this adds a SiteSetting read to the translation fast path and raises NoMethodError if default_locale is nil/blank or if the DB is unavailable during boot, migrations, asset precompile, or setup. Consequence is crashed requests or missing translations instead of falling back to :en.

title: Fallback locales are not loaded in translate path
body: I18n.translate in lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb only calls load_locale(config.locale). It never loads the other locales in the fallback chain (SiteSetting.default_locale, :en) and ignores an explicit locale: option which bypasses cache but still loads config.locale. Only ApplicationController#set_locale calls I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!. Background jobs, mailers, console, and any explicit-locale lookup will therefore miss fallback translations and return missing-translation errors even though fallbacks are enabled.

title: Translation LRU cache ignores fallback chain
body: The cache key in lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb is "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}". The resolved string now depends on SiteSetting.default_locale and the fallback files, which are not part of the key. Changing the site default locale (or updating a fallback file without reload) serves the previously cached fallback string for the same locale, i.e. stale wrong-language output.

title: Loaded-locales check races and can be nil
body: I18n.ensure_loaded! and I18n.translate in lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb read @loaded_locales.include? outside LOAD_MUTEX, while load_locale mutates it inside the mutex. @loaded_locales is only initialized in reload!/ensure_loaded!, so a first translate before either raises NoMethodError on nil.include?. Concurrent requests can also double-load locale files or see a partially updated list.

title: Fallback lookup crashes on nil default_locale
body: FallbackLocaleList#[] in config/initializers/i18n.rb builds [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact. Calling to_sym before compact means a nil or missing SiteSetting.default_locale raises NoMethodError instead of falling back to :en. Because this method runs on every I18n fallback lookup, including error pages and boot/migration paths where SiteSetting may be unavailable, a single missing setting turns every translation into an exception.

title: Translation cache key ignores fallback chain
body: I18n.translate in lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb caches with key "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}". With fallbacks enabled the result depends also on SiteSetting.default_locale and the :en fallback. Changing the site default locale does not change the key and does not clear @cache, so requests for the same key and user locale keep returning the old fallback translation indefinitely until I18n.reload!.

title: Interpolated/pluralized lookups do not load fallback locales
body: I18n.translate in lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb only calls load_locale(config.locale) and returns early via translate_no_cache for calls with options such as count or interpolation. It never ensures the fallback locales from FallbackLocaleList are loaded. Outside ApplicationController#set_locale, for example in background jobs, mailers, or console, I18n.t with options will report translation missing even when SiteSetting.default_locale or :en has the key, while option-less lookups from the same process may succeed.

title: Denial-cache key omits identity type, causing cross-identity false denies
body: In Service.Check the denial key is built as userPermDenialCacheKey(namespace, userUID, action, name, parent) with no identity type. Anonymous subject 'anonymous:0' and renderer subject 'render:0' both resolve to UID '0', and user vs service-account UIDs can also collide as strings. A denial cached for one identity type (e.g. anonymous denied dashboards:read on dash1) will therefore hit for a different identity type on the same namespace/action/resource (e.g. renderer, which is allowed dashboards:read/folders:read) and Check returns Allowed:false without consulting permissions. The fix is to include IdentityType in the denial key.

title: Negative caching reintroduces stale denies for newly granted access
body: Service.Check caches every deny in permDenialCache for shortCacheTTL (30s) and short-circuits future Checks on a hit before reading permissions. If a user is denied and then granted access to the same dashboard/folder (the exact creator flow this PR fixes, role/team/assignment change, or folder-tree refresh), subsequent Checks within the TTL incorrectly return denied without hitting the DB. The fast deny path defeats the new fallback-to-DB logic for the most important transition from deny to allow.

title: Every cached deny now forces a full DB permission fetch
body: Check first reads getCachedIdentityPermissions and, if the cached scope map does not contain the resource, unconditionally calls getIdentityPermissions. The cache-hit fast paths were removed from getUserPermissions and getAnonymousPermissions, so that call always queries basic roles, teams and permissions from the DB. Previously a fresh permCache hit decided allow/deny without I/O. Now any user without access to a resource hits the DB on first Check per resource, and scanning N distinct denied resources causes N DB permission builds (only the second identical-resource hit is absorbed by the denial cache). This turns deny-heavy workloads into a DB storm.

title: List still serves stale cached permissions with no DB fallback
body: Check was changed to fall back to the DB when cached permissions do not contain the requested resource, but List was changed to use getCachedIdentityPermissions with no equivalent fallback: on a permCache hit it directly calls listPermission. A newly granted dashboard/folder will therefore be missing from List results for up to shortCacheTTL while Check already allows it, leaving Check and List inconsistent and the creator flow still broken for listings.

title: Denial-precedence test stores false instead of true
body: TestService_CacheCheck 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry' seeds permCache with map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false} and claims this proves the denial entry is checked instead of the allow. Since checkPermission treats a false map value the same as missing (it tests truthiness), both caches deny. The test never exercises denial-wins-over-allow. It should seed map value true, otherwise a regression that ignores permDenialCache would still pass.

title: Denial cache key omits identity type
body: In Service.Check the denial key is built from namespace, UserUID, action, name and parent folder, but not IdentityType. Different subject types can yield the same UserUID (for example user:test-uid vs service-account:test-uid, or anonymous:0 vs render:0). A denial cached for one identity type will then cause Check for a different identity type with the same UID string to return Allowed:false without consulting the database. This is an authorization correctness bug that can deny legitimate access across user, service-account, anonymous and render identities.

title: Denial cache creates stale-deny window blocking DB fallback
body: Check returns immediately on permDenialCache hit and only falls back to getIdentityPermissions from the DB when there is no denial entry. A denial is then cached for shortCacheTTL (30s) whenever the DB path denies. If permissions are granted after a deny, or the DB read lagged behind the write (replica lag, or Check raced the permission commit), every retry within the TTL hits the denial cache and never re-queries the DB. This reintroduces the staleness the PR claims to fix and can lock out a dashboard/folder creator for up to the TTL after an initial premature deny.

title: DB fallback still uses stale team, role and folder caches
body: The new Check fallback calls getIdentityPermissions to get fresh permissions, but getUserPermissions reuses getUserBasicRole, getUserTeams and buildFolderTree, all of which are themselves cached for shortCacheTTL. A new grant via team membership, basic-role change, or a new folder hierarchy therefore still resolves with stale teams/roles/tree, denies, and then stores a per-resource denial. The fallback is not actually fresh for inherited or team-based permissions, so the creator-can-access fix is incomplete.

title: Unbounded per-resource denial keys
body: userPermDenialCacheKey includes resource name and parent folder, so there is one cache entry per user per action per resource, whereas permCache has one entry per user per action. Enumerating many random dashboard/folder UIDs creates unbounded denial entries that live for the full TTL, evicting useful entries and growing memory. An attacker or scanner can churn the shared local cache this way. Denial caching should be bounded or avoid per-resource negative caching.

title: Denial cache key shares namespace with permission cache
body: In pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go userPermDenialCacheKey builds namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent while userPermCacheKey builds namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action. A denial key can equal a permission key (e.g. perm action "a_b_c" vs denial action "a" name "b" parent "c"). They share the same underlying cache.Cache instance, so a permCache.Get can read a bool denial value and a permDenialCache.Get can read a map value. Both fail JSON unmarshal and log warnings, turning hits into misses and causing extra DB load. Use a distinct prefix such as ".perm_deny_".

title: Denial cache key omits identity type causing cross-principal false deny
body: In pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go Check builds permDenialKey from namespace, UserUID, action, name and parent only, before branching on IdentityType. Different identity types can share the same UserUID string (e.g. subject "anonymous:0" and "render:0" both yield UID "0", and "user:X" vs "service-account:X" can collide). A denial cached for one type will be returned for the other without ever consulting permissions, so renderer which should be allowed via wildcard for dashboards:read/folders:read can be incorrectly denied because anonymous was denied for the same resource, and vice versa.

title: Denial cache short-circuits DB fallback and reintroduces stale deny
body: In pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go Check returns Allowed:false immediately on permDenialCache hit without re-querying the DB. The rest of the PR adds fallback to the DB when cached permissions do not contain the resource precisely to see newly granted/created permissions. Once a resource is denied, the denial entry (30s TTL) blocks that fallback for its whole lifetime, so a grant made after the denial (including the creator-access case the PR fixes if the first check races creation) remains invisible until expiry. List in the same file does not even have the fallback and serves stale cached permission sets.

title: Missing React key on Grafana list item
body: In FilterViewResults the grafana branch renders <GrafanaRuleListItem> without key={key} while the datasource and unknown branches do pass key. Without a stable key React cannot reconcile the infinite-scroll list correctly, causing duplicate-key warnings, wrong item reuse/state preservation and extra re-mounts when pages load.

title: Pause action can never show in ruler-less list view
body: AlertRuleMenu computes canPause as ruler-ability OR grafana-prom-ability to support the list view without ruler data, but the Pause menu item is still gated on rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule). When rulerRule is undefined (the new list view) that predicate is false, so Pause is never rendered even when canPause is true via promRule. Users with pause permission lose the Pause/Unpause action.

title: Silence drawer never opens for prom-only rules
body: RuleActionsButtons allows Silence via useGrafanaPromRuleAbility on promRule alone, calling setShowSilenceDrawer(true), but the drawer is rendered only if rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) where rule is the optional RulerRuleDTO. In the new Grafana list view rule is undefined, so the condition is always false and clicking Silence does nothing. The menu offers an action that has no effect.

title: Federated rule protection removed
body: useAllRulerRuleAbilities previously set immutableRule using isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) to block Edit/Delete/Pause on federated Mimir groups. The PR replaces it with const isFederated = false with a TODO. Federated groups are now treated as mutable, so users will be offered Edit/Delete/Pause on rules that must be immutable, risking failed API calls or unintended mutations.

title: Provisioned check fails open when provenance missing
body: isProvisionedPromRule returns Boolean(promRule.provenance) and the new provenance field on GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase is optional. Any response without that field (older server, cache, mock) evaluates to false, so provisioned Grafana rules are classified as editable/removable/pausable. Combined with the new prom-only abilities path, provisioned rules can show Edit/Duplicate/Delete/Pause in the list view.

title: Creating/deleting states silently dropped
body: GrafanaGroupLoader no longer fetches the ruler group or runs matchRules. Rules that exist only in ruler (just created, Prometheus not yet synced) now disappear entirely instead of showing Creating, and rules deleted from ruler but still in Prometheus now render as normal instead of Deleting. Users see stale normal rows that will fail on edit/delete, or missing rows with no explanation.

title: Prom-only non-Grafana rules lose all actions
body: getEditableIdentifier returns undefined for a prom-only rule that is not a Grafana prom rule, and RuleActionsButtons returns null in that case. That removes the entire Stack including the More menu (Copy link, Silence, etc.), not just Edit. Any consumer rendering a cloud Prometheus-only rule without ruler data gets no actions at all.

title: Pause menu item impossible without rulerRule
body: In AlertRuleMenu.tsx line 123 the pause item is gated on `canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) && groupIdentifier.groupOrigin === 'grafana'`. In the list view rulerRule is undefined by design, so even when `canPause` is true via the new promRule ability path the condition is false. Consequence: Pause/Unpause can never be shown from the list view despite the OR-combined ability check.

title: Delete menu item requires rulerRule
body: In AlertRuleMenu.tsx line 165 the delete item is rendered only if `canDelete && rulerRule`. When the caller passes only promRule (new GrafanaRuleListItem path) canDelete can be true via useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities but rulerRule is undefined, so no Delete item is ever rendered. Consequence: delete disappears from the list view and the handleDelete path requiring RulerRuleDTO is unreachable.

title: Silence drawer never opens for prom-only rules
body: In RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx lines 104-106 the drawer is rendered only if `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` where `rule` is the optional RulerRuleDTO. List-view callers now pass only promRule, so `rule` is undefined, the condition is false, but AlertRuleMenu still shows Silence via grafana abilities and calls setShowSilenceDrawer(true). Consequence: clicking Silence notifications does nothing, no drawer appears.

title: Federated rule immutability removed
body: In useAbilities.ts useAllRulerRuleAbilities now hardcodes `isFederated = false` with a TODO, removing the prior `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` check. immutableRule therefore no longer covers federated groups. Consequence: federated Mimir/Enterprise rule groups that must be read-only become editable/deletable/pausable from the UI.

title: Missing React key on Grafana list items
body: In FilterView.tsx the map over rules renders `<GrafanaRuleListItem>` without a `key` prop, while the datasource and unknown branches pass `key={key}`. The `key` is computed into state but not forwarded. Consequence: React reconciliation warnings, incorrect reuse of list item state, and degraded infinite-scroll behavior.

title: Malformed grafana rule key with extra brace
body: In FilterView.tsx getGrafanaRuleKey returns `grafana-${namespace.uid}-${groupName}-${rule.uid}}` with a trailing extra `}`. Consequence: frontend-only keys are malformed, risking confusion or collisions when deduplicating or debugging list keys.

title: Silence drawer never opens for prom-only rules in list view
body: In public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/components/RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx the silence drawer is gated on `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`. In the new list view GrafanaRuleListItem only passes `promRule`, so `rule` is undefined. Clicking Silence sets showSilenceDrawer true but the condition stays false, so SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer never renders and the action appears to do nothing.

title: Pause menu item requires rulerRule so never shows in list view
body: In AlertRuleMenu.tsx canPause is computed as OR of ruler and prom abilities, but rendering is gated on `canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)`. In the list view rulerRule is undefined by design, so the Pause item never renders even when the prom-based ability says pause is supported and allowed. Users lose pause/unpause from the list.

title: Delete menu item requires rulerRule so never shows in list view
body: In AlertRuleMenu.tsx delete is gated on `canDelete && rulerRule`. In the list view rulerRule is undefined, so Delete never appears even when grafana prom abilities allow it. The handler in RuleActionsButtons.V2 only needs identifier/groupIdentifier, so the extra rulerRule requirement unnecessarily removes delete from the list.

title: Federated rule protection removed
body: In useAbilities.ts useAllRulerRuleAbilities hardcodes `isFederated = false` with a TODO, replacing the previous `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` check. Federated Mimir groups (with source_tenants) are therefore no longer treated as immutable, so Update/Delete/Pause abilities become supported when they should be blocked, allowing edit attempts that will fail or corrupt federated groups.

title: Missing React key for Grafana list items
body: In FilterView.tsx the grafana branch renders `<GrafanaRuleListItem rule={rule} ... />` without `key={key}`, while the datasource and unknown branches pass `key={key}`. Without keys React cannot correctly reconcile the infinite-scroll list, causing warnings, unnecessary remounts, and potential state/menu mix-ups when pages load.

title: Rule view link drops returnTo parameter
body: In GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx href is built as `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` without returnTo, while the removed GrafanaRuleLoader used `createReturnTo()` and passed `{ returnTo }`. Navigating to View from the list no longer preserves where to return, breaking back navigation to filtered/group list context.

title: Interpolating before range-variable guard defeats no-split rule
body: In querySplitting.ts runSplitQuery now does .filter(expr).map(applyTemplateVariables) and then partitions with querySupportsSplitting which checks !isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr). Because applyTemplateVariables expands template variables via replace (as the new test shows for $__auto/$step), an expr containing $__range/$__range_s/$__range_ms no longer contains that marker after interpolation. The guard therefore never fires and range-variable queries that must not be split are split. All split sub-requests then reuse the full-range interpolated value instead of each split range getting its own $__range, returning incorrect data.

title: Filter-before-interpolate lets empty-after-interpolation queries through
body: In shardQuerySplitting.ts runShardSplitQuery changed from interpolateVariablesInQueries(...).filter(expr).filter(!hide) to request.targets.filter(expr).filter(!hide).map(applyTemplateVariables). If a variable expands to empty (e.g. expr '$var' with empty value) the old code dropped the query after interpolation, the new code keeps it because emptiness is tested on the raw expr. That causes needless fetchLabelValues for __stream_shard__ with a bad selector and downstream shard sub-queries with empty selectors.

title: Empty check runs on raw expr instead of interpolated expr
body: In querySplitting.ts runSplitQuery filters !hide and query.expr before calling datasource.applyTemplateVariables. A query like expr '$expr' is non-empty before interpolation but can become '' after interpolation. Because the empty filter already ran, the query is kept, grouped, split and sent to runQuery instead of being ignored like other empty queries. This wastes requests and can send invalid empty selectors to the backend.

title: Empty-expression filter runs before interpolation
body: In runSplitQuery targets are filtered by `query.expr` truthiness on lines 296-298 and only then mapped through `datasource.applyTemplateVariables`. A raw expr like `$var` is truthy so it passes the filter, but after interpolation it can become empty string. That empty query is then classified by isLogsQuery/metric path, partitioned, and executed via datasource.runQuery instead of being skipped like other empty queries. The filter must run after interpolation.

title: Shard path interpolates twice via nested runSplitQuery
body: runShardSplitQuery now maps every target through datasource.applyTemplateVariables, then builds subRequest objects and calls runSplitQuery which maps the same targets through applyTemplateVariables again in querySplitting.ts. The updated test in shardQuerySplitting.test.ts asserts applyTemplateVariables is called 5 times for a single target, proving per-shard-group re-interpolation. This is redundant template work scaling with shard count and makes correctness depend on applyTemplateVariables being perfectly idempotent for expr and step.

title: Empty check runs before interpolation
body: In runSplitQuery the code filters request.targets by !query.hide and query.expr and only then maps through datasource.applyTemplateVariables. A query whose expr is a variable that interpolates to empty string (e.g. expr='$var' with empty value) passes the truthy check and is then split, grouped and executed via runQuery. It should be ignored like other empty queries. The filter for empty expr must run after interpolation, not before. Same pattern exists in shardQuerySplitting.ts.

title: Shard path interpolates twice via nested runSplitQuery
body: runShardSplitQuery now maps every target through datasource.applyTemplateVariables and then calls runSplitQuery on each shard sub-request, and runSplitQuery maps through applyTemplateVariables again. The updated test proves it: a single target causes 5 applyTemplateVariables calls. This is redundant work on every dashboard query and risks freezing range-dependent variables to the outer range instead of the split range if interpolation is not idempotent. The inner time-splitting path should reuse the already-interpolated queries.

title: TestLogger.FromContext discards logged output
body: TestLogger.FromContext in pkg/plugins/log/fake.go returns NewTestLogger() instead of the receiver. LoggerMiddleware now does m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), so when tests inject a TestLogger the Info/Warn/Error call goes to a fresh throwaway instance. The original TestLogger under test never records Calls/Message/Ctx, making log assertions impossible and hiding regressions.

title: Missing nil-request guard causes panic before LoggerMiddleware
body: ContextualLoggerMiddleware QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics in contextual_logger_middleware.go dereference req.PluginContext and req fields unconditionally. LoggerMiddleware in the same package explicitly checks if req == nil and bypasses logging, proving nil requests are expected. Because ContextualLoggerMiddleware is ordered outer to LoggerMiddleware, a nil request panics in instrumentContext path before reaching the nil-safe logger.

title: MetricsMiddleware dereferences nil request
body: MetricsMiddleware.QueryData in metrics_middleware.go does for _, v := range req.Queries and CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics access req.PluginContext/req.Body without a nil check. The sibling LoggerMiddleware handles req == nil, so nil is a valid input. Placed outer in the chain, this middleware will panic with nil dereference on such requests.

title: Adding FromContext to Logger interface breaks implementers
body: Logger interface in pkg/plugins/log/ifaces.go gains a new required method FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger. Any existing implementation of plugins/log.Logger outside this PR (other mocks, wrappers, external code) will fail to compile. Adding a method to a public interface is a breaking API change and requires updating all implementers or providing a default.

title: Fragile type assertion silently drops contextual logger
body: grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext in pkg/plugins/log/logger.go does d.l.FromContext(ctx).(*log.ConcreteLogger) and on failure returns d.New() with no attributes. If the infra logger returns a different implementation of its Logger interface or nil, all contextual attributes added by ContextualLoggerMiddleware (endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname) are silently discarded and the Plugin Request Completed log loses its correlation fields.

title: ContextualLoggerMiddleware panics on nil requests
body: QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth and CollectMetrics dereference req (e.g. req.PluginContext) without a nil check. LoggerMiddleware in the same package explicitly guards `if req == nil`, showing nil requests are expected. A nil request through this middleware causes a nil-pointer panic instead of delegating to next.

title: TestLogger.FromContext discards logged output
body: TestLogger.FromContext returns a brand new TestLogger instead of itself or a logger sharing storage. LoggerMiddleware now does `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`, so when tests inject a TestLogger the Info/Warn/Error counts go to the discarded instance. Assertions on the original InfoLogs/WarnLogs/ErrorLogs will always see zero calls, breaking test observability and diverging from the real wrapper which preserves the underlying logger.

title: MetricsMiddleware shares mutable instance across clients
body: NewMetricsMiddleware creates one *MetricsMiddleware and on each decoration does `imw.next = next; return imw`. The same struct is reused for every plugin client, mutating `next` without synchronization. Concurrent decoration or multiple clients causes data races and requests routed to the wrong `next` client. ContextualLoggerMiddleware in the same PR correctly creates a new struct per decoration.

title: Adding FromContext breaks Logger interface implementers
body: The Logger interface gains a new required method `FromContext(context.Context) Logger`. Any out-of-tree implementation of the old 5-method interface no longer compiles. This is a breaking API change made without a fallback, adapter, or major-version note, while only the in-tree wrapper and test fake were updated.

title: LoggerMiddleware drops traceID from request logs
body: The old logRequest explicitly added `traceID` from `tracing.TraceIDFromContext` plus pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname. The new version only logs status/duration/eventName and relies on `m.logger.FromContext(ctx)`. The context enrichment in instrumentContext only adds endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname and never adds traceID, so Plugin Request Completed logs lose trace correlation unless the underlying logger injects it, which the removed code did not rely on.

title: TestLogger.FromContext discards recorded logs
body: pkg/plugins/log/fake.go FromContext returns NewTestLogger() instead of the receiver. pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/logger_middleware.go now logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...). When the injected logger is a TestLogger, the Info call goes to a fresh instance, so callers asserting on the original TestLogger see 0 calls and lose message/ctx. The fake diverges from the real wrapper which derives from the base logger, breaking test observability.

title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware panics on nil request
body: ContextualLoggerMiddleware QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth and CollectMetrics dereference req (e.g. req.PluginContext) without a nil check. LoggerMiddleware in the same package explicitly guards req==nil and passes through. Because CreateMiddlewares places ContextualLoggerMiddleware outside LoggerMiddleware, a nil request panics in the new middleware before the existing guard is reached, turning a pass-through case into a crash.

title: LoggerMiddleware loses explicit fields and depends on outer middleware
body: logger_middleware.go removed explicit pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName, dsUID and traceID from logParams and now relies on m.logger.FromContext(ctx) populated by ContextualLoggerMiddleware. The new contextual_logger_middleware.go instrumentContext only adds endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname and does not add traceID that the old logRequest added via tracing.TraceIDFromContext. Result: Plugin Request Completed logs lose trace correlation, and any use of LoggerMiddleware without the new middleware in front of it or in a different order silently loses plugin context that was previously self-contained.

title: Cache is populated before DB write, so rejected devices bypass limit
body: In pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go tagDeviceUI() checks localCache, then calls SetDefault(key) before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice(). If CreateOrUpdateDevice() returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the cache entry is left in place. The next request for the same new deviceId hits the early-return cache path and returns nil without touching the DB, so authentication succeeds even though the device was never persisted. The limit is therefore only enforced once per cache TTL. Fix: only Set the cache after a successful create/update, and do not cache failures.

title: Count-then-insert check is not atomic and can exceed device limit
body: In pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go CreateOrUpdateDevice() does CountDevices() and if count >= deviceLimit falls back to update-only, otherwise does an upsert INSERT. The check and the insert are two separate transactions with no lock or unique-count constraint. Two concurrent requests for different new devices can both observe count < limit and both insert, overshooting the configured limit. Fix with a transaction/serializable guard, atomic insert guarded by count, or document that the limit is best-effort.

title: Anonymous auth now blocks on synchronous DB write with no timeout
body: In pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go Authenticate() previously tagged the device in a background goroutine with a 2-minute timeout using context.Background(), so login never waited for the DB. The PR changed it to call anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...) synchronously on the request context, which does CountDevices() plus an insert/update. Every anonymous request now pays DB latency on the auth hot path, and a slow DB stalls login with no bound other than request cancellation. This is a latency/availability regression. Fix: keep enforcement but add a short timeout, fail-open on timeout/DB error, or revert to async with enforcement only where needed.

title: ProvideAnonymousDeviceService breaks DI by replacing AnonStore with sqlStore
body: In pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go ProvideAnonymousDeviceService() changed its injected parameter from anonStore anonstore.AnonStore to sqlStore db.DB and now hard-codes anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore(sqlStore, cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit) internally. Any wire injector, enterprise override, or test that provided a custom/mock AnonStore no longer compiles or can inject a fake. It also makes the service untestable without a real DB. Fix: keep accepting AnonStore and inject the limit separately, or provide a constructor overload.

title: updateDevice uses ? placeholders on all DB types, breaks Postgres
body: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go updateDevice builds UPDATE with ? placeholders for all drivers. CreateOrUpdateDevice right below switches on GetDBType and uses $1..$5 for Postgres because Postgres does not accept ?. updateDevice has no such switch, so on Postgres the Exec will fail with syntax error when the device limit is reached, meaning limit enforcement is broken on Postgres.

title: Device cache set before DB write lets rejected devices bypass limit on retry
body: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go tagDeviceUI does localCache.SetDefault(key) before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice and never removes it on error. If CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the cache entry for that new deviceID remains. The next Authenticate with the same deviceID hits the cache in tagDeviceUI and returns nil, so authentication succeeds without a DB row. An attacker denied once can retry with the same ID to bypass the limit.

title: Count-then-insert check is not atomic, limit can be exceeded
body: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go CreateOrUpdateDevice does CountDevices then, if count >= limit, update-only else unconditional INSERT/UPSERT in separate sessions/transactions. Concurrent anonymous logins can both observe count < limit and both insert, exceeding the configured deviceLimit. There is no transaction, lock, or unique-count constraint to make the check atomic.

title: Expired existing device cannot re-activate once limit is reached
body: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go updateDevice requires updated_at BETWEEN now-30d AND now+1m and returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when rowsAffected==0. CountDevices only counts rows in that same active window, so a device whose row expired (>30d old) is not counted but its update also matches 0 rows and is rejected as over-limit. A returning stale device can never refresh its row while at limit, permanently locking it out.

title: Anonymous auth changed from async fire-and-forget to synchronous DB writes
body: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go Authenticate previously tagged the device in a background goroutine with its own timeout so login never waited on the anon_device table. It now calls TagDevice synchronously on the request context, which when deviceLimit>0 adds a SELECT COUNT(*) plus INSERT/UPDATE to the critical auth path of every anonymous request. This adds latency, DB load, and couples login availability to the anon store; request cancellation also cancels tagging.

title: ProvideAnonymousDeviceService breaks DI by replacing AnonStore with db.DB
body: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go ProvideAnonymousDeviceService changed its parameter from anonstore.AnonStore to db.DB and now constructs the store internally via ProvideAnonDBStore(sqlStore, cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit). Callers, wire injectors, and tests that injected a mock/fake AnonStore can no longer do so, and the service cannot be unit-tested without a real DB. The constructor should keep accepting the interface and pass the limit separately.

title: Failed device-limit check is cached, allowing bypass
body: In AnonDeviceService.tagDeviceUI in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go the localCache entry is set with SetDefault before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice. If the DB call fails with ErrDeviceLimitReached for a new device, the cache entry remains for ~29 minutes. The next request for the same deviceID hits the cache early-return nil path and authenticates successfully, so the device limit denies only the first request and then allows the device. Cache should only be populated after a successful store, or evicted on failure.

title: Count-then-insert device limit is racy
body: In AnonDBStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go the code does CountDevices, then if count >= limit calls updateDevice, otherwise does an upsert, in separate sessions with no transaction or lock. Concurrent anonymous logins can all observe count < limit and all insert, exceeding the configured limit. A hard limit needs atomic enforcement e.g. transaction with locking, serialized insertion, or post-insert trimming.

title: Unchanged UPDATE reports limit-reached for existing devices
body: In AnonDBStore.updateDevice in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go rowsAffected==0 is mapped unconditionally to ErrDeviceLimitReached. On MySQL an UPDATE that sets columns to their existing values affects 0 rows without CLIENT_FOUND_ROWS, and similarly any no-op heartbeat can return 0. An existing device that is still within the 30-day window but sends identical client_ip/user_agent would then be treated as over-limit and denied authentication, even though updates for existing devices should succeed when limited.

title: Anonymous tagging moved to synchronous auth path
body: In pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go Anonymous.Authenticate previously tagged the device in a background goroutine with a 2-minute timeout and never blocked login. It now calls TagDevice synchronously with the request context, which does CountDevices plus Insert/Update. Every cache-miss anonymous authentication now pays two DB round-trips on the login path, increasing p99 login latency and making anonymous logins fail or hang when the DB is slow, and tying tagging lifetime to request cancellation.
