title: Constructor signature change breaks DI / callers
body: In pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go ProvideAnonymousDeviceService was changed from taking anonStore anonstore.AnonStore to taking sqlStore db.DB and internally calling ProvideAnonDBStore(sqlStore, cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit), while ProvideAnonDBStore now requires an int64 deviceLimit. Any wire/fx provider set or test that supplies AnonStore or calls ProvideAnonDBStore with one argument no longer resolves; a plain int64 cannot be auto-wired. This is a breaking provider contract that needs wire set updates or a separate config-injected constructor.

title: No test that existing device can update after limit reached
body: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database_test.go only verifies that a second distinct deviceID is rejected with ErrDeviceLimitReached when limit=1. It never verifies the intended allowed path: re-tagging the first existing device after the limit is reached should succeed via updateDevice. The negative-cache bug and the unchanged-row bug above would not be caught by the current tests.

title: Unintended 10x increase in cleanup frequency
body: In pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go the ticker was changed from time.Minute*10 to time.Minute*1 with no mention in the PR description. This runs all cleanup jobs (snapshots, versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs, query history) every minute instead of every 10 minutes, increasing DB and IO load 10x and making the annotation cleanup that this PR is trying to de-escalate run far more often.

title: Leftover Error-level debug logging floods logs
body: In pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go CleanAnnotations and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags log every batch with r.log.Error including the full ids slice, cond, and err which is nil on success. With batch sizes up to 32767 this emits tens of thousands of IDs per batch at Error level on every cleanup cycle, polluting error logs, triggering false alerts, and causing log volume and performance problems. These statements should be removed or demoted to Debug.

title: Unintended 10x increase in cleanup frequency
body: pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go line 77 changes the background ticker from 10 minutes to 1 minute with no mention in the PR description. This affects all cleanup jobs (snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs, query history), increasing DB and IO load 10x in production and partially defeating the deadlock-reduction goal. It looks like leftover debugging and should be reverted.

title: Leftover Error-level debug logging with full ID lists
body: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, 579 call r.log.Error on every cleanup batch for normal operation, logging count, full ids slice (up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize, e.g. 32767 IDs), cond, and a nil err. This will emit Error-level false alarms on every run (now every minute), with huge log lines causing log volume, CPU, disk and ingestion cost, and can mask real errors. These debug statements should be removed or demoted to Debug without dumping all IDs.

title: Cleanup ticker changed from 10m to 1m without explanation
body: pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go:77 changes time.NewTicker(time.Minute*10) to time.NewTicker(time.Minute*1). The PR description only discusses splitting annotation cleanup queries to avoid MySQL deadlocks. Running every cleanup job (snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs, query history) 10x more often massively increases DB and IO load and is unrelated to the fix. Revert to 10 minutes or justify separately.

title: Debug logging left at Error level in cleanup path
body: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go lines 534,537,554,557,576,579 call r.log.Error for routine operation (e.g. "Annotations to clean by time", "cleaned annotations by time", "Tags to clean") with err==nil and including full id lists and cond on every batch. Every successful cleanup run will emit Error-level logs, triggering false alerts and log spam and potentially logging thousands of IDs. These should be Debug (or removed).

title: Split fetch/delete loop can stop early on concurrent deletes
body: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:656 in untilDoneOrCancelled stops when affected==0. With the old single-statement DELETE, zero affected meant no more rows matched. With the new split SELECT ids then DELETE BY ids, affected==0 no longer implies done: the fetched IDs may have been concurrently deleted while unfetched deletable rows remain. The loop then exits prematurely and leaves work for the next cycle. Termination should be based on empty fetch (len(ids)==0), not RowsAffected.

title: Quadratic string building for large SQLite IN list
body: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:609-612 builds the SQLite IN list with values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v) in a loop. With batch sizes up to 32767 (covered by the new test) this is O(n^2) copying. Since IDs are int64 from the DB, use strings.Builder with strconv.AppendInt to build the list in linear time.

title: Async legacy write inherits cancelled request context
body: In Create (and identically in Delete/Update/DeleteCollection) the goroutine does context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...) where ctx is the incoming request context that already has the klog value added. When the API request completes the parent context is cancelled, which immediately cancels the child, so the best-effort legacy write can be aborted before it runs. The consequence is the legacy backup silently diverges. The async work must derive from a detached context (e.g. context.WithoutCancel or context.Background) plus timeout.

title: Legacy Create replicates pre-storage input instead of stored result
body: Create writes d.Storage.Create(ctx, obj, ...) to get `created`, but the background goroutine calls d.Legacy.Create(ctx, obj, ...) with the original input object. Any defaulting, UID/ResourceVersion, creationTimestamp or mutation performed by unified storage is lost in legacy, leaving the two stores permanently divergent. The legacy call should replicate `created`.

title: Legacy Update reuses same UpdatedObjectInfo concurrently
body: Update calls d.Storage.Update with objInfo and then reuses the identical objInfo interface value in a background goroutine for d.Legacy.Update. UpdatedObjectInfo.UpdatedObject() is invoked once per store against different old objects and can be stateful/one-shot; invoking it a second time asynchronously can produce a wrong object, resourceVersion conflict, or data race. The consequence is failed or corrupt legacy writes. Snapshot the updated object from the storage result instead of re-invoking objInfo.

title: Delete records object name as metrics kind label
body: In Delete the success path calls d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage) where the third argument is the metric kind label but `name` (the object name) is passed instead of options.Kind. This mislabels delete latency and creates unbounded high-cardinality label values, one series per object name, which can overload Prometheus.

title: Legacy DeleteCollection recorded as storage duration
body: In DeleteCollection the background legacy call ends with d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy). It measures a legacy-store operation but records it with the storage histogram, so legacy latency/errors are invisible and storage metrics are polluted. It should call d.recordLegacyDuration.

title: Storage Create/Update failures recorded as legacy duration
body: In Create on d.Storage.Create error the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...), and Update does the same on d.Storage.Update error at line 129. A storage failure is recorded against the legacy histogram and no storage failure is recorded, inverting observability and alerting. Both error branches should call d.recordStorageDuration(true, ...).

title: Async legacy failures are never logged
body: All four background legacy writes (Create, Delete, Update, DeleteCollection) capture the legacy error only for the err != nil metric flag and then discard it with no log. Unlike the prior synchronous code that logged legacy errors, operators now have no message identifying which object/kind failed to replicate to legacy. Log the legacy error with the request logger before dropping it.

title: Delete discards enriched logger context
body: Delete builds log := d.Log.WithValues(name, kind, method) but then does ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log), putting the base logger instead of `log` into the context. All downstream log calls and the storage call lose the name/kind/method fields, hampering debugging. It should pass `log`.

title: Async legacy write inherits cancelled request context
body: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go Create (and same pattern in Delete, Update, DeleteCollection) the background goroutine does context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...) where ctx is the incoming request context. When the API handler returns, the request context is cancelled, which immediately cancels the derived context and aborts the async legacy write. The result is that mode 3's best-effort legacy backup frequently never happens, leaving legacy and unified storage diverged. Fix by deriving from a detached context such as context.WithoutCancel(ctx) or context.Background().

title: Async legacy Create shares mutable obj causing race and stale write
body: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go Create passes the original obj pointer to the async d.Legacy.Create goroutine while also returning it to the caller. The caller can mutate the object after return while the goroutine reads it concurrently, which is a data race. It also writes the pre-storage object instead of the created result returned by Storage, so server-assigned fields (UID, resourceVersion, defaults) are lost in legacy. Fix by DeepCopying the storage result and passing that copy to legacy.

title: Create storage error recorded as legacy duration
body: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go Create, when d.Storage.Create fails the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) for the storage attempt. All other error paths record storage duration for storage failures. This misattributes latency/error metrics, hiding unified-storage failures and inflating legacy metrics. Should call recordStorageDuration.

title: Update storage error recorded as legacy duration
body: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go Update, when d.Storage.Update fails the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) instead of d.recordStorageDuration. This corrupts the mode/kind/method metrics and makes storage failures invisible. Should mirror Delete and DeleteCollection error handling.

title: Delete success metric uses object name as kind label
body: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go Delete success path calls d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, ...) where the third argument is the object name. Every other call passes options.Kind as the kind label. This creates unbounded high-cardinality metric labels (one series per object name) and breaks dashboards that group by kind. Should pass options.Kind.

title: DeleteCollection legacy outcome recorded as storage metric
body: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go DeleteCollection the async legacy block calls d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...) for the legacy call. The Create/Delete/Update paths correctly call recordLegacyDuration for legacy work. This misclassifies legacy latency/errors as storage, making legacy backup health unobservable. Should call recordLegacyDuration.

title: Delete drops enriched logger when building context
body: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go Delete builds log with name/kind/method but then does klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log) instead of klog.NewContext(ctx, log). All other methods propagate the enriched logger. The consequence is Delete request logs lose name/kind/method fields, hindering debugging. Should pass log.

title: Async legacy write inherits request context and will be cancelled
body: In Create (line 51) and identically in Delete (line 110), Update (line 135) and DeleteCollection (line 163), the background goroutine does context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...) where ctx is the incoming request context. When the API handler returns, that parent context is cancelled, which immediately cancels the child. So the intended asynchronous write to legacy will almost always be cancelled/timed out and never complete, silently diverging legacy and unified storage. The async work must be detached, e.g. with context.WithoutCancel or context.Background, before applying the 10s timeout.

title: Create replicates stale input object to legacy instead of stored result
body: Create writes to Storage and gets back `created`, but the async legacy write calls d.Legacy.Create(ctx, obj, ...) with the original input `obj`. The storage result typically contains assigned UID, resourceVersion, creationTimestamp and defaults/mutations. Legacy will therefore receive a stale object missing those fields, permanently diverging the two stores. It should replicate `created` (ideally a deep copy, since it is shared with the returned response and the goroutine).

title: Update reuses single-use UpdatedObjectInfo for two stores concurrently
body: Update calls d.Storage.Update with `objInfo` synchronously and then reuses the same `objInfo` in an async goroutine for d.Legacy.Update. The previous implementation fetched the updated object once and wrapped it in an updateWrapper so both stores wrote the identical object. Re-invoking UpdatedObjectInfo.UpdatedObject a second time can compute a different object, fail on resourceVersion/concurrency checks, or race with request-scoped state. The storage result should be captured and replayed to legacy instead of re-executing objInfo.

title: Storage errors recorded as legacy metrics (Create/Update)
body: On synchronous storage failure, Create line 45 and Update line 129 call recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) with startStorage. The failure was in Storage, not legacy, and no legacy call was made. This misattributes latency/error metrics, hiding storage failures and inflating legacy error rates. They should call recordStorageDuration(true, ...).

title: Delete storage metric uses object name as kind label
body: Delete success path calls d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, ...) passing the object `name` where the `kind` label (options.Kind) is expected. Every deleted object name becomes a distinct metric label value, causing high cardinality and making kind-based dashboards/alerts useless. It should pass options.Kind like the error path and other methods do.

title: DeleteCollection legacy result recorded as storage metric
body: Inside the async legacy goroutine for DeleteCollection, the code calls d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...) instead of d.recordLegacyDuration. Legacy delete-collection latency/errors will therefore be attributed to unified storage, corrupting both sets of metrics. It should call recordLegacyDuration like Create/Delete/Update do.

title: Delete discards enriched logger when building context
body: Delete builds `log := d.Log.WithValues(name, kind, method)` but then does klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log), discarding those values. All downstream storage/legacy logs and context-derived logging lose name/kind/method correlation, unlike Create/Get/Update/DeleteCollection which propagate `log`. It should pass `log`.

title: Mode3 tests never verify async legacy writes
body: Mode3 writes are now asynchronous via `go func()`, but TestMode3_Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection only assert the synchronous storage return value and return immediately. They never wait for or assert the legacy mock was called, and several cases don't even set up a legacy expectation. A broken or missing legacy replication (wrong object, cancelled context, wrong metrics) would still pass. Tests need synchronization/assertion of the background legacy call.

title: Missing second cache check after acquiring write lock
body: GetWebAssets does a check under RLock at line 45 and then acquires the write Lock at line 48 without re-checking entryPointAssetsCache. Two goroutines that both observe ret==nil can then both proceed to do file/CDN I/O sequentially and publish. This causes thundering-herd I/O on cold start and allows a later writer to overwrite a good value just published by an earlier writer, including overwriting it with a failure.

title: Failure result unconditionally overwrites cache
body: Line 69 does entryPointAssetsCache = result even when readWebAssetsFromFile/CDN returned an error and result is nil. Combined with the missing re-check, a transient failure in one concurrent caller wipes a good EntryPointAssets value just cached by another caller, turning subsequent requests into errors and forcing repeated disk reads. The cache should only be updated when err==nil and result!=nil.

title: Missing re-check of cache after acquiring write lock
body: In pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go GetWebAssets does a fast-path RLock read, then unconditionally takes the write Lock and reloads. It never re-checks entryPointAssetsCache after acquiring the write lock. If N goroutines miss the fast path concurrently, they queue on Lock and each reloads assets-manifest.json (and CDN) sequentially even though the first one already repopulated the cache. This is broken double-checked locking that causes thundering-herd file/network I/O in production.

title: Error result overwrites last-good cache
body: In pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go GetWebAssets unconditionally does entryPointAssetsCache = result before returning. If readWebAssetsFromFile/CDN fails, result is nil and err is non-nil, so a transient failure wipes a previously cached good value (notably in Dev mode where every call reloads). Callers then get nil plus error even though a valid value existed. Cache should only be updated when err == nil and result != nil.

title: Exclusive lock held across blocking file/network I/O
body: In pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go GetWebAssets holds entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock() (deferred unlock) across readWebAssetsFromFile and readWebAssetsFromCDN, which do disk I/O and an HTTP request. While one caller is blocked in I/O, all other callers block on the mutex, and pending writers starve new RLocks in Go's RWMutex. This serializes all web-asset lookups on slow I/O. Load outside the lock (or use singleflight) and only hold the lock to publish the result.

title: Write lock held across I/O without re-checking cache
body: GetWebAssets takes entryPointAssetsCacheMu.RLock to snapshot the cache, releases it, then unconditionally takes entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock and performs file and potentially network I/O (readWebAssetsFromFile/CDN, GetContentDeliveryURL) while holding the exclusive lock, without re-reading entryPointAssetsCache after acquiring it. Two goroutines that both observe nil on the fast path will therefore both do the full load serially and last-writer-wins, and all concurrent readers block on RLock for the duration of that I/O. In Dev mode where the fast path never hits, every call takes the exclusive lock and is fully serialized. The fix should re-check the cache after acquiring the write lock and should not hold the exclusive lock across slow I/O (load outside the lock, then swap under lock, or bypass the global entirely in Dev).

title: SQL disable helper always returns false but still dereferences FeatureToggles
body: pkg/expr/reader.go:195 defines enableSqlExpressions() as `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...)` followed by `if enabled { return false }; return false`, so it always returns false. The feature-flag read is dead code with inverted logic, but it still dereferences h/h.features. Any SQL expression query with a nil reader or nil FeatureToggles (tests, minimal wiring) now panics instead of returning the intended 'not implemented' error, where the old SQL path never touched features. It also invites a future 'cleanup' of the inversion that silently re-enables CVE-2024-9264. It should just return false with a security comment and no flag read.

title: Legacy SQL path not explicitly disabled, bypasses new reader gate
body: pkg/expr/sql_command.go:25 NewSQLCommand() and :51 UnmarshalSQLCommand() have no disabled/feature check; only pkg/expr/reader.go:128-132 rejects SQL expressions. The old rawNode path is therefore blocked only incidentally because pkg/expr/sql/db.go is now a stub returning errors. That is single-point, fragile defense: any future fix to the stub, alternate constructor, or direct caller restores DuckDB RCE/LFI via the legacy path. Both NewSQLCommand and UnmarshalSQLCommand should fail fast with an explicit 'sql expressions disabled for security' error instead of attempting TablesList/QueryFramesInto.

title: Stub DB uses generic 'not implemented' hiding security disable
body: pkg/expr/sql/db.go:12-26 replaces the DuckDB backend with type DB and methods TablesList/RunCommands/QueryFramesInto that all return generic errors.New('not implemented'), and keeps the constructor name NewInMemoryDB(). A maintainer reading only this file sees a TODO to implement rather than an intentional security disable for CVE-2024-9264, risking reintroduction of the vulnerable DuckDB dependency. Errors are also indistinguishable from transient failures and, in sql_command.go Execute, become rsp.Error with nil Go error. Return an explicit disabled error referencing the CVE and comment why it must stay disabled.

title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false with inverted flag check and nil-unsafe dereference
body: In pkg/expr/reader.go enableSqlExpressions does `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions)` then returns false in both branches, so it always returns false. The negation is backwards (true when the flag is off) and dead, so a future maintainer fixing it to `return true` will enable SQL when the flag is off and disable it when on. It also unconditionally dereferences h.features; previously QueryTypeSQL had no feature check, so any caller constructing ExpressionQueryReader with nil FeatureToggles will now panic on IsEnabledGlobally instead of getting a clean error. It should just return false with a comment, or nil-guard the toggles.

title: Legacy SQL ingestion path has no explicit disable check
body: pkg/expr/reader.go now explicitly rejects QueryTypeSQL in ReadQuery, but pkg/expr/sql_command.go UnmarshalSQLCommand/NewSQLCommand have no such gate. They are only incidentally blocked because pkg/expr/sql/db.go is a stub returning 'not implemented' from TablesList/QueryFramesInto. That leaves two entry points with different errors, no defense-in-depth, and silent re-enablement of the DuckDB RCE/LFI surface if the DB implementation is ever restored. Both constructors should explicitly return a disabled error consistent with ReadQuery.

title: Data race on shared err and counter in init workers
body: searchSupport.init launches one errgroup goroutine per namespace. Inside the closure it does totalBatchesIndexed++ and _, _, err = s.build(...) where err is the outer variable from GetResourceStats. Multiple goroutines read/write the same err variable and increment the same int with no synchronization. This is a data race that corrupts the error return and the indexed count and will be flagged by -race. Use a local variable and return it, and use an atomic counter.

title: Narrowed BuildIndex lock allows duplicate builds for same key
body: BuildIndex previously held cacheMu for the whole build, which serialized builds. It now only locks around b.cache[key] = idx. Two concurrent getOrCreateIndex calls for the same NamespacedResource can both observe a miss, both call bleve.New on the same file directory and both run the builder, then last-writer-wins in the map. The loser index is leaked, IndexTenants metrics are double-incremented, and concurrent bleve.New on the same path can fail or corrupt the on-disk index. A per-key singleflight or double-checked lock is needed.

title: TotalDocs reads cache map without lock
body: TotalDocs iterates b.cache with no RLock while BuildIndex concurrently does b.cache[key] = idx under Lock. Concurrent map read and write is a fatal data race in Go and can crash the process. It must hold cacheMu.RLock during iteration. The race window was widened by allowing concurrent builds.

title: Watch loop uses Background context and ignores closed channel
body: searchSupport.init creates watchctx := context.Background() and then loops with v := <-events followed by handleEvent(watchctx, v). If the storage WatchWriteEvents channel closes, the receive returns nil forever, causing a hot infinite loop and a nil-pointer dereference inside handleEvent when it accesses evt.Type. The Background context is also never cancelled, so polling queries are not tied to server shutdown. Derive the watch context from the server context and check the ok result of the receive.

title: History/Origin panic when search is not configured
body: Search checks if s.search == nil and returns an error, but History and Origin unconditionally call s.search.History and s.search.Origin. When Search.Resources is nil, newSearchSupport is skipped and s.search stays nil, so any History or Origin RPC causes a nil-pointer panic. Add the same nil guard as Search.

title: Removing per-RPC Init checks removes stop gate
body: All handlers previously called s.Init(ctx) which returned s.initErr, so after Stop set initErr to stopping/stopped, new Read/List/Create/Update/Delete/Watch/Search calls failed fast. After this change NewResourceServer calls Init once and handlers never consult initErr, so after Stop cancels the broadcaster context the server keeps serving reads and writes against the backend. Either re-check a stopped/failed flag per RPC or document that Stop no longer gates traffic.

title: Silently skipping postgres storage-server test
body: The test now skips when GRAFANA_TEST_DB is postgres with only a TODO comment. If eager Init at startup breaks postgres, this skip hides the regression and reduces coverage for exactly the backend this PR touches. The skip should be justified with a linked issue or removed before merge.

title: Data race on init counter
body: In searchSupport.init the errgroup goroutines each execute totalBatchesIndexed++ on a plain int captured from the outer scope. With initWorkers > 1 this is a concurrent read-modify-write without atomic or mutex, so it is a data race and the reported namespaced_indexed count is unreliable.

title: TotalDocs reads cache map without lock
body: bleveBackend.TotalDocs ranges over b.cache with no cacheMu held, while BuildIndex concurrently does b.cache[key]=idx under lock and GetIndex uses RLock. Concurrent map read and write in Go is a fatal error / race. After removing the coarse BuildIndex lock, concurrent builds during startup make this reachable, and searchSupport.init calls TotalDocs after concurrent builds.

title: Concurrent duplicate BuildIndex for same key corrupts file index
body: Removing the global cacheMu around BuildIndex leaves only a short lock for the final map store. Two goroutines for the same NamespacedResource can both miss GetIndex, both call bleve.New on the same directory path and both build, then last-writer-wins in the map. Concurrent bleve.New on the same dir can fail or leave a partially written index, wastes work, double-increments IndexTenants, and leaks the loser index.

title: Watch loop never ends and panics on closed channel
body: searchSupport.init creates watchctx as context.Background, starts WatchWriteEvents, then loops as for { v := <-events; s.handleEvent(watchctx, v) } with no ok check and no cancellation tied to server Stop. When the backend poller stops it closes the channel, the receive returns nil, and handleEvent immediately dereferences evt.Type causing a nil panic. The goroutine also leaks after Stop because it does not watch any done context.

title: handleEvent dereferences IndexMetrics without nil check
body: searchSupport.init guards IndexMetrics with if IndexMetrics != nil, implying it can be nil, but handleEvent calls IndexMetrics.IndexedKinds.WithLabelValues(...).Inc/Dec and IndexMetrics.IndexLatency...Observe unconditionally. Any deployment or test with nil metrics will panic on the first watch event.

title: Stop no longer gates RPCs after lazy Init removal
body: server.Stop sets initErr to stopping/stopped, which previously caused all later RPCs to fail via their s.Init(ctx) check using sync.Once state. The PR removes all those checks, so after Stop the server keeps serving Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/Blobs. It also makes NewResourceServer block on full index build and fail construction where callers previously expected lazy initialization, and leaks the background cancel func when Init fails.

title: Postgres storage-server test disabled
body: The integration test for the storage-server target now skips postgres entirely. Since this PR changes startup initialization ordering that is backend-sensitive, losing postgres coverage hides regressions the test was meant to catch.

title: Data race on index counter during parallel init
body: In file pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go line 189, `totalBatchesIndexed++` is executed inside `group.Go` goroutines limited by `initWorkers` with no atomic or mutex. Concurrent increments of a plain int are a data race and can undercount or trigger the race detector. Use atomic or collect counts after `group.Wait()`.

title: TotalDocs reads cache map without lock
body: In file pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go line 146, `TotalDocs()` iterates `b.cache` with no lock, while `BuildIndex` writes `b.cache[key]` under `cacheMu.Lock` and `GetIndex` uses `RLock`. Concurrent init builds plus `TotalDocs()` called from `searchSupport.init` log line causes concurrent map read/write, which panics in Go. Hold `RLock` in `TotalDocs`.

title: Finer-grained lock allows duplicate builds for same key
body: In file pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go line 137, the lock was narrowed to only the final `b.cache[key]=idx` store. Two concurrent `BuildIndex` calls for the same `NamespacedResource` now both create bleve indexes, both run the expensive builder, both `Inc` tenant metrics, and race on `bleve.New(dir)` for file-backed indexes, with the loser leaking. Need per-key singleflight or check-and-set under lock.

title: Search watch loop leaks and panics on channel close
body: In file pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go line 209, init creates `watchctx := context.Background()` then loops `for { v := <-events; s.handleEvent(watchctx, v) }` with no `ok` check and no `ctx.Done` select. When the SQL poller closes the stream on shutdown, the receive returns nil forever, `handleEvent` dereferences nil `evt`, and the goroutine never exits because Background is never cancelled, leaking the watcher and the underlying poller.

title: Missing nil guard for IndexMetrics in watch handler
body: In file pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go lines 263 and 271, `handleEvent` calls `IndexMetrics.IndexedKinds.WithLabelValues(...).Inc()/Dec()` without checking `IndexMetrics != nil`, while the same file guards every other `IndexMetrics` use. If metrics are disabled `IndexMetrics` is nil and any write event panics the search watcher goroutine.

title: History/Origin panic when search disabled
body: In file pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go line 925 and 930, `History` and `Origin` unconditionally dereference `s.search`, while `Search` checks for nil. When `Search.Resources` is nil `s.search` is nil and these RPCs panic with nil dereference. The removal of lazy `Init` did not add the missing guard.

title: Call to non-existent zero-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled breaks compilation
body: UsernameForm.java line 47 calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments. The only definition in the superclass UsernamePasswordForm is isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring one argument. There is no zero-arg overload. The code cannot compile, breaking the whole services module. It should pass the user, e.g. isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()).

title: Passkeys conditional UI now requires a known user, disabling it on initial login
body: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) returns webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null. It is used in authenticate() and challenge() to decide whether to call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context). Previously the code filled the form when passkeys were enabled and context.getUser() == null (initial login). Now it only fills when context.getUser() != null (re-authentication). Initial login with no user therefore never gets ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI, challenge, RP ID or webauth form, breaking username-less / conditional-UI passkey login. The PR's own tests still expect //form[@id='webauth'] on the first page.

title: Re-authentication attributes set on throwaway form instance are lost
body: setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError() does LoginFormsProvider form = context.form(); form.setAttribute(USERNAME_HIDDEN,true); form.setAttribute(REGISTRATION_DISABLED,true); and then returns. The caller in AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler() and WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse() then creates a different instance via challenge()/errorChallenge.apply() which internally calls context.form() again. Each context.form() returns a new LoginFormsProvider, so attributes set on the first instance never reach the rendered response. After a failed password/passkey during re-authentication the page will show the regular login with editable username and registration link instead of hidden-username re-authentication.

title: Error response discards webauthn form state via multiple context.form() instances
body: createErrorResponse() calls context.form().setError(...), context.form().setAttribute(...), AuthenticatorUtils.setup...(context) which uses another context.form(), fillContextForm(context) whose returned LoginFormsProvider with new challenge and attributes is discarded, then return errorChallenge.apply(context) which builds yet another fresh form. Because each context.form() is a new instance, the error, ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI flag, and the fresh challenge/attributes never make it into the returned Response. On passkey failure the user gets a page without the error displayed and without valid conditional-UI data, and the auth-session challenge note does not match what was rendered.

title: Call to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not compile
body: UsernameForm.java line 47 calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with zero arguments, but the only definition in the parent class UsernamePasswordForm.java takes a UserModel argument: protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user). There is no zero-arg overload. The module will fail to compile, so nothing in this PR can build or ship.

title: Conditional passkeys disabled on initial login where user is null
body: UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate previously called webauthnAuth.fillContextForm when passkeys were enabled and no user was selected, which is the normal first-login conditional-UI case. The new code gates it with isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), which requires user != null. When context.getUser() is null on the initial login page the method returns false, so no challenge, no ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI attribute and no passkeys data are prepared. Usernameless/discoverable-key login on the first page is broken; the existing tests expect form[@id='webauth'] to be present on initial login.

title: Error challenge drops passkeys setup for initial login
body: The overridden challenge(context, error, field) changed from if (context.getUser() == null && webauthn enabled) to if (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())), which is only true when context.getUser() != null. On the initial login where the user is still unknown, a failed username/password attempt will re-render the login form without calling webauthnAuth.fillContextForm, so conditional passkeys disappear after the first error. The correct condition must allow passkeys regardless of whether a user is already selected, not invert the old user==null case to user!=null.

title: Call to zero-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not compile
body: UsernameForm.java line 47 calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only definition in parent UsernamePasswordForm.java takes a UserModel argument (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)). There is no zero-arg overload. The module will fail to compile, so the PR is unmergeable as shown.

title: Passkeys conditional-UI setup now skipped when no user is selected
body: Old code in authenticate() called webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) whenever passkeys were enabled. New code gates it with isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), which requires user != null (same gate added in challenge() at line 137). On the initial username/password page context.getUser() is null, so no challenge, RP-ID, or ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI is set up. That breaks usernameless/discoverable passkey login and autofill on first render, while the fix was only meant to add setup for the re-authentication case where user != null. The gate should be passkeys-enabled, not user != null.

title: getForLogin cache ignores organization invalidations
body: In InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin the cache is bypassed only if isInvalid(cacheKey) where cacheKey is realm+mode. In contrast getByOrganization at line 173 also checks isInvalid(orgId). Organization updates, disables, removals and link/unlink via OrganizationProvider register invalidation for the orgId, not for the login key. As a result a cached getForLogin(ORG_ONLY/ALL) list keeps returning IDs of brokers belonging to a disabled, removed or unlinked organization until some IDP create/update/remove happens. Callers that do not re-check isEnabled will display stale login options.

title: remove/update can NPE on missing IDP
body: In InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.remove, storedIdp from idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) can be null when the alias does not exist. If isInvalid(cacheKey) is true the code calls registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp) which dereferences idp.getInternalId() and throws NullPointerException instead of returning false. The same pattern exists in update where getById can return null and is passed to registerIDPInvalidation. Removing or updating a non-existent IDP should not throw.

title: Test cleanup uses literal alias instead of variable
body: In OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPByOrg and testCacheIDPForLogin the cleanup is getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) using the literal string "alias" instead of the created alias variable (e.g. alias, "org-idp-"+i, "idp-alias-"+i). The same mistake is repeated at lines 381 and 425. No cleanup is registered for the 10-20 IDPs actually created, leaving realm data behind and polluting other tests.

title: getForLogin ignores organization invalidations
body: In InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin only isInvalid(cacheKeyForLogin) is checked. In contrast getByOrganization checks isInvalid(cacheKeyOrgId) || isInvalid(orgId). Organization updates, removals, enable/disable, and link/unlink of IDPs via OrganizationProvider invalidate the orgId, not the login key. As a result a cached login list keyed by FetchMode continues to be served stale after org changes, returning IDPs that should have appeared/disappeared.

title: Login predicate NPE when IDP config is null
body: LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate now does idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC). If an IdentityProviderModel has a null config map, calling getForLogin invalidation via registerIDPLoginInvalidation/registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate throws NullPointerException. This breaks create/update/remove of such IDPs. The predicate must be null-safe for both the model and the config map.

title: remove/update NPE when IDP does not exist
body: In InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.remove the code fetches storedIdp via idpDelegate.getByAlias and unconditionally passes it to registerIDPInvalidation which dereferences idp.getInternalId(). If the alias does not exist storedIdp is null, so remove of a non-existent alias throws NPE instead of returning false. The same pattern exists in update where getById can return null and is passed to registerIDPInvalidation.

title: REALM_ONLY login path missing enabled re-check
body: The patch adds filter idp.isEnabled() to the ORG_ONLY and ALL paths from getForLogin with comment that cached IDPs might be wrapped and stale, but leaves the REALM_ONLY path filtering only on alias. A stale cached list can therefore still expose a disabled realm IDP on the login page, inconsistent with the other modes.

title: Login predicate NPEs when IdP config map is null
body: File server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java line 254 does idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC) without null-checking getConfig(). If an IdentityProviderModel has a null config map, getLoginPredicate().test(idp) throws NullPointerException. The predicate is called on every create/remove/update in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider to decide login-cache invalidation, so a single IdP with null config breaks those write paths. Use null-safe access like getConfig() != null and getOrDefault.

title: Update uses organization-aware wrapper for invalidation decision
body: File model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java line 91 fetches original via getById() which returns an organization-aware wrapper whose isEnabled() returns false when the linked organization is disabled. That wrapper is then passed to registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate which evaluates LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() using isEnabled(). When the org is disabled the original incorrectly evaluates as non-login, so an update that changes real login status (e.g. disabling the IdP) looks like false->false and skips invalidation. After the org is re-enabled the getForLogin cache still contains the stale IdP id. Fetch the raw delegate model for the predicate comparison instead of the wrapped model.

title: Test cleanup removes literal alias instead of created IdPs
body: File testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/organization/cache/OrganizationCacheTest.java line 303 (repeated at lines 381 and 425) does getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) with the literal string "alias" instead of the alias just created (org-idp-i / idp-alias-i / idp-alias-20). The cleanup therefore never removes the 20+10 IdPs created by testCacheIDPByOrg and testCacheIDPForLogin, leaving realm state polluted for subsequent tests and masking cache-isolation assertions.

title: New order() method has no default and breaks external implementations
body: CryptoProvider.java adds `int order()` without a default implementation. Every existing out-of-tree implementation of CryptoProvider will now fail to compile/link with NoSuchMethodError. The in-tree DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider were updated, but third-party providers were not. Consequence is a breaking API change; it should be a `default` method (e.g. default 0/100) to remain backwards compatible.

title: Multiple crypto providers silently ignored instead of failing
body: detectProvider() in CryptoIntegration.java previously threw IllegalStateException when more than one CryptoProvider was on the classpath. It now sorts by order() and silently picks the first, logging only at debug level. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return order 200, so if e.g. both default and FIPS jars are present the choice among equals is ServiceLoader-order dependent and non-deterministic. Consequence is misconfiguration (notably FIPS vs non-FIPS) is now hidden and the server may run with the wrong crypto stack without any warning.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns unrelated KeyStore provider
body: AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider() in AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, typically the JDK SUN provider, and presents it as the BouncyCastle provider. Callers that expect a BC/BCFIPS provider name or BC-specific algorithms via BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER will get the wrong provider, causing NoSuchAlgorithmException or silently using a different implementation. A lightweight provider should return null (like WildFlyElytronProvider does) or throw, not a misleading unrelated provider.

title: ECDSA conversion does not validate lengths and silently truncates
body: In AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java, concatenatedRSToASN1DER() assumes signature.length == signLength without checking and will throw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException on malformed input instead of IOException. Conversely asn1derToConcatenatedRS()/integerToBytes() truncates when BigInteger is negative or larger than qLength by copying only the low bytes without any check. Consequence is malformed or attacker-controlled DER signatures are silently mapped to a different valid-looking raw R||S value instead of being rejected, which is a signature-parsing integrity risk. Both directions must validate sizes and sign and throw IOException.

title: readSequence accepts indefinite length and trailing garbage
body: ASN1Decoder.readSequence() in ASN1Decoder.java calls readLength() which can return -1 for indefinite-length encoding 0x80, but readSequence() does not reject -1 and will return an empty list, later reported only as size != 2. It also never verifies that the declared sequence length was exactly consumed and that no trailing bytes remain after the sequence. Consequence is malformed DER signatures with indefinite lengths or appended garbage can be accepted into the ECDSA conversion path instead of being strictly rejected as required for DER.

title: Test reuses P-256 key for ES384/ES512 and never verifies signature
body: ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java generates one EC KeyPair with `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair()` (default P-256/secp256r1) in the constructor and reuses it for ES256, ES384 and ES512 tests. The ES384/ES512 cases therefore do not exercise real P-384/P-521 keys and lengths (e.g. 96/132 byte R||S), only zero-padded P-256 values. The test also only checks round-trip rs->DER->rs equality and never verifies the converted DER with Signature.verify() or compares to JCA output. Consequence is the test passes while giving false confidence about interop for larger curves and about correctness of the DER encoding.

title: New abstract order() breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: File common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoProvider.java line 44 adds abstract `int order()` to the public SPI without a default. Any out-of-tree implementation of CryptoProvider that compiled against the old interface will fail at runtime with AbstractMethodError and fail at compile time. The consequence is a breaking API change for custom providers. It should be a `default` method (e.g. default 0/100) to remain backwards compatible.

title: Same-order providers now silently win instead of failing fast
body: File common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java line 57 sorts by order and picks index 0, only logging ignored providers at debug. Previously multiple providers caused IllegalStateException. Now DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return 200, so if more than one is on the classpath the choice among them depends on ServiceLoader iteration order and is silently accepted. The consequence is non-deterministic crypto behavior and hidden misconfiguration (e.g. FIPS vs non-FIPS) that previously failed fast.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns non-BC provider violating contract
body: File authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java line 61 implements getBouncyCastleProvider() by returning `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, typically SUN/JKS, not BouncyCastle. The interface documents it as BouncyCastle provider and WildFlyElytronProvider returns null when there is no BC. Callers expecting BC/FIPS semantics that receive SUN will misbehave. It should return null like the Elytron provider when no BC is present.

title: concatenatedRSToASN1DER does not validate input length
body: File authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java line 103 splits `signature` into r/s with `len=signLength/2` via System.arraycopy without checking `signature.length == signLength`. A short or odd input throws raw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of IOException, and a long input is silently truncated. The consequence is unchecked runtime exceptions and potential silent mis-signing instead of a clean invalid-signature error.

title: integerToBytes silently truncates oversized/negative ECDSA integers
body: File authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java line 151 in integerToBytes() strips leading bytes when `qLength < bytes.length` and pads otherwise, without checking negativity or whether stripped bytes are zero. A DER INTEGER that is negative or larger than the curve order (invalid for ECDSA) is silently truncated to the low `qLength` bytes and accepted. The consequence is acceptance of malformed signatures and incorrect raw R||S values instead of throwing IOException.

title: readSequence ignores trailing bytes and indefinite length
body: File authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/ASN1Decoder.java line 49 readSequence() loops while `length>0` but never verifies that exactly `length` bytes were consumed and that no trailing bytes remain, and treats indefinite length -1 as empty. A DER signature with trailing garbage after the SEQUENCE will be silently accepted by asn1derToConcatenatedRS. The consequence is lenient parsing of malformed signatures that strict DER should reject.

title: Test reuses one P-256 key for ES384/ES512 and only checks round-trip
body: File authz/client/src/test/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/test/ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java line 46 `test()` uses a single `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair()` (default curve, effectively P-256) for ES256, ES384 and ES512, just padding the decoded values to the larger `getSignatureLength()`. It then only asserts `rsConcat` equals `rsConcat2` after DER->raw->DER->raw, never verifying with real P-384/P-521 keys nor verifying the JWS signature. The consequence is false confidence: interop/size errors for ES384/ES512 and invalid-value handling are not exercised.

title: New abstract order() breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: File common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoProvider.java adds abstract `int order();` without a default. Any out-of-tree CryptoProvider that implements the interface will fail to compile and, if already compiled, will fail at runtime with AbstractMethodError when ServiceLoader instantiates it. The method should be a `default` (e.g. return 0) to preserve backward compatibility.

title: Multiple providers silently resolved, ties are arbitrary
body: File common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java previously threw when more than one CryptoProvider was on the classpath. It now sorts by `order()` reversed and returns the first, logging ignored providers only at debug. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return 200, so a classpath containing two of them (a misconfiguration) is now silently resolved by ServiceLoader discovery order instead of failing fast, leading to non-deterministic crypto behavior.

title: readSequence does not reject trailing garbage or check constructed bit
body: File authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/ASN1Decoder.java `readSequence()` consumes `length` bytes of content but never verifies the outer buffer is fully consumed, so extra trailing bytes after the SEQUENCE are silently ignored. It also accepts indefinite-length (0x80 returns -1, yielding empty list) and primitive tag 0x10 instead of requiring constructed 0x30. For signature parsing this non-strict DER acceptance enables malleable/forged signatures to pass where strict verification should reject them.

title: Oversized/negative ECDSA integers are truncated instead of rejected
body: File authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java `integerToBytes()` truncates with `System.arraycopy(bytes, bytes.length - qLength, ...)` when `bytes.length > qLength`, and left-pads otherwise, without validating. Combined with `ASN1Decoder.readInteger()` using signed `new BigInteger(bytes)`, a DER signature containing a huge or negative r/s is silently truncated to `signLength/2` bytes and returned as a valid concatenated signature instead of throwing IOException. Attacker-controlled signatures must be rejected, not coerced.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns non-BC provider
body: File authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java `getBouncyCastleProvider()` returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, typically the SUN JKS provider, not a BouncyCastle provider. Callers that expect a BC/BCFIPS provider (registration, algorithms, `BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER`) will get the wrong provider, causing incorrect behavior or failures. It should return null like WildFlyElytronProvider or throw unsupported, not a misleading unrelated provider.

title: Dead ASN1Encoder calls in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
body: File authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java lines 114-115 call `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and the same for sBigInteger and discard the results before building the real sequence on lines 117-121. The dead encodes indicate leftover/copy-paste code and waste work; they should be removed. No input length validation is done either, so a wrong-sized `signature` fails with ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of IOException.

title: Test uses wrong curve and only checks round-trip self-consistency
body: File authz/client/src/test/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/test/ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java generates one default `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC")` key (P-256) and reuses it for ES256, ES384 and ES512, then only asserts `asn1->raw->der->raw` round-trips to itself. It never verifies the signature cryptographically, never uses P-384/P-521 keys, known vectors, leading-zero/high-bit r/s cases, or rejection of malformed/trailing/oversized DER, so truncation and strictness bugs are not caught.

title: FGAP listener breaks under V2 (UnsupportedOperationException)
body: registerListener now guards only on Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ but then calls management(...).clients()/roles()/groups().setPermissionsEnabled(). When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whose ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled (and likely other V2 variants) throws UnsupportedOperationException. So with V2 enabled (alone with V1, or both V1+V2 enabled) any ClientRemovedEvent/RoleRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent will throw from the event listener and break deletion. The guard must exclude V2 or handle V2 no-op.

title: Resource lookup uses wrong owner, per-client and global checks miss
body: hasPermission(ClientModel,String) does resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()) and hasPermission(String) does findByName(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, server.getId()). Resources are created in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource/init with owner resourceServer.getClientId() (or no owner for type resources) and looked up elsewhere with findByName(server, name) with no owner. Filtering by server.getId() as owner will not match, so per-instance resources are treated as missing and the global Clients type resource in hasPermission(String) is never found, making canManage()/canView()/canManageClientScopes() always false for V2 grants.

title: Null dereference when all-clients resource is missing
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel,String) when the per-client resource is null the code does resource = SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) and then immediately calls authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource). getResourceTypeResource returns null if the Clients type resource does not exist. Passing null resource to findByResource causes NPE instead of denying permission.

title: Global all-clients grant ignored once per-client resource exists
body: hasPermission(ClientModel,String) evaluates only one resource: if an instance resource for the client exists it evaluates that resource alone; only if it is missing does it fall back to the Clients type resource. So a caller with a valid all-clients permission (e.g. MAP_ROLES/MANAGE/VIEW on type Clients) is denied for any client that happens to have its own resource object created for a different scope. Correct evaluation must OR the instance-resource decision with the type-resource decision.

title: getResourceName does not handle Clients resource type
body: getResourceName only resolves USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE to a username (or 'All users') and falls through to resource.getDisplayName() for everything else. After adding CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, client permission resources (whose name is the client UUID and which never get a displayName in getOrCreateResource/init) return null/meaningless names, and a deleted client does not raise a clear error like the user path does. It needs a CLIENTS branch resolving clientId similarly.

title: Per-client resource lookup uses wrong owner so it never matches
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel,String) the code does resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()). Resources are created in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource with owner resourceServer.getClientId() (the clientId string), not server.getId() (the internal UUID). The same wrong 3-arg lookup is used in hasPermission(String) at line 244. The lookup therefore never finds the existing per-client or all-clients resource, causing fallback to all-clients handling or false denies, and granting/denying incorrectly.

title: Global Clients permission ignored when per-client resource exists
body: hasPermission(ClientModel,String) only evaluates the all-clients resource when resourceStore.findByName for the specific client returns null. If a per-client resource exists (e.g. created for a VIEW grant), a caller with a global MANAGE/CONFIGURE/VIEW/MAP_ROLES grant on the Clients type resource is then evaluated only against the per-client resource and denied, even though the global permission should grant access. Global checks must be evaluated in addition to the object check, not only as a null-fallback.

title: Null dereference when Clients type resource does not exist
body: When the per-client resource is missing the code loads the type resource via getResourceTypeResource and immediately calls authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource). On existing realms migrated before the Clients type existed, or if init has not created it, getResourceTypeResource returns null, so findByResource is called with null and throws NPE, turning a permission check into a 500 error instead of deny/grant.

title: getResourceName does not handle Clients type
body: getResourceName special-cases USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE to return 'All users' or the username, but has no branch for CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE. Client permissions therefore fall through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is null for resources created by getOrCreateResource, so admin UI/API shows blank names for client resources and throws ModelIllegalStateException handling is missing for deleted clients.

title: Delete listener can throw UnsupportedOperationException under V2
body: registerListener is now gated only on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1), but management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled. ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException. If both features are enabled, deleting a client/role/group calls the V2 implementation and throws, breaking deletion. The gate must also exclude V2 or route to V1 handling.

title: V2 cleanup path throws or leaks orphan resources
body: File services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/AdminPermissions.java line 77 gates the RoleRemoved/ClientRemoved/GroupRemoved listener on Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) only, but management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled. If both features are enabled the listener runs and calls MgmtPermissionsV2.clients().setPermissionsEnabled() / roles().setPermissionsEnabled() which in ClientPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException, breaking realm/client/role/group deletion with 500. If only V2 is enabled the listener does nothing, so per-client authz Resources created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource are never removed on client deletion and accumulate as orphans.

title: Per-client check ignores all-clients grant and can NPE
body: File services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java line 207 hasPermission(ClientModel,String) looks up the per-client Resource by client.getId() and if found evaluates only that Resource. It never also evaluates the all-clients Resource (Clients). So once any per-client Resource exists (e.g. a permission created for another admin), an admin with a valid all-clients MANAGE/VIEW/CONFIGURE grant is denied for that client. Conversely, when the per-client Resource is missing it falls back to SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource() without null-checking it before calling findByResource(server,resource) on line 219, causing NullPointerException if the Clients type resource is missing.

title: getClientsWithPermission returns type resource name as client id
body: File services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java line 138 iterates resourceStore.findByType(CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and adds resource.getName() for every granted resource. That iteration includes the aggregate type resource whose name is literally Clients created in AdminPermissionsSchema.init(). The returned Set<String> is documented/consumed as client ids/uuids, so callers receive a spurious Clients entry, causing incorrect list filtering or lookup of a non-existent client when only or also the all-clients permission is granted.

title: getResourceName has no Clients branch
body: File server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java line 304 getResourceName() special-cases USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE (returns All users or resolves userId to username via users().getUserById) but has no branch for CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE added in this PR. Per-client Resources are stored with name equal to client UUID and all-clients Resource with name Clients, so for Clients it falls through to resource.getDisplayName() which was never set by getOrCreateResource/init, returning null/empty instead of All clients or the clientId/client name and breaking permission/resource display and any code relying on that name.

title: Default strategy test skips enabling rolling-updates feature
body: In operator/src/test/java/org/keycloak/operator/testsuite/integration/UpgradeTest.java createInitialDeployment() returns early when updateStrategy == null without adding Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES to FeatureSpec. The docs added in this PR state the Operator will fail while in preview unless rolling-updates is enabled, and the non-null path was updated to enable it. Consequence: the null/default parameterized cases of testImageChange and testCacheMaxCount run without the required feature and will fail or test an unsupported configuration, and the default-strategy rolling behavior is left uncovered.

title: New exit-code contract not asserted
body: In quarkus/tests/integration/src/test/java/org/keycloak/it/cli/dist/UpdateCommandDistTest.java testFeatureNotEnabled only checks the error text for the metadata subcommand and does not assert exit code 4 (CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED), does not cover the check subcommand which has the same gate, and testWrongVersions does not assert exit codes after CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was changed from 4 to 3. Consequence: the breaking exit-code renumbering and the disabled-feature path can regress silently and automation relying on exit codes 3 vs 4 is unverified.

title: Default strategy test skips enabling rolling-updates feature
body: In operator/src/test/java/org/keycloak/operator/testsuite/integration/UpgradeTest.java createInitialDeployment() returns early when updateStrategy is null without setting FeatureSpec enabledFeatures to rolling-updates, while the non-null path does enable it. The docs in this PR state the operator will fail unless rolling-updates is enabled. Consequence: the null/default-strategy parameterized cases run in a different feature configuration than the Recreate cases, so they either will fail once the gate is enforced or currently do not test the documented required configuration.

title: Feature-disabled gate only tested for metadata, exit code never asserted
body: In quarkus/tests/integration/src/test/java/org/keycloak/it/cli/dist/UpdateCommandDistTest.java testFeatureNotEnabled only exercises update-compatibility metadata without --features, and only asserts the error text. The identical gate added in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java is never exercised for the disabled case, and neither test asserts the documented exit code 4 (FEATURE_DISABLED) nor exit code 3 for incompatible versions. Consequence: a regression in the check-command gate or wrong exit code would go unnoticed, breaking the scriptable/GitOps contract documented in update-compatibility.adoc.

title: Update strategy table documents no Rolling value
body: In docs/guides/operator/advanced-configuration.adoc the section lists Supported Updates Types as Rolling Updates and Recreate Updates, but the Possible field values table only has <not set> and Recreate rows with no value to select rolling updates. Consequence: a reader cannot tell how to enable the rolling strategy from the docs, contradicting the preceding description.

title: Null strategy path skips rolling-updates feature enablement
body: In operator/src/test/java/org/keycloak/operator/testsuite/integration/UpgradeTest.java createInitialDeployment() returns early when updateStrategy == null without setting FeatureSpec enabledFeatures to rolling-updates. The docs in this same PR state the Operator will fail while in preview unless rolling-updates is enabled. As a result the parameterized runs with null strategy deploy a CR without the required feature and will fail or test different behavior than the RECREATE runs, making the test setup inconsistent and invalid.

title: Recreate exit code changed from 4 to 3 breaks existing automation
body: In quarkus/runtime/src/main/java/org/keycloak/quarkus/runtime/compatibility/CompatibilityResult.java RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is changed from 4 to 3 and new FEATURE_DISABLED=4 reuses the old value. Any script, CI/CD pipeline, or Operator logic built against the previous release that treats exit 4 as recreate-required will now misinterpret recreate as feature-disabled and vice versa. The docs are updated but there is no compatibility handling, so existing automation silently takes the wrong upgrade path.

title: Feature gate and new exit codes not asserted
body: In quarkus/tests/integration/src/test/java/org/keycloak/it/cli/dist/UpdateCommandDistTest.java testFeatureNotEnabled only covers the metadata subcommand and only checks the error message, and testWrongVersions never asserts exit codes. After this PR introduces exit 4 for feature-disabled and changes recreate from 4 to 3, there is no test verifying those exit codes or that check also enforces the gate. Regressions in exit-code contract documented in update-compatibility.adoc would go undetected.

title: Rolling strategy documented as supported but has no field value
body: In docs/guides/operator/advanced-configuration.adoc the Supported Updates Types section lists Rolling Updates and Recreate Updates, but the Possible field values table only documents <not set> and Recreate with no value for selecting Rolling. A reader following the docs cannot configure a rolling update and cannot tell what spec.update.strategy value enables it, making the documented feature unusable.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses authz resource ID instead of group ID
body: GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() iterates resources of type Groups and calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(),...) then does granted.add(groupResource.getId()). In V2 the authz Resource name is the group ID (see AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup/getOrCreateResource) and the Resource ID is a generated UUID. Passing the UUID to hasPermission() makes findByName(server, groupId) miss and fall back to the all-groups resource, and the returned set contains UUIDs not group IDs. Consumers like UsersResource.getUsersCount() and searchForUser() pass this set as group IDs to filter users, so per-group view-members/manage-members permissions will return empty/wrong user lists and counts, or grant all groups if an all-groups policy exists.

title: Global canManage() granted by view-only group permission
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true if hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE) succeeds. That means holding only the view scope on the all-groups resource grants global manage, which is checked by GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() via requireManage() for creating top-level groups and other manage operations. Per-group canManage(GroupModel) correctly requires only MANAGE, and UserPermissions global canManage requires only manage. View must not imply manage; the check should be for MANAGE only.

title: V2 group permission management throws and breaks group deletion cleanup
body: GroupPermissionsV2 overrides setPermissionsEnabled/isPermissionsEnabled/resource/getPermissions to throw UnsupportedOperationException. MgmtPermissionsV2.groups() now returns this class, so AdminPermissions.registerListener() on GroupModel.GroupRemovedEvent which calls management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group,false) will throw for any realm with ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled, aborting group removal. V2 still creates per-group Resources that need cleanup on deletion, so the method cannot unconditionally throw.

title: Group view-member enumeration mixes resource ID and resource name
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission the code iterates resources of type Groups and calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(),...) and granted.add(groupResource.getId()). Per AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup/getOrCreateResource the resource name is the groupId (group.getId()) and the store ID is an internal UUID. hasPermission() then does resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId), so passing getId() never finds the per-group resource and always falls back to the all-groups resource, and the returned set contains authz resource UUIDs instead of group IDs. Consumers put this set in session attribute UserModel.GROUPS for user search/count filtering, so filtering by group membership is broken (wrong users visible / invisible). Use getName() for lookup and for the result set.

title: Global canManage() granted by view-only group permission
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true for hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE). A caller with only view permission on all-groups therefore passes requireManage(), which gates GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup (create top-level group). Per-group canManage(GroupModel) correctly requires only MANAGE. The global check must require only MANAGE, otherwise a view-only administrator can create groups (privilege escalation).

title: Per-user resource shadows all-users permission
body: UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission() looks up resourceStore.findByName(server, user.getId()); if found it evaluates only that resource, otherwise it evaluates the Users type resource. When both a per-user resource and an all-users permission exist, the all-users grant is ignored. An admin with MANAGE/VIEW on all-users loses access to any user that has a per-user resource created for another admin, breaking the documented fallback to all-users/all-groups. The check must OR the specific resource evaluation with the type-resource evaluation. Same pattern exists in GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission().

title: Possible NPE when all-groups type resource does not exist
body: GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission() does resource = SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...); if (policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()) without null-checking resource. getResourceTypeResource() returns null when the schema is unsupported or init has not created the type resource. Passing null resource to findByResource and later dereferencing resource.getScopes() throws NPE, turning an authorization check into a 500. Same pattern in UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission(). Guard for null and return false.

title: Global canManage() grants manage on VIEW scope
body: File GroupPermissionsV2.java canManage() returns hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE). This means an admin with only the view scope on all-groups passes requireManage(), which guards POST /groups (addTopLevelGroup), addChild and group updates. View permission must not imply manage/create; per-group canManage(GroupModel) correctly checks only MANAGE. Consequence is privilege escalation: read-only group viewers can create and modify groups.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses authz resource id instead of group id
body: File GroupPermissionsV2.java getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() iterates V2 group resources and calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) then granted.add(groupResource.getId()). hasPermission(String) expects a Keycloak group id and does resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId), so passing the internal authorization resource UUID misses and falls back to the all-groups resource for every iteration. The set is also populated with internal resource UUIDs, but callers in UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource put the set into session attribute UserModel.GROUPS and getUsersCount(..., groupIds), which expect Keycloak group ids. Consequence is broken member filtering: counts return 0 and search pre-filtering with wrong ids, inconsistent with per-user canView filtering.

title: Missing null check for all-groups type resource causes NPE
body: File GroupPermissionsV2.java hasPermission() does resource = SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE) when the specific group resource is absent, then unconditionally calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource). getResourceTypeResource() can return null if the type resource was never created (e.g. upgraded realm, disabled schema). Passing null resource causes NullPointerException or store failure, denying all group evaluations. Same pattern exists in UserPermissionsV2.java for USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE. A null check returning false is required.

title: getResourceName does not resolve Groups resources
body: File AdminPermissionsSchema.java getResourceName() special-cases only USERS to return username or All users, otherwise returns resource.getDisplayName(). Group resources created by getOrCreateResource() are named by group id with no displayName set, so group permissions UI/API shows raw UUIDs or null instead of group name/path. The new Groups type needs the same resolution as users via session.groups().getGroupById().

title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
body: Line 101 sets totpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare: which is Italian, not Lithuanian. The previous Lithuanian value was removed to strip HTML, but the replacement is in the wrong language. Shipping this will show Italian to Lithuanian users. It needs a proper Lithuanian translation without HTML.

title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
body: Line 71 sets loginTotpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare: which is Italian in a Lithuanian (lt) bundle. Same copy-paste error as the account bundle. Lithuanian users will see Italian. Provide a Lithuanian string without anchor tags.

title: Simplified-Chinese bundle uses Traditional characters
body: Line 112 is totpStep1=在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一： which uses Traditional forms (手機, 應用程式) in a zh_CN Simplified-Chinese file. Simplified should use 手机/应用. This looks copied from zh_TW. Fix to Simplified characters.

title: Missing English file throws RuntimeException instead of MojoExecutionException
body: verifySafeHtml() loads the English counterpart and on IOException throws new RuntimeException. verify() only converts IOException to MojoExecutionException, so this escapes as an unchecked crash with stack trace instead of a proper plugin error. It also fires when verifying an English file whose derived path is missing or any translation without an _en counterpart. Wrap and throw MojoExecutionException.

title: Anchor mismatch message omits key and file
body: When an anchor tag does not match the source, the code adds "Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string" without the bundle key or file path, unlike the Illegal HTML message on line 111 which includes both. A maintainer seeing this failure cannot tell which key or locale failed. Include key and file in the message.

title: Anchor check does not detect dropped anchors and has no passing test
body: santizeAnchors() only iterates over anchors found in the translated value and compares them in order to English anchors. If a translation drops a required ... link entirely the loop never fires and no error is reported. There is also no test asserting that a valid translation produces zero messages, so over- or under-strict behavior is not caught. Add a check for missing expected anchors and positive test cases.

title: Diff snippet can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException
body: In verifySafeHtml the code computes a common prefix `start` and common suffix `end` independently and then does value.substring(start, value.length()-end). When sanitized is longer than value and they share prefix and suffix, start+end can exceed the string length, e.g. value="aaa" sanitized="aaaa" gives start=3 end=3 and substring(3,0). That throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException and aborts the whole verification instead of reporting illegal HTML. The end calculation must be bounded by length-start.

title: Missing English bundle throws RuntimeException instead of MojoExecutionException
body: verifySafeHtml opens the English source file with FileInputStream and on IOException throws new RuntimeException.
