A missing or unreadable English file therefore crashes the mojo with an unchecked exception and stack trace instead of a proper MojoExecutionException message. This is reachable for any new locale or mis-derived englishFile path and hides which file failed.

title: Dropped anchor tags in translation are silently accepted
body: santizeAnchors only iterates over anchors found in the translated value and compares them to the English anchors in order. If the translation deletes a required ... link, matcher.find() is false on entry, the loop never executes, no message is added, and verification passes. The result is a translation that loses a functional link/email action with no verifier warning, while added/changed anchors are flagged.

title: English file derivation uses over-matching replaceAll
body: String englishFile is built with replaceAll("resources-community","resources") and replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties","_en.properties"). replaceAll replaces every occurrence, not just the suffix, and the class [a-zA-Z-_] contains the range Z-_ which also matches [, \, ], ^. A path containing underscores elsewhere or those characters can be rewritten to the wrong file, causing false positives, false negatives, or the RuntimeException above when the derived file does not exist.

title: Lithuanian bundle contains Italian text
body: totpStep1 was changed to "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:" which is Italian, not Lithuanian. Lithuanian users will see Italian text in the account console. The same Italian string was also put in the login Lithuanian bundle, indicating a copy-paste error in this bulk fix.

title: Lithuanian login bundle contains Italian text
body: loginTotpStep1 was changed to "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:" which is Italian, not Lithuanian. Lithuanian login pages will render Italian text. This appears to be a wrong-language substitution made to satisfy the new HTML verifier.

title: Lithuanian message replaced with Italian text
body: Line 101 in messages_lt.properties is now 'totpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' which is Italian, not Lithuanian. The previous Lithuanian value was removed to strip HTML links, but the replacement was copied from the Italian bundle. Consequence: Lithuanian account UI will show Italian text to users.

title: Lithuanian login message replaced with Italian text
body: Line 71 in messages_lt.properties for login is now 'loginTotpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' which is Italian, not Lithuanian. Same copy-paste error as the account bundle. Consequence: Lithuanian login UI shows Italian text.

title: Simplified Chinese file contains Traditional Chinese
body: Line 112 in messages_zh_CN.properties is 'totpStep1=In your mobile phone install one of the following apps' written with Traditional characters (手機, 應用程式) instead of Simplified (手机, 应用). The zh_CN bundle should use Simplified Chinese. Consequence: inconsistent locale, Simplified-Chinese users see Traditional wording.

title: Anchor regex matches non-anchor tags starting with a
body: In VerifyMessageProperties.java the pattern is '</?a[^>]*>'. Since 'a' is not followed by a word boundary, it matches '<address>', '<abbr>', '<article>', etc. as if they were anchors. Consequence: santizeAnchors() can strip or mis-report innocent tags, producing misleading 'Didn't find anchor tag' errors and hiding the real illegal-HTML violation.

title: Dropped anchors are never reported
body: In VerifyMessageProperties.java santizeAnchors() only loops over anchors found in the translation and checks they exist in English. It never checks the reverse: if English has an anchor and the translation omits it, the loop simply ends with no error. Consequence: a translation that drops a required link (breaking login/email flows) passes verification.

title: Anchor error message lacks key and file
body: In VerifyMessageProperties.java the anchor-mismatch branch adds "Didn't find anchor tag " + matcher.group() + " in original string" with no key name and no file name, unlike the Illegal HTML message which includes both. Consequence: when the verifier runs over hundreds of bundles, maintainers cannot locate which key/file failed without reproducing manually.

title: Missing English reference aborts with RuntimeException
body: In VerifyMessageProperties.java verifySafeHtml() catches IOException for the English reference file and throws new RuntimeException("unable to read file " + englishFile). verify() only declares MojoExecutionException for normal failures. Consequence: a missing or mis-mapped _en.properties file crashes the build with a stack trace instead of a collected verifier message, and aborts checking of all remaining files.

title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing custom grants
body: File adds abstract String getShortcut() to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory with no default. Any existing third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementation compiled against the old interface will fail at runtime with AbstractMethodError / NoSuchMethodError when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory calls gtf.getShortcut(), and will fail to compile on upgrade. A new SPI method must have a default implementation (e.g. default return "na") to remain backward compatible.

title: Removed public copy constructor Context(Context)
body: The diff deletes the public Context(Context context) copy constructor. External grant implementations or extensions that copied the context will no longer compile, and even if recompiled the grantType field would not be copied. The constructor should be retained (deprecated if desired) and updated to copy the new grantType field.

title: NPE when formParams is null or missing grant_type
body: In OAuth2GrantType.Context constructor, code does formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE) with no null check on formParams. Callers that construct a Context with null formParams will get NullPointerException during token request handling. Must null-check formParams before reading grant_type.

title: Copy-paste null check validates grantType twice, never rawTokenId
body: Constructor does Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null grantType not allowed"); followed by Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");. The second check should validate rawTokenId, so a null rawTokenId is never rejected and later causes NullPointerException in encodeTokenId when concatenating ':' + rawTokenId, with a confusing failure.

title: Token issuance fails hard on unknown grant type
body: encodeTokenId() throws IllegalStateException when factory.getShortcutByGrantType() returns null for an unrecognized grantType. TokenManager.initToken() calls this unconditionally for every access token with no try/catch or fallback to raw UUID. Any custom grant, ad-hoc ClientSessionContext, or future grant not in the maps turns a token request into a 500 error. Encoding must fall back to the UNKNOWN "na" shortcut instead of throwing.

title: Decoder throws on malformed/legacy token IDs
body: getTokenContextFromTokenId() throws IllegalArgumentException when the prefix before ':' is not exactly 6 chars or contains unknown shortcuts. Old UUID-only tokens are handled only when there is no colon; any legacy or foreign ID that happens to contain a colon, or a truncated/corrupt ID, will throw and, once callers use this for introspection/userinfo/session lookup, will cause request failures instead of gracefully returning UNKNOWN context. Should return UNKNOWN context for unparseable IDs.

title: Unchecked cast breaks startup with custom grant factories
body: postInit() and getGrantTypeByShortcut() blindly cast every OAuth2GrantType provider factory to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory. If a deployment provides a custom OAuth2GrantType factory that does not implement the new sub-interface (possible before this API change), server startup throws ClassCastException and the whole server fails to boot. Must use instanceof filtering or defensive handling.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher inverted and uses wrong offsets
body: Matcher does if (items[0].substring(3,5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false; which returns false exactly when the grant matches (inverted logic, should be !equals). It also extracts substring(3,5) while the 6-char prefix is session(0-1)+token(2-3)+grant(4-5), so grant is at substring(4,6). The helper will reject correct token IDs and accept wrong ones, and can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException on short prefixes without a length check.

title: Copy-paste null-check validates grantType twice, never validates rawTokenId
body: In AccessTokenContext constructor line 73 is Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed"); It checks grantType a second time instead of rawTokenId. As a result a null rawTokenId is accepted and stored, causing an NPE later in encodeTokenId when concatenating ':' + rawTokenId, and a null grantType failure reports the wrong message. Fix to requireNonNull(rawTokenId).

title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks all existing custom grant factories
body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory adds String getShortcut() with no default implementation. Any third-party provider that implements OAuth2GrantTypeFactory will fail to compile and existing deployed jars will fail at runtime with AbstractMethodError when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory calls getShortcut(). This is an incompatible SPI change. It should be a default method returning e.g. UNKNOWN/"na" or a derived value.

title: Context constructor dereferences formParams without null check
body: In OAuth2GrantType.Context constructor the new line this.grantType = formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE) assumes formParams is non-null. If any caller constructs a Context with null formParams, token requests fail with NPE before grant processing. Add a null guard and fall back to null/UNKNOWN grant type.

title: Removed Context(Context) copy constructor breaks API compatibility
body: The diff deletes the public copy constructor Context(Context context) without deprecation or replacement. External grant implementations or extensions that copied the context will no longer compile or link (NoSuchMethodError). The constructor should be retained and updated to also copy the new grantType field.

title: Unchecked cast to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory causes startup ClassCastException
body: In postInit and getGrantTypeByShortcut the code casts every OAuth2GrantType provider factory to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory without instanceof check. A custom grant factory written against the old interface (only ProviderFactory<OAuth2GrantType>) will cause a ClassCastException during server startup, preventing boot. Guard with instanceof or lookup only factories implementing the new interface.

title: initToken assumes TokenContextEncoderProvider always exists
body: initToken does TokenContextEncoderProvider encoder = session.getProvider(TokenContextEncoderProvider.class) then immediately dereferences it. If the SPI is disabled, overridden, or unavailable in tests/embedded mode, getProvider returns null and every access-token creation throws NPE. Add a null fallback to the old behavior token.id(KeycloakModelUtils.generateId()).

title: Lightweight determination uses session context client instead of token client
body: getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext calls AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session), which reads session.getContext().getClient(). That is the request context client, not necessarily the client the token is being issued for (passed as realm/client to TokenManager.initToken). In flows like token-exchange where context client and target client can differ, the encoded TokenType (regular vs lightweight) will be wrong. The client should be passed explicitly.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher logic inverted and uses wrong offsets
body: In isAccessTokenId the check if (items[0].substring(3,5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false; is backwards — it rejects matching tokens and accepts non-matching ones. It also uses substring(3,5) while the 6-char prefix layout is 0-1 session, 2-3 tokenType, 4-5 grant, so the grant shortcut is substring(4,6). The helper will pass wrong grant types and fail correct ones, hiding regressions in token-ID encoding.

title: Copy-paste null-check validates grantType twice, never validates rawTokenId
body: In services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java line 73 the constructor does Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") instead of checking rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted and later used in encodeTokenId as ':' + null, producing a corrupt token id ("...:null") or NPEs downstream, while the duplicate grantType check adds no value.

title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks all existing custom grant factories
body: In server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java the new method String getShortcut() is abstract with no default. Any third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory compiled against the old interface will fail at runtime with AbstractMethodError/NoSuchMethodError when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory casts to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory and calls getShortcut(), breaking server startup/token issuance. It should be a default method returning "na"/null.

title: Context constructor dereferences formParams without null check
body: In server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java line 102 the constructor does this.grantType = formParams.getFirst(...). If formParams is null the token endpoint fails with NullPointerException. The old constructor never touched formParams, so this is a new crash path for any caller constructing a Context with null/delayed form params.

title: Removal of Context(Context) copy constructor breaks API compatibility
body: In server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java the public copy constructor Context(Context context) was deleted. External grant implementations or extensions that copied the context will no longer compile/link. Removal is unnecessary for adding the grantType field and should be restored or deprecated.

title: No null handling for missing user/client session causes token issuance NPE
body: In services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java line 47 getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext unconditionally does clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getUserSession() and then userSession.getPersistenceState()/isOffline(). For service-account, token-exchange transient, or any flow with no user session this throws NullPointerException inside TokenManager.initToken, turning all access-token creation into a 500 error. It should map missing session to UNKNOWN.

title: Unknown grant type makes access-token creation throw instead of falling back
body: In services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java lines 109-111 encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException when factory.getShortcutByGrantType returns null. TokenManager.initToken calls this unconditionally for every access token, so any token with a grant id that is not a registered OAuth2GrantType (custom grants, implicit/hybrid, admin API, SAML exchanges) fails issuance with 500. Missing grant already falls back to "na"; unknown grants should do the same.

title: Malformed token IDs throw instead of returning UNKNOWN context
body: In services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java lines 74-93 getTokenContextFromTokenId throws IllegalArgumentException when the prefix before ':' is not exactly 6 chars or shortcuts are unknown. Token IDs are untrusted input presented on introspection/userinfo/resource endpoints; throwing forces every future caller to catch or it becomes a 500 instead of invalid_token handling. No-colon legacy IDs correctly return UNKNOWN, malformed colon IDs should do the same.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher inverted and checks wrong substring
body: In testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java line 483 isAccessTokenId does if (items[0].substring(3,5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false; This is backwards (returns false on match) and slices the wrong characters: for a 6-char prefix like "onrtac" the grant occupies substring(4,6), not (3,5). The result is correct tokens fail the assertion and wrong-grant tokens can pass, plus short prefixes throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of returning false.

title: Federated recovery codes stored as raw plaintext
body: In CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential the raw codes from the form (generatedCodes) are serialized to JSON and sent to user storage via UserCredentialModel, while the local-DB path stores RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel which contains hashed codes. External storage therefore receives and persists usable plaintext recovery codes, whereas local storage persists hashes. Anyone with read access to the federated store can impersonate the user.

title: Federated recovery-code validation allows infinite reuse
body: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE only checks generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse())) and never marks the used code as consumed. The local RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider burns a code on successful isValid and tracks allCodesUsed. The federated path therefore leaves all codes valid forever, so one leaked code can be replayed indefinitely and exhaustion is never detected.

title: getCredentials loses ID and NPEs on unknown user
body: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials, myUser is dereferenced without a null check, so lookup of a user not in the map throws NullPointerException. When present, the method rebuilds the credential via RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...) from credentialData/createdDate only, discarding the stored CredentialModel id set in updateCredential. Every call returns a different random id, so callers that use the id for removal or display (e.g. removeStoredCredentialById) can never match the persisted credential.

title: Exhausted federated recovery credential never removed
body: After successful validation the code loads the credential via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential which prefers federated credentials, then unconditionally calls credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById when allCodesUsed(). removeStoredCredentialById only deletes local Keycloak-DB credentials. A federated credential is therefore never cleaned up, and the test provider's disableCredentialType does not even support the recovery type, leaving an exhausted credential in external storage.

title: Unchecked Optional.get causes 500 when credential missing
body: RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean calls RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) then immediately credentialModelOpt.get() without checking isPresent, followed by getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get(). If the credential was just consumed, removed, or the user only has the other storage type in a race, this throws NoSuchElementException and produces a 500 during login-form rendering instead of a handled error or re-setup.

title: Exhausted federated recovery codes never removed
body: After a successful recovery-code login the code fetches the credential via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential() which can now return a federated user-storage credential, but cleanup still calls removeStoredCredentialById(). That API only removes a locally stored (Keycloak DB) credential and does not call UserStorageProvider/CredentialInputUpdater.disableCredentialType. Consequence: when recovery codes live in user storage an exhausted set is never deleted, isConfiguredFor stays true, and the user is not correctly forced through re-configuration.

title: Federated storage cannot disable/remove recovery codes
body: disableCredentialType() only handles OTP types and logs recovery-codes as unsupported, and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream() never advertises RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE. Consequence: even if production code tried the correct federated removal path (disableCredentialType), this provider would leak the credential, and account/admin removal flows cannot work for user-storage recovery codes. The test double therefore hides the production cleanup bug.

title: Federated recovery-code validation does not consume codes
body: isValid() for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE just does anyMatch on the stored raw list and returns true without marking the used code as consumed/removed. The real RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider marks a code used on validation so allCodesUsed() can become true. Consequence: federated codes are infinitely reusable in the test double, allCodesUsed() never becomes true, and the exhaustion / re-configure path added in RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator is never exercised.

title: Unchecked Optional.get() on missing recovery credential
body: Constructor does RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user).get() with no isPresent check before createFromCredentialModel and getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get(). If the user has no federated or local recovery credential the bean throws NoSuchElementException, producing a 500 during login-form rendering instead of a handled error. Someone reading only this finding understands: always check the Optional and fail gracefully.

title: Exhausted federated recovery codes removed with wrong API
body: In RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.isRecoveryAuthnCodeInputValid the code loads the credential with RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential() which can return a federated (user-storage) credential, then calls authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(id) when allCodesUsed(). removeStoredCredentialById() only removes local Keycloak-DB credentials, not federated credentials which require disableCredentialType/remove federated handling. Consequence: when recovery codes live in user storage and are exhausted they are never deleted/disabled, isConfiguredFor stays true and used codes may remain accepted, plus the required-action re-add logic operates on stale state.

title: Federated recovery credential drops label and timestamp
body: CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential() builds UserCredentialModel("", credentialModel.getType(), recoveryCodesJson) where recoveryCodesJson is only the JSON array of raw codes. The userLabel and generatedAt contained in the passed RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel are never transferred to the user-storage provider. Consequence: a recovery credential stored in user storage permanently loses its label/metadata, unlike the local-DB path which persists them via credentialModel, and any UI/account display or audit depending on them shows null/wrong values.

title: getCredentials discards stored recovery credential ID
body: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials() reconstructs the recovery credential with RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...) but never copies the ID assigned in updateCredential() (via KeycloakModelUtils.generateId()). It returns a model with a fresh/transient ID. Consequence: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential() returns an ID that does not match the stored federated credential, so removeStoredCredentialById(), account-console delete, and any lookup by ID operate on a non-existent ID and silently fail, leaving the real credential orphaned.

title: Federated recovery codes cannot be disabled/removed
body: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.disableCredentialType() only handles OTP types and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream() only advertises OTP, while supportsCredentialType/isConfiguredFor/updateCredential/isValid all handle RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE. Consequence: admin disableCredentialType, account-console credential delete, and exhausted-code cleanup can never remove a federated recovery credential, so tests asserting no DB credentials pass while the federated credential is effectively undeletable.

title: Federated recovery code validation does not consume codes
body: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid() for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE only checks generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse())) and never removes/marks the used code. The local Keycloak recovery-code provider consumes a code on successful validation so it is single-use. Consequence: federated recovery codes can be replayed indefinitely, and the new testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin test logging in once cannot detect reuse or allCodesUsed cleanup failures.

title: Sibling getSubGroupsStream methods still NPE on concurrent delete
body: The PR fixes NPE in getSubGroupsCount() by null-checking modelSupplier.get(), but the three overloads getSubGroupsStream(search,first,max), getSubGroupsStream(first,max) and getSubGroupsStream(search,exact,first,max) still do modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) with no null check. If the group is deleted concurrently before the lazy supplier is first loaded, get() returns null and these methods throw NullPointerException, causing the same 500 failure the PR claims to fix. They need the same null handling as getSubGroupsCount().

title: Concurrent test never joins reader thread, assertion is racy
body: The test starts a background thread that loops while(!deletedAll.get()) calling the admin API, then deletes groups, sets deletedAll to true, and immediately asserts caughtExceptions is empty without joining the thread. The assert can run while the reader is still in-flight, so a failure occurring after the assert is missed (false pass) and the thread can leak into the next test. If the delete loop throws, deletedAll is never set and the thread spins forever. The tight loop with no pause/backoff also floods the server with Integer.MAX_VALUE queries.

title: Concurrent delete still NPEs in getSubGroupsStream overloads
body: File GroupAdapter.java line 256 (and lines 262, 268) dereferences modelSupplier.get() without a null check, while the fix on getSubGroupsCount in the same file acknowledges getGroupById can return null when the group was concurrently deleted. If the group is deleted between cache lookup and DB lookup, modelSupplier.get() returns null and these three getSubGroupsStream variants throw NullPointerException, leaving the same 500-error race the PR claims to fix.

title: Reader thread never joined before assertion
body: File GroupTest.java line 139 starts a background reader thread and line 157 asserts on caughtExceptions immediately after deletedAll.set(true) without joining the thread. A request already in flight can fail after the assertion, so failures are missed and the test can falsely pass, and the thread can outlive the test and interfere with later tests. If the delete loop throws, deletedAll is never set and the tight polling loop spins forever.

title: Concurrent-delete NPE remains in getSubGroupsStream overloads
body: GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount was fixed to null-check modelSupplier.get(), but the three getSubGroupsStream overloads at lines 253-269 still do return modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) without a null check. If the group is deleted concurrently, modelSupplier.get() returns null and these methods still throw NullPointerException, so the concurrent-access fix is incomplete and listing/searching subgroups can still fail with 500.

title: Reader thread never joined and can spin forever
body: The test starts a raw new Thread that busy-loops while(!deletedAll.get()) issuing groups(null,0,Integer.MAX_VALUE,true) with no sleep, no stored reference, no join/timeout. deletedAll.set(true) is after the delete loop with no try-finally, so if any remove() throws the flag is never set and the thread loops forever hammering the server. Even on success the assertion runs without waiting for the reader thread to finish, so it is racy and the thread can leak into subsequent tests and grow caughtExceptions unboundedly.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator breaks datetime ordering
body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does math.floor/ceil directly on getattr(item, self.key) and value_from_cursor returns cursor.value as int. The only caller in src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py uses order_by="-datetime", so the key is a datetime object. math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError and filtering a datetime column against int 0 in build_queryset is a type mismatch. Consequence: any request with optimized_pagination=true crashes with 500 or paginates incorrectly instead of behaving like DateTimePaginator.

title: Negative queryset slice crashes instead of paginating
body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result allows start_offset=cursor.offset when enable_advanced_features and offset<0, then does queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django QuerySets explicitly reject negative indexing with AssertionError/ValueError, they do not wrap like Python lists. The comment claiming Django handles negative slicing automatically is false. Consequence: an attacker-controlled cursor string like value:-10:0 reaches an unhandled exception and returns 500, a remotely triggerable availability issue.

title: Unknown paginate kwarg enable_advanced_features
body: In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py the optimized branch calls self.paginate(..., paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator, enable_advanced_features=True). Base endpoint paginate does not define that parameter and does not forward arbitrary kwargs to the paginator constructor in the established codebase. Consequence: the optimized path either raises TypeError for unexpected keyword argument returning 500, or silently drops the flag so the paginator never actually enables the intended mode, making the branch dead/broken.

title: Global BasePaginator offset clamp is inconsistent and wrong
body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py BasePaginator.get_result was changed for all APIs from queryset[offset:offset+limit+extra] to start_offset=max(0,offset) for forward cursors but keeps raw offset for is_prev cursors and for the later check len(results)==offset+limit+extra. Other paginators in the same file (OffsetPaginator, ChainPaginator, CombinedQuerysetPaginator) reject offset<0 with BadPaginationError (400). Consequence: this global change silently coerces invalid forward cursors to page 0 instead of 400, still crashes for is_prev negative offsets, and miscomputes has_more when clamping because the length check uses the unclamped offset.

title: New paginator and endpoint branch have no tests
body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py a new OptimizedCursorPaginator class and a modified BasePaginator path plus a new optimized_pagination branch in OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint were added with no unit or API tests. Consequence: the datetime-key crash, negative-slice crash, and paginate-kwarg mismatch above are uncaught, and future changes to global pagination have no regression coverage.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator breaks datetime ordering
body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does math.floor/ceil directly on getattr(item, self.key). The audit-log endpoint uses it with order_by="-datetime" where the key is a datetime object, so math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError. DateTimePaginator exists precisely to convert datetimes via strftime/timestamp. Any request to OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint with optimized_pagination=true will crash instead of paginating.

title: Client-controlled negative offset passed to queryset slicing
body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset < 0 it sets start_offset = cursor.offset and does queryset[start_offset:stop]. Cursor offset comes from the user-supplied cursor string and Django QuerySet explicitly forbids negative indexing and raises AssertionError, so a crafted cursor causes an unhandled 500. The comment claiming Django properly handles negative slicing automatically and that it is safe because permissions are checked at queryset level is false; it enables denial of service and establishes an unsafe pagination primitive.

title: BasePaginator now allows negative slice on prev path
body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py BasePaginator.get_result was changed to start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset. Offset is attacker-controlled via Cursor.from_string. For is_prev cursors a negative offset is now passed directly to queryset[start_offset:stop], which Django rejects with AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported, turning a bad cursor into a 500. For forward cursors the same bad input is silently clamped to 0 and returns the first page, so behavior is inconsistent and boundary validation is lost.

title: Unknown paginate kwarg breaks optimized path
body: In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py the optimized branch calls self.paginate(..., paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator, ..., enable_advanced_features=True). Base endpoint paginate does not define an enable_advanced_features parameter; it constructs the paginator itself. Passing a paginator-specific constructor argument through paginate will raise TypeError for unexpected keyword argument, so every request with optimized_pagination=true fails with 500 instead of returning audit logs.

title: Negative queryset slice causes unhandled exception / DoS
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result in src/sentry/api/paginator.py allows attacker-controlled negative offsets to reach Django ORM slicing: if enable_advanced_features and cursor.offset < 0 then start_offset = cursor.offset and results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop]). Cursor offsets come from the `cursor` query param via Cursor.from_string which does int(bits[1]) with no range check, so `cursor=0:-100:0` yields offset -100. Django QuerySets do not support negative slicing and raise AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported. The code comment claiming the ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically is false. Consequence is an unhandled 500 instead of 400 BadPaginationError as used by OffsetPaginator/ChainPaginator, giving any user who can reach the optimized path a trivial DoS / error-probe vector.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator breaks datetime ordering
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key in src/sentry/api/paginator.py does getattr(item, self.key) followed by math.floor/ceil, which only works for numeric keys. The only caller in src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py passes order_by="-datetime", so self.key is "datetime" and the value is a Python datetime. math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError. Similarly value_from_cursor returns raw cursor.value (int) while build_queryset expects a datetime for this ordering. Consequence is every request to the optimized_pagination path crashes with 500 instead of returning audit logs.

title: Clamped offset not used consistently causes wrong page trimming
body: BasePaginator.get_result in src/sentry/api/paginator.py now computes start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset and slices queryset[start_offset:stop], but the later is_prev trimming check still uses the original offset: elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra. When offset was negative and clamped to 0, or when is_prev allows a negative offset, the length comparison is off by the clamp amount. Consequence is incorrect dropping/keeping of the extra boundary row and incorrect has_results in the cursor, causing duplicate, missing, or oversized pages. The is_prev branch also still passes a potentially negative start to Django which raises AssertionError.

title: Unsafe advanced pagination gated by overly broad check
body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint.get in src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py enables the new negative-offset path when request.GET.get("optimized_pagination")=="true" and (request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access), then passes enable_advanced_features=True. has_global_access is true for many non-owner roles and the raw GET param bypasses AuditLogQueryParamSerializer validation. Consequence is a much wider population than superusers can drive attacker-controlled cursors into the unsafe negative-slice code path described above, expanding DoS/crash exposure on the audit-log endpoint which previously used DateTimePaginator.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator allows negative-offset DB slicing
body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset < 0, the code sets start_offset = cursor.offset (negative) and slices queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django QuerySets do not support negative slicing and raise AssertionError, so a crafted cursor string like "0:-5:0" causes a 500/DoS. The comment claiming Django handles negative slicing automatically is false, and other paginators in the same file explicitly reject offset < 0 with BadPaginationError.

title: Hidden optimized_pagination flag switches to vulnerable paginator
body: The endpoint adds an undocumented ?optimized_pagination=true query param that, for any superuser or member with has_global_access, switches from DateTimePaginator to OptimizedCursorPaginator with enable_advanced_features=True. This exposes the negative-offset path to a broad set of users on a sensitive audit-log endpoint with no tests or validation, widening attack surface unrelated to the spans-buffer title.

title: BasePaginator now passes negative offset for prev cursors
body: BasePaginator.get_result was changed from queryset[offset:stop] to start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset. For is_prev cursors the offset is used unclamped, so a client-supplied cursor with negative offset and is_prev=1 still reaches queryset[negative:stop]. This is inconsistent with OffsetPaginator/ChainPaginator which reject negative offsets, and causes AssertionError or undefined paging.

title: Mandatory end_timestamp_precise lookup crashes consumer on missing field
body: process_batch now does val["end_timestamp_precise"] with direct dict access. Any span event missing that field raises KeyError inside the Arroyo batch, failing the whole batch, blocking commits and causing consumer crash-loop/backlog instead of skipping or defaulting. Previously Span did not require the field.

title: ZUNIONSTORE without AGGREGATE MAX corrupts scores on duplicates
body: The migration from SUNIONSTORE to ZUNIONSTORE uses default SUM aggregation. If the same payload member exists in both source sets (retry, duplicate ingest, overlapping parent/span buffers), its score (end_timestamp_precise) is summed to 2x timestamp, corrupting ordering and future ZPOPMIN eviction victims. Should use AGGREGATE MAX.

title: max_segment_spans enforcement removed, truncation is silent
body: _load_segment_data no longer checks max_segment_spans, drops the segment_span_count_exceeded metric and error log, and leaves max_segment_spans config unused. Oversized segments are now silently truncated to 1000 in Lua via ZPOPMIN (hardcoded, off-by-one vs 1001 default) and flushed as incomplete instead of being skipped/logged, causing silent span loss.

title: Redirect traversal cut from 10000 to 1000 fragments deep traces
body: The redirect-following loop was reduced from 10000 to 1000 iterations. Traces/segment trees deeper than 1000 will stop early with an unresolved set_span_id, so spans that should merge into one segment stay in separate Redis keys and flush as fragmented segments. This is a correctness regression for deep traces to save Lua time.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator allows attacker-controlled negative offsets
body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py:877 OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result explicitly allows negative slicing (start_offset = cursor.offset when offset < 0) when enable_advanced_features is true. Cursor values come from the user-controlled cursor query param via Cursor.from_string, so any caller can supply a negative offset. The comment claims Django ORM properly handles negative slicing, which is false — Django raises ValueError/AssertionError for negative slicing. Consequence is at minimum a 500/DoS on crafted cursors and unexpected queryset slicing semantics exposed to API users.

title: Audit-log endpoint exposes vulnerable advanced paginator via query param
body: In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:82 the endpoint switches to OptimizedCursorPaginator with enable_advanced_features=True when ?optimized_pagination=true and requester has global access. This exposes the negative-offset code path in paginator.py to remote authenticated users. There is no test or need for this path, and permission gating does not mitigate the crash/incorrect-pagination behavior because the cursor offset itself remains attacker-controlled.

title: BasePaginator has inconsistent negative-offset handling
body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 BasePaginator.get_result now does start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset. For is_prev cursors a negative offset is still passed to queryset[start_offset:stop], which Django rejects, while the later length check uses the original offset (len(results) == offset + limit + extra). Consequence is crashes on crafted prev cursors and wrong prev-page trimming logic.

title: SET to ZSET type change breaks existing Redis keys
body: In src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 ingestion changed from SADD to ZADD and from SSCAN to ZSCAN, and src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua changed SCARD/SUNIONSTORE to ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZPOPMIN for keys span-buf:s:*. Existing production keys with 3600s TTL are SET type. ZADD/ZCARD/ZSCAN against a SET raises WRONGTYPE, so after deploy every write/read to a live segment fails until keys expire. Consequence is ingestion errors, lost segments, and consumer stalls with no migration or versioning.

title: ZUNIONSTORE without AGGREGATE sums timestamps
body: In src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:47 and :53 ZUNIONSTORE is called as zunionstore(set_key, 2, set_key, span_key) with default AGGREGATE SUM. Members are span payloads scored by end_timestamp_precise. If the same payload exists in both inputs (retries, overlapping batches, re-joins), the score becomes sum of timestamps instead of the timestamp, corrupting ordering and the ZPOPMIN eviction that is supposed to drop oldest spans. Should be AGGREGATE MAX/MIN. Consequence is wrong eviction and inflated scores that pin duplicates.

title: Hard KeyError on end_timestamp_precise crashes consumer
body: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py:141 process_batch does val["end_timestamp_precise"] with direct indexing. Any malformed, old-schema, or Relay message missing that field raises KeyError inside the Arroyo processing step, failing the whole batch and causing retries/stalls. Previously the field was not required. Consequence is a single bad Kafka message can block progress; should use .get with fallback/validation and dead-letter handling.

title: Hardcoded 1000 cap diverges from max_segment_spans config
body: In src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:62 eviction uses hardcoded if span_count > 1000 then zpopmin, while SpansBuffer defines max_segment_spans=1001 and the old Python-side span-count guard and metric segment_span_count_exceeded were deleted in src/sentry/spans/buffer.py. Consequence is operators cannot tune the cap, the metric/log disappears, and Python/ Lua limits disagree, silently truncating segments without visibility.

title: Redirect-depth limit cut from 10000 to 1000 splits deep traces
body: In src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 the redirect-chain loop was reduced from 10000 to 1000 iterations. Traces/segment trees deeper than 1000 redirects will no longer resolve to a single set_key, so spans that should be joined stay in separate Redis sets and flush as duplicate/split segments. Consequence is data fragmentation and duplicate segments for very deep traces with no benefit shown.

title: Negative offset bypasses pagination validation
body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result allows attacker-controlled Cursor.offset < 0 to be passed directly to Django queryset slicing as queryset[start_offset:stop] when enable_advanced_features is true. Django does not support negative slicing and other paginators explicitly reject offset < 0 with BadPaginationError. The comment that Django handles it automatically is false. Consequence is unhandled AssertionError/500 denial of service and bypass of established pagination bounds checking.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate datetime keys
body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does int(math.floor(value)) on getattr(item, self.key) and value_from_cursor returns cursor.value as int. When used from organization_auditlogs.py with order_by='-datetime' the key value is a datetime object, not a number, so math.floor raises TypeError and the cursor value (int) compared against a datetime column in build_queryset produces wrong SQL or DB error. Consequence is the optimized audit-log path is broken and crashes instead of paginating.

title: Query-param-gated switch to vulnerable paginator
body: In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py a request with ?optimized_pagination=true plus is_superuser or has_global_access switches from DateTimePaginator to OptimizedCursorPaginator with enable_advanced_features=True. This exposes the negative-offset path and numeric-only cursor logic to any user satisfying that weak gate on a sensitive audit-log endpoint. Consequence is expanded attack surface for DoS and incorrect access to audit data beyond normal pagination.

title: Inconsistent negative-offset handling in BasePaginator
body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py BasePaginator.get_result now clamps negative offsets to 0 for forward cursors with max(0, offset) but passes offset unchanged for is_prev cursors to queryset[offset:stop]. A crafted prev cursor with negative offset therefore still reaches Django queryset slicing which rejects negative indexing, causing 500, while forward cursors silently rewrite invalid input to 0 hiding client bugs. Both cases should raise BadPaginationError like other paginators. Consequence is inconsistent errors and silent correction of invalid cursors.

title: ZUNIONSTORE without aggregate corrupts scores on duplicates
body: In src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua merging uses redis.call('zunionstore', set_key, 2, set_key, span_key) with default AGGREGATE SUM. Members are span payloads with score end_timestamp_precise. If the same payload already exists in both sets, for example on retry or duplicate ingest, the score is summed and doubled instead of preserved. Consequence is inflated timestamps, wrong zpopmin eviction order and wrong segment ordering.

title: Oversized-segment guard removed, silent truncation without observability
body: In src/sentry/spans/buffer.py _load_segment_data no longer enforces max_segment_spans and the constructor field max_segment_spans is now dead. The Lua script truncates sets to 1000 with zpopmin without emitting metrics.incr or logging, unlike the previous path that dropped too-large segments with segment_span_count_exceeded and an error log. Consequence is silent data loss where oldest spans including a potential root span can be evicted with no alerting and operators cannot tune via max_segment_spans.

title: Direct required-field access crashes consumer on bad message
body: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py process_batch does val['end_timestamp_precise'] with direct indexing. Any message missing that field raises KeyError inside the Arroyo processing step, stalling or crash-looping the spans consumer on a poison message instead of skipping or defaulting. Consequence is availability risk for the whole partition on malformed input.

title: Unstable hash() cache key with 60s stale allowlist returns wrong counts
body: In src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py the cache key is built with Python hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))). Python hash() is salted per-process, so different workers produce different keys and never share cache, and collisions are possible. Worse, the cached value is only allowlist eligibility cached for 60 seconds. If the allowlist changes, queries for up to 60s use the stale decision and return upsampled sum(sample_weight) instead of count() or vice versa. invalidate_upsampling_cache is defined but never called anywhere, so there is no invalidation. The new endpoint tests reuse the same org and project ids with different mocked allowlists, so the second test will hit the first test's cached True and get wrong results.

title: Upsampling check uses outer dataset and request instead of scoped query
body: In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_events_stats.py _get_event_stats receives scoped_dataset and query as arguments but calls is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request) using the outer closure dataset and the original request. The dashboard-split factory calls the same function with split_dataset=discover and rewritten queries like (query) AND !event.type:transaction. Because the check ignores scoped_dataset and the query argument and instead inspects request.GET, split queries are evaluated against the wrong dataset and wrong query string, so errors routed to discover will not be upsampled and transactions routed elsewhere may be.

title: Error detection only matches event.type:error substring
body: In src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py _is_error_focused_query returns True only if the lowercased request query string contains event.type:error. It misses the queries this endpoint itself generates for the discover split, e.g. (query) AND !event.type:transaction, misses empty or default discover queries that include errors, and misses event.type:default/error variants. It also false-positives on substring matches like message:event.type:error. Consequence is discover error traffic silently uses raw count() instead of upsampled_count() or vice versa, producing inconsistent charts.

title: upsampled_count assumes sample_weight exists and truncates with toInt64
body: In src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py upsampled_count is defined as toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) with no coalesce, ifNotFinite, or null handling. The helper comments admit it assumes sample_weight exists for all events in allowlisted projects. Older events, non-sampled events, or transactions in a mixed discover query will have NULL/missing sample_weight, so sum can be NULL/0 and counts collapse to 0. toInt64 also truncates fractional weights like 1/0.3=3.33, systematically undercounting. The result is wrong chart values instead of falling back to count().

title: Transform only handles bare count() and discards original alias
body: In src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling only rewrites columns where lowered stripped value equals count(), always emitting upsampled_count() as count. It drops any original alias like COUNT() as my_count, does not handle yAxis forms with aliases, equations, or count_if/count_unique, and leaves other count-like aggregates unconverted. Consequence is broken aliases for top-events/orderby that expect the original name and dashboards mixing upsampled and raw counts in the same response.

title: Test helper silently overwrites sample_rate with unvalidated value
body: In src/sentry/testutils/factories.py _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling wraps all access in bare try/except pass, checks if client_sample_rate truthy, then does float(client_sample_rate) with another swallowed exception and unconditionally assigns normalized_data[sample_rate]. It does not validate 0 < rate <= 1, so 0, negative, >1, or string values either silently pass or silently fail, and it overwrites any legitimate existing sample_rate. This creates invalid test fixtures that do not represent production validation and can mask missing server-side checks.

title: Cache invalidation helper is dead code
body: In src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py invalidate_upsampling_cache deletes the eligibility key, but nothing in the pull request calls it when issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist changes. Combined with the 60 second TTL, allowlist removals keep returning upsampled counts and additions keep returning raw counts until expiry. The function gives a false impression of consistency while the stale-read window remains.

title: Cache key uses Python hash() which is randomized per process
body: Line 27 builds cache_key with hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids))). Python's hash() for tuples is salted per process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so the same project set maps to different keys in different workers, defeating the cache, and can be negative/collide. Use a deterministic hash (e.g. hashlib) or joined IDs. Consequence is cache misses across hosts and potential cross-key collisions causing wrong eligibility.

title: 60s cached allowlist eligibility returns stale counts
body: is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects caches _are_all_projects_error_upsampled for 60 seconds keyed only by org+projects. If the allowlist changes, queries within the window apply (or skip) sum(sample_weight) incorrectly, over- or under-counting by 1/sample_rate (e.g. 10x). invalidate_upsampling_cache is defined but never called in the diff, so there is no invalidation path. Eligibility must not be cached across requests or must be versioned with the option.

title: Upsampling check uses outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset
body: Inside _get_event_stats the code calls is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request) with the outer closure dataset, not the scoped_dataset argument. The dashboard-split factory below calls _get_event_stats with discover vs scoped_dataset for the same request, so the eligibility decision is made for the wrong dataset. Consequence is upsampling applied (or skipped) for the wrong store, producing wrong timeseries values.

title: Error-query detection misses !event.type:transaction errors-only queries
body: _is_error_focused_query only returns True when the raw query string contains event.type:error. The caller in organization_events_stats.py builds errors-only split queries as (query) AND !event.type:transaction, which contain no event.type:error and therefore return False. Those errors-only queries will skip the upsampled_count transform and under-count by the sample factor, while empty-query discover requests are also mishandled. String matching cannot replace proper query AST parsing.

title: upsampled_count sum(sample_weight) mishandles NULLs and truncates
body: The new SnQLFunction does toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) with no null handling. Backfilled, unsampled, or mixed events have NULL/missing sample_weight, so sum can be NULL or under-count, and toInt64 truncates fractional weights (e.g. 1/0.3) instead of rounding. The comment assumes sample_weight always exists for allowlisted projects, which is false during rollout. Consequence is NULL buckets or systematically low error counts.

title: Test factory unconditionally overwrites sample_rate without validation
body: _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling does if client_sample_rate: normalized_data[sample_rate] = float(client_sample_rate) with bare except: pass. It clobbers any real sample_rate already set on the event, accepts out-of-range/NaN/Inf values (only float() conversion checked), and treats 0 as absent. Consequence is test (and any reused helper) events get a corrupt sample_rate that changes sample_weight calculation and hides production null-handling bugs.

title: Non-deterministic hash() used for shared cache key
body: cache_key uses hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))). Python's hash() is randomized per process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so different API workers generate different keys for the same projects in a shared Redis/memcached cache. Caching becomes ineffective and invalidate_upsampling_cache() cannot delete keys created by another worker, leaving stale entries.

title: 60s eligibility cache returns stale allowlist decisions
body: is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects caches _are_all_projects_error_upsampled for 60s and invalidate_upsampling_cache is never called on allowlist change. A project added/removed from issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist will get wrong counts (upsampled 10x vs true count) for up to 60s. Tests in test_organization_events_stats.py mock different allowlists with same org/project_ids without clearing cache, so they pollute each other.

title: Upsampling check uses outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset
body: _get_event_stats receives scoped_dataset which can differ from the outer dataset when dashboard-split logic retries with discover vs scoped_dataset, but eligibility is checked with the outer dataset variable. A discover split query for errors evaluated against a metrics/transactions dataset will never upsample, and vice versa.

title: Error-focus check reads request.GET instead of executed query
body: _is_error_focused_query inspects request.GET.get('query') while _get_event_stats executes a potentially rewritten query argument (e.g. errors_only_query='(query) AND !event.type:transaction' or transactions_only_query). Split queries therefore get the wrong upsampling decision. Empty discover queries also default to False even when the executed query is error-only.

title: upsampled_count defined only for discover but applied to errors dataset
body: _should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns True for dataset == errors unconditionally, then organization_events_stats rewrites count() to upsampled_count(). upsampled_count is only registered in discover.py function_converter, so errors-dataset timeseries/top-events queries will fail to resolve the function or hit a missing sample_weight column in Snuba.

title: sum(sample_weight) without null handling and truncating cast
body: upsampled_count is toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) with comment assuming the column always exists. Events without sample_weight (old rows, unsampled relays, transactions mixed in) make sum NULL/0 and undercount, and toInt64 truncates fractional weights (e.g. 1/0.33). Counts can silently drop to zero or lose precision instead of falling back to count.

title: Only bare count() is rewritten
body: transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling only matches column_lower == 'count()'. Common variants like 'count() as count', 'count_if(...)', 'count_unique(...)' or equations pass through unchanged, so an allowlisted error query silently returns un-upsampled numbers while the caller assumes upsampling was applied.

title: Internal upsampled_count exposed as public function
body: The neighboring count() SnQLFunction is declared private=True, but the new upsampled_count omits private, making it callable directly via Discover search. Users can bypass the allowlist gate and get incorrect sums on projects without sample_weight.

title: Test factory silently overwrites sample_rate
body: _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling unconditionally sets normalized_data['sample_rate'] from contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate with bare except:pass and if client_sample_rate truthiness check. It overwrites any explicit sample_rate, accepts out-of-range values, and changes behavior for every store_event caller globally, not just upsampling tests.

title: fetch_error_details misaligns error IDs with nodestore results
body: In fetch_error_details the code does zip(error_ids, events.values()) where events is the dict returned by nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids). Dict values order does not correspond to error_ids order, and missing keys shift alignment. The result attributes the wrong title/message/timestamp to the wrong error ID, or drops/duplicates entries. It should look up each node_id individually in the dict.

title: get_merged_pr_single_issue_template calls truncate on wrong class
body: CommitContextIntegration defines _truncate_title but get_merged_pr_single_issue_template calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title). PRCommentWorkflow does not define that method in this change, so the call raises AttributeError when formatting suspect-issue comments. It should call self._truncate_title or CommitContextIntegration._truncate_title.

title: Detector update reads wrong validated_data key for type
body: update() does validated_data.get("detector_type", instance.group_type).slug while the serializer field is named type and create() uses validated_data["type"].slug. The update path therefore never sees the new type and always keeps the old group type, so changing a detector's type via PUT silently does nothing.

title: age/timestamp mutual-exclusion check uses truthiness not presence
body: validate_timestamp checks if self.initial_data.get("age") and validate_age checks if self.initial_data.get("timestamp"). Values of 0 are falsy, so a report containing both age and timestamp where one is 0 passes validation even though the two specs are mutually exclusive. Timestamp has min_value 0 so 0 is legal. The checks should test key presence or is not None.

title: Table widget flag renders empty table discarding real results
body: When organization.features includes use-table-widget-visualization the code renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded empty columns and empty data/meta instead of the fetched tableResults. Users with the flag see an empty table and lose access to real dashboard table data. The branch should convert result.data/meta to tabular props or not be merged until implemented.

title: Direct dict indexing of slow conditions can KeyError
body: After refactoring, get_condition_query_groups and get_groups_to_fire do dcg_to_slow_conditions[dcg.id] without fallback. If a data condition group in the passed list is missing from the pre-fetched map, this raises KeyError and fails delayed workflow processing. The previous code fetched inside the function for exactly the groups being processed. It should use .get with a default or ensure full coverage.

title: Analytics recorded before feature-flag and auth checks
body: analytics.record for preprod_artifact.api.assemble runs before the organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble feature check and before request validation. Disabled, unauthorized, or malformed requests are still counted, inflating metrics and recording user_id even when the request will be rejected with 404/400. The record call should happen after the feature gate passes.

title: fetch_error_details misaligns error IDs to nodestore data
body: In fetch_error_details the code builds node_ids from error_ids, calls nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids) which returns a dict keyed by node_id, then does zip(error_ids, events.values()). Dict values order is not guaranteed to match error_ids order, and if any node is missing the lengths differ so zip truncates and shifts. The result pairs the wrong event_id with the wrong title/message/timestamp, sending incorrect error context to Seer and misattributing errors.

title: age/timestamp mutual-exclusion check fails for 0 values
body: validate_timestamp uses if self.initial_data.get("age") and validate_age uses if self.initial_data.get("timestamp"). When age is 0 or timestamp is 0 the .get() value is falsy, so a report containing both age and timestamp passes validation. Age 0 (fresh report) and timestamp 0 are legal values, so mixed-spec reports that should be rejected with 422 will be accepted, and neither field is required so reports with neither also pass.

title: get_merged_pr_single_issue_template references undefined PRCommentWorkflow
body: CommitContextIntegration.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title) but _truncate_title is defined as a staticmethod on CommitContextIntegration in this file. PRCommentWorkflow is not the class that defines it (and is not imported in the shown context), so calling the merged-PR comment path raises AttributeError/NameError and breaks suspect-issue PR comments for GitHub and GitLab.

title: Analytics recorded before feature-flag/permission check
body: ProjectPreprodArtifactAssembleEndpoint.post calls analytics.record(preprod_artifact.api.assemble) before checking organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble and before validating the body. Disabled, unauthorized, or malformed requests are therefore counted as assemble attempts, inflating metrics and recording user_id/organization_id/project_id for requests that should have been rejected with 404/400.

title: Table widget visualization renders empty data behind flag
body: When organization.features includes use-table-widget-visualization the code renders <TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data:[], meta:{fields:{},units:{}}}} /> instead of passing the actual result.meta, result.data, fields and renderers used by StyledSimpleTableChart. Enabling the flag replaces every dashboard table with an empty table, losing all query results.

title: Column fallback crashes when meta.fields is missing
body: The fallback columnOrder does Object.keys(tableData?.meta.fields). If tableData is undefined or meta/fields is undefined (empty result, loading, or error shape), this throws TypeError: Cannot convert undefined to object and crashes the widget. It should guard with fallback to empty array, e.g. Object.keys(tableData?.meta?.fields ?? {}).

title: fetch_error_details mismatches error IDs to nodestore data
body: fetch_error_details builds node_ids from error_ids, calls nodestore get_multi, then does zip(error_ids, events.values()). get_multi returns a dict keyed by node_id and values() order is not guaranteed to match error_ids order, and missing keys shift alignment. The result pairs the wrong title/message/timestamp with the wrong id, corrupts chronological interleaving in gen_request_data, and sends wrong error context to Seer. It should look up each node_id individually instead of zipping values().

title: TableWidgetVisualization rendered with empty data
body: When the use-table-widget-visualization flag is on, tableResultComponent renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded columns={[]} and tableData {data:[], meta:{fields:{},units:{}}}, discarding the actual result.data, result.meta, fields, and custom renderers computed just above. Every dashboard table under the flag will render empty instead of its query results.

title: age/timestamp mutual-exclusion check uses truthiness
body: validate_timestamp checks if self.initial_data.get("age") and validate_age checks if self.initial_data.get("timestamp"). Falsy-but-valid values like timestamp 0 or age 0 bypass the check, so a report containing both fields can pass validation. It also allows reports with neither field since both are required=False. The checks should test key presence, not truthiness, and require exactly one of the two.

title: Analytics recorded before feature/auth check
body: analytics.record for preprod_artifact.api.assemble runs before the organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble feature check. Disabled, unauthorized, or invalid requests are counted as assembles, inflating the metric and recording user/project IDs for requests that should be rejected with 404. The record call should happen after the feature gate passes.

title: Unmemoized projectIds churns query key every render
body: projectIds is derived inline via projects.map(...) or selection.projects, creating a new array identity on every render, but it is a dependency of the useMemo that builds queryOptions and the queryKey. The queryKey therefore changes every render, causing useQuery to refetch trace-item attribute keys continuously. projectIds should be memoized.

title: KeyError crash when Integration metadata has no sender
body: In src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py GitHubInstallation.dispatch does pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") != integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]. If the Integration was created before sender tracking, via the normal pipeline without a webhook, or metadata lacks sender, this raises KeyError/TypeError resulting in a 500 instead of the intended github-integration-failed.html error page. It is a denial-of-service and breaks reinstall of legacy integrations.

title: Fresh installs skip GitHub-user ownership check
body: In src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py GitHubInstallation.dispatch returns pipeline.next_step() immediately when Integration.DoesNotExist for the supplied installation_id, without comparing github_authenticated_user to the installer. The sender comparison on lines 501-505 only runs when an Integration row already exists (e.g. created by webhook). A fresh installation_id with no row yet therefore creates an Integration without proving the Sentry user is the GitHub user who installed the app, defeating the PR's stated mismatch protection and depending on a webhook race.

title: Unhandled token-exchange / user-info failures give 500 not error page
body: In src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py OAuthLoginView.dispatch calls safe_urlopen for the OAuth access_token exchange and get_user_info(payload["access_token"]) without try/except. Network errors, non-2xx, or GitHub ApiError from /user will propagate as an unhandled exception (500) instead of the intended Invalid installation request error page described in the PR. Only the missing-access_token and missing-login cases are handled.

title: installation-not-found 404 path no longer tested
body: In tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py test_installation_not_found stubs a 404 for /app/installations/{id} but then drives the new OAuthLoginView with code/state ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05 that mismatches pipeline.signature, so it asserts b"Invalid installation request." from the state check and never exercises build_integration's 404 handling ("The GitHub installation could not be found."). The 404 branch is now uncovered.

title: KeyError when Integration metadata lacks sender
body: GitHubInstallation.dispatch does integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] with direct dict indexing. Integrations created before sender was stored, or where build_integration had no state sender, have no metadata sender key. That raises KeyError resulting in a 500 instead of the intended github-integration-failed error page, breaking reinstall/repair flows for existing installs.

title: Unhandled token-exchange/userinfo failures cause 500
body: OAuthLoginView calls safe_urlopen for the access_token exchange and get_user_info without try/except, then checks "login" not in authenticated_user_info. Network errors, non-2xx responses, ApiError from the user API, or a None return all raise instead of returning the error template. A GitHub outage, bad/reused code, or malformed user response turns installation into a 500 rather than the intended Invalid installation request page.

title: installation_not_found test no longer covers 404 path
body: test_installation_not_found stubs a 404 for /app/installations but then calls setup with state ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05 which does not equal the pipeline signature. The request therefore fails at the state-mismatch check in OAuthLoginView and asserts Invalid installation request. The build_integration 404 branch raising The GitHub installation could not be found is never exercised.

title: Fresh installs skip GitHub-user verification
body: In GitHubInstallation.dispatch, when Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id) raises Integration.DoesNotExist the code immediately returns pipeline.next_step() with no comparison of pipeline.fetch_state('github_authenticated_user') to the installer. That is the normal first-install path (proven by test_basic_flow which creates an Integration with no prior webhook). An attacker can complete installation without ever matching the GitHub App installer, or win a race against the installation webhook that creates the Integration row, defeating the security check this PR claims to add.

title: Unsafe sender lookup can 500 instead of failing install
body: The check uses integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] directly. Metadata sender is optional (build_integration only sets it if state.get("sender"), and installation API fixtures have no sender). If an Integration exists without sender metadata, this raises KeyError and returns HTTP 500 instead of the intended github-integration-failed.html error page, breaking reinstalls and leaking internal error handling.

title: Token exchange and user lookup have no error handling
body: OAuthLoginView.dispatch calls safe_urlopen for the code->token exchange and get_user_info for /user outside any try/except (only safe_urlread/parse_qsl is wrapped). Network errors, non-2xx from GitHub, timeouts, or ApiError from get_user_info will propagate as an unhandled exception and HTTP 500. The PR description says bad/reused code should show the installation-failed page, but only the missing-access_token case is handled; all transport/API failures crash instead of returning error(request, ...).

title: queued default evaluated once at import time
body: In src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py the field is declared as `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`. The call to timezone.now() runs once when the module is imported, so every AssignmentSource created without an explicit queued value shares the same timestamp. It should be `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. Consequence: provenance timestamps are wrong and any future debounce / ordering logic based on queued will be broken.

title: to_dict/from_dict datetime does not survive task queue round-trip
body: AssignmentSource.to_dict() in src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py uses dataclasses.asdict, which leaves `queued` as a datetime object. src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py puts that dict into `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async` kwargs, which must be JSON serializable for Celery. After JSON round-trip the value comes back as a string, and AssignmentSource.from_dict() does `cls(**input_dict)` with no parsing, so `queued` becomes a str violating the declared datetime type. Consequence: task enqueue can fail or produce type-confused objects; serialization should use isoformat and parse back.

title: Same-integration check does not stop multi-integration ping-pong
body: In src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py should_sync() returns False only when `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id`. src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py fans outbound assignee sync out to every GroupLink for the group. If one Sentry group is linked to two different integrations A and B, an inbound assign from A is blocked from echoing to A but still syncs to B, B's webhook then re-enters as inbound from B and syncs to A, forming an infinite A->B->A loop. Consequence: the described fix only breaks single-integration echo, not the general issue-sync cycle.

title: Missing coverage for allow-other-integration and deassign blocking
body: In tests/sentry/models/test_groupassignee.py the only cycle test is test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration which asserts outbound is suppressed when source equals target. There is no test that a different source integration still syncs outward, nor that deassign with a matching AssignmentSource is suppressed. Consequence: a regression that over-suppresses all outbound sync or that leaves the deassign loop unfixed would not be caught.

title: queued default evaluated once at import
body: In src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py the dataclass defines `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`. Dataclass defaults are evaluated once at class definition time, so every AssignmentSource instance shares the same timestamp from import. Any recency/expiry/debounce logic using `queued` will be wrong. It must be `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

title: AssignmentSource datetime not safe for Celery kwargs round-trip
body: In src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py `to_dict()` returns `asdict(self)` including a raw `datetime` for `queued`. That dict is passed as `assignment_source_dict` to `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async` in src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py. Celery task kwargs must be JSON-serializable; a datetime will fail serialization or arrive as an ISO string. `from_dict()` then does `cls(**input_dict)` without parsing strings, so a round-tripped value becomes a `str` where `datetime` is expected, breaking type invariants and any time comparison.

title: Corrupt source dict fails open and re-enables cycle
body: In src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py an unparseable `assignment_source_dict` makes `AssignmentSource.from_dict()` return None, and the code then calls `should_sync` with None, i.e. no source. That permits outbound sync back to the integration that originated the inbound change, exactly the loop this PR claims to fix. A parse failure should fail closed (skip/log) rather than silently dropping loop protection.

title: should_sync signature change breaks existing overrides
body: In src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py `should_sync` was changed from `should_sync(attribute)` to `should_sync(attribute, sync_source=None)` and the outbound task now calls it with two positional arguments. Any existing IssueBasicIntegration/IssueSyncIntegration subclass that overrides the old one-argument signature will raise TypeError when called with the new argument, breaking outbound sync for that provider. The base call needs backward-compatible handling for overrides that do not accept the new parameter.

title: Frozen dataclass uses evaluated-once default for queued timestamp
body: In src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py line 18, `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` calls timezone.now() once at import time. Every AssignmentSource created via from_integration() without an explicit queued value therefore shares the same timestamp for the life of the process. The queued field cannot be used for ordering, debugging, or expiry. Fix is dataclasses.field(default_factory=timezone.now).

title: to_dict/from_dict not Celery-JSON safe, breaks outbound enqueue
body: In src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py, to_dict() returns asdict() including a raw datetime object for queued. In src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py sync_group_assignee_outbound passes that dict as assignment_source_dict to sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async kwargs. Celery JSON serialization cannot serialize datetime, so any inbound assignment (which sets a source) will fail to enqueue outbound tasks to other integrations or raise serialization errors. Conversely from_dict() does cls(**input_dict) with no datetime parsing, so after JSON round-trip queued would be a string violating the declared type. Serialize queued to ISO string and parse it back.

title: Outbound call passes undocumented assignment_source kwarg
body: In src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py line 59-61, the task calls installation.sync_assignee_outbound(external_issue, user, assign=assign, assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source). The abstract contract in src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py for sync_assignee_outbound is (external_issue, user, assign=True, **kwargs) with no explicit assignment_source parameter, unlike sync_status_outbound which was updated.
