Any concrete IssueSyncIntegration subclass that overrides sync_assignee_outbound with an exact signature without **kwargs will raise TypeError on every outbound sync, breaking all assignee sync. Update the base signature to declare assignment_source explicitly.

title: Loop suppression keyed only on integration_id over-suppresses and fail-opens
body: In src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py line 390, should_sync returns False when sync_source.integration_id equals org_integration.integration_id. AssignmentSource carries only integration_id, not organization_id. A single integration shared by multiple organizations will therefore suppress outbound sync for all organizations when only the originating organization should be suppressed. Separately, in src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py, AssignmentSource.from_dict returns None on malformed input, and should_sync(None) returns True, so any deserialization failure silently disables loop protection and reintroduces the cycle the PR fixes.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler was changed to subclass StatefulDetectorHandler but provides no implementations. StatefulDetectorHandler declares abstract members counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the new build_occurrence_and_event_data. A subclass that does not override them remains abstract, so group_type.detector_handler(self) in src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py will raise TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class. process_detectors does not catch this, so any detector of this type will crash evaluation instead of being skipped.

title: get_state_data KeyErrors when counter_names is empty
body: get_state_data initializes counter_updates as {} and only populates it inside if self.counter_names:. The result construction unconditionally does counter_updates[gk]. When a detector defines counter_names as an empty list, which the if-guard explicitly anticipates, this raises KeyError for every group key. The fallback for no counters should be None or {} per key, not a missing dict entry.

title: evaluate docstring still says list after change to dict
body: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate was changed to return dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult], but its docstring still says it returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult with one result per group key. Readers of only the docstring will expect the old contract.

title: get_state_data crashes when counter_names is empty
body: In StatefulDetectorHandler.get_state_data the code initializes counter_updates={} and only populates it inside `if self.counter_names:`. It then unconditionally does `counter_updates[gk]` when building DetectorStateData. If a detector implements `counter_names` as [] (no counters to track), the dict stays empty and the lookup raises KeyError, crashing evaluation for every group_key. The fallback should be an empty dict or dict of Nones per group_key.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler became abstract and cannot be instantiated
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler was changed from DetectorHandler (which only required `evaluate`, which it implemented) to StatefulDetectorHandler with `pass`. StatefulDetectorHandler has four abstract members: `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. With no implementations the subclass remains abstract, so `MetricAlertDetectorHandler(detector)` via `Detector.detector_handler` raises TypeError. The previous version returned [] and was instantiable; this is a regression for any detector with type `metric_alert_fire`.

title: get_group_key_values type excludes None group_key
body: The abstract signature is `-> dict[str, int]` but `DetectorGroupKey` is `str | None` and the codebase routinely uses `None` as a group_key (tests use `{None: 6}`, `build_dedupe_value_key` explicitly handles `None`). The annotation is wrong and hides None-handling requirements from implementers and type checkers. It should be `dict[DetectorGroupKey, int]`.

title: Stale docstring says evaluate returns a list
body: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate was changed to return `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]` but its docstring still says it “returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult”. Readers relying on the docstring will expect list semantics instead of dict keyed by group_key.

title: Mock occurrence builder ignores value so wrong forwarding is not caught
body: build_mock_occurrence_and_event takes `value: int` but never uses it, and TestProcessDetectors.test_state_results_multi_group builds the group_2 expectation with value 6 while the data packet contains group_2:10. Because the helper ignores the argument the tests pass regardless of what `value` StatefulDetectorHandler passes to `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. A bug that swaps or mis-forwards group values would not be detected.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract and cannot be instantiated
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but defines no methods with just `pass`. StatefulDetectorHandler has abstract members counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values and build_occurrence_and_event_data, so the subclass remains abstract. Detector.detector_handler does `group_type.detector_handler(self)` which will raise TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class, breaking any processing of metric_alert detectors.

title: get_state_data KeyErrors when counter_names is empty
body: counter_updates dict is only populated inside `if self.counter_names:`. The result loop unconditionally does `counter_updates=counter_updates[gk]`. A detector with no counters (counter_names == []) will therefore raise KeyError for every group key instead of returning empty counter dicts.

title: Redis key builders conflate None and empty-string group keys
body: build_dedupe_value_key and build_counter_value_key map `None` to `""` before formatting, so group_key None and group_key "" produce the identical Redis key (e.g. `123::dedupe_value`). DB state and fingerprints treat them as distinct (NULL vs empty string, fingerprint `123` vs `123:`), so dedupe/counter values for the two keys will overwrite each other.

title: Missing-grouptype log loses detector type
body: When no grouptype is registered, the error extra logs `"group_type": str(group_type)` where group_type is None/ falsy, so it always logs "None". The useful value is `self.type` (the slug that failed lookup, already available as detector_type), so on-call debugging loses which slug was invalid.

title: Stale evaluate docstring says list
body: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate docstring still says it "returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult" after the signature was changed to return `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`. Readers will expect list semantics.

title: Empty Redis pipeline still executes
body: _bulk_commit_redis_state calls `pipeline.execute()` unconditionally, even when both dedupe_updates and counter_updates are empty. Every detector evaluation with no state change therefore still pays a Redis round-trip.

title: Multi-group test does not verify value propagation
body: test_state_results_multi_group processes group_vals {"group_1": 6, "group_2": 10} but builds the expected occurrence for group_2 with value 6, and build_mock_occurrence_and_event ignores the value argument entirely. A bug passing the wrong value to build_occurrence_and_event_data would not be caught.

title: Monitor context discards schedule_type display conversion
body: In get_monitor_environment_context a copy of monitor.config is made in `config` and `config['schedule_type']` is replaced with get_schedule_type_display(), but the returned dict uses `monitor_environment.monitor.config` instead of `config`. The conversion is therefore dead code and callers always receive the raw schedule_type value in the occurrence context.

title: IndexError when previous_checkins window is empty
body: In try_incident_threshold `starting_checkin = previous_checkins[0]` is accessed without checking length. If the DB query returns no rows, or failure_issue_threshold is 0 or negative so the slice is empty, this raises IndexError and crashes mark_failed processing instead of creating or skipping the incident gracefully.

title: get_failure_reason mishandles empty or unmapped statuses
body: get_failure_reason filters check-ins to HUMAN_FAILURE_STATUS_MAP and only handles the single-count case. If failed_checkins is empty or contains only statuses like OK or in-progress that are filtered out, status_counts is empty, the single-item branch is skipped, and the plural branch formats an empty list into '%(problem_checkins)s check-ins detected', producing malformed evidence such as ' check-ins detected' for the monitor issue.

title: Zero/negative flusher_processes silently disables flushing
body: In SpanFlusher.__init__ num_processes is min(max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards)) with max_processes = max_processes or len(...). A value of 0 falls back to len() silently, a negative value is truthy so num_processes becomes negative, range(negative) is empty and no processes are created. With empty assigned_shards num_processes is also 0. In all these cases submit() still accepts messages and advances drift but no background process ever calls flush_segments(), so segments sit in Redis forever with no error. Validate max_processes >=1 and assigned_shards non-empty or fall back to 1 process.

title: Flusher restart leaks old worker and double-flushes shards
body: In _ensure_processes_alive the old worker is replaced via _create_process_for_shards() immediately after process.kill() without join()/close(). For the threading.Thread test path the isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) guard is false so nothing stops the old thread at all. The old worker keeps looping on the same shards while the new worker starts, so two workers call buffer.flush_segments()/done_flush_segments() and produce() for the same shards concurrently, causing duplicate Kafka produces and racing Redis deletes. Kill must be followed by join/close and threads must be stopped before replacement.

title: join() abandons remaining flusher processes on timeout
body: In SpanFlusher.join() the loop computes remaining_time and does break when the deadline expires. Breaking exits the for loop entirely, so any processes not yet waited on are never joined nor terminated and join() returns while workers are still alive. The single-process predecessor always waited then terminated its worker. The loop should continue to terminate remaining workers or record that shutdown timed out, not silently leave them running.

title: Inconsistent metric tag shard vs shards
body: SpanFlusher.main emits spans.buffer.flusher.produce with tags={"shard": shard_tag} on line 185 but spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce with tags={"shards": shard_tag} on line 199. Dashboards and alerts grouping by shard will miss half the timers. Use the same tag key in both timers.

title: Multi-process flusher test never flushes
body: test_flusher_processes_limit creates 4 partitions with flusher_processes=2, asserts process counts and shard totals, then joins without submitting any spans, advancing drift, or checking output, backpressure, or per-process shard assignment. It cannot catch duplicate production, lost shards, or the restart/join bugs introduced by sharding. Extend it to write spans on multiple shards and verify each segment is produced exactly once.

title: Spawn flusher processes are never killed on restart
body: In _ensure_processes_alive the code does `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.kill()`. Processes are created via `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, i.e. `SpawnProcess`, which is not an instance of the default-context `multiprocessing.Process` (both only share BaseProcess). So the check is always False, the old hung/crashed process is never killed, and _create_process_for_shards starts a second process for the same shards. Consequence: leaked processes, two flushers competing on the same Redis shards and double-producing segments to buffered-segments.

title: Spawn flusher processes are never terminated on join
body: In join() the code does `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.terminate()`. For the same reason as above, spawn-context processes fail this isinstance check, so a hung flusher that ignores the `stopped` flag is never force-terminated. Consequence: join() spins until deadline and then leaks the hung child process, blocking clean shutdown/rebalance.

title: Negative flusher_processes silently disables flushing
body: Flusher does `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` then `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))`. A negative value is truthy, so e.g. --flusher-processes=-1 yields num_processes=-1, `range(-1)` is empty, no flusher processes/buffers are created. Consequence: segments are never flushed, Redis grows unboundedly and data is lost, with no error. There is no validation clamping the CLI/factory value to >=1.

title: Restart helper leaks old process/thread
body: _create_process_for_shard() calls _create_process_for_shards() which overwrites self.processes[process_index] and self.buffers[process_index] without stopping/killing/joining the previous entry. For the threading (test) mode there is not even an attempt to stop the old thread since `stopped` is global. Consequence: if ever used, duplicate workers flush the same shards concurrently, causing duplicate Kafka produces and leaked threads/processes.

title: Inconsistent metric tag name shards vs shard
body: In SpanFlusher.main the produce timer uses tags={"shard": shard_tag} and segment_size uses "shard", but the wait_produce timer uses tags={"shards": shard_tag}. Consumers of these metrics expecting a single tag key will see split series. The plural key should be "shard" for consistency.

title: Spawn flusher processes are never killed/terminated
body: In _ensure_processes_alive and join the code checks isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) but processes are created with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, whose type is multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, not multiprocessing.Process on Linux where the default context is fork. The isinstance check is therefore False for real flusher processes, so process.kill() on unhealthy restart and process.terminate() on join never run. A crashed/hung flusher is then replaced while the old OS process keeps running and flushing the same Redis shards, causing duplicate produces and leaked zombies.

title: join() timeout logic leaks remaining flusher processes
body: In SpanFlusher.join remaining_time is computed but never used to bound the wait, and if the deadline expires the loop just breaks without terminating the un-joined processes. Earlier processes can consume the whole timeout in next_step.join(timeout) plus their own busy wait, leaving later entries in self.processes alive and never terminated. Shutdown/rebalance can then leak flusher processes that keep flushing and producing.

title: Flusher restart leaks thread-mode workers
body: When produce_to_pipe is set the worker is a threading.Thread. On unhealthy detection _ensure_processes_alive skips kill for threads because of the multiprocessing.Process check and immediately calls _create_process_for_shards, which starts a second thread sharing the same stopped/drift/backpressure/healthy Values while the old thread is still in its while not stopped.value loop. Both threads then flush the same shards and call produce, duplicating output and never reclaiming the old thread.

title: Unused _create_process_for_shard would orphan running worker
body: The helper _create_process_for_shard loops the shard map and calls _create_process_for_shards without stopping, joining, killing, or terminating the existing entry in self.processes, and it overwrites self.processes and self.buffers. It is currently dead code, but if wired up it would leak the old process/thread while two workers flush the same shards.

title: Partition lock creation is racy
body: In src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py OffsetTracker._get_partition_lock does get then setdefault on partition_locks dict with no global lock. Two threads for the same new Partition can both miss the get and create different Lock objects, so add_offset/complete_offset/get_committable_offsets for that partition can run under different locks. Consequence is corrupted all_offsets/outstanding sets and wrong committable offsets, causing duplicate processing or skipping offsets.

title: Commit scan loops over offset gaps
body: In src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets iterates range(start, max_offset+1) to find contiguous completion. If offsets are sparse (e.g. 100 and 1_000_100 after a gap, filtering, or different assignment), it loops ~1M times per partition on every 1s commit tick. Consequence is CPU burn and stalled commit thread, delaying all commits.

title: Failed work is still marked complete and committed
body: In src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py OrderedQueueWorker.run catches all Exceptions from result_processor, logs, then unconditionally calls offset_tracker.complete_offset in finally. The class docstring claims only successful processing is committed. Consequence is a poison or transient failure advances the committed offset past the failed message, so the message is lost with no retry or DLQ.

title: Unbounded queues provide no backpressure
body: In src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py FixedQueuePool creates queue.Queue() with no maxsize while claiming natural backpressure. If a queue's worker stalls on a slow subscription, submit keeps appending via non-blocking put. Consequence is unbounded memory growth and OOM, instead of blocking the Arroyo poll loop.

title: Shutdown abandons queued work
body: In src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets worker.shutdown=True before draining, and OrderedQueueWorker.run exits when that flag is set after the current item. Remaining queued WorkItems are never processed and their offsets never completed. SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close calls this path, so normal close/rebalance drops in-memory work and forces redelivery or stalls commits.

title: Shared queue pool is shut down by per-partition strategy
body: In src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/result_consumer.py create_thread_queue_parallel_worker shares factory.queue_pool across all strategies from create_with_partitions, but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close/terminate calls queue_pool.shutdown. Closing one partition assignment (e.g. on rebalance) kills workers for all current and future assignments reusing the factory pool, after which submit either blocks or raises queue.ShutDown and messages stop being processed.

title: join ignores timeout and always closes
body: In src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.join(timeout) ignores the timeout argument and unconditionally calls close, which joins the commit thread for 5s and shuts down the pool. Callers expecting Arroyo join semantics (wait up to timeout without destroying the strategy) instead get a destructive shutdown.

title: wait_until_empty ignores in-flight work
body: In src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py FixedQueuePool.wait_until_empty and get_stats use only Queue.qsize. An item taken by a worker but not yet finished or offset-completed leaves qsize at 0. Consequence is callers conclude processing is done while work is still in flight, causing premature commits checks and flaky tests.

title: Partition lock creation is racy, breaks offset mutual exclusion
body: OffsetTracker._get_partition_lock reads/writes self.partition_locks dict with no global lock. Two threads creating a lock for the same new Partition can each create a different threading.Lock via setdefault race, so add_offset/complete_offset/get_committable/mark_committed for that partition then synchronize on different locks. get_committable also does list(self.all_offsets.keys()) while add_offset can mutate the dict, risking RuntimeError or missed partitions. Consequence is corrupted outstanding/all_offsets sets and wrong committable offsets (duplicate processing or stalled commits).

title: Unbounded queues provide no backpressure, risk OOM
body: FixedQueuePool creates queue.Queue() with no maxsize and submit() never blocks, while SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit/poll never apply backpressure. The docstring claims natural backpressure when queues fill up, but queues never fill. A slow group_key lets the consumer keep polling Kafka and enqueueing unbounded WorkItems (which retain full Message payloads), growing memory until OOM. qsize-based stats/metrics also under-report because qsize drops on get() before processing finishes.

title: Failed items are marked complete and committed
body: OrderedQueueWorker.run catches all Exceptions from result_processor, logs, then unconditionally calls offset_tracker.complete_offset in finally. The strategy docstring claims only commits offsets after successful processing, but failures become committable and are committed by the commit loop, bypassing retry and Arroyo DLQ handling. A transient DB error or bug in handle_result is silently skipped and the Kafka offset advances, losing the result forever.

title: Shared queue pool is shut down by per-partition strategy close
body: ResultsStrategyFactory creates one FixedQueuePool in __init__ shared by every SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy returned from create_with_partitions, but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close/terminate calls self.queue_pool.shutdown(). On rebalance Arroyo closes the old strategy, which sets worker.shutdown=True and shuts down queues used by the new strategy, discarding queued work and stopping workers. Multiple strategies also each spawn a commit thread sharing one OffsetTracker but committing via different commit closures, causing duplicate or partition-incorrect commits.

title: Shutdown discards queued but unprocessed items
body: FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets worker.shutdown=True before draining, and OrderedQueueWorker.run loops on while not self.shutdown. After finishing the current item a worker exits even if its queue still holds items. Those WorkItems were already add_offset-tracked but never complete_offset, so close/join does not flush them. Combined with use of queue.Queue.shutdown/queue.ShutDown (Python 3.13+ only), on older runtimes q.shutdown raises AttributeError which is swallowed, leaving workers blocked on get() forever and join() timing out with leaked daemon threads.

title: OffsetTracker partition-lock creation is racy
body: In src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:49 _get_partition_lock() does get() then setdefault() on self.partition_locks with no lock. Two worker/submit threads creating the same new Partition can create two different Lock objects and then use different locks to guard all_offsets/outstanding/last_committed. Consequence is lost mutual exclusion, corrupted offset sets, and committing an offset whose predecessors are still outstanding, causing message loss on restart.

title: Unbounded queues contradict claimed backpressure
body: In src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:185 FixedQueuePool creates plain queue.Queue() with no maxsize and submit() in line 204 just puts. poll() never blocks. The class docstring claims natural backpressure, but the Arroyo poll loop can enqueue without bound if one group stalls. Consequence is unbounded memory growth/OOM instead of slowing the Kafka consumer, defeating the stated goal of isolating slow items.

title: Shutdown cannot drain and depends on Queue.shutdown
body: In src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:231 shutdown() sets worker.shutdown=True then calls q.shutdown(immediate=False). OrderedQueueWorker.run() in line 129 loops while not self.shutdown, so after the flag is set it exits after the current item instead of draining. Also queue.Queue.shutdown only exists on Python 3.13+; on older runtimes it raises AttributeError which is swallowed, leaving workers blocked forever in get(). Consequence is either dropped queued work on graceful shutdown or hung/leaked worker threads and a join storm.

title: Failed items are still marked complete and committed
body: In src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:149 OrderedQueueWorker.run() calls offset_tracker.complete_offset() in finally unconditionally, and ResultProcessor.__call__ already swallows all exceptions. The strategy docstring promises only commits after successful processing, but any exception still advances the contiguous committable offset. Consequence is poison-pill / transient DB failures are acked and never retried, silently losing uptime results.

title: Shared queue pool is destroyed by one strategy close
body: In src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/result_consumer.py:133 the factory creates one FixedQueuePool shared by every SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy returned from create_with_partitions, but in src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:335 SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()/terminate() shuts down that shared pool and join() calls close(). On rebalance or multi-partition assignment closing one strategy kills workers/queues for all other live strategies reusing the same pool. Consequence is stalled consumption after the first rebalance requiring process restart.

title: Offsets committed from background thread
body: In src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:273 SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy._commit_loop runs on its own thread and calls the Arroyo Commit callable and mark_committed(). Arroyo expects commit to be driven from the processing strategy poll/join path; concurrent commits race with partition revocation and with other strategies sharing the same OffsetTracker. Consequence is committing offsets for revoked partitions, double commits, or missing the final commit on close, breaking at-least-once guarantees.

title: Password check bypassed when totpCode is supplied with backupCode
body: In `authorize`, password verification is gated by `if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)`. The new branch `if (user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode)` is evaluated afterwards. An attacker can send both `totpCode` (any dummy value) and `backupCode`: the first condition is false so no password is verified, the second branch is true so login succeeds on backup-code alone. Backup-code login then becomes single-factor instead of password + backup code, violating the 2FA contract.

title: Throwing instead of returning 500 breaks error contract
body: When encryption key is missing or twoFactorSecret is missing/invalid the handler does `throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError)` instead of `return res.status(500).json(...)`. An uncaught throw in a Next.js API route results in a generic 500 HTML/unhandled rejection, not the `{error: ...}` JSON the client (`DisableTwoFactorModal`) expects. The UI will show generic failure and logs leak, and the same pattern is repeated for the backup-code path.

title: Backup-code verification is case-sensitive and crashes on non-string
body: Login does `credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` and `indexOf` directly. Generated codes in `setup.ts` are lowercase hex (`randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`) displayed as `XXXXX-XXXXX`, but user input in uppercase or with surrounding whitespace will not match and returns IncorrectBackupCode. Worse, if `backupCode` is an array/object (truthy), `.replaceAll` throws and crashes authorize instead of returning an error code.

title: Backup-code consumption has read-then-write race allowing reuse
body: Login reads decrypted `backupCodes`, finds the index, sets `backupCodes[index]=null` and writes back with a separate `prisma.user.update`. Two concurrent logins with the same backup code can both read the same array before either writes, so the same single-use code can be used twice. Single-use codes need an atomic compare-and-set/transaction or DB-level guard.

title: Backup-code login can bypass password check
body: In packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts password is only verified when `!credentials.totpCode` (line 121). The new branch `if (user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode)` (line 131) is entered even when a totpCode is also present. An attacker who obtains a single valid backup code can send `{"email":victim, "totpCode":"anything", "backupCode":valid}`: the password check is skipped because totpCode is truthy, and the backup-code check then succeeds without ever verifying the password. This reduces login to single-factor possession of a long-lived backup code and allows account takeover without the password.

title: Used backup codes nulled with no regeneration, leading to lockout
body: In packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts a consumed backup code is replaced with `null` and re-encrypted, so after 10 uses the stored value is `[null,...]`. The check `if (!user.backupCodes)` never becomes true again, so `MissingBackupCodes` is never returned; further backup attempts return `IncorrectBackupCode`. There is no endpoint to regenerate codes while 2FA is enabled (setup rejects with TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled). A user who loses their authenticator and exhausts codes is permanently locked out with a misleading error.

title: Non-string backupCode crashes disable endpoint
body: In apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts line 61 calls `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-","")` unconditionally once the truthy branch is taken, with no type check. If the client sends a non-string truthy value (number, object, array) this throws TypeError, uncaught, producing a 500 instead of a 400 validation error. The same unsafe call exists for login. It also throws `new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError)` for missing key/secret (lines 51,77,82) instead of returning `res.status(500).json()`, breaking the client's `response.json()` error handling.

title: Backup codes and secret not cleared on reset, stale sensitive data retained
body: In apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx `resetState()` only clears password, error and step, but leaves `backupCodes`, `backupCodesUrl`, `dataUri` and `secret` in state. If the modal is cancelled after codes are fetched and reopened, the previous user's secret and backup codes remain in memory and the old object URL is never revoked, leaking sensitive 2FA material across sessions and leaking Blob URLs.

title: Password check bypassed when backupCode + totpCode both supplied
body: Password verification is gated on `if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)` while second-factor selection is gated on `if (user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode)`. An attacker who knows only the victim email and one valid backup code can send backupCode plus any dummy totpCode: the first condition is false so password is never verified, the second condition is true so only the backup code is verified. Backup codes become a single-factor login, bypassing the password. Require password verification independent of totpCode/backupCode presence.

title: Go back / Lost access buttons submit login form
body: TwoFactorFooter renders Buttons inside the login <form> without type="button" and only toggles twoFactorLostAccess / clears fields. A plain Button defaults to submit, so clicking Go back or Lost access also triggers form onSubmit and a credentials signIn call with partial codes. Add type="button" to non-submit footer buttons.

title: Lost access / Cancel buttons submit disable form
body: The Lost access toggle and Cancel buttons are inside <Form> without type="button" and without preventDefault. Clicking them will also submit handleDisable, sending password plus empty totpCode/backupCode and surfacing spurious 2fa_required/incorrect errors or unintended requests. Give them type="button".

title: Throwing instead of returning 500 breaks API contract
body: When CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY is missing or secret length is invalid the handler does `throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError)`. In a Next.js API route this becomes an unhandled exception / HTML 500 instead of the JSON `{error}` shape the client expects (`await response.json()` will fail). Return `res.status(500).json({error: ...})` like setup.ts does. Same risk for JSON.parse/symmetricDecrypt failures on corrupted backupCodes.

title: resetState leaves backup codes and secret in memory
body: resetState clears password, error and step but not backupCodes, backupCodesUrl, dataUri or secret. After closing the DisplayBackupCodes step via backup-codes-close, the plaintext codes and TOTP secret remain in component state and the object URL is never revoked, so reopening or another session on the same page can re-render stale secrets. Clear those fields and revoke the object URL on close/unmount.

title: No coverage for backup-code login or disable
body: The PR adds backup-code login in next-auth-options, backup-code disable in the disable endpoint, and single-use nulling of codes, but the e2e only tests download/copy/close buttons and leaves an explicit TODO for login + disabling with backup codes. There is no test that a backup code logs in once and is then rejected, or that disable with a backup code works/fails correctly.

title: updateEvent calendar fallback is dead code, passes undefined calendarId
body: In updateEvent selectedCalendar is computed as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When externalCalendarId is falsy the else-branch searches for `externalId === externalCalendarId` (null/undefined/empty) which can never match, so selectedCalendar is always undefined on that path. Google `events.update` is then called with undefined calendarId and will fail instead of falling back to the event's destination calendar or primary.

title: deleteEvent calendar fallback is dead code, passes undefined calendarId
body: In deleteEvent calendarId is computed as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When externalCalendarId is falsy the fallback compares against that same falsy value and never matches, so calendarId is undefined and the code relies on `calendarId ? calendarId : defaultCalendarId` only by accident. For any truthy-but-mismatched case and for future edits this logic cannot select the correct destination calendar and deletes from the wrong calendar.

title: Meet fallback dereferences possibly undefined destination calendar
body: Code does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` then `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"`. If destinationCalendar is undefined, null, or empty array, the destructured value is undefined and accessing `.integration` throws TypeError, crashing event creation for bookings without a destination calendar. Must use optional chaining with fallback.

title: Collective team calendars silently dropped when organizer has no calendar
body: evt.destinationCalendar is built as `eventType.destinationCalendar ? [..] : organizerUser.destinationCalendar ? [..] : null` and later `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` for COLLECTIVE. When both organizer sources are missing the value is null, optional chaining skips the push, so all collected teamDestinationCalendars for the other hosts are lost and only one/no calendar event is created.

title: Non-Google services ignore credentialId and always use first calendar
body: Google createEvent was updated to select `destinationCalendar.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)` but Office365, Lark (line 128: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []`), and BaseCalendarService still only use the first array entry. EventManager loops per-destination and passes the credential, so the second collective host's event is still created in the first host's calendar for all non-Google integrations.

title: Breaking Calendar interface and webhook payload change
body: Changing `destinationCalendar?: DestinationCalendar | null` to `DestinationCalendar[] | null` and `createEvent(event)` to `createEvent(event, credentialId: number)` breaks all external Calendar implementations and changes webhook payloads from `destinationCalendar: null` to `[]` (as updated in webhook.e2e.ts). Consumers expecting null or single object will break. The new parameter should be optional and payload compatibility should be preserved or documented as breaking.

title: updateEvent calendar fallback can never resolve
body: In updateEvent the code is `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When the fallback branch runs externalCalendarId is falsy, so the find compares against that same falsy value and always returns undefined. The previous code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`. Now updates without an externalCalendarId call `calendar.events.update` with an undefined calendarId and fail.

title: deleteEvent calendar fallback can never resolve
body: In deleteEvent the code is `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When externalCalendarId is missing the find uses that same missing value and never matches, so calendarId is undefined and the delete falls back only to primary instead of the booking's destination calendar. The old code used `event.destinationCalendar.externalId` as fallback.

title: Crash when destinationCalendar is empty
body: EventManager.create does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []; if (... && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")`. If destinationCalendar is null/undefined/empty the destructured value is undefined and accessing `.integration` throws TypeError, breaking booking creation for users without a destination calendar. It needs optional chaining.

title: Collective second-host calendars dropped when organizer has none
body: The new evt sets `destinationCalendar` to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has one, then does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. With null the optional chain no-ops, so collective hosts' destinationCalendars collected in teamDestinationCalendars are silently discarded and second hosts never get calendar events.

title: Inverted IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED slug logic
body: This PR flips organization creation from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && {slug})` / `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && {requestedSlug: slug})` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? {slug} : {})` / `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? {requestedSlug: slug} : {})`. That stores slug vs requestedSlug in the opposite billing mode from before, an unrelated breaking change to org provisioning that should not be in a destinationCalendar fix.

title: updateEvent called with undefined credential
body: In updateAllCalendarEvents when reference.credentialId is set but the credential is found neither in memory nor in the DB, `credential` remains undefined and the code still calls `updateEvent(credential, ...)`. getCalendar(undefined) throws, turning a missing-credential case for one host into a failure instead of being skipped or reported per-reference.

title: Google updateEvent fallback calendar lookup can never match
body: In updateEvent, selectedCalendar is computed as externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId. When externalCalendarId is falsy the else-branch searches for cal.externalId === externalCalendarId (null/undefined/empty), so it always yields undefined. Updates for bookings without an externalCalendarId therefore call calendar.events.update with calendarId undefined instead of falling back to the destination calendar, causing update failures.

title: Google deleteEvent fallback calendar lookup can never match
body: In deleteEvent, calendarId uses the same pattern: externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId. When externalCalendarId is missing the find predicate compares against the same missing value and returns undefined, so deletion falls back to primary even when a destinationCalendar is present, deleting from / missing the event on the wrong calendar.

title: Unhandled undefined when no destinationCalendar breaks Google Meet fallback
body: const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [] followed by mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar" dereferences possibly-undefined. When evt has no destination calendar (empty array, which this PR now explicitly creates), this throws TypeError and breaks all event creation, instead of falling back to Cal Video.

title: Collective destination calendars silently dropped when organizer has none
body: evt.destinationCalendar is set to null when neither eventType nor organizer has a calendar, then evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars) is used for COLLECTIVE events. Optional chaining on null is a no-op, so hosts' destination calendars collected in teamDestinationCalendars are discarded and only the organizer calendar (none) is used. Collective hosts then never get calendar events created. It should initialize to [] not null.

title: Webhook payload contract changed without updating all expectations
body: CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar changed from object/null to array, so webhook payloads now emit [] instead of null. This test still asserts destinationCalendar: null for BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED (lines 119, 373) while only BOOKING_REJECTED was updated to []. This is a breaking change for webhook consumers and leaves stale assertions that will fail / mask the new shape.

title: Missing prisma import causes runtime ReferenceError
body: File uses prisma.credential.update at line 96 but there is no import of @calcom/prisma in the file. Any Salesforce calendar operation calling getClient will throw ReferenceError: prisma is not defined, breaking all Salesforce calendar functionality.

title: Refreshed Salesforce token fetched but never used
body: After refreshing and persisting new tokens, the returned jsforce.Connection is constructed from the old credentialKey.instance_url/accessToken/refreshToken instead of accessTokenParsed.data. The refresh network call therefore has no effect and the client continues to use the expired access token.

title: Refresh error check uses statusText instead of ok/status
body: Code checks response.statusText !== "OK" to detect refresh failure. Fetch statusText is implementation-dependent and often empty, so failures can be missed or successes incorrectly rejected. Should check !response.ok or response.status.

title: Minimum token schema is invalid and strips required fields
body: The schema uses computed keys like [z.string().toString()] which evaluate to literal strings such as "[object Object]", not a catch-all. Zod objects strip unknown keys by default, so validating an external sync response with this schema will drop expiry/refresh fields or fail unexpectedly. Should use .passthrough()/.catchall() instead.

title: Missing refresh_token replaced with dummy string
body: If the parsed response has no refresh_token, the code mutates it to the literal string "refresh_token". Callers then persist this to credential.key, permanently corrupting the stored credential with a non-functional refresh token.

title: Sync path returns fetch Response incompatible with callers
body: When credential syncing is enabled the helper returns a raw fetch Response, but Google (expects res.data), Hubspot (expects token object), and Zoho Bigin/CRM (expects axios response with .data) callers treat the result as their original library type. For example Google does res?.data which is undefined for a fetch Response, causing TypeError on token.access_token. The helper needs to normalize shapes or callers must handle both.

title: Passes credentialId as userId to sync endpoint
body: refreshOAuthTokens is called with credentialId where the userId parameter is expected, so the sync endpoint receives calcomUserId equal to the credential ID, not the user ID. The remote lookup will fail or return another user's token.

title: Unvalidated request handling allows method abuse and 500s
body: Handler has no HTTP method check so GET/PUT also create/update credentials, and z.object.parse plus JSON.parse/symmetricDecrypt are called without try/catch. Invalid bodies, malformed encrypted payloads, or wrong encryption keys throw uncaught and return 500 instead of 400, and expose stack traces.

title: Missing prisma import causes runtime ReferenceError
body: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts calls prisma.credential.update at line 96 but the file never imports prisma. Every instantiation of SalesforceCalendarService via getClient will throw ReferenceError: prisma is not defined, breaking all Salesforce calendar operations.

title: Refreshed Salesforce tokens never used, stale tokens persist
body: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts fetches and stores refreshed tokens in accessTokenParsed but then constructs the jsforce.Connection with the old credentialKey.instance_url, credentialKey.access_token and credentialKey.refresh_token. The refresh is wasted and subsequent API calls keep using the expired access token, causing persistent auth failures.

title: Refresh failure check uses statusText instead of ok/status
body: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts checks if (response.statusText !== "OK") to detect refresh failure. statusText is implementation-dependent, empty under HTTP/2, and not a reliable success signal. Successful refreshes can throw HttpError while real failures with different statusText pass through to JSON parsing.

title: Zod SafeParse wrapper stored as credential key
body: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts assigns const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...) which returns a Zod SafeParse result { success, data/error }, then writes that wrapper object directly to prisma.credential.update data.key. The DB credential becomes { success, data } instead of tokens, so later googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) fails and calendar access breaks.

title: Minimum token schema is malformed and injects fake refresh_token
body: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts builds minimumTokenResponseSchema with computed keys like [z.string().toString()], which evaluates to a literal string such as ZodString, not a catch-all. Extra provider fields are stripped and validation is meaningless. It then mutates the result with refresh_token = "refresh_token" when missing, persisting a bogus refresh token to the database that will corrupt future refreshes.

title: Sync endpoint returns fetch Response incompatible with callers
body: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts in sharing mode returns a raw fetch Response, but callers expect provider-specific shapes: Google reads res.data, Hubspot assigns the return directly to HubspotToken and reads .expiresIn, Zoho/Bigin read .data.error. Without parsing JSON, checking response.ok, or normalizing shape, sync mode yields undefined tokens, TypeErrors, and bad DB writes. The POST also sends no Content-Type, no webhook secret, and no error handling.

title: Passes credentialId as userId to credential sync endpoint
body: packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts calls refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId) where credentialId is credential.id. The helper forwards that value as calcomUserId to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT. The external service will look up the wrong user, leaking or refreshing tokens for the wrong account.

title: Webhook lacks method check and crashes on bad payload
body: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts accepts any HTTP method and calls schema.parse, JSON.parse, and symmetricDecrypt without try/catch. Invalid bodies, malformed encrypted keys, or wrong encryption key throw uncaught exceptions resulting in 500s instead of 400s, and GET requests can hit DB/decrypt logic unintentionally.

title: Missing prisma import causes ReferenceError
body: File uses prisma.credential.update at line 96 but there is no import of @calcom/prisma in the file. Any instantiation of SalesforceCalendarService will throw ReferenceError: prisma is not defined when getClient() runs, breaking all Salesforce operations.

title: Refreshed Salesforce token never used for connection
body: getClient() fetches a new token and persists accessTokenParsed.data to the DB, but then constructs the jsforce.Connection with the old credentialKey.instance_url/accessToken/refreshToken instead of the newly parsed values. The refresh is therefore wasted and the client continues to use the expired access token.

title: Salesforce refresh checks statusText instead of ok
body: Line 86 throws only if response.statusText !== "OK". With fetch, statusText is often empty or implementation-dependent even on success, and non-2xx responses can have arbitrary text. The check should be !response.ok / status code. As written valid refreshes can throw and invalid refreshes can pass through to JSON parsing.

title: Minimum token schema uses invalid computed keys
body: minimumTokenResponseSchema is declared with [z.string().toString()] as object keys, which evaluates to a literal string like "[object Object]" instead of a catch-all. Zod does not support dynamic string keys that way. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is on, validation does not mean what the comment says and legitimate minimal {access_token, expiry} payloads can fail or pass incorrectly.

title: Dummy refresh_token placeholder corrupts stored credentials
body: If the parsed payload has no refresh_token the code injects the literal string "refresh_token" and callers persist it. Subsequent real OAuth refreshes will then send refresh_token="refresh_token" to the provider and fail, and Google/Office/Zoom code paths that merge tokenResponse.data will overwrite a valid stored refresh token with the placeholder.

title: Sync branch returns fetch Response incompatible with callers
body: When credential sync is enabled the helper returns a raw fetch Response from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT. Callers expect provider-specific shapes: Google expects {data:{access_token,expiry_date}}, HubSpot expects a HubspotToken object, Zoho/Bigin expect an axios response with .data. For example HubSpot casts the result directly to HubspotToken and reads .expiresIn, and Google reads res?.data, so the sync path yields undefined/NaN tokens and breaks refresh for those integrations.

title: Bigin passes credentialId as userId to sync endpoint
body: refreshOAuthTokens expects (fn, appSlug, userId) and sends it as calcomUserId to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT. Bigin calls it with credentialId (credential.id) instead of credential.userId. The remote endpoint receives a credential ID where it expects a user ID, causing wrong-user lookups and leaking/mixing tokens across users.

title: Webhook has no method check and unhandled validation errors
body: Handler accepts any HTTP method and calls appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse without try/catch. Invalid bodies throw a ZodError that becomes an unhandled 500 instead of a 400, and GET/DELETE can create/update credentials. Also symmetricDecrypt/JSON.parse can throw unhandled. The endpoint should restrict to POST and return 400 on validation/decryption failure.

title: Team admin/owner check requires both instead of either
body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as `await isTeamAdmin(...) && await isTeamOwner(...)`. A team admin who is not also an owner (the normal case) will fail this check and be denied, while the intent is admin OR owner. The consequence is legitimate team admins cannot add guests; only owners who are also admins (or organizers/attendees via the other clauses) pass. Change && to ||.

title: Guest dedup and blacklist bypass via case/whitespace
body: uniqueGuests filters with `guest === attendee.email` and `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` but only the blacklist list is lowercased — the incoming guest is not normalized (no trim/toLowerCase). An existing attendee `Foo@x.com` can be re-added as `foo@x.com`, and a blacklisted `spam@x.com` can be bypassed as `Spam@X.com` or with whitespace. This creates duplicate Attendee rows differing only by case and defeats BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.

title: Email routing uses unfiltered guest list
body: Attendees are created from `uniqueGuests` (duplicates/existing/blacklisted filtered out) but `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is called with the original `guests` input. In packages/emails/email-manager.ts new vs existing is decided by `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`, so a pre-existing attendee re-submitted in the request will be misclassified as new and receive AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, and case differences break the match. Pass `uniqueGuests`.

title: Unbounded guests array with no dedup limit
body: Schema is `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no min/max length, no uniqueness refinement, and no trimming/normalization. A caller can submit hundreds/thousands of emails in one request, creating that many Attendee rows, calendar updates, and outbound emails. The duplicate-within-request case is also not rejected server-side, risking unique-constraint errors or duplicate attendees. Add max length, nonempty, uniqueness and normalization.

title: No booking status/time guard before adding guests
body: Handler only checks NOT_FOUND then permission, never checks booking.status or startTime/endTime. Guests can therefore be added to CANCELLED/REJECTED or already-ended bookings, which then triggers calendar updates and confirmation ICS emails for a dead event. The UI also exposes Edit > Additional guests for past confirmed bookings. Reject non-ACCEPTED/past bookings server-side and hide the action in BookingListItem.

title: Team permission check requires admin AND owner instead of OR
body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...)). A team admin who is not an owner (and vice-versa) will fail the check and get FORBIDDEN, while the intent and the variable name is admin-or-owner. The operator should be ||. Consequence: legitimate team admins are denied adding guests; the only team users who pass are those satisfying both predicates.

title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive and miss intra-request duplicates
body: blacklistedGuestEmails are lowercased but compared with !blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) without lowercasing guest, so Blacklisted@Example.com bypasses the blocklist. The same filter compares guest === attendee.email case-sensitively and never de-duplicates guests against each other, while the server schema in addGuests.schema.ts does not enforce uniqueness. Consequence: blocked addresses can be added by changing case, and one request can create duplicate Attendee rows.

title: Email routing uses unfiltered guests list instead of actually-added guests
body: Handler filters to uniqueGuests for the DB insert but calls sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) with the original input. sendAddGuestsEmails in email-manager.ts uses newGuests.includes(attendee.email) to decide between AttendeeScheduledEmail (new guest) and AttendeeAddGuestsEmail (existing). Consequence: an address that was filtered out because it already attended is still classified as new and gets the wrong full scheduled invite, and case variants/blacklisted entries misroute notifications.

title: Validation error flag never cleared on valid retry
body: handleAdd sets setIsInvalidEmail(true) on failed safeParse but never sets it back to false when validation later succeeds; it is only cleared on cancel. Consequence: after one invalid attempt the 'Emails must be unique and valid' banner stays visible even after the user fixes the addresses and successfully submits.

title: Team permission check uses AND instead of OR
body: In addGuests.handler.ts the isTeamAdminOrOwner flag is computed as (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...)). This requires the caller to be both admin AND owner at the same time, so a team admin who is not an owner (and vice versa) is denied. Combined with the later FORBIDDEN check, legitimate team admins/owners cannot add guests unless they are also organizer/attendee. It should be OR.

title: Duplicate/blacklist checks are case-sensitive and bypassable
body: uniqueGuests is filtered with guest === attendee.email and blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest), but only the blacklist is lowercased. An existing attendee Guest@x.com can be re-added as guest@x.com, and a blacklisted address can bypass by case. Server schema also does not normalize email case, so duplicate Attendee rows with different case can be created.

title: Wrong guest list passed to email sender misclassifies attendees
body: Handler computes uniqueGuests (deduplicated against existing attendees and blacklist) for DB insert, but calls sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) with the raw input. In email-manager.ts sendAddGuestsEmails decides new vs existing by newGuests.includes(attendee.email). An already-existing attendee re-submitted in guests will therefore receive the new-guest AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, and filtered/blacklisted addresses affect classification. Pass uniqueGuests.

title: No booking status check allows adding guests to cancelled/past/rejected bookings
body: Handler only checks booking existence, then inserts new Attendee rows and calls eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees and sends emails. There is no guard for status CANCELLED/REJECTED or endTime in the past. Adding attendees to a cancelled or finished meeting corrupts data, updates calendars incorrectly, and sends confusing invites. Reject non-ACCEPTED/PENDING or past bookings.

title: Server schema allows duplicate and unbounded guest lists
body: ZAddGuestsInputSchema is z.array(z.string().email()) with no uniqueness refinement, min/max, or normalization, while the client dialog enforces uniqueness. A direct API call can submit ["a@x.com","a@x.com"] causing duplicate Attendee creates (or DB unique errors) and can submit an arbitrarily large array, spamming calendar/email updates. Enforce unique, lowercase, and a reasonable max length server-side.

title: Validation error flag is never cleared on valid input
body: handleAdd sets isInvalidEmail(true) on failed safeParse but never sets it back to false when validation succeeds. Once shown, the emails_must_be_unique_valid error persists even after the user fixes the emails and on subsequent opens until Cancel, confusing users. Reset the flag on successful validation/change.

title: DB write not atomic with calendar update, leaves partial state on failure
body: Attendees are persisted via prisma.booking.update createMany before eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees. If the calendar update throws, the DB already contains the new guests but calendars/emails are not updated, with no rollback or compensation. Wrap in a transaction-safe order or clean up / surface the failure instead of diverging sources of truth.

title: Retry-count delete filter deletes non-SMS reminders
body: The deleteMany uses OR with a second branch of only retryCount gt 1 with no method: SMS constraint (lines 29-45). Once any WorkflowReminder of any method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) has retryCount > 1 it will be deleted by this SMS cron job, even if it is scheduled for the future and unrelated to SMS. This is data loss beyond the intended SMS cleanup; the retryCount branch must also be scoped to method SMS (and likely scheduled: false).

title: Non-atomic retryCount increment loses retries
body: Both failure paths update with data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 } using the value read at the start of the cron run (lines 184 and 195) instead of an atomic increment. If two cron invocations or overlapping executions process the same reminder, one increment overwrites the other, so failures are under-counted and bad numbers are retried forever. Use increment: 1.

title: Missing sendTo/message never increments retryCount, retries forever
body: RetryCount is only incremented when twilio.scheduleSMS returns falsy or throws, inside if (message?.length && sendTo). When sendTo is missing (e.g. invalid/missing phone number) or message is empty, the loop does nothing and leaves the reminder unscheduled with unchanged retryCount. That reminder will be re-fetched on every cron run forever, which is exactly the infinite-rescheduling problem the PR claims to fix for invalid numbers.

title: retryCount cleanup deletes EMAIL/WHATSAPP reminders
body: The deleteMany OR's second branch is { retryCount: { gt: 1 } } with no method filter, so any WorkflowReminder of any method with retryCount > 1 is deleted. Only SMS reminders ever get retryCount incremented by this cron, but EMAIL/WHATSAPP rows share the table and default, and any future/other writer setting retryCount will cause cross-method data loss. Scope the branch to method SMS, e.g. AND method SMS with retryCount > 1.

title: Non-atomic retryCount increment can lose retries
body: Both failure paths do data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 } using the value read earlier in findMany. Concurrent cron executions or overlapping runs will both read the same value and write back the same increment, losing one retry and delaying deletion indefinitely for persistently failing numbers. Use atomic increment: data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } }.

title: Missing sendTo/empty message never retried or cleaned up
body: When message is empty or sendTo is falsy (e.g. invalid/missing phone number, the exact case in the PR description) the code falls through the if without any prisma update. retryCount is never incremented so the reminder is refetched on every cron run until its scheduledDate passes, defeating the retry-limit. Increment retryCount or delete in that no-op path as well.

title: retryCount cleanup deletes non-SMS reminders
body: File packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts line 39: the deleteMany OR second branch is { retryCount: { gt: 1 } } with no method filter, while the first branch is scoped to method SMS. As written any WorkflowReminder of any method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) with retryCount > 1 will be deleted, even though retryCount is only maintained by this SMS cron. This causes unintended data loss for other channels; the condition should also require method SMS (and likely scheduled:false).

title: Non-atomic retryCount increment loses retries
body: File packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts line 184 (repeated line 195): retry is recorded as data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 } using the value read earlier in findMany. If the cron overlaps or two instances run concurrently, both read the same value and write the same incremented value, losing one retry and delaying deletion forever. Use atomic data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } } instead.

title: Missing message/sendTo path never increments retryCount
body: File packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts line 158: retryCount is only incremented inside if (message?.length && sendTo) else-branch or on thrown exception. When sendTo is missing (e.g. no smsReminderNumber) or message is empty, the loop does nothing and leaves the reminder with scheduled:false and unchanged retryCount. That reminder will be refetched on every cron run until scheduledDate, defeating the PR goal of stopping infinite retries for invalid/missing numbers; it needs an else that increments or deletes.

title: Public findMany method removed without updating callers
body: The diff deletes InsightsBookingService.findMany (which executed bookingTimeStatusDenormalized.findMany with auth+filter AND) and replaces it with getBaseConditions returning Prisma.Sql. Only two files are changed, so any existing caller still importing/calling findMany will fail to compile or throw at runtime. Removing a public service method is a breaking API change and requires migrating all call sites to $queryRaw with the new conditions.

title: OR fragments built without outer parentheses cause precedence bugs
body: buildFilterConditions builds `("eventTypeId" = X) OR ("eventParentId" = X)` with no surrounding parens, and buildOrgAuthorizationCondition/buildTeamAuthorizationCondition build `(${acc}) OR (${condition})` with no outer parens. getBaseConditions only wraps when both auth and filter exist. If a caller uses the fragment directly as `WHERE ${auth} AND <extra>` or `WHERE ${filter} AND <extra>`, SQL AND binds tighter than OR, so e.g. `a AND b OR c AND d AND e` evaluates as `(a AND b) OR ((c AND d) AND e)` instead of the intended `((a AND b) OR (c AND d)) AND e`, leaking or hiding rows. Fragments containing OR must be parenthesized at construction.

title: Public findMany() removed without updating callers
body: insightsBooking.ts replaces the public findMany(findManyArgs) method that applied authorization and filter conditions via Prisma findMany with getBaseConditions() returning Prisma.Sql. The diff shows no other files updated and no compatibility shim. Any existing caller importing InsightsBookingService and calling findMany will fail to compile or throw at runtime, breaking the insights booking API contract.

title: OR fragments returned without outer parentheses enable precedence bypass
body: buildOrgAuthorizationCondition, buildTeamAuthorizationCondition, and buildFilterConditions return fragments like A AND B OR C AND D and A OR B with no surrounding parentheses. The class exposes them publicly via getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions. If any consumer composes them as WHERE ${auth} AND <extra> then SQL precedence (AND binds tighter than OR) evaluates as A OR (C AND <extra>), so rows matching the first disjunct bypass the extra predicate. getBaseConditions wraps them today, but the public fragments are unsafe to compose. Wrap OR-joined fragments in parentheses at construction.

title: Caching coverage deleted
body: The test file deletes the entire Caching describe block that verified getAuthorizationConditions and getFilterConditions are cached. The service in insightsBooking.ts still implements cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions. Removing the tests leaves stale-cache or mutation bugs undetected with no replacement coverage.

title: Breaking removal of findMany without updating callers
body: The diff deletes InsightsBookingService.findMany (the Prisma BookingTimeStatusDenormalized findMany wrapper that merged auth/filter conditions) and replaces it with getBaseConditions returning Prisma.Sql. Only two files are changed in this PR, so any existing caller that imports InsightsBookingService and calls findMany will fail to compile at TypeScript time or throw TypeError: service.findMany is not a function at runtime. A service conversion must either keep findMany as a compatibility wrapper or migrate all call sites in the same PR.

title: Org-scope test assumes deterministic DB ordering
body: The org-scope authorization test asserts teamIds equal [org.id, team.id, team2.id, team3.id] and userIds equal [user.id, user2.id, user3.id] via toEqual on Prisma.sql. The service builds those arrays from TeamRepository.findAllByParentId and MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds with no orderBy, so Postgres return order is undefined. The test will be flaky and can fail even when authorization logic is correct, and it masks real ordering-independent correctness. Order results before comparing or compare as sets.

title: Delete-cache success never refreshes cache status
body: deleteCacheMutation onSuccess in CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx only shows a toast and calls onSuccess?.(), unlike disconnectMutation which invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars and viewer.apps.integrations in onSettled. The connectedCalendars query provides cacheUpdatedAt, so after deleting the cache the dropdown will keep showing the old Last updated timestamp until a manual refetch. Invalidate the connectedCalendars query on delete success/settled.

title: Cache status includes expired rows
body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds() in calendar-cache.repository.ts groups all CalendarCache rows by credentialId with no expiresAt filter, while getCachedAvailability() explicitly ignores rows with expiresAt < now. The UI therefore shows Cache Status / Last updated even when every cache row is expired and will never be used, and deleting only expired data looks broken. Filter to expiresAt >= now, consistent with reads.

title: Empty updateMany to bump updatedAt is wasteful and may fail
body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache() in CalendarService.ts calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) after every cache population. Passing empty data relies on implicit @updatedAt handling that Prisma updateMany with {} does not guarantee and can reject as empty data, and on success it rewrites every SelectedCalendar row for the credential on every cache refresh just to touch a timestamp the frontend does not even read (frontend uses CalendarCache.updatedAt). Remove this write or set an explicit field.

title: Throws generic Error instead of TRPCError
body: deleteCacheHandler in deleteCache.handler.ts throws new Error("Credential not found or access denied") when the credential does not belong to the caller. A plain Error surfaces as an internal server error instead of NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN, leaking no useful status to the client and conflating not-found with forbidden. Throw a TRPCError with the appropriate code.

title: Unfiltered credentialIds passed to cache status query
body: connectedCalendars.handler.ts builds credentialIds by mapping every connectedCalendar without filtering null/undefined values or non-Google credentials and calls getCacheStatusByCredentialIds() unconditionally, even when the list is empty. Null credentialIds will fail Prisma validation for an Int filter, and the query runs for Outlook and other integrations that never have CalendarCache rows. Filter to defined Google credentialIds and skip the query when empty.

title: BSD-only sed breaks on Linux
body: test-gcal-webhooks.sh uses sed -i '' -E to rewrite GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL. The empty backup-suffix form is BSD/macOS syntax; GNU sed on Linux treats '' as a script and fails, so the helper script cannot update the env file on Linux. Use a portable sed invocation or a non-sed rewrite.

title: Cache timestamp hardcoded to en-US
body: CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx formats cacheUpdatedAt with new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...) regardless of the user's locale from useLocale(). Users in other locales see a foreign date format for Last updated. Pass the active locale to the formatter.

title: updateManyByCredentialId called with empty data will throw
body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}). Prisma updateMany requires at least one field to update; an empty data object throws a validation error. This runs after every successful cache population, so watching/subscribing a calendar will fail after the cache write. If the intent is to bump updatedAt, pass { updatedAt: new Date() } explicitly.

title: Unfiltered credentialIds can break cache status query
body: credentialIds is built as connectedCalendars.map((cal) => cal.credentialId) with no filtering. Delegation or in-memory credentials can have undefined/null/negative credentialIds, and a user with no calendars yields an empty array. Passing those values to prisma.calendarCache.groupBy where credentialId: { in: credentialIds } can throw or return wrong results, breaking the whole connectedCalendars query. Filter to finite positive numbers and early-return when empty.

title: Cache status includes expired cache rows
body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups all CalendarCache rows by credentialId with no expiresAt filter, while getCachedAvailability only honors rows with expiresAt >= now. After expiry the UI will still show a Last updated timestamp and offer Delete cached data for data that will never be used. Add the same expiresAt: { gte: new Date() } filter used elsewhere.

title: Cache delete never refreshes cache status UI
body: deleteCacheMutation onSuccess only shows a toast and calls onSuccess, but unlike disconnectMutation it never invalidates trpc.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. The cacheUpdatedAt timestamp fetched by connectedCalendarsHandler therefore stays stale after deletion and the dropdown still shows the old Last updated time until a manual reload.

title: Helper script uses macOS-only sed and fragile relative path
body: The script writes with ENV_FILE="../.env" relative to the current working directory, so running from anywhere except scripts/ clobbers the wrong file. It also uses sed -i '' -E which only works on macOS BSD sed and fails on Linux/GNU sed. Committing it as-is breaks Linux developers and CI.

title: Empty update data throws and doesn't bump updatedAt
body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) with empty data. Prisma updateMany rejects empty data with a validation error, so this line will throw and break cache warm-up. Even if it did not throw, updateMany does not auto-touch @updatedAt, so an empty update would never change updatedAt. Pass an explicit timestamp like { updatedAt: new Date() }.

title: Delete-cache success never refreshes cache status
body: deleteCacheMutation onSuccess only shows a toast and calls onSuccess?.(). Unlike disconnectMutation it never invalidates trpc.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars, so after deleting the cache the dropdown still shows the old cacheUpdatedAt until a full page reload. Invalidate the connectedCalendars query on settle/success.

title: Cache status includes expired rows
body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups all CalendarCache rows by credentialId with no expiresAt filter, while getCachedAvailability only honors rows with expiresAt >= now. The UI will therefore show Last updated for credentials whose cache is entirely expired and unusable. Add the same expiresAt: { gte: new Date() } filter.

title: Unfiltered credentialIds passed to cache query
body: credentialIds is built as connectedCalendars.map((cal) => cal.credentialId) with no filtering/dedup. If the list is empty or contains null/undefined (e.g. delegation-credential entries without a DB credentialId), prisma.calendarCache.groupBy with credentialId: { in: [...] } receives invalid values and throws, failing the whole connectedCalendars query. Filter to finite numbers and dedupe before calling.

title: Helper script is macOS-only and writes wrong .env
body: ENV_FILE is set to ../.env so running the script from the repo root edits the parent directory instead of the repo .env, and sed -i '' -E is BSD/macOS syntax that fails on GNU/Linux. The script also silently rewrites GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL in the env file. Fix the path resolution and make the sed invocation portable or document it as macOS-only.

title: Paid-booking early return skips workflow-reminder cancellation
body: In handleCancelBooking.ts the paid-booking branch refunds, updates status to REJECTED and returns at req.statusCode = 200 before reaching the workflow-reminder cancellation block at line 485. A cancelled paid booking therefore never marks email reminders cancelled nor cancels/deletes SMS reminders, so scheduled SendGrid/Twilio reminders for that booking will still be sent.

title: immediateDelete cancels SendGrid but leaves WorkflowReminder row
body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder with immediateDelete=true does the SendGrid POST cancel and then returns without deleting or marking the WorkflowReminder row. Callers for reschedule and workflow/step delete rely on this to clean up the old booking, so the DB row stays scheduled=true forever (until the past-date sweeper deletes it). It is an orphan leak and inconsistent with the SMS path which deletes the row.

title: One SendGrid failure aborts all pending email cancellations
body: The cron loops remindersToCancel with await client.request inside a single try/catch. If any batch_id is null, already sent, or SendGrid errors, the exception jumps to the catch, skips Promise.all for already-queued deletes and skips all remaining reminders. One bad reminder therefore prevents cancellation of all later reminders, so cancelled/rescheduled emails will still be sent.

title: Past-due sweep deletes DB rows without cancelling SendGrid
body: The handler first does deleteMany where scheduledDate <= now for EMAIL reminders without calling SendGrid cancel. A reminder marked cancelled=true whose scheduledDate passes before the 1-hour cancel window runs (cron downtime, delay, or clock skew) will be deleted from the database but the SendGrid scheduled send remains live, so the email for a cancelled/rescheduled booking will still be delivered.

title: Reschedule reminder cancellations are fire-and-forget
body: originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach calls async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder without awaiting. The surrounding try/catch cannot catch async rejections and the handler continues to reschedule and return. Cancellations may not complete, fail silently, or race with new reminder creation, leaving old reminders to still send.

title: Cancel-booking reminder cancellations are not awaited
body: updatedBookings.forEach with nested workflowReminders.forEach invokes async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder without awaiting or collecting promises. Failures are unobserved and the API can return success before SendGrid/Twilio cancellation or the cancelled=true update has happened, making cancellation unreliable under load or on process exit.

title: Single SendGrid failure aborts all cancellations and skips DB deletes
body: In scheduleEmailReminders.ts the loop awaits client.request for each reminderToCancel sequentially and only collects prisma.workflowReminder.delete promises to run in Promise.all after the loop. If any one cancel request throws (e.g. null referenceId, expired batch_id, network error), control jumps to the outer catch, Promise.all is never reached, and even reminders already cancelled at SendGrid are never deleted from the DB. They will be retried every 15 min and other pending cancellations in the same batch are starved, so cancelled/rescheduled emails can still be sent.

title: immediateDelete cancels SendGrid but never removes DB row
body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder with immediateDelete=true sends POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends cancel and then returns without deleting or updating the WorkflowReminder row. Callers in handleNewBooking.ts reschedule path and workflows.tsx delete-workflow/delete-step paths pass true expecting the reminder to disappear. The row stays with scheduled=true and referenceId set, leaking indefinitely and never matching the cron cancelled=true cleanup, so DB accumulates orphans pointing at old bookings.
