title: Unscheduled-reminder query ignores cancelled flag
body: The cron finds unscheduled email reminders with method=EMAIL, scheduled=false, scheduledDate within 72h but with no filter on cancelled. Any reminder marked cancelled=true that is still unscheduled (or becomes cancelled between marking and scheduling) will be picked up and scheduled/sent via SendGrid. The fix relies on cancelled to suppress sends, so the schedule query must exclude cancelled=true, otherwise cancelled/rescheduled bookings still get emails.

title: Async reminder cancellations fired in forEach without await
body: handleCancelBooking.ts, bookings.tsx requestReschedule, and handleNewBooking.ts reschedule all call deleteScheduledEmailReminder / deleteScheduledSMSReminder (async DB update + network) inside Array.forEach without awaiting or Promise.all. The handler returns success before the prisma update cancelled=true completes, errors become unhandled rejections, and on process reuse or failure the cancellation can be lost so the 15-min cron never sees cancelled=true and the email is still sent.

title: Cancelled unscheduled reminders are still scheduled and sent
body: The unscheduledReminders query filters on method=EMAIL, scheduled=false and scheduledDate<=now+72h but does not exclude cancelled=true. A BEFORE_EVENT reminder that was marked cancelled=true while still unscheduled (scheduled=false, referenceId=null) therefore remains eligible for scheduling in the same cron run and will be sent via SendGrid with a new batchId, defeating the cancellation for cancelled/rescheduled bookings.

title: immediateDelete cancels SendGrid but leaks the DB row
body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder with immediateDelete=true performs the POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends cancel and then returns without deleting or updating the WorkflowReminder row. Callers in handleNewBooking reschedule and workflows delete/update rely on this to remove the old reminder. The row stays scheduled=true with a now-cancelled batchId forever (until the past-date sweeper), leaving stale state and diverging from deleteScheduledSMSReminder which does delete the row.

title: Cancellation sweeper missing method/scheduled/reference filters and aborts batch on error
body: remindersToCancel selects any row with cancelled=true and scheduledDate<=now+1h, without restricting to method=EMAIL, scheduled=true, or referenceId NOT NULL. SMS/unscheduled rows would be sent to SendGrid with a null batch_id, and a single SendGrid failure throws out of the for-loop so remaining reminders are never cancelled and already-queued Prisma deletes after the loop are never awaited. Per-reminder error handling and precise filters are required.

title: Async reminder cancellations fire-and-forget via forEach
body: updatedBookings.forEach calls async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder without awaiting or collecting promises, same pattern in handleNewBooking, bookings.tsx requestReschedule, and workflows.tsx. The handler can return and finish the request before the prisma update to cancelled=true or the Twilio/SendGrid cancel completes, so cancellations can be lost and rejections are unobserved. Use Promise.all over mapped promises.

title: Async deletion in forEach is never awaited
body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {... await getCalendar ...}) launches an async callback whose returned promise is discarded by forEach. The function then sends the reschedule email and returns true without waiting for calendar.deleteEvent / deleteMeeting to finish, and the surrounding try/catch cannot catch rejections from the async callback. Consequence: calendar/video events may never be deleted or failures are silently lost as unhandled rejections while the booking is already marked rescheduled.

title: Async deletion in forEach is never awaited
body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {... await getCalendar ...}) discards the promise returned by each async iteration. The code proceeds to send email and return without awaiting deletions, and errors inside the callback bypass the enclosing try/catch. Consequence: old calendar/video events can be orphaned and deletion errors become unhandled rejections.

title: Async calendar/video cancellation in forEach is fire-and-forget
body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {... await getCalendar ... calendar?.deleteEvent ...}) does not await the per-booking deletions. The mutation continues to send the reschedule email and webhooks immediately. Consequence: the previous slot may not be freed before the user reschedules, failures are unobserved, and rejections escape error handling.

title: Recurring-cancel apiDeletes populated from unawaited forEach
body: For recurring cancellation the code does bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... apiDeletes.push(await calendar?.deleteEvent(...)); }). Because forEach does not await the async callbacks, the later await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) can run while apiDeletes is still empty. Adding await getCalendar moves the push even later, worsening the race. Consequence: recurring bookings are marked CANCELLED in the DB while external calendar events are never deleted.

title: Async forEach pushes to apiDeletes after it is awaited
body: In handleCancelBooking.ts the recurring-cancel path does `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })`. Because forEach does not await async callbacks, the outer flow continues and later does `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` before the callbacks have finished awaiting getCalendar and pushing. The result is calendar deleteEvent promises are never awaited and may never be observed, so recurring cancellations can leave orphan events on external calendars and swallow errors.

title: Async forEach makes calendar/video deletes fire-and-forget and uncaught
body: In vital/lib/reschedule.ts `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... })` is not awaited and the surrounding try/catch cannot catch rejections from an async forEach callback. The function then sends reschedule email and returns true without waiting for deleteEvent/deleteMeeting to finish, so failures become unhandled rejections and old calendar/video events may not be deleted before return.

title: Async forEach makes calendar/video deletes fire-and-forget and uncaught
body: In wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... })` is not awaited and the surrounding try/catch cannot catch rejections from an async forEach callback. The function then sends reschedule email and returns true without waiting for deleteEvent/deleteMeeting to finish, so failures become unhandled rejections and old calendar/video events may not be deleted before return.

title: Async forEach for reschedule deletes is never awaited
body: In bookings.tsx requestReschedule does `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })` with no await, Promise.all, or return of the promises. The mutation therefore finishes, sends reschedule email and webhooks without waiting for external calendar/video deletions, and any rejection inside the callback is unhandled and invisible to the caller.

title: Async forEach is fire-and-forget, calendar/video deletions never awaited
body: File packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts line 125 uses bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...await getCalendar...}). forEach does not await async callbacks, so Reschedule returns true and sends the reschedule email before deleteEvent/deleteMeeting complete, rejections become unhandled, and the surrounding try/catch cannot catch them because the promises escape the try block.

title: Async forEach is fire-and-forget, calendar/video deletions never awaited
body: File packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts line 125 uses bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...await getCalendar...}). forEach does not await async callbacks, so the function returns before deleteEvent/deleteMeeting finish, errors are unhandled, and the surrounding try/catch is ineffective for the now-async getCalendar/delete calls.

title: Async forEach leaves calendar/video cleanup unawaited on reschedule
body: File packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx line 553 uses bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...await getCalendar... return calendar?.deleteEvent...}). The returned promises are discarded, so old calendar events and video meetings may never be deleted before the response/emails proceed, and any rejection from the dynamic import or deleteEvent is unhandled.

title: Async forEach pushes to apiDeletes after it is already awaited, losing recurring cancellations
body: File packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts around line 458 does bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); }). Because the callback awaits before pushing, the outer flow reaches await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) before the pushes happen. Recurring-booking calendar deletions are therefore lost and old events remain on external calendars while the booking is marked CANCELLED.

title: Dayjs objects compared with === always false
body: In checkIfIsAvailable the code tests `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` to detect an empty/full-day-block override. `dayjs()` returns a new object every call, so `===` compares object identity and is never true. The intended unavailable-day case is therefore never detected, and a date override meant to block the whole day falls through to the `dateOverrideExist` path and can incorrectly return available.

title: Working-hours end check uses slot start instead of slot end
body: In checkIfIsAvailable both `start` and `end` are computed from `slotStartTime.hour()*60+slotStartTime.minute()`. `end` never adds `eventLength` (unlike `slotEndTime` computed above). A slot starting inside working hours but ending outside is therefore accepted. Combined with the fixed-host filter added by this PR, this allows bookings that overrun working hours and date-override boundaries.

title: Availability re-check uses UTC day/time instead of organizer timezone
body: checkIfIsAvailable converts the slot to UTC (`slotStartTime = time.utc()`) and then tests `workingHour.days.includes(slotStartTime.day())` and `slotStartTime.hour()/minute()` against per-user `workingHours`, and matches date overrides after an inverted `utcOffset` adjustment (`utcOffset()* -1` then `add`). Working hours and date-override days are defined in the organizer/schedule timezone, not UTC. Near midnight and across timezones the UTC day/hour differs from the organizer-local day/hour, so slots are accepted/rejected on the wrong day and the claimed timezone fix does not hold. It also means a fixed host with no working hours that day matches nothing in `find` and falls through to the busy check returning true, leaving round-robin slots bookable when the fixed host is unavailable.

title: Date-override day matching and time shift drops day overflow
body: getSlots selects `activeOverrides` with `dayjs.utc(override.start).isBetween(startOfInviteeDay, startOfInviteeDay.endOf('day'))` where `startOfInviteeDay` is midnight in the invitee timezone, mixing a UTC instant with a zoned day boundary so overrides are attributed to the wrong invitee day. The subsequent offset correction only keeps `hour()*60+minute()` after shifting, discarding any day carry. An override that shifts to the previous/next day in the invitee timezone is therefore rendered on the wrong day or with wrapped hours, and multi-day/cross-midnight overrides are clipped.

title: Dayjs objects compared with === is always false
body: In checkIfIsAvailable the code does `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` to detect a zero-length/unavailable date override. These are two distinct Dayjs objects, so === is always false. As a result a full-day block override is never recognized and slots on a day the fixed host marked unavailable will still be returned as available, allowing booking when no fixed host is free.

title: Working-hours check ignores event length
body: In checkIfIsAvailable both `start` and `end` are computed from `slotStartTime.hour()*60+slotStartTime.minute()`. The slot end (start + eventLength) is never used, so a slot that starts inside working hours but ends after workingHours.endTime is treated as available. This re-introduces bookable slots past the end of availability for fixed/loose host filtering.

title: Working-hours exclusion uses ANY instead of ALL logic
body: The code does `workingHours.find(wh => slot outside wh)` and returns unavailable if any entry matches. With split working hours, multiple intervals, or aggregated collective hours, a slot inside one valid interval is still outside another interval, so find succeeds and the slot is wrongly rejected. The correct check is that the slot is inside at least one applicable interval; otherwise valid fixed-host slots disappear.

title: Date-override timezone shift drops day overflow
body: Overrides are converted to `hour()*60+minute` after applying the organizer-to-invitee offset, discarding the date. If the offset pushes the override past midnight, the minutes wrap (e.g. 23:30 + 60min becomes 00:30) but are still applied to the original invitee day, and the activeOverrides filter only tests the override start instant against the invitee day. Overrides near midnight or with large organizer/invitee offsets are therefore applied to the wrong day or truncated.

title: Date-override day/range comparison mixes shifted and unshifted times
body: checkIfIsAvailable computes `utcOffset = dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1` then compares `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset).format('YYYY MM DD')` to `slotStartTime.format('YYYY MM DD')` where slotStartTime is UTC. Shifting the override instant by the negated offset before comparing to an unshifted UTC slot corrupts both the day match and the start/end range checks whenever the organizer timezone is not UTC, so overrides are matched to the wrong day or judged with wrong boundaries.

title: Dayjs objects compared with === never match
body: In checkIfIsAvailable the zero-length/unavailable override branch does `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)`. Dayjs instances are objects so === is always false. The intended all-day-blocked override case is therefore dead code and such overrides fall through to the generic inside/outside logic instead of returning unavailable.

title: Working-hours check rejects valid slots and accepts days with no hours
body: The added workingHours guard uses `workingHours.find(...)` where the predicate returns true when the slot is outside that single entry. With multiple entries for the same weekday (split hours) one matching entry and one non-matching entry makes find() truthy, so a slot inside valid hours is rejected. Conversely if no workingHours entry contains slotStartTime.day(), find() returns undefined and the slot falls through to the busy check and is treated as available, so days with no working hours become bookable.

title: Date overrides filtered by start only and reduced to time-of-day
body: In getSlots activeOverrides only tests `override.start` against the invitee day range and then converts overrides to `startTime/endTime` minutes from `hour()*60+minute()`, discarding the day. An override that starts on another calendar day in the invitee timezone but spills into this day, or one whose timezone shift pushes it across midnight, is either ignored for this day or wraps to start>end / truncated minutes, producing wrong or no slots for invitee timezones far from the organizer.

title: Override offset uses string parsing inconsistent with time math
body: Offset is computed from `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(...).utcOffset()` while times are computed from `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset)`. toString() renders in server-local format and re-parsing it before applying tz is locale/DST fragile and inconsistent with the second computation, so organizer-to-invitee shift can be off by the server offset or DST difference.

title: before_validation crashes on blank host
body: In app/models/embeddable_host.rb the before_validation block calls self.host.sub! unconditionally. If host is nil or blank (e.g. admin submits empty host), this raises NoMethodError instead of failing validation. The record can never report a clean validation error and the request 500s.

title: update/destroy 500 on missing id instead of 404
body: In app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb update does EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first then save_host(host) without checking for nil, and destroy calls host.destroy without checking. A bad/stale id causes NoMethodError on nil (undefined method `host=' or `destroy') resulting in a 500 instead of a 404 / not-found error.

title: case-insensitive host lookup not lowercased
body: In app/models/embeddable_host.rb record_for_host does where("lower(host) = ?", host) where host is uri.host verbatim. If either the stored value or the lookup URL contains uppercase, lower(host) = 'EVILtrout.COM' never matches. The query must downcase the parameter (host.downcase) to actually be case-insensitive, otherwise host_allowed? incorrectly rejects valid referers.

title: SQL injection via string-interpolated host in migration
body: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the data migration builds INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...) by interpolating the old site_setting value directly. A host containing a quote breaks out of the literal and allows SQL injection / migration failure. It must use quoting/parameterization or sanitize.

title: migration assumes rows exist and crashes on fresh DB
body: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb category_id is derived via execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i without checking for empty results. On a fresh install or DB without embed_category / uncategorized_category_id rows, [0] is nil and the migration raises NoMethodError and cannot migrate. The same applies to the uncategorized fallback lookup.

title: _hydrateEmbedded assumes plural ids are always arrays
body: In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6 _hydrateEmbedded now handles xxx_ids by calling obj[k].map directly. If the payload has null, undefined, or a non-array for a plural id key, this throws TypeError and breaks hydration of the whole record. It also leaves undefined entries in the hydrated array when _lookupSubType misses, instead of filtering them.

title: no uniqueness constraint on host allows duplicates
body: In app/models/embeddable_host.rb there is no validates_uniqueness_of :host (case-insensitive) and db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb creates the table without a unique index. Duplicate hosts can be created via the admin UI, making record_for_host (.first) ambiguous and allowing inconsistent category mappings.

title: Migration interpolates host directly into SQL
body: File db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb line 25 builds INSERT with VALUES ('#{h}', ...) where h comes from the site_settings value. A host containing a single quote, backslash or SQL breaks out of the string literal and allows SQL injection / migration failure. Values from the database must be quoted with connection.quote or inserted via ActiveRecord, not string interpolation.

title: Migration crashes when settings rows are missing
body: File db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb lines 9-16 do execute(...)[0]['id'] and execute(...)[0]['value'] without checking for empty results. On a fresh database or where embed_category / uncategorized_category_id rows are absent, [0] is nil and calling ['id'] raises NoMethodError, failing the whole migration. It also calls .to_i on nil-derived values and uses cmd_tuples which is Postgres-specific.

title: Update/destroy dereference nil when host not found
body: File app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb lines 10 and 15 do EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and then immediately call save_host(host) or host.destroy. If the id does not exist, host is nil, so save_host calls nil.host= and destroy calls nil.destroy, raising NoMethodError and returning 500 instead of 404. An attacker or stale admin UI can trigger it.

title: before_validation crashes on nil host
body: File app/models/embeddable_host.rb lines 5-8 call self.host.sub! twice unconditionally. If host is nil (blank form submission, API call without host param), this raises NoMethodError: undefined method sub! for nil instead of failing validation cleanly. Guard for blank host before stripping scheme/path.

title: Hosts with ports never match
body: File app/models/embeddable_host.rb: before_validation keeps the port (only strips scheme and path) so example.com:8080 is stored with port, but record_for_host extracts URI#host which strips the port and queries lower(host) = ? with the bare hostname. A stored host with a port will therefore never be found by host_allowed?, breaking embedding on non-standard ports. Normalize consistently and downcase the lookup value for the case-insensitive query.

title: Embedded _ids array handling crashes on null
body: File app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6 line 198 does obj[k].map(...) when the key ends in _ids. If the server returns null for that key (e.g. color_ids: null), calling map on null throws TypeError and breaks hydration of the whole record. Must guard for null/non-array before mapping.

title: Migration SQL injection via embeddable host value
body: The migration interpolates raw site-setting values directly into SQL: execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)". A stored host containing a single quote breaks the statement or allows SQL injection. An admin-controlled setting should never be string-interpolated into SQL; use quoting/sanitization or ActiveRecord creates.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category setting is missing/blank
body: The migration does execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name='embed_category'")[0]['id']. If the setting row is missing, blank, or does not match a category name, [0] is nil and ['id'] raises, aborting the migration for all installs. It must handle zero rows and fall back to uncategorized_category_id.

title: before_validation crashes on nil host
body: app/models/embeddable_host.rb calls self.host.sub! twice without a nil guard. Creating/updating an EmbeddableHost with a missing host raises NoMethodError instead of a validation error, turning a 422 into a 500.

title: Case-insensitive host lookup is broken
body: app/models/embeddable_host.rb queries where("lower(host) = ?", host) without downcasing the argument. A host stored lowercase will not match a mixed/upper-case referer URL host, so EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? incorrectly rejects allowed hosts and embedding/retrieval fails.

title: update/destroy dereference nil when host not found
body: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb looks up the host with where(id: params[:id]).first and then calls save_host(host) or host.destroy without a nil check. An unknown id raises NoMethodError (500) instead of 404, and save_host will also crash on nil.

title: No uniqueness constraint on embeddable host
body: EmbeddableHost validates format but has no validates_uniqueness_of nor unique DB index on host. Admins can create duplicate host rows, making host_allowed?/category mapping ambiguous and allowing divergent categories for the same host.

title: Plural embedded ids assume non-null array
body: In _hydrateEmbedded the plural branch calls obj[k].map without checking for null/non-array. If a payload has color_ids: null or a singular value, the client throws TypeError and hydration fails. It should guard and filter missing lookups.

title: Duplicate `downsize` definition removes 4-arg API
body: app/models/optimized_image.rb defines self.downsize twice: at line 145 as downsize(from,to,max_width,max_height,opts) and again at line 149 as downsize(from,to,dimensions,opts). In Ruby the second definition overwrites the first, so any existing caller using the max_width,max_height form now gets ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments). The resize/downsize refactor must support both arities, e.g. with splat args, not two methods with the same name.

title: Stale tempfile.size causes unconditional 5x 80% downsizing
body: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb line 66 loops while tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes. tempfile is an open File/Tempfile object modified in place by an external convert process in line 67. File#size on the open descriptor does not reliably reflect the new on-disk size, so the condition can stay true even after the file is already small enough. The result is up to 5 successive 80% resizes (~0.8^5 ~= 0.33 scale) degrading quality and wasting CPU when one pass would suffice. Use File.size(tempfile.path) re-stat after each pass and break when under limit.

title: Downsize return value ignored and SVG/vector images corrupted
body: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb line 67 calls OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...) in a loop without checking its boolean return. If convert fails the code retries 4 more times then uploads the original oversized file anyway. Worse, the guard uses FileHelper.is_image?(filename) which includes SVG, but OptimizedImage.create_for explicitly skips resizing SVG by just copying it because vector-to-raster convert with -resize/[0] mangles or fails on SVG. Downsizing SVG in place can corrupt it or needlessly rasterize it. Skip SVG and break on false return.

title: Client max upload size hardcoded to 10MB ignoring SiteSetting
body: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js lines 182 and 246 replace Discourse.SiteSettings max_image_size_kb / max_attachment_size_kb with hardcoded 10*1024. This breaks admin configurability: instances with smaller or larger limits now validate against the wrong value client-side and show a wrong max_size_kb in the file_too_large error. A file rejected by the server will appear allowed locally and vice versa. Restore use of Discourse.SiteSettings['max_'+type+'_size_kb'] and max_image_size_kb.

title: API URL download limit hardcoded to 10MB bypassing setting
body: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb line 55 changes FileHelper.download(url, SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, ...) to FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...). An admin who configured a small max_image_size_kb to bound bandwidth, disk and ImageMagick CPU can now be forced to download and process up to 10MB per API upload. The limit should remain derived from SiteSetting, with any headroom added explicitly, not a fixed 10MB.

title: Duplicate `downsize` definition silently drops width/height API
body: File defines `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` at line 145 and then immediately redefines `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts)` at line 149. Ruby has no overloading, so the second definition overwrites the first. Any existing caller using the 4-arg form (max_width, max_height) will now get wrong arity / misinterpreted arguments and raise ArgumentError or produce a malformed geometry string. The 80% string form needed by uploads_controller should be a separate arity-tolerant method.

title: Loop re-checks stale `tempfile.size` after in-place convert
body: The downsizing loop checks `tempfile.size` before and on each iteration, but `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` rewrites the file via an external `convert` process. The open `tempfile` descriptor still refers to the old inode/size, so `tempfile.size` does not reflect the new on-disk size. The loop can therefore run all 5 iterations even when already small enough, or never terminate early, and the later `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile.size, ...)` stores a stale filesize.

title: In-place convert with same source/dest and unchecked failure
body: Call uses `tempfile.path` as both `from` and `to` for `convert from[0] ... to`. Reading and writing the same path in one ImageMagick invocation risks truncating/corrupting the upload if the command fails partway. Return value is also ignored and `attempt` is always decremented, so 5 expensive converts run even when conversion fails, after which an still-oversized file is passed to `Upload.create_for`.

title: Client validation hardcodes 10MB for all upload types
body: validateUploadedFile replaced `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` with `10 * 1024`. That lifts the limit for `attachment` uploads as well as `image` uploads, so oversized attachments pass client checks only to be rejected by the server (bad UX and wasted upload), and sites with a lower or higher configured limit get a wrong error message. Only images are auto-downsized server-side, so attachments must still respect their site setting.

title: Duplicate downsize definition removes 5-arg overload
body: app/models/optimized_image.rb defines self.downsize twice: at line 145 as downsize(from,to,max_width,max_height,opts) and again at line 149 as downsize(from,to,dimensions,opts). In Ruby the second definition overwrites the first. Any existing caller using the max_width,max_height form (4-5 arguments) will now either raise ArgumentError or have max_height misinterpreted as opts hash. The resize wrapper was correctly migrated to a dimensions string, but downsize needs a single method handling both forms or distinct names.

title: In-place downsize overwrites source and ignores failure
body: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb line 67 calls OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...) using the same path for source and destination and discards the boolean return value. If convert/gifsicle fails (convert_with returns false and logs only), the original upload file can be truncated or corrupted, yet the loop continues and Upload.create_for proceeds with the damaged file. Use a separate temp file, check the return value, and abort on failure instead of overwriting in place.

title: Client max size hardcoded to 10MB ignoring site settings
body: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js lines 182 and 246 replace Discourse.SiteSettings['max_'+type+'_size_kb'] and max_image_size_kb with hardcoded 10*1024. This breaks admin configuration: attachments still need max_attachment_size_kb enforcement (server does not downsize non-images), and sites with max_image_size_kb larger than 10MB will have valid uploads incorrectly rejected client-side while sites with smaller limits will allow uploads that then rely on server downsizing. Restore per-type site-setting lookup.

title: Downsize loop mishandles SVG and animated GIFs
body: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb line 64 only checks FileHelper.is_image?(filename) before downsizing. For SVG this will rasterize/alter a vector image via ImageMagick convert, unlike OptimizedImage.create_for which special-cases .svg with a plain copy. For animated GIFs it passes dimensions "80%" to downsize_instructions_animated which delegates to gifsicle --resize-fit, an option that expects WxH geometry not a percentage, so conversion will fail every retry. Skip SVG and pass valid GIF geometry or use gifsicle --scale.

title: Unsubscribe crashes when TopicUser row does not exist
body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb TopicsController#unsubscribe does TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) and then immediately dereferences tu.notification_level and tu.save!. A user who was never tracked on the topic, e.g. notified via mailing-list mode or group, has no TopicUser row, so tu is nil and the request raises NoMethodError on nil instead of unsubscribing.

title: State-changing unsubscribe performed on GET without CSRF protection
body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb TopicsController#unsubscribe mutates notification_level and saves, but it is routed as GET t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe and t/:topic_id/unsubscribe in config/routes.rb. GET requests are not checked for CSRF tokens, so any third-party page/image can force a logged-in user's browser to downgrade that topic's notification level, and crawlers/prefetchers can trigger it accidentally.

title: Unsubscribe bypasses TopicUser.change callbacks and reason tracking
body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb the action assigns tu.notification_level directly and calls tu.save! instead of TopicUser.change. That skips setting notifications_changed_at/notifications_reason_id, skips MessageBus notification_level_change publishing done in TopicUser.change, and skips validation of the level, leaving clients and tracking state out of sync.

title: New unsubscribe_link template requires unsubscribe_url for all emails
body: config/locales/server.en.yml changed unsubscribe_link to require %{unsubscribe_url}, and lib/email/message_builder.rb interpolates it in body and html_part whenever add_unsubscribe_link is true. Any email built with add_unsubscribe_link:true but without unsubscribe_url in template_args will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument / render a broken link, so all current and future callers must supply it and there is no fallback.

title: Unsubscribe crashes when TopicUser row does not exist
body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb TopicsController#unsubscribe does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` then immediately calls `tu.notification_level`. If the user never visited/tracked the topic there is no TopicUser row, so `tu` is nil and the request raises NoMethodError and returns 500. Email recipients who never interacted are exactly the users most likely to click the new per-topic unsubscribe link, so this breaks the feature.

title: State-changing unsubscribe via GET is CSRF-able
body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb the new `unsubscribe` action mutates `TopicUser.notification_level` and saves, but config/routes.rb exposes it as `GET t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` and `GET t/:topic_id/unsubscribe`. Any logged-in user visiting an attacker page with `` or a crawler/prefetcher following the email link will silently mute/regularize the topic with no CSRF token or confirmation. Mutating actions must not be GET.

title: Unsubscribe lacks visibility/authorization check
body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb `unsubscribe` builds `TopicView.new(params[:topic_id], current_user)` and then mutates notification state without `guardian.ensure_can_see!` and without rescuing `Discourse::InvalidAccess` the way `show` does. This lets a logged-in user probe private-message/secured-category topic IDs and change state on topics they cannot see, and turns forbidden topics into unhandled 500s instead of 403/404.

title: Unsubscribe email template now requires unsubscribe_url and can break delivery
body: In lib/email/message_builder.rb `body` and `html_part` unconditionally interpolate `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` when `add_unsubscribe_link` is true. After config/locales/server.en.yml changed `unsubscribe_link` to require `%{unsubscribe_url}`, any builder with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` but no `unsubscribe_url` in opts raises `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` and fails the email. The builder is generic, `user_preferences_url` was always present but `unsubscribe_url` is only supplied by `send_notification_email`, so one missed caller breaks all delivery for that email.

title: Unsubscribe crashes when TopicUser row is missing
body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb TopicsController#unsubscribe does TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) and then immediately dereferences tu.notification_level. Users who were never tracked in a topic (e.g. emailed via mailing-list mode, digest, or just lurkers) have no TopicUser row, so tu is nil and the request raises NoMethodError on nil instead of unsubscribing. Use TopicUser.change/get-or-create or handle nil before changing notification_level.

title: State-changing unsubscribe via GET enables CSRF
body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb TopicsController#unsubscribe mutates notification_level and saves on a GET route (config/routes.rb get t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe). GET requests have no CSRF token check, so any third-party image/link visited by a logged-in user can silently downgrade/mute their topic subscription. State changes must use POST/PUT/DELETE with CSRF protection or a signed single-use token.

title: New unsubscribe_link interpolation breaks emails without unsubscribe_url
body: In config/locales/server.en.yml unsubscribe_link now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, and lib/email/message_builder.rb renders it unconditionally in body (line 90) and html_part (line 67) whenever add_unsubscribe_link is true. Any caller that sets add_unsubscribe_link without passing unsubscribe_url (only UserNotifications#send_notification_email was updated) will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and fail to send the email. Provide a default/fallback or keep the old text when unsubscribe_url is absent.

title: SPA unsubscribe page never calls server unsubscribe action
body: In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6 the model hook calls PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id), which hits the normal topic show endpoint, not TopicsController#unsubscribe. A user navigating client-side to /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe therefore never executes the server-side notification_level downgrade; the mutation only happens on full-page Rails render. Either have the route call the unsubscribe endpoint or move the mutation to an explicit user action.

title: Validator has DB write side-effect and non-atomic counter
body: In app/models/blocked_email.rb, BlockedEmail.should_block? increments match_count/last_match_at and calls save, and it is called from EmailValidator.validate_each on every User validation where email changed. That means a read/validation path writes to the database, updates stats even for validations that ultimately fail or are just probed, and does read-modify-write via match_count += 1 plus save which loses increments under concurrent signups and can fail validation silently.

title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive and bypassable
body: In app/models/blocked_email.rb line 12, the lookup is BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first with no downcasing/normalization, and the unique index on blocked_emails.email is case-sensitive. Since email addresses are case-insensitive, an attacker blocked as bad@spammers.org can sign up as BAD@spammers.org or Bad@Spammers.org and BlockedEmail.should_block? will return false, defeating the block.

title: Whitelist/blacklist regex allows suffix bypass
body: In lib/validators/email_validator.rb, email_in_restriction_setting? builds Regexp.new("@(#{domains})", true) with no end-anchor after escaping only dots. A whitelist entry like allowed.com therefore matches user@allowed.com.evil.com, so an attacker can pass the whitelist (or dodge/match the blacklist incorrectly) by appending a suffix domain, defeating the domain restriction.

title: Blocked-email match is case/whitespace sensitive and bypassable
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? does BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first with the raw value, while other paths normalize with Email.downcase(...).strip (see UsersController#change_email). An attacker can bypass a block by changing case or adding whitespace, and the uniqueness validation plus unique index on blocked_emails are also case-sensitive so the same address can exist in multiple forms. Normalize (downcase/strip) on write and on lookup.

title: Non-atomic match_count increment with side effect inside validation
body: should_block? does record.match_count += 1; record.last_match_at = ...; record.save when a record matches, and it is called from EmailValidator#validate_each. That makes every validation attempt perform a read-modify-write DB write, so concurrent signups lose increments, failed validations still inflate statistics, and validation now has a persistent side effect. Use an atomic counter update separated from the boolean check.

title: change_email path bypasses blocked-email validation
body: UsersController#change_email only checks User.where("email = ?", lower_email).exists? and then creates an email_token and sends an authorization email. It never runs User email validation / EmailValidator / BlockedEmail.should_block?, so a blocked address rejected at signup can still be adopted via the email-change flow. Enforce the same block check before creating the token.

title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive so block can be bypassed
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? does BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first with the raw value. User-supplied emails vary in case and surrounding whitespace while the blocked list is stored as-is, so Block@Example.com will not match block@example.com. An attacker can bypass an explicit block by changing case, defeating the purpose of the feature.

title: Non-atomic read-modify-write of match_count loses updates
body: should_block? does record.match_count += 1 followed by record.save. Under concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked email two processes read the same count and write back the same value, losing one increment and clobbering last_match_at. Use an atomic counter update such as increment_counter/update_counters instead.

title: Validator performs database writes on every validation
body: EmailValidator#validate_each calls BlockedEmail.should_block?(value), which increments match_count and updates last_match_at and saves. Validation is expected to be side-effect free and can run multiple times per request or on unrelated validations, so statistics are inflated, extra writes happen on the signup hot path, and a failed/rolled-back user creation still leaves mutated blocked_email rows.

title: rejectedEmails array on prototype is shared mutable state
body: rejectedEmails: Em.A([]) is defined in the object literal passed to extend, so the same array instance is shared by every instance of CreateAccountController. pushObject in createAccount mutates shared state, leaking one user's rejected/blocked emails into another controller instance and growing without bound. Initialize the array in init instead.

title: Email validation will not refresh on rejectedEmails push
body: emailValidation depends on rejectedEmails.@each but rejectedEmails is an array of strings mutated with pushObject. @each observes properties of array items, not array membership, so adding a newly rejected email may not invalidate the computed property. The dependent key should observe array membership such as rejectedEmails.[] or rejectedEmails.length.

title: cook_method default is raw_html, converts all existing posts
body: Migration sets default: 1, null:false. Post.cook_methods is Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html) so regular=0 and raw_html=1. Every existing row backfilled with 1 will hit `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` in app/models/post.rb and bypass the markdown/sanitize pipeline, rendering raw markdown source as cooked HTML.

title: raw_html cook bypass returns unsanitized remote HTML
body: Post#cook returns `raw` verbatim for cook_method raw_html. TopicEmbed.import/import_remote store RSS/Readability HTML and Disqus content with that flag and render it with `raw post.cooked` in embed/best.html.erb. There is no sanitization, so arbitrary <script>, <iframe>, on* attributes from a feed or scraped page become persistent XSS for every viewer of the topic and embed.

title: Reflected XSS via unescaped request.referer in JS
body: The layout interpolates `<%= request.referer %>` inside a single-quoted JavaScript string without escaping. Referer is attacker-controlled request header, so a value like `');alert(1);//` breaks out of the string and executes script in the embed origin.

title: postMessage targetOrigin uses full referer URL instead of origin
body: The second argument to parent.postMessage is `'<%= request.referer %>'` which includes path/query. Browsers require an origin of the form scheme://host:port or *, so delivery with a full URL never matches and auto-resize breaks. It also leaks the embedding page path.

title: Reversed substring origin check on postMessage
body: postMessageReceived does `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` instead of comparing origins for equality. Any e.origin that happens to be a substring of discourseUrl (for example a one-character string like `/` or `:`) passes, while the correct check must verify e.origin equals the Discourse origin. This lets a malicious frame resize/inject messages.

title: Unsafe open() on admin-configured feed URL
body: Code calls `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` via Kernel#open from open-uri. Kernel#open interprets a leading `|` as a command pipe and follows redirects/SSRF to internal hosts. Must parse/validate the URL and use URI.open with timeouts, not bare open.

title: Nil feed item content crashes poller
body: poll_feed does `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assuming every RSS/Atom entry has content. Items with only link/title/description have nil content, raising NoMethodError and aborting the whole hourly poll so no items are imported.

title: SSRF and unhandled fetch in import_remote
body: import_remote does `open(url).read` on an embed_url supplied by any site visitor via EmbedController/TopicRetriever with no host allowlist check at this layer, no timeout, and no rescue. An attacker can make the server fetch internal hosts/files and a single failure or slow origin raises out of the Sidekiq job.

title: Check-then-create race on embed_url unique index
body: import does `where(embed_url: url).first` then `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a transaction without handling concurrent creators. Two simultaneous retrieve_topic jobs for the same new URL both see blank and one raises RecordNotUnique on the unique index, failing the job instead of reusing the winner's row.

title: Non-atomic throttle setnx+expire can leak key
body: retrieved_recently? does `$redis.setnx(key,1)` then `$redis.expire(key,60)` as two commands. If the process crashes between them the key never expires and that embed_url is throttled forever. Use a single atomic SETEX/SET NX EX.

title: Spec expects TopicRetriever but controller enqueues job
body: EmbedController#best does `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` while the spec mocks `TopicRetriever.new` and expects `retrieve`. The test does not verify actual behavior and will fail/pass for the wrong reason, leaving the loading path uncovered.

title: Wrong default for cook_method flips existing posts to raw_html
body: The migration adds cook_method with default 1, null false. Post.cook_methods is Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html) so regular is 0 and raw_html is 1. Every existing row therefore defaults to raw_html, and Post#cook returns raw without cooking. After migrating, all historic cooked HTML is bypassed and raw markdown is rendered, breaking display and bypassing sanitization.

title: Stored XSS via unsanitized imported HTML rendered raw
body: TopicEmbed.import stores feed/readability HTML with cook_method raw_html, Post#cook returns raw verbatim, and app/views/embed/best.html.erb renders it with raw post.cooked. There is no sanitization of tags, attributes, script, or of the interpolated url in the imported_from footer. A malicious feed or embedded page can store arbitrary JS that executes in the embed iframe and, via postMessage/parent context, attacks the host site.

title: Reflected XSS via unescaped request.referer in postMessage
body: The layout interpolates <%= request.referer %> directly inside a single-quoted JS string for postMessage targetOrigin. Referer is attacker-controlled by the embedding site and is not JS-escaped. A referer containing a quote and script breaks out of the string and executes in the embed origin. It is also the wrong value: targetOrigin must be an origin, not a full URL.

title: Reversed postMessage origin check allows prefix spoof
body: The handler checks discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1, i.e. whether the configured URL contains the event origin. An attacker origin that is a prefix of discourseUrl passes, e.g. e.origin http://forum.example accepted when discourseUrl is http://forum.example.com/. The check must compare origins for equality, not test containment in the wrong direction.

title: PollFeed crashes on nil content and unhandled fetch errors
body: SimpleRSS items may have nil content/link. The code calls i.content.scrub and CGI.unescapeHTML on it unconditionally, raising NoMethodError and aborting the hourly job. open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) and SimpleRSS.parse can also raise on network, timeout, or malformed feed with no rescue, so one bad poll kills the whole import.

title: Unbounded raw URL used as Redis throttle key
body: retrieved_recently? builds retrieved:#{@embed_url} directly from user-supplied embed_url with no hashing, length limit, or namespacing. An attacker can create unlimited distinct keys and very long keys in Redis, causing memory growth and keyspace pollution. The URL should be hashed, e.g. SHA1, before use as a key.

title: Import mutates caller string with << causing double footer
body: contents << footer mutates the caller's string in place instead of duplicating it. Reusing the same string for a second import appends the Imported from footer twice, changing content_sha1 and stored raw on every call and breaking idempotent update detection.

title: absolutize_urls raises InvalidURIError on bad URL
body: absolutize_urls calls URI(url) with no rescue. import only guards with url =~ /^https?\:\/\//, which still allows strings that URI rejects. An exception escapes PostCreator/TopicRetriever/PollFeed paths and turns a single bad feed item or embed_url into a 500 or failed job instead of skipping it.

title: Embed controller spec expects TopicRetriever but code enqueues job
body: The controller enqueues Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) on a miss, but the spec stubs TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed to nil and expects TopicRetriever.new/retrieve. The spec does not exercise the actual code path and will fail or pass for the wrong reason, leaving the loading branch untested.

title: Reflected XSS via unescaped request.referer in postMessage targetOrigin
body: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb line 11 interpolates '<%= request.referer %>' directly into a JavaScript string. Referer is attacker-controlled request input and is only HTML-escaped, not JS-string escaped. A referer containing ', </script>, or backslashes breaks out of the string/script context and executes arbitrary JS in the embed origin. It is also functionally wrong because postMessage targetOrigin must be an origin, not a full URL with path.

title: Stored XSS via raw_html cook bypass for imported feed content
body: app/models/post.rb line 133 returns raw unconditionally when cook_method is raw_html, skipping PrettyText cooking/sanitization and Plugin::Filter. app/models/topic_embed.rb imports untrusted RSS/Atom/Readability HTML and stores it as raw_html, then app/views/embed/best.html.erb renders it with `raw post.cooked`. Remote <script>, <iframe>, on* handlers and similar survive end-to-end and execute for forum visitors in both embed and normal topic views.

title: SSRF and unhandled fetch in import_remote via open()
body: app/models/topic_embed.rb line 48 does open(url).read on an embed_url / feed link with no allowlist beyond a /^https?/ regex, no timeout, size limit, redirect limit, or error handling. Combined with lib/topic_retriever.rb fetch_http and app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, an attacker-influenced URL can force the server to fetch internal hosts, hang the job, raise and retry, or read large payloads. open-uri can also have surprising behaviors on unexpected schemes/redirects.

title: Unescaped URL interpolation and caller-string mutation in import
body: app/models/topic_embed.rb line 13 appends "#{url}" with raw url from RSS/remote input into stored raw_html. A URL containing a single quote or HTML breaks the attribute and injects markup/JS that is later rendered raw. The same line mutates the caller's contents string with <<, surprising callers that reuse the string.

title: Non-atomic throttle with unbounded Redis key
body: lib/topic_retriever.rb lines 25-28 use $redis.setnx then a separate $redis.expire for key "retrieved:#{@embed_url}". If the process crashes between calls the key never expires and throttles that URL forever. The key embeds the full attacker-influenced URL unhashed, so varying paths/queries create unbounded distinct 60s keys and allow Redis memory exhaustion even though the host is constrained.

title: PollFeed crashes on feed items without content
body: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb line 35 calls i.content.scrub unconditionally. SimpleRSS items commonly have nil content (title/link only) or nil link/title, causing NoMethodError that aborts the whole hourly poll so no items are imported. The feed_key method for conditional polling is also defined but never used, so every run refetches and re-revises.

title: Embed controller spec does not match implementation
body: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb lines 40-45 expect EmbedController to instantiate TopicRetriever directly, but app/controllers/embed_controller.rb enqueues Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic,...). The spec therefore cannot pass against the shipped code and leaves the actual async path, loading render, and user_id passing untested.

title: order() mixin off-by-one for legacy box spec
body: In mixins.scss the order() mixin emits -webkit-box-ordinal-group: $val and -moz-box-ordinal-group: $val with the same value as order: $val. By definition box-ordinal-group is 1-based while order is 0-based, so box-ordinal-group must be order + 1. As written, @include order(3) in header.scss and @include order(2) in topic.scss produce ordinal-group 3/2 instead of 4/3, so legacy -webkit-box/-moz-box browsers order header panel and extra-info-wrapper incorrectly relative to modern flexbox browsers.

title: Invalid -ms-align-items property emitted
body: The align-items() mixin in mixins.scss outputs -ms-align-items: $alignment. That property never existed; IE10/11 only understands -ms-flex-align. The invalid declaration is dropped, so IE10/11 falls back to whatever -ms-flex-align resolves to or stretches, meaning @include align-items(center) in header.scss and @include align-items(baseline) in badges.css.scss do not align as intended in those browsers.

title: float layout ignored inside new flex container breaks small-action
body: In topic-post.scss .small-action is now a flex container via @include flexbox(), so its direct children .topic-avatar, .small-action-desc and button become flex items. Per CSS flexbox, float and clear on flex items are ignored. The code keeps float: left on .topic-avatar and float: right on button with no flex equivalent such as margin-left: auto or justify-content, so the dismiss button that used to be pinned right will now sit immediately after the text and the avatar/text spacing changes.

title: order() mixin off-by-one for legacy box spec
body: In mixins.scss the order() mixin sets -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group to the same value as order. The legacy box spec is 1-indexed (ordinal-group = order + 1), so @include order(2) / order(3) used in topic.scss and header.scss renders as 2/3 instead of 3/4 in old WebKit/Firefox. Consequence is wrong visual ordering of header .panel vs .extra-info-wrapper on those browsers.

title: float:right ignored on flex item breaks small-action button
body: .small-action is made a flex container in topic-post.scss but its child button still relies on float: right and .topic-avatar on float: left. Per CSS Flexbox, float and clear have no effect on flex items, so the button will no longer stick to the right edge and will instead lay out inline after the description. The layout needs justify-content or margin-left:auto instead of float.

title: Invalid -ms-align-items property in align-items mixin
body: The align-items() mixin in mixins.scss emits -ms-align-items, which was never a valid IE10 property; IE10 only understands -ms-flex-align. The invalid declaration is dropped, and -ms-flex-align does not support all modern values such as baseline used for .badge-wrapper.bullet. Consequence is dead code and inconsistent vertical alignment in IE10.

title: order() mixin off-by-one for legacy box ordinal-group
body: In mixins.scss the order() mixin sets -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group to the same $val as order. The legacy box spec is 1-indexed while flex order is 0-indexed, so ordinal-group must be $val + 1. With @include order(2) and order(3) used in topic.scss and header.scss, legacy WebKit/Firefox will render items one position earlier than modern browsers, breaking header ordering.

title: small-action button float:right ineffective in flex container
body: topic-post.scss makes .small-action a flexbox container via flexbox() but leaves button { float: right; } to push the dismiss button to the right edge. Per CSS Flexbox, float and clear on flex items are ignored (computed to none). The button will now sit immediately after .small-action-desc instead of right-aligned, a visual regression. Flex alignment requires margin-left: auto or justify-content, not float.

title: Header float layout removed with no non-flex fallback
body: header.scss converts .d-header .contents to flexbox and deletes .title { float: left; } and .panel { float: right; }. Browsers with no flexbox support (e.g. IE9 and below) ignore the prefixed flex displays and now have no floats to position title vs panel, so header items stack as full-width blocks. Floats should be retained before the flexbox declarations as a fallback.

title: Invalid -ms-align-items property in align-items mixin
body: In mixins.scss align-items() emits -ms-align-items: $alignment which never existed in any IE implementation. IE10 only understands -ms-flex-align. The invalid declaration is dead code and suggests the prefix mapping was not verified; for values like baseline it will silently do nothing in IE10 where -ms-flex-align also lacks baseline support.

title: Conditional serializer method missing `?` so it never runs
body: File app/serializers/user_serializer.rb defines `def include_website_name` without a question mark. ActiveModel::Serializers looks for `include_website_name?` (as used for every other conditional attribute in this file, e.g. `include_stats?`, `include_suspend_reason?`). Because the name does not match, the gate is never called, so `website_name` is always serialized even when `website` is blank/nil, contrary to intent.

title: website_name bypasses TL0 untrusted-attribute hiding
body: File app/serializers/user_serializer.rb adds `:website_name` to `attributes` but does not add it to `untrusted_attributes` (which hides `website`, `bio_*`, `location`, etc. from anonymous viewers for TL0 users via `scope.restrict_user_fields?`). Its own `include_website_name` check only tests `website.present?`. As a result a TL0 user's website host/path is still exposed via `website_name` even when `website` itself is correctly suppressed.

title: Host comparison is case-sensitive and can crash on nil hostname
body: File app/serializers/user_serializer.rb `website_name` compares `URI(website.to_s).host == Discourse.current_hostname` and calls `discourse_host.split` / `ends_with?` without normalizing or nil-guarding. DNS hosts are case-insensitive, so `Example.COM` vs `example.com` fails to match and falls through to the host-only branch. If `Discourse.current_hostname` is nil/empty the splits raise NoMethodError, breaking user serialization.

title: Conditional serializer hook misnamed, never called
body: In app/serializers/user_serializer.rb the method is defined as `def include_website_name` without a trailing `?`. ActiveModel::Serializers looks for `include_website_name?` (as used for every other conditional attribute like `include_stats?`, `include_email?` in the same file), so this hook is never invoked. Consequence: `website_name` is always serialized even when `website` is blank, returning a null key, and any intended presence gating is bypassed.

title: website_name bypasses TL0 anonymous hiding
body: In app/serializers/user_serializer.rb `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` so it is suppressed for TL0 users viewed as anonymous via `restrict_user_fields?`, but the new `website_name` attribute is added to `attributes` without adding it to `untrusted_attributes` and its `include_website_name` check only tests `website.present?`. Consequence: an anonymous viewer who is correctly denied `website` still receives `website_name` (the host plus path for same-domain URLs), leaking the private profile field the restriction was meant to hide.

title: Conditional-serialize predicate misnamed, so website_name is always serialized
body: File app/serializers/user_serializer.rb defines `def include_website_name` without a question mark, while ActiveModel::Serializer looks for `include_website_name?` (as used for every other attribute like include_email?, include_stats?). The misnamed method is never called, so website_name is serialized even when `website` is blank, returning null and wasting payload, and the intended gating does not work.

title: website_name bypasses TL0 anonymous hiding for website
body: File app/serializers/user_serializer.rb adds :website_name to `attributes` but does not add it to `untrusted_attributes`, which is what suppresses bio/location/website for TL0 users seen by anonymous via dynamically defined include_?_methods. As a result an anonymous viewer who is denied `website` will still receive `website_name` derived from it, leaking a profile field that was intentionally hidden.

title: Untrusted-attributes test not updated for website_name
body: File spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb line 11 lists untrusted attributes without website_name, so the test `doesn't serialize untrusted attributes` cannot catch the leak where website_name remains visible for TL0 users seen as anonymous. The list must include website_name to lock in the privacy contract.

title: Light-theme color changed from 30% to 70%
body: In .embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a the old value was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The new code uses scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) as the light-theme branch of dark-light-choose. That lightens the link in the default light theme instead of preserving it; the dark branch alone should have been added as scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%) with primary kept at 30%.

title: Custom-message-length lightness flipped 70% to 30%
body: Old value was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%). New light branch is scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). Desktop modal.scss for the same selector correctly keeps 70% / 30%. The mobile change darkens the text in the light theme and diverges from desktop.

title: Topic-map h3 lightness changed 20% to 50%
body: Old value was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%). New code is dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)). Desktop topic-post.scss keeps the equivalent h3 at 20% / 80%. The mobile edit changes the light-theme appearance instead of only adding a dark-theme branch.

body: Old .group-member-info .name was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). New light branch is 50%, i.e. dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)). Adjacent .username a / .name rules use 30% / 70%. title: Group member name lightness changed 30% to 50% on mobile
body: Old .group-member-info .name was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). New code uses dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)). That alters the established light-theme value; consistent with the rest of the PR it should be 30% for $primary and 70% for $secondary.

title: Wrong lightness for mobile group-member name

title: Wrong lightness for mobile topic-map h3

Both branches are wrong: light should stay 30% and dark should be 70% to sum to 100% like common/base/user.scss. This alters light-theme appearance and gives wrong dark-theme contrast.

body: Same as desktop: old scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) was replaced with dark-light-choose with 50%/50% values. Light-theme color is unintentionally changed and dark-theme fallback should be 70% lightness on $secondary, not 50%.

title: topic-map h3 light value changed 20% to 50%
body: Old value was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%). New value is dark-light-choose with 50%/50%. Preserving light theme requires keeping 20% for $primary and using 80% for $secondary. The current 50% makes headings much lighter on light themes.

title: Admin member routes supply :id but controller requires :group_id
body: config/routes.rb declares delete/put "members" inside resources :groups without a collection block, so the URL is /admin/groups/:id/members and the group id arrives as params[:id]. app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb add_members/remove_member do params.require(:group_id). A real request therefore raises ActionController::ParameterMissing (400) even though controller specs pass by injecting group_id directly. Fix routing or param name.

title: totalPages off-by-one when count is exact multiple of limit
body: totalPages is Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. For example 100 members with limit 50 yields 3 instead of 2, so the pager shows a phantom empty last page and showingLast/next logic is wrong. It should be ceil(user_count / limit).

title: Next pagination can advance to empty offset == user_count
body: next computes offset as Math.min(offset+limit, user_count). With user_count 100 and limit 50, from offset 50 it moves to offset 100, which is one past the last valid page (50) and returns no members. The cap should be (totalPages-1)*limit, not user_count.

title: Group members endpoint allows unbounded limit and negative offset
body: GroupsController#members does limit=(params[:limit]||50).to_i and offset=params[:offset].to_i with no clamping. A caller can request limit=1000000 to load the whole membership table (DoS/memory) or offset=-5/limit=0 to produce SQL errors or empty results. Clamp limit to a max (e.g. 50-200) and offset to >=0.

title: add_members does not strip whitespace so comma-space lists fail
body: add_members does usernames.split(",").each with User.find_by_username(username) and no strip. The user-selector produces comma-separated values that commonly contain spaces ("alice, bob"), so every username after the first fails lookup and is silently skipped, returning success with nothing added. Strip each token and skip blanks.

title: remove_member bypasses Group membership logic
body: remove_member does group.users.delete(user_id) then group.save. Direct association delete skips any Group#remove bookkeeping (e.g. primary_group cleanup, counters, callbacks) that the rest of the codebase uses via group.add/group.remove. Use the model removal API so state stays consistent.

title: findMembers returns undefined instead of promise on empty name
body: findMembers now does bare return when name is empty, previously Ember.RSVP.resolve([]). Callers such as next/previous return group.findMembers() and expect a thenable; getting undefined breaks chaining and error handling. Return a resolved promise.

title: Automatic-group remove_member test uses wrong HTTP verb
body: The remove_member route is DELETE per config/routes.rb, but the cannot-remove-members-from-automatic-groups example issues xhr :put. The controller test bypasses routing so it passes without exercising the real route, leaving the route/verb/param contract unverified.

title: totalPages off-by-one for exact multiples
body: totalPages is Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, so 100 members with limit 50 yields 3 pages instead of 2. The controller's next action clamps offset to user_count, so the UI can navigate to a third empty page and shows currentPage/totalPages incorrectly.

title: members limit is unbounded
body: limit is taken as (params[:limit] || 50).to_i with no maximum or negative check. A caller can request limit=1000000 or larger, forcing order/limit/offset over the whole group membership and serializing it in one response, which is a CPU/memory DoS vector. Clamp limit to a sane maximum.

title: add_members does not strip whitespace around usernames
body: usernames.split(",") passes each token directly to User.find_by_username. Comma+space separated input like "bob, alice" leaves a leading space on the second token so the lookup fails and the user is silently skipped. Strip each token and skip blanks.

title: findMembers returns undefined instead of a promise
body: When the group name is empty findMembers does bare return, previously it returned Ember.RSVP.resolve([]). Callers such as the next/previous actions return group.findMembers() and route setup expects a thenable, so they now get undefined and any .then chaining throws.

title: remove_member spec uses wrong HTTP verb
body: The spec calls xhr :put, :remove_member but config/routes.rb defines delete members => groups#remove_member. Controller specs bypass routing, so the test passes without ever exercising the real DELETE route and would not catch a verb/routing mismatch.

title: stray closing div inside table
body: The members table contains a stray before {{/each}} with no matching opening div, producing invalid HTML inside the table. Browsers will repair it unpredictably, which can break row layout.

title: totalPages off-by-one when count is exact multiple of limit
body: In app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6 totalPages is Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50/50, 100/50) this reports one extra empty page, enables the next button to advance to an empty page, and shows e.g. 1/2 instead of 1/1. It should be ceil(user_count/limit).

title: Next pagination can set offset to user_count (empty page)
body: In app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6 the next action clamps offset with Math.min(offset+limit, user_count). For user_count=100, limit=50, offset=50 this moves to offset=100 which is past the last record and fetches an empty page. The max valid offset is the start of the last page, not user_count.

title: add_members does not strip whitespace so comma-space lists fail
body: In app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb add_members does usernames.split(",").each with no strip. A normal input like "alice, bob" yields " bob" with a leading space, User.find_by_username fails, and the user is silently skipped. The old usernames= path handled this. Strip each token and skip blanks.

title: remove_member bypasses Group#remove logic via users.delete
body: In app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb remove_member calls group.users.delete(user_id) directly. Elsewhere membership changes use group.add(user)/group.remove(user), which encapsulate join-model callbacks, counters and side-effects. Deleting the association directly bypasses those and then calls group.save on an already-mutated collection, risking inconsistent group state.

title: members limit/offset unvalidated allows huge or negative paging
body: In app/controllers/groups_controller.rb members does limit=(params[:limit]||50).to_i and offset=params[:offset].to_i with no clamping. A caller can request limit=1000000 causing a huge ORDER BY/LIMIT query (DoS/perf), or negative limit/offset which ActiveRecord may interpret unexpectedly. Clamp limit to a sane max and force offset/limit >=0.

title: findMembers returns undefined instead of promise on empty name
body: In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js findMembers changed from returning Ember.RSVP.resolve([]) to bare return when name is empty. Callers expecting a thenable (previous afterModel hooks and any .then chaining) will throw on undefined.then. Return a resolved promise instead.

title: remove_member spec uses wrong HTTP verb so route is untested
body: In spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb the automatic-group remove_member test calls xhr :put, :remove_member, but config/routes.rb only defines delete members => groups#remove_member. Controller specs dispatch by action name so the test passes while never exercising the real route; a PUT in production would 404. Change the spec to xhr :delete.

title: Fallback lookup hits SiteSetting and can raise on nil
body: FallbackLocaleList#[] in config/initializers/i18n.rb calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym on every lookup. I18n::Backend::Fallbacks calls fallbacks[locale] on every translated key, so every I18n.t now touches SiteSetting instead of using a cached chain. Worse, if default_locale is nil or empty the to_sym call raises NoMethodError before uniq.compact can run, breaking all translation with a 500. The lookup should handle nil safely and avoid per-translation SiteSetting access.

title: Translation LRU cache ignores fallback chain
body: I18n.translate in lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb builds its LRU key as key + config.locale + backend object_id. With the new fallback chain of user locale -> SiteSetting.default_locale -> :en, the same key+locale can resolve differently when the site default locale changes or when different fallback files are loaded, but the cache key does not include the fallback locales. Changing SiteSetting.default_locale will keep serving stale cached strings until LRU eviction, and missing-translation results cached before fallbacks are loaded are frozen in.

title: translate only loads current locale, not fallbacks
body: I18n.translate in lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb calls load_locale(config.locale) only, while loading of the fallback locales is done separately via I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! called only from ApplicationController#set_locale. Any translation outside a web request (background jobs, mailers, console, initializers, model callbacks) will resolve fallbacks against unloaded YAML files, producing missing-translation strings that are then stored in the LRU cache. The translate path itself must ensure the full fallback chain is loaded.

title: ensure_loaded! on every request does redundant locale loads
body: ApplicationController#set_locale calls I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! on every request, which iterates user locale, site default locale, and :en and calls I18n.ensure_loaded! for each. This runs before preload_json and other translation-heavy work on every request even when the locales are already loaded, adding SiteSetting.default_locale lookups and @loaded_locales scans per request. It also only covers the controller path, leaving other entry points without loaded fallbacks.

title: Translate only lazy-loads current locale, so fallbacks stay unloaded
body: I18n.translate in lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb calls load_locale(config.locale) only for the active locale. With the new fallback chain [user locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en], the fallback locales may never have been loaded via I18n.ensure_loaded!. I18n fallback lookup cannot find translations in unloaded files and returns translation-missing even though the yml exists. ApplicationController#set_locale calls I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!, but mailers, background jobs, and any code outside a controller request never do, so those paths get missing translations.

title: Translation LRU cache key ignores fallback chain
body: The cache key in lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb is "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}". After this PR the translated value also depends on SiteSetting.default_locale and the content of fallback locales (:en plus site default). A cached hit/miss for a locale is never invalidated when the site default changes or when a fallback locale file is loaded later, so requests can keep serving the wrong language or a stale translation-missing string until I18n.reload! clears the whole cache.

title: Fallback list does not normalize locales and can raise on blank default
body: FallbackLocaleList#[] in config/initializers/i18n.rb builds [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact without normalizing locale to a symbol, so string 'en' and symbol :en are not deduped, and if SiteSetting.default_locale is nil or empty string, to_sym raises NoMethodError or produces :"" and breaks every I18n lookup that needs a fallback. It also hits SiteSetting (DB/cache read) on every fallback resolution, i.e. on every missing key, adding overhead to the translation miss path.

title: Fallback lookup hits SiteSetting on every translation
body: In config/initializers/i18n.rb FallbackLocaleList#[] calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym to build the chain [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]. I18n::Backend::Fallbacks calls I18n.fallbacks[locale] for every missing-key lookup, so this puts a SiteSetting (DB/Redis/cache) read on the hot translation path and will also fail during boot/asset-precompile when the DB is unavailable. Cache the site default per-request or memoize it instead of reading it per lookup.

title: Translate only preloads current locale, not fallbacks
body: In lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb I18n.translate calls load_locale(config.locale) only for the active locale. Fallback locales (site default and :en) are only preloaded in ApplicationController#set_locale via I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!. Any translation outside a web request (Sidekiq jobs, mailers, console, rake) will therefore resolve fallbacks against unloaded translation files and return missing-translation errors even though the fallback string exists.

title: Translation LRU cache ignores fallback chain
body: In lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb the cache key is "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}" with no component for the fallback chain. A key that fell back to SiteSetting.default_locale or :en is cached under just key+locale, so changing SiteSetting.default_locale (or loading a previously-missing fallback file) leaves stale fallback values in the 300-entry ThreadSafeCache until process restart or I18n.reload!. Include the resolved fallback locales or default-locale version in the cache key or invalidate the cache on locale-setting change.

title: Denial cache serves stale denies and is never cleared on allow
body: In Service.Check the denial cache is checked first (permDenialCache.Get) and on a hit returns Allowed:false without querying the DB, and on a DB-verified deny it does permDenialCache.Set for shortCacheTTL (30s). Nothing ever deletes that entry on grant or on a later allow. So sequence deny -> grant permission in DB (share dashboard, add role/team permission, wildcard grant) -> Check within TTL still hits the denial key (namespace+user+action+name+parent) and denies even though the DB would allow. This reintroduces the exact staleness the PR tries to fix, but in the opposite direction, and prolongs it because the fast-path prevents the DB fallback from ever running until expiry.

title: DB fallback still uses stale cached folder tree
