body: Check falls back to getIdentityPermissions when cached scopes miss, but checkPermission/checkInheritedPermissions then calls buildFolderTree which is itself cached in folderCache for shortCacheTTL. If the resource involves a newly created folder or new parent/ancestor relationship, the fresh permission scopes will be evaluated against the old tree, Ancestors(parent) will be empty/wrong, and the check will still deny and then populate the denial cache. The fix for newly created dashboards/folders is therefore incomplete for inherited folder permissions and List results.

title: Denial key uses raw subject instead of canonical UID
body: permDenialKey is built from checkReq.UserUID directly from the request subject, while permCache keys are built from resolved store.UserIdentifiers.UID after GetUserIdentifiers (which maps numeric IDs to UIDs). The same user checking as user:123 vs user:uid-string gets different denial keys, so denies can be bypassed or duplicated, and anonymous/render paths are inconsistent with the permission-cache keying.

title: Negative denial cache causes stale denies with no invalidation
body: In pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go Check() first returns Allowed=false on permDenialCache hit and only sets that entry when a full DB check denies (line 154). The entry lives for shortCacheTTL (30s) and is never invalidated when permissions change. Consequence: if a user is denied once then granted access (e.g. creator of a new dashboard/folder, role/team change), subsequent Checks for that exact name/parent are short-circuited to deny for the TTL window, re-introducing the exact bug the PR claims to fix and extending denial beyond the existing permCache staleness.

title: List still serves stale permission cache with no DB fallback
body: In pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go List() uses getCachedIdentityPermissions and, on hit, lists directly from the cached scope map without verifying freshness. Check() was changed to fall back to the DB when the cached map does not contain the requested resource, but List() has no equivalent revalidation. Consequence: newly created dashboards/folders will still be missing from list responses for up to shortCacheTTL even when Check() would now allow them, leaving the user-visible fix incomplete.

title: Denial and permission caches share overlapping keyspace on shared backend
body: In pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go userPermCacheKey() and userPermDenialCacheKey() both use the prefix namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action, with the denial key just appending "_" + name + "_" + parent. All cacheWrap instances share the same underlying cache.Cache. Consequence: with underscores in UIDs/actions/names (all joined by _ with no escaping or distinct prefix), a permission key can equal a denial key for different parameters, so a Set on one type overwrites the other and a Get unmarshals bool JSON as map[string]bool or vice versa, causing lost entries, cache misses, and either stale allows requiring DB reload or lost denials.

title: Denial cache short-circuits DB fallback and causes stale denies
body: Check() checks permDenialCache first (line 117) and returns Allowed:false immediately on hit, without consulting the DB. The entry is set after a DB-backed deny (line 154) with shortCacheTTL (30s) and is never cleared when permissions are granted. So if a user is denied once and then granted access, all Checks for that namespace/user/action/name/parent are incorrectly denied until TTL expires. This reintroduces the exact staleness the PR claims to fix (creator/grant propagation) and defeats the new cachedPerms->DB fallback on lines 123-139, which is unreachable when a denial is cached.

title: List serves stale cached permissions with no revalidation
body: List() uses getCachedIdentityPermissions and, on hit, returns listPermission directly from the cached scope map with no DB fallback. Unlike Check(), which was changed to requery the DB when the cached map does not authorize the requested name, List has no way to detect staleness. Newly granted scopes (e.g. just-created dashboard/folder) will be missing from List results until permCache TTL (30s) expires, contradicting the PR goal of fetching newly created resources.

title: DB fallback still uses stale cached folder tree
body: Even when Check() falls back to getIdentityPermissions on a cached-permission miss, checkPermission/checkInheritedPermissions calls buildFolderTree which returns the cached folderTree if present (shortCacheTTL 30s). A dashboard in a newly created folder, or a newly granted parent-folder permission, will still evaluate against the old tree and be denied. The PR refreshes permission scopes but never refreshes/invalidates folderCache, so inherited-permission checks remain stale.

title: Pause menu never renders in list view
body: In AlertRuleMenu.tsx canPause is now OR of ruler and prom (GrafanaProm) abilities, but rendering is still gated on `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)`. In the list view rulerRule is undefined by design, so even when grafanaPauseAbility is true the Pause item never renders. Users lose pause/unpause from the list.

title: Delete menu never renders without rulerRule
body: canDelete is OR of ruler and prom abilities, but the Delete Menu.Item is gated on `canDelete && rulerRule`. GrafanaRuleListItem no longer passes rulerRule, so Delete never appears in the list even for users with delete permission, despite handleDelete path in RuleActionsButtons supporting prom-only identifiers.

title: Silence action does nothing prom-only
body: RuleActionsButtons now allows Silence via promRule ability and passes handleSilence to AlertRuleMenu, but the drawer is rendered only if `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` where `rule` is the optional RulerRuleDTO. When only promRule is provided (new list view) clicking Silence sets showSilenceDrawer true but no SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer is ever mounted, so the button appears to do nothing.

title: Missing key on Grafana list items
body: FilterViewResults maps rules to GrafanaRuleListItem without `key={key}` while datasource and unknown branches pass key. The key is still computed via getRuleKey but discarded for grafana origin, causing React key warnings, incorrect reconciliation on pagination/filter, and loss of the duplicate-key protection the key was added for.

title: Recording rules lose Export/Pause abilities
body: useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities gates ModifyExport, Pause, Restore and DeletePermanently on `isAlertingRule` (prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule). The old ruler-based version gated on any Grafana-managed rule (alerting or recording). Grafana recording rules have provenance/isPaused and should be exportable/pausable, so they now incorrectly get unsupported for those actions.

title: Missing React key on Grafana list item
body: In FilterViewResults the `grafana` case renders <GrafanaRuleListItem> without `key={key}` while the `datasource` and `unknown` cases pass `key`. The `key` field was computed to prevent duplication (`getRuleKey`). Without it React will warn and mis-reconcile list updates during infinite scroll/filtering, causing wrong rows to be reused or state to leak between rules.

title: Delete/Pause unreachable without rulerRule
body: AlertRuleMenu ORs ruler and prom abilities to compute canDelete/canPause, but rendering is still gated on ruler data: line 123 requires `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` for Pause and line 165 requires `rulerRule &&` for Delete. GrafanaRuleListItem in the list view now passes only promRule, so rulerRule is undefined and Delete/Pause never render even when grafana abilities allow them, breaking delete/pause from the alert list.

title: Silence drawer never opens for prom-only rules
body: RuleActionsButtons shows Silence menu via promRule abilities, but the drawer is gated on `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` where `rule` is the optional rulerRule. When only promRule is provided (new list view), the condition is always false, so clicking Silence notifications sets showSilenceDrawer but renders nothing. The user gets no drawer and no error.

title: Missing React key on Grafana list item
body: In FilterViewResults the grafana branch now renders <GrafanaRuleListItem> without key={key} while the datasource and unknown branches still pass key. Without a stable key React will warn and can reuse the wrong component instance when rules are appended during infinite scroll, causing incorrect state, actions, or expanded content per row.

title: Silence drawer never opens for prom-only rules
body: AlertRuleMenu now derives canSilence from promRule so Silence notifications can appear in the ruler-less list view, but the drawer is still gated on rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) with the ruler DTO. When only promRule is present, handleSilence sets showSilenceDrawer to true yet the SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer which requires rulerRule is never rendered, so clicking Silence appears to do nothing.

title: Federated-rule immutability check removed
body: useAllRulerRuleAbilities hardcodes isFederated to false with a TODO, and useAllAlertRuleAbilities was refactored to delegate without passing the CombinedRule group. Previously federated groups detected via isFederatedRuleGroup made rules immutable for Update/Delete/Pause/Restore. Now federated Mimir/Cortex rules are treated as mutable, so UI can offer edit, delete, pause and duplicate on rules that should be blocked.

title: Early interpolation defeats $__range no-split guard
body: runSplitQuery() now calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables() before querySupportsSplitting(). querySupportsSplitting() excludes queries where isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr) is true because $__range must be interpolated per split chunk on the backend. After up-front interpolation the expr no longer contains $__range, so the check never fires, the query is time-split, and every chunk keeps the full-range value baked in at line 296-300. The result is wrong $__range_s/$__range_ms values in split sub-queries.

title: Queries interpolated twice on shard-split path
body: runShardSplitQuery() interpolates with applyTemplateVariables at line 48-52 and then delegates each shard group to runSplitQuery(), which interpolates again at querySplitting.ts. The updated test expects 5 applyTemplateVariables calls for a single target (1 + 1 per shard group). This is redundant work that grows with shard count and time chunks, and risks double-expansion of non-idempotent variables.

title: Filter-before-interpolate changes empty-query handling
body: runShardSplitQuery now does request.targets.filter(query.expr).filter(!hide).map(applyTemplateVariables). The old code called interpolateVariablesInQueries first and then filtered on the interpolated expr. A query whose raw expr is truthy but interpolates to empty (e.g. a variable that resolves to empty) will now be kept and sent to fetchLabelValues / sharding instead of being dropped, and a query with empty raw expr that would interpolate to a selector is now dropped. Filtering must happen after interpolation to preserve the old semantics.

title: Empty check runs on uninterpolated expr
body: runSplitQuery filters on query.expr and only then maps through datasource.applyTemplateVariables. Queries that become empty only after interpolation (variable resolves to empty string) will still be grouped, time-partitioned and executed, and the hidden/empty tracking expectations no longer match the executed targets. The empty-expr filter should be applied to the interpolated query, not the raw query.

title: Shard path interpolates twice via nested runSplitQuery
body: runShardSplitQuery interpolates with applyTemplateVariables and then delegates each shard group to runSplitQuery, which interpolates again. The updated test expects applyTemplateVariables to be called 5 times for a single target instead of 1. Repeated template replacement is wasted work and unsafe if replacement is not idempotent (an interpolated value containing $ or $__ syntax would be re-expanded/corrupted on the second pass).

title: Shard path interpolates template variables twice
body: runShardSplitQuery() now maps targets through datasource.applyTemplateVariables() at line 52, but the sub-request it builds is later passed to runSplitQuery() (shardQuerySplitting.ts line 163 -> querySplitting.ts line 296), which now also maps targets through applyTemplateVariables(). The same logical query is therefore interpolated twice, including re-application of request.filters ad-hoc filters. Template replacement is idempotent but ad-hoc filter injection is not, so the second pass can duplicate label matchers in the expr and change query semantics. The updated test expecting 5 calls instead of 1 confirms the double execution.

title: MetricsMiddleware shares one mutable instance across all decorated clients
body: NewMetricsMiddleware creates a single MetricsMiddleware once and the middleware func does imw.next = next; return imw. Every decorated client therefore shares the same object and overwrites next. If two clients are decorated, the first client's next is replaced, and concurrent decoration/use races on imw.next. The new ContextualLoggerMiddleware in the same PR correctly allocates a new struct per next; MetricsMiddleware should do the same.

title: ContextualLoggerMiddleware dereferences request without nil check
body: QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth and CollectMetrics unconditionally read req.PluginContext. LoggerMiddleware in the same chain explicitly guards if req == nil and passes through, so a nil request is expected to be tolerated. With ContextualLoggerMiddleware placed before LoggerMiddleware in CreateMiddlewares, a nil request panics in instrumentContext before it ever reaches the nil guard.

title: TestLogger.FromContext discards logs by returning a new logger
body: FromContext returns NewTestLogger() instead of the receiver. Code under test now logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), so logs go to the fresh instance and the original TestLogger records zero calls. Any test asserting on InfoLogs/WarnLogs/ErrorLogs of the injected logger will silently see nothing, hiding regressions.

title: LoggerMiddleware drops traceID and plugin fields with no fallback
body: The diff removes explicit pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName, dsUID and traceID from logParams and relies solely on m.logger.FromContext(ctx). The new instrumentContext in contextual_logger_middleware.go only adds endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID and uname, never traceID from tracing.TraceIDFromContext. Plugin Request Completed logs therefore lose trace correlation, and any standalone use of LoggerMiddleware without the outer ContextualLoggerMiddleware loses all plugin context.

title: TestLogger.FromContext discards log state
body: TestLogger.FromContext returns NewTestLogger() instead of itself. LoggerMiddleware now logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), so calls made through the middleware are recorded on a fresh discarded instance, not on the injected fake. Tests asserting InfoLogs.Calls/Message on the original fake will see zero calls and cannot verify pluginId/endpoint/error logging.

title: Adding FromContext breaks Logger implementers
body: The Logger interface gains a new required method FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger. Any existing out-of-tree implementation of plugins/log.Logger will fail to compile after this change. This is a breaking interface change done as a chore/rename with no deprecation or adapter.

title: Plugin request logs lose traceID and identifying fields
body: LoggerMiddleware.logRequest previously logged pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName, dsUID and traceID (via tracing.TraceIDFromContext) explicitly. The new version only logs status, duration, eventName and time_before_plugin_request and relies on m.logger.FromContext(ctx). The new ContextualLoggerMiddleware.instrumentContext only adds endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname and never adds traceID, so the traceID correlation and any fields when the contextual middleware is absent or ordered differently are permanently lost from 'Plugin Request Completed' logs.

title: Streaming endpoints skip contextual logger
body: QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth and CollectMetrics wrap the context with instrumentContext, but SubscribeStream, PublishStream and RunStream just forward ctx unchanged. Those streaming requests therefore never get endpoint/pluginId/ds/uname contextual attributes, so downstream logging via FromContext for streams is inconsistent with the other endpoints even though those request types also carry a PluginContext.

title: TestLogger.FromContext discards logs
body: TestLogger.FromContext in pkg/plugins/log/fake.go returns NewTestLogger() instead of the receiver. LoggerMiddleware now logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), so with this fake the Info call goes to a throwaway instance and the injected TestLogger never records Calls/Message/Ctx. Any test asserting on the original logger will see zero calls and cannot verify logging.

title: Missing nil guard causes panic on nil request
body: ContextualLoggerMiddleware.QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics in pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/contextual_logger_middleware.go dereference req (e.g. req.PluginContext) without checking req == nil. LoggerMiddleware in the same package explicitly handles nil requests, proving nil can occur. With the new ordering the contextual middleware runs before the logger middleware, so a nil request panics instead of being passed through.

title: traceID no longer logged for plugin requests
body: LoggerMiddleware.logRequest in pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/logger_middleware.go removed the explicit traceID, pluginId, endpoint, dsName/dsUID, uname fields and now relies only on m.logger.FromContext(ctx). The new instrumentContext only adds endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname and never adds traceID. The result is Plugin Request Completed logs lose traceID correlation that was previously added via tracing.TraceIDFromContext.

title: Adding FromContext breaks Logger implementers
body: The Logger interface in pkg/plugins/log/ifaces.go gains a new required method FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger. Any out-of-tree implementation of plugins/log.Logger that previously satisfied the interface will fail to compile after this change. This is a breaking API contract change introduced as a chore/rename.

title: Local cache is populated before DB write, letting limit-blocked devices bypass limit
body: tagDeviceUI() checks localCache, then calls localCache.SetDefault(key) before calling anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice(). If CreateOrUpdateDevice fails with ErrDeviceLimitReached, the cache entry remains. The next request for the same new deviceID will hit the cache and return nil without touching the DB, so Authenticate will succeed. A rejected device is therefore only rejected once per ~29m cache TTL and then allowed, defeating the device limit.

title: Expired devices can never re-register once limit is reached
body: When count >= deviceLimit, CreateOrUpdateDevice delegates to updateDevice which does UPDATE ... WHERE device_id=? AND updated_at BETWEEN ? AND ?. A device that exists but whose updated_at is older than anonymousDeviceExpiration (30d) matches 0 rows, so updateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. The count query only counts active devices in the last 30d, so this stale device is not counted but is still rejected and can never be re-inserted/updated. Returning devices after expiry are permanently locked out while the limit is saturated.

title: Count-then-write limit check is racy and unenforceable under concurrency
body: CreateOrUpdateDevice does CountDevices() then, in a separate session/statement, either updateDevice or INSERT. There is no transaction, row lock, or unique-count constraint. Concurrent anonymous logins can both observe count < limit and both INSERT, overshooting the limit. Conversely two concurrent inserts for the same new device can race. The limit cannot be reliably enforced with this check-then-act pattern.

title: ProvideAnonymousDeviceService signature breaks DI/wire contract
body: ProvideAnonymousDeviceService changed its third parameter from anonStore anonstore.AnonStore (interface) to sqlStore db.DB and now constructs the store internally with cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit. Any wire provider, test, or downstream (e.g. enterprise) constructing the service by injecting a mocked AnonStore will fail to build. It also removes the ability to decorate/mock the store and couples the service to a concrete DB, an unnecessary breaking API change; the limit could be passed as a separate param while keeping the store injectable.

title: Anonymous auth now blocks on synchronous DB write
body: Authenticate() previously tagged the device in a background goroutine with its own timeout and never blocked login. It now calls anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...) synchronously on the request context, which when device_limit is enabled does a COUNT plus an INSERT/UPDATE on every anonymous request. This adds DB latency to the hot auth path and makes anonymous logins fail/slow when the DB is slow, and request cancellation aborts the tag. The tagging should stay async or use a detached context with timeout, with only the limit-reached case enforced synchronously if needed.

title: Device limit check has TOCTOU race, limit can be bypassed
body: CreateOrUpdateDevice() does CountDevices() then, if count < limit, falls through to an unconditional upsert INSERT ... ON CONFLICT. Two concurrent requests for two new devices can both observe count < limit and both insert, exceeding the limit. There is no unique-count enforcement in the DB, transaction, or advisory lock. Under burst anonymous traffic the configured limit is not actually enforced.

title: Any zero-row update is reported as device-limit-reached
body: updateDevice() returns ErrDeviceLimitReached whenever RowsAffected == 0. That conflates 'new device, limit reached' (intended) with 'device row is older than 30 days so outside the BETWEEN window', 'row was just deleted by cleanup', or transient zero-row cases. In particular a stale device returning after 30d of inactivity (row still present until the 61d cleanup) can never refresh once the limit is reached, and a legit insert that lost a race is misreported. Callers in client.go treat this error as fatal auth failure, so misclassification locks users out.

title: Provider signature change breaks DI and testability
body: ProvideAnonymousDeviceService() changed its injected dependency from anonStore anonstore.AnonStore to sqlStore db.DB and now constructs the store internally with cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit. This breaks any existing wire caller/test that supplied a custom AnonStore (e.g. mocks/fakes), removes the ability to decorate the store, and hides the limit wiring inside the constructor. Keep accepting AnonStore (or both) and wire ProvideAnonDBStore separately so DI graph and tests remain stable.

title: AnonymousDeviceLimit serializes 0 instead of omitting unlimited
body: FrontendSettingsDTO.AnonymousDeviceLimit is int64 without omitempty, so the unlimited default (0) is sent as 0 while the TypeScript config declares anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined. Frontend code cannot distinguish 'unlimited' from 'limit of 0', risking a UI that thinks no devices are allowed. Use *int64 with omitempty or omit zero, matching other optional frontend settings.

title: Failed device tag is cached, disabling the limit
body: tagDeviceUI does localCache.SetDefault(key) before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice, and never removes it on error. When CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the caller in client.go denies auth once, but the key is now cached, so the next request from the same new device hits `if _, ok := localCache.Get(key); ok { return nil }` and succeeds without touching the DB. The device limit is therefore only enforced once per device per cache lifetime (~29m) and then bypassed.

title: updateDevice uses ? placeholders on all dialects
body: updateDevice builds `UPDATE anon_device ... WHERE device_id = ? ...` with `?` placeholders for every database, while CreateOrUpdateDevice in the same file special-cases Postgres to use $1..$5. On Postgres the update path (the only path taken when count >= deviceLimit) will fail with a syntax/argument error instead of returning ErrDeviceLimitReached or updating, so the limit feature is broken on Postgres.

title: Count-then-insert check is not atomic
body: CreateOrUpdateDevice does CountDevices, then if count >= limit calls updateDevice, otherwise does INSERT. Two concurrent requests for two different new devices can both observe count < limit and both INSERT, overshooting the limit. There is no unique-constraint/transaction guard on the count, so the limit cannot be strictly enforced under concurrency or across multiple Grafana instances.

title: Anonymous auth now blocks on DB synchronously
body: Authenticate was changed from fire-and-forget goroutine with background context and timeout to synchronous `TagDevice(ctx, ...)` using the request context. Every anonymous request with a cache-miss device now pays for CountDevices plus INSERT/UPDATE in the auth path, adding latency and making anonymous login availability depend on the anon_device table. A slow table or cancelled request context directly slows/fails authentication.

title: Service constructor now takes db.DB instead of AnonStore
body: ProvideAnonymousDeviceService signature was changed from `anonStore anonstore.AnonStore` to `sqlStore db.DB` and internally calls ProvideAnonDBStore. This breaks wire DI overrides, enterprise patches, and tests that inject a fake/mock AnonStore, and removes the seam that allowed testing the service without a real DB. It should keep accepting the interface and wire the limit into the store provider instead.

title: Cleanup ticker interval reduced 10x without justification
body: cleanup.go changes the background cleanup ticker from 10 minutes to 1 minute. The PR description only discusses annotation deadlock avoidance and does not justify running all cleanup jobs (snapshots, dashboard versions, images, invites, short URLs, query history, annotations) 10x more often. This greatly increases DB load and may itself worsen contention. Revert to 10 minutes or justify separately.

title: Loop terminates on zero rows-affected instead of zero rows-fetched
body: untilDoneOrCancelled stops when affected==0. In the new fetch-then-delete split, affected is RowsAffected from DELETE BY IDs. If IDs were fetched (len(ids)>0) but the DELETE affected 0 rows due to concurrent deletion or race, the loop exits as done even though more rows matching the condition may remain. Termination must be based on empty fetch (len(ids)==0), not on delete row count. Consequence is premature stop and leftover expired annotations/tags that should have been deleted in this cycle.

title: Leftover Error-level logging dumps full ID batches every cycle
body: CleanAnnotations and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags log at Error level on every batch with count, full ids slice (up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize, tested at 32767), cond and err (lines 534,537,554,557,576,579). This will spam error logs on every cleanup run, inflate log storage, hurt performance formatting tens of thousands of IDs, and mask real errors. These were clearly debug statements and should be removed or demoted to Debug.

title: Unrelated 10x increase in cleanup frequency
body: The ticker was changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute with no mention in the PR description. This runs all cleanup jobs (snapshots, versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs, query history) 10x as often, increasing DB and I/O load cluster-wide. Revert unless intentional.

title: Debug logging left at Error level with full ID lists
body: CleanAnnotations and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags log at r.log.Error on every batch, including the full ids slice, cond and err (lines 534,537,554,557,576,579). A batch can hold tens of thousands of IDs, so every cleanup run will spam error logs and can blow up log volume/storage. These should be Debug or removed before merge.

title: Split fetch/delete can exit early leaving work undone
body: untilDoneOrCancelled stops when a batch returns affected==0. With the new two-step flow a batch can fetch non-empty ids but have deleteByIDs report 0 RowsAffected due to a concurrent deleter already removing those rows. The loop then returns success while matching rows still remain, deferring them to the next cycle or stalling max-count enforcement. Termination should be based on empty fetch, not zero rows-affected.

title: SQLite fallback builds IN-list quadratically and on wrong condition
body: The SQLite large-batch path is chosen when cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > 999 rather than len(ids) > 999, so small trailing batches still take the string-interpolation path. Worse, it builds the list with repeated fmt.Sprintf in a loop, which is O(n^2) copying for batches up to 32767 IDs. Check len(ids) and use strings.Builder.

title: Cleanup ticker changed from 10m to 1m
body: The diff changes the background cleanup ticker from every 10 minutes to every 1 minute with no mention in the PR description. That runs all cleanup jobs (snapshots, versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs, query history) 10x more often, adding significant DB and IO load. Revert to 10 minutes or justify the change separately.

title: Debug logging left at Error level with full ID lists
body: CleanAnnotations and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags log every batch with r.log.Error including the full ids slice, cond and err (lines around 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, 579). On a normal run this emits Error-level logs continuously, will trip error alerting/dashboards, and for large batches (test uses 32767 IDs) dumps tens of thousands of IDs per iteration causing log volume and performance problems. These should be removed or demoted to Debug.

title: Async legacy write inherits request context and is cancelled
body: Create (and Delete/Update/DeleteCollection) spawn `go func()` deriving the async context with `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)` where `ctx` is the request context. When the API request completes the request context is cancelled, so the background legacy write is immediately cancelled / times out and legacy silently diverges from storage. The async context must be detached, e.g. derive from `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` or `context.Background()` with values copied.

title: Storage error recorded as legacy metric
body: In `Create` when `d.Storage.Create` fails the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` with the storage start time. The same mistake is in `Update` at line 129. Storage failures are therefore counted against legacy latency/error metrics and storage metrics miss the failure, corrupting dashboards/alerts for mode 3.

title: Delete storage metric uses name as kind label
body: In `Delete` the success path calls `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, ...)` passing the object name where the kind label is expected (error path correctly uses `options.Kind`). This creates high-cardinality / wrong kind labels for delete metrics.

title: Legacy DeleteCollection recorded as storage metric
body: In `DeleteCollection` the async legacy goroutine calls `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...)` for the legacy call. It should call `d.recordLegacyDuration`. Legacy delete-collection latency/errors are attributed to storage and legacy metrics are never emitted.

title: Delete installs wrong logger in context
body: In `Delete` the code builds `log` with name/kind/method values but then does `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` instead of `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, log)`. All other methods install the enriched `log`. Downstream storage/legacy calls from Delete lose the per-request fields.

title: Async legacy write races on input object / objInfo
body: The `go func()` closures capture and use `obj` in `Create` and `objInfo, createValidation, updateValidation, options` in `Update` without a deep copy. The caller may mutate/reuse the object after return and `Storage.Create/Update` may mutate it in place, so the concurrent legacy write races with the caller and can write corrupted/divergent data. A copy must be made before spawning the goroutine, and the returned `created`/`res` object should be the source for legacy, not the pre-storage input.

title: Create error path records legacy metric instead of storage metric
body: In DualWriterMode3.Create when Storage.Create fails the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) with startStorage. No storage call succeeded and no legacy call was made, so the storage failure is recorded under the legacy histogram and the storage histogram misses the failure. The same copy-paste error is in Update at line 129. This corrupts mode/kind/method duration metrics and hides storage errors.

title: Delete success records storage duration with object name as kind
body: In DualWriterMode3.Delete the success path calls d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage) passing the object name where every other call passes options.Kind. The kind label will get unbounded high-cardinality values (one per object name) and dashboards/alerts grouped by kind will be wrong for mode 3 deletes.

title: DeleteCollection legacy completion recorded as storage duration
body: In DualWriterMode3.DeleteCollection the background goroutine finishes a Legacy.DeleteCollection call but reports it with d.recordStorageDuration(... startLegacy). It should be d.recordLegacyDuration like Create/Delete/Update do. Legacy delete-collection latency/errors will appear under the storage metric and legacy metric will miss them.

title: Async legacy write derives timeout context from request context
body: Create (line 51), Delete (line 110), Update (line 135) and DeleteCollection (line 163) do go func() { ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...) ; d.Legacy.*(ctx, ...) } capturing the incoming request ctx. When the API request finishes the request context is cancelled, so the fire-and-forget legacy write can be cancelled before it runs, defeating the mode-3 goal of keeping legacy as a safety copy. An async write must use a detached context such as context.WithoutCancel(ctx) or context.Background() with timeout, not the live request context.

title: Async legacy writes silently drop errors and use stale object
body: Create passes the original obj to Legacy.Create in the background goroutine instead of the created object returned by Storage, so server-assigned defaults/resourceVersion are not propagated to legacy and stores diverge. More generally all four write paths (Create line 55, Delete line 112, Update line 139, DeleteCollection line 165) discard the legacy error with only a metrics counter and no log, so legacy/unified drift in mode 3 is invisible. At minimum log the legacy failure with the object identity.

title: Delete installs wrong logger in context
body: Delete builds log with name/kind/method but then does ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log) instead of klog.NewContext(ctx, log) as Create/Update/List do. The per-request fields are dropped from the context logger, so subsequent storage/legacy log calls lose the name/kind context.

title: Async legacy write inherits cancelled request context
body: Create, Update, Delete and DeleteCollection all do `go func() { ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx,...)` where `ctx` is the request-scoped context. Once the handler returns the parent context is cancelled, so the 10s timeout child is immediately cancelled and the legacy write is aborted. The consequence is mode 3 silently never mirrors to legacy, defeating its safety purpose. Use a detached context e.g. `context.WithoutCancel` / `context.Background()` plus timeout and copy of logger/values.

title: Reusing UpdatedObjectInfo concurrently in background goroutine
body: Update calls `d.Storage.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)` synchronously and then passes the same `objInfo` to `d.Legacy.Update` in a `go` routine. `rest.UpdatedObjectInfo.UpdatedObject()` is generally single-use and not safe for concurrent/repeated evaluation, and the previous implementation deliberately wrapped the already-computed `updated` object in an `updateWrapper`. Re-invoking it for legacy can return a different object, fail, or race, causing legacy/storage divergence.

title: Legacy Create uses pre-storage input object instead of created result
body: Create writes `created` back to the caller but asynchronously writes the original input `obj` to legacy. Any defaults, UIDs, resourceVersions or mutations applied by unified storage are lost in legacy, guaranteeing permanent divergence between the two stores. The legacy call should use the `created` object snapshot.

title: Storage Create failure recorded as legacy duration
body: When `d.Storage.Create` fails, Create calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` with `startStorage`. The same copy-paste error exists on the Update storage-error path at line 129. This misattributes storage latency/errors to legacy metrics, hiding storage outages and breaking dashboards/alerts keyed on mode/kind/method.

title: Delete records object name in kind label
body: On successful storage Delete the code calls `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, ...)` passing the object `name` where every other call passes `options.Kind`. This creates unbounded high-cardinality metric label values (one series per object name) and makes delete latency unqueryable by kind.

title: Legacy DeleteCollection recorded as storage duration
body: The background legacy DeleteCollection path calls `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...)` instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration`. Legacy delete-collection latency/errors will never appear under the legacy metric and will pollute storage metrics.

title: Delete drops enriched logger context
body: Delete builds `log := d.Log.WithValues("name", name, "kind", ..., "method", ...)` but then does `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` instead of using `log` like Create/Update/DeleteCollection do. Request-scoped logs and the background legacy delete lose name/kind/method fields, hindering debugging.

title: Exclusive lock held across slow I/O with no re-check
body: In pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go GetWebAssets takes entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock() and then does readWebAssetsFromCDN (network) and readWebAssetsFromFile (disk) while still holding it, and never re-checks the cache after acquiring the write lock. This means every cache miss serializes all other callers, including fast-path cache hits that only need RLock, behind file/network latency, and N concurrent missers will each reload sequentially (thundering herd) instead of one winner populating the cache. Fix with double-checked locking and load outside the critical section: RLock check, unlock, load, then Lock only to publish (with a second check for non-Dev mode).

title: Missing second cache check after acquiring write lock
body: After the RLock fast-path miss, GetWebAssets acquires entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock() but never re-checks entryPointAssetsCache before doing I/O. Two goroutines that miss concurrently will therefore both read assets-manifest.json / CDN sequentially and both overwrite the global. Worse, a loser that fails can overwrite a winner's good value with nil. Re-check the cache under the write lock and return early if it is now populated.

title: Failed load overwrites valid cache with nil
body: entryPointAssetsCache = result is executed unconditionally, even when readWebAssetsFromFile/readWebAssetsFromCDN returned an error and result is nil. In Dev mode (where the early return is bypassed) or on concurrent missed loads, this discards a previously cached good value and forces every subsequent request to fail/re-read instead of falling back to stale good assets. Only assign the global on success (err == nil && result != nil).

title: Write lock held across file and network I/O
body: GetWebAssets acquires entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock() at line 48 and holds it (via defer Unlock) while doing readWebAssetsFromCDN (HTTP request) and readWebAssetsFromFile (disk I/O) at lines 56 and 60. Every concurrent caller, including the RLock fast-path readers, blocks for the full I/O latency. In Dev mode where the cache is bypassed on every call, this serializes all requests. The load should be done outside the lock with only publish under lock plus a second cache check.

title: Missing second cache check after acquiring write lock
body: The fast-path check at line 45 reads the cache under RLock, but after acquiring the write lock at line 48 the cache is never re-checked before doing I/O. Concurrent cache misses all proceed to read and parse assets-manifest.json (and potentially fetch CDN) redundantly instead of only the first miss loading and the rest reusing it.

title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false but still dereferences feature flag
body: pkg/expr/reader.go: enableSqlExpressions computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions)` then returns false on both branches. Since the intent is to unconditionally disable SQL expressions, it should just return false. As written it needlessly dereferences h/h.features, so a nil reader or nil FeatureToggles panics instead of returning the safe 'not implemented' error, turning a blocked query into a crash/DoS, and the inverted negation leaves a trap where a future edit to re-enable will enable when the flag is off.

title: tablesFromAST indexes ast[0] without length check
body: pkg/expr/sql/parser.go: tablesFromAST does `flatten.Flatten(ast[0], ...)` with no check that ast is non-empty. A JSON payload of `[]` (e.g. empty result from RunCommands / json_serialize_sql) causes an index-out-of-range panic, crashing the query path. Caller TablesList only checks json.Unmarshal error, not len(ast)==0, so an attacker-controlled SQL string that serializes to an empty array causes DoS.

title: NoData result immediately overwritten by TableData
body: pkg/expr/sql_command.go: Execute sets `rsp.Values = NoData{Frame}` when `frame.Rows()==0` then unconditionally overwrites it on the next lines with `rsp.Values = TableData{Frame}`. The NoData branch is dead, so empty SQL results are never reported as NoData, breaking downstream no-data/alerting semantics.

title: enableSqlExpressions dereferences features without nil check causing panic
body: In pkg/expr/reader.go enableSqlExpressions unconditionally does h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...). The SQL path previously never touched features, so callers/tests with a nil *ExpressionQueryReader or nil FeatureToggles worked. Now a SQL query with such a reader panics with nil-pointer/nil-interface dereference instead of returning the controlled "sqlExpressions is not implemented" error, turning a rejected query into a server panic/DoS.

title: Legacy SQL entry point has no explicit disabled guard
body: In pkg/expr/sql_command.go UnmarshalSQLCommand/NewSQLCommand has no enableSqlExpressions check. The PR only guards ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery in pkg/expr/reader.go and relies on the stub sql.DB in pkg/expr/sql/db.go returning "not implemented" from TablesList to fail NewSQLCommand. Any caller of the legacy rawNode path, direct construction of SQLCommand, mock DB, or future restoration of a real DB bypasses the explicit disable and re-exposes SQL execution/RCE that this CVE fix is supposed to hard-disable. Both entry points need an explicit reject.

title: NoData result is unconditionally overwritten
body: In pkg/expr/sql_command.go Execute(), when frame.Rows() == 0 rsp.Values is set to mathexp.NoData and then unconditionally overwritten on the next lines with mathexp.TableData. The empty-result branch is dead, so callers never see NoData for SQL expressions and always get an empty table instead.

title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false and adds nil-toggle panic risk
body: In pkg/expr/reader.go enableSqlExpressions() computes enabled as negated flag then returns false on both branches, so it always disables SQL. It also newly dereferences h.features.IsEnabledGlobally on the SQL path which previously did not touch feature toggles, so a nil or missing FeatureToggles where SQL previously parsed will now panic instead of returning an error.

title: Data race on init counter
body: In searchSupport.init totalBatchesIndexed++ executes concurrently in multiple errgroup goroutines limited by initWorkers with no atomic/mutex protection. This is a data race that corrupts the count reported in the 'namespaces indexed' span event and can be detected by -race. Use an atomic counter or collect results after group.Wait.

title: Concurrent BuildIndex for same key can corrupt index
body: The change removes the mutex covering the whole BuildIndex and only locks around the final cache store. Two concurrent builds for the same NamespacedResource (from init workers plus getOrCreateIndex/Search/watch paths) can now both call bleve.New on the same file directory, both run the builder, both increment IndexTenants metrics, and then last-writer-wins in the map, leaking the loser. There is no per-key singleflight/locking to prevent duplicate builds.

title: TotalDocs reads cache map without lock
body: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without holding cacheMu while BuildIndex writes b.cache[key] under Lock and GetIndex reads under RLock. With the new finer-grained locking builds run highly concurrently, so this is a concurrent map read/write race that can panic or corrupt. The read must hold RLock.

title: Failed Init leaks server context
body: NewResourceServer creates a cancelable context for the server, stores cancel in the server struct, then calls s.Init(ctx) synchronously. On Init error it returns nil, err without calling cancel, leaking the context and any resources started before the failure. Call cancel before returning the error.

title: History/Origin panic when search disabled
body: Search checks s.search == nil, but History calls s.search.History and Origin calls s.search.Origin unconditionally. When SearchOptions.Resources is nil (search disabled) these RPCs nil-dereference and panic the gRPC server. With lazy Init removed there is no other guard. Add the same nil check as Search.

title: Postgres storage-server path skipped
body: The test now skips whenever GRAFANA_TEST_DB is postgres, so the storage-server target with instrumentation server is never exercised on postgres in CI. Since the PR moves unified storage initialization to startup and changes lifecycle ordering, losing that coverage risks regressions on the postgres dialect going unnoticed.

title: BuildIndex no longer prevents duplicate builds for same key
body: BuildIndex in bleve.go removed the coarse lock that serialized whole builds and now only locks around the final map insert. getOrCreateIndex does check-then-build (GetIndex returns nil, then BuildIndex), so two concurrent Search/init workers for the same NamespacedResource can both enter BuildIndex. For file-backed indexes both will call bleve.New on the same directory, one will fail or corrupt, and metrics IndexTenants is incremented twice. One overwrites the other in the cache, leaking the loser. Need per-key singleflight/mutex.

title: TotalDocs reads cache map without lock
body: TotalDocs in bleve.go iterates b.cache without holding cacheMu, while GetIndex takes RLock and BuildIndex takes Lock for writes. If a late index is built via Search/getOrCreateIndex concurrent with TotalDocs (called during init logging), this is a concurrent map read/write data race and can panic. Hold RLock in TotalDocs.

title: init errgroup closure races on shared err and counter
body: searchSupport.init in search.go launches one goroutine per stat that does totalBatchesIndexed++ and _,_,err = s.build(...). Both totalBatchesIndexed and err are outer variables shared by all goroutines with no atomic/mutex and no shadowing. This is a data race, corrupts the indexed count in the trace event and can clobber errors. Use local variables and atomic counter.

title: Stop mutates initErr without synchronization
body: server in server.go guards initialization with sync.Once and initErr, but Stop unconditionally assigns s.initErr. Concurrent Init (or NewResourceServer init) and Stop access initErr without a mutex, causing a data race. Stop also poisons future Init calls to return 'service is stopped' even if startup already succeeded. Guard initErr with mutex/atomic.

title: History/Origin panic when search is not configured
body: Search in server.go checks s.search == nil, but History and Origin directly dereference s.search.History/Origin. When SearchOptions.Resources is nil, s.search is nil and those RPCs panic with nil dereference. Add the same nil guard as Search.

title: New postgres skip hides storage-server failure
body: module_server_test.go adds an unconditional skip for postgres for the storage-server instrumentation test. This reduces coverage for the exact backend this PR touches (unified storage init/startup) and can hide the regression the PR is fixing. Fix or track the test instead of skipping.

title: TotalDocs reads cache without lock while BuildIndex writes
body: bleveBackend.TotalDocs iterates b.cache without any RWMutex, while BuildIndex now does b.cacheMu.Lock()/Unlock() around b.cache[key]=idx. After the PR removed the coarse lock around the whole BuildIndex, concurrent index builds race with TotalDocs and with GetIndex. This is a data race that can corrupt map iteration, panic with concurrent map read/write, and return wrong counts when called from searchSupport.init logging.

title: Concurrent BuildIndex for same key can duplicate work and corrupt file index
body: The PR removed the b.cacheMu.Lock around the entire BuildIndex to allow parallelism, leaving only a short lock for the final cache insert. There is no per-key singleflight/dedup (getOrCreateIndex even has a TODO about it). Two goroutines building the same NamespacedResource can now both run bleve.New on the same directory, both run the builder, both Inc IndexTenants, and last-writer-wins in the map, leaking the other index. For file-backed indexes this races on the same on-disk path.

title: Search watch goroutine never exits and panics on closed channel
body: searchSupport.init creates watchctx as context.Background() and loops as for { v := <-events; s.handleEvent(watchctx,v) } with no ok check and no select on context cancellation. If the storage WatchWriteEvents channel is closed, receive returns nil and handleEvent dereferences evt.Type causing a nil-pointer panic. The goroutine also has no stop condition tied to server Stop, leaking forever and keeping Background-derived work alive.

title: totalBatchesIndexed incremented concurrently without synchronization
body: In searchSupport.init each errgroup goroutine does totalBatchesIndexed++ with no mutex or atomic. With initWorkers >1 this is a data race, and the span attribute namespaces_indexed logged at the end can be wrong or trigger the race detector.

title: Integration test disabled for postgres instead of fixed
body: The PR adds a skip for postgres in TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer with comment test not working in Drone. This removes coverage for the unified-storage startup path on postgres exactly when startup initialization behavior changed, hiding regressions the PR could introduce.

title: handleEvent uses IndexMetrics without nil check
body: handleEvent calls IndexMetrics.IndexedKinds.Inc/Dec and IndexMetrics.IndexLatency.Observe unconditionally, while init guards with if IndexMetrics != nil. If metrics are not registered (tests, nil global), any watch event panics the background indexing goroutine and kills search updates.

title: Call to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not match its signature
body: UsernameForm.authenticate calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only definition in the parent UsernamePasswordForm is isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) which requires a user argument. Someone reading only this call cannot resolve it, and javac will fail with cannot find symbol. The re-authentication path in this file therefore does not compile.

title: Conditional passkeys now require a known user, breaking usernameless login
body: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) returns true only when user != null, and authenticate at line 115 and challenge at line 137 now gate webauthnAuth.fillContextForm on that predicate. Previously the form was filled whenever passkeys were enabled, even with no user set, which is exactly what WebAuthn conditional UI / discoverable passkeys need on the initial login page. With this change an anonymous first-factor login gets no ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI attribute, no challenge, and no webauth form, so usernameless passkey login/autofill is lost while only the re-authentication case with context.getUser() != null keeps working.

title: Call to undefined zero-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled breaks compilation
body: UsernameForm.authenticate calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but UsernamePasswordForm only defines isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user). AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator defines no such method. The code as shown does not compile, so the browser flow with UsernameForm cannot build/deploy.

title: Conditional passkeys only filled when user is set breaks usernameless login
body: authenticate() now calls webauthnAuth.fillContextForm only if isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), which requires user != null. For a fresh login context.getUser() is null, so no WebAuthn challenge / ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI is set on the initial username/password page. Discoverable passkeys / conditional UI therefore disappear on first login, contradicting the tests that expect form#webauth on the initial page.

title: Error challenge also suppresses passkeys for anonymous users
body: challenge(context,error,field) now only refills WebAuthn data when context.getUser() != null. Failed logins before a user is established (invalid username/password on the initial page) will re-render without the passkeys challenge, losing conditional UI after the first error.

title: shouldShow overridden without shouldDisplay causes inconsistent form state
body: shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators is forced to false for conditional UI, so IS_USER_IDENTIFIED is always false and ALLOWED_AUTHENTICATORS is never set, but shouldDisplayAuthenticators inherited from WebAuthnAuthenticator still returns true when context.getUser() != null. The login template can then be told to display authenticators with no list / as unidentified during re-authentication.

title: Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() breaks compilation
body: UsernameForm.java line 47 calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only definition in the parent UsernamePasswordForm.java (line 160) is isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) taking one argument. There is no no-arg overload in the hierarchy, so the code does not compile and no build with this change can succeed.

title: Conditional passkeys disabled for anonymous login, breaking discoverable logins
body: authenticate() was changed from filling WebAuthn conditional-UI data when passkeys are realm-enabled (previous code did it for the user==null branch) to only when isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) is true, which requires context.getUser() != null. First-visit login has no user, so no challenge, allow-list, or conditional-UI flag is prepared and discoverable passkey login on the initial username/password page stops working. The same inversion is in challenge(context,error,field) at line 137 (old: user==null, new: user!=null). The gate should be realm passkeys-enabled, not user!=null.

title: Re-authentication can no longer skip username step for users without passkeys
body: The skip-if-context-user-exists fast path is now disabled whenever the realm has passkeys enabled, because isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() only checks global feature + realm policy + user!=null, not whether that user actually has a passkey credential. As a result every re-authentication (e.g. prompt=login) in a passkeys-enabled realm forces the extra username form even for users who can never use passkeys, regressing the previous hasLinkedBrokers-only skip logic.

title: getForLogin ignores organization invalidations, serving stale login lists
body: getForLogin() only checks isInvalid(cacheKey) for the per-FetchMode key, while getByOrganization() in the same file checks isInvalid(cacheKey) || isInvalid(orgId). Linking/unlinking an IDP to an organization, removing an organization, or updating an organization via OrganizationProvider invalidates the org/orgId entries, not the .idp.login keys. A cached getForLogin(ORG_ONLY/ALL, orgId) list of internalIds will therefore not be refreshed and the login page will show removed/unlinked brokers or miss newly linked public brokers until natural eviction.

title: getLoginPredicate dereferences possibly-null IDP config
body: LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() now evaluates idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC). If an IdentityProviderModel has a null config map the call throws NullPointerException. The predicate is invoked on every create/remove/update invalidation path in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider (registerIDPLoginInvalidation / registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate), so a single IDP with null config breaks IDP writes with a 500 instead of correctly deciding to (not) invalidate the login caches.

title: Login predicate NPEs when IDP config is null
body: LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() now does idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC) without a null check. An IdentityProviderModel with a null config map (possible on create/update representations that set no config) will throw NullPointerException inside registerIDPLoginInvalidation / registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate, breaking create/update/remove. Use a null-safe config lookup.

title: Login cache not invalidated on organization link/unlink or org state change
body: getForLogin() caches ID lists per FetchMode, but invalidation is only registered from IDP create/update/remove. Linking/unlinking an IDP via OrganizationProvider, disabling/enabling/removing an Organization, or changing org membership does not call registerIDPLoginInvalidation, so the cached REALM_ONLY/ORG_ONLY/ALL ID sets become stale (e.g. a realm IDP linked to an org still appears in REALM_ONLY, a private org IDP still appears, or IDPs of a disabled org are still listed).

title: removeAll() and remove/update null paths leave login cache stale or NPE
body: removeAll() only invalidates the count key and never invalidates cacheKeyForLogin keys, so cached getForLogin results survive a bulk delete except by incidental self-heal. Separately, remove() dereferences storedIdp via registerIDPInvalidation() and update() dereferences original.getOrganizationId() without null checks, so removing/updating a non-existent alias/id throws NPE instead of delegating.

title: Login predicate NPEs when org-linked IDP has null config
body: In IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java getLoginPredicate() does idp.getConfig().get(...) without a null check. If an IDP linked to an organization has a null config map, calling the predicate throws NullPointerException. The predicate is now called on create/update/remove paths in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider to decide login-cache invalidation, so an admin create/update/remove of such an IDP fails instead of invalidating or skipping invalidation.

title: remove() NPEs when alias does not exist
body: In InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java remove() fetches storedIdp via idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) which is null when the alias does not exist, then unconditionally calls registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp) on the isInvalid(cacheKey) branch. registerIDPInvalidation dereferences idp.getInternalId() and idp.getAlias(), so removing a non-existent alias throws NullPointerException instead of returning false from idpDelegate.remove().

title: getForLogin cache not invalidated by organization lifecycle changes
body: In InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java getForLogin() caches ID sets per realm+FetchMode with organizationId as search key, but invalidation is only registered from IdentityProviderStorageProvider create/update/remove. Organization-level operations that change the login-visible set without touching the IDP model through that provider - e.g. organization disable/enable, organization removal, or direct org membership mapping changes - do not invalidate the .idp.login keys. The cached ID list is then stale and login pages can show IDPs that should be hidden or miss IDPs that should appear until the login keys happen to be invalidated by an unrelated IDP write.

title: Equal order values make provider selection nondeterministic
body: CryptoIntegration.detectProvider now sorts by CryptoProvider.order() reversed and picks index 0. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return order()=200, so ties are broken only by ServiceLoader iteration order, which is classpath dependent. The old code failed fast on multiple providers; the new code can silently pick a different crypto implementation (e.g. FIPS vs non-FIPS) depending on classpath ordering.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns unrelated KeyStore provider
body: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider(), i.e. whatever JCA provider supplies the default keystore type, not a BouncyCastle provider. Callers using this as the BouncyCastle/BCFIPS provider (algorithm lookups, BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER assumptions) will get the wrong provider or null behavior, causing NoSuchAlgorithm/NoSuchProvider failures or wrong implementations.

title: concatenatedRSToASN1DER lacks length validation
body: concatenatedRSToASN1DER splits signature with len=signLength/2 and System.arraycopy without checking that signature.length==signLength or that signLength is even/positive. A short, long, or odd signLength causes ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException or silent truncation/padding, producing a corrupt DER signature instead of a clean IOException.

title: Negative/oversized ECDSA integers silently truncated
body: asn1derToConcatenatedRS decodes r/s as BigInteger without checking sign or range, and integerToBytes() silently keeps only the low qLength bytes when bytes.length>qLength. A crafted DER with negative or oversized integers is truncated into a valid-looking concatenated signature instead of rejected, hiding malformed input and enabling signature malleability issues.

title: readSequence does not enforce exact DER length
body: readSequence() loops while(length>0) subtracting each TLV's total size but never checks for length<0, trailing bytes after the sequence, or indefinite-length (-1) encoding. Overlong inner elements make length go negative and silently succeed, and indefinite length returns an empty list, so malformed signatures are accepted or reported with a misleading error.

title: Most CryptoProvider operations throw UnsupportedOperationException
body: AuthzClientCryptoProvider throws UnsupportedOperationException for getSignature, getKeyFactory, getKeyPairGen, createECParams, getCertificateUtils, getPemUtils, getX509CertFactory and others. When authz-client runs standalone (only this provider on the classpath, which CryptoIntegration.init now auto-selects), any code path needing signing, JWT client authentication, or cert handling fails at runtime. Plain-JCA defaults could be returned without BouncyCastle.

title: Test reuses one EC key for all curves and never verifies
body: ECDSAAlgorithmTest generates a single KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC") key (typically P-256) and reuses it for ES256/ES384/ES512, then only asserts round-trip concatenated->DER->concatenated equality. It never verifies the signature with Signature.verify, so wrong signLength padding, truncation, or interop failures against real verifiers are not detected.

title: New abstract order() breaks external CryptoProvider implementations
body: CryptoProvider is a public SPI that third parties can implement. This PR adds `int order();` as an abstract method with no default. Any existing out-of-tree implementation will no longer compile or load (AbstractMethodError) after upgrading. The method should have a default (e.g. `default int order() { return 0; }`) to preserve binary/source compatibility.

title: Multiple crypto providers silently resolved by unstable order tie
body: detectProvider() previously failed when more than one CryptoProvider was on the classpath. It now sorts by order() reversed and picks the first. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return 200, so a classpath containing e.g. both default and FIPS providers ties and the winner depends on ServiceLoader/classpath order (stable sort preserves input order). This can silently run non-FIPS crypto in a FIPS deployment instead of failing fast.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns unrelated KeyStore provider
body: AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider() returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, e.g. SUN/JKS provider, not a BouncyCastle provider. Callers use this method to obtain BC-specific algorithms. Returning an arbitrary JCA provider is semantically wrong and will cause NoSuchAlgorithm or wrong-provider behavior; like WildFlyElytronProvider it should return null or throw UnsupportedOperationException.

title: DER decoder accepts indefinite-length encoding and trailing data
body: readLength() explicitly returns -1 for 0x80 indefinite-length encoding, which DER forbids, and readSequence() loops `while (length > 0)` without rejecting negative remainder or trailing bytes after the SEQUENCE. Malformed/crafted ECDSA signatures can therefore be accepted or mis-parsed instead of rejected by the authz-client signature conversion path.

title: Oversized ECDSA integers silently truncated instead of rejected
body: integerToBytes() used by asn1derToConcatenatedRS() truncates to the last qLength bytes when `bytes.length > qLength`. An r or s value larger than the curve size (e.g. more than qLength+1 bytes) should be rejected as an invalid signature, but here high-order bytes are silently dropped, masking invalid signatures and weakening signature validation.

title: ES384/ES512 tests reuse a P-256 key and prove nothing
body: The test generates one key with `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair()` (default P-256) and reuses it for ES256, ES384 and ES512, only varying the requested concatenated length. Converting a P-256 DER signature to 96/132-byte concatenations and back round-trips trivially but never exercises real P-384/P-521 keys, real signature sizes, or verification with Signature.verify, so bugs in those curves would not be caught.

title: New abstract method order() breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: CryptoProvider adds `int order();` without a `default` implementation. Any third-party or downstream implementation of CryptoProvider that compiled against the old interface will fail at runtime with AbstractMethodError and will fail to compile against the new interface. For a service-loaded SPI this is a breaking contract change. It should be a `default` method (e.g. `default int order() { return 0; }`) so old providers keep working and the new AuthzClientCryptoProvider with order 100 stays lowest priority.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns unrelated KeyStore provider
body: AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider() returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, typically the SUN/JDK provider, not a BouncyCastle provider. Callers use this method to obtain the BC/BCCFIPS provider for BC-specific operations. Returning an arbitrary JDK provider is misleading and will cause ClassCast or NoSuchAlgorithm failures when BC-specific behavior is expected. Like WildFlyElytronProvider it should return null or throw UnsupportedOperationException if no BC provider is available.

title: Authz client crypto provider cannot sign or load keys
body: AuthzClientCryptoProvider throws UnsupportedOperationException from getSignature, getKeyFactory, getKeyPairGen, createECParams, getCertificateUtils, getPemUtils and others. The authz-client needs those for common paths such as private_key_jwt client authentication, JWKS parsing and JWT verification via CryptoIntegration.getProvider(). With only this provider on the classpath, AuthzClient.create() now succeeds in CryptoIntegration.init but fails later with confusing UOE instead of working. Those methods should delegate to the default JCA (e.g. Signature.getInstance without provider, KeyFactory.getInstance) rather than unconditionally throwing.

title: Test reuses one P-256 key for ES384/ES512 and only round-trips
body: ECDSAAlgorithmTest generates a single default EC KeyPair (P-256) in the constructor and reuses it for ES256, ES384 and ES512, and only checks asn1->concat->DER->concat round-trip equality. It never verifies the signature, never exercises real P-384/P-521 key sizes, and padding/truncation bugs in integerToBytes for the larger signLength values (e.g. left-padding a 32-byte value to 48/66 bytes) still round-trip successfully. The test therefore cannot catch incorrect length handling or interop failures with JCA verifiers.

title: Cleanup listener disabled when only V2 feature enabled
body: registerListener now requires Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ to fire, while evaluator() uses ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. If only V2 is enabled, RoleRemoved/ClientRemoved/GroupRemoved events are ignored, so management().*.setPermissionsEnabled(...,false) is never called and orphaned authorization objects/permissions are left behind.

title: Wrong owner used for resource lookup breaks per-client checks
body: hasPermission(ClientModel,String) uses resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()) and hasPermission(String) uses findByName(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, server.getId()). AdminPermissionsSchema creates/finds resources with findByName(server,name) and create(server,name,server.getClientId()). Using server.getId() as owner will not match, so per-client resources are never found and every check falls back to the all-clients resource, causing false denies for single-client grants and false allows for all-clients grants.

title: Possible NPE when all-clients resource does not exist
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel,String) when the client-specific resource is null, code does resource = SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) which can return null (unsupported schema, null type, or missing resource) and then immediately calls authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) without a null check. That throws NPE and turns an authorization check into a 500 error.

title: getClientsWithPermission returns aggregate type resource name
body: getClientsWithPermission iterates resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) and adds resource.getName() for every granted resource. The aggregate Clients resource itself has that type, so a grant on all-clients adds the literal name Clients to the returned set. Callers expecting client IDs will filter/list incorrectly.

title: getResourceName has no Clients branch
body: getResourceName special-cases USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE to return All users or the username, but has no branch for CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE added in this PR. Client resources fall through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is not populated for FGAP resources, so UI/API displays null instead of the clientId for client permissions.

title: Removal listener gated on V1 flag and breaks on V2
body: The listener is now wrapped in Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ). When only ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled the Role/Client/Group removal cleanup never runs, leaking authorization resources/policies. When V1 is enabled but the realm uses V2, management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled() dispatches to ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled which unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException, so a client/role/group delete will throw out of the provider event listener.

title: Per-client check never falls back to all-clients permission and can NPE
body: hasPermission(ClientModel,String) loads the per-client resource and if it exists evaluates only that resource. A caller with a valid all-clients (resource-type) grant is then denied whenever any per-client resource happens to exist for that client. Conversely when the per-client resource does not exist it loads the type resource without null-checking it, so findByResource(server,null) / resource.getScopes() can NPE if the Clients type resource is missing.

title: getScope NPEs on unknown/null resourceType
body: getScope() does SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType).getScopes() without checking that the map entry exists. An unknown or null resourceType causes NullPointerException instead of the intended ModelValidationException, breaking REST validation for bad resource types.

title: getResourceName has no Clients branch
body: getResourceName() special-cases Users (All users vs username lookup) but has no branch for Clients. Client permissions therefore fall through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is not set for FGAP resources whose name is the client UUID, so UI/API display names for client permissions are wrong/null where Users correctly resolves to username.

title: getClientsWithPermission can return aggregate resource name
body: getClientsWithPermission() iterates resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and adds every granted resource.getName(). That includes the aggregate Clients type resource itself (named Clients) if granted, so callers filtering clients by ID get a bogus Clients entry mixed with real client UUIDs.

title: canMap* drops realm admin role / manage fallback
body: ClientPermissionsV2.canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles and canMapClientScopeRoles only call hasPermission(client, ...) and never check root.hasOneAdminRole(MANAGE_CLIENTS) or manage permission. A caller with the manage-clients realm role or global MANAGE permission therefore loses role-mapping ability under V2, a privilege regression versus V1 and versus canManage/canConfigure in the same file which do check the role. Fix by OR-ing the admin-role / manage check as done for other operations.

title: getClientsWithPermission includes All-clients type resource
body: getClientsWithPermission iterates resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and adds resource.getName() for every granted resource. That enumeration includes the 'All clients' placeholder resource named 'Clients' created in AdminPermissionsSchema.init. The returned set will then contain the literal 'Clients' string, which is not a client UUID, polluting list/filter results and lookups. Filter out the type resource or resources whose name equals the type.

title: Removal listener can throw UnsupportedOperationException when V2 enabled
body: registerListener is now guarded only by Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1), but management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, whose clients().setPermissionsEnabled / roles()/groups() V2 paths throw UnsupportedOperationException. With both features enabled the ClientRemovedEvent/RoleRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent handler will call the V2 implementation and throw, breaking client/role/group deletion. Guard must exclude V2 (e.g. require V1 enabled and V2 disabled) or dispatch to V1 implementation.

title: getScope NPE on unknown/null resourceType
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getScope does SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType).getScopes().contains(...) without null-checking the map lookup. An unknown or null resourceType causes NullPointerException (500) instead of ModelValidationException (400). This is reachable from permission creation/update paths with an invalid type. Add explicit null check for the ResourceType before dereferencing.

title: getResourceName has no Clients branch
body: getResourceName only special-cases USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE ('All users' / username lookup) and falls through to resource.getDisplayName() for everything else. Client resources store the client UUID as name, so admin-permission representations for Clients will show UUID/null instead of clientId/client name. Add a CLIENTS branch mirroring the user branch (all-clients label plus clientId lookup, throwing ModelIllegalStateException if missing).

title: Feature flag only enabled for non-default strategy
body: createInitialDeployment() returns early when updateStrategy == null without enabling Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES, while the RECREATE path does enable it. Docs in this PR state the operator will fail while in preview unless rolling-updates is enabled, so the parameterized runs with null strategy will run without the required feature and fail or test the wrong configuration. Move the feature-enable block before the null early-return.

title: Disabled-feature test does not verify exit code 4
body: testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the stderr text for update-compatibility metadata without the flag. The PR introduces CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED=4 and docs promise exit code 4 when rolling-updates is disabled. Without asserting cliResult.exitCode() == 4 the test cannot catch a regression where run() prints the message but exits 0, which would make automation assume a rolling upgrade is possible.

title: Default strategy test skips enabling rolling-updates feature
body: In createInitialDeployment() the method returns early when updateStrategy == null before the FeatureSpec with ROLLING_UPDATES is added (lines 105-106 vs 115). So the parameterized case with null strategy runs without the preview feature enabled, while the RECREATE case runs with it. Per the new docs the Operator will fail while on preview stage if rolling-updates is not enabled, so the null case will either fail or test a different code path than intended, and rolling behavior for the default strategy is not covered.

title: Feature-disabled path only tested for metadata, without exit code
body: testFeatureNotEnabled only launches update-compatibility metadata without --features and only asserts the error text. There is no equivalent test for the check subcommand which has the same gate in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java, and neither test asserts the new exit code CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED (4) defined in CompatibilityResult.java. A regression that prints the message but returns the wrong exit code (e.g. 0) or that breaks one subcommand would not be caught.

title: Null strategy test deployment misses required rolling-updates feature
body: createInitialDeployment() returns early when updateStrategy == null without enabling the preview feature, while the RECREATE branch enables Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES. Per the updated operator docs the operator fails while on preview unless `rolling-updates` is enabled, so the `null` parameterized cases in testImageChange/testCacheMaxCount run with a CR that the operator will reject or handle differently, making the tests fail or not exercise the intended upgrade path. Enable the feature for all created deployments, not only when updateStrategy != null.

title: Global canManage() grants manage on view-only permission
