body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() calls hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE). Anyone with only the VIEW scope on the all-groups resource therefore passes canManage(), which gates group creation, update, delete and child creation. Per-group canManage(GroupModel) correctly requires only MANAGE, so global and per-object checks disagree and view-only admins gain write access.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses resource ID instead of group ID
body: The method iterates resources of type Groups whose names are group IDs, but calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) and adds groupResource.getId() to the result. Resource.getId() is the internal authz UUID, not the group ID stored in the resource name. The lookup by name then misses, falls back to the all-groups resource, and the returned set contains authz IDs that callers use as group IDs for user search/count filtering, so filtering is wrong and no users or wrong users are returned.

title: NPE when all-groups type resource does not exist
body: hasPermission() falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) which can return null if the type resource was never created or was deleted, then unconditionally calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource). That dereferences a null resource and turns a permission check into a 500 error.

title: NPE when all-users type resource does not exist
body: UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission() loads the all-users type resource as fallback and calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) without a null check. If the Users type resource is missing, any per-user view/manage/map-roles/membership check throws NullPointerException instead of denying.

title: getScope() NPEs on unknown resource type
body: getScope() does SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType).getScopes() without checking that resourceType exists. An unknown or null resource type causes NullPointerException instead of the intended ModelValidationException about scope not found for resource type.

title: getResourceName() only resolves Users, not Groups
body: getResourceName() special-cases USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE to return 'All users' or the username, but has no branch for GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE or CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE. Group permission resources therefore fall through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is not set for schema-created resources, yielding null/wrong display names in admin UI/API responses.

title: canManage() grants manage on view scope
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() calls hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE). A caller with only the Groups VIEW scope for all-groups therefore passes canManage(), which guards create/update/delete group, add child, and role-mapping endpoints. VIEW must not imply MANAGE; only MANAGE should be checked.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses resource id instead of group id
body: The loop over findByType uses groupResource.getId() both to evaluate permission and to populate the result set. Resources are stored by group id in the resource name (findByName(server, groupId)), as done in hasPermission() and in the V1 implementation which uses resource.getName(). Using the internal authz resource UUID means the lookup misses and falls back to the all-groups evaluation, and the returned set contains authz UUIDs instead of group IDs. Downstream users search (session attribute UserModel.GROUPS, getUsersCount(...,groupIds)) expects group IDs, so filtering is wrong.

title: Possible NPE when all-groups resource does not exist
body: hasPermission() falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource() which can return null if the type resource is missing, then unconditionally calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource). Passing a null resource can throw NPE and break every group permission check. The same pattern exists in UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission(). A null check is required before querying policies.

title: canManage() grants manage from view-only permission
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() evaluates hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE). Any caller with only the view scope on the all-groups resource therefore passes canManage(), and can create/update/delete groups, add children and map roles. Global manage must require only MANAGE, like canManage(GroupModel) does on line 79.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses resource ID instead of resource name
body: AdminPermissionsSchema stores per-group resources with name equal to the group ID. hasPermission(String groupId) looks up via resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId) and the granted set is expected to contain group IDs. The loop passes groupResource.getId() (internal authz UUID) to hasPermission and adds getId() to the result. Lookup by UUID misses, falls back to the all-groups resource, and returns UUIDs instead of group IDs, so user search filtering by UserModel.GROUPS gets wrong/empty values and leaks or hides users.

title: Missing null check on all-groups type resource causes NPE
body: hasPermission() falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource() which can return null when the schema is not supported or the type resource does not exist, then immediately calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource). A null resource causes NullPointerException, breaking canView/canManage evaluation for admins without a per-group resource.

title: Diff trimming can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException
body: In VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml the code trims common prefix (start) and suffix (end) and then does value.substring(start, value.length() - end). start is bounded by min length and end is bounded by min length independently, so start+end can exceed the string length when one string is a repetition/prefix of the other, e.g. value="a" vs sanitized="aaa" gives start=1, end=1 and substring(1,0). Someone reading only this finds the verifier itself can crash instead of reporting Illegal HTML.

title: Anchor stripping iterates stale Matcher after mutating value
body: santizeAnchors creates Matcher on the original value then mutates value with replaceFirst inside the while(matcher.find()) loop. After the first removal the Matcher positions no longer correspond to the new string, so with two or more <a> tags the second tag can be skipped, double-counted, or the wrong occurrence removed via replaceFirst. This lets mismatched/translated anchors pass or produces false Didn't find anchor tag errors.

title: English reference lookup is fragile and aborts on RuntimeException
body: englishFile is built with replaceAll("resources-community","resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties","_en.properties"). The second replaceAll replaces every match, not just the locale suffix, so any underscore in a directory/file prefix corrupts the path, and failures are thrown as RuntimeException which aborts the whole verification instead of reporting a file error. Someone reading only this understands a translated file can break the build or be compared against the wrong English source.

title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
body: This PR replaces totpStep1 containing <a> tags with "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:" which is Italian, not Lithuanian, in a messages_lt.properties file. The same Italian sentence is also used for login/messages/messages_lt.properties. Merging this ships the wrong language to Lithuanian users; it should be Lithuanian or the English fallback.

title: Simplified Chinese file gets Traditional Chinese text
body: The replacement totpStep1 in messages_zh_CN.properties is "在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一:" which uses Traditional characters, while the file is Simplified Chinese (zh_CN). Merging this introduces a locale inconsistency for Simplified Chinese users.

title: PropertyResourceBundle loaded with wrong charset mangles UTF-8 translations
body: File is loaded with new PropertyResourceBundle(FileInputStream) at line 68 (and English file at line 77), which decodes as ISO-8859-1, while the message properties files contain raw UTF-8 (Chinese, Arabic, Thai, etc.). Non-ASCII values are garbled before sanitizing, so comparison of sanitized vs value is done on mojibake and can both miss real HTML and produce false Illegal HTML reports. Use a Reader with UTF-8.

title: Missing English file throws RuntimeException instead of reporting
body: If the derived englishFile cannot be opened, verifySafeHtml throws RuntimeException at line 79, aborting the whole theme-verifier mojo. A missing/corrupt reference file should produce a MojoExecutionException or a collected message like other checks, not crash the build.

title: Anchor check iterates stale matcher while mutating value
body: santizeAnchors creates Matcher on the original value then mutates value with replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(...)) inside the while(matcher.find()) loop. The matcher still walks the old CharSequence, and replaceFirst removes the first literal occurrence anywhere, not the matched offset. With duplicate or reordered anchors the wrong tag can be removed, letting a changed malicious href pass or flagging a correct file. Iterate over lists or track offsets instead.

title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
body: totpStep1 in the Lithuanian account bundle is now Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare: which is Italian, not Lithuanian. Same mistake in login/messages_lt.properties. Stripping HTML should not replace the sentence with another locale's text.

title: Simplified Chinese file uses Traditional characters
body: totpStep1 in messages_zh_CN.properties is now in Traditional Chinese (手機, 應用程式之一) while zh_CN must be Simplified (手机, 应用程序). The sanitizer fix copied the zh_TW wording into the zh_CN file.

title: Java ChoiceFormat syntax breaks JS {{}} interpolation contract
body: error-invalid-multivalued-size was changed from Attribute {{0}} ... {{2}} value(s) to Attribute {0} ... {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}. The account-ui and admin-ui bundles are consumed by JavaScript React/i18n code that interpolates {{0}}, not Java MessageFormat. Single-brace ChoiceFormat will be rendered literally and pluralization will not work in the UI.

title: English reference lookup is fragile and throws unchecked exception
body: verifySafeHtml() derives the English file with file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll("resources-community", "resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties") and on IOException throws RuntimeException. Any layout that does not match that string rewrite (new theme location, Windows separators, already-English file, missing _en counterpart) aborts verification with an unchecked exception instead of a MojoExecutionException message. The second replaceAll also uses character class [a-zA-Z-_] where the hyphen forms a Z-_ range, so hyphenated locales are not matched as intended.

title: Anchor allow-list mutates a different string than it matched
body: santizeAnchors() iterates Matcher over the original value string but mutates a separate value variable with value.replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(englishMatcher.group()), ""). When the groups are equal it deletes the first occurrence of the English anchor, not the matched occurrence, so reordered or repeated anchors are handled incorrectly. When they differ (e.g. changed href) it adds a message without key/file context, breaks after the first mismatch hiding further anchors, and leaves the offending anchor in place so the same key is reported a second time as Illegal HTML by the caller.

title: Properties read as ISO-8859-1 instead of UTF-8
body: verifySafeHtml() loads bundles with new PropertyResourceBundle(FileInputStream). That constructor decodes as ISO-8859-1, while the message properties in this repo contain raw UTF-8 (Arabic, Chinese, Thai, etc.). Non-ASCII values are therefore garbled before comparison/sanitizing. The code should load via a Reader with UTF-8, e.g. Files.newBufferedReader(path, UTF_8) plus new PropertyResourceBundle(Reader).

title: Constructor validates grantType twice, never validates rawTokenId
body: AccessTokenContext constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) twice and never checks rawTokenId, despite the second message saying 'Null rawTokenId not allowed'. A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted and later produces an id like 'onrtac:null' or an NPE in encodeTokenId / getRawTokenId consumers.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher is inverted and uses wrong substring
body: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId the check is `if (items[0].substring(3,5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. It returns false when the shortcut matches and true when it does not, so tests pass for wrong grants and fail for correct ones. The offsets are also wrong: the encoded prefix is 6 chars (session 0-2, token-type 2-4, grant 4-6), so the grant shortcut must be substring(4,6), not substring(3,5).

title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks all existing custom grant factories
body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory adds abstract String getShortcut() with no default implementation. Any third-party provider implementing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory will fail to compile and existing deployed providers will throw AbstractMethodError when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory calls getShortcut() in postInit. It should have a default method or fallback.

title: Duplicate shortcut/ID validation by map-size comparison is ineffective
body: postInit detects duplicate grant IDs or shortcuts by comparing grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size(). If two grants collide on both maps consistently, or one overwrites the other in both maps, sizes stay equal and the collision is missed, silently mapping a shortcut to the wrong grant. If they collide on only one side the error message is cryptic. Explicit duplicate checks on put are required.

title: Decoding a token id throws on any unexpected format instead of falling back
body: getTokenContextFromTokenId throws IllegalArgumentException when the prefix before ':' is not exactly 6 chars or contains an unknown shortcut. Any token whose id contains ':' for other reasons, or was issued by a custom grant with a shortcut longer than 2 chars, or after a grant is undeployed, will cause an exception to bubble to callers (e.g. introspection/userinfo/session lookup) instead of returning UNKNOWN context like the no-colon legacy path does. This turns malformed or forward-compatible tokens into 500 errors.

title: Unchecked cast of all OAuth2GrantType factories can cause ClassCastException
body: postInit and getGrantTypeByShortcut cast every OAuth2GrantType provider factory to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory. A custom OAuth2GrantType provider whose factory does not implement the new sub-interface will cause a ClassCastException at server startup or on first decode, breaking boot. Code should use instanceof filtering or lookup.

title: Constructor validates grantType twice, never validates rawTokenId
body: AccessTokenContext constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) twice and never checks rawTokenId, so a null rawTokenId is accepted and stored. Later encodeTokenId() concatenates ':' + rawTokenId, producing a malformed ID like "onrtac:null" or throwing NPE, breaking token creation and decoding.

title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing custom grant factories
body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory adds String getShortcut() with no default implementation. Any existing third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory outside this repo will fail compilation and fail at runtime with AbstractMethodError when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory casts to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory and calls getShortcut(). It must have a default value.

title: Removed Context copy constructor and added NPE on null formParams
body: The diff deletes the public Context(Context) copy constructor and adds grantType = formParams.getFirst(...) unconditionally in the remaining constructor. External grant implementations that copied contexts or passed null/lazy formParams will now fail to compile or throw NullPointerException. This is an incompatible SPI change.

title: No null checks for clientSession/userSession when deriving session type
body: getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext() dereferences clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getUserSession() and userSession.getPersistenceState() without checks. TokenManager.initToken() now calls this for every access token, including client-credentials, token-exchange, and other flows where clientSession or userSession can be null or persistenceState null, turning a simple generateId() into an NPE that fails token issuance.

title: Decoder throws on malformed/foreign token IDs instead of returning UNKNOWN
body: getTokenContextFromTokenId() throws IllegalArgumentException when the prefix before ':' is not length 6 or contains an unknown shortcut. If this decoder is later used on incoming tokens for the optimization described in the PR (introspection, userInfo, session lookup), any attacker-supplied, legacy, or foreign-issuer jti with a colon will cause an unhandled exception/500 instead of graceful fallback like the no-colon path that returns UNKNOWN.

title: getShouldUseLightweightToken can NPE when session client is null
body: The method dereferences session.getContext().getClient().getAttribute(...) without null checks. It is now called from DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext() during TokenManager.initToken() for all tokens, where the session context client is not guaranteed to be set, so token creation can throw NPE where it previously just generated an ID.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher inverted and checks wrong substring
body: matchesSafely() returns false when items[0].substring(3,5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut), i.e. it rejects correct tokens and accepts wrong ones. Additionally substring(3,5) is wrong: the 6-char prefix is session(0-1)+tokenType(2-3)+grant(4-5), so the grant shortcut is substring(4,6). The helper will never validate the intended grant type.

title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks all existing custom grant factories
body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory adds `String getShortcut()` with no default implementation. Any third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory outside this repo will fail to compile/link after upgrade. It should have a default (e.g. return UNKNOWN/"na") to remain backward compatible.

title: Public copy constructor Context(Context) silently removed
body: The diff deletes the `public Context(Context context)` copy constructor from the public SPI class OAuth2GrantType.Context. External grant implementations or decorators that copied context will break at compile/runtime. Removal is unrelated to adding grantType and should be retained or deprecated.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher logic inverted and offset wrong
body: In `isAccessTokenId` the check `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns false when the shortcut matches and true when it differs, so tests pass for wrong grants and fail for correct ones. The offset is also wrong: a 6-char prefix encodes session(0-1), token(2-3), grant(4-5), so grant must be `substring(4,6)`, not `substring(3,5)`.

title: Constructor validates grantType twice, never validates rawTokenId
body: The constructor calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType,...)` twice, the second time with message about rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted and later causes NPE in `encodeTokenId()` when concatenating `':' + rawTokenId` or in decoding logic.

title: Decoding attacker-controlled token id throws unchecked exception
body: getTokenContextFromTokenId() throws IllegalArgumentException for wrong prefix length or unknown shortcuts. The encoded id comes from the `jti` of a presented access token, i.e. attacker-controlled. Any future caller using it on introspection/userinfo/token-exchange paths will turn a malformed/forged token into a 500 instead of invalid-token handling. It should return UNKNOWN context or throw a handled OAuth error.

title: No enforcement that grant shortcuts are 2 chars breaks fixed 6-char format
body: Encoder/decoder assume `session(2)+token(2)+grant(2)=6` chars and throw if length !=6. Nothing validates `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` length (javadoc even says 3-letters). A custom grant returning 1, 3, or longer shortcut will produce IDs that can never be decoded, causing IllegalArgumentException/IllegalStateException at token creation or validation.

title: Recovery-code update reads wrong UserCredentialModel field
body: CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential builds UserCredentialModel("",type,recoveryCodesJson) which puts the JSON in getValue(). BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential stores input.getChallengeResponse() as credentialData, which is null for this input. The result is a null/empty federated recovery-codes credential, so setup appears to succeed via hasRecoveryCodes() but later getCredentials/isValid deserialization fails. The provider should read input.getValue() (as the OTP branch does) or the helper should set challengeResponse.

title: getCredentials NPE for unknown user
body: getCredentials() does var myUser = getMyUser(user) and immediately dereferences myUser.recoveryCodes without a null check. All other methods (isConfiguredFor, isValid, getDisableableCredentialTypesStream) guard against myUser==null. When the user is not in the map, this throws NullPointerException instead of returning an empty stream, breaking credential listing for federated users.

title: Exhausted federated recovery codes never removed
body: On successful recovery-code login the code fetches the credential via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential() which may be a federated (user-storage) credential, but exhaustion is handled with removeStoredCredentialById(). That API only deletes local DB credentials, not federated ones. For a user-storage credential the delete is a no-op/failure, the exhausted credential remains configured and the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action logic relies on a local delete that never happens.

title: Raw recovery codes handed to user storage in plaintext
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes generatedCodes (the raw printable codes) to JSON and passes them as the UserCredentialModel value to user.credentialManager().updateCredential(). The local path stores RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel with hashed codes, but the federated path persists raw codes in the external store. Any user-storage provider following this contract (as the test provider does) must store and compare plaintext codes, leaking reusable credentials outside the hashed local model.

title: getCredentials NPE for unknown/local users
body: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials the code does `var myUser = getMyUser(user)` then dereferences `myUser.recoveryCodes` and `myUser.otp` without a null check. getMyUser returns null when the username is not in the `users` map (e.g. a purely local DB user). Other methods like isConfiguredFor and isValid guard against null. The new override will therefore throw NullPointerException for any user not known to this storage when the credential-manager enumerates federated credentials, breaking login / credential listing for local users.

title: Exhausted federated recovery credential never removed
body: On successful recovery-code use the code calls `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())` when `allCodesUsed()`. That API only removes a locally stored (DB) credential. When the credential was created in user storage via CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential, there is no local credential to remove; the federated credential must be disabled/removed via disableCredentialType / federated path. As written, an exhausted federated recovery-code set is left in the external storage, so the user keeps an empty/used credential and the cleanup semantic diverges between local and federated users.

title: Unchecked Optional.get causes 500 when credential missing
body: RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean does `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` then unconditionally `credentialModelOpt.get()`. If no federated nor local recovery credential exists (race, deleted credential, mis-configured flow) this throws NoSuchElementException during login form rendering, producing a 500 instead of a handled error. The previous code had the same pattern but the new helper explicitly returns Optional to signal absence and callers should handle the empty case.

title: Raw recovery codes handed to user storage in clear text
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes the raw generated codes to JSON and passes them as UserCredentialModel to `user.credentialManager().updateCredential()`. The local path stores `credentialModel` which contains only hashed codes via RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues, but the federated path persists the raw codes. Any UserStorageProvider that simply stores `input.getChallengeResponse()`/`getValue()` (as the bundled test provider does) will keep all 12 recovery codes in clear text outside Keycloak DB with no hashing or single-use consumption enforced by the helper, weakening the security property that recovery codes are stored hashed.

title: Recovery codes passed in wrong UserCredentialModel field
body: Line 123 builds `new UserCredentialModel("", credentialModel.getType(), recoveryCodesJson)` which puts the JSON list into the `value` field. Federated validators/readers for recovery codes expect the payload in `challengeResponse` (as used by `UserCredentialModel.buildFromBackupAuthnCode`, and by the test provider at `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential`/`isValid` which call `input.getChallengeResponse()`). The OTP path in the same file correctly uses `getValue()`, proving the two credential types use different fields. Consequence: a user-storage provider reading `getChallengeResponse()` receives null, stores null/corrupt credentialData and validation fails or NPEs, so creation in user storage is broken.

title: getCredentials NPE for users not in storage map
body: `getCredentials` does `var myUser = getMyUser(user)` then immediately dereferences `myUser.recoveryCodes` without a null check, while every other method in the same class (`isConfiguredFor`, `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream`, `isValid`) guards `myUser == null`. `getCredentials` is invoked via federated-credential streams even for users that are not owned by this provider. Consequence: NullPointerException when listing federated credentials for any non-storage or unknown user, breaking credential listing / login flows.

title: Exhausted recovery codes not removed when stored in user storage
body: After successful validation the code fetches the credential via `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` which now can return a federated (user-storage) credential, but cleanup unconditionally calls `removeStoredCredentialById`. That API only removes local DB credentials and is a no-op for federated credentials, which must be removed/disabled via the storage provider (`disableCredentialType`/`updateCredential`). Consequence: when recovery codes live in user storage and all codes are used, the exhausted credential is never deleted from the external storage, leaving stale state.

title: Same concurrent-delete NPE remains in getSubGroupsStream overloads
body: The fix null-checks modelSupplier.get() in getSubGroupsCount, but getSubGroupsStream(search,first,max), getSubGroupsStream(first,max), and getSubGroupsStream(search,exact,first,max) still do modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) with no null check. If the group is deleted concurrently the supplier returns null (the exact case this PR fixes) and those methods still throw NullPointerException, so the concurrent list/brief path is not fixed.

title: Concurrent test thread is never joined
body: The test starts a reader thread with new Thread(...).start() and then asserts caughtExceptions immediately after setting deletedAll without join/wait. The assertion can run before the reader thread finishes, so failures can be missed, and the leaked thread can keep hitting the server during subsequent tests causing flakiness and resource leaks.

title: Concurrent-delete NPE not fixed in sibling methods
body: getSubGroupsCount() was made null-safe via modelSupplier.get() null-check, but getSubGroupsStream(search,first,max) at line 256, getSubGroupsStream(first,max) at line 260, and getSubGroupsStream(search,exact,first,max) at line 268 still unconditionally dereference modelSupplier.get(). If the group is deleted concurrently the supplier returns null and these methods still throw NullPointerException, so the fix is incomplete for the same race.

title: Reader thread never joined, assertion races
body: createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti starts a raw new Thread that loops until deletedAll is set, but never stores the Thread, never joins it, and asserts caughtExceptions immediately after deletedAll.set(true). An exception added by the reader after the assertion is missed, and the still-running thread leaks into subsequent tests and can use a closed admin client/session. The test must join the thread (with timeout) before asserting.

title: Remaining NPE on concurrent delete in getSubGroupsStream overloads
body: The fix null-checks modelSupplier.get() only in getSubGroupsCount(), but the three getSubGroupsStream overloads on the lines immediately above/below still do modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) without a null check. If the group is deleted concurrently, getGroupById returns null, so LazyModel supplies null and these methods still throw NullPointerException. The fix is incomplete for the stated concurrent-access bug.

title: Concurrent group delete still NPEs in hierarchy population
body: populateGroupHierarchyFromSubGroups loops while currGroup.getParentId() != null and does session.groups().getGroupById(realm, currGroup.getParentId()) with no null check. If the parent was deleted concurrently by the scenario this PR tests, parentModel is null and the next lines dereference it via groupEvaluator.canView(parentModel), toRepresentation(..., parentModel, ...) and populateSubGroupCount(parentModel, ...), causing NullPointerException. The PR claims to fix concurrent group access but leaves this reader path unfixed.

title: Reader thread never joined, assertion races
body: The new test starts a bare new Thread() that loops until deletedAll is set, but never stores the Thread reference, never joins it, and asserts on caughtExceptions immediately after deletedAll.set(true). Exceptions added by an in-flight request after the assertion are missed, failures can be flaky, and the thread can leak past the test method. The test must keep the thread handle and join it with a timeout before asserting.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator breaks datetime ordering
body: src/sentry/api/paginator.py OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key/value_from_cursor copy Paginator numeric logic (math.floor/ceil on value, cursor.value as-is) but src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py uses it with order_by="-datetime". For datetime fields value is a datetime, so math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError and integer cursor values are compared against a datetime column in build_queryset, producing wrong queries or crashes. It must subclass DateTimePaginator logic, not numeric Paginator logic.

title: Client-controlled negative offset passed to Django queryset slice
body: src/sentry/api/paginator.py OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result allows start_offset=cursor.offset when cursor.offset<0 and enable_advanced_features is true. cursor.offset comes from the user-supplied cursor string via Cursor.from_string. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indexes and raises AssertionError (Negative indexing is not supported), so a crafted cursor like 0:-100:0 causes a 500 instead of a 400 BadPaginationError as OffsetPaginator/ChainPaginator do. The comment claiming Django handles negative slicing automatically is false.

title: BasePaginator silently clamps invalid forward offsets
body: src/sentry/api/paginator.py BasePaginator.get_result changed from queryset[offset:stop] to max(0,offset) for non-prev cursors. Other paginators in the same file explicitly reject offset<0 with BadPaginationError. Silently rewriting a tampered negative cursor to 0 returns the first page instead of an error, hiding invalid cursors and making pagination behavior inconsistent across paginators.

title: Cursor allows negative offsets without validation
body: src/sentry/utils/cursors.py Cursor.__init__/from_string accept any int(offset) including negatives with only a comment change. All existing pagination validation assumed offsets are non-negative (e.g. SequencePaginator asserts offset>-1, OffsetPaginator raises on offset<0). Removing that invariant at the shared primitive enables the negative-slice crashes above and invalid prev/next cursors built by build_cursor.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator allows client-controlled negative offsets
body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result explicitly uses cursor.offset directly when enable_advanced_features and offset < 0: start_offset = cursor.offset. Cursor offset/value/is_prev come from the client-supplied cursor string (Cursor.from_string), so an attacker can send e.g. value:offset:is_prev with a negative offset. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing/slicing (raises AssertionError) and Python sequences wrap around, so this breaks the offset>=0 invariant enforced by OffsetPaginator, ChainPaginator and SequencePaginator, causing 500s / DoS or returning rows from the end of the set outside the intended window. Fix: reject negative offsets with BadPaginationError like other paginators.

title: BasePaginator now passes through negative offsets for prev cursors
body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py BasePaginator.get_result was changed from queryset[offset:stop] to start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset. For is_prev cursors the raw client-controlled offset is now used without clamping. A crafted cursor with is_prev=1 and negative offset therefore reaches queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start. This violates the pagination contract, triggers Django's negative-slicing AssertionError (500) or unintended wrap-around semantics, and is reachable on all endpoints using BasePaginator/DateTimePaginator without any advanced flag. Fix: clamp/validate to offset>=0 for both directions.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator incompatible with datetime ordering
body: In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py the optimized path uses OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime". Its get_item_key/value_from_cursor in src/sentry/api/paginator.py do int(math.floor(value)) / return cursor.value, i.e. the numeric Paginator logic, not the DateTimePaginator logic that converts datetime to/from timestamp with multiplier and timezone. Passing a datetime object to math.floor/math.ceil raises TypeError, and integer cursor values will not filter datetimes correctly in build_queryset. The endpoint will 500 or paginate incorrectly when optimized_pagination=true. Fix: do not use this paginator for datetime keys or implement datetime conversion.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator uses numeric key logic on datetime field
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does getattr(item, self.key) then math.floor/ceil and value_from_cursor returns raw cursor.value. The audit log endpoint instantiates it with order_by='-datetime' where the key is a datetime object. math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError, and even if it did not, comparing a datetime column in build_queryset against an int cursor value is type-wrong. Every call through the optimized path will crash in build_cursor when computing keys or produce an invalid WHERE clause, so the new endpoint branch is completely broken.

title: Client-controlled negative offset reaches queryset slice
body: When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset < 0, the code does queryset[cursor.offset:stop] with a negative start. Cursor offset is parsed from the user-supplied cursor string via Cursor.from_string, so any caller of this paginator can craft e.g. value:offset:is_prev with a negative offset. The comment claiming Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically is false: Django asserts start >= 0 and PostgreSQL OFFSET cannot be negative, so this raises AssertionError/DB error and returns 500. Other paginators in the same file explicitly reject offset < 0 with BadPaginationError. Negative offsets must be validated and rejected, not passed to the ORM.

title: BasePaginator clamps offset but later uses unclamped offset
body: BasePaginator.get_result now computes start_offset = max(0, offset) for non-prev cursors but keeps offset for is_prev, then slices with start_offset. The later prev-page adjustment checks len(results) == offset + limit + extra using the original offset, not start_offset. With a clamped or negative offset the length comparison is wrong, so the code can drop the wrong end of the page or fail to drop the extra before-row, causing duplicated/missing rows, wrong has_more, and inconsistent forward/backward navigation. It also still forwards negative is_prev offsets to queryset slicing which Django rejects.

title: Optimized pagination branch exposes broken unsafe paginator
body: The endpoint switches to OptimizedCursorPaginator with enable_advanced_features=True when ?optimized_pagination=true and the member has_global_access or is superuser. That exposes the broken datetime-key handling and negative-offset slicing described above to any global-access member, not just superusers, with no fallback or validation. Since the default DateTimePaginator path already works, this opt-in branch adds a crash/500 path to a security-sensitive audit-log API without tests or need.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator allows negative slice causing crash or wrong rows
body: File src/sentry/api/paginator.py line 880 does queryset[start_offset:stop] with start_offset = cursor.offset when cursor.offset < 0 and enable_advanced_features is true. Cursor.offset is attacker-controlled via the cursor string (Cursor.from_string parses int(bits[1]) with no validation). Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing/slicing and raise AssertionError, turning a crafted cursor into a 500, and the comment claiming Django handles negative slicing automatically is false. Even if it did not raise, Python/DB OFFSET semantics would return wrong page. Fix: reject offset<0 with BadPaginationError like OffsetPaginator does.

title: BasePaginator passes negative offset through for is_prev cursors
body: File src/sentry/api/paginator.py line 182 computes start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset. When cursor.is_prev is true a negative offset is passed directly to queryset[start_offset:stop]. That preserves the old crash/incorrect behavior for prev cursors and contradicts the clamping done for forward cursors. A crafted prev cursor with negative offset causes AssertionError/500 or wrong results. Fix: clamp or validate offset >=0 for both directions.

title: Direct dict access on end_timestamp_precise crashes consumer on missing field
body: File src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py line 141 does val["end_timestamp_precise"] with no fallback. Any span event without that field raises KeyError inside process_batch, failing the whole batch, blocking commits and causing backlog/consumer crash-loop. The field was previously optional for tests and the schema may not guarantee it. Fix: use val.get with fallback to message timestamp/now and add validation.

title: Removal of max_segment_spans guard hides silent eviction data loss
body: File src/sentry/spans/buffer.py around line 449 removed the len(payloads)>max_segment_spans check that emitted spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded and skipped oversize segments. The Lua script now silently ZPOPMINs everything over 1000 members. Oversize segments are therefore truncated with no metric/log, max_segment_spans config is dead, and downstream flush will emit incomplete segments while has_root_span/timeout logic still assumes full data. Fix: keep a metric/log for evicted spans and either enforce max_segment_spans or remove the option.

title: Redirect depth cut from 10000 to 1000 breaks deep segments
body: File src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua line 30 changed the redirect chase loop from 10000 to 1000 iterations. Traces with redirect chains deeper than 1000 will stop resolving early, leaving set_span_id pointing at an intermediate set. Subsequent ZUNIONSTORE merges then split one logical segment across multiple keys, producing duplicate/incomplete flushed segments. There is no justification for the reduction; restore 10000 or make it configurable.

title: ZUNIONSTORE without AGGREGATE corrupts scores on duplicates
body: File src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua lines 47 and 53 call ZUNIONSTORE with default AGGREGATE SUM. Scores are end_timestamp_precise. If the same payload member exists in both source sets (retries, duplicate ingestion, overlapping merges) its score is doubled, corrupting ordering and causing the later ZPOPMIN eviction to keep/drop the wrong spans. Fix: pass AGGREGATE MAX (or MIN) explicitly to preserve timestamp semantics.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator allows attacker-controlled negative slice
body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result() explicitly allows cursor.offset < 0 when enable_advanced_features is true and slices queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and raise AssertionError, and Python slicing with negative start wraps from the end. An unauthenticated cursor string from the query param therefore controls DB slicing beyond normal bounds. The comment claiming Django handles it automatically and permissions at queryset level make it safe is false. Consequence is DoS (500s) and bypass of intended pagination bounds.

title: Audit-log endpoint exposes advanced paginator on weak gate
body: In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py the endpoint switches to OptimizedCursorPaginator with enable_advanced_features=True when request.GET optimized_pagination==true and request.user.is_superuser or member.has_global_access. has_global_access is true for many org admins, not just superusers, so any such user can trigger the negative-offset path by crafting a cursor. The queryset remains filtered but pagination logic is now attacker-influenced. Consequence is privilege-adjacent attack surface for the DoS/bounds issue in the paginator.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator used with datetime ordering will crash
body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key() does int(math.floor(value)) assuming a numeric key, identical to Paginator. The caller in organization_auditlogs.py uses order_by=-datetime, so value is a datetime object. math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError on every page that builds a cursor. Consequence is the optimized audit-log path is broken and returns 500s.

title: Mandatory end_timestamp_precise access crashes consumer on missing field
body: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py process_batch() does val[end_timestamp_precise] with direct key access. Any span event without that field, malformed Relay output, or schema evolution raises KeyError inside the Arroyo batch processor. Because the exception occurs after Kafka receipt but before offset commit, the same message will be retried and can stall the spans consumer. Consequence is poison-pill crash loop and pipeline backlog. It should use .get with fallback or validation.

title: Silent span eviction with zpopmin causes unmonitored data loss
body: In src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua after merging sets the script does if span_count>1000 then zpopmin(set_key, span_count-1000). Combined with src/sentry/spans/buffer.py removing the max_segment_spans skip-and-log check in _load_segment_data, oversized segments are no longer skipped with metrics/logs but silently truncated to 1000 members, dropping earliest spans by score. Consequence is permanent loss of span data in large traces with no alert, and ZUNIONSTORE default SUM aggregate also corrupts scores for duplicate members, breaking timestamp ordering.

title: BasePaginator prev-path still passes negative offset to queryset
body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py BasePaginator.get_result() was changed to start_offset = max(0,offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset. When cursor.is_prev is true a negative offset is passed directly to queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django raises AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported for such slices. Consequence is a crafted prev cursor causes 500 errors and breaks reverse pagination.

title: ZUNIONSTORE uses SUM aggregate, corrupting scores on duplicates
body: In src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua the merges use `zunionstore(set_key, 2, set_key, span_key)` with default AGGREGATE SUM. Members are span payloads, so a re-processed or duplicate payload present in both sets will have its score (end_timestamp_precise) summed/doubled instead of preserved. This corrupts time ordering, breaks zpopmin eviction (oldest-first) and zscan ordering. Use AGGREGATE MIN (or MAX) or ZADD NX semantics.

title: Direct end_timestamp_precise access can crash consumer
body: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py process_batch does `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` with no fallback. Any message missing that field (old producer, schema evolution, bad payload) raises KeyError inside RunTask/BatchStep, failing the whole batch and blocking offset commit. The score is only needed for ZADD ordering and should use .get with a sane default like timestamp/now.

title: Negative-offset slicing allows crafted cursor to break queryset
body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result explicitly allows `cursor.offset < 0` and slices as `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with negative start. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing/slicing and raise AssertionError, so a user-supplied cursor string (value:offset:is_prev) with a negative offset triggers a 500. The comments claiming Django handles it automatically and that it is safe are wrong. Same issue in BasePaginator change at line 182 where is_prev preserves negative offset.

title: Unvalidated pagination switch exposes untested paginator
body: In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py the new `optimized_pagination=true` flag is read raw from request.GET bypassing the serializer, and enabled for anyone with `has_global_access` (not just superuser/admin). This routes audit-log reads through OptimizedCursorPaginator with enable_advanced_features=True, an untested path with different boundary handling, widening attack surface on a sensitive audit endpoint.

title: Removal of max_segment_spans guard leaves no fallback if eviction fails
body: In src/sentry/spans/buffer.py _load_segment_data the check for `len(payloads[key]) > max_segment_spans` and `segment_span_count_exceeded` was deleted, leaving only byte-size guard. The Lua cap is hardcoded to 1000 while SpansBuffer defaults to max_segment_spans=1001, so the config is now dead. If the Lua script is old/cached, eviction is bypassed, or ZSET scores collide, oversized segments are now fully loaded into memory and produced instead of skipped.

title: Redirect depth cut from 10000 to 1000 can split deep segments
body: In src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua the redirect-chain loop was reduced from 10000 to 1000 iterations. Traces/segments with chain depth >1000 will stop resolving early and write to the wrong set_key, producing split or duplicated segments that never join. This is a correctness regression disguised as optimization.

title: Unstable cache key built with Python hash()
body: Line 27 builds the cache key with hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids))). Python's hash() for tuples is salted per-process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so the same project set maps to different keys in different workers/restarts, defeating the shared cache and causing inconsistent behavior. It can also be negative and can collide. Use a stable deterministic encoding such as comma-joined sorted ids instead.

title: Stale allowlist cache returns wrong counts with no invalidation
body: is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects caches allowlist eligibility for 60s and invalidate_upsampling_cache is defined but never called. A stale True applies sum(sample_weight) (~10x inflation) to projects just removed from the allowlist; a stale False under-counts projects just added. Count correctness must not depend on eventual consistency for a global option lookup.

title: Upsampling check uses outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset
body: _get_event_stats takes scoped_dataset (which the dashboard-split factory changes to discover vs the original dataset) but calls is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects with the outer closure variable dataset. After a split decision the eligibility decision and column transform are therefore made for the wrong dataset, applying upsampling to transaction-like queries or skipping it for error queries.

title: upsampled_count sums nullable sample_weight and truncates with toInt64
body: upsampled_count is defined as toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) with no coalesce/default. Rows without sample_weight contribute NULL/0 and are silently dropped from the count, under-counting mixed data, and toInt64 truncates fractional weights (e.g. 1/0.3). The helper even states it assumes the column always exists. Use coalesce/ifNull handling and avoid lossy integer truncation.

title: Discover error detection misses negated/default error queries
body: _is_error_focused_query only returns True when the literal string event.type:error appears. The same file's caller and the dashboard-split code issue error queries as (query) AND !event.type:transaction and empty/default queries, which will therefore skip upsampling on discover while the errors dataset upsamples, producing inconsistent under-counts.

title: Sample-rate test helper swallows errors and mishandles falsy/invalid rates
body: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling the lookups and float conversion are wrapped in bare except Exception: pass and gated by if client_sample_rate:. This hides malformed contexts, treats 0/0.0 as absent, and accepts out-of-range values like >1 or negative, writing a bad sample_rate into normalized_data that then drives sample_weight in tests.

title: Cache key uses Python hash() which is unstable across processes
body: cache_key embeds hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))). Python string/tuple hash is salted per process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so different web workers compute different keys for the same projects when cache is shared (memcached/Redis). Result is cache never hits cross-process (perf loss) and invalidate_upsampling_cache computes a different key than the writer in another process, so invalidation cannot work.

title: 60s cached allowlist eligibility returns stale upsampled vs real counts
body: is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects caches _are_all_projects_error_upsampled for 60 seconds. If the project_allowlist option changes, queries within the window get the old decision and transform count() to upsampled_count() or vice versa, returning ~1/sample_rate inflated or deflated counts. invalidate_upsampling_cache is never called anywhere in the diff, so there is no way to close the window.

title: Eligibility check uses outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset
body: Inside _get_event_stats the code calls is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request) with the closure-captured dataset, not the scoped_dataset argument. The dashboard-split factory calls _get_event_stats with discover vs scoped_dataset for the same outer dataset, so _should_apply_sample_weight_transform sees the wrong dataset and can upsample transactions or skip upsampling errors.

title: Discover-split queries bypass error detection because only request.GET is inspected
body: _is_error_focused_query reads request.GET.get('query') while _get_event_stats builds split queries like f"({query}) AND !event.type:transaction" in the query argument. An errors-only split on discover without literal event.type:error in the URL therefore returns False and skips the upsampling transform, undercounting by the sample factor. Conversely the check cannot see the actual Snuba query string being executed.

title: Transform only handles exact count() and misses aliases/other counts
body: transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling only rewrites column_lower == 'count()'. yAxis values with aliases (e.g. 'count() as total'), extra whitespace variants, count_if/count_unique or equations pass through unchanged, so an allowlisted query silently returns raw sampled counts instead of upsampled counts when the frontend sends an aliased column.

title: upsampled_count sums nullable sample_weight without fallback
body: The new SnQLFunction is toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) with a comment assuming sample_weight exists for all events. Old/backfilled or non-sampled error rows have NULL/missing sample_weight, which sum skips, so those events contribute 0 instead of 1. Mixing sampled and unsampled rows undercounts; correct form needs coalesce/ifNull e.g. sum(coalesce(sample_weight,1)) or similar.

title: Test helper sets sample_rate not sample_weight with swallowed errors
body: _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling copies contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate to normalized_data['sample_rate'] inside try/except pass blocks, with if client_sample_rate: skipping 0. The production aggregation sums sample_weight, so the test only passes if some other pipeline derives sample_weight from sample_rate; if not, the endpoint integration test asserting count==10 is testing the wrong column. Broad except also hides malformed contexts type errors.

title: Unstable Python hash() used for shared cache key
body: In src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py the cache key is built with hash(tuple(sorted(...))). Python's hash() is salted per-process, so the same project list maps to different keys in different workers/restarts, and invalidate_upsampling_cache() computed in another process will delete a different key. Consequence: the 60s cache never shares across processes and invalidation does not work cross-process, defeating the optimization and leaving stale eligibility.

title: upsampled_count uses bare sum(sample_weight) with no null fallback
body: In src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py upsampled_count is defined as toInt64(sum(sample_weight)). Events without a sample_weight (older events, non-sampled ingestion, transactions mixed in discover) have NULL/missing values which sum ignores or turns to NULL/0. Consequence: upsampled counts silently undercount instead of counting such rows as 1, producing wrong chart numbers. It needs coalesce/ifNotFinite handling, not an assumption that the column always exists.

title: Upsampling check uses outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset
body: In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_events_stats.py _get_event_stats() calls is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request) with the outer closure dataset, not the scoped_dataset argument it is about to query. The dashboard-split factory calls the same helper with discover vs metrics datasets to split errors/transactions. Consequence: split queries get the wrong upsampling decision, e.g. a discover errors-only split query evaluated against a metrics dataset will skip upsampling, or vice versa, returning inconsistent counts.

title: Discover errors-only queries via negation never upsampled
body: In src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py _is_error_focused_query() only returns True for the literal substring event.type:error. The endpoint itself builds errors-only discover queries as (query) AND !event.type:transaction, and users commonly filter errors by exclusion. Consequence: those errors-only discover queries return False and use plain count() while explicit event.type:error queries use upsampled_count(), so the same logical data shows different numbers depending on query spelling.

title: upsampled_count only registered on discover but applied to errors dataset
body: In src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py the new SnQLFunction upsampled_count is added to the discover dataset converter, but src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py returns True for the errors dataset unconditionally and organization_events_stats.py rewrites count() to upsampled_count() for scoped_dataset==errors and for RPC paths. Consequence: errors-dataset timeseries/top-events and RPC queries will request an unknown function and fail or behave inconsistently because the function is not registered there.

title: Test helper blindly overwrites sample_rate from error_sampling context
body: In src/sentry/testutils/factories.py _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling() does normalized_data.get(contexts,{}).get(...) inside a bare except, checks if client_sample_rate: (skipping 0), then float()s anything and overwrites normalized_data[sample_rate] without validating range or preserving an existing explicit sample_rate. Consequence: invalid rates like 2.0, negative, or strings pollute stored events in tests, and real sample_rate values are silently replaced, making upsampling tests unrealistic and masking production null-handling bugs.

title: Browser report age/timestamp mutual-exclusion check uses truthiness
body: validate_timestamp does `if self.initial_data.get("age")` and validate_age does `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp")`. A value of 0 is falsy, so a report with `timestamp: 0` plus `age` passes validation, and a report with `age: 0` plus `timestamp` passes. The check must be presence-based (`"age" in self.initial_data` / `is not None`), otherwise the Working Draft vs Editor's Draft exclusivity is not enforced and invalid mixed reports are accepted.

title: Merged-PR template calls _truncate_title on wrong class
body: CommitContextIntegration.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template does `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title)` but `_truncate_title` is defined as a staticmethod on CommitContextIntegration, not on PRCommentWorkflow. At runtime this raises AttributeError when rendering a merged-PR suspect-issue comment, breaking GitHub/GitLab PR commenting. It should call `self._truncate_title` or `CommitContextIntegration._truncate_title`.

title: Detector update reads wrong validated_data key for type
body: update() does `validated_data.get("detector_type", instance.group_type).slug` while create() uses `validated_data["type"].slug` and the serializer field is named `type`. Because `detector_type` is never present, update always falls back to the existing group_type, so changing a detector's type via PUT silently does nothing.

title: Error details misaligned by zipping ids with dict values
body: fetch_error_details does `zip(error_ids, events.values())` where `events` is the dict returned by `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)`. Dict value order is not guaranteed to match `error_ids` order, and missing nodes shrink the values list, so titles/messages/timestamps can be attributed to the wrong error id or dropped. The code must look up each node id individually instead of zipping.

title: Table widget flag renders empty table instead of real results
body: When `organization.features.includes('use-table-widget-visualization')` the branch renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}}} />`, discarding `result.data`, `result.meta`, `fields`, loading state and custom renderers. Enabling the flag blanks every dashboard table widget.

title: Analytics recorded before feature gate and validation
body: analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble") runs before the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` feature check and before body validation. Disabled-feature, unauthorized, and malformed requests are all counted as assemble attempts, polluting metrics. The record call should happen after the feature gate (and ideally after validation).

title: fetch_error_details misaligns error IDs with nodestore results
body: fetch_error_details builds node_ids from error_ids, calls nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids), then does zip(error_ids, events.values()). get_multi returns a dict keyed by node_id with no ordering guarantee matching error_ids, and filters out misses, so values() order does not correspond to error_ids order. The consequence is error titles/messages/timestamps get attached to the wrong error id, producing incorrect error context in the Seer summarization request.

title: get_merged_pr_single_issue_template calls _truncate_title on wrong class
body: CommitContextIntegration defines _truncate_title but get_merged_pr_single_issue_template calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title). PRCommentWorkflow does not define that helper, so rendering a merged-PR suspect-issues comment raises AttributeError. The consequence is GitHub/GitLab PR comment workflows crash when formatting the issue list instead of posting the comment.

title: Browser report age/timestamp exclusivity check uses truthiness
body: validate_timestamp checks self.initial_data.get("age") and validate_age checks self.initial_data.get("timestamp"). A value of 0 is falsy, so a report with timestamp=0 and age present, or age=0 and timestamp present, passes validation when the specs require them to be mutually exclusive. The consequence is invalid mixed-spec reports are accepted and valid edge-case reports can be misclassified.

title: Table widget visualization discards real query results
body: When organization.features includes use-table-widget-visualization, tableResultComponent renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded empty columns=[] and empty tableData data:[]/meta instead of the fetched result, fields, and metadata used by the legacy table path. The consequence is dashboards show an empty table with no rows or headers when the flag is on, a data-loss regression.

title: Error IDs misaligned with nodestore results
body: fetch_error_details builds node_ids from error_ids, calls nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids), then does zip(error_ids, events.values()). Dict values are not guaranteed to be in error_ids order, and missing keys shrink values but not error_ids, so titles/messages/timestamps get attached to the wrong error id. Lookup each id via its node id instead, e.g. events.get(node_id), and skip missing entries.

title: Wrong class referenced for title truncation
body: CommitContextIntegration.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title), but _truncate_title is defined on CommitContextIntegration, not on PRCommentWorkflow/OpenPRCommentWorkflow in this file. This raises AttributeError/NameError at comment-render time. It should call self._truncate_title or CommitContextIntegration._truncate_title.

title: Mutual-exclusion check uses truthiness, misses 0
body: validate_timestamp checks self.initial_data.get("age") and validate_age checks get("timestamp"). A valid timestamp of 0 or age of 0 is falsy, so a payload containing both age and timestamp=0 (or vice versa) passes validation when it should be rejected. Check key presence (e.g. "age" in initial_data) instead of truthiness.

title: Detector type update reads wrong validated key
body: update() does validated_data.get("detector_type", instance.group_type).slug while create() and validate_type() use key "type". validated_data never contains "detector_type", so updates silently keep the old type and a type change via the API is ignored. Use validated_data.get("type", instance.group_type).

title: New table visualization renders empty data
body: When organization.features includes use-table-widget-visualization, tableResultComponent renders <TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data:[], meta:{fields:{},units:{}}}}/>, discarding result.data, result.meta, fields, loading and title computed just above. Every dashboard table behind the flag will show an empty table instead of real data. Map the actual query result into columns/tableData.

title: Analytics recorded before auth/feature check
body: analytics.record for preprod_artifact.api.assemble runs before the features.has check and before body validation, so unauthenticated, feature-disabled, and malformed requests are logged as assembles with organization/project/user ids. This pollutes analytics and logs user ids for requests that should be rejected early. Move recording after the feature/permission and validation gates.

title: Unhandled exceptions during OAuth token exchange cause 500 instead of install error
body: OAuthLoginView.dispatch calls safe_urlopen, safe_urlread and get_user_info without any try/except around the network calls. If GitHub returns an error for a bad/re-used code, safe_urlopen raises, and get_user_info can also raise ApiError. The code only handles the case where payload lacks access_token, so the cases the PR description claims to handle (bad code, re-used code, user-info failure) will raise an unhandled exception and return 500 instead of the intended github-integration-failed.html error page.

title: Direct metadata['sender']['login'] access can KeyError and breaks old integrations
body: GitHubInstallation.dispatch compares pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") to integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] with direct dict indexing. Integrations created before sender tracking, or where the webhook did not store sender, have no metadata sender key. That raises KeyError and turns a reinstall/repair into a 500 instead of the controlled error page. It must use safe .get() access and treat a missing sender as a verification failure.

title: New-install path skips authenticated-user verification
body: GitHubInstallation.dispatch returns pipeline.next_step() immediately when Integration.DoesNotExist, without comparing github_authenticated_user to anything. Only the branch where an Integration row already exists (created by the webhook with sender info) performs the attacker-vs-installer check. A fresh installation_id that has no Integration row yet therefore bypasses the security check this PR is supposed to add and proceeds to build the integration.

title: KeyError crash when Integration metadata has no sender
body: GitHubInstallation.dispatch does integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]. In build_integration sender is optional (only set if state.get("sender")), so older or webhook-less Integrations have no sender key. A second-org install or reinstall for such an Integration raises KeyError resulting in a 500 instead of the intended error page, blocking legitimate installs.

title: Fresh-install path skips authenticated-user check
body: GitHubInstallation returns pipeline.next_step() immediately when Integration.DoesNotExist for the supplied installation_id, without comparing pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") to the installer. An attacker can win the race before the installation webhook creates the Integration, or use an installation_id that has never been seen, and complete the pipeline having only passed OAuth as themselves, defeating the mismatch check described in the PR.

title: Unhandled token-exchange / user-info failures cause 500
body: OAuthLoginView calls safe_urlopen for the access_token exchange and get_user_info(payload["access_token"]) with only payload-parsing wrapped in try/except. Network errors, non-200 GitHub responses, or ApiError from get_user_info propagate as 500 instead of rendering the github-integration-failed template. The code only handles missing access_token/login keys, not exceptions from those calls.

title: Unvalidated installation_id used in GitHub API path
body: installation_id is taken from request.GET or pipeline state and bound without validation, then later interpolated into client.get(f"/app/installations/{installation_id}") in get_installation_info. A value containing slashes or path segments lets a caller make the server issue JWT-authenticated GETs to arbitrary /app/ paths on api.github.com, beyond the intended installation lookup.

title: KeyError on integration without sender metadata crashes install
body: GitHubInstallation.dispatch compares pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") to integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] with direct dict indexing. build_integration only sets metadata["sender"] when state.get("sender") is present, and older/existing Integration rows have no sender key. For those rows this line raises KeyError resulting in a 500 instead of the intended github-integration-failed error page, breaking reinstall/re-link flows.

title: Unhandled token-exchange failure returns 500 instead of error page
body: OAuthLoginView.dispatch calls safe_urlopen for the GitHub access_token exchange outside any try/except; only the body parsing is wrapped. Network errors, non-2xx responses, or rate limiting from GitHub will raise and produce a 500. The PR description says a failure to generate an access_token (wrong/reused code) should show the integration-failed page, but that only happens if the endpoint returns a parseable body without access_token.

title: Unhandled get_user_info failure returns 500 instead of error page
body: OAuthLoginView.dispatch calls get_user_info(payload["access_token"]) with no error handling and only checks for missing login key. Any ApiError, auth error, or network failure raised while calling GET /user propagates as an unhandled exception and 500s, instead of returning the intended Invalid installation request error page.

title: Query-param installation_id overrides bound pipeline state
body: GitHubInstallation.dispatch does request.GET.get("installation_id", pipeline.fetch_state("installation_id")) and then re-binds it, so an attacker/crafted OAuth callback URL with ?code=&state=<valid>&installation_id=<other> replaces the installation_id bound in OAuthLoginView before the github_authenticated_user vs sender check. The validated user is then compared against a different installation than the one the pipeline started with, weakening the user-mismatch security check the PR is adding.

title: installation_not_found test no longer exercises 404 path
body: test_installation_not_found stubs GET /app/installations/<id> to 404 but then drives the second step with state ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05, which does not match the pipeline signature. The pipeline therefore fails at the state-mismatch check in OAuthLoginView and never reaches build_integration/get_installation_info. The test asserts Invalid installation request but no longer proves the 404 installation-not-found branch returns a clean error page.

title: Mutable import-time default for `queued` timestamp
body: In src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py line 18, `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` evaluates `timezone.now()` once at import time. Every AssignmentSource created without an explicit `queued` shares the same timestamp. It should be `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. Consequence is stale/incorrect `queued` metadata on all sources and broken tests that assume freshness.

title: AssignmentSource.to_dict emits non-JSON datetime into Celery task
body: AssignmentSource.to_dict() in src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py uses dataclasses.asdict, which leaves `queued` as a `datetime` object. src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py then puts that dict into `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs={... assignment_source_dict ...})`. Celery kwargs must be JSON-serializable, so enqueue will raise a serialization error and outbound assignee sync will never run. Even if serialized by another serializer, `from_dict` does not parse an ISO string back to datetime, so the round-trip is broken and a malformed dict returns None and fails open to re-syncing.

title: Shared `queued` default timestamp
body: File src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py line 18 defines `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`. In a dataclass the default expression is evaluated once at import time, so every AssignmentSource created without an explicit `queued` shares the same timestamp. It must use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. Consequence is all sources carry a stale identical time, breaking any ordering, debugging, or expiry logic based on `queued`.

title: `to_dict` not Celery/JSON serializable
body: File src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py `to_dict` returns `asdict(self)` which includes the raw `datetime` object for `queued`. File src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py then puts that dict into `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs={... assignment_source_dict ...})`. Celery task kwargs must be JSON-serializable; a datetime will fail serialization or round-trip as a string that `from_dict` then stores as a str, not a datetime. Consequence is outbound sync tasks can fail to enqueue or lose type fidelity. Serialize `queued` to ISO format and parse it back in `from_dict`.

title: Outbound assignee source param not in abstract API
body: File src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py line 60 calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)`, but file src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py line 397 abstract `sync_assignee_outbound` is still declared as `(external_issue, user, assign=True, **kwargs)` with no explicit `assignment_source`, while sibling `sync_status_outbound` was given an explicit `assignment_source` param that no caller ever passes. Any concrete integration overriding `sync_assignee_outbound` without `**kwargs` will raise TypeError on inbound-triggered assignments, and status-sync loops are left unwired. Consequence is runtime crashes for strict overrides and an inconsistent public integration API.

title: Mutable default timestamp evaluated once at import
body: File src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py line 18 defines `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` as a dataclass default. This calls `timezone.now()` once at import time, so every AssignmentSource instance created without an explicit `queued` shares the same timestamp. It should use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. Consequence is all sources carry a stale identical queued time, breaking any ordering/debounce logic and the test expectation of freshness.

title: to_dict emits non-JSON-serializable datetime for Celery
body: File src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py `to_dict()` returns `asdict(self)` including the raw `datetime queued`. File src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py passes that dict as `assignment_source_dict` into `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs=...)` which must be JSON-serializable for Celery. A datetime payload fails serialization / deserialization, so outbound sync tasks will fail or be lost. After JSON round-trip `from_dict` would also receive a string for `queued` and store a str where datetime is expected, with no ISO parsing.

title: Passing unexpected assignment_source kwarg to installations
body: File src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py line 59 calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)` but the abstract in src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py defines `sync_assignee_outbound(self, external_issue, user, assign=True, **kwargs)` without an explicit parameter, and concrete integrations are not updated. Any concrete `sync_assignee_outbound` without `**kwargs` or explicit `assignment_source` will raise TypeError at runtime. Tests mock the method so the break is hidden. Consequence is outbound assignee sync crashes for real providers.

title: Invalid source dict fails open and re-creates sync loop
body: File src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py lines 53-56 parse `assignment_source_dict` with `AssignmentSource.from_dict` which returns None on ValueError/TypeError, then calls `should_sync(..., None)`. A malformed or version-skewed dict therefore degrades to no-source and syncs to the originating integration, re-creating the exact assignee sync cycle this PR claims to fix. It should fail closed (skip) or log when a dict was provided but unparseable.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler was changed from DetectorHandler (which it implemented with `return []`) to StatefulDetectorHandler with `pass`. StatefulDetectorHandler adds new abstract members: `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and new `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. A subclass that does not implement them remains abstract, so `group_type.detector_handler(self)` in Detector.detector_handler will raise TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class when the detector type is metric_alert_fire. Previously this handler was concrete.

title: get_state_data KeyErrors when detector has no counters
body: In get_state_data, `counter_updates` is initialized to `{}` and only populated inside `if self.counter_names:`. The result construction unconditionally does `counter_updates=counter_updates[gk]`. For any StatefulDetectorHandler with `counter_names == []`, this raises KeyError on every evaluate, crashing detection. It should default to an empty dict per group key when there are no counters.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler cannot be instantiated
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler which has abstract methods counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the new build_occurrence_and_event_data, but the class body is just pass. Instantiating it via Detector.detector_handler (group_type.detector_handler(self)) will raise TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class. Any detector with type metric_alert_fire is therefore broken.

title: Duplicate group keys silently overwritten without logging
body: process_detectors previously detected duplicate group_key results and logged Duplicate detector state group keys found. After changing evaluate to return dict keyed by group_key, evaluate does results[result.group_key] = result and process_detectors just iterates values. Conflicting results for the same key now last-wins with no log or metric, losing observability of a detector bug that the old code explicitly called out as shouldn't happen.

title: get_state_data KeyErrors when counter_names is empty
body: get_state_data initializes counter_updates to {} and only populates it inside if self.counter_names:. It then unconditionally does counter_updates[gk] when building DetectorStateData. A stateful detector that returns [] for counter_names will raise KeyError for every group key instead of returning empty/default counters.

title: Mock occurrence helper ignores value and uses fixed IDs
body: build_mock_occurrence_and_event takes value but never uses it and always returns the same IssueOccurrence id and event_id. test_state_results_multi_group sends group_2 value 10 but builds the expected occurrence with value 6 and still passes, and two different groups get identical IDs. Tests therefore cannot verify value propagation or ID/fingerprint uniqueness required by the new build_occurrence_and_event_data hook.

title: get_state_data KeyErrors when counter_names is empty
body: get_state_data initializes counter_updates as {} and only populates it inside `if self.counter_names:`. The result-building loop then unconditionally does `counter_updates[gk]`.
