A detector with `counter_names == []` and any group keys therefore raises KeyError, making stateless-counter detectors unusable. Fix by defaulting to empty dict per group key, e.g. `counter_updates.get(gk, {})`.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler cannot be instantiated
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler was changed to subclass StatefulDetectorHandler but remains `pass`. StatefulDetectorHandler has abstract members `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and new `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Instantiating the handler via `Detector.detector_handler` will raise TypeError for an abstract class, turning every metric-alert detector evaluation into an exception instead of the previous no-op returning []. Implement the methods or keep it as a plain DetectorHandler until ready.

title: Converted config copy is discarded, raw config returned
body: In get_monitor_environment_context a copy of the monitor config is made and schedule_type is converted to its display value, but the returned dict uses monitor_environment.monitor.config instead of the converted local variable config. The conversion is therefore dead code and the occurrence context carries the raw schedule_type value instead of the intended human-readable display value.

title: Computed display config is discarded, raw config returned
body: get_monitor_environment_context copies monitor.config into local `config` and converts schedule_type to its display value, but then returns monitor_environment.monitor.config instead of the local `config`. The conversion is dead code and event context contains the raw schedule_type value instead of the intended human-readable display value.

title: Transformed config is computed but never used
body: get_monitor_environment_context copies monitor.config into local `config` and translates `schedule_type` to its display value, but then returns the original `monitor_environment.monitor.config` instead of `config`. The translation is dead code and consumers always get the raw schedule_type value. Return the transformed `config` variable.

title: Public helpers removed/renamed without aliases
body: The refactor deletes `mark_failed_threshold`, `create_issue_platform_occurrence`, `get_failure_reason`, `get_monitor_environment_context`, and `SimpleCheckIn` from `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed` and reintroduces them under new names/locations (`try_incident_threshold` in `incidents.py`, `create_incident_occurrence` in `incident_occurrence.py`, `SimpleCheckIn` in `monitors.types`). Any existing importer of the old names breaks at import time. Keep backwards-compatible aliases in `mark_failed.py` or update all callers in the same change.

title: Zero flusher processes possible causes crash / silent data loss
body: self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards)) with no validation. If --flusher-processes 0 (or negative) is passed, num_processes becomes 0, then `i % self.num_processes` raises ZeroDivisionError, or if there are zero shards no processes are created and segments are never flushed. The CLI option defaults to 1 but accepts any int. This can crash the consumer on startup or silently drop all segments.

title: Inconsistent metric tag shards vs shard
body: Produce timer uses tags={"shard": shard_tag} but wait_produce uses tags={"shards": shard_tag}. The plural key splits the metric series, breaking dashboards/alerts that filter on shard and hiding flusher latency after the multiprocess change.

title: Restart leaks thread/process and double-flushes shards
body: _ensure_processes_alive only kills when isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process). In test/thread mode (produce_to_pipe set) and for hung threads, _create_process_for_shards overwrites self.processes/process entry without stopping the old thread. Two threads then run SpanFlusher.main on the same shards concurrently, causing duplicate Kafka produces and races in flush_segments/done_flush_segments. The unused _create_process_for_shard helper has the same leak.

title: join() ignores timeout and terminates healthy processes
body: join() computes remaining_time but never uses it, polls with `while process.is_alive() and deadline > time.time()`, then unconditionally calls process.terminate() even if the process already exited, and `break`s out of the loop on deadline leaving remaining processes never waited on or terminated. Shutdown/rebalance can hang, leak processes, or SIGTERM a cleanly-exited flusher.

title: Flaky sync after mocking time.sleep to no-op
body: test_basic monkeypatches time.sleep to lambda _: None for aggressive flushing, then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting to give flusher threads time to process after drift change. The mocked sleep does nothing, so there is no synchronization with the background flusher thread; the test relies on a race and can flake. The new test_flusher_processes_limit also only asserts process counts and never verifies segments from shared shards are actually flushed.

title: Spawned flusher processes are never killed/terminated
body: In _ensure_processes_alive and join the code guards cleanup with isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process). Processes are created with self.mp_context.Process where mp_context is multiprocessing.get_context("spawn"), whose class is SpawnProcess (a BaseProcess sibling of the default ForkProcess exposed as multiprocessing.Process). The isinstance check is therefore False for real flusher processes, so process.kill() on hang/crash and process.terminate() in join() never run. Consequence: hung processes are not reaped while a replacement is started (duplicate flushing of the same shards, fd/process leaks), and join() can wait/hang instead of terminating children.

title: Invalid flusher-process count can silently disable flushing
body: self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards) treats 0 as unset, and self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards)) accepts negative values. The --flusher-processes CLI option has no validation, so --flusher-processes 0 silently becomes shard-count instead of 0, and a negative value yields range(negative) == empty, i.e. zero entries in process_to_shards_map and zero flusher processes. With zero processes nothing ever calls flush_segments/done_flush_segments, so segments accumulate in Redis forever and are never produced to buffered-segments.

title: Inconsistent metric tag name shards vs shard
body: Produce timer uses tags={"shard": shard_tag} but the wait_produce timer uses tags={"shards": shard_tag}. Consumers of spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce grouped by shard will see a new tag key after this change, breaking existing dashboards/alerts and splitting series. The tag key should be shard in both places.

title: isinstance check never matches spawn processes so unhealthy flushers are never killed
body: Processes are created with `self.mp_context.Process` where `mp_context` is `multiprocessing.get_context('spawn')`, i.e. `SpawnProcess` instances. Both `_ensure_processes_alive` and `join` guard `kill()`/`terminate()` with `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. On Linux the default `multiprocessing.Process` is the fork context's Process, not `SpawnProcess`, so the check is False for the actual flusher processes. The old process is then orphaned and `self.processes[process_index]` is overwritten with a new process while the old one keeps flushing the same shards, causing duplicate produces to buffered-segments, Redis contention, and process leaks. The same guard in `join` means hung spawn processes are never terminated.

title: Restarting one flusher shard-group leaks the old worker and duplicates flushing
body: `_ensure_processes_alive` calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` to replace a dead/hung worker. For the `threading.Thread` test path there is no stop/kill at all, and for the process path the kill is skipped by the bad isinstance check. All workers also share a single global `stopped` flag, so there is no way to stop only the replaced worker. The old worker keeps running `SpanFlusher.main` on the same shards while the new worker starts, so two workers concurrently call `flush_segments`/`done_flush_segments` and `produce` for the same shards, duplicating Kafka messages and corrupting flush bookkeeping.

title: Inconsistent metric tag shard vs shards breaks flusher dashboards
body: `SpanFlusher.main` emits `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` with `tags={"shard": shard_tag}` but emits `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` with `tags={"shards": shard_tag}`. The singular vs plural tag name means the three timers for the same flusher cannot be correlated/grouped, breaking existing dashboards and alerts that filter on `shard`.

title: Partition lock creation is racy
body: OffsetTracker._get_partition_lock reads and writes self.partition_locks dict without any synchronization. Two threads calling add_offset/complete_offset for a new Partition can both miss in .get() and setdefault different Lock objects, so callers end up holding different locks and all_offsets/outstanding/last_committed are mutated without mutual exclusion. This corrupts committable-offset computation leading to duplicate processing or skipped commits.

title: Committable scan loops over full offset range
body: get_committable_offsets does for offset in range(start, max_offset+1) over Kafka offsets. A single missing offset (gap from filtered/decode-failed or not-yet-seen message) leaves all later offsets in all_offsets forever, so the range grows unboundedly and this runs every second per partition. With large or sparse offsets this is CPU-heavy and all_offsets/outstanding grow without bound (memory leak) blocking all later commits.

title: close() stops commits before draining workers
body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close sets shutdown_event and joins the commit thread, then shuts down the queue pool. Any work item that completes after the commit thread exits will call complete_offset but never be turned into a commit via mark_committed/commit_function. On graceful shutdown processed messages are therefore never committed and will be reprocessed on restart, and there is no final flush.

title: Offsets committed from background thread
body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy._commit_loop runs in its own Thread and calls the Arroyo commit callable asynchronously every second, while submit/poll run on the StreamProcessor thread. Arroyo expects commit to be called from the processing thread for the owned partitions; concurrent commit during rebalance/shutdown can commit offsets for revoked partitions, race with StreamProcessor shutdown, and mark_committed races across multiple strategy instances sharing the same OffsetTracker.

title: Single shared queue pool across partitions/rebalances
body: ResultsStrategyFactory creates one FixedQueuePool/OffsetTracker in __init__ and reuses it for every create_with_partitions call. Each call then creates a SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy with its own commit thread but sharing the tracker. Each commit thread calls its own partition-scoped commit with committable offsets for all partitions, misrouting commits, and close/terminate of one strategy shuts down the pool still used by other partitions.

title: shutdown clears queue_pool breaking rebalance
body: ResultsStrategyFactory.shutdown shuts down the pool and sets self.queue_pool to None. Arroyo factories are long-lived and create_with_partitions is called again after a rebalance; create_thread_queue_parallel_worker then asserts queue_pool is not None and fails. The factory cannot serve new assignments after any shutdown/close.

title: Failed work items marked complete and committed
body: OrderedQueueWorker.run catches all Exceptions from result_processor, logs, and then unconditionally calls offset_tracker.complete_offset in finally. Despite the class docstring claiming only successful processing is committed, poison messages are treated as done and their offsets become committable, silently skipping data instead of blocking/retrying/DLQing.

title: Shutdown flag causes queued items to be dropped
body: FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets worker.shutdown=True before draining, and OrderedQueueWorker.run checks `while not self.shutdown` at the top of the loop. A worker that has just finished one item will exit on the next iteration even if many items remain in its queue. q.shutdown(immediate=False) is meant to drain, but the flag defeats it. Consequence is silent loss of results that were already accepted and tracked in OffsetTracker, they will never be processed nor committed.

title: Single shared queue_pool used by multiple partition strategies
body: ResultsStrategyFactory creates one FixedQueuePool in __init__ but create_thread_queue_parallel_worker creates a new SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy per partition assignment sharing that same pool, offset_tracker, and queues, each with its own commit_thread and commit closure. Concurrent commit loops race on get_committable/mark_committed, and close/terminate of one strategy shuts down the pool still in use by other partitions. Consequence is double commits, missed commits, and premature worker shutdown on rebalance.

title: join() destroys processing state instead of flushing
body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.join calls close(), which stops the commit thread and shuts down all queue workers. In Arroyo join(timeout) is expected to block until in-flight work is done without tearing down the strategy, and may be called repeatedly. Consequence is that a poll/join cycle or rebalance can permanently kill the shared pool and lose queued work.

title: wait_until_empty ignores in-flight work
body: FixedQueuePool.wait_until_empty and get_stats use only Queue.qsize(), which drops to zero as soon as a worker has dequeued an item, before result_processor finishes and before OffsetTracker.complete_offset. Callers checking total_items==0 conclude processing is done while work is still running. Consequence is flaky tests and premature commit/shutdown decisions in production code that polls queue depth.

title: Partition lock creation is racy and leaks state
body: OffsetTracker._get_partition_lock does get then setdefault on plain dict partition_locks without any global lock. Concurrent add/complete from many workers can create multiple Lock objects and mutate all_offsets/outstanding/last_committed dicts concurrently. In CPython this can return different locks to different threads, breaking the per-partition mutual exclusion that get_committable_offsets relies on. Consequence is corrupted offset sets and unsafe commits.

title: Commit scan iterates full offset range
body: OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets computes min/max of all_offsets then loops `for offset in range(start, max_offset+1)`. If there is any gap the loop cost is proportional to the offset distance, not the number of tracked messages. A large skipped offset or long backlog makes the 1-second commit loop scan hundreds of thousands of integers per partition while holding the partition lock. Consequence is commit-thread stalls and blocked add/complete.

title: FilteredPayload triggers exception log path on every skip
body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit calls decoder unconditionally, but the real decoder ResultsStrategyFactory.decode_payload asserts `not isinstance(payload, FilteredPayload)` and raises AssertionError for filtered messages. The strategy relies on the outer except to then add+complete the offset, logging an exception stack for normal operation. Consequence is noisy error logs and dependence on exception handling for a routine case; filtered messages should be completed without logging an error.

title: Failed items are still marked complete and committed
body: OrderedQueueWorker.run() calls offset_tracker.complete_offset() in a finally block even when result_processor raises. ResultProcessor.__call__ also swallows exceptions internally and returns normally. In both cases the offset becomes committable and _commit_loop will commit it. A poison or transiently failing result is therefore acked with no retry, DLQ, or requeue, causing silent data loss.

title: Strategy close shuts down shared queue pool breaking rebalances
body: FixedQueuePool is created once in ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__ and shared across all strategies returned by create_with_partitions, but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()/terminate()/join() call queue_pool.shutdown(). On Kafka rebalance Arroyo closes the old strategy, which shuts down workers and queues still referenced by the new strategy. Subsequent submits go to shut-down queues and workers never process again.

title: Commit scan iterates over offset number range and leaks memory on stall
body: OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets() does for offset in range(start, max_offset+1) where start/max are Kafka offsets. A gap from a stalled head-of-line item or a large log jump makes this loop iterate millions of integers every second in _commit_loop. Meanwhile all_offsets only shrinks on mark_committed, so if offset N never completes all later offsets accumulate unbounded in two sets, growing memory until the stall clears.

title: Partition lock map accessed without synchronization
body: OffsetTracker._get_partition_lock() reads and mutates self.partition_locks dict with get/setdefault and no global lock, while add_offset/complete_offset/get_committable_offsets/mark_committed can run concurrently from submit, worker threads, and commit thread. Concurrent creation for a new Partition can create duplicate Lock objects or raise, so two threads can then guard the same partition with different locks and corrupt all_offsets/outstanding.

title: wait_until_empty ignores in-flight items
body: wait_until_empty() and get_stats() use only queue.qsize(). An item already removed from the queue by a worker but not yet processed and completed via complete_offset() is invisible, so the function can return True while work is still in flight. Any caller using it as a drain barrier will proceed prematurely.

title: Backup-code login can bypass password check
body: authorize() skips password verification when credentials.totpCode is truthy, but takes the backup-code branch whenever credentials.backupCode is truthy. An attacker who knows a victim's email and one valid backup code can send password=wrong, totpCode=anything, backupCode=valid. The password check is skipped because totpCode is present, the backup-code check succeeds, and login returns success. This reduces 2FA to single-factor (backup code only) and allows account takeover without the password. Password must be verified for CAL users regardless of second-factor fields.

title: OAuth/SAML users blocked from using backup codes
body: The early guards throw ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled and IncorrectEmailPassword when credentials.totpCode is missing, without considering credentials.backupCode. A Google/SAML user with 2FA who loses their authenticator and submits only email+backupCode via the lost-access UI will always hit the third-party error and can never use a backup code. The checks must also accept backupCode as satisfying the second-factor presence.

title: Backup-code match is case-sensitive and whitespace-sensitive
body: Generated codes are lowercase hex but displayed with placeholder XXXXX-XXXXX and formatted with a dash, so users will naturally type uppercase or paste with spaces/newlines. The code only does replaceAll("-","") and indexOf, with no toLowerCase() or trim(). A correct code typed in uppercase or with surrounding whitespace fails with IncorrectBackupCode, causing false lockout. Same pattern exists in the disable endpoint. Normalize case and whitespace before comparison.

title: Non-string backupCode crashes disable endpoint
body: The handler guards only truthiness of req.body.backupCode then unconditionally calls req.body.backupCode.replaceAll. If a client sends a truthy non-string JSON value such as a number, array, or object, replaceAll throws TypeError, producing an unhandled 500 instead of a 400 IncorrectBackupCode. Validate typeof backupCode === 'string' before string operations.

title: Backup-code single-use check has TOCTOU race
body: Login does read-decrypt-indexOf-encrypt-write as separate steps: it reads backupCodes, finds the index, sets that slot to null, and writes back. Two concurrent logins with the same backup code can both read the same array before either writes, both find the code, and both succeed. This allows replay of a supposedly single-use backup code. The consume must be atomic via transaction, row lock, or optimistic concurrency.

title: No test for backup-code login or disable
body: The PR adds backup-code generation, login via credentials provider, and disable via backup code, including single-use invalidation and new error codes. The e2e file explicitly leaves TODO for login + disabling with backup and only asserts download filename and copy toast. There is no automated proof that a valid backup code logs in, that reuse fails, or that disable with backup works, leaving the critical auth paths uncovered.

title: Backup-code login can bypass password verification
body: Password is only verified when `!credentials.totpCode` (line 121). The backup-code branch (line 131) does not verify password at all. An attacker who knows only a victim's email and one valid backup code can send both `totpCode=<anything>` and `backupCode=<valid>` to /api/auth/callback/credentials: the dummy totpCode skips the password check, the backup branch ignores totp validity and grants login. This turns a second factor into a password replacement and allows account takeover without the password.

title: Backup-code single-use is not atomic and allows concurrent reuse
body: Login does read-decrypt-indexOf, then sets `backupCodes[index]=null` and writes back with a separate prisma update. Two concurrent authorize calls with the same backup code can both read the same array, both find the index, and both succeed before either write nulls it. This violates the advertised exactly-once property and lets one code be used twice.

title: Existing 2FA users can never obtain backup codes
body: Setup rejects with TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled if twoFactorEnabled is true. The migration adds nullable backupCodes, so all pre-existing 2FA users have NULL. There is no regenerate endpoint, so they stay without codes forever, login/disable with backup always returns MissingBackupCodes, and the UI message telling them to generate codes in settings is a dead end.

title: Backup-code handling crashes on non-string input and rejects pasted codes
body: Disable calls req.body.backupCode.replaceAll without type check, trim, or case normalization. A non-string value (array/object/number) throws TypeError and returns 500 instead of 400. Pasted codes with trailing spaces/newlines from the downloaded file also fail because only dashes are stripped. The same pattern exists in next-auth-options authorize, so login has the same crash and usability failure.

title: Exhausted backup codes reported as incorrect instead of missing
body: Used codes are nulled in place, so after 10 uses the column contains JSON like [null,...] which is truthy. The check only tests column null, so exhausted users fall through to indexOf failure and get IncorrectBackupCode instead of MissingBackupCodes. They cannot distinguish wrong vs exhausted, and with no regeneration endpoint they are permanently stuck if they lose their authenticator.

title: Backup codes kept only in memory are permanently lost on refresh
body: Codes are fetched at setup time and held only in React state, then shown after enable succeeds. If the user reloads, closes the tab, or loses network between enable and saving, the in-memory codes are gone. Because setup is blocked once twoFactorEnabled is true and there is no re-view or regenerate API, the user permanently loses their backup codes immediately after enrollment.

title: Backup-code login can bypass password check with dummy totpCode
body: authorize() only verifies the password when `!credentials.totpCode` (line 121), but the backup-code branch is taken whenever `credentials.backupCode` is truthy without requiring totpCode to be empty. An attacker who knows a valid backup code can send email + valid backupCode + any dummy totpCode, which skips password verification and then succeeds on backup-code check alone without ever verifying password or TOTP. Consequence is second-factor-only login: password is not required, so a leaked or guessed 10-char backup code alone yields account takeover.

title: Backup codes stored with reversible encryption instead of hash
body: Backup codes are persisted with symmetricEncrypt, which is reversible with CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY, and later decrypted for comparison. Unlike the TOTP secret which must be reversible, backup codes only need comparison and should be one-way hashed like passwords. Consequence is that any database plus encryption-key compromise exposes all long-lived backup codes in plaintext, allowing persistent bypass of the authenticator.

title: Backup-code check-then-update race allows reuse
body: Login reads the decrypted backupCodes array, finds the matching index, then in a separate prisma.user.update writes the array back with that entry nulled. Two concurrent authorize() calls with the same code can both pass the indexOf check before either write completes, so both succeed. Consequence is the exactly-once guarantee for backup codes is broken under concurrency.

title: Lost-access toggle button unintentionally submits disable form
body: The Lost access / Go back button is rendered inside the Form that handles disable but has no type="button" and no preventDefault, so browsers treat it as type submit. Clicking it to switch between TOTP and backup-code inputs also triggers handleDisable with empty codes. Consequence is spurious disable requests and confusing incorrect-code errors when the user only intended to switch modes.

title: Download backup-codes button also submits enable form
body: The download link and Button are inside the Form whose submit handler verifies the TOTP code, but unlike the Copy and Close buttons which call preventDefault, the Download button has no type button handling or preventDefault. Clicking Download therefore also submits the enable form with the stale totpCode. Consequence is duplicate enable API calls on every download, possible error states on the backup-codes screen where no error is displayed.

title: Throwing Error instead of JSON response breaks client handling
body: When the encryption key is missing or the 2FA secret is missing the handler does throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError) instead of returning res.status(500).json({error}). An uncaught throw in a Next.js API route produces a non-JSON 500 page, while the modal client always does await response.json() and expects {error}. Consequence is unhandled exceptions, failed JSON parsing, and generic UI failure instead of a structured error.

title: Backup-code verification is case and whitespace sensitive
body: Generated codes are lowercase hex displayed as XXXXX-XXXXX, but verification only does replaceAll("-","") with no trim or toLowerCase, same pattern in the disable endpoint. A user typing uppercase, pasting with spaces, newlines, or surrounding whitespace gets IncorrectBackupCode even with a correct code. Consequence is legitimate backup codes are rejected and users can be locked out when they most need recovery.

title: Used codes nulled not removed so exhaustion never detected
body: After a successful backup-code login the code sets backupCodes[index] = null and re-encrypts the same-length array. After all 10 codes are used the column is still a non-null JSON array of nulls, so the MissingBackupCodes check for !user.backupCodes never fires and later attempts always return IncorrectBackupCode. Consequence is stale data accumulates and users get a misleading error with no signal that they are out of codes and must re-generate via disable/enable.

title: No coverage for login or disable with backup code
body: This PR adds backup-code authentication in next-auth, the login page Lost access flow, and the disable-with-backup-code endpoint, but the e2e only exercises download, copy, and close of the backup-codes dialog and explicitly leaves a TODO for login plus disabling with backup. Consequence is single-use invalidation, password interaction, and IncorrectBackupCode/MissingBackupCodes paths ship untested.

title: updateEvent fallback can never match, calendarId becomes undefined
body: In updateEvent selectedCalendar is externalCalendarId when truthy else event.destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId). When the else branch runs externalCalendarId is falsy (null/undefined/''), so comparing stored externalIds to a falsy value never matches and the result is always undefined. Updates without an externalCalendarId therefore call Google with calendarId undefined instead of falling back to the destination calendar, causing update failures.

title: deleteEvent fallback can never match, deletes from wrong calendar
body: In deleteEvent calendarId uses the same pattern: externalCalendarId when truthy else find destination where externalId equals externalCalendarId. The else branch only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy so the find always returns undefined and the code falls back to 'primary'. A booking whose destination is a non-primary calendar but has no externalCalendarId will therefore delete from primary and leave the real event orphaned.

title: createEvent patch ignores primary fallback
body: createEvent inserts with calendarId selectedCalendar || 'primary' but the follow-up patch for hangoutLink uses raw selectedCalendar. When no destination matches credentialId, selectedCalendar is undefined, so insert goes to primary while patch is sent with undefined calendarId and fails, leaving the description without the hangout link.

title: Google Meet fallback crashes when no destinationCalendar
body: EventManager.create does const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [] then reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining. When destinationCalendar is null or empty the destructured value is undefined, so accessing .integration throws TypeError and crashes booking creation for Google Meet events without a destination calendar. It should be mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration.

title: updateAllCalendarEvents reuses stale credential across references
body: In updateAllCalendarEvents credential is declared outside the for loop and only reassigned when a lookup succeeds. If a reference has a credentialId that is found in neither memory nor DB, credential keeps the value from the previous iteration (or undefined on first). The code then calls updateEvent with the wrong credential, updating the wrong user's calendar and leaving the intended calendar stale, or throwing when undefined.

title: Collective hosts dropped when organizer has no destinationCalendar
body: handleNewBooking initializes evt.destinationCalendar to null when neither eventType nor organizer has one, then does evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars) for COLLECTIVE events. Optional chaining on null is a no-op, so second hosts' destinationCalendars collected in teamDestinationCalendars are silently discarded and those hosts never get calendar events.

title: CalDAV service ignores per-credential destination, only uses first host
body: BaseCalendarService.createEvent takes only event and picks const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []. EventManager loops over every destination and passes credential/externalId, but this implementation ignores credentialId and always filters to the first destination. For collective bookings with multiple CalDAV/Lark/Office365 hosts this duplicates into the first host calendar and never creates in the others. Same limitation exists in Lark and Office365 services which also only read index 0.

title: destinationCalendar changed from single object to array, breaking webhooks
body: CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar changed from DestinationCalendar|null to DestinationCalendar[]|null. Webhook payloads, emails and any external consumers expecting an object or null now receive an array. The e2e file shows the inconsistency: some triggers still expect null while BOOKING_REJECTED now expects [], proving the contract is both breaking and inconsistent across code paths that return null vs [].

title: Calendar.createEvent now requires credentialId, breaking implementations
body: The Calendar interface changed to createEvent(event, credentialId: number) with required second param, but Lark, Office365 and CalDAV implementations still declare createEvent(event) only. Callers passing only one arg get undefined credentialId at runtime, and third-party Calendar implementations will fail type-check. The param should be optional or all implementations updated.

title: updateEvent fallback calendar lookup can never match
body: In updateEvent selectedCalendar is computed as externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId. When externalCalendarId is falsy the else branch searches for a destination whose externalId equals that same falsy value, which never matches, so selectedCalendar becomes undefined instead of falling back to the booking's destination calendar. The Google events.update/patch calls then receive undefined calendarId and fail. Previously it fell back to event.destinationCalendar.externalId.

title: deleteEvent fallback calendar lookup can never match
body: In deleteEvent calendarId is computed as externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId. When externalCalendarId is null/undefined the fallback searches for externalId equal to null/undefined and always returns undefined, so deletion falls back to primary instead of the stored destination calendar. Previously it used event.destinationCalendar.externalId. This breaks deletes for bookings without an explicit externalCalendarId.

title: Crash when destinationCalendar is empty in Meet fallback
body: In EventManager.create the code does const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [] then checks mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar" without optional chaining. When destinationCalendar is null, undefined or [] the destructured value is undefined and accessing .integration throws TypeError, aborting booking creation. Bookings without a destination calendar, which previously took the fallback path via optional chaining, now crash. It should be mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration.

title: Collective team calendars dropped when organizer has no destination calendar
body: evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to null when neither eventType nor organizer has a destination calendar, then collective hosts are added via evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars). When it is null the optional chain no-ops and all teamDestinationCalendars are silently lost. Subsequent creation only writes evt.destinationCalendar[0] to the Booking, so secondary hosts never get calendar invites. Initialize to [] instead of null.

title: Inverted slug condition in organization creation
body: The spread was changed from ...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }) to ...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}). The original set slug directly when team billing was disabled and only set requestedSlug when enabled. The new code does the opposite: sets slug when billing is enabled and sets no slug when disabled. This breaks org creation in both modes and is unrelated to the destinationCalendar fix.

title: updateLocation loses externalCalendarId in references
body: In updateLocation referencesToCreate is built as externalCalendarId: result.externalId. Results there come from CalendarManager.updateEvent, which never returns externalId or credentialId (unlike createEvent which does). So externalCalendarId is always undefined and newly created booking references lose the calendar ID needed for future updates/deletes. It should preserve booking.references externalCalendarId or the event destination.

title: Webhook destinationCalendar contract broken and tests inconsistent
body: CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar changed from single object/null to array, which changes the public webhook payload shape. The PR updates only the BOOKING_REJECTED expectation to [] while BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED still expect null. Consumers expecting an object or null will break, and the e2e suite will fail for the unchanged cases. This is a breaking API change needing migration/docs and consistent test updates.

title: Crash when destinationCalendar is empty
body: In packages/core/EventManager.ts line 119 the code does const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [] and then accesses mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining. When destinationCalendar is null, undefined or [], the destructured variable is undefined and accessing .integration throws TypeError. Previously evt.destinationCalendar?.integration was safe. Consequence: any booking/create without a destination calendar crashes event creation and falls back from Google Meet to Cal Video check never runs.

title: updateEvent fallback calendar is dead code
body: In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts lines 254-256 selectedCalendar is externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId. The else branch only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, but then it searches for cal.externalId === externalCalendarId which can never match, so it always yields undefined. Previously it fell back to event.destinationCalendar.externalId. Consequence: updates without externalCalendarId call Google with calendarId undefined and fail.

title: deleteEvent fallback calendar is dead code
body: In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts lines 315-317 calendarId is externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId. The else branch only executes when externalCalendarId is falsy and therefore the find predicate never matches, yielding undefined and falling back to primary. Previously it fell back to the stored destinationCalendar. Consequence: deletions for old bookings without externalCalendarId delete from wrong calendar or silently miss.

title: patch uses undefined calendarId after primary fallback
body: In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts line 168 calendar.events.patch uses calendarId: selectedCalendar while insert uses calendarId: selectedCalendar || primary. When no destination matches credentialId, selectedCalendar is undefined, insert goes to primary but patch is called with undefined. Consequence: Google patch call fails or throws after successful insert when hangoutLink is present.

title: Collective second host gets first host organizer email
body: In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts lines 100-103 and 122-124 mainHostDestinationCalendar is always element 0 of destinationCalendar and its externalId is used as organizer email for every create/update. EventManager now loops over each destination and calls createEvent per credentialId, but the payload still uses the first host calendar. Consequence: events created in the second host calendar carry the first host email as organizer, causing wrong invites and ownership.

title: Required credentialId breaks Calendar interface
body: In packages/types/Calendar.d.ts line 221 createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number) makes the second argument required, while Lark, Office365 and BaseCalendarService still implement createEvent(event) with one param and other callers may call with one arg. In TypeScript implementations with fewer params are allowed but callers with one arg now fail type checking. Consequence: breaking contract change; it should be credentialId?: number to remain backward compatible.

title: Collective destinations lost when organizer has no calendar
body: In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts evt.destinationCalendar is set to null when neither eventType nor organizer has a calendar, then code does evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars) for COLLECTIVE. When it is null the optional push is a no-op. Consequence: for collective events without organizer destination, team host calendars collected in teamDestinationCalendars are silently dropped and hosts never get calendar invites.

title: Recurring collective cancel only deletes organizer calendars
body: In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts lines 449-461 the allRemainingBookings recurring path iterates only bookingToDelete.user.credentials to delete updatedBookings references. For collective bookings other hosts credentials and calendars are not in that user object. Consequence: cancelling all recurring instances leaves orphan events on co-host calendars.

title: Missing prisma import causes ReferenceError
body: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts uses prisma.credential.update at line 96 but never imports prisma. Every Salesforce getClient call will throw ReferenceError and break all Salesforce calendar operations, and TypeScript build fails.

title: Stores Zod safeParse wrapper instead of token data
body: In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the full safeParse result {success, data}. The code stores that wrapper as credential.key instead of .data. The next load via googleCredentialSchema.parse will fail because the stored shape is {success,data} not tokens, corrupting Google credentials after first refresh.

title: Placeholder refresh_token overwrites real refresh token
body: parseRefreshTokenResponse injects refresh_token='refresh_token' literal when missing. The PR docs say the external sync endpoint returns only access_token and expiry. Callers in Office365, Zoom and Webex persist that object, overwriting the valid stored refresh_token with the dummy string and permanently destroying the ability to refresh via the provider.

title: Lenient token schema uses broken computed keys and strips fields
body: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses [z.string().toString()] as object keys, which evaluates to a literal string like Zod object toString, not a wildcard. Zod by default strips unknown keys, so expiry_date, expires_in, instance_url, signature and other required fields are dropped. Downstream merges then lose expiry and Salesforce loses instance_url, corrupting credentials.

title: Sync path returns fetch Response but code expects .data
body: When credential sync is enabled refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response. Google code does res?.data expecting a Gaxios response with .data. fetch Response has no .data, so token is undefined and token.access_token throws TypeError, breaking Google refresh for all sync-enabled users.

title: Sync response treated as HubspotToken without parsing
body: Hubspot refresh expects a HubspotToken object from hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken. When sync is enabled refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response. The code then reads .expiresIn/.accessToken directly from the Response and computes expiryDate as NaN, storing invalid tokens and breaking Hubspot integration.

title: Passes credentialId as calcomUserId to sync endpoint
body: zoho-bigin refreshAccessToken receives credentialId which is credential.id and passes it as the userId argument to refreshOAuthTokens, which sends it as calcomUserId. The sync endpoint will look up the wrong user or fail, returning wrong tokens. It should pass credential.userId like all other calendar services.

title: Assumes axios shape but sync path returns fetch Response
body: Bigin code does tokenInfo.data.error assuming an axios response. When sync is enabled refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response which has no .data, so tokenInfo.data is undefined and accessing .error throws TypeError, breaking Bigin refresh in sync mode.

title: Assumes axios shape but sync path returns fetch Response
body: Zohocrm code does zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error assuming axios. When sync is enabled refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response with no .data, so .data.error throws TypeError. The sync response is never parsed via .json(), breaking Zoho CRM refresh.

title: Sync response fed to Lark-specific error parser
body: Lark refresh passes the result of refreshOAuthTokens to handleLarkError which expects a Lark envelope {code:0,data:{...}}. The sync endpoint is documented to return only access_token and expiry, so the parser will throw even on success, breaking Lark refresh when sync is enabled. Sync path needs separate parsing.

title: Returns connection with stale tokens after refresh
body: After refreshing and updating the DB with accessTokenParsed.data, Salesforce getClient builds the jsforce.Connection from the old credentialKey.access_token and credentialKey.instance_url instead of the new tokens. All subsequent Salesforce calls use the expired token until the credential is reloaded.

title: Checks statusText instead of status code
body: Salesforce refresh checks response.statusText !== 'OK' to detect failure. statusText is an optional reason phrase that varies by server and is often empty. It should check !response.ok or response.status. The current check causes false failures or missed failures.

title: Bypasses sync helper yet uses lenient schema
body: Unlike every other service, Salesforce getClient always fetches Salesforce directly and never calls refreshOAuthTokens, so sync mode is ineffective. Worse, when sharing is enabled parseRefreshTokenResponse uses the lenient schema that strips instance_url/signature/scope, and the truncated object is persisted, corrupting Salesforce credentials.

title: Wrong appSlug sent to sync endpoint for Zoom
body: Zoom refresh passes appSlug 'zoomvideo' but the DB appId and credential type use 'zoom' and 'zoom_video'. All other services pass the DB slug. The sync endpoint receiving 'zoomvideo' will not match the Zoom app and cannot return tokens, breaking Zoom refresh in sync mode. It should be 'zoom'.

title: Mutating webhook allows any HTTP method
body: The app-credential webhook creates/overwrites user credentials but never checks req.method. GET, HEAD and other methods can mutate state, exposing encrypted keys in logs/caches and enabling CSRF. It should reject non-POST with 405.

title: Unhandled Zod decrypt and JSON errors return 500
body: The webhook calls zod .parse, symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse without try/catch. Invalid body, wrong encryption key or non-JSON plaintext throws and results in unhandled 500 instead of 400, and can crash the handler. It should use safeParse and handle decrypt failures.

title: Webhook header lookup not normalized to lowercase
body: Node lowercases incoming header names, but the code looks up req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME] verbatim. If the operator configures an uppercase header name the lookup always misses and all valid webhooks return 403. The env value should be lowercased before lookup.

title: Find-then-create race can duplicate credentials
body: The webhook does findFirst then update or create as two separate queries. Concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user and app can both miss and both create, leaving duplicate credentials where later reads use findFirst arbitrarily. It should use an atomic upsert or transaction.

title: Sync fetch has no auth, no error check and no fallback
body: refreshOAuthTokens POSTs calcomUserId and appSlug to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT with no secret/HMAC, no Content-Type, no response.ok check and no fallback to direct provider refresh. If the endpoint is down or returns an error, refresh fails even though the provider would succeed, causing availability regression, and the unauthenticated callback is spoofable.

title: Overwrites expiry_date even when sync returns it
body: Office365 video always sets expiry_date from expires_in with fallback 0. If the sync endpoint returns expiry_date instead of expires_in, the valid expiry is overwritten with approximately Date.now(), causing immediate expiry and a refresh loop. It should preserve an existing expiry_date.

title: Sharing flag is string not boolean
body: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is assigned process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY, which is a string or undefined, not a boolean. Strict boolean checks will misbehave. It should be coerced with Boolean or !!.

title: Webhook accepts any HTTP method
body: The handler in apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts never checks req.method, so a state-changing credential create/update can be triggered by GET, HEAD or any verb. That enables CSRF, caching and log exposure of the operation. It should reject everything except POST with 405.

title: Uncaught validation/decryption exceptions return 500
body: The webhook calls zod .parse on the body, then symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse on the encrypted keys with no try/catch or safeParse. Any bad payload, wrong encryption key, or non-JSON plaintext throws and Next.js returns 500 instead of 400, leaking internals and making client errors indistinguishable from server failures.

title: findFirst overwrites arbitrary credential
body: The webhook looks up an existing credential with findFirst by userId+appId and updates that one row. Users can have multiple credentials for the same appId (e.g. two Google accounts, team vs user). findFirst picks an arbitrary row, so a sync can overwrite the wrong account's key and leave duplicates, corrupting calendar/video access.

title: Minimum token schema uses computed literal keys
body: minimumTokenResponseSchema declares properties like [z.string().toString()]: z.number(). In JavaScript that evaluates to a literal key such as "[object Object]", not a catch-all. It does not accept arbitrary expiry fields and requires a nonsense property, so safeParse fails for valid sync-endpoint responses and every synced refresh throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". It should use catchall/passthrough/record.

title: Missing refresh_token replaced with dummy string
body: When the parsed response has no refresh_token, the helper mutates it to the literal string "refresh_token". Callers that spread the result into the stored credential (office365, salesforce, zoom) then permanently overwrite the real refresh token with that dummy value, destroying the ability to refresh again. Missing tokens should be preserved from the old credential, not faked.

title: Sync branch returns raw fetch Response incompatible with callers
body: When credential sharing is enabled the helper returns a raw fetch Response from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT. Google expects GaxiosResponse with .data, HubSpot expects a HubSpot token object, Zoho Bigin/ZohoCRM expect an axios response with .data. Accessing .data, .accessToken or .expiresIn on a fetch Response yields undefined and crashes or stores garbage. The helper also sends URLSearchParams with no Content-Type, no auth, and never checks response.ok before returning.

title: Stores SafeParse wrapper as credential key
body: Google refresh calls parseRefreshTokenResponse which returns a SafeParse result { success, data/error }. The code stores that whole wrapper as prisma.credential.key instead of .data. The next load does googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) on { success, data } and fails, permanently bricking the Google credential after one synced refresh.

title: Uses prisma without importing it
body: Salesforce CalendarService calls prisma.credential.update to persist refreshed tokens, but the file has no import of prisma from @calcom/prisma. At runtime this throws ReferenceError: prisma is not defined, so every Salesforce operation that constructs a client crashes.

title: Refresh status checked via statusText and runs unconditionally
body: Salesforce getClient unconditionally POSTs to login.salesforce.com on every instantiation with no expiry check, adding latency and rate-limit risk. It then validates with response.statusText !== "OK" instead of response.ok/status. statusText is unreliable and often empty with HTTP/2/fetch, so valid token responses can be rejected and errors missed.

title: Passes credentialId as userId and mismatches axios/fetch shape
body: Bigin refresh calls refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId) where credentialId is credential.id, but the third parameter is userId. The sync endpoint receives a credential ID as calcomUserId, and team credentials with null userId are incorrectly treated as syncable. When sync is enabled the helper returns a fetch Response with no .data, so the following tokenInfo.data.error access throws TypeError.

title: Expects axios response but gets fetch Response when synced
body: ZohoCRM refresh wraps an axios call with refreshOAuthTokens. With sync enabled the helper returns a fetch Response which has .json() not .data. The code then reads zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error and zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.access_token, which are undefined for a fetch Response, causing a TypeError and failure to persist the new token.

title: Wrong appSlug sent to credential sync endpoint
body: Zoom refresh passes "zoomvideo" as appSlug to the sync endpoint, but the app's real slug/appId is "zoom" as used in the callback and credential creation. The external endpoint will receive an unknown slug and cannot locate the user's Zoom tokens, so synced Zoom refresh never works.

title: Missing prisma import causes runtime crash
body: File packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts calls prisma.credential.update at line 96 but never imports prisma. Any instantiation of SalesforceCalendarService will throw ReferenceError: prisma is not defined, breaking all Salesforce calendar operations after this PR.

title: Stores Zod SafeParse wrapper as credential key
body: In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts the code does const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...) and then saves key directly as the credential key. parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the SafeParse result object { success, data/error }, not the parsed tokens. The DB will contain { success:true, data:{...} } instead of tokens, so subsequent googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) will fail and calendar calls break. Other services correctly use .data.

title: Minimum token schema does not allow arbitrary keys
body: In packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts the minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys like [z.string().toString()] which evaluates to a literal string such as ZodString, not a wildcard. Zod object defaults to stripping unknown keys, so expiry_date, expires_in, refresh_token etc. are stripped from data. When credential sharing is enabled this causes loss of expiry/refresh data and downstream credential corruption.

title: Injects dummy refresh_token overwriting real token
body: In packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts if the refresh response has no refresh_token the code sets data.refresh_token to the literal string refresh_token. Callers then persist this (Google, Office365 spread, Zoom/Webex assignment). This overwrites a valid stored refresh_token with a dummy value, permanently breaking future refreshes and hiding the fact the provider did not rotate the token.

title: External branch returns fetch Response mismatching callers
body: In packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts the sharing-enabled branch returns a raw fetch Response, while the fallback returns whatever refreshFunction returns. Google expects res.data, Hubspot expects a HubspotToken object with accessToken/expiresIn, Zoho Bigin/CRM expect an axios response with .data. A fetch Response has no .data, so Google gets undefined tokens, Hubspot computes NaN expiry, Zoho throws cannot read property error of undefined. No json parsing or response.ok check is done.

title: Webhook allows any method and crashes on bad input
body: In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts the handler has no HTTP method check, so GET/PUT can create/update credentials. It calls zod parse, symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse without try/catch, so invalid body, wrong encryption key, or malformed JSON throws unhandled and returns 500 instead of 400. This exposes stack behavior and makes integration debugging unreliable for a credential-writing endpoint.

title: Refreshed Salesforce token never used for connection
body: In packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts getClient fetches a new access token and saves it, but then constructs jsforce.Connection with the old credentialKey.instance_url/access_token/refresh_token instead of the parsed refreshed values. The refresh is wasted and subsequent API calls continue using the expired token.

title: Salesforce refresh checks statusText instead of ok
body: In packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts the code throws if response.statusText !== OK. statusText is implementation-dependent and may be empty in fetch polyfills, causing false failures or missed HTTP errors. It should check response.ok or status code.

title: Passes credentialId as userId to sync endpoint
body: In packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts refreshAccessToken calls refreshOAuthTokens with credentialId as the third userId argument. The helper sends it as calcomUserId to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, so the external service receives a credential ID instead of a user ID and will look up the wrong user or fail.

title: Wrong appSlug sent for Zoom refresh sync
body: In packages/app-store/zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts the refresh calls refreshOAuthTokens with appSlug zoomvideo, but the app is stored as appId zoom in the callback and credential. The external credential-sync endpoint receiving zoomvideo will not match the real slug zoom, so synced refresh will fail to resolve the user app.

title: Team admin/owner check uses && instead of ||
body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts line 46, isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...)). This requires the caller to be both admin and owner at the same time. Since those roles are exclusive, pure admins (and pure owners depending on helper semantics) will always fail the check and be denied even when they should be allowed. Consequence: legitimate team admins/owners who are not the organizer/attendee cannot add guests; authorization is broken.

title: Guest deduplication and blacklist bypass via case/whitespace
body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts lines 74-77, filtering does guest === attendee.email and blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) where the blacklist is lowercased but guest is not normalized or trimmed. Email comparison is therefore case-sensitive. Consequence: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS can be bypassed with different casing (e.g. Foo@spam.com vs foo@spam.com) and duplicate Attendee rows differing only by case/whitespace can be created, causing duplicate invites and blacklist evasion.

title: No server-side deduplication of emails within one request
body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts around line 92, the server schema is only z.array(z.string().email()) with no uniqueness check, and the handler only filters against existing attendees, not within the input itself. A payload like ["a@x.com","a@x.com"] passes the filter twice and is inserted via createMany as two Attendee rows. Consequence: duplicate attendee records, duplicate calendar invitees and duplicate emails, corrupting guest counts.

title: Sends original guests list instead of filtered uniqueGuests to mailer
body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts line 168, the handler inserts only uniqueGuests into the database but then calls sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) with the original unfiltered input. The mailer in packages/emails/email-manager.ts uses newGuests.includes(attendee.email) to decide between full scheduled email vs add-guests email. Consequence: pre-existing attendees re-submitted in the request are misclassified as new guests and receive the wrong template, and filtering intent is lost.

title: No booking status/time guard before adding guests
body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts after line 44, there is no check of booking.status, startTime or endTime before inserting attendees, updating the external calendar, and sending emails. Consequence: callers can add guests to cancelled, rejected, or long-past bookings, triggering calendar updates and confusing add-guests emails for dead events.

title: Unbounded guests array allows bulk insert/email abuse
body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts line 5, guests is defined as z.array(z.string().email()) with no min, max, or uniqueness limit. Consequence: a single authenticated call can submit hundreds or thousands of emails, causing a large createMany, many getTranslation lookups, a huge calendar update payload, and fan-out of emails — enabling spam and DoS.

title: Calendar update uses requestor credentials instead of organizer
body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts line 158, credentials are loaded via getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) and EventManager is built from the requestor, even though the booking query already includes booking.user credentials and organizer info. If a team admin or attendee adds guests, the external calendar update runs with calendars that do not own the event. Consequence: updateCalendarAttendees fails or updates the wrong calendar, leaving external calendars out of sync while the database was already mutated.

title: Add-guests emails ignore disableStandardEmails setting
body: In packages/emails/email-manager.ts line 525, sendAddGuestsEmails takes only (calEvent, newGuests) and unconditionally sends organizer and attendee emails, unlike sendScheduledEmails, sendLocationChangeEmails and others which check eventTypeDisableHostEmail/eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail. Consequence: event types or workspaces that disabled standard host/attendee emails will still send add-guests notifications, violating user settings.

title: Validation error flag never cleared on success
body: In apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx around line 36, onSuccess resets the email list and closes the dialog but does not reset isInvalidEmail, while Cancel does. Consequence: after one failed validation followed by a successful add, reopening the dialog still shows the stale 'Emails must be unique and valid' error.

title: Team permission check requires both admin AND owner
body: In addGuests.handler.ts isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as `await isTeamAdmin(...) && await isTeamOwner(...)`. The name and intent is admin OR owner, but && requires the caller to be both at once. If roles are mutually exclusive no team member ever passes, and otherwise pure admins or pure owners are incorrectly denied with FORBIDDEN. The feature then only works for the organizer/attendee, breaking team delegation. Change && to ||.

title: Duplicate and blacklist checks are case-sensitive, blacklist bypassable
body: In addGuests.handler.ts the blacklist is lowercased on load but guest emails are compared verbatim: `guest === attendee.email` for duplicates and `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` for blocks. Emails are case-insensitive, so Blocked@spam.com bypasses blacklist entry blocked@spam.com, and User@x.com creates a second Attendee row alongside user@x.com. Intra-request duplicates like ["a@x.com","a@x.com"] are also not deduped server-side, creating duplicate rows. Normalize with trim().toLowerCase() on both sides and dedupe the request.

title: Guests array unbounded with no dedup allows email bombing
body: In addGuests.schema.ts guests is defined as `z.array(z.string().email())` with no min, max, or uniqueness. Any authenticated caller allowed by the handler, including any existing attendee, can submit hundreds or thousands of addresses in one call. The handler then creates that many Attendee rows, patches calendars, and fans out that many emails. This enables DB bloat, spam/email bombing, and DoS of calendar integrations. Add min/max limits and uniqueness.

title: Email helper called with unfiltered guests list
body: In addGuests.handler.ts the handler filters input into uniqueGuests for the database insert but then calls sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) with the original unfiltered array. The email helper decides new vs existing via newGuests.includes(attendee.email). A re-submitted existing address is therefore misclassified as new and gets a full AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, inconsistent with what was stored. Pass uniqueGuests instead of guests.

title: Calendar update uses caller's credentials instead of organizer's
body: In addGuests.handler.ts credentials are loaded as getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) where ctx.user is whoever called the endpoint, which can be a team admin or attendee, and used to build EventManager for updateCalendarAttendees. The calendar event belongs to the booking owner, not the caller. When a non-organizer adds guests the patch runs with the wrong OAuth tokens, fails or touches the wrong calendar, while the DB already has new attendees. This leaves database and Google/Outlook calendars diverged. Load the organizer's credentials via booking.userId.

title: No guard against adding guests to cancelled or past bookings
body: In addGuests.handler.ts the handler only checks that the booking exists, then inserts attendees for any bookingId. There is no check for status CANCELLED/REJECTED or endTime in the past. Adding guests to a cancelled or finished meeting still creates Attendee rows, attempts calendar patches on dead events, and sends new_guests_added emails for meetings that will never happen. Reject unless booking is active/upcoming.

title: Add-guests emails ignore standard-email disable settings
body: In email-manager.ts sendAddGuestsEmails takes only (calEvent, newGuests) and unconditionally emails organizer, team members, and all attendees. Unlike sendScheduledEmails, sendLocationChangeEmails and others, it never checks disableStandardEmails metadata or host/attendee disabled flags. Workspaces that disabled standard emails for privacy or noise control will still get spammed via this path. Thread eventTypeMetadata and disabled flags through like other send functions.

title: Empty-state Add button missing type button submits parent forms
body: In MultiEmail.tsx the empty-state Add Emails Button has no type attribute while the other add button correctly uses type button. Inside any HTML form a button defaults to submit, so clicking to add an email row in a form using this reusable component submits the whole form instead, triggering validation or navigation. Add type="button" to that Button.

title: Validation error flag never cleared on success
body: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx isInvalidEmail is set true on failed validation, but the onSuccess handler only closes the dialog and clears emails without clearing the flag, and overlay/X close also leaves it set. The next time the dialog is opened the red emails_must_be_unique_valid banner is still visible despite fresh input, confusing users. Reset isInvalidEmail on success, on close, and when input changes.

title: Team admin check requires both admin AND owner
body: In addGuests.handler.ts the authorization computes isTeamAdminOrOwner as (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...)). Requiring both means a team admin who is not an owner, or an owner who is not flagged admin, is denied. It should be OR. Consequence: legitimate team admins cannot add guests while the error appears as forbidden, breaking team workflows.

title: Duplicate and case-variant guest emails bypass dedup filter
body: In addGuests.handler.ts uniqueGuests only filters guests that exactly equal an existing attendee email and lowercases only the blacklist, not the guest. It does not dedupe within the request, trim, or case-normalize. Guests like [a@x.com, a@x.com] or [A@x.com, a@x.com] or blacklist bypass via case all pass, then createMany inserts duplicate Attendee rows. Consequence: duplicate attendees, duplicate calendar invites and emails, and corrupted attendee list.

title: Original guests list sent to email helper instead of filtered list
body: In addGuests.handler.ts the handler computes uniqueGuests filtering out existing attendees and blacklisted emails, creates only uniqueGuests in the DB, but then calls sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) with the original unfiltered input. In email-manager.ts newGuests.includes determines who gets AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. Consequence: an already-existing attendee re-submitted in the request is misclassified as new and gets the wrong invitation email.

title: Guests can be added to cancelled, rejected or past bookings
body: In addGuests.handler.ts after loading the booking the handler only checks existence, never booking.status or booking.endTime/startTime. There is no guard against CANCELLED, REJECTED, or ended bookings. Consequence: callers can append attendees to meetings that will never occur, writing useless Attendee rows and triggering calendar updates and guest emails for an invalid event.

title: Calendar attendee update uses requesting user's credentials
body: In addGuests.handler.ts the handler fetches the booking with organizer user.credentials but then does getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) and new EventManager({...user}) with the caller. When a team admin or attendee adds guests, updateCalendarAttendees runs with their calendars, not the organizer's. Consequence: external calendar (Google/Outlook) update fails or targets the wrong account while the DB was already updated, leaving DB and calendar diverged.

title: Unbounded guests array enables DB and email spam
body: In addGuests.schema.ts guests is defined as z.array(z.string().email()) with no max length or non-empty check. The handler creates one Attendee row per entry and sendAddGuestsEmails fans out to all attendees plus calendar API calls. Consequence: any authorized attendee can submit thousands of emails in one call, bloating the Attendee table and triggering mass email/calendar spam and DoS.

title: Invalid email error never clears after fixing input
body: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx handleAdd sets setIsInvalidEmail(true) on validation failure, but nothing ever sets it back to false except Cancel. Editing the emails to valid values does not clear the flag. Consequence: the 'Emails must be unique and valid' banner persists even after the user fixes the input, confusing users and suggesting failure on success.

title: Add-guests emails ignore disableStandardEmails settings
body: In email-manager.ts sendAddGuestsEmails takes only (calEvent, newGuests) and never checks eventTypeDisableHostEmail or eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail, unlike sendScheduledEmails, sendRescheduledEmails and sendLocationChangeEmails. Consequence: event types that explicitly disabled standard host/attendee emails still send OrganizerAddGuestsEmail and AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, violating host privacy and preference.

title: Index as key mixes up email inputs on removal
body: In MultiEmail.tsx the email list renders <li key={index}> with controlled EmailField values. When a middle row is removed via splice, React reuses DOM nodes by index. Consequence: values, focus and validation state shift to the wrong rows, so users can accidentally submit the wrong email addresses.

title: Add guests offered for past confirmed bookings
body: In BookingListItem.tsx bookedActions which contains edit_booking -> add_members is rendered when isBookingInPast && isConfirmed. The AddGuestsDialog and backend have no date guard. Consequence: users are offered and can submit new guests for meetings that already ended, creating useless attendees and sending invites for a past event.

title: Retry-count cleanup deletes non-SMS reminders
body: In packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts the leading prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany uses OR: [{method:SMS, scheduledDate<=now}, {retryCount:{gt:1}}]. The second branch has no method filter, so it matches EMAIL and WHATSAPP WorkflowReminders as well as SMS. Only the SMS path increments retryCount today, but any non-SMS row that ever reaches retryCount 2 will be silently deleted, losing the reminder and suppressing the notification. Fix by adding method: SMS (and scheduled:false) to the retryCount branch.

title: Retry count increment is not atomic
body: In packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts both failure paths do prisma.workflowReminder.update with data {retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1} using the value read earlier in findMany. Overlapping cron executions can read the same stale value and both write back the same incremented value, losing a count and allowing more retries than the intended limit of 2. Use atomic update {retryCount:{increment:1}} instead.

title: Reminders with missing phone/message never increment retryCount
body: In packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts the loop only updates the DB inside if (message?.length && message?.length>0 && sendTo). If sendTo is missing (e.g. no smsReminderNumber) or the rendered message is empty, the code does nothing: scheduled stays false and retryCount is unchanged. That same row is returned again by the unscheduledReminders query on every cron tick until scheduledDate ages out (up to 7 days), defeating the new 2-retry limit and causing unbounded reprocessing. The skip path must also bump retryCount or otherwise resolve the reminder.

title: Failure-handler update can throw and prevent response
body: In packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts the catch block does await prisma.workflowReminder.update to bump retryCount with no inner error handling. If that update itself fails (row just deleted by the leading deleteMany in a concurrent run, booking/step deleted, transient DB error, P2025 not-found), the exception escapes the handler, no HTTP response is sent, and the cron run fails. Wrap the cleanup update in its own try/catch or use updateMany and always return a response.

title: Retry-count cleanup deletes non-SMS reminders
body: In packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts the deleteMany OR second branch filters only on retryCount gt 1 with no method filter, while the first branch correctly filters method SMS. This deletes WorkflowReminder rows of any method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) that ever have retryCount > 1, not just failed SMS reminders, causing unintended data loss. Fix by adding method: WorkflowMethods.SMS to the retryCount branch.

title: Non-atomic retryCount increment loses retries
body: In packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts the failure paths do data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 } based on the value read earlier instead of an atomic increment. If two cron invocations process the same reminder concurrently, one increment is lost, so the reminder can be retried indefinitely and never reach the gt 1 delete threshold, or exceed the intended 2-attempt limit. Use atomic increment operation instead.

title: Missing sendTo/message never counts toward retry limit
body: In packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts the guard if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo) does nothing when message is empty or sendTo is falsy: it neither schedules nor increments retryCount. That reminder stays scheduled:false with unchanged retryCount and will be returned by findMany on every cron tick until scheduledDate expires, defeating the PR goal of deleting persistently failing reminders after 2 tries and wasting cron work.

title: Retry-count cleanup deletes non-SMS reminders
body: The deleteMany uses OR where the first branch is scoped to method SMS with past scheduledDate but the second branch is just retryCount gt 1 with no method or scheduled filter. That second branch will delete any WorkflowReminder of any method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP, SMS) with retryCount > 1, even if scheduled true and due in the future. This is irreversible data loss and orphans provider jobs by deleting referenceId tracking. The retry branch must also filter method SMS and scheduled false.

title: Non-atomic retryCount increment loses retries
body: Both failure paths update with retryCount set to reminder.retryCount + 1 using the value read when unscheduledReminders were fetched. If two cron invocations overlap, both read the same old value and both write the same new value, losing one retry. A perpetually failing number can then never reach gt 1 and will be retried forever. Use atomic retryCount increment instead of read-modify-write.

title: Missing sendTo/message never increments retry
body: When sendTo is falsy (e.g. booking has no smsReminderNumber) or message is empty, the guard around twilio.scheduleSMS is false and the code does no database update at all, leaving scheduled false and retryCount unchanged. The same reminder will be re-fetched on every cron run until its scheduledDate expires, and the same applies to the continue path when workflowStep or booking is missing. Since the PR goal is to stop endless rescheduling on invalid/missing numbers, these no-op paths must also increment retryCount or be cleaned up.

title: Removal of findMany breaks existing callers
body: In packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts the public method findMany(findManyArgs) that performed prisma.bookingTimeStatusDenormalized.findMany with authorization plus filter conditions was deleted and replaced by getBaseConditions() returning Prisma.Sql. Any existing caller that imports InsightsBookingService and calls findMany will now fail at compile/runtime with TypeError. More seriously, callers must now manually do prisma.$queryRaw with WHERE ${baseConditions}; if any caller is not migrated or forgets to include the fragment, authorization is silently bypassed. This PR updates no callers.

title: ANY(array) binding without cast can fail in Postgres
body: In packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts buildOrgAuthorizationCondition and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition build fragments like ("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})) and ("userId" = ANY(${uniqueUserIds})). A JS number[] is passed as a single bound parameter with no ::int[] cast and without Prisma.join. Postgres cannot always infer the element type of ANY($1), resulting in errors like could not determine data type or operator integer = unknown[]. The PR description states tests were never successfully run, so this is unverified. Consequence is runtime query failure for org/team scoped insights.

title: Org scope test assumes deterministic DB ordering
body: In packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts the org-scope expectation compares Prisma.Sql with toEqual, which compares the bound values arrays order-sensitively. The expected teamIds [org.id, team.id, team2.id, team3.id] and userIds [user.id, user2.id, user3.id] come from TeamRepository.findAllByParentId and MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds which have no ORDER BY.
