Database return order is undefined, but ANY() semantics are order-insensitive. Consequence is a flaky test that fails despite correct authorization logic.

title: Event-type filter OR lacks outer parentheses
body: In packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts buildFilterConditions returns Prisma.sql`("eventTypeId" = $) OR ("eventParentId" = $)` with no outer parentheses. getFilterConditions is public. Any direct composition like WHERE ${filter} AND <other> will evaluate AND before OR in SQL, so rows matching eventParentId bypass the other predicate and leak unauthorized/incorrect rows. Current getBaseConditions happens to wrap it, but the fragment itself is unsafe to reuse. Fix is to return Prisma.sql`(("eventTypeId" = $) OR ("eventParentId" = $))`.

title: Public options type loses required teamId for team scope
body: In packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts the constructor changed from the discriminated union InsightsBookingServiceOptions (which requires teamId when scope is team) to InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions with optional teamId for all scopes. A call with scope team and missing teamId now compiles and only fails safeParse at runtime to null, which later yields 1=0 and an empty result. Consequence is silent empty insights instead of a compile-time error, hiding caller bugs.

title: Public findMany API removed without caller migration
body: InsightsBookingService previously exposed findMany(findManyArgs) that applied authorization plus filter conditions through the Prisma client. This PR deletes that method and replaces it with getBaseConditions() returning a Prisma.Sql fragment for manual $queryRaw use. Any existing production caller that still calls service.findMany() will throw TypeError at runtime and break insights endpoints. The PR itself proves the contract was in use because the integration test had to be rewritten from findMany to $queryRaw. Keep a findMany-compatible wrapper or update all production call sites atomically in the same PR.

title: Auth/filter fragments with top-level OR are unsafe to compose
body: buildFilterConditions returns bare SQL like ("eventTypeId" = X) OR ("eventParentId" = X) with no outer parentheses, and buildOrgAuthorizationCondition/buildTeamAuthorizationCondition return (... AND ...) OR (... AND ...) with no outer parentheses. getBaseConditions happens to wrap them as (auth) AND (filter), but getAuthorizationConditions and getFilterConditions are public and return the unwrapped OR fragments. A caller that writes WHERE ${fragment} AND <other> without adding its own parentheses gets AND-binds-tighter-than-OR semantics, e.g. A OR B AND C becomes A OR (B AND C), returning rows that should have been filtered out. That is an authorization/filter bypass and data leak. Parenthesize each fragment at construction time.

title: Org scope test asserts exact ANY array order from unordered queries
body: The org-scope test uses toEqual against Prisma.sql containing teamIds [org.id, team.id, team2.id, team3.id] and userIds [user.id, user2.id, user3.id]. The service builds those arrays from TeamRepository.findAllByParentId and MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds with no ORDER BY, so database return order is undefined. SQL ANY is order-insensitive, but toEqual on Prisma.Sql values is order-sensitive, so the test can fail intermittently even when logic is correct and enforces an irrelevant ordering. Sort arrays or compare as sets.

title: Caching and empty-membership/invalid-team paths no longer tested
body: This PR deletes the Caching describe block while the service still caches Prisma.Sql auth/filter fragments, so stale-cache or shared-mutable-fragment regressions are now undetected. It also adds no coverage for the single-clause branches: team with zero members, org with no child teams or no members, and teamId not in org returning 1=0. Those branches change SQL shape from OR to a single AND clause and are the exact place where an empty ANY array would produce wrong or invalid SQL. Restore caching tests for Sql and add edge-case tests.

title: Public findMany API removed without caller migration
body: The old InsightsBookingService exposed findMany(findManyArgs) that applied authorization plus filter conditions via Prisma findMany. This PR deletes findMany and replaces it with getBaseConditions() returning Prisma.Sql. Only the service and its test are changed, no callers are updated. Any existing production caller that still calls service.findMany() will fail at compile time or throw TypeError at runtime, breaking insights endpoints.

title: Authorization SQL fragment with top-level OR is not parenthesized
body: buildOrgAuthorizationCondition and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition return a fragment of the form (team condition) OR (user condition) with no outer parentheses, and getBaseConditions returns that fragment bare when there is no filter. SQL AND binds tighter than OR, so a caller composing WHERE ${baseConditions} AND <extra> gets teamCond OR (userCond AND extra) instead of (teamCond OR userCond) AND extra. Extra restrictions like date ranges or additional checks are then bypassed for one branch, returning rows that should have been excluded.

title: Event-type filter OR fragment is not parenthesized
body: buildFilterConditions for eventTypeId returns ("eventTypeId" = $1) OR ("eventParentId" = $1) with no outer parentheses. getBaseConditions happens to wrap it, but getFilterConditions is public and returns bare OR. Any direct use as WHERE ${filter} AND <other> evaluates as A OR (B AND other) because AND has higher precedence, producing wrong filter results.

title: Org scope drops individual bookings when org has no child teams
body: buildOrgAuthorizationCondition computes teamIds as [orgId, ...childTeamIds] but only queries memberships when teamsFromOrg.length > 0, otherwise uses empty user list. When an org has no child teams the query for orgId memberships is skipped, so the (userId = ANY(...) AND isTeamBooking=false) branch is omitted. An org owner then sees no individual bookings, only team bookings, even though org members have individual bookings that should be visible.

title: Org scope test assumes deterministic order for ANY arrays
body: The org-scope test asserts exact equality with Prisma.sql containing team ID array [org, team, team2, team3] and user ID array [user, user2, user3]. Those arrays come from findAllByParentId and findAllByTeamIds which have no ORDER BY, so database return order is not guaranteed. Since = ANY is order-insensitive, the implementation is correct regardless of order but the toEqual on Sql values will flake when the DB returns a different order.

title: updateMany with empty data always throws
body: In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts line 1024 fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) with empty data. Prisma updateMany requires non-empty data and throws PrismaClientValidationError for {}. This runs after the cache upserts, so every cache warmup fails and watchCalendar/unwatchCalendar flows that call it will error.

title: Delete cache does not invalidate calendar query
body: In packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx the deleteCache mutation onSuccess only shows a toast and calls onSuccess prop, while the disconnect mutation invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars and viewer.apps.integrations. After deleting cache the cacheUpdatedAt value stays in the React Query cache, so the dropdown still shows the old timestamp and user thinks deletion failed until a full reload.

title: Cache status ignores expiry
body: In packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.ts getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups all CalendarCache rows by credentialId with no expiresAt filter, while getCachedAvailability only considers rows with expiresAt >= now. Credentials with only expired rows will still report an updatedAt, causing the UI to show Cache Status and a Delete button for cache that will never be used.

title: credentialId input allows floats and negatives
body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/_router.tsx the deleteCache input is z.object({ credentialId: z.number() }). It accepts NaN, floats, zero and negatives. Prisma expects Int, so floats cause a Prisma validation 500 instead of a 400 input error. It should be z.number().int().positive().

title: macOS-only sed breaks script on Linux
body: In scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh line 68 uses sed -i '' -E which is BSD/macOS syntax. On GNU/Linux sed interprets '' as a file name and fails, so the script cannot update GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL for most contributors and CI. It needs OS detection or portable in-place edit handling.

title: Cache timestamp hardcodes en-US locale
body: In packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx the cache last-updated timestamp is formatted with new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...). This ignores the user's locale from useLocale, so non-US users see MM/DD dates inconsistent with the rest of the localized app.

title: Unrelated dev:cron switch to npx tsx without dep
body: In apps/web/package.json dev:cron was changed from ts-node to npx tsx unrelated to calendar cache. tsx is not in dependencies/devDependencies, so npx will fetch it on demand, breaking offline/hermetic installs and adding latency, while ts-node remains in devDependencies. It should be reverted or done in a separate PR with a declared dependency.

title: Empty updateMany data throws and never bumps updatedAt
body: In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts line 1024 fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) with empty data. Prisma updateMany requires non-empty data and throws a validation error for {}, so every cache warmup fails after fetching availability. Even if it did not throw, an empty update would not touch updatedAt, defeating the stated intent to update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt. Fix by passing explicit data like { updatedAt: new Date() }.

title: Delete-cache success never refreshes cache status
body: In packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx the deleteCacheMutation onSuccess only shows a toast and calls optional onSuccess prop, while disconnectMutation invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars and viewer.apps.integrations onSettled. After deleting cache the connectedCalendars query still holds the old cacheUpdatedAt, so the UI keeps showing the old Last updated timestamp unless the parent happens to refetch. Invalidate connectedCalendars on delete success/settled.

title: Cache status includes expired entries
body: In packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.ts getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups by credentialId with no expiresAt filter, while getCachedAvailability only returns rows with expiresAt >= now. The UI therefore shows Cache Status / Last updated even when all rows for that credential are expired and will never be used, misleading users and offering Delete cached data for dead data. Filter status query to non-expired rows.

title: Throws generic Error instead of TRPCError
body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts credential ownership failure throws new Error('Credential not found or access denied'). As a plain Error it surfaces as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR 500 instead of NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN, client cannot distinguish auth failure, and it pollutes server error logs. Throw TRPCError with appropriate code like the rest of the codebase.

title: BSD-only sed breaks script on Linux
body: In scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh line 68 uses sed -i '' -E which is macOS BSD syntax. On GNU/Linux sed -i '' is parsed as an empty backup suffix plus a script file named '', so the GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL replacement fails and webhook local testing is broken on Linux. Use a portable update or OS-specific branch, and resolve ENV_FILE relative to script dir.

title: Cache timestamp hardcoded to en-US
body: In packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx the cache timestamp uses new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', ...) ignoring the user's locale from useLocale. Users in other locales see MM/DD/YYYY format inconsistent with the rest of the app. Pass the current locale instead of hardcoding en-US.

title: Empty updateMany data will throw and break cache warming
body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) with empty data. Prisma updateMany requires a non-empty data object and throws a validation error for {}. This means every call to fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache will throw after writing cache, breaking watch/unwatch flows. Fix by passing an explicit touch like { updatedAt: new Date() }.

title: Cache status not refreshed after delete
body: deleteCacheMutation onSuccess only shows a toast and calls the optional onSuccess prop, while disconnectMutation invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars and viewer.apps.integrations. After Delete cached data succeeds the connectedCalendars query still holds the old cacheUpdatedAt, so the UI keeps showing Last updated and the delete option until a manual reload. Invalidate connectedCalendars on delete success.

title: Cache status includes expired rows
body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups all calendarCache rows by credentialId with max(updatedAt) and no expiresAt filter, while getCachedAvailability only serves rows with expiresAt >= now. The UI will therefore show Cache Status / Last updated for cache that will never be hit and offer Delete for unusable data. Filter to non-expired rows.

title: Generic Error instead of TRPCError
body: deleteCacheHandler throws new Error("Credential not found or access denied") when the credential is not owned by the caller. A plain Error becomes INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, hiding NOT_FOUND vs FORBIDDEN and preventing correct client handling. Use TRPCError with code NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN.

title: Bypasses disabled-cache mock and always hits DB
body: connectedCalendarsHandler directly instantiates new CalendarCacheRepository() instead of using the CalendarCache factory/mock that returns empty when calendar-cache is disabled. This forces a calendarCache.groupBy query on every connectedCalendars fetch even when caching is disabled and can surface cache status when the feature is off. Reuse the same enabled-check/factory used elsewhere.

title: macOS-only sed breaks script on Linux
body: The script updates .env with sed -i '' -E, which is BSD/macOS syntax. On GNU/Linux sed -i '' treats '' as a filename and fails, so GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is never updated in containers/CI which are Linux. Use a portable update or branch on OS.

title: Env path relative to cwd not script
body: ENV_FILE is set to ../.env relative to the current working directory. If run from the repo root as scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh it resolves outside the repo and creates/updates the wrong file. Resolve relative to the script directory.

title: dev:cron uses npx tsx without dependency
body: dev:cron was changed from ts-node to npx tsx but tsx is not in dependencies or devDependencies. Every invocation will fetch tsx from the network, making the script slow, non-hermetic, and a supply-chain risk. Add tsx as a devDependency or revert.

title: Hard-coded en-US date format ignores locale
body: Cache timestamp is formatted with new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...) instead of the user's locale from useLocale. Non-US users will see MM/DD/YYYY short dates inconsistent with the rest of the app. Pass the current locale.

title: Immediate email cancel leaves WorkflowReminder row behind
body: In deleteScheduledEmailReminder when immediateDelete is true the function POSTs batch_id cancel to SendGrid and then returns without deleting or updating the WorkflowReminder row. Callers like reschedule in handleNewBooking and workflow/step delete expect the reminder to be gone, and the SMS path deleteScheduledSMSReminder does delete the row. Consequence is stale rows with scheduled:true remaining linked to the old booking, DB leak, and repeated cancel attempts on an already-cancelled batch_id. The branch must also delete the row.

title: Fire-and-forget cancelled-flag update can be lost
body: handleCancelBooking marks email reminders via deleteScheduledEmailReminder which performs an async prisma.workflowReminder.update to set cancelled:true, but calls it inside forEach without await and without adding it to the awaited prismaPromises. The handler can return before the update commits and errors are unobserved. If the update is lost, cancelled stays null, the scheduleEmailReminders cron never selects it, and the SendGrid email is still sent, which is the bug this PR claims to fix. The same unawaited pattern is repeated in handleNewBooking, bookings.tsx and workflows.tsx and must be awaited via Promise.all.

title: Single SendGrid failure aborts all cancellations and deletes
body: The cron builds prisma delete clients while awaiting each SendGrid cancel sequentially inside one try block. If any client.request throws, control jumps to catch and skips the Promise.all of deletes, so already-queued deletes never execute and remaining reminders are never attempted. One bad batch_id blocks cancellation of all later reminders, causing emails that should have been cancelled to still be sent. Each iteration needs its own try/catch and deletes must still run.

title: Cancel query not restricted to scheduled emails
body: remindersToCancel selects any row with cancelled:true due within an hour, with no filter on method, scheduled, or referenceId. SMS reminders store Twilio SIDs, not SendGrid batch_ids, and unscheduled email reminders have null referenceId. Posting such a value as batch_id to /v3/user/scheduled_sends fails and aborts the whole batch. The query must filter to method EMAIL, scheduled:true, and referenceId not null.

title: Unscheduled scan can resurrect cancelled reminders
body: unscheduledReminders selects EMAIL reminders with scheduled:false due within 72 hours but does not exclude cancelled:true and does not check booking status. Any leftover cancelled row, for example due to the unawaited update racing the cron or an edited workflow leaving a cancelled row alongside a new row, will be sent to SendGrid and marked scheduled:true, sending a reminder for a cancelled or rescheduled booking. The query must exclude cancelled:true and non-accepted bookings and re-check before send.

title: Nullable cancelled column creates three-state logic
body: The migration adds cancelled as nullable BOOLEAN with no default, so all existing rows become NULL and new rows can be NULL. Code checks cancelled:true for cancellation and treats everything else as active, so filters for false miss NULLs and semantics depend on null versus false. The column should be NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE with backfill of existing rows.

title: Single try around cancel loop aborts all remaining cancels and drops queued deletes
body: In packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts the code fetches remindersToCancel then enters one try block that loops with await client.request for each reminder and only after the loop does Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete). If any single SendGrid POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends fails (bad batch_id, already sent, network), execution jumps to catch, remaining reminders are never attempted and the delete promises already pushed are never awaited. Consequence: one bad reminder blocks cancellation of all others in that cron run, so cancelled/rescheduled bookings still get emails, which is the bug this PR claims to fix.

title: immediateDelete path cancels SendGrid but never deletes/flags DB row
body: In packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts deleteScheduledEmailReminder with immediateDelete=true does a SendGrid cancel then returns without deleting the WorkflowReminder row and without setting cancelled=true. Callers like handleNewBooking reschedule rely on this to clean up the old booking's reminders. Consequence: stale rows with scheduled=true and valid referenceId remain linked to the old bookingUid forever until past-date cleanup, DB state says scheduled while SendGrid says cancelled, and the cron cancel query on cancelled=true will never pick them up.

title: SMS DB delete skipped when Twilio cancel throws
body: In packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts deleteScheduledSMSReminder does await twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId) then await prisma.workflowReminder.delete inside the same try. If cancelSMS throws (already sent, unknown SID, Twilio error) the delete is skipped and the error is only logged. Consequence: the WorkflowReminder row for a cancelled/rescheduled booking is left in the DB indefinitely and will never be retried, leaking data and leaving incorrect scheduled state.

title: Fire-and-forget forEach for reminder cancellation can lose updates
body: In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts updatedBookings.forEach calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder which are async and return promises, but forEach does not await them and they are not added to prismaPromises. The same pattern exists in handleNewBooking, viewer/bookings requestReschedule, and viewer/workflows. Consequence: the API can return and the serverless function can freeze before the prisma update to cancelled=true or delete completes, so cancellations are silently lost and reminder emails/SMS are still sent.

title: Reschedule uses immediate SendGrid cancel defeating deferred-cancel fix
body: In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts the reschedule path calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true) which does an immediate SendGrid POST cancel. The PR description says the fix is to only set cancelled=true and let the cron within one hour do the SendGrid cancel to avoid the 100 pending-cancellations limit. Consequence: reschedules again do immediate cancels under load, reintroducing the SendGrid limit failure that caused emails to still be sent, and is inconsistent with the cancel path which correctly defers.

title: Cancel query lacks method/scheduled filter and can SendGrid-cancel SMS
body: In packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts remindersToCancel queries only cancelled=true and scheduledDate lte now+1h, with no filter on method=EMAIL, scheduled=true, or referenceId not null. It then unconditionally POSTs batch_id to SendGrid scheduled_sends. Consequence: any SMS/Twilio reminder ever marked cancelled or any unscheduled row with null referenceId would trigger a SendGrid call with wrong/null batch_id, causing errors that trigger the whole-batch abort, and SMS reminders would be deleted without ever calling Twilio cancel.

title: immediateDelete path never deletes/flags DB row
body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder with immediateDelete=true sends POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends cancel to SendGrid and then returns without deleting the WorkflowReminder row or setting cancelled=true. Callers in handleNewBooking reschedule rely on this to clean up the old booking's reminders. The row stays with scheduled=true and the old referenceId. If the SendGrid call fails it is swallowed inside the function so there is no cron retry (cron only looks for cancelled=true), so the old scheduled email will still be sent after reschedule. Even on success it leaves stale rows until they age out via past-date deletion.

title: One SendGrid failure aborts all cancellations and deletes
body: The cron wraps the entire for-loop over remindersToCancel plus Promise.all of deletes in a single try/catch. If client.request cancel fails for one reminder, execution jumps to catch, skipping remaining reminders and skipping Promise.all for deletes already collected. One bad batch_id therefore leaves all other cancelled emails still scheduled in SendGrid, so they will still be sent.

title: Cancel query missing method/scheduled/referenceId filters
body: remindersToCancel selects where cancelled=true and scheduledDate within next hour, without filtering method=EMAIL, scheduled=true, or referenceId NOT NULL. Any cancelled SMS row or unscheduled row with null referenceId would be sent to SendGrid POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends with batch_id null or a Twilio SID. That request fails and, combined with the single outer try/catch, blocks all valid email cancellations.

title: Reminder cancels fired without await
body: updatedBookings.forEach with nested workflowReminders.forEach calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder without awaiting or collecting promises. Those functions do prisma update/delete and SendGrid/Twilio calls. The handler then proceeds to Promise.all of other deletes and returns success. In serverless the DB update marking cancelled=true may not complete, so the cron never sees it and the supposedly cancelled email/SMS is still sent. Same fire-and-forget pattern is repeated in handleNewBooking, bookings requestReschedule and workflows update/delete.

title: Twilio failure prevents DB delete with no retry
body: deleteScheduledSMSReminder does twilio.cancelSMS then prisma.workflowReminder.delete inside the same try. If cancelSMS throws, the delete is skipped and the error is only logged. Unlike email which has a deferred cancelled flag processed by cron, SMS has no retry path, so the row stays scheduled=true and the SMS will still be sent even though cancellation was requested.

title: Async forEach is fire-and-forget, deletions not awaited
body: In packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts line 125 bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {... await getCalendar() ...}) does not wait for the async callbacks. forEach ignores returned promises, so Reschedule returns true and sends the reschedule email before calendar.deleteEvent / deleteMeeting complete. The surrounding try/catch cannot catch rejections from the async callbacks, causing unhandled rejections and leaving external calendar/video events undeleted, keeping old time blocked.

title: Async forEach is fire-and-forget, deletions not awaited
body: In packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts line 125 bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {... await getCalendar() ...}) does not wait for the async callbacks. forEach discards the promises, so the function returns before calendar.deleteEvent / deleteMeeting finish. Errors inside become unhandled rejections not caught by the surrounding try/catch, leaving stale external events and incorrect availability.

title: requestReschedule deletions fired without awaiting
body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx line 553 bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {... await getCalendar() ... calendar.deleteEvent ... deleteMeeting ...}) is not awaited. The mutation sends the reschedule email and returns while deletions are still in flight. Failures are unhandled rejections with no logging, so old calendar/video events can remain and the previous slot is not freed.

title: Recurring cancel pushes to apiDeletes from unawaited forEach
body: In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts line 460 credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(await calendar.deleteEvent(...)) }) populates apiDeletes asynchronously. The later await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) snapshots apiDeletes before the async callbacks have pushed, so recurring-booking cancellations do not wait for external calendar deletions. On serverless the background work can be killed, leaving ghost events on Google/Office calendars and inconsistent state.

title: Video adapters loaded sequentially instead of in parallel
body: In packages/core/videoClient.ts line 24 getVideoAdapters loops for (const cred of withCredentials) { await appStore[...] } awaiting each dynamic import one by one. Previously adapter creation was synchronous. With multiple video credentials this serializes module loads and slows getBusyVideoTimes/createMeeting/updateMeeting. It should use Promise.all to load in parallel.

title: Dynamic imports are eager, not lazy
body: In packages/app-store/index.ts lines 3-30 the object is built as { applecalendar: import('./applecalendar'), ... }. Each import() executes immediately when the module is first imported, so all 29 apps start loading upfront. This defeats lazy code-splitting, retains the startup cost the PR intended to remove, and creates long-lived rejected promises if any app fails to load instead of loading on demand.

title: Dynamic import rejection not handled, breaks availability
body: In packages/app-store/_utils/getCalendar.ts line 15 await appStore[...] can reject if the dynamic import fails. There is no try/catch, so getCalendar now rejects instead of returning null with a warning. Callers like getCachedResults do await Promise.all(credentials.map(getCalendar)) with no handling, so one broken app import fails the entire availability fetch for a booking page rather than skipping that calendar.

title: Async forEach leaves calendar/video deletions unawaited
body: In packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts line 125 bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...) is used after making getCalendar async. Array.forEach does not await async callbacks and returns void, so promises from await getCalendar(), calendar.deleteEvent() and deleteMeeting() are fire-and-forget. The surrounding try/catch cannot catch their rejections, and the function returns true and sends the reschedule email while deletions are still pending. Consequence: external calendar/video events are not reliably deleted, leaving orphan events and silent failures.

title: Async forEach leaves calendar/video deletions unawaited
body: In packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts line 125 bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...) is used. Array.forEach does not await async callbacks, so the await getCalendar() and subsequent calendar.deleteEvent()/deleteMeeting() promises are never awaited and their rejections escape the surrounding try/catch. Consequence: reschedule completes and returns true while external deletions may still be pending or have failed, leaving stale events on user calendars.

title: Async forEach for reschedule cleanup is not awaited
body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx line 553 bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...) ... }) is fire-and-forget. forEach ignores returned promises, so calendar.deleteEvent() and deleteMeeting() are not awaited before sendRequestRescheduleEmail and webhook dispatch. Consequence: previous slot may not be freed, errors are unobserved, and the mutation reports success while external cleanup failed.

title: Async forEach populates apiDeletes after it is consumed
body: In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts line 460 bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... apiDeletes.push(...) }) runs async callbacks without awaiting them. apiDeletes is later consumed by Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)). Because pushes happen after an await, the array is still empty when it is read for recurring cancellations with allRemainingBookings. Consequence: recurring booking cancellations skip deleting external calendar events, leaving ghost events on Google/Office calendars.

title: getCalendarCredentials now returns promises in sync return value
body: In packages/core/CalendarManager.ts line 28 const calendar = getCalendar(credential) now stores a Promise<Calendar|null> because getCalendar became async, but getCalendarCredentials itself stayed synchronous and still returns [{integration, credential, calendar}]. The contract changed from Calendar|null to Promise without a signature change. Any consumer not updated to await item.calendar will treat a Promise object as truthy Calendar, so checks like if (!calendar) never trigger and calls like calendar.listCalendars fail. Only getConnectedCalendars was updated to await; other importers break.

title: Promise.all on getCalendar makes one bad integration fail all availability
body: In packages/core/CalendarManager.ts line 142 const calendars = await Promise.all(calendarCredentials.map((credential) => getCalendar(credential))) awaits dynamic imports together. If any single import() rejects or getCalendar throws, the whole Promise.all rejects and getCachedResults throws, discarding availability for all other healthy calendars. Previously sync lookup could return null per credential. Consequence: one broken calendar app breaks availability for the entire user.

title: Eager dynamic imports load all apps upfront anyway
body: In packages/app-store/index.ts lines 3-30 the object literal evaluates import("./applecalendar"), import("./googlecalendar"), etc. immediately when the module is first imported. All 27 app chunks therefore start loading upfront just like static imports, with no on-demand lazy loading. Consequence: no cold-start or bundle-size benefit is achieved while every getCalendar/getVideoAdapter now pays an extra async tick and error-handling burden; true laziness requires functions or getters like applecalendar: () => import(...).

title: Async calendar/video deletions in forEach are never awaited
body: In packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts the code does bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...)/deleteMeeting(...); }). Array.forEach does not await async callbacks, so the deletions run fire-and-forget. The surrounding try/catch cannot catch their rejections, and the function proceeds to send the reschedule email and return true immediately. Consequence is orphaned events on external calendars/video providers on failure and unhandled promise rejections. Use Promise.all or for...of with await.

title: Async calendar/video deletions in forEach are never awaited
body: In packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts the code does bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...)/deleteMeeting(...); }). Array.forEach does not await async callbacks, so the deletions run fire-and-forget. The surrounding try/catch cannot catch their rejections, and the function proceeds to send the reschedule email and return true immediately. Consequence is orphaned events on external calendars/video providers on failure and unhandled promise rejections. Use Promise.all or for...of with await.

title: Reschedule deletions fired in forEach without awaiting
body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx requestReschedule does bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...)/deleteMeeting(...); }) and then immediately sends reschedule email and webhooks without awaiting. Because forEach never awaits the async callback, calendar/video deletions may not have started or finished, errors are lost as unhandled rejections, and the previous time slot may stay blocked. Collect promises and await Promise.all.

title: Recurring cancel pushes to apiDeletes from unawaited forEach
body: In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts recurring cancellation does bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); for (...) apiDeletes.push(await calendar?.deleteEvent(...)); }). The outer forEach is not awaited, but apiDeletes is later consumed by Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)). Because the pushes happen asynchronously after the await of getCalendar, Promise.all can run with an incomplete apiDeletes list, so some recurring calendar deletions are silently skipped and errors inside are uncaught. Use for...of with await or await Promise.all of mapped promises.

title: getCalendarCredentials now stores a Promise as calendar but stays sync
body: In packages/core/CalendarManager.ts getCalendarCredentials does const calendar = getCalendar(credential) after getCalendar became async, so calendar is Promise<Calendar|null>, not Calendar|null. The function remains synchronous and returns objects with a promise in the calendar field. Only getConnectedCalendars was patched to do await item.calendar. Any other consumer expecting a Calendar will get a Promise (e.g., calling listCalendars/createEvent on it fails), and the return type is now misleading. Make getCalendarCredentials async and resolve calendars before returning.

title: getVideoAdapters serializes independent dynamic imports
body: In packages/core/videoClient.ts getVideoAdapters loops for (const cred of withCredentials) { const app = await appStore[...]; ... } which awaits each dynamic import sequentially. The imports are independent, so latency adds up, notably for getBusyVideoTimes and availability paths with multiple video credentials. Use Promise.all to load adapters in parallel.

title: Dayjs objects compared with === never equal, full-day unavailable override ignored
body: In checkIfIsAvailable the code tests `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` to detect an unavailable-day override where start equals end. `===` on Dayjs objects compares object identity, never value equality, so it is always false. As a result a date override that should block the whole day sets dateOverrideExist but never matches the find, falls through to `if (dateOverrideExist) return true`, and the slot is reported as available when the host is unavailable, allowing bookings on blocked days.

title: Date-override hit returns available without checking busy times
body: After scanning dateOverrides, if any override covers the slot day the function does `if (dateOverrideExist) return true` immediately. That early return skips the later `busy.every(...)` calendar/booking check. On any day with a date override, existing Cal bookings, calendar busy blocks, and selected-slot holds for that fixed host are ignored, so double-bookings become possible on override days.

title: Working-hours end uses slot start, ignores event length
body: The working-hours guard computes both `start` and `end` as `slotStartTime.hour()*60+slotStartTime.minute()`. `end` should be slot end (start + eventLength). An event that starts inside working hours but ends after them, e.g. 60-min event starting 30 min before close, passes the `end > workingHour.endTime` test and is offered as bookable, causing bookings that overrun availability.

title: Working-hours outside check inverted for split days and empty days
body: The code uses `workingHours.find(h => slot outside h)` to decide the slot is outside working hours. If a user has two intervals in one day, e.g. morning and afternoon, a valid morning slot is outside the afternoon interval, so `find` succeeds and the valid slot is rejected. Conversely if no interval lists that weekday, `find` returns undefined and the code falls through to the busy check, treating a non-working day as available. Valid slots are hidden and invalid days can appear bookable.

title: Date-override timezone used without fallback and via toString round-trip
body: TimeRange.timeZone is optional, but getSlots does `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` with no guard. When timeZone is missing, tz gets undefined and produces an invalid/NaN offset or throws, breaking slot generation for legacy overrides. Even when present, `override.start.toString()` serializes the instant in server-local format and re-parses it before converting, which is locale-dependent and fragile compared to using the Date directly with a fallback to organizerTimeZone.

title: No test for round-robin fixed-host date overrides
body: The PR description claims it fixes date overrides of fixed hosts being ignored for round-robin events, which is implemented in the new checkIfIsAvailable filtering in viewer/slots.ts. The only test added covers the same UTC slots under a different invitee timezone for a single-user event. There is no scenario with a ROUND_ROBIN event, fixed vs loose hosts, and conflicting date overrides, so the main claimed fix and the new working-hours/date-override branches are untested and regressions would not be caught.

title: Dayjs equality uses === so full-day unavailable override never matches
body: In checkIfIsAvailable the code tests `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` to detect an unavailable-day override where start equals end. Dayjs instances are objects, so === compares identity and is always false. The branch never fires, dateOverrideExist stays true, and the function later returns true, so a day the host marked as fully unavailable becomes bookable.

title: Slots on date-override days return available without checking busy times
body: After detecting that a slot falls on a date-override day, checkIfIsAvailable does `if (dateOverrideExist) return true` before the busy-calendar check. That early return skips the `busy.every(...)` verification, so existing Cal bookings and external calendar blocks on override days are ignored and double-booking becomes possible.

title: Working-hours end uses start time so events overrunning closing time pass
body: In the working-hours fallback both `start` and `end` are computed from `slotStartTime.hour()*60+slotStartTime.minute()`. The end should be derived from slot end time (start + eventLength). As written an event that starts inside working hours but ends outside is still considered available, allowing bookings past closing time.

title: Outside-working-hours test uses find so split shifts reject valid slots
body: The code uses `workingHours.find` to look for any entry where the slot is outside that entry and then rejects the slot. With multiple intervals on the same weekday (e.g. morning and afternoon), a slot that fits the second interval still matches the outside condition of the first interval, so find succeeds and the valid slot is incorrectly rejected.

title: Override offset parses via toString and crashes when timeZone missing
body: The override conversion does `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)`. TimeRange.timeZone is optional and can be undefined, in which case tz() is invalid, and toString() round-trips through server locale strings losing millisecond/offset fidelity. This yields NaN or wrong utcOffset, shifting override start/end minutes and producing wrong slots or a runtime error.

title: Active overrides filtered only by start instant misses overlapping day
body: activeOverrides keeps an override only if `dayjs.utc(override.start)` falls inside the invitee day. An override that overlaps the day but starts on an adjacent day due to timezone shift or an evening interval spanning midnight is dropped, so the day falls back to regular working hours and shows wrong availability. The later hour/minute math also drops day overflow, assigning shifted times to the wrong day.

title: No test for round-robin fixed-host override or unavailable/busy override cases
body: The PR claims to fix fixed-host date overrides for round-robin events, but the only added test checks that a personal-event override returns the same UTC slots in two invitee timezones. There is no coverage for fixed vs loose hosts, for start==end unavailable days, or for busy bookings on override days, so the === bug and the early-return that skips busy checks are not caught.

title: Dayjs objects compared with === never match
body: At line 114 the code does `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` to detect a full-day unavailable date override. `===` on objects compares references, so two separately created Dayjs instances are never equal. The branch never runs, `dateOverrideExist` becomes true but `find` returns falsy, and the function falls through to `return true`. A day marked unavailable by a date override is therefore reported as available, including for fixed hosts in round-robin events, allowing bookings that should be blocked.

title: Working-hours check ignores duration and inverts multi-block logic
body: The `workingHours.find` check computes both `start` and `end` from `slotStartTime.hour()*60+minute`, ignoring `eventLength` and `slotEndTime`, so a slot that starts inside but ends outside working hours passes. It also returns true if ANY block does not contain the slot, instead of checking if NO block contains it. With two blocks on the same weekday (e.g. morning and afternoon) a valid slot inside one block is outside the other and is marked unavailable, while a weekday with no matching `days` entry returns falsy and is treated as available. Fixed hosts can appear available when they have no hours and unavailable when they have split hours.

title: Date-override containment misses end overrun and exact boundary
body: The override test only rejects a slot if `slotEndTime <= overrideStart` or `slotStartTime.isAfter(overrideEnd)`. It never checks `slotEndTime > overrideEnd`, and uses `isAfter` instead of same-or-after for the end. A slot starting inside the override but ending after it (e.g. override 10:00-11:00, slot 10:30-11:30) does not match either condition, `find` returns falsy, and with `dateOverrideExist=true` the function returns true. Bookings can extend beyond the override window, and a slot starting exactly at override end is also considered inside.

title: Date-override day match mixes local and UTC timezones
body: `utcOffset` is derived with `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset()*-1` then applied to `dayjs(date.start)` which is parsed in server-local time, while `slotStartTime` is `time.utc()`. Formatting both with `YYYY MM DD` compares a local-calendar day to a UTC-calendar day. Unless the server runs in UTC the day equality and the shifted start/end comparisons can be off by a day, causing overrides to apply to the wrong date or be ignored for organizers/invitees in other zones.

title: Offsets derived from Date.toString() parsing are fragile
body: Organizer and invitee offsets are computed as `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(zone).utcOffset()`. `Date.toString()` is locale and server-timezone dependent (e.g. includes local abbrev) and is not a stable input for dayjs parsing with a zone. It can parse incorrectly or yield Invalid Date/NaN, producing NaN start/end minutes and dropping all slots or shifting them. It should use `dayjs(override.start).tz(zone)` directly without stringifying.

title: Active override filtered by wall-encoded instant not true instant
body: The filter `dayjs.utc(override.start).isBetween(startOfInviteeDay, ...)` uses the stored override Date directly, but that Date encodes organizer wall time as UTC hours. The true UTC instant is wall minus organizer offset. Near midnight a wall time and its true instant fall on different invitee calendar days (e.g. true 23:30 UTC with +5:30 organizer becomes 05:00 wall next day). The override can then be attached to the wrong invitee day or missed entirely for invitees in distant timezones.

title: Availability check ignores variable duration
body: Slots are generated with `eventLength: input.duration || eventType.length` but `availabilityCheckProps` hard-codes `eventLength: eventType.length`. For event types with multiple duration options the `checkIfIsAvailable` busy/override/working-hours window uses the wrong length, so a longer selected duration can be reported as available when it overruns an override, working hours, or busy block, or vice versa.

title: Migration SQL injection and un-normalized hosts
body: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb line 25 the migration builds SQL with string interpolation: VALUES ('#{h}', ...). A host containing a quote breaks the migration, and admin-controlled input is not quoted. It also inserts the raw old setting value without stripping scheme/path, while EmbeddableHost strips scheme/path on validation and host_allowed? compares only URI.host. Migrated rows like 'http://discourse.org' or 'https://example.com/1234' will never match, so previously allowed embeds become blocked. Quote values and normalize with the same stripping logic.

title: Migration uses cmd_tuples for SELECT, skipping data
body: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb line 19 the code checks embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0 to decide if old hosts exist. For a SELECT, PG returns cmd_tuples 0 and row count in ntuples/ntuples. The condition is false even when rows exist, so no hosts are migrated, then line 31 deletes site_settings embeddable_hosts/embed_category. This silently loses all configured hosts. Use ntuples/any?/empty? check.

title: Migration crashes when settings missing
body: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb line 9 the code does execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i assuming a row exists for embed_category join and line 15 assumes uncategorized_category_id exists. On fresh installs or when embed_category does not match a category name, [0] is nil and nil['id'] raises NoMethodError, failing the whole migration. Guard empty results and default safely.

title: before_validation crashes on nil host
body: In app/models/embeddable_host.rb line 6 before_validation calls self.host.sub! twice without a nil guard. If host is nil (blank form, missing param, direct create), this raises NoMethodError instead of a validation error, turning user error into 500 in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#create/update. Guard with return if host blank and add presence validation.

title: No uniqueness validation or index on host
body: In app/models/embeddable_host.rb line 2 there is only format validation and no uniqueness validation, and the migration creates embeddable_hosts without a unique index. Admins can create duplicate host rows, making TopicEmbed.import category mapping ambiguous (record_for_host returns first) and host_allowed? nondeterministic. Add validates_uniqueness_of case-insensitive and a unique lower(host) index.

title: Host lookup case-sensitive and port-mismatched
body: In app/models/embeddable_host.rb line 17 record_for_host does where("lower(host) = ?", host) where host is URI.host as-is, not downcased, so an uppercase referer fails to match a stored lowercase host even though comparison lowercases only the column. Stored values may also include :port (validation allows it) while lookup compares only hostname without port, so hosts with ports never match. Downcase the input and normalize port handling consistently.

title: Update/destroy crash on missing record instead of 404
body: In app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb line 10 update does EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first then save_host(host) without nil check, so unknown id calls methods on nil and 500s. Same pattern in destroy at line 15 where host.destroy on nil 500s. Return 404 for missing records.

title: Plural embedded hydration crashes on null
body: In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6 line 197 _hydrateEmbedded does obj[k].map for keys matching *_ids without checking for null. If the payload contains a null ids array, this throws TypeError and breaks store.find/findAll hydration. Guard for non-array values and filter unresolvable ids instead of inserting undefined.

title: Edit loses category when hydration absent, save ignores server
body: In app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6 line 26 edit() reads host.category.id only. After store hydration, category_id is deleted and only category remains; if category failed to resolve, categoryId becomes undefined and saving overwrites the real category with blank (resetting to uncategorized). Line 38 then sets category from local Category.findById instead of the server response, so server-side defaulting to uncategorized is not reflected until reload. Fall back to category_id and apply server-returned values.

title: No coverage for embeddable-hosts CRUD
body: In spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb line 5 and the matching embedding_controller_spec, the only test is subclass-of-AdminController. There is no coverage for create/update/destroy auth, validation errors, missing-record 404s, category defaulting, or host normalization. Bugs in save_host nil handling and duplicate hosts can merge unnoticed. Add request specs for those paths.

title: Exposes unimplemented embeddable_hosts routes
body: In config/routes.rb line 153 resources :embeddable_hosts generates index/show/new/edit plus create/update/destroy, but Admin::EmbeddableHostsController only implements create/update/destroy. Extra routes 404 with ActionNotFound and widen the admin surface. Restrict to only: [:create, :update, :destroy].

title: Admin check replaces only first underscore
body: In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/adapters/rest.js.es6 line 22 basePath does type.replace('_','-') which replaces only the first underscore. Types with multiple underscores will not match ADMIN_MODELS and will use '/' instead of '/admin/', causing 404s. Use a global replace.

title: before_validation crashes on nil host
body: In app/models/embeddable_host.rb the before_validation block calls self.host.sub! twice without checking presence. If host is nil or missing (e.g. admin submits blank host), this raises NoMethodError on nil instead of failing validation. Consequence: POST/PUT to Admin::EmbeddableHostsController with blank host returns 500 instead of a 422 validation error and breaks the admin UI error path.

title: Update/destroy do not handle missing record
body: In app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb update does EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first then calls save_host(host), and destroy does the same lookup then host.destroy. If the id does not exist host is nil, so save_host(nil) calls nil.host= and nil.destroy raises NoMethodError. Consequence: requesting a non-existent id causes a 500 exception instead of a 404/not-found response.

title: Migration assumes site_settings rows exist
body: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb line 9 does execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name='embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i without nil checks. On a fresh install where embed_category was never persisted there are zero rows, so [0] is nil and ['id'] raises. Consequence: rake db:migrate fails for new databases.

title: Migration SQL-injects host value
body: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration builds INSERT with string interpolation: VALUES ('#{h}', ... ) where h comes from the old embeddable_hosts site setting split by newline. A host containing a single quote breaks the SQL and allows SQL injection/error. Consequence: migration can fail or execute unintended SQL; must use quoting/sanitization or ActiveRecord models.

title: Migration inserts unnormalized hosts that never match
body: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the loop inserts raw setting lines h directly, bypassing EmbeddableHost normalization that strips scheme and path. Old settings commonly contain values like http://discourse.org or https://example.com/1234, so the new table ends up with scheme/path included. EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares URI.host (bare hostname) to the stored string, so those migrated rows never match. Consequence: embedding silently stops working after upgrade.

title: Host lookup is case-sensitive and ignores port mismatch
body: In app/models/embeddable_host.rb record_for_host does where("lower(host) = ?", host) where host is uri.host as-is, without downcasing, so lower(stored) is compared to mixed-case input and uppercase URLs miss. Additionally validation allows host:port but lookup extracts uri.host without port, so a stored example.com:3000 never equals example.com. Consequence: legitimate embed URLs are rejected as invalid referer host.

title: _hydrateEmbedded crashes on null plural ids
body: In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6 _hydrateEmbedded for keys matching *_ids does obj[k].map(...) with no array guard. If the server serializes an empty association as null/undefined instead of [], this throws TypeError. Consequence: store.find/findAll for any model with a null plural id field crashes the client; should check Array.isArray or fallback to [].

title: Fabricator file contents are swapped
body: In spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb the file now defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host) while spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines Fabricator(:category) and related categories. The contents are in the wrong files. It still loads but is misleading and will confuse maintainers; the definitions should be moved back to their matching filenames.

title: No real coverage for new admin endpoints
body: In spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb and embedding_controller_spec.rb the only test is that the controller is a subclass of AdminController. There is no coverage for create/update/destroy validation, 404 handling, auth (admin vs moderator/anon), category fallback, or serialization. Consequence: regressions in the new embedding admin API, including the nil-handling and validation bugs above, will not be caught.

title: Migration interpolates host values into SQL
body: Line 25 builds INSERT with VALUES ('#{h}', ...) where h comes from the site_settings.embeddable_hosts value. A host containing a single quote breaks the statement or allows SQL injection. The migration will fail or corrupt data on such input. Use connection.quote / sanitize instead of string interpolation.

title: Migration crashes when embed settings are absent
body: Lines 9-16 do execute(...)[0]['id'] and [0]['value'] without checking for empty results. On a fresh install or when embed_category / uncategorized_category_id / embeddable_hosts rows are missing, [0] is nil and nil['id'] raises NoMethodError, failing the whole migration and blocking deploy. Guard for empty results and defaults.

title: Update/destroy crash on unknown id instead of 404
body: Update does EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first then save_host(host) which does host.host=, and destroy does host.destroy. If the id does not exist, host is nil and both actions raise NoMethodError resulting in a 500 instead of 404. Add not-found handling.

title: before_validation crashes on nil host
body: The callback calls self.host.sub! twice without guarding nil. Creating/updating with missing or nil host (e.g. blank form submit via Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host) raises NoMethodError before validation runs, turning a validation error into a 500. Guard with return if host.blank? or use to_s.

title: Host lookup is not case-insensitive despite lower()
body: record_for_host does where("lower(host) = ?", host) where host is uri.host without downcasing. Comparing lower(column) to a mixed-case value like Example.COM never matches, so EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? incorrectly returns false and valid embeds/referers are rejected. Downcase the parameter or compare lower(host)=lower(?).

title: Stored host with port can never match lookup
body: before_validation strips scheme and path but keeps :port, and the format validation allows (:port), so example.com:3000 can be saved. record_for_host uses URI(host).host which strips the port, then compares to the stored value including port, so such a record never matches and EmbedController/TopicRetriever always deny it. Either strip/normalize ports on save or include them in lookup, or disallow ports.

title: No uniqueness validation on host
body: EmbeddableHost only validates format, not uniqueness. Admins can create duplicate host rows with different categories. record_for_host then picks an arbitrary first row, making category assignment and allow-list ambiguous. Add case-insensitive uniqueness validation and a unique DB index.

title: Plural _ids hydration crashes on null
body: The new plural branch does obj[k].map(...) without checking that obj[k] is an array. If the server sends null or undefined for an *_ids field, this throws TypeError and breaks store.find/findAll hydration for that model, including the new embedding payload. Guard for null and filter missing lookups.

title: No coverage for new embedding admin endpoints
body: Both new controller specs only assert subclass of AdminController. There are no tests for create/update/destroy validation, blank host, unknown id 404, auth, or EmbeddingController#show. The nil-deref and validation bugs above are therefore undetected. Add request specs for success and error paths.

title: Fabricator file contents are swapped
body: spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb now defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host) and spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines Fabricator(:category) and related categories. The definitions are in the wrong files. It works only because all fabricators are loaded globally, but it is confusing and fragile. Swap the contents back so each file defines its namesake.

title: Duplicate downsize definition overwrites 4-arg version
body: File app/models/optimized_image.rb defines self.downsize twice: line 145 as (from,to,max_width,max_height,opts) and line 149 as (from,to,dimensions,opts). Ruby has no overloading, so the second definition replaces the first and the first becomes dead code. Any existing caller using the 4-argument form will bind max_width to dimensions and max_height to opts, so opts becomes an Integer and opts[:allow_animation] raises TypeError. The API contract for downsize is broken.

title: In-place downsize overwrites source file
body: In app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb line 67 the code calls OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...) using the same path for source and destination. If convert/gifsicle fails, is killed, or partially writes, the original upload is truncated or corrupted with no backup. A failing conversion destroys the only copy before Upload.create_for runs. Use a separate temp file and replace only on success.

title: Loop checks stale tempfile.size and ignores downsize failure
body: In app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb the while condition uses tempfile.size after an external ImageMagick/ImageOptim process rewrites the file at tempfile.path, and line 72 passes the same tempfile.size to Upload.create_for. An open Tempfile descriptor does not reliably reflect an external truncate/replace, so the loop can run all 5 iterations even after the file is already under SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, over-shrinking to 0.8^5 of dimensions, and the filesize stored in the database can mismatch the bytes on disk. The return value of OptimizedImage.downsize is also ignored, so 5 failing converts are spawned on corrupt input and a corrupt file can still be passed to Upload.create_for.

title: Hardcoded 10MB client limit ignores image vs attachment settings
body: In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js validateUploadedFile replaced Discourse.SiteSettings['max_'+type+'_size_kb'] with hardcoded 10*1024. The server only downsizes images, not attachments, so attachments larger than max_attachment_size_kb but under 10MB now pass client validation only to fail server-side, and images are blocked at 10MB even if the admin raised max_image_size_kb above 10MB. The same hardcoding at line 246 for 413 errors shows users the wrong max_size_kb.

title: Extension-only image check sends SVG and spoofed files to convert
body: In app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb line 64 gating uses FileHelper.is_image?(filename), which checks the filename extension. Large SVG vectors will therefore be sent to convert -resize 80%, rasterizing/flattening a vector format that OptimizedImage.create_for explicitly avoids converting by copying. Conversely a large non-image renamed to .jpg triggers up to 5 ImageMagick processes, wasting CPU. Content/type validation and an SVG exclusion are needed.

title: Hardcoded 10MB client limit ignores per-type site settings
body: In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js line 182, validateUploadedFile now uses hardcoded `10*1024` instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_'+type+'_size_kb']`. The old code used max_image_size_kb for images and max_attachment_size_kb for attachments. Now both types are limited to 10MB: sites allowing e.g. 50MB attachments will incorrectly reject them client-side, and sites with e.g. 1-2MB limits will incorrectly allow them client-side only to fail later on the server with a confusing message showing 10240.

title: 413 error handler shows wrong hardcoded limit
body: In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js line 246, the 413 handler now reports hardcoded `10*1024` instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`. The displayed max_size_kb will be wrong whenever the admin configured a different limit, misleading users about why the upload was rejected.

title: API URL download limit hardcoded to 10MB bypasses admin setting
body: In app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb line 55, FileHelper.download limit was changed from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to hardcoded `10.megabytes`. If admin sets a smaller limit the server still fetches/downloads/processes up to 10MB (extra bandwidth/disk/CPU and policy bypass), and if admin allows larger than 10MB the download is needlessly truncated/failed.

title: In-place image downsize corrupts tempfile and uses stale size
body: In app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb line 67, `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` uses the same path for input and output. External `convert from[0] ... to` can truncate/replace the output before reading finishes, corrupting the upload. After the external rewrite the open Tempfile descriptor may still point at the old inode while `tempfile.size` is stale, so the `while tempfile.size > limit` check and final `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile.size)` can use wrong size/bytes. Return value is also ignored, so on convert failure it loops 5 times doing expensive convert+ImageOptim work then fails late. Use a separate temp file, check success, and stat `File.size(path)`.

title: Large SVG uploads sent through ImageMagick rasterizer
body: In app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb line 64, the auto-downsize guard is true for any `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` including `.svg`, and then runs `OptimizedImage.downsize` via `convert -resize`. Elsewhere in app/models/optimized_image.rb lines 45-47 SVGs are explicitly excluded from ImageMagick (just copied) because convert rasterizes them. A large SVG over the limit will therefore be mangled/converted instead of preserved or rejected; SVGs should be skipped in the downsize loop.

title: Duplicate downsize definition removes 4-arg overload
body: In app/models/optimized_image.rb lines 145 and 149 there are two `self.downsize` definitions: one taking `(from,to,max_width,max_height,opts)` and one taking `(from,to,dimensions,opts)`. In Ruby the last definition wins, so the 4-arg version is dead code. Any existing caller using `downsize(from,to,width,height)` now raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments). Keep one method supporting both arities or different names.

title: Duplicate downsize definition deletes 4-arg API
body: The file now defines self.downsize twice: once as downsize(from,to,max_width,max_height,opts) and immediately again as downsize(from,to,dimensions,opts). Ruby has no overloading, so the second definition overwrites the first and the first becomes dead code. Any existing caller using the width/height pair form will get ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments) after this merge. Only the new percent-string form works.

title: In-place downsize overwrites source file
body: create_upload calls OptimizedImage.downsize with tempfile.path as both source and destination. ImageMagick convert reading and writing the same path is unsafe, and if conversion fails the original upload bytes are already truncated or destroyed. Upload.create_for then stores the corrupt/truncated file, causing permanent data loss for that upload. A separate temp output file that is only moved into place on success is required.

title: Loop ignores downsize failure and checks stale size
body: The while loop checks tempfile.size on the open File handle while the external convert command rewrites the file via its path, so the observed size can stay stale if the converter replaces the inode, and the boolean return value of downsize is never checked. The loop therefore can run all 5 iterations even when the first pass already brought the file under the limit or when conversion keeps failing, shrinking images to about 0.8^5 of dimensions unnecessarily, wasting 5 ImageMagick runs, and passing a stale size to Upload.create_for.

title: Animated GIFs stripped and SVGs rasterized by downsize
body: The downsize gate fires for any filename where FileHelper.is_image? is true, including .gif and .svg, with no special case. Animation selection in OptimizedImage.optimize checks the source path for /.GIF$/i, but here the source is tempfile.path which is a generated RackMultipart or download name without the original extension, so it never matches. The fallback ImageMagick command uses from[0] which keeps only the first frame, silently destroying animation even when allow_animated_thumbnails is true. SVGs which are copied verbatim elsewhere are sent through convert and rasterized. The animated branch also delegates to gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH, not the passed 80% string.

title: Hardcoded 10MB client limit breaks per-type site settings
body: validateUploadedFile replaced Discourse.SiteSettings['max_'+type+'_size_kb'] with a fixed 10*1024 for both images and attachments, and the 413 handler similarly hardcodes max_image_size_kb. Sites with max_attachment_size_kb different from 10MB now validate attachments incorrectly, either allowing files the server will reject or rejecting files the server would allow, and sites with max_image_size_kb larger than 10MB incorrectly reject images on the client.

title: URL download cap ignores larger configured image limit
body: FileHelper.download for API URL uploads was changed from SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes to a fixed 10.megabytes. On sites where the administrator configured max_image_size_kb larger than 10MB, remote URL uploads between 10MB and the configured limit will now fail or be truncated even though they are allowed. The limit should be the maximum of the configured setting and the auto-downsize allowance.

title: Unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when TopicUser row is missing
body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107, TopicsController#unsubscribe does TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) and then immediately reads tu.notification_level. find_by returns nil when the user has no TopicUser row for that topic, which is common for email recipients who never visited the topic, were emailed via mailing-list mode, or were invited. Dereferencing nil raises NoMethodError and returns 500, so clicking the email unsubscribe link crashes instead of unsubscribing. The code must handle nil via TopicUser.change or find-or-create.

title: State-changing unsubscribe via GET enables CSRF and prefetch unsubscribes
body: In config/routes.rb:440, the per-topic unsubscribe URL is a GET that maps to TopicsController#unsubscribe, which mutates TopicUser.notification_level on every hit. GET requests have no CSRF token protection and are automatically fetched by browsers, email link prefetchers, antivirus scanners, and crawlers. An attacker can force a logged-in victim to downgrade/mute arbitrary topics with an tag, and legitimate users can be unsubscribed without ever clicking. Mutations must use POST/PUT with authenticity-token protection plus explicit user confirmation.

title: Email unsubscribe link requires login so logged-out recipients cannot use it
body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:28, :unsubscribe is added to ensure_logged_in. Email recipients normally open links without an active Discourse session, so they are redirected to the login page and the TopicUser mutation never runs, and after login they are not replayed through the mutation. The email copy promising 'click here to stop receiving notifications about this particular topic' therefore does nothing for logged-out users. Email unsubscribe needs a signed single-use token usable without a session, like DigestUnsubscribeKey.

title: Direct save bypasses notification-level bookkeeping and live updates
body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:113, the action assigns tu.notification_level directly and calls tu.save! instead of using TopicUser.change. That bypasses setting notifications_changed_at and notifications_reason_id and bypasses the MessageBus publish of notification_level_change that TopicUser.change performs. As a result open topic pages keep stale notification state, tracking-state observers are not run, and audit fields are wrong. The action should use TopicUser.change with an appropriate reason.

title: Client-side unsubscribe route never calls server unsubscribe action
body: In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:6, the Ember model hook loads the topic with PostStream.loadTopicView, which hits the normal topic show API, not TopicsController#unsubscribe. A full page load to /t/slug/id/unsubscribe hits Rails and auto-downgrades the level, but an in-app transition to the same URL only runs this hook and never mutates, while the template still says the user will stop receiving notifications. Behavior depends on navigation path and the displayed text can be false.

title: New unsubscribe_link translation breaks callers without unsubscribe_url
body: In lib/email/message_builder.rb:90, email bodies append I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args). The PR changed server.en.yml unsubscribe_link to require both %{user_preferences_url} and a new %{unsubscribe_url}, but MessageBuilder only supplies user_preferences_url by default; unsubscribe_url is present only if the caller passes it. Any existing caller, plugin, or test that sets add_unsubscribe_link:true without unsubscribe_url now raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and fails to deliver mail, where it previously succeeded. The template needs a default or separate handling when unsubscribe_url is absent.

title: Unsubscribe crashes when TopicUser row is missing
body: In TopicsController#unsubscribe the code does TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) then immediately calls tu.notification_level. find_by returns nil when the user has no row for the topic, for example a user who was @mentioned or mailed but never visited. That raises NoMethodError on nil and returns 500 instead of unsubscribing. It must handle nil via TopicUser.change or find-or-create.

title: State-changing unsubscribe on GET enables CSRF/prefetch unsubscribe
body: TopicsController#unsubscribe is routed as GET in config/routes.rb but mutates notification_level and saves. Browsers, email link scanners, and crawlers prefetch GETs, and an attacker can embed the URL as an image to force a logged-in victim's browser to unsubscribe with no CSRF token. Safe methods must not mutate; GET should render confirmation and mutation should require POST/PUT.

title: Per-topic email link requires login so logged-out clicks fail
body: TopicsController#unsubscribe is in the ensure_logged_in list, yet the URL is mailed as a one-click unsubscribe link. A recipient who clicks while logged out, on another device, or after session expiry is redirected to login and never unsubscribed. The existing global unsubscribe uses email/unsubscribe/:key token auth for this reason; the per-topic link needs token auth or it is dead on arrival for logged-out users.

title: Watching/tracking users are only downgraded, not unsubscribed
body: The code sets notification_level to regular when it is greater than regular, else to muted. A watching (3) or tracking (2) user who clicks the email promise to stop receiving notifications about this topic is left at regular (1), which still generates reply/mention/watch emails. It takes a second visit to reach muted. It should set muted directly for an email unsubscribe.

title: Direct TopicUser save bypasses reason, timestamp and live update
body: The action assigns tu.notification_level and calls tu.save! instead of TopicUser.change used by set_notifications. That skips setting notifications_changed_at, notifications_reason_id, and publishing MessageBus notification_level_change. The result is stale audit fields and open topic pages/tracking state that do not update live, diverging from all other notification-level changes.

title: List-Unsubscribe header not updated to per-topic URL
body: The email body now includes a per-topic unsubscribe_url, but header_args still sets List-Unsubscribe to only user_preferences_url even when unsubscribe_url is present. Email clients that use the header for one-click unsubscribe will send the user to generic preferences instead of unsubscribing from the topic, making header and body inconsistent and defeating the feature for those clients.

title: No test verifies per-topic unsubscribe URL or controller behavior
body: The spec adds unsubscribe_url to the builder fixture but only asserts the generic user_preferences_url in the body and presence of the header. Nothing asserts the body/header contain the per-topic unsubscribe_url, and there is no controller test for TopicsController#unsubscribe covering missing TopicUser, downgrade-vs-mute, login/token, or GET side effects, so the bugs above ship undetected.

title: Unsubscribe crashes when TopicUser row is missing
body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb line 105-107, `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)` can return nil (e.g. category watcher, first notification, never visited topic) and the next line does `tu.notification_level` with no nil guard. This raises NoMethodError and returns 500 instead of unsubscribing. Should use TopicUser.change/get-or-create with muted level.

title: State-changing unsubscribe on GET enables CSRF/prefetch mutation
body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb line 98, `TopicsController#unsubscribe` is routed as GET (config/routes.rb) and immediately mutates `tu.notification_level` and `tu.save!`. Visiting, prefetching, crawling or CSRF-loading the email link changes notification state without confirmation or POST/CSRF token. GET must be idempotent; mutation should require POST/PUT.

title: Email unsubscribe requires login with no token, fails logged-out
body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb line 28, `:unsubscribe` is in `ensure_logged_in`, and `Topic#unsubscribe_url` contains only `/t/slug/id/unsubscribe` with no key. Email links are typically opened logged-out or on another device, so clicking the per-topic link forces a login redirect and loses the intent instead of unsubscribing. Needs a signed/token auth like digest unsubscribe.

title: Unsubscribe downgrades watchers to regular instead of muting
body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb lines 107-111, if `notification_level > regular` it sets to `regular`, otherwise to `muted`. A watching/tracking user clicking 'stop receiving notifications' stays at regular and still gets reply/mention emails, contradicting the email copy 'To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here' and the page copy 'You will stop receiving notifications'. Should set muted unconditionally.

title: Direct save bypasses TopicUser side-effects
