body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb line 113, `tu.notification_level=` + `tu.save!` bypasses `TopicUser.change` which sets `notifications_changed_at`, `notifications_reason_id`, publishes MessageBus `notification_level_change` and updates tracking state. Consequence is stale UI, missing audit reason and inconsistent timestamps. Should call TopicUser.change.

title: New unsubscribe_link requires unsubscribe_url, breaks emails missing it
body: In lib/email/message_builder.rb lines 67 and 90, `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}` (config/locales/server.en.yml). If any caller sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url`, I18n raises MissingInterpolationArgument and email delivery fails. Only `send_notification_email` was updated; other present/future paths and queued jobs are fragile. Make interpolation optional or default.

title: Assumes post.topic exists and offers mute for PMs
body: In app/mailers/user_notifications.rb line 295, `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url` assumes `post.topic` is non-nil and meaningful. If topic is deleted/nil it raises NoMethodError in the mail job, and for private messages muting does not stop PM emails, so the link is misleading. Needs nil guard and PM handling.

title: afterModel assumes details exists and ignores load failures
body: In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6 lines 6 and 14, `PostStream.loadTopicView` promise has no catch, and `afterModel` does `topic.set('details.notificationReasonText', null)` without checking `details`. If topic is invisible/deleted or has no details, this throws or leaves a blank page with unhandled rejection instead of 404/login. Needs guard and error handling.

title: No coverage for per-topic unsubscribe behavior
body: In spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb lines 169-180, the test adds `unsubscribe_url` param but never asserts it appears in body/HTML or in List-Unsubscribe, and there are no controller specs for TopicsController#unsubscribe (nil TopicUser, auth, GET side-effect, regular vs muted). The new feature can regress undetected.

title: Validator performs DB write causing double-counted block stats
body: EmailValidator#validate_each calls BlockedEmail.should_block?, which increments match_count and saves the BlockedEmail record. UsersController#create calls user.valid? and then user.save, each of which runs validations, so one signup attempt updates stats twice. Validation must be side-effect free; the result is inflated match_count, misleading last_match_at, and extra writes on the validation path.

title: Non-atomic match_count increment loses updates
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? does record.match_count += 1 followed by record.save, a read-modify-write sequence. Concurrent signup attempts matching the same blocked email can read the same value and overwrite each other, losing counts. Use an atomic operation such as increment_counter or update_counters.

title: Case-sensitive blocked email lookup allows bypass
body: BlockedEmail.where(email: email) does an exact case-sensitive match, while email addresses are case-insensitive and the codebase normalizes with Email.downcase elsewhere. An address blocked as bad@spammers.org can be reused as BAD@spammers.org and should_block? will miss it. Uniqueness validation is also case-sensitive. Normalize emails to downcased stripped form on write and on lookup.

title: Wrong Ember dependent key prevents rejected email UI update
body: emailValidation depends on rejectedEmails.@each, but rejectedEmails is an array of primitive strings updated with pushObject. Ember requires rejectedEmails.[] to observe membership changes; bare @each observes properties of members, not addition of strings. After the server rejects an email, emailValidation does not recompute, so the field still shows as valid until the user edits the email.

title: Moved whitelist/blacklist logic has no coverage
body: The whitelist/blacklist domain logic was moved from User to EmailValidator, but the new spec only tests the blocked-email branch with BlockedEmail.should_block? stubbed. There is no test that email_domains_whitelist or email_domains_blacklist still accept or reject correctly, so a regression in the moved code would go unnoticed.

title: Email validation mutates DB causing double-counted block stats
body: EmailValidator.validate_each calls BlockedEmail.should_block?, which increments match_count, updates last_match_at and saves. Validation is supposed to be side-effect free. UsersController#create calls user.valid? and then user.save, each of which runs validations, so a single blocked signup attempt increments the counter twice. Any other call to valid? (admin UI, console, tests) also mutates stats even if the user is never saved. Consequence is inflated match_count and misleading last_match_at, making abuse metrics unreliable.

title: Non-atomic match_count increment loses concurrent updates
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? does read-modify-write: record.match_count += 1 followed by record.save. Concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked email can interleave reads and overwrite each other, losing increments. The save also runs full validations including an extra uniqueness SELECT. Consequence is lost counts under load and wasted queries. Should use an atomic increment such as increment_counter or update_counters that bypasses validations.

title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive allowing bypass
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? looks up with BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first using the raw user-supplied string with no downcasing or stripping, and the model validates uniqueness case-sensitively. Email delivery treats addresses case-insensitively in practice and users can add case changes or whitespace. An attacker blocked as bad@spam.com can sign up as BAD@spam.com or Bad@spam.com and miss the block, and admins can create logically duplicate block entries. Should normalize emails on save and lookup, e.g. with Email.downcase and strip.

title: change_email action bypasses blocked-email check
body: UsersController#change_email lowercases the new address, checks only whether another User already owns it, then creates an EmailToken and enqueues authorization without ever running EmailValidator or checking BlockedEmail.should_block?. An address rejected at signup as blocked can therefore still be adopted by an existing account via the email-change flow. Consequence is the blocklist is ineffective after account creation. The new address should be validated the same way as signup.

title: Wrong Ember dependent key prevents rejected-email UI update
body: emailValidation is declared dependent on accountEmail and rejectedEmails.@each. In Ember, @each observes properties of array items, not array membership; pushing a string with pushObject does not invalidate the computed property. The correct key is rejectedEmails.[] or length. After the server rejects an email and it is pushed into rejectedEmails, the validation still returns ok and submitDisabled stays false until the user edits the email, so the user can immediately resubmit the same blocked email repeatedly.

title: Shared mutable rejectedEmails array on prototype
body: CreateAccountController is extended with rejectedEmails: Em.A([]) as a prototype property. That single array instance is shared by all instances of the controller. Pushes of server-rejected emails leak across modal instances and persist after close/reopen, causing stale addresses to be treated as rejected for future unrelated signups. Mutable defaults should be created per-instance in init or reset when the modal opens.

title: Domain whitelist regex not anchored allows subdomain spoof
body: email_in_restriction_setting? builds Regexp.new("@(domains)") with no end anchor and matches by substring. A whitelist entry like example.com therefore matches user@example.com.evil.com because the string contains @example.com, even though the real domain is evil.com. The whitelisted user passes validation incorrectly. Similarly a blacklist can over-match. The regex should be anchored to the end of the address and handle domain boundaries correctly.

title: Validator with DB write double-counts block hits
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? increments match_count and saves the record every time it is called, and EmailValidator calls it from validate_each. UsersController#create calls user.valid? and then user.save, which runs validations a second time. A single signup attempt therefore increments match_count twice and updates last_match_at twice. Any other valid? check also pollutes statistics. Validation must be read-only; counting should be done once outside validation.

title: Case-sensitive exact block lookup is bypassable
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? does BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first with the raw submitted value, with no downcasing or stripping. Blocked entry bad@spam.com will not match BAD@SPAM.COM, Bad@spam.com, or ' bad@spam.com '. An attacker blocked under one spelling can register by changing case or adding whitespace. Lookup and storage must be normalized the same way User emails are normalized with Email.downcase/strip.

title: Non-atomic match_count increment loses updates
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? does record.match_count += 1 followed by record.save. Under concurrent signups with the same blocked email two processes read the same count, increment, and save, so one increment is lost and last_match_at can be clobbered. It also runs full validations and callbacks for a counter update. Use an atomic counter update such as increment_counter/update_counters instead of read-modify-write.

title: Domain whitelist/blacklist regex not anchored allows bypass
body: email_in_restriction_setting? builds Regexp.new("@(#{domains})", true) with no end anchor and only dots escaped. A whitelist of example.com therefore matches user@example.com.evil.com because the pattern matches the substring @example.com. The same flaw causes blacklist false positives/negatives and lets an attacker pass a whitelist with a subdomain-suffix address. Anchor the domain to end of string and properly escape/parse the setting.

title: change_email bypasses blocked-email validation
body: UsersController#change_email downcases the new address, checks only whether it is already taken, then creates an email_token and sends an authorization email. It never checks SiteSetting email_domains_whitelist/blacklist or BlockedEmail.should_block?. A blocked address rejected at signup can therefore be adopted via the email-change flow, defeating the new block.

title: Wrong dependent key prevents rejected-email UI update
body: emailValidation is declared .property('accountEmail', 'rejectedEmails.@each') but rejectedEmails is an array of strings updated with pushObject. In Ember, pushObject notifies '[]', not '@each', which only observes properties on array items. After the server rejects an email the computed property does not recompute, so the inline invalid message is not shown and submitDisabled is not updated until the user edits the email field. The dependent key should be rejectedEmails.[].

title: Unrestricted cook_method allows raw HTML injection
body: lib/post_creator.rb:216 copies opts[:cook_method] onto the post without any permission check. Combined with Post#cook returning raw un-sanitized HTML when cook_method is raw_html, any caller that can reach PostCreator with user-controlled opts can create a post that bypasses Markdown cooking and HTML sanitization, resulting in persistent stored XSS executed for all viewers of the topic.

title: raw_html cook mode returns unsanitized raw
body: app/models/post.rb:133 returns raw directly when cook_method is raw_html, skipping PrettyText cooking, sanitization and Plugin::Filter. TopicEmbed.import uses this mode for untrusted RSS/Readability HTML and embed views render it with raw post.cooked, so an attacker controlling a feed or embedded page can inject script, iframe, javascript: URLs and event handlers that execute in Discourse and embed contexts.

title: Embed import stores unsanitized external HTML and mutates input
body: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 appends an imported_from footer via contents <<, mutating the caller's string so reusing the same object appends multiple footers and changes SHA on every call, and interpolates url directly into <a href='...'> without escaping. The resulting string is absolutized only for leading-slash href/src and stored as raw_html with no sanitization of script tags, javascript: URLs or event attributes, giving stored XSS from RSS/remote content.

title: Referer injected into JS and used as postMessage targetOrigin
body: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 embeds request.referer, which is attacker-controlled HTTP header data, directly into a script as parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>'). postMessage requires an origin (scheme+host+port), not a full URL with path/query, so this throws or mis-delivers the resize message. It also relies on HTML-escaping inside raw script text, which is the wrong context for JS string encoding.

title: postMessage origin check uses reversed substring test
body: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 tests discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1 instead of comparing origins for equality. This accepts any e.origin that happens to be a substring of discourseUrl (for example empty string) and rejects valid cases where formatting differs (trailing slash, port). An attacker frame can then drive iframe resizing or future message handling.

title: open(feed_url) allows command execution and SSRF
body: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) via Kernel#open/open-uri with no validation, timeout, size limit or redirect control. A value starting with | executes a shell command in Ruby, and any http URL causes server-side request forgery to internal hosts, with the job hanging on slow remotes.

title: Feed item with missing content crashes entire poll
body: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 does CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) assuming every RSS/Atom item has non-nil content. Items with only description/summary or nil content raise NoMethodError, aborting the loop so no later items are imported and the hourly job fails.

title: import_remote fetches arbitrary URL without safeguards
body: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 does open(url).read without requiring open-uri in this file, without timeout, size limit, redirect/host allowlist or rescue. It enables SSRF to internal services, memory exhaustion on large pages, unhandled network/Readability exceptions that fail RetrieveTopic jobs, and on hosts without open-uri loaded it tries to open a local file path instead of HTTP.

title: Incorrect success check and race on unique embed_url
body: app/models/topic_embed.rb:24 tests if post.present? after PostCreator, but PostCreator returns an unsaved post object with errors on failure, so TopicEmbed.create! can run with nil topic_id/post_id. Concurrent imports for the same URL both see embed.blank? and both create topics, then the second unique index on embed_url raises RecordNotUnique with no handling, leaving duplicate topics.

title: Non-atomic throttle leaves permanent Redis key
body: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27-28 uses $redis.setnx followed by separate $redis.expire to throttle to once per 60s. If the process crashes between the two calls the key never expires and that embed_url is throttled forever. The key also embeds the raw user-controlled URL with no normalization or length bound, allowing Redis bloat by requesting many unique URLs.

title: Missing embed_by_username crashes retriever
body: lib/topic_retriever.rb:49 calls SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase without checking presence. If the admin has not configured embed_by_username, this raises NoMethodError on nil, failing every RetrieveTopic job instead of bailing out cleanly as PollFeed does.

title: Spec expects TopicRetriever but controller enqueues job
body: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:43 expects TopicRetriever.new/retrieve when no embed is found, but app/controllers/embed_controller.rb enqueues Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic). The test does not match the implementation so it will fail or pass for the wrong reason and provides no coverage for the actual async path, referer validation, or error cases.

title: Adding column with default locks posts table
body: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 adds posts.cook_method with default 1 NOT NULL. On Postgres versions of this era this rewrites the entire large posts table and takes an exclusive lock, causing long downtime on production forums. It should add nullable without default, backfill, then set default/not-null.

title: Stored XSS via unescaped URL and unsanitized raw_html
body: In app/models/topic_embed.rb line 13, TopicEmbed.import interpolates the attacker-controlled url directly into HTML: "#{url}" with only a /^https?:\/\// prefix check. A URL like http://embeddable_host/'> passes the check and has the allowed host, so TopicRetriever will accept it. The resulting HTML is stored as a Post with cook_method raw_html (line 22) which bypasses all cooking/sanitization in Post#cook, and rendered with raw post.cooked in app/views/embed/best.html.erb line 19. Consequence is persistent stored XSS executed in browsers viewing the embed or topic.

title: Nil feed content crashes entire poll
body: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb line 35, poll_feed does CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub). RSS 2.0 items often have no content element (only description/title) and SimpleRSS returns nil for i.content. Calling scrub on nil raises NoMethodError with no rescue, aborting the loop. Consequence is one legacy item prevents all feed items from being imported/updated and fails the hourly scheduled job.

title: Unsafe open of feed URL with no error handling
body: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb line 29, code does SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) using Kernel#open/open-uri on an admin setting with no URI validation, timeout, or rescue. It allows file:// or pipe arguments in older Ruby, follows redirects arbitrarily (SSRF), and any network/DNS/parse error raises out of the scheduled job. Consequence is job failure, Sidekiq noise, and potential local-file read or internal-network fetch.

title: import_remote uses open without require or rescue
body: In app/models/topic_embed.rb line 48, import_remote does open(url).read without requiring open-uri in that file and without begin/rescue/timeout/validation. If open-uri was not already loaded it does local file open, and any 404/timeout/invalid URL raises. Called from TopicRetriever.fetch_http and Disqus import, the exception bubbles and fails the RetrieveTopic job. Consequence is embed retrieval never completes and repeated retries on every embed view.

title: Mutates caller string with <<
body: In app/models/topic_embed.rb line 13, import does contents << "\n<hr>..." which mutates the caller's String in place instead of duping. If the caller reuses the string it gets a second footer on retry, and frozen strings raise RuntimeError. Consequence is duplicated imported-from footers, surprising side effects, and crashes with frozen literals.

title: No handling for missing/deleted embed post
body: In app/models/topic_embed.rb line 32, the update path does post = embed.post then PostRevisor.new(post).revise! with no nil check. If the post/topic was deleted, trashed, or never created due to failed PostCreator, post is nil and revise! raises NoMethodError. There is also no check that revise! succeeded before embed.update_column(:content_sha1). Consequence is poll/retrieve jobs crash mid-loop and sha can diverge from actual post content.

title: downcase on possibly nil embed_by_username
body: In lib/topic_retriever.rb line 49, fetch_http does SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase with no blank check. If the setting is nil (default/unset in tests and fresh installs) this raises NoMethodError. Unlike PollFeed#execute which guards present?, every embed retrieval via RetrieveTopic hits this. Consequence is all embed fetches raise instead of no-op until admin configures the user.

title: Non-atomic throttle with raw URL as Redis key
body: In lib/topic_retriever.rb line 27, retrieved_recently? does $redis.setnx(key,1) then separate $redis.expire(key,60). If the process crashes between calls the key never expires and that embed_url is throttled forever. The key is "retrieved:#{@embed_url}" using unbounded user input, allowing huge keys and memory abuse. Consequence is permanent denial of retrieval for a URL and Redis bloat; should use SET NX EX atomically and hash the URL.

title: postMessage origin check is reversed
body: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js line 17, the check is discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)===-1, i.e. does discourseUrl contain e.origin, instead of checking e.origin equals the Discourse origin. Any origin that is a prefix/substring passes, e.g. discourseUrl http://example.com contains attacker origin http://example.co. Consequence is a malicious page can send discourse-resize messages to control iframe height, and the pattern invites broader message forgery if more types are added.

title: postMessage targetOrigin uses full referer
body: In app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb line 11, code calls parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>') where request.referer is the full URL including path/query, not an origin. The postMessage spec requires scheme+host+port; passing a full URL means the message is never delivered (or throws). When referer is nil it passes empty string which throws. Consequence is embed auto-resize is broken and relies on attacker-controlled header for security boundary.

title: absolutize_urls raises on malformed URL
body: In app/models/topic_embed.rb line 57, absolutize_urls does URI(url) with no rescue. Any malformed embed_url or feed link raises URI::InvalidURIError and aborts import/revise and the calling job. It also only handles href/src starting with / and mishandles protocol-relative //host/path, leaving broken or wrong absolute URLs. Consequence is single bad URL fails feed poll or embed retrieval.

title: Disqus replies pass ignored cooked param
body: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor line 160, the importer builds attrs with raw: p[:cooked], cooked: p[:cooked]. PostCreator.setup_post only reads raw and computes cooked via Post#cook; the cooked key is ignored. First post is created as raw_html via TopicEmbed.import_remote but replies are created as regular markdown posts containing raw HTML. Consequence is Disqus HTML is escaped/sanitized inconsistently, breaking formatting and losing intended rendering.

title: Spec mocks TopicRetriever but controller enqueues job
body: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb line 40, the test expects TopicRetriever.new/retrieve directly, while app/controllers/embed_controller.rb line 15 does Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic,...). If test jobs run inline the mock may accidentally pass, otherwise it fails, and in production the async path with user_id/embed_url args, throttling, and host validation is never asserted. Consequence is the real enqueue contract is untested and regressions will not be caught.

title: Unescaped embed URL stored as raw HTML enables stored XSS
body: In app/models/topic_embed.rb line 13 the embed URL is interpolated directly into HTML "#{url}" without escaping. Validation is only url =~ /^https?\:\/\// which only checks the prefix, so a URL like http://example.com/' onmouseover='alert(1) passes. The result is saved with cook_method raw_html and later rendered with raw post.cooked in embed/best.html.erb, so an attacker who controls a feed link or embed URL gets persistent script execution in the embed iframe and topic page.

title: Unescaped request.referer in postMessage allows XSS and breaks resize
body: In app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb line 11 request.referer is interpolated directly into a single-quoted JS string for parent.postMessage. Referer is attacker-controlled via the parent page URL and is not JS-escaped, so a value containing ' or </script> breaks out to execute script. Additionally the second argument to postMessage must be an origin (scheme+host+port) but a full referer URL with path is passed, so browsers reject it and auto-resize never works.

title: Nil feed item content crashes polling job
body: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb line 35 the code does CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) without checking for nil. RSS/Atom items are not required to have content, and SimpleRSS returns nil for missing fields. A single item without content raises NoMethodError, aborting the whole hourly poll so no feed items are imported.

title: Missing guard on embed_by_username crashes retrieve
body: In lib/topic_retriever.rb line 49 fetch_http does SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase without checking presence. If the setting is blank, nil.downcase raises NoMethodError. Unlike Jobs::PollFeed#execute which guards with present?, every RetrieveTopic job and every embed page miss will crash when the forum has not configured the username.

title: Inverted substring origin check for postMessage
body: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js line 17 the check is discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1. This tests whether the expected URL contains the message origin as a substring instead of testing equality of origins. Any origin that happens to appear as a substring of discourseUrl is accepted, and the logic is backwards from the safe pattern of comparing e.origin to the expected origin, allowing crafted messages to resize the iframe.

title: Check-then-create race violates unique embed_url index
body: In app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 20-28 import does TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first and if blank creates a topic then TopicEmbed.create!. Two concurrent RetrieveTopic jobs for the same URL can both see blank and both insert, so the second hits the unique index on topic_embeds.embed_url and raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, failing the job and potentially leaving a duplicate orphan topic.

title: Non-atomic throttle with setnx+expire can stick forever
body: In lib/topic_retriever.rb lines 27-29 throttling does $redis.setnx then $redis.expire as two separate commands. If the process crashes between them the key is left without a TTL, so that embed_url is throttled forever and never re-fetched. The key also embeds the raw URL unbounded, and should use an atomic SET with NX+EX and a hashed key.

title: Every cache miss triggers full feed poll enabling DoS
body: In lib/topic_retriever.rb line 41 perform_retrieve calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) which fetches and imports the entire RSS feed on every missing embed. Throttling is per-URL (retrieved:#{@embed_url}), so an attacker requesting many distinct paths on the embeddable host bypasses it and forces the server to repeatedly download and process the whole feed, causing load and slow embed responses.

title: Spec tests TopicRetriever path that controller never uses
body: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb the test expects TopicRetriever.new and retrieve when no embed is found, but app/controllers/embed_controller.rb enqueues Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic,...) and never calls TopicRetriever directly. The test therefore does not verify real behavior, will fail against the implementation, and leaves the async job enqueue path untested.

title: Disqus import loses original dates and adds remote fetch
body: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor line 148 the import was changed from PostCreator with created_at from the Disqus export to TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link]). import_remote fetches the live URL over HTTP and ignores t[:created_at], so imported topics get current timestamps instead of original dates, imports fail or are slow when links are dead, and the removed category option silently drops categorization.

title: order() mixin off-by-one for legacy box-ordinal-group
body: The order() mixin copies $val directly to -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group, but the legacy box model is 1-indexed while modern order is 0-indexed (correct mapping is box-ordinal-group = order + 1). As written, @include order(2) in extra-info-wrapper and @include order(3) in the header panel produce groups 2/3 in old WebKit/Firefox instead of 3/4, so ordering is wrong where those prefixes apply. Fix by emitting ($val + 1) for the box-ordinal-group properties.

title: align-items mixin emits non-existent -ms-align-items property
body: The align-items mixin outputs -ms-align-items, which was never implemented in any browser; IE10/11 use -ms-flex-align for this purpose. The declaration is dead code that bloats every call site using align-items(center/baseline) and signals a typo. It should be removed, leaving -ms-flex-align plus the standard align-items.

title: float:right on .small-action button ignored inside flex container
body: .small-action was changed to display:flex via flexbox(), making its direct children (avatar, description, button) flex items. Per the Flexbox spec float and clear on flex items compute to none, so the button's float:right no longer pushes it to the right edge; it will render inline right after the description text. This breaks small-action rows that expect a right-aligned button. Replace the float with margin-left:auto or justify-content:space-between.

title: margin-left:auto replacement for float:right breaks legacy/non-flex browsers
body: .d-header .panel lost its float:right fallback and now relies on margin-left:auto inside a flex container to sit on the right. The flexbox() mixin also emits display:-webkit-box/-moz-box, where auto margins are ignored, and browsers with no flex support get no positioning at all, so the panel will stay left or stack and overlap the logo/title. Keep a float:right fallback before the flex rules or add an explicit legacy packing fallback.

title: order mixin off-by-one for legacy box-ordinal-group
body: In app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss the order() mixin copies $val directly into -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group. The legacy 2009 box ordinal-group is 1-based (default 1 corresponds to modern order 0), so correct fallback is $val + 1. As written @include order(2) / order(3) in header/topic emit ordinal-group 2/3 which mean modern order 1/2, so legacy WebKit/Firefox order header elements differently than modern browsers, and any future order(1) will tie with the default group 1 and not reorder at all in legacy browsers.

title: float:right on flex item is ignored, action button not right-aligned
body: In app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic-post.scss .small-action is now a flex container, making .topic-avatar, .small-action-desc and button flex items. Per CSS Flexbox spec float has no effect on flex items, so button { float: right; } is dead. The button will sit immediately after the description instead of at the far right edge, crowding text and breaking the previous small-action layout. It needs margin-left: auto or justify-content handling, not float.

title: margin-left:auto fallback fails with 2009 flexbox prefixes
body: In app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/header.scss .panel uses margin-left: auto to push it right inside .contents which uses the new flexbox() mixin. That mixin emits display: -webkit-box / -moz-box 2009 fallbacks where auto margins do not absorb free space or push items to the end. In browsers that only understand those prefixed values the header panel will not be right-aligned and will collapse next to the title, breaking the header the mixin claims to support.

title: align-items mixin emits invalid property and misses Firefox prefix
body: In app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss align-items() emits -ms-align-items which does not exist and is dead code, while omitting -moz-box-align even though flexbox() emits display: -moz-box. Old Firefox therefore gets a legacy flex container with no alignment declaration and loses the vertical centering/baseline alignment used for the header and bullet badges. The mixin also forwards modern values verbatim to -ms-flex-align/-webkit-box-align whose keyword sets differ, inviting future misuse.

title: website_name include hook misnamed so it never runs
body: In app/serializers/user_serializer.rb the method is defined as `include_website_name` without a trailing `?`, while ActiveModel::Serializers looks for `include_website_name?` (as used by every other hook in the file like `include_email?` and `include_stats?`). As a result the `website.present?` guard is never called and `website_name` is always serialized, even when `website` is blank (as nil). Fix by renaming to `include_website_name?`.

title: website_name leaks TL0 user website to anonymous users
body: `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` so it is hidden from anonymous viewers for TL0 users via `scope.restrict_user_fields?`, but the newly added `website_name` (host plus path) is only added to `attributes` and not to `untrusted_attributes`. An anonymous client can therefore learn a TL0 user's website domain/path from `website_name` even when `website` itself is suppressed. Fix by adding `website_name` to the untrusted list / making its include check respect `restrict_user_fields?`.

title: Host comparison is case-sensitive and nil-unsafe
body: In app/serializers/user_serializer.rb `website_name` compares `URI(website).host` directly to `Discourse.current_hostname` with `==` and calls `split`/`ends_with?` on `discourse_host` without guarding nil or case. Hostnames are case-insensitive, so `http://EXAMPLE.COM/foo` on host `example.com` fails the equality and returns only the host without the path. If `Discourse.current_hostname` is ever nil, `split` raises NoMethodError and breaks all user serialization with a 500. Fix by downcasing both hosts and guarding nil.

title: TL0 untrusted test omits website_name
body: The spec's `untrusted_attributes` list in spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb does not include `website_name`, so the test that TL0 attributes are hidden from anonymous never checks the new field. This allows the privacy leak above to pass CI. Fix by adding `website_name` to that list.

title: include_website_name missing ? so filter is never called
body: In app/serializers/user_serializer.rb the serializer defines def include_website_name without a question mark. ActiveModel::Serializer checks include_<attr>? to decide whether to include an attribute, as used elsewhere in the same file for include_stats?, include_suspend_reason?, etc. Because the ? is missing the method is ignored, the website.present? guard is dead code, and website_name is always serialized even when website is blank or nil.

title: website_name bypasses TL0 anonymous hiding for website
body: In app/serializers/user_serializer.rb website is listed in untrusted_attributes so it is hidden from anonymous viewers when scope.restrict_user_fields?(object) is true for TL0 users. website_name was added to attributes on line 43 but was not added to untrusted_attributes. As a result a TL0 user's website host plus path is still sent as website_name even when website itself is suppressed, leaking the private profile field the restriction is meant to hide.

title: website_name drops port, query string and fragment
body: In app/serializers/user_serializer.rb website_name is built as website_host + URI(website.to_s).path in all three branches. That discards port, query string and fragment, so http://example.com/page?x=1#y and http://example.com:8080/page are both displayed as example.com/page. Two distinct user URLs become indistinguishable and the displayed text does not match the linked href, contrary to the stated goal of showing the complete path.

title: Host comparison is case-sensitive
body: In app/serializers/user_serializer.rb website_host is compared to Discourse.current_hostname with == and ends_with? without downcasing. DNS hostnames are case-insensitive, so a user website like http://EXAMPLE.COM/foo on an instance at example.com will be treated as an external domain and shown without path, producing inconsistent display for the same host.

title: Untrusted-attributes test omits website_name
body: In spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb the TL0 anonymous test lists bio_raw, bio_cooked, bio_excerpt, location, website, profile_background, card_background but not website_name. It therefore cannot catch that website_name is still serialized for TL0 users seen as anonymous while website is hidden.

title: Conditional serializer hook misnamed and never runs
body: In app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:153 the method is defined as `include_website_name` without a trailing `?`. ActiveModel::Serializer looks for `include_website_name?` as done for every other conditional attribute in the file (`include_email?`, `include_stats?`). Therefore the `website.present?` guard never runs and `website_name` is always serialized, even when `website` is blank where it returns nil.

title: website_name leaks for TL0 users hidden from anonymous
body: In app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:105 `untrusted_attributes` hides `website`, `location`, `bio_*`, etc. from anonymous viewers when the user is TL0 via `restrict_user_fields?`, but newly added `website_name` is not in that list. An anonymous client is therefore still sent the website host via `website_name` even when `website` itself is suppressed, defeating the trust-level privacy protection and disclosing user data.

title: Subdomain comparison matches unrelated domains sharing public suffix
body: In app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:144 same-length hosts are considered same-site if `split('.')[1..-1].join('.')` is equal. That only compares the last N-1 labels, so unrelated domains sharing a public suffix like website `evil.co.uk` vs instance `other.co.uk` both share `co.uk` and are treated as same site. The code then returns host plus path as if internal, misleading users into thinking an external site is part of the instance.

title: Nil current hostname crashes user serialization
body: In app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:139 `discourse_host = Discourse.current_hostname` is used without a nil guard, then `discourse_host.split('.')` on line 144 and `discourse_host.ends_with?` on line 149 are called. If the hostname is nil in console, tests, or misconfiguration, serialization raises NoMethodError and breaks the entire UserSerializer response with a 500.

title: Untrusted-attributes test omits website_name
body: In spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:11 the `untrusted_attributes` list checked for TL0 anonymous hiding does not include `website_name`. The test therefore still passes while the serializer leaks `website_name` for those users, so the privacy regression has no coverage.

title: Pagination totalPages off-by-one shows empty last page
body: In app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6 line 13 totalPages is Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50 users with limit 50) this returns 2 instead of 1, and 100/50 returns 3 instead of 2. Consequence: showingLast is wrong, the next action in the same file allows offset to become equal to user_count via Math.min(offset+limit, user_count), and the admin is able to navigate to a final empty page.

title: Unvalidated limit/offset allows 500 error and unbounded load
body: In app/controllers/groups_controller.rb lines 22-23 GroupsController#members does limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i and offset = params[:offset].to_i with no clamping, then passes them to limit().offset(). A negative offset produces SQL OFFSET -N which raises in Postgres and returns 500, and a huge or missing-capped limit (e.g. limit=1000000) loads an unbounded number of users via serialize_data, causing memory/CPU DoS. The endpoint should clamp offset to >=0 and limit to a sane max.

title: Admin members routes mismatch frontend URL and controller params
body: In config/routes.rb lines 49-50 delete/put "members" are defined bare inside resources :groups with no on: :member / member block, so the route does not provide a :group_id segment. The frontend in app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js calls PUT/DELETE /admin/groups/<id>/members.json with the id in the path, while app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb add_members/remove_member do params.require(:group_id). Real requests therefore either fail routing with 404 or fail with ActionController::ParameterMissing 400 for missing group_id, so add/remove member is completely broken.

title: add_members fails on usernames with spaces
body: In app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb line 71 add_members does usernames.split(",").each without stripping whitespace and then User.find_by_username(username). A normal input like "alice, bob" yields " bob" with a leading space which will not match, so the valid user is silently skipped and the admin gets success_json while nothing was added. The loop should strip each token.

title: remove_member bypasses Group#remove domain logic
body: In app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb line 90 remove_member does group.users.delete(user_id) instead of the Group#add/Group#remove domain methods used by the old update_patch code and still used by add_members via group.add(user). Association delete skips ActiveRecord callbacks, validations and any bookkeeping inside Group#remove, then group.save is called on an already-mutated join. Consequence is risk of stale user_count/counters, missed side-effects, and divergent add vs remove code paths leaving inconsistent membership state.

title: Specs bypass routing, use wrong verb, miss pagination
body: In spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb line 115 the automatic-group remove_member test uses xhr :put while config/routes.rb defines remove_member as DELETE, and all controller specs invoke actions directly with group_id so they never exercise routing. As a result the route/param mismatch that breaks /admin/groups/:id/members.json is not caught, and there is no coverage for GroupsController#members pagination, limit/offset validation, or whitespace handling in add_members.

title: add/remove member actions require :group_id but route and client supply :id
body: Admin JS calls PUT/DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members.json with only user_id/usernames in the body. The Rails member route `delete/put 'members'` under `resources :groups` supplies the group id as params[:id], not params[:group_id]. Both add_members (line 66) and remove_member (line 85) do Group.find(params.require(:group_id).to_i), so every real request raises ActionController::ParameterMissing and the admin add/remove member feature is broken. Specs pass only because they call the action directly with group_id, bypassing routing.

title: totalPages off-by-one creates phantom empty page
body: totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 instead of ceil. For example 50 members with limit 50 yields 2 pages instead of 1, 100/50 yields 3 instead of 2. Combined with next action capping offset at Math.min(offset+limit, user_count), the UI can navigate to offset == user_count which returns zero members, showing an empty last page and wrong 2/2 or 3/3 counters.

title: Public group members page only loads first page with no pagination
body: The public members route now sets the model to the Group object and calls model.findMembers() once, which defaults to limit 50 offset 0. There is no next/previous UI on the public members template. Previously non-automatic groups returned all members, so any group with more than 50 members now permanently shows only the first 50 with no way to see the rest.

title: Unbounded limit/offset params allow DoS and invalid queries
body: Members action does limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i and offset = params[:offset].to_i with no clamping. A caller can request limit=1000000 to force loading huge numbers of users into memory, or negative limit/offset which produces SQL errors or surprising results. Limit should be clamped to a sane max (e.g. 1..200) and offset to >=0.

title: Group create ignores alias_level sent by client
body: The JS Group.asJSON() sends name, alias_level and visible, and update handles alias_level, but create only assigns name and visible. A group created with a non-default alias level silently loses that choice and gets the default, requiring a second update to fix.

title: Adding members splits on comma without stripping whitespace
body: add_members does usernames.split(',').each with no strip. Input like 'alice, bob' from a user-selector leaves a leading space on the second name, so User.find_by_username(' bob') returns nil and that user is silently skipped while the endpoint still returns success. The admin thinks all users were added when only a subset was.

title: remove_member uses low-level association delete bypassing domain logic
body: remove_member does group.users.delete(user_id) while the add path uses group.add(user) and the old code used group.remove(user). Direct association delete bypasses Group model callbacks and counter maintenance, then calls group.save redundantly. This risks stale user_count and missed side effects, and is inconsistent with the add path.

title: remove_member automatic-group test uses wrong HTTP verb
body: The test for cannot remove members from automatic groups does xhr :put, :remove_member while the route is DELETE members => remove_member. Controller specs invoke the action directly regardless of verb, so the test passes while masking that a real PUT would not route and that the controller/route :group_id vs :id mismatch is not exercised. It gives false confidence for the member-removal endpoint.

title: totalPages off-by-one creates empty last page
body: In app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6 line 13 totalPages is Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50 users, limit 50) this returns 2 instead of 1, and 100 users with limit 50 returns 3 instead of 2. The correct value is Math.ceil(user_count / limit). Consequence: pagination shows a phantom page, showingLast never becomes true on the real last page, and the next action can set offset equal to user_count which fetches an empty page.

title: group-member itemView uses wrong template context
body: In app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group_member.hbs line 1 the template used as itemView for {{each member in members}} references {{member.username}}, {{avatar member}} and {{#unless automatic}}. Inside an Ember itemView the context is already the member User object, so member is undefined and automatic resolves on the User instead of the Group. Consequence: avatar/username render blank, {{action removeMember member}} passes undefined causing member.get(username) to throw, and the remove link is shown even for automatic groups where removal should be hidden.

title: members limit/offset unvalidated allows DoS and 500
body: In app/controllers/groups_controller.rb lines 22-23 limit is (params[:limit] || 50).to_i and offset is params[:offset].to_i with no clamping. An attacker can request limit=1000000 to load the entire group into memory in one request, or offset negative which makes ActiveRecord generate OFFSET -5 and raises a 500. Consequence: performance denial of service and unhandled exceptions on public group members endpoint.

title: add_members does not strip whitespace around usernames
body: In app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb line 71 usernames.split(",").each passes each token directly to User.find_by_username. A normal input like "bob, alice" leaves a leading space on " alice" which will not match, so the user is silently skipped. Consequence: adding multiple members appears to succeed but only the first is added with no error.

title: remove_member deletes immediately then checks save
body: In app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb line 90 group.users.delete(user_id) executes DELETE SQL immediately for a has_many through association, then line 92 calls group.save to decide success. If save fails the deletion is already persisted with no rollback, and if delete is a no-op for a non-member it still returns success. Consequence: misleading success/error responses and no transactional integrity for membership changes.

title: add/remove_member expects group_id but route provides id
body: In app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb lines 66 and 85 the actions do Group.find(params.require(:group_id).to_i), but in config/routes.rb lines 49-50 delete members and put members are defined as bare member routes inside resources :groups, which provide :id like the suspend and other member routes in the same file, not :group_id. Consequence: every real HTTP request raises ActionController::ParameterMissing and add/remove member is completely broken; the controller specs mask it by passing group_id directly and bypassing routing.

title: findMembers returns undefined instead of promise
body: In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js line 21 findMembers does return ; when name is empty, whereas before it returned Ember.RSVP.resolve([]). It also no longer returns the members array, resolving to undefined. Consequence: any caller chaining findMembers().then throws TypeError on empty names and existing callers expecting an array break.

title: admin group route no longer waits or handles members errors
body: In app/assets/javascripts/admin/routes/admin_group_route.js line 13 setupController just calls model.findMembers() without returning or awaiting it, whereas before afterModel waited and stored members. The same pattern is in discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6. Consequence: first render shows empty member list with wrong pagination, and failures like 403/500 are swallowed instead of transitioning to an error route, leaving an empty table with no feedback.

title: remove_member spec uses wrong HTTP verb
body: In spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb line 115 the test for cannot remove members from automatic groups does xhr :put, :remove_member while the route is DELETE members. Controller specs bypass routing so the test passes without verifying the real route. Consequence: the group_id vs id routing mismatch and verb mismatch are not caught by tests.

title: Fallback chain crashes on nil default locale and hits DB on every lookup
body: FallbackLocaleList#[] builds [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact. to_sym is called before compact, so if SiteSetting.default_locale is nil (unseeded DB, test setup, migration) it raises NoMethodError instead of falling back to :en. Worse, this method is called by I18n::Backend::Fallbacks on every I18n.t to compute the fallback chain, so every translation now triggers a SiteSetting (DB/cached-setting) read and any DB outage or early-boot call (migrations, asset precompile, console, initializers) breaks all translations.

title: LRU translation cache ignores site default locale, serves stale fallback
body: I18n.translate caches with key "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}", which includes only key and current locale. With the new fallback order of user locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, then :en, the result for the same key+locale changes when the admin changes the site default locale. The cache is never invalidated on that change, so after a default-locale change users keep receiving the previously cached fallback language until entries are evicted or the process restarts.

title: Fallback locale files only preloaded in controller, missing elsewhere
body: I18n.translate only calls load_locale(config.locale) for the current locale, while preloading of the full fallback chain (current locale, site default, :en) only happens in ApplicationController#set_locale via I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!. Because translations are loaded lazily on demand, any I18n.t outside a web request (Sidekiq jobs, mailers, rake tasks, console) or any I18n.t with an explicit locale: option can resolve to a fallback locale whose YAML was never loaded, so lookup returns translation-missing even though the translation exists on disk.

title: Nil default_locale crashes fallback instead of falling back
body: In config/initializers/i18n.rb FallbackLocaleList#[] does [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact. If SiteSetting.default_locale is nil or blank the .to_sym call raises NoMethodError before .compact ever runs, so the compact is dead code. Any missing translation then raises instead of falling back to :en, turning a translation miss into a 500 during setup, migrations, or if the setting is cleared.

title: Translation LRU cache ignores fallback chain
body: In lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb I18n.translate caches with key "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}", which omits SiteSetting.default_locale and the fallback list. A miss resolved via fallback (e.g. fr -> de -> en) is cached under the request locale alone. If the admin later changes SiteSetting.default_locale, the cached fallback value is still served until I18n.reload! or process restart, showing the old language.

title: Fallback files only preloaded on web requests
body: In app/controllers/application_controller.rb set_locale calls I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! to load the user locale, site default, and :en. But lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb I18n.translate only does load_locale(config.locale) for the current locale. Any I18n.t outside a controller request — Sidekiq jobs, mailers, background email rendering, console, rake — never preloads the fallback locales, so a key missing in the current locale returns translation-missing even though it exists in the site default or English.

title: DB lookup on every fallback miss
body: In config/initializers/i18n.rb FallbackLocaleList#[] calls SiteSetting.default_locale on every lookup. The I18n fallback backend calls fallbacks[locale] for every missing key, so every untranslated key does a SiteSetting read in the hot translation path instead of using a cached value, adding Redis/DB overhead to pages with many missing keys.

title: Fallback lookup crashes when site default locale is nil
body: In config/initializers/i18n.rb line 17 FallbackLocaleList#[] builds [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact. Calling to_sym before compact means a nil site setting raises NoMethodError instead of being removed by compact. Any translation that needs fallback resolution then raises instead of falling back to English, turning a missing string into a 500 error. This is reachable during boot, migrations, tests, or if Redis/DB is unavailable. Fix by handling nil/blank safely before to_sym.

title: Translation cache ignores fallback chain and poisons misses
body: In lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb line 72 the cache key is "#{key}#{config.locale}#{backend.object_id}" with no site default locale or fallback list. A key missing in the user locale but present in the fallback locale caches the fallback result under only the user locale. Changing SiteSetting.default_locale later still returns the old cached language, and worse a lookup done before fallback files are loaded caches the 'translation missing' string forever until eviction or I18n.reload!. Fix by including the resolved fallback chain in the key and not caching missing translations, and invalidating on locale-setting change.

title: Translate preloads only current locale, ignores fallbacks and explicit locale
body: In lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb line 67 I18n.translate only calls load_locale(config.locale) and never loads the fallback locales (site default, :en). It also ignores an explicit locale option in args when deciding what to load. So I18n.t(key, locale: :de) while global locale is :en only ensures :en is loaded, and any use outside ApplicationController#set_locale (Sidekiq, mailers, console, explicit-locale emails) gets 'translation missing' even though the string exists in the fallback file, because on-demand loading never loaded that file. Fix by ensuring the full fallback chain for the requested locale inside translate.

title: DB lookup on every fallback resolution
body: In config/initializers/i18n.rb FallbackLocaleList#[] calls SiteSetting.default_locale on every fallback resolution, i.e. on every translation miss. That puts a SiteSetting (Redis/DB-backed) lookup on the hot translation path, adding overhead per missing key plus per-request ensure_loaded! cost, and makes all translated error pages depend on DB availability. If the DB is down during early boot or outage, translation itself raises. Memoize/cache the site locale per request or fall back to I18n.default_locale without DB access.

title: No tests for fallback order and lazy loading
body: In config/initializers/i18n.rb a new user-locale to site-locale to English fallback chain plus on-demand loading is introduced, but the pull request changes no specs. There is no coverage that a missing key in the user locale resolves from the site locale then English, that fallback files are loaded on demand in controllers and background jobs, or that explicit locale arguments work. Regressions in ordering or missing-file handling would ship undetected.

title: Denial cache key omits identity type, poisoning across principals
body: userPermDenialCacheKey builds a key from namespace, userUID, action, name and parent only, with no identity type. Anonymous subject 'anonymous:0' and render subject 'render:0' both resolve to UID '0', so they share the identical denial key for the same namespace/action/resource. Service.Check checks this denial cache first and returns Allowed:false on hit without evaluating permissions. Consequence: a denial cached for anonymous causes a later renderer check for the same dashboard/folder to be denied without ever consulting renderer wildcard logic, and any user/service-account UID overlap across types shares the same fate, causing false denies for up to the 30s TTL.

title: Denial cache short-circuits fresh DB read, preserving stale denies
body: Check looks up permDenialCache and on hit immediately returns Allowed:false without consulting cached permissions or the database. Denial entries are set after a DB-backed deny and live 30 seconds with no invalidation. If access is granted after the denial was cached, for example a newly created dashboard/folder grant or role change, checks for that same name+folder within the TTL still deny even though the DB would now allow. This defeats the PR's own fallback that requeries the DB when cached scopes miss, because the denial hit prevents that fallback. Consequence: newly granted access remains invisible until expiry.

title: Every cached deny triggers DB fetch, nullifying permission cache
body: After a denial-cache miss, Check loads cached permissions; if they hit but checkPermission returns false it falls through to getIdentityPermissions which queries the DB for identifiers, roles, teams and permissions. Previously a cached scope map served denies without DB work. Now every Check for a distinct resource the user lacks access to costs full DB queries, with the per-resource denial cache only helping repeats of the exact same name+parent. Enumerating many random names or normal deny-heavy traffic causes one DB permission fetch per distinct resource. Consequence: large latency and DB load regression and easy DoS amplification.

title: List serves stale cached permissions with no outdated-cache fallback
body: List calls getCachedIdentityPermissions and if it hits uses that scope map directly to build the response, only querying the DB on cache miss. Unlike Check there is no revalidation when the cached map is outdated. If the per-user/action permCache entry was populated before a dashboard/folder was created or granted, List omits the new item until the 30s entry expires. Consequence: the stated goal of letting users fetch newly created dashboards/folders still fails on the List path.

title: Folder hierarchy cache not refreshed on deny, breaking inherited grants
body: checkInheritedPermissions calls buildFolderTree which returns the cached folderTree if present and otherwise never refreshes it on permission denial. Check's new fallback refreshes permission scopes from the DB but leaves the folder tree stale. If a child folder or dashboard is created under a parent the user can access, the stale tree lacks the new node so Ancestors/Children lookups still fail, the check denies even with fresh scopes and then caches a per-resource denial. Consequence: new nested folders/dashboards relying on inherited folder permissions stay inaccessible until the folder cache expires.

title: DB fallback reuses stale team and role caches, missing new team grants
body: getUserPermissions, used for the fallback DB read, first calls getUserBasicRole and getUserTeams which return cached values when present. The subsequent permissionStore.GetUserPermissions query is built from those possibly stale team IDs and role. If access was newly granted via team membership or basic-role change, the fallback still queries with old teams/role and returns no permission, so Check denies and caches denial. Consequence: requerying permissions from the DB does not fix freshness for team/role-driven grants until those caches expire.

title: Denial key concatenation ambiguous, distinct resources share entry
body: The denial key is namespace + '.perm_' + userUID + '_' + action + '_' + name + '_' + parent with plain underscore separators and no escaping. Different tuples collide, for example name 'a_b' with parent 'c' produces the same suffix as name 'a' with parent 'b_c', and UIDs or actions containing underscores add more collisions. Since dashboard/folder UIDs can contain underscores, two distinct resources can map to the same denial key. Consequence: a denial cached for one resource falsely denies an unrelated resource for up to the TTL.

title: Denial cache key omits identity type, cross-principal denial
body: In pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go Check builds permDenialKey from namespace, UserUID, action, name and parent only, without IdentityType. Different identity types can share the same UID string, e.g. anonymous:0 yields UID 0 and render:0 also yields UID 0, and user vs service-account can share UID strings. A denial cached for one principal will therefore cause Check for a different principal with the same UID/action/resource to return Allowed:false without consulting the DB, incorrectly denying e.g. renderer reads that should always be allowed.

title: Denial cache short-circuit reintroduces stale deny after grant
body: In pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go Check returns Allowed:false immediately on permDenialCache hit without requerying the DB, and caches every DB-computed denial for shortCacheTTL (30s). If permissions are granted after a denial was cached, the user continues to be denied until TTL expiry. This reintroduces the same staleness window the PR claims to fix, just moved from permCache to permDenialCache.

title: List serves stale cached permissions with no DB fallback
body: In pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go List uses getCachedIdentityPermissions and if it hits returns that stale map directly to listPermission, only querying the DB on cache miss. Unlike Check which falls back to the DB when cached perms deny, List has no revalidation. A dashboard/folder created after the permCache entry was populated will be missing from List Items/Folders for up to 30s, so the stated goal of fetching newly created dashboards/folders is not fixed for list operations.

title: False deny from stale folder tree is cached in denial cache
body: In pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go Check refreshes permissions from the DB on cached deny but reuses the same cached folderTree inside checkPermission/checkInheritedPermissions for both the cached and fresh evaluation. If folderCache is stale, the fresh evaluation can still return false, and that false is then stored in permDenialCache. The result stacks TTLs: a stale tree causes a denial entry that continues to deny even after the folder cache refreshes, extending the deny window beyond either TTL alone.

title: Denial-cache test stores deny instead of allow
body: In pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go TestService_CacheCheck Should deny on explicit cache deny entry sets permCache to map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false} with a comment saying it allows access to prove the denial cache is checked first. Since the value is false, checkPermission would deny even without the denial cache, so the test passes whether or not the denial short-circuit works. It should store true to prove precedence, leaving the denial path effectively untested.

title: Denial cache key is ambiguous with underscore separator
body: In pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go userPermDenialCacheKey concatenates userUID, action, name and parent with _ separators. UIDs, dashboard names and folder UIDs can contain _, so different tuples can produce the same key (e.g. name b_c parent d vs name b parent c_d). A collision causes one resource's denial to incorrectly deny a different resource.

title: Per-resource denial cache serves stale denies and blocks fresh grants
body: In Service.Check the server first checks permDenialCache and returns Allowed:false immediately on hit, without consulting the DB. On a DB-backed deny it inserts an entry with 30s TTL. If permissions are granted after a deny (new role binding, new dashboard/folder grant, team membership change), subsequent Checks for the same namespace/user/action/name/parent are denied from the denial cache for the full TTL even though a DB query would now allow. The denial is also checked before cached allows, so a stale deny wins over a freshly refreshed permCache entry that would allow. Consequence is 30s of incorrect Forbidden after grants, defeating the PR's freshness goal for the grant path.

title: List still serves stale cached permissions with no DB fallback
body: Service.List loads permissions with getCachedIdentityPermissions and on cache hit uses them directly to build the list response. Unlike Service.Check, which was changed to re-query the DB when the cached scope map does not contain the requested resource, List has no outdated-cache fallback. A dashboard or folder created after the user's permCache entry was populated will be missing from List Items/Folders until that 30s permCache entry expires. Consequence is newly created resources remain invisible in list views while single-item Check may already allow them.

title: Stale folder-tree cache breaks fresh checks for new folders
body: Service.Check refreshes permission scopes from the DB on cached miss/deny, but inherited folder checks in checkInheritedPermissions still use buildFolderTree which is cached for 30s. For a dashboard in a newly created folder, or a new subfolder under an ancestor the user can access, the stale tree does not contain the new folder UID so Ancestors(newFolder) returns empty. Even with a fresh scopeMap containing the ancestor folders:uid grant, the check returns false. Consequence is the creator still cannot access dashboards/folders in new hierarchy until the folder cache expires, undermining the fix.

title: Denial cache key concatenation can collide on underscores
body: userPermDenialCacheKey builds a key as namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent with no escaping. Dashboard, folder and user UIDs can contain underscores. For example action=a, name=b_c, parent=d produces the same suffix as action=a, name=b, parent=c_d. Two different resources then share one denial entry, so a deny cached for one resource causes an incorrect fast-path deny for the other resource. Consequence is spurious Forbidden for unrelated resources until expiry.

title: Every cached deny now forces a DB query
body: Service.Check on a permCache hit that does not allow falls through to getIdentityPermissions which queries basic roles, teams and permission store from the DB. Previously a deny could be served from the cached scope map with no DB work. Now any check for a resource UID not present in the cached map hits the DB. The per-resource denial cache only helps exact repeats of the same name+parent within 30s. Consequence is large increase in DB/QPS for deny-heavy or enumeration workloads, and an attacker probing random names can force a DB query per request.

title: Denial-precedence test seeds impossible false permission value
body: TestService_CacheCheck case 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry' claims to prove the denial cache short-circuits even when an allow exists, but it seeds permCache with map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}. Production getScopeMap only ever inserts true values and checkPermission tests truthiness of the value, so that entry would deny anyway. The test passes even if the denial cache is removed. It should seed true to actually exercise precedence. Consequence is the denial-priority behavior is untested and future regressions will not be caught.

title: Denial key uses raw subject instead of canonical UID
body: The denial key is built from checkReq.UserUID, which is the raw string parsed from the request subject, before GetUserIdentifiers canonicalization. The permCache key uses the canonical UID returned from the store. GetUserIdentifiers explicitly handles numeric IDs versus string UIDs mapping to the same user. The same logical user requesting as user:123 versus user:uid-abc gets different denial keys for the same resource. Consequence is cache fragmentation, missed denial hits and extra DB queries, and inconsistent behavior by subject representation.

title: Missing React key for Grafana rules in filter view
body: In FilterView.tsx the grafana branch renders GrafanaRuleListItem without a key prop, while the datasource branch passes key={key}. Without a stable key React warns and cannot correctly reconcile the infinite-scrolling list, causing state leakage between rows, wrong row updates on load-more/filter, and degraded performance.

title: Pause action can never show in prom-only list view
body: AlertRuleMenu computes canPause as OR of ruler and Grafana prom abilities, implying prom-only rules should be pausable, but rendering additionally requires rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) to be truthy. In the new list view rulerRule is undefined, so the Pause menu item never renders even when the user has pause permission. Users lose Pause from the list view.

title: Delete action can never show in prom-only list view
body: AlertRuleMenu computes canDelete as OR of ruler and Grafana prom abilities, but rendering is gated on canDelete && rulerRule. In the new list view only promRule is passed and rulerRule is undefined, so Delete never appears even for users with delete permission. The computed Grafana delete ability is dead code and delete is regressed.

title: Silence drawer never opens for prom-only rules
body: RuleActionsButtons sets showSilenceDrawer true when Silence is clicked from AlertRuleMenu, which now appears via Grafana prom abilities, but the drawer is only rendered if rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) where rule is the optional ruler rule. In the prom-only list view rule is undefined, so the condition is always false and clicking Silence notifications does nothing with no error.

title: skipToken still grants Duplicate for non-Grafana rules
body: useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities maps skipToken to undefined and calls useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined). For undefined the hook still returns supported=true for Duplicate based on Grafana create permission. ORed with ruler abilities in AlertRuleMenu, this shows Duplicate for data-source rules to users who have Grafana rule create but lack external write permission, over-exposing the action.

title: Federated rule protection removed
body: The old useAllAlertRuleAbilities checked isFederatedRuleGroup to mark federated groups immutable and block Update/Delete/Pause. The new useAllRulerRuleAbilities hardcodes isFederated to false with a TODO. Federated Mimir rules now appear editable, removable and pausable in the UI, allowing users to attempt mutations that should be blocked.

title: Rule view link drops returnTo navigation
body: The previous GrafanaRuleListItem built the view href with createReturnTo and passed returnTo as a query param so the detail page can navigate back to the filtered list. The new GrafanaRuleListItem builds href as /alerting/grafana/<uid>/view without returnTo, so Back navigation from the rule view loses list context.

title: Newly created rules disappear until Prometheus syncs
body: GrafanaGroupLoader previously merged ruler and Prometheus and rendered ruler-only rules as Creating and prom-only rules as Deleting to hide eventual consistency. It now renders only promResponse rules. A rule just created in the ruler but not yet in Prometheus vanishes from the list instead of showing Creating, and recently deleted rules appear as normal, confusing users and inviting duplicate creates or repeated edits.

title: Missing React key for Grafana rules in filtered list
body: In FilterViewResults the rules.map destructures key but the grafana branch renders GrafanaRuleListItem without key={key} while the datasource branch passes it. Without stable keys React reuses DOM and component state incorrectly during infinite scroll and filter changes, causing wrong rows, lost focus, or actions opening for the wrong rule.

title: Silence drawer never opens for Prometheus-only rules
body: RuleActionsButtons now accepts prom-only Grafana rules with optional ruler rule and AlertRuleMenu enables Silence from prom abilities. handleSilence sets showSilenceDrawer true, but rendering is gated on rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) where rule is the optional ruler DTO. In the list view rule is undefined so the condition is always false, SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer never mounts and clicking Silence does nothing.

title: Pause action hidden for Prometheus-only rules
body: AlertRuleMenu computes canPause as OR of ruler and prom abilities to support the list view without ruler fetch, but the Pause menu item still requires rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule). When called from the new list with only promRule, rulerRule is undefined so Pause never renders even when the prom ability says it is supported and allowed, removing pause/unpause from the list.

title: Delete action hidden for Prometheus-only rules
body: canDelete is computed as OR of ruler and prom abilities, but the Delete menu item is gated on canDelete && rulerRule. With only promRule in the list view rulerRule is undefined so Delete never appears even with permission, making Grafana rules undeletable from the list. The handler signature also still requires a ruler DTO so no prom-aware delete path exists.

title: Duplicate allowed for cloud rules via Grafana permissions
body: useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities maps skipToken to undefined, and useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities still returns Duplicate as supported with allowed based on Grafana create permission even when rule is undefined. AlertRuleMenu calls it with skipToken for non-Grafana rules and ORs with the ruler result, so a user with Grafana create but without external write permission gets Duplicate enabled for Mimir/Loki/Cortex rules.

title: Export disabled for Grafana recording rules
body: In useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities ModifyExport is [isAlertingRule, exportAllowed] where isAlertingRule is true only for alerting type. The ruler version used isGrafanaManagedAlertRule which is true for both alerting and recording. As a result Grafana recording rules always report export unsupported and lose the Export menu item.

title: Federated rules no longer treated as immutable
body: useAllAlertRuleAbilities previously checked isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) to block Update/Delete/Pause for federated groups. It now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities with only rulerRule and group identifier, which hardcodes isFederated to false. Federated rules now report edit and delete as supported, offering actions that must be blocked.

title: Rule view link drops returnTo navigation state
body: The previous list item built the detail href as /alerting/grafana/<uid>/view with a returnTo query so the detail page can navigate back to the list with filters. The new GrafanaRuleListItem builds the href without returnTo, so Back from rule details loses list context.

title: Grafana branch in FilterView omits React key
body: In FilterView.tsx the list maps rules to components with a computed `key`, but the `grafana` case returns `<GrafanaRuleListItem>` without `key={key}` while the `datasource` and unknown cases pass it. Missing keys cause React warnings and incorrect reconciliation during infinite scroll and filter updates, so state, focus, or action menus can attach to the wrong rule row.

title: View link drops returnTo navigation context
body: The old GrafanaRuleLoader built the rule view href with `createRelativeUrl(..., { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`. The new GrafanaRuleListItem builds `href` as `/alerting/grafana/<uid>/view` with no `returnTo`. Users opening a rule from the list lose the back-navigation context, so returning from the detail view no longer restores the list/filter state.

title: Pause action can never show in ruler-less list view
body: AlertRuleMenu computes `canPause` as ruler-ability OR grafana-prom-ability to support the list view without ruler data, but the Pause menu item still requires `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)`. In the new list view `rulerRule` is undefined because ruler requests were removed, so the condition is always false and Pause never renders even when the prom-based ability says the user can pause.

title: Delete action can never show in ruler-less list view
body: AlertRuleMenu computes `canDelete` via ruler OR grafana-prom abilities, but the Delete menu item is guarded by `canDelete && rulerRule`. In the new list view `rulerRule` is undefined, so Delete is never rendered for Grafana rules even for users with delete permission. The delete flow in RuleActionsButtons only needs an identifier from prom data, so gating on rulerRule is an unnecessary regression that removes delete from the list.

title: Silence drawer never opens without rulerRule
body: RuleActionsButtons shows a Silence menu item based on prom-based abilities, and clicking it sets `showSilenceDrawer`. The drawer itself is rendered only if `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` where `rule` is the optional ruler rule. In the list view only `promRule` is passed, so the predicate is false and `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` never mounts. Users see Silence but clicking it does nothing.

title: Skipped grafana ability grants Duplicate to cloud rules
body: For non-Grafana prom rules AlertRuleMenu calls `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` with `skipToken`, which becomes `undefined` in `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`. With undefined rule, `duplicateSupported` is true and Duplicate ability is `[true, hasGrafanaCreatePermission]`. OR-ing ruler and grafana Duplicate abilities then shows Duplicate for Mimir/Loki/cloud rules based on Grafana create permission instead of external write permission, exposing an action the user may not be allowed to perform on that datasource.

title: Federated rule immutability check removed
body: The old combined-rule abilities marked groups with `source_tenants` as federated via `isFederatedRuleGroup` and made them immutable. The new `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` hardcodes `isFederated = false` with a TODO.
