Mimir federated rule groups are read-only, but they will now appear editable and deletable in the UI, leading to failed API calls and attempts to modify rules that must not be edited.

title: Provisioned check fails open when prom provenance missing
body: `isProvisionedPromRule` returns true only if `promRule.provenance` is truthy, and `GrafanaRuleListItem` uses `Boolean(provenance)` for the provisioned badge. The PR adds `provenance` to the prom DTO without a backend change in the same diff. Any prom response without that field, stale cache, or recording rule without provenance evaluates to not-provisioned, so file-provisioned rules appear editable and lose their provisioned indicator, whereas the old ruler-based check used `grafana_alert.provenance`.

title: Creating and deleting states silently dropped
body: The old GrafanaGroupLoader matched ruler rules against prom rules to render Creating items for ruler-only rules and Deleting items for prom-only rules. The new loader renders only `promResponse.data.groups.at(0).rules`. Newly created rules not yet visible in Prometheus disappear from the list, and rules being deleted appear as normal actionable rules instead of a Deleting state, so users can act on stale rules and miss pending rules.

title: Stale comment claims ruler preload still happens
body: The cache-population block still comments that it preloads ruler rules to improve UX, but the `alertRuleApi.util.prefetch('getGrafanaRulerGroup')` call was removed. The comment is now wrong and will mislead future maintainers about what is cached and why initial load behaves as it does.

title: Early interpolation defeats $__range split guard and freezes range
body: runSplitQuery now calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables on every target before querySupportsSplitting/isQueryWithRangeVariable is checked. applyTemplateVariables expands template variables (new test proves it expands $__auto and $step), so it will also expand $__range/$__range_s/$__range_ms before the guard sees them. The guard !isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr) will then pass and a query that must not be split will be split. All split sub-requests will carry $__range/$__interval frozen to the full-range value instead of per-split-range backend interpolation described in the code comment, returning wrong data.

title: Double interpolation duplicates ad-hoc filters
body: runShardSplitQuery interpolates with datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters), then delegates each shard group to runSplitQuery via subRequest={...request, targets:...} which interpolates again with the same scopedVars/filters. The updated test expecting 5 calls for 1 target confirms the double pass. Applying template variables with request.filters rewrites expr to add ad-hoc filters; running it twice appends them twice and re-expands variables, producing over-constrained/wrong LogQL and wasted work. Interpolation with filters should happen once.

title: Empty check runs before interpolation
body: runSplitQuery filters with .filter((query)=>query.expr) before .map((query)=>datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...)). A query whose raw expr is truthy but interpolates to empty (e.g. expr is a variable that is empty/undefined) passes the filter and then flows into isLogsQuery/partition/grouping and datasource.runQuery. This issues backend requests for empty queries and can misclassify them. The same pattern exists in shardQuerySplitting.ts. Filter for empty expr after interpolation.

title: Shard path interpolates template variables twice
body: runShardSplitQuery in shardQuerySplitting.ts now calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables on every target, then passes the already-interpolated targets to runSplitQuery in querySplitting.ts which calls applyTemplateVariables again on the same queries (with shard selector added). The updated test expects 5 applyTemplateVariables calls for a single query, proving the double pass. The second pass re-applies scopedVars and request.filters including ad-hoc filters to an expression that already contains them, which duplicates ad-hoc filter clauses, re-expands values containing $ and wastes work. Interpolation should happen once or the second pass must be skipped.

title: Early interpolation defeats $__range split exclusion
body: runSplitQuery in querySplitting.ts now interpolates every query with applyTemplateVariables before calling querySupportsSplitting, which excludes queries containing the $__range variable because $__range must be interpolated per split on the backend with the split time range. Because the same interpolation expands macros like $__auto to concrete values as shown in the new test, it will also expand $__range before the guard is checked, so isQueryWithRangeVariable never matches. Range-variable queries that must not be split will then be time-split with a frozen full-range value baked into every chunk, returning wrong data.

title: Empty-after-interpolation queries are no longer dropped
body: Both runSplitQuery and runShardSplitQuery filter on raw query.expr truthiness before calling applyTemplateVariables. A query like $var that is non-empty before interpolation but interpolates to an empty string is therefore kept. In the shard path this is a regression because the old code interpolated with interpolateVariablesInQueries first and then filtered, so variable-to-empty queries were dropped. The kept empty queries now go to fetchLabelValues for __stream_shard__ and to runQuery with an empty selector, causing backend errors and wasted shard requests. Filtering must also happen after interpolation.

title: Plugin request logs no longer include traceID
body: In pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/logger_middleware.go line 49, logRequest builds logParams with only status, duration, eventName and time_before_plugin_request. The old code explicitly added traceID via tracing.TraceIDFromContext. The new code removed that and relies on m.logger.FromContext(ctx). The context enrichment in pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/contextual_logger_middleware.go instrumentContext only adds endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname, never traceID. So traceID is silently dropped from 'Plugin Request Completed' logs, breaking trace-to-log correlation for plugin requests.

title: TestLogger.FromContext discards logs
body: In pkg/plugins/log/fake.go line 46, TestLogger.FromContext returns NewTestLogger(), a fresh empty logger, ignoring the receiver. The real implementation in pkg/plugins/log/logger.go returns a wrapper sharing the underlying sink with contextual attributes. After the change LoggerMiddleware does m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), so the Info call lands on the throwaway object, not on the injected m.logger. Tests asserting on the original TestLogger's InfoLogs/WarnLogs will see zero calls, making the new logging path unobservable and untestable.

title: ContextualLoggerMiddleware panics on nil request
body: In pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/contextual_logger_middleware.go line 40, QueryData (and similarly CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) dereferences req.PluginContext without checking req for nil. The sibling LoggerMiddleware in the same package explicitly guards if req == nil before touching it, showing nil is considered possible. Since ContextualLoggerMiddleware is wired outer to LoggerMiddleware in pluginsintegration.go, a nil request panics with nil dereference before reaching Logger's guard, crashing the request path.

title: FromContext silently drops context on type assertion failure
body: In pkg/plugins/log/logger.go line 48, grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext asserts d.l.FromContext(ctx) to *log.ConcreteLogger and on failure returns d.New(), a fresh logger with no contextual attributes. That silently discards endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID and uname added by ContextualLoggerMiddleware, with no error or fallback to the original logger. If the infra logger ever returns a different Logger implementation, plugin request logs lose all context invisibly.

title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware panics on nil request
body: ContextualLoggerMiddleware in pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/contextual_logger_middleware.go dereferences req without a nil check, e.g. req.PluginContext in QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics. LoggerMiddleware in the same package explicitly guards with if req == nil, proving nil requests are considered possible. Because CreateMiddlewares orders ContextualLogger outer to Logger, a nil request panics in ContextualLogger before it can reach Logger's guard, crashing the plugin request path instead of passing through.

title: MetricsMiddleware panics on nil request
body: MetricsMiddleware in pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/metrics_middleware.go dereferences req without a nil check, e.g. req.Queries in QueryData and req.PluginContext / req.Body in CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics. LoggerMiddleware guards if req == nil, showing nil is expected. Since MetricsMiddleware is ordered outer to LoggerMiddleware, a nil request causes a nil-pointer panic in metrics code before Logger's guard is reached.

title: Plugin request log loses traceID correlation
body: LoggerMiddleware in pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/logger_middleware.go previously added traceID from tracing.TraceIDFromContext to the Plugin Request Completed log. The PR removes that logic and the replacement instrumentContext in contextual_logger_middleware.go only adds endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID and uname, never traceID. As a result the backend-request log can no longer be correlated to traces, breaking trace-to-log queries and dashboards that relied on the traceID field.

title: TestLogger.FromContext discards log observations
body: TestLogger.FromContext in pkg/plugins/log/fake.go returns a brand-new TestLogger instead of the receiver. LoggerMiddleware now logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info, so with the fake the Info/Warn/Error call is recorded on a throwaway instance while the original instance under test still shows zero Calls. Tests asserting on the injected logger cannot observe the log, causing false negatives and hiding regressions in log content.

title: ContextualLoggerMiddleware panics on nil request
body: ContextualLoggerMiddleware.QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth and CollectMetrics in pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/contextual_logger_middleware.go dereference req (e.g. req.PluginContext) without a nil check. LoggerMiddleware in the same chain explicitly handles req == nil, proving nil requests are expected. Since CreateMiddlewares registers ContextualLoggerMiddleware before LoggerMiddleware, a nil request panics in the outer middleware before it ever reaches the nil guard, crashing the call instead of delegating to next.

title: MetricsMiddleware panics on nil request
body: MetricsMiddleware.QueryData iterates req.Queries and reads req.PluginContext, and CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics read req.PluginContext/req.Body, without checking req == nil. LoggerMiddleware shows nil requests must be tolerated. MetricsMiddleware is outermost in CreateMiddlewares, so a nil request panics here before LoggerMiddleware's nil guard can handle it.

title: TestLogger.FromContext discards logs under test
body: TestLogger.FromContext in pkg/plugins/log/fake.go ignores both receiver and context and returns a brand-new empty TestLogger. LoggerMiddleware now logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), so the Info call is recorded on a temporary object that is immediately discarded. A test that injects NewTestLogger into LoggerMiddleware and asserts on InfoLogs.Calls/Message on the original will always see zero calls, making the middleware untestable and hiding regressions.

title: Adding FromContext breaks Logger implementers
body: Adding FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger to the Logger interface in pkg/plugins/log/ifaces.go breaks every existing implementation of the old 5-method interface. Any out-of-tree mock or custom logger that satisfied the old interface no longer compiles against the new interface. A rename chore should not silently introduce a breaking public-interface change without migration or adapter.

title: FromContext fallback drops contextual attributes
body: grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext in pkg/plugins/log/logger.go type-asserts the infra logger result to *log.ConcreteLogger and on failure returns d.New(), a fresh logger with no context. If the underlying logger returns any other Logger implementation, all contextual attributes added by ContextualLoggerMiddleware (endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname) are silently discarded and Plugin Request Completed logs lose plugin identification. It should preserve the returned logger or the original instead of discarding context.

title: Logger loses plugin fields and traceID
body: LoggerMiddleware in pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/logger_middleware.go no longer logs pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName, dsUID and traceID explicitly and relies solely on m.logger.FromContext(ctx). The context populated by ContextualLoggerMiddleware contains endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname but never adds traceID, and the old explicit tracing.TraceIDFromContext handling was deleted. Plugin Request Completed logs therefore lose trace correlation and depend entirely on an outer middleware being present; used alone they contain no plugin identification.

title: MetricsMiddleware reuses single shared instance
body: NewMetricsMiddleware in pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/metrics_middleware.go creates one MetricsMiddleware once and on each middleware creation does imw.next = next and returns the same pointer. If the middleware decorates more than one client chain, each decoration overwrites the previous chain's next pointer, misrouting requests, and concurrent decoration races. NewContextualLoggerMiddleware in the same PR correctly allocates a new struct per call; MetricsMiddleware should do the same.

title: No test for new contextual logger behavior
body: After the split, pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/metrics_middleware_test.go still defines TestInstrumentationMiddleware testing only counters/histograms, and there are no tests for the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware (context attributes, ordering relative to LoggerMiddleware, nil requests) nor for LoggerMiddleware's new FromContext dependency. A regression that drops plugin context or panics on nil would go undetected.

title: Local cache poisoning lets any new device bypass the device limit on retry
body: tagDeviceUI in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go checks localCache, then calls localCache.SetDefault(key) before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice. When the DB returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the cache entry is already stored and never removed. The next request for the same deviceID hits the cache early-return nil, so TagDevice succeeds and Anonymous.Authenticate succeeds. Any blocked device can therefore get anonymous access by making a second request, and transient DB errors also cause permanent 29-minute under-counting. Fix by caching only after successful DB write or evicting on failure.

title: Count-then-insert race allows exceeding the device limit
body: CreateOrUpdateDevice in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go does CountDevices, then if count < deviceLimit falls through to INSERT. There is no transaction, row lock, or unique count constraint. Two concurrent new devices when count == limit-1 can both observe count < limit and both INSERT different device_ids, ending with limit+1 active devices. Under load, when the limit matters most, it is unenforceable. Fix with atomic guard e.g. serializable transaction, conditional insert, or DB-side enforcement.

title: Anonymous tagging moved from background to synchronous auth hot path
body: Anonymous.Authenticate in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go previously tagged devices in a go routine with context.Background and 2-minute timeout and never blocked login. This PR calls anonDeviceService.TagDevice synchronously with the request ctx, which on cache miss does CountDevices plus INSERT/UPDATE. Every new anonymous login now pays extra DB round-trips and inherits DB slowness/failure, coupling login availability and p99 latency to the anon_device table. Fix by keeping tagging async/off-request or using detached context with timeout for the non-limit path.

title: Provider signature change breaks DI wiring and testability
body: ProvideAnonymousDeviceService in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go changed from taking anonstore.AnonStore to taking db.DB and constructing ProvideAnonDBStore internally with cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit. No wire_gen update is in the PR, so existing generated code passing an AnonStore will fail to compile. It also hard-codes the DB implementation, preventing mocks/fakes or alternate stores. Fix by regenerating wire, or keep injecting AnonStore and inject the limit separately.

title: Unlimited limit sent as 0 mismatches frontend undefined contract
body: FrontendSettingsDTO in pkg/api/dtos/frontend_settings.go adds AnonymousDeviceLimit int64 with json:"anonymousDeviceLimit" and no omitempty, so unlimited (0 in Cfg) serializes as 0. Frontend types declare anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined with default undefined. After lodash merge, 0 overwrites undefined, so UI cannot distinguish unlimited from a zero-device limit if it checks for undefined. Use pointer with omitempty or document that 0 means unlimited on both sides.

title: No test that existing devices can still update when at limit
body: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database_test.go only verifies a second distinct deviceID gets ErrDeviceLimitReached. It never verifies the intended allow-path that an already-counted deviceID can still be updated when count >= limit, nor expiry-window or cache interaction. A regression breaking legitimate returning devices would not be caught. Add a test that re-tags the first device after the limit is reached and expects success and updated timestamp.

title: Cache-before-DB lets blocked devices bypass device limit on retry
body: tagDeviceUI in AnonDeviceService inserts the device CacheKey into localCache before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice, and returns nil immediately on cache hit without touching the DB. When the limit is reached the first TagDevice for a new device returns ErrDeviceLimitReached and denies auth, but the key stays cached. The next request for the same blocked device hits the cache, returns success, and anonymous auth is allowed. The limit therefore only blocks the first request per 29-minute cache window.

title: Count-then-insert race allows exceeding device limit
body: CreateOrUpdateDevice enforces the limit with a separate CountDevices query followed by an INSERT ... ON CONFLICT/ON DUPLICATE KEY if count is below the limit, otherwise an UPDATE. There is no transaction, lock, or unique-count constraint between the check and the insert. Two concurrent requests for different new devices can both observe count below the limit and both insert, permanently exceeding the configured limit.

title: Anonymous auth now blocks synchronously on device tagging with no timeout
body: Authenticate previously tagged the device in a background goroutine with a 2-minute timeout using a detached context, so slow DB never blocked login. This change calls TagDevice synchronously on the request context with no timeout, and TagDevice now does a COUNT plus an upsert when a limit is configured. Every cache-miss anonymous login now pays that DB latency, and a slow or hung DB will stall anonymous authentication instead of being best-effort.

title: No test that existing devices can still update after limit reached
body: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only verifies that a second distinct device is rejected with ErrDeviceLimitReached when the limit is 1. It never verifies the intended allowed path that an already-counted device within the 30-day window can still be updated via updateDevice when the limit is reached. A regression breaking updates for existing devices while blocking new ones would not be caught.

title: Failed device tag stays cached and bypasses limit
body: In pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go tagDeviceUI caches the device key with SetDefault before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice and never evicts on failure. When the device limit is reached the first request returns ErrDeviceLimitReached and client.go blocks auth, but the key remains in localCache for 29 minutes. The next request from the same rejected device hits the cache early-return nil and authenticates successfully. Consequence: the limit blocks only one request per TTL and is effectively unenforced on retry.

title: Count-then-insert race allows exceeding device limit
body: In pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go CreateOrUpdateDevice does CountDevices in one DB session and then INSERT or updateDevice in a second session with no transaction or lock. Concurrent anonymous requests can both observe count < deviceLimit and both insert. Consequence: under concurrent load the stored device count can overshoot the configured limit, so the limit is not strictly enforced.

title: Zero rows affected misclassified as limit reached on MySQL
body: In pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go updateDevice maps rowsAffected==0 to ErrDeviceLimitReached. On MySQL an UPDATE that matches a row but does not change any column values reports 0 rows affected. An existing active device re-tagging with the same IP/user-agent within the same second-precision updated_at will therefore be rejected as over-limit. Consequence: legitimate returning anonymous devices are blocked when the limit is reached.

title: Provider signature change breaks wiring and custom stores
body: In pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go ProvideAnonymousDeviceService was changed from taking anonStore AnonStore to taking sqlStore db.DB and constructing the store internally with cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit, and ProvideAnonDBStore now requires a deviceLimit int64. No wire_gen update is included and callers can no longer inject a custom AnonStore for testing or enterprise overrides. Consequence: existing server wiring and any external caller using the old provider signatures fails to compile.

title: No test that existing device still updates after limit
body: In pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database_test.go TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only checks that a second distinct device gets ErrDeviceLimitReached. It never checks that updating the first existing device after the limit is reached still succeeds via the updateDevice path. Consequence: the core guarantee that returning devices remain allowed to authenticate when the limit is reached is untested and regressions will go unnoticed.

title: Cleanup ticker changed from 10m to 1m without justification
body: pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go line 77 changes the background cleanup ticker from time.Minute*10 to time.Minute*1. This makes all cleanup jobs (snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs, query history) run 10x more often. The PR description only discusses annotation deadlocks and never mentions frequency. This increases DB/CPU load and risks overlapping with the 9-minute cleanup timeout. It looks like a debug leftover and should be reverted.

title: Routine cleanup logs at Error level with full ID lists
body: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go logs normal cleanup progress with r.log.Error at lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576 and 579, including the full ids slice (up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize, e.g. 32767 IDs) and cond on every batch even on success. The err field logged on the fetch path is nil at that point. This will flood error logs, trigger false error alerts/monitors, and pay large serialization cost per batch. These leftover debug logs should be removed or demoted to Debug without dumping all IDs.

title: Unrelated cleanup interval change from 10m to 1m
body: pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go changes the background ticker from time.Minute*10 to time.Minute*1. This runs all cleanup jobs (snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs, query history) 10x more often, increasing DB/CPU load and potentially worsening the MySQL deadlock this PR tries to fix. The PR description never mentions this change, so it looks like leftover debug code and should be reverted.

title: Leftover error-level debug logging with full ID lists
body: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go logs at Error level on every cleanup batch in CleanAnnotations and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags, including the full ids slice (up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize, e.g. 32767 IDs) plus cond and err which is nil on success. This floods error logs with hundreds of KB per batch, triggers error alerts for normal operation, and wastes CPU. These are leftover debug statements and should be removed or demoted to Debug without dumping IDs.

title: Quadratic string building for large SQLite IN clause
body: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go builds the SQLite DELETE IN list with values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v) inside a loop over ids. This copies the growing string on every iteration, giving O(n^2) time and allocations. With batch sizes up to 32767 as in the new test this builds a ~200KB statement by copying gigabytes total, slowing cleanup. Use strings.Builder, strings.Join, or strconv.AppendInt instead.

title: Cleanup ticker interval reduced 10x without justification
body: In pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go line 77 the ticker was changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute. The PR description does not mention this and it is unrelated to the deadlock fix. Consequence: all cleanup jobs (snapshots, versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs, query history) now run 10x as often, increasing DB load 10x and making overlapping runs likely since the job has a 9 minute timeout but fires every minute. Should be reverted.

title: Routine cleanup progress logged at Error level with full ID lists
body: In pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, 579 routine progress ("Annotations to clean by time/count", "cleaned annotations", "Tags to clean") is logged with r.log.Error, including the full ids slice (up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize, e.g. 32767 IDs), cond, and a nil err. Consequence: every cleanup cycle emits Error-level logs with up to hundreds of KB per batch, flooding error logs, triggering false alerts, hiding real errors, and adding CPU/IO cost. Should be Debug and should not log every ID.

title: Split SELECT OFFSET + DELETE can delete annotations that should be retained
body: In pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go CleanAnnotations MaxCount path (around line 549) the code first does SELECT id FROM annotation WHERE <type> ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT batch OFFSET MaxCount in one session, then DELETE FROM annotation WHERE id IN (...) in a separate session. The old single-statement DELETE with subquery was atomic. With concurrent inserts between SELECT and DELETE the ranking shifts: IDs that were beyond MaxCount at SELECT time can be within the newest MaxCount that must be kept at DELETE time, yet they are still deleted. Consequence: recently created annotations that should be retained are incorrectly deleted (data loss). MaxAge path is stable on cutoff time, but MaxCount path is order-unstable.

title: Batched loop stops on zero rows affected instead of empty fetch
body: In pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go untilDoneOrCancelled line 656 stops when affected==0, where affected is RowsAffected from DELETE. If fetchIDs returns N IDs but the subsequent DELETE affects 0 rows due to a concurrent deleter racing the same IDs, the loop exits even though many rows beyond the first LIMIT batch remain unvisited. The correct termination is empty fetch, not zero affected. Consequence: incomplete cleanup that needs extra cycles to drain, and starvation under contention.

title: SQLite ID list built with quadratic string concatenation
body: In pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go line 611 the SQLite fallback builds the IN list with values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v) in a loop over ids. This copies the growing string each iteration, O(n^2). With batch sizes like 32767 exercised in tests this copies hundreds of MB. Consequence: CPU and latency spike during cleanup. Should use strings.Builder.

title: Create storage error recorded as legacy duration
body: In DualWriterMode3.Create, when Storage.Create fails the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage) instead of d.recordStorageDuration. The timed interval is the storage call, not a legacy call, and no legacy call was made. Consequence: storage failures are invisible in storage metrics and falsely inflate legacy error metrics, hiding unified-storage outages.

title: Update storage error recorded as legacy duration
body: In DualWriterMode3.Update, when Storage.Update fails the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage) instead of d.recordStorageDuration. No legacy call occurred on this path. Consequence: same as Create — storage update errors are misattributed to legacy, breaking alerts/dashboards for mode 3.

title: Delete success records object name as kind label
body: In DualWriterMode3.Delete success path the code calls d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage) where name is the object name, while every other call passes options.Kind as the kind label. Consequence: per-object high-cardinality values pollute a Prometheus kind label, causing metric cardinality explosion and useless kind breakdowns.

title: DeleteCollection legacy result recorded as storage duration
body: In DualWriterMode3.DeleteCollection the background goroutine calls d.Legacy.DeleteCollection but then calls d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy) instead of d.recordLegacyDuration. Consequence: legacy delete-collection latency/errors are never observed and are double-counted as storage, so legacy backup failures are invisible.

title: Delete drops structured log values from context
body: In DualWriterMode3.Delete the code builds log := d.Log.WithValues(name, kind, method) but then does ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log) instead of using log. All other methods put the per-request log in the context. Consequence: request-scoped fields for delete are lost from downstream logs, hampering debugging.

title: Async legacy backup inherits cancellable request context
body: Create, Delete, Update and DeleteCollection all do go func() { ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, 10s, ...) ; d.Legacy.*(ctx, ...) } where ctx is the incoming request context. After the API handler returns the request context is cancelled, so the derived context is immediately Done and the 10s timeout does not help. Consequence: legacy backup writes described as a safe measure are routinely cancelled with context canceled, leaving legacy and unified stores diverged.

title: Legacy async write reuses mutable input without copy
body: In Create the code returns created to the caller while a goroutine concurrently reads obj, options and createValidation via d.Legacy.Create(ctx, obj, createValidation, options). Storage implementations commonly mutate obj in place and may alias created, creating a data race. Even without aliasing, legacy gets the pre-storage object without storage-assigned UID/resourceVersion. Update has the same flaw by re-invoking objInfo for legacy instead of reusing the storage result res, so legacy computes a different object from a different old state. Consequence: races/crashes under -race and persistent divergence between stores.

title: Mode3 tests never verify async legacy writes
body: TestMode3_Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection share one mock.Mock between legacy and storage mocks, return immediately without waiting for the background goroutine, and never assert legacy was called. The Create error case even registers the failure on setupLegacyFn while Storage.Create is the call that fails, passing only because the mock is shared. Consequence: a regression that stops the legacy backup write entirely would still pass, and unexpected background calls can panic after the test finishes.

title: Async legacy write derives context from cancelled request context
body: Create (and Delete line 110, Update line 135, DeleteCollection line 163) spawns `go func()` then does `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`, where `ctx` is the incoming request context. The method returns immediately, the apiserver cancels the request context, and any child derived from it is cancelled immediately. The background Legacy.Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection will therefore almost always run with a cancelled parent and fail/timeout, so the legacy copy is never kept in sync despite mode 3 promising best-effort legacy writes. Use a detached context like `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` or `context.Background()` for the async work.

title: Update re-invokes UpdatedObjectInfo for legacy causing divergence
body: Update forwards the same `objInfo` to `Storage.Update` and then asynchronously to `Legacy.Update`. Each store calls `UpdatedObject(ctx, old)` with its own different `old` object. If the transformer is not idempotent or depends on old resourceVersion/spec, the two stores compute different new objects or one fails with conflict. The previous implementation fetched the updated object once and reused it via `updateWrapper` so legacy got the storage result. Legacy should be written with the object returned from storage, not by re-executing user logic against stale legacy state, otherwise storage and legacy diverge.

title: Delete success records object name as kind metric label
body: On successful storage delete the code calls `recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, ...)` where `name` is the object name like `foo`, while the error path and all other methods pass `options.Kind`. The `kind` label will get unbounded high-cardinality values (one series per object name), exploding Prometheus series and breaking dashboards/alerts that expect kind. It should be `options.Kind`.

title: DeleteCollection legacy result recorded as storage metric
body: The background goroutine for DeleteCollection calls `recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...)` for the `Legacy.DeleteCollection` result instead of `recordLegacyDuration`. Legacy latency and errors are attributed to the storage histogram and legacy metrics are never emitted for this method, corrupting SLOs and hiding legacy failures. All other async paths correctly call `recordLegacyDuration`.

title: Create/Update storage errors recorded as legacy metrics
body: When `Storage.Create` fails the code calls `recordLegacyDuration(true, ..., startStorage)` and Update does the same on line 129 for `Storage.Update` failure. A storage failure is counted as a legacy failure with the storage start time, so storage error rate/latency is missing and legacy error rate is inflated. The error paths should call `recordStorageDuration` like Delete and DeleteCollection do.

title: Delete discards per-request logger when installing context
body: Delete builds `log := d.Log.WithValues("name", name, "kind", options.Kind, "method", method)` but then does `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` instead of `log`. Downstream storage calls and any `klog.FromContext` logs lose name/kind/method fields, inconsistent with Create/Get/List/Update/DeleteCollection which install the enriched logger, harming correlation and debugging.

title: Async legacy failures are never logged
body: All four background legacy writes only call `recordLegacyDuration`/`recordStorageDuration` and drop the error. There is no `log.Error` with name/kind/UID. Operators will not see why the legacy safety copy failed in logs, unlike the previous synchronous code which logged legacy errors. At minimum log the async legacy error with identifying fields.

title: Mode3 tests do not verify async legacy dual-write
body: Mode3 write tests return immediately after the synchronous storage call and never wait for the background legacy goroutine (no sleep/Eventually/AssertCalled). Delete and DeleteCollection tests set no legacy expectation at all, and legacy and storage share the same `*mock.Mock` so `Create/Update/Delete` calls cannot be attributed to a store. Tests pass even if legacy is never written (masking the cancelled-context bug above) and are flaky if the goroutine runs after the test finishes and hits an unexpected mock call.

title: Async legacy writes inherit request context and are cancelled
body: Create, Delete, Update and DeleteCollection all do `go func() { ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx,...)` where ctx is the request context. When the handler returns the request context is cancelled, so the child context is immediately cancelled and the async Legacy.Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection fails with context canceled. Mode 3's safety backup to legacy therefore never happens. Fix by detaching with context.WithoutCancel/background plus timeout.

title: Legacy create replicates input object instead of storage result
body: Create returns `created` from Storage but async replication calls `d.Legacy.Create(ctx, obj, ...)` with the original input `obj`. Storage-assigned fields like generated names, UID, resourceVersion and defaults are lost. For generateName creates the two stores will generate different names and diverge, corrupting the legacy backup. Should replicate `created` (deep copy) and not share caller-owned `obj` pointer with an async goroutine.

title: Update re-invokes UpdatedObjectInfo for legacy causing divergent writes
body: Update calls `d.Storage.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)` then asynchronously calls `d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)` with the same objInfo. Each store internally calls `objInfo.UpdatedObject(ctx, old)` with its own old object, so the transformer runs twice against different old objects and can produce different results or resourceVersion conflicts. The old code fetched the updated object once and reused it via updateWrapper for both stores. Reusing objInfo breaks atomic dual-write consistency.

title: Storage duration metric uses object name as kind label
body: Delete success path calls `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, ...)` where `name` is the object name, while all other calls pass `options.Kind`. If the third parameter is the kind label, passing user-controlled object names creates unbounded Prometheus label cardinality and can OOM the metrics system. Should be `options.Kind`.

title: Storage and legacy metrics recorded with wrong function
body: On Storage.Create failure it calls `recordLegacyDuration`, on Storage.Update failure it calls `recordLegacyDuration`, and on async legacy DeleteCollection it calls `recordStorageDuration` instead of `recordLegacyDuration`. Failures are attributed to the wrong store, hiding unified-storage errors and legacy replication errors from dashboards and alerts. Each should record for the store that actually failed.

title: Async legacy failures are never logged
body: All four async legacy branches only call `recordLegacyDuration/recordStorageDuration` and discard the error without `log.Error`. Operators have no log line to diagnose why legacy and unified storage diverged in mode 3, unlike the previous synchronous code that logged. Should log the legacy error with object identity.

title: Delete puts wrong logger in context
body: Delete builds `log := d.Log.WithValues(name, kind, method)` but then does `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` instead of `log`. The enriched fields are dropped from the context while Create/Update/List/DeleteCollection propagate the enriched logger, making Delete logs inconsistent and harder to correlate.

title: Mode3 unit tests do not verify async legacy writes
body: Tests share one `mock.Mock` for both legacy and storage mocks, set up only storage expectations for Delete/DeleteCollection, and return immediately without waiting for the background goroutine. They cannot prove legacy was or was not called, cannot catch panics from missing mock expectations in the goroutine, and pass even if async replication is broken. Need separate mocks plus Eventually/AssertCalled for legacy.

title: Mode3 integration tests assume synchronous legacy consistency
body: The new file/unified mode-3 subtests reuse `doPlaylistTests` which does immediate `getFromBothAPIs` and legacy list checks right after k8s Create/Update. Since mode 3 replicates to legacy asynchronously with up to 10s timeout, the legacy read can race and the test will be flaky or falsely fail. Needs retry/eventual-consistency polling for legacy assertions in mode 3.

title: Exclusive lock held across file and network I/O blocks all readers
body: In pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48 GetWebAssets acquires entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock() with defer Unlock() and then performs disk I/O in readWebAssetsFromFile and potentially network I/O in readWebAssetsFromCDN while still holding the exclusive lock. Consequence is that every concurrent caller, including production fast-path readers that only need RLock to read the already-cached pointer, blocks for the duration of the file read and any HTTP fetch. During cold start this serializes the thundering herd and adds latency spikes; if CDN fetching is enabled a slow network stalls all page renders. The lock should only guard pointer publication: read outside the lock then Lock, re-check, and swap.

title: Missing second cache check after acquiring write lock causes redundant reloads
body: In pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:45-48 GetWebAssets implements double-checked locking incorrectly: it checks entryPointAssetsCache under RLock, releases it, then takes the write Lock without re-checking. If two goroutines both observe nil (cold start) or race a Dev/Prod transition, both will sequentially execute readWebAssetsFromFile and the second overwrites the first. Consequence is N expensive manifest parses and file reads instead of one, plus possible inconsistency if the file changes between reads. After acquiring the write lock it should re-check if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil and return early.

title: Missing second cache check after acquiring write lock causes thundering herd
body: GetWebAssets does a fast-path check under RLock and if it misses acquires entryPointAssetsCacheMu in write mode, but it never re-checks entryPointAssetsCache after acquiring the write lock. If N goroutines concurrently observe a nil cache before the first load finishes, each will queue on the write lock and each will re-read assets-manifest.json/CDN and overwrite the global. The consequence is redundant disk/network I/O on cold start, wasted work, and different callers getting different pointers when one shared load would suffice.

title: Exclusive lock held across file and network I/O blocks all readers
body: GetWebAssets acquires entryPointAssetsCacheMu with Lock and defers Unlock, so the exclusive lock is held across readWebAssetsFromFile and readWebAssetsFromCDN, which perform file-system reads and HTTP fetches plus GetContentDeliveryURL. While the writer holds the lock, every other caller blocks even for RLock fast-path cache hits. In Dev mode every call takes the write lock, so concurrent requests fully serialize on disk I/O. This adds latency and contention; the load should happen outside the lock with a second check/singleflight and the lock held only to publish the result.

title: Failed load overwrites good cache with nil
body: GetWebAssets unconditionally executes entryPointAssetsCache = result even when the load failed and result is nil with err non-nil. In Dev mode the read bypasses the cache but the write still overwrites it, so one transient failure reading assets-manifest.json discards the previously good cached EntryPointAssets shared by all goroutines. Subsequent callers then see a nil cache and fail or must reload until a later success. The global should only be updated on success (err == nil and result != nil) to preserve the last good value.

title: Missing second cache check after acquiring write lock
body: In pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go GetWebAssets does double-checked locking: it takes RLock to snapshot entryPointAssetsCache, releases it, then takes Lock to rebuild. After acquiring the write Lock it never re-checks entryPointAssetsCache. If two goroutines both miss the fast path, both will do file/CDN I/O serially and the second will discard/replace the first's result. This wastes work and lets a slow or failing second loader clobber a good value just installed by the first. Re-check if cache became non-nil (in non-Dev mode) after acquiring the write lock and return it without reloading.

title: Failed load overwrites good cached assets with nil
body: In pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go GetWebAssets unconditionally does entryPointAssetsCache = result at the end, even when readWebAssetsFromFile/CDN failed and result is nil with non-nil err. Combined with concurrent cache misses, a goroutine that succeeds and caches good assets can have its value immediately replaced with nil by another in-flight loader that fails. Subsequent callers then see a miss and must reload/fail. Only assign the global when err == nil and result != nil, preserving the last good value on error.

title: Exclusive lock held across file and network I/O blocks all readers
body: In pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go GetWebAssets acquires entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock() with defer Unlock() before calling readWebAssetsFromFile and readWebAssetsFromCDN, which do filesystem reads and HTTP fetches. While that I/O is in flight, every other caller blocks in RLock on the fast path or Lock on the slow path, so the RWMutex provides no read concurrency and one slow disk/CDN stall stalls all asset lookups. Load into a local variable outside the lock (with double-check/singleflight) and only hold the lock briefly to publish the result.

title: Empty SQL result never returns NoData, always overwritten with TableData
body: In pkg/expr/sql_command.go Execute() sets rsp.Values to mathexp.NoData when frame.Rows()==0 and then unconditionally overwrites rsp.Values with mathexp.TableData on the next lines. The NoData assignment is dead code and never observed by callers. Consequence: downstream no-data/alerting logic that distinguishes NoData from TableData will misclassify empty SQL results as data tables.

title: tablesFromAST indexes ast[0] without empty check causing panic
body: In pkg/expr/sql/parser.go tablesFromAST() does flatten.Flatten(ast[0], ...) without checking len(ast) > 0. If the unmarshalled JSON is an empty array, null, or otherwise yields zero elements, this panics with index out of range. Consequence: a crafted SQL expression that produces such JSON crashes the handler/goroutine, a denial-of-service robustness bug that should be a returned error instead.

title: enableSqlExpressions has inverted check and always returns false via dead branches
body: In pkg/expr/reader.go enableSqlExpressions() computes enabled as negation of FlagSqlExpressions then returns false in both the if branch and fallthrough. The flag check is dead code and the negation obscures intent. Consequence: the disable looks like a logic mistake, inviting a future cleanup to flip one return to true and silently re-enable the DuckDB RCE/LFI path fixed for CVE-2024-9264; it should be an unconditional false with an explicit security comment.

title: Security disable of SQL expressions has no regression test
body: This PR disables SQL expressions to fix critical RCE/LFI CVE-2024-9264 by gating pkg/expr/reader.go ReadQuery for QueryTypeSQL and stubbing pkg/expr/sql DB, but adds no test verifying that ReadQuery, NewSQLCommand/TablesList, and Execute reject SQL input even when FlagSqlExpressions is enabled. Consequence: a one-line future change to the stub or gate can silently reintroduce remote code execution/file access with no automated guard.

title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false with inverted dead logic
body: In pkg/expr/reader.go enableSqlExpressions computes enabled as !IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions) and then returns false in both the if-branch and the fall-through, so it always denies. The negation is backwards and the branch is dead code. The intent to unconditionally disable SQL is achieved, but the confusing logic invites a future cleanup to return enabled, which would silently re-enable DuckDB SQL expressions and reintroduce the CVE-2024-9264 RCE/LFI. Simplify to an unconditional return false with a comment explaining the intentional security disable.

title: Legacy UnmarshalSQLCommand path not explicitly disabled
body: In pkg/expr/sql_command.go UnmarshalSQLCommand parses the expression and calls NewSQLCommand with no disabled check, while pkg/expr/reader.go ReadQuery explicitly rejects QueryTypeSQL. The legacy rawNode path is therefore only blocked incidentally because the stubbed sql.TablesList always returns not implemented. Relying on incidental DB failure instead of an explicit deny means restoring a real DB implementation or changing error handling silently re-exposes DuckDB execution and the RCE/LFI vulnerability. Both entry points must explicitly reject SQL expressions.

title: TablesList still attempts DuckDB json_serialize_sql instead of hard-failing
body: In pkg/expr/sql/parser.go TablesList still builds SELECT json_serialize_sql('...') with strings.Replace quote doubling and fmt.Sprintf and calls RunCommands. With the current stub it fails, but the vulnerable DuckDB-specific code path and injection-prone string interpolation are preserved. If the stub is ever replaced with a real DuckDB connection the RCE/LFI returns. TablesList should return an explicit disabled error immediately without constructing or executing any SQL.

title: No regression test that SQL stays disabled regardless of flag
body: In pkg/expr/reader.go the QueryTypeSQL case is now supposed to always fail, but the PR adds no automated test verifying rejection via ReadQuery and via the legacy UnmarshalSQLCommand path with FlagSqlExpressions both on and off. Without a regression test a later refactor can accidentally re-enable DuckDB SQL execution and reintroduce RCE/LFI without detection. Add tests asserting an explicit disabled error in all flag states.

title: Concurrent index init has data races on counter and error
body: In searchSupport.init each errgroup worker runs `totalBatchesIndexed++` and `_, _, err = s.build(...)` where both variables are shared across workers without synchronization. Concurrent increments lose counts and concurrent assignments to the outer err race, so one worker can overwrite another's error before it is returned and the race detector will flag it. Use a local err variable inside the closure and an atomic counter.

title: TotalDocs reads cache map without lock
body: bleveBackend.TotalDocs iterates `b.cache` with no lock while BuildIndex writes `b.cache[key] = idx` under cacheMu and GetIndex reads under RLock. Concurrent map read and write is a data race that can panic at runtime. The PR makes concurrent builds expected, and the search watch goroutine can trigger builds concurrent with the TotalDocs call in init.

title: Removing global BuildIndex lock allows duplicate builds for same key
body: BuildIndex previously held cacheMu for the whole build; now it only locks for the final map insert. Two concurrent getOrCreateIndex calls for the same NamespacedResource can both see GetIndex return nil, both build separate bleve indexes, and last-writer-wins. This wastes work, double-increments IndexTenants metrics, leaks the loser's index, and for file-backed indexes both call bleve.New on the same directory so one fails.

title: Search watch loop uses uncanceled Background context and ignores close
body: searchSupport.init creates watchctx as context.Background with no cancel and loops `for { v := <-events; handleEvent(watchctx, v) }` without checking channel closure. The goroutine never exits on server Stop, leaking forever, and when the backend closes the channel the loop spins on zero values and handleEvent dereferences a nil event and panics.

title: Broadcaster pipe ignores channel close and cancellation
body: server.initWatcher starts a goroutine doing `v := <-events` without checking ok, then logs v.Type, stores v.ResourceVersion and blocks on `out <- v` with no select on context. When the storage backend closes the stream the loop receives nil forever and panics on dereference, and if the broadcaster stops the send blocks forever and leaks the goroutine.

title: Eager Init leaks cancel and blocks startup with no timeout
body: NewResourceServer creates a cancelable server context then calls s.Init synchronously. On Init failure it returns nil and error without calling cancel, leaking the context. More broadly the long synchronous search-index build now blocks module startup; transient DB or index errors that previously surfaced on first RPC now prevent the whole server from being constructed.

title: History and Origin panic when search is disabled
body: When Search.Resources is nil, s.search stays nil. server.Search checks for nil and returns an error, but server.History and server.Origin directly call s.search.History and s.search.Origin with no guard, causing a nil pointer dereference panic instead of an error.

title: Trace context still discarded on write path
body: WriteEvent and create/update/delete still do `_, span := tracer.Start` and pass the original context to children, so child spans become siblings of the parent instead of children. Only GetResourceStats was fixed to `ctx, span`, leaving the main write and read trace hierarchy broken despite the PR claiming to fix propagation.

title: Skipping postgres integration test hides regressions
body: The change adds a skip for the storage-server instrumentation test when GRAFANA_TEST_DB is postgres with only a TODO. Unified storage behavior is dialect dependent, so skipping removes coverage for the exact startup and init path this PR changes without a linked issue or alternative coverage.

title: Data race on shared counter and error in parallel index init
body: In searchSupport.init the errgroup goroutine does totalBatchesIndexed++ and _, _, err = s.build(...) where totalBatchesIndexed and err are outer variables shared by all workers. With initWorkers > 1 this is concurrent unsynchronized read-modify-write and concurrent writes to the same err variable. It triggers the race detector, corrupts the indexed count reported in the span, and can lose or overwrite build errors so group.Wait returns the wrong error.

title: TotalDocs iterates cache map without lock while builds write concurrently
body: bleveBackend.BuildIndex now only holds cacheMu for the final cache insert so many builds run in parallel, and GetIndex uses RLock. TotalDocs loops over b.cache with no lock at all. Concurrent iteration with concurrent map writes is a data race and can panic with concurrent map iteration and map write. It is called at the end of init and can run concurrently with on-demand builds from Search or watch events.

title: Search watch goroutine leaks and panics on closed channel
body: searchSupport.init creates watchctx as context.Background with a comment new context and then runs for { v := <-events; s.handleEvent(watchctx, v) } with no ok check and no exit on cancellation. When the sql backend poller exits it closes the channel, so receives return nil forever. handleEvent dereferences evt.Type and evt.Key and will panic on nil, otherwise it busy-loops. The Background context is never cancelled so the goroutine also leaks on shutdown and loses tracing and admin claims.

title: Stop shutdown guard is dead after removing lazy Init checks
body: server.Stop sets s.initErr to service is stopping/stopped to make future calls fail. Previously every RPC called s.Init which returned that stored error. This PR removes all Init calls from Create, Update, Delete, Read, List, Watch, Search, History, Origin, IsHealthy, PutBlob and GetBlob. Nothing now reads the value written by Stop, so the server keeps serving new requests after Stop instead of rejecting them, breaking graceful shutdown.

title: Check-then-act race allows duplicate builds for same index
body: getOrCreateIndex does GetIndex and if nil calls build without per-key singleflight. Previously bleve BuildIndex held a global lock for the whole build so duplicates were serialized. Now it only locks the final map insert. Two goroutines for the same NamespacedResource from parallel init, Search, or watch handling can both see nil and both run ListIterator plus bleve.New. This wastes work, double-increments IndexTenants and IndexedKinds metrics, leaks the loser index with last-writer-wins, and for file-backed indexes concurrently creates the same directory which fails with index already exists or lock contention.

title: Eager Init blocks NewResourceServer on full index build
body: NewResourceServer now calls s.Init synchronously, which runs lifecycle init plus full search index build over all namespaces before returning. The PR description says the build takes too long for a gRPC context. Doing it synchronously in the constructor moves the same long blocking work to startup, delaying readiness and risking startup timeouts. On error it returns nil without calling the cancel func for the internal context, leaking that context.

title: Trace context still discarded in bleve BuildIndex
body: The PR claims to fix trace propagation by keeping the Start context, and search.go and GetResourceStats were changed to ctx, span. bleveBackend.BuildIndex still does _, span := tracer.Start and discards the child context, so the builder callback and ListIterator inside the build are not children of the BuildIndex span. The same pattern remains in sql backend WriteEvent, ReadResource and ListIterator, so propagation is only partially fixed.

title: Postgres storage-server test skipped instead of fixed
body: The change adds a skip for GRAFANA_TEST_DB=postgres in TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer with a TODO. This removes integration coverage for the storage server target on postgres, so regressions in the unified storage startup path on postgres will not be caught in CI.

title: Data races on shared err and counter in concurrent init
body: In pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go init() launches one errgroup goroutine per namespace stat. Each goroutine does totalBatchesIndexed++ and _, _, err = s.build(...) where err is the outer variable from stats, err := GetResourceStats and totalBatchesIndexed is a plain int shared by all workers. With initWorkers > 1 this is concurrent unsynchronized read-modify-write on the same variables while the parent is blocked in group.Wait() and then reassigns err. This is a data race that corrupts the count, loses build errors, and trips the race detector.

title: Removing BuildIndex lock allows duplicate builds for same key
body: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go BuildIndex() previously held cacheMu for the whole build and now only locks around b.cache[key] = idx. GetIndex() only takes RLock and returns nil while a build is in flight, so concurrent init workers or concurrent Search-triggered getOrCreateIndex() for the same NamespacedResource will both run bleve.New(), both run the ListIterator builder, both increment IndexTenants, and both write the same file directory for file-backed indexes. The loser is leaked without Close and bleve file creation on the same path can fail with index-exists/lock errors. A coarse lock was slow but correct; the fix needs per-key singleflight, not no lock.

title: TotalDocs reads cache map without lock
body: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go TotalDocs() iterates for _, v := range b.cache with no cacheMu held while BuildIndex() concurrently does b.cache[key] = idx under Lock. In Go concurrent map read and write is a fatal runtime panic, not just a race. With builds now parallelized the window is large, and any concurrent metrics/logging call to TotalDocs during a lazy getOrCreateIndex build can crash the storage server.

title: Watch goroutine never exits and panics on closed channel
body: In pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go init() starts watchctx := context.Background() and go func() { for { v := <-events; s.handleEvent(watchctx, v) } } with no ok check and no Done handling. The sql backend poller does defer close(stream) on shutdown. After close, receive returns nil forever in a hot loop and handleEvent dereferences evt.Type on nil, causing nil panic and CPU spin. The goroutine also uses a Background context that is never cancelled on server Stop, so it leaks even on clean shutdown. It must watch server context Done and break on !ok.

title: History/Origin panic when search not configured
body: In pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go Search() checks if s.search == nil and returns an error, but History() and Origin() unconditionally do s.search.History/Origin. When SearchOptions.Resources is nil, newSearchSupport is skipped and s.search stays nil, which is a valid configuration. Any gRPC History or Origin call then nil-pointer panics and crashes the server instead of returning search-not-configured.

title: Synchronous full reindex in constructor blocks startup
body: In pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go NewResourceServer() now calls s.Init(ctx) synchronously, where ctx is the server-lifetime Background context. Init builds every search index via ListIterator over all namespaces before returning. Construction therefore blocks from milliseconds to minutes with no timeout and no way for the caller to cancel, delaying module readiness/health and making any index failure fatal to server creation. Previously reads/writes blocked only on first use; now nothing can start serving until all indexes finish.

title: Skipping postgres storage-server test hides init regression
body: In pkg/server/module_server_test.go the change adds a skip for postgres for TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer. This test exercises storage-server startup, which is exactly what the PR changes from lazy to eager init with DB-dependent GetResourceStats/ListIterator/watch polling. Skipping it means the new startup path is never validated on postgres in CI, so postgres-specific init hangs or failures will not be caught.

title: Call to undefined zero-arg method breaks compilation
body: UsernameForm.authenticate calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only definition in parent UsernamePasswordForm is protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user). There is no zero-arg overload, so the code does not compile and the project cannot build. The call should pass the current user, e.g. isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()).

title: Conditional passkeys never initialized for anonymous first login
body: New helper isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) returns webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null. It is used in authenticate and in challenge(error,field) to decide whether to call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm. When no user is selected yet (initial login, context.getUser()==null) it is always false, so no WebAuthn challenge or ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI attribute is set. Previously the code filled the form when the user was null. Tests still expect //form[@id='webauth'] on the initial page, so initial conditional-UI passkey login is broken while re-authentication is fixed.

title: Call to undefined zero-arg method breaks compilation
body: UsernameForm.authenticate calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only definition in the hierarchy is UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) which requires one argument. There is no zero-arg overload, so the changed file does not compile. The intended call was likely isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()). Until fixed the module cannot build.

title: Conditional passkeys disabled for anonymous first login
body: New helper isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, and both authenticate and challenge(error,field) only call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm when it returns true. Previously authenticate filled WebAuthn conditional-UI data when the user was not yet selected (anonymous first login) and challenge did the same when context.getUser()==null. After the change anonymous logins with user==null never set challenge, rpId, or ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI, so the login page loses the webauthn form, username autocomplete, and discoverable passkey login. The correct condition for initializing conditional UI should not require a known user; it should be enabled for both first login and re-authentication.

title: Only one of two display hooks disabled for conditional UI
body: WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm uses shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators to decide whether to populate ALLOWED_AUTHENTICATORS and separately uses shouldDisplayAuthenticators to set SHOULD_DISPLAY_AUTHENTICATORS. The subclass overrides only shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators to return false, leaving shouldDisplayAuthenticators returning true whenever context.getUser()!=null. During re-authentication the form is therefore told to display authenticators while no authenticator list is provided, causing an empty/mismatched UI section instead of fully hiding it as the comment intends.

title: Call to zero-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not compile
body: UsernameForm.java line 47 calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments. The only definition in the superclass UsernamePasswordForm takes a UserModel argument: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user). There is no zero-arg overload in the changed files, so the module does not compile and the whole PR cannot be built or merged.

title: Conditional passkeys disabled for initial userless login
body: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) returns webauthnAuth != null && isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null. Both call sites in UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate and UsernamePasswordForm.challenge now only call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm when this returns true, i.e. only when context.getUser() != null. The old code filled the form when the user was null to enable usernameless discoverable-key login with conditional UI autofill. After the change the first login page and its error page never get a WebAuthn challenge or conditional-UI flag, so passkey autofill on initial login is broken.

title: Re-auth forces username form for all users when passkeys enabled
body: Once fixed to pass the user, the guard context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(...) is true for any non-null user whenever the realm has passkeys enabled, because isConditionalPasskeysEnabled only checks feature flag, realm policy and user != null, not whether that user has a passkey credential. Password-only users without passkeys who previously skipped the username step on re-authentication via context.success() will now always be shown the username form and forced to re-enter their username.

title: getForLogin cache ignores organization invalidation and goes stale on org disable/remove
body: In InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin only the per-mode login key is checked for invalidation. In contrast getByOrganization checks both its own key and the organization id, so organization updates evict org queries. Nothing in the change invalidates the login keys when only organization state changes (disable/enable, remove) and getForLogin never consults organization invalidation. A cached login entry therefore keeps internal ids of brokers from an organization that was later disabled or deleted, resolving them via getById still succeeds, so getForLogin keeps returning brokers that no longer qualify for login. The added isEnabled re-check in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean only fixes the login page, other callers of getForLogin still get stale results and users can be offered brokers from disabled organizations.

title: Cleanup uses literal "alias" so created test IDPs are never removed
body: In OrganizationCacheTest the cleanup hook uses the literal string "alias" instead of the loop variable, for example get("alias")::remove while the created broker is "org-idp-"+i or "idp-alias-"+i. Removing alias "alias" finds nothing, so the 10 org-idp brokers and the 20+1 idp-alias brokers are never deleted. Leftovers remain in the test realm and are counted by later assertions that expect exact sizes like 5, 10 or 11, making the tests order-dependent and flaky and leaking state to other organization tests. The same literal appears at three places in the new test.

title: update() uses organization-aware wrapper for login invalidation, missing invalidations when org disabled
body: update() loads the original with getById(), which returns an organization-aware wrapper whose isEnabled() is false when its organization is disabled. registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate() decides with getLoginPredicate() which includes isEnabled(), so for an IdP in a disabled org both original and updated test as non-login. Changes to hideOnLogin, linkOnly or brokerPublic while the org is disabled therefore skip invalidation, leaving stale internalIds in the .idp.login caches. After the org is re-enabled OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean only re-checks isEnabled(), so a now-hidden, link-only or non-public broker from the stale list is displayed on the login page.

title: Generic login paths re-check only isEnabled, allowing stale hidden brokers to show
body: The specific-organization branch filters organization brokers by isEnabled() and !isLinkOnly() and !isHideOnLogin() and brokerPublic. The ORG_ONLY-without-org and ALL branches that use cached getForLogin() filter only by isEnabled(). If the login cache is stale or racy for hideOnLogin, linkOnly or brokerPublic, those stale IdPs remain in the cached id set, resolve successfully via getById(), pass the isEnabled() check, and are rendered on the login page when they should be hidden.

title: Test cleanup uses literal "alias" instead of created alias, leaking IdPs
body: The new test creates idp-alias-0..20 in a loop but registers cleanup as testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove with the literal string "alias" instead of the loop variable. That cleanup removes nothing, so 20+ brokers remain in the realm. Leftover brokers pollute counts asserted in the same test (5/6/10/11) and any later tests using the realm, causing flakiness. Same pattern appears for org-idp creation and idp-alias-20.

title: removeAll() does not invalidate login caches
body: removeAll() only registers invalidation for the count key and delegates, leaving realm .idp.login.* entries and org-id list queries in the cache. If removeAll() is ever called without deleting the realm, subsequent getForLogin() returns deleted brokers. It should invalidate login keys the same way create/remove do.

title: Test cleanup removes wrong alias, leaking IDPs
body: In testCacheIDPByOrg and testCacheIDPForLogin the test creates IDPs in a loop with variable alias (e.g. "org-idp-"+i / "idp-alias-"+i) but registers cleanup as testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove with the literal string "alias". That cleanup tries to delete a non-existent IDP named "alias" and never deletes the 10-20 IDPs actually created. The same wrong literal is repeated at lines 381 and 425. Consequence: created brokers leak into the test realm, pollute counts for later assertions on cached login/org queries, and make the suite order-dependent and flaky.

title: update/remove dereferences null IDP model causing NPE
body: update() does IdentityProviderModel idpById = getById(model.getInternalId()) which returns null when the id is null or not found, then unconditionally calls registerIDPInvalidation(idpById) which calls idp.getInternalId() and idp.getAlias(). remove() has the same pattern with storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) followed by registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp) when the alias key is invalidated. If the alias/id does not exist, storedIdp/idpById is null and the call throws NullPointerException. Consequence: updating or removing a missing broker fails with a 500 NPE instead of returning false / proper not-found handling.

title: getForLogin ignores organization invalidations and serves stale brokers
body: getByOrganization bypasses cache when isInvalid(cacheKey) || isInvalid(orgId), but the new getForLogin only checks if (isInvalid(cacheKey)). getForLogin results depend on organization state: which orgs exist/are enabled and which IDPs are linked to a given orgId (searchKey is organizationId). When an organization is updated, disabled, or removed its orgId is invalidated but the login query objects keyed by realm+FetchMode are not considered invalid. Subsequent getForLogin calls therefore hit the stale IdentityProviderListQuery and return ID sets containing brokers from disabled/removed orgs or missing newly linked/unlinked brokers. The added isEnabled re-check in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean only patches two UI branches, not the provider contract, so direct callers of getForLogin get stale login options.

title: New abstract order() breaks external CryptoProvider implementations
body: In common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoProvider.java:44 the interface adds abstract `int order()` with no default. CryptoProvider is a ServiceLoader SPI that third parties can implement outside this repo. Adding an abstract method breaks source and binary compatibility: existing custom providers fail to compile and fail at runtime with AbstractMethodError when loaded. The fix is to provide a default, e.g. `default int order() { return 0; }`, so old implementations keep working and the new AuthzClientCryptoProvider (order 100) still loses to built-ins (order 200).

title: Multiple crypto providers silently resolved instead of failing, tie is nondeterministic
body: In common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java:56 detectProvider now sorts by order() reversed and returns the first, only logging ignored providers at debug. Previously >1 providers threw IllegalStateException. All built-ins DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider now return order 200, so a misconfigured classpath with both FIPS and non-FIPS has a tie resolved by ServiceLoader iteration order, which is undefined. Consequence is silent use of the wrong crypto stack, e.g. running non-FIPS while FIPS compliance was expected, with no visible warning. Should at least throw on equal top orders or log at warn.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns wrong JCA provider
body: In authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:61 getBouncyCastleProvider() returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, typically SUN/JKS, not a BouncyCastle provider. The contract is to return the BouncyCastle provider, and WildFlyElytronProvider returns null when there is none. Callers that use this to select BC algorithms, register the provider, or check provider ID will get SUN behavior or mis-identify the stack, causing subtle crypto failures. Should return null or throw UnsupportedOperationException like the other unimplemented methods.

title: ECDSA DER-to-raw conversion silently truncates oversized/negative integers
body: In authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:151 integerToBytes() does `if (qLength < bytes.length) copy last qLength bytes` with no validation. A DER INTEGER for P-256 (qLength 32) that is 34 bytes long, or a negative INTEGER that new BigInteger(bytes) accepts as signed, is truncated to the low bytes instead of rejected. Only the case bytes.length==qLength+1 with leading 0x00 is valid; larger values or negative values must throw IOException. Silent wrapping maps an invalid attacker-supplied signature to a different valid-looking raw R/S pair, enabling signature malleability and bypass of strict DER checks.

title: Missing validation of raw ECDSA signature length
body: In authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:103 concatenatedRSToASN1DER(byte[] signature, int signLength) assumes signature.length==signLength and signLength even without checking, then does System.arraycopy with len=signLength/2. A short buffer throws raw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of IOException/IllegalArgumentException, and a long buffer silently ignores trailing bytes. This produces confusing errors and can hide caller bugs where e.g. a P-521 signature is passed with ES256 length. Must validate signLength>0, even, expected (64/96/132) and signature.length==signLength.

title: ASN.1 SEQUENCE parser does not enforce exact length and accepts non-DER
body: In authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/ASN1Decoder.java:49 readSequence() loops `while(length>0){length-=bytes.length;}` with no check that final length==0 and no check for trailing bytes, and readLength() returns -1 for indefinite-length 0x80 instead of rejecting. A parent length smaller than the children sum goes negative and is still accepted if 2 elements were read, and extra bytes after the SEQUENCE are ignored. DER requires definite lengths and exact consumption. Consequence is acceptance of malformed/non-canonical ECDSA signatures, signature malleability and interop differences versus BouncyCastle/JCA strict parsers.

title: ECDSA test reuses one P-256 key and only checks round-trip
body: In authz/client/src/test/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/test/ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java:46 the helper generates one EC KeyPair with default curve (P-256) and reuses it for ES256/ES384/ES512, then only asserts decode(encode(decode(sign))) equals decode(sign). It never verifies the DER with Signature.verify nor compares raw/DER against a reference implementation or fixed vectors. A systematically wrong encoder/decoder that is self-consistent still passes, and real 48/66-byte component sizes are never exercised. Should generate P-256/P-384/P-521 keys per algorithm and verify signatures end-to-end.

title: New abstract order() breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: CryptoProvider added abstract method int order() with no default implementation. Any out-of-tree custom CryptoProvider compiled against the old interface will fail at runtime with AbstractMethodError when CryptoIntegration sorts by CryptoProvider::order, and will fail to compile against the new interface. As a public SPI this is a binary and source incompatible change. It should be a default method returning a sensible default.

title: Equal-order providers selected nondeterministically, losing fail-fast
body: Previously multiple CryptoProviders on the classpath threw IllegalStateException. Now providers are sorted by order() reversed and the first is silently used, with others only logged at debug. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return 200, so if any two are present the winner depends on ServiceLoader iteration order which is classpath order dependent. This can silently swap FIPS for non-FIPS or vice versa with no warning, violating compliance expectations and hiding misconfiguration.
