title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns default KeyStore provider instead of BouncyCastle
body: The method contract is to return the BouncyCastle security provider, but the implementation returns KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider(), which on a standard JDK is SUN or SunJSSE, not BouncyCastle. Callers expecting BouncyCastle-specific behavior will get the wrong provider. WildFlyElytronProvider returns null when there is no BouncyCastle provider; this implementation should do the same or throw UnsupportedOperationException instead of returning a misleading provider.

title: ECDSA integer conversion silently truncates oversized and negative values
body: asn1derToConcatenatedRS decodes r/s with new BigInteger(bytes) which accepts negative integers, then integerToBytes truncates to qLength by copying the last qLength bytes without checking the dropped bytes. A DER value larger than the curve size or negative will be silently truncated to a different valid-looking value instead of throwing IOException. This masks invalid signatures, accepts non-canonical encodings, and can cause incorrect verification decisions. Dropped bytes must be verified to be zero and negatives rejected.

title: readSequence does not enforce exact length and ignores trailing data
body: readSequence loops while length > 0 subtracting each element size but never checks that length ends at exactly zero and never checks that no bytes remain after the sequence. An inner element that overruns the declared outer length makes length negative and the loop exits successfully, and trailing garbage after the sequence is ignored. DER signature parsing must be strict and reject overlong, short, or trailing-data encodings to avoid malleability.

title: concatenatedRSToASN1DER lacks length validation and throws AIOOBE
body: The method assumes the input signature length equals signLength and immediately does System.arraycopy with len = signLength/2 without validation. A caller passing a truncated, overlong, or odd signLength gets ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of the declared IOException, and odd lengths are silently mishandled by integer division. It should validate signature != null, signature.length == signLength, and signLength even, and throw IOException otherwise.

title: Test reuses P-256 key for ES384/ES512 and never verifies signature
body: The test generates one EC key pair with the default curve, typically P-256, and reuses it for ES256, ES384 and ES512 while only varying the target concatenated length. For ES384 and ES512 the conversion just zero-pads, so the round-trip assert passes without exercising real P-384 or P-521 sizes. It also only checks round-trip equality and never calls Signature.verify on the re-encoded DER, so a conversion that produces cryptographically invalid DER would still pass.

title: New abstract order() breaks external CryptoProvider implementations
body: In common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoProvider.java line 44 the interface adds abstract method int order(). Any third-party CryptoProvider implementation compiled against the old interface will fail at runtime with AbstractMethodError/NoSuchMethodError and will fail to compile against the new interface. This is a binary and source incompatible change. It should be a default method e.g. default int order() { return 0; } to preserve compatibility.

title: Same order for all server providers makes selection nondeterministic
body: In common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java line 57 detectProvider sorts by order reversed and picks element 0. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return 200, AuthzClientCryptoProvider returns 100. For equal order ServiceLoader order is classpath dependent, so a classpath containing both FIPS and non-FIPS/default providers now silently picks an arbitrary one instead of failing fast as before. Previously multiple providers threw IllegalStateException. Silently picking non-FIPS when FIPS is required (or vice versa) is a compliance and security failure and masks misconfiguration.

title: readSequence does not enforce exact length match
body: In authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/ASN1Decoder.java line 57 readSequence loops while(length>0) subtracting each child TLV length from the declared SEQUENCE content length but never checks that the remainder is exactly zero. If children total more than declared, length goes negative and the loop exits silently returning e.g. 2 elements. Malformed DER with trailing/mismatched lengths is accepted as valid instead of throwing IOException, which can cause invalid ECDSA signatures to be accepted by asn1derToConcatenatedRS.

title: integerToBytes silently mangles negative and oversized integers
body: In authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java line 151 integerToBytes converts DER INTEGER BigInteger to fixed-length bytes by truncating leading bytes if too long and zero-padding if too short. It does not reject negative values or values >= 2^(8*qLength). E.g. DER -1 (bytes 0xFF) becomes 32 bytes of 0x00..FF (255), and an oversized r/s is truncated to low bytes. Invalid out-of-range signature values are thus transformed into different in-range values instead of throwing IOException, hiding malformed signatures and enabling signature malleability.

title: concatenatedRSToASN1DER lacks input length validation
body: In authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java line 103 concatenatedRSToASN1DER splits signature into r/s with len=signLength/2 and System.arraycopy without checking signature.length==signLength. A short or long input throws unchecked ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of declared IOException, and odd signLength silently drops a byte. Callers expecting IOException handling will get unexpected runtime exceptions.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns non-BouncyCastle provider
body: In authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java line 61 getBouncyCastleProvider contract states it returns the BouncyCastle security provider (FIPS or non-FIPS). Implementation returns KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider(), typically SUN or SunJSSE, not BouncyCastle. Callers using the returned Provider for BC-specific algorithms will get wrong behavior or NoSuchAlgorithmException. Like WildFlyElytronProvider it should return null when BC is not used.

title: AuthzClient.create poisons global CryptoIntegration singleton
body: In authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/AuthzClient.java line 95 create() calls CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader()). CryptoIntegration holds a static volatile singleton initialized only once and never re-evaluated for a different ClassLoader. If authz-client initializes first with a ClassLoader that only sees the fallback AuthzClientCryptoProvider (order 100), a later server init that could see Default/FIPS/Elytron (order 200) is ignored. In modular runtimes where visibility differs per loader this permanently locks in the weak provider and breaks server crypto.

title: Test reuses P-256 key for ES384/ES512 and only checks round-trip
body: In authz/client/src/test/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/test/ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java line 42 a single KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair() (default P-256) is reused for ES256 (64 bytes), ES384 (96 bytes) and ES512 (132 bytes). Signing P-256 keys with SHA384/SHA512 still yields P-256 sized DER that is zero-padded to larger lengths, so the test passes without exercising real P-384/P-521 sizes. The test also only asserts asn1->concat->asn1 round-trip equality and never verifies with Signature.verify or known vectors, so truncation, leading-zero and negative-value bugs are not detected.

title: init() never adds Clients scopes/resources to existing realms
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns immediately if realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() already exists. Realms created before the Clients type existed therefore never get the new scopes (configure, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite, etc.) or the 'Clients' all-resource. Creating a Clients scope permission on such a realm then fails in getOrCreateResource with ModelException No scopes found, and global Clients checks return false. Init must be idempotent and add missing scopes/resources on upgrade.

title: NPE when all-clients resource is missing
body: ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel,String) falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource() when no per-client resource exists. That helper can return null if the Clients type resource was deleted or schema checks fail. The code then calls findByResource(server, null) and later new ResourcePermission(null, ...) without a null check, causing NullPointerException and HTTP 500 on any client permission check. A null guard returning false is required.

title: Per-client check ignores all-clients grant when specific resource exists
body: ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel,String) looks up the per-client resource by client id. If it exists it evaluates only that resource; the Clients type (all-clients) resource is only evaluated when the per-client resource is absent. Example: grant view on client A creating its resource, then grant manage on all clients. A check for manage on A finds A's resource, sees only view, and denies despite the all-clients manage grant. Both the specific and the type resources must be evaluated with OR semantics.

title: Client removal listener throws with V2 permissions
body: AdminPermissions.registerListener() calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client,false) on ClientRemovedEvent. When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whose clients() is now ClientPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException. The listener is gated only on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ, so with both features enabled deleting any client throws from the event listener; with only V2 enabled orphan authz resources leak. V2 needs a proper cleanup or no-op path.

title: getResourceName has no Clients branch
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName() special-cases only the Users type, returning All users or the username. For the new Clients type it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is null for resources created by getOrCreateResource that stores the client UUID as name. Client permission UI therefore shows null instead of All clients or the clientId. A Clients branch mirroring the Users branch is missing.

title: getScope NPE on unknown resourceType
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getScope() does SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType).getScopes() without checking that resourceType exists. An unknown or null resourceType causes NullPointerException instead of ModelValidationException, turning a bad request into HTTP 500. A null check is needed before dereferencing.

title: requireView docs say Returns instead of Throws
body: ClientPermissionEvaluator.requireView() and requireViewClientScopes() are void methods that throw ForbiddenException on denial, but their Javadoc says Returns true if canView returns true, copied from the can* methods. Readers will expect a boolean return. The docs must say Throws ForbiddenException if the corresponding can* returns false.

title: NPE when all-clients resource is missing in per-client check
body: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel,String) when no per-client resource is found it falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource for Clients. That helper can return null, for example on upgraded realms without a Clients resource or if it was deleted. The code then calls findByResource(server, resource) with null without a null check, causing NullPointerException and HTTP 500 on admin client endpoints instead of safely denying access.

title: Global client grant ignored when per-client resource exists
body: ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel,String) evaluates only one resource: if a per-client resource exists it evaluates only that resource, otherwise it evaluates the all-clients resource. If a per-client resource was created for one scope like view, a check for another scope like manage or map-roles on the same client will evaluate only the per-client policies and ignore a valid all-clients grant, incorrectly denying access. Correct authorization requires OR of per-object and all-type grants.

title: getClientsWithPermission never finds per-client resources
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with only name and owner and never sets the Resource type, so their type is null. ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission enumerates candidates with findByType for Clients type, which only matches the single all-clients resource. Per-client grants are therefore never enumerated, and the global resource name Clients which is not a client id would be added to the result, so filtered client listing with per-client permissions returns empty or wrong results.

title: Global canView ignores MANAGE grant
body: ClientPermissionsV2.canView without arguments returns true only for view permission, while canView for client scopes checks view or manage and per-client canView is true via canConfigure and canManage. An admin granted only manage on all clients will have canManage true but canView false, so global list and view checks deny managers who should be able to view. This is inconsistent with the transitive manage-implies-view behavior expected for users and scopes.

title: NPE on invalid resourceType in getScope
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getScope does SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType).getScopes() without checking that resourceType exists. If resourceType is null or unknown the get returns null and getScopes throws NullPointerException resulting in HTTP 500. It should throw ModelValidationException with 400 like other schema validations for bad permission input.

title: getResourceName does not handle Clients type
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName special-cases only Users to return All users or username. For Clients it falls through to resource.getDisplayName, but per-client resources created by getOrCreateResource have no display name set and are named by internal UUID. Admin UI and permission display for client permissions will therefore show null or UUID instead of All clients or clientId.

title: init does not migrate existing realms for new Clients type
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init returns early if the admin-permissions client already exists, so realms created before this change never get the new Clients scopes and all-clients resource. Creating a client permission on such realms then fails scope lookup with ModelException No scopes found, and global client checks return false. Upgrade needs to add missing scopes and type resources to existing clients.

title: Permission cleanup disabled and broken for V2
body: AdminPermissions.registerListener now only runs when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ V1 is enabled. With only V2 enabled, deletion of clients, roles and groups leaks V2 authorization resources and policies because setPermissionsEnabled is never called. With both V1 and V2 enabled, management returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whose setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, so deleting a client, role or group will fail with 500.

title: V2 evaluator throws 500 for unsupported operations
body: ClientPermissionsV2 implements methods like canExchangeTo, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource and getPermissions by throwing raw UnsupportedOperationException. When admin REST management endpoints or token-exchange checks call these in V2 mode the exception becomes HTTP 500 instead of a proper deny or 400 error, breaking API contract and availability.

title: Wrong Javadoc for void require methods
body: ClientPermissionEvaluator documents void methods requireView and requireViewClientScopes as Returns true if canView returns true. They return void and throw ForbiddenException on denial. The incorrect contract misleads callers into expecting a boolean result instead of exception-based enforcement.

title: Duplicate scopes not de-duplicated on init
body: In AdminPermissionsSchema.init the code collects ScopeRepresentation objects into a Set to get rid of duplicities when USERS and CLIENTS share scopes (manage, view, map-roles). ScopeRepresentation does not implement equals/hashCode by name, so the Set contains one object per occurrence (11 objects for 8 distinct names). The realm init then tries to create duplicate scopes named manage/view/map-roles, which can fail or create duplicates for every new realm with admin permissions enabled.

title: Per-client check ignores all-clients grant when specific resource exists
body: ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel,String) looks up the per-client resource by client id and only if it is null falls back to evaluating the all-clients resource named Clients. If a per-client resource exists (created for any prior per-client permission) the method evaluates only that resource and never evaluates the all-clients resource. An admin granted manage/view/configure/map-roles on all clients is therefore incorrectly denied on any client that happens to have a per-client resource, breaking the documented all-clients fallback.

title: getClientsWithPermission returns type resource as client id
body: getClientsWithPermission iterates resourceStore.findByType for type Clients and adds every granted resource.getName() to the result. The all-type resource itself has type Clients and name Clients, so it is also visited. If the all-clients permission is granted, the returned set contains the bogus id Clients instead of real client ids, and per-client checks do not consider the all-type grant. Callers filtering clients by this set get wrong results.

title: Missing null check before findByResource causes NPE
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel,String) when no per-client resource is found the code loads the all-clients resource via getResourceTypeResource, which can return null if the Clients type resource is missing, and then immediately calls findByResource(server, resource) with that value. Passing null throws NullPointerException/IllegalArgumentException instead of returning false, turning a permission check into a 500 error.

title: getResourceName has no handling for Clients type
body: getResourceName special-cases the Users type to return All users or the username for a user resource, but has no branch for the new Clients type. For client permissions it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is not set for auto-created client resources (name is the client UUID). Permission listings for clients will show null/blank instead of the clientId.

title: Removal listener disabled for V2 leaves orphan authz resources
body: registerListener now only runs when feature ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) is enabled. When only ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, ClientRemovedEvent/RoleRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent are ignored and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException so there is no alternative path. Deleting a client in V2 therefore leaves its per-client authorization resource and associated policies orphaned in the store.

title: Wrong Javadoc for requireView methods
body: The interface documents void requireView() as Returns true if canView() returns true and void requireViewClientScopes() as Returns true if canViewClientScopes() returns true. Both methods return void and throw ForbiddenException on denial. The copy-pasted return documentation misleads implementers and callers about the contract.

title: Null strategy test path skips required rolling-updates feature
body: In UpgradeTest.java createInitialDeployment() returns early when updateStrategy is null without enabling the rolling-updates feature, while the non-null path enables it via FeatureSpec. The same PR documents that the Operator will fail while in preview unless the rolling-updates feature is enabled. As a result the parameterized runs with null (testImageChange-null, testCacheMaxCount-null) deploy a Keycloak CR without the required feature and will fail reconciliation or test different behavior than the RECREATE runs. The feature enablement must happen before the early return for all strategies.

title: Feature gate only tested for metadata, not check, and exit code not verified
body: UpdateCommandDistTest.java adds testFeatureNotEnabled only for update-compatibility metadata when rolling-updates is disabled, but the PR adds the identical gate to update-compatibility check (UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java) with a new exit code FEATURE_DISABLED=4. There is no test that check without the feature prints the disabled message and exits with 4, and the existing test does not assert the exit code. A regression in the check path or wrong exit code would not be caught despite docs promising exit code 4 for disabled feature.

title: Default strategy test deployment omits required rolling-updates flag
body: In UpgradeTest.createInitialDeployment the method returns early when updateStrategy is null without enabling the rolling-updates feature, while the non-null path enables it via FeatureSpec. The operator docs in this same PR state the feature must be enabled otherwise the Operator will fail. Consequence: the parameterized runs with null strategy deploy a Keycloak CR without the required flag, so reconciliation will fail or will test different behavior than documented, invalidating testImageChange and testCacheMaxCount for the default strategy.

title: Test helper overwrites enabled features instead of appending
body: In UpgradeTest.createInitialDeployment the code calls setEnabledFeatures(List.of(rolling-updates key)). That replaces the entire enabled-features list coming from getTestKeycloakDeployment instead of adding to it. Consequence: any features already enabled on the base deployment are silently dropped, so the test runs with the wrong feature set and can false-pass or false-fail.

title: Feature gate only tested for metadata and exit codes never asserted
body: UpdateCommandDistTest adds testFeatureNotEnabled only for update-compatibility metadata, with no equivalent test for the check subcommand which has the same gate in UpdateCompatibilityCheck. It also only asserts stderr text and never asserts exit code 4 for disabled feature, and testWrongVersions never asserts exit code 3 for recreate. This PR changes RECREATE exit from 4 to 3 and adds 4 for FEATURE_DISABLED, and automation relies on those codes. Consequence: a missing gate on check or a wrong exit code regression would not be caught by tests.

title: Default upgrade-strategy test never enables rolling-updates feature
body: In createInitialDeployment the method returns early when updateStrategy is null without configuring spec.features.enabled to include rolling-updates, while the RECREATE path does configure it. The guide added in the same PR states the Operator requires the rolling-updates preview feature or it will fail. As a result the parameterized cases with null/default strategy run without the required feature, so they fail for the wrong reason and never exercise the intended default-strategy upgrade path. The feature setup must happen before the early return for all strategies.

title: Failure exit codes for update-compatibility tool are not verified
body: The documented contract for automation is the exit code: 0 rolling possible, 3 recreate required, 4 feature rolling-updates disabled. This PR renumbers RECREATE from 4 to 3 and adds 4 for disabled, but testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the stderr text and never asserts exit code 4, and testWrongVersions never asserts exit code 3. Only the happy path asserts exit code 0. A regression that prints the correct message but returns the wrong code, including 0 on failure, would pass tests and break scripts and operator logic that branches on the exit code.

title: Docs claim Operator fails without rolling-updates, breaking all existing CRs
body: The added CAUTION says while in preview the rolling-updates feature must be enabled otherwise the Keycloak Operator will fail. Rolling-updates is a new feature so every existing Keycloak CR lacks it. Failing all reconciliations until every CR is edited is an unnecessary breaking change. The compatible behavior is to fall back to pre-existing behavior when the feature is disabled and only fail the specific CR that requests the preview update strategy without the flag. As written the docs either mandate an overly broad outage or are inaccurate since no operator code in the PR scopes the failure.

title: Global group manage check accepts view scope
body: In services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java line 70, canManage() returns hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE). Global manage should require MANAGE only, as per-group canManage(GroupModel) correctly does. Since GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup, adding children and role mapping are guarded by requireManage(), an admin with only VIEW on all-groups can create and modify groups. This is privilege escalation.

title: Group view-member enumeration uses authz IDs instead of group IDs
body: In services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java line 122, getGroupIdsWithViewPermission iterates findByType(Groups) and calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId()) then adds groupResource.getId(). Authz resource IDs are internal UUIDs while group IDs are stored in resource names (AdminPermissionsSchema creates resources with name=groupId). hasPermission looks up by name via findByName, so lookup with an ID misses and falls back to the all-groups resource, and the returned set contains authz IDs not group IDs. Callers in UsersResource and BruteForceUsersResource expect group IDs for UserModel.GROUPS filtering and counts, so results are wrong or empty. Per-group resources are also created without a type, so findByType misses them entirely.

title: Per-group check ignores all-groups permission when specific resource exists
body: In services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java line 143, hasPermission only loads the all-groups resource when no per-group resource exists. Once any permission creates a per-group resource for a group, an admin holding only an all-groups MANAGE or VIEW grant is evaluated solely against that per-group resource and denied, even though the all-groups grant should apply. This causes false denials for all-groups admins as soon as specific group permissions exist, and NPEs when the all-groups resource is missing.

title: Per-user check ignores all-users permission when specific resource exists
body: In services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/UserPermissionsV2.java line 107, hasPermission only falls back to the all-users resource when no per-user resource exists. After a per-user resource is created for a user, a different admin with only an all-users grant is evaluated only against that per-user resource and denied. This breaks OR semantics between all-users and single-user permissions and causes false denials.

title: V2 group management methods throw breaking deletion cleanup
body: In services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java line 174, setPermissionsEnabled and other GroupPermissionManagement methods throw UnsupportedOperationException. AdminPermissions.registerListener calls management().groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group,false) on GroupRemovedEvent. With V2 active this aborts group deletion with an exception, or if the listener is not registered leaves orphan authz resources with no cleanup path.

title: Existing realms never get Groups resource type and scopes
body: In server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java line 251, init returns early if the admin-permissions client already exists. Scopes and all-resource resources including the new Groups type are only created for brand-new realms. Upgraded realms keep the old client without Groups scopes or all-groups resource, so group checks in V2 deny or hit null resources after upgrade. No migration is provided.

title: Group permission display name not resolved
body: In server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java line 349, getResourceName handles only Users (returning All users or username) and falls through to resource.getDisplayName() for Groups. Group resources are created with name=groupId and no displayName, so permission listings show null or raw UUIDs instead of All groups or the group name.

title: Group listing lost global-view fast path
body: In services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/GroupsResource.java line 113, getGroups changed from caching canViewGlobal once to filtering with groupsEvaluator.canView for every group, same in GroupResource.getSubGroups. For an admin granted via all-groups permission each per-group check re-evaluates the all-groups policy, turning one evaluation into N evaluations and severely slowing listings with many groups.

title: Test cleanup captures mutable group field
body: In tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java line 76, onBefore registers cleanup with lambda using topGroup.getId() where topGroup is a mutable field overwritten each test. The lambda reads the ID at cleanup time, not registration time, so earlier cleanups delete the latest ID and leak earlier groups, causing cross-test pollution.

title: Global group canManage incorrectly accepts view scope
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() the fallback check is hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE) on the all-groups resource, identical to canView(). This means an admin with only the view scope on Groups passes requireManage(), which guards create top-level group, delete and other manage operations. A view-only delegated admin can therefore create, update and delete groups, which is a privilege escalation.

title: Group view permission scan uses resource ID instead of group ID
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission the code iterates resources of type Groups and calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) and granted.add(groupResource.getId()). For admin permissions, resource name equals the group ID and resource ID is a generated UUID. The lookup must use getName(), as V1 does with getName().substring(prefix). Using getId() means the per-group evaluation looks up a non-existent resource and the returned set contains authz UUIDs instead of group IDs, so user search filtered by UserModel.GROUPS returns empty or wrong results for group-scoped admins.

title: Per-group check shadows all-groups permission
body: GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission loads resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId) and only if it is null falls back to the all-groups resource. If a per-group resource exists at all, for example created for a different admin, the all-groups permission is never evaluated. An admin with MANAGE or VIEW on all groups is then denied for that specific group despite the all-groups grant. The same pattern exists for users, breaking the expected all-users/all-groups transitive semantics.

title: Per-user check shadows all-users permission
body: UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission loads resourceStore.findByName(server, user.getId()) and only if null falls back to the all-users resource. If a per-user resource exists for the target user, for example created for another admin, the all-users permission is never evaluated. An admin with MANAGE or VIEW on all users loses access to that user, so creating any single-user permission revokes all-users access for other admins.

title: Missing null check for all-groups resource causes NPE on upgrade
body: GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource for Groups and immediately calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) without checking for null. Realms upgraded from before Groups existed, or realms where the resource server is not fully initialized, have no Groups type resource, so resource is null and the call throws NullPointerException, crashing every group permission check. UserPermissionsV2 line 111 has the same unchecked pattern.

title: Scope deduplication via Set does not work
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init collects new ScopeRepresentation objects into a Set to get rid of duplicities, but ScopeRepresentation does not implement equals/hashCode so each new instance is distinct. Scopes like manage and view that appear in Clients, Groups and Users types remain duplicated in the list passed to RepresentationToModel.toModel, causing duplicate scope creation attempts or failures when first enabling admin permissions.

title: getScope NPE on unknown resource type
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getScope does SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType).getScopes() without checking that resourceType exists. A null or unknown resourceType causes NullPointerException instead of ModelValidationException, turning a bad admin API request into a 500 error.

title: getResourceName does not handle Groups type
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName only special-cases Users, returning All users or the username, and otherwise returns resource.getDisplayName(). Group resources store the group ID as name with no displayName, so group permissions resolve to null or blank names in the admin UI and APIs. The new Groups type needs an All groups case and group name resolution like users.

title: requireManageMembers javadoc references wrong method
body: The javadoc on requireManageMembers says it throws if canManageMembership returns false, duplicating the comment on requireManageMembership. It should reference canManageMembers. Readers cannot tell which check is enforced without reading the implementation.

title: Global canManage() grants manage on VIEW
body: In services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:70, canManage() returns hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), identical to canView(). This lets an admin with only VIEW on the all-groups resource pass requireManage(), e.g. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup which requires global manage. Consequence is privilege escalation: read-only group viewers can create top-level groups. Fix is to check only MANAGE for global manage, matching per-group canManage(group) which correctly checks only MANAGE.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses resource UUID instead of group ID
body: In services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:122-123, findByType iterates group resources but calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId()) and granted.add(groupResource.getId()). Per AdminPermissionsSchema group resources are named by groupId (resolveGroup returns groupId) while getId() is the internal authz UUID, so findByName lookup misses and the granted set contains authz UUIDs not group IDs. UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource then filter user searches and counts by UserModel.GROUPS with bogus IDs, returning empty or wrong user sets and breaking pagination.

title: Per-object group resources created without type breaks findByType
body: In server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:121, getOrCreateResource creates a resource with resourceStore.create(server, name, clientId) and updates scopes but never calls setType(resourceType), while init() for aggregate resources does setType(type). GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission relies on resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE). Since per-group resources have null type they are never found, the method always returns empty, disabling store-level filtering of users by view-members and forcing full scans with in-memory filtering and incorrect first/max pagination.

title: V2 group management methods throw breaking deletion
body: In services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:174, setPermissionsEnabled (and isPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions, view/manage permission accessors) throw UnsupportedOperationException. AdminPermissions.registerListener calls management().groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group,false) on GroupRemovedEvent, and GroupResource management/permissions endpoints call the same methods. With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled, deleting any group aborts the transaction with 500 and leaks authz resources, and the management endpoints always fail.

title: Existing realms never get Groups resource and scopes
body: In server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:250, init() returns early if realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() already exists. Existing realms that already have the admin-permissions client (with only Users/Clients) therefore never get the new Groups aggregate resource nor the new scopes manage-members/view-members/manage-membership. Later getOrCreateResource for Groups then throws ModelException No scopes found because scopeStore.findByName returns null, breaking group permission creation on upgrade.

title: Missing null-check for all-groups fallback causes NPE
body: In services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:147, hasPermission falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource for Groups when no per-group resource exists, then immediately calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) and new ResourcePermission(resource,...) without checking for null. getResourceTypeResource explicitly can return null (unsupported schema, missing type, missing resource). Consequence is NullPointerException during any group permission check when the aggregate Groups resource is absent, e.g. upgraded realms or misconfigured servers.

title: Impersonation with requester evaluates wrong identity
body: In services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/UserPermissionsV2.java:71, canImpersonate(user, requester) builds DefaultEvaluationContext with new UserModelIdentity(root.realm, user) when requester != null, then evaluates IMPERSONATE on the target user's resource with that context. That evaluates as the target user, not the admin attempting impersonation (plus kc.client.id claim). Legitimate admin impersonation with a requesting client will fail policy checks for the admin and may incorrectly succeed/deny based on target attributes. Correct context should use the admin identity with the client-id claim, as V1 does for admin checks.

title: Removed global-view short-circuit causes per-group evaluations
body: In services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/GroupsResource.java:113 (and GroupResource.java:179), the filter was changed from cached canViewGlobal || canView(g) to stream.filter(groupsEvaluator::canView). For V2, global VIEW via all-groups permission now requires a full authz evaluation per group instead of one cached evaluation with short-circuit, turning group listing into O(N) policy evaluations. Consequence is severe latency on realms with many groups for admins with all-groups access.

title: Lithuanian message replaced with Italian text
body: In the Lithuanian account bundle line 101 totpStep1 is now 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' which is Italian, not Lithuanian. Lithuanian users will see an Italian sentence in the account console. The change was meant to remove <a> links, but copied the Italian translation instead of a Lithuanian one.

title: Lithuanian login message replaced with Italian text
body: In the Lithuanian login bundle line 71 loginTotpStep1 is now 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' which is Italian. Users with Lithuanian locale will see Italian instructions on the TOTP setup page. This is the same copy-paste error as in the account bundle.

title: Simplified Chinese file uses Traditional characters
body: In the zh_CN account bundle line 112 totpStep1 is now 'In your mobile install one of the following apps' written with Traditional characters (手機, 應用程式, 安裝). The file is Simplified Chinese which should use 手机, 应用程序, 安装. Simplified-Chinese users will see the wrong script variant.

title: Diff snippet can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException
body: When sanitized and original values differ, the code strips common prefix (start) and suffix (end) then does value.substring(start, value.length()-end). It never checks that start+end does not exceed the length. If the common prefix and suffix overlap the substring bounds are inverted and substring throws, aborting verification with an exception instead of reporting illegal HTML.

title: Throws RuntimeException instead of MojoExecutionException on read failure
body: verifySafeHtml wraps failure to read the checked file and failure to read the English reference file in RuntimeException. The public verify() contract is MojoExecutionException for IO problems. A missing English file therefore crashes the Maven plugin with an unchecked exception and stack trace instead of a clean Mojo failure.

title: PropertyResourceBundle with InputStream misdecodes UTF-8
body: The verifier loads message bundles with new PropertyResourceBundle(new FileInputStream(file)), which decodes as ISO-8859-1. The message files contain raw UTF-8 (Arabic, Chinese, Lithuanian, etc.), so non-ASCII values are mojibake when inspected. Error reports will show garbled text and all comparisons run on corrupted strings. It should use the Reader constructor with UTF-8.

title: Stray 'n' left in Danish email HTML
body:
In the Danish email bundle line 9 identityProviderLinkBodyHtml contains '

nHvis du ikke vil...' with an extra leading n, while the plain-text version has correct 'Hvis'. Recipients will see a paragraph starting with 'nHvis'. The PR fixed the missing

but left the typo.

title: Stray 'n' left in Lithuanian email HTML
body:
In the Lithuanian email bundle line 3 emailVerificationBodyHtml contains '

nJei paskyros...' with an extra leading n, while the plain-text version has correct 'Jei'. Recipients will see a paragraph starting with 'nJei'.

title: Anchor mismatch message lacks key and file
body: When a translated anchor does not exactly match the English anchor the verifier adds "Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string" with no key name and no file name, unlike the Illegal HTML message which includes both. When run over hundreds of bundles this failure is unactionable and requires manual search to locate.

title: No positive test that valid HTML passes
body: All tests assert that bad fixtures produce a message with hasItem, but there is no test asserting that a valid translation with allowed tags or identical anchors produces zero messages. A false positive in the sanitizer would therefore go unnoticed, and the duplicate-keys test would still pass even with extra spurious errors.

title: Lithuanian message replaced with Italian text
body: The totpStep1 value in the Lithuanian account bundle is now the Italian sentence 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' instead of Lithuanian. Lithuanian users will see Italian instructions for OTP setup. The edit was meant to remove HTML links but copied the wrong language.

title: Lithuanian login message replaced with Italian text
body: The loginTotpStep1 value in the Lithuanian login bundle is now the Italian sentence 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' instead of Lithuanian. Lithuanian users will see Italian instructions. The change was meant to strip anchor tags but inserted the wrong language.

title: Simplified Chinese file uses Traditional characters
body: The new totpStep1 value in the Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) account bundle uses Traditional characters such as mobile-phone and application words written in Traditional form. Users with Simplified Chinese locale will see Traditional text. The file should use Simplified characters like the surrounding entries.

title: Missing anchors in translation are never detected
body: santizeAnchors only loops over anchor tags found in the translated value and checks each against English. It never checks that every anchor from the English source was consumed. A translation that deletes a required link entirely will therefore pass with no error, resulting in broken UI where the link is silently missing but the build stays green.

title: Anchor mismatch error lacks key and file
body: The message added for a changed anchor contains only the tag text and the words in original string, without the message key or file name. The Illegal HTML message in the same file includes both key and file. When verification fails on a large bundle the maintainer cannot locate the offending key without reproducing locally.

title: Verbatim compare causes false positive on br tag formatting
body: The verifier compares OWASP sanitizer output verbatim to the input. The sanitizer normalizes a self-closing break from br-slash form to br-space-slash form. A safe translation using the first form is therefore reported as Illegal HTML even though it is semantically identical. The PR had to rewrite more than twenty existing translations only to add that space, proving future contributions will be falsely rejected.

title: Missing English file crashes verifier with RuntimeException
body: If the English counterpart file cannot be opened, verifySafeHtml throws an unchecked RuntimeException. The public verify method is declared to throw MojoExecutionException for IO problems. A single missing English file will therefore crash the theme-verifier plugin with a stack trace instead of producing a readable verification failure.

title: HTML detection is case-sensitive
body: The patterns for detecting HTML and anchor tags only match lowercase tag names. HTML tag names are case-insensitive, so an English source containing uppercase tags like B or A would be classified as containing no HTML and select the wrong sanitizer policy, mishandling a matching translation.

title: Illegal HTML fixture is truncated
body: The fixture value ends with open-div without the final closing bracket. The test therefore exercises a truncated tag rather than a proper disallowed element. It can pass for the wrong reason and does not document the intended illegal-tag case.

title: No positive test for valid translations
body: All tests assert that bad fixtures produce an error, but none asserts that good fixtures produce zero errors. For example there is no check that the valid English file or a translation with allowed formatting passes cleanly. A verifier that false-positives on every legitimate message would still pass the suite.

title: Lithuanian message replaced with Italian text
body: File themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_lt.properties line 101 sets totpStep1 to Italian 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' while the file is Lithuanian and surrounding keys are Lithuanian. The previous value was Lithuanian. Consequence is Lithuanian users will see Italian instructions. It should be Lithuanian text without HTML, not a copy of the Italian translation.

title: Lithuanian login message replaced with Italian text
body: File themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties line 71 sets loginTotpStep1 to Italian 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' while the file is Lithuanian and neighboring keys are Lithuanian. Consequence is Lithuanian login page shows Italian. It should be the Lithuanian translation without anchor tags.

title: Simplified Chinese file contains Traditional Chinese
body: File themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_zh_CN.properties line 112 sets totpStep1 to 'In your mobile...' using Traditional characters手机/應用程式/裝 while the file is zh_CN Simplified which elsewhere uses simplified 手机/应用 and surrounding lines are Simplified. Consequence is script inconsistency for Simplified Chinese users. It should use Simplified characters like 手机 and 应用程序.

title: Missing English counterpart throws instead of reporting
body: In VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml when the derived English file cannot be opened the code throws new RuntimeException. That aborts the whole verify() call, discarding any messages already collected and producing a stack trace instead of a normal verifier message. Consequence is a single community-only key or mis-mapped path fails the entire theme-verifier plugin with an exception and hides all other errors. It should record a message and continue.

title: Dropped anchors pass silently and error lacks key/file
body: Method santizeAnchors in VerifyMessageProperties iterates only over anchor tags found in the translation and strips exact matches. If the translation drops an anchor that exists in English, the loop runs zero times and passes with no error, so a lost link is never reported. When it does report, it adds only "Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string" with no key name and no file name, unlike the Illegal HTML message which includes both. Consequence is functional regressions are missed and failures that are reported are unactionable in logs covering hundreds of files.

title: Semantically identical HTML flagged due to normalization
body:
VerifyMessageProperties compares policy.sanitize(value) for exact string equality with the raw translation. The OWASP sanitizer normalizes markup such as
to
and to , so a safe translation using a different but equivalent spacing is reported as Illegal HTML. The PR itself proves this by having to rewrite dozens of webauthn-error and other messages only to add a space in
. Consequence is future translators writing valid
will fail verification. The verifier should normalize or allow equivalent serializations before comparing.

title: No negative test for valid translations
body:
All tests in VerifyMessagePropertiesTest assert hasItem for illegal cases such as duplicate keys, illegal tags, extra HTML, and changed anchors. There is no test asserting that a valid translation yields an empty message list, for example that noHtml_en, changedAnchor_en, or an English string with allowed /

/
passes. Consequence is false positives from sanitizer normalization or anchor stripping would not be caught by the test suite.

title: Constructor validates grantType twice, never validates rawTokenId
body: In AccessTokenContext constructor both null-checks use grantType, the second message says rawTokenId but still checks grantType. A null rawTokenId therefore passes validation and later encodeTokenId produces a jti ending in ':null' and getRawTokenId returns null, corrupting token identity and breaking round-trip decode.

title: New abstract getShortcut breaks existing grant factories
body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory adds abstract String getShortcut() with no default implementation. Any existing third-party or downstream OAuth2GrantTypeFactory that implements the old interface will fail to compile and at runtime will throw AbstractMethodError, preventing server startup. A default method returning unknown sentinel or requiring migration would preserve compatibility.

title: grantType cached at construction becomes stale and can NPE
body: Context constructor caches grantType via formParams.getFirst(grant_type) but setFormParams can later replace formParams without updating the cached field, so getGrantType returns stale value while getFormParams returns new value and tokens are encoded with wrong grant. Previously the constructor only assigned formParams so null was tolerated; now a null formParams causes NullPointerException in the constructor.

title: Removed public copy constructor Context(Context)
body: The public Context(Context) copy constructor was deleted. Custom OAuth2GrantType implementations or extensions that copied context via new Context(context) will no longer compile and break source and binary compatibility with no deprecation or replacement.

title: Decoder throws on malformed token IDs instead of graceful fallback
body: getTokenContextFromTokenId returns UNKNOWN context for IDs without colon but throws IllegalArgumentException for IDs with colon and wrong prefix length or unknown shortcuts. When this decoder is used on jti values taken from presented JWTs for introspection/userInfo/session optimization, attacker-supplied or foreign IDs will cause unhandled exceptions and 500s instead of falling back to UNKNOWN and doing normal lookup.

title: No validation that grant shortcuts are 2 chars and colon-free
body: postInit copies arbitrary strings from OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut into maps with no check for length 2 or absence of colon, while the decoder assumes exactly 6-char prefix split as 2+2+2 and uses colon as delimiter. A custom grant with 3-char shortcut or colon produces token IDs that can never be decoded and validation comparing map sizes does not catch length violations.

title: Lazy grant map refresh races and can clobber mappings
body: getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut do non-atomic check-then-put on shared ConcurrentHashMaps and blindly overwrite shortcut to grant mappings without collision detection. Concurrent token issuance and decoding can interleave, lose updates, or overwrite one grant's shortcut with another's, permanently corrupting decode for the victim grant.

title: Access token ID matcher has inverted logic and wrong offsets
body: isAccessTokenId splits on colon then checks items[0].substring(3,5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut) and returns false when equal. Correct grant position for 6-char prefix on+tt+gt is substring 4,6, and logic should fail when not equal. As written any UUID-suffixed ID passes regardless of grant and short prefixes can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, so tests never verify grant encoding.

title: Constructor never null-checks rawTokenId
body: AccessTokenContext constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType) twice, the second with message "Null rawTokenId not allowed", and never checks rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted and later encoded as the string "null" after ':' or causes NPE on decode, producing corrupt token IDs and misleading error messages.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher logic inverted and wrong offset
body: The matcher splits token ID on ':' then does if (items[0].substring(3,5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false. It should reject when NOT equal and grant shortcut occupies chars 4-6 (substring 4,6) of the 6-char prefix session(0-1)+token(2-3)+grant(4-5). As written any 6-char prefix with a valid UUID passes regardless of grant, so tests for authorization_code, device, refresh and ciba grants never actually verify the encoded grant and give false confidence.

title: New abstract getShortcut breaks custom grant providers
body: Adding abstract String getShortcut() to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory breaks source and binary compatibility for any third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementation. Existing custom grants will fail compilation and throw AbstractMethodError at runtime when loaded. It should be a default method returning a safe fallback like "na".

title: Removed public copy constructor breaks compatibility
body: The public Context(Context context) copy constructor was deleted. Any existing custom grant code or extension that copied grant context with new Context(oldContext) will fail compilation and throw NoSuchMethodError at runtime. It should be retained as deprecated and delegate to field copies plus grantType.

title: grantType becomes stale after setFormParams and can NPE
body: Context captures grantType once in the constructor from formParams.getFirst("grant_type") without null-checking formParams, then setFormParams() replaces the map without updating grantType. If formParams is null construction NPEs, and if params are replaced the encoded grant will be the stale value, causing wrong grant shortcut in the access-token ID.

title: Decoding untrusted token ID throws instead of returning UNKNOWN
body: getTokenContextFromTokenId returns UNKNOWN session/token/grant when there is no ':' (old UUID tokens) but throws IllegalArgumentException for wrong prefix length or unknown shortcuts. The input is the jti from a client-presented JWT, so a crafted or legacy ID containing ':' triggers an unhandled exception and 500/log spam. Handling should be consistent and return UNKNOWN for undecodable IDs.

title: Lightweight detection uses context client not token client
body: getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext determines lightweight vs regular via AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session), which reads session.getContext().getClient(). TokenManager.initToken already has the correct ClientModel parameter for the token being created. If context client differs from token client or is null, the encoded tokenType is wrong and initToken can NPE, breaking token issuance on a hot path that previously never touched the context client.

title: Initial offline tokens encoded as online
body: Session type is derived only from userSession.isOffline() at initToken time. For an authorization-code flow requesting offline_access, the user session is still online when the access token is created and the online session is removed only afterwards in OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse. The first access token for an offline grant is therefore encoded as ONLINE while refreshed tokens are OFFLINE, defeating the stated optimization of avoiding double session lookup.

title: Unknown grant aborts token creation instead of falling back
body: encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException when factory.getShortcutByGrantType returns null. It is called from TokenManager.initToken for every access token. Any token whose ClientSessionContext grant attribute is set to a value without a registered OAuth2GrantTypeFactory, such as implicit/hybrid flows or custom values, will fail the whole token request with 500 instead of falling back to the existing "na" unknown-grant encoding.

title: Lazy grant-map updates are non-atomic and unchecked
body: getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut lazily do grantsByShortcuts.put plus grantsToShortcuts.put as two separate ConcurrentHashMap operations with no synchronization and no duplicate-shortcut validation. Concurrent first use can leave the two maps inconsistent, and a new grant reusing an existing shortcut silently overwrites the decode mapping, making future token IDs ambiguous.

title: Constructor validates grantType twice instead of rawTokenId
body: In AccessTokenContext the constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") instead of checking rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId therefore passes validation and later produces a corrupt encoded id (e.g. prefix + ":null") or an NPE far from the source, while a null grantType produces a misleading message. Fail-fast validation is lost.

title: Access-token-id matcher has inverted logic and wrong offset
body: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId the check is if (items[0].substring(3,5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false, which fails when the shortcut matches instead of when it mismatches. The offset is also wrong: grant shortcut is the last 2 chars of the 6-char prefix (indexes 4,6), not (3,5), which is second char of token-type plus first char of grant. There is no length guard before substring, so short ids throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. The result is tests only verify colon+UUID and never verify the grant, giving false confidence.

title: New abstract getShortcut breaks existing grant factories
body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory adds abstract String getShortcut() with no default implementation. Any third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory compiled against the old interface will throw AbstractMethodError when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit calls getShortcut(), preventing server startup. It should be a default method returning the unknown value.

title: grantType becomes stale after setFormParams
body: In OAuth2GrantType.Context grantType is captured once in the constructor from formParams.getFirst(grant_type), but setFormParams() replaces formParams without updating grantType. If form params are mutated after construction, OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse stores a stale GRANT_TYPE attribute and the encoded token id will contain the wrong grant.

title: Removal of public Context copy constructor breaks callers
body: The public constructor Context(Context) was removed from OAuth2GrantType.Context. Existing custom grant code that copied the context via new Context(oldContext) no longer compiles. The copy constructor should be retained (and copy the new grantType field) or deprecated, not deleted.

title: getShouldUseLightweightToken changed to static and can NPE
body: AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken was changed from an instance package-private method to public static, which breaks any subclass that overrode it and changes polymorphic behavior. The body also dereferences session.getContext().getClient() without null checks, so callers with no ambient client (now including the token encoder) get an NPE instead of a safe default.

title: Token context creation NPEs and uses wrong client for lightweight flag
body: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext the code dereferences clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getUserSession() with no null checks, so any context with null session fails token issuance with NPE. It also determines lightweight vs regular via the ambient session context client instead of the token's client from the ClientSessionContext, so when the ambient client differs or is null the encoded token-type disagrees with actual token content, causing downstream lightweight optimizations to read roles from the wrong place.

title: Grant shortcuts not validated to be 2 chars without colon
body: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit grant shortcuts are stored without validating length or content, while the encoder/decoder hard-codes a 6-char prefix (2+2+2) with ':' as separator. A custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory returning a 3-char shortcut (as the javadoc even suggests) or containing ':' will encode to a prefix the decoder rejects with IllegalArgumentException, breaking round-trip for that grant.

title: Malformed token ids throw instead of returning UNKNOWN
body: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId legacy ids without ':' return an UNKNOWN context, but any id with ':' and wrong prefix length or unknown shortcut throws IllegalArgumentException. Once this decoder is used on request paths like introspection/userInfo as the PR intends, attacker-controlled or foreign jti values will cause unhandled 500s instead of invalid-token handling. It should return UNKNOWN for forward compatibility.

title: NPE in getCredentials for users not in storage map
body: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials the code does var myUser = getMyUser(user) and then dereferences myUser.recoveryCodes without a null check. getFederatedCredentialsStream calls this for every user, including local users never added to the map. When myUser is null this throws NullPointerException, breaking credential listing, login and account APIs for local users whenever the provider is installed.

title: Federated recovery credential loses its stored ID
body: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials a new RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel is built with createFromValues() from the stored credentialData, but the stored ID from myUser.recoveryCodes.getId() is never copied to the new model. Every call therefore returns a different random ID. Callers that later call removeStoredCredentialById(model.getId()) use a non-existent ID, so deletion of an exhausted federated recovery credential silently fails and the old credential is never removed.

title: Federated recovery code validation never consumes codes
body: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE the code only checks generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse())) and returns true. It never marks the used code as consumed or persists any state change, unlike the local RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider which invalidates a code after use. Consequence: the same recovery code can be replayed indefinitely, getNextRecoveryAuthnCode never advances, and allCodesUsed never becomes true, defeating the single-use security property of recovery codes.

title: disableCredentialType does not support recovery codes
body: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.disableCredentialType only clears myUser.otp for OTP types and logs unsupported for everything else. Federated recovery codes can therefore never be disabled or deleted through the standard disable path used by admin REST and account console. After all codes are used or when an admin disables the type, the federated recovery credential remains in the map and stays valid.

title: Exhausted federated credential removed with local-only API
body: In RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.isRecoveryAuthnCodeInputValid the code loads the credential with RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential which now prefers federated storage, but on allCodesUsed it always calls removeStoredCredentialById(id). That API removes a locally stored credential; federated credentials must be removed via the user-storage disable/remove path. For a federated recovery credential the call does nothing, so an exhausted credential is left in user storage while only adding the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action.

title: Unchecked Optional.get() causes 500 when credential missing or exhausted
body: In RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean the constructor does credentialModelOpt.get() and then getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get() without isPresent checks. If the user has no recovery credential or all codes are already used, this throws NoSuchElementException during login page rendering, producing a 500 error instead of a handled authentication failure or required-action redirect.

title: Recovery storage test does not verify single-use or removal
body: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin the test only sets up codes and logs in once with code 0. Unlike the OTP tests it never verifies that the used code is consumed, that reuse is rejected, that exhaustion triggers re-setup, or that disable/delete via admin/account APIs clears federated storage. The replay and deletion bugs above therefore pass undetected.

title: getCredentials NPE for users not in federated map
body: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java at line 232, getCredentials() does var myUser = getMyUser(user) then dereferences myUser.recoveryCodes without a null check, while isConfiguredFor() and isValid() explicitly handle null. When the storage provider is enabled Keycloak calls getFederatedCredentialsStream/getCredentials for every user including purely local users not in the users map, so myUser is null and this throws NullPointerException, breaking credential listing and login for unrelated users.

title: Federated recovery-code validation does not consume codes
body: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java at line 340, isValid() for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE only does generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(...) and returns true without removing or marking the used code as consumed. The local keycloak-recovery-authn-codes provider makes codes single-use and tracks allCodesUsed() to force regeneration and deletion. With this implementation the same federated recovery code can be replayed indefinitely, allCodesUsed() never becomes true, and the test only logs in once so reuse is never caught.

title: Federated getCredentials discards stored credential ID
body: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java at line 237, getCredentials() builds the returned value via RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...) which creates a new CredentialModel with a fresh ID, discarding the ID assigned in updateCredential() to myUser.recoveryCodes. Any later operation by ID such as account-console DELETE /credentials/{id} or RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.removeStoredCredentialById() when all codes are used will use an ID that does not match the stored federated credential, so deletion silently fails and a stale credential remains.

title: Federated recovery codes cannot be disabled/deleted
body: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java at line 217, disableCredentialType() only handles OTP types and logs unsupported for anything else, and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream() at line 254 only advertises OTP. As a result admin disableCredentialType and account-management deletion for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE are no-ops for federated users: federated recovery codes can never be removed via the supported APIs and remain valid.

title: Unchecked Optional.get() causes 500 on recovery login
body: In RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean.java at line 19, the constructor calls RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) then immediately does credentialModelOpt.get() without checking isPresent. A user-storage provider is allowed to implement CredentialInputValidator.isValid without exposing credentials via getCredentials(), or the credential may be missing/mismatched between federated and local stores. In that case this throws NoSuchElementException and produces a 500 error when rendering the recovery-code login form instead of a handled authentication failure.

title: Raw recovery codes sent to user storage in plaintext
body: In CredentialHelper.java at line 123, createRecoveryCodesCredential() serializes the raw generatedCodes list to JSON and passes it as the UserCredentialModel to user.credentialManager().updateCredential(), while the local path stores only hashed codes inside RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel. External user storage therefore persists recoverable plaintext recovery codes, as demonstrated by the test provider storing credentialData verbatim, so compromise of the external store yields all codes. Hashed material could be stored and verified like the local provider does.

title: Exhausted federated recovery credential never removed
body: In RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.java at line 86, after successful validation the code loads the credential via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential() which now may return a federated credential and then calls removeStoredCredentialById() when allCodesUsed(). Federated credentials are managed via the UserStorageProvider disable path, which the bundled test provider does not implement for recovery codes, so for federated users this deletion is a no-op: exhausted codes remain stored and the addRequiredAction(CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES) logic dependent on removal breaks.

title: Recovery-code creation uses wrong UserCredentialModel field
body: In CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential the JSON of raw codes is passed via new UserCredentialModel("", type, recoveryCodesJson), which populates getValue() (same pattern as createOTPCredential where storage reads getValue()). But BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential for recovery codes reads input.getChallengeResponse() to populate credentialData. Validation via UserCredentialModel.buildFromBackupAuthnCode uses challengeResponse, so creation and validation use different fields. Consequence is the federated provider receives null for credentialData, so recovery codes are not persisted correctly and subsequent login/validation fails or stores null.

title: Federated recovery-code validation never consumes codes
body: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE only checks generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse())) and never updates or removes the used code. Local recovery-code provider marks a code as used on successful isValid, and RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator relies on that to eventually detect allCodesUsed. With this implementation the same recovery code remains valid forever, defeating one-time use, and allCodesUsed never becomes true. The added test only uses one code once, so reuse is never caught.

title: getCredentials can NPE for unknown user
body: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials the code does var myUser = getMyUser(user) then immediately dereferences myUser.recoveryCodes without null check, unlike isValid and isConfiguredFor which check for null. If getCredentials is called for a user not in the map, myUser is null and this throws NullPointerException, breaking credential listing for federated users.

title: Cannot disable/remove federated recovery codes
body: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.disableCredentialType only clears myUser.otp for OTP types and logs otherwise, and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream only advertises OTP. There is no handling for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE. As a result admin REST disableCredentialType, account-console delete, and any flow that disables recovery codes does nothing when codes live in user storage, leaving stale/exhausted credentials behind.

title: Exhausted federated recovery credential removed via wrong API
body: After successful validation the code looks up the credential via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential, which prefers getFederatedCredentialsStream, then calls removeStoredCredentialById with that ID when allCodesUsed. removeStoredCredentialById operates on local stored credentials, not federated credentials, and the test storage does not support disabling recovery codes. For a user whose codes live in user storage the exhausted credential is therefore never removed from the external store, so the user keeps an empty credential and the required-action logic diverges from local-storage behavior.

title: Unchecked Optional.get causes 500 when credential missing
body: RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean constructor does RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) then immediately calls credentialModelOpt.get() without isPresent check, then getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get(). If the user has no recovery credential or all codes are used, this throws NoSuchElementException during login-page rendering, producing a 500 instead of a handled error or redirect to setup.

title: Same concurrent-delete NPE remains in getSubGroupsStream overloads
body: GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount was fixed to null-check modelSupplier.get() because the delegate returns null when the group was deleted concurrently. The three getSubGroupsStream overloads still do modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) with no null check. Under the same race the delegate returns null, modelSupplier.get() returns null, and dereferencing it throws NullPointerException, causing the same 500 failure this PR claims to fix. All paged/search subgroup lookups need the same null handling as getSubGroupsCount.

title: Concurrency test asserts without joining reader thread
body: The new test starts a raw Thread that loops groups() reads while the main thread deletes 100 groups, then sets deletedAll and immediately asserts caughtExceptions is empty without keeping a Thread reference or joining. Exceptions that arrive after the assert are missed, the test can pass while the background request later fails, and the leaked thread keeps calling the admin client after the test/realm is torn down, causing flakes and cross-test noise. The test must join the reader with a timeout before asserting and stop hammering the server in a tight loop.

title: Concurrent delete still causes NPE in getSubGroupsStream overloads
body: In model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/GroupAdapter.java the three getSubGroupsStream overloads do return modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) with no null check. If the group is deleted concurrently, cacheSession.getGroupDelegate().getGroupById() returns null so modelSupplier.get() returns null and the dereference throws NullPointerException. The PR fixes the identical pattern in getSubGroupsCount() by returning null when the delegate is null, but leaves the overloads at lines 255, 261 and 267 unfixed, so the same concurrent delete during subgroup listing still causes NPE/500.

title: Concurrent test thread is never joined and can leak/race
body: In tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti starts a new Thread that loops calling groups(null,0,Integer.MAX_VALUE,true) and discards the handle via new Thread(...).start(). The test then deletes groups, sets deletedAll to true, and immediately asserts caughtExceptions is empty without joining the reader. The assertion can run while a request is still in flight so later failures are missed, the reader can outlive the test and interfere with subsequent tests, and if the delete loop throws deletedAll is never set leaving an infinite tight busy-loop hammering the server.

title: Concurrent delete still causes NPE in getSubGroupsStream overloads
body: This PR acknowledges that modelSupplier.get() can return null when the group was deleted concurrently and makes getSubGroupsCount null-safe. The three getSubGroupsStream overloads in the same file still do modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) without any null check. If the group disappears between cache lookup and DB lookup they throw NullPointerException, the exact failure this PR claims to fix. Consequence is 500 errors remain for concurrent list/search of subgroups. They need the same null handling as getSubGroupsCount, e.g. return Stream.empty().

title: Background reader thread never joined and flag not set on failure
body: The new test starts a background thread that loops calling the admin API until deletedAll becomes true, deletes groups on the main thread, then immediately asserts without joining. If any delete throws, deletedAll.set(true) is skipped and the reader spins forever, leaking a thread. Even on success the assert can run while a read is still in-flight, so later exceptions are missed and the still-running tight loop with no sleep hammers the server and can interfere with subsequent tests. Consequence is hangs, leaks, flaky results and missed regressions. Store the Thread, set the flag in finally, join with timeout, and throttle the loop.

title: Concurrency test never requests subgroup counts so it does not cover the fix
body: The fixed method is GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount, which is only invoked when subgroup counts are requested via GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount when subGroupsCount is true. The new test only calls groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true), i.e. brief representation without subgroup counts. Because it never enables that path it exercises neither the old NullPointerException nor the new null handling, so it would pass with or without the fix and gives false confidence. The concurrent reads must request subgroup counts/hierarchy to be a valid regression test.

title: Negative queryset slice from user-controlled cursor
