body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result allows cursor.offset < 0 to flow directly into queryset[start_offset:stop] when enable_advanced_features is true. Offset comes from the user-supplied cursor string (Cursor.from_string parses int(bits[1]) with no range check). Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and raise ValueError, so a crafted cursor like 0:-5:0 turns a paginated GET into a 500 instead of a 400, giving any caller who can reach the endpoint a trivial DoS. The comment claiming the ORM handles negative slicing automatically is false, and on list-like semantics a negative start wraps from the end and returns unintended tail rows.

title: Numeric cursor key used for datetime-ordered audit logs
body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does math.floor/ceil on getattr(item, self.key) and value_from_cursor returns the raw int cursor value. The only caller in src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py uses order_by='-datetime', so the key is a datetime object. math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError when building next/prev cursors, breaking page 2+ with a 500, and build_queryset would compare a datetime column to int 0/cursor value, causing a DB type error or wrong filtering and full scan.

title: Forward negative offset silently clamped to zero
body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py BasePaginator.get_result now does start_offset = max(0, offset) for non-prev cursors instead of rejecting it. Every other offset-based paginator in the same file raises BadPaginationError (400) for offset < 0. Silently rewriting a corrupt/forged cursor to 0 returns the first page as if valid, causing duplicate pages and infinite client loops and hiding caller bugs, while the is_prev path still passes negative offsets through to Django slicing where they raise ValueError.

title: Overly broad gate for unsafe pagination path
body: In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py the optimized/advanced pagination path is gated by request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access. has_global_access means access to all teams, not an admin/owner/audit role, and can be true for regular members. This exposes the negative-offset pagination path advertised as for authorized administrators to a much larger population than intended.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate datetime ordering
body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py line 840, OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does int(math.floor(value))/int(math.ceil(value)) on the sort-key attribute. The only caller added in this PR (src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py line 80) uses order_by="-datetime", so value is a datetime.datetime, not a number, which raises TypeError on every page. Even if it did not raise, value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor value while build_queryset compares it against a datetime column with >=/<=, producing type-mismatched SQL or wrong pages. Consequence: the new optimized path always 500s or returns incorrect audit-log pages.

title: Negative queryset slicing is unsupported and attacker-triggerable
body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py line 882, when enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset < 0 the code executes list(queryset[start_offset:stop]) with a negative start_offset. Django QuerySets explicitly do not support negative indexing/slicing and raise AssertionError, contrary to the inline comment claiming Django handles it automatically. Cursor strings of the form value:offset:is_prev are client-controlled via Cursor.from_string, so a caller of the new optimized_pagination=true path can craft a negative-offset cursor to trigger an unhandled 500 (DoS). If the slice ever operated on a list, negative start would wrap around and return tail rows outside the requested page, breaking completeness of audit logs.

title: BasePaginator still passes negative offsets for prev cursors
body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py line 182, BasePaginator.get_result now does start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset, so forward pagination clamps negatives but prev-page (is_prev=True) pagination passes the raw negative offset to queryset[start_offset:stop]. This still hits Django's unsupported negative-slice path and raises AssertionError on a crafted prev cursor, turning all existing cursor-paginated endpoints into a 500 instead of rejecting the cursor. The later check len(results) == offset + limit + extra also uses the negative offset, so prev-page extra-row trimming is mathematically wrong even if slicing succeeded, causing duplicated or missing rows.

title: Untested privileged pagination path for compliance-critical logs
body: In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py lines 70-83, a new public query parameter optimized_pagination=true switches audit-log listing from DateTimePaginator to OptimizedCursorPaginator for superusers or members with global access. No tests are added for the branch or for OptimizedCursorPaginator, despite audit logs being compliance-critical. Consequence: a broken datetime-incompatible paginator with unsafe offset handling is exposed to privileged viewers without coverage, risking outages and incomplete/duplicated audit history going undetected.

title: Negative queryset slice allowed via enable_advanced_features
body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset < 0 the code does queryset[cursor.offset:stop] directly. Django QuerySets do not support negative slicing and raise AssertionError('Negative indexing is not supported'), so a forged cursor such as '0:-5:0' with ?optimized_pagination=true triggers a 500/DoS. The comments admit the intent ('enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds') which is an unsafe pagination primitive, opposite to OffsetPaginator/ChainPaginator/MergingOffsetPaginator in the same file which all raise BadPaginationError on offset < 0. Fix by rejecting negative offsets with BadPaginationError.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator breaks datetime ordering
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does math.floor/ceil on getattr(item, self.key) and value_from_cursor returns raw cursor.value as int. The only caller orders by '-datetime' where the attribute is a datetime object. math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError, and build_queryset would compare a datetime column to integer 0 via extra where clause. DateTimePaginator exists specifically to convert via timestamp*1000. Consequence: any audit-log request using the optimized path crashes instead of paginating. Fix by reusing DateTimePaginator logic or disallowing this paginator for date keys.

title: Unknown kwarg enable_advanced_features passed to Endpoint.paginate
body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint calls self.paginate(..., paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator, ..., enable_advanced_features=True). This PR does not change the base Endpoint.paginate implementation, whose signature only accepts request/queryset/paginator_cls/order_by/on_results/count_hits etc. Passing an arbitrary paginator kwarg through paginate will raise TypeError: paginate() got an unexpected keyword argument, breaking the optimized path for superusers/global-access users. Fix by not adding query-param-gated paginator kwargs or by explicitly constructing the paginator.

title: BasePaginator silently clamps negative offsets instead of rejecting
body: BasePaginator.get_result was changed from queryset[offset:stop] to max(0,offset) for forward cursors while prev cursors still use raw offset, and the later check len(results)==offset+limit+extra still uses the original offset. Other paginators in the same file raise BadPaginationError for offset<0. Consequence: a forged forward cursor with negative offset now silently returns the first page instead of an error, hiding client bugs and producing inconsistent next/prev cursors, while a prev-direction negative offset still crashes in the ORM. Fix by validating offset and raising BadPaginationError.

title: New paginator added without tests
body: The PR adds a 90-line OptimizedCursorPaginator and changes BasePaginator boundary handling with no tests. There is no coverage for negative offsets, datetime ordering, cursor round-trip, or the ?optimized_pagination=true endpoint branch, so the TypeError on datetime keys and the negative-slice crash would not be caught. Add unit tests for paginator with numeric and datetime keys and for rejection of negative offsets.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator passes attacker-controlled negative slice to Django
body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result allows start_offset = cursor.offset when enable_advanced_features and offset < 0, then does queryset[start_offset:stop]. Cursor comes from user-supplied cursor string parsed as value:offset:is_prev, so an attacker can supply a negative offset. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing/slicing and raise AssertionError/ValueError, causing a 500/DoS. The comment claiming Django handles negative slicing automatically is false. If slicing ever succeeded Python semantics would return the tail of the table, bypassing the intended cursor position.

title: Sensitive audit-log endpoint gated to buggy paginator by weak check
body: In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py a user-controlled query param optimized_pagination=true combined with enable_advanced = is_superuser or member.has_global_access routes AuditLogEntry queries to OptimizedCursorPaginator with enable_advanced_features=True. has_global_access is true for many non-admin members, far broader than administrators, so many users can reach the new negative-offset pagination path on a sensitive audit-log dataset. This expands attack surface for DoS and incorrect pagination on security-relevant data.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator uses numeric key logic for datetime ordering
body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does math.floor/ceil on getattr(item, self.key) assuming a numeric sort key. The audit-log endpoint uses it with order_by='-datetime' where the key is a datetime object. math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError, so building next/prev cursors for any optimized audit-log request crashes instead of paginating.

title: BasePaginator now allows negative slices for prev cursors
body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py BasePaginator.get_result was changed to start_offset = max(0, offset) if not is_prev else offset. For is_prev cursors a negative offset is passed directly to queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django does not support negative slicing and raises, so a crafted prev cursor value:negative-offset:1 crashes all BasePaginator users with a 500. For forward cursors it silently clamps invalid negative offsets to 0, returning the first page instead of an error and masking bad cursors.

title: ZUNIONSTORE without AGGREGATE corrupts span scores by summing
body: In src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua the merges use zunionstore(set_key, 2, set_key, span_key) with default AGGREGATE SUM. The Python bulk zadd puts a whole subsegment into the parent key, then the per-span loop unions that parent key into the destination repeatedly, so after the first iteration destination and source overlap on the same payload members. Overlapping members get their end_timestamp_precise scores added (doubled, tripled), corrupting timestamps, breaking zpopmin eviction order so newest/oldest selection is wrong, and polluting scores for later merges. It must use AGGREGATE MAX.

title: Redirect-chain limit cut from 10000 to 1000 fragments deep traces
body: In src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua the redirect-following loop was reduced from 10000 to 1000 iterations. Traces with redirect chains deeper than 1000 will stop early with an unresolved set_span_id, leaving spans that belong to one segment in separate Redis sets. Those flush as fragmented segments with wrong segment_id and is_segment flags, causing duplicates and incomplete segments downstream with no metric for truncation.

title: Direct end_timestamp_precise access crashes consumer on old messages
body: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py process_batch does val["end_timestamp_precise"] with no fallback. Kafka messages buffered before the deploy, produced by older relays, or malformed will lack the field and raise KeyError inside the batch task. That crashes the processing step, stalls commits, causes backlog and repeated retry on a poison message. The field was previously optional for the buffer path, so this is a breaking contract change.

title: Python max-segment-spans guard removed, risks huge segment loads
body: In src/sentry/spans/buffer.py _load_segment_data no longer checks max_segment_spans (1001) and drops oversized segments; it only checks max_segment_bytes. A segment with many tiny spans can be far over the count limit while staying under 10 MiB, causing huge in-memory lists, slow zscan loops, and oversized Kafka produces that can OOM the consumer or downstream. Redis-side zpopmin eviction to 1000 is best-effort and does not cover pre-existing SET keys, races, or other writers, so the Python guard is still needed. max_segment_spans is now dead config.

title: Misleading comment claims negative offsets are safe
body: In src/sentry/utils/cursors.py the Cursor constructor comment says negative offsets are a performance optimization for advanced pagination. Negative offsets are not safe: Django QuerySets reject negative slices and other paginators explicitly raise BadPaginationError for negative offsets. The comment encourages callers to rely on unsafe behavior and contradicts the actual pagination contracts.

title: BasePaginator allows negative slice that crashes
body: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 computes start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset and then does queryset[start_offset:stop], so a prev cursor with negative offset is passed directly to Django. Django QuerySets reject negative slice bounds with AssertionError (negative indexing is not supported), unlike Python lists, while sibling paginators raise BadPaginationError for offset<0. A client-supplied cursor like 0:-5:1 therefore causes an unhandled exception. Consequence: any authenticated user can trigger 500 errors on BasePaginator-based endpoints via crafted cursor (DoS).

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator breaks datetime ordering
body: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/ceil directly on getattr(item, self.key) and value_from_cursor returns the raw int cursor.value. When used with order_by='-datetime' as in OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint, the attribute is a datetime object so math.floor raises TypeError, and build_queryset compares a datetime column to an int instead of converting via datetime.fromtimestamp like DateTimePaginator does. Consequence: the optimized audit-log path crashes with 500 or filters incorrectly.

title: Negative-offset slicing crashes instead of paginating
body: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:880 enables queryset[start_offset:stop] with negative start_offset when enable_advanced_features is true, claiming Django handles negative slicing and that it is safe because permissions are checked at queryset level. Django QuerySets reject negative slice bounds with AssertionError, unlike Python lists. A client-supplied cursor such as 0:-10:0 therefore raises an unhandled exception. Consequence: crafted cursor causes 500 errors (DoS) and the safety comment is false; other paginators correctly raise BadPaginationError for offset<0.

title: Undocumented optimized pagination exposes broken paginator
body: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:82 adds a client-controlled ?optimized_pagination=true switch that constructs OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by='-datetime' and enable_advanced_features=True for superusers or members with global access. That paginator only supports numeric keys and explicitly enables negative-offset slicing, neither of which works for datetime-ordered audit logs. Consequence: privileged callers can trigger 500s and get inconsistent pagination behavior versus the default DateTimePaginator via an undocumented param.

title: Misleading comment endorses negative offsets without validation
body: src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:28 adds a comment saying negative offsets are allowed for advanced pagination, but Cursor.__init__/from_string still accepts any int offset with no validation, while OffsetPaginator, ChainPaginator and others reject offset<0 with BadPaginationError and BasePaginator/OptimizedCursorPaginator crash on negatives. Consequence: developers are misled to pass negative cursors expecting support, leading to 500 errors.

title: Negative cursor offset passed to queryset slicing
body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py:880 OptimizedCursorPaginator allows attacker-controlled cursor.offset < 0 to be used directly as queryset[start_offset:stop] when enable_advanced_features is true. All other paginators reject offset < 0 with BadPaginationError. Django QuerySets do not support negative slicing and raise AssertionError, and the comment claiming Django handles it automatically is false. An attacker can supply a cursor like '0:-5:0' via the cursor query param to trigger a 500/DoS or unintended row windows, bypassing pagination bound checks.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator assumes numeric key but used with datetime ordering
body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py:839 OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does math.floor/ceil on getattr(item, self.key) and value_from_cursor returns cursor.value as int. The audit-logs endpoint uses it with order_by='-datetime' where the key is a datetime. math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError and the queryset filter comparing a datetime column to an int is type-wrong. Requesting organization_auditlogs with optimized_pagination=true will crash instead of paginating.

title: BasePaginator allows negative offset for prev cursors
body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 start_offset is max(0,offset) for forward cursors but raw offset for is_prev cursors, so queryset[offset:stop] can receive a negative start. Django raises AssertionError for negative slices, causing 500s on crafted prev cursors. The later trimming check len(results)==offset+limit+extra still uses the original negative offset while the query used start_offset, so page trimming is also inconsistent.

title: SET to ZSET change breaks existing Redis keys
body: In src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 process_spans now uses ZADD and src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua uses ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZPOPMIN and _load_segment_data uses ZSCAN, but existing keys were written as SETs with SADD/SUNIONSTORE/SSCAN. Redis enforces one type per key and returns WRONGTYPE on mismatch. During rollout or with leftover keys, inserts, merges, and loads will error, losing or stalling spans. No migration or dual-read handling is provided.

title: ZUNIONSTORE default SUM corrupts scores on duplicates
body: In src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:47 zunionstore is called without AGGREGATE option, so Redis defaults to SUM. Members are span payloads scored by end_timestamp_precise. If the same payload exists in both source sets due to retries, reprocessing, or overlapping merges, its timestamp is summed (e.g., doubled), corrupting ordering and causing zpopmin eviction to keep/drop the wrong spans.

title: Missing end_timestamp_precise crashes consumer batch
body: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py:141 process_batch does val['end_timestamp_precise'] with direct indexing. Previously Span did not require this field and old messages lack it. A single message without the field raises KeyError, failing the whole batch and, as a poison pill, repeatedly blocking progress and causing backlog/lag. It needs .get with validation or fallback.

title: Redirect depth cut fragments deep traces
body: In src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 the redirect-following loop was cut from 10000 to 1000 iterations. Traces with parent chains deeper than 1000 will stop early without fully resolving set_span_id, leaving the segment split across multiple span-buf:s: keys that never merge, causing duplicate/incomplete flushed segments.

title: Span-count guard removed, silent truncation without observability
body: In src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:150 max_segment_spans remains configured but _load_segment_data no longer checks len(payloads) against it or emits segment_span_count_exceeded/log. Oversized segments are now silently truncated at insert by zpopmin to 1000 lowest scores evicted with no metric or log. Operators lose visibility and oldest spans are silently dropped, changing the prior drop-entire-segment behavior to silent partial data loss.

title: Cache key uses Python hash() which is unstable across processes
body: In src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py at line 27 the cache key is built with hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids))). Python's hash() for tuples is salted per process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so different web workers compute different keys for the same projects and never share cache entries, defeating the optimization. hash() can also be negative and can collide, causing two different project sets to share an eligibility entry and return upsampled counts for non-allowlisted projects or vice versa. Use a deterministic encoding such as comma-joined sorted ids or hashlib.

title: 60s cached allowlist eligibility returns wrong counts after config change
body: In src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py at line 38 allowlist eligibility is cached for 60 seconds. If the project allowlist option changes, queries for up to 60s will use the stale boolean and either apply sum(sample_weight) to non-allowlisted projects (10x inflation) or use raw count() for allowlisted projects (10x undercount). The helper invalidate_upsampling_cache is never called anywhere, so there is no invalidation path. Either remove the cache (options.get is already cheap/cached) or wire invalidation/versioning.

title: upsampled_count sum(sample_weight) without null handling undercounts
body: In src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py at line 1046 upsampled_count is defined as toInt64(sum(sample_weight)). Events that were not client-sampled or predate the column have NULL/missing sample_weight and contribute 0/NULL to sum instead of 1, so mixing sampled and unsampled events undercounts. toInt64 on NULL/errors and truncation of fractional weights also corrupts results. It needs coalesce/ifNull handling e.g. sum(coalesce(sample_weight,1)) with rounding, not a bare sum.

title: Error-query check only matches event.type:error substring
body: In src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py at line 137 _is_error_focused_query returns True only if 'event.type:error' is a substring of request query. The common Discover error filter '!event.type:transaction' (used in the same endpoint for dashboard split) is therefore never recognized, so Discover error queries silently skip upsampling and undercount 10x. Conversely a query like 'event.type:error OR event.type:transaction' contains the substring and would incorrectly upsample transaction rows, inflating counts.

title: Upsampling eligibility uses outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset
body: In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_events_stats.py at line 220 _get_event_stats checks is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects with the outer closure variable dataset instead of its scoped_dataset argument. The dashboard-split factory calls _get_event_stats with different datasets (discover vs metrics/transactions) but the upsampling decision stays tied to the original dataset, so split error queries can be incorrectly skipped or applied.

title: Split error query string never seen by upsampling check
body: In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_events_stats.py at line 383 the dashboard-split path builds errors_only_query and transactions_only_query as local strings, but _is_error_focused_query inspects request.GET['query'], not the query argument passed to _get_event_stats. The appended 'AND !event.type:transaction' / 'AND event.type:transaction' therefore never affects the upsampling decision, so split Discover error queries are misclassified even if substring handling is fixed.

title: upsampled_count exposed as public function bypasses allowlist
body: In src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py at line 1041 upsampled_count is registered without private=True, unlike the neighboring internal SnQLFunction. Any user can explicitly query upsampled_count() even for projects not in the error-upsampling allowlist, getting 10x-inflated numbers or errors when sample_weight is missing, bypassing the server-side allowlist gate in error_upsampling.py.

title: Only exact count() is rewritten, other aggregates silently stay raw
body: In src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py at line 92 transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling rewrites only columns where lower().strip() == 'count()'. Dashboards/widgets using count_if, count_unique, failure_count, equations, or count() with different aliasing/casing variations keep raw counts while count() buckets are multiplied by sample weight, producing internally inconsistent charts with mixed raw and upsampled series.

title: Integration tests share upsampling cache across mocked allowlists
body: In tests/snuba/api/endpoints/test_organization_events_stats.py at line 3552 the OrganizationEventsStatsErrorUpsamplingTest cases mock options.get with different allowlists but use the same organization and project ids and never clear the cache in error_upsampling.py. The first test's cached eligibility (60s TTL) leaks into later tests with partial/empty allowlists, making the suite order-dependent and able to falsely pass/fail. Tests must clear the cache key or patch the cache.

title: Unstable Python hash() used for shared cache key
body: The eligibility cache key is built with hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids))). Python documents hash() as unstable across processes and versions (hash randomization), so the same project set maps to different keys in different workers/restarts. Since the cache is shared (memcached/Redis), cross-process lookups miss and each process creates its own key for the same projects, defeating the 60s caching and bloating the cache. Use a stable encoding such as comma-joined sorted IDs or hashlib.

title: 60-second eligibility cache returns stale upsampling decisions
body: is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects caches allowlist eligibility (True/False) for 60 seconds keyed only by org and projects. If the project allowlist changes, queries for up to 60s use the old decision and return raw count() when scaled upsampled_count() was required or vice versa, with errors scaled by 1/sample_rate (e.g. 10x). The invalidate_upsampling_cache helper defined in the same file is never called in the PR, so there is no invalidation path.

title: Upsampling check uses outer dataset instead of executed scoped_dataset
body: _get_event_stats receives scoped_dataset, the dataset actually queried. The dashboard-split logic calls it with different datasets (scoped_dataset vs discover for errors-only and transactions-only subqueries). The eligibility check passes the outer dataset closed over from get(), not scoped_dataset, so an errors-only subquery run on discover can be judged as a metrics/transactions query and skip upsampling, or a transaction query can be judged as errors and get upsampled, returning wrong counts.

title: Error-focus check reads original HTTP query and only matches event.type:error
body: _is_error_focused_query inspects request.GET.get("query"), the original HTTP parameter, not the query string argument actually sent to Snuba. Dashboard-split code re-executes _get_event_stats with rewritten queries like (query) AND !event.type:transaction for errors and (query) AND event.type:transaction for transactions while request.GET is unchanged. The check also only matches substring event.type:error, so a discover errors-only query built from !event.type:transaction is treated as non-error and undercounts, while a transactions-only subquery issued when the HTTP query contained event.type:error is treated as error and sums sample_weight which does not exist for transactions.

title: upsampled_count sums nullable sample_weight without fallback and truncates
body: The new Discover function is toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) with no null handling. Any error row without sample_weight (events written before sampling, backfills, mixed data) contributes 0/NULL instead of 1, so buckets undercount and can collapse to 0. toInt64 also truncates fractional weights, so a rate that does not evenly divide 1 (e.g. 0.33 -> weight ~3.03) is systematically biased low on every bucket. It should sum coalesced weights with rounding, e.g. sum(ifNull(sample_weight, 1)).

title: Internal upsampled_count function exposed as public API
body: SnQLFunction upsampled_count is registered without private=True, unlike neighboring internal aggregates. That makes upsampled_count() directly queryable by any Discover user. Because it sums the internal sample_weight column, callers can invoke it on non-allowlisted projects or datasets where the column is missing or 1 and receive misleading scaled numbers, and can probe internal sampling state. Internal upsampling helpers should be private.

title: Test factory blindly trusts client-supplied sample rate
body: _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling copies client-controlled contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate into normalized_data[sample_rate] with no validation. It uses if client_sample_rate so rate 0 is dropped, swallows all errors with bare except pass, overwrites any existing sample_rate, and accepts out-of-range or non-numeric values. Tests built on it therefore validate upsampling against arbitrary client-supplied weights (a client sending 0.001 would inflate counts 1000x) that production ingestion must reject, making endpoint tests unrealistic and hiding a trust-boundary issue.

title: Column transform only handles exact count() and hardcodes alias
body: transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling only rewrites a column whose lowercased stripped value equals exactly count(). Variants such as count() as foo, count_if, count_unique, or equations containing count() are left as raw counts, so a request mixes raw and scaled series in one response. When it does match it forces upsampled_count() as count, discarding the caller's alias and injecting AS syntax into RPC y_axes paths that expect bare aggregates, risking validation failures or mislabeled series.

title: Main upsampling entry point and cache behavior untested
body: The test class exercises only private helpers (_are_all_projects_error_upsampled, transform, _is_error_focused_query, _should_apply_sample_weight_transform) and never calls the public is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects. Cache-key construction, 60s staleness, hash instability, and dataset/request interaction therefore have zero unit coverage, and the SnubaParams fixture with start=None/end=None is never used, so the caching bugs shipped in this PR cannot be caught.

title: 60s eligibility cache returns stale upsampling decisions
body: In src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py at line 27-38, is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects caches _are_all_projects_error_upsampled result for 60 seconds keyed by organization.id and hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))). invalidate_upsampling_cache is never called in the PR, so adding or removing a project from issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist has no effect for up to 60s. During the window queries use the wrong aggregation: removed projects keep using sum(sample_weight) and overcount by 1/sample_rate (10x in the added tests), added projects keep using count() and undercount. The key also uses Python hash() so distinct project sets can collide and share an entry, and includes organization.id though the check ignores organization.

title: Upsampling check uses outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset
body: In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_events_stats.py at line 221, _get_event_stats receives scoped_dataset which varies for dashboard-widget split (discover vs metrics-enhanced) but passes the outer closure variable dataset to is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects. For example a metrics-enhanced widget split that executes an errors-only query on discover will be judged as a metrics dataset, _should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns False, so no upsampling is applied and sampled errors are undercounted by the sampling factor. The opposite mismatch can enable upsampling for the wrong dataset.

title: Upsampling decision reads original request instead of executed query
body: In src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py at line 135, _is_error_focused_query reads request.GET.get("query") while src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_events_stats.py executes rewritten queries passed as the query argument (e.g. errors_only_query "(orig) AND !event.type:transaction" and transactions_only_query). The eligibility check therefore ignores the actual query: an errors-only split derived from an empty original query will not upsample and will undercount, and a transactions-only split derived from an error query will upsample and overcount or drop rows.

title: Substring error check misclassifies negated and mixed queries
body: In src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py at line 137, _is_error_focused_query uses 'event.type:error in query.lower()'. This is True for '!event.type:error' which means NOT error (transactions-only), so a discover transactions-only query will be upsampled with sum(sample_weight) which the code itself says does not exist for transactions, causing wrong counts or missing-column errors. The same check returns True for mixed 'event.type:error OR event.type:transaction' (upsampling transactions) and False for empty queries that include errors, so sampled errors are undercounted.

title: upsampled_count sums nullable weight and truncates
body: In src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py at line 1041, upsampled_count is defined as toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) with no coalesce or rounding. Historical events from before allowlisting, backfilled events, and any mixed transaction rows have NULL/missing sample_weight and will be ignored or make the sum NULL, undercounting. Float weights (e.g. 1/0.3) are truncated by toInt64 instead of rounded, systematically biasing counts low.

title: Internal upsampling aggregate exposed publicly
body: In src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py at line 1041, SnQLFunction("upsampled_count") omits private=True unlike neighboring internal aggregates. Any API user can therefore query upsampled_count() directly via discover, bypassing the allowlist gate in is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects and obtaining raw sum(sample_weight) for non-allowlisted projects, creating unintended API surface and inconsistent counts.

title: Test factory overwrites sample_rate without validation
body: In src/sentry/testutils/factories.py at line 344, _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling unconditionally overwrites normalized_data["sample_rate"] from contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate even if a rate was already set, with no range check. It accepts >1, negative, NaN/inf and non-numeric input (swallowed by bare except: pass), producing unrealistic test events. The integration tests then depend on this path to assert 10x counts, masking ingestion bugs.

title: No coverage for caching entry point
body: In tests/sentry/api/helpers/test_error_upsampling.py at line 19, tests import only _are_all_projects_error_upsampled, _is_error_focused_query, _should_apply_sample_weight_transform and transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling and never exercise is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects. The 60s cache, hash-based key, and dataset/request interaction that determine real counts are untested. The endpoint tests mock options but never clear the shared cache, allowing stale eligibility to leak across test cases.

title: Error IDs mismatched to nodestore data via zip(values())
body: In fetch_error_details the code builds node_ids from error_ids, calls nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids) which returns a dict keyed by node_id, then does zip(error_ids, events.values()). Dict values order is not guaranteed to match error_ids order, and missing keys shrink values. The result pairs the wrong title/message/timestamp with the wrong error id. Consequence is wrong error context merged into replay breadcrumb logs sent to Seer, producing misleading AI summaries.

title: Flagged table visualization discards real query results
body: When organization.features includes use-table-widget-visualization the code renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded columns={[]} and tableData {data:[], meta:{fields:{}, units:{}}} instead of using result.data, result.meta, fields, and fieldAliases computed above. Consequence is dashboards behind the flag show empty tables regardless of query results.

title: Merged-PR template calls truncate on wrong class
body: The diff defines _truncate_title as a staticmethod on CommitContextIntegration but get_merged_pr_single_issue_template calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title. PRCommentWorkflow is not the class defining the helper in this file. If PRCommentWorkflow does not provide that method this raises NameError/AttributeError at runtime. Consequence is suspect-issues PR comment generation for GitHub and GitLab crashes and no comment is posted.

title: Age/timestamp exclusivity uses truthiness and neither is required
body: validate_timestamp checks if self.initial_data.get("age") and validate_age checks get("timestamp"). Values of 0 are falsy, so a report with age=0 plus timestamp or timestamp=0 plus age incorrectly passes, and both age and timestamp are optional so a report with neither also passes. The Reporting specs require exactly one of age or timestamp. Consequence is invalid reports are accepted and mixed-spec reports with zero values are not rejected.

title: Column fallback crashes when meta is missing
body: The fallback does Object.keys(tableData?.meta.fields) and tableData?.meta.fields[key]. The optional chain only guards tableData, not meta. If tableData is undefined or has no meta, this throws TypeError. Consequence is dashboard or story rendering an empty or loading table crashes instead of rendering empty.

title: Attribute-keys query key omits organization and changes caching
body: The refactor replaces useApiQuery with path /organizations/<slug>/trace-items/attributes/ with useQuery keyed only as ['use-trace-item-attribute-keys', queryOptions] where queryOptions has no org slug. Switching organizations reuses the prior org cached TagCollection. It also drops staleTime 0, refetchOnWindowFocus false, and retry false. Consequence is stale cross-org attribute suggestions and extra retries and refetches.

title: Analytics recorded before feature and validation checks
body: analytics.record for preprod_artifact.api.assemble runs before the organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble feature check and before schema, missing-chunk, and state validation. Every POST including disabled-feature, malformed, and unauthorized calls is counted. Consequence is inflated assemble metrics and stored organization/project/user ids for requests that should not count.

title: fetch_error_details misaligns errors via zip(events.values())
body: In src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py fetch_error_details builds node_ids from error_ids, calls nodestore.get_multi(node_ids), then zips error_ids with events.values(). Dict values order is not guaranteed to match error_ids order, and missing keys are omitted rather than None, so titles/messages/timestamps get attributed to the wrong error id and some errors are dropped/duplicated. The Seer prompt then receives wrong error context. Fix by looking up each node_id in the returned dict.

title: TableWidgetVisualization rendered with empty data
body: In static/app/views/dashboards/widgetCard/chart.tsx when organization.features includes use-table-widget-visualization the code renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded columns={[]} and tableData {data:[], meta:{fields:{}, units:{}}}, discarding result.data, result.meta, fields, and custom renderers computed just above. Enabling the flag turns every dashboard table into an empty table. Wire the real query results into the new visualization.

title: get_merged_pr_single_issue_template calls wrong class
body: In src/sentry/integrations/source_code_management/commit_context.py CommitContextIntegration.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title, but _truncate_title is defined on CommitContextIntegration. This raises AttributeError/NameError at runtime when formatting suspect-issue PR comments for GitHub/GitLab, breaking merged-PR comments. Call the local implementation instead.

title: Mutual-exclusivity check uses truthiness, allows age/timestamp 0
body: In src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py validate_timestamp checks if self.initial_data.get("age") and validate_age checks if self.initial_data.get("timestamp"). Falsy values like 0 bypass the check, so a report containing both age:0 and timestamp:0 (or timestamp:0 with age) passes validation despite the spec requiring them to be mutually exclusive. Check key presence instead of truthiness.

title: error_ids depends on client field param, error context lost
body: In src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py the endpoint calls process_raw_response with fields=request.query_params.getlist("field") and then reads response[0].get("error_ids"). The frontend AI tab calls the endpoint with no field param, so error_ids is empty and fetch_error_details is never populated. The new error-context feature is dead unless callers guess to pass field=error_ids. Explicitly request error_ids for the internal query.

title: Analytics recorded before feature/validation checks
body: In src/sentry/preprod/api/endpoints/organization_preprod_artifact_assemble.py analytics.record for preprod_artifact.api.assemble runs before the organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble feature check and before body validation. Disabled, unauthorized, or malformed requests are counted as assembles, inflating metrics. Move the record call after the feature gate and successful validation.

title: Column fallback crashes when meta.fields is missing
body: In static/app/views/dashboards/widgets/tableWidget/tableWidgetVisualization.tsx the fallback columnOrder does Object.keys(tableData?.meta.fields). If tableData or meta.fields is undefined/null from an empty or malformed response, Object.keys throws TypeError and the whole widget crashes. Guard with fallback to empty object.

title: Header alignment uses display name instead of field key
body: In static/app/views/dashboards/widgets/tableWidget/defaultTableCellRenderers.tsx renderDefaultHeadCell calls fieldAlignment(column.name, ...) while the body renderer uses column.key. When a custom display name is supplied (e.g. Count of Span Duration), alignment is computed from the display string instead of the field type, so numeric columns can be left-aligned. Use column.key for alignment.

title: Mismatched error IDs to nodestore data via zip(values)
body: In src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py line 118, fetch_error_details pairs IDs with data via zip(error_ids, events.values()). nodestore get_multi returns a dict keyed by node ID, and values() order is not guaranteed to match error_ids order, and missing keys shrink the dict. This misaligns titles/messages/timestamps to the wrong error IDs or drops them, causing the AI breadcrumb summary to include incorrect error context.

title: Mutual-exclusion check uses truthiness, misses zero values
body: In src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py lines 52 and 58, validate_timestamp checks if self.initial_data.get("age") and validate_age checks if self.initial_data.get("timestamp"). When the other field is 0 (falsy, e.g. timestamp 0 or age 0) the check does not trigger, so a payload containing both age and timestamp can pass validation. This violates the Working Draft vs Editor's Draft exclusivity rule and lets invalid reports through to metrics.

title: Analytics recorded before feature and validation checks
body: In src/sentry/preprod/api/endpoints/organization_preprod_artifact_assemble.py line 81, analytics.record for preprod_artifact.api.assemble runs before the feature flag check and before body/chunk validation. Requests that will be rejected with 404/400 and unauthenticated requests are still counted, inflating analytics and recording user_id for failed requests. The record call should occur after auth, feature, and validation succeed.

title: PR comment helpers defined on wrong class, causing AttributeError
body: In src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py line 406 (and same in gitlab integration), the workflow calls self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template and self.get_environment_info. In src/sentry/integrations/source_code_management/commit_context.py those helpers are defined on CommitContextIntegration, not on PRCommentWorkflow, and get_merged_pr_single_issue_template internally calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title while _truncate_title is defined on CommitContextIntegration. At runtime this raises AttributeError, breaking suspect-issues PR comments for GitHub and GitLab.

title: Flagged table visualization discards real query results
body: In static/app/views/dashboards/widgetCard/chart.tsx around line 165, when organization.features includes use-table-widget-visualization the code renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded columns={[]} and empty tableData data:[] meta fields:{} instead of mapping result.data, result.meta, fields, and field aliases. Enabling the flag turns every dashboard table widget blank, losing data the old StyledSimpleTableChart displayed.

title: Crash when table meta is missing
body: In static/app/views/dashboards/widgets/tableWidget/tableWidgetVisualization.tsx line 94, fallback columns use Object.keys(tableData?.meta.fields). Optional chaining only guards tableData, not meta, so if tableData exists but meta is undefined this throws TypeError. The component should use tableData?.meta?.fields ?? {} and similarly guard type lookup, otherwise dashboards with empty/error responses crash.

title: Hook can return undefined attributes breaking callers
body: In static/app/views/explore/hooks/useTraceItemAttributeKeys.tsx line 59, the hook returns attributes as isFetching ? previous : data where data from useQuery is undefined on first load or error and previous is undefined initially. Callers expect TagCollection object and do Object.keys, spread, or hasOwnProperty. Returning undefined causes TypeError. It should default to {} like the previous useApiQuery implementation did.

title: Changing autofix default retroactively disables existing projects
body: In src/sentry/projectoptions/defaults.py line 205 (and constants/projectoptions), default for sentry:autofix_automation_tuning changes from low to off. Project options without an explicit value inherit the new default, so existing projects that never opted out silently change from low automation to off without migration or epoch gating. This is a behavioral contract break that disables autofix broadly.

title: KeyError crash when Integration metadata lacks sender
body: GitHubInstallation.dispatch does integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] to compare the OAuth-authenticated GitHub user to the installer. Sender is only set in build_integration when state contains sender, so legacy integrations or records created without a webhook have no sender key. Any reinstall attempt for such an installation raises KeyError and returns HTTP 500 instead of rendering github-integration-failed.html, blocking installation and exposing an internal error.

title: OAuth token exchange failures raise 500 instead of install error
body: OAuthLoginView.dispatch calls safe_urlopen to exchange code for access_token and then get_user_info to fetch login outside any try/except. Network errors, timeouts, GitHub 4xx/5xx, or invalid/expired/reused code can raise instead of returning a payload without access_token. Only the parse_qsl body parsing is guarded, so those failures bubble up as HTTP 500 instead of the intended github-integration-failed.html error page described in the PR.

title: Fresh installations bypass installer identity check
body: GitHubInstallation.dispatch returns pipeline.next_step() immediately when Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id) raises DoesNotExist, without comparing pipeline github_authenticated_user to anything. Installation IDs are small sequential integers enumerable via the GitHub App API, so anyone who knows or guesses an installation_id can link another account's GitHub installation to their own Sentry organization if the webhook-created Integration row has not arrived yet, defeating the PR's stated goal of ensuring the completer is the installer.

title: test_installation_not_found no longer covers 404 handling
body: test_installation_not_found stubs GET /app/installations/{id} with 404 but then drives the OAuth step with state ddd023... which does not match the pipeline signature 9cae5e... used elsewhere. OAuthLoginView therefore returns Invalid installation request on state mismatch before build_integration is ever reached. The 404 branch in build_integration that raises The GitHub installation could not be found is left unexercised, so regressions there will not be caught.

title: New installations bypass GitHub-user validation
body: In GitHubInstallation.dispatch when Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id) raises DoesNotExist the code returns pipeline.next_step() without comparing pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") to the installer. The sender check on lines 501-505 only runs when an Integration row already exists. Since the Integration row is created asynchronously by the GitHub webhook, an attacker can complete the pipeline before the webhook creates the row, or when the webhook is delayed/failed, and link an arbitrary installation_id without proving they installed the GitHub App. The existing tests prove this: assert_setup_flow creates an integration with no webhook/sender and succeeds.

title: Unhandled KeyError on missing integration sender metadata
body: The check does integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] with direct indexing. Metadata is not guaranteed to contain sender: build_integration only sets metadata["sender"] if state.get("sender"), and the pipeline only ever binds installation_id and github_authenticated_user, so pipeline-created integrations have no sender. Pre-existing/old integrations also lack it. When an orphaned Integration exists with no OrganizationIntegration, a retry hits this line and raises KeyError, producing a 500 instead of the intended github-integration-failed.html error page and breaking reinstall flows.

title: OAuth token exchange and user lookup can raise 500
body: OAuthLoginView calls safe_urlopen for the access_token exchange and get_user_info for /user with no try/except. Network errors, non-2xx from GitHub, or an invalid/expired code/token will raise instead of returning a payload without access_token/login. Only missing keys in the parsed payload are handled. The consequence is a 500 on exactly the failure cases the PR description says should show the friendly Invalid installation request page.

title: Pipeline state poisoned before OAuth state validation
body: OAuthLoginView binds request.GET installation_id into pipeline state before checking if request.GET state equals pipeline.signature. A request with an invalid/forged state still mutates the stored installation_id before error() is returned. A subsequent legitimate retry that relies on pipeline.fetch_state("installation_id") will then use the attacker-controlled value, allowing fixation of the installation that will later be compared or built.

title: Empty installation_id bypasses App redirect
body: GitHubInstallation checks if installation_id is None, not if it is falsy. A request like ?installation_id= yields empty string, skips the redirect to the GitHub App URL, does Integration.objects.get(external_id="") and on DoesNotExist calls pipeline.next_step(). This proceeds to build_integration with an empty ID and a needless GitHub API call, instead of redirecting to install the App.

title: installation_not_found test no longer exercises 404
body: test_installation_not_found now sends state ddd023... which does not match the expected pipeline signature 9cae5e..., so OAuthLoginView rejects with Invalid installation request before GitHubInstallation/build_integration ever calls GET /app/installations. The stubbed 404 is never hit and the assertion was changed from The GitHub installation could not be found. The 404 handling in build_integration is therefore untested.

title: KeyError crash when Integration metadata lacks sender
body: In src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py line 503 GitHubInstallation does integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] with direct indexing. Integrations created before this feature, created via the fresh-install path in build_integration which only sets sender if state has it, or with webhook payloads lacking sender will have no "sender" key. Direct indexing raises KeyError resulting in a 500 instead of the intended install-failed page, blocking legitimate second-org installs and reinstalls after upgrade.

title: Unhandled token exchange/user lookup errors cause 500
body: In src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py OAuthLoginView calls safe_urlopen to exchange code for access_token and get_user_info to fetch login outside any handling; only body parsing is in try/except. Network errors, timeouts, non-2xx from GitHub, or ApiError from /user propagate as 500. The PR description says bad/reused code and failed token generation should show the install-failed page, but those paths crash instead of returning error().

title: First-time installs skip GitHub-user verification
body: In src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py GitHubInstallation only compares github_authenticated_user to sender when an Integration row already exists. On Integration.DoesNotExist it immediately returns pipeline.next_step() and build_integration creates the Integration without ever checking the authenticated user. An attacker who guesses an unused sequential installation_id or wins the webhook race can link a victim GitHub installation to their own Sentry org, defeating the hijack protection that only covers the already-exists branch.

title: Pipeline state mutated before OAuth state validation
body: In src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py OAuthLoginView binds request installation_id into persistent pipeline state before checking if request state equals pipeline.signature. A request with an invalid state still poisons the stored installation_id. The later legitimate GitHub callback with valid state and no installation_id then reuses the poisoned value via fetch_state fallback in GitHubInstallation, enabling installation_id fixation across steps. State must be validated before any bind_state.

title: Installation-not-found and token-failure paths no longer tested
body: In tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py test_installation_not_found stubs 404 for /app/installations but then drives setup with state ddd023... which does not match the pipeline signature, so OAuthLoginView rejects on state mismatch before build_integration ever calls GitHub. The test never exercises the 404 handling it names, and there are no tests for missing access_token, code reuse, or explicit state mismatch, leaving the new security-critical branches without coverage.

title: AssignmentSource queued timestamp frozen at import time
body: In src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py line 18, `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once at import time, so every AssignmentSource created without an explicit queued shares the same timestamp (process start time). It should be `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. Consequence is stale/wrong queued metadata in to_dict/from_dict, breaking any ordering, debugging, or expiry logic that relies on creation time.

title: to_dict returns non-JSON-serializable datetime for Celery task
body: In src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py line 28, `to_dict()` uses `asdict()` and returns a raw datetime object for `queued`. That dict is passed as `assignment_source_dict` to `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async()` in src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py. Celery task kwargs must be JSON-serializable and datetime is not, so enqueueing outbound sync for any inbound-triggered assignment will fail serialization or require pickle and break cross-silo transport. Fix by serializing queued to ISO string and parsing/validating it in from_dict.

title: should_sync signature change breaks existing overrides
body: In src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py line 382, `should_sync(self, attribute, sync_source=None)` adds a second positional argument. Any existing integration that overrides the old `def should_sync(self, attribute)` single-arg form will raise TypeError when src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py calls `should_sync('outbound_assignee', source)` with two args. Consequence is crashed outbound-sync tasks for those integrations. Needs backward-compatible *args/**kwargs handling.

title: Outbound task passes assignment_source kwarg not declared in abstract
body: In src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py line 60, the task calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=...)`, but the abstract in src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py declares `sync_assignee_outbound(self, external_issue, user, assign=True, **kwargs)` with no explicit assignment_source. Implementations matching the old exact signature without **kwargs will raise TypeError, retried 5 times then dropped, losing the sync. Those with **kwargs silently swallow the context. Tests mock ExampleIntegration so the mismatch is not caught. Fix by adding explicit param to the abstract and all implementers.

title: Status sync cycle not actually prevented (dead parameter)
body: In src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py line 416, `sync_status_outbound` gains an `assignment_source` parameter, but no caller in the diff passes it and no `should_sync(..., source)` gate is added for the status outbound path, unlike the assignee path. Inbound status changes therefore still fan out to all integrations. Consequence is resolve/unresolve sync loops remain despite the PR goal, and the dead parameter misleads callers. Wire source through status inbound/outbound like assignee or revert the param.

title: Missing test that different integration still syncs
body: In tests/sentry/models/test_groupassignee.py line 180, the new test only verifies that same-integration source suppresses outbound (`assert_not_called`). There is no test that a different linked integration still receives outbound sync, which is the intended behavior per the code comment about allowing other integrations to propagate. Consequence is a future change could over-suppress all outbound without test failure, breaking multi-integration sync.

title: Shared default timestamp evaluated at import time
body: In src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py line 18, AssignmentSource declares `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`. The default is evaluated once at import, so every AssignmentSource created via from_integration or from_dict without an explicit queued shares the same timestamp. Someone reading only this finding should understand: all inbound assignments get identical queued times, making the field useless for ordering, debugging, or any future debounce logic. Fix with `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

title: Raw datetime in Celery payload breaks serialization round-trip
body: In src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py to_dict uses asdict and returns a raw datetime for queued, and src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py passes that dict as assignment_source_dict to sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async. Celery task kwargs must be JSON-serializable; a datetime object either fails to enqueue or arrives as an ISO string. from_dict then does cls(**input_dict) with no string-to-datetime parsing and only catches ValueError/TypeError, so a string queued silently creates an object with queued as str or fails. Consequence: inbound-originated outbound syncs that now carry a source can fail to serialize or lose type instead of being cleanly filtered.

title: Malformed source fails open and re-creates sync loop
body: In src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py lines 53-56, AssignmentSource.from_dict returning None on bad input is treated the same as no source, then installation.should_sync is called with None which returns True if outbound sync is enabled. A malformed or type-mismatched assignment_source_dict therefore propagates the update instead of suppressing it. Consequence: the exact Jira rapid-reassign loop this PR claims to fix can still occur when the payload is corrupted or has unexpected types, failing open instead of failing closed or logging.

title: Shared default timestamp for all instances
body: In src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py line 18, `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` calls `timezone.now()` once at import time. Every AssignmentSource created without an explicit `queued` shares the same timestamp. The field no longer reflects when the assignment was queued, breaking debugging, ordering, and any future staleness/TTL logic. Fix with `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

title: to_dict returns non-JSON-serializable datetime for Celery
body: In src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py `to_dict` returns `asdict(self)` containing a raw `datetime` for `queued`. Callers in `sync_group_assignee_outbound` pass this dict as `assignment_source_dict` to `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async` kwargs, which must survive Celery serialization. With JSON serialization this raises a serialization error and outbound sync fails/retries; after a JSON round-trip `queued` comes back as a string, violating the declared `datetime` type. Serialize `queued` to ISO format and parse it back in `from_dict`.

title: from_dict accepts wrong types and defeats cycle check
body: In src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py `from_dict` does `cls(**input_dict)` and only catches ValueError/TypeError. A dict like `{'source_name': 'x', 'integration_id': '123', 'queued': '2024-...'}` succeeds but yields `integration_id` as str and `queued` as str. Later `should_sync` checks `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id` where the latter is int, so int vs str is False and same-integration suppression silently fails, reintroducing the sync loop. Validate/coerce types and return None on mismatch.

title: Corrupt source fails open and reintroduces loop
body: In src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py the task does `AssignmentSource.from_dict(...) if assignment_source_dict else None` and then calls `should_sync(..., parsed_source)`. If `from_dict` returns None due to corrupt/extra/missing keys, the code proceeds with None, which `should_sync` treats as no source and returns True, so it syncs outbound anyway. A malformed payload therefore disables the cycle protection this PR adds and resumes the loop. It should skip/log and return instead of failing open.

title: sync_assignee_outbound contract missing assignment_source
body: In src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py the abstract `sync_assignee_outbound` is declared as `(external_issue, user, assign=True, **kwargs)` with no explicit `assignment_source`, yet `sync_assignee_outbound` task calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=parsed_source)` and tests assert it is passed explicitly. Any concrete integration implementing the strict 3-arg signature without `**kwargs` will raise TypeError at runtime, and with `**kwargs` the value is silently swallowed. Add the explicit `assignment_source` parameter to the abstract as done for `sync_status_outbound`.

title: Stateful subclass leaves abstract methods unimplemented and cannot be instantiated
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler, which declares abstract methods counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data. The subclass body is only pass, so it stays abstract. Detector.detector_handler does group_type.detector_handler(self), which will raise TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class for any detector with type metric_alert_fire. Previously it implemented evaluate returning [] and was instantiable. Consequence is a runtime crash in process_detectors instead of a no-op.

title: get_state_data crashes with KeyError when detector defines no counters
body: In get_state_data, counter_updates is initialized to {} and only populated inside if self.counter_names:. The final loop unconditionally builds DetectorStateData with counter_updates=counter_updates[gk]. When counter_names is empty list, the dict stays empty and the lookup raises KeyError for every group key. Consequence is evaluate crashes for any stateful detector that legitimately tracks zero counters, even though an empty list should be allowed.

title: Stale docstring says evaluate returns a list
body: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate signature was changed to return dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult], but its docstring still says it returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult with one result per group key. A reader or future handler author relying on the docstring will expect a list. Consequence is confusion and potential misuse of the new dict-keyed contract.

title: Expected occurrence built with wrong group key causing fingerprint mismatch
body: In TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe the expected occurrence is built via build_mock_occurrence_and_event with group_key val1, but evaluate_group_key_value is invoked with group_key group_key. The helper derives fingerprint via build_fingerprint(group_key), so expected fingerprint is <detector_id>:val1 while actual is <detector_id>:group_key. DetectorEvaluationResult equality includes the occurrence, so the test does not compare like-for-like. Consequence is the test is incorrect and does not validly verify the occurrence produced for group_key.

title: Multi-group test uses wrong value and helper ignores value
body: In TestProcessDetectors.test_state_results_multi_group the data packet has group_vals {group_1: 6, group_2: 10}, but the expected occurrence for group_2 is built with value 6. Moreover build_mock_occurrence_and_event never uses its value argument. The new hook build_occurrence_and_event_data receives value from evaluate_group_key_value, but no test verifies the correct per-group value reaches it. Consequence is a bug passing the wrong value to occurrence creation would not be caught.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler left abstract and cannot be instantiated
body: In src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py line 11, MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but implements nothing (pass). StatefulDetectorHandler has abstractmethods counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data, so the subclass remains abstract. Detector.detector_handler does group_type.detector_handler(self) with no try/except, so accessing the handler for type metric_alert_fire will raise TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class. Consequence: any detector of that type crashes process_detectors and blocks other detectors in the same batch, whereas before it returned [].

title: get_state_data KeyErrors when counter_names is empty
body: In src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py line 222, get_state_data initializes counter_updates={} and only populates it inside if self.counter_names:. It then unconditionally does counter_updates[gk] when building DetectorStateData. If a StatefulDetectorHandler defines counter_names=[] (valid for a detector with no counters), the guard is falsy, the dict stays empty, and every lookup raises KeyError. Consequence: any counter-less stateful detector crashes on every evaluate call.

title: evaluate docstring still says returns a list
body: In src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py line 230, StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate docstring says it returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult, but the signature and implementation in this PR return dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]. Consequence: readers and future implementers are misled about the contract.

title: Test builds expected occurrence with wrong group_key
body: In tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py line 537, TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds occurrence via build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", ...) whose fingerprint is derived from "val1", but the expected DetectorEvaluationResult and the actual evaluate_group_key_value call use group_key "group_key". Since fingerprint includes group_key, expected vs actual IssueOccurrence differ, so the equality assertion is wrong. Consequence: the test fails or does not actually validate the dedupe path it claims to cover.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract but implements nothing
body: In src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py line 11, MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler with only `pass`. StatefulDetectorHandler has abstract members counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data. A subclass that does not implement them cannot be instantiated - Python raises TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class. If a Detector with type metric_alert_fire is processed, Detector.detector_handler tries to instantiate this handler and will raise instead of returning None, crashing process_detectors for the whole batch.

title: get_state_data crashes when counter_names is empty
body: In src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py line 222, get_state_data does `counter_updates=counter_updates[gk]`. When self.counter_names is empty/falsy, the code skips the Redis fetch and leaves counter_updates as {}. The later indexing then raises KeyError for every group_key. The `if self.counter_names:` guard shows empty list is intended to be valid for detectors that track no counters, but such detectors will crash on every evaluate call instead of getting empty/default counters.

title: Multi-group test uses wrong value and helper ignores value
body: In tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py line 191, test_state_results_multi_group creates a DataPacket with group_vals {"group_1": 6, "group_2": 10} but builds the expected occurrence for group_2 with value 6. The helper build_mock_occurrence_and_event never uses the `value` argument to build the IssueOccurrence, so the test passes despite the mismatch. As a result the test does not verify that evaluate forwards the correct per-group value to build_occurrence_and_event_data, masking bugs where the wrong value is used.

title: Docstring still says returns list after changing to dict
body: In src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py line 230, StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate docstring says "returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult" but the PR changed the signature to return dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]. The stale docstring misleads implementers and callers about the contract.

title: Spawn flusher processes are never killed on restart
body: The flusher creates processes via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, whose type is SpawnProcess. The restart path guards cleanup with isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process), where multiprocessing.Process is the default-context (fork) Process class on Linux and is not a base class of SpawnProcess, so the check is False. As a result when _ensure_processes_alive detects a dead/hung process it calls _create_process_for_shards without killing the old process. A hung process keeps flushing the same Redis shards while the replacement also flushes them, causing duplicate Kafka produces, Redis contention, fd/pid leaks and unbounded process growth. The same isinstance guard in join() prevents terminate() of hung spawn processes on shutdown.

title: Zero/negative process count crashes or disables flushing
body: num_processes is computed as min(max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards)) where max_processes is max_processes or len(...). If assigned_shards is empty on rebalance, or max_processes is 0/negative, num_processes becomes 0 or negative. That yields an empty process_to_shards_map and then i % self.num_processes raises ZeroDivisionError for 0, or i % -1 returns 0 and raises KeyError because the map is empty. With 0 processes submit/record/backpressure loops become no-ops so segments are never flushed, causing silent data loss instead of a clear startup error.

title: --flusher-processes accepts invalid values that crash consumer
body: The new --flusher-processes click Option defaults to 1 with type=int and no range validation, so 0 or negative values are accepted and passed as max_processes to SpanFlusher. In the flusher that leads to zero/negative num_processes, which crashes with ZeroDivisionError/KeyError or silently creates no flusher processes. The CLI should reject values <1.

title: Inconsistent metric tag shard vs shards
body: The produce timer is emitted with tags={"shard": shard_tag} while the wait_produce timer uses tags={"shards": shard_tag} for the same shard-group value. Consumers of metrics querying by one tag name will miss the other, breaking dashboards and alerts for flusher produce latency.

title: Mocked sleep makes flush wait a no-op, test is racy
body: The test replaces time.sleep with lambda _: None, then after advancing current_drift calls time.sleep(0.1) intending to give background flusher threads time to flush. Because sleep is mocked the wait does nothing. join() sets stopped=True immediately, so whether the flusher flushes before exiting is a race. The test can flakily pass/fail and does not deterministically verify multiprocessed flushing.

title: Spawn flusher processes are never killed/terminated due to wrong isinstance
body: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py the flusher creates processes via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, whose type is SpawnProcess, but restart and shutdown check isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process), which on Linux is ForkProcess. A SpawnProcess is not an instance of ForkProcess (both only share BaseProcess), so the check is False in production. As a result process.kill() on hang/crash restart and process.terminate() in join() are never executed. Hung flusher processes leak and the replacement process flushes the same shards concurrently, causing duplicate Kafka produces, Redis contention, and unbounded process accumulation.

title: join() abandons remaining flusher processes on timeout
body: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py join() sets a deadline, joins next_step with the full timeout, then iterates over flusher processes and breaks out of the loop when the deadline is exceeded. Processes after the break are never waited on nor terminated, and if next_step consumed the whole timeout no flusher is even waited on. Hung or slow flushers are left running after rebalance/shutdown, leaking processes/threads and continuing to flush and produce.

title: Inconsistent metric tag shard vs shards breaks dashboards
body: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py the produce timer uses tags={"shard": shard_tag} while the wait_produce timer on the next line uses tags={"shards": shard_tag}, and segment_size_bytes uses "shard". The pluralization mismatch splits what should be one sharded metric family into different tag keys, breaking aggregation, dashboards, and alerts per shard.

title: Test-mode flusher threads share mutable SpansBuffer with parent
body: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py when produce_to_pipe is set the code uses threading.Thread with target partial(SpanFlusher.main, shard_buffer) and also stores the same shard_buffer object in self.buffers for the parent thread to call record_stored_segments() and get_memory_info() in submit(). In production with real processes the child gets a pickled copy, but in tests both threads mutate/read the same SpansBuffer instance concurrently with flush_segments() and its any_shard_at_limit flag without locking. This is a data race that makes tests flaky and unrepresentative of production process isolation.

title: Spawned flusher processes are never killed/terminated
body: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py _ensure_processes_alive checks `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` before kill, and join does the same before terminate. Processes are created with `multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process` which is SpawnProcess, a sibling of the default ForkProcess exposed as multiprocessing.Process, not a subclass. The isinstance is therefore always False for real subprocesses, so hung processes are never killed and join never terminates them. On hang detection a new process is started for the same shards while the old hung process keeps running, causing duplicate flush/produce to buffered-segments, Redis contention, and leaked zombies.

title: Join timeout break leaves remaining flusher processes unwaited
body: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py join loops over all flusher processes but does `if remaining_time <= 0: break` out of the for-loop. If the deadline expires while waiting for an early process, later processes are never waited on nor terminated, leaving background processes running after rebalance/shutdown. Old and new generations can then flush the same Redis shards concurrently and duplicate segments to Kafka.

title: Inconsistent metric tag shard vs shards
body: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py the produce timer uses tags={"shard": shard_tag} while the wait_produce timer on the next line uses tags={"shards": shard_tag}. The pluralization mismatch splits what should be the same dimension, breaking dashboards/alerts grouped by shard and creating extra tag cardinality.

title: Negative flusher_processes causes KeyError, zero silently ignored
body: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py `max_processes or len(...)` treats 0 as unset and `num_processes = min(max_processes, len(...))` accepts negatives. The --flusher-processes CLI option has no validation, so --flusher-processes=-1 makes num_processes negative, process_to_shards_map empty, and `i % num_processes` maps every shard to 0 which raises KeyError on startup. Zero does not mean zero processes but silently falls back to one-process-per-shard, opposite of user intent.

title: Added flusher wait is no-op because sleep is mocked
body: In tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py the test patches `time.sleep` to a no-op and then calls `time.sleep(0.1)` to give flusher threads time to process after advancing drift. Because sleep is mocked the wait does nothing, so join can set stopped before the background thread flushes. The test relies on a busy-loop race and will be flaky, not deterministically verifying the flush.

title: Non-atomic partition lock creation breaks mutual exclusion
