body: OffsetTracker._get_partition_lock does get then setdefault on partition_locks without holding a global lock. Two threads submitting/completing/committing the same Partition concurrently can each create a different threading.Lock and then guard add_offset/complete_offset/get_committable_offsets/mark_committed with different locks. Mutual exclusion is then lost, causing lost offset updates, wrong committable calculation, duplicate processing or skipping offsets. Use a single global lock to protect lock creation and dict access.

title: Unbounded work queues allow unbounded memory growth
body: FixedQueuePool creates queue.Queue() with no maxsize and submit() never blocks, while poll() only emits metrics. If workers are slow the consumer keeps pulling from Kafka and enqueuing WorkItem objects holding full Messages, growing memory without bound until OOM, contrary to the docstring claim of natural backpressure. Use bounded queues with blocking submit or explicit backpressure.

title: Closing one strategy shuts down factory-shared queue pool
body: FixedQueuePool is created once in ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__ and shared by every strategy returned from create_with_partitions, but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() and join() call queue_pool.shutdown() which stops all workers and shuts down all queues. After a Kafka rebalance Arroyo closes the old strategy and creates a new one reusing the same dead pool, so subsequent processing stalls or raises and the consumer never recovers without restart. Pool lifetime must be owned by the factory, strategy close should not destroy it.

title: Each strategy leaks a commit thread sharing one tracker with stale commits
body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.__init__ starts its own background commit thread polling the shared factory-level OffsetTracker. On rebalance the old strategy's thread is never stopped by ResultsStrategyFactory.shutdown and terminate() does not join it, so multiple threads poll the same tracker and invoke different captured commit callables, including revoked-partition commits, causing duplicate commits, commits via invalid closures, and thread leaks.

title: Offsets committed from background thread
body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy._commit_loop invokes the Arroyo commit callable from a dedicated daemon thread every second instead of from poll/join. Arroyo Commit is expected to be called from the processing thread and is not safe to call concurrently with rebalance/shutdown, risking commits for revoked partitions, races with StreamProcessor shutdown, and lost or mis-ordered commits. Commits should happen synchronously in poll/join.

title: Shutdown abandons queued work instead of draining
body: FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets every worker.shutdown=True before shutting down queues, and OrderedQueueWorker.run loops on while not self.shutdown. Workers therefore exit immediately even when queues still contain submitted WorkItems. SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() thus discards pending work, leaving offsets never completed to be redelivered in bulk or, if already partially committed, losing ordering guarantees. Shutdown should let workers drain via queue shutdown without a separate flag.

title: decode_payload asserts on FilteredPayload instead of skipping
body: ResultsStrategyFactory.decode_payload asserts not isinstance(payload, FilteredPayload), but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit passes message.payload which can be FilteredPayload. Every filtered message then raises AssertionError, logs Error submitting message to queue, and only gets skipped via the generic exception path. Filtered payloads are normal and should return None without an exception.

title: wait_until_empty and stats miss in-flight work
body: get_stats and wait_until_empty use Queue.qsize(), which counts only items waiting in the queue, not the item a worker already removed via get() and is still processing. wait_until_empty can return True while workers are still handling results, and total_queued metrics undercount load. Callers using it to decide completion or shutdown can proceed prematurely. Track outstanding work via OffsetTracker outstanding counts or task_done/unfinished_tasks instead of qsize.

title: Partition lock creation is racy
body: OffsetTracker._get_partition_lock in src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py does get then setdefault on partition_locks with no global lock. Two threads adding the same new Partition concurrently can create two different Lock objects and then synchronize on different locks. That breaks the claimed per-partition mutual exclusion for add_offset/complete_offset/get_committable_offsets/mark_committed, allowing lost updates and wrong committable offsets, which causes duplicate processing or skipped commits.

title: Unbounded queues with no backpressure
body: FixedQueuePool creates each work queue as queue.Queue() with no maxsize, and SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit/poll never blocks or returns a backpressure signal, despite the docstring claiming natural backpressure. If workers stall on a slow subscription, the Arroyo poll loop keeps submitting and memory grows without bound, leading to OOM and growing commit lag. poll only emits a gauge.

title: Strategy close shuts down factory-shared pool, breaks rebalance
body: ResultsStrategyFactory creates one FixedQueuePool in __init__ and reuses it for every strategy returned by create_with_partitions, but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close calls queue_pool.shutdown which kills all workers. On Arroyo rebalance/reassignment where the old strategy is closed and a new one is created from the same factory, the shared pool is left shut down with dead workers, so subsequent submits pile up unprocessed. Multiple concurrent strategies would also share one OffsetTracker with multiple commit threads double-committing.

title: terminate leaks commit thread
body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.terminate in src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py sets shutdown_event and shuts down workers but never joins the commit_thread, unlike close. The daemon commit thread keeps running and keeps calling commit_function and mark_committed on the shared OffsetTracker after termination, causing use-after-terminate commits and thread leaks.

title: Worker swallows failures yet commits offsets
body: OrderedQueueWorker.run catches all Exceptions from result_processor, logs, then unconditionally calls offset_tracker.complete_offset in finally. Failed results are therefore treated as completed and the commit loop will commit past them, so failures are never retried and never reach Arroyo DLQ handling. ResultProcessor.__call__ already swallows exceptions, so mocking it to raise still gets committed, losing uptime results silently.

title: assert used for control flow on message type
body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit uses assert isinstance(message.value, BrokerValue) to get partition/offset. Asserts are stripped with python -O, leaving partition/offset unbound, and for any non-BrokerValue message the AssertionError is caught by the blanket except and the message is silently dropped without tracking. FilteredPayload also hits assert not FilteredPayload inside decode_payload and relies on the exception path to mark progress, making normal filtering depend on exceptions.

title: wait_until_empty/get_stats miss in-flight work
body: FixedQueuePool.get_stats and wait_until_empty use Queue.qsize, which counts only queued items not the item already removed by get and being processed by a worker. wait_until_empty can return True while offsets are still outstanding, and total_queued metrics undercount. Tests that wait on total_items==0 plus call counts are racy and can pass before processing or committing finishes, hiding ordering and commit bugs.

title: Queue.shutdown does not exist on Python <3.13, shutdown hangs
body: FixedQueuePool.shutdown calls q.shutdown(immediate=False). queue.Queue.shutdown was added in Python 3.13. On older runtimes this raises AttributeError, which is caught and logged per-queue, leaving workers blocked forever in work_queue.get(). Worker.join(timeout=5.0) then times out and close()/terminate() never actually stops workers. Consequence is leaked daemon threads and hung consumer shutdown/rebalance.

title: Offsets marked complete even when processing fails
body: OrderedQueueWorker.run calls offset_tracker.complete_offset in a finally block after result_processor. Any exception is logged and swallowed, then the offset is still marked done, so get_committable_offsets advances past failures. This contradicts the class docstring 'Only commits offsets after successful processing' and bypasses Arroyo DLQ handling, which requires the strategy to raise. Consequence is silent data loss: transient DB/cache errors cause uptime results to be skipped and committed as if successful.

title: Unbounded queues provide no backpressure
body: FixedQueuePool creates queue.Queue() with no maxsize, and submit() does add_offset then non-blocking put. The docstring claims 'Natural backpressure when queues fill up' but there is no bound, so if Kafka polling outpaces workers the process enqueues unboundedly. Consequence is unbounded memory growth and OOM when a queue backs up, plus unbounded growth of OffsetTracker sets.

title: Offsets committed from background thread
body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy spawns a commit_thread that every second calls get_committable_offsets then commit_function, which in result_consumer.py calls Arroyo commit(). That Commit callback is owned by the StreamProcessor poll thread and tied to partition assignment. Calling it concurrently from a background thread races with rebalance/close/terminate, committing revoked partitions or committing while Arroyo is tearing down the strategy. Consequence is commit errors, lost commits, or duplicates.

title: Factory-shared queue pool is shut down by per-assignment strategy
body: ResultsStrategyFactory creates one FixedQueuePool in __init__ and hands the same object to every SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy returned by create_with_partitions. But SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()/terminate() calls queue_pool.shutdown(), and factory.shutdown() also shuts it down. After a rebalance the old strategy kills workers/queues still referenced by the factory, so the next strategy reuses a dead pool and stops processing, while multiple live strategies would share one OffsetTracker with multiple commit loops. Consequence is a stalled consumer after the first rebalance.

title: close() loses final commits; terminate() leaks commit thread
body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close sets shutdown_event then joins commit_thread before draining workers via queue_pool.shutdown(). Offsets completed while workers drain after the commit thread exited are never committed. terminate sets the event but never joins the commit thread at all, leaving a daemon thread that can keep calling commit_function after partitions are revoked. Consequence is duplicate reprocessing on restart and commit-after-revoke errors.

title: Committable scan iterates full offset range
body: OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets computes min/max of all_offsets then loops for offset in range(start, max_offset+1). With a sparse gap the loop cost is proportional to the numeric gap, not the number of tracked offsets. A single missing offset with a large max can cause millions of iterations every second per partition. It should iterate the sorted tracked set instead. Consequence is CPU spikes and stalled commit loop under gaps.

title: FilteredPayload handled via AssertionError
body: ResultsStrategyFactory.decode_payload starts with assert not isinstance(payload, FilteredPayload). SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit passes message.payload straight to this decoder, so every filtered message raises AssertionError, logs 'Failed to decode' or 'Error submitting message to queue', then is marked complete via the exception path. Filtered messages should return None explicitly without assert/exception. Consequence is noisy exception logs for normal filtered traffic and exception-driven control flow.

title: wait_until_empty and stats ignore in-flight work
body: FixedQueuePool.get_stats sums q.qsize() and wait_until_empty polls total_items==0. qsize only counts items still queued, not the item already removed by Queue.get() and being processed by a worker with its offset still outstanding. wait_until_empty therefore can return True while work is still in flight and offsets uncommitted. Consequence is premature test synchronization and any production use would incorrectly assume quiescence.

title: Hash distribution test is flaky
body: test_different_groups_distributed asserts that 20 keys group0..group19 with hash(key)%3 hit all 3 queues. Python string hash is salted per process, so hitting all buckets is probabilistic, not guaranteed. The test can fail on some hash seeds despite correct code. It should mock hashing or assert consistency only, not full coverage. Consequence is flaky CI.

title: Queue-depth assertion races with workers
body: test_stats_reporting submits 10 items then immediately asserts get_stats total_items>0. Workers start in FixedQueuePool.__init__ and can drain the unbounded queues before the assertion runs, making total_items==0 and failing the test nondeterministically. The test needs to pause workers or poll until expected state instead of asserting transient queue depth. Consequence is flaky CI.

title: Backup-code login is case-sensitive while codes are presented as uppercase-style codes
body: Backup codes are generated as lowercase hex in the setup endpoint, displayed/copyable as XXXXX-XXXXX, and this login check only strips '-' before doing backupCodes.indexOf(...). If a user transcribes a valid code in uppercase (a-f become A-F), or an authenticator/backup note uppercases it, indexOf returns -1 and a valid single-use code is rejected with IncorrectBackupCode. The lookup should normalize the submitted code (e.g. trim and toLowerCase) before comparison.

title: Disabling 2FA with a backup code has the same case-sensitivity bug
body: This endpoint computes backupCodes.indexOf(req.body.backupCode.replaceAll('-', '')) without lowercasing/trimming. A correctly transcribed backup code entered in uppercase therefore returns IncorrectBackupCode, so a user who has lost their authenticator cannot disable 2FA with a valid code. Normalize the input the same way codes are generated/stored before checking membership.

title: Single-use backup codes can be replayed concurrently
body: Authorize reads user.backupCodes, checks indexOf, then later does a separate prisma.user.update setting backupCodes[index] = null. There is no atomic/conditional update or transaction locking the row between check and consumption. Two parallel login attempts using the same backup code can both read the pre-consumption array, both pass indexOf, and both be authenticated before either update lands, violating the documented 'each backup code can be used exactly once' guarantee. Consumption must be atomic (e.g. conditional update/transaction) so only one request can claim a code.

title: Parent is only notified of enabled 2FA when the backup-code Close button is clicked
body: On successful enable, handleEnable now only advances to DisplayBackupCodes instead of calling onEnable(). onEnable() is invoked solely from the backup-codes Close button. If the user dismisses the dialog via the Dialog's onOpenChange path (X button, outside click, Escape) after the server has already set twoFactorEnabled=true, the parent/security page is never refreshed and resetState() is not run, leaving the UI showing 2FA as disabled (and stale secret/backup-code state in the modal) until a full reload. The dialog-close path should perform the same completion/cleanup as the Close button.

title: External IdP users in the totpEmail flow cannot reach the backup-code option
body: When totpEmail is present (the flow used for Google/SAML users who have 2FA enabled), the footer is ExternalTotpFooter, which only offers Cancel, instead of TwoFactorFooter which contains the 'Lost access' toggle. The BackupCode form is rendered only when twoFactorLostAccess becomes true, and that state can never be set in this flow, even though the credentials authorize callback now supports backupCode. External-IdP 2FA users who lost their authenticator therefore still have no backup-code login path.

title: Users who enabled 2FA before this feature can never obtain backup codes
body: Setup returns TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled for anyone with twoFactorEnabled=true, and this PR adds no regenerate/view endpoint or settings action. All pre-existing 2FA users therefore have backupCodes=null forever unless they disable and re-enable 2FA; if they try a backup code at login they get MissingBackupCodes, whose message says 'Please generate them in your settings' even though no such settings action exists. Add a regeneration flow for already-enabled users or change the message/flow so these users are not dead-ended.

title: No test exercises actually logging in or disabling 2FA with a backup code
body: The added e2e coverage only clicks the backup-code download/copy buttons and checks the filename/toast during setup; the file itself notes 'TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup'. The security-critical new behavior — valid backup code logs in, the same code cannot be reused, an invalid code is rejected, and a backup code can disable 2FA — is entirely untested, so regressions in next-auth-options.ts or disable.ts would not be caught.

title: Backup code can be used without the account password
body: Password verification is skipped whenever any totpCode is present (`if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)`), while the new branch at line 131 accepts a backupCode independently of totpCode. A direct credentials request supplying a valid backupCode plus any non-empty dummy totpCode therefore skips verifyPassword entirely and logs in with the backup code as a single factor. Backup codes are long-lived recovery secrets meant to replace only the TOTP factor, not the password, so anyone who obtains one code (e.g. a photographed/stored list) gains full account access without knowing the password.

title: Single-use backup code can be replayed by concurrent logins
body: Consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write: authorize() reads user.backupCodes, checks indexOf, then updates the row nulling that entry. Two simultaneous login attempts with the same code can both read the pre-consumption value, both pass the check, and both write back an equivalent list, so the supposedly single-use code (promised as 'can be used exactly once' in the UI copy) authenticates more than once. Consumption needs an atomic/transactional compare-and-update or locking to guarantee one-time use.

title: Backup-code comparison is case-sensitive and does not trim whitespace
body: Codes are generated as lowercase hex and displayed/copyable as `XXXXX-XXXXX`, but verification only does `credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` with no toLowerCase() or trim(). A user who transcribes the code in uppercase (as the placeholder's uppercase X styling suggests) or with surrounding whitespace is rejected with IncorrectBackupCode even though they typed the correct code, effectively locking recovery users out. The same un-normalized comparison exists in the disable endpoint (disable.ts line 61); normalize (trim + lowercase) in both places.

title: Closing the modal on the backup-codes step desyncs 2FA state
body: On successful enable the handler now only advances to DisplayBackupCodes and defers onEnable() (which refreshes the parent page's 2FA state) and resetState() to the explicit Close button (lines 261-270). If the user dismisses the dialog any other way (X/Esc/backdrop via onOpenChange), the parent still shows 2FA as disabled even though the server enabled it, and the modal's step state remains DisplayBackupCodes, so reopening it lands on stale backup codes instead of the password step. onEnable/reset must also run on dialog close once enablement has succeeded.

title: First 2FA test never dismisses the new backup-codes step and backup login is untested
body: The 'enable 2FA and login using 2FA' test still proceeds straight from fillOtp to asserting the two-factor switch, but enabling now ends on the DisplayBackupCodes step and onEnable is only fired by the backup-codes Close button, so this test no longer drives the flow it asserts on. Only the second test was updated (download/copy/close), and the file itself notes at line 12 that login and disable with a backup code are untested. The new security-critical paths — successful backup-code login, rejection of a wrong code, and single-use invalidation of a consumed code — have no coverage, so regressions in them would ship undetected.

title: Backup code can bypass password verification when a dummy TOTP code is also supplied
body: Password verification only runs when `!credentials.totpCode`, while the new branch at line 131 authorizes solely on `credentials.backupCode` and ignores the TOTP value. An attacker who obtains one backup code can call the credentials provider directly with that code plus any non-empty totpCode (e.g. "x") and an empty/wrong password: the password check is skipped and the backup-code check succeeds, so a second-factor recovery code becomes a complete password replacement. Password must be verified whenever a password account is logging in, regardless of which second factor is presented, or the second-step flow must use a trustworthy proof that password verification already occurred.

title: Single-use backup code can be replayed by concurrent logins
body: Consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write: authorize() reads and decrypts user.backupCodes, checks indexOf, then updates the row at lines 149-156. Two concurrent sign-in requests using the same code can both read the pre-consumption array and both pass the index check before either update commits, violating the documented exactly-once property and allowing one leaked code to create multiple sessions. The consumption needs an atomic/conditional update, transaction with row locking, or equivalent compare-and-swap so only one request can claim a code.

title: Users who enabled 2FA before this feature can never obtain backup codes
body: Backup codes are only generated in setup, and setup returns TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled for anyone with twoFactorEnabled already true. All pre-existing 2FA users therefore have backupCodes = null forever unless they disable and re-enroll in 2FA; the new MissingBackupCodes error even tells them to generate codes in settings, where no generation/regeneration endpoint or UI exists. This leaves the recovery flow permanently unusable (and the error text misleading) for the population most likely to need it.

title: Backup-code comparison rejects valid codes typed in different case or with surrounding whitespace
body: Generated codes are lowercase hex (crypto.randomBytes(5).toString('hex') in setup) and are shown/downloaded in that form, but verification only strips '-' before a case-sensitive indexOf; the same logic is used in the disable endpoint. A user who manually transcribes a code in uppercase (as suggested by the XXXXX-XXXXX placeholder in BackupCode.tsx) or pastes it with leading/trailing whitespace gets IncorrectBackupCode and may be locked out, even though hex case is semantically irrelevant. Normalize input with trim().toLowerCase() (and server-side, not just in the form) before comparison in both verification paths.

title: No test exercises actually logging in or disabling 2FA with a backup code, or its single-use property
body: The added e2e coverage only clicks download/copy/close on the code display, and line 12 explicitly defers login and disable-with-backup-code tests. Nothing proves a generated code authenticates, that a wrong code is rejected at login, that a consumed code cannot be reused (including the second login attempt), or that a code works in DisableTwoFactorModal. This is the security-critical behavior of the PR, so at least login-with-code plus reuse-rejection should be covered before merging.

title: Google Meet fallback crashes when there is no destination calendar
body: The code destructures `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` into `mainHostDestinationCalendar` and then accesses `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. When destinationCalendar is null, undefined, or an empty array (handleNewBooking explicitly sets it to null when neither the event type nor organizer has one), this throws a TypeError during EventManager.create, breaking booking creation instead of falling back to Cal Video.

title: Google update/delete no longer fall back to the destination calendar
body: In updateEvent and the analogous deleteEvent code, the fallback is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` inside the branch where externalCalendarId is already falsy, so the find can never match and returns undefined. Previously this returned destinationCalendar.externalId. Updates therefore call Google with an undefined calendarId and deletes fall back to "primary", so reschedules/cancellations for events stored on a non-primary destination calendar fail or target the wrong calendar.

title: Non-Google calendar services still create collective events only on the first host's calendar
body: Office365 createEvent (like Lark at CalendarService.ts:128 and CalDAV at packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156) selects `event.destinationCalendar[0]` and ignores which credential the service instance was created for, even though EventManager now loops over every collective host's destination and invokes a separate credential's service. For the second and later hosts it therefore tries to write to the main host's externalId with another user's token, causing failures or events in the wrong calendar; it should select the destination whose credentialId matches the instance's credential (Google does this via the new credentialId argument).

title: updateLocation now creates booking references without calendar/credential IDs
body: updateLocation builds referencesToCreate from `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`, but CalendarManager.updateEvent's returned EventResult (CalendarManager.ts:313-322) never sets either field. Previously these came from evt.destinationCalendar. Edit-location therefore persists BookingReference rows with externalCalendarId and credentialId undefined, losing the link needed by later reschedule, update, and cancellation flows to target the correct external calendar.

title: Collective team calendars are dropped when the organizer has no destination calendar
body: evt.destinationCalendar is set to null when neither eventType.destinationCalendar nor organizerUser.destinationCalendar exists, and the collective calendars are then added with `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. The optional chain silently no-ops on null, so a collective event whose non-organizer hosts have destination calendars but whose organizer/event type does not will create no calendar events for those hosts, defeating the purpose of the change.

title: Unrelated change inverts organization slug persistence condition
body: This file is unrelated to destinationCalendar, but the diff changes organization creation from setting `slug` when team billing is disabled (and `requestedSlug` in metadata when it is enabled) to setting both `slug` and `requestedSlug` only when team billing is enabled, and neither otherwise. Organizations created without team billing will now have no slug persisted, breaking org URL/domain handling that expects it.

title: Google Meet fallback crashes when there is no destination calendar
body: The code destructures the first element of evt.destinationCalendar and then accesses mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining. When destinationCalendar is null, undefined, or an empty array (handleNewBooking can set it to null, and several other callers set it to []), mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined and this throws a TypeError, breaking EventManager.create for events using Google Meet location without a destination calendar. The previous code used evt.destinationCalendar?.integration.

title: Unrelated organization slug condition is inverted
body: This change flips the slug assignment from ...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }) to ...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}). Organizations are now given a slug exactly when team billing is enabled and denied one when it is disabled, the opposite of the previous behavior, while requestedSlug in metadata still uses the billing-enabled condition. This unrelated change can break organization creation/routing depending on the billing flag.

title: Google update/delete fallback can never find the destination calendar
body: When externalCalendarId is falsy, the fallback searches destinationCalendar for an entry whose externalId equals externalCalendarId (the falsy value), so it can never match and returns undefined. updateEvent then calls calendar.events.update with calendarId undefined instead of falling back to the booking's destination calendar as before, and deleteEvent has the same dead fallback at line 315. Reschedules/location updates for Google bookings without an externalCalendarId will fail or target the wrong calendar.

title: Lark events for collective hosts always use the first host's calendar
body: createEvent ignores the credential being processed and always uses destinationCalendar[0]. EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents loops over every collective host's destination calendar and calls createEvent once per credential, so for the second and later hosts Lark will try to create the event on the organizer's calendar ID using another host's credentials, which will fail or write to the wrong calendar. Google was changed to select the destination matching credentialId, but Lark (and similarly Office365 at CalendarService.ts:73 and CalDAV at packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156) was only converted to read the first array element.

title: Video booking references lose their credentialId on creation
body: referencesToCreate now sets credentialId to result.credentialId only for calendar results and undefined for everything else. Previously video results kept result.credentialId. Dedicated video meetings (e.g. Zoom/Meet alternatives stored as *_video references) will now be persisted with credentialId undefined, so cancellation/update flows that look up the specific video credential by reference.credentialId cannot find it and may not delete/update the video meeting.

title: Reschedule merge deletes only the first old calendar event
body: When newBookingId is provided, the cleanup uses booking.references.find(...) to locate a single old calendar reference and deletes only that one event. Collective bookings now have multiple calendar references (one per host), so the old events on the other hosts' calendars are never deleted on reschedule, leaving orphaned duplicate events. It should iterate all old *_calendar references, as updateAllCalendarEvents now does for updates.

title: Collective team destination calendars are dropped when organizer has none
body: evt.destinationCalendar is set to null when neither eventType.destinationCalendar nor organizerUser.destinationCalendar exists, and the collective handling then does evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars). In that case the optional chain silently skips the push, so team members' destination calendars collected in teamDestinationCalendars are lost and those hosts receive no calendar event. It should initialize an array (or assign teamDestinationCalendars) instead of relying on push.

title: Recurring collective cancellation deletes only first reference per booking, repeatedly
body: Inside the new loop over every calendar reference, the recurring branch maps over all of the organizer's calendar credentials and for each updated booking picks updBooking.references.find(...) - only the first calendar reference. With multiple collective hosts/references this both repeats the same deletion pass once per outer reference (duplicate delete calls pushed into apiDeletes) and still misses the non-first calendar events of each recurring booking, leaving them on other hosts' calendars after cancellation.

title: Google Meet fallback crashes when destinationCalendar is empty or null
body: When evt.destinationCalendar is null/undefined or an empty array, `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` yields undefined, and `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` then throws a TypeError. Previously this was `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, which safely treated a missing calendar as not Google Calendar and fell back to Cal Video. Any Google Meet booking without a destination calendar now fails in EventManager.create instead of falling back.

title: Unrelated inversion of organization slug assignment
body: This changes `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to set `slug` only when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true. That inverts the previous behavior: with team billing enabled the slug should be deferred as `requestedSlug` in metadata until billing is set up, and without billing the slug should be set directly. Organizations created with billing enabled will now get a slug immediately, and organizations created without billing will be created with no slug. This change is unrelated to destinationCalendar.

title: Google update/delete fallback to destination calendar is broken
body: In updateEvent (and the same pattern in deleteEvent at line 315), the fallback is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`, but this branch only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, so the find can never match and selectedCalendar/calendarId becomes undefined. Previously it fell back to `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`. Updates/deletes called without an externalCalendarId (e.g. older booking references) will now call Google with an undefined calendarId instead of the booking's destination calendar.

title: Credential from previous calendar reference is reused for next reference
body: In updateAllCalendarEvents, `credential` is declared outside the `for (const reference of calendarReference)` loop. If a later reference's credentialId is not in this.calendarCredentials and the DB lookup fails or returns an app without a slug, `credential` is never reset and still holds the previous host's credential, so `updateEvent(credential, ...)` at line 542 updates the wrong host's calendar (or updates the same calendar twice with another reference's uid). Each iteration must start with credential undefined.

title: Video booking references lose their credentialId on creation
body: referencesToCreate now sets `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`. Previously non-calendar (video) results kept `result.credentialId`. Booking references for dedicated video integrations will now be persisted with credentialId undefined, so later update/delete/reschedule flows that look up the specific video credential by reference.credentialId cannot find it and may fall back to a wrong credential or fail to update/delete the meeting.

title: Organizer email always taken from first host for every host's calendar
body: createEvent correctly selects the target calendar by matching credentialId (lines 147-149), but the organizer attendee email is taken from mainHostDestinationCalendar (the first destinationCalendar entry) regardless of which credential/calendar is being written to. For a collective event, creating the event on the second host's Google calendar sends the first host's calendar externalId as the organizer email, which does not belong to that account and can cause Google to reject the insert or attribute the event to the wrong organizer. The entry matching credentialId should be used here, as it already is for selectedCalendar.

title: Office365 (and other non-Google services) ignore credentialId and always use first destination calendar
body: The Calendar interface now passes credentialId to createEvent so each destination calendar can be matched to its credential, but Office365CalendarService.createEvent still destructures only the first entry of event.destinationCalendar and builds `/me/calendars/{firstExternalId}/events` with whichever credential EventManager is iterating. For collective events the second host's event is attempted against the first host's calendar id using the second host's token, producing 404/duplicates rather than an event on the second host's calendar. The same first-entry pattern remains in LarkCalendarService.createEvent and BaseCalendarService.createEvent, so the multi-host fix only works for Google Calendar.

title: Collective team destination calendars are dropped when organizer has none
body: evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer user has a destination calendar, and the collective handling then does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. With optional chaining on null this silently does nothing, so team members' destination calendars collected in teamDestinationCalendars are discarded and those hosts receive no calendar event — exactly the collective case this PR aims to fix when only the non-organizer hosts have calendars connected.

title: destinationCalendar shape change breaks webhook payload contract
body: Changing CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar from `DestinationCalendar | null` to `DestinationCalendar[] | null` changes the JSON sent to webhook subscribers (evt is spread into sendPayload) from an object/null to an array, and call sites are inconsistent — some now emit [] (confirm, cancel, payment webhooks) while handleNewBooking can still emit null. External webhook consumers expecting an object will break, and consumers cannot rely on a single shape. This needs to be kept consistent (always an array) and treated as a breaking payload change, or the webhook payload should retain the old field shape.

title: Minimum token schema strips required token fields
body: The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` do not create catch-all Zod fields. The resulting object schema therefore only retains `access_token` and strips fields such as `expires_in`, `expiry_date`, `scope`, `token_type`, and the real `refresh_token` when credential sharing is enabled. Callers that persist or consume the parsed data lose expiry and refresh information and can store unusable credentials.

title: Missing refresh token is replaced with a literal placeholder
body: When the parsed response has no `refresh_token`, this code sets it to the literal string `"refresh_token"`. Zoom's adapter copies `newTokens.refresh_token` into the stored credential and Google/Office flows can persist the parsed result, so the real refresh token is overwritten by a placeholder. The next refresh will fail and the user must reconnect the app.

title: Google credential update stores the SafeParse wrapper instead of token data
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod `SafeParseReturnType` object (`{success, data}`), but this code assigns that whole object to `key` and writes it to `prisma.credential.update`. Previously `googleCredentialSchema.parse` returned the credential object itself. The stored key becomes `{success:true,data:{...}}`, so the next `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` in `googleAuth` will fail because the token fields are nested under `data`.

title: Salesforce refresh uses prisma without importing it
body: The newly added refresh block calls `prisma.credential.update`, but this file has no `prisma` import (imports only include `getAppKeysFromSlug` and `parseRefreshTokenResponse`). Every Salesforce client construction will throw a ReferenceError after the token request, breaking the integration entirely.

title: Salesforce client is built with the old access token
body: After fetching and parsing a refreshed token, `getClient` constructs the jsforce Connection with `accessToken: credentialKey.access_token` and `refreshToken: credentialKey.refresh_token` from the pre-refresh credential instead of `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`. If the old token was expired, the returned client still carries the expired token and Salesforce calls will fail despite the refresh.

title: Sync branch returns a raw fetch Response incompatible with most callers
body: When sync is enabled this returns the raw `fetch` Response without checking `response.ok` or parsing JSON, while the fallback returns whatever the app-specific refresh function returns (HubSpot token object, axios response, Google token response, etc.). Callers such as HubSpot (`hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn/accessToken`), Zoho CRM/Bigin (`tokenInfo.data.*`), and Office365Video expect those app-specific shapes, so with sync enabled they read undefined fields, compute NaN expiries, and persist broken credentials instead of using the synced access token.

title: Zoho Bigin passes credentialId where refreshOAuthTokens expects userId
body: `refreshOAuthTokens`' third parameter is `userId` and is sent to the sync endpoint as `calcomUserId`. This call passes `credentialId` (the credential primary key) instead. The parent platform will look up the wrong user (or no user) and return another user's/no tokens, so synced Zoho Bigin refreshes cannot work correctly and could cross users.

title: Office365 refresh loses expiry transformation under sync schema
body: With sync enabled `parseRefreshTokenResponse` uses the minimum schema, which strips `expires_in` instead of applying `refreshTokenResponseSchema`'s transform of `expires_in` into an absolute expiry timestamp. The merged credential written at line 265 keeps the old expired `expires_in`, and `getToken` at line 278 checks `refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(...).success && !isExpired(o365AuthCredentials.expires_in)`, so the credential is treated as permanently expired and refreshed on every call.

title: Zoom expiry becomes NaN with sync token parsing
body: Under sync parsing `expires_in` is stripped from `newTokens`, so `Math.round(Date.now() + newTokens.expires_in * 1000)` evaluates to NaN and is stored as `key.expiry_date` at line 124, together with the placeholder refresh token from `parseRefreshTokenResponse`. The persisted Zoom credential is corrupted and `zoomTokenSchema.parse` on the next `getToken` call will reject it.

title: Webhook secret is compared with non-constant-time equality
body: The shared secret that authorizes writing arbitrary third-party credentials for any userId is checked with `!==` on the header value. This is vulnerable to timing side-channel disclosure of the secret; the comparison should use a length-checked `crypto.timingSafeEqual`. A leaked secret allows an attacker to overwrite any user's app credentials.

title: Webhook handler has no error handling for invalid body or decrypt failures
body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` at line 31 and `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` at lines 57-59 throw on malformed JSON, a wrong encryption key, or non-JSON plaintext. There is no try/catch and no HTTP method check, so bad requests produce unhandled 500s (and stack/error leakage depending on runtime config) instead of a controlled 400 response, making integration failures hard to distinguish from server faults.

title: New refresh code uses prisma without importing it
body: The newly added refresh block calls `prisma.credential.update(...)`, but this file has no `prisma` import (imports are jsforce, rrule, zod, CalEventParser, constants, HttpError, logger, types and getAppKeysFromSlug). Every Salesforce client construction will fail type-checking / throw ReferenceError at runtime before a connection can be created, breaking the integration entirely, not only when credential sync is enabled.

title: Refreshed Salesforce access token is discarded and stale token is used
body: getClient fetches and persists `accessTokenParsed.data`, but then constructs the jsforce Connection with `accessToken: credentialKey.access_token` (the old credential key) and `instanceUrl: credentialKey.instance_url`. After an expiry-driven refresh the client therefore continues calling Salesforce with the expired token, so the new refresh logic does not actually fix/perform authenticated calls.

title: SafeParse result object is stored as the Google credential key
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod SafeParse result (`{success, data}`), whereas the previous code stored `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` (the credential object itself). This line stores that wrapper as `key` in prisma.credential.update. The persisted key no longer has top-level access_token/refresh_token/expiry_date, so subsequent `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` calls fail and the user's Google credential is corrupted.

title: Missing refresh_token is replaced with the literal string "refresh_token"
body: When the (sync) token response has no refresh_token, this mutates the parsed data to `refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. Callers such as Zoom and Office365 then copy that value into the stored credential (`key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token` / spreading tokenResponse.data), permanently overwriting the real refresh token with a placeholder. The next refresh will fail with invalid_grant and the user must reconnect; the correct behaviour is to preserve the existing stored refresh token.

title: Minimum sync schema strips all fields except access_token
body: The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` do not express wildcard/ passthrough fields in Zod; a plain z.object strips unknown keys by default. In sync mode the returned data therefore contains essentially only access_token (plus the fabricated refresh_token), losing expires_in/expiry_date, token_type, scope and provider-specific fields. Zoom then computes `expiry_date = Date.now() + undefined*1000` (NaN) and Office365 never updates its transformed expiry, causing broken expiry handling and repeated/invalid refreshes.

title: Sync branch returns a fetch Response incompatible with non-fetch callers
body: When sync is enabled this returns the raw `fetch` Response, but several wrapped refresh functions do not return a Response: HubSpot returns a HubspotToken object, Zoho CRM/Bigin return AxiosResponses with `.data`, and Google's wrapper returns `fetchTokens.res`. Callers then read properties like `.accessToken`, `.expiresIn` or `.data.error`/`.data.access_token` directly off the Response, getting undefined (and NaN expiry in HubSpot) or throwing. The sync path is therefore broken for those apps while the non-sync path works, because the helper changes the return-type contract based on an env flag.

title: Credential ID is passed where refreshOAuthTokens expects a user ID
body: refreshOAuthTokens' third argument is `userId` and is sent to the sync endpoint as `calcomUserId`; every other caller passes `credential.userId`. This caller passes `credentialId` (the credential row id, captured as credentialId in biginAuth). The parent platform will look up tokens for the wrong user (or a non-existent user), returning wrong/no tokens, and team credentials would incorrectly be treated as user credentials.

title: Webhook secret is compared with non-constant-time string equality
body: The shared secret that alone authorizes creating/updating arbitrary users' third-party credentials is checked with `!==` against the header value. This is subject to timing side-channels and, because there is no method restriction or try/catch around the subsequent `schema.parse` (line 31) and `symmetricDecrypt`/`JSON.parse` (lines 57-59), malformed unauthenticated-adjacent requests also produce unhandled 500s. Use a timing-safe comparison (with length handling) and return 400 for parse/decrypt failures instead of leaking stack-level 500 errors.

title: Minimum token schema strips all fields except access_token
body: The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` do not create wildcard/ passthrough keys; they create the same literal property name. Zod objects strip unknown keys by default, so in sharing mode `refresh_token`, `expires_in`, `expiry_date`, `scope`, `token_type` and provider-specific fields are removed from `data`. Callers then compute expiry from a missing `expires_in` (e.g. Zoom `Date.now() + undefined*1000` = NaN) and lose the real refresh token, corrupting the refreshed credential.

title: Missing refresh_token is replaced with literal string "refresh_token"
body: When the parsed response has no `refresh_token` (always the case in sharing mode because the schema strips it, and possible in normal mode where it is optional), this line sets `data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. Callers such as Zoom and Webex copy that value into the stored credential key, so the database now contains a bogus refresh token and any later non-synced refresh will fail with invalid_grant.

title: Synced branch returns raw fetch Response incompatible with most callers
body: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns `refreshFunction()` in the normal branch but a raw `fetch` Response in the synced branch. Callers expect incompatible shapes: Google expects `res.data`, HubSpot expects a `HubspotToken` object with `accessToken`/`expiresIn`, and Zoho Bigin/ZohoCRM/HubSpot expect Axios-style `.data`. In synced mode those properties are undefined, causing crashes (`token.access_token` on undefined) or storing a serialized Response/NaN expiry and destroying the credential. Only fetch-based callers can work with this return value.

title: SafeParse result object is stored as the credential key
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod SafeParse result `{success, data}`, but this line assigns it directly as `key` and persists it with `prisma.credential.update`. Previously `googleCredentialSchema.parse()` returned the credential itself. The next load does `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` on `{success:true,data:{...}}`, which fails, and the stored access/refresh tokens are nested under `data` instead of at the top level, breaking Google Calendar after the first refresh.

title: Google refresh assumes synced response has `.data`
body: In synced mode `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a fetch `Response`, which has no `.data` property and its JSON body is never read. `const token = res?.data` is therefore undefined and `token.access_token` throws a TypeError. The catch block treats any non-`invalid_grant` message as recoverable and returns the old auth object, so synced Google credentials can never be refreshed and silently keep using an expired token.

title: prisma is used without being imported
body: The newly added refresh block calls `prisma.credential.update(...)`, but this file has no `prisma` import (imports are only jsforce, RRule, zod, helpers, types, getAppKeysFromSlug and parseRefreshTokenResponse). This is a TypeScript compile error and, if transpiled without checking, a runtime ReferenceError on every Salesforce client creation, breaking the Salesforce integration entirely.

title: Salesforce connection is built with the stale pre-refresh access token
body: After fetching and persisting a refreshed token, `new jsforce.Connection` is constructed with `accessToken: credentialKey.access_token` and `refreshToken: credentialKey.refresh_token` — the old values from before the refresh, not `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`. The service therefore continues calling Salesforce with the expired token it just tried to replace. The refresh is also performed unconditionally on every `getClient` call, even when the stored token is still valid.

title: Credential ID is passed where refreshOAuthTokens expects userId
body: `refreshOAuthTokens(refreshFn, appSlug, userId)` sends its third argument as `calcomUserId` to the sync endpoint and only enables sync when it is truthy. This caller passes `credentialId` (the credential's primary key, threaded through `refreshAccessToken(credentialId, ...)`) instead of `credential.userId`. The parent platform will be asked for tokens for the wrong user (or a non-existent user whose id equals the credential id), returning wrong/no credentials.

title: Webhook handler has no error handling or method check
body: The handler accepts any HTTP method and calls `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` (line 31) and `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` (lines 57-59) with no try/catch. Malformed JSON, an invalid body, or undecryptable `keys` throws an unhandled exception resulting in an opaque 500 (and potentially a stack-bearing error response) instead of a 400, and non-POST requests are processed the same as POST. There are also no tests for this new credential-writing endpoint.

title: Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time string inequality
body: The shared secret that authorizes overwriting any user's third-party credentials is checked with `!==` on line 25-27, which short-circuits on the first differing byte and is susceptible to timing attacks. A secret protecting credential write access should be compared in constant time (e.g. `crypto.timingSafeEqual` after length checks).

title: Team permission requires being both admin and owner
body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`, so a team admin who is not the owner, or an owner who is not also returned as an admin, fails the check. Unless the caller is also the organizer or an attendee, legitimate team admins/owners are incorrectly rejected with FORBIDDEN. The two role checks should be combined with OR.

title: Any attendee can add arbitrary guests to a booking
body: The authorization accepts anyone whose email appears in booking.attendees. An invited guest can therefore call this mutation directly to add unlimited arbitrary people to the organizer's booking, causing database attendees, calendar updates, and invitation emails to be created in the organizer's name. The new UI is on the organizer's bookings page, so attendee access is an unnecessary privilege expansion; only the organizer and authorized team admins/owners should be able to modify the guest list.

title: Calendar is updated with the caller's credentials instead of the organizer's
body: EventManager is constructed from ctx.user and getUsersCredentials(ctx.user). When the caller is a team admin/owner or another authorized user who is not the booking organizer, the calendar event is updated using the caller's credentials (or fails to find the organizer's calendar), even though the handler loads booking.user with credentials/destinationCalendar. The guests are already persisted before this step, so the database and the organizer's calendar can diverge.

title: Guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, or past bookings
body: The handler checks authorization but never checks booking.status or booking.endTime before creating attendees, calling updateCalendarAttendees, and sending scheduled/add-guests emails. A cancelled, rejected, or already-finished booking can therefore gain new attendees and trigger fresh calendar invitations and emails as if it were still an upcoming confirmed event. The server should reject non-confirmed or past bookings, not only rely on which actions the list UI happens to render.

title: Guest list has no uniqueness or size limit on the server
body: ZAddGuestsInputSchema only requires each entry to be an email string. Direct API callers can submit duplicate addresses, duplicates differing only by case, or an arbitrarily large array; the client-side uniqueness refine in AddGuestsDialog does not protect the API. The handler's duplicate and blacklist checks are also case-sensitive for the submitted guest (the blacklist is lowercased, the guest is not), so createMany can insert duplicate attendees and the mutation can be used to fan out unbounded calendar updates and emails.

title: Emails are classified using the unfiltered guest list
body: The handler filters submissions into uniqueGuests (removing people already on the booking and blacklisted addresses) and persists only those, but then calls sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) with the original list. In email-manager, any attendee whose email is in that list is sent AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, so an existing attendee who was resubmitted receives a fresh scheduled/invitation email rather than the guests-added notification. Pass uniqueGuests so email selection matches the attendees actually added.

title: Add-guests emails ignore disabled standard email settings
body: sendAddGuestsEmails always sends organizer, team-member, and attendee emails and accepts no eventTypeMetadata, unlike the neighboring location-change/scheduled flows which honor metadata.disableStandardEmails for hosts and attendees. The addGuests handler also does not pass booking.eventType.metadata. Event types that have disabled standard emails will still emit this new set of emails.

title: Team admin/owner authorization requires both roles instead of either
body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. A team admin who is not the owner (and vice versa) therefore fails this check and, unless they are also the organizer or an attendee, gets FORBIDDEN when adding guests to a team booking they administer. The two checks must be combined with OR, as team admin and team owner are alternative privileged roles.

title: Any attendee can add arbitrary guests and modify the organizer's calendar event
body: Authorization succeeds if the caller's email merely matches any existing attendee (`isAttendee`). That grants a non-organizer guest write access to the booking: they can add unlimited arbitrary people, who are persisted as attendees, receive scheduled-event emails/ICS invites, and are pushed to the organizer's calendar via updateCalendarAttendees. The bookings UI only exposes this to the booking owner/team, so the API is substantially more permissive than the intended organizer/team-admin surface.

title: No booking status or timing check before adding guests
body: After only checking the booking exists, the handler creates attendees, updates the calendar event, and sends invite/update emails. It never rejects CANCELLED, REJECTED, PENDING, or already-ended bookings. The UI also exposes the action for past confirmed bookings (bookedActions are shown for isBookingInPast && isConfirmed), so guests can be added to meetings that will not happen or have already happened, corrupting attendee lists and generating spurious calendar invites and emails.

title: Duplicate and blacklist filtering is case-sensitive and intra-request duplicates are not removed
body: uniqueGuests compares `guest === attendee.email` with exact case, compares the raw guest against a lower-cased blacklist (`blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without lower-casing guest), and never de-duplicates the guests array against itself; the server schema also has no uniqueness refine (only the client does). Sending `A@x.com` plus `a@x.com`, an already-attending email with different casing, or the same email twice via a direct tRPC call creates duplicate Attendee rows and duplicate invites, and a differently-cased blacklisted address bypasses the blacklist.

title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials instead of the organizer's
body: EventManager is built from `ctx.user` and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`, even though the booking (including `booking.user.credentials`/`destinationCalendar`) belongs to the organizer loaded from booking.userId. When a team admin/owner (or attendee) adds guests, the code tries to update the calendar event with the caller's credentials, so the organizer's calendar is not updated (or another user's calendar integration is used). It should load and use the booking organizer's user/credentials, as the booking owner is whose calendar holds the event.

title: Emails are sent for the unfiltered guest list rather than the guests actually added
body: The handler filters the request to uniqueGuests (removing existing attendees and blacklisted addresses) and persists only those, but then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the original unfiltered list. In email-manager that list decides who gets AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail by `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`, so a pre-existing attendee whose email was re-submitted (and thus not newly added) incorrectly receives a fresh scheduled/invite email, and the new-vs-existing distinction is wrong whenever filtering removed anything. Pass uniqueGuests instead.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores event-type disabled-email settings
body: Unlike the neighbouring sendLocationChangeEmails/sendScheduledEmails, sendAddGuestsEmails never checks eventTypeDisableHostEmail/eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail and takes no eventTypeMetadata parameter. Event types that configured disableStandardEmails (all.host / all.attendee) will still emit organizer emails, team-member emails, and attendee emails for added guests, violating the event type's email-suppression contract.

title: Guest list has no size limit, enabling attendee/email spam
body: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no .min(1)/.max() bound. A single authorized (including merely-attendee, per the handler) call can create an unbounded number of Attendee rows and trigger a calendar update plus an email/ICS to every address, making the endpoint usable for bulk unsolicited invites and resource exhaustion. Bound the array (and reject empty arrays explicitly rather than via the misleading uniqueness error).

title: MultiEmail imports @calcom/ui from inside the ui package, creating a circular import
body: This file lives in packages/ui and is exported from packages/ui/index.tsx via MultiEmailLazy, yet it imports Button, EmailField, Icon and Tooltip from "@calcom/ui" (the package's own barrel) instead of relative component paths. That creates a self-referential/circular dependency through the barrel (which also loads the lazy MultiEmail), risking undefined components at runtime and defeating the lazy-loading/bundle-splitting purpose stated in MultiEmailLazy. Import from the relative component modules like other form components in this package do.

title: Team admin/owner check uses AND instead of OR
body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...). A team member is normally either an admin or an owner, not both, so legitimate team admins and owners will almost always fail this check and receive FORBIDDEN unless they also happen to be the organizer or an attendee. The condition should be a logical OR.

title: Calendar is updated with the caller's credentials instead of the organizer's
body: The handler loads credentials for ctx.user and constructs EventManager from ctx.user, then calls updateCalendarAttendees for a booking owned by booking.user. When the caller is an attendee or a team admin/owner, this uses the wrong account's calendar credentials (or none at all), so the organizer's calendar event is not updated even though attendees are added in the database and notification emails are sent. It should use the booking organizer's user and credentials, as the booking query already loads booking.user.credentials.

title: Guest de-duplication and blacklist checks are case-sensitive and do not deduplicate the input
body: uniqueGuests compares guest === attendee.email exactly and checks blacklistedGuestEmails (which were lowercased) against the raw guest string. 'Guest@Example.com' therefore bypasses both the existing-attendee check and the blacklist, and because the server schema has no uniqueness refinement, the same address repeated in one guests array is inserted multiple times via createMany, producing duplicate Attendee rows. Emails should be normalized (trim/lowercase) and the input deduplicated server-side.

title: Guests array is unbounded, enabling bulk attendee/email abuse
body: ZAddGuestsInputSchema accepts an array of arbitrary length. Any organizer, attendee, or (intended) team admin can submit thousands of arbitrary email addresses in one call, creating thousands of Attendee rows, one calendar update, and a scheduled/invitation email to every address — effectively using Cal.com's mail infrastructure to spam third parties and inflating the booking. Add a reasonable .min(1).max(...) bound (and reject empty strings) in the server schema.

title: Guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, or past bookings
body: After the NOT_FOUND check the handler never inspects booking.status or booking.endTime. addGuests will happily insert attendees, call updateCalendarAttendees, and send 'guests added'/scheduled emails for a cancelled, rejected, or already-ended event, resurrecting notifications and calendar invites for a dead booking. The handler should reject non-ACCEPTED (and past) bookings; note the UI also exposes the action for past confirmed bookings.

title: Emails are sent using the unfiltered guests list instead of uniqueGuests
body: sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) is passed the raw input rather than uniqueGuests. In sendAddGuestsEmails, attendees whose email is in that list receive a full AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the AttendeeAddGuestsEmail notice, so pre-existing attendees who were filtered out of the insert (already on the booking) still get re-sent a fresh scheduled invitation, and case-mismatched addresses are misclassified. Pass uniqueGuests (normalized) instead.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores disableStandardEmails event-type metadata
body: Unlike sendLocationChangeEmails/sendScheduledEmails, which check eventTypeDisableHostEmail/eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail, sendAddGuestsEmails always emails the organizer, team members, and every attendee, and the handler does not even pass the event type metadata. Event types configured with disableStandardEmails (e.g. for workflow-only notifications) will leak standard 'guests added' and scheduled emails. Thread the metadata through and honor the host/attendee disable flags.

title: Stale validation error survives a successful submission
body: onSuccess resets multiEmailValue and closes the dialog but never calls setIsInvalidEmail(false); the Cancel button does reset it. If a user first submits an invalid/duplicate email (setting isInvalidEmail), corrects it, and succeeds, the 'Emails must be unique and valid' error is still shown the next time the dialog opens for any booking. Reset isInvalidEmail in onSuccess (and on dialog close via onOpenChange, which currently also leaves both the emails and the error in place when dismissing with the X/backdrop).

title: Retry-count deletion branch is not restricted to SMS reminders
body: The second OR branch in the deleteMany is only `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }`, with no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (or `scheduled: false`) restriction, while `retryCount` is a column on the shared WorkflowReminder table used for EMAIL, SMS and WHATSAPP reminders. Any non-SMS reminder whose retryCount exceeds 1 will therefore be deleted by this SMS cron job even though it was never attempted here. The branch should be scoped to SMS (and unscheduled) reminders like the first branch.

title: Unguarded update inside catch can abort the whole cron run
body: The catch block now performs `prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` without any nested try/catch. If that update fails — e.g. Prisma P2025 because the reminder was deleted concurrently by a booking cancellation/reschedule, or a transient DB error (which may be the same error that triggered the catch) — the exception propagates out of the for loop and out of the handler. All remaining unscheduled reminders in the batch are then skipped and the cron returns an error, whereas previously the catch only logged and the loop continued with the next reminder.

title: Reminders with no recipient or empty message never increment retryCount
body: The retry increment only runs inside `if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo)` (either the else branch for a falsy Twilio result or the catch). When `sendTo` is falsy — e.g. `booking.smsReminderNumber` is null/missing for SMS_ATTENDEE, a permanently invalid case — or when the rendered message is empty, neither branch executes, so retryCount stays 0 and the reminder is re-selected by every cron invocation until its scheduledDate passes. This leaves unfixed the endless-rescheduling loop the PR is meant to stop for missing/invalid numbers.

title: Retry counter uses stale read-modify-write instead of atomic increment
body: Both increment sites write `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value read at the start of the run. If two cron invocations overlap (a run processing many reminders can outlive the cron interval), both read the same value and write the same incremented value, losing a failure count and causing extra scheduling attempts (including possible duplicate Twilio calls). Use Prisma's atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` instead.

title: Retry cleanup deletes workflow reminders for all methods
body: The second OR branch only checks retryCount > 1 and does not also require method: WorkflowMethods.SMS (or scheduled: false). Because Prisma OR branches are independent, this SMS cron job can delete EMAIL and WHATSAPP WorkflowReminder rows whose retryCount ever exceeds 1, even if they are future/unsent reminders owned by other delivery flows. The retry deletion should be scoped to the same SMS reminders this handler manages.

title: Missing message or recipient never increments retryCount
body: Retry counting only happens when twilio.scheduleSMS returns falsy inside the `if (message?.length && sendTo)` block, or when an exception is thrown. If sendTo is missing/empty (for example booking.smsReminderNumber is null) or the rendered message is empty, the handler silently skips the reminder without incrementing retryCount or deleting/scheduling it. Such reminders are fetched again on every cron run until their scheduledDate passes, so this common invalid-recipient failure mode is not bounded by the new retry limit.

title: Retry update inside catch can abort the whole cron run
body: The catch block now performs an awaited prisma.workflowReminder.update without its own error handling. If that update fails, for example because the reminder was deleted between findMany and processing (booking cancellation/reschedule cleanup) or because of a transient DB error (P2025/connection error), the exception escapes the per-reminder try/catch, stops processing all remaining unscheduled reminders, and prevents the success response. Previously the catch only logged and continued to the next reminder.

title: Retry increment uses stale read-modify-write value
body: Both retry paths write `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value fetched at the start of the run instead of an atomic `{ increment: 1 }`. If two cron invocations overlap (or the row is updated concurrently), both can write the same next value, losing a failure count and allowing reminders to be retried more than twice or never reach the `retryCount > 1` deletion threshold.

title: Retry-count deletion is not scoped to SMS reminders
body: The second OR branch matches only `retryCount > 1` and does not require `method: SMS`, `scheduled: false`, or a future/past scheduledDate. This SMS cron therefore deletes EMAIL and WHATSAPP WorkflowReminder rows as well whenever their retryCount exceeds 1, even though it never attempted to schedule them and their own handlers may still need them. The retry cleanup should be restricted to the unscheduled SMS reminders this job actually retries.

title: Retry-count update inside catch can abort the whole cron run
body: The catch block now awaits `prisma.workflowReminder.update` without its own error handling. If that update fails — for example the row was deleted by a concurrent cron invocation (Prisma P2025) or the original error was a transient database failure — the new exception escapes the catch, terminates the for loop, and the handler returns an error instead of processing the remaining unscheduled reminders. One bad reminder can therefore block all later reminders in the run; the increment should be best-effort or use a delete/updateMany that tolerates a missing row.

title: Reminders with no recipient or no message never get a retry count
body: Retry counting only happens inside `if (message?.length && sendTo)` (via the scheduledSMS-null branch) or in the catch block. A reminder whose booking has no `smsReminderNumber`, whose workflow step has no `sendTo`, or whose message resolves to empty silently falls through with retryCount unchanged and `scheduled` still false, so it is re-fetched and re-processed on every cron invocation until its scheduledDate finally passes — exactly the endless-rescheduling loop this PR is meant to eliminate for undeliverable SMS reminders.

title: Retry count is written from a stale read instead of an atomic increment
body: Both retry writes set `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value read at the start of the run. If two cron invocations overlap, both read the same retryCount (e.g. 1), both fail, and both write 2's predecessor value 2-minus-one (i.e. both write 2 when starting from 1 is fine, but starting from 0 both write 1), so failed attempts are under-counted and the `retryCount > 1` deletion threshold can be postponed indefinitely under repeated overlap. Use Prisma's atomic `{ increment: 1 }` update instead.

title: Public findMany API removed without migrating call sites
body: The conversion deletes InsightsBookingService.findMany and changes getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions from Prisma WhereInput objects to Prisma.Sql, but this PR updates no production call sites. Any existing caller using findMany or composing the returned WhereInput objects will fail to compile or break at runtime; callers must be migrated to embed getBaseConditions() in a $queryRaw statement in the same change.

title: Event-type filter fragment is not parenthesized against OR leakage
body: The eventTypeId condition is returned as `("eventTypeId" = X) OR ("eventParentId" = X)` with no outer parentheses. It is only safe inside getBaseConditions(), which happens to wrap it; getFilterConditions() is public and if a caller composes it as `WHERE <auth> AND ${filter}` or `${filter} AND <other>`, SQL precedence evaluates it as `a OR (b AND c)`, letting eventTypeId matches bypass the other condition. The fragment itself should be wrapped in parentheses.

title: Array ANY authorization SQL is never actually executed against the database
body: The only $queryRaw execution uses user scope with scalar parameters. The org and team authorization paths, which rely on `"teamId" = ANY(${number[]})` and `"userId" = ANY(${number[]})` parameter binding, are only compared as Prisma.Sql objects with toEqual, so a runtime array-serialization/type error or wrong result from Postgres would pass all tests despite being the highest-risk part of the conversion.

title: Org-scope expectation depends on unspecified database result ordering
body: The test expects teamIds in [org, team, team2, team3] order and userIds in [user, user2, user3] order, but neither findAllByParentId nor MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds guarantees an ORDER BY. The ANY arrays can legitimately be returned in a different order, making this integration test flaky even though the generated SQL is semantically equivalent.

title: Caching behavior tests deleted while caching remains in the service
body: The PR removes the entire Caching describe block, but InsightsBookingService still caches authorization and filter conditions in cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions. Nothing now verifies that repeated calls reuse the cached Prisma.Sql conditions, so a regression in the caching logic (kept through the conversion) would go undetected.

title: Org and team ANY conditions are never executed against the database
body: The only test that executes SQL through $queryRaw uses scope "user", which produces no array parameter. The org and team authorization tests only compare Prisma.Sql objects with toEqual, so they verify the stored strings/values but not that PostgreSQL and Prisma accept and correctly bind `= ANY(${numberArray})` at runtime. If array serialization or parameter typing fails for ANY, every org/team insights query would fail in production while these tests pass; an executed org or team $queryRaw case is needed.

title: Single event-type filter returns an unparenthesized OR expression
body: When eventTypeId is the only filter, buildFilterConditions returns `("eventTypeId" = ...) OR ("eventParentId" = ...)` with no outer parentheses. The previous Prisma WhereInput preserved this OR as a grouped unit in any composition. Now, any caller that composes the public getFilterConditions() result as `... AND ${filter}` gets `( ... AND eventTypeId = ...) OR eventParentId = ...` due to AND/OR precedence, potentially returning bookings matching eventParentId outside the intended preceding conditions. getBaseConditions happens to wrap it, but the standalone filter condition is unsafe and inconsistent with the combined-filter case, which does add parentheses.

title: Public options type allows a team scope without teamId
body: InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions makes teamId optional for every scope, so `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` now compiles. The runtime schema then rejects it, stores options as null, and all queries silently return the 1=0 condition instead of the caller getting a compile-time error as with the previous discriminated-union options type. This turns a programming error into silently empty insights data.

title: Caching behavior lost its test coverage
body: The service still caches authorization and filter conditions (cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions at lines 49-50 and the checks at lines 84-94), but this PR deletes the previous "Caching" describe block from the integration tests and adds no replacement. A regression that stops returning the cached Prisma.Sql, rebuilds conditions on every call, or mishandles the cached null filter result would no longer be detected.

title: Public findMany method removed without migrating callers
body: The conversion deletes InsightsBookingService.findMany, which previously accepted BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedFindManyArgs and executed the query, and replaces it with getBaseConditions that only returns a Prisma.Sql fragment. No caller in this PR is updated to construct and execute a $queryRaw query instead. Any existing consumer calling service.findMany(...) will now fail TypeScript compilation (and would fail at runtime if untyped), breaking the insights data path until every call site is migrated.

title: Event-type filter returns an unparenthesized OR expression
body: buildFilterConditions stores the event-type condition as `("eventTypeId" = X) OR ("eventParentId" = X)` with no parentheses around the whole OR, and when it is the only filter getFilterConditions returns that fragment unchanged. getBaseConditions happens to wrap it, but the public getFilterConditions result is unsafe to interpolate into a larger WHERE clause: `WHERE "userId" = 1 OR "eventParentId" = 2 AND <other>` is parsed by PostgreSQL as `"userId" = 1 OR ("eventParentId" = 2 AND <other>)` because AND binds tighter than OR, so rows can be returned that ignore the additional constraints.
