The previous structured Prisma where-object preserved this grouping automatically. The fragment should be wrapped as `((...) OR (...))` at construction.

title: Multi-branch authorization conditions are not wrapped as a single expression
body: buildOrgAuthorizationCondition and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition reduce their branches to `(<branch A>) OR (<branch B>)` without enclosing the complete OR in parentheses, and the single-branch case returns a bare AND expression. getBaseConditions wraps the result, but the public getAuthorizationConditions result loses the grouping guarantee the old Prisma where-object provided: a caller interpolating it as `WHERE ${auth} AND <date/status condition>` gets `branchA OR (branchB AND <condition>)`, so branch A rows bypass the caller's date/status restrictions. This is an authorization-adjacent correctness risk; the builders should return a fully parenthesized expression.

title: Org and team raw SQL is never actually executed against the database
body: The org/team authorization tests only compare the returned Prisma.Sql object with an expected Prisma.Sql built from the same template syntax, and the sole $queryRaw execution test at line 481 exercises only the user scope. Consequently invalid PostgreSQL produced for org/team scopes — for example the `= ANY(${array})` parameter binding on lines 333-343 of the test / in the service, quoted identifiers, or boolean comparisons — would pass these tests and only fail (or misbehave) when a real org/team insights query runs. At least one org-scope and one team-scope test should execute the conditions via $queryRaw against the seeded data and assert the returned booking ids, especially since the PR description states the tests were not successfully run during development.

title: Caching coverage deleted while caching logic remains
body: This PR removes the entire 'Caching' describe block that verified repeated getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions calls return cached results, but the service still implements that caching (cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions in insightsBooking.ts). No replacement test covers it, so a regression that removes or breaks the cache — causing repeated membership/team database lookups on every insights query — would go undetected. The caching tests should have been ported to Prisma.Sql expectations like the other tests instead of deleted.

title: Delete-cache mutation never refreshes connectedCalendars data
body: The deleteCacheMutation onSuccess only shows a toast and calls the optional external onSuccess callback. Unlike the disconnect mutation in the same file (onSettled invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars), it never invalidates that query, and SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper's own query is not refetched by the external onChanged callback. After a successful deletion the dropdown therefore keeps showing the old cacheUpdatedAt timestamp and 'Delete cached data' action until a manual reload, making it look like the deletion did nothing.

title: Cache status ignores cache expiry
body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups all CalendarCache rows by credentialId with no expiresAt filter, whereas getCachedAvailability only serves rows with expiresAt >= now. Credentials whose only cache entries are expired (up to a month old, no longer served) will still be reported as having cache, so the UI displays a 'Last updated' status and offers deletion for data that is already unusable, and the timestamp does not reflect any live cache.

title: Pre-existing cache rows get migration time as updatedAt
body: Adding updatedAt as NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW() stamps every legacy CalendarCache row with the migration/deployment time rather than its actual last-write time. Immediately after deploy, the new UI will present that deployment timestamp as 'Cache last updated' for all existing credentials, even for cache entries written weeks earlier, giving users a misleading freshness signal until each row happens to be rewritten.

title: Handler bypasses the calendar-cache repository abstraction and always queries
body: The handler directly instantiates the concrete CalendarCacheRepository on every connectedCalendars call, instead of going through the CalendarCache/calendar-cache-disabled path that CalendarCacheRepositoryMock exists for. This adds a groupBy query to every connected-calendars load (including users with no Google credentials and orgs with calendar-cache disabled, where the mock would return []) and surfaces cache status/deletion for stale rows even when the cache feature is off.

title: Committed dev script only works on macOS and writes outside the repo
body: `sed -i ''` is BSD/macOS syntax; GNU sed on Linux treats '' as an input file and fails, so the script cannot update GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL on Linux. Additionally ENV_FILE is hardcoded to ../.env relative to the caller's working directory, so running it from the repo root writes the tunnel URL to a .env outside the repository instead of the repo's .env. This unrelated local-testing script should not be merged in this form.

title: dev:cron now depends on unpinned npx tsx which is not a declared dependency
body: tsx is not listed in apps/web (or root) dependencies, so `npx tsx cron-tester.ts` will download an unpinned package from the registry on first run. That breaks offline/air-gapped dev environments, is a supply-chain risk, and can silently change behavior as tsx releases change; tsx should be added as a pinned devDependency or the previously available ts-node kept.

title: Cache timestamp is always formatted in en-US regardless of user locale
body: The 'last updated' timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', ...) even though the surrounding UI is localized via useLocale. Non-English users will see US-style dates (e.g. 7/15/25) inside otherwise translated text; the format should use the current user's locale.

title: Deleting cache does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query
body: The deleteCacheMutation only shows a toast and calls the optional onSuccess callback, unlike disconnectMutation which invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars in onSettled. The parent passes onChanged as onSuccess, which is optional and often undefined, and the connectedCalendars query is configured with refetchOnWindowFocus:false. After a successful deletion the dropdown therefore continues to display the old cacheUpdatedAt timestamp and 'Delete cached data' action until some unrelated refetch, making it look as if deletion failed.

title: Cache status includes expired cache entries
body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups all CalendarCache rows for the credentials without filtering on expiresAt. The actual cache-read path (getCachedAvailability) treats rows with expiresAt in the past as misses. Expired, unusable cache will therefore be displayed in the UI as current cache with a 'Last updated' time and a delete action, misreporting the real cache status.

title: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache rewrites updatedAt on every SelectedCalendar for the credential
body: updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) is called unconditionally at the end of fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache, touching every SelectedCalendar row (all users' event-type and user-level rows sharing that credentialId, since there is no userId/eventTypeId filter) purely to bump @updatedAt. This adds a write on every cache fill, and destroys the meaning of SelectedCalendar.updatedAt as the time the selection itself last changed, which other code selecting updatedAt (e.g. UserWithCalendars) can no longer rely on. The frontend in this PR does not even read SelectedCalendar.updatedAt; it uses CalendarCache.updatedAt via cacheUpdatedAt.

title: Cache timestamp is always formatted with the en-US locale
body: The 'last updated' timestamp is formatted with new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', ...) even though the component already uses useLocale() for translations. Non-English users will see US date/time ordering (e.g. 7/15/25, 4:06 PM) alongside otherwise localized strings, instead of formatting in their configured locale.

title: Tunnel helper script is macOS-only and writes outside the repo from repo root
body: The added dev script uses BSD-only 'sed -i ''' syntax, which GNU sed on Linux interprets as an input filename and fails, and ENV_FILE is hard-coded to ../.env, which only points at the repo .env when invoked from a subdirectory. Run from the repo root it reads/writes an .env outside the repository. This unrelated local-testing script will fail or touch the wrong file for Linux contributors.

title: dev:cron now depends on an undeclared, unpinned tsx fetched via npx
body: The script was changed from ts-node (which is declared in devDependencies) to 'npx tsx', but tsx is not added as a dependency anywhere in this change. Running yarn dev:cron will download an unpinned executable from the registry at runtime, failing offline and introducing an unreviewed supply-chain dependency, instead of using a lockfile-pinned tool.

title: Deleting cache does not invalidate connectedCalendars query
body: The deleteCache mutation only shows a toast and calls the optional onSuccess callback, unlike disconnectMutation below it which invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars and viewer.apps.integrations on settle. SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper passes onChanged which may be undefined, so after a successful deletion the connectedCalendars query is not refetched, cacheUpdatedAt remains truthy, and the dropdown continues to show 'Cache Status' and 'Delete cached data' for cache that no longer exists until a manual reload.

title: Cache status includes expired cache entries
body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups all CalendarCache rows for the credentials without filtering on expiresAt, whereas getCachedAvailability only serves rows with expiresAt >= now. After the one-month caching period expires, the UI will still report a 'Last updated' cache status and offer 'Delete cached data' for an entry that is never actually served, misleading users and support about whether cached availability is in effect.

title: Cache timestamp is hardcoded to en-US locale
body: The timestamp is formatted with new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...) regardless of the user's configured locale obtained via useLocale. Non-English users will see US-style dates (e.g. 7/15/25) mixed into an otherwise localized UI; the formatter should use the active locale (and ideally be memoized rather than constructed on every render).

title: Tunnel script is macOS-only and silently reports failure as success
body: Line 68 uses BSD/macOS syntax `sed -i '' -E ...`, which fails under GNU sed on Linux ('' is treated as an input file), so GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is never updated there. Additionally, the failure paths at lines 46-58 call cleanup(), which unconditionally `exit 0`, so rate-limit and 'failed to extract URL' failures are reported to callers/CI as success. ENV_FILE is also hardcoded to ../.env, which only resolves correctly when invoked from a specific working directory.

title: dev:cron depends on undeclared tsx fetched via npx
body: The script was changed from ts-node (a declared devDependency) to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, but tsx is not declared in this package's dependencies/devDependencies. In this Yarn-workspaces repo the command will attempt to download an unpinned tsx from the network at runtime, failing offline and introducing an unreviewed, unpinned executable into the dev workflow; tsx should be added as a pinned devDependency or the ts-node runner retained.

title: deleteCache throws a generic Error instead of a tRPC error and has no tests
body: When the credential does not belong to the user the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`, which tRPC surfaces as an opaque INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) rather than a NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN client error, so the client can only show the generic 'Error deleting cache' toast and monitoring records a server fault for a routine authorization denial. The new mutation also ships without any test covering the ownership check or the deletion, so a future refactor could allow deleting another user's cache (prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany is keyed only by the input credentialId) without failing CI.

title: One failed SendGrid cancellation aborts cancellation of all remaining reminders
body: The entire cancellation loop is wrapped in a single try/catch and each SendGrid request is awaited inside it. If cancelling one reminder fails (for example an invalid or already-cancelled batch_id), the exception exits the loop, the remaining reminders in the next-hour window are never sent a cancellation request, and the Prisma delete operations already queued in workflowRemindersToDelete are never awaited (they are lazy Prisma promises), so even successfully-cancelled reminders keep their rows. Those uncancelled SendGrid emails will still be delivered for cancelled/rescheduled bookings. Each reminder needs its own error handling so one failure does not block the rest.

title: Last-minute cancellations are deleted without ever cancelling the SendGrid email
body: Deferred cancellation only happens when the cron job runs and finds cancelled=true with scheduledDate within the next hour, but at the top of the same handler all EMAIL workflowReminders with scheduledDate <= now are deleted unconditionally before the cancellation block runs. If a booking is cancelled after the last cron run before its reminder's send time (the PR states the cron runs every 15 minutes), the next run can cross the scheduledDate, delete the DB row first, and never issue the SendGrid cancel for that batch; SendGrid has already dispatched the email. The reminder for a just-cancelled booking is therefore still sent in this window, and the row deletion removes any chance of a later retry.

title: immediateDelete path leaves the reminder row active with no retry if SendGrid fails
body: When immediateDelete is true, deleteScheduledEmailReminder issues the SendGrid cancel request and returns without deleting the WorkflowReminder row and without setting cancelled=true. The reschedule caller in handleNewBooking.ts relies on this path and does not delete the old booking's reminders via cascade, so the old row remains scheduled=true/cancelled=null; the cron job only retries rows with cancelled=true, so if the SendGrid request throws (the error is only logged inside this function) nothing ever retries the cancellation and the old booking's reminder email is still sent. It also leaves stale scheduled reminder rows attached to the superseded booking until their scheduledDate passes.

title: Reminder cancellations are fired without awaiting persistence of the cancelled flag
body: updatedBookings.forEach(...) calls the async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder and discards the returned promises. The handler then deletes attendees/references, sends cancellation emails and returns 200 without guaranteeing the prisma update that sets cancelled=true (or the SMS/Twilio cancellation and row deletion) has completed. In a serverless/short-lived invocation the process can finish or be frozen before the update lands, leaving the reminder active for the cron/SendGrid to send; the same un-awaited pattern in the try/catch in handleNewBooking.ts also means that try/catch can never observe failures. These promises should be collected and awaited (e.g. Promise.all) before responding.

title: One SendGrid failure prevents cancellation of all other reminders
body: The entire cancellation loop is wrapped in a single try/catch and the Prisma deletes are only executed via Promise.all after the loop finishes. If client.request fails for any one reminder (e.g. an invalid/already-handled batch_id or a transient SendGrid error), the catch is taken, the remaining reminders are never sent a cancel request, and even the deletes already queued for earlier reminders are discarded. Those WorkflowReminder rows stay cancelled=true and their already-scheduled SendGrid emails are still delivered, so a single bad reminder can break cancellation for every other reminder in that cron run.

title: immediateDelete path has no cron fallback if the SendGrid cancel fails
body: When immediateDelete is true (used for rescheduled bookings in handleNewBooking and for deleted workflows/steps in workflows.tsx) the function POSTs status=cancel to SendGrid and returns without deleting the WorkflowReminder row and without setting cancelled=true. deleteScheduledEmailReminder also catches and only logs SendGrid errors. If that immediate POST fails - including hitting the 100 pending-cancellations limit that this PR is meant to work around - nothing marks the reminder for the scheduleEmailReminders cron to cancel later, so the old reminder email is still sent for the rescheduled/deleted booking.

title: Reminders cancelled shortly before send time can still be delivered
body: Cancellation is deferred until scheduledDate is within one hour (scheduledDate <= now+1h) and this cron is described as running every 15 minutes, while the job's first statement deletes EMAIL reminders whose scheduledDate has passed without issuing any SendGrid cancel. A booking cancelled, say, 10 minutes before a reminder's send time can therefore have its next cron run only after SendGrid has already sent the email; the row is then silently deleted by the lte:now deleteMany and the cancellation is lost. There is no check at cancellation time for how soon the reminder fires.

title: Workflow reminder cancellations are fired without being awaited
body: updatedBookings.forEach(...) calls the now-async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder and discards the returned promises; the same fire-and-forget pattern is used for the reschedule path in handleNewBooking.ts and the requestReschedule path in bookings.tsx. The handler can return (and, in a serverless invocation, the process can be frozen/terminated) before the prisma update that sets cancelled=true (or deletes an unscheduled reminder) has completed, and the surrounding try/catch in handleNewBooking cannot observe async failures. The booking is reported cancelled while its reminder may never be marked cancelled, so the scheduled email/SMS is still sent. These calls should be collected and awaited with Promise.all.

title: Workflow-reminder cancellation is fire-and-forget and may never persist
body: updatedBookings.forEach calls the now-async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder without returning or awaiting them (same pattern in handleNewBooking reschedule and bookings.requestReschedule). deleteScheduledEmailReminder performs the prisma update that sets cancelled=true inside that unawaited promise, and the previous implementation's awaited prisma deleteMany was removed. The handler can finish/return (and a serverless invocation can freeze) before the update runs, and errors are only swallowed by the callee's catch, so a cancelled booking can keep an active SendGrid/Twilio reminder and the email/SMS is still sent.

title: One failing SendGrid cancellation aborts cancellation of all remaining reminders
body: The for loop awaits client.request for each reminder inside a single try/catch, and the prisma deletes are only executed via Promise.all after the loop completes. If any one request throws (e.g. a null/invalid referenceId, an already-handled batch, or a transient SendGrid error), the catch is taken immediately: reminders later in the list are never cancelled, and even reminders already successfully cancelled at SendGrid are never deleted from the DB. Because the failing reminder stays first-class on the next cron run, it can repeatedly block/poison all other pending cancellations and those emails will be sent at their scheduled time. Each reminder needs per-item error isolation and deletion.

title: immediateDelete path loses the cancellation if SendGrid rejects it, with no deferred retry
body: When immediateDelete is true (used for rescheduled bookings in handleNewBooking and for deleted workflows/steps in workflows.tsx) the function POSTs status=cancel to SendGrid and returns without deleting the WorkflowReminder row or setting cancelled=true. If that POST fails - e.g. the very 100-pending-cancellations limit this PR is meant to work around - the internal catch only logs it, so the DB still shows a normal scheduled reminder, the scheduleEmailReminders cron (which only acts on cancelled=true rows) will never retry it, and SendGrid will send the reminder for the rescheduled/deleted booking. The immediate path should fall back to marking the row cancelled on failure (and should remove/mark the row on success, since rescheduled bookings are not cascade-deleted).

title: Deferred cancellation window lets imminently-due reminders be sent after cancellation
body: Non-immediate cancellations only set cancelled=true; the email is only actually cancelled by this cron, which runs periodically (per PR description every 15 minutes) and picks up rows whose scheduledDate is within the next hour. If a booking is cancelled/rescheduled (via the non-immediate paths) shortly before a reminder's scheduledDate - e.g. 5 minutes before a 24h-before reminder fires - and the next cron run lands after that date, SendGrid dispatches the email before it is ever cancelled; the cron's first deleteMany then just deletes the past-due row. Cancellation needs an immediate SendGrid cancel when the scheduled time is near (or a much tighter guarantee), not purely deferred handling.

title: Dynamic imports are all executed eagerly, not lazily per app
body: Every value in the appStore object literal is an import() call, so merely importing packages/app-store/index.ts immediately starts loading all ~30 app modules; accessing appStore.zoomvideo does not lazily load only Zoom. This defeats the stated goal of async/lazy app loading, keeps the startup/bundle cost the PR aims to remove, and creates stored promises for apps that are never used (including possible unhandled rejections if an unused app fails to load). Values should be thunks such as `zoomvideo: () => import("./zoomvideo")` and call sites should invoke then await them.

title: Recurring-booking calendar deletions race with Promise.all(apiDeletes)
body: The recurring-event branch still uses `.forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent) })`. Because getCalendar is now async, the pushes into apiDeletes happen after the synchronous forEach returns and potentially after `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` near the end of the handler has already snapshot the array. Those deleteEvent calls can therefore never be awaited, may be dropped when the request/serverless function ends, and their rejections are unhandled, leaving calendar events undeleted while the booking is reported successfully cancelled.

title: Async forEach makes calendar/video cancellation fire-and-forget and bypasses try/catch
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })` discards the promises returned by the callback. Reschedule() can return true and the reschedule email can be sent before deletions finish, deletions can be lost on process termination, and a rejection from the now-async getCalendar/deleteMeeting is not caught by the surrounding try/catch (which only catches synchronous throws), producing an unhandled rejection instead of the logged error. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` inside the try.

title: Async forEach makes calendar/video cancellation fire-and-forget and bypasses try/catch
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })` discards the promises returned by the callback. Reschedule() can return true and the reschedule email can be sent before deletions finish, deletions can be lost on process termination, and a rejection from the now-async getCalendar/deleteMeeting is not caught by the surrounding try/catch (which only catches synchronous throws), producing an unhandled rejection instead of the logged error. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` inside the try.

title: requestReschedule does not await calendar/video deletions
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) / deleteMeeting(...) })` discards the async callback promises. The mutation proceeds to send the reschedule email and webhooks and returns without guaranteeing the old calendar/video events were deleted, and any rejection from getCalendar/deleteEvent/deleteMeeting becomes an unhandled rejection rather than being surfaced or logged. Replace forEach with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))`.

title: Dynamic imports are still started eagerly for every app
body: Every value in the appStore object is the result of calling import() when this module is first evaluated, e.g. applecalendar: import("./applecalendar") on line 3 and similarly for all 29 apps. Any module that imports appStore (videoClient, payment helpers, booking handlers, etc.) therefore starts loading every app package even when it only needs one, defeating the purpose of async/lazy loading and paying the import side-effect cost up front. A rejected import for an unused app also becomes an unhandled promise rejection because nothing ever awaits that particular promise. These should be thunks, e.g. applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar"), with callers invoking the thunk so only the requested app is loaded.

title: Recurring-booking calendar deletions are pushed to apiDeletes asynchronously and never awaited
body: In the allRemainingBookings branch, credentials are iterated with .forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); }). The async callbacks suspend at the await, so the main flow continues past this block before any push happens; the later await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) at line 652 snapshots apiDeletes without these entries (and the pushed value is the already-awaited result, not a promise). Calendar deleteEvent calls for recurring bookings are thus fire-and-forget: the handler can send cancellation emails and return (or the serverless function can freeze) before the external calendar events are deleted, leaving zombie events, and any rejection is unhandled. Use for...of or Promise.all over map() and push the deleteEvent promises before the Promise.all.

title: Async forEach makes calendar/video cancellation fire-and-forget and escapes the try/catch
body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); }) is not awaited, and the surrounding try/catch (lines 124-139) cannot catch rejections from the async callback because forEach ignores the returned promises. Reschedule() proceeds to send the reschedule email and return true before the old calendar/video events are actually deleted, and a failing dynamic import or deleteEvent becomes an unhandled rejection instead of being logged. Replace with await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...)) inside the try block.

title: Async forEach makes calendar/video cancellation fire-and-forget and escapes the try/catch
body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); }) is not awaited, and the surrounding try/catch (lines 124-139) cannot catch rejections from the async callback because forEach ignores the returned promises. Reschedule() proceeds to send the reschedule email and return true before the old calendar/video events are actually deleted, and a failing dynamic import or deleteEvent becomes an unhandled rejection instead of being logged. Replace with await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...)) inside the try block.

title: requestReschedule does not await calendar/video deletions before emailing and returning
body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); }) discards the promises returned by the async callbacks. The mutation immediately continues to sendRequestRescheduleEmail and the webhook flow and can return while getCalendar/deleteEvent/deleteMeeting are still in flight; on serverless runtimes the work may be dropped entirely, leaving the original calendar/video event in place after the booking is marked CANCELLED, and failures are unhandled rejections. Await the deletions, e.g. await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => { ... })), before sending the email.

title: Dynamic imports are evaluated eagerly, not lazily
body: Every value in the appStore object literal is an immediately invoked import() (e.g. `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")` on line 3 and likewise for all ~29 apps). Evaluating this object when the module is first imported therefore starts loading every app at once, so importing appStore from any file (getCalendar, videoClient, payment handlers, routers) still pulls in all apps and defeats the lazy/on-demand loading this PR is meant to achieve. The values need to be thunks (e.g. `() => import(...)`) with call sites invoking them, or an equivalent lazy lookup, to actually defer loading until an app is requested.

title: appStore value type changed from module to Promise without a compatible accessor
body: appStore previously mapped each key to a module namespace object, so consumers could synchronously use `appStore[key].lib`, `'lib' in appStore[key]`, etc. It now maps each key to a Promise of the module, which is not backward compatible: any consumer not converted to `await appStore[key]` in this PR will receive a Promise, find no `lib` property (`'lib' in promise` is false), and silently skip calendar/video/payment functionality (or fail type-checking). This PR only updates a subset of call sites, so the exported contract break needs either a full audit/conversion of every appStore consumer or a compatibility-preserving accessor.

title: async forEach callback makes calendar/video deletion fire-and-forget
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` ignores the promise returned by the callback. Because getCalendar is now awaited inside, the actual `calendar.deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` calls no longer even start synchronously; Reschedule() proceeds to send the reschedule email and return true before deletion begins, and on serverless/request completion the deletions may never run, leaving stale calendar/video events. The surrounding try/catch (lines 124-139) also cannot catch rejections from the async callback, so failures become unhandled rejections instead of being logged. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` (or a for...of loop) so deletion completes and errors are handled.

title: async forEach callback makes calendar/video deletion fire-and-forget
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` ignores the promise returned by the callback. Because getCalendar is now awaited inside, `calendar.deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` no longer start synchronously; Reschedule() proceeds to send the reschedule email and return true before deletion begins, and if the request/process ends first the deletions are lost, leaving stale calendar/video events. The surrounding try/catch (lines 124-139) cannot catch rejections from the async callback, so failures become unhandled rejections instead of being logged. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` (or a for...of loop).

title: async forEach callback makes reschedule deletion fire-and-forget
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... })` discards each callback's promise. The mutation then immediately sends the reschedule email, fires webhooks, and returns, so the calendar/video deletions for the old booking may not have started, let alone finished; if the request context is torn down they are silently dropped and the old events remain. Rejections inside the callback are also unhandled. Replace with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` before sending email/webhooks.

title: Recurring-booking calendar deletions are pushed to apiDeletes after it is awaited
body: In the recurring-cancellation branch, `bookingToDelete.user.credentials...forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })` runs its pushes only after awaiting getCalendar (now a dynamic import) and deleteEvent. Later, `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` (line 652) snapshots whatever apiDeletes contains at that moment, so entries pushed afterwards are never awaited; the handler can delete booking references/attendees and report success while the recurring calendar events are never deleted. Convert this branch to a for...of loop or collect the per-credential work with Promise.all and push/await those promises, as was done for the non-recurring branch.

title: Date-override path bypasses busy-time checks
body: When a slot falls inside a date override, dateOverrideExist is set to true and checkIfIsAvailable returns true at line 135 without reaching the busy.every(...) check at line 153. Consequently calendar events and existing Cal bookings are ignored for every slot on an override day, so a fixed or round-robin host can be double-booked on days with a date override.

title: Dayjs object identity comparison never detects empty overrides
body: dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...) compares two distinct Dayjs objects by reference, so it is always false. The branch intended to recognize a zero-length override (start equals end, i.e. unavailable for that override period/day) is dead code, and such overrides are not handled as intended.

title: Slots only partially overlapping a date override are accepted
body: The override test only rejects slots that end at/before the override start or start after the override end. A slot that starts before the override and ends inside it, starts inside it and ends after it, or starts exactly at override end (slotStartTime.isAfter(end) is false when equal) falls through to dateOverrideExist and is returned as available. checkIfIsAvailable therefore does not enforce that the whole [slotStart, slotEnd) interval is contained in the override, allowing fixed-host bookings partially outside their override availability.

title: Working-hours guard uses slot start twice and lets non-working days pass
body: In the workingHours.find callback, both start and end are computed from slotStartTime.hour()/minute(), so a slot starting inside working hours but ending after workingHour.endTime is accepted. Additionally, find only returns true when a working hour exists for slotStartTime.day() and the slot is outside it: if no working hour includes that weekday at all, or another same-day range covers the slot while an earlier range does not, the logic either falls through to the busy check as available or incorrectly rejects. This defeats the new fixed-host filtering for hosts whose hours end earlier, who don't work that day, or who have split ranges.

title: No test covers round-robin fixed-host date overrides
body: The only added test re-queries a single-user event (hosts: []) with a different invitee timezone. It does not create a ROUND_ROBIN event with a fixed host and a loose host, does not give only the fixed host a date override, and does not exercise the new checkIfIsAvailable dateOverrides/workingHours filtering added for fixed/loose hosts in slots.ts. The main scenario described in the PR (slots must be limited by the fixed host's override) can regress without any test failing.

title: Slots inside a date override skip busy-time checks
body: When a slot's date matches a date override and the slot is inside the override window, dateOverrideExist is set and checkIfIsAvailable returns true at line 133-135 before reaching the busy.every(...) check at the end. Consequently a fixed or round-robin host who has a calendar event or an accepted Cal booking during their override hours will still be reported available, allowing double-bookings on override days.

title: Working-hours check uses slot start for both start and end
body: Both start and end are computed as slotStartTime.hour()*60+slotStartTime.minute(); slotEndTime is never used. A slot that starts inside working hours but ends after workingHour.endTime (e.g. a 60-minute slot starting 30 minutes before closing) therefore passes the check, so checkIfIsAvailable can approve slots that overrun the host's working hours.

title: Working-hours check rejects split shifts and approves days with no working hours
body: The code returns unavailable if workingHours.find(...) finds ANY entry for that weekday outside which the slot falls. With split working hours (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00) a 13:00 slot is outside the first entry, so it is incorrectly rejected. Conversely, if no entry includes slotStartTime.day(), find returns undefined and the check passes, so a fixed host with no working hours that day is treated as available for a slot generated by another (round-robin) host — defeating the fixed-host enforcement this PR adds.

title: Dayjs object identity comparison for empty override never matches
body: dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...) compares two distinct Dayjs objects by reference, so it is always false. The intended special case for an empty override (start equals end, i.e. unavailable all day) is dead code; an early-morning slot on such a day (e.g. 00:00, where slotEnd is not before start and slotStart is not after end) falls through with dateOverrideExist=true and is returned as available.

title: Slots partially overlapping the end of a date override are accepted
body: A slot is only considered outside the override if its end is at/before the override start or its start is after the override end. A slot starting inside the override but ending after it (e.g. override 14:00-15:00, 60-minute slot at 14:30) satisfies neither condition, so it is accepted even though half the slot lies outside the host's override availability. The same find()-based logic also stops at the first override for the date, so a slot valid under a second override range on the same day can be rejected because it is outside the first.

title: Timezone-shifted overrides that cross midnight are placed on the wrong day or dropped
body: startTime/endTime are derived only from hour()*60+minute() after adding the invitee-organizer offset, discarding any day shift caused by that offset. An override near midnight in the organizer timezone (e.g. 01:00 in UTC+14 viewed by a UTC-10 invitee, shifting to the previous day) is rendered at 01:00-style minutes on the invitee day selected by activeOverrides instead of the shifted day, and if the shifted end passes midnight endTime becomes smaller than startTime so buildSlots discards the range (start >= end). Override slots near midnight will be missing or shown on the wrong date.

title: No test covers round-robin fixed-host date overrides, and the timezone test cannot detect a shift
body: The stated main fix — date overrides of fixed hosts restricting round-robin events — has no test: every scenario added/used here is a single-user event with hosts: []. The added different-timezone assertion at lines 788-804 re-queries with the exact same UTC startTime/endTime window and expects identical UTC slot times, which passes by construction (slots are returned in UTC) and would not catch an override being applied on the wrong local date or shifted across a day boundary in the invitee timezone.

title: Date-override slots bypass busy-time checks
body: When a slot's day matches a date override, checkIfIsAvailable returns true at line 133-135 before reaching the busy.every(...) check at the end of the function. Consequently a fixed or round-robin host who has a date override but also has a conflicting Cal booking or connected-calendar event during the override window is still reported as available, allowing double bookings on override days.

title: Working-hours check never checks the slot end time
body: Both start and end are computed identically from slotStartTime (hour*60+minute); slotEndTime is never used. A slot that starts inside working hours but ends after workingHour.endTime (e.g. a 60-minute event starting 30 minutes before the end of availability) therefore passes the check and is offered outside the host's working hours.

title: Working-hours find logic rejects valid split shifts and accepts days with no availability
body: The code uses workingHours.find(...) and returns unavailable if ANY entry for that weekday is outside the slot. With split/multiple working-hour ranges on the same day, a slot valid in the second range is rejected because it is outside the first. Conversely, if no entry includes slotStartTime.day(), find returns undefined and execution falls through to the busy check, so a host with no working hours that day is treated as available — defeating the per-fixed-host check this PR adds, since getTimeSlots only receives aggregated hours.

title: Multiple date overrides on the same day are handled incorrectly
body: dateOverrides.find(...) stops at the first override for which the callback returns true, and the callback returns true when the slot is OUTSIDE that override. With two override ranges on the same day, a slot inside the first range but outside the second makes find succeed and the function returns false, incorrectly hiding slots that are inside one of the day's overrides.

title: Zero-length date override comparison uses object identity
body: dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...) compares two distinct Dayjs objects with ===, which is always false. The intended special case for an empty override (start equals end, i.e. unavailable all day) is therefore never detected via this branch and relies on accidental fall-through of the surrounding comparisons, so empty overrides are not reliably honoured.

title: Override conversion assumes timeZone is present and loses day overflow
body: override.timeZone is optional in the TimeRange type (packages/types/schedule.d.ts), but line 212-213 unconditionally calls .tz(override.timeZone); callers passing overrides without timeZone get a guessed/default timezone offset and wrong slots. Additionally startTime/endTime are reduced to hour*60+minute after adding the offset, so an override pushed past midnight by the offset wraps to a small minute value, producing endTime <= startTime which buildSlots discards (start >= end), causing override availability near midnight in another timezone to disappear rather than appear on the correct invitee day.

title: No test for the round-robin fixed-host date override fix
body: The PR description states the main fix is that fixed hosts' date overrides constrain round-robin events, but the only added test exercises a personal event in a different invitee timezone. There is no scenario with schedulingType ROUND_ROBIN, a fixed host with a date override, and a loose host, verifying that slots outside the fixed host's override are hidden and slots inside it remain — so the new checkIfIsAvailable fixed-host path (including its busy-time and working-hours behaviour) is untested and regressions would not be caught.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category is not set in the database
body: The migration unconditionally does execute(...)[0]['id'] for the embed_category lookup. On a fresh install, or any site that never changed embed_category (site_settings only stores non-default values), that query returns zero rows, so [0] is nil and nil['id'] raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration and leaving the upgrade half-applied. The same pattern on line 15 for uncategorized_category_id has the same problem. The lookup needs to handle an empty result before indexing into it.

title: Migration interpolates stored host values directly into SQL and stores them unsanitized
body: Each line from the old embeddable_hosts setting is interpolated unescaped into an INSERT statement ('#{h}'). A host value containing a single quote breaks the migration, and a crafted value can inject arbitrary SQL executed with the migration's privileges. Additionally the raw value is stored verbatim, so legacy entries like 'http://discourse.org' or 'https://example.com/1234' (both valid in the old setting) are stored with scheme/path intact; EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares them against URI(host).host, which never equals such a string, so those hosts silently stop being allowed after migration. The values should be inserted with quoting/bound parameters and normalized the same way the model normalizes them (strip scheme and path).

title: before_validation crashes when host is nil
body: The before_validation block calls self.host.sub! without checking for nil, and there is no presence validation evaluated before this callback. Creating a host with a missing host parameter (Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host assigns params[:embeddable_host][:host], which is nil when the key is absent) raises NoMethodError instead of failing validation and returning a JSON error, producing a 500.

title: Duplicate and case-variant hosts are allowed, making category selection nondeterministic
body: There is no uniqueness validation on host. An admin can create two embeddable_hosts rows for the same hostname (including case variants, since stored case is preserved and matching lowercases only the column side) pointing at different categories. EmbeddableHost.record_for_host then returns .first with no ORDER BY, so which category embedded topics land in, and effectively which row governs the host, is arbitrary database order. A case-insensitive uniqueness validation (and matching index) is needed.

title: Host validation permits ports and rejects long TLDs, inconsistent with host matching
body: The format regex explicitly allows a port (':[0-9]{1,5}') and paths, but record_for_host matches against URI(referer).host, which excludes the port, so a validated host like 'example.com:3000' can never match and embedding from it is always rejected. Conversely the regex limits the TLD to 2-5 letters, so legitimate hosts on newer/longer TLDs (e.g. .technology, .international) cannot be added at all. The accepted format and the matching logic need to agree.

title: Update and destroy crash with a 500 for a nonexistent host id
body: Both update and destroy use EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and immediately call save_host(host) or host.destroy without a nil check. A stale admin UI (e.g. a host deleted in another tab) or a hand-crafted request with an unknown id therefore raises NoMethodError on nil instead of returning a 404. save_host also dereferences params[:embeddable_host] without checking its presence, with the same 500-on-malformed-request problem.

title: Edit action crashes when a host has no resolvable category
body: The edit action does this.get('host.category.id') unconditionally. host.category is only populated by the store's embedded hydration via Discourse.Category.findById(category_id); if the referenced category was deleted or is not among the site's loaded categories, category is undefined and clicking edit throws a TypeError, making the row impossible to edit or fix from the UI. The same assumption appears on save (line 38), where a blank categoryId sets host.category to undefined even though the server silently substitutes the uncategorized category, so the row displays no category until reload.

title: Fabricator file contents are swapped between category and embeddable_host files
body: category_fabricator.rb now defines only Fabricator(:embeddable_host), while the newly added embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains all the category fabricators (:category, :diff_category, :happy_category, :private_category). Fabrication loads every file so tests still pass, but the swapped contents are misleading for future maintainers editing or adding fabricators, and any tooling that loads fabricator files selectively by name will register the wrong definitions. The contents should be moved back into their eponymous files.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category is unset or unmatched
body: The migration unconditionally calls [0]['id'] on the result of joining categories to the embed_category site setting. On installs that never set embed_category, or whose stored value is not exactly a category name, the query returns no rows, [0] is nil, and nil['id'] raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration and blocking deployment/upgrades. The fallback on line 15 has the same unsafe [0]['value'] pattern.

title: Migrated hosts are inserted verbatim and can break host matching or the migration
body: Hosts from the old embeddable_hosts setting are interpolated directly into INSERT SQL without normalization or quoting. Values stored as 'http://discourse.org' or 'https://example.com/1234' (forms the old setting and specs explicitly allowed) are inserted with scheme/path intact, but EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares them against URI(host).host (a bare hostname), so migrated sites silently lose embedding permission for those hosts. A host containing a single quote also breaks/injects the raw SQL and aborts the migration.

title: before_validation crashes when host is nil
body: The before_validation block calls self.host.sub! without checking for nil. Creating an EmbeddableHost with a missing/blank host (e.g. a direct API POST with no host param reaching the model, or EmbeddableHost.new.valid?) raises NoMethodError instead of failing the format validation and returning a validation error, producing a 500 rather than render_json_error.

title: Update/destroy raise NoMethodError for unknown ids instead of returning 404
body: update and destroy look up the host with where(id: params[:id]).first and immediately call save_host(host)/host.destroy on the result. For a stale or invalid id the lookup returns nil, so save_host dereferences nil.host= and destroy calls nil.destroy, returning a 500. save_host also dereferences params[:embeddable_host] on line 23 without checking presence, so malformed requests crash the same way.

title: Edit action crashes for hosts whose category cannot be resolved
body: The edit action does this.get('host.category.id') unconditionally. A host whose category_id points at a deleted category, the uncategorized sentinel, or a category not present in the client's category list hydrates with category undefined/null (store._lookupSubType returns Discourse.Category.findById(id), which can be undefined), so clicking the pencil throws a TypeError and the row can never be edited or fixed in the UI.

title: Plural _id hydration discards ids and fabricates undefined entries when the collection is not sideloaded
body: For any *_ids key, the new code maps ids through _lookupSubType, assigns the result (which may be an array of undefined when root does not contain the sideloaded collection), and deletes the original *_ids key. Unlike the singular branch, which only replaces the key when a record is found, the plural branch loses the id data and leaves an array of undefined objects for any payload that carries ids without embedding the records, a regression affecting all RestModel types, not just fruits/embeddable hosts.

title: No uniqueness constraint allows ambiguous duplicate hosts
body: Neither the model nor the migration adds a uniqueness validation/index on host. Admins can create two EmbeddableHost rows for the same hostname with different categories; record_for_host then returns whichever row the database happens to return first, so embedded topics from that host are filed into an unpredictable category and host_allowed?/category selection becomes nondeterministic.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category site setting has no database row
body: The expression execute(...)[0]['id'] assumes the SELECT joining categories to the embed_category site_setting returns a row. Site settings are only stored in site_settings when overridden, and the joined category may also have been deleted, so on a fresh or typical install the result is empty, [0] is nil, and nil['id'] raises NoMethodError. The migration then fails and blocks deployment/upgrades; the fallback to uncategorized_category_id on line 15 is unreachable in this case.

title: Migration inserts legacy hosts verbatim via string-interpolated SQL
body: Legacy embeddable_hosts values are inserted with VALUES ('#{h}', ...) without escaping or the normalization EmbeddableHost normally applies (stripping http://, https:// and paths). A value containing a single quote breaks the SQL or alters it, and values such as 'http://discourse.org' or 'https://example.com/1234' are stored verbatim. EmbeddableHost.record_for_host later compares lower(host) to the bare URI hostname, so those migrated rows never match, silently disabling embedding/comment retrieval for previously allowed hosts after upgrade.

title: before_validation crashes on a nil host instead of failing validation
body: The callback unconditionally calls self.host.sub!. If an admin API request omits embeddable_host.host (or sends it as null), host is nil and the callback raises NoMethodError before validates_format_of can run. Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host passes params[:embeddable_host][:host] straight through, so a malformed create/update returns a 500 rather than a validation error.

title: Update and destroy return 500 for a non-existent host id
body: update (lines 10-11) and destroy (lines 15-16) use EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and then unconditionally call save_host(host)/host.destroy. For a stale or invalid id (e.g. a host already deleted in another tab) host is nil, producing NoMethodError and a 500 instead of a 404/not-found response.

title: Editing a host without a resolvable category crashes the component
body: The edit action does this.get('host.category.id') with no guard. host.category is undefined when category_id is null, points at the uncategorized fallback the server assigns for blank categories (SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id, which save() itself can produce via Discourse.Category.findById(categoryId) returning undefined for a null/unknown id on line 38), or the category was deleted. Clicking edit on such a host throws a TypeError and the row cannot be edited or fixed in the UI.

title: No uniqueness constraint on host makes its category mapping ambiguous
body: The model only validates host format; neither a uniqueness validation nor a unique index (the migration creates the table without one) prevents two EmbeddableHost rows for the same hostname with different categories. EmbeddableHost.record_for_host uses .first with no ordering, so TopicEmbed.import will non-deterministically file imported topics under whichever duplicate the database returns first, and admins can create conflicting mappings from the new UI.

title: Plural *_ids hydration discards ids and injects undefined entries when a subtype is not embedded
body: For plural associations the new code maps every id through _lookupSubType, assigns the result to obj[pluralized subtype] and deletes the original *_ids key unconditionally. Unlike the singular branch (which only replaces the key when hydration succeeds), if the related collection is absent from the payload/root (or Discourse.Category.findById misses), the array is filled with undefined entries and the original ids are lost, so consumers iterating the association (e.g. embedding.embeddable_hosts) can hit undefined objects instead of simply having no hydrated association.

title: Second downsize definition overrides the width/height version
body: OptimizedImage now defines self.downsize twice: at line 145 as downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) and again at line 149 as downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}). In Ruby the later definition replaces the earlier one, so any existing caller passing separate width and height arguments will raise ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments), and the line-145 implementation is dead code. The width/height API must be kept working or all callers updated/removed deliberately.

title: Percentage downsize breaks animated GIF handling
body: The controller calls OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails). When allow_animation is true and the file is a GIF, OptimizedImage.optimize dispatches to downsize_instructions_animated/resize_instructions_animated, which passes the dimensions to gifsicle as --resize-fit. Gifsicle expects WxH dimensions, not "80%" (the value also gets a trailing \> from the non-animated path conventions), so it will fail to resize animated GIFs. The loop then retries the failing operation up to 5 times and the oversized GIF proceeds to Upload.create_for still over the limit, so large animated uploads are not actually downsized.

title: Downsize failures are ignored and the same file is used as input and output
body: The resizing loop ignores the boolean return value of OptimizedImage.downsize and uses tempfile.path as both source and destination. If convert/gifsicle fails (corrupt image, unsupported format such as SVG, unsupported geometry), convert_with returns false but the loop still runs up to 5 expensive attempts and then uploads whatever is left at that path. Using the same path for input and output also risks truncating/corrupting the only copy of the uploaded tempfile if the external tool fails part-way, and for non-animated GIFs the [0] selector in downsize_instructions silently reduces the image to its first frame. Failures should be checked and the resize should go through a separate temporary output file that replaces the original only on success.

title: Client-side upload limit hardcoded to 10MB ignores site settings and upload type
body: validateUploadedFile previously used Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], respecting different configured limits for images vs attachments. It now hardcodes maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 for every file type. Sites with a lower max_attachment_size_kb/max_image_size_kb will let users select files the server will reject, and sites configured above 10MB will incorrectly block uploads they intend to allow. The same regression is repeated in displayErrorForUpload at line 246, which reports 10MB as the limit on a 413 response regardless of the actual configured/server limit.

title: Remote download limit hardcoded to 10MB bypasses configured image limit before validation
body: FileHelper.download for API-provided URLs previously capped the download at SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes; it now always allows 10.megabytes. Combined with the new in-request downsizing, an API caller can force the server to download and run up to 5 ImageMagick/ImageOptim passes over a 10MB untrusted image even on sites whose configured max_image_size_kb is much smaller, increasing bandwidth/CPU (decompression-bomb) exposure. If the image still exceeds max_image_size_kb after 5 attempts it is only then rejected by normal upload validation, after the expensive work has been done.

title: Second downsize definition overrides the existing width/height API
body: Ruby does not support method overloading. The new self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) at line 149 replaces the self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) defined at line 145. Existing callers that pass separate width and height values will now raise ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments), breaking thumbnail/avatar downsizing paths that use the original signature.

title: Animated GIF detection fails for extensionless upload tempfiles
body: Upload and downloaded-file tempfiles normally have paths without a .gif extension. OptimizedImage.optimize selects its animated instructions only when the source path matches /\.GIF$/i, so passing tempfile.path here never selects that path despite allow_animation being supplied. The normal downsize instructions use `#{from}[0]`, selecting only the first frame, so an oversized animated GIF is silently flattened instead of being resized as an animation. The extensionless destination can also prevent ImageMagick from inferring the intended output format.

title: Failed image conversions are retried blindly and then ignored
body: The loop ignores the boolean result of OptimizedImage.downsize. If conversion fails—for example for an unsupported/corrupt image or an SVG matched by FileHelper.is_image?—it invokes the same failing conversion up to five times and then proceeds to Upload.create_for with the original oversized file. This wastes external-process work and makes the automatic-downsizing feature fail opaquely instead of falling back or reporting the conversion failure.

title: Hardcoded 10 MB client limit ignores configured image and attachment limits
body: Replacing Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'] with a fixed 10 MB breaks sites whose configured limits differ: attachments or images allowed above 10 MB by an administrator are rejected client-side, while files above a lower configured limit pass client validation and fail later on the server. The hardcoded value in the 413 handler at line 246 likewise reports 10 MB even when the server limit that produced the rejection is different.

title: URL download limit is changed to a fixed 10 MB for every upload type
body: The API URL-download cap no longer uses SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb and is fixed at 10 megabytes regardless of whether the upload is an image or an attachment. This rejects remotely fetched files that the site configuration would allow above 10 MB, and it downloads non-image attachments up to 10 MB even when the applicable configured limit is lower; those attachments cannot be downsized and are only rejected after the transfer.

title: Second downsize definition overrides the existing five-argument version
body: Ruby does not support method overloading. Defining self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) at line 149 replaces self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) at line 145, making the latter dead code. Any existing caller passing separate width and height will now raise ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments, 5 for 4) instead of resizing. The old signature must be preserved or all its callers migrated, e.g. by handling both a String dimension and width/height in one method.

title: Animated GIFs cannot be downsized with a percentage dimension
body: The controller passes "80%" to OptimizedImage.downsize with allow_animation taken from SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails. When animation is allowed, OptimizedImage.optimize routes GIFs to downsize_instructions_animated/resize_instructions_animated, which passes the dimension to `gifsicle --resize-fit`; gifsicle expects a WIDTHxHEIGHT geometry, not "80%", so it fails and the GIF is never reduced. When animation is not allowed, the non-animated path uses `convert from[0]`, which keeps only the first frame and silently flattens an animated upload into a static image. Either way animated GIF uploads are broken by this feature.

title: Downsize result is ignored while converting a file onto itself
body: OptimizedImage.downsize is invoked with tempfile.path as both input and output and its boolean return value is discarded. convert_with returns false on a failed ImageMagick/gifsicle/ImageOptim run, and an in-place convert that fails or is interrupted can leave the target truncated or partially written. The loop then retries up to five times on that possibly-corrupt file and create_upload proceeds to Upload.create_for with it, so a transient conversion failure turns a valid upload into a corrupt stored file instead of keeping the original or reporting an error.

title: Hardcoded 10 MB client limit ignores site settings and upload type
body: validateUploadedFile previously used Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so images and attachments each respected the admin-configured limit. Replacing it with a fixed 10 * 1024 makes the client accept files above a site's configured max_image_size_kb/max_attachment_size_kb (attachments are not downsized server-side at all, and images still exceeding the limit after five reductions are rejected by the server with a confusing error after upload), and rejects nothing for sites that configured a limit above 10 MB. The same hardcoding in the 413 handler at line 246 also reports a wrong max_size_kb in the error message for such sites.

title: Synchronous downsizing loop enables expensive processing of huge/decompression-bomb images
body: The change raises the accepted image size to 10 MB (line 55 for URL downloads and the JS limit) and then runs up to five full ImageMagick convert plus ImageOptim passes over the file inside the request/deferred upload job, gated only on compressed file size. A small compressed file can decode to enormous pixel dimensions, so each pass can consume very large CPU/memory, and an attacker can repeat this per upload. There is no pixel-dimension bound or timeout before invoking convert, creating an image-bomb denial-of-service vector that did not exist with the previous size gate.

title: Unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser record
body: TopicUser.find_by can return nil for users who receive a topic email without ever having visited/interacted with the topic (e.g. category watchers notified of a new topic, or mentioned/quoted users). The next line calls tu.notification_level on nil, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 instead of unsubscribing. Use a creating/upserting API such as TopicUser.change instead of assuming a row exists.

title: State-changing unsubscribe is an unauthenticated-by-token GET request
body: GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe immediately mutates the currently logged-in user's notification level, with no signed per-recipient token and no confirmation step. Email link scanners/prefetchers will trigger it automatically, anyone the email is forwarded to who is logged in will change their own settings instead of the recipient's, and an attacker can embed the (predictable, enumerable topic id) URL in an on an external page to silently downgrade/mute a logged-in victim's topic notifications (CSRF on a GET, with check_xhr skipped). Unsubscribe links should carry a signed key identifying the recipient, and/or require a non-GET confirmation.

title: Direct save! bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping
body: Assigning notification_level and calling tu.save! skips the logic in TopicUser.change that stamps notifications_changed_at, sets notifications_reason_id to user_changed, observes after-save callbacks, and publishes a MessageBus notification_level_change. Other open clients therefore keep showing the old notification state and the change is not recorded consistently with every other notification-level change in the app. Call TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...) instead.

title: First click does not actually stop notifications for watching/tracking users
body: If notification_level is above regular (watching or tracking), the action only downgrades it to regular, not muted. A regular user still receives mention/quote/reply notifications for the topic, so the email promise 'To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here' and the landing page text 'You will stop receiving notifications' are false after the click the email invites; the user must discover and operate the extra dropdown to finish unsubscribing.

title: unsubscribe_link translation now hard-requires unsubscribe_url for every sender
body: The shared unsubscribe_link string now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}, and Email::MessageBuilder passes template_args to I18n.t whenever add_unsubscribe_link is true (in both body and html_part). I18n raises MissingInterpolationArgument when a key is absent, so any current or plugin mailer that sets add_unsubscribe_link: true without also passing unsubscribe_url (previously a valid, working combination) will now crash while building email. Only include the per-topic sentence when unsubscribe_url is present, or supply a default in MessageBuilder.

title: No test covers the new unsubscribe behaviour end-to-end
body: The only spec change adds unsubscribe_url to an existing MessageBuilder fixture, but the examples still assert only the user-preferences URL and List-Unsubscribe header; nothing asserts the per-topic URL actually appears in text/HTML bodies, and there is no controller spec for TopicsController#unsubscribe at all (level transitions watching->?, regular->muted, missing TopicUser row, wrong slug redirect, logged-out user). The nil-row crash and downgrade semantics above would not be caught by the test suite.

title: Unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser row
body: TopicUser.find_by can return nil, for example when the user is receiving notifications through a watched category or has never visited/interacted with the topic in a way that created a topic_users row. Lines 107-113 then call tu.notification_level and tu.save! unconditionally, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 instead of unsubscribing. The action should create/update the row (e.g. via TopicUser.change, as set_notifications does) rather than assuming one exists.

title: Per-topic unsubscribe mutates notification state on a GET request
body: The new routes in config/routes.rb expose unsubscribe as GET and this action immediately changes and saves notification_level. Any logged-in browser request to the emailed URL therefore mutates state without confirmation or CSRF protection, so mail-scanner link prefetching, browser prefetch, or a cross-site /link to /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe can silently mute/downgrade a topic the user never intended to unsubscribe from. A state change like this should require POST (or an explicit confirmation step) with CSRF protection.

title: Unsubscribe bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping and live updates
body: Unlike TopicsController#set_notifications, which uses TopicUser.change, this action assigns tu.notification_level and calls tu.save! directly. That bypasses the notifications_changed_at/notifications_reason_id (user_changed) bookkeeping and the MessageBus /topic/:id notification_level_change publish (and after-save observers) performed by TopicUser.change, so other open clients and topic-tracking state keep showing the old watching/tracking level until a full reload, and the change is not recorded as a user-initiated notification change.

title: unsubscribe_link translation now hard-requires unsubscribe_url for every unsubscribe email
body: config/locales/server.en.yml changes the shared unsubscribe_link string to include %{unsubscribe_url}, and both the HTML path here and body (line 90) render it via I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args) whenever add_unsubscribe_link is true. template_args only contains unsubscribe_url when the caller passes it, and MessageBuilder treats it as optional (only UserNotifications#send_notification_email supplies it). Any other current/future/test caller that sets add_unsubscribe_link: true without a topic-specific URL will now raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and fail to send; the new spec change that had to add unsubscribe_url to an existing generic builder illustrates the coupling. The per-topic line should be conditional or the translation should be given a safe default.

title: No tests cover the new unsubscribe endpoint or that the topic URL reaches the email
body: The only spec change adds unsubscribe_url to the fixture builder but adds no expectation that the unsubscribe_url appears in the body/HTML, and there are no controller specs for TopicsController#unsubscribe at all. The watching/tracking -> regular and regular/muted -> muted transitions, the missing-TopicUser case, the slug-redirect case, and unauthenticated/inaccessible-topic behavior are all untested, so the nil-row crash and level-transition regressions above would pass CI undetected.

title: Unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser row
body: TopicUser.find_by can return nil for a logged-in user who has no topic_users row for this topic (for example, opening the emailed link in a different browser/session where no row was ever created, or after the row was removed). Line 107 immediately calls tu.notification_level, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 instead of unsubscribing. Use TopicUser.change (which creates the row when missing) or otherwise handle the nil case.

title: State-changing unsubscribe is performed by a plain GET request
body: The unsubscribe action is routed as GET (config/routes.rb lines 440-441) and mutates notification_level on every request. Email link scanners, antivirus prefetchers, browser prefetch, and simply reloading the page will therefore change the user's notification state without any intentional confirmation click. A mail security gateway that follows links can silently mute topics for users who never clicked anything.

title: Unsubscribe is not idempotent and does not actually mute on first click
body: Each visit steps the level down exactly one notch: watching/tracking becomes regular, and only a second visit (or a refresh of the landing page) becomes muted. So the first click on the email link leaves the user at regular — still notified of mentions/quotes/replies to their posts — while the landing page claims 'You will stop receiving notifications', and a refresh unexpectedly changes state again. The action should set a single deterministic target level (muted) in one idempotent operation.

title: Direct save! bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping
body: Mutating tu.notification_level and calling save! bypasses TopicUser.change, which is the canonical path used by set_notifications: it stamps notifications_changed_at, sets notifications_reason_id to user_changed, publishes a MessageBus /topic/:id notification_level_change message, and runs observe_after_save_callbacks_for. As written, already-open clients keep showing the old notification level and downstream observers/audit data are never updated.

title: unsubscribe_link translation now requires unsubscribe_url for every unsubscribe email
body: config/locales/server.en.yml changes the shared unsubscribe_link string to interpolate %{unsubscribe_url}, and MessageBuilder#body (line 90) and #html_part (line 67) render that string for any message built with add_unsubscribe_link: true. Only UserNotifications#send_notification_email was updated to pass unsubscribe_url; any other current or future caller that sets add_unsubscribe_link without unsubscribe_url will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and fail to deliver mail entirely, instead of simply omitting the per-topic sentence. The per-topic line should be conditional on unsubscribe_url being present.

title: Ember route/controller/template names for unsubscribe do not match
body: The route is registered as top-level 'topicUnsubscribe' (with controller controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6 and view views/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6, i.e. topic-unsubscribe), but the template is placed at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs, which is the name for a nested topic.unsubscribe route. Ember's resolver will look for a topic-unsubscribe template for this route and find none, so the unsubscribe landing page renders empty/without the notification-state controls even though the server-side mutation already happened.

title: No test covers the new unsubscribe behavior end-to-end
body: The only spec change adds unsubscribe_url to an existing fixture but adds no assertion that the per-topic URL appears in the body/HTML, and there are no controller specs for TopicsController#unsubscribe at all (missing TopicUser row, watching vs regular vs muted starting levels, slug redirect, JSON vs HTML). The nil-row crash and the one-notch-at-a-time behavior above would both have been caught by such specs.

title: Blocked-email lookup can be bypassed by changing letter case
body: should_block? performs an exact, case-sensitive database lookup for the supplied email, and neither BlockedEmail nor User normalizes email addresses to lowercase before saving or validation. An address stored as blocked@example.com therefore will not match a signup attempt using Blocked@Example.com or BLOCKED@example.com, allowing a trivial bypass of the block list (PostgreSQL string equality and the unique index are case-sensitive). Normalize addresses (downcase/strip) on both BlockedEmail save and lookup, or use a case-insensitive comparison.

title: should_block? uses a non-atomic read-modify-write inside a validator
body: should_block? increments match_count with `record.match_count += 1` followed by `save`. It is called from EmailValidator during ordinary model validation, so a single signup attempt that calls user.valid? and then user.save runs it at least twice and double-counts one attempt, and two concurrent attempts can read the same match_count and overwrite each other, losing counts. The write also makes validation itself have a database side effect that can fail or participate unexpectedly in surrounding transactions. Use an atomic SQL increment (e.g. update_counters/increment_counter with update for last_match_at) and ideally move the stat update out of the pure predicate/validator path so one rejected attempt is counted once.

title: rejectedEmails is a shared prototype array that is never cleared
body: rejectedEmails is defined as Em.A([]) directly on the controller class prototype, so the same mutable array is shared by controller instances, and createAccount only ever pushObject()s into it. Once an email is rejected it stays rejected for the life of the page session even if the server-side reason disappears (address unblocked, conflicting account removed, admin fixes the record), forcing a page reload before the user can retry that address. Initialize the array per controller instance and clear it when the modal/account flow is reset.

title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive and unnormalized
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? looks up the supplied address with an exact `where(email: email)` match, and neither BlockedEmail nor EmailValidator normalizes case or surrounding whitespace before lookup/storage. A blocked address such as bad@spam.example can therefore be resubmitted as Bad@Spam.Example and will not match, bypassing the block even though mail delivery treats the domain case-insensitively. Normalize (at minimum downcase/strip) both when creating BlockedEmail records and when checking them.

title: match_count increment is a non-atomic read-modify-write
body: should_block? does `record.match_count += 1` followed by `record.save`. Two concurrent registration attempts matching the same blocked email can both read the same match_count and both write count+1, losing an increment, and the full save also runs validations/callbacks on a hot validation path. Use an atomic increment (e.g. update_counters/increment_counter with last_match_at updated via update_all) instead.

title: Validation has a write side effect and double-counts a single signup attempt
body: EmailValidator calls BlockedEmail.should_block?, which increments match_count and writes last_match_at. Validations run repeatedly for one logical attempt: UsersController#create calls user.valid? and then user.save (which validates again), so one blocked signup is counted at least twice, and any other code that merely checks user.valid?
