(tests, console, unrelated flows) also falsely records a match. The statistics update should happen once per actual blocked attempt, not inside a reusable EachValidator.

title: rejectedEmails array is shared mutable prototype state
body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` declares one array on the controller prototype, so pushObject in createAccount mutates state shared by every instance of CreateAccountController rather than per-instance state. Rejected addresses can leak between controller instances (notably tests and any non-singleton use) and are never reset. Initialize the array per instance (e.g. in init) and clear it when the modal/account flow is reset.

title: Blocked-email matching is case-sensitive and never normalizes addresses
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? looks up `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` with the exact string supplied, and neither BlockedEmail nor EmailValidator downcases/strips the address (nor is there normalization when a BlockedEmail record is created). PostgreSQL string equality is case-sensitive, so a blocked address such as `bad@spam.com` is bypassed by registering as `Bad@Spam.com`, `BAD@spam.com`, etc., defeating the block list this PR introduces. Normalize (downcase/strip) on both BlockedEmail save and in should_block?/the validator lookup.

title: should_block? performs a non-atomic read-modify-write save during validation, double-counting and losing concurrent updates
body: should_block? is called from EmailValidator during User validation, yet it mutates and saves the BlockedEmail record (`match_count += 1; last_match_at = ...; record.save`). Validation is not a single occurrence: UsersController#create calls `user.valid?` and then `user.save`, which re-validates, so one signup attempt increments match_count at least twice, and any other `valid?` check also permanently increments it even if the user is never saved. The read-modify-write is also not atomic, so concurrent attempts reading the same match_count overwrite each other and lose counts. Use an atomic increment (e.g. update_counters/increment_counter with a separate last_match_at update) and avoid counting purely on validation, or at minimum make the update atomic.

title: rejectedEmails array is defined on the controller prototype and shared across instances
body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` declares a mutable array as a class/prototype property. Ember shares prototype object/array values across instances until reassigned, and createAccount mutates it in place with `pushObject(result.values.email)` rather than setting a new array. Rejected addresses can therefore leak/persist across controller instances and account-creation attempts instead of starting empty per instance. Initialize it per-instance (e.g. in init/create) rather than as a shared prototype array.

title: Untrusted feed/remote HTML is stored and rendered without sanitization
body: TopicEmbed.import passes feed or remotely fetched HTML directly to PostCreator with cook_method raw_html, and Post#cook returns that raw value as cooked. PollFeed supplies RSS/Atom content with no HTML sanitization, and the normal post rendering path trusts cooked HTML. A malicious or compromised feed item containing a script event handler or other active markup can therefore be stored and executed in the browsers of users viewing the resulting topic, not only in the embed view.

title: Referer is interpolated unsafely and incorrectly as postMessage targetOrigin
body: The layout inserts the full user-controlled request.referer into a JavaScript string as the targetOrigin for parent.postMessage. A referer containing a quote or script-breaking sequence can break out of the string and execute attacker JavaScript in the embed page. Even for legitimate referers, a full URL such as http://host/post-path is not a valid targetOrigin (which must be an origin), so browsers may reject the message and the parent iframe will never receive the resize height.

title: postMessage origin check uses reversed substring matching
body: The handler accepts a message when discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) is not -1, i.e. when the sender origin is merely a substring of the configured Discourse URL string. Origin validation must be an exact origin comparison; substring matching accepts origins that are prefixes/substrings of the forum URL and is fragile with trailing slashes, ports, and look-alike hosts. A frame able to send a message from an accepted non-forum origin could resize the embed iframe unexpectedly.

title: Embed view does not check whether the viewer can see the topic
body: When a TopicEmbed exists, the controller builds a TopicView for that topic id and the embed template outputs raw post.cooked for its best posts. There is no guardian/can-see check comparable to the normal topic controller. If an originally public imported topic is later moved into a restricted category, made invisible, or otherwise access-controlled, anonymous visitors framing the embed from the allowed host can still read its best posts through /embed/best.

title: PollFeed crashes on feed items without a content element
body: The job unconditionally calls i.content.scrub and passes the result to CGI.unescapeHTML. Many RSS/Atom items expose only title/link/description or use a namespaced content field, so SimpleRSS can return nil for content. A single such item raises NoMethodError/TypeError and aborts the whole hourly poll, preventing all remaining items in that feed from being imported.

title: TopicEmbed.import has a check-then-create race on embed_url
body: Import first queries TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first and only later creates the row inside a block, while the migration adds a unique index on embed_url. Two concurrent retrievals or feed polls for the same new URL can both see no embed, both create topics/posts, and then one fails with RecordNotUnique on TopicEmbed.create!, rolling back or orphaning work after external effects/jobs have been enqueued. Concurrent imports for the same URL should be serialized or the uniqueness violation handled as an update.

title: Controller spec expects synchronous TopicRetriever but controller enqueues a job
body: The success example stubs TopicRetriever.new and expects retrieve to be called, but EmbedController#best now calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) and never references TopicRetriever directly. This example therefore fails against the implementation it ships with, and it leaves the actual enqueue arguments and loading-template behaviour unverified. The adjacent TopicView example also stubs TopicView.new to return nil, after which best.html.erb dereferences @topic_view.posts, so the success-path rendering is not genuinely exercised.

title: Disqus import silently drops the category option and now requires fetching each source URL
body: The thor command removes the documented -c/--category option, so existing import invocations passing it will now fail as an unknown switch. It also replaces local creation of the opening post from the Disqus export with TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...), which performs an HTTP fetch and readability extraction for every thread; threads whose link is blank, offline, blocked, or no longer readable produce no opening post and their Disqus replies are skipped entirely, whereas previously they were imported from the export file alone.

title: Imported feed/remote HTML is stored and rendered without sanitization
body: TopicEmbed.import creates posts with cook_method raw_html, and Post#cook returns raw unchanged for such posts. Neither import nor absolutize_urls strips script tags, event-handler attributes, javascript: URLs, or other dangerous markup, and PollFeed passes RSS/Atom content directly into import. A malicious or compromised feed item can therefore store arbitrary HTML/JavaScript as post.cooked, which is rendered raw in Discourse and in embed views, giving stored XSS in forum visitors' browsers.

title: PollFeed crashes on feed items without a content element
body: poll_feed unconditionally calls i.content.scrub for every item. Ordinary RSS items commonly have description instead of content (and Atom/RSS variants expose different fields), so i.content can be nil and this raises NoMethodError. Because the exception is inside rss.items.each with sidekiq retry disabled, one such item aborts the whole hourly poll and prevents all remaining items from being imported.

title: Concurrent imports for the same URL race the unique embed_url index
body: import does a non-atomic check-then-create: it looks up TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first and only creates the embed after PostCreator runs. Two concurrent RetrieveTopic/PollFeed executions for the same new URL can both see no embed, both create topics/posts, and then the second TopicEmbed.create! raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique from the unique index instead of returning the already-created post, failing the job after doing duplicate creation work. The lookup/create needs an atomic rescue/retry or locking strategy.

title: Embed controller spec expects synchronous TopicRetriever but controller enqueues a job
body: The 'tells the topic retriever to work' example stubs TopicRetriever.new/retrieve, but EmbedController#best never instantiates TopicRetriever; it calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...). The mock expectation will not be satisfied and this spec fails, leaving the actual enqueue arguments (user_id and embed_url) untested. The spec should expect Jobs.enqueue with :retrieve_topic instead.

title: Disqus import drops the category option and now depends on fetching the live source site
body: The import task removed the --category option and replaced local topic creation (with the thread's title, permalink body, created_at, and chosen category) with TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...), which performs open(url).read on each Disqus thread link. Existing invocations using -c will no longer place topics in the requested category, threads whose original site is offline, moved, or blocks fetching will fail the import, and the thread's original creation date is no longer used for the imported topic.

title: absolutize_urls only fixes root-relative URLs, leaving other relative links broken
body: absolutize_urls only rewrites href/src values that start with '/'. Feed and readability content frequently uses document-relative URLs such as href="page2.html" or src="images/pic.jpg" and protocol-relative URLs such as src="//cdn.example.com/x.jpg"; those are left untouched, so after import they resolve against the Discourse host instead of the source site and produce wrong links or 404 images in the imported post.

title: import_remote fetches arbitrary URLs server-side with no timeout or size limit
body: TopicEmbed.import_remote does open(url).read with no timeout, redirect restriction, or response-size cap before Readability parsing. Via EmbedController/RetrieveTopic the URL is user-influenced (constrained only by host equality at the retriever layer), so requests can make the server fetch large or slow resources on the embeddable host, exhausting job workers/memory; the fetched result is then published as a topic, which can also disclose content the server can reach but an anonymous visitor could not. Add timeouts, size limits, and scheme/host validation inside import_remote itself.

title: Imported feed/remote HTML is stored and rendered without sanitization
body: TopicEmbed.import creates posts with cook_method raw_html (and the update path at line 36 does the same), and Post#cook returns raw verbatim for such posts, so cooked == raw. Neither PollFeed content nor the absolutize_urls step sanitizes the HTML: script tags, event-handler attributes (e.g. ), javascript: URLs etc. from an RSS/Atom feed item survive into the stored post and are output with `raw post.cooked` in the embed view and in normal topic rendering. Anyone who can influence a polled feed (or a page fetched via import_remote, where the PollFeed path bypasses Readability's tag whitelist entirely) gets stored XSS in the browsers of forum visitors and admins.

title: request.referer is interpolated unescaped into a script and misused as postMessage targetOrigin
body: The layout embeds '<%= request.referer %>' directly inside a single-quoted JavaScript string with no escaping (no j/escape_javascript or JSON encoding). A referer containing a single quote or </script> breaks out of the string and executes attacker script in the embed page on the Discourse origin. Independently, postMessage's targetOrigin must be an origin (scheme://host:port), but a full referer URL including path is passed, so browsers will not deliver the discourse-resize message and iframe resizing silently never works.

title: postMessage origin check is an inverted substring test
body: The handler accepts a message when `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is false, i.e. when e.origin appears anywhere as a substring of discourseUrl, instead of comparing e.origin for equality with the Discourse origin. Short or partial origins that happen to be substrings of the configured URL (for example a bare scheme or host fragment) are accepted, letting pages from unintended origins drive the discourse-resize handling. The check should parse discourseUrl to its origin and require strict equality.

title: import_remote fetches an attacker-influenced URL with open() and no SSRF safeguards
body: TopicRetriever only compares URI(embed_url).host to embeddable_host, then TopicEmbed.import_remote does open(url).read with no timeout, size limit, or redirect control. open-uri follows redirects, so a URL on the allowed host that redirects to an internal address (e.g. 169.254.169.254 or localhost admin endpoints) bypasses the host check and the server fetches internal content (SSRF); a slow or huge response also ties up the Sidekiq worker indefinitely. Fetching should re-validate the host after redirects, block private/link-local addresses, and set open/read timeouts and a size cap.

title: poll_feed crashes on feed items without content (and on Ruby < 2.1)
body: CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) raises NoMethodError whenever an RSS/Atom item has no content element (SimpleRSS returns nil for missing fields, common for summary-only feeds), and String#scrub does not exist on the Ruby 1.9/2.0 runtimes this codebase targets. Because there is no per-item rescue, one such item aborts the whole hourly poll mid-loop: remaining items are never imported and the job fails on every run. The title at line 36 can likewise be nil. Guard nil fields and isolate failures per item.

title: Every request for an unknown embed_url enqueues a new retrieve job
body: When no TopicEmbed exists, each GET /embed/best enqueues another Jobs::RetrieveTopic, and the loading page auto-reloads every 30 seconds, so a single embedded page (or a bot hitting the endpoint with rotating embed_url values, needing only a matching Referer) can flood Sidekiq with jobs and outbound fetches. The 60-second throttle lives inside TopicRetriever at job-execution time, so it does not stop unbounded enqueueing. Deduplicate/throttle at enqueue time (e.g. a redis setnx keyed by embed_url before Jobs.enqueue).

title: Check-then-create race on embed_url despite the unique index
body: import does TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first and only creates the embed inside the transaction when blank, but topic_embeds has a unique index on embed_url. Two concurrent executions (hourly PollFeed overlapping a RetrieveTopic job for the same URL, or two retrieve jobs) can both see no embed, both create a topic/post via PostCreator, and then one raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique on TopicEmbed.create!, rolling back and failing the job after side effects such as job enqueues from post creation. The create path needs to rescue RecordNotUnique and reload the winning embed, or serialize import per URL.

title: Embed controller spec expects synchronous TopicRetriever but controller enqueues a job
body: The 'tells the topic retriever to work' example stubs TopicRetriever.new and expects retrieve to be called, but EmbedController#best never references TopicRetriever; it calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...). As written the mocha expectation is never satisfied and this example fails, so the PR's own test suite is red and the actual enqueued-args behaviour (user_id, embed_url) is untested. Update the spec to expect Jobs.enqueue with :retrieve_topic and the right arguments.

title: order() mixin is off by one for legacy WebKit flexbox
body: The mixin emits `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: $val`, but the legacy box ordinal-group property is 1-based (its default is 1), whereas the standard `order` property is 0-based. The legacy value therefore needs to be `$val + 1`. As written, calls such as `@include order(2)` on .extra-info-wrapper and `@include order(3)` on .d-header .panel produce inconsistent ordering between legacy -webkit-box browsers and browsers using the standard `order` property, and an eventual `order(0)` or `order(1)` would collide with the default group. Fix the legacy declaration to `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: $val + 1` (and apply the same adjustment to -moz-box-ordinal-group).

title: Converting .small-action to flexbox silently disables the action button's float:right
body: Making .small-action a flex container (lines 264-265) makes its direct children flex items, and `float` has no effect on flex items. The nested `button` rule at lines 306-310 still relies on `float: right` to pin the small-action button to the right edge, but that declaration is now ignored and no flex replacement (e.g. `margin-left: auto` on the button) is provided. The button will instead sit immediately after .small-action-desc, changing the layout of small action posts. Add `margin-left: auto` (or equivalent flex positioning) to the button and remove the dead float.

title: order() mixin maps flex order incorrectly for 2009 flexbox syntax
body: The order() mixin sets -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group to the same value as the standard order property, but box-ordinal-group is 1-based (the default is 1) while flex order is 0-based (the default is 0). For equivalence, the legacy properties must be $val + 1. As written, order(2) on .extra-info-wrapper and order(3) on .d-header .panel behave as orders 1 and 2 in old WebKit/Firefox, and any future order(0) would be invalid/ignored there, so legacy browsers can order header elements differently from modern browsers.

title: align-items() emits an invalid -ms- property and does not translate values for legacy syntax
body: The mixin emits '-ms-align-items', which is not a recognized property; IE10's legacy property is -ms-flex-align. It also passes the standard value verbatim to -webkit-box-align and -ms-flex-align, whose legacy value grammars use start/end rather than flex-start/flex-end. Current call sites use center/baseline, which happen to coincide, but the new shared mixin silently produces invalid declarations for flex-start/flex-end and provides no IE10 alignment despite claiming legacy flexbox support.

title: Small-action button loses its right alignment inside the new flex container
body: .small-action is now display:flex via flexbox() at line 264, making its direct children flex items. The button rule inside it still relies on 'float: right' (line 309), but floats have no effect on flex items per the flexbox spec. With no margin-left:auto on the button or justify-content on the container, the button will now sit immediately after .small-action-desc instead of at the far right of the row, changing the layout of small-action posts (e.g. close/split notices).

title: Flex header children cannot shrink, so a long topic title can push the panel out of the header
body: Making .d-header .contents a flex container turns .title, .extra-info-wrapper, and .panel into flex items, which default to min-width:auto and therefore cannot shrink below their content size. .extra-info-wrapper (given order(2) in topic.scss) contains the current topic title/category badges and has no flex, min-width:0, or overflow constraint added in this change. A long title will consequently force .panel (order(3), margin-left:auto) to overflow/clip at the right edge of the header instead of the title area truncating as it could under the previous float layout.

title: order() mixin has off-by-one legacy box ordinal
body: The order() mixin sets -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group to the same value as the modern order property, but legacy box ordinal groups are 1-based while order is 0-based (the default/unset flex item is order:0 / ordinal-group:1). As written, order(1) collides with unordered items (both ordinal-group:1) and order(0) produces an invalid ordinal-group:0, so legacy WebKit/Firefox builds targeted by the -webkit-box/-moz-box display values in flexbox() will not order items the same way as modern browsers. The legacy properties should use $val + 1.

title: align-items() is incomplete/invalid for the legacy syntaxes flexbox() targets
body: align-items() emits -webkit-box-align but no -moz-box-align, so old Firefox using display:-moz-box from flexbox() gets no alignment at all, and it emits -ms-align-items which is not a real property (IE10 uses -ms-flex-align). It also passes modern values straight through to the legacy properties, which use start/end rather than flex-start/flex-end, so any future align-items(flex-start/flex-end) call will silently break in the legacy browsers these mixins exist to support. Add the -moz-box-align mapping (with value translation) and drop or fix the invalid -ms- property.

title: Small-action button loses right alignment when container becomes flex
body: Making .small-action a flex container (flexbox + align-items(center)) turns its direct-child button into a flex item, and floats are ignored on flex items, so the button's existing float:right (line 309) no longer has any effect. Nothing replaces it: .small-action-desc has no flex-grow and the button has no margin-left:auto, unlike .panel in header.scss which was given margin-left:auto for the same conversion. The dismiss/action button that previously sat at the far right of small-action rows (e.g. split/closed notices) will now sit immediately after the description text. Add margin-left:auto to the button or flex-grow:1 to .small-action-desc.

title: Flex header contents has no shrink protection for long topic titles
body: .contents is now display:flex, and flex items default to min-width:auto, meaning the .title/.extra-info-wrapper item cannot shrink below its content size. A long topic title shown in the docked header (via .extra-info-wrapper, ordered at topic.scss:30) can therefore force the .panel icons off the right edge or overflow the header instead of truncating, where the previous float layout constrained it. The title/extra-info flex item needs min-width:0 (with text-overflow handling on the title) to allow it to shrink within the flex row.

title: website_name leaks websites that are hidden as untrusted attributes
body: website is listed in untrusted_attributes (lines 105-111), so it is hidden from anonymous viewers for TL0 users to prevent spam/abuse, but the newly added website_name attribute is not added to that list. An anonymous viewer of a TL0 profile therefore receives website_name, which is derived directly from the hidden website and reveals its host and, in the same-domain case, its full path, defeating the restriction and rendering the website link text even though website itself was withheld.

title: include_website_name is missing the question mark and will never be called
body: Every other conditional inclusion hook in this serializer is named include_<attribute>? (e.g. include_email?, include_card_image_badge_id?, include_stats?). The new hook is defined as include_website_name without the '?', so ActiveModel::Serializer will not use it to gate inclusion. website_name is therefore serialized even when website is blank, producing a website_name: nil key instead of omitting the attribute as intended.

title: Root domain versus www subdomain is not treated as the same domain
body: The same-domain check handles sibling subdomains of equal depth (www.example.com vs forum.example.com, lines 144-146) and a parent website domain (example.com vs forums.example.com, line 149), but not the common root/www pair: with Discourse at example.com and a website of http://www.example.com/user, the lengths differ (2 vs 3) so it falls to the else branch, example.com does not end with .www.example.com, and only www.example.com is returned without /user. The inverse direction works, so the displayed website name depends asymmetrically on which host carries the www prefix.

title: website_name discards query string and fragment from the website URL
body: When the website is on the instance domain, website_name is built as host + URI(website).path only. Any query string or fragment in the user's website (e.g. http://example.com/profile?tab=posts) is silently dropped from the displayed text, so the link label no longer shows the complete URL even though the stated purpose of the change is to show the complete URL path for same-domain websites.

title: Conditional inclusion method is missing the required question mark
body: The method is defined as `include_website_name` instead of `include_website_name?`. Other inclusion predicates in this serializer use the `?` form, and ActiveModelSerializers only invokes `include_<attribute>?` to decide whether to emit an attribute. As a result this guard is never called, so `website_name` is emitted (as null) even when `website` is blank, instead of being omitted from the JSON.

title: website_name bypasses the untrusted-user restriction applied to website
body: `website_name` is added to the general attributes list but not to the `untrusted_attributes` list at lines 105-111, which hides `website`, `location`, bios, etc. from anonymous viewers of TL0 users via `scope.restrict_user_fields?`. Anonymous viewers therefore still receive the website host, and the full path when it matches the instance domain, even though the underlying `website` attribute is deliberately withheld from them.

title: Invalid website URIs can raise during serialization after the rescued parse
body: Only the first `URI(website.to_s).host` call on line 138 is protected by the modifier `rescue nil`. The subsequent `URI(website.to_s).path` calls on lines 143, 146 and 149 are unprotected, so a stored website that parses to a host but raises `URI::InvalidURIError` on re-parsing (for example containing spaces or invalid characters in the path) will raise out of `website_name` and break serialization of the whole user profile instead of falling back to the host name.

title: Same-domain detection is inconsistent for website subdomains of the instance domain
body: If the website is a subdomain of the instance domain (website `blog.example.com`, instance `example.com`), the first branch fails, the equal-label-count branch fails, and `discourse_host.ends_with?('.' + website_host)` is also false, so only the host is shown. The reverse parent case and the sibling case (`www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`, line 146) do show the full path, so equally same-registrable-domain URLs are treated inconsistently and the feature silently does not apply to subdomain websites.

title: New website_name branches and edge cases are untested
body: The new specs cover only unrelated domains, exact host match, and website-as-parent. They do not cover the sibling-subdomain branch added at serializer lines 144-146, a website subdomain of the instance host, a website without a scheme or with invalid URI characters, a blank website (verifying the attribute is omitted), or the TL0-anonymous restriction. Regressions in those branches, including serialization errors and information leakage, would pass this suite.

title: website_name bypasses the TL0/untrusted-user restriction applied to website
body: website is listed in untrusted_attributes (lines 105-111), whose generated include_website? hides it from anonymous viewers when scope.restrict_user_fields?(object) is true (e.g. a TL0 profile). The new website_name attribute is added to the plain attributes list but not to untrusted_attributes, so an anonymous viewer who may not see website still receives website_name, which contains the website host and, in the same-domain cases, the full path. This defeats the anti-spam/privacy restriction that hiding website is meant to enforce. website_name should be gated by the same restrict_user_fields? check ( taking care that a manually defined include_website_name? later in the class does not override the untrusted check).

title: include_website_name is missing the '?' so the inclusion guard is never called
body: The serializer framework and the rest of this file use the include_<attribute>? convention (e.g. include_email?, include_card_image_badge_id?, and the methods generated by staff_attributes/private_attributes/untrusted_attributes). The new method is named include_website_name without the question mark, so it will not be invoked when deciding whether to serialize website_name. As a result website_name is emitted even when website is blank (as a nil value) instead of being omitted, contrary to the guard's intent.

title: Same-registrable-domain check misses the common www-host vs apex-host case
body: The equal-length branch only handles sibling subdomains such as www.example.com vs forum.example.com. When the lengths differ it only checks whether the Discourse host ends with '.' + website_host. So website http://www.example.com/user on an instance at example.com falls into the else branch, example.com does not end with .www.example.com, and only 'www.example.com' is shown instead of the full path, while the reverse pairing (website example.com, instance www.example.com) does show the full path. The www/apex pairing is the most common same-domain configuration, so the feature silently does not work for it; the comparison should be based on the registrable domain rather than host-length and suffix checks.

title: New website_name branches have no coverage for sibling subdomains or restricted viewers
body: The added examples cover only unrelated hosts, an exact host match, and a parent-domain website, but not the equal-length sibling-subdomain branch in website_name (e.g. website www.example.com vs instance forum.example.com), the www-vs-apex pairing, or serialization of website_name for a TL0 user viewed anonymously. Those are precisely the branches with the non-trivial domain logic and the restriction interaction, so regressions or the bypass of the website restriction would not be caught by this spec.

title: Light/dark lightness values swapped for embedded-post author link
body: The original rule was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The change writes dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)), so the light-theme value is changed from 30% to 70% and the dark-theme value is 30% instead of the complementary 70%. Both themes therefore get the opposite shade from the intended conversion, changing light-theme appearance and giving a too-dark colour on dark themes. It should be dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)).

The change writes dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)), so the light-theme value is changed from 70% to 30% and the dark-theme value is 70% instead of the complementary 30%. title: Missed scale-color($primary) conversion in category badge-notification
body: .topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification still uses bare color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%) while every other $primary scale-color in this file was wrapped in dark-light-choose(..., scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)). Instead both branches use 50%, lightening the light-theme heading substantially and giving the dark theme a mid-grey with lower contrast than the intended 80% secondary colour.

title: Group-member name light-theme colour changed from 30% to 50%

title: totalPages is off by one when member count is an exact multiple of the page size
body: totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 unconditionally. For user_count=50 and limit=50 this yields 2 pages instead of 1, and for 100/50 it yields 3 instead of 2. showingLast therefore stays false on the real last page, and the next action advances offset to user_count, causing findMembers to render an empty extra page.

title: Members endpoint accepts unbounded and invalid limit/offset values
body: limit and offset are taken directly from request parameters with only to_i conversion. A caller can request limit=1000000 to force loading and serializing an entire large group in one request, or supply negative values that can produce database errors. The server should clamp limit to a sane maximum and clamp both values to be non-negative instead of trusting the JavaScript client to do so.

title: Public group members page now silently truncates groups to the first 50 members
body: The members endpoint now always applies limit/offset with a default limit of 50, whereas non-automatic groups previously returned all members. The public group-members route/template has no pagination controls or next/previous actions (those exist only in the admin controller), so for any group with more than 50 members the remaining members become unreachable in the public UI.

title: Group creation ignores the alias_level sent by the client
body: The JavaScript asJSON payload includes alias_level and the admin form exposes the alias-level selector before saving, but Admin::GroupsController#create only assigns name and visible. A newly created group therefore silently gets the database default alias_level (0/nobody) regardless of what the admin selected, while update does honor alias_level, making create and update inconsistent.

title: Remove-member control is shown for automatic groups
body: The template guards the remove link with {{#unless automatic}}, but this item view's context is the individual member (a User), not the group, so automatic is undefined/falsy and the remove control renders even for automatic groups. Clicking it calls the admin endpoint which rejects automatic-group changes with 422, and the model's removeMember/addMembers promises have no error handler, so the failure is silent to the admin.

title: findMembers no longer returns a promise when the group name is empty
body: findMembers previously returned Ember.RSVP.resolve([]) for an empty name, preserving its promise contract; it now bare-returns undefined. Any caller that chains .then() on the result (the pattern the old routes used) will throw a TypeError for unsaved/nameless groups. It should return a resolved promise to keep the contract uniform with the AJAX path.

title: Automatic-group remove_member spec uses the wrong HTTP verb
body: The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' example issues xhr :put, :remove_member, but the route added in config/routes.rb only maps DELETE to remove_member. Because controller specs bypass routing, the test passes even though it never exercises the real request path; it should use :delete like the successful-removal example below it, so a routing/verb regression would be caught.

title: add_members crashes if usernames is supplied as an array parameter
body: add_members calls usernames.split(',') assuming params[:usernames] is always a String. A request sending usernames as an array (e.g. usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b, a natural form-encoded API input) makes params[:usernames] an Array and raises NoMethodError, returning a 500 instead of adding members or a clean 4xx. The action should normalize Array and String inputs before splitting.

title: totalPages is off by one when member count is an exact multiple of the page size
body: totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. For user_count=50 and limit=50 this reports 2 pages instead of 1, and for 100/50 it reports 3 instead of 2. Because showingLast compares currentPage to this inflated totalPages, the Next control stays enabled on the real last page and navigates to an empty phantom page. The formula should be a ceiling division (with the zero-count case handled separately).

title: Group creation silently discards the alias_level chosen in the UI
body: The client's Group#asJSON sends alias_level (along with name and visible) on POST /admin/groups, and the admin form renders the alias-level selector for new groups, but Admin::GroupsController#create only assigns name and visible. A group created with e.g. alias_level 'everyone' is therefore saved with the column default (0/nobody) with no error, and the admin must edit the group again to set the intended mentioning permissions.

title: Members endpoint accepts unbounded and invalid limit/offset parameters
body: limit and offset are taken directly from params with only to_i coercion. A caller can pass limit=1000000 to force the server to load and serialize every member of a very large (e.g. automatic) group in a single request, defeating the new pagination and causing heavy memory/response load; negative values (limit=-1, offset=-5) are passed to ActiveRecord/Postgres and can raise a 500 error. Both values need clamping to a sane range (e.g. limit within 1..some maximum, offset >= 0).

title: remove_member automatic-group spec uses the wrong HTTP verb
body: The spec calls xhr :put, :remove_member, but config/routes.rb only routes DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members to remove_member (the companion success example on line 125 correctly uses :delete). Controller specs dispatch by action name rather than through the router, so this test passes even though the verb it documents does not exist; it would not catch a routing/verb mismatch and misdocuments the API contract. It should use :delete like the success case.

title: totalPages is off by one when member count is an exact multiple of the page size
body: totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, so a group with exactly 100 members and limit 50 reports 3 pages instead of 2. Because showingLast compares currentPage to this inflated totalPages, the Next control stays enabled on the real last page and the next action advances offset to 100, where findMembers returns an empty member list. The page count and pagination state are therefore wrong for every exact-multiple group size.

title: Members endpoint accepts unbounded, zero, and negative limit/offset values
body: limit and offset are taken directly from params with only to_i and no clamping. A caller who can view a group can pass limit=1000000 to force loading and serializing an arbitrarily large member set in one request, pass limit=0 (which also makes the client's totalPages divide by zero), or pass a negative offset/limit, which raises a database error and returns a 500. The endpoint should clamp limit to a sane range (e.g. 1..some max) and offset to >= 0.

title: Public group members page silently truncates membership to the first 50 users
body: findMembers now always requests the default limit of 50 members, and GroupsController#members now applies that limit to all groups (previously non-automatic groups returned their full member list and automatic groups defaulted to 200). The public template discourse/templates/group/members.hbs renders `members` with no pagination controls, unlike the new admin UI, so for any group with more than 50 members the remaining members are unreachable from the public members page.

title: Group creation silently discards the alias_level sent by the client
body: The client's Group.asJSON() sends alias_level and the group form shows the alias-level combo-box even for a not-yet-saved group, but Admin::GroupsController#create only assigns name and visible before saving. Any alias level chosen while creating a group is silently lost and the group is created with the default alias_level; only editing and re-saving afterwards sets it. Create should assign params[:alias_level] like update does.

title: findMembers clamps offset to user_count, landing on an empty page after the last member of a page is removed
body: The requested offset is clamped with Math.min(user_count, offset). Removing the sole member shown on the last page (e.g. offset 50 of 51 members) triggers removeMember -> findMembers while user_count is still the stale 51, so offset 50 is requested even though only 50 members remain, and the server returns an empty page with total 50. Combined with the inflated totalPages, the admin is left staring at an empty page instead of being moved back to the previous page; the clamp should be based on the last valid page start, not user_count.

title: remove_member automatic-group spec uses PUT although only DELETE is routed
body: The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' example calls xhr :put, :remove_member, but config/routes.rb only routes DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members to remove_member and the JavaScript client uses DELETE. Controller specs dispatch directly to the action and bypass routing, so this test passes even if the DELETE route or verb handling were broken, and it documents the wrong verb for the endpoint. It should use :delete like the neighbouring removal example.

title: Fallback locales are not loaded before cached translation lookup
body: `translate` only loads `config.locale`, not the fallback locales configured in `FallbackLocaleList`. Outside `ApplicationController#set_locale` (background jobs, mailers, console, or translations before that filter) a key missing from the current locale will be looked up in fallback locales whose YAML files have never been loaded via the lazy-loading patch, so it returns a missing-translation string. Worse, the no-argument path stores that result in the LRU cache (`@cache.getset(k) { translate_no_cache(key).freeze }`), so the missing string stays cached under `key+locale` even after the fallback locale is later loaded, until eviction/reload. Fallbacks must be ensured-loaded inside `translate` (or the backend lookup) before computing/caching the value, and the cache must not persist results computed before fallback locales were loaded.

title: Fallback loading is only wired into web requests
body: The PR is described as server-side localization fallbacks, but `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is only invoked from `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Server-side code that sets `I18n.locale` and translates without going through this controller (Sidekiq jobs, mailers, rake tasks, plugin background work) never loads the site-default/English fallback files, so with the lazy translation loader those fallbacks silently return missing translations there. The ensure-loaded step belongs in the shared translation path (e.g. `I18n.translate`/`load_locale` logic), not solely in a controller filter.

title: Fallback lookup queries SiteSetting on every translation
body: `FallbackLocaleList#[]` is called by the I18n fallbacks backend on every translation lookup, and it calls `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` each time. That puts a site-setting lookup (backed by Discourse's setting provider/cache machinery) on the hottest possible path — the very path `translate_accelerator.rb` exists to optimize — and it also raises `NoMethodError` if `default_locale` is ever nil/blank (e.g. early boot or a cleared setting). The fallback chain should be computed without a per-lookup setting query, or at minimum memoized/guarded with a safe default such as `:en`.

title: No tests cover the custom fallback chain or its lazy loading
body: This PR introduces a custom `FallbackLocaleList`, replaces the Rails `config.i18n.fallbacks` mechanism, removes the standalone pluralization initializer, and adds `I18n.ensure_loaded!`, but adds no specs. There is nothing verifying that a key missing in the user locale falls back to the site default and then English, that fallback locale files actually get loaded under the lazy-loading patch (including outside controllers), or that pluralized fallback strings still work. Regressions in this global I18n behavior would only surface as missing-translation strings in production; add specs for the fallback order, loading, and a pluralized fallback lookup before merging.

title: Fallback lookup depends on database-backed SiteSetting on every miss
body: FallbackLocaleList#[] calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym every time I18n::Backend::Fallbacks handles a missing translation. SiteSetting is database/cache backed, so translation lookups made during boot, migrations, seed/rake tasks, or when the settings table/cache is not yet available can raise or fail instead of falling back, and hot missing-translation paths repeatedly pay a settings lookup. It also raises NoMethodError if default_locale is ever nil. Capture/derive the site default without a per-lookup database-backed call, handle nil, and refresh it when the setting changes.

title: Fallback locales are only loaded for web requests
body: Fallback locale files are loaded only from ApplicationController#set_locale via I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!. The patched backend's translate path in lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb still loads only config.locale, while this codebase explicitly loads locale YAML on demand. Mailers, background jobs, rake tasks, console, and any translation performed before this before_filter therefore look up the fallback locale in a backend that has never loaded its YAML file, so they return 'translation missing' instead of the site-default/English string. Loading must happen in the translation/fallback path itself, not only in the web controller.

title: Loading a fallback locale does not invalidate the translation LRU cache
body: ensure_loaded!/load_locale add translations for a newly loaded locale but never clear @cache. I18n.translate caches no-argument results (including a frozen 'translation missing' result produced before the fallback locale was loaded) keyed only by key, current locale, and backend. After ensure_loaded! later loads the fallback file, subsequent lookups can keep returning the cached missing/frozen string for the life of the process (until an unrelated reload!). Clear the cache when a locale is actually loaded.

title: Fallback list mixes String and Symbol locale identities
body: The list is built as [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq: locale and I18n.locale are not normalized to Symbol here, so a String locale such as "de" and the Symbol :de are treated as distinct entries by uniq, by @loaded_locales.include? in the accelerator, and by backend translation hashes. That can cause duplicate fallback attempts, repeated loading of the same YAML file under a different key type, and missed loaded-checks. Normalize every entry to a Symbol (and drop nil before uniq) before returning the chain.

title: No tests cover fallback ordering, loading, or pluralized fallbacks
body: This change replaces the global I18n.fallbacks object, moves pluralization setup, removes config.i18n.fallbacks from production/profile, and adds on-demand fallback loading, but adds no specs. There is nothing verifying user-locale -> site-default -> :en ordering, fallback of pluralized/interpolated keys (which bypass the accelerator cache), behaviour when the site default changes, or non-request contexts. Add backend-level specs for those cases before relying on this in production.

title: Fallback translations can be permanently cached as missing
body: I18n.translate only loads config.locale before consulting the LRU cache, not the fallback locales configured in config/initializers/i18n.rb. If a no-argument translation is first looked up when its fallback locale (site default or :en) has not been loaded, translate_no_cache returns a 'translation missing' string and lines 71-76 freeze and cache it under the current locale. Loading the fallback locale later does not invalidate @cache, so the missing-translation string keeps being served until LRU eviction or reload, defeating the fallback feature.

title: Fallback locales are only loaded for web requests
body: ensure_loaded! is only called from ApplicationController#set_locale. Server-side translations also happen in background jobs, mailers, rake tasks, console and model code, where no controller before_filter runs. In those contexts I18n.translate loads only the current locale, so keys missing from that locale but present in the site-default or English files return 'translation missing' instead of falling back, making the feature inconsistent between requests and jobs/mailers.

title: FallbackLocaleList breaks the I18n.fallbacks Hash contract
body: FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but overrides [] to ignore anything stored in the hash and always synthesize a value. Code using the documented I18n fallbacks API, e.g. I18n.fallbacks[:de] = [:fr] or the Fallbacks#map helper provided by the i18n gem/Rails, will write entries that are never read back, and enumeration/keys/empty? report an empty hash even though [] returns entries. Per-locale fallback customization is therefore silently discarded.

title: Every fallback lookup queries SiteSetting and crashes if it is unset
body: The i18n Fallbacks backend calls I18n.fallbacks[locale] on each translation lookup, and this implementation calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym every time. That ties hot-path translation (including translations with arguments, which bypass the accelerator cache) to the DB-backed settings store, adds a settings lookup per translation, breaks translations performed before the database/settings are available (boot, migrations), and raises NoMethodError if default_locale is ever nil instead of degrading to :en.

title: No tests cover the new fallback ordering or loading behavior
body: The PR adds a custom FallbackLocaleList, a new I18n.ensure_loaded!, and a per-request loading hook, and removes the Rails config.i18n.fallbacks settings, but adds no specs. There is no coverage that a missing key in the user locale resolves to the site-default then English text, that duplicate locales (user == default == :en) are de-duplicated, or that fallback files are loaded in non-controller contexts, so the cache-poisoning and jobs/mailers gaps above can regress undetected.

title: Stale denial cache takes precedence over fresher permission cache
body: Check returns a cached denial before consulting permCache, and no code invalidates permDenialCache when fresh permissions are loaded (for example by List calling getIdentityPermissions and repopulating permCache). If a user is denied, is then granted access, and any path refreshes permCache with the new grant, Check for the same namespace/user/action/name/parent still returns Allowed:false until the denial TTL expires. This can make List show a resource while Check denies it and reintroduces up to 30s of stale denial for permission grants.

title: Denials caused by a stale folder tree are cached as authoritative denials
body: When the fresh-permission check fails, Check unconditionally writes permDenialCache. checkPermission/checkInheritedPermissions can fail solely because buildFolderTree returned the 30s-cached folder tree that does not yet contain a newly created or moved parent folder. Such a transient, infrastructure-staleness denial is then stored under the denial key and short-circuits later checks even after the folder tree and permissions have refreshed, extending incorrect denial and undermining the stated goal of letting creators access newly created folders/dashboards promptly in inherited-permission cases.

title: List still trusts stale cached permissions and never re-queries on outdated cache
body: Unlike Check, List returns listPermission directly from getCachedIdentityPermissions whenever a permCache entry exists, regardless of whether that entry predates a newly created dashboard/folder or a new grant. Because the client-side cache was removed in this PR, callers will reach this server List more often but can still omit newly accessible resources for the full shortCacheTTL (30s). The PR goal of fetching newly created dashboards/folders therefore remains broken for list/fetch flows that rely on List rather than a single Check.

title: Denial cache key is ambiguous underscore-concatenation of variable fields
body: userPermDenialCacheKey concatenates namespace, userUID, action, name and parent with '_' separators and no escaping or length encoding. Distinct tuples can produce the same key, e.g. name='a_b', parent='c' versus name='a', parent='b_c' (UIDs may contain underscores). A denial recorded for one dashboard/folder can therefore incorrectly deny a different resource for the denial TTL.

title: Every cached non-allow now triggers a full database permission load
body: If cached permissions do not allow the request, Check always calls getIdentityPermissions, which reloads identifiers/basic role/teams (subject to their caches) and queries the permission store and rewrites permCache. The denial cache only helps exact repeats of the same action/name/parent; probing or legitimately checking many distinct resources a user cannot access bypasses it and amplifies each check into a DB query. This removes the negative-case protection previously provided by permCache and creates an easy DB load path via enumeration of resource UIDs.

title: Denial cache blocks newly granted permissions and is never invalidated on allow
body: Check returns Allowed:false immediately when permDenialCache contains the key, before consulting fresh permissions or the DB, and the allowed paths (cached-allow at line 131 and DB-allow after line 146) never delete a denial entry. A denial recorded just before a dashboard/folder is created or a grant is added therefore keeps denying the creator/grantee for the full shortCacheTTL (30s), undermining the stated goal of letting creators access newly created resources. Concurrent requests make it worse: a request that started before a grant can finish afterwards, record a denial, and that denial then overrides another request's fresh allow result because nothing clears it.

title: Denied result from stale folder tree is promoted into a longer-lived denial
body: On a cached-permission miss Check re-queries only permissions from the DB; checkPermission still resolves folder inheritance through buildFolderTree, which serves the 30s-cached folder tree. For a dashboard/folder under a newly created folder, the inherited-permission check can therefore still fail after the DB re-query, and line 154 then stores that failure in permDenialCache for a fresh 30s. The stale-folder denial can thus persist up to roughly a folder-cache TTL plus a denial TTL, so the fix does not reliably let creators reach resources in newly created folders.

title: Denial cache key is ambiguously encoded and omits part of the request identity
body: userPermDenialCacheKey concatenates namespace, userUID, action, name and parent with '_' separators and does not include identity type, group or resource. Grafana UIDs can contain underscores, so distinct tuples such as name='a_b', parent='c' and name='a', parent='b_c' produce the same key, and resources that map to the same action string can also share an entry. A denial cached for one resource can consequently fast-path-deny a different resource for 30s. Use an unambiguous encoding (e.g. length-prefixed or hashed components) and include the resource/group and identity type.

title: Every cache-hit-but-not-allowed Check now performs a full DB permission fetch
body: getUserPermissions and getAnonymousPermissions no longer check permCache, so the getIdentityPermissions call at line 139 always runs the basic-role, team-membership and permission-store queries whenever the cached scope map does not allow the request, even when that scope map was just read fresh from permCache. The only mitigation is the per-(action,name,parent) denial entry, so checks against many distinct resource names (including legitimate UI probing or enumeration of non-existent UIDs) each trigger several DB queries; singleflight only deduplicates concurrent identical keys, not sequential requests.

title: Denial-cache key omits identity type and can poison renderer checks
body: The denial key is built only from namespace, raw subject UID, action, name, and parent folder, ignoring checkReq.IdentityType. Anonymous subjects and the render service both commonly use UID "0"; an anonymous denial for dashboards:read on a dashboard is therefore cached under the same key as a render-service check for that dashboard. The later render check returns Allowed:false from permDenialCache before getRendererPermissions can return its wildcard read permission, incorrectly breaking rendering for up to the 30-second denial TTL. Include the identity type (or do not denial-cache synthetic identities such as renderer) in the key.

title: Denial-cache key uses ambiguous underscore concatenation
body: userPermDenialCacheKey concatenates userUID, action, name, and parent with '_' without escaping or length-prefixing. Grafana UIDs can contain underscores, so distinct triples produce the same key: for example name="a_b", parent="c" and name="a", parent="b_c" both produce "..._dashboards:read_a_b_c". A denial for one resource can consequently fast-path-deny a different resource for 30 seconds. Use an unambiguous encoding such as separated, escaped, or hashed components.

title: Denials caused by the stale folder tree are cached, extending folder staleness
body: On a cached-permission miss Check re-queries permissions from the DB, but checkPermission/checkInheritedPermissions still resolve ancestors through buildFolderTree, which returns the short-TTL cached folder tree without refreshing it. For a dashboard whose access is inherited from an ancestor above its immediate parent, a newly created/re-parented folder can therefore still produce Allowed:false, and lines 153-155 then write that result into permDenialCache. The false denial is now pinned for another denial-cache TTL even after the folder tree refreshes, partially defeating the PR's goal for newly created folders. Do not denial-cache denials that depended on the folder tree, or refresh/bypass the folder cache on the DB fallback path.

title: Every denied check for a new resource name bypasses the permission cache to the DB
body: If cached permissions do not allow the requested name, Check always falls through to getIdentityPermissions, which after this PR always queries the permission store. The denial cache only helps repeats of the exact same (user, action, name, parent); a caller probing or enumerating many distinct dashboard/folder names—each a distinct denial key—forces a full permission DB query per name, with singleflight only deduplicating concurrent identical requests. This removes the previous cache protection against sequential negative-check DB load and needs a bound (for example revalidate at most once per cached permission-set generation/TTL window) rather than per-resource requery.

title: Delete action can never appear in the ruler-less list view
body: canDelete is now computed as ruler-ability OR Grafana prom-rule ability, but rendering is still gated by `canDelete && rulerRule`. In the new list view RuleActionsButtons.V2/GrafanaRuleListItem pass only promRule and no rulerRule, so Delete never renders there even for users with delete permission, despite the new prom-rule ability check. The Grafana-prom delete branch is dead code; the guard (or the handleDelete contract, which currently requires a RulerRuleDTO) must be adapted for prom-only rules.

title: Pause action can never appear in the ruler-less list view
body: canPause is now computed as ruler-ability OR Grafana prom-rule ability, but the menu item is only rendered when `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` is true and it renders MenuItemPauseRule with that rulerRule. In the new list view no rulerRule is supplied, so Pause is always hidden for Grafana rules even when the prom-rule ability allows it, making the newly added grafanaPauseAbility check ineffective for this action.

title: Silence drawer never opens for prom-only Grafana rules
body: AlertRuleMenu can now show Silence based on the Grafana prom-rule ability and calls handleSilence, which sets showSilenceDrawer=true. The drawer itself is only rendered when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true, but the new list view passes only promRule and leaves `rule` undefined. Clicking 'Silence notifications' in the list view therefore does nothing instead of opening SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer.

title: Grafana rule list items are rendered without a React key
body: The grafana branch returns <GrafanaRuleListItem> without the `key={key}` that GrafanaRuleLoader had and that the datasource branch still has. FilterView appends pages and batches of rules over time, so React will reconcile these items by index; component-local state in RuleActionsButtons/AlertRuleMenu (delete modal, silence drawer, clone redirect) can be reused for a different rule and list updates will be inefficient/incorrect. Restore key={key} on GrafanaRuleListItem.

title: Federated rule groups lose their immutable protection
body: useAllAlertRuleAbilities previously computed isFederated via isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) and treated federated rules as immutable (Update/Delete/Pause unsupported). It now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, where isFederated is hardcoded to false with a TODO. CombinedRule consumers will therefore offer edit/delete/pause for federated (cross-tenant Mimir) rule groups that must not be edited this way, leading to enabled actions that should be unsupported and will fail or act on the wrong tenant scope.

title: Delete menu item is never shown in the prom-only list view
body: AlertRuleMenu now computes canDelete from useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities so the list view (which no longer loads ruler rules) can authorize deletion, but the Delete item is still rendered only when `canDelete && rulerRule`. In GrafanaRuleListItem/RuleActionsButtons.V2 rulerRule is undefined, so Delete never appears for Grafana rules in the new list view even for users with delete permission, despite RuleActionsButtons' handleDelete only needing the identifier/groupIdentifier.

title: Pause menu item is never shown in the prom-only list view
body: canPause is computed as ruler-ability OR grafana-prom-ability, but the Pause item is rendered only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` and renders MenuItemPauseRule with that rulerRule. With rulerRule removed from the list view this condition is always false, so Pause/Unpause is unavailable there even when the new grafana prom ability grants it.

title: Silence action does nothing for prom-only rules
body: The Silence menu item can now be shown via useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities and clicking it sets showSilenceDrawer, but the drawer is rendered only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` where rule is the ruler rule. In the new list view rule is undefined, so SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer (which requires a rulerRule) never opens and silencing from the list silently fails.

title: GrafanaRuleListItem in filtered list is missing its React key
body: The 'grafana' case returns <GrafanaRuleListItem> without key={key}, unlike the datasource and unknown cases and unlike the previous GrafanaRuleLoader usage. In an incrementally appended/paginated list React cannot reliably reconcile items, causing warnings and potentially stale/duplicated row state (e.g. open menus/drawers) being reused for a different rule when results change.

title: Federated rule groups are no longer treated as immutable
body: The refactored useAllRulerRuleAbilities (now also backing the deprecated useAllAlertRuleAbilities for CombinedRule) hardcodes `const isFederated = false` with a TODO, whereas previously useAllAlertRuleAbilities used isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) and marked federated rules immutable. Federated (Mimir cross-tenant) rules will now report Update/Delete/Pause/Duplicate as supported (subject to permissions), offering edits that should be blocked for federated groups.

title: Pause action is never rendered in the ruler-free list view
body: The menu only renders MenuItemPauseRule when `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` is true. In the new list view (GrafanaRuleListItem/GrafanaGroupLoader/FilterView) no rulerRule is passed, so rulerRule is undefined and the condition is always false, even though the PR computes grafanaPauseAbility from promRule at lines 67-83. Users in the alert list can therefore never pause/unpause a Grafana rule from this menu.

title: Delete action is never rendered in the ruler-free list view
body: The Delete menu item is gated by `canDelete && rulerRule`. In the new list view rulerRule is undefined by design (ruler requests were removed), so despite grafanaDeleteAbility being computed from promRule at lines 67-87, Delete never appears. This is confirmed by GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx, which grants AlertingRuleDelete and expects only 4 menu items with no Delete. Users cannot delete Grafana rules from the list view menu.

title: Silence drawer cannot open in the ruler-free list view
body: handleSilence in AlertRuleMenu sets showSilenceDrawer=true, but the drawer is only rendered when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true and it requires `rulerRule={rule}`. In the list view RuleActionsButtons is now called with only promRule (see GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx line 47), so rule is undefined, the condition is false, and clicking 'Silence notifications' (which the new Grafana abilities can enable) does nothing.

title: Federated rule groups are no longer treated as immutable
body: useAllAlertRuleAbilities previously computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` and used it to block Update/Delete/Pause/Duplicate for federated (Mimir cross-tenant) groups. The refactor hard-codes `const isFederated = false` with only a TODO. CombinedRule consumers will now report federated rules as supported for edit/delete/pause (subject only to isEditable/isRemovable), allowing actions the backend/UI previously forbade for federated groups.

title: GrafanaRuleListItem in filtered list is rendered without a React key
body: The 'grafana' branch returns <GrafanaRuleListItem> without `key={key}`, unlike the 'datasource' branch on line 165 and the Unknown branch on line 168 which both pass key. FilterView builds a deduplicated artificial key via getRuleKey for exactly this purpose. Without it React warns and, more importantly, may reuse component instances (including RuleActionsButtons state such as silence drawer/delete modal/redirect state) for different rules when the infinite-scroll list appends or reorders, showing actions for the wrong rule.

title: Grafana recording rules lose Pause/Restore abilities in list view
body: useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities gates Pause and Restore (and ModifyExport/DeletePermanently) on `isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`, which is false for recording rules. The ruler-based implementation gated Pause on `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`, which includes Grafana recording rules, and GrafanaPromRuleDTO carries isPaused for both types. In the ruler-free list view a recording rule can therefore no longer be paused/resumed (and AlertRuleMenu's pause item would be disabled even if it were rendered).

title: Rule link loses the returnTo parameter
body: The deleted GrafanaRuleLoader.GrafanaRuleListItem built the view href as `createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view', { returnTo })` using createReturnTo(), so navigating back from the rule detail returned to the list with its filters. The new component builds the href with no query params, so the detail view loses the return-to-list context the old list item preserved.

title: Shard-split queries are interpolated twice
body: runShardSplitQuery now calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables for every target, and the resulting sub-requests are then passed to runSplitQuery, which at querySplitting.ts:299 calls applyTemplateVariables again for the same targets (the updated shard test even expects 5 calls for 1 initial query plus 4 shard sub-requests). Loki's applyTemplateVariables is not guaranteed idempotent: it applies request.filters/ad-hoc filters to the expression in addition to replacing variables, so a second pass can append the same ad-hoc label/filter twice, and any variable value containing a '$'-expression can be re-expanded. Shard splitting should interpolate only once, either here or in runSplitQuery, not both.

title: Queries that interpolate to an empty expression are no longer dropped
body: The empty check runs on the raw expression before interpolation: .filter((query) => query.expr).map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...)), with no re-filter afterwards (the same ordering is used in shardQuerySplitting.ts:49-52). A target whose expression is only a template variable, e.g. expr: '$expr', passes the raw check but can interpolate to '' when the variable has no value; it is then classified by isLogsQuery/querySupportsSplitting, grouped, and sent to Loki as an empty query instead of being skipped like a directly-empty query, producing backend parse errors for the whole panel request. Filter again after applyTemplateVariables (or interpolate first, then filter).

title: Shard-split queries are interpolated twice
body: runShardSplitQuery() now interpolates every target with datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters), but each resulting sub-request is then passed to runSplitQuery() (shardQuerySplitting.ts:163), which after this PR interpolates the same targets again with the same scopedVars/filters (querySplitting.ts:299). applyTemplateVariables is not an idempotent no-op: it performs template replacement and applies ad-hoc filters from request.filters, so a second pass can duplicate ad-hoc label/filter injection into an already-filtered LogQL expression (potentially producing duplicate matchers/filters or invalid LogQL) and can re-expand '$' sequences introduced by the first expansion (e.g. variable/label values containing '$'), corrupting the expression. The updated test even encodes this by expecting applyTemplateVariables to be called 5 times for one original target. Interpolate only once: either let shard splitting do the pre-shard interpolation and have runSplitQuery accept already-interpolated targets/skip re-interpolation, or remove the duplicate work while preserving the interpolation needed before fetchLabelValues/getSelectorForShardValues.

title: Empty-expression filtering now happens before interpolation in shard splitting
body: The previous code interpolated all targets first (interpolateVariablesInQueries) and only then filtered out empty/hidden queries, so a target whose expr is a variable that expands to an empty string was dropped. The new code filters on the raw pre-interpolation expr (lines 50-52) and never re-checks after applyTemplateVariables, so a variable-backed expr that interpolates to '' is retained and flows into requestSupportsSharding/getSelectorForShardValues/fetchLabelValues and query execution as an empty LogQL query, instead of being ignored like empty queries elsewhere. Move the emptiness check (or add a second one) after interpolation in runShardSplitQuery.

title: Interpolating before querySupportsSplitting defeats the $__range guard
body: Queries are now passed through datasource.applyTemplateVariables() on line 299 before partition() calls querySupportsSplitting() on line 300. querySupportsSplitting() (lines 282-289) relies on isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr) still seeing the literal $__range / $__range_s / $__range_ms variable, with the comment explaining such queries must not be split because the variable must be evaluated against the full, unsplit range. Once applyTemplateVariables expands that variable using the original request's range/scopedVars, the check can no longer detect it, so a query such as count_over_time({a="b"}[$__range]) is treated as splittable and is executed once per daily chunk, each chunk incorrectly using the full-range duration instead of being sent as a single unsplit request. This silently changes query semantics and results for $__range queries.

title: Shard-split queries are interpolated twice, including ad-hoc filter application
body: runShardSplitQuery() now interpolates every target with datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters) on line 52, but the resulting targets are later passed to runSplitQuery() (shardQuerySplitting.ts line 163), which after this PR interpolates every target again with the same scopedVars and filters (querySplitting.ts line 299). Template interpolation is not guaranteed idempotent: applyTemplateVariables also applies ad-hoc filters to the expression, so shard-split queries with ad-hoc filters get the same label matcher/filter appended twice, and variable values introduced by the first expansion that contain $-patterns can be expanded again on the second pass. The updated test even codifies this by expecting applyTemplateVariables to be called 5 times for one original target. Shard splitting should either skip the second interpolation or not pass filters/re-interpolate already-interpolated targets, otherwise shard queries can produce duplicated or corrupted LogQL compared with the non-shard path.

title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a detached logger that discards log records
body: FromContext returns NewTestLogger(), a fresh instance unrelated to the receiver. LoggerMiddleware now logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), so any test that injects a TestLogger into LoggerMiddleware and then asserts on that instance's InfoLogs (calls/message/context) will observe nothing: the log record is counted on the throwaway logger returned here. The fake should return the receiver (or a logger sharing the same Logs state) so tests can observe logs emitted through FromContext.

title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware has no test coverage for the moved contextual-logging behavior
body: This PR moves responsibility for enriching the request context with endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname from MetricsMiddleware into the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware, and LoggerMiddleware now depends on that enrichment via logger.FromContext(ctx) instead of adding those fields itself. No test was added for ContextualLoggerMiddleware (there is no contextual_logger_middleware_test.go), and the renamed metrics test only verifies Prometheus metrics. If the new middleware is mis-ordered in CreateMiddlewares, fails to enrich the context, or drops a field, the 'Plugin Request Completed' log line silently loses plugin/endpoint/datasource/user context with no failing test.

title: Plugin Request Completed log line loses traceID
body: Before this change logRequest explicitly added "traceID" from tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false) plus pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname to logParams. The new code replaces those params with m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), and the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware only stores endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID and uname via log.WithContextualAttributes -- it never stores a trace ID. Unless the infra logger independently injects trace IDs (grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext only adds stored contextual attributes), the 'Plugin Request Completed' line will no longer be correlatable by traceID, a regression for tracing/debugging plugin requests.

title: TestLogger.FromContext discards the receiving logger's recorded state
body: FromContext returns NewTestLogger() instead of the receiver or a logger sharing the receiver's Logs storage. LoggerMiddleware now logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), so any test that constructs a TestLogger, passes it to the middleware, and then asserts on that instance's InfoLogs.Calls/Message/Ctx will observe zero calls because the log was recorded on a throwaway instance. The fake should return f (or share its state) so FromContext logging remains observable in tests.

title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware and FromContext logging are untested
body: This PR moves contextual-attribute enrichment out of MetricsMiddleware into the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware and makes LoggerMiddleware depend on it (and on middleware ordering in CreateMiddlewares) to retain endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname fields. No test is added for ContextualLoggerMiddleware, and no existing test verifies that a logger obtained via FromContext after this middleware emits those attributes or that LoggerMiddleware still emits them end-to-end. A middleware-ordering or context-key regression would therefore silently drop those fields without failing tests; the renamed metrics test even still declares TestInstrumentationMiddleware at metrics_middleware_test.go:21.

title: TestLogger.FromContext discards the logger used to record log calls
body: FromContext returns NewTestLogger() instead of the receiver (or a logger sharing the receiver's recorded state). LoggerMiddleware now logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), so any test that constructs LoggerMiddleware with a TestLogger and asserts on that instance's InfoLogs will see zero calls because the message is recorded on a new, inaccessible TestLogger. The fake should return the receiver (f) so tests can observe logs emitted through FromContext.

title: "Plugin Request Completed" logs lose the explicit traceID field
body: logRequest previously added traceID (from tracing.TraceIDFromContext) to the log parameters, but that logic was removed and the replacement contextual attributes in ContextualLoggerMiddleware (endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname) do not include a trace ID. Unless infra/log.FromContext independently injects a trace ID, the completed-request log can no longer be correlated with traces by the traceID field that was present before this rename. The trace ID should be added to the contextual attributes or retained explicitly in logRequest.

title: Adding FromContext to Logger breaks existing implementations of the interface
body: Logger is an interface, and this PR adds a required FromContext method to it. Only grafanaInfraLogWrapper and TestLogger in this repo's changed files are updated; any other implementations (other packages, generated/manual fakes, or downstream/enterprise code implementing plugins/log.Logger) will fail to compile until they add the method. This is a breaking interface change that should be called out and all in-tree implementations/fakes verified, or the method should be exposed via a separate optional interface.

title: Renamed middleware test keeps old name and provides no coverage for moved contextual logging
body: The test function is still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware after the rename to MetricsMiddleware, and the PR adds a new ContextualLoggerMiddleware plus LoggerMiddleware's dependency on Logger.FromContext with no tests verifying that QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics contexts carry endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname or that LoggerMiddleware emits those fields. Rename the test and add coverage for the new middleware and its interaction with LoggerMiddleware so the moved contextual-logger behavior cannot silently regress.

title: Device-limit rejection is cached, allowing the rejected device on its next request
body: tagDeviceUI inserts the device ID into localCache before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice and does not remove the entry when that call returns ErrDeviceLimitReached.
