body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no client-specific resource exists, the code loads the all-Clients resource via AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource(...) and immediately calls authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) without a null check. getResourceTypeResource returns null when the Clients resource is absent (e.g. the resource server was initialized before Clients support or the resource was not created), so the permission check throws NullPointerException instead of returning false. The String-scope overload in the same class does guard the analogous lookup, showing the missing check is an oversight; the result can be a 500 error on ordinary client view/manage/configure checks.

title: Existing admin-permissions clients never receive the new Clients scopes/resource
body: init() returns immediately whenever realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is non-null. Realms that already enabled FGAPv2 therefore keep a resource server created with only the Users scopes and the Users all-resource resource; the new Clients resource type, its 'Clients' all-resource resource, and the new scopes 'configure', 'map-roles-client-scope' and 'map-roles-composite' are never added. Creating Clients permissions in such realms will fail (missing scopes/resources) and client permission evaluation can hit missing-resource paths, so an upgrade/migration path for existing admin-permissions clients is required.

title: getClientsWithPermission returns the all-Clients placeholder instead of client ids
body: getClientsWithPermission iterates every resource of type Clients and adds resource.getName() for granted resources. That iteration includes the all-resource resource whose name is literally 'Clients', while client-specific resources are named by client id. If the caller only has an all-Clients grant, the method returns {"Clients"} and none of the real client ids, so any consumer filtering clients by this id set will not match the clients the admin is permitted to access. Conversely it can expose a bogus identifier that is not a client. The all-resource case must be expanded to actual client ids (or excluded with callers handling the all-clients grant separately).

title: Resource display names are not resolved for the Clients resource type
body: getResourceName only special-cases the Users resource type: it returns 'All users' for the all-resource resource and resolves a user id to a username for user-specific resources. The new Clients branch is missing, so Clients permissions fall through to resource.getDisplayName(). For the all-Clients resource that yields no meaningful 'All clients' label, and for client-specific resources whose name is the client UUID it yields the UUID/display name rather than the client's clientId. Authorization representations for Clients permissions will therefore show confusing or empty resource names in clients that consume getResourceName.

title: New and changed CLI exit codes are not asserted by tests
body: This PR changes RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3, introduces FEATURE_DISABLED=4, and documents that automation should rely only on the check command's exit code, but no test asserts those codes. testFeatureNotEnabled (line 47-50) checks only the error text for the metadata subcommand and does not assert exit code 4, there is no equivalent disabled-feature test for the check subcommand, and testWrongVersions (lines 86-107) does not assert exit code 3 for an incompatible result. A regression or a swapped/misreported exit code (consequential because 4 previously meant recreate) would therefore pass the suite while breaking scripts and consumers that follow the documented exit-code contract.

title: Default-strategy tests do not enable rolling-updates feature
body: createInitialDeployment returns immediately when updateStrategy is null, before setting FeatureSpec.enabledFeatures to rolling-updates at lines 112-115. Both parameterized tests use the null case: testCacheMaxCount with null expects a rolling upgrade and testImageChange with null expects the operator to determine a recreate upgrade. With the new gating, the update-compatibility commands exit with FEATURE_DISABLED when rolling-updates is not enabled, so the null-strategy cases no longer exercise the intended default upgrade-decision path and will either fail or pass for the wrong (feature-disabled) reason. The feature must be enabled for every deployment created here, regardless of whether an explicit update strategy is set.

title: Feature-disabled exit code and check subcommand are untested
body: The new testFeatureNotEnabled only launches the metadata subcommand and only asserts the stderr message; it does not assert the new exit code 4 (CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED) and does not cover UpdateCompatibilityCheck, which has its own duplicated feature-gate in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run(). A regression that prints the message but exits 0, or that breaks the gate in the check subcommand only (the subcommand whose exit code is documented for scripting in update-compatibility.adoc), would not be caught. Add a check-subcommand case and assert exit code 4 for both subcommands.

title: Feature-disabled exit-code contract is only partially tested
body: The new testFeatureNotEnabled test covers only the metadata subcommand and asserts only the stderr text. It does not cover the check subcommand, which has its own new Profile.isFeatureEnabled branch in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run(), and it does not assert exit code 4 (CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED) for either subcommand. The exit code is the documented scripting contract for this feature, so a regression that prints the message but exits 0, 1, or the old recreate code would pass this test while breaking automation that distinguishes feature-disabled (4) from recreate (3).

title: Default update-strategy deployments do not enable rolling-updates in the CR
body: createInitialDeployment returns immediately when updateStrategy is null, before setting FeatureSpec.enabledFeatures to rolling-updates, so both parameterized tests run their default-strategy cases without the feature enabled in the Keycloak CR. The operator guide added in this PR states the rolling-updates feature must be enabled for operator update handling and shows it alongside the update strategy, so the default path's CR-level feature propagation is left untested; these cases can only pass because the shared custom test image bakes --features=rolling-updates in at build time (operator/scripts/Dockerfile-custom-image), masking a regression for images that rely on the CR to enable the feature.

title: VIEW-only group permission grants global group manage
body: canManage() with no group argument returns hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), so an admin granted only the view scope on all Groups passes requireManage(). That check is used, for example, by GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup to authorize creating top-level groups, so a read-only FGAP admin can create groups. Unlike canManage(GroupModel), which correctly requires only MANAGE, the global check should not treat VIEW as sufficient.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns and looks up authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
body: The method passes groupResource.getId() to hasPermission(), but hasPermission() treats that argument as a group ID and calls resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId). For resources created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource, the resource name is the group ID while getId() is the authorization store's generated resource ID, so the lookup misses and falls back to the all-groups resource. It also adds groupResource.getId() to the returned set, whereas callers such as UsersResource.searchForUser and getUsersCount expect real group IDs for the UserModel.GROUPS filter/count. Per-group view-members/manage-members grants can therefore be lost or produce counts/filters that match no group; the resource name (the group ID) should be used in both places.

title: hasPermission can NPE when the all-groups resource does not exist
body: When no specific group resource is found, hasPermission() assigns resource from getResourceTypeResource() and immediately calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) without a null check, and later dereferences resource.getScopes(). getResourceTypeResource() returns null when the Groups type resource has not been created (for example before schema initialization completes or after it is removed), so permission checks such as canView()/canManage() can fail with a NullPointerException/500 instead of returning false/Forbidden.

title: getResourceName does not resolve Groups resources
body: getResourceName() special-cases only the Users resource type: it returns 'All users' and resolves individual user IDs to usernames, but has no corresponding branch for GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE. Group policies therefore fall back to resource.getDisplayName(), which for schema-created group resources is the group ID rather than the group name (and never yields an 'All groups' label), so the admin authorization UI/API shows opaque IDs for the newly added Groups resource type.

title: VIEW permission on all groups grants global group manage permission
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), so an admin granted only the 'view' scope on the all-groups resource passes canManage(). This is used by requireManage(), e.g. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() for creating top-level groups, so a view-only FGAP admin can perform manage operations that should require the 'manage' scope. canManage() should check only MANAGE, unlike canView() which may accept VIEW or MANAGE.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
body: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), groupResource.getId() is the authorization-store resource UUID, while group resources are named by the Keycloak group ID (AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup returns group.getId() and hasPermission() looks up resources by name via findByName). Passing getId() to hasPermission() therefore never finds the per-group resource and falls back to the all-groups resource, ignoring per-group view-members/manage-members grants. Adding groupResource.getId() to the result is also wrong: callers such as UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource put the returned values in UserModel.GROUPS to filter users by their actual group IDs, so even a successful check would filter by non-existent group IDs and return no members. Both places should use groupResource.getName().

title: Missing all-groups resource causes NullPointerException instead of denying permission
body: hasPermission() falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource() when a specific group resource is not found, but does not check whether that fallback resource is null before calling policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) and later resource.getScopes(). Realms whose admin-permissions client was created before the Groups resource type was introduced have no 'Groups' all-groups resource (AdminPermissionsSchema.init() only creates it when the client is first created), so any group permission check for such a realm, or any realm where that resource is absent, can throw an NPE/500 instead of returning false.

title: VIEW permission incorrectly grants global group manage permission
body: canManage() evaluates hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE) against the all-groups resource, so an administrator granted only the view scope for all groups passes requireManage() checks such as creating a top-level group in GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup. Group creation/modification must require MANAGE only; VIEW should grant read access. This is a privilege-escalation bug not covered by the tests, which only verify creation with MANAGE.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns and evaluates authorization-resource IDs instead of group IDs
body: For V2 group resources the group ID is stored as the resource name (AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup returns group.getId() and getOrCreateResource creates the resource with that as its name), while Resource.getId() is the authorization store's own resource UUID. This code passes groupResource.getId() to hasPermission(String groupId, ...), which looks up resources by name, so specific-group resources are never found and evaluation falls back to the all-groups resource. It also adds groupResource.getId() to the returned set, but callers in UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource and getUsersCount expect actual group IDs for filtering users by group membership. The result is wrong user visibility/counts for admins with view-members/manage-members on specific groups.

title: hasPermission can throw NullPointerException when the all-groups resource does not exist
body: When no specific group resource is found, the code loads the all-groups resource via getResourceTypeResource and immediately calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) and later constructs a ResourcePermission with it, without a null check. If the Groups type resource is absent (for example the resource server was initialized before it was created, or admin permissions resources were not (re)initialized), every canView/canManage/canViewMembers check for a group without its own resource throws an NPE instead of denying access.

title: Existing FGAP V2 realms never get the new Groups scopes/resource
body: init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is non-null, and this is the only place shown that creates the schema's scopes and all-resource-type resources. Realms that already enabled admin permissions before this change therefore keep a resource server with only the old Users/Clients scopes and resources: the Groups all-resource and the manage-membership/manage-members/view-members scopes are never added. Creating Groups scope permissions in such realms then fails scope resolution/validation, and group evaluations hit the missing-resource path, so the feature only works for newly initialized realms unless a migration/backfill is added.

title: Missing English bundle aborts verification with an unhandled RuntimeException
body: verifySafeHtml() derives the English file by regex-replacing the locale and community path in the absolute path, then throws a raw RuntimeException if that file cannot be opened. verify() only translates IOException from reading the target file into MojoExecutionException, so a properties file with no matching _en counterpart (or a path the regex does not rewrite as expected) crashes the whole verifier run with a stack trace instead of producing a per-file verification message or checking the remaining files.

title: Anchor pattern matches non-anchor tags and misses uppercase anchors
body: ANCHOR_PATTERN is '</?a[^>]*>' with no word boundary and no case-insensitivity. It therefore treats tags such as <abbr>, <article> or <address> as anchors and can strip them from the checked value when they happen to match the English string, bypassing the HTML policy for elements that were never intended to be whitelisted. Conversely a legitimate <A HREF=...> anchor identical to the English source is not recognised, is left in the value and is then reported as illegal HTML. The pattern needs a boundary after 'a' (and case-insensitive matching) to represent anchor tags only.

title: Anchor-mismatch message identifies neither the key nor the file
body: When a translated anchor does not match the English source, santizeAnchors() adds only "Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string". Unlike the Illegal HTML message it omits the message key and the file being verified, so when the plugin checks hundreds of properties files in CI the maintainer cannot locate the offending entry from the build output without re-running or searching manually.

title: Lithuanian account totpStep1 was replaced with Italian text
body: The Lithuanian account message totpStep1 now reads 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' which is Italian, not Lithuanian. The previous Lithuanian sentence was replaced while removing its anchor tags, apparently by copying the corresponding Italian string, so Lithuanian users will see an Italian instruction on the TOTP setup page.

title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 was replaced with Italian text
body: The Lithuanian login message loginTotpStep1 now reads 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' which is Italian, not Lithuanian. As with the account bundle, removing the FreeOTP/Google Play anchors replaced the Lithuanian translation with the Italian sentence, so the login TOTP instructions will be shown in the wrong language.

title: No positive test that legitimate HTML and matching anchors pass
body:
All new tests only assert that a violation is reported (illegal tag, HTML where English has none, changed anchor). There is no fixture asserting an empty result for a translation that reuses exactly the English string's allowed HTML (

//
) and identical anchor, nor for the special-case normalisations (choice formats, templateHelp). A regression that flags every HTML-containing translation would still pass the whole suite while breaking the verifier for the real message bundles.

title: Anchor validation requires anchors in English order and rejects legitimate reordering
body: santizeAnchors() advances the translation matcher and the English matcher in lock-step and requires matcher.group() to equal the next English anchor. A translation that legitimately reorders two different links relative to English (common when word order differs between languages) therefore reports 'Didn't find anchor tag' on the first anchor and breaks, even though both anchors are present unchanged. The check should compare the anchors as a multiset/set rather than requiring identical order.

title: Anchor pattern also matches unrelated tags starting with 'a'
body: ANCHOR_PATTERN is '</?a[^>]*>' with no word boundary or tag-name terminator, so it matches <abbr>, <address>, <article>, <aside> and any other a-prefixed tag, not just <a>. Such tags in a translation are either falsely reported as missing anchors, or, if the same a-prefixed tag exists in English, are stripped by santizeAnchors() and thereby whitelisted past the OWASP check regardless of their attributes. The pattern should be something like '</?a(\\s[^>]*)?>'.

title: Missing English bundle aborts verification with RuntimeException instead of reporting a problem
body: If the derived *_en.properties file does not exist (a new locale/theme, or a properties file whose path does not match the resources-community/resources and locale-suffix rewriting), verifySafeHtml() throws an unchecked RuntimeException. verify() only documents/declares MojoExecutionException and its callers expect a List<String> of problems, so one missing English file aborts the whole verification run and hides all other findings for all files instead of producing a per-file message.

title: Lithuanian totpStep1 replaced with Italian text
body: The Lithuanian account message totpStep1 was changed from the Lithuanian FreeOTP/Google Authenticator text to 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', which is Italian. Lithuanian users will see instructions in the wrong language; the anchor removal should have kept a Lithuanian sentence such as the generic 'install one of the following applications on your mobile' wording in Lithuanian.

title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 replaced with Italian text
body: The Lithuanian login message loginTotpStep1 was changed from the Lithuanian FreeOTP/Google Authenticator text to 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', which is Italian. Lithuanian users will see instructions in the wrong language; the anchor removal should have kept a Lithuanian sentence such as the generic 'install one of the following applications on your mobile' wording in Lithuanian.

title: Simplified Chinese file now uses Traditional Chinese characters for totpStep1
body: messages_zh_CN.properties is the Simplified Chinese bundle, but the replacement totpStep1 uses Traditional forms (手機/安裝/應用程式 instead of 手机/安装/应用程序). Simplified Chinese users will see text in the wrong script; the replacement should use Simplified Chinese characters.

title: No test that legitimate HTML passes verification cleanly
body:
All new tests assert only that a problem message is present (hasItem 'Illegal HTML' / 'Didn't find anchor tag'); there is no fixture asserting an empty result for a valid translation, e.g. one that copies the English

//
markup or reuses the identical anchor from English. A regression that flags every value (wrong policy, wrong
normalization, wrong English-file derivation) would still pass the whole suite.

title: Java MessageFormat syntax used in an i18next resource bundle
body: This account-ui bundle uses i18next interpolation everywhere else (e.g. {{0}}, {{name}}, <0>{{username}}</0>). Changing error-invalid-multivalued-size to Java MessageFormat syntax '{0} ... {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}' means the React/i18next renderer will not substitute the arguments or evaluate the choice; users will see the raw placeholders/choice expression instead of 'Attribute X must have at least ... and at most ... values'. The Java-style choice form belongs only in the server-side themes bundles, not this JS bundle.

title: Java MessageFormat syntax used in an i18next resource bundle
body: This admin-ui bundle is rendered by the JavaScript UI with i18next interpolation ({{0}} style). Changing error-invalid-multivalued-size to '{0} ... {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}' introduces Java MessageFormat/ChoiceFormat syntax that i18next cannot evaluate, so the validation message will be shown literally with unsubstituted placeholders instead of the attribute name and limits. Keep the {{0}}/{{1}}/{{2}} form for the JS bundle and use the choice form only in server-side message bundles.

title: Lithuanian totpStep1 replaced with Italian text
body: totpStep1 in the Lithuanian (messages_lt) account bundle was changed to 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', which is Italian, not Lithuanian. Lithuanian users will see instructions in the wrong language. Replace it with a Lithuanian translation of 'Install one of the following applications on your mobile:'.

title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 replaced with Italian text
body: loginTotpStep1 in the Lithuanian (messages_lt) login bundle was changed to 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', which is Italian, not Lithuanian. This is the same wrong-language copy-paste as in the account bundle and will show Italian instructions to Lithuanian users during TOTP setup. Use a Lithuanian translation instead.

title: Missing English bundle aborts verification with an unchecked exception
body: verifySafeHtml() derives the English file by regex-rewriting the input path and throws a raw RuntimeException when that file cannot be opened. This bypasses verify()'s contract of returning collected messages / throwing MojoExecutionException: a single locale file whose path does not rewrite to an existing _en.properties (e.g. a new locale, a locale containing characters outside [a-zA-Z-_], or a file verified standalone) crashes the whole plugin run instead of reporting a verification problem for that file. Catch this case and report it through the messages list or a MojoExecutionException naming both files.

title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks all custom grant-type factories
body: getShortcut() was added as an abstract interface method with no default implementation. Every existing custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory outside this PR (and any test/deployment extension implementing the old interface) will fail to compile, and already-compiled implementations will throw AbstractMethodError when the encoder factory calls getShortcut() during postInit or token issuance. A default method (e.g. returning the unknown shortcut) is needed to preserve SPI compatibility.

title: Public copy constructor of OAuth2GrantType.Context was removed
body: The public Context(Context) copy constructor was deleted and replaced by initialization of grantType from formParams. Code that copied a grant context (custom grants, token-exchange flows, tests) no longer compiles. In addition, grantType is now captured once from formParams at construction, so a later setFormParams() call silently leaves getGrantType() returning the stale original value, which is then encoded into the access-token ID.

title: Token issuance now fails for any unregistered grant type
body: encodeTokenId() throws IllegalStateException whenever getShortcutByGrantType() returns null, and TokenManager.initToken() now calls this for every access token. Previously token creation never depended on the grant type being known to this registry. Any flow that sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE to a value without a registered OAuth2GrantTypeFactory with that exact ID (custom grants, non-grant issuance paths that propagate a grant string, or a grant whose factory is feature-disabled and absent from the session factory) will now fail token creation entirely instead of issuing a token with an unknown-context ID.

title: Shortcut length/uniqueness contract is not validated but decoder assumes exactly 2 chars
body: postInit() registers whatever getShortcut() returns without checking it is non-null and exactly 2 characters, and the interface javadoc even suggests 'usually like 3-letters'. encodeTokenId() simply concatenates the shortcut, so a 1- or 3-character (or null) shortcut produces a token ID whose prefix is not 6 characters (or an NPE from ConcurrentHashMap.put for null), and getTokenContextFromTokenId() will then reject every such token with IllegalArgumentException. The factory only checks duplicate map sizes, not the format the wire encoding depends on.

title: Constructor validates grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId
body: Line 72 checks grantType and line 73 checks grantType again with the message 'Null rawTokenId not allowed'; rawTokenId itself is never null-checked. A null rawTokenId therefore passes construction and later produces a token ID ending in ':null' from encodeTokenId(), or corrupt data returned from getRawTokenId(), instead of failing fast at the point of the programming error.

title: Decoder throws on any colon-containing token ID that is not in the new format
body: getTokenContextFromTokenId() returns UNKNOWN only when the ID contains no ':' at all; any other ID containing a colon but with a prefix that is not exactly 6 known characters throws IllegalArgumentException. Token IDs are attacker/client-influenced input (jti of presented tokens) and older or externally/custom-generated IDs may legitimately contain colons. Future consumers using this decoder for introspection/userinfo/session lookup (the stated purpose of the PR) will turn such tokens into 500 errors instead of treating the context as unknown like pre-upgrade UUID tokens.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic and wrong substring offset
body: The encoded prefix is session(0-1)+tokenType(2-3)+grant(4-5), but the matcher checks substring(3,5), and returns false when that substring equals the expected grant shortcut instead of when it differs. As written it rejects (partly) matching IDs for the wrong reason and accepts IDs whose grant shortcut is wrong, so expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken do not actually verify the grant-type encoding this PR introduces. It should check substring(4,6) and return false on inequality.

title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
body: getShortcut() was added as an abstract interface method with no default implementation. Every custom/out-of-tree OAuth2GrantTypeFactory compiled against the previous interface will fail to compile/link until it implements this method, even though such a grant could safely fall back to the encoder's unknown shortcut. Add a default method (e.g. returning the unknown shortcut) to preserve compatibility.

title: OAuth2GrantType.Context copy constructor was removed
body: The public Context(Context) copy constructor present in the base version was deleted while changing the main constructor. Custom grant types or other callers that copied a Context (to wrap/extend a grant request) will no longer compile and will fail at linkage if already compiled. This is an unnecessary public API break unrelated to capturing grantType; the copy constructor should be retained and also copy the new grantType field.

title: Shortcut documentation says 3 letters but encoding requires exactly 2
body: The javadoc describes the shortcut as 'usually like 3-letters', but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider builds a fixed 6-character prefix (2 chars session type + 2 chars token type + 2 chars grant type) and getTokenContextFromTokenId rejects any prefix whose length is not 6. A factory author following the documentation and returning a 3-letter shortcut will produce token IDs that cannot be decoded. The contract must state and enforce exactly 2 characters.

title: Grant shortcuts are never validated for null or length
body: postInit (and the lazy refresh in getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut) puts whatever getShortcut() returns into ConcurrentHashMaps without checking for null or for the required 2-character length. A null shortcut causes a NullPointerException from ConcurrentHashMap.put during startup/lookup, and a 1- or 3-character shortcut is silently accepted and then produces token IDs that getTokenContextFromTokenId rejects with IllegalArgumentException. Validate shortcuts at registration and fail fast with a clear error.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic and wrong substring offset
body: The encoded prefix is sessionType[0,2) + tokenType[2,4) + grantType[4,6), so the grant shortcut is substring(4,6), not substring(3,5). Additionally the check returns false when the substring equals the expected shortcut instead of when it differs. As written, for a normal ID like 'onrtac:...' substring(3,5) is 'ta', never equals 'ac', so the matcher passes for any grant type as long as the suffix is a UUID, and would fail if it ever did match. The new grant-type assertions in expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/etc. therefore test nothing.

title: Constructor validates grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId
body: Line 73 repeats Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) instead of checking rawTokenId (the message even says 'Null rawTokenId not allowed' on the wrong argument in spirit). A null rawTokenId is accepted and encodeTokenId then silently produces an ID ending in ':null', which decodes to the literal string 'null' rather than failing at construction. Fix the second check to requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...).

title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing custom grant factories
body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is an extension interface, but getShortcut() is added as an abstract method with no default implementation. Every existing custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory will fail to compile, and already-deployed implementations will throw AbstractMethodError when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() iterates all factories and calls getShortcut(). Token issuance/server startup can therefore break on upgrade; the method should have a default (e.g. unknown/na) implementation.

title: Public copy constructor of OAuth2GrantType.Context was removed
body: The previously public Context(Context) copy constructor is deleted in this change. Code (including custom grant types/token-exchange code) that copied a grant Context will fail to compile and deployed binaries will fail with NoSuchMethodError. No replacement/deprecation is provided, so this is an unnecessary breaking API change in server-spi-private.

title: Token issuance now fails for any grant type without a registered shortcut
body: encodeTokenId() throws IllegalStateException when factory.getShortcutByGrantType() returns null, and TokenManager.initToken() now calls this for every access token. Previously a token could be issued for a grant/context whose grant_type string is not a registered OAuth2GrantTypeFactory id (custom grants that call TokenManager directly, internal flows that set Constants.GRANT_TYPE themselves, or a grant factory returning no shortcut); now createClientAccessToken() aborts and no token is returned. Encoding context should fall back to the existing UNKNOWN ('na') shortcut instead of failing token issuance.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted and off-by-one grant check
body: The encoded prefix is session(0-1)+tokenType(2-3)+grant(4-5), but the matcher checks substring(3,5) and returns false when that substring equals the expected grant shortcut. As written it rejects (partly) matching ids and accepts ids whose grant does not match, so expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken no longer verify the grant type encoded in TOKEN_ID.

title: Constructor validates grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId
body: Line 73 repeats Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") instead of checking rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted and encodeTokenId() silently produces an id ending in ':null' (which then decodes to the literal string "null"), corrupting the token id instead of failing fast at construction.

title: Federated recovery codes are never marked as used and can be replayed
body: After credentialManager().isValid() succeeds, this code only checks RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.allCodesUsed() on the fetched credential. For a local credential, Keycloak's recovery-code provider consumes the code as part of validation and persists that state; for a federated credential, validation is delegated to the user storage's CredentialInputValidator, which merely validates the input (as the test provider does) and does not update the hashed code list or its used flags. Nothing here calls updateCredential/disableCredentialType to persist consumption. Consequently the same federated recovery code can be reused indefinitely, and RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean will keep asking for the first unused code instead of advancing to the next code.

title: Exhausted federated recovery credentials are not removed
body: When allCodesUsed() is true, the code calls authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(...). That operation removes credentials from Keycloak's local credential store only; it does not delete or disable a credential owned by a federated user storage. Because getCredential() now preferentially returns the federated credential, an exhausted federated credential can remain configured after this call while a CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action is also added, leaving stale/used codes in the external storage and potentially causing repeated setup or inconsistent configuredFor state.

title: Raw recovery codes are sent to user storage instead of the hashed credential data
body: credentialModel already contains the recovery codes in Keycloak's hashed credential representation, but createRecoveryCodesCredential discards that data and sends JsonSerialization.writeValueAsString(generatedCodes), i.e. the plaintext codes, as the UserCredentialModel challenge response. A federated provider that persists the challenge response verbatim (the added BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage does exactly that) will store usable recovery codes in plaintext, unlike local storage which stores hashes. Compromise of the federated store would therefore disclose valid recovery codes; the helper should pass the hashed credential data or clearly require/implement hashing in the storage contract.

title: Federated recovery credential loses user label and generation time
body: The UserCredentialModel sent to user storage is constructed only from credentialModel.getType() and the generated-code JSON. It does not carry credentialModel's userLabel or createdDate/generation time, even though RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(generatedCodes, generatedAtTime, generatedUserLabel) was built with those values in RecoveryAuthnCodesAction. Federated providers therefore cannot persist the label/date chosen at setup; the test provider substitutes the current time and a null label, so account/console displays and credential metadata for federated recovery codes will be wrong or empty.

title: Federated recovery-code test does not verify single-use or code advancement
body: testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin logs in once with the code at index 0 and logs out. It does not attempt to reuse the same code, log in again with the next code, verify that the login page requests the next code number, or verify behavior when all codes are exhausted. Those are the main behavioral differences between local hashed recovery credentials and federated validation, so the current test would pass even though federated codes remain replayable and never advance.

title: Raw recovery codes are sent to and expected to be stored by user storage
body: The local path stores RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, whose credential data contains hashed recovery codes, but the federated path serializes the raw generatedCodes and passes them as the UserCredentialModel challenge response. A user-storage provider that persists this value as received, as the new test provider does, therefore stores all unused recovery codes in recoverable plaintext. Disclosure of the external store would reveal valid second-factor bypass codes, defeating the hashing used for local credentials; the federated input should carry hashed code data or otherwise not require plaintext persistence.

title: Successful federated recovery-code use is never consumed
body: After credentialManager().isValid succeeds, this code only removes the credential when allCodesUsed() is already true; it never records consumption of the just-used code in federated storage (for example via an updateCredential call). For a federated credential, allCodesUsed() is computed from data returned by the storage provider, and a provider whose isValid only validates, like the added BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid, leaves every code unused. The same recovery code can therefore be replayed indefinitely and the all-used removal/required-action branch is never reached, violating the single-use property of recovery codes.

title: Federated creation discards recovery credential label and generation time
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential receives a fully populated RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel containing the user label and generated-at timestamp, but for the user-storage path it builds UserCredentialModel("", type, rawCodesJson) and discards everything except the type and codes. Providers consequently cannot persist the label or original creation date; later reads must synthesize a date and lose the label, so account/admin credential metadata for federated recovery codes differs from locally stored credentials created from the same required action.

title: Federated getCredentials returns a recovery credential with a different ID from the stored one
body: updateCredential assigns recoveryCodesModel an ID via KeycloakModelUtils.generateId(), but getCredentials builds a fresh RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel via createFromValues without copying myUser.recoveryCodes.getId() (unlike the OTP branch, which returns the stored model). Callers such as the authenticator's all-codes-used cleanup use credentialModel.getId() to remove the credential, so that ID will not match the stored federated credential and removal/identification cannot work reliably; the test double masks real ID-based lifecycle behavior.

title: Federated recovery codes are sent and may be stored in plaintext, losing hashed model data
body: The local path stores RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, whose codes are hashed, together with its user label and generation time. The federated path instead serializes the raw generatedCodes list into UserCredentialModel. A user-storage provider that stores the challenge response as received therefore persists usable recovery codes in plaintext, so compromise of the external store exposes all unused codes. The label and generated-at values contained in credentialModel are also not transmitted. Send the hashed credential data/model in a defined format, or explicitly require and demonstrate hashing by the storage provider, rather than handing over the raw code list.

title: Exhausted federated recovery credential is not removed
body: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential now prefers a federated credential, but when allCodesUsed() is true this code calls removeStoredCredentialById(), which removes a locally stored credential and does not delete a credential held by user storage. The exhausted federated credential therefore remains configured for the user; although a required action is added, if that action is not completed the dead credential remains and subsequent recovery-code login can again select it instead of a valid local credential.

title: Login bean crashes when the selected federated credential has no unused code
body: The bean now selects a federated credential first and unconditionally calls getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get(). If that federated credential is present but all its codes are used (which can happen because the authenticator cannot remove federated credentials via removeStoredCredentialById), getNextRecoveryAuthnCode() is empty and this throws NoSuchElementException, breaking rendering of the login form instead of treating the user as having no usable recovery credential or forcing regeneration.

title: Test user-storage validator does not consume used recovery codes
body: isValid() returns true whenever the submitted code matches any code in the stored JSON list, but it never removes or marks that code as used. Consequently the same recovery code can be replayed for unlimited logins for federated users in this provider, unlike local recovery codes which are single-use. The new test logs in only once, so this replay behaviour is not detected; update the stored credential to consume the matched code (and add a reuse-fails test).

title: getCredentials can NPE and returns a credential without the stored id or label
body: getCredentials() dereferences getMyUser(user) without the null check used by isConfiguredFor(), so it can throw NullPointerException for a user absent from the map. When a user is present, RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...) builds a fresh model from the raw codes, created date and (always unset) user label, discarding recoveryCodesModel.getId() and getUserLabel(); callers that rely on a stable credential id (display, deletion, removal when exhausted) therefore receive a null/ephemeral id and lose the label.

title: Concurrent-deletion NPE remains in paginated subgroup methods
body: The fix null-checks only getSubGroupsCount(). The three paginated getSubGroupsStream overloads at lines 254-269 still do modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) without a null check. If the cached group is deleted concurrently and the delegate lookup therefore returns null, these methods throw the same NullPointerException the PR is intended to eliminate, e.g. when listing/searching subgroups of a group being deleted.

title: getSubGroupsCount now returns null instead of a count
body: When the delegate no longer exists this returns null for a Long count that persistent implementations always return as a non-null query result. GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount propagates that null into GroupRepresentation.subGroupCount, so a concurrently deleted group can appear in a listing with a null count and any caller that unboxes/compares the count can NPE. Returning 0L for a deleted group would preserve the non-null contract while avoiding the original NPE.

title: Reader thread is never joined, making the regression test racy and leaky
body: The reader thread is started but never joined. The main thread sets deletedAll at line 155 and immediately asserts caughtExceptions is empty at line 157, while the reader may still be inside groups() and may record an exception only after the assertion, producing false passes. Conversely the unjoined busy-loop thread can outlive the test and keep calling managedRealm.admin() during/after test teardown, interfering with subsequent tests. The test should keep a Thread reference, set the flag, and join it (with timeout) before asserting.

title: Other lazy-delegate accessors still NPE for a concurrently deleted group
body: getSubGroupsCount() was made null-safe, but the three getSubGroupsStream(search/first/max) overloads at lines 254-269 still do modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) without a null check. LazyModel/modelSupplier returns null when the group has been deleted from the database after its CachedGroup was loaded, which is exactly the concurrent-deletion scenario this PR fixes, so calling any of these overloads on such a stale GroupAdapter still throws NullPointerException instead of degrading gracefully.

title: Reader thread is never joined before asserting no exceptions
body: The test starts a reader thread that records failures in caughtExceptions, sets deletedAll=true after deleting the groups, and immediately asserts caughtExceptions is empty at line 157 without joining the reader thread. The reader may still be inside managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...) at that moment and may record the very concurrent-deletion failure the test is meant to catch only after the assertion has passed, making the regression test able to pass spuriously; the unjoined non-daemon thread can also keep issuing requests into subsequent tests.

title: Test does not guarantee the reader overlaps the deletions
body: The reader thread is started with new Thread(...).start() and the main thread immediately proceeds to delete all 100 groups with no latch or other synchronization confirming the reader has performed at least one groups() call before deletions begin. On a busy or single-core CI runner the reader may be scheduled only after deletions finish, in which case the test never exercises concurrent read-versus-delete access and cannot reproduce the original NPE.

title: Concurrent-deletion NPE remains in other lazy-delegate accessors
body: The fix null-checks modelSupplier.get() only in getSubGroupsCount(), but the same lazy delegate is dereferenced without a null check in getSubGroupsStream(String,Integer,Integer) at line 256, getSubGroupsStream(Integer,Integer) at line 262, and getSubGroupsStream(String,Boolean,Integer,Integer) at line 268. When another transaction deletes the group, LazyModel/getGroupById returns null exactly as in the getSubGroupsCount() case, so these methods still throw NullPointerException instead of handling the deleted group. The reported concurrent-access NPE therefore remains reachable through subgroup listing/search paths.

title: Reader thread is never joined, making the new concurrency test racy and leaky
body: The test starts a reader thread looping while deletedAll is false, then sets deletedAll=true at line 155 and immediately asserts caughtExceptions is empty at line 157 without joining the thread. An iteration already inside groups() can still add an exception after the assertion (false pass), or the still-running thread can leak into subsequent tests using the same managed realm/admin client and add failures there. The tight loop also hammers the server with no pause, so unrelated client/timeout errors can be collected unboundedly in the CopyOnWriteArrayList and make the test flaky. The thread should be stored, joined (with timeout) before asserting, and terminated in a finally block.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator is incompatible with the endpoint's datetime ordering
body: The endpoint instantiates OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime", but that paginator copies Paginator.get_item_key/value_from_cursor rather than DateTimePaginator's: get_item_key calls math.floor()/math.ceil() directly on the datetime attribute, which raises TypeError, and value_from_cursor returns the raw numeric cursor value instead of converting milliseconds back to a timezone-aware datetime for build_queryset filtering. The optimized path therefore fails on the first page when build_cursor computes keys, and would filter incorrectly on later pages.

title: Negative offsets passed to a Django QuerySet slice raise AssertionError
body: When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset is negative, get_result executes queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start (and possibly a negative stop). Django QuerySets explicitly reject negative indexing with AssertionError: 'Negative indexing is not supported', contrary to the comment claiming the ORM handles it automatically. The advertised advanced/negative-offset path therefore returns a 500 instead of results whenever it is exercised.

title: BasePaginator change still forwards negative offsets for prev cursors into QuerySet slicing
body: BasePaginator.get_result now clamps the offset only when cursor.is_prev is false (`max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`). A user-supplied prev cursor such as `0:-5:1` is parsed by Cursor.from_string without offset validation and reaches queryset[negative:stop], raising Django's negative-indexing AssertionError. This affects every BasePaginator/DateTimePaginator endpoint, not just the new optimized one, turning a malformed cursor into a 500.

title: organization_context.member may be None and is dereferenced unconditionally
body: The gate computes `organization_context.member.has_global_access` without a None check. RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is optional (notably for superuser access without an organization membership, one of the two groups this branch is meant to enable), so organization_context.member can be None and this line raises AttributeError, breaking the audit-log endpoint for exactly those users instead of selecting a paginator.

title: No tests cover OptimizedCursorPaginator or the optimized audit-log branch
body: The PR adds a new paginator class, changes BasePaginator slicing for all callers, and adds a query-param/permission-gated branch in OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint, but adds no tests. There is no coverage that would have caught the datetime key incompatibility, the Django negative-slice failure, or behavior for superuser/global-access versus regular members, so these regressions ship undetected.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot handle the endpoint's datetime ordering key
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil directly on getattr(item, self.key). The only caller, OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint, uses order_by='-datetime', so the value is a datetime and this raises TypeError whenever build_cursor processes a non-empty page. DateTimePaginator exists precisely to convert datetimes via strftime before scaling. The optimized_pagination=true path therefore returns a 500 instead of audit-log results for authorized users.

title: value_from_cursor does not convert cursor timestamps back to datetimes
body: value_from_cursor returns cursor.value unchanged, unlike DateTimePaginator.value_from_cursor which converts the millisecond timestamp to a timezone-aware datetime. BasePaginator.build_queryset then uses that raw numeric value as the bound in an extra() comparison against AuditLogEntry.datetime. Subsequent pages will compare/filter a datetime column against an integer timestamp, producing incorrect filtering or a database/type error, so even fixing get_item_key would not make multi-page optimized pagination return the correct rows.

title: Negative queryset slicing raises AssertionError, despite the comment claiming Django handles it
body: The advanced-features branch does list(queryset[cursor.offset:stop]) with cursor.offset < 0, accompanied by the false claim that 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically.' Django QuerySet slicing explicitly raises AssertionError: 'Negative indexing is not supported.' A crafted cursor such as 0:-1:0 supplied by an authorized admin therefore causes an unhandled 500. The same crash remains for negative offsets with is_prev cursors in the fallback branch at line 886 and in BasePaginator.get_result at line 184, which now clamps only non-prev cursors.

title: New optimized pagination path is added without any tests
body: This PR adds a user-controlled optimized_pagination branch, a new OptimizedCursorPaginator, and changes slicing behavior in the shared BasePaginator, but adds no tests. There is no coverage for first/next/prev pages over datetime-ordered audit logs, crafted negative-offset cursors, or the superuser/global-access gating. Such tests would have caught that the new paginator crashes on datetime keys and on negative offsets before merge.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes on datetime sort keys
body: The audit-log endpoint uses this paginator with order_by='-datetime', so getattr(item, self.key) returns a datetime. get_item_key passes that datetime directly to math.floor/math.ceil, which raises TypeError. DateTimePaginator avoids this by converting via strftime and a multiplier. Consequently build_cursor's key calls fail and the optimized audit-log path returns a 500 whenever a page contains results.

title: value_from_cursor does not convert cursor timestamps to datetime
body: value_from_cursor returns cursor.value unchanged. For the audit-log endpoint the cursor value must be interpreted as a datetime timestamp and converted to an aware datetime, as DateTimePaginator does; instead the raw numeric value is passed to BasePaginator.build_queryset and used in the datetime column comparison in queryset.extra(where=["...datetime <= %s"]). Subsequent pages will therefore filter incorrectly or fail at the database layer, so cursor navigation cannot work even if get_item_key is fixed.

title: Negative-offset branch uses unsupported negative QuerySet slicing
body: When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset is negative, the code executes list(queryset[start_offset:stop]) with a negative start_offset. Django QuerySets explicitly do not support negative indexing and raise AssertionError ('Negative indexing is not supported'), contrary to the comment claiming the ORM handles it automatically. A crafted or generated negative cursor therefore crashes the request instead of providing reverse pagination.

title: BasePaginator change only clamps negative offsets for non-prev cursors
body: In the shared BasePaginator.get_result used by many endpoints, start_offset is clamped with max(0, offset) only when cursor.is_prev is false; for prev cursors the raw offset is still used as queryset[start_offset:stop]. A user-supplied cursor such as 'value:-1:1' parsed by Cursor.from_string therefore still reaches Django with a negative slice index and raises AssertionError, producing a 500. The change is inconsistent and leaves the claimed negative-offset handling unsafe in the common paginator.

title: No tests cover OptimizedCursorPaginator or the optimized audit-log path
body: The PR adds a new paginator class, changes shared BasePaginator slicing, and adds a new query-param-gated branch in OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint, but adds no tests. In particular there is no test exercising OptimizedCursorPaginator with a datetime key, a second-page cursor, a prev cursor, or a negative offset, which would have caught the datetime conversion and negative-slicing failures before merge.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes on the datetime ordering used by its only caller
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil directly on getattr(item, self.key). The audit-log endpoint enables this paginator with order_by='-datetime', so the value is a datetime, not a number, and math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError. build_cursor invokes get_item_key for results, so any authorized request with optimized_pagination=true fails with a 500 instead of returning a page. DateTimePaginator handles this by converting via strftime first; this class does not. Its value_from_cursor also returns the raw integer cursor value, while build_queryset for a datetime column needs the datetime conversion DateTimePaginator performs, so subsequent pages would filter incorrectly even if the key conversion were fixed.

title: Negative-offset slicing raises AssertionError on Django querysets
body: When enable_advanced_features is set and cursor.offset is negative, this passes a negative start (and possibly a negative stop when limit+extra is smaller than the offset magnitude) into queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django querysets explicitly do not support negative indexing and raise AssertionError ('Negative indexing is not supported'), contrary to the comment claiming the ORM handles it automatically. Since cursor offsets are parsed from the user-supplied cursor string, an authorized audit-log user can craft a negative-offset cursor and trigger an unhandled 500 rather than a BadPaginationError or a valid page. The same unguarded negative offset remains reachable for is_prev cursors in BasePaginator.get_result at line 182.

title: organization_context.member can be None for superusers without org membership
body: The new gate dereferences organization_context.member.has_global_access unconditionally whenever the optimized path is evaluated (for every request, since enable_advanced is computed before the branch). For a superuser accessing an organization they are not a member of, member can be None, so this raises AttributeError and breaks the previously working audit-log endpoint for exactly the superuser case the check tries to allow (the 'or' short-circuit only helps when is_superuser is already true; a non-superuser request still evaluates member, and contexts where member is None for other reasons crash as well). The member access needs a None guard.

title: Switching span sets from SET to ZSET breaks in-flight segments with WRONGTYPE errors
body: This changes the on-Redis type of span-buf:s:* keys from a Redis SET (sadd/sscan/scard/sunionstore) to a ZSET (zadd/zscan/zcard/zunionstore in buffer.py and add-buffer.lua) with no key versioning, draining, or dual-type handling. During a rolling deploy, keys created by old consumers are SETs; new code calling ZADD/ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZSCAN on them returns WRONGTYPE, failing process_spans/flush for those traces, and old consumers similarly fail on new ZSET keys during rollback. Buffered keys live up to redis_ttl (3600s), so in-flight segments will error and can be dropped for up to an hour around deploys.

title: Insert-time eviction can silently drop the segment/root span and leaves has_root_span stale
body: When a segment exceeds 1000 spans, zpopmin evicts the lowest-scored (earliest end_timestamp_precise) members with no metric or log, silently discarding real span payloads rather than flagging the oversized segment as the previous flush-time check did. The evicted members can include the segment/root span (e.g. a short root span, clock skew, or a root whose children report later precise end times); the has_root_span flag computed just below still returns true because it is based on the stored flag or is_root_span of the current insert, so the now root-less segment is queued with the short root timeout and flushed as an incomplete segment. Buffer.py also removed the max_segment_spans guard in _load_segment_data (line 449), so there is no longer any flush-side detection of oversized segments produced by pre-change keys or any path that bypasses this eviction.

title: No test covers the new eviction, score-ordering, or paginator behavior
body: The test changes only add the now-required end_timestamp_precise field to existing Span constructions. Nothing exercises a segment growing past 1000 spans to verify zpopmin eviction keeps the intended (latest/root) spans, nothing verifies segments are ordered or deduplicated correctly after the SET-to-ZSET migration, and there are no tests at all for OptimizedCursorPaginator or the optimized_pagination branch in the audit-log endpoint, which currently crash on datetime keys and negative offsets. The core behavioral change of this PR is therefore unverified.

title: Switching span buffers from sets to sorted sets breaks in-flight Redis data
body: The script and SpansBuffer now use ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZADD/ZSCAN on span-buf:s:* keys, but segments already buffered before deployment are Redis SETs created with SADD. Redis returns WRONGTYPE for sorted-set commands on those keys, so process_spans/flush_segments will error for in-flight segments until their TTL expires (redis_ttl defaults to 3600s), losing or stalling those spans. No migration, type check, or dual-read handling is included.

title: ZUNIONSTORE defaults to SUM and corrupts duplicate span scores
body: Both zunionstore calls omit an AGGREGATE clause, so Redis defaults to SUM. If the same span payload exists in both the destination and source sorted sets (e.g. a re-delivered span, or a span already zadded under the destination key by process_spans before the Lua merge), its score becomes the sum of the two end_timestamp_precise values (roughly double, e.g. year 2077). Eviction via ZPOPMIN then orders by corrupted scores, so duplicated spans are effectively never evicted and eviction order no longer reflects end time. Use AGGREGATE MAX (or MIN) explicitly.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator is incompatible with the datetime ordering of its only caller
body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint calls this paginator with order_by='-datetime', but get_item_key does int(math.floor(value)) on the datetime attribute and value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor value instead of converting it back to a datetime as DateTimePaginator does. build_cursor calls get_item_key on every non-empty page (TypeError on datetime) and build_queryset compares the datetime column against an int. The optimized_pagination=true path will therefore 500 or mis-filter for audit logs instead of paginating them.

title: Negative-offset slicing raises instead of being handled by Django
body: The advanced-features branch passes cursor.offset (parsed from the user-supplied cursor string) directly as queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start, claiming the Django ORM handles this. Django querysets explicitly raise AssertionError ('Negative indexing is not supported') on negative slices, and the same applies to the is_prev branch in BasePaginator.get_result (line 182-184) which also leaves offset unclamped. Any admin hitting the audit-log endpoint with a crafted negative-offset cursor gets a 500, so the advertised feature does not work and adds a trivial error/DoS path.

title: Unrelated audit-log pagination feature is bundled into the spans change
body: This PR is titled and described as a spans-buffer optimization, but it also adds a new user-controlled 'optimized_pagination' mode to the organization audit-log endpoint, gated on is_superuser/has_global_access and backed by the new OptimizedCursorPaginator. This changes behavior of a sensitive audit-log API (whose paginator is broken for datetime keys and crashes on negative offsets, per the paginator findings) without any endpoint tests, changelog, or feature-flag rollout. It should be split out and reviewed/tested independently rather than shipped hidden inside the spans change.

title: Redirect depth limit silently reduced from 10000 to 1000
body: The redirect-following loop cap drops from 10000 to 1000 and the comment explaining that deeper segment trees may not be joined correctly is deleted. Traces whose parent chain exceeds 1000 redirects will now stop following redirects early, so spans land in separate span-buf:s:* sets and are flushed as fragmented/incomplete segments rather than one segment. This is a correctness regression for deep traces unrelated to the 1000-span eviction cap (chain depth and span count are different dimensions).

title: Flush-side max_segment_spans safeguard removed while insert cap is inconsistent
body: _load_segment_data no longer drops segments exceeding max_segment_spans (the metric and logger.error branch were removed), so the only remaining span-count protection is the Lua cap. That cap is hardcoded to 1000 while SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans defaults to 1001 and is configurable, and it only runs on the insert path: segments created before this change, created while script loading fails, or grown by the Python-side ZADD pipeline before Lua runs can now be loaded and flushed unbounded (bounded only by the 10MiB byte cap), reintroducing the memory/segment-size risk the removed guard protected against, with no metric when eviction truncates a segment.

title: process_batch now hard-requires end_timestamp_precise and will crash the batch if absent
body: Span previously did not need end_timestamp_precise; the existing consumer test payload omitted it and had to be modified in this PR to add it. Using val['end_timestamp_precise'] raises KeyError for any ingest-spans message lacking the field, failing the entire batch in process_batch (and, under Arroyo, causing redelivery/retry of the same poison batch) instead of defaulting the score (e.g. val.get('end_timestamp_precise', 0) or the message timestamp). Either tolerate a missing value or prove from the schema that it is mandatory and add a test for the missing-field case.

title: No test covers eviction, the sorted-set merge, or the reduced redirect depth
body: The test changes in this PR only add the new end_timestamp_precise argument to existing Span constructions. There is no test that inserts more than 1000 spans into one segment to verify ZPOPMIN eviction (which spans survive, whether the root/segment span can be evicted, and final flushed contents), no test with duplicate payloads across merged sets to verify score handling, and no test near the new 1000 redirect-depth limit. The core behavioral change of the PR is therefore unverified.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot handle the datetime ordering it is used with
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does math.floor/math.ceil directly on getattr(item, self.key) and value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor value. The only caller, OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint, uses order_by='-datetime', so get_item_key receives a datetime and raises TypeError, and build_queryset would compare a datetime column against an integer cursor value. DateTimePaginator exists precisely to convert datetimes via timestamps. Any superuser/global-access user requesting optimized_pagination=true will get a 500 instead of audit logs.

title: Negative-offset slicing crashes Django querysets and is not a permission-safe feature
body: When enable_advanced_features is set and cursor.offset is negative, this passes a negative start to queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django querysets explicitly raise AssertionError ('Negative indexing is not supported'), so the advertised advanced pagination path crashes rather than paginating. The same problem remains in BasePaginator.get_result at line 182 for is_prev cursors. The comments claiming the ORM handles this and that queryset-level permissions make it safe are false; cursors are user-controlled via the cursor query parameter.

title: ZUNIONSTORE defaults to SUM, corrupting scores of spans present in both sets
body: Both zunionstore calls omit AGGREGATE/WEIGHTS, so Redis sums the scores of members present in both the destination and source sorted sets. A span payload already in set_key that is also in span_key/parent_key (duplicate delivery or overlapping merge) gets its end_timestamp_precise roughly doubled, moving it to ~year 2077. That corrupts the ordering used by ZPOPMIN eviction: duplicated spans become effectively unevictable while legitimate spans are evicted instead. The old SUNIONSTORE had no such side effect; AGGREGATE MAX (or equivalent) is required.

title: Set-to-sorted-set conversion breaks on all pre-existing Redis buffer keys
body: process_spans now ZADDs into span-buf:s:* keys that existing deployments hold as Redis SETs (previously SADD), and the Lua script and _load_segment_data now use ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZSCAN on them. Redis returns WRONGTYPE for these commands on set-typed keys, so every in-flight segment buffered before deploy will fail processing/flushing until its TTL (up to redis_ttl, 3600s) expires, stalling or erroring batches. There is no key versioning, migration, or type check in the PR.

title: New required Span field inserted before a defaulted field breaks existing constructors
body: end_timestamp_precise is added as a required positional field immediately before is_segment_span, which previously was the seventh positional/keyword field with a default. Any Span(...) construction elsewhere (other consumers, scripts, tests not in this diff) that omits the new field now raises TypeError, and any construction passing is_segment_span positionally will silently assign a bool as end_timestamp_precise, which then becomes a Redis sorted-set score of 0/1. Adding it at the end with a default, or updating all call sites verifiably, is needed.

title: Direct indexing of end_timestamp_precise turns a missing field into a poison-pill batch
body: process_batch now does val['end_timestamp_precise'] for every Kafka message. Previously this field was not read, and the updated tests themselves show messages legitimately lacking it before this change. A single span without the field raises KeyError, failing the whole batch; with Arroyo retries this becomes a poison pill blocking the partition. A defensive .get with a fallback (e.g. end_timestamp or 0) or explicit schema guarantee plus dead-letter handling is needed.

title: Insert-time eviction silently discards the earliest-ending spans, possibly the segment span
body: When a segment exceeds 1000 spans, ZPOPMIN silently deletes the spans with the smallest end_timestamp_precise with no metric, log, or downstream signal. The flushed segment is then emitted as if complete while missing spans; if an evicted span carried parent/redirect relationships, or the segment span itself is evicted for long-running roots whose children end later, flush_segments marks no span is_segment and produces a rootless segment under the wrong segment_id. The hard-coded 1000 also disagrees with SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans=1001 and ignores the configurable limit entirely.

title: Flush-time max_segment_spans enforcement removed without an equivalent guarantee
body: _load_segment_data no longer aborts segments exceeding self.max_segment_spans; it now loads and returns arbitrarily many spans (bounded only by the 10MiB byte check). The Lua cap does not fully replace this: it is hard-coded to 1000 rather than the configured value, only runs on the insert/merge path for the final set_key, and does not protect against keys created or grown outside that path (including pre-existing keys). Oversized segments that were previously skipped with a metric/error will now be produced downstream.

title: Redirect chain limit cut from 10000 to 1000 regresses deep segment trees
body: The redirect-following loop limit drops from 10000 to 1000 iterations (and the explanatory comment is deleted). For span trees deeper than 1000 redirects — previously supported up to 10k — set_span_id stops mid-chain, so the span is written to a wrong/intermediate set and the segment is split into multiple segments that flush separately with incorrect segment_ids. This is an unannounced behavioral regression unrelated to the eviction change.

title: No test covers eviction, score merging, or the new paginator path
body: All updated buffer tests use identical end_timestamp_precise values and at most 5 spans, so the headline behavior — eviction above 1000 spans, which spans are chosen for eviction, ZUNIONSTORE score handling for duplicates, and ordering by end time — is entirely untested, as is OptimizedCursorPaginator/negative offsets and the audit-log optimized branch. The regressions above (score summing, root eviction, datetime paginator crash, negative-slice crash) would all pass the current suite.

title: upsampled_count undercounts events without sample_weight
body: upsampled_count computes toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) with no coalesce/fallback to 1 for rows where sample_weight is NULL. Allowlisted projects can contain events predating client error sampling, events from SDKs that do not send error_sampling context, or otherwise unsampled events; for those rows sum() ignores NULLs, so a bucket containing only such events returns NULL/0 instead of its real count and mixed buckets silently undercount. The transform in error_upsampling.py applies this to every count() for allowlisted projects, so historical/normal error events disappear from charts. Use a per-row fallback such as coalesce(sample_weight, 1) before summing.

title: Negated or quoted event.type:error incorrectly triggers upsampling
body: _is_error_focused_query does a raw substring check for 'event.type:error' on the lowercased query string. A query such as '!event.type:error' (explicitly excluding errors, e.g. transaction/default events) contains that substring and returns True, as would the text inside a quoted title/message value. The endpoint then rewrites count() to sum(sample_weight), which does not exist/apply for those non-error events, producing wrong (likely zero/NULL) counts. The query needs to be parsed (or at minimum negation/quoting handled) rather than substring-matched, and spaced forms like 'event.type: error' are also missed by the current check.

title: Upsampling decision uses outer dataset and request query, not the scoped query actually executed
body: _get_event_stats receives scoped_dataset and query arguments that differ from the closure values during dashboard discover-split handling (e.g. split_dataset=discover, errors_only_query with '!event.type:transaction', transactions_only_query), but the eligibility call passes the outer 'dataset' and the helper reads request.GET['query'] instead of the 'query' argument. Consequently split error-only queries can fail to upsample while split transaction/other queries can be decided from the unrelated original request query, and the split has_errors/has_transactions comparisons can mix upsampled and non-upsampled results. Pass scoped_dataset and the effective query string into the decision.

title: Cached allowlist eligibility can go stale and be inconsistent within one request
body: Eligibility is cached for 60 seconds under a key built from hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))), but invalidate_upsampling_cache is never called from anywhere (option changes have no invalidation hook), so removing a project from the allowlist keeps upsampling its counts (and adding one delays it) with no bound tied to config changes. Additionally _get_event_stats re-evaluates this on every invocation, and the dashboard-split flow invokes it several times per request; a cache expiry mid-request can make the error, original, and transaction sub-queries disagree. Combined with hash() collisions between different project sets for the same organization, one set can also inherit another set's cached eligibility. Compute the decision once per request (or key the cache deterministically on the project IDs) instead of relying on an uninvalidated TTL cache.

title: upsampled_count is exposed as a public function for non-allowlisted projects
body: Unlike neighbouring internal aggregates, the new SnQLFunction 'upsampled_count' in discover.py is not marked private, and transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling emits it as a user-visible column string. Any user can therefore send yAxis=upsampled_count() directly for any project/dataset, bypassing the all-projects-allowlisted gate in is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects, and get sum(sample_weight) results (NULL/0 for projects without sampling) presented as legitimate counts. Mark the function private like the other internal-only aggregates so it can only be produced by the server-side rewrite.

title: Stray subproject file committed at repository root
body: This adds a file named 'sentry-repo' containing only 'Subproject commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a', which looks like an accidental git submodule/gitlink artifact rather than intended source. It should be removed before merge to avoid confusing tooling and repository layout.

title: No tests for the public eligibility entry point, caching, or mixed sample_weight data
body: The new tests only cover the private helpers _are_all_projects_error_upsampled, _is_error_focused_query (happy paths), _should_apply_sample_weight_transform, and the column rewrite. is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects itself — including its 60s cache behaviour, the errors-vs-discover dataset gate combined with allowlist state, negated queries like '!event.type:error', and events in allowlisted projects that have no sample_weight/client_sample_rate — is never exercised at the unit level, and the Snuba tests only store events that all carry client_sample_rate=0.1. These are exactly the paths where counts can silently become 0 or be wrongly upsampled, so regression coverage should be added before merging.

title: Accidental gitlink/submodule added to repository root
body: This adds a file named `sentry-repo` containing only `Subproject commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a`, i.e. an accidental nested-repository gitlink unrelated to error upsampling. Merging it creates a bogus submodule entry at the repo root that can break checkouts/tooling expecting it to be a normal path and pollutes the tree; it should be removed from the PR.

title: Upsampling eligibility uses closure `dataset` instead of `scoped_dataset` actually queried
body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset` (which `get_event_stats_factory` changes for dashboard discover-split widgets, e.g. passing `discover` or the original scoped dataset), but the eligibility check passes the outer closure variable `dataset`. When the two differ, counts are transformed for a dataset that is not being queried (e.g. upsampling a transactions/discover query, where `sample_weight` is invalid/zero) or not transformed for the errors query that is actually run, producing wrong counts or Snuba errors for split dashboard widgets.

title: Error-focus check reads request.GET instead of the query actually being executed
body: `_is_error_focused_query` only inspects `request.GET['query']`, ignoring the `query` argument passed to `_get_event_stats`. That argument is rewritten by callers (dashboard split builds `({query}) AND !event.type:transaction` and `({query}) AND event.type:transaction`, and event-stats can execute multiple/derived queries). Consequently a transaction-only subquery can be upsampled because the original request mentioned errors, while an error-only subquery whose request parameter is empty or formatted differently is not upsampled, yielding incorrect `sum(sample_weight)` counts for transactions or missed upsampling for errors.

title: Allowlist eligibility is cached for 60s with a dead invalidation function and a hash()-based key
body: Eligibility is stored under `error_upsampling_eligible:{org}:{hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))}` for 60 seconds, but `invalidate_upsampling_cache` (line 67) is never called anywhere and no option-change hook invokes it, so removing a project from `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` keeps inflating its counts (and adding one delays correct counts) until expiry.
