Zod strips unknown keys by default, so when sharing is enabled expires_in/expiry_date, scope, token_type, instance_url and other fields required by callers are dropped from .data. Zoom then computes expiry_date as Date.now()+undefined*1000 (NaN), Office365 keeps a stale expiry, and Salesforce loses id/instance_url/signature, producing invalid or immediately-expired credentials.

title: Dummy refresh_token overwrites the real refresh token
body: When the (stripped) parsed response has no refresh_token, this sets refresh_token to the literal string "refresh_token". Callers persist that value: Zoom assigns key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token and Office365 spreads tokenResponse.data into the stored credential. With credential sharing enabled the real refresh token in the database is irreversibly replaced by the placeholder, so disabling sharing later or falling back to the provider leaves the credential permanently unrefreshable.

title: Sync branch returns a raw fetch Response incompatible with most callers
body: When sharing is enabled this returns the raw fetch Response, but callers expect the shape of their original refreshFunction. Google expects res.data.access_token/expiry_date, HubSpot expects a HubspotToken object with expiresIn/accessToken, and Zoho CRM/Bigin expect an axios response with .data.error/access_token. A fetch Response has none of those properties, so those integrations store undefined tokens/expiry or throw on .data access instead of using the synced access token. Only fetch-based callers that parse JSON themselves are compatible.

title: Passes credentialId where refreshOAuthTokens expects userId
body: refreshOAuthTokens(refreshFunction, appSlug, userId) sends its third argument to the sync endpoint as calcomUserId. Here credentialId (the credential row id, captured in biginAuth) is passed instead of credential.userId, which this method does not even receive. The parent platform will look up a user by a credential id, so it will return tokens for the wrong user or no user, and the refreshed token can be stored against this credential.

title: Refreshed Salesforce token is discarded and stale token is used
body: getClient unconditionally refreshes on every construction, parses and persists accessTokenParsed.data, but then constructs the jsforce Connection with accessToken: credentialKey.access_token (the old token from before the refresh) and the old instance_url. The new access token is never used for API calls, so an expired stored token still fails, while every service construction now adds a Salesforce token request and a DB write. It also bypasses refreshOAuthTokens, so it does not honour credential-sync mode.

title: Webhook secret compared non-constant-time and errors are unhandled
body: The shared secret is compared with !== against a request header, which is timing-unsafe for a secret that alone authorizes overwriting any user's third-party credentials for any app. The handler also has no method check and no try/catch around appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body) (line 31) or symmetricDecrypt/JSON.parse (lines 57-59), so malformed or wrongly-encrypted payloads throw unhandled 500s instead of controlled 400 responses. The secret check should use a constant-time comparison and parsing/decryption failures should be caught.

title: Minimum token schema is malformed and strips required token fields
body: The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` do not create wildcard/dynamic Zod keys; they create literal '[object Object]'-style keys, one of which is a required number. Responses containing only access_token/expiry from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT therefore fail safeParse and throw 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned', while Zod's default stripping also drops fields such as refresh_token, expiry_date/expires_in, scope and provider-specific fields that callers persist. Credential-sync refresh is effectively broken for Google, Office365, Zoom and Salesforce.

title: Missing refresh_token is replaced with the literal string 'refresh_token'
body: When the sync endpoint correctly returns only an access token, this code invents refresh_token='refresh_token' instead of preserving the stored refresh token. Callers such as Zoom (key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token), Office365 (spreading tokenResponse.data over stored credentials) and Google then persist that placeholder, destroying the real refresh token so the next refresh fails with invalid_grant and the credential becomes unusable.

title: Sync path returns a raw fetch Response incompatible with most callers
body: When sync is enabled this returns the raw fetch Response, but callers were written for incompatible return types: HubSpot expects a HubspotToken object (accessToken/expiresIn become undefined), ZohoCRM/Zoho-Bigin expect an Axios response with .data (tokenInfo.data is undefined on a Response and .error access crashes/misbehaves), and Google expects res.data (token.access_token throws). Only fetch-based callers expecting a Response can work, so enabling sync breaks refresh for several apps. It also never checks response.ok or parses JSON, so HTTP errors from the sync endpoint are treated as successful token responses.

title: SafeParse result object is persisted as the credential key
body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the Zod SafeParse result ({success, data}), but this code does `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...); prisma.credential.update({data:{key}})`, whereas previously googleCredentialSchema.parse returned the token data itself. The stored key becomes {success:true, data:{...}}, so googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) on the next use fails/missing access_token and refresh_token, corrupting the Google credential even without credential sync enabled.

title: New Salesforce refresh code uses unimported prisma and discards the refreshed token
body: getClient now calls prisma.credential.update but prisma is never imported in this file, causing a TypeScript/ReferenceError on every Salesforce client creation. Even if it ran, the jsforce Connection at lines 101-108 is built with credentialKey.access_token (the old, expired token) instead of accessTokenParsed.data.access_token, so the freshly fetched and persisted token is never used.

title: Credential ID is passed where refreshOAuthTokens expects a user ID
body: refreshOAuthTokens' third argument is userId and is sent to the sync endpoint as calcomUserId, but Bigin passes credentialId (the credential primary key) instead of credential.userId. With sync enabled the parent platform will look up/refresh tokens for the wrong user (or no user), returning wrong credentials or failing refresh. The service does not retain credential.userId in biginAuth, only credential.id.

title: Webhook secret is compared with non-constant-time equality and handler has no error handling
body: The shared secret used to authorize writing arbitrary user credentials is compared with !==, allowing timing-based secret recovery, instead of a constant-time comparison (e.g. crypto.timingSafeEqual with length checks). Additionally the handler imposes no HTTP-method check and lets z.object.parse (line 31), symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse (lines 57-59) throw uncaught, turning malformed/unauthenticated-shape payloads into 500s rather than controlled 400 responses.

title: Uses prisma without importing it
body: The newly added refresh block calls prisma.credential.update at line 96, but this file has no prisma import (imports are jsforce, RRule, zod, CalEventParser, constants, HttpError, logger, types, getAppKeysFromSlug and parseRefreshTokenResponse). This is a ReferenceError/TypeScript compile error and, if it compiled, would crash every Salesforce client construction at runtime.

title: Fabricates dummy refresh_token and strips real token fields when sharing is enabled
body: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is set, minimumTokenResponseSchema is a plain z.object, so Zod strips all fields except access_token (its computed keys are z.string().toString(), i.e. nonsense keys that do not allow other properties). Lines 25-27 then invent refresh_token='refresh_token'. Callers such as Zoom (key.refresh_token=newTokens.refresh_token; key.expiry_date=Date.now()+newTokens.expires_in*1000) therefore persist a fake refresh token and compute expiry_date as NaN, and Office365/Google lose expires_in/expiry, scope and token_type, permanently corrupting the stored credential so the next refresh fails.

title: Stores SafeParse wrapper object as the credential key
body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the SafeParse result {success,data}, not the parsed data. Previously this line used googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials) which returns the credential object itself. Now prisma.credential.update stores {success:true,data:{access_token,refresh_token}} as key. On the next use googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) at line 75 will fail/misread because the stored key has the wrong shape, breaking the Google credential after the first refresh even when credential sharing is disabled.

title: Returns raw fetch Response to callers expecting SDK/axios objects
body: When sync is enabled this returns the raw fetch Response, but callers were written for incompatible return types: HubSpot expects a HubspotToken object (hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn/accessToken in hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:192,202), ZohoCRM and Zoho Bigin expect an axios response with tokenInfo.data (zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts:217, zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:96), and Google expects res.data (googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94-96, a fetch Response has no .data and needs .json()). Enabling sync therefore yields undefined tokens/expiry or TypeErrors for those integrations instead of refreshed tokens. No response.ok check or JSON parsing is done here either.

title: Passes credentialId where refreshOAuthTokens expects userId
body: refreshOAuthTokens(refreshFunction, appSlug, userId) sends its third argument as calcomUserId to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT and only enables sync when it is truthy as a user id. This call passes credentialId (the credential primary key, captured at line 53) rather than credential.userId, which is not even retained in biginAuth. The parent application will be asked to refresh tokens for the wrong/nonexistent user.

title: New Salesforce refresh discards refreshed token and corrupts stored key
body: getClient now unconditionally refreshes on every construction, parses with parseRefreshTokenResponse, then at lines 96-99 overwrites the stored key with only {...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token} — in sharing mode the minimum schema strips id, issued_at, instance_url, signature, scope and token_type required by salesforceTokenSchema/future use. It then constructs the jsforce Connection at lines 101-108 with the old credentialKey.access_token/refresh_token, not the refreshed token, so the refresh has no effect apart from corrupting the DB row.

title: Webhook secret compared non-constantly and header name not normalized; malformed input causes unhandled 500s
body: The secret is compared with !== against req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || 'calcom-webhook-secret']; Node lower-cases incoming header names, so a configured value with any uppercase letter (the code does not toLowerCase it) will always reject legitimate calls, and the plain string comparison is timing-unsafe for a credential-writing endpoint. Separately, z.parse at line 31 and JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) at lines 57-59 are uncaught, so an invalid body or undecryptable keys payload throws and returns an unhandled 500/stack behaviour instead of a 400, and there is no HTTP-method check.

title: Team admin/owner check requires both roles instead of either
body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...). A team admin who is not the owner, and an owner whose admin check does not also return true, therefore fail this test. Unless such a user is also the booking organizer or an attendee, legitimate team admins/owners are incorrectly rejected with FORBIDDEN when adding guests. The condition should be an OR.

title: Any attendee account can add arbitrary guests and disclose the meeting
body: Authorization accepts any booking attendee whose account email matches an attendee email. That attendee can then add arbitrary email addresses; the handler adds them to the booking, updates the calendar event, and sends new guests an AttendeeScheduledEmail containing the event details and joining information. An attendee therefore does not need organizer or team-admin approval to expand access to a private meeting. This endpoint is also directly callable through tRPC even though the new UI is on the organizer bookings page.

title: Guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, pending, or past bookings
body: After checking that the booking exists, the handler never checks booking.status or whether the booking is still upcoming. It creates attendees, calls updateCalendarAttendees, and sends scheduled/add-guests emails even for cancelled or rejected bookings and for events that have already ended. The UI also exposes booked actions for past confirmed bookings. This can resurrect calendar invites and meeting emails for events that should no longer accept guests.

title: Server schema allows duplicate, empty-sized, and unbounded guest lists
body: The server input is only z.array(z.string().email()): it has no uniqueness constraint, minimum, or maximum. The handler's filter only compares each guest with the booking's pre-existing attendees, so guests:['a@example.com','a@example.com'] creates two attendee rows for the same person, and case variants such as A@example.com/a@example.com also bypass both attendee and blacklist comparisons (the blacklist is lower-cased but guests are not). A caller bypassing the client dialog can also submit thousands of guests, causing bulk attendee creation, calendar updates, and emails. Enforce a bounded, case-normalized unique set on the server and pass that normalized set to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of raw guests.

title: Calendar is updated using the caller's credentials rather than the organizer's
body: getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) and the EventManager are built from the authenticated caller. When the caller is an attendee or a team admin rather than booking.userId, updateCalendarAttendees is attempted with the wrong user's calendar/video credentials (or none), so the organizer's calendar event is not reliably updated with the new attendees even though the database rows were already created and success may be reported. The EventManager should be constructed for the booking organizer, as the calendar event belongs to that user.

title: MultiEmail imports from its own package index, creating a circular import
body: This file lives inside @calcom/ui but imports Button, EmailField, Icon, and Tooltip from '@calcom/ui'. The package index exports MultiEmail from MultiEmailLazy, which dynamically imports this file, so the module graph cycles back through the partially initialized package entry point. Depending on bundling/chunking this can yield undefined components at runtime. Import these components via their relative paths inside packages/ui instead of the package self-reference.

title: Team admin/owner check requires being both admin and owner
body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...). Team membership roles are distinct, so a user who is only a team admin or only a team owner fails this check. Non-organizer team admins/owners who should be able to manage a team booking are therefore incorrectly rejected with FORBIDDEN unless they also happen to be the organizer or an attendee. The condition should be an OR.

title: Any attendee can add arbitrary guests without organizer approval
body: The handler authorizes the request if the caller is merely listed as an attendee (isAttendee based on matching email). The UI only exposes Add Guests to the booking owner in their bookings list, but the API allows any attendee with a Cal.com account using the same email to add arbitrary people to someone else's booking, triggering calendar updates and invitation emails to all attendees. This exceeds the organizer-only capability exposed by the product UI.

title: Duplicate and case-variant guests are not deduplicated server-side
body: uniqueGuests only filters out emails exactly equal to an existing attendee and does not deduplicate within the submitted guests array itself, and all comparisons are case-sensitive while the blacklist check lowercases only the blacklist entries (guest is not lowercased). The server schema in addGuests.schema.ts likewise has no uniqueness refinement. A direct API call with ['a@x.com','a@x.com'] or case variants such as 'A@x.com' vs existing 'a@x.com' creates duplicate Attendee rows, duplicate calendar attendees and duplicate emails, and a blacklisted address can be bypassed by changing its case.

title: Guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, pending or past bookings
body: The handler loads the booking by id but never checks booking.status or booking.endTime before creating attendees, calling EventManager.updateCalendarAttendees and sending 'guests added'/scheduled emails. Guests can therefore be added to cancelled or rejected bookings (reviving calendar invites for an event that will not happen) or to bookings already in the past. The server should reject non-ACCEPTED and/or past bookings regardless of what the client UI shows.

title: Calendar is updated with the caller's credentials instead of the organizer's
body: getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) and the EventManager construction use the requesting user, not booking.user (the organizer whose calendar holds the event). When a team admin or an attendee adds guests, updateCalendarAttendees runs with the wrong user's calendar/video credentials, so it will fail to update the organizer's calendar event or attempt updates against the caller's own integrations, leaving the database attendees and the external calendar out of sync. Credentials/EventManager should be built for the booking organizer.

title: Email classification uses unfiltered guests list instead of uniqueGuests
body: sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the raw input `guests` rather than `uniqueGuests`. Addresses that were filtered out because they are already attendees are therefore classified inside sendAddGuestsEmails as newly added guests and receive an AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the guests-added notification, and the new/existing attendee classification no longer matches who was actually created in the database. Pass uniqueGuests.

title: Unbounded guests array allows mass attendee creation and email spam
body: guests is z.array(z.string().email()) with no .min(1)/.max() bound. Any authorized caller can submit thousands of addresses in one request, causing a createMany of attendee rows, an EventManager calendar update with thousands of attendees, and sendAddGuestsEmails to fan out organizer, team and per-attendee emails (plus a scheduled email to every new guest). This is an email-spam/resource-exhaustion vector; bound the array size (and reject empty arrays) server-side.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores event-type disabled-email settings
body: Unlike sendLocationChangeEmails/sendScheduledEmails, sendAddGuestsEmails does not accept eventTypeMetadata and never checks eventTypeDisableHostEmail/eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail. Event types that have standard host or attendee emails disabled (metadata.disableStandardEmails) will still send organizer, team-member and attendee emails when guests are added, violating the organizer's configured email preferences.

title: MultiEmail imports @calcom/ui from inside the @calcom/ui package
body: MultiEmail.tsx lives in packages/ui but imports { Button, EmailField, Icon, Tooltip } from '@calcom/ui' (the package's own public entrypoint, which re-exports MultiEmailLazy -> MultiEmail). This self-referential/circular import through the package index can cause circular-dependency initialization problems and pulls the entire UI index into the lazily loaded chunk, defeating the lazy loading introduced in MultiEmailLazy. Sibling form components should be imported via their relative paths inside the package.

title: Team admin/owner check requires being both admin and owner
body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. A team admin who is not the owner (and vice versa) therefore evaluates to false, so legitimate team admins/owners who are not also the booking organizer or an attendee get FORBIDDEN. The condition should be an OR, matching the variable name and the intended authorization.

title: Any attendee can add arbitrary guests to someone else's booking
body: Authorization passes if the caller is merely an attendee (matched by email). The UI only exposes this action on the organizer's bookings page, but via the API any attendee with a Cal.com account can add unlimited arbitrary guests to the organizer's booking, triggering calendar updates and invitation emails from the organizer without organizer approval. This is a privilege escalation beyond the organizer-only feature being added.

title: No booking status or timing check before adding guests
body: The handler never checks booking.status or start/end time. Guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, pending, or already-ended bookings; the handler then persists attendees, calls updateCalendarAttendees, and sendAddGuestsEmails emits ICS files with status CONFIRMED. This can resurrect/confuse dead bookings and sends misleading confirmed invites for events that will not happen. It should reject non-accepted and past bookings.

title: Calendar is updated with the caller's credentials instead of the organizer's
body: credentials are loaded via getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) and EventManager is built from the calling user, while evt.destinationCalendar belongs to the booking organizer. When the caller is a team admin or attendee (both explicitly authorized above), the organizer's calendar event is updated using the wrong user's credentials, so the calendar update will fail or target the wrong account even though the DB attendees were already added. Credentials/EventManager should be based on booking.user (already loaded with credentials in the query).

title: Server schema allows duplicate, case-variant, and unbounded guest lists
body: guests is just z.array(z.string().email()) with no uniqueness, normalization, or max length. The handler's dedupe is case-sensitive (`guest === attendee.email`) and does not dedupe within the input itself, and the blacklist check lowercases the blacklist but not the guest. An API caller can therefore create duplicate attendee rows (e.g. 'A@x.com' and 'a@x.com', or the same email twice, causing createMany duplicates) and submit arbitrarily large lists to spam calendar invites/emails. The client-side refine in AddGuestsDialog does not protect the API.

title: Emails are classified using the raw guest list instead of the guests actually added
body: sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) is passed the raw input rather than uniqueGuests. sendAddGuestsEmails treats any attendee whose email is in that list as a new guest and sends them a full AttendeeScheduledEmail. An existing attendee who was filtered out as already-present therefore incorrectly receives a fresh scheduled invitation instead of the 'guests added' notification, and filtered/blacklisted handling diverges from what was actually persisted. Pass uniqueGuests.

title: Reminders with no message or recipient are never counted or deleted
body: The retry increment only runs when twilio.scheduleSMS returns null or throws. If message is empty/null or sendTo is falsy, the `if (message?.length && ... && sendTo)` block is skipped entirely: the reminder stays unscheduled with retryCount 0, is re-fetched on every cron run, and the new `retryCount > 1` cleanup never fires. This leaves the exact infinite-rescheduling loop the PR aims to fix in place for missing/invalid phone numbers or empty templates (and similarly for the `continue` at lines 68-70 when workflowStep/booking is missing, which also never increments).

title: Retry increment is a stale read-modify-write, not atomic
body: Both increments (lines 184 and 195) write `reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value snapshotted by the findMany at the start of the run. If two cron invocations overlap, both read retryCount 0 and both write 1, so the counter never exceeds 1, the `retryCount > 1` deletion never triggers, and failing reminders are retried forever (and may also double-schedule with Twilio). Using Prisma's atomic `{ increment: 1 }` avoids the lost update.

title: Unhandled update inside catch can abort the whole cron run
body: The catch block now awaits `prisma.workflowReminder.update` without its own error handling. If that update fails (e.g. P2025 because the reminder was deleted by the concurrent cleanup/another run, or a transient DB error), the exception propagates out of the per-reminder try/catch, aborting the loop so all remaining unscheduled reminders are skipped and the handler returns 500 instead of `SMS scheduled`. Previously the catch only logged. The increment should be wrapped so a failure to record a retry does not break processing of the other reminders.

title: Retry-count deletion clause is not scoped to SMS reminders
body: The original deleteMany was scoped to `method: SMS`; in the new OR the second branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no method (or scheduled/date) constraint, so it deletes WorkflowReminder rows of any method (EMAIL/WHATSAPP share this table per WorkflowMethods) once their retryCount exceeds 1, even if they are future-dated and not this SMS cron's responsibility. Scoping it to SMS (like the first branch) keeps this handler from deleting other channels' reminders.

title: Retry-count deletion is not restricted to SMS reminders
body: The second branch of the deleteMany OR only checks retryCount > 1, with no method, scheduled, or scheduledDate restriction. As written it deletes WorkflowReminder rows of any method (EMAIL/WHATSAPP as well as SMS) once their retryCount exceeds 1, even though this cron is only supposed to clean up SMS reminders. The SMS filter from the original query must be applied to the retry-count branch as well (or hoisted outside the OR), otherwise any present or future code that increments retryCount on non-SMS reminders will have those reminders silently deleted by the SMS cron.

title: Reminders with no message or no recipient never consume a retry
body: When message is empty/null or sendTo is falsy, the `if (message?.length && sendTo)` block is skipped entirely: the reminder is not marked scheduled, retryCount is not incremented, and nothing is logged. Such reminders (e.g. a booking with no smsReminderNumber) are therefore re-fetched and re-processed on every cron run until their scheduledDate passes, which is exactly the unbounded retry loop this PR claims to eliminate. This path needs to increment retryCount (or delete/handle the reminder) so it terminates after two failures.

title: Retry-count update inside catch can throw and abort the whole cron run
body: The catch block now awaits prisma.workflowReminder.update without its own error handling. If the original error was a database/connection problem, or the reminder was deleted concurrently, this update throws out of the for loop: all remaining unscheduled reminders are skipped and the handler never sends its 200 response. Before this change the catch only logged and continued with the next reminder. The increment should be guarded (nested try/catch) so one failing reminder cannot abort processing of the rest.

title: Retry count uses stale read-modify-write instead of an atomic increment
body: Both increment sites write `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value read at the start of the run. If two cron invocations overlap (or the row changes between findMany and update), both writers store the same value and a failure is lost, so a permanently failing reminder can take far more than two attempts to be deleted, or never pass the gt:1 threshold under repeated overlap. Use Prisma's atomic `{ increment: 1 }` instead.

title: Retry-count deletion is not scoped to SMS reminders
body: The deleteMany OR's second branch only checks retryCount > 1, without method: WorkflowMethods.SMS (and without scheduled: false). Because WorkflowReminder rows are shared by EMAIL, SMS and WHATSAPP methods, any non-SMS reminder whose retryCount ever exceeds 1 will be deleted by this SMS cron, losing its referenceId/cancellation handle even though this job never processed it. The SMS-only condition from the original first branch does not carry over to the second OR branch.

title: Missing recipient or empty message never increments retryCount
body: The retry increment only happens inside `if (message?.length && sendTo)` when twilio.scheduleSMS returns falsy, or in the catch block. If sendTo is null/empty (e.g. booking has no smsReminderNumber / step has no sendTo) or the rendered message is empty, neither branch runs: the reminder stays scheduled:false with retryCount 0 and is re-fetched and re-processed on every cron run until its scheduledDate passes. This is one of the permanent-failure modes the PR is meant to bound, so those reminders are still retried indefinitely.

title: Unhandled update in catch block can abort the whole cron run
body: The catch block now awaits prisma.workflowReminder.update without any nested error handling. If that update rejects (e.g. the reminder was deleted by the top-of-run deleteMany of a concurrent invocation, a booking-cancellation cleanup, or a transient DB error - Prisma throws P2025 for a missing record), the exception propagates out of the per-reminder loop, the handler returns 500, and all remaining unscheduled reminders in the batch are never processed in this run. Previously the catch only logged and the loop continued.

title: Retry increment uses stale snapshot instead of atomic increment
body: Both increments write `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value read by the earlier findMany. If two cron invocations (or overlapping executions of the same invocation window) process the same unscheduled reminder concurrently, both read the same count and both write the same count+1, losing an increment; likewise a concurrent successful scheduling can be overwritten in effect because the failure writer does not condition on scheduled:false. This lets a permanently failing reminder be attempted more than the intended two times and makes the >1 deletion threshold unreliable. Use Prisma's atomic `{ increment: 1 }` (ideally guarded by scheduled:false).

title: Unparenthesized OR authorization conditions leak when composed with other WHERE clauses
body: getBaseConditions returns authConditions directly when there are no filter conditions (line 75), and for org/team scopes that condition is built as `(A) OR (B)` without outer parentheses (lines 171-174 and 204-207). A caller composing it as `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND <date/status condition>` gets `(A) OR (B) AND <condition>` because AND binds tighter than OR in SQL, so the first authorization branch ignores the caller's additional condition. The old Prisma WhereInput guaranteed this OR was grouped. The returned fragment should be wrapped, e.g. Prisma.sql`(${authConditions})`, so composition is safe.

title: Public findMany method is removed without migrating any call sites
body: This change deletes InsightsBookingService.findMany, which previously ran bookingTimeStatusDenormalized.findMany with the authorization and filter conditions merged into the caller's where clause, and replaces it with getBaseConditions that only returns a SQL fragment. No caller in this PR is updated to issue its own $queryRaw query, so any existing consumer of findMany breaks (TypeScript compile error / runtime 'findMany is not a function'), and former consumers that passed select/orderBy/etc. lose that behavior entirely. Call sites must be migrated in the same PR or findMany retained on top of the new conditions.

title: ANY(array) authorization branches are never executed against the database
body: The only test that executes SQL against Postgres is the user-scope test at lines 480-491, which exercises `userId = $1 AND teamId IS NULL`. The org and team scopes, which rely on `"teamId" = ANY(${numberArray})` and `"userId" = ANY(${numberArray})` parameter binding, are only asserted by Prisma.Sql object equality (lines 295-343). Object equality cannot detect a Postgres runtime failure or wrong typing when Prisma binds a JavaScript number array to ANY(...), so the highest-risk raw-SQL authorization paths could fail at query time while all tests pass. Add $queryRaw executions for org and team scopes.

title: Caching tests were deleted while the caching behavior remains
body: The PR removes the 'Caching' describe block that verified repeated getAuthorizationConditions()/getFilterConditions() calls return the cached result, but insightsBooking.ts still implements cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions (lines 84-95). There is now no coverage guarding that cache against regressions (e.g. returning stale or uncached conditions), and the deletion is unrelated to the Prisma.sql conversion since the same assertions work with SQL fragments.

title: Public findMany() API is removed without migrating callers
body: The previous public findMany(findManyArgs) method, which callers used to query BookingTimeStatusDenormalized with authorization and filter conditions applied, is deleted and replaced by getBaseConditions(). No call sites are updated in this PR, so any existing consumer of InsightsBookingService.findMany will fail TypeScript compilation / break at runtime. Either keep a compatible findMany wrapper built on the raw conditions or update all callers in the same PR.

title: Caching behavior tests were deleted while caching remains in the service
body: The PR removes the entire 'Caching' describe block that verified repeated getAuthorizationConditions()/getFilterConditions() calls return cached results, but InsightsBookingService still implements cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions. Nothing now guards against regressions such as stale or incorrectly shared Prisma.Sql conditions, despite the conversion changing the cached value type from Prisma where-input objects to Sql objects.

title: Org-scope SQL expectation depends on unspecified database ordering
body: The org-scope test expects teamIds exactly as [org, team, team2, team3] and userIds exactly as [user, user2, user3] inside ANY(...) arrays. The service builds these arrays from findAllByParentId/findAllByTeamIds results, which have no ORDER BY guarantee, so the exact Prisma.sql equality assertion can fail intermittently under a different database return order even though the authorization semantics are unchanged.

title: Public findMany API is removed without migrating any callers
body: This change replaces the service's public findMany(findManyArgs) method with getBaseConditions() and only updates this service and its integration test. Any existing caller that invoked InsightsBookingService.findMany to fetch BookingTimeStatusDenormalized rows will now fail TypeScript compilation/runtime, and no caller in this PR is migrated to construct a $queryRaw query with the returned conditions. Either keep a compatible findMany implemented on top of the raw conditions or update/search for all callers in the same change.

title: Authorization fragments return unparenthesized top-level OR conditions
body: buildOrgAuthorizationCondition (and the team equivalent at line 196-207) returns SQL of the form `(team condition) OR (user condition)` with no outer parentheses, and getFilterConditions likewise returns an unparenthesized `(eventTypeId = ...) OR (eventParentId = ...)` for a single filter. These are public composable fragments; if a caller embeds them as `WHERE ${conditions} AND <date/status predicates>` instead of going through getBaseConditions, SQL AND binds tighter than OR, so the second OR branch escapes the preceding predicates and can return bookings outside the intended date/status/auth-filter window. Wrap each composite condition in outer parentheses at construction so the fragments are safe to compose anywhere.

title: Org/team ANY(array) raw SQL is never actually executed against the database
body: The org and team authorization tests only assert structural equality of Prisma.sql objects (strings/values); the sole test that executes SQL (line 481) uses user scope, whose condition contains no ANY(array) parameter and no OR branch. Whether Prisma/Postgres binds a JavaScript number[] supplied as `= ANY(${teamIds})` / `= ANY(${userIds})` correctly is therefore unverified, even though org/team insights depend entirely on that binding. Extend the $queryRaw integration test to org and team scopes (and to an OR filter combination) so a binding or precedence failure fails the suite instead of shipping silently.

title: Caching behavior tests were deleted while the service still caches conditions
body: The PR removes the entire 'Caching' describe block, but InsightsBookingService still keeps cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions and short-circuits on them (insightsBooking.ts lines 49-50, 83-95). There is now no test that a second call returns the cached Prisma.Sql or that repeated calls do not rebuild/re-query memberships, so a regression in the caching fields (e.g. caching the shared NOTHING_CONDITION result incorrectly across calls) would go undetected. Restore the caching tests adapted to Prisma.sql expectations.

title: Deleting cache does not invalidate connectedCalendars query
body: deleteCacheMutation only shows a toast and calls the optional onSuccess callback. Unlike disconnectMutation (lines 61-64) it never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars, and in SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper onChanged is props.onChanged which may be undefined. After a successful deletion the cached query still contains the old cacheUpdatedAt, so the dropdown continues to show 'Cache Status / Delete cached data' as if the cache still exists until a manual refetch/remount.

title: Cache status includes expired cache entries that will never be served
body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups all CalendarCache rows for the credentials without filtering expiresAt. getCachedAvailability treats rows with expiresAt < now as a cache miss, so connectedCalendars can report cacheUpdatedAt and the UI can offer 'Delete cached data' for a cache that is already expired/dead. The status query should only consider unexpired rows (expiresAt >= now), matching the read path.

title: Authorization failure is thrown as a generic Error instead of a TRPCError
body: When the credential does not belong to the session user the handler throws `new Error('Credential not found or access denied')`. In tRPC this surfaces as an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) rather than a NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN client error, so clients and monitoring treat a routine bad/foreign credentialId as a server failure. Throw a TRPCError with an appropriate code instead, as other viewer handlers do.

title: sed invocation is macOS-only and the script exits 0 on failure
body: `sed -i '' -E ...` uses BSD/macOS syntax; on GNU/Linux sed treats '' as an input file and fails, so GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is never updated while the script continues and prints success. Additionally the failure paths at lines 49 and 58 call cleanup(), which unconditionally `exit 0`, masking rate-limit and tunnel-start failures. Use a portable in-place edit (or OS detection) and exit non-zero on the error paths.

title: dev:cron now depends on unpinned npx-fetched tsx that is not a declared dependency
body: The script was changed from ts-node (a declared devDependency, line 196) to `npx tsx`, but tsx is not declared anywhere in this package's dependencies. Running dev:cron therefore requires a network fetch of an unpinned package on first use, fails offline/in locked-down installs, and is a supply-chain/reproducibility regression unrelated to the calendar-cache feature. Add tsx as a devDependency (pinned by the lockfile) or keep ts-node.

title: Deleting cache does not invalidate the connected-calendars query
body: The deleteCache mutation only shows a toast and calls the optional onSuccess prop. Unlike the disconnect mutation in the same component, it never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. In SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper onSuccess is just the optional onChanged callback, which may be undefined, so after a successful deletion the list keeps its stale cacheUpdatedAt and continues to show 'Delete cached data' with the old timestamp until a manual refetch.

title: Cache status includes expired cache entries
body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups all CalendarCache rows for the credentials without filtering expiresAt >= now. Cached availability is only served when expiresAt is in the future (see getCachedAvailability), so an expired, unusable cache still produces a cacheUpdatedAt, causing the UI to display a cache status and offer deletion for cache that is effectively absent.

title: Authorization failure is thrown as a generic Error instead of a tRPC error
body: When the credential does not belong to the user the handler throws `new Error('Credential not found or access denied')`. tRPC will surface this as an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) rather than a NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN client error, so clients and monitoring cannot distinguish an access/lookup problem from a server failure, and the mutation's error handling behaves accordingly.

title: Cache timestamp is always formatted in en-US
body: The 'last updated' timestamp uses a hardcoded Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', ...) regardless of the user's configured locale from useLocale. Non-English users will see US date/time ordering in an otherwise localized UI.

title: Webhook helper script only works on macOS and masks failures
body: `sed -i '' -E ...` uses BSD/macOS sed syntax; on GNU/Linux sed treats '' as a filename and fails, so the .env update does not work for Linux developers. Additionally, cleanup() always exits 0 and is invoked on failure paths (e.g. when no tunnel URL was extracted), so callers/CI cannot detect that the script failed.

title: dev:cron now depends on undeclared, unpinned tsx fetched via npx
body: The script was changed from ts-node (a declared devDependency) to `npx tsx`, but tsx is not declared in this package's dependencies. Every run may download an unpinned package from the registry, making the local cron workflow non-reproducible, slower, and broken offline; tsx should be added as a pinned devDependency or the declared runner kept.

title: Deleting cache does not invalidate the connected-calendars query
body: The deleteCacheMutation only shows a toast and calls onSuccess, unlike disconnectMutation below it which invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars and viewer.apps.integrations on settle. When onChanged/onSuccess is undefined (or does not refetch), the parent keeps the old query data, so cacheUpdatedAt remains set, the 'Cache Status / Delete cached data' entry stays visible, and the user sees stale status immediately after a successful deletion.

title: Cache status ignores cache expiry
body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups all CalendarCache rows for the credentials with no expiresAt filter, while getCachedAvailability only serves rows with expiresAt >= now. Credentials whose cache expired (one month after write) will therefore still report a cacheUpdatedAt in connectedCalendars, display 'Cache Status' in the UI, and offer to delete data that is never actually served.

title: Handler bypasses the calendar-cache disabled/mock repository path
body: The handler directly instantiates the concrete CalendarCacheRepository instead of going through the CalendarCache initialization that substitutes CalendarCacheRepositoryMock when calendar cache is disabled. Every connectedCalendars request now performs a CalendarCache groupBy query and can surface cache status even for users/organizations where the calendar-cache feature is disabled, adding an unconditional DB query to a hot settings endpoint.

title: Cache timestamp is always formatted in en-US locale
body: The timestamp is formatted with new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', ...) regardless of the user's configured locale obtained via useLocale. Non-English users will see US-style dates (e.g. MM/DD/YYYY) inconsistent with the rest of the localized UI.

title: updateManyByCredentialId accepts the wrong Prisma input type
body: The method types data as Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput but passes it to prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany, which expects SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput. UpdateInput permits nested relation operations (e.g. user: { connect }) that updateMany cannot execute, so the public repository signature promises operations that will fail or fail type-checking at the Prisma call; it should use the UpdateMany mutation input type.

title: sed in-place edit uses macOS-only syntax and breaks on Linux
body: sed -i '' -E ... is BSD/macOS syntax; GNU sed on Linux interprets the empty string as a filename and errors out, so updating an existing GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL in .env fails for Linux developers. Use a portable form (e.g. sed -i.bak and remove the backup, or detect the OS).

title: dev:cron now depends on undeclared, unpinned tsx fetched via npx
body: The script was changed from ts-node (declared in devDependencies) to 'npx tsx', but tsx is not declared in this package's dependencies. On a fresh/offline install npx will try to download an unpinned package from the registry, making the script non-reproducible and failing without network access; tsx should be added as a pinned devDependency or the ts-node invocation kept.

title: New destructive deleteCache mutation has no tests
body: This PR adds a mutation that deletes all CalendarCache rows for a credential, guarded only by the credential-ownership check in this new handler, plus the new getCacheStatusByCredentialIds repository method, with no tests covering: deleting one's own cache, rejecting another user's credentialId, and returning cache status per credential. A regression in the ownership where-clause would let one user purge another user's calendar cache without any test failing.

title: One failing SendGrid cancellation blocks all other cancellations
body: The whole cancellation loop is wrapped in a single try/catch and every SendGrid request is awaited inside the loop. If one request fails (e.g. an invalid/empty batch_id for a reminder that was marked scheduled without an actual mail, a SendGrid 400, or a transient error), execution jumps to the catch, the queued Prisma deletes in workflowRemindersToDelete are never awaited/executed, and none of the remaining reminders in remindersToCancel are cancelled. The same failing reminder is returned by findMany on every subsequent cron run, so it can permanently poison the batch and cancelled emails for other bookings continue to be sent. Each reminder should be cancelled/deleted in its own try/catch.

title: Reschedule path bypasses the deferred-cancellation fix and leaks the reminder row
body: For a rescheduled booking this calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true). With immediateDelete=true that function (emailReminderManager.ts lines 213-223) immediately POSTs a SendGrid 'cancel' for the batch and returns without deleting the WorkflowReminder row and without setting cancelled=true. This is exactly the immediate-cancellation behaviour the PR description says stopped working once SendGrid accumulated 100 pending cancellations, so mass reschedules can still fail to cancel and the old reminder email is still sent; additionally the stale row remains scheduled=true in the DB until its scheduledDate passes. The reschedule path should use the same deferred cancelled=true mechanism as the cancel path.

title: Reminder cancellations are fired without await, racing the cron scheduler
body: updatedBookings.forEach(...) calls the now-async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder but discards the returned promises; the handler then only awaits attendeeDeletes/bookingReferenceDeletes/apiDeletes and returns success. The cancelled=true update (or row delete for unscheduled reminders) may therefore not have completed when the response returns, and the scheduleEmailReminders cron running concurrently can pick up a still-scheduled:false, not-yet-cancelled reminder, schedule it with SendGrid, and afterwards the late delete-by-id (referenceId read as null) removes the DB row while the newly created SendGrid batch is never recorded or cancelled, so the reminder is sent for a cancelled booking. The same un-awaited forEach pattern is used in handleNewBooking.ts line 966 and trpc bookings.tsx line 488. These promises need to be collected and awaited.

title: Reminders cancelled shortly before send time can still be delivered between cron runs
body: Cancellation now only takes effect when this cron next runs and finds cancelled=true with scheduledDate <= now+1h. If a booking is cancelled after the last cron run before the reminder's scheduledDate (the PR description states the cron runs every 15 minutes), SendGrid delivers the email at scheduledDate before any subsequent cron invocation can POST the cancel. The previous code cancelled the batch synchronously at booking-cancellation time; the new design reintroduces a send window for all cancellations made within one cron interval of the send time, so 'cancelled booking' reminders will still occasionally be sent. An immediate cancel is needed for reminders whose scheduledDate is before the next expected cron run.

title: One failed SendGrid cancellation aborts cancellation and deletion of all other reminders
body: The whole cancellation loop is wrapped in a single try/catch and the Prisma deletes are only executed with Promise.all after the loop finishes. If client.request fails for any reminder (e.g. a null/already-sent/already-cancelled referenceId), the loop aborts, the already-collected workflowRemindersToDelete are never executed, and no later reminders in remindersToCancel are cancelled at SendGrid. Those emails can still be sent, and the poison reminder will block the batch again on every subsequent cron run.

title: immediateDelete cancels at SendGrid but leaves the reminder row active in the database
body: When immediateDelete is true the function POSTs the SendGrid cancel and returns without deleting the WorkflowReminder row or setting cancelled=true. Callers such as the reschedule path in handleNewBooking therefore leave the old reminder scheduled:true/cancelled unset, so the new deferred cron mechanism in scheduleEmailReminders (which only acts on cancelled=true rows) will never retry it. If that single immediate SendGrid cancel fails or hits the 100 pending-cancellations limit described in the PR, the old reminder email is still sent for the rescheduled booking.

title: Reminder cancellations are fired without await before the handler completes
body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are async (they update/delete the WorkflowReminder row and, for SMS, call Twilio), but they are invoked inside forEach callbacks whose promises are discarded and are not included in the subsequent Promise.all. The handler can return (and in a serverless environment the invocation can be frozen/terminated) before cancelled=true is persisted, so the cron job that now depends on that flag may never see the cancellation and the scheduled email is sent for the cancelled booking. The same un-awaited pattern is used for the new cancellation calls in handleNewBooking and the bookings/workflows tRPC routers.

title: Cancellation query does not restrict to scheduled email reminders with a referenceId
body: remindersToCancel matches any WorkflowReminder with cancelled=true and scheduledDate <= now+1h, with no method=EMAIL, scheduled=true, or referenceId-not-null filter. Any cancelled row without a SendGrid batch id (or a non-email row) is passed to SendGrid as batch_id: null, which will error; combined with the single try/catch around the loop this prevents cancellation/deletion of all valid reminders in the same run.

title: One failed SendGrid cancellation blocks all remaining cancellations in the cron run
body: The loop over remindersToCancel awaits client.request inside a single try/catch that wraps the whole loop, and the Prisma deletes are only executed after the loop finishes. If cancelling any one reminder fails (e.g. SendGrid error or a stale/null referenceId), the catch aborts the loop: every later reminder is never attempted, and even reminders already cancelled at SendGrid are not deleted from the DB in this run. Worse, the failing reminder stays first in the result set on subsequent runs, so it can poison every 15-minute cron invocation and workflow emails for cancelled/rescheduled bookings keep being sent. Each reminder's cancellation and deletion should be isolated in its own try/catch.

title: Rescheduled bookings still use immediate SendGrid cancellation, defeating the deferred-cancellation fix
body: For a reschedule, deleteScheduledEmailReminder is called with immediateDelete=true, which immediately POSTs status=cancel to SendGrid. Per the PR description, cancelled scheduled sends accumulate in SendGrid's scheduled_sends (capped at 100 pending cancellations) until their scheduled date, and once that cap is hit further cancellations fail and the old email is still sent. Reschedules therefore remain subject to exactly the bug this PR claims to fix for rescheduled bookings; they should be marked cancelled=true and left for the scheduleEmailReminders cron to cancel within the last hour, like the cancellation paths do.

title: immediateDelete path leaves the WorkflowReminder row neither deleted nor marked cancelled
body: When immediateDelete is true and a referenceId exists, the function cancels the send at SendGrid and returns without deleting the workflowReminder row or setting cancelled=true. Callers that do not subsequently cascade-delete the row (notably handleNewBooking's reschedule path, where the old booking and its reminders persist) leave a row with scheduled=true pointing at an already-cancelled batch. The stale row is only cleaned up by the cron's past-scheduledDate sweep, and any logic that later iterates the old booking's workflowReminders will try to cancel the same batch again.

title: Workflow reminder cancellations are fired without being awaited
body: updatedBookings.forEach calls the async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder without awaiting or collecting the promises (the same pattern is used in handleNewBooking's reschedule block, where the surrounding try/catch cannot catch async rejections either). The handler can return 'Booking successfully cancelled' before the cancelled=true update (or SMS cancellation/row deletion) has actually been persisted; if the serverless invocation is torn down after the response, the flag is never written and the scheduled reminder email is still sent for the cancelled booking. The cancellation promises should be collected and awaited (e.g. Promise.all over flatMap).

title: Dynamic imports are eagerly executed for every app
body: All `import(...)` expressions are evaluated immediately when the `appStore` object literal is constructed, so importing `appStore` starts loading all 29 app modules regardless of which app is actually needed. This defeats the stated lazy/async-import purpose, retains the startup/bundle-loading cost for every consumer, and creates promises for unused apps whose rejection (e.g. a broken optional app) would be an unhandled rejection since nothing ever awaits that entry. Imports should only be initiated on access, e.g. via factory functions `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")` with callers awaiting the factory.

title: Calendar/video deletions are fire-and-forget and outside the try/catch
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` discards the promises returned by the async callback. The surrounding try/catch (lines 124-139) therefore cannot catch errors from `await getCalendar(...)` or `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting`, and `Reschedule` can return and send the reschedule email before the old calendar/video events are deleted, leaving orphaned events; on serverless runtimes the deletions may never run at all. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` inside the try.

title: Calendar/video deletions are fire-and-forget and outside the try/catch
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` discards the promises returned by the async callback. The surrounding try/catch (lines 124-139) therefore cannot catch errors from `await getCalendar(...)` or `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting`, and `Reschedule` can return and send the reschedule email before the old calendar/video events are deleted, leaving orphaned events; on serverless runtimes the deletions may never run at all. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` inside the try.

title: requestReschedule deletions are not awaited before mutation completes
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); })` discards all returned promises. The mutation proceeds immediately to send the reschedule email and webhooks and returns while deletions are still pending (and any failure becomes an unhandled rejection), so the old calendar/video event can survive a successful reschedule response. Replace with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))`.

title: Recurring-booking calendar deletions race with apiDeletes consumption
body: In the recurring-cancellation branch, deletions are pushed into `apiDeletes` from inside a `.forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })` callback. Because `getCalendar` is now async, none of these pushes happen synchronously, so the later `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` at line 652 (and the `await apiDeletes` at line 617) typically snapshot an empty/incomplete array. The handler can finish and the process can terminate before the external calendar events are deleted. Await the per-credential work with `Promise.all`/`for...of` and push the deletion promises before they are consumed.

title: Dynamic imports are still eagerly started for every app
body: The object literal evaluates all 30 `import(...)` calls as soon as `@calcom/app-store` is imported, so every consumer still loads/parses every app module (just asynchronously and concurrently) instead of lazily loading only the requested app. This defeats the purpose of the PR, adds startup/bundle-fetch cost to every route importing appStore, and means a failing chunk/module for an unused app creates a cached rejected promise that can surface as an unhandled rejection. Store thunks such as `() => import(...)` and update callers to invoke them, or otherwise only start the import on lookup.

title: Reschedule deletions are fired with async forEach and never awaited
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` returns immediately, so `Reschedule` proceeds to send the reschedule email and returns `true` before `getCalendar`/`calendar.deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` finish; on serverless the process may be frozen before deletion completes, leaving the old calendar/video event alive. The surrounding try/catch also cannot catch rejections from the async callbacks. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` (with per-item error handling) before returning.

title: Reschedule deletions are fired with async forEach and never awaited
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` returns immediately, so `Reschedule` proceeds to send the reschedule email and returns `true` before `getCalendar`/`calendar.deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` finish; on serverless the process may be frozen before deletion completes, leaving the old calendar/video event alive. The surrounding try/catch also cannot catch rejections from the async callbacks. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` (with per-item error handling) before returning.

title: requestReschedule does not await calendar/video deletions
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); })` discards the promises, so the mutation sends the reschedule email/webhooks and completes while deletions are still pending (and any rejection is unhandled). The old calendar/video event can therefore survive a booking already marked CANCELLED/rescheduled. Replace with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` and handle errors explicitly.

title: Recurring-booking calendar deletions race the final Promise.all
body: In the recurring-cancellation branch, credentials are iterated with `.forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... const deletedEvent = await calendar?.deleteEvent(...); apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })`. Because of the new `await getCalendar`, `apiDeletes.push` happens asynchronously after the handler reaches `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` at line 652, so `apiDeletes` is snapshotted (likely empty/partial) and the external calendar deletions are neither awaited nor error-handled before attendees/references are deleted and the success response is returned. Use `for...of` or collect `Promise.all` over credentials/bookings and push the delete promises synchronously.

title: getVideoAdapters now loads credential apps sequentially
body: The `for (const cred of withCredentials) { const app = await appStore[...]; ... }` loop serializes dynamic-import resolution per credential, whereas the previous synchronous reduce had no such latency; for users with several video credentials `getBusyVideoTimes`/`createMeeting` fallbacks pay the sum of import latencies. Map credentials to promises and `await Promise.all(...)` (preserving order) instead.

title: Dynamic imports are eagerly started, not lazy
body: Every value is an already-executed import() call in the object literal, so importing appStore immediately initiates loading all ~30 app modules instead of loading only the requested app on first use. This defeats the stated purpose of the PR and keeps the startup/bundle-evaluation cost (and side effects) of every app for any caller that needs just one. The promises should be wrapped in thunks, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, with callers invoking them. A related consequence is that a failing optional app creates a rejected promise at import time that may surface as an unhandled rejection even if that app is never used.

title: Recurring-booking calendar deletions race with Promise.all(apiDeletes)
body: The recurring-cancellation branch uses `.forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })`. The async callback suspends at the await, so execution reaches `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` (and the success response) before the pushes happen. Previously getCalendar was synchronous and the pushes happened during forEach. Now calendar deleteEvent calls for recurring bookings are typically never awaited and may not even have started when the handler returns, leaving events on external calendars; errors from them are also unhandled.

title: Async forEach makes calendar/video cancellation fire-and-forget and bypasses try/catch
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); })` is never awaited: forEach ignores the returned promises, and the surrounding try/catch cannot catch rejections from the async callback. Reschedule() proceeds to send the reschedule email and return true before (and regardless of whether) the old calendar/video events are deleted, so failures are silently lost as unhandled rejections and stale events can remain. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` inside the try block.

title: Async forEach makes calendar/video cancellation fire-and-forget and bypasses try/catch
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); })` is never awaited: forEach ignores the returned promises, and the surrounding try/catch cannot catch rejections from the async callback. Reschedule() proceeds to send the reschedule email and return true before (and regardless of whether) the old calendar/video events are deleted, so failures are silently lost as unhandled rejections and stale events can remain. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` inside the try block.

title: requestReschedule does not await async calendar/video deletions
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); })` discards the promises returned by the async callback. The mutation immediately sends the reschedule email and webhooks and returns, so the previous calendar/video events may still exist (or fail silently as unhandled rejections) when the user reschedules via the emailed link. Await the deletions, e.g. with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))`, before proceeding.

title: Slots inside a date override bypass busy-time checks
body: When a slot is on a date-override day and inside the override window, the find callback returns nothing, dateOverrideExist is true, and checkIfIsAvailable returns true at line 134 without reaching the busy.every() check at the bottom. A fixed or round-robin host can therefore be shown/booked during a date-override slot even when they have an accepted Cal booking or a busy calendar event overlapping that slot.

title: Working-hours check rejects slots covered by any non-first range and uses wrong end/day
body: This block returns unavailable if ANY workingHour entry for that weekday does not contain the slot (find on start<startTime||end>endTime), instead of checking whether NO entry contains it. Users with split/multiple ranges on the same day will lose slots covered by a later range. Additionally end at line 142 is copied from slotStartTime rather than slotEndTime, so a slot starting inside working hours but ending after endTime passes, and both day()/hour() are taken from the UTC slot time while WorkingHours days/startTime/endTime are expressed in the organizer's schedule timezone, so non-UTC hosts are compared on the wrong day and hour.

title: Empty date-override comparison uses object identity and never matches
body: dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...) compares two distinct Dayjs objects with ===, which is always false, so the intended zero-length override (whole day unavailable) branch is dead. A slot that straddles the equal start/end instant then falls through both boundary checks, sets dateOverrideExist, and is returned as available instead of unavailable.

title: Date override shifted across midnight is truncated/wrong-day
body: startTime/endTime are derived only from hour()*60+minute() after adding the invitee-organizer offset. If the offset pushes the override across midnight (common when organizer and invitee are on opposite sides of the date line), endTime can become smaller than startTime or both wrap to the next day's clock time while activeOverrides still matched the override against the unshifted invitee day at line 207. buildSlots discards start>=end boundaries, so such overrides disappear or appear on the wrong day.

title: No test for the round-robin fixed-host date-override fix
body: The PR description claims fixed hosts' date overrides are now honoured for round-robin events, but the only added test re-queries the existing personal-event date-override scenario in Asia/Dhaka and expects identical UTC slots. There is no scenario with schedulingType ROUND_ROBIN, a fixed host with an override, and a loose host, nor a case where the fixed host's calendar/booking conflicts inside the override, so the new checkIfIsAvailable filtering for fixed/loose hosts is untested and the busy-bypass regression above would not be caught.

title: Date-override path bypasses busy/booking check
body: When dateOverrideExist is true and the slot is inside the override, checkIfIsAvailable returns true immediately at lines 133-135 without reaching the busy.every() check at line 153. Therefore a fixed or round-robin host who has a Cal booking or external-calendar busy event overlapping a date-override slot will still be reported available for that slot, allowing double-bookings on override days.

title: Empty (unavailable-day) override comparison is always false
body: dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...) compares two distinct Dayjs objects by reference, so it is always false. The intended detection of a zero-length override (the representation of a day marked unavailable) never fires; a slot straddling that instant then finds no exclusion, sets dateOverrideExist, and is returned as available instead of unavailable.

title: Slot starting exactly at override end is treated as inside override
body: The exclusion for slots after the override uses slotStartTime.isAfter(overrideEnd) only. A slot starting exactly at overrideEnd is not after it, its slotEnd is also not before/equal overrideStart, so find() returns falsy, dateOverrideExist remains true, and the slot is returned available even though it starts at the moment the override window closes. It should be isSameOrAfter the end.

title: Working-hours check breaks split hours and never checks slot end
body: Lines 140-146 set both start and end to the slot-start minutes, so a slot starting inside working hours but ending after endTime (eventLength beyond the window) is accepted. Also, find() returns true if ANY workingHour entry for that weekday excludes the slot: with split hours such as 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00, a 10:00 slot matches the second entry (10:00 < 13:00) and is rejected. Since getSlots already aggregates availability, this new second filter will incorrectly remove valid slots for users with multiple intervals on a day and keep slots that overrun the window.

title: Override conversion fails/wraps when shifted time crosses midnight
body: Lines 218-223 reduce the shifted override start/end to hour*60+minute within a single invitee day. If applying inviteeUtcOffset-organizerUtcOffset pushes the override end past midnight (or start before midnight), endTime becomes smaller than startTime or belongs to the adjacent day; buildSlots skips start>=end ranges and drops/ truncates those slots. This reintroduces the timezone bug for overrides near day boundaries in far-apart timezones, the exact scenario the PR claims to fix.

title: No test for fixed-host date override in round-robin events
body: The PR description says the primary fix is that a fixed host's date override restricts round-robin availability, but the only added test (lines 788-804) repeats the existing single-user date-override scenario in Asia/Dhaka timezone. There is no round-robin/collective scenario with a fixed host having an override and a loose host available, so the new checkIfIsAvailable fixed/loose-host filtering added in slots.ts is untested and regressions would not be caught.

title: Date-override slots bypass busy-time checks
body: When a slot's date matches a date override, checkIfIsAvailable sets dateOverrideExist and returns true at lines 133-135 before reaching the busy.every() check at line 153. Therefore a fixed (or round-robin) host who has a calendar/Cal booking overlapping a slot on an override day is reported available for that slot, so overlapping bookings can be created precisely on override days.

title: Empty (unavailable-day) override check compares Dayjs objects with ===
body: dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...) compares two distinct Dayjs object references, so it is always false. An override with start == end, used to mark a whole day unavailable, is therefore never detected as such; slots at/after that instant fall through, have dateOverrideExist=true, and are returned as available instead of being blocked for the day.

title: Working-hours check rejects slots covered by any one of multiple ranges and ignores slot end
body: The code uses find() for any workingHour on that weekday where the slot start is before its startTime or after its endTime, and sets both start and end from the slot start (lines 141-142, so eventLength is never checked). With split availability on one day (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00) a 09:00 slot matches the second range as 'outside' and is rejected, while a slot starting inside a range but ending after it ends is accepted. This breaks fixed-host filtering for users with split or multiple same-day ranges.

title: Override conversion assumes timeZone is present and loses day-boundary crossing
body: TimeRange.timeZone is optional (added as timeZone? in schedule.d.ts) and other getSlots callers need not supply it, yet lines 212-213 unconditionally call .tz(override.timeZone); with undefined this does not give the organizer offset. Additionally lines 218-223 reduce the shifted start/end to hour*60+minute, discarding the date: an override shifted by the invitee/organizer offset across midnight produces endTime <= startTime (or a time belonging to the adjacent invitee day), which buildSlots discards via start >= end, so those override slots disappear instead of appearing on the correct day.

title: No test for the round-robin fixed-host override fix
body: The PR description claims fixed hosts' date overrides are now honoured for round-robin events, but the only added test (lines 788-804) re-queries the existing single-user date-override scenario in Asia/Dhaka and asserts identical UTC slots. There is no scenario with schedulingType ROUND_ROBIN, a fixed host with an override and a non-fixed host, nor an unavailable/empty override or a busy time on an override day, so the new checkIfIsAvailable filtering path for fixed hosts is untested and regressions in it would not be caught.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category site setting is absent
body: Site settings are only persisted in site_settings when overridden, so most installs have no 'embed_category' row. `execute(...)[0]` is then nil and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration (and deployment). The fallback on line 15 has the same problem for 'uncategorized_category_id'. The lookups must handle an empty result set.

title: Migration interpolates stored host values directly into SQL and stores them unnormalized
body: Each legacy host string `h` is interpolated unescaped into the INSERT statement, so a host value containing a single quote breaks the migration and is a SQL-injection vector. Additionally the raw legacy values (which per the old specs may be like 'http://discourse.org' or 'https://example.com/1234') are inserted verbatim, bypassing EmbeddableHost's scheme/path stripping; EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares lower(host) against the bare URI host, so such migrated rows will never match and embedding for those sites silently breaks after upgrade.

title: before_validation crashes on a nil host instead of failing validation
body: `self.host.sub!(...)` raises NoMethodError when host is nil, e.g. an admin POSTs an embeddable_host with a blank/missing host field from Admin::EmbeddableHostsController. Instead of a 422 validation error via render_json_error, the request 500s. Guard against nil (or use non-mutating sub with to_s) and add a presence validation.

title: update/destroy raise NoMethodError for a nonexistent host id
body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for an unknown id, and both update (via save_host calling host.host=) and destroy (line 16, host.destroy) then raise NoMethodError, producing a 500 instead of a 404. This is reachable with a stale admin page after a host was deleted in another tab.

title: edit action crashes when the host has no resolvable category
body: `this.get('host.category.id')` throws if host.category is undefined. That happens for a host whose category was deleted, and also after save() sets `host.category` to Discourse.Category.findById(categoryId) which is undefined when no category was chosen (the server silently substitutes the uncategorized category, which the client does not mirror). Clicking Edit then breaks the admin page; use a safe get (host.category && host.category.id) and sync the category returned by the server.

title: No uniqueness constraint on host allows duplicate hosts with conflicting categories
body: There is no uniqueness validation on host and the migration creates no unique index. Admins can create two rows for the same host pointing at different categories; record_for_host then returns whichever row the database happens to return first, so embedded topics are filed into an unpredictable category and host_allowed?/category selection becomes nondeterministic.

title: Fabricator file contents are swapped between the two fabricator files
body: category_fabricator.rb now defines only Fabricator(:embeddable_host), while the new embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines :category, :diff_category, :happy_category and :private_category. Fabrication loads every file so tests still pass, but the swapped names are misleading and invite a future duplicate-definition error when someone adds a fabricator to the file matching its name.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category setting or category is absent
body: The migration unconditionally dereferences execute(...)[0]['id'] and, on line 15, execute(...)[0]['value']. On a fresh install or any site that never saved embed_category/uncategorized_category_id in site_settings, [0] is nil, so the migration raises NoMethodError and cannot complete, blocking deployment/upgrades.

title: Migration inserts legacy hosts verbatim without normalization and via string interpolation
body: Legacy SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts values could contain values such as 'http://discourse.org' or 'https://example.com/1234' (as existing specs used). This raw INSERT stores them verbatim, bypassing EmbeddableHost's before_validation stripping of scheme/path, so record_for_host (which compares against URI#host) will never match those migrated rows and embedding silently breaks for them. Interpolating h directly into SQL also breaks on quotes and allows SQL injection through a crafted setting value.

title: before_validation crashes on nil host
body: self.host.sub! is called unconditionally. Creating an EmbeddableHost with no host (e.g. an admin API POST missing embeddable_host[host], or EmbeddableHost.new.valid?) raises NoMethodError for nil instead of failing validates_format_of gracefully with a validation error the controller can render.

title: Update/destroy of nonexistent host raises NoMethodError instead of 404
body: update looks up EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and passes it to save_host, and destroy (line 15-16) calls host.destroy, without checking for nil. A stale UI row or a request with a bad id therefore returns a 500 NoMethodError rather than a handled not-found/error response.

title: No uniqueness validation on host makes category selection nondeterministic
body: host has no uniqueness validation (and the migration creates no unique index).
