Admins can create two rows for the same hostname with different categories; record_for_host then uses .first with no ordering, so TopicEmbed.import can arbitrarily pick either category_id for new embedded topics depending on database return order.

title: Plural embedded hydration inserts undefined entries and drops unmatched ids
body: In the new _ids branch, obj[k].map returns whatever _lookupSubType returns, which is undefined when the subtype collection is absent from the payload root or the id is not in it (e.g. the special-cased category lookup returning undefined). The resulting plural array contains undefined elements (later code expecting models will fail), and unlike the singular branch it deletes obj[k] unconditionally (line 201), discarding the original ids even when nothing was hydrated.

title: Edit action crashes for hosts without a category
body: edit() does this.get('host.category.id') with no guard. A host whose category was deleted (belongs_to does not prevent orphan category_id, and category_id can also be hydrated as undefined by the store) has category == null/undefined, so clicking Edit throws a TypeError and the row can never be edited or fixed in the UI.

title: Category and embeddable_host fabricators are placed in each other's files
body: category_fabricator.rb now defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host) while the new embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines :category, :diff_category, :happy_category and :private_category. Tests still pass because all fabricator files are loaded, but maintainers editing or selectively loading the conventionally named file will modify/load the wrong definitions.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category or uncategorized setting rows are absent
body: The migration does execute(...)[0]['id'] and execute(...)[0]['value'] without checking for an empty result. On a fresh install or any site that never saved embed_category/uncategorized_category_id in site_settings, [0] is nil and nil['id'] raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration and blocking deployment/upgrades.

title: Migration inserts un-normalized hosts via unsanitized raw SQL
body: Legacy embeddable_hosts values such as 'http://discourse.org' or 'https://example.com/1234' are interpolated directly into INSERT without the protocol/path stripping performed by EmbeddableHost.before_validation and without SQL escaping. The stored host therefore will not match EmbeddableHost.record_for_host, which compares lower(host) to the bare URI hostname, so migrated sites silently lose embed access; a value containing a single quote also breaks or injects into the INSERT.

title: before_validation crashes on a nil host instead of returning a validation error
body: self.host.sub! is called unconditionally in before_validation. Creating an EmbeddableHost with a blank/missing host (reachable from Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#create when the admin submits an empty host) raises NoMethodError on nil instead of failing validates_format_of and rendering a JSON error, producing a 500.

title: Update/destroy crash with 500 for a non-existent host id
body: update and destroy use EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first, which returns nil for a stale or invalid id, then call save_host(nil)/nil.destroy. This raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a 404/not-found response, e.g. when two admins delete/edit the same host concurrently.

title: Edit action crashes when a host has no resolvable category
body: edit() does this.get('host.category.id') without a guard. If the host's category_id points to a deleted category or the category is not present in the client-side category list, host.category is undefined and clicking Edit throws a TypeError, making that host uneditable in the admin UI.

title: Plural embedded hydration inserts undefined entries and discards the ids
body: For *_ids fields, _hydrateEmbedded maps each id through _lookupSubType and unconditionally deletes the original obj[k]. When the referenced collection is not present in the payload root (or a category is not loaded), _lookupSubType returns undefined, so the model gets an array containing undefined instead of the objects/ids, and the source ids are lost. The singular branch preserves the id when hydration fails; the plural branch does not.

title: Category and embeddable_host fabricators were swapped into each other's files
body: category_fabricator.rb now contains only Fabricator(:embeddable_host), while embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains all the :category/:diff_category/:happy_category/:private_category fabricators. Fabrication loads by scanning files so tests may still pass, but the misplacement makes the fabricators hard to find and risks duplicate-definition or missing-definition errors if either file is later edited, moved, or selectively loaded.

title: Second downsize definition silently overrides the existing width/height API
body: Lines 145-151 define OptimizedImage.downsize twice: first as downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) and then as downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}). In Ruby the second definition replaces the first, so any existing caller using the four-argument width/height form will now either raise ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments) or have its max_width value interpreted as a complete dimensions string. This is an API/contract break for other thumbnail/downsize callers, not just the new uploads-controller caller.

title: Percentage downsizing is incompatible with the animated-GIF instructions
body: The new upload path passes dimensions "80%" with allow_animation taken from SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails. When that setting is true and the file is a GIF, optimize() dispatches to downsize_instructions_animated, which forwards "80%" to resize_instructions_animated as the argument to gifsicle's --resize-fit. --resize-fit expects a WxH geometry, not a percentage scale (gifsicle uses a different option for scaling), so animated GIF downsizing will fail; convert_with returns false, the controller ignores that result, retries the same failing command up to five times, and then proceeds with the still-oversized file.

title: Downsize result is ignored and the loop neither guarantees nor verifies the size limit
body: The while loop at lines 66-69 calls OptimizedImage.downsize up to five times but discards its boolean return value and performs no check after the loop. If conversion fails, produces a larger file (possible when re-encoding formats such as PNG without a quality/compression change in downsize_instructions), or five 80% reductions are still not enough to get under SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, create_upload silently continues to Upload.create_for with an oversized/corrupt intermediate file. The feature therefore either fails later with the old size error after expensive retries or stores an upload that does not satisfy the stated invariant.

title: In-place conversion uses the same path for input and output
body: OptimizedImage.downsize is called with tempfile.path as both source and destination. The downsize instructions run ImageMagick `convert <file>[0] ... <file>` (and for animated images gifsicle with --output set to the input file), rather than converting to a separate temporary file and atomically replacing the original only on success. Tools that truncate/create the output before fully consuming the input, or that fail part-way, can leave the user's only uploaded copy truncated or corrupted; because the return value is ignored and ensure only closes the tempfile, the corrupted file is then passed to Upload.create_for instead of preserving the original upload.

title: Hardcoded 10 MB client limit ignores configured image and attachment limits
body: validateUploadedFile previously used Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], which distinguishes images from attachments and respects admin configuration; it now always allows 10 * 1024 KB. If an admin configures a lower limit, the client will accept and upload files the server then rejects (the server-side downsizing only applies to images, so oversized attachments are uploaded in full just to fail), and if an admin configures a higher limit, the client incorrectly blocks valid uploads. The hardcoded value also makes the file_too_large message report 10240 KB regardless of the actual configured limit.

title: 413 error handler reports a fabricated 10 MB maximum
body: In displayErrorForUpload's 413 branch, the message previously used Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb and now always interpolates 10 * 1024 KB as max_size_kb. A 413 is generated by the web server/proxy limit, which is unrelated to this constant, so users will be told the limit is 10 MB even when the proxy or site setting allows far less or more, sending them to retry with files that will continue to fail.

title: Second downsize definition overwrites the existing four-argument method
body: Ruby does not support method overloading. Defining self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) at line 149 replaces the self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) defined at line 145. Existing callers that pass separate width and height will now raise ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments), breaking thumbnail/image downsizing outside this new upload path. The two signatures must be merged into one method that accepts either a dimension string or width/height.

title: Downsizing uses an extensionless tempfile path, so ImageMagick cannot infer formats and animation is lost
body: The uploaded/downloaded tempfile paths (file.tempfile and FileHelper.download's tempfile) normally have no image extension. OptimizedImage.downsize passes tempfile.path as both input and output to `convert`, so ImageMagick cannot infer the output format from the destination extension and conversion can fail. In addition, OptimizedImage.optimize only selects the animated instructions when the source path ends in .GIF, which an extensionless tempfile never does, so downsize_instructions uses `#{from}[0]` and reduces an animated GIF to its first frame despite passing allow_animation. The image should be downsized via a temp file carrying the original extension (and a separate output path) before replacing the upload.

title: Downsize loop ignores failure and never verifies the result is within the limit
body: The loop ignores OptimizedImage.downsize's boolean return value and, after at most five 80% reductions, unconditionally proceeds to Upload.create_for. If conversion fails (unsupported/corrupt/SVG image) it pointlessly retries five times on the same in-place file, which may have been truncated by the failed convert, and if five reductions still leave the file larger than max_image_size_kb.kilobytes the oversized upload is passed on anyway to be rejected (or stored over the limit). The code should abort/retry sensibly on failure and check the final size before creating the upload.

title: Hardcoded 10MB client limit ignores per-type site settings
body: validateUploadedFile previously used Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so images and attachments each honored the admin-configured limit. Replacing it with a fixed 10MB means sites with a lower max_attachment_size_kb/max_image_size_kb let users select files the server will reject, and sites configured above 10MB incorrectly block allowed files with a 'file too large' alert citing 10240 KB. The same hardcoded value at line 246 makes the 413 error message state the wrong configured maximum. The client limit needs to remain setting/type-aware (at minimum, the raised cap should apply only where the server actually downsizes, i.e. images).

title: Remote-download cap hardcoded to 10MB bypasses the configured image limit for non-image/API cases
body: FileHelper.download now always allows 10 megabytes instead of SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes. The compensating downsize loop only runs when FileHelper.is_image?(filename) is true, so any API URL fetch whose filename is not recognized as an image (or whose image later fails to downsize below the limit) can now pull and store a file up to 10MB regardless of the admin's configured maximum. The raised download cap should be conditional on the file actually being a downsizable image, with the configured limit retained otherwise.

title: Second `downsize` definition silently overwrites the first in Ruby
body: Ruby does not support method overloading: defining `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 replaces the `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` defined at line 145. Any existing caller passing separate width and height (5 positional arguments including opts) will now raise ArgumentError, breaking thumbnail/downsize paths that use the old signature. The two signatures must be merged into one method that handles both forms.

title: Animated downsize passes a percentage to gifsicle as WxH dimensions
body: `downsize_instructions_animated` delegates to `resize_instructions_animated`, which passes `dimensions` to `gifsicle --resize-fit`. The new caller in UploadsController passes `"80%"`, but gifsicle expects a `WIDTHxHEIGHT` geometry, not a percentage, so animated GIFs that exceed the size limit will fail to be downsized (or error out) while the upload loop keeps retrying, and the oversized GIF is ultimately rejected or stored unshrunk.

title: Downsize loop ignores failure and proceeds with an oversized upload
body: The loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize` up to 5 times but never checks its boolean return value and never verifies the result after the loop. If `convert` fails (unsupported format such as SVG, corrupt image, missing tool) or 5 reductions of 20% are not enough, execution falls through to `Upload.create_for` with the still-oversized tempfile, producing an opaque validation failure instead of a meaningful error, after wasting up to 5 external-process invocations.

title: In-place ImageMagick conversion reads and writes the same file
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` runs `convert <path>[0] ... <same path>`. ImageMagick is not guaranteed to handle in-place conversion safely: the output file can be truncated/created before the input is fully read, corrupting the upload (especially on failure mid-write, the original tempfile is destroyed). Convert to a separate temp file and atomically replace the original only on success.

title: Hardcoded 10 MB client limit ignores configured per-type size settings
body: Replacing `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` with a constant `10 * 1024` breaks the admin-configured contract for both images and attachments: sites that lowered `max_image_size_kb`/`max_attachment_size_kb` will now accept files client-side that the server/model then rejects (or expensively downsizes), and sites that raised the limit above 10 MB will have valid uploads blocked client-side. The same regression is repeated for the 413 handler at line 246, which also now always reports 10 MB even for attachment uploads.

title: Hardcoded 10 MB remote-download and unbounded direct-upload downsizing invite resource exhaustion
body: The API URL branch now always downloads up to 10 megabytes regardless of `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, and the new downsize block runs ImageMagick (up to 5 passes) on any image tempfile above the limit with no upper bound on its incoming size. A user can supply a very large/high-resolution image (within the web server's body limit) and force repeated decompression/conversion of it in the deferred job, consuming disproportionate CPU/memory; previously the download was capped at the configured image limit and oversized files were rejected cheaply by validation.

title: Unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser row
body: TopicUser.find_by can return nil for a logged-in user who has never visited, posted in, or otherwise interacted with the topic (for example, opening the unsubscribe URL directly or after the row was removed). The next line calls tu.notification_level on nil, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 instead of unsubscribing. The action should create/update the record through the existing TopicUser.change mechanism (as set_notifications does) so a missing row is created with the muted/regular level.

title: State-changing unsubscribe is performed by a plain GET request
body: The new server route is GET t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe and this action immediately mutates notification_level and saves it. Email security scanners, link prefetchers, browser pre-rendering, or a third party tricking a logged-in user into loading the URL (CSRF via GET, which Rails forgery protection does not cover) will unsubscribe/mute the user without any intentional click or confirmation. The GET should only render a confirmation page and the mutation should require a non-GET request, as the Ember notification dropdown already can perform.

title: Direct TopicUser save bypasses notification-change bookkeeping and leaves stale state
body: Mutating tu.notification_level and calling tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change, which is the established path used by set_notifications: it stamps notifications_changed_at, sets notifications_reason_id to user_changed, runs observe_after_save_callbacks_for, and publishes a MessageBus /topic/:id notification_level_change event. Because @topic_view was also built before the mutation, the rendered/serialized response and any already-open client can keep showing the old watching/tracking level even though the database changed, and downstream observers never learn of the change. Use TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...) instead.

title: topicUnsubscribe route is shadowed by topic.fromParamsNear
body: The topic resource defined just above already has a child route fromParamsNear with path '/:nearPost', i.e. /t/:slug/:id/:nearPost, which matches the literal segment 'unsubscribe'. Ember's router recognises routes in definition order, so /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe is matched as the normal topic page with nearPost='unsubscribe' before the later top-level topicUnsubscribe route is considered; the unsubscribe template/controller therefore never renders on a full page load or transition. The unsubscribe route needs to be defined so it wins recognition over the :nearPost wildcard (or handled inside the topic route).

title: Emails with add_unsubscribe_link but no topic unsubscribe_url now raise
body: The server locale string unsubscribe_link now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}, and both body (line 90) and html_part (line 67) call I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args) whenever add_unsubscribe_link is true. MessageBuilder is generic: any caller that sets add_unsubscribe_link without also passing unsubscribe_url (previously valid, and the behaviour the existing specs exercised before they were edited to pass a URL) will now raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and fail to deliver the email instead of falling back to the plain user-preferences unsubscribe text. The per-topic sentence should only be appended when unsubscribe_url is present.

title: No test covers the new unsubscribe behaviour end-to-end
body: The only spec change passes unsubscribe_url into an existing builder fixture but adds no assertion that the topic unsubscribe URL appears in the text body or HTML part, and there are no controller specs for TopicsController#unsubscribe at all (level transitions watching/tracking->regular and regular->muted, missing TopicUser row, wrong slug redirect, JSON vs HTML). The core state-transition logic of this feature can regress or crash without any test failing.

title: Unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser record
body: TopicUser.find_by can return nil, but lines 107-113 immediately call tu.notification_level and tu.save!. A user can receive a topic notification without a TopicUser row (for example via a watched category for a newly created topic, before ever visiting it), and a user who was emailed via mailing-list mode may also not have visited. Clicking the email unsubscribe link for such a topic then raises NoMethodError (500) instead of creating a muted/regular record (e.g. via TopicUser.change, which creates the row when missing) and showing the unsubscribe page.

title: State-changing unsubscribe is performed on an unauthenticated-token GET and is not idempotent
body: The unsubscribe action mutates notification_level on a plain GET (routed in config/routes.rb, with check_xhr skipped and only cookie login required). Any link prefetcher, email security scanner (e.g. SafeLinks), or cross-site /link loaded in a logged-in browser will trigger it without user intent or a CSRF token. It is also not idempotent: watching/tracking (>regular) is demoted only to regular, so merely reloading/refreshing the unsubscribe page demotes regular to muted, silently changing the setting again on a safe-method request. The mutation should require a confirmation/POST (or a signed unsubscribe token) and set a single terminal level.

title: unsubscribe_link translation now hard-requires unsubscribe_url for every add_unsubscribe_link email
body: config/locales/server.en.yml changes unsubscribe_link to interpolate %{unsubscribe_url}, and both body (line 90) and html_part (line 67) render it whenever opts[:add_unsubscribe_link] is true. Only UserNotifications#send_notification_email was updated to pass unsubscribe_url; any other current/plugin/future caller that sets add_unsubscribe_link: true without unsubscribe_url will now raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and fail to send mail instead of rendering the previous preferences-only footer. MessageBuilder should supply a default/empty unsubscribe_url or only append the per-topic sentence when a URL is present.

title: No test covers the new unsubscribe endpoint or asserts the per-topic URL in email output
body: The only spec change adds unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe" to an existing builder fixture but adds no expectation that the URL appears in the text body or HTML part, and there are no controller specs for TopicsController#unsubscribe at all (existing-user demotion, already-regular/muted user, user with no TopicUser row, wrong slug redirect, JSON vs HTML). The nil-TopicUser crash and the level-transition behavior introduced by this feature can therefore regress or already be broken without any failing test.

title: Unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser record
body: TopicUser.find_by can return nil (for example a logged-in user who opens or is forwarded an unsubscribe link for a topic they have never visited/interacted with, so no topic_users row exists). Lines 107-113 unconditionally call tu.notification_level and tu.save!, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 instead of unsubscribing. Use TopicUser.change (which creates the row) or guard/create the record before updating.

title: State-changing unsubscribe is exposed as an unauthenticated-token GET request
body: The unsubscribe action mutates notification_level on a plain GET, requires only the ambient login cookie (ensure_logged_in) and skips check_xhr. Any cross-site page can force a logged-in victim's browser to request /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe (e.g. via an tag) and downgrade/mute arbitrary topics for that victim without CSRF protection or a per-user/per-topic signed token. Email unsubscribe links should carry an unguessable token, or require a confirmation POST.

title: Unsubscribe action is not idempotent and progressively mutes the topic
body: If notification_level is above regular it is set to regular, otherwise it is set to muted. Re-opening the same email link, refreshing the landing page, or a mail scanner/prefetcher hitting the link a second time therefore takes a user who already unsubscribed (regular) and mutes the topic, which also removes it from topic lists — a stronger effect than requested. Repeated hits should converge on one terminal level (regular), not toggle downwards on each GET.

title: Unsubscribe template path does not match the topicUnsubscribe route
body: The Ember route is the top-level route 'topicUnsubscribe' (app-route-map.js.es6 line 13, routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6, controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6, views/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6), whose template name resolves to 'topic-unsubscribe'. The template is instead placed at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs, which registers as 'topic/unsubscribe' (a nested topic route that does not exist). The unsubscribe page will therefore render with a missing/empty template and the notification dropdown in this file will not be shown.

title: Direct TopicUser save bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping
body: Setting notification_level directly and calling save! bypasses TopicUser.change, which is the codebase path that stamps notifications_changed_at, sets notifications_reason_id to user_changed, runs observe_after_save callbacks and publishes the /topic/:id MessageBus notification_level_change. Clients already viewing the topic and derived tracking state can therefore keep showing the old watching/tracking level after an unsubscribe until a reload, and the change is not recorded with a reason/time.

title: Global unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url for every email that uses it
body: unsubscribe_link is interpolated by Email::MessageBuilder for any mail built with add_unsubscribe_link: true (body and html_part), using template_args merged from the caller's opts. The new template unconditionally references %{unsubscribe_url}, but only UserNotifications#send_notification_email supplies unsubscribe_url; any other current/future caller with add_unsubscribe_link and no unsubscribe_url will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument (or render a broken link) when building the email. The per-topic sentence should be conditional or a default unsubscribe_url should be provided, and no new spec covers the unsubscribe controller action or an email built without unsubscribe_url.

title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive and can be bypassed by changing letter case
body: should_block? does an exact database string match on the supplied email, and neither BlockedEmail nor EmailValidator normalizes case (or surrounding whitespace) before lookup/storage. Email addresses are treated case-insensitively elsewhere (e.g. User.email_hash downcases), so a blocked address such as bad@spamclub.com can register as Bad@Spamclub.com and evade the block. Normalize emails to a canonical form (strip + downcase) on BlockedEmail save and in should_block? before querying.

title: should_block? performs a non-atomic read-modify-write and mutates state during validation
body: should_block? is called from EmailValidator.validate_each, i.e. during model validation, yet it increments match_count/last_match_at with a non-atomic read-modify-write save. Two consequences: (1) concurrent registration attempts with the same blocked email lose increments (both read the same match_count and write the same +1 value) — use an atomic update such as update_all('match_count = match_count + 1'); (2) a single signup attempt validates twice (UsersController#create calls user.valid? and then user.save, which re-validates), and attempts rejected for unrelated reasons also persist a count, so match_count does not reflect actual blocked attempts. The counter update should be atomic and ideally separated from the pure predicate.

title: rejectedEmails is a mutable array defined on the controller prototype and shared by all instances
body: rejectedEmails: Em.A([]) is defined in the object passed to Discourse.Controller.extend, so the same array instance lives on the prototype and is shared across every instance of the controller rather than being per-instance state. pushObject in createAccount therefore leaks rejected addresses across controller instances / modal lifecycles for the whole page session, permanently flagging an address as invalid client-side even in a fresh signup attempt. Initialize the array in init (or set it when the modal opens) instead of on the prototype.

title: action_type is not validated against BlockedEmail.actions
body: The model validates only presence/uniqueness of email. Any integer (or a typo'd value inserted via console/import) is accepted for the NOT NULL action_type column, and should_block? treats every value other than actions[:block] as non-blocking, so a malformed block entry silently fails open instead of surfacing an error. Add an inclusion validation over BlockedEmail.actions.values for action_type.

title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive and can be bypassed
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? performs `where(email: email)` with the raw address, and neither BlockedEmail nor User normalizes case before this check (PostgreSQL string equality is case-sensitive). A blocked address stored as `bad@spamclub.com` will not match a signup attempt with `Bad@SpamClub.com`, so the central block introduced by this PR can be trivially evaded by changing letter case. Blocked emails should be downcased on save and the lookup value downcased (as elsewhere via Email.downcase) before comparison.

title: Validation has a write side-effect that double-counts and races
body: should_block? is called from EmailValidator during ActiveModel validation, yet it increments match_count and saves the record. Validation is not a committed signup attempt and can run multiple times for one attempt — UsersController#create calls `user.valid?` and then `user.save`, which revalidates — so a single blocked signup increments match_count at least twice, and mere `valid?` checks in code/specs also mutate statistics. The read-modify-write (`record.match_count += 1; record.save`) is also non-atomic, so concurrent attempts can lose increments. Counting should happen once, atomically (e.g. update_counters/increment_counter), ideally outside pure validation.

title: rejectedEmails array is shared on the controller prototype
body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` creates one mutable Ember array on the class prototype shared by all instances of CreateAccountController. `pushObject` in createAccount mutates that shared array rather than per-instance state, so a rejected email leaks into any later/other instance of the signup controller for the lifetime of the page/app and can incorrectly mark that address invalid there. Initialize the array per-instance (e.g. in init) instead of as a prototype property.

title: Domain whitelist/blacklist regexp is not anchored to the end of the address
body: email_in_restriction_setting? builds `Regexp.new("@(#{domains})", true)` with no end anchor. For a whitelist entry `good.com`, `attacker@good.com.evil.example` matches and is accepted even though its actual domain is evil.example, defeating the whitelist; conversely blacklist matching can fire on look-alike suffix domains. The pattern should anchor the domain to the end of the address (and properly escape/split the configured domains) rather than matching the whitelisted string anywhere after '@'.

title: Blocked-email matching is case-sensitive and unnormalized
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? looks up `where(email: email)` with the exact string supplied, and neither BlockedEmail nor the validator normalizes case or surrounding whitespace before lookup/storage. A blocked address such as `bad@spam.com` can therefore be bypassed by registering as `Bad@Spam.com`, and administrators can also create duplicate block entries that differ only by case despite the unique index. Normalize (strip/downcase) the email both when saving BlockedEmail records and when checking should_block?.

title: match_count increment is a non-atomic read-modify-write
body: `record.match_count += 1` followed by `record.save` reads the counter into memory and writes it back. Two concurrent registration attempts with the same blocked email will both read the same value and both write value+1, losing one increment and potentially overwriting last_match_at inconsistently. Use an atomic database increment (e.g. update_counters/increment_counter with a separate atomic last_match_at update) instead.

title: Validation mutates BlockedEmail statistics and can count one attempt multiple times
body: EmailValidator calls BlockedEmail.should_block?, which saves match_count/last_match_at as a side effect of validation. Validation is not the same as a registration attempt: UsersController#create calls `user.valid?` and then `user.save` (which validates again), so a `do_nothing` match is counted twice for one signup, and any other code that merely checks validity (forms, console, related saves) inflates the statistics and performs a DB write during a nominally read-only check. Move the counter update out of the validator or make should_block? pure and record the match explicitly at the point of an actual blocked attempt.

title: rejectedEmails array is shared mutable state on the controller prototype
body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` defines one array on the prototype; `pushObject` in createAccount mutates that shared array rather than an instance-owned copy. Rejected addresses therefore persist across controller instances/recreation and can incorrectly mark an email invalid in a later, unrelated account-creation flow. Initialize rejectedEmails per instance (e.g. in init) instead of sharing the prototype array.

title: Raw-HTML posts bypass all sanitization, enabling stored XSS from feeds/remote pages
body: Post#cook returns `raw` verbatim when cook_method is raw_html, and TopicEmbed.import creates such posts from untrusted RSS/Atom content (Jobs::PollFeed) and arbitrary remote-page content extracted by Readability (TopicEmbed.import_remote). Neither path sanitizes script tags, event-handler attributes, or javascript: URLs before storage, and views output post.cooked (e.g. embed/best.html.erb uses `raw post.cooked`, and normal topic views trust cooked HTML). A malicious or compromised feed/page on the embeddable host therefore stores active HTML/JS that executes in the Discourse origin for every reader, not only in the embed iframe.

title: Unescaped referer interpolated into JavaScript and used as postMessage targetOrigin
body: `'<%= request.referer %>'` inserts the Referer header into a single-quoted JS string with no JavaScript/HTML escaping. A referer containing a quote or `</script>` breaks out of the string/script context and executes attacker JS in the Discourse origin inside the embed iframe. Additionally, postMessage's targetOrigin must be a serialized origin (scheme/host/port), not a full URL with a path; passing the full referer will cause browsers to drop the resize message, so legitimate resizing also fails.

title: postMessage origin check uses substring matching instead of origin equality
body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any e.origin that happens to be a substring of discourseUrl, rather than requiring e.origin to equal the Discourse origin (scheme + host + port, with trailing slash stripped). Shortened/prefix origins therefore pass, weakening the check that is supposed to ensure only the Discourse iframe can resize the embed. Compare the normalized origin exactly instead.

title: import_remote fetches arbitrary URLs server-side with open() and no timeout/validation
body: TopicEmbed.import_remote does `open(url).read` on a URL ultimately derived from the user-supplied embed_url parameter (EmbedController -> Jobs::RetrieveTopic -> TopicRetriever). TopicRetriever only compares URI host to embeddable_host; there is no timeout, size limit, scheme validation inside import itself, or protection against redirects to internal addresses (open-uri follows redirects). A URL on the allowed host that redirects to an internal/metadata endpoint, or a slow/huge response, can be used for SSRF or to tie up Sidekiq workers. Validate the final URL, set open/read timeouts, and cap response size.

title: PollFeed crashes on feed items without content and one bad item aborts the whole import
body: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` raises NoMethodError when an RSS/Atom item has no content element (common for summary-only feeds; SimpleRSS may return nil or a different field such as description/summary). Because there is no per-item rescue, the exception aborts poll_feed mid-loop, so all remaining items are never imported and the hourly job fails on every run for such a feed. Guard nil content (fall back to description/summary) and isolate failures per item.

title: Spec expects TopicRetriever in controller but implementation enqueues Jobs::RetrieveTopic
body: The 'tells the topic retriever to work' example stubs/expects TopicRetriever.new and retriever.retrieve, but EmbedController#best at app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 instead calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...). TopicRetriever is never referenced by the controller, so this expectation fails (Jobs.enqueue is not stubbed and may enqueue a real job). The test as shipped does not pass against the implementation and does not verify the RetrieveTopic job arguments; update it to expect Jobs.enqueue with user_id/embed_url.

title: import mutates caller's contents string and interpolates unescaped URL into HTML
body: `contents << "...#{url}..."` mutates the string passed by the caller (raising FrozenError for frozen literals and corrupting reused strings, e.g. feed item content reused on retry), and the URL is interpolated unescaped into a single-quoted href attribute. A URL containing a quote can break out of the attribute and inject markup into the raw-HTML post. Duplicate the contents string first and HTML-escape/attribute-escape the URL when building the imported-from link.

title: Disqus import silently drops the --category option and now requires fetching each thread URL
body: The change removes the documented `method_option :category` (breaking existing invocations that pass -c, which Thor will now reject/ignore) and replaces local PostCreator creation with TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...), which performs a live HTTP fetch of each Disqus thread link. If a link is dead, redirects, or the site is offline, post becomes nil and all comments for that thread are silently skipped, whereas previously the topic was created locally from the export data. Preserve category support or document its removal, and fall back to creating the topic from export data when the remote fetch fails.

title: RSS/feed content is stored and rendered as unsanitized raw HTML
body: TopicEmbed.import creates posts with cook_method raw_html and skip_validations, and Post#cook returns raw verbatim for such posts. The PollFeed path passes feed-supplied i.content (only CGI.unescapeHTML) with no sanitization, unlike import_remote which at least restricts Readability tags/attributes. A malicious or compromised feed item containing

title: Referer is interpolated unescaped into JavaScript and misused as postMessage targetOrigin
body: request.referer is attacker-influenced (the embedding page / a crafted link can control it within the allowed host check on host only, and its path/query are unchecked) and is inserted verbatim inside a single-quoted JS string: a referer containing `'` or `</script>` breaks out and executes arbitrary script in the Discourse origin inside the iframe. Separately, postMessage's targetOrigin must be an origin (scheme://host[:port]), not a full URL with path, so passing the whole referer makes browsers drop the discourse-resize message and iframe resizing silently never works. Emit only the referer's origin, escaped with a JS/JSON encoder (e.g. to_json).

title: postMessage origin check is a substring test, not an origin equality test
body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any e.origin that happens to be a substring of discourseUrl (e.g. a truncated/scheme-only-looking origin or a host that is a prefix of the configured URL string), rather than requiring exact equality with the Discourse origin. Any such sender page can then drive the discourse-resize handler and resize the embed iframe. Parse discourseUrl to its origin and compare `e.origin === thatOrigin` exactly.

title: PollFeed crashes on feed items without content (and on Ruby without String#scrub)
body: SimpleRSS items frequently lack a `content` element (using description/summary instead or nothing), so `i.content` is nil and `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError, aborting poll_feed mid-loop so remaining items are never imported and the hourly job fails every run for such a feed. String#scrub is also Ruby 2.1+, while this codebase supports Ruby 1.9-era installs, where it raises NoMethodError for every item. Guard with `(i.content || i.description || '').to_s` and a compatible encoding cleanup.

title: Feed-supplied URL is interpolated unescaped into an HTML anchor
body: The imported_from suffix builds `#{url}` directly from the feed/retrieved URL. import() only checks the URL starts with http(s)://; a URL containing a single quote, `<`, or `&` (obtainable from a feed item's link/id, which PollFeed accepts) breaks out of the href attribute and injects arbitrary markup into the raw_html post, compounding the stored-XSS risk, and at minimum produces malformed links. HTML-escape the URL and attribute-escape/validate it before interpolation.

title: Embed controller spec expects synchronous TopicRetriever the controller no longer uses
body: The 'tells the topic retriever to work' example sets `TopicRetriever.expects(:new).returns(retriever)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)`, but EmbedController#best implements retrieval via `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: ..., embed_url: ...)` and never references TopicRetriever. Mocha will fail this expectation at teardown and the actual enqueue arguments are untested, so the spec suite goes red / gives false confidence. Rewrite it to expect Jobs.enqueue with :retrieve_topic and the correct user_id/embed_url.

title: Imported feed/remote HTML is stored and rendered without sanitization
body: TopicEmbed.import stores attacker-controlled RSS/Atom or scraped page contents as a Post with cook_method raw_html. Post#cook returns raw verbatim for that method, and the cooked HTML is rendered raw in topic and embed views. No sanitization is applied on this path (PollFeed passes feed content straight through), so a feed item or embedded page containing <script>/event-handler markup becomes stored XSS for every forum visitor who views the imported topic.

title: PollFeed crashes on feed items without content
body: i.content is nil for RSS/Atom items that only provide a summary/description (SimpleRSS does not guarantee content), so i.content.scrub raises NoMethodError and aborts the whole hourly poll, preventing all remaining items from being imported. String#scrub also does not exist on the Ruby 1.9/2.0 runtimes this codebase targets, so this raises NoMethodError even when content is present.

title: Unescaped referer is interpolated into inline JavaScript
body: request.referer is inserted verbatim inside a single-quoted JS string passed to postMessage. The controller only checks the referer's host, so a referer such as http://<embeddable_host>/'-alert(1)-' contains a quote that breaks out of the string and executes arbitrary script in the embed page on the Discourse origin. The referer must be JS/HTML-escaped (and reduced to an origin) before interpolation.

title: Full referer URL used as postMessage targetOrigin never matches
body: postMessage's targetOrigin must be an origin (scheme://host:port), but this passes the entire request.referer including its path and query. Browsers compare it against the parent window's origin, so the discourse-resize message is silently never delivered and the embed iframe added by embed.js never gets resized to its content height.

title: Unauthenticated requests can flood the retrieve_topic job queue
body: Every GET for an unknown embed_url enqueues a RetrieveTopic job. The 60-second throttle lives inside TopicRetriever#retrieve, which only runs when a job is executed, not before enqueueing. Anyone who can present the embeddable referer can therefore issue many requests for distinct or identical URLs faster than jobs drain and fill Sidekiq with jobs that each may fetch remote pages/feed content, instead of throttling/deduplicating at enqueue time.

title: Spec expects synchronous TopicRetriever use that the controller no longer performs
body: This test expects TopicRetriever.new/retrieve to be called during EmbedController#best, but the controller instead calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...). The mock expectations can never be satisfied by the implementation under test, so this example fails and provides no coverage of the actual enqueued job arguments (user_id and embed_url).

title: import_remote fetches arbitrary URLs server-side with no validation
body: TopicEmbed.import_remote calls open(url) on the supplied URL before TopicEmbed.import's scheme check runs, and performs no host allowlist, private-address, or redirect validation. Callers that pass externally influenced URLs (e.g. thread links from a Disqus export) can make the server issue requests to internal/metadata addresses (SSRF) and import the response. Host validation in TopicRetriever does not protect this entry point.

title: postMessage origin check uses substring matching instead of origin equality
body: The handler accepts a message whenever discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) !== -1, i.e. whenever the sender's origin is any substring of the configured Discourse URL, rather than requiring e.origin to equal the Discourse origin. Origins that are prefixes/substrings of the configured URL are accepted, weakening the check that the resize message actually came from the Discourse embed iframe; the origin should be parsed once and compared exactly.

title: order() mixin is off by one for legacy box layout
body: The mixin emits the supplied value unchanged for both modern `order` and legacy `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`/`-moz-box-ordinal-group`, but the legacy properties are 1-based while `order` is 0-based (legacy default is 1, modern default is 0). Thus `order(2)` on .extra-info-wrapper and `order(3)` on .panel behave as ordinal-groups 2/3 in old WebKit/Firefox versus orders 2/3 in modern browsers, and any future `order(0)` would be invalid and `order(1)` would collide with unordered items in legacy browsers. The legacy declarations should use `$val + 1` so both models produce the same ordering.

title: Flex conversion strands .small-action button next to the text instead of at the right edge
body: `.small-action` is now `display: flex` (line 264), so its children become flex items and the `float: right` on its `button` (line 309) is ignored per the flexbox spec. Previously the float pinned the button (e.g. the dismiss/close control) to the right side of the row; now, with no `margin-left: auto`, `justify-content`, or explicit `order`/alignment on the button, it will sit immediately after `.small-action-desc` on the left. Add `margin-left: auto` to the button (and drop the dead float) to preserve the right-aligned placement.

title: align-items() omits the -moz-box alignment counterpart it claims to support
body: `flexbox()` emits `display: -moz-box` for legacy Firefox, but `align-items()` provides no `-moz-box-align`, so the vertical alignment supplied here (e.g. `center` for `.d-header .contents` and `.small-action`, `baseline` for bullet badges) silently does not apply in the very legacy-Firefox layout mode the mixin set targets, leaving those rows top-aligned there. Also note `-ms-align-items` on line 121 is not a real IE10 property (IE10 uses `-ms-flex-align`), so it is dead code. Add `-moz-box-align: $alignment;` (and remove/ignore the bogus -ms line) for consistent coverage.

title: order() maps flex order incorrectly to 2009 box ordinal-group
body: The 2009 flexbox properties -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group are 1-based (the default/initial value is 1, equivalent to flex order: 0), while the modern order property is 0-based. Passing $val unchanged means order(2) on .extra-info-wrapper and order(3) on .d-header .panel behave as order:1 and order:2 respectively in old WebKit/Firefox, and any future order(0) would be invalid/equal to the default. The mixin should emit $val + 1 for the box-ordinal-group properties to preserve the requested ordering across engines.

title: Floated button inside new flex .small-action is no longer right-aligned
body: .small-action is now display:flex (lines 263-265), so its direct children become flex items and float has no effect on flex items per the flexbox spec. The button rule at lines 306-310 still relies on float: right to push the action button to the far edge, which will now be ignored and the button will sit immediately after .small-action-desc in flow order. It needs margin-left: auto (or equivalent flex alignment) instead of/in addition to the dead float.

title: align-items() emits an invalid -ms- property and omits the -moz- box equivalent
body: Line 121 emits -ms-align-items, which is not a recognized IE10 property (the 2011 syntax is -ms-flex-align, already present on line 120), so it is dead CSS. Conversely the mixin emits the 2009 -webkit-box-align on line 118 and flexbox() claims -moz-box support, but there is no -moz-box-align, so old Firefox box-layout engines get no alignment while getting display:-moz-box from flexbox(). Add -moz-box-align and drop the invalid -ms-align-items.

title: order() mixin is off by one for the 2009 flexbox syntax
body: The order() mixin copies $val verbatim into -webkit-box-ordinal-group/-moz-box-ordinal-group, but the 2009 syntax is 1-based (default ordinal-group is 1 and values < 1 are invalid) while flex order is 0-based (default 0). To emulate order:N on old WebKit/Firefox the ordinal-group must be N+1. As written, order(0) would be invalid/dropped and ordered items are shifted one group toward unordered items, so the legacy-prefixed rendering this mixin exists for (used by .panel order(3) in header.scss and .extra-info-wrapper order(2) in topic.scss) can order header children differently from the standard `order` rendering.

title: Flex .small-action loses the right-aligned action button
body: Making .small-action a flex container (lines 264-265) makes float have no effect on its flex items, including the direct-child button styled `float: right` at lines 306-310. No replacement positioning is added (no margin-left: auto on the button, no justify-content, and .small-action-desc has no flex-grow), so the button that was previously pinned to the right edge of the row now sits immediately after the description text, changing the layout of small-action rows (e.g. topic timer / close / split notices).

title: Header panel loses all positioning in browsers without flexbox
body: .panel's `float: right` was replaced with `margin-left: auto` plus `@include order(3)` (lines 35-40), and .title's float was removed in favour of .contents being display:flex (lines 14-19). In browsers with no flexbox support at all (e.g. IE9, which the -webkit-box/-moz-box fallbacks in mixins.scss show this codebase still targets with legacy syntax), margin-left:auto/order are inert and nothing floats or positions the panel, so the header icons/login buttons collapse to the left after the title instead of sitting at the right edge. A float fallback (kept alongside the flex rules, since floats are ignored on flex items) is needed.

title: align-items() emits invalid/non-standard legacy values and properties
body: align-items() passes $alignment verbatim to -webkit-box-align, whose 2009-syntax value set is start/end/center/baseline/stretch (not flex-start/flex-end), omits -moz-box-align entirely despite flexbox() emitting -moz-box, and emits -ms-align-items (line 121), which is not a real property (IE10 uses -ms-flex-align, line 120). Current call sites only pass center/baseline so they happen to survive, but as a shared foundation mixin any future align-items(flex-start/flex-end) call will silently do nothing in legacy WebKit and Firefox, producing inconsistent alignment across browsers.

title: include_website_name is missing the question mark and will never be used
body: The serializer defines `def include_website_name` without the trailing `?`, while every other inclusion predicate in this file (e.g. include_email?, include_card_image_badge_id?) and the ActiveModel::Serializer convention require `include_website_name?`. As a result the `website.present?` guard is dead code and `website_name` is serialized even when the user has no website, emitting `website_name: null` in the API payload instead of omitting the attribute.

title: website_name bypasses the untrusted-attribute restriction for TL0 users viewed anonymously
body: `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes`, so it is hidden from anonymous viewers when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` applies (TL0 users), but the newly added `website_name` attribute is not added to that list. `website_name` is derived directly from the website URL (host, and in the same-domain case host plus full path), so anonymous visitors can still learn a TL0 user's website host/path from `website_name` even though `website` itself is suppressed, defeating the anti-spam/privacy restriction.

title: Sibling-subdomain branch of website_name has no test coverage
body: The second branch (lines 144-146) implements distinct logic for sibling subdomains such as www.example.com versus forum.example.com, stripping the first DNS label before comparing. The new specs in spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb only cover unrelated domains, identical domains, and a parent-domain website; none exercise this equal-length, >2-label branch, so a regression in the label-stripping comparison would ship undetected.

title: website_name drops query string and shows a trailing slash for root URLs
body: When the domains match, the method returns `website_host + URI(website).path` only. For a website such as `http://example.com/user?tab=posts` the displayed name silently loses `?tab=posts` despite the feature claiming to show the complete URL path, and for `http://example.com/` it returns `example.com/` instead of the bare host that the old client-side `website.split('/')[2]` produced.

title: include_website_name is missing the trailing question mark and will never be invoked
body: ActiveModel::Serializers in this codebase gate conditional attributes with methods named `include_<attribute>?`, as seen in include_email?, include_card_image_badge_id?, and the methods generated by untrusted_attributes. The new method is named `include_website_name` without `?`, so the serializer will not call it and `website_name` will be emitted (as nil when there is no parseable host) even when `website` is blank, defeating the intended conditional inclusion.

title: website_name bypasses the untrusted-attribute restriction for TL0 users viewed anonymously
body: `website` is listed in untrusted_attributes (lines 105-111), which suppresses it for trust-level-0 users seen by anonymous visitors. The newly added `website_name` is derived directly from `website` but is not added to that list, and its (misnamed) include method adds no restriction, so anonymous visitors can still learn a TL0 user's website host and, in the same-domain case, its full path even though the underlying website field is deliberately hidden from them.

title: Same-domain detection is asymmetric for www hostnames
body: When the website is `www.example.com/path` and the instance host is `example.com`, the first branch fails (hosts differ), the second branch fails (segment counts 3 vs 2 differ), and the else branch checks whether `example.com` ends with `.www.example.com`, which is false, so only the host is shown. The reverse combination (website `example.com/path`, instance `www.example.com`) does show the full path via the suffix check. The 'same domain' UX therefore depends on which side carries the www prefix, contradicting the PR goal; the sibling-subdomain branch (www vs forum) is also untested.

title: Tests cover neither the anonymous TL0 leak nor the subdomain branches of website_name
body: The new specs only cover exact-host match, parent-host match, and unrelated hosts for a regular user. The untrusted_attributes list in the TL0/anonymous context is unchanged and no example asserts website_name is hidden there, and there is no example for the equal-length subdomain branch in the serializer (e.g. website www.example.com vs instance forum.example.com, or the asymmetric www-vs-bare-domain cases), so the privacy regression and the hostname-matching edge cases would pass CI undetected.

title: include_website_name is missing the trailing ? so it is never used
body: ActiveModelSerializers in this codebase gates attributes with methods named `include_<attr>?`, as seen in include_email?, include_card_image_badge_id?, include_stats? and the methods generated by untrusted_attributes. The new method is defined as `include_website_name` without `?`, so the serializer will never call it. Consequently website_name is serialized even when website is blank (as a nil value), and the intended present? check provides no protection; the method must be renamed to `include_website_name?`.

title: website_name is not hidden for untrusted TL0 users viewed anonymously
body: `website` is listed in untrusted_attributes so it is suppressed when scope.restrict_user_fields?(object) applies (TL0 user seen by anonymous, to prevent spam/abuse harvesting), but the newly added `website_name` attribute at line 43 is not added to that list (lines 105-111) and has no equivalent restriction check. Anonymous visitors therefore still receive the website host and, for same-domain sites, the full path derived directly from the hidden website field, defeating the existing restriction. website_name should be added to untrusted_attributes (or otherwise gated the same way), and the spec's untrusted_attributes list should cover it.

title: Displayed website_name drops query string and fragment, so 'complete URL' text can be incomplete/misleading
body: When the website host matches the instance host, the code returns `website_host + URI(website).path` only. For a website such as http://example.com/?page=user or http://example.com/profile#section the display text becomes just `example.com/` / `example.com/profile`, omitting the query/fragment that distinguish the actual target while the link still points to the full URL. The visible label therefore does not show the complete URL as the PR title promises; query (and fragment) should be appended when present.

title: Embedded-post author link swaps the light and dark lightness values
body: This rule originally used scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The change writes dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)), so the light-theme argument is 70% instead of the original 30% and the dark-theme argument is 30% instead of the complementary 70%. Light-theme embedded-post author links become much lighter than before and dark-theme links do not get the intended lightened secondary color. It should be dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)).

title: Custom-message length swaps the light and dark lightness values
body: This rule originally used scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%). The change writes dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)), so the light-theme value changes from 70% to 30% and the dark-theme value is 70% instead of the complementary 30%. The hint text becomes much darker in light themes than before the PR. It should be dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)), as in the corresponding desktop modal rule.

title: Topic-map heading changes the original 20% lightness to 50%
body: The .topic-map h3 rule originally used scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%). The change writes dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)), changing the light-theme color from 20% to 50% and giving dark themes 50% instead of the complementary 80%. Headings become noticeably lighter in light themes than intended. It should be dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%)), matching the desktop topic-map h3 rule.

title: Group-member name changes the original 30% lightness to 50%
body: The .group-member-info .name rule originally used scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The change writes dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)), so the light-theme name color lightens from 30% to 50% and the dark-theme value is 50% instead of the complementary 70%. It should be dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)).

title: Group-member name changes the original 30% lightness to 50%
body: The .group-member-info .name rule originally used scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The change writes dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)), so the light-theme name color lightens from 30% to 50% and the dark-theme value is 50% instead of the complementary 70%. It should be dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)).

title: Embedded-post author link swaps light and dark colours
body: This was originally scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The correct dark-theme conversion preserves that as the light branch and uses scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%) for dark, but the change writes dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)) — both branches are swapped. Light themes therefore get a much lighter author-link colour than before and dark themes get a much darker one, the opposite of the intended contrast.

title: Custom-message-length swaps light and dark colours
body: This was originally scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%). The change writes dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)), swapping the two values. Light themes lose the original 70% colour (regressing existing appearance) and dark themes receive 70% instead of the complementary 30%, so the branches should be choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)).

title: Topic-map h3 changes the existing light-theme colour
body: This was originally scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), and the corresponding desktop rule was correctly converted to choose(..., 20%, ..., 80%). Here it is converted to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)), so the unchanged light theme gets 50% instead of 20% and the dark theme gets 50% instead of 80%. Mobile topic-map headings become noticeably lighter/less contrasted than intended and inconsistent with desktop.

title: Group-member name changes the existing light-theme colour
body: This .group-member-info .name rule was originally scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). It is converted to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)) instead of preserving 30% for light and using 70% for dark. Both themes therefore render a mid-grey different from the intended 30%/70% pair, lightening the name on the default light theme.

title: Group-member name changes the existing light-theme colour
body: This .group-member-info .name rule was originally scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). It is converted to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)) instead of preserving 30% for light and using 70% for dark. Both themes therefore render a mid-grey different from the intended 30%/70% pair, lightening the name on the default light theme.

title: Missed scale-color($primary) conversion for category badge-notification
body: This PR's stated purpose is to make every scale-color($primary, $lightness: ...) usable on dark themes via dark-light-choose(..., scale-color($secondary, ...)), and it converts the identical 50% rules throughout this file. Line 115, .topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification, still uses bare color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%). On a dark theme $primary is light, so scaling its lightness to 50% yields a dark colour on a dark background, leaving this badge count poorly contrasted while neighbouring elements adapt.

title: Light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 70% for embedded-post author link
body: This was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) before the PR, but the new dark-light-choose uses scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) as the light-theme argument and scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%) as the dark-theme argument. The pattern elsewhere is primary X% / secondary (100-X)%, so this should be 30%/70%. As written the light (default) theme link becomes much lighter/less contrasted than before, and the dark-theme value is also not the complement.

title: Light/dark lightness values inverted for .custom-message-length
body: This was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) before the PR, but the new value is dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)). The desktop counterpart in desktop/modal.scss correctly uses 70% for $primary and 30% for $secondary. As written mobile light-theme text becomes much darker than before and dark-theme text much lighter, inverting the intended shading.

title: Light-theme lightness changed from 20% to 50% for topic-map h3
body: This was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%) before the PR, but the new dark-light-choose uses 50% for both $primary and $secondary. The desktop counterpart in desktop/topic-post.scss correctly preserves 20% for $primary with 80% for $secondary. As written the mobile light-theme heading becomes significantly lighter/greyer than before, regressing the default theme, not just adding a dark-theme variant.

title: Light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 50% for group-member-info name
body: The .group-member-info .name rule was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) before the PR, but the new dark-light-choose uses scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%) / scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%). Following the PR's own pattern it should be 30%/70%. As written names are rendered lighter in the light (default) theme than before, an unintended visual change beyond adding dark-theme support.

title: Light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 50% for group-member-info name
body: The .group-member-info .name rule was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) before the PR, but the new dark-light-choose uses scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%) / scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%). Following the PR's own pattern it should be 30%/70%. As written names are rendered lighter in the light (default) theme than before, an unintended visual change beyond adding dark-theme support.

title: totalPages is off by one when member count is an exact multiple of the page size
body: totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 unconditionally. For user_count=50 and limit=50 this reports 2 pages instead of 1 (and for 100 it reports 3 instead of 2), so showingLast stays false on the real last page and the Next action advances to an empty page. It should use Math.ceil(user_count / limit) for non-zero counts.

title: Public group members page now silently truncates to the first 50 members
body: members now always applies limit (default 50) and offset, but the public discourse/templates/group/members.hbs view and discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6 route add no pagination controls or further fetching. Previously non-automatic groups returned all members and automatic groups up to 200. Groups with more than 50 members will now show only the first 50 on the public members page with no way to reach the rest.

title: Group creation silently ignores the alias_level sent by the client
body: The client's Group.asJSON() sends name, alias_level and visible on POST /admin/groups, but create only assigns name and visible. A non-default alias level chosen in the admin form for a new group is silently discarded and the model default is used instead; update handles alias_level, so create should assign params[:alias_level] the same way.

title: Members endpoint accepts unbounded, zero or negative limit/offset
body: limit and offset are taken from params with only to_i and no clamping. A request such as members.json?limit=1000000 forces serializing that many users in one response (memory/CPU/DoS risk), while limit=0 is echoed back in meta.limit and makes the admin client's totalPages/currentPage divide by zero, and negative values go straight into SQL limit/offset. Clamp limit to a sane range (e.g. 1..200) and offset to >= 0.

title: Remove-member link visibility checks `automatic` on the wrong context
body: This template is rendered per member via {{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}, so its context is the member (a Discourse.User), which has no `automatic` property. {{#unless automatic}} therefore always renders the remove link, including for automatic groups whose members the server refuses to remove (422 from can_not_modify_automatic). The check needs the group's automatic flag, not the member's.

title: Automatic-group remove_member spec uses the wrong HTTP verb
body: The spec calls xhr :put, :remove_member, but config/routes.rb only routes DELETE members to groups#remove_member and the client issues DELETE. Controller specs bypass routing, so this test passes even if the DELETE route were broken or missing, and it is inconsistent with the sibling test at line 125 which correctly uses :delete. It should use xhr :delete.

title: totalPages is off by one when member count is an exact multiple of the page size
body: totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, so a group with exactly 50 members and limit 50 reports 2 pages instead of 1 (100 members reports 3 instead of 2). Because showingLast compares currentPage to this inflated totalPages, the Next control stays enabled on the real last page; the next action then sets offset to user_count and findMembers returns an empty member list, leaving the admin on a phantom empty page.

title: Group creation silently discards the alias_level chosen in the UI
body: Discourse.Group#asJSON sends name, alias_level and visible, and the admin form exposes the alias-level combo box even for a new group, but Admin::GroupsController#create only assigns name and visible. Any alias level selected before first saving a group is therefore lost and the group is persisted with the database default of 0 (nobody), with no error shown to the admin.

title: Public group members page is now silently truncated to 50 members with no pagination
body: The members endpoint now always applies limit (default 50) and offset, whereas previously non-automatic groups returned all members. The public discourse/templates/group/members.hbs template gained no next/previous controls (pagination was only added to the admin template), so for any group with more than 50 members the public members page silently shows only the first 50 in username order and the remaining members are unreachable.

title: Members endpoint accepts unbounded and negative limit/offset parameters
body: limit and offset are taken straight from params with only to_i coercion. Any user who can view a group can request limit=1000000 to force the server to serialize the entire membership in one response (defeating the new pagination and enabling an expensive request), and a negative limit or offset is passed to ActiveRecord/PostgreSQL, producing a 500 error instead of a clamped or rejected value. The values should be clamped to a sane range (e.g. limit between 1 and a fixed maximum, offset >= 0).

title: findMembers no longer returns a promise when the group name is empty
body: findMembers previously returned Ember.RSVP.resolve([]) for a nameless group, so callers could safely chain .then() on the result. It now returns undefined in that branch while returning an ajax promise otherwise, breaking the method's contract; any caller that chains off the return value (including the next/previous actions in the admin group controller, which return group.findMembers()) will throw a TypeError for a group without a name.

title: remove_member spec exercises the wrong HTTP verb and cannot catch a routing break
body: The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' example calls xhr :put, :remove_member, but config/routes.rb only routes DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members to remove_member (and the client in group.js issues a DELETE). Controller specs bypass routing, so this test passes even if the DELETE route is broken or removed, and it misleadingly documents PUT as the removal verb while the sibling success example on line 125 uses DELETE.

title: Total page count is off by one when membership is an exact multiple of the page size
body: totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 unconditionally. For user_count=50 and limit=50 this returns 2 instead of 1, and for 100/50 it returns 3 instead of 2. showingLast therefore stays false on the real last page, the Next control stays enabled, and navigating forward requests an offset beyond the data and displays an empty page. The count should use ceiling division (with the existing zero-count special case) rather than floor+1.

title: Remove-member button appears for automatic groups because `automatic` is read from the member, not the group
body: This template is rendered via {{each member in members itemView="group-member"}} in group.hbs, so its context is the member User object, which has no `automatic` property. {{#unless automatic}} is therefore always true and the remove (x) link is shown even for automatic groups, unlike the Add-members section in group.hbs which checks the group's flag correctly. Clicking it issues DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members for an automatic group, which the server rejects with 422, and Group.removeMember has no error handler, so the admin gets a dead control with silent failure.

title: create ignores alias_level sent by the client, silently losing the setting on new groups
body: The group form always shows the alias-level combo box (even before a group has an id) and Discourse.Group#asJSON sends alias_level on POST /admin/groups, but create only assigns name and visible. A non-default alias level chosen while creating a group is silently discarded and the new group is persisted with the model default; update handles alias_level, create must do the same (or the control must be hidden until the group exists).

title: members endpoint accepts unbounded, unvalidated limit/offset
body: limit and offset are taken directly from params and passed to .limit/.offset. Any user who can see a group can request limit=1000000 to force the server to load and serialize the entire membership in one request (defeating the new pagination and enabling bulk scraping of member lists), and a negative limit raises a database error producing a 500. The parameters need clamping to a sane range (e.g. limit between 1 and the previous maximum) and offset to >= 0.

title: Automatic-group remove_member test uses the wrong HTTP verb and cannot catch a routing break
body: The test issues xhr :put, :remove_member while config/routes.rb only routes DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members to remove_member. Because controller specs dispatch directly to the action, the test passes regardless of the verb, so it gives false confidence that the endpoint the JS calls (DELETE, per Group.removeMember) is wired up. It should use :delete like the neighboring success-case test at line 125.

title: findMembers no longer returns a promise when the group has no name
body: Previously the empty-name branch returned Ember.RSVP.resolve([]); it now returns undefined. Any caller (including route hooks or future code) that chains .then() off findMembers() for a not-yet-named group - exactly the state of a newly created group object in the admin UI - will throw 'cannot read property then of undefined'. The branch should return a resolved promise to preserve the method's contract.

title: SiteSetting is consulted on every fallback translation lookup
body: FallbackLocaleList#[] calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym every time I18n asks for the fallback chain, which happens during translation lookups rather than once per request. This adds a site-setting lookup (and potential cache/database work) to hot translation paths and also makes translation depend on SiteSetting being available; if default_locale is nil/blank during boot, migrations, or in a bare console/job context, to_sym on nil (or loading a blank locale) can break otherwise-valid translations. Compute/cache the site default safely (e.g. per request or with a nil/blank guard) instead of querying it inside the fallback map.

title: Cached translations can permanently cache a missing-translation result before fallback locales are loaded
body: translate() caches translate_no_cache(key) in the LRU under only key+locale+backend, but with fallbacks the result depends on whether the site-default and :en locale files have been loaded yet. If a key is first translated in the user locale before its fallback locales are loaded, I18n returns a 'translation missing' string and that string is frozen and cached; loading the fallback locale afterwards does not clear @cache (only reload! does), so users can keep seeing missing-translation text until restart/reload. The cache must be invalidated when load_locale loads a new locale, or translations must ensure all fallback locales are loaded before caching.

title: Fallback locales are only ensured loaded for web requests
body: I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! is called only from ApplicationController#set_locale. Background jobs, mailers, rake tasks, and other code paths that set I18n.locale without going through this controller will translate with only config.locale loaded (translate_accelerator only auto-loads config.locale), so fallback lookups against the site default/:en can return missing translations instead of the English/site text. Move the ensure-loaded logic into the I18n translation/load path itself (or into every locale-setting entry point), not just the request cycle.

title: FallbackLocaleList is a Hash in name only and drops configured fallback semantics
body: I18n.fallbacks is normally an I18n::Locale::Fallbacks object that supports defaults, explicit per-locale mappings, and locale expansion (e.g. en_US -> en). Replacing it with a Hash subclass whose [] ignores any stored entries and always fabricates [locale, site_default, :en] means code or gems that assign/inspect fallbacks (I18n.fallbacks[:de] = [...], defaults, include?) silently lose those settings, and regional locales get no parent-language fallback (zh_TW never falls back to zh, pt_BR never to pt). Implement the fallback object API or subclass I18n::Locale::Fallbacks and override compute instead of faking a Hash.

title: Fallback locales are only loaded for web requests, not jobs/mailers
body: I18n.translate only calls load_locale(config.locale), never the fallback locales returned by I18n.fallbacks.
