title: Conditional passkeys now disabled on initial login, breaking discoverable/ID-less passkey login
body: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) now requires user != null, and authenticate() (lines 115-117) and challenge(error,field) (lines 137-139) only call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm() when it returns true. On the initial UsernamePasswordForm login page no user has been identified yet (context.getUser() == null), so the WebAuthn challenge, RP id and conditional-UI attributes are never put on the form. Previously fillContextForm() was called precisely when no user was selected, enabling discoverable credentials to identify the user. As a result the existing ID-less/passwordless flow (e.g. webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey in PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest, which expects automatic login from the first page) can no longer trigger navigator.credentials.get(), and users must enter a username/password first. The re-authentication case (user != null) should be added without removing the unauthenticated case.

title: Call to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments does not compile
body: UsernameForm.authenticate() calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only method added to its superclass UsernamePasswordForm is isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) at line 160. There is no no-arg overload, so services module fails to compile and none of the PR can be built or tested. The call should pass context.getUser().

title: Conditional passkeys are now disabled for unauthenticated (ID-less) login
body: authenticate() previously called webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) when context.getUser() was null, which sets the WebAuthn challenge/RP attributes needed for discoverable-passkey (ID-less) login on the initial username/password page. The new code only calls it when isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) is true, and that helper at lines 160-162 requires user != null. Consequently first-time/anonymous login pages get no challenge and no conditional-UI webauthn form, breaking passkey login for users not yet identified (existing tests such as webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey and passwordLoginWithExternalKey in PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest expect the webauth form on the initial page). The helper should not require a non-null user; fillContextForm is already made safe for an identified user by WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() returning false.

title: Error challenge also loses conditional passkeys for unauthenticated users
body: challenge(context, error, field) previously refilled WebAuthn data when context.getUser() == null, i.e. after a failed initial login attempt. It now delegates to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), which returns false for a null user. After an invalid username/password attempt by an unauthenticated user the re-rendered form therefore has no WebAuthn challenge/conditional-UI data, so the user cannot retry with a discoverable passkey from the error page, regressing the pre-existing behaviour that the authenticate() change also breaks.

title: getForLogin cache loses the ordering of login identity providers
body: The delegate getForLogin stream has a deterministic order, but the cached path collects internal IDs into a Set (Collectors.toSet at line 229/238) and then copies them into a HashSet at line 244 before returning identityProviders.stream(). HashSet iteration order is unrelated to the delegate/guiOrder order, so once the cache is used the login providers can be returned in a different, unstable order than on the uncached/invalidated path. Callers that do not re-sort (and the login-page ordering contract) will see IdPs shuffled. Preserve order (e.g. LinkedHashSet / ordered list) when caching and reconstructing the result, as the ID set is the only thing stored.

title: Test cleanup registers removal of a literal "alias" IdP instead of the created IdPs
body: Inside the loop creating idp-alias-0..19, cleanup is registered as testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove, using the literal string "alias" rather than the loop alias ("idp-alias-" + i). The same literal is used again at line 425. Cleanup therefore tries to remove a non-existent IdP named alias and leaves the 21 created providers behind, which can pollute subsequent tests/methods sharing the realm and mask or cause failures unrelated to the cache assertions. Register cleanup for the actual alias created in each iteration.

title: Update invalidation compares an organization-aware model against a raw model
body: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate receives `original` from getById(), which returns createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel(): its isEnabled() is false whenever the linked organization is disabled, regardless of the IdP's stored enabled flag. `updated` is the raw caller-supplied model whose isEnabled() ignores organization state. The LoginFilter.ENABLED predicate therefore measures different things on the two sides. For example, while an organization is disabled, changing a public org IdP from hideOnLogin=false to hideOnLogin=true yields predicate(original)=false (org disabled) and predicate(updated)=false (hidden), so no invalidation is registered; yet the cached getForLogin ID set was populated from the JPA delegate, which selects on stored fields only and contains this IdP. Once the organization is re-enabled, the stale cached set returns the now-hidden IdP (its per-IdP model is freshly fetched, so it appears enabled), and login-page callers that only re-check isEnabled() will display it. The invalidation decision must be made on comparable, storage-level enabled/linkOnly/hideOnLogin/brokerPublic values for both models.

title: getForLogin loses the delegate's result ordering
body: The cached IDs are collected into a Set (Collectors.toSet() at line 229/238) and the result is rebuilt by iterating a new HashSet (line 244) and returning identityProviders.stream(). Unlike the uncached path, which preserves the JPA/delegate stream order, the cached path returns IdPs in hash iteration order. IdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin has no documented unordered contract, so callers that do not explicitly sort (the contract previously returned getAllStream order) can see login IdPs in a different, unstable order once the cache is populated versus on the first, uncached call.

title: Test cleanup removes a literal alias instead of the created IdPs
body: Inside the loop creating idp-alias-0..19, the cleanup is registered as testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove, using the literal string "alias" rather than the loop variable (alias/idp-alias-i). The cleanup therefore never removes the 20 created identity providers (and likewise the idp-alias-20 cleanup at line 425). Leftover enabled/public IdPs can leak into subsequent tests sharing the realm and skew login-IdP counts, making this and other cache tests order-dependent.

title: getForLogin loses the delegate's result ordering
body: The cached branch collects identity-provider IDs and then the matching models into a HashSet and returns identityProviders.stream(). HashSet iteration order is unspecified and unrelated to the JPA delegate's ordering, so callers of getForLogin that consume the stream in order (e.g. take the first matching broker) can now observe a different, unstable provider order compared with the uncached path. Preserve encounter order (e.g. LinkedHashSet / ordered list) when materialising the cached IDs.

title: Login-cache update check compares an organization-aware original against a raw updated model
body: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate is called from update() with 'original' obtained via getById(), which returns createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel(): its isEnabled() also returns false when the linked organization is disabled. The 'updated' model is the raw caller-supplied model whose isEnabled() only reflects the IdP flag, while the JPA getForLogin query that built the cache also only checks the IdP enabled flag. For an IdP in a disabled organization that is enabled/public (so its ID is in the cached login list), an update that sets hideOnLogin/linkOnly therefore yields predicate(original)=false and predicate(updated)=false and skips invalidation, leaving the now-hidden/link-only IdP's ID in the cached login list; callers such as OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean only re-check isEnabled, so it can still be offered on the login page. Compute the original predicate from the unwrapped stored model (or the same semantics as the JPA query) before deciding to skip invalidation.

title: New order() method is abstract and breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: CryptoProvider is a public SPI interface, but order() was added as an abstract method rather than a default method. Every existing third-party or downstream implementation that does not define order() will now fail to compile, and already-compiled implementations loaded through ServiceLoader will fail with AbstractMethodError when CryptoIntegration sorts providers. Give order() a default implementation (for example returning 100) so existing providers remain source- and binary-compatible.

title: Equal provider orders make selection between FIPS and non-FIPS providers nondeterministic
body: Providers are now sorted only by order() and the first entry is silently selected instead of failing when multiple providers are present. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider all return order 200, so when two of them are on the classpath the winner depends on ServiceLoader/classpath iteration order preserved by the stable sort. In particular a deployment expecting the FIPS provider can silently start with the non-FIPS DefaultCryptoProvider, losing FIPS compliance without any error. The previously strict multiple-provider failure should be retained for equal highest orders, or the built-in providers need distinct, documented priorities with deterministic tie-breaking.

title: AuthzClient creation can permanently install the minimal Authz provider as the JVM-wide crypto provider
body: Every AuthzClient.create(Configuration) call now initializes the static, initialize-once CryptoIntegration singleton. In a JVM where AuthzClientCryptoProvider is the only provider visible to AuthzClient's classloader at that moment, it becomes the global provider for the lifetime of the JVM; later CryptoIntegration.init calls with a fuller provider are no-ops. Subsequent code using CryptoIntegration for PEM handling, signatures, key factories, certificate utilities, AES ciphers, or ECDSA getPublicFromPrivate will then fail with UnsupportedOperationException from AuthzClientCryptoProvider instead of using a full provider that becomes available or is initialized later.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns an arbitrary JCA provider instead of a BouncyCastle provider
body: getBouncyCastleProvider() is contracted to return the BouncyCastle (or BC-FIPS) provider, but this implementation returns the provider of the JVM default KeyStore type, which is typically a JDK provider such as SUN/SunJCE and is unrelated to BouncyCastle. Callers that pass this provider to BouncyCastle-specific APIs, check its name against CryptoConstants.BC_PROVIDER_ID, or rely on BC algorithm availability can fail or silently use different cryptography. The method should either return a real BC provider if one is available or signal that it is unsupported, not mislabel the default KeyStore provider.

title: ECDSA tests reuse one default-curve key pair for ES256, ES384 and ES512 and never verify the converted signature
body: The test generates a single KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair() (the JDK default curve) and uses it for ES256, ES384 and ES512, whose JOSE signature lengths correspond to P-256, P-384 and P-521. It then only asserts that converting DER -> concatenated RS -> DER -> concatenated RS preserves the concatenated bytes, without checking the expected R/S component lengths for each curve or verifying the re-encoded DER signature against the public key. Bugs in handling leading zero bytes or component truncation/padding for real P-384/P-521 signatures can therefore pass unnoticed. Generate a key pair on the correct curve per algorithm and verify the DER round-trip with java.security.Signature.

title: New order() method is abstract and breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: Adding `int order();` as an abstract interface method is a source- and binary-incompatible change for any CryptoProvider implementation outside the three implementations updated in this PR (custom providers, downstream projects, test providers). Such implementations will fail to compile or throw AbstractMethodError when loaded. It should be a default method (e.g. returning 0 or a documented neutral priority) so existing providers continue to work and can opt in to ordering.

title: Equal order() values silently select an arbitrary provider instead of detecting ambiguity
body: detectProvider now sorts by order() descending and silently takes element 0, but DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return 200. If two of those are on the same classpath (the exact situation that previously threw 'Multiple crypto providers loaded'), the winner now depends on ServiceLoader iteration order rather than any intended priority, so an application can silently run with the non-FIPS provider in FIPS mode or vice versa. Ties at the highest order need to remain an error, or the providers need distinct, intentional order values.

title: ES384/ES512 tests reuse a default-curve key pair and only assert a self round-trip
body: The constructor generates one EC key pair with no ECGenParameterSpec, i.e. the JCA default curve (normally P-256), and reuses it for ES256, ES384 and ES512. The ES384/ES512 cases therefore never produce real 48- or 66-byte R/S components and only assert asn1->RS->asn1->RS returns the same bytes, which would still pass for DER output that a JDK Signature verifier would reject. Each algorithm should use its matching curve (P-256/P-384/P-521) and the converted DER signature should be verified with Signature.verify (and vice versa) to prove interoperability.

title: New abstract order() breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: order() is added as an abstract interface method with no default implementation. Any CryptoProvider implementation outside this repository (custom server providers, downstream Elytron/FIPS variants, test doubles) will fail to compile and, if compiled against the old interface, throw AbstractMethodError when CryptoIntegration sorts providers by order(). This should be a default method (e.g. returning a defined default priority) so existing providers keep working and only providers needing precedence override it.

title: Equal-order providers are now silently chosen non-deterministically instead of failing fast
body: Previously detectProvider() threw IllegalStateException when more than one CryptoProvider was on the classpath. Now it sorts by order() descending and silently ignores the rest, but DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return order 200. If two of those are co-present (e.g. default + Elytron in WildFly, or default + FIPS), the winner depends only on unspecified ServiceLoader iteration order among equal keys, so a non-FIPS provider could be selected in FIPS mode or vice versa with only a debug log. Equal top orders should either retain the fail-fast error or have a deterministic, documented tie-break.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the default KeyStore provider, not BouncyCastle
body: The method contract in CryptoProvider is to return the BouncyCastle (or BCFIPS) security provider, and callers use it for BC-specific algorithms and provider names. This implementation returns KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider(), which on a stock JDK is typically the SUN provider, not BouncyCastle. Any authz-client code path (or synced keycloak-client code path) that consults getBouncyCastleProvider() expecting BC capabilities will get the wrong provider and can fail with NoSuchAlgorithm/NoSuchProvider or behave differently. It should return null like WildFlyElytronProvider if no BC provider is available, or an actually-registered BC provider.

title: ES384/ES512 tests use a P-256 key and only assert round-trip equality
body: The shared constructor creates one KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair() key, which defaults to a 256-bit curve, and reuses it for ES256, ES384 and ES512. asn1derToConcatenatedRS merely zero-pads/truncates r and s to algorithm.getSignatureLength()/2, so the round-trip assertion passes for ES384/ES512 even though no P-384/P-521 key or real signature of that size is ever produced or verified. The test never verifies the produced DER signature with Signature.verify(), so conversion defects for larger curves or leading-zero r/s values would go undetected. Each algorithm should generate a key on its matching curve and verify the converted signature cryptographically.

title: Possible NullPointerException when the all-Clients resource does not exist
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no client-specific resource exists the code falls back to getResourceTypeResource(...) and immediately calls findByResource(server, resource) without a null check. getResourceTypeResource returns null when the 'Clients' resource is absent, which can happen for realms whose admin-permissions client was created before the Clients resource type was introduced or if the resource was not initialized. This turns a permission check that should deny access into an NPE/500 error. The String-scope overload at line 244 does null-check the same lookup, showing the missing check here.

title: Role-mapping checks ignore manage-clients admins and manage scope
body: canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles (line 96), and canMapClientScopeRoles (line 101) only evaluate the exact FGAP scope for the client. Unlike canManage(ClientModel), they do not accept the MANAGE_CLIENTS admin role, and unlike the transitive permission model used elsewhere they do not accept a granted MANAGE scope. Consequently, when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, a traditional realm admin with manage-clients (or an FGAP admin granted only manage on a client) is denied role/composite/client-scope role mapping operations that were previously allowed, breaking admin functionality for fully privileged admins.

title: getClientsWithPermission includes the all-Clients type resource and misses all-clients grants
body: getClientsWithPermission iterates every resource of type 'Clients', including the synthetic all-clients resource whose name is literally 'Clients', and adds resource.getName() to the returned set of client IDs. Callers expect this set to contain client IDs for filtering client lists. When permission is granted only on the all-clients resource, the method returns {'Clients'} instead of the IDs of all clients, so list filtering can return no clients; when mixed with specific grants it also pollutes the ID set with a non-client identifier. The synthetic type resource must be excluded and an all-clients grant handled separately.

title: getResourceName has no Clients branch
body: getResourceName only translates Users resources: it returns 'All users' for the type resource and the username for a specific user. For the newly added Clients type it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), which for FGAP-created client resources is not set to the clientId (the resource name is the client's internal UUID). Permission/resource representations for clients will therefore show an opaque UUID or blank display name instead of the clientId, unlike the user behavior this PR extends, making client permissions hard to identify in the authorization UI/API.

title: Fallback to all-clients resource can throw NullPointerException
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no resource exists for the specific client, the code loads the all-clients resource via getResourceTypeResource() and immediately passes it to policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) and later to new ResourcePermission(resource, ...). getResourceTypeResource() can return null (e.g. the Clients type resource is absent for a resource server created before this type existed, or was not initialized), so the permission check throws an NPE/500 instead of safely returning false.

title: getClientsWithPermission returns the all-clients sentinel instead of client ids
body: getClientsWithPermission iterates every resource of type Clients, including the type-level resource whose name is literally "Clients", and adds resource.getName() to the result. Callers expect the set to contain client ids (specific-client resources are named by client id), so a grant on all clients contributes the useless entry "Clients" and does not expand to the ids of clients that have no individual resource. Filtering by this set therefore misses clients covered only by an all-clients permission.

title: getResourceName has no Clients branch
body: getResourceName only special-cases the Users resource type: it returns "All users" for the type resource and the username for a user resource, otherwise falling back to resource.getDisplayName(). Client resources created by this PR are named by client id and have no display name set, so representations of Clients permissions/resources will show a null/empty name instead of "All clients" or the client's clientId, unlike Users.

title: Client-removed listener can call unsupported V2 setPermissionsEnabled when both FGAP features are enabled
body: The listener now runs when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (v1) is enabled, but AdminPermissions.management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is also enabled, and MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() now returns ClientPermissionsV2 whose setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) throws UnsupportedOperationException. With both features enabled, deleting a client fires ClientRemovedEvent and this call throws, potentially failing the client-deletion operation instead of being a no-op in V2.

title: Role-mapping checks lose manage/admin fallback
body: canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles, and canMapClientScopeRoles only evaluate the corresponding fine-grained scope for the client. They do not fall back to canManage(client), unlike the V1 evaluator where an administrator who can manage a client (including via the manage-clients admin role) can map its roles. A full realm admin or a user granted only the Clients 'manage' scope is therefore incorrectly forbidden from role/composite/client-scope role mapping in V2.

title: Resource display name is not resolved for Clients resources
body: getResourceName only special-cases the Users resource type: it returns 'All users' for the type resource and resolves instance resources to usernames. Clients resources fall through to resource.getDisplayName(), but instance resources created by getOrCreateResource are named by client id and have no display name set, and the 'Clients' type resource is not translated to 'All clients'. Permission/resource representations for Clients will consequently expose a null/blank name instead of the client id or 'All clients'.

title: Missing all-clients resource causes NullPointerException during evaluation
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no instance resource exists the code loads the all-clients resource via getResourceTypeResource and immediately calls findByResource(server, resource) and later builds a ResourcePermission from it without a null check. getResourceTypeResource returns null when the 'Clients' resource is absent (for example in realms whose admin-permissions client was initialized before the Clients type existed, since init() returns early when the client already exists and never adds the new scopes/resources). Permission checks for such realms then throw NullPointerException instead of denying permission or lazily creating the type resource.

title: Removal listener can dispatch to V2 evaluator that throws on cleanup
body: The listener now runs whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) is enabled, but management() dispatches to MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is also enabled. ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, so when both features are enabled, role/client/group removal events invoke V2 cleanup and fail with UnsupportedOperationException instead of disabling permissions. The guard needs to exclude the V2 case (or the dispatch needs to use the V1 evaluator for this cleanup).

title: Default-strategy deployment still does not enable rolling-updates despite documented operator requirement
body: createInitialDeployment returns immediately when updateStrategy is null without enabling the rolling-updates feature, and both parameterized tests then expect that deployment to become ready. This contradicts docs/guides/operator/advanced-configuration.adoc, which states that while rolling-updates is in preview the feature must be enabled or the Operator will fail. Either the null/default path will fail in the operator (making these parameterized cases invalid/failing) or the documentation overstates the requirement for deployments without an explicit update strategy; the PR leaves the two inconsistent and does not test the documented failure/default behavior.

title: Feature-disabled exit code 4 is not verified and check subcommand gating is untested
body: The new testFeatureNotEnabled test only launches the metadata subcommand and only asserts the error message. It does not assert the newly introduced CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED exit code (4), which is the script-facing contract documented in update-compatibility.adoc, and it does not exercise the separate gating branch added to UpdateCompatibilityCheck. A regression that prints the message but exits with 0, or that fails to gate the check subcommand, would therefore pass the test suite.

title: Feature-disabled and changed exit codes are not verified for the check command
body: The new test covers only the metadata subcommand and asserts only the error message; it does not assert exit code 4 and does not exercise the check subcommand with rolling-updates disabled. At the same time CompatibilityResult changes RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 and reuses 4 for FEATURE_DISABLED, a scripting/operator-facing contract. Without tests asserting 4 for disabled metadata and check, and 3 for an incompatible check result, a regression that returns the wrong code (for example picocli.exit not taking effect or the two codes being swapped) would pass while breaking automation that relies on these codes.

title: Caution overstates that the operator will fail without rolling-updates
body: The added caution says that while in preview the rolling-updates feature must be enabled, otherwise the Keycloak Operator will fail. The PR itself only enables the feature in UpgradeTest when an explicit update strategy is set, and the same section documents the default '<not set>' strategy as supported/mimicking 26.1 behavior. As written, existing users who do not use the new update-strategy feature would read that their operator deployment will fail unless they enable a preview feature, which contradicts the documented default path; the caution should be scoped to when the update strategy / rolling-updates functionality is used.

title: Feature-disabled gating is only tested for metadata and its exit code is not asserted
body: The new test covers only `update-compatibility metadata` without `--features=rolling-updates` and only asserts the error message. It does not cover the separately added gating in `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` and does not assert exit code 4 (`CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED`) for either subcommand. A regression that leaves `check` ungated, or returns the picocli software/usage error codes instead of 4, would therefore pass while breaking scripts and the operator flow that rely on distinguishing feature-disabled from recreate (3) and rolling (0).

title: Caution overstates that the operator will fail without rolling-updates
body: The new caution says that while in preview the `rolling-updates` feature must be enabled, otherwise the Keycloak Operator will fail. That is not scoped to using `spec.update.strategy`, and it contradicts the PR's own operator test setup in UpgradeTest.createInitialDeployment, where the default/null-strategy deployment returns before enabling `rolling-updates` and is still expected to deploy and upgrade. As written, users with ordinary CRs will believe every deployment must enable a preview feature or the operator fails; the text should be limited to deployments that use the update-strategy feature.

title: Exit code 4 is described as a compatibility verdict although no check ran
body: The table describes exit code 4 as 'Rolling Upgrade is not possible' when the feature is disabled. In that case UpdateCompatibilityCheck and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata return before validating/reading metadata or computing compatibility, so compatibility is unknown rather than disproven. Scripts following this wording may permanently choose a recreate/downtime path for a merely misconfigured invocation instead of treating 4 as an enablement/configuration error distinct from the recreate verdict (3).

title: Group view permission grants global group manage permission
body: canManage() (no-arg) evaluates hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), so an admin granted only the 'view' scope on all Groups passes requireManage() checks that use the no-arg method, e.g. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() for creating top-level groups. A read-only FGAP admin can therefore create groups; canManage() should only accept MANAGE, as canManage(GroupModel) at line 79 does.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization resource IDs and looks them up as names
body: In V2 a group's authorization resource is created with its name set to the group ID (AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup/getOrCreateResource) while Resource.getId() is a separate generated authorization-store ID. This loop passes groupResource.getId() to hasPermission(), which does resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId), so per-group resources are never found and evaluation falls back to the all-Groups resource; it also adds groupResource.getId() to the returned set, which callers (UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource) use as UserModel.GROUPS group IDs to restrict user searches. Per-group view-members/manage-members grants are thus missed and the returned IDs never match real group memberships. It should pass and return groupResource.getName().

title: hasPermission can NPE when the all-Groups resource does not exist
body: When no specific group resource is found, hasPermission() loads the all-Groups resource via SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(), which returns null if that resource has not been created (e.g. admin permissions enabled before this schema/resource existed, or resources not yet initialized). It then unconditionally calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) and, if not empty-check bypassed, constructs a ResourcePermission with that resource, causing a NullPointerException/500 on ordinary group view/manage checks instead of simply denying permission. A null check returning false is needed, mirroring the server==null guard above.

title: canManage() grants manage to admins with only view permission
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (no-arg) returns hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), so an admin granted only the 'view' scope on all Groups passes requireManage(). GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() relies on requireManage() to create top-level groups, so a view-only FGAP admin can create groups (and any other caller of groups().requireManage()/canManage()). It should check MANAGE only, like canManage(GroupModel) does.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization resource IDs, not group IDs
body: In V2 a specific group resource's name is the group id (see hasPermission(), which looks it up with resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)), while Resource.getId() is the internal authorization-store id. getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() passes groupResource.getId() into hasPermission(), so the findByName lookup misses the specific resource and falls back to the all-groups resource, and it adds groupResource.getId() to the returned set. Callers such as UsersResource.searchForUser() and BruteForceUsersResource put that set into UserModel.GROUPS to restrict the user query to those group ids, so the query is restricted by non-group ids (returning no members) or not restricted per-group at all. It should use groupResource.getName() both for the lookup and for the returned group id.

title: hasPermission can NPE when the all-groups resource does not exist
body: When no specific group resource is found, hasPermission() calls AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource(), which returns null if the 'Groups' resource-type resource has not been created (e.g. admin permissions not initialized for the realm), and then immediately calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) and later resource.getScopes() with that null resource. This turns a simple permission check (canView/canManage/canViewMembers, invoked on ordinary group/user listing paths) into a NullPointerException/500 instead of returning false. A null check after getResourceTypeResource() is needed.

title: canManage() grants manage to holders of only the view scope
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), so an admin granted only the 'view' scope on all Groups passes canManage(). requireManage() is based on this method and is used e.g. by GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup to create top-level groups, so a view-only FGAP admin can create groups (and perform other operations gated only by requireManage()). canManage() should require only the MANAGE scope, as canManage(GroupModel) on line 79 already does.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs/names
body: Resources for Groups are looked up by name, where the resource name is the group ID (AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup returns group.getId() and hasPermission(String) does resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)). Here the code passes groupResource.getId() (the authorization resource's own UUID) to hasPermission, so findByName misses and evaluation falls back to the all-Groups resource, ignoring per-group view-members/manage-members grants. It then adds groupResource.getId() to the result, but callers such as UsersResource.searchForUser/getUsersCount and BruteForceUsersResource expect actual group IDs for the UserModel.GROUPS filter. Consequently admins with per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS see no group members in user searches/counts. Both places should use groupResource.getName().

title: getResourceName has no handling for the new Groups resource type
body: getResourceName() special-cases only the Users resource type, returning the username for a user resource and 'All users' for the type resource. For the newly added Groups type it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), but group resources created by getOrCreateResource have the group ID as their name and no display name set, so permission listings for group resources will show a null/blank or raw ID instead of the group name (and no 'All groups' label). Add the analogous Groups branch resolving the group by resource name and returning its name.

title: Java MessageFormat syntax breaks Account UI interpolation
body: This file is consumed by the JavaScript Account UI, whose translations use i18next-style {{0}} placeholders, as shown by the surrounding entries. Changing error-invalid-multivalued-size to Java MessageFormat syntax '{0} ... {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}' means the UI will not interpolate the values and will render the literal placeholders/choice syntax to users. The same change in js/apps/admin-ui messages_en.properties has the same problem; the MessageFormat form is only appropriate for the Java theme properties.

title: Java MessageFormat syntax breaks Admin UI interpolation
body: This Admin UI resource uses i18next-style {{0}} placeholders, but error-invalid-multivalued-size was changed to '{0} ... {2,choice,...}'. The Admin UI does not evaluate Java MessageFormat/ChoiceFormat, so users will see literal {0}/{1} and choice syntax instead of the attribute size limits. The Java-style text should be confined to themes/src/main/resources Java message bundles.

title: Lithuanian totpStep1 replaced with Italian text
body: The Lithuanian (lt) value for totpStep1 was replaced with Italian text 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' when removing the disallowed anchor tags. Lithuanian users will now see an Italian instruction on the TOTP setup page. The same wrong Italian string was also inserted into themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties loginTotpStep1.

title: Diff-trimming can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of reporting illegal HTML
body: The start/end trimming loops are computed independently and can overlap when the value and sanitized strings share repeated prefix/suffix characters (for example value 'aaa' vs sanitized 'aa': start advances to 2 and end advances to 2). Then value.substring(start, value.length()-end) is called with start greater than the end index, throwing StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. A malformed translation therefore crashes the verifier instead of producing the intended 'Illegal HTML' message.

title: Missing English bundle aborts verification with an unchecked exception
body: verifySafeHtml derives the English file by regex-replacing the locale suffix and path segment, and throws RuntimeException if that file cannot be opened. verify() only documents/handles MojoExecutionException and only catches IOException around the call, so a properties file without a matching _en.properties at the derived location (new locale directory, non-standard layout, or a base messages.properties) aborts the whole verification run instead of reporting a per-file problem or skipping/comparing sensibly.

title: Any English HTML unlocks all allowed HTML tags in translations
body:
containsHtml only tests whether the English value contains any ''; if true, the translation is checked with POLICY_SOME_HTML allowing br, p, strong and b regardless of which tags the English source actually uses. A translator can therefore add

/
// markup to a message whose English source only contains, for example, a or an anchor, contrary to the stated intent of allowing HTML in translations only mirroring the source. The policy should be derived from the tags present in the English value, as is done for anchors.

title: Java MessageFormat choice syntax used in JavaScript i18next bundle
body: This account-ui bundle and the corresponding admin-ui bundle use i18next interpolation, as shown by surrounding keys such as '{{0}}' and '{{name}}'. Changing error-invalid-multivalued-size to 'Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.' therefore will not be interpolated by the JavaScript UI; users will see literal placeholders/choice syntax instead of the attribute name and limits. The Java choice-format conversion is appropriate for the server-side theme bundles, but the js/apps account/admin bundles must retain their {{...}} interpolation (with pluralization expressed in an i18next-compatible way if needed).

title: Lithuanian message replaced with Italian text
body: The Lithuanian (lt) account bundle now has totpStep1='Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', which is Italian, not Lithuanian (the same Italian string was also put into the Lithuanian login bundle). Lithuanian users will see instructions in the wrong language; the anchor tags should be removed from a Lithuanian translation of 'Install one of the following applications on your mobile:' instead.

title: Traditional Chinese text put into Simplified Chinese bundle
body: The zh_CN (Simplified Chinese) bundle now has totpStep1='在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：', written in Traditional Chinese characters (手機/安裝/應用程式). Simplified Chinese users should get the Simplified rendering (e.g. 手机/安装/应用程序), consistent with the rest of this file.

title: Verifier aborts with RuntimeException when no English counterpart exists
body: verifySafeHtml() derives the English file by regex-rewriting the absolute path and throws an unchecked RuntimeException if that file cannot be opened. verify() only catches IOException, so a single translated file without a resolvable *_en.properties counterpart (a newly added locale, or a bundle whose English source lives in a differently-named tree than the 'resources-community'->'resources' rewrite assumes) aborts the whole verification run with a stack trace instead of producing a per-file verification message or checking the remaining files.

title: Any HTML in English enables all allowed tags in every translation
body:
containsHtml() only tests whether the English value contains any tag, and then POLICY_SOME_HTML unconditionally allows br, p, strong and b in the translation. A translation of a key whose English text contains a single
(or only an anchor, which also satisfies HTML_TAGS) can therefore freely add

, and markup that never existed in the source, and it will pass verification. Only the anchor tags are compared against the English original in santizeAnchors(); the other allowed elements should likewise be restricted to those present in the English value if the goal is to prevent translators from introducing new HTML.

title: Anchor check requires translations to keep English anchor order
body: santizeAnchors() walks the translation's anchors and the English anchors in lockstep and reports 'Didn't find anchor tag' as soon as the next pair differs, then breaks. Legitimate translations, especially for languages with different word order, may reorder the same anchors relative to the English sentence; those will be falsely flagged (and, because the remaining anchors are left in the value, will typically also produce a second spurious 'Illegal HTML' message). The check should compare the multiset of anchor tags rather than their sequence, and its message also omits the key and file, unlike the Illegal HTML message, making failures hard to locate in large bundles.

title: Lithuanian totpStep1 replaced with Italian text
body: The Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 (and the same change in account/messages_lt.properties totpStep1) was replaced with 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', which is Italian, not Lithuanian. Lithuanian users will see instructions in the wrong language on the TOTP setup screens; the previous Lithuanian text that contained the illegal anchors should have been translated/adapted, not replaced with the Italian string.

title: MessageFormat choice syntax breaks JS i18next interpolation
body: error-invalid-multivalued-size was changed from the JS UI convention 'Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).' to Java MessageFormat syntax 'Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.'. Every other placeholder in this account-ui file (and in js/apps/admin-ui messages_en.properties, changed the same way) uses {{n}} for the React/i18next renderer, which does not evaluate {n,choice,...}; users in the account/admin consoles will see the raw placeholders/choice expression instead of the interpolated counts. The choice/plural form is only valid for the server-side themes properties.

title: Missing English counterpart crashes verifier instead of reporting a verification error
body: verifySafeHtml() derives the English file purely by string replacement on the absolute path and throws RuntimeException('unable to read file ...') when that derived file does not exist. verify() only catches IOException and converts it to MojoExecutionException, so a locale file whose English source lives elsewhere or whose name does not match the '_xx.properties' -> '_en.properties' pattern (e.g. a messages.properties without locale suffix, or a new theme location) aborts the whole plugin run with an unhandled stack trace instead of producing a collected verification message or a clear Mojo failure.

title: HTML allowance is keyed only to presence of any HTML in English, not the tags actually used
body: containsHtml() returns true if the English value contains any '<[a-z]+...>' tag, and then POLICY_SOME_HTML unconditionally allows br/p/strong/b in the translation even if the English string used none of them (for example an English value containing only an <a> anchor, which is stripped by santizeAnchors). Conversely, legitimate English markup outside br/p/strong/b/a is rejected in translations even when copied verbatim. This makes the check both permissive for injected formatting tags not present in the source and prone to false positives, weakening the stated guarantee that only HTML present in the English source may appear in translations.

title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks all custom grant-type factories
body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is a provider-factory SPI implemented by extensions outside this repository. Adding getShortcut() as an abstract interface method makes every existing custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory fail to compile/load until it implements the new method. This should be a default method (for example returning a safe unknown shortcut or deriving one) so existing providers continue to work, with built-in factories overriding it.

title: Public copy constructor of OAuth2GrantType.Context was removed
body: The previously public Context(Context) copy constructor has been deleted as a side effect of adding grantType capture. Custom grant types and token-exchange code compiled against the old SPI may use that constructor to clone/wrap a grant context; removing it is a binary- and source-incompatible API break unrelated to encoding token IDs. The copy constructor should be retained and updated to also copy grantType.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted and off-by-one grant check
body: For an encoded prefix such as 'onrtac', the two grant characters are at indexes 4-5 ('ac'), but the matcher extracts substring(3, 5) ('ta'). It also returns false when the extracted value equals the expected shortcut. Because of the off-by-one extraction it will essentially never equal a real shortcut, so the equality branch is never taken and the matcher accepts access-token IDs with any grant type as long as the suffix is a UUID. The updated event assertions therefore cannot catch tokens encoded with the wrong grant.

title: Constructor validates grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId
body: Line 72 checks grantType and line 73 checks grantType again with the message 'Null rawTokenId not allowed'; rawTokenId itself is never null-checked. A null rawTokenId is accepted and later produces an encoded ID ending in ':null' from DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId instead of failing fast at construction.

title: Startup fails with opaque NPE if a grant factory returns no shortcut
body: postInit unconditionally puts gtf.getShortcut() as a key into ConcurrentHashMap grantsByShortcuts (and as a value in grantsToShortcuts). A custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory returning null - easy to do when stubbing the newly required method, and not prohibited by the interface contract - causes a NullPointerException during provider post-initialisation, preventing startup rather than a clear configuration error or a fallback to the unknown grant encoding. Null/duplicate shortcut validation should be explicit here.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher is inverted and uses wrong substring offsets
body: The grant shortcut in an encoded id like 'onrtac:<uuid>' occupies characters 4-5 (0-based substring(4,6)), but the matcher checks substring(3,5), i.e. 'ta' for authorization_code. It also returns false when that substring equals the expected shortcut and only proceeds when it differs. Consequently expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken will fail for correctly encoded tokens and can pass for tokens from the wrong grant, so the new encoding is not actually verified by these tests.

title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks all custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is an SPI implemented by extensions outside this repository. Adding getShortcut() as an abstract interface method makes every existing custom factory fail to compile and, if deployed as an old binary, throw AbstractMethodError when Keycloak enumerates grant factories in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit/getShortcutByGrantType. It should be a default method (e.g. returning a fallback/'na' or a derived 2-char value) so existing grants keep issuing tokens.

title: Public copy constructor of OAuth2GrantType.Context was removed
body: The PR deletes the public Context(Context) copy constructor while adding grantType extraction to the main constructor. Any grant/token-exchange code or custom extension that wrapped an existing Context via the copy constructor will no longer compile and old binaries will throw NoSuchMethodError. The copy constructor should be retained (and updated to copy grantType) or explicitly deprecated rather than removed.

title: Token issuance now hard-fails for unknown or custom grant types
body: TokenManager.initToken unconditionally calls encodeTokenId for every access token. getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext only falls back to 'na' when the GRANT_TYPE attribute is null; if the attribute holds any value not registered as an OAuth2GrantTypeFactory id (custom grants, internal/direct token creation paths that set a grant string, or grants whose factory returns no shortcut) getShortcutByGrantType returns null and encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException, aborting token issuance entirely instead of encoding the token with the 'na' unknown marker.

title: Documented 3-letter shortcuts are incompatible with the fixed 6-character decoder
body: The getShortcut() Javadoc says the shortcut is 'usually like 3-letters', but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider encodes session(2)+token(2)+grant(shortcut) and getTokenContextFromTokenId rejects any prefix whose length is not exactly 6. A factory following the documented contract and returning a 3-letter (or 1-letter) shortcut produces ids that can be issued but never decoded, throwing IllegalArgumentException on parsing. Either validate at postInit that every shortcut is exactly 2 characters and fail fast, or fix the Javadoc/format to state and enforce that requirement.

title: Constructor validates grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId
body: Line 73 repeats Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) with the message 'Null rawTokenId not allowed' instead of checking the rawTokenId parameter. A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted, later producing an encoded id ending in ':null' or an NPE downstream, and decoding such an id yields a context whose raw id is the literal string 'null'. The second check should be Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...).

title: Null or duplicate shortcuts put into ConcurrentHashMap cause NPE or misleading startup failure
body: postInit unconditionally does grantsByShortcuts.put(gtf.getShortcut(), grantName) and grantsToShortcuts.put(grantName, grantShortcut) on ConcurrentHashMaps. If any grant factory (in particular a legacy/custom one given a default getShortcut, or one returning null) returns null, ConcurrentHashMap throws NullPointerException during startup with no indication of which grant caused it. Shortcut nullness/length/uniqueness should be validated explicitly with the grant id in the error message before inserting.

title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks all custom grant-type factories
body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is an SPI implemented by out-of-tree/custom grant types. Adding getShortcut() as an abstract interface method means every existing custom factory no longer compiles and, if deployed as an old binary, throws AbstractMethodError when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() iterates provider factories. This is a breaking SPI change for a feature that could degrade gracefully. The method should be a default method (e.g. returning the unknown shortcut) so existing grants continue to work.

title: Copy constructor of OAuth2GrantType.Context removed and constructor can now NPE
body: The public Context(Context) copy constructor is deleted, breaking any grant implementation that cloned/modified the context before processing. In addition the remaining constructor now unconditionally calls formParams.getFirst(GRANT_TYPE), so code that constructed a Context with null formParams (previously valid) now throws NullPointerException at construction. Both changes break external grant types without a deprecation path.

title: Token issuance now fails for unknown or unregistered grant types
body: getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext() copies the raw GRANT_TYPE attribute into AccessTokenContext, and encodeTokenId() throws IllegalStateException if that string has no registered shortcut. TokenManager.initToken() now calls this for every access token, so any flow or custom grant that sets a grant_type value that is not exactly a registered OAuth2GrantType factory id (or a custom provider returning a null/duplicate shortcut, which also causes a ConcurrentHashMap NPE in the factory refresh path) will fail token creation with a 500 instead of issuing a token. Previously such tokens were issued with a plain UUID. Encoding should fall back to the 'na' unknown shortcut rather than aborting issuance.

title: Lightweight-token detection uses ambient context client and can NPE or misclassify
body: getShouldUseLightweightToken(session) reads session.getContext().getClient().getAttribute(...) (AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper line 86) and does not use the client from clientSessionContext. TokenManager.initToken() is invoked from flows where the KeycloakContext client is not set or differs from the client session's client (e.g. internally created/exchanged tokens), so this can throw NullPointerException during initToken or encode 'lt'/'rt' based on the wrong client. The client should be taken from clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getClient() and null-checked.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher is inverted and off-by-one
body: The encoded prefix is 2 chars session type + 2 chars token type + 2 chars grant type, so the grant shortcut is substring(4,6), not substring(3,5). The matcher also returns false when substring equals expectedGrantShortcut and otherwise does not reject a mismatching grant at all. Consequently expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken will fail for correct tokens and pass for wrong grant types, masking regressions. It should be: if (!items[0].substring(4,6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false; (with a length guard to avoid StringIndexOutOfBounds).

title: Constructor validates grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId
body: Line 73 calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") instead of requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...). A null rawTokenId therefore passes construction and produces a token id ending in ':null' from encodeTokenId(), instead of failing fast as the message intends.

title: Exhausted federated recovery credential is removed through local-storage API
body: After RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential() was changed to return federated credentials first, the allCodesUsed() branch still calls authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId()). removeStoredCredentialById only removes a locally stored credential; for a credential owned by a user-storage provider (whose getCredentials() model may also have a null or provider-generated id not present in local storage) this is a no-op or fails, so the exhausted federated credential remains. The user is given the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action but the old exhausted credential stays in the federation, so configuredFor()/getCredential() keep seeing it and the login form can keep presenting it instead of a clean re-registration.

title: Federating recovery codes drops userLabel and generated-at timestamp
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential builds the federated UserCredentialModel only from credentialModel.getType() and the JSON list of raw codes. The credentialModel passed by RecoveryAuthnCodesAction also carries the user-supplied label (generatedUserLabel) and the generation timestamp, which the local-storage fallback preserves via createCredential(realm, user, credentialModel), but the federated path discards both. A user-storage provider therefore cannot persist/display the label the user entered (it is shown for the credential in account/admin views) and must invent its own creation date, so federated and local recovery-code credentials behave inconsistently.

title: Login bean assumes federated credential is a fully parsed RecoveryAuthnCodes model
body: The bean calls RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) and immediately does credentialModelOpt.get(), createFromCredentialModel(...), and getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get() with no empty/exhausted handling. getCredential() now returns whatever the federation returns from getFederatedCredentialsStream(), which for a provider that supports the type for validation/update may be a plain CredentialModel whose credentialData is not the hashed RecoveryAuthnCodes credential-data structure (the new update path in CredentialHelper sends only a raw JSON list of codes). In that case createFromCredentialModel produces a model with no codes and getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get() throws NoSuchElementException, turning the recovery-code login page into a server error instead of rendering the code prompt.

title: New getCredentials() NPEs for unknown user
body: getCredentials() does var myUser = getMyUser(user); and immediately dereferences myUser.recoveryCodes / myUser.otp without the null check that isConfiguredFor() and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream() perform. getMyUser() returns null for a username not present in the storage map, so any credential listing for such a user (e.g. via getFederatedCredentialsStream during login/account calls) throws NullPointerException instead of returning an empty credential stream.

title: Old local recovery codes are not removed when new codes are created in user storage
body: When updateCredential succeeds in the federated storage, this method only logs and never deletes any pre-existing local recovery-authn-codes credential for the user. SubjectCredentialManager.isValid checks both federated and local credentials, so codes from the previous local credential remain valid after the user regenerates recovery codes in user storage. Regeneration therefore does not revoke the old codes, contrary to the expectation that generating a new set replaces the old set.

title: Exhausted federated recovery credential is removed through the local-storage API
body: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential now prefers a federated credential, but when all its codes are used this code calls removeStoredCredentialById, which only removes a credential from Keycloak's local DB. A federated credential (whose id is owned by, and may not even be set by, the user storage) is therefore not deleted/disabled in its storage, remains configured for the user, and can leave an exhausted credential in place despite the required action being re-added; removal should go through the federated credential-disable/update path for federated credentials.

title: User label and generation time are dropped when recovery codes are written to user storage
body: The federated write builds UserCredentialModel solely from the credential type and the JSON list of raw codes. The supplied RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel also carries the userLabel entered on the setup form and its generatedAt/createdDate, but neither is passed to the user storage, so a federated credential cannot be returned/displayed with the label (or original creation date) that the equivalent locally stored credential has.

title: Login bean still dereferences an empty Optional for users without a readable recovery credential
body: The PR changes this bean to use RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential, which returns Optional, but immediately calls credentialModelOpt.get() (and then getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get()) with no presence check. If the federated storage returns no credential, returns one whose credentialData cannot be parsed as RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialData, or all codes are used, rendering the recovery-code login page throws NoSuchElementException instead of handling the unconfigured/exhausted state, producing a 500 during login.

title: Raw recovery codes are handed to and persisted by user storage in plaintext
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes the generatedCodes list (the raw, human-usable recovery codes) as JSON and passes it as the UserCredentialModel challenge response to user.credentialManager().updateCredential(). Unlike the local path, which stores RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel data containing hashes of the codes, a user-storage provider that persists this input verbatim (as the PR's own BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage does at updateCredential/getCredentials) ends up storing all unused recovery codes in plaintext at rest. Anyone with read access to the external store then obtains valid second-factor bypass codes for the user. The codes should be hashed before leaving Keycloak, or the storage contract must require and document hashing, so federated persistence is not weaker than local persistence.

title: Federated recovery codes are never consumed or removed after successful use
body: After credentialManager().isValid() succeeds, the code only checks recoveryCodeCredentialModel.allCodesUsed() on the model returned by RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential() and calls removeStoredCredentialById() when exhausted. For a federated credential this does not work: consumption/marking-used is performed by the local RecoveryAuthnCodes credential provider when it updates its stored credential, whereas a user-storage validator (such as the PR's BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid(), which only compares the input against the stored list) does not mutate the stored codes, so allCodesUsed() stays false and the same code remains replayable indefinitely. Additionally removeStoredCredentialById() removes local DB credentials by id and cannot delete a credential held in user storage (federated credentials must be disabled/updated via the storage provider), so even an exhausted federated credential is not removed and the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES regeneration path can be bypassed. Single-use semantics for recovery codes are therefore broken for federated users.

title: getCredential prefers federated over local without aligning with validation, risking wrong code state when both exist
body: getCredential() returns the first federated recovery-codes credential if any exists and only falls back to the locally stored credential otherwise. This helper now drives both the login form's next-code number (RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean) and the post-login allCodesUsed()/removal decision (RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator), but credential validation through credentialManager().isValid() can be satisfied by the local credential provider. For a user who has both a stale local credential and a federated one (e.g. codes created locally before the storage started supporting the type, and then re-created in storage via the new fallback logic in CredentialHelper), the UI will prompt for the code number from the federated set and exhaustion will be evaluated against the federated set, while validation/consumption may act on the local set. The result is a wrong requested code index and failure to regenerate/remove the credential that was actually consumed. Lookup precedence must match the validator's precedence, or dual credentials must be prevented/deduplicated.

title: getCredentials dereferences MyUser without the null check used by sibling methods
body: The new getCredentials() does var myUser = getMyUser(user); and immediately accesses myUser.recoveryCodes (line 235) and myUser.otp (line 247). getMyUser() returns users.get(...), which is null for a username not present in the map, and sibling methods such as isConfiguredFor() and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream() explicitly guard against that. If credential listing is invoked for a user not in this storage's map, the provider throws NullPointerException instead of returning an empty credential stream, breaking credential listing/account flows for such users.

title: Reader thread is never joined before asserting no exceptions occurred
body: The test starts a reader thread but keeps no reference to it and never joins it. It only sets deletedAll=true after deleting the groups and immediately asserts caughtExceptions is empty, while the reader may still be inside managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...) and may record an exception after the assertion has run. The test can therefore pass despite the concurrent-access NPE occurring, and the unjoined thread can also continue issuing requests against the managed realm after the test method has finished. The thread should be retained and joined (with a timeout) after deletedAll is set and before the assertion.

title: Other lazy-delegate dereferences still NPE when the group is deleted concurrently
body: This change null-checks only getSubGroupsCount(), but the three getSubGroupsStream(...) overloads at lines 254-269 still call modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) with no null check. If another transaction deletes the group, modelSupplier.get() returns null in exactly the same way it does for getSubGroupsCount(), so these paths still throw NullPointerException instead of handling the deleted group. The same concurrent-deletion scenario exercised via subgroup listing/search can therefore still fail with an NPE; these dereferences need the same null handling (or a consistent contract) as getSubGroupsCount().

title: Concurrent-deletion NPE remains in the other lazy-delegate accessors
body: This PR null-checks the delegate in getSubGroupsCount() because modelSupplier.get() can return null when the group is deleted concurrently, but getSubGroupsStream(String,Integer,Integer) at line 256, getSubGroupsStream(Integer,Integer) at line 262, and getSubGroupsStream(String,Boolean,Integer,Integer) at line 268 all still call modelSupplier.get().<method>() unconditionally. A group deleted after its CachedGroup was loaded will therefore still throw NullPointerException through any of these paths, so the concurrent-access NPE fixed for the subgroup-count path remains reachable via the subgroup-listing paths on the same adapter.

title: Reader thread is never joined, making the regression test racy and leaky
body: The test starts a reader thread, deletes the groups, sets deletedAll to true at line 155, and immediately asserts caughtExceptions is empty without joining the reader thread. A request already in flight when deletedAll is set can still fail (including with the original NPE, surfaced to the client as a server error) after the assertion has run, so the test can pass even without the fix. Conversely, if a delete call throws, deletedAll is never set because it is not in a finally block, so the non-daemon busy-loop thread keeps hammering the server indefinitely and can leak into subsequent tests.

title: Concurrent-deletion NPE remains in the other lazy-delegate methods
body: The fix null-checks only getSubGroupsCount() at line 275, but getSubGroupsStream(String,Integer,Integer) at line 256, getSubGroupsStream(Integer,Integer) at line 262, and getSubGroupsStream(String,Boolean,Integer,Integer) at line 268 still dereference modelSupplier.get() without a null check. If the group is deleted concurrently, the delegate lookup returns null exactly as in getSubGroupsCount(), so these methods throw NullPointerException instead of handling the deleted group. The reported concurrent-access NPE therefore remains reachable through subgroup listing/search, not just subgroup counting.

title: Reader thread is never joined, making the concurrency assertion racy and leaking the thread
body: The test starts a reader thread at line 139 that loops while deletedAll is false, sets deletedAll to true at line 155, and immediately asserts caughtExceptions is empty at line 157 without joining the thread. A request already in flight can still fail and add to caughtExceptions after the assertion, so a real concurrent-access failure can be missed and the test can pass spuriously. Conversely the unjoined busy-loop thread can outlive the test, continue issuing admin requests against a realm/client being torn down or reused, and pollute subsequent tests.

title: Unthrottled reader loop can overwhelm the test server and collect unbounded failures
body: The reader thread at lines 140-149 spins with no pause, repeatedly requesting all groups with Integer.MAX_VALUE results while 100 groups are deleted, and appends every exception to an unbounded CopyOnWriteArrayList. Depending on timing/machine speed this can hammer the server and admin-client token endpoint enough to create timing-dependent failures or resource pressure unrelated to the bug under test, making the regression test flaky rather than a deterministic check.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator uses numeric key handling for a datetime ordering
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does int(math.floor(value)) on getattr(item, self.key) and value_from_cursor returns cursor.value unchanged. The only caller, OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint, orders by '-datetime', so value is a datetime: math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError when build_cursor computes next/prev cursors, making the optimized path return 500 on any non-empty page. Even if it did not crash, value_from_cursor would pass a raw integer timestamp into build_queryset's datetime comparison instead of converting it with DateTimePaginator's multiplier/fromtimestamp logic, producing wrong filtering. The paginator should reuse DateTimePaginator's key conversion or the endpoint should not use it for -datetime.

title: Negative-offset queryset slicing raises AssertionError, not graceful pagination
body: When enable_advanced_features is true and a user supplies a cursor with a negative offset (Cursor.from_string accepts e.g. '0:-100:0'), this branch does queryset[start_offset:stop] with start_offset<0. Django QuerySets explicitly raise AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported, contrary to the comment claiming the ORM handles it automatically. Any superuser/global-access user can craft ?optimized_pagination=true&cursor=... to reliably 500 the audit-log endpoint, and stop can also become <=0 giving meaningless slices. Negative offsets must be rejected/clamped with BadPaginationError as OffsetPaginator/ChainPaginator do.

title: BasePaginator change still allows negative offsets for prev cursors on all endpoints
body: The shared BasePaginator.get_result now clamps negative offsets only when not cursor.is_prev; for is_prev cursors it passes the raw user-controlled offset to queryset[start_offset:stop]. Since every DateTimePaginator/Paginator endpoint parses cursors from the query string without rejecting negative offsets, a crafted prev cursor (e.g. value:-5:1) reaches a negative Django queryset slice and raises AssertionError/500. This expands the crash beyond the gated audit-log path to all BasePaginator users, instead of validating offset<0 once in get_result/Cursor.from_string.

title: No tests for optimized pagination branch or negative/malformed cursors
body: The PR adds a new query-param/gating branch (optimized_pagination=true plus is_superuser/has_global_access) and a whole new paginator class, but adds no tests. Existing audit-log tests only exercise DateTimePaginator, so the datetime-key crash and negative-offset crash above are not caught, nor is the authorization gate (non-privileged users must stay on the old paginator, privileged users must get identical rows/cursors). Tests should cover first/next/prev pages via the optimized path, equivalence with DateTimePaginator results, negative-offset cursors, and the gate on/off.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator uses numeric key logic for a datetime-ordered endpoint
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key() does math.floor/math.ceil directly on getattr(item, self.key) and value_from_cursor() returns cursor.value unchanged. The only caller orders by '-datetime', so the key value is a datetime: math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError when build_cursor computes cursors, and build_queryset receives a raw numeric timestamp instead of the datetime that DateTimePaginator.value_from_cursor() reconstructs via datetime.fromtimestamp(.../multiplier). The optimized audit-log path therefore crashes or filters incorrectly on any non-empty page and is not cursor-compatible with DateTimePaginator.

title: Negative queryset slicing raises AssertionError, contrary to claimed ORM handling
body: When enable_advanced_features is set and a user-supplied cursor has offset < 0, this passes queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start (and possibly negative stop) to Django. Django QuerySets explicitly raise 'AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported' for such slices; it does not handle boundary conditions automatically as the comment claims. A crafted cursor such as '0:-1:0' from a superuser/global-access user therefore produces an unhandled 500 instead of a 400/BadPaginationError, unlike OffsetPaginator/CombinedQuerysetPaginator which validate offset < 0.

title: BasePaginator change affects all paginators and still allows negative prev offsets to crash
body: BasePaginator.get_result is shared by Paginator, DateTimePaginator and subclasses across the API, not just audit logs. The change silently clamps negative offsets to 0 for non-prev cursors (masking malformed/tampered cursors and returning the first page) while leaving offset untouched for is_prev cursors, so queryset[offset:stop] with a negative prev offset still raises Django's negative-indexing AssertionError and returns 500. This is a global contract/behaviour change introduced under an audit-log optimization with no validation at Cursor.from_string either.

title: Undocumented optimized_pagination switches cursor format for privileged users
body: The new 'optimized_pagination=true' query parameter is not declared in AuditLogQueryParamSerializer or the published API schema, and it switches the endpoint from DateTimePaginator cursors (millisecond timestamp values) to OptimizedCursorPaginator cursors (raw integer key values). A client that obtains a cursor from one mode and replays it in the other, or toggles the flag, gets incorrect filtering/results. The gate also expands to any member with has_global_access, not just superusers as the 'authorized administrators' comment implies, exposing the untested code path broadly within an organization.

title: No tests for OptimizedCursorPaginator or the optimized audit-log path
body: The PR adds a new paginator class, a new negative-offset branch, a change to shared BasePaginator slicing, and a new endpoint branch, but adds no tests. Existing paginator/audit-log tests exercise DateTimePaginator only, so the datetime key mismatch, negative-offset AssertionError, and cursor incompatibility above are not caught. Tests should cover positive/prev/negative cursors, empty and non-empty datetime-ordered pages, and the endpoint with and without optimized_pagination for eligible and ineligible users before merging.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot handle the endpoint's datetime ordering key
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key copies the numeric Paginator implementation and calls math.floor/math.ceil directly on getattr(item, self.key). The audit-log endpoint uses order_by='-datetime', so the value is a datetime and math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError. value_from_cursor also returns the raw millisecond cursor value instead of converting it back to a datetime as DateTimePaginator does, so build_queryset compares the datetime column against a number. Any optimized request that returns rows (or builds next/prev cursors via build_cursor) will 500 instead of paginating.

title: Negative cursor offsets are passed directly into queryset slicing
body: When enable_advanced_features is set, a user-supplied cursor offset < 0 is used verbatim as queryset[start_offset:stop]. Cursor strings are attacker-controlled (Cursor.from_string accepts any integer), so an authorized admin/superuser can craft offsets such as -1000000. Django querysets explicitly reject negative indexing with AssertionError ('Negative indexing is not supported'), causing unhandled 500s, and if this pattern is reused with list-backed querysets it wraps around and returns rows outside the intended page bounds. Other paginators in this file validate this case and raise BadPaginationError; this path adds no validation, bound, or max_offset check.

title: BasePaginator change exposes all existing paginated endpoints to negative-offset crashes
body: The shared BasePaginator.get_result now branches on is_prev: for prev cursors the raw cursor.offset is still passed to queryset[offset:stop], and the comment claims 'the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions'. It does not: Django raises AssertionError on negative slices. Because this edits the base class used by every DateTimePaginator/Paginator endpoint, any user who can supply a crafted prev cursor with a negative offset to any existing endpoint can trigger an unhandled 500. The change also silently changes non-prev behavior (clamping to 0) without tests for either direction.

title: Unconditional member access can crash requests for users without a member record
body: enable_advanced is computed on every GET, even when optimized_pagination is not requested: `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`. For a non-superuser whose organization_context.member is None (e.g. access granted without a member row), this raises AttributeError and breaks the previously working default DateTimePaginator path for all audit-log requests, not just optimized ones. The check should be short-circuited behind use_optimized and guard against member being None.

title: Cursor offset remains unvalidated while PR relies on negative offsets being safe
body: Cursor.__init__ stores int(offset) with no lower bound, and from_string therefore accepts arbitrary negative offsets from the query string. The added comment asserts this 'enables efficient reverse pagination', but no consumer validates it: SequencePaginator asserts offset > -1, OffsetPaginator/ChainPaginator raise BadPaginationError for negative offsets, and Django querysets raise AssertionError. Landing the comment/behavior contract without central validation leaves each paginator to fail inconsistently (assert, 500, or wrap-around) on the same crafted cursor.

title: New paginator and endpoint branch have no tests
body: The PR adds OptimizedCursorPaginator, changes BasePaginator slicing, and adds an optimized branch in OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint, but includes no tests.
