body: Users who enabled 2FA before this feature have backupCodes = null. The setup endpoint rejects anyone with twoFactorEnabled already true, and this PR adds no endpoint or settings UI to generate backup codes for an already-enabled account. Such users who click 'Lost access' only get MissingBackupCodes and a message telling them to generate codes in settings, which is impossible without disabling and re-enabling 2FA (and the message does not say that), leaving the recovery path a dead end for all existing 2FA users.

title: resetState leaves backup codes, secret, and download URL in memory
body: resetState only clears the password, error, and step; it never clears backupCodes, dataUri, secret, or backupCodesUrl, and never revokes the Blob object URL. The modal component stays mounted after Close/Cancel, so the plaintext backup codes and a working download URL for them remain live in the page for as long as it is open, contrary to the expectation that closing the backup-code screen discards them. Clear those states and call URL.revokeObjectURL in resetState.

title: No test exercises logging in or disabling with a backup code
body: The added e2e coverage only checks that the download/copy/close buttons work after enabling 2FA; as the TODO on this line admits, nothing tests the actual new authentication paths: login with a backup code, disabling 2FA with a backup code, rejection of a wrong code, or rejection when reusing an already-consumed code. These are the security-critical behaviors of the feature (especially single-use invalidation in next-auth-options.ts), and the PR description's own checklist confirms no such tests were added, so a regression in them would ship undetected.

title: Password visibility toggle is removed from keyboard navigation globally
body: Adding tabIndex={-1} to the show/hide-password button in the shared PasswordField makes the toggle unreachable by keyboard for every form in the app, not just the 2FA modals this PR touches. Keyboard and assistive-technology users can no longer reveal a typed password to check it. This unrelated global accessibility regression should be reverted or scoped to the specific field that motivated it.

title: Backup code can bypass the password when combined with a dummy TOTP field
body: Password verification at the top of authorize() only runs when credentials.totpCode is absent, while this new branch runs whenever credentials.backupCode is present and never validates the supplied TOTP value. An attacker can call the public credentials endpoint directly with an email, any totpCode value, and a valid backup code, skipping password verification entirely. A backup code therefore becomes a single-factor credential instead of a replacement for only the authenticator factor.

title: Backup-code consumption is not atomic, so one code can be reused concurrently
body: The code performs a read, indexOf check, and separate prisma.user.update() to null out the used code. Two parallel login requests with the same backup code can both read the original encrypted list, both find the code, and both authenticate before either update is visible. This violates the stated exactly-once property of backup codes; consumption needs an atomic/transactional compare-and-update or locking.

title: Successful 2FA enablement is only reported to the parent from the backup-codes Close button
body: handleEnable() now replaces onEnable() with setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes), and the only remaining call to onEnable() is the footer Close button for that step. If the dialog is dismissed through its normal onOpenChange path (close control, Escape, or outside interaction) after the server has already enabled 2FA, the parent is never notified and keeps rendering 2FA as disabled until a reload, while the modal also remains on the stale backup-codes step when reopened.

title: Users who enabled 2FA before this feature can never obtain backup codes
body: The migration leaves backupCodes null for every existing 2FA user, and this setup endpoint is the only place in the PR that generates backup codes, but it rejects anyone with twoFactorEnabled=true with TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled. Those users are nevertheless offered the Lost access backup-code flow at login and when disabling 2FA, and will only receive MissingBackupCodes, despite the error copy telling them to generate codes in settings where no such action exists.

title: Backup-code comparison rejects uppercase and whitespace-padded entry
body: Generated codes are lowercase hex (crypto.randomBytes(5).toString('hex')), but verification only strips '-' and does an exact indexOf match, with no trim() or case normalization; the disable endpoint repeats the same logic. A user who manually transcribes a saved code in uppercase, or pastes it with surrounding whitespace, is told the code is incorrect even though they supplied the right code. The supplied value should be normalized (trim, remove dashes, lowercase) before comparison in both verification paths.

title: resetState leaves backup codes, TOTP secret, and the download URL in memory
body: resetState() clears only the password, error message, and step. It does not clear backupCodes, secret, dataUri, or backupCodesUrl, and never revokes the Blob object URL containing all plaintext backup codes. The modal component stays mounted on the settings page, so the full set of recovery codes and the TOTP secret remain retrievable in component state and via the still-valid blob URL long after the backup-codes screen is closed.

title: No test exercises actually logging in or disabling 2FA with a backup code
body: The added e2e coverage only checks that the backup-codes download has the right filename, that copy shows a toast, and that the dialog closes, with explicit TODOs for checking file contents and for login/disable backup-code tests. The security-critical new behavior - login with a correct backup code, rejection of a wrong code, single-use invalidation of a consumed code, users with no stored codes, and disabling 2FA with a backup code - has no automated coverage, so regressions in these paths would ship undetected.

title: Password visibility toggle is removed from keyboard navigation for every PasswordField
body: Adding tabIndex={-1} to the show/hide password button in the shared PasswordField component makes that control unreachable by keyboard for all password fields across the app, not just in the 2FA modals touched by this PR. Keyboard and assistive-technology users can no longer toggle password visibility, an accessibility regression unrelated to backup codes.

title: Google Meet fallback crashes when there is no destination calendar
body: The code destructures the first element of evt.destinationCalendar (defaulting to []) and then dereferences mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining. When destinationCalendar is undefined, null, or an empty array, mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined and this throws a TypeError, aborting EventManager.create for bookings that have no destination calendar configured instead of falling back to Cal Video as the previous evt.destinationCalendar?.integration check did.

title: Google update/delete lose the destination-calendar fallback
body: In updateEvent (lines 254-256) and deleteEvent (lines 315-317), when externalCalendarId is falsy the fallback searches destinationCalendar for an entry whose externalId equals that same falsy externalCalendarId, which can never match. Previously it fell back to the event's destination calendar. Updates therefore call Google with calendarId undefined, and deletes fall back to 'primary' instead of the calendar the event was created on, so collective/other-host events can fail to update or be deleted from the wrong calendar.

title: Non-Google calendar services still always use the first destination calendar
body: EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents now calls createEvent once per destination calendar/credential, but Office365 (lines 73-77), Lark (CalendarService.ts lines 128-129), and the CalDAV base service (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts line 156) ignore the credentialId/externalId for the current iteration and always select destinationCalendar[0]. For a collective booking, the second host's credential is therefore used to create an event on the organizer's calendar id: it will typically 404/fail, or duplicate the event on the wrong calendar, and the other host's own calendar never receives the event. Only the Google service was taught to find the destination matching credentialId.

title: Team destination calendars are silently dropped when the organizer has none
body: evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, and the collective handling then does evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars). When it is null the optional-chained push is a no-op, so destination calendars collected from collective team members (users.slice(1)) are discarded even though those hosts do have calendars, and their calendar events are never created.

title: Video booking references lose their credentialId on creation
body: referencesToCreate now sets credentialId to result.credentialId only for calendar results and to undefined for everything else. Previously video results kept result.credentialId. Booking references for video meetings are consequently persisted without a credentialId, and later flows that look up the specific video credential from the reference (e.g. cancellation deleting the meeting only when reference.credentialId is present) can no longer find/delete the meeting, leaving orphaned video meetings.

title: updateLocation creates booking references with no calendar/credential identifiers
body: updateLocation now builds references from result.externalId and result.credentialId, but CalendarManager.updateEvent's returned EventResult never populates either field (its return object contains only appName/type/success/uid/updatedEvent/originalEvent/calError/calWarnings). editLocation.handler persists these referencesToCreate, so after a location change the booking's calendar references have externalCalendarId and credentialId undefined, breaking subsequent updates/cancellations that need them to address the correct host calendar.

title: Unrelated change breaks organization slug assignment
body: This PR changes slug handling from 'set slug when team billing is disabled, set requestedSlug when it is enabled' to 'set both slug and requestedSlug only when billing is enabled, and neither otherwise'. On non-billing/self-hosted instances organizations are now created with no slug at all, and on billing instances the slug is assigned immediately, bypassing the requested-slug verification flow. This is unrelated to destination calendars and can break org routing/creation.

title: Reschedule merge deletes only the first old calendar event
body: When newBookingId is supplied, the cleanup uses booking.references.find(...) to locate a single old calendar reference and deletes only that event. Bookings created by this PR can have one reference per collective host, so the old events on all other hosts' calendars are left behind as orphaned/stale events after a reschedule merge.

title: Confirming a collective booking only creates the organizer's calendar event
body: The confirmation path rebuilds the CalendarEvent with only booking.destinationCalendar or the confirming user's destinationCalendar as a one-element array; the other collective hosts' destination calendars stored at booking time are not reconstructed (the Booking row itself only persists the first one). Since calendar events for requiresConfirmation bookings are created on confirmation via handleConfirmation/EventManager.create, the non-organizer hosts will not receive calendar events for confirmed collective bookings, which is the scenario this PR sets out to fix. The same single-calendar reconstruction exists in the Stripe/PayPal payment-success handlers.

title: Webhook payload shape for destinationCalendar changes and is inconsistent
body: CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar changes from a DestinationCalendar object/null to an array, and CalendarEvent objects are spread directly into webhook payloads. External consumers (webhooks/Zapier) that read payload.destinationCalendar.externalId will break. The value is also now inconsistent for 'no destination': handleNewBooking emits null while confirm/cancel/payment flows emit [], so consumers cannot rely on a single shape; only one of the three webhook e2e expectations was updated to match.

title: Google Meet fallback crashes when destinationCalendar is empty or absent
body: In EventManager.create, evt.destinationCalendar is destructured with `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`, which yields undefined when the array is empty or missing, but the next condition dereferences `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. For a Google Meet booking with no destination calendar this throws a TypeError instead of falling back to Cal Video, breaking booking creation.

title: Google updateEvent fallback cannot find the destination calendar
body: In GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent, when externalCalendarId is falsy the fallback searches for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`, comparing calendar IDs to the same falsy value that triggered the fallback, so selectedCalendar is always undefined. calendar.events.update is then called with calendarId undefined and fails, whereas the previous code used the event's destination calendar externalId.

title: Google createEvent uses main host organizer email for every host calendar
body: In GoogleCalendarService.createEvent, selectedCalendar is correctly chosen by matching credentialId, but the payload organizer email still comes from mainHostDestinationCalendar, the first destinationCalendar entry, for every credential. When EventManager creates the event on a second collective host's Google calendar, that event is created with the main host's calendar/externalId as organizer email, which does not match the authenticated host and can produce a wrong organizer or rejected/misattributed event.

title: Office365 createEvent ignores credential-specific destination calendar
body: Office365CalendarService.createEvent always uses the first entry of event.destinationCalendar as mainHostDestinationCalendar and does not accept or use the credentialId now passed by CalendarManager. For collective events, EventManager calls this once per host credential, so a second Office365 host's event is attempted against the main host's calendar externalId with the second host's token, causing failures or an event targeted at the wrong calendar.

title: Lark createEvent always targets the first destination calendar
body: LarkCalendarService.createEvent derives calendarId only from the first destinationCalendar entry and does not use the credentialId supplied for the new multi-destination flow. When EventManager loops over collective hosts and invokes Lark for another host, it will reuse the main host's Lark calendar ID with that host's credentials, so creation fails or targets the wrong calendar instead of that host's destination calendar.

title: CalDAV createEvent can silently create no event for non-main hosts
body: BaseCalendarService.createEvent filters the credential's calendars to those matching mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId, always the first destination calendar. For a second collective host using CalDAV, that externalId is a calendar URL from the main host's server and normally matches none of this host's calendars; the Promise.all then resolves over an empty list and the method returns a generated uid as success even though no calendar object was created, leaving a booking reference pointing to a nonexistent event.

title: updateAllCalendarEvents can reuse the previous reference's credential
body: In EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents, `credential` is declared outside the loop over calendar references. If a later reference's credential is not in calendarCredentials and the DB lookup does not produce a credential, the variable still holds the previous iteration's credential, and updateEvent is pushed with that wrong credential. That can update the previous host's calendar again and leave the intended host's event unchanged.

title: Video booking references lose their credentialId on creation
body: In EventManager.create, referencesToCreate now sets `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`, so non-calendar results such as video meetings always get credentialId undefined. Previously video results preserved result.credentialId. Later cancellation and update flows look up the video credential by booking reference credentialId, so losing it can prevent the video meeting from being updated or deleted.

title: updateLocation creates calendar references without externalCalendarId or credentialId
body: In EventManager.updateLocation, references are built from result.externalId and result.credentialId, but CalendarManager.updateEvent does not return externalId or credentialId in its EventResult. Calendar references created after a location change therefore lose both identifiers, weakening later update/cancel operations that rely on reference.credentialId and reference.externalCalendarId to target the correct calendar.

title: Recurring collective cancellation repeatedly deletes only the first calendar reference
body: In handleCancelBooking's recurring/allRemainingBookings path, the code now loops over every calendar reference of the booking, but inside that loop it again iterates credentials and for each updated booking selects only `updBooking.references.find(ref => ref.type.includes('_calendar'))`, the first calendar reference. With multiple collective hosts this deletes the first host's recurring events repeatedly and never deletes the other hosts' calendar events, leaving orphaned events after cancellation.

title: Collective team destination calendars are dropped when organizer has none
body: In handleNewBooking, evt.destinationCalendar is set to null when neither eventType.destinationCalendar nor organizerUser.destinationCalendar exists, and the collective handling later does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. If only non-organizer collective hosts have destination calendars, teamDestinationCalendars is collected but never added because the optional-chained push is a no-op on null, so those hosts receive no calendar events.

title: Confirming a collective booking only creates the organizer's calendar event
body: confirmHandler builds evt.destinationCalendar from only booking.destinationCalendar or the confirming user's destinationCalendar, converted to a one-element array. For collective bookings that require confirmation, calendar events are created at confirmation time via this evt, so the other fixed hosts' destination calendars are never passed to EventManager and those hosts do not get calendar events when the booking is confirmed.

title: Crash when Google Meet booking has no destination calendar
body: The code destructures the first element of evt.destinationCalendar and then accesses mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining or a null check. When destinationCalendar is null or an empty array (handleNewBooking explicitly sets it to null when neither the event type nor organizer has one), this throws a TypeError whenever evt.location is Google Meet, aborting EventManager.create instead of falling back to Cal Video as the previous optional-chained code did.

title: Google updateEvent fallback can never find a calendar
body: When externalCalendarId is falsy, selectedCalendar is computed by finding a destination calendar whose externalId equals that same falsy externalCalendarId, which can never match a real calendar id, so selectedCalendar is undefined and calendar.events.update is called with calendarId: undefined. The previous behaviour fell back to the destination calendar's externalId. Legacy bookings and any update path without a stored externalCalendarId will therefore fail to update the Google event. The same dead fallback exists in deleteEvent, which then silently falls back to 'primary' and may delete from the wrong calendar.

title: Secondary hosts' Google events use the main host's calendar as organizer email
body: createEvent always uses the first destination calendar's externalId as the organizer attendee email, even when credentialId identifies a different (secondary collective) host whose calendar is selected via the credentialId lookup below. The secondary host's event is therefore created on their calendar but attributed to the main host's calendar address, which Google can reject or display with the wrong organizer. The organizer email should come from the destination calendar matching the passed credentialId, not destinationCalendar[0]; updateEvent has the same defect.

title: Office365 createEvent ignores credentialId and always uses first host's calendar
body: EventManager now calls createEvent once per destination calendar with that host's credential, but this implementation does not accept/use credentialId and always targets destinationCalendar[0]. For a collective event, the second host's Office365 token is used to POST to /me/calendars/{first host's externalId}/events, which will 404 or create on the wrong calendar, so non-Google collective hosts do not actually receive their event despite the PR's goal. LarkCalendarService and the CalDAV BaseCalendarService have the identical first-element-only pattern.

title: Lark createEvent always uses the main host's calendar id
body: createEvent (and createAttendees) destructure only destinationCalendar[0] and ignore the credential being used. When EventManager iterates to the second collective host and instantiates Lark with that host's credential, it still creates the event and attendees on the first host's Lark calendar id, causing API failures or events on the wrong calendar. It needs the same per-credential destination selection Google received.

title: CalDAV createEvent filters by main host calendar for every host
body: BaseCalendarService.createEvent filters the credential's calendars to the first destination calendar's externalId. For a secondary collective host whose CalDAV account does not contain the main host's calendar, the filter yields zero calendars, Promise.all resolves empty, and the method still returns a fabricated uid as success, so EventManager records a booking reference for an event that was never created on the second host's calendar.

title: Video booking references lose their credentialId
body: referencesToCreate now sets credentialId to undefined for every non-calendar result, whereas previously video results kept result.credentialId. Dedicated video (e.g. Zoom/Daily) booking references are persisted without credentialId, and later flows such as handleCancelBooking only delete the video meeting when bookingVideoReference.credentialId is present, so video meetings for new bookings may leak/not be deleted or updated.

title: References created without externalId in fallback/other-calendar branches
body: In the branches where a destination has no credentialId, where no destination exists, and for the trailing other_calendar credentials (lines 380, 391, 403), createEvent is called without destination.externalId, so CalendarManager returns externalId undefined and the persisted BookingReference has externalCalendarId undefined. Previously references derived externalCalendarId from evt.destinationCalendar. Updates/deletes for those events then depend on the broken per-service fallbacks and can target 'primary' or no calendar instead of the calendar the event was created on.

title: Reschedule merge deletes only the first old calendar event
body: updateAllCalendarEvents now loops over all calendar references for updates, but the newBookingId cleanup still uses booking.references.find(...) and deletes only the first old calendar event. For a collective booking with one reference per host, the other hosts' old events are never deleted when merging into the new booking, leaving orphaned duplicate events on those hosts' calendars after reschedule.

title: Recurring cancellation duplicates deletes with wrong credentials
body: The new outer loop iterates every calendar reference, and inside the recurring/allRemainingBookings branch it again maps over all of the organizer's calendar credentials and, for each updated booking, picks only the first calendar reference via find(). Each recurring event is therefore delete-attempted once per reference times per credential, mostly with a credential that does not own that reference's uid/externalCalendarId. This produces spurious delete failures (and possible wrong-calendar deletions) for collective recurring bookings instead of deleting each reference once with its own credentialId.

title: Confirming a collective booking only creates the organizer's calendar event
body: The evt built for handleConfirmation contains only booking.destinationCalendar or the confirming user's destinationCalendar as a single-element array, with no destination calendars for the other collective hosts. Since EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents now creates events solely by iterating evt.destinationCalendar, a requires-confirmation collective booking that is later confirmed will only create an event for one host, defeating the multi-host fix on the confirmation path. The Stripe/PayPal webhook handlers build the same single-destination evt.

title: Collective team calendars are dropped when organizer has no destination calendar
body: evt.destinationCalendar is set to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, and the collective merge then does evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars). With null, the optional chain silently no-ops, so all collected team hosts' destination calendars are lost and EventManager falls back to the first connected calendar instead of creating an event per host.

title: Unrelated inversion of organization slug assignment
body: This file is unrelated to destination calendars, but the change flips slug assignment from 'slug when team billing is NOT enabled' to 'slug only when team billing IS enabled' (and now sets both slug and requestedSlug in the billing case). Organizations created without team billing will be created without a slug, breaking their org URL/routing, while billing-enabled orgs get a final slug before the requested-slug flow expects it.

title: Salesforce service uses prisma without importing it
body: This code calls prisma.credential.update, but the file's imports do not include prisma. This is a TypeScript/ runtime ReferenceError, so Salesforce client construction fails when it reaches the credential update and the Salesforce integration cannot be used.

title: Refreshed Salesforce access token is persisted but not used
body: getClient unconditionally refreshes the token on every construction, parses and stores the refreshed token, but then creates the jsforce Connection with credentialKey.access_token, the old and potentially expired token. API calls made through this connection therefore still fail authentication even though a valid token was just obtained.

title: Google credential is stored as a Zod SafeParse wrapper object
body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the Zod SafeParse result ({success, data}), whereas the previous googleCredentialSchema.parse returned the credential object itself. The result is assigned to key and persisted to the credential. On the next use, googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) cannot find the expected top-level token fields, corrupting the Google credential after its first refresh regardless of whether credential sharing is enabled.

title: Minimum token schema strips expiry and replaces the real refresh token with a placeholder
body: The computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] do not create the intended dynamic fields, and Zod strips unknown keys by default, so in sharing mode only access_token survives. Lines 25-27 then set refresh_token to the literal string "refresh_token". Callers such as Zoom and Office365 consequently lose expires_in/expiry information (producing NaN or stale expiry) and persist the dummy refresh token over the real one, breaking subsequent refreshes.

title: Sync-mode return value is incompatible with most refresh callers
body: When sharing is enabled this returns the raw fetch Response without checking response.ok or parsing JSON, while the fallback returns whatever each provider-specific refresh function returns. HubSpot expects token fields such as accessToken/expiresIn, Zoho apps expect an Axios response with .data, and Google expects a response with .data; a fetch Response provides none of these. Those integrations will throw, use undefined tokens, or persist an invalid credential object in sync mode.

title: Credential-sync request is sent without any authentication
body: The POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT contains only calcomUserId and appSlug, with no shared-secret header, signature, or other credential the parent application can use to authenticate Cal.com. An endpoint implemented to this contract cannot distinguish legitimate Cal.com requests from arbitrary callers who enumerate user IDs to elicit third-party access tokens.

title: Zoho Bigin passes credentialId where refreshOAuthTokens expects userId
body: refreshOAuthTokens treats its third argument as the Cal.com user ID and sends it as calcomUserId to the sync endpoint. This call passes credentialId instead of credential.userId. Credential and user IDs are unrelated, so in sync mode the parent application will look up the wrong user or fail to find one and return the wrong/no tokens.

title: Webhook handler has no error handling for malformed or undecryptable payloads
body: The Zod parse at line 31 and the symmetricDecrypt/JSON.parse at lines 57-59 are not wrapped in error handling, and the handler does not restrict the HTTP method. A malformed body, invalid ciphertext, or non-JSON decrypted value throws an unhandled exception and produces a 500 rather than a controlled 400 response, making integration failures indistinguishable from server faults.

title: New credential webhook and token-refresh branching have no tests
body: This PR adds an authenticated credential create/update webhook, AES decryption, a new token-response parser, and sync-mode branches across many calendar/video services, but adds no tests for valid/invalid webhook secrets, decryption failures, create versus update, or sharing-enabled versus disabled refresh behavior. Several of the shipped paths change return shapes and persisted credential formats, and there is no regression coverage to catch that corruption.

title: Minimum token schema does not implement the intended permissive schema
body: The two computed keys are both produced by calling toString() on Zod objects, so they collapse to the same property name ("[object Object]") instead of creating number/unknown catch-all entries. The resulting schema only retains access_token, and Zod strips the provider's other fields such as refresh_token, expires_in/expiry, scope and token_type. Callers that persist or spread the parsed data therefore lose the fields needed for subsequent refreshes.

title: Helper injects the literal string "refresh_token" as a real refresh token
body: When the parsed response has no refresh_token, the helper sets refresh_token to the literal placeholder "refresh_token". This is especially harmful in credential-sharing mode because the minimum schema strips any real refresh_token before this check. Callers that persist parsed data overwrite the stored provider refresh token with the placeholder, so later direct provider refreshes fail with an invalid grant.

title: Credential-sync branch returns a different type from the normal refresh branch
body: The normal branch returns whatever refreshFunction returns, which varies by caller: a Google response object with .data, a HubSpot SDK token object, or an Axios response with .data. The sync branch always returns a raw fetch Response, which has none of those shapes. Google then reads res.data.access_token, HubSpot reads expiresIn/accessToken, and the Zoho services read tokenInfo.data, so synced refreshes return undefined values, throw, or persist an unusable Response object instead of refreshed credentials.

title: Google refresh stores the SafeParse wrapper object as the credential key
body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod SafeParse result ({ success, data }), but this code assigns that whole result to `key` and writes it to prisma.credential. The stored key is therefore { success: true, data: {...credentials} } rather than the credential fields themselves. The next GoogleCalendarService construction calls googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key), which no longer matches, breaking the credential after the first token refresh even when credential sharing is disabled.

title: Salesforce refresh uses prisma without importing it
body: The newly added refresh block calls prisma.credential.update, but this file has no prisma import. Constructing the Salesforce service after a token refresh will fail type checking and, if emitted, throw a ReferenceError at runtime, breaking Salesforce event creation.

title: Salesforce token schema requires fields Salesforce refresh responses do not return
body: salesforceTokenSchema requires scope in addition to id, issued_at, instance_url, signature, access_token and token_type. Salesforce's refresh-token response normally returns access_token, instance_url, id, token_type, issued_at and signature, without scope. With credential sharing disabled parseRefreshTokenResponse uses this schema and throws, and with sharing enabled the minimum schema strips the fields anyway, so valid Salesforce refreshes are rejected.

title: Salesforce client is built with the old access token after refreshing
body: getClient fetches and stores a refreshed token, but constructs the jsforce Connection with accessToken: credentialKey.access_token, i.e. the expired token from the original credential, instead of accessTokenParsed.data.access_token. The API calls made through this connection will still use the stale token and fail authentication until some later construction happens to reload the credential.

title: Zoho Bigin sends the credential ID as the Cal.com user ID to the sync endpoint
body: refreshOAuthTokens expects its third argument to be the credential owner's userId and sends it as calcomUserId, but this call passes credentialId (the credential row ID). The parent platform will look up the wrong user, fail to find tokens, or return another user's access token, which would then be stored under this credential and used for this user's Zoho Bigin account.

title: Synced Office 365 refresh loses the expiry transform and overwrites the refresh token
body: In sharing mode parseRefreshTokenResponse strips expires_in, so the refreshTokenResponseSchema transform that converts expires_in into an absolute expiry never runs, leaving the stored expiry in the past and forcing a refresh on every API call. The helper also adds the placeholder refresh_token, and the spread of tokenResponse.data overwrites the real stored Microsoft refresh token with that placeholder.

title: Synced Zoom refresh persists a placeholder refresh token and NaN expiry
body: In sharing mode the minimum schema strips expires_in and refresh_token from the sync endpoint response, then the helper inserts refresh_token: "refresh_token". This code assigns newTokens.refresh_token into the stored key and computes expiry_date from newTokens.expires_in, which is undefined, producing NaN. The persisted Zoom credential is corrupted and subsequent zoomTokenSchema parsing/refresh attempts fail.

title: Webex synced refresh can never satisfy the refreshed-token schema
body: refreshOAuthTokens documents that the sync endpoint returns only an access token and expiry, but this code still validates the response with webexRefreshedTokenSchema, which requires the literal Webex scope, token_type Bearer, a real refresh_token and refresh_token_expires_in. A conforming sync-endpoint response is therefore always rejected with "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned", so Webex token refresh does not work when credential sharing is enabled.

title: Webhook handler has no error handling for malformed or undecryptable payloads
body: appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse, symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse can all throw, and the handler has no try/catch or safeParse handling. An authenticated caller sending a malformed body, non-encrypted keys string, or non-JSON decrypted payload causes an unhandled exception and a 500 response instead of a controlled 400, making integration failures hard to diagnose and retry correctly.

title: Credential create/update is a racy find-then-write with no uniqueness guard
body: The handler does findFirst for (userId, appId) and then creates a credential if none is found. Two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user and app can both observe no credential and both insert one, creating duplicate credentials; later deliveries only update the first row found, leaving a stale duplicate that other findFirst-based code may pick up. The comment acknowledges upsert cannot be used, but no transaction or unique handling replaces it.

title: Webhook secret is compared with a timing-unsafe string comparison
body: The shared webhook secret that authorizes writing arbitrary user credentials is checked with !==, which short-circuits on the first differing character and can leak prefix information through response timing. This endpoint should compare the supplied header and CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET with a constant-time comparison such as crypto.timingSafeEqual (with length handling).

title: New credential-writing webhook and token-sync helpers have no tests
body: This PR adds a security-sensitive endpoint that authenticates by shared secret, decrypts payloads and creates/updates stored OAuth credentials, plus token-refresh helpers used by many integrations, but adds no tests (the PR checklist also states tests were not added). There is no coverage proving disabled-sharing rejection, wrong-secret rejection, decrypt/create/update behavior, or that synced refresh responses preserve expiry and refresh tokens for each provider shape, which is how the return-shape and field-stripping regressions above shipped unnoticed.

title: Salesforce refresh uses prisma without importing it
body: The newly added token-refresh block calls prisma.credential.update, but this file never imports prisma. Every Salesforce client construction that reaches the refresh block will throw ReferenceError: prisma is not defined, breaking Salesforce event creation, updates, searches, and deletions even when credential sharing is disabled.

title: Google credential update stores the Zod SafeParse wrapper instead of the token
body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a SafeParse result shaped {success, data}, but this code stores that whole object as the credential key. Previously the parsed credential itself was stored. After the first token refresh, credential.key no longer has access_token/refresh_token at the top level, so the next googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) in googleAuth will fail and the Google Calendar credential becomes unusable. This affects normal non-sharing refreshes too.

title: Minimum token schema strips real fields and fabricates a refresh_token
body: When sharing is enabled, minimumTokenResponseSchema only declares access_token plus nonsense computed keys, and Zod strips undeclared fields such as expires_in, expiry timing, scope, token_type, and the real refresh_token. The helper then sets refresh_token to the literal string "refresh_token". Callers such as Office365 and Zoom spread/copy that result into the stored credential, overwriting the real refresh token with a placeholder and losing expiry data (producing NaN expiry in Zoom), so the credential is corrupted and the next refresh fails.

title: Sync path returns a fetch Response to callers expecting axios/SDK token objects
body: refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response when sharing is enabled, but several wrapped refresh functions do not return fetch Responses: HubSpot expects a HubspotToken object with accessToken/expiresIn, Zoho Bigin/CRM expect an axios response with .data, and Google expects an object whose .data contains the token. In sharing mode those callers read undefined properties, compute NaN expiry dates, throw when dereferencing .data, or persist an empty/incorrect token object, so token refresh breaks for those apps instead of using the synced token.

title: Zoho Bigin sends credential id as the Cal.com user id to the sync endpoint
body: biginAuth/refreshAccessToken only receives credentialId (the Credential row id), and this call passes that value as refreshOAuthTokens' userId argument. The sync endpoint therefore receives calcomUserId=<credential id>, not the owner's user id, so it can return tokens for the wrong user or fail to find the user, causing wrong-account credentials or broken Zoho Bigin refreshes.

title: Salesforce now refreshes unconditionally and then uses the old access token
body: getClient now performs a Salesforce refresh-token POST on every service construction, regardless of whether the stored token is valid or credential sharing is configured, and rejects based on response.statusText !== "OK" even though statusText can be empty for successful HTTP/2 responses. Worse, after parsing/updating the refreshed token, the returned jsforce Connection is still built with credentialKey.access_token (the old token) at line 106, so the refresh cost/failure mode is added but the refreshed token is not used for the API connection.

title: Lark refresh expects provider-shaped nested data that the sync contract does not provide
body: refreshOAuthTokens documents the sync endpoint response as only an access token and expiry date, but Lark's refresh code builds new credentials from data.data.refresh_token, data.data.refresh_expires_in, and data.data.expires_in. A minimal synced response will make those fields undefined, storing refresh_token=undefined and NaN refresh/access expiry dates in the credential and returning an undefined access token, corrupting the Lark credential after the first synced refresh.

title: Webex synced refresh is rejected by the unchanged full Webex token schema
body: When sharing is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens is supposed to return only an access token and expiry, but Webex still validates the response with webexRefreshedTokenSchema, which requires the literal Webex scope, Bearer token_type, refresh_token, and refresh_token_expires_in. A minimal synced token response will always fail safeParse and reject with 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned', so Webex cannot refresh tokens in sharing mode.

title: Webhook handler lets validation and decryption errors throw as unhandled 500s
body: The handler calls appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body) and later symmetricDecrypt plus JSON.parse with no try/catch or safeParse handling. Malformed JSON, an invalid userId/appSlug type, a bad encryption key, or non-JSON decrypted keys will throw out of the Next.js handler and produce an unhandled 500 rather than a controlled 400 response, making integration failures hard to diagnose and retry correctly.

title: Credential webhook has a find-then-create race that can create duplicates
body: The handler does prisma.credential.findFirst for (userId, appId) and then creates a credential if none was found, with no unique constraint/upsert or transaction covering the check. Two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user and app can both observe no credential and both create rows; later webhooks update only the findFirst row while other code may read a stale duplicate, leading to inconsistent synced credentials.

title: No tests cover the credential-sharing webhook or refreshed-token branches
body: This PR adds a security-sensitive webhook that authenticates with a shared secret, decrypts third-party OAuth keys, and creates/updates credentials, plus sharing branches in many token-refresh paths, but adds no tests for valid sync creation/update, wrong-secret rejection, disabled sharing, malformed encrypted payloads, or the sharing-enabled refresh behavior. The PR description also states tests were not added, so the credential-corruption and return-type regressions in these paths are not guarded against.

title: Team admin/owner check uses AND instead of OR
body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...). Team admins who are not owners (and, depending on the helpers' role checks, potentially all non-owner admins) therefore fail this test and receive FORBIDDEN unless they are also the organizer or an attendee, so the team-admin path the variable name promises does not work. The two checks should be combined with OR.

title: Guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, pending, or past bookings
body: After the permission check the handler unconditionally creates attendees, updates the calendar event, and sends confirmation-style emails, without checking booking.status or that the booking is in the future. Adding guests to a CANCELLED/REJECTED/PENDING or already-ended booking persists bogus attendees and emits AttendeeScheduled/AddGuests emails with CONFIRMED ICS invites for an event that is not a confirmed future event.

title: Duplicate and blacklist filtering is case-sensitive and ignores duplicates within the request
body: uniqueGuests only removes a guest when guest === attendee.email exactly and when blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) exactly, even though the blacklist entries were lower-cased. Case variants such as Guest@Example.com vs guest@example.com are treated as new, and two identical (or case-variant) emails inside the same guests array both pass because the filter never de-duplicates the input against itself; createMany then inserts duplicate Attendee rows and duplicate calendar/email recipients.

title: Guests array is unbounded
body: guests is z.array(z.string().email()) with no min/max or uniqueness constraint. Any authorized caller (including a mere attendee of the booking) can submit thousands of addresses in one request, causing thousands of Attendee rows, a getTranslation call per attendee, a calendar-attendee update, and an email fan-out to the organizer, team, and every attendee. A reasonable cap (and server-side uniqueness) is needed.

title: Email classification uses the raw guests list instead of the filtered uniqueGuests
body: The handler filters the request into uniqueGuests for insertion but then calls sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) with the original list. sendAddGuestsEmails decides who is a 'new' guest via newGuests.includes(attendee.email), so an address that was filtered out because the person is already an attendee is misclassified as newly added and receives an AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the AttendeeAddGuestsEmail sent to other existing attendees. Pass uniqueGuests instead.

title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials rather than the booking organizer's
body: EventManager is built from getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) and {...user}, i.e. whoever called the mutation. The handler explicitly authorizes team admins/owners and attendees, but for those callers their credentials will not contain the organizer's calendar credential (the booking query even loads booking.user.credentials, which are then ignored), so updateCalendarAttendees cannot update the organizer's calendar event while the database rows and notification emails still go out, leaving calendar invites inconsistent with the booking.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores disabled standard emails configuration
body: Unlike the other send* functions in this file, sendAddGuestsEmails accepts no eventTypeMetadata and never checks eventTypeDisableHostEmail/eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail, and the handler does not pass booking.eventType.metadata. Event types that have disabled standard host/attendee emails will still send organizer, team, and attendee emails when guests are added.

title: Invalid-email error state is not cleared after success or manual close
body: isInvalidEmail is set to true on a failed validation but onSuccess only resets multiEmailValue, and closing via Dialog onOpenChange (the X/Escape path calling setIsOpenDialog directly) resets neither value. After fixing the input and successfully adding guests, or after dismissing the dialog, reopening it can immediately show the stale 'Emails must be unique and valid' error before the user types anything.

title: Team admin/owner check requires both roles instead of either
body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. A team admin who is not the owner, and in role models where admin and owner are distinct membership roles an owner who is not also recorded as admin, therefore fails the check. Despite the variable name and intended permission, the team admin/owner authorization path is effectively dead and those users receive FORBIDDEN unless they are also the organizer or an attendee. The condition should be an OR.

title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials instead of the booking organizer's
body: The handler explicitly permits non-organizers (team admins/owners and attendees), but then calls getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) and constructs EventManager from ctx.user. For those callers this does not contain the booking organizer's calendar credential/destination calendar, even though the booking query loaded booking.user with credentials. updateCalendarAttendees can therefore fail to update the organizer's external calendar, or attempt to use an unrelated credential of the caller, while the database attendees and emails claim the guests were added. The organizer's booking user/credentials should drive the calendar update.

title: Guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, pending, or past bookings
body: After loading the booking, the handler never checks booking.status or whether the event has ended before inserting attendees, updating the calendar, and sending emails. The new email templates generate ICS data with status CONFIRMED, so adding a guest to a cancelled booking can send a confirmed invitation and push attendees back toward the external calendar event, and adding guests to a past event sends meaningless invitations. The mutation, and ideally the UI action, should be restricted to appropriate upcoming confirmed bookings.

title: Duplicate and blacklist checks are case-sensitive and do not deduplicate the request itself
body: uniqueGuests filters only by exact `guest === attendee.email`, does not lowercase/trim guests, and does not deduplicate guests against each other; the server schema also only validates that each string is an email. Blacklisted addresses are lowercased before comparison while incoming guests are not, so `Blocked@Example.com` can bypass a lowercase blacklist entry. A direct tRPC caller can likewise submit the same address twice, or an existing attendee address with different casing, and create duplicate Attendee rows. Normalize emails and enforce uniqueness server-side before createMany.

title: Email sender receives the raw guest list rather than the guests actually added
body: The handler filters the request into uniqueGuests for insertion, but calls sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) with the original unfiltered list. In email-manager, any attendee whose email is in that list is classified as a new guest and receives AttendeeScheduledEmail. Consequently, when a request mixes an already-existing attendee with a genuinely new guest (reachable from the dialog, which does not know existing attendees), the existing attendee is sent a fresh full scheduling invitation even though they were not added. Pass uniqueGuests instead.

title: Guest list has no maximum size
body: guests is an unbounded array of emails. An authorized caller can submit thousands of addresses in one mutation, causing a large createMany, one translation load per attendee, a calendar update, and an email fan-out to every attendee. This enables resource exhaustion and use of the deployment as an invitation-email relay. Add a reasonable server-side max (and min) to the schema rather than relying on the dialog UI.

title: Add-guests emails ignore disabled standard email settings
body: sendAddGuestsEmails always sends organizer and attendee emails and does not accept or check eventTypeMetadata, unlike sendLocationChangeEmails and the other booking email helpers that honor disableStandardEmails for host/attendee. The handler loads booking.eventType but does not pass its metadata, so event types that have disabled standard emails will still generate these notifications. Thread the metadata through and apply the existing host/attendee disable checks.

title: Invalid-email error state is not reset after success or dialog dismissal
body: isInvalidEmail is set when validation fails, but the mutation onSuccess only resets multiEmailValue and closes the dialog; it does not reset isInvalidEmail. Closing via the dialog's onOpenChange (for example the X/Escape path) also bypasses the Cancel button's reset. Reopening Add Guests after a corrected, successful submission can therefore show 'Emails must be unique and valid' above a fresh empty form. Reset the flag on success and whenever the dialog closes or its value changes.

title: Team admin/owner authorization uses AND instead of OR
body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...), so a team admin who is not also the team owner fails the check. Such users are rejected with FORBIDDEN unless they are separately the organizer or an attendee, even though the variable name and intended permission indicate admin OR owner should be sufficient.

title: Guest de-duplication and blacklist checks are case-sensitive and do not de-duplicate the request itself
body: uniqueGuests only removes guests that exactly match an existing attendee email and compares the raw guest string against a lower-cased blacklist. It does not lower-case guests or de-duplicate within the submitted array. A direct API call such as ['A@example.com', 'a@example.com'], or re-adding an existing attendee with different capitalization, can create duplicate attendee rows and duplicate invites, and a blacklisted address can bypass the blacklist by changing capitalization.

title: Email sender receives the raw guest list instead of the filtered unique guest list
body: The handler filters duplicates/blacklisted addresses into uniqueGuests for the database write, but then calls sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) with the original unfiltered input. Existing attendees who were correctly filtered out of the write are therefore classified as new guests by sendAddGuestsEmails and receive a fresh AttendeeScheduledEmail invitation instead of the guests-added notification.

title: Guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, pending, or past bookings
body: The handler never checks booking.status or booking.endTime before creating attendees, updating the calendar, and sending guests-added/scheduled emails with a CONFIRMED ICS. A direct API caller can therefore mutate a cancelled, rejected, unconfirmed, or already-ended booking and cause new calendar/email invitations to be sent for an event that is not an accepted upcoming booking.

title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials instead of the booking organizer's
body: The handler explicitly authorizes non-organizers (team admins/owners and attendees), but then loads credentials with getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) and constructs EventManager from the caller. The calendar event and destination calendar belong to booking.user/organizer, so for those authorized non-organizer callers EventManager cannot use the organizer's calendar credential and the external calendar attendee update can silently fail while the database and emails succeed, leaving systems inconsistent. The booking organizer's credentials/user should be used.

title: Guest list has no maximum length
body: The input schema accepts an arbitrarily large guests array. The handler then creates all attendees, loads a translation per attendee, updates the calendar, and sends email to the organizer/team plus every attendee. Any authorized caller, including an attendee, can use this for large-scale email fan-out/resource consumption and send platform-generated meeting invitations to many arbitrary addresses; the server should enforce a reasonable cap.

title: Guests-added emails ignore disabled standard email settings
body: sendAddGuestsEmails unconditionally emails the organizer, team members, and all attendees and takes no eventTypeMetadata argument. Unlike the other booking-change senders in this file, it does not check eventTypeDisableHostEmail/eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail, and the handler does not pass booking.eventType metadata. Event types configured to disable standard host/attendee emails will still send these emails.

title: MultiEmail imports the @calcom/ui barrel from inside the same package
body: MultiEmail lives in @calcom/ui but imports Button, EmailField, Icon, and Tooltip from the '@calcom/ui' barrel, while that barrel exports MultiEmailLazy which dynamically imports this file. This creates a self-referential import cycle and pulls the whole UI barrel into a component that was specifically made lazy, risking circular-chunk/undefined-import problems and defeating the intended code splitting. The component should import from relative component paths.

title: Dialog state is not reset when closed without Cancel
body: multiEmailValue and isInvalidEmail are only cleared by the explicit Cancel button or on mutation success. Closing the dialog through the dialog close affordance, Escape, or overlay only calls setIsOpenDialog, so previously typed emails and a stale validation error remain the next time the dialog is opened and can be submitted accidentally. Editing the emails also does not clear isInvalidEmail after the user fixes the input.

title: No tests cover the new addGuests mutation
body: This PR adds a new mutation with organizer/team-admin/team-owner/attendee authorization branches, duplicate and blacklist filtering, database writes, calendar updates, and email fan-out, but adds no handler or integration tests. Tests should cover at least outsider rejection, admin versus owner access, organizer/attendee access, duplicate/blacklisted guests, and non-accepted bookings so authorization and filtering regressions are caught.

title: Retry-based deletion is not scoped to unscheduled SMS reminders
body: The second OR branch matches any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1, regardless of method or scheduled state. It can therefore delete EMAIL/WHATSAPP reminders and, if an SMS reminder reaches retryCount 2 while also becoming scheduled, delete a reminder already scheduled with Twilio. Deleting the scheduled row removes the referenceId needed to cancel that Twilio message if the booking is cancelled or rescheduled, so the SMS can still be delivered. Scope this branch to method SMS and scheduled: false.

title: Reminders with no recipient or message never accrue retries
body: Scheduling, the retry increment for a null Twilio result, and error handling only occur when both message and sendTo are truthy. A reminder whose booking has no smsReminderNumber/sendTo, or whose generated message is empty, remains scheduled:false with retryCount 0 and is fetched again on every cron run until its scheduledDate passes, which is the retry loop this PR is meant to eliminate. Such permanently unschedulable reminders should increment retryCount or otherwise be logged and eventually removed.

title: Unguarded retry update in catch can abort the whole cron run
body: The catch block now awaits prisma.workflowReminder.update without its own error handling. If that update rejects, for example because the row was deleted concurrently, the database is transiently unavailable, or the original exception came from a workflowReminder update, the exception escapes the per-reminder loop and handler. All remaining unscheduled reminders are then skipped for that run and the endpoint errors instead of continuing as the previous log-and-continue behavior did. The increment should be best-effort and not abort processing of subsequent reminders.

title: Retry increments use a stale read instead of an atomic increment
body: Both retry paths set retryCount to reminder.retryCount + 1 using the value fetched at the start of the cron run. Overlapping cron invocations, which are possible while this handler sequentially makes slow Twilio calls, can read the same count, both fail, and both write the same incremented value, losing failures and keeping bad reminders alive beyond the intended two failures. Use Prisma's atomic data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } } operation instead.

title: No tests cover the new retry and deletion state machine
body: The PR adds retry increments on Twilio-null and exception paths and deletion when retryCount exceeds 1, but adds no automated tests. There is no coverage proving that a failure increments once, a successful schedule does not get deleted, reminders are removed only after the intended number of failures, or one reminder's failure does not prevent later reminders from being processed. Add handler tests with mocked Prisma and Twilio for these cases.

title: Retry-count deletion is not restricted to SMS reminders
body: The second branch of the deleteMany OR only checks retryCount > 1, without method: WorkflowMethods.SMS or any scheduled/scheduledDate restriction. This SMS cron therefore owns deletion for EMAIL and WHATSAPP WorkflowReminder rows as well, and can delete a future or already-scheduled reminder solely because retryCount exceeds 1. The deletion scope should be restricted to the SMS reminders this handler manages.

title: Reminders with no recipient or message never reach the retry limit
body: retryCount is incremented only when twilio.scheduleSMS returns a falsy value or throws inside the if (message?.length && sendTo) block. If sendTo is missing/empty or the generated message is empty, scheduleSMS is never called and retryCount is never incremented, so the reminder is rescanned on every cron run until its scheduledDate passes. That leaves one of the permanently-failing cases this PR is meant to stop retrying unbounded; the same applies to reminders skipped at the workflowStep/booking check.

title: Unguarded update in catch block can abort the whole cron batch
body: The catch block now awaits prisma.workflowReminder.update without its own error handling. If that update fails, for example because the reminder was deleted after findMany when its booking was cancelled (Prisma P2025) or because of a transient database error, the exception escapes the catch, terminates the for loop, prevents all remaining unscheduled reminders from being processed in that run, and the handler returns an error instead of completing. The retry-count update should be guarded so one bad reminder cannot poison the batch and the original error is still logged.

title: Retry count uses a stale read-modify-write instead of an atomic increment
body: Both retry increments write reminder.retryCount + 1 using the value read at the start of the handler. If two cron invocations overlap, which is possible because this endpoint can be triggered while a previous long-running loop is still processing reminders, both invocations can read the same count and write the same incremented value, losing a failure and keeping a permanently failing reminder alive beyond the intended two attempts. Use Prisma's atomic { increment: 1 } operation instead.

title: Retry-count deletion is not scoped to unscheduled SMS reminders
body: The second branch of the deleteMany OR only checks retryCount > 1, without method: SMS or scheduled: false. As written it can delete EMAIL/WHATSAPP WorkflowReminder rows that have retryCount > 1, and can delete an already-scheduled reminder, losing its referenceId so a Twilio message already scheduled can no longer be tracked or cancelled. The retry cleanup should be scoped to SMS (and unscheduled) reminders like the fetch below.

title: Missing recipient or message never increments retryCount
body: The retry increment only happens inside `if (message?.length && sendTo)` when Twilio returns a falsy result, or in the catch block when an exception is thrown. If sendTo is missing/empty (e.g. no smsReminderNumber) or the generated message is empty, the block is skipped entirely: no scheduling attempt, no retryCount increment, and the row stays scheduled:false and is re-fetched on every cron run until its scheduledDate passes. That leaves one of the failure modes this PR is meant to bound retrying indefinitely; the empty-recipient/message case needs an increment or removal path too.

title: Unhandled update in catch block can abort the whole cron run
body: The catch block now awaits prisma.workflowReminder.update without any nested error handling. If that update fails — for example the reminder was deleted between findMany and the catch (Prisma P2025), or the original error was a database failure — the exception escapes the per-reminder loop, all remaining unscheduled reminders are never processed, and the handler returns an error instead of continuing. Previously the catch only logged and moved on. The increment should be wrapped so a failure to record the retry is logged without poisoning the rest of the batch.

title: Retry increment uses a stale read instead of an atomic increment
body: Both increments (here and in the catch block at line 195) write `reminder.retryCount + 1` from the value fetched at the start of the run. The handler has no lock and makes slow sequential Twilio calls, so overlapping cron invocations can both read retryCount 0, both fail, and both write 1, losing increments and potentially keeping a permanently failing reminder below the >1 deletion threshold forever. Use Prisma's atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` instead.

title: findMany is removed without migrating production callers
body: The public findMany method is replaced by getBaseConditions, and getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions now return Prisma.Sql instead of Prisma WhereInput objects. The PR changes only this service and its test, with no production caller migrated to $queryRaw with getBaseConditions. Any existing caller using service.findMany or passing the returned conditions into a Prisma where clause will fail TypeScript compilation; all such call sites must be migrated in this PR or a compatibility adapter retained.

title: Event-type filter returns an unparenthesized OR fragment
body: When eventTypeId is the only filter, buildFilterConditions returns `("eventTypeId" = ...) OR ("eventParentId" = ...)` without outer parentheses. If a caller composes it naturally as `WHERE ${authConditions} AND ${filterConditions}`, PostgreSQL precedence parses it as `(auth AND eventTypeId = ...) OR (eventParentId = ...)`, allowing the eventParentId branch to bypass the authorization conditions. getBaseConditions happens to wrap the fragment, but the public getFilterConditions result no longer guarantees the grouping that the previous Prisma WhereInput object provided; the predicate itself should be wrapped in parentheses.

title: Team and org raw SQL branches are never executed against the database
body: The org and team authorization tests only compare Prisma.Sql objects constructed with the same template helper as the implementation, while the sole $queryRaw execution in the suite uses user scope with scalar userId/teamId predicates. The `= ANY(array)` bindings and `"isTeamBooking"` predicates used exclusively by team/org scopes are therefore never sent to PostgreSQL, so invalid array-parameter encoding, column names, or SQL syntax would pass these tests and fail only at runtime. Add $queryRaw execution tests for team and org scopes.

title: Public options type loses discriminated-union type safety
body: InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions makes teamId optional for every scope, replacing the previous discriminated union that required teamId exactly when scope is "team". A call site such as { scope: "team", userId, orgId } now compiles, fails zod validation inside the constructor, and silently yields the 1=0 condition for every query, turning a programming error into an empty insights result instead of a compile-time error. Keep the discriminated union for typed callers or make untrusted-input handling explicit.

title: Caching tests are deleted while caching logic remains
body: The PR deletes the Caching describe block, but InsightsBookingService still maintains cachedAuthConditions and cachedFilterConditions and returns those cached Prisma.Sql objects on subsequent calls. No remaining test verifies that a second call reuses the cached conditions instead of rebuilding them and repeating the membership/team database queries. Restore caching coverage, for example by asserting repeated calls return the identical object, or remove the caching logic intentionally.

title: PublicOptions weakens the discriminated-union contract for scope/teamId
body: InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions makes teamId optional for every scope, replacing the previous discriminated union in the constructor signature. A caller can now compile with scope: "team" and no teamId and will silently get the NOTHING_CONDITION (no insights data) instead of a compile-time error, and user/org callers can pass an irrelevant teamId that is silently ignored. Runtime zod validation still rejects the shape, but the exported type no longer documents or enforces the scope-specific requirements that callers previously got from InsightsBookingServiceOptions.

title: Public findMany method removed without migrating callers
body: The conversion deletes InsightsBookingService.findMany, which previously queried BookingTimeStatusDenormalized with the authorization and filter conditions, and replaces it with getBaseConditions returning only a Prisma.Sql fragment. No caller is updated in this PR, so any existing consumer calling service.findMany(...) will fail TypeScript compilation and lose the previous query behavior (including merging caller-supplied where/select arguments). Migrate all call sites to $queryRaw with getBaseConditions in the same change, or keep a compatible findMany wrapper.

title: OR authorization/filter fragments are returned without outer parentheses
body: buildOrgAuthorizationCondition and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition return fragments such as (A AND B) OR (C AND D) with no enclosing parentheses, buildFilterConditions similarly returns an unparenthesized eventType OR at line 106, and getBaseConditions returns these fragments unwrapped when only one kind of condition exists. Because AND binds tighter than OR in SQL, a caller composing the public result as WHERE ${conditions} AND <date or status condition> will apply the extra condition only to the last OR branch; the first team-booking branch will ignore it, returning rows outside the requested range/filter. Wrap each top-level returned condition in parentheses so the fragments are safely composable.

title: Team/org ANY(array) SQL is never executed against the database
body: The team-scope (line 278) and org-scope (line 305) tests only assert equality between two locally constructed Prisma.sql objects. The sole executed $queryRaw test at line 481 uses user scope, which contains no array parameter. Therefore the new "teamId" = ANY(${number[]}) and "userId" = ANY(${number[]}) parameter binding is never verified against PostgreSQL; if Prisma/Postgres cannot infer or encode the JS array parameter for these queries, both scopes fail at runtime while all tests pass. Add executed $queryRaw integration tests for team and org scopes asserting the returned booking ids.

title: Caching tests were deleted while caching logic remains
body: This PR removes the entire Caching describe block that verified repeated getAuthorizationConditions and getFilterConditions calls reuse cached results, but InsightsBookingService still maintains cachedAuthConditions and cachedFilterConditions state. No replacement test covers the cached paths, including the cached null filter case, so a regression in cache initialization or invalidation would go undetected. Restore the caching tests adapted to compare Prisma.Sql results instead of Prisma where-objects.

title: Deleting cache does not invalidate the connected-calendars query
body: The deleteCache mutation only shows a toast and invokes the optional onSuccess callback, unlike the disconnect mutation in the same component which invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars on settle. Callers are not required to pass onSuccess (the wrapper forwards an optional prop), so after a successful deletion the connectedCalendars query keeps returning the old cacheUpdatedAt, hasCache stays true, and the UI continues to show the stale timestamp and a Delete action for cache that no longer exists until some unrelated refetch occurs.

title: Cache status counts expired cache entries as live cache
body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups rows by credentialId and returns _max(updatedAt) with no expiresAt filter. CalendarCache rows are not removed when they expire (getCachedAvailability treats expiresAt < now as a miss, but the row remains), so the new UI will display 'Cache Status / Last updated' and offer Delete for credentials whose only cache rows are already expired and are never actually served.

title: Authorization failure is thrown as a generic Error instead of a TRPCError
body: When the credential does not belong to the session user the handler throws a plain Error('Credential not found or access denied'). tRPC wraps non-TRPCError throws as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, so a client error (unknown or foreign credentialId) is reported and logged as a server failure and callers cannot distinguish it. This should be a TRPCError (e.g. NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN) with an appropriate code.

title: Cache timestamp is always formatted in en-US regardless of user locale
body: The component localizes all strings through useLocale but formats cacheUpdatedAt with Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', ...). Users on non-US locales will see US-style dates/times (e.g. month/day order) in an otherwise localized UI; the formatter should use the user's locale returned by useLocale/i18n.

title: Unconditional empty updateMany marks every SelectedCalendar for the credential as freshly updated
body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) after the per-event-type loop. The write is unconditional and credential-wide: it bumps updatedAt on every SelectedCalendar row for the credential, including event-type-scoped rows and rows whose calendars were not in the fetched groups, and it runs even when the grouped map is empty and no cache entry was written. Anything reading SelectedCalendar.updatedAt as a freshness marker will be told calendars were refreshed when no cache fetch happened, and every cache population now pays an extra blanket UPDATE.

title: Webhook helper uses macOS-only sed syntax and still reports success on Linux
body: The in-place edit uses BSD/macOS syntax 'sed -i '' -E ...'. With GNU sed the empty string is taken as the script, the substitution is treated as a filename, and the edit fails; because the script has no 'set -e' or error check it then prints 'Updated GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL ...' anyway, leaving developers on Linux with a stale or missing webhook URL while believing it was set. The script is also unrelated to the calendar-cache feature it ships with.

title: dev:cron now shells out to unpinned npx tsx, which is not a declared dependency
body: The script was changed from ts-node (declared in devDependencies) to 'npx tsx cron-tester.ts', but tsx is not declared in apps/web's dependencies. npx will resolve and download whatever latest tsx is available at run time (failing offline and bypassing the lockfile's pinned versions), making the dev script non-reproducible. This unrelated tooling change should either declare tsx as a devDependency or be dropped.

title: No tests cover the new destructive deleteCache endpoint or cache-status query
body: The PR adds a destructive, ownership-checked tRPC mutation, a new groupBy repository method, and cache-status enrichment of connectedCalendars, but adds or updates no tests. The security-critical cases are unverified: deleting cache for one's own credential succeeds, deleting another user's credentialId is rejected and deletes nothing, and getCacheStatusByCredentialIds returns the latest updatedAt per credential. A regression in the findFirst ownership check would let any authenticated user wipe another user's calendar cache without any test failing.

title: Successful cache deletion does not refresh the connected-calendars query
body: The deleteCache mutation only shows a toast and calls the optional onSuccess callback, unlike the disconnect mutation below it which invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars on settle. In SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper the internal suspense query that supplies cacheUpdatedAt is therefore not refetched (onChanged is an optional external callback and may be undefined), so after a successful deletion the dropdown keeps showing the old timestamp and 'Delete cached data' action until a manual reload.

title: Cache status ignores expiry and reports dead cache entries as live
body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups all CalendarCache rows for the credentials without filtering expiresAt, while getCachedAvailability only serves rows with expiresAt >= now and entries expire after CACHING_TIME (30 days). A credential whose cache expired long ago is therefore reported to the UI as having a current cache with a 'Last updated' timestamp and a delete action, even though that cache is never used.

title: updateManyByCredentialId accepts the wrong Prisma input type
body: The method types its data parameter as Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput, which is the single-record update type and permits nested relation operations, but forwards it to prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany, which only accepts scalar SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput fields. Callers that pass relation data allowed by this signature will fail Prisma validation at runtime; the signature should use the update-many mutation input type (and the sole caller in CalendarService.ts passes {} relying on implicit @updatedAt behaviour rather than an explicit updatedAt value).

title: Committed webhook test script is macOS-only and writes outside the repo
body: This unrelated dev script uses `sed -i ''`, which is BSD/macOS syntax and fails under GNU sed on Linux, and it resolves ENV_FILE as '../.env' relative to the caller's working directory rather than the script/repo root, so running it from the repo root edits a .env file outside the repository. Its cleanup() also exits 0 even when no tunnel URL was obtained (lines 56-59), masking failures from callers.

title: dev:cron now depends on an unpinned npx download
body: The unrelated change replaces ts-node with `npx tsx cron-tester.ts` without adding tsx to devDependencies.
