Every run may download the latest unpinned tsx from the network, making the script fail offline and non-reproducible/supply-chain sensitive; tsx should be pinned as a devDependency (invoked via yarn) or the change dropped from this PR.

title: Cache timestamp is always formatted in en-US regardless of user locale
body: The 'Last updated' timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', ...) even though the component already uses useLocale for translations. Non-US users will see US date/time ordering and conventions instead of formatting in their configured locale.

title: No tests for the new cache deletion authorization or cache-status query
body: This PR adds a new destructive, ownership-checked mutation (deleteCacheHandler) and a new getCacheStatusByCredentialIds repository query consumed by connectedCalendarsHandler, but includes no tests at all. There is no coverage proving a user cannot delete another user's cache by credentialId, that deletion removes only that credential's rows, or that cacheUpdatedAt is mapped to the correct credential, so an authorization or mapping regression would ship undetected.

title: Expired cache entries are reported as active cache
body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups all CalendarCache rows for the credentials without filtering on expiresAt. getCachedAvailability treats rows with expiresAt in the past as cache misses, but this method will still return their updatedAt, so the UI displays an expired, unusable cache as present and offers to delete it. Filter to unexpired rows (expiresAt >= now) when computing status.

title: Deleting cache does not refresh the connected-calendars query
body: deleteCacheMutation only shows a toast and calls the optional onSuccess prop; unlike disconnectMutation below it never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. In SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper onChanged is optional and often undefined, so after a successful deletion the dropdown keeps showing the old cacheUpdatedAt timestamp and 'Delete cached data' action until a manual refetch, contradicting the success toast.

title: Handler bypasses the calendar-cache disabled/mock repository selection
body: The handler directly instantiates the concrete CalendarCacheRepository instead of going through the CalendarCache factory used elsewhere (CalendarCache.init), which returns CalendarCacheRepositoryMock returning [] when calendar-cache is disabled. When the feature is disabled, this endpoint will still query CalendarCache and surface cache status/deletion for leftover rows that the rest of the system intentionally ignores.

title: Cache deletion ignores disableConnectionModification gating
body: canDisconnect respects delegationCredentialId and disableConnectionModification, but hasCache is computed only from integration type and cacheUpdatedAt, and the early return is `if (!canDisconnect && !hasCache)`. On screens that set disableConnectionModification to make the connection read-only/managed, a Google credential with cache still renders the dropdown and enables the destructive delete-cache mutation, defeating the flag that hides disconnect in the same UI.

title: Every cache refresh rewrites all SelectedCalendar rows via an empty update
body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache now calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(credential.id, {}) on every cache population. That performs a write touching updatedAt for every SelectedCalendar row of the credential (including event-type-scoped rows), so updatedAt no longer reflects user selection changes, adds a DB write to a hot availability path, and is not even used by the new UI, which displays CalendarCache.updatedAt via cacheUpdatedAt.

title: Ownership failure is thrown as a generic 500 error
body: When the credential does not exist or does not belong to the caller, the handler throws a plain Error('Credential not found or access denied'). tRPC will surface this as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR rather than a client error such as TRPCError with NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN, polluting server-error monitoring and giving API consumers the wrong contract for an expected authorization outcome.

title: No tests for the new cache-status query or ownership-checked deletion
body: The PR adds a new authenticated mutation that deletes data based on credential ownership, a groupBy status query, and a mock implementation, but adds no tests. There is no coverage that another user's credentialId is rejected, that only the caller's credential cache is deleted, or that getCacheStatusByCredentialIds returns the latest updatedAt per credential, so an authorization or mapping regression would ship undetected.

title: Committed tunnelmole helper is macOS-only, cwd-dependent, and masks failures
body: `sed -i ''` is BSD/macOS syntax and fails under GNU sed on Linux; ENV_FILE='../.env' resolves relative to the caller's working directory rather than the script/repo root, so running it from the repo root writes ../.env outside the repo; and cleanup() always exits 0, so the failure paths at the tunnel-URL check report success to callers. This unrelated dev script should be fixed or removed from the feature PR.

title: dev:cron now depends on unpinned, undeclared tsx via npx
body: The script changes `ts-node cron-tester.ts` (ts-node is a declared devDependency) to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, but tsx is not declared anywhere in the workspace dependencies. Running the script will download an unpinned package at runtime, failing offline and introducing version/supply-chain drift; it is also unrelated to the calendar-cache feature. Add tsx as a devDependency or keep ts-node.

title: Cache timestamp is always formatted with the en-US locale
body: The cache_last_updated timestamp is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', ...)` regardless of the user's locale from useLocale. Non-English users will see US date/time formatting in an otherwise localized UI; format with the active locale instead.

title: Rescheduled bookings bypass the new delayed-cancellation mechanism
body: For a reschedule this calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true). The immediateDelete branch in emailReminderManager POSTs an immediate SendGrid cancel and returns without setting cancelled=true and without deleting the WorkflowReminder row. This reintroduces exactly the failure mode described in the PR (immediate cancels accumulate in SendGrid scheduled_sends until the 100 pending-cancellation limit makes new cancels fail, and failures are only logged/swallowed), and because the row is never marked cancelled the scheduleEmailReminders cron (which only retries rows with cancelled=true) will never retry it, so the old reminder email can still be sent for a rescheduled booking.

title: One failing SendGrid cancellation blocks all other cancellations in the cron run
body: The whole cancellation loop is wrapped in a single try/catch and awaits each client.request sequentially. If any one reminder fails (e.g. an invalid/null referenceId or a transient SendGrid error), execution jumps to the catch: all remaining reminders in remindersToCancel are never cancelled, and the prisma.workflowReminder.delete promises already collected in workflowRemindersToDelete are never awaited (Prisma promises are lazy, so they never execute). On the next run the same failing reminder can block the batch again, so reminders whose send time falls in that one-hour window will be delivered despite their bookings being cancelled/rescheduled. Each reminder needs its own try/catch and its row should only be deleted after its own cancel succeeds.

title: Workflow-reminder cancellation is fire-and-forget and may never be persisted
body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are async (the email path now does the prisma update that sets cancelled=true, or deletes an unscheduled row), but they are invoked inside forEach with no await or Promise.all. The handler then finishes and returns success without guaranteeing those updates completed; if the serverless invocation is frozen/terminated after the response, or the cron runs before the update lands, the reminder is never marked cancelled, is not picked up by the delayed-cancellation cron, and the scheduled email is still sent for the cancelled booking. The same un-awaited pattern is used in the other changed call sites.

title: Deleting a workflow/step loses any chance to retry a failed reminder cancellation
body: Workflow deletion (line 214) and step deletion (line 521) call deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., true), which only POSTs an immediate SendGrid cancel and intentionally retains the row, but the code then deletes the workflow/workflowStep, whose onDelete: Cascade relations delete the WorkflowReminder rows. If that immediate SendGrid call fails (including hitting the 100 pending-cancellation limit this PR is meant to avoid) or is lost because the call is not awaited, there is no row left with cancelled=true for the scheduleEmailReminders cron to retry, so the already-scheduled reminder email will still be sent even though the workflow/step is gone.

title: No tests cover the new delayed-cancellation state machine
body: This PR introduces a time-windowed cancellation flow (mark cancelled on booking cancel/reschedule, actually cancel at SendGrid only when scheduledDate is within one hour, delete unscheduled rows immediately, immediate-cancel for workflow/step deletion) but adds no automated tests for any of it. The branches in deleteScheduledEmailReminder and the cron selection/deletion in scheduleEmailReminders are exactly where regressions silently turn into emails being sent for cancelled bookings, so unit/integration tests mocking prisma and the SendGrid client for the scheduled, unscheduled, immediate and cancelled-within-one-hour cases should accompany the fix.

title: One failed SendGrid cancellation blocks all remaining cancellations
body: The entire cancellation loop is wrapped in a single try/catch and each SendGrid request is awaited inside the loop, while the accumulated prisma delete promises are only executed after the loop finishes. If one reminder fails to cancel (for example its batch was already cancelled, already sent, or SendGrid returns an error), execution jumps to the catch block, the deletes for already-cancelled reminders are never run, and every later reminder in remindersToCancel is never cancelled. Because the failing row is also not deleted or marked differently, the next cron run can hit the same poison-pill reminder again and repeatedly block other reminders that are due within the next hour, so those emails are still sent.

title: immediateDelete path has no deferred fallback if the SendGrid cancel fails
body: When immediateDelete is true, deleteScheduledEmailReminder posts the SendGrid cancellation and returns without deleting the workflowReminder row and without setting cancelled=true. This path is used for rescheduled bookings, deleted workflows, and deleted workflow steps. If that single SendGrid request fails, including the over-100-pending-cancellations failure this PR is meant to fix, the outer catch only logs the error and the reminder is left scheduled and not cancelled, so the scheduleEmailReminders cron query for cancelled=true reminders will never retry it and the old email will still be delivered. For reschedules there is also no cascade that removes the leftover row.

title: Workflow reminder cancellation is fire-and-forget after previously being awaited
body: updatedBookings.forEach calls the async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder functions but discards their promises. Before this change, the database reminder deletions were collected and awaited as part of prismaPromises; now setting cancelled=true for email reminders, or deleting SMS reminders, happens only inside these unawaited calls. The handler can return before those writes complete, their failures are not reliably observed, and the later cron job depends entirely on the cancelled flag having been persisted, so a lost or delayed write means the cron never cancels the SendGrid email for the cancelled booking.

title: Reschedule reminder cancellation try/catch cannot catch the async work and is not awaited
body: The code wraps originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach in try/catch, but deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are async and their returned promises are discarded. Asynchronous failures therefore do not reach log.error in the catch block, and rescheduling proceeds immediately to EventManager.reschedule and later scheduleWorkflowReminders without knowing whether the old reminders were cancelled or marked. If the unawaited cancellation is delayed or fails, the previous booking's reminder can remain live and be sent for the old time in addition to reminders for the rescheduled booking.

title: Bookings cancelled shortly before a reminder is due can still receive it
body: Cancelled reminders are only cancelled by the periodic cron once scheduledDate is within one hour, rather than at cancellation time. If a booking is cancelled after the last cron run but before the reminder's SendGrid sendAt time, for example five minutes before the reminder is due, the next cron run can occur after SendGrid has already delivered the message. The database row is marked cancelled=true in that interval, but nothing checks that flag at send time, so the new deferred design reintroduces a delivery window for last-minute cancellations and reschedules that the previous immediate cancellation avoided.

title: Twilio cancellation failure now prevents deleting the workflow reminder row
body: deleteScheduledSMSReminder now performs twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId) and the prisma workflowReminder delete in the same try block. If Twilio throws, for example because the message is already sent, already cancelled, or the SID is no longer cancellable, the catch block skips the database delete. Callers in this PR no longer delete the reminder row separately as they did before, so a failed Twilio cancellation leaves the scheduled reminder row in place instead of cleaning it up independently of the provider result.

title: One failing SendGrid cancellation blocks all other cancellations
body: All reminders are cancelled sequentially inside a single try block, while the Prisma delete operations are only executed by the Promise.all after the loop. If client.request throws for one reminder (for example an invalid, expired, or already-cancelled batch), the catch is taken, none of the queued deletes run, and every later reminder in remindersToCancel is never even attempted. The same failing reminder will be retried first on the next cron run, so other reminders whose scheduled time falls within the next hour can still be dispatched by SendGrid.

title: Deferred-only cancellation misses reminders that are due imminently
body: For a scheduled email this function now only sets cancelled=true and never cancels with SendGrid immediately, regardless of how soon the reminder is due. Cancellation therefore depends entirely on the periodic scheduleEmailReminders cron running before the SendGrid sendAt time. If a booking is cancelled a few minutes before its reminder and the next cron run happens after that time, SendGrid will already have sent the email; the cron's initial deleteMany for past scheduledDate rows then just removes the DB record. The previous immediate-cancellation behaviour covered this last-minute case.

title: Reschedule path bypasses the deferred cancellation mechanism and loses failures
body: Rescheduling calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true), which immediately POSTs a SendGrid cancellation instead of setting cancelled=true. This reintroduces the exact SendGrid pending-cancellations cap (100) that this PR is meant to work around for rescheduled bookings. Worse, if that POST fails, deleteScheduledEmailReminder only logs the error and returns without deleting the row or setting cancelled, so the scheduleEmailReminders cron (which only looks for cancelled=true) will never retry and the reminder for the old booking time will still be sent.

title: Workflow deletion uses immediate cancellation then destroys the retry record
body: Deleting a workflow calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., true), which immediately cancels in SendGrid but neither deletes nor marks the WorkflowReminder row; the code then deletes the workflow at line 220, and the WorkflowStep/WorkflowReminder cascade deletes the reminder rows. If the immediate SendGrid cancellation fails (including via the pending-cancellation cap described in the PR, or a transient error), the error is swallowed inside deleteScheduledEmailReminder and the DB record that the new cron-based deferred cancellation could have retried is gone, so the scheduled email will still be sent for a deleted workflow. The same pattern is used when a workflow step is deleted.

title: Workflow reminder cancellations are fired without being awaited
body: updatedBookings.forEach(... deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...) / deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)) discards the promises returned by these async functions. The handler then awaits only unrelated attendee/reference deletions and returns a 200 response, so there is no guarantee the prisma update setting cancelled=true (or the SMS/Twilio cancellation and row deletion) has completed before the request finishes; in a serverless invocation the work can be cut short after the response, leaving cancelled=false in the database and allowing the cron/SendGrid schedule to send the reminder for the cancelled booking. The surrounding code cannot observe or retry the failure because the promise is dropped.

title: Dynamic imports are all started eagerly, defeating lazy loading
body: Every value in the appStore object literal is an already-invoked import() call, so importing this module immediately starts loading all 28 app packages and their dependencies, even when the caller only needs one app. This defeats the intended on-demand loading, and because most of these promises are never awaited for a given request, a rejection from an unused optional app can surface as an unhandled promise rejection instead of being handled by the code that selected that app. Store lazy thunks such as () => import(...) or otherwise create the import only for the requested key.

title: Async forEach leaves calendar/video deletions unawaited and outside try/catch
body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) returns immediately, so Reschedule proceeds to send the reschedule email and return true before getCalendar and deleteEvent/deleteMeeting finish. Rejections from the async callback are not caught by the surrounding try/catch and become unhandled rejections, and on serverless runtimes the deletions may never complete after the response returns. Use await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...)) so deletions finish and errors are handled before continuing.

title: Async forEach leaves calendar/video deletions unawaited and outside try/catch
body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) returns immediately, so Reschedule proceeds to send the reschedule email and return true before getCalendar and deleteEvent/deleteMeeting finish. Rejections from the async callback are not caught by the surrounding try/catch and become unhandled rejections, and on serverless runtimes the deletions may never complete after the response returns. Use await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...)) so deletions finish and errors are handled before continuing.

title: Async forEach races reschedule email/webhook against booking deletions
body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) is not awaited, so the requestReschedule mutation immediately sends the reschedule email and webhooks while calendar/video deletion for the old booking is still pending at the dynamic-import step. The deletions can be lost if execution is frozen after the mutation returns, and failures become unhandled rejections rather than being surfaced or logged. Await Promise.all over a map of the deletion operations before sending the email/webhooks.

title: Recurring-booking calendar deletions are pushed to apiDeletes after it is awaited
body: The recurring-cancellation branch uses credentials.forEach(async ...) and pushes into apiDeletes only after awaiting getCalendar and calendar.deleteEvent. Because the forEach is never awaited, the handler reaches Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) at the end (and the earlier await apiDeletes in the paid path) before those pushes happen, so recurring calendar events are not reliably deleted before attendee/booking-reference rows are removed and the cancellation response is sent. Replace the forEach with an awaited for...of loop or await Promise.all(map(...)) that fills apiDeletes before it is consumed.

title: Dynamic imports are executed eagerly instead of lazily
body: Every value in the appStore object is created by immediately calling import(), so merely importing appStore starts loading all 29 app modules, including apps unrelated to the current request. This defeats the intended lazy/code-split loading, adds startup and module-evaluation cost to every consumer of getCalendar, videoClient, and payment code, and creates rejected promises for unused apps that may surface as unhandled rejections if a module fails to load. Store loader functions such as () => import('./applecalendar') and invoke them at call sites, or provide an async getter.

title: Async forEach leaves calendar/video deletions unawaited
body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) discards the callback promises. Now that getCalendar must be awaited, deleteEvent/deleteMeeting are not even invoked before the function sends the reschedule email and returns true; in a short-lived/serverless invocation they can be dropped, and any rejection becomes an unhandled rejection rather than being caught by the surrounding try/catch, which only catches synchronous errors. Replace forEach with await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...)) so deletions complete and failures are logged.

title: requestReschedule does not await async calendar/video deletions
body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) discards the callback promises. After this change the callbacks suspend at await getCalendar, while the mutation immediately proceeds to send the reschedule email and webhooks and can finish before the old calendar/video events are deleted, leaving orphan events that keep the old time busy; failures are also unhandled rejections. Use await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...)) before sending the email/returning.

title: Recurring-booking calendar deletions race past apiDeletes collection
body: In the allRemainingBookings recurring branch, credentials are processed with .forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(...) }). Those callbacks suspend at the await, so when line 652 later evaluates Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)), concat snapshots an apiDeletes array that does not yet contain the calendar deletions. The handler can therefore delete attendees/booking references and return while recurring calendar events are still present or never deleted, and deletion errors are unhandled. Replace the async forEach with a for...of loop or await Promise.all(...map(...)) that populates apiDeletes before it is awaited.

title: Dynamic imports are started eagerly for every app
body: Every value in the appStore object literal is an import() call, so all 28 calls are evaluated as soon as this module is loaded. Code that needs only one app (for example getCalendar for a single credential) therefore still starts loading every calendar, video, CRM, and payment app and retains all of their side effects and memory/startup cost, defeating the intended per-app lazy loading. A rejected import for an app that is never used can also surface later as an unhandled rejection from the cached promise. Store thunks such as `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")` and invoke the thunk at lookup time instead.

title: Async forEach leaves calendar/video deletion fire-and-forget
body: The forEach callback was made async to await getCalendar, but Array.prototype.forEach ignores the returned promises. Reschedule therefore proceeds to send the reschedule email and return true without waiting for calendar.deleteEvent or deleteMeeting to even start (the await on getCalendar defers them past the forEach), so in a request-scoped/serverless execution the old events can be left behind, and any rejection becomes an unhandled rejection that the surrounding try/catch cannot catch. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` or a for...of loop.

title: requestReschedule does not wait for old calendar/video deletion
body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach now takes an async callback whose promise is discarded. Immediately afterwards the mutation sends the reschedule email and webhooks and returns, while the awaited getCalendar/deleteEvent and deleteMeeting work is still pending; it may be abandoned when the request ends and its failures are unhandled, leaving the supposedly cancelled calendar event and video meeting active. Await the deletions with Promise.all over map (or a for...of loop) before continuing.

title: Recurring-cancellation deletions can miss the later Promise.all entirely
body: For recurring bookings, calendar deletions are collected by pushing into apiDeletes from inside an async forEach callback that first awaits getCalendar and then awaits deleteEvent before pushing. The handler later awaits Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)), but concat snapshots apiDeletes at that moment, typically before those async callbacks have pushed anything. The handler can therefore delete the booking's attendees/references (losing the external uids needed to retry) and return while the external calendar deletions are not awaited or have not run, orphaning events on users' calendars. Collect the deletion promises synchronously via map/Promise.all or a sequential for...of and await them before the database cleanup completes.

title: Slots inside a date override bypass the busy-time check
body: In checkIfIsAvailable, when a slot's date matches a date override and the slot is inside the override window, the function returns true immediately. It never reaches the busy.every(...) check against existing Cal bookings and connected-calendar busy times. A fixed or round-robin host who has a date override on a day can therefore be shown as available at times when they already have a booking or calendar event, allowing double-bookings on override days.

title: Only the first same-day date override is considered
body: The dateOverrides.find(...) callback returns true as soon as the slot falls outside the first override that shares the slot's date. If a user has two override ranges on the same day (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-17:00, which Cal.com allows as separate availability rows), a slot inside the second range is judged against the first range, find() stops, and checkIfIsAvailable returns false. Valid slots in the second and later override ranges of the day are incorrectly removed, notably for fixed hosts in round-robin events.

title: Override containment check admits partially overlapping slots
body: A slot is treated as inside a date override unless its end is at/before the override start or its start is strictly after the override end. A slot that starts before the override begins but ends inside it (e.g. 13:30-14:30 for a 14:00-18:00 override) is not flagged as outside and is reported available, and a slot starting exactly at the override end is also treated as inside because isAfter is used instead of isSameOrAfter. Bookings can therefore start before the host's override availability begins or exactly when it ends.

title: Empty date-override detection compares Dayjs objects with ===
body: The condition dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes') === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, 'minutes') compares two distinct Dayjs object references, so it is always false and the intended zero-length override case never triggers. For an 'unavailable' date override where start equals end, a slot straddling that instant satisfies neither the before-start nor after-end branch, so the function falls through to returning true and offers a slot on a day the host marked unavailable.

title: Working-hours gate is wrong for split schedules and days off
body: The workingHours.find(...) check returns 'outside working hours' if ANY working-hour entry for that weekday does not cover the slot, so a host with split hours (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00 on the same day) has afternoon slots rejected because the morning entry does not cover them. Conversely, if no entry lists the slot's weekday at all, find() returns nothing and the check passes entirely, so a fixed host can still be booked on a day off whenever a round-robin host's availability generated that slot. Both cases defeat the fixed-host enforcement this block was added for.

title: Working-hours end check uses the slot start instead of the slot end
body: Both start and end are computed as slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute(), so the end > workingHour.endTime comparison never looks at when the proposed booking actually finishes. A 60-minute slot starting at 16:30 in a 09:00-17:00 schedule passes the check even though it ends at 17:30, letting fixed hosts be booked beyond the end of their working hours.

title: Timezone-shifted override can be assigned to the wrong invitee day
body: The new code converts the override wall time by the invitee-minus-organizer offset and keeps only hour/minute, discarding the resulting date, while the activeOverrides filter above still selects overrides by comparing the unshifted UTC-encoded start against the invitee day. For an organizer ahead of the invitee (e.g. a 09:00 override in UTC+10 viewed from UTC), the converted time is 23:00 on the previous invitee day, but the filter attaches it to the following invitee day, so the slot is offered a day late instead of on the correct day.

title: No test covers the fixed-host round-robin override scenario
body: The PR description states the main fix is that date overrides of fixed hosts restrict round-robin events, but the only added test re-queries a personal (non-team) event in Asia/Dhaka versus Asia/Kolkata and expects identical UTC slots. Nothing exercises a ROUND_ROBIN event type with an isFixed host who has a date override, the new checkIfIsAvailable override/working-hours paths for fixed and loose hosts, or a timezone change that crosses a date boundary, so regressions in the primary claimed behavior would go undetected.

title: Slots inside a date override bypass all busy-time checks
body: In checkIfIsAvailable, when a slot is on a date-override day and is not detected as outside the override, dateOverrideExist is true and the function immediately returns true. It never reaches the busy.every(...) check at the end, so calendar events and accepted Cal bookings overlapping that slot are ignored for fixed and round-robin hosts on override days, allowing double-booking.

title: Date-override check mishandles multiple and partially-overlapping overrides
body: The dateOverrides.find callback returns true as soon as a slot is outside one override on that day, even if the slot is inside a second override the same day (e.g. split availability 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-17:00), so valid slots are rejected. Conversely it only tests slotStartTime.isAfter(override end), not slotEndTime, so a slot starting inside an override but ending after it (17:30 for 60 minutes with an override ending 18:00) is treated as inside and made bookable.

title: Working-hours check rejects split shifts and allows non-working days
body: The workingHours.find callback returns true when the slot is outside ANY one working-hour entry, so with split hours on a day (09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00) every slot is outside at least one entry and gets rejected. If no entry includes slotStartTime.day() at all, find returns nothing and execution falls through to the busy check, treating a non-working day as available. Additionally lines 141-142 compute both start and end from slotStartTime, so a slot starting before closing time but ending after workingHours.endTime is never rejected.

title: Empty date-override comparison uses Dayjs object identity
body: dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...) compares two distinct Dayjs objects by reference and is always false, so the intended detection of a zero-length override (start equals end, meaning unavailable) never triggers. A slot exactly at the shifted start of such an override then falls through, sets dateOverrideExist, and is returned as available.

title: Converted overrides lose day shifts when the invitee-local time crosses midnight
body: The override conversion extracts only hour()*60+minute() from the offset-shifted start and end, discarding any date change. For example an organizer override ending after midnight in the invitee timezone yields an endTime smaller than startTime (e.g. 20:30-00:30 becomes 1230-30), and buildSlots skips boundaries where start >= end; because the user's normal working hours were already removed for that override, the user incorrectly shows no availability instead of the evening portion, and overrides shifted to the previous/next invitee day are placed on the wrong day.

title: Optional override timeZone is used without a fallback
body: TimeRange.timeZone is optional in packages/types/schedule.d.ts, but getSlots unconditionally calls dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone). Callers that supply dateOverrides without timeZone (permitted by the type, and the pre-existing shape) will have the organizer offset computed against the system/default timezone instead of the organizerTimeZone already passed into getSlots, producing wrongly shifted override slots rather than falling back to organizerTimeZone.

title: No test covers the claimed round-robin fixed-host date-override fix
body: The only added test queries a single-user event in a second timezone and asserts the same UTC slots. There is no scenario with schedulingType ROUND_ROBIN, a fixed host with a date override and a loose host, nor a busy booking on an override day, so the new checkIfIsAvailable dateOverride/workingHours filtering for fixed and loose hosts - the main behaviour this PR claims to fix - is untested and regressions such as busy times being ignored on override days would not be caught.

title: Working-hours check rejects split schedules and allows days off
body: The new check returns unavailable when Array.find locates ANY same-weekday working-hour range that the slot start is outside. A host with split hours on one day (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00) will have a valid 10:00 slot rejected because it is outside the second range. Conversely, if the host has no working-hour entry for that weekday, find returns undefined, execution falls through to the busy check, and the host can be considered available on a day off. Additionally lines 141-142 set both start and end from the slot start, so a slot starting inside working hours but ending after them is never rejected. The predicate must instead require that at least one range fully contains [slotStart, slotEnd].

title: Slots inside a date override bypass busy-time checks
body: When a slot is deemed inside a date override, checkIfIsAvailable returns true at line 133-135 before reaching the busy.every check at the end of the function. Therefore a fixed or round-robin host who has a date override covering a time but also has a Cal booking or connected-calendar event at that time is reported available, and the slot remains bookable (for round-robin the host also remains in slot.userIds). Date-override availability must still be intersected with busy times.

title: Date-override matching mishandles multiple ranges and boundary-straddling slots
body: The find callback returns true as soon as the slot is outside the first override for that date, so a slot contained in a second override range on the same date is rejected. The containment test is also incomplete: a slot that starts before an override starts but ends inside it triggers neither the slotEnd<=overrideStart nor slotStart>overrideEnd branch, so it is treated as inside although part of the event lies outside the override; a slot starting exactly at override end is likewise treated as inside because isAfter is false. Slots should be accepted only when some override satisfies slotStart >= overrideStart and slotEnd <= overrideEnd.

title: Empty date-override comparison is always false
body: Line 114 compares two distinct Dayjs objects with ===, which compares object identity and is always false, so the special case for a zero-length override (start equal to end, used to mark a date unavailable) is dead code. A slot straddling that instant (slotStart before it and slotEnd after it) then falls through, dateOverrideExist is true, and the function returns the host as available on a day they marked unavailable. The instants must be compared with isSame/valueOf.

title: Timezone-converted override loses day rollover across midnight
body: The converted override start/end are reduced to hour()*60+minute(), discarding any day shift produced by adding the invitee-organizer offset. If applying the invitee offset pushes the override end past local midnight, endTime wraps to a small value while startTime stays large, so buildSlots discards the range as start>=end and the override disappears entirely (both the pre-midnight part on the start day and the post-midnight part on the next day, which activeOverrides will not select because the override did not start that day). Minutes outside the 0-1439 range, or an explicit split at midnight, are needed.

title: No test exercises the round-robin fixed-host date-override fix
body: The only added test is a second timezone query on the pre-existing single-user scenario (hosts: [], no ROUND_ROBIN schedulingType). The PR's primary claim - that a fixed host's date override restricts a round-robin event while round-robin hosts remain bookable - and the new checkIfIsAvailable path for fixed/loose hosts are therefore never exercised, so regressions such as split working hours, multiple override ranges, or overrides combined with busy bookings would pass this suite.

title: Migration assumes legacy embed settings always have database rows
body: The migration dereferences execute(...)[0]['id'] for the embed_category lookup and, if that is 0, does the same for uncategorized_category_id on line 15. Site settings are only persisted when overridden, so a site that never set embed_category (or whose stored value does not exactly match a category name) has no joined row; indexing the empty result raises instead of falling back, aborting the upgrade. The embeddable_hosts lookup below correctly checks cmd_tuples, but these two lookups do not.

title: Migration inserts legacy hosts verbatim, bypassing normalization and using unsafe SQL interpolation
body: Legacy embeddable_hosts values could contain entries such as http://example.com/path (the old SiteSetting check handled those), but this INSERT stores each raw line directly in embeddable_hosts.host, bypassing EmbeddableHost's before_validation stripping. EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares lower(host) against URI(referer).host (a bare hostname), so migrated scheme/path entries will never match and previously-allowed sites stop embedding after upgrade. The '#{h}' interpolation also breaks the migration (or injects SQL) if a stored line contains a single quote.

title: Update and destroy return 500 for a missing embeddable host
body: update uses EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and passes the result to save_host, which immediately calls host.host=; destroy similarly calls host.destroy on the result. A stale or mistyped id (for example a record deleted in another admin tab) yields nil and a NoMethodError/500 instead of a 404 response.

title: before_validation crashes when host is nil
body: The callback unconditionally calls self.host.sub!, and the model has no presence validation. Creating or updating a record without a host (reachable through the new admin API by omitting embeddable_host.host) raises NoMethodError before validates_format_of can produce a validation error, turning bad input into a 500. Guard nil and add a presence validation.

title: Plural embedded hydration replaces missing records with undefined and discards the ids
body: For *_ids keys the new code maps every id through _lookupSubType and unconditionally assigns the result and deletes the original key. When an id is not present in the side-loaded root collection (or the collection is absent), _lookupSubType returns undefined, so the model property becomes an array containing undefined entries and the original ids are lost. The singular branch only replaces the id when a record was found; the plural branch should likewise preserve ids or omit unresolved entries rather than manufacturing undefined associations (affects embeddable_hosts, colors, and other *_ids payloads).

title: Saved host does not reflect the server-assigned default category
body: When categoryId is null the Rails controller substitutes SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id, but the save callback ignores the returned category_id and instead sets category from the stale local categoryId via Discourse.Category.findById(null). The row is then displayed with no category even though the server stored the uncategorized category, and a later edit action dereferences host.category.id (line 26), which can throw for exactly these rows. Use the category_id returned by save (or look the category up from it) before clearing edit mode.

title: Duplicate hosts are allowed, making the per-host category ambiguous
body: There is no uniqueness validation on host and the new table has no unique index. An admin (or a double submit) can create two EmbeddableHost rows for the same hostname with different categories; record_for_host then uses .first with no ordering, so TopicEmbed.import can assign imported topics to an arbitrary one of those categories and the result can change as rows are added or removed.

title: Hosts saved with a port can never match an incoming referer
body: The format validation on line 2 explicitly permits host values such as example.com:8080 and the before_validation only strips scheme and path, so the port is stored. record_for_host compares lower(host) to URI(host).host, and Ruby's URI#host strips the port, so it compares 'example.com:8080' to 'example.com' and never matches. Such a host validates in the admin UI but can neither embed comments nor determine a category for imported topics; strip the port on save or compare host and port consistently.

title: Category and embeddable-host fabricators were written to each other's files
body: spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb now contains only the embeddable_host fabricator, while the newly added spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains the category, diff_category, happy_category and private_category fabricators. Fabrication loads both files so tests still pass, but the swapped contents are misleading and make it likely a future edit or deletion removes the wrong definitions; move each fabricator into the file named for it.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category was never customized
body: When the legacy embed_category setting has no row in site_settings (the common case where the default '' was never overridden) or its named category no longer exists, the JOIN returns zero rows and execute(...)[0] is nil, so ['id'] raises NoMethodError. The intended `if category_id == 0` fallback is never reached, blocking the upgrade; the uncategorized fallback lookup on line 15 has the same unguarded [0] pattern.

title: Migration stores legacy hosts verbatim so prefixed hosts stop matching
body: Legacy embeddable_hosts values could contain entries such as 'http://discourse.org' or 'https://example.com/1234' (the old SiteSetting matcher stripped scheme/path). This raw-SQL INSERT bypasses EmbeddableHost's before_validation trimming, so the stored host remains the full URL while EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares lower(host) against only URI(url).host ('discourse.org'); such migrated hosts will silently stop being allowed after the upgrade until manually re-saved. The unescaped '#{h}' interpolation also breaks the INSERT if a legacy value contains a single quote.

title: Update/destroy return 500 for a stale or nonexistent host id
body: update and destroy assign host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first, which is nil for an unknown or already-deleted id, and then call save_host(host)/host.destroy on nil. Concurrent admins deleting/editing the same row (or a stale client) therefore get a NoMethodError 500 instead of a 404/JSON error.

title: before_validation crashes on a nil host instead of failing validation
body: The callback unconditionally calls self.host.sub!. If create/update is called without a host key, the controller assigns nil and validation raises NoMethodError, returning a 500 rather than the render_json_error 422 path that a blank/invalid host should take.

title: Hosts with an explicit port can be saved but never match
body: The format validation on line 2 explicitly permits a port suffix (e.g. 'example.com:8080'), and before_validation strips only scheme and path, so such a host is stored with its port. record_for_host then extracts uri.host, which drops the port, and compares it to the stored 'example.com:8080', so host_allowed? is always false for a host the admin UI accepted.

title: Edit crashes when a host has no resolvable category
body: The edit action does this.get('host.category.id') without a guard. When category_id is dangling (category deleted) or hydration could not resolve the category, host.category is undefined and clicking edit throws a TypeError, making that row impossible to fix from the UI. The save path has the related issue of setting host.category from Category.findById(null) when no category is chosen, even though the server defaults a blank category_id to the uncategorized category.

title: Plural embedded hydration replaces missing records with undefined and discards the ids
body: For *_ids keys the new code unconditionally maps each id through _lookupSubType, assigns the result to the plural property, and deletes the original *_ids key. Unlike the singular branch (which preserves the id when nothing is found), if the root payload lacks the side-loaded collection or omits one record, the property becomes an array containing undefined entries and the original ids are lost, so consumers iterating the collection (e.g. embedding's embeddable_hosts) hit undefined objects instead of knowing which ids were referenced.

title: No uniqueness constraint on embeddable host names
body: The table has no unique index on host and EmbeddableHost validates only the host format, so the same host (including case variants like 'Example.com' vs 'example.com', which record_for_host matches case-insensitively) can be created multiple times with different categories. record_for_host then returns .first with no ordering, making the category chosen for embedded topics from that host arbitrary.

title: Category and embeddable-host fabricator file contents are swapped
body: spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb now defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host), while the new spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines the :category, :diff_category, :happy_category and :private_category fabricators. Tests still pass only because all fabricator files are loaded together; the swapped names mislead future edits and deleting or modifying the 'embeddable host' fabricator file would actually remove the category fabricators used across the suite.

title: Migration crashes when the legacy embed_category setting was never persisted
body: The migration dereferences execute(...)[0]['id'] for a query joining site_settings to categories on the embed_category setting. Site settings that were never customized are not stored as rows, so for the common case where embed_category was never set this query returns zero rows, [0] is nil, and nil['id'] raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration and the deploy/upgrade. The fallback on lines 14-16 makes the same assumption about an uncategorized_category_id row existing. The migration must handle missing rows (e.g. check cmd_tuples / nil before indexing) and fall back safely.

title: Migration inserts legacy hosts verbatim, bypassing normalization, so migrated hosts stop matching
body: Legacy embeddable_hosts values are inserted with raw SQL instead of going through EmbeddableHost, so the model's before_validation stripping of scheme and path never runs. Values previously accepted and handled by SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? such as 'http://discourse.org' or 'https://example.com/1234' are stored verbatim, while EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares lower(host) against URI(referer).host (e.g. 'discourse.org'), so those migrated hosts will never be allowed after the upgrade and embedding silently breaks for them. The unescaped interpolation of h into the INSERT also breaks the migration if a stored value contains a single quote. Normalize (and safely quote/bind) each host before inserting it.

title: Host format validation is inconsistent with host lookup and rejects valid hosts
body: The format regex allows an optional port (:[0-9]{1,5}), but record_for_host looks up URI(host).host, which strips the port, so a saved host like 'example.com:8080' can never equal the stored string and will never be allowed or assigned a category. Conversely the regex restricts the TLD to 2-5 letters, rejecting valid embed hosts the old free-form setting accepted, such as example.museum or example.technology. Validation, storage normalization, and lookup need to agree on ports and TLD length.

title: before_validation crashes on a nil host instead of failing validation
body: The before_validation block calls self.host.sub! unconditionally. When host is nil (EmbeddableHost.new with no attributes, or a create/update request missing the host param), this raises NoMethodError and produces a 500 rather than a validation error rendered by render_json_error. There is also no presence validation for host or category_id. Guard the normalization for blank values and add a presence validation so invalid input is reported cleanly.

title: No uniqueness constraint on host makes the host-to-category mapping ambiguous
body: Nothing prevents duplicate host rows: the model has no uniqueness validation and the migration creates the table without a unique index. An admin can create the same host twice with different categories, after which record_for_host's unordered .first picks an arbitrary row, so topics imported from that host are filed into a nondeterministic category and host_allowed?/category behavior depends on database row order. Add a case-insensitive uniqueness validation and a unique database index (after normalizing case in storage).

title: Update and destroy raise NoMethodError for a nonexistent host id
body: Both update (line 10) and destroy (line 15) use EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and then immediately call save_host(host) or host.destroy. For a stale or invalid id the record is nil, so save_host fails setting host.host and destroy fails on nil.destroy, returning a 500 instead of a 404. Look the record up with find (letting ActiveRecord raise RecordNotFound) or explicitly render a not-found error when it is absent.

title: Clicking edit crashes when the host has no resolved category
body: The edit action does this.get('host.category.id') without checking that category exists. A host's category is undefined when its category was deleted, and also right after saving a new host without choosing a category: save() sets category from Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')) with a null categoryId while the server silently defaults to the uncategorized category, leaving host.category undefined in the client. Clicking the pencil then throws a TypeError and the row can no longer be edited until a page reload. Guard the lookup (host.category && host.category.id) and set the client category to what the server actually assigned.

title: Category and embeddable-host fabricator file contents are swapped
body: spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb now contains only the embeddable_host fabricator, while the newly added spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains all of the category fabricators (category, diff_category, happy_category, private_category). Tests still pass because Fabrication loads every file regardless of name, but the mislabeled files are misleading and invite duplicate-definition mistakes when someone edits the file matching the fabricator name. Move each definition into the file named after it.

title: New admin endpoints have no behavioral test coverage
body: The specs for Admin::EmbeddableHostsController and Admin::EmbeddingController only assert that the classes inherit from Admin::AdminController. None of the new behavior is exercised: create/update success and validation failure, the blank-category fallback to the uncategorized category in save_host, destroy, or the embedding show payload with its hosts. Regressions in these endpoints (including the nil-record handling) would not be caught. Add request/controller specs covering those paths for a logged-in admin.

title: Duplicate downsize definition silently replaces the original API
body: Ruby does not support method overloading, so the new three-argument self.downsize at line 149 replaces the four-argument self.downsize defined at line 145. Existing callers that pass separate max_width and max_height (optionally with opts) will now raise ArgumentError instead of resizing, while the first definition becomes dead code. Remove the old definition and update all callers, or implement a single signature that handles both dimension forms.

title: Client upload limit is hardcoded and ignores site and file-type settings
body: validateUploadedFile previously used Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so images and attachments could have different configured limits. Replacing it with a constant 10 MB rejects valid uploads on sites configured above 10 MB and accepts attachments or images that the server will later reject on sites configured below 10 MB. The same hardcoded value at line 246 also makes the 413 error message report 10 MB regardless of the actual configured limit.

title: Remote-image download cap no longer respects max_image_size_kb
body: FileHelper.download is now always limited to 10 megabytes instead of SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes. Sites allowing images larger than 10 MB will fail to fetch otherwise valid remote images, while sites with a smaller limit will download and process needlessly large files before downsizing. The pre-downsize fetch cap should be derived consistently with the client limit and the configured settings.

title: Percentage downsizing is passed to gifsicle as an invalid WxH dimension
body: The controller calls OptimizedImage.downsize with the dimension string "80%", but for animated GIFs downsize_instructions_animated forwards that string to resize_instructions_animated, producing `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`. Gifsicle expects a WxH size for --resize-fit (percentage scaling is done with --scale), so the command fails, animated GIFs are not downsized, and the controller retries the failing command five times before the oversized upload is rejected.

title: Downsize failures are ignored while converting the upload in place
body: OptimizedImage.downsize returns false when conversion or optimization fails, but this loop ignores the result and repeats the operation up to five times on the same tempfile.path used as both source and destination. A failing or partially successful conversion therefore wastes expensive ImageMagick/ImageOptim runs and can leave the only copy of the upload truncated or converted before Upload.create_for consumes it. Convert to a separate temporary output, check the result, and only replace the original after a successful downsize (breaking out of the loop on failure).

title: No tests cover the new automatic downsizing behavior
body: The PR adds the downsize loop, changes OptimizedImage.downsize's public signature, and changes client/server size limits, but adds no specs. There is no coverage that an oversized image is reduced below max_image_size_kb, that an image still oversized after five attempts is rejected cleanly, that animated GIFs work, or that existing width/height downsize callers still function, so regressions such as the duplicate downsize definition would not be caught.

title: Second downsize definition overrides the existing width/height API
body: Ruby does not support method overloading by arity. This new three-argument downsize definition replaces the width/height version defined immediately above it at lines 145-147. Existing callers using downsize(from, to, width, height) will now treat width as a complete dimensions string and height as opts, producing wrong geometry or a TypeError, while callers passing width, height, and opts will raise ArgumentError. The old signature must be retained compatibly or every existing caller updated.

title: In-place downsizing ignores conversion failure and can destroy the upload
body: OptimizedImage.downsize returns false when conversion or optimization fails, but this call ignores the result and uses the same tempfile path as both input and output. A failed or partial ImageMagick/ImageOptim operation can therefore truncate or corrupt the only copy of the uploaded file, after which the loop retries the failed operation up to five times and line 72 proceeds with whatever remains. Downsizing should write to a separate file, check the result, and only replace the original after success.

title: No server-side size limit is enforced before expensive image conversion
body: The 10 MB limits added elsewhere are only in client-side JavaScript and in the URL-download branch. A direct multipart request can bypass JavaScript and submit a much larger image, causing this code to run as many as five full ImageMagick and ImageOptim passes before Upload.create_for performs its normal size validation. An authenticated user can consequently trigger very large CPU, memory, and disk consumption, including with a highly compressed image that expands greatly when decoded. The controller should enforce the intended maximum input size server-side before invoking downsizing.

title: Downsizing is applied unsafely to SVG and animated image originals
body: The condition accepts every filename considered an image and sends it through convert with the first-frame selector. This bypasses the SVG special case elsewhere in OptimizedImage, where SVG files are copied rather than converted, so an oversized vector can be rasterized, invalidated, or changed in format. Likewise, when animated thumbnails are disabled, an animated GIF original is reduced to its first frame rather than merely having a static thumbnail. SVG handling and preservation of animation for the stored original need separate treatment.

title: Hard-coded 10 MB client limit ignores per-type site settings
body: validateUploadedFile receives a type and previously used the corresponding max_image_size_kb or max_attachment_size_kb setting. Replacing that lookup with a fixed 10 MB value means attachments larger than 10 MB are rejected even when the site allows them, while non-image attachments above a lower configured attachment limit pass the client check, are not downsized by the server, and then fail only after being uploaded. The same hard-coded value is repeated for the 413 error at line 246. The image pre-downsizing allowance should not replace attachment validation or disregard configured limits.

title: No tests cover the new downsizing behavior
body: The pull request adds a percentage-based OptimizedImage.downsize form, a five-attempt controller loop, changed client limits, and changed download limits, but includes no spec or JavaScript test changes. There is therefore no coverage proving percentage geometry works, that the loop terminates at the configured byte limit, that conversion failure preserves or rejects the upload safely, or that animated and vector images retain their expected format.

title: Second downsize definition overrides the width/height version
body: Ruby replaces a method when it is defined again, so the three-argument downsize defined here makes the width/height downsize at line 145 dead code. Any existing caller passing from, to, width, and height will now raise ArgumentError instead of resizing, breaking the previous public API. The two signatures need to be merged or given different names.

title: Percentage downsizing does not work correctly for animated GIFs
body: This passes the dimension string "80%" while forwarding SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails. For an animated GIF, OptimizedImage dispatches to the gifsicle path, whose --resize-fit option expects pixel geometry such as 800x600 rather than a percentage, so the command can fail or produce an unintended size. When animated thumbnails are disabled, the ordinary ImageMagick path reads only frame [0], silently flattening an uploaded animated GIF based on a thumbnail preference rather than preserving the original animation.

title: Failed in-place downsizing can corrupt the uploaded file
body: The same tempfile path is used as both conversion source and destination, and the boolean result of OptimizedImage.downsize is ignored. If conversion or ImageOptim fails, the loop retries up to five times against a file that may have been partially overwritten and then line 72 uploads whatever bytes remain, instead of retaining the original file or returning a clean error. Conversion should write to a separate temporary file and replace the upload only after success.

title: Remote-download limit ignores the configured maximum size
body: API URL downloads are now always capped at a hard-coded 10 megabytes instead of SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb. Sites that configured a lower limit will have the server fetch, store temporarily, and process files beyond their policy, while sites that configured a higher limit are incorrectly capped; the new image-only downsizer also does not make oversized non-image downloads conform to the relevant attachment limit.

title: Client validation hard-codes 10 MB for every upload type
body: validateUploadedFile receives a type but no longer uses Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so image and attachment limits are both replaced by 10 MB. Administrators with smaller limits get avoidable large uploads and server-side rejections, administrators with larger limits get incorrect client-side rejections, and the 413 handler at line 246 similarly reports 10 MB regardless of the configured limit.

title: State-changing unsubscribe is performed by an unauthenticated-token GET request
body: TopicsController#unsubscribe is exposed as a GET route in config/routes.rb and immediately changes the current user's notification level before rendering the Ember unsubscribe page. A logged-in browser therefore mutates state on any GET, with no confirmation or CSRF token: mail-scanner/link prefetching, a page refresh, or an tag on a third-party site can trigger it. It is also non-idempotent: watching/tracking is first downgraded to regular, and a second visit to the same email link then downgrades regular to muted, so merely reopening the confirmation page further changes the user's settings than the original click intended.

title: Unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser row
body: TopicUser.find_by can return nil for a logged-in user who has never visited or interacted with the topic, for example when an email link is opened while logged in as a different account than the recipient. The next line dereferences tu.notification_level, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 instead of creating a TopicUser record at the desired level (as TopicUser.change would) or handling the no-subscription case.

title: Unsubscribe bypasses the canonical TopicUser.change update path
body: The action assigns notification_level directly and calls tu.save!, bypassing TopicUser.change (used by TopicsController#set_notifications). TopicUser.change is the path that stamps notifications_changed_at and notifications_reason_id=user_changed and publishes a MessageBus /topic/:id notification_level_change message. Direct assignment leaves the change metadata stale and means other open clients showing this topic are not updated to the new notification level until reload.

title: unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url but MessageBuilder provides no fallback
body: config/locales/server.en.yml changes the shared unsubscribe_link string to interpolate %{unsubscribe_url}, and MessageBuilder#body (line 90) and #html_part (line 67) render that string whenever add_unsubscribe_link is true. MessageBuilder supplies defaults for site_name/base_url/user_preferences_url but not unsubscribe_url, and only UserNotifications#send_notification_email passes it. Any other existing caller that builds mail with add_unsubscribe_link: true alone (previously valid, as the old spec did) will now raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument for unsubscribe_url and fail to send. The builder should only append the per-topic sentence when unsubscribe_url is present, or provide a safe fallback.

title: New unsubscribe behaviour has no meaningful test coverage
body: The only spec change adds unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe" to the message_with_unsubscribe fixture; no example asserts that the per-topic URL actually appears in the text body or HTML part, and the PR adds no controller spec for TopicsController#unsubscribe at all. The slug-mismatch redirect, the watching/tracking->regular and regular->muted transitions, repeat-visit behaviour, anonymous access, and the missing-TopicUser case are therefore all untested and could regress silently.

title: Unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser row
body: TopicUser.find_by can return nil, for example when a mentioned or invited user, or a different logged-in user opening a forwarded email link, has never created a topic_users row for this topic. The next line calls tu.notification_level on nil, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 instead of creating or updating the notification level.

title: State-changing unsubscribe is performed by an unauthenticated-token GET request
body: The unsubscribe action mutates TopicUser.notification_level on a plain GET and the email link contains no signed token tied to the recipient. Any page, image, mail scanner, or link prefetcher that loads the URL in a logged-in browser will change that session user's notification level without a confirmation or CSRF token, and a forwarded link acts on whoever is logged in rather than the intended recipient.

title: Unsubscribe downgrade is not idempotent, so refreshing changes the level again
body: The action downgrades exactly one step on every GET: watching/tracking (levels 3/2) becomes regular (1), and a subsequent reload of the same unsubscribe URL then turns regular into muted (0). The final state therefore depends on how many times the email link is opened, prefetched, or refreshed, rather than always ending at the intended unsubscribed state.

title: Template name does not match the topicUnsubscribe route
body: The route added in app-route-map.js.es6 is the top-level route topicUnsubscribe, whose route, controller, and view files are all named topic-unsubscribe, so Ember looks for a topic-unsubscribe template. This file is registered as topic/unsubscribe, which corresponds to a nested topic.unsubscribe route that is never defined, so the unsubscribe outlet will not render this template and the page can be blank or raise a missing-template error.

title: unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url for every add_unsubscribe_link email
body: config/locales/server.en.yml adds %{unsubscribe_url} to the shared unsubscribe_link translation, and both body and html_part interpolate it from template_args, which has no default for unsubscribe_url. Email::MessageBuilder previously allowed add_unsubscribe_link: true by itself (the existing spec did exactly that before being edited here); any such caller or plugin mailer that does not also pass unsubscribe_url will now raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and fail to send.

title: Direct save! bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping
body: set_notifications and other notification-level changes go through TopicUser.change, which sets notifications_changed_at and notifications_reason_id and publishes a MessageBus notification_level_change. Assigning tu.notification_level and calling save! skips all of that, so open clients keep showing the old watching/tracking state and the change is recorded without the usual reason or timestamp.

title: No tests cover the new unsubscribe endpoint
body: The PR adds a state-changing TopicsController#unsubscribe action but the only spec change adds an unsubscribe_url argument to an existing MessageBuilder example without asserting the URL reaches the body. There is no controller spec exercising level transitions for watching/tracking/regular/muted users, the missing-TopicUser case, slug redirects, or unauthenticated access, so the main regressions in this feature would not be caught.

title: Unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser record
body: TopicUser.find_by can return nil, for example when a logged-in user opens an unsubscribe URL for a topic they have never visited, tracked, or been emailed about (such as a forwarded email link). The next lines call tu.notification_level and tu.save! without a nil check, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 instead of creating a muted/regular record for that user and topic.

title: State-changing unsubscribe is performed by an unauthenticated-token GET request
body: The unsubscribe action mutates notification_level on a plain GET with only the session cookie for authorization and no CSRF token or signed unsubscribe key. Any third-party page, forum post, email link scanner, or browser prefetcher that causes the victim's browser to request /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe will silently change the victim's notification setting. The mutation is also not idempotent: each repeated visit steps the level down again (watching/tracking to regular on the first visit, then regular to muted on a refresh or second visit), so prefetching, reloading the confirmation page, or revisiting the link produces a different result from the first click and can undo a level the user just re-selected on that page.

title: Unsubscribe bypasses the established TopicUser.change mechanism
body: set_notifications and other notification-level changes go through TopicUser.change, which stamps notifications_changed_at, sets notifications_reason_id to user_changed, creates the row if missing, and publishes a MessageBus notification_level_change so live clients update. This action instead assigns tu.notification_level directly and calls save!, so the change is recorded with a stale reason/timestamp and already-open clients and topic tracking state are never notified of the new level.

title: unsubscribe_link translation now requires an unsubscribe_url that MessageBuilder does not guarantee
body: config/locales/server.en.yml now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url} into the shared unsubscribe_link string, and both html_part (line 67) and body (line 90) render that string whenever add_unsubscribe_link is true. MessageBuilder provides defaults for site_name, base_url, and user_preferences_url but not for unsubscribe_url, so any caller that sets add_unsubscribe_link without also passing the new, undocumented unsubscribe_url (as the previous message_builder spec did) will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and fail to send the email. The builder should supply a fallback or only include the per-topic sentence when an unsubscribe_url is present.

title: New unsubscribe behavior has no effective test coverage
body: The only spec change adds unsubscribe_url to the MessageBuilder fixture but the example still only asserts that the user preferences URL appears in the body; it never asserts the per-topic unsubscribe URL is rendered in either the text or HTML part. There are also no specs for TopicsController#unsubscribe covering the watching/tracking-to-regular and regular-to-muted transitions, the slug redirect, or the missing-TopicUser case, so the endpoint's core behavior can regress (or crash) without a failing test.

title: Blocked-email lookup can be bypassed by changing letter case or whitespace
body: should_block? performs an exact database lookup with BlockedEmail.where(email: email), and neither BlockedEmail nor User normalizes email addresses before storage or comparison. PostgreSQL string equality is case-sensitive, so registering with Bad@SpamExample.com or with surrounding whitespace bypasses a blocked entry stored as bad@spamexample.com. The blocklist therefore does not reliably block the addresses it is meant to block; both blocked entries and candidate addresses should be stripped and downcased consistently before comparison/storage.

title: should_block? has a non-atomic write side effect during validation and can count one attempt multiple times
body: should_block? increments match_count with a read-modify-write (record.match_count += 1; record.save) from inside email validation. Concurrent registration attempts can read the same count and lose increments, and ordinary flows that call valid? and then save (as UsersController#create does) run validation twice, so one signup attempt increments the counter twice and performs two writes. A predicate used by a validator should be side-effect-free, or the statistics update should be a single atomic increment performed once outside validation.

title: Whitelist/blacklist domain regexp is not anchored to the end of the address
body: email_in_restriction_setting? builds Regexp.new("@(#{domains})") with no end anchor or domain-boundary check, so it matches a substring anywhere after '@'. With a whitelist of gmail.com, an address such as user@gmail.com.evil.example passes because it contains '@gmail.com', even though its actual domain is gmail.com.evil.example; user@gmail.comm also passes. Domain restrictions should compare the parsed domain (including an end anchor) instead of searching for a substring.

title: EmailValidator never checks that the value is a well-formed email address
body: validate_each only applies the whitelist/blacklist settings and the BlockedEmail check; it adds no format error for malformed values. Since User now relies on validates :email, email: true for server-side email checking, a direct POST to UsersController#create (bypassing the client-side Discourse.Utilities.emailValid check) with an email such as 'not-an-email' passes validation whenever no domain whitelist/blacklist is configured, creating an account whose activation mail can never be delivered.

title: rejectedEmails is a mutable array shared on the controller prototype
body: rejectedEmails: Em.A([]) is defined on the controller prototype, so the same array object is shared by every instance/reuse of the controller and is mutated by pushObject in createAccount. The list is never cleared, meaning an address rejected once (for example because it was temporarily blocked or taken) stays locally marked invalid for the rest of the session and can incorrectly block a later signup attempt with that address without any server re-check. It should be initialized per instance (e.g. in init) and reset when the modal/account flow starts.

title: Specs stub out the integration they should prove, so a disconnected User validation would still pass
body: The validator spec stubs BlockedEmail.should_block? and invokes validate_each directly, while blocked_email_spec only tests BlockedEmail in isolation. No spec verifies that building/saving a User with a blocked email actually fails validation (i.e. that validates :email, email: true in User resolves to this validator, is loaded, and runs under the email_changed? condition), and there are no regression specs for the whitelist/blacklist behavior moved out of User. The whole feature could be unwired from registration and all new tests would still pass.

title: Blocked-email matching is case-sensitive and can be bypassed
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? looks up the exact string with `where(email: email)`, and BlockedEmail neither downcases nor strips the address before saving or lookup. A blocked address such as bad@spam.com can therefore be resubmitted as Bad@Spam.com or with surrounding whitespace and miss the block, while the case-insensitive portions of Discourse treat those as the same email. The unique database/model check is likewise case-sensitive, so differently-cased duplicates of a blocked address can coexist. Normalize with the same email downcasing used elsewhere on both record creation and lookup (and ideally a case-insensitive uniqueness guarantee).

title: Validation performs a database write, so match statistics are counted repeatedly
body: EmailValidator calls BlockedEmail.should_block? during validation, and should_block? increments and saves match_count/last_match_at. Validation is not a one-time commit event: UsersController#create calls user.valid? and then user.save (which validates again), so one blocked signup attempt increments the counter at least twice, and any other code that merely calls valid?/save on a user with a changed email also records a 'match' even if the user is never persisted. Move the accounting out of the predicate/validator or make it happen once per create attempt; a validator query should be side-effect free.

title: match_count increment is a non-atomic read-modify-write
body: `record.match_count += 1` followed by `record.save` reads a value, increments it in memory, and writes it back. Two concurrent registration attempts matching the same blocked email can read the same count and both save count+1, losing an increment, and the full-record save can also overwrite concurrent changes to fields such as action_type. Use an atomic database increment (e.g. update_counters/increment_counter or a single UPDATE ... SET match_count = match_count + 1) for the statistics update.

title: The new email validator never checks that the value is an email address
body: EmailValidator.validate_each only applies the whitelist/blacklist domain settings and the BlockedEmail check; it contains no format check. Since User now relies on `validates :email, email: true` (app/models/user.rb:47) as its email validator, a direct API request with a malformed value such as 'not-an-email' passes server-side validation as long as it is present and unique, creating an account whose activation/welcome mail can never be delivered. Add a format validation (using the project's existing email format rules) before the domain/blocked checks.

title: Specs stub out the integration they are meant to prove
body: The validator spec stubs BlockedEmail.should_block? and calls validate_each directly on a fabricated user, while blocked_email_spec tests BlockedEmail in isolation.
