Nothing exercises the full path that a User with a real blocked email fails to save through `validates :email, email: true, if: :email_changed?`, so a broken validator registration, autoload problem, or email_changed? condition would let blocked signups through while all new specs still pass. Add a User-level example (and a whitelist/blacklist example for the logic moved out of User) that saves/validates against a real BlockedEmail record without stubbing.

title: Blocked-email lookup can be bypassed by changing email case
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? performs an exact where(email: email) lookup using the raw user-supplied value, and neither BlockedEmail nor EmailValidator downcases or strips the address before storage or lookup; User.new_from_params also assigns the submitted email unchanged. PostgreSQL string comparison and the unique index are case-sensitive, so an address blocked as bad@spam.example can register as Bad@SPAM.example, and BlockedEmail rows differing only by case can coexist. Normalize the email (for example with Email.downcase and strip) both when creating BlockedEmail records and when checking them.

title: Validation has a write side effect and counts one signup attempt multiple times
body: EmailValidator.validate_each calls BlockedEmail.should_block?, which increments match_count and saves the BlockedEmail row. Validation is not a single commit-time event: UsersController#create calls user.valid? and then user.save, and save validates again, so one blocked signup attempt increments the counter twice. Any other valid? check, or a save that ultimately fails for an unrelated reason such as the password, also records a match even though no account attempt completed. Separate the pure blocked check from hit recording, or record the hit only once at the point an attempt is actually rejected.

title: match_count increment is a non-atomic read-modify-write
body: should_block? loads the BlockedEmail row, does record.match_count += 1 in memory, and saves it. Two concurrent attempts with the same blocked email can both read the same count and both write count+1, losing one hit; the full-row save can also overwrite concurrent changes to the record. Use an atomic database increment such as update_all("match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ...") or increment_counter instead.

title: rejectedEmails is shared mutable state on the controller prototype
body: rejectedEmails is initialized as Em.A([]) in the class definition passed to extend(). In Ember, mutable array/object values declared this way live on the prototype and are shared rather than copied per instance, and createAccount mutates that array with pushObject while nothing ever clears it. Rejected addresses can therefore leak across controller instances and remain rejected for the lifetime of the app/session instead of being scoped to one account-creation flow. Initialize the array per instance (for example in init) and reset it when the create-account modal is shown or closed.

title: Raw-HTML posts bypass HTML sanitization
body: Post#cook returns the stored raw text verbatim for the new raw_html cook method, and TopicEmbed uses that method for imported content. The feed-polling path passes arbitrary RSS/Atom HTML directly to TopicEmbed without Readability's tag whitelist or any other sanitizer, after which the result is stored as cooked HTML and rendered raw. A malicious or compromised feed item containing script tags, event-handler attributes, or other active markup therefore becomes stored XSS for forum visitors. Imported HTML must be passed through a whitelist sanitizer before it is saved as cooked content.

title: Imported URL is interpolated unescaped into stored HTML
body: TopicEmbed.import builds the 'Imported from' anchor by inserting the supplied URL directly into an HTML string, both as the href attribute value and as the link text. The only earlier check is that the string starts with http:// or https://, so a URL containing quotes or angle brackets can break out of the anchor and inject arbitrary markup. Because the resulting post uses raw_html rendering, that injected markup is stored and served without sanitization. The URL and link text must be HTML/attribute escaped, or the anchor must be built with a DOM builder.

title: Remote import performs unrestricted server-side fetching
body: TopicEmbed.import_remote calls open(url).read before TopicEmbed.import performs its scheme check, with no timeout, response-size limit, or restriction on redirect targets or private IP addresses. The on-demand retrieval flow validates only the initial URL's host, while open-uri follows HTTP redirects, so an embeddable-host URL can redirect the server to localhost, link-local, or internal services and have the fetched content converted into a public topic; a very large response is also read entirely into memory. Fetching needs an explicit HTTP(S) client with scheme/final-URI validation, private-address blocking, timeouts, and a size cap.

title: Feed polling crashes on items without full content
body: poll_feed unconditionally calls i.content.scrub for every feed item. Many RSS/Atom items provide only a description or summary and no content/content:encoded element, in which case i.content is nil and this raises NoMethodError. The job is configured with retry: false and has no per-item error handling, so one such item aborts the entire hourly import and prevents all remaining items from being processed. The code should fall back to description/summary when content is absent and isolate failures per item.

title: Unknown embed URLs enqueue unbounded background jobs
body: Every request for an unknown embed_url enqueues a RetrieveTopic job, and the loading page automatically reloads and repeats the request. The Referer check is trivially spoofable by non-browser clients, and TopicRetriever's 60-second throttle is only applied after a job is dequeued, so an attacker can flood Sidekiq with jobs and use distinct URLs on the embeddable host to trigger repeated outbound fetch attempts. Host validation and an atomic throttle/deduplication check need to happen before enqueueing, with throttled requests returning the loading response without creating another job.

title: Embed creation has a check-then-create race
body: TopicEmbed.import first queries for an existing embed and then creates the topic, post, and embed record without any locking. The scheduled feed poller and an on-demand RetrieveTopic job (or two concurrent retrieves) can both observe no embed for the same URL and both create content; the loser then hits the unique index on topic_embeds.embed_url at create! and the whole job fails with RecordNotUnique even though the URL was successfully imported by the winner. Creation should be made atomic or rescue RecordNotUnique and return the existing embed's post.

title: Disqus import now depends on live thread URLs and drops the category option
body: The importer previously created each topic locally from the Disqus export, but now calls TopicEmbed.import_remote, which fetches t[:link] over the network for every thread. If a linked article has moved, returns 404, or the import runs offline, open() raises and aborts the entire import, losing comments that are fully present in the export file. The same change removes the --category Thor option, breaking existing import invocations that pass it and leaving no way to place imported threads in a category. The export-based creation needs to remain as a fallback and the category option needs to be plumbed through to topic creation.

title: Only root-relative URLs are absolutized in imported content
body: absolutize_urls only rewrites href/src values that start with '/'. Relative references such as 'images/photo.jpg' or 'page2.html', which are common in feed content, are left unchanged and will resolve against the Discourse host instead of the source article, producing broken images and links. Conversely, a protocol-relative URL like '//cdn.example.com/x.js' starts with '/' and is incorrectly rewritten onto the article's host. All non-absolute references should be resolved with URI.join against the source URL, which handles relative, root-relative, and protocol-relative forms correctly.

title: postMessage origin is validated by substring matching
body: The resize handler trusts a message when discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) is not -1, i.e. when the sender's origin merely appears as a substring of the configured Discourse URL. For example, when discourseUrl includes a port such as https://forum.example.com:3000/, a page served from the distinct origin https://forum.example.com (default port) passes the check and can drive the iframe's height. The handler should parse discourseUrl, extract its exact origin, and require strict equality with e.origin.

title: Feed-setting guard specs pass without exercising the guards
body: The specs for 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' stub only the setting named in the example. Jobs::PollFeed#execute checks feed_polling_enabled? first, and that setting defaults to false, so execute short-circuits before the stubbed setting is ever consulted and poll_feed is never called regardless of whether the URL/username guards exist. These examples would still pass if those two guards were deleted. Each example needs the preceding conditions stubbed to their enabling values (enabled true, and a present URL for the username example) so only the guard under test can block polling.

title: Imported feed HTML is stored and rendered without sanitization
body: TopicEmbed.import creates posts with cook_method raw_html for content supplied by Jobs::PollFeed, and Post#cook returns that raw content verbatim as cooked HTML. The PollFeed path does not pass the content through Readability or any HTML sanitizer, so script elements, event-handler attributes, javascript: URLs, and other active markup from an RSS/Atom item are persisted and later rendered to forum readers. This is a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability if any imported feed item contains malicious or compromised content.

title: Embed URL is interpolated unescaped into raw HTML
body: TopicEmbed.import appends an imported-from footer by interpolating the supplied URL directly into an href attribute and link text. The URL is checked only for an http/https prefix, so a URL containing a single quote or markup can close the attribute or element and inject additional HTML. Because the resulting post uses raw_html cooking, that injected markup is stored and rendered without the normal cooking sanitization.

title: Referer is embedded unescaped in a JavaScript string
body: The embed layout interpolates request.referer directly inside a single-quoted JavaScript string passed to parent.postMessage. A referer containing an apostrophe or crafted path can terminate the string and alter the script executed on the Discourse-origin embed page. The target origin should be derived and serialized safely on the server, for example by extracting the referer's origin and emitting it with proper JavaScript/JSON escaping.

title: Feed polling crashes on items without content
body: poll_feed unconditionally calls i.content.scrub for every feed item. RSS items commonly provide only a description or summary and can therefore have nil content, raising NoMethodError. Because there is no per-item rescue, one such item aborts the entire hourly poll, prevents all remaining items from being imported, and will recur on every run until the feed changes.

title: Unknown embeds enqueue an unbounded retrieval job on every request
body: EmbedController#best enqueues Jobs::RetrieveTopic whenever no TopicEmbed exists, with no controller-side throttling or deduplication. The 60-second throttle is only checked after a job is dequeued, and the loading page automatically reloads, while non-browser clients can spoof the Referer check trivially. Repeated or malicious requests for a URL that can never be retrieved can therefore flood the Sidekiq queue indefinitely.

title: Remote import fetches arbitrary redirected URLs without timeouts or size limits
body: TopicEmbed.import_remote calls open(url).read with no timeout, response-size limit, or validation of the final URI after redirects. TopicRetriever validates only the initial embed_url host, so a page on the embeddable host can redirect the server-side request to another host, including internal services, and a slow or very large response can tie up a background worker or exhaust memory. A bounded HTTP fetch that revalidates redirect targets is needed.

title: Disqus import now depends on live remote pages and aborts on fetch failures
body: The Disqus importer replaces local topic creation with TopicEmbed.import_remote for each thread link. If a link is missing, stale, offline, or returns an HTTP error, open() raises and aborts the whole Thor import, leaving later threads unprocessed; if import_remote returns no post, that thread's Disqus comments are silently skipped. Previously the topic could be created from the export itself, so this change risks losing exported comments solely because the original site is unavailable.

title: Embed controller spec expects synchronous retrieval the controller no longer performs
body: The spec expects TopicRetriever.new and retrieve to be called when no embed exists, but EmbedController#best never references TopicRetriever; it enqueues Jobs::RetrieveTopic instead. Mocha will report the unmet TopicRetriever expectation, so this test fails and provides no valid coverage of the actual enqueue behavior. The spec should expect the retrieve_topic job enqueue with the user id and embed_url.

title: Protocol-relative URLs are incorrectly rewritten to the source host
body: absolutize_urls treats every href or src beginning with '/' as a path on the source host. Protocol-relative URLs such as //cdn.example.com/image.jpg therefore become http://source-host/cdn.example.com/image.jpg instead of retaining the CDN host, breaking external links and images in imported content; the same faulty transformation is applied to img src attributes below. Protocol-relative and ordinary relative URLs need distinct handling.

title: Unsanitized feed HTML is stored and rendered as raw HTML
body: PollFeed passes CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) directly to TopicEmbed.import without sanitizing it. TopicEmbed.import creates the post with cook_method raw_html, and Post#cook returns raw verbatim for that method, so feed-supplied markup such as script elements or event-handler attributes becomes the post's cooked HTML and is rendered to forum visitors. A malicious or compromised RSS/Atom feed can therefore achieve stored XSS in users' browsers, including administrators.

title: Embed URL is interpolated unescaped into raw HTML
body: TopicEmbed.import appends "#{url}" to the post body without HTML-escaping or URL-encoding url. Because the resulting post uses raw_html rendering, a feed- or import-supplied URL containing a single quote can break out of the href attribute and inject additional attributes or markup, for example an onclick handler. The URL must be escaped before it is embedded in the generated footer HTML.

title: PollFeed crashes on feed items without a content field
body: The job unconditionally calls i.content.scrub. RSS items commonly provide only description/summary rather than content, in which case i.content is nil and this raises NoMethodError. The exception aborts processing of all remaining items, and because the scheduled job is configured with retry: false, a single such item can prevent every later valid feed entry from being imported on each poll.

title: Embed controller spec expects the old synchronous retriever flow
body: This spec expects TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve to be called, but EmbedController#best now calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: ..., embed_url: ...). The mocha expectation will therefore fail, and depending on test job settings the enqueued job may also run for real. The spec should expect Jobs.enqueue with :retrieve_topic and the correct arguments instead.

title: TopicEmbed.import has a check-then-create race on embed_url
body: Import first queries TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url) and only creates the embed record if none exists, but concurrent PollFeed and RetrieveTopic jobs (the latter bypasses throttling for staff) can both observe no record for the same new URL and both create a topic/post. The unique database index on embed_url then makes one TopicEmbed.create! raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, failing that job and rolling back its work. The creation path needs to handle the uniqueness conflict or serialize creation per URL.

title: Retrieval throttle key can be left without an expiry
body: retrieved_recently? sets the Redis throttle key with setnx and only afterwards calls expire as a separate command. If the process crashes or Redis errors between the two commands, the key persists forever with no TTL, permanently blocking retrieval for that embed URL and leaving visitors on the loading page. The key should be created atomically with its 60-second expiry.

title: Disqus import now depends on the original site being reachable
body: The import previously created the topic locally from the Disqus export, but now calls TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...), which fetches t[:link] over HTTP. If a thread's link is missing, malformed, or the original article is offline, open() raises or TopicEmbed.import returns nil and that thread's Disqus comments are skipped or the whole import aborts, losing data that is fully present in the export file. The removed --category option also means existing import invocations using it will fail and imported topics can no longer be placed in a category.

title: absolutize_urls mishandles common relative URL forms
body: Only href/src values beginning with '/' are rewritten. Plain relative references such as images/photo.jpg are left relative and will resolve against the Discourse host, producing broken links/images, while protocol-relative references such as //cdn.example.com/photo.jpg are incorrectly rewritten onto the source origin as http://source.example.com//cdn.example.com/photo.jpg. URL resolution should use URI joining against the source URL instead of string prefix checks.

title: Unauthenticated clients can flood retrieval with non-canonical URLs
body: Any client that spoofs the Referer header (the only embeddable-host check is that header, trivially set by non-browser clients) can call embed/best with arbitrary distinct URLs on the embeddable host, and every miss enqueues a RetrieveTopic job. The only throttling is per exact URL string inside the job and TopicEmbed is keyed by the exact URL string, so adding random query parameters, fragments, or other variants of the same article bypasses the throttle, floods the job queue with server-side fetches of the remote host, and can create duplicate topics for the same article. Retrieval needs canonical URL handling and a global/origin rate limit before enqueueing.

title: order() mixin is off by one for legacy box layouts
body: The mixin copies the same value to -webkit-box-ordinal-group/-moz-box-ordinal-group and to modern order, but the legacy box ordinal-group properties are 1-based while order is 0-based. Thus order(0) produces an invalid ordinal-group below 1, and order(1) collides with unordered items (legacy default group 1) while placing the item second in modern browsers. The legacy values should be $val + 1. This makes the new reusable mixin produce different ordering in the legacy WebKit/Mozilla engines it explicitly targets.

title: align-items() does not translate values for legacy flexbox properties
body: The mixin passes $alignment verbatim to -webkit-box-align and -ms-flex-align, but those legacy properties use start/end rather than the modern flex-start/flex-end keywords, so a natural call such as align-items(flex-start) or align-items(flex-end) will be dropped by the legacy engines the prefixes exist for. It also emits -ms-align-items on line 121, which is not a recognized IE10 property (the recognized one, -ms-flex-align, is already present), and omits -moz-box-align despite flexbox() emitting display:-moz-box. Current callers use center/baseline, which coincide in both vocabularies, but the generic mixin contract is broken for other valid alignments.

title: Small-action button loses its right-edge alignment in the new flex row
body: .small-action is now a flex container (lines 264-265), so its direct children become flex items and the button's float:right on line 309 is ignored by flex layout. Neither the button nor .small-action-desc is given flex-grow, width:100%, or margin-left:auto, so the delete button will sit immediately after the description text at a position that varies with text length instead of at the far right of the row as the floated layout placed it. Add e.g. margin-left:auto to the button (or make the description flex-grow) to preserve the alignment, as was done for .panel in header.scss.

title: Flex conversion breaks right-aligned small-action button
body: Making .small-action a flex container makes its direct children flex items, and floats do not apply to flex items. The button rule at lines 306-310 still relies on float: right, with no margin-left: auto, justify-content, or other flex positioning to replace it. A small-action delete button will therefore sit immediately after .small-action-desc instead of at the right edge of the post row.

title: order mixin mistranslates values for legacy box ordinal groups
body: The mixin copies $val directly to -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group, but legacy ordinal groups are 1-based (initial value 1 and values below 1 are invalid) while flex order is 0-based (initial value 0). Consequently order(0) emits an invalid legacy declaration and the legacy translation does not faithfully represent the standard value; the legacy properties should use $val + 1.

title: align-items mixin passes incompatible values to legacy alignment properties
body: The mixin passes $alignment unchanged to -webkit-box-align and -ms-flex-align, but those legacy properties accept start/end rather than flex-start/flex-end, so a caller using the standard align-items value flex-start or flex-end will get invalid legacy declarations and lose alignment in the prefixed browsers this mixin targets. It also emits -ms-align-items, which is not the IE10 property. The mixin should translate flex-start/flex-end to start/end for the legacy properties. Current callers use center and baseline, which happen to be spelled the same in both syntaxes.

title: Right-floated small-action button loses alignment in new flex container
body: .small-action is made a flex container at lines 264-265, but its direct-child button still relies on float: right at line 309. Floats do not apply to flex items, and no margin-left: auto, justify-content, or equivalent replacement is added, so the button will sit immediately after .small-action-desc instead of at the right edge of the row.

title: order() mistranslates flex order for legacy WebKit/Mozilla box layout
body: The order() mixin copies the same value to order and to -webkit-box-ordinal-group/-moz-box-ordinal-group, but the legacy ordinal-group properties are 1-based and unordered items default to group 1, whereas flex order is 0-based and unordered items default to 0. Thus order(0) is invalid for legacy box layout and order(1) collides with unordered items there while following them in modern flex layout; the legacy properties need $val + 1 to preserve the same ordering.

title: align-items() has incomplete and invalid legacy vendor mappings
body: flexbox() and inline-flex() emit -moz-box/-moz-inline-box displays, but align-items() provides no -moz-box-align, so alignment is ignored by the legacy Mozilla box implementation for the header centering, .small-action centering, and bullet-badge baseline alignment. The block also emits the non-existent -ms-align-items property at line 121 while the actual IE10 property is -ms-flex-align, so that line is dead code and does not provide the intended support.

title: extra-info-wrapper becomes a flex item without shrink/truncation constraints
body: Adding order(2) makes .extra-info-wrapper participate as a flex item between the header title and the order(3) panel in the new .d-header .contents flex container, but it gets no flex sizing, min-width: 0, overflow, or truncation rules. A long topic title with category badges therefore cannot shrink below its content size and can push or compress the panel, causing the header controls to overflow or be clipped on narrow widths instead of the topic info truncating.

title: include_website_name predicate is missing the required question mark
body: The serializer defines `include_website_name` without a trailing `?`, while ActiveModelSerializers and every other conditional in this serializer (e.g. `include_email?`, `include_card_image_badge_id?`) invoke `include_<attribute>?`. This method is therefore never called, so `website_name` is serialized as null for users without a website instead of being omitted when `website` is blank.

title: website_name bypasses the untrusted-attributes restriction for TL0 users
body: `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes`, so it is hidden from anonymous viewers when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` applies to a TL0 user, but the newly added `website_name` attribute is not added to that list. Anonymous viewers will consequently receive the website host and, in the matching-domain case, its full path even though the website itself is supposed to be hidden, and the untrusted-attributes spec was not updated to cover `website_name`.

title: Same-domain detection is asymmetric when the website is a subdomain of the instance
body: The logic handles an instance that is a subdomain of the website (e.g. instance `forums.example.com`, website `example.com/user` returns `example.com/user`) and equal-depth siblings, but not the reverse: with instance `example.com` and website `http://www.example.com/user` or `http://blog.example.com/user`, the lengths differ, the equal-length branch is skipped, and `example.com.ends_with?('.www.example.com')` is false, so only the host is returned and the path is discarded despite the website sharing the instance's domain.

title: No spec covers the sibling-subdomain branch of website_name
body: The new specs cover only an unrelated domain, an exact host match, and a website that is the parent of the instance host. They do not exercise the distinct equal-depth sibling branch in the serializer (e.g. website `www.example.com/user` with instance `forum.example.com`, which should return `www.example.com/user`, and a same-depth host on a different registrable domain, which should not), so that branch's first-label-stripping comparison can regress unnoticed.

title: include_website_name predicate is missing the question mark
body: ActiveModelSerializers decides whether to emit an attribute by calling `include_<attribute>?`, as used by every other predicate in this serializer (e.g. include_email?, include_stats?). The new method is named `include_website_name` without `?`, so it is never invoked: `website_name` is serialized for every user, with a nil value when the user has no website, instead of being omitted as intended.

title: website_name bypasses the untrusted-user field restrictions
body: `website_name` is added to the public attributes but not to the `untrusted_attributes` list (lines 105-111), which hides fields such as `website`, `location` and `bio_cooked` from anonymous viewers of TL0 users via scope.restrict_user_fields?. Because website_name is derived directly from the hidden website, an anonymous visitor can still learn a TL0/spam account's website host and, in the same-domain case, its full path, defeating the restriction that hides `website` itself.

title: website_name discards the query string and fragment
body: The display text is built as `website_host + URI(website).path`, so for a website such as `http://example.com/blog?author=alice` or `http://example.com/#about` the serialized name becomes just `example.com/blog` or `example.com/`. The PR's goal is to show the complete URL when it points at the instance's domain, but the shown text silently loses the query/fragment that distinguishes the target (the href still contains it, so text and link disagree).

title: Same-domain detection only works for subdomains of equal depth
body: The elsif branch treats two hosts as the same base domain only when they have the same number of labels and everything after the first label matches (e.g. www.example.com vs forum.example.com). A website at blog.example.com (3 labels) viewed on an instance at www.forum.example.com (4 labels) falls through to the final branch, fails the ends_with? parent check, and loses its path even though both are under example.com; conversely the drop-first-label heuristic equates unrelated sites under a shared suffix such as alice.blogspot.com vs an instance-related bob.blogspot.com. The result is inconsistent with the stated same-domain rule.

title: No spec covers the sibling-subdomain branch or restricted visibility of website_name
body: The new specs cover only an unrelated domain, an exact host match, and a parent-domain website. They do not exercise the elsif sibling-subdomain branch in website_name (www.example.com vs forum.example.com, or the negative case where the remaining labels differ), nor the TL0-user-seen-as-anonymous context at the top of the file, so neither a regression in that branch nor website_name leaking for restricted users would be caught.

title: website_name include predicate is misnamed and bypasses untrusted-user hiding
body: The conditional is defined as include_website_name instead of the include_website_name? convention used by ActiveModel Serializers and by the other predicates in this file, so it is never invoked and website_name is always serialized. Additionally, :website_name is absent from untrusted_attributes, which hides :website for TL0 users viewed anonymously. Anonymous visitors therefore receive the host and path derived from a website that was intended to be hidden, and profiles without a website also gain a spurious website_name: nil key.

title: Same-domain check is asymmetric for apex and www hosts
body: When the website is http://www.example.com/me and the instance is example.com, the hosts have different label counts, so execution reaches the final branch, which only checks whether the instance host ends with the website host. That check fails and only www.example.com is shown. The reverse configuration, website example.com/me on instance www.example.com, does return example.com/me. The common apex/www combination is therefore handled inconsistently and the requested full path is not shown.

title: Stripping the first host label falsely matches domains under public suffixes
body: The sibling-subdomain branch assumes the registrable domain is always the last two labels. For example, website example.co.uk/user and an unrelated instance at other.co.uk both reduce to co.uk after removing the first label, so the serializer incorrectly displays example.co.uk/user as though the website belonged to the instance domain. The same false positive applies to other multi-part public suffixes and shared suffixes such as github.io.

title: Displayed website text drops query string and fragment
body: For a matching domain the display text is built from URI#path only. A website such as http://example.com/user?tab=posts#details is displayed as example.com/user even though the actual link points to the full URL, so the supposedly complete URL shown to readers is truncated and can misrepresent the destination, particularly for URLs whose identity is in the query string.

title: New website_name branches and visibility rules are untested
body: The added examples cover only an unrelated two-label domain, an exact host match, and a website that is the parent of the instance host. They do not exercise the equal-length sibling-subdomain branch, the apex-versus-www case, a blank or malformed website, or serialization of website_name for a TL0 user viewed anonymously; the untrusted_attributes list in the TL0 context is also unchanged. The untested include predicate and subdomain logic can therefore regress, or leak the hidden website, without any spec failing.

title: Embedded-post author link lightness values are transposed
body: This rule originally used scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), so the dark-theme conversion should be dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)). Instead it uses primary 70% for light themes and secondary 30% for dark themes. Light-theme links become much paler than before, while dark-theme links become a dark grey on a dark background with poor contrast.

title: Custom-message-length lightness values are transposed
body: This rule originally used scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), and the corresponding desktop modal rule correctly converts it to primary 70% / secondary 30%. This mobile rule instead uses primary 30% for light themes and secondary 70% for dark themes, reversing the intended muted colour in both themes and making it inconsistent with desktop.

title: Topic-map heading changes the original 20% lightness to 50%
body: The mobile .topic-map h3 originally used scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), so preserving the light theme and adding a dark variant requires primary 20% / secondary 80%, as done for the equivalent desktop rule. This line instead uses 50% for both, making the light-theme heading substantially paler and the dark-theme heading less bright than intended.

title: Group-member name changes the original 30% lightness to 50%
body: The .group-member-info .name rule originally used scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), so the conversion should retain primary 30% for light themes and use secondary 70% for dark themes. It instead uses 50% for both, lightening the light-theme name, dimming the dark-theme name, and removing the original contrast distinction from the adjacent .title rule which was already 50%.

title: Group-member name changes the original 30% lightness to 50%
body: The mobile .group-member-info .name rule originally used scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), so the conversion should retain primary 30% for light themes and use secondary 70% for dark themes. It instead uses 50% for both, lightening the light-theme name, dimming the dark-theme name, and removing the original contrast distinction from the adjacent .title rule which was already 50%.

title: Category badge-notification still uses $primary scale-color without a dark variant
body: This .topic-list.categories .badge-notification rule still uses only scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), unlike the analogous badge-notification and muted-text rules converted throughout this PR. On a dark theme $primary is already light, so scaling its lightness by 50% does not produce the intended muted colour from $secondary; the PR's dark-theme fix is incomplete for this element.

title: Embedded-post author link swaps the light and dark lightness values
body: This rule originally used scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), so the conversion should be dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)). The changed line instead uses 70% for $primary and 30% for $secondary. Light themes therefore get a much paler color than before, and dark themes get the wrong muted shade, reducing contrast in both themes.

title: Group-member name changes the original 30% lightness to 50%
body: This rule originally used scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), so the conversion should keep 30% for the light-theme $primary branch and use scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%) for dark themes. The changed line uses 50% for both branches, making the name paler than intended on light themes and too dark/muted on dark themes.

title: Custom-message-length swaps the light and dark lightness values
body: This rule originally used scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), so the conversion should be dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The changed line instead uses 30% for $primary and 70% for $secondary. Light themes therefore get a much darker color than before, and dark themes get the opposite, overly light shade.

title: Topic-map heading changes the original 20% lightness to 50%
body: This .topic-map h3 rule originally used scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), so the conversion should keep 20% for the light-theme $primary branch and use scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%) for dark themes, as the corresponding desktop rule does. The changed line uses 50% for both branches, making the heading substantially paler on light themes and giving the wrong shade on dark themes.

title: Group-member name changes the original 30% lightness to 50%
body: This rule originally used scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), so the conversion should keep 30% for the light-theme $primary branch and use scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%) for dark themes. The changed line uses 50% for both branches, making the name paler than intended on light themes and too dark/muted on dark themes.

title: Embedded-post username colour has its light/dark lightness values swapped
body: The original rule was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). A correct dark-theme conversion must keep 30% for the light branch and use scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%) for the dark branch, but this line uses 70% for $primary and 30% for $secondary. Light-theme embedded-post usernames therefore become far paler than before and the dark-theme colour is far darker than intended, reducing readability in both themes.

title: Group-member name colour changes the original 30% lightness to 50%
body: The original rule was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). This line converts it to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)) instead of preserving 30% for light and using 70% on $secondary for dark. The light-theme name colour is therefore changed unnecessarily and the dark-theme colour is darker than the intended equivalent, weakening contrast.

title: Custom-message-length colour has its light/dark lightness values swapped
body: The original rule was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%). A correct conversion must keep 70% for the light branch and use scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%) for the dark branch, matching the equivalent desktop/modal.scss rule, but this line uses 30% for $primary and 70% for $secondary. Both themes therefore get the opposite shade from the one intended for the character-count hint.

title: Mobile topic-map heading colour changes the original 20% lightness to 50%
body: The original mobile rule was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), and the equivalent desktop topic-map heading correctly converts to 20% on $primary with 80% on $secondary for dark. This line instead uses 50% for both branches. Mobile topic-map headings become much paler in the light theme and much darker than intended in the dark theme, losing heading contrast.

title: Mobile group-member name colour changes the original 30% lightness to 50%
body: The original rule was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). This line converts it to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)) instead of preserving 30% for light and using 70% on $secondary for dark. The light-theme name colour is therefore changed unnecessarily and the dark-theme colour is darker than the intended equivalent, weakening contrast.

title: totalPages is off by one when member count is an exact multiple of the page size
body: totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 unconditionally. With 100 members and limit 50 this reports 3 pages instead of 2, and with 50 members it reports 2 instead of 1. showingLast therefore stays false on the real last page, the next action advances offset to user_count, and the admin sees an empty extra page.

title: Members endpoint accepts unbounded and invalid limit/offset values
body: limit and offset are taken directly from params and passed to the query with no clamping or validation. A request such as members.json?limit=1000000 forces counting/serializing the entire membership of a large group in one response, while negative limit or offset values produce database/ActiveRecord errors and a 500. The previous automatic-group path capped the page size; this change removes any cap for all groups.

title: Public group members page now silently shows only the first 50 members
body: This route calls model.findMembers(), which now requests the server-paginated members endpoint with the model's default limit of 50, and the public group/members.hbs template simply iterates `members` with no pagination controls (unlike the new admin template). For any group with more than 50 members, everyone after the first alphabetical page is unreachable from the public members page, a regression from the previous behavior of returning the full member list.

title: Group creation silently discards the selected alias_level
body: The client's Group.asJSON() sends name, alias_level and visible when creating a group, but Admin::GroupsController#create only assigns name and visible. A non-default alias level chosen in the new-group form is therefore lost on creation and the group is persisted with the model default until an admin edits and saves it a second time.

title: findMembers no longer always returns a promise
body: When the group name is empty, findMembers now does a bare `return;` instead of the previous Ember.RSVP.resolve([]). Any caller that does findMembers().then(...) will throw a TypeError on undefined. The two routes in this PR were adjusted, but the model's public contract is broken for any other current or future caller.

title: add_members crashes if usernames is not a string
body: add_members calls usernames.split(",") on the raw required parameter. A request sending usernames as an array or hash (e.g. usernames[]=a) makes params.require return an Array/ActionController::Parameters, raising NoMethodError and returning an unhandled 500 instead of a client error or a handled list of names.

title: Automatic-group remove_member spec uses the wrong HTTP verb
body: The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' example issues xhr :put to :remove_member, but config/routes.rb only routes DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members to remove_member and the client issues DELETE. Controller specs bypass routing, so the test passes even though a PUT request would 404 in production; it should use :delete like the successful-removal example below it.

title: Total page count is off by one for exact multiples of the page size
body: totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. For a group with exactly 100 members and limit 50 this reports 3 pages instead of 2, so showingLast is false on the real last page and the Next action advances offset to 100, fetching and displaying an empty page. It should use a ceiling calculation, e.g. Math.ceil(user_count / limit) for non-zero counts.

title: Public group members page now silently shows only the first 50 members
body: The members action now always paginates with the client's default limit of 50, whereas non-automatic groups previously returned all members. The public group/members template and GroupMembers route were not given any pagination controls or follow-up fetching, so members beyond the first 50 of a large group are unreachable in the public UI.

title: Members pagination parameters are not validated or clamped
body: limit and offset are taken directly from request params via to_i. A request such as members.json?limit=-1 or offset=-1 can produce a database error/500, limit=0 returns a meta limit of 0 that breaks client page calculations, and a huge limit lets any user who can see a group serialize its entire membership in one request, defeating the new pagination and creating an expensive response for large automatic groups. Clamp limit to a sane range and offset to at least 0.

title: Creating a group silently discards the selected alias level
body: The client sends alias_level in Group#asJSON and the group form shows the alias-level selector for unsaved groups, but Admin::GroupsController#create only assigns name and visible. A newly created group therefore always gets the default alias_level regardless of what the admin selected; #update handles alias_level, so create should assign it too.

title: PATCH membership updates are now ignored and flip group visibility off
body: The old PATCH branch that applied changes:{add,delete} has been removed, but Rails still routes PATCH to #update. A legacy/API PATCH request now ignores its membership changes, and because line 38 unconditionally sets visible = (params[:visible] == "true"), a PATCH that does not include visible silently makes the group invisible while returning success. Either keep handling PATCH changes or reject unsupported PATCH/partial updates instead of applying the visibility default.

title: Automatic-group remove_member spec uses the wrong HTTP verb
body: The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' example calls xhr :put, :remove_member, but the route added in config/routes.rb and the successful removal example use DELETE. Because controller specs dispatch directly to the action and bypass routing, this example passes even if the DELETE route is broken or removed, so it does not test the endpoint clients actually call.

title: totalPages is off by one when member count is an exact multiple of the page size
body: totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. For user_count=50 and limit=50 this returns 2 instead of 1, and for 100/50 it returns 3 instead of 2. showingLast therefore stays false on the real last page, the Next link stays enabled, and clicking it loads an empty page at offset == user_count. It should use Math.ceil(user_count / limit) (with the existing zero-count special case).

title: Public group members page now silently truncates to the first 50 members with no way to reach the rest
body: The members endpoint now defaults to limit=50 and Group#findMembers always sends limit=50, but this same endpoint/model is used by the public discourse/routes/group-members route and templates/group/members.hbs, which have no pagination controls at all (pagination was only added to the admin template). Previously non-automatic groups returned all members and automatic groups up to 200. Now any group with more than 50 members only ever displays the first 50 alphabetically on its public members page.

title: Members endpoint accepts unbounded and negative limit/offset
body: limit and offset are taken from params with only to_i and no clamping. A caller who can view a group can pass limit=1000000 to force counting/serializing the entire membership in one request (automatic groups were previously capped at 200), or a negative limit/offset to trigger a database error and a 500. Clamp limit to a sane range (e.g. 1..200) and offset to >= 0.

title: Group update silently hides the group when the visible parameter is omitted
body: update guards alias_level with present? and name with an explicit nil check, but assigns group.visible = params[:visible] == "true" unconditionally. Any PUT/PATCH that updates only some fields (for example a rename or alias change from another API client, or the legacy PATCH membership call whose handling was removed) will force visible to false and return success, silently hiding the group. Only assign visible when the parameter is present.

title: Creating a group discards the alias_level chosen in the form
body: The admin form always shows the alias_level combo box and Group#asJSON sends alias_level on create, but the new create action only assigns name and visible. A group created with a non-default alias level is saved with the default 0 while the in-memory Ember object still shows the chosen value, so the setting appears applied until the page is reloaded. Assign params[:alias_level] in create as update does.

title: Stale usernames input leaks between group edit pages
body: AdminGroupController is a singleton and its new plain `usernames` property is never reset; setupController only sets the model and loads members. Text typed into the Add Members selector for one group is still bound and visible when the admin opens a different group, and clicking Add there would submit the previous group's usernames to the new group. Clear controller usernames (and stale paging state) in setupController or after a successful add.

title: remove_member automatic-group spec uses the wrong HTTP verb
body: The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' example calls xhr :put, :remove_member, but the route added in config/routes.rb is DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members (and the other remove_member example correctly uses :delete). Controller specs dispatch by action name and bypass routing, so this test would still pass even if the DELETE route were missing or mapped to the wrong action, and it misdocuments the API contract.

title: Fallback locales are loaded only during web requests
body: I18n.translate loads only config.locale before delegating to the backend, while the new code loads the site-default and English fallback files only from ApplicationController#set_locale. Background jobs, mailers, rake tasks, console code, and model-level translations therefore query fallback locales whose YAML files were never loaded and receive 'translation missing'. Worse, argument-less lookups cache that missing result in the LRU cache at lines 71-76, so the missing string can persist after a later web request loads the fallback locale. Fallback loading belongs in the translation/load path, not only in the controller.

title: Every fallback lookup depends on SiteSetting and can fail outside a ready request stack
body: FallbackLocaleList#[] unconditionally calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, and I18n::Backend::Fallbacks invokes this method for translation misses in any context, not just after ApplicationController has already resolved the locale. If the setting is blank or the settings/DB layer is unavailable during boot, migrations, seeding, or job startup, a routine missing translation becomes a NoMethodError or database error instead of falling back to :en. The hot missing-translation path should use a guarded or cached default that safely degrades to English.

title: Cached translations ignore the dynamic fallback chain
body: The LRU cache key contains only the key, current locale, and backend object_id, but after this change the result for a key missing in the current locale also depends on SiteSetting.default_locale, which FallbackLocaleList reads dynamically. Changing the site default locale does not change the cache key or clear the cache, so users can keep receiving text in the previous fallback language until entries are evicted or translations are manually reloaded.

title: No tests cover the new fallback behaviour
body: The pull request introduces a custom FallbackLocaleList, backend Fallbacks inclusion, fallback-file loading, and a controller hook, but adds no specs. There is no coverage proving that a key missing in the user locale resolves first to the site default and then to English, that fallback locale files are loaded before lookup, or that pluralized/interpolated fallback translations work, so regressions would silently surface as 'translation missing' text.

title: Fallback locales are only loaded for web requests
body: The only call to I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! is in ApplicationController#set_locale. Server-side translations also occur in Sidekiq jobs, mailers, rake tasks, and console/background processes, where this filter never runs. The lazy loader in translate_accelerator only loads config.locale, not the site-default or :en fallback locales, so in a job-only process those YAML files may never enter the backend store and a missing translation will return 'translation missing' instead of falling back. Fallback loading should be ensured from I18n.translate/load_locale or from the job/mailer locale setup, not only from the web controller.

title: Translation cache can retain missing or stale fallback results after locales load
body: The LRU cache key is only key + current locale + backend object_id, and load_locale/ensure_loaded! add translations without clearing @cache (only reload! clears it). If a key is first translated before its fallback locale has been loaded, the 'translation missing' string produced for that lookup is stored by getset and will keep being returned after the fallback file is loaded, until eviction or reload. The same staleness occurs when SiteSetting.default_locale changes, because FallbackLocaleList then points at a different fallback locale while the cache key is unchanged, so strings cached from the old fallback locale continue to be served. Loading a locale should invalidate the cache, or missing results and the effective fallback chain must be accounted for in caching.

title: Fallback lookup consults SiteSetting on every translation
body: I18n::Backend::Fallbacks invokes I18n.fallbacks[locale] for each backend translation, and the translate accelerator bypasses its cache for the common calls that pass interpolation, count, or locale options. This implementation therefore rebuilds the fallback array and calls the DB-backed SiteSetting.default_locale (with to_sym) on a per-translation hot path, and makes plain I18n.t depend on site-settings availability even in boot or isolated job contexts. The chain should be computed when the locale/site default is set, or memoized keyed by the current site/default locale with invalidation when that setting changes.

title: No tests cover the new fallback behavior
body: The PR adds FallbackLocaleList, fallback-backend inclusion, lazy fallback loading, and a controller hook, but adds no specs. There is no coverage proving the user-locale -> site-default -> :en order, that fallback translation files are loaded on demand (including pluralized/interpolated keys that bypass the accelerator cache), or that non-controller translation paths fall back correctly. Such tests are needed because the failure mode is silent: missing keys degrade to 'translation missing' strings rather than raising in production.

title: Fallback locales are not loaded on the translation path
body: I18n.translate only calls load_locale(config.locale), while ApplicationController#set_locale is the only caller of I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!. Code outside a web request, such as background jobs and mailers, and translations using an explicit locale: option can therefore invoke the new Fallbacks backend before the site-default and :en YAML files have been lazily loaded. Those lookups return 'translation missing' instead of falling back; for calls without interpolation arguments, that missing string is also stored frozen in the LRU cache keyed only by key and locale, so it can continue to be served after a later request loads :en until cache eviction or reload. All fallback locales for the effective or explicit locale should be loaded inside translate/lookup before consulting or caching the backend.

title: Custom fallbacks object discards I18n::Locale::Fallbacks behavior
body: FallbackLocaleList inherits directly from Hash and replaces the I18n::Locale::Fallbacks object previously configured by Rails, but its [] ignores anything stored in the hash and the class provides neither Locale::Fallbacks' defaults nor its map configuration API. It also loses parent-tag expansion: for a locale such as en_GB, a missing key is resolved in SiteSetting.default_locale before its parent :en, because :en appears only as the final entry. Existing or plugin code using the documented fallbacks API can therefore be silently ignored or fail, and regional locales can receive the site language instead of their parent language. The custom ordering should be implemented by subclassing or extending I18n::Locale::Fallbacks rather than replacing it with a plain Hash.

title: Every backend lookup now consults SiteSetting
body: I18n::Backend::Fallbacks calls I18n.fallbacks[locale] for every uncached translation, localization, and pluralization lookup, and this implementation calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym on every such call. That puts the DB-backed settings subsystem on the hot translation path that translate_accelerator otherwise optimizes through lazy loading and caching, and it also makes translations attempted during boot, rake, or asset tasks depend on SiteSetting being loadable before the fallback chain can even be computed. The chain should be cached and invalidated when default_locale changes, rather than recomputed through SiteSetting for each lookup.

title: No tests cover the custom fallback backend or lazy loading
body: This change replaces the Rails fallback configuration with a custom Hash, moves pluralization setup into config/initializers/i18n.rb, removes config.i18n.fallbacks from the environment files, and adds lazy loading of fallback locales, but it adds no specs. Nothing verifies that a key missing from the user locale falls back first to the site default and then to :en, that the relevant locale files are loaded outside ApplicationController, or that pluralized strings obtained through a fallback still use the fallback locale's pluralization rules. Regressions would surface only as wrong-language text or 'translation missing' strings in production.

title: Denial cache key does not include identity type
body: userPermDenialCacheKey is built only from namespace, the raw subject identifier, action, name and parent. Anonymous subjects (anonymous:0) and the render service (render:0) both have identifier "0", and user/service-account identifiers can also overlap. If an anonymous check for dashboards:read on dash1 is denied and cached, a subsequent render-service check for the same action/name/parent hits that denial at service.go:117 and returns Allowed=false, even though getRendererPermissions grants the renderer read access to all dashboards/folders. Different identity types must not share denial entries; include the identity type (or identity-specific prefixes like the permission cache uses) in the key.

title: Every distinct cache-negative Check now issues a fresh permissions DB query
body: When cached permissions do not allow the request, Check unconditionally calls getIdentityPermissions, and getUserPermissions/getAnonymousPermissions no longer consult permCache before querying permissionStore. The denial cache is per user+action+name+parent, so it only suppresses repeats for the exact same resource. Checking N different dashboards/folders a user cannot access (e.g. an authorizer evaluating many objects, or a client probing/enumerating UIDs) therefore causes N sequential SQL permission queries for the same user/action, even though the scope map was already fetched and refreshed by the first query; singleflight only coalesces concurrent identical calls. This defeats the 30s permission cache for denial-heavy workloads and amplifies DB load proportional to distinct resource names.

title: Cached denial blocks access immediately after a grant or resource creation
body: Any DB-confirmed denial is stored in permDenialCache for shortCacheTTL (30s), and lines 116-121 return that denial without re-querying permissions. If the denied check happened just before the resource was created or before a permission/role was granted for that same name/parent (a common pre-creation or permission-assignment flow), the creator/grantee is still denied for up to 30s, which is exactly the newly-created dashboard/folder scenario this PR aims to fix. The denial timestamp also starts after the underlying permission/team/role caches were populated, so it can extend staleness beyond their expiry.

title: List still serves stale cached permissions, so newly created resources do not appear
body: List returns getCachedIdentityPermissions whenever the cache lookup succeeds, with no revalidation, freshness check, or DB fallback. If a user creates a dashboard/folder (adding a permission not present in the cached scope map) and then lists dashboards/folders within the 30s permCache TTL, the new resource is omitted from the List response even though a Check for that same resource would now re-query the DB and allow it. This leaves Check and List inconsistent and does not fully deliver the stated goal of letting users fetch newly created dashboards/folders.

title: DB fallback does not refresh team, basic-role or folder-tree caches before caching a denial
body: The fallback at lines 139-155 re-queries only the permission rows: getUserPermissions still obtains basic role and team memberships from basicRoleCache/teamCache, and the second checkPermission still obtains ancestors from the cached folderCache via buildFolderTree. If access should be granted because of a recent team/role change or via a newly created intermediate folder, the fallback still evaluates with the stale role/team/folder-tree data, returns false, and then writes a fresh 30s denial entry, extending the incorrect denial beyond the expiry of those underlying caches. Re-querying permissions alone is insufficient for inherited or role/team-based grants.

title: Denial key uses raw subject identifier and ambiguous underscore concatenation
body: permDenialKey is built from checkReq.UserUID, the raw identifier parsed from the subject, whereas permCache is keyed by the canonical UID returned by GetUserIdentifiers. The same person addressed as user:<numeric-id> versus user:<uid> therefore gets separate denial entries and inconsistent fast-path behaviour. Additionally userPermDenialCacheKey joins action, name and parent with '_' without escaping, so pairs such as (name='a_b', parent='c') and (name='a', parent='b_c') produce the same key and one resource's denial can incorrectly deny the other for that user.

title: Negative cached checks re-query permissions for every distinct resource
body: When cached permissions do not allow a request, Check unconditionally calls getIdentityPermissions, and the user/anonymous permission paths no longer consult permCache before querying the permission store. The new denial cache only suppresses repeats for the exact namespace/user/action/name/parent combination. Consequently, checking N distinct resources that a user legitimately cannot access causes N permission-store queries, even though the first query has just refreshed that user's permissions for the action. This removes the permission cache's protection for negative authorization checks and can create substantial database load when many resources are checked or filtered.

title: Denial cache blocks permissions granted after an initial denial
body: Check returns immediately from permDenialCache before re-querying permissions, while line 154 populates that cache after any fresh denial for the shortCacheTTL period. If a dashboard or folder is created, a creator permission is added, or an administrator grants access after an initial denied check, subsequent identical checks continue to return false without consulting the database until the denial expires. An intervening check during creation can therefore poison access to the newly created resource and defeat the PR's intended fresh-permission re-query for up to the denial TTL.

title: Denial cache key does not uniquely identify an authorization check
body: userPermDenialCacheKey concatenates namespace, raw user UID, action, resource name, and parent with underscores, and its caller does not include the identity type. Anonymous and render subjects both use UID 0, so an anonymous denial can incorrectly deny the render service for the same action, resource, and folder even though the render service is granted read access. The ambiguous underscore encoding also makes distinct pairs such as name='a_b', parent='c' and name='a', parent='b_c' produce the same key. These collisions can incorrectly deny unrelated checks until the denial entry expires.

title: Refreshed permission check still uses stale folder tree and then caches the denial
body: After a cached check fails, Check re-runs checkPermission with refreshed permissions, but inherited-permission evaluation still uses buildFolderTree's cached folder tree and does not refresh or invalidate it. For a dashboard in a newly created folder whose access is inherited from an ancestor folder, the ancestor lookup can miss because the new folder is absent from the cached tree; the resulting false result is then stored in permDenialCache at line 154. This both prevents the permission re-query from fixing newly created nested resources in this case and can extend the incorrect denial beyond the folder cache's own expiry.

title: Denial-cache test does not actually prove the denial short-circuit
body: The test comment says it allows access through permCache to prove that path is not checked, but it stores map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}. With that value, the cached-permission check would also deny, and the fallback fake store returns no permissions, so the test would still pass if the denial-cache early return were removed. The cached permission should be true and the test should preferably assert that the permission store is not consulted, so it genuinely verifies that a denial entry takes precedence.

title: Denial cache key does not include the identity type
body: The denial key is built only from namespace, the raw subject UID, action, resource name, and parent folder, but permission resolution switches on identity type and returns different permission sets for the same UID. In particular, anonymous and render-service subjects both use UID "0", while anonymous receives Viewer-role permissions and the render service is granted read access to all dashboards and folders. A denial recorded for anonymous:0 can therefore short-circuit and incorrectly deny render:0 for the same dashboard for up to the denial TTL, and the same collision can occur between user and service-account spellings. The key must include the identity type, preferably together with the canonical resolved UID.

title: Denial cache key concatenation is ambiguous
body: userPermDenialCacheKey joins variable-length UID, action, name, and parent values with plain underscores and no escaping, length prefixes, or hashing. Distinct tuples can consequently produce the same key: for example name "a_b" with parent "c" and name "a" with parent "b_c" both produce the same suffix. Grafana resource and folder UIDs may contain underscores, so a denial for one resource can incorrectly deny a different resource until the entry expires. Build the key from a structured, unambiguously encoded or hashed tuple.

title: Denial entries shadow fresher permissions and undermine immediate access after a grant
body: Check consults permDenialCache before checking the ordinary permission cache, and neither getUserPermissions' permission-cache refresh nor List's refresh deletes existing denial entries. After a permission is granted, such as the creator permission inserted for a new dashboard or folder, a later check or list for another resource can refresh permCache with a scope map that now allows the denied resource, yet checks for that resource will still return the old denial until the denial TTL expires. A denial recorded by a check made just before the grant has the same effect. This partially defeats the PR's goal of letting creators fetch newly created resources immediately; cached allowances should be honoured before denials or denials should be invalidated when permissions are refreshed.

title: Every distinct cached denial now forces a database permission fetch
body: When cached permissions do not allow a check, Check unconditionally calls getIdentityPermissions, and the permission-store cache lookup was removed from getUserPermissions/getAnonymousPermissions, so this performs a fresh database permission query. The new denial cache only suppresses repeats for the exact namespace/user/action/name/parent tuple for 30 seconds. A user checking many distinct dashboards or folders they do not own therefore causes one permission query per resource instead of one query per user/action as before, multiplying database load in denial-heavy or enumeration-heavy workloads and increasing cache cardinality. The revalidation needs a freshness or negative-cache strategy that does not scale database queries with the number of distinct denied resources.

title: Denial-cache test would pass even if the denial cache were ignored
body: The test named "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" sets the permission cache to map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}; despite the comment saying this allows access, checkPermission treats a false map value as no permission, and the fake permission store also returns no granting permission. The request therefore denies through the ordinary cached/DB path even if permDenialCache is never consulted, so the test does not prove the new short-circuit works. It should configure the underlying store or permission cache to allow dash1, or assert that the permission store is not called when the denial entry is present.

title: Pause action is never shown in the ruler-free list view
body: The pause menu item requires rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) in addition to canPause. In the new list view rulerRule is intentionally undefined, so even though the Grafana Prometheus ability can set canPause to true, the Pause/Unpause item is never rendered there. Users can no longer pause or resume Grafana rules from the list view.

title: Delete action is never shown in the ruler-free list view
body: The Delete menu item is gated by `canDelete && rulerRule`. In the new list view rulerRule is undefined, so the newly added Grafana Prometheus delete ability has no effect and users with delete permission cannot delete a Grafana rule from the list's More menu. The underlying delete handler in RuleActionsButtons.V2 operates on the rule identifier and does not need the ruler rule object.

title: Silence menu action does nothing in the ruler-free list view
body: Clicking Silence in AlertRuleMenu sets showSilenceDrawer to true, but the drawer is only rendered when rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) is true. In the list view `rule` is undefined while the Prometheus-based ability still makes the Silence menu item visible, so clicking Silence opens nothing and the user cannot create a silence from the list view.

title: skipToken does not neutralize the Duplicate ability for non-Grafana rules
body: useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities converts skipToken to undefined, and useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities treats an undefined rule as supported because useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable returns loading=false for no rule. Duplicate therefore becomes [AlwaysSupported, grafana AlertingRuleCreate permission]. When AlertRuleMenu renders a cloud/data-source rule, a user who has Grafana rule-create permission but not the external rule-create permission incorrectly gets the Duplicate action via the OR of ruler and Grafana abilities.

title: Combined-rule abilities no longer treat federated groups as immutable
body: useAllAlertRuleAbilities previously used isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) and marked rules in federated groups as not supported for update/delete/pause-type actions. The refactored useAllRulerRuleAbilities hardcodes isFederated to false, so federated Mimir rule groups can now appear editable/removable in consumers using CombinedRule abilities, regressing the previous protection for federated groups.

title: Grafana recording rules lose pause and export abilities
body: The Prometheus-based abilities gate Pause, Restore, DeletePermanently, and ModifyExport on prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule). The ruler-based path used isGrafanaManagedAlertRule, which includes Grafana recording rules as well as alerting rules. As a result, Grafana recording rules in the ruler-free list view cannot be paused or exported even though those actions were supported for them through the ruler-based path.

title: Grafana rule list items are rendered without a React key
body: The filtered results map returns GrafanaRuleListItem without passing key={key}, unlike the previous GrafanaRuleLoader branch and the data-source branch in the same switch. React will reconcile these stateful list items by index, causing console warnings and risking child state such as modals/drawers in RuleActionsButtons being associated with the wrong rule if the rendered order changes.

title: Grafana rule link drops the returnTo parameter
body: The deleted GrafanaRuleListItem built its view href with createReturnTo() so the rule detail view received a returnTo query parameter pointing back to the current list context. The new component links directly to /alerting/grafana/${uid}/view without returnTo, so navigation back from a rule opened from the filtered/group list loses the list context that the previous link explicitly preserved.

title: Menu test codifies the missing Delete item instead of covering it
body: The test grants AlertingRuleDelete globally and in folder access control and defines a delete menu selector, but the More-menu test expects exactly four menu items and never asserts Delete. This hides the regression that Delete is not rendered in the ruler-free Grafana list even for users with delete permission.

title: Pause action never appears in the ruler-less list view
body: The menu computes canPause from the new Grafana Prometheus abilities, but rendering still requires rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule). In the new list view rulerRule is always undefined, so the Pause/Unpause item can never be rendered there, despite the PR adding prom-based pause ability checks for that view. Users lose pause/unpause from the rule list and must open another view.

title: Delete action never appears in the ruler-less list view
body: The Delete menu item is gated on `canDelete && rulerRule`, while the new list view supplies only promRule and no rulerRule. Although canDelete can now be true from useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, the item is always hidden in that view. This removes delete-from-list functionality that was available when ruler data was loaded; the delete handler in RuleActionsButtons.V2 only needs the identifier/groupIdentifier, so the rulerRule gate is not necessary for invoking it.

title: Silence menu action opens no drawer in the ruler-less list view
body: In the new list view `rule` (the ruler rule) is undefined and only promRule is passed. The Silence menu item can be shown via the new prom abilities and sets showSilenceDrawer=true, but the drawer is rendered only when rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) is true. Clicking Silence therefore does nothing for Grafana rules in the list view.

title: skipToken does not actually disable Grafana duplicate ability
body: useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities/useGrafanaPromRuleAbility convert skipToken to undefined, and useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities treats an undefined rule as supported: loading is false, isProvisioned/isPluginProvided are false, so MaybeSupported becomes AlwaysSupported. Duplicate then becomes [supported=true, allowed=global Grafana create permission]. AlertRuleMenu ORs this with the ruler ability, so a cloud/data-source rule (for which skipToken is passed) can incorrectly show Duplicate for users who have Grafana create permission but lack the external rule-create permission.

title: Federated rule groups are no longer treated as immutable
body: useAllAlertRuleAbilities previously computed isFederated with isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) for CombinedRule callers and used it to block Update/Delete/Pause for federated groups. It now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which hard-codes isFederated=false. Federated Mimir/cloud rule groups can consequently be presented as editable, removable, and pausable even though they should remain immutable in the UI.

title: Grafana rules in filtered list are rendered without a React key
body: The grafana branch returns <GrafanaRuleListItem> without the key that the previous GrafanaRuleLoader element and the datasource branch use. In this dynamically appended/paginated list React will warn and may reuse component state (for example delete-modal, silence-drawer, or clone-redirect state in RuleActionsButtons) by position for a different rule when results change.

title: Rule detail link drops the returnTo parameter
body: The previous GrafanaRuleListItem built its view link with createReturnTo() so navigating to the rule detail could return to the current list context. The new component links only to `/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view` with no returnTo. Users opening a rule from the filtered or grouped list lose that explicit return destination and may not be taken back to the same list state.

title: Pause action is never rendered for Prometheus-only Grafana rules
body: The new list view supplies only a promRule and no rulerRule, and this PR computes canPause from the new Grafana prom abilities. Rendering still requires rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule), which is false when rulerRule is undefined, and MenuItemPauseRule also requires that ruler rule. Consequently Pause never appears in the new rule list even for editable, unpaused Grafana rules, despite the newly added ability check.

title: Delete action is never rendered for Prometheus-only Grafana rules
body: canDelete can now become true through useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities when only a promRule is available, but the Delete menu item is additionally gated by `rulerRule &&` and its handler is typed to require a RulerRuleDTO. In the new GrafanaGroupLoader/FilterView list, rulerRule is always undefined, so users with delete permission cannot delete a rule from the list. The GrafanaGroupLoader test even encodes this by expecting only four menu items despite granting delete permission.

title: Silence action opens no drawer for Prometheus-only rules
body: In the new list view RuleActionsButtons receives only promRule, so `rule` is undefined. Clicking Silence in AlertRuleMenu sets showSilenceDrawer to true, but this line only mounts SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer when rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) is true. The click therefore has no visible effect and silencing from the alert list is broken, even though the new prom abilities may show the Silence menu item.

title: skipToken does not actually skip Grafana prom abilities
body: Callers pass skipToken for cloud rules, non-Grafana prom rules, or absent prom rules, but useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities converts it to undefined and useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities still computes real abilities. For an undefined rule, Duplicate becomes [AlwaysSupported, Grafana-rule-create permission] because provisioned/plugin checks are false and loading is false. AlertRuleMenu ORs this with the ruler result, so Duplicate can appear for cloud or ruler-only rules based solely on an unrelated Grafana create permission. A skipped rule should return [false, false] for every action.

title: Federated rule groups lose their immutable status
body: useAllAlertRuleAbilities previously derived isFederated from isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) for CombinedRules and marked federated rules unsupported for Update/Delete. It now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which discards the group and hardcodes isFederated to false.
