The cache therefore conflates the two cases, so getForLogin(ORG_ONLY or ALL, "") can return the cached all-organizations result, or the reverse ordering can make a null-organization request reuse an empty/specific-organization result. Use a distinct sentinel that cannot be a supplied organizationId, or include the organizationId in the cache key.

title: New cache test cleans up a literal "alias" IdP instead of the created IdPs
body: The cleanup registration uses testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove, which binds a resource for an IdP literally named "alias" rather than each created idp-alias-i provider; the same mistake is repeated for idp-alias-20 at line 425. Cleanup will attempt to delete a non-existent provider and leave the twenty-plus created IdPs in the shared test realm, making the test order-dependent and potentially polluting other tests in the class. Capture each created alias in a lambda that deletes that alias.

title: Login-cache test never creates or removes a login-qualified IdP
body: testCacheIDPForLogin only creates a hideOnLogin IdP and removes a disabled IdP to assert that non-qualifying operations do not invalidate the caches, and it exercises invalidation only through an update that changes login availability. It never creates an enabled login-qualified IdP, nor removes one, after the login caches are populated, so a regression in the new positive invalidation paths in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.create() and remove() would not be caught. Add cases asserting that both operations clear the REALM_ONLY/ORG_ONLY/ALL login caches and that subsequent getForLogin calls return the updated membership.

title: New order() method is abstract and breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: CryptoProvider is an SPI loaded through ServiceLoader, but order() was added as an abstract method. Existing external or test implementations compiled against the previous interface do not implement it, so recompilation fails and already-compiled providers will throw AbstractMethodError when CryptoIntegration sorting invokes order(). This can prevent crypto-provider detection at startup. order() should be a default method, with only providers that need non-default precedence overriding it.

title: Equal-priority crypto providers are silently selected in classpath-dependent order
body: The change removes the previous fail-fast error for multiple CryptoProvider implementations and instead sorts by order() and silently uses the first provider, logging the others only at debug level. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider all return order 200, so when more than one is present the winner depends on ServiceLoader/classpath iteration order. In particular, an environment accidentally containing both FIPS and non-FIPS providers could silently run with the non-FIPS provider instead of failing, creating a compliance and security risk. The providers need distinct priorities, especially for FIPS, or detection should fail/warn prominently on a tie for the highest priority.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the default keystore provider instead of a BouncyCastle provider
body: This method returns KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider(), which is normally a JDK provider such as Sun and can change with the JVM default keystore configuration. That violates the CryptoProvider contract that this method returns the BouncyCastle or BouncyCastle-FIPS provider. Callers using the returned provider for BouncyCastle-specific algorithms, curves, paddings, or keystore types can fail with NoSuchAlgorithmException/NoSuchProviderException or silently use a different implementation than expected. It should return null or an explicit unsupported result, consistent with having no BouncyCastle provider, rather than misidentifying an arbitrary JDK provider.

title: ES384 and ES512 tests reuse a default P-256 key and only test self round-tripping
body: The test constructor generates one EC key pair without specifying a curve, normally P-256, and reuses it for ES256, ES384, and ES512. Consequently the 48-byte ES384 and especially 66-byte ES512 integer paths and DER long-form sequence lengths over 127 bytes produced by real P-521 signatures are not exercised. The assertions also only check that this provider can decode its own encoding; they never verify the generated ASN.1 DER against the original JDK signature or with JDK Signature.verify(). Mutually inverse encoding/decoding errors could therefore pass while producing non-interoperable signatures. Tests should generate P-256, P-384, and P-521 keys respectively and verify interoperability with the JDK signature implementation.

title: No test covers ServiceLoader registration or the new provider-ordering selection
body: The central behavior of this change is that AuthzClientCryptoProvider is discoverable through META-INF/services and that CryptoIntegration chooses the highest-order provider when several providers are present, but the only new test directly constructs AuthzClientCryptoProvider. A broken service registration, an incorrect order value, or a regression in CryptoIntegration sorting would not be caught. A test should load providers through CryptoIntegration/ServiceLoader and assert that the authz provider is selected when alone and that a higher-order provider such as DefaultCryptoProvider wins when both are present.

title: Equal-order providers are silently and nondeterministically selected instead of failing fast
body: DefaultCryptoProvider, FIPS1402Provider, and WildFlyElytronProvider all return order() 200. This change sorts providers by order and silently uses the first one, retaining ServiceLoader/classpath iteration order for ties and only logging the ignored providers at debug level. If the default and FIPS providers, or Elytron and default providers, accidentally coexist on the classpath, the selected provider is therefore classpath-dependent; in particular a non-FIPS provider can silently be selected in an environment expecting FIPS cryptography. Previously detection failed fast when multiple providers were present. A tie for the highest order should still fail, or the mutually exclusive server providers should have distinct deterministic priorities.

title: New abstract order() method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: Adding abstract int order() to the public CryptoProvider interface is source- and binary-incompatible for implementations outside this repository. Existing compiled implementations will throw AbstractMethodError when CryptoIntegration invokes order() through its comparator, and existing source implementations will no longer compile. A default method, for example returning 0, would preserve compatibility while allowing the built-in providers to declare their higher precedence.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns an unrelated JVM-default KeyStore provider
body: The CryptoProvider contract states that getBouncyCastleProvider returns the BouncyCastle (or BCFIPS) provider, but this implementation returns the provider associated with KeyStore.getDefaultType(), typically SUN/SunPKCS12 and configurable through JVM security settings. Callers that use the returned provider by name or expect BouncyCastle-only services such as BCFKS or AES/CBC/PKCS7Padding can therefore fail or silently use a different provider depending on JVM configuration. If no BouncyCastle provider is available, the method should fail clearly or return null as other non-BC providers do rather than masquerading as BouncyCastle.

title: ECDSA tests use one default EC key and only verify self-consistent round-tripping
body: The test creates a single EC key pair without specifying a curve, so on the usual SunEC provider it is a P-256 key even for the ES384 and ES512 cases, while the conversion is told to use 48- or 66-byte R/S components and merely zero-pads the P-256 values. It also only asserts concat -> DER -> concat round-tripping with the same implementation under test and never compares the DER result with the original Signature.sign() output or verifies it with Signature.verify(). A standards-incorrect but self-consistent encoder/decoder pair, or incorrect curve-length handling for real P-384/P-521 signatures, can therefore pass; each algorithm should use a key on its corresponding curve and validate against the JCA signature.

title: New order() method is abstract and breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: CryptoProvider is a ServiceLoader SPI, but order() was added as an abstract method instead of a default method. Any existing out-of-tree or downstream implementation compiled against the previous interface will throw AbstractMethodError when CryptoIntegration calls CryptoProvider::order during provider detection, and source implementations or mocks will no longer compile. Adding a default implementation, for example returning 0, would preserve compatibility while allowing built-in providers to declare higher precedence.

title: Equal provider orders make selection nondeterministic and silently ignore conflicting providers
body: Providers are now sorted only by order(), while DefaultCryptoProvider, FIPS1402Provider, and WildFlyElytronProvider all return 200. If more than one of them is accidentally present, the previous explicit 'multiple crypto providers' error is replaced by silently choosing whichever ServiceLoader/classpath ordering returns first. This can silently select the non-FIPS provider in a deployment expecting FIPS, and ServiceLoader instantiation can already have run the other providers' constructors and their global Java Security provider registration side effects. Built-in providers need distinct priorities or ties at the highest order should remain an error.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the default KeyStore provider instead of BouncyCastle
body: The CryptoProvider contract for getBouncyCastleProvider() is to return the BouncyCastle security provider, but this implementation returns the provider backing a newly created default-type KeyStore, typically the SUN provider for PKCS12. Callers that use the returned provider for BouncyCastle-specific algorithms, keystore types, or provider-name checks will therefore fail or misidentify the active crypto mode. It should return an actual BouncyCastle provider, return null as the Elytron provider does when BouncyCastle is unavailable, or throw UnsupportedOperationException like the other unsupported methods in this class.

title: ES384 and ES512 tests reuse a default-curve key and only assert round-trip identity
body: The test creates one EC key pair with KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair() and no ECGenParameterSpec, so it does not create P-384 or P-521 keys for ES384/ES512. It then only asserts that concatenated R/S converted to DER and back equals the padded concatenated value, without verifying the DER signature against the public key, comparing it with the original JCA DER signature, or checking the expected curve-specific lengths. Defects in 48/66-byte R/S handling, leading-zero stripping, or the long-form DER length needed for real ES512 signatures can therefore pass undetected. Each algorithm should generate a key on its corresponding curve and verify the reconverted DER signature.

title: Malformed zero-length ASN.1 integer escapes as NumberFormatException instead of IOException
body: readInteger() passes the decoded byte array directly to new BigInteger(bytes). A malformed DER integer with length 0 makes that constructor throw NumberFormatException, although callers such as asn1derToConcatenatedRS() are written to handle IOException for invalid signatures. Invalid input can consequently abort processing with an unchecked exception instead of the declared, handled error type. Zero-length and otherwise invalid integer encodings should be rejected with IOException before constructing the BigInteger.

title: Event listener still runs V2 code when both FGAP features are enabled
body: The new guard only checks ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ, but management() in this same class selects MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, regardless of the V1 flag. If both features are enabled, a ClientRemovedEvent therefore reaches ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(), which unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException, instead of the V2 case being skipped. The guard needs to exclude V2 (e.g. V1 && !V2) or the handler will throw on every client removal in that configuration.

title: NullPointerException when the all-clients resource does not exist
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no per-client resource exists the code falls back to SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...), which can return null when the 'Clients' all-resource is absent from the store. The result is passed unchecked to policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) and later dereferenced via resource.getScopes(), so a permission check crashes with an NPE/500 instead of returning false. The String-scope overload at lines 244-247 does null-check its resource; this overload needs the same guard.

title: Existing FGAP V2 realms never receive the new Clients resource type
body: init() returns immediately when the realm already has an admin-permissions client, so realms that enabled FGAP V2 while the schema contained only Users will never get the new 'configure', 'map-roles-client-scope' and 'map-roles-composite' scopes nor the 'Clients' all-resource created later in this method. For those realms, creating Clients permissions fails with missing-scope errors and evaluation has no all-clients resource to fall back to. Initialization needs to be idempotent and add missing scopes/resources for existing clients, or a migration must create them.

title: getClientsWithPermission returns the synthetic 'Clients' resource as a client id
body: findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) also matches the all-clients resource, which AdminPermissionsSchema.init creates with both name and type set to 'Clients'. When an all-clients permission grants the scope, granted.add(resource.getName()) therefore inserts the literal string 'Clients' into a set whose contract is client ids. Callers filtering clients by id get a bogus entry, a non-empty check can pass while the set contains no real client, and an all-clients-only grant yields no actual client ids from this method. The resource-type resource must be skipped or expanded to the real clients it covers.

title: canExchangeTo predicate now throws instead of returning a decision
body: canExchangeTo is a boolean authorization predicate; before this change MgmtPermissionsV2 inherited the V1 ClientPermissions implementation and callers received true/false. Now that MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2, every token-exchange permission check in a V2 deployment hits this unconditional UnsupportedOperationException, surfacing as a server error instead of a permit/deny decision and breaking client token exchange even for realms not using the new Clients permissions. The predicate should deny gracefully (or evaluate the applicable check) rather than throw.

title: getResourceName has no Clients branch
body: getResourceName only special-cases the Users resource type (returning 'All users' or the username) and falls through to resource.getDisplayName() for everything else. Client resources are created by getOrCreateResource with the client UUID as the resource name and no clientId-based display name, so permission and resource representations for the new Clients type expose a UUID, and the all-clients resource exposes 'Clients', instead of the clientId and an 'All clients' label analogous to Users. This makes the admin permission listings for clients misleading and inconsistent.

title: canView(ClientModel) bypasses a client-specific negative permission
body: canView(ClientModel) returns true immediately when canView() is true, and V2 canView() only evaluates the all-Clients resource for VIEW. If an administrator is granted VIEW on all clients but explicitly denied VIEW on one sensitive client through a negative policy on that client's resource, requireView(sensitiveClient) still passes. The client-specific denial is never evaluated, unlike canManage/canConfigure which evaluate the specific client resource, so the denied client remains directly viewable.

title: Role-mapping checks do not imply manage or the manage-clients admin role
body: canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles, and canMapClientScopeRoles only evaluate their exact FGAP scope and never fall back to canManage(client). An administrator with the MANAGE_CLIENTS realm role, or with a V2 MANAGE permission for the client (which canManage/canConfigure treat as the higher privilege), is therefore denied mapping that client's roles, composites, and client-scope roles. This is inconsistent with the manage > configure > view transitivity implemented elsewhere in this class and with the Users V2 behaviour where manage implies map-roles.

title: getClientsWithPermission returns the all-Clients resource name as a client id
body: resourceStore.findByType(server, "Clients") also returns the synthetic all-Clients resource created by AdminPermissionsSchema.init, whose name is the literal string "Clients". When the caller has an all-clients grant, the returned set contains "Clients" instead of (or in addition to) real client UUIDs, and when only an all-clients grant exists no actual client ids are returned at all. Callers expecting a set of client ids to filter client listings will match nothing for the all-clients case. The synthetic resource must be excluded and an all-clients grant expanded to real clients (or handled by the caller).

title: NullPointerException when the all-Clients resource does not exist
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no client-specific resource exists the code loads the all-Clients resource via getResourceTypeResource and immediately calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) without a null check (the String overload of hasPermission does check for null). getResourceTypeResource returns null whenever the Clients resource was never provisioned - e.g. realms whose admin-permissions client was created before the Clients type existed, since AdminPermissionsSchema.init returns early when that client already exists - so every canView/canManage/canConfigure check for such a realm throws instead of returning false, breaking admin client operations with a 500.

title: Listener still calls V2-unsupported methods when both FGAP features are enabled
body: The listener is now guarded only by Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1), but AdminPermissions.management()/evaluator() prefer MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever the V2 feature is also enabled. With both features on, deleting a client fires ClientRemovedEvent, passes the new guard, and calls MgmtPermissionsV2.clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which in ClientPermissionsV2 unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException. The guard needs to also exclude the V2 case (or management() must not return the V2 implementation here), otherwise client deletion fails or logs an exception and the V1 cleanup is not performed.

title: getResourceName has no Clients branch
body: getResourceName only special-cases the Users resource type (returning "All users" or the username) and falls through to resource.getDisplayName() for everything else. Client resources created by getOrCreateResource are named by the client UUID and have no display name set, so authorization representations for the new Clients permissions will show a null/blank or raw-UUID name instead of "All clients" or the client's clientId. Add the analogous Clients branch resolving the client via session.clients().

title: Existing admin-permissions clients never receive the new Clients type or scopes
body: init() returns immediately whenever realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is non-null. A realm that already enabled FGAP V2 for Users therefore keeps the old resource server, which has no 'Clients' all-resource and lacks the new configure, map-roles-client-scope, and map-roles-composite scopes. Creating Clients permissions using those scopes then fails when their scopes cannot be found, and all-clients evaluation has no 'Clients' resource to evaluate, so the new Clients support does not work on already-initialized realms until the admin-permissions client is somehow recreated.

title: Removal listener still dispatches to V2 when both FGAP features are enabled
body: The new guard only checks ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1), but AdminPermissions.management() selects MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, regardless of V1. With both features enabled, a ClientRemovedEvent therefore calls ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(), which unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException, instead of the V1 cleanup the listener intends to run. The guard needs to exclude the V2 case, e.g. run only when V1 is enabled and V2 is not.

title: Map-roles checks ignore manage permission and manage-clients admins
body: canMapRoles(), canMapCompositeRoles(), and canMapClientScopeRoles() only check their exact FGAP scope for the client. Unlike canConfigure(), which first delegates to canManage(client), they do not treat a caller with the MANAGE_CLIENTS admin role or an FGAP manage grant on that client (or on all clients) as able to map roles. Such a full client administrator can create, update, configure, and delete the client but is denied client role-mapping and composite-role operations under V2, breaking role administration for otherwise fully privileged admins.

title: Global canView does not include an all-clients MANAGE grant
body: canView() only checks the default role-based view check or an FGAP VIEW grant on the all-clients resource. A caller granted only MANAGE on all clients passes canManage() and canView(ClientModel) for each client (through canConfigure/canManage), and canView(ClientScopeModel) explicitly accepts MANAGE, but fails the no-argument canView(). Endpoints that gate on requireView()/canViewClientScopes()/canList-style global checks therefore return 403 for a manage-only administrator who is otherwise allowed to manage and view every client.

title: getResourceName has no Clients branch
body: getResourceName() special-cases only the Users resource type, translating a user resource id to the username and the Users all-resource to 'All users'. Client resources fall through to resource.getDisplayName(), which for resources created by getOrCreateResource() is the client UUID, and the Clients all-resource is not labelled 'All clients'. Permission and resource representations for the new Clients type will therefore show opaque client UUIDs instead of the clientId, unlike the human-readable names provided for Users.

title: New exit-code contract for rolling updates is not asserted
body: The PR changes the recreate exit code from 4 to 3 and introduces exit code 4 for a disabled rolling-updates feature, and the documentation states that scripts should rely on the check command's exit code. However, testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the error message for the metadata subcommand and does not assert exit code 4, no test covers the disabled-feature branch of the check subcommand, and testWrongVersions asserts only messages without asserting the new recreate exit code 3. A regression that swaps or breaks these exit codes would therefore pass the tests while breaking automation and consumers that distinguish rolling, recreate, and feature-disabled outcomes.

title: Feature-disabled check path and changed exit codes are not verified
body: The new testFeatureNotEnabled test launches only the update-compatibility metadata subcommand and asserts only its error message. The check subcommand has a separate feature gate in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run(), so removing or breaking that gate would not fail any test despite the documentation promising that both commands fail when rolling-updates is disabled. The test also does not assert the new FEATURE_DISABLED exit code 4, and testWrongVersions does not assert the recreate exit code after CompatibilityResult changed it from 4 to 3 and reassigned 4 to feature-disabled. Because the guide explicitly tells automation to rely on the exit code rather than messages, these contract changes could regress without detection.

title: Default-strategy deployments are created without the required rolling-updates feature
body: createInitialDeployment() returns immediately when updateStrategy is null, before enabling Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES. Both parameterized tests use the null/default strategy: testCacheMaxCount expects a rolling upgrade for the null case, and testImageChange also exercises the operator upgrade flow. The PR's own operator documentation states that the rolling-updates feature must be enabled or the operator will fail, and the CLI check now exits with FEATURE_DISABLED when it is not enabled. The null-strategy cases therefore either fail/recreate instead of rolling or are not actually testing the new feature-gated path. Enable rolling-updates for the default case as well, or explicitly document and adjust the expectations if the default path is exempt.

title: New exit-code contract for disabled feature and recreate is not asserted
body: This PR changes RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 and introduces FEATURE_DISABLED=4, while the guide tells users to rely only on the check command's exit code. However testFeatureNotEnabled only launches the metadata subcommand and only asserts the stderr text; it does not assert exit code 4, and there is no equivalent disabled-feature test for the check subcommand. testWrongVersions likewise asserts messages but not exit code 3. A regression that swaps or breaks these codes would therefore pass the tests while breaking scripts and the operator that consume the numeric codes.

title: Caution incorrectly implies all operator deployments fail without rolling-updates
body: The added caution says that while in preview the rolling-updates feature must be enabled, otherwise the Keycloak Operator will fail. As written this is unconditional, but the same section documents '<not set>' as the default strategy that mimics Keycloak 26.1 or older behavior, which is a supported configuration that does not opt into the new update-strategy handling. Readers running the operator without spec.update.strategy will conclude they must enable a preview feature or their existing deployment will break. Scope the caution to deployments that actually use the update feature/strategy (for example when spec.update.strategy is set), mirroring whatever the operator really requires.

title: VIEW permission incorrectly grants global group manage permission
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() evaluates hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), so an FGAP admin granted only the Groups 'view' scope passes the no-arg manage check. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup relies on auth.groups().requireManage(), therefore a view-only admin can create top-level groups and perform other operations gated only by canManage(), a privilege escalation beyond read-only access. canManage() should only accept MANAGE.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
body: In GroupPermissionsV2, per-group authorization resources are named with the GroupModel id (AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup returns group.getId() as the resource name), while Resource.getId() is the authorization-store UUID. This code passes groupResource.getId() to hasPermission(), which looks the value up with resourceStore.findByName(), and then adds groupResource.getId() to the returned set. Callers such as UsersResource.getUsersCount() and searchForUser() pass that set to user queries as actual group ids, so members of groups the admin may view/manage are miscounted or filtered out, and the specific-group check silently falls back to the all-Groups resource. It should pass and return groupResource.getName().

title: Lazily created resources are not assigned their resource type
body: getOrCreateResource() creates a resource for a known resourceType but never calls resource.setType(resourceType), unlike AdminPermissionsSchema.init() and the V1 permission initializers which explicitly set the type. The new GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() enumerates candidates with resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE), so lazily created per-group resources will not be found by that lookup even after fixing which identifier is returned. The created resource should have its type set to the requested resourceType.

title: Existing admin-permissions clients never receive the new Groups type, scopes, or aggregate resource
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() already exists. Realms that enabled FGAP V2 before this change therefore keep a client/resource server created from the old schema: the 'Groups' aggregate resource and group-specific scopes such as manage-members, view-members, and manage-membership are never added. On those realms group permission creation can fail when resolving scopes and GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission() can dereference a missing Groups type resource, so the new Groups support only works for newly initialized realms unless an upgrade path populates the missing scopes/resources.

title: VIEW permission is treated as MANAGE for global group operations
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when the caller has either VIEW or MANAGE on the all-Groups resource. This no-arg check is used by GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() via requireManage(), so an admin granted only view on all groups can create top-level groups. canManage() should require MANAGE only, as canManage(GroupModel) correctly does.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
body: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), groupResource.getId() is the internal authorization-resource UUID, while the group's ID is stored as the resource name (see AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource/resolveGroup, and hasPermission() which looks resources up by name). Passing getId() to hasPermission() therefore fails the findByName lookup and falls back to the all-Groups resource, and the set returned contains authorization UUIDs rather than group IDs. Callers such as UsersResource.getUsersCount() and searchForUser() pass this set to user queries as group IDs, so counts/searches for members of a group with view-members/manage-members permission return wrong (typically empty) results.

title: Existing FGAP V2 realms never get the new Groups resource or scopes
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns immediately when the realm already has an admin-permissions client. Realms that enabled admin permissions before this PR therefore never receive the new 'Groups' all-resource or the group-only scopes (manage-members, view-members, manage-membership) that init() would create from the schema. Creating a group permission in such a realm will fail when getOrCreateResource() cannot find those scopes, and getResourceTypeResource() for Groups will return null during evaluation. A migration/backfill for existing resource servers is needed.

title: getResourceName does not translate group resources to group names
body: getResourceName() special-cases the Users resource type to return the user's username instead of the resource name (which is the user's ID), but has no equivalent branch for the new Groups resource type. Group resources are also named by their group ID, so policy/permission representations for group resources will fall through to resource.getDisplayName() and expose the group UUID rather than a human-readable group name.

title: VIEW permission on all groups grants global group manage
body: canManage() with no group argument returns true for either VIEW or MANAGE on the all-groups resource. This method backs GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup via requireManage(), so an FGAP admin granted only view access to all groups can create top-level groups and perform other global manage operations. Unlike canManage(GroupModel), which correctly requires only MANAGE, the global check should require MANAGE only.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
body: Group authorization resources are created with the group ID as the resource name, while Resource.getId() is an unrelated internal authorization-store UUID. This loop calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...), which does findByName(server, UUID) and therefore misses the per-group resource and falls back to the all-groups resource, and then adds that same UUID to the granted set. Callers such as UsersResource.searchForUser and getUsersCount expect actual GroupModel IDs in UserModel.GROUPS, so per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS grants are not correctly used to filter or count group members. It should pass and return groupResource.getName() and must not treat the all-groups type resource (named 'Groups') as a group.

title: Existing FGAP v2 realms never receive the new Groups resource or scopes
body: init() returns immediately whenever the realm already has an admin-permissions client. Realms that enabled FGAP v2 before this change therefore keep a resource server containing only the previously defined Clients and Users all-type resources and scopes, with no Groups resource and no manage-members/view-members/manage-membership scopes. Group permissions cannot be created or evaluated correctly in such realms; GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission can also receive null from getResourceTypeResource and pass it to policyStore.findByResource. The schema initialization needs an upgrade path that adds missing resource types and scopes for an existing admin-permissions client, or evaluation needs null-safe handling.

title: MessageFormat choice branches are excluded from HTML sanitization
body: For linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit* and error-invalid-multivalued-size, normalizeValue() replaces the entire '{n,choice,...}' segment with '...' before the OWASP sanitizer runs. Any HTML placed inside a choice branch, for example '{0,choice,0#<script>alert(1)</script>|1#second|1<seconds}', is therefore never inspected, while Java MessageFormat will emit the selected branch text at runtime. Only the choice-limit syntax such as '1<' should be neutralized, or each choice branch should be extracted and sanitized, rather than discarding the whole user-controlled segment.

title: Missing English bundle aborts verification with an unchecked exception
body: verifySafeHtml() derives the English file name from the localized file and throws a RuntimeException when that derived file cannot be read. verify() only declares MojoExecutionException and its caller-facing contract is to return collected verification messages, so a locale bundle whose English counterpart is missing or whose name does not match the derivation regex aborts the whole plugin run with a stack trace instead of reporting the offending file and continuing or failing as a MojoExecutionException.

title: Anchor mismatch message does not identify the key or file
body: When santizeAnchors() rejects a translation it adds only 'Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string', without the message key or properties file, unlike the Illegal HTML diagnostic which includes both. The verifier runs over hundreds of message files, so a translator or maintainer seeing this build failure cannot locate the offending entry from the message alone.

title: Java MessageFormat choice syntax breaks Account UI i18next message
body: This bundle is rendered by the Account UI with i18next-style placeholders, as the surrounding error messages use {{0}}, {{1}} and {{2}}. Changing this entry to Java MessageFormat '{0}' plus '{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}' means i18next will not substitute the values or evaluate the choice; users will see the literal braces/choice expression instead of a formatted sentence. The Java choice form belongs only in the server-side theme bundle, not in this UI bundle.

title: Java MessageFormat choice syntax breaks Admin UI i18next message
body: As in the Account UI bundle, this Admin UI bundle uses i18next {{0}}-style interpolation for its error messages. Replacing 'Attribute {{0}} ... {{2}} value(s).' with '{0}' and '{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}' introduces syntax i18next cannot evaluate, so the message will render literally without the attribute name and bounds substituted. Keep the UI bundle in {{ }} form and apply the choice-format change only to the server-side Java bundle.

title: Lithuanian totpStep1 was replaced with Italian text
body: The Lithuanian account bundle now contains 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', which is Italian for 'Install one of the following applications on your mobile phone'. Lithuanian users will see instructions in the wrong language; the previous Lithuanian sentence should be kept, translated without the removed anchor tags.

title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 was replaced with Italian text
body: The Lithuanian login bundle now contains the Italian sentence 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' instead of a Lithuanian translation of 'Install one of the following applications on your mobile:'. Lithuanian users will see Italian on the login TOTP setup page; restore a Lithuanian translation without the removed anchor tags.

title: Traditional Chinese text inserted into Simplified Chinese bundle
body: totpStep1 now reads '在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：', using Traditional Chinese characters (手機, 應用程式) in the messages_zh_CN bundle whose other entries use Simplified Chinese (手机, 应用程序). Convert it to Simplified Chinese, e.g. '在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：', so zh_CN users do not see a different script.

title: No test that legitimate HTML or matching anchors pass
body:
Every test asserts that an error message is present; none asserts that a clean bundle returns an empty result. Legitimate cases such as noHtml_en itself, a translation whose anchors exactly match the English anchors, allowed

//
markup when the English value contains HTML, numeric <0> placeholders and MessageFormat choice values are untested, so a regression that makes the sanitizer reject all HTML would still pass this suite while breaking valid translations.

title: Missing English bundle aborts verification with an unchecked exception
body: verifySafeHtml() derives the English file by rewriting the translated file's path and throws a bare RuntimeException when that file cannot be opened. verify() only declares and handles MojoExecutionException/IOException for reading the target file, so a translation whose English counterpart is absent or named differently (new theme type, renamed bundle, or a standalone properties file) crashes the whole verification run with a stack trace instead of producing a collected verification message, and no other files/keys are reported.

title: Anchor-mismatch message does not identify the key or file
body: When santizeAnchors() rejects an anchor tag it adds only "Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string", without the message key or the properties file. The Illegal HTML branch at line 111 includes both, but this branch runs over hundreds of keys in dozens of locale files, so a build failure from this message gives maintainers/translators no way to locate the offending entry.

title: No test that legitimate HTML passes verification
body:
All new tests assert that a violation is present (illegal tag, HTML where English has none, changed anchor); there is no fixture asserting an empty result for a translation that legitimately reuses the English string's allowed HTML, e.g. matching anchors plus

/
/, numeric placeholder tags, or a MessageFormat choice value. A regression that flags every HTML-bearing translation (for example in santizeAnchors() or the canonical
comparison) would therefore still pass the whole test suite.

title: Lithuanian totpStep1 replaced with Italian text
body: The Lithuanian account bundle now contains totpStep1="Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:", which is Italian, not Lithuanian. It replaced a Lithuanian sentence when the FreeOTP/Google Authenticator links were removed, so Lithuanian users will see TOTP setup instructions in Italian.

title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 replaced with Italian text
body: The Lithuanian login bundle now contains loginTotpStep1="Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:", which is Italian, not Lithuanian. It replaced a Lithuanian sentence when the FreeOTP/Google Authenticator links were removed, so Lithuanian users will see TOTP setup instructions in Italian on the login pages.

title: Simplified Chinese bundle now uses Traditional Chinese for totpStep1
body: totpStep1 was changed to "在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：", written in Traditional Chinese characters (手機, 應用程式, 之一), while the rest of this messages_zh_CN (Simplified Chinese) bundle uses Simplified characters. Simplified Chinese users will see an inconsistent script for the TOTP setup instruction; the Simplified rendering of the new English sentence should be used instead.

title: HTML inside MessageFormat choice branches is never sanitized
body: normalizeValue() replaces each complete {n,choice,...} expression with "..." before the OWASP sanitizer runs. Consequently, markup placed in a choice branch for keys such as linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit.* or error-invalid-multivalued-size is never inspected: for example a branch containing a script or malicious anchor passes verification if the rest of the value passes, but MessageFormat can select and output that branch at runtime. The verifier should check the text of each choice alternative after removing only the choice syntax and comparison operators, rather than discarding the whole expression.

title: Java MessageFormat choice syntax breaks Account UI interpolation
body: This Account UI resource uses i18next-style double-brace placeholders ({{0}}, {{1}}, etc.) throughout the file, but error-invalid-multivalued-size was changed to Java MessageFormat syntax: {0}, {1}, and {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}. i18next does not evaluate MessageFormat choice expressions, so this value will render literal or unresolved placeholders instead of the interpolated limits and pluralized noun. Keep the UI resource in its double-brace/value(s) form and handle that form in the verifier instead.

title: Java MessageFormat choice syntax breaks Admin UI interpolation
body: As in the other React UI resources, this file previously used i18next-style {{0}}/{{1}}/{{2}} placeholders for error-invalid-multivalued-size, but it was changed to Java MessageFormat {0}/{1}/{2,choice,...}. The Admin UI's i18next interpolation does not evaluate MessageFormat choice expressions, so the formatted error can show literal placeholders instead of the attribute limits. The Java choice form belongs only in the server-side theme properties, not in this UI resource.

title: Lithuanian totpStep1 was replaced with Italian text
body: The Lithuanian account message totpStep1 now reads "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:", which is Italian, replacing the previous Lithuanian sentence. Lithuanian users will see setup instructions in the wrong language. Replace it with a Lithuanian translation of "Install one of the following applications on your mobile:" without the removed anchor tags.

title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 was replaced with Italian text
body: The Lithuanian login message loginTotpStep1 now reads "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:", which is Italian, replacing the previous Lithuanian sentence. Lithuanian users will see TOTP setup instructions in the wrong language during login. Replace it with the Lithuanian translation of the anchor-free English sentence.

title: Simplified Chinese file now uses Traditional Chinese text
body: The new totpStep1 text "在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：" uses Traditional Chinese characters (手機, 應用程式) in the messages_zh_CN (Simplified Chinese) file. It should use the Simplified Chinese equivalent, e.g. "在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：", to match the locale.

title: Anchor mismatch error does not identify the file or key
body: santizeAnchors() receives the message key but never uses it, and the added message only says "Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string". Unlike the Illegal HTML message, it contains neither the key nor the file. When the verifier runs over hundreds of properties files and thousands of keys, a translator cannot locate the offending entry from this message. Include the key and file in the anchor-mismatch message.

title: Missing English counterpart aborts verification with an unchecked exception
body: verifySafeHtml() derives the English file by rewriting the locale suffix and throws a raw RuntimeException if that derived file cannot be read. verify() only converts IOException to MojoExecutionException and callers otherwise receive collected message strings, so a properties file without a matching _en counterpart (or with a differently named English locale) aborts the whole verification run and masks all other results instead of producing a locatable verification/build error for that file.

title: No positive test that legitimate HTML and anchors pass verification
body: All new sanitizer tests assert that violations are reported; none asserts an empty result for a valid translation that uses allowed HTML (p/strong/b/br) when the English source contains HTML, or for a translation reusing the exact English anchor. A regression that strips or flags all allowed markup, or breaks the anchor-removal logic so legitimate translations always fail, would still pass this suite. Add clean English/translation fixtures expecting no messages.

title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing OAuth2 grant factories
body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory previously had no abstract methods, so existing custom grant factories implement only the old methods. Adding abstract getShortcut() means such factories fail to compile when rebuilt, and already-deployed binaries throw AbstractMethodError when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit iterates all OAuth2GrantType factories and calls getShortcut(). This can break server startup/token issuance for deployments with custom grants. Provide a default method (for example returning the unknown shortcut) instead of an abstract method, or otherwise handle factories that do not supply a shortcut.

title: OAuth2GrantType.Context copy constructor was removed
body: The public Context(Context) copy constructor was removed while Context is the object passed to custom OAuth2GrantType implementations. Code that wrapped or copied a grant context (for example to adjust form parameters before delegating) will no longer compile, and deployed code using the constructor will fail with NoSuchMethodError. Restore the copy constructor and make it copy the newly added grantType field, rather than deleting it.

title: Token issuance now fails for an unregistered grant type instead of using unknown encoding
body: getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext substitutes UNKNOWN only when the GRANT_TYPE attribute is null. If the attribute contains any non-null grant string that is not found in the factory shortcut maps, encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException. Since TokenManager.initToken now calls this for every access token, previously working flows/custom grants whose grant string is not identical to a registered OAuth2GrantType factory id will fail token creation with a server error instead of issuing a token. Fall back to the UNKNOWN/'na' shortcut for unmapped grant types (and log it) rather than failing issuance.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic and wrong substring offsets
body: Encoded token ids are 2 chars session type + 2 chars token type + 2 chars grant type, so the grant shortcut is substring(4, 6). The matcher uses substring(3, 5) and returns false when that substring equals the expected shortcut (if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false). It therefore does not verify the grant type at all for normal ids and can reject only by coincidence. Events asserting CODE_TO_TOKEN/REFRESH/DEVICE/CIBA token ids will pass even if the wrong grant was encoded. Change to reject when !items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut).

title: Constructor checks grantType twice and never checks rawTokenId
body: The constructor has Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") on line 73 instead of requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...). A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted and later encoded as the literal string "null" after the colon by DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId, producing a corrupt token id rather than failing fast at construction. Fix the argument to rawTokenId.

title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks all custom grant-type factories
body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is the extension point implemented by custom OAuth2 grant types, but getShortcut() was added as an abstract interface method with no default implementation. Every existing third-party factory therefore fails to compile/link against this version, and a factory that returns null at runtime will also fail startup when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory puts the null shortcut into a ConcurrentHashMap. Add a default method (for example returning the unknown shortcut) so existing providers continue to work.

title: Public copy constructor of OAuth2GrantType.Context was removed
body: The public Context(Context) copy constructor was deleted while the main constructor now also dereferences formParams to capture grantType. Code outside this PR (custom grant types or wrappers that cloned a Context before delegating) can no longer compile, and any caller constructing Context with a null formParams map now gets a NullPointerException from formParams.getFirst(...) instead of merely storing null. Restore/deprecate the copy constructor and handle a null formParams if that was previously tolerated.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic and wrong substring offsets
body: The encoded prefix is 6 characters laid out as sessionType[0,2) tokenType[2,4) grantType[4,6), but the matcher checks substring(3,5) and returns false when that substring equals the expected grant shortcut. As written it accepts token IDs with any grant shortcut (substring(3,5) will normally not equal the expected value, so it falls through to the UUID check) and can reject a correct one, so expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken do not actually verify the new grant encoding and will mask missing/incorrect GRANT_TYPE wiring in the grants they cover. It should be: if (!items[0].substring(4,6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;

title: Constructor validates grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId
body: Line 73 repeats Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") instead of checking rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted and later produces a token ID ending in ':null' (or an NPE downstream) instead of failing fast at construction. Change the second check to requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...).

title: encodeTokenId does not validate the 2-character shortcut length required by the decoder
body: encodeTokenId concatenates session/token/grant shortcuts without checking that the grant shortcut is exactly 2 characters, while getTokenContextFromTokenId (line 74) rejects any prefix whose length is not exactly 6. A grant factory returning a 1- or 3-character shortcut (the new OAuth2GrantTypeFactory javadoc even says 'usually like 3-letters') will silently mint access tokens whose IDs can never be decoded, throwing IllegalArgumentException on later use. Validate shortcut length (and uniqueness) at encode/startup time and fix the javadoc to state the 2-character requirement.

title: Token issuance now fails hard for any unregistered grant type instead of using the unknown fallback
body: getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext maps a missing grant type to the UNKNOWN shortcut 'na', but encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException when a non-null grant string has no registered shortcut. Because TokenManager.initToken now runs this encoder for every access token, any flow that sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE to a value not backed by an OAuth2GrantTypeFactory id (legacy/custom token-endpoint grants or extensions that set the attribute themselves) changes from successfully issuing a token to failing the whole token request with a 500. Fall back to the UNKNOWN shortcut for unmapped grants instead of aborting issuance.

title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks custom grant-type factories
body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is an extension interface, but getShortcut() was added as an abstract method without a default implementation. Existing custom grant factories compiled against the old interface will fail with AbstractMethodError when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() iterates all OAuth2GrantType factories and calls getShortcut(), and source implementations will no longer compile. This can break server startup or token issuance for deployments with custom grants. Provide a default implementation, for example returning the unknown shortcut, so existing factories continue to work.

title: Public OAuth2GrantType.Context copy constructor was removed
body: The previously public Context(Context) copy constructor has been removed while changing the main constructor to derive grantType from formParams. Code in custom grant types or delegating/wrapping grant implementations that used new OAuth2GrantType.Context(existingContext) will now fail to compile, and already-compiled code will fail with NoSuchMethodError. The copy constructor should be retained, copying grantType as well, or at least deprecated through a compatibility cycle.

title: Unknown grant type now fails all access-token issuance instead of falling back
body: TokenManager.initToken() calls encodeTokenId() for every access token, and encodeTokenId() throws IllegalStateException when the GRANT_TYPE client-session attribute is a non-null value that is not exactly a registered OAuth2GrantTypeFactory id. Token creation previously succeeded in that situation, and getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext() already treats a missing grant as the unknown value 'na'; an unregistered, aliased, or extension-supplied grant string now turns token issuance into a server error instead of using the same unknown fallback.

title: Grant shortcut length is documented inconsistently and never validated
body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() javadoc describes the value as 'usually like 3-letters', but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider encodes session, token and grant shortcuts without validating length and getTokenContextFromTokenId() requires the whole encoded prefix to be exactly 6 characters, i.e. exactly 2 characters per shortcut. A factory following the javadoc and returning a 3-letter shortcut, or returning a 1-letter/empty/null shortcut, produces token IDs that the decoder rejects, or fails with an NPE from the ConcurrentHashMap, instead of being rejected clearly at startup. Document exactly two characters and validate uniqueness and length in postInit() and in the lazy refresh paths.

title: Decoding throws on malformed or newer token IDs instead of returning UNKNOWN
body: getTokenContextFromTokenId() returns UNKNOWN for legacy token IDs without a colon, but throws IllegalArgumentException for any colon-containing ID whose prefix is not exactly 6 characters or whose session/token/grant shortcut is unknown to this node. That is inconsistent backward-compatibility handling: during rolling upgrades, or when the planned introspection/userinfo consumers decode tokens issued by a newer node with a new shortcut, validation would fail with an exception rather than falling back to the normal session lookup. Unknown or malformed encodings should be treated like legacy IDs and return UNKNOWN context.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher checks the wrong substring and inverts the comparison
body: The encoded token ID format is two chars session type, two chars token type, then two chars grant type, so the grant shortcut is items[0].substring(4, 6). The matcher uses substring(3, 5) and returns false when that substring equals expectedGrantShortcut. For a normal ID such as onrtac the checked substring is 'ta', never 'ac', so expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken and expectAuthReqIdToToken pass regardless of the encoded grant type as long as the raw part is a UUID; the new grant-encoding behaviour is effectively untested by these integration assertions.

title: Constructor validates grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId
body: The fourth constructor check is Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed"), repeating the grantType check instead of checking the rawTokenId parameter. A null rawTokenId therefore slips through and encodeTokenId() silently produces an ID ending in ':null', which later decodes to the literal raw ID "null" rather than failing fast at construction.

title: Federated recovery codes are never marked as used
body: After a successful validation, this code only checks whether the retrieved credential reports allCodesUsed(); it does not persist that the just-used code is now consumed. For a locally stored credential the local credential provider performs that consumption during isValid(), but for a federated user validation is delegated to the user-storage validator and that local side effect does not happen. The storage implementation added in this PR likewise only checks for a matching raw code and its getCredentials() recreates every code as unused. Consequently the same federated recovery code can be replayed indefinitely, getNextRecoveryAuthnCode() keeps prompting for the first code, and the exhaustion check/regeneration required action at lines 85-92 never triggers.

title: Login bean throws NoSuchElementException when federated credential cannot be retrieved
body: The constructor unconditionally calls credentialModelOpt.get() (and then getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get() on line 21). RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential() now prefers getFederatedCredentialsStream(), which is a different provider capability from the isConfiguredFor() check that allowed the user into this flow: a federated validator can report the user as configured and validate codes without exposing a readable credential model, in which case both the federated and local lookups are empty. The login form then fails with NoSuchElementException/500 instead of rendering the recovery-code challenge.

title: getCredentials() loses the stored recovery credential's identity, label and used state
body: updateCredential() stores a CredentialModel with a generated id at line 195, but getCredentials() discards that stored model and fabricates a new RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel via createFromValues(rawCodes, createdDate, userLabel) without copying the stored id, and with every code re-created as unused (the stored userLabel is also never set in updateCredential(), so it is always null). Production code depends on this model both for the next-code number (LoginBean) and for removeStoredCredentialById(model.getId()) when codes are exhausted (RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator), so neither flow can address or track the actual federated credential correctly.

title: Federated recovery credential cannot be disabled or deleted
body: This PR adds recovery codes to supportsCredentialType(), updateCredential(), isConfiguredFor() and isValid(), but disableCredentialType() still only handles OTP types and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream() still only returns OTP. Federated credential removal (used by admin/account deletion and by RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator when all codes are used via removeStoredCredentialById) is delegated to disableCredentialType(), so a federated recovery credential silently survives deletion attempts and remains valid afterwards.

title: No test covers the fallback to local storage for federated users
body: The new test only covers a federated provider that supports recovery codes, asserting the codes land in user storage and not in the DB. The other half of the feature title/branch in CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential() - updateCredential() returning false (federated provider does not support the type, read-only storage, or imported user) and the credential then being created in the local DB and still usable for login - is never exercised for a federated user, so a regression in the local fallback for federated users would not be caught.

title: Exhausted federated recovery credential is removed with local-only API
body: After this change RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential can return a credential from getFederatedCredentialsStream, but when allCodesUsed is true the code still calls credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId()). That API removes a locally stored credential, not a credential owned by a user-storage provider, and the federated model's id may be null or synthetic. The exhausted federated credential therefore remains in user storage while the user is only given the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action; if that action is not completed, the stale exhausted credential remains and subsequent login can again select it. Federated exhaustion needs disableCredentialType/removal through the federated updater rather than removeStoredCredentialById.

title: Login bean crashes when federated recovery credential is absent, type-only, or exhausted
body: The bean now obtains the credential through RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential and immediately calls credentialModelOpt.get(), RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel on it, and getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get(). For a local user configuredFor was previously backed by the same stored stream that the bean read, but a federated provider can report isConfiguredFor/supportsCredentialType while its getCredentials returns no recovery model, a type-only model without local-format credentialData, or a model whose codes are all used. Any of those cases throws NoSuchElementException or a credential-data parsing RuntimeException while rendering the login form, producing a server error instead of a usable challenge or required-action flow.

title: Recovery-code user label is dropped when creating the credential through updateCredential
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential builds the UserCredentialModel only from credentialModel.getType() and the JSON codes, without transferring credentialModel.getUserLabel() (the device/label) or the generation time. The previous required-action code called createCredential with the full RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel built from generatedCodes, generatedAt and generatedUserLabel, preserving the label for local storage. Now the updateCredential path used for user storage, and for local storage when the recovery provider handles updateCredential, receives no label, so the created recovery-code credential loses the user-provided label that is shown for credential management.

title: Federated recovery codes in the test storage are reusable and one-time use is not tested
body: The new federated isValid implementation returns true if any stored raw code equals the input, without removing or marking that code as used, and getCredentials rebuilds every stored code as unused via createFromValues. Consequently the new integration test, which logs in only once with code index 0, runs with indefinitely replayable recovery codes and can never exercise the authenticator's allCodesUsed cleanup/required-action branch for federated users. The test should consume/mark the used code in the storage double and assert that reusing the same code fails and that the next login requests the next code.

title: Federated getCredentials discards the stored recovery credential id
body: updateCredential stores the recovery credential with an id generated at line 195, but getCredentials creates a fresh RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel via createFromValues from the raw codes and never copies myUser.recoveryCodes.getId() onto the returned model, unlike the OTP branch which returns the stored credential with its id. Callers that use the federated credential id, such as deletion from account credential management and the authenticator's cleanup of exhausted codes, therefore receive a null or unrelated id and cannot address the credential actually stored in the user storage, making those federated flows untestable/incorrect with this storage double.

title: Login form crashes when federated credential cannot be retrieved
body: The bean calls credentialModelOpt.get() without checking whether RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) found a credential, and line 21 also calls getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get() without checking for an exhausted credential. For federated users, configuredFor/isConfiguredFor and getFederatedCredentialsStream are independent storage-provider operations: a provider can report the user as configured and validate codes while returning no credential model, or can return a credential whose codes are all used. In either case rendering the recovery-code login form throws NoSuchElementException instead of showing the form, potentially locking the user out.

title: Successful federated recovery code is not consumed
body: After credentialManager.isValid succeeds, this code only deletes the credential if the retrieved model already reports allCodesUsed(); it never persists a used state for the code that was just consumed. The storage implementation added by this PR likewise validates by checking whether any stored raw code equals the input and does not remove or mark that code, while its getCredentials method recreates every stored code as unused. Therefore, with the PR's federated implementation, the same recovery code can be replayed indefinitely, the prompt continues to request the first code, and the all-used regeneration path is never reached, defeating the single-use property of recovery codes.

title: Creating codes in user storage leaves an existing local credential valid
body: When updateCredential succeeds in user storage, the method only logs and does not remove or disable any recovery-code credential already stored in Keycloak's local database. This matters on upgrade and regeneration: before this change, recovery codes for federated users were always created locally, so regenerating them after the change creates a different set in user storage while the old local set remains. Credential validation can still accept credentials from either store even though getCredential prefers the federated set for display, so rotating recovery codes does not reliably invalidate the previous, possibly compromised, codes.

title: No test for federated user falling back to local storage or for code consumption
body: testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin covers only the branch where the test storage accepts the recovery credential and then logs in once using the first code. It does not cover a federated user whose storage rejects updateCredential and therefore must receive and use a local credential, nor does it verify that a used code cannot be reused, that the next requested code advances, that exhausted codes trigger regeneration, or that regenerated codes invalidate the old set. Those are the main new branches and security semantics introduced by the change, so regressions in them would not be caught.

title: Same concurrent-delete NPE remains in getSubGroupsStream overloads
body: The fix handles modelSupplier.get() returning null in getSubGroupsCount when a cached group is deleted before its database delegate is loaded, but the three getSubGroupsStream overloads at lines 256, 262 and 268 still dereference modelSupplier.get() unconditionally. The same cache-hit/delegate-miss race therefore still throws NullPointerException and produces a server error when subgroups of a concurrently deleted group are listed or searched. These overloads should return an empty stream, or otherwise handle a null delegate consistently.

title: getSubGroupsCount now returns null instead of a valid count
body: When the delegate group no longer exists, this returns null, whereas the persistent GroupModel implementations return a numeric count (0 when there are no subgroups). The null is propagated by GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount into GroupRepresentation.subGroupCount, so API consumers expecting a number receive no count and any caller that unboxes getSubGroupsCount() will still throw NullPointerException, only later. Returning 0L for a deleted group preserves the method contract and the representation.

title: Reader thread is never joined, making the concurrency test racy and leaky
body: The reader thread started at line 139 is never joined and there is no latch guaranteeing it has performed a read before deletions begin. The main thread sets deletedAll at line 155 and immediately asserts at line 157 while a read may still be in flight, so a late exception can be missed; conversely the thread may not have run at all before deletion finishes, giving false confidence. The unjoined non-daemon thread can also outlive the test and keep calling managedRealm.admin() during realm cleanup or subsequent tests, causing interference and flakiness. The test should signal that reading has started and join the thread before asserting.

title: Other subgroup-stream methods still dereference a possibly deleted delegate
body: The fix recognizes that modelSupplier.get() can return null when the cached group is deleted concurrently, but the three paginated/search getSubGroupsStream overloads at lines 256, 262, and 268 still call modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) without a null check. If deletion occurs after the GroupAdapter is obtained but before one of these methods delegates to the database, the same concurrent-deletion scenario therefore still produces a NullPointerException and a server error instead of being handled consistently with getSubGroupsCount().

title: Reader thread is never joined before asserting that no exceptions occurred
body: The background reader thread is started without keeping a reference, and after deletedAll is set the test immediately asserts that caughtExceptions is empty. The reader may still be in the middle of a groups request at that point and may add the very server-error exception this regression test is meant to catch only after the assertion has passed, so the test can pass spuriously. The unjoined thread can also leak into subsequent tests and keep calling the admin API; if a deletion throws, deletedAll is never set and the loop can run indefinitely. Store the thread, stop it in a finally block, and join it before asserting on caughtExceptions.

title: Concurrent-delete NPE remains in filtered and paged sub-group methods
body: The three getSubGroupsStream overloads at lines 254-269 still dereference modelSupplier.get() without a null check. That supplier ultimately calls getGroupById, which can return null when another transaction deletes the group after this cached adapter was created. A concurrent delete therefore still causes a NullPointerException for filtered or paged sub-group access, even though the same race was fixed for getSubGroupsCount. These overloads should handle a null delegate consistently, for example by returning an empty stream.

title: getSubGroupsCount now violates its non-null count contract
body: For an existing group, the delegate's count query returns a non-null Long, but this change returns null when the group was concurrently deleted. That null is propagated by GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount into GroupRepresentation.subGroupCount, changing the API value from a number to null and risking a later, harder-to-diagnose NullPointerException in consumers that unbox the count. Returning 0L for a deleted group would avoid the original NPE while preserving the method's non-null contract.

title: Reader thread is neither joined nor reliably stopped before the assertion
body: The reader thread started at line 139 is never joined. The main thread sets deletedAll at line 155 and asserts at line 157 that no exceptions were captured, but an in-flight groups() call can still fail and add an exception after that assertion, producing a false pass. Conversely, if a group removal throws before line 155, deletedAll is never set and the non-daemon reader keeps issuing requests after the test, potentially interfering with later tests. The flag should be set in a finally block, the thread should be retained and joined with a timeout before asserting, and coordination should guarantee that polling actually overlapped the deletions.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes on datetime sort keys
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key() applies math.floor()/math.ceil() directly to getattr(item, self.key). Its only caller, OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint, orders by -datetime, so the value is a datetime and math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError. build_cursor() calls this key function for non-empty result sets, so the first non-empty optimized audit-log page returns a 500 instead of results. It should reuse DateTimePaginator's timestamp conversion rather than the numeric Paginator implementation.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator does not convert cursor timestamps to datetimes
body: value_from_cursor() returns cursor.value unchanged. For audit logs that value is the millisecond epoch timestamp produced by DateTimePaginator-style cursors, but BasePaginator.build_queryset() compares it directly against the datetime column. Unlike DateTimePaginator.value_from_cursor(), which converts the timestamp to an aware datetime, this passes a number into a datetime comparison, causing a database/type error or incorrect filtering on every page after the first.

title: Negative offsets do not work on Django querysets
body: When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset is negative, this code executes queryset[negative_offset:stop]. Django querysets explicitly reject negative slicing with AssertionError ('Negative indexing is not supported'); they do not automatically handle it as the comments claim. A crafted cursor such as '0:-5:0' therefore produces an unhandled 500 rather than the claimed efficient reverse pagination. Negative offsets should be rejected with BadPaginationError or normalized before slicing.

title: BasePaginator still allows negative offsets for previous-page cursors
body: The new boundary handling clamps negative offsets only when cursor.is_prev is false: 'max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset'. A user-supplied cursor with is_prev=1 and a negative offset, for example '<value>:-5:1', still reaches queryset[negative:stop] and raises Django's negative-indexing AssertionError. This affects all existing BasePaginator/DateTimePaginator endpoints, not just the optimized audit-log path; negative offsets should be consistently rejected or clamped before slicing.

title: organization_context.member may be None
body: This line unconditionally dereferences organization_context.member.has_global_access for every non-superuser request, and it is evaluated even when optimized_pagination is not requested. RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is optional and can be None for principals granted organization access without an organization membership. For such requests this newly added code raises AttributeError and breaks the previously working default pagination path; it needs a None check or an access-based check.

title: No tests cover OptimizedCursorPaginator or the new endpoint branch
body: The PR adds a new paginator class, negative-offset behavior, and a query-parameter/superuser gated branch in OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint, but adds no tests. Tests using the audit-log endpoint's actual -datetime ordering, multi-page cursors, previous-page cursors, and negative offsets would have caught the datetime-key crash, timestamp-conversion bug, and Django negative-slicing failure before merge.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator is incompatible with datetime ordering used by audit logs
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key() applies math.floor/math.ceil directly to getattr(item, self.key), and value_from_cursor() returns cursor.value unchanged. The audit-log endpoint uses this paginator with order_by="-datetime", so the key is a datetime: math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError when build_cursor() computes next/prev cursors, causing a 500 on the first optimized page. Even if that did not crash, returning the raw millisecond cursor value instead of converting it to a datetime like DateTimePaginator.value_from_cursor() would make build_queryset() compare a datetime column against an integer. The optimized audit-log path is therefore unusable.

title: Negative-offset branch crashes because Django querysets reject negative slicing
body: When enable_advanced_features is true and a client supplies a cursor with a negative offset, this branch executes list(queryset[start_offset:stop]) with start_offset < 0 (and stop may also be <= 0). The comment claims the Django ORM handles negative slicing automatically, but Django QuerySet slicing explicitly raises AssertionError: "Negative indexing is not supported." A privileged audit-log user can craft e.g. a cursor with offset -1 and turn the request into a 500 instead of getting the claimed reverse-pagination behavior.

title: BasePaginator change still allows negative offsets for previous-page cursors on every endpoint
body: The new line clamps the offset only when cursor.is_prev is false: start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset. Cursor values are client-controlled (parsed from the cursor query parameter), so any user of any BasePaginator/DateTimePaginator/Paginator endpoint can supply a negative offset with is_prev=1 and still reach queryset[negative:stop], which Django rejects with AssertionError. This ungated change to the shared paginator does not fix the negative-index crash it appears to address and leaves a trivially triggerable 500 across all endpoints using these paginators, not just the admin-gated audit-log path.

title: Unconditional dereference of organization_context.member can crash non-optimized requests
body: enable_advanced is computed for every request as request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access, even when optimized_pagination is not requested. RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is optional (None when the caller has no membership record for the organization), and because of the unconditional evaluation before the branch, such a request raises AttributeError and returns 500 instead of serving the normal DateTimePaginator path. The member check should be guarded (e.g. member is not None) and ideally only evaluated when use_optimized is true.

title: New OptimizedCursorPaginator and endpoint branch have no test coverage
body: The PR adds a new paginator class, modifies shared BasePaginator slicing, changes Cursor documentation to endorse negative offsets, and adds a new query-param/permission-gated branch in OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint, but includes no tests. A single test exercising OptimizedCursorPaginator with the endpoint's actual -datetime ordering, plus tests for negative, zero, and previous-page cursors, would have caught the datetime TypeError and Django negative-slicing AssertionError described above before merge.
