title: OptimizedCursorPaginator is incompatible with the audit log's datetime ordering
body: The only caller enables this paginator with order_by="-datetime", so self.key is "datetime" and getattr(item, self.key) returns a datetime. get_item_key passes that datetime to math.floor/math.ceil, which raises TypeError for a non-empty page when build_cursor computes next/prev cursors. value_from_cursor also returns the raw cursor integer instead of converting the millisecond timestamp back to a datetime like DateTimePaginator does, so a subsequent page would filter the datetime column against an integer. The optimized audit-log path therefore cannot return a usable first or subsequent page.

title: Negative offsets do not work on Django querysets and will raise AssertionError
body: When enable_advanced_features is true and a client supplies a cursor with a negative offset, this code slices the Django queryset as queryset[negative:stop]. Django explicitly rejects negative queryset indexing with AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported (and stop can itself become negative for sufficiently negative offsets), contrary to the comment claiming the ORM handles it automatically. A privileged user requesting the advertised advanced mode can therefore trigger an unhandled 500 instead of receiving a page; the trimming check at line 891 also compares len(results) with offset+limit+extra even though a negative slice contains limit+extra rows, so the extra-row logic is inconsistent for this branch.

title: BasePaginator change still passes negative offsets for previous-page cursors and affects every paginator user
body: This modifies the shared BasePaginator used by many endpoints, not only audit logs. It clamps negative offsets only when cursor.is_prev is false; a user-controlled cursor such as <value>:-1:1 still reaches queryset[negative:stop] and raises Django's negative-indexing AssertionError. For forward cursors, silently clamping to 0 also changes the contract for all existing paginators and can produce next cursors derived from the original negative offset in build_cursor, risking repeated or inconsistent pages rather than rejecting a malformed cursor.

title: Unconditional dereference of organization_context.member can break previously valid requests
body: organization_context.member is nullable for some authorized principals (for example non-member/token or application-style access that is not a superuser), but this line evaluates organization_context.member.has_global_access on every GET, even when optimized_pagination is not requested. For a non-superuser request with member=None this raises AttributeError and turns a previously working audit-log request into a 500; the check should be guarded or only evaluated when the optimized branch is actually requested.

title: No tests cover the new paginator or optimized audit-log branch
body: The change adds OptimizedCursorPaginator, alters shared BasePaginator slicing, and adds a gated branch in OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint, but the PR contains no tests. There is no coverage showing that a datetime-ordered queryset can produce next/prev cursors, that the endpoint gate selects the intended paginator, or what happens for negative, prev, and boundary cursors; those untested cases include the datetime TypeError and negative-slice AssertionError above.

title: Comment claims negative cursor offsets are now safely supported, but no such support is implemented
body: This change only adds a comment; Cursor.__init__ still just does int(offset), exactly as before, and downstream paginators/querysets still reject or mishandle negative offsets. The comment incorrectly suggests a completed, safe behavior change in a shared cursor type and may lead future callers to rely on negative offsets that currently cause errors.

title: New sorted-set operations are incompatible with existing Redis segment keys
body: Existing span-buf:s:* keys created before this change are Redis sets, but process_spans now issues ZADD against them and the Lua script and _load_segment_data use ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZSCAN. Redis will return WRONGTYPE for those keys, so batches for traces active during deployment can fail until the keys expire after redis_ttl (3600s), and mixed old/new consumers during rollout will break each other. No key-version bump, conversion, or fallback is provided.

title: ZUNIONSTORE sums duplicate span scores instead of preserving timestamps
body: Both merge sites call ZUNIONSTORE without an AGGREGATE clause, so Redis defaults to SUM. When the same payload exists in both the destination and source sorted sets (e.g. duplicate delivery or a span stored under two keys before redirects converge), its score becomes roughly twice its end_timestamp_precise. That corrupts the ordering later used by ZPOPMIN eviction, causing duplicated spans to be retained while unrelated spans are evicted. The merge should use AGGREGATE MAX (or MIN) to preserve a real timestamp.

title: Insert-time eviction silently flushes incomplete segments as if complete
body: When a segment exceeds a hard-coded 1000 spans, ZPOPMIN discards the lowest end_timestamp_precise spans with no metric, log, or marker on the flushed segment. Those spans are permanently lost, yet flush_segments will emit the remainder as a normal segment (and the has-root flag/queue timeout may already have been set, so it flushes on the short root timeout). This replaces the previous explicit too-large-segment handling with silent partial data, ignores the configurable SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans (default 1001), and with tied scores eviction order is lexicographic by payload, so even a needed span can be dropped arbitrarily.

title: Redirect chain resolution regresses from 10000 to 1000 hops
body: The loop that follows span-buf:sr redirects was reduced from 10000 to 1000 iterations, removing the comment that explained the 10k limit. Segment trees whose parent chain needs more than 1000 redirect hops will stop at an intermediate span ID, so later spans are merged into the wrong set and the trace is flushed as multiple split segments instead of one segment. No test or justification covers chains between 1000 and 10000 hops.

title: Flush-time max_segment_spans protection was removed without an equivalent guard
body: _load_segment_data no longer checks len(payloads[key]) against self.max_segment_spans, drops the segment_span_count_exceeded metric/log, and returns arbitrarily large segments as long as they stay under the byte limit. Segments created before the Lua eviction existed, created by mixed-version workers, or built under a different configured limit will now be loaded and produced downstream regardless of the configured span cap, risking oversized Kafka messages and memory pressure during flush.

title: process_batch now crashes the whole batch if end_timestamp_precise is absent
body: Span construction changed from tolerating minimal span payloads to requiring val["end_timestamp_precise"] via direct indexing; the cast to SpanEvent is typing-only and does not validate the runtime JSON. A single older or malformed message missing that field raises KeyError, aborting process_batch for every span in the batch and causing the same batch to be retried instead of only the bad message being dropped or defaulted.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate the datetime-ordered audit log endpoint
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does math.floor/math.ceil on getattr(item, self.key), and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor integer. Its only caller, OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint, orders AuditLogEntry by -datetime, so the value is a datetime: build_cursor will raise TypeError from math.floor(datetime) on any non-empty first page, and on later pages build_queryset would compare a datetime column against a raw integer timestamp instead of the datetime conversion DateTimePaginator performs. The optimized audit-log path therefore returns 500 instead of results.

title: Negative-offset pagination crashes Django querysets despite claiming ORM support
body: When enable_advanced_features is set and a caller supplies a cursor with a negative offset (Cursor.from_string accepts negative integers), get_result slices queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start. Django querysets explicitly reject negative indexing with AssertionError ('Negative indexing is not supported'), contrary to the comment claiming the ORM handles it; stop can also become <= 0 for sufficiently negative offsets. A privileged audit-log user can thus force a 500 with a crafted cursor, and BasePaginator's similar change at the shared get_result only clamps non-prev cursors, leaving prev cursors unclamped.

title: No tests cover eviction, score merging, or the new paginator path
body: The added/updated tests only supply end_timestamp_precise for existing small-segment scenarios. Nothing inserts more than 1000 spans into one segment to verify how many and which spans survive ZPOPMIN, whether the root span is retained, or how duplicate payloads merged by ZUNIONSTORE keep their scores, and there are no tests for OptimizedCursorPaginator against a datetime-ordered queryset or for negative cursors. The riskiest new behaviors in this change are therefore unverified.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator is incompatible with datetime-ordered audit logs
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key applies math.floor/math.ceil directly to the ordering value and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor integer. The audit-log endpoint that uses this paginator orders by -datetime, so the ordering value is a datetime: build_cursor will raise TypeError when a non-empty page is returned, and any cursor round-trip compares a datetime column against a millisecond integer rather than a datetime. The optimized audit-log path therefore returns 500 or incorrect results instead of functioning as a faster DateTimePaginator.

title: Unrelated audit-log endpoint exposes an unvetted negative-offset pagination path
body: This spans-buffer change also adds a new optimized_pagination mode to the control-silo audit-log API. It is enabled for organization members with has_global_access, not only superusers, while pagination cursors and their offsets are client-controlled. Combined with OptimizedCursorPaginator's explicit negative-offset handling, this exposes an untested privileged pagination mode whose stated boundary handling is not provided by the underlying ORM; the unrelated API surface should not ship as part of the spans-buffer optimization.

title: Negative-offset slicing does not work on Django querysets
body: When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset is negative, this code slices the queryset as queryset[negative:stop]. Django querysets explicitly reject negative indexing with AssertionError; they do not automatically handle or wrap negative slices as the comment claims. A crafted or generated prev/negative cursor therefore causes a 500 instead of advanced pagination. BasePaginator's changed logic at line 182 likewise leaves negative offsets untouched for is_prev cursors.

title: Set-to-sorted-set conversion has no migration for in-flight Redis segments
body: Existing span-buf:s:* keys created before deployment are Redis sets, but process_spans now issues ZADD against them, add-buffer.lua issues ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE against them, and _load_segment_data issues ZSCAN against them. Those commands return WRONGTYPE for pre-existing segments, so batches and flushes can fail until the old keys expire, and a rollback would similarly break newly created sorted sets. The change needs a key-version bump, drain, or explicit type migration.

title: ZUNIONSTORE corrupts scores for spans present in both merged sets
body: Both ZUNIONSTORE calls omit an AGGREGATE argument, so Redis defaults to SUM. When the same payload/member exists in the destination and source sets, for example after redelivery or an earlier partial merge, its end_timestamp_precise score is doubled. That corrupts the ordering used by ZSCAN and makes duplicated spans artificially resistant to ZPOPMIN eviction; the merge should use an aggregate such as MAX that preserves a real timestamp.

title: Redirect resolution depth is silently reduced from 10000 to 1000
body: The redirect-following loop previously allowed depth 10000 and documented that deeper segment trees might not be joined correctly. Reducing it to 1000 without a corresponding product limit means traces with redirect chains deeper than 1000 are split into multiple segments, producing incomplete segments and incorrect root/segment assignment. Deep-tree tests only exercise a handful of spans and do not cover this regression.

title: Insert-time eviction silently truncates segments using a hardcoded limit
body: The script always ZPOPMIN-evicts down to 1000 spans, ignoring SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans (whose Python default is 1001 and which callers can configure), and records no metric or log for discarded spans. Legitimate large segments are now silently flushed as incomplete data rather than being handled by the previous explicit oversized-segment path. Because eviction removes the lowest end_timestamp_precise scores and the separate has-root flag is not recomputed, an evicted segment/root span can also leave the has-root state inconsistent with the remaining payloads, while evicted span IDs remain in the redirect hash until expiry.

title: Flush-time max_segment_spans protection is removed and the setting becomes dead
body: _load_segment_data no longer enforces self.max_segment_spans or emits the segment_span_count_exceeded metric/log; after this change the constructor setting has no remaining effect in the flush path. Any segment that bypasses the Lua cap, including data produced by another writer or a future merge change, can now be loaded and emitted without the previous span-count bound, risking oversized Kafka messages and memory pressure. If insert-time eviction is intended to replace this check, the obsolete setting and its contract should be removed consistently rather than left silently ignored.

title: No test covers the new eviction or sorted-set merge behavior
body: The updated buffer tests only add the required end_timestamp_precise field to existing small cases; every scenario uses at most five spans. There is no test that inserts more than the eviction limit, verifies which spans are retained, checks behavior when the segment/root span would be evicted, exercises duplicate payloads across merged sorted sets, or verifies redirect chains near the reduced depth limit. The central behavioral change of the PR is therefore untested.

title: Unrelated audit-log change enables unvetted advanced pagination for non-superusers
body: This spans-buffer PR also switches the audit-log endpoint to OptimizedCursorPaginator when optimized_pagination=true is supplied and the caller is a superuser OR merely has organization_context.member.has_global_access. has_global_access is team-access scope for ordinary organization members, not proof of administrator/superuser status as the comment claims. This exposes a separate, user-controlled pagination implementation on a sensitive endpoint, unrelated to span buffering, and should be removed or reviewed/tested as its own API change.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator is incompatible with the datetime ordering of its only caller
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does math.floor/math.ceil directly on getattr(item, self.key), and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor integer. Its only caller orders AuditLogEntry by -datetime, for which DateTimePaginator is required: it converts epoch-millis cursor values to timezone-aware datetimes and formats item keys with strftime. With -datetime, build_queryset receives an integer instead of a datetime and build_cursor calls math.floor on a datetime, so the optimized audit-log path will raise TypeError/database comparison errors instead of returning a page.

title: Negative cursor offsets are passed to Django queryset slicing, which does not support them
body: Cursor values and offsets come from the request query string and Cursor.from_string accepts negative offsets. The optimized branch deliberately uses cursor.offset as the slice start when enable_advanced_features is set, and BasePaginator at line 182 likewise preserves negative offsets for is_prev cursors. The claim that Django ORM handles this is false: Django QuerySet slicing asserts 'Negative indexing is not supported', so a crafted cursor such as a negative-offset prev/next cursor produces a 500 rather than safely paging from the end. Pagination bounds need explicit validation/clamping before slicing.

title: ZUNIONSTORE defaults to SUM and corrupts span end-timestamp scores on overlaps
body: The old SUNIONSTORE deduplicated identical payloads without changing metadata. The new redis.call('zunionstore', set_key, 2, set_key, span_key) uses Redis' default AGGREGATE SUM, so a payload present in both sorted sets (duplicate delivery, a merge of overlapping partial segments, or destination/source overlap) gets score roughly end_timestamp+end_timestamp instead of its end timestamp. That corrupts the score later used by zpopmin eviction, artificially protecting duplicated spans and causing other spans to be evicted first. Use an explicit AGGREGATE MAX (or MIN) to preserve one real timestamp.

title: SET-to-ZSET switch breaks in-flight Redis segments with WRONGTYPE errors
body: Existing buffered segment keys were created as Redis SETs by sadd and can remain live until the one-hour redis_ttl/flush timeouts expire. This change immediately issues ZADD in process_spans, and the Lua script likewise issues ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZPOPMIN, while flush uses ZSCAN. Redis returns WRONGTYPE when a sorted-set command is used on an existing SET key, so during rollout process_spans fails for traces already buffered, batches retry/stall, and unflushed spans can be lost when the old keys expire. The PR contains no key versioning, drain, dual-type handling, or other migration for in-flight keys.

title: Flush-time max_segment_spans guard removed while insert cap ignores the configured limit
body: _load_segment_data no longer enforces SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans; after this change that constructor setting is effectively dead. Eviction is instead hardcoded to 1000 in add-buffer.lua, so the default changes from 1001 to 1000 and any custom max_segment_spans value is silently ignored. Segments that bypass insert eviction, including pre-existing large segments, are now loaded and emitted regardless of span count, bounded only by max_segment_bytes, increasing memory and downstream segment-size risk.

title: Redirect resolution depth silently reduced from 10000 to 1000
body: The redirect-following loop previously allowed 10000 hops, with a comment acknowledging that deeper segment trees might not be joined correctly. Reducing it to 1000 makes that failure mode ten times more likely: when the cap is exhausted the script proceeds with an unresolved set_span_id and no error, so spans for a deep chain can be placed in a different segment key and flushed as split/incomplete segments rather than being joined to their root segment.

title: Insert-time eviction silently drops spans with no metric or truncation signal
body: When a segment exceeds 1000 spans, zpopmin permanently discards the earliest-ending spans during insert. Unlike the removed flush-time span-count guard, which emitted spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded and logged the segment size, this path emits no metric/log and marks the flushed segment in no way as truncated. Operators cannot measure span loss and downstream consumers receive an incomplete segment indistinguishable from a complete one.

title: No test covers the new eviction, sorted-set merge, or score behavior
body: The test changes only add the newly required end_timestamp_precise field to existing Span constructions. No test inserts more than 1000 spans into one segment, asserts which spans zpopmin retains, covers duplicate payloads across merged partial segments, or verifies that scores remain real end timestamps after ZUNIONSTORE. The central data-loss behavior introduced by this PR is therefore untested.

title: Upsampling cache can return stale or colliding eligibility results
body: Eligibility is cached for 60 seconds under a key containing only organization ID and hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))). The defined invalidate_upsampling_cache helper is never called when the project allowlist option changes, so projects removed from the allowlist can continue to be overcounted and newly added projects can continue to be undercounted until expiry; a hash collision between different project sets would also reuse the wrong eligibility. The TTL can additionally expire between the multiple _get_event_stats calls made by the dashboard-split flow, producing inconsistent transformations within one request.

title: Upsampling decision uses the outer dataset instead of the dataset actually queried
body: _get_event_stats receives scoped_dataset and executes the query against it, but is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects is called with the closure variable dataset. The dashboard-split factory calls _get_event_stats with discover or another split_dataset that can differ from the original dataset, so an errors split query can be denied upsampling because the outer dataset was metrics/transactions-like, or upsampling can be considered based on a dataset different from the one that will run the query.

title: Substring event.type check misclassifies discover queries in both directions
body: _is_error_focused_query only searches request.GET['query'] for the substring 'event.type:error'. A negated query such as '!event.type:error' therefore returns True and applies sum(sample_weight) to non-error events, while valid error-focused forms such as '!event.type:transaction', 'event.type:[error,default]', or the errors-only split query constructed by the endpoint ('(<query>) AND !event.type:transaction') return False because the helper also ignores the actual query argument passed to _get_event_stats. This causes overcounting for excluded-error queries and missed upsampling for legitimate error queries.

title: upsampled_count has no fallback for events without sample_weight
body: The aggregate is toInt64(sum(sample_weight)), replacing a row count that counted every event. Any stored error row whose sample_weight is null or 0 (for example events ingested before client sampling was enabled/configured for an allowlisted project, or events without a client_sample_rate) contributes 0 instead of 1, so historical or unsampled buckets in the retention window can drop to zero or be undercounted after the transformation. The added tests only cover events explicitly given client_sample_rate through the new factory helper.

title: upsampled_count is exposed as a public Discover function
body: The new SnQLFunction does not set private=True, unlike internal-only aggregates, so it becomes user-callable through the Discover query builder. A caller can submit upsampled_count() directly as a yAxis/field for projects and datasets that never passed the organization-events-stats allowlist and dataset checks, bypassing the gating in error_upsampling.py and receiving raw sum(sample_weight) results (including misleading zero values for transaction data).

title: Accidental git submodule added to the repository root
body: This new file adds 'Subproject commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a' as a submodule named sentry-repo at the repository root. It is unrelated to the upsampling feature and will change checkout/CI behavior for every developer by introducing a nested Sentry checkout; it should be removed before merging.

title: Upsampling eligibility uses the outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset
body: _get_event_stats executes against its scoped_dataset argument, but is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects is called with the closure variable dataset. The dashboard-split factory calls _get_event_stats with discover or another split_dataset while dataset may be metrics_performance/metrics_enhanced_performance, so error split queries are incorrectly judged ineligible and never upsampled; conversely a transaction-like scoped query can inherit eligibility from the outer dataset. Pass scoped_dataset to the eligibility check.

title: upsampled_count drops events whose sample_weight is NULL instead of counting them once
body: The aggregate is sum(sample_weight) with no coalesce/ifNull fallback. Allowlisted projects will contain events without client error sampling (historical events, unsampled/default events, events from SDKs that do not set the context), and any row with NULL sample_weight contributes 0 rather than 1, so enabling upsampling can collapse those buckets to undercounted or zero counts. The new tests only store events with client_sample_rate=0.1 and never cover this case. Use a fallback such as sum(ifNull(sample_weight, 1)).

title: Error-focus detection ignores the actual query being executed
body: _is_error_focused_query re-reads request.GET['query'] and only matches the exact substring 'event.type:error'. _get_event_stats receives an explicit query argument that callers modify, e.g. the dashboard-split path builds '({query}) AND !event.type:transaction' and other derived queries, but the helper cannot see those strings, so eligibility is decided from a different query than the one sent to Snuba. It also misses equivalent formatting/casing variations of the executed query. Thread the query argument through is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects/_should_apply_sample_weight_transform instead of reading the request.

title: Internal upsampled_count function is exposed for direct user queries
body: The new SnQLFunction 'upsampled_count' does not set private=True, unlike internal-only functions around it. Because the function converter also resolves user-supplied yAxis values, any caller can request yAxis=upsampled_count() directly for any project or event type, bypassing the allowlist and error-only gating in error_upsampling.py and obtaining weighted counts (or meaningless zeroes where sample_weight is absent). Mark it private so only the server-side column transformation can introduce it.

title: Accidental nested-repository gitlink added to the repository root
body: This adds 'sentry-repo' as a subproject/gitlink pointing at the base commit, with no .gitmodules entry or purpose described in the PR. It is unrelated to upsampling and will pollute the tree, confuse submodule/checkout tooling, and should be removed before merge.

title: Cache invalidation helper is dead code, so allowlist changes have no invalidation path
body: invalidate_upsampling_cache is introduced with a docstring saying it should be called when the allowlist configuration changes, but nothing in the PR (or the option-setting machinery) calls it. Eligibility is cached for 60 seconds under a key derived only from organization and project ids, so removing a project from the allowlist keeps returning upsampled counts, and adding one keeps returning raw counts, until TTL expiry, with no way to force consistency. Either wire invalidation into the allowlist change path or remove the helper and document that TTL expiry is the only mechanism.

title: Integration tests miss the errors dataset, topEvents, and unsampled-event cases
body: The new Snuba tests only exercise the default/discover timeseries path with fully sampled events. They do not cover dataset=errors (a branch _should_apply_sample_weight_transform explicitly enables), the separate topEvents transformation branch in _get_event_stats, or an allowlisted project containing events without error_sampling context. Those are exactly the paths where an unregistered function, a missed column transformation, or NULL sample_weight handling would silently fail or return wrong counts, so add cases for them.

title: Upsampling decision uses the outer dataset instead of the dataset actually being queried
body: _get_event_stats receives scoped_dataset, which is the dataset that will execute the query, but the eligibility check passes the closure variable dataset from the request. The dashboard-split factory calls _get_event_stats with different datasets, including discover for error splits and the scoped dataset for transaction-like splits. Consequently, an error split can incorrectly miss upsampling, while a metrics or transaction-like query can receive upsampled_count() even though that builder or table does not support sample_weight. The decision should be based on scoped_dataset and the query actually being executed.

title: Error-focus detection ignores the actual query and uses a naive substring check
body: The transform decision reads only request.GET['query'] and checks whether it contains 'event.type:error'. _get_event_stats is not given the opportunity to pass its query argument, which may be an internally constructed dashboard query such as '(...) AND !event.type:transaction' or a widget query that differs from the request parameter. The substring check also misses forms such as '!event.type:transaction' and 'event.type:[error, default]', while incorrectly matching the negated query '!event.type:error'. Error charts can therefore remain unupsampled, or non-error queries can have count() replaced by a sum of sample_weight.

title: upsampled_count has no fallback for missing sample weights and truncates fractional weights
body: The aggregate is toInt64(sum(sample_weight)). Events in an allowlisted project that were ingested before error sampling was enabled, or that otherwise have a null or zero sample_weight, contribute nothing instead of counting as one event, so historical and unsampled errors disappear from upsampled series. Additionally, toInt64 truncates fractional sums produced by float sample weights, systematically undercounting estimated errors. Missing weights should default to 1 and the fractional estimate should be rounded or retained rather than truncated.

title: Internal upsampled_count function is exposed as a public Discover function
body: The new SnQLFunction does not set private=True, unlike neighboring internal-only aggregation helpers. It therefore expands the public Discover function surface and can be requested directly through query builders using DiscoverDatasetConfig, bypassing the stats endpoint's project-allowlist and dataset checks. On non-allowlisted projects or datasets backed by tables without meaningful error sample weights, this can return misleading counts or produce invalid Snuba queries. The function should remain internal to the gated transformation.

title: Cached allowlist eligibility can remain stale and the invalidation helper is never used
body: Eligibility is cached for 60 seconds, but invalidate_upsampling_cache has no caller in this change and there is no hook from option changes to that helper. After a project is removed from issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist, the endpoint can continue replacing count() with upsampled counts; after a project is added, it can continue returning raw counts until the entry expires. Either wire invalidation to allowlist changes or remove the unused invalidation API and explicitly accept only TTL-based expiry.

title: Stray subproject file is unrelated to the feature
body: This change adds a root-level 'sentry-repo' file containing only 'Subproject commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a'. That resembles an accidentally recorded nested-repository gitlink without any corresponding submodule configuration and is unrelated to error upsampling. It can confuse checkout and submodule tooling and should be removed before merging.

title: Tests do not exercise the public eligibility entry point used by the endpoint
body: The unit tests import and test only the private helpers _are_all_projects_error_upsampled, _is_error_focused_query, _should_apply_sample_weight_transform, and the column transform. They do not test is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects, the only function called by organization_events_stats, including its caching behavior, dataset handling, or interaction with a scoped/split dataset. The Snuba tests also cover only events that already carry client_sample_rate=0.1, leaving unsampled events and the resulting sample_weight behavior unverified, so regressions in the actual production path can pass the added tests.

title: Table widget feature flag renders an empty table instead of the query results
body: When the organization has the use-table-widget-visualization feature, tableResultComponent renders TableWidgetVisualization with columns={[]} and a hard-coded tableData containing data: [] and empty meta fields/units. It discards result.data, result.meta, fields, field aliases, custom renderers, loading state, and titles from the actual widget query. Enabling the flag therefore makes every dashboard table widget appear empty rather than showing its queried data.

title: Error events and replay segment events are compared using different timestamp units
body: fetch_error_details stores ErrorEvent.timestamp from the nodestore event timestamp, which is seconds since the epoch, while replay recording segment events use rrweb millisecond epoch timestamps. gen_request_data sorts and interleaves them with a direct '<' comparison at line 154, so an error timestamp around 1.7e9 is always considered earlier than segment timestamps around 1.7e12. All errors are consequently emitted before the first breadcrumb instead of in chronological order, and the log text also mixes second-based error times with millisecond-based breadcrumb times for Seer. Normalize one side (for example multiply the error timestamp by 1000) before sorting, merging, and formatting.

title: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES are only hidden while a search query is active
body: sortedAndFilteredAttributes returns the full sorted attribute list unchanged when searchQuery is empty; the HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES exclusion for is_segment, project_id, and received is only applied inside the search-filter branch. As a result these internal attributes are still shown in the default span Attributes view and only disappear after the user starts typing a search, which defeats the purpose of the hidden list. Apply the hidden-attribute filter before/independently of the text search filter.

title: Browser reports with neither age nor timestamp pass validation
body: BrowserReportSerializer marks both age and timestamp required=False and only adds field-level validators that reject the fields when both are present. A report containing neither field therefore passes validation even though the Working Draft format requires age and the Editor's Draft format requires timestamp. The endpoint accepts and counts spec-invalid reports. Add object-level validation requiring exactly one of age or timestamp (also note the current get() checks treat a present value of 0 as absent).

title: Truncated issue titles exceed ISSUE_TITLE_MAX_LENGTH
body: _truncate_title is governed by ISSUE_TITLE_MAX_LENGTH = 50, but for an over-long title it returns title[:50].rstrip() + '...', producing up to 53 characters. The rendered PR/MR comment therefore violates the stated 50-character title limit. Truncate to max_length - len('...') before appending the ellipsis if the constant is meant to bound the final title length.

title: Table widget feature flag renders a hardcoded empty table
body: When the organization has the use-table-widget-visualization feature, tableResultComponent ignores the actual tableResults entry and renders TableWidgetVisualization with columns=[] and tableData containing empty data and empty meta. Every dashboard table for such an organization will therefore appear blank regardless of the query results, loading state, fields, or title. The real result data must be converted and passed to the new visualization instead of the hardcoded empty placeholder.

title: Error and breadcrumb timestamps are compared in different units
body: fetch_error_details stores the error event timestamp as a Unix timestamp in seconds, while recording-segment events from rrweb carry timestamps in milliseconds. gen_request_data directly compares error_events[error_idx]['timestamp'] with event['timestamp'], so virtually every error will compare as earlier than the first breadcrumb and all errors will be emitted at the start instead of in chronological order. Normalize both timestamps to the same unit before sorting and interleaving.

title: Browser report validation does not require exactly one of age or timestamp
body: The serializer makes both age and timestamp optional and only rejects them when the other field is truthy via self.initial_data.get(...). A report with neither field is accepted even though it conforms to neither supported Reporting API format, and a report with age=0 or timestamp=0 together with the other field also passes because 0 is falsy. This allows malformed reports to be counted as valid. Enforce presence of exactly one field using key presence rather than truthiness.

title: Hidden span attributes are only hidden while searching
body: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES is checked only inside the filter that runs when searchQuery is non-empty. When the search box is empty, sortedAndFilteredAttributes returns the sorted attributes unchanged, so is_segment, project_id, and received are still displayed by default and disappear only after the user starts typing a search. Apply the hidden-attribute exclusion before or independently of the search-text filter.

title: Assemble analytics are recorded before the feature-flag check
body: The endpoint records the preprod_artifact.api.assemble analytics event before checking organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble and before validating the request body. Requests from organizations without the feature, which return 404, and malformed requests, which return 400, are therefore counted as artifact assembly events and pollute downstream analytics. Move analytics.record after the feature and validation checks, ideally only for requests that actually proceed toward assembly.

title: Issue titles are inserted unescaped into a Markdown link
body: MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE interpolates the issue title directly into link text as [**{title}**]({url}). Issue titles are derived from error data and can contain closing brackets or Markdown link syntax, so a title containing a sequence such as ](https://example.invalid) can break out of the intended link, corrupt the PR comment formatting, or substitute a misleading destination. Escape or strip Markdown link delimiters from the truncated title before formatting the template.

title: PR-comment helpers are defined on the integration class but invoked on the workflow class
body: The new _truncate_title, get_environment_info, and get_merged_pr_single_issue_template helpers are added to CommitContextIntegration, but GitHubPRCommentWorkflow and GitlabPRCommentWorkflow call self.get_environment_info() and self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(); those workflows inherit from PRCommentWorkflow/OpenPRCommentWorkflow, not CommitContextIntegration. The helper also calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title even though _truncate_title was defined on CommitContextIntegration. Generating the first suspect-issue comment will therefore raise AttributeError and fail the PR/MR comment workflow instead of posting the comment. The helpers should live on PRCommentWorkflow (or be called via self.integration) and the truncation call should reference the class that actually defines it.

title: Table-widget feature-flag path discards the real table data
body: When the organization has the use-table-widget-visualization feature, tableResultComponent renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded columns=[] and a hardcoded empty tableData ({data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}) instead of converting the current result (result.data, result.meta, fields/eventView, aliases, custom renderers). Every table widget for a flagged organization will render an empty table regardless of the query results. The flagged branch must pass the actual table result data/meta and column definitions, or not be wired into the production chart path yet.

title: Error timestamps and replay-segment timestamps are compared in different units
body: fetch_error_details stores the error event timestamp from nodestore, which is epoch seconds, while replay recording-segment (rrweb) events carry epoch milliseconds. gen_request_data then directly compares error_events[i]['timestamp'] < event.get('timestamp'), so with real data an error timestamp in seconds will almost always be smaller than a segment timestamp in milliseconds and all errors will be emitted before the first breadcrumb (or in the wrong position), destroying the chronological context sent to Seer. Normalize both sides to the same unit (for example multiply the error timestamp by 1000) before sorting/comparing; the added tests mask this by using seconds for the segment timestamps as well.

title: Browser reports with neither age nor timestamp (or with age=0 plus timestamp) pass validation
body: age and timestamp are both declared required=False and there is no object-level validation requiring exactly one of them, so a report missing both fields is accepted and counted. The field validators also test self.initial_data.get('age')/get('timestamp') for truthiness, so a payload with age=0 and a timestamp present bypasses the mutual-exclusion check even though 0 is a legitimate age value. Add a validate() method that requires exactly one of age/timestamp using presence ('in' / is not None) rather than truthiness.

title: Hidden span attributes are only hidden while a search query is active
body: sortedAndFilteredAttributes returns the full sorted attribute list unchanged when the search box is empty, and only applies the HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES exclusion (is_segment, project_id, received) inside the branch that runs when a search query is present. As a result these internal attributes are shown in the default attributes view and then mysteriously disappear as soon as the user starts typing. Apply the hidden-attribute filter unconditionally before/regardless of the search-term filter.

title: Unsuccessful summary generation with feedback present renders an empty summary panel
body: tooFewFeedbacks is only set when numFeedbacksUsed === 0 and success is false. If the summary endpoint returns success=false with summary=null after having used one or more feedbacks (for example an LLM failure), FeedbackSummary does not hide itself (it only hides on tooFewFeedbacks or isError, and this is a successful HTTP response) and renders the 'Feedback Summary' header with an empty body. The hook/component should treat a missing summary or success=false as a hide condition, not only the zero-feedback case.

title: Sender validation is bypassed when no Integration row exists yet
body: In GitHubInstallation.dispatch, the Integration.DoesNotExist branch immediately returns pipeline.next_step() without comparing the pipeline's github_authenticated_user to the user who installed the GitHub app. Creation of the Integration row by the GitHub webhook is asynchronous and can race or be missed, so an attacker who knows or guesses a victim's incremental GitHub installation_id and starts the linking flow before that row exists can finish the pipeline; build_integration then creates/links the integration based only on installation_id. This defeats the new mismatch protection and can attach a victim's GitHub installation to the attacker's Sentry organization.

title: Sender check crashes when Integration metadata has no sender
body: The check dereferences integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] unconditionally. Integrations created through the pipeline itself only receive metadata.sender when state contains sender (build_integration), and no pipeline view binds sender into state, so pipeline-created or older orphaned ACTIVE integrations can lack metadata.sender. When such an integration exists without an OrganizationIntegration, dispatch raises KeyError/TypeError and returns a 500 instead of a graceful installation error or a successful relink.

title: GitHub token exchange failures can raise instead of showing the installation error
body: OAuthLoginView calls safe_urlopen for the OAuth access-token exchange outside the try block that only covers safe_urlread/parse_qsl, and then calls get_user_info without exception handling. If GitHub's token or user endpoints return an HTTP error, time out, or otherwise fail at the safe_urlopen layer, the exception propagates as an unhandled 500 rather than rendering the github-integration-failed page that the PR intends for bad or reused authorization codes. Both external calls need to be covered and mapped to the error response.

title: Integration lookups do not filter by provider
body: The lookups in GitHubInstallation use Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id) even though Integration identity is unique only by (provider, external_id), not by external_id alone. If another integration provider has a record with the same external_id as a GitHub installation_id, get() raises MultipleObjectsReturned, which is not caught because only DoesNotExist is handled, causing a 500; it could also select the wrong integration's metadata for the sender comparison. The queries should filter provider to the GitHub provider key.

title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the installation-not-found path
body: The test stubs GET /app/installations/{id} to return 404, but its callback request supplies state ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05, which does not match the pipeline signature. OAuthLoginView therefore returns the generic invalid-installation page before GitHubInstallation/build_integration can call get_installation_info, so the test would pass even if the 404 handling in build_integration were broken or removed. The callback should use the valid pipeline state and assert the installation-not-found outcome.

title: Sender validation is bypassed when the Integration row does not exist yet
body: GitHubInstallation only compares github_authenticated_user with the installer when an Integration row already exists. If Integration.objects.get raises DoesNotExist it immediately calls pipeline.next_step(), which proceeds to create and link the integration. The Integration row is normally created by GitHub's asynchronous installation webhook, and GitHub provides no ordering guarantee between that webhook and the browser redirect/OAuth pipeline. A user whose GitHub login differs from the installer can therefore claim the installation if they reach this step before the webhook is processed, or if the webhook is delayed or missed, defeating the validation added by this PR.

title: Missing sender metadata causes a KeyError instead of the installation error page
body: The new check directly indexes integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]. Integrations created before sender metadata was recorded, or created through paths where no sender was stored, do not have this key. If such an ACTIVE integration remains after its OrganizationIntegration is removed and someone attempts to install it again, this line raises KeyError/TypeError and returns a 500 instead of either proceeding safely or showing the intended invalid-installation page. The metadata should be read defensively and a missing sender handled explicitly.

title: GitHub token-exchange and user-info failures are not converted to the installation error page
body: safe_urlopen at line 423 is called outside the try block, and get_user_info at line 434 is also unguarded. Network failures, GitHub HTTP errors, or an invalid/unusable access token can therefore raise out of OAuthLoginView.dispatch and produce a 500. This contradicts the PR's stated behavior that failures to obtain a valid access token or verify the GitHub user should show the invalid-installation error page.

title: Installation now depends on separate GitHub login OAuth credentials
body: OAuthLoginView uses GitHubIdentityProvider.get_oauth_client_id/get_oauth_client_secret, which are the github-login.* credentials for GitHub SSO, not the github-app.client-id/github-app.client-secret credentials used to configure the GitHub App integration. Deployments that configured only the GitHub App, as previously sufficient for installing this integration, will now redirect to GitHub with an empty or invalid client_id and cannot complete installation at all. The flow should use the GitHub App's OAuth credentials or otherwise not make GitHub login configuration a new prerequisite.

title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the installation-not-found path
body: The test replaces the GitHub installation endpoint with a 404, but its second setup request supplies a state value that does not match the pipeline signature, so OAuthLoginView returns the generic invalid-installation page before build_integration can call the installation endpoint. The 404 stub is therefore never meaningfully exercised and the assertion would pass even if the installation-not-found handling regressed; the test needs a valid OAuth state/code exchange before asserting the 404 behavior.

title: Sender validation is bypassed when the Integration row does not exist yet
body: In GitHubInstallation.dispatch, the Integration.DoesNotExist branch immediately returns pipeline.next_step(), while the github_authenticated_user versus integration.metadata["sender"] comparison at lines 500-505 only runs when an Integration already exists without an OrganizationIntegration. A newly installed GitHub App therefore completes without any sender check if the installation webhook has not yet created the Integration row (a normal race, since GitHub sends the webhook and the user redirect independently) or if the webhook was missed/delayed. An attacker who installed the app can have a different Sentry user claim that installation_id during that window, defeating the validation this PR is intended to add; the check needs to fail closed or obtain the installer identity from a source available at build_integration/finish time rather than relying solely on a pre-existing row.

title: Sender check raises KeyError for integrations created without sender metadata
body: The check unconditionally indexes integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]. Integrations created through the normal pipeline only get metadata["sender"] when state happens to contain a sender (the updated test's basic flow asserts metadata with no sender key), and integrations created before sender tracking existed likewise lack it. When such an Integration exists but its OrganizationIntegration has been removed, this line raises KeyError and returns a 500 instead of either proceeding or showing the integration-failed page, breaking reinstallation/moving of those integrations. The lookup should use a safe .get() chain and define the behavior when sender is absent.

title: Token-exchange network errors escape the graceful error handling
body: OAuthLoginView calls safe_urlopen() before the try block; only safe_urlread()/decoding/parsing is wrapped. If GitHub's access-token endpoint is unreachable, resets the connection, or safe_urlopen rejects/errors on the request, the exception propagates as an unhandled 500 instead of rendering the github-integration-failed page that the PR promises for a failed code exchange. The safe_urlopen call (and the unguarded get_user_info call that follows) should be covered by the same failure path that handles a missing access_token.

title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the installation-not-found path
body: The rewritten test supplies state=ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05, which does not match the pipeline signature, so OAuthLoginView returns the generic invalid-request page before build_integration/get_installation_info is ever reached. The test therefore passes even if the GitHub 404 handling ('The GitHub installation could not be found.') is broken or removed, and it silently drops the previous coverage/assertion for that message. The test should drive the flow with the correct pipeline state and an installation_id step so the mocked 404 from /app/installations/{id} is what produces the failure.

title: New assignment_source kwarg breaks existing sync_assignee_outbound implementations
body: The task now unconditionally calls installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source), including when the value is None. Existing IssueSyncIntegration implementations such as the Jira, GitHub, GitLab, and Azure DevOps integrations define sync_assignee_outbound(self, external_issue, user, assign=True) without **kwargs or an assignment_source parameter, so every outbound assignee task for those providers will raise TypeError instead of syncing and will be retried until exhaustion. The added tests mask this because ExampleIntegration.sync_assignee_outbound is replaced with a MagicMock that accepts any arguments. Either update all implementations to accept the new parameter or avoid passing it to implementations that do not support it.

title: AssignmentSource.queued timestamp is evaluated once at import time
body: The dataclass field is declared as queued: datetime = timezone.now(), which executes timezone.now() once when the class is defined rather than when each AssignmentSource is created. Every source created by a long-lived process therefore carries the same increasingly stale import-time timestamp instead of its actual queueing time, making the field incorrect for logging, debugging, or any future staleness/expiry check. Use field(default_factory=timezone.now) instead.

title: AssignmentSource queued datetime is not round-trip safe through the outbound task payload
body: assignment_source.to_dict() returns the queued value as a datetime object, and that dict is placed directly into sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async kwargs. After task transport/JSON serialization the value arrives as a string, but AssignmentSource.from_dict does not parse it back, so the reconstructed object violates its declared queued: datetime type and round-tripping to_dict()/from_dict() is not type-preserving. Serialize queued as an ISO-formatted string and parse it in from_dict, or remove queued from the serialized payload.

title: No test proves non-matching integrations still sync or that inbound deassign is suppressed
body: The only new matching-source test covers assign through GroupAssignee.objects.assign directly. There is no test with an AssignmentSource whose integration_id differs from the target integration, so a regression in which should_sync returns False for any non-None source would still pass even though the PR intends other integrations to keep receiving outbound updates. There is also no mocked/eager-task assertion for the inbound deassign path in sync_group_assignee_inbound, so forgetting to propagate assignment_source there would not be caught. Add non-matching-source assign/deassign cases asserting sync_assignee_outbound is still called, and a matching-source deassign/inbound-deassign case asserting it is not.

title: queued timestamp is evaluated once at import time
body: The dataclass declares `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`, which Python evaluates once when the class is defined rather than for each AssignmentSource instance. Every source created by from_integration(), and every source reconstructed by from_dict() without an explicit queued value, therefore carries the stale module-import timestamp instead of the time that assignment was queued. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` if this timestamp is meant to describe an individual assignment.

title: AssignmentSource dictionary does not round-trip queued through the Celery boundary
body: to_dict() returns the queued value as a datetime object, and sync_group_assignee_outbound passes that dictionary as a Celery task argument in sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py. After JSON task serialization the value arrives as a string, while from_dict() constructs AssignmentSource without parsing it back, producing an object whose queued field violates its declared datetime type. Serialize queued as an ISO string and parse it in from_dict(), or remove the unused field before relying on this round-trip.

title: Task passes assignment_source to a method whose abstract contract does not declare it
body: This task now unconditionally calls sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source), even when the value is None, but IssueSyncIntegration.sync_assignee_outbound in sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py does not declare an assignment_source parameter and relies only on implementations accepting **kwargs. The PR instead adds the explicit parameter to the unrelated abstract sync_status_outbound, which this task does not call. An issue-sync implementation with an explicit sync_assignee_outbound(self, external_issue, user, assign=True) signature will raise TypeError on every outbound assignee sync and trigger task retries. Add assignment_source to the sync_assignee_outbound contract and remove or justify the unused change to sync_status_outbound.

title: No test proves non-matching integrations still sync or that deassignment cycles are suppressed
body: The only new outbound test covers assignment when the source integration exactly matches the linked integration. It does not test the stated intended behavior that an assignment originating from one integration still propagates to a different linked integration, nor does it test inbound deassignment with a matching source through GroupAssignee.deassign(). A regression that blocks every non-None AssignmentSource, or that only works for assign=True, would pass the added tests while breaking cross-integration propagation or leaving the deassignment cycle intact.

title: queued timestamp is evaluated once at import time
body: The dataclass field is declared as `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`, so timezone.now() runs once when the class is defined rather than for each AssignmentSource. Every instance created without an explicit queued value therefore shares the process import time, making queued incorrect as a record of when an assignment was queued. Use field(default_factory=timezone.now) instead.

title: to_dict produces a non-JSON-serializable Celery argument and breaks round-trip typing
body: to_dict() uses asdict(), leaving queued as a datetime object. sync_group_assignee_outbound puts this dict directly into sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async kwargs, which must cross Sentry's task serialization boundary; a datetime is not a plain JSON value, and if encoded as an ISO string, from_dict will construct an AssignmentSource whose queued field is a string rather than a datetime. Serialize queued explicitly (for example as an ISO timestamp) and parse it back in from_dict so the round trip is safe and type-consistent.

title: Outbound suppression is only tested for assignment, not deassignment or other integrations
body: The new matching-source test covers only GroupAssignee.assign. The deassign suppression uses separate branches in GroupAssignee.deassign and in sync_group_assignee_inbound's assign=False path, so a regression there would still echo unassignments back to the originating integration and would not be caught. There is also no test that an assignment sourced from one integration still syncs to a different linked integration, so over-suppression would not be caught either.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now inherits StatefulDetectorHandler but implements none of its abstract members: counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the newly added build_occurrence_and_event_data. Python will raise TypeError when Detector.detector_handler tries to instantiate this class for a metric_alert_fire detector, and process_detectors does not handle that exception, so processing can abort instead of being skipped. Previously this handler was a concrete no-op whose evaluate() returned []. The subclass needs stub implementations of the abstract methods, or it should remain a DetectorHandler until the stateful implementation is available.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler can no longer be instantiated
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now inherits from StatefulDetectorHandler but implements none of its abstract members (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the newly added build_occurrence_and_event_data). Instantiating it via Detector.detector_handler will therefore raise TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class, instead of behaving like the previous implementation whose evaluate() returned []. process_detectors only handles a missing handler, not this exception, so any detector of type metric_alert_fire will crash processing rather than being skipped or producing no results.

title: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate docstring still documents a list return
body: The evaluate() signature and implementation were changed to return dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult], but the docstring still says it 'returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult'. Implementers and callers following the documentation will use the wrong contract (e.g. list append/iteration semantics) for the new dict-keyed API.

title: Mock occurrence builder ignores the value passed to the new hook
body: build_mock_occurrence_and_event accepts a value argument but never uses it when constructing the IssueOccurrence or event_data, and MockDetectorStateHandler.build_occurrence_and_event_data forwards the evaluated value only into this helper. The tests themselves pass mismatched values (for example group_2 has packet value 10 but the expected occurrence is built with 6, and several evaluate tests expect occurrences built with 6 for values 8/100). Consequently a regression that passes the wrong value to build_occurrence_and_event_data would not be caught by these tests, even though real handlers will typically use that value in titles/evidence/event data.

title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler with just `pass`, but StatefulDetectorHandler declares abstract members counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the new build_occurrence_and_event_data. This class implements none of them, so `Detector.detector_handler` calling `group_type.detector_handler(self)` for a metric_alert_fire detector raises TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class, and process_detectors crashes instead of the previous no-op behaviour where evaluate() returned []. Implement stub versions of the abstract methods, provide defaults in StatefulDetectorHandler, or keep this placeholder on DetectorHandler until it is implemented.

title: TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds the expected occurrence for the wrong group key
body: The expected occurrence is built with build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", 6, ...), so its fingerprint is [<detector_id>:val1], but evaluate_group_key_value is then called with group_key "group_key" and value 10, so the handler builds an occurrence with fingerprint [<detector_id>:group_key]. IssueOccurrence equality includes the fingerprint, so the expected DetectorEvaluationResult cannot equal the actual result and this test fails / does not verify the intended dedupe path. Build the expected occurrence with "group_key" (and the value actually passed, 10).

title: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
body: The docstring says evaluate "returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult", but this PR changes the signature and implementation to return dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]. Implementers relying on the docstring will implement or consume the wrong return type; update the docstring to describe the dict keyed by group_key.

title: Non-positive flusher process count can silently disable flushing
body: The new --flusher-processes option accepts any integer. A value of 0 is silently treated as unspecified because of `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, while a negative value makes num_processes negative and produces an empty process_to_shards_map. With no workers, submit() has no buffers or backpressure state to check but still forwards messages to the committer, so spans can be committed and accumulate in Redis without ever being flushed. Fail fast on flusher_processes < 1 (and on an empty assigned-shard set) instead of starting a consumer with no flusher.

title: join() can leave most flusher processes running after the timeout expires
body: join() computes the deadline before calling self.next_step.join(timeout), which may consume the entire timeout, and then breaks out of the process loop when no time remains. terminate() is only reached for processes the loop has already visited, so remaining spawn processes are neither terminated nor joined. Because strategies are closed/joined and recreated in the same parent process during rebalancing, leftover daemon flushers can keep polling their shards alongside the replacement SpanFlusher and race it to produce segments. All processes should be signalled to stop/terminate before waiting on each of them subject to the deadline.

title: Unhealthy flusher is replaced before the old worker has actually stopped
body: _ensure_processes_alive() only signals a spawn process with kill() and never waits for it to exit; for threading.Thread workers the isinstance check skips termination entirely. It then immediately starts a replacement and overwrites self.processes/self.buffers for the same shards, losing the handle to the old worker. The old and new workers can therefore both run SpanFlusher.main() over the same shards, concurrently calling flush_segments/produce/done_flush_segments and potentially producing duplicate segments. The old worker should be terminated and joined (and the thread-based test path handled explicitly) before its replacement is started.

title: Comma-joined shard list corrupts flusher metric tags
body: When one worker handles multiple shards (including the CLI default of one flusher process), shard_tag is a value such as '0,1,2'. Passing that as a single statsd-style tag value means the commas are interpreted as tag separators, yielding shard=0 plus stray tags '1' and '2' and losing correct per-shard attribution; the wait_produce timer also inconsistently uses the key 'shards' instead of 'shard'. Emit metrics per shard or use a sanitized, single-valued tag consistently.

title: Multiprocess flusher test checks counts but not shard routing or delivery
body: test_flusher_processes_limit only asserts that there are two processes and that the shard lists total four entries. A broken mapping with duplicated and missing shards (for example [[0, 0], [1, 2]]) would still pass, and the test never submits spans or asserts that segments from each assigned shard are produced. The core new behavior (exact shard assignment, multi-worker flushing, and aggregation across workers) is therefore untested; add an end-to-end multi-partition case asserting the exact shard set and the produced segment payloads.

title: Hung flusher processes are never killed before replacement
body: In production, processes are created with multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, producing SpawnProcess objects. SpawnProcess is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process (the default-context process class on Linux), so isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is false and process.kill() is never called. _create_process_for_shards then starts a replacement for the same shards while the hung original remains alive; both can call flush_segments and produce for the same Redis shards, causing duplicate segment production and leaked processes. The check should use multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or exclude threading.Thread instead.

title: join() can return without terminating all flusher processes
body: join() waits for processes sequentially against a shared deadline. If the deadline expires while waiting for an early process, the loop breaks and never calls terminate() on the remaining processes. The terminate() call that is reached is also guarded by isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process), which is false for SpawnProcess objects created through the spawn context. A process hung in flushing or producing can therefore survive join() and continue running alongside a new flusher after rebalance, risking duplicate flushes. Daemon status does not help because the parent consumer process remains alive across rebalances.

title: Invalid flusher process counts are not validated
body: max_processes is accepted without requiring a positive value. An explicit 0 is treated by 'max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)' as unset and unexpectedly spawns one process per shard, while a negative value makes num_processes negative, creates an empty process_to_shards_map, and then fails with an opaque KeyError when shards are assigned. Since --flusher-processes accepts any integer in src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py, operators can trigger either excessive process creation or a consumer startup crash instead of a clear configuration error. Validate the value at the CLI and/or SpanFlusher boundary.

title: Comma-joined shard metric tag corrupts per-shard metrics for shared processes
body: shard_tag is built by joining multiple shard IDs with commas and then used as a single metric tag value. This is the common case when one flusher process handles several shards, including the CLI default of one process. In StatsD-style tag encoding, commas separate tags, so a value such as '0,1,2' is parsed as shard:0 plus stray tags rather than one shard dimension, making the produce and segment-size metrics unusable for per-shard analysis. The wait_produce timer at line 199 also inconsistently names the tag 'shards' instead of 'shard'. Emit metrics per shard or use a sanitized single-value grouping tag consistently.

title: New multiprocess test never exercises spawning or actual multi-shard flushing
body: test_flusher_processes_limit passes produce_to_pipe, which forces SpanFlusher to use threading.Thread instead of the production spawn-process path, and it only asserts process counts and shard-map totals without submitting or flushing any spans. Consequently the tests do not cover spawn pickling of per-shard SpansBuffer objects, run_with_initialized_sentry argument handling, per-process Kafka production, shared-process flushing for multiple shards, or process kill/restart behavior. A regression in the production multiprocess path could pass while the consumer duplicates or loses flushed segments.

title: --flusher-processes accepts zero and negative values
body: The new --flusher-processes option accepts any integer. In SpanFlusher, 0 is treated as unset because it uses `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, so `--flusher-processes 0` unexpectedly starts one heavy spawned Sentry/Kafka-producer process per assigned shard. Negative values flow into `min()` and shard modulo indexing, which can raise a KeyError or start no flusher workers during consumer construction. Validate this as a positive integer, for example with click.IntRange(min=1) and equivalent validation in SpanFlusher/ProcessSpansStrategyFactory.

title: Comma-joined shard list corrupts metrics tags
body: When one flusher process handles multiple shards, which is the normal case when flusher_processes is smaller than the shard count and always the case for the CLI default of 1, `shard_tag` becomes a value such as `0,1,2`. Passing that comma-containing value as a StatsD/DogStatsD tag makes the backend parse it as `shard:0` plus stray tags `1` and `2`, so the produce, wait-produce, and segment-size metrics cannot be correctly attributed by shard. Emit these metrics per flushed segment/shard or otherwise use a single sanitized shard tag value.

title: Multi-shard flusher test never flushes any spans
body: test_flusher_processes_limit creates four shards mapped to two flusher processes, but it only asserts process counts and then joins without submitting spans or advancing the flush clock. The existing basic test covers only one shard/process, so the central new behavior—a shared process correctly flushing, producing, and completing segments for multiple shards, without drops or duplicates—is untested. Add an end-to-end test that stores spans across several shards with fewer flusher processes than shards and asserts the produced segments for each shard.

title: Queues are unbounded, so the strategy provides no backpressure
body: FixedQueuePool creates each queue.Queue with no maxsize and submit() always returns after put(). Because SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit therefore never blocks or rejects a message, Arroyo can keep polling Kafka and accumulating decoded WorkItems, OffsetTracker entries, and queued payloads in memory whenever workers fall behind—the exact slow-consumer scenario this mode is meant to handle. This contradicts the strategy docstring's claimed natural backpressure and can OOM the consumer instead of pausing consumption.

title: Failed work items are marked complete and become committable
body: OrderedQueueWorker catches every exception from result_processor, then its finally block calls offset_tracker.complete_offset(). SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit has the same problem for grouping/submission failures at lines 317-325: it logs, adds the offset, and immediately completes it. A failed uptime result can consequently be committed as if successfully processed, with no retry or DLQ handling, despite the class docstring promising that offsets are committed only after successful processing.

title: Closing one strategy shuts down the factory-shared queue pool
body: ResultsStrategyFactory creates one FixedQueuePool in __init__ and passes that same pool to every SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy it creates. Arroyo closes the old strategy when partitions are revoked and then asks the same factory for a new strategy, but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() calls queue_pool.shutdown(), shutting down all queues and workers. The replacement strategy then reuses a dead pool; subsequent queue.put calls raise queue.ShutDown, which submit() catches and marks complete, so messages after a rebalance can be silently dropped and committed.

title: Graceful shutdown does not drain queued work
body: FixedQueuePool.shutdown() sets worker.shutdown=True before calling Queue.shutdown(immediate=False). OrderedQueueWorker checks that flag in its while condition, so after finishing—or waking from—its current item it exits even if its queue still contains items that immediate=False was supposed to let it drain. SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() also never waits for the queues to empty before shutting the pool down, so close() abandons queued work rather than completing it before Arroyo tears down the assignment.

title: terminate() can commit offsets after the strategy has terminated
body: terminate() sets shutdown_event but does not join commit_thread, unlike close(). _commit_loop waits for one second and then computes and calls commit_function without rechecking shutdown_event before committing, so a terminated strategy whose partitions may already have been revoked can still invoke Arroyo's commit callback after termination.

title: Group assignment uses Python's randomized hash()
body: get_queue_for_group() uses built-in hash(group_key), whose result for strings is randomized per Python process unless PYTHONHASHSEED is fixed. The mapping is therefore not the consistent hashing claimed in the docstring across restarts or across consumer processes; the same subscription can move to a different worker/queue in another process, weakening the within-group ordering guarantee for results that are not confined to one process/partition assignment. A stable digest-based hash should be used instead.

title: Commit scan is O(backlog) every second and holds the partition lock
body: get_committable_offsets() runs every second and iterates range(start, max_offset + 1) while holding the partition lock. When one early offset is stuck, mark_committed never prunes all_offsets/outstanding, so every later offset for that partition makes the retained sets and the scanned range larger; the commit thread repeatedly rescans the whole backlog while blocking worker threads that need the same lock in add_offset()/complete_offset(). This degrades precisely under a slow-item backlog.

title: Queues are unbounded, so the strategy provides no backpressure
body: FixedQueuePool creates every work queue with queue.Queue() and no maxsize, and submit() therefore never blocks or raises MessageRejected. The Arroyo processor can keep polling Kafka and enqueueing messages faster than workers process them, causing unbounded memory growth in both the queues and OffsetTracker's offset sets and potentially an OOM. This also contradicts the strategy docstring's claim of natural backpressure when queues fill up.

title: Failed work items are marked complete and their offsets are committed
body: OrderedQueueWorker.run catches any exception from result_processor, logs it, and then unconditionally calls offset_tracker.complete_offset in the finally block. The commit loop can consequently commit offsets for messages whose processing failed, so those Kafka messages will not be redelivered or sent to a DLQ. This contradicts the strategy's stated guarantee that offsets are committed only after successful processing.

title: Shutdown flag causes workers to abandon queued items
body: FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets worker.shutdown=True before shutting down the queues, while OrderedQueueWorker.run checks that flag at the top of every loop iteration. A worker blocked in get() may process at most one queued item after shutdown begins and then exit, leaving the rest of its queue unprocessed despite queue.shutdown(immediate=False) being intended to drain it. Graceful shutdown therefore strands accepted work; those offsets remain uncompleted and the messages must be reprocessed after restart.

title: Commit loop is stopped before queued work is drained
body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close sets shutdown_event and joins the commit thread before calling queue_pool.shutdown(). Any offsets completed by workers while the pool is draining afterwards have no commit thread left to commit them, so successfully processed messages are not checkpointed on graceful close and will be delivered and processed again after restart.

title: Closing a strategy destroys the shared pool reused after rebalance
body: ResultsStrategyFactory creates one FixedQueuePool and passes that same object to every SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy it creates, but this strategy's close() shuts the shared pool down. Arroyo closes and joins the old strategy when partitions are revoked and then creates a new strategy from the same factory for the new assignment, so the new strategy reuses queues that are already shut down and workers that have exited. Subsequent puts raise queue.ShutDown, which SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit catches and then marks the offset complete, allowing unprocessed messages to be committed and permanently lost after a routine rebalance.

title: Rebalanced strategy reuses an irreversibly shut-down queue pool
body: The factory creates FixedQueuePool once during construction, while SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() shuts that pool down.
