Arroyo creates a new strategy from the same factory when partitions are revoked and reassigned, so the new strategy receives workers that have exited and queues on which shutdown() has already been called. Subsequent queue.put() calls raise queue.ShutDown; SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit() catches that exception and marks the offset complete, allowing messages to be committed without being processed. A normal Kafka rebalance can therefore cause silent data loss until the process is restarted.

title: Failed work items are marked complete and their offsets are committed
body: OrderedQueueWorker.run() logs an exception from result_processor but unconditionally calls complete_offset() in the finally block. The commit loop can consequently commit the offset for a result that was never successfully handled, contradicting the strategy's stated guarantee that offsets are committed only after successful processing and causing failed uptime results to be lost rather than redelivered.

title: Unbounded queues provide no Arroyo backpressure
body: Each work queue is created with queue.Queue() and therefore has no maximum size, and submit() never raises MessageRejected or otherwise blocks. If workers process more slowly than Kafka delivers, Arroyo can continue submitting messages indefinitely, growing memory use and hiding the backlog from Kafka flow control. This also makes the class documentation's claim of natural backpressure when queues fill up incorrect because these queues never fill.

title: Close stops offset committing before workers finish and shutdown drops queued work
body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() stops and joins the commit thread before shutting down the queue pool, so results completed by workers afterward have no commit loop left to commit their offsets and will be redelivered. In addition, FixedQueuePool.shutdown() sets each worker's shutdown flag before calling queue.shutdown(immediate=False); a busy worker exits after its current item instead of draining its queue. Graceful close therefore both leaves processed offsets uncommitted and abandons queued work rather than finishing it within the strategy's join period.

title: Python's salted hash does not provide consistent group-to-queue assignment
body: get_queue_for_group() uses the built-in hash() for a string group key. Python randomizes string hashing per interpreter unless PYTHONHASHSEED is fixed, so the same subscription can map to different queues after a restart or when processed by another consumer process. That undermines the documented consistent-assignment and per-group ordering guarantee across rebalances and deployments; a stable digest such as hashlib.md5 or sha256 should be used instead.

title: Invalid max_workers values are silently accepted for thread-queue-parallel mode
body: The CLI accepts any integer for --max-workers, and this code converts 0 to 20 with 'or' while passing a negative value through as num_queues. A negative value creates no queues or workers; submissions then fail with an index/modulo error, are caught by SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit(), and are marked complete, so their offsets can be committed without processing. The option should be validated as a positive integer before constructing the pool.

title: Blocked offsets make commit checks repeatedly scan an ever-growing set
body: OffsetTracker retains every offset after a blocked or very slow offset, because offsets can only be removed after a contiguous commit. get_committable_offsets() is called once per second and computes both min() and max() over that retained set each time. During exactly the slow-item backlog this feature is meant to tolerate, the set can grow to a large number of completed offsets and the commit loop becomes repeated O(n) work while also retaining unbounded tracking state.

title: Password verification is skipped whenever a TOTP code is present, enabling second-factor-only login
body: In the credentials authorize function, the password is only verified when credentials.totpCode is absent. The new backup-code branch is selected whenever credentials.backupCode is present, even if credentials.totpCode is also present. As a result, a CAL user with a password can authenticate with only a valid TOTP code, and a valid backup code plus any non-empty totpCode also bypasses password verification. This defeats the first authentication factor for 2FA logins. Password verification should be required for accounts that have a password, especially for backup-code use, instead of being skipped whenever totpCode is present.

title: Backup-code consumption is not atomic, allowing reuse or resurrection of used codes
body: During login, the encrypted backup-code array is read, a matching index is set to null, and the user row is updated in a separate write. Concurrent successful logins can both read the same unused backup code before either update completes, allowing the same one-time code to be used more than once. Concurrent use of different codes can also cause last-write-wins to overwrite another request's nulling, effectively resurrecting a used code. This breaks the one-time-use guarantee. Use a transaction or an atomic/conditional update when consuming a backup code.

title: Backup-code login is blocked for non-CAL identity-provider accounts
body: The early checks for non-CAL identity providers only exempt credentials.totpCode, not credentials.backupCode. If a user with 2FA enabled has a non-CAL identity provider (for example after identity-provider conversion/linking), supplying a backup code without a TOTP code throws ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled or IncorrectEmailPassword. The disable endpoint supports backup codes, but the login flow effectively makes backup recovery unavailable for these accounts. The checks should also allow backupCode where appropriate.

title: Successful 2FA enable is not propagated if the modal is dismissed without clicking the explicit Close button
body: After the TOTP code is accepted, the modal moves to the backup-code screen and only calls onEnable when the user clicks the explicit Close button. If the dialog is dismissed through onOpenChange, such as ESC, backdrop click, or a parent-controlled close, onEnable is not called and the modal state is not reset. The settings screen can remain showing 2FA as disabled even though it is enabled on the server, and reopening the modal may show a stale step. The modal should handle close/dismiss by resetting state and notifying the parent appropriately.

title: resetState does not clear form values or sensitive generated 2FA state
body: resetState clears only password, error message, and step. It leaves the react-hook-form totpCode value, backupCodes, backupCodesUrl, dataUri, and secret in state. A stale six-digit totpCode can trigger the auto-submit effect again if the modal is remounted or revisited, and stale QR/backup-code state can be shown unexpectedly. It also retains the blob URL containing backup codes. resetState should call form.reset(), clear all generated 2FA state, and revoke the object URL.

title: E2E assertion checks a Promise instead of the actual checked state
body: The test uses await expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy(). locator.isChecked() returns a Promise, and asserting that the Promise is truthy does not verify that the switch is actually checked. This can pass even when 2FA was not enabled. The test also does not handle the new backup-code screen in this first flow. Use a web-first assertion such as toBeChecked() and handle the backup-code dialog.

title: No E2E coverage for backup-code login or one-time consumption
body: The PR adds backup-code login and consumes backup codes on use, but the E2E tests only verify that backup codes are displayed, copied, and downloaded during setup. There is no test that logs in with a backup code, verifies that a used backup code is rejected, or disables 2FA using a backup code. The TODO in the test file acknowledges this gap. These flows should be covered before merge.

title: Backup-code normalization only strips dashes
body: The backup-code check removes dashes with replaceAll('-', '') but does not trim whitespace or normalize letter case. Generated codes are lowercase hexadecimal strings. If a user copies a code with surrounding whitespace or uppercase characters, a valid code will be rejected. The same normalization issue exists in the disable endpoint. Trim and lowercase user input before comparison.

title: Backup code can be submitted empty despite the input being marked required
body: The login form uses noValidate and the Zod schema only validates email/password while passing through other fields. When the user switches to the lost-access backup-code screen, the BackupCode input's required attribute is not enforced and there is no schema validation for backupCode. Submitting an empty backup code sends an empty value to the server, which then falls back to the TOTP path and returns a confusing second-factor-required error. Add validation for backupCode or avoid disabling native validation for this field.

title: Copy button shows success even if clipboard write fails
body: The copy handler calls navigator.clipboard.writeText without awaiting it or catching errors, then immediately shows a success toast. If the Clipboard API is unavailable, permission is denied, or the write rejects, the user still sees a success message, and an unhandled rejection may occur. Await the clipboard operation and show success only when it actually succeeds.

title: Backup-code blob URL is not revoked on close or unmount
body: The component creates an object URL containing the user's backup codes for download. It only revokes a previous URL when a new setup response is received. If the modal is closed, cancelled, or the component unmounts, the object URL remains alive for the page lifetime, unnecessarily retaining sensitive backup-code data in memory. Revoke the object URL during reset/cleanup.

title: Disable-2FA modal state persists when closed via dialog controls
body: The modal does not reset twoFactorLostAccess, form values, or error message when the dialog is closed through onOpenChange rather than through Cancel or successful disable. If a user opens the lost-access view, closes the modal, and reopens it, the modal can unexpectedly remain in lost-access mode or retain stale input/error state. Reset modal state when the dialog is closed or reopened.

title: Password verification can be bypassed when a backup code is submitted with an arbitrary totpCode
body: In the credentials authorize flow, password verification is only performed when credentials.totpCode is absent. A client can send a valid backupCode together with any non-empty totpCode; the password check is skipped, and the new backup-code branch then authenticates the user if the backup code is valid. For password-based CAL accounts this allows a stolen backup code to be used without the account password. The password must be verified whenever password login is being used, including when a backup code is submitted.

title: Backup codes are consumed with a non-atomic read-modify-write
body: During backup-code login, the encrypted backup-code array is decrypted, checked in memory, mutated, re-encrypted, and written back in a standalone Prisma update. Two concurrent login attempts using the same backup code can both read the array before either update commits, causing both to succeed and violating the one-time-use property. Concurrent use of different backup codes can also overwrite each other's updates and resurrect consumed codes. Consumption should be atomic, transactional, or modeled as individually hashed/unique codes.

title: backupCode is used without validating that it is a string
body: The disable endpoint calls req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "") without first validating that req.body.backupCode is a string. A JSON request body that supplies an object, array, number, or null for backupCode will throw a TypeError and produce a 500 instead of returning a validation error. Validate and normalize request fields before using string methods.

title: Backup codes are not trimmed or lower-cased before comparison
body: Generated backup codes are lowercase hex strings, but the login path only removes dashes before comparing. If a user types or pastes a code with surrounding whitespace or uppercase characters, the comparison fails even though the code is valid. The same issue exists in the disable endpoint. Input should be trimmed and lower-cased before comparison.

title: Empty backup-code submission gives no user feedback
body: The login form uses noValidate and the Zod schema does not validate backupCode. If the user is on the backup-code screen and submits an empty value, the server returns SecondFactorRequired because neither backupCode nor totpCode is present, and the handler only keeps twoFactorRequired true without setting an error message. The UI therefore appears to do nothing instead of telling the user a backup code is required.

title: No automated test exercises backup-code login or disable-with-backup-code
body: The added e2e coverage only checks that backup codes are displayed, downloadable, and copyable after enabling 2FA. It does not test the newly added authentication paths: logging in with a backup code via 'Lost access' or disabling 2FA using a backup code. These are security-critical flows and should have explicit tests.

title: missing_backup_codes message is misleading during login
body: The missing_backup_codes string says 'Please generate them in your settings.' This is not actionable when the message is shown on the login lost-access flow, because the user is locked out and cannot access settings. The message should state that no backup codes are available for this sign-in attempt.

title: Closing the dialog after 2FA is enabled does not reset state or notify the parent
body: EnableTwoFactorModal passes onOpenChange directly to Dialog. If the user dismisses the dialog via the close control or backdrop while the backup-code step is displayed after 2FA has already been enabled, neither resetState nor onEnable is called. If the modal remains mounted, reopening it can show stale state, and the parent settings screen is not notified that 2FA was enabled.

title: Backup-code sign-in can bypass password/first-factor verification
body: In the CredentialsProvider authorize function, the password is verified only when `!credentials.totpCode` (line 121). The backup-code path at line 131 is taken whenever `credentials.backupCode` is present. A caller can therefore POST credentials containing a valid `backupCode` and an arbitrary non-empty `totpCode`; the password check is skipped and the backup code alone authenticates the user. For password accounts this removes the password factor, and for non-CAL identity-provider accounts it also bypasses the OAuth/SAML first factor. Consequence: account takeover if a backup code is known or leaked.

title: Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write
body: After decrypting `user.backupCodes`, the code sets the used entry to null and writes the whole encrypted array back. Two parallel successful logins can read the same array before either update completes; one update can overwrite the other, restoring an already-used code, or the same code can be accepted by both requests. One-time backup codes are therefore not guaranteed to be single-use. Use a transaction/row lock or an atomic consumption mechanism.

title: Backup codes are compared case-sensitively and without trimming
body: The server only removes dashes before doing `indexOf`. Generated codes are lowercase hex, while the UI placeholder uses uppercase. If a user types or pastes uppercase letters, leading/trailing whitespace, or other formatting, the comparison fails even for a valid code. Normalize by trimming, removing separators, and lowercasing before comparison. The same issue exists in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`.

title: Modal state reset does not clear react-hook-form/TOTP value
body: `resetState` only clears password, error, and step; it does not call `form.reset()` or clear the registered `totpCode`. Because the component auto-submits when `totpCode?.trim().length === 6` (line 157), a stale six-digit value left from a previous enable attempt can trigger an unintended enable request or surface errors when the modal is reopened. It also leaves secret/backup-code state and object URLs in memory.

title: 2FA enable success is not propagated if backup-code dialog is dismissed
body: After `handleEnable` succeeds, the modal moves to the backup-code step and calls `onEnable` only from the explicit Close button. If the user closes the dialog with Escape/overlay/close affordance, `onOpenChange` closes the modal without calling `onEnable`, even though 2FA has already been enabled server-side. The settings UI can remain in the disabled/stale state until a refresh.

title: Blob object URL for backup-code download is not revoked on close/unmount
body: `URL.createObjectURL` is called during setup, but the URL is only revoked if setup runs again. Closing the modal or unmounting the component leaves the blob URL alive, causing a small memory leak. Revoke the URL in a cleanup effect or when the modal closes.

title: No e2e coverage for the new backup-code login/disable paths
body: The PR adds UI for backup codes and server-side consumption, but the tests only verify that the codes are displayed/copied/downloaded. The TODO acknowledges missing tests for logging in or disabling 2FA with a backup code. Without coverage, the critical backup-code authentication/consumption logic can regress unnoticed.

title: Password visibility toggle is removed from keyboard focus
body: Adding `tabIndex={-1}` to the show/hide password button prevents keyboard users from focusing and activating it. This makes the password field less accessible; the control should remain focusable or provide an equivalent keyboard-accessible alternative.

title: Backup code input is assumed to be a string
body: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll` is called without validating the body field type. A malformed POST with a number/object/array for `backupCode` will throw a TypeError and return a 500 instead of a validation error. Validate/sanitize the field as a string before processing; the same assumption exists in the NextAuth credentials handler.

title: Submitting an empty backup-code form can fail silently
body: The login form has `noValidate`, so the BackupCode input's required/minLength attributes are not enforced. If a user is on the lost-access screen and submits an empty backup code, the server falls back to the TOTP branch and returns `second-factor-required`; the client merely keeps the two-factor screen and displays no error, leaving the user stuck. Show an error or validate the backup code client-side before submitting.

title: TypeError when destinationCalendar is missing or empty
body: mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined when evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array. The code then accesses .integration, which throws a TypeError. Several handlers now pass [] when no calendar exists, so creating a booking with a Google Meet location can crash before any event is created. Use optional chaining and handle the empty-array case.

title: Fallback credential filter uses impossible type 'calendar'
body: When destinationCalendar is missing or empty, the fallback selects this.calendarCredentials.filter(cred => cred.type === 'calendar'). The credentials collected here are types such as google_calendar or office365_calendar and are filtered by endsWith('_calendar'), so an exact 'calendar' type will not exist. The fallback therefore never creates a traditional calendar event.

title: Team destination calendars are dropped when organizer has no destination calendar
body: evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to null when neither eventType nor organizer has a calendar. The later collective-only code uses evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars), which is a no-op on null. All team host calendars are discarded, so collective hosts will not receive calendar events.

title: loadUsers can return undefined instead of an empty array
body: The new loadUsers returns users.length ? users : eventType.users, while the old code returned eventType.users || []. If hosts is empty and eventType.users is undefined, loadUsers resolves to undefined; downstream code that expects an array, such as users.length or users[0], can throw.

title: Organization slug condition inverted
body: The slug spread changed from including slug when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is false to including it when true. This reverses the previous behavior: organizations created while billing is disabled will have no slug, while billing-enabled organizations get a slug immediately, likely breaking organization creation or the billing flow.

title: Google event patch can use undefined calendarId
body: selectedCalendar can be undefined when no destination calendar matches the credential. The insert call falls back to 'primary', but the follow-up patch call passes calendarId: selectedCalendar without the same fallback. This can fail to update the event description with the hangout link or produce an unhandled API error.

title: Google updateEvent may receive undefined calendarId
body: If externalCalendarId is null or empty, selectedCalendar becomes undefined because the fallback searches for a calendar whose externalId equals undefined. calendar.events.update is then called with an undefined calendarId, which will fail for events created on primary or for older references without externalCalendarId.

title: Google createEvent selects calendar only by credentialId
body: CalendarManager passes the destination calendar externalId, but Google createEvent chooses the calendar only by matching credentialId. If the same credential has multiple possible destination calendars, the first match is used instead of the intended externalId, so the event can be created in the wrong calendar and the stored externalId can be wrong.

title: Lark createEvent always uses first destination calendar
body: For collective events, EventManager creates an event for each host credential, but Lark createEvent always uses event.destinationCalendar[0].externalId. When a non-main host credential is used, it will attempt to create the event in the first host's calendar or fail, so multiple-host Lark calendars are not handled correctly.

title: Office 365 createEvent always uses first destination calendar
body: Office 365 createEvent always uses the first entry of event.destinationCalendar to build /me/calendars/{externalId}/events. For collective multiple hosts, secondary host credentials will target the first host's calendar or fall back incorrectly, so events may be created in the wrong calendar or fail.

title: CalDAV createEvent can silently create no event for secondary hosts
body: CalDAV createEvent filters listCalendars by the first destination calendar's externalId. For a secondary host credential, that externalId may not exist in the account, so the filter yields zero calendars and Promise.all([]) resolves successfully. The method returns a created-event object even though no calendar event was created.

title: updateLocation creates references without credential or external calendar IDs
body: referencesToCreate maps result.externalId and result.credentialId, but CalendarManager.updateEvent does not populate these fields. editLocation.handler then creates booking references with null credentialId/externalCalendarId, which can break later updates, reschedules, or cancellations that rely on those references.

title: Reschedule merge deletes only first old calendar reference
body: When merging/rescheduling with newBookingId, only the first old calendar reference is found and deleted. For collective bookings with multiple host calendar references, the other old calendar events are left behind.

title: Video credentialId is dropped in create references
body: In create(), credentialId is only preserved for calendar results; non-calendar results such as video now get credentialId: undefined. If createMeeting returns a credentialId, it is dropped from referencesToCreate, making later video updates rely on ambiguous type matching.

title: updateEvent may be called with undefined credential
body: If reference.credentialId is present but the credential is not in this.calendarCredentials and the DB lookup does not produce a usable credential, credential remains undefined and is passed to updateEvent. CalendarManager.updateEvent will then access properties on undefined and reject.

title: Duplicate events for non-traditional calendars
body: createAllCalendarEvents processes destinationCalendar entries and then unconditionally creates events for every credential whose type includes 'other_calendar'. If a destinationCalendar entry is itself an other_calendar integration, this creates duplicate events.

title: createEvent reports success when calendar adapter is unavailable
body: createEvent initializes success to true and does not set it false when getCalendar returns null. It then returns a successful EventResult with no createdEvent, which can cause callers to store or reference a calendar event that was never created.

title: Awaiting array instead of promises
body: In the paid cancellation branch, await apiDeletes awaits the array itself rather than the promises it contains. The handler can return before calendar/video deletions finish, and rejected delete promises may become unhandled.

title: Recurring cancellation deletes wrong or duplicate calendar events
body: For recurring cancellations, inside each calendar reference the code iterates all user calendar credentials and deletes the first calendar reference found on each updated booking. This can use the wrong credential, delete the same event multiple times, and miss events belonging to other calendar references or hosts.

title: Confirming a collective booking only includes one destination calendar
body: When confirming a booking, evt.destinationCalendar is built only from booking.destinationCalendar or the confirming user's destination calendar. For collective events, other hosts' destination calendars are not included, so EventManager.create will not create calendar events for all hosts.

title: Stripe payment success only includes one destination calendar
body: handlePaymentSuccess builds evt.destinationCalendar from a single booking/user calendar. For paid collective events, other hosts' destination calendars are omitted, so their calendar events will not be created after payment confirmation.

title: PayPal payment success only includes one destination calendar
body: handlePaymentSuccess builds evt.destinationCalendar from a single booking/user calendar. For paid collective events, other hosts' destination calendars are omitted, so their calendar events will not be created after PayPal payment confirmation.

title: Webhook/API payload contract changed for destinationCalendar
body: CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar changed from a singular object/null to an array. Webhook payloads and other external consumers that expect the previous shape may break, for example null vs [] vs object. If intentional, this contract change should be documented; otherwise external payloads should preserve the old shape.

title: Meet fallback crashes when destinationCalendar is empty
body: mainHostDestinationCalendar can be undefined when evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, but the code accesses mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining. Booking creation using Google Meet without a destination calendar will throw a TypeError instead of falling back to Cal Video.

title: Team destination calendars are dropped when main destination calendar is null
body: evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. The later collective-only code uses evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars), so team members' destination calendars are silently ignored. Hosts with connected calendars can miss calendar events.

title: Reschedule merge deletes only the first old calendar event
body: When a newBookingId is provided, updateAllCalendarEvents finds only the first calendar reference from the old booking and deletes that event. Collective bookings can have multiple calendar references, so the other hosts' old calendar events are left behind after reschedule.

title: updateEvent result omits credentialId and externalId needed for references
body: CalendarManager.updateEvent returns an EventResult without credentialId or externalId, but EventManager.updateLocation now builds referencesToCreate from result.credentialId and result.externalId. Calendar references created after an location edit can lose the credential and external calendar linkage.

title: Google update fallback cannot select a calendar when externalCalendarId is missing
body: selectedCalendar is computed as externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId. When externalCalendarId is null or undefined, the fallback searches for externalId === undefined and returns undefined, so updateEvent can call the Google API with an undefined calendarId instead of falling back to the main destination calendar.

title: Google hangout-link patch may use undefined calendarId
body: createEvent inserts the event with selectedCalendar || 'primary', but the follow-up patch to add the hangout link uses selectedCalendar without the same fallback. If no matching destination calendar is found, the patch request has an undefined calendarId and the event description may not be updated.

title: Google delete fallback may target the primary calendar instead of the event calendar
body: deleteEvent uses the same faulty fallback as updateEvent when externalCalendarId is missing and then falls back to 'primary'. If the event was created on a non-primary calendar and no externalCalendarId is stored, deletion can hit the wrong calendar, receive a 404, and silently leave the event undeleted.

title: Organizer email uses the first destination calendar for all host calendars
body: In createEvent, the organizer attendee email is taken from the first destination calendar in the event, while the event may be created on another host's calendar using a different credentialId. For collective events this can mark the wrong user as organizer or send incorrect calendar notifications on non-main host calendars.

title: Lark createEvent always uses the first destination calendar
body: EventManager can invoke createEvent once per host credential for collective events, but LarkCalendarService always uses event.destinationCalendar[0].externalId. Events for additional hosts can either fail because the credential does not own that calendar or create duplicate events on the first host's calendar.

title: Office 365 createEvent always uses the first destination calendar
body: Office365CalendarService.createEvent selects the first entry of event.destinationCalendar regardless of the credential being used. With multiple collective hosts, calls made with another host's credential may try to create the event in the first host's calendar or fail, so non-main hosts are not reliably invited.

title: CalDAV createEvent filters calendars by the first destination calendar only
body: BaseCalendarService.createEvent filters listCalendars results using only the first destination calendar's externalId. When called for another host's credential, no calendar may match, resulting in zero createCalendarObject calls while still returning success; the other host's event is silently not created.

title: Recurring cancellation deletes only the first calendar reference and ignores other hosts
body: In the recurring-cancellation branch, for each updated booking the code uses references.find(ref => ref.type.includes('_calendar')) and iterates only the organizer's credentials. Collective bookings can have multiple calendar references belonging to different hosts, so other hosts' recurring calendar events may not be deleted.

title: Paid cancellation does not await deletion promises
body: The paid cancellation path executes 'await apiDeletes' where apiDeletes is an array of promises. Awaiting the array does not wait for the contained promises, so calendar/video deletions may still be pending or may fail without being handled before the handler returns success.

title: Organization slug condition appears inverted
body: The change now includes slug when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, whereas the previous logic included slug when billing was disabled. This can create or reserve an organization slug during the billing-enabled flow where only metadata.requestedSlug was expected, potentially breaking the paid slug flow.

title: Webhook payload destinationCalendar changed from object/null to array
body: CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar is now an array, which changes the shape of webhook payloads and other external consumers that previously received a single object or null. The tests also show inconsistent expectations between null and empty array depending on trigger, making this a public API compatibility risk.

title: Missing credential causes all calendar updates to fail
body: In updateAllCalendarEvents, if a booking reference has a credentialId that cannot be found in memory or in the database, credential remains undefined and updateEvent is still called. The rejected promise causes Promise.all to fail, so the catch handler returns failure for all calendar references instead of skipping only the missing credential.

title: Crash when destinationCalendar is empty and location is Google Meet
body: In EventManager.create, mainHostDestinationCalendar can be undefined when evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array. The condition checks mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining, so bookings/reschedules with Google Meet selected and no destination calendar throw a TypeError instead of falling back to Cal Video.

title: Collective team destination calendars are dropped when the main destination calendar is null
body: handleNewBooking initializes evt.destinationCalendar as null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. It then uses evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars), so if it is null the collected team/host destination calendars are silently discarded. Collective events with an organizer who has no destination calendar will not create calendar events for other hosts.

title: updateLocation creates references without calendar credential/external IDs
body: EventManager.updateLocation maps update results to referencesToCreate using result.externalId and result.credentialId, but CalendarManager.updateEvent does not set these fields on successful update results. It also uses result.createdEvent, while update results contain updatedEvent. As a result, references created after editing a location can have empty uid and undefined credentialId/externalCalendarId, breaking later calendar updates/cancellations.

title: Google updateEvent fallback cannot select a calendar when externalCalendarId is missing
body: In GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent, selectedCalendar is set to externalCalendarId if truthy; otherwise it searches event.destinationCalendar for a calendar whose externalId === externalCalendarId. When externalCalendarId is null/undefined, this comparison can never match, so selectedCalendar becomes undefined and the Google Calendar API update is called with an undefined calendarId. This breaks updates/reschedules for older references that lack externalCalendarId.

title: Google createEvent patch can use undefined calendarId
body: GoogleCalendarService.createEvent inserts the event with calendarId: selectedCalendar || 'primary', but the follow-up patch to add the hangout link uses calendarId: selectedCalendar. If no destination calendar matches the credentialId, selectedCalendar is undefined, so the event is created on 'primary' but the patch request is made with an undefined calendarId.

title: Google deleteEvent fallback ignores destination calendar when externalCalendarId is missing
body: GoogleCalendarService.deleteEvent falls back to finding a destination calendar by comparing externalId to externalCalendarId even when externalCalendarId is undefined/null. That fallback cannot match, so deletion defaults to 'primary'. If the event was created on a non-primary calendar and the reference lacks externalCalendarId, deletion can target the wrong calendar and leave the event behind.

title: Office365 createEvent always uses the first destination calendar for all hosts
body: Office365CalendarService.createEvent selects only the first entry from event.destinationCalendar and builds the Graph URL from that externalId. CalendarManager may call createEvent once per host destination calendar/credential for collective events, but this implementation ignores the credential being used. For a second host, it will attempt to create the event in the first host's calendar, which can fail or create the event in the wrong calendar.

title: Lark createEvent always uses the first destination calendar for all hosts
body: LarkCalendarService.createEvent uses only event.destinationCalendar[0].externalId. When multiple host destination calendars are supplied for a collective event, CalendarManager creates one event per destination/credential, but Lark will repeatedly target the first host's calendar instead of the calendar associated with the credential being used. This prevents multiple hosts from receiving correct Lark calendar events.

title: CalDAV createEvent filters calendars by the first destination calendar only
body: BaseCalendarService.createEvent filters listCalendars(event) using event.destinationCalendar[0].externalId. For multiple host destination calendars, a call for another host's credential will filter that host's calendars using the first host's externalId. If no calendar matches, no calendar object is created but the method still returns success, silently failing to create events for non-main hosts.

title: Organization slug condition is inverted
body: The organization creation data now includes slug when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true. The previous logic included slug when billing was disabled and stored requestedSlug in metadata when billing was enabled. This reversal means organizations may get a slug immediately when billing is enabled and may have no slug when billing is disabled, breaking the intended billing/organization provisioning flow.

title: Recurring cancellation deletes with all organizer credentials and first reference only
body: In handleCancelBooking, when cancelling all remaining recurring events and a calendar reference has a credentialId, the code loops over all of the organizer's calendar credentials and deletes the first calendar reference found on each updated booking. It ignores the specific credentialId/externalCalendarId being processed and repeats this for every calendar reference. With multiple calendar references this causes duplicate or cross-credential delete attempts and can miss non-organizer credentials fetched from the DB.

title: await apiDeletes does not await the queued deletion promises
body: In the paid cancellation branch, apiDeletes is an array of promises from calendar/video deletion calls, but the code executes await apiDeletes. Awaiting an array does not wait for the promises inside it, so the handler can return before deletions complete and rejected promises may become unhandled. It should use Promise.all or Promise.allSettled on apiDeletes.

title: updateAllCalendarEvents can pass an undefined credential to updateEvent
body: In EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents, if a booking reference has credentialId but the credential is not present in this.calendarCredentials and cannot be loaded from the database with an app slug, credential remains undefined. The code still calls updateEvent(credential, ...), causing the update to reject and all calendar updates to fail instead of skipping or reporting only the broken reference.

title: Google refresh stores Zod safeParse envelope instead of token data
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a Zod `safeParse` result (`{ success, data }`), but this line assigns that entire object to `key` and saves it as `credential.key`. The Google credential schema expects the token object itself (access_token, refresh_token, expiry_date). After one successful refresh, the stored credential no longer parses, breaking Google Calendar authentication.

title: Broken minimum token schema and placeholder refresh_token corrupt credentials
body: The `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses computed keys like `[z.string().toString()]`, which do not create a Zod index signature; they only create literal properties. Since Zod objects strip unknown keys by default, sync-mode parsing removes refresh tokens, expiry fields, and provider-specific fields such as instance_url. The function then inserts the literal string "refresh_token" when `refresh_token` is missing. Saving this result can overwrite real refresh tokens or required metadata, leaving credentials unusable.

title: Salesforce credential refresh uses undefined prisma import
body: This file calls `prisma.credential.update` but does not import `prisma` from `@calcom/prisma`. This will fail type checking and cause a runtime ReferenceError when Salesforce token refresh is attempted.

title: Sync-mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response for callers expecting different types
body: When credential sharing is enabled, this function bypasses the provider refresh function and returns the raw `fetch` Response from `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`. Callers were not updated to a common contract: Google expects a response with `.data`, HubSpot expects a parsed token object, and ZohoCRM/Bigin expect an Axios response with `.data`. In those integrations the returned Response lacks the expected properties, causing undefined access and failed token refreshes.

title: Bigin token refresh sends credential ID as calcomUserId
body: `refreshOAuthTokens` expects a Cal.com user ID, but this call passes `credentialId`, the credential primary key. The external sync endpoint will receive `calcomUserId` equal to a credential ID, not the user's ID, so it cannot identify the correct user token to return.

title: Salesforce client is created with stale access token after refresh
body: After fetching a new access token and updating the credential, the returned `jsforce.Connection` is still constructed with `credentialKey.access_token`, the old access token. The newly fetched `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token` is not used, so API calls may continue to use an expired token.

title: Salesforce refresh is not synced but still uses the destructive minimum schema
body: Salesforce token refresh does not call `refreshOAuthTokens`, so it does not use the configured external sync endpoint. However it does call `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, which switches to the minimal sync schema when credential sharing is enabled. That minimal schema strips required Salesforce fields such as `instance_url` before the credential is saved, corrupting Salesforce credentials.

title: Zoho CRM token validity check is inverted
body: `isTokenValid` returns true when `expiryDate < Date.now()`, i.e. when the token is expired. `getToken` then resolves without refreshing when `isTokenValid` is true and refreshes when it is false. This causes expired Zoho CRM tokens to be used and valid tokens to be refreshed unnecessarily.

title: Credential webhook does not reset invalid flag on update
body: When updating an existing credential, the handler only updates `key`. If the credential was previously marked `invalid`, it remains invalid even after new synced keys are written. The update should also set `invalid: false` when accepting new credentials.

title: Credential webhook find-then-update/create can duplicate credentials
body: The handler searches for an existing credential and then creates or updates it without a transaction or unique constraint. Concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user/app can both miss the existing record and create duplicates. If duplicates already exist, `findFirst` updates an arbitrary one.

title: Webhook handler accepts all HTTP methods
body: The handler does not check `req.method`, so any HTTP method can reach the credential creation/update logic if the secret header is supplied. It should only accept POST and reject other methods with 405.

title: Unhandled Zod, decryption, and JSON parse errors return 500
body: Zod parsing of the request body, symmetric decryption, and `JSON.parse` of the decrypted payload can throw. There is no try/catch to convert invalid payloads into a 400 response, so malformed webhook requests result in 500 errors.

title: Credential sync endpoint is called without authentication or response validation
body: The outbound sync request sends `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` without any authentication, signature, or shared secret, and it does not validate `response.ok` before returning. If the endpoint is reachable, callers may accept forged or malformed token responses, and failures are not handled explicitly.

title: Team credential creation lacks admin check
body: When OAuth state includes `teamId`, the code only verifies that the user is an accepted team member before creating a team credential. It does not check that the user has admin access to the team. Because OAuth state is client-supplied JSON, a non-admin team member can craft a state with a team id and create team app credentials.

title: Salesforce refresh checks statusText instead of response.ok
body: Using `response.statusText !== "OK"` to detect OAuth failure is unreliable; HTTP/2 and some fetch implementations return an empty statusText even for successful responses. This can cause successful token refreshes to throw. Use `response.ok` or the HTTP status code instead.

title: No tests for credential sync webhook and token refresh changes
body: This PR adds a secret-authenticated credential ingestion endpoint and changes token refresh behavior across many providers, but no tests are included. Tests are needed for webhook authentication/validation, idempotent credential create/update, and refresh behavior with credential sync enabled and disabled.

title: Webhook handler does not restrict HTTP method
body: The handler creates or updates credentials regardless of req.method. This state-changing webhook should reject non-POST requests; otherwise proxies or clients that send a body with other methods can trigger credential writes, and unexpected methods produce confusing parse errors.

title: Webhook secret is compared with strict equality instead of a constant-time comparison
body: The webhook secret is compared using !==. For secret validation, use a constant-time comparison such as crypto.timingSafeEqual after normalizing both values to buffers/strings, to reduce timing-based secret disclosure.

title: Credential lookup-then-create can create duplicate credentials
body: The endpoint does findFirst and then update/create without a transaction or unique constraint. Two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user/app can both see no existing credential and both create one, leaving duplicate credentials. Later lookups with findFirst may then choose an arbitrary row.

title: Credential update does not clear the invalid flag
body: When updating an existing credential, only key is written. If the credential was previously marked invalid, for example after an invalid_grant error, it remains invalid even though a new valid key was synced. The update should also set invalid: false, or otherwise validate and reset the flag when new credentials are accepted.

title: minimumTokenResponseSchema does not create the intended dynamic/index validation
body: The schema uses computed keys like [z.string().toString()]. This does not create a Zod index signature; it creates ordinary object properties named the schema's string representation. The intended catch-all validation for numeric expiry properties is therefore not implemented, and valid token responses may fail validation when credential sharing is enabled.

title: Generic minimum schema is used for all refreshes when sync env vars are enabled
body: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, this helper ignores the provider-specific schema for every token refresh, even when the refresh request was made to the real OAuth provider. This can strip or reject provider-specific fields that are required for the integration to keep working.

title: Missing refresh_token is replaced with the literal string 'refresh_token'
body: If the parsed response has no refresh_token, the code assigns the placeholder string 'refresh_token'. OAuth refresh responses often omit a new refresh_token, meaning the existing one should be retained. This placeholder can be persisted and overwrite a valid refresh token, corrupting the credential and making future refreshes impossible.

title: Sync mode returns a raw fetch Response while many callers expect provider-specific parsed objects
body: In credential-sharing mode, refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT. Many call sites still expect the original provider response shape: Google expects an object with .data, HubSpot expects a token object, and Zoho callers expect an AxiosResponse with .data. This mismatch causes runtime failures or invalid token persistence when syncing is enabled.

title: Google credential refresh persists the Zod SafeParse wrapper instead of the parsed key
body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod SafeParse result, but GoogleCalendarService assigns that result to key and writes it to prisma.credential.key. The stored credential becomes an object like { success, data } instead of the actual token object. Subsequent parsing of credential.key will fail, breaking Google Calendar authentication. The code should persist the parsed data, not the SafeParse wrapper.

title: Google token refresh assumes a provider response shape that sync mode does not provide
body: After refreshOAuthTokens, the code reads res?.data.access_token and res?.data.expiry_date. In credential-sharing sync mode, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, which has no .data property. This will throw or store undefined token values when the sync endpoint is used.

title: HubSpot refresh treats sync fetch Response as a parsed HubSpot token object
body: When credential syncing is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but this code treats the result as a HubspotToken object and reads expiresIn. A fetch Response has no expiresIn, so expiryDate becomes NaN and the credential is updated with invalid token data.

title: Zoho Bigin refresh assumes AxiosResponse .data, which sync mode does not return
body: refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response when credential syncing is enabled, but this code accesses tokenInfo.data.error as if the result were an AxiosResponse. This will throw a TypeError because fetch Response objects do not have a .data property.

title: Zoho CRM refresh assumes AxiosResponse .data, which sync mode does not return
body: refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response when credential syncing is enabled, but this code accesses zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error as if the result were an AxiosResponse. This will throw a TypeError because fetch Response objects do not have a .data property.

title: Salesforce refresh bypasses the credential sync endpoint
body: Unlike the other modified adapters, Salesforce's getClient calls Salesforce's token endpoint directly and never uses refreshOAuthTokens. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are configured, Salesforce tokens are therefore not refreshed from the self-hosted source of truth, breaking the intended credential-sync contract for this app.

title: Salesforce client refreshes the access token on every construction
body: getClient unconditionally calls the Salesforce token endpoint whenever the service is constructed, without checking whether the existing access token is still valid. This adds an extra token refresh for each use of the Salesforce integration and can cause unnecessary latency and rate-limit pressure.

title: Salesforce token refresh checks response.statusText instead of response.ok
body: The code treats any response whose statusText is not 'OK' as an error. HTTP/2 and some fetch implementations may return an empty statusText even for successful responses, and other successful statuses may not use 'OK'. This can make valid token refreshes fail. Use response.ok instead.

title: Salesforce CalendarService uses prisma without importing it
body: prisma.credential.update is called in this file, but prisma is not imported. This will fail TypeScript compilation or cause a runtime ReferenceError when the Salesforce calendar service refreshes credentials.

title: Salesforce credential update can lose provider-specific fields such as instance_url
body: The credential key is replaced with accessTokenParsed.data plus the old refresh_token. When credential sharing is enabled, parseRefreshTokenResponse uses a generic minimum schema that does not preserve Salesforce-specific fields such as instance_url. Persisting the reduced object can corrupt the credential and break later Salesforce connections.

title: Salesforce connection is created with the stale access token after refresh
body: After refreshing and persisting the new access token, the jsforce Connection is constructed using credentialKey.access_token from the old credential object instead of the newly parsed access token. The refreshed token is therefore not used for subsequent Salesforce API calls.

title: Outbound credential sync request has no authentication
body: The POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends calcomUserId and appSlug but does not include a shared secret, signature, or other authentication header. The remote endpoint has no built-in way to verify that the request originated from this Cal.com instance.

title: Minimum token schema does not allow arbitrary token fields
body: The computed keys in minimumTokenResponseSchema (e.g. [z.string().toString()]) do not create a catch-all/index signature in Zod; they only add fixed, unintended properties. As a result, when app credential sharing is enabled, normal OAuth fields such as refresh_token, expires_in, expiry_date, and provider-specific fields are stripped from the parsed token. This causes loss of token data and broken refresh flows. Use z.record/catchall or an explicit schema.

title: Placeholder refresh_token is written into credentials
body: If the parsed token lacks refresh_token, the helper assigns the literal string 'refresh_token' as the refresh token. Because the minimum schema strips refresh_token from real responses, this placeholder can be persisted over a real refresh token or stored when none was returned, making future OAuth refreshes impossible. It should preserve the previous refresh token or fail when a required refresh token is missing.

title: Google credential update stores SafeParse result instead of token data
body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod SafeParse result, but this code stores that entire result as the credential key. The saved key becomes { success: true, data: ... } rather than the credential object. Subsequent parsing of credential.key with googleCredentialSchema will fail, breaking Google Calendar token refresh for all modes. The code should store parseRefreshTokenResponse(...).data or change the helper to return data.

title: Sync path returns a fetch Response while callers expect provider-specific response objects
body: When sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT; otherwise it returns the provider refresh function's result. Callers are written for the provider result: Google expects res.data, HubSpot expects a token object with accessToken/expiresIn, and Zoho Bigin/CRM expect Axios responses with .data. With sync enabled these callers read undefined properties, throw, or save invalid credentials. The sync response must be normalized to the shape expected by each app.

title: prisma is used but not imported
body: The added credential update calls prisma.credential.update, but the file does not import prisma from @calcom/prisma. This will fail type checking or throw a ReferenceError at runtime when the Salesforce calendar service attempts to refresh credentials.

title: Salesforce client is created with stale access token after refresh
body: After fetching a new Salesforce access token, the code persists it but then constructs jsforce.Connection using credentialKey.access_token, which is the old token read before the refresh. If the old token is expired or rotated, the connection will not be authorized. Use the newly parsed access token when creating the connection.

title: Zoho Bigin sends credential ID as calcomUserId
body: refreshOAuthTokens's third parameter is used as the Cal.com user ID sent to the external sync endpoint. Bigin passes credentialId here, so the sync payload contains the credential row ID instead of the user ID. The external token provider will not be able to identify the correct user. Pass credential.userId (or store it in the service) instead.

title: Zoom refresh uses wrong app slug
body: The sync helper is called with appSlug 'zoomvideo', but the Zoom app credential is stored/identified by the slug 'zoom' (for example, the OAuth callback creates appId 'zoom'). The external sync endpoint will receive an unrecognized app slug and may return the wrong token or fail. Use 'zoom'.

title: Updating synced credential does not clear invalid flag
body: The webhook update path only updates key. If the existing credential has invalid: true from a previous failed refresh, the newly synced valid key remains marked invalid and may be skipped by adapters. The update should also set invalid: false when accepting new synced credentials.

title: Find-then-create/update credential is not atomic
body: The endpoint performs findFirst followed by create/update without a transaction or unique-constraint upsert. Concurrent webhook calls for the same user/app can both miss an existing credential and create duplicate credentials, or overwrite each other in an undefined order. This can cause stale or ambiguous OAuth credentials. Use atomic updateMany/create or a transaction with proper uniqueness.

title: Outbound credential sync request has no authentication or HTTPS enforcement
body: The outbound request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends only calcomUserId and appSlug and does not include a shared secret, signature, or client authentication. It also does not require HTTPS. If the endpoint is reachable outside a trusted internal network, it can be abused to obtain user tokens, and token responses may be exposed in transit. Add authentication/signing and enforce HTTPS.

title: Webhook handler accepts all HTTP methods
body: The handler does not check req.method. A GET or other non-POST request will still execute the webhook logic and likely throw during body parsing, returning a 500 instead of a 405. Restrict the route to POST.

title: Salesforce client refreshes token unconditionally
body: getClient always calls the Salesforce OAuth token endpoint before creating a connection, even if the stored access token has not expired. This creates unnecessary refresh requests and can cause rate limiting or latency. Check the token expiry and refresh only when needed.

title: No automated tests for credential sync webhook
body: This adds a security-sensitive webhook that can create/replace OAuth credentials and changes token refresh flows across many apps, but no automated tests are included for authentication, encryption/decryption, invalid payloads, duplicate handling, or sync-enabled refresh behavior. Without tests these regressions are easy to reintroduce.

title: Team admin/owner authorization check uses AND instead of OR
body: In addGuestsHandler, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. The name and permission intent are admin OR owner, but the code requires the user to satisfy both checks. Depending on how the role queries treat OWNER/ADMIN, legitimate team admins (and possibly owners) will be denied access to add guests. Replace `&&` with `||`.

title: Calendar update uses requester's credentials instead of booking owner's credentials
body: addGuestsHandler constructs EventManager with `ctx.user` and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`, even though the mutation is allowed for attendees and team admins/owners. External calendar events are normally owned by the booking organizer/host, so using the requester's credentials can fail to update the correct calendar or update nothing. The handler loads `booking.user.credentials` but does not use them. Use the booking owner/host (or the credentials associated with the destination calendar) for the calendar update.

title: No booking status check before adding guests
body: After loading the booking, addGuestsHandler only checks existence and permissions. It does not reject cancelled, rejected, or otherwise inactive bookings. The API can therefore add attendees to cancelled or past bookings, send notification emails, and attempt calendar updates for events that should no longer be modified. Add a status/eligibility check (for example, only upcoming accepted bookings unless intentionally broader).

title: Guest emails are not normalized or deduplicated server-side
body: In addGuestsHandler, `uniqueGuests` filters input emails case-sensitively and does not remove duplicates within the request. As a result, `guests: ["a@example.com", "A@Example.com"]` or repeated emails can create duplicate attendee rows or bypass the existing-attendee check. The blacklist comparison is also case-sensitive because only the blacklist is lowercased, so `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` can be bypassed with uppercase input. Normalize (trim/lowercase) and deduplicate guest emails before comparing, persisting, and sending emails.

title: Email dispatch receives original guests instead of actually added guests
body: addGuestsHandler calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` after filtering to `uniqueGuests`. `sendAddGuestsEmails` uses the supplied list to decide whether an attendee receives the new-guest invitation or the existing-attendee notification. If the original `guests` array contains duplicates, blacklisted emails, existing attendee emails, or case variants, the wrong email template can be sent (for example, an existing attendee may be treated as a new guest). Pass the normalized `uniqueGuests` list that was actually inserted.

title: Bookings without a user crash when looking up organizer
body: addGuestsHandler does `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. For bookings where `userId` is null (possible for some team bookings), this queries user id 0 and throws, producing an error instead of handling the team/organizer case. The handler should support bookings without a direct user or fall back to the appropriate team/primary email.

title: Add-guests emails ignore event-type email disable settings
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails` sends organizer/host and attendee emails unconditionally. Other email flows accept `eventTypeMetadata` and check `eventTypeDisableHostEmail`/`eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail`, respecting `disableStandardEmails` settings. This new flow does not, so emails can be sent even when the event type is configured to suppress host or attendee standard emails. Pass and honor event-type metadata.

title: Guests array is unbounded
body: The mutation schema allows `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no maximum length or minimum count. A client can submit an arbitrarily large number of emails, causing bulk attendee creation and mass email fan-out. Add a reasonable `.min(1).max(N)` and server-side uniqueness validation.

title: Error toast fallback is unreachable
body: In AddGuestsDialog, `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` always produces a non-empty string, so `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), ...)` never uses the fallback. If `err.data?.code` or `err.message` is missing, users may see `undefined: ...` instead of a friendly message. Build the message conditionally.

title: Dialog state is not consistently reset when closed
body: AddGuestsDialog resets `multiEmailValue` only on cancel or successful mutation, and does not reset `isInvalidEmail` on success. Closing via `onOpenChange` (for example, Escape or overlay click) leaves previous emails and validation errors in state, so reopening can show stale values or stale invalid-email warnings. Reset form state whenever the dialog closes or opens.

title: Hardcoded English tooltip in MultiEmail
body: The remove-email control uses `<Tooltip content="Remove email">`, which is not localized through `t()`. Users in non-English locales will see English text. Use a translation key.

title: No tests for new addGuests mutation
body: The PR introduces a privileged mutation with nontrivial permission checks, guest deduplication/case handling, blacklist filtering, calendar updates, and email selection, but no automated tests are included. Maintainers would want coverage for organizer/attendee/team admin permissions, cancelled bookings, duplicate/case-variant emails, blacklisted emails, and the email template selection.

title: Duplicate guest emails in a single request are inserted
body: The handler filters incoming guests only against existing booking attendees and does not de-duplicate the request payload. Because the schema also does not enforce uniqueness, a request containing the same email twice will pass validation and create multiple attendee rows for the same booking, or cause a database constraint failure if one exists. This can corrupt attendee data and send duplicate emails. De-duplicate and normalize guests before creating attendees.

title: Email comparisons are case-sensitive and blacklist can be bypassed
body: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is lowercased, but incoming guest emails are not normalized before comparison. An uppercase variant of a blacklisted address can bypass the block. Existing attendee emails are also compared with strict equality, so User@example.com and user@example.com are treated as different addresses, allowing duplicate attendees. Normalize email addresses before comparing them to attendees, the blacklist, and before storing them.

title: No upper bound on number of guest emails
body: The guests array is unbounded. An authenticated user can submit a very large list of email addresses, causing a large createMany write and potentially triggering mass notification emails. Add a reasonable maximum length to the guests array.

title: Team permission check uses && instead of ||
body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed by combining isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, meaning a user must pass both checks. The name and intended behavior imply admin or owner should be allowed. As written, team admins who are not owners can be incorrectly rejected. Use a logical OR or a single role check that matches the intended permission.

title: Emails are sent using the unfiltered guest list
body: sendAddGuestsEmails receives the original guests input instead of uniqueGuests, the list of guests actually inserted. If the request includes an existing attendee email, that attendee may be treated as a new guest and receive a normal scheduled email instead of the add-guests notification. Duplicate inputs can also cause duplicate emails. Pass the normalized, de-duplicated list of newly added guests.

title: No booking status or time validation
body: The handler only checks whether the caller can access the booking; it does not check whether the booking is cancelled, rejected, or already in the past. The API can therefore add guests to bookings that should no longer be modified, sending emails and updating calendar events unnecessarily. Validate booking status and timing before allowing guests to be added.

title: Calendar update uses requester's credentials instead of booking owner's
body: EventManager is constructed with credentials for ctx.user, while the booking query already loads booking.user.credentials. If a team admin or attendee adds guests, the request may use credentials that do not own the target calendar event, causing calendar updates to fail or update the wrong calendar. Use the appropriate booking owner/host credentials for the calendar update.

title: Add-guests emails ignore email-disable settings
body: sendAddGuestsEmails always sends organizer, team-member, and attendee emails and does not accept or honor event-type email disabling metadata. Similar email flows check eventTypeDisableHostEmail and eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail. Event types configured to suppress standard emails will still send add-guest emails.

title: Organizer lookup throws for bookings without a user
body: The organizer lookup uses booking.userId || 0 with findFirstOrThrow. If a booking has no associated user, this queries user id 0 and throws an unhandled Prisma error instead of returning a controlled TRPC error. Handle missing booking owners explicitly.

title: Invalid-email error state is not reset
body: isInvalidEmail is set to true when client-side validation fails, but it is not cleared when the user edits the email list or when the mutation succeeds. After a failed validation followed by a successful submission, reopening the dialog can show a stale invalid-email error. Reset the flag on input changes and on successful submission.

title: Error fallback toast is unreachable
body: The error message is created with a template string, so it is always truthy even when err.data?.code or the translated message is missing. The fallback t("unable_to_add_guests") therefore never runs, and users may see messages like undefined: ... Build the message conditionally before showing the toast.

title: Hardcoded English tooltip
body: The remove-email tooltip uses the hardcoded string Remove email instead of a translated locale key. Non-English users will see untranslated text. Use the locale system for this label.

title: Unsafe access to first attendee
body: The organizer email subject accesses this.calEvent.attendees[0].name without checking that attendees exist. If the attendees array is empty, email rendering throws. Use optional chaining or a fallback value.

title: Team permission check requires admin and owner instead of either
body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...)). This requires the caller to satisfy both checks, so a team admin who is not an owner, or an owner who is not considered an admin by the first query, is denied even though the intended check is admin OR owner. Use || and avoid running both queries when there is no team.

title: Emails are sent for the original guest list instead of the guests actually added
body: sendAddGuestsEmails is called with input.guests instead of uniqueGuests. Emails are therefore decided using addresses that may not have been added, such as existing attendees, duplicates, or blacklisted addresses. In particular, an existing attendee included in the request will be treated as a new guest and receive AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the add-guests notification.

title: Guest email filtering is case-sensitive and blacklist can be bypassed
body: blacklistedGuestEmails is lowercased but incoming guest emails are not normalized, and duplicate detection uses strict equality. A blacklisted address or an existing attendee email can bypass the block/duplicate detection by using different casing or surrounding whitespace. Normalize and trim guest emails before comparing.

title: Read-then-create attendee update can create duplicates under concurrent requests
body: The handler reads existing attendees, filters guests, then creates attendees without a transaction, upsert, or guaranteed unique constraint. Two simultaneous addGuests calls with the same email can both pass the filter and create duplicate attendee rows, or cause unhandled database errors if a constraint exists.

title: Add-guests emails ignore standard email disable settings
body: sendAddGuestsEmails sends organizer and attendee emails unconditionally. Unlike other email helpers, it does not accept eventTypeMetadata or check eventTypeDisableHostEmail/eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail, so event types configured to disable standard emails will still emit add-guests emails.

title: Calendar update uses caller credentials instead of booking owner credentials
body: EventManager is constructed with ctx.user and credentials from getUsersCredentials(ctx.user), even when the caller is only an attendee or team admin. The handler fetches booking.user.credentials but never uses them, so calendar updates may fail or target the caller's calendar rather than the booking owner's destination calendar.

title: Guests can be added to cancelled or past bookings via API
body: After loading the booking, the handler does not check booking.status or whether the event has ended before inserting attendees, updating calendars, and sending emails. An authenticated organizer/attendee can call addGuests for cancelled or past bookings, causing inappropriate notifications and calendar updates.

title: No maximum limit on guests array
body: The guests field is an unbounded array of emails. An authenticated user could submit a very large list, causing bulk attendee creation, mass email sending, and calendar API load. Add a reasonable maximum array length.

title: Seated event types are not handled when adding guests
body: For event types using seatsPerTimeSlot, the handler creates plain attendee rows without checking remaining seats or creating seat references. This can exceed seat capacity and leave seated bookings in an inconsistent state.

title: Organizer lookup throws for bookings without a userId
body: The organizer lookup uses prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow with id: booking.userId || 0. If a booking can have a null userId, such as some team bookings, this queries user id 0 and throws, causing a 500 instead of handling the team/userPrimaryEmail case.

title: Error toast always prefixes undefined and never falls back
body: onError builds a message string from err.data?.code and err.message, then uses message || t('unable_to_add_guests'). When err.data?.code is absent, the message becomes 'undefined: ...' and is truthy, so the fallback is never shown. Build the message conditionally and provide a proper fallback.

title: Hardcoded English tooltip
body: The Tooltip content 'Remove email' is hardcoded instead of using the i18n t() function, so it will not be localized.

title: Retry cleanup deletes WorkflowReminders of any method
body: The deleteMany query uses OR with a second condition that only checks retryCount > 1. This deletes every WorkflowReminder row with retryCount > 1, not just unscheduled SMS reminders. Since retryCount is on the shared WorkflowReminder table, EMAIL/WHATSAPP reminders or scheduled SMS rows that ever have retryCount > 1 can be deleted. Scope the retry cleanup to method: WorkflowMethods.SMS and likely scheduled: false.

title: Retry count is incremented from a stale value
body: Both failure paths (lines 184 and 195) set retryCount to reminder.retryCount + 1 using the value read before the SMS attempt. If two cron executions process the same reminder, or if the row is updated between the read and write, increments can be lost or applied incorrectly, preventing deletion after two failures. Use Prisma's atomic increment and guard the update for unscheduled reminders.

title: Retry update in catch can abort the whole cron handler
body: The catch block awaits prisma.workflowReminder.update to increment retryCount. If that update fails, for example because the reminder was deleted after the initial findMany or due to a DB error, the exception is not caught and will terminate the loop, leaving remaining reminders unprocessed. The same applies to the failure-path update. Use updateMany or wrap the retry increment in its own try/catch and ignore not-found errors.

title: No tests for the new retry/deletion behavior
body: The PR introduces a retry counter and deletes reminders after repeated SMS scheduling failures, but no automated tests verify that retryCount is incremented on failure, that reminders are deleted only after the intended number of failures, and that non-SMS reminders are unaffected. This logic is prone to regressions.

title: Retry-count cleanup deletes workflow reminders outside the intended SMS failure scope
body: The deleteMany query deletes any WorkflowReminder with retryCount greater than 1 because the second OR branch is not scoped to method: WorkflowMethods.SMS or scheduled: false. This can remove EMAIL or WHATSAPP reminders, or an SMS reminder already marked scheduled with a referenceId, if retryCount ever exceeds 1. That can cause unintended data loss and orphaned provider messages. The branch should be limited to unscheduled SMS reminders, e.g. { method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, scheduled: false, retryCount: { gt: 1 } }.

title: retryCount is incremented from a stale read instead of atomically
body: Both failure paths set retryCount to reminder.retryCount + 1 using the value read before the scheduling attempt. If two cron executions overlap, or the row is updated between the read and write, increments can be lost or overwritten. This can cause more than two attempts, premature deletion, or incorrect cleanup state. Use Prisma's atomic update, e.g. data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } }.

title: Unsendable reminders with no message or recipient never increment retryCount
body: If message is empty or sendTo is falsy, the reminder is skipped without incrementing retryCount, marking it scheduled/cancelled, or deleting it. A permanently unsendable reminder, such as one with a missing phone number, will be fetched and skipped on every cron run until scheduledDate passes, bypassing the intended delete-after-two-failures behavior. This case should increment retryCount or explicitly cancel/delete the reminder.

title: Error handler can throw while trying to increment retryCount
body: In the catch block, the retryCount update is not protected from failure. If the reminder was deleted concurrently or the update otherwise fails, the update error masks the original scheduling error and aborts processing of the remaining reminders. Using updateMany or wrapping the retry-count update in its own try/catch would make the cron job more resilient.

title: Retry-count cleanup is not limited to SMS reminders
body: The deleteMany query uses an OR branch with a bare `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` condition. That condition is not scoped to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`, so this SMS cron job can delete any WorkflowReminder row (including EMAIL or WHATSAPP reminders) once its retryCount exceeds 1. The retry-based deletion should be scoped to SMS reminders, and likely to unscheduled SMS reminders, to avoid deleting unrelated reminder rows.

title: Reminders with no message or no sendTo never increment retryCount
body: When `message` is empty or `sendTo` is falsy, the code skips the SMS scheduling call but does not update `retryCount`, mark the reminder as failed, or delete it.
