Such reminders remain `scheduled: false` and will be selected again on every cron run until their scheduledDate passes. This preserves the endless retry behavior for bad/missing data that the PR is trying to avoid; these cases should also count as failures or be handled explicitly.

title: retryCount is updated using a stale read instead of an atomic increment
body: Both failure paths update with `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`, using the value read before the scheduling attempt. If two cron executions overlap or the same reminder is processed concurrently, both may read the same retryCount and write the same incremented value, losing a retry count. Using Prisma's atomic `{ increment: 1 }` would make the retry limit reliable. This also applies to the catch block update at line 195.

title: Update inside catch can throw and abort processing of remaining reminders
body: The catch block awaits `prisma.workflowReminder.update` to increment retryCount, but this update is not wrapped in error handling. If the reminder was deleted between the initial `findMany` and this update (for example due to booking cancellation or concurrent cleanup), or if the update otherwise fails, the new exception escapes the catch block and stops the loop. That can prevent the remaining unscheduled reminders from being processed and cause the endpoint to return a 500. Using `updateMany`, ignoring not-found errors, or wrapping this update in its own try/catch would be safer.

title: Any exception is treated as an SMS scheduling failure, including failures after Twilio scheduling
body: The catch block increments retryCount for every error, including errors thrown by the database update after `twilio.scheduleSMS` has already succeeded. In that case the Twilio scheduled message exists, but `scheduled` and `referenceId` may not be persisted, so the reminder remains unscheduled in the database and may be scheduled again on a later run. Repeated failures can also delete the WorkflowReminder while an externally scheduled SMS still exists. Consider distinguishing provider failures from persistence failures and handling/cleaning up the external scheduled message when the DB update fails.

title: Authorization OR fragment can be returned without enclosing parentheses
body: buildOrgAuthorizationCondition and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition may produce SQL shaped like (A) OR (B), but getBaseConditions returns authConditions unchanged when there is no filter condition. If a caller composes this fragment with additional predicates, for example WHERE ${baseConditions} AND another_condition, SQL precedence makes the added predicate apply only to the last OR branch, potentially returning rows outside the authorized set. The exposed condition should always be wrapped in parentheses, or the builders should return parenthesized fragments.

title: Org scope excludes direct org members' individual bookings when there are no child teams
body: buildOrgAuthorizationCondition only fetches member user IDs when teamsFromOrg.length > 0. If an organization has no child teams, teamIds still contains the org ID and direct org memberships can exist, but the generated condition only matches team bookings (teamId = ANY([orgId]) AND isTeamBooking = true). Individual bookings of org members (isTeamBooking = false) are omitted. Memberships should be fetched for [orgId, ...childTeamIds] regardless of whether child teams exist.

title: Member enumeration for raw authorization does not explicitly filter accepted memberships
body: isOrgOwnerOrAdmin checks membership.accepted, but buildOrgAuthorizationCondition and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition call MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds without an accepted filter. If that repository method can return pending or invited memberships, their user IDs are included in the userId = ANY(...) condition and their individual bookings become visible in org/team insights. Add an explicit accepted filter or ensure the repository guarantees it.

title: Org-scope expectation depends on unspecified ordering of repository results
body: The test expects exact arrays inside ANY(...) in a specific order, but the service builds those arrays from findAllByParentId and findAllByTeamIds without explicit ordering. If the database returns teams or memberships in a different order, the Prisma.sql values differ and the test fails even though the SQL is semantically the same. Sort IDs deterministically in the service or make the assertion order-independent.

title: No integration test executes the org/team ANY raw SQL paths
body: The only $queryRaw integration test uses user scope, which generates simple equality predicates. The org/team authorization conditions that use = ANY(${array}) are only compared as Prisma.sql objects and never run against the database. This leaves array parameter binding and the actual row-filtering behavior of the high-risk org/team scopes unverified. Add integration tests that execute org/team base conditions and assert included and excluded rows.

title: Public findMany API removed without replacement or caller updates
body: The diff deletes findMany and changes the public condition methods from returning Prisma where-input objects to returning raw Prisma.Sql fragments. Any existing caller that used InsightsBookingService.findMany or composed the old where objects will break. Since no consumer files are updated in this PR, confirm the service is unused elsewhere or update callers or provide a compatibility adapter before merging.

title: getBaseConditions may return an unwrapped top-level OR predicate
body: When only authorization conditions exist, getBaseConditions returns authConditions as-is. For org and team scopes, the generated authorization SQL is a top-level OR expression. If a caller composes this fragment with additional SQL using AND, such as `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND ...`, SQL operator precedence will bind the added condition only to the right-hand OR branch, producing incorrect filtering and potentially bypassing added restrictions. The returned base condition should always be parenthesized as a single boolean expression.

title: Exact SQL array assertions depend on nondeterministic DB ordering
body: The org-scope test compares generated Prisma.sql fragments against exact arrays of team IDs and user IDs. The service builds those arrays from TeamRepository.findAllByParentId and MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds without enforcing an ORDER BY or sorting the IDs afterward. PostgreSQL does not guarantee row order without ORDER BY, so these tests can pass or fail nondeterministically. Sort the IDs in the service before constructing the SQL, or assert order-insensitively.

title: Org scope skips member lookup when the org has no child teams
body: buildOrgAuthorizationCondition only queries memberships when teamsFromOrg.length > 0. However, teamIds always includes options.orgId, and an organization can have direct memberships even if it has no child teams. In that case userIdsFromOrg is forced to an empty array, so the generated condition only matches team bookings and excludes all non-team bookings for org users. The membership lookup should not be gated on the existence of child teams.

title: No integration test executes the org/team ANY(array) authorization conditions
body: The only raw-query integration test exercises a user-scope condition with simple equality filters. The org/team authorization paths, which rely on `teamId = ANY(...)` and `userId = ANY(...)`, are only asserted by structural Prisma.sql equality. If the array binding or generated SQL is invalid at runtime, the current tests will not catch it. Add an integration test that executes an org/team base condition against seeded bookings.

title: Public findMany method removed, breaking existing callers
body: The diff removes `InsightsBookingService.findMany` and replaces it with `getBaseConditions`, which only returns a raw SQL fragment. Any code that currently calls `service.findMany(...)` will fail to compile or throw at runtime. Since the PR only updates the service and its tests, callers need to be updated or a compatible query method needs to remain.

title: Org scope skips org memberships when there are no child teams
body: `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` always includes `orgId` in `teamIds`, but it only fetches memberships when `teamsFromOrg.length > 0`. For an organization that has direct members but no child teams, `userIdsFromOrg` becomes empty, so the generated condition omits the `userId = ANY(...) AND "isTeamBooking" = false` branch and excludes non-team bookings for org members. Fetch memberships for `teamIds` unconditionally.

title: SQL fragment assertions depend on array order and internal representation
body: The org-scope test compares the returned `Prisma.Sql` fragment with a literal fragment containing exact `teamIds` and `userIds` arrays. The service builds those arrays from repository queries that do not show explicit ordering, and it composes fragments with `reduce`. If rows are returned in a different order, or if Prisma represents composed fragments differently, the test can fail even though the SQL condition is semantically correct. Normalize the SQL text/values or sort/compare IDs unordered.

title: Condition caching can trigger duplicate concurrent DB queries
body: `getAuthorizationConditions` checks `this.cachedAuthConditions === undefined` and then awaits `buildAuthorizationConditions()`. If multiple callers invoke it before the first build completes, all see the cache as undefined and issue duplicate membership/team queries. Cache the in-flight promise if this service can be called concurrently.

title: Delete cache mutation does not refresh connected calendars query
body: The deleteCache mutation only shows a toast and calls onSuccess. It does not invalidate or refetch trpc.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars, which is the query supplying cacheUpdatedAt to this component. After a successful cache deletion, the UI can continue showing the old cache status until some other refetch happens. The disconnect mutation already invalidates related queries; deleteCache should do the same.

title: Cache status includes expired CalendarCache rows
body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds returns the max updatedAt for all CalendarCache rows for a credential, without filtering expiresAt >= now(). Other cache-read paths ignore expired rows. This can make the UI display a cache status and delete action for expired/stale cache entries that would not actually be served.

title: deleteCache authorization only allows directly owned credentials
body: The handler checks credential ownership with { id: credentialId, userId: user.id }. Connected calendars can include delegation/team/service-account style credentials, and the UI explicitly handles delegationCredentialId. If a visible credential is not directly owned by the session user, the UI may show 'Delete cached data' but the mutation will fail. The authorization check should match the access model used to expose the credential, or the UI should hide the action when deletion is not permitted.

title: dev:cron uses npx tsx without adding tsx as a dependency
body: The script uses 'npx tsx cron-tester.ts', but tsx is not present in dependencies or devDependencies. npx may download tsx on demand, causing nondeterministic versions, network dependence, and failures in offline or restricted environments. Add tsx as a devDependency or use the already available ts-node.

title: Attempting to touch SelectedCalendar.updatedAt with an empty updateMany
body: SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) is used to update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt. An empty data object is fragile: depending on Prisma behavior it may be a no-op or may not reliably update @updatedAt for updateMany. If the intent is to touch records, pass an explicit update such as { updatedAt: new Date() }.

title: UserWithCalendars now requires additional selected-calendar fields
body: The exported UserWithCalendars type now requires updatedAt and googleChannelId on allSelectedCalendars and userLevelSelectedCalendars entries. This is a potentially breaking change for consumers of this exported/legacy type that construct or mock these objects, especially if they do not have these fields. If the fields are required by downstream code, this should be documented and call sites updated; otherwise consider keeping them optional.

title: No automated tests for deleteCache authorization or cache status aggregation
body: The PR introduces a destructive deleteCache mutation and a new cache-status aggregation method, but no unit/integration tests are included. Tests should cover at least: authorized deletion, rejection for another user's credential, correct getCacheStatusByCredentialIds behavior for multiple/expired cache rows, and connectedCalendars enrichment.

title: Hardcoded en-US date format ignores user locale
body: The cache timestamp is formatted with new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', ...). This always renders US English formatting even when the user has another locale. Use the active app locale or the user's locale instead of hardcoding en-US.

title: Credential lookup fetches full credential row unnecessarily
body: prisma.credential.findFirst is called without a select, retrieving the entire credential record including encrypted secrets, only to check existence/ownership. Use select: { id: true } or select only the fields needed for authorization to avoid loading sensitive credential material into memory.

title: Authorization failure throws generic Error instead of TRPCError
body: Throwing a plain Error for a missing or unauthorized credential produces a generic/internal tRPC error. Use TRPCError with NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN so clients can distinguish authorization failures from unexpected server errors.

title: connectedCalendars handler bypasses CalendarCache initialization/mock
body: The handler instantiates CalendarCacheRepository directly, while other cache read paths use CalendarCache.init(...), which can return a mock/no-op implementation when calendar-cache is disabled. If that gating is intentional, this handler can still expose DB-backed cache status even when calendar-cache functionality is disabled. Use the same factory or make the direct DB access intentional and documented.

title: updateManyByCredentialId accepts overly broad Prisma update type
body: The method types data as Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput, which can include relational nested updates. prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany only supports scalar/mutation update fields. Use Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput or a narrower type to prevent invalid callers from compiling or failing at runtime.

title: Actions container renders even when dropdown is hidden
body: The wrapper always renders <div className="flex w-32 justify-end"> around CredentialActionsDropdown. When the dropdown returns null, such as for a delegation credential with no cache or when connection modification is disabled, this still reserves layout space and may misalign cards/alerts. Render the actions container only when an action is actually visible.

title: sed -i '' is macOS/BSD-specific
body: The script uses sed -i '' -E, which fails on GNU/Linux because GNU sed treats '' as a backup suffix/file argument. If the script is intended to be cross-platform, use a portable in-place editing approach or detect the platform.

title: ENV_FILE relative path depends on current working directory
body: ENV_FILE="../.env" assumes the script is run from the scripts directory. If run from the repository root or another directory, it may create or modify the wrong .env file. Derive the path from the script location or use a repository-root-relative path.

title: Delete-cache mutation does not refresh connected calendars
body: The deleteCache mutation only shows a toast and calls the optional onSuccess callback. It does not invalidate or refetch viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars, unlike the disconnect mutation. Since SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper displays cache status from that query and may not provide an onChanged handler that invalidates it, the UI can keep showing the old cache status and timestamp after cache deletion succeeds.

title: Cache status includes expired CalendarCache rows
body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds returns the maximum updatedAt for CalendarCache rows without filtering by expiresAt, while getCachedAvailability only treats rows with expiresAt >= now as valid. As a result, connectedCalendars can report cacheUpdatedAt and show cache actions for credentials whose cache entries are expired, misleading users about whether valid cached data exists.

title: Disabled scope is not propagated to credential actions
body: The wrapper computes shouldDisableConnectionModification as isDisabled || disableConnectionModification, but ConnectedCalendarList receives only disableConnectionModification. When disabledScope matches the current scope, calendar switches are disabled, but CredentialActionsDropdown can still allow deleting cache or disconnecting the integration, defeating the disabled-scope restriction.

title: Cache timestamp is formatted with hardcoded en-US locale
body: The cache last-updated timestamp is formatted using Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US') regardless of the user's locale. This ignores localized date preferences and can show an English/US-formatted timestamp to non-English users.

title: Empty actions container is rendered when dropdown is hidden
body: The actions prop always renders a fixed-width div around CredentialActionsDropdown. When the dropdown returns null, such as for delegation credentials with no cache or when connection modification is disabled, the empty container remains and creates unnecessary blank space in the list item or alert action area.

title: Authorization failure throws generic Error instead of TRPCError
body: deleteCacheHandler throws a plain Error when the credential is missing or not owned by the current user. This will be surfaced/logged as an internal server error rather than an explicit tRPC FORBIDDEN or NOT_FOUND error, making client error handling and observability less accurate.

title: Webhook helper script uses macOS-only sed and fragile relative env path
body: The script uses sed -i '' which is BSD/macOS syntax and will fail on GNU/Linux. It also writes to ../.env relative to the current working directory rather than the script location, so running it from the repository root or another directory can modify the wrong file or create an unexpected .env file.

title: dev:cron uses npx tsx without declaring tsx
body: The dev:cron script was changed to npx tsx cron-tester.ts, but tsx is not listed as a devDependency. npx may download or prompt to install tsx at runtime, making the script network-dependent and less reproducible across environments.

title: No automated tests for cache deletion authorization/status
body: There are no automated tests for the new deleteCache handler's ownership check, the cache deletion behavior, or the connectedCalendars cache-status enrichment. These paths affect authorization and user-visible data, and regressions could go unnoticed without coverage.

title: Cache status includes expired CalendarCache rows
body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups CalendarCache rows only by credentialId and does not filter on expiresAt, while getCachedAvailability only treats rows with expiresAt >= now as valid. As a result, the connected-calendars API can report a cacheUpdatedAt timestamp for a credential whose cache entries are all expired, causing the UI to show stale cache status and offer delete actions based on invalid data. Add an expiresAt: { gte: new Date() } condition or otherwise exclude expired rows.

title: Handler bypasses calendar-cache factory/mock
body: connectedCalendarsHandler directly instantiates CalendarCacheRepository instead of using the cache initialization path used elsewhere, which can select a mock or disabled behavior for calendar cache. This can query the real CalendarCache table and expose cache status even in environments or feature configurations where calendar caching is supposed to be disabled or mocked, and it makes tests that rely on the mock ineffective. Use the same cache factory/abstraction used by the rest of the calendar-cache code.

title: Delete-cache mutation does not refresh connected calendars data
body: The deleteCache mutation only calls the optional onSuccess prop after success; it does not invalidate trpc.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars, unlike the disconnect mutation. If the parent does not provide an onChanged handler that invalidates or refetches, the UI will continue to display the old cacheUpdatedAt value after cache deletion. Invalidate the connected-calendars query in onSuccess or onSettled.

title: Empty updateMany payload may not update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt
body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) to bump SelectedCalendar.updatedAt. Passing an empty data object relies on Prisma implicitly updating timestamps and may be treated as a no-op or be fragile across Prisma versions, making the timestamp update unreliable. If this operation fails or does nothing, the intended updatedAt refresh will not happen. Use an explicit update such as { updatedAt: new Date() }.

title: Empty actions container rendered when dropdown has no items
body: ConnectedCalendarList always wraps CredentialActionsDropdown in a div with fixed width and right alignment. When the dropdown returns null, for example for delegation credentials with no cache status, the empty container still occupies layout space in the card or alert actions area. Render the wrapper conditionally or move the container inside CredentialActionsDropdown so it can return nothing without leaving an empty spacer.

title: Cache timestamp is formatted with hardcoded en-US locale
body: The dropdown formats cacheUpdatedAt with Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', ...), ignoring the user's locale from useLocale. Users in other locales will see a US-formatted date/time in an otherwise localized UI. Use the active locale or i18n language when constructing Intl.DateTimeFormat.

title: Generic Error thrown for authorization or not-found case
body: deleteCacheHandler throws a plain Error('Credential not found or access denied') when the credential is missing or not owned by the user. tRPC will generally surface this as an internal error rather than a semantic FORBIDDEN or NOT_FOUND response, and it may create unnecessary server error logs. Throw a TRPCError with an appropriate code instead.

title: credentialId schema accepts any number
body: The deleteCache input uses z.number() for credentialId, which allows negative, zero, and non-integer values. Credential IDs are positive integers, so use z.number().int().positive() to reject invalid input early.

title: Webhook helper script uses BSD/macOS-only sed syntax
body: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh runs sed -i '' -E ..., which is BSD/macOS syntax and is not portable to GNU sed on Linux. On Linux this can fail or create unintended backup files, preventing the script from updating GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL. Use a portable in-place edit strategy and consider resolving ../.env relative to the script location rather than the current working directory.

title: dev:cron depends on npx tsx without declaring tsx
body: The dev:cron script now invokes npx tsx cron-tester.ts, but tsx is not declared as a dependency or devDependency. npx may download it on demand or prompt interactively, making the script network-dependent and less reproducible. Add tsx to devDependencies or use an already installed runner such as ts-node.

title: Reschedule cancellation bypasses the new cancelled-state fallback
body: handleNewBooking cancels reminders from the original booking with immediateDelete = true. That path in deleteScheduledEmailReminder only calls SendGrid and neither sets WorkflowReminder.cancelled nor deletes the local reminder. If the SendGrid cancellation fails (for example because of the pending-cancellation limit this PR addresses), there is no cron fallback and the old reminder can still be sent for a rescheduled booking. The promise is also not awaited.

title: immediateDelete leaves the WorkflowReminder unchanged
body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder's immediateDelete branch returns after the SendGrid request without updating or deleting the WorkflowReminder row. Callers that do not cascade-delete the reminder (for example the reschedule path) leave a stale scheduled reminder, and if the external cancellation fails there is no state that can be retried or cleaned up by the cron job.

title: Paid booking cancellation skips workflow reminder cancellation
body: In the paid booking branch the handler returns before reaching the workflow reminder cancellation loop. Canceled/refunded paid bookings therefore do not cancel scheduled workflow emails or SMS, so reminders can still be sent.

title: Reminder cancellations are fire-and-forget
body: The reminder cancellation loop calls async deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder inside forEach without awaiting them. The request can finish before the database updates or external cancellations complete, which is especially risky in serverless environments; cancellations may be lost and reminders may still be sent.

title: Reschedule request does not await reminder cancellations
body: requestReschedule calls async deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder inside forEach without awaiting them. The mutation can return before cancellations complete, so if the environment terminates work after the response or a call fails, old reminders may remain and be sent.

title: Workflow deletion does not await external reminder cancellations
body: When deleting a workflow, scheduled reminder cancellations are started in a forEach and not awaited before workflow.deleteMany runs. Cascade deletion can remove the reminder rows and the request can end before the SendGrid/Twilio cancellation completes; if the external cancel fails, scheduled messages for a deleted workflow may still be sent.

title: A single failing SendGrid cancel aborts cancellation of all cancelled reminders
body: The cron cancellation loop awaits each SendGrid cancellation inside a single try/catch. If any reminder fails (null or invalid referenceId, SendGrid error, rate limit, etc.), control jumps to the catch and the remaining cancelled reminders are not canceled or deleted. Because the failing reminder remains in the table, subsequent runs can repeatedly stop at the same reminder, leaving other emails to be sent.

title: Delayed cron cancellation leaves a race window where emails can still be sent
body: Cancellations are only processed by a cron job every 15 minutes. If a booking is canceled shortly after a cron run and a reminder is scheduled to send before the next run, the reminder will still be sent. This leaves a last-minute cancellation race even though the booking is canceled.

title: SMS cancellation has no fallback when Twilio cancel fails
body: deleteScheduledSMSReminder only deletes the reminder after a successful Twilio cancellation. If twilio.cancelSMS throws, the error is logged and the reminder remains scheduled, and there is no cancelled flag or cron retry for SMS. A transient Twilio failure can therefore cause SMS reminders for canceled or rescheduled bookings to be sent.

title: Cancel query does not filter by EMAIL or non-null referenceId
body: The query for reminders to cancel does not restrict to EMAIL reminders or require a non-null referenceId. If a SMS reminder or a reminder with a null referenceId ever has cancelled = true, the code will pass that referenceId to SendGrid, likely causing an error that aborts the cancellation loop.

title: Workflow update ignores asynchronous reminder maintenance
body: The workflow update mutation starts asynchronous reminder cancellation and creation in map/forEach callbacks without awaiting them. The mutation can return before those operations finish, causing inconsistent reminder state, silent failures, and unhandled promise rejections.

title: Paid cancellation path skips the new workflow-reminder cancellation logic
body: The paid/refund branch returns before the code that cancels workflow reminders runs. For paid bookings that are cancelled or rejected, WorkflowReminder rows are left active, so scheduled workflow emails or SMS can still be sent despite the booking no longer occurring.

title: Workflow reminder cancellations are fire-and-forget during booking cancellation
body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are async, but they are called inside forEach without awaiting their promises or adding them to the awaited promise list. In serverless or Next.js API-route execution, the response can complete and execution can be terminated before the cancellation writes or provider calls finish, leaving reminders active.

title: Reschedule cancels old workflow reminders without awaiting the async operations
body: When handling a reschedule, the original booking's workflow reminders are cancelled inside a forEach loop, but the returned promises are not awaited. The booking request can finish before the reminder cancellations are persisted or accepted by the email/SMS providers, so old reminders may remain scheduled and be sent.

title: Cancelled-reminder query does not restrict rows to scheduled email reminders with a reference ID
body: The remindersToCancel query filters only by cancelled=true and scheduledDate. It does not require method=EMAIL, scheduled=true, or referenceId not null. The subsequent SendGrid cancellation request uses reminder.referenceId as batch_id, so a non-email row or a row with a null reference ID can cause the API call to fail and interfere with cancellation of valid reminders.

title: A single SendGrid failure aborts cancellation of all remaining cancelled reminders
body: The SendGrid cancellation request is inside a for loop wrapped by a single try/catch. If one request throws, such as from an invalid batch ID, rate limit, or provider error, the loop stops and the remaining cancelled reminders are neither cancelled in SendGrid nor deleted from the database. Those reminders may still be sent.

title: Unscheduled reminders are scheduled without checking booking status or cancellation state
body: The unscheduledReminders query selects email reminders only by method, scheduled=false, and scheduledDate. It does not exclude cancelled reminders or verify that the associated booking is still accepted. If a cancellation write races, fails, or leaves a stale row, the cron job can schedule and send reminders for cancelled or rescheduled bookings.

title: immediateDelete cancels SendGrid but does not persist cancellation state
body: When immediateDelete is true and a referenceId exists, deleteScheduledEmailReminder only sends a cancellation request to SendGrid and returns. It does not delete the WorkflowReminder row or set cancelled=true. If the SendGrid request fails or is rejected, there is no durable cancellation state or retry path, and the reminder can still be sent. This also leaves stale reminder rows for rescheduled bookings.

title: Deferred email cancellation can miss reminders that are due before the next cron run
body: For non-immediate cancellations, the function only sets cancelled=true and relies on the scheduleEmailReminders cron job to cancel the SendGrid email. Because the cron runs periodically, a reminder whose scheduled date occurs before the next cron execution can still be sent even though the booking was cancelled or rescheduled.

title: SMS cancellation failure leaves no retry path
body: deleteScheduledSMSReminder attempts to cancel the Twilio SMS before deleting the WorkflowReminder row. If the Twilio cancellation throws, the error is logged but the row remains without a cancelled state or retry mechanism. The scheduled SMS may still be sent, and no cron job will attempt to cancel it again.

title: Request-reschedule cancels workflow reminders without awaiting async operations
body: In requestReschedule, deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called inside forEach without awaiting the promises. The mutation can return before cancellation writes or provider calls complete, so reminders for the old booking may remain active and be sent.

title: Workflow update cancels removed-eventType reminders without awaiting them
body: When a workflow is removed from event types, the code calls async deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder inside forEach but does not await the promises. The update mutation can return before the reminders are marked cancelled or deleted, especially in serverless environments, so removed workflow reminders may still be sent.

title: Workflow reminder cancellations are not awaited when cancelling bookings
body: In handleCancelBooking, deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called inside forEach loops without collecting or awaiting their promises. The handler then continues and returns. In Next.js/serverless execution the process may be frozen after the response, so the database update marking email reminders as cancelled or the SMS cancellation may never complete. This can leave reminders active for cancelled bookings and cause emails/SMS to still be sent.

title: Paid booking cancellation path skips workflow reminder cancellation
body: When bookingToDelete.paid is true, handleCancelBooking refunds the payment and returns before reaching the code that cancels scheduled jobs and workflow reminders. As a result, paid bookings that are rejected/cancelled do not have their workflow reminders cancelled, so reminder emails or SMS can still be sent for these bookings.

title: Reschedule path uses immediateDelete but leaves old email reminder rows active
body: When rescheduling, old email reminders are cancelled with immediateDelete=true. deleteScheduledEmailReminder's immediate path only calls SendGrid and does not delete the WorkflowReminder row or set cancelled=true. Since the original booking is not deleted, the old reminder row remains scheduled=true and cancelled=false. If the SendGrid cancellation fails or the un-awaited call does not finish, there is no database state to retry or prevent the old reminder from being sent.

title: Cron cancellation query does not restrict to valid scheduled email reminders
body: The remindersToCancel query selects all WorkflowReminder rows with cancelled=true but does not filter by method=EMAIL, scheduled=true, or referenceId non-null. The code then posts reminder.referenceId to SendGrid as batch_id. Any SMS reminder or email reminder with a null referenceId in this state will cause an invalid SendGrid request, which can abort the cancellation loop for all reminders.

title: One failed cancellation aborts processing of all remaining cancelled reminders
body: The SendGrid cancellation loop is wrapped in a single try/catch. If any one client.request or delete fails, execution jumps to the catch block and the remaining cancelled reminders are neither cancelled in SendGrid nor deleted from the database. The endpoint then continues and may return success. A single bad or stale reminder can therefore block cancellation of all cancelled workflow emails on every cron run.

title: Unscheduled reminder query does not exclude cancelled reminders
body: The unscheduledReminders query filters only on method=EMAIL and scheduled=false; it does not exclude rows where cancelled=true. If a reminder ever reaches this state due to a race condition, manual data correction, or future code change, the cron will schedule and send an email for a cancelled booking. The query should exclude cancelled=true rows.

title: immediateDelete cancels SendGrid but does not delete or mark the reminder record
body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder's immediateDelete branch cancels the SendGrid scheduled send but returns without deleting the WorkflowReminder row or setting cancelled=true. Only callers that immediately cascade-delete the reminder can tolerate this, and even there the call is not awaited. For callers such as rescheduling, this leaves stale scheduled reminder rows and removes any ability to retry a failed cancellation.

title: Deferred cancellation can still send imminent reminders
body: For non-immediate cancellations, deleteScheduledEmailReminder only sets cancelled=true, while the cron job cancels SendGrid emails only when the scheduled date is within the next hour and runs every 15 minutes. If a booking is cancelled shortly before a reminder is due, for example a few minutes before sending, the reminder may be sent before the cron job performs the SendGrid cancellation. Near-term reminders should be cancelled synchronously or immediately.

title: requestReschedule does not await reminder cancellation
body: In the requestReschedule mutation, deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called inside a forEach loop without awaiting the promises. The mutation can return before the email reminders are marked cancelled or SMS cancellations complete, so old reminders for a rescheduled booking may still be sent.

title: Workflow deletion cancels external scheduled messages without awaiting them
body: When deleting a workflow, scheduled reminders are cancelled with async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder calls inside forEach, and then the workflow is deleted without awaiting those operations. Because deleting the workflow cascades to reminder rows, if the external SendGrid/Twilio cancellation does not finish or fails, no database record remains to retry and the scheduled email/SMS may still be sent.

title: Workflow update mutation does not await async step processing
body: In the workflow update mutation, userWorkflow.steps.map(async ...) performs step deletion/update, reminder cancellation, and reminder creation, but the returned promises are not awaited. The mutation can return before these operations complete, leaving workflow steps, active event types, or reminders in an inconsistent state, especially in serverless environments.

title: Failed SMS cancellation leaves reminder active with no retry
body: deleteScheduledSMSReminder calls twilio.cancelSMS and only deletes the WorkflowReminder if that call succeeds. If the Twilio request throws, the error is swallowed and the reminder row remains scheduled. There is no cancelled state or retry mechanism for SMS reminders, so a transient provider failure can result in an SMS reminder still being sent for a cancelled or rescheduled booking.

title: Eager dynamic imports of all apps can cause unhandled rejections and needless loading
body: The appStore object calls import('./...') for every integration as soon as this module is evaluated. Any import of appStore therefore starts loading all app bundles, even if only one app is needed. It also creates promises that may never be awaited; if one dynamic import or module evaluation rejects, Node/Next can observe an unhandled promise rejection. A lazy cached loader per app or explicit catch/handling would avoid both the startup cost and crash risk.

title: Async forEach is not awaited when deleting recurring calendar events
body: Array.prototype.forEach does not wait for async callbacks. In the recurring cancellation path, getCalendar and deleteEvent are awaited inside the callback, and only the resolved delete result is later pushed into apiDeletes. The later Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) can therefore run before these operations are finished or before anything is pushed. External calendar deletions may not complete before the response, and rejections are unhandled. Use Promise.all(credentials.map(...)) and collect the deletion promises.

title: `await apiDeletes` does not wait for the queued integration deletions
body: apiDeletes is an array of promises/values, but `await apiDeletes` awaits the array itself, not its elements. In the paid cancellation branch the handler continues immediately, so external calendar/video deletions are not awaited and any rejection becomes unhandled. Use `await Promise.all(apiDeletes)` if these operations should be awaited.

title: Reschedule deletion loop uses async forEach without awaiting
body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) starts calendar/video deletion but forEach ignores the returned promises. The surrounding try/catch only catches synchronous errors, so failures from getCalendar, deleteEvent, or deleteMeeting are not handled. Reschedule returns true and sends the reschedule email before the old events are reliably removed. Use Promise.all over the refs and await/handle the results.

title: Reschedule deletion loop uses async forEach without awaiting
body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) starts calendar/video deletion but forEach ignores the returned promises. The surrounding try/catch only catches synchronous errors, so failures from getCalendar, deleteEvent, or deleteMeeting are not handled. Reschedule returns true and sends the reschedule email before the old events are reliably removed. Use Promise.all over the refs and await/handle the results.

title: requestReschedule does not await calendar/video deletions
body: The requestReschedule mutation iterates refs with forEach(async ...) and then sends the reschedule email and returns. The async deletions are not awaited and have no catch, so old calendar/video events may remain and rejections become unhandled. Await Promise.all of the deletion operations and handle/log errors.

title: One failing calendar import can reject all availability results
body: getCachedResults uses Promise.all over getCalendar calls. getCalendar now awaits dynamic app imports, so a rejected import or initialization error for one credential rejects the whole Promise.all and makes availability fail for all calendars. Consider Promise.allSettled or a per-credential catch that returns null/empty for the failing calendar.

title: Video adapter loading failures bypass the Cal Video fallback
body: createMeeting awaits getVideoAdapters before the try/catch that implements the Cal Video fallback. Since getVideoAdapters now awaits dynamic imports, a rejected import for the selected video app will throw before the try block, so the intended fallback to Cal Video never runs. Wrap adapter resolution in the try/catch or handle import failures explicitly.

title: Video adapters are loaded sequentially
body: getVideoAdapters awaits each appStore dynamic import inside a for...of loop. When multiple credentials are supplied, module loading is serialized even though the imports are independent. Use Promise.all(withCredentials.map(...)) to load adapters in parallel.

title: Warning logs the module object instead of the app identifier
body: The warning interpolates paymentApp, which is the resolved module namespace or undefined, so it prints [object Module]/undefined rather than the missing app identifier. Log paymentAppCredentials.app?.dirName or appId to make the warning actionable. The same pattern exists in other payment-app lookups.

title: Recurring calendar deletions are started in an async forEach and never awaited
body: In the recurring-cancellation branch, calendar deletions are performed inside `.forEach(async (credential) => { ... })`. `forEach` does not wait for async callbacks, so the request can continue and return before the external calendar events are deleted. It also means the asynchronous pushes into `apiDeletes` may happen after the later `Promise.all`/await has already run, and any rejection from `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent` becomes an unhandled promise rejection.

title: Reschedule deletion loop is fire-and-forget
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` awaits `getCalendar`/`deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` inside the callback, but the mutation never awaits the promises returned by the async callbacks. The function proceeds to send reschedule emails and webhooks before the calendar/video events are necessarily deleted, and any error thrown during those deletions is swallowed/unhandled.

title: try/catch cannot catch errors from async forEach
body: The deletion loop uses `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)`. Because `forEach` does not await async callbacks, the surrounding `try/catch` will not catch promise rejections from `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent`, or `deleteMeeting`, and the reschedule flow returns without waiting for the external deletions to complete.

title: try/catch cannot catch errors from async forEach
body: The deletion loop uses `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)`. Because `forEach` does not await async callbacks, the surrounding `try/catch` will not catch promise rejections from `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent`, or `deleteMeeting`, and the reschedule flow returns without waiting for the external deletions to complete.

title: Awaiting an array does not await its promises
body: `await apiDeletes;` awaits the array object itself, not the promises inside it. In the paid-cancellation path, integration deletion promises are therefore not waited on, so the handler can return before calendars/videos are cleaned up and rejected deletion promises may become unhandled. This should be `await Promise.all(apiDeletes);`.

title: Video adapter loading is outside the fallback try/catch
body: `createMeeting` awaits `getVideoAdapters([credential])` before the `try` block that falls back to Cal Video. With dynamic imports, `getVideoAdapters` can reject if an app module fails to load; that rejection bypasses the fallback logic and makes meeting creation fail hard instead of degrading to the default video provider.

title: Eager dynamic imports create possibly unhandled rejected promises
body: The appStore object immediately invokes `import(...)` for every app when the module is loaded. If any app module fails to load or throws during evaluation, its promise becomes rejected. Since not every app promise is necessarily awaited in every request, this can produce unhandled promise rejections. It also starts loading all apps even when only one is needed.

title: Dynamic import failures cause getCalendar to throw instead of returning null
body: `getCalendar` awaits `appStore[...]` without catching dynamic-import failures. A rejected app import will make `getCalendar` reject rather than returning `null`. Callers such as `getCachedResults` use `Promise.all`, so one broken calendar integration can fail all calendar operations instead of being treated as unavailable.

title: lastAttendee condition is always false
body: The condition checks `.length < 0`, which can never be true. If the intent is to detect that no other attendees remain, it should be `.length === 0`. As written, the branch that deletes integrations and marks the booking cancelled for the last attendee can never run.

title: getCalendar does not handle dynamic import failures
body: getCalendar awaits appStore[...] where each entry is now a dynamic import promise. If the app chunk fails to load, that promise rejects. The function signature and most callers expect Calendar or null and handle null, but they do not necessarily handle exceptions. Without a try/catch around the import, a missing or broken app chunk can turn an unsupported calendar into a thrown error and break booking, cancellation, or reschedule flows.

title: Async calendar/video cleanup is not awaited in Reschedule
body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach is passed an async callback. forEach does not await those callbacks, so the surrounding try/catch cannot catch rejections from getCalendar, deleteEvent, or deleteMeeting. The function proceeds to send the reschedule email and return true before remote events are actually deleted. This can leave stale calendar/video events and cause unhandled promise rejections. Use Promise.all with map and await the result.

title: Async calendar/video cleanup is not awaited in Reschedule
body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach is passed an async callback. forEach does not await those callbacks, so the surrounding try/catch cannot catch rejections from getCalendar, deleteEvent, or deleteMeeting. The function proceeds to send the reschedule email and return true before remote events are actually deleted. This can leave stale calendar/video events and cause unhandled promise rejections. Use Promise.all with map and await the result.

title: Reschedule cleanup promises are fire-and-forget
body: In requestReschedule, bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) is not awaited. Calendar and video deletions run in the background, errors are not caught, and sendRequestRescheduleEmail/webhooks execute before deletions complete. This can leave stale events and produce unhandled promise rejections. Use Promise.all with map and await the deletions before sending notifications.

title: Recurring cancellation deletes are not awaited and are lost from apiDeletes
body: In the recurring cancellation branch, credentials.forEach(async ...) is not awaited. The callback awaits getCalendar and deleteEvent and then pushes resolved values into apiDeletes, so the outer code cannot reliably wait for those deletions; apiDeletes may be incomplete when Promise.all is called. Rejections are unhandled and recurring calendar events may remain undeleted. Use Promise.all over the async work and push deletion promises instead of awaited values.

title: await apiDeletes does not wait for the promises in the array
body: apiDeletes is an array of promises, but awaiting the array itself does not wait for its elements or catch rejections. In the paid cancellation path, the handler can return success while calendar/video deletions are still pending or have failed. Use await Promise.all(apiDeletes) to actually wait for and propagate integration deletion errors.

title: getCalendarCredentials now returns calendar promises without an async API
body: getCalendar became async, but getCalendarCredentials still calls it without await and returns objects whose calendar property is now a Promise. Only getConnectedCalendars in this file was updated to await item.calendar. Any other consumer of the exported getCalendarCredentials may now receive a Promise where it previously received Calendar or null, causing incorrect truthiness checks or runtime type errors. Make getCalendarCredentials async and await the calendars, or update and document all consumers.

title: createMeeting can reject before its Cal Video fallback can run
body: createMeeting awaits getVideoAdapters outside the try/catch that implements the Cal Video fallback. Since getVideoAdapters now awaits dynamic app imports, a rejected import or app lookup will throw from createMeeting instead of triggering the fallback. Move the await into the try block or catch adapter-loading errors so fallback behavior works.

title: One failing video app import aborts all video adapter operations
body: getVideoAdapters awaits each appStore import without catching errors. If one credential maps to a broken or missing app module, the whole function rejects, causing getBusyVideoTimes, createMeeting, updateMeeting, or deleteMeeting to fail even for other valid credentials. Catch per-credential import errors and skip the failing adapter instead of aborting the entire operation.

title: All app dynamic imports are started eagerly
body: appStore calls import() for every app during module initialization. This starts loading all app chunks immediately rather than lazily loading only the requested app, and it stores promises without catch. If an import rejects before it is awaited, it can also produce an unhandled rejection. Consider lazy getters or a loader function with error handling if code-splitting and graceful failure are intended.

title: Date override check skips busy-time validation
body: In checkIfIsAvailable, when a date override exists for the slot's day and the slot is not rejected by the override loop, the function returns true immediately before executing the busy.every check. This means existing bookings or calendar busy times are ignored for slots covered by a date override, which can expose already-booked slots and allow double bookings.

title: Multiple date overrides for the same day are handled incorrectly
body: The dateOverrides.find callback returns true when the slot is outside the particular override it is checking. If a user has multiple date overrides on the same date, a slot that is inside one override will be outside another override, causing find to return that other override and checkIfIsAvailable to return false. Valid slots can therefore be hidden whenever multiple date overrides exist for one day.

title: Dayjs objects are compared with ===
body: The condition `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two Dayjs object references, not their timestamps. This is never true for equal times. If a zero-length date override is used to represent an unavailable period or special case, this branch will not behave as intended. Use `.isSame()` instead.

title: Date override date comparison depends on server local timezone
body: The code formats `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` using the server's local timezone, while `slotStartTime` is formatted as UTC. If the server timezone is not UTC, a converted date override near midnight can be assigned to the wrong calendar date, causing overrides to be matched or ignored incorrectly. The comparison should use UTC explicitly.

title: Working-hours validation rejects multi-interval schedules and can treat users with no hours as available
body: The workingHours.find logic returns true when the slot is outside a particular working-hours interval. If a user has multiple working intervals in one day, a slot inside one interval is outside another interval, so the slot is rejected. Conversely, if the user has no working-hours entry for that weekday, the function falls through to the busy check and may mark the user available even though they have no availability. The check should require the slot to be contained in at least one working-hours interval and reject when none matches.

title: Working-hours end time uses slot start instead of slot end
body: In the working-hours check, `end` is computed from `slotStartTime` twice instead of using the slot end time or start time plus event length. As a result, a slot that starts before the working-hours end but extends past it passes the check, allowing bookings that run outside the configured availability.

title: Active date override filter compares wall-clock override start as a UTC instant
body: The override conversion treats `override.start` as a wall-clock time encoded in UTC, but activeOverrides filters by comparing `dayjs.utc(override.start)` directly against the invitee day's UTC interval. For large timezone offsets, this can exclude an override that belongs to the invitee date or include one that belongs to another date. For example, an override stored as 14:00Z for an invitee in UTC+14 may be filtered out because the invitee date spans roughly D-1 10:00Z to D 10:00Z, even though the converted local time is D 22:30.

title: Timezone shift drops date changes when an override crosses midnight
body: After adding the timezone offset, the code extracts only `.hour()` and `.minute()` to build startTime and endTime. If the offset moves the override across midnight, the date change is discarded. The override can then be placed on the wrong invitee day or produce an end time earlier than the start time, causing missing or incorrect slots.

title: No regression test for round-robin fixed-host date overrides
body: The PR description says it fixes date overrides for fixed hosts in round-robin events, but the added test only checks timezone conversion for a personal event. There is no automated test creating a round-robin event with a fixed host and asserting that only slots within the fixed host's date override are returned.

title: Date override short-circuits busy-time check
body: In checkIfIsAvailable, when a date override exists for the day, the function returns true before running the busy.every overlap check. Any calendar busy time or existing booking during the override is ignored, so slots can be offered even though the host is busy. This can cause double bookings, especially for fixed hosts whose availability must block the whole event.

title: Date override validation allows partially overlapping slots
body: The override exclusion only tests whether the slot ends before the override starts or starts after the override ends. It does not test whether the slot starts before the override or ends after it. Therefore a slot that only partially overlaps the override is treated as inside it. For fixed hosts, a slot such as 09:30-10:30 can pass even if the host override is only 10:00-11:00.

title: Working-hours check accepts slots when no working hours cover the day
body: The new workingHours validation only rejects a slot if it finds a workingHours entry for the slot weekday and the slot is outside that entry. If the host has no workingHours entry for that weekday, or workingHours is empty, find returns undefined and the host is treated as available subject only to busy times. This allows fixed hosts to be booked on days they have no scheduled availability.

title: Multiple date overrides on the same day make valid slots unavailable
body: The date override loop marks the slot as outside if it is outside any override on that date. If a user has two overrides on the same day, a slot inside one override is outside the other, causing dateOverrides.find to return true and checkIfIsAvailable to return false. The logic should accept a slot if it is contained in at least one override.

title: Working-hours end boundary uses slot start time
body: The variable end is calculated from slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime. The check therefore ignores the event duration when validating the end of working hours. A slot that starts inside working hours but ends after endTime will pass, potentially offering slots beyond a host's working hours.

title: Multiple working-hour intervals are handled incorrectly
body: workingHours.find returns true when the slot is outside any single working-hours interval. If a user has split working hours, such as 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00, a valid slot in one interval is outside the other, so the slot is rejected. The code should accept a slot if it fits in at least one interval.

title: Dayjs objects are compared with strict equality
body: The check comparing date.start and date.end uses === between two Dayjs objects. This compares object identity, not timestamp, so it is always false. The intended handling of a zero-length override where start equals end never triggers. Use .isSame() instead.

title: Date override date matching is not done in UTC
body: dayjs(date.start).add(...) creates a local-mode Dayjs, while slotStartTime is explicitly UTC. The YYYY MM DD comparison therefore depends on the server's local timezone and can mismatch near date boundaries. The adjusted override times should be constructed in UTC before formatting and comparing.

title: Timezone-converted overrides can wrap to another day without handling
body: After applying the invitee/organizer offset, start and end minutes are derived from hour() and minute(), which wrap at midnight. If the timezone conversion moves an override into the previous or next local day, the code still assigns those minutes to the current invitee day, which can drop the override or place slots on the wrong day. Converted ranges that cross midnight need to be split or filtered by the resulting date.

title: Missing tests for fixed-host round-robin override behavior
body: The added test only checks a personal event with a different attendee timezone. The PR description says it fixes round-robin events with fixed hosts and date overrides, but there is no test asserting that a fixed host's date override restricts round-robin slots, nor that busy times inside an override remain unavailable. Those regressions are not covered.

title: Date override path skips busy-time checks
body: In checkIfIsAvailable, when a date override exists for the slot's day and the slot is not rejected by the override bounds, the function returns true before executing the busy.every check. Existing bookings and calendar busy times inside date overrides are therefore ignored, which can allow double bookings.

title: Day.js objects are compared with ===
body: The code checks dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...). Day.js instances are objects, so === compares identity and is always false. The intended start-equals-end unavailable-date case is never detected, which can incorrectly mark slots as available.

title: Multiple date overrides on the same day are handled incorrectly
body: checkIfIsAvailable uses dateOverrides.find and returns true from the callback as soon as the slot is outside a same-day override. If a user has multiple date overrides on the same day, a slot inside a later override but outside the first one will be rejected. The logic should check whether the slot is contained in at least one override instead of rejecting on the first non-matching override.

title: Date override containment ignores slot boundaries
body: The date override check only rejects slots that end before the override starts or start after the override ends. It does not require slotStartTime >= override start and slotEndTime <= override end. Slots that overlap the beginning or end of a date override are therefore treated as available.

title: Working-hours check ignores event end time and misuses find
body: In checkIfIsAvailable, end is computed from slotStartTime rather than slotEndTime, so event length is ignored and slots extending past working hours can pass. Additionally, workingHours.find returns true if any same-day working-hours range does not contain the slot, so multiple ranges can reject a valid slot, and if no range matches the day the code falls through and may return true.

title: Date override date matching uses inconsistent timezone handling
body: checkIfIsAvailable computes utcOffset from dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone), then applies it to dayjs(date.start), which is parsed in the server's local timezone, and formats it while slotStartTime is UTC. On a server not set to UTC, the YYYY MM DD comparison can mismatch, causing date overrides to be missed or misapplied.

title: Timezone adjustment for date overrides drops day shifts
body: When converting date overrides to minutes, the code adds the timezone offset and then takes only hour() and minute(). If the offset moves the override across midnight, the day shift is discarded. Combined with the activeOverrides filter that does not account for the shifted date, overrides can be generated on the wrong invitee day for large timezone differences.

title: No regression test for round-robin fixed-host date overrides
body: The PR description says it fixes date overrides for fixed hosts in round-robin events, but the added test only covers a personal event date override in a different attendee timezone. There is no automated test creating a round-robin event with a fixed host and asserting that slots outside the fixed host's date override are removed.

title: Migration crashes when the old embed_category setting has no stored row
body: The migration reads the old embed_category setting with execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i. Discourse only stores site settings that have been changed, so on many sites this query returns zero rows. In that case result[0] is nil and calling ['id'] raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration. The same unsafe pattern is used for uncategorized_category_id on line 15.

title: Migration interpolates setting values directly into SQL
body: The INSERT into embeddable_hosts interpolates the raw site setting line into the SQL string: VALUES ('#{h}', ...). The value comes from site_settings and can contain quotes or malicious SQL. Use ActiveRecord's connection.quote or parameterized SQL to avoid injection or broken migrations.

title: Migrated embeddable hosts are not normalized
body: The migration inserts old embeddable_hosts setting lines verbatim, including possible http:// prefixes, paths, or surrounding whitespace. EmbeddableHost only strips scheme/path in before_validation callbacks, which do not run for raw SQL inserts. Since record_for_host compares URI host to lower(host), migrated rows like 'http://example.com' or 'example.com/path' will not match incoming referers, breaking embedding after migration.

title: Migration is not reversible
body: The change migration deletes site_settings rows with execute. Rails cannot reverse this automatically, so rolling back will raise an irreversible migration error and the old settings cannot be restored. Consider implementing down or preserving the old values if rollback is expected.

title: record_for_host returns false instead of nil
body: EmbeddableHost.record_for_host returns false when the URI is invalid or has no host. Callers such as TopicEmbed.import do `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` and then `eh.try(:category_id)`. `try` only guards against nil, not false, so false.category_id raises NoMethodError. A malformed embed URL can crash the import/retrieval flow. The method should return nil when no record can be found.

title: before_validation calls sub! on a possibly nil host
body: The before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! without checking that host is present. Creating or updating an EmbeddableHost with a blank host, which is possible through a direct API request, raises NoMethodError instead of failing validation. Add a presence validation or guard the normalization.

title: Host values are not unique
body: The model only validates the format of host; there is no uniqueness validation and the migration does not create a unique index. Duplicate hosts can therefore be inserted. EmbeddableHost.record_for_host uses .first, so with duplicates the selected record/category is arbitrary. Add a uniqueness validation and a unique database index on host.

title: Hosts saved with a port will never match incoming referers
body: The host validation allows values with ports, such as 'example.com:8080'. However record_for_host parses the incoming URL and compares only uri.host, which excludes the port. A stored host 'example.com:8080' will not match 'http://example.com:8080/page', so embeds from hosts with non-default ports are rejected. Either include the port in matching or disallow ports in the stored value.

title: update crashes when the embeddable host does not exist
body: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update finds the record with EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and passes it to save_host. If the id is invalid, host is nil and save_host calls host.host=..., causing a NoMethodError and a 500 response. It should return a 404 or an error JSON response.

title: destroy crashes when the embeddable host does not exist
body: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy finds the record with .first and immediately calls host.destroy. If the id is invalid, host is nil and destroy raises NoMethodError. The action should handle a missing record and return a 404 or error response.

title: save_host assumes params[:embeddable_host] is present
body: save_host accesses params[:embeddable_host][:host] and params[:embeddable_host][:category_id] without requiring the key or checking that it exists. A malformed or hand-crafted admin request without the embeddable_host parameter will raise NoMethodError. Use params.require(:embeddable_host) or handle the missing payload gracefully.

title: category_id is accepted without validating that the category exists
body: The controller assigns the supplied category_id directly and only substitutes the uncategorized category when the value is blank. It does not verify that the category exists. Nonexistent or invalid category IDs can be persisted, leaving embeddable hosts with dangling category references and causing embedded topic creation to use an invalid category.

title: PUT /admin/customize/embedding is a no-op
body: Admin::EmbeddingController#update ignores all submitted params and simply renders the freshly fetched embedding object. The client has a saveChanges action that calls embedding.update({}), which implies persistence. If this endpoint is meant to save embedding settings, it currently does nothing; otherwise the endpoint and client action should be removed.

title: Edit action loses the existing category when category object is not hydrated
body: The edit action sets categoryId from this.get('host.category.id') only. If the category was not hydrated on the client, host.category may be undefined even though host.category_id is present. The edit UI will show no category, and saving can silently change the host to uncategorized. Use host.get('category_id') as a fallback.

title: Save success handler can overwrite category with undefined
body: After a successful save, the component sets category to Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')). If categoryId is blank, the server assigns the uncategorized category, but the client will set category to undefined based on the stale local value. The UI then loses the category until refresh. Use the category returned by the server or the saved record's category_id.

title: Delete action does not handle failed destroyRecord
body: The delete action calls host.destroyRecord().then(...) but has no catch handler. If the server request fails, the rejection is unhandled and the user receives no feedback. Add popupAjaxError or another error handler.

title: No functional tests for embeddable host CRUD
body: The controller spec only asserts inheritance from Admin::AdminController. There are no tests for create, update, destroy, authorization, missing records, invalid hosts, blank category handling, or category persistence. The embedding controller spec is similarly limited. Add coverage for the new endpoints and error paths.

title: Fabricator definitions are in swapped files
body: category_fabricator.rb now defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host), while embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines the category fabricators. This may still load correctly, but it is misleading and makes future test setup errors likely. Move the fabricators to files matching the models they define.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category setting has no row
body: The migration dereferences [0]['id'] from the embed_category lookup query without checking whether any row was returned. Site settings are typically only stored when overridden, so many installs will have no embed_category row, or the stored value may not match an existing category name. In that case result[0] is nil and the migration raises NoMethodError, failing the upgrade.

title: Migration imports hosts with unescaped, unnormalized values
body: The migration interpolates the old embeddable_hosts setting values directly into an INSERT statement without SQL escaping, so values containing quotes or SQL can break the migration or execute SQL. It also stores the raw line, including any scheme or path, while EmbeddableHost.record_for_host later compares only uri.host. Migrated values like http://example.com will not match example.com, breaking embedding after migration. Blank lines can also be inserted.

title: create_table uses force: true
body: create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true will drop an existing table with that name if present. For a new migration this is unnecessary and can silently delete data if the table already exists from a previous migration or plugin. Normal create_table should be used.

title: Host uniqueness is not enforced
body: EmbeddableHost only validates the format of host. There is no uniqueness validation and the migration does not add a unique index. Duplicate host rows can be created, making record_for_host return an arbitrary row and causing unpredictable category assignment and embed-access checks.

title: before_validation crashes when host is nil
body: The before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! without guarding against nil and the model has no presence validation for host. Creating or updating a record without a host, for example via a direct API request, raises NoMethodError instead of returning a validation error.

title: category_id is not validated
body: EmbeddableHost accepts any integer for category_id; there is no existence validation or foreign key constraint. Admin API clients can save dangling category IDs, which will leave host.category nil in the UI and may pass invalid categories to PostCreator during imports.

title: Saved hosts with ports will never match
body: The host validation allows an optional port, and the before_validation callback does not strip it, but record_for_host queries using uri.host, which excludes the port. A record saved as example.com:3000 will not match a request from http://example.com:3000/..., so the host is effectively unusable.

title: update action 500s for unknown id
body: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update uses EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and passes the result to save_host. If the record does not exist, host is nil and save_host calls host.host= on nil, causing a 500 error instead of returning a 404.

title: destroy action 500s for unknown id
body: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy calls host.destroy on the result of EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first. If no record matches the id, this raises NoMethodError instead of handling the missing record gracefully.

title: Embedded has-many hydration can insert undefined records
body: In _hydrateEmbedded, keys ending in _ids are mapped through _lookupSubType and the result is assigned directly to the pluralized property. If any id cannot be resolved, the array contains undefined. The singular case checks whether the lookup succeeded, but the plural case does not filter missing records, which can cause template or runtime errors.

title: Client may show wrong or blank category after save
body: After saving, the component sets host.category to Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')). If categoryId is blank or invalid, the server defaults category_id to the uncategorized category, but the client sets category to nil/undefined, so the displayed category does not match the saved record until reload.

title: Deletion failures are not surfaced
body: destroyRecord is called without a catch handler. If the DELETE request fails, the host remains in the UI and the user receives no error feedback.

title: Embeddable hosts resource defines unimplemented actions
body: resources :embeddable_hosts creates index, show, new and edit routes, but Admin::EmbeddableHostsController only implements create, update and destroy. Requests to the unimplemented routes will error. The route should be restricted to only the implemented actions.

title: PUT /admin/customize/embedding is a no-op
body: Admin::EmbeddingController#update simply re-renders the fetched embedding object and ignores any submitted attributes. If the endpoint is not intended to update anything, it should be removed; otherwise it silently discards changes.

title: Admin embedding controller specs only assert inheritance
body: The new controller specs only check that the controllers subclass Admin::AdminController. They do not test show/update, create/update/delete of embeddable hosts, missing records, invalid hosts, category handling, or staff authorization, leaving the new endpoints and migration behavior largely untested.

title: Migration can crash when expected site setting rows do not exist
body: The migration indexes directly into the first row of raw SQL results: execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i. On fresh installs, or on sites where embed_category was never changed, the site_settings row will not exist, so [0] is nil and the migration raises NoMethodError. The same unsafe pattern is used at line 15 for uncategorized_category_id. This can block the migration completely.

title: Migration interpolates old site setting values into raw SQL
body: The INSERT statement embeds the old embeddable_hosts setting line directly into SQL: VALUES ('#{h}', ...). A stored value containing a single quote or SQL fragment can break the migration or execute unintended SQL. These values should be inserted through parameterized SQL or at least connection.quote.

title: Existing embeddable hosts are migrated without normalization
body: The migration copies old embeddable_hosts lines verbatim into embeddable_hosts.host. The new model only strips scheme and path in an ActiveRecord before_validation callback, which migrations bypass. Existing values like http://example.com, https://example.com/path, or blank lines will be stored as-is or as empty rows. Since EmbeddableHost.record_for_host later compares only the URI host against lower(host), these migrated rows may never match, silently breaking embedding after upgrade.

title: Update and destroy assume the embeddable host record exists
body: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update and #destroy use EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first without checking for nil. If an unknown id is supplied, update calls save_host(nil) and destroy calls host.destroy, causing a NoMethodError and a 500 response instead of a 404.

title: before_validation mutates host without guarding against nil
body: EmbeddableHost's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! unconditionally. If host is nil, for example from a malformed admin API request, this raises NoMethodError before validations can run. The callback should guard against blank/nil host, and the model should have an explicit presence validation.

title: Category ID is accepted without validating that the category exists
body: save_host assigns category_id directly from request parameters and only replaces it when blank. A nonexistent numeric category id, or category_id=0, can be persisted. TopicEmbed.import later uses EmbeddableHost#category_id when creating topics, so invalid category references can cause data integrity problems or failed topic creation.

title: No uniqueness constraint or validation on host
body: EmbeddableHost does not validate uniqueness of host, and the migration does not create a unique index. Duplicate host rows can therefore be created. EmbeddableHost.record_for_host uses where(...).first without an order, so if duplicates exist with different categories, the category used for imported topics is arbitrary.

title: Hosts saved with a port will never match incoming referers
body: The host validation regex allows an optional port, so example.com:8080 can be saved. However record_for_host parses the incoming URL with URI and compares only uri.host, which excludes the port. As a result, a configured host with a port will never match http://example.com:8080/, making port-specific host entries unusable.

title: Plural embedded ID hydration can create undefined records or throw
body: _hydrateEmbedded assumes any key ending in _ids is an array and calls obj[k].map. If the payload contains null or undefined for that key, this throws. If some IDs cannot be found via _lookupSubType, the resulting association array contains undefined entries, and the original *_ids key is deleted anyway. UI code iterating that association may then fail.

title: Saved host category is set from local selection instead of server response
body: After saving, the component sets host.category using Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')).
