If the selected category was blank and the server normalized it to the uncategorized category, or if the local categoryId is undefined, the UI may display the wrong category or no category. It should use the category_id returned in the saved host payload.

title: resources :embeddable_hosts exposes routes with no controller actions
body: resources :embeddable_hosts generates index, show, new, edit, create, update, and destroy routes, but Admin::EmbeddableHostsController only implements create, update, and destroy. Requests to the extra routes will result in missing action errors. The route should be restricted to only the implemented actions.

title: New admin endpoints have no functional controller coverage
body: The specs for Admin::EmbeddableHostsController and Admin::EmbeddingController only assert controller inheritance. There are no tests for create/update/destroy behavior, invalid ids, malformed parameters, host normalization, category handling, or the data migration. Given the number of edge cases in this feature, this is a significant test gap.

title: Host format regex rejects valid hostnames
body: The validation regex restricts the top-level domain to [a-z]{2,5}. This rejects valid modern domains with longer TLDs, such as .travel or .agency, and also prevents using localhost in development. The host validation is more restrictive than necessary for the feature.

title: PUT /admin/customize/embedding does not update anything
body: Admin::EmbeddingController#update ignores all request parameters and simply renders the current embedding object. The client defines a saveChanges action that issues this update, but the endpoint cannot persist any embedding-level changes. If no attributes are intended to be editable here, the route/action should be removed or the endpoint should be implemented.

title: Client-side upload size limit hardcoded to 10 MB
body: The validation now uses a fixed `10 * 1024` KB instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. This ignores the configured maximum for both images and attachments: attachments larger than the site limit can be selected/uploaded, and images may be blocked even if the configured image limit is larger than 10 MB. It also makes client-side enforcement inconsistent with the server-side behavior introduced in this PR.

title: 413 error message uses hardcoded 10 MB limit
body: On HTTP 413 the code reports `max_size_kb: 10 * 1024` instead of the relevant site setting. Users can be told the limit is 10 MB even when the configured maximum image or attachment size is different, so the error message no longer reflects the actual upload policy.

title: URL uploads are downloaded with a fixed 10 MB limit
body: `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` replaces the previous `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` limit and is used before knowing whether the URL is an image. API URL uploads can now fetch up to 10 MB even when the configured maximum is lower, and non-image/attachment URL uploads are not subject to the attachment limit. This can bypass site limits and waste bandwidth or memory.

title: Downsizing overwrites the input tempfile in place
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` uses the same path as input and output. ImageMagick/gifsicle are not guaranteed to safely overwrite the file they are reading, and in-place rewriting can truncate or corrupt the original upload if the tool opens the output for writing before fully reading the input or if the operation fails. A temporary output file should be created and atomically replace the original only on success.

title: Failed or ineffective downsizing is ignored
body: The loop does not check the boolean returned by `OptimizedImage.downsize` and does not abort if the file is still larger than `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` after five attempts. If conversion fails, the code will retry pointlessly and then continue to `Upload.create_for` with an unchanged or corrupted file, possibly storing an invalid or oversized upload or returning a confusing error.

title: Tempfile path lacks original extension, breaking animation/format detection
body: The automatic downsize passes `tempfile.path` to `OptimizedImage.optimize`, which only uses the animated code path when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. Rack/Tempfile paths for uploads usually do not carry the original filename extension, so GIFs will not be detected as animated and will be processed by ImageMagick with `[0]`, stripping animation even when `allow_animation` is enabled. The missing extension can also make ImageMagick choose the wrong output format. Use a temp file with the original extension or pass the desired format explicitly.

title: SVG/vector images are downsized like raster images
body: The condition treats any filename matching `FileHelper.is_image?` as resizable, which includes SVG in Discourse. Unlike `OptimizedImage.create_for`, this code has no special case for `.svg`; calling ImageMagick `convert` on an SVG to reduce file size can rasterize or otherwise alter the vector file, or fail. Large SVG uploads can therefore be corrupted or lose their original content.

title: Duplicate `downsize` definition overwrites the four-argument method
body: Ruby does not overload methods by arity. The second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` replaces the preceding four-argument `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`. The four-argument version is dead code, and any existing caller using width/height will have `height` interpreted as `opts`, likely causing errors or malformed ImageMagick dimensions. If both signatures are needed, use distinct method names or a single method that normalizes arguments.

title: No tests for automatic downsizing and changed upload limits
body: The PR introduces server-side image downsizing, changes URL download limits, and alters client-side upload validation, but no test files are added or updated. Without coverage for oversized images, failed conversions, SVG/GIF handling, and attachment limits, regressions in these upload paths are likely.

title: Client-side upload size limit is hardcoded to 10MB
body: validateUploadedFile previously used Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the limit depended on whether the upload was an image or attachment and on the admin-configured site setting. It now always allows 10MB. This can let users select attachments larger than the configured attachment limit, and can also block images when the configured image limit is larger than 10MB.

title: 413 error message reports a hardcoded 10MB limit
body: displayErrorForUpload now tells the user that the maximum upload size is 10MB after a 413 response, regardless of the actual site setting or web server limit. This can display an incorrect maximum size to the user.

title: URL downloads ignore configured upload size limits
body: FileHelper.download was changed from SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes to a fixed 10.megabytes for all URL-based API uploads. This ignores both max_image_size_kb and any attachment size limit, allowing the server to download up to 10MB even when the configured limit is lower.

title: In-place downsizing can corrupt or destroy the uploaded tempfile
body: The loop calls OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...) and ignores the return value. If the conversion or optimization fails, truncates the file, or produces a corrupt image, the original uploaded data has already been overwritten and the controller may continue to Upload.create_for with a damaged or zero-byte file. A separate output file and explicit failure handling are needed.

title: Animated GIF downsizing is invoked with an invalid percentage geometry
body: The controller passes dimensions='80%' to OptimizedImage.downsize. For animated GIFs, OptimizedImage uses gifsicle --resize-fit #{dimensions}, and gifsicle expects WIDTHxHEIGHT rather than a percentage. The command will fail, so large animated GIFs will not be downsized and the loop will either retry uselessly or proceed with an oversized file.

title: Automatic downsizing is attempted for vector images such as SVG
body: The condition uses FileHelper.is_image?(filename), which treats SVG as an image elsewhere in Discourse. OptimizedImage.downsize is a raster ImageMagick resize and cannot meaningfully or safely reduce an SVG file in place. Large SVG uploads will repeatedly fail downsizing or may be corrupted before upload; vector formats should be excluded or handled separately.

title: Duplicate downsize method definition breaks the previous four-argument API
body: Ruby keeps only the last definition of self.downsize, so the new three-argument method at line 149 silently replaces the four-argument version at line 145. Existing callers using downsize(from, to, width, height) will now have height interpreted as opts, or will raise ArgumentError if an options hash is also supplied. This is an API break and can cause TypeErrors or invalid resize dimensions.

title: No tests cover the new automatic downsizing behavior
body: There are no tests for the new server-side downsizing loop, including oversized images, failed conversions, animated GIFs, SVGs, or interaction with configured size limits. These cases are likely to regress and are risky areas of this change.

title: Client-side upload limit is hardcoded to 10 MB
body: The client validation replaces Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'] with a fixed 10 MB limit. This ignores the configured max_image_size_kb and max_attachment_size_kb values, so users can attempt uploads that are not allowed (especially attachments), and configurations with limits above or below 10 MB are no longer respected in the UI.

title: 413 error message uses a hardcoded 10 MB limit
body: The 413 handler now reports a fixed 10 MB maximum size instead of using the relevant site setting. If the actual limit differs, users receive an inaccurate error message.

title: Remote download limit is hardcoded to 10 MB
body: FileHelper.download now uses 10.megabytes instead of a site-setting-based limit for URL uploads. The later automatic downsizing only applies to recognized images, so non-image URL uploads, or images when the size setting is disabled, are no longer constrained by the configured limit at this stage.

title: Upload proceeds even if the image is still too large after five attempts
body: The loop makes at most five 80% resize attempts and then falls through without checking whether the file is now within SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb. If the file is still oversized, or if re-encoding fails to reduce size, the code continues to Upload.create_for, risking an oversized stored image or an expensive delayed failure.

title: In-place downsizing uses the same input and output path
body: OptimizedImage.downsize is called with tempfile.path as both source and destination. ImageMagick or gifsicle may truncate or corrupt the file while reading and writing the same path, and the boolean return value is ignored. A failed conversion can therefore leave a corrupted or zero-byte upload that is then passed to Upload.create_for.

title: SVG files are sent through raster downsizing
body: The new block downsizes every file accepted by FileHelper.is_image?, but does not exclude SVG. Elsewhere, OptimizedImage.create_for explicitly copies SVGs instead of resizing them. Running ImageMagick convert on an SVG can rasterize or corrupt the vector image while keeping the original filename, producing a damaged upload.

title: Animated-image handling depends on temporary file extension
body: OptimizedImage.optimize selects the animated code path only when the input path ends in .gif. The controller downsizes temporary upload paths that may not preserve the original extension, so animated GIFs can be processed with convert file[0] and flattened to a single frame. The supplied '80%' dimension is also an ImageMagick-style geometry and may not be valid for gifsicle.

title: Nil tempfile is not handled before calling tempfile.size
body: If FileHelper.download fails, tempfile is nil because of rescue nil. The code then calls Upload.create_for with tempfile.size, which raises NoMethodError instead of returning a graceful upload error.

title: Duplicate downsize method definitions break the previous API
body: Ruby does not support method overloading. The second downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) definition replaces the preceding four-argument downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) definition. The old width/height API becomes dead code, and any existing caller using four positional size arguments will now pass the fourth argument as opts or raise an argument error.

title: No tests cover the new automatic downsizing behavior
body: The PR changes upload limits and mutates uploaded files, but adds no tests for the downsizing loop, failed conversions, files that remain oversized, SVG/GIF edge cases, or the changed OptimizedImage.downsize API. These are high-risk paths that can corrupt uploads or bypass configured limits.

title: GET /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe changes notification state
body: The new endpoint is exposed as GET and TopicsController#unsubscribe immediately persists a new notification_level. Because GET requests are exempt from Rails CSRF verification and the controller skips the XHR check, any page the user visits, or a browser/link prefetch, can issue a request to /t/<id>/unsubscribe with the user's session cookies and silently change their notification state. State-changing operations should use POST/PUT or require a signed token.

title: Unsubscribe crashes when no TopicUser row exists
body: TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) can return nil if the user has no topic_users row for the topic (for example they have never visited it). The following conditional calls tu.notification_level, causing NoMethodError and a 500 instead of handling the unsubscribe. The code should create/update via TopicUser.change or guard against nil.

title: Direct TopicUser#save bypasses notification-change bookkeeping
body: The controller updates the record with tu.save! rather than TopicUser.change. TopicUser.change is the established path for notification-level changes: it sets notifications_changed_at and notifications_reason_id and publishes a MessageBus message. Bypassing it leaves stale reason/timestamp data and other browser tabs/clients will not be notified of the change.

title: unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url interpolation
body: The default unsubscribe_link translation now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}. Email::MessageBuilder appends this translation whenever add_unsubscribe_link is true, but the builder does not require or default unsubscribe_url. Any current/plugin/future caller that sets add_unsubscribe_link without providing unsubscribe_url will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument while rendering the body/html, causing email send failures. It also makes the global text topic-specific.

title: track_visit! assigns topic_id as user_id for integer user argument
body: In track_visit!, the fallback for a non-User user argument is topic instead of user: user_id = user.is_a?(User) ? user.id : topic. Callers such as TopicsController#track_visit_to_topic pass a numeric user id, so user_id becomes the topic id. This writes topic_users rows for the wrong user (or creates rows keyed by topic_id as user_id), corrupting visit/notification tracking. It should be user_id = user.is_a?(User) ? user.id : user.

title: No tests for new unsubscribe endpoint
body: There are no controller/request specs for the new unsubscribe action. The PR changes state, adds redirects, and depends on TopicUser presence, but tests do not cover successful level changes, missing TopicUser, slug redirects, HTML vs JSON, or the unsafe GET behavior.

title: State-changing unsubscribe action is a GET route without CSRF/token
body: The unsubscribe action changes TopicUser.notification_level in response to a GET request and skips XHR checks. Rails CSRF protection does not apply to GET, so any logged-in user visiting a malicious page could have topics silently muted or downgraded by an image or link to /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe. Email unsubscribe links should use a signed one-time key or a POST route.

title: Unsubscribe crashes when no TopicUser row exists
body: TopicsController#unsubscribe does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then dereferences `tu.notification_level`. For users without an existing topic_users row for the topic, `tu` is nil and the action raises NoMethodError. The action should create or update the row, for example via TopicUser.change or find_or_create_by.

title: Direct TopicUser#save! bypasses notification-level bookkeeping
body: The unsubscribe action mutates notification_level with `tu.save!` instead of `TopicUser.change`. This skips setting notifications_changed_at and notifications_reason_id and does not publish the MessageBus level-change event. Leaving notifications_reason_id nil can allow later automatic tracking to override the user's mute, and open clients will not receive the state change.

title: Global unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url for all callers
body: The `unsubscribe_link` translation was changed to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}`, but Email::MessageBuilder only has that value when the caller passes `unsubscribe_url`. Only `send_notification_email` was updated. Any other email or plugin that builds with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` but omits `unsubscribe_url` will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and fail to send.

title: track_visit! uses topic id as user_id when passed ids
body: In `TopicUser.track_visit!`, `user_id = user.is_a?(User) ? user.id : topic` falls back to the `topic` argument rather than the `user` argument when the second argument is not a User object. TopicsController calls this with integer topic_id/user_id, so it can create or update topic_users rows with user_id equal to the topic_id, corrupting per-user topic state. The fallback should be `user`.

title: Spec does not assert the new unsubscribe_url is included
body: The updated spec passes `unsubscribe_url` to Email::MessageBuilder but only asserts that the body contains `user_preferences_url`. It never checks that the new per-topic unsubscribe URL appears in the body or HTML, so the new interpolation/link behavior is untested.

title: Unsubscribe crashes when no TopicUser row exists
body: TopicsController#unsubscribe calls TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) and immediately reads tu.notification_level. If the current user has no topic_users row for that topic (for example they never visited the topic, the row was removed, or the URL is visited directly), find_by returns nil and the action raises NoMethodError instead of handling the unsubscribe. Use find_or_initialize_by, or TopicUser.change, so a missing row is created or handled safely.

title: State-changing unsubscribe is performed by an unauthenticated GET
body: The new /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe endpoint changes the user's topic notification level in response to a GET request, skips the XHR check, and has no token or confirmation. Because Rails CSRF protection does not apply to GET requests, a third-party page can cause a logged-in user to mute or downgrade notifications for arbitrary topic IDs by loading an image or link. Email prefetching or link previews can also trigger the change unintentionally. Use a POST/PUT action, a signed per-user unsubscribe token, or at least require an explicit confirmation step.

title: Direct TopicUser save bypasses notification-change side effects
body: TopicsController#unsubscribe updates the TopicUser record directly and calls save!, bypassing TopicUser.change. TopicUser.change is the normal path for notification-level changes and sets notifications_changed_at/notifications_reason_id and publishes the notification_level_change MessageBus event. With the direct save, open clients will not be notified of the new notification level, and the reason/audit metadata for the change is lost. It also does not handle the missing-row case the way TopicUser.change does.

title: track_visit! uses the topic id as the user id when passed an id
body: TopicUser.track_visit! computes user_id as `user.is_a?(User) ? user.id : topic`. When the second argument is a user id integer, as in TopicsController#track_visit_to_topic (`TopicUser.track_visit! topic_id, user_id`), the method assigns the topic id to user_id. This creates or updates topic_users rows for the wrong user, corrupting visit tracking and potentially notification-related state. The else branch should return `user`, not `topic`.

title: Shared unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url for all callers
body: The shared `unsubscribe_link` translation now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. Email::MessageBuilder renders this translation for any email built with `add_unsubscribe_link`, but only `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` was updated to supply `unsubscribe_url`. Any other current/future caller or plugin that enables the unsubscribe link without providing `unsubscribe_url` will fail email rendering/sending with a missing interpolation argument. Make the per-topic line conditional, provide a default, or update all callers.

title: No specs for the new unsubscribe endpoint
body: The PR adds a state-changing TopicsController#unsubscribe endpoint but includes no controller/request specs. Important cases are untested: missing TopicUser row, slug mismatch redirects, JSON vs HTML behavior, permission handling, and the fact that the action mutates notification state. A spec would catch the nil TopicUser crash and the missing MessageBus/metadata behavior.

title: Blocked-email match counters can be incremented multiple times for one signup attempt
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? is called from EmailValidator during User validation. UsersController#create calls user.valid? and then user.save, and save runs validations again. Each call executes record.match_count += 1 and record.save, so a single rejected account creation can increment match_count more than once and persists the increment even though no user is created. This corrupts the blocklist statistics and adds unnecessary writes.

title: Match count update is not atomic and save failures are ignored
body: should_block? loads a BlockedEmail row, increments match_count in Ruby, and saves it. Concurrent attempts with the same blocked email can read the same match_count and overwrite each other's increments. The return value of record.save is also ignored, so a failed update still leaves the method to decide blocking based on stale in-memory data. Use an atomic counter update if accurate statistics are needed.

title: Blocked email lookup is exact and unnormalized, so blocks can be bypassed by case or whitespace
body: should_block? queries BlockedEmail.where(email: email) using the raw value. Neither this model nor the changed User validations normalize the address by stripping and downcasing it. A block entry for user@example.com will not match USER@EXAMPLE.COM or an address with surrounding whitespace, allowing a blocked user to register by changing case or whitespace. Normalize emails before storing and querying blocked entries.

title: Domain whitelist/blacklist regex is not anchored and can match unintended domains
body: email_in_restriction_setting? builds a regex of the form @(domains) with only dots escaped and matches it anywhere in the address. With a whitelist of example.com, user@example.com.attacker.com matches because it contains @example.com as a substring, so the whitelist can be bypassed. With a blacklist it can produce false positives for domains that merely contain a blocked domain as a prefix. Compare the actual domain or anchor the regex to the end of the address and escape each domain.

title: rejectedEmails is defined as a shared mutable array on the controller prototype
body: rejectedEmails: Em.A([]) is placed directly on the Ember object prototype. Arrays defined this way are shared by all instances of the controller unless reinitialized in init. If the controller is instantiated more than once, including in tests, rejected email addresses leak between instances and persist unexpectedly. Initialize the array in init or reset it when the create-account modal is opened.

title: Blocked email check is exact-match only and not normalized
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? queries with where(email: email) using the raw value, and neither this model nor EmailValidator strips or downcases the address. Discourse otherwise treats emails case-insensitively in several places, so a blocked address can be bypassed by changing case or adding surrounding whitespace. The table/model also allow duplicate blocked rows that differ only by case. This defeats the blocked-email enforcement.

title: Domain allow/block regex is unanchored and can be bypassed
body: email_in_restriction_setting? builds an unanchored, case-insensitive regular expression from the site setting. With a whitelist of allowed.com, an address such as user@allowed.com.attacker.com still matches because the regex does not anchor the domain to the end of the email. This allows email-domain whitelist restrictions to be bypassed; blacklist behavior can also overmatch unintended domains.

title: Blocked-email validation writes match statistics during model validation
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? is a predicate that also increments match_count, sets last_match_at, and saves the record. EmailValidator calls it during User validation. UsersController#create calls user.valid? and then user.save, so the same email can be counted multiple times for one request, and counts are updated even when the user record is ultimately invalid or not saved. This makes validation non-idempotent and corrupts the blocked-email statistics.

title: Match counter is incremented in Ruby and saved non-atomically
body: should_block? reads a BlockedEmail row, performs record.match_count += 1, and then saves it. Concurrent validation attempts can read the same match_count and overwrite each other's increments, losing statistics. Save failures are also ignored while the method still returns the block decision. An atomic counter update would be needed for reliable statistics.

title: rejectedEmails is a mutable array defined on the controller prototype
body: rejectedEmails: Em.A([]) is defined in the controller class body, so the mutable array is shared rather than initialized per instance. pushObject mutates this shared state, and it is not reset when the create-account modal is reopened. Previously rejected emails can persist across controller instances or modal sessions and incorrectly invalidate a later form.

title: Validator specs stub BlockedEmail and omit security-relevant cases
body: The EmailValidator spec only stubs BlockedEmail.should_block? and does not cover the whitelist/blacklist regex, case/whitespace normalization, or actual interaction with BlockedEmail records. Because this PR centralizes security-relevant email blocking logic, these untested paths can regress or remain bypassable without detection.

title: Blocked email lookup and uniqueness are not normalized
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? queries the exact email string, and the model does not downcase or strip the address before validation or storage. If an admin blocks bad@example.com, a signup using Bad@Example.com, or the same address with surrounding whitespace, will not match and will bypass the block. The uniqueness validation and database index are also case-sensitive, allowing duplicate blocked rows that differ only by case. Normalize emails before saving and querying.

title: Domain whitelist regex is not anchored and can be bypassed
body: email_in_restriction_setting? builds a case-insensitive regex of the form @(domains) without anchoring the domain to the end of the address and escapes only dots. With a whitelist of example.com, an address such as user@example.com.evil.com matches the regex and is accepted, defeating the whitelist. The same pattern can also overmatch blacklisted domains. Parse the domain list explicitly, escape regex metacharacters, and anchor each allowed or blocked domain.

title: should_block? writes statistics during validation and can double-count
body: should_block? loads a BlockedEmail row, increments match_count in Ruby, and saves it while being called from an ActiveModel validator. In UsersController#create, user.valid? is called and then user.save runs validations again, so one signup attempt can increment the same blocked-email row twice. The read-modify-write is also non-atomic, so concurrent requests can lose increments. Move counting out of the predicate or use an atomic counter update once per request.

title: Blocked email specs do not cover normalization or controller integration
body: The specs only exercise exact-case matches, and the validator spec stubs BlockedEmail.should_block? rather than testing the real flow. There is no test that a User save is rejected when a blocked email is supplied with different casing or whitespace, nor a request/controller test that the signup endpoint actually blocks creation and returns the expected error. Add integration-level coverage for these paths.

title: Import stores unsanitized remote HTML as raw_html posts
body: TopicEmbed.import creates posts with skip_validations and cook_method raw_html from fetched/RSS content. Post#cook returns raw for this method and the embed view outputs post.cooked with `raw`, so untrusted HTML from the remote page/feed is stored and rendered without sanitization. This can lead to stored XSS, for example via javascript: links or other active content.

title: Invalid ERB block terminator `<%- end if %>`
body: The template closes the if/else block with `<%- end if %>`. ERB will emit `end if` into the Ruby code, which is not a valid way to terminate an if block, so the template will fail to compile/render. It should be `<%- end %>`.

title: Referer is interpolated into inline JavaScript unsafely
body: `request.referer` is inserted into an inline script string and used as the postMessage target origin without JavaScript escaping or reducing it to an origin. A referer containing special characters can break the script or be used in the wrong context. Use `escape_javascript` and send the message to `URI(request.referer).origin` rather than the full referer.

title: Feed polling crashes when an item has no content
body: Many RSS/Atom items do not provide a `content` field, for example RSS items with only `description`. `i.content` can be nil, so calling `.scrub` on it raises NoMethodError and aborts the whole poll job. Use a fallback field and guard against nil.

title: Remote import uses open-uri without redirect or timeout restrictions
body: `import_remote` fetches URLs with `open(url).read`. open-uri follows redirects and has no connect/read timeout by default. Since the URL can be triggered through embed retrieval, a redirect from an allowed host can be used to reach unintended hosts/internal services, and a slow endpoint can hang the job. Use a restricted HTTP client with timeouts and controlled redirects.

title: Unknown embed URLs trigger a synchronous full feed poll
body: When feed polling is enabled, each missing embed URL runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline. This downloads and imports the entire feed just to check for one URL. Anonymous embed requests can enqueue many RetrieveTopic jobs, throttled only per URL, causing repeated expensive feed polling and Sidekiq backlog.

title: content_sha1 is updated even if the post revision fails
body: In the update path, `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` is called after `revise!` without checking the result or rescuing save failures. If the revision does not persist, the embed record still records the new hash, so future imports will think the content is up to date and will not retry.

title: Loading response is cached for one minute
body: `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is called even when the controller renders the loading page. If the loading response is cached, the iframe's 30-second reload can continue to show the cached loading page after the background job has created the topic. The loading state should be non-cacheable or expire much sooner.

title: Throttle key set and expiry are not atomic
body: `$redis.setnx` followed by `$redis.expire` is not atomic. If the process dies between the two commands, the key can remain forever without a TTL, permanently blocking retrieval for that embed URL. Use an atomic SET with NX and EX, or an equivalent atomic primitive.

title: Blank embed_url is accepted and enqueues a failing job
body: `params.require(:embed_url)` only requires the key to be present; an empty string passes. The controller then enqueues RetrieveTopic with a blank embed_url, and the job raises Discourse::InvalidParameters. Validate presence/non-blank before enqueuing.

title: Embed URLs are not normalized before lookup/create
body: TopicEmbed records are matched by exact `embed_url`. Equivalent URLs, such as http vs https, trailing slash differences, or harmless query/fragment variations, will be treated as different embeds and can create duplicate topics for the same article. Canonicalize URLs before lookup and storage.

title: Only root-relative URLs are absolutized
body: `absolutize_urls` rewrites only `href`/`src` values that start with `/`. Relative paths without a leading slash and protocol-relative URLs like `//host/...` are left unchanged, so imported posts can contain broken links/images. Resolve all relative URLs against the source URL.

title: No guard when #discourse-comments is missing
body: The script calls `comments.appendChild(iframe)` without checking whether `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` returned null. If the embedding page lacks that element, JavaScript throws and the embed iframe is never inserted.

title: Assumes discourseUrl ends with a trailing slash
body: The iframe src is built by concatenating `discourseUrl` with `embed/best...`. If `discourseUrl` does not end with `/`, the resulting URL is invalid, for example `https://forum.example.comembed/best`. Normalize the base URL before concatenating.

title: create_table uses force: true
body: `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` will drop an existing `topic_embeds` table and its data before creating the new one. Production migrations should not silently drop tables; use `create_table` without `force` and handle pre-existing tables explicitly if needed.

title: Existing migration changed to force table recreation
body: This edits an existing migration and adds `force: true` to `create_table :top_topics`. If the migration is rerun or run after the table already exists, it will drop and recreate the table, causing data loss. Migrations should generally be immutable and not use force in this way.

title: Loading page reloads forever if retrieval never succeeds
body: The loading template reloads the page every 30 seconds indefinitely. If the embed cannot be retrieved due to an invalid URL, host mismatch, or remote errors, this creates an endless request loop on the embedding page. Add a failure state or backoff.

title: Template assumes post.user is present
body: The embed view calls `post.user.small_avatar_url` and `post.user.username` without nil checks. If a displayed post has a deleted or missing user, the template raises NoMethodError and the embed fails to render. Use a fallback user/display for nil users.

title: Feed fetch has no timeout/error handling
body: `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` is called without timeouts or rescue. A slow or unresponsive feed can hang the scheduled Sidekiq job and delay other scheduled work. Use an HTTP client with connect/read timeouts and handle fetch errors.

title: External embed content is stored and rendered as raw HTML
body: TopicEmbed.import creates posts with skip_validations and cook_method set to Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]. Content imported from RSS/Atom feeds or remote pages is not sanitized before storage, and Post#cook returns the raw HTML for this cook method. This allows untrusted external HTML, including scripts and dangerous markup, to be stored and later rendered in Discourse pages.

title: ERB syntax error in embed best view
body: The template closes the first conditional with '<%- end if %>', which is not valid ERB/Ruby. Rendering the embed best view will raise a syntax error, causing the embed endpoint to fail whenever this template is rendered.

title: Feed polling crashes when item content is missing
body: PollFeed calls i.content.scrub for every feed item. Many RSS/Atom items may not have a content element, in which case i.content is nil and nil.scrub raises NoMethodError. The scheduled job will abort and no further items in the feed will be processed.

title: NoMethodError when embed_by_username is blank
body: TopicRetriever#fetch_http calls SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase without checking whether the setting is present. If embed_by_username is blank, this raises NoMethodError. This can happen when embedding is partially configured: embeddable_host is set, but no import username has been chosen.

title: Host validation does not reject a blank embeddable host
body: TopicRetriever#invalid_host? compares SiteSetting.embeddable_host with the URI host. If embeddable_host is blank and the parsed URI also has a nil host, the method returns false instead of treating the URL as invalid. The retriever should explicitly reject retrieval when no embeddable host is configured.

title: Redis throttle key can be left without expiry
body: retrieved_recently? uses $redis.setnx followed by $redis.expire. If the process crashes or the expire call fails between these two operations, the Redis key remains forever without a TTL, permanently throttling retrieval for that embed URL. An atomic SET with NX and expiry should be used.

title: Embed retrieval runs the entire feed poll synchronously
body: When feed polling is enabled, TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve instantiates Jobs::PollFeed and executes it synchronously just to see whether one embed URL appears in the feed. This imports every item in the configured feed, which can be expensive and can create many unrelated topics during a single embed request.

title: Embed permalink footer is built with unescaped HTML
body: TopicEmbed.import appends an imported-from footer by interpolating the URL directly into an HTML anchor tag without escaping. A URL containing quotes or markup can break the HTML or inject additional markup into the post. The URL should be HTML-escaped before being inserted into the footer.

title: Readability import allows href/src without scheme sanitization
body: import_remote uses ruby-readability with an allow-list that includes a and img tags and href/src attributes, but it does not sanitize attribute URL schemes. Dangerous URLs such as javascript: links can survive and be stored in the post. Since imported posts are rendered as raw HTML, this creates an XSS risk.

title: Failed post creation can still attempt TopicEmbed creation
body: After PostCreator#create returns, TopicEmbed.import checks post.present? before creating the TopicEmbed record. PostCreator can return an unsaved post object after a rollback, for example when host spam detection triggers. In that case post.present? is true but post.id/topic_id are nil, so TopicEmbed.create! will fail or raise a database error. The code should check that the post was persisted.

title: Updating an embed crashes if the post was deleted
body: When an existing TopicEmbed is found, the update path uses embed.post without verifying that the post still exists. If the embedded topic or post has been deleted, embed.post is nil and PostRevisor.new(post) will raise. Feed polling or retrieval for that URL will then repeatedly fail.

title: content_sha1 is updated even if the revision fails
body: TopicEmbed.import updates embed.content_sha1 immediately after calling PostRevisor#revise!, without checking whether the revision succeeded. If the post cannot be saved, the stored SHA1 will no longer match the post contents, and future legitimate content changes may be skipped because the embed record believes it is already up to date.

title: URL absolutizer mishandles protocol-relative and relative URLs
body: absolutize_urls only rewrites href/src values that start with '/'. Protocol-relative URLs such as '//cdn.example.com/x' are also matched and incorrectly rewritten to the current host, and ordinary relative URLs such as 'page.html' are left unchanged. This can break links and images in imported content.

title: PostCreator accepts arbitrary cook_method without validation
body: PostCreator now assigns post.cook_method from @opts[:cook_method] without validating the value or restricting which callers may use raw_html. Since the raw_html cook method bypasses the normal sanitization pipeline, exposing or forwarding this option accidentally could allow unsafe HTML to be stored.

title: Embed iframe URL assumes discourseUrl has a trailing slash
body: embed.js builds the iframe src as discourseUrl + 'embed/best?...'. If discourseUrl is provided without a trailing slash, the resulting URL becomes invalid, for example 'https://forum.example.comembed/best'. The script should normalize discourseUrl or insert a slash when missing.

title: Embed script crashes if target element is missing
body: The embed script calls comments.appendChild(iframe) after document.getElementById('discourse-comments'). If the host page does not contain an element with id discourse-comments, comments is null and the script throws a TypeError, preventing any further script execution.

title: Migration uses force: true and can drop existing data
body: CreateTopicEmbeds creates the topic_embeds table with force: true. In a migration this will drop the table if it already exists, destroying any existing topic embed records. Migrations should not use force: true unless intentional data loss is explicitly desired.

title: Unrelated migration changed to force table recreation
body: This PR modifies the existing create_top_topics migration to use force: true. That change is unrelated to embed handling and can drop an existing top_topics table, losing data if the table already exists in an environment where this migration is applied or reapplied.

title: Feed fetch has no timeouts
body: PollFeed uses open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without configuring connect/read timeouts. A slow or unresponsive feed can hang the job and occupy a Sidekiq worker indefinitely.

title: Controller spec does not test the enqueued job
body: The spec expects TopicRetriever to be instantiated and retrieve directly, but EmbedController#best enqueues Jobs::RetrieveTopic instead. The test therefore does not verify the actual behavior of the controller unless jobs are executed inline, and it does not assert the job arguments.

title: Invalid ERB `end if` will prevent the template from rendering
body: The first conditional is closed with `<%- end if %>`, which compiles to invalid Ruby (`end if` is not legal). Rendering the `best` embed view will raise a syntax error. It should be a plain `<% end %>`.

title: Client-controlled Referer is interpolated into JavaScript without JavaScript escaping
body: The embed layout outputs `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')`. The Referer header is controlled by the embedding page and is not escaped for JavaScript. A crafted referer can break the script context or potentially inject JavaScript into the Discourse origin, and it also controls the postMessage target origin. Use `escape_javascript`/`to_json` and validate the target origin explicitly.

title: URL scheme validation uses line-start anchor instead of string-start anchor
body: `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` uses `^`, which in Ruby matches the beginning of any line. A multiline string containing a non-http scheme followed by a newline and an http URL can pass this check. Use `\A` (and preferably validate the whole URL) to enforce the scheme.

title: Imported URL is interpolated into raw HTML footer without escaping
body: `TopicEmbed.import` appends `"#{url}"` to imported content. The URL is only loosely checked and is not HTML-escaped. Since imported posts use the `raw_html` cook method and are rendered with `raw`, a malicious URL containing quotes, tags, or script can produce stored XSS.

title: `import` assumes `contents` is a non-nil mutable string
body: `TopicEmbed.import` immediately mutates its `contents` argument with `contents << ...`. If a caller passes nil (possible from feed/readability extraction) or a frozen string, the import raises instead of failing cleanly. Validate or normalize the content before appending.

title: `raw_html` cook method bypasses sanitization and is rendered raw
body: The new `cook` path returns `raw` unchanged when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. Imported external HTML is untrusted, and the embed view renders `post.cooked` with `raw`. Without sanitization this enables stored XSS from feeds or retrieved embed pages.

title: `import_remote` opens the URL before validating scheme or safely restricting it
body: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read` before `TopicEmbed.import` applies its http/https check, and `TopicRetriever` only compares the URI host to `embeddable_host`. A URL with a matching host but non-HTTP scheme can reach `open`, allowing unintended fetches or local file access if an open-uri handler supports it. Validate scheme and URL format before opening.

title: postMessage origin check uses substring matching
body: The listener accepts messages when `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) !== -1`. This is not an exact origin comparison; an origin that is a prefix or substring of `discourseUrl` can pass. Compare `e.origin` against the parsed origin of `discourseUrl` exactly.

title: Feed items without content crash the poller
body: `i.content.scrub` assumes every feed item has a content field. RSS/ATOM items may have only description/summary or nil content, causing `NoMethodError`. With `retry: false`, the scheduled job stops. Handle nil content and fall back to other item fields.

title: Post side effects are enqueued before the outer embed transaction commits
body: Inside `Topic.transaction`, `PostCreator#create` runs and enqueues jobs/publishes messages after its own inner transaction but before the surrounding `TopicEmbed` transaction commits. If `TopicEmbed.create!` later fails and the outer transaction rolls back, asynchronous work remains queued for records that were not persisted.

title: Check-then-create embed can raise unique-index errors under concurrency
body: `import` checks for an existing `TopicEmbed` and then creates one, while the database has a unique index on `embed_url`. Concurrent first imports of the same URL can both pass the check; one will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`. Rescue the unique violation and reload/use the existing record.

title: Redis throttle key is set and expired non-atomically
body: `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)` is not atomic. If the process crashes between the two calls, the key can remain without TTL and permanently throttle retrieval for that embed URL. Use an atomic SET with NX and expiration.

title: Embed content SHA is updated even if the revision fails
body: After `PostRevisor#revise!`, `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` runs unconditionally. If the post cannot be revised or saved, the stored SHA no longer matches the post content, causing future content changes to be skipped. Check the revision result before updating the SHA.

title: `absolutize_urls` can raise on borderline URLs
body: `URI(url)` is called without rescuing `URI::InvalidURIError`. The preceding URL check only requires an http(s) prefix, so strings with spaces or other invalid characters can reach this method and crash import/retrieval jobs. Validate or rescue invalid URLs and skip them.

title: `force: true` will drop an existing topic_embeds table
body: The migration creates `topic_embeds` with `force: true`, which drops the table first. If the table already exists from a prior installation or branch, existing embed mappings are destroyed. Avoid `force: true` in migrations that may run against existing data.

title: Adding `force: true` to the top_topics migration can drop data
body: Changing `create_table :top_topics` to use `force: true` makes the migration drop and recreate the table if rerun. This can silently delete existing `top_topics` data. Migrations should not destructively recreate tables that may already contain production data.

title: Script throws if `discourse-comments` element is absent
body: `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` may return null on pages that include `embed.js` but do not have the expected container. The subsequent `comments.appendChild(iframe)` throws and prevents the embed from loading. Guard against the missing element.

title: Flex container breaks existing right-floated small-action button
body: Making .small-action a flex container causes its child button's existing float: right rule to be ignored, because float does not apply to flex items. Unless the button is given a flex-aware rule such as margin-left: auto, it will no longer be positioned at the right edge, causing a layout regression in small-action items.

title: align-items mixin omits -moz-box-align
body: The new align-items() mixin emits -webkit-box-align but not -moz-box-align, even though flexbox() emits display: -moz-box. Browsers that fall back to the old Mozilla box model will not receive the requested alignment, so align-items(center) or align-items(baseline) will not work in that fallback path.

title: order mixin uses CSS order values for older 1-based ordinal-group properties
body: order() passes the same value to -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group, which are 1-based, while the standard order property is 0-based. The current uses with 2 and 3 happen to preserve the intended relative order, but future uses such as order(0) or order(1) will not behave consistently across the prefixed and unprefixed implementations.

title: Small action button can lose right alignment after switching to flexbox
body: `.small-action` is changed to a flex container, but the styles still rely on `float: right` for the action button and do not give `.small-action-desc` flexible growth or give the button `margin-left: auto`. In a flex row, floats on flex items are ignored and non-growing items do not fill the remaining width, so the button may no longer be pushed to the right edge as in the previous float/block layout.

title: align-items mixin omits -moz-box-align for legacy Firefox flexbox
body: The flexbox mixins emit legacy Firefox display values such as `display: -moz-box` and `display: -moz-inline-box`, but `align-items` does not emit the corresponding legacy alignment property `-moz-box-align`. Browsers using that legacy box model will not apply the requested `center` or `baseline` alignment.

title: Invalid -ms-align-items declaration
body: `-ms-align-items` is not a valid Microsoft-prefixed flexbox property. IE10/11 used `-ms-flex-align` for the old syntax or the unprefixed `align-items`, and the mixin already emits both. The extra declaration is invalid CSS and can trigger linter or validator failures.

title: Button in .small-action will no longer be right-aligned
body: Adding `@include flexbox()` to `.small-action` makes its direct children flex items. The existing `button` rule still uses `float: right` (line 309), but float is ignored on flex items, so the button will not be pushed to the right edge as it was in the float-based layout. Use `margin-left: auto`, `order`, or a spacer element to position the button.

title: Header flex container may overflow because flex-wrap is not set
body: `.d-header .contents` is converted to a flex container without setting `flex-wrap`. Flexbox defaults to `nowrap`, so header children such as the title, extra topic info, and panel will stay on one line and can overflow horizontally on narrow viewports, unlike the previous float-based layout that could drop/wrap. Add `flex-wrap: wrap` or appropriate responsive constraints if wrapping is required.

title: align-items mixin has incomplete/invalid legacy flexbox prefixes
body: The `align-items` mixin omits `-moz-box-align` even though `flexbox()`/`inline-flex()` emit `-moz-box`/`-moz-inline-box`, so old Mozilla box implementations will not receive the alignment. It also emits the non-existent `-ms-align-items` property and does not map modern values such as `flex-start`/`flex-end` to the legacy `start`/`end` values. Add `-moz-box-align`, remove `-ms-align-items`, and map values if legacy support is intended.

title: order mixin does not convert values for legacy ordinal groups
body: Legacy 2009 flexbox ordinal groups (`-webkit-box-ordinal-group`, `-moz-box-ordinal-group`) are 1-based, while the standard `order` property is 0-based and can be negative. Passing `$val` unchanged can produce incorrect or invalid ordering in browsers that use the legacy prefixes. Convert the value for those prefixes (for example, add 1 for non-negative orders) or avoid exposing the raw standard value.

title: website_name leaks restricted users' website data
body: `:website_name` is exposed as an ordinary serializer attribute while `:website` is protected by `untrusted_attributes`. When `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` hides a TL0/new user's website from anonymous viewers, `website_name` is still computed from that hidden value and serialized, leaking the host and, for same/related domains, the full path. The derived attribute needs the same restriction, e.g. by adding it to `untrusted_attributes` or by using an equivalent include guard.

title: Inclusion guard is missing the required question mark
body: `def include_website_name` will not be called by ActiveModel::Serializer; the expected hook is `include_website_name?`. As written, the guard `website.present?` has no effect, so the attribute cannot be omitted when blank/invalid and any intended suppression is bypassed. Rename the method to `include_website_name?`, or rely on `untrusted_attributes` to generate the correct guard.

title: Same-domain check misses common reverse subdomain case
body: The fallback only appends the path when the Discourse hostname ends with the website hostname, such as `forum.example.com` versus `example.com`. It does not handle the reverse common case where Discourse is at `example.com` and the user's website is `www.example.com/path`; the result will be `www.example.com` instead of the intended full path. The hostname comparison should handle both directions or compare registrable domains.

title: Naive suffix comparison can treat unrelated hosts as the same domain
body: The code compares hosts by dropping the first label (`host.split('.')[1..-1]`). This does not account for public suffixes or shared platform domains, so hosts such as `foo.github.io` and `bar.github.io` can be considered the same domain and cause the path to be displayed. A proper registrable-domain/public-suffix-aware comparison would avoid false positives.

title: Untrusted-attribute spec does not cover website_name
body: The test that asserts restricted attributes are omitted lists `website` but not the newly added `website_name`. Because `website_name` is derived from the restricted `website`, the spec should include it, preferably with a populated website, to prevent leaking the derived field for TL0 users viewed anonymously.

title: website_name is not properly guarded and can leak restricted website data
body: UserSerializer uses include_<attribute>? methods to decide whether an attribute is serialized. The new method is named include_website_name without the trailing question mark, so it is not used as an inclusion guard. In addition, website_name is derived from website, which is listed in untrusted_attributes, but website_name itself is not treated as untrusted. As a result, a TL0 user's website host/path can be exposed to anonymous viewers even though website is supposed to be hidden. Use include_website_name? and/or add :website_name to untrusted_attributes.

title: Domain comparison can match unrelated hosts and misses some related subdomains
body: The same-domain logic compares raw DNS labels with ends_with? and by stripping the first label, rather than comparing registrable domains. This can treat public suffixes or hosts such as com, co.uk, or shared IP octets as the same domain, showing the full path incorrectly. It also does not handle the reverse subdomain case where the Discourse host is the parent of the website host, for example Discourse at example.com and website at blog.example.com. A proper registrable-domain check or explicit subdomain rules would avoid incorrect display.

title: Spec does not cover website_name visibility for restricted/untrusted users
body: The untrusted_attributes spec list was not updated to include website_name. Since website_name is derived from website and the serializer does not correctly guard it, the current tests will not fail when website_name is leaked for a TL0 user viewed anonymously. Add a test that website_name is absent when website is restricted, and tests for blank/invalid website values.

title: website_name leaks website data for restricted TL0 users
body: UserSerializer adds :website_name to the public attributes but does not add it to untrusted_attributes, unlike :website. When an anonymous or low-trust viewer sees a TL0 user, restrict_user_fields? hides website, but website_name is still serialized. Because website_name is derived from the hidden website, it exposes the user's website host/path. Add :website_name to untrusted_attributes and update the spec.

title: Inclusion guard is missing the question mark
body: include_website_name will not be used by ActiveModel::Serializer, which looks for include_website_name?. As written, the serializer includes website_name unconditionally, even when website is blank, yielding a null field. Rename the method to include_website_name? and base it on the presence of the value that should be exposed.

title: Domain comparison treats unrelated hosts as same
body: The same-domain check drops only the first label of each hostname and compares the rest. This treats unrelated hosts such as forum.co.uk and example.co.uk, or a.github.io and b.github.io, as the same domain, so the serializer will append the website path when it should display only the host. The logic is also asymmetrical for example.com vs www.example.com. Use a proper registrable-domain comparison or a simpler exact/subdomain rule.

title: Untrusted attribute test does not cover website_name
body: The spec's untrusted_attributes list was not updated to include :website_name, so it does not verify that the new derived field is hidden for TL0 users viewed anonymously. Since website is untrusted, the test should also assert that website_name is omitted.

title: website_name can become stale after profile edits
body: The template now binds to model.website_name, but that value is generated on the server and is not recomputed when model.website changes. User#save only updates bio_excerpt from the response, so after editing a profile website the displayed website name can remain stale until a reload. The previous controller computed property observed model.website and avoided this.

title: Light-theme color changed for embedded post author link
body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a`, the previous light-theme color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new code uses `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` for the light-theme branch and `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)` for the dark branch. This makes the author link much lighter in light themes and likely inverts the intended 30/70 pair, reducing readability.

title: Custom message length hint appears to have swapped light/dark values
body: `.custom-message-length` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The change makes the light-theme value 30% and the dark-theme value 70%, which is the opposite of the desktop modal treatment and changes the light-theme text from light gray to dark gray. This looks like an accidental swap.

title: Mobile topic map heading light-theme value changed unexpectedly
body: In `.topic-map h3`, the previous light-theme value was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`, but the new code uses 50% for the light-theme branch. Desktop keeps the 20/80 relationship for the same kind of heading. This changes the existing light-theme appearance and reduces contrast without being required by the dark-theme fix.

title: Group member name light-theme color changed from 30% to 50%
body: `.user-main .user-stream .group-member-info .name` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new code uses 50% in the light-theme branch, altering the existing light-theme contrast rather than only adding a dark-theme alternative.

title: Mobile group member name light-theme color changed from 30% to 50%
body: `.user-main .user-stream .group-member-info .name` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new code uses 50% in the light-theme branch, changing the existing light-theme appearance rather than only adding a dark-theme alternative.

title: Missed scale-color($primary) occurrence in category badge notification
body: `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still uses `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` without `dark-light-choose`. Since the rest of the PR wraps comparable `scale-color($primary, ...)` calls, this occurrence will not use the intended `$secondary`-based value in dark themes.

title: Notification badge may have low contrast in dark themes
body: `.badge-notification` keeps `color: $secondary` while its background becomes `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)` in dark themes. Because both the text color and background are derived from the dark theme's secondary/background color, the badge text may have very low contrast and be hard to read.

title: Dark-theme badge-notification background no longer contrasts with its $secondary text
body: .badge-notification keeps `color: $secondary`, but the new dark-theme background is `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)`. In dark color schemes `$secondary` is the dark background color, so the text and background are both dark and the badge count can become unreadable. Previously the background was based on `$primary`, which is light in dark schemes and preserved contrast with `$secondary` text.

title: Embedded-reply author link color uses inverted/wrong lightness values
body: The original color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but it was changed to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. This makes the author link much lighter in light themes and much darker in dark themes, while comparable username links use 30% in light themes and 70% in dark themes. The result is poor contrast/inconsistent styling for `.topic-meta-data h5 a`.

title: Mobile topic-map h3 lightness changed from 20% to 50%
body: The original `.topic-map h3` color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`, but the change uses 50% for both light and dark themes. The desktop equivalent uses 20% in light themes and 80% in dark themes. This reduces heading contrast/prominence on mobile and creates an inconsistency with desktop styling.

title: Mobile custom-message-length values appear swapped relative to desktop
body: Desktop modal uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))` for the same hint text, preserving the original 70% light-theme value. Mobile now uses 30%/70%, changing the light-theme appearance and making the two views inconsistent. This looks like the light/dark values were accidentally swapped.

title: Group member name color changed from 30% to 50% in light themes
body: `.group-member-info .name` originally used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but the change uses 50% for both light and dark themes. This alters the existing light-theme contrast and makes the name color identical to `.title`. If the intent was only to add a dark-theme equivalent, the expected pair would be 30% for light and 70% for dark.

title: Mobile group member name color changed from 30% to 50% in light themes
body: `.group-member-info .name` originally used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but the change uses 50% for both light and dark themes. This changes the existing light-theme appearance and removes the visual distinction from `.title`. If this was not an intentional design change, the dark-theme replacement should preserve the original 30% light-theme value.

title: Comment no longer matches the coldmap color implementation
body: The comment says the default table cell color is `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`, but the surrounding styles now use `dark-light-choose(...)` with a secondary-based value for dark themes. The comment should be updated to avoid misleading future maintainers.

title: Dark-theme badge notification background may have very low contrast with its text
body: .badge-notification sets its text color to $secondary, while this change makes its background dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 70%), scale-color($secondary, 30%)). In a dark scheme, $secondary is the dark background/text color, so the dark-theme branch produces a dark background with dark text. The previous primary-based light background gave contrast with $secondary text; the new value can make notification counts hard or impossible to read.

title: Embedded-post author link color appears inverted, reducing contrast
body: The rule for .embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a previously used scale-color($primary, 30%). It was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 70%), scale-color($secondary, 30%)), which makes the light-theme color much lighter and the dark-theme color much darker. Comparable author/name links use 30% in light schemes and 70% of $secondary in dark schemes, so this looks reversed and will make the link faint in both themes.

title: Mobile custom-message-length uses inverted light/dark lightness values
body: .custom-message-length was changed from scale-color($primary, 70%) to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 30%), scale-color($secondary, 70%)). The desktop modal uses 70% for light schemes and 30% for dark schemes for this subtle caption. The mobile change therefore changes the light-theme appearance and likely provides the wrong dark-theme contrast; it should probably remain primary 70% / secondary 30% if the intent is to preserve the existing visual hierarchy.

title: Mobile topic-map heading color was changed in light theme as well as dark theme
body: .topic-map h3 originally used scale-color($primary, 20%). The change replaces it with dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 50%), scale-color($secondary, 50%)), which lightens the heading substantially in light schemes and does not use the expected high-lightness secondary value for dark schemes. The desktop equivalent preserves the 20% light value and uses 80% for dark schemes, so this looks like an incorrect replacement rather than a dark-theme-only fix.

title: Category badge notification color still uses only $primary
body: In .topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification, the color remains scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%) while nearby topic-list text colors were converted to dark-light-choose with a $secondary-based dark-theme value. This leaves one similar text color using the old primary-based calculation, causing inconsistent dark-theme styling.

title: Public group members page only loads first 50 members
body: The route calls model.findMembers(), and Discourse.Group defaults limit to 50. The group members template iterates members and has no pagination controls, so groups with more than 50 members will display an incomplete member list. Previously non-automatic groups loaded all members.

title: Members endpoint accepts unbounded and negative limit/offset
body: limit and offset are taken directly from request parameters without validation. Negative values can generate invalid SQL, limit=0 produces a zero limit in meta, and an arbitrarily large limit can load and serialize every member of a group from a public endpoint. Clamp limit to a sane positive maximum and ensure offset is non-negative.

title: totalPages adds an extra page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
body: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is exactly divisible by limit (for example 50 users with limit 50), this returns 2 instead of 1. That makes showingLast false on the real last page and allows Next to request an empty page. Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit), with special handling for zero users.

title: Admin group route does not reset pagination offset
body: setupController calls model.findMembers() without resetting the group's offset. Admin group models are cached in the adminGroups controller, so a previously selected page offset can persist. Returning to a group may load a later page or an empty page instead of the first page of members. Reset offset before calling findMembers.

title: findMembers clamps offset to user_count instead of the last valid page start
body: findMembers clamps offset with Math.min(user_count, Math.max(offset, 0)). An offset equal to user_count is a page past the end and will return no members. The offset should be clamped to a valid page start, for example Math.max(0, user_count - limit), or otherwise normalized before requesting members.

title: Group creation ignores alias_level sent by the client
body: The admin UI sends alias_level in Group.asJSON when creating a group, but the create action only assigns name and visible. The group is persisted with the default alias_level while the client-side model still holds the selected value, causing the UI and database to disagree until another explicit save occurs. Create should assign alias_level or the client should not send it on create.

title: add_members silently skips invalid usernames
body: add_members splits the usernames string and ignores any token that does not match a user. It also does not strip whitespace around tokens. The endpoint still returns success, so an admin can mistype usernames or paste a malformed list and receive no indication that some or all users were not added. Invalid or skipped usernames should be reported.

title: Breaking change to /groups/:group_id/members response shape
body: The members endpoint previously rendered an array of serialized users, but now returns an object with members and meta. Any external client, plugin, or script consuming the old array response will break. If this endpoint is considered a public or stable API, the change needs compatibility handling or clear versioning/documentation.

title: remove_member spec uses PUT instead of DELETE
body: The route for remove_member is a DELETE route, but the automatic-group test issues xhr :put, :remove_member. This does not exercise the actual route/verb and can mask routing regressions. The test should use xhr :delete.

title: No specs for the new paginated members endpoint
body: The public members action was changed to accept limit/offset and return members plus meta, but there are no controller/request specs covering normal paging, total counts, invalid/negative/huge limit or offset values, or permissions. Add tests for the new response contract and edge cases.

title: add_members assumes usernames parameter is a string
body: params.require(:usernames) is passed directly to split. If a client sends usernames as an array, for example usernames[], split raises NoMethodError and the endpoint returns a 500 instead of a validation error. Validate/coerce the parameter or accept arrays.

title: remove_member treats invalid user_id as 0
body: user_id is coerced with to_i, so non-numeric values become 0. The action may then perform no deletion and still return success. The controller should validate that user_id identifies a real user and that the user is a member before reporting success.

title: Save error handler assumes JSON errors payload
body: The save failure handler does $.parseJSON(e.responseText).errors. If the server returns non-JSON, an empty response, or JSON without an errors property, this throws and the user receives no useful error message. Use safer error handling consistent with Discourse's AJAX error conventions.

title: Unclosed/malformed each block in group member list
body: The template uses `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` without a corresponding `{{/each}}` and without block syntax (`{{#each ...}}`). In Ember/Handlebars this will either fail template compilation or cause the surrounding markup to be treated incorrectly, breaking the admin group member list.

title: remove_member deletes with an integer ID instead of a user record
body: `group.users.delete(user_id)` passes an integer ID to an ActiveRecord association `delete`, which expects User records (and may not behave correctly for a through association). This is likely a no-op or raises an exception, so members may not actually be removed. Use the join association or load the user first, e.g. `group.group_users.where(user_id: user_id).destroy_all` or `group.users.find(user_id)` followed by `group.users.delete(user)`.

title: totalPages overcounts when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
body: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When the member count is exactly divisible by the page limit (for example 50 members with limit 50), this returns one extra page. The UI will show an extra page and allow navigating to an empty member list.

title: findMembers allows offset equal to total user_count
body: `findMembers` clamps offset with `Math.min(this.get("user_count"), ...)`, which permits `offset == user_count`. That requests a page starting after the last record and returns an empty list. The clamp should prevent moving past the last valid page, or pagination should be computed from page numbers rather than allowing offset equal to total.

title: Public members endpoint does not validate limit/offset
body: The public members endpoint accepts arbitrary `limit` and `offset` values and only calls `.to_i`. Negative values can produce invalid SQL or errors, `limit=0` can cause confusing client behavior, and very large limits can load and serialize all group members. This creates a resource-exhaustion risk on a public endpoint.

title: Group creation ignores submitted alias_level
body: The JavaScript model sends `alias_level` when creating a group, but the `create` action only assigns `name` and `visible`. Any alias level chosen while creating a new group is silently discarded, so the group is created with the default alias level.

title: Members endpoint response shape changed from array to object
body: The members endpoint now returns `{ members: ..., meta: ... }` instead of a serialized array. This changes the public JSON contract and will break existing API clients or integrations that expect the previous array response.

title: add_members silently ignores invalid usernames and whitespace
body: `add_members` splits the comma-separated usernames without stripping whitespace and ignores unknown usernames. A payload like `'a, b'` may fail to match `' b'`, and the action still returns success even if no valid users were added, giving administrators no feedback about failed additions.

title: visible parameter handling only accepts the string 'true'
body: `params[:visible] == "true"` treats JSON boolean `true` as false. If an API client sends a JSON payload with `visible: true`, the group will be saved as not visible. The controller should cast the parameter using a boolean-aware conversion.

title: Save error handler assumes JSON error payload
body: The save failure handler executes `$.parseJSON(e.responseText).errors`. If the request fails with no response body, a non-JSON body, or a different error format, this line throws and masks the original failure instead of showing a useful error message.

title: remove_member automatic-group test uses PUT instead of DELETE
body: The spec tests `remove_member` with `xhr :put`, but the route is defined as DELETE. This does not exercise the real HTTP verb/route and can hide routing or method mismatches.

title: No specs cover the changed public members endpoint
body: The public `members` action was changed to add pagination metadata and a new response envelope, but no controller/request specs cover the new payload shape, limit/offset behavior, invalid parameters, or authorization boundaries.

title: Member list uses an invalid non-block each helper
body: The template uses {{each member in members itemView="group-member"}} without the block form {{#each ...}} and without a closing {{/each}}. In Ember/Handlebars this will not render the collection (or may fail to compile), so the admin group page will not display members even though the controller/model load them.

title: Group member item view template name appears wrong
body: The view sets templateName to 'admin/templates/group_member'. Discourse/Ember template names are normally registered without the 'templates' segment, e.g. 'admin/group_member'. If the resolver follows that convention, this view will not find its template and each member item will render blank even if the each helper is fixed.

title: totalPages is off by one for exact multiples of limit
body: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is exactly divisible by limit, such as 50 users with limit 50, it returns 2 pages instead of 1. This allows the UI to navigate to an empty extra page.

title: findMembers allows an offset equal to the total member count
body: findMembers clamps offset to Math.min(user_count, offset), but the last valid offset is generally user_count - limit. Allowing offset == user_count requests an empty page. This can happen after deleting the last member on the last page or via the pagination next logic, leaving the UI showing no members.

title: Group members endpoint accepts unbounded and negative pagination values
body: The members action uses params[:limit].to_i and params[:offset].to_i without validating bounds. A client can request an extremely large limit, causing a large database query and serialization, or negative limit/offset values, which can trigger database errors. This is an availability risk on an endpoint that may be accessible to non-admin users.

title: add_members silently ignores invalid or whitespace-padded usernames
body: add_members splits the usernames string and only adds users found by User.find_by_username. It does not strip whitespace and does not report unknown usernames. If some or all usernames are invalid, the action still returns success, so the admin UI indicates members were added when they were not.

title: create ignores alias_level sent by the client
body: The client sends alias_level when creating a group, but Admin::GroupsController#create only assigns name and visible. Any alias level selected while creating a new group is discarded, and the group is created with the default alias level.

title: update resets visible to false on partial updates
