If a real DB implementation is reintroduced, or TablesList is changed to succeed, this entry point would allow SQL expressions despite the guard added in ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery. The disablement should be enforced in NewSQLCommand/UnmarshalSQLCommand or the SQL path should be removed.

title: enableSqlExpressions logic is inverted and always returns false
body: enableSqlExpressions sets enabled to the negation of FlagSqlExpressions and then returns false in both branches. The feature toggle therefore has no effect and the code does not communicate that SQL expressions are intentionally hard-disabled. A future change could easily misread this and accidentally re-enable the feature. If the intent is permanent disablement, return false unconditionally or remove the toggle; if the toggle should matter, fix the condition.

title: No automated regression test for disabled SQL expressions
body: The PR disables SQL expressions to address CVE-2024-9264 but adds no unit test asserting that QueryTypeSQL queries are rejected and that SQL command execution cannot reach a database implementation. Because this is a security boundary, an automated test is needed to prevent accidental re-enablement when dependencies or parsing code change.

title: NoData result is immediately overwritten by TableData
body: In Execute, when frame.Rows()==0, rsp.Values is set to mathexp.NoData, but the following unconditional assignment replaces it with mathexp.TableData. The no-data branch therefore has no effect. This is currently masked because the stubbed DB returns an error before reaching this code, but if SQL execution is ever restored, zero-row results will be returned as table data instead of NoData.

title: Nil pointer dereference in reduce expression replace mode
body: In ReadQuery, when a reduce query has settings.mode set to Replace but replaceWithValue is absent, the code sets err at line 83 and then dereferences q.Settings.ReplaceWithValue unconditionally at line 85. This panics before the error is returned. A malformed expression query can crash query handling. Return immediately after the nil check or only dereference when non-nil.

title: Unload threshold command used before error check
body: In the threshold branch, NewThresholdCommand for firstCondition.UnloadEvaluator may return an error and a nil command, but unloading.Invert is set on line 162 before err is checked on line 163. An invalid unload evaluator can therefore cause a nil pointer dereference. Check the error before mutating unloading.

title: FlagSqlExpressions is ignored by always-false enablement helper
body: enableSqlExpressions computes enabled as !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions) and then returns false in both branches. The feature flag cannot enable SQL expressions, and the helper's name/logic are misleading. If SQL expressions are intentionally hard-disabled for security, return false explicitly and deprecate/remove the flag or update docs; otherwise this dead/inverted logic invites accidental misuse.

title: No automated test locks in the SQL-expression disablement
body: The PR makes QueryTypeSQL return an error and removes the DuckDB implementation, but no test is added to verify that SQL expressions are rejected, including when FlagSqlExpressions is enabled. Without a regression test, a future change could silently re-enable the vulnerable SQL expression path.

title: NoData result is immediately overwritten by TableData
body: In SQLCommand.Execute, when frame.Rows() == 0 the code sets rsp.Values to NoData at lines 111-113, then unconditionally overwrites rsp.Values with TableData at line 116. The zero-row NoData case is therefore never returned. This is currently dormant because SQL execution is stubbed/disabled, but it will produce incorrect results if the SQL path is re-enabled.

title: enableSqlExpressions is dead/inverted and ignores the feature toggle
body: The helper computes enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions) but then returns false in both branches. As a result FlagSqlExpressions has no effect and the code reads as though it might enable SQL expressions when it never can. If the intent is a hard security disable, return false unconditionally or remove the SQL path; if the intent is toggle-controlled behavior, the current logic is wrong. This leaves a misleading feature-toggle contract for operators and future maintainers.

title: No automated test verifies that SQL expressions are disabled
body: The security fix adds a gate in ReadQuery for QueryTypeSQL but no unit test is included. Without a test asserting that a SQL expression query returns an error both when FlagSqlExpressions is enabled and disabled, a future refactor could accidentally re-enable the SQL expression path and reintroduce the vulnerability.

title: Zero-row SQL result NoData value is immediately overwritten
body: In SQLCommand.Execute, when frame.Rows() == 0 the code sets rsp.Values to mathexp.NoData, but the following unconditional assignment replaces it with mathexp.TableData. Therefore the no-data case is never returned. SQL expressions are currently disabled, but if this code path is ever reached the result type will be wrong for empty results.

title: Cache lock no longer prevents concurrent index builds for the same key
body: BuildIndex now only locks cacheMu when inserting into b.cache. It does not prevent two goroutines from building the same NamespacedResource concurrently. searchSupport.getOrCreateIndex can call BuildIndex concurrently for a missing index (search requests plus the watch event handler). Concurrent builds can create duplicate indexes, overwrite the cache entry, lose watch writes already applied to the replaced index, and for file-backed indexes may contend on the same directory. A per-key lock/singleflight or check-for-existing under lock is needed.

title: TotalDocs reads the index cache without locking
body: TotalDocs ranges over b.cache without acquiring cacheMu, while BuildIndex can write to the map concurrently (now only briefly locked). Concurrent map iteration and write can race and panic. It should take cacheMu.RLock before iterating.

title: errgroup workers share outer err and increment counter without synchronization
body: In searchSupport.init, each errgroup worker assigns to the outer err variable from GetResourceStats and increments totalBatchesIndexed without atomics or a mutex. Because group.Go runs concurrently, this is a data race; the span count is unreliable and a worker can return an error value that another goroutine overwrote. Use a local err inside the closure and an atomic counter or mutex for totalBatchesIndexed.

title: Initial index build discards the resource version, allowing missed events
body: searchSupport.build returns the resource version it indexed up to, but init discards that value and only after all builds calls storage.WatchWriteEvents, which starts from the backend's current latest version. Events written between the initial list/build and starting the watch are not replayed into the index, so the search index can remain stale. Start watching before backfilling or pass/use the returned resource version.

title: Search watch loop does not handle channel closure and cannot be canceled
body: The watch goroutine started in searchSupport.init reads from events without checking whether the channel is closed and uses context.Background. If the backend closes the watch channel (for example during Stop), the receive returns nil repeatedly and handleEvent will dereference a nil event, causing a panic or busy loop; the goroutine also cannot be canceled by ResourceServer.Stop. Use the server context and a comma-ok/select loop.

title: History and Origin dereference s.search without nil check
body: When search is not configured, s.search is nil. Search guards for nil, but History and Origin call s.search.History and s.search.Origin directly, causing a nil pointer panic if those gRPC methods are invoked. Add nil checks or return a clear configuration error.

title: initWatcher event-forwarding loop does not handle channel closure
body: The event-forwarding goroutine in initWatcher reads from the backend watch channel without checking ok. If the backend closes the channel, v is nil and the next log/metric access dereferences v, causing a panic during shutdown or backend failure. It should handle channel closure and context cancellation.

title: Init failure leaks context cancel and lifecycle resources
body: NewResourceServer creates a cancellable context and may run lifecycle.Init before calling s.Init. If s.Init fails, the constructor returns without calling cancel or stopping lifecycle hooks, leaking the context and any resources started during initialization. Cleanup should be performed on failure.

title: Data race in search init worker pool
body: In searchSupport.init, totalBatchesIndexed is incremented inside errgroup.Go closures that run concurrently, and the same closures assign to the outer err variable when calling s.build. Neither variable is protected by a mutex or atomic, so this is a data race. The trace/metric count can be wrong and concurrent writes to err can produce undefined error handling.

title: Watch pump cannot be stopped and can panic on closed channel
body: The event pump started in searchSupport.init receives from events without checking whether the channel is closed and uses context.Background rather than a cancellable server context. If the storage backend closes the event channel during shutdown, the loop receives nil values indefinitely and handleEvent will dereference a nil *WrittenEvent. The goroutine also cannot be stopped by server shutdown.

title: Initial index build can miss writes that happen during startup
body: searchSupport.init builds all indexes first and only then calls storage.WatchWriteEvents. The resource versions returned by build are discarded, so mutations that occur while an index is being built, and before the watch starts, are neither included in the initial build nor replayed from the watch. This can leave the search index stale for affected resources until another mutation happens for that resource.

title: Concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key are no longer serialized
body: BuildIndex no longer holds the backend-wide lock during the expensive build, and searchSupport.getOrCreateIndex has no per-key single-flight. Two concurrent requests for the same missing namespace/resource can both call BuildIndex, duplicate expensive work, and both write b.cache[key], with the last write silently replacing the other index. For file-backed Bleve indexes this may also contend on the same index directory.

title: TotalDocs iterates cache map without locking
body: TotalDocs ranges over b.cache without acquiring cacheMu, while BuildIndex mutates the same map under cacheMu. This is a concurrent map read/write race that can panic or return incorrect document counts, especially now that index builds are more concurrent.

title: Existing Bleve index is replaced without being closed
body: BuildIndex stores the newly created index in b.cache[key] without closing any previous index for that key. If a concurrent or repeated build replaces an existing entry, the old Bleve index remains open, leaking memory/file handles and potentially holding directory locks.

title: File-backed BuildIndex may reuse stale documents from previous runs
body: For file-backed indexes, bleve.New(dir, mapper) opens an existing Bleve directory if present. BuildIndex then writes current documents but never removes documents that no longer exist, for example resources deleted while the process was stopped. Unless the directory is ephemeral, stale/deleted resources can remain searchable after restart.

title: Nil IndexMetrics can panic in handleEvent
body: handleEvent increments and decrements IndexMetrics.IndexedKinds without checking whether IndexMetrics is nil, while other call sites guard for nil. If metrics are not initialized, processing an ADDED or DELETED watch event will panic.

title: Nil IndexMetrics can panic in Bleve BuildIndex
body: BuildIndex increments resource.IndexMetrics.IndexTenants without checking whether resource.IndexMetrics is nil. Since other code treats IndexMetrics as optional, this can panic during index creation when metrics are not initialized.

title: DocCount error can skip Flush and fail the whole build
body: index.DocCount is called only for metrics/logging, but its error overwrites err and then prevents index.Flush from running and causes the build to fail. A doc-count failure should not abort index creation or skip flushing; use a separate error variable for DocCount.

title: No cleanup when NewResourceServer initialization fails
body: NewResourceServer calls s.Init(ctx) and returns immediately on error without calling cancel or Stop. If initialization partially succeeded before the failure, for example lifecycle hooks ran or the search watch started, the constructed server's context and goroutines/resources are leaked.

title: History and Origin can nil-pointer panic when search is disabled
body: History and Origin call s.search.History and s.search.Origin without checking whether s.search is nil. NewResourceServer can create a server with search disabled, so these gRPC methods will nil-pointer panic instead of returning a not-configured error like Search does.

title: Postgres integration test is skipped
body: The postgres integration test is now skipped, removing coverage for a supported database path at the same time startup initialization behavior changes. Postgres-specific regressions may go undetected unless this skip is tracked and temporary.

title: Shared variables are written concurrently in search init
body: In searchSupport.init, each errgroup goroutine assigns to the outer err variable and increments totalBatchesIndexed without synchronization. This is a data race: the stored error and counter are nondeterministic, and race-detector runs will fail. Use a local error per goroutine and an atomic counter or channel.

title: Initial index build can miss writes that occur while building
body: searchSupport.init builds indexes first and discards the resource version returned by build, then calls WatchWriteEvents after all builds are complete. The watch starts from the latest resource version at that later time, so writes that happen during the potentially long initial build are not applied to the new indexes. This can leave search results stale until affected resources are written again. Start watching before building or backfill events from the RV returned by build.

title: Watch event goroutine does not handle a closed events channel
body: The goroutine in searchSupport.init receives from events with a single-value receive and ignores whether the channel is closed. If the storage backend closes the channel, the loop receives nil events forever and handleEvent will dereference a nil *WrittenEvent, causing a panic or tight loop. Use v, ok := <-events and return when !ok, and select on a cancellable context.

title: Search watcher is started with an uncancellable background context
body: searchSupport.init creates watchctx := context.Background() and starts an event-processing goroutine with no way to stop it. server.Stop cancels the server context but does not cancel this context, so the goroutine can leak, especially in tests or when resource servers are recreated. Use a cancellable context tied to the server lifecycle.

title: IndexMetrics is used without nil checks in event handling
body: handleEvent updates IndexMetrics.IndexedKinds for ADDED and DELETED events without checking whether IndexMetrics is nil, while other code paths in the same file guard with if IndexMetrics != nil. If metrics are not initialized, the first watch event will panic. Add nil checks or ensure metrics are always initialized.

title: History and Origin can panic when search is not configured
body: server.History and server.Origin call s.search.History and s.search.Origin without checking whether s.search is nil. server.Search performs this check, but History and Origin do not. If the resource server is created without search support and these gRPC methods are called, the server will panic. Return a not-configured error when s.search is nil.

title: Update swallows backend read errors
body: In server.Update, if s.backend.ReadResource returns a response with Error set, the method returns an empty UpdateResponse and a nil error without setting rsp.Error. Clients cannot distinguish a backend failure from a successful response with no data. Propagate the backend error in rsp.Error or return an error.

title: Constructor does not clean up when Init fails
body: NewResourceServer creates a cancelable context and may initialize lifecycle/search state, but if s.Init fails it returns without calling cancel or stopping lifecycle hooks. This can leak goroutines or backend resources during failed startups or in tests. Call cancel and appropriate cleanup before returning the error.

title: BuildIndex no longer serializes builds for the same index key
body: The global cache lock was removed from bleveBackend.BuildIndex, and only the final cache insertion is locked. searchSupport.getOrCreateIndex has no single-flight or per-key lock, so concurrent requests for a missing index can call BuildIndex for the same NamespacedResource simultaneously. This can create duplicate memory indexes, concurrently open or write the same file-based directory, and overwrite the cache entry, causing wasted work, leaks, or corrupted indexes. Add per-key locking or single-flight semantics.

title: TotalDocs iterates cache without holding cacheMu
body: bleveBackend.TotalDocs ranges over b.cache without acquiring cacheMu.RLock, while BuildIndex writes to b.cache under cacheMu.Lock. Concurrent map reads and writes can panic or return inconsistent counts. Add a read lock around the iteration.

title: Replacing a cache entry does not close the previous index
body: BuildIndex assigns the newly built bleveIndex into b.cache without closing any existing index for the same key. If a rebuild or a concurrent build race replaces an entry, the old bleve.Index remains open, leaking memory/file handles and possibly retaining locks on file-based indexes. Close or remove old indexes when replacing cache entries.

title: Poller span is not ended when listLatestRVs fails
body: In backend.poller, a span is started for each poll tick. If b.listLatestRVs returns an error, the code logs and continues without calling span.End(), leaking tracing state. End the span before continuing, for example with defer or an explicit span.End().

title: Span name has a doubled dot
body: GetResourceStats creates a span with tracePrefix + '.GetResourceStats' while tracePrefix already ends with a dot, producing 'sql.resource..GetResourceStats'. Use tracePrefix + 'GetResourceStats' or adjust the prefix.

title: Call to undefined no-argument isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()
body: UsernameForm.authenticate() calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only method added/available in UsernamePasswordForm is isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel). No no-arg method is defined in the shown class hierarchy, so this will not compile.

title: Passkey conditional UI is disabled whenever the context user is null
body: UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) returns false when user is null, and it is used in authenticate() and challenge() to decide whether to fill WebAuthn conditional UI data. On first login, and after a failed username/password attempt before context.setUser() has been called, context.getUser() is null. The previous code filled WebAuthn data in the null-user case; the new code does not. This breaks passkey autofill/discoverable-key login for new sessions and passkey retry after a failed first login.

title: Conditional passkey suppresses authenticator list but not shouldDisplayAuthenticators
body: WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator overrides shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() to false to avoid showing passkey authenticator lists, but it does not override shouldDisplayAuthenticators(). During re-authentication with a known user, WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm() will still set SHOULD_DISPLAY_AUTHENTICATORS to true while not setting ALLOWED_AUTHENTICATORS. This can produce an inconsistent or empty authenticator UI, contrary to the stated intent.

title: Undefined no-argument isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() call
body: UsernameForm.authenticate calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments. The changed sources only add protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) in UsernamePasswordForm and do not define a no-argument method in UsernameForm, UsernamePasswordForm, or AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator. As written this will not compile; use the new overload, for example isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), or add the missing no-arg helper.

title: Passkey conditional UI is no longer initialized for unauthenticated first login
body: authenticate() now calls webauthnAuth.fillContextForm only when isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) is true, and that helper returns false when the user is null. The previous code explicitly filled the WebAuthn context in the user==null branch, so the initial login page, and error pages before a user is identified via the challenge override at line 137, no longer receive the WebAuthn challenge and conditional-UI attributes. This breaks first-time passkey/discoverable-credential login and contradicts the updated tests that expect the webauthn form on the initial login page.

title: Call to undefined method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()
body: UsernameForm.authenticate calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments. The superclass UsernamePasswordForm only defines isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) in this PR, and no no-argument method exists in this class or its parents. This is a compile-time error. The intended call is likely isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), or a no-arg helper needs to be added.

title: Conditional passkey setup is skipped when no user is known
body: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) returns false unless user != null. Both authenticate (line 115) and the error challenge override (line 137) use this method to decide whether to call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context). On the initial login screen and after errors such as unknown username, context.getUser() is null, so the WebAuthn conditional UI challenge/attributes are not set. This regresses passkey login from the first login form and contradicts tests that expect the webauth form on the initial page.

title: Update invalidation uses organization-aware model and can miss login-cache invalidation
body: In update(), the original model is fetched via getById(), which wraps the IDP so isEnabled() also requires the linked organization to be enabled. registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate() then uses this wrapped model in getLoginPredicate(). If the organization is disabled, the original predicate evaluates to false even when the IDP itself is enabled/public. An update that changes hideOnLogin, linkOnly, or brokerPublic to another non-login state can then satisfy !P(original) && !P(updated) and skip invalidation. The login cache may keep the IDP, and when the organization is re-enabled getForLogin can return a hidden, link-only, or non-public organization broker. Use the raw delegate model for the original state or compare the login-relevant fields directly instead of relying on the organization-aware predicate result.

title: Cached getForLogin results are returned without re-validating login predicate
body: getForLogin() caches only internal IDP IDs and, when serving from cache, loads each IDP and returns it without re-applying LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() or checking that the model is still enabled, not hidden, not link-only, and public if organization-linked. Organization state changes do not invalidate this cache, and the update invalidation logic can miss changes while an organization is disabled. As a result, the method can return IDPs that no longer satisfy the SPI contract for login-suitable providers. The changed login-page caller only re-checks isEnabled(), not hideOnLogin/linkOnly/brokerPublic, so stale entries can still be exposed.

title: Test cleanup removes literal "alias" instead of created identity provider aliases
body: The cleanup registration uses testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove with the literal string "alias" instead of the variable alias used when creating the provider. The same mistake appears in testCacheIDPForLogin at lines 381 and 425 for the created idp-alias-* providers. Consequently the test does not remove the identity providers it creates, leaking realm state and potentially making other tests or assertions flaky.

title: Test cleanup registers removal of literal "alias" instead of the created IDP aliases
body: In testCacheIDPForLogin, the cleanup added inside the creation loop uses testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias") instead of the alias actually created ("idp-alias-" + i). The same mistake occurs at line 425 for "idp-alias-20". As a result, the identity providers created by this test are not removed by the registered cleanup, which can leave stale providers in the test realm and affect other tests. The cleanup should capture and use the generated alias.

title: Null and empty-string organizationId share the same cache search key
body: getForLogin uses `organizationId != null ? organizationId : ""` as the search key. A call with `organizationId == null` and a call with an empty-string `organizationId` therefore collide in the cache, even though the delegate query treats empty string as a non-null organization filter and can return a different result. Once one variant is cached, the other may return stale or incorrect providers. A distinct sentinel for null, or a key that preserves the null/non-null distinction, would avoid this. For FetchMode.REALM_ONLY, organizationId is ignored by the query, so keying by it also creates unnecessary cache entries.

title: getForLogin does not consider organization invalidation for organization-specific results
body: getForLogin can cache organization-specific results under the same per-mode cache key, but it only bypasses the cache when the login cache key itself is invalid. Unlike getByOrganization, which also checks `isInvalid(orgId)`, this method does not check whether the supplied organizationId has been invalidated. If an organization is removed or invalidated without an IDP create/update/remove also invalidating the login cache key, a stale organization-specific login list may be served. Consider bypassing the cache when `organizationId != null && isInvalid(organizationId)` or ensuring all organization changes invalidate these login keys.

title: Login cache entry per FetchMode can accumulate unbounded organization search keys
body: For each realm and FetchMode, getForLogin stores all organization-specific results in a single IdentityProviderListQuery, using the organizationId as a search key inside that entry. In realms with many organizations, this single cache entry can grow without bound and is rewritten whenever a new organizationId is queried (see the invalidate/merge path around lines 234-241). This can cause memory pressure and cache churn. A per-organization cache key or some bound/eviction strategy would be more scalable.

title: Possible NullPointerException in remove() for unknown alias when cache key is invalid
body: remove(alias) fetches `storedIdp` from the delegate, which is null if the alias does not exist. If `isInvalid(cacheKey)` is true, the code calls `registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp)`, which dereferences the model and will throw a NullPointerException. remove() should safely return false for unknown aliases; guard against a null storedIdp before invalidating, or make registerIDPInvalidation null-safe.

title: Login-cache invalidation on update can miss changes because it uses an organization-aware model
body: update() retrieves the current identity provider via getById(), which returns an organization-aware wrapper whose isEnabled() also checks whether the linked organization exists and is enabled. registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate() then applies LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate(), whose ENABLED filter calls this overridden isEnabled(). If the linked organization is disabled or missing, the original model is treated as not available for login even though it may still be present in the .idp.login cache. An update that changes hideOnLogin, linkOnly, or BROKER_PUBLIC while the organization is disabled can therefore hit the 'both not login' no-invalidation branch, leaving stale cached login lists. When the organization is enabled again, getForLogin() can return identity providers that should now be hidden, link-only, or not public. The invalidation decision should be based on the raw persisted IDP fields (or the delegate model), not the organization-aware dynamic isEnabled(), and/or organization lifecycle changes should invalidate these login caches.

title: REALM_ONLY login cache entries are duplicated per organizationId
body: getForLogin() uses organizationId as the search key for all fetch modes. For FetchMode.REALM_ONLY the organizationId parameter is semantically ignored, so calls with different organization IDs can create separate cached search entries under the same REALM_ONLY cache key containing the same realm-level identity providers. This wastes cache space and can cause unnecessary delegate lookups. For REALM_ONLY, organizationId should be normalized to the empty search key.

title: Single login cache entry accumulates results for all organization IDs
body: The login cache is keyed only by realm and FetchMode, while different organizationId values are stored as additional search keys inside the same IdentityProviderListQuery. In realms with many organizations, the ORG_ONLY/ALL cache entry can grow without bound as distinct organization logins occur, and any qualifying identity-provider change invalidates the whole entry. This can create a large cache object and a contention hotspot. Consider per-organization cache keys or another strategy to bound the accumulated search-key state.

title: Cleanup removes literal "alias" instead of the created identity provider aliases
body: In testCacheIDPForLogin, the cleanup registration uses testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove instead of the actual created alias ("idp-alias-" + i). The same mistake occurs later for idp-alias-20. As a result, the test does not clean up the identity providers it creates and may attempt to remove a nonexistent provider named "alias", leaking realm state or causing cleanup failures.

title: New non-default order() method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: CryptoProvider is a public interface, and this PR adds int order() as an abstract method. Any existing implementation compiled against the previous interface will fail to compile against the new API and can fail at runtime with AbstractMethodError when provider selection calls order(). Adding a default order() implementation would preserve compatibility.

title: Provider selection is undefined when multiple providers have the same order
body: detectProvider sorts discovered CryptoProvider instances only by order() and then picks the first one. Existing full providers such as DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider all return 200. If two providers with the same order are present, the selected provider depends on ServiceLoader iteration order, while the others are only logged at debug level. A misconfigured classpath can therefore silently select the wrong crypto provider.

title: Ignored crypto providers are still instantiated and may mutate global security state
body: detectProvider loads and instantiates every discovered CryptoProvider before choosing one. Some providers perform global JCA registration or security-property changes in their constructors, for example FIPS1402Provider. Because this PR allows multiple providers to be present and only selects the highest-order one, an ignored provider can still register security providers or alter JVM-wide security state even though it is not the selected CryptoProvider.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns an unrelated default KeyStore provider
body: AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider returns KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider(). This returns whatever JCA provider implements the default keystore type, often a JDK provider, not a BouncyCastle provider. Callers using CryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider may therefore receive an unexpected provider and behave incorrectly.

title: concatenatedRSToASN1DER does not validate the input signature length
body: concatenatedRSToASN1DER assumes the supplied signature array has exactly signLength bytes. If it is shorter, System.arraycopy throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException; if it is longer, extra bytes are silently ignored. Malformed signature input should be validated and rejected with IOException instead.

title: ECDSA conversion silently truncates oversized integer values
body: In asn1derToConcatenatedRS, integerToBytes copies only the last qLength bytes when BigInteger.toByteArray() is longer than expected. For a malformed DER signature whose R or S value is larger than the expected coordinate size, high-order bytes are silently discarded instead of rejecting the signature. This can hide malformed input and produce an incorrect concatenated RS signature.

title: Indefinite-length ASN.1 integer causes NegativeArraySizeException
body: readLength can return -1 for indefinite-length encoding, but readInteger passes that value directly to read(int), which allocates new byte[length]. A malformed DER signature using indefinite length will therefore cause NegativeArraySizeException instead of an IOException. The decoder should reject indefinite-length encodings in this DER-oriented use case.

title: ECDSA test does not use curve-appropriate keys or verify conversion correctness
body: The test generates one default EC key pair and uses it for ES256, ES384, and ES512. For ES384 and ES512 this likely exercises smaller coordinates than the real target curves, mostly testing padding rather than full-size values. It also only asserts that concatenated RS -> DER -> concatenated RS is stable, not that the re-encoded DER matches the original signature or that the converted signature verifies, so incorrect conversion logic could still pass.

title: Multiple crypto providers are now silently selected, with no tie-break for equal orders
body: CryptoIntegration.detectProvider now sorts all discovered CryptoProvider services and returns the first one instead of failing when multiple services are present. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider all return order 200, so if more than one is accidentally on the classpath the winner is determined only by ServiceLoader/classpath order. In addition, all providers are instantiated before selection, so constructors that register JCA security providers run even for ignored providers. This can silently select a non-FIPS provider in a FIPS deployment or leave multiple security providers registered, breaking the previous fail-fast guarantee and creating a security/compliance risk.

title: New order() method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: CryptoProvider is a public interface, but order() was added as an abstract method. Existing implementations outside this repository, or older modules compiled against the previous interface, will fail to compile and may fail at runtime with AbstractMethodError when ServiceLoader sorting invokes order(). A default method would preserve compatibility.

title: Oversized ECDSA integers are truncated instead of rejected
body: In AuthzClientCryptoProvider's ECDSA converter, integerToBytes truncates any BigInteger whose byte array is longer than qLength by copying only the last qLength bytes. For a valid ECDSA signature, r and s must not be larger than the coordinate size, allowing at most one leading zero byte. Silently truncating oversized DER integers accepts malformed signatures and changes the numeric value, which can create signature malleability or unexpected verification behavior. The method should reject values that do not fit and should also reject negative integers.

title: ASN.1 sequence parsing is too lenient and can ignore malformed or trailing data
body: ASN1Decoder.readSequence does not validate that the declared SEQUENCE length is exactly consumed. If a child TLV is longer than the remaining sequence length, the remaining length becomes negative and parsing stops without error. If trailing bytes exist after the SEQUENCE, they are ignored because asn1derToConcatenatedRS only reads the first sequence. This lenient DER parsing can accept malformed or appended signature bytes. It should reject non-zero remaining length, child lengths that exceed the sequence, and unconsumed trailing input.

title: Indefinite-length ASN.1 values can cause NegativeArraySizeException
body: ASN1Decoder.readLength returns -1 for indefinite-length ASN.1 encoding, but callers do not handle it. readInteger passes that -1 to read(int), which executes new byte[-1] and throws NegativeArraySizeException rather than IOException. readSequence treats -1 as an empty sequence. DER signatures must use definite length, so indefinite length should be rejected explicitly.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns an unrelated JCA provider
body: AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider returns the provider of KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()), which may be the default JDK keystore provider and has no relation to BouncyCastle. The CryptoProvider contract says this method returns the BouncyCastle security provider. If any caller uses the returned provider expecting BouncyCastle services, it can pick the wrong provider or fail. If this minimal provider has no BouncyCastle provider, it should return null or avoid exposing an incorrect provider.

title: concatenatedRSToASN1DER does not validate input signature length
body: concatenatedRSToASN1DER assumes the supplied concatenated signature has exactly signLength bytes. It does not validate signature.length before System.arraycopy. A shorter array causes ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, while a longer array silently ignores trailing bytes. Cryptographic conversion should require the exact expected length to avoid crashes and malformed-signature acceptance.

title: ECDSA conversion test does not use the expected curves or verify signatures
body: ECDSAAlgorithmTest generates a default EC key pair and only asserts that concatenated R/S bytes are stable across conversion. It does not initialize the generator with the curves associated with ES256, ES384, and ES512, does not verify the reconstructed DER signature with the public key, and does not cover edge cases such as r/s values with the high bit set, leading zeros, extreme values, or malformed DER. This leaves the custom ASN.1 conversion insufficiently tested.

title: New non-default order() method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: CryptoProvider is a public interface. Adding int order() as an abstract method breaks source and binary compatibility for existing implementations. A pre-compiled third-party CryptoProvider will fail with AbstractMethodError when CryptoIntegration.detectProvider calls order(). This should be a default method, for example returning a neutral order value, unless an intentional breaking change is accepted.

title: Multiple crypto providers are now selected silently with no deterministic tie-break
body: detectProvider now sorts all discovered CryptoProvider instances by order and returns the first one. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return 200, so if more than one is present accidentally, the winner depends on ServiceLoader/classpath ordering. The previous fail-fast behavior was replaced by debug-level logging only, which can silently select the wrong security provider in security-sensitive deployments.

title: Ignored crypto providers are still instantiated and may mutate global security state
body: Provider discovery collects all ServiceLoader providers before choosing one, which instantiates every discovered provider. Some constructors, notably FIPS1402Provider and DefaultCryptoProvider, register JCA security providers and modify global Security properties. If such a provider is discovered but ignored because another provider has equal or higher order, those global side effects remain even though the provider is not the selected CryptoProvider.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns an arbitrary keystore provider instead of BouncyCastle
body: AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider returns the provider of the default KeyStore type. That provider may be SUN or another JCA provider and is not necessarily BouncyCastle. Callers expecting the BouncyCastle provider may use the wrong security provider or get confusing failures. If BouncyCastle is not supported by this provider, the method should fail explicitly or return a documented unsupported value rather than masquerading as a BouncyCastle provider.

title: DER-to-raw ECDSA conversion silently truncates oversized integers
body: integerToBytes copies the last qLength bytes when the encoded integer is longer than qLength. This silently truncates oversized R/S values instead of rejecting them. DER-to-raw ECDSA signature conversion should only strip a single leading zero byte and should reject values that do not fit in the expected fixed length; otherwise malformed signatures are transformed into incorrect raw values instead of causing a validation error.

title: concatenatedRSToASN1DER does not validate signature length
body: concatenatedRSToASN1DER assumes the provided signature array has at least signLength bytes and that signLength is even. A short or malformed signature causes ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException from System.arraycopy instead of a descriptive IOException. Cryptographic parsing code should validate input lengths and throw an appropriate exception.

title: Indefinite-length ASN.1 encoding is not handled safely
body: readLength returns -1 for indefinite-length BER encoding, but callers are not prepared for that value. readSequence treats -1 as an empty sequence, and readInteger passes -1 to read(), resulting in NegativeArraySizeException. Since DER signatures must not use indefinite length, the decoder should throw IOException when 0x80 is encountered.

title: ECDSA conversion test does not use algorithm-specific curves or verify signatures
body: The test generates one default EC key pair and uses it for ES256, ES384 and ES512. JOSE ES256/ES384/ES512 require P-256, P-384 and P-521 respectively, with different signature lengths. Using a default key, likely P-256, for ES512 only exercises padding/round-trip and does not test real P-521 signature sizes. The test also does not verify the converted DER signature with Signature.verify, so it cannot detect semantically invalid conversions.

title: All-clients permissions are ignored when a client-specific resource already exists
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), the type-level 'Clients' resource is only evaluated when no client-specific resource is found. If any authorization resource already exists for the client (for example because another permission referenced that client), the method evaluates only that specific resource and never checks type-level permissions. As a result, a grant on all clients for MANAGE, CONFIGURE, MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE, or MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE can be denied for clients that have an unrelated specific resource. The implementation should evaluate both the specific client resource and the type resource, or otherwise include type-level grants.

title: NullPointerException possible when fallback type resource is missing
body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) can return null if the admin schema is not supported for the resource server or the 'Clients' type resource does not exist. The following call authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) dereferences resource without a null check. This can turn a missing initialization or migration condition into a NullPointerException and HTTP 500 instead of safely returning false.

title: Entity-specific resources are created without setting their resource type
body: getOrCreateResource creates concrete user/client resources with resourceStore.create(...) and updates their scopes, but it never calls resource.setType(resourceType) even though the resource type is available. ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission later searches with resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...). If the created specific resources do not have their type persisted, type-based lookups will not find them, so clients granted permissions through client-specific resources can be invisible to getClientsWithPermission and other type-based queries.

title: getClientsWithPermission can return the literal type resource name instead of client IDs
body: getClientsWithPermission adds resource.getName() to the granted set for every resource with permission. For the all-clients resource, the name is 'Clients' (AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE), not a client identifier. The method contract is to return client IDs that have the given permission. Returning the literal type name, and not expanding an all-clients grant into actual client identifiers, can cause callers that filter client lists by the returned set to behave incorrectly.

title: getResourceName does not handle the new Clients resource type
body: getResourceName special-cases only the Users resource type. For the newly added Clients resource type it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(). Client-specific resources are created using the internal client ID as the resource name and without a display name, and the all-clients type resource also has no meaningful display name. Consequently permission representations for clients may expose null or internal IDs instead of a client identifier or an 'All clients' label.

title: Provider event cleanup may call unsupported V2 methods
body: registerListener guards role/client/group removal cleanup with Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ, but AdminPermissions.management returns MgmtPermissionsV2 when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled. ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException. If V1 and V2 fine-grained authz features can be enabled together, or if V2 depends on V1, removal events will invoke these unsupported methods and may fail the removal operation. The listener should skip V2 or the V2 implementations should no-op.

title: Existing admin-permissions realms are not migrated to include the new Clients scopes/resource
body: init returns immediately if realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() already exists. Realms that already have the admin permissions client will not get the new 'configure', 'map-roles-client-scope', 'map-roles-composite' scopes or the 'Clients' type resource. Subsequent creation or evaluation of client permissions in those realms can fail with missing scope/resource errors. An idempotent re-initialization or migration step is needed when the schema changes.

title: Missing null/type validation in getScope can cause NullPointerException
body: getScope calls SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType).getScopes() without checking that resourceType is non-null or present in the schema. If this method is reached with an invalid or missing resource type while the admin permissions schema is active, it throws NullPointerException instead of a controlled ModelValidationException.

title: No test covers coexistence of all-clients and client-specific permissions
body: The new tests verify either a client-specific permission or an all-clients permission, but not the case where an all-clients permission exists while a client-specific authorization resource also exists. That scenario is needed to catch the issue where hasPermission(ClientModel, String) evaluates only the specific resource and ignores the type-level grant. A test should grant an all-clients scope and another specific permission/resource for the same client, then assert the all-clients scope still allows access.

title: Individual admin permission resources are created without a resource type
body: getOrCreateResource creates the resource with resourceStore.create(...) and updates its scopes, but never sets resource.setType(resourceType). ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission looks up resources with resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...), so individually created client resources will not match type-based queries. This can make per-client grants invisible to code that enumerates clients by type, breaking client listing/filtering based on permissions.

title: Existing realms are not migrated to the new Clients resource type and scopes
body: init returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is not null. Realms initialized before this change therefore do not get the Clients type resource or the new configure, map-roles-client-scope, and map-roles-composite scopes. Subsequent client permission evaluation can silently deny access or fail because the schema expects those objects to exist.

title: Possible NullPointerException when Clients type resource is missing
body: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) calls AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) and immediately dereferences the result in authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource). getResourceTypeResource can return null if the Clients type resource has not been created, for example on an existing realm, causing a NullPointerException instead of returning false.

title: Removed-entity cleanup is disabled for V2 and can throw if V1 and V2 are both enabled
body: The provider-event cleanup is now gated on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ. When only ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, client removal no longer triggers cleanup, so authorization resources referencing removed clients can remain orphaned. If both features are enabled, management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 and clients().setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException because ClientPermissionsV2 marks it unsupported.

title: getResourceName does not handle Clients resources
body: getResourceName only special-cases the Users resource type. For Clients resources it falls back to resource.getDisplayName(), but client resources are created with the client ID as the name and no display name, and the type-level Clients resource has no label. This can leave permission/resource representations with null or meaningless names in the admin API/UI.

title: No test exercises map-roles-client-scope
body: The PR adds the map-roles-client-scope scope to the Clients resource type and implements canMapClientScopeRoles, but the added tests only cover map-roles and map-roles-composite. A wiring or evaluation regression for map-roles-client-scope would not be caught.

title: Existing admin-permissions clients are not migrated for new Clients scopes/resources
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init returns as soon as realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() exists. Realms initialized before this change only contain the Users scopes and the Users all-resource. After this change, the Clients scopes configure, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite and the Clients all-resource are required, but init will never create them for existing realms. As a result, creating or evaluating client permissions in upgraded realms can fail due to missing scopes or missing all-clients resources.

title: All-clients permissions are ignored when a client-specific authorization resource exists
body: ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String) only falls back to the Clients all-resource when resourceStore.findByName for the specific client returns null. If a client-specific resource exists for any reason, such as a permission for another scope or a deny policy, the method evaluates only that specific resource and never evaluates permissions attached to the all-clients resource. Consequently, an all-clients permission such as MANAGE or VIEW can stop working for that client, producing unexpected authorization denials. The specific resource and the all-resource should be evaluated together.

title: getClientsWithPermission can return the literal "Clients" type-resource name
body: getClientsWithPermission iterates over all resources whose type is Clients, which includes the schema's all-resource named "Clients". If an all-clients permission grants the requested scope, hasGrantedPermission returns true for that type resource and the method adds resource.getName(), i.e. "Clients", to the set of client IDs. This is not a valid client ID and does not represent all actual clients, so callers that use the returned set to filter or lookup clients will behave incorrectly.

title: V2 has no cleanup for removed clients, and listener gating can be inconsistent
body: registerListener now only performs permission cleanup when Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled. When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled instead, MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, and there is no replacement cleanup for client removal. Deleting a client that has V2 authorization resources or permissions therefore leaves orphan resources and stale permissions. If both V1 and V2 features can be enabled together, the listener will call the unsupported V2 method and may fail client removal.

title: Client-specific denies can be bypassed by global canView()
body: ClientPermissionsV2.canView(ClientModel) returns true immediately if canView() is true. canView() evaluates only the global/all-clients VIEW permission or admin roles, not client-specific resources. Therefore, if an all-clients VIEW permission is granted and a client-specific negative VIEW permission exists, canView(client) still returns true without evaluating the client-specific deny. Explicit deny policies for a client can be bypassed.

title: getResourceName does not handle Clients resource type
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName special-cases only the Users resource type. For policies whose resource type is Clients, it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(). Client resources created by getOrCreateResource are named by client UUID and do not have a display name set, so representations or UI can show null or an unhelpful name instead of the client identifier or "All clients".

title: Possible NullPointerException when all-clients resource cannot be resolved
body: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String), if the specific client resource is absent, AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource is called. That method can return null when the authorization schema is not supported for the current realm or resource server. The following call to authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) does not check resource for null, which can cause a NullPointerException. hasPermission only guards against a null ResourceServer, not against a null type resource.

title: Exit code for recreate changed and old value repurposed
body: This change moves RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 and assigns FEATURE_DISABLED to 4. The documentation tells users to rely on these exit codes for automation, so existing scripts or tests written against the previous runtime behavior may now misinterpret exit code 4 as feature-disabled rather than recreate, and recreate results will move to 3. If this is intentional, it should be clearly noted as a behavior change; otherwise a new unused exit code should be chosen for the feature-disabled case.

title: Documented exit codes are not asserted in tests
body: The tests only assert message text, not exit codes, even though the PR introduces/changes documented exit codes: 0 for compatible, 3 for recreate-required, and 4 for feature disabled. For example, testFeatureNotEnabled should assert exit code 4 and testWrongVersions should assert exit code 3, and the successful check path should assert 0. Without these assertions, regressions in the exit-code contract would not be caught.

title: Enabled features are overwritten instead of preserved
body: setEnabledFeatures(List.of(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey())) replaces any existing enabled features in the FeatureSpec. If the shared test deployment setup already enables other features, this test will silently disable them when testing the RECREATE strategy, potentially changing test behavior or causing unrelated failures. Adding the feature to the existing list would be safer.

title: Feature-flag caution is ambiguous for default update behavior
body: The caution states that the operator will fail if the rolling-updates feature is not enabled, but the same section also documents a default <not set> behavior, and the UpgradeTest exercises a null update strategy without enabling the feature. If the feature is only required when spec.update or an explicit strategy is used, the documentation should say that explicitly; otherwise the statement is inconsistent with the described default behavior and tests.

title: Exit-code contract is changed and code 4 is reused for a different meaning
body: The update-compatibility documentation tells users to rely on the command exit code, but this change moves the recreate-required result from exit code 4 to 3 and assigns exit code 4 to 'feature disabled'. Any script or pipeline written against the previous behavior may misinterpret the result, for example treating feature-disabled as recreate-required or failing to recognize the new recreate code. If this exit-code contract has already been exposed, consider keeping 4 for recreate and using a new unused code for feature disabled, or explicitly handle this as a breaking change.

title: Feature-disabled test does not verify the documented exit code
body: testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the error message. The PR introduces and documents exit code 4 for the case where the rolling-updates feature is disabled, but the test does not assert that the CLI exits with 4. Without this assertion, regressions in the documented exit-code contract can go unnoticed.

title: Incompatible-version tests do not verify the recreate exit code
body: testWrongVersions asserts only the error message after running update-compatibility check with mismatched Keycloak or Infinispan versions. Since the PR changes the recreate-required exit code to 3 and documents that value, the test should also assert that the command returns exit code 3 in these incompatibility cases.

title: Test setup overwrites existing enabled features
body: createInitialDeployment calls setEnabledFeatures(List.of(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey())), replacing any features that may already be present in the FeatureSpec. If the base Keycloak deployment used by the test enables other features, they will be silently disabled for these tests. The code should preserve existing enabled features and append rolling-updates, and preferably use a mutable list if the CR model may later be modified.

title: Documentation overstates or ambiguously states the rolling-updates feature requirement
body: The caution says that while the functionality is preview, the rolling-updates feature must be enabled or the Keycloak Operator will fail. However, the same section describes a default/unset update strategy, and the UpgradeTest only enables rolling-updates when an explicit update strategy is set. The documentation should clarify whether the feature is required only when spec.update is used, or the operator/test behavior should be aligned with the stated requirement.

title: Exit-code contract changed for recreate and feature-disabled reuses old code
body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is changed from 4 to 3 and FEATURE_DISABLED is assigned 4. The update-compatibility check command is documented as scriptable and users are told to rely on its exit codes. Any existing automation that interpreted exit code 4 as 'recreate required' will now interpret it as 'rolling-updates feature disabled'. If the command has already been consumed, this is a breaking contract change.

title: Documented exit codes are not asserted in CLI tests
body: The PR introduces exit code 4 for a disabled feature and changes the recreate exit code to 3, and the documentation tells users to rely on these exit codes. However the distribution tests only assert messages: testFeatureNotEnabled does not assert exit code 4, testCompatible does not assert the check command exits 0, and testWrongVersions does not assert exit code 3. Add exit-code assertions to protect the scripted contract.

title: Feature list is overwritten with an immutable list
body: createInitialDeployment calls setEnabledFeatures(List.of(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey())) after only checking whether FeatureSpec is null. If a FeatureSpec already contains enabled features, they are silently replaced, and the stored list is immutable. Later test code or framework code that appends features will throw UnsupportedOperationException. Preserve existing entries and use a mutable list when adding rolling-updates.

title: Global group canManage() grants manage rights for VIEW permission
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when the caller has either VIEW or MANAGE on the Groups resource type. This method is used by GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup through requireManage(), so a permission that only grants view on all groups allows creating or moving top-level groups. Global manage should require MANAGE only.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
body: GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission adds groupResource.getId() to the returned set. Callers such as UsersResource.searchForUser and UsersResource.getUsersCount expect group IDs, but authorization resource IDs are internal IDs. The loop also processes the type resource named Groups. As a result, user search and count can filter on wrong IDs and return incorrect or empty results when group member-view permissions are used. The code should skip the type resource and add the resource name, which is the group ID.

title: Individual authorization resources are created without a resource type
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates individual resources for users, clients, and groups with a name and scopes but never calls resource.setType(resourceType). GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission relies on resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) to enumerate group resources, so individually created group resources will not be found. This breaks enumeration of group-scoped permissions for user search and counts.

title: V2 group permissions throw UnsupportedOperationException from existing lifecycle/API paths
body: GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, but existing code still calls it. AdminPermissions.registerListener calls management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false) on GroupRemovedEvent, and GroupResource.setManagementPermissionsEnabled calls it through the groups management/permissions endpoint. When V2 is active this can cause group deletion events to fail or the REST endpoint to return 500, and no cleanup of group authorization resources is performed.

title: Group permission evaluation does not filter granted permissions by resource ID
body: GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission evaluates permissions for a group resource but does not filter returned Permission objects by resource ID. UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission performs this filter, which is necessary when evaluation can include permissions attached to the resource type or other resources. Without the filter, all-groups permissions may be treated as granted during group-specific checks even when a specific group resource exists, potentially bypassing intended restrictions or negative permissions.

title: getScope can throw NullPointerException for unknown resource type
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getScope calls SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType).getScopes() without checking whether resourceType is null or whether the map lookup returns null. A null or unknown resource type will cause a NullPointerException instead of a validation error, turning invalid input into a 500 response.

title: getOrCreateResource throws IllegalStateException for unknown entity IDs
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource throws IllegalStateException when resolveGroup, resolveUser, or resolveClient returns null. A REST caller creating a scope permission with a non-existent group, user, or client ID can trigger a 500 response instead of a 400/404 validation error.

title: getResourceName does not resolve group resource names
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName only resolves user resources. For group resources it returns resource.getDisplayName(), but individual group resources are created with the group ID as the name and no display name. Admin UI or policy representations will therefore show an empty value or internal ID instead of the group name.

title: Global group manage check grants manage permission for view-only permissions
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when the caller has either VIEW or MANAGE on the all-groups resource. Global manage should require MANAGE only. This method is used by GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() via requireManage(), so a principal with only view permission on all groups can create top-level groups. The check should use only AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), the code calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) and adds groupResource.getId() to the returned set. hasPermission() expects the group ID, which is stored as the authorization resource name for instance resources, not the internal authorization resource ID. As a result, group-specific VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions are not found, and the method can return internal resource IDs (including the ID of the all-groups type resource) instead of realm group IDs. User search and user count filtering that relies on these IDs will then return wrong results or no results. It should use the resource name for instance resources and skip the Groups type resource.

title: Individual authorization resources are created without a resource type
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() creates instance resources for Clients, Groups, and Users but never calls resource.setType(resourceType). GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() relies on resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) to locate group instance resources. Without the type being set, those instance resources will not be returned by findByType(), so group-scoped member permissions cannot be collected. The resource type should be set when creating the resource.

title: All-groups permissions are ignored whenever a group-specific resource exists
body: GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission() falls back to the all-groups type resource only when no resource exists for the requested group ID. If a group-specific resource exists, permissions attached to the all-groups resource are not evaluated at all. This means an all-groups MANAGE or VIEW_MEMBERS grant can be shadowed by the mere existence of a group-specific resource, even if that resource does not grant the requested scope, leading to unexpected forbidden operations. Evaluation should consider both the instance resource and the type resource, or fall back when the instance resource does not grant the requested scopes.

title: Existing realms are not initialized with the new Groups scopes and resources
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns immediately if realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() already exists. Realms that were initialized before this change will not get the new Groups resource type or the manage-membership, manage-members, and view-members scopes. Subsequent group permission evaluation or resource creation can fail because the Groups type resource or required scopes are missing. An idempotent initialization or migration is needed to add missing schema objects to existing realms.

title: Possible NullPointerException in getScope for missing or unknown resource type
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getScope() dereferences SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType) without checking whether resourceType is null or whether the map lookup returns null. If this method is called with a missing or unsupported resource type, it will throw a NullPointerException and likely produce an HTTP 500 instead of a validation error. The resource type should be validated before accessing its scopes.

title: Possible NullPointerException when Groups type resource is missing
body: GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission() falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) and immediately calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource). getResourceTypeResource() can return null if the Groups type resource has not been initialized, which would cause a NullPointerException. A null check should return false or throw a meaningful exception.

title: Missing return when brute force protection is disabled
body: BruteForceUsersResource.getBruteForceStatus() sets default brute force status when realm.isBruteForceProtected() is false but does not return. The method then continues to look up login failures and may overwrite the default status with stale failure data even though brute force protection is disabled. It should return after setting the default status when brute force protection is off.

title: Group resource names are not resolved for display
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName() only resolves Users resources to a human-readable username. For Groups resources it falls back to resource.getDisplayName(), but group instance resources are created with the group ID as the name and no display name. As a result, group resources can be shown as raw group IDs in admin-facing responses. Group resources should be resolved to their group name, or a display name should be set when creating the resource.

title: Global group canManage() grants manage rights for VIEW permission
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when the caller has either VIEW or MANAGE on the all-groups resource (hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)). This method is used by GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup through requireManage(), so a principal granted only the Groups view scope can create or move top-level groups. The global manage check should require MANAGE only.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
body: GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() adds groupResource.getId() to the returned set. Callers such as UsersResource.searchForUser and getUsersCount expect realm group IDs and pass this set to user search/count queries via UserModel.GROUPS. The authorization resource ID is not the group ID (the group ID is stored as the resource name), so user searches and counts restricted by group-view permissions will filter on wrong IDs, producing missing or incorrect results and breaking pagination.

title: Group-type resource is processed as an individual group in getGroupIdsWithViewPermission
body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() iterates all resources of type Groups using resourceStore.findByType. This includes the resource-type resource named Groups created by AdminPermissionsSchema.init. The loop treats it as an individual group, so an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS or MANAGE_MEMBERS permission can cause the type resource identifier to be added to the set of group IDs used for user searches. The type-level resource should be skipped or handled as an all-groups case.

title: getResourceName does not resolve Groups resources
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName() only special-cases the Users resource type. For Groups resources, whose resource name is the group ID and which are created without a useful display name, it falls back to resource.getDisplayName(), which will be null or the raw ID. This can cause admin UI/API responses for permissions referencing groups to show no meaningful name. A branch should resolve GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE resources to the group name or path.

title: Possible NullPointerException in getScope for invalid resource type
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getScope() calls SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType).getScopes() when the authorization schema is supported. If resourceType is null or not one of the known types, get() returns null and the subsequent getScopes() throws NullPointerException instead of returning a validation error. This can turn malformed or unsupported input into a 500 error.

title: Group removal listener can call unsupported V2 method
body: AdminPermissions.registerListener() still calls management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false) on GroupRemovedEvent. When the V2 evaluator is selected, GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException. If the V1 fine-grained authz feature is enabled alongside V2, group removal events can fail during listener processing. The V2 implementation should no-op or the listener should account for V2.

title: Removing global canView short-circuit forces per-group authorization checks
body: GroupsResource.getGroups now filters every returned group with groupsEvaluator::canView instead of first checking groupsEvaluator.canView() and skipping per-item checks when global view is available. In V2, each canView(group) can perform resource lookups and policy evaluation; for large group listings with an all-groups permission this may significantly increase latency. The same pattern was applied in GroupResource.getSubGroups.

title: Message bundles are read with PropertyResourceBundle(InputStream), which is not UTF-8
body: verifySafeHtml() constructs PropertyResourceBundle from a FileInputStream for the target file at line 68 and for the English reference file at line 77. PropertyResourceBundle(InputStream) loads properties as ISO-8859-1, while Keycloak theme message files are UTF-8 and contain non-ASCII translated text. The verifier therefore compares mojibake for many translations, making the HTML check unreliable and likely to produce false positives or false negatives. Use PropertyResourceBundle(Reader) with an InputStreamReader using StandardCharsets.UTF_8.

title: Unescaping sanitizer output can hide sanitization changes
body: After the OWASP sanitizer produces output, the code unescapes HTML entities with StringEscapeUtils.unescapeHtml4() before comparing the sanitized value to the original value. If the sanitizer neutralizes markup by escaping it, this conversion can restore the original markup representation and make the two strings compare equal. That can hide cases where sanitization actually changed the value, so the verifier may accept HTML that was not truly unchanged/safe.

title: Anchor regex matches tags that are not anchors
body:
ANCHOR_PATTERN is defined as ]*>, which matches any tag whose name begins with the letter a, such as ,
, or , not just and . santizeAnchors() removes matching tags before the OWASP allow-list is applied. If such a tag appears in both the English and translated value, it can bypass the intended HTML policy even though only anchor tags were meant to be treated specially. The pattern should match only anchor tags.

title: English reference file is derived with fragile path rewriting
body: The verifier locates the English bundle by rewriting the absolute file path: replacing resources-community with resources and then applying a locale-suffix regex to the whole path. This assumes every verified file has a locale suffix matching that regex and that an English file exists at the rewritten path. Files without the expected suffix, locale-like path elements elsewhere in the path, or community-only messages can resolve to the wrong file or cause a RuntimeException instead of a normal verification message. This makes the verifier brittle and can fail builds for reasons unrelated to HTML safety.

title: Difference reporting can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException
body: When reporting a sanitization mismatch, the code computes a common prefix and a common suffix independently, then calls substring(start, length - end) without ensuring that the prefix and suffix do not overlap. If one string is an extension of the other at the beginning or end, start can become greater than length - end, causing String.substring to throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. The verifier should clamp or otherwise handle overlapping prefix/suffix ranges before creating the diagnostic substrings.

title: templateHelp whitelist removes arbitrary uppercase tags before sanitization
body: normalizeValue() removes substrings matching CLAIM.<uppercase letters> before HTML sanitization. This is broader than the intended CLAIM.<NAME> placeholder and can hide uppercase HTML-style tags prefixed with CLAIM. from the sanitizer check, while the actual resource value still contains them. Whitelist only the exact expected placeholder, or normalize it in a way that does not silently remove arbitrary tag-like content.

title: Account UI message changed from i18next placeholders to Java MessageFormat
body: The account-ui bundle uses i18next-style interpolation elsewhere, such as {{date}} and {{0}}. Changing error-invalid-multivalued-size to Java MessageFormat placeholders and a choice subformat means the JS UI will not interpolate this message correctly; users are likely to see literal {0}/{2,choice,...} text or an incorrectly formatted message. If pluralization is needed in the UI, use the UI's i18n plural mechanism rather than Java MessageFormat.

title: Admin UI message changed from i18next placeholders to Java MessageFormat
body: This admin-ui bundle previously used i18next-style double-curly placeholders for this key. Replacing {{0}}, {{1}}, and {{2}} with Java MessageFormat placeholders and a choice subformat is inconsistent with the JS i18n format and can break interpolation in the admin UI. The message will likely render with literal placeholder text or fail to pluralize correctly.

title: Lithuanian account translation contains Italian text
body: The Lithuanian account message totpStep1 is set to the Italian sentence Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:. This is not Lithuanian and will be shown to Lithuanian users.

title: Lithuanian login translation contains Italian text
body: The Lithuanian login message loginTotpStep1 is set to the Italian sentence Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:. This is not Lithuanian and will be shown to Lithuanian users.

title: Simplified Chinese locale uses Traditional Chinese text
body: The zh_CN account message totpStep1 uses Traditional Chinese characters in a Simplified Chinese locale. The string should be localized using Simplified Chinese characters consistent with zh_CN.

title: Tests do not cover UTF-8/non-ASCII message bundles
