body: The added tests use only ASCII fixtures and do not exercise real-world UTF-8 translated message files. Because the implementation reads property bundles in a way that is sensitive to character encoding, the current tests cannot catch encoding-related false positives or false negatives. Add fixtures containing non-ASCII UTF-8 characters, HTML, and locale-specific path/name patterns.

title: English reference file path is derived with an unsafe, unanchored regex
body: The verifier maps a translated file to its English reference by applying replaceAll to the full absolute path with an unanchored locale-suffix pattern. The pattern is also written with an unescaped hyphen and does not explicitly cover numeric locale tags. If the path contains another matching underscore segment, or if a locale such as messages_es_419.properties is used, the computed English file can be wrong or missing. This can make the verifier compare against the wrong bundle or fail with a RuntimeException.

title: ChoiceFormat normalization removes HTML from sanitized input
body: normalizeValue() replaces the entire ChoiceFormat block with '...' before OWASP sanitization for keys starting with linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit and for error-invalid-multivalued-size. Any HTML placed inside the choice alternatives is therefore removed before sanitization and never checked. A malicious translation could use something like '{2,choice,0#<script>alert(1)</script>values}' and bypass the HTML verification, while the message may still be rendered as HTML in emails or login pages.

title: Anchor tags are stripped before sanitization and are not validated
body: santizeAnchors() removes anchor tags that match the English source before policy.sanitize() is called. When verifying the English file itself, the value and the English value are identical, so all anchors are removed before the sanitizer ever sees them. As a result, an English source string containing an unsafe anchor such as <a href='javascript:alert(1)'> passes verification. The logic also does not detect translations that omit an anchor present in the source.

title: Illegal HTML diff computation can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException
body: The code strips common prefix and suffix characters before printing the differing substring, but it never ensures that the prefix and suffix do not overlap. If sanitized and value differ by inserted characters while still sharing beginning and ending characters, start can become greater than length - end, causing substring() to throw. This would abort verification instead of reporting the offending key.

title: Account UI message changed from i18next syntax to Java MessageFormat/ChoiceFormat
body: This account-ui message file uses i18next/React syntax throughout, for example other error-* keys use {{0}} and some messages use Trans tags like <0>. The changed error-invalid-multivalued-size now uses Java MessageFormat/ChoiceFormat syntax with {0} and {2,choice,...}. The account UI will not evaluate that server-side Java format, so users are likely to see raw placeholders or broken pluralization.

title: Admin UI message changed from i18next syntax to Java MessageFormat/ChoiceFormat
body: The previous value used {{0}}, matching the admin UI's i18next-style interpolation. The new value uses Java MessageFormat/ChoiceFormat syntax with {0} and {2,choice,...}. If this key is rendered by the admin UI frontend, the placeholders and choice expression will not be processed, producing a broken user-facing validation message.

title: Lithuanian account message replaced with Italian text
body: The Lithuanian account console message totpStep1 was changed to the Italian sentence 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' instead of Lithuanian. Lithuanian users will see Italian text in the account UI.

title: Lithuanian login message replaced with Italian text
body: The Lithuanian login message loginTotpStep1 was changed to the Italian sentence 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' instead of Lithuanian. Lithuanian users will see Italian text on the login page.

title: Simplified Chinese account message uses Traditional Chinese characters
body: The zh_CN account console message totpStep1 was changed to '在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：', which uses Traditional Chinese characters. messages_zh_CN is Simplified Chinese, so this is inconsistent with the locale and the rest of the file.

title: Danish HTML email contains stray 'n' before 'Hvis'
body:
identityProviderLinkBodyHtml contains the paragraph '

nHvis du ikke vil forbinde disse konti...'. The leading 'n' is a typo and should be '

Hvis du ikke vil forbinde disse konti...'. This text is visible in the HTML email.

title: Anchor allow-list regex matches any tag starting with 'a'
body: ANCHOR_PATTERN is '</?a[^>]*>', which matches tags such as <article>, <abbr>, and <area>, not just <a>. In santizeAnchors(), matching tags are removed from the value before OWASP sanitization. If the English source and translation both contain such a non-anchor tag, it will be stripped from the checked value and can pass verification even though the tag is not allowed by the HTML policy. Use a word boundary, for example '</?a\b[^>]*>'.

title: Choice formats are removed wholesale before HTML validation
body: normalizeValue() replaces the whole '{n,choice,...}' expression with '...' for linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit* and error-invalid-multivalued-size. Any HTML placed inside the choice alternatives is therefore never passed to the sanitizer. For example, a malicious or malformed choice such as '{0,choice,0#<script>}' would be stripped out before validation and could pass. The choice content should be validated or sanitized rather than ignored.

title: Diff substring computation can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException
body: When reporting a sanitizer mismatch, start and end are computed independently from the beginning and end of the strings. There is no check that start + end is less than or equal to each string length. If the sanitized value is shorter and shares both prefix and suffix characters with the original value, substring(start, length - end) can have an end index before start and throw, causing the verifier to fail with an unexpected exception instead of reporting the HTML problem.

title: Missing English reference file fails with RuntimeException instead of MojoExecutionException
body: verifySafeHtml() wraps failure to read the derived English properties file in a RuntimeException. In a Maven plugin context this produces a less controlled build failure than the MojoExecutionException used by verify(). If an expected English file is missing or the derived path is wrong, the build fails with an unchecked exception instead of a clear plugin error message.

title: Java MessageFormat choice syntax used in JavaScript account-ui bundle
body: error-invalid-multivalued-size was changed from '{{0}}', '{{1}}', '{{2}}' to '{0}' and '{2,choice,...}'. This file is a JavaScript account-ui message bundle where other parameterized messages use double-curly interpolation. Java MessageFormat placeholders and choice syntax will not be processed by the UI i18n layer, so users are likely to see raw braces/choice text instead of a localized, formatted message.

title: Java MessageFormat choice syntax used in JavaScript admin-ui bundle
body: error-invalid-multivalued-size was changed from '{{0}}', '{{1}}', '{{2}}' to '{0}' and '{2,choice,...}'. Admin UI message bundles use double-curly interpolation elsewhere, so Java MessageFormat choice syntax is unlikely to be evaluated by the admin UI. This can break parameter substitution and pluralization for this validation message in the admin console.

title: Lithuanian account message contains Italian text
body: totpStep1 in the Lithuanian account bundle is 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', which is Italian. Lithuanian users will see an Italian instruction on the account/OTP setup page. It should be replaced with the proper Lithuanian translation.

title: Lithuanian login message contains Italian text
body: loginTotpStep1 in the Lithuanian login bundle is 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', which is Italian. Lithuanian users will see Italian text during login TOTP setup. It should be replaced with the proper Lithuanian translation.

title: Simplified Chinese bundle uses Traditional Chinese wording
body: totpStep1 in messages_zh_CN.properties uses Traditional Chinese characters such as '手機上安裝以下應用程式之一'. A Simplified Chinese bundle should use Simplified characters, for example '在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：'.

title: Stray 'n' in Danish HTML email text
body:
identityProviderLinkBodyHtml now contains '

nHvis du ikke vil forbinde...'. The leading 'n' before 'Hvis' will be visible in the rendered email. It should be '

Hvis du ikke vil forbinde...'.

title: No positive tests for allowed HTML or matching anchor tags
body:
The added tests only verify that illegal HTML, disallowed HTML, or changed anchors are detected. There are no tests showing that valid allowed tags such as ,
, or identical anchor tags from the English source pass without producing verifier messages. Without positive fixtures, future changes to sanitizer normalization could introduce false positives unnoticed.

title: Lightweight-token check uses the session-context client instead of the client session's client
body: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext determines whether the access token is lightweight by calling AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session), which reads session.getContext().getClient(). The token being created is associated with the client session available from clientSessionContext, and that client may be different or the session-context client may be unset in some flows. This can cause a NullPointerException or encode the wrong token type. The client used for the token should be taken from the client session / token creation context.

title: Access token ID matcher checks the grant shortcut with the wrong index and inverted logic
body: AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId is intended to verify that the encoded access token ID contains the expected grant shortcut. The encoded format is sessionType(2) + tokenType(2) + grantShortcut(2) + ':' + rawId, so the grant shortcut is at substring(4, 6). The code checks substring(3, 5) and returns false when that value equals the expected shortcut. As written, the matcher does not validate the grant shortcut correctly and can pass even when the encoded grant is wrong, weakening the event tests for code-to-token, refresh, device, and CIBA flows.

title: Constructor validates grantType twice and does not validate rawTokenId
body: AccessTokenContext's constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") instead of checking rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted despite the constructor contract. Later encoding concatenates the null value and can produce a token ID ending in ':null', breaking the assumption that the raw token ID is a generated unique identifier.

title: New non-default getShortcut method breaks existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is an SPI interface, but getShortcut is added as a new abstract method without a default implementation. Existing third-party implementations compiled against the previous interface will fail at runtime with AbstractMethodError when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit calls getShortcut. This is an SPI/API compatibility break.

title: Public OAuth2GrantType.Context copy constructor removed
body: The public Context(Context) copy constructor was removed from OAuth2GrantType.Context. Extensions or custom grant implementations that used this constructor will fail to compile against the new version or fail at runtime with NoSuchMethodError. If the removal is intentional, it is an SPI/API break that should be called out or replaced with an explicit alternative.

title: Unsafe cast of all OAuth2GrantType provider factories to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory
body: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit iterates over all provider factories for OAuth2GrantType and casts each one to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory. If an extension provides a ProviderFactory<OAuth2GrantType> that does not implement OAuth2GrantTypeFactory, server startup will fail with ClassCastException. The code should filter for OAuth2GrantTypeFactory instances or otherwise validate the factory type.

title: Null or malformed grant shortcuts are not validated before being stored
body: postInit puts the value returned by OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut directly into ConcurrentHashMaps. If a factory returns null, the server fails with NullPointerException instead of a clear startup error. There is also no validation that shortcuts are non-null, two characters long, and safe for the token ID encoding. Invalid shortcuts will cause encoding/decoding failures later rather than a clear configuration error.

title: setFormParams does not update the cached grantType
body: OAuth2GrantType.Context.grantType is initialized from formParams in the constructor, but setFormParams replaces the form parameters without recalculating grantType. If setFormParams is used after construction, getGrantType returns the grant type from the old parameter map, and that stale value can be written into ClientSessionContext and encoded into the access token ID.

title: Shortcut Javadoc says 3 letters but encoding requires exactly 2 characters
body: The Javadoc for OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut says the shortcut is usually like a 3-letter shortcut. The token ID encoder, however, reserves exactly two characters for the grant shortcut and rejects encoded contexts that are not six characters total. Implementers following the Javadoc could provide a three-character shortcut and break token ID encoding/decoding.

title: Token ID matcher does not verify the expected grant prefix
body: In isAccessTokenId, the grant shortcut is expected to be encoded in the new token ID format 'ssttgg:uuid', where the grant shortcut occupies indices 4-5 of the prefix. The matcher uses items[0].substring(3, 5) and returns false when that substring equals the expected shortcut. This is both the wrong substring and inverted logic, so it accepts token IDs whose actual grant prefix does not match the expected grant and can fail only accidentally. It may also throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException for short prefixes. As a result, the updated event assertions do not validate the encoded grant type.

title: Constructor validates grantType twice instead of rawTokenId
body: AccessTokenContext's constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") instead of checking rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId can therefore be stored. Later, DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId concatenates the raw token ID into the encoded token ID, which can produce an ID ending in ':null' or cause failures in consumers expecting a valid opaque token ID.

title: New getShortcut method is a breaking SPI change
body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is an existing SPI interface. Adding String getShortcut() as an abstract method without a default implementation breaks existing custom grant-type factory implementations at compile time and can cause AbstractMethodError at runtime for binary extensions. If this is required, the compatibility impact should be explicit; otherwise a default method should be provided.

title: Public Context copy constructor removed
body: The diff removes the public copy constructor OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context). This is a source and binary compatibility break for any extension code that copied an existing Context. If this type is considered stable enough for custom grant implementations, the removal should be avoided or clearly documented as a breaking change.

title: Lightweight-token check depends on session-context client
body: getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext determines whether the token is lightweight by calling AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session), which reads session.getContext().getClient().getAttribute(...). Token creation already has a client available via TokenManager.initToken and the client session. If a caller creates an access token without setting the client in the session context, or if the context client differs from the token's client, this can throw NullPointerException or encode the wrong token type. The decision should use the client associated with the token being created.

title: Javadoc says 3-letter shortcut but format requires exactly 2 characters
body: The Javadoc for OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut says it returns 'usually like 3-letters shortcut', but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider encodes and decodes exactly two characters for the grant type field. Custom grant factories following this Javadoc could return three-character shortcuts, producing token IDs that cannot be parsed. The documentation should state that the shortcut must be exactly two characters.

title: Lazily registered grant shortcuts can overwrite existing mappings
body: Startup validates grant shortcut uniqueness by comparing the sizes of grantsByShortcuts and grantsToShortcuts. However, getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut lazily insert mappings for grant factories discovered later without re-validating uniqueness or format. A newly discovered grant with a conflicting shortcut can silently overwrite the shortcut-to-grant mapping, causing token IDs to decode to the wrong grant type while still encoding successfully.

title: Null check validates grantType twice instead of rawTokenId
body: AccessTokenContext constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) for the rawTokenId argument, so a null rawTokenId is accepted. encodeTokenId would then append null to the token ID and downstream consumers may treat it as a valid raw ID. The check should be performed on rawTokenId.

title: New non-default getShortcut() breaks existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is an SPI interface implemented by grant providers. Adding an abstract method and invoking it during factory initialization breaks source and binary compatibility for any existing custom implementation; older providers will fail to compile or throw AbstractMethodError at startup. A default method or optional capability would avoid this.

title: Shortcut contract says 3 letters but encoding requires exactly 2 characters
body: The Javadoc for getShortcut says shortcuts are usually 3 letters, but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider assumes each field is exactly 2 characters and validates a 6-character prefix. A provider returning a 3-character or otherwise malformed shortcut would produce undecodable token IDs. The contract should require exactly 2 characters and validate it.

title: Removal of OAuth2GrantType.Context copy constructor is an API break
body: The public Context(Context) constructor was removed from OAuth2GrantType.Context. Custom grant implementations that created a context by copying an existing one will no longer compile or will fail at runtime. If the removal is intentional, provide a replacement or compatibility path.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher uses wrong substring and inverted comparison
body: The matcher extracts items[0].substring(3, 5) instead of substring(4, 6) for the grant shortcut and returns false when the value equals the expected shortcut. As a result it does not verify the intended grant prefix and can reject valid values if the wrong position matches. It also does not check that the prefix is long enough before calling substring.

title: Grant shortcut cache updates are not conflict-safe or atomic
body: getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut add entries to the shared ConcurrentHashMap after a cache miss without checking whether the shortcut or grant ID conflicts with existing entries, and the check-then-put sequence is not atomic. A dynamically discovered grant with a duplicate shortcut can overwrite an existing mapping, causing token IDs to decode to the wrong grant type. Use putIfAbsent/compute and validate uniqueness.

title: Token type is derived from session context client instead of the token's client
body: getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext determines lightweight mode via AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session), which reads session.getContext().getClient(). If the session context client is not set or differs from the client for which the access token is created, the encoded token type may be wrong or a NullPointerException may occur. The client associated with the client session or the client passed to TokenManager.initToken should be used.

title: Incorrect-grant test passes by catching RuntimeException from a null factory
body: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.testIncorrectGrantType catches RuntimeException broadly. Because the factory is not post-initialized, the decoder path can throw NullPointerException from a null sessionFactory, so the test passes without asserting the intended IllegalArgumentException or validating the decoder. Initialize or mock the factory and assert the exact exception.

title: Federated recovery credential is not removed when all codes are used
body: After a successful recovery-code login, RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential can return a credential supplied by a user-storage provider. If all codes are used, the code calls authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(...), which only removes credentials stored in Keycloak's local storage. A federated/user-storage credential will therefore not be removed or disabled. This can leave an exhausted recovery-code credential configured in the external storage and can break assumptions in later code that the credential no longer exists. A storage-aware disable/remove path should be used instead of removeStoredCredentialById.

title: Unsafe Optional/get calls can cause NoSuchElementException during login
body: RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean calls credentialModelOpt.get() without checking whether RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) returned a credential, and then calls getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get() without checking that an unused code exists. If the credential is absent, or if a user-storage provider reports a recovery credential with no remaining unused codes, rendering the recovery-code login page throws NoSuchElementException and results in a 500 error instead of a graceful failure or redirect to credential setup.

title: Possible NullPointerException when recovery-code form fields are missing
body: processAction reads generatedRecoveryAuthnCodes and generatedAt from the form and immediately calls generatedAtTimeString.equals(...) and generatedCodesString.equals(...). If a client submits the required-action request without those hidden fields, the method throws NullPointerException instead of treating the submission as invalid and re-challenging. Null checks or null-safe comparisons are needed.

title: User-storage recovery codes are not consumed and single-use behavior is not tested
body: The test storage validates a recovery code by comparing the raw input against stored raw codes and never records that the code was consumed. getCredentials also rebuilds the credential from the raw list, so the credential always appears unused. As a result, a recovery code accepted once remains valid indefinitely for this user-storage implementation. Recovery codes are intended to be single-use, but the added test only performs one successful login and therefore does not verify consumption. The test/provider should enforce and verify one-time use, or the core changes need a mechanism to mark federated recovery codes as used.

title: getCredentials does not preserve credential ID or usage state
body: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials deserializes the stored recovery-code JSON and calls RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...) without copying the stored CredentialModel's ID or any used-state. The returned credential therefore has a transient or missing ID and always appears unused. Code that relies on the credential ID to remove/disable the credential, or on used flags to compute the next recovery-code number, will not work correctly with this storage.

title: Existing local recovery-code credentials are not cleared when a federated credential is created
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential treats a true return from user.credentialManager().updateCredential() as sufficient and does not remove any existing local recovery-authn-codes credentials. If a federated user already had a local recovery-code credential, generating new codes in the user storage can leave the old local credential in place. Because validation can consider existing stored credentials, previously issued codes may remain valid after rotation, breaking the expected one-time/replace semantics.

title: Plaintext recovery codes are passed to user storage
body: The helper serializes the raw generated recovery codes and sends them to the user storage provider. The local path stores only hashed codes, but this federated path exposes plaintext bearer secrets to the storage implementation. A storage that simply persists the supplied challenge response will retain recoverable plaintext codes. It would be safer to pass a hashed representation, or make the hashed-storage contract explicit, rather than handing out raw codes.

title: Test storage permits replay of recovery codes
body: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid compares the submitted recovery code with the stored list but never removes or marks the code as used. Recovery codes are one-time credentials, so this test storage allows the same code to be replayed indefinitely. The added test only uses a code once, so it does not catch this. The test storage should consume the code on successful validation and the test should assert reuse fails.

title: Federated recovery credential is returned without a stable ID
body: getCredentials constructs the recovery credential via RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues but does not copy the stable ID from the stored CredentialModel. If the returned credential has a null or newly generated ID on each call, Keycloak features that delete or reference the credential by ID, such as cleaning up exhausted recovery codes or account-console credential management, will not work reliably for this storage.

title: Unsafe Optional.get can cause a 500 if recovery credential is absent
body: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential returns Optional, but the bean immediately calls credentialModelOpt.get() and then getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get(). If the credential is missing because of a race, a misconfigured flow, or a storage provider returning no credential, the login page rendering fails with NoSuchElementException instead of handling the absent-credential state gracefully.

title: Missing coverage for recovery-code consumption and fallback behavior
body: The new test only covers setup and one successful login with the first federated recovery code. It does not verify that used codes are consumed, that exhausting all codes triggers CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES, or that local storage is used when a user storage provider does not support recovery codes. Those are core behaviors introduced by this PR.

title: Existing local recovery-code credentials are not removed when credential is written to user storage
body: When updateCredential returns true, the method only logs and does not create or replace the local recovery-code credential. If the user already has a locally stored recovery credential (for example created before the external storage supported recovery codes), that credential remains in Keycloak's database. Because recovery codes are supposed to be replaced when regenerated, stale local credentials can keep old codes valid and undermine credential rotation.

title: Local credential removal is used for credentials that may be federated
body: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential can now return a federated credential supplied by a user storage provider, but the cleanup path calls removeStoredCredentialById. That method removes credentials from Keycloak's local store, not from an external user storage. If the last recovery code was consumed in a federated credential, this call may silently do nothing or use an id that is not meaningful locally, leaving the external credential state inconsistent with the required-action logic.

title: Missing null checks for hidden form fields can cause NPE
body: The hidden form fields generatedRecoveryAuthnCodes and generatedAt are read with getFirst and then used without null checks. If a POST to the required action omits one of these fields, generatedAtTimeString.equals(...) or generatedCodesString.split(...) throws NullPointerException. This turns a malformed or replayed form submission into a server error instead of re-challenging or failing gracefully.

title: Unsafe Optional.get and next-code get can throw during login
body: The constructor calls credentialModelOpt.get() and then getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get() without verifying that a credential exists and that an unused code is available. If the recovery credential is missing, was removed concurrently, or all codes are used, the login page bean throws and the user gets an error page instead of a graceful challenge.

title: Plaintext recovery codes are passed to external user storage
body: The helper serializes the generated recovery codes in plaintext and passes them to the user storage via UserCredentialModel. The local path stores only hashed codes, but an external storage that persists the supplied challenge response (as the test storage does) will store recoverable one-time codes unhashed. This weakens the security model for federated storages unless hashing is explicitly documented or enforced.

title: No coverage for fallback to local storage when user storage does not support recovery codes
body: The new test makes BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage support recovery codes, so it only verifies the user-storage branch. There is no test in this change for the fallback path where the user storage does not support recovery codes and Keycloak should create the credential locally. Since the PR's purpose is to support both locations, that fallback should be covered.

title: Null delegate is only handled in getSubGroupsCount; other getSubGroupsStream overloads can still NPE
body: The PR adds a null check for modelSupplier.get() in getSubGroupsCount because the group can be deleted concurrently. The same modelSupplier.get() result is dereferenced without a null check in getSubGroupsStream(String, Integer, Integer) (line 256), getSubGroupsStream(Integer, Integer) (line 262), and getSubGroupsStream(String, Boolean, Integer, Integer) (line 268). If a stale cached group is accessed after deletion, these paths will still throw NullPointerException. They should handle a null model consistently, e.g. return Stream.empty() or invalidate/throw a controlled exception.

title: Concurrency test asserts before reader thread has finished and can hang
body: createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti starts a reader thread but never joins or awaits it. The main thread sets deletedAll and immediately asserts caughtExceptions is empty, so an in-flight request can fail after the assertion, and exceptions thrown later are missed. The test also does not guarantee that the reader performed any request before deletions completed. If a delete call throws, deletedAll is never set and the non-daemon thread may loop indefinitely. Use a latch/ExecutorService, wait for at least one read and for termination with a timeout, and assert after awaiting.

title: Paged/search subgroup methods still dereference a possibly-null model supplier
body: getSubGroupsCount() was changed to handle modelSupplier.get() returning null when a group has been deleted concurrently, but getSubGroupsStream(String, Integer, Integer) at line 256, getSubGroupsStream(Integer, Integer) at line 262, and getSubGroupsStream(String, Boolean, Integer, Integer) at line 268 still call modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) without a null check. Under the same concurrent-delete scenario the supplier can return null, so these methods can throw the same NullPointerException the PR is trying to fix.

title: Concurrency test can pass without exercising the race and may miss exceptions
body: The test starts a reader thread, deletes groups, sets deletedAll, and immediately asserts that caughtExceptions is empty. It never ensures that the reader thread actually performed requests, and it does not join or otherwise await termination before asserting. If the thread is not scheduled before deletions complete, the loop may never run; if it is still running when the assertion executes, later exceptions are missed; and the thread can continue after the test. Use a latch/count to guarantee reads occur during deletion, await the reader thread, then assert.

title: NPE fix is not applied to other cached subgroup accessors
body: In GroupAdapter, the PR only null-checks the delegate loaded by modelSupplier in getSubGroupsCount(). The subgroup paging/search methods still dereference the supplier result directly: line 256 (getSubGroupsStream(String, Integer, Integer)), line 262 (getSubGroupsStream(Integer, Integer)), and line 268 (getSubGroupsStream(String, Boolean, Integer, Integer)). If the group is deleted concurrently, modelSupplier.get() can return null, so these methods can still throw the NullPointerException the PR is intended to fix.

title: Concurrency test is racy and may pass without exercising the race
body: The new concurrency test starts a reader thread but does not coordinate shutdown before asserting. deletedAll can be set before the reader performs any request, so the test may pass without exercising the race; exceptions appended by the reader after assertThat(caughtExceptions, ...) are missed; and if a group deletion throws before deletedAll.set(true), the reader loop never stops. The test should ensure the reader has started, stop it in a finally block, join it with a timeout, and then assert.

title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate datetime-ordered audit logs
body: The endpoint selects OptimizedCursorPaginator while ordering by -datetime. OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil on getattr(item, self.key), and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor value. For AuditLogEntry.datetime this means math.floor receives a datetime and cursor values are not converted back to datetimes, so the first non-empty optimized request or any non-zero cursor will raise TypeError or a database type error.

title: Optimized paginator uses unsupported negative QuerySet slicing
body: When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset is negative, OptimizedCursorPaginator allows start_offset to remain negative and then slices the Django QuerySet with that offset. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing, so this raises an exception instead of paginating efficiently. Because cursor offsets are client-supplied, this can cause 500 errors for any admin using or being sent a crafted cursor.

title: BasePaginator now passes negative offsets to QuerySet slicing for previous pages
body: The change sets start_offset directly to cursor.offset when cursor.is_prev is true. If a cursor contains a negative offset, the paginator will slice the QuerySet with a negative start index. Django QuerySets reject negative indexing, so a malformed or malicious cursor with is_prev true can cause an unhandled exception on any endpoint using a BasePaginator subclass.

title: Cursor offsets are accepted as negative without validation
body: Cursor.__init__ converts offset with int(offset) and the added comment explicitly permits negative offsets, but there is no validation or paginator-level contract for this behavior. Existing cursor pagination logic generally assumes offsets are non-negative, and negative offsets can propagate into QuerySet slicing or cursor arithmetic. If negative offsets are intended, they need explicit validation and safe paginator support; otherwise they should be rejected or clamped.

title: Ordering reversal is lost due to assignment to order_b instead of order_by
body: In BasePaginator.build_queryset, when converting an existing descending order to ascending, the code assigns the new ordering tuple to queryset.query.order_b rather than queryset.query.order_by. The ordering change is silently discarded, so backward pagination may continue to use the wrong sort direction and return incorrect or inconsistent pages.

title: No tests cover the new optimized pagination behavior
body: The PR introduces a query-parameter-controlled paginator switch, an admin-only advanced mode, negative-offset handling, and a new OptimizedCursorPaginator, but no tests are included for these paths. Tests should verify datetime cursor compatibility, safe handling or rejection of negative offsets, and that the optimized path is only used by authorized users.

title: BasePaginator can pass negative offsets to Django queryset slicing
body: The new slicing logic keeps cursor.offset unchanged when cursor.is_prev is true. Cursor offsets are parsed from client-supplied cursor strings and can be negative. A previous-page cursor such as 0:-1:1 will cause queryset[start_offset:stop] to be evaluated with a negative start or stop. Django QuerySets do not support negative slicing and will raise an error, so endpoints using BasePaginator can be made to return 500s. Even if negative slicing were emulated, it would not provide the intended pagination semantics. Offsets should be validated or clamped to non-negative values before slicing.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator intentionally uses unsupported negative QuerySet slices
body: When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset is negative, OptimizedCursorPaginator sets start_offset to that negative value and slices the queryset with it. Django ORM does not support negative slicing; this will raise an error for the new audit-log optimized path whenever an advanced user sends a negative-offset cursor. The comment claiming the underlying ORM handles negative slicing is incorrect. Negative offsets should be rejected as invalid pagination input.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator is incompatible with datetime ordering used for audit logs
body: The endpoint orders audit logs by -datetime but uses OptimizedCursorPaginator, whose get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil on the ordered field value. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime object, so any optimized_pagination=true request that returns at least one row will raise TypeError while building the cursor. A datetime-aware paginator, or an optimized paginator implementing DateTimePaginator-style key conversion, is required.

title: Cursor offsets are accepted as arbitrary signed integers
body: Cursor.__init__ casts offset to int without validating that it is non-negative, and Cursor.from_string therefore accepts negative offsets from query parameters. The pagination changes in this PR expose or rely on negative offsets, but Django queryset pagination cannot handle them. This creates a client-controlled path to invalid paginator state and server errors. Unless a paginator explicitly supports signed offsets, cursor offsets should be validated and negative values rejected.

title: Extra-row trimming logic is incorrect for negative offsets
body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, after slicing with a negative offset, the code tests len(results) == offset + limit + extra to decide whether to drop the extra sentinel row. With a negative offset, this expected length is wrong and can be non-positive, so the sentinel row may not be removed or the result set may be trimmed incorrectly if negative slicing were ever supported. This can produce incorrect page contents and wrong next/prev cursor flags.

title: No tests cover the new optimized pagination path
body: The PR adds a new paginator, a query-parameter opt-in, permission gating, and negative-offset handling, but no tests are included. Tests are needed for the audit-log endpoint with optimized_pagination enabled, datetime cursor generation, negative or invalid cursor offsets, and fallback behavior for non-privileged users. Without tests, the datetime incompatibility and negative-slicing regressions are easy to ship.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate AuditLogEntry.datetime
body: The endpoint selects OptimizedCursorPaginator while ordering by -datetime. Unlike DateTimePaginator, OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil directly on the field value and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor value instead of converting it to a datetime. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime, so the first non-empty optimized page raises TypeError when build_cursor computes a key, and any non-zero cursor would also filter a datetime column with a numeric value. This makes the optimized pagination path fail with 500 or invalid queries. Use DateTimePaginator or make OptimizedCursorPaginator handle datetime conversion.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator uses unsupported negative QuerySet slicing
body: When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset is negative, the code sets start_offset to the negative offset and executes queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indices, so this raises an AssertionError rather than performing efficient reverse pagination. Because cursor offsets are parsed from client input, a crafted cursor can trigger a 500 on endpoints using this paginator. Negative offsets should be rejected or handled without negative QuerySet slices.

title: BasePaginator change allows invalid negative offsets for prev cursors
body: The new start_offset calculation uses cursor.offset unchanged when cursor.is_prev is true. Cursor.from_string accepts negative integers, so a cursor like 0:-1:1 causes queryset[-1:stop], which Django QuerySets do not support, leading to a 500 on any BasePaginator-derived endpoint. For non-prev cursors, negative offsets are silently coerced to 0, which can mask malformed input and return the wrong page. Cursor offsets should be validated as non-negative.

title: Extra-row drop condition compares against an impossible length
body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, after slicing from start_offset, results can contain at most limit + extra rows, but the code checks len(results) == offset + limit + extra. When cursor.offset is greater than zero, this condition cannot be true, so the extra row fetched for backward pagination may not be removed. This can return one too many rows or produce incorrect prev-cursor state. The check should compare against the number of rows actually requested, e.g. limit + extra or stop - start_offset.

title: Typo order_b prevents changing queryset ordering
body: In BasePaginator.build_queryset, when converting an existing descending order to ascending, the code assigns to queryset.query.order_b instead of queryset.query.order_by. The intended ordering change is silently lost, so previous-page pagination can query in the wrong order and return incorrect results. This affects BasePaginator and its subclasses used by the new optimized path.

title: No tests for the new pagination path
body: The PR introduces a query-parameter-controlled paginator switch and a new paginator with cursor, datetime, and negative-offset behavior, but no tests. At minimum, tests are needed for the optimized audit-log endpoint covering empty and non-empty pages, next and prev cursors, malformed or negative offsets, and permission fallback when optimized_pagination is absent or the user lacks access. Without tests, these failure modes are easy to regress.

title: BasePaginator now allows negative offsets that Django QuerySets cannot slice with
body: BasePaginator.get_result now uses cursor.offset directly when cursor.is_prev is true and then slices the queryset with that offset. Cursor strings can contain negative offsets, and this change permits them for previous pages. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indexing or negative offsets, so a client-supplied cursor such as 0:-1:1 can raise AssertionError or produce invalid SQL, causing 500s on any endpoint using this paginator.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator explicitly slices querysets with negative offsets
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result sets start_offset to cursor.offset when enable_advanced_features is true and the offset is negative, then slices the Django queryset. Django does not support negative QuerySet indexing or slicing, so this will fail at runtime rather than provide efficient pagination. The audit-log endpoint enables this feature, so a negative cursor can crash the request. The negative offset is also left in later length checks, making result trimming unreliable.

title: Optimized pagination is used with a datetime ordering field but only supports numeric keys
body: The endpoint selects OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by=-datetime. Unlike DateTimePaginator, OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor or math.ceil on the field value, and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor value instead of converting it to a datetime. With any non-empty audit-log page, get_item_key will receive a datetime and raise TypeError, and cursor values would not be converted correctly for the datetime filter. The optimized audit-log pagination path is therefore broken.

title: Span buffer keys are changed from Redis sets to sorted sets without migration
body: The previous implementation stored span payloads in Redis sets using sadd, scard, sunionstore, and sscan. This change makes the Lua script and Python buffer operate on the same span-buf:s:* keys as sorted sets using zcard, zunionstore, zpopmin, zadd, and zscan. During deployment, in-flight keys created by the old code will still be sets, so new operations will fail with WRONGTYPE and span ingestion or flushing can break. A key namespace change, migration, or drain is needed.

title: ZUNIONSTORE uses the default SUM aggregation and can corrupt span scores
body: The sorted-set members are span payloads and their scores are end_timestamp_precise. ZUNIONSTORE is called without AGGREGATE MIN or MAX, so if a member exists in both source sets, for example due to duplicate messages or a span being present in both an old and merged buffer, Redis adds the two scores together. The resulting timestamp score is wrong, which can cause incorrect eviction ordering and make some spans never eligible for zpopmin.

title: Segments over 1000 spans are silently truncated during insertion
body: When a merged span buffer has more than 1000 members, the script pops and discards the lowest-scored members. There is no metric, log, or tombstone indicating that spans were dropped, and the eviction can remove spans needed to assemble a complete segment, including potentially important root or parent spans. Flushed segments can therefore be incomplete without any observable signal. The limit is also hardcoded in Lua and ignores the Python max_segment_spans configuration.

title: Redirect resolution limit lowered to 1000 can leave deep segment trees unjoined
body: The script follows at most 1000 redirect hops to find the canonical span buffer. If a redirect chain is longer than that, it stops early and stores the new span against an intermediate set instead of the final merged set. This can split a single trace segment into multiple buffers and produce incomplete or duplicated flushed segments. The previous limit was 10000, so this increases the correctness risk for deep or pathological traces.

title: No tests cover the new optimized audit-log pagination path
body: The endpoint adds a conditional OptimizedCursorPaginator path with advanced pagination behavior, but no API or paginator tests were added for it. The datetime incompatibility and negative-offset behavior introduced by this paginator are therefore unverified, and regressions in this privileged pagination path would not be caught.

title: No tests cover the new sorted-set eviction or large-segment behavior
body: The PR introduces sorted-set storage, score-based eviction at 1000 spans, and a reduced redirect-depth limit, but the updated tests only add end_timestamp_precise to small fixtures. There is no test that inserts more than 1000 spans, verifies which spans are evicted, checks behavior when duplicate members are merged, or exercises redirect chains near the new limit.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator is incompatible with datetime pagination
body: The optimized branch uses OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by='-datetime', but OptimizedCursorPaginator implements numeric cursor key handling (math.floor/math.ceil on the field value and raw numeric values from cursors). AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime field, so building cursors will raise TypeError, and any cursor-based WHERE clause would compare the wrong type. Requests using optimized_pagination=true will fail.

title: Negative offsets are passed to Django queryset slicing, which Django does not support
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator allows start_offset to be negative when enable_advanced_features is true and then executes queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django QuerySet slicing raises AssertionError for negative start/stop values; the comment claiming the ORM handles this is incorrect. This can turn invalid or crafted cursors into endpoint 500 errors.

title: BasePaginator still permits negative offsets for previous cursors
body: The new offset handling clamps negative offsets only when cursor.is_prev is false. For previous-page cursors, a negative offset is passed directly to queryset[start_offset:stop]. Since Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indices, a malformed cursor can crash any endpoint using BasePaginator-derived paginators.

title: Typo assigns queryset.query.order_b instead of queryset.query.order_by
body: In build_queryset, when reversing an existing descending ordering for previous-page pagination, the code assigns queryset.query.order_b = tuple(new_order_by) instead of queryset.query.order_by. The ordering change is silently dropped, which can cause wrong ordering, duplicated rows, or skipped rows when paginating backwards over a queryset that already has descending ordering.

title: Switching span buffer keys from sets to sorted sets without migration breaks existing Redis data
body: process_spans now uses ZADD on span-buf:s:* keys, and add-buffer.lua uses ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE, but existing keys created by prior versions are Redis sets with the same key names. During rollout, operations on those existing set-type keys will fail with WRONGTYPE errors, causing span-buffer script failures and potential loss of in-flight spans. A new key namespace or drain/migration strategy is needed.

title: Eviction limit is hardcoded in Lua and ignores SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans
body: The Lua script caps segment buffers at 1000 members, while SpansBuffer still accepts max_segment_spans (default 1001) and no longer enforces it in Python. This makes the configuration option ineffective and creates a mismatch between the configured default and the actual enforced limit.

title: Eviction can remove the root span while the has-root-span flag remains set
body: zpopmin evicts the lowest-scored members by end_timestamp_precise. If the root/segment span is among the evicted members, the span-buf:hrs:* key may still indicate that the segment has a root span, causing the segment to be flushed under root-span timing while no flushed payload is marked is_segment. This can produce inconsistent or rootless segments.

title: __reduce__ passes redis_ttl as the segment_page_size constructor argument
body: SpansBuffer.__reduce__ returns four positional constructor arguments: assigned_shards, span_buffer_timeout_secs, span_buffer_root_timeout_secs, and self.redis_ttl. The constructor's fourth positional parameter is segment_page_size; redis_ttl is the seventh parameter. When SpansBuffer is unpickled (for example, when used with multiprocessing), it will be restored with segment_page_size set to the TTL value and redis_ttl reset to its default.

title: Direct access to end_timestamp_precise can crash the consumer on missing field
body: process_batch reads val["end_timestamp_precise"] directly. If any incoming span message omits this field (for example, a legacy producer, malformed message, or schema evolution case), the consumer raises KeyError and can stall or poison-pile processing. A fallback or explicit validation/handling should be used for the new required score field.

title: No coverage for eviction, large segments, or storage-format migration
body: The buffer tests only exercise small segments and add end_timestamp_precise values. There are no tests for segments exceeding the new 1000-member eviction cap, behavior when existing Redis keys are still sets from the previous storage format, or correctness of eviction order/root-span handling. These are high-risk parts of the change and need tests.

title: Optimized paginator is incompatible with datetime ordering
body: The endpoint uses OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by='-datetime'. OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil on the field value and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor value, while AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime. Any non-empty optimized page will raise TypeError, and the cursor value would also be compared to a timestamp column as an integer.

title: Negative offset slicing in OptimizedCursorPaginator will crash
body: When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset is negative, OptimizedCursorPaginator slices the queryset with a negative start offset and possibly a negative stop offset. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing, so this raises AssertionError. Since cursor offsets come from client-provided cursor strings and the audit-log endpoint enables advanced features, an authorized user can trigger a 500.

title: BasePaginator now passes negative prev offsets to QuerySet slicing
body: The new start_offset logic uses cursor.offset directly when cursor.is_prev is true. If a client supplies a negative offset in a previous-page cursor, the queryset is sliced with a negative offset. Django QuerySets do not support negative offsets, so this raises AssertionError. This affects all BasePaginator subclasses, including DateTimePaginator.

title: Typo prevents reversing queryset ordering for previous pages
body: In BasePaginator.build_queryset, when converting an existing '-key' ordering to ascending for a previous page, the code assigns to queryset.query.order_b instead of queryset.query.order_by. The queryset ordering is therefore not changed, so previous-page pagination can query with the wrong ORDER BY and return incorrect results. This affects paginators built on BasePaginator, including the new OptimizedCursorPaginator.

title: Changing span-buf:s:* keys from sets to sorted sets is not migration-safe
body: The PR changes span buffer keys from Redis sets (SADD/SCARD/SSCAN) to sorted sets (ZADD/ZCARD/ZSCAN) while keeping the same key names. Existing in-flight keys written by the old code can remain for up to redis_ttl, default 3600 seconds. New ZADD/ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZSCAN operations on those set-typed keys will return WRONGTYPE errors, causing span buffering and flushing failures during rollout.

title: Silent eviction can drop spans, including root spans, and ignores configured limits
body: The Lua script uses ZPOPMIN to remove the lowest-scored members whenever a segment has more than 1000 spans. This silently discards spans, can evict the root/segment span while leaving the has_root_span flag set, and bypasses the Python max_segment_spans configuration. There is no metric or log, so incomplete segments can be produced without observability.

title: ZUNIONSTORE default SUM can corrupt span scores
body: The Lua script uses ZUNIONSTORE without specifying AGGREGATE. If the same span payload/member exists in both source sorted sets, Redis sums the end_timestamp_precise scores. The corrupted score changes eviction order and can prevent the span from being evicted when expected. An explicit AGGREGATE MAX or MIN should be used.

title: max_segment_spans parameter is now ignored
body: SpansBuffer still accepts and stores max_segment_spans, but the new Lua script hardcodes the cap at 1000 and the Python flush path no longer enforces max_segment_spans. Callers configuring this parameter will get a different silent limit and a behavior change from skipping oversized segments to evicting spans.

title: Consumer assumes end_timestamp_precise is present and valid
body: process_batch indexes val['end_timestamp_precise'] and passes it directly to Redis ZADD as a score. If a message lacks the field, has null, or has a non-numeric value, the consumer raises KeyError/TypeError and processing stops. Since this field is newly required by the buffer, invalid or older messages need validation or a safe fallback.

title: Redirect-chain limit reduced to 1000 may split deep traces
body: The redirect resolution loop was lowered from 10000 to 1000. If a redirect chain is longer than 1000, the script stops early and maps the span to an intermediate set, which can prevent related spans from being merged into the same segment. This trades correctness for bounded runtime and should be documented or metered.

title: No tests cover eviction, large segments, or sorted-set migration
body: The updated tests only add end_timestamp_precise to small segments. They do not create more than 1000 spans, do not verify which spans are evicted by score, do not test duplicate-member ZUNIONSTORE behavior, and do not cover interaction with old set-typed keys. Given the new data-dropping behavior, this is a significant test gap.

title: Optimized audit-log pagination path has no tests
body: The new optimized_pagination branch and OptimizedCursorPaginator are not covered by tests. Given the datetime incompatibility and negative-offset crash paths, this endpoint/paginator combination needs explicit tests before merging.

title: Accidental git submodule added
body: The PR adds a gitlink/submodule entry `sentry-repo` pointing at commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a. This is unrelated to the upsampling feature and introduces an unwanted submodule, which can break clones or repository tooling. Remove it before merging.

title: upsampled_count can undercount or return NULL when sample_weight is missing
body: The new aggregate computes `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` with no null/default handling. If any row in an allowlisted project query has missing or NULL `sample_weight` (older SDK events, events without error-sampling context, or non-error rows included by mistake), those rows contribute zero or the aggregate may become NULL, causing silently wrong error counts. Use a default such as coalesce/ifNull(sample_weight, 1) or prove the column is always populated.

title: upsampled_count is exposed as a public query function
body: The `upsampled_count` SnQL function is added without `private=True`. If it is selectable through public query APIs, callers can bypass the allowlist and dataset guards and request upsampled counts in contexts where they are not valid, causing incorrect results or query failures. Mark it private if it is only meant for internal rewriting.

title: Discover error-focus detection uses unsafe substring match
body: `_is_error_focused_query` returns true whenever the raw query contains `event.type:error`. This also matches negated filters like `!event.type:error`, mixed queries like `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`, and text inside quoted values. For discover queries this can rewrite count() for non-error data and produce wrong counts. Parse the query or require a strictly error-only condition.

title: Upsampling decision ignores the actual scoped dataset and query
body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset` and `query`, but the eligibility check uses the outer `dataset` and original HTTP request. In split/fallback paths the executed query can have additional conditions or a different dataset, so the upsampling decision can be made from stale context. Pass the actual scoped dataset and final query to the eligibility helper.

title: Eligibility cache key is lossy and not invalidated when the allowlist changes
body: The cache key uses `hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))`, which is a lossy key: different project sets can collide and Python's built-in hash is not meant to be a stable external identifier. The cache also has no automatic invalidation when the allowlist option changes; `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is unused. This can reuse an eligibility result for the wrong projects or serve stale allowlist state. Use an explicit key such as sorted IDs joined or SHA-256, and wire invalidation or remove the dead helper.

title: Top-event ordering is not transformed for upsampling
body: When upsampling is enabled for top events, only the y-axis columns are rewritten. The `orderby` value passed to top-events queries is not transformed, so if the request orders by count() the top-N selection can be based on raw counts while the returned series use upsampled counts. Transform or validate ordering expressions as well.

title: Tests do not cover failure modes introduced by upsampling
body: The endpoint tests only cover explicit `event.type:error` discover queries with allowlisted projects. They do not cover missing/null `sample_weight`, mixed or negated discover filters, the errors dataset, top-event ordering, or cache staleness/invalidation. These are the primary paths where the new transformation can silently change counts, so they need coverage.

title: Test factory skips zero sample rates and swallows errors
body: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` uses truthiness, so a valid client_sample_rate of 0 is ignored, and broad exception handling hides malformed contexts. If zero-rate events are meaningful for upsampling, tests will not exercise them. Use an is-not-None check and narrower error handling.

title: Accidental submodule/gitlink added to the repository
body: The PR adds a file `sentry-repo` containing `Subproject commit ...`, which Git treats as a gitlink/submodule. This appears unrelated to the upsampling feature and can break clones, CI, packaging, or tooling because it introduces an implicit submodule without a `.gitmodules` entry. It should be removed from the PR.

title: Upsampling eligibility is computed from the wrong dataset
body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset`, but the eligibility check calls `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(..., dataset, ...)` using the outer request `dataset`. The dashboard-split logic can call `_get_event_stats` with a different dataset (for example `discover`), so the decision to transform `count()` is based on the original request dataset rather than the dataset actually being queried. This can skip upsampling for an eligible query or apply the wrong dataset assumptions. The check should use `scoped_dataset`.

title: Error-focused query detection uses an unsafe substring match
body: `_is_error_focused_query` returns true whenever the raw query contains the substring `event.type:error`. This matches negated queries such as `!event.type:error` or `NOT event.type:error`, mixed queries such as `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`, and text inside quoted strings. In those cases `count()` is rewritten to `upsampled_count()` even though the result set may include non-error events or no errors, which can produce incorrect counts or reference `sample_weight` where it is not valid. The query should be parsed, or the transform should require an unambiguous positive error-only filter.

title: upsampled_count does not handle missing sample_weight
body: The new aggregate is implemented as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`. Events without a `sample_weight` value (historical events from before upsampling rollout, events with missing/invalid sampling context, or non-error rows accidentally included) will not contribute a fallback count of 1. This can silently produce zero or severely undercounted results. A safer expression would coalesce missing weights to 1, e.g. `sum(coalesce(sample_weight, 1))`, or otherwise conditionally fall back to normal counting.

title: upsampled_count truncates fractional sample weights
body: `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` truncates the summed weight. Sample weights derived from sample rates are often fractional (for example rate 0.3 gives weight about 3.333), so truncating biases error counts downward, especially in small time buckets. Consider returning a float/number or applying an explicit rounding strategy after summing.

title: upsampled_count is exposed as a public query function
body: The new `upsampled_count` SnQL function is not marked `private=True`, unlike adjacent internal functions. If users can select arbitrary functions in discover/events queries, they could invoke `upsampled_count()` directly and bypass the allowlist/dataset gating in `error_upsampling.py`, potentially producing incorrect results or causing Snuba errors on datasets/rows without `sample_weight`. Mark the function private or add server-side validation if it is intended only for internal transformation.

title: Eligibility cache has no effective invalidation
body: The helper caches allowlist eligibility for 60 seconds, but `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is never called and the cache key does not include the allowlist value or a configuration version. If `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` changes, queries can continue using stale eligibility for up to 60 seconds, potentially applying or omitting upsampling incorrectly. Wire invalidation to option changes or include a hash/version of the allowlist in the cache key.

title: Cache key relies on Python tuple hash
body: The cache key uses `hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))`. Python hash output is not a transparent or collision-resistant serialization for cache keys; a collision would allow one project set to reuse another set's cached eligibility. Use a deterministic key such as comma-joined project IDs or a digest of that string.

title: Integration tests do not isolate the upsampling eligibility cache
body: The new endpoint tests change the mocked allowlist between tests for the same organization/project IDs but do not clear or invalidate the `error_upsampling_eligible` cache. If the real cache is active in tests, the first test can cache eligibility and later partial/no-allowlist tests become order-dependent or produce misleading results. Clear or patch the cache in these tests.

title: Accidental submodule/gitlink added to repository root
body: The PR adds a file named `sentry-repo` containing a Git subproject commit pointer. This looks like an accidental embedded repository/submodule rather than an intentional source change. There is no corresponding `.gitmodules` entry or documented reason for it, and it can break clones, CI checkouts, and tooling that does not expect an embedded repository at the repo root. It should be removed from the PR.

title: Upsampling decision uses the original dataset/request instead of the query actually executed
body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset`, and may later execute a modified query such as a dashboard-split query (`... AND !event.type:transaction` or `... AND event.type:transaction`). However the upsampling eligibility check is computed from the outer `dataset` and the original HTTP request only: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)`. It does not consider the actual `scoped_dataset` or the final `query` being executed. This can cause the `count()` rewrite to be applied to a transaction-like query, or skipped for an error-only split query, leading to incorrect counts or query failures. The eligibility check should be based on the actual dataset and query passed to the query executor.

title: Substring check for `event.type:error` can misclassify discover queries
body: `_is_error_focused_query` returns True whenever the raw query string contains the substring `event.type:error`. This is unsafe for Sentry search syntax: it matches negated queries such as `!event.type:error`, compound queries such as `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`, and text inside quoted values. For the discover dataset this enables `upsampled_count()` for mixed or non-error event queries, where `sample_weight` may be missing, zero, or inapplicable, producing silently incorrect counts. The check needs to parse/understand the query rather than using a raw substring match.

title: `upsampled_count` assumes valid integral `sample_weight` values
body: The new `upsampled_count` aggregate is implemented as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`. This has two data-correctness risks: (1) if any event in an allowlisted project has a NULL/missing/zero `sample_weight`, the contribution can be dropped or become zero even though the event exists; (2) if `sample_weight` can be fractional, `toInt64` truncates the summed result and biases counts downward. Project-level allowlisting does not by itself guarantee every event has a valid integral weight. Consider using an explicit fallback such as `coalesce(sample_weight, 1)` and avoiding lossy integer casting unless weights are guaranteed integral.

title: Eligibility cache can serve stale upsampling decisions and invalidation is not wired
body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` caches project allowlist eligibility for 60 seconds keyed by organization and project set. If the `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` option changes during that window, especially when a project is removed from the allowlist, queries can continue to use upsampled counts incorrectly. The provided `invalidate_upsampling_cache` helper is not called from anywhere, and it only invalidates one exact project-set key rather than all affected keys. This creates a data-integrity window after configuration changes. Include a config/version token in the cache key or wire up broader invalidation.

title: Cache key construction sorts and hashes all project IDs on every call
body: The cache key is built with `hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))` before checking whether the dataset/query is even eligible for upsampling. For organizations with many projects, this adds sorting and hashing overhead to every events-stats request, including datasets where upsampling is never applied. A cheaper early-out for non-applicable datasets, or a more efficient stable key, would avoid undermining the stated performance optimization.

title: Endpoint tests do not exercise the explicit `errors` dataset path
body: The upsampling helper unconditionally applies for the `errors` dataset, but the added endpoint tests only use the default/discover path and one explicit `dataset=discover` case. There is no test with `dataset=errors`, so the branch where the rewrite is always enabled for the errors dataset is not covered. This is important because the new SnQL function was added in the discover dataset configuration and the errors-dataset behavior may differ.

title: Analytics recording assumes request.user.id is always available
body: The endpoint records analytics with user_id=request.user.id before checking feature flags or request-body validity. This endpoint also supports org auth tokens (it later checks is_org_auth_token_auth(request.auth)), where request.user may be anonymous or not a normal user. If request.user has no usable id, this can fail or record invalid analytics. Since user_id is optional in the analytics event, this should be guarded (e.g., getattr(request.user, 'id', None)).

title: Unbounded report array can cause resource exhaustion on an unauthenticated endpoint
body: The browser reporting collector endpoint is unauthenticated and iterates over every element in the incoming JSON array, validating each one with a DRF serializer. There is no cap on the number of reports or on the size/depth of each report body. A malicious client can POST a very large array or deeply nested bodies, causing CPU, memory, and log pressure. Add a maximum report count and/or body-size limits.

title: age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validation uses truthiness and misses zero values
body: validate_timestamp checks self.initial_data.get('age') and validate_age checks self.initial_data.get('timestamp') using truthiness. Because 0 is falsy, a report with timestamp present and age=0, or age present and timestamp=0, bypasses the intended mutual-exclusion validation. Additionally, age has no min_value, so negative ages are accepted. This allows invalid browser reports to be accepted and counted.

title: Full unauthenticated request body is logged at INFO level
body: The endpoint logs the entire browser reporting request body at INFO level: logger.info('browser_report_received', extra={'request_body': request.data}). These reports are unauthenticated and can contain URLs, user-agent strings, and other potentially sensitive or user-controlled data. This can create privacy issues and log-volume abuse. Log only metadata or redact/sanitize request bodies.

title: Error events can be mismatched with nodestore data when zipping values
body: fetch_error_details builds node_ids from error_ids, calls nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids), then zips error_ids with events.values(). get_multi returns a mapping, and missing keys or implementation-specific ordering mean events.values() is not guaranteed to align with error_ids. This can associate the wrong title/message/timestamp with an error id or silently drop entries, producing incorrect AI summary input. Look up each event by its generated node id instead of zipping values.

title: Feature-flagged table widget renders hardcoded empty data instead of widget results
body: When organization.features.includes('use-table-widget-visualization') is true, WidgetCardChart renders TableWidgetVisualization with columns={[]} and tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}}. It ignores the actual table result data, meta, fields, aliases, and loading state. Users with this flag enabled will see an empty table instead of the dashboard widget's query results. The visualization needs to be wired to result.data, result.meta, and the derived columns.

title: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES are only hidden while searching
body: The Attributes component returns the sorted attribute list unchanged when searchQuery is empty, and only applies the HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES filter inside the search branch. As a result, internal attributes such as is_segment, project_id, and received remain visible in the default unfiltered view. The hidden-attribute filter should be applied before or independent of search filtering.

title: PR comment template inserts unescaped issue title and environment into Markdown
body: MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE formats issue titles and environment names directly into a Markdown link: '* ‼️ [**{title}**]({url}){environment}'. Issue titles and environment names can contain Markdown metacharacters such as brackets or backticks, which can break the link formatting or produce unintended Markdown in GitHub/GitLab PR comments. Escape or sanitize these values before templating.

title: PR comment generation may call get_recommended_event for each top issue
body: get_environment_info calls issue.get_recommended_event() while building the merged-PR comment body. This is invoked for each issue in the comment, potentially causing expensive event lookups inside a task that formats PR comments. The broad exception handling also hides failures while still adding latency. Consider caching, limiting this lookup, or making environment enrichment asynchronous/optional.

title: zip(error_ids, events.values()) misaligns error IDs with event data when some events are missing
body: In fetch_error_details, `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a dict that only contains entries for node_ids that were found. If some events are missing from nodestore, `events.values()` will have fewer items than `error_ids`, and `zip(error_ids, events.values())` will pair the wrong error_id with the wrong event data. For example, if error_ids=[A,B,C] but only A and C are found, zip will pair A with A's data and B with C's data. The fix should iterate over error_ids and look up each node_id individually in the events dict, e.g., `for event_id in error_ids: data = events.get(Event.generate_node_id(project_id, event_id=event_id))`.

title: Mutual exclusion validation for age/timestamp uses truthiness instead of key presence
body: In validate_timestamp, the check `if self.initial_data.get("age")` will be falsy when age=0, which is a valid value. Similarly in validate_age, `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp")` will be falsy when timestamp=0. This means a report with both age=0 and timestamp=5 will pass validation when it should be rejected. The checks should use `"age" in self.initial_data` and `"timestamp" in self.initial_data` respectively.

title: Feature-flagged TableWidgetVisualization renders empty table with no actual data
body: When the `use-table-widget-visualization` feature flag is enabled, the code renders a TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded empty data (`columns={[]}`, `tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}}`) instead of passing the actual `result.data`, `result.meta`, and column information. This means enabling this feature flag will cause all dashboard table widgets to display empty tables, losing all data visibility. The actual table results (fields, data, meta, etc.) need to be wired through to the new component.

title: Full request body logged at INFO level on unauthenticated endpoint
body: The endpoint logs `logger.info("browser_report_received", extra={"request_body": request.data})` for every request. Since this is an unauthenticated endpoint (permission_classes=()) that receives browser Reporting API data, this will log URLs, user agents, and potentially sensitive report bodies (CSP violations can contain page content details) at INFO level in production logs. This creates a privacy concern and could lead to log volume issues. Consider logging at DEBUG level or only logging metadata (report type, count) rather than full bodies.

title: analytics.record with request.user.id may fail for org auth token authentication
body: The analytics.record call uses `user_id=request.user.id` unconditionally. While the analytics event defines user_id as `required=False`, the code always attempts to access `request.user.id`. If the request is authenticated via an org auth token where `request.user` might be an AnonymousUser or a token-based identity without a traditional `.id`, this will raise an AttributeError and fail the entire request before any processing occurs. The code later checks `is_org_auth_token_auth(request.auth)` suggesting token auth is supported. Consider using `getattr(request.user, 'id', None)` or recording analytics after determining the user identity.

title: get_merged_pr_single_issue_template references PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title which may not exist on that class
body: The static method `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` on `CommitContextIntegration` calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title)`, but `_truncate_title` is defined as a static method on `CommitContextIntegration` itself (line 577).
