title: Inconsistent destinationCalendar format in webhook payloads: null vs empty array
body: The BOOKING_CREATED webhook test expects `destinationCalendar: null` (line 119) while BOOKING_REJECTED expects `destinationCalendar: []` (line 249). This inconsistency in the webhook payload format is a breaking change for webhook consumers who may be checking for `null` specifically. The BOOKING_CREATED path likely still serializes `destinationCalendar` as `null` when no calendar is set, while BOOKING_REJECTED now sends an empty array. A consistent format should be chosen.

title: await on array does not wait for promises to resolve
body: At line 619, `await apiDeletes` awaits an array of promises directly, which resolves immediately without waiting for the individual promises to settle. This should be `await Promise.all(apiDeletes)` or `await Promise.allSettled(apiDeletes)`. As a result, the function may return success before calendar events are actually deleted from external providers. While this is a pre-existing issue, the surrounding code was significantly modified in this PR.

title: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys that evaluate to literal strings, making the schema non-functional
body: The expressions `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` evaluate to the literal strings `"ZodString"` and `"ZodOptional"` respectively, not dynamic key patterns. This means the schema requires a property literally named "ZodString" with a number value, which no real OAuth token response will have. When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is true, `safeParse` will always fail, causing `parseRefreshTokenResponse` to throw "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned" for every token refresh, completely breaking the credential sharing feature. The intended behavior was likely `.passthrough()` or `.catchall(z.unknown())`.

title: Inconsistent return type breaks callers when credential sharing is enabled
body: When credential sharing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch` `Response` object. When disabled, it returns whatever `refreshFunction()` returns (e.g., a GaxiosResponse with `.data` for Google, a HubspotToken object for Hubspot, an AxiosResponse with `.data` for Zoho). Callers like Google Calendar (`res?.data`), Hubspot (`hubspotRefreshToken.expiryDate`), and Zoho Bigin (`tokenInfo.data.error`) will crash or produce undefined values when credential sharing is enabled because a `Response` object doesn't have those properties.

title: `prisma` is used but never imported, causing a ReferenceError at runtime
body: The newly added code calls `prisma.credential.update(...)` on line 96, but `prisma` is not imported anywhere in this file. The existing imports include jsforce, rrule, zod, and various @calcom packages, but not `@calcom/prisma`. This will throw a ReferenceError the first time the Salesforce calendar service attempts to refresh a token.

title: Placeholder string "refresh_token" stored as actual refresh token value
body: When the parsed token response lacks a `refresh_token` field, the code sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` (a literal placeholder string). This value is then persisted to the database via `prisma.credential.update` in callers like Google Calendar and Office 365. On the next token refresh cycle, this placeholder will be sent to the OAuth provider, which will reject it, permanently breaking the credential until manually fixed.

title: Webhook secret comparison is not timing-safe
body: The webhook secret is compared using `!==` (line 25-27), which is vulnerable to timing attacks. An attacker can iteratively guess the secret character by character by measuring response times. For security-sensitive secret comparisons, `crypto.timingSafeEqual` should be used after ensuring both buffers are the same length.

title: No HTTP method restriction on credential webhook endpoint
body: The handler does not check `req.method`, so it accepts GET, PUT, DELETE, etc. in addition to POST. This increases the attack surface (e.g., secrets could appear in server access logs via GET query parameters if a proxy rewrites headers). The endpoint should restrict to POST only.

title: Credential ID passed where user ID is expected in refreshOAuthTokens call
body: The third argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is `credentialId` (the credential's database primary key from line 53), but the function's parameter is named `userId` and is sent to the external sync endpoint as `calcomUserId`. The external service will receive a credential ID instead of a user ID, making it unable to look up the correct user's tokens. It should be the user's ID associated with the credential.

title: Zod parse throws unhandled error returning 500 instead of 400 for invalid input
body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` will throw a `ZodError` if the request body doesn't match the schema. Without a try/catch or `.safeParse()`, this results in an unhandled exception and a 500 Internal Server Error response instead of a proper 400 Bad Request, leaking implementation details in the error response.

title: Hubspot token refresh will crash when credential sharing is enabled due to type mismatch
body: When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is true, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch` Response object. The code assigns it to `hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken` and immediately accesses `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` (line 192) and `hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken` (line 202), which are properties of the HubSpot SDK's token object, not of a `Response`. This will result in `undefined` values being stored and used, breaking the HubSpot integration.

title: refresh_token is set to the literal string "refresh_token" when missing
body: When `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token` is falsy, the code sets it to the literal string `"refresh_token"`. This is clearly a placeholder/debug value that was accidentally left in. This will corrupt the stored credential by overwriting a missing refresh token with a meaningless string, causing all subsequent token refresh attempts to fail permanently for that credential.

title: Invalid Zod schema definition using z.string().toString() as object key
body: `z.string().toString()` evaluates to the literal string `"ZodString"` at runtime, not a catchall key. The schema `minimumTokenResponseSchema` will have a property literally named `"ZodString"` that expects a number, rather than acting as a catchall for arbitrary numeric properties. This means the schema will not validate token responses correctly when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is true, likely causing valid responses to fail validation or invalid ones to pass.

title: prisma is used but never imported
body: The `getClient` method calls `prisma.credential.update(...)` on line 96, but `prisma` is never imported in this file. The imports include `getAppKeysFromSlug`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, `HttpError`, `logger`, etc., but not `prisma from "@calcom/prisma"`. This will cause a `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` at runtime whenever a Salesforce credential is refreshed.

title: Return type inconsistency causes runtime errors in callers expecting parsed tokens
body: When credential syncing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch` `Response` object. When disabled, it returns whatever the `refreshFunction` returns (which varies: Axios responses for Zoho, HubspotToken objects for HubSpot, GaxiosResponse for Google). Callers like HubSpot (`hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn`), Zoho Bigin (`tokenInfo.data.error`), and Google Calendar (`res?.data`) access properties that don't exist on a raw `Response` object, causing `undefined` access and silent data corruption or crashes when syncing is enabled.

title: Webhook endpoint does not restrict HTTP method
body: The handler does not check `req.method`, so it accepts GET, DELETE, PUT, PATCH, etc. in addition to POST. A webhook endpoint that creates/updates credentials should only accept POST requests. Accepting other methods increases the attack surface and could lead to unexpected behavior with caching proxies or preflight requests.

title: Race condition between findFirst and create/update
body: The code first searches for an existing credential with `findFirst`, then either updates or creates it. Between these two operations, a concurrent request could create the same credential, leading to duplicate credentials for the same user+app combination. Since `userId` and `appId` are not unique constraints in the schema (as evidenced by the `findFirst` usage), this can result in multiple credentials for the same user-app pair, with unpredictable behavior on which one gets used.

title: credentialId passed as userId to refreshOAuthTokens
body: The third argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is `credentialId` (the credential's database ID), but the function expects `userId` (the user's ID). When credential syncing is enabled, the sync endpoint will receive the credential ID instead of the user ID in the `calcomUserId` parameter, causing it to look up tokens for the wrong entity.

title: Uncaught exception when decryption or JSON parsing fails
body: If `symmetricDecrypt` throws (e.g., wrong key, corrupted data) or `JSON.parse` throws (decrypted content is not valid JSON), the error is unhandled and will result in an unformatted 500 response. Since this is an externally-facing webhook endpoint, malformed payloads are expected and should be handled gracefully with a 400 response.

title: tokenResponse.success check is dead code after parseRefreshTokenResponse change
body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` now throws an error if parsing fails (line 21-23 of that file), so it never returns a result with `success: false`. The expression `tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data` on line 264 will always evaluate to `tokenResponse.data`. While not a crash, the spread `...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data)` is misleading and the `tokenResponse.success` check gives a false sense of safety. If `parseRefreshTokenResponse` behavior changes in the future, this pattern silently produces `false` being spread (which is a no-op) instead of handling the error.

title: No authentication on outbound request to credential sync endpoint
body: The `fetch` call to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends the user's `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` without any authentication header, API key, or webhook secret. If the endpoint URL is compromised or misconfigured, any party that can observe or intercept the request could enumerate user IDs and app slugs. The inbound webhook requires a secret, but the outbound sync request does not verify the identity of the sync endpoint.

title: Missing `prisma` import causes compilation failure
body: The newly added code at line 96 calls `prisma.credential.update(...)`, but `prisma` is never imported in this file. The imports section (lines 1-20) does not include `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"`. This will cause a TypeScript compilation error and prevent the build from succeeding.

title: Missing refresh_token is replaced with literal placeholder string, corrupting stored credentials
body: When `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token` is falsy, it is set to the literal string `"refresh_token"`. This placeholder value will be persisted to the database via `prisma.credential.update` in all callers. On the next token refresh attempt, this invalid string will be sent to the OAuth provider as the refresh token, causing the refresh to fail permanently. The credential becomes unusable until the user re-authenticates.

title: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses invalid Zod computed keys that don't create a catch-all
body: `[z.string().toString()]` evaluates to a literal string key (the toString representation of a ZodString instance, e.g. something like `"ZodString"`), not a dynamic catch-all index signature. Zod does not support this pattern for passthrough/catchall behavior. The schema will only validate `access_token` and the two literal computed keys, rejecting or ignoring all other properties depending on strictness. The intended behavior should use `.passthrough()` or `.catchall(z.unknown())` on the object schema.

title: Token refresh crashes when credential sharing is enabled because Response object has no `.data` property
body: When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is true, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch` `Response` object from the sync endpoint. The code then accesses `res?.data` (line 94), but a `Response` object does not have a `.data` property—it needs `.json()` to be called first. This means `token` is `undefined`, and `token.access_token` on line 95 throws a TypeError, breaking all Google Calendar operations for users when credential sharing is enabled.

title: credentialId passed instead of userId to refreshOAuthTokens
body: The third argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is `credentialId` (which is `credential.id`, the credential's database primary key), but the function's parameter is named `userId` and it is sent as `calcomUserId` to the credential sync endpoint. The sync endpoint expects the Cal.com user ID to look up the correct tokens. Passing the credential ID instead means the external system will receive the wrong identifier and likely return incorrect or no tokens.

title: Webhook secret comparison vulnerable to timing attacks
body: The webhook secret is compared using strict inequality (`!==`), which short-circuits on the first differing character. An attacker can measure response times to progressively determine the secret character by character. A constant-time comparison function (e.g., `crypto.timingSafeEqual`) should be used instead.

title: Race condition between findFirst and create/update can produce duplicate credentials
body: The code performs a `findFirst` to check for an existing credential, then conditionally creates or updates it. If two concurrent webhook requests arrive for the same user and app, both may pass the `findFirst` check (finding no existing credential) and both proceed to `create`, resulting in duplicate credential rows. This should use a database-level upsert or a transaction with a unique constraint.

title: Webhook endpoint does not restrict HTTP method
body: The handler function does not check `req.method`, so it accepts GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, and any other HTTP method. A webhook endpoint that creates/updates credentials should only accept POST requests. Allowing GET means the endpoint could be triggered via image tags, link prefetching, or browser preloading, potentially with cached or logged query parameters.

title: Credential sync endpoint called without authentication, exposing user tokens to any network-reachable service
body: The fetch to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` with no authentication headers, API keys, or signed payloads. If this endpoint is reachable beyond the intended internal network (e.g., misconfigured firewall, exposed on a public IP), any caller can request OAuth tokens for arbitrary users by guessing or enumerating user IDs.

title: Zod parse failure returns unhandled 500 instead of 400
body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a `ZodError` if the request body doesn't match the schema. Since there's no try/catch around this call and no custom error handler, Next.js will return a generic 500 Internal Server Error. The endpoint should catch the ZodError and return a 400 with validation details so callers can diagnose malformed requests.

title: Authorization logic uses AND instead of OR for team admin/owner check
body: The condition `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))` requires the user to be BOTH a team admin AND a team owner. The intent is clearly that either role should be sufficient (i.e., `||`). As written, a team admin who is not an owner (or vice versa) will be denied access to add guests unless they also happen to be the organizer or an attendee. This effectively breaks the feature for most team members.

title: Email sending uses unfiltered `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`
body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the raw input `guests` array, but `uniqueGuests` is the filtered list that was actually added to the booking (excluding already-existing attendees and blacklisted emails). Inside `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the `newGuests` parameter is used to decide whether to send a full 'scheduled' email (to new guests) or a 'guests added' notification (to existing attendees). If some input emails were filtered out (e.g., duplicates of existing attendees), those existing attendees will incorrectly receive a full scheduled email instead of the notification.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails does not respect eventType email disable settings
body: Unlike peer functions such as `sendLocationChangeEmails` and `sendCancelledEmails`, `sendAddGuestsEmails` does not accept or check `eventTypeMetadata` for `disableStandardEmails` settings. Users who have disabled host or attendee emails at the event type level will still receive add-guests emails, violating their configured preferences.

title: Initial state of [""] causes spurious validation error on empty submit
body: `multiEmailValue` is initialized to `[""]` (array containing one empty string). When the user clicks 'Add' without entering any email, `multiEmailValue.length` is 1, so the early-return guard on line 49 does not trigger. The Zod schema then fails validation on the empty string, showing the user an 'Emails must be unique and valid' error even though they haven't entered anything. The initial state should be `[]` or the guard should also check for empty/whitespace-only strings.

title: addGuests uses authedProcedure instead of bookingsProcedure
body: The `editLocation` endpoint uses `bookingsProcedure` which likely includes additional booking-specific authorization or middleware. The new `addGuests` endpoint uses the more permissive `authedProcedure`. While the handler performs its own authorization check, this inconsistency means any cross-cutting concerns handled by `bookingsProcedure` (e.g., booking existence checks, rate limiting, audit logging) are bypassed for this endpoint.

title: Organizer email subject uses attendees[0].name which may be a newly added guest with empty name
body: The subject line uses `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` for the `{{name}}` interpolation. Since newly added guests have `name: ""` (set in the handler), if a new guest happens to be first in the attendees array, the subject will read 'Guests Added: <eventType> with  at <date>' with a blank name. The original booking's primary attendee or organizer name would be more appropriate.

title: Authorization check uses AND instead of OR for team admin/owner
body: The condition `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))` requires the user to be BOTH a team admin AND a team owner simultaneously. This is almost certainly a logic error — the intent is to allow access if the user is either a team admin OR a team owner. As written, team admins who are not owners (and vice versa) will be incorrectly denied access with a FORBIDDEN error. The operator should be `||`.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails receives unfiltered `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`
body: On line 168, `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the original input `guests` array, which may include emails that were filtered out on lines 74-78 (already-existing attendees or blacklisted emails). Inside `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the `newGuests` parameter is used to decide whether an attendee receives a full 'AttendeeScheduledEmail' (for new guests) or an 'AttendeeAddGuestsEmail' (for existing attendees). If a pre-existing attendee's email is still in `guests`, they will incorrectly receive the 'you have been scheduled' email instead of the 'new guests were added' notification. The call should pass `uniqueGuests` instead.

title: Blacklist check is case-sensitive for guest emails but blacklist is lowercased
body: The `blacklistedGuestEmails` array is lowercased (line 71), but the incoming `guest` email addresses are compared without lowercasing. A guest email like `Blocked@Example.com` would not match `blocked@example.com` in the blacklist, allowing blacklisted emails to bypass the restriction. The comparison should lowercase the guest email: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest.toLowerCase())`.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails does not respect eventType email disable settings
body: Unlike other email-sending functions in this file (e.g., `sendLocationChangeEmails`, `sendScheduledEmails`), `sendAddGuestsEmails` does not accept or check `eventTypeMetadata` for `disableStandardEmails`. This means organizer and attendee emails will be sent even when the event type has explicitly disabled them, violating the user's configuration.

title: Any attendee can add guests to a booking without further authorization
body: The `isAttendee` check on line 52 allows any booking attendee to add arbitrary guests. Depending on the product intent, this may be too permissive — for example, in a team booking scenario, a single attendee could add unlimited external guests. Consider whether this should be restricted to organizers or team admins only, or at least documented as intentional.

title: No rollback if calendar update fails after attendees are persisted
body: The attendees are written to the database on line 92 via `prisma.booking.update`, but the subsequent `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` call on line 165 can fail independently. If it does, the database will have the new attendees but external calendars (Google Calendar, etc.) will not be updated, leading to data inconsistency. There is no compensating transaction or retry mechanism.

title: Hardcoded English string in Tooltip instead of using i18n
body: The Tooltip content `"Remove email"` on line 46 is a hardcoded English string. It should use the `t()` translation function (e.g., `t("remove_email")`) to support internationalization, consistent with the rest of the component which uses `useLocale`.

title: No upper bound on the number of guests that can be added
body: The `guests` array in the input schema has no `.max()` constraint. A malicious or buggy client could submit thousands of email addresses in a single request, causing excessive database writes, email sends, and calendar API calls. Adding a reasonable `.max(N)` limit would mitigate this.

title: Authorization check uses AND instead of OR, blocking legitimate team admins/owners
body: The variable `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&` (logical AND) between `isTeamAdmin(...)` and `isTeamOwner(...)`. This means a user must be BOTH a team admin AND a team owner to pass this check. A team admin who is not an owner (or vice versa) will be denied access. The intent, as indicated by the variable name and the error message on line 55, is clearly to allow either role. The operator should be `||` (logical OR).

title: Passes unfiltered `guests` to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of `uniqueGuests`
body: On line 168, `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the raw `guests` input array. However, `guests` may contain emails that were filtered out on lines 74-78 (already-existing attendees or blacklisted emails). The email function uses this list to decide whether each attendee receives a 'new booking' email (`AttendeeScheduledEmail`) or a 'guests added' notification (`AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`). Passing the unfiltered list means already-existing attendees whose email appears in `guests` will incorrectly receive a full booking confirmation email instead of the 'new guests added' notification. The correct argument is `uniqueGuests`.

title: No check for cancelled or rejected booking status before adding guests
body: The handler fetches the booking and proceeds to add guests without verifying `booking.status`. Adding guests to a cancelled or rejected booking is logically incorrect and could cause confusion (emails sent about a booking that no longer exists, calendar events updated for a cancelled meeting, etc.). A guard such as `if (booking.status === 'CANCELLED' || booking.status === 'REJECTED') throw ...` is missing.

title: isInvalidEmail state not reset on successful submission
body: When `handleAdd` succeeds (validation passes and mutation fires), `setIsInvalidEmail(false)` is never called. If a user first triggers a validation error, then corrects the input and successfully submits, the red error banner will persist in the UI the next time the dialog is opened (assuming the component is not unmounted). The `onSuccess` callback resets `multiEmailValue` but not `isInvalidEmail`.

title: Race condition between attendee existence check and insert
body: The handler reads existing attendees on line 26, filters out duplicates on line 74, then inserts new attendees on line 92. Between the read and the write, a concurrent request could insert the same guest emails, resulting in duplicate attendee rows. Without a database-level unique constraint on (bookingId, email) or a transaction with row-level locking, this can silently create duplicate attendees.

title: Unsafe access to attendees[0] without null check
body: `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` will throw a TypeError if the attendees array is empty. While a booking should normally have at least one attendee, defensive coding (e.g., optional chaining or a fallback) would prevent a crash in edge cases such as data corruption or a booking with all attendees removed.

title: deleteMany OR condition missing method filter will delete non-SMS reminders
body: The second branch of the OR in deleteMany (`{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }`) does not include a `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter. This means any WorkflowReminder row (including EMAIL and WHATSAPP methods) with retryCount > 1 will be deleted. While currently only this SMS code path increments retryCount, the query is semantically incorrect and will silently delete reminders of other methods if retryCount is ever used elsewhere or if data is manually modified. The fix is to add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to the second OR condition.

title: Database update inside catch block can throw and crash the handler
body: If the `prisma.workflowReminder.update` inside the catch block (line 190) itself throws (e.g., the reminder was already deleted by the deleteMany at the top of the handler, or a transient DB error), the exception will propagate unhandled out of the for-loop, aborting processing of all remaining reminders. This inner database call should be wrapped in its own try-catch to ensure one failed update does not prevent other reminders from being processed.

title: Stale retryCount value used for increment may lose updates under concurrent execution
body: The update uses `reminder.retryCount + 1` based on the value read at the start of the loop iteration. If the cron job is invoked concurrently (e.g., overlapping cron schedules or retries), two executions could read the same retryCount and both write retryCount+1, effectively losing one increment. Using Prisma's atomic increment (`retryCount: { increment: 1 }`) would be safer and also more idiomatic.

title: deleteMany with retryCount condition lacks method filter, will delete non-SMS reminders
body: The second condition in the OR clause `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method` filter. This means any WorkflowReminder row (including EMAIL and WHATSAPP methods) with a retryCount greater than 1 will be deleted by this query. While currently only SMS reminders have their retryCount incremented in this file, the query is semantically incorrect and poses a data integrity risk if any other code path ever increments retryCount for non-SMS reminders. The condition should include `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to match the intent described in the PR.

title: retryCount deletion condition does not filter by scheduled status, may delete successfully scheduled reminders
body: The `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` condition in the deleteMany does not include `scheduled: false`. If a reminder was successfully scheduled (scheduled=true, referenceId set) but somehow its retryCount was incremented in a prior failed attempt before eventually succeeding, it would be deleted by this condition, potentially orphaning a valid Twilio scheduled message. Adding `scheduled: false` to the condition would make the intent clearer and safer.

title: deleteMany with retryCount > 1 is not scoped to SMS method, risking deletion of EMAIL/WHATSAPP reminders
body: The second branch of the OR condition `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method` filter. This means any WorkflowReminder row (including EMAIL and WHATSAPP methods) with retryCount > 1 will be deleted by this cron job. While currently only SMS reminders have their retryCount incremented, this is fragile: any future code that touches retryCount on non-SMS reminders, or any data migration/bug that sets it, would cause silent deletion of email or WhatsApp reminders. The condition should include `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to match the intent described in the PR.

title: retryCount increment uses read-then-write pattern instead of atomic increment
body: The code reads `reminder.retryCount` at query time and later writes `reminder.retryCount + 1`. If two cron executions overlap (e.g., due to scheduling delays or retries), both could read the same value and write the same incremented value, effectively losing a retry count. Using Prisma's atomic `{ increment: 1 }` operator instead of `reminder.retryCount + 1` would prevent this lost-update scenario. The same issue exists in the catch block at line 195.

title: Breaking API change: `findMany` method removed without migration path
body: The public `findMany` method that was the primary query interface for consumers of this service has been completely removed and replaced with `getBaseConditions()` which only returns raw SQL conditions. Any existing caller using `service.findMany(...)` will break at compile time. The PR does not show updates to any callers, nor does it provide an equivalent high-level query method. This is a breaking change to the service's public API.

title: Dead code branches in `getBaseConditions` due to always-truthy `authConditions`
body: `getAuthorizationConditions()` always returns a `Prisma.Sql` object (never null or undefined), and `Prisma.Sql` objects are always truthy in JavaScript. Therefore the condition `if (authConditions && filterConditions)` on line 72 effectively only checks `filterConditions`. The `else if (filterConditions)` branch (line 76) and the final `else` branch (line 78) are unreachable dead code. While not a runtime bug, this is misleading and could mask future issues if the return type of `getAuthorizationConditions` changes.

title: Integration test asserts exact result set without isolating from pre-existing data
body: The test `should combine authorization and filter conditions` asserts `expect(results).toEqual([{ id: userBooking.id }])`, expecting exactly one row. If the test database contains other bookings that match the combined conditions (same userId, teamId IS NULL, matching eventTypeId), the test will fail with extra rows. Unlike the old `findMany` test which used Prisma's structured queries with the same isolation concern, this raw query test provides no additional scoping (e.g., by booking UID or creation timestamp) to guarantee isolation from other data.

title: Caching behavior tests removed without replacement
body: The previous test suite included explicit tests verifying that `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions` return cached results on subsequent calls. These tests were removed entirely. While the caching logic still exists in the service (lines 84-95 of insightsBooking.ts), there is no test coverage confirming it works correctly with the new `Prisma.Sql` return type, particularly that the cached `Prisma.Sql` object maintains referential or structural equality across calls.

title: Breaking API change: `findMany` removed and replaced with `getBaseConditions`
body: The public method `findMany(findManyArgs)` has been removed and replaced with `getBaseConditions()` which returns raw SQL conditions instead of executing a query. Any existing callers of `service.findMany(...)` will break at compile time. The PR does not include updates to callers, so this is either an incomplete change or requires a coordinated update in consuming code.

title: Dead code: `else if (filterConditions)` and `else` branches in `getBaseConditions` are unreachable
body: `getAuthorizationConditions()` has return type `Promise<Prisma.Sql>` and always returns a `Prisma.Sql` object (including `NOTHING_CONDITION`), never null or undefined. Therefore `authConditions` is always truthy, making the `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else` branches unreachable dead code. While not a runtime bug, it misleads readers into thinking authorization conditions can be absent.

title: Caching tests removed without replacement
body: The previous test suite included tests verifying that `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions` return cached results on repeated calls. These tests were removed entirely. Since the caching mechanism (`cachedAuthConditions`, `cachedFilterConditions`) still exists in the service, there is no test coverage ensuring it works correctly after the refactor, particularly that `Prisma.Sql` objects are cached and returned by reference or value consistently.

title: Constructor type relaxed from strict discriminated union to loose public type
body: The constructor parameter type changed from `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` (a strict zod-inferred discriminated union that requires `teamId` when `scope` is `"team"`) to `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` (which makes `teamId` optional for all scopes). While runtime validation via `safeParse` still catches invalid input, callers that previously got compile-time errors for missing `teamId` with team scope will now silently pass type-checking and receive `NOTHING_CONDITION` at runtime, potentially hiding integration bugs.

title: Org scope includes org ID in team booking condition, which may match unintended bookings
body: In `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition`, `teamIds` is constructed as `[options.orgId, ...teamsFromOrg.map(t => t.id)]` and used in `("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})) AND ("isTeamBooking" = true)`. This means bookings where `teamId` equals the org's own ID and `isTeamBooking` is true will match. If the org itself is not expected to have direct team bookings (only its child teams should), this could return unintended results. The old code had the same behavior, but this is worth verifying as part of the raw SQL conversion since the semantics are now more explicit.

title: Public method `findMany` removed without replacement, breaking existing callers
body: The previous public API method `findMany(findManyArgs: Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedFindManyArgs)` has been removed and replaced with `getBaseConditions()` which returns a raw `Prisma.Sql` fragment. Any existing callers of `findMany` in the codebase will fail at compile time. Since only two files are changed in this PR, callers elsewhere are not updated. This is a breaking API change that requires coordinated updates or a deprecation path.

title: Dead code branches in `getBaseConditions` — `authConditions` is always truthy
body: `getAuthorizationConditions()` has return type `Promise<Prisma.Sql>` and always returns a `Prisma.Sql` object (never null or undefined). Therefore the `else if (filterConditions)` branch (line 76) and the `else` branch (line 78) in `getBaseConditions` are unreachable dead code. While the function still produces correct results, the misleading control flow may confuse future maintainers into thinking `authConditions` can be falsy, and the `NOTHING_CONDITION` fallback on line 79 can never be reached from this path.

title: Caching behavior tests removed without replacement
body: The previous test suite included a 'Caching' describe block that verified `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions` return cached results on repeated calls. These tests were removed in this PR, but the caching logic (using `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions` fields) still exists in the service. There is now no test coverage for this behavior, meaning a regression that breaks caching (e.g., accidentally removing the cache check) would go undetected.

title: Integration test assumes exact result set from a denormalized view without controlling all data
body: The `getBaseConditions` test at line 481 queries `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized` with `WHERE ${baseConditions}` and asserts the result is exactly `[{ id: userBooking.id }]`. If other tests running in parallel (or leftover data from failed tests) create bookings matching the same user-scope condition (`userId = X AND teamId IS NULL`), this assertion will fail non-deterministically. The test creates its own user but does not isolate against concurrent test data that might reference the same user or match the condition.

title: Authorization check only verifies direct user ownership, missing team/delegation credential support
body: The `deleteCacheHandler` checks `userId: user.id` to verify credential ownership. However, credentials can belong to teams or be used via delegation. If a user is a team member with access to a team credential's calendar cache, they will be denied access with 'Credential not found or access denied'. The UI (CredentialActionsDropdown) shows the delete option based on `cacheUpdatedAt` presence without checking whether the current user can actually authorize the deletion, leading to a guaranteed error for non-directly-owned credentials.

title: deleteCache mutation does not invalidate connectedCalendars query after success
body: After successfully deleting cache, the `deleteCacheMutation` calls `onSuccess?.()` but does not invalidate the `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` tRPC query. Unlike the `disconnectMutation` which explicitly invalidates queries in `onSettled`, the delete cache mutation leaves the UI showing stale `cacheUpdatedAt` data. The cache status label ('Last updated: ...') will remain visible until an unrelated refetch occurs, giving the user incorrect information that cache still exists.

title: Hardcoded 'en-US' locale for date formatting ignores user's locale preference
body: The `Intl.DateTimeFormat` on line 89 hardcodes `'en-US'` as the locale. The component already uses `useLocale()` for translations, but the date formatting does not respect the user's actual locale. Users with non-US locales will see dates formatted in US style (MM/DD/YYYY) rather than their preferred format. The locale should be derived from the user's settings or at minimum use `undefined` to respect the browser's locale.

title: CalendarCacheRepository instantiated directly without checking if calendar cache feature is enabled
body: The handler creates `new CalendarCacheRepository()` and queries the database for cache statuses on every `connectedCalendars` call, regardless of whether the calendar cache feature is enabled for the user's organization. Other parts of the codebase use `CalendarCache.init(null)` which respects feature flags and returns a mock when disabled. This results in unnecessary database queries (`groupBy` on CalendarCache) for all users, even those who don't use calendar cache.

title: Migration warning comment contradicts the actual SQL statement
body: The auto-generated warning comment states 'Added the required column updatedAt to the CalendarCache table without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty.' However, the actual SQL on line 9 uses `DEFAULT NOW()`, which does provide a default value and is safe for non-empty tables. The misleading warning could cause confusion during migration review or if someone considers reverting/modifying the migration.

title: UserWithCalendars type now requires updatedAt and googleChannelId fields, potentially breaking callers
body: The `UserWithCalendars` type was changed to require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` on `allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` entries. Any code outside this PR that constructs a `UserWithCalendars` object (e.g., in tests, other handlers, or platform consumers) will now fail type checking if it doesn't include these fields. The `findUnlockedUserForSession` in `user.ts` was updated, but other callers of `getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb` may not have been.

title: sed -i '' is macOS-specific and will fail on Linux
body: The script uses `sed -i '' -E ...` which is the macOS/BSD sed syntax. On Linux (GNU sed), the correct syntax is `sed -i -E ...` without the empty string argument. Running this script on a Linux development machine will produce an error: 'sed: can't read : No such file or directory'. Since this is a developer utility script, it should either detect the OS or use a portable alternative.

title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds returns expired cache entries
body: The `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` method queries all `CalendarCache` rows for the given credential IDs without filtering by `expiresAt`. This means the UI will display a `cacheUpdatedAt` timestamp even for cache entries that have already expired, misleading users into thinking their cache is still active. The query should include `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` in the `where` clause to only return statuses for valid (non-expired) cache entries.

title: deleteCache mutation does not invalidate connectedCalendars query
body: After successfully deleting cache, the `deleteCacheMutation` calls `onSuccess?.()` but never invalidates the `trpc.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` query. The `disconnectMutation` correctly invalidates it in `onSettled`, but `deleteCacheMutation` does not. As a result, the UI will continue to display the stale `cacheUpdatedAt` timestamp until the user navigates away and returns or manually refreshes. An `onSettled` callback should be added to invalidate `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`.

title: Plain Error thrown instead of TRPCError results in generic 500 response
body: When the credential is not found or access is denied, the handler throws a plain `Error('Credential not found or access denied')`. TRPC will wrap this as an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) with the message potentially hidden from the client depending on configuration. It should throw a `TRPCError` with code `NOT_FOUND` or `FORBIDDEN` so the client receives an appropriate error code and can handle it correctly.

title: Hardcoded 'en-US' locale in date formatting ignores user's locale
body: The `Intl.DateTimeFormat` is hardcoded to `"en-US"` locale. Since this is a user-facing component in an internationalized application (using `useLocale`), it should use the user's actual locale for date formatting. This will display dates in US format (e.g., 'MM/DD/YYYY') for all users regardless of their locale preference.

title: Migration warning comment contradicts the actual SQL statement
body: The auto-generated warning comment states 'Added the required column `updatedAt` to the `CalendarCache` table without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty.' However, the actual SQL on line 9 includes `DEFAULT NOW()`, which means it IS safe for non-empty tables. The misleading warning could cause unnecessary concern during migration review or cause someone to incorrectly believe the migration will fail on existing data.

title: Authorization check only matches direct userId, missing team/shared credentials
body: The credential lookup uses `userId: user.id` which only matches credentials directly owned by the user. In cal.com, credentials can be team-owned or delegated. A user with legitimate access to a team credential (e.g., through team membership or delegation) would receive 'Credential not found or access denied' when trying to clear its cache. If team credentials should be manageable by team members, the authorization check needs to account for team membership.

title: Authorization check only covers user-owned credentials, not team or delegation credentials
body: The credential lookup uses `userId: user.id` which only matches credentials directly owned by the user. Team credentials (where `userId` may be null or belong to a team member) and delegation credentials cannot have their cache deleted through this endpoint, even by users who have legitimate access. Conversely, if the authorization model should also allow team admins to delete cache for team credentials, this check is insufficient. Consider also checking team membership or using a broader authorization pattern consistent with how other credential operations work in this codebase.

title: No cache invalidation after successful deleteCache mutation
body: After `deleteCacheMutation` succeeds, the component calls `onSuccess?.()` but does not invalidate the `trpc.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` query. The `onChanged` prop passed from `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` is an optional external callback that may not trigger a refetch. As a result, the UI will continue showing the stale `cacheUpdatedAt` timestamp until the user manually refreshes or navigates away and back. The `disconnectMutation` correctly invalidates queries in `onSettled`, but `deleteCacheMutation` does not.

title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds returns expired cache entries
body: The `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` method queries all `CalendarCache` rows matching the given credential IDs without filtering by `expiresAt`. Since cache entries have a TTL (one month per `CACHING_TIME`), expired entries will still be included in the result, causing the UI to display a 'Last updated' timestamp for cache that is no longer being served. This misleads users into thinking active cache exists. The query should include `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` in the `where` clause to only report active cache.

title: Plain Error thrown instead of TRPCError results in misleading INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR
body: The handler throws `new Error('Credential not found or access denied')` when authorization fails. tRPC wraps unrecognized errors as `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` (500), which is misleading for an authorization failure. This should use `TRPCError` with code `FORBIDDEN` or `NOT_FOUND` so the client receives an appropriate status code and can handle the error correctly.

title: Hardcoded 'en-US' locale in Intl.DateTimeFormat ignores user's locale
body: The date formatting for `cache_last_updated` uses `new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', ...)` which always renders dates in US English format regardless of the user's actual locale. The component already has access to the user's locale via `useLocale()`. The locale should be passed to `Intl.DateTimeFormat` to respect the user's language/region settings.

title: sed -i '' syntax is macOS-only and will fail on Linux
body: The `sed -i '' -E` invocation uses the BSD/macOS syntax for in-place editing. On Linux (GNU sed), this will fail because GNU sed interprets `''` as the backup file extension argument differently. Since this is a repository script that developers on different platforms may use, it should either detect the OS or use a portable alternative (e.g., `sed -i.bak` and then remove the backup, or use a temp file).

title: Dark mode subtitle text uses white instead of a muted color
body: The cache status subtitle (the 'Last updated: ...' line) uses `dark:text-white` which makes it the same color as the title text in dark mode, removing visual hierarchy. It should use a muted color like `dark:text-gray-400` to maintain the distinction between the title and the timestamp, consistent with the light mode styling where the title is `text-gray-900` and the subtitle is `text-gray-500`.

title: `immediateDelete` path cancels SendGrid email but never deletes the DB record
body: When `immediateDelete` is true and `referenceId` is not null, the function calls SendGrid to cancel the scheduled email and then returns without deleting the `workflowReminder` row from the database. In the reschedule flow (`handleNewBooking.ts` line 968), the old booking is not deleted—only its status changes to CANCELLED—so these reminder rows are never cascade-deleted. They remain orphaned indefinitely (with `cancelled` still null), accumulating over time. The old code deleted these rows; the new code should either delete the row after the SendGrid call or set `cancelled: true` so the CRON job can clean it up.

title: A single SendGrid failure in the cancellation loop aborts all remaining cancellations and skips DB deletes
body: The `for` loop iterates over `remindersToCancel`, calling SendGrid and collecting Prisma delete promises. If any single `client.request` call throws (e.g., network timeout, rate limit), the `catch` block is entered, `Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` is never reached, and none of the DB records are deleted—even for reminders whose SendGrid cancellation already succeeded. On the next CRON run those already-cancelled reminders will be re-processed, potentially causing duplicate cancellation attempts. Consider wrapping each iteration in its own try-catch or performing the DB deletes for successfully-cancelled reminders before continuing.

title: Async `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are not awaited inside `forEach`
body: The calls to `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are asynchronous but are invoked inside a `forEach` without `await`. The surrounding `try/catch` (line 963) will never catch errors thrown by these promises because `forEach` does not propagate rejections. If the process exits or the request completes before the promises settle, the SendGrid cancellation or DB update may not finish. Use `for...of` with `await` or `Promise.all` with `.map()` to ensure completion and proper error handling.

title: Async reminder cancellation calls are fire-and-forget in cancel booking handler
body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async functions called inside `forEach` without `await`. The handler may return a success response to the client before the `cancelled: true` flag is actually persisted to the database. If the server process is recycled or the request times out, reminders will not be marked as cancelled and the CRON job will not cancel the corresponding SendGrid emails, causing the original bug to persist for those bookings.

title: Workflow deletion does not await async reminder cancellation before cascade delete
body: In the `delete` mutation, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` (with `immediateDelete=true`) and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are called inside `forEach` without `await`. Immediately after, `ctx.prisma.workflow.deleteMany` is awaited, which cascade-deletes the `WorkflowReminder` rows. The SendGrid cancellation requests are still in flight and may fail silently. While the DB records are cleaned up by the cascade, if the SendGrid call fails the scheduled email will still be delivered to the user despite the workflow being deleted.

title: Reminder cancellation for disabled event types is not awaited
body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are called inside a `forEach` without `await` at line 376. The mutation continues and may complete before the `cancelled: true` flag is written. If the request finishes and the connection is released before the DB update commits, reminders will not be marked as cancelled.

title: immediateDelete path does not clean up the database record
body: When `immediateDelete` is true, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` cancels the email in SendGrid but returns without deleting or updating the `workflowReminder` row in the database. The record remains with `scheduled: true` and no `cancelled` flag. In the reschedule flow (`handleNewBooking.ts` line 968), the old booking is not deleted—only marked cancelled—so this orphaned reminder row persists indefinitely until the CRON's `deleteMany` eventually removes it (only after `scheduledDate` passes). If the scheduled date is far in the future, this is a long-lived orphan record. The function should delete the row or set `cancelled: true` after the SendGrid cancel call.

title: Async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder called without await inside forEach
body: The calls to `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async functions invoked inside `forEach` without `await`. This means: (1) the HTTP response is returned before the database updates (setting `cancelled: true` or deleting SMS reminders) complete, so if the process is interrupted the cancellation may be lost; (2) any errors thrown become unhandled promise rejections rather than being caught. The same pattern appears in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx` line 488 and `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx` lines 376, 519, 574. Use `for...of` with `await` or `Promise.all` with `.map()` to ensure the operations complete before proceeding.

title: try-catch around forEach with async callbacks does not catch promise rejections
body: In the reschedule path, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., true)` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)` are async calls inside `forEach`, wrapped in a try-catch. However, `forEach` does not propagate rejected promises to the enclosing try-catch. If the SendGrid or Twilio API call fails, the error becomes an unhandled promise rejection and is never logged by `log.error`. The try-catch gives a false sense of safety. Replace with a `for...of` loop and `await`, or use `Promise.allSettled`.

title: Single try-catch around entire cancellation loop causes partial processing on failure
body: The SendGrid cancellation loop (lines 56-73) is wrapped in one try-catch. If the `client.request` call fails for one reminder (e.g., network timeout), the loop aborts and remaining reminders in `remindersToCancel` are not cancelled. They will be retried on the next CRON run, but if the failure is persistent (e.g., a malformed `referenceId`), all subsequent reminders in the batch are blocked. Move the try-catch inside the loop so each reminder is handled independently.

title: Unscheduled reminders query does not exclude cancelled reminders
body: The query for unscheduled reminders (line 80-98) filters on `scheduled: false` but does not exclude `cancelled: true`. Currently, `cancelled` is only set on reminders that already have a `referenceId` (i.e., `scheduled: true`), so this is safe today. However, if a future code path sets `cancelled: true` on an unscheduled reminder (or if data is manually edited), the CRON would schedule and send an email that should have been cancelled. Adding `cancelled: { not: true }` (or `OR: [{ cancelled: false }, { cancelled: null }]`) to the where clause would make this defensive.

title: Async forEach with await inside callback does not sequence operations
body: At line 574, `remindersToUpdate.forEach(async (reminder) => { ... })` uses an async callback. The `forEach` method ignores the returned promise, so all iterations start concurrently and the outer function does not wait for them to finish. This means the workflow update response is sent before all reminders are cancelled. If a reminder cancellation fails, there is no error propagation. This is the same fire-and-forget pattern as in other files but is particularly notable here because new reminders are created immediately after (line 581+), potentially racing with the cancellations.

title: Async functions called in forEach without await — DB updates may not complete
body: In `handleCancelBooking.ts` lines 485-493, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async functions invoked inside `forEach` without `await`. Since `forEach` does not wait for promises, the handler may return (and in a serverless environment, the process may be killed) before the `prisma.workflowReminder.update` that sets `cancelled: true` completes. If the update doesn't persist, the CRON job will never see the reminder as cancelled, and the email will still be sent — reproducing the exact bug this PR aims to fix.

title: Async functions called in forEach without await in requestReschedule
body: In the `requestReschedule` mutation (lines 488-494), `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async functions called inside `forEach` without `await`. The mutation can return before the database updates (setting `cancelled: true`) complete. In a serverless environment the execution context may be recycled before these fire-and-forget promises resolve, leaving reminders uncancelled and causing emails to still be sent for rescheduled bookings.

title: Async reminder cancellation in forEach is fire-and-forget during reschedule
body: In `handleNewBooking.ts` lines 966-972, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are called inside `forEach` without `await`. Although wrapped in try/catch, the catch will never trigger because unhandled promise rejections from forEach callbacks don't propagate to the enclosing try/catch. More critically, the reschedule flow continues and returns a response before these DB updates complete, risking that `cancelled: true` is never persisted and the old reminders are still sent.

title: Single SendGrid failure aborts cancellation of all remaining reminders in batch
body: The try/catch on line 53 wraps the entire for-loop that iterates over `remindersToCancel`. If `client.request` throws for any single reminder (e.g., network timeout, rate limit), the loop breaks and no subsequent reminders are cancelled. Their DB records are also not deleted. Since the CRON only targets reminders with `scheduledDate <= now + 1 hour`, if the failure persists across CRON runs and the scheduled time passes, those emails will be sent despite being cancelled. Each reminder's SendGrid call should be individually try/caught to isolate failures.

title: immediateDelete cancels in SendGrid but leaves orphaned DB record
body: When `immediateDelete` is true (lines 213-223), the function cancels the scheduled send in SendGrid and returns without deleting or marking the `workflowReminder` record in the database. Callers (reschedule in `handleNewBooking.ts`, workflow/step deletion in `workflows.tsx`) also do not delete the record. These orphaned records with `scheduled: true` and a stale `referenceId` will persist until the CRON's first `deleteMany` removes them after their `scheduledDate` passes, causing unbounded table growth for bookings far in the future.

title: Unscheduled reminders query does not exclude cancelled reminders
body: The query for unscheduled reminders (line 80-98) filters on `scheduled: false` but does not exclude `cancelled: true`. While in the current flow `cancelled` is only set on already-scheduled reminders (so `scheduled` would be true), there is no database constraint preventing a reminder from being both `cancelled: true` and `scheduled: false`. Adding `cancelled: { not: true }` (or `OR: [{ cancelled: false }, { cancelled: null }]`) would be a defensive safeguard against scheduling a cancelled reminder.

title: Async reminder cancellation in forEach without await when editing workflow steps
body: In the `update` mutation, `remindersToUpdate.forEach(async (reminder) => {...})` on line 574 calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` without awaiting the forEach itself. The mutation proceeds to create new reminders and returns a response before the old ones are marked as cancelled. If the execution context is recycled (serverless), the old reminders may never be marked cancelled and could still be sent by the CRON job.

title: forEach with async callback causes recurring event calendar deletions to be silently skipped
body: The `forEach(async (credential) => {...})` on line 460 does not await the async callbacks. Since `getCalendar` is now async, the callbacks haven't finished by the time execution reaches `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` on line 652. At that point `apiDeletes` is still empty (or incomplete), so calendar events for recurring bookings are never actually deleted. This should use a `for...of` loop or `Promise.all` with `.map()` to ensure the deletions are collected and awaited.

title: forEach with async callback makes try/catch ineffective
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` on line 125 is wrapped in a try/catch (lines 124-139), but `forEach` does not await the async callbacks. Any error thrown inside the callback (e.g., from `await getCalendar(...)` or `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)`) will result in an unhandled promise rejection rather than being caught by the surrounding try/catch. Use `Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => {...}))` instead.

title: forEach with async callback makes try/catch ineffective
body: Same issue as vital/lib/reschedule.ts: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` on line 125 is inside a try/catch that will never catch errors from the async callbacks. Errors from `await getCalendar(...)` or `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` become unhandled promise rejections.

title: forEach with async callback makes calendar/video deletions fire-and-forget
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` on line 553 fires off async calendar and video deletion operations without awaiting them. The function proceeds to send the reschedule email (line 570) before the deletions complete. If a deletion fails, the error is silently lost. This should use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` to ensure deletions complete (or at least errors are handled) before continuing.

title: getCalendarCredentials returns Promise in calendar field without being async, breaking the return type contract
body: `getCalendarCredentials` is a synchronous function that now returns objects where the `calendar` field is `Promise<Calendar | null>` (because `getCalendar` is now async). While `getConnectedCalendars` correctly awaits `item.calendar`, any other consumer of `getCalendarCredentials` that previously accessed `item.calendar` as a resolved `Calendar | null` will now receive a Promise object. This is a subtle breaking change in the function's return type that could cause runtime errors in callers not updated in this PR.

title: All dynamic imports are initiated eagerly at module load time, negating lazy-loading benefits
body: Every `import("./...")` call in the appStore object literal is executed immediately when the module is evaluated. This means all app modules are fetched in parallel at startup rather than on demand. If the goal is to reduce initial bundle size or startup time, the imports should be deferred (e.g., by wrapping them in functions or using a getter pattern) so they are only loaded when actually accessed.

title: forEach with async callback discards promises; try/catch is ineffective
body: Using `forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` does not await the async callbacks. The returned promises are discarded, so: (1) the surrounding try/catch on line 124 will never catch errors thrown inside the callback, and (2) the function may return `true` (line 151) before calendar/video deletions have actually completed. This should be replaced with `for...of` or `Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` to properly await and catch errors.

title: forEach with async callback discards promises; try/catch is ineffective
body: Same issue as in vital/lib/reschedule.ts: `forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` fires async callbacks without awaiting them. The try/catch on line 124 cannot catch rejections from the async callbacks, and the function proceeds to send emails before deletions complete.

title: forEach with async callback causes race condition between deletion and email
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` starts async calendar/video deletion operations but does not await them. The code immediately proceeds to `sendRequestRescheduleEmail` on line 570 without waiting for the deletions to finish. This means the reschedule email can be sent while calendar events are still being deleted, and any errors from deletion are silently lost as unhandled promise rejections.

title: forEach with async callback means apiDeletes may be empty when Promise.all is called
body: On lines 458-470, `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => {...})` pushes results into `apiDeletes` inside async callbacks that are not awaited. By the time `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` is reached on line 652, the forEach callbacks may not have executed yet, so `apiDeletes` could be empty or incomplete. Calendar events for recurring bookings may never actually be deleted. Replace with a `for...of` loop or collect promises with `map`.

title: getCalendarCredentials implicitly returns Promise in calendar field without being async
body: `getCalendarCredentials` is a synchronous function that calls `getCalendar(credential)` which now returns `Promise<Calendar | null>`. The returned array elements have `calendar: Promise<Calendar | null>` instead of `calendar: Calendar | null`. While `getConnectedCalendars` correctly awaits `item.calendar`, any other consumer of `getCalendarCredentials` that expects a resolved Calendar will receive a Promise. The function's return type has silently changed, which is a contract break for external callers.

title: Sequential awaits in getVideoAdapters loop instead of parallel
body: The `for...of` loop with `await appStore[appName]` on line 26 processes each credential sequentially. Since each dynamic import is independent, using `Promise.all(withCredentials.map(...))` would resolve them in parallel, reducing latency when multiple video credentials are present.

title: forEach with async callback: promises are fire-and-forget, try/catch is ineffective
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` does not await the async callbacks. The surrounding `try/catch` on line 124 will never catch errors thrown inside the async callback because `forEach` returns `undefined`, not a Promise. Additionally, the function may return `true` (line 151) and send the reschedule email before calendar/video events are actually deleted. Use `Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => {...}))` instead.

title: forEach with async callback: promises are fire-and-forget, try/catch is ineffective
body: Same issue as vital/lib/reschedule.ts: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` does not await the async callbacks. The surrounding try/catch will never catch rejections from `getCalendar` or `deleteMeeting`, and the function proceeds to send emails before deletions complete. Use `Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` instead.

title: forEach with async callback: calendar/video deletions are not awaited
body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` fires async callbacks without awaiting them. The `getCalendar` and `deleteMeeting` calls inside will produce unhandled promise rejections on failure, and the mutation handler will return before the calendar/video events are actually deleted. This can leave stale events on users' calendars after a reschedule. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` instead.

title: forEach with async callback: apiDeletes array may be empty when consumed
body: Inside the recurring-event branch, `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => {...})` pushes results into `apiDeletes` from async callbacks that are never awaited. By the time `apiDeletes` is consumed at line 617 (`await apiDeletes`) or line 652 (`await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))`), the array may still be empty because the forEach callbacks haven't finished. This means calendar events for recurring bookings may never be deleted. Replace with a `for...of` loop or `Promise.all(...map(...))` and collect the promises properly.

title: Sequential await in loop where parallel loading is possible
body: `getVideoAdapters` now uses a `for...of` loop with `await appStore[appName]` inside, loading each video app module sequentially. Previously all app lookups were synchronous. Since each `import()` is independent, they could be loaded in parallel with `Promise.all(withCredentials.map(...))` to avoid unnecessary sequential latency, especially when multiple video credentials are present.

title: getCalendarCredentials returns objects with unresolved Promise in calendar field
body: `getCalendar` is now async but `getCalendarCredentials` is synchronous and stores the returned Promise directly in the `calendar` property without awaiting it. While `getConnectedCalendars` correctly does `await item.calendar`, any other consumer of `getCalendarCredentials` that accesses `.calendar` expecting a `Calendar | null` will get a Promise instead. The return type of `getCalendarCredentials` should be updated to reflect that `calendar` is `Promise<Calendar | null>`, or the function should be made async.

title: Dayjs objects compared with === always returns false
body: The expression `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` uses strict equality (`===`) to compare two Dayjs instances. Since these are distinct object references, this comparison always evaluates to `false`, regardless of whether the two moments represent the same point in time. The intended check (whether start equals end, indicating an "unavailable" date override) will never trigger. Use `.isSame()` instead.

title: Copy-paste error: `end` computed from slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
body: In the working hours check, `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()` uses `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`. This means the end of the slot is never actually checked against working hour boundaries—only the start time is checked twice. A slot that starts within working hours but extends past the end of the working window would incorrectly pass this check.

title: Working hours check logic is inverted: marks slot unavailable if outside ANY single working hour entry
body: The code uses `workingHours.find(...)` to return `true` if the slot is outside a particular working hour entry, then treats a match as "slot is outside working hours → return false (unavailable)." When a user has multiple working hour entries for the same day (e.g., 9–12 and 14–18), a slot at 10:00 is outside the 14–18 entry, so `find` returns that entry and the slot is incorrectly marked unavailable. The correct logic should check that the slot is not inside ANY working hour entry (i.e., use `!workingHours.some(...)` with an "is inside" predicate).

title: Potential runtime error when override.timeZone is undefined
body: `override.timeZone` is typed as optional (`timeZone?: string` in `TimeRange`). If a `DateOverride` object does not have `timeZone` set (which is possible since the field was just added and is optional), `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(undefined)` will be called. Depending on the dayjs timezone plugin version, this may throw an exception or produce an incorrect offset, causing slot generation to fail silently or crash.

title: dateOverrides.find() uses side-effect mutation of dateOverrideExist but find short-circuits unpredictably
body: The variable `dateOverrideExist` is set to `true` inside the `find` callback as a side effect. However, `find` stops iterating as soon as the callback returns a truthy value. If the first date override matches the day but the slot IS within it (callback returns undefined/falsy), `dateOverrideExist` is set to true and iteration continues. But if a second override for a different day is encountered, the day check fails and `dateOverrideExist` remains true from the first override. If no override returns `true` from `find`, the code falls through to `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;`—which is correct. However, if the first override matches the day and the slot is within it, but a later override for the SAME day has the slot outside it, `find` returns that later override and the function returns `false`. This is correct for a single user, but the interplay between the side-effect flag and `find`'s short-circuit behavior makes the logic fragile and hard to reason about, and could produce wrong results if overrides are not sorted by relevance.

title: Dayjs objects compared with === instead of .isSame()
body: The expression `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two distinct Dayjs object references with strict equality. This will always evaluate to `false`, meaning the check for a zero-length date override (which typically represents a day-off/unavailable day) will never trigger. Should use `.isSame()` instead.

title: Working hours end-time check uses slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
body: The variable `end` is computed as `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`, which is identical to `start`. It should use `slotEndTime` to verify the entire slot (start + eventLength) fits within working hours. As written, a slot that starts within working hours but extends past the end of the working window will be incorrectly considered available.

title: Working hours availability check logic is inverted for multiple time blocks
body: The `workingHours.find(...)` returns the first working-hour block where the slot does NOT fit, and then marks the slot as unavailable. If a user has multiple working-hour blocks on the same day (e.g., 9–12 and 14–17), a slot at 14:00 will fail the check against the 9–12 block and be incorrectly rejected, even though it fits within 14–17. The logic should only reject the slot if it doesn't fit within ANY working-hour block for that day.

title: Multiple date overrides on the same day can incorrectly reject available slots
body: The `dateOverrides.find(...)` callback returns `true` (marking the slot as outside the override) for the first override on the matching day where the slot doesn't fit. If there are multiple overrides on the same day and the slot falls within one of them but not another, `find` may return the non-matching override and the slot is rejected. The logic should check whether the slot is within ANY override on that day before rejecting it.

title: override.timeZone may be undefined, causing dayjs.tz() to behave unpredictably
body: The `TimeRange` type defines `timeZone` as optional (`timeZone?: string`). If a date override lacks a `timeZone` value, `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(undefined)` will not produce a meaningful offset, potentially causing incorrect slot calculations or runtime errors. A fallback (e.g., to `organizerTimeZone`) should be provided.

title: Using .toString() on Date before passing to dayjs is fragile
body: `dayjs(override.start.toString())` converts the Date to a locale-dependent string representation (e.g., 'Thu Jan 01 1970 14:00:00 GMT+0000') and then re-parses it. This is unnecessary since `dayjs(override.start)` accepts Date objects directly, and the string format may not parse reliably across environments or locales.

title: No test for round-robin fixed host date override scenario
body: The PR description states it fixes date overrides of fixed hosts being taken into account for round-robin events, but no test is added that verifies this behavior (e.g., a round-robin event with a fixed host who has a date override, ensuring only the fixed host's override slots are shown). Only the timezone adjustment for personal events is tested.

title: Dayjs objects compared with === instead of .isSame(), always evaluates to false
body: The expression `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` uses strict equality (`===`) to compare two Dayjs object instances. This always returns `false` because `===` compares object references, not date values. The intent is to detect "unavailable all day" date overrides (where start equals end). Because this check never passes, such overrides will not correctly block all slots on that day. Use `.isSame()` instead.

title: Copy-paste error: `end` uses slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
body: The variable `end` is computed as `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`, which is identical to `start` on the line above. It should use `slotEndTime` to correctly check whether the slot's end time exceeds the working hours boundary. As written, a slot whose end time extends past the working hours end time will not be detected as out-of-bounds, potentially showing unavailable slots as bookable.

title: Working hours check incorrectly rejects slots when multiple ranges exist for the same day
body: The `workingHours.find(...)` logic returns `false` (unavailable) if the slot is outside ANY single working hour range for that day. If a user has multiple working hour ranges (e.g., 9–12 and 14–17), a slot at 10:00 is within the first range but outside the second. The `find` will match the second range and incorrectly mark the slot as unavailable. The correct logic should return `false` only if the slot is not within ANY working hour range for that day (i.e., use `!workingHours.some(...)` or equivalent).

title: override.timeZone may be undefined, causing incorrect offset calculation
body: The `TimeRange` type defines `timeZone` as optional (`timeZone?: string`). In `slots.ts`, the code calls `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()` without guarding against `override.timeZone` being `undefined`. When `undefined` is passed to `.tz()`, dayjs may fall back to the system's local timezone or behave unpredictably, producing an incorrect UTC offset and thus wrong slot times. A fallback (e.g., to `organizerTimeZone`) should be provided.

title: No test for the primary fix: round-robin with fixed hosts and date overrides
body: The PR description states the main fix is that date overrides of fixed hosts are now taken into account for round-robin events, preventing bookings where fixed hosts are unavailable. However, no test is added that creates a round-robin event with a fixed host, sets a date override on that fixed host, and verifies that only slots within the override are shown. The only added test checks timezone adjustment for a personal event, not the round-robin + fixed host scenario.

title: SQL injection in migration via string interpolation of host values
body: The migration interpolates the value of `h` (from the old `embeddable_hosts` site setting) directly into a raw SQL INSERT statement without any escaping or parameterization. If the stored setting value contains single quotes or other SQL metacharacters, this allows SQL injection. Use `execute sanitize_sql_array(...)` or a parameterized query instead.

title: record_for_host returns false instead of nil on failure paths
body: `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` returns the boolean `false` (lines 12 and 15) when the URI is invalid or the host is blank, rather than `nil`. While current callers use `.present?` or `.try(:category_id)` which happen to work with `false`, this is semantically wrong for a finder method. Any future caller that does `record_for_host(url).category_id` without `.try` will get a `NoMethodError` on `false`. Return `nil` instead.

title: destroy action does not handle missing record, causing NoMethodError
body: In the `destroy` action, `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns `nil` if no record matches. Calling `host.destroy` on `nil` raises `NoMethodError`, resulting in a 500 error. The same issue exists in `update` (line 10) where `save_host(host)` will fail on a nil host. Add a nil check or use `find` with a rescue to return a 404.
