title: before_validation callback crashes when host is nil
body: The `before_validation` block calls `self.host.sub!(...)` without checking if `self.host` is nil. When creating a new `EmbeddableHost` without assigning `host` first (e.g., `EmbeddableHost.new` followed by validation), this raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil:NilClass`. Add a guard like `self.host&.sub!(...)` or check for presence.

title: No uniqueness validation on host column
body: The `EmbeddableHost` model has no uniqueness validation on the `host` attribute, and the migration does not add a unique index. This allows duplicate host entries to be created, which could cause ambiguous lookups in `record_for_host` (it uses `.first` so it picks an arbitrary one) and confusing admin UI behavior.

title: create_table uses force: true which drops existing table
body: `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` will silently drop the `embeddable_hosts` table if it already exists, destroying any data. This is unusual for a migration and dangerous if the migration is re-run or if the table was created by another means. Use `create_table` without `force: true` and handle the existing-table case explicitly if needed.

title: update action is a no-op that doesn't persist any changes
body: The `update` action in `Admin::EmbeddingController` simply re-serializes the current embedding without applying any changes from the request. The frontend calls `this.get('embedding').update({})` which hits this endpoint. While individual host saves go through `EmbeddableHostsController`, this endpoint gives the false impression that it does something. If it's intentionally a no-op placeholder, it should be documented or removed.

title: record_for_host returns false instead of nil, creating inconsistent return types
body: The method `record_for_host` returns `false` (a boolean) when the URI is invalid or the host is blank, but returns an ActiveRecord object or `nil` from the query otherwise. This inconsistent return type is error-prone. In `topic_embed.rb` it's used as `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` followed by `eh.try(:category_id)`. While `try` happens to handle `false` gracefully (returning nil since FalseClass doesn't respond to `category_id`), any future caller using a simple nil-check (`if record_for_host(url)`) would get unexpected truthy behavior from `false`. The method should return `nil` instead of `false` for consistency.

title: No nil check on record lookup in update and destroy actions
body: In both `update` (line 10) and `destroy` (line 15), `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can return `nil` if the record doesn't exist. In `update`, `save_host(nil)` will raise `NoMethodError` when calling `host.host = ...`. In `destroy`, `host.destroy` will similarly raise. This results in a 500 error instead of a proper 404 response. The controller should either use `find` (which raises RecordNotFound and is handled by Rails) or add an explicit nil check.

title: SQL injection via string interpolation of user-controlled data in migration
body: The migration interpolates the variable `h` (which comes from the `embeddable_hosts` site setting, a value that admins can set to arbitrary strings) directly into a SQL string: `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. If the stored value contains a single quote or other SQL metacharacters, this will either break the migration or allow SQL injection. Use parameterized queries or at minimum `quote(h)` / `connection.quote(h)` to escape the value.

title: Migration will crash if embed_category site setting doesn't exist
body: The query on lines 9-11 joins `categories` with `site_settings` where `s.name = 'embed_category'`. If the `embed_category` site setting was never configured (which is the default empty-string case), the INNER JOIN returns zero rows. Accessing `[0]['id']` on an empty result set raises `NoMethodError: undefined method '[]' for nil:NilClass`, causing the migration to fail. The code should handle the case where the query returns no rows.

title: Fabricator file contents are swapped with their filenames
body: The file `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now contains only the `embeddable_host` fabricator, while `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the category fabricators. The file contents are inverted relative to their names. While Fabrication loads all files in the directory regardless of name, this is confusing for maintainers and could cause issues if any tooling or convention relies on filename-to-content correspondence.

title: before_validation callback will raise NoMethodError if host is nil
body: The `before_validation` callback calls `self.host.sub!(...)` which will raise `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil:NilClass` if `self.host` is nil. This can happen if a new `EmbeddableHost` is validated before the host attribute is assigned, or if the host parameter is missing/nil in the controller. The callback should guard against nil, e.g., `self.host&.sub!(...)` or check for presence first.

title: SQL injection via string interpolation in migration
body: The host value `h` from the `embeddable_hosts` site setting is interpolated directly into the SQL INSERT statement without any sanitization or parameterization: `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. If a site admin had previously entered a malicious value into the `embeddable_hosts` setting (e.g., containing a single quote), this migration would execute arbitrary SQL. Use a parameterized query or at minimum `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h)`.

title: Migration crashes when embed_category setting doesn't match any category
body: The query `SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'` will return zero rows when the `embed_category` site setting is empty (its default) or doesn't match any category name. In that case, `execute(...)[0]` returns `nil`, and calling `['id']` on `nil` raises `NoMethodError`, crashing the migration. This will affect most sites since the default value of `embed_category` was an empty string. The nil check on line 14 (`if category_id == 0`) is never reached.

title: record_for_host returns false instead of nil, inconsistent return type
body: `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` returns `false` on lines 12 and 15 when the URI is invalid or the host is blank, but returns an `EmbeddableHost` record or `nil` from the `where(...).first` call on line 17. Callers like `TopicEmbed.import` use `eh.try(:category_id)` which works with `false` (returns nil), but the method contract is broken: any caller that checks `result.nil?` or tries to use the return value as a record will behave incorrectly. The method should return `nil` consistently instead of `false`.

title: before_validation callback crashes when host is nil
body: The `before_validation` callback calls `self.host.sub!(...)` which raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil:NilClass` if `self.host` is nil. This can happen when `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#create` is called with a missing or nil `params[:embeddable_host][:host]`, since `save_host` assigns the param value to `host.host` before calling `save`, which triggers the callback. A guard like `self.host&.sub!` or a presence check is needed.

title: destroy action raises NoMethodError when host not found
body: In the `destroy` action, `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns `nil` if no record matches. Calling `host.destroy` on `nil` raises `NoMethodError`. The same issue exists in the `update` action (line 10-11) where `save_host(nil)` would crash when trying to assign attributes. Both actions should handle the not-found case, e.g., by using `find` (which raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` and returns a 404) or by explicitly checking for nil.

title: Fabricator file contents are swapped with their filenames
body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now contains only the `embeddable_host` fabricator, while `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the category fabricators. The file contents are swapped relative to their names. While Fabrication loads all files in the fabricators directory so tests may still pass, this is confusing for maintenance and could cause issues if fabricators are loaded selectively or if developers look for a fabricator by filename.

title: _focusOnInput runs when editing becomes false, targeting a non-existent element
body: The `_focusOnInput` method is triggered by `@observes('editing')` which fires whenever the `editing` property changes, including when it changes to `false` (e.g., after saving or cancelling). When `editing` is false, the `.host-name` input is not rendered, so `this.$('.host-name')` returns an empty jQuery object. While jQuery's `.focus()` on an empty set is a no-op, the intent is clearly to only focus when entering edit mode. Adding a guard like `if (this.get('editing'))` would make the behavior explicit and avoid unnecessary DOM queries.

title: Duplicate `downsize` method definition silently overrides the 4-argument version
body: Two `self.downsize` methods are defined: one at line 145 accepting `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and another at line 149 accepting `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. In Ruby the second definition completely replaces the first. Any existing callers that pass width and height as separate numeric arguments (e.g., `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 200)`) will now have `200` interpreted as the `opts` hash, causing silent misbehavior or errors. The first method is dead code.

title: Tempfile position not reset after external process rewrites the file
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` invokes a shell command (`convert`) that truncates and rewrites the file at `tempfile.path`. The Ruby `Tempfile` object's file descriptor position is not updated by this external write and may remain at or beyond the old EOF. When `Upload.create_for` subsequently reads from `tempfile`, it may read zero bytes or partial/corrupt data. A `tempfile.rewind` (or `tempfile.seek(0)`) is needed after the downsize loop before passing the tempfile to `Upload.create_for`.

title: Client-side upload size limit hardcoded to 10 MB, ignoring admin-configured site settings
body: The previous code read the limit from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, respecting the administrator's configuration. It is now hardcoded to `10 * 1024` KB. This means users can upload files up to 10 MB regardless of the configured `max_image_size_kb` or `max_attachment_size_kb`. For attachments (non-images), there is no server-side downsize logic, so oversized attachments will be accepted. The error message shown to users will also incorrectly state 10 MB as the limit.

title: Downsize loop does not check return value; may loop uselessly on failure
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns `false` when the underlying `convert` command fails (e.g., corrupt or unsupported image). The while-loop ignores this return value, so if downsize fails on the first attempt it will retry 4 more times with no effect, wasting time and potentially holding the request open. The loop should break early when `downsize` returns `false`.

title: Image still uploaded even if it exceeds max_image_size_kb after all downsize attempts
body: After up to 5 downsize iterations, there is no final check that `tempfile.size <= SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`. If the image is still too large (e.g., a very large PNG that doesn't shrink much with dimension reduction), it is uploaded and stored without any error returned to the user, defeating the purpose of the size limit.

title: API URL download limit raised to 10 MB without corresponding server-side guard for non-images
body: The download limit for API-provided URLs was changed from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes`. For non-image uploads via the API (attachments), there is no downsize logic and no subsequent size check, so an API caller can store attachments up to 10 MB regardless of the configured `max_attachment_size_kb`.

title: Duplicate method definition silently overrides the first `downsize`
body: Two `self.downsize` methods are defined (lines 145 and 149). In Ruby the second definition completely replaces the first, so the 4-argument version `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` is dead code. Any existing callers in the codebase that invoke `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, width, height)` will now have `width` interpreted as the `dimensions` string and `height` interpreted as `opts`, producing incorrect behavior or errors.

title: Using the same file path as both input and output for ImageMagick `convert`
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` passes the same path as source and destination. ImageMagick's `convert` command opens the output file for writing (truncating it) before it finishes reading the input, which can produce an empty or corrupted file. A safe approach is to write to a temporary file and then replace the original.

title: Upload proceeds even if downsize loop fails to reduce size below the limit
body: After the while-loop (lines 66-69), execution unconditionally falls through to `Upload.create_for` on line 72. If after 5 iterations the image is still larger than `max_image_size_kb`, the oversized image is stored anyway, defeating the purpose of the feature. There should be a check after the loop to reject or further handle images that could not be reduced to the allowed size.

title: Client-side max size is hardcoded, ignoring the admin-configured site setting
body: The client-side validation now always allows uploads up to 10 MB regardless of the `max_image_size_kb` or `max_attachment_size_kb` site settings. If an admin configures a smaller limit, users will not see a client-side error until the server responds, and the error message shown (line 184) will incorrectly state the limit is 10 MB. The original code correctly read from `Discourse.SiteSettings`.

title: Tempfile read position may be stale after in-place modification by shell command
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` writes to `tempfile.path` via a shell command, bypassing the Ruby Tempfile IO object. If the Tempfile's internal file descriptor has been read from or seeked (e.g., by a prior `.size` call on some Ruby versions or by `Upload.create_for` expecting position 0), subsequent reads from the Tempfile may return empty or partial data. Calling `tempfile.rewind` after the downsize loop would make this safe.

title: Download limit for API URL uploads is hardcoded to 10 MB regardless of site setting
body: The original code used `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` as the download cap, preventing excessively large downloads. Now any URL up to 10 MB will be downloaded even if the admin has set a much lower limit, increasing bandwidth and memory usage on the server for sites with restrictive settings.

title: Duplicate method definition silently replaces the previous `downsize` signature
body: Ruby does not support method overloading. The second definition of `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` on line 149 completely replaces the first definition `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` on line 145. Any existing callers using the old 4-argument form (e.g., `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, out, 100, 200)`) will now have `max_width` interpreted as `dimensions` and `max_height` interpreted as `opts`, producing incorrect behavior or errors. The old method should either be removed entirely (if no callers remain) or kept under a different name.

title: `tempfile.size` will not reflect changes made by the external `convert` process
body: The while loop checks `tempfile.size` to decide whether to keep downsizing. However, `Tempfile#size` returns the size via `fstat` on the file descriptor that was opened when the Tempfile was created. `OptimizedImage.downsize` invokes ImageMagick's `convert` as a subprocess writing to the same path. ImageMagick typically writes to a temporary file and renames it over the target, which means the tempfile's file descriptor still points to the old (now unlinked) inode. As a result, `tempfile.size` will never decrease, the loop will always run all 5 iterations without effect, and the feature will not actually downsize the upload. Use `File.size(tempfile.path)` after each iteration, or re-stat the path, to get the actual on-disk size.

title: No check on `OptimizedImage.downsize` return value before continuing the loop
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns `false` when the image processing fails (e.g., ImageMagick error, unsupported format). The loop does not check this return value, so if downsizing fails on the first attempt, it will silently retry 4 more times, wasting time and resources before proceeding to upload the unmodified file. The loop should break if `downsize` returns false.

title: Client-side max file size is hardcoded to 10 MB, ignoring the admin-configurable site setting
body: The original code read `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, allowing administrators to configure per-type upload limits. Replacing this with a hardcoded `10 * 1024` means the client will permit uploads up to 10 MB regardless of the server's configured limit. Users will be able to select files that the server will reject, producing a confusing experience, and the error message will incorrectly state the limit is 10 MB even when the server enforces a different value.

title: API URL download limit hardcoded to 10 MB, bypassing `max_image_size_kb` setting
body: The original code used `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` as the download size limit for URL-based uploads via the API. This is now hardcoded to `10.megabytes`. If an admin has configured a smaller `max_image_size_kb`, the server will still download up to 10 MB from the remote URL before the downsize loop attempts to reduce it. This wastes bandwidth and memory, and if the downsize loop fails (as noted above), oversized files could be stored.

title: NoMethodError when TopicUser record does not exist
body: TopicUser.find_by on line 105 can return nil if the user has never visited the topic (no TopicUser row exists). Line 107 then calls tu.notification_level on nil, raising NoMethodError. This will happen when a user clicks the unsubscribe link in an email for a topic they were notified about but never actually opened in the browser. A nil check or use of TopicUser.change (which handles upsert) is needed.

title: State-changing action exposed via GET request enables CSRF
body: The unsubscribe route is defined as a GET request (get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe") but the controller action mutates the notification_level. Rails CSRF protection does not apply to GET requests. An attacker can embed or a link in any page/email to silently change a user's notification level. Browsers, link previewers, and crawlers may also trigger this unintentionally. This should be a POST/PUT route with CSRF token verification.

title: unsubscribe_link locale now requires unsubscribe_url, breaking other callers
body: The unsubscribe_link locale string now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}. Any code path that calls build_email with add_unsubscribe_link: true but does not pass unsubscribe_url in opts will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument at runtime. While the current notification email path provides it, plugins or future code using add_unsubscribe_link without unsubscribe_url will break. A default or conditional interpolation should be considered.

title: Typo in property name: stopNotificiationsText
body: The property is named stopNotificiationsText (with an extra 'i' — 'Notificiations' instead of 'Notifications'). While it is used consistently in the template so it won't cause a runtime error, it introduces a confusing misspelling that will trip up future developers searching for 'notification' in the codebase.

title: No controller spec for the unsubscribe action
body: The unsubscribe action introduces new behavior (mutating notification level, redirecting on slug mismatch, rendering the topic view) but has no corresponding controller spec. The nil TopicUser bug and the GET-based state mutation would both be caught by basic request specs. At minimum, tests should cover: successful unsubscribe when TopicUser exists, behavior when TopicUser is missing, and slug mismatch redirect.

title: Triple-mustache renders unescaped HTML including user-controlled topic title
body: The template uses {{{stopNotificiationsText}}} (triple mustache, no escaping). The value includes model.fancyTitle which is HTML-escaped server-side via ERB::Util.html_escape, so it is currently safe. However, this creates a fragile dependency: if fancyTitle is ever changed to not escape, or if a different title property is substituted, this becomes an XSS vector. A safer pattern would be to use a component or helper that explicitly marks only the <strong> wrapper as safe.

title: NoMethodError when TopicUser record does not exist
body: TopicUser.find_by returns nil when the user has never visited the topic (no TopicUser row exists). The very next line (107) calls tu.notification_level on this potentially-nil value, which will raise NoMethodError. This will happen for any user who clicks an unsubscribe link for a topic they received a notification about but never actually opened.

title: State-changing action on GET request is vulnerable to CSRF
body: The unsubscribe action modifies the user's notification level (a state change) but is routed as a GET request (config/routes.rb line 440-441). GET requests are not protected by Rails' CSRF token mechanism. An attacker can trick a logged-in user into changing their notification level by embedding the unsubscribe URL in an tag, a link preview, or any other mechanism that causes the browser to issue a GET request. This should be a POST/PUT action.

title: Missing authorization check for topic visibility
body: The unsubscribe action creates a TopicView and proceeds without calling guardian.ensure_can_see! on the topic. Unlike the show action which rescues Discourse::InvalidAccess, this action does not verify the user has permission to see the topic. For private messages or secure-category topics, this could allow a user to interact with (and confirm the existence of) a topic they should not have access to.

title: unsubscribe_link locale now requires unsubscribe_url interpolation which may not always be provided
body: The unsubscribe_link locale string now contains %{unsubscribe_url}. This string is rendered in Email::MessageBuilder#body (line 90) whenever add_unsubscribe_link is true. If any current or future caller sets add_unsubscribe_link: true without also providing unsubscribe_url in the opts, I18n will raise MissingInterpolationArgument and the email will fail to send. Currently only send_notification_email provides both, but this creates a fragile coupling.

title: Typo in computed property name: stopNotificiationsText
body: The property is named stopNotificiationsText (with 'ii' instead of 'io' in Notifications). While the template references the same misspelled name so it works, this makes the code harder to maintain and search for, and could cause confusion if someone tries to reference it by the correct spelling.

title: Triple-mustache renders unescaped HTML including user-controlled topic title
body: The template uses {{{stopNotificiationsText}}} which renders raw HTML without escaping. The value includes model.fancyTitle interpolated into the locale string. While Discourse's fancyTitle applies some server-side sanitization, using triple-mustache with user-generated content (topic titles) is risky. If fancyTitle ever contains unescaped user input (e.g., via a bug or a plugin), this becomes an XSS vector. Consider using a component or helper that explicitly escapes the title before inserting it into the HTML string.

title: NoMethodError when TopicUser record does not exist
body: In the `unsubscribe` action, `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` on line 105 can return `nil` if the user has never interacted with the topic (no TopicUser row exists). Line 107 then calls `tu.notification_level` on nil, raising a NoMethodError and returning a 500 to the user. This is easily triggered by a user clicking the unsubscribe link in an email for a topic they were invited to but never visited.

title: GET request performs state-changing unsubscribe operation
body: The unsubscribe route is defined as a GET request (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`), but the controller action modifies the database (changes notification_level and saves). GET requests should be idempotent and safe. Email clients, link prefetchers, crawlers, and browser preview features may issue GET requests to this URL, inadvertently unsubscribing users. This should be a POST or PUT request with proper CSRF protection.

title: Unescaped HTML rendering of topic title via triple-stache
body: The template uses `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` (triple-stache, no escaping). The underlying locale string is `"You will stop receiving notifications for {{title}}."` where `title` is `model.fancyTitle`. While `fancyTitle` on the server applies HTML escaping before SmartyPants, the client-side `fancyTitle` property may not guarantee the same escaping in all code paths. If any path provides an unescaped title, this becomes a stored XSS vector. The safe approach is to use a computed property that explicitly escapes the title and only allows the known `` tag, or use double-stache with a SafeString for the known markup.

title: unsubscribe_link locale now requires unsubscribe_url but not all callers provide it
body: The `unsubscribe_link` locale string was changed to include `%{unsubscribe_url}`. This string is rendered via `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` in `Email::MessageBuilder#body` and `#html_part` whenever `add_unsubscribe_link` is true. If any caller (current or future, including plugins) sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without providing `unsubscribe_url` in the options, I18n will raise `MissingInterpolationArgument`. The locale should handle the missing key gracefully, or the message builder should conditionally include the per-topic line only when `unsubscribe_url` is present.

title: Unsubscribe action does not verify user can see the topic
body: The `unsubscribe` action creates a `TopicView` and proceeds to modify the notification level without calling `guardian.ensure_can_see!(@topic_view.topic)`. While the practical impact is limited (the user only changes their own notification level), it leaks information: a user can confirm a topic ID exists and observe its title/slug in the rendered response even if they lack permission to view it.

title: Typo in property name: stopNotificiationsText
body: The computed property is named `stopNotificiationsText` (with 'Notificiations' misspelled — extra 'i' and missing 'o'). While this is consistently used in the template so it won't cause a runtime error, it makes the code harder to search for and maintain, and could cause confusion if other code tries to reference the correctly-spelled name.

title: Test does not verify unsubscribe_url appears in the email body
body: The test adds `unsubscribe_url` to the builder options but only asserts that `user_preferences_url` appears in the body and that the `List-Unsubscribe` header is present. There is no assertion that the per-topic unsubscribe URL actually appears in the rendered body or HTML part, which is the core feature being added. A test verifying that `unsubscribe_url` is interpolated into the body would catch regressions if the locale string or message builder changes.

title: Email lookup is case-sensitive, allowing blocked emails to bypass the block
body: `should_block?` performs a case-sensitive lookup with `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first`. Email addresses are case-insensitive per RFC 5321. If an admin blocks "Spam@Example.com", a user signing up with "spam@example.com" will not be blocked. The email should be normalized (e.g., downcased) both when storing and when looking up, similar to how `User` uses `Email.downcase` elsewhere in the codebase.

title: should_block? has side effects during validation, corrupting match statistics
body: `should_block?` increments `match_count` and sets `last_match_at` as a side effect. This method is called from `EmailValidator#validate_each`, which runs during `user.valid?`. If the user record subsequently fails to save for an unrelated reason (e.g., username taken), the match_count is still incremented. This means match_count reflects validation attempts rather than actual blocked registrations, making the statistics unreliable.

title: record.save can fail silently, losing statistics without indication
body: In `should_block?`, `record.save` is called without checking its return value or using `save!`. If the save fails (e.g., due to the uniqueness validation triggering a race condition, or a database error), the match_count increment and last_match_at update are silently lost. The method still returns the block decision based on the in-memory object, hiding the failure. Consider using `update_columns` to bypass validations for this statistics update, or at minimum checking the return value.

title: BlockedEmail.should_block? is called even when value is nil or blank
body: `validate_each` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)` without first checking if `value` is present. If `value` is nil (e.g., during an intermediate validation state), this will execute a database query with `where(email: nil)` and attempt to call `match_count += 1` on a nil record (which is safe due to the `if record` guard), but it still issues a pointless database query on every validation of a record with a nil email. A guard clause like `return if value.blank?` at the top would be more robust.

title: Domain setting is insufficiently escaped before use in regex, allowing regex injection
body: `email_in_restriction_setting?` only escapes dots via `gsub('.', '\.')` before interpolating the admin-provided setting into `Regexp.new`. If the setting contains other regex metacharacters (e.g., `(`, `)`, `+`, `*`, `[`), they will be interpreted as regex syntax. A malicious or mistaken admin input could cause a `RegexpError` crash or unintended matching behavior. Use `Regexp.escape` on each domain segment, or at minimum document that `|` is the only expected special character and validate the input format.

title: should_block? issues a full save with validations just to update statistics
body: Calling `record.save` triggers the full ActiveRecord lifecycle including `before_validation :set_defaults` and the `validates :email, presence: true, uniqueness: true` checks. The uniqueness validation issues an additional SELECT query. Since the record already exists and we're only updating counters, `record.update_columns(match_count: record.match_count, last_match_at: Time.zone.now)` would be more efficient and avoid the unnecessary validation overhead on every blocked-email check.

title: Non-atomic read-modify-write of match_count in should_block?
body: The `should_block?` method reads `match_count`, increments it in Ruby memory, then calls `save`. Under concurrent requests (e.g., two signups with the same blocked email simultaneously), both requests can read the same value, increment it, and save, resulting in a lost update. Use an atomic SQL update like `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all(['match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?', Time.zone.now])` instead.

title: save can fail silently in should_block?, losing match statistics
body: `record.save` returns false on failure (e.g., validation error) without raising. If the save fails, the match_count increment and last_match_at update are silently lost. Since this is called during user validation, a failure here would go unnoticed. Consider using `update_columns` to bypass validations/callbacks, or at minimum `save!` with error handling.

title: Validator has write side-effect: should_block? mutates database during validation
body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` performs a database write (incrementing match_count, updating last_match_at) every time it is called. Since this is invoked from a model validator, any call to `user.valid?` — including dry-run checks, admin previews, or repeated validations before save — will increment the counter. This makes match_count unreliable as a metric and introduces unexpected writes in contexts that should be read-only. The counting logic should be separated from the blocking check, or moved to an after_save/after_create callback.

title: Email lookup is case-sensitive, allowing blocked emails to be bypassed
body: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` performs a case-sensitive comparison. If an admin blocks `spammer@evil.com` but a user signs up with `Spammer@Evil.com`, the lookup will not find the record and the email will not be blocked. The codebase has an `Email.downcase` helper used elsewhere (e.g., `users_controller.rb#change_email`). The email should be normalized (downcased) before lookup, and ideally also normalized before storage via a `before_validation` callback.

title: Domain whitelist/blacklist regex does not escape all special characters
body: `setting.gsub('.', '\.')` only escapes dots, but the setting value could contain other regex metacharacters (e.g., `+` in `sub+domain.com`). This could cause incorrect matching or regex errors. Use `Regexp.escape` on each domain segment, or split on the delimiter and escape individually.

title: rejectedEmails persists across modal sessions on singleton controller
body: `rejectedEmails` is initialized as `Em.A([])` on the controller prototype. In Ember, controllers are singletons, so this array accumulates rejected emails across multiple opens of the create-account modal. If an admin later unblocks an email, the client will still reject it until a full page reload. The array should be cleared when the modal is opened or the controller is reset.

title: No test coverage for whitelist/blacklist logic in EmailValidator
body: The spec only tests the `BlockedEmail.should_block?` path (stubbed). The whitelist and blacklist logic that was moved from `User#email_validator` into `EmailValidator` has no test coverage in this new spec file. If the refactor introduced a regression in domain matching, it would not be caught.

title: Email matching is case-sensitive, will miss blocked emails with different casing
body: The `should_block?` method uses `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` which performs an exact string match. Since email addresses are case-insensitive (per RFC 5321, the local part is case-sensitive in theory but universally treated as case-insensitive in practice), a blocked email stored as 'Spam@Example.com' will not match a signup attempt with 'spam@example.com'. The email should be downcased before lookup, and ideally stored in a normalized (lowercased) form, consistent with how the User model handles emails.

title: Validation has write side-effects: should_block? mutates match_count on every validation call
body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` increments `match_count` and updates `last_match_at` in the database. This is called from a validator, meaning any call to `user.valid?` (not just `user.save`) will increment the counter. In the `UsersController#create` action, `user.valid?` is called explicitly on line 168 before `user.save` on line 172, so the match_count will be incremented twice for a single signup attempt. More broadly, any code path that calls `.valid?` or `.errors` on a user with a blocked email will produce spurious increments.

title: Silent failure if record.save fails in should_block?
body: If `record.save` returns false (e.g., due to a validation error or database issue), the method still returns the blocking decision based on the in-memory `record.action_type`. The match_count and last_match_at updates are silently lost. The return value of `save` should be checked or `save!` should be used, or at minimum the failure should be logged.

title: Incomplete regex escaping in email_in_restriction_setting? allows regex injection via site settings
body: The method only escapes dots with `setting.gsub('.', '\.')` before interpolating into a regex. Other regex metacharacters (e.g., `+`, `*`, `(`, `)`, `[`, `]`, `{`, `}`, `|`, `^`, `$`) are not escaped. A malicious or mistaken admin could set `email_domains_whitelist` to something like `.*` or `(a{1,10000000})` causing either overly broad matching or a ReDoS attack. `Regexp.escape` should be used on each domain individually.

title: Race condition in should_block? between read and write of match_count
body: Under concurrent requests, two processes can read the same `match_count` value, both increment it in memory, and both save. One write will overwrite the other, resulting in a lost update. This is a minor data integrity issue for statistics, but could be fixed with an atomic `update_all` or `increment!` instead of read-modify-write.

title: Email validator spec does not test whitelist/blacklist domain logic
body: The spec only tests the blocked email path. The whitelist and blacklist domain checking logic (which was moved from user.rb) has no test coverage in this new spec file. Since this logic was refactored into a new class, it should have dedicated tests to ensure the behavior is preserved, especially edge cases around regex matching.

title: XSS via unescaped request.referer in JavaScript context
body: The referer is interpolated into a JavaScript string using ERB's `<%= %>` which only HTML-escapes. In Rails 3.2, `html_escape` does not escape single quotes. Since the value is placed inside a single-quoted JS string (`'<%= request.referer %>'`), an attacker who controls a page on the embeddable host can craft a URL containing a single quote to break out of the string and execute arbitrary JavaScript. For example, a referer like `http://embeddable-host.com/'); alert(document.cookie); ('` would pass the host check in `ensure_embeddable` but inject code. Use `j` (escape_javascript) helper or `raw json_escape` instead.

title: URL interpolated into HTML attribute without escaping enables attribute injection
body: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the URL is interpolated directly into an HTML anchor tag: `"#{url}"`. Although the URL is validated against `^https?\:\/\/`, it can still contain single quotes (e.g., `http://example.com/' onclick='alert(1)`). Since this content is stored with `cook_method: raw_html` (which returns raw as-is) and rendered with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in the embed view, this allows HTML attribute injection leading to XSS. The URL should be HTML-escaped before interpolation.

title: NoMethodError when RSS item has no content element
body: The line `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` will raise a NoMethodError if `i.content` is nil. Many RSS feeds use `<description>` instead of `<content:encoded>`, and SimpleRSS may return nil for `content` in such cases. This would crash the entire feed polling job, preventing any items from being imported. A nil check or fallback to `i.description` is needed.

title: Non-atomic setnx + expire can permanently block URL retrieval
body: The throttle mechanism uses two separate Redis commands: `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process crashes or is killed between these two calls, the key will exist without a TTL, permanently preventing retrieval of that embed URL. Use `$redis.set(retrieved_key, "1", ex: 60, nx: true)` (or the equivalent for the Redis version in use) to make this atomic.

title: Origin check uses substring match instead of strict equality
body: The postMessage origin validation uses `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` which checks if `e.origin` is a substring of `discourseUrl`. While not easily exploitable in most configurations, a strict equality check (`e.origin !== discourseUrl.replace(/\/$/, '')`) would be more robust. For example, if discourseUrl is `https://forum.example.com/` and a message arrives from origin `https://forum.example.com`, indexOf returns 0 (passes), but if discourseUrl were `https://forum.example.com.evil.com/`, a message from `https://forum.example.com` would also pass because it's a substring.

title: Server-side request forgery via open-uri in import_remote
body: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read` using open-uri, which follows redirects and can access internal network resources. While `TopicRetriever` validates the host against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, `import_remote` is also called directly from the Disqus import task with arbitrary URLs from an XML file. If the initial URL redirects to an internal address (e.g., `http://169.254.169.254/` for cloud metadata), this could leak sensitive information. Consider using a restricted HTTP client that doesn't follow redirects to private IP ranges.

title: Imported RSS content rendered without sanitization
body: Posts imported via RSS use `cook_method: raw_html` which bypasses all Discourse sanitization (the `cook` method returns `raw` directly). The embed view then renders this with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. If an RSS feed contains malicious HTML (script tags, event handlers, etc.), it will be rendered as-is in the embed iframe. The content should be sanitized (e.g., using the `Sanitize` gem already in the Gemfile) before storage or before rendering.

title: XSS via unescaped request.referer in JavaScript context
body: The `request.referer` value is interpolated directly into a JavaScript string literal (`'<%= request.referer %>'`) without any escaping. An attacker who can influence the Referer header (e.g., by embedding the iframe from a page with a crafted URL containing a single quote) can break out of the string and inject arbitrary JavaScript that executes in the context of the Discourse domain. Use `j` (escape_javascript) or `raw escape_javascript(...)` to sanitize the value.

title: Weak postMessage origin validation using indexOf
body: The origin check `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` uses substring matching rather than exact comparison. If `discourseUrl` is `https://forum.example.com/`, then a malicious origin like `https://forum.example.com.evil.com` would pass the check because it is a substring of `discourseUrl`. This allows a malicious page to send forged `discourse-resize` messages. Use an exact equality check (e.g., compare `e.origin` to the origin portion of `discourseUrl`).

title: Unsanitized raw HTML rendered from external feed content
body: `<%= raw post.cooked %>` outputs the post's cooked content without any HTML sanitization. When `cook_method` is `raw_html` (as set for imported feed content), `Post#cook` returns the raw input directly. This means any `<script>` tags or event handlers present in the RSS/Atom feed content will execute in the user's browser on the Discourse domain, enabling stored XSS. The content should be sanitized (e.g., with the `Sanitize` gem already in the Gemfile) before rendering.

title: String#scrub is not an HTML sanitization method
body: `i.content.scrub` calls `String#scrub` which was introduced in Ruby 2.1 to replace invalid byte sequences in a string's encoding — it does not strip or sanitize HTML tags. This means raw HTML from the feed (including potentially dangerous markup) is passed through to `CGI.unescapeHTML` and then to `TopicEmbed.import` without any tag filtering. If the intent was to strip HTML, a different method should be used; if the intent was to allow HTML, the call is a no-op at best and misleading at worst.

title: embed_url parameter not validated against embeddable_host before enqueuing fetch job
body: The `embed_url` parameter from user input is passed directly to `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` without verifying that its host matches `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. Although `TopicRetriever` performs a host check, the controller should also validate this to avoid enqueuing unnecessary jobs for arbitrary URLs and to provide defense in depth against SSRF if the retriever's check is ever bypassed or changed.

title: Mutating the contents parameter with << causes side effects for callers
body: `contents << "\n<hr>\n<small>..."` mutates the string object passed by the caller. In `poll_feed.rb`, `i.content.scrub` returns a new string so it's safe there, but in `import_remote` the `doc.content` result is passed directly. If any caller reuses the string or passes a frozen string, this will raise a `FrozenError` or produce unexpected results. Use `contents = contents + ...` or `contents.dup` before appending.

title: Test expects synchronous TopicRetriever call but controller enqueues a background job
body: The test mocks `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)`, expecting a synchronous call. However, the controller implementation calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`, which enqueues a Sidekiq job rather than calling `TopicRetriever` directly. This test will fail against the actual implementation, meaning the controller's retrieval path is not properly tested.

title: open-uri used to fetch arbitrary URL without redirect restrictions
body: `open(url).read` in `import_remote` uses Ruby's `open-uri` which follows HTTP redirects by default. Even though `TopicRetriever` checks the initial host, a malicious embeddable host could respond with a redirect to an internal network address (e.g., `http://169.254.169.254/` for cloud metadata), enabling SSRF. Consider using a library that restricts redirects or validates the final resolved host.

title: Non-standard ERB syntax 'end if' may cause confusion or errors
body: Line 6 uses `<%- end if %>` which is non-standard ERB. While Ruby may parse `end if` as a valid (albeit unusual) modifier expression, the intent is clearly just `<%- end %>`. This could confuse future maintainers and some ERB processors may not handle it correctly.

title: XSS via unescaped request.referer in inline JavaScript
body: The `request.referer` value is interpolated directly into a JavaScript string literal without any escaping: `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')`. Although the `ensure_embeddable` before_filter validates the referer's host, the referer string can still contain characters like single quotes or backslashes that break out of the JS string context. An attacker who controls the Referer header (e.g., via a crafted link or redirect from the allowed host) could inject arbitrary JavaScript into the embedded iframe, which runs in the Discourse origin.

title: XSS via unescaped URL interpolated into HTML
body: The `url` parameter is interpolated directly into an HTML string: `"#{url}"`. While the URL is validated to start with `http://` or `https://`, it can still contain HTML metacharacters (e.g., `http://example.com/'>`). Since posts are stored with `cook_method: :raw_html` and rendered with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, this allows stored XSS in the embed view.

title: Weak origin validation using substring match
body: The postMessage origin check uses `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`, which is a substring test rather than an exact origin comparison. If `discourseUrl` is `https://forum.example.com/`, a malicious origin like `https://forum.example` (a different domain) would pass the check because it is a prefix of `discourseUrl`. The check should parse the URL and compare the origin exactly (protocol + host + port).

title: NoMethodError when RSS item has no content element
body: `i.content.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError: undefined method 'scrub' for nil:NilClass` when an RSS/Atom feed item does not have a `content` element (many feeds only provide `description`). This will crash the entire feed polling job, preventing all items from being imported.

title: NoMethodError when embed_by_username site setting is blank
body: `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase` will raise `NoMethodError` if the `embed_by_username` setting is blank or nil. The `fetch_http` method is called from `perform_retrieve` without checking whether `embed_by_username` is configured, unlike `PollFeed#execute` which guards against this. This can crash the RetrieveTopic background job.

title: Incorrect default port check in absolutize_urls
body: The condition `uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443` does not account for the URL scheme. An HTTPS URL on port 80 (unusual but valid) would incorrectly get `:80` appended, and an HTTP URL on port 443 would incorrectly get `:443` appended. The check should be scheme-aware: omit the port only when it matches the default for the scheme (80 for http, 443 for https).

title: Server-side request via open() without scheme validation in import_remote
body: `import_remote` calls `open(url).read` without validating the URL scheme. While callers like `TopicEmbed.import` check for `https?://`, `import_remote` is a public method that can be called directly (e.g., from the disqus.thor task with `t[:link]`). Ruby's `open` with `open-uri` can be abused with certain inputs. A scheme validation should be added at the `import_remote` level as defense in depth.

title: Unnecessary user_id passed to RetrieveTopic job for anonymous users
body: When `current_user` is nil (anonymous visitor), `current_user.try(:id)` returns nil, and the job receives `user_id: nil`. Inside the job, `User.where(id: nil).first` executes a database query that returns nil, which is harmless but wasteful. More importantly, the `no_throttle` logic in TopicRetriever relies on `user.try(:staff?)` which will be nil for anonymous users, meaning the throttle always applies—this is correct behavior but the code path is unclear.

title: `-ms-align-items` is not a valid CSS property
body: The `align-items` mixin outputs `-ms-align-items: $alignment;` but this property does not exist in any version of Internet Explorer or Edge. The correct IE10 property is `-ms-flex-align` (already included on line 120). This line produces dead CSS and suggests a copy-paste error. It should be removed.

title: `order` mixin uses wrong value for old flexbox ordinal-group properties
body: `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group` use 1-based indexing, while the modern `order` property is 0-based. Passing `order(3)` (as done in header.scss for `.panel`) outputs `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: 3` which actually means position 2 in the old spec. The mixin should output `$val + 1` for these two properties to achieve equivalent ordering in older browsers.

title: `float: right` on button is ignored inside flex container
body: `.small-action` is now a flex container (via `@include flexbox()`), but the `button` child still uses `float: right` to position itself at the trailing edge. Float has no effect on flex items, so the button will no longer be pushed to the right. It should use `margin-left: auto` or an `order` value instead.

title: Removal of `.title` float rule may break layout if `.title` elements exist outside flex context
body: The diff removes the `.d-header .title { float: left; }` rule entirely. If any markup still contains a `.title` element inside `.d-header` but outside `.contents` (the new flex container), or if a plugin/theme relies on this rule, the element will lose its float. Within the flex container float is ignored anyway, so if `.title` is always inside `.contents` this is safe, but the removal is silent with no migration note.

title: `align-items` mixin does not map modern keywords to legacy equivalents
body: The mixin passes `$alignment` verbatim to `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`. If a future caller passes `flex-start` or `flex-end` (valid modern values), the legacy properties will receive invalid values since they expect `start`/`end`. Currently only `center` and `baseline` are used (which are identical across specs), but the mixin's interface is misleading and will silently break with other valid inputs.

title: `-ms-align-items` is not a valid CSS property
body: The `align-items` mixin outputs `-ms-align-items: $alignment;` which is not a real CSS property in any version of Internet Explorer or Edge. The correct legacy IE property is `-ms-flex-align` (already included on line 120). This line is dead code that will be silently ignored by all browsers, but it indicates a misunderstanding that could lead to confusion. It should be removed.

title: `order` mixin does not account for 1-based indexing of legacy box-ordinal-group
body: The `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group` properties are 1-indexed (first item is group 1), while the modern `order` property is 0-indexed (first item is order 0). The mixin passes `$val` directly to both, so `@include order(3)` produces `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: 3` which places the element in the 3rd position in old browsers but the 4th position (after items with order 0, 1, 2) in modern browsers. On older WebKit/Mozilla browsers that only support the old box model, `.panel` in the header will appear one position earlier than intended. The mixin should add 1 to the value for the old ordinal-group properties.

title: Removal of `.title { float: left }` may break header layout
body: The diff removes the `.title { float: left; }` rule from `.d-header`. While `.contents` is now a flex container (which handles child positioning), the `.title` class is still used in header markup. If any child of `.d-header` outside `.contents` uses the `.title` class, or if there are plugins/themes that rely on `.d-header .title` being floated, this removal could cause a layout regression. The PR provides no replacement styling for `.title` elements.

title: `align-items` mixin does not map modern values to legacy equivalents
body: The mixin passes `$alignment` directly to `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`, which only accept `start`, `end`, `center`, `baseline`, `stretch` — not the modern `flex-start` or `flex-end` values. While current usages (`center`, `baseline`) happen to be valid in both syntaxes, the mixin will silently produce invalid CSS if called with `flex-start` or `flex-end` in the future. A proper implementation should map `flex-start` → `start` and `flex-end` → `end` for the legacy properties.

title: order mixin uses wrong value for old box-model ordinal-group properties
body: The `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group` properties are 1-based, while the standard `order` property is 0-based. The mixin passes `$val` directly to both, so `@include order(2)` produces `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: 2` (which means "second position" in old syntax) but `order: 2` (which means "after two other groups" in standard syntax). The old prefixes should use `$val + 1` to produce equivalent visual ordering. This causes incorrect element ordering in browsers that only support the old box model (e.g., older Safari/iOS).

title: -ms-align-items is not a valid CSS property
body: The property `-ms-align-items` does not exist. The correct IE/Edge prefixed property for align-items is `-ms-flex-align` (already included on line 120). This line is dead code that will be silently ignored by all browsers, but it may mislead future maintainers into thinking IE alignment is handled by this line.

title: align-items mixin does not map values for old vendor prefixes
body: The old `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align` properties use different keywords than standard `align-items` for some values: `flex-start` should become `start` and `flex-end` should become `end`. The mixin passes `$alignment` verbatim to all prefixes, so it will silently fail if called with `flex-start` or `flex-end`. Current call sites only use `center` and `baseline` (which happen to be identical across specs), but the mixin is now a public utility that will break for future callers using other values.

title: Removing .title float rule may break header layout for elements that still depend on it
body: The diff removes `.title { float: left; }` from `.d-header` and replaces the parent `.contents` with flexbox. However, if any child elements within `.title` (or `.title` itself in certain templates/plugins) rely on the float to establish a block formatting context or to position sibling elements, they will now behave differently. More critically, `.title` is no longer explicitly styled at all—if it contains inline content that previously relied on the float to size correctly, it may now collapse or overflow in the flex container. Verify that `.title` renders correctly as a flex item without any explicit display or sizing rules.

title: Removing bullet badge margin-top in extra-info-wrapper may cause vertical misalignment
body: The rule `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` was removed and replaced with `line-height: 1.5` on the parent. The `line-height` increase affects all inline content in the wrapper, not just the bullet badge, and may not produce the same vertical offset for the bullet dot specifically. This could cause a visual regression where bullet category badges in the extra-info (docked header) appear misaligned relative to the title text.

title: `include_website_name` is missing the trailing `?` so it is never used as a guard
body: ActiveModel::Serializer looks for methods named `include_<attribute>?` (with a question mark) to decide whether to include an attribute in the output. The method is defined as `include_website_name` without the `?`, so it is just a regular method that is never invoked by the serialization framework. As a result, `website_name` will always be serialized even when `website` is blank, potentially outputting `nil` or causing unexpected behavior.

title: `website_name` is not listed in `untrusted_attributes`, leaking website info for TL0 users
body: The `untrusted_attributes` list (lines 105–111) includes `:website` so that it is hidden from anonymous viewers when the profile belongs to a TL0 user (`scope.restrict_user_fields?` returns true). However, `:website_name` is not in that list, so even when `website` is suppressed for untrusted users, `website_name` will still be serialized and exposed, effectively leaking the same information that `untrusted_attributes` is meant to protect. `website_name` should be added to `untrusted_attributes` or its include guard should also check `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`.

title: Subdomain comparison logic fails for certain domain structures (e.g., co.uk TLDs)
body: The heuristic on line 144 compares `website_host.split('.')[1..-1]` with `discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1]` when both have the same number of dot-separated parts and more than 2 parts. For domains like `www.example.co.uk` vs `forum.example.co.uk`, this would compare `example.co.uk` with `example.co.uk` and incorrectly treat them as the same base domain (which happens to be correct here), but for `www.example.co.uk` vs `forum.other.co.uk` it would compare `example.co.uk` with `other.co.uk` and correctly reject. However, for a case like `sub.domain.com` vs `other.domain.com` where the actual registrable domains differ but share a TLD, the logic may produce unexpected results. More critically, the `else` branch (line 149) only checks if `discourse_host` ends with `website_host`, not the reverse, so `www.example.com` as the website with `example.com` as the instance host would not match, even though they share the same registrable domain.

title: `include_website_name` is missing the trailing `?` so it will never be used as a guard
body: ActiveModel::Serializer recognizes conditional inclusion methods by the naming convention `include_<attribute>?` (with a question mark). Every other guard in this file follows that convention (e.g. `include_email?`, `include_stats?`, `include_user_fields?`). Because `include_website_name` lacks the `?`, the serializer will never call it, and `website_name` will be serialized unconditionally—even when `website` is blank—producing a `null` value in the JSON payload instead of omitting the key.

title: `website_name` is not listed in `untrusted_attributes`, leaking website info for TL0 users
body: The `website` attribute is listed in `untrusted_attributes` (line 109), which hides it from anonymous viewers when the profile belongs to a TL0 user. However, `website_name` is not included in that list. Because `website_name` exposes the same underlying data (the website URL's host and path), it will still be serialized for TL0 users viewed by anonymous visitors, defeating the privacy restriction that `untrusted_attributes` is meant to enforce.

title: `URI(website.to_s)` is parsed redundantly on every branch
body: `URI(website.to_s)` is first parsed on line 138 to extract the host, then parsed again on lines 143, 146, and 149 to extract the path. Parsing should be done once and the resulting URI object reused, avoiding repeated allocations and potential inconsistency if the value were ever to change between calls.

title: No test covers the sibling-subdomain branch (e.g. www.example.com vs forum.example.com)
body: The `website_name` method has three branches: exact host match, same subdomain depth (sibling subdomains), and parent-domain match. The tests cover the first and third branches but not the second (lines 144–146 of the serializer). A test with `Discourse.current_hostname` returning e.g. `forum.example.com` and a website of `http://www.example.com/page` would exercise that path and verify the expected output `www.example.com/page`.

title: `include_website_name` is missing the trailing `?` so it will never be called as a guard
body: ActiveModel::Serializer recognizes conditional inclusion methods by the naming convention `include_<attribute>?` (with a question mark). The method is defined as `include_website_name` without the `?`, so the serializer framework will never invoke it as a guard. As a result, `website_name` will always be serialized (as `null` when website is blank) rather than being omitted. Rename to `include_website_name?` to match the convention.

title: `website_name` is not listed in `untrusted_attributes`, leaking info for TL0 users to anonymous viewers
body: The `website` attribute is listed in `untrusted_attributes` (line 109), which hides it from anonymous users viewing TL0 profiles. However, `website_name` is only in the regular `attributes` list and is not added to `untrusted_attributes`. This means anonymous visitors can still see the website name (and potentially the full path) for TL0 users even though the raw `website` URL is hidden. Add `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` call to maintain consistent visibility rules.

title: Test for untrusted attributes does not include `website_name`
body: The `untrusted_attributes` list in the spec (line 11) does not include `:website_name`. Since `website_name` should be hidden for TL0 users seen by anonymous viewers (same as `website`), it should be added to this list so the test verifies it is properly suppressed. Without this, the missing `untrusted_attributes` entry in the serializer goes undetected.

title: `URI(website.to_s)` is parsed multiple times redundantly
body: The `website_name` method calls `URI(website.to_s)` up to four times (lines 138, 143, 146, 149). Parsing the URI once into a local variable at the top of the method and reusing it would be clearer and avoid redundant parsing, especially since this runs on every user profile serialization.

title: group.users.delete(user_id) passes an integer instead of a User object
body: In `remove_member`, `group.users.delete(user_id)` is called where `user_id` is an integer (from `params.require(:user_id).to_i`). title: Unclosed {{each}} block causes broken template

The `` on line 22 closes the parent div immediately after opening the each block, meaning member items will never render and the template will likely throw a Handlebars compilation error or produce malformed HTML.

title: No upper bound on limit parameter allows unbounded queries
body: The `members` action accepts `params[:limit]` with no maximum cap: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i`. A client can pass an arbitrarily large value (e.g., limit=999999) to force the server to load and serialize the entire group membership in a single query, potentially causing memory exhaustion or denial of service for large groups. A reasonable upper bound should be enforced.

title: remove_member test uses wrong HTTP method (:put instead of :delete)
body: The test 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' uses `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...` but the route defines `remove_member` as a DELETE endpoint (`delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`). While controller specs can invoke actions directly regardless of HTTP verb, this inconsistency with the other remove_member test on line 125 (which correctly uses `:delete`) suggests a copy-paste error and means the test doesn't verify the actual request path a client would use.

title: Missing semicolon after addMembers promise chain
body: The `addMembers` method's `.then()` call on line 59 is missing a trailing semicolon. While JavaScript's ASI will likely handle this in most cases, it is inconsistent with the `removeMember` method (line 48) which does have a semicolon, and could cause subtle issues with certain minifiers or if code is later appended on the next line.

title: group.users.delete(user_id) passes an integer instead of a User record
body: ActiveRecord's `CollectionProxy#delete` expects record objects, not integer IDs. `group.users.delete(user_id)` where `user_id` is an integer will not remove the user from the group — it will either raise an error or silently do nothing depending on the Rails version. The correct approach is to find the user first (e.g., `group.users.delete(User.find(user_id))`) or use `group.users.where(id: user_id).destroy_all`.

title: totalPages overcounts when user_count is evenly divisible by limit
body: The formula `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` returns one extra page when user_count is exactly divisible by limit. For example, with 100 users and limit 50, it returns 3 instead of 2. The correct formula is `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`. This also causes `showingLast` to be wrong, allowing the user to navigate to an empty page.

title: Test for remove_member on automatic group uses wrong HTTP method
body: The test uses `xhr :put, :remove_member` but the route is defined as `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`. A PUT request to this route will result in a routing error (404), not the expected 422. The test should use `xhr :delete, :remove_member` to match the route definition. The second test in the same context correctly uses `:delete`.

title: add_members does not strip whitespace from usernames after splitting
body: When the client sends usernames like "user1, user2" (with spaces after commas, which is common from autocomplete UIs), `usernames.split(",")` produces `["user1", " user2"]`. The leading space in `" user2"` will cause `User.find_by_username` to fail, silently skipping that user. Each username should be stripped: `username.strip`.

title: create action ignores alias_level sent by the frontend
body: The frontend's `asJSON()` method includes `alias_level` in the payload for both create and save operations. However, the server-side `create` action only sets `name` and `visible`, ignoring `alias_level`. If a user sets an alias level before creating a new group, that setting will be silently lost. The `update` action does handle `alias_level`, making this inconsistent.

title: No upper bound on limit parameter allows unbounded queries
body: The `members` action accepts `params[:limit]` without any upper bound validation. A client can request `limit=999999999`, causing the database to attempt loading an enormous result set. This is a denial-of-service vector. The limit should be clamped to a reasonable maximum (e.g., 1000).

title: next action can set offset equal to user_count, producing an empty page
body: In the `next` action, `Math.min(group.get("offset") + group.get("limit"), group.get("user_count"))` can produce an offset equal to `user_count` (e.g., offset=50, limit=50, user_count=100 → new offset=100). This offset is then clamped to `user_count` in `findMembers` and sent to the server, which will return zero members. The offset should be capped at `user_count - limit` or the `showingLast` guard should prevent this case (which it fails to do due to the `totalPages` bug).

title: group.users.delete(user_id) passes an integer ID instead of a record object
body: ActiveRecord's CollectionProxy#delete expects model instances, not integer IDs. Passing `user_id` (an integer from `params.require(:user_id).to_i`) will not match any User record in the association, so the member will silently not be removed. The fix is to find the user first (e.g., `user = User.find(user_id)` then `group.users.delete(user)`) or use `group.user_ids -= [user_id]`.

title: totalPages computed property over-counts by one when user_count is evenly divisible by limit
body: The formula `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an incorrect result when user_count is an exact multiple of limit. For example, 50 users with limit 50 yields totalPages=2, but there is only 1 page. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` instead.

title: Each helper is never closed with {{/each}}
body: The `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` block on line 21 is opened but never closed with `{{/each}}`. The next line (22) is the closing `` for the parent container. This will cause a Handlebars template compilation error or malformed DOM, preventing group members from rendering correctly.

title: Unbounded limit parameter allows dumping entire user table
body: The `limit` parameter from user input is used directly in the query with no upper bound. A malicious or careless client can pass an extremely large value (e.g., limit=999999999) to force the database to return and serialize all group members in a single response, causing memory pressure and slow responses. Cap the limit to a reasonable maximum (e.g., 1000).

title: Test uses PUT but the route for remove_member is DELETE
body: The test `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42` sends a PUT request, but the route is defined as `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`. While controller specs may bypass routing and call the action directly, this test does not verify that the correct HTTP method is enforced. It should use `xhr :delete` to match the route definition and catch potential routing misconfigurations.

title: Missing semicolon after .then() in addMembers may cause ASI issues
body: The `addMembers` method's promise chain ends with `})` on line 59 without a trailing semicolon. While JavaScript's automatic semicolon insertion usually handles this, it can cause subtle bugs if the next line in a minified or concatenated bundle begins with `(` or `[`.

title: Cached translations not invalidated when SiteSetting.default_locale changes
body: The `translate` method in `translate_accelerator.rb` caches results using a key of `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`. When a translation is missing in the user's locale, the fallback chain (which includes `SiteSetting.default_locale`) is used to resolve it, and the result is cached. If an admin later changes `SiteSetting.default_locale` at runtime, previously cached translations will still reflect the old fallback locale until the LRU cache evicts them or the process restarts. The cache key should incorporate the default locale, or the cache should be cleared when the default locale setting changes.

title: FallbackLocaleList extends Hash but never populates it
body: `FallbackLocaleList` inherits from `Hash` but overrides `[]` to always compute a fresh array without ever storing entries. This means any code that relies on standard Hash behavior (e.g., `each`, `keys`, `key?`, `fetch`, or serialization) will see an empty hash. If the `i18n` gem or any middleware ever calls a method other than `[]` on `I18n.fallbacks`, it will get unexpected results. Consider inheriting from `Object` instead, or documenting that only `[]` and `ensure_loaded!` are supported.

title: Non-atomic `@loaded_locales ||= []` in ensure_loaded!
body: In a multi-threaded server (e.g., Puma), two threads could both observe `@loaded_locales` as `nil`, each create a new empty array, and one assignment silently overwrites the other. While `load_locale` is mutex-protected, the check-then-load pattern in `ensure_loaded!` (`@loaded_locales.include?(locale)` followed by `load_locale`) is not atomic with respect to `reload!` setting `@loaded_locales = []`. A thread could pass the `include?` check, then `reload!` resets the array, and the thread proceeds to call `load_locale` which re-adds the locale to the fresh array — benign in this case, but the `||=` initialization is a data race under the Ruby memory model.

title: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` called on every request
body: `ensure_loaded!` iterates over all fallback locales (up to 3) and checks `@loaded_locales.include?` for each on every request, even when locales are already loaded. This is a minor per-request overhead. Consider a fast-path check (e.g., a flag or comparing against a cached set) to skip the iteration when nothing has changed, or move the call to only trigger when the locale actually changes from the previous value.

title: Fallback locales are only preloaded in controller context, not in background jobs or mailers
body: `ensure_loaded!` is only invoked from `ApplicationController#set_locale` (a before_filter). In contexts outside the request/response cycle—background jobs (Sidekiq), mailers, rake tasks, the Rails console—the fallback locales returned by `FallbackLocaleList#[]` are never loaded via `I18n.ensure_loaded!`. When the i18n Fallbacks module attempts to look up a missing key in a fallback locale, that locale's YAML translations will not have been loaded by the translate_accelerator's lazy-loading mechanism, so the lookup returns nil and the fallback silently fails, producing a missing-translation string instead of the intended fallback value.

title: FallbackLocaleList#[] allocates a new array on every translation lookup
body: The `[]` method builds a fresh array (`[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact`) on every invocation. The i18n Fallbacks module calls `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` on every single translation lookup. In a high-traffic Discourse instance this creates significant GC pressure. The result should be memoized (e.g., store in the underlying Hash via `super` or a local cache) and invalidated only when `SiteSetting.default_locale` changes.

title: Non-atomic initialization of @loaded_locales in ensure_loaded!
body: `@loaded_locales ||= []` is performed outside any mutex. If two threads enter `ensure_loaded!` concurrently when `@loaded_locales` is still nil, each may assign a distinct empty array. The subsequent `load_locale` call acquires `LOAD_MUTEX` and appends to whichever array is current at that moment, but the losing thread's local reference (captured before the mutex) may point to the discarded array, causing a locale to appear unloaded on the next check. In practice MRI's GIL makes this unlikely to manifest, but under JRuby/TruffleRuby or with future Ruby changes it could cause a locale to be loaded twice or a check to incorrectly miss a loaded locale.

title: ensure_loaded! acquires a mutex check on every request even when locales are already loaded
body: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` iterates over up to three locales and calls `I18n.ensure_loaded!` for each. Although `ensure_loaded!` short-circuits with an `include?` check before calling `load_locale`, it still performs the array lookup and method call overhead on every single request. For a hot path like `set_locale`, a simple guard (e.g., a boolean flag or checking `@loaded_locales` size against expected count) could avoid the per-request cost entirely after initial load.

title: Cache key does not account for fallback chain changes
body: The LRU cache key is `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`. With the new FallbackLocaleList, the fallback chain depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale`, which can be changed at runtime by an admin. If `default_locale` changes, previously cached translations (which were resolved using the old fallback chain) will continue to be served from cache with incorrect fallback results. The cache key should incorporate the fallback chain or `SiteSetting.default_locale` to avoid stale translations.

title: translate only loads the current locale, not fallback locales
body: The `translate` method calls `load_locale(config.locale)` to ensure the current locale is loaded, but does not load fallback locales. When I18n fallbacks are active, `translate_no_cache` will attempt lookups in fallback locales (e.g., `SiteSetting.default_locale` and `:en`). If those locale files haven't been loaded yet (e.g., in background jobs, mailers, or any code path that doesn't go through `ApplicationController#set_locale` which calls `ensure_loaded!`), the fallback lookups will silently fail to find translations, defeating the purpose of this PR for non-controller contexts.

title: FallbackLocaleList is a top-level class that inherits from Hash but never stores entries
body: `FallbackLocaleList` inherits from `Hash` and overrides `[]` to compute results dynamically, but never calls `super` or stores anything. Any code that iterates over the fallbacks object (e.g., `I18n.fallbacks.each`, `I18n.fallbacks.keys`) or checks `I18n.fallbacks.empty?` will get unexpected results from the empty underlying Hash. Consider inheriting from a simpler base or documenting that only `[]` is supported.

title: ensure_loaded! acquires a mutex check on every request for each fallback locale
body: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is called on every request in `set_locale`. It iterates over the fallback chain (up to 3 locales) and for each calls `I18n.ensure_loaded!`, which checks `@loaded_locales.include?(locale)`. While the check short-circuits before the mutex when the locale is already loaded, this still adds per-request overhead proportional to the fallback chain length. For high-traffic sites, consider memoizing at the request level or checking once whether all fallbacks are loaded.

title: Denial cache key is ambiguous due to underscore separator
body: `userPermDenialCacheKey` concatenates `name` and `parent` with underscores, but both values can themselves contain underscores. This means distinct (name, parent) pairs can produce identical cache keys. For example, name="a_b", parent="c" and name="a", parent="b_c" both yield the same key suffix "a_b_c". A denial cached for one resource/folder combination would incorrectly block access to the other. Consider using a separator that cannot appear in UIDs (e.g., a null byte or a structured encoding), or hashing the components separately.

title: Denial cache can block access to a resource immediately after it is created
body: The denial cache is checked before any other permission source. If a Check request for a specific resource is made before that resource exists (e.g., a pre-flight check, a shared link accessed before creation completes, or a retry from the UI), the denial is cached with a 30-second TTL. Once the resource is created and permissions are written to the DB, the user will still be denied for up to 30 seconds because the denial cache short-circuits before the permission cache or DB are consulted. This is the exact scenario the PR aims to fix (creator can't access newly created dashboard/folder), so the denial cache can reintroduce the bug under these timing conditions.
