body: `UsernameForm.authenticate()` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the only such method defined in the class hierarchy is `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` which requires a `UserModel` parameter. No no-arg overload exists in `UsernameForm`, `UsernamePasswordForm`, `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator`, or their parents. This will cause a compilation error. The call should likely be `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`.

title: Passkeys conditional UI no longer set up during initial login (user == null)
body: In `authenticate()`, the webauthn setup condition was changed from being inside the `else` branch (user is null, i.e. initial login) to `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` which requires `user != null`. This means passkeys conditional UI will no longer be rendered on the initial login page when no user has been identified yet. The tests in this PR (e.g. `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey` and `PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey`) expect the webauthn form element to be present on the initial login page, which contradicts this code. The condition for the `authenticate` method should likely be `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` (without the user-null check) to preserve initial-login behavior while also enabling the re-authentication case.

title: Passkeys no longer available on error during initial login
body: The overridden `challenge(context, error, field)` method now only fills the webauthn context when `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is true, which requires user != null. Previously it was `context.getUser() == null && webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`. This means that if a user enters an invalid username during initial login (user is still null after the failed attempt), the passkey option will not be shown on the error page, preventing them from retrying with a passkey. This is a UX regression for the initial-login error flow.

title: Missing @Override annotation on shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators
body: The method `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(AuthenticationFlowContext context)` overrides `WebAuthnAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` but is missing the `@Override` annotation. While not a runtime issue, this reduces compile-time safety and clarity of intent.

title: Test cleanup references non-existent alias "alias" instead of the actual IDP alias
body: The cleanup lambda `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove` uses the literal string "alias" instead of the dynamically generated alias `"idp-alias-" + i`. This means the cleanup will attempt to look up and remove an IDP with alias "alias" which does not exist, so the 20+ IDPs created by this test will never be cleaned up. This can cause test pollution and interference with other tests that assume a clean realm state. The same bug exists on line 425 for the additionally created IDP.

title: getLoginPredicate may throw NPE if IdentityProviderModel.getConfig() returns null
body: The newly added predicate clause `idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)` will throw a NullPointerException if `getConfig()` returns null. While most IdentityProviderModel implementations initialize the config map, the predicate is now used in the cache invalidation path (`registerIDPLoginInvalidation`) which is called during create/remove operations. If any code path constructs an IdentityProviderModel without initializing the config map, this would cause an unhandled NPE during cache invalidation, potentially leaving the cache in a stale state.

title: getForLogin returns results in non-deterministic order due to HashSet
body: The `getForLogin` method collects resolved identity providers into a `HashSet<IdentityProviderModel>` and returns its stream. HashSet provides no ordering guarantees, so the returned stream order is non-deterministic. While the current known caller (`OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean`) sorts results, any other caller of `getForLogin` that relies on a stable order (e.g., for pagination or display) would get inconsistent results across invocations. The same pattern exists in `getByOrganization`, but since `getForLogin` is a new public API surface, it's worth considering using a `LinkedHashSet` to preserve the delegate's ordering.

title: Cleanup uses literal string "alias" instead of the actual IDP alias
body: In `testCacheIDPForLogin`, the cleanup registration `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` uses the literal string `"alias"` instead of the actual alias `"idp-alias-" + i`. This means the cleanup will attempt to look up a non-existent IDP with alias "alias" and will never actually remove the 20 IDPs created in the loop. This can cause test pollution, affecting subsequent tests that assume a clean realm state. The same issue exists on line 425 for the additional IDP created in step 1.

title: getForLogin cache does not check organization invalidation unlike getByOrganization
body: The `getByOrganization` method (line 173) checks `isInvalid(cacheKey) || isInvalid(orgId)` before serving from cache, but `getForLogin` only checks `isInvalid(cacheKey)`. If an organization is invalidated (e.g., disabled), the login cache will still return the organization's IDPs. The `isEnabled()` re-check added in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` mitigates this for the login page, but any other caller of `getForLogin` that does not re-check `isEnabled()` could receive IDPs from a disabled organization. Consider adding an `isInvalid(organizationId)` check similar to `getByOrganization`, or documenting that callers must always re-check `isEnabled()` on results.

title: registerIDPLoginInvalidation may silently skip invalidation when BROKER_PUBLIC is toggled on an org-linked IDP via create
body: In `registerIDPLoginInvalidation`, the predicate `getLoginPredicate().test(idp)` includes the check `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`. If an IDP is created with `organizationId` set but `BROKER_PUBLIC` not yet in config (e.g., it will be set in a subsequent update), the predicate returns false and the login cache is not invalidated on creation. While the subsequent update would trigger invalidation via `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate`, there is a brief window where the cache is stale. This is a minor concern since the typical flow sets all config at creation time, but worth noting for correctness.

title: getForLogin can return IDPs with isEnabled()==false when their organization is disabled
body: The cached getForLogin resolves IDP IDs via getById, which wraps them with createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel. This wrapper's isEnabled() returns false if the IDP's organization is disabled. However, the getForLogin method returns these models without filtering by isEnabled(), unlike the delegate implementation which filters at the DB level (ENABLED=true). This means the Infinispan getForLogin can return IDPs that are not actually available for login. The PR adds isEnabled() re-checks in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean to compensate, but any other caller of getForLogin that trusts the method's documented contract ('Returns all identity providers available for login') would receive disabled IDPs. Consider filtering by isEnabled() before returning, or invalidating the login cache when an organization's enabled status changes.

title: registerIDPLoginInvalidation does not invalidate when a non-login IDP is removed but was previously cached in a login query due to a prior state
body: registerIDPLoginInvalidation only invalidates if getLoginPredicate().test(idp) returns true for the removed IDP. However, consider this sequence: (1) IDP is enabled and has no org → it's cached in the login list; (2) IDP is updated to be disabled → registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate correctly invalidates; (3) IDP is updated to be re-enabled but with hideOnLogin=true → predicate fails, no invalidation (correct, it's not a login IDP); (4) IDP is removed → registerIDPLoginInvalidation checks the predicate on the removed model (hideOnLogin=true), predicate fails, no invalidation. This is actually correct because the IDP was already removed from the login cache in step 2. However, if between step 2 and step 4 a cache miss repopulates the login cache (which wouldn't include this IDP since it's hidden), the remove correctly doesn't invalidate. So this is actually fine on deeper analysis, but the logic is fragile and relies on the predicate being evaluated against the current state rather than the cached state.

title: Test cleanup references wrong alias, IDPs created in test won't be cleaned up
body: The cleanup registration uses the literal string "alias" instead of the actual IDP alias (e.g., "idp-alias-" + i): getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove). This means the 20 IDPs created in testCacheIDPForLogin won't be properly cleaned up after the test, potentially affecting other tests. The same issue exists in testCacheIDPByOrg (pre-existing). The cleanup should reference the actual alias, e.g., final String aliasCopy = alias; getCleanup().addCleanup(() -> testRealm().identityProviders().get(aliasCopy).remove()).

title: getForLogin always resolves each cached ID via getById, causing N individual cache lookups
body: The getForLogin method iterates over the cached set of IDs and calls session.identityProviders().getById(id) for each one. While getById itself uses caching, this results in N individual cache lookups plus N potential organization lookups (inside createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel's isEnabled() override) per getForLogin call. For realms with many identity providers, this could be a performance concern on the login page. The existing getByOrganization method has the same pattern, so this is consistent, but worth noting as a potential optimization opportunity (e.g., batch resolution or caching the resolved models).

title: Dead code: two ASN1Encoder instances created and immediately discarded
body: Lines 114-115 create two `ASN1Encoder` instances, call `.write()` on them, and discard the results. The actual encoding is correctly performed on lines 117-121. These two lines are dead code (likely leftover from development) that allocate objects for no purpose. They should be removed to avoid confusion.

title: New abstract method `order()` added to public interface breaks existing implementations
body: Adding `int order()` as a non-default method to the `CryptoProvider` interface is a source-incompatible change. Any third-party or extension module that implements `CryptoProvider` will fail to compile after upgrading. Consider providing a default implementation (e.g., `default int order() { return 0; }`) to preserve backward compatibility.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider() does not return a BouncyCastle provider
body: The method `getBouncyCastleProvider()` returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, which is typically the SUN or SunJSSE provider, not BouncyCastle. Any caller relying on this method to obtain a BouncyCastle `Provider` instance (e.g., for algorithm lookups by provider name) will get incorrect behavior. Since this provider is meant for limited use, consider throwing `UnsupportedOperationException` like the other unsupported methods, or document clearly that this returns a fallback provider.

title: Silent selection among multiple providers may mask misconfiguration
body: Previously, having multiple `CryptoProvider` implementations on the classpath would throw an `IllegalStateException`, alerting users to a misconfiguration. Now the highest-order provider is silently selected and the rest are logged at DEBUG level. In production environments where DEBUG is typically disabled, a misconfiguration (e.g., accidentally including both FIPS and non-FIPS crypto jars) would go unnoticed, potentially leading to unexpected cryptographic behavior.

title: Dead code: two ASN1Encoder instances created and immediately discarded
body: In `concatenatedRSToASN1DER`, lines 114-115 create two `ASN1Encoder` instances via `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger)` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger)`, but their results are never used. The actual encoding is performed on lines 117-121. These lines are dead code that allocate objects unnecessarily and suggest a copy-paste error. They should be removed.

title: New abstract method `order()` on public interface breaks external implementations
body: The `order()` method is added to the `CryptoProvider` interface without a default implementation. Any external code that implements `CryptoProvider` (e.g., custom providers in downstream projects or the keycloak-client repository before it is synced) will fail to compile. Providing a default method (e.g., `default int order() { return 0; }`) would preserve backward compatibility while still allowing the ordering mechanism.

title: `getBouncyCastleProvider()` returns the default KeyStore provider, not BouncyCastle
body: The method `getBouncyCastleProvider()` is documented to return the BouncyCastle security provider, but this implementation returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, which is typically the SUN or SunJSSE provider. If any code path in the authz-client (or future code) calls this method expecting an actual BouncyCastle provider instance (e.g., to pass to `getInstance` calls), it will get the wrong provider. While most operations in this class throw `UnsupportedOperationException`, this method silently returns a misleading value.

title: `readSequence` silently returns empty list for indefinite-length encoding
body: If `readLength()` returns -1 (indicating indefinite-length encoding per line 134), the `while (length > 0)` condition in `readSequence` is immediately false, and an empty list is returned without any error. While ECDSA DER signatures should not use indefinite-length encoding, this silent failure could mask malformed input. A check for `length == -1` with an appropriate exception would be safer.

title: `CryptoIntegration.init()` called on every `AuthzClient.create()` invocation
body: `CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader())` is called unconditionally on every `AuthzClient.create(Configuration)` invocation. While `init` is idempotent (it checks `cryptoProvider == null`), it still acquires the `lock` object's monitor on every call after the first due to the outer null check being non-synchronized. Consider caching a flag or documenting that this is intentional to avoid confusion about repeated initialization cost.

title: New non-default method `order()` on public interface breaks external implementations
body: Adding `int order()` as an abstract method to the `CryptoProvider` interface is a binary and source incompatible change. Any third-party or external module that implements `CryptoProvider` (which is a public interface in the `keycloak-common` module) will fail to compile or get a `NoSuchMethodError` at runtime. This should be a `default` method with a sensible fallback value (e.g., `default int order() { return 0; }`) to preserve backward compatibility.

title: Dead code: two ASN1Encoder instances created and written but results discarded
body: Lines 114-115 (`ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger); ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);`) create encoder instances, write to them, but the results are never used. The actual encoding is performed on lines 117-121. This is dead code that causes unnecessary object allocations on every call to `concatenatedRSToASN1DER`. It appears to be a leftover from development/refactoring.

title: `getBouncyCastleProvider()` does not return a BouncyCastle provider
body: The method `getBouncyCastleProvider()` returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, which is whatever JCA provider backs the default keystore type (typically SUN or SunJSSE), not BouncyCastle. The method's contract (per the interface Javadoc: 'BouncyCastle security provider. Can be either non-FIPS or FIPS based provider') is violated. If any code path calls this method expecting BouncyCastle-specific capabilities, it will fail or behave incorrectly. Consider throwing `UnsupportedOperationException` like the other unsupported methods, or documenting why this approximation is acceptable.

title: Silent selection among multiple providers may mask classpath misconfiguration
body: Previously, having multiple `CryptoProvider` implementations on the classpath threw an `IllegalStateException`, alerting users to a misconfiguration. Now the highest-order provider is silently selected and the others are only logged at DEBUG level. In production environments where DEBUG logging is typically disabled, a misconfigured classpath (e.g., accidentally including both `keycloak-crypto-default` and `keycloak-crypto-fips1402`) will no longer produce any visible error, potentially leading to subtle security or behavioral issues that are hard to diagnose.

title: `CryptoIntegration.init` called on every `AuthzClient.create()` may race with server-side initialization
body: `CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader())` is called unconditionally in `AuthzClient.create(Configuration)`. If the authz-client JAR is used in the same JVM as a Keycloak server (e.g., in integration tests or embedded scenarios), and the authz-client's classloader only sees `AuthzClientCryptoProvider` (order 100), there is a race: if the authz-client initializes first, the static `cryptoProvider` will be set to `AuthzClientCryptoProvider`, and subsequent server-side `init` calls will be no-ops, leaving the server with a provider that throws `UnsupportedOperationException` for most operations. The init call should be guarded or the authz-client should use `setProvider` only if no provider is already set.

title: setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException but is invoked by the client-removal event listener
body: AdminPermissions.registerListener calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) when a ClientRemovedEvent fires and ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) is enabled. Since MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, removing any client while V2 is active will crash the event handler with an unhandled exception, likely aborting the client deletion. The method should be a no-op (or the event listener should skip V2-incompatible operations) instead of throwing.

title: canView() does not account for MANAGE permission, breaking manage-implies-view invariant
body: canView() only checks canViewClientDefault() (role-based) and hasPermission(VIEW). It does not check hasPermission(MANAGE). A user granted a global MANAGE permission on all clients will have canManage() return true but canView() return false, which is inconsistent: manage should imply view. This can cause the user to be unable to list clients even though they can manage them. The method should also return true when hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE) is true.

title: getResourceName does not handle the new CLIENTS resource type
body: getResourceName handles USERS by resolving the user and returning the username, but has no branch for CLIENTS. When a policy's resourceType is "Clients", the method falls through to resource.getDisplayName(). For individual client resources the name is the internal client ID (set by resolveClient), and getDisplayName() is likely null or unhelpful. A branch analogous to USERS should resolve the ClientModel and return client.getClientId(), and return "All clients" for the type-level resource.

title: Dead code: getEvaluationContext method is defined but never called
body: The private method getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) at line 262 is never invoked anywhere in the class. It also references the unused static import of TOKEN_EXCHANGE (line 46). This dead code adds confusion about the intended design and should be removed or wired in if it is needed for canExchangeTo support in the future.

title: canMapRoles does not fall back to admin role check, unlike canManage and canConfigure
body: canMapRoles(ClientModel) only calls hasPermission(client, MAP_ROLES). Unlike canManage(ClientModel) which first checks root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS), canMapRoles does not check any admin role. In V1, having MANAGE_CLIENTS role allowed mapping roles. If the intent in V2 is that MANAGE_CLIENTS role should still grant MAP_ROLES capability (as the interface Javadoc implies by referencing the V1 scope), the admin role check is missing. If it is intentionally excluded, the interface Javadoc should be updated to clarify.

title: Potential NullPointerException when getResourceTypeResource returns null
body: In `hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)`, when no specific resource is found for the client, the code calls `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)`. This method can return null (e.g., if `supportsAuthorizationSchema` returns false internally, or if the 'Clients' type resource was never created). The result is then immediately dereferenced on line 219 with `authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()`, which will throw a NullPointerException if `resource` is null. A null check should be added after the call to `getResourceTypeResource`.

title: registerListener will call setPermissionsEnabled which throws UnsupportedOperationException in V2 mode
body: The `registerListener` method now gates event handling behind `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)`. However, when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is enabled (which is the focus of this PR), `management()` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2`, whose `clients()` returns `ClientPermissionsV2`. The `setPermissionsEnabled` method in `ClientPermissionsV2` (line 193) throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. If both V1 and V2 features are enabled simultaneously (which is typical since V2 builds on V1), removing a client will trigger this listener and cause an unhandled `UnsupportedOperationException`, breaking client deletion. The same applies to `roles().setPermissionsEnabled` and `groups().setPermissionsEnabled` if their V2 implementations also throw.

title: Dead code: getEvaluationContext method is never called
body: The private method `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel authorizedClient, AccessToken token)` at line 262 is never invoked anywhere in the class. The `canExchangeTo` method that would logically use it throws `UnsupportedOperationException` instead. This dead code, along with the unused imports (`EvaluationContext`, `ClientModelIdentity`, `DefaultEvaluationContext`, `AccessToken`, `Scope`, and the static import of `TOKEN_EXCHANGE`), should be removed to avoid confusion.

title: getResourceName does not handle CLIENTS resource type, may return null
body: The `getResourceName` method handles the USERS resource type by resolving the username, but does not handle the newly added CLIENTS resource type. For client resources, the resource name is set to the client's internal ID (from `resolveClient`). The method falls through to `return resource.getDisplayName()` which may return null if no display name was explicitly set on the resource (the `resourceStore.create` call in `getOrCreateResource` does not set a display name). This could result in null being returned where a human-readable name is expected in the UI or API responses.

title: canMapRoles does not check MANAGE_CLIENTS admin role unlike other methods
body: In `canMapRoles`, `canMapCompositeRoles`, and `canMapClientScopeRoles`, the code only checks fine-grained permissions via `hasPermission(client, ...)`. Unlike `canManage(ClientModel)` which first checks `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS)`, these methods do not check any admin role. In V1 (`ClientPermissions`), `canMapRoles` checks for `MANAGE_CLIENTS` role first. If this asymmetry is unintentional, an admin with `MANAGE_CLIENTS` role but without explicit FGAP `map-roles` permission would be unable to map client roles in V2 mode, which is a behavioral regression. If this is intentional V2 design, it should be documented.

title: getResourceName does not handle CLIENTS resource type
body: The `getResourceName` method handles the USERS resource type (returning 'All users' for the type resource, or the username for specific user resources), but does not handle the newly added CLIENTS resource type. When a policy has resourceType 'Clients', the method falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`. For the type-level resource this returns 'Clients' which is acceptable, but for specific client resources (whose name is the client's internal ID/UUID), it will return the raw UUID instead of the human-readable clientId. This will result in poor UX when displaying which resources a permission applies to in the admin console.

title: canMapRoles does not check admin roles, inconsistent with canManage
body: In `ClientPermissionsV2`, `canManage(ClientModel)` first checks `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS)` before falling back to permission evaluation, but `canMapRoles`, `canMapCompositeRoles`, and `canMapClientScopeRoles` only check for explicit permissions without any admin role fallback. This means a user with the `MANAGE_CLIENTS` admin role can update/delete clients but cannot map their roles unless a separate MAP_ROLES permission is explicitly granted. In V1, having MANAGE_CLIENTS implicitly allowed role mapping. This inconsistency may cause unexpected authorization failures for administrators who have the MANAGE_CLIENTS role but no explicit fine-grained permissions.

title: Dead code: getEvaluationContext method is never called
body: The private method `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel authorizedClient, AccessToken token)` at line 262 is defined but never invoked anywhere in the class. It appears to be leftover code from a previous design for `canExchangeTo`, which now throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. This dead code should be removed to avoid confusion.

title: Unused static import TOKEN_EXCHANGE
body: The static import `org.keycloak.services.resources.admin.permissions.AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE` on line 46 is never referenced in the class. The `canExchangeTo` method that would have used it now throws `UnsupportedOperationException`.

title: Arrays.asList used for single-element list in hasPermission
body: In both `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` (line 225) and `hasPermission(String)` (line 250), `Arrays.asList(scope)` is used to create a single-element list that is then checked with `contains()` inside a nested loop. Since there's only one expected scope, this could be simplified to a direct `scope.equals(s)` comparison (as done in `hasGrantedPermission` at line 279), avoiding the unnecessary list allocation and contains() overhead on every permission evaluation.

title: Event listener guard only checks V1 feature flag, may cause UnsupportedOperationException if both V1 and V2 are enabled
body: The event listener is now guarded by `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` (V1 flag). If both V1 and V2 features are enabled simultaneously, `management()` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2`, whose `clients().setPermissionsEnabled()` throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. This would cause an unhandled exception during client removal events. The guard should either also exclude V2 (`!Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2)`) or the V2 implementation should handle `setPermissionsEnabled` gracefully (e.g., as a no-op instead of throwing).

title: Breaking change: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changed from 4 to 3
body: The exit code for 'recreate upgrade needed' was changed from 4 to 3, and exit code 4 is now repurposed for 'feature disabled'. Any existing automation scripts or CI/CD pipelines that were checking for exit code 4 to detect that a recreate upgrade is required will now misinterpret the result. While this is a preview feature, the documentation previously (and in this PR's updated docs) defines these exit codes as a stable contract for scripting. Consider whether this renumbering is necessary or if FEATURE_DISABLED could use a different code (e.g., 5) to preserve backward compatibility with the existing exit code contract.

title: Feature-disabled test does not verify exit code and only covers metadata subcommand
body: The test `testFeatureNotEnabled` only verifies the error message but does not assert that the exit code is 4 (FEATURE_DISABLED). Additionally, there is no equivalent test for the `check` subcommand when the feature is disabled. Since the exit code is documented as a stable contract for automation (per the update-compatibility.adoc guide), the test should verify `cliResult.assertExitCode(4)` or equivalent, and a similar test should be added for the `check` subcommand.

title: Missing test for 'check' subcommand when feature is disabled
body: The `testFeatureNotEnabled` test only verifies that the `metadata` subcommand fails when the `rolling-updates` feature is not enabled. The `check` subcommand (`UpdateCompatibilityCheck`) has the same feature gate (line 46 of UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java), but there is no corresponding test verifying it also fails with the expected error message and exit code 4 when the feature is disabled.

title: Breaking change: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changed from 4 to 3
body: The `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` constant was changed from 4 to 3, and exit code 4 was repurposed for `FEATURE_DISABLED`. Any existing scripts or automation that were already using exit code 4 to detect 'recreate upgrade needed' (as was the case before this PR) will now silently misinterpret the result. While this is a preview feature, the documentation should explicitly call out this exit code change for early adopters, or the old value should be preserved and a different code chosen for FEATURE_DISABLED.

title: testWrongVersions does not assert exit code for incompatible versions
body: The `testWrongVersions` test verifies the error message content but does not assert that the exit code equals `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` (3). Given that this PR changes that exit code from 4 to 3, an assertion on the exit code would protect against future regressions and confirm the documented exit code contract.

title: Feature flag not enabled when updateStrategy is null, but test still expects upgrade status condition
body: In `createInitialDeployment`, when `updateStrategy` is null the method returns early without enabling the `rolling-updates` feature. However, `testImageChange` with a null strategy still calls `eventuallyRecreateUpgradeStatus`. If the operator's reconciler requires the feature flag to be enabled to produce any upgrade status condition (as implied by the CAUTION in the docs saying the operator will fail without it), this test case may not be exercising the intended code path or may fail once the operator enforces the feature gate. The relationship between the feature flag and the default (null) strategy behavior should be clarified or tested explicitly.

title: Breaking change to RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3
body: The exit code for RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was changed from 4 to 3, and the new FEATURE_DISABLED constant takes exit code 4. Any existing scripts or automation that were written against the previous exit code 4 to detect 'recreate upgrade needed' will now silently misinterpret the result (exit code 4 now means 'feature disabled'). Although this is a preview feature, the documentation in update-compatibility.adoc previously documented exit code 4 for the recreate case, so users who adopted the preview may have built automation around it. Consider whether a deprecation period or migration note is warranted.

title: testFeatureNotEnabled only covers the metadata subcommand, not check
body: The test `testFeatureNotEnabled` only verifies that the `metadata` subcommand fails when the feature is disabled. There is no corresponding test verifying that the `check` subcommand also correctly fails with exit code 4 and the appropriate error message when the feature is not enabled. Since both commands have identical feature-gate logic, a test for `check` would provide symmetric coverage.

title: Feature not enabled when updateStrategy is null, potentially inconsistent with operator behavior
body: When `updateStrategy` is null, `createInitialDeployment` returns early without enabling the `rolling-updates` feature. The documentation in advanced-configuration.adoc states 'While on preview stage, the feature rolling-updates must be enabled. Otherwise, the Keycloak Operator will fail.' If the operator enforces this check whenever it processes update logic (even for the default/null strategy path), this test case would fail at runtime. If the operator only requires the feature when `updateSpec` is explicitly set, the documentation should clarify this to avoid user confusion.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
body: In `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`, the code adds `groupResource.getId()` to the granted set. However, `getId()` returns the internal ID of the authorization resource entity in the policy store, not the group ID. In V2, resources are named by the group ID (see `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup()` which returns `group.getId()` as the resource name). The V1 implementation correctly extracts the group ID from the resource name (`resource.getName().substring(RESOURCE_NAME_PREFIX.length())`). The fix should be `granted.add(groupResource.getName())`. This bug causes the group-based user visibility filtering to silently fail: the session attribute `UserModel.GROUPS` will contain meaningless authorization resource IDs instead of actual group IDs, so no users will match the group filter.

title: canManage() grants manage access with only VIEW permission on all groups
body: The no-argument `canManage()` method checks `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, meaning a user with only VIEW permission on the all-groups resource would pass the `requireManage()` check. This method gates group creation in `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup()`. In contrast, `canManage(GroupModel group)` correctly checks only `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE`. A user who should only be able to view groups would be able to create new top-level groups. If this is intentional, the Javadoc on the interface should clarify the rationale; otherwise, the VIEW scope should be removed from this check.

title: canManage() grants manage access to users with only VIEW permission on groups
body: The no-arg `canManage()` method checks `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, meaning a user with only VIEW permission on all groups will pass this check. This method is used by `requireManage()` which gates `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup()` (group creation). A user with only VIEW permission on groups would be able to create new top-level groups, which is a privilege escalation. The V1 implementation (`GroupPermissions.canManage()`) correctly only checks `AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS`. The fix should be to only check `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` scope, not VIEW.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
body: In `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`, `groupResource.getId()` returns the internal authorization resource ID, not the group ID. In V2, resources are created with the group ID as their *name* (see `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup()` which returns `group.getId()` as the resource name). Callers of this method (e.g., `UsersResource.getUsersCount`, `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, ...)`) expect actual group IDs. Additionally, `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` will fail to find the specific resource by name (since the auth resource ID is not the group ID), causing it to fall back to the all-groups resource type check, making per-group permission evaluation incorrect. Both usages should use `groupResource.getName()` instead of `groupResource.getId()`.

title: Javadoc for canManage() incorrectly documents VIEW as sufficient for manage
body: The Javadoc for `canManage()` states 'For V2 only: Also if it has permission to VIEW or MANAGE groups.' This documents a privilege escalation as intended behavior. Since `canManage()` gates write operations (group creation, deletion, update), only MANAGE permission should be sufficient. The documentation should be corrected to match the expected security semantics (MANAGE only), and the implementation in `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` should be fixed accordingly.

title: testManageAllGroups does not register cleanup for the group created by realmAdminClient
body: In `testManageAllGroups()`, a group named 'testGroup' is created via `realmAdminClient` at line 165, but no cleanup is registered for it (unlike other tests that use `realm.cleanup().add(...)`). If the test fails after group creation, the group will persist and may affect subsequent test runs. A cleanup should be added similar to the pattern used elsewhere in the test class.

title: getResourceName does not handle Groups resource type, falls back to displayName which may be null
body: The `getResourceName` method only handles the USERS resource type explicitly. For GROUPS resources, it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`. Since group resources in V2 are created with the group ID as their name and no explicit display name is set, `getDisplayName()` may return null or the raw group ID rather than the human-readable group name. This could cause UI issues when displaying resource names in the admin console.

title: canManage() grants manage access to users with only VIEW permission
body: The no-arg `canManage()` method checks for both `AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW` and `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` scopes: `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. This means a user who only has VIEW permission on all groups will pass `requireManage()`, which is called by `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup()`. Such a user would be able to create new top-level groups despite only having view permission. The VIEW scope should be removed from this check, leaving only MANAGE.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() adds authorization resource ID instead of group ID
body: In `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`, the code adds `groupResource.getId()` (the internal authorization resource ID) to the `granted` set. However, this set is consumed by `UsersResource.searchForUser()` and `UsersResource.getUsersCount()` as actual group IDs (set via `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` and passed to `getUsersCount` overloads). Since the authorization resource ID is not the same as the group ID, user filtering by group membership will silently fail to match any users. The code should use `groupResource.getName()` instead, which holds the group ID as set by `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup()`.

title: getResourceName does not handle GROUPS resource type
body: The `getResourceName` method has explicit handling for `USERS` resource type (resolving user ID to username) but no handling for `GROUPS` resource type. When a policy references a specific group resource, the method falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`, which may return null or an unhelpful value since group resources are created with the group ID as the name and no display name is set. This could result in poor UI representation of group resources in permission listings.

title: StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when start + end exceeds string length
body: The diff-display logic at line 111 computes `start` (matching prefix length) and `end` (matching suffix length) independently, but does not guard against `start + end > value.length()` or `start + end > sanitized.length()`. For example, if `value = "aa"` and `sanitized = "aaa"`, then `start = 2` and `end = 2`, making `value.substring(2, 2-2)` throw `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` because the begin index exceeds the end index. This will crash the verifier on certain inputs where one string is a prefix-extension of the other.

title: Italian text mistakenly placed in Lithuanian translation file
body: The value `totpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` is Italian, not Lithuanian. This appears to be a copy-paste error introduced by this PR when replacing the previous HTML-containing Lithuanian translation. The same issue exists in `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties` at line 71 (`loginTotpStep1`). Lithuanian users will see Italian text.

title: Regex character class `[a-zA-Z-_]` includes unintended characters due to range interpretation
body: In the regex `_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties`, the sequence `Z-_` inside the character class is interpreted as a range from `Z` (0x5A) to `_` (0x5F), which includes `[`, `\`, `]`, and `^`. While unlikely to cause issues with real file paths, the intent was clearly to match locale codes (letters, hyphens, underscores). The hyphen should be placed at the start or end of the class, or escaped: `[a-zA-Z_\\-]`.

title: santizeAnchors uses replaceFirst on modified string but matcher iterates original
body: In `santizeAnchors`, the `matcher` is created from the original `value` string, but `value` is reassigned via `replaceFirst` inside the loop. If the same anchor tag text appears multiple times in the value, `replaceFirst` will remove the first occurrence in the current (possibly already modified) string, which may not correspond to the occurrence the matcher is currently pointing at in the original string. This could lead to incorrect stripping when duplicate anchor tags exist.

title: Non-static instance fields POLICY_SOME_HTML and POLICY_NO_HTML are re-created per instance
body: `POLICY_SOME_HTML` and `POLICY_NO_HTML` are instance fields (not static, not final) but are immutable policy factories that could be shared. They use ALL_CAPS naming convention suggesting they should be constants. Making them `private static final` would avoid unnecessary re-creation and clarify intent.

title: verifySafeHtml throws RuntimeException instead of MojoExecutionException on I/O failure
body: When the English reference file cannot be read (line 79) or the file itself cannot be re-read (line 70), a raw RuntimeException is thrown. The calling method `verify()` only catches IOException and wraps it in MojoExecutionException. Since RuntimeException is not an IOException, it propagates uncaught through `verify()` and will surface as an unhandled exception in the Maven build rather than a clean MojoExecutionException with a descriptive message. This produces a less helpful error output (stack trace instead of a clear 'unable to read file' message) and is inconsistent with the error handling contract established by the `verify()` method signature.

title: santizeAnchors modifies value while Matcher operates on original string
body: The method creates a Matcher from `value`, then inside the loop modifies `value` via `value.replaceFirst(...)`. The Matcher continues to operate on the original string snapshot, so after the first replacement, subsequent `matcher.find()` calls return positions relative to the original string while `value` has already been shortened. If a value contains multiple anchor tags, `replaceFirst` may remove the wrong occurrence or the method may produce incorrect results. The method should either rebuild the matcher after each modification or collect all matches first and then process them.

title: containsHtml only detects lowercase HTML tags
body:
The regex `<[a-z]+[^>]*>` only matches lowercase tag names. If an English source string contains uppercase or mixed-case HTML tags (e.g., `
`, ``), `containsHtml` returns false, causing the stricter `POLICY_NO_HTML` to be applied to translations. This could produce false-positive 'Illegal HTML' errors for translations that legitimately mirror the English source's HTML.

title: Fragile path check for email theme detection
body: The condition `file.getAbsolutePath().contains("email")` is used to decide whether to strip RTL style attributes. This matches any path containing the substring 'email' anywhere (e.g., a directory named 'email_templates' or a user home directory). A more precise check, such as matching a path segment, would avoid false positives.

title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 replaced with Italian text
body: The Lithuanian translation for `loginTotpStep1` is being replaced with the Italian string 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' instead of a proper Lithuanian translation. This will show Italian text to Lithuanian-speaking users. The same issue appears in the account messages_lt.properties file.

title: Lithuanian account totpStep1 replaced with Italian text
body: The Lithuanian translation for `totpStep1` in the account theme is replaced with Italian text 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' instead of a Lithuanian equivalent. This is the same issue as in the login messages file.

title: Java MessageFormat/ChoiceFormat syntax used in i18next-based React UI
body: The `error-invalid-multivalued-size` message is changed from i18next interpolation syntax (`{{0}}`, `{{1}}`, `{{2}}`) to Java MessageFormat syntax (`{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}`) with a Java ChoiceFormat expression (`{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}`). The account-ui is a React application using i18next for client-side interpolation, which does not understand Java's ChoiceFormat. Unless there is server-side pre-processing that resolves this before the string reaches the client, the pluralization will not work and users may see the raw `{2,choice,...}` expression.

title: English file path derivation may fail for files without locale suffix
body: The regex `_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties` used to derive the English file path assumes all non-English files have a locale suffix preceded by an underscore. If a properties file without a locale suffix (e.g., `messages.properties`) is verified, the regex won't match and the replacement won't produce a valid English file path, leading to a RuntimeException when trying to open the non-existent file.

title: PolicyFactory instances recreated per VerifyMessageProperties instance
body: POLICY_SOME_HTML and POLICY_NO_HTML are instance fields initialized inline, meaning new PolicyFactory objects are created for every VerifyMessageProperties instantiation. Since these policies are immutable and stateless, they should be static final constants to avoid unnecessary object creation when verifying many files.

title: Copy-paste bug: rawTokenId is never null-checked
body: Line 73 checks `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` but should check `rawTokenId` instead of `grantType` again. This means a null `rawTokenId` will not be rejected at construction time and will cause a NullPointerException later (e.g., in `encodeTokenId` when concatenating the string).

title: Inverted logic in isAccessTokenId matcher: returns false when grant shortcut matches
body: The condition `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns false (non-match) when the grant shortcut equals the expected value. This is backwards — it should return false when they are NOT equal (i.e., `!equals`). As written, the matcher rejects tokens that have the correct grant type and accepts tokens with the wrong grant type.

title: Wrong substring index for grant type shortcut in isAccessTokenId
body: The token ID format is `<sessionType:2><tokenType:2><grantType:2>:<uuid>`, so the grant type shortcut occupies characters at indices 4 and 5 (i.e., `substring(4, 6)`). The code uses `substring(3, 5)` which extracts the last character of the token type and the first character of the grant type (e.g., "ta" from "onrtac"). Combined with the inverted logic bug, the matcher never actually validates the grant type, making the test assertions ineffective.

title: Removal of public copy constructor from OAuth2GrantType.Context is a source-incompatible SPI change
body: The copy constructor `Context(Context context)` was removed from `OAuth2GrantType.Context`, which is a public class in the `server-spi-private` module. Any extension or custom grant type that constructs a Context from an existing Context instance will fail to compile after upgrading. This is a breaking API change for SPI consumers.

title: Package-private mutable fields exposed for testing
body: `grantsByShortcuts` and `grantsToShortcuts` are declared with package-private access (no modifier) to allow direct manipulation in the unit test. This bypasses encapsulation and means any class in the same package can mutate these maps. Consider using a test-specific factory setup or making these fields accessible via a protected method instead.

title: Copy-paste error: rawTokenId is never null-checked
body: Line 73 reads `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` but should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`. The `grantType` parameter is checked twice (lines 72 and 73), while `rawTokenId` is never validated. A null `rawTokenId` will silently pass construction and cause a NullPointerException later when the token ID is encoded or used.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted condition and wrong substring indices
body: The matcher has two bugs: (1) The condition `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` is inverted — it returns false (mismatch) when the grant shortcut equals the expected value, and returns true (match) when it does not. It should be `!equals`. (2) The substring indices are wrong: the token format is `stttgt:uuid` (positions 0-1 session type, 2-3 token type, 4-5 grant type), so the grant shortcut is at `substring(4, 6)`, not `substring(3, 5)`. Together these bugs make the matcher accept tokens with the wrong grant type and reject tokens with the correct one, rendering all tests using this matcher unreliable.

title: Removal of Context copy constructor is a breaking API change for extensions
body: The `Context(Context context)` copy constructor was removed from `OAuth2GrantType.Context`. This is a public class in `server-spi-private`, which is the SPI layer that extensions compile against. Any third-party extension that was using this copy constructor will fail to compile after upgrading. If this is intentional, it should be documented as a breaking change in release notes.

title: getTokenContextFromTokenId does not handle null input
body: If `encodedTokenId` is null, `encodedTokenId.indexOf(':')` will throw a NullPointerException with no meaningful message. Since this method may be called with token IDs parsed from incoming requests, a defensive null check with a clear error message would be safer.

title: Duplicate shortcut validation does not detect all collision scenarios
body: The check `grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size()` detects when a shortcut is reused across grants (because one map loses an entry) but it does not detect the case where a grant's `getShortcut()` returns the same value as `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.UNKNOWN` ("na"). In that case, the `put` on line 75 silently overwrites the UNKNOWN entry added on line 78, and the sizes remain equal, so no error is raised. The UNKNOWN mapping is then lost, causing `getShortcutByGrantType("na")` to return the colliding grant name instead of "na".

title: Unused import of TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory
body: The import `org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.grants.TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory` is added but never used in this file. The code on line 237 uses `OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE` directly.

title: Null check validates grantType twice instead of rawTokenId
body: Line 73 reads `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` but should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`. This is a copy-paste error: `rawTokenId` is never null-checked, so a null `rawTokenId` will pass construction and cause a NullPointerException later (e.g., in `encodeTokenId` when concatenating).

title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic and wrong substring indices
body: Two bugs in `isAccessTokenId`: (1) The condition `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` is inverted—it returns false when the shortcut matches instead of when it doesn't match (missing `!`). (2) The substring indices are wrong: in the 6-char prefix (e.g., `onrtac`), the grant type occupies indices 4–5, but the code extracts `substring(3, 5)` which gives characters at indices 3–4 (e.g., `ta` from `onrtac`). The correct call is `substring(4, 6)`. Combined, the matcher almost always returns true regardless of the actual grant type, making the test assertions ineffective.

title: Removal of Context copy constructor is a breaking change
body: The `Context(Context context)` copy constructor was removed from `OAuth2GrantType.Context`. Although this is in `server-spi-private`, any extension or internal code that was constructing a `Context` from an existing `Context` instance will fail to compile after this change. If this constructor was used anywhere in the codebase or by known extensions, this is a source-incompatible change that should be documented or deprecated first.

title: Duplicate shortcut validation does not detect all collision scenarios
body: The check `grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size()` only detects collisions when two grants share the same shortcut (shrinking grantsByShortcuts) or two shortcuts map to the same grant name (shrinking grantsToShortcuts). If two grants have the same shortcut AND the same ID (unlikely but possible with misconfiguration), both maps would have the same size and the collision would go undetected. A more robust approach would be to check that the number of entries inserted equals the number of grant factories iterated.

title: removeStoredCredentialById will not remove credential from federated storage
body: When `getCredential` returns a credential from federated storage (the first branch of `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential`), calling `removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())` attempts to remove the credential from local storage only. The ID returned by a federated storage provider's `getCredentials()` method is typically a locally-generated UUID (as seen in the test storage's `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues` call), which does not exist in local storage. This means that when all recovery codes are used and the credential resides in federated storage, the credential is never actually removed. The stale credential persists in the external storage, and subsequent authentication attempts may continue to find it via `getCredential`, leading to a state where `allCodesUsed()` is true but the credential is never cleaned up.

title: NoSuchElementException if no recovery code credential exists
body: The call `credentialModelOpt.get()` on line 19 will throw `NoSuchElementException` if the Optional is empty (i.e., the user has no recovery code credential in either federated or local storage). While the bean is presumably only instantiated when the credential is expected to exist, a race condition or misconfiguration could cause this to surface as an unhandled 500 error to the user. The previous code had the same pattern (`.findFirst().get()`), but the refactoring introduces a slightly different code path that could expose this more readily if `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` and `getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream()` both return empty.

title: Raw (unhashed) recovery codes are passed to external user storage
body: The `createRecoveryCodesCredential` method serializes the raw generated codes to JSON and passes them to the user storage via `UserCredentialModel`. The `credentialModel` parameter (which contains hashed codes) is only used for the local storage fallback. This means any external user storage provider receives the plaintext recovery codes. If the external storage is compromised, all recovery codes are exposed. While this mirrors the existing OTP pattern (raw secret passed to user storage), recovery codes are bearer tokens that grant full access, making their exposure more critical. The Javadoc should explicitly document that user storage providers receive raw codes and are responsible for hashing them, or the API should be designed to pass hashed codes and let the storage provider handle verification differently.

title: getCredential may return a stale federated credential when both federated and local credentials exist
body: The `getCredential` method checks federated credentials first via `getFederatedCredentialsStream()`, then falls back to local storage. If a user has recovery codes in both federated and local storage (e.g., after a storage provider is added or during migration), the method will always return the federated credential, potentially ignoring a newer or more up-to-date local credential. There is no mechanism to detect or resolve this conflict, which could lead to authentication failures if the federated credential is outdated.

title: getCredentials creates a new credential model with a different ID than what was stored
body: In `getCredentials`, a new `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` is created via `createFromValues` each time the method is called, which generates a fresh UUID. This ID differs from the one stored in `myUser.recoveryCodes` (set during `updateCredential`). Any operation that relies on the credential ID for lookups or removal (such as `removeStoredCredentialById` in the authenticator) will fail because the ID is ephemeral and not persisted. This accurately models a real-world federated storage but also demonstrates why the `removeStoredCredentialById` approach in `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` is broken for federated credentials.

title: NoSuchElementException if no recovery credential exists
body: The constructor calls `credentialModelOpt.get()` without checking `isPresent()`. If `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` returns an empty Optional (e.g., the user has no recovery codes credential in either federated or local storage), this will throw `NoSuchElementException` at runtime. The new `getCredential` method has a more complex lookup path (federated first, then local) which increases the chance of returning empty compared to the previous direct local lookup. A guard or explicit exception with a meaningful message should be added.

title: removeStoredCredentialById may not remove federated credentials
body: When all recovery codes are consumed, `removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())` is called. However, `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential()` now returns credentials from federated storage first. If the credential originates from a federated/user storage provider, `removeStoredCredentialById` targets the local credential store and may silently fail to remove the credential from the external storage. This leaves a stale credential with all codes consumed. On subsequent logins, the authenticator's `configuredFor` check may still see the credential as present, but validation will fail since all codes are used, potentially confusing the user or causing unexpected behavior until the required action to regenerate codes is completed.

title: NullPointerException in getCredentials if user not found in map
body: In `getCredentials(RealmModel realm, UserModel user)`, `getMyUser(user)` can return null if the user is not present in the `users` map. The subsequent access to `myUser.recoveryCodes` on line 235 will throw a NullPointerException. A null check on `myUser` should be added before accessing its fields, returning an empty stream if the user is not found.

title: updateCredential may return false for reasons other than unsupported type
body: The method `createRecoveryCodesCredential` interprets `updateCredential` returning `false` as 'user storage does not support this credential type' and falls back to local storage. However, `updateCredential` on a user storage provider may return `false` for other reasons (e.g., validation failure, transient error). In such cases, the code silently creates the credential locally instead of propagating the error, which could lead to inconsistent state where the user storage rejected the update for a valid reason but the credential is still created locally. The existing `createOTPCredential` method has the same pattern, but it's worth documenting or handling this distinction.

title: No test for fallback to local storage when user storage does not support recovery codes
body: The test only covers the scenario where the user storage supports recovery codes (the `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage` was modified to support them). There is no test verifying that when a user storage provider does NOT support recovery codes (i.e., `updateCredential` returns false or `supportsCredentialType` returns false), the credential is correctly created in the local Keycloak database. This is the core fallback behavior introduced by this PR and should be tested.

title: removeStoredCredentialById may fail for federated recovery code credentials
body: When `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential()` returns a credential from federated storage (via `getFederatedCredentialsStream()`), the code at line 86 calls `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())`. This method is designed for locally stored credentials. If the credential originated from a federated/user storage provider, the ID may not be recognized by the local credential store, causing the removal to silently fail or throw an exception. As a result, exhausted recovery codes from federated storage would never be cleaned up, and the user might not be prompted to generate new ones.

title: NoSuchElementException when credential Optional is empty
body: At line 19, `credentialModelOpt.get()` is called without checking `isPresent()`. If the user has no recovery code credential in either federated or local storage (e.g., credential was removed between page render and bean construction, or a race condition), this will throw `NoSuchElementException` and result in an unhandled 500 error during login. The refactoring to use `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential()` was an opportunity to add a guard but did not.

title: Raw (unhashed) recovery codes are passed to external user storage
body: The `createRecoveryCodesCredential` method serializes the plaintext `generatedCodes` list into JSON and passes it to the external user storage via `UserCredentialModel`. Unlike the local storage path (which hashes codes via `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues`), the federated path transmits and expects storage of unhashed codes. If the external storage does not independently hash them (as the test implementation demonstrates), recovery codes are stored in plaintext, meaning a compromise of the external store exposes all recovery codes. Consider documenting this security expectation or hashing before transmission.

title: Recovery code validation uses plaintext comparison without constant-time comparison
body: At line 340, `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))` performs a plaintext string comparison of recovery codes. This is vulnerable to timing attacks that could allow an attacker to determine valid codes character by character. Additionally, the codes are stored and compared in plaintext (never hashed), unlike the local Keycloak storage path which uses SHA-512 hashing.

title: Raw type List used in JSON deserialization may cause ClassCastException
body: At line 238, `JsonSerialization.readValue(myUser.recoveryCodes.getCredentialData(), List.class)` uses a raw `List` type. The deserialized elements will be `Object` (likely `String` at runtime, but not guaranteed by the compiler). If the JSON contains non-string elements or the deserialization produces unexpected types, a `ClassCastException` could occur at runtime when the list is passed to `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues` which expects `List<String>`. A `TypeReference<List<String>>` should be used instead.

title: getCredential may return stale federated credential when local credential also exists
body: The `getCredential` method prioritizes `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` over `getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream()`. If a user has recovery codes in both federated storage and local storage (e.g., after a storage migration or misconfiguration), the federated credential is always returned even if the local one is more recent. This could lead to using outdated or already-consumed codes from the federated storage while ignoring valid local codes.

title: Returning null from getSubGroupsCount() may cause NPE at call sites
body: When the group is deleted concurrently, `modelSupplier.get()` returns null and this method returns `null`. The caller `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount` passes the result to `representation.setSubGroupCount(group.getSubGroupsCount())`. If `setSubGroupCount` takes a primitive `long`, this will NPE on unboxing. Even if it takes `Long`, downstream code that unboxes will fail. The rest of this class throws `IllegalStateException` when the model is not found (see `getDelegateForUpdate()` line 61 and `isUpdated()` line 74), so this is inconsistent with the established error-handling pattern.

title: Same NPE risk exists in other methods using modelSupplier.get() without null check
body: The fix only guards `getSubGroupsCount()`, but `getSubGroupsStream(String, Integer, Integer)` (line 256), `getSubGroupsStream(Integer, Integer)` (line 261), and `getSubGroupsStream(String, Boolean, Integer, Integer)` (line 268) all call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` without a null check. Under the same concurrent-deletion scenario that this PR addresses, these methods will still throw an NPE. The fix is incomplete.

title: Test has a race condition: reader thread may never execute during deletion window
body: The reader thread is started and then groups are immediately deleted. There is no synchronization (e.g., a CountDownLatch or similar) to guarantee the reader thread has actually begun executing `groups()` calls before deletions start. On a fast machine or under thread-scheduling pressure, all 100 deletions could complete before the reader thread gets its first iteration, making the test pass vacuously without ever exercising the concurrent path it intends to test.

title: No join() on reader thread; assertion may run before thread completes
body: After setting `deletedAll.set(true)`, the test immediately asserts on `caughtExceptions`. The reader thread may still be in-flight (between the `while` condition check and the `groups()` call) when the assertion runs. Although unlikely to cause a false pass (the thread would need to throw after the assertion), a `thread.join()` before the assertion would make the test deterministic and correct.

title: Test does not register cleanup for created groups
body: Other tests in this class use `managedRealm.cleanup().add(...)` to ensure resources are removed after the test. This test creates 100 groups and deletes them inline, but if the test fails during creation (e.g., at group 50), the already-created groups are left behind and may interfere with subsequent tests or leave the realm in a dirty state.

title: Test does not join the reader thread before asserting
body: The test starts a reader thread but never calls `join()` on it. After `deletedAll.set(true)`, the main thread immediately asserts `caughtExceptions` is empty. However, the reader thread may still be in the middle of an HTTP request at that point. This means the assertion can pass even if the reader thread would have caught an exception, making the test unreliable (false negatives). A `thread.join()` should be called before the assertion.

title: Other modelSupplier.get() call sites still lack null checks
body: The fix adds a null check for `modelSupplier.get()` in `getSubGroupsCount()` (line 274), but the same pattern exists without null checks in `getSubGroupsStream(String search, Integer firstResult, Integer maxResults)` (line 256), `getSubGroupsStream(Integer firstResult, Integer maxResults)` (line 262), and `getSubGroupsStream(String search, Boolean exact, Integer firstResult, Integer maxResults)` (line 268). If the group is deleted concurrently, these methods will still throw an NPE when `modelSupplier.get()` returns null, which is the exact scenario this PR aims to fix.

title: Test may not reliably exercise the concurrent read-during-delete scenario
body: The reader thread is started and then the main thread immediately begins deleting all 100 groups. There is no synchronization to ensure the reader thread has actually made at least one request before deletions begin. If the deletion loop completes before the reader thread's first HTTP call is issued, the test passes trivially without ever exercising the race condition it is designed to detect. Consider using a latch or verifying at least one read occurred before starting deletions.

title: Test has a race condition: reader thread is not joined before assertion
body: After setting `deletedAll.set(true)`, the test immediately asserts that `caughtExceptions` is empty. However, the reader thread may still be in the middle of its last `groups()` call (it passed the `while (!deletedAll.get())` check before the flag was set). If that call throws, the exception is added to `caughtExceptions` after the assertion has already executed, making the test non-deterministic. The thread should be joined (e.g., store the Thread reference and call `thread.join()`) before asserting on `caughtExceptions`.

title: Returning null from getSubGroupsCount() is inconsistent with the class's error-handling contract
body: When the group is not found in the database (deleted concurrently), this fix returns `null` from `getSubGroupsCount()`. However, other methods in the same class (`getDelegateForUpdate()` at line 61 and `isUpdated()` at line 74) throw `IllegalStateException("Not found in database")` in the same situation. Returning null silently propagates a potentially unexpected value to callers (e.g., `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount` calls `representation.setSubGroupCount(group.getSubGroupsCount())`), which may cause NPEs or incorrect data downstream. A more consistent approach would be to throw the same `IllegalStateException` or handle the missing group at a higher level.

title: Same potential NPE exists in getSubGroupsStream overloads that call modelSupplier.get() without null check
body: Lines 256, 262, and 268 all call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` without a null check on the result of `modelSupplier.get()`. These have the same race condition that this PR fixes in `getSubGroupsCount()` — if the group is deleted concurrently, `modelSupplier.get()` returns null and a NullPointerException is thrown. The fix should be applied consistently to these methods as well.

title: Test may not exercise the fixed code path
body: The test calls `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)` with `briefRepresentation=true`. The NPE fix is in `getSubGroupsCount()`, which is invoked via `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount` only when the `subGroupsCount` flag is true. If the brief representation path does not trigger `getSubGroupsCount()`, this test does not actually reproduce the original bug. The test should verify it exercises the specific code path that was fixed (e.g., by requesting full representation with subgroup counts, or by adding a comment explaining why brief=true is sufficient).

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key crashes on datetime fields
body: The endpoint uses `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `order_by="-datetime"`, but `get_item_key` calls `math.floor(value)` / `math.ceil(value)` directly on the attribute value. Since the `datetime` field on `AuditLogEntry` is a Python `datetime` object, this will raise `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime`. The existing `DateTimePaginator` correctly converts via `float(value.strftime("%s.%f")) * self.multiplier` before applying floor/ceil. This paginator will crash on every request that uses the optimized path.

title: Negative offset passed to Django queryset slicing raises AssertionError
body: When `enable_advanced_features` is True and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code sets `start_offset = cursor.offset` (a negative integer) and then slices the queryset with `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django's QuerySet does not support negative indexing and will raise `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported.` The comment claiming 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is factually incorrect. Since cursor offset is parsed from user-supplied input via `Cursor.from_string()` with no lower-bound validation, any authenticated admin can trigger a 500 error by crafting a cursor string with a negative offset.

title: BasePaginator change removes offset clamping for is_prev across all subclasses
body: The change from `queryset[offset:stop]` to `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` means that when `cursor.is_prev` is True, the offset is used without clamping to zero. Since `Cursor.from_string()` parses user input with `int(bits[1])` and performs no non-negativity check, a malicious or malformed cursor string with a negative offset and `is_prev=1` will pass a negative value to queryset slicing in every `BasePaginator` subclass (DateTimePaginator, Paginator, etc.), causing an AssertionError. This is a regression affecting all existing paginators, not just the new one.

title: No validation that cursor offset is non-negative allows user-controlled negative values
body: The `Cursor.__init__` accepts any integer for `offset` (via `int(offset)`) and `Cursor.from_string` parses user-supplied cursor strings without validating that the offset component is >= 0. Combined with the paginator changes in this PR that use offset values directly in queryset slicing, this allows an attacker to inject negative offsets. Even without the paginator changes, negative offsets could cause unexpected behavior in cursor comparison logic (e.g., `_build_next_values` and `_build_prev_values` arithmetic). A guard like `self.offset = max(0, int(offset))` or raising `BadPaginationError` for negative values would be appropriate.

title: Authorization check uses has_global_access which may be broader than intended
body: The condition `organization_context.member.has_global_access` grants access to the 'optimized' paginator path for any member with global access (typically org owners, managers, and admins). The PR description and comments frame this as an admin-only feature, but `has_global_access` is a broader permission level. If the intent is truly superuser-only, the check should be `request.user.is_superuser` alone. If the broader access is intentional, the security rationale in the comments ('permissions are checked at the queryset level') is misleading since the queryset is already filtered to the organization—the gate here is about enabling a buggy code path, not about data access.

title: Non-advanced path in OptimizedCursorPaginator still allows unclamped offset for is_prev
body: In the else branch (line 884), `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` replicates the same problematic pattern from BasePaginator. When `cursor.is_prev` is True and offset is negative (possible via user-crafted cursor strings), this passes a negative value to queryset slicing, causing a crash. The 'advanced features' gate only controls one branch; the fallback branch has the same vulnerability.

title: Django QuerySets do not support negative slicing
body: The code passes a negative `start_offset` to `queryset[start_offset:stop]` when `enable_advanced_features` is True and `cursor.offset < 0`. Django QuerySets explicitly raise `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported` when sliced with negative indices. The comment claiming 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is false. This will crash at runtime for any request that triggers this code path with a negative offset.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key cannot handle datetime fields
body: The endpoint uses `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `order_by="-datetime"`, so `self.key` is `"datetime"` and `getattr(item, self.key)` returns a Python `datetime` object. The `get_item_key` method then calls `math.floor(value)` or `math.ceil(value)` on it, which raises `TypeError`. The existing `DateTimePaginator` correctly converts the datetime to a numeric value first via `float(value.strftime("%s.%f")) * self.multiplier`. This paginator is a copy of the numeric `Paginator` and is incompatible with datetime fields.

title: BasePaginator.get_result behavior changed for all subclasses
body: The change from `results = list(queryset[offset:stop])` to `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` modifies the base class used by `Paginator`, `DateTimePaginator`, and all other subclasses. When `cursor.is_prev` is False, negative offsets are now silently clamped to 0 instead of being passed through (which would have raised an error from Django). While this may be defensively safe, it silently changes error behavior for all existing paginators and could mask bugs in callers that incorrectly produce negative offsets.

title: enable_advanced_features kwarg may not reach the paginator constructor
body: The `self.paginate()` helper in Sentry's base endpoint typically accepts a fixed set of parameters (request, queryset, paginator_cls, order_by, on_results, etc.) and constructs the paginator internally. Passing `enable_advanced_features=True` as an extra keyword argument will either be silently ignored (if `self.paginate` uses `**kwargs` but doesn't forward them) or raise a TypeError. If it's silently ignored, `OptimizedCursorPaginator` will be instantiated with `enable_advanced_features=False` (the default), making the 'advanced' code path unreachable.

title: Authorization check uses organization_context.member without null check
body: The expression `organization_context.member.has_global_access` will raise `AttributeError` if `organization_context.member` is None. Depending on how the endpoint is invoked and what authentication states are possible, this could result in a 500 error rather than a proper 403. The `OrganizationAuditPermission` may guarantee a member exists, but this is fragile and not explicitly defended here.

title: Misleading comment added without corresponding code change
body: The comment 'Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination scenarios' is added to `Cursor.__init__`, but the code `self.offset = int(offset)` already accepted any integer including negative values before this PR. The comment implies a behavioral change was made here, but no actual validation was removed or added. This is misleading for future maintainers and the real (broken) negative offset handling is in the paginator, not here.
