If the hash function happens to map all 20 keys to fewer than 3 buckets (extremely unlikely but possible), the test would fail non-deterministically. A more robust approach would be to verify the property over a larger sample or use a deterministic hash in the test.

title: Shutdown sets worker.shutdown flag before draining queues, causing in-queue items to be lost
body: In `FixedQueuePool.shutdown()`, `worker.shutdown = True` is set on all workers BEFORE calling `q.shutdown(immediate=False)`. When a worker finishes its current item and loops back to `while not self.shutdown`, it sees `True` and exits immediately without processing remaining items in the queue. Even though `q.shutdown(immediate=False)` would allow workers to drain remaining items, the flag check prevents this. The result is that any items enqueued but not yet picked up by a worker are silently lost on shutdown, and their offsets (already added to the tracker) will never be completed or committed.

title: Offsets are marked complete even when processing fails, causing silent data loss
body: In `OrderedQueueWorker.run()`, the `finally` block unconditionally calls `self.offset_tracker.complete_offset(...)` regardless of whether `result_processor` succeeded or raised an exception. This means failed messages have their offsets marked as complete, which allows them to be committed by the commit loop. The class docstring states 'Only commits offsets after successful processing' but this guarantee is violated. A transient error (e.g., database timeout) will cause the message to be permanently lost with no retry. The offset should only be completed on success, or there should be a retry mechanism.

title: Unbounded queues provide no backpressure despite documentation claiming otherwise
body: `queue.Queue()` is created without a `maxsize` argument, making it unbounded. The class docstring for `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` claims 'Natural backpressure when queues fill up' as a guarantee, but there is no mechanism to slow down or block the consumer when queues grow. If workers are slow (e.g., due to a downstream outage), memory usage will grow without bound until the process is OOM-killed. A `maxsize` should be set on the queues, or `submit()` should check queue depth and apply backpressure (e.g., by raising `MessageRejected` to signal the Arroyo framework to slow down).

title: Python's built-in hash() is randomized per process, making queue assignment non-deterministic across restarts
body: `get_queue_for_group` uses `hash(group_key) % self.num_queues`. Python's string hash is randomized per process invocation (via PYTHONHASHSEED). While this is consistent within a single process lifetime, it means that after a consumer restart, the same group key will likely be assigned to a different queue. If there are messages in-flight during a rebalance or restart scenario where ordering across the boundary matters, this could cause ordering violations. Using a deterministic hash like `hashlib.md5(group_key.encode()).hexdigest()` or `zlib.crc32(group_key.encode())` would provide stable assignment across restarts.

title: test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling asserts no commits on failure, contradicting the implementation
body: The test asserts `assert len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets`, expecting that processing errors prevent offset commits. However, the implementation in `OrderedQueueWorker.run()` always completes offsets in a `finally` block regardless of success or failure, meaning the commit loop will commit these offsets. This test either passes due to timing (the commit loop hasn't run yet within the test's timeout) making it flaky, or it's asserting behavior that doesn't match the implementation. The test should either be updated to match actual behavior (offsets ARE committed even on failure) or the implementation should be fixed to not complete offsets on failure.

title: OffsetTracker._get_partition_lock has a TOCTOU race on non-CPython implementations
body: The pattern `lock = self.partition_locks.get(partition); if lock: return lock; return self.partition_locks.setdefault(partition, threading.Lock())` relies on the GIL for thread safety. While safe on CPython, on other implementations (PyPy with STM, GraalPy) two threads could simultaneously see `None` from `get()` and both create separate Lock objects, leading to different threads using different locks for the same partition and breaking mutual exclusion. Using a single global lock for partition_locks access, or pre-creating locks for known partitions, would be more robust.

title: shutdown() sets queue_pool to None, preventing strategy recreation on rebalance
body: `ResultsStrategyFactory.shutdown()` sets `self.queue_pool = None` after shutting it down. If the Arroyo framework calls `create_with_partitions` again after a rebalance (which triggers `shutdown()` then `create_with_partitions`), the `assert self.queue_pool is not None` in `create_thread_queue_parallel_worker` will fail, crashing the consumer. The factory should either recreate the queue pool in `create_with_partitions` or not set it to None in `shutdown()`.

title: Backup-code login can bypass password verification
body: In the credentials authorize callback, the password is only verified when `!credentials.totpCode` (line 121). The new backup-code branch at line 131 is entered whenever `credentials.backupCode` is present, even if a non-empty `totpCode` is also supplied. An attacker can send credentials containing any non-empty `totpCode` and a valid backup code; the password check is skipped and the backup code alone authenticates. This turns a backup code into a single-factor credential and allows login without the account password.

title: Backup-code single-use guarantee is not atomic
body: After matching a backup code, the code is invalidated by decrypting the stored array, setting the matched entry to null, and writing it back with a separate `prisma.user.update`. This read-modify-write is not transactional or protected against concurrent updates. Two simultaneous login attempts using the same backup code can both read it as unused and both succeed. Concurrent uses of different codes can also overwrite each other's updates and resurrect a previously used code.

title: Dialog can be dismissed after enabling 2FA without notifying parent or resetting state
body: After TOTP verification succeeds, the modal switches to the backup-code screen, but `onEnable` and `resetState` are only invoked by the explicit Close button. If the user dismisses the dialog through `onOpenChange` (for example via backdrop click, close icon, or Escape), the parent is not notified that 2FA has been enabled and the modal state is not reset. The settings UI can remain stale until a reload, and sensitive state such as backup codes or object URLs may persist.

title: Backup-code matching is case- and whitespace-sensitive
body: Backup codes are generated as lowercase hex strings, but during login they are compared with `indexOf` after only removing dashes. The value is not trimmed or lowercased. A user who enters a valid code in uppercase, which is suggested by the UI placeholder, or with surrounding whitespace will be rejected despite having a valid backup code.

title: Disable endpoint rejects uppercase backup codes
body: The disable endpoint compares the supplied backup code after removing dashes but without trimming or lowercasing it. Since generated codes are lowercase hex, a valid backup code entered in uppercase or with surrounding whitespace is rejected, preventing a user from disabling 2FA with a valid code.

title: No tests cover actual backup-code authentication or single-use behavior
body: The PR adds a security-critical backup-code login and disable flow, but the e2e tests only verify that backup codes can be downloaded, copied, and closed. There is no test that logs in with a backup code, disables 2FA with a backup code, or asserts that a consumed backup code cannot be reused, so the core feature and its single-use guarantee are untested.

title: Password verification is skipped when any totpCode is present, allowing backup-code login without a password
body: In the credentials authorize function, the password is only verified when `user.password && !credentials.totpCode`. The new backup-code branch runs whenever `credentials.backupCode` is present. Therefore a request can authenticate to a password-protected account by sending a valid backup code plus an arbitrary non-empty `totpCode`, causing the password check to be skipped. The same logic also allows login with only a valid TOTP code and no password for password-based accounts. Second factors should be checked in addition to the password, not as a replacement for it; verify the password for accounts that have one regardless of whether a TOTP or backup code is supplied.

title: Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write and can allow reuse
body: Backup-code login decrypts the stored array, finds the used index, sets that entry to null, then writes the whole array back. Two concurrent login requests using the same backup code can both read the array before either update is committed, causing both requests to succeed and defeating the one-time-use property. Use a database transaction with re-reading/locking, an atomic conditional update, or store backup codes as individually hashed/used records.

title: QR-screen Continue button submits the TOTP enable form
body: The Continue button on the QR-code step has `type="submit"` and is inside the outer form whose submit handler calls `handleEnable`, but its `onClick` only changes the step and does not call `preventDefault`. Clicking it therefore sends an enable request with an empty TOTP code before/while navigating to the OTP step, causing spurious errors or race conditions. It should be `type="button"` or prevent the default submit behavior.

title: Backup-code screen can be dismissed without resetting state or notifying the parent
body: After 2FA is enabled, the modal shows backup codes. Only the explicit Close button calls `resetState()` and `onEnable()`. The dialog still allows dismissal through `onOpenChange`, so if the user closes the modal by overlay/escape/close UI, the component can remain mounted with `step` still set to `DisplayBackupCodes` and the backup codes still in state. Reopening the modal may then show backup codes again without re-authentication, and the parent screen may not refresh to show that 2FA is enabled. The backup-code step should block dismissal or perform the same cleanup/notification on dismiss.

title: TOTP form value is not cleared when the digit inputs are emptied
body: The effect only calls `methods.setValue("totpCode", value)` when `value` is truthy. If a user enters a six-digit code and then clears the inputs, react-hook-form keeps the previous TOTP value, so a later submission or auto-submit may send a stale code. The effect should always synchronize the form value, including setting an empty string when the input value is empty.

title: Assertion checks Promise truthiness instead of checkbox state
body: `await expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` asserts that the Promise returned by `isChecked()` is truthy, which is always true, so the test can pass even if the 2FA switch is not checked. Use `await expect(page.locator(...)).toBeChecked()` or await the boolean result explicitly.

title: No e2e coverage for using backup codes to log in or disable 2FA
body: The PR adds backup codes as an authentication fallback, but the tests only cover displaying/copying/downloading them and leave a TODO for login/disable flows. Because backup-code login and disabling 2FA with a backup code are security-critical paths, they should have explicit automated coverage.

title: Empty backup code can be submitted without a useful validation error
body: The login form uses `noValidate`, and the Zod schema only validates email/password while passing other fields through. The BackupCode input's native `required` attribute is therefore not enforced, so submitting an empty backup code sends an empty string. The server then responds as if a second factor is still required, and the UI does not show an incorrect-backup-code or required-field error. Add schema validation or explicit handling for an empty backup code.

title: Disable endpoint assumes backupCode is a string and can throw a 500
body: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` will throw a TypeError if the request body supplies a non-string value such as an object, array, or number. This turns malformed input into an internal server error instead of a validation failure. Validate the request body shape and types before using string methods.

title: Backup code comparison is case-sensitive while the UI suggests uppercase codes
body: Generated backup codes are lowercase hexadecimal strings, and the server only strips dashes before comparing. The login input placeholder uses `XXXXX-XXXXX`, which may lead users to enter uppercase letters. Since the comparison is case-sensitive, uppercase input will be rejected even if the code is otherwise correct. Normalize backup codes by trimming whitespace and lowercasing before comparison on the server, and ideally enforce the same on the client.

title: Password check can be bypassed when a backup code is submitted with a dummy totpCode
body: The credentials authorize function skips password verification whenever credentials.totpCode is truthy. Because the new backup-code branch is taken when credentials.backupCode is present, an attacker who knows a valid backup code for a password-based CAL account can also send any non-empty totpCode and bypass the account password check. Password verification should be enforced for password-based accounts when using backup codes, not skipped merely because a totpCode field is present.

title: Backup-code login is blocked for non-CAL identity providers
body: In the credentials authorize function, the early checks for non-CAL users only treat credentials.totpCode as a valid second-factor presence. A Google/SAML user who has 2FA enabled and submits a backup code without a TOTP code hits the ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled error at line 113, and can also hit IncorrectEmailPassword at line 117. These checks need to account for credentials.backupCode as well, otherwise backup codes do not work for SSO/Google 2FA users.

title: Lost access button is unavailable in the external TOTP login flow
body: When totpEmail is present, which is the flow used after Google/SAML authentication when 2FA is enabled, the login page renders ExternalTotpFooter instead of TwoFactorFooter. ExternalTotpFooter only contains a Cancel button, while the Lost access button that switches to the backup-code input is only in TwoFactorFooter. As a result, users in the external 2FA flow cannot reach the backup-code form.

title: Backup-code consumption is not atomic and can allow reuse
body: During backup-code login, the code decrypts the stored backup-code array, finds the matching index, then writes the modified array back in a separate update. Two concurrent login attempts using the same backup code can both read the array before either update commits, both pass validation, and both succeed. This violates the intended one-time-use property of backup codes.

title: Dismissing the modal after 2FA is enabled can leave the UI stale
body: After handleEnable succeeds, 2FA is already enabled server-side and the modal shows backup codes. The explicit Close button calls resetState and onEnable, but dismissing the dialog through onOpenChange, for example via Escape, backdrop click, or dialog close chrome, does not. In that case the parent settings UI is not notified that 2FA was enabled, and the component retains stale backup codes and secret state.

title: resetState does not clear the TOTP form value or sensitive state
body: resetState only clears password, error message, and step. It does not reset the react-hook-form totpCode value, clear backupCodes/secret/dataUri, or revoke backupCodesUrl. Because the component auto-submits whenever totpCode has length 6, a stale six-digit code from a previous enable attempt can be submitted automatically the next time the OTP step is opened.

title: E2E coverage for backup-code authentication is missing and the enable test does not dismiss the backup-code screen
body: The PR adds backup codes but the tests do not exercise logging in or disabling 2FA with a backup code. In addition, the first enable-2FA test now stops after entering the TOTP while the new backup-codes dialog is open; it never clicks backup-codes-close, even though onEnable is only called from that close action. This means the test does not validate the new backup-code screen and may pass while the modal is still blocking the UI.

title: Backup-code comparison is case-sensitive and does not trim input
body: The backup-code check uses credentials.backupCode.replaceAll('-', '') and then performs a strict array lookup. Generated codes are hexadecimal, but users may enter uppercase characters, especially given the XXXXX-XXXXX placeholder, or accidental surrounding whitespace. Valid codes can therefore be rejected. The code should normalize input, for example trim and lowercase it, in both login and disable flows.

title: Disable modal can reopen in the Lost access state after being closed
body: The modal does not reset twoFactorLostAccess, or error state, when it is closed via cancel or dialog dismissal. If a user switches to the backup-code Lost access view and then closes the modal without disabling 2FA, reopening the modal can unexpectedly show the backup-code input instead of the TOTP input.

title: TypeError when destinationCalendar is empty and location is Google Meet
body: In EventManager.create, mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar ?? []. If destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined, but the next line reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining. This will throw a TypeError for Google Meet events that have no destination calendar, breaking booking creation.

title: Video credentialId is no longer stored in references created by EventManager.create
body: referencesToCreate now sets credentialId only when the result is a calendar result. Previously, non-calendar results preserved result.credentialId. As a result, video booking references can be created with credentialId undefined. Later cancellation or update flows that look up the video credential by reference.credentialId may fail to delete or update the meeting.

title: updateEvent can be called with undefined or stale credential
body: In updateAllCalendarEvents, when a booking reference has credentialId, the code assigns credential from in-memory credentials or the database. If no credential is found, credential may remain undefined or retain the value from a previous loop iteration, and updateEvent is still pushed. This can cause updates to fail or be attempted with the wrong credential.

title: Only the first old calendar reference is deleted when merging bookings
body: When newBookingId is provided, updateAllCalendarEvents deletes the old calendar event by finding only the first booking reference whose type includes _calendar. For collective or multi-host bookings there can be multiple calendar references, so the remaining old calendar events will not be deleted and can remain on host calendars.

title: Fallback credential filter looks for exact type calendar
body: createAllCalendarEvents falls back to this.calendarCredentials.filter(cred => cred.type === 'calendar') when no destinationCalendar is present. Calendar credential types are normally values like google_calendar or office365_calendar, so this exact equality will usually match nothing. The stated fallback to the first connected calendar will therefore not create any calendar event.

title: Possible duplicate creation for other_calendar integrations
body: createAllCalendarEvents first creates events for each entry in event.destinationCalendar, then unconditionally creates events for every credential whose type includes other_calendar. If a destinationCalendar entry is itself an other_calendar credential, the same integration event can be created twice.

title: updateLocation can create booking references without credential or external calendar identifiers
body: updateLocation maps results into referencesToCreate using result.externalId and result.credentialId. Calendar update results from CalendarManager.updateEvent do not populate these fields, so calendar references produced by updateLocation can have undefined credentialId and externalCalendarId. Handlers that persist these references may store incomplete reference rows.

title: Team destination calendars are dropped when organizer has no destination calendar
body: For collective team events, evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to null when neither eventType nor organizer has a destinationCalendar. The later call evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars) then does nothing because of optional chaining on null. Hosts' destination calendars are silently lost, so their calendar events may not be created.

title: Organization slug logic was inverted for billing-enabled and billing-disabled environments
body: The previous code set slug when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED was false and set metadata.requestedSlug when it was true. The new code sets slug when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true and omits slug when billing is disabled. This changes organization creation behavior and can create organizations without a slug when billing is disabled or with a slug prematurely when billing is enabled.

title: Google updateEvent lost its fallback to a destination calendar
body: selectedCalendar is set to externalCalendarId when truthy; otherwise it searches event.destinationCalendar for a calendar whose externalId === externalCalendarId. When externalCalendarId is null or undefined, this lookup cannot find anything and selectedCalendar becomes undefined. Existing references without externalCalendarId will cause Google event updates to be called with an undefined calendarId instead of falling back to the event's destination calendar.

title: Google deleteEvent fallback can target the wrong calendar
body: deleteEvent now only uses externalCalendarId when provided; otherwise it attempts to find a destination calendar with externalId === externalCalendarId, which is undefined when no externalCalendarId was passed. It then falls back to primary. If the event exists on a non-primary calendar and externalCalendarId is missing, deletion can fail silently with a 404 or leave the event on the correct calendar.

title: Google event patch can use undefined calendarId
body: createEvent inserts the event with calendarId selectedCalendar || 'primary', but the subsequent events.patch call uses calendarId: selectedCalendar without the same fallback. If selectedCalendar is undefined, the patch request can fail even though the event was created on primary.

title: Google createEvent ignores destination externalId when credentialId is absent
body: createEvent now chooses the Google calendar by finding a destinationCalendar entry with the same credentialId. Older or incomplete destinationCalendar records may have externalId but no credentialId. In that case the service falls back to primary, whereas the previous behavior could use destinationCalendar.externalId. This can create events on the wrong calendar after the migration to arrays.

title: Lark createEvent only uses the first destination calendar for multi-host events
body: LarkCalendarService.createEvent destructures the first entry from event.destinationCalendar and ignores the credential that is creating the event. When EventManager creates events for multiple hosts, each host's credential receives the same full destinationCalendar array, but Lark always tries to use the first host's calendar. This can create events on the wrong calendar or fail for other hosts.

title: Office365 createEvent only uses the first destination calendar for multi-host events
body: Office365CalendarService.createEvent uses the first entry of event.destinationCalendar and ignores the credentialId passed by CalendarManager. For collective events with multiple destination calendars, every host's credential will attempt to create the event in the first host's calendar, which can fail or produce incorrect events for the other hosts.

title: CalDAV createEvent only uses the first destination calendar for multi-host events
body: BaseCalendarService.createEvent filters calendars by the first entry of event.destinationCalendar. It does not select the destination calendar that corresponds to the credential creating the event. With multiple host destination calendars, CalDAV events for non-first hosts can be created on the wrong calendar or fail.

title: Recurring cancellation only deletes the first calendar reference per booking
body: When cancelling all remaining recurring bookings, the code finds only the first reference whose type includes _calendar for each updated booking and attempts deletes using the organizer's calendar credentials. Multi-host bookings can have multiple calendar references, including credentials that are not in bookingToDelete.user.credentials, so some host calendar events may not be deleted.

title: Awaiting the apiDeletes array does not await deletion promises
body: In the paid cancellation branch, the code executes await apiDeletes where apiDeletes is an array of promises. This does not wait for the promises or catch their rejections. Calendar or video deletions may still be running when the handler returns, and failures will not be handled by the surrounding try/catch.

title: Confirming a pending collective booking only includes one destination calendar
body: confirmHandler builds evt.destinationCalendar from only booking.destinationCalendar or user.destinationCalendar. It does not include destination calendars for other collective hosts. When a pending collective booking is confirmed, EventManager.create will therefore only create the organizer's calendar event, not events for all hosts.

title: Webhook payload destinationCalendar is inconsistent between events
body: The test expects destinationCalendar to be [] for BOOKING_REJECTED but expects null for BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED elsewhere in the same file. The migration to an array-backed destinationCalendar should use a consistent empty representation across webhook payloads to avoid breaking consumers.

title: Crash when Google Meet location is used without destination calendars
body: In `EventManager.create`, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or an empty array. The condition immediately accesses `.integration` on it, which throws a TypeError. This breaks booking creation for Google Meet events when no destination calendar is set. Use optional chaining or a safe default before comparing integration.

title: updateEvent can be called with an undefined credential
body: In `updateAllCalendarEvents`, when a booking reference has `credentialId` but the credential is not present in memory and cannot be loaded from the database, `credential` remains undefined. The code still pushes `updateEvent(credential, ...)`, which will crash in `CalendarManager.updateEvent` when it reads credential properties or calls `getCalendar`. Add a guard and emit a failed result instead.

title: Duplicate event creation possible for other_calendar integrations
body: `createAllCalendarEvents` processes destination calendars and then unconditionally creates events for every credential whose type includes `other_calendar`. If a destination calendar entry already points to an `other_calendar` credential, the same event is created twice, causing duplicate CRM/non-traditional calendar entries. Deduplicate by credential or type.

title: Only the first old calendar event is deleted when merging bookings
body: When `newBookingId` is provided, `updateAllCalendarEvents` finds only the first old calendar reference from the original booking and deletes it. For collective bookings with multiple host calendar references, the remaining old calendar events are not deleted, leaving stale external calendar entries. Delete all relevant old calendar references.

title: Collective host destination calendars are discarded when main calendar is absent
body: The collective booking path initializes `evt.destinationCalendar` to null when neither event type nor organizer has a destination calendar, then uses `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. If it is null, the push is skipped and all team-member destination calendars are lost, so their calendar events will not be created. Initialize the array before pushing.

title: Google updateEvent fallback cannot select a calendar when externalCalendarId is missing
body: In `updateEvent`, if `externalCalendarId` is falsy the fallback searches `event.destinationCalendar` for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`, i.e. for undefined/empty. This returns no calendar, so the Google API update may be called with an undefined `calendarId` and fail. It should fall back to the first/primary destination calendar.

title: Google deleteEvent may target primary calendar when actual destination is unknown
body: In `deleteEvent`, when `externalCalendarId` is missing the fallback again searches for `externalId === externalCalendarId` and yields undefined. The code then falls back to `primary`. If the event was created on a non-primary calendar, deletion will 404 and resolve without deleting the actual event, leaving stale calendar entries.

title: Google hangout-link patch can use undefined calendarId
body: `createEvent` inserts the event with `calendarId: selectedCalendar || 'primary'`, but the follow-up `events.patch` uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar`. If no selected calendar was found, the event is created on primary but the patch is sent with undefined calendarId, so updating the description with the hangout link can fail. Use the same fallback for the patch.

title: Lark createEvent always uses the first destination calendar
body: `LarkCalendarService.createEvent` ignores the credential being used and always takes the first entry of `event.destinationCalendar`. For collective events with multiple destination calendars, this can use a calendar belonging to another provider/host or fail when the first entry is not a Lark calendar. It should select the destination calendar matching the credential/integration.

title: Office 365 createEvent always uses the first destination calendar
body: `Office365CalendarService.createEvent` builds the Graph URL from the first entry of `event.destinationCalendar`. When multiple hosts have different calendars, this can target a non-Office external ID or the wrong host calendar, causing event creation to fail. It should choose the destination calendar associated with the credential being used.

title: CalDAV createEvent can silently skip event creation for secondary hosts
body: `BaseCalendarService.createEvent` filters calendars by the first destination calendar's `externalId`. If this service is invoked for a secondary host or the first destination is not in this CalDAV account, the filtered calendar list is empty and the method returns success without creating any event. This silently drops calendar events.

title: Recurring cancellation deletes only the first calendar reference per booking
body: For recurring cancellations, the code loops over all user calendar credentials and, for each updated booking, deletes only the first calendar reference it finds. With multiple host calendar references this leaves other hosts' events undeleted and also attempts deletes with credentials that may not own the reference. It should iterate all matching booking references and use their credential IDs.

title: `await apiDeletes` does not await deletion promises
body: In the paid cancellation branch, `apiDeletes` is an array of promises, but `await apiDeletes` awaits the array itself rather than its promises. The handler can return success before calendar deletions finish and will not catch their failures. Use `await Promise.allSettled(apiDeletes)` or equivalent.

title: Organization slug condition is inverted
body: The slug spread was changed from including `slug` when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is false to including it when true. This reverses the previous behavior: organizations get a slug in billing-enabled environments and no slug when billing is disabled, which can break organization creation/billing flows.

title: Breaking/inconsistent destinationCalendar payload change
body: Changing `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` from a single object/null to an array changes webhook/API payload shape. Handlers are also inconsistent: some emit `[]` while others can emit `null`. External consumers expecting the previous shape may break; this should be normalized or documented as a breaking change.

title: Webhook tests do not consistently cover new destinationCalendar shape
body: The test now expects `destinationCalendar: []` for BOOKING_REJECTED but still expects `null` for BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED. This inconsistency indicates the payload shape after the array change is not uniformly covered, and there are no automated tests for the collective multiple-host calendar behavior introduced by this PR.

title: Crash when destinationCalendar is missing/empty and location is Google Meet
body: In EventManager.create(), `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is destructured from `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is null/undefined/empty, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined, but the next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. This throws a TypeError for events with no destination calendar when the location is Google Meet, breaking booking creation/payment confirmation flows.

title: updateLocation creates calendar references from `createdEvent` instead of `updatedEvent`
body: In EventManager.updateLocation(), `referencesToCreate` maps all results and reads `result.createdEvent?.id`. Calendar results returned by `updateAllCalendarEvents()` are update results and populate `updatedEvent`, not `createdEvent`. Therefore calendar references are created with empty `uid`, `meetingId`, etc., which can create invalid/duplicate booking references and break later update/cancel operations.

title: updateLocation stores undefined credentialId/externalCalendarId for calendar references
body: In EventManager.updateLocation(), `referencesToCreate` uses `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`. Calendar update results produced by `CalendarManager.updateEvent()` do not include `externalId` or `credentialId` (only create results do). As a result, edited-location bookings can get calendar references with null/undefined credential and external calendar IDs, causing later reschedules/cancellations to use incorrect fallback logic or fail.

title: updateAllCalendarEvents can call updateEvent with an undefined credential
body: In EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents(), when a booking reference has `credentialId`, the code tries to find the credential in memory and then in the DB. If it is not found, or if the DB credential has no app slug, `credential` remains undefined, but the code still calls `updateEvent(credential, ...)`. `CalendarManager.updateEvent` expects a valid credential and will crash or reject when accessing credential fields.

title: Reschedule merge deletes only the first old calendar reference
body: In EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents(), when `newBookingId` is provided, the old calendar event deletion uses `booking.references.find(...)` and deletes only the first `_calendar` reference. With collective/multiple-host events there can be multiple calendar references; the remaining old calendar events are not deleted, leaving stale events on secondary host calendars after reschedule.

title: Google createEvent ignores destination externalId when credentialId is absent
body: GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() now selects the calendar only by matching `destinationCalendar.credentialId === credentialId`. For legacy destination calendars that have an `externalId` but no `credentialId`, no match is found and the code falls back to `primary`. Previous behavior used the stored `externalId`, so events may now be created in the wrong calendar.

title: Google createEvent patch can use undefined calendarId
body: In GoogleCalendarService.createEvent(), `selectedCalendar` may be undefined when no destination calendar matches the credential. The insert call safely uses `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the subsequent patch call uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar` without the fallback. This can issue a Google API patch request with an undefined calendarId.

title: Google updateEvent fallback cannot find a calendar and may pass undefined calendarId
body: In GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent(), if `externalCalendarId` is falsy the fallback searches `event.destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)`, i.e. it searches for `undefined`. This will not find a calendar, so `selectedCalendar` is undefined and `calendar.events.update` is called with an undefined `calendarId`, causing updates to fail when no external calendar ID is stored.

title: Google deleteEvent fallback may delete from primary instead of the intended calendar
body: In GoogleCalendarService.deleteEvent(), when `externalCalendarId` is absent the fallback searches destination calendars by the same absent value and then defaults to `primary`. If the event was created on a non-primary calendar and the reference lacks `externalCalendarId`, the delete request targets the wrong calendar.

title: Lark createEvent always uses the first destination calendar for all hosts
body: LarkCalendarService.createEvent() takes the first entry of `event.destinationCalendar` and ignores the credential for which the event is being created. In the new multiple-host flow, CalendarManager calls createEvent once per host credential; Lark will repeatedly try to create the event in the first host's calendar, which can fail for secondary credentials or miss the secondary host's calendar entirely.

title: Office365 createEvent always uses the first destination calendar for all hosts
body: Office365CalendarService.createEvent() uses only the first `destinationCalendar` entry to build `/me/calendars/{externalId}/events`. In collective events with multiple destination calendars, this means secondary host events are created against the main host's calendar ID using secondary credentials, which can fail or create events in the wrong calendar.

title: CalDAV createEvent can silently succeed without creating any calendar object
body: BaseCalendarService.createEvent() filters the account's calendars by the first destination calendar's `externalId`. When called for a secondary host credential whose calendars do not contain that externalId, the filtered list is empty, `Promise.all([])` resolves, and the method returns a successful NewCalendarEventType even though no event was created. This silently loses calendar events for secondary hosts.

title: Team destination calendars are dropped when organizer/eventType has no destination calendar
body: In handleNewBooking(), `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` when neither eventType nor organizer has a destination calendar. The later collective-event merge uses `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`, which is a no-op when the value is null. Therefore team member calendars are ignored exactly in the case where the organizer has no destination calendar, defeating the purpose of supporting multiple host calendars.

title: Organization slug condition appears inverted
body: The organization creation data changed from including `slug` when `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` to including it when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`. This reverses the previous behavior: organizations will get a slug only when team billing is enabled and no slug when billing is disabled. Unless this reversal is intentional, it will break organization slug handling for non-billing or billing environments.

title: Recurring cancellation ignores resolved credential and multiple calendar references
body: In handleCancelBooking(), when cancelling all remaining recurring events and a calendar reference has `credentialId`, the code resolves `calendarCredential` (possibly from DB) but then iterates only `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` to delete events. It also finds only the first `_calendar` reference on each updated booking. For collective/multiple-host bookings, credentials not present on the organizer user or secondary calendar references can be missed or deleted with the wrong credential, leaving stale calendar events.

title: Paid cancellation does not await calendar deletion promises
body: In the paid booking cancellation branch, the code does `await apiDeletes;` where `apiDeletes` is an array of promises. Awaiting the array does not await the contained promises, so the handler can return before calendar deletions finish and the try/catch will not catch deletion failures. It should await `Promise.all` or `Promise.allSettled` on `apiDeletes`.

title: Webhook secret is compared with ===
body: The endpoint authenticates requests by comparing the incoming header to process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET using JavaScript equality. String equality can short-circuit and may be vulnerable to timing analysis, allowing an attacker to gradually infer the secret. Use crypto.timingSafeEqual on fixed-length buffers after verifying both values exist.

title: Credential upsert is not atomic and can create duplicates
body: The handler searches for an existing credential with findFirst and then creates or updates it in separate queries. There is no transaction or unique constraint on (userId, appId). Concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user/app can both miss an existing row and insert duplicates, or if duplicates already exist findFirst may update an arbitrary row. This can leave users with multiple/stale credentials and app adapters may use the wrong one.

title: Malformed webhook payloads cause unhandled errors
body: appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse, symmetricDecrypt, and JSON.parse can all throw. The handler does not catch these errors, so malformed payloads produce an unhandled 500 instead of a 400. These should be caught and returned as validation errors.

title: Webhook accepts all HTTP methods
body: The API route does not check req.method, so any HTTP method is processed. It should only accept POST, or the documented method, and return 405 for others.

title: minimumTokenResponseSchema is not a valid permissive Zod schema
body: The schema uses computed keys such as [z.string().toString()] to try to allow arbitrary properties. This creates literal property names from the schema's string representation rather than a catchall or record schema, so it will either require nonsensical keys or strip expected fields such as expires_in. In app-credential syncing mode this can reject valid token responses or remove expiry data before saving credentials.

title: Missing refresh_token is replaced with literal placeholder
body: If a token response does not include refresh_token, the code sets it to the literal string 'refresh_token'. This placeholder can be persisted into credential.key and later sent to OAuth providers, making future refreshes fail and corrupting the credential. Missing refresh tokens should preserve the existing refresh token or mark the credential invalid, not insert a fake value.

title: parseRefreshTokenResponse throws despite callers expecting safeParse result
body: The helper calls safeParse but then throws an Error when validation fails, while several callers still check .success to handle invalid tokens gracefully. This changes the contract and turns recoverable invalid-token responses into unhandled exceptions or bypasses intended error handling in apps such as Zoom and Salesforce.

title: Sync path returns a fetch Response while callers expect parsed tokens
body: When credential syncing is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT. Existing callers are written to receive the same type as the provider refresh function: Google expects a response object with .data, HubSpot expects a parsed token object with accessToken/expiresIn, and Zoho Bigin/ZohoCRM expect an AxiosResponse with .data. In sync mode these callers will read undefined properties, compute NaN expiries, or throw TypeErrors, breaking token refresh for those apps.

title: Zoho Bigin sends credential ID as calcomUserId
body: refreshOAuthTokens is called with credentialId, the credential's primary key, as the third argument. refreshOAuthTokens then sends that value as calcomUserId to the credential sync endpoint. The sync endpoint will receive a credential ID instead of the Cal.com user ID, so it can return tokens for the wrong user or fail. credential.userId should be passed instead.

title: prisma is used but never imported
body: The new token-refresh code calls prisma.credential.update, but the file does not import prisma from @calcom/prisma. This will cause a ReferenceError at runtime, and likely a TypeScript/build error, whenever Salesforce credential refresh is attempted.

title: Salesforce connection is created with the old access token after refresh
body: getClient refreshes the Salesforce token and stores the new token in the database, but then returns a jsforce.Connection using credentialKey.access_token and credentialKey.instance_url from the old credential object. The newly fetched access token is not used, so if the old token was expired the next API calls still fail. Use the parsed refresh response's access_token and instance_url.

title: Salesforce client refreshes token on every instantiation
body: getClient performs an OAuth token refresh every time a SalesforceCalendarService is constructed, regardless of whether the existing access token is still valid. Calendar operations instantiate services frequently, which can cause unnecessary calls to Salesforce, rate limiting, and increased latency. The token expiry should be checked before refreshing.

title: Zoho CRM token validity check is inverted
body: isTokenValid treats expiryDate < Date.now() as valid, which is true only after the token has expired. getToken resolves without refreshing when isTokenValid is true and refreshes when it is false, so expired tokens are used and unexpired tokens trigger refreshes. The expiry is also set using Date.now() + 60 * 60, which is only a few seconds in milliseconds, making the problem worse.

title: Credential sync request has no authentication or signature
body: The POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT only sends calcomUserId and appSlug; it does not include a shared secret, signature, or other authentication. If the sync endpoint is reachable, it may be possible to request or rotate tokens based on unauthenticated requests. Add a configurable secret/signature header and verify it on the external app store.

title: No automated tests for privileged credential-sync webhook
body: The PR introduces a webhook that can create or update arbitrary user credentials, plus multiple token-refresh code paths, but no tests are included. At minimum, tests should cover secret verification, disabled feature behavior, malformed or undecryptable payloads, duplicate credential handling, and sync-enabled refresh flows.

title: Minimum token schema uses invalid computed keys and is not a catch-all
body: The minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed object keys like [z.string().toString()]. This does not create a Zod catch-all for arbitrary expiry fields; it creates fixed, meaningless property keys and leaves the object schema to strip unknown fields. When credential sync is enabled, valid token responses containing expires_in, expiry_date, instance_url, or refresh_token can fail validation or be reduced to only access_token, causing corrupted saved credentials.

title: Placeholder refresh_token is written when response omits it
body: If a refreshed token response does not include refresh_token, the code assigns the literal string 'refresh_token' to refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token. Many OAuth providers omit refresh_token on refresh and expect the existing refresh_token to be preserved. Callers that merge or save this parsed data can overwrite the real refresh token with an invalid placeholder, breaking future refreshes.

title: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns validation wrapper, not parsed token
body: The function returns the Zod SafeParse result object rather than the parsed token data. Callers must remember to use .data. At least one caller stores the returned object directly as the credential key, persisting a wrapper like { success, data } instead of the actual OAuth token fields.

title: Sync mode returns a fetch Response to callers expecting provider-specific objects
body: When credential sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT. Existing callers expect different response shapes: Google expects a Gaxios-like response with .data, HubSpot expects an SDK token object, and Zoho Bigin/ZohoCRM expect Axios responses with .data. This mismatch causes runtime TypeErrors, undefined token fields, or malformed credential updates.

title: Google Calendar stores Zod validation wrapper as credential key
body: In refreshAccessToken, parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a SafeParse result, but the returned value is passed directly to prisma.credential.update as key. The stored credential becomes a wrapper object containing success and data instead of the actual access/refresh token fields, so subsequent Google Calendar authentication will fail.

title: Google Calendar refresh assumes sync response has .data
body: With app credential sync enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but GoogleCalendarService reads res?.data and then token.access_token. A fetch Response has no .data property, so token is undefined and refreshing Google credentials throws an exception.

title: HubSpot refresh treats sync fetch Response as HubSpot token object
body: When sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but HubSpotCalendarService casts it to HubspotToken and reads properties such as accessToken and expiresIn. Those properties do not exist on a fetch Response, resulting in undefined tokens, NaN expiry values, and a broken HubSpot integration.

title: Zoho Bigin sends credential ID as calcomUserId
body: refreshOAuthTokens is called with credentialId as the third argument. That value is the credential primary key, not the Cal.com user ID. The sync endpoint therefore receives the wrong identifier as calcomUserId and cannot reliably sync tokens for the intended user.

title: Zoho Bigin refresh expects Axios .data but sync returns fetch Response
body: In sync mode, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but the Zoho Bigin refresh code accesses tokenInfo.data.error and mutates tokenInfo.data. Since a fetch Response has no .data property, this will throw or store undefined token data.

title: ZohoCRM refresh expects Axios .data but sync returns fetch Response
body: When sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but ZohoCRM code checks zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error and reads zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.access_token. A fetch Response has no .data property, causing token refresh to fail or corrupt the credential record.

title: Salesforce service uses prisma without importing it
body: The added Salesforce refresh code calls prisma.credential.update, but the file does not import prisma from @calcom/prisma. This will fail TypeScript compilation or throw a ReferenceError at runtime.

title: Salesforce connection is built with stale access token after refresh
body: getClient refreshes the Salesforce access token and updates the database, but then returns a jsforce.Connection using credentialKey.access_token from the old credential object instead of the newly parsed access token. The current service instance continues to use the stale or expired token.

title: Salesforce refresh checks statusText instead of response.ok
body: The Salesforce token refresh treats a response as failed when response.statusText is not 'OK'. Many HTTP/2 or serverless fetch implementations return an empty statusText even for successful responses. The code should use response.ok to avoid rejecting valid token responses.

title: Salesforce token parsing loses instance_url when sync mode is enabled
body: parseRefreshTokenResponse switches to the generic minimum schema when credential sync is enabled. That schema does not preserve Salesforce-specific fields such as instance_url. Saving the parsed result can remove instance_url from the credential, making future Salesforce API calls impossible to route correctly.

title: Credential sync update does not clear invalid flag
body: When an existing credential is updated, only key is written. If the credential was previously marked invalid, for example after an invalid_grant error, syncing new valid keys does not make it usable again. The update should also set invalid: false.

title: Credential upsert is not atomic and can create or leave duplicates
body: The webhook uses findFirst and then creates or updates the credential outside a transaction. Concurrent webhook calls for the same user/app can both create credentials, producing duplicates. If duplicate credentials already exist, only one arbitrary row is updated, leaving other credentials stale.

title: Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time equality
body: The webhook secret header is compared using !==. For shared secrets, a constant-time comparison such as crypto.timingSafeEqual is preferable to reduce timing side-channel leakage.

title: Encryption key generation instruction does not produce a 32-byte AES-256 key
body: The comment says CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY must be 32 bytes but suggests openssl rand -base64 24, which produces 18 random bytes encoded as 24 base64 characters. This can cause AES-256 decryption failures. The documentation should specify a command that produces 32 bytes, such as openssl rand -base64 32 or openssl rand -hex 32 depending on the expected encoding.

title: Outgoing credential sync request has no authentication or signing
body: The POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT includes calcomUserId and appSlug but provides no shared secret, signature, or other authentication mechanism. The receiving endpoint cannot verify that the request originated from Cal.com. If the endpoint is reachable publicly, an attacker could attempt to retrieve or refresh credentials.

title: Zoom refresh can store NaN expiry when sync response omits expires_in
body: In sync mode, parseRefreshTokenResponse may use the generic minimum schema, which can strip expires_in from the response. The Zoom code then computes key.expiry_date = Math.round(Date.now() + newTokens.expires_in * 1000). If expires_in is undefined, expiry_date becomes NaN, breaking later token validity checks.

title: Invalid webhook payloads and decryption failures are unhandled
body: Zod parsing, symmetricDecrypt, and JSON.parse can all throw, and the handler does not restrict HTTP methods or catch these errors. Malformed requests will result in unhandled exceptions and 500 responses instead of explicit 400/405 responses.

title: No automated tests for credential sync webhook and refresh overrides
body: This PR adds a security-sensitive webhook and changes token refresh behavior across many app adapters, but no automated tests are included. Tests should cover webhook secret validation, encrypted payload handling, credential create/update behavior, invalid-flag reset, and sync-mode refresh behavior for affected apps.

title: Minimum token schema uses invalid computed object keys
body: The minimum OAuth token schema uses computed keys like [z.string().toString()], which evaluate to a literal string key rather than creating a Zod record/catchall. This means the schema does not accept arbitrary OAuth token fields and will reject normal refreshed token responses when app credential sharing is enabled, causing token refresh failures across affected apps.

title: Placeholder refresh_token can overwrite real refresh token
body: If a refreshed token response does not include refresh_token, the code sets refresh_token to the literal string "refresh_token". Callers that spread this parsed data into stored credentials, such as Office 365 and Zoom, can overwrite the real refresh token with this placeholder, permanently breaking future OAuth refreshes for that credential.

title: App-specific token validation is bypassed whenever sync is enabled
body: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, parseRefreshTokenResponse ignores the app-specific schema for every credential, even when refreshOAuthTokens falls back to the normal refresh path, such as for team credentials. This skips required app-specific validation and transforms, for example Office 365's expires_in conversion, and can store unusable credential keys.

title: Google refresh assumes response.data but sync returns fetch Response
body: refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response when credential sync is enabled, but GoogleCalendarService treats the result as a Google API response and accesses res?.data. In sync mode res.data is undefined, so accessing token.access_token throws and Google Calendar token refresh fails.

title: Google stores Zod SafeParse result instead of parsed credential key
body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod SafeParse result, but GoogleCalendarService assigns that whole return value to key and saves it in credential.key. Subsequent credential reads will fail googleCredentialSchema.parse because the stored key is wrapped with success/data instead of containing the raw OAuth credentials.

title: HubSpot treats sync fetch Response as parsed HubSpot token
body: When credential sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but HubspotCalendarService treats the return value as a parsed HubspotToken and reads expiresIn from it. This produces undefined/NaN expiry values and can store a Response-like object as the credential key, breaking HubSpot authentication.

title: Zoho Bigin refresh expects Axios response data but sync returns fetch Response
body: The normal Zoho Bigin refresh path returns an Axios response with a data property, but when credential sync is enabled refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response. The code then reads tokenInfo.data.error and mutates tokenInfo.data, which will throw or corrupt token handling for Zoho Bigin credentials.

title: Zoho CRM refresh expects Axios response data but sync returns fetch Response
body: The normal Zoho CRM refresh path returns an Axios response with a data property, but when credential sync is enabled refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response. The code then reads zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error and mutates zohoCrmTokenInfo.data, which will throw or corrupt token handling for Zoho CRM credentials.

title: Salesforce uses prisma without importing it
body: SalesforceCalendarService calls prisma.credential.update but does not import prisma. This will throw a ReferenceError at runtime whenever Salesforce credential refresh attempts to persist the new access token.

title: Salesforce forces a token refresh on every client construction
body: getClient performs an OAuth refresh-token request unconditionally, even if the stored access token is still valid. Because calendar service instances are created during normal event operations, this can generate excessive Salesforce token refresh requests, hit rate limits, and cause token rotation problems.

title: Salesforce does not use the credential sync refresh path
body: Unlike the other updated OAuth integrations, Salesforce refreshes directly against login.salesforce.com and never calls refreshOAuthTokens. When app credential sharing is enabled, Salesforce will not use CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT as the source of truth, defeating the purpose of the sync feature for this app.

title: Zoom refresh sends incorrect app slug to sync endpoint
body: refreshOAuthTokens is called with appSlug "zoomvideo", but the Zoom credential/app identifier used elsewhere is "zoom". A self-hosted sync endpoint may fail to identify the app or refresh the wrong integration because the payload contains the wrong app slug.

title: Credential sync helper returns raw response without a consistent contract
body: refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT without checking response.ok or parsing JSON, while callers expect different shapes: some expect a parsed token object, some an Axios response, and some a fetch Response. This inconsistency causes runtime crashes or corrupted credential updates in several app adapters and hides sync endpoint errors.

title: Webhook credential upsert is racy and can create duplicates
body: The webhook handler performs findFirst followed by update or create without a transaction or unique constraint. Concurrent webhook calls for the same user/app can both find no existing credential and create duplicate credentials, leading to unpredictable app behavior and future updates only touching one duplicate.

title: Credential sync update does not clear invalid flag
body: When updating an existing credential, the webhook only writes key. If the credential was previously marked invalid, for example after an invalid_grant refresh failure, the newly synced valid credential remains marked invalid and may continue to be unusable.

title: Webhook secret is compared with strict equality
body: The webhook secret header is compared to CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET using !== instead of a constant-time comparison. For a secret-protected endpoint that can write OAuth credentials, a constant-time comparison is safer against timing-based secret leakage.

title: Team permission check uses AND instead of OR
body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. This only allows users who are both team admin and team owner; team admins who are not owners are denied. The intended check appears to be admin OR owner, so the endpoint's authorization does not match the variable name and likely product intent.

title: Guest emails are not deduplicated or normalized before insert
body: The handler filters guests only against already-persisted attendees. It does not deduplicate the incoming guests array or normalize email casing. A request containing the same email twice, or case variants of an existing attendee email, can pass the filter and create duplicate attendee records and duplicate email sends. Server-side validation should dedupe and normalize emails rather than relying on the dialog.

title: Blacklist check can be bypassed by casing or whitespace
body: blacklistedGuestEmails is lowercased, but the incoming guest email is not lowercased or trimmed before the includes check. A blacklisted address submitted as `Foo@Example.com` or with surrounding whitespace can bypass the blacklist.

title: Emails are sent using the original guests list instead of the filtered list
body: sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the original input array after the handler has computed uniqueGuests. If the request included an existing attendee email, that attendee is treated as a new guest for email selection and can receive the wrong email; duplicates in the input can also cause duplicate emails. Pass the filtered/deduped new guest list instead.

title: Any attendee can modify the guest list
body: The permission check treats any attendee whose email matches the authenticated user's email as allowed to add guests. This lets a participant, not just the organizer/host, modify the guest list and trigger invitation emails to arbitrary addresses. Unless this is an explicit product decision, the endpoint should restrict this action to hosts/team admins.

title: Endpoint does not validate booking status
body: The handler fetches the booking but never checks its status or timing. The API can therefore add guests to cancelled, rejected, pending, or past bookings even if the UI hides the action. This can send notifications and update calendar events for bookings that should no longer be modified.

title: No limit on number of guest emails
body: guests is validated only as an array of email strings with no maximum length. An authenticated user can submit a very large array, causing a large createMany operation and mass email sending. Add a reasonable max length.

title: Organizer lookup can throw for bookings without a user
body: The organizer lookup uses `booking.userId || 0` with findFirstOrThrow. If a booking has no userId, for example in some team/round-robin cases, this queries user id 0 and throws a Prisma not-found error, producing a 500 instead of handling the missing organizer.

title: Attendees are persisted before calendar update without a transaction
body: Attendees are persisted with prisma.booking.update before calling eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees, and the whole operation is not transactional. If the calendar update fails, guests remain attached to the booking while the client receives an error, leaving Cal.com attendees and external calendar attendees inconsistent.

title: Add-guest emails ignore email-disable settings
body: sendAddGuestsEmails does not accept or check event-type email disable settings, unlike other email-sending helpers. Add-guests notifications will be sent even when standard host/attendee emails are disabled for the event type.

title: Invalid-email error state is not reset after successful submission
body: The mutation success handler closes the dialog and resets the email list but does not reset isInvalidEmail. If a previous submission failed validation and a later submission succeeds, reopening the dialog can still show the stale validation error.

title: Error toast fallback is never used
body: The error message is built with a template string that is always non-empty, so the fallback to t('unable_to_add_guests') never runs. Users may see a message like `undefined: ...` when no TRPC error code is present.

title: To address can be malformed for guests with empty name
body: New guest attendees are created with an empty name, and the email sets `to` to `${attendee.name} <${attendee.email}>`. This can produce a malformed display name such as ` <guest@example.com>`. Use the email address as a fallback when name is empty.

title: Hard-coded English tooltip
body: The remove-email tooltip content is hard-coded as 'Remove email' instead of using the translation hook, so it will not be localized.

title: No tests for the new add-guests endpoint
body: No automated tests are added for the new tRPC endpoint, including its permission logic, duplicate/blacklisted email handling, and email selection. These are security-sensitive paths that would benefit from regression tests.

title: Team permission check requires admin AND owner instead of admin OR owner
body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...)). The name and intended authorization logic imply that a team admin or team owner should be allowed. With &&, a team admin who is not an owner is denied, and depending on how isTeamOwner/isTeamAdmin classify roles, even some owners could be denied. This blocks legitimate team users from adding guests.

title: Any attendee can add guests to a booking
body: The handler grants permission if the authenticated user's email matches any attendee email on the booking. This means an invited guest who has a Cal.com account can add arbitrary additional guests, trigger emails, and update calendar attendees. Unless this is an explicit product decision, guest-management should be restricted to the organizer/host/team admins.

title: Guest emails are not normalized or deduplicated before insert
body: uniqueGuests uses strict equality against existing attendee emails and does not lowercase/normalize guest emails. It also does not remove duplicates within the incoming guests array. This allows duplicate attendee rows via case variations such as a@example.com and A@example.com, and it can bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS because the blacklist is lowercased while the incoming guest email is not.

title: Booking status is not validated before adding guests
body: The handler only checks that the booking exists and that the caller has permission. It does not reject cancelled or rejected bookings, and it does not consider whether the booking is in a state where adding guests is valid. API callers can therefore add guests to cancelled bookings and send incorrect emails/calendar updates.

title: Emails are sent for the original guests array instead of the guests actually added
body: After filtering to uniqueGuests and inserting only those attendees, the handler calls sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests). sendAddGuestsEmails uses newGuests.includes(attendee.email) to decide whether an attendee receives a full invite or an add-guest notification. If the request includes an existing attendee together with at least one new guest, the existing attendee will be treated as newly added and receive the wrong email. The handler should pass uniqueGuests, ideally normalized.

title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores event-type email disable settings
body: Unlike other email-sending helpers, sendAddGuestsEmails does not accept eventTypeMetadata and does not check eventTypeDisableHostEmail or eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail. Add-guests emails will therefore be sent even when the event type is configured to disable standard host or attendee emails.

title: No maximum length for guests array
body: ZAddGuestsInputSchema accepts an arbitrary-length array of email addresses. An authenticated user could submit thousands of guest emails, causing bulk database writes and mass email sending. Add a reasonable maximum length to the guests array.

title: Attendee creation is not atomic with the existing-attendee check
body: The handler reads booking.attendees, filters guests, then creates attendees in a separate update. There is no transaction or database-level uniqueness check preventing the same guest from being added by concurrent requests. Two simultaneous addGuests calls for the same email can both pass the filter and create duplicate attendee rows.

title: Calendar update uses the requesting user's credentials rather than the booking owner's credentials
body: The handler fetches booking.user.credentials but then constructs EventManager with ctx.user and credentials from getUsersCredentials(ctx.user). If a team admin or attendee who is not the booking owner adds guests, the requester may not own the calendar credential associated with the booking, so updateCalendarAttendees may fail or update the wrong calendar. The calendar update should use the booking owner/host credentials or the credential associated with the booking reference.

title: Team member add-guests email is rendered with the organizer as the attendee
body: OrganizerAddGuestsEmail can be sent to a team member via this.teamMember?.email, but renderEmail is called with attendee: this.calEvent.organizer. Any recipient-specific rendering such as greeting, locale, timezone, or time format may use the organizer instead of the actual team-member recipient. It should pass this.teamMember || this.calEvent.organizer.

title: Closing the dialog via onOpenChange does not reset form state
body: AddGuestsDialog passes onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}, which only toggles visibility. Closing via overlay or Escape does not reset multiEmailValue or isInvalidEmail; only the Cancel button does. Reopening the dialog can show stale emails or stale validation errors.

title: Validation error state is not cleared after a later valid submission
body: When validation fails, isInvalidEmail is set to true, but when a later submission validates successfully and calls addGuestsMutation.mutate, isInvalidEmail is not set back to false. If the mutation succeeds and the dialog is reopened, the validation error may be displayed before the user has done anything invalid.

title: Error toast fallback is unreachable and may display undefined
body: The error handler builds message as a template string: `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`. Because the template string is always truthy, the fallback t(unable_to_add_guests) is never used. If err.data?.code is undefined, users may see a toast beginning with undefined. Build the message conditionally.

title: Hard-coded English tooltip in MultiEmail
body: The remove-email control uses Tooltip content Remove email instead of a translated string. Non-English users will see English text. Add a locale key and use t.

title: No tests for addGuests authorization and edge cases
body: This PR adds a privileged mutation with permission checks, duplicate/case-sensitive email handling, blacklist filtering, email behavior, and calendar updates, but no automated tests are included. Tests should cover organizer/team permissions, attendee access, duplicate emails, case variations, cancelled bookings, and email selection.

title: Team admin/owner authorization uses AND instead of OR
body: In addGuestsHandler, isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...)). The variable name and access check intend to allow team admins OR team owners. Using && requires both checks to pass, so legitimate team admins or owners can be denied access. It also short-circuits the owner check when isTeamAdmin returns false.

title: Server does not de-duplicate guest emails
body: uniqueGuests filters only emails already attached to the booking or blacklisted; it does not remove duplicates from the incoming guests array, and the Zod schema does not enforce uniqueness. A direct API call with duplicate emails can create multiple attendee rows for the same booking, and concurrent requests can also create duplicates.

title: Email addresses are not normalized before duplicate/blacklist checks
body: Guest emails are compared to existing attendees and lowercased blacklist entries without being lowercased or trimmed first. Because email addresses are case-insensitive at least for the domain, Guest@Example.com can bypass a blacklist entry guest@example.com and can also be added as a duplicate of guest@example.com. Normalize emails before validation, persistence, and email sending.

title: No booking-status check before adding guests
body: The handler only verifies that the booking exists and that the caller has access. It does not reject cancelled, rejected, or otherwise inactive bookings. A direct API call can add attendees, attempt calendar updates, and send invitation emails for a cancelled or rejected event. The endpoint should restrict this mutation to appropriate active booking statuses.

title: Organizer lookup fails for bookings without a userId
body: The organizer is loaded with prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } }). If a booking has no userId, which the fallback suggests is possible, this queries user ID 0 and throws, producing a server error instead of handling the booking gracefully. The handler should either validate that a host exists or derive the organizer/team safely.

title: No capacity check for seat-limited events
body: The mutation adds attendees without checking booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot or the current attendee count. For event types with limited seats, a direct API call can overbook the booking by adding more attendees than the configured capacity.

title: No rollback if calendar update fails after attendees are added
body: Attendees are persisted before eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees is called. If the calendar update fails, the API returns an error but the added attendees remain in the database, leaving the booking record and external calendar inconsistent. Consider transactional handling, compensation, or at least validating/preparing external updates before persisting.

title: Emails are sent using the original input instead of filtered uniqueGuests
body: sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) passes the raw request emails rather than the normalized, de-duplicated uniqueGuests that were actually inserted. sendAddGuestsEmails uses that list to decide which attendees receive a full scheduled email versus a 'guests added' notification, so existing or blacklisted emails included in the request can cause the wrong email template to be sent.

title: Calendar update uses requester's credentials instead of booking owner's
body: EventManager is constructed with ctx.user and credentials from getUsersCredentials(ctx.user). When the caller is a team admin or an attendee rather than the booking owner, calendar updates may not have access to the organizer's calendar or may update the wrong calendar. The booking owner's credentials/references should be used when updating the booking's calendar event.

title: No limit on number or length of guest emails
body: guests: z.array(z.string().email()) has no max count and no per-email length limit. An authenticated client can submit a very large array, causing bulk attendee creation, many translation lookups, calendar updates, and mass email sending. Add a reasonable maximum array length and email string length.

title: Add-guest emails ignore email-disable settings
body: sendAddGuestsEmails does not accept or honor eventTypeMetadata disableStandardEmails settings, nor host/attendee email disabled flags, unlike other email-sending helpers. Event types configured to disable standard host or attendee emails will still send organizer and attendee emails when guests are added.

title: Error toast fallback is unreachable and can show 'undefined'
body: In onError, message is built as `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`. If err.data?.code is undefined, the toast displays 'undefined: ...'. Also, because the template string is always truthy, `message || t('unable_to_add_guests')` never falls back to the intended generic error message.

title: Dialog state is not reset when closed outside the Cancel button
body: The dialog resets multiEmailValue and isInvalidEmail only on Cancel or successful submission. Closing via Dialog onOpenChange, such as Escape or clicking outside, leaves previous email values and validation error state behind. isInvalidEmail is also not cleared when the user edits the email fields, so a stale error can remain visible after correction.

title: Hard-coded English tooltip 'Remove email'
body: The remove-email button tooltip uses the literal string 'Remove email' instead of a translated key. This UI text will not be localized. Add a locale key and use the translation function.

title: No tests for addGuests authorization and edge cases
body: This PR adds a privileged mutation that modifies attendees, calendars, and emails, but no tests are included for permission checks, duplicate/case-insensitive emails, blacklist filtering, inactive booking statuses, seat capacity, or email-template selection. These are high-risk paths that should be covered before merge.

title: Retry-count cleanup deletes workflow reminders too broadly
body: The deleteMany OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` is not scoped to SMS reminders or to unscheduled reminders.
