As written, any WorkflowReminder row (including EMAIL or WHATSAPP reminders, or a reminder that is already scheduled) will be deleted if its retryCount is greater than 1. This can delete data outside the intended SMS retry flow; the condition should include at least `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` and likely `scheduled: false`.

title: Retry count is incremented from a stale read instead of atomically
body: Both failure paths set `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value read before the SMS attempt. If two executions of this endpoint process the same reminder concurrently, the absolute writes can overwrite each other and the reminder may not reach the deletion threshold as intended. Use Prisma's atomic update, e.g. `retryCount: { increment: 1 }`, including in the catch block at line 195.

title: Reminders with an empty message or missing recipient never count as failed
body: The retry count is only incremented when `message?.length > 0 && sendTo` is true and scheduling fails. If `sendTo` is missing or the rendered message is empty, the reminder is skipped without incrementing `retryCount`, so it will be re-selected on every cron run until `scheduledDate` passes instead of being cleaned up by the new retry logic. These cases should either increment retryCount or be explicitly deleted/cancelled.

title: No tests cover the new retry/deletion behavior
body: The PR introduces destructive cleanup based on retryCount but no tests verify that failed SMS attempts increment the counter, that reminders are deleted only after the intended number of failures, and that the deletion query is correctly scoped. Without coverage, regressions in this background job could silently drop workflow reminders.

title: Retry-count cleanup is not limited to SMS reminders
body: In the initial deleteMany, the second OR branch only checks retryCount > 1. It is not scoped to method: WorkflowMethods.SMS or to unscheduled reminders, so any WorkflowReminder row (including EMAIL or WHATSAPP reminders, or already scheduled reminders) with retryCount greater than 1 will be deleted. This can delete records outside the SMS retry flow. Scope the retry condition to SMS reminders, for example by putting method: WorkflowMethods.SMS at the top level of the where clause or inside the retry branch.

title: Retry count increments use stale read value
body: Both failure paths update retryCount to reminder.retryCount + 1 using the value read before the SMS attempt. If overlapping cron executions or duplicate requests process the same reminder, they can read the same retryCount and write the same new value, losing increments and preventing deletion after two failures. Use Prisma's atomic increment, e.g. retryCount: { increment: 1 }, and consider claiming rows before processing.

title: Unsendable reminders are not counted as failures
body: When message is empty or sendTo is falsy, the code skips scheduling without incrementing retryCount or deleting the reminder. A reminder with a missing recipient or unrenderable message will therefore be picked up repeatedly until scheduledDate passes, instead of being stopped by the new retry limit. Treat this as a failure case or delete the reminder explicitly.

title: Cron authentication passes when CRON_API_KEY is undefined
body: The authentication check compares process.env.CRON_API_KEY with the supplied key. If CRON_API_KEY is not set and no key is supplied, both values are undefined, so process.env.CRON_API_KEY !== apiKey is false and the request is accepted. The handler should reject requests when the environment key is missing or empty, and compare against a configured secret.

title: Retry-count cleanup deletes workflow reminders of all methods
body: The deleteMany query deletes any WorkflowReminder with retryCount greater than 1 because the second OR branch does not include method: WorkflowMethods.SMS. This can delete EMAIL or WHATSAPP reminders, or any future reminder type, even though the PR only intends to stop retrying SMS reminders. Add a method filter to the retry-count branch or make method a top-level AND condition.

title: Error handler can abort the whole cron batch if retry-count update fails
body: In the catch block, the retry-count update is not protected. If the reminder was deleted by another process or the database update fails, this update throws and terminates the handler, preventing the remaining reminders in the batch from being processed. Use updateMany or wrap this update in its own try/catch.

title: All exceptions count toward the SMS retry limit
body: The catch block increments retryCount for any exception thrown while preparing the SMS, including transient database errors, metadata validation errors, or template errors. After two such errors the reminder is deleted, even if the SMS provider was never contacted or the failure is transient. Consider counting only SMS provider failures or using a separate failure-handling path for unexpected errors.

title: Retry count is updated with a stale value instead of an atomic increment
body: Both failure paths set retryCount to reminder.retryCount + 1 using the value read before the scheduling attempt. If the same reminder is processed concurrently or updated between read and write, increments can be lost. Use Prisma's atomic increment operation instead.

title: Reminders with no message or destination are retried forever
body: When message is empty or sendTo is falsy, the code skips scheduling and does not increment retryCount. Such reminders remain unscheduled and are re-fetched on every cron run until their scheduledDate passes, which defeats the retry-limit behavior for permanently unsendable reminders. Consider incrementing retryCount, marking them cancelled, or deleting them after a failure threshold.

title: Returned SQL condition is not always parenthesized and can compose incorrectly
body: getAuthorizationConditions can return an OR predicate for org/team scope, and getBaseConditions returns that auth condition unwrapped when there are no filters. If a caller adds more predicates, e.g. `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND startTime > x`, SQL operator precedence makes the extra predicate apply only to one side of the OR, potentially returning rows that should be filtered out. The service should return a fully parenthesized predicate, or wrap the final result in getBaseConditions, so the fragment is safe to embed alongside other conditions.

title: Public options type makes teamId optional for team scope
body: InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions makes `teamId` optional for every scope, and the constructor accepts this loose type. TypeScript callers can pass `{ scope: 'team', userId, orgId }` without `teamId`; Zod validation then fails, `options` becomes null, and all queries silently use `1=0`. The previous discriminated union type would have caught the missing `teamId` at compile time. Use a discriminated public type or surface validation errors.

title: Org scope skips org memberships when org has no child teams
body: In buildOrgAuthorizationCondition, `userIdsFromOrg` is only fetched when `teamsFromOrg.length > 0`, even though `teamIds` already includes the org id. For an organization with no child teams, org memberships are never loaded, so the generated condition only matches team bookings and excludes individual bookings for org members. Fetch memberships for `teamIds` regardless of whether child teams exist.

title: Exact SQL equality assertions depend on unordered repository result order
body: The org-scope test asserts exact Prisma.sql equality with arrays of team and user IDs in a specific order, but the service builds those arrays from repository queries without explicit ordering. The SQL semantics are unaffected by order, but the assertion can fail nondeterministically if rows are returned in a different order. Sort IDs in the service or compare normalized sets.

title: Breaking service API change without caller migration in this PR
body: The class removes the previous public `findMany` method and changes condition methods to return `Prisma.Sql` instead of Prisma where inputs. This is a breaking contract change for any existing caller of the service. If callers are expected to compose raw SQL now, they should be updated in this PR or the old API should be retained/deprecated.

title: Org scope ignores direct org memberships when there are no child teams
body: buildOrgAuthorizationCondition only fetches user memberships when teamsFromOrg.length > 0, even though teamIds always includes options.orgId. For an organization with no child teams, direct org memberships are skipped, so the condition only allows team bookings and excludes personal bookings of org members. When at least one child team exists, those same org memberships are included, making the authorization behavior inconsistent and potentially returning incomplete insights.

title: Org-scope expectation depends on unordered repository result order
body: The test expects Prisma.sql values containing teamIds and userIds in a fixed order, but the service builds those arrays from repository queries without explicit ordering. Since ANY array order is semantically irrelevant but toEqual compares array order, the test can be flaky if the database returns teams or memberships in a different order. Sorting the IDs before building the SQL or comparing unordered sets would be safer.

title: Database test does not exercise array ANY raw SQL conditions
body: The only $queryRaw execution uses the user-scope condition, which has no array parameters. The org and team authorization paths that use teamId = ANY(...) and userId = ANY(...) are only compared as Prisma.sql objects. If Prisma or the Postgres driver does not bind these array parameters as intended, the integration tests will not catch the failure despite this being a raw-SQL conversion.

title: Org/team raw SQL conditions are never executed against the database
body: The only actual database execution in this suite is the simple user-scope query. The org and team authorization paths generate array predicates and top-level OR conditions, but the tests only compare Prisma.sql fragment objects. That does not prove the generated SQL is valid or returns the correct rows. Add integration tests that execute getBaseConditions for team and org scopes against seeded bookings that should be included and excluded.

title: Public service API changed from findMany/Prisma where inputs to raw SQL fragments
body: The previous public findMany method is removed, and authorization/filter helpers now return Prisma.Sql instead of Prisma where input objects. Any existing consumer of InsightsBookingService will break unless updated. If this service is used elsewhere, callers need to be migrated in this change or a compatible query API should be preserved.

title: Org scope skips org-member individual bookings when the org has no child teams
body: buildOrgAuthorizationCondition always includes the org id in teamIds, but it only fetches membership user IDs when teamsFromOrg.length > 0. For an organization with no child teams, userIdsFromOrg becomes empty, so individual bookings from org members are excluded. If at least one child team exists, org memberships are included. This makes org-scope visibility inconsistent. Query memberships for the org id and child team ids unconditionally.

title: getBaseConditions can return an unwrapped top-level OR fragment
body: When there are no filter conditions, getBaseConditions returns authConditions directly. For org/team scopes this may be a top-level OR expression. If a caller composes the returned fragment with additional AND predicates, SQL operator precedence can change the meaning of the query. Return a parenthesized fragment or clearly document that the result must only be used as a complete WHERE clause.

title: Membership lookups do not use the injected Prisma client
body: The service receives a Prisma client and uses it for TeamRepository, but membership checks call static MembershipRepository methods without passing the injected client. If those static methods use a global/default client, authorization checks may run on a different connection, transaction, or read replica than the rest of the service. Pass the injected client to membership repository calls or confirm the static methods intentionally use the same client.

title: Delete-cache mutation does not invalidate connected calendars query
body: After `deleteCacheMutation` succeeds, the component only calls `onSuccess`. It does not invalidate `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` (unlike the disconnect mutation). In `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper`, `onChanged` is optional and may not refetch the query, so the cache status/timestamp can remain visible after the cache rows are deleted. Invalidate the connectedCalendars query or update its cache in `onSettled`.

title: Cache status query includes expired cache entries
body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups all `CalendarCache` rows for the credentials but does not filter `expiresAt >= now()`, while cache reads (`getCachedAvailability`) only use unexpired rows. The UI can therefore show a cache status and allow deleting cache data that is already expired and not being served. Filter by `expiresAt` if the status is meant to represent active cache.

title: Empty updateMany may not update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt
body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` calls `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` to bump `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`. Prisma `updateMany` with an empty data object is not a reliable way to update `@updatedAt` fields; if the timestamp update is needed, pass `{ updatedAt: new Date() }` explicitly. Otherwise this call is dead code and can be removed.

title: updateManyByCredentialId accepts relation-update input not supported by updateMany
body: `updateManyByCredentialId` types `data` as `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput`, which includes relation operations such as connect/disconnect. `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany` only supports scalar update-many inputs, so the repository signature can accept payloads that will fail at runtime. Use `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput` or `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUncheckedUpdateManyInput`.

title: Actions container renders empty space when dropdown is hidden
body: `CredentialActionsDropdown` returns `null` when there is no cache action and no disconnect action, but it is wrapped in a fixed-width `<div className="flex w-32 justify-end">`. This leaves an empty 8rem action area in list cards/alerts for delegation credentials or when modifications are disabled. Render the wrapper conditionally or move the width styling into the dropdown component.

title: Cache timestamp ignores user locale and time format
body: The cache status timestamp is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` regardless of the user's locale or time-format settings. Non-English users will see a US-formatted date/time. Use the user's locale (and time format/time zone preferences where available) instead of hardcoding en-US.

title: deleteCache throws generic Error instead of TRPCError
body: When the credential is missing or access is denied, the handler throws a plain `Error`. tRPC will treat this as an internal error rather than a structured NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN error, making client handling and user-facing messages harder. Use `TRPCError` with an appropriate code.

title: credentialId validation allows non-integer numbers
body: The `deleteCache` input validates `credentialId` only as `z.number()`. Credential IDs are integers; accepting floats can pass validation and then produce unexpected Prisma behavior. Use `z.number().int()`.

title: Existing CalendarCache rows are backfilled with migration timestamp
body: Adding `updatedAt` with `DEFAULT NOW()` sets every existing cache row to the deployment/migration time. The new UI will show legacy cache entries as recently updated even though their contents may be much older. If accurate status matters, backfill from a meaningful timestamp or treat pre-existing rows specially.

title: dev:cron uses npx tsx without declaring tsx dependency
body: The script changed from `ts-node` to `npx tsx`, but `tsx` is not listed as a devDependency. `npx` may prompt to download the package or fail in offline/CI environments. Add `tsx` to devDependencies or keep an already-installed runner.

title: ENV_FILE path is relative to current working directory
body: `ENV_FILE="../.env"` depends on where the script is executed. Running `scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` from the repository root will target the parent directory of the repo, not the repo root. Resolve the path relative to the script location (e.g. `$(dirname "$0")/../.env`).

title: sed invocation is macOS-only
body: `sed -i '' -E ...` uses BSD/macOS in-place syntax. On GNU/Linux, `sed` interprets the empty string as a backup filename and the command fails. Use a portable approach or detect the platform.

title: Delete-cache mutation does not invalidate connected calendars query
body: The deleteCache mutation's onSuccess only calls the optional onSuccess callback. It does not invalidate `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, unlike the disconnect mutation. In SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper, `onChanged` may be undefined, so after deleting cache the UI can continue to display the old `cacheUpdatedAt` until a manual refetch. Invalidate the connectedCalendars query after deletion.

title: Cache timestamp ignores user locale
body: The cache timestamp is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US")`, hardcoding English formatting even though the component uses `useLocale`. Non-English users will see an en-US date/time format. Use the active locale or a localized date formatter.

title: Empty actions container rendered when CredentialActionsDropdown returns null
body: The wrapper always wraps CredentialActionsDropdown in `<div className="flex w-32 justify-end">`. When the dropdown returns null (for example, a delegation credential with no cache or connection modification disabled), the empty div still occupies layout space in AppListCard/Alert actions. Render the container only when actions are present or move it inside the dropdown component.

title: Disabled scope is not propagated to credential actions
body: The wrapper computes `shouldDisableConnectionModification = isDisabled || disableConnectionModification`, but passes only `disableConnectionModification` to ConnectedCalendarList. When the current scope is disabled, CredentialActionsDropdown can still show and execute disconnect/delete-cache actions. Pass `shouldDisableConnectionModification` if the disabled scope is meant to prevent modifications.

title: Cache status query includes expired CalendarCache rows
body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups all CalendarCache rows for the credential without filtering `expiresAt`. Since `getCachedAvailability` only uses rows where `expiresAt >= now`, expired rows can still make the UI show a cache status and delete action. Add an `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` filter if the status should represent active cache.

title: Delete-cache authorization does not account for delegation credentials shown in UI
body: The UI shows delete-cache for Google calendars with a cache timestamp even when `delegationCredentialId` is present, but the handler only allows credentials where `userId` equals the session user. If the underlying credential is a delegation/team credential not owned by the user, the mutation fails despite the UI offering the action. Handle delegation credentials or align UI visibility with authorization.

title: Cache refresh updates all SelectedCalendar rows for the credential
body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` calls `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})`, which touches every selected calendar under the credential, including event-type-level rows not part of the calendars just cached. If the only purpose is to bump `updatedAt`, this creates unnecessary writes/timestamp churn; scope the update to affected calendars or remove it if unused.

title: UserWithCalendars type now requires additional selected-calendar fields
body: Adding `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` to `allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` changes the shape of a type exposed through the legacy `getConnectedDestinationCalendars` export. External or platform consumers constructing this object with only the previous fields will break. If intentional, document it; otherwise consider making the new fields optional or updating consumers.

title: dev:cron uses npx tsx without a pinned/installed dependency
body: The script was changed to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, but `tsx` is not in dependencies/devDependencies. This makes the dev script depend on npx downloading an unpinned package at runtime, which can fail offline and is nondeterministic. Add `tsx` as a devDependency or pin the version.

title: Webhook test script uses CWD-relative env path and macOS-only sed
body: `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved from the current working directory, so running `scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` from the repo root writes to the parent directory rather than the repo env file. The script also uses `sed -i ''`, which is BSD/macOS syntax and fails on GNU/Linux. Resolve the env file relative to the script/repo root and use portable sed invocation.

title: No automated tests for deleteCache authorization and deletion
body: The new deleteCache handler contains authorization logic and deletes CalendarCache rows, but the PR adds no tests covering unauthorized credential IDs, non-existent credentials, or successful deletion. Add handler/repository tests to prevent regressions in access control and cache deletion.

title: Deleting cache does not refresh connected calendars
body: The deleteCache mutation only shows a toast and calls onSuccess; it never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. After a successful deletion the tRPC cache still contains the old cacheUpdatedAt, so the dropdown continues to display the stale timestamp and may still show Delete cached data until a manual refetch. Invalidate the connectedCalendars query, preferably in onSuccess or onSettled.

title: Cache status includes expired cache rows
body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups CalendarCache rows without an expiresAt filter, while getCachedAvailability only serves rows where expiresAt >= now. Expired cache rows therefore still produce a cacheUpdatedAt value, causing the UI to report an active cache status and last-updated time for data that will not be used. Add expiresAt: { gte: new Date() } to the where clause.

title: Empty updateMany may not bump SelectedCalendar.updatedAt
body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) to touch SelectedCalendar.updatedAt. An empty Prisma updateMany payload is fragile: depending on Prisma behavior it may fail validation or not update the timestamp, defeating the stated intent and potentially causing webhook/cron errors. Pass an explicit updatedAt value, for example { updatedAt: new Date() }, and type the repository method with SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput.

title: Cache deletion authorization only handles directly owned credentials
body: deleteCacheHandler authorizes only credentials where userId equals the requesting user. Connected calendars can include delegated credentials, as shown by the UI passing delegationCredentialId, and those may not be directly owned by the user. If such a credential has cache entries, the UI can show Delete cached data but the mutation will fail. Use the same access logic as credential deletion or explicitly authorize delegated/team credentials, and return a TRPC FORBIDDEN/NOT_FOUND error rather than a generic Error.

title: credentialId input should be an integer
body: The input schema uses z.number(), which accepts floating-point values, but credential IDs are integer primary keys. Use z.number().int(), and optionally positive, so malformed input is rejected before reaching Prisma.

title: Cache timestamp is always formatted with en-US
body: The cache timestamp is formatted with Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US') even though the component uses useLocale. Non-English users will see a US locale format. Use the active locale when creating the formatter.

title: dev:cron depends on undeclared tsx runtime
body: dev:cron now runs npx tsx cron-tester.ts, but tsx is not declared as a devDependency. This makes the script depend on npx downloading tsx at runtime, which is non-reproducible and can fail offline or in CI. Add tsx to devDependencies or keep using the already declared ts-node.

title: Webhook test script is not portable and uses fragile env path
body: The helper script uses BSD/macOS-specific sed -i '' and assumes ENV_FILE='../.env' relative to the current working directory. On Linux the sed command fails, and when run from the repository root the env path points outside the repo. Use a repo-root-relative .env path and a portable sed invocation.

title: Booking cancellation does not await workflow reminder cancellations
body: handleCancelBooking cancels workflow reminders by calling async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder inside nested forEach loops and never awaits the returned promises or includes them in the request's awaited promises. The handler can return before SendGrid/Twilio cancellations and Prisma updates/deletes finish; in serverless deployments the unfinished work may be terminated. As a result, reminders for cancelled bookings can still be sent, which is the exact issue this PR is trying to fix.

title: Reschedule endpoint does not await old reminder cancellations
body: In requestReschedule, bookingToReschedule.workflowReminders.forEach calls async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder without awaiting them. The tRPC mutation can complete before the old booking's reminders are actually marked cancelled/deleted or canceled with the provider, so old reminders may still be delivered.

title: Rescheduled booking reminder cancellation is fire-and-forget and bypasses deferred cancel
body: handleNewBooking cancels the original booking's reminders in a forEach without awaiting the async calls, so the surrounding try/catch cannot catch failures and the request may finish before cancellation completes. It also passes immediateDelete=true for email reminders; if the immediate SendGrid cancellation fails, no cancelled flag or DB cleanup is left for retry. Old reminders from a rescheduled booking can therefore still be sent.

title: Workflow deletion cancels scheduled emails fire-and-forget before cascade delete
body: In the workflow delete mutation, scheduledReminders.forEach calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., true)/deleteScheduledSMSReminder without awaiting. The workflow is then deleted, cascading away WorkflowReminder rows. If the external SendGrid/Twilio cancellation does not complete or fails, there is no DB state left to retry, and scheduled emails/SMS for the deleted workflow may still be sent.

title: Workflow update cancels reminders without awaiting provider/DB operations
body: When removing event types from a workflow, and similarly when deleting/editing steps around lines 519 and 574, the update mutation calls async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder inside forEach without awaiting. The mutation can return before reminders are marked cancelled or canceled, and errors are swallowed. Stale reminders may remain active and be sent.

title: Cron authentication can pass when CRON_API_KEY is unset
body: The cron handler compares process.env.CRON_API_KEY with the supplied apiKey using strict inequality. If CRON_API_KEY is not configured, both sides are undefined for a request with no key, so the endpoint is accessible without authentication. This endpoint can cancel and schedule workflow emails, so it should require a configured CRON_API_KEY and reject unauthenticated requests.

title: Cron cancellation query is too broad and can include rows without a SendGrid batch id
body: scheduleEmailReminders selects remindersToCancel only by cancelled=true and scheduledDate. It does not filter method=EMAIL, scheduled=true, or referenceId not null. The loop then sends reminder.referenceId as batch_id to SendGrid. A row with a null/invalid referenceId, or a non-email reminder if cancelled is ever set, can make the request fail; due to the surrounding error handling, that can prevent other valid cancellations from being processed.

title: A single failure aborts the whole cron cancellation loop
body: The cancellation logic awaits each SendGrid request inside one try/catch around the whole for loop. If any request throws, such as from rate limiting, a network error, or an invalid batch id, control jumps to catch and the remaining reminders are neither canceled in SendGrid nor deleted from WorkflowReminder. Those reminders can still be sent. Each reminder should be canceled with independent error handling.

title: Cron may schedule stale reminders without checking booking status or cancelled flag
body: The unscheduledReminders query filters only method=EMAIL, scheduled=false, and scheduledDate. It does not exclude cancelled=true rows and does not require the related booking to still be ACCEPTED. If a reminder row remains after a booking is cancelled/rescheduled, which is possible because cancellation calls are fire-and-forget or can race, the cron will schedule and send an email for that booking.

title: immediateDelete cancels SendGrid but leaves no reliable DB state
body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder's immediateDelete branch posts a cancellation to SendGrid and returns without deleting the WorkflowReminder row or marking cancelled=true. In reschedule flows this leaves stale scheduled reminder rows. More importantly, if the SendGrid call fails, the function catches/logs and returns success, so there is no retryable state and the originally scheduled email may still be sent.

title: Paid booking cancellation returns before cancelling workflow reminders
body: In handleCancelBooking, the paid branch refunds the booking, updates it to REJECTED, and returns before the later code that cancels workflow reminders. Therefore cancelled paid bookings can retain scheduled workflow reminders. Since the PR is intended to stop reminders for cancelled bookings, this early return should also perform the reminder cancellation or move cancellation before the return.

title: Reminder cancellations are fire-and-forget in booking cancellation
body: The cancellation loop calls async deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder but never awaits the returned promises. The request can return before the database update setting cancelled=true or the Twilio cancellation completes, especially in serverless environments where the function may be frozen after the response. As a result, reminders for cancelled bookings can still be sent.

title: Reschedule endpoint does not await reminder cancellations
body: In requestReschedule, workflow reminder cancellations are started inside forEach without collecting or awaiting the promises. The mutation can complete before the reminder rows are marked cancelled or external SMS/email cancellations finish, so reminders for the rescheduled/cancelled booking may still be delivered.

title: Workflow deletion cancels external reminders without awaiting completion
body: When deleting a workflow, scheduled reminder cancellations are fired in a forEach and then the workflow is deleted immediately. Because the cancellation promises are not awaited, the workflow and its reminder rows can be deleted before SendGrid/Twilio cancellation completes. If an external cancellation fails, there may be no reminder row left to retry from, and the scheduled message can still be sent.

title: Workflow update does not await step/reminder mutation promises
body: The update endpoint uses userWorkflow.steps.map(async ...) but never awaits the resulting promises. Step deletion/update, reminder cancellation, and creation of replacement reminders may continue after the mutation returns. This can leave the workflow partially updated and can silently drop cancellation or scheduling work if the process ends.

title: Reschedule cancellation uses immediate SendGrid cancel but leaves no retryable DB state
body: For a reschedule, previous email reminders are cancelled with deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., true). That immediateDelete path only calls SendGrid and returns without deleting the WorkflowReminder or setting cancelled=true. The loop is also not awaited. If the SendGrid cancellation fails or the request ends before it completes, there is no cancelled flag for the cron job to retry, so the old booking's reminder can still be sent.

title: One failed SendGrid cancellation aborts cancellation of all remaining reminders
body: The cancellation loop awaits each SendGrid request inside a single try/catch. If any one reminder has an invalid or null referenceId, or if the SendGrid call fails, execution jumps to the catch block and the remaining reminders are not processed. The queued prisma.workflowReminder.delete promises are also not awaited in that failure path, so valid cancellations can be skipped entirely.

title: Cancelled-reminder query does not ensure a SendGrid batch reference exists
body: remindersToCancel is selected only by cancelled=true and scheduledDate. It does not filter method=EMAIL, scheduled=true, or referenceId not null, but the following code unconditionally posts reminder.referenceId to SendGrid. A cancelled reminder without a SendGrid batch ID, or a non-email reminder with unexpected cancelled state, can cause an API error and block cancellation of subsequent reminders.

title: Paid booking cancellation returns before cancelling workflow reminders
body: The refund branch for paid bookings returns before the later updatedBookings.forEach blocks that cancel scheduled jobs and workflow reminders. A paid booking that is cancelled/refunded, with status changed to REJECTED, can therefore leave workflow reminders active and still trigger reminder emails or SMS.

title: immediateDelete cancels SendGrid but does not delete or mark the reminder row
body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder with immediateDelete=true cancels the SendGrid batch but does not delete the WorkflowReminder row or set cancelled=true. Callers such as the reschedule flow rely on this to cancel old reminders. If the external cancellation fails, the database contains no state indicating cancellation, so there is no retry or cleanup path.

title: Deferred cancellation can miss reminders scheduled to send soon
body: The cron job only cancels reminders whose scheduledDate is within the next hour and is described as running every 15 minutes. If a booking is cancelled or rescheduled less than 15 minutes before a reminder's scheduled send time, the cron may not run before SendGrid sends the email, so the reminder can still be delivered despite the cancellation.

title: Paid booking cancellation returns before cancelling scheduled reminders/jobs
body: The handler refunds paid bookings and returns before reaching the scheduled-job cancellation and workflow reminder cancellation code later in the function. As a result, cancelled/rejected paid bookings can keep active workflow reminders and scheduled jobs, so reminder emails/SMS may still be sent.

title: Workflow reminder cancellations are fired without being awaited
body: The cancellation loop calls async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder inside forEach but never collects or awaits the promises. The request can finish before SendGrid/Twilio cancellation and Prisma writes complete, especially in serverless environments, leaving reminders active or inconsistently cancelled.

title: Paid branch awaits an array instead of its promises
body: `await apiDeletes` awaits the array object, not `Promise.all(apiDeletes)`. Calendar/video deletion promises in the paid cancellation path are therefore not waited for, can reject as unhandled rejections, and external events may remain while the API reports success.

title: Reschedule path cancels old reminders without awaiting promises
body: originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach invokes async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder without awaiting them. The surrounding try/catch cannot catch asynchronous rejections, so the reschedule can complete before the old reminders are actually cancelled.

title: Reschedule uses immediate SendGrid cancellation without persisting cancellation state
body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder is called with immediateDelete=true for rescheduled bookings. That path only calls SendGrid and does not delete or mark the WorkflowReminder row. If the SendGrid call fails or is not awaited, there is no local cancelled state and no retry, so the old reminder can still be sent.

title: Deferred cancellation can miss reminders that occur before the next cron run
body: The non-immediate cancellation path only sets cancelled=true and relies on a cron job that runs every 15 minutes. If a booking is cancelled shortly before a reminder's scheduled time and the next cron run happens after that time, SendGrid can send the reminder before cancellation is applied.

title: Cancelled-reminder query does not restrict to scheduled email reminders with a batch ID
body: remindersToCancel finds all rows with cancelled=true and scheduledDate within an hour, without filtering method: EMAIL, scheduled: true, or referenceId not null. A cancelled SMS row or an email row without a SendGrid batch ID can cause invalid SendGrid requests and block processing of valid cancellations.

title: One failing SendGrid cancellation stops processing of all remaining cancellations
body: The try/catch surrounds the entire cancellation loop. If client.request throws for any reminder, the remaining cancelled reminders are neither cancelled nor deleted. A single bad or transient record can repeatedly prevent the cron job from cancelling any cancelled emails.

title: Unscheduled email reminders are scheduled without checking cancelled flag or booking status
body: The unscheduledReminders query filters only by method EMAIL, scheduled false, and scheduledDate. It does not exclude cancelled=true rows or verify that the associated booking is still accepted. Stale reminders for cancelled or rescheduled bookings can therefore be scheduled and emailed.

title: immediateDelete cancels SendGrid but does not update/delete the local reminder
body: When immediateDelete is true and referenceId exists, deleteScheduledEmailReminder sends a cancellation to SendGrid and returns without deleting the WorkflowReminder or setting cancelled. Unless the caller separately deletes the row after success, failed cancellations are not retried and local state no longer reflects the scheduled email.

title: Reschedule mutation cancels workflow reminders without awaiting them
body: bookingToReschedule.workflowReminders.forEach calls async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder but does not await the promises. The mutation can return before reminders are marked cancelled/deleted, so a cancelled/rescheduled booking may still have active reminders.

title: Workflow deletion cancels reminders asynchronously and then deletes the workflow
body: scheduledReminders.forEach starts SendGrid/Twilio cancellations without awaiting them, then the workflow is deleted. Cascade deletion can remove the local reminder records before provider cancellation completes; if cancellation fails or is interrupted, scheduled emails/SMS remain active and cannot be retried.

title: Cancellations for disabled event types are not awaited
body: In the workflow update mutation, remindersToDelete.flat().forEach calls async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder without awaiting them before deleting relationships and scheduling new reminders. Reminders for event types that are no longer active may remain active if the async work fails or terminates early.

title: Workflow update does not await processing of existing steps
body: userWorkflow.steps.map(async ...) creates promises for deleting/updating steps, cancelling old reminders, and scheduling replacements, but the promises are never awaited. The mutation can return before cancellations and scheduling finish, leaving old reminders active or new reminders missing.

title: No tests for new cancelled reminder cron/cancellation behavior
body: The PR introduces a new cancelled flag and cron-based cancellation logic but adds no automated tests verifying that cancelled/rescheduled bookings do not receive reminders, that the cron cancels only due cancelled emails, and that a failing cancellation does not block the queue.

title: All app-store imports are started eagerly, not lazily
body: The appStore object initializes every entry with import(...) at module load. Importing appStore therefore starts loading every app chunk, even if only one integration is used. This defeats much of the benefit of async imports and can increase startup/network cost. It also creates many promises that may never be awaited; if one dynamic import fails and that app is never used, the rejection may become unhandled. A lazy getter or function that imports only the requested app would be safer.

title: Dynamic import failures in getCalendar reject instead of returning null
body: getCalendar now awaits appStore[...] but does not catch errors from the dynamic import. Previously an unknown or unavailable calendar type could return null after a warning; now a rejected import throws. Callers such as CalendarManager.getCachedResults use Promise.all over getCalendar, so one broken app can fail all calendar availability requests. Wrap the import lookup in try/catch and return null, or otherwise handle the failure.

title: Async forEach does not await calendar/video deletions
body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...) starts asynchronous getCalendar/deleteEvent/deleteMeeting operations, but Array.prototype.forEach does not wait for the callbacks' promises. The surrounding try/catch will not catch rejections, and Reschedule can send the reschedule email and return before the external events are deleted. Use Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...)) or a for...of loop with await.

title: Async forEach does not await calendar/video deletions
body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...) starts asynchronous getCalendar/deleteEvent/deleteMeeting operations, but Array.prototype.forEach does not wait for the callbacks' promises. The surrounding try/catch will not catch rejections, and Reschedule can send the reschedule email and return before the external events are deleted. Use Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...)) or a for...of loop with await.

title: Reschedule mutation fires calendar/video deletions without awaiting them
body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...) performs awaited getCalendar and returns deleteEvent/deleteMeeting promises, but forEach ignores those promises. The mutation can complete, send emails, and call webhooks before external calendar/video events are deleted, and any deletion failure becomes an unhandled promise rejection. Use Promise.all or a for...of loop and await the deletions.

title: Async forEach can leave apiDeletes unpopulated and unawaited
body: The recurring-calendar cancellation branch uses .forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... apiDeletes.push(...) }). Because forEach does not await async callbacks, later code may reach await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) before apiDeletes is fully populated, so calendar deletions may not be awaited or may be skipped. Errors from those async callbacks are also unhandled. Use a for...of loop or collect promises with map and Promise.all.

title: Awaiting the apiDeletes array does not await its promises
body: In the paid cancellation path, await apiDeletes; awaits the array object, not the promises it may contain. The handler can return before calendar/video deletion promises settle, and rejections from those promises may become unhandled. It should be await Promise.all(apiDeletes), after ensuring apiDeletes is fully populated.

title: Async forEach is not awaited, so deletions and errors are not handled
body: The callback passed to bookingRefsFiltered.forEach is async. Array.prototype.forEach does not wait for the returned promises, so the surrounding try/catch cannot catch rejections from await getCalendar, calendar?.deleteEvent, or deleteMeeting. The reschedule flow can return and send emails before the calendar/video events are actually deleted, and failed deletions become unhandled promise rejections. Use await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...)) or a for...of loop.

title: Async forEach is not awaited, so deletions and errors are not handled
body: The callback passed to bookingRefsFiltered.forEach is async. Array.prototype.forEach does not wait for the returned promises, so the surrounding try/catch cannot catch rejections from await getCalendar, calendar?.deleteEvent, or deleteMeeting. The reschedule flow can return and send emails before the calendar/video events are actually deleted, and failed deletions become unhandled promise rejections. Use await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...)) or a for...of loop.

title: requestReschedule fires async deletion callbacks without awaiting them
body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach is given an async callback but the mutation never awaits the resulting promises. The request can complete before calendar/video events are deleted, and any rejection from await getCalendar, calendar?.deleteEvent, or deleteMeeting is unhandled. Use await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...)) or a for...of loop.

title: Recurring cancellation uses unawaited async forEach for calendar deletions
body: In the recurring-cancellation branch, bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async ...) is not awaited. The outer handler later awaits apiDeletes, but these callbacks may not have finished or even pushed their work yet, and any rejection is unhandled. The callback also awaits calendar?.deleteEvent and pushes the resolved value, so apiDeletes would not contain a promise for that deletion anyway. Use Promise.all over deletion promises or a for...of loop and await the results.

title: await apiDeletes does not await the promises in the array
body: In the paid-cancellation path, await apiDeletes awaits the array object rather than its contents. Any integration deletion promises stored in apiDeletes are not awaited before the handler returns, so the response can finish while calendar/video deletions are still pending and rejections may be missed. Use await Promise.all(apiDeletes).

title: Dynamic-import failure can bypass the Cal Video fallback in createMeeting
body: getVideoAdapters now performs dynamic imports and can reject if an app chunk fails to load. The await on getVideoAdapters is outside the try/catch that implements the fallback to Cal Video, so an import failure causes createMeeting to reject instead of falling back. Move this call inside the try block or catch the error and use the fallback path.

title: All app dynamic imports are started eagerly when appStore is imported
body: The appStore object literal evaluates import() for every app as soon as this module is imported. This starts loading all app modules even when only one app is needed, which defeats lazy code-splitting and may increase startup latency. If an unused app's import rejects, it may also become an unhandled rejection. If lazy loading is intended, expose functions or getters that call import() on demand.

title: getCalendar can reject on dynamic-import failure instead of returning null
body: await appStore[...] can reject if the dynamic import fails, but getCalendar only handles missing or invalid apps by returning null. Several callers, such as CalendarManager.createEvent, await getCalendar without try/catch, so a failed app import can throw and break booking creation instead of being treated as an unavailable calendar. Consider catching import failures in getCalendar and returning null with a warning.

title: Async forEach is not awaited when deleting calendar/video events
body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) starts asynchronous getCalendar/deleteEvent/deleteMeeting work, but the surrounding Reschedule function does not await those promises. The try/catch around forEach cannot catch async rejections, so the function sends the reschedule email and returns before external events are reliably deleted. Failed deletions can leave stale calendar/video events and cause unhandled promise rejections. Use Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...)) instead.

title: Async forEach is not awaited when deleting calendar/video events
body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) starts asynchronous getCalendar/deleteEvent/deleteMeeting work, but the surrounding Reschedule function does not await those promises. The try/catch around forEach cannot catch async rejections, so the function sends the reschedule email and returns before external events are reliably deleted. Failed deletions can leave stale calendar/video events and cause unhandled promise rejections. Use Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...)) instead.

title: requestReschedule does not await calendar/video deletion promises
body: In requestReschedule, bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) fires asynchronous calendar/video deletion operations without awaiting them. The mutation then sends the reschedule email and webhooks and returns while deletions may still be pending. Errors from those deletions are not handled and can become unhandled promise rejections. Use Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...)) and await it before continuing.

title: Recurring cancellation calendar deletions are not awaited or reliably collected
body: For recurring cancellations, the code calls credentials.filter(...).forEach(async ...), awaits getCalendar/deleteEvent inside the callback, and only then pushes the delete promise into apiDeletes. Because forEach does not await async callbacks, the handler can reach Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) before those promises are pushed, so calendar deletions may not be awaited or included at all. This can leave cancelled recurring events in external calendars and cause unhandled rejections. Use a for...of loop or Promise.all over mapped credentials and await the resulting promises.

title: Awaiting the apiDeletes array does not wait for integration deletions
body: In the paid cancellation branch, `await apiDeletes;` awaits the array object rather than the promises inside it. As a result, deleteMeeting/calendar delete operations may still be pending when the handler returns, and their rejections are not observed. Use `await Promise.all(apiDeletes)` to wait for all integration deletion promises.

title: Dynamic import failures bypass createMeeting's fallback handling
body: createMeeting awaits getVideoAdapters before the try/catch that handles broken video integrations and falls back to Cal Video. Since getVideoAdapters now performs dynamic imports from appStore, a rejected import throws before that try/catch, so the broken-integration email and Cal Video fallback do not run and booking creation can fail hard. Move the getVideoAdapters call into the try block or catch import failures and fall back.

title: getCalendar propagates dynamic import rejections instead of degrading gracefully
body: The awaited appStore lookup can reject if an app chunk fails to load. getCalendar does not catch this rejection, so callers such as CalendarManager.createEvent/updateEvent and booking cancellation flows can throw instead of treating the calendar as unavailable. For resilience, catch import errors, log them, and return null (or otherwise normalize the failure) where callers already handle missing calendars.

title: Video adapters are loaded sequentially
body: getVideoAdapters loops over credentials and awaits each appStore dynamic import one at a time. When multiple video credentials are present, this serializes module loading and delays availability checks, meeting creation, updates, and deletions. Use Promise.all to import the needed app modules concurrently.

title: Date override availability skips busy-time check
body: In checkIfIsAvailable, when dateOverrideExist is true and the slot is not rejected by the date-override predicate, the function returns true before executing the busy.every check. This means any busy time from bookings, calendars, or other sources is ignored for slots covered by a date override. A host who is already busy can still be shown as available, which can lead to invalid slot offers and double-booking risks.

title: Working-hours check rejects slots if any interval does not contain them
body: workingHours.find is used as if it detects whether a slot is outside working hours, but the callback returns true whenever the slot is outside the current working-hour interval. If a user has multiple working-hour intervals in one day, a slot inside one interval will be outside another interval and the whole check returns false, hiding valid availability. Conversely, if there is no working-hour entry for that weekday, the check falls through and treats the slot as available. The logic should require that at least one working-hour interval fully contains the slot.

title: Working-hours check ignores event duration
body: The end variable is computed from slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime. This checks only the start of the slot against working hours and allows slots whose end time falls after the working-hour boundary. As a result, events that begin inside availability but extend past it can be marked available.

title: Date-override containment allows partially overlapping slots
body: The date-override check only rejects slots that end before or exactly at the override start, or start after the override end. It does not reject slots that start before the override start or end after the override end. It also treats a slot starting exactly at the override end as valid because isAfter is used instead of an isSame-or-after boundary check. Therefore, slots that only partially overlap a date override can pass availability.

title: Multiple date overrides for the same day are not handled correctly
body: The dateOverrides.find callback sets dateOverrideExist as a side effect and returns true for the first override that the slot is outside. If a user has two date overrides on the same date, a slot inside the second override can be rejected because it is outside the first override, and find stops at that first rejection. Availability with multiple per-day overrides will be incorrect.

title: Dayjs objects compared with ===
body: The zero-length override check compares two dayjs instances with ===. This compares object identity and is always false for separately created dayjs objects. The intended start-equals-end handling will never trigger; use isSame() instead.

title: getSlots now relies on optional timeZone being populated
body: TimeRange.timeZone was added as an optional field, but getSlots now calls dayjs(...).tz(override.timeZone) unconditionally. Only the trpc slots router was updated to populate timeZone on date overrides. Other callers of getSlots that pass DateOverride objects without timeZone may get invalid timezone handling, incorrect slots, or runtime failures. The type should make this requirement explicit or the code should safely fall back.

title: Timezone-converted overrides can lose cross-midnight information
body: Override start and end times are converted to minutes using hour() * 60 + minute() after applying a timezone offset. If the timezone conversion moves an override across local midnight, the date portion is discarded. endTime can become numerically smaller than startTime, causing buildSlots to skip the range, or the override can be attached to the wrong invitee day. This makes late-night overrides unreliable for invitees in different timezones.

title: No automated test for the fixed-host round-robin date override fix
body: The added test only checks a personal event date override in a different invitee timezone. The PR's primary stated fix is that fixed hosts' date overrides must constrain round-robin availability, but there is no test with a round-robin event, a fixed host, and a date override. There is also no test that busy times still block slots inside date overrides. This leaves the main behavior and the critical busy-time interaction untested.

title: fixedHosts is recomputed for every slot
body: Inside timeSlots.filter, fixedHosts = userAvailability.filter(...) is computed for every slot. The set of fixed hosts does not change during the request. Hoisting this computation outside the slot filter avoids repeated O(number_of_slots * number_of_users) filtering.

title: typeof result compared to undefined instead of a string
body: The condition typeof availabilityCheckProps.currentSeats !== undefined is always true because typeof returns a string, and the later condition typeof availabilityCheckProps.currentSeats === undefined is always false. If currentSeats is undefined while occupied seats exist, the code can call map or push on undefined and crash. The checks should compare against the string 'undefined' or use availabilityCheckProps.currentSeats !== undefined directly.

title: Date override check skips busy-time validation
body: In checkIfIsAvailable, once a date override exists for the slot day (dateOverrideExist is true) and the slot is not rejected by the override predicate, the function returns true before reaching the busy.every(...) conflict check. This ignores existing bookings/calendar busy times on date-override days and can expose slots for hosts who are actually busy, allowing double bookings.

title: Multiple same-day date overrides are handled incorrectly
body: The date override logic uses dateOverrides.find where the callback returns true when the slot is outside that override. If a user has multiple overrides on the same date, the first override that does not contain the slot makes find return and the function returns false, even if a later override does contain the slot. Split overrides such as 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-17:00 can therefore make all slots unavailable.

title: Slots overlapping the edge of a date override are treated as available
body: The override check only rejects slots that end at/before the override start or start after the override end. It does not require the whole slot to be inside the override. A slot that starts before the override and ends inside it, or starts inside and ends after it, is accepted. A slot starting exactly at the override end is also accepted because line 123 uses isAfter without also treating isSame(end) as outside. This can show slots where the fixed host is not fully available.

title: Day.js objects are compared with ===
body: The expression dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...) compares object identity, not timestamp values, so it is always false. Any intended special handling for equal start/end overrides, such as a zero-length override marking unavailability, never runs.

title: Working-hours validation ignores the slot end time
body: In the working-hours check, end is computed from slotStartTime.hour() and slotStartTime.minute() instead of slotEndTime. The event length is therefore ignored when validating working hours, so a slot that starts within working hours but extends past workingHour.endTime is incorrectly considered available.

title: Working-hours validation is wrong for multiple intervals
body: The code uses workingHours.find and returns true, making the slot unavailable, if any working-hour interval on that day does not contain the slot. With multiple intervals in a day, a slot contained in one interval can be rejected because another interval does not contain it. The logic should verify that at least one interval fully contains the slot, or that no interval contains it.

title: Absence of working hours is treated as unrestricted availability
body: If workingHours is empty or has no entry whose days include the slot day, the find call returns undefined and the function falls through to the busy check. For fixed hosts this can allow slots on days with no configured working hours, which defeats the purpose of enforcing fixed-host availability in round-robin events.

title: Date override day comparison can use server-local timezone
body: dayjs(date.start).add(...).format(YYYY MM DD) formats in the server's local timezone, while slotStartTime is a UTC Day.js object. On a non-UTC server, an override near midnight may be matched to the wrong calendar date. The date should be normalized with .utc() before formatting.

title: getSlots assumes optional override.timeZone is present
body: The new override conversion calls .tz(override.timeZone) for every active override, but TimeRange.timeZone is optional and existing callers may provide date overrides without it. If override.timeZone is undefined, dayjs timezone behavior may fall back to the system timezone or fail, causing incorrect slot times or runtime errors. The code should require/validate timeZone or explicitly fall back to organizerTimeZone.

title: Offset is calculated from Date.toString()
body: dayjs(override.start.toString()) parses the output of Date.prototype.toString, which is implementation/locale dependent and unnecessary. This can parse to a different instant than override.start in some environments. Use dayjs(override.start).tz(override.timeZone) directly.

title: Missing test for round-robin fixed-host date overrides
body: The PR description says it fixes date overrides for fixed hosts in round-robin events, but the added test only covers a personal event with a date override in another timezone. There is no test creating a ROUND_ROBIN event with a fixed host and verifying that only slots where the fixed host is available are returned.

title: Date override path returns available without checking busy times
body: checkIfIsAvailable sets dateOverrideExist when it sees any override on the slot's UTC date and, if the slot is not rejected by the override conditions, returns true before the busy.every() check. As a result, any busy periods or accepted bookings for that user are ignored for slots covered by a date override, so users can be offered and potentially book slots that are already busy.

title: Multiple date overrides for the same day are handled as mutually exclusive
body: The date override test uses dateOverrides.find and returns false when the slot is outside the iterated override. If a user has two date overrides on the same date, a slot inside the first override is outside the second, so find returns the second override and the slot is rejected. The correct condition is that the slot is inside at least one override, not outside any override.

title: Date override check allows slots that only partially overlap the override
body: The code treats a slot as outside an override only if slotEndTime is before or equal to the override start, or slotStartTime is after the override end. Therefore a slot that starts before the override and ends inside it, or starts inside and ends after it, is considered inside the override. For fixed-host round-robin availability this can expose slots when the fixed host is not available for the full event duration.

title: Working-hours check is inverted for multiple intervals and ignores event end time
body: checkIfIsAvailable uses workingHours.find and marks the slot unavailable if any working-hours entry reports the slot outside that entry. With multiple working-hour entries on the same day, a slot that is valid in one entry is outside another, so it is incorrectly rejected. Additionally, end is calculated from slotStartTime rather than slotEndTime, so slots that start inside working hours but end after working hours pass. The check should determine that the full slot is contained in at least one working-hours interval.

title: Day.js objects are compared with ===
body: The zero-length override check compares two Day.js objects with ===. This compares object identity and is always false for distinct Day.js instances, even if they represent the same instant. Use .isSame() if start and end equality is intended.

title: Override timezone conversion assumes optional timeZone is present
body: getSlots now reads override.timeZone to compute offsets, but TimeRange.timeZone is optional and no fallback is provided. If dateOverrides without timeZone are passed to getSlots, the offset calculation may use an unintended zone or fail depending on dayjs behavior. A fallback or required type should be used.

title: Missing tests for the fixed-host round-robin override behavior
body: The PR description says round-robin slots must respect fixed hosts' date overrides, but the added test only checks a personal event in another timezone. There is no regression test for round-robin with fixed hosts, multiple overrides, or busy times during a date override.

title: Fixed hosts list recomputed for every slot
body: Inside timeSlots.filter, fixedHosts = userAvailability.filter(...) is computed for each slot. Since userAvailability does not change during the loop, this repeats work for every slot; compute fixedHosts once before filtering.

title: Migration assumes the embed_category setting and matching category exist
body: The migration calls execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i without checking whether the query returned a row. If the old embed_category site setting is absent, blank, or does not match a category name, result[0] is nil and the migration raises NoMethodError. The same assumption is made for uncategorized_category_id on line 15.

title: Migration copies old embeddable hosts without normalizing them
body: The migration inserts the old site-setting lines verbatim into embeddable_hosts.host. Old values could include schemes or paths, and the old code explicitly handled them. Direct SQL inserts bypass the model's before_validation normalization, while EmbeddableHost.record_for_host later matches only URI#host. Migrated rows like http://example.com or example.com/path will therefore never match incoming referers, breaking embedding after upgrade.

title: Migration interpolates host values directly into SQL
body: The INSERT statement embeds the host string h directly into the SQL string. If an old setting value contains a single quote or other SQL metacharacter, the migration can fail or execute unintended SQL. Use connection.quote or a parameterized insert.

title: Destructive setting deletion is not reversible in a change migration
body: The migration deletes the old embeddable_hosts and embed_category site settings inside a change method. Rails cannot automatically reverse this execute DELETE, so rolling back will not restore the previous configuration. Use up/down or make the data movement reversible if rollback support is expected.

title: before_validation crashes when host is nil
body: The before_validation callback unconditionally calls self.host.sub!. If a record is saved with a nil host, such as an API request that omits embeddable_host[host], this raises NoMethodError instead of producing a validation error. Guard against blank host and add a presence validation.

title: Update and destroy do not handle missing records
body: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update and #destroy fetch the record with EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and do not handle nil. For a nonexistent ID, update calls save_host(nil) and destroy calls nil.destroy, causing a 500 error. The actions should return a 404 when the host is not found.

title: save_host assumes the embeddable_host params exist
body: save_host accesses params[:embeddable_host][:host] and params[:embeddable_host][:category_id] without checking that params[:embeddable_host] is present. A request without that root key will raise NoMethodError. Use params.require or safe access with defaults.

title: Host lookup does not downcase the parsed host
body: record_for_host compares lower(host) in SQL to uri.host, but does not downcase uri.host before binding it. If a referer or URL contains an uppercase hostname, the comparison can fail because the literal is not lowercased. Use host.downcase or lower both sides in the query.

title: Host lookup ignores ports even though validation allows ports
body: The hostname validation regex allows a :port suffix, but record_for_host extracts only URI#host and queries the stored host column. A record saved as example.com:8080 will not match a request whose URI host is example.com, so hosts entered with ports will never be considered allowed. Port handling should be normalized consistently.

title: No uniqueness validation or unique index on host
body: EmbeddableHost does not validate host uniqueness and the table has no unique index. Duplicate host rows, including case variations, can be created. EmbeddableHost.record_for_host uses .first without an order, so category assignment becomes ambiguous if duplicates exist. Add a case-insensitive uniqueness validation and a unique index.

title: Hostname regex rejects valid TLDs longer than five characters
body: The host validation regex requires the TLD to be two to five letters. Valid domains with longer TLDs, such as .museum or newer gTLDs, cannot be saved as embeddable hosts.

title: category_id is not validated
body: save_host assigns category_id from request parameters and only replaces blank values with the uncategorized category ID. It does not verify that the category exists, so invalid or deleted category IDs can be persisted. This can leave embeddable hosts pointing at nonexistent categories and break category resolution in the client or importer.

title: Plural embedded ID hydration assumes the value is an array
body: The new plural hydration branch calls obj[k].map(...) for any key matching *_ids. If a serializer emits null or a non-array value for such a key, the store will throw TypeError. The code should verify the value is an array before mapping.

title: record_for_host returns false instead of nil
body: EmbeddableHost.record_for_host returns false when the input URL is invalid, but its name and usage imply it returns a record or nil. Returning false can cause surprising behavior for callers that expect a finder-style result. It should return nil in the failure cases.

title: Controller specs only check inheritance
body: The new admin controller specs only assert that the controllers subclass AdminController. They do not exercise create, update, destroy, missing records, missing params, invalid hosts, or category assignment. These are the paths where the migration/model/controller issues above occur.

title: Migration interpolates old site setting values into raw SQL
body: The migration builds INSERT statements by interpolating each line from the old embeddable_hosts site setting directly into SQL. A value containing a single quote can crash the migration, and a deliberately crafted admin-set value could execute arbitrary SQL during the migration. Use connection.quote or a parameterized insert.

title: Migration assumes settings rows exist and will crash on many upgrades
body: The migration reads execute(...)[0]['id'] for embed_category and execute(...)[0]['value'] for uncategorized_category_id. Site settings are often only stored when changed, and the embed_category join may return zero rows. In those cases [0] is nil and the migration raises NoMethodError. Use safe access and defaults.

title: Migration does not normalize old embeddable host values
body: The model normalizes hosts by stripping scheme and path, and lookup matches only the URI host, but the migration inserts old setting lines verbatim. Existing values such as http://discourse.org or https://example.com/1234 will be stored with scheme/path and will never match EmbeddableHost.record_for_host after upgrade. Blank or whitespace-only lines can also be inserted. Normalize/trim values and skip blanks during migration.

title: No uniqueness constraint or validation for hosts
body: Neither the model nor the migration enforces a unique host, including case-insensitive uniqueness. Duplicate hosts can be created in the UI or inserted by the migration. EmbeddableHost.record_for_host uses an unordered .first, so if duplicates have different categories, imported topics may be assigned to an arbitrary category. Add a case-insensitive uniqueness validation and a unique index on lower(host).

title: before_validation crashes when host is nil
body: before_validation calls self.host.sub! without checking that host is present. Creating or updating an EmbeddableHost with a missing host parameter raises NoMethodError instead of returning a validation error. Add a presence validation or guard before mutating the attribute.

title: Host matching ignores ports and may not normalize case
body: The validation allows hosts with ports, and the port is stored, but record_for_host queries using URI(...).host, which excludes the port. Therefore a host saved with a port never matches referers/URLs. The parsed host should also be downcased before comparing to lower(host), otherwise uppercase hostnames may fail to match. Normalize host matching or remove port support.

title: update and destroy do not handle missing records
body: update and destroy fetch the record with EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and then call save_host or destroy. If the id does not exist, host is nil and the action raises NoMethodError. A non-numeric id can also cause a database type error. Use find_by(id: params[:id].to_i) and return 404 when missing.

title: save_host assumes params[:embeddable_host] exists
body: save_host dereferences params[:embeddable_host][:host] and params[:embeddable_host][:category_id] without requiring the embeddable_host hash. A request without that key raises NoMethodError. Use params.require/permit or guard for missing parameters.

title: category_id value of 0 is not treated as uncategorized and is not validated
body: The controller replaces category_id only when blank?, but in Rails 0 is not blank. A no-category value of 0, or an invalid id cast to 0, can be persisted as a dangling category_id. The model also does not validate that the category exists. Treat 0 as uncategorized and validate category existence.

title: Edit action crashes when host category is missing
body: edit() sets categoryId from this.get('host.category.id'). If the category was not hydrated, was deleted, or the stored category_id is invalid, host.category is undefined and clicking Edit throws TypeError. Use host.category_id or safe navigation.

title: Plural embedded id hydration assumes value is an array
body: The new _ids hydration calls obj[k].map without checking that obj[k] is an array; a null or undefined plural id field will throw. It also deletes the original *_ids key even when lookup fails, producing arrays containing undefined records. Guard with Array.isArray and skip or filter missing objects.

title: Existing embeds remain expandable after all allowed hosts are removed
body: expandable_first_post? no longer checks that any embeddable hosts are configured. If admins delete all EmbeddableHost records to disable embedding, previously imported topic embeds can still be expanded and can still trigger remote fetches via TopicEmbed.expanded_for. If removing hosts is meant to disable embedding, restore a host-allowed check.

title: resources :embeddable_hosts exposes actions that are not implemented
body: The route declaration creates index/show/new/edit routes, but Admin::EmbeddableHostsController only implements create, update, and destroy. Requests to the unused routes will hit missing actions. Use only: [:create, :update, :destroy].

title: Host regex restricts TLD length to five characters
body: The host validation regex requires the TLD to be 2 to 5 letters, which rejects valid modern domains such as example.technology. Consider using a less restrictive hostname validation or URI-based validation.

title: New admin endpoints have no functional tests
body: The added controller specs only assert inheritance from AdminController. There are no tests for create/update/delete, invalid or missing hosts, missing parameters, category assignment, duplicate hosts, or migration normalization. Add functional tests for the new endpoints and model behavior.

title: Legacy embeddable_hosts values are inserted without normalization
body: The migration copies each line from the old embeddable_hosts site setting directly into embeddable_hosts.host. Existing values may include a scheme or path, but EmbeddableHost.record_for_host later parses the referer/embed URL and searches only by URI host. Rows such as `http://example.com` or `example.com/path` therefore will not match `example.com`, so hosts that were allowed before the upgrade can stop working.

title: Unescaped values in migration SQL
body: The INSERT statement interpolates the site-setting line `h` directly into SQL. A stored value containing a single quote can break the migration or execute unintended SQL. Use quoted/parameterized values rather than string interpolation.

title: Migration assumes site-setting/category rows exist
body: The migration calls `execute(...)[0]['id']` without checking whether a row was returned. On installations where `embed_category` was never changed, or where the uncategorized category setting row is absent, this raises NoMethodError and aborts the migration. The same pattern appears for `uncategorized_category_id` at line 15.

title: Data migration is not reversible
body: The migration uses raw INSERT/DELETE statements inside a `change` method. Rails cannot automatically reverse these operations, so rolling back the migration will raise an irreversible migration error. Use `up`/`down` or an explicit reversible block.

title: before_validation crashes when host is nil
body: The callback calls `self.host.sub!` without guarding against nil. Creating or updating an EmbeddableHost with a missing host value raises NoMethodError instead of returning a normal validation error.

title: No uniqueness enforcement for host
body: The model validates only the format of `host`; there is no uniqueness validation and the migration does not add a unique index. Duplicate host rows can be created, and `record_for_host` uses `.first`, making the selected category nondeterministic when duplicates exist.

title: Hostname regex rejects valid modern TLDs
body: The validation regex limits the TLD to 2-5 letters, which rejects valid modern domains such as `.solutions` or `.photography`. Admins would be unable to add real embeddable hosts that use newer TLDs.

title: Port handling is inconsistent
body: The validation regex permits stored hosts with ports, but `record_for_host` compares only `URI#host`, which excludes the port. A stored host like `example.com:8080` will not match requests to that port, while a stored host without a port implicitly matches all ports.

title: Missing record handling causes 500 errors
body: Update fetches the record with `.first` and passes it to `save_host` without checking for nil. Destroy does the same and calls `destroy`. A request with an unknown id raises NoMethodError instead of returning a 404 or error JSON.

title: Unsafe assumption that params[:embeddable_host] exists
