body: `save_host` indexes `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` directly. If the request body does not include an `embeddable_host` object, the controller raises NoMethodError instead of returning a validation or parameter error.

title: category_id is not validated against existing categories
body: The controller assigns any supplied `category_id` and only replaces blank values with the uncategorized category id. It does not verify that the category exists, and it does not treat 0 as uncategorized. This can create embeddable hosts with dangling category ids, leading to missing categories in the UI and undefined behavior.

title: PUT /admin/customize/embedding does nothing
body: The update action renders the current embedding object but never applies or persists any parameters. The client controller has a saveChanges action that calls `embedding.update({})`; any future editable embedding attributes sent to this endpoint would silently not save.

title: Edit action assumes host.category is present
body: `this.get('host.category.id')` throws if `host.category` is undefined. This can happen when the category was deleted, the stored category_id is invalid, or the category is not present in the client-side category list. The component should use `host.category_id` or guard against a missing category.

title: Client state after save can diverge from server
body: After saving, the component sets `category` by looking up the local `categoryId`, but does not update `category_id`, and the lookup may return undefined. If the server coerces a blank category to uncategorized or the category cannot be found, the displayed row may show no category or stale state.

title: Hydrating embedded ids assumes property is an array
body: For keys ending in `_ids`, the code calls `obj[k].map` without checking that `obj[k]` is present and array-like. If a serializer emits null or omits the ids value for an empty relation, store hydration throws a TypeError. A guard such as `(obj[k] || []).map` is needed.

title: No functional controller tests for new admin endpoints
body: The specs only assert controller inheritance. There are no tests for create/update/destroy behavior, invalid parameters, missing records, invalid categories, duplicate hosts, or authorization. Given that these endpoints control which external hosts may embed the forum, this is a significant coverage gap.

title: Duplicate `downsize` definition overwrites the previous method
body: Ruby does not support method overloading. The second `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` replaces the earlier four-argument `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`. Existing callers using the old width/height signature will either raise ArgumentError if they pass an options hash as a fifth argument, or have the height argument treated as the options hash, causing a TypeError when `optimize` calls `opts[:allow_animation]`. This breaks the public API and any existing callers.

title: In-place downsizing uses the same path as an open tempfile
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` rewrites the uploaded file in place while the `tempfile` object remains open. Subsequent code uses `tempfile.size` and passes `tempfile` to `Upload.create_for` without reopening or rewinding it. If ImageMagick/gifsicle/ImageOptim replace the file, truncate it, or leave the descriptor at an old offset, the loop may read stale size/content and the upload may store the original or corrupted file. Use a separate output file and then reopen/rewind/replace the tempfile.

title: Downsizing loop ignores failures and final size
body: The loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize` up to five times but ignores its boolean result and proceeds to create the upload even if every attempt fails or the file is still larger than `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`. This can accept oversized/unchanged images or fail later with an unrelated error. It should check the return value and final size and return an error when the image cannot be reduced enough.

title: Remote URL downloads are hardcoded to 10 MB and bypass site limits
body: `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` now downloads remote uploads up to 10 MB regardless of `max_image_size_kb` or attachment-size settings. The later automatic downsizing only applies to files recognized as images, so non-image URL uploads can be fetched and possibly processed above configured limits, and even image downloads can consume more bandwidth/memory than the site allows. The download limit should be derived from the appropriate site setting/type.

title: Client-side upload size validation is hardcoded to 10 MB
body: `validateUploadedFile` now uses `10 * 1024` instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. The client no longer enforces or displays the configured limits for images/attachments; users may be allowed to upload files the server will reject, or prevented from uploading files the server would allow. The same hardcoding in the 413 handler makes error messages inaccurate.

title: Client-side upload limit is hardcoded to 10MB
body: The upload validator now uses a constant 10MB limit for every file instead of the type-specific site setting (`max_image_size_kb` or `max_attachment_size_kb`). This makes client-side enforcement inconsistent with admin configuration: files above the configured limit can be submitted, and files below a higher configured limit can be rejected. The too-large alert also reports the wrong limit.

title: 413 error message uses a hardcoded limit
body: When a 413 response is received, the message is generated with a fixed 10MB maximum. This is incorrect for attachments and for sites where the configured upload limit differs from 10MB.

title: URL downloads ignore configured upload size limits
body: API uploads supplied by URL are downloaded with a fixed 10MB cap rather than the configured limit. The subsequent automatic reduction only runs for filenames that look like images, so non-image files, or images that cannot be reduced, may be processed despite lower site limits, and the server will fetch more data than configured.

title: Downsizing rewrites the uploaded tempfile in place
body: The downsize operation passes the same filesystem path as source and destination to external image tools. In-place rewriting of an open tempfile is not safe for ImageMagick or gifsicle; a tool failure or partial write can truncate or corrupt the original uploaded file before it is stored. A separate output file should be used and replaced only after success.

title: Animated GIFs can be silently flattened
body: Animated GIF handling is selected by checking whether the source path ends in .gif, but the tempfile path used for uploads generally does not include the original extension. As a result, an animated GIF can be processed with ImageMagick's first-frame-only path and reduced to a static image, silently losing animation even when animation is allowed.

title: Failed downsize operations are ignored
body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns false if conversion or optimization fails, but this return value is ignored. The loop can retry a failing conversion five times and then continue to create an upload from the unchanged or corrupted tempfile instead of returning a clear error.

title: Upload proceeds without verifying final image size
body: After at most five 80% reductions, the code calls `Upload.create_for` without confirming that the file is now within `max_image_size_kb`. If downsizing cannot reach the limit, the request either depends on downstream validation or stores an oversized image, and the user does not get a specific failure for the automatic downsizing step.

title: Duplicate `downsize` definition silently overwrites previous method
body: Ruby does not support method overloading. This second definition of `self.downsize` replaces the previous width/height version. Existing callers that pass `max_width` and `max_height` will now have `max_height` treated as the options argument, or receive an ArgumentError for five arguments, breaking the previous API.

title: No tests for automatic downsizing behavior
body: No tests were added for the new automatic downsizing flow. The behavior includes conditional size checks, external command failure handling, animation preservation, and in-place tempfile mutation, all of which are likely to regress without controller and model specs.

title: Client-side upload size validation is hardcoded to 10 MB and ignores site settings
body: validateUploadedFile previously used Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the limit depended on whether the upload was an image or attachment and on admin settings. The change replaces this with a constant 10 MB. Users can now select attachments or images larger than the configured limit (up to 10 MB), and the displayed 'file too large' error reports 10 MB even when the forum limit is lower or higher. Attachments are not downsized server-side by this PR, so this can bypass or confuse enforcement of attachment size limits.

title: 413 upload error message uses hardcoded limit instead of site setting
body: When the server or web server returns HTTP 413, the alert now always says the maximum size is 10 MB. The previous code used Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb. If the configured limit or the web server limit differs, users receive an incorrect error message, making upload failures confusing and harder to diagnose.

title: API URL downloads are capped at 10 MB for all upload types, ignoring configured limits
body: FileHelper.download now always allows 10 MB, regardless of SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb or attachment size limits. For images the PR attempts to downsize afterward, but for non-image attachments there is no downsizing step. This can permit or attempt uploads larger than admin-configured limits and increases resource usage by downloading oversized remote files.

title: Downsizing rewrites the same open Tempfile in place
body: OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...) uses the same path as input and output for an external image tool while the Ruby tempfile object remains open. If the tool truncates, replaces, or renames the output file, the open file descriptor can point at stale data, so tempfile.size and later Upload.create_for may read the wrong bytes or an old inode. A failed conversion can also corrupt the only copy of the upload. Write to a separate temporary file and replace tempfile only after a successful conversion.

title: Downsizing loop can stop while the image is still too large or conversion failed
body: The loop makes at most five 80% resize attempts and ignores the boolean returned by OptimizedImage.downsize. If conversion fails or five attempts are insufficient, execution still proceeds to Upload.create_for with a file that may exceed SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb. The controller should verify the final size and return an error if it cannot reduce the file enough, rather than relying on later behavior.

title: Duplicate downsize method definition silently removes width/height API
body: Ruby does not support method overloading. The second self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) at line 149 overrides the previous self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) at line 145. The older width/height variant is dead code, and any existing caller using separate width and height arguments will now pass the height argument as opts, likely causing TypeError or wrong behavior. Remove the dead method or use a distinct method name if both signatures are needed.

title: Image processing command is executed via string interpolation without escaping
body: convert_with runs a shell command built from instructions.join(' ') using backticks. Paths are inserted as unquoted, unescaped arguments. The new automatic downsizing passes temporary file paths to this code; if a path contains spaces or shell metacharacters, the command can fail or execute unintended commands. Use system with an argument array or Shellwords.escape instead of interpolating into a shell string.

title: GET unsubscribe endpoint mutates notification state
body: The `unsubscribe` action changes the user's `TopicUser.notification_level` while being served by GET routes (`t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` and `t/:topic_id/unsubscribe`). GET requests can be issued by link prefetchers, email-client previews, crawlers, or third-party HTML using the user's session. Because the new level depends on the current level, repeated or prefetched requests can silently change the subscription (for example watching -> regular -> muted). State-changing operations should require POST/PUT or a confirmation/token rather than occur on page load.

title: NoMethodError when TopicUser record is absent
body: `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil for a logged-in user who has no existing TopicUser row for the topic. The following `tu.notification_level` call will raise NoMethodError and return a 500. The action should upsert the TopicUser (for example with `find_or_initialize_by` plus sensible defaults, or via `TopicUser.change`) instead of assuming the row exists.

title: Unsubscribe does not consistently mute the topic
body: The endpoint downgrades tracking/watching topics to `regular` instead of `muted`. Regular is not the same as muted and can still produce notifications for interactions such as mentions or replies, so a user clicking an unsubscribe link may continue receiving notifications. If the feature is meant to stop notifications for that topic, set the level to muted or make the desired target level explicit.

title: Direct save bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping
body: Instead of using `TopicUser.change`, the action updates the row with `save!`. `TopicUser.change` is the established path for notification-level changes: it sets `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` and publishes a MessageBus notification-level change. Bypassing it can leave client state out of sync and lose the reason/audit information for the subscription change.

title: Global unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url
body: The `unsubscribe_link` translation now includes `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `Email::MessageBuilder` appends/renders `unsubscribe_link` whenever `add_unsubscribe_link` is true, but only notification emails were updated to provide `unsubscribe_url`. Existing or plugin emails that set `add_unsubscribe_link` without supplying this new interpolation key will raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` when building the email body or HTML part. Use a separate key, provide a safe default, or make the topic-specific line conditional.

title: Missing tests for new unsubscribe endpoint
body: No controller/request specs were added for the new unsubscribe endpoint. Tests are needed for successful notification-level changes, missing TopicUser rows, unauthorized or private topics, slug redirects, JSON versus HTML responses, and repeated GET requests.

title: track_visit! uses the topic id as the user id for non-User arguments
body: `TopicUser.track_visit!(topic, user)` sets `user_id = user.is_a?(User) ? user.id : topic`. `TopicsController#track_visit_to_topic` calls this with a topic id and a user id, so the second argument is an Integer and the false branch assigns the topic id to `user_id`. This updates or creates `topic_users` rows for the wrong user, corrupting visit tracking and potentially causing foreign-key errors. The else branch should return `user`.

title: Unsubscribe action assumes a TopicUser row exists
body: `TopicsController#unsubscribe` looks up `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and immediately reads `tu.notification_level`. A logged-in user can request this route for a topic where no `topic_users` row exists yet, so `tu` is nil and the action raises `NoMethodError`, producing a 500. Use `TopicUser.change` or find-or-create the record before mutating it.

title: Notification level change bypasses TopicUser.change side effects
body: The unsubscribe action mutates `notification_level` and calls `save!` directly. `TopicUser.change` is the normal API for this operation and also sets `notifications_changed_at`/`notifications_reason_id`, publishes the MessageBus notification-level change, and runs observer callbacks. Bypassing it can leave client state stale and make notification-level changes inconsistently recorded.

title: GET unsubscribe immediately mutates notification settings
body: The route maps GET `/t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` to an action that changes the user's topic notification level before rendering anything. Because the mutation happens on a GET, link prefetching, email-client scanners, previews, or repeated reloads can change a logged-in user's notification state without an explicit confirmation. A state-changing unsubscribe should require POST/PUT or an explicit user action.

title: unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url for all callers
body: `MessageBuilder#body` and `#html_part` append `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` whenever `add_unsubscribe_link` is true, but the updated locale string interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. Only `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` was updated to pass `unsubscribe_url`; any other Discourse or plugin caller enabling `add_unsubscribe_link` without that key may get a missing-interpolation error or broken email text, and non-topic emails will incorrectly refer to a particular topic.

title: Missing tests for the new unsubscribe behavior
body: The spec only adds `unsubscribe_url` to the builder but does not assert that the body or HTML part includes the topic unsubscribe link. There are also no controller/request specs for `TopicsController#unsubscribe` covering missing `TopicUser` rows, slug redirects, permissions, or the GET mutation, which are the main failure modes introduced by this PR.

title: Unsubscribe action crashes when no TopicUser row exists
body: TopicsController#unsubscribe looks up TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) and immediately calls tu.notification_level. If the user has no topic_users row for that topic, tu is nil and the request raises NoMethodError. The action should handle the missing record or use TopicUser.change, which creates the row when needed.

title: State-changing unsubscribe is performed via GET
body: The /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe route is a GET route and TopicsController#unsubscribe immediately mutates TopicUser.notification_level. GET requests are not protected by Rails CSRF tokens and can be triggered by link prefetching, email-client previews, or embedded resources while a user is logged in. Repeated GETs also move regular users to muted. Use a POST/PUT action with CSRF protection or require an explicit confirmation before changing state.

title: Unsubscribe bypasses TopicUser.change and loses notification-change side effects
body: The action updates TopicUser with tu.save! instead of TopicUser.change. TopicUser.change is the normal path for notification-level changes; it sets notifications_changed_at and notifications_reason_id and publishes the MessageBus notification_level_change event. Bypassing it can leave client state stale and loses notification-change metadata.

title: track_visit! uses the topic id as the user id for non-User arguments
body: TopicUser.track_visit! assigns user_id as user.is_a?(User) ? user.id : topic. Callers such as TopicsController#track_visit_to_topic pass integer user ids, so the fallback uses the topic argument as the user id. This creates or updates topic_users rows for the wrong user and corrupts per-user topic state. The fallback should be the user argument.

title: unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url for every use
body: The shared unsubscribe_link translation was changed to include %{unsubscribe_url}. Email::MessageBuilder appends this translation whenever add_unsubscribe_link is true. Any existing or plugin caller that enables add_unsubscribe_link but does not supply unsubscribe_url will fail interpolation or emit a broken link. Make the topic-specific line conditional on unsubscribe_url being present or update all callers.

title: Topic title is rendered unescaped with triple braces
body: The template renders {{{stopNotificiationsText}}}, and that property interpolates model.fancyTitle into an HTML string. Triple braces bypass Handlebars escaping, so any HTML in the topic title, or in a future representation of fancyTitle, would be injected into the page. Escape the title or render it through a safe component.

title: No meaningful coverage for the new unsubscribe behavior
body: The PR adds a state-changing unsubscribe endpoint and a new required unsubscribe_url interpolation, but the only spec change merely passes unsubscribe_url to Email::MessageBuilder and still only asserts the global preferences URL. There are no controller/request specs for TopicsController#unsubscribe, including missing TopicUser rows, notification-level transitions, slug redirects, or HTML/JSON behavior, and no spec asserting that the topic unsubscribe URL appears in email bodies or HTML.

title: Blocked email lookup is not normalized
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? queries the raw email value without stripping or downcasing it, and BlockedEmail records are not normalized before save. A block for bad@example.com can be bypassed with Bad@Example.com or surrounding whitespace, and the uniqueness validation allows case-variant duplicates. Consequence: blocked email addresses can still be used.

title: Domain whitelist/blacklist regex is unanchored and under-escaped
body: email_in_restriction_setting? builds a case-insensitive regular expression from the setting after escaping only dots and without anchoring the domain. A whitelist entry of example.com will accept user@example.com.evil.com because the address contains @example.com. Other regex metacharacters in the setting are not escaped. Consequence: domain restrictions can be bypassed or misapplied.

title: Side-effecting, non-atomic increment inside validation double counts matches
body: should_block? increments match_count and saves a BlockedEmail record during validation. UsersController#create calls user.valid? and later user.save, so the email validator runs twice and do_nothing records are counted twice. The read-modify-write is also not atomic, so concurrent requests can lose increments, and save failures are ignored. Consequence: inaccurate statistics and unnecessary writes.

title: blocked_emails.email may be shorter than users.email
body: The migration creates blocked_emails.email as a default Rails string, typically varchar(255), while users.email is shown as string(256) in the schema. If a 256-character email is accepted by User, it cannot be stored in blocked_emails, causing insertion failures or inability to block that address.

title: Client-side rejected email list is case-sensitive and not normalized
body: The client-side rejectedEmails check uses exact string equality without normalization. If the server rejects a normalized/lowercased email or the user changes capitalization/whitespace, the UI will not disable submission for that email. This is primarily a UX issue because the server still validates, but it undermines the intended immediate rejection.

title: Missing coverage for normalization and repeated validation passes
body: The specs only test exact-match, single-call behavior for should_block?. They do not cover mixed-case or whitespace variants, nor the fact that User creation can invoke the validator more than once via valid? followed by save. As a result, the blocked-email bypass and double-counting behavior are not caught by tests.

title: Blocked email check mutates records during validation
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? increments match_count, sets last_match_at, and saves the record every time it is called. It is invoked from EmailValidator while validating User, and UsersController#create calls user.valid? and then user.save, so a single blocked signup attempt can update the blocked-email row twice. The write also happens even if the user record is ultimately invalid or not saved, and concurrent requests can lose increments because this is a non-atomic read-modify-write. Validation should be read-only; update statistics separately, ideally atomically, if that behavior is desired.

title: Blocked email lookup is not normalized, allowing case/whitespace bypass
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? queries BlockedEmail.where(email: email) using the raw value, and neither the model nor the migration normalizes case or whitespace. The changed code also does not downcase or strip the email before validation during account creation. A blocked address such as foo@example.com can therefore be bypassed with Foo@Example.com or surrounding whitespace, and the case-sensitive unique index permits duplicate blocked rows that differ only by case. Normalize emails before storing and querying, and use a case-insensitive unique index or normalized column.

title: Domain whitelist/blacklist regex is unanchored and under-escaped
body: email_in_restriction_setting? builds Regexp.new('@(#{domains})', true) after only escaping dots. The pattern is not anchored to the end of the address, so with a whitelist of example.com, user@example.com.evil.com matches and is treated as allowed. Other regex metacharacters in the setting are also not escaped, which can cause unintended matches or regexp errors. Split the setting into domains, escape each domain, and anchor the match to the actual domain portion of the email address.

title: Rejected emails are stored in a shared/non-reset array
body: rejectedEmails is defined as Em.A([]) on the controller prototype. Mutable array properties on an Ember prototype are shared across controller instances and are not reset when the modal is reopened. Once an email has been rejected, it can remain rejected for the lifetime of the page/controller state even if the form state should be fresh, potentially preventing legitimate retries. Initialize or reset the array per controller instance/modal open.

title: Email validator tests stub the blocked-email check and omit domain-restriction cases
body: The spec only stubs BlockedEmail.should_block? and asserts that an error is added or not. It does not exercise the real whitelist/blacklist logic, email normalization, or the side effects of blocked-email matching. Because the domain regex and blocked-email handling are security-relevant, add tests that use real BlockedEmail records and SiteSetting values, including case variations and suffix domains such as user@example.com.evil.com.

title: Blocked email matching is exact and case-sensitive
body: BlockedEmail.should_block? queries BlockedEmail.where(email: email), and neither the model nor the migration normalizes email case. Discourse treats emails case-insensitively in other places, so a block entry for 'bad@example.com' will not match 'Bad@Example.com'. A blocked user can bypass the block by changing case, and the unique index permits case-variant duplicate block rows.

title: Validation query mutates blocked-email records
body: should_block? increments match_count, sets last_match_at, and saves the record every time it is called. It is invoked from EmailValidator during User validation. UsersController#create calls user.valid? and later user.save, which reruns validations, so one signup attempt can update the blocked-email row multiple times; updates made inside a failing save may also be rolled back while those from a standalone valid? call remain. The counters and timestamps become unreliable, and validation performs database writes. The return value of save is ignored.

title: Non-atomic counter update
body: The match count is updated by loading the row, incrementing it in Ruby, and saving it. Concurrent requests using the same blocked email can lose increments. An atomic increment_counter/update_counters call would preserve the statistic.

title: Domain restriction regex is not anchored
body: email_in_restriction_setting? builds a case-insensitive regular expression from the raw setting after escaping only dots, and it does not anchor the domain's end. With a whitelist of 'example.com', an address like 'user@example.com.attacker.com' can match and be accepted, defeating the whitelist and potentially causing incorrect blacklist behavior.

title: Validator tests stub the blocking logic
body: The EmailValidator spec stubs BlockedEmail.should_block? and only checks whether an error is added. It does not exercise the actual blocked-email lookup, case handling, counter side effects, or the moved whitelist/blacklist domain logic, so regressions in the real validation path are not covered.

title: Imported embed content is stored and rendered as raw HTML without sanitization
body: TopicEmbed.import creates posts with skip_validations and cook_method Post.cook_methods[:raw_html], so Post#cook returns the imported feed/readability HTML unchanged. The embed view renders post.cooked with raw. Untrusted RSS/Atom or scraped content can therefore contain script tags, event handlers, or javascript: URLs, leading to stored XSS in Discourse and embedding pages.

title: Import footer interpolates the embed URL into HTML without escaping
body: TopicEmbed.import appends an imported-from footer containing #{url} to the content before saving it as raw HTML. The only validation is that the URL starts with http(s)://, so quotes, angle brackets, or script-bearing URL components can inject markup into the post.

title: request.referer is embedded in inline JavaScript without escaping
body: The embed layout outputs request.referer directly inside a script string for parent.postMessage. A Referer header containing a single quote or other script-breaking characters can inject JavaScript into the Discourse embed page. The value should be JSON/JS-escaped or replaced with a validated origin.

title: Invalid ERB end tag will break template compilation
body: The first conditional in best.html.erb is closed with <%- end if %>, which compiles to invalid Ruby syntax. Rendering this template will raise a syntax error. It should be closed with a normal ERB end tag.

title: Unknown embed URLs trigger background retrieval without validating the URL host
body: EmbedController#best only validates the Referer host, then enqueues :retrieve_topic for any embed_url parameter. The embed_url host is only checked later inside TopicRetriever. This allows a client that can present an acceptable Referer to enqueue many jobs for arbitrary URLs, causing Sidekiq load and unwanted fetch attempts. Validate and/or throttle embed_url before enqueuing.

title: Feed item content is assumed present
body: poll_feed calls i.content.scrub for every feed item. Many feeds provide only description/summary or may have nil content, in which case SimpleRSS returns nil and the job raises NoMethodError, aborting the entire poll. It should fall back safely to other item fields.

title: Feed fetch has no timeout or error handling
body: SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) uses open-uri without timeouts, redirect controls, or rescue for network and parse errors. A slow, unreachable, or malformed feed can hang or crash the scheduled job.

title: Redis throttle uses non-atomic SETNX + EXPIRE
body: retrieved_recently? calls $redis.setnx and then $redis.expire. If the process crashes between those calls, or expire fails, the key remains without a TTL and that embed URL can be throttled forever. Use an atomic SET with NX and EX, or another safe Redis pattern.

title: Missing embed URLs trigger a full synchronous feed poll
body: perform_retrieve executes Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) inline whenever a single unknown embed URL is requested and feed polling is enabled. Each distinct unknown URL can force a complete fetch and import of the configured feed, which is expensive and can be abused. The feed poll should be debounced or enqueued asynchronously.

title: content_sha1 is updated even if the revision fails
body: In the update branch, TopicEmbed.import calls PostRevisor#revise! and then unconditionally updates the embed content_sha1. If the revision/save fails or returns false, the stored SHA will no longer match the post body and future legitimate content changes may be skipped.

title: Post creation success is checked with present? instead of persisted?
body: After PostCreator#create, TopicEmbed.import checks if post.present?. PostCreator can return an unsaved Post object with errors after a rollback, so this condition can be true for a non-persisted post. The subsequent TopicEmbed.create! can then fail on nil topic_id/post_id or create inconsistent data. Check post.persisted? and errors before creating the embed.

title: TopicEmbed records are not cleaned up when topic or post are deleted
body: TopicEmbed belongs_to :topic and :post but has no dependent destroy or cleanup callback. If a topic or post is destroyed, stale topic_embed rows remain. topic_id_for_embed can then return a deleted topic id, and update code may later call methods on a nil post.

title: PostCreator jobs are enqueued inside the outer Topic.transaction
body: TopicEmbed.import wraps PostCreator#create in a Topic.transaction. PostCreator enqueues background jobs after its own Post.transaction block, but that block is nested inside the outer transaction, so jobs may be queued before the topic/embed data is committed. Workers can race and fail to see the new records.

title: Remote import fetch has no timeout or failure handling
body: TopicEmbed.import_remote calls open(url).read without timeouts or error handling. A slow or failing remote host can hang the retrieve-topic worker. This fetch should use explicit timeouts and rescue network errors.

title: postMessage origin check uses substring matching
body: The resize listener accepts messages if discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1 is false. This substring test can match origins that are prefixes or otherwise embedded in the discourseUrl string. Use an exact origin comparison after normalizing scheme/host/port.

title: Default-port handling is scheme-independent
body: absolutize_urls omits the port whenever it is 80 or 443, regardless of URI scheme. For http://host:443/ or https://host:80/, it will generate URLs without the required port. Compare the port against the default port for the URI scheme instead.

title: Template assumes post.user is present
body: The embed/best view calls post.user.small_avatar_url and post.user.username without nil checks. Posts can have missing or deleted users, which will cause a NoMethodError when rendering the embedded topic.

title: create_table with force: true can drop an existing table
body: Changing this migration to create_table :top_topics, force: true means the migration will drop the top_topics table if it already exists. If this migration is rerun or run against a database where the table was created previously, data can be lost. Use a new migration or conditional DDL instead.

title: Invalid ERB closing tag breaks the embed template
body: The template uses `<%- end if %>` after the if/else block. ERB compiles that as Ruby code, but `end if` is not valid Ruby, so rendering embed/best raises a SyntaxError. The closing tag should be `<%- end %>`.

title: Imported external content is posted as raw HTML without sanitization
body: TopicEmbed.import creates posts from external RSS/readability content with cook_method raw_html and skip_validations. Post#cook then returns the raw string and the embed view renders cooked with `raw`, so untrusted HTML from the feed or fetched page can include scripts or event handlers and cause stored XSS. The content should be sanitized or cooked through the normal safe pipeline.

title: Embed URL is interpolated into HTML without escaping
body: The imported_from footer is built by interpolating the source URL directly into an HTML anchor: `#{url}`. The URL is not HTML-escaped, and the resulting content is stored/rendered as raw HTML. A crafted URL or feed item can inject markup/JavaScript into the imported post. Escape the URL or build the footer with a safe HTML helper.

title: Referer is embedded directly into JavaScript without escaping
body: The embed layout outputs `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')`. The Referer header comes from the embedding page and can contain single quotes or other metacharacters; inserting it unescaped into a script block can break the JavaScript or inject code that runs on the Discourse origin. Use `escape_javascript`/a safe JSON payload and send to a validated origin.

title: postMessage origin check uses substring match
body: The message handler checks `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`, which is a substring test rather than an origin comparison. An origin that is a prefix or otherwise appears inside discourseUrl can be accepted (for example ports whose numeric strings are prefixes). Parse discourseUrl and compare its origin exactly with e.origin.

title: Redis throttle key can be set without expiry
body: retrieved_recently? creates the throttle key with `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, '1')` and then calls `$redis.expire`. If the process crashes or expire fails between the two calls, the key remains without a TTL and the URL is permanently throttled. Use an atomic SET ... EX 60 NX operation.

title: URL validation is insufficient for URI parsing
body: TopicEmbed.import only checks that the URL begins with http:// or https:// before later calling URI(url) in absolutize_urls. Strings that pass the loose prefix check but are not valid URIs will raise URI::InvalidURIError and abort feed polling/topic retrieval. Validate or rescue URI parsing before processing the URL.

title: Feed items without content crash the poller
body: PollFeed assumes every feed item has content: `i.content.scrub`. RSS/Atom entries can omit content or only provide a summary, in which case i.content is nil and the job raises NoMethodError, stopping the poll. Handle blank/nil content before scrubbing/unescaping.

title: Feed URL is fetched with open-uri and no timeouts
body: The feed is fetched with `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` using open-uri. There is no timeout or explicit restriction to safe HTTP(S) endpoints, and open-uri can follow redirects, so a bad/misconfigured feed URL can hang the job or reach internal/local resources. Use an HTTP client with timeouts, scheme allow-listing, and controlled redirects.

title: Update branch does not handle missing posts or failed revisions
body: In the update branch, TopicEmbed.import assumes embed.post exists and ignores the result of PostRevisor#revise! before updating content_sha1. If the associated post was deleted, PostRevisor.new(post) raises; if the revision/save fails, the SHA is still updated, so future imports think the content is current and leave the post stale. Handle missing posts and only persist content_sha1 after a successful revision.

title: Missing embed URLs trigger synchronous full feed polling
body: When feed polling is enabled, TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve instantiates and executes Jobs::PollFeed inline for each missing embed URL. This can fetch and parse the full feed synchronously inside the retrieve job, repeatedly and with no feed-modified caching, causing unnecessary latency and Sidekiq load. Enqueue the poller or cache feed state instead.

title: Embed script assumes #discourse-comments exists
body: The embed script calls `comments.appendChild(iframe)` without verifying that `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` returned an element. On pages missing that container the script throws TypeError and no iframe is inserted. Guard against the missing element or create it.

title: Invalid ERB closing tag breaks embed view
body: The template closes the `if @topic_view.posts.present?` block with `<%- end if %>`. ERB will emit Ruby code `end if` with no condition, which is a syntax error, so rendering app/views/embed/best.html.erb will fail. Use `<%- end %>` instead.

title: Raw HTML cook method bypasses sanitization
body: Post#cook returns the post's raw HTML unchanged when cook_method is Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]. Imported embed/RSS posts are created with this cook method and app/views/embed/best.html.erb renders post.cooked with `raw`, bypassing Discourse's sanitization. Any script, event handler, or dangerous URL in imported HTML can execute as stored XSS. Imported content must be sanitized or cooked through the safe pipeline.

title: Unescaped embed URL is injected into stored HTML
body:
TopicEmbed.import appends `
...#{url}...` to the post contents without HTML-escaping the URL. Because imported posts use raw HTML rendering, a URL containing quotes or angle brackets can inject arbitrary markup/JavaScript into the stored post. Escape the URL or build the anchor with a safe helper.

title: RSS content is HTML-unescaped and then stored as raw HTML
body: Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed calls CGI.unescapeHTML on feed item content and then imports it as raw HTML. This turns entity-escaped markup such as <script> into active HTML and stores it without sanitization, allowing stored XSS from an RSS/ATOM feed. Do not unescape feed content into raw HTML; sanitize or treat it as untrusted text.

title: NoMethodError when an RSS item has no content
body: poll_feed calls i.content.scrub, but RSS/ATOM items may not have a content element and simple-rss can return nil or omit the field. This raises NoMethodError and aborts the scheduled feed-polling job. Use a safe fallback such as i.content || i.description || '' and convert to string before scrubbing.

title: Missing open-uri require for remote import
body: TopicEmbed.import_remote uses open(url) but the file does not require 'open-uri'. If open-uri has not been loaded by another code path, open will not understand HTTP(S) URLs and remote import will fail. Add require 'open-uri' and preferably use a hardened HTTP client.

title: import_remote fetches URL before validating scheme/host
body: TopicEmbed.import_remote calls open(url).read before validating that url is an allowed http/https URL. TopicEmbed.import only rejects non-http(s) URLs after the fetch, so untrusted URLs can cause open-uri to read local files or internal services. Validate scheme/host and use a hardened HTTP client before fetching.

title: Feed fetch has no timeout or size limit
body: poll_feed fetches the feed with open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) and no open/read timeout or body-size limit. A slow or malicious feed can hang the Sidekiq worker or exhaust memory. Use an HTTP client with timeouts and a maximum response size.

title: Missing embed URLs can trigger full feed polling synchronously
body: TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve executes Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) whenever feed polling is enabled and an embed URL is missing. This lets many unknown embed URLs on the allowed host trigger full feed downloads/imports synchronously, causing significant load and possible abuse. Feed polling should stay scheduled/globally debounced.

title: postMessage origin check uses substring match
body: The embed script accepts a postMessage event if discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) !== -1. This substring/prefix match can accept a different origin, for example https://forum.example.co matches https://forum.example.com/. Compare e.origin to the exact origin parsed from discourseUrl.

title: postMessage target is the full referer and is interpolated into JavaScript
body: The embed layout sends parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>'). postMessage targetOrigin should be an origin (scheme/host/port), not a full referer URL; path/query can make the browser reject the target. The referer header is also interpolated into JavaScript; use URI(request.referer).origin and JavaScript-escape it.

title: Throttle key set with separate SETNX and EXPIRE
body: TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently? creates the Redis throttle key with setnx and then calls expire separately. If the process crashes between those calls, the key has no TTL and the URL is throttled forever. Use an atomic SET ... EX 60 NX operation.

title: content_sha1 updated even if post revision fails
body: When an existing embed's content changes, TopicEmbed.import calls PostRevisor#revise! and then updates topic_embeds.content_sha1 without checking whether the revision saved successfully. If the post update fails, the embed record is marked as up to date and future imports will skip it, leaving the SHA and post content inconsistent.

title: revise! returns true even when Post#save fails
body: PostRevisor#update_post ignores the return value of @post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations]), yet revise! returns true if the raw text changed. Callers can therefore believe a post was updated when it was not persisted. Check the save result and surface errors.

title: PostCreator side effects are not rolled back if TopicEmbed creation fails
body: TopicEmbed.import wraps PostCreator#create and TopicEmbed.create! in a Topic.transaction. PostCreator performs non-transactional side effects such as enqueuing jobs before TopicEmbed.create! runs; if TopicEmbed.create! fails, for example due to a uniqueness race on embed_url, the transaction may roll back the post while the enqueued jobs remain. Create/verify the embed record before triggering post-creation side effects or handle the race explicitly.

title: Migration uses create_table force: true, which drops existing data
body: The changed migration now creates top_topics with force: true. In Rails this drops the table if it exists before recreating it. If the table already exists in any environment, existing top_topics data can be destroyed. Use a guarded create_table or a separate migration.

title: New gems are not added to the Rails 3 lockfile
body: The Gemfile adds ruby-readability and simple-rss, but only Gemfile_rails4.lock is updated. When RAILS3 mode is used, Bundler uses the default Gemfile.lock; if that lockfile lacks the new gems, installation/booting will fail. Update all supported lockfiles or remove Rails 3 dual-boot support.

title: Non-standard X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL header
body: EmbedController sets response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = 'ALLOWALL'. ALLOWALL is not a standard X-Frame-Options value and is ignored by some browsers, so it does not reliably restrict framing. If only the configured embeddable host should frame the page, use CSP frame-ancestors with that origin.

title: Flexing .small-action breaks its float-based right-aligned button
body: Adding flexbox to .small-action makes its direct children flex items, so the existing float declarations on .topic-avatar and button are ignored. The button that previously used float:right will no longer be positioned at the right edge; without flex-grow on .small-action-desc, justify-content spacing, or margin-left:auto on the button, it will render immediately after the description text. This is likely a visual regression wherever small-action buttons appear.

title: align-items mixin passes standard values to prefixed properties unchanged
body: The mixin forwards $alignment directly to legacy prefixed properties such as -webkit-box-align and -ms-flex-align. Standard align-items values like flex-start and flex-end are not valid for those legacy syntaxes, which expect start/end. Current call sites only use center and baseline, but this reusable mixin will silently produce incorrect alignment for common future uses unless values are mapped.

title: align-items mixin emits invalid -ms-align-items property
body: The mixin outputs -ms-align-items, which is not a recognized Microsoft flexbox property. IE10/old Edge used -ms-flex-align, which is already emitted on the previous line. The invalid declaration only adds dead CSS and can confuse linting or debugging, so it should be removed.

title: order mixin uses legacy ordinal-group values incorrectly
body: The order mixin emits the same numeric value for standard order and legacy -webkit-box-ordinal-group / -moz-box-ordinal-group. The old ordinal-group property is 1-based, while standard order is 0-based, so order(0) or mixed positive/negative ordering can behave inconsistently or invalidly in legacy browsers. The legacy value should be adjusted, typically $val + 1, or the legacy declarations should be omitted unless specifically required.

title: Flexing .small-action breaks its right-aligned button
body: `.small-action` is now a flex container, but its `button` still relies on `float: right` (line 309). Floats are ignored for flex items, so the button will be laid out directly after `.small-action-desc` instead of being pinned to the right edge. Add `margin-left: auto` to the button or use an appropriate flex alignment/justify setting.

title: align-items mixin omits -moz-box-align
body: `flexbox()` and `inline-flex()` emit `-moz-box`/`-moz-inline-box`, but `align-items()` only emits `-webkit-box-align`, `-webkit-align-items`, `-ms-flex-align`, and standard `align-items`. In older Firefox using the Mozilla box syntax, alignment will not be applied to `.d-header .contents`, `.small-action`, or `.badge-wrapper.bullet`, causing vertical misalignment. Add `-moz-box-align: $alignment;` (with any needed value mapping).

title: Button will no longer be right-aligned in .small-action
body: Adding `@include flexbox()` to `.small-action` makes it a flex container, but the action button still relies on `float: right` (line 309). Floats are ignored for direct children of a flex container, so the button will be placed in source order after the description instead of being pushed to the right edge. Use `margin-left: auto`, `order`, or another flex mechanism to position the button.

title: Header right alignment lacks a fallback for the prefixed flex syntaxes
body: `.d-header .panel` is now positioned with `margin-left: auto` inside `.d-header .contents`, and the previous float-based layout was removed. Auto-margin alignment is not supported by the old `-webkit-box`/`-moz-box` flex syntaxes emitted by the new mixins, and non-flex browsers have no fallback. In those environments the panel may not be pushed to the right, breaking the header layout.

title: align-items mixin omits -moz-box-align and emits an invalid -ms property
body: The `align-items` mixin outputs `-webkit-box-align`, `-webkit-align-items`, `-ms-flex-align`, and standard `align-items`, but it does not output `-moz-box-align`. Since `flexbox()`/`inline-flex()` emit `-moz-box`/`-moz-inline-box`, old Firefox layouts are being targeted, yet alignment will not apply there. The mixin also outputs `-ms-align-items`, which is not a valid property. This can break vertical alignment in header, small-action, and badge layouts in legacy Firefox.

title: order mixin does not translate values for legacy ordinal groups
body: `order()` passes the modern `order` value directly to `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group`. The old box syntax uses 1-based ordinal groups and does not have the same zero/negative semantics as modern flex `order`, so values such as `0` or `1` will not behave correctly in legacy WebKit/Firefox. If these prefixes are meant to be supported, the mixin should convert the value (commonly `$val + 1`) or avoid emitting legacy properties.

title: website_name bypasses untrusted user-field restrictions
body: The new website_name attribute is added to the public attributes, but it is not added to untrusted_attributes (lines 105-111) like website is. For a TL0 user viewed by an anonymous user, scope.restrict_user_fields? will hide website, but website_name will still be computed from object.user_profile.website and serialized, leaking the hidden website host/path. website_name should be subject to the same untrusted restriction.

title: Serializer inclusion guard is missing the required question mark
body: Discourse/ActiveModel serializers use include_<attribute>? methods to decide whether an attribute is serialized. include_website_name without the trailing question mark will not be used as the inclusion hook, so the intended website.present? guard is not applied. This can serialize website_name even when it should be omitted, and may include nil values when no host can be parsed. Rename it to include_website_name? or rely on untrusted_attributes.

title: Hostname comparison is naive and can produce incorrect website_name values
body: The same-domain logic compares raw DNS label counts and suffixes instead of registrable domains. It can treat unrelated hosts as equivalent under shared public suffixes (for example forum.github.io vs evil.github.io, or hosts under co.uk-style suffixes) and misses some true same-registrable-domain cases such as example.com vs www.example.com when the instance hostname is the apex. This causes the wrong display name to be shown.

title: Untrusted attribute spec does not cover website_name
body: The test that asserts untrusted attributes are omitted for a TL0 user seen anonymously lists website but not website_name. Because website_name is derived from the restricted website field, the spec should include :website_name and assert that it is absent; otherwise the privacy regression is not caught.

title: website_name is not hidden by the untrusted-attribute rules
body: `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes`, so it is suppressed for TL0 users when anonymous viewers are restricted, but the new derived attribute `website_name` is not. Since `website_name` exposes the host/path of the same user-supplied website, anonymous users can see the website URL (or parts of it) via `website_name` even when `website` itself is hidden. Add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` or apply the same `scope.restrict_user_fields?` check.

title: include_website_name is missing the question mark expected by the serializer
body: Discourse/ActiveModel::Serializer inclusion gates use `include_<attribute>?` (e.g. `include_email?`, `include_stats?`). The method is named `include_website_name`, so it will not be called to decide whether `website_name` should be serialized. The intended `website.present?` condition is therefore ineffective, and the field may be serialized even when blank or invalid. Rename it to `include_website_name?` or rely on `untrusted_attributes` for the inclusion logic.

title: Same-domain check misses website subdomains of the Discourse host
body: The logic appends the path when the hosts are equal, when both have the same label count and share a suffix, or when the Discourse host is a subdomain of the website host. It does not handle the common reverse case where Discourse is on the apex domain and the user's website is a subdomain, e.g. Discourse `example.com` and website `http://www.example.com/user`. In that case `discourse_host.ends_with?(".www.example.com")` is false, so only the host is shown even though it is the same site. The comparison needs to handle this direction too, ideally using registrable-domain logic.

title: Domain comparison is naive and can match unrelated public-suffix domains
body: The host comparison treats hosts as equivalent if they share the suffix after removing the first label. This can falsely match unrelated hosts on public suffixes, such as `a.github.io` vs `b.github.io` or `www.gov.uk` vs `forum.gov.uk`, causing the serializer to display the full path for websites that are not actually on the same registered domain as the instance. A proper eTLD+1/registrable-domain comparison would avoid these false positives.

title: Untrusted attribute spec does not cover website_name
body: The spec asserting that TL0 users seen by anonymous do not serialize untrusted attributes lists `website` but omits the new `website_name`. Because `website_name` exposes the same user-supplied website information, it should be included in this list once the serializer treats it as untrusted. Without this coverage, the current leakage of `website_name` for restricted users is not detected.

title: website_name is not refreshed after saving a changed website
body: The profile template now displays the server-generated `model.website_name` instead of computing it from `model.website` on the client. However `User.save` only updates `bio_excerpt` from the PUT response and does not update `website_name` or merge the returned user payload. If a user changes their website in preferences, the locally cached `website_name` can remain stale or nil until the user model is reloaded, whereas the previous client-side computed `websiteName` would have tracked `model.website`. Update the model from the server response or recompute the display client-side.

title: website_name leaks restricted website data for untrusted users
body: The serializer adds website_name as a public attribute, but website is listed in untrusted_attributes and is hidden when scope.restrict_user_fields?(object) applies (for example, a TL0 user viewed anonymously). website_name is derived from the same hidden website value and has no equivalent restriction, so it can expose the user's website host/path even when website itself must not be serialized. It should be treated as untrusted or its inclusion should enforce the same restriction as website.

title: include_website_name is missing the required question mark
body: ActiveModel::Serializer uses include_<attribute>? methods to decide whether an attribute should be serialized. The added method is named include_website_name instead of include_website_name?, so it will never be called. The intended guard based on website.present? is ineffective, and website_name may be serialized unconditionally, including when it is nil or should be omitted.

title: tests do not cover website_name restriction for untrusted users
body: The untrusted-attribute spec lists website but not the newly added website_name, and there is no test asserting that website_name is omitted when a TL0 user is viewed anonymously. Since website_name reveals the same information as website, this missing coverage allows the privacy regression to pass tests.

title: hostname comparison can treat unrelated sites as the same domain
body: The same-domain heuristic strips the first hostname label and compares the remainder, and also uses simple suffix matching. This can classify unrelated hosts that share a parent domain as the same site, such as myforum.github.io and someuser.github.io, causing the full website path to be shown when only the hostname should be shown. A more precise same-site check is needed.

title: Embedded post author link color is inverted relative to the intended light/dark mapping
body: `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` was previously `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new value is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. Since the first argument is the light-theme value, this changes the light-theme link color and uses the inverse of the 30/70 mapping used for other 30% primary values. The result can be poor contrast and inconsistent styling.

title: Mobile custom-message-length color changes the light-theme value and differs from desktop
body: `.custom-message-length` was previously `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The mobile rule now uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, while the desktop equivalent uses 70% primary for the light theme and 30% secondary for the dark theme. This changes the light-theme appearance and is inconsistent with the stated dark-theme correction.

title: Mobile topic-map h3 color does not follow the 20/80 mapping used elsewhere
body: `.topic-map h3` was previously `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` but is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The desktop equivalent keeps 20% primary for the light theme and uses 80% secondary for the dark theme. This appears to be a copy/paste error, reducing heading hierarchy in light themes and not applying the intended dark-theme mapping.

title: Group member name color was changed from 30% to 50% in light theme
body: `.group-member-info .name` was previously `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` but is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. Other conversions of 30% primary text use 30% primary for light themes and 70% secondary for dark themes. This makes group member names lighter in light themes and inconsistent with similar name styles.

title: Mobile group member name color was changed from 30% to 50% in light theme
body: `.group-member-info .name` was previously `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` but is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. Other conversions of 30% primary text use 30% primary for light themes and 70% secondary for dark themes. This makes group member names lighter in light themes and inconsistent with similar name styles.

title: Dark notification badge background is paired with dark `$secondary` text
body: `.badge-notification` keeps `color: $secondary` (and `&[href] { color: $secondary; }`) while the new dark-theme background becomes `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)`. In a dark theme `$secondary` is the dark background color, so both the text and the badge background are dark, making the badge count unreadable. Before this change the dark-theme background was derived from `$primary`, which would be light. The text color or background needs to be adapted for dark themes.

title: Embedded-post author link light-theme color changed from 30% to 70%
body: The diff replaces `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. This changes the light-theme color from a relatively dark gray to a very light gray, making embedded-post author links much fainter than before and inconsistent with similar username links that preserve 30% for light themes. The likely intended value is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

title: Mobile custom-message-length uses inverted light/dark lightness values
body: The original rule used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, and the desktop modal counterpart preserves that light value with a dark value of 30%. This mobile change uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, which changes the light-theme appearance and makes mobile inconsistent with desktop. The values appear to have been inverted accidentally.

title: Mobile topic-map h3 light value changed from 20% to 50%
body: The original mobile style for `.topic-map h3` used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The desktop version preserves 20% for light themes and uses 80% secondary for dark themes, but this mobile change uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. That changes the light-theme heading color and reduces contrast relative to the intended styling.

title: Category badge notification color still uses unconverted `scale-color($primary)`
body: `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still uses `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`, while the rest of the PR converts comparable `scale-color($primary, $lightness: ...)` colors to `dark-light-choose(... scale-color($secondary ...))`. This missed occurrence means dark themes will not use the secondary-derived color, leaving this badge text inconsistent with the rest of the updated styles.

title: Light-theme value appears swapped for embedded post author link
body: The previous rule used scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The replacement uses dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). Since the first argument of dark-light-choose is the light-theme value in these replacements, this changes the existing light-theme color from 30% to 70%. The values look swapped; the light-theme value should remain 30% and the dark-theme value should likely be the lighter secondary variant.

title: Mobile modal custom-message length color percentages were reversed
body: The original color was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%). The change uses dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)). This changes the light-theme appearance and is the inverse of the desktop modal rule, which preserves 70% for the light theme and uses 30% for the dark theme. Unless a visual change is intended, the light-theme value should remain 70%.

title: Notification badge may become low-contrast in dark mode
body: The badge keeps color: $secondary, but its dark-theme background is now scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%). In a dark scheme, $secondary is the dark background color, so both the badge text and background are dark. Notification counts may be difficult or impossible to read; the text color or the dark-theme background needs a contrast-aware adjustment.

title: Topic map heading color changed from 20% to 50% in light theme
body: The original h3 color was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%). The replacement uses 50% for both light and dark themes. This changes the existing light-theme heading color and also gives dark mode a mid-gray heading rather than a lighter equivalent such as 80%, which is closer to the desktop treatment. If the intent was only to add dark-theme support, the original 20% light value should be preserved.

title: Group member name light-theme color changed from 30% to 50%
body: The previous color was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The new dark-light-choose uses 50% as the light-theme value, which changes the existing light-theme appearance rather than only adding a dark-theme variant. If this was not an intentional design change, preserve the original 30% light value and choose a suitable dark-theme equivalent.

title: Mobile group member name light-theme color changed from 30% to 50%
body: The previous color was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The replacement uses dark-light-choose with 50% as the light-theme value, altering the existing light-theme appearance. If the change is only meant to add dark-theme support, the original 30% light value should be preserved.

title: Pagination total pages is off by one when count is a multiple of limit
body: totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is exactly divisible by limit (for example 50 users with limit 50), this returns one extra page. The UI will show and allow navigation to a blank page. Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit), and guard against limit <= 0.

title: Member pagination can keep or request an offset beyond the last page
body: findMembers clamps offset to user_count, but offset == user_count is past the last record; the maximum useful offset is user_count - limit. This can request an empty page, and after deleting the last member on a later page it can leave the UI stuck on an empty page. Clamp offset to Math.max(0, user_count - limit).

title: Public members endpoint does not cap or validate limit
body: members sets limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i with no lower or upper bound. A caller can pass a huge limit and force loading/serializing all group members, or pass 0/negative values causing empty responses, client-side division by zero, or SQL errors. Clamp limit to a positive maximum.

title: Negative offset is accepted and can cause errors
body: offset is taken directly as params[:offset].to_i. A negative offset is invalid for ActiveRecord/SQL and can result in a 500 error. Clamp offset to zero or greater.

title: Group members JSON contract changed from array to object
body: The members endpoint previously rendered a serialized array of users. It now returns an object with members and meta. Any existing API clients expecting an array will break. If this change is intentional, it should be documented or versioned; otherwise maintain backward compatibility.

title: Admin group create/update payload changed incompatibly
body: Create/update now expect flat params and no longer accept the previous nested group[...] payload or usernames during create/update. Existing API clients or plugins using the old contract will fail or silently ignore fields such as usernames and name. If intentional, provide documentation or a compatibility path.

title: Group creation ignores alias_level
body: The client sends alias_level when creating a group, but Admin::GroupsController#create only assigns name and visible. Any alias level selected while creating a group is silently dropped. Assign alias_level on create or remove the control for unsaved groups.

title: Visible flag only accepts the literal string 'true'
body: visible is set with params[:visible] == "true". JSON API clients sending boolean true, or values such as "1", will be treated as false, causing groups to be created or updated as hidden unexpectedly. Use proper boolean casting.

title: add_members parsing is fragile and succeeds silently on invalid input
body: add_members splits usernames on commas, does not strip whitespace, and silently ignores unknown usernames. Input like "bob, alice" or a typo can return success without adding the intended users. It also assumes a String; an array parameter would raise NoMethodError on split. Strip entries, validate usernames, and return errors for invalid input.

title: remove_member automatic-group spec uses the wrong HTTP verb
body: The test for refusing removal from automatic groups uses xhr :put, but the route is declared as DELETE and the successful removal test uses :delete. Controller specs bypass routing, so this does not verify the real endpoint verb.

title: Save error handler assumes response is JSON with errors
body: The failure handler does $.parseJSON(e.responseText).errors. If the server responds with non-JSON output or a JSON body without errors, this throws and the user gets no feedback. Parse defensively and show a generic error message.

title: Total pages is one too high when user count is an exact multiple of limit
body: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. For example, 50 users with limit 50 reports 2 pages instead of 1. This leaves the Next button enabled on the real last page and causes a request for an empty page. Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit), while keeping the zero-count special case.

title: Members endpoint accepts unbounded and negative pagination parameters
body: GroupsController#members casts params[:limit] and params[:offset] to integers without validation. A limit of 0 is returned to clients and can cause division-by-zero in the Ember pagination code, negative limit/offset values can cause SQL errors, and very large limits can dump huge member lists and degrade performance. Clamp limit to a positive maximum and offset to a non-negative value.

title: Public group members page can now show only the first 50 members
body: The members action now always applies a default limit of 50, but the public group members template in this PR has no pagination or load-more mechanism. Previously non-automatic groups were not limited in this way. Users viewing a group with more than 50 members will see an incomplete member list unless the client is updated to paginate.

title: remove_member deletes via users association with a raw user id
body: remove_member calls group.users.delete(user_id), passing an integer ID to an association delete that expects User records or requires explicit removal of the corresponding group_user join record. This can raise an exception, silently fail to remove the membership, or otherwise behave unpredictably while the action may still return success. Use the model's removal method or delete the group_users row for the given user_id.

title: Group creation ignores alias_level sent by the client
body: The admin UI sends alias_level when creating a group and shows the alias-level control for new groups, but Admin::GroupsController#create only assigns name and visible. The selected alias level is silently lost for newly created groups. Assign alias_level in create, or hide/disable the control until the group exists.

title: add_members silently ignores unknown or whitespace-padded usernames
body: add_members splits the comma-separated usernames without stripping whitespace and skips any username that is not found, then returns success. Admins receive no indication that some users were not added, and input like alice, bob can fail for the spaced username. Strip each username and report or reject unknown usernames.

title: Members endpoint response format changed incompatibly
body: The /groups/:group_id/members.json endpoint previously returned a serialized array of members. It now returns an object with members and meta. Any external or mobile clients expecting the old array shape will break. If this endpoint is treated as a public API, provide backward compatibility or version the change.

title: Group edit route does not reset pagination offset before loading members
body: setupController calls model.findMembers without resetting offset. Because the Group model stores offset across navigations, returning to a group can load a previously viewed page or an empty page instead of the first page of members. Reset offset to 0 before the initial findMembers call.

title: addMembers/removeMember resolve before member list is reloaded
body: removeMember and addMembers call self.findMembers inside their success handlers but do not return its promise. Callers that chain the returned promise may continue before the refreshed members and user_count are available, causing stale UI state. Return self.findMembers() from the then handler.

title: Group member pagination total page count is incorrect
body: `totalPages` is calculated as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. For member counts that are an exact multiple of the limit (for example 50 members with a limit of 50), this returns one extra page. The UI will show an incorrect page count and allow navigating to an empty page. It should use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` with a zero-count guard.

title: Public group members endpoint has unvalidated pagination parameters
body: The public members endpoint uses `params[:limit]` and `params[:offset]` without type coercion, bounds, or non-negative validation. A client can pass a very large limit and force serialization of the entire group membership, causing resource exhaustion. Negative limit/offset values can produce invalid SQL errors, and array-style params such as `limit[]=1` can raise because `Array#to_i` is undefined. The values should be coerced to strings/integers and clamped to a safe range.

title: Adding group members fails for usernames with surrounding whitespace
body: `add_members` splits the comma-separated usernames but does not strip each token. Input like `"user1, user2"` produces `" user2"`, which will not match a username and is silently ignored. The parameter should also be coerced to a string, and each username should be stripped before lookup.

title: add_members returns success even when unknown usernames are skipped
body: The action silently ignores usernames that do not match a user and still returns `success_json`, even if none or only some of the requested users were added. The client has no way to know that the operation did not fully succeed. Invalid or missing usernames should be reported in the response.

title: Breaking change to group members JSON response shape
body: The members endpoint previously rendered a serialized array of users, but now returns an object with `members` and `meta` keys. Any existing client or plugin expecting a top-level array will break. If this change is intentional, it should be called out/migrated because it is a public JSON API contract change.

title: Group update treats missing visible parameter as false
body: `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` unconditionally assigns the attribute. A PUT request that omits `visible` will hide the group, and a JSON boolean `true` is also treated as false because it is compared to the string `"true"`. This can cause unintended visibility changes for API clients performing partial updates.

title: remove_member automatic-group test uses the wrong HTTP verb
body: The route for removing a group member is defined as DELETE (`delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`), but this spec calls `xhr :put, :remove_member`. The test therefore does not exercise the actual route verb and could mask routing regressions; it should use `:delete`.

title: Fallback locales are only ensured loaded in web controllers
body: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is only called from `ApplicationController#set_locale`. The translate accelerator's `I18n.translate` loads only `config.locale`, and `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` performs fallback lookups by calling the backend directly for the fallback locales, so it will not trigger loading of the default or English translation files. Any server-side translation done outside this controller before-filter (Sidekiq jobs, mailers, rake tasks, or `I18n.with_locale` blocks) will therefore not have the fallback locales loaded and missing translations will not fall back.

title: Fallback chain can raise when SiteSetting/default locale is unavailable or blank
body: `FallbackLocaleList#[]` calls `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` unconditionally. This method is invoked by I18n during fallback lookups, which can happen early in boot, in rake tasks, or when a translation is missing. If `SiteSetting.default_locale` is nil, blank, or SiteSetting is not ready, this raises instead of falling back (the subsequent `compact` cannot remove a nil because `to_sym` is called first). A missing translation can become an exception.

title: Lazy initialization of @loaded_locales is not thread-safe
body: `ensure_loaded!` initializes `@loaded_locales` with `||=` outside the existing `LOAD_MUTEX`, while `translate` reads `@loaded_locales` without a nil guard and `load_locale` mutates it under the mutex. In a multithreaded process, first-use races can overwrite the array or leave it uninitialized for a thread that calls `translate` first, causing duplicate locale loads or a NoMethodError on `@loaded_locales.include?`.

title: Custom I18n.fallbacks object does not behave like the standard fallback object
body: `I18n.fallbacks` is replaced with a `Hash` subclass that only overrides `[]` and adds `ensure_loaded!`. It returns a new array on every lookup, does not cache fallback chains, and ignores normal hash mutation/assignment. Code or plugins expecting the standard `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks` API (for example `defaults`, cached lookup results, or appending to `I18n.fallbacks[locale]`) will not work and may fail silently.

title: Fallback locales are only loaded for the locale set in controller requests
body: The new call loads fallback locale files only from ApplicationController#set_locale. The translate accelerator still loads only I18n.config.locale in I18n.translate, and I18n backend fallbacks do not invoke that lazy loader for each fallback locale. Any translation performed outside a controller request, after changing I18n.locale later in the same process, or with an explicit :locale option can therefore miss fallback files and return missing-translation strings instead of falling back to the site default or English.

title: Loading fallback locales does not invalidate cached translations
