If `Init` fails, the constructor returns an error without calling the cancel function and without stopping any components that were partially initialized. If lifecycle initialization succeeded, or if `search.init` started its event goroutine before a later watcher failure, those resources and goroutines are leaked on construction failure.

title: handleEvent can panic when IndexMetrics is nil
body: `searchSupport.handleEvent` uses `IndexMetrics.IndexedKinds` for ADDED and DELETED events without checking whether `IndexMetrics` is nil. Other code paths guard this global with `if IndexMetrics != nil`. If metrics are not initialized, processing a watch event will panic.

title: BuildIndex can panic when IndexMetrics is nil
body: `bleveBackend.BuildIndex` increments `resource.IndexMetrics.IndexTenants` without checking whether `resource.IndexMetrics` is nil. Other parts of the code guard this global, so building an index can panic when metrics are not initialized.

title: builderCache.get can return a nil DocumentBuilder without error
body: `builderCache.get` falls back to `s.defaultBuilder` and returns it without error. `newBuilderCache` does not require a default builder unless the configuration list is empty, so for an unregistered group/resource this can return a nil `DocumentBuilder` with a nil error. Callers such as `searchSupport.build` and `searchSupport.handleEvent` then call `BuildDocument` on the nil builder and panic.

title: Bleve index is not closed when BuildIndex fails after creation
body: In `bleveBackend.BuildIndex`, if `getAllFields` or the builder callback fails after `bleve.New` or `bleve.NewMemOnly` has created an index, the function returns without closing the newly created `bleve.Index`. For file-backed indexes this leaks file handles and can leave a locked index directory behind.

title: Poller span is not ended when listLatestRVs fails
body: In `backend.poller`, a span is started on every poll tick. If `listLatestRVs` returns an error, the code resets the ticker and continues without calling `span.End()`. Repeated failures will leak spans and retain tracing state unnecessarily.

title: Postgres coverage is skipped for storage server startup test
body: The integration test now skips all Postgres runs. Since this PR changes startup initialization and indexing behavior, Postgres coverage for the storage server target is lost, and the failure mode that motivated the skip is only annotated with a TODO.

title: Search event consumer does not handle a closed events channel
body: In searchSupport.init, the goroutine consumes events with `v := <-events` in an infinite loop. If the storage backend closes the channel (for example during shutdown), the receive returns a nil *WrittenEvent repeatedly, and handleEvent will dereference evt.Type, causing a panic. There is also no select on a context, so the goroutine cannot be stopped. Use a `for v := range events` loop or select on context/channel-ok and stop cleanly.

title: Resource-server watcher also reads events without handling channel closure
body: In server.initWatcher, the piping goroutine reads `v := <-events` in an infinite loop and then accesses v.ResourceVersion. If the backend closes the events channel during shutdown, this receive returns nil forever and the next field access panics. The loop should range over the channel or select on context and channel-ok.

title: Initial index build can permanently miss writes that happen during startup
body: searchSupport.init builds all initial indexes first and only then calls StorageBackend.WatchWriteEvents. The watch starts from the latest resource version at the time it is created, while the index snapshots were taken earlier. The resource versions returned by the builds are discarded, so writes that occur while the initial index build is running are not replayed into the index. Because startup indexing can take a long time, this can leave search results stale until another write touches the same resources. Start watching before the backfill or replay events from the build resource version.

title: BuildIndex no longer serializes index creation for the same key
body: bleveBackend.BuildIndex now locks cacheMu only when assigning the completed index to the cache. Concurrent callers that see a nil index from GetIndex can therefore build the same NamespacedResource simultaneously. For file-backed indexes this can contend on the same directory, for memory indexes it creates duplicate indexes, and the final assignment can overwrite an existing index without closing it. Use a per-key mutex or singleflight so only one BuildIndex runs for a given key.

title: History and Origin can nil-pointer panic when search is not configured
body: server.History and server.Origin call s.search.History and s.search.Origin without checking whether s.search is nil. NewResourceServer can leave s.search nil when search is not configured, and Search already guards for this case. A History or Origin request in that configuration will panic. Add the same nil-check used by Search.

title: Constructor does not clean up if Init fails
body: NewResourceServer creates a cancelable context and then calls s.Init. If Init fails after starting long-lived work, such as searchSupport.init starting its event consumer before initWatcher is attempted, the constructor returns an error without calling cancel or stopping the started components. This leaks goroutines and the cancel function. On Init failure, cancel the context and stop anything that was started.

title: Data race on totalBatchesIndexed and shared err during index initialization
body: In searchSupport.init, each errgroup goroutine increments totalBatchesIndexed and assigns to the outer shared err variable. With multiple worker goroutines this is a data race, and the error value can be corrupted or racy. Use a local error inside each closure and either return counts through errgroup or use an atomic counter.

title: TotalDocs iterates cache without holding cacheMu
body: bleveBackend.TotalDocs iterates over b.cache without acquiring cacheMu, while BuildIndex writes to b.cache under the write lock. Concurrent map read/write in Go is a data race and can crash. TotalDocs should take cacheMu.RLock for the iteration.

title: Unsynchronized shared writes in search init workers
body: searchSupport.init starts multiple errgroup workers that all increment totalBatchesIndexed and assign to the outer err variable. These are shared variables with no mutex, atomic, or local handling, so concurrent index builds race. The reported indexed count can be wrong, an error can be overwritten, and the Go race detector will fail.

title: BuildIndex can run concurrently for the same namespaced resource
body: The patch removes the global lock around BuildIndex but adds no per-key synchronization or singleflight. GetIndex returns nil until BuildIndex inserts the finished index, so concurrent Search or watch-event calls for the same namespace/group/resource can both start builds. This duplicates work, can open the same file-backed bleve directory concurrently, and lets the last writer replace another live index in the cache without closing it. Add a per-key lock or reserve the key while building.

title: TotalDocs iterates the index cache without locking
body: bleveBackend.TotalDocs ranges over b.cache while BuildIndex may concurrently write to that map. TotalDocs does not take cacheMu.RLock, so this is an unsynchronized map read/write that can panic or return wrong totals. This is more likely now that BuildIndex only locks for the cache insertion.

title: History and Origin dereference s.search without nil checks
body: server.History calls s.search.History and server.Origin calls s.search.Origin, but s.search can be nil when search is not configured. server.Search checks for this case, while History and Origin will panic on a nil pointer if invoked. Add nil checks or return a not-configured error.

title: Watch loop does not handle closed event channel
body: The goroutine started in searchSupport.init receives from events with v := <-events and passes v to handleEvent. If the storage backend closes the channel, the receive returns a nil *WrittenEvent repeatedly, and handleEvent dereferences evt.Type, causing a panic. The loop also has no context.Done branch, so it cannot be stopped cleanly. Use v, ok := <-events and stop when !ok, and select on a cancellable context.

title: IndexMetrics is used without nil checks in handleEvent
body: handleEvent increments and decrements IndexMetrics.IndexedKinds for added and deleted events without checking whether IndexMetrics is nil. Other parts of the code guard with if IndexMetrics != nil. If metrics are not initialized, any ADDED or DELETED watch event will panic.

title: BuildIndex uses IndexMetrics without nil check
body: BuildIndex increments resource.IndexMetrics.IndexTenants unconditionally. Since other code paths check whether IndexMetrics is nil, this can panic when metrics are disabled or uninitialized. Guard the metric calls or guarantee initialization.

title: Constructor leaks context/lifecycle resources when Init fails
body: NewResourceServer creates a cancellable context and may run lifecycle initialization before s.Init. If s.Init returns an error, the constructor returns without calling cancel or stopping lifecycle hooks, leaking the context and any initialized backend resources. Clean up on the error path.

title: Initial index build can miss events written before the watch starts
body: searchSupport.init builds all indexes first and only then calls WatchWriteEvents. Writes that happen while the initial build is running are not included in the built index and are not replayed by the watcher, which starts after the build. In deployments with concurrent writers or other instances, the search index can remain stale until affected resources are written again.

title: Postgres storage-server integration test is skipped
body: The test now skips for GRAFANA_TEST_DB=postgres, so the storage server startup path is not exercised against Postgres in CI. Since this PR changes initialization timing and index building, this reduces coverage for a supported database; the skip should be tied to a tracked fix rather than left as an indefinite TODO.

title: Call to undefined method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()
body: UsernameForm.authenticate calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the superclass UsernamePasswordForm only defines isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) after this change. There is no no-arg overload in the changed file, so this file cannot compile. The call likely needs to pass context.getUser() or a no-arg helper method must be added.

title: Passkey conditional UI is no longer initialized when no user is set
body: The new isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) method returns false when the user is null, and it is used in UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate (line 115) and UsernamePasswordForm.challenge (line 137) to decide whether to call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(). During first-time login and after invalid-username errors, the authentication context has no user, so the WebAuthn challenge and conditional-UI attributes are not added to the login page. This regresses discoverable passkey login and passkey availability after username errors, contradicting the updated tests that expect the webauthn form to be present in those states.

title: Call to undefined isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()
body: UsernameForm.authenticate calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the changed UsernamePasswordForm only defines isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel). No no-argument version is shown in UsernameForm, UsernamePasswordForm, or AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator. As provided, this will not compile; if the intent was to check whether passkeys are enabled for the realm/user, the corresponding method is missing or the call is wrong.

title: Conditional passkeys are disabled when no user is known
body: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) returns false when user is null, and authenticate()/challenge() call it with context.getUser(). Conditional passkeys are expected to be available on the initial login form before a user is identified, so this prevents webauthnAuth.fillContextForm() from running on first login or after invalid-username errors. That removes the passkey/conditional UI from the initial login page and contradicts the updated tests that expect the webauth form before username entry.

title: shouldDisplayAuthenticators not disabled for conditional UI
body: WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator overrides shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() to false so authenticators are not listed, but it does not override shouldDisplayAuthenticators(). During re-authentication context.getUser() is non-null, so WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm() will set SHOULD_DISPLAY_AUTHENTICATORS to true while not setting ALLOWED_AUTHENTICATORS. This can cause the login template to display or expect an authenticator list that the conditional UI intentionally suppresses.

title: Broad exception catch can hide unexpected test failures
body: The test catches Exception when checking that the webauth form is absent. This swallows any unexpected runtime failure (wrong page, stale element, unexpected Selenium error, etc.) and treats it as the expected absence of the element. It should catch NoSuchElementException specifically, here and in the similar block around line 315.

title: Call to undefined isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()
body: UsernameForm.authenticate calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the changed UsernamePasswordForm only defines isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel). No no-arg method is present in UsernameForm, UsernamePasswordForm, or AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator, so this change will not compile. If the intent is to check the current user, call isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()); otherwise add the missing no-arg helper.

title: Conditional passkeys are no longer initialized for user-less first login
body: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) returns false when user is null, and it is used in authenticate (line 115) and challenge (line 137) to decide whether to call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm. The previous code initialized conditional passkey data when no user was known, which is the normal first-login / ID-less passkey scenario. After this change, the initial login page and error states where the user has been cleared will not receive the WebAuthn challenge/attributes, so passkey autofill/passwordless passkey login is unavailable. This regresses first-login passkey behavior and contradicts the tests asserting that //form[@id='webauth'] is present on the initial login page.

title: Update invalidation can miss login-cache invalidation because it uses an organization-aware original model
body: In update(), the original model is fetched via getById(), which wraps the model so isEnabled() also checks whether the linked organization is enabled. registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate() then applies LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate(), which includes the enabled check. If the linked organization is disabled, the original model fails the predicate even though the IDP itself is storage-enabled. An update that makes the IDP unsuitable for login while the organization is disabled (for example setting hideOnLogin or linkOnly to true) can therefore have both original and updated predicates evaluate to false, so no login-cache invalidation is registered. When the organization is later enabled again, stale cached getForLogin results may still include an IDP that should be hidden or link-only. The original state should be evaluated with the raw storage model, or invalidation should be conservative here.

title: getForLogin does not check invalidation of the requested organization
body: getForLogin() only checks whether the realm/fetch-mode cache key is invalid. Unlike getByOrganization(), it does not check whether the supplied organizationId itself has been invalidated. If an organization is updated, disabled, removed, or its IDP association changes in a way that registers an organization invalidation, this method can still serve a stale cached list for that organization. Because the cached list is later resolved only by ID, the result may no longer match the requested organization or login availability.

title: Cached getForLogin results are returned without revalidating login eligibility
body: After a cache hit, getForLogin() resolves the cached internal IDs and returns them without re-applying LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() or verifying that each provider still matches the requested FetchMode and organizationId. Correctness therefore depends entirely on invalidations being perfect. Given the update-invalidation issue with organization-aware enabled state and the missing organization invalidation check, this can return providers that are currently disabled, hidden, link-only, or associated with a different organization. Filtering the resolved models before returning would make the cache robust against missed invalidations.

title: Single per-realm login cache entry grows with every distinct organization search
body: The login cache stores one IdentityProviderListQuery per realm and FetchMode, with internal search keys for each requested organizationId. Every distinct organization ID used in getForLogin is merged into the same cache object. In realms with many organizations, this single cache entry can become large, and each new organization search invalidates and rewrites the whole entry, causing cache churn and potential contention. A per-organization cache key or bounded structure would avoid unbounded growth and repeated invalidation of the shared entry.

title: broker_public changes on realm-level IDPs may not invalidate ORG_ONLY login cache
body: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate() skips invalidation when both old and new models satisfy the login predicate and the organization ID is unchanged. For an IDP with organizationId == null, the predicate is true regardless of the broker_public config. However the default getForLogin(ORG_ONLY, null) query filters by OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC, so changing broker_public on a realm-level IDP can change the ORG_ONLY result set. Because the organization ID remains null, this update can leave the ORG_ONLY login cache stale.

title: Test cleanup removes literal alias 'alias' instead of the created identity provider alias
body: In testCacheIDPForLogin, the cleanup registration uses testRealm().identityProviders().get('alias')::remove instead of using the generated alias such as 'idp-alias-' + i. This does not remove the identity providers created by the test and may cause cleanup failures or state leakage into other tests. The same pattern appears again for the later created idp-alias-20 cleanup.

title: Login cache does not account for organization invalidation or dynamic enabled state
body: getForLogin decides whether to use the cache only by checking isInvalid(cacheKey). It does not check whether the requested organization is invalidated (unlike getByOrganization, which checks isInvalid(orgId)), and the PR does not invalidate these login cache keys when an organization is removed or disabled. Because the organization-aware wrapper's isEnabled() can become false solely due to organization state, and getForLogin returns the resolved models without a final isEnabled() filter, stale cached entries can return providers that are no longer usable for login.

title: Update invalidation can miss BROKER_PUBLIC changes for realm-level providers
body: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate skips invalidation when both old and new models satisfy getLoginPredicate() and the organization ID is unchanged. For providers with organizationId == null, the predicate ignores BROKER_PUBLIC, but the default getForLogin for ORG_ONLY/ALL without a specific organization filters on BROKER_PUBLIC. Toggling that flag on a realm-level provider can therefore change the result set while the login cache remains valid.

title: ORG_ONLY no-organization path may include realm-level providers with BROKER_PUBLIC
body: The onlyOrganizationBrokers branch without a resolved organization calls getForLogin(ORG_ONLY, null) and filters only on isEnabled() and alias. The default getForLogin for ORG_ONLY without an organization adds BROKER_PUBLIC=true but does not require organizationId to be non-null, so a realm-level identity provider with BROKER_PUBLIC=true can be returned and displayed as an organization broker, contrary to the ORG_ONLY contract.

title: Login cache entry can accumulate unbounded organization search keys
body: getForLogin stores results for each distinct organizationId as a separate search key inside a single IdentityProviderListQuery keyed only by realm and FetchMode. In realms with many organizations, this cache entry can grow without bound as different organizations are resolved during login, increasing memory usage and making each invalidation discard all organization-specific login results.

title: Test cleanup registers removal of literal 'alias' instead of the created aliases
body: In testCacheIDPForLogin, cleanup is registered with testRealm().identityProviders().get('alias')::remove instead of using the created alias (for example 'idp-alias-' + i, and similarly at line 425 for 'idp-alias-20'). As a result, the created identity providers are not removed by this cleanup, and the cleanup may attempt to remove a non-existent provider named alias.

title: Login-cache invalidation can be skipped when the original IDP is resolved through an organization-aware wrapper
body: In update(), the original model is loaded with getById(), which returns an organization-aware IdentityProviderModel whose isEnabled() is false when the linked organization is disabled. registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate() then applies LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() to this wrapped original. If the organization is disabled, an update that removes login eligibility (for example hideOnLogin=true, linkOnly=true, or broker.public=false) can be evaluated as false -> false and no login-cache invalidation is registered. When the organization is later enabled, the stale getForLogin cache can still contain the provider, and callers that only re-check isEnabled() may display a hidden, private, or link-only provider. Use the raw delegate model for the original state, or invalidate whenever login-related fields change.

title: getForLogin cache does not react to organization invalidation
body: getForLogin() checks only isInvalid(cacheKey), where cacheKey is realm+FetchMode. It stores organization-specific result sets inside that mode-level cache entry using organizationId as a search key, but it does not check organization invalidation or otherwise tie the entry to organization lifecycle changes. getByOrganization() at least checks isInvalid(orgId). As a result, organization changes such as enable/disable or update do not refresh these cached login lists, so stale organization-scoped IDP lists can be returned until an unrelated IDP change invalidates the mode key.

title: Cached getForLogin results are returned without re-validating login eligibility
body: In the cached path, getForLogin() resolves each cached internal ID and adds the model to the result without verifying that it still satisfies the login criteria (enabled, not link-only, not hidden, and public when organization-linked). The correctness of the cache therefore depends entirely on invalidations being complete. If an invalidation is missed, for example when an IDP is updated while its organization is disabled, this method can return providers that should no longer be available for login. Filtering cached entries before returning them would prevent stale ineligible providers from being exposed.

title: Test cleanup registers removal of the wrong alias
body: testCacheIDPForLogin creates providers with aliases idp-alias-0 through idp-alias-19 and later idp-alias-20, but registers cleanup for the literal alias instead of the generated alias. The created providers are therefore not removed, leaving test data behind and potentially affecting other tests. The same problem occurs at line 425. Cleanup should use the actual provider alias.

title: Mode-level login cache can accumulate unbounded organization search keys
body: cacheKeyForLogin() is keyed only by realm and FetchMode, while each distinct organizationId queried is stored as another search key inside the same IdentityProviderListQuery. There is no eviction of individual organization search keys; adding a new one invalidates and replaces the whole entry. In realms with many organizations this cached object can grow large and cause extra invalidation/replication overhead. Consider keying by organization or limiting/evicting search keys.

title: Possible NullPointerException in remove() for a nonexistent alias
body: remove() fetches storedIdp from the delegate before deletion. If the alias does not exist and isInvalid(cacheKey) is true, storedIdp is null and registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp) dereferences it, causing a NullPointerException. This can turn removal of a nonexistent alias into an internal error in some cache states. Guard against a null storedIdp before registering invalidation.

title: New order() method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: CryptoProvider is loaded via ServiceLoader and can be implemented outside this repository. Adding `int order()` as a non-default interface method breaks source and binary compatibility for existing providers: older implementations will fail to compile against the new API and may throw AbstractMethodError at runtime when CryptoIntegration sorts them. A default method should be provided instead.

title: Multiple providers with equal order are selected silently and non-deterministically
body: detectProvider now loads all registered CryptoProviders, sorts them by order descending, and returns the first one. All full providers in this PR return the same order (200), so if more than one real provider is present (for example default and FIPS/Elytron), the selected provider depends on ServiceLoader/classpath ordering. The previous fail-fast behavior was removed and ignored providers are only debug-logged. This can silently select an unintended crypto provider, with security-sensitive consequences. Consider failing on ties for the highest order, or at least logging a warning and assigning distinct orders.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns an arbitrary keystore provider
body: AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider returns the provider of a default KeyStore instance. The CryptoProvider contract asks for the BouncyCastle security provider, but this code may return any JCA provider depending on the JVM configuration. Callers that rely on the returned provider name or capabilities may fail with NoSuchAlgorithmException or use an unintended provider. An explicit fallback should be used instead of repurposing a keystore provider.

title: Indefinite-length ASN.1 values are not handled safely
body: readLength returns -1 for indefinite-length encoding, but callers do not support this value. readSequence will silently stop parsing, while readInteger/readNext can end up passing a negative or otherwise invalid length to read(int), causing NegativeArraySizeException or reading incorrect bytes. Malformed ASN.1 input should be rejected with IOException rather than causing undefined behavior.

title: Zero-length INTEGER causes NumberFormatException instead of IOException
body: readInteger reads the length and then constructs a BigInteger from the read bytes. If a malformed DER INTEGER has length 0, `new BigInteger(bytes)` throws NumberFormatException, an unchecked exception, instead of the IOException used for other ASN.1 parsing failures. The parser should validate that the integer length is positive and throw IOException for malformed input.

title: integerToBytes silently discards leading bytes of oversized coordinates
body: In the ECDSA conversion, when BigInteger.toByteArray() returns more bytes than the expected coordinate length, integerToBytes copies only the last qLength bytes without verifying that the discarded leading bytes are zero. A valid positive integer may be one byte longer due to a DER sign byte, but a larger or corrupted value will be silently truncated, producing an incorrect concatenated R/S signature. The method should reject oversized values or verify that all dropped bytes are zero.

title: ECDSA tests do not use algorithm-appropriate curves or verify signatures
body: The test generates a default EC key pair and uses it for ES256, ES384, and ES512, so the larger algorithms are not exercised with their expected curves or key sizes. It also only checks that concatenated R/S values round-trip through the converter; it never verifies that the DER-encoded signature produced by concatenatedRSToASN1DER is accepted by Signature.verify, nor does it cover edge cases such as coordinates with leading zeros or the high bit set. Add curve-specific key generation and signature verification tests.

title: New non-default order() method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: CryptoProvider is a public service-loader interface. Adding `int order()` as a non-default method breaks source and binary compatibility for any external or extension implementation compiled against the previous interface. Such implementations will fail to compile, or fail at runtime with an AbstractMethodError/NoSuchMethodError when CryptoIntegration sorts discovered providers. A default method would preserve compatibility.

title: Multiple CryptoProviders are now silently resolved, including equal-order ties
body: detectProvider no longer fails when multiple CryptoProvider implementations are present; it instantiates all of them, sorts by order, and selects the first. Default, Elytron, and FIPS providers all return order 200, so if two are accidentally present the chosen provider depends on ServiceLoader/classpath ordering. This can silently select the wrong crypto implementation. It also means ignored providers are still constructed; providers such as FIPS1402Provider register JCA providers and modify global security properties in their constructors, so an ignored provider can still affect the JVM.

title: ECDSA conversion does not validate raw signature length
body: concatenatedRSToASN1DER assumes the raw concatenated ECDSA signature has exactly `signLength` bytes and immediately copies `signLength / 2` bytes from it. If a malformed signature is shorter than expected, this throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of IOException; if it is longer, extra bytes are silently ignored. The method should validate `signature.length == signLength` and reject invalid input with IOException.

title: ECDSA integer-to-bytes conversion silently truncates or mishandles invalid values
body: integerToBytes copies only the last `qLength` bytes when a parsed BigInteger encoding is longer than expected, silently truncating an oversized r/s value. It also does not reject negative ASN.1 INTEGER values; converting a negative BigInteger with zero padding produces an incorrect unsigned fixed-length octet string. Malformed ECDSA signature components should be rejected rather than transformed.

title: Indefinite-length ASN.1 encoding is not handled
body: readLength can return -1 for indefinite-length encoding, but readInteger passes that value directly to read(int), causing NegativeArraySizeException. readSequence also treats -1 as an empty sequence instead of rejecting the input. DER-encoded ECDSA signatures should not use indefinite length; the decoder should throw IOException when it encounters this case.

title: Sequence parsing is not strict about lengths or trailing data
body: readSequence subtracts each child TLV length from the declared sequence length but does not verify that a child length fits within the remaining sequence bytes, so malformed overlong children can make the remaining length negative without error. It also does not verify that all input bytes were consumed after parsing the sequence, allowing trailing garbage after the DER sequence. Cryptographic signature parsing should reject such malformed DER input.

title: ECDSA tests do not use curve-specific keys or verify signatures
body: The test generates one default EC key pair and uses it for ES256, ES384, and ES512, then only asserts that DER-to-concatenated and concatenated-to-DER conversions round-trip. It does not verify that the converted signature is valid for the expected curve/key size, nor does it use P-256, P-384, and P-521 keys or known test vectors. This can miss incorrect handling of curve-specific signature lengths or malformed signatures.

title: New abstract order() method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
body: CryptoProvider is a public extension point. Adding int order() without a default method breaks source and binary compatibility for external implementations. At runtime CryptoIntegration.detectProvider sorts providers with Comparator.comparingInt(CryptoProvider::order), so an older implementation that does not have this method will cause AbstractMethodError. A default method should be added to preserve compatibility.

title: Provider selection is nondeterministic when order values tie
body: detectProvider sorts providers only by order() in descending order. DefaultCryptoProvider, FIPS1402Provider and WildFlyElytronProvider all return 200. If multiple providers with the same highest order are present on the classpath, the selected provider depends on ServiceLoader/classpath iteration order. Since the previous fail-fast behavior for multiple providers was removed, a misconfigured classpath may silently select an unintended provider. A deterministic tie-breaker or an error on equal highest order would be safer.

title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns an unrelated JCE provider
body: CryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider is documented as returning the BouncyCastle, or FIPS BouncyCastle, provider. AuthzClientCryptoProvider instead returns the provider of the default KeyStore type, which may be SUN, SunJSSE, or another unrelated provider. Callers that rely on the returned provider or its name may attempt to use algorithms that are not provided or may get unexpected behavior. If no BouncyCastle provider is available, returning null or a clearly documented fallback would be less misleading.

title: ECDSA raw-to-DER conversion does not validate signature length
body: concatenatedRSToASN1DER computes len = signLength / 2 and copies len bytes from offset 0 and len bytes from offset len without checking that signature.length == signLength, that signLength is positive, or that it is even. If the supplied signature is shorter than expected, System.arraycopy throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException; if it is longer, trailing bytes are silently ignored. Malformed input should be rejected with IOException or IllegalArgumentException.

title: integerToBytes silently truncates oversized or malformed integers
body: In asn1derToConcatenatedRS, integerToBytes copies the last qLength bytes whenever BigInteger.toByteArray() is longer than qLength. This is only correct when the extra byte is a leading zero sign byte for a positive integer. The method does not check that the BigInteger is positive, that the value fits in qLength, or that discarded bytes are zero. A malformed or oversized DER integer can therefore be silently converted into an incorrect fixed-length R/S coordinate instead of being rejected.

title: Indefinite or negative ASN.1 lengths can cause NegativeArraySizeException
body: ASN1Decoder.readLength returns -1 for indefinite-length encoding, but readInteger passes that value directly to read(int), which allocates new byte[length]. Malformed DER input with an indefinite length therefore causes NegativeArraySizeException instead of a controlled IOException. readSequence also treats a -1 length as an empty sequence rather than rejecting it. The decoder should explicitly reject indefinite and negative lengths.

title: readSequence does not enforce the declared SEQUENCE length
body: readSequence subtracts each parsed child TLV length from the declared sequence length and stops when the remaining length is no longer positive. If a child TLV is longer than the remaining declared length, the remaining length becomes negative and parsing stops without error. This accepts malformed DER instead of rejecting it. The parser should throw when the remaining length becomes negative or when the declared content is not consumed exactly.

title: ECDSA conversion test only checks self-roundtrip, not standard DER validity
body: The test converts a Java-produced DER signature to concatenated R/S and back, then asserts that the two concatenated arrays are equal. It does not verify that the regenerated DER signature is accepted by java.security.Signature.verify, and it uses a default EC key pair rather than curve-specific keys for ES384/ES512. A self-consistent but non-standard DER encoding could pass this test while failing interoperability. The test should verify the regenerated DER with the public key and/or use known test vectors for each curve.

title: Client-specific permission check does not fall back to all-clients permission when a resource already exists
body: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String), the all-clients type resource is consulted only when no resource named after the client's ID exists. If a client-specific resource exists (for example because another scope was granted or a resource was left behind), the method evaluates only that resource. A valid permission on the Clients type resource is then ignored for the requested scope, so an administrator who has an all-clients permission can be denied for that client.

title: Null type resource causes NullPointerException in client permission check
body: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String), AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) can return null when the realm does not support the admin authorization schema or when the Clients type resource has not been created. The following call authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) does not check for null, so the permission check throws NullPointerException instead of returning false.

title: Provider event listener can invoke unsupported V2 setPermissionsEnabled
body: registerListener executes cleanup only when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled. However management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled. If both features are enabled, removal events call V2 implementations such as ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled, which throw UnsupportedOperationException. This can break provider event processing or leave old permission data uncleared. The listener should be skipped when V2 is active or should explicitly use the V1 management implementation.

title: getScope can NPE for missing or unknown resource type
body: In AdminPermissionsSchema.getScope, when the authorization schema is supported, the code dereferences SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType).getScopes() without verifying that the map lookup returned a ResourceType. A null or unknown resource type causes a NullPointerException (HTTP 500) rather than a ModelValidationException.

title: Existing admin-permissions clients are not upgraded with Clients scopes/resources
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns immediately if realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is not null. Realms that were initialized before this change therefore do not get the new client scopes (configure, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite) or the Clients all-resource. Existing deployments can then fail scope lookups or evaluate client permissions incorrectly after upgrade.

title: getClientsWithPermission can return the resource-type name and misses all-clients grants
body: ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission adds resource.getName() for every resource of type Clients that grants the scope. This includes the type resource named 'Clients', so the returned set can contain the literal string 'Clients' instead of a client ID. It also only includes individually created client resources; if the caller has an all-clients permission but no individual client resources exist, no real client IDs are returned, which can make client filtering/listing incorrect.

title: getResourceName does not resolve client resources
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName only special-cases Users. For Clients resources it falls back to resource.getDisplayName(), but client resources are created with the client's UUID as the resource name and no display name. As a result, client permissions/resources may be represented with null or raw UUID names instead of a readable client identifier or 'All clients'.

title: Missing coverage for all-clients permission when a client-specific resource exists
body: The new tests exercise single-client permissions and all-client permissions separately, but do not test the case where a client-specific authorization resource already exists and an all-clients permission should still grant access. That scenario covers the fallback logic in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission and would catch regressions where all-clients permissions are ignored once a specific resource exists.

title: Schema initialization does not migrate existing admin-permissions clients to the new Clients type/scopes
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() already exists. This PR adds the Clients resource type and new scopes (configure, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite), but realms that already initialized the admin permissions client with the previous Users-only schema will never get the new scopes or the 'Clients' all-resource. Subsequent client-permission creation or evaluation can fail with validation errors such as missing scopes, or with null type-resource lookups. An idempotent schema sync/migration is needed when the schema changes.

title: Removed-client cleanup is not handled for V2 and may throw when V1 and V2 are both enabled
body: registerListener is now gated on Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (v1), but AdminPermissions.management returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled. If only V2 is enabled, ClientRemovedEvent is ignored and authorization resources/permissions created for the removed client are left orphaned. If V1 and V2 are both enabled, the listener calls ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled, which throws UnsupportedOperationException, causing client-removal event processing to fail. V2 needs its own cleanup path or the listener must explicitly avoid unsupported V2 calls.

title: getClientsWithPermission can return the literal type-resource name instead of client IDs
body: ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission iterates all resources of type 'Clients', which includes the schema's all-resource named 'Clients'. When a type-wide permission grants the requested scope, hasGrantedPermission returns true for that all-resource and the method adds the literal string "Clients" to the returned set. The method contract is to return client identifiers; it neither expands a type-wide grant to actual client IDs nor filters out the type resource. Callers using this set to filter or query clients may miss all clients covered by a type-wide permission or include an invalid identifier.

title: getResourceName does not resolve display names for Clients resources
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName was not updated for the newly added Clients resource type. It only special-cases Users; for Clients it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(). Client resources created by getOrCreateResource are named by the client's database ID and do not have a display name set, so policy/evaluation representations will expose null or a non-human-readable name for client resources.

title: No test coverage for the new map-roles-client-scope permission
body: The PR adds the MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope and ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles, but the added tests only exercise MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE. There is no integration test verifying that a MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE permission allows mapping client roles to client scopes, so this new authorization path is untested.

title: Existing admin permissions client is not migrated when Clients scopes/resource are added
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init returns immediately if realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() already exists. This PR adds a new Clients resource type and new scopes (configure, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite), but realms that already have the admin permissions client will not get the new scopes or the 'Clients' all-resource created. Subsequent client-permission creation/evaluation can fail or silently deny, e.g. getOrCreateResource throws ModelException when a required scope is missing. An update/migration path is needed for existing realms.

title: Possible NullPointerException when all-clients resource cannot be resolved
body: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no client-specific resource exists, the code calls AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) and immediately passes the result to PolicyStore.findByResource. getResourceTypeResource can return null if the authorization schema is not supported for the realm/resource server. In that case this method throws NullPointerException instead of returning false. A null check is needed before using the resource.

title: Individual authorization resources are created without persisting their resource type
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates individual user/client resources with resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId()) but never calls resource.setType(resourceType). ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission then searches with resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE). If individual client resources do not have the type persisted, they will not be found by this query, so clients with individual permissions can be omitted from permission-based filtering, and only type-level resources may be processed. The resource type should be set when creating the resource.

title: getResourceName does not resolve names for Client resources
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName special-cases only the Users resource type. For Client resources it falls back to resource.getDisplayName(), but client resources created by getOrCreateResource are stored with the client's internal ID as the name and no display name. As a result, permission representations/UI can show null or an internal ID instead of a useful client identifier. A Clients branch should resolve the client and return something meaningful such as client_id.

title: Provider-event cleanup is gated on V1 feature and can break or skip cleanup under V2
body: The listener now only runs when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) is enabled. However AdminPermissions.management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled. If both features are enabled, removal events will call setPermissionsEnabled on ClientPermissionsV2, which throws UnsupportedOperationException. If only V2 is enabled, removed clients can leave orphan FGAP authorization resources because no V2 cleanup is performed. The listener should either explicitly exclude V2 and provide V2-specific cleanup/no-op behavior.

title: getClientsWithPermission evaluates every client resource individually
body: ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission iterates over all resources of type Clients and calls root.evaluatePermission for each one. In realms with many clients this becomes an N+1-style authorization evaluation and may make client listing/permission filtering expensive. A batched or cached evaluation strategy may be needed for large realms.

title: No test coverage for the new map-roles-client-scope client permission
body: The PR adds the map-roles-client-scope scope and ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles, but the new client permission tests only exercise MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE. There is no integration test verifying that MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE allows or denies mapping client roles through client scopes, leaving the newly added scope unverified.

title: CLI exit code for recreate changed and 4 repurposed
body: The PR changes RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 and introduces FEATURE_DISABLED=4. Any automation written against the previous runtime behavior, where exit code 4 meant a recreate upgrade was required, may now misinterpret exit code 4 as feature-disabled and may miss the recreate result signaled by exit code 3. Since the guide documents these exit codes as a scripting contract, this change is a backward-incompatible CLI contract change and should be explicitly validated and called out.

title: Exit-code contract for the new feature gate is not tested
body: The PR adds exit code 4 for the disabled rolling-updates feature and changes the recreate exit code to 3, but the distribution tests only assert log messages. testFeatureNotEnabled asserts the error string but does not assert exit code 4, testWrongVersions does not assert exit code 3, and only the metadata subcommand is exercised for the disabled-feature path. Because the documentation presents these exit codes as a scriptable contract, regressions in the exit-code behavior would not be caught.

title: Enabled features are overwritten instead of appended
body: createInitialDeployment calls setEnabledFeatures(List.of(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey())), which replaces any already-configured enabled features in the FeatureSpec. If the shared test fixture or future test setup enables other features, this helper will silently disable them. It should add rolling-updates to the existing enabled-feature list rather than overwrite the list.

title: Test setup replaces enabled features with an immutable list
body: `kc.getSpec().getFeatureSpec().setEnabledFeatures(List.of(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey()))` replaces any already-configured enabled features with a new immutable list. If the base Keycloak CR used for tests already enables other features, they are silently dropped. If later test or operator code tries to modify the enabled-features list, it will throw `UnsupportedOperationException`. Appending to the existing list or using a mutable list would be safer.

title: No test covers operator behavior when update strategy is set without the preview feature
body: The documentation added in this PR states that the operator will fail if the `rolling-updates` preview feature is not enabled, but the integration test only sets `spec.update.strategy` when it also enables the feature. There is no negative test that sets an update strategy while leaving `rolling-updates` disabled and asserts that the operator rejects or fails the CR. Without such a test, the feature-gating behavior can regress unnoticed.

title: Changing recreate exit code from 4 to 3 breaks the documented command contract
body: `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` is changed from 4 to 3, while 4 is repurposed as `FEATURE_DISABLED`. The update-compatibility documentation tells users to rely on the command exit code for automation. If the previous exit code was already consumed by scripts or CI pipelines, this change can cause existing automation to misinterpret a recreate result as feature-disabled, or vice versa, unless this is explicitly treated as a breaking change and documented.

title: Non-zero exit codes are not verified
body: The PR introduces or changes meaningful exit codes (0, 3, 4), but the distribution tests do not assert them. `testFeatureNotEnabled` only checks the error message and does not verify exit code 4, and `testWrongVersions` does not verify exit code 3. Since the documentation presents these exit codes as a contract for automation, regressions in the exit-code behavior would not be caught.

title: Exit-code contract changed for recreate upgrade and reused for feature disabled
body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE is changed from 4 to 3, and the new FEATURE_DISABLED code uses 4. The update-compatibility command is documented as scriptable and its exit codes are part of its contract, so existing automation written against the previous code may now interpret a recreate-required result as feature-disabled. If this breaking change is intentional, it should be explicitly called out; otherwise consider preserving the old code and using a new value.

title: Feature-disabled behavior is not fully tested
body: testFeatureNotEnabled only exercises the metadata subcommand and only asserts the error message. It does not assert the new exit code 4, and it does not cover the identical feature-disabled branch added to UpdateCompatibilityCheck. Adding assertions for the exit code and for both metadata and check subcommands would protect the documented exit-code contract.

title: canManage() treats VIEW permission on all groups as MANAGE
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() calls hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE). This method is used for group-management checks without a specific group, for example GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup(). As a result, a permission granting only 'view' on the Groups resource type can authorize creation or top-level movement of groups. The check should require only MANAGE.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), the code calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) and adds groupResource.getId() to the returned set. hasPermission expects a realm group ID because it looks up the authorization resource by name, and callers such as UsersResource put the returned set into UserModel.GROUPS to filter user searches by group membership. Authorization resource IDs are not realm group IDs, so the returned set is wrong. This breaks user search/count filtering based on group view-members permissions and can cause empty or inconsistent results.

title: Per-instance authorization resources are created without a resource type
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() creates authorization resources for individual clients, groups, and users but never calls resource.setType(resourceType). Only the type-level resources created during init() have a type. Consequently type-based lookups such as resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) in GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission cannot find instance resources, breaking enumeration of groups with permissions.

title: No migration of scopes/resources for existing admin-permissions clients
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns immediately if realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already present. Existing realms that initialized V2 before this change will not receive the new Groups scopes or the Groups type resource. Subsequent use of group permissions can fail with missing scopes or null type resources. Initialization should idempotently add missing scopes/resources to existing admin-permissions clients.

title: Provider event cleanup is incompatible with V2 group permissions
body: On GroupRemovedEvent the listener calls management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false). When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 and groups() returns GroupPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException. This can cause group deletion failures or swallowed errors. If the V1 feature is disabled, the listener is not registered at all and V2 authorization resources may be orphaned. A V2-aware cleanup path is needed.

title: getScope can throw NullPointerException for unknown or missing resource type
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getScope() validates schema scopes with SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType).getScopes() without checking whether resourceType is null or whether the map lookup returns null. Invalid or missing resource types will cause a NullPointerException instead of a ModelValidationException.

title: Fallback to all-groups resource can NPE if the type resource is missing
body: GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission() falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) and then calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource). getResourceTypeResource can return null if the Groups type resource was not initialized, leading to a NullPointerException. The same pattern exists in UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission. The code should handle a missing type resource gracefully.

title: getResourceName does not handle the new Groups resource type
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName() only special-cases Users resources. For Groups resources it falls back to resource.getDisplayName(), but group instance resources are created with the group ID as the name and no display name. Administrative UI or policy representations may therefore show blank names for group resources.

title: Javadoc for requireManageMembers is incorrect
body: The Javadoc for requireManageMembers says it throws ForbiddenException if canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false, but implementations check canManageMembers(GroupModel). The same interface also documents getGroupIdsWithViewPermission as returning a Stream while the method returns a Set.

title: Global group manage check grants manage for VIEW permission
body: `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` returns true when the caller has either `VIEW` or `MANAGE` on the all-groups resource (`hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`). The no-argument `canManage()` is used by `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup()` through `requireManage()`. A scope permission granting only `view` on `Groups` therefore allows creating or moving top-level groups, which is a privilege escalation. The check should require only `MANAGE`.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
body: `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is used to populate `UserModel.GROUPS` for user queries and counts. In V2, group instance resources are named by the realm group ID (`AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup()` returns `group.getId()`), but this method adds `groupResource.getId()` (the internal authorization resource ID) and also passes that value to `hasPermission()`, which expects a group ID and looks the resource up by name. The returned set therefore does not contain realm group IDs, so user search/count filtering by group permissions is wrong. It should use `groupResource.getName()` for both the lookup and the returned set.

title: Instance resources are created without a resource type
body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource()` creates instance resources for `Clients`, `Groups`, and `Users` but never calls `resource.setType(resourceType)`. `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` relies on `resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` to find group instance resources. If instance resources have no type, they will not be returned, so group-scoped `view-members`/`manage-members` permissions are not translated into group IDs for user queries/counts. The created resource should have its type set to `resourceType`.

title: Type-level group member permissions are not handled in getGroupIdsWithViewPermission
body: `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` scans all resources of type `Groups`, which includes the type-level resource named `Groups` representing all groups. If a permission grants `view-members`/`manage-members` on all groups, this method either adds the type resource identifier (currently the wrong ID, but even with `getName()` it would be the literal string `Groups`) or cannot represent the grant as a set of group IDs. User count/search APIs that use this set will not reflect all-groups member permissions. The method needs explicit handling for the type-level resource.

title: Unsupported operations are thrown from V2 group permission management while existing code still calls them
body: `GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled()` (and `isPermissionsEnabled()`) throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. However `AdminPermissions.registerListener()` calls `management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false)` on `GroupRemovedEvent` when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled, and `GroupResource` management/permissions endpoints call `isPermissionsEnabled`/`setPermissionsEnabled`. If V1 and V2 fine-grained authz features are both enabled, group deletion or these endpoints can fail with an exception/500. For V2, cleanup/disable should be a no-op or the endpoints/listener must be guarded; throwing from lifecycle event handling is unsafe.

title: Group-based user creation only checks V1 fine-grained authz feature
body: `UsersResource.canCreateGroupMembers()` returns false unless `Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled. This PR implements V2 fine-grained authz group scopes (`ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2`), and `AdminPermissions.evaluator()` may use V2 even when the V1 feature is disabled. In that configuration, callers with V2 `manage-members`/`manage-membership` group permissions cannot create users with initial group membership because the fallback permission check is skipped. The check should also consider V2/admin permissions enabled.

title: Possible NullPointerException in getScope for missing/unknown resource type
body: In `AdminPermissionsSchema.getScope()`, when the authorization schema is supported, the code calls `SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType).getScopes()` without checking whether `resourceType` is null or present in the map. An invalid or missing resource type will cause an NPE and HTTP 500 instead of a validation error. It should validate `resourceType` and throw a `ModelValidationException`.

title: Fallback to all-groups resource can NPE when type resource is unavailable
body: `GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission()` falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` and immediately calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)`. `getResourceTypeResource()` can return null if the realm does not support the schema or the type resource has not been initialized. The method should null-check the fallback resource and return false instead of throwing NPE.

title: getResourceName does not resolve Groups resources
body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName()` special-cases only `USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE`. For `Groups`, instance resources are stored with the group ID as the name and no display name is set, so this method returns `resource.getDisplayName()` (likely null) or the raw ID instead of a useful group name/path, and it does not return a label for the all-groups type resource. This can degrade or break UI/API representations of permissions referencing groups.

title: No coverage for user count/query filtering driven by getGroupIdsWithViewPermission
body: The tests verify user search after granting group `view-members`, but they do not verify `/users/count` or paginated query behavior that relies on `GroupPermissionEvaluator.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`. Because the V2 implementation of that method is broken for group resources, the missing coverage allows incorrect count/query filtering to pass. Add tests for user counts and paginated search with group member permissions.

title: Global group manage check treats VIEW as MANAGE
body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when the caller has either the VIEW or MANAGE scope on the all-groups resource. This global check is used by GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() through auth.groups().requireManage(), so a caller who only has 'view' on Groups can create top-level groups. The manage check should evaluate only the MANAGE scope.

title: Individual authorization resources are created without a resource type
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() creates individual resources for groups, users, and clients with resourceStore.create(...) and updates their scopes, but it never calls resource.setType(resourceType). GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() later looks up group resources with resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...). Because individual group resources have no type, that query only finds the type-level 'Groups' resource and misses all per-group resources, breaking group-restricted user queries and counts.

title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
body: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), the code evaluates and stores groupResource.getId(). For V2 group resources, the actual group ID is the resource name, not the authorization resource ID. The returned set is later used as group IDs for user search/count filtering (UserModel.GROUPS), so filtering is done with internal authorization IDs, and may also include the 'Groups' type resource. This makes group-based user search restrictions, pagination, and user counts incorrect. The method should use the resource name as the group ID, skip the type-level resource, and handle all-groups permissions explicitly.

title: Group removal listener is not V2-aware and can throw UnsupportedOperationException
body: AdminPermissions.registerListener() registers a GroupRemovedEvent listener that calls management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false). When V2 admin permissions are enabled, management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 and GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled() throws UnsupportedOperationException. Depending on feature configuration, this can either make group deletion fail with an exception or leave V2 authorization resources orphaned. The listener needs V2-aware cleanup or a safe no-op.

title: Group management/permissions endpoints can return 500 under V2
body: GroupResource.getManagementPermissions() calls permissions.groups().isPermissionsEnabled(group), and the corresponding PUT endpoint calls setPermissionsEnabled(). GroupPermissionsV2 implements these methods by throwing UnsupportedOperationException. If the V2 feature is active and the V1 feature gate allows the endpoint, requests to /groups/{id}/management/permissions will fail with HTTP 500 instead of returning a safe disabled state or a proper unsupported response.

title: Impersonation evaluation uses the target user's identity when a requester client is provided
body: UserPermissionsV2.canImpersonate(UserModel user, ClientModel requester) builds a DefaultEvaluationContext with UserModelIdentity(root.realm, user), i.e. the identity of the user being impersonated, and then evaluates the IMPERSONATE scope. This means the caller/requester identity is not used for the permission evaluation when a requester client is present. Policies granting the calling client or admin the right to impersonate may not match, while policies tied to the target user may control the result. canClientImpersonate() delegates to this method, so client-initiated impersonation authorization is likely incorrect.

title: Group count endpoint ignores fine-grained group permissions
body: GroupsResource.getGroupCount() only calls requireList() and then returns realm-wide group counts via getGroupsCountByNameContaining() or getGroupsCount(). Because canList() can be true through QUERY_GROUPS while GET /groups is filtered by canView(group), a caller who cannot view any groups can still learn the total number of groups and the number of groups matching a search string. The count should be filtered using the same permissions as the group listing.

title: NullPointerException in getScope for missing or unknown resource type
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getScope() calls SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType).getScopes() without checking whether resourceType is null or present in the map. A request creating or updating a scope permission with a missing/invalid resource type can therefore cause a NullPointerException and HTTP 500 instead of a validation error.

title: Possible NullPointerException when the all-groups resource is missing
body: GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission() falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) when a specific group resource is not found, then immediately calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource). getResourceTypeResource() can return null if the schema is not supported or the type resource was not initialized, leading to a NullPointerException. The same pattern exists in UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission().

title: Group permission lookup evaluates every group resource on user searches
body: GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() iterates over all Group resources and performs a full policy evaluation for each one. This method is invoked by user search/count endpoints such as UsersResource and BruteForceUsersResource whenever the caller lacks global user view permission. In realms with many groups, every restricted user search can trigger O(number of groups) authorization evaluations, which may be very slow.

title: Group resource names are not resolved for display
body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName() only resolves resource names for the Users resource type. For Groups resources it returns resource.getDisplayName(), but individual group resources are created with the group ID as the name and no display name. As a result, authorization policy UIs or representations may show an empty or meaningless identifier instead of the group name/path. A GROUPS case should resolve the group and return a useful name.

title: Java MessageFormat/choice syntax used in an i18next-based UI message
body: The account UI message 'error-invalid-multivalued-size' was changed from i18next-style interpolation ('{{0}}', '{{1}}', '{{2}}') to Java MessageFormat syntax ('{0}', '{2,choice,...}'). The surrounding account-ui messages still use '{{...}}' placeholders and react-i18next/Trans tags such as '<0>', so this value will not be formatted by the UI. Users will likely see the literal pattern, including the raw choice expression, instead of a localized validation message.

title: Java MessageFormat/choice syntax used in an i18next-based admin UI message
body: The admin UI message 'error-invalid-multivalued-size' was changed from i18next-style interpolation ('{{0}}', '{{1}}', '{{2}}') to Java MessageFormat syntax ('{0}', '{2,choice,...}'). Admin UI message resources generally use '{{...}}' interpolation, so this key will not be substituted or pluralized client-side. The UI will display the raw MessageFormat/choice pattern instead of a properly formatted error message.

title: PropertyResourceBundle is constructed from an InputStream and will not read UTF-8 properties reliably
body: verifySafeHtml() creates PropertyResourceBundle directly from FileInputStream for both the checked file and its English counterpart. PropertyResourceBundle(InputStream) uses the legacy ISO-8859-1 properties encoding, while Keycloak theme message files in this PR contain UTF-8 translated text. Non-ASCII message contents will be mangled before sanitization/comparison, which can cause false positives, false negatives, or confusing verifier diagnostics. Use an InputStreamReader with StandardCharsets.UTF_8 for both bundles.

title: Lithuanian account message replaced with Italian text
body: In the Lithuanian account messages file, 'totpStep1' is now 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', which is Italian. The surrounding messages are Lithuanian, so Lithuanian users will see an Italian instruction line in the account UI/theme.

title: Lithuanian login message replaced with Italian text
body: In the Lithuanian login messages file, 'loginTotpStep1' is now 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', which is Italian. The surrounding messages are Lithuanian, so Lithuanian users will see an Italian instruction line during login/OTP setup.

title: Simplified Chinese account message uses Traditional Chinese characters
body: The zh_CN account messages file sets 'totpStep1' to '在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：', which uses Traditional Chinese characters. This file is for Simplified Chinese (zh_CN), while other entries in the same file use Simplified Chinese, so the text is inconsistent for the locale.

title: Danish email paragraph starts with stray 'n' character
body:
identityProviderLinkBodyHtml contains '

nHvis du ikke vil forbinde disse konti...', where 'nHvis' appears to be a typo for 'Hvis'. Since this line was touched to add the closing '

' tag, the user-visible Danish email text should also be corrected.

title: HTML detection only matches lowercase tag names
body:
HTML_TAGS is '<[a-z]+[^>]*>', so it only detects lowercase HTML tags. If an English source string contains HTML with uppercase or mixed-case tags such as '
' or '', containsHtml() will return false and translations using the same tags will be rejected as illegal HTML even though the source string contains HTML. The tag detection should be case-insensitive or otherwise more robust.

title: English companion file is derived by regex-replacing the whole absolute path
body: englishFile is computed by applying replaceAll('resources-community', 'resources') and replaceAll('_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties', '_en.properties') to file.getAbsolutePath(). This can alter unrelated parts of a path if they contain those strings and assumes the locale suffix pattern appears only once at the end of the file name. It would be safer to resolve the sibling file name and replace only the final locale suffix of the file name.

title: Mismatch trimming can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException
body: When reporting an HTML mismatch, the code computes a common prefix (`start`) and common suffix (`end`) independently and then calls `value.substring(start, value.length() - end)` and `sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end)`. If the common prefix and suffix overlap (for example when one string is the other string plus repeated characters, such as `value="aa"` and `sanitized="aaa"`), `start` can be greater than `length - end`, causing a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. This would abort the verifier with an obscure stack trace instead of reporting a validation message.

title: Message properties are read with ISO-8859-1 instead of UTF-8
body: `new PropertyResourceBundle(fis)` reads the input stream using the ISO-8859-1 charset (via `Properties.load(InputStream)`), while Keycloak message bundles are UTF-8 and the same file is earlier read with `Files.readString`, which defaults to UTF-8. Non-ASCII translations may therefore be misinterpreted, causing false positives, false negatives, or confusing validation failures in the HTML sanitizer. A UTF-8 `Reader` should be used when constructing the bundles.

title: Choice-format normalization bypasses HTML validation
body: `normalizeValue()` replaces the entire `{n,choice,...}` construct with `...` for keys such as `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*` and `error-invalid-multivalued-size` before HTML sanitization. Any HTML placed inside the choice alternatives is therefore never checked by the OWASP sanitizer. If these messages are rendered as HTML, a malicious or malformed translation can smuggle markup through these keys despite the PR’s stated goal of sanitizing translated message resources.

title: Lithuanian account message contains Italian text
body: `totpStep1` in the Lithuanian account messages was changed to `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian. Lithuanian users will see Italian instructions in the account console.

title: Lithuanian login message contains Italian text
body: `loginTotpStep1` in the Lithuanian login messages was changed to `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian. Lithuanian users will see Italian instructions on the login page.

title: Simplified Chinese locale uses Traditional Chinese text
body: `totpStep1` in `messages_zh_CN.properties` uses Traditional Chinese characters such as `手機上安裝以下應用程式之一`, while the `zh_CN` locale is Simplified Chinese. The translation should use Simplified Chinese wording.

title: JUnit 5 tests may not run because Surefire/JUnit engine is not configured
body: The module declares `junit-jupiter-api` but no `junit-jupiter-engine` or other test runtime, and the `maven-surefire-plugin` is declared without a version or explicit JUnit 5 configuration. With Maven defaults, the new JUnit Jupiter tests may be silently skipped, so the added verifier tests may not actually protect the build.

title: Java MessageFormat syntax introduced into an i18next message bundle
body: The account-ui message bundle uses i18next/react-i18next placeholders elsewhere, such as '{{app}}' and '{{date}}'. The changed 'error-invalid-multivalued-size' message now uses '{0}', '{1}', and '{2,choice,...}', which i18next will not interpolate or evaluate as Java MessageFormat. As a result, the account UI will show the raw pattern or a broken validation message when this error occurs. This key should keep i18next-compatible interpolation/pluralization or the UI localization layer needs explicit support for this format.

title: Java MessageFormat syntax introduced into an i18next message bundle
body: The admin-ui message bundle is used with i18next-style interpolation, and this key previously used '{{0}}', '{{1}}', and '{{2}}'. It was changed to '{0}', '{1}', and '{2,choice,...}', which is Java MessageFormat syntax and is not understood by i18next. The admin UI will therefore not substitute the parameters or pluralize the message correctly. This is a user-visible localization/contract break for the admin UI.

title: Lithuanian account message contains Italian text
body: The 'totpStep1' value in the Lithuanian account messages was changed to 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', which is Italian. Lithuanian users will see the wrong language for the OTP setup instruction. The value should be restored to a proper Lithuanian translation.

title: Lithuanian login message contains Italian text
body: The 'loginTotpStep1' value in the Lithuanian login messages was changed to 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', which is Italian. Lithuanian users will see the wrong language during OTP setup. The value should be restored to a proper Lithuanian translation.

title: Property resource bundles are read without explicit UTF-8 decoding
body: verifySafeHtml() constructs PropertyResourceBundle directly from a FileInputStream. That path uses the legacy Properties InputStream loading behavior, which is not appropriate for the UTF-8 theme message files used by Keycloak (Arabic, Chinese, Cyrillic, etc.). Non-ASCII values can be garbled before HTML verification, leading to incorrect validation results or spurious failures. Use an InputStreamReader with StandardCharsets.UTF_8 when creating the PropertyResourceBundle.

title: Choice expressions are stripped before sanitization, hiding any markup they contain
body: normalizeValue() replaces the entire '{n,choice,...}' expression with '...' for linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit* keys and error-invalid-multivalued-size. Any HTML placed inside the choice alternatives is therefore never passed to the OWASP sanitizer. Since these messages can be rendered in HTML themes or emails, markup can bypass the check by being embedded in a choice expression. The verifier should validate the textual choice alternatives instead of discarding the whole expression.
