title: English companion file path is derived with fragile replaceAll regexes
body: The English file path is computed by applying replaceAll('resources-community', 'resources') and replaceAll('_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties', '_en.properties') to the absolute path. This operates on the whole path rather than the file name, so matching substrings outside the message file name can produce a wrong path. It can also fail for locale suffixes not matched by the regex. If the derived path is wrong, verification fails with an inability-to-read-file error. Resolve the English companion from the file name and locale instead of regex-replacing the absolute path.

title: templateHelp normalization removes arbitrary uppercase tags after CLAIM.
body: The normalization for templateHelp removes any uppercase tag following 'CLAIM.' rather than only the intended literal text 'CLAIM.<NAME>'. This hides markup such as 'CLAIM.<B>' or 'CLAIM.<SCRIPT>' from the sanitizer. If this help text is ever rendered as HTML, the verifier could pass unsafe markup. Use an exact quoted replacement for 'CLAIM.<NAME>' or a precise allow-list.

title: Simplified Chinese account message uses Traditional Chinese characters
body: The 'totpStep1' value in messages_zh_CN.properties was changed to '在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：', which uses Traditional Chinese characters. The zh_CN locale should use Simplified Chinese, for example '在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：'.

title: Danish email HTML still contains a stray 'n' before 'Hvis'
body:
identityProviderLinkBodyHtml was fixed to close the final paragraph, but the text still reads '

nHvis du ikke vil forbinde disse konti...'. The leading 'n' appears to be a typo or leftover and will be shown to users. It should be '

Hvis du ikke vil forbinde disse konti...'.

title: Test resource loading uses URL.getFile() without URL decoding
body: getFile() creates a File from resource.getFile(). URL.getFile() does not decode URL-encoded characters such as '%20', so tests can fail when the repository path contains spaces or other characters that are percent-encoded. Use Paths.get(resource.toURI()).toFile() instead.

title: Constructor validates grantType twice instead of rawTokenId
body: AccessTokenContext's constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, 'Null rawTokenId not allowed') instead of checking rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId can therefore be stored and later encoded as the literal string 'null' or produce an invalid token ID. The check should validate rawTokenId, and ideally reject empty values as well.

title: isAccessTokenId matcher does not validate the expected grant shortcut
body: AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId uses items[0].substring(3, 5) and returns false when that value equals the expected grant shortcut. The grant shortcut is at zero-based positions 4 and 5, i.e. substring(4, 6), and the condition should reject mismatches. As written, the matcher checks the wrong two characters and inverts the test, so it does not verify the grant shortcut at all. It also calls substring without checking that the prefix is at least six characters, which can throw for malformed IDs.

title: Grant shortcuts are not validated for format or null values
body: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit reads OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() and stores it directly in maps. The encoder/decoder assumes every shortcut is exactly two characters, because the token prefix must be six characters total, but there is no validation that shortcuts are non-null, non-empty, exactly two characters, or safely unique. A custom grant factory returning a three-character shortcut, which is encouraged by the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory Javadoc saying '3-letters', will produce token IDs that getTokenContextFromTokenId later rejects. A null shortcut will cause a NullPointerException.

title: New getShortcut method is a backward-incompatible SPI change
body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is an existing provider-factory interface, and this PR adds an abstract String getShortcut() method without a default implementation. Existing implementations outside this repository will fail to compile and already-compiled implementations can fail at runtime with AbstractMethodError when Keycloak invokes the new method. If this interface is intended to be implemented by extensions, this should be introduced in a compatible way, for example with a default method or explicit migration guidance.

title: Lazy shortcut map updates bypass duplicate validation and can overwrite mappings
body: getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut lazily insert entries into grantsByShortcuts and grantsToShortcuts when an unknown grant or shortcut is encountered. These lazy updates do not re-run the startup validation for duplicate shortcuts or IDs, so a dynamically available grant with a colliding shortcut can silently overwrite an existing mapping and cause incorrect grant-type resolution. The two maps are also updated separately, so they can be observed in a temporarily inconsistent state.

title: getTokenContextFromTokenId does not handle null or malformed IDs safely
body: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId immediately calls encodedTokenId.indexOf(':') without checking for null, so a null token ID causes a NullPointerException. It also accepts inputs such as 'onrtac:' and creates a context with an empty raw token ID, because AccessTokenContext does not properly validate rawTokenId. If this method is used to parse token IDs from incoming requests, malformed IDs should result in controlled validation errors rather than NPEs or invalid contexts.

title: Constructor validates grantType twice instead of rawTokenId
body: AccessTokenContext's constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") instead of checking rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted and can later be concatenated into the encoded token ID, producing IDs ending with ":null" or causing failures downstream. The validation message is also misleading.

title: Token ID event matcher uses wrong offset and inverted check
body: AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId is intended to verify the 2-character grant shortcut in positions 4-5 of the 6-character token-ID prefix, but it uses items[0].substring(3, 5) and returns false when that value equals expectedGrantShortcut. The offset is wrong and the condition is inverted, so the event assertions do not actually validate the grant encoded in token IDs. This can hide incorrect encoding in tests, and malformed short prefixes can also cause StringIndexOutOfBoundsException.

title: New mandatory getShortcut() breaks existing grant factories
body: Adding String getShortcut() to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory without a default method makes all existing implementations of this factory interface fail to compile. If custom or extension grant factories are supported, this is a breaking SPI change; a default method or compatibility path is needed.

title: Public Context copy constructor removed
body: The PR removes the public copy constructor OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context) while adding the grantType field. Any custom grant implementation or extension that created a copy of a Context will no longer compile. This is an API contract break separate from the added grantType behavior.

title: setFormParams does not refresh grantType
body: OAuth2GrantType.Context.grantType is derived from formParams in the constructor, but setFormParams only replaces formParams and does not recalculate grantType. If form parameters are changed after construction, getGrantType() returns a stale value, which can then be encoded into token IDs or events.

title: Lightweight-token decision uses global session client instead of client session
body: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext determines whether the token is lightweight via AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session), which reads session.getContext().getClient(). The client session context already provides the client; using the global session context can pick the wrong client or throw NullPointerException if the session context client is not set, causing the wrong token-type shortcut to be encoded or token issuance to fail.

title: Grant shortcuts are not validated for format
body: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit reads gtf.getShortcut() and stores it in maps without validating that it is non-null, exactly two characters, and safe for the fixed-width token ID format. A custom grant factory returning null or a longer/shorter shortcut can cause a startup NullPointerException or produce token IDs that cannot be parsed by getTokenContextFromTokenId.

title: Lazy shortcut registration can overwrite existing grant mappings
body: getShortcutByGrantType lazily registers a shortcut for a newly discovered grant by putting it into grantsByShortcuts without checking whether that shortcut already maps to another grant. A dynamically deployed or custom grant with a duplicate shortcut can silently overwrite an existing mapping, so token IDs later decode to the wrong grant type. The same lack of uniqueness validation exists in getGrantTypeByShortcut.

title: Javadoc says 3-letter shortcut but encoder requires 2 characters
body: The Javadoc for getShortcut says 'usually like 3-letters shortcut', but the encoder/decoder in this PR assumes every grant shortcut is exactly two characters, because the total encoded context is fixed at six characters. The documentation should state the actual required format.

title: Constructor validates grantType twice instead of rawTokenId
body: The AccessTokenContext constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") on line 73, so rawTokenId is never null-checked. If a null raw token ID is supplied, the object is created and encodeTokenId can produce an ID ending in ':null' or later code can fail in an uncontrolled way. The check should be Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed").

title: Token ID event matcher uses wrong substring and inverted check
body: AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId checks items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut) and returns false when it is equal. The grant shortcut is the last two characters of the six-character prefix, so the code should use substring(4, 6), and the condition should reject when the value is not equal. As written, for a correct ID such as 'onrtac:...' with expected grant shortcut 'ac', substring(3, 5) is 'ta', so the matcher passes without verifying the grant type. This means the event tests do not actually validate the encoded grant shortcut and can hide regressions.

title: Grant shortcuts are accepted without null or length validation
body: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit stores OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() directly without checking that it is non-null and exactly two characters long. The default encoder/decoder hard-codes a six-character context prefix composed of three two-character shortcuts. A null shortcut will cause a NullPointerException when inserted into ConcurrentHashMap, and a one- or three-character shortcut will produce token IDs whose prefix cannot be parsed by getTokenContextFromTokenId, which expects length 6. Shortcut format should be validated when factories are registered.

title: New abstract getShortcut method breaks existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
body: Adding String getShortcut() to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory without a default implementation is a source and binary compatibility break for custom grant type factories compiled against earlier Keycloak versions. Existing implementations will fail to compile or can fail at runtime when the token-context encoder invokes the missing method. If this SPI is expected to be implemented by extensions, a default method or explicit migration contract is needed.

title: Copy constructor removed from OAuth2GrantType.Context
body: The change removes the public copy constructor OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context). If custom grant implementations or downstream code used this constructor, they will break at compile time or runtime with NoSuchMethodError. The addition of the grantType field could have preserved the copy constructor, or the removal should be explicitly documented as an incompatible SPI change.

title: Dynamic grant shortcut refresh is non-atomic and does not enforce uniqueness
body: getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut lazily add mappings for newly deployed grant types by writing to two separate ConcurrentHashMap instances without synchronization or duplicate-shortcut validation. If a newly deployed grant uses a shortcut already used by another grant, it can overwrite the existing shortcut-to-grant mapping, causing previously issued token IDs to decode to the wrong grant type. Concurrent updates can also observe partially updated state between the two maps. The maps should be updated atomically and uniqueness should be rechecked before insertion.

title: testIncorrectGrantType succeeds due to NullPointerException from uninitialized sessionFactory
body: The test creates DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory without calling postInit, so sessionFactory is null. When getTokenContextFromTokenId sees the unknown shortcut 'ac', it attempts to refresh grant mappings and throws NullPointerException, which is caught as RuntimeException. The test therefore does not verify the intended invalid-grant-shortcut behavior; it should initialize or mock the factory and assert the specific IllegalArgumentException.

title: setFormParams does not update cached grantType
body: OAuth2GrantType.Context.grantType is derived from formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE) only in the constructor. setFormParams replaces the form parameters but leaves grantType unchanged, so getGrantType() can return a stale value if the form parameters are modified after construction. The setter should update grantType or getGrantType should compute it from the current formParams.

title: Javadoc says 3-letter shortcut but token encoding requires 2 characters
body: The Javadoc for OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut says the shortcut is usually a 3-letter shortcut, but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider requires every grant shortcut to be exactly two characters to build the fixed six-character token ID prefix. Following the documented guidance would produce token IDs that cannot be decoded by the default provider. The documentation should state the required two-character format.

title: Exhausted recovery-code credential from user storage is removed with local-only API
body: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential can return a federated credential, but the cleanup calls removeStoredCredentialById, which only removes locally stored credentials. If an external user storage reports that all recovery codes are used, the federated credential is not disabled or removed. The user can remain configured for recovery codes with an exhausted credential, leading to repeated recovery-code challenges or login failures instead of forcing regeneration.

title: Unsafe Optional.get can throw during login page rendering
body: The constructor calls credentialModelOpt.get() and then getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get() without checking whether the credential or next code exists. If the recovery credential is missing, has been removed, or is returned in an exhausted state, this throws NoSuchElementException while rendering the login page, causing a 500 instead of a recoverable flow transition.

title: Missing null checks before tamper validation can cause NPE
body: generatedAtTimeString and generatedCodesString are read from the form and may be null if the hidden fields are omitted. The tamper check calls equals on these values, so a malformed or tampered required-action submission causes a NullPointerException instead of re-challenging the user.

title: Test storage accepts recovery codes without consuming them
body: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid accepts a recovery code but never marks it used or removes it from the stored list. Consequently the new test can authenticate repeatedly with the same recovery code and does not verify one-time use or the all-codes-used path for user-storage credentials.

title: Exhausted federated recovery credential is deleted with local-only API
body: The lookup was changed to RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(), which can return a federated credential. The subsequent call to authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById() only removes credentials from Keycloak's local credential store. If the found recovery credential came from an external user storage provider, this deletion will not affect that credential (and may target an ID that is not local). As a result, an exhausted federated recovery-code credential can remain present while Keycloak only adds the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action, leaving inconsistent credential state and potentially stale credentials visible.

title: Unchecked Optional.get() can break login page rendering
body: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) returns an Optional, but the bean immediately calls credentialModelOpt.get(). It also calls recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get() on line 21. If the recovery credential is missing (for example, removed concurrently, not returned by external storage, or no remaining codes exist), this throws NoSuchElementException and can surface as a 500 error while rendering the login page instead of failing gracefully or redirecting to the required action.

title: Existing local recovery-code credential is not cleaned up when user storage creation succeeds
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential() treats a true result from user.credentialManager().updateCredential() as success in user storage and does not remove any pre-existing local recovery-authn-code credential. If a user previously had locally stored recovery codes and their user storage later accepts recovery codes, both the old local credential and the new federated credential can coexist. This leaves stale backup codes behind and makes the effective credential set ambiguous; recovery credentials should be replaced or explicitly cleaned up.

title: Plaintext recovery codes are handed to external user storage
body: The helper serializes the generated raw recovery codes and passes them to user storage via UserCredentialModel. Keycloak's local path stores hashed recovery codes, but this code sends the full plaintext list to any external user storage provider. The included test storage also persists these values unhashed. Because recovery codes are bearer secrets, this can lead to plaintext persistence or exposure in external systems. If external storage can operate on hashed values, those should be used; otherwise the security contract should be explicit.

title: Test storage and test do not enforce one-time use of recovery codes
body: The test storage's isValid() for recovery codes only checks whether the submitted code exists in the stored list; it never removes or marks the code as used. The added test logs in once with a recovery code but does not verify that the same code is rejected on a second use. Since recovery codes are one-time credentials, this leaves the new user-storage path untested for replay and the sample storage implementation demonstrates replayable recovery codes.

title: getCredentials() can throw NullPointerException for missing user
body: getCredentials() calls getMyUser(user) and then immediately dereferences myUser.recoveryCodes. getMyUser() can return null if the user is not present in the map, while other methods in this class guard against a missing user. If getCredentials() is invoked for an unknown user, the provider throws NullPointerException instead of returning an empty stream.

title: New recovery codes in user storage do not replace/remove existing local recovery credentials
body: createRecoveryCodesCredential treats a true return from user.credentialManager().updateCredential as success and returns without removing any pre-existing local recovery-authn-code credentials. If a federated user already has a local recovery-code credential, for example created earlier as a fallback, that credential remains in the local store and can still be validated. Newly generated codes therefore do not reliably revoke older codes.

title: Exhausted federated recovery credential is not removed
body: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential can now return a federated/user-storage recovery credential, but when allCodesUsed is true the code only calls removeStoredCredentialById. There is no corresponding disable/remove call for the user-storage credential. If the selected credential is federated, the exhausted credential can remain in the external storage and Keycloak can keep reporting the credential type as configured, leaving inconsistent state.

title: Unsafe Optional.get can cause login page failure when recovery credential is missing or exhausted
body: The bean calls RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user).get() and then getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get() without checking presence. If the credential is absent, removed concurrently, or remains visible after all codes are used, rendering the recovery-code login page throws NoSuchElementException instead of failing gracefully.

title: User-storage test provider does not enforce single-use recovery codes
body: isValid only checks whether the submitted recovery code is present in the stored list; it never marks the code as used or removes it. The added test also uses a code only once and does not attempt reuse or exhaustion. As a result, the new user-storage path is not validated for the required single-use behavior, and a replayable recovery-code storage would pass.

title: Missing null checks on form fields can cause NPE
body: processAction reads generatedAt and generatedRecoveryAuthnCodes from the form and immediately calls equals on generatedAtTimeString. A POST without one of those hidden fields causes a NullPointerException instead of redisplaying the challenge. Null-safe comparison or explicit null checks are needed.

title: Other subgroup methods still dereference a possibly-null model supplier
body: The fix in getSubGroupsCount acknowledges that modelSupplier.get() can return null when a cached group has been deleted concurrently. However, getSubGroupsStream(String, Integer, Integer) at line 256, and the overloads at lines 262 and 268, still call modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) without a null check. If one of these methods is invoked for a cached group whose delegate no longer exists, it will throw a NullPointerException instead of handling the missing group consistently. This leaves the same concurrent-deletion race able to produce 500 errors in other subgroup query paths.

title: getSubGroupsCount can now return null and expose null subGroupCount in responses
body: When the delegate group cannot be loaded, getSubGroupsCount now returns null. Callers such as GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount pass this value directly to GroupRepresentation.setSubGroupCount, so admin API responses can contain a null subgroup count for a cached group that has disappeared. This is a different contract from a numeric count and may confuse clients or cause NullPointerExceptions in consumers that unbox the Long. The code path also does not register cache invalidation, unlike getDelegateForUpdate, so it does not actively clear the stale cached entry.

title: Concurrency test does not wait for the reader thread and can miss failures
body: The test starts a background thread that records exceptions, then deletes groups, sets deletedAll, and immediately asserts that caughtExceptions is empty. There is no join, latch, or timeout, so the assertion can run before the reader thread finishes its current request, and exceptions added after the assertion are missed. The test also does not verify that any read actually overlapped with the deletes. If the delete loop throws, deletedAll may never be set, leaving the reader thread running after the test. Use a join/CountDownLatch, ensure at least one concurrent read occurred, and stop the thread reliably in a finally block.

title: Concurrent-deletion NPE remains in getSubGroupsStream overloads
body: GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount now guards against modelSupplier.get() returning null, but getSubGroupsStream(String, Integer, Integer), getSubGroupsStream(Integer, Integer), and getSubGroupsStream(String, Boolean, Integer, Integer) still call modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...). If the group is deleted concurrently, getGroupModel() can return null for the cached adapter, so these methods will still throw NullPointerException. This leaves the same race unfixed for subgroup pagination/search paths.

title: New concurrency test can pass without detecting failures and may leak thread
body: createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti starts a reader thread but never joins it or otherwise waits for it to complete. The main thread sets deletedAll and immediately asserts caughtExceptions is empty; the reader may not have performed any request yet, may still be in a request, or may add an exception after the assertion. If a delete call throws before deletedAll is set, the reader thread also loops forever. The test is therefore racy, can pass even when the NPE exists, and can leave background admin requests running after the test.

title: Concurrent test does not wait for the reader thread and can pass vacuously or hang
body: The test starts a non-daemon reader thread, deletes the groups, sets deletedAll, and immediately asserts that caughtExceptions is empty. It never joins the thread or waits for at least one read to occur during deletion, so the assertion can run before the reader performs any request or after it has already stopped, missing the race the test is meant to catch. If a delete call throws before deletedAll.set(true), the reader loop may also run indefinitely. Use a latch/join, ensure reads overlap with deletes, and stop the thread in a finally block.

title: Other subgroup methods still dereference modelSupplier without a null check
body: The fix in getSubGroupsCount acknowledges that modelSupplier.get() can return null when the group has been deleted concurrently. However, getSubGroupsStream(String, Integer, Integer) at line 256, getSubGroupsStream(Integer, Integer) at line 262, and getSubGroupsStream(String, Boolean, Integer, Integer) at line 268 still call modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) directly. If the underlying group no longer exists, modelSupplier.get() can be null and these methods will still throw NullPointerException, leaving the same concurrency bug for subgroup search/pagination paths.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator is incompatible with the datetime ordering used here
body: The endpoint passes `paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `order_by=-datetime`, but `OptimizedCursorPaginator` uses numeric key extraction (`math.floor`/`math.ceil`) and does not convert cursor values to datetimes like `DateTimePaginator`. When audit log entries exist, `get_item_key` receives a datetime and raises TypeError; cursor filtering would also use the wrong type. Any privileged request with optimized_pagination=true will fail.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator attempts negative QuerySet slicing
body: When `enable_advanced_features` is true and `cursor.offset` is negative, the paginator slices the Django QuerySet with a negative start (`queryset[start_offset:stop]`). Django QuerySets do not support negative slicing, so this raises instead of returning rows. A crafted or malformed cursor can cause a 500 on the optimized audit-log path.

title: BasePaginator allows negative offsets for previous cursors to reach QuerySet slicing
body: The modified offset logic uses the raw offset for previous-page cursors, so a negative offset parsed from a user-supplied cursor is passed to QuerySet slicing. Django does not support negative offsets; this can crash any endpoint using `BasePaginator` or `DateTimePaginator`. Negative offsets should be rejected with a controlled validation error such as `BadPaginationError`.

title: Cursor accepts negative offsets without validation
body: `Cursor` casts `offset` to int but does not validate that it is non-negative, and `Cursor.from_string` parses user-provided cursor strings with negative offsets. Combined with the paginator changes, invalid negative offsets reach database slicing code. Validation should reject negative offsets instead of allowing them to propagate.

title: Typo prevents reversing ordering for previous-page pagination
body: In `BasePaginator.build_queryset`, when converting an existing descending order to ascending, the code assigns `queryset.query.order_b` instead of `queryset.query.order_by`. The queryset therefore keeps the descending order while the cursor logic uses ascending operators and later reverses results, which can return incorrect pages. This affects paginators inheriting from `BasePaginator`, including the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator`.

title: No tests for the new paginator or the endpoint's optimized path
body: The PR adds a new paginator class, changes core offset handling in `BasePaginator`, and conditionally switches the audit-log endpoint to the new paginator, but includes no tests. Important cases are untested: datetime ordering with `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, negative or malformed cursor offsets, permission gating of optimized pagination, and backward compatibility with existing cursors. These omissions are risky because pagination bugs can cause incorrect pages or 500 errors.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator is incompatible with datetime ordering
body: The endpoint selects OptimizedCursorPaginator while ordering AuditLogEntry by '-datetime'. OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does int(math.floor/ceil(getattr(item, self.key))) and value_from_cursor returns a raw integer. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime, so math.floor/ceil raises TypeError on the first non-empty result page, and an integer cursor value would also be compared to a timestamp column. The result is that any privileged request with optimized_pagination=true that returns audit logs fails with a 500 error.

title: Negative offset slicing is not supported by Django querysets
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator's advanced path sets start_offset to cursor.offset when cursor.offset is negative and then executes queryset[start_offset:stop]. Cursor offsets come from client-supplied cursor strings and can be negative. Django QuerySet slicing explicitly rejects negative indexes with AssertionError, so a cursor such as 0:-1:1 can cause an unhandled 500. The inline comment claiming the ORM handles negative slicing is incorrect.

title: BasePaginator also passes negative prev offsets to queryset slicing
body: BasePaginator.get_result was changed to clamp negative offsets only when cursor.is_prev is false. When is_prev is true, a negative offset is passed directly to queryset[start_offset:stop]. Because Cursor.from_string parses negative integers, any BasePaginator-based endpoint, including the default DateTimePaginator path for audit logs, can be made to crash by a client-supplied previous cursor with a negative offset.

title: Typo assigns to query_b instead of order_by
body: In BasePaginator.build_queryset, the branch that flips an existing '-key' ordering to ascending assigns tuple(new_order_by) to queryset.query_b instead of queryset.query.order_by. The queryset ordering is therefore left unchanged, so backward pagination over a queryset already ordered descending can use the wrong sort direction and return incorrect pages or cursors.

title: No tests for the new pagination toggle or OptimizedCursorPaginator
body: The PR adds a query-parameter-gated paginator, an admin-only advanced feature, and negative-offset handling, but includes no tests for the new endpoint behavior, cursor parsing, forward/backward pagination, or invalid/negative cursors. Given the runtime crashes with datetime fields and negative offsets, this is a high-risk untested change.

title: Optimized pagination branch uses a paginator that cannot handle datetime sort keys
body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint.get passes order_by='-datetime' with OptimizedCursorPaginator. OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil on the raw model field and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor value, unlike DateTimePaginator which converts to/from timestamps. When any audit-log rows are returned, the key function receives a datetime and raises TypeError, and any non-empty cursor value would be compared as an integer to a datetime column. The optimized path is therefore broken and can return 500 or generate invalid queries.

title: Negative offsets are passed to Django QuerySet slicing, which is unsupported
body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset < 0, start_offset is set to the negative offset and queryset[start_offset:stop] is evaluated. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative start/stop values and raises AssertionError. Because cursor offsets are parsed from client-supplied strings, this allows a request to trigger a 500 instead of paginating.

title: BasePaginator can pass negative previous-page offsets to QuerySet slicing
body: The modified BasePaginator.get_result sets start_offset to cursor.offset whenever cursor.is_prev is true. Cursor.from_string accepts negative offsets, so a previous-page cursor such as 0:-1:1 causes queryset[-1:...] to be evaluated. Django does not support negative QuerySet indexing, so existing BasePaginator/DateTimePaginator endpoints can return 500 on malformed cursors.

title: No tests cover the new optimized pagination mode
body: The PR adds a query-parameter-controlled paginator switch, privileged access logic, negative-offset handling, and a new paginator, but no tests are included. Without tests for optimized_pagination=true, non-admin fallback, datetime cursor generation, and negative cursor offsets, these regressions are easy to miss.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate datetime fields but is used for audit logs
body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint uses OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by='-datetime'. OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil on getattr(item, self.key), but AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime object. Any non-empty optimized page will raise TypeError. This paginator needs DateTimePaginator-style key/value handling or must not be used for datetime columns.

title: Negative offsets are now passed to Django QuerySet slicing
body: BasePaginator now uses cursor.offset unchanged for previous-page cursors, and OptimizedCursorPaginator explicitly allows negative offsets when advanced features are enabled. Django QuerySets do not support negative slice indices, so a crafted cursor with a negative offset can raise an exception instead of returning a page. Negative offsets should be rejected or normalized before slicing.

title: Span buffer switches from Redis sets to sorted sets without migration or key namespacing
body: Existing span-buf:s:* keys created by the previous code are Redis sets. The new code calls ZADD on those keys and the Lua script uses ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE. If any in-flight segment from the old version exists during deployment, Redis will return WRONGTYPE and processing will fail, causing stuck or dropped spans. A new key prefix, migration, or drain procedure is needed.

title: ZPOPMIN eviction can remove root spans or other semantically important spans
body: The script caps each segment at 1000 members by removing the lowest-scored members, where score is end_timestamp_precise. It has no special protection for the segment/root span. If the root span has one of the lowest end timestamps, or a missing/zero timestamp, it can be evicted. The segment may then be marked as having a root span while the root payload is missing, breaking downstream segment semantics.

title: Redirect resolution depth was reduced to 1000 and can fragment deep traces
body: The loop follows at most 1000 redirects in the span redirect map. If a redirect chain is longer, the script stops at an intermediate set and stores the span there, which can prevent related spans from being joined into one segment. The previous limit was 10000 and the correctness tradeoff was at least documented; the new lower limit changes behavior for deep traces without tests or migration notes.

title: SpansBuffer.__reduce__ reconstructs the object with the wrong positional arguments
body: __reduce__ returns SpansBuffer with (assigned_shards, span_buffer_timeout_secs, span_buffer_root_timeout_secs, redis_ttl). The fourth positional argument of SpansBuffer.__init__ is segment_page_size, not redis_ttl, and max_segment_bytes/max_segment_spans/redis_ttl are not preserved. When SpansBuffer is pickled for multiprocessing, the unpickled buffer will have incorrect configuration.

title: Flush path no longer enforces a span-count limit
body: _load_segment_data removed the check that skipped segments larger than max_segment_spans. The Lua script only evicts when new inserts push a set above 1000 members, so pre-existing or otherwise unevicted segments can contain many small spans under max_segment_bytes and be loaded, serialized, and produced in one flush, causing memory/CPU spikes or oversized downstream messages.

title: Typo assigning queryset.query.order_b leaves ordering unchanged
body: In build_queryset, when converting an existing descending order to ascending, the code assigns to queryset.query.order_b instead of queryset.query.order_by. The intended ordering change is silently dropped, which can produce incorrect previous-page results for paginators relying on this branch.

title: No tests cover the new eviction cap or set-to-zset migration behavior
body: The test changes only add end_timestamp_precise to existing fixtures. There are no tests that insert more than 1000 spans to verify ZPOPMIN eviction, verify that root spans are preserved, or verify behavior when old Redis set keys exist. Given the data-loss and compatibility risks introduced by this PR, these cases need coverage.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate datetime fields
body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint uses OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by='-datetime', but OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor()/math.ceil() on the field value. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime, so this raises TypeError on the first page with results. value_from_cursor also returns a numeric value instead of a datetime, making this paginator incompatible with the endpoint.

title: Negative offsets are passed to Django QuerySet slicing
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result allows start_offset to be negative and then executes queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django QuerySets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError. The comment that the ORM handles boundary conditions is incorrect; a crafted or stale cursor can cause unhandled 500 errors.

title: BasePaginator permits negative offsets for previous-page cursors
body: The modified BasePaginator.get_result uses cursor.offset directly when cursor.is_prev is true, so a negative offset parsed from a cursor string can reach queryset slicing. Cursor.from_string accepts negative offsets, and BasePaginator-derived paginators do not validate or reject them, creating a path to invalid slicing or incorrect pagination.

title: Typo prevents reversing queryset ordering for previous pages
body: In BasePaginator.build_queryset, when converting an existing descending order_by such as '-datetime' to ascending for a previous-page cursor, the modified ordering tuple is assigned to queryset.query.order_b instead of queryset.query.order_by. The queryset therefore keeps the old ordering while the WHERE clause uses ascending comparison, which can return incorrect pages.

title: Possible AttributeError when organization_context.member is None
body: The endpoint evaluates organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking whether member is None. RpcUserOrganizationContext.member can be absent for some user/organization contexts. If request.user.is_superuser is false and member is None, this will raise AttributeError instead of failing permission checks cleanly.

title: Switch from Redis sets to sorted sets is not migration-safe
body: process_spans now uses ZADD on span-buf:s:* keys, and the Lua script uses ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZPOPMIN/ZSCAN on those keys. Existing in-flight segments created by the previous code are plain Redis sets. During deployment, any existing set-typed key will cause WRONGTYPE errors, breaking ingestion and flushing for those traces because there is no type check, migration, or drain path.

title: ZUNIONSTORE default aggregation can corrupt scores
body: The merge uses ZUNIONSTORE without specifying AGGREGATE, so members present in multiple source sorted sets have their scores summed. Since scores are end_timestamp_precise values, duplicate spans or a self-merge where span_key equals set_key can produce doubled or otherwise incorrect timestamps. This breaks timestamp-based eviction and can delete the wrong spans. AGGREGATE MIN/MAX and a guard against self-merges are needed.

title: Insert-time eviction can silently drop spans and leave stale redirects
body: When span_count exceeds 1000, the script removes the lowest-scored members with ZPOPMIN. This may remove root spans or other important spans, producing incomplete segments without any metric or log. Evicted span IDs also remain in the redirect hash because done_flush_segments only deletes redirects for spans that are actually flushed, so stale redirects can later route spans to deleted or incorrect segment keys.

title: ZPOPMIN returns all evicted members unnecessarily
body: The eviction uses ZPOPMIN with a count, which returns every popped member to the Lua script even though the result is discarded. If a large number of spans must be evicted, this creates unnecessary Redis reply construction and Lua memory pressure. ZREMRANGEBYRANK would remove the same range without returning all members.

title: Redirect resolution depth was lowered without handling truncation
body: The redirect-following loop was reduced from 10000 to 1000 iterations. If a redirect chain is longer than the new limit, the script stores a redirect to an intermediate set rather than the final segment key. This can leave traces fragmented across multiple span buffers instead of being joined correctly.

title: __reduce__ passes redis_ttl as segment_page_size
body: SpansBuffer.__reduce__ reconstructs the object with (assigned_shards, span_buffer_timeout_secs, span_buffer_root_timeout_secs, self.redis_ttl), but the fourth constructor argument is segment_page_size; redis_ttl is the seventh argument. When the buffer is pickled, for example for multiprocessing, segment_page_size becomes the TTL value and redis_ttl falls back to its default.

title: max_segment_spans is no longer enforced
body: SpansBuffer still accepts and stores max_segment_spans, but the flush-time span-count check was removed and the Lua script hardcodes a 1000-span eviction limit. The parameter is now misleading and has no effect on runtime behavior.

title: No tests cover eviction or sorted-set merge semantics
body: The tests only exercise small segments. They do not verify behavior when a segment exceeds 1000 spans, whether ZUNIONSTORE preserves or corrupts scores, whether existing set-typed keys are handled during deployment, or whether redirects for evicted spans are cleaned up. These are high-risk areas of the change and need explicit tests.

title: Negative cursor offsets are now passed to Django QuerySets
body: BasePaginator.get_result now uses cursor.offset directly when cursor.is_prev is true. Cursor.from_string accepts negative offsets, but Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indices. A crafted cursor such as 0:-10:1 can cause an AssertionError or database error and result in a 500 response on any endpoint using BasePaginator or DateTimePaginator.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator explicitly allows invalid negative QuerySet offsets
body: When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset is negative, OptimizedCursorPaginator slices the queryset with a negative start offset. Django ORM querysets do not support negative slicing, and the computed stop offset may also be negative or nonsensical. The comment stating that the ORM handles boundary conditions is incorrect; this will cause exceptions or undefined pagination behavior.

title: OptimizedCursorPaginator is incompatible with datetime ordering
body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil directly on the ordered field value, and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor value. In organization_auditlogs.py it is used with order_by='-datetime'. For any non-empty result page, math.ceil(datetime) raises TypeError, and for non-zero cursors the WHERE clause would compare a datetime column to a numeric value. The optimized audit-log pagination path is therefore broken.

title: Unguarded access to organization_context.member may raise AttributeError
body: The code accesses organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking whether organization_context.member is None. If a request has an organization context without a member, this will raise AttributeError and return a 500 instead of denying access or falling back safely.

title: New optimized pagination path is untested
body: The PR adds a new optimized_pagination query-parameter branch and uses OptimizedCursorPaginator, but no tests cover this endpoint behavior or the new paginator. Given the datetime incompatibility and negative-offset handling, this is a high-risk untested code path.

title: Switch from Redis sets to sorted sets is not backward compatible with in-flight data
body: Existing span-buf:s:* keys created by the previous code are Redis sets. The new code uses ZADD here, and the Lua script uses ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE, while flushing uses ZSCAN. During a rollout, pre-existing set-typed keys will cause WRONGTYPE errors, causing span buffering or flushing to fail until those keys expire. This needs a migration strategy, dual-type handling, or a new key namespace.

title: ZUNIONSTORE default SUM aggregation can corrupt span scores
body: ZUNIONSTORE defaults to AGGREGATE SUM. If the same span payload exists in both the destination and source sorted sets, for example due to duplicate delivery, retries, or overlapping buffer keys, its score becomes the sum of end_timestamp_precise values rather than the original timestamp. This corrupts eviction ordering. The union should use an explicit aggregation such as MAX or MIN.

title: Eviction can silently drop spans, including root spans, while preserving has-root state
body: The script evicts the lowest-scored members with ZPOPMIN when a segment exceeds 1000 spans. There is no metric or explicit signal that data was dropped. If the evicted member is the root span, the has_root_span key may still be set because is_root_span was observed, causing the segment to be flushed with root-based timing while missing its root span. This can produce incomplete or inconsistent trace segments.

title: Reduced redirect-following limit may fragment deep traces
body: The redirect traversal loop was reduced from 10000 to 1000. If a trace has a redirect chain longer than 1000, new spans will stop at an intermediate redirect target and be stored under the wrong set key, fragmenting the segment. The PR provides no migration or test coverage for this behavioral change.

title: Consumer hard-fails if end_timestamp_precise is missing
body: The consumer now reads val['end_timestamp_precise'] directly. If an incoming span message omits this field or provides null due to schema drift, older producers, or malformed data, the consumer will raise KeyError or later fail when using the value as a Redis score. This makes the consumer fragile to upstream variations.

title: No tests cover the new eviction behavior or sorted-set migration
body: The core behavioral changes in this PR are the switch from sets to sorted sets and eviction of segments above 1000 spans, but the tests only add end_timestamp_precise values. There is no coverage for segments exceeding the span cap, eviction order, root-span eviction, stale queue entries, or compatibility with old set-typed Redis keys.

title: Accidental submodule committed
body: This PR adds a git submodule named 'sentry-repo' pointing at a commit. That appears unintentional and can break clones, CI, or repository layout. Remove the submodule/gitlink before merging.

title: Upsampling eligibility uses outer dataset instead of the dataset actually queried
body: _get_event_stats receives scoped_dataset, but eligibility is computed with the outer 'dataset' variable. In dashboard-split/fallback paths _get_event_stats can be called with a different dataset (e.g. discover), so the decision to transform count() can be based on the wrong dataset. This can skip upsampling or apply it inconsistently.

title: Error-focused query detection is a naive substring check
body: _is_error_focused_query returns true whenever 'event.type:error' appears in the raw request query. This matches negated clauses such as '!event.type:error', mixed queries like 'event.type:error OR event.type:transaction', and text inside quoted values. It also fails to treat '!event.type:transaction' as error-focused. Since this controls whether count() is replaced by sum(sample_weight), it can apply weights to non-error events or miss error-only queries, producing incorrect counts. Parse the search syntax or use the final query string instead.

title: Eligibility cache can serve stale allowlist decisions and has no wired invalidation
body: Allowlist eligibility is cached for 60 seconds, but invalidate_upsampling_cache is never called when the 'issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist' option changes. If the allowlist is updated, queries can continue using the old upsampling decision for up to a minute, returning incorrect counts. Include a config version in the cache key or invoke invalidation on option changes.

title: Cache key uses Python hash() of project IDs
body: The cache key embeds hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))). Tuple hashes can collide and are not a stable, collision-safe identifier for cached correctness. A collision between different project sets could reuse an eligibility decision for the wrong projects. Use a deterministic unique key such as joined sorted project IDs or a stable hash.

title: Only literal count() is transformed and aliasing is forced
body: The transform only rewrites columns that exactly match 'count()' after lower/strip and rewrites them to 'upsampled_count() as count'. It does not handle aliased forms like 'count() as total', other count variants, or equations. This can leave some count aggregations unupsampled while changing the output alias for others, causing inconsistent API responses for clients expecting the original field name.

title: Allowlist membership check uses list lookups
body: _are_all_projects_error_upsampled checks 'project_id in allowlist' where allowlist is a list. On a cache miss this is O(number of queried projects * allowlist size). Convert the allowlist to a set before checking membership.

title: upsampled_count is exposed as a public query function
body: The new upsampled_count SnQL function is added without private=True, unlike neighboring internal functions. This may allow API callers to invoke it directly in queries, bypassing the allowlist/error-upsampling checks and potentially exposing sample-weight-derived counts. Mark the function private or gate it appropriately.

title: upsampled_count does not handle missing/null sample weights
body: The aggregate is toInt64(sum(sample_weight)). If any event in an allowlisted project has a NULL or unpopulated sample_weight (for example historical events before upsampling metadata existed), those events can contribute zero or nothing to the sum, causing severe undercounting. Use coalesce(sample_weight, 1) or another explicit default unless the schema guarantees a non-NULL weight of 1 for every row.

title: toInt64 truncates fractional upsampled sums
body: sample_weight values can be fractional, and sum(sample_weight) may therefore be fractional. Wrapping it in toInt64 truncates rather than rounding, biasing the estimated error count downward. Consider rounding or returning a numeric/float result.

title: Endpoint tests do not clear or test the upsampling eligibility cache
body: The tests patch the allowlist option but do not clear the 'error_upsampling_eligible:*' cache entries. Since the eligibility cache lives for 60 seconds, a value cached by one test can affect later tests with the same organization/project IDs, making the suite order-dependent and preventing validation of stale-cache behavior. Clear the cache in setUp or add explicit cache invalidation/staleness tests.

title: Missing coverage for key upsampling paths
body: The new tests only cover simple stats requests with 'event.type:error'. They do not cover the errors dataset, top-events paths, RPC paths, aliased/equation count columns, dashboard split queries, or mixed/negated event.type queries. These are the paths where the transform is applied and are likely to regress.

title: Accidental gitlink/submodule added
body: The PR adds a `sentry-repo` gitlink (subproject commit) at the repository root. There is no `.gitmodules` entry or apparent use for it, so it looks like an accidental nested repository/submodule. This can break checkouts or tooling and should be removed before merge.

title: Substring query check can misclassify mixed or negated queries as error-only
body: `_is_error_focused_query` returns true whenever the raw query contains the substring `event.type:error`. This matches negated filters like `!event.type:error`, mixed queries like `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`, and even tag/message text containing that substring. In those cases the endpoint rewrites `count()` to `upsampled_count()`, which can undercount or zero out non-error rows that do not have a meaningful `sample_weight`.

title: Upsampling decision ignores the actual executed query string
body: `_is_error_focused_query` inspects `request.GET['query']`, but `_get_event_stats` can execute a different `query` argument, for example dashboard-split queries that append conditions such as `AND !event.type:transaction`. The upsampling decision should be based on the query actually being executed; otherwise transformed columns may be applied to a non-error query or omitted for an error-only split query.

title: Upsampling eligibility uses the outer dataset instead of the dataset being queried
body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset` because callers can execute the query with a different dataset, but the eligibility check passes the outer `dataset` variable. When the executed dataset differs, the decision may enable upsampling for the wrong dataset or fail to enable it for an error dataset. The check should use the dataset that will actually execute the query.

title: Upsampling is enabled for the errors dataset without corresponding tested aggregate registration
body: The helper returns true for `dataset == errors`, but the new `upsampled_count` aggregate is only added in `src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py`. If the errors resolver does not inherit this function converter, allowlisted errors-dataset requests using `count()` will be rewritten to an unknown function and fail. This path is not covered by the tests.

title: upsampled_count drops events with missing or null sample_weight
body: The aggregate is implemented as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`. If any event in an allowlisted project has a missing/null `sample_weight` (old events, events without error-sampling context, malformed sample rates, etc.), that event contributes zero rather than one, silently undercounting errors. A default such as coalescing missing weights to 1, or an explicit guarantee that every row has a valid weight, is needed.

title: toInt64 truncates fractional upsampled counts
body: `upsampled_count` casts `sum(sample_weight)` to Int64. If `sample_weight` can be fractional, which is likely for inverse sample rates, the result is truncated rather than rounded. This systematically biases estimated error counts downward. Return a numeric result or explicitly round if integer output is required.

title: upsampled_count is exposed as a public query function
body: The new SnQLFunction does not set `private=True`, unlike neighboring internal functions. API callers can request `upsampled_count()` directly, bypassing the allowlist/error-focused checks and potentially producing misleading weighted counts on data where upsampling should not apply. Mark the function private if it is only intended for internal column transformation.

title: Eligibility cache key uses a lossy Python hash and lacks effective invalidation
body: The cache key uses `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`. This is not a collision-resistant identifier, and different project sets could theoretically share a key. In addition, `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is not wired to allowlist changes and only deletes one exact project-set key, so allowlist updates can leave stale eligibility entries for up to 60 seconds. Use a deterministic digest or explicit key contents and provide real invalidation if needed.

title: Tests miss unsafe upsampling paths
body: The new endpoint tests only cover simple `event.type:error` and `event.type:transaction` queries on discover. They do not cover negated or mixed queries, dataset=errors, topEvents, RPC paths, events missing `sample_weight`, or cache staleness. These are the paths most likely to expose wrong counts or query failures.

title: Accidental submodule/gitlink added
body: The PR adds a gitlink/submodule (`Subproject commit ...`) at repository root. This is unrelated to the feature and can break checkouts/builds or accidentally vendor another repository. It should be removed.

title: Eligibility cache has no effective invalidation
body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` caches allowlist eligibility for 60 seconds, but nothing invalidates these keys when `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` changes. The unused `invalidate_upsampling_cache` helper also only deletes one exact project-set key. If the allowlist changes, API responses can return upsampled or non-upsampled counts incorrectly for up to a minute.

title: Cache key uses Python hash() of project IDs
body: The cache key embeds `hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))`. Python hash values are not a stable, collision-resistant way to build cache keys across processes/versions, and different project sets could collide. Use a deterministic key such as sorted project IDs joined together.

title: Error-only detection is a naive substring match
body: `_is_error_focused_query` treats any occurrence of `event.type:error` in the raw query as an error-only query. This matches negated filters like `!event.type:error`, OR clauses that also include transactions, and text/tag values. For discover queries this can replace `count()` with `upsampled_count()` when non-error events are included, producing wrong counts.

title: upsampled_count is exposed as a public aggregate
body: The new `upsampled_count` SnQL function is not marked `private=True`, unlike neighboring internal functions. API callers may be able to request it directly, bypassing the allowlist/eligibility logic that only rewrites `count()`, and get incorrect results on projects or datasets where sample weights should not be used.

title: upsampled_count does not handle missing sample_weight
body: `upsampled_count` is implemented as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`. If any queried event has NULL/missing `sample_weight` (for example historical events before upsampling was enabled, malformed events, or non-error rows accidentally included in discover), the aggregation can ignore those rows or return NULL/zero, silently changing counts. A fallback or explicit row filtering is needed.

title: Upsampling can be enabled for errors dataset without function registration
body: `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns true for the errors dataset, but the PR only registers `upsampled_count` in the discover dataset converter. If the errors dataset does not inherit that converter, allowlisted requests using `dataset=errors` will generate queries referencing an unknown function and fail.

title: Upsampling decision uses request dataset instead of executed dataset
body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset` but determines upsampling using the outer `dataset` captured from the request. When the factory substitutes a split dataset (for example dashboard widget split queries), the eligibility check can be based on the wrong dataset, causing the transform to be applied or skipped incorrectly.

title: Top-events path only transforms timeseries columns
body: For `topEvents > 0`, the PR transforms `timeseries_columns`/`y_axes` but leaves `selected_columns`, `equations`, and `orderby` untransformed. If those fields contain or depend on `count()`, top-event selection/ordering may use raw counts while returned timeseries use upsampled counts, making rankings and values inconsistent.

title: Tests miss high-risk upsampling paths
body: The endpoint tests cover only simple discover queries with explicit `event.type:error`. They do not cover `dataset=errors`, top events, dashboard split queries, negated/ambiguous event.type conditions, direct use of `upsampled_count()`, or cache expiry/invalidation. These are the paths most likely to expose incorrect counts or query failures.

title: NameError: PRCommentWorkflow is not defined in CommitContextIntegration scope
body: In `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template`, the code calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title)`, but `PRCommentWorkflow` is not imported or defined in this file. The `_truncate_title` static method is defined on `CommitContextIntegration` itself. This will raise a `NameError` at runtime whenever a merged PR comment is generated (called from both GitHub and GitLab integration `get_comment_body`). The fix is to use `CommitContextIntegration._truncate_title(title)` or simply `_truncate_title(title)` since it's a static method on the same class.

title: zip(error_ids, events.values()) may pair wrong event IDs with wrong data
body: `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a dict that may omit missing keys and does not guarantee ordering matches the input list. Using `zip(error_ids, events.values())` will silently pair the wrong event_id with the wrong event data when any node is missing from the result. For example, if error_ids=['a','b','c'] but only nodes for 'a' and 'c' are found, 'a' gets paired with 'a's data correctly only by coincidence; 'b' would be paired with 'c's data. The correct approach is to iterate over `error_ids` and look up each corresponding node_id in the returned dict.

title: TableWidgetVisualization rendered with hardcoded empty data when feature flag is enabled
body: When `organization.features.includes('use-table-widget-visualization')` is true, the component renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />` with completely empty columns and data. The actual table results available in `result.data`, `result.meta`, `fields`, etc. from the surrounding `tableResults.map` iteration are never passed. Users with this feature flag enabled will see an empty table instead of their dashboard widget data.

title: Mutual exclusion validation uses truthiness check, allowing age=0 with timestamp present
body: `validate_timestamp` checks `self.initial_data.get('age')` which is a truthiness test. If a report contains both `timestamp` and `age=0`, the check evaluates to falsy and no validation error is raised, violating the spec constraint that these fields are mutually exclusive. The same issue exists in `validate_age` with `self.initial_data.get('timestamp')` if timestamp were 0 (though min_value=0 makes 0 valid). Use `'age' in self.initial_data` instead of truthiness to correctly detect field presence.

title: Migration test removed without replacement for the corrected migration
body: The test for migration 0917 is deleted, and migrations 0917 and 0920 are gutted to no-ops referencing `0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py` as the correct migration. However, migration 0921 and its test are not included in this PR. If the replacement migration is landed separately, there's a window where the data conversion has no test coverage, and if it's not landed, the conversion silently never happens for environments that haven't yet applied 0917/0920.

title: get_request_data mutates the input error_events list via in-place sort
body: `error_events.sort(key=lambda x: x['timestamp'])` sorts the list in place. The `error_events` list is constructed in the endpoint's `get` method and passed via `functools.partial` to `analyze_recording_segments`. While currently safe because the list is only used once, in-place mutation of a caller-owned list is fragile and can cause subtle bugs if the list is reused or if the function is called multiple times with the same list.

title: zip(error_ids, events.values()) misaligns error IDs with event data when nodestore returns partial results
body: In fetch_error_details, nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids) returns a dict that may omit missing node_ids. The subsequent zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes a 1:1 positional correspondence between the error_ids list and the dict values. If any event is missing from nodestore, the dict will have fewer entries than error_ids, causing all subsequent error_ids to be paired with the wrong event data. This produces ErrorEvent objects with mismatched id/title/message, corrupting the AI summary input. The fix is to iterate over zip(node_ids, error_ids) and look up each node_id in the events dict individually.

title: Static method references PRCommentWorkflow which may not be in scope in commit_context.py
body: get_merged_pr_single_issue_template is a @staticmethod on CommitContextIntegration and calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title). However, _truncate_title is defined as a @staticmethod on CommitContextIntegration itself in this same class. If PRCommentWorkflow is not defined or imported in this module (it appears to be defined in or imported by the GitHub/GitLab integration modules), this will raise a NameError at runtime when any PR comment is generated. The call should be CommitContextIntegration._truncate_title(title) to reference the method on the class where it is actually defined.

title: Mutual exclusion validation between age and timestamp uses truthiness, missing zero-valued fields
body: validate_timestamp checks 'if self.initial_data.get("age")' and validate_age checks 'if self.initial_data.get("timestamp")'. These are truthiness checks, so if a browser sends age=0 alongside timestamp (or timestamp=0 alongside age), the validation will not detect the conflict and will accept the report as valid. The spec requires these fields to be mutually exclusive. The check should use 'is not None' or '"age" in self.initial_data' to correctly detect presence regardless of value.

title: get_request_data mutates its input list via in-place sort
body: get_request_data calls error_events.sort(key=lambda x: x["timestamp"]) which sorts the list in place. The caller (analyze_recording_segments) passes the error_events list received from the endpoint. While the list is not reused after this call in the current code path, mutating a function argument is a hidden side effect that can cause subtle bugs if the caller's expectations change. Using sorted(error_events, key=...) would avoid the mutation.

title: Timestamp unit mismatch between error events and replay segment events may cause incorrect interleaving
body: gen_request_data compares error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"] with event.get("timestamp", 0) to interleave errors chronologically. Error event timestamps from nodestore are Unix epoch seconds (float). Replay segment event timestamps may be in seconds or milliseconds depending on the SDK version and platform. If the units differ, all errors will be sorted before or after all breadcrumb events, producing a nonsensical timeline for the AI summary. The code should normalize both timestamp sources to the same unit before comparison.

title: analytics.record accesses request.user.id unconditionally which may fail for non-user auth
body: The analytics.record call passes user_id=request.user.id. While the endpoint requires ProjectReleasePermission, if the request is authenticated via an org auth token (as suggested by the is_org_auth_token_auth check later in the method), request.user may not be a standard User object with an id attribute. The analytics event defines user_id as required=False, so passing None or omitting it would be safer than assuming request.user.id always exists.

title: zip(error_ids, events.values()) misaligns when nodestore returns fewer results
body: In fetch_error_details, `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a dict that may omit keys for missing events. The code then does `zip(error_ids, events.values())`, which pairs error_ids positionally with whatever values the dict contains. If any event_id is not found in nodestore, the dict will have fewer entries than error_ids, causing subsequent event_ids to be paired with the wrong event data. For example, with error_ids=[a,b,c] and only a,c found, the zip produces (a,data_a) and (b,data_c), attributing c's data to b. The fix is to iterate over node_ids and look up each in the returned dict, e.g. `for node_id, event_id in zip(node_ids, error_ids): data = events.get(node_id)`.

title: Falsy check on age/timestamp allows both fields when age=0
body: validate_timestamp uses `if self.initial_data.get("age")` and validate_age uses `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp")`. Since `age` is an IntegerField with no min_value, a value of 0 is valid but falsy. If a report contains both `"age": 0` and `"timestamp": 123`, the `self.initial_data.get("age")` check returns 0 (falsy), so the mutual-exclusion validation is silently skipped and both fields are accepted. The check should use `"age" in self.initial_data` or `self.initial_data.get("age") is not None` instead.

title: update() reads 'detector_type' key but serializer field is named 'type', so type can never be updated
body: In BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update(), the code does `validated_data.get("detector_type", instance.group_type)`. However, the serializer field is declared as `type = serializers.CharField()` and `validate_type` returns a GroupType, so the validated_data dict will contain the key `"type"`, not `"detector_type"`. This means the `.get("detector_type", ...)` always falls back to `instance.group_type`, making it impossible to update the detector type via PUT. The key should be `"type"` to match the serializer field name.

title: TableWidgetVisualization rendered with hardcoded empty data instead of actual query results
body: When the `use-table-widget-visualization` feature flag is enabled, the code renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />`, completely ignoring the actual `result.data`, `result.meta`, `fields`, and other props that are available in scope. This means enabling the feature flag will show empty tables in all dashboard widget cards instead of real data. The actual data from `result` should be passed to the component.

title: get_recommended_event() called per issue in PR comment generation may be expensive
body: get_environment_info calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` for each issue (up to 5) when generating a merged PR comment. get_recommended_event typically involves a nodestore fetch or event lookup. This happens synchronously during comment body construction, adding latency to the PR comment workflow. Consider caching or batching these lookups, or making environment info best-effort with a timeout.

title: Typo 'segements' in comment
body: The comment on line 88 reads 'If no segments were ingested then we can skip deleting the segements.' — 'segements' should be 'segments'.

title: Analytics event recorded before feature flag check, may record events for disabled orgs
body: analytics.record('preprod_artifact.api.assemble', ...) is called unconditionally before the `features.has('organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble', ...)` check. This means every request to this endpoint generates an analytics event even when the feature is disabled and the request will return 404. If this is not intentional, the analytics call should be moved after the feature flag check.

title: Data migrations gutted to no-ops with reference to migration 0921 not present in this PR
body: Both migrations 0917 and 0920 are changed to no-ops with a comment referencing '0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py', but that migration is not included in this PR. The test for migration 0917 is also removed. If migration 0921 does not already exist in the codebase, the saved-search-to-views data conversion is effectively lost. Ensure 0921 exists and has its own test coverage before merging.

title: Integration.DoesNotExist path skips the new installer identity check
body: GitHubInstallation.dispatch returns pipeline.next_step() when no Integration row exists for the supplied installation_id. The github_authenticated_user comparison is only performed later for an existing active Integration. If the webhook has not yet created the Integration, failed, or the row was deleted, the pipeline completes and build_integration will create/link the installation using only the user-supplied installation_id. That bypasses the PR's stated validation that the OAuth-authenticated GitHub user matches the installer, potentially allowing a user to bind a GitHub installation they did not install if they know or guess its installation_id. The flow should fail closed, or wait until sender metadata is available, when the installer cannot be verified.

title: Unsafe access to metadata['sender']['login'] can 500
body: The mismatch check assumes integration.metadata contains a 'sender' dict with a 'login' key. Integrations created before this change, created through the Integration.DoesNotExist path, or created from webhook payloads lacking sender will not have this key. In those cases the request raises KeyError and returns a 500 instead of the controlled installation-failed page, and users may be unable to install or reinstall. Use a safe lookup and reject the installation when sender/login is absent.

title: Integration lookups do not filter by provider
body: Both Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id) at line 478 and the later get at line 494 omit provider='github'. If another integration provider has the same external_id, the code can fetch the wrong Integration, produce incorrect 'installed on another organization' errors, apply the sender check to the wrong record, or raise MultipleObjectsReturned. Filter these queries by GitHubIntegrationProvider.key.

title: installation_id is bound before OAuth state is validated
body: OAuthLoginView.dispatch binds installation_id into pipeline state before checking request.GET['state'] against pipeline.signature. A request with an invalid state value can therefore still mutate pipeline state. Since this is a GET pipeline endpoint and installation_id later controls which GitHub installation is linked, validating state before binding, or not binding installation_id when state is present, would avoid unnecessary state tampering.

title: OAuth token exchange omits redirect_uri
body: The authorize redirect includes redirect_uri, but the access-token exchange created at lines 416-420 does not send it. OAuth servers use redirect_uri at the token endpoint to enforce that the code was issued for the expected callback URL. If the GitHub OAuth app ever has multiple callback URLs, omitting it weakens protection against authorization-code injection. Include the same redirect_uri in the token request.

title: Network/API failures in OAuth exchange are unhandled
body: safe_urlopen and get_user_info can raise exceptions for network failures or GitHub API errors, but only the response body parsing is wrapped in try/except. A transient failure during installation will produce a 500 instead of the intended installation-failed error page. Catch the expected HTTP/API exceptions and return error().

title: Empty installation_id is treated as present
body: installation_id = request.GET.get('installation_id', pipeline.fetch_state(...)) followed by 'if installation_id is None' accepts an empty string from ?installation_id=. The code then binds '' and queries or requests GitHub with an empty installation id, causing avoidable errors. Treat empty or whitespace-only values as missing and redirect to the app URL.

title: No tests for missing sender metadata or missing Integration path
body: The added tests cover the happy path and a mismatch when metadata.sender exists, but not the cases where Integration exists without metadata.sender/login or where Integration.DoesNotExist causes the pipeline to continue. Those paths can raise KeyError or bypass the new security check, so they need regression tests.

title: test_installation_not_found does not exercise installation lookup
body: The test sends a state value that does not match the pipeline signature, so OAuthLoginView returns the generic invalid-request error before reaching the mocked 404 for /app/installations/{installation_id}. The assertion therefore does not verify the intended installation-not-found behavior. Use a valid pipeline state and complete the OAuth step to test the 404 path.

title: User validation is skipped when the Integration row does not exist
body: GitHubInstallation.dispatch returns pipeline.next_step() when Integration.DoesNotExist, before any installer validation. The new OAuth-user check only runs when an active Integration row already exists. If the webhook that creates the Integration is delayed or fails, if the row has been deleted, or if an installation_id is supplied directly, the pipeline can create/claim a GitHub installation without verifying that the OAuth-authenticated GitHub user installed the app. This is a fail-open bypass of the stated mismatch protection. The flow should fail closed or otherwise verify installer identity before advancing when no Integration/sender data is available.

title: Direct metadata access can crash when sender is missing
body: The sender comparison accesses integration.metadata['sender']['login'] unconditionally. If metadata is missing, sender is missing, or sender lacks login (for example, integrations created without a webhook sender, older integrations, or failed webhooks), this raises KeyError/TypeError and returns a 500 instead of the intended error page. Use safe access and return the installation-failed error when the required sender identity is absent.

title: Matching on mutable GitHub login instead of immutable user ID
body: The implementation binds and compares GitHub logins. GitHub logins are mutable and can be renamed; old logins may later be registered by another user. This can block a legitimate installer after a rename and, in the worse case, allow a different user who acquired the old login to satisfy the check. Use the stable GitHub user ID from both the webhook sender and OAuth user info, and fail if IDs are unavailable.

title: Integration lookups omit provider filter
